Title: Nutritional risk, inflammation, and hospitalization after hemodialysis initiation.
Abstract: Evidence linking nutritional and inflammatory markers at hemodialysis initiation to subsequent hospital stay remains limited. We examined whether the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at hemodialysis initiation were associated with prolonged post-initiation hospital stay. This single-center retrospective study included patients who initiated hemodialysis during hospitalization and transitioned to maintenance hemodialysis between 2004 and 2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for 30 days or longer after hemodialysis initiation. Multivariable logistic regression was used with adjustment for age, sex, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, initiation modality, calendar period, and pre-hemodialysis vascular access status. Among 517 patients, 501 were included in multivariable analysis, and 166 patients (32.1%) experienced prolonged post-initiation stay. A higher GNRI was associated with lower odds of prolonged stay (odds ratio per 1-unit increase, 0.955; 95% confidence interval, 0.925-0.986; p = 0.005), whereas higher log-transformed CRP was associated with higher odds (odds ratio, 1.203; 95% confidence interval, 1.055-1.372; p = 0.006). The low GNRI/high CRP group had the highest odds of prolonged stay (odds ratio, 3.180; 95% confidence interval, 1.489-6.787; p = 0.003), without significant multiplicative interaction. Lower GNRI and higher CRP at hemodialysis initiation were independently and jointly associated with prolonged post-initiation stay. These findings describe associations rather than validated predictions, and prospective evaluation is required before these markers are applied to individual-level risk assessment.

Title: Association between nursing assessment indicators and adverse outcomes in hospitalized patients with atrial fibrillation: A retrospective observational study.
Abstract: This retrospective observational study examines the association between routinely collected admission nursing assessment indicators and in-hospital adverse outcomes among hospitalized patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). A total of 312 hospitalized patients with AF admitted to a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2021 and December 2024 were included. The Morse Fall Scale, Barthel Index, Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002), and Braden Scale were assessed within 24 hours of admission. Clinical characteristics, vital signs, and laboratory data were extracted from electronic medical records. The composite adverse outcome comprised in-hospital death, unplanned intensive care unit admission, worsening heart failure requiring treatment escalation, major bleeding requiring medical intervention, or thromboembolic events. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to examine associations with the composite outcome. Among 312 patients, 68 (21.8%) experienced at least one adverse outcome. In the adjusted analysis, a higher Morse Fall Scale score was associated with higher odds of adverse outcomes (OR 1.031, 95% CI 1.012-1.051; P = .002), whereas a higher Barthel Index score was associated with lower odds (OR 0.978, 95% CI 0.961-0.995; P = .012). A higher NRS-2002 score was associated with higher odds (OR 1.376, 95% CI 1.083-1.748; P = .009), and a higher serum albumin level was associated with lower odds (OR 0.953, 95% CI 0.920-0.988; P = .010). AF type and Braden Scale score were not independently associated with the composite outcome after adjustment. Admission nursing assessments of fall risk, functional status, and nutritional risk, together with serum albumin, were independently associated with in-hospital adverse outcomes. These results support their use as complementary markers of vulnerability and for closer clinical surveillance, but they do not establish causality or justify changing guideline-directed AF treatment. Prospective multicenter studies are required before these measures can be incorporated into validated clinical decision tools.

Title: Association of systemic immune-inflammation index with all-cause, cardiovascular and cancer-related mortality in cancer survivors: A population-based cohort study.
Abstract: Chronic inflammation plays an important role in the development of multiple diseases, including carcinogenesis and cancer progression. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), a composite biomarker derived from routine blood cell counts, reflects systemic inflammatory status. However, whether this index is associated with mortality outcomes among diverse cancer survivors in a nationally representative population remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the associations between SII and all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer-related mortality among cancer survivors in the United States. This study included 2624 cancer survivors from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles conducted between 1999 and 2018, with mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations between SII and mortality outcomes. Restricted cubic spline analyses, piecewise linear regression, and subgroup analyses were further performed to examine potential nonlinear associations. In the fully adjusted model, the adjusted hazard ratio for all-cause mortality was 1.39 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.19-1.62) for participants in Q3 compared with those in Q2. For cancer-related mortality, the adjusted hazard ratios were 1.61 (95% CI, 1.19-2.19) for Q1 and 1.60 (95% CI, 1.19-2.15) for Q3, respectively, compared with Q2. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a U-shaped nonlinear association between lnSII (ln-transformation SII) and all-cause mortality and cancer-related mortality, with inflection points of 6.251 and 6.326, respectively. Our findings suggest a U-shaped nonlinear association between lnSII and all-cause mortality and cancer-related mortality in cancer survivors. SII may represent a potential biomarker for future mortality risk-stratification research; however, its clinical utility requires further validation in prospective studies and external cohorts.

Title: Exploratory clinical predictors of prolonged hospital stay in patients with patent foramen ovale undergoing transthoracic echocardiography- or X-ray-guided closure.
Abstract: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) can be managed using different image-guided treatment modalities; however, the determinants of prolonged hospitalization remain insufficiently defined. This retrospective study aimed to identify clinical predictors associated with length of hospital stay and to develop a machine learning model for predicting prolonged hospitalization in patients with PFO. Clinical data from 216 patients with PFO treated at Gansu Provincial People's Hospital were retrospectively analyzed. Among them, 106 patients underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-guided treatment and 110 underwent X-ray-guided treatment. According to the median length of stay, patients were divided into a short-stay group (≤7 days) and a prolonged-stay group (>7 days). Baseline variables were compared between groups. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection. Five machine learning algorithms were then developed and compared in the training cohort, followed by validation in an independent validation cohort. Thirteen baseline variables showed significant between-group differences. LASSO regression retained 10 candidate predictors for model construction. Among the evaluated models, the random forest model showed the best overall performance. In the validation cohort, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.692, a precision of 0.708, a recall of 0.850, an F1-score of 0.773, and an AUC of 0.711, indicating moderate discrimination. The random forest model demonstrated moderate predictive discrimination for prolonged hospital stay. Given the limited sample size and single-center retrospective design, the model should be considered exploratory and requires external validation in larger independent cohorts before clinical use.

Title: Relationship between coronary flow reserve and coronary calcium burden in patients with suspected coronary artery disease: A retrospective analysis.
Abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) measures atherosclerotic burden, while coronary flow reserve (CFR) measures coronary vasodilator function. The study aimed to assess the relationship between CAC burden and CFR and to define clinical and imaging factors independently associated with compromised CFR. This retrospective observational study included 467 patients aged 16 to 93 years who underwent clinically indicated CAC assessment and quantitative ^82Rb PET/computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging with pharmacological vasodilator stress between January 2024 and June 2026. CAC was categorized as 0, 1 to 99, 100 to 399, or ≥400 Agatston units. CFR was calculated as stress-to-rest myocardial blood flow, with CFR < 2.0 defined as impaired. Correlation, multivariable linear regression, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Mean age was 61.8 ± 13.7 years, with 59.1% male participants; 39.6% had impaired CFR. Mean CFR decreased progressively from 2.43 ± 0.62 in patients with CAC = 0 to 1.57 ± 0.47 with CAC ≥ 400 (P for trend < .001), while impaired CFR increased from 25.9% to 67.1%. CFR was inversely correlated with CAC (Spearman r = -0.43, P < .001). After adjustment, CAC 100 to 399 and ≥400 remained independently associated with impaired CFR (adjusted OR 2.41, 95% confidence interval 1.35 to 4.30 and OR 3.28, 95% confidence interval 1.72 to 6.25, respectively). Age, diabetes, and abnormal myocardial perfusion were also independently associated with impaired CFR. CAC was independently associated with lower CFR and a higher prevalence of impaired CFR. This association remained after multivariable adjustment, and also on sensitivity analysis, indicating that these 2 approaches to coronary assessment complement each other. The results of this study are presented as associations, due to its retrospective cross sectional design.

Title: Treatment outcomes and associated factors among acute coronary syndrome patients admitted to Jimma University Medical Centre, Jimma, Ethiopia: A 5-year retrospective study.
Abstract: In developing countries, acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is becoming a more common cause of cardiovascular death. Although thrombolytic treatments and limited percutaneous coronary intervention have been introduced, in-hospital mortality from ACS is still high in sub-Saharan countries. This study aimed to evaluate the treatment outcome of ACS and its associated factors among patients attending Jimma University Medical Center, Jimma, Ethiopia. A retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 ACS patients. Patient records from admissions between November 1st, 2017, and October 31st, 2022 were reviewed, with data collected between December 1st and 31st, 2022. Data were collected using a structured checklist, entered, and analyzed using Statistical Package for Social science version 26. Descriptive analysis was used to summarize baseline characteristics and determine treatment outcomes. Bivariable and multivariable regression analyses were employed to determine factors affecting poor treatment outcomes. The odds ratio with a 95% confidence interval was computed, and a P value < .05 was considered significant. Among the 300 ACS patients included in our study, 35.3% died during hospitalization. Hypertension was the most common risk factor, present in 88.3% of the patients. In addition, 20.3% were classified as Killip class III or IV. 20.7% had a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of less than or equal to 30%, and 79.3% had an LVEF > 30%. Regarding treatment, an aspirin loading dose, clopidogrel loading dose, beta-blockers, statins, morphine, and nitrates were given to 284 (94.7%), 286 (95.3%), 227 (75.7%), 283 (94.3%), 109 (36.3%), and 80 (26.7%) patients, respectively. Factors significantly associated with in-hospital mortality were older age (P ≤ .001), history of diabetes (P = .004), ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction diagnosis (P = .003), and Killip class III and IV (P ≤ .001), whereas LVEF > 30% was associated with significantly lower odds of in-hospital death (P < .001). The proportion of in-hospital mortality attributable to ACS was found to be high. As a result, timely evidence-based therapy should be included in the setup.

Title: Factors associated with subtype classification and 3-month functional outcome in ischemic stroke, focusing on large-artery atherosclerosis and small-vessel occlusion: A retrospective observational study.
Abstract: Ischemic stroke accounts for a rising share of the total stroke burden. This retrospective observational study aimed to identify factors associated with subtype classification and 3-month functional outcome among patients with ischemic stroke, focusing on large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA) and small-vessel occlusion (SVO). This retrospective study included patients with ischemic stroke admitted to a regional tertiary hospital between 2019 and 2021, who were classified using the Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) criteria. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with each subtype (vs all other subtypes) and with an excellent 3-month outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-1) within the LAA and SVO groups. Among 1823 patients, the etiologies were LAA (30.33%), cardioembolism (18.87%), SVO (41.09%), and other stroke types (9.71%). Female sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.71; P = .005) was inversely and age (aOR, 1.02 per year; P < .001) positively associated with LAA, whereas dyslipidemia (aOR, 1.81; P < .001) was positively associated, and ischemic heart disease (aOR, 0.54; P = .023) and older age (aOR, 0.68; P < .001) were inversely associated, with SVO. For an excellent 3-month outcome, female sex was associated with lower odds (aOR, 0.54; P = .003) and obesity with higher odds (aOR, 1.59; P = .015) in the LAA group, whereas age (aOR, 0.97 per year; P < .001) and hypertension (aOR, 0.70; P = .033) were associated with lower odds, and obesity with higher odds (aOR, 1.39; P = .044), in the SVO group. After additional adjustment for initial stroke severity, the associations of female sex, obesity, and age persisted, whereas that of hypertension was attenuated; with functional independence (mRS 0-2) as the outcome, age, hypertension, and obesity were no longer significant. The factors associated with subtype classification and with 3-month functional outcome differ between ischemic stroke subtypes. Because only patients with ischemic stroke were included and the primary outcome models were not adjusted for initial stroke severity, these results are hypothesis-generating and may inform subtype-specific strategies in stroke management and future research.

Title: Major re-amputation after initial diabetic foot amputation: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: Reamputation after initial diabetic foot amputation remains a major clinical challenge associated with substantial morbidity. Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation. This retrospective cohort study included 141 patients who underwent lower-extremity amputation for diabetic foot disease between 2020 and 2025. Demographic variables, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), infection history, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) were analyzed. Major reamputation was defined as a subsequent ipsilateral amputation progressing to a below-knee or above-knee level; contralateral amputations and more proximal minor amputations confined to the foot were not considered outcome events. The median follow-up was 3.0 years (range, 1-5). Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and categorical variables using the Pearson chi-square test. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate major reamputation-free survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to evaluate factors associated with time to major reamputation. A Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis was additionally performed considering death before major reamputation as a competing event. Major reamputation occurred in 31 patients (22.0%). Patients with reamputation had significantly lower BMI and PNI values and higher HbA1c levels (all P < .001). Smoking and PAD were significantly more frequent in the reamputation group (both P < .001), whereas no significant between-group differences were observed for age, sex, serum albumin, or infection history. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, PAD (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.13-18.32, P < .001) and higher HbA1c (adjusted HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.19-1.65, P < .001) were independently associated with an increased hazard of major reamputation, whereas higher PNI was associated with a reduced hazard (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99, P = .009). Lower BMI, higher HbA1c, reduced PNI, smoking, and PAD were associated with major reamputation. In multivariable time-to-event analysis, PAD, HbA1c, and PNI remained independently associated with the outcome. These findings demonstrate associations between routinely available clinical parameters and major reamputation and warrant further evaluation in prospective studies.

Title: Efficacy and safety of herbal medicine for Hymenoptera stings: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hymenoptera stings can cause severe anaphylaxis and venom-induced multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. Although conventional medicine (CM) can effectively control acute symptoms, its ability to prevent delayed venom-related organ injury remains limited. Therefore, herbal medicine (HM) combined with CM has been investigated to enhance venom detoxification and elimination. However, comprehensive evidence-based syntheses evaluating these interventions remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of HM + CM in mitigating venom-induced toxicity.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials was conducted. Major electronic databases were searched for studies comparing HM + CM and CM alone. Outcomes included total effective rate and biomarkers of hepatic, renal, cardiac, and inflammatory responses.
RESULTS: Overall, 11 randomized controlled trials involving 1443 patients were included. While the total effective rate was statistically higher in the HM + CM group than in the CM-alone group (risk ratio, 1.03), this represents a modest 3% relative improvement with limited clinical relevance for acute symptom control. Instead, adjunctive HM was significantly associated with lower levels of biomarkers of hepatic injury (aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and total bilirubin), cardiac injury (creatine kinase and creatine kinase-myocardial band), systemic inflammation (C-reactive protein or high-sensitivity C-reactive protein), and renal dysfunction (serum creatinine), reflecting favorable changes in laboratory biomarkers associated with multi-organ toxicity. Although no adverse events were reported among the limited number of studies that formally assessed safety, the available evidence is insufficient to establish the definitive safety of HM.
CONCLUSION: HM combined with conventional care appears to be a potentially useful adjunctive approach for Hymenoptera stings. While its additive effect on acute symptom resolution is clinically modest in the context of standard emergency care, adjunctive HM may offer a broader therapeutic scope. Specifically, it may complement clinical recovery while attenuating venom-induced systemic inflammation and improving related laboratory biomarkers.

Title: Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.
Abstract: This study aimed to investigate clinical correlates of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults, compare seven classification models, and interpret the selected gradient boosting machine (GBM) classifier. This single-center observational study included 572 adults reported to be aged ≥ 60 years who received care between June 2021 and June 2023, comprising 385 participants classified as having persistent AF and 187 comparators. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) were used for candidate-variable assessment and feature reduction. Logistic regression and six machine-learning models-support vector machine, GBM, neural network, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), AdaBoost, and CatBoost-were compared using a reported 70:30 development/test split and tenfold cross-validation during model development. Model performance and interpretation were examined using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), decision-curve analysis (DCA), and SHapley additive explanations (SHAP). The sequence of feature selection and data partitioning could not be verified. Fourteen candidate variables were significantly associated with persistent AF in univariable analysis, of which 9 remained significant after multivariable adjustment. LASSO retained 5 features: glycated hemoglobin, C2HEST score, heart failure, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and CO2. GBM achieved a development-set AUC of 0.970 (95% CI 0.957-0.983). In the test set, GBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost achieved AUCs of 0.919 (95% CI 0.874-0.963), 0.920 (95% CI 0.876-0.963), and 0.919 (95% CI 0.876-0.962), respectively. DCA suggested favorable net benefit for GBM across selected threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified ALT as the feature with the greatest contribution to GBM predictions, followed by the C2HEST score. GBM achieved the highest development-set AUC, whereas test-set AUCs were similar across GBM, CatBoost, and XGBoost. The five-feature classifier warrants further investigation for distinguishing persistent AF status in older adults. Verification of the analytical workflow, external validation, and calibration assessment are required before clinical application.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Association of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index with self-reported stroke among U.S. adults: a cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
Abstract: Systemic inflammation and insulin resistance are implicated in the pathophysiology of stroke. The C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index (CTI) integrates inflammatory and metabolic information, but its association with self-reported stroke in a representative U.S. population remains uncertain. We examined the association between CTI and self-reported stroke and explored potential nonlinear patterns. This cross-sectional analysis used National Health And Nutrition Examination Survey data from 2005 to 2010 and included 6053 adults aged 20 years or older. CTI was calculated as 0.412 × Ln(CRP [mg/L]) + Ln(TG [mg/dL] × FPG [mg/dL]/2). Stroke was defined by self-reported physician diagnosis. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed. Multiple imputation and sensitivity analyses excluding participants with coexisting cardiovascular disease were conducted to assess robustness. In Model 3, continuous CTI was not significantly associated with self-reported stroke (odds ratio [OR] = 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.93-1.48; P = .200). Multiple imputation yielded consistent results (OR = 1.28; 95% CI: 0.94-1.74; P = .125). After excluding 496 participants with coexisting cardiovascular disease, the association remained nonsignificant (OR = 1.30; 95% CI: 0.90-1.86; P = .155; P for trend = .723). Evidence of nonlinearity was observed in the unadjusted model (P for nonlinearity = .0172) but not after covariate adjustment (Model 2, P = .3420; Model 3, P = .6407). Significant interactions were observed for age, marital status, body mass index, and diabetes status (P for interaction = .002, .025, .001, and .001, respectively). The nonlinear pattern observed in the unadjusted analysis was attenuated after covariate adjustment, and the fully adjusted linear association was not statistically significant. These cross-sectional findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies with clinically adjudicated stroke outcomes.

Title: Temporal trends and disparities in mortality associated with heart failure and underlying ischemic heart disease in the US population: A Nationwide retrospective cross-sectional study (1999-2023).
Abstract: Heart Failure (HF) remains a significant public health concern, frequently associated with ischemic heart disease (IHD) as a major underlying condition in mortality statistics. Using national death certificate data, we evaluated population-level mortality trends and estimates among individuals in whom IHD was recorded as the underlying cause and HF as a contributing factor to characterize long-term epidemiological shifts and identify high-risk subgroups. We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research database and extracted Multiple Cause-of-Death records for adults aged 25 and older from 1999 to 2023. We isolated cases where IHD was the underlying cause and HF was a contributing factor. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 persons of the underlying United States population and standardized to the 2000 United States standard population. Temporal trends were evaluated using Join point regression to compute the annual percent change annual percent change across demographic and geographic strata. A total of 2050,021 deaths were identified during the study period. Overall AAMRs declined significantly from 1999 to 2012 (annual percent change -4.89), but this reduction plateaued to a milder decline through 2023. Males exhibited consistently higher mortality than females. While older adults experienced continuous mortality declines, rates among middle-aged and young adults have increased significantly over the past decade. Geographically, the Midwest region and non-metropolitan areas maintained the highest AAMRs. Despite substantial reductions in HF-associated mortality with IHD as the underlying cause between 1999 and 2012, this progress has recently stabilized. Persistent disparities across sex, age, race, and location emphasize the need for targeted preventive strategies.

Title: Alfred Kocher technique for prevention of patient-prosthesis mismatch in paediatric patients.
Journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
Abstract: Aortic valve replacement requires special considerations in paediatric patients, who are not yet fully grown. The Ross procedure remains the gold standard in paediatric patients as it offers growth potential. If the Ross procedure is not feasible, or the size of the aortic annulus precludes placement of an adult-sized mechanical prosthesis, the problem of patient-prosthesis mismatch and subsequent aortic valve reinterventions arises. The standardized option for this patient cohort is the Konno incision and patch ventriculoplasty in combination with an adult-sized mechanical prosthesis, which carries substantial procedural complexity and risk. This video tutorial demonstrates posterior aortic root enlargement using the Alfred Kocher technique in a 7-year-old female with a functionally unicuspid aortic valve and a bicuspid pulmonary valve. The bicuspid pulmonary valve was an unplanned intraoperative finding, making the patient ineligible for a durable autograft transplantation. The technique involves an inverted T-shaped incision in the centre of the non-coronary sinus, and reconstruction with a barrel-shaped patch tailored from a 28 mm Valsalva prosthesis to augment the non-coronary sinus in an anatomical fashion, allowing upsizing by 5 mm in annular diameter. This technique enabled implantation of a 21 mm size mechanical prosthesis (diameter = 24 mm) upsized from a 19 mm annulus.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Video-Audio Media; Case Reports

Title: Elevated Systemic Inflammation Response Index on Admission Indicates Stress Ulcer Risk in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress ulcers following acute ischemic stroke worsen prognosis and increase healthcare burden. Inflammatory mechanisms are involved, yet the association between the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) and ulcer risk remains unclear. This study investigates the correlation between SIRI levels and post-stroke stress ulcer risk.
METHODS: We analyzed data from a prospective registry of adult stroke patients admitted within seven days of onset. SIRI was defined as neutrophil count × monocyte count / lymphocyte count. SIRI levels were categorized into quartiles (Q1-Q4). Using the lowest quartile as reference, Cox regression models with full adjustment for confounders assessed the hazard ratios for ulcer risk across SIRI groups. Restricted cubic spline and subgroup analyses were employed.
RESULTS: Among 1,171 patients, 86 (7.3%) developed stress ulcers within 7 days. After full adjustment, higher SIRI levels were independently associated with increased risk, with adjusted hazard ratios of 3.17 (95% CI: 1.06-9.50) for Q3 and 5.61 (95% CI: 1.93-16.33) for Q4. A linear dose-response relationship was observed, with risk rising notably when SIRI exceeded 1.1. This association was modified by age, NIHSS score, and infarct location.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated SIRI levels are significantly associated with an increased risk of post-stroke stress ulcers. As an easily accessible biomarker, it can be used to identify high-risk patients at an early stage, thereby guiding targeted prevention strategies.

Title: Machine learning-driven ECG screening for early coronary artery disease detection.
Abstract: BackgroundElectrocardiography (ECG) is inexpensive and widely available, yet its ability to detect early and nonobstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) is limited when interpreted using conventional criteria. We evaluated whether a deep learning model applied to standard 12-lead-ECG images can identify angiographically confirmed CAD and enable clinically meaningful risk stratification in a real-world population.MethodsIn this multicentric study, 15,890 ECG-angiography pairs (12-lead ECG paired with coronary angiography [CA] or coronary CT angiography [CCTA]) were included between November 2021 and January 2024. A DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network was trained to predict CAD from ECG images. Temporal validation was performed on a prospectively collected, independent cohort of 2168 samples from February to May 2024. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), PR-AUC, and standard diagnostic metrics. Robustness across varying disease prevalence was evaluated using simulation, and prevalence-dependent predictive performance was summarized using PPV and NPV prevalence curves (AUCppv and AUCnpv).ResultsThe model was trained on 13,299 samples, validated on 1,002, and tested on 1339 (CAD prevalence 52.9%). On the test set, ROC-AUC was 0.80 and PR-AUC 0.83. At the optimal 0.50 threshold, sensitivity was 87% (618/708 CAD cases detected) and specificity 50% (317/631 non-CAD correctly classified). On the temporal validation set (n = 2168; 64% CAD), ROC-AUC was 0.81 and PR-AUC 0.83, with sensitivity 0.67, specificity 0.78, PPV 0.84, and NPV 0.57. Simulated prevalence analyses demonstrated robust PPV/NPV trends across distributions.ConclusionDeep learning analysis of routinely acquired ECG images can identify patients at increased risk of CAD and may support low-cost, scalable CAD risk stratification.

Title: Measurement-Informed and Fluid-Sparing Cardiovascular Resuscitation Strategies in Pediatric Septic Shock: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: BackgroundPediatric septic shock resuscitation requires restoration of tissue perfusion while avoiding unnecessary fluid accumulation. The available comparative evidence includes both measurement-informed cardiovascular strategies and protocolized early vasoactive/fluid-sparing strategies, which differ substantially in mechanism and implementation.MethodsWe conducted a prospectively registered systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of pediatric septic shock. To address clinical heterogeneity, interventions were classified post hoc, without changing eligibility criteria or outcomes, as measurement-informed technology-enabled strategies, structured early vasoactive/fluid-sparing strategies, or a hybrid phenotype-informed strategy. Randomized and nonrandomized evidence were analyzed separately. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood; Wald 95% confidence intervals were primary and Hartung-Knapp intervals were examined for every pooled outcome. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty using GRADE.ResultsSix comparative studies involving 422 children met eligibility criteria, including five randomized controlled trials and one prospective comparative study. The exploratory mortality synthesis across randomized strategies showed no statistically detectable difference (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.60-1.28; very-low-certainty evidence); the measurement-informed subgroup yielded RR 0.77 (95% CI 0.46-1.27). Two small randomized trials of measurement-informed resuscitation suggested lower total fluid administration during the first 24 h (MD -11.47 mL/kg, 95% CI -16.88 to -6.05; moderate-certainty evidence). Evidence for acute kidney injury was very uncertain (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.15-1.57). Other outcomes were synthesized narratively because definitions, time points, or estimands were not sufficiently comparable.ConclusionsThe pediatric evidence base comprises mechanistically distinct cardiovascular resuscitation strategies rather than a single uniform intervention. Exploratory mortality pooling does not establish benefit or equivalence. Two small measurement-informed trials suggest lower 24-h fluid administration, but whether this process-level effect improves patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. Future trials should prospectively link measured physiological variables or protocolized treatment rules to standardized clinical outcomes.

Title: Association of ALI and mCONUT With In-Hospital De Novo Heart Failure in Patients With STEMI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: De novo heart failure (HF) during the first ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) hospitalization significantly increases mortality and readmission. While nutritional and inflammatory indicators like the advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI) and modified Controlling Nutritional Status (mCONUT) score are gaining attention, their exact association with post-STEMI de novo HF remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective study (January 2016 to June 2025) included 1598 first-time STEMI patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. Patients were categorized into de novo HF and non-HF groups to evaluate the association of ALI and mCONUT scores with HF development.
RESULTS: The HF group exhibited significantly lower ALI and higher mCONUT scores compared to the non-HF group. Multivariate logistic regression identified lower ALI and higher mCONUT scores as independent predictors of HF risk. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated that mCONUT possessed better predictive performance than ALI, with effects remaining highly consistent across subgroups. Sensitivity analyses and NRI/IDI results confirmed that mCONUT provides independent incremental predictive value beyond traditional risk models (optimism-corrected C-statistic 0.785 vs. 0.751). These associations were independent of admission hemodynamic status (Killip class) and treatment era.
CONCLUSION: Both ALI and mCONUT scores are independently associated with in-hospital de novo HF in STEMI patients. The mCONUT score demonstrates superior predictive performance, serving as a promising indicator for early risk stratification.

Title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
Abstract: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification. Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.

Title: Impact of Computed Tomography-Derived Body Composition on Mortality and Conduction Disturbances After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Sex-Specific Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed for severe aortic stenosis with improving procedural success rates; however, post-procedural complications remain a significant clinical challenge. Growing evidence suggests that sarcopenia may adversely affect morbidity and mortality in this patient population.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 171 patients undergoing elective TAVI (January 2018-February 2024). Muscle area (MA), visceral, subcutaneous (SATA), and total adipose tissue area (TATA) were measured at the L3 vertebral level from pre-procedural computed tomography angiography (CTA). Primary endpoints were all-cause and cardiac mortality; secondary endpoints were permanent cardiac conduction defect, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI), and hospital stay.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 95 women (55.5%) and 76 men (44.5%), median age 78.9 years, society of thoracic surgeons score 6.30 (IQR = 4.37-9.33). Over 21.8 ± 17.9 months, 43 patients (25.1%) died, including 12 cardiac deaths (7.0%). Lower MA and MA/body mass index (BMI) ratio were independently associated with cardiac mortality in men (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 0.935, P = .016 and OR = 0.983, P = .042). Permanent cardiac conduction defect occurred in 44 patients (27.7%); lower SATA and TATA were independent predictors in women (OR = 0.990, P = .031 and OR = 0.994, P = .024). Permanent pacemaker implantation was required in 30 patients (18.6%); adipose tissue parameters were associated with PPI in women on univariate analysis but did not retain significance after multiple adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural CTA-derived body composition assessment may contribute to the prediction of mortality and morbidity in TAVI patients without additional cost or radiation exposure. The association of lower MA with cardiac mortality in men, and of reduced adipose tissue with conduction disturbances in women, suggests that sex-specific body composition parameters may provide prognostic value beyond conventional risk scores.

Title: Functional Mitochondrial States in Heart Failure: Mechanistic Hypotheses and Therapeutic Testing.
Abstract:
SIGNIFICANCE: Mitochondrial function links myocardial energy demand to substrate metabolism, calcium handling, redox regulation, and tissue repair. These processes vary within heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, creating opportunities for mechanistic phenotyping across conventional clinical categories.
RECENT ADVANCES: Human myocardial metabolomics and proteomics reveal heterogeneous metabolic remodeling, while experimental cardiac studies connect organelle dynamics, quality control, contact sites, and immune-cell metabolism to functional adaptation and injury. Contrasting substrate and intervention findings emphasize the importance of direction, cellular origin, and physiological context.
CRITICAL ISSUES: Eight interacting modules organize the measurement space. Five illustrative configurations connect energetic and substrate abnormalities, calcium-transfer defects, and downstream injury or immune activity to research questions. They represent different biological levels and have not been jointly derived or validated in human cohorts. Ferroptotic execution and inflammation require separate measurements; their coupling in human HF remains a hypothesis.
FUTURE DIRECTIONS: We propose a worked research rule, a concrete exploratory biomarker panel, and a validation pathway incorporating tissue provenance, temporal behavior, and randomized treatment interactions. Adequate target engagement without cardiac or clinical benefit can challenge therapeutic relevance or patient selection. Clinical application requires reproducible human measurements that improve treatment decisions and outcomes; validated individual assignment is currently unavailable. Antioxid. Redox Signal. 00, 000-000.

Title: White Blood Cell Count-related Biomarkers for Acute Myocardial Infarction: Integrative Analysis of Mouse Models and Clinical Samples.
Journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although white blood cell count (WBC) is an accessible prognostic marker, the relationship between WBC-related genes and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear.
METHODS: A retrospective study of 1,917 patients with AMI was conducted to estimate prognostic indicators. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was used to identify potential genes associated with the prognostic indicators, and the resulting genes were intersected with differentially expressed genes from the key monocyte subset identified in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyses. Key genes were screened by integrating 52 machine learning algorithms. The expression of key genes was validated by RT-qPCR with clinical samples. In addition, an AMI mouse model was established, and the expression of related proteins was further validated by western blotting and immunohistochemistry.
RESULTS: Age, WBC, and serum potassium (K) level were identified as prognostic indicators for AMI. Eight key genes were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that these genes were significantly enriched in immune- and inflammation-related pathways. RT-qPCR validation showed that the expression trends of five key genes (ITGA4, RASA3, ATG7, HSPA6, and ITGAM) were consistent with the bioinformatics results, whereas DSTN, FES, and MCL1 did not reach statistical significance. Additionally, WB and IHC further validated HSP70 family protein upregulation in the AMI mouse model.
DISCUSSION: Eight AMI-related genes were identified and might contribute to disease progression through inflammatory regulation. The integration of multi-omics analysis and experimental validation underscores the translational potential of these genes. Although further experimental validation is warranted, these findings may offer novel insights for the development of therapeutic strategies for AMI.
CONCLUSION: This study identified eight key WBC-related genes that may serve as potential biomarkers for AMI.

Title: [Clinical efficacy of spermatic vein shunt on nutcracker syndrome with severe varicocele].
Journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
Abstract: Objective To explore the clinical efficacy of spermatic vein shunt in the treatment of patients with nutcracker syndrome accompanied by severe varicocele. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 27 patients with nutcracker syndrome complicated with severe varicocele who were treated with microscopic spermatic vein shunt at Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital from January 2020 to January 2023. The surgical time, intraoperative blood loss, hospital stay duration, postoperative semen and urine improvement, symptom alleviation, postoperative complications, and recurrence rate of varicocele within one year were recorded. Results The surgeries for 27 patients were successful, with an average operation time of (2.5±0.5) hours, an average intraoperative blood loss of (30.0±4.8) mL, and an average postoperative hospital stay of (5.0±1.3) days. All 27 patients completed the follow-up. Post-surgery ultrasound imaging showed unobstructed blood flow in the anastomosed vessels. Follow-up assessments revealed that one patient experienced a recurrence of varicocele after nine months of operation, resulting in a recurrence rate of 3.7% (1 out of 27 patients). Postoperative sperm concentration and motility improved compared to preoperative levels. Postoperative sperm concentration and motility improved compared to preoperative levels. There was no significant difference in concentration (P >0.05), but there was a statistically significant difference in motility (P<0.05). There was no improvement in sperm morphology. There was no case of hematuria after the surgery. Two patients developed hydrocele three days after the surgery, while none of the other patients experienced complications such as scrotal edema, epididymitis, scrotal discomfort, or wound infections in the following years. Conclusion For the patients with nutcracker syndrome complicated with severe varicocele, microscopic spermatic vein shunt can be performed with the advantage of low recurrence rate of varicocele postoperatively and significant improvement of semen quality and hematuria, which can result in minimal trauma and fewer complications. This surgical procedure is suitable for clinical promotion.

Title: [Effect of Guilu Taohong decoction on spermatogenic function and sex hormone levels in a rat model of varicocele].
Journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
Abstract: Objective To investigate the effects and mechanisms of Guilu Taohong decoction on spermatogenic function and sex hormone levels in a rat model of varicocele (VC). Methods Forty-eight SPF-grade male SD rats (6 weeks old) were randomly assigned to the sham-operated group, model group, Guilu Taohong decoction group and L-carnitine group. Except for the sham operation group, the other groups were respectively given corresponding drug intragastric intervention for 8 weeks after modeling. After the intervention, the diameters of the left spermatic vein in each group of rats were detected. The morphological structure of testicular, epididymal and renal tissues was observed by HE staining, and the degree of testicular interstitial fibrosis was evaluated by Masson staining. The levels of serum testosterone (T), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and inhibin B (INH-B) were detected by ELISA. The expressions of hypoxia-inducible factor-1 α (HIF-1α) and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) in testicular tissue were detected by Western blot.Results Compared with the sham-operated group, the left spermatic vein of rats in the model group was significantly dilated (P<0.01), the tissue structure of the testis and epididymis was disordered, spermatogenic cells decreased, and interstitial fibrosis was obvious. The levels of serum T and INH-B decreased significantly (all P<0.01), the levels of FSH and LH increased (all P<0.01), and the expressions of HIF-1α and VEGFA were significantly upregulated (all P<0.01). Compared with the model group, the Guilu Taohong decoction group exhibited significantly reduced left spermatic vein diameter (P<0.05), improved testicular and epididymal structure, increased spermatogenic cell number, attenuated interstitial fibrosis, elevated serum T and INH-B(all P<0.01), decreased FSH and LH levels (all P<0.05), and downregulated HIF-1α and VEGFA expression (all P<0.01). Compared with the sham-operated group，the L-carnitine group showed increased T and INH-B levels (all P<0.05), decreased FSH and LH levels (all P<0.01), and reduced HIF-1α and VEGFA expression (all P<0.05). But Guilu Taohong decoction group exhibited more pronounced T elevation and HIF-1α reduction (P<0.05). The renal tissue structures of rats in each group were intact, and no obvious pathological changes were observed. Conclusions Guilu Taohong decoction effectively improves spermatic vein dilation and spermatogenic function in VC model rats. Its mechanisms may involve inhibition of HIF-1α/VEGFA expression, alleviation of local hypoxia and tissue fibrosis, and restoration of reproductive endocrine homeostasis, with good safety.

Title: [Effect of integrin α5β1 on erectile function of spontaneously hypertensive rats].
Journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
Abstract: Objective To explore the mechanism by which inhibition of integrin α5β1 in the context of hypertension downregulates the expression of RAS homolog gene family members (RhoA)/Rho-associated kinase (ROCK) signaling proteins in the penile corpus cavernosum tissue, and affects the erectile function of rats.Methods Fifteen 12-week-old spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) were randomly divided into the SHR group, SHR+LV-empty group(transfected with empty lentiviral vector) and SHR+LV-siRNA group (transfected with lentivirus carrying siRNA targeting integrin α5β1), with 5 rats in each group. Fifteen 12-week-old normotensive Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats were randomly divided into the WKY rat group, WKY+LV-empty group (transfected with empty lentiviral vector) and WKY+LV-siRNA group (transfected with lentivirus carrying siRNA targeting integrin α5β1), with 5 rats in each group. In the WKY group and SHR group, 20 μL of normal saline was injected into the middle part of the penile corpus cavernosum. While in the SHR + LV-empty group and WKY + LV-empty group, 20 μL of empty lentiviral vector (titer 1×108 TU/mL) was injected into the middle part of the penile corpus cavernosum. In the SHR+LV-siRNA group and WKY+LV-siRNA group, 20 μL of lentivirus carrying integrin α5β1 interference (titer 1×108 TU/mL) was injected into the middle part of the penile corpus cavernosum. One week after transfection, the body weight, levels of serum testosterone, ratio of the maximum intracavernous pressure to the mean arterial pressure (ICPmax/MAP) of rats in each group, the expression of integrin α5β1, FAK, ROCK1, ROCK2, and eNOS in penile corpus cavernosum, as well as the content of nitric oxide (NO) were measured. Results There was no statistically significant difference in body weight and serum testosterone levels among the rats in each group (P> 0.05). Compared with the WKY group, the ICPmax/MAP in the SHR group was significantly lower (P< 0.05), and the expressions of integrin α5β1, FAK, ROCK1, and ROCK2 in the penile corpus cavernosum of the SHR group were significantly higher (P<0.05), while the expression of eNOS and the content of NO decreased significantly (P<0.05). After successful transfection with integrin α5β1 interfering lentivirus, compared with the WKY+LV-empty group, there were no statistically significant differences in ICPmax/MAP, eNOS expression in the penile corpus cavernosum, and NO content in the WKY+LV-siRNA group (P>0.05), but the expressions of integrin α5β1, FAK, ROCK1, and ROCK2 were significantly decreased (P<0.05). Compared with the SHR+LV-empty group, the ICPmax/MAP in the SHR+LV-siRNA group was significantly increased (P<0.05). There were no statistically significant differences in eNOS expression in the penile corpus cavernosum and NO content (P>0.05). While the expressions of integrin α5β1, FAK, ROCK1, and ROCK2 were significantly decreased (P< 0.05). Conclusion Hypertension upregulates the expression of integrin α5β1 in the penile corpus cavernosum, activates the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway, and leads to penile erectile dysfunction. Inhibiting the expression of integrin α5β1 in penile cavernous tissue of SHRs downregulates the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway and improves the erectile function of SHRs.

Title: Outcomes of extended septal myectomy for hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy in an Asian cohort.
Abstract: BackgroundHypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) is a complex cardiac disorder often treated with septal myectomy, the gold-standard surgical intervention that improves symptoms and survival. Long-term outcome data with paired echocardiographic follow-up from the Indian subcontinent remain limited.MethodsThis was a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing extended septal myectomy for HOCM at a single tertiary referral centre between 2014 and 2024, analysed from a prospectively maintained clinical registry. Demographic, clinical, echocardiographic, operative and follow-up data were analysed. Survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method.ResultsA total of 399 patients underwent extended septal myectomy (mean age 41.2 ± 16.5 years; 282/399, 70.7% male; 46/399, 11.5% aged under 18 years). Septal hypertrophy was mainly mid-septal (255/399, 63.9%), with basal (110/399, 27.6%) and apical (34/399, 8.5%) involvement. Myectomy was isolated in 247/399 patients (61.9%) and combined with a concomitant procedure in 152/399 (38.1%); 15/399 patients (3.8%) had undergone a prior cardiac intervention, including alcohol septal ablation in 1/399 (0.3%) and previous cardiac surgery in 9/399 (2.3%). In-hospital mortality was 6/399 (1.5%). Mean follow-up was 5.4 ± 3.1 years, and median follow-up was 5.9 years (interquartile range 2.5-6.7); vital status was complete for all patients. Survival was 98.1% (95% CI 96.7-99.5) at 5 years and 95.9% (95% CI 92.7-99.0) at 10 years.ConclusionsExtended septal myectomy provides excellent structural, functional, and survival outcomes, comparable to leading centres. It should remain the preferred surgical treatment for symptomatic HOCM.

Title: Clinical Significance of Atherogenic Index of Plasma in Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy A Case Control Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is one of the most common and debilitating complications of diabetes mellitus (DM). The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), calculated from triglyceride and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels, is an indicator of atherogenic lipid profile. The present study aimed to investigate the clinical significance of AIP in patients with DPN.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This study included 200 patients with DM and 200 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. The diabetic patients comprised 100 patients with DPN and 100 patients without DPN. All participants underwent detailed history taking, thorough clinical examination, nerve conduction studies, and standard laboratory investigations.
RESULTS: AIP differed significantly among the three groups, with DPN patients having significantly higher AIp values than diabetic patients without DPN and healthy controls [median (IQR): 0.37 (0.21-0.52) vs. 0.24 (0.09-0.49) and 0.08 (-0.07-0.19), respectively; p<0.001]. Among patients with DPN, those with AIP ≥ the median had a significantly higher frequency of cardiovascular comorbidities (79.7% vs. 51.6%, p=0.008) and severe DPN (40.6% vs. 12.9%, p=0.018). ROC curve analysis showed that AIP had modest discriminatory ability for distinguishing patients with DPN from diabetic patients without DPN [AUC (95% CI): 0.63 (0.55-0.71)].
DISCUSSION: Patients with DPN had significantly higher AIP levels than diabetic patients without neuropathy and healthy controls. Among patients with DPN, higher AIP levels were associated with a greater frequency of severe neuropathy and cardiovascular comorbidities. These findings suggest an association between an atherogenic lipid profile and the presence and clinical characteristics of DPN, although the modest discriminatory performance of AIP indicates that it should not be considered a standalone diagnostic marker for DPN.
CONCLUSION: Patients with DPN had significantly higher AIP levels than diabetic patients without neuropathy and healthy controls. Among patients with DPN, higher AIP levels were associated with more severe neuropathy and a higher frequency of cardiovascular comorbidities. Further studies are warranted to determine whether AIP has an independent or predictive role in DPN.

Title: Case Volumes and Outcomes of Early-Career Operators Performing TAVR in the United States.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Operator experience is a key determinant of outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, whether early-career operators achieve comparable results to more experienced peers is unknown. Herein, we evaluate case volumes, patient risk profiles, and 30-day outcomes of early-career versus non-early-career operators performing TAVR in the United States.
METHODS: Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry, we identified isolated TAVR procedures from October 2011 through March 2024. Early-career status was defined as ≤5 years in independent practice (based on board certification or first TAVR date); non-early-career status was >5 years. Multivariable hierarchical models adjusted for patient-, procedural-, operator-, and site-level factors, including annualized institutional TAVR volume, while accounting for clustering of procedures within operators and operators within sites. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and a composite of death, stroke, major bleeding, stage III acute kidney injury, or moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak.
RESULTS: A total of 634 723 TAVR procedures were performed by 3126 operators across 847 sites, including 90 376 (14.2%) by early-career operators. Median annualized lifetime volume was lower for early-career operators (13 [interquartile range, 5-31] versus 19 [interquartile range, 7-42] cases per year; P<0.001). After adjustment, 30-day mortality was similar between early-career and non-early-career operators (2.38% versus 2.44%; risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.92-1.01]; P=0.293), whereas the composite end point was lower among early-career operators (11.19% versus 11.77%; risk ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.93-0.98]; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In a national TAVR registry, early-career operators performed fewer cases but achieved similar 30-day mortality and a modestly lower adjusted composite event rate relative to more experienced peers. These findings suggest that within the structured, team-based environment of contemporary TAVR programs, early-career status alone is not associated with inferior procedural outcomes and should not be viewed as a barrier to independent practice.

Title: Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions and reshape ventricular geometry in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Early experience demonstrated reductions in mitral regurgitation and improvements in heart failure symptoms.
METHODS: The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Division of Intramural Research Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty Early Feasibility Study was an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter study. Between 1 and 5 years, vital status, serious adverse events, routine clinical documentation, and site-reported transthoracic echocardiography findings were collected.
RESULTS: Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants (63% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, 37% heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). Median age was 73 years, and 63% were female. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant underwent left ventricular assist device implantation after 2 years, and 1 participant underwent mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair after 3 years; none underwent heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, including 4 requiring new cardiac implantable electronic devices. Among participants with available follow-up echocardiography, site-reported imaging demonstrated mitral regurgitation reduction and improved left ventricular ejection fraction through 5 years. Symptomatic improvement was most apparent during the first year and attenuated thereafter.
CONCLUSIONS: Cerclage ventriculoplasty was associated with mitral regurgitation reduction and improved ventricular function among participants with available long-term follow-up. Symptomatic benefit was greatest during the first year and diminished thereafter, suggesting that favorable remodeling may not fully offset progression of the underlying cardiomyopathy.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03929913.

Title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non-Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.

Title: Motion-Informed Neural Network Towards Diastolic Mechanics in Takotsubo Syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pathophysiology of Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) remains perplexing. We developed a motion-informed neural network (MiNN-Echo) using echocardiograms to elucidate the diastolic mechanics of TTS.
METHODS: We trained and validated MiNN-Echo, a deep convolutional neural network (2D+t) echocardiographic prediction model using multi-vendor echocardiograms from 1142 patients (596 TTS and 546 anterior myocardial infarction) in a multi-institutional cohort. A total of 68 expert echocardiographic readers performed human interpretation. The network's dual-branch architecture independently learns spatial and temporal features, using 2-dimensional image frames for spatial representation and segmentation, and optical flow with sinusoidal phase encoding for temporal dynamics. The MiNN-Echo model integrates static cardiac anatomic changes with motion details from 2-dimensional echocardiographic videos to produce interpretable disease predictions.
RESULTS: The MiNN-Echo model achieved an area under the curve of 0.77, compared with 0.69 among human readers in differentiating TTS from acute myocardial infarction. Myocardial motion features during diastole contributed more (≈71%) to the differential diagnosis than those during systole. Compared with patients with acute myocardial infarction, TTS patients showed increased isovolumic relaxation time (112.5 [interquartile range (IQR), 68.75-165.94] ms versus 87.5 [IQR, 54.17-140] ms, P<0.001; 28% versus 19% of diastolic time, P<0.001), decreased passive ventricular filling (before atrial contraction) time (176.04 [IQR, 114.2-248.12] ms versus 258.62 [IQR, 199.89-331.9] ms, P<0.001; 44% versus 54% of diastolic time, P<0.001), and a different mitral-annulus motion trajectory: lower pixel-wise myocardial displacement in the isovolumic relaxation (0.35 [IQR, 0.26-0.47] versus 0.38 [IQR, 0.28-0.51]; P=0.006), passive (0.45 [IQR, 0.33-0.58] versus 0.50 [IQR, 0.38-0.68]; P<0.001), and active ventricular filling (0.43 [IQR, 0.32-0.56] versus 0.48 [IQR, 0.35-0.63]; P=0.001) phases, and altered rotation angles (away from the horizontal A-V plane) in the passive ventricular filling phase (-70.19 [IQR, -89.62 to -41.33] versus -60.34 [IQR, -87.07 to -30.84]; P=0.020).
CONCLUSIONS: MiNN-Echo in echocardiograms elucidates unique myocardial relaxation kinematics to characterize TTS-associated diastolic mechanics.

Title: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors and renal outcomes in patients with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors (ARNi) significantly improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF). Their effects on kidney function in this population remain incompletely characterized. A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed to explore the impact of ARNi on renal outcomes.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and PubMed databases were searched for randomized trials comparing ARNi with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) alone. Outcomes included the incidence of worsening renal function, hyperkalaemia, hypotension, >50% decrease in eGFR, end-stage renal disease, rise in serum creatinine >2.5 mg/dl, and acute kidney injury. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROB 2.0 tool.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies with 31 574 individuals were included. Mean age was 67 years and 33% were female. ARNi significantly reduced the incidence of worsening renal function events [relative risk (RR): 0.83, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.71-0.96; P = .01], corresponding to 13 fewer events per 1000 patients. ARNi were also associated with a lower risk of >50% decline in eGFR (RR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.47-0.78; P < .001) and acute kidney injury events (RR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.69-0.97; P = .024) compared with RAASi alone. There was no significant difference in the incidence of hyperkalaemia >5.5 mmol/L between groups, while ARNi were associated with a higher incidence of symptomatic hypotension (RR: 1.54, CI 95%: 1.35-1.76; I2 = 69%; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: ARNi are associated with a lower risk of adverse renal outcomes compared with RAASi in patients with heart failure. However, this benefit should be interpreted alongside an increased risk of symptomatic hypotension.

Title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension in adult congenital heart disease: prevalence, outcomes and treatment patterns.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive, life-threatening complication of congenital heart disease (CHD). We aimed to determine the burden of clinically relevant PAH in a well-characterised adult CHD population.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 35 235 adult CHD patients from the Australian National CHD Registry, of whom 392 had clinically significant PAH (mean±sd age 43.4±13.9) (prevalence 1.11%). We prospectively defined clinically significant PAH as 1) prescription of PAH-specific therapy and/or 2) known Eisenmenger syndrome. 330 patients (84.2%) received PAH pharmacotherapy during the study period and 193 patients (49.2%) had Eisenmenger syndrome, 62 (32.1%) of whom were untreated.
RESULTS: During the study period, 141 (36.0%) patients died, PAH treatment was associated with a numerically lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio (HR) 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.11; p=0.22). Patients with moderate complexity CHD had a significantly higher risk of death than the mild group (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.08-2.92; p=0.023), whilst severe complexity patients had >2.5 times the risk of death (p<0.001). At last follow-up, 211 (63.9%) of treated patients were prescribed monotherapy, 90 (27.3%) dual and 29 (8.8%) triple therapy. From initial treatment to last follow-up, 123 (37.3%) of the treated group had switched therapy, 100 (30.3%) died, 75 (22.7%) continued their initial pharmacotherapy, 25 (7.6%) added additional drugs and seven (2.1%) underwent transplantation.
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1.11% of a large adult CHD population had clinically significant PAH. Mortality is high (6.9% at age 30 years, 35.7% at age 50 years) and treatment has shifted towards increased utilisation of combination therapy.

Title: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E status prior to COPD- or cardiovascular-related death: a nationwide study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: COPD is the third leading cause of death worldwide. However, little is known about the characteristics of patients who die from COPD. The aim of this study was to determine the relationship between change or persistence in Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease group E (GOLD-E) status over time and COPD- and cardiovascular (CV)-related death.
METHODS: Patients with COPD were identified by International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes in the French national health insurance database. Patients who died from COPD or CV diseases between 1 January 2017 and 31 December 2022 were matched with living COPD patients. We performed a case-control analysis to compare the impact of the change in GOLD-E status between two periods: 13-24 months (period 2 (2026)) and 0-12 months (period 1 (2025)) prior to death or the index date.
RESULTS: A total of 500 673 COPD patients died during the study period. Of these, 67 250 died from COPD and 41 585 from CV events. Of the patients whose deaths were COPD related, the proportion of patients with GOLD-E 2026 status increased between the two periods (58.3% versus 79.2%), but decreased in their matched living controls (58.3% versus 36.9%). Of the patients with GOLD-E 2026 status during period 2, becoming and remaining GOLD-E 2026 within their final 12 months was associated with COPD-related death (odds ratios 5.40 (95% CI 5.03-5.79) and 4.16 (95% CI 3.87-4.48), respectively; p<0.0001).
INTERPRETATION: These data demonstrate that being GOLD-E for 2 years in a row is associated with a high risk of COPD-related death, of the same magnitude as being GOLD-E for 1 year.

Title: Gut microbiome and aging-related disorders: mechanistic insights and emerging microbiome-targeted therapies for healthy aging.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The human gut harbors a diverse and dense microbial community that maintains metabolic, immune, and intestinal homeostasis through a symbiotic relationship with the host. Aging is a complex biological process that involves alterations in the gut microbiome, including decreased microbial diversity and a decline in beneficial microbiota that produce useful metabolites, which impair intestinal barrier function and enhance chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging).
SCOPE: This review explores current evidence on the interaction between aging and the gut microbiome, emphasizing its impact on age-associated diseases, such as frailty and sarcopenia, cardiovascular issues, type 2 diabetes, obesity, osteoporosis, and neurodegenerative conditions. It further delves into the distinct microbial profiles of centenarians and evaluates microbiome-targeted interventions, such as dietary approaches, probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplants, caloric restriction, intermittent fasting, and pharmaceutical agents, by synthesizing evidence from both human and animal research to emphasize their potential in fostering healthy aging and increased longevity.
KEY FINDINGS: Evidence from human and preclinical studies suggests that alterations in the gut microbiome associated with aging facilitate immune dysregulation, metabolic dysfunction, and the progression of various chronic diseases. Whereas, centenarians possess distinctive microbial signatures rich in beneficial metabolites that could promote healthy aging and prolonged life. Additionally, microbiome-targeted interventions have demonstrated promise in enhancing gut microbial diversity and host wellbeing, though their clinical effectiveness needs additional validation.
CONCLUSION: The gut microbiome is a potential focus for supporting healthy aging and warding off age-related illnesses. Nonetheless, its significant inter-individual variability emphasizes the necessity for personalized microbiome-based approaches, which require validation through extensive longitudinal studies and properly structured randomized controlled trials to demonstrate causality and verify long-term effectiveness.

Title: Predictors of cardiovascular events in multiple myeloma: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Novel therapies have significantly improved survival in patients with multiple myeloma (MM), but cardiovascular (CV) events have become a major challenge, impairing treatment continuity and increasing mortality. This systematic review aimed to identify predictors of CV events in MM to support risk stratification and cardio-oncology management.
METHODS: This review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251084727). Five electronic databases were searched from inception to August 2025. Studies reporting multivariable predictors of CV events in MM were included. Methodological quality was assessed using QUIPS tool.
RESULTS: Eleven studies were included, comprising nine retrospective cohort studies, one prospective observational study, one case-control study. Overall, most studies were judged to be at moderate risk of bias. A total of 20 candidate predictors of CV events were identified. Among these, six were reported in at least two studies, but only hypertension had sufficiently comparable adjusted effect estimates for exploratory meta-analysis. Among treatment-related factors, carfilzomib-based therapy and longer duration of proteasome-inhibitor treatment were associated with a higher risk of CV event in individual studies. Limited evidence from a single prospective study suggests that dynamic natriuretic peptide assessment may have prognostic value, with elevation of natriuretic peptides during the first treatment cycle showing a stronger predictive value (HR 9.5) compared to baseline elevation alone (HR 4.1).
CONCLUSIONS: CV risk in MM appears to be multifactorial, involving both pre-existing vulnerability and treatment-related toxicity. Although several candidate predictors have been identified, the current evidence remains limited by heterogeneity and methodological weaknesses. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required to validate these predictors and to define standardized CV risk assessment and surveillance strategies in MM.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: identifier CRD420251084727.

Title: Predictors of Severe Hospitalization in Patients Admitted With Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in a Community Hospital: A Retrospective Chart Review.
Abstract: Background Hospitalization for acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) is associated with substantial morbidity and healthcare utilization in community hospitals. Because in-hospital mortality may be infrequent in single-center chart reviews, composite morbidity/utilization endpoints may better capture clinically meaningful adverse hospital trajectories. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective chart review at a community hospital using unique-patient index admissions only (earliest admission per medical record number (MRN)), yielding 163 patients. The primary outcome was a composite adverse hospital course defined as any ICU admission, endotracheal intubation, prolonged length of stay (LOS > 5 days; cohort median), 30-day readmission, or in-hospital mortality. Baseline comparisons used Mann-Whitney U tests and chi-square/Fisher's exact tests. Multivariable logistic regression was used for the composite outcome. Thirty-day readmission (post-discharge) occurred in 21 cases; therefore, the primary readmission analysis used a pre-specified parsimonious model (age, congestive heart failure (CHF), creatinine, and discharge against medical advice (AMA)) with Firth penalized logistic regression as a sensitivity analysis to mitigate overfitting. LOS was modeled using negative binomial regression. AUROC and calibration were assessed as internal/apparent performance (no external validation). Results The composite adverse outcome occurred in 105/163 (64.4%) index admissions. ICU admission occurred in 53/163 (32.5%), noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in 58/163 (35.6%), intubation in 9/163 (5.5%), in-hospital mortality in 3/163 (1.8%), and 30-day readmission in 21/163 (12.9%).
