In multivariable analysis of the composite outcome, CHF (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 3.11, 95% CI 1.15-8.43) and hypercapnia (PaCO₂ per 10 mmHg; aOR 1.94, 95% CI 1.25-3.00) were associated with higher odds of adverse course. In the parsimonious standard logistic readmission model, CHF (aOR 4.16, 95% CI 1.54-11.20) and creatinine (per 0.5 mg/dL; aOR 1.23, 95% CI 1.05-1.45) were associated with readmission; estimates were attenuated in the Firth penalized model. In negative binomial LOS modeling, NIV (adjusted incidence rate ratio (aIRR) 1.58, 95% CI 1.03-2.42) and intubation (aIRR 2.97, 95% CI 1.36-6.49) were associated with longer LOS. Apparent discrimination was AUROC 0.7192 for the composite model and AUROC 0.722 for the parsimonious readmission model. Conclusion In this community hospital chart review of 163 unique AECOPD index admissions, an adverse hospital course was common and largely reflected utilization and prolonged recovery rather than mortality. CHF and hypercapnia were associated with adverse composite outcomes, and CHF and renal dysfunction were associated with 30-day readmission in parsimonious modeling. Performance metrics represent internal/apparent estimates without external validation; larger, externally validated studies are needed before clinical deployment of prediction tools.

Title: Robotic Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Assessing Longitudinal Geographic Miss.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inaccurate measurement of lesion length during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) increases the risk of restenosis and poor clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Two interventional cardiologists evaluated angiographic images and made visual estimates of target lesion length and stent length selection. A 2 mm stent overlap of both the proximal and distal lesion edges was considered to be optimal. The target lesion was also assessed for lesion length using the millimetre controls of the CorPath®GRX system (Siemens Healthineers AG, formerly Corindus). Measurements for 10 lesions (randomly selected) were repeated to assess inter-observer variability. The primary endpoint was longitudinal geographic miss (LGM), defined as an absolute difference of 2 mm or more between visual and vascular robotics measurements.
RESULTS: A total of 21 lesions in 19 patients were evaluated. LGM was detected in 16/21 lesions. Visual lesion length measurements were short for 15 (71%), long for one lesion (5%) and appropriate for five (24%). Stent or drug-coated balloon length selections were short for 15 lesions and appropriate for six.
CONCLUSION: The CorPath GRX robotic PCI system increases the accuracy of lesion length evaluation and stent length selection compared with visual estimation.

Title: Cardiovascular effects and mortality of short-acting bronchodilators in asthma and COPD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior research has focused on short-acting β2-agonist (SABA) overuse-related adverse outcomes in asthma patients. Evidence on the association between use of short-acting bronchodilators in general and cardiovascular events in asthma/COPD populations remains limited.
METHODS: Adult patients with chronic treatment of asthma or COPD were identified in a Belgian nationwide cohort between 2017 and 2022. A Cox model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, socioeconomic status, exacerbation history, comorbidities and medication use, was used to investigate the association between SABA, short-acting muscarinic antagonist (SAMA) and SABA+SAMA use with cardiovascular risk and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: The cohort included 226 314 asthma patients (mean age 57.8 years, 60.5% females) and 57 446 COPD patients (mean age 72.2 years, 38.0% females). Compared with no use, SAMA and SABA+SAMA use (1-2 and ≥3 canisters per baseline year) was associated with increased heart failure (1.2-1.4-fold), arrhythmia (1.1-1.4-fold) and mortality risk (1.1-1.7-fold) in asthma and COPD patients. Among asthma patients, use of 1-2, and ≥3 SABA+SAMA canisters per year were additionally associated with increased myocardial infarction (1.2-1.4-fold) and ischaemic stroke risk (1.2-1.3-fold), and ≥3 SABA+SAMA canisters per year with a 1.4-fold myocardial infarction risk in COPD patients. Compared with no SABA users, ≥3 SABA canisters per year was associated with a 1.1-fold increased heart failure and mortality risk in asthma and COPD patients, while no increased risks were observed for 1-2 SABA canisters.
CONCLUSION: Increased use of SAMA or SABA+SAMA was associated with increased risks of cardiovascular events and mortality in patients with asthma and COPD. Collecting three or more SABA canisters per year was associated with increased mortality.

Title: Body composition has limited influence on the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio in older women.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney function is best estimated using both creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). A low ratio between eGFR based on cystatin C and eGFR based on creatinine (eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio <0.7), termed selective glomerular hypofiltration syndromes, is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. While differences in filtration for molecules with different molecular masses may explain this, non-renal factors such as body composition have also been proposed. We aimed to assess whether body composition determines the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio in older women.
METHODS: In 1044 women aged 75 from the Osteoporosis Prospective Risk Assessment (OPRA) cohort, followed to ages 80 (n = 715) and 85 (n = 382), we analyzed associations between the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio and body composition (fat and appendicular lean mass), muscle strength (knee extension, Nm), and sarcopenia [European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) criteria]. Adjusted R² was reported from linear regression model assessing the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio as the dependent variable adjusted for high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), smoking, and steroid treatment.
RESULTS: Associations between body composition measures and the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio were generally low and attenuated with age. No significant association was observed between fat mass and the ratio at any age. Muscle mass was positively associated with the ratio at ages 75 and 80, but not at age 85. Muscle strength was consistently associated with the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio across all ages, although the proportion of explained variance declined with increasing age (adjusted R 2 7.4%, 6.0%, and 2.4% at ages 75, 80, and 85, respectively). Sarcopenia was inversely associated with the ratio at ages 75 and 85, but not at age 80.
CONCLUSION: Body composition, muscle strength, and sarcopenia showed only weak associations with the eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio in older women. These findings suggest that non-body composition factors, including intrinsic renal mechanisms such as selective filtration of larger molecules, may contribute to a low eGFRcys/eGFRcrea ratio.

Title: Fibrocalcific phenotypes in calcific aortic valve disease: imaging characterization, treatment timing, and efficacy assessment.
Abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease involves two structural processes, fibrous matrix remodeling and mineral deposition, that contribute unequally between patients, so leaflets of similar hemodynamic severity need not share the same tissue composition. Histologic and multi-omics studies have mapped this heterogeneity across sex, age, and valve morphology, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography angiography (CTA) has brought compositional assessment into living patients and into longitudinal follow-up. Calcific burden behaves consistently: it tracks stenosis severity, predicts progression, and carries prognostic weight. Findings for noncalcified tissue are less settled and depend on the population studied and on how the measurement is made. Whether total fibrocalcific volume performs well as a structural endpoint and whether CTA-derived noncalcified tissue volume adds predictive value beyond calcification are consequently two separate questions, and the literature often merges them. Pharmacologic trials in patients have almost always measured calcification progression or hemodynamics rather than longitudinal change in the fibrous matrix. Randomized lipid-lowering and mineral-targeted trials in patients have been negative, whereas animal and cell experiments show that established mineral lesions, cell states, and function can sometimes be modified, although these responses do not necessarily move together. This review integrates histology, multimodality imaging, clinical cohorts, pharmacologic trials, and preclinical intervention studies to define the fibrocalcific phenotype, distinguish prevention from slowing and reversal, and align therapeutic timing with endpoints at the levels of activity, tissue burden, valve function, myocardial response, and clinical events. Longitudinal measurement of leaflet composition and validation of treatment-induced change against functional outcomes remain the central gaps.

Title: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography for quantifying mitral annular calcification in mitral valve surgery and association with outcomes.
Journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
Abstract:
AIMS: Evaluation of mitral annular calcification (MAC) on non-contrast computed tomography (CT) has been associated with clinical outcomes. There is no accepted methodology for evaluating MAC using contrast CT. This study aimed to validate MAC quantification using contrast CT and evaluate its clinical impact in patients undergoing mitral valve (MV) surgery.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Between 2011 and 2020, 303 patients with native MV dysfunction who underwent contrast CT prior to surgery were included. In a validation cohort of 50 patients undergoing both contrast and non-contrast CT, Agatston scores were correlated to derive contrast-specific thresholds. Baseline clinical parameters and a multi-parametric MAC score (range: 2-12) were recorded for the entire cohort. The contrast-enhanced CT MAC score consisted of Agatston score (1 point: <650 AU; 2 points: 650-1700AU; 3 points: 1700-2800 AU; 4 points: >2800 AU), MAC circumferential angle (1 point: <90°; 2 points: 90-<180°; 3 points: 180-<270°; 4 points: 270-360°), trigone involvement (1 point: single trigone; 2 points: both trigones), myocardial infiltration (1 point), and left ventricular outflow tract involvement (1 point). Associations between MAC score and clinical outcomes were evaluated. Higher MAC scores predicted increased total operating time (P < 0.001), cross-clamp time (P < 0.001), intensive care unit stay (P < 0.001), open surgical approach (P < 0.001), in-hospital complications (P < 0.001), and pacemaker implantation (P = 0.055). Contrast-enhanced CT MAC score independently predicted all-cause mortality (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: A multiparametric MAC score on contrast CT enables assessment of MAC severity, and is associated with operative approach and postoperative outcomes in patients with MV dysfunction undergoing surgery.

Title: Balancing innovation and safety in percutaneous treatment of coronary artery calcification.
Abstract: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Under-preparation of calcified plaque predisposes to stent under-expansion, mal-apposition, restenosis, and stent thrombosis, while over-aggressive debulking strategies carry risk of dissection, perforation, and no-reflow. The interventional armamentarium for calcium modification has expanded from high-pressure and non-high pressure specialty balloons including intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) to dedicated atherectomy devices i.e., rotational atherectomy (RA), orbital atherectomy (OA), and excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA), each with a distinct mechanism, evidence base, and risk profile. Additionally, comprehensive assessment of coronary calcium is central to guiding lesion preparation and selecting treatment strategy, with IVUS and OCT providing detailed intravascular characterisation, and CT emerging as a complementary non-invasive tool for procedural planning. Appropriate procedural planning and judicious selection of calcium-modification tools are paramount to maximising procedural safety, minimising complications, and improving clinical outcomes. This review summarizes the pathophysiology of CAC, describes each modification technique, synthesizes the pivotal and recent randomised evidence, outlines current guideline position, and proposes a practical framework for balancing procedural innovation against patient safety. Current evidence supports an individualized, imaging-guided approach to calcium modification. Balloon-based strategies, IVL, atherectomy, and ELCA each have specific strengths and limitations, and no modality has demonstrated universal superiority across lesion subsets. Atherectomy and laser remain important for selected uncrossable, undilatable, or highly resistant lesions, whereas IVL and specialty balloons may provide effective alternatives in appropriately selected crossable lesions. Evidence for many technologies is stronger for procedural and imaging endpoints than for long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Association Between Wound Exudate Severity and Time to Healing Among Patients with Venous Leg Ulcers (VLUs): A Real-World Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the relationship between wound exudate severity and time to healing among venous leg ulcers (VLUs).
DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using Net Health WoundExpert electronic health record data from United States outpatient wound care centers 2002-2020. The status of VLUs was followed from the initial wound clinic visit until healing or censoring.
METHODS: Exudate severity (none, mild, moderate, or heavy) was modeled as a time-varying exposure, and the outcome was time to complete healing. Weighted Royston-Parmar flexible parametric survival models were used to fit marginal structural models. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment and censoring weights were applied to address time varying confounding and informative censoring. The weight models included demographic characteristics, clinical factors, and wound specific variables. Effect measures included average hazard ratios, healing probabilities, and restricted mean survival time (RMST).
RESULTS: The cohort included 8,184 patients (mean age 67.8 years; 48.1% male) contributing 18,435 VLUs. Increasing exudate severity was associated with progressively lower rates of healing, with adjusted hazard ratio for mild (HR 0.24; 95% CI 0.20-0.29), moderate (HR 0.20; 95% CI 0.16-0.25), and heavy exudate (HR 0.15; 95% CI 0.10-0.22), compared with ulcers without exudate. Interval-specific average hazard ratios showed similar patterns. At 12 weeks, higher exudate levels were associated with substantially lower healing probabilities (46.1%, 29.4%, and 18.4% for mild, moderate, and heavy exudate vs 92.7% with no exudate) and longer time unhealed (62.8, 70.4, and 75.3 days vs 31.4 days).
CONCLUSION: Higher wound exudate severity was associated with markedly delayed healing among VLUs in routine outpatient care. Because "no exudate" is not a typical clinical state for an active VLU, these estimates are best interpreted as relative prognostic contrasts along the exudate gradient rather than as expected trajectories for a hypothetical exudate-free VLU. Routine exudate assessment may provide useful prognostic information regarding healing trajectories among patients with VLUs.

Title: Mortality prediction in patients with acute myocardial infarction and prior ischemic stroke: a prospective cohort study with explainable machine learning and SHAP analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and a prior history of ischemic stroke (IS) represent a high-risk population with limited prognostic tools. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting all-cause mortality in AMI patients with prior IS.
METHODS: This prospective single-center cohort included 543 consecutive patients with AMI and prior IS who underwent Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI). Candidate predictors were screened using univariable Cox regression, Boruta, and LASSO Cox regression. Six survival models were compared: Cox, elastic-net Cox, random survival forest (RSF), GBM survival, XGBoost survival, and Survival SVM. Internal validation used 100 bootstrap resamples with out-of-bag (OOB) evaluation. Performance was evaluated using Harrell's C-index, IPCW time-dependent AUC, calibration measures, Brier score, and decision-curve analysis. SHAP-based and permutation analyses were used for model interpretation.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 3.03 years, 66 patients (12.2%) died. Six predictors were selected: age, hemoglobin, prognostic nutritional index, estimated glomerular filtration rate, atherogenic index of plasma, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio. Although RSF achieved the numerically highest OOB C-index, elastic-net Cox showed comparable discrimination, better calibration, a lower 3-year Brier score, and greater interpretability and was selected as the final model. Its OOB C-index was 0.714 (95% CI 0.616-0.790), and its 1-, 2-, and 3-year IPCW AUCs were 0.745, 0.704, and 0.701, respectively. Age and hemoglobin made the largest contributions to model predictions. Elastic-net Cox showed numerically better performance than GRACE, but statistical superiority in discrimination was not demonstrated.
CONCLUSIONS: The six-variable elastic-net Cox model provided moderate discrimination and relatively favorable calibration. Independent external validation and prospective implementation studies are required before clinical use.

Title: Clinical outcome implications of novel auscultation device of artificial intelligence (NAVI-HF) in predischarge acute heart failure patients.
Abstract:
AIM: This study evaluated the prognostic significance of a novel auscultation device of artificial intelligence (NAVI-HF) in predicting clinical outcomes in predischarge acute heart failure (HF) patients.
METHODS: This second, prognostic phase of a prospective observational cohort study extends our prior diagnostics phase, in which NAVI-HF demonstrated good performance compared with lung ultrasound (LUS) B-lines as the reference standard. Patients were classified as NAVI-HF positive or negative prior to discharge and followed for 6 months for evaluation.
RESULTS: A total of 239 patients were included of whom 111 (45.1%) were NAVI-HF positive. NAVI-HF positive patients had a worse clinical profile and higher NT-proBNP (p < 0.05). During a median follow-up of 6 months, 82 composite events (34.3%) occurred. In univariate Cox analysis, NAVI-HF positive was associated with significant increased risk of composite outcome (HR 1.59, CI 1.03-2.47; p 0.03) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.64, CI 1.05-2.46; p 0.02), but not all-cause mortality (p 0.24). The association in composite and HF hospitalization outcomes remained significant after adjustment for age and sex but was attenuated after adjustment for other prognostic variables.
CONCLUSION: NAVI-HF-detected congestion was associated with increased adverse clinical outcomes in predischarge acute HF patients.

Title: Peripheral microvascular function and in-stent late lumen loss after percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective cohort study with an exploratory analysis by implanted stent diameter.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peripheral microvascular endothelial function measured by the reactive hyperemia index (RHI) with EndoPAT predicts cardiovascular outcomes, and post-procedural RHI has been associated with binary in-stent restenosis. Whether pre-procedural RHI relates to in-stent late lumen loss (LLL) measured by quantitative coronary angiography (QCA) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and whether any association depends on device caliber, has not been established.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 132 patients who underwent EndoPAT before PCI (index PCI 2009-2016). The primary endpoint was in-stent LLL at follow-up angiography (n = 91; median follow-up 9.4 months). Because in-stent LLL was highly skewed, the primary analysis used Spearman correlation and a robust (HC3) multivariable regression adjusting for age, diabetes, hypertension, number of diseased vessels, and pre-PCI minimal lumen diameter. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation (MICE, m = 20) for missing follow-up and lesion-level generalized estimating equations (GEE). Subgroup analyses by implanted stent diameter (≤2.75 versus >2.75 mm) and diabetes were exploratory.
RESULTS: RHI showed only a borderline inverse correlation with in-stent LLL (ρ = -0.19, p = 0.07) and was not independently associated with it (adjusted β = -0.11, 95% CI -0.39 to +0.18, p = 0.45); multiple imputation (β = -0.08) and GEE (β = -0.07) were concordant, and no correlation survived false-discovery-rate correction. Stratification by native reference vessel diameter showed no association, whereas stratification by implanted stent diameter revealed an inverse RHI-LLL correlation confined to small-diameter stents (≤2.75 mm, n = 33; ρ = -0.375, p = 0.032) but not larger stents (ρ = -0.055). However, the stent-diameter × RHI interaction was not significant (p = 0.48), so this caliber-dependent signal is hypothesis-generating and tracks the achieved implanted caliber rather than the native reference vessel. Inflammation explained neither result. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was unrelated to RHI (ρ = -0.02) and to in-stent LLL (ρ = +0.15), and adding it to the primary model left the RHI estimate unchanged. Small-caliber recipients had similar hs-CRP but more diabetes (57.6% versus 27.6%, p = 0.009) and worse renal function (p = 0.008), indicating a higher-risk phenotype rather than a pure caliber stratum.
DISCUSSION: Pre-procedural EndoPAT RHI was not independently associated with in-stent LLL. The exploratory signal confined to small-caliber stents is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective, device-caliber-stratified validation pairing pre- with post-procedural RHI.

Title: Lipid control in a cohort of patients with cardiorenal disease (LIPID-REN): a subanalysis of the CARDIOREN registry.
Abstract:
AIMS: Advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) confers a very high cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, requiring comprehensive risk factor assessment. However, real-world data on current practices in patients with cardiorenal disease remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the control of cardiovascular risk factors, with a focus on lipid management, in a contemporary cardiorenal cohort.
METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis was conducted within the CARDIOREN Registry, which enrolled patients with chronic heart failure from 13 tertiary hospitals in Spain (2021-2022). Of 1107 patients, 885 with complete data on low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), albuminuria, and atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) were eligible. The present analysis was restricted to the patients who met the definition of advanced CKD, defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 ml/min/1.73 m² or eGFR 30-45 ml/min/1.73 m² with albuminuria >30 mg/g. ASCVD was defined as prior ischemic heart disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial disease. The proportion of patients with LDL-C <55 mg/dl was assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models, including a parsimonious primary model and sensitivity analyses, were used to identify factors associated with lower LDL-C levels.
RESULTS: Advanced CKD was present in 221 patients (25%); median age was 79 years, 58.8% were male, and 52.9% had ASCVD. Median LDL-C was 73 mg/dl, and only 22.6% achieved an LDL-C <55 mg/dl. Achievement of LDL-C <55 mg/dl was significantly lower in patients without ASCVD compared with those with ASCVD (13.4% vs. 30.7%; P = .002). In multivariable analysis, ASCVD was independently associated with a higher likelihood of achieving LDL-C <55 mg/dl, whereas female sex was independently associated with a lower likelihood of achieving this level.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with advanced CKD, lipid control was below cardiology guideline recommendations for patients at very high CVD risk, particularly among those without ASCVD and in women.

Title: Design and Rationale of the Niigata Cardiovascular Disease Registry Using Linked Administrative and Clinical Data (NiCARDIA).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: As populations age, cardiovascular disease (CVD) increasingly affects functional independence, an issue of growing importance among older adults. However, long-term trajectories of functional decline in patients receiving contemporary CVD care remain poorly characterized, so the Niigata Cardiovascular Disease Registry using Health Insurance Claims (NiCARDIA) was established to address this gap by integrating hospital-based clinical data with administrative datasets through a prefecture-wide data-sharing platform.
METHODS AND RESULTS: NiCARDIA is a multicenter, prospective observational cohort enrolling 8,500 adults hospitalized with CVD at 16 hospitals across Niigata Prefecture, Japan. Baseline data include demographics, biomarkers, echocardiographic findings, and other clinical variables. Eligible participants are insured under Japan's public health insurance schemes, enabling deterministic linkage to longitudinal medical, long-term care, and health check-up data. Administrative datasets will be updated every 6-12 months through to 2045. The primary outcome is longitudinal change in functional independence assessed by certified long-term care-need levels. Secondary outcomes include death, hospitalizations, treatment patterns, and prediction of functional decline.
CONCLUSIONS: By linking detailed clinical data with population-level administrative datasets, NiCARDIA will enable comprehensive evaluation of long-term functional trajectories and their clinical and social determinants in contemporary CVD patients.

Title: Registry-defined incident chronic kidney disease following acute kidney injury after primary PCI for STEMI and its association with long-term outcomes: a multicenter landmark analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) frequently occurs in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Kidney recovery after AKI is heterogeneous, and the prognostic significance of kidney dysfunction persisting to the 3-6-month assessment remains incompletely defined. We evaluated whether registry-defined incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) following AKI was associated with subsequent death and myocardial infarction (MI).
METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected multicenter PCI registry included STEMI patients treated with primary PCI between January 2010 and November 2020. AKI was defined according to KDIGO criteria. Kidney trajectory was classified as no AKI, transient AKI with recovery, or registry-defined incident CKD following AKI based on kidney function assessed at 3-6 months. To minimize guarantee-time bias, Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses began at a 6-month landmark. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, LVEF, and baseline MDRD eGFR.
RESULTS: Among 1,239 patients, 941 had no AKI, 56 had transient AKI, and 242 had incident CKD following AKI; the overall AKI incidence was 24.1%. The strict 6-month landmark cohort comprised 1,129 patients (869 no AKI, 48 transient AKI, and 212 incident CKD). Compared with no AKI, incident CKD was associated with all-cause death (multivariable Cox HR 4.06, 95% CI 1.23-13.45; P = 0.022), MI (multivariable Cox HR 4.49, 95% CI 1.79-11.30; P = 0.001), and death and/or MI (multivariable Cox HR 4.35, 95% CI 2.07-9.14; P < 0.001), whereas transient AKI was not significantly associated with these outcomes. In the two-group analysis, incident CKD was similarly associated with death (multivariable Cox HR 3.44, 95% CI 1.18-10.06; P = 0.024), MI (multivariable Cox HR 3.75, 95% CI 1.59-8.87; P = 0.003), and death and/or MI (multivariable Cox HR 3.61, 95% CI 1.83-7.14; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Registry-defined incident CKD after in-hospital AKI identified a subgroup of STEMI survivors with substantially higher post-landmark risks of death and MI. Kidney recovery trajectory may provide clinically useful prognostic information beyond the occurrence of AKI alone.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04650529. Registered on 25 January 2021. Retrospectively registered.

Title: Early Direct Oral Anticoagulant Initiation After Intracranial Hemorrhage Among Japanese Patients With Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation: SAFE-ICH Registry 12-Month Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the effects of early direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) (re)initiation after intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in atrial fibrillation is crucial. Previous 30-day outcomes in the SAFE-ICH Registry showed acceptable ischemic/hemorrhagic risks; therefore, we evaluated the 12-month outcomes.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The SAFE-ICH Registry, a prospective, observational cohort study conducted at 32 hospitals in Japan, included 240 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) who experienced ICH and in whom DOAC therapy was (re)initiated ≤14 days after ICH. Short-term (≤30 days) and long-term (≤12 months) ischemic/hemorrhagic outcomes were investigated. Data were collected through clinical assessments, imaging or telephone interviews over 12 months. The 12-month composite outcome incidence (symptomatic ICH, any stroke, all-cause death) was 22.5% (29.1/100 person-years). The secondary outcome incidence was 6.3% (7.9/100 person-years) for symptomatic ICH, 6.7% (8.4/100 person-years) for any stroke (ischemic: 2.9% [3.6/100 person-years]; hemorrhagic: 3.8% [4.6/100 person-years]), and 14.2% (17.3/100 person-years) for all-cause death. The major bleeding incidence was 6.7% (8.4/100 person-years). Hemorrhagic stroke first appeared approximately 3 months after DOAC (re)initiation, and by month 10, its rate was comparable to that of ischemic stroke. Most deaths were due to aspiration pneumonia.
CONCLUSIONS: Early DOAC (re)initiation after ICH in NVAF was associated with a numerically higher long-term hemorrhagic than ischemic stroke risk. These risks warrant careful consideration when determining the optimal DOAC duration and timing after ICH.

Title: Vasospastic Angina and Cardiac Arrest.
Abstract: Vasospastic angina (VSA) is an important and potentially treatable cause of cardiac arrest (CA) and may account for approximately 2-10% of otherwise unexplained cases of out-of-hospital CA. VSA can sometimes be diagnosed by spontaneous coronary spasm during emergency coronary angiography or by transient ST-segment elevation during a spontaneous attack after resuscitation. However, because coronary spasm is transient and may not be evident during the initial evaluation, provocation testing after clinical stabilization may be required to establish the diagnosis in otherwise unexplained cases. Once VSA is diagnosed, vasodilator therapy, particularly calcium-channel blockers, is the mainstay of treatment. Nevertheless, survivors of VSA-related CA may remain at risk of recurrent lethal ventricular arrhythmias despite medical therapy. Evaluation for alternative or overlapping arrhythmogenic disorders, including cardiomyopathies and channelopathies, should therefore be considered even after a diagnosis of VSA, and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation may be considered in selected patients according to the risk of recurrence and response to medical therapy. Further prospective studies, including randomized controlled trials, are needed to determine whether systematic provocation testing followed by targeted therapy reduces recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and CA and improves long-term outcomes.

Title: Association of Mean Left Atrial Pressure With Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: Subanalysis of the Shinshu Catheter Ablation (Shinshu-AB) Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association of invasively measured mean left atrial pressure (LAP) during catheter ablation (CA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) with clinical characteristics and outcomes remains unclear.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed the data of 480 patients from the Shinshu Catheter Ablation Registry who underwent CA for AF (median age, 69 years; 146 women [30.4%]; 207 patients [43.1%] with persistent AF). Patients were categorized by mean LAP as normal (<12 mmHg; n=318 [66.3%]), mildly elevated (12 to <15 mmHg; n=78 [16.3%]), or elevated (≥15 mmHg; n=84 [17.5%]). Study endpoints were early AF recurrence within the 8-week blanking period, late AF recurrence, and composite adverse clinical events (heart failure hospitalization, symptomatic stroke, or all-cause death) during the 1-year follow-up after CA. Patients in the higher LAP groups had a higher prevalence of obesity and persistent AF, and a larger left atrial volume index. Early AF recurrence differed significantly across the LAP groups and was highest in the elevated LAP group (log-rank P=0.017). After multivariable adjustment, early AF recurrence risk increased across the LAP groups (hazard ratio per-category increase, 1.41; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-1.90; P for trend=0.028). In contrast, late AF recurrence and composite adverse clinical events did not differ significantly across the LAP groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Mean LAP during CA for AF was associated with AF-related clinical characteristics and early AF recurrence.

Title: Optical coherence tomography-defined radial artery calcification: frequency, phenotypes, and correlates in a retrospective transradial PCI cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The frequency, distribution, and optical coherence tomography (OCT) features of radial artery calcification (RAC) remain poorly defined. We assessed OCT-defined RAC and factors associated with patient-level RAC.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 461 patients with analyzable radial artery OCT (RA-OCT) between January 2021 and August 2025. RAC was assessed at the patient, segment, and lesion levels. Clinical characteristics, radial artery plaque features, coronary OCT findings, and factors associated with patient-level RAC were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 461 patients in the final analytic cohort, OCT-defined RAC was identified in 61 (13.2%). RAC involved the proximal, middle, and distal segments in 17/461 (3.7%), 25/461 (5.4%), and 52/461 (11.3%) patients, respectively. Among 214 calcified lesions, spotty calcification was the most common morphology (151/214, 70.6%). In exploratory patient-level analyses, all five radial artery plaque features were associated with RAC after multivariable adjustment, and all associations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. In multivariable analysis, older age, diabetes mellitus, and coronary calcific nodule remained associated with RAC, whereas coronary calcium score was not statistically associated with RAC after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, OCT-defined RAC was identified in 13.2% of patients, was more frequent in the distal segment, and showed heterogeneous lesion-level phenotypes. Older age, diabetes mellitus, and coronary calcific nodule were associated with RAC. Exploratory analyses also showed associations between RAC and multiple noncalcified radial artery plaque features.

Title: Prevalence and Prognostic Impact of Sarcopenic Dysphagia in Older Patients With Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysphagia is common in older patients with heart failure (HF), but evidence regarding sarcopenic dysphagia remains limited. The purpose of this retrospective study was to clarify the prevalence of sarcopenic dysphagia and its relationship with swallowing-related measures and prognosis in older patients with HF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The study group included patients aged ≥65 years admitted with HF between June 2021 and December 2023. Patients were classified into 3 groups using the diagnostic algorithm for sarcopenic dysphagia at discharge: robust (without sarcopenia), sarcopenia (with sarcopenia only), and sarcopenic dysphagia (with sarcopenia and dysphagia). Outcomes were swallowing-related measures (maximal tongue pressure, geniohyoid muscle area, and geniohyoid muscle echogenicity) and a 1-year composite outcome (all-cause death or HF-related readmission). Of 524 screened patients, 363 were analyzed (median age 83 years [Q1-Q3: 78-90 years], 46.6% women); 61 patients were robust (16.8%), 215 had sarcopenia (59.2%), and 87 had sarcopenic dysphagia (24.0%). In the analysis of covariance, swallowing-related measures were poorer in the sarcopenic dysphagia group compared with the robust group (P<0.05). In the Cox regression analysis compared with robust, sarcopenia was not statistically significantly associated with prognosis, but sarcopenic dysphagia was associated with a higher risk (hazard ratio 2.53, 95% confidence interval 1.30-4.90, P=0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenic dysphagia affected 24.0% of patients with HF, and was associated with poorer swallowing-related measures and prognosis.

Title: Clinical Profiles and Guideline-Directed Therapy Patterns in Heart Failure With Preserved Versus Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study From Pakistan.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Heart failure (HF) poses a growing global burden with regional and phenotypic variations. This study compared clinical characteristics, biomarker profiles, and guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use between HF subtypes in a Pakistani tertiary-care population.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 575 adults admitted with HF at a tertiary hospital in Karachi, Pakistan (2020-2023). Patients were classified as HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF; ≥50%), mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF; 41-49%) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF; ≤40%). Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were extracted from electronic records. GDMT score (0-4) reflected use of β-blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker/angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality and 30-day HF readmission.
RESULTS: Mean age was 67.67±13.12 years; 46% were male. 18 (3.1%) had HFmrEF; these patients were described descriptively because of limited sample size. HFpEF patients were mostly female (78.9% vs. 39.7%, p<0.001). HFrEF had more ischemic heart disease (58.6% vs. 37.7%, p<0.001). Pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels were higher in HFrEF than HFpEF (9,142 [3,938-20,308] vs. 4,102 [1,410-9,758] pg/mL; p<0.001). GDMT scores were greater in HFrEF (1.72±1.22 vs. 1.12±0.92, p<0.001). Mortality (6.3%) and 30-day readmission (31.0%) did not differ by phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: HFpEF and HFrEF show distinct clinical and biomarker patterns, but GDMT uptake remains suboptimal. Despite similar short-term outcomes, strengthening evidence-based therapy is essential to improve HF care in resource-limited settings.

Title: Low Diastolic Blood Pressure and Cardiometabolic Burden Predict Heart Failure in Treated Hypertensive Patients: Insights From the Korean Hypertension Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Hypertension is associated with an elevated risk of heart failure (HF). Although blood pressure (BP) lowering reduces HF risk, the relative contributions of individual BP components and coexisting cardiometabolic factors to HF in treated hypertensive patients remain unclear.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the Korean Hypertension Cohort (n=9,422) linked with the National Health Insurance Service-National Health Information Database. Hypertensive patients were compared with age- and sex-matched non-hypertensive controls. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify determinants of HF, focusing on systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), pulse pressure (PP), metabolic syndrome, and albuminuria.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 10 years, HF occurred more frequently in hypertensive than in non-hypertensive individuals (6.1% vs. 4.5%). In hypertensive patients, compared with DBP <70 mmHg, higher DBP categories (70-79, 80-89, and ≥90 mmHg) were associated with progressively lower risk (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.69, 0.60, and 0.51, respectively; all p<0.01). In contrast, SBP and PP were not independently associated with HF after adjustment. Metabolic syndrome was associated with a 35% higher risk of HF (adjusted HR, 1.35; 95% confidence interval, 1.12-1.63; p<0.01), and albuminuria conferred incrementally greater risk across severity categories (HR, 1.24 for ±, p=0.03; HR, 1.26 for +/++/+++; p<0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Hypertensive patients had a markedly higher long-term incidence of HF. Beyond BP levels, metabolic syndrome and albuminuria were independent determinants of HF development, highlighting the importance of comprehensive cardiometabolic and renal risk assessment in hypertensive patients.

Title: Cancer Therapeutics-Related Cardiac Toxicity and Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Unresolved Challenges.
Abstract: As cancer survival continues to improve, cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity, including cancer therapeutics-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) and heart failure (HF), has emerged as a major clinical challenge. Growing evidence supports a bidirectional relationship between cancer and HF, driven by shared risk factors, overlapping pathophysiological mechanisms, and the cardiotoxic effects of anticancer therapies. Advances in imaging modalities and cardiac biomarkers have enabled earlier detection of subclinical myocardial injury. Preventive strategies including modification of cancer therapy and pharmacologic cardioprotection have been extensively investigated. However, randomized trials evaluating neurohormonal antagonists, statins, and other agents have yielded heterogeneous results, and most evidence derives from selected populations. Management of asymptomatic and symptomatic HF in patients with cancer generally follows current HF guidelines, yet major HF trials have largely excluded patients with active or recent malignancy. Consequently, uncertainties remain regarding optimal prevention and treatment strategies in cancer patients. This review focuses on CTRCD and the HF associated with it, and summarizes current evidence on risk assessment, early detection, prevention, and management, while highlighting unresolved challenges and future directions.

Title: Warfarin anticoagulation control and risks of cerebral small vessel disease and cognitive impairment among elderly patients with ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study applied individual exposure metrics derived from population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PopPK/PD) modelling to investigate the associations between warfarin anticoagulation quality, cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) burden, and cognitive outcomes among older adults with ischemic stroke and non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF).
METHODS: We included 300 patients aged ≥65 years with ischemic stroke and AF who had received warfarin for ≥3 months between January and December 2025. A nonlinear mixed-effects model was used to estimate individualized pharmacokinetic parameters and steady-state exposure metrics. Multivariable regression was performed to assess the associations of these metrics with CSVD burden, cognitive impairment, and the composite endpoint; the ability to identify high CSVD burden was compared between model-derived exposure metrics and conventional anticoagulation quality metrics, including time in therapeutic range (TTR) and international normalized ratio (INR) variability.
RESULTS: Steady-state average concentration (Cavgss) was significantly positively associated with CSVD burden (per 100 ng/mL increment: OR = 1.32, p < 0.001), whereas TTR was not associated with burden (p = 0.444). High CSVD burden was significantly associated with cognitive impairment (Cox HR = 2.04, p = 0.007). The incidence of cognitive impairment increased stepwise across exposure tertiles (42.2%, 54.0%, and 75.4%, p < 0.001). The composite endpoint occurred significantly more often in patients with INR standard deviation (INR_SD) > 0.5 (p = 0.009). For identifying high CSVD burden, PopPK/PD-derived exposure parameters demonstrated differing within-cohort discrimination for identifying high CSVD burden: steady-state peak concentration (Cmaxss), Cavgss, and degree of fluctuation (DF) (AUC = 0.695, 0.679, and 0.651, respectively), with better discrimination compared with INR_SD and TTR (AUC = 0.557 and 0.493, respectively; p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Within this cohort, PopPK/PD-derived individualized exposure parameters showed better discrimination for identifying patients with high CSVD burden compared with traditional TTR and INR variability, although discriminative ability remained modest for all markers, including those whose anticoagulation quality appeared adequate by conventional metrics. These findings provide a pharmacological foundation for refined anticoagulation quality assessment in this high-risk elderly population.

Title: Association between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio and short-term prognosis in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical evidence regarding the prognostic value of the platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) for short-term outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains limited, particularly its independent predictive role for in-hospital and ICU all-cause mortality, which lacks validation in large-scale, multi-center settings. This study investigated the association between PWR and in-hospital and ICU mortality in AMI patients, aiming to evaluate its impact on short-term prognosis in this population.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2,381 AMI patients from the MIMIC-IV database as the derivation cohort, with validation performed in 7,054 AMI patients from the multi-center eICU-CRD database and 252 AMI patients from a single-center internal cohort. Restricted cubic spline and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess nonlinearity and survival differences. Multivariable logistic regression examined the independent association between PWR and in-hospital and ICU mortality. Decision curve analysis assessed the clinical utility of PWR. Subgroup analyses, Cox regression, Fine-Gray competing-risk models, and mediation analyses were conducted for robustness assessment and mechanistic exploration.
RESULTS: In the derivation cohort of this study, 316 patients (13.3%) died during hospitalization and 237 (10.0%) died during ICU stay. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a consistent linear relationship between PWR and the risks of in-hospital and ICU mortality. Multivariable logistic regression revealed a significant inverse association between PWR and in-hospital mortality (OR = 0.976, 95% CI: 0.960-0.991, P = 0.003) as well as ICU mortality (OR = 0.977, 95% CI: 0.959-0.994, P = 0.012). The robustness of this inverse association was further supported by Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. The results were consistently reproduced in both the external eICU-CRD validation cohort and the single-center internal validation cohort. Additionally, Kaplan-Meier curves showed that patients in the higher PWR group had significantly better cumulative survival than those in the lower PWR group. Decision curve analysis further showed that PWR provided some net benefit at clinically relevant thresholds for both outcomes, supporting its clinical utility. In subgroup analyses, the inverse association between PWR and short-term mortality remained directionally consistent across all subgroups, with no significant interactions after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Mediation analysis indicated that SAPS II score and vasopressor use mediated 25.9% and 18.6% of the protective effect of PWR, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: PWR is a simple, low-cost composite marker derived from routine complete blood counts. It is significantly and inversely associated with short-term in-hospital and ICU mortality in AMI patients. Our findings suggest that PWR may serve as a convenient and inexpensive adjunctive tool for early risk stratification and identification of high-risk individuals. However, its clinical application warrants further validation in larger, multi-center prospective studies.

Title: Longer collapse-to-first-medical-contact interval is independently associated with ROSC in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a paradoxical finding that may reflect case-mix differences.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shortening prehospital time intervals is a cornerstone of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) management, with earlier medical contact generally assumed to improve survival. However, this assumption has rarely been scrutinized at the level of individual time metrics, particularly the interval from witnessed collapse to first medical contact (collapse-to-FMC), whose relationship with resuscitation outcomes independent of case-mix remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between core prehospital time intervals and the achievement of prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 152 consecutive OHCA patients managed by the Cixi Emergency Center between April 2023 and March 2026. Time intervals were derived from synchronized dispatch center logs and onboard system timestamps, including dispatch-to-scene arrival, collapse-to-first medical contact, and collapse-to-CPR initiation intervals. Candidate variables for multivariable modeling were selected based on a prespecified causal rationale and clinical relevance, rather than solely on univariate statistical significance. Univariate logistic regression was performed for descriptive purposes to examine crude associations with prehospital ROSC. The main model included the two core time intervals (collapse-to-FMC and collapse-to-CPR initiation). Model 1 further adjusted for age, a clinically important confounder that did not reach statistical significance in univariate analysis. Model 2 additionally adjusted for etiology of arrest and presence of a shockable rhythm, which were selected a priori as pre-exposure confounders based on established prognostic importance in OHCA research. This approach ensured that clinically important confounders were retained regardless of their univariate P values. A main model included only time variables, and an adjusted model further incorporated clinical covariates. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors, and model calibration was evaluated with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. Discriminative ability was assessed by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed by age (<65 vs. ≥65 years) and etiology (cardiac vs. non-cardiac).
RESULTS: Among 152 patients, 52 (34.2%) achieved prehospital ROSC. Conventional dispatch-related intervals did not differ between groups. The collapse-to-first medical contact interval was significantly longer in the ROSC group (20.0 vs. 13.1 min, P < 0.001) and remained independently associated with ROSC after adjustment for prespecified pre-exposure confounders, including age, etiology of arrest, and presence of a shockable rhythm (OR 1.188, 95% CI: 1.079-1.307, P < 0.001). Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.882 (95% CI: 0.827-0.936), with a calibration intercept of -0.063, a calibration slope of 0.972, and a Brier score of 0.132, indicating adequate calibration. In subgroup analyses, this association was predominantly observed in patients younger than 65 years (adjusted P = 0.037), and the interval from collapse to CPR initiation became significant in the cardiac etiology subgroup after adjustment (OR 1.567, 95% CI: 1.054-2.329, P = 0.026).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of OHCA patients, a longer collapse-to-first medical contact interval was paradoxically associated with increased odds of prehospital ROSC, independent of prespecified pre-exposure confounders. This counterintuitive finding suggests that the interval may reflect patient salvageability and unmeasured case-mix characteristics rather than treatment delay alone. These results challenge the conventional premise that shorter time to medical contact uniformly translates to better outcomes, and underscore the need for a more nuanced understanding of how patient characteristics shape the relationship between prehospital timing and resuscitation success.

Title: Natriuretic Peptides for Predicting Treatment Response in Heart Failure: Insights From Recent Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) has emerged as a cornerstone biomarker in heart failure (HF), serving as a diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacodynamic tool in randomized controlled trials. Recent HF trials have generated substantial evidence regarding 2 interrelated roles: (1) the relationship between baseline NT-proBNP levels and differential treatment efficacy across drug classes, and (2) the proportional relationship between NT-proBNP reduction and clinical outcome improvement. We synthesize data from pivotal trials of sacubitril/valsartan (angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, ARNI), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs), vericiguat, and omecamtiv mecarbil. Across trials in both HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction, some drug classes including ARNI, SGLT2 inhibitors, MRA, and device therapies demonstrated consistent relative treatment benefits regardless of baseline NT-proBNP levels. Notable exceptions were vericiguat, a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, where patients with higher baseline NT-proBNP derived no benefit; omecamtiv mecarbil, which showed selective benefit in patients with higher NT-proBNP levels; and spironolactone in HFpEF, where benefit was concentrated in patients with the lowest baseline NT-proBNP. With respect to NT-proBNP dynamics, a geometric mean ratio of on-treatment to baseline NT-proBNP consistently parallels the hazard ratio for clinical outcomes across ARNI trials, supporting NT-proBNP change as a robust surrogate endpoint. SGLT2 inhibitors consistently show clinical benefit exceeding the extent of NT-proBNP reduction, reflecting pleiotropic mechanisms. These insights position NT-proBNP not merely as a prognostic marker, but as an outcome-predictive biomarker that may inform patient selection and response monitoring in precision HF management.

Title: Antiprotozoal drug exposure and reduced long-term mortality and morbidity: a multi-cohort pharmacoepidemiologic study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Medications may affect age-related morbidity and overall survival beyond their original indications. Systematic identification of such effects may inform drug repurposing strategies for healthy aging. We aimed to identify medications associated with longevity and reduced age-related morbidity using large-scale electronic health record data.
METHODS: We conducted a stepwise pharmacoepidemiologic investigation in two independent healthcare systems. Using electronic health records from a nationwide health provider, we performed an exploratory medication-wide case-control screen comparing medication exposure during a 10-year window between 14,986 individuals who died before sex-specific median life expectancy and matched controls who survived beyond their life expectancy. Two leading candidate drugs, atovaquone-proguanil and mefloquine, are antiprotozoal agents with activity against Toxoplasma gondii. Their effects on mortality and age-related morbidity were further evaluated within a historical cohort of 3,876 exposed individuals and 77,520 matched controls using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline characteristics. External validation was performed in the United States-based TriNetX network, including cohorts exposed to atovaquone-proguanil (n = 24,498), mefloquine (n = 3,400), and nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (n = 124,681), each matched to unexposed controls.
RESULTS: Atovaquone-proguanil and mefloquine, together with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir, a protease inhibitor with reported antiprotozoal effects, were associated with consistent reductions in all-cause mortality across cohorts and lower incidence of multiple age-related conditions, including dementia, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and selected malignancies. Consistent increases in specific conditions were also observed, including hearing loss, Sjögren's syndrome/dry eye, and lichen planus, suggesting shared underlying mechanisms, although confounding cannot be excluded.
DISCUSSION: Findings were consistent across healthcare systems and drug classes, including in populations exposed to non-travel-associated medications. While causality cannot be established, these results support further investigation into potential links between chronic protozoal infections and aging-related diseases.

Title: Multimodal integration of carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics and dynamic systemic immune-inflammation trajectories for subacute risk stratification after stroke thrombectomy: development and internal validation of an exploratory prognostic model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We hypothesized that integrating macroscopic carotid plaque architecture, quantified via ultrasound radiomics, with downstream micro-cellular temporal dynamics, defined by longitudinal immune trajectories, would yield a highly accurate prognostic framework for 90-day functional outcomes in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery (N = 221) and an internal validation cohort (N = 95) using stratified random sampling. To capture temporal inflammatory heterogeneity, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) was measured at days 0, 1, 3, and 7, and clustered using Latent Class Mixed Models (LCMM). Concurrently, high-dimensional radiomic features strictly adhering to the Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) guidelines were extracted from baseline two-dimensional carotid ultrasound images. A radiomics score (Rad-score) was constructed utilizing Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Four progressive predictive models were developed, culminating in an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) multimodal architecture. The primary endpoint was an unfavorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 3 to 6).
RESULTS: An unfavorable outcome occurred in 166 of 316 patients (52.5%). The LCMM objectively identified three longitudinal SII phenotypes. The "persistent high-inflammation" trajectory (Class 3, 17.0% of patients) was independently associated with an increased risk of an unfavorable outcome compared to the "rapid resolution" trajectory (Class 1) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 4.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.20 to 10.85; p < 0.001]. The ultrasound Rad-score, comprising 9 core textural features, also demonstrated robust independent predictive value (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92 per 0.1-point increase; p < 0.001). In the strictly isolated internal validation cohort, the full multimodal XGBoost model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86 to 0.97), with an accuracy of 86.3%, sensitivity of 88.0%, and specificity of 84.4%. This performance was statistically superior to the standard clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.63 to 0.84; p < 0.001 via DeLong test). Furthermore, the multimodal paradigm demonstrated clinical reclassification utility, yielding a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.985 (95% CI, 0.684 to 1.286) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (95% CI, 0.128 to 0.260).
CONCLUSION: An exploratory model integrating baseline carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics with Day-0-to-Day-7 systemic immune-inflammation trajectories was associated with 90-day functional outcome after EVT and, on internal validation, discriminated outcomes more strongly than a conventional clinical model. Because the immune-trajectory component is only complete at Day 7, the model is intended for subacute post-EVT risk stratification rather than acute treatment selection, and requires external, prospective validation before any clinical application.

Title: External validation and cross-center transportability of phenotypic age acceleration and laboratory frailty for postoperative mortality prediction: a dual-center cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phenotypic Age Acceleration (PAA) and the Laboratory Frailty Index (FI-Lab) can be derived from routine biomarkers to describe biologic aging and accumulated laboratory deficits. Their prognostic behavior across different clinical settings, however, remains uncertain. We examined whether associations with postoperative mortality were consistent between two hospitals and whether either measure added predictive information beyond standard clinical variables.
METHODS: We analyzed 1,223 adults (671 from Shandong and 552 from Jiangsu) with linked health-examination/questionnaire information, perioperative characteristics, and follow-up through 540 days. Phenotypic Age was calculated from chronological age and nine biomarkers. Primary PAA used the Shandong age-Phenotypic Age relation as a fixed reference, and FI-Lab was the proportion of 17 prespecified laboratory deficits. Center-specific and center-stratified Cox models assessed 540-day mortality. Ridge logistic models were trained in Shandong and externally validated in Jiangsu for 365-day mortality; the reverse direction was treated as a secondary reciprocal transportability sensitivity analysis. As the fixed Shandong reference induced age dependence in Jiangsu, sensitivity analyses recalculated PAA as center-specific age-Phenotypic Age residuals with center-specific standardization. Secondary analyses covered the 12-month composite of death or incident diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or cardiovascular disease. Longitudinal analyses of within-person PAA and FI-Lab changes were exploratory; exact person-specific reassessment intervals were unavailable, and follow-up chronological age for PAA was approximated as baseline age + 1 year. All laboratory measurements used to calculate PAA and FI-Lab were obtained from the preoperative panel within 24 h before the index operation, and completeness of this panel was required for inclusion.
RESULTS: During 1,694.66 person-years, 74 participants died, including 57 within 365 days. In the fully adjusted center-stratified model, each 1-SD increase in PAA was associated with mortality [hazard ratio (HR), 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.03-1.75], whereas the FI-Lab estimate was borderline (HR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.00-1.65). Cross-center interaction estimates were imprecise (PAA interaction ratio, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.68-1.65; FI-Lab interaction ratio, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.94-2.32). Fixed-reference PAA was strongly inversely correlated with chronological age in Jiangsu (r = - 0.74); when PAA was recalculated using center-specific age-Phenotypic Age residuals and standardized within center, the fully adjusted pooled association remained (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.09-1.77). In the primary Shandong-to-Jiangsu external validation, the study clinical model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.60 (95% CI, 0.45-0.73); adding PAA, FI-Lab, or both yielded AUCs of 0.60, 0.63, and 0.63, respectively, without a consistent decision-curve net-benefit gain. FI-Lab, but not PAA, was associated with the 12-month death-or-incident-disease composite (RR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.08-1.71). Among 820 participants with repeated measurements, exploratory mean changes were + 2.90 years for PAA and + 0.02 for FI-Lab. Calibration estimates in the primary external-validation cohort were imprecise because only 23 deaths occurred by 365 days; nonsignificant calibration tests were not interpreted as evidence of good calibration.
CONCLUSIONS: Laboratory-derived aging and frailty measures were related to postoperative mortality across the two cohorts, and the PAA association was robust to center-specific residualization. However, absolute fixed-reference PAA values were not directly transportable across centers because the age-Phenotypic Age relations differed. Neither marker consistently improved prediction beyond the study clinical model, whose external discrimination was modest; calibration remained imprecise. Larger multicenter studies with rigorous cross-center laboratory harmonization are needed before routine perioperative use.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study

Title: Eight-week flexi-bar vibration exercise improves cardiovascular function accompanied by altered gut microbiota and metabolites in middle-aged and elderly women: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate the impact of 8-week FE on cardiovascular health in middle-aged and elderly women and explore correlational associations involving gut microbiota and its metabolites.
METHODS: Thirty middle-aged and elderly women were randomly divided into FE group and control group. Body composition parameters were assessed using a body composition analyzer. cfPWV and baPWV were detected to assess central and systemic arterial stiffness, respectively. To evaluate central hemodynamic parameters and cardiac autonomic function, HR, augmentation index, SEVR, and HRV were measured. Biochemical factors in serum were detected by ELISA. Gut microbiota and SCFAs levels in Fecal samples were assessed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and GC-MS.
RESULTS: FE helped preserve water, inorganic salts, muscle mass, and fat-free mass, while prevented the accumulation of body weight and body fat. FE also significantly decreased HR, central systolic and diastolic blood pressure, cfPWV and R-baPWV. The HRV analysis demonstrated that FE increased SDNN and NN50 (time-domain indices) and high-frequency band, while decreasing low-frequency band. Moreover, FE significantly up-regulated the serum eNOS level and down-regulated ICAM1 level. Meanwhile, FE increased Bacteroidota abundance and decreased Firmicutes abundance, alongside elevated fecal acetic acid, propionic acid, and caproic acid in fecal samples.
CONCLUSIONS: 8-week FE improves cardiovascular function in middle-aged and elderly women by enhancing parasympathetic activity, reducing sympathetic overactivity, and mitigating arterial stiffness. Parallel shifts in gut microbiota composition and elevated SCFAs were observed following FE intervention, highlighting FE as an effective intervention for cardiovascular health in this population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: http://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2000041245.

Title: Multi-label auxiliary decision-making model for pharmacotherapy of ischemic stroke based on BR-SA-LightGBM using real-world electronic medical records.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke poses a substantial global health burden owing to its high prevalence, recurrence, disability, and mortality rates. Pharmacotherapy for ischemic stroke is highly heterogeneous across patients, with complex polypharmacy regimens and intricate interdependencies between drug classes. Precise, personalised medication recommendations are therefore indispensable for optimising therapeutic outcomes and improving patient prognosis.
METHODS: This study framed pharmacotherapeutic decision-making for ischemic stroke as a multi-label learning task. Using retrospective electronic medical records from 7,335 ischemic stroke patients admitted to a single tertiary hospital (Cangzhou Central Hospital), we developed and evaluated an integrated model, termed BR-SA-LightGBM, which combines Binary Relevance (BR), Simulated Annealing (SA), and the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) to provide personalised recommendations across eight first-line drug categories.
RESULTS: In an independent test cohort (n = 2,200), the BR-SA-LightGBM model achieved an accuracy of 0.90, an F1-score of 0.87, and a markedly low Hamming loss of 0.09. It significantly outperformed ML-KNN, Power-Set, and the unoptimized BR-LightGBM model across all evaluation metrics (P < 0.05). Across drug classes, age, the number of comorbidities, atrial fibrillation, carotid plaque, and fibrinogen were among the most influential predictors of medication selection.
CONCLUSIONS: The BR-SA-LightGBM model established herein enables accurate, personalised, auxiliary decision support for drug prescribing in ischemic stroke. It is intended as an auxiliary decision-support tool that has the potential to reduce medication errors and omissions and may assist clinicians in improving clinical efficiency; it also provides a novel methodological framework for precision medicine in stroke care.

Title: UACR adjustment attenuates associations of selected routine blood markers with documented diabetic retinopathy more than eGFR adjustment: a cross-sectional study in type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies of routine blood markers and diabetic retinopathy often adjust for estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), although albuminuria captures a different aspect of kidney damage. We compared these associations under eGFR and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) adjustment.
METHODS: We analyzed 8,159 adults hospitalized with type 2 diabetes from January 2020 to March 2026. Primary exposures were serum albumin, total bilirubin, fibrinogen and the FIB-4 index. Four models were fitted in a fixed complete-case sample, with additional adjustment for eGFR, log UACR, or both. The outcome was documented diabetic retinopathy (DR), based on ophthalmological assessment and discharge diagnosis; DR = 0 included unassessed patients without a DR diagnosis. Prevalence ratios were estimated by marginal standardization.
RESULTS: Among 3,978 complete-case patients, 958 (24.1%) had documented DR. Adjustment for log UACR attenuated the serum albumin association more than adjustment for eGFR (73.3% versus 34.3%; difference 38.9 percentage points, 95% CI 30.7 to 49.0) and moved the fibrinogen estimate close to one. Binary albuminuria produced substantially less attenuation than continuous log UACR. Multiple imputation supported the renal-adjustment comparison, although the albumin interval included the null after mutual renal adjustment. Serum albumin remained associated with documented DR after restriction to eGFR ≥90 mL/min/1.73 m2 (prevalence ratio 0.762, 95% CI 0.649 to 0.873), whereas no clear evidence of an eGFR association was observed within this stratum (0.981, P = 0.823). Conclusions: In this single-center inpatient cohort, eGFR and UACR adjustment yielded different estimates for the studied blood-marker associations with documented DR. Attenuation denotes proportional reduction in the absolute log prevalence-ratio estimate, not a causal proportion explained. Dichotomizing UACR discarded information and reduced attenuation in these models.

Title: Early Vericiguat Initiation After First Hospitalization for Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Observational Study From the VERIFY-HF Registry and Institutional Cohorts.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitalization for the first episode of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) represents an important opportunity to initiate evidence-based therapies. In this study, we aimed to clarify the role of vericiguat after first hospitalization for HFrEF in routine clinical practice.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with HFrEF at their first hospitalization between June 2021 and September 2023 identified from the nationwide Verifying Characteristics and Outcomes in Heart Failure Patients Treated with Vericiguat registry (vericiguat group, n=104) and 2 institutional databases (control group, n=206) (mean age, 67 years; 71% male). The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death or HF rehospitalization within 1 year. In inverse probability of treatment weighting-adjusted Cox models, vericiguat use was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, compared with controls (hazard ratio, 0.26; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.81). Sensitivity analysis using alternative weighting methods and a doubly robust model yielded consistent results.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world Japanese cohort of patients at first hospitalization for HFrEF, vericiguat initiation during index hospitalization was associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular death or HF rehospitalization after discharge. The observed association was directionally consistent with previous trials and pooled analyses, suggesting a potential benefit for this intermediate real-world population.

Title: Residual Risk Despite High Short Physical Performance Battery Scores in Older Patients With Heart Failure: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), which is widely used to assess physical function and prognostic risk in patients with heart failure (HF), is unclear in patients with high SPPB scores. In this study we evaluated whether sarcopenia-related factors defined by the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia in 2019 provided additional prognostic value in this population.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study of the J-Proof HF registry included 3,044 patients aged ≥65 years with a discharge SPPB score ≥10. Impairments in handgrip strength, five-times chair stand test, and calf circumference were aggregated into a composite physical function score (range, 0-3). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or rehospitalization for HF within 1 year, which occurred in 25.0% of the cohort. The composite outcome risk increased in a stepwise manner with each additional impaired domain (adjusted hazard ratio per 1-point increase, 1.245; 95% confidence interval 1.132-1.370; P<0.001). The fully adjusted model showed acceptable discrimination (Harrell's C-index=0.694). Each domain independently demonstrated a similar magnitude of association with the outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Even among older patients with HF and preserved physical performance (SPPB ≥10), accumulation of sarcopenia-related impairments was associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes. Supplementing the SPPB with simple functional assessments may improve risk stratification in clinical practice.

Title: Whole-Exome Sequencing in Patients With Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: An Exploratory Analysis of Rare Variant Burden and Apical Aneurysm.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apical aneurysm complicates apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (ApHCM), but its genetic determinants remain unclear.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed in 72 Japanese patients with ApHCM, including 8 with apical aneurysms. Rare-variant burden was evaluated in core HCM genes, extended cardiomyopathy genes, and candidate remodeling pathways. No prespecified gene set was significantly enriched in aneurysm cases. ALPK3 missense variants were identified only in non-aneurysm cases.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cohort, WES did not detect a clear rare coding variant burden signal associated with apical aneurysm.

Title: Clinical effectiveness of mavacamten on cardiac function and disease-related indicators in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the clinical effects of mavacamten and conventional pharmacotherapy on cardiac function and related disease indicators in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed in patients with oHCM who were hospitalized between January 2024 and May 2025. The intervention group included 126 patients who received mavacamten for the first time, while the control group consisted of 134 patients treated with conventional medications. Baseline clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, and imaging findings were collected. All patients were followed up for 30 weeks after discharge. Changes in relevant clinical indicators were recorded and compared at weeks 6 (W6), 18 (W18), and 30 (W30).
RESULTS: A total of 222 patients (111 per group) completed the 30-week follow-up and were included in the final analysis. After 30 weeks of treatment, the resting left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) peak gradient fell to 23.76 ± 4.09 mmHg in the intervention group but persisted at 78.49 ± 13.21 mmHg in the control group (t = 24.074, p < 0.001). Similarly, the Valsalva-provoked LVOT peak gradient decreased to 48.95 ± 11.10 mmHg versus 113.59 ± 14.92 mmHg in the control group (t = 21.147, p < 0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was 55.12% ± 4.85% in the intervention group and 56.78% ± 5.42% in the control group (p = 0.312), with 9.5% of mavacamten-treated patients experiencing LVEF decline to <50% (vs. 2.2% in controls). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) levels were significantly lower in the intervention group (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Mavacamten indicates significant clinical association with improved outcomes in improving cardiac function and related disease indicators in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, with sustained reductions in both resting and provoked LVOT gradients.

Title: Postoperative Mortality and Risk Factors in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease Undergoing Cardiovascular Surgery: Insights From the Japanese Registry Data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) are prone to complications and usually require surgical intervention, but the surgical risk factors remain poorly defined.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed data from April 2013 to March 2023 in the nationwide Japanese Registry of All Cardiac and Vascular Disease-Diagnostic Procedure Combination (JROAD-DPC) to assess postoperative cardiac death and its predictors. This study included ACHD patients aged ≥18 years who underwent cardiovascular surgery, and the primary outcome was in-hospital death. A total of 10,535 patients (median age 53 [interquartile range 36-68] years; 50.4% female) were classified into mild (n=6,831), moderate (n=2,388), and severe (n=1,316) complexity groups. Among the 146 in-hospital deaths (1.4%), the highest mortality rate was observed in patients with severe complexity (2.4%). Multivariable analysis showed that age (hazard ratio [HR] 1.15), severe complexity (HR 1.77), renal disease (HR 1.74), pulmonary hypertension requiring medications (HR 2.01), chromosome abnormality (HR 6.22), and high-risk surgery (Fontan surgery or coronary artery bypass grafting) (HR 1.67) were significantly associated with increased in-hospital deaths.
