Subgroup analyses showed that age, renal disease, and high-risk surgery were prognostic factors in the mild group. Age was not significant in the moderate or severe groups.
CONCLUSIONS: The in-hospital mortality rate after cardiovascular surgery in ACHD was low overall but increased with disease complexity, supporting the need for disease complexity-based, individualized risk assessments in surgical planning.

Title: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential and Heart Failure: Mechanisms, Risk Stratification, and Therapeutic Implications.
Abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is an age-related expansion of hematopoietic clones carrying somatic driver variants and has been consistently associated with cardiovascular disease. Observational studies associate CHIP with incident heart failure (HF) and adverse outcomes, with substantial heterogeneity according to driver gene and clone size. The most coherent phenotype-specific evidence involves older, inflammation-enriched populations and HF with preserved ejection fraction, particularly TET2-related CHIP; evidence in HF with reduced ejection fraction, ischemic HF, and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy is less mature and largely prognostic. Gene-specific experimental models show that TET2 loss can amplify interleukin-1β/NOD-, LRR- and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 signaling, DNMT3A-mutant hematopoiesis can promote fibroblast activation, and JAK2V617F can enhance thrombo-inflammation. These findings provide biological plausibility but do not establish CHIP as a causal driver of HF in humans. Any future clinical translation will require standardized sequencing and variant interpretation, validated variant allele frequency thresholds, demonstration of incremental prognostic utility and cost-effectiveness, and evidence that CHIP-guided management improves clinical outcomes. No CHIP-directed HF therapy or routine testing strategy is currently recommended. Exploratory genomic analyses of CANTOS and ongoing inflammation-enriched trials provide opportunities to evaluate CHIP as a prognostic, trial-enrichment, or predictive biomarker. This review synthesizes current epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence, highlights phenotype-specific limitations, and outlines priorities for prospective validation.

Title: Comparative effects of different magnetic stimulation modalities on upper limb motor function and activities of daily living in patients with stroke: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of different magnetic stimulation (MS) modalities on upper limb motor function and activities of daily living (ADL) in patients with stroke through a network meta-analysis.
METHODS: Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, Wanfang, VIP, and CNKI were searched from inception to January 2026 for randomized controlled trials evaluating MS interventions for upper limb motor function and activities of daily living (ADL) in patients with stroke. A frequentist network meta-analysis was performed using standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% confidence interval (CI). The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to estimate the relative ranking probabilities of interventions. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: A total of 48 randomized controlled trials were included. For upper limb motor function, rPMS (SMD = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.19 to 1.12), rTMS (SMD = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.68 to 1.24), and combined MS (SMD = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.47 to 1.55) were all superior to conventional rehabilitation. SUCRA rankings suggested that combined MS ranked highest, followed by rTMS. However, pairwise comparisons among active magnetic stimulation interventions did not reach statistical significance. For ADL, rPMS (SMD = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.26 to 0.95), rTMS (SMD = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.56 to 0.97), and combined MS (SMD = 1.27, 95% CI: 0.94 to 1.59) significantly improved ADL compared with conventional rehabilitation. Combined MS was also superior to rPMS and rTMS alone. Sensitivity analysis excluding studies that reported only the Barthel Index showed broadly consistent results. No clear evidence of publication bias or small-study effects was detected. The certainty of evidence was rated as low.
CONCLUSION: MS interventions may improve upper limb motor function and ADL in patients with stroke. Combined MS and rTMS showed relatively high ranking probabilities for upper limb motor recovery, whereas combined MS showed the highest ranking probability for ADL improvement. Given the heterogeneity among included studies, non-significant differences in some direct comparisons, and low certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed by high-quality head-to-head trials.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261302905, Identifier: CRD420261302905.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study

Title: Interpreting dynamic right ventricular free wall strain in intradialytic hypotension.
Abstract: Kim et al. reported that greater dialysis-induced reductions in right ventricular (RV) free wall strain were associated with intradialytic hypotension. Because both strain change and hypotension were determined across the same dialysis session, dynamic RV strain may represent a concurrent physiological response rather than a prospective risk predictor. Clarifying the predictive value of pre-dialysis RV strain could better define its role in identifying patients vulnerable to intradialytic hemodynamic instability.

Title: Determinants of MoCA improvement in post-ischemic stroke patients receiving acupuncture: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acupuncture is commonly integrated into multimodal rehabilitation programs for post-ischemic stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), but the factors associated with cognitive improvement in this complex treatment context remain unclear. This retrospective study investigated factors associated with cognitive improvement in stroke patients receiving acupuncture as part of a standardized multimodal inpatient rehabilitation program.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 226 ischemic stroke patients treated with acupuncture between January 2023 and December 2025 were enrolled. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, acupuncture treatment parameters, and laboratory indicators were collected from electronic medical records. Cognitive function was assessed using MoCA, MMSE, LOTCA, MBI, HAMD, HAMA, and PSQI scales. Patients were categorized into improvement (ΔMoCA ≥2) and non-improvement groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with cognitive improvement.
RESULTS: Among the 226 patients, 148 (65.49%) achieved improvement. After treatment, the improvement group showed significant improvements in MoCA and MMSE scores compared with baseline and the non-improvement group [between-group difference for post-treatment MoCA: 1.59 (95% CI 0.82 to 2.36; p < 0.001); MMSE: 2.44 (95% CI 1.69 to 3.19; p < 0.001)]. Significant improvements were also observed in LOTCA, MBI, HAMD, HAMA, and PSQI scores in the improvement group (p < 0.001). Univariate analysis identified age, education years, admission NIHSS score, diabetes mellitus, time to acupuncture intervention, treatment frequency, and total treatment course as factors associated with recovery (p < 0.05). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that advanced age (OR = 1.208, p < 0.001), higher NIHSS score (OR = 1.643, p = 0.001), longer time from stroke onset to acupuncture intervention (OR = 1.162, p = 0.011) and diabetes mellitus (OR = 4.737, p = 0.018) were associated with a lower probability of achieving the ΔMoCA improvement threshold. In contrast, longer education duration (OR = 0.740, p = 0.006), higher treatment frequency (OR = 0.271, p < 0.001), and longer treatment course (OR = 0.248, p < 0.001) were associated with a higher probability of meeting the improvement threshold. However, as treatment frequency and total course were determined during the clinical course rather than at baseline, these associations should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating, and do not imply causality.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort of PSCI patients receiving acupuncture within a multimodal inpatient rehabilitation setting, shorter time from stroke onset to acupuncture initiation, higher weekly frequency, and longer treatment duration were exploratory factors associated with a greater likelihood of meeting the predefined ΔMoCA improvement threshold in this cohort. These hypothesis-generating observations may inform the design of future prospective studies and suggest patient characteristics that warrant further investigation. However, given the uncontrolled design, these findings cannot establish acupuncture-specific efficacy and should be considered hypothesis-generating, warranting confirmation through prospective randomized controlled trials.

Title: Optimizing aprocitentan dosing in elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension: a PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm modeling study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aprocitentan is a dual endothelin receptor antagonist for resistant hypertension (RH), but its optimal use in elderly Chinese patients remains unclear. This study aimed to develop an integrated physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK)/pharmacodynamic (PD)-circadian rhythm model to suggest precision dosing and administration-time optimization in this special population.
METHODS: A PBPK model was developed using published clinical pharmacokinetic data and linked to a direct-effect sigmoid maximal effect model. Circadian blood pressure (BP) variation was described by a triple-harmonic cosine function. After validation against independent pharmacokinetic (PK) and PD datasets, the model was extrapolated to elderly Chinese patients by incorporating age-related physiology, uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 activity variability, and mild hepatic impairment. Sensitivity analyses and simulations were performed to evaluate exposure, BP response, and dosing time.
RESULTS: The model showed acceptable predictive performance. Sensitivity analyses indicated that aprocitentan exposure was mainly influenced by ionization-, binding-, and distribution-related parameters. Plasma unbound fraction and liver volume were the major determinants of cumulative and steady-state area under the curve (AUC), while lipophilicity predominantly affected early exposure, mean residence time, and terminal half-life. Compared with healthy elderly Caucasian subjects, simulated steady-state AUC increased by 20.6% in elderly Chinese patients and by 52.5% in those with mild hepatic impairment. Among the simulated regimens, 6.25 mg once daily provided the most balanced exposure profile and maintained AUC and maximum plasma concentration within the prespecified reference range in both populations. The model identified 12:00-13:00 as an alternative administration window associated with a favorable simulated 24-hour BP profile. Under the model-predicted regimen, simulated reductions in systolic BP/diastolic BP were 13.04/8.97 mmHg in elderly Chinese RH patients and 13.63/9.37 mmHg in those with mild hepatic impairment, with 24-hour BP remaining mainly within the Grade 1 hypertension range.
CONCLUSIONS: This study established an integrated PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm model for aprocitentan in elderly Chinese patients with RH. The simulations identified 6.25 mg once daily and midday administration as candidate strategies for further clinical evaluation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective PK/PD, ambulatory BP, safety, adherence, and clinical validation before implementation in clinical practice.

Title: Registry-recorded stroke and transient ischaemic attack diagnoses in Saudi Arabia, 2016-2025: a national descriptive analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a major cause of death and disability globally, and its prevalence is growing as modifiable risk factors become more prevalent and the population ages. In Saudi Arabia, evidence is mainly from hospital or local data, and national descriptions of cerebrovascular diagnoses recorded in routinely collected health data remain limited in Saudi Arabia.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the cumulative registry-recorded burden of adults with a qualifying stroke-related or transient ischemic attack (TIA) diagnosis in the Population Health Observatory (PHO) in Saudi Arabia, using linked national health data from 2016 to 2025. This includes the registry-recorded burden, demographics and characteristics, comorbidities and healthcare utilization.
METHODS: We conducted a national retrospective descriptive analysis of de-identified aggregate outputs from linked PHO data for 2016-2025, a descriptive statistical analysis of 68,634 stroke-diagnosed individuals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The observational study was conducted using PHO data from 2016 to 2025.
RESULTS: The PHO identified 68,634 unique adults with a qualifying cerebrovascular diagnosis. Stroke burden was disproportionately concentrated in males (64.45%) and in both genders aged 60-69 years (23.27%). The accumulated count corresponded to 0.26% of the 2025 adult population; this is a crude descriptive ratio, not prevalence. Najran had the highest crude regional ratio at 0.38%. BMI was missing/invalid for 39,481 (57.52%). Among 29,153 with valid BMI, 10,494 (36.00%) were overweight and 9,930 (34.06%) were obese. The PHO low-multimorbidity category contained 42,882 individuals (62.48%); it is an administrative stratum, not a validated cardiovascular-risk score; most visits were to outpatient departments.
CONCLUSION: Saudi Arabia's recorded stroke burden is concentrated among older males. The findings describe patterns captured by the PHO and should not be interpreted as prevalence, incidence, or causal associations, which indicate the need for better prevention, management of chronic diseases and a robust national surveillance system to inform policies based on evidence to support Saudi Vision 2030.

Title: Distinct temporal neuropsychiatric outcomes associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists versus SGLT2 inhibitors after acute kidney disease in type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurological and neuropsychiatric complications may persist after acute kidney disease (AKD), particularly among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) provide established cardiorenal benefits, their associations with neurological outcomes after AKD remain uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults with T2DM and dialysis-requiring AKD receiving GLP-1RAs or SGLT2is were identified and balanced using 1:1 propensity score matching, yielding 3,398 patients in each group. Incident delirium and other neuropsychiatric outcomes were evaluated. The 90-365-day period was the primary analysis, with 90-180- and 90-720-day windows used to assess temporal patterns. Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During 90-365 days, GLP-1RA use was associated with better delirium-free survival than SGLT2i use (118/3,032 vs. 155/2,982 events; log-rank P = 0.009). This association remained significant after multivariable adjustment (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.668; 95% CI, 0.488-0.914; P = 0.012). Statin use was independently associated with lower delirium risk (adjusted HR, 0.674; 95% CI, 0.492-0.924; P = 0.014), while exploratory analyses suggested a distinct association between LDL cholesterol of 100-129.9 mg/dL and delirium risk. In contrast, SGLT2i use showed a favorable association with depression during early follow-up, which attenuated over time. The GLP-1RA-delirium association was also attenuated by 90-720 days. Exploratory sensitivity analyses using non-overlapping follow-up intervals showed outcome-specific associations: adjusted differences in delirium were not significant, whereas depression and overall neurological complications were more frequent with GLP-1RA than with SGLT2i.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with dialysis-requiring AKD and T2DM, GLP-1RA and SGLT2i use showed outcome-specific associations with subsequent neuropsychiatric events. Although the primary analysis suggested a lower delirium risk with GLP-1RA, this association was not consistently observed in adjusted time-stratified analyses. These findings should be considered exploratory and require prospective validation.

Title: Correction to "Risk of Heart Failure Hospitalization Associated With Hypoxia-Inducible Factor Prolyl Hydroxylase Inhibitors Versus Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agents: A Nationwide Claims-Based Cohort Study".
Association of the Neutrophil-to-HDL-C Ratio With Coronary Artery Disease and Coronary Stenosis Severity in Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: Results From the Iranian-CARDIO Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Inflammation plays a central role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis, with neutrophils and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) being key components. The neutrophil-to-HDL-C ratio (NHR) has recently been proposed as a potential biomarker of CAD. This study is aimed at evaluating the association of NHR with the presence and angiographic severity of CAD.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study was conducted on 250 patients who were referred for suspected CAD and underwent coronary angiography at Afshar Hospital, Yazd, Iran. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were collected, and the severity of CAD was assessed using the Gensini score. NHR was calculated as the neutrophil count (×103/μL) divided by HDL-C (mmol/L). Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed; the model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, body mass index, and blood pressure (Model III) was designated as the primary model, and a fully adjusted model (Model IV) served as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: The findings showed that patients with CAD had a significantly higher NHR than patients without CAD (3.9 ± 1.8 vs. 3.1 ± 1.28, p = 0.001). NHR increased across Gensini score tertiles (p = 0.04). In the primary adjusted model, each 1-SD increase in NHR was independently associated with CAD (OR = 2.01, 95% CI 1.28-3.14; p = 0.002) and a high Gensini score (OR = 1.56, 95% CI 1.14-2.12; p = 0.005). Bootstrap resampling (1000 replicates) confirmed the stability of these estimates. These findings were consistent in the fully adjusted model (OR = 2.31 and 1.62, respectively). NHR showed only modest discriminative ability for CAD (AUC = 0.638) and a high Gensini score (AUC = 0.620).
CONCLUSION: NHR was independently associated with the presence and severity of CAD in patients referred for coronary angiography. However, its discriminative ability was modest, and its incremental value and prognostic utility require validation in independent prospective cohorts.

Title: [Grading assessment of diabetic macular edema based on fundus photography].
Journal: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the association between fundus photographic features and the severity of diabetic macular edema (DME) and evaluate their diagnostic performance. Methods: It was a retrospective case series study. Data of patients with diabetic retinopathy who were diagnosed at the Xiamen Eye Center of Xiamen University from June 2023 to June 2024 were included. All patients underwent best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure, fundus photography and optical coherence tomography (OCT). According to the extent of DME involvement, the eyes were divided into 4 groups. Statistical analyses were performed using one-way analysis of variance, chi-square test, Kruskal-Wallis H test, and Bonferroni correction. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) was used to assess the correlation between fundus photographic features and retinal thickness in different regions. Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis was used to identify the risk factors for DME grading, and the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were adopted to assess diagnostic performance. Results: A total of 196 patients (207 eyes) were enrolled, 114 male patients and 82 female patients. The mean age was (57.36±9.83) years. CCA demonstrated a significant correlation between OCT-measured retinal thickness and fundus photographic features (first canonical correlation coefficient ρ=0.66,P<0.05), and hard exudates had the highest canonical loading (0.69). Eyes with definite hard exudates presented the greatest retinal thickening at the superior macular retina [(43.23±13.47) μm]. Multivariate binary logistic regression indicated that, relative to no DME eyes, stepwise increments in total hard exudates were associated with odds ratios (ORs) of 4.77, 6.54 and 7.25 for perifoveal, parafoveal and central DME (P<0.01). Positional changes of hard exudates had ORs of 3.14 and 3.23 for parafoveal and central DME (P<0.01). The ORs of total amount and positiona changes of punctate hemorrhages for central DME were 1.46 and 2.09 respectively (P<0.01). The AUC of hard exudates was 0.835-0.844(sensitivity 81.9%-89.1%, specificity 61.1%-70.3%), the AUC of punctate hemorrhages was 0.766-0.768 (sensitivity 73.6%-81.8%, specificity 61.1%-64.9%). Combining clinical features, the diagnostic performance was significantly improved. Only positional changes of hard exudates exerted a significant effect in the classification of non-center-involved (nci) DME and center-involved (ci) DME (OR=4.70, P<0.01), and the overall discriminative ability of the model (Nagelkerke R²=0.371) was lower than that of the ETDRS grid-based DME classification model (R²=0.756). Conclusions: Changes in hard exudates on fundus photography are independent risk factors for DME severity. Punctate hemorrhages indicates central DME. The combination of fundus photographic features and clinical features can improve diagnostic performance.

Title: [Mechanism of endothelial cell-derived S100A11 in promoting radiation-induced cardiac fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice].
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the role and mechanism of cardiac endothelial cell-derived S100A11 in promoting radiotherapy-induced cardiac fibrosis in C57BL/6 mice. Methods: Eight 6-week-old female C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into a control group (n=4) and a radiotherapy group (n=4) using a random number table. The control group received no intervention, while the radiotherapy group received a single high-dose irradiation of 16 Gy to the left thorax to establish a mouse model of cardiac injury. At 12 weeks after radiotherapy, echocardiography was performed to measure left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular fractional shortening (LVFS), and left ventricular internal dimension at end-systole (LVIDs). Western blotting was used to detect the expression of collagen type Ⅰ (COL Ⅰ) and alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) in mouse cardiac tissue. The mouse cardiac endothelial cell line MCEC were divided into a control group and a radiotherapy group (medium was replaced after endothelial cell adherence, followed by radiotherapy and continued culture for 24 h before sample collection). The supernatants from the control and radiotherapy endothelial cell groups were mixed with complete medium at a 1∶1 ratio and used to culture primary cardiac fibroblasts extracted from C57BL/6 mouse cardiac tissue. These fibroblasts were divided into a control group and a treatment group. Western blotting was used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression and a scratch assay was used to assess cell migration ability. Endothelial cells were divided into a control group and a radiotherapy group. Western blotting, quantitative real-time PCR, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) were used to detect the expression and secretion of S100 calcium-binding protein A11 (S100A11) in endothelial cells. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was used to knock down S100A11 gene expression in endothelial cells. Two siRNAs targeting S100A11 and a siRNA negative control group were separately transfected into endothelial cells. Western blotting was used to verify whether S100A11 expression in endothelial cells was successfully knocked down. The S100A11-knockdown endothelial cells were then subjected to radiotherapy and divided into a control group, siRNA-1 group, and siRNA-2 group. The sample collection method and the method for co-culturing primary fibroblasts were the same as described above, with groups designated as control, siRNA-1, and siRNA-2. Western blotting was used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression. Primary fibroblasts were treated with recombinant S100A11 protein (100 ng/ml) for 24 h, and Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to detect COL Ⅰ and α-SMA expression. Transcriptome sequencing was used to detect gene expression changes in primary fibroblasts treated with recombinant S100A11 protein for 24 h. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was used to knock down integrin subunit beta-like 1 (ITGBL1) gene expression in primary fibroblasts. Two siRNAs targeting ITGBL1 (siRNA-1 and siRNA-2) (i.e., the siRNA group) and a siRNA negative control (si-NC) group were separately transfected into primary fibroblasts. Western blotting was used to verify knockdown of ITGBL1 expression in primary fibroblasts. Primary fibroblasts with ITGBL1 knockdown were cultured with recombinant S100A11 protein for 24 h, and Western blotting and immunofluorescence were used to detect COLⅠ and α-SMA protein expression. Results: Compared with the control group, echocardiography showed that LVEF and LVFS were lower in the radiotherapy group (both P<0.001), and COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression levels in cardiac tissue were higher in the radiotherapy group (both P<0.001). Perivascular fibrotic tissue in the hearts of irradiated mice was increased than that of the control group (all P<0.05). The mRNA, protein, and supernatant protein expression of S100A11 in endothelial cells were higher in the radiotherapy group than in the control group (all P<0.001). The supernatant from radiotherapy-treated endothelial cells increased and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts compared with the control group (all P<0.05). In S100A11-knockdown endothelial cells subjected to radiotherapy, COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts in the siRNA groups were lower than in the control group (all P<0.05). Recombinant S100A11 protein increased COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts compared with the control group (all P<0.05). Transcriptome sequencing indicated that ITGBL1 gene expression levels were higher in primary fibroblasts treated with recombinant S100A11 protein than in the control group. After ITGBL1 knockdown, S100A11 promoted COL Ⅰ and α-SMA protein expression in primary fibroblasts were lower than in the control group (P<0.05). Conclusions: After radiotherapy, S100A11 expression and secretion are increased in cardiac endothelial cells. This effect can further activate cardiac fibroblasts in C57BL/6 mice and promote the development and progression of cardiac fibrosis.

Title: [Expert consensus on the application of energy metabolism monitoring in nutritional support therapy (2026 edition)].
Abstract: Energy metabolism is the foundation for sustaining life activities. Accurate measurement of energy expenditure is crucial for formulating individualized nutritional support therapy. This consensus was jointly initiated by the China International Exchange and Promotive Association for Medical and Health Care Clinical Nutrition Health Branch, Chinese Society of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition, and the Chinese Nutrition Society Branch of Clinical Nutrition. A multidisciplinary team of experts systematically reviewed the evidence on the application of indirect calorimetry (IC) in energy metabolism monitoring based on the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system. This consensus proposes 11 clinical questions and 15 recommendations covering clinical scenarios including critically ill patients, obesity and metabolic diseases, chronic diseases (cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, respiratory and hepatic diseases), malignant tumors, burns and trauma, as well as special populations (pregnant and lactating women, neonates). The consensus emphasizes that IC serves as an important reference method for assessing resting energy expenditure. In critically ill and burn or trauma patients, IC helps more accurately determine individual energy requirements and reduce the risks of underfeeding or overfeeding. In patients with chronic diseases, obesity, malignant tumors, pregnancy, and neonates, IC is mainly used to improve the individualization of energy requirement assessment; its impact on clinical endpoints (such as mortality and length of stay) remains to be confirmed by further high-quality studies. It also suggests alternative methods that when IC is unavailable. This consensus aims to provide evidence-based guidance for clinicians to apply indirect calorimetry rationally and standardly, thereby promoting precision in nutritional support therapy.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Consensus Statement; English Abstract

Title: [Clinical implementation pathway and standardized measures for the "five prescriptions" in the treatment of adult obesity in China].
Abstract: The prevalence of overweight and obesity continues to increase globally. Obesity is a chronic, relapsing disease and a major risk factor for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and several malignancies. Drawing on current guidelines, expert consensus statements, systematic reviews, and pivotal randomized trials, this article proposes an integrated framework of five prescriptions for Chinese adults with obesity: nutrition, exercise, mental health and behavioral care, smoking cessation and alcohol restriction, and pharmacotherapy. Implementation begins with comprehensive assessment and risk stratification. Nutrition and exercise form the foundation, while mental health and behavioral support connect the interventions, sleep is managed through a stratified pathway. Smoking cessation and alcohol restriction support long-term risk reduction, and pharmacotherapy provides evidence-based intensification for eligible patients. This framework translates complex, long-term, relapse-prone obesity care into a standardized pathway that is assessable, prescribable, actionable, monitorable, iterative, and sustainable.

Title: Interpretable multimodal network analysis of lipid-lowering therapies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Multimodal integration of clinical and omics data could clarify the hepatic mechanisms of lipid-lowering therapies, but interpretable methods for heterogeneous data remain limited. The objective was to apply interpretable multimodal networks (IMNs), a topology-aware framework that condenses heterogeneous omics and clinical data into compact, cross-modal modules, to characterize treatment-specific hepatic responses to simvastatin and ezetimibe.
EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: In the Stockholm Study, patients scheduled for cholecystectomy were randomized for 4 weeks to simvastatin, ezetimibe, their combination or placebo. We integrated liver transcriptomics and DNA methylation with plasma/bile biochemistry, including lipoprotein functionality, on the human protein-protein interactome to build treatment-specific IMNs and evaluated selected network-derived predictions in a human hepatocyte-like model (SOAT2-only-HepG2).
KEY RESULTS: IMNs reduced dimensionality while preserving network topology, producing distinct molecular signatures for simvastatin, ezetimibe and combination therapy that mapped to different biological processes; the placebo network was less multimodal and more fragmented. IMNs highlighted apolipoprotein-centred modules and predicted drug effects on APOA2, PPARA and PTPRS, linked to plasma C-peptide. In SOAT2-only-HepG2 cells, selected predictions were supported experimentally, including APOA2 induction and ezetimibe-associated PTPRS upregulation.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: IMNs provide a practical, interactome-based route from multimodal patient data to focused, testable hypotheses about lipid-lowering therapies, yielding compact features suitable for downstream predictive modelling while retaining biological interpretability.

Title: Long-Term Outcomes After Coronary Absorb BVS Implantation Guided by Intravascular Imaging.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery implantation of the absorb bioresorbable vascular scaffold (BVS) without intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance resulted in greater adverse events compared with metallic drug-eluting stents during 3-year follow-up.
AIMS: We assessed the 10-year outcomes of BVS implanted with routine use of IVI guidance.
METHODS: Between November 2014 and October 2016, 100 consecutive patients in whom the operator elected to implant a BVS were treated with 190 BVS devices in 171 lesions at a single center in Brazil. IVI was performed before and after BVS implantation in all patients. Clinical follow-up was complete in all patients (no losses to follow-up) for at least 8.8 years.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 9.5 years (25th percentile 9.2, 75th percentile 10.1), range 8.8-10.8 years. Through the latest follow-up, no patient experienced a cardiac death or definite scaffold thrombosis, and only one patient had a target-vessel MI (TVMI). Major adverse cardiac events (the composite of all-cause death, any MI, or any revascularization) occurred in 29 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimated 10-year rate 29.4%); target vessel failure (TVF) (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization) occurred in 15 patients (10-year rate 15.0%); and target lesion failure (the composite of cardiac death, TVMI, or ischemia-driven target-lesion revascularization) occurred in 10 patients (10-year rate 10.0%). In the landmark analysis, TVF between 3 and 10 years occurred in 7 patients (7.6%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center, non-randomized observational study, the long-term outcomes of BVS implantation in simple and complex coronary lesions with routine IVI guidance were favorable. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in adequately powered randomized studies.

Title: Risk Stratification of Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma: Predictive Value of First-Year Biomarker Trajectories Identified by Group-Based Trajectory Modeling.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple myeloma (MM) exhibits significant heterogeneity. Traditional risk stratification often relies on static baseline data, failing to capture the dynamic evolution of biomarkers. This study aimed to develop a prognostic model incorporating longitudinal biomarker trajectories to improve risk stratification for newly diagnosed MM patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 635 patients from West China Hospital between February 1, 2017 and December 30, 2022. Biomarkers including M protein, free light chains (FLC), creatinine (Cr), hemoglobin (Hb), immunoglobulin levels, and others were collected monthly within the first-year post-treatment. Patients were randomly divided into an internal training (70%) and validation (30%) cohort. Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) and Kaplan-Meier analysis were used to identify distinct biomarker evolution patterns, and the GBTM risk model was validated by the lowest mean squared error (LMSE) method. Cox regression analysis and a nomogram were employed to develop a prognostic model to provide individualized survival probability estimates and were validated in the internal validation cohort using time-dependent ROC analysis.
RESULTS: GBTM identified dFLC, IgM, Cr, and Hb trajectories as significant prognostic factors. Patients scoring ≥ 3 (high-risk) showed significantly poorer overall survival than those scoring < 3 (low-risk) in both the training (median OS 32.2 months vs. not reached, p < 0.0001) and validation cohorts (36.8 months vs. not reached, p < 0.005). Then we established a nomogram that included the GBTM risk group, ISS stage, age, frontline treatment, pulmonary disease, cardiovascular disease, and thrombotic events. The nomogram demonstrated good predictive performance with AUC values consistently above 0.7 for 2- and 3-year survival in both cohorts (Training: 0.71, 0.70; Validation: 0.70, 0.70).
CONCLUSION: Our study successfully developed a prognostic risk stratification model for MM patients using biomarker trajectories. This model may help identify high-risk patients and predict long-term survival, offering a valuable tool for personalized treatment planning.

Title: Structural Damage of Coronary Microcatheters During Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Interventions: The Prospective Multicenter Cross Registry.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microcatheters are essential in chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but their structural failure has mainly been described through passive surveillance.
AIMS: We aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and procedural impact of microcatheter structural damage during contemporary CTO PCI.
METHODS: The prospective multicentre CROSS registry included 2137 CTO PCI procedures performed at high-volume centers between 2024 and 2025. Suspected damaged microcatheters underwent centralized assessment and were classified as grade 1 (superficial deformation), grade 2 (significant deformation without complete fracture), or grade 3 (complete fracture).
RESULTS: Structural damage occurred in 109 procedures (5.1%); 58.7%, 5.5%, and 35.8% were grade 1, 2, and 3, respectively. Independent predictors of structural microcatheter damage were moderate-to-severe calcification (adjusted OR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.27-2.94), retrograde approach (adjusted OR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10-2.67), moderate-to-severe tortuosity (adjusted OR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.04-2.50), and longer procedure duration (adjusted OR per 30-min increase, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30). Structural damage was associated with increased periprocedural complications (25.7% vs. 7.7%; OR: 4.12, 95% CI: 2.60-6.52; p < 0.0001) and failed CTO PCI (11.0% vs. 3.1%; OR: 3.86, 95% CI: 2.01-7.39; p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: Structural microcatheter damage occurred in approximately 1 in 20 CTO PCIs and was associated with anatomical complexity, demanding procedural circumstances, and substantially worse procedural outcomes.

Title: Optimizing AI-Derived CAC Volume Thresholds on Non-Gated Chest CT for Detection of Actionable Coronary Artery Calcium: A Validation Against Agatston Scoring and Radiologist Reporting.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) visually estimated on non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated chest CTs is reported inconsistently, limiting identification of high-risk individuals. Although automated AI-derived CAC scoring offers the potential to standardize reporting and improve reliability, this method warrants rigorous validation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three hundred thirty-two patients (59% female, median age 62) who underwent a non-gated chest CT within 1-year of a dedicated cardiac CT with Agatston's CAC score (CACscore) were identified between 2016 and 2022. AI-Rad Companion (Siemens) was used to compute CAC volume (AI-CACvol). AI-CACvol performance was compared with radiologists' qualitative CAC reports (H-CACqual) using optimized thresholds for identifying actionable CAC. Model performance was further validated in a postimplementation population.
RESULTS: Median AI-CACvol was 20.3 mm³ (IQR 0-188.65), strongly correlated with CACscore (Spearman ρ=0.91, 95% CI: 0.88-0.94); median 31.55 Agatston Units (AU), IQR: 0 to 250). Agreement with CACscore was higher for AI-CACvol versus H-CACqual (weighted kappa 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84, 0.91; vs. 0.85, 95% CI: 0.82, 0.88; P=0.022). At a cutoff of 70 mm³, AI-CACvol demonstrated superior sensitivity compared with H-CACqual for detecting CAC≥100 AU, with greater sensitivity (95% vs. 75%) and comparable specificity (92% vs. 94%). In a validation cohort of 39 patients (64% female, median age 67 y), median CACscore was 43 AU (IQR 0-215) and median AI-CACvol 29.7 mm³ (IQR: 0 to 219.4). The same 70 mm³ cutoff achieved 100% sensitivity and 88% specificity for CAC≥100 AU (n=13).
CONCLUSION: AI-derived CAC volume from non-gated chest CTs correlates strongly with reference CAC scores, showing high sensitivity at actionable thresholds. This supports potential opportunistic screening, though impact on outcomes requires study.

Title: Effects of umbilical cord milking versus delayed cord clamping on cerebral oxygenation and ductus arteriosus closure in preterm infants: RCT.
Abstract: BackgroundDelayed cord clamping (DCC) and umbilical cord milking (UCM) are placental transfusion techniques that improve oxygen delivery and cardiac output. UCM enhances cerebral oxygenation without delaying resuscitation. Functional closure of the ductus arteriosus (DA) usually occurs within 48 hours after birth in full-term infants, with a high incidence of persistent DA in premature infants.ObjectiveTo investigate the effects of UCM and DCC on functional ductus arteriosus closure and cerebral tissue oxygenation.MethodsThis randomized controlled clinical trial included 100 preterm infants who were allocated to either the UCM group (n = 50) or the DCC group (n = 50). crSO2 and cfTOE were measured after resuscitation and at 12, 24, and 48 hours of life. Echocardiography was performed at 6, 12, 18, 24, and 48 hours of life to assess functional DA closure.ResultsRepeated-measures analysis showed no statistically significant between-group differences in changes in crSO2 (P = 0.194), cfTOE (P = 0.140), or functional DA closure (P = 0.372).ConclusionUCM and 60-second DCC showed no statistically significant differences in cerebral tissue oxygenation improvement or functional ductus arteriosus closure during the first 48 hours of life.

Title: Smoking cessation duration and risk of acute myocardial infarction: A nationwide cohort study in Korea.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While smoking cessation reduces cardiovascular risk, the precise timeline and temporal dynamics of risk reduction using granular time intervals remain poorly characterized. We aimed to estimate the association between smoking cessation duration and cardiovascular risk using 2-year intervals in a large Asian cohort.
DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: South Korea, using the nationwide National Health Insurance Service database (2002-2023).
PARTICIPANTS: 1 349 545 adults without prior acute myocardial infarction (AMI) or AMI requiring percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) who underwent at least four biennial health examinations, comprising 1 059 469 never smokers, 60 927 quitters and 229 149 current smokers.
MEASUREMENTS: Smoking status was classified from repeated self-reported examinations; quitters were grouped by cessation duration in 2-year intervals up to ≥8 years. Outcomes were incident AMI and AMI requiring PCI, over a mean follow-up of 10.6 years. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic, clinical and lifestyle covariates including pack-years, with current smokers and never smokers as reference groups.
RESULTS: Using current smokers as reference, adjusted HRs decreased progressively with longer cessation duration. Statistically significant risk reduction was evident within 2-3 years [AMI: HR = 0.475, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.403-0.559; AMI requiring PCI: HR = 0.437, 95% CI = 0.359-0.532]. Quitters who maintained cessation for ≥8 years achieved risk levels comparable to never smokers (AMI: HR = 0.396, 95% CI = 0.284-0.552 vs. HR = 0.407, 95% CI = 0.386-0.429; AMI requiring PCI: HR = 0.321, 95% CI = 0.209-0.493 vs. HR = 0.366, 95% CI = 0.343-0.389).
SUMMARY: In a nationwide Korean cohort, the risk of acute myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction requiring percutaneous coronary intervention declined progressively with longer smoking cessation; after 8 or more years of sustained abstinence, risk was no longer distinguishable from that of never-smokers.

Title: Nineteen-year experience with total anomalous pulmonary venous return at a tertiary care hospital in a low- and middle-income country: a single-centre retrospective study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR) is a rare congenital defect requiring surgical correction. Outcomes are influenced by associated anomalies and preoperative pulmonary venous obstruction, which increase morbidity, mortality, and postoperative pulmonary hypertension risk. This study reviews our institutional experience with pediatric TAPVR repair, emphasizing postoperative outcomes and prognostic determinants.
METHODOLOGY: This single-centre retrospective cohort (2006-2024) at Aga Khan University Hospital included pediatric TAPVR patients (< 18 years). Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative data were analyzed. Continuous variables summarized as mean/SD or median/IQR and categorical as frequencies, with appropriate statistical tests applied.
RESULTS: Our cohort included 80 patients (65% male, mean weight 7.6 ± 6.3 kg). Subtypes were supracardiac 43.8%, cardiac 35%, infracardiac 6.3%, and mixed 15%. Mean age at presentation was 20.1 ± 38.5 months, with 55.6 ± 80.5 days to surgery. ASD (86.3%) was most common. Median CPB and cross-clamp times were 90 and 45 min, respectively. Open-chest (23.8%) and extracorporeal support (70%) showed no subtype significance. Median hospital stay was 8 (9) days with CICU stay as 4 (6). Postoperative outcomes included PAH (22.5%), sepsis (18.8%), PVO (6.3%), tracheostomy (7.5%), reoperation (5%) and mortality reported in 17.5% (higher in cardiac TAPVR, p = 0.044). Univariate analysis linked younger age, low weight, TAPVD subtype, postop PVO, and reduced RV function to outcomes; multivariate confirmed only reduced RV function. While preop PVO was significantly associated with postoperative PAH.
CONCLUSION: TAPVR repair yielded favourable outcomes; however vigilant monitoring of RV function and preoperative PVO is essential to improve survival and reduce complications.

Title: Machine learning framework to enhance and automate cardiovascular outpatient triage for patients with atrial fibrillation.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent arrhythmia, placing a substantial burden on the healthcare system. Patients with AF are cared for in a variety of settings, including primary care and cardiovascular (CV) clinics, while some require cardiac electrophysiology (EP) clinics that offer specialized drugs or procedures. Triage of AF referrals to these specific clinics will lead to timely and proper care and reduce inefficiency in the health system. The goal is to develop a machine learning framework to triage the likelihood of patient referrals to EP-directed treatments.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 6,755 patients who were referred to CV with a referral diagnosis of AF. Data encompassed patient demographics, relevant comorbidities, medications, prior procedures, medical notes analyzed using natural language processing (NLP), and Holter monitoring data. A two-stage framework, predicting the necessity for specialized EP care, was developed: the construction of the machine learning model, followed by post-refinement based on established clinical criteria.
RESULTS: The Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) model emerged as the most effective model in the first stage, achieving an area under the curve of 0.77, an accuracy of 72%, a true positive rate (TPR) of 67%, and a false positive rate of 23%. The post-refinement stage further improved TPR to as much as 83%. This framework resulted in increased identification of EP-direct patient care from the current reported 20% to 46%.
CONCLUSIONS: Our framework effectively identifies patients who are likely to require specialized EP care, thereby enhancing the automation of the AF referral triage process and potentially improving efficiency.

Title: Associations between nut and seed intake and non-traditional lipid indices: a cross-sectional study from the isfahan cohort study 2.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Emerging evidence suggests that novel lipid indices may enhance cardiovascular risk prediction beyond conventional measures; however, their associations with dietary factors such as nut and seed consumption remain understudied. This cross-sectional study investigated associations between nut and seed intake and novel lipid indices among Iranian adults.
METHODS: Using baseline data from 2514 participants in the Isfahan Cohort Study 2, nut and seed intake were assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Novel lipid indices, including Atherogenic Index of Plasma (AIP), Castelli's Risk Indices (CRI-I/II), Atherogenic Coefficient (AC), Atherogenic Combined Index (ACI), Remnant Lipoprotein Cholesterol (RLPC), Triglycerides to High-density lipoprotein Cholesterol ratio (TG/HDL-C), Lipoprotein Combined Index (LCI), and Non-High-density lipoprotein Cholesterol (NHC) were calculated from fasting blood samples. Multivariable adjusted linear and logistic regression models evaluated relationships across nut and seed intake quartiles.
RESULTS: Participants in the highest quartile of nut and seed intake had significantly lower odds of elevated AIP (odds ratio (OR) = 0.58, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.37-0.92), ACI (OR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.50-0.91), CRI-I (OR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.28-0.75), NHC (OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.54-1.03), LCI (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), and TG/HDL-C (OR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.51-0.95) compared to the lowest quartile after adjustment for potential confounders. The risk reductions for RLPC, AC, and CRI-II did not consistently reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: This cross-sectional analysis indicated that higher nut and seed intake was associated with favorable lipid profiles. These findings support the potential role of nuts and seeds in cardiovascular health. However, due to the study's observational design, causal relationships cannot be established. Further prospective studies and randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these associations and explain the underlying mechanisms.

Title: Serum vitamin B12, vitamin D, and zinc in type 2 diabetes mellitus and their association with diabetic retinopathy: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Within complications of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a frequent microvascular disorder. Recognizing nutritional and clinical factors modifiable through intervention is crucial for prevention; however, earlier studies reported inconsistent findings on micronutrient levels and their role in DR progression.
METHODS: This case-control study was carried out in ophthalmology clinics of Urmia University of Medical Sciences (Iran) between October 2024 and February 2025, enrolling 140 T2DM patients: 70 with confirmed DR and 70 without. DR severity was graded by a vitreoretinal specialist using the International Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Scale, from mild non-proliferative to proliferative stages. Serum vitamin B12, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and zinc were classified as deficient, insufficient, or sufficient. Demographic (age, sex), clinical (weight, BMI, blood pressure, diabetes duration, insulin use, physical activity), and biochemical parameters (fasting blood sugar, creatinine) were collected. Statistical analyses were performed using chi-square, linear-by-linear association, and binary logistic regression to account for possible confounders.
RESULTS: Patients with DR had reduced serum vitamin B12 levels compared with control subjects (p < 0.001), and this association persisted after adjustment. Longer diabetes duration, higher creatinine, insulin therapy, and lower physical activity were also significantly associated with DR. Zinc status reached significance only in categorical chi-square analysis, while vitamin D showed no difference.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower vitamin B12, longer diabetes duration, insulin therapy, and reduced physical activity were independently associated with DR. Routine B12 monitoring and managing these modifiable risks may help prevent DR. Larger prospective studies with additional biomarkers and sex-specific analyses are needed.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical trial number: Not applicable. This study was observational in design and did not require clinical trial registration.

Title: Skeletal muscle quality as an independent associated factor of oxygen utilization efficiency in interstitial lung disease: a cardiopulmonary exercise testing study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) is associated with poor prognosis. Oxygen pulse (O2 pulse) reflects exercise circulatory efficiency, but its determinants at submaximal exercise remain unclear. Phase angle (PhA) has recently emerged as a surrogate marker of muscle quality.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between lower-limb PhA and submaximal O2 pulse at the ventilatory threshold (VT), which reflects daily physical activity independent of maximal volitional effort, in patients with ILD.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 111 patients with ILD enrolled in an educational hospitalization program (April 2024-March 2026). Among these, 35 patients completed cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Lower-limb PhA was assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis. The association between PhA and O2 pulse at VT was evaluated using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis adjusted for age, %FVC, and tricuspid regurgitation velocity (TRV).
RESULTS: The analyzed CPET sub-cohort (n = 35) had a mean age of 69.0 ± 8.4 years, 74.2% male, and %FVC of 85.3 ± 18.1%. Lower-limb PhA was significantly correlated with O2 pulse at VT (r = 0.629, p < 0.001). In multiple regression analysis, PhA remained independently associated with O2 pulse (β = 0.748, p = 0.001), with a model R2 of 0.433.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower-limb PhA is an independent associated factor of O2 pulse in patients with mild-to-moderate ILD. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective nature of this study, these findings do not establish causality but suggest that muscle quality may be a relevant clinical indicator that warrants further prospective and interventional investigation.

Title: Association between ankle-brachial index and body composition parameters measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis in patients with high-risk type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a common macrovascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) associated with substantial morbidity. The ankle-brachial index (ABI) is a simple, non-invasive, and widely recommended tool for PAD screening, while alterations in body composition may influence cardiovascular risk. This study investigated the association between bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-derived body composition parameters and ABI in patients with T2DM.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 100 high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus attending a tertiary diabetes clinic were consecutively recruited between December 2024 and December 2025. Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) was assessed using the ankle-brachial index (ABI), and body composition was measured by multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were also collected. Comparisons of body composition parameters across ABI categories were performed using non-parametric tests. Multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the independent associations of representative body composition parameters with PAD after assessment of multicollinearity. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, with p-Value < 0.05 considered statistically significant. All analyses were conducted using R statistical software for Windows (v 4.5.2, R Core Team 2025).
RESULTS: Body composition parameters did not differ significantly across ABI categories (p-Value > 0.05). Patients with PAD had lower HDL-C and higher TSH levels than those without PAD (p-Value = 0.02 and p-Value = 0.01, respectively). In separate multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and hypertension, neither muscle mass nor visceral fat area showed an independent association with PAD.
CONCLUSION: Representative BIA-derived body composition parameters showed no independent association with PAD in high-risk patients with T2DM. Given the limited number of PAD events, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger, adequately powered prospective studies.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Comorbidities in individuals with intellectual disabilities with and without hearing loss: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both intellectual disability (ID) and hearing loss (HL) are associated with a high prevalence of certain comorbidities. However, a combined analysis and overview classified according to the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11), is lacking. HL is disproportionately common among individuals with ID and often remains undetected. We evaluated: (1) which comorbidities are most common in ID; (2) how disease prevalence differs between those with and without HL; (3) whether the degree of ID or HL influences the number of additional diseases, surgeries, or medication intake.
METHODS: This study is part of a prospective cohort study investigating effectiveness and feasibility of repeated universal hearing screenings and interventions for people with ID. We included 1,053 participants with ID (37% female, 63% male, and < 1% intersex; age range 1-90 years). Medical history assessment and on-site hearing testing were combined. Diseases were ICD-11-coded. Descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression models assessed associations between common diseases and age, sex, HL, and ID.
RESULTS: Nearly all comorbidities observed in participants with HL (prevalence > 5% [= 14]) were more frequent in participants with HL vs. without (13/14), eight showing odds ratios [OR] and 95% confidence interval [CI] > 1: visual impairment; hypertension; trisomy 21; obesity; mental, behavioural, or neurodevelopmental disorders; spinal conditions; diabetes; hypothyroidism. Logistic regression underscored associations between: (1) HL and visual impairment, trisomy 21, spinal conditions, hypothyroidism; (2) age and hypertension, obesity, diabetes; (3) female sex and trisomy 21, hypothyroidism. Epilepsy occurred similarly (OR 1.01, 95% CI: 0.65-1.56) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) less often in the HL-subcohort (OR 0.42, 95% CI: 0.24-0.73). Trisomy 21 was 3-4 times more frequent in the HL-subcohort, showed a female preponderance and high rates of cardiovascular, metabolic, and visual diseases. Associated comorbidities (mean 2.75 vs 1.65) and multimorbidity (≥ two diseases, 63% vs. 42%) were higher in persons with HL than without, as was medication intake (mean 2.73 vs. 0.84).
CONCLUSION: In our study individuals with ID and HL showed increased comorbidity, multimorbidity, and higher medication intake than those without HL. Heightened awareness and individualised, multidisciplinary management are essential in order to ensure equitable care and prevent secondary complications.

Title: Participant attrition in a multi-regional population-based study in Africa: insights from the AWI-Gen study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attrition in longitudinal studies, defined as the loss of participants over time, may threaten the validity of study results. This study examined patterns, magnitude, and risk factors for attrition in the AWI-Gen cohort.
METHODS: The study included 12,032 participants from six African sites, with a median baseline age of 51 years (IQR: 45-57 years). Exploratory data analysis was conducted to examine attrition patterns and magnitude, and fixed-effects logistic regression models were used to identify significant factors associated with different causes of attrition (all-cause, non-death vs death, preventable vs non-preventable) while accounting for site-specific variation. Sensitivity analyses, including Bonferroni adjustments, imputation, and site-specific analyses, were used to assess model robustness. Model goodness-of-fit was evaluated, and adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were reported, with a significance threshold of p < 0.05.
RESULTS: After five years, AWI-Gen experienced 40% attrition. Causes included being unreachable by cell phone (42.6%), refusal (26.0%), death (13.9%), relocation (10.5%), and being recorded as too ill to participate (3.9%), with variations across sites. Male sex and lower socioeconomic status were consistently associated with increased odds across attrition outcomes, while older age, tobacco use, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease were additionally associated with death-related and non-preventable attrition.
CONCLUSION: This study underscores the importance of reporting attrition causes for consistency in longitudinal research. Male participants, individuals of lower socioeconomic status, older adults, tobacco users, and those living with chronic conditions such as hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease were at increased risk of attrition. Tailored retention strategies, including enhanced participant tracing and communication, targeted engagement of men and socioeconomically disadvantaged groups, regular contact with older participants, and integration of follow-up activities with chronic disease management services, may improve participant retention and help preserve the validity of longitudinal research.

Title: CURB-65 score for predicting deep vein thrombosis in severe community-acquired pneumonia: a cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe community-acquired pneumonia (SCAP) are at significantly increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Traditional VTE risk assessment tools like the Caprini and Padua prediction scores are often underutilized in acute care settings due to their complexity. The CURB-65 score, a routine severity assessment tool for pneumonia, may offer a simplified and integrated approach for VTE risk stratification, but its predictive value for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in SCAP patients requires validation.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 766 adults with SCAP admitted to Beijing Chao-Yang Hospital between January 1, 2015 and August 31, 2024. Baseline characteristics, CURB-65, Caprini, and Padua prediction scores, VTE prophylaxis details, and the occurrence of ultrasound confirmed in-hospital DVT were collected. Multivariable logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors for DVT. We further performed a sensitivity analysis restricted to proximal DVT. The predictive performance of the scores was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Patients were stratified into low-risk (CURB-65 < 3) and high-risk (CURB-65 ≥ 3) groups for further analysis, including Kaplan-Meier survival analysis to compare cumulative DVT incidence. A separate multivariable analysis was conducted in the subgroup of patients who received VTE prophylaxis.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of DVT was 30.3% (232/766), with the clinically actionable proximal DVT accounting for 3.0% (23/766) and distal DVT comprising 27.3% (209/766). Multivariable analysis identified a higher CURB-65 score as an independent predictor of DVT (adjusted Odds Ratio [OR] = 1.936, 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.503-2.495, P < 0.001). The sensitivity analysis limited to proximal DVT demonstrated that CURB-65 remained an independent predictor (adjusted OR = 1.759, 95%CI:1.431-2.162, P < 0.001). The predictive performance of the CURB-65 score (AUC = 0.717, 95% CI: 0.684-0.749) was statistically higher than that of the Caprini prediction score (AUC = 0.648; raw P = 0.002 for these two curves) and comparable to the Padua prediction score (AUC = 0.680; raw P = 0.052 for these two curves). The high-risk group (CURB-65 ≥ 3, n = 391) had a significantly higher DVT incidence (47.3%) compared to the low-risk group (12.5%, P < 0.001), with Kaplan-Meier curves confirming a higher cumulative incidence (Log-rank P < 0.001). In the prophylaxis subgroup (n = 626), the CURB-65 score remained an independent risk factor for DVT (adjusted OR = 1.953, 95% CI: 1.488-2.562, P < 0.001), and the overall DVT incidence was 30.8% (193/626).
CONCLUSION: The CURB-65 score shows moderate performance in predicting DVT risk among SCAP patients, and retains stable predictive capacity for clinically critical proximal DVT, with discriminative capacity comparable to dedicated VTE assessment tools, though all three scoring systems deliver only fair-to-moderate discrimination. Routine calculation at admission may provide auxiliary clues to preliminarily screen patients with elevated residual DVT risk and facilitate risk-stratified monitoring and individualized thromboprophylaxis. Patients with CURB-65 ≥ 3 remain at substantial residual DVT risk despite standard prophylaxis, supporting the need for future research to optimize preventive strategies in this high-risk population. In addition to pneumonia severity assessment, the CURB-65 score may serve as a convenient auxiliary marker for DVT risk stratification.

Title: Woodhouse-Sakati syndrome presenting with progressive dystonia and white matter disease: a case report and literature review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Woodhouse-Sakati syndrome (WSS) is a rare autosomal recessive multisystem disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in DCAF17. It is associated with variable neurological, endocrine, and ectodermal manifestations. This article aims to describe a genetically confirmed case of WSS and to review the neurological and neuroimaging features reported in the literature.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 30-year-old Saudi Arabian male with a 13-year history of progressive hoarseness and dysarthria, followed by jaw protrusion, painful oromandibular spasms, impaired chewing, craniocervical and oromandibular dystonia, mild spastic paraparesis, bilateral lower limb dystonia, and a spastic dystonic gait. Brain MRI showed stable periventricular and subcortical white matter lesions without spinal cord involvement. Whole exome sequencing identified a homozygous pathogenic frameshift variant in DCAF17, c.436del, p.(Ala147Hisfs*9), confirming WSS. The literature review identified 249 individuals from 46 published articles and the present case. Cognitive impairment was the most frequently reported neurological manifestation (63.85%), followed by hearing impairment (46.98%) and movement disorders (46.98%). Dystonia was the predominant movement disorder phenotype, reported in 45.38% of the total reported cohort. Neuroimaging data were available for 197 individuals. Among them, markers of possible iron deposition were the most frequently reported abnormality, present in 40.60% of patients when explicitly reported iron deposition and T2 hypointensity involving deep gray or brainstem structures were considered together. White matter changes were reported in 38.57%, followed by pituitary atrophy or hypoplasia in 35.02%.
CONCLUSION: WSS should be considered in young adults with progressive craniocervical or oromandibular dystonia, dysarthria, endocrine abnormalities, alopecia, characteristic craniofacial features, and white matter lesions. The accompanying literature review reinforces the broad neurological and neuroimaging spectrum of WSS, with dystonia representing the predominant movement disorder phenotype. Recognition of the broader syndromic pattern, supported by molecular confirmation of DCAF17 pathogenic variants, is essential to establish the diagnosis and guide family evaluation.

Title: Circadian rhythm dysregulation and brain functional connectivity alterations in stroke patients: an exploratory study of peripheral and central clock interactions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The human circadian rhythm system is governed by a transcriptional-translational feedback loop of clock genes, including Bmal1, which exhibits a near-24-hour oscillatory period. Emerging evidence highlights the critical contribution of circadian genes to stroke pathogenesis and outcomes, yet mechanistic insights into their regulatory roles remain limited. To bridge this knowledge gap, we aimed to determine whether the serum of stroke patients could affect changes in the molecular clock and whether such changes in the molecular clock were potentially linked to abnormal brain functional connectivity in stroke patients.
METHODS: This prospective case-control study included 17 patients with stroke and 17 age-matched healthy participants. All participants were required to complete a standardized comprehensive questionnaire. Transfected human osteosarcoma cells (U2OS) stably expressing Bmal1-dluc reporters were treated with serum from both groups to monitor changes in the daily oscillation period of Bmal1. We also compared the changes in resting-state hypothalamic intrinsic functional connectivity(FC) between the two groups. Further, we explored the correlation between the differences in FC between the two groups and the daily oscillation period of Bmal1.
RESULTS: Compared to the healthy control group, stroke patients exhibited a significantly prolonged peripheral Bmal1 circadian oscillation period (24.32 ± 0.41 h vs. 23.81 ± 0.48 h, t = 3.352, p = 0.002). In FC analysis, the stroke group showed enhanced connectivity from the hypothalamus to the right occipital lobe and the right insular region. Notably, the degree of this connectivity enhancement demonstrated a significant positive correlation with the length of Bmal1 oscillation period (r = 0.369, p = 0.032; r = 0.393, p = 0.022).
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that serum from stroke patients lengthens the circadian period in U2OS cells and may be associated with alterations in brain functional connectivity. However, the small sample size limits statistical power, and these exploratory results require replication in larger independent cohorts.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2000031671(April 4, 2020).

Title: Assessing mortality risk in colorectal cancer survivors with congestive heart failure: a cohort study from the Taiwan Cancer Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The rising incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) and cardiovascular diseases, driven by aging populations and lifestyle changes, highlights congestive heart failure (CHF) as a critical comorbidity that significantly affects survival and treatment decisions in CRC patients. CHF not only affects survival outcomes but also complicates clinical decision-making. This study aims to investigate the impact of CHF on mortality among CRC survivors and explore potential factors of mortality.
METHODS: This cohort study analyzed data from the Taiwan Cancer Registry and National Health Insurance Research Database. CRC patients aged 20 years or older (ICD-10-CM: C18-C20) who survived at least five years after diagnosis were included. After a 1:4 exact matching based on age, sex, and clinical stage, Cox regression was used to estimate mortality risk between CRC survivors with and without CHF.
RESULTS: A total of 535 CRC survivors with CHF and 2140 without CHF were enrolled in this study after matching. CRC survivors with CHF had a significantly higher overall mortality rate than those without CHF (36.64% vs. 15.23%, p < 0.001). After adjusting for potential confounders, CRC survivors with CHF had 1.93-folds risk of mortality (95% CI: 1.54-2.41, p < 0.001) compared to those without CHF. Subgroup analyses by sex, age, clinical stage, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and treatment types also show that CRC survivors with CHF had significantly higher mortality risk than those without CHF. The top three highest mortality risk ratios were observed in subgroups with a CCI score of 0 (AHR: 2.63, 95% CI: 1.08-6.39), age < 65 years (AHR: 1.87, 95% CI: 1.23-5.57), and advanced clinical stage (AHR: 2.03, 95% CI: 1.51-2.72).
CONCLUSION: CRC survivors with CHF demonstrated significantly higher overall mortality compared to those without CHF. This finding presented the prognostic impact of CHF in CRC survivors, so integrated care and early cardiovascular monitoring are essential to improve long-term outcomes.

Title: Early postoperative prediction of gastrointestinal bleeding after surgery for acute type A aortic dissection: a five-variable logistic regression model benchmarked against machine learning.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding is a clinically important complication after emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection. Dedicated postoperative risk-stratification tools for this high-risk population remain limited. We aimed to develop and internally validate an early postoperative prediction model for gastrointestinal bleeding after acute type A aortic dissection repair and to compare logistic regression with commonly used machine-learning classifiers.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of 1,345 consecutive patients who underwent emergency acute type A aortic dissection repair between 5 December 2017 and 4 August 2022. Comprehensive clinical data, laboratory findings, imaging results, operative variables, transfusion data, and postoperative outcomes were collected. The cohort was divided into training and validation sets at a 70:30 ratio using stratified sampling. Candidate predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression, and a clinically interpretable five-variable logistic regression model was developed. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, repeated-split analysis, temporal validation, and comparison with tuned machine-learning classifiers.
RESULTS: Overall, 108 patients (8.0%) developed postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding, which was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (26.9% vs. 8.2%; p < 0.001). The final model included red blood cell transfusion volume, lactate, cardiac troponin I, coronary artery disease, and continuous renal replacement therapy. The logistic regression model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.834 in the training set and 0.832 in the validation set, with a validation Brier score of 0.061. Calibration estimates were imprecise, supporting local recalibration before implementation. Temporal validation showed a test area under the curve of 0.869. Tuned machine-learning classifiers showed similar discrimination but no clinically meaningful advantage in calibration, decision-curve performance, or interpretability.
CONCLUSIONS: A five-variable logistic regression model provided stable and clinically interpretable early postoperative risk stratification for gastrointestinal bleeding after acute type A aortic dissection repair. In this structured, low-event clinical dataset, machine-learning classifiers did not materially outperform a transparent regression model. External multicentre validation and local recalibration remain warranted before routine clinical implementation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Validation Study; Comparative Study

Title: Effectiveness of telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation programs have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional center-based rehabilitation, offering improved accessibility and convenience for patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This review aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation in improving clinical outcomes in this population.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE, EMBASE, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and the Cochrane Library from July 2012 to June 2024. Randomized controlled trials and non-randomized studies evaluating telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation after PCI were included. Outcomes assessed included exercise capacity, blood pressure, body mass index (BMI), quality of life, smoking cessation, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction, and mortality. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed using standardized mean differences (SMDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. Telehealth-based interventions significantly improved exercise capacity (SMD = 0.703, 95% CI: 0.382-1.023; p < 0.001) and quality of life (SMD = 0.529, 95% CI: 0.232-0.826; p < 0.001). No statistically significant effects were observed for blood pressure, BMI, smoking cessation, myocardial infarction, or mortality. A potentially clinically important but statistically non-significant trend toward reduced MACE was observed (RR = 0.487, 95% CI: 0.233-1.019; p = 0.056). Although the point estimate corresponds to an approximately 51% relative risk reduction, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because only four studies contributed to the analysis, the confidence interval crossed the null value, and MACE definitions varied across studies.
CONCLUSION: Telehealth-based cardiac rehabilitation improves exercise capacity and quality of life in patients undergoing PCI. A potentially clinically important trend toward reduced MACE was also observed, although this finding remains uncertain because of the limited number of contributing studies, wide confidence interval, and variability in MACE definitions. Evidence for other cardiovascular risk factors and clinical endpoints remains limited. Further adequately powered randomized controlled trials with standardized interventions, outcome definitions, and longer follow-up are required.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ID: CRD420261287216.

Title: Body mass index is positively associated with cardiovascular risk measured by non-invasive cardiovascular parameters: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epidemiological studies on body mass index (BMI) and novel non-invasive cardiovascular parameters that measure cardiovascular risk are limited and inconsistent, particularly for rural U.S. adults. To provide more informative data for further prevention and control, we examined associations between BMI, as well as overweight/obesity, and non-invasive cardiovascular parameters and their dose-response relationships in adults from the rural Appalachian Region of North Carolina.
METHODS: A total of 71 participants were included in this cross-sectional analysis.
