Non-invasive cardiovascular parameters included carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity for measuring central arterial stiffness, augmentation index at 75 bpm for gauging peripheral arterial stiffness, ejection time for indicating left ventricular performance, and Buckberg index for measuring coronary microvascular circulation. When most cardiovascular values were below clinical cutoff points, variables were dichotomized at the sample median to facilitate direct clinical and practical decision-making. Penalized logistic regression models were used as a primary analysis.
RESULTS: Every unit (kg/m2) increase in BMI was associated with 21% statistically significant increased multivariable-adjusted odds of higher central arterial stiffness (odds ratio: 1.21; 95% confidence interval: 1.04-1.46), and 19% statistically significant increased adjusted odds of worse coronary microvascular circulation. Overweight/obesity was associated with 447% statistically significant increased odds of higher arterial stiffness (5.47; 1.62-22.46), and 408% statistically significant increased odds of worse left ventricular performance after adjusting for age, sex, and physical activity.
CONCLUSION: Increased BMI, especially overweight/obesity, was significantly associated with an increased risk of worse cardiovascular health, as measured by non-invasive cardiovascular parameters. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the small sample size and potential instability of estimates. Further studies in larger, adequately powered prospective cohorts are needed to confirm these relationships and clarify their clinical relevance.

Title: Upgrading right ventricular pacing to left bundle branch area pacing in pacemaker-induced cardiomyopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic right ventricular pacing (RVP) causes pacemaker-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) in 10-20% of patients. Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) restores His-Purkinje activation and offers an alternative upgrade strategy; however, no formal pooled analysis comparing LBBAP versus biventricular pacing (BiVP) exists.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus from inception to March 2026, and pooled effect sizes using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) methods. Nine studies contributed to the single-arm meta-analysis; one further study (Huang et al.) provided comparative LBBAP-versus-BiVP data only. Full database-specific search strategies are provided in Supplemental Text S1.
RESULTS: Nine observational studies (N = 242) were eligible. LBBAP succeeded in 96.4% of the procedures (95% CI 92.2-99.3%). Pooled left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improved by 11.72% points (95% CI + 9.85 to + 13.59), paced QRS narrowed by 51.83 ms, left ventricular end diastolic diameter (LVEDD) decreased by 4.10 mm (k = 5), and NYHA improved by 0.98 points (all p < 0.001). Three non-fatal device-related complications were recorded across 242 patients (pooled rate 1.8%). In two observational head-to-head studies (N = 170) - one of which (Huang et al.) contributed comparative data only and is not among the nine single-arm studies - LBBAP was associated with a 4.59%-point greater LVEF improvement than BiVP (95% CI + 2.23 to + 6.95); with only two nonrandomized studies, this comparison is hypothesis-generating. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the single-arm estimates.
CONCLUSION: LBBAP upgrade was associated with improvement in LVEF and symptoms in patients with PICM. Limited observational data suggest greater LVEF improvement with LBBAP than BiVP, but this finding remains hypothesis-generating. Adequately powered randomized trials with hard clinical endpoints are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261381943) after the search but before data extraction: Upgrading right ventricular pacing to left bundle branch area pacing in pacemaker-induced cardiomyopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

Title: Combined predictive value of triglyceride-glucose index and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio for carotid plaque in a physical examination population: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid atherosclerosis is a major precursor of ischemic stroke and adverse cardiovascular events. Conventional imaging and risk stratification tools are limited by cost, accessibility, or low predictive accuracy for subclinical disease. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index (a surrogate of insulin resistance) and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (a marker of systemic inflammation) are readily available biomarkers. However, their synergistic value for predicting carotid plaque remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled 837 participants who underwent health examination and carotid ultrasound. Multivariate logistic regression was used to evaluate independent and combined associations of TyG index and NLR with carotid plaque. Restricted cubic spline models were applied to explore nonlinear dose-response relationships. Predictive performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Carotid plaque was present in 328 (39.2%) participants. Plaque patients had significantly higher TyG index and NLR than non-plaque participants (both P < 0.001). In adjusted analysis, high NLR alone or combined with high TyG index was independently associated with elevated carotid plaque risk, whereas high TyG index alone was not. Nonlinear thresholds were identified: plaque risk rose sharply when TyG index > 9.0 or NLR > 2.0. The combined TyG + NLR model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.914, with 85.1% sensitivity and 87.4% specificity, significantly outperforming either marker alone. The model showed excellent calibration and favorable clinical net benefit across a wide threshold range.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated NLR, alone or combined with high TyG index, is a strong risk factor for carotid plaque. The integrated TyG + NLR model provides a highly accurate, non-invasive, and cost-effective tool for early risk stratification of carotid atherosclerosis, supporting large-scale screening and timely intervention in clinical practice.

Title: Association of cumulative SPISE and two-point SPISE patterns with incident cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: a prospective landmark cohort analysis of CHARLS.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-point insulin sensitivity estimation (SPISE) can be calculated from routine metabolic and anthropometric measures, but longitudinal evidence for cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains limited. We examined whether cumulative SPISE and outcome-blind two-point SPISE patterns were associated with incident CVD in middle-aged and older Chinese adults.
METHODS: We performed a 2015-landmark cohort analysis using the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Participants were required to have valid 2011 and 2015 SPISE measurements, be free of CVD during the exposure window, and have post-landmark outcome or death follow-up. Cumulative SPISE was calculated as the mean of the two values multiplied by each participant's actual assessment interval. Cox models with 100 multiple imputations, restricted cubic splines, outcome-blind K-means clustering, subgroup analyses, and prespecified sensitivity analyses were used.
RESULTS: Among 4,737 participants, 893 incident CVD events occurred during a median 5.0 years of post-landmark follow-up. In the primary Model 3, each 1-SD higher cumulative SPISE was associated with lower incident CVD (hazard ratio [HR] 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.74-0.86), and the HR for the highest versus lowest quartile was 0.57 (95% CI 0.46-0.69; P for trend < 0.001). The four-knot spline showed an overall association (P < 0.001) without evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.227). K-means selected two SPISE patterns; the higher versus lower SPISE pattern had an adjusted HR of 0.63 (95% CI 0.54-0.73). The main result was directionally consistent in prespecified sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher cumulative SPISE and a higher two-point SPISE pattern were associated with lower subsequent self-reported incident CVD. These observational findings support cumulative SPISE as a longitudinal metabolic exposure for research, while two measurements do not justify causal or trajectory-based conclusions.

Title: Prognostic impact of the right-to-left atrial volume index ratio on mortality and length of stay in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial remodeling is a key mechanism influencing prognosis in cardiovascular diseases [1]. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of the right-to-left atrial volume index ratio (RAVI/LAVI) for 2-month all-cause mortality and length of hospital stay in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective observational study, a total of 267 hospitalized patients were included. Patients were stratified into two groups according to the median RAVI/LAVI ratio (median value = 0.78) (below-median vs. above-median). Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were compared between groups. The primary endpoint was 2-month all-cause mortality after CABG, and the secondary endpoint was length of hospital stay. Predictors of mortality were evaluated using logistic regression analysis.
RESULTS: Mortality was significantly higher in the high RAVI/LAVI group (35.2% vs. 12.8%, p < 0.001), and the length of hospital stay was markedly longer (24.9 days vs. 11.4 days, p < 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the RAVI/LAVI ratio remained an independent predictor of mortality (OR 6.67; 95% CI 1.96-22.73; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: The RAVI/LAVI ratio demonstrates a strong and independent association with mortality and length of hospital stay. This ratio may represent a practical and robust echocardiographic marker for risk stratification in vascular and cardiac patients.

Title: Transthoracic echocardiography as a predictor of spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension in cesarean section: a prospective observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension (SAIH) is a common complication during cesarean delivery and is closely associated with maternal intravascular volume status. However, reliable real-time assessment of volume changes remains challenging. This study aimed to evaluate whether transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived ventricular volume parameters could dynamically reflect peri-anesthetic volume changes and predict SAIH.
METHODS: A total of 100 healthy singleton parturients scheduled for elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia were prospectively enrolled. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) and left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV) were measured by transthoracic echocardiography using the biplane Simpson method at three predefined time points: after admission (T1), after crystalloid fluid preloading (T2), and after stabilization of the sensory block (T3). Systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and heart rate (HR) were recorded simultaneously. SAIH was defined as an SBP < 90 mmHg or a decrease of > 30% from baseline. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of SAIH.
RESULTS: Eighty-four parturients completed the study, and 26 (30.95%) developed SAIH. Following crystalloid fluid preloading at T2, both LVEDV and LVESV increased significantly compared with baseline. At T3, parturients who subsequently developed SAIH exhibited significant reductions in LVEDV and LVESV compared with T2. Multivariable logistic regression identified baseline LVEDV (T1) and LVESV (T1) as independent predictors of SAIH (P = 0.023 and P = 0.010, respectively). The predictive model demonstrated moderate discrimination, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.725 (95% confidence interval, 0.600-0.850).
CONCLUSION: TTE-derived LVEDV and LVESV were associated with peri-anesthetic volume changes and demonstrated moderate ability to identify parturients at risk of SAIH. These findings suggest that bedside TTE may provide complementary information for peri-anesthetic volume assessment rather than serving as a standalone predictor.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100042973). February 2, 2021 (Retrospectively registered).

Title: Predictive value of creatinine muscle index reflecting muscle mass for cardiovascular disease among middle-aged and older adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The creatinine muscle index (CMI, mg/day/1.73 m²) may be an accessible potential indicator for evaluating muscle mass. However, the correlation between CMI and muscle mass has not yet been validated, and its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD) is unclear. We aimed to assess the correlation between CMI and muscle mass and investigate the association of CMI with CVD.
METHODS: Participants aged 45-65 years without CVD from the 2011 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study were included and followed until 2020. CMI was calculated using serum creatinine and cystatin C-estimated glomerular filtration rate. Spearman's correlation was used to assess the relationship between CMI and appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM) estimated via a validated anthropometric prediction equation. Cox proportional hazards regression models and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were employed to analyze the association between CMI and CVD.
RESULTS: Among the 5122 participants, 1100 participants developed CVD. CMI was correlated with ASMM in males (r = 0.60, P < 0.001) and females (r = 0.53, P < 0.001). After adjusting for multiple factors, higher CMI (tertile 3 versus 1) was associated with reduced risks of CVD in males (HR [95% CI]: 0.74 [0.57-0.95]) and females (HR [95% CI]: 0.79 [0.64-0.97]). RCS revealed a linear relationship between CMI and CVD (all P for non-linearity > 0.05). Subgroup analyses showed protective effects of higher CMI (tertile 3) against CVD in participants aged 45-65 years, married individuals, urban residents, and those without kidney disease.
CONCLUSIONS: CMI may serve as a potential surrogate for muscle mass, and elevated CMI levels are independently associated with reduced CVD risk.

Title: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis complicating eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: a case report and narrative review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an uncommon antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and multisystem involvement. Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and myositis are both infrequent manifestations of EGPA, and their co-occurrence in the same patient has rarely been reported.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 46-year-old man with adult-onset asthma, chronic sinusitis, and marked peripheral eosinophilia was diagnosed with EGPA in 2015. Over six years of follow-up, he had recurrent pulmonary relapses with migratory infiltrates and developed gastrointestinal involvement, nondilated cardiomyopathy, coronary artery disease, myositis, and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage; he was positive for myeloperoxidase (MPO)-ANCA. Disease activity persisted despite high-dose glucocorticoids, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, and mycophenolate mofetil. Because the disease was severe, organ-threatening, and predominantly vasculitic, an anti-interleukin-5 agent was not chosen for remission induction; instead, rituximab was started and induced sustained remission.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that refractory, MPO-ANCA-positive EGPA may respond to B-cell depletion with rituximab. The randomized REOVAS trial did not show rituximab to be superior to conventional remission-induction therapy; however, it was not designed to establish equivalence with cyclophosphamide in severe disease, and the optimal strategy for severe refractory disease remains undefined. ANCA status, together with the pattern and severity of organ involvement, may help individualize treatment in this setting.

Title: Oral anticoagulation with or without antiplatelet therapy for secondary stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation and atherosclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: Patients with ischemic stroke (IS), atrial fibrillation (AF), and atherosclerosis have an increased risk of recurrent ischemic events. Addition of antiplatelet therapy (APT) to oral anticoagulant therapy (OAC) may offer additional protection against these events, at the cost of an increased risk of bleeding. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of combined antithrombotic therapy versus OAC alone in this population. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through September 2026 for randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing OAC plus APT versus OAC alone in adults with IS, AF, and atherosclerosis. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251164174). Seven studies (4 retrospective, 2 prospective, 1 randomized trial; n= 9,924) were included. Combined therapy was not associated with a reduction in vascular composite outcome (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.61-1.96), recurrent IS (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.91-1.16), major bleeding (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.86-1.59), or all-cause mortality (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.60-1.36). In the subgroup with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis, combined therapy showed no significant difference in vascular composite risk (HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.83-3.33). Combined antithrombotic therapy with OAC plus APT was not associated with a reduction in recurrent IS, vascular composite outcome, major bleeding, or all-cause mortality in patients with IS, AF, and atherosclerosis. In patients with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis, combined therapy was not associated with a significant difference in the risk of the vascular composite outcome. These findings suggest that the addition of APT to OAC should be approached with caution in this population, and may be best reserved for select clinical contexts.

Title: A Study on the Association Between Frailty and Primary Caregiver Burden Among Elderly Stroke Survivors.
Abstract:
AIM: To investigate the association between multidimensional frailty among elderly stroke survivors and caregiver burden among their primary family caregivers.
DESIGN: A cross-sectional observational study.
METHODS: Elderly stroke survivors and their primary family caregivers were recruited from the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, Luzhou, Sichuan, China, between November 2025 and March 2026. Eligible stroke survivors and their primary caregivers were recruited using convenience sampling from the accessible inpatient population during the study period. Data were collected using a self-designed general demographic questionnaire, the Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI) and the Caregiver Burden Inventory (CBI).
RESULTS: A total of 350 patient-caregiver pairs received questionnaires, and 323 valid paired responses were included in the analysis (effective response rate, 92.29%). The mean total Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI) score was 6.90 ± 4.19, and the mean total Caregiver Burden Inventory (CBI) score was 56.26 ± 16.29. Total TFI scores were positively correlated with total CBI scores (r = 0.647, p < 0.001). In the primary multivariable model, living separately from the patient and providing < 12 h of care per day (vs. > 18 h) were associated with lower caregiver burden, whereas sleeping < 6 h per day (vs. > 8 h) was associated with higher burden. The three frailty dimensions were not statistically significant after adjustment. The primary model explained 79.8% of the variance in caregiver burden (adjusted R2 = 0.792). The expanded sensitivity model had a higher R2 (0.962) but substantial multicollinearity (maximum VIF = 51.86), limiting the interpretability of its individual coefficients. Subgroup analyses were exploratory. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

Title: Utilisation patterns and exploratory short-term outcomes of drug-coated balloon versus drug-eluting stent in percutaneous coronary intervention: a single-centre observational cohort study.
Journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are an established alternative to drug-eluting stents (DESs) for selected coronary lesions, offering the potential advantages of a stent-free strategy while avoiding permanent metallic implantation. This study compared real-world utilisation patterns, clinical outcomes, and patient-reported outcomes following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with DCBs and DESs.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up included 214 consecutive patients who underwent PCI with either a DCB (n = 64) or DES (n = 150) between January 2023 and March 2026. Baseline demographic, angiographic, procedural, and clinical characteristics were compared. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at follow-up using a questionnaire adapted from the domains of the Seattle Angina Questionnaire. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent factors associated with DCB utilisation.
RESULTS: The study included 214 patients (mean age 56.55 ± 11.49 years), of whom 72.9% were male. Clinical presentation differed significantly between groups (p = 0.042), the ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) group more frequently underwent DES (46.0% vs. 29.7%), whereas non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) (37.5% vs. 30.7%) and Unstable Angina​ (UA) (15.6% vs. 6.0%) were more common in the DCB group. DCBs were preferentially used in patients with previous coronary revascularization, ISR, small-vessel disease and elective PCI, whereas DESs were more commonly used for acute PCI, total occlusive lesions, and lesions with calcification or thrombus (all p < 0.05). Previous coronary revascularization was associated with increased odds of DCB use, while acute PCI was associated with reduced odds of DCB use compared with elective PCI. No significant differences were observed between groups in mortality at 1, 3, or 6 months, other early clinical outcomes, or patient-reported outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: DCBs were preferentially used in specific clinical and anatomical settings while demonstrating low observed rates of short-term clinical events and no statistically significant between-group differences in patient-reported outcomes. Despite differences in lesion complexity and treatment selection, no significant differences in early outcomes were observed compared with DES. These findings describe contemporary real-world DCB utilisation in a Sri Lankan PCI centre and provide a basis for further multicentre evaluation.

Title: Category and Modifier Accuracy in a Five-Model Evaluation of Large Language Model Extraction of CAD-RADS 2.0 from Coronary CT Angiography Reports.
Journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
Abstract: This study evaluates large language model (LLM) extraction of Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from coronary CT angiography (CCTA) reports using a guideline-derived specification and examines instruction-related improvement, repeatability, and the limitations of extracting plaque and ischemia modifiers alongside the category. Five LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Copilot) processed 400 deidentified CCTA report entries under unprompted, specified, and repeated-specified conditions. The primary outcome was exact category agreement with a report-derived consensus reference under the specification (n = 400). Secondary outcomes included three-component agreement (n = 396), modifier accuracy, instruction-related changes, and repeatability. Inference used report-text cluster bootstrap and paired or permutation tests with Holm adjustment. For the primary outcome, category accuracy under the specification was 92.8-95.5% (371-382/400); secondary outcomes included run-to-run category agreement of 97.5-98.8%, whereas three-component accuracy was 59.3-81.6% (235-323/396). Among assigned references, plaque accuracy was 79.2-94.0% (236-280/298) and ischemia accuracy 45.1-90.3% (79-158/175). The specification improved category accuracy in four of five models and three-component, plaque, and ischemia accuracy in all five. Models did not differ significantly in category accuracy (Cochran Q = 8.73; adjusted p = 0.077) but differed in three-component accuracy (Q = 116.48; adjusted p < 0.001). Category extraction was accurate under the specification, with improvement in most models and high repeatability. Joint evaluation of category, plaque, and ischemia revealed limitations in modifier extraction. External and prospective validation is needed to develop a reliable clinical tool and establish its value in routine practice.

Title: Opportunistic abdominal aortic calcification assessment on spine radiographs in women with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis: linking cardiovascular burden and femoral neck bone loss.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and osteoporosis are major comorbidities in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). We assessed abdominal aortic calcification (AAC) opportunistically on spine radiographs and examined its associations with CVD, estimated cardiovascular risk, bone mineral density (BMD), and fragility fractures in women with longstanding RA.
METHOD: This cross-sectional study included 196 consecutive women with longstanding RA followed at a tertiary hospital. All underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and conventional spine radiography. AAC was graded using the Kauppila score (KS) and categorized as absent, mild-to-moderate (KS 1-6), or extended (KS > 6). Multivariable models evaluated factors associated with AAC and overt CVD.
RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 62.8 ± 9.6 years and median RA duration of 21 years. AAC was present in 48 women (24.5%), including extended AAC in 25 (12.7%). Overt CVD was documented in 32 participants (16.3%). Extended AAC was independently associated with hypertension (OR 8.57, 95% CI 1.10-67.02), longer RA duration (OR 1.05 per year, 95% CI 1.004-1.09), and lower femoral neck T-score (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.35-0.95). AAC of any severity was associated with overt CVD (OR 2.89, 95% CI 1.26-6.63).
CONCLUSIONS: AAC detected on routine spine radiographs was common among women with longstanding RA and was associated with cardiovascular burden and lower femoral neck BMD. Opportunistic AAC assessment may complement cardiovascular and skeletal risk evaluation in RA. Larger cohorts are needed to confirm these exploratory associations, and prospective studies are needed to establish predictive value.

Title: Timing of pharmacological thromboprophylaxis in severe traumatic brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) presents competing risks of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and intracranial haemorrhage progression, rendering pharmacological thromboprophylaxis (PTP) timing uniquely contentious. The dilemma is most acute in severe TBI, where both risks are greatest. This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD420261388300) evaluates early versus late PTP on VTE, intracranial haemorrhage progression, and mortality in adults with severe TBI, applying a strict severity definition (Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 8 or less in 100% of the analysed cohort) to confirm and refine findings from prior mixed-severity syntheses.
METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 1 May 2026. Studies enrolling adults with severe TBI (GCS 8 or less throughout analysed cohort) were eligible. Primary outcomes were VTE, intracranial haemorrhage progression, and in-hospital mortality. Definitions of VTE, and timing thresholds for early and late PTP were those used by the investigators in the individual studies. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using ROBINS-I and GRADE. Random-effects meta-analysis generated pooled odds ratios (ORs).
RESULTS: Seven reports representing six unique cohorts (6,825 patients) were included. Definitions used for early and late PTP timing varied across studies. Earlier PTP was associated with lower odds of VTE (pooled OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.23-0.99; I2 = 30.6%; p = 0.046). The association was of borderline statistical significance: it did not persist on leave-one-out removal of either large contributing cohort, and was non-significant when re-estimated as a risk ratio (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.25-1.02; p = 0.057). No difference in in-hospital mortality was observed (pooled OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.90-1.46; p = 0.253). Evidence regarding haemorrhage progression was derived from a single cohort with three total events (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.03-11.52; p = 0.701); assessment relied on qualitative binary radiological review, which is insensitive to small-to-moderate progression. Among patients receiving PTP, pooled VTE prevalence was 10.1% (95% CI 5.9-15.3%), varying nearly fourfold (5.5%-20.7%) according to surveillance intensity. Three cohorts were judged at moderate and three at serious risk of bias; certainty of evidence was very low for all primary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with severe TBI (defined by GCS 8 or less in 100% of the analysed cohort), earlier PTP was associated with lower VTE risk of borderline statistical significance, and no difference in in-hospital mortality. The direction was consistent with prior mixed-severity syntheses, but the estimate was fragile under sensitivity analyses. The safety of earlier PTP with respect to intracranial haemorrhage progression remains unresolved, as only one cohort contributed this outcome using qualitative assessment. Adequately powered randomised evidence with quantitative haemorrhage assessment is warranted.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Applying geographic information systems data linkages for an exposome-wide association study in the Personalized Environment and Genes Study.
Journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Affordable genomics assays have enabled new study designs such as genome-wide association studies (GWAS), advancing scientific understanding of disease etiology, prevention, and treatment.
OBJECTIVE: A standardized process for linking study participants' residential histories with publicly available geospatial environmental data across existing and future epidemiologic cohorts could enable cost-effective geographic information systems (GIS)-based exposome-wide association studies (GIS-ExWAS), similarly expanding scientific understanding of disease.
METHODS: To explore this approach, we used open-source GIS software to link data from 7531 Personalized Environment and Genes Study (PEGS) participants on 11 common disease phenotypes with multiple types of GIS data from various sources to develop 88 GIS-based exposure indicators. We then estimated cross-sectional associations between these exposure indicators and the selected phenotypes using covariate-adjusted logistic regression, inverse probability of treatment weighted (IPTW), and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) models.
RESULTS: The IPTW and LASSO models identified GIS-phenotype associations complementary to those found in a prior ExWAS in questionnaire-based data from the PEGS cohort, including associations between air pollution and cardiovascular disease, as well as novel suggestive associations between several phenotypes and environmental factors not previously assessed by PEGS.
SIGNIFICANCE: Our results suggest GIS linkages can enhance exposome assessment but also highlight key methodological complexities that must be overcome to develop standardized GIS-based ExWAS that can be broadly applied. Developing standardized open-source tools for GIS data linkage and exposure assessment could enhance public health practice, precision medicine, and scientific understanding of the exposome's impacts on health.
IMPACT: GIS linkages can enhance exposome assessment and offer benefits for public health and clinical research. Adding GIS-based exposome assessments to survey-based data from cohort studies can help detect exposure-phenotype associations not detectable in survey data alone. Developing a standardized exposome assay based on GIS data would enable low-cost baseline geospatial assessments of environmental quality using only a residential address. Open-source GIS data linkage tools leveraging geospatially linked publicly available data would improve research, clinical practice, and public health.

Title: Association of preserved ratio impaired spirometry and restrictive spirometric pattern with incident atrial fibrillation: a cohort study.
Abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with an increased risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). To our knowledge, no studies have examined the association of preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) or restrictive spirometric pattern (RSP) with incident AF. We included participants without prevalent AF who had incident AF ascertainment and available spirometry and excluded those with airflow limitation. PRISm and RSP were evaluated as binary exposures and as four mutually exclusive spirometric patterns. Missing covariates were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations, and logistic regression estimates were pooled using Rubin's rules. Sensitivity analyses used an individual lower limit of normal (LLN) for the forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio, complete-case analysis, and an alternative smoking model including pack-years and current smoking. A total of 2219 participants were included, with a mean age of 62.4 years, of whom 43.6% were male. During follow-up, 247 incident AF events (11.1%) were recorded. In fully adjusted models, PRISm was associated with incident AF (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.12, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.35-3.31, P = 0.001), and RSP was also associated with incident AF (aOR = 2.38, 95% CI 1.58-3.60, P < 0.001). When participants were categorized into four mutually exclusive groups, PRISm+RSP remained associated with incident AF (aOR = 2.62, 95% CI 1.63-4.22, P < 0.001), whereas PRISm alone (aOR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.21-2.81, P = 0.690) and RSP alone (aOR = 1.88, 95% CI 0.93-3.80, P = 0.077) were not statistically significant. Results were consistent in sensitivity analyses. Among adults without airflow limitation, binary PRISm and RSP were associated with higher odds of incident AF. In mutually exclusive analyses, the clearest association was observed in participants with concurrent reductions in FEV1 and FVC.

Title: Impact of socioeconomic status on treatment and survival in multiple myeloma in Australia.
Abstract: Outcomes in multiple myeloma (MM) have improved significantly but remain heterogeneous. We assessed the impact of non-biological social determinants of health on treatment and survival outcomes in Australia using data from the Australian and New Zealand Myeloma and Related Diseases Registry. A total of 4405 patients diagnosed with MM between June 2012 and October 2025 across 44 Australian sites were assigned an area-level socioeconomic status (SES) using individual postcodes. Baseline characteristics, treatment and survival outcomes were compared across high (n = 1484), medium (n = 1463), and low (n = 1458) SES tertiles. Lower neighbourhood SES was associated with higher BMI, poorer functional status, more comorbidities (diabetes, cardiac and pulmonary disease), Asian ethnicity and greater remoteness. Independent of these baseline differences, patients from lower SES neighbourhoods were less likely to receive an autologous stem cell transplant (odds ratio = 1.1 medium vs low, p = 0.41; 1.5 high vs low, p < 0.01) and time to reach ASCT following induction was longer (p < 0.001) despite this being standard-of-care therapy with proven survival benefit. Median overall survival was shorter for the low SES group at 78.5 months compared to 92.5 months (HR = 0.85, p = 0.01) and 86.7 months (HR = 0.85, p = 0.01) for the medium and high SES groups respectively. These findings demonstrate significant disparities in treatment and outcomes favouring higher SES, independent of biological factors, within a universal healthcare system. This suggests that non-biological factors continue to influence access to standard-of-care therapy and survival, warranting further research to identify and address barriers to equitable care.

Title: Aberrant cerebrovascular reactivity presents as an early biomarker of psychosis susceptibility in patients with 22q11.2DS.
Abstract: The brain's ability to regulate blood flow is fundamental to both its function and development. In the context of neurodevelopmental disorders such as schizophrenia, understanding the complex interactions between cerebrovascular health and brain function is crucial for unraveling the pathophysiology of psychosis. This study investigates the developmental trajectory of cerebrovascular reactivity (CVR) in 22q11 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) compared to healthy controls, and its association with psychosis susceptibility. Using one of the largest longitudinal data-set of resting-state fMRI, we mapped for the first time voxel-level CVR across development. We found an early reduction in CVR in 22q11.2DS, and in particular in those who later developed positive psychotic symptoms (PPS + ). These reductions were evident within the anterior cingulate cortex, frontal lobes, and globi pallidi (GP). We propose that the pattern of CVR alterations presenting early during childhood is possibly linked to altered blood-brain barrier integrity or permeability, potentially involving endothelial or tight-junction dysfunction; however, BBB integrity was not directly measured in this study. A decrease in CVR during childhood and within the frontal regions and GP was predictive of subsequent development of positive psychotic symptoms), which often occurs during adolescence in 22q11.2DS patients. These findings suggest that cerebrovascular health is critical for normal brain development, particularly in regions like the striatum, which are vulnerable to vascular damage due to their anatomical features. These results underline the potential of CVR as an early biomarker for psychosis vulnerability, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to mitigate neurodevelopmental disruptions of cerebrovascular health in 22q11.2DS.

Title: Association of brain glymphatic system with risk of incident mortality and morbidity.
Abstract: Brain glymphatic system function as measured by diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index has been associated with brain disorders, but its association with mortality and other diseases remains underexplored. This prospective study included 34,268 participants from the UK Biobank with MRI data collected since August 2014. The DTI-ALPS indices‌ of the left and right hemispheres and the average index were calculated‌. The incident mortality and morbidity were defined as the death and disease (cancer, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, and neurodegenerative disease) reported between the MRI collection date and December 2021. Cox proportional hazard regression analyses were used to assess the association of DTI-ALPS indices with all-cause and cause-specific mortality and morbidity. We found that a higher DTI-ALPS index, indicated better glymphatic function, was associated with reduced risks of all-cause mortality (HR, 95% CI: 0.85, 0.78-0.93; P < 0.001), cardiovascular disease (CVD)-specific mortality (HR, 95% CI: 0.77, 0.63-0.93; P = 0.01), and neurodegenerative disease-specific mortality (HR, 95% CI: 0.56, 0.37-0.84; P = 0.01). Furthermore, an elevated DTI-ALPS index was associated with reduced risks of CVD (HR, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.89-0.96; P < 0.001) and neurodegenerative disease (HR, 95% CI: 0.68, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). The findings deepen the understanding of the role of brain glymphatic system in health.

Title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Four Novel Monoclonal Antibody PCSK9 Inhibitors: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Lipid and Safety Outcomes.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Four novel monoclonal antibody proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors-tafolecimab, ongericimab, ebronucimab, and recaticimab-lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in placebo-controlled trials but have never been compared head to head.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to 8 June 2026 and performed a Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials across eight lipid outcomes, analyzed by dose-interval regimen, and adverse events, analyzed by drug (PROSPERO CRD420261422519). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with CINeMA. Lipid effects are placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change from baseline with 95% credible intervals (CrIs).
RESULTS: Thirteen trials were included. In the LDL-C network (4,517 patients; 16 regimens), every regimen lowered LDL-C (-45.2% to -80.2%), with concordant reductions in non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and total cholesterol. Most between-agent differences were small, but some indirect contrasts had CrIs excluding zero; most consistently, ongericimab 150 mg every 2 weeks lowered LDL-C more than the three phase 3 recaticimab regimens (differences -14.4% to -18.6%), robust to adjustment for background statin therapy and baseline LDL-C. Rank intervals were wide. The largest triglyceride and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol effects of recaticimab were confined to small phase 1b/2 regimens. No agent differed from placebo for any adverse event or serious adverse events, although information was limited; injection-site reactions were more frequent with active treatment. Certainty of evidence was moderate to very low versus placebo and very low between agents.
CONCLUSIONS: All four antibodies produced substantial reductions in atherogenic lipids without a detected safety signal beyond injection-site reactions. Indirect between-agent differences are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a hierarchy; head-to-head and cardiovascular outcome trials are needed.

Title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Dialysis Patients: Insights from a Nationwide Registry Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-radial intervention (TRI) has become the standard of care for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, in patients on dialysis, trans-femoral intervention (TFI) remains predominant to preserve upper-limb vessels for arteriovenous fistula despite heightened hemorrhagic risk. This study aimed to compare TRI and TFI in dialysis patients undergoing PCI.
METHODS: We used the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry to compare patients on dialysis who underwent PCIs with TRI versus TFI from January 2018 to June 2025. An instrumental variable analysis with the institutional proportion of TRI use was performed to assess the risk of access-site bleeding and other peri-procedural outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 137,702 dialysis patients who underwent PCI, 28.3% of patients underwent TRI (n=38,901), while 71.7% patients underwent TFI (n=98,801). TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding at the access site (adjusted risk difference [aRD]: -0.35%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.56% to -0.15%). Overall bleeding (aRD: -1.38%; 95% CI: -1.89% to -0.87%), access-site hematoma (aRD: -0.86%; 95% CI: -1.13% to -0.60%), myocardial infarction (aRD: -0.21%; 95% CI: -0.39% to -0.03%), and mortality (aRD: -1.07%; 95% CI: -1.64% to -0.51%) were also less frequently observed in TRI. Conversely, TRI was associated with a higher risk of stroke (aRD: 0.23%; 95% CI: 0.001% to 0.45%), driven primarily by ischemic stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: TRI was associated with a lower risk of bleeding events, but the effect size was modest. The higher observed stroke risk highlights a potential ischemic trade-off and warrants further study.

Title: Overview of the 2025 FDA circulatory systems devices panel advisory committee meeting on the V-Wave Ventura Interatrial Shunt System.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial shunting is a novel strategy to reduce left atrial pressure and heart-failure (HF) morbidity. The Ventura Interatrial Shunt System (V-Wave) was evaluated in the randomized, sham-controlled RELIEVE-HF trial and reviewed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Circulatory Systems Devices Panel.
OBJECTIVES: To summarize the scientific and regulatory deliberations among the sponsor, FDA, and Advisory Panel regarding the safety, effectiveness, and benefit-risk profile V-Wave.
METHODS: We reviewed publicly available FDA documents, sponsor presentations, FDA analyses, and Advisory Panel discussions from the December 2025 meeting, with emphasis on trial design, endpoint selection, subgroup interpretation, and regulatory standards.
RESULTS: The sponsor emphasized reductions in recurrent HF events among patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), supported by prespecified recurrent-event analyses and echocardiographic data, while arguing that the hierarchical win-ratio primary endpoint underestimated benefits. In contrast, the FDA highlighted the failure to meet the prespecified primary endpoint in the intention-to-treat population, the fragility of subgroup findings, lack of outcome improvement, and consistent harm in patients with preserved ejection fraction. Advisory Panel members acknowledged acceptable procedural safety but expressed concern regarding the absence of clear, reproducible efficacy, challenges in phenotype-based labeling, and the inability of post-approval registries to resolve evidence gaps.
CONCLUSIONS: The Advisory Panel unanimously concluded that, despite procedural safety, the evidence did not demonstrate a favorable benefit-risk profile for the V-Wave device. The deliberations underscore the challenges of relying on subgroup analyses, recurrent-event endpoints, and post-market data to support approval of permanent intracardiac devices in this population.

Title: Early Deep Sedation and Short-term Outcomes After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Retrospective Multicenter Cohort Study Using the MIMIC-IV and eICU Databases.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between early sedation depth and short-term outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to characterize the dose-response relationship between sedation depth and mortality.
DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter observational cohort study using the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) and eICU (v2.0) databases.
SETTING: Multi-institutional; intensive care units contributing to the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) and eICU (v2.0) databases.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 2,556 adults (≥18 years) undergoing isolated CABG with invasive mechanical ventilation ≥24 hours. This cohort represents a higher-acuity subset of CABG patients requiring prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation (≥24 hours).
INTERVENTIONS: None. Participants were stratified by mean Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) score during the first 24 hours after intensive care unit admission: deep sedation (RASS ≤-3), light sedation (-3 < RASS < 1, reference), and agitation (RASS ≥1).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes were ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay. Deep sedation was associated with higher in-hospital mortality (41.0% v14.1%, p < 0.001), which persisted after adjustment (pooled generalized linear mixed-model odds ratio 3.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.52-4.00; propensity-matched odds ratio 3.08, 95% CI 2.33-4.10). Deep sedation was associated with increased mortality hazard (hazard ratio 2.05, 95% CI 1.71-2.44) and reduced successful extubation in Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis (subdistribution hazard ratio 0.65, 95% CI 0.57-0.74). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a J-shaped relationship between RASS and mortality, with the lowest risk between RASS -1 and 0. Exploratory XGBoost/Shapley Additive Explanations analysis showed consistent patterns.
CONCLUSIONS: Early deep sedation was independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality and reduced extubation success in mechanically ventilated CABG patients requiring prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation. The RASS range of -1 to 0 was associated with the lowest mortality and may inform prospective studies of sedation optimization in this high-acuity population. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation before clinical implementation and should not be extrapolated to routine low-risk CABG patients with an uncomplicated postoperative course and early extubation.

Title: Segmental arterial mediolysis: An underrecognized rare vascular disease requiring an interprofessional diagnostic and therapeutic pathway.
Abstract: Segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) is a rare, non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic arteriopathy that predominantly affects the visceral circulation and may cause dissection, aneurysm, hemorrhage, or ischemia. Its diagnosis is challenging because imaging findings overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia, vasculitis, connective tissue disorders, atherosclerosis, and mycotic aneurysm. This narrative review synthesizes the available evidence into an interprofessional diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. The proposed framework links radiological suspicion with structured exclusion of major mimics, multidisciplinary vascular assessment, treatment selection, management of hemodynamic instability, and longitudinal imaging surveillance. Conservative management is appropriate for stable patients without active hemorrhage, whereas endovascular treatment is generally preferred when intervention is required and anatomically feasible, with surgery reserved for failed stabilization or uncontrolled bleeding. Because current evidence is largely observational and case-based, the pathway should be regarded as a literature-based framework requiring prospective validation rather than a validated clinical guideline.

Title: Beyond the Stethoscope: Artificial Intelligence for Heart Failure Diagnosis and Phenotyping.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping cardiovascular medicine by transforming routinely collected clinical data into tools for earlier disease detection and more precise phenotyping. Heart failure (HF) represents a particularly compelling opportunity for AI-driven innovation, as many patients with structural heart disease remain unrecognized and traditional diagnostic frameworks often fail to capture disease heterogeneity. AI-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG) models, including EchoNext and PRESENT-SHD, highlight the potential for scalable opportunistic screening strategies for structural heart disease. Multimodal approaches, using ECGs and echocardiograms, are enabling earlier recognition of specific HF phenotypes, such as transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Successful implementation of these technologies will require prospective evaluation, thoughtful workflow integration, and responsible deployment. Early-career cardiologists are uniquely positioned to lead this transformation of AI in clinical medicine, ensuring that AI serves as a tool to augment clinical reasoning and ultimately advances more personalized, patient-centered cardiovascular care.

Title: Closing the Artificial Intelligence Implementation Gap for Heart Failure Care: How Recent Science Shapes the Next Steps.
Abstract: Despite major advances in the treatment and monitoring of heart failure, many patients are still diagnosed late, incompletely phenotyped, and insufficiently managed over time. Artificial intelligence (AI) is well positioned to address these gaps, yet recent studies show that strong algorithmic performance does not reliably translate into measurable clinical benefit. We draw on recent prospective evidence to examine this AI implementation gap and argue that successful AI implementation does not depend on model performance but rather on how models are designed, evaluated, embedded in clinical workflows and underpinned by governance structures that ensure responsible use. We propose a reorientation across 4 fronts. First, AI models should be designed backward from clinical decisions, not optimized for benchmark performance. Second, deployment must shift from unselected, low-prevalence populations to settings where pretest probability supports clinical utility and model outputs are embedded in actionable workflows. Third, evidence generation should include independent validation to reduce developer bias, simulation-based validation to approximate clinical reality, and prospective trials with meaningful clinical outcomes. Fourth, governance frameworks should shift from model-level oversight to system-level accountability, with defined responsibility across clinicians, institutions, and developers.

Title: Digital Phenotyping, Remote Monitoring, and Risk Prediction of Heart Failure in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review With Narrative Synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), particularly preeclampsia, are associated with acute cardiovascular morbidity and future heart failure (HF). Current surveillance relies largely on blood pressure, symptoms, laboratory abnormalities, and clinician-triggered evaluation. Digital phenotyping, remote monitoring, electronic health record-based prediction, and machine learning may enable earlier cardiovascular risk identification.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically identify and narratively synthesize studies evaluating remote monitoring, digital health, machine learning, or risk-prediction approaches for HF-related phenotypes or cardiovascular morbidity in HDPs.
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published from January 2020 through April 10, 2025. Studies evaluating prediction or monitoring approaches in HDPs underwent sequential assessment for HF-related or cardiovascular morbidity outcomes. Screening and full-text reviews were performed by 2 independent reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Given substantial heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Of 3366 records imported for screening, 6 studies met the inclusion criteria. Studies used clinical prediction models, electronic health record (EHR)-based models, and remote monitoring to evaluate acute cardiovascular morbidity, HFpEF, cardiac remodeling, and cardiovascular readmission. Model discrimination ranged from modest to strong (AUROC approximately 0.70-0.94). Recurrent predictors included severe hypertensive disease, earlier gestational age at delivery, kidney disease, pre-existing cardiac disease, pulmonary hypertension, maternal age, obesity-related measures, blood pressure, and postpartum volume retention. Most prediction models lacked external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Preliminary evidence suggests that clinical, EHR-derived, and remotely monitored data may support risk stratification for selected cardiovascular morbidity and HF-related phenotypes after HDPs. Prospective validation, physiological marker integration, and evaluation of risk-guided interventions are needed.

Title: Artificial Intelligence‒Guided Phenotyping of Cardiomyopathies: From Detection to Surveillance.
Abstract: The management of cardiomyopathies relies on timely diagnosis, precise phenotyping, multimodal risk stratification, and longitudinal monitoring. These tasks require integration of high-dimensional signals from patient history, electrocardiography, imaging, biomarkers, and longitudinal health records, data streams well-suited to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled pattern recognition and prediction. Among inherited and acquired cardiomyopathies, hypertrophic (HCM) and transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) best exemplify this opportunity. Both remain systematically underdiagnosed, span a continuous phenotypic spectrum, and are increasingly actionable through disease-modifying therapies. Emerging AI approaches applied to multimodality data streams can identify latent disease, quantify its severity, and predict its trajectory. Beyond diagnosis, AI paves the path for opportunistic screening, longitudinal surveillance, risk stratification, and novel clinical trial designs. Realizing this promise requires careful attention to label quality, generalizability, false-positive burden in low-prevalence settings, and prospective evidence that the human-AI synergy improves outcomes. In this review, we use HCM and ATTR-CM as key examples to synthesize the current evidence of AI in cardiomyopathies and propose a forward-looking framework for AI-guided disease phenotyping, with emphasis on regulation, implementation, and clinical evaluation.

Title: Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Incident Heart Failure from Routine Electronic Health Record Data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is largely preventable. Contemporary therapies can reduce incident HF among at-risk individuals, making scalable and accurate identification of high-risk patients a priority. Risk prediction models are traditionally developed from long-term epidemiologic cohorts, but machine learning (ML) can derive interpretable models directly from electronic health record (EHR) data captured in routine care. We developed an interpretable ML model for incident HF from health-system EHR data and compared it with established risk equations.
METHODS: We developed ML-based models for 5-year incident HF using EHR data from the Stanford Healthcare system, incorporating over 2000 predictors including structured data, temporal transformations, and variable interactions. We applied a neural additive model that combines feature selection and nonparametric survival analysis to develop the AIHF-Base model. We removed implausible predictors in an adjusted model (AIHF-Refined) to enhance clinical interpretability. We internally validated the models using a holdout Stanford sample and externally validated them in an independent national Veterans Affairs (VA) cohort with 10-year follow-up. Model discrimination was compared between the AIHF models and two benchmark HF prediction models, PCP-HF and PREVENT-HF.
RESULTS: The AIHF-Base model achieved an AUC of 0.847 in the Stanford cohort and 0.750 in the VA cohort. The AIHF-Refined model had an AUC of 0.840 (Stanford) and 0.741 (VA). Discrimination was comparable to that of PREVENT-HF and PCP-HF in both cohorts; in the VA cohort the AUC was 0.764 for PREVENT-HF and 0.738 for PCP-HF. Of the 14 features in the AIHF-Refined model, representing 13 distinct clinical variables, 7 used longitudinal EHR data. Age and smoking were the only features used by all models. Of 27 total features across models, 8 were used in at least one AIHF and one benchmark model, 19 were used only by AIHF or benchmark models.
CONCLUSIONS: Interpretable ML models built from routine EHR data identified clinically coherent predictors of incident HF and achieved discrimination comparable to established risk equations. By drawing on data already captured in clinical care, including longitudinal trends, this approach offers a scalable, transparent strategy for identifying patients at risk for HF and targeting them for prevention.

Title: Natural Language Processing for the Adjudication of Heart Failure with Reduced and Preserved Ejection Fraction in the Electronic Health Record.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Administrative billing codes commonly misclassify complex diseases like heart failure (HF) in the electronic health record (EHR). Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, including natural language processing (NLP), may improve disease adjudication.
OBJECTIVES: We validated an existing NLP model and specifically examined accuracy across HF subtypes (preserved vs reduced ejection fraction: HFpEF, EF ≥50%; HFrEF, EF <50%) in an EHR-based sample.
METHODS: We identified individuals who sought primary care between 2004-2014 at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. Incident HF hospitalizations were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes, and gold-standard HF adjudication was performed in 500 random cases. We applied a preexisting NLP model to classify each case and then further fine-tuned the model. We calculated diagnostic metrics for overall HF and by subtype.
RESULTS: Among 156,409 individuals, 5014 incident HF cases were identified. The fine-tuned NLP model outperformed primary ICD codes, yielding a superior kappa (0.73 vs 0.49), negative predictive value (93% vs 73%), and sensitivity (89% vs 52%), with similar positive predictive value (79% vs 87%) and specificity (86% vs 94%). Notably, NLP performance was robust across HF subtypes, whereas primary ICD codes had worse performance for identification of HFpEF. When applied to the full cohort, NLP identified 84% more HFrEF and 99% more HFpEF candidate cases than primary ICD codes.
CONCLUSION: NLP accurately classifies HF cases across subtypes, with improved accuracy after fine-tuning. AI-based approaches represent a critical opportunity to improve disease ascertainment at scale, nearly doubling the number of HF cases identified in the EHR.

Title: Deep Learning-Based BNP and NT-proBNP Evaluation From Wearable-Compatible Single-Lead ECGs for Heart Failure Assessment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) are critical biomarkers for diagnosing and managing heart failure. With the growing availability of wearable technologies, single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) images have emerged as a practical and noninvasive source of clinical information. This study explores the use of a deep learning-based approach to estimate BNP and NT-proBNP levels from single-lead ECG images, aiming to support rapid, noninvasive screening in real-world settings.
METHODS: We analyzed 528,654 lead I ECGs from 237,686 unique patients within the Houston Methodist Health System, each paired with a corresponding BNP value obtained within 24 hours. A modified VGG16 convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained to classify BNP levels into clinically relevant thresholds: ≥100, ≥400, and ≥900 pg/mL. To prevent data leakage and ensure patient-level independence, the dataset was split by unique patients into training, validation, and testing sets. Additionally, the model's generalizability was evaluated by using an external Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV-ECG testing cohort comprising 18,549 unique patients and 42,377 electrocardiograms (ECGs) with corresponding NT-proBNP measurements, with predictions assessed against established NT-proBNP thresholds of ≥125, ≥450, and ≥900 pg/mL. We then examined the association between ECG-predicted BNP (ECG-BNP) and incident HF in 706,715 patients at Houston Methodist.
RESULTS: In the testing dataset, the model demonstrated robust performance, with area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) values ranging from 0.84-0.86 and from 0.79-0.85 across the 3 classification thresholds of BNP and NT-proBNP, respectively. For the prediction of severe BNP elevation (≥900 pg/mL), the model achieved a sensitivity of 0.87 and a specificity of 0.70. The overall accuracy for distinguishing normal (<100 pg/mL) from elevated BNP levels (ie, ≥100 pg/mL) was 0.76. For NT-proBNP, the discriminative ability was higher at the lower cutoff (≥125 pg/mL) and declined slightly as thresholds increased, with AUROC values of 0.85, 0.82, and 0.79 for ≥125, ≥450, and ≥900 pg/mL, respectively. Consistent performance was observed across various demographic groups (sex and age categories) for all BNP and NT-proBNP thresholds. Higher baseline ECG-derived BNP levels were retrospectively associated with subsequent HF diagnosis across follow-up intervals extending up to 10 years, with stronger associations observed among patients whose baseline ECGs were temporally closer to HF diagnosis.
CONCLUSION: This study developed and validated a deep-learning model for classifying clinically relevant BNP and NT-proBNP thresholds from single-lead ECG images. The model demonstrated strong discrimination and external validation, supporting further investigation of single-lead ECG-derived natriuretic peptide classification for scalable cardiovascular screening and risk assessment.

Title: Automated Deep Learning Pipeline for Characterizing Left Ventricular Diastolic Function.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) is most commonly evaluated by echocardiography. However, without a sole identifying metric, LVDD is assessed by a diagnostic algorithm relying on secondary characteristics that is laborious and has the potential for interobserver variability.
METHODS: To characterize concordance in clinical evaluations of LVDD, we evaluated historical echocardiogram studies at 2 academic medical centers for variability between clinical diastology reported by clinicians and the 2016 and 2025 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) guidelines. We developed a workflow of 8 deep learning (DL) models trained on over 155,000 studies to automate LVDD assessment. Model performance was evaluated on held-out test sets from 3 academic centers.
RESULTS: In 592 studies from Cedars-Sinai Medical Center (CSMC), DL demonstrated 80.4% agreement and a weighted Cohen kappa of 0.62 with the 2016 ASE guideline assessment. In contrast, the CSMC clinician evaluation had 52.2% agreement and a kappa of 0.46 with the 2016 guidelines. In the Stanford Healthcare (SHC) cohort of 1572 studies, DL had 66.7% agreement and a kappa of 0.33 with the 2016 guidelines vs clinical diastology, with 32.7% agreement and a kappa of 0.14. Our DL workflow showed strong concordance with the 2025 guidelines, with agreements of 81.8% in CSMC and 68.1% in SHC. In a third validation cohort of 204 studies from the University of Chicago, DL had 34.3% agreement with the 2025 guidelines.
CONCLUSIONS: Evaluating LVDD has high heterogeneity. We developed DL measurement-driven diastolic dysfunction, a pipeline of models that automates the clinical workflow of grading LVDD and can contribute to improved diagnosis of heart failure.

Title: Socioeconomic characteristics of individuals who were and were not enrolled in two cardiovascular registry-based randomised controlled trials in Sweden: a descriptive cross-sectional study.
Correlation between proteinuria and cardiac biomarker levels in kidney transplant recipients.
Abstract: Kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment for end-stage kidney disease, with improved short-term outcomes; however, long-term graft and patient survival remain suboptimal. Proteinuria is a strong predictor of adverse graft and cardiovascular outcomes. We investigated the relationship between proteinuria and selected cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers, including the interleukin-33 (IL-33)/soluble ST2 (sST2) axis, malondialdehyde, neprilysin, growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15), and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), in kidney transplant recipients, with a focus on patients with heart failure. Methods: Sixty-five transplant recipients were included: 15 kidney transplant recipients with heart failure and 49 controls consisting of kidney or heart transplant recipients without heart failure. Patients were followed between November 2023 and June 2024 at the Division of Nephrology at the University of Debrecen. Proteinuria was assessed using the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio. Laboratory analyses included routine biochemical parameters, inflammatory markers, NT-proBNP, soluble IL-33 receptor (sST2), neprilysin, GDF-15, and ACE2 activity. Discrete data were described as percentages and analyzed with Fisher's exact test. Group comparisons were performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, and correlations were assessed using non-parametric methods. Across all study groups, urinary protein excretion correlated weakly positively with sST2 levels (r = 0.27, p = 0.0448). Patients with heart failure had more pronounced anemia (p = 0.0470) and lower serum iron levels (p = 0.0041). Proteinuria was weakly positively associated with circulating sST2 concentrations. Further studies are needed to clarify the prognostic significance of this pathway in kidney transplant outcomes.

Title: Untargeted Metabolomic Analysis of Acute Kidney Injury After Maze-Inclusive Cardiac Surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The maze procedure is considered as the standard surgical treatment for atrial fibrillation and might be an independent risk factor for postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI). This study aimed to investigate the metabolic alterations associated with AKI following maze-inclusive cardiac surgery using untargeted metabolomics.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 50 patients who underwent the maze procedure with concomitant cardiac surgery. AKI was diagnosed as an absolute increase in serum creatinine level of ≥ 0.3 mg/dL from baseline within 48 hours, or a ≥ 50% increase in serum creatinine within 7 days after surgery. Plasma samples were collected in operation and 24 hours after surgery, and untargeted metabolomic analysis was performed. Differential metabolites were identified and subjected to pathway enrichment analysis. Clinical variables and related metabolites were analyzed to elucidate relationship with AKI.
RESULTS: The concomitant surgeries were valve surgeries in 37 patients, followed by coronary artery (8 patients), and aorta (5 patients). Postoperative AKI occurred in 23 patients (46%). Metabolomic profiling revealed upregulation of tryptophan metabolism in AKI patients, with five candidate metabolites implicated. Among them, kynurenic acid exhibited the most significant metabolite associated with AKI, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.93. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified kynurenic acid as independent possible predictors of AKI.
CONCLUSION: Tryptophan metabolism is significantly upregulated in patients with AKI after maze-inclusive cardiac surgery. Kynurenic acid presumed in this study represents as candidate metabolite of postoperative AKI, providing an opportunity to gain insight into the underlying pathophysiology through further targeted metabolomics.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0011192.

Title: Multi-omics analyses of HFpEF progression and regression reveals multi-organ-specific metabolic dysregulation and impaired inflammation resolution.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex cardiometabolic syndrome with limited effective therapies. Given its heterogeneity, whether withdrawal of cardiometabolic stress reverses HFpEF-associated inflammatory, metabolic, and molecular remodeling remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To characterize multi-organ metabolic, molecular, and bioactive-lipid remodeling in an obesity-hypertension HFpEF model and determine the extent of recovery during an 8-week combined high-fat diet withdrawal and L-NAME cessation protocol using parallel multi-omics profiling.
METHODS: HFpEF was induced in C57BL/6 mice using a high-fat diet plus nitric oxide synthase inhibition(H + L). A regression cohort(R-H + L) underwent simultaneous return to standard chow and L-NAME cessation for 8 weeks. Multi-omics profiling included targeted and untargeted lipidomics, cardiac transcriptomics, metabolomics, fecal microbiome, and plasma short-chain fatty acid analyses, with detailed assessment of the left ventricle.
RESULTS: H + L mice developed an obesity-hypertension HFpEF phenotype characterized by predominant diastolic dysfunction, concentric remodeling, hypertension, and increased fat mass. The combined regression of H + L protocol attenuated these phenotypic abnormalities but did not restore all measures to control levels. H + L was associated with multi-organ remodeling marked by altered arachidonic acid-derived oxylipid pathways, depletion of triacylglycerols and phospholipids, and enrichment of diacylglycerols and lysophospholipids, consistent with altered resolution-related lipid signaling. Cardiac transcriptomics revealed changes in immune, circadian, vascular, and mitochondrial gene programs, whereas metabolomics revealed altered energy, arginine, and redox metabolism. H + L was also associated with reduced microbial diversity and altered short-chain fatty acids, particularly acetate and propionate. Within the 8-week recovery window, partial reprogramming occurred, but differences remained in lipid signaling, metabolic stress responses, and microbiome-associated measures.
CONCLUSIONS: The HFD/L-NAME model is accompanied by extensive multi-organ metabolic and molecular remodeling. Combined withdrawal of HFD/L-NAME attenuates the HFpEF phenotype however did not fully normalize molecular profiles within the 8-week recovery period. Persistent lipid-remodeling and metabolic dysregulation may represent potential therapeutic targets thus warrants pathway specific investigation.

Title: Isosilybin ameliorates chronic stress induced metabolic syndrome.
Journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
Abstract: Chronic stress contributes to the development of metabolic syndrome through disturbances in glucose metabolism, lipid homeostasis, and neuroendocrine regulation, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Isosilybin, a bioactive flavonolignan derived from Silybum marianum (milk thistle), has demonstrated therapeutic potential in various metabolic disorders. However, its effects on chronic stress induced metabolic syndrome and its effects on SIRT6 and PGC-1α expression under chronic stress conditions remain unclear. The present study investigated the effects of isosilybin in a rat model of chronic unpredictable stress induced metabolic syndrome. A total of 24 rats were randomly allocated into four experimental groups (n = 6 per group). Fasting blood sugar levels, systolic blood pressure, lipid markers, and insulin resistance were evaluated. SIRT6 (sirtuin 6), c-Jun (transcription factor Jun), and PGC-1α (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 alpha) expression levels were also assessed in the pancreatic and liver tissues. During the final two weeks (weeks 7-8) of the eight week CUS protocol, rats received isosilybin (10 mg/kg/day, orally) while CUS exposure was continued. Isosilybin treatment markedly improved metabolic disturbances. Significant reductions were observed in all metabolic parameters compared with untreated stressed rats. Molecular analyses demonstrated partial restoration of SIRT6 expression together with normalisation of stress-induced alterations in c-Jun immunoreactivity and PGC-1α mRNA expression in hepatic and pancreatic tissues. The findings suggest that isosilybin attenuates chronic stress-induced metabolic syndrome by improving key metabolic parameters and is associated with changes in Sirt6 expression and PGC-1α mRNA levels.

Title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of Tafamidis-treated ATTR-CM patients in a real-world cohort: Comparison with the results of pivotal trials.
Journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive and life-threatening disease that leads to heart failure and increased mortality. Pivotal clinical trials - ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B - have provided robust evidence supporting the efficacy of TTR stabilizers (Tafamidis and Acoramidis) and the TTR-synthesis inhibitor Vutrisiran in reducing mortality and cardiovascular events. This study aims to compare the clinical characteristics and cardiovascular outcomes of a real-world Portuguese cohort of patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis to those reported in pivotal clinical trials.
METHODS: Single-center, observational study including consecutive patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis 61 mg once a day. Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic data were collected and compared with published results from the ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM, and HELIOS-B trials. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 24 months, assessed by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and quality of life, assessed by KCCQ-OS during follow-up, both of which were compared across studies.
RESULTS: A total of 89 patients were included (76 males; 39 with hereditary ATTR-CM and 50 with wild-type ATTR-CM). The Portuguese real-world cohort was older than the ATTR-ACT and HELIOS-B study populations (mean age 78.6 vs. 74.5 vs. 77.0 years, respectively; p<0.001) and exhibited better functional capacity as assessed by New York Heart Association class compared to ATTR-ACT, ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B (New York Heart Association (NYHA) I: 30 vs. 9 vs. 12 vs. 15%, respectively; p<0.001). Echocardiography showed higher LVEF (55 vs. 48%, p<0.001) and better GLS (-15 vs -9%, p<0.001) compared with ATTR-ACT. NT-proBNP levels were comparable across cohorts (2639 vs. 2996 vs. 2946 vs. 2021 pg/mL, respectively; p>0.05). Hereditary ATTR was significantly more prevalent in the Portuguese cohort (44%) compared to ATTR-ACT (24%), ATTRibute-CM (10%), and HELIOS-B (11%; p<0.001), reflecting the endemic p.Val50Met mutation in Portugal. Over a follow-up of 27.4 ± 19.3 months, seven patients (7.9%) experienced heart failure hospitalizations and five patients (5.4%) died, including three cardiovascular deaths, corresponding to an annualized cardiovascular-related hospitalization rate of 0.034 events per patient-year. The 24-month all-cause mortality of 5.6% was considerably lower than reported in ATTR-ACT (24.2%), ATTRibute-CM (15.9%), and HELIOS-B (11.4%). However, KCCQ-OS scores were lower than in ATTRibute-CM and HELIOS-B (both p<0.001), likely reflecting comorbidities, and neurological involvement in hereditary cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients receiving tafamidis 61 mg for ATTR-CM in this real-world cohort were older, had a higher prevalence of hereditary ATTR, and demonstrated better baseline functional capacity compared to those enrolled in pivotal clinical trials. These observational data provide valuable real-world evidence complementing clinical trials, supporting the use, and safety of tafamidis in this Portuguese cohort.

Title: Moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe combination therapy versus high-intensity statin on coronary atherosclerotic plaque.
Abstract:
