BACKGROUND: Effect of moderate-intensity statin and ezetimibe is known to be non-inferior to high-intensity statin in prevention of adverse clinical events in patients with coronary atherosclerotic disease. However, data regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque remains limited.
METHODS: In this randomized, non-inferiority trial, patients with intermediate coronary artery stenosis were randomly assigned 1:1 to either moderate-intensity rosuvastatin (10 mg) with ezetimibe or high-intensity rosuvastatin (20 mg) group. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) was performed at baseline and after 12 months or longer to quantify the coronary plaque response. Primary end point was absolute changes in percent atheroma volume (PAV) between baseline and follow-up IVUS, and non-inferiority margin was as 2.5%. Secondary end point was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), which was a composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and unplanned repeat revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 280 patients underwent randomization. Follow-up IVUS showed absolute changes in PAV were - 1.286 ± 3.704% and - 1.302 ± 3.586%, respectively for moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe group and high-intensity rosuvastatin group. Mean difference between 2 groups (0.017%; 95% confidence interval: -0.957% to 0.991%) did not exceed noninferiority margin (non-inferiority p < 0.001). Both groups showed acceptable side effect profiles without group differences.
CONCLUSION: Compared with high-intensity rosuvastatin monotherapy, moderate-intensity rosuvastatin and ezetimibe was non-inferior regarding regression of coronary atherosclerotic plaque (Supported by Hanmi Pharmaceutical co., ltd; ROSUZET-IVUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03169985).

Title: Clinical effects of istaroxime in acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock: A patient-level pooled analysis of four phase II randomized clinical trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Istaroxime is an inotropic and lusitropic agent tested in acute heart failure (AHF) or AHF-related cardiogenic shock (AHF-CS). We aimed to assess its efficacy and concy in a pooled analysis of all randomized trials performed to date.
METHODS: Patient-level data from four phase II randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials were pooled. The effects of istaroxime 0.5-1.0 µg/kg/min for up to 48 hours vs. placebo on hemodynamics, cardiac function, and clinical outcomes were assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 284 patients were included (n=200 AHF, n=84 AHF-CS). Compared with placebo, istaroxime increased systolic blood pressure through 6 hours (least square [LS] mean difference in the area under the change from baseline curve 28.9 mmHg*h, 95% CI 18.1 to 39.8 mmHg*h) and through 24 hours (LS mean difference 121.4 mmHg*h, 95% CI 63.9 to 179.0 mmHg*h). Reductions in heart rate, body weight, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and echocardiographic E/e' ratio, and an increase in echocardiographic stroke work index and stroke volume were observed with istaroxime, with a numerically greater improvement in invasive cardiac output and creatinine. Numerically, dyspnea and quality of life were improved, and length of index hospitalization, worsening HF and death were lower with istaroxime. Serious adverse events were similar between the istaroxime and placebo arms.
CONCLUSIONS: In this patient-level pooled analysis, istaroxime 0.5-1.0 µg/kg/min was associated with improvement in SBP and hemodynamic and echocardiographic measurements of cardiac performance, without tachycardia or serious safety concerns. These findings support a phase III program to investigate the impact of istaroxime administration on outcomes.

Title: Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes With the E-tegra™ Stent Graft System for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: Endoleaks, Limb Patency, Reinterventions, Aneurysm Sac Behaviour, and Mid-Term Follow-Up.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize the published clinical evidence regarding endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the E-tegra™ stent graft system, evaluating technical success, endoleaks, limb patency, reinterventions, aneurysm sac behavior, and mid-term follow-up outcomes.
METHODS: Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included. Because of cohort overlap and heterogeneous endpoint definitions, data were synthesized narratively and descriptively without formal quantitative pooling.
RESULTS: Three eligible publications were identified, representing 209 unique patients across two underlying cohorts: the multicenter TIGRE registry (147 patients) and an independent single-center series (62 patients). Primary technical success was high, reaching 99.3% in the registry and 100% in the single-center cohort, with zero perioperative mortality across both. At mid-term follow-up (ranging from 18 months to 2 years), type II endoleak and iliac limb occlusion emerged as the primary complications. The TIGRE update reported 16 total complications (10.88%), including 8 type II endoleaks and 6 iliac limb occlusions, with a 2-year reintervention rate of 4.76%. In the single-center series, 1 type IIIa endoleak (1.6%) and 3 clinically significant type II endoleaks requiring embolization were observed. Favorable mid-term sac behavior was noted in the registry, with 72.11% of patients demonstrating >10-mm aneurysm sac shrinkage. Predefined anatomical hostility did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with adverse outcomes or reinterventions in the registry data.
CONCLUSIONS: Early and mid-term evidence for the E-tegra stent graft demonstrates high procedural success and acceptable clinical outcomes with competitive mid-term complication and reintervention rates. However, the current literature is strictly limited to single-arm observational data with short-to-medium horizons (18-24 months). Long-term durability and structural performance relative to well-established companion platforms remain unestablished, highlighting the critical need for continued prospective surveillance and comparative, long-term multicenter trials.

Title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR.
METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed.
RESULTS: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions.
CONCLUSION: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

Title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane.
REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE.
RESULTS: A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I2 = 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I2 = 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I2 = 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I2 = 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I2 = 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I2 = 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I2 = 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I2 = 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.

Title: Longitudinal Changes in Physical Performance with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Coronary Artery Disease.
Journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical performance provides valuable insights into metabolic and cardiovascular health, particularly regarding metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and coronary artery disease (CAD).
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the relationship between longitudinal changes in physical performance, assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test, and indicators of MASLD, CAD, and body fat distribution over time.
METHODS: This 3-year longitudinal prospective cohort study included 1,096 older adults. Participants underwent baseline and follow-up assessments. Based on TUG results, participants were categorized into four groups: Normal→Normal (Group 1), Impaired→Normal (Group 2), Normal→Impaired (Group 3), and Impaired→Impaired (Group 4). MASLD indicators (Fibrosis-4 index [FIB-4], MASLD liver fat score, and hepatic steatosis index [HSI]), CAD indicators (coronary artery calcium [CAC] and coronary artery volume [CAV] scores), and body fat distribution (L3 cross-sectional visceral fat area [L3VFA], L3 cross-sectional subcutaneous fat area [L3SFA], and visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio [VSR]) were also analyzed.
RESULTS: At baseline, groups with impaired TUG exhibited worse MASLD, CAD, and fat distribution profiles. Longitudinally, within-group analyses revealed distinct trajectories based on TUG changes over 3 years. For MASLD, the FIB-4 index significantly increased in participants whose TUG declined from normal to impaired (Group 3) or remained persistently impaired (Group 4)(p<0.05). For CAD, CAC and CAV scores increased significantly across all four groups (p<0.001). Regarding fat distribution, subcutaneous fat (L3SFA) significantly increased in Groups 3 and 4. Additionally, the proportion of individuals with high visceral fat (VFA ≥160 cm²) increased in these impaired groups, whereas it decreased in those who maintained or improved to a normal TUG (Groups 1 and 2).
CONCLUSION: Baseline TUG impairment and within-group longitudinal TUG deterioration were associated with adverse MASLD, CAD, and fat distribution profiles. While causal relationships cannot be established, TUG performance may serve as a functional marker reflecting metabolic and cardiovascular health status in older adults.

Title: Excessive Intrapancreatic Fat Deposition and the Potential Therapeutic Role of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: A Systematic Review.
Journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
Abstract: Excessive intrapancreatic fat deposition, also called non-alcoholic fatty pancreas disease, is marked by abnormal fat accumulation in pancreatic tissue and inked to metabolic syndrome, obesity, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite its clinical importance, intrapancreatic fat deposition lacks standardized diagnostic criteria and is often underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the pathogenesis, diagnostic challenges, and clinical relevance of intrapancreatic fat deposition, with particular attention to the therapeutic potential of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. A literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, supplemented by a post-review verification search, identified six studies (two preclinical and four clinical studies) meeting pre-specified eligibility criteria for original data on a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist intervention with a pancreatic fat outcome, following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidance; several sources considered during full-text review are reclassified as secondary literature or as not evaluating a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist and are cited instead as background. Preclinical evidence indicates that liraglutide and semaglutide can attenuate pancreatic endoplasmic reticulum stress, islet-cell apoptosis, and lipid dysregulation in diet-induced obesity models. Clinical evidence is mixed: a retrospective study reported a significant reduction in pancreatic fat with liraglutide in patients with intrapancreatic fat deposition, whereas randomised trials of liraglutide, exenatide, and dulaglutide have not consistently shown a significant between-group reduction, and direct pancreatic fat outcome data for semaglutide in humans are lacking. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials across glucose-lowering drug classes reported a significant pooled reduction in intrapancreatic fat deposition with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, providing independent, quantitative support for a class effect. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are already established to confer benefits beyond glycaemic control and pancreatic fat, including cardiovascular, renal, and broader weight-related metabolic benefits; their potential role in intrapancreatic fat deposition is one facet of this wider profile rather than a distinct "dual-purpose" mechanism. Given small samples, heterogeneous imaging, and inability to separate pancreas-specific effects from hepatic and visceral fat reductions, evidence suggests an unconfirmed role for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in intrapancreatic fat deposition. Prospective powered trials with standardised imaging and hepatic/visceral fat measurements are needed before clinical practice.

Title: Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease.
Journal: RoFo : Fortschritte auf dem Gebiete der Rontgenstrahlen und der Nuklearmedizin
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: Severely calcified lesions of the femoropopliteal segment have always presented very complex conditions for endovascular therapy of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). In particular, the rigidity and instability of the heavily calcified vessel wall result in a limited initial lumen gain after angioplasty, frequent recoil, early restenosis, and an increased rate of reinterventions. In this context, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is increasingly becoming the focus of interest. By using low-energy shock waves, both superficial and deep intimal and medial calcifications are selectively micro-fractured. This leads to improved vessel compliance and enables effective angioplasty. At low inflation pressures of 4-6 atm, the barotrauma acting on the vessel wall during IVL is overall reduced. Randomized clinical studies demonstrate a higher technical success rate of IVL compared to PTA plus DCB-PTA, with a lower complication rate and significantly better 1- and 2-year patency. IVL can be used both as a stand-alone therapy and for vessel preparation in combination with DCBPTA, and also presents an alternative therapy to atherectomy, cutting, scoring, and high-pressure balloon angioplasty. This review focuses on the methodological description of the IVL with the Shockwave system in the femoropopliteal segment, considering both technical and clinical success data.
KEY POINTS: · IVL enables effective vessel preparation in severe calcified femoropopliteal lesions.. · IVL works with low inflation pressures thereby reducing barotrauma, dissections, and bail-out stenting.. · Patency rates of IVL plus DCB are superior to conventional angioplasty plus DCB..
CITATION FORMAT: · Hölting MS, Bekker I, Stehr A et al. Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2907-7766.

Title: Sex-specific clinical and psychosocial characteristics among individuals with familial hypercholesterolemia reporting side-effects of lipid-lowering therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Symptoms attributed to lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) may affect adherence. We explored sex-specific clinical and psychosocial characteristics associated with self-perceived side-effects of LLT in individuals with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH).
METHODS: Adults (N = 2709) with FH, identified through a quality registry, were invited to a cross-sectional study. Participants completed a self-report questionnaire covering side-effects, use of LLT, muscle symptoms, pain treatment and psychosocial factors.
RESULTS: Among 613 participants (22.6% response rate), median age was 55 (IQR; 43, 65) years and 56% were women. Forty-five (13%) women and 47 (17%) men reported self-perceived side-effects of LLT. In both sexes, self-perceived side-effects were associated with significantly higher perceived sensitivity to medicines, more concerns about LLT, higher ratings of muscle symptoms and pain intensity, and lower self-rated general health. Among women, those with side-effects were more frequently living alone (38% vs 20%, p = 0.017) and reported more musculoskeletal complaints (62% vs 37%, p = 0.004). Among men, those reporting side-effects had higher median LDL-cholesterol (2.5 vs 2.1, p = 0.032), and higher prevalence of depressive symptoms (30% vs 11%, p = 0.003) and insomnia (60% vs 41%, p = 0.045). Adjustment for age, cardiovascular comorbidity and BMI made only minor changes in the effect estimates in logistic regression analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Participants with FH and self-perceived side-effects reported a significant symptom burden and concerns about the use of LLT. Women with side-effects more frequently reported musculoskeletal complaints and living alone, whereas psychological distress and insomnia were more prominent among men reporting side-effects. Individual assessments of sex-specific characteristics may be valuable for improving follow-up.

Title: Upstream behavioural and biological contributions to socioeconomic disparities in cardiovascular disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the relative contributions of smoking and adiposity phenotypes to the association between socioeconomic status (SES) and prevalent cardiovascular disease (CVD).
STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study.
METHODS: We analysed 4772 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) with available socioeconomic, anthropometric, controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), and cardiovascular data. SES was defined using the poverty income ratio (high/low), with continuous SES examined in sensitivity analyses. Prevalent CVD comprised self-reported myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, or heart failure. Primary mediators included smoking, body mass index, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and CAP. Counterfactual mediation analyses with 1000 bootstrap simulations were adjusted for age, sex, and ethnicity.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 1683 individuals with low SES and 3089 with high SES. Low SES was associated with higher smoking prevalence (24.0% vs 9.6%) and CVD prevalence (13% vs 8.6%; both p < 0.001). Higher SES was associated with lower odds of prevalent CVD (OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.75-0.85; p < 0.001), with attenuation after adjustment for behavioural, adiposity, and cardiometabolic factors (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.81-0.94; p < 0.001). Smoking demonstrated the largest mediated proportion, accounting for 19.9% of the SES-CVD association (95% CI 7.3-34.2). Among adiposity measures, WHtR demonstrated the largest contribution (10.4%), exceeding waist circumference (5.0%), body mass index (4.6%), and CAP (1.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Smoking and central adiposity represent important pathways underlying socioeconomic disparities in prevalent CVD. Smoking demonstrated the largest mediated proportion, while WHtR was the strongest adiposity-related mediator. These findings highlight potentially modifiable behavioural and adiposity-related pathways alongside broader socioeconomic determinants of cardiovascular health.

Title: Autonomic syncope admissions: Evaluation of current practice and application of the ESC guideline on syncope.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The majority of syncope emergency department (ED) presentations is due to autonomic syncope, which comprises reflex syncope and orthostatic hypotension. Despite the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines many patients with autonomic syncope are still admitted. Therefore we studied the indications for, and the factors associated with, clinical admission in the prospective SYNERGY database.
METHODS: We performed a post-hoc-analysis of patients visiting the ED with an adjudicated diagnosis of autonomic syncope from the SYNERGY database. We analyzed admission indications based on the ESC guideline risk (initial diagnosis+risk stratification); RISC-score, and clinical admission indications. We combined these admission indications and compared with observed patient management. Furthermore, we analyzed the factors associated with the decision for admission.
RESULTS: We analyzed 388 adjudicated autonomic syncope patients, of whom 39.4%(n = 153) were admitted. 2.8%(11/388) had a guideline risk admission indication, 14.0%(53/388) had a RISC-score admission indication; 26.0%(101/388) had clinical admission indications. The combination of clinical indications and guideline risk yielded 26.3%(102/388) admission indications, combination with the RISC-score yielded 33.5% (130/388) for high-risk and 46.9% (182/388) for intermediate-risk admission indications. Factors associated with admission were age; diagnostics/consultations unrelated to syncope; and any ECG abnormalities without guideline ECG-risk features. In contrary, execution of an active-standing test was associated with a lower likelihood of admission.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with autonomic syncope are frequently admitted to the hospital, over one-third of these admissions is not guideline-indicated. Optimizing the implementation of the guideline-based initial evaluation process may reduce unindicated admissions of autonomic syncope patients.

Title: Image quality assessment of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CT angiography.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lower-extremity CT angiography (CTA) is widely used for the assessment of peripheral arterial disease. Reducing iodinated contrast medium is desirable, particularly in patients with impaired renal function. This study evaluated the impact of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) on image quality in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 60 patients who underwent lower-extremity spectral CTA with 40 mL of iodinated contrast medium were included. Conventional reconstructions and 40-keV VMI were compared regarding vascular attenuation, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), iodine concentration, and subjective image quality across predefined arterial segments. Qualitative image quality was independently assessed by two readers using a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: Compared with conventional reconstructions, 40-keV VMI significantly increased vascular attenuation, SNR, and CNR across all arterial segments (all p < 0.001). Subjective ratings for vessel contrast, vessel sharpness, overall image quality, and diagnostic confidence were significantly higher with VMI for both readers across all evaluated arterial segments (all p < 0.05). Iodine concentration decreased progressively from proximal to distal arterial segments, whereas the CNR advantage of VMI remained preserved throughout the arterial tree.
CONCLUSION: Forty-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction significantly improves quantitative and qualitative image-quality parameters in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA compared with conventional reconstructions. These findings suggest that low-keV VMI may improve image-quality characteristics in reduced-contrast CTA protocols, particularly in distal arterial segments.
IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Low-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction may support reduced-contrast lower-extremity CTA protocols by improving image quality without increasing contrast medium volume. This approach may be particularly valuable for patients in whom minimizing iodinated contrast medium exposure is desirable.

Title: Machine Learning Reveals Prognostic Value of Medical History in Suspected Coronary Artery Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification in suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) relies on clinical history and imaging, but longitudinal medical history may provide additional prognostic information.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data improves prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) beyond demographics and stress perfusion cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with suspected CAD.
METHODS: A total of 2,159 patients (65 ± 12 years, 44% women) undergoing stress perfusion CMR were included. Models used demographics, CMR findings, and registry diagnoses and procedures from the prior 10 years. MACE was defined as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or coronary intervention. Random Forest models were used for binary prediction, and Random Survival Forests (RSF) and penalized Ridge Cox regression for time-to-event analysis.
RESULTS: During 2.7 ± 0.9 years of follow-up, 212 patients (9.8%) experienced MACE. For binary prediction, the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.66 (95% CI: 0.62-0.69) using demographics and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.68-0.75; P = 0.001) after adding historical registry data. The full model achieved an AUROC of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.79-0.85) and outperformed the demographics-plus-CMR model (AUROC: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.78-0.84; ΔAUROC: 0.014; 95% CI: 0.002-0.027; P = 0.029). In time-to-event analysis, RSF and Cox regression performed similarly using demographics and CMR (concordance index [C-index] 0.80 for both; P = 0.546). After including registry data RSF achieved a C-index of 0.81 (P = 0.144), and Cox performance decreased to C-index 0.77 (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with suspected CAD, machine learning models using 10-year historical registry data have the potential to improve prognostic risk prediction beyond demographics and stress perfusion CMR.

Title: Advanced Age in Acute Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock by Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Status.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a leading cause of in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although advanced age is associated with worse outcomes, associations across out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) strata remain incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the association between octogenarian status and in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI-related CS (AMI-CS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and to examine this association in analyses stratified by OHCA status.
METHODS: We analyzed patients with AMI-CS enrolled in the multicenter Kanagawa-ACuTe cardIoVascular rEgistry who underwent PCI. Octogenarian status (≥80 years) was the primary exposure. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate associations with in-hospital mortality, with additional analyses stratified by OHCA status.
RESULTS: Among 658 patients, 177 (26.9%) were octogenarians, and 279 (42.4%) died during hospitalization. Octogenarian status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.32-3.48; P = 0.002). In stratified analyses, octogenarian status was associated with higher mortality among patients without OHCA, whereas no statistically significant association was observed among those with OHCA. The interaction between octogenarian status and OHCA was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.422). Higher heart rate, unmeasurable heart rate, higher serum creatinine, and lower serum albumin were independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AMI-CS undergoing PCI, octogenarian status was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. Although estimates differed numerically across OHCA strata, the interaction was not statistically significant, precluding a conclusion that the association differed according to OHCA status. These stratified findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Chronological age should be considered within a comprehensive clinical assessment rather than in isolation.

Title: Associations of objectively measured daytime and nighttime light exposure with the severity of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome and all-cause mortality: Evidence from a national cohort and genetic analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Light exposure is an increasingly recognized modifiable environmental factor in cardiometabolic health, but its associations with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, as well as with mortality (from any cause), remain unclear.
METHODS: Adults with valid measurements of ambient light from wrist-worn devices from the 2011-2014 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey were included. Daily, daytime, and nighttime light intensity and duration were assessed. Survey-weighted regression and unweighted Cox models examined associations with CKM stage, advanced CKM syndrome, and all-cause mortality. Mediation analysis evaluated circulating levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]. Mendelian randomization assessed genetically predicted 25(OH)D level, ease of skin tanning, and outdoor time.
RESULTS: Higher daily and daytime light intensity was associated with lower CKM stage and lower odds of advanced CKM syndrome. Longer exposure to light >1000 lx was also associated with lower odds of advanced CKM syndrome, whereas nighttime light intensity showed no independent association. Among individuals with CKM syndrome, higher daily and daytime light intensity was associated with lower all-cause mortality. However, these associations were substantially attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for baseline CKM stage. Circulating 25(OH)D partially mediated associations between light intensity and mortality, but not advanced CKM syndrome. Mendelian randomization findings were mixed after multiple-testing correction.
CONCLUSION: Greater objectively measured daytime light exposure was associated with a more favorable CKM profile and lower all-cause mortality among individuals with CKM syndrome. The association with lower all-cause mortality was attenuated after adjustment for baseline CKM stage, suggesting that it may not be independent of CKM severity. Further prospective studies are warranted.

Title: Burden of pruritus in older non-dialysis CKD stage 4-5 patients: 7-year follow-up of the EQUAL study.
Journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Chronic Kidney Disease-associated Pruritus (CKD-aP) is among the top 10 most prevalent and burdensome symptoms in kidney failure, but little is known in CKD stage 4-5 patients. Therefore, the aim of this study is to investigate the prevalence, incidence, and burden of pruritus in older non-dialysis (ND) CKD stage 4-5 patients.
METHODS: The European Quality (EQUAL) study is a prospective, multicenter study involving patients aged ≥ 65 years with an incident drop in eGFR to ≤20 ml/min/1.73m2. Pruritus presence and burden were assessed every 3-6 months between March 2012 and May 2022, using the Dialysis Symptom Index with a five-point Likert scale. High burden was defined as a score 4-5. Cumulative incidence of pruritus was estimated with the cumulative incidence function.
RESULTS: We included 1 380 patients who completed at baseline the pruritus question (yes/no). Patients were observed for a maximum of 7 years. At baseline, 66% were men, mean(SD) for age was 76(7) years, for eGFR 17(5) ml/min/1.73m2, for serum phosphate 1.3(0.3) mmol/L, 41% had diabetes, and 47% had cardiovascular disease. At baseline, 53% reported having pruritus, and 26% experienced a high burden. During 7-years of follow-up, the average proportion of patients with pruritus was 55%, with a mean burden score of 2.8 (95%CI: 2.8 to 2.9). Pruritus status was dynamic, with > 10% of patients alternating between presence and absence every six months. Among those initially without pruritus, the 7-year cumulative incidence was 43% (95%CI: 39 to 47%).
CONCLUSIONS: Pruritus affected approximately 55% of older patients with ND-CKD stage 4-5, with one in four reporting a high symptom burden. Pruritus status was dynamic over time. These findings highlight the need for greater awareness among healthcare professionals and underscore the importance of timely recognition and management of pruritus, with the potential to improve patients' quality of life.

Title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain.
METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64).
DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

Title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors.
RESULTS: Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52, p = 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58, p = 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11, p = 0.049).
DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

Title: Climate, Air Quality, and Emergency Department Use in Northern Germany: Protocol for a Multicenter Register Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change threatens population health through temperature extremes, air pollution, and altered infectious disease patterns. Emergency departments (EDs) are sensitive indicators of climate-related health impacts; however, comprehensive multicenter investigations integrating meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease surveillance across different health care provision levels remain scarce in Germany, particularly in maritime climate regions.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize the impact of meteorological factors, air quality, and infectious disease dynamics on ED presentations across multiple health care facilities and care provision levels in northern Germany over an 11-year period.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, observational study will examine ED presentations across 4 facilities representing different care provision levels in the greater Lübeck area and southeastern Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, from January 2014 to December 2024. Clinical data, including ICD (International Classification of Diseases)-coded diagnoses, patient demographics, and temporal information, will be linked with meteorological data from the German Weather Service, air quality measurements from state environmental monitoring, and infectious disease surveillance from the Robert Koch Institute. The primary outcomes will be daily ED visits overall and stratified by disease category (cardiovascular, respiratory, psychiatric, infectious, renal, neurological, and surgical/traumatic). Distributed lag nonlinear models within a generalized additive modeling framework will be used to characterize temperature-health relationships, accounting for delayed and nonlinear effects, and adjusted for temporal trends, seasonality, and infectious disease incidence. Subgroup analyses will examine vulnerable populations by age, sex, and socioeconomic status.
RESULTS: Project planning and conceptualization began in June 2024, and ethical approval was granted in July 2025. Following approval, clinical data were transferred sequentially across participating sites in July 2025, August 2025, and October 2025. Data from 3 of the 4 participating hospitals have been successfully received, while the final outstanding dataset is expected in the second half of 2026. Meteorological data collection was completed in October 2025 and air quality data in January 2026. While preliminary descriptive statistical analyses have already commenced, inferential statistics will be performed once data collection is fully completed.
CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter study will provide systematic evidence on climate-sensitive ED utilization in a maritime climate region of northern Germany. By integrating clinical, meteorological, air quality, and infectious disease data across 4 hospitals of varying care complexity, the study is well positioned to characterize nonlinear and delayed health effects of temperature extremes across a broad spectrum of acute conditions. Results are expected to inform regional health care capacity planning, early warning systems, and public health preparedness, while contributing to the broader evidence base on climate and health.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Chronic kidney disease in heart failure: results from an Ecuadorian registry.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Heart failure (HF) frequently coexists with chronic kidney disease (CKD), a combination that is associated with worse outcomes. Data from Ecuador remain limited. We estimated the prevalence of CKD among patients with HF and described prognostic impact according to left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted using a single-center HF registry in Ecuador. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 60 mL/min/1.73m2. HF was categorized by LVEF into reduced (HF with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF], ≤ 40%), mildly reduced (HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction [HFmrEF], 41-49%), and preserved (HF with preserved ejection fraction [HFpEF], ≥ 50%). The median follow-up was 2.28 years.
RESULTS: Among 706 patients (age 69.9 ± 13.3 years; 31.4% women), 50.3% had an eGFR ≥ 60, 33.1% had an eGFR of 30-59, and 16.6% had an eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2. CKD prevalence was 57.8% in HFrEF, 41.8% in HFmrEF, and 53.5% in HFpEF (p = 0.003). CKD patients were older and had higher rates of hypertension (HT), atrial fibrillation, and cerebrovascular disease, with higher NT-proBNP levels, larger diastolic diameters, lower LVEF, more tricuspid regurgitation, and pulmonary HT (all p < 0.05). CKD was associated with increased all-cause mortality (49.3 vs. 26.8%), cardiovascular mortality (28.8 vs. 11.8%), all-cause hospitalizations (47.6 vs. 25.9%), and HF hospitalizations (22.2 vs. 11.0%). Predictors of mortality were LVEF ≤ 40% (Hazard ratio [HR] 1.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.1-2.2; p = 0.048), moderate/severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.1-2.2; p = 0.008), and prior HF hospitalization (HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.6-3.1; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CKD was highly prevalent among patients with HF, particularly among those with LVEF < 50%. Its presence was associated with a more adverse clinical and echocardiographic profile, as well as higher hospitalization, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality.

Title: Early ambulatory re-evaluation and follow-up of patients admitted in the acute cardiac care unit - Practical aspects on ambulatory follow-up of acute care patients: acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias, conductance disorders, myocarditis, pericarditis, other acute cardiac settings A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC.
Journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
Abstract: Early, structured ambulatory follow-up after hospitalization for acute cardiac events remains a key unmet need in cardiovascular care. This clinical consensus statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care of the ESC provides pragmatic, condition-specific guidance on post discharge management and (early) ambulatory re-evaluation for patients admitted to an acute cardiac care unit. It complements existing disease-oriented guidelines by focusing on the vulnerable transition from hospital to home rather than on acute in-hospital treatment. The document first defines key concepts and outlines general principles regarding timing, content, and organization of the first post-discharge contacts, including risk stratification, medication reconciliation, symptom assessment, evaluation of psychosocial status and comorbidities, patient and family education, and integration of cardiac rehabilitation. In practice, the consensus statement discusses the patient's path after discharge: how should the follow-up team look like, when should the first and subsequent visits be planned, what should be done at each contact, and how can multidisciplinary teams and hybrid (in-person plus remote) models be implemented according to local resources. Supplementary material highlights major evidence gaps, including the optimal timing and intensity of follow-up, the composition of ambulatory teams, the role of telemonitoring and digital health, and the needs of vulnerable populations. Overall, this consensus aims to support clinicians in designing structured, individualized, and scalable ambulatory pathways after acute cardiac care.

Title: Association between height and blood pressure in healthy adults from Mexico City: a cross-sectional analysis from the Tlalpan 2020 cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The association between adult height and blood pressure (BP) remains inconsistent across populations. We aimed to evaluate this association in a cohort of clinically healthy adults from Mexico City, Mexico.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of non-diabetic, normotensive adults residing in Mexico City. Bivariate analyses were performed to explore differences in systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP (DBP) across sex-specific height quartiles. Subsequently, sex-stratified multivariable linear regression models were constructed to assess the association between height and BP, adjusting for covariates selected based on their established relationship with BP.
RESULTS: A total of 3,250 participants were included (mean age, 37.1 ± 9.1 years). Among women (n = 2.069), SBP and DBP did not differ significantly across height quartiles. In men, DBP was slightly higher in shorter quartiles, whereas no significant differences were observed for SBP. For each 10-cm increase in height, SBP decreased by 1.08 mmHg in women and 1.61 mmHg in men, while DBP decreased by 0.61 mmHg and 1.71 mmHg, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort of clinically healthy adults from Mexico City, taller stature was modestly associated with lower BP. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design, potential residual confounding, and limited generalizability.

Title: Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Coronary artery disease commonly coexists with severe aortic stenosis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) candidates, yet optimal revascularization remains debated. We meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials comparing routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before or concomitant with TAVI versus conservative management. Major databases were searched through May 2026. Random-effects models calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and evidence certainty was evaluated via the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Three randomized controlled trials (1156 patients; PCI: n = 579, conservative: n = 577) were included. Routine PCI was not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.70-1.15; P = 0.40), cardiac death (RR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.51-1.08; P = 0.12), myocardial infarction (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64; P = 0.64), stroke (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.48-1.03; P = 0.07), or hospitalization (RR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.87-1.32; P = 0.52). However, PCI significantly increased major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.34; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P = 0.0008), while reducing urgent and repeat revascularization. In conclusion, routine PCI before or concomitant with TAVI reduces subsequent revascularization without conferring survival or ischemic benefit, while increasing bleeding complications. Given the moderate-to-low certainty of evidence, limited cumulative sample size, and clinical heterogeneity across trials, these findings warrant cautious interpretation and favor an individualized, Heart Team-guided revascularization strategy over routine PCI.

Title: Targeted urine metabolomics for enhanced diagnosis of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy in newborns: A pilot study.
Abstract: While therapeutic hypothermia (cooling treatment) is successful in preventing hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), current diagnosis is limited to clinical features and serum lactate. Many newborns at risk of HIE are not identified within the therapeutic window and consequently miss the opportunity for cooling treatment. We hypothesized that metabolomic analysis could more accurately identify infants at risk of HIE compared to other commonly used techniques, such as serum lactate. Newborns admitted for therapeutic hypothermia for HIE, were recruited (n = 11) and compared to four healthy infants. A targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) platform was used to measure metabolites in urine samples. We identified 15 metabolites that differentiated infants with HIE from healthy controls. The metabolomic signature was subsequently utilized to blindly and accurately re-identify the same infants 3 days later, after clinical recovery, with 100% accuracy, as their metabolic profiles resembled those of non-hypoxic healthy infants. The diagnostic performance of LC-MS/MS was superior to that of lactate alone. Urine metabolomic profiling has the potential to more accurately identify neonates at risk of long-term neurologic injury than lactate alone.

Title: Anti-inflammatory therapy in patients with coronary artery disease: A new era in the treatment of atherosclerosis or false hopes?
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aim: To investigate the potential use of anti-inflammatory drugs in patients with acute myocardial infarction (MI).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Materials and Methods: During December 2025, a comprehensive search was conducted in the scientometric databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar for data from peer-reviewed English-language studies on the use of anti-inflammatory drugs in patients with CAD, published over the past 10 years. The search used the following terms: anti-inflammatory drugs, MI, acute coronary syndrome, chronic coronary syndrome, CVE, CAD, atherosclerosis. Preference was given to the most relevant sources of information, results of randomized placebo-controlled trials, international recommendations, metaanalyses, and more recent literary sources. A total of 94 literary sources were analyzed.
CONCLUSION: Conclusions: Measuring levels of inflammatory markers and using anti-inflammatory agents, particularly colchicine, in addition to baseline therapy in patients with acute MI to prevent recurrent index events is justified and promising.

Title: Contemporary Outcomes of Catheter Ablation of Long-Standing Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in mapping and ablation have improved the safety and efficacy of catheter-based ablation (CA) of atrial fibrillation (AF). Patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF) historically have poor ablation outcomes; however, they are underrepresented in contemporary reports.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate ablation approaches and long-term rhythm control following contemporary catheter ablation for LSPAF.
METHODS: A single-center, retrospective analysis of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF between 2021 and 2025 was performed. Demographic and procedural characteristics were analyzed; 1-year arrhythmia free survival and atrial arrhythmia burden were assessed.
RESULTS: Ninety-five patients (median age 68 years [IQR, 63-73]; 80% male; median BMI 32.4 kg/m2 [IQR, 28.6-35.6]; median ejection fraction 55% [IQR, 49%-60%]; 37% with prior CA) were followed for a median of 20.2 months (IQR, 10.2-29.7). Radiofrequency ablation alone was used in 74 patients (78%), pulsed-field ablation alone in 13 (14%), and both in 8 (8%). Pulmonary veins were isolated in all patients, 88 (93%) underwent additional left atrial ablation, including linear ablation in 88 (93%), posterior wall isolation or ablation in 72 (76%), vein of Marshall ethanol infusion or ablation in 25 (26%), coronary sinus ablation in 24 (25%), and cavotricuspid isthmus ablation in 23 (24%). Fourteen of 92 post-blanking evaluable patients (15.2%) were receiving a class I or III antiarrhythmic drug at last follow-up. Among 57 patients with adequate post-blanking follow-up after a first AF ablation (of 60 first-ablation patients overall), 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 39.3% (95% CI, 27.8%-55.4%). Among all patients and after allowing repeat procedures, 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 53.5% (95% CI, 43.3%-66.1%). Among patients with continuous monitoring, median arrhythmia burden decreased from 90.1% (IQR, 21.1%-99.4%) before ablation to 0.0% (IQR, 0.0%-3.8%) at 6 months and 0.0% (IQR, 0.0%-20.0%) at 12 months.
CONCLUSION: In this contemporary cohort of patients undergoing CA for LSPAF, 1-year arrhythmia-free survival was 53.5% when repeat procedures were allowed. Among patients with implanted cardiac devices, arrhythmia burden was markedly reduced after ablation and may complement conventional time-to-first-recurrence endpoints.

Title: Effects of Remote Ischemic Conditioning on Cerebral Blood Flow Regulation in Atherosclerosis: A Randomized Trial.
Journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
Abstract: Impaired dynamic cerebral autoregulation (dCA) contributes to cerebral perfusion instability in patients with cerebrovascular atherosclerosis. Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) has shown neuroprotective potential; however, its acute effects on dCA in this population remain unclear. In this randomized, sham-controlled trial, patients with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) and/or extracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ECAS) received a single session of RIC or sham-RIC. dCA was assessed at baseline and at 0-1, 6-9, and 24 h using transfer function analysis. The prespecified primary endpoint was the affected-side phase difference (PD) at 6-9 h. Of the 140 randomized participants, 132 with valid primary endpoint data were included in the primary analysis. For the primary outcome, the affected-side PD at 6-9 h was significantly greater in the RIC group than in the sham-RIC group (adjusted β = 12.166, 95% CI: 6.787-17.545; p < 0.001). Secondary analyses at other time points and of the unaffected side supported an acute physiological effect of RIC on dCA. These findings suggest that a single RIC session may rapidly improve impaired dCA in patients with ICAS and/or ECAS. Larger studies are needed to determine whether this response varies across clinical presentations and vascular territories.

Title: Early ventricular function assessed by speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) in extremely preterm infants.
Abstract: ObjectivesTo evaluate the relationship between early speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE)-derived longitudinal strain and conventional measures of ventricular systolic function in extremely preterm infants and assess their association with mortality before hospital discharge.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included inborn infants born at less than 29 weeks of gestation admitted to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between October 2023 and December 2025. Standardised targeted neonatal echocardiography was performed within 72 hours of birth. Left ventricular (LV) and right ventricular (RV) longitudinal strain and conventional measures of ventricular function were evaluated in relation to mortality. Each measure was entered separately into multivariable models adjusted for gestational age and 5-min Apgar score, with bootstrap internal validation.ResultsAmong 144 infants, 32 (22.2%) died before hospital discharge. Infants who died had less negative LV and RV longitudinal strain and lower conventional measures of LV and RV systolic function than survivors (all p < 0.001). LV strain correlated strongly with LV ejection fraction (r = -0.811) and fractional shortening (r = -0.868), while RV strain correlated strongly with RV fractional area change (r = -0.898) and RV output (r = -0.780) (all p < 0.001). All evaluated echocardiographic measures showed high apparent discrimination for mortality (AUC 0.910 to 0.955; all p < 0.001), without significant differences between strain and conventional measures, and remained associated with mortality after adjustment (optimism-corrected c-statistics 0.915 to 0.964).ConclusionsSTE-derived longitudinal strain was closely associated with conventional measures of ventricular systolic function, while both deformation-based and conventional measures were associated with mortality; these exploratory findings require external validation. STE may provide a complementary component of early neonatal haemodynamic assessment in extremely preterm infants.

Title: Impact of structured patient education on leg ulcer recurrence prevention following healing: results after one year.
Journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous leg ulcers (VLUs) are chronic, recurrent wounds associated with significant physical, psychological and healthcare burden. Despite effective healing rates with compression therapy, recurrence rates remain high, often exceeding 60% within 1 to 2 years. Patient education has been identified as a key strategy to improve adherence to preventive measures and support long-term self-management.
AIM: To evaluate the impact of a structured education programme on leg ulcer recurrence prevention and self-management following ulcer healing.
METHODS: This interim analysis reports findings from the first year of a 4-year longitudinal evaluation conducted within a community-based leg ulcer service in Ireland. Eighty-five patients with recently healed VLUs participated in a 1-hour nurse-led education session covering venous insufficiency, compression hosiery, skin care, exercise and recurrence prevention. Educational materials, practical demonstrations and hosiery application aids were provided. Data were collected using pre- and post-intervention questionnaires, follow-up telephone reviews and recurrence monitoring over 12 months.
RESULTS: Baseline recurrence data demonstrated a recurrence rate of 78% prior to programme implementation. Following the intervention no ulcer recurrences were recorded at 6 months and recurrence at 12 months was 5%. Improvements were observed in self-management behaviours, including reduced difficulty with compression hosiery application (67% to 35%), skin care (39% to 28%) and exercise participation (47% to 27%). All participants reported improved understanding of ulcer prevention and satisfaction with the programme.
CONCLUSION: Structured patient education delivered by specialist nurses was associated with substantial reductions in VLU recurrence and improved self-management. This approach may represent an effective and practical strategy for long-term recurrence prevention within community leg ulcer services.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Dialysis: A New Therapy Or Have We Been Here before.
Journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN

Title: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation with Vitaflow prosthesis in Latin America.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robust long-term data on the performance and durability of novel transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) valve designs, especially in Latin America, are lacking and warrant further investigation.
OBJECTIVES: To provide a 1 year follow-up data regarding a novel TAVI device.
METHODS: A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted in Latin America of patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis treated with the Vitaflow prosthesis from June 2022 to June 2023. The clinical endpoints were all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, vascular and bleeding complications, permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM), and heart failure admission. Echocardiographic outcomes were the transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak at 1 year of follow-up.
RESULTS: A total of 46 consecutive patients were included. The mean age of the patients was 80.9 ± 6.13 years; 50% were men, the mean STS score was 4.64 ± 2.67, and 60.8% were in NYHA class III/IV. The most used valve size was the 27 mm (47.1%). All-cause death at 1-year follow-up occurred in 4 patients (8.7%), of which 3 were cardiovascular (6.5%). There were 2 strokes, 1 vascular event, 2 major bleeding events, 4 new PPMs, and no myocardial infarctions or heart failure admissions. The 1-year mean transvalvular gradient was 7 ± 4 mmHg, and 3 patients (6.4%) had moderate paravalvular leak, with no severe leaks.
CONCLUSIONS: In a Latin American population, the Vitaflow TAVI valve has proved good safety and efficacy outcomes at 12 months of follow-up in the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis.

Title: A Disease Trajectory Representation Framework With Risk-Aware Pseudotime Analysis for Electronic Health Records: Application to Heart Failure Risk Stratification.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure develops through complex longitudinal interactions among multiple chronic diseases, making longitudinal disease trajectories an important source of clinical information. Longitudinal disease trajectories contain rich structural information that reflects disease evolution and comorbidity interactions. However, this information is often lost when electronic health record (EHR) data are summarized using conventional pooling strategies or sparse International Classification of Diseases (ICD) representations.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an interpretable trajectory representation that preserves structural characteristics of longitudinal disease evolution for heart failure risk stratification using EHRs.
METHODS: Longitudinal ICD trajectories were represented using Node2Vec embeddings and summarized with information gain (IG)-weighted geometric features, including historical means, directional shifts, dispersion, and deviation relative to high-risk disease representations. The resulting maximum IG-weighted deviation geometric (mIGwDG) representation was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation against conventional embedding aggregation strategies, sparse ICD one-hot encoding, and a long short-term memory (LSTM) model. To facilitate interpretation of longitudinal disease evolution, we further developed a risk-aware pseudotime framework to organize patient trajectories along a model-inferred risk continuum and used a framework combining IG with the positive pointwise mutual information (PPMI) framework to characterize clinically relevant comorbidity patterns.
RESULTS: The proposed framework achieved an out-of-fold (OOF) area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.667 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.888, outperforming conventional embedding aggregation methods. Compared with sparse ICD one-hot encoding, the proposed framework reduced feature dimensionality by approximately 75% while maintaining comparable predictive performance. Combining mIGwDG with sparse ICD one-hot features further improved both logistic regression (LR) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), suggesting that the proposed representation captures complementary longitudinal disease trajectory information. In addition, the risk-aware pseudotime framework organized heterogeneous patient trajectories along a model-inferred risk continuum, while IG×PPMI analysis highlighted clinically relevant comorbidity patterns that supported the interpretation of longitudinal disease organization.
CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework provides a compact and interpretable representation of longitudinal disease trajectories while maintaining comparable predictive performance. By combining geometric trajectory characterization with risk-aware pseudotime visualization, the framework facilitates the representation of longitudinal EHRs, the visualization of disease evolution, and risk stratification.

Title: High-Sensitivity Troponin Pathway and Emergency Department Length of Stay.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays are the diagnostic standard for acute coronary syndrome but present significant implementation and workflow complexity.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether implementation of a structured, electronic health record (EHR)-integrated hs-cTn pathway was associated with changes in emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS) and serial troponin testing times.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective quality improvement study compared preimplementation conventional cTn assay (June 1, 2021, to March 31, 2022) with a postimplementation integrated hs-cTn pathway (June 1, 2022, to March 31, 2023) in 4 urban EDs within a single health system. Participants were adults (aged ≥18 years) presenting with chest pain and at least 1 troponin assay result. Data analysis was performed from April to September 2024.
EXPOSURES: Implementation of an hs-cTn assay within an EHR-integrated clinical pathway.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was ED LOS, defined as time from patient registration to ED departure. Secondary outcomes included time from first clinician evaluation to disposition (discharge or admission) and interval from the first troponin assay order to the second troponin assay result in patients with serial assays.
RESULTS: Of the 16 094 patient encounters analyzed (9151 [56.9%] female; mean [SD] age, 49.5 [17.4] years), 8486 (52.7%) were in the hs-cTn and 7608 (47.3%) were in the conventional cTn cohort. Overall, hs-cTn implementation with workflow integration was associated with decreased mean ED LOS, from 6.18 (95% CI, 6.10-6.26) hours to 5.64 (95% CI, 5.57-5.71) hours. Compared with conventional cTn, implementation of the hs-cTn pathway was associated with shorter mean ED LOS in admitted patients (9.60 [95% CI, 9.35-9.87] hours vs 10.50 [95% CI, 10.22-10.78] hours; P = .003) and discharged patients (5.02 [95% CI, 4.96-5.08] hours vs 5.33 [95% CI, 5.26-5.40] hours; P = .006). Pathway implementation was also associated with shorter time from evaluation to disposition in patients receiving 2 or more troponin measurements (5.06 [95% CI, 4.97-5.15] hours vs 6.68 [95% CI, 6.52-6.85] hours; P < .001) and time from first troponin order to second troponin result in both admitted patients (3.18 [95% CI, 3.11-3.25] hours vs 5.16 [95% CI, 5.01-5.31] hours; P < .001) and discharged patients (2.78 [95% CI, 2.75-2.82] hours vs 4.54 [95% CI, 4.46-4.62] hours; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this quality improvement study, an EHR-integrated hs-cTn pathway was associated with significantly reduced ED LOS and, in patients with serial troponin measurements, reduced time from evaluation to disposition and reduced time to serial assay results. The findings suggest this structured EHR approach may mitigate operational challenges of hs-cTn adoption and could serve as a scalable model to improve ED efficiency for patients with chest pain.

Title: Closing the Gap in Thromboprophylaxis: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Approach Among Medical Inpatients.
Journal: The American journal of managed care
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of a multidisciplinary quality improvement (QI) framework on guideline-directed venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis adherence among hospitalized patients.
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective, pre-post interventional study conducted in internal medicine wards with historically low baseline prophylaxis rates.
METHODS: Following a retrospective baseline assessment, a multicomponent QI initiative was executed across 2 Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles in adult internal medicine wards at a university hospital between September and November 2022. Interventions included the following: (1) physician education on the Padua Prediction Score and International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism Bleeding Risk Score; (2) implementation of an electronic health record clinical decision-support tool prompting VTE risk assessments; and (3) integration of clinical pharmacists into daily multidisciplinary rounds to provide active audit and feedback.
RESULTS: At baseline, 62.1% of high-risk patients received guideline-recommended VTE prophylaxis. Post intervention, this rate increased to 79.1% in the first cycle and 82.1% in the second cycle ( P  = .006). Among clinical pharmacists' 27 recommendations, 70.4% were accepted and implemented. The multidimensional strategy demonstrated sustained improvements in guideline adherence with minimal adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementing a multidisciplinary QI framework significantly enhanced guideline-directed VTE prophylaxis use among hospitalized patients. This collaborative approach underscores the value of electronic decision support, clinical audit-feedback loops, and pharmacist-physician integration in driving patient safety. Ultimately, this system-level strategy provides a scalable model for improving preventive care protocols across diverse hospital settings.

Title: An exploration of whole-blood transcriptomic alterations associated with obesity in the absence of overt metabolic disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity poses significant health risks including metabolic complications, cardiovascular disease, and cancer. However, a subgroup of individuals with obesity do not meet diagnostic criteria for overt cardiometabolic disease. These individuals are often described as having obesity without clinically manifest metabolic complications. Despite this apparent clinical profile, obesity may still be associated with systemic alterations in gene expression and molecular pathways.
METHODS: In this exploratory study, we conducted a comprehensive transcriptomic analysis of whole blood samples from individuals with obesity without overt metabolic abnormalities (OBO) and lean healthy controls (LHC) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and pathway-level differences. Unsupervised dimensionality reduction was used to visualize global transcriptional patterns between groups.
RESULTS: Differential expression analysis revealed 106 upregulated and 322 downregulated genes in OBO, with the de-ubiquitinase USP17 family and snoRNAs among the most significantly altered. Pathway enrichment analysis identified 33 differentially enriched pathways, predominantly showing lower inferred enrichment of immune-related and DNA damage/repair-associated gene sets in OBO compared with LHC.
CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory findings demonstrate that obesity, even in the absence of overt metabolic disease, is associated with distinct whole-blood transcriptomic signatures. The results provide a hypothesis-generating framework for understanding early systemic molecular alterations associated with obesity.

Title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist use with mortality and healthcare utilization in patients with vascular dementia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Patients with vascular dementia (VD) have high mortality and frequent acute care use, and no treatment has been shown to improve these outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are associated with a lower incidence of dementia and with cardiovascular benefit in type 2 diabetes, but their association with clinical outcomes in patients with established VD is unknown.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study using a national database identified patients with VD from 2016 to 2025. Patients receiving GLP-1RAs within one month of diagnosis were propensity-score matched with non-users (n = 613 per group). Primary outcome was mortality at 1, 3, and 5 years; secondary outcomes included hospitalizations and emergency visits.
RESULTS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risk of mortality at 1 year (8.7% vs. 15.9%; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34-0.71), 3 years (23.3% vs. 33.8%; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.44-0.76), and 5 years (34.4% vs. 54.3%; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.41-0.69) (all p < 0.001). In addition, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risk of inpatient admissions and emergency visits.
CONCLUSION: GLP-1RA use in patients with VD was associated with lower risk of mortality and healthcare utilization. These beneficial associations warrant prospective randomized trials.

Title: Heatwaves in HF: From risk to clinical action.
Abstract: Extreme heat represents an important clinical challenge for patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD). Individuals with heart failure (HF) may be particularly vulnerable because heat dissipation requires cutaneous vasodilation, increased skin blood flow, and sweating, whereas HF may limit cardiovascular reserve and increase susceptibility to hypotension, renal dysfunction, and electrolyte disturbances. Risk is further amplified by advanced age, chronic kidney disease (CKD), frailty, cognitive impairment, limited access to cooling, and the use of medications that influence volume status, blood pressure (BP), or thermoregulation. Observational evidence links high ambient temperatures with cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, and recent HF-specific data support an association between short-term heat exposure and increased mortality. However, evidence directly guiding the clinical management of chronic HF during heatwaves remains limited. No randomized controlled trial (RCT) has established whether or how guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) should be modified solely in response to hot weather. This focused narrative review proposes a cautious, phenotype-driven approach. Local heat alerts should prompt anticipatory risk assessment, patient education, and temporary intensification of surveillance, whereas treatment changes should be determined by the interaction between symptoms, congestion, BP, weight, oral intake, urine output, renal function, and electrolytes rather than ambient temperature alone. Telemonitoring may provide an enabling infrastructure for this strategy, although heat-alert-triggered remote management has not been prospectively validated. Extreme heat should therefore prompt increased clinical vigilance rather than automatic medication withdrawal. Prospective studies are needed to validate heat-specific monitoring pathways, hydration strategies, and medication-review protocols in chronic HF.

Title: After ENRICH: Evidence boundaries and unresolved questions for early minimally invasive evacuation in lobar intracerebral hemorrhage.
Abstract: The ENRICH trial renewed interest in early minimally invasive surgery (MIS) for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), with its clearest treatment signal observed in selected patients with lobar hemorrhage. However, prior and subsequent surgical trials differ substantially in patient population, hematoma location, timing, technique, device, endpoint selection, and procedural execution.
