How these heterogeneous data should inform clinical interpretation and trial generalizability remains uncertain. We performed a structured narrative review with an evidence-oriented synthesis focused on randomized trials, major guidelines, systematic reviews, post hoc analyses, and technical or mechanistic studies relevant to MIS for spontaneous supratentorial ICH. Original targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were supplemented by targeted update searches during revision to incorporate peer-review-identified and newly relevant literature. Evidence was organized according to source of support, including trial-derived criteria, post hoc or procedural-quality findings, mechanistic or anatomical inference, and patient-centered clinical modifiers. This review was not designed as a systematic review, meta-analysis, or guideline. The most direct trial-level support for early MIS after ENRICH applies to selected patients with lobar ICH treated within the ENRICH-tested operational window. Other considerations, including surgical accessibility, hematoma geometry, clinically meaningful mass effect, and expected evacuation quality, remain incompletely validated as treatment-effect modifiers. We therefore reframe post-ENRICH interpretation as an evidence-boundary map rather than a clinical algorithm. Relevant considerations are separated into trial-tested protocol features, post hoc or procedural-quality observations, mechanistic or anatomical hypotheses, and contextual clinical considerations. None of these categories should be used to rank patients, define futility, or determine treatment eligibility without prospective validation. Population-level estimates suggest that only a small minority of lobar ICH patients, approximately 4-7% in available estimates, may resemble the ENRICH-tested population. Residual hematoma volume is discussed as a procedural quality target and potential future trial endpoint, not as a firm preoperative exclusion criterion. Current evidence supports cautious, selective interpretation of early MIS for lobar ICH rather than broad generalization. This evidence-boundary synthesis is intended to clarify where trial-level evidence ends and where post hoc findings, surgical inference, and patient-centered judgment begin. Prospective validation in multicenter registries or future trials is required before this evidence can be translated into a clinical decision tool.

Title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point.
CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Title: A Validated Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy Claims-Based Coding Algorithm: ValidATTR-US.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lack of a validated United States (US) claims-based method for identifying transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) limits the reliability and comparability of real-world evidence. We developed and validated a US claims-based coding algorithm (ValidATTR-US) to identify patients with ATTR-CM.
METHODS: ValidATTR-US was developed by optimizing previously published algorithms using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes and refining them using the STAnford Research Repository (STARR, claims/electronic health record-linked database; N = 61,908) to define the index cohort (n = 694). The Stanford ATTR-CM Patient Registry (N = 634) served as the validation cohort for cross-referencing the index cohort. Index cohort inclusion criteria were age ≥ 60 years at diagnosis and ≥ 2 ATTR-CM diagnosis codes (ICD-10-CM, E85.[0, 1, 2, 4, 82]) on separate days and ≥ 2 cardiac-related codes or ≥ 1 tafamidis claim. Exclusion criteria were multiple myeloma (C90), light chain amyloidosis (E85.81), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (Z94.84), and organ-limited amyloidosis (E85.4) when co-occurring with cerebral amyloid angiopathy (I68.0), end-stage renal disease (N18.6), or skin disorders (L99). Performance metrics included accuracy ({true positives [TPs] + true negatives [TNs]}/total sample), specificity (TNs/{TNs + false positives [FPs]}), and sensitivity (TPs/{TPs + false negatives [FNs]}).
RESULTS: Accuracy was 99.51% (95% confidence interval [CI] 99.45-99.56%), specificity 99.70% (99.65-99.74%), and sensitivity 80.76% (77.47-83.76%) for detecting patients with ATTR-CM (TP, n = 512; TN, n = 61,092; FP, n = 182; FN, n = 122). Individual ICD-10-CM codes were strongly predictive of ATTR-CM case status (area under the curve [AUC] 0.84) and genotype classification (AUC 0.88).
CONCLUSION: ValidATTR-US is the first US claims-based ATTR-CM coding algorithm validated against a clinically confirmed ATTR-CM registry. Broader application may improve identification of patients with ATTR-CM in real-world datasets and help characterize prevalence and treatment patterns. Graphical abstract available for this article.

Title: Proton pump inhibitors in antithrombotic therapy: gastroprotection, drug interactions, and clinical management.
Abstract: Antithrombotic therapy is central to the prevention of thromboembolic and ischaemic events in patients with coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, and after percutaneous coronary intervention, but is accompanied by an increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) can reduce upper GIB, although their optimal use across different antithrombotic regimens, potential drug interactions, and inability to prevent lower GIB remain clinically relevant concerns. This structured narrative review examines PPI co-therapy in patients receiving antiplatelet agents, oral anticoagulants, or combined antithrombotic treatment. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026, supplemented by contemporary cardiology and gastroenterology guidelines. Randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and large observational studies were prioritized. Evidence indicates that PPIs provide clinically meaningful protection against acid-related upper GIB, particularly in high-risk patients receiving aspirin-containing regimens, dual antiplatelet therapy, or intensified antithrombotic therapy, whereas evidence in isolated oral anticoagulation remains predominantly observational. PPI co-therapy should therefore be targeted according to gastrointestinal bleeding risk and antithrombotic intensity, with periodic reassessment as treatment changes, rather than used as universal gastrointestinal protection. KEY POINTS: • Proton pump inhibitors can reduce the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding in patients receiving antithrombotic therapy, but their benefit is greatest in patients with additional gastrointestinal bleeding risk factors • Their use should therefore be individualized according to gastrointestinal risk and the intensity of antithrombotic treatment rather than prescribed routinely to all patients • The need for gastroprotection should be reassessed whenever the antithrombotic regimen or the patient's bleeding risk changes.

Title: Physiological prehabilitation for patients undergoing cellular therapy in multiple myeloma and lymphoma: a systematic review.
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate physiological prehabilitation for adults with multiple myeloma or lymphoma undergoing cellular or immune-based therapies and to describe intervention characteristics and programme duration.
BACKGROUND: Fatigue, physical deconditioning, and muscle weakness can compromise treatment readiness and quality of life (QoL). Evidence on exercise begun before these therapies remains limited.
METHODS: Six databases were searched from inception to 4 September 2026. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and quasi-experimental studies were eligible if exercise began before stem cell transplantation, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, or bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) therapy and assessed physical function plus muscle strength, QoL, or fatigue. Joanna Briggs Institute tools informed methodological appraisal. Findings were synthesised narratively by outcome, alongside exercise characteristics and duration.
RESULTS: Twelve studies (501 participants), comprising three pilot RCTs and nine quasi-experimental studies, were included. Ten evaluated transplantation and two CAR-T therapy; none evaluated BiTE therapy. Aerobic plus resistance or strength exercise predominated, and nine programmes reported a central or protocol duration within 4-8 weeks. Physical function and lower-limb performance findings were generally favourable; handgrip strength, QoL, and fatigue findings were mixed. Heterogeneous methods and predominantly uncontrolled designs limited interpretation.
CONCLUSIONS: Physiological prehabilitation shows preliminary promise for functional preparation before treatment. Aerobic and resistance exercise and the commonly reported programme durations warrant comparative evaluation.
IMPLICATIONS: Adequately powered, therapy-specific RCTs should standardise exercise reporting, assess clinically meaningful outcomes, and evaluate safety and sustained recovery after treatment.

Title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE.
METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model.
RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Arrhythmia management in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
Journal: Netherlands heart journal : monthly journal of the Netherlands Society of Cardiology and the Netherlands Heart Foundation
Abstract: Arrhythmias are common in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and contribute substantially to morbidity at all disease stages. The arrhythmogenic substrate-reflecting diffuse amyloid infiltration, atrial myopathy, autonomic dysfunction, and conduction system involvement-differs fundamentally from that in other cardiomyopathies. Prospective rhythm monitoring reveals a burden substantially higher than previously recognised and predominantly asymptomatic, with bradyarrhythmias and atrial fibrillation (AF) dominating and sustained ventricular arrhythmias remaining rare.This review examines key aspects of arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM. Conduction system disease is frequently encountered, and pacing strategies-including conduction system pacing-are discussed in the context of progressive infiltrative disease. We address the rationale for lifelong anticoagulation in AF irrespective of CHA2DS2-VA-score, and emerging considerations for anticoagulation in selected sinus rhythm patients with impaired atrial function. Rhythm control strategies are reviewed in light of extensive atrial substrate, high AF recurrence rates, and the absence of randomised trial data. The role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators is examined, with emphasis on the lack of proven survival benefit for primary prevention. Finally, we explore disease-modifying therapies and their potential to attenuate the arrhythmogenic substrate. Overall, structured surveillance, rhythm control, and individualised device decisions form the cornerstones of modern arrhythmia management in ATTR-CM.

Title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
Abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

Title: Serum Galectin-3 Levels and Aortic Dimensions in Children with Bicuspid Aortic Valve.
Abstract: This study aimed to compare serum galectin-3 levels between children with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and healthy controls and to investigate the association between galectin-3 levels and aortic dimensions in children with BAV. This prospective, single-center, cross-sectional, controlled study included 47 children with echocardiographically confirmed BAV and 43 healthy controls. Echocardiographic aortic dimensions and corresponding Z-scores, anthropometric measurements, and serum galectin-3 levels were assessed. Aortic dilation was defined as an ascending aorta Z-score > 2. Age, body mass index, and cardiac function were similar between groups, whereas sex distribution differed significantly. Ascending aorta diameter and Z-score were significantly greater in the BAV group than in controls (27.94 ± 5.56 vs. 21.52 ± 2.53 mm, p < 0.001; 2.34 ± 1.54 vs. 0.31 ± 0.72, p < 0.001). Aortic dilation was present in 28 (59.6%) BAV patients. Serum galectin-3 levels did not differ between BAV patients and controls [8.70 (7.03-11.38) vs. 8.05 (6.10-13.15) ng/mL, p = 0.566]. No significant correlation was found between galectin-3 levels and aortic dimensions or Z-scores. Galectin-3 levels were also similar in BAV patients with and without aortic dilation [8.80 (6.58-12.30) vs. 8.15 (6.30-10.95) ng/mL, p = 0.537]. Serum galectin-3 levels were not associated with aortic dimensions or aortic dilation in children with BAV. Longitudinal studies incorporating serial assessment of aortic dimensions and complementary markers of aortic disease are warranted.

Title: Long Term Outcomes of Pediatric Patients After Catheter Ablation for Possible Arrhythmia Induced Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract: Arrhythmia induced cardiomyopathy (AiCM) is reversible, and catheter ablation has become the standard treatment for most arrhythmias. However, as the diagnosis of AiCM can be made only in retrospect, management is often challenging. A single center retrospective study included patients who had ablation for presumed AiCM after January 2011 to assess the outcomes of ablation, and the final diagnosis. 22 patients (11 female) were included in the study with the following distribution of arrhythmias: Atrial Ectopic Tachycardia (AET) = 8, Permanent Junctional Reciprocating Tachycardia (PJRT) = 6, Ventricular Tachycardia = 3, Premature Ventricular Contraction = 1, Atrial Flutter = 1, Atrioventricular Reciprocating Tachycardia = 1. There were two patients where an EP study did not show a specific arrhythmia substrate and the patients proceeded in the transplantation pathway. Of the 20 patients with confirmed tachycardia, four (20%) had complete normalization of function with+ medical management. The remaining 16 patients (80%) achieved no or partial functional recovery, with ablation playing even more important role in these patients. One AET patient showed no recovery of function despite successful ablation, consequently requiring heart transplant due to later confirmed gene-positive cardiomyopathy. Overall, 19 patients (95%) showed normal cardiac function at the end of study period with diagnosis of AiCM. There was one significant complication with AV block due to RF ablation on ECMO in a newborn with PJRT. While medical management can achieve functional recovery in some pediatric AiCM cases, most patients will require catheter ablation with 88% success rate. However, once functional recovery is achieved, long term outcome is excellent. Very rarely ventricular function will not recover despite successful ablation as genetic cardiomyopathies can present with secondary arrhythmia.

Title: Ketamine Vs. Etomidates and Cardiovascular Collapse During Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Secondary Analysis of the DEVICE and PREOXI Trials.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Emergency tracheal intubation in critically ill adults is a high-risk procedure.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate associations of ketamine vs. etomidate with cardiovascular collapse and other peri-intubation outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Secondary analysis of individual-participant data from the DEVICE and PREOXI trials, treating induction medication as an observational exposure. The cohort included 2357 adults intubated in emergency departments or ICUs; 1822 received etomidate, 312 ketamine, and 223 other induction regimens.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was cardiovascular collapse, defined as new or increased vasopressor use, nadir systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg, or cardiac arrest between induction and 2 minutes after intubation. Secondary outcomes included severe hypoxemia (oxygen saturation < 80%) and procedural outcomes.
RESULTS: In weighted analyses, cardiovascular collapse occurred in 14.0% of etomidate recipients and 20.4% of ketamine recipients. In weighted, covariate-adjusted models, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.80; 95% CI, 1.24-2.62) and new or increased vasopressor use (aOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.02-2.23), nominally lower odds of severe hypoxemia (aOR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.88), and shorter modeled time to successful intubation (hazard ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.02-1.33). The latter two associations were not significant after multiplicity adjustment. Estimates for systolic blood pressure below 65 mm Hg and cardiac arrest were too imprecise for reliable inference. Successful intubation on the first attempt and 28-day in-hospital mortality did not clearly differ between ketamine and etomidate.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Compared with etomidate, ketamine was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular collapse, primarily reflecting new or increased vasopressor use. Associations with severe hypoxemia and intubation time did not remain significant after multiplicity adjustment. Because induction medication was not randomized and residual confounding remains possible, these associations should not be interpreted as causal.

Title: Divergent Cost Trends for 3 Advanced Cancers, 2013 vs 2022: A Commercial Claims Analysis.
Journal: The American journal of managed care
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cancer is cited by most employers as the leading condition driving rising health care benefit costs. This study examined the components of and trends in health care costs for patients with 3 advanced cancers, focusing on employer-sponsored insurance. We evaluated how the costs of various cancer care modalities changed between 2013 and 2022 during a period marked by the introduction of novel therapies alongside generic and biosimilar competition.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational claims analysis.
METHODS: Using MarketScan Commercial Claims and Encounters data, we compared 12-month health services costs for patients newly diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), or multiple myeloma in 2013 vs 2022.
RESULTS: Metastatic colorectal cancer costs decreased 15% (from $239,003 in 2013 to $203,499 in 2022), coinciding with generic competition for chemotherapy and biosimilar entry for supportive medications. Conversely, costs for metastatic NSCLC increased by 25% (from $220,662 to $276,883), and costs for multiple myeloma increased by 51% (from $216,337 to $327,495), both due to immunotherapy. Censoring rates were lower in 2022 for all 3 cancers, significantly so for metastatic NSCLC.
CONCLUSIONS: Cancer costs for employers are not uniformly increasing, but instead, shifting based on market competition and therapeutic innovation. Where costs are rising, they are driven by novel therapies that offer a potential value trade-off, coinciding with survival improvements reported in the literature.

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of prehospital capillary high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in patients with acute chest pain: the prospective multicenter VALIDATE study.
Journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) plays a central role in the diagnosis and management of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), including rule-out and rule-in strategies in the emergency department. Extending hs-cTnI testing to the prehospital setting could accelerate patient orientation and clinical decision-making, but the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI remains insufficiently studied.
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of prehospital capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge.
DESIGN: The study is a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with blinded index test results.
SETTINGS AND PARTICIPANTS: Four French emergency medical service systems with 10 mobile intensive care units. Adult patients presenting with acute chest pain were included.
INDEX TEST: Prehospital hs-cTnI measurement using a point-of-care device (Atellica VTLi) on capillary samples. Treating clinicians were blinded to hs-cTnI results.
OUTCOME MEASURES AND ANALYSIS: The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of capillary hs-cTnI for the diagnosis of NSTEMI at hospital discharge. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Clinically relevant thresholds were defined a priori based on predefined safety criteria.
MAIN RESULTS: Among 659 patients included in the primary analysis, 71 (10.8%) had NSTEMI. Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI demonstrated good diagnostic performance [area under the curve (AUC) = 0.83, 95% CI = 0.78-0.88]. A rule-out threshold of <2.2 ng/L, evaluated according to prespecified performance criteria, identified 7.1% of patients, with a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI = 0.92-1.00). A rule-in threshold of >43.6 ng/L identified 6.5% of patients, with a positive predictive value of 0.65 (95% CI = 0.51-0.79). In the predefined sensitivity analysis, venous hs-cTnI showed similar diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.84, 95% CI = 0.79-0.89).
CONCLUSION: Prehospital capillary hs-cTnI showed good diagnostic performance for NSTEMI, although feasibility in routine practice was challenged by unavailable or uninterpretable measurements. Further external validation is warranted before implementation in prehospital diagnostic pathways.

Title: The Subclinical Cardiovascular Effects of Nonoptimum Ambient Temperature: A Longitudinal Study in 15 Chinese Cities.
Abstract: Short-term ambient temperature is linked to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, but subclinical responses remain unclear. Using repeated health examinations from 247,641 adults in 15 Chinese cities (2013-2020), we assessed 20 cardiovascular indicators with linear mixed-effects and distributed lag nonlinear models. The indicator-specific sample sizes ranged from 1119 to 219,090 participants. Exposure-response relationships were near-linear or inversely J-shaped for ten indicators, U-shaped or inverted U-shaped for seven, and atypical or unclear for three. Low temperature was associated with 18 indicators, peaking at lags 0-5 days, whereas high temperature was associated with seven, peaking at lags 0-6 days. Relative to the reference temperatures, extremely low-temperature exposure (P1, -9 °C) was associated with cumulative increases over lag days 0-10 of 6.52%-13.99% in blood pressure, 4.63%-46.23% in inflammatory markers, 5.11%-10.48% in cardiac-associated enzymes, and 6.29% in homocysteine, as well as cumulative changes ranging from -2.68% to 5.36% in hemorheological parameters and from -4.96% to 12.05% in lipid-related indicators. Extremely high-temperature exposure (P99, 32 °C) was associated with cumulative changes ranging from -1.47% to 4.84% in hemorheological parameters and increases of 1.62%-1.91% in lipid indicators and 1.32%-15.13% in cardiac-associated enzymes. These findings provide multicenter evidence that nonoptimum temperature is associated with early cardiovascular alterations.

Title: The Role of Urine Specific Gravity in Predicting Contrast-Induced Nephropathy in Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: A Prospective Study.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between preprocedural urine specific gravity (USG) and contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) and to evaluate its role in risk prediction.
METHOD: This prospective study included 191 consecutive patients undergoing CAG. USG was measured 30 minutes before the procedure. CIN was defined as a ≥25% increase from baseline or an absolute increase of ≥0.5 mg/dL in serum creatinine 48-72 hours after the procedure. Factors predicting the development of CIN were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: The median age of the study population was 63.0 years (IQR: 55.0-71.0), and CIN developed in 33 patients (17.3%). Preprocedural USG was significantly higher in the CIN(+) group than in the CIN(-) group (1020.9+-5.4 vs. 1017.7+-6.6; P =.002). Multivariate analysis identified USG (OR: 1.10, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18; P =.010), non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) (OR: 3.32, 95% CI: 1.33-8.25; P =.010), New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III/IV (OR: 15.90, 95% CI: 2.76-91.50; P =.002), and bundle branch block (OR: 6.60, 95% CI: 1.78-24.42; P =.005) as independent predictors of CIN. The area under the curve (AUC) for USG was 0.671. At a cutoff value of 1017, USG demonstrated 81.8% sensitivity, 53.2% specificity, and a 93.3% negative predictive value (NPV). Although its overall discriminatory performance was similar to that of the Mehran risk score, USG exhibited a complementary diagnostic profile.
CONCLUSION: Elevated preprocedural USG is an independent risk factor for CIN. Given its high NPV, USG may serve as a modest, noninvasive, complementary bedside tool for risk stratification. The observed independent association between bundle branch block and CIN should be regarded strictly as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

Title: Echocardiographic Stratification of Diuretic Response via TAPSE-Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure Integration in Decompensated Heart Failure.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Right ventricular (RV) function is a key determinant of prognosis in heart failure (HF). Although echocardiographic parameters such as tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) and pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) are widely used, their interpretation in isolation has limitations, and the relationship between right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling and diuretic response remains insufficiently defined. We hypothesized that a composite TAPSE-PASP (TP) score would better reflect RV-PA coupling and be associated with the natriuretic response. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the TP score and diuretic response, as assessed by spot urinary sodium.
METHOD: This retrospective, single-center study included 81 hospitalized patients with HF. Standard transthoracic echocardiography was performed to measure TAPSE, PASP, and derived indices. A TP score was created using quartile-based categorization. Diuretic response was assessed by spot urinary sodium. Patients were classified as good or poor responders using a threshold of 50 mEq/L.
RESULTS: Poor responders had lower spot urinary sodium levels (28.1 +- 11.3 vs. 95.5 +- 24.1 mmol/L, P < 0.001) and a higher prevalence of worsening renal function (69% vs. 23%, P < 0.001). Individual measures (TAPSE/PASP and TAPSE × PASP) were not significantly associated with diuretic response, whereas the TP score showed a weak but significant correlation with urinary sodium (r = 0.248, P = 0.03). Lower TP scores were associated with impaired RV function markers and a lower natriuretic response.
CONCLUSION: The TP score integrates RV systolic performance and pulmonary vascular load and demonstrated a weak but significant association with diuretic response in patients with HF. Given the retrospective design and lack of external validation, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Title: Inflammatory and Combined Indices Outperform Metabolic Indices in Predicting One-Year MACE in NSTEMI with Type 2 Diabetes.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) carry a high residual cardiovascular risk that is inadequately captured by conventional risk scores. We aimed to compare the prognostic value of ten composite blood-based indices from metabolic, inflammatory, combined, and nutritional categories for one-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in this population.
METHOD: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 557 consecutive NSTEMI patients with T2DM who underwent coronary angiography were enrolled. Ten indices were calculated from admission blood samples: TyG, AIP, and METS-IR as metabolic indices; SIRI, PIV, and NLR as inflammatory indices; CTI and CAR as combined indices; and PNI and HALP as nutritional indices. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with DeLong comparison, independent predictors were identified by multivariate logistic regression, and survival separation was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: One-year MACE occurred in 118 patients (21.2%). Inflammatory indices outperformed metabolic indices in ROC analysis (SIRI AUC 0.764 vs. TyG 0.638; P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, CTI (OR 2.446; 95% CI 1.746-3.427; P < 0.001), SIRI (OR 1.242; 95% CI 1.088-1.417; P = 0.001), and PNI (OR 0.918; 95% CI 0.884-0.954; P < 0.001) remained independent predictors alongside left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), SYNTAX score, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Pure metabolic indices lost significance after CTI entered the model. SIRI yielded the widest Kaplan-Meier survival separation (29.5 percentage points; P < 0.001). CTI remained significant across all subgroups, whereas SIRI lost independence in patients with reduced ejection fraction.
CONCLUSION: In NSTEMI patients with T2DM, CTI, SIRI, and PNI independently predict one-year MACE based on routine admission blood tests. Inflammatory and combined indices outperform pure metabolic surrogates, supporting a shift toward multidimensional risk stratification in this high-risk population.

Title: Design and Validation of a Custom-Made Electrocardiogram Machine for Low-Cost, High-Fidelity Cardiac Monitoring.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Electrocardiography (ECG) is an essential diagnostic tool in cardiovascular medicine; however, access remains limited in low-resource settings because of cost and infrastructure requirements. This study aimed to develop and preliminarily validate a low-cost, custom-made ECG device capable of real-time cardiac monitoring and arrhythmia detection.
METHOD: A portable ECG system incorporating a low-noise analog front-end, microcontroller-based digital processing, and Bluetooth-enabled wireless transmission was designed. Preliminary validation was performed using simultaneous recordings from one healthy volunteer and three patients with documented cardiac arrhythmias, and the results were compared with those of a commercial ECG system in terms of signal quality and rhythm interpretation.
RESULTS: The custom-made device provided stable real-time ECG recordings with satisfactory signal fidelity and low noise levels. Comparative analysis demonstrated encouraging agreement with the commercial ECG system in waveform morphology and arrhythmia identification. Wireless data transmission was reliable throughout the recordings.
CONCLUSION: This pilot proof-of-concept study demonstrates the technical feasibility of a low-cost, custom-made ECG system for real-time rhythm monitoring and preliminary detection of selected cardiac arrhythmias. The device showed satisfactory signal fidelity and agreement with a commercial ECG system in a small validation cohort. Larger prospective studies are required to establish diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical generalizability.

Title: Association Between Brain Natriuretic Peptide Level and Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: Background and objectivesPrevious studies suggest a link between brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels and atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the nature of this relationship is disputed. To address this, we conducted a study to gather and assess evidence on the association between BNP and AF.MethodologyStudies were systematically searched and collected from four databases and different types of gray literature. After the screening, the selected articles' quality and risk of bias assessment were evaluated. Meta-analysis calculated std. Mean difference on the extracted data. Furthermore, heterogeneity, sensitivity, subgroups, and publication bias analyses were assessed.ResultsSixteen studies were included in this systematic review. The meta-analysis of 11 studies, comprising 1,418 cases and 3,343 controls, showed a significant and positive association between BNP levels and AF (pooled Std.Mean Difference = 1.08; 95% CI = 0.67, 1.49; P < 0.0001), with no publication bias (P = 0.212). Among the subgroups, significant differences in Std. Mean Differences were observed primarily when stratified by region or risk of bias; however, these analyses were unable to fully account for the observed heterogeneity.ConclusionsElevated BNP levels are strongly associated with prevalent AF. In prospective studies measuring BNP prior to onset, elevated levels served as a modest predictor of incident AF, suggesting its role in identifying underlying atrial myopathy. Further investigations in both molecular and clinical fields with proper methodology and more detailed information are needed to clear the interactive aspects of BNP level in AF patients.

Title: Intraoperative Hypotension and Risk of Cuff Blood Pressure Inaccuracy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hypotension is associated with cardiovascular complications and mortality, making accurate blood pressure (BP) monitoring essential. However, the accuracy of noninvasive oscillometric cuff BP (Cuff BP) during hypotension is uncertain. We examined the association between intraoperative hypotension and Cuff BP inaccuracy.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort included 22 812 adults undergoing noncardiac surgery from April 2013 through November 2023, with 348 888 simultaneous Cuff BP and invasive arterial BP (Arterial BP) pairs. Pairs with arterial systolic BP >120 mm Hg or diastolic BP >80 mm Hg were excluded to focus on the hypotensive range. Hypotension was defined as arterial mean arterial pressure (MAP)<65 mm Hg and categorized as mild (55 to <65), moderate (45 to <55), or severe (35 to <45 mm Hg). Cuff BP inaccuracy was defined as an absolute MAP difference >10 mm Hg from Arterial BP. Multivariable generalized estimating equation models estimated adjusted odds ratios and 95% CIs.
RESULTS: Compared with normal MAP (≥65 mm Hg), hypotension was associated with higher odds of Cuff BP inaccuracy (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 [95% CI, 1.40-1.50]). Adjusted odds ratios increased with severity (P value for trend <0.001): 1.28 (95% CI, 1.24-1.32) for mild, 2.33 (95% CI, 2.20-2.46) for moderate, and 7.00 (95% CI, 6.13-8.00) for severe hypotension. Sensitivity for correct MAP classification decreased from 87.4% for normal MAP to 32.6%, 20.2%, and 9.6% for mild, moderate, and severe hypotension.
CONCLUSIONS: We found a significantly higher risk of Cuff BP inaccuracy in patients with intraoperative hypotension, supporting cautious interpretation of Cuff BP during intraoperative hypotension.

Title: Extravascular Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension: First-in-Human Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-based intravascular renal denervation produces modest, variable blood pressure reductions, partly because renal sympathetic nerves lie at variable depths within the periarterial adventitia and because accessory or early branching arteries are inaccessible to intraluminal catheters. We developed an extravascular renal denervation system (HyperQure) delivering circumferential radiofrequency energy from outside the artery and assessed its safety and efficacy. Here, we report the primary 3-month outcomes.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, single-arm, first-in-human pilot trial enrolled 10 patients with resistant hypertension (office blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg and daytime ambulatory systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥135 mm Hg despite ≥3 antihypertensive agents) across 7 Korean centers. All underwent bilateral extravascular renal denervation on stable antihypertensive regimens. The primary end point was 3-month change in 24-hour ambulatory SBP; safety outcomes were assessed through 3 months.
RESULTS: All 10 patients (median age, 52.5 years; 7 men) completed follow-up. Seven patients (70%) had accessory or early branching arteries <3 mm typically ineligible for intravascular renal denervation; all were successfully ablated. Median 24-hour ambulatory SBP decreased by 25.0 mm Hg (P=0.008) and median office SBP by 39.5 mm Hg (P=0.002). Seven of 10 (70%) achieved office SBP <140 mm Hg despite a reduction in median antihypertensive burden from 6.0 to 4.5 agents. No major or procedure-related adverse events occurred; follow-up computed tomography angiography showed no vascular complications and renal function was preserved.
CONCLUSIONS: Extravascular renal denervation using the HyperQure renal denervation System warrants evaluation in a larger controlled trial, particularly in patients with complex renal arterial anatomy.

Title: Non-invasive vascular assessment in gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period: a systematic review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate evidence on non-invasive vascular assessment techniques used during pregnancy and/or the postpartum period to identify vascular abnormalities associated with gestational hypertension and explore potential implications for long-term cardiovascular health.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and gray literature (to May-2024) identified studies assessing vascular structure or function using pulse-wave velocity, carotid intima-media thickness, flow-mediated dilation, ophthalmic artery Doppler, and retinal imaging. Forty-nine studies involving 32,683 participants. Due to the heterogeneity in study design and methodology, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Women with gestational hypertension generally demonstrated increased arterial stiffness (elevated pulse wave velocity and augmentation index), impaired endothelial function (reduced flow-mediated dilation), and increased intima-media thickness during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Several studies reported persistence of these abnormalities from weeks to years after delivery, although findings were inconsistent. Ophthalmic artery Doppler studies showed variable alterations in peak systolic velocity ratios and pulsatility index reported in hypertensive pregnancies. Retinal imaging identified alterations in retinal vessel caliber during pregnancy and the postpartum period, with some abnormalities reported up to six years postpartum.
CONCLUSION: Non-invasive vascular assessments can help identify macrovascular, microvascular, and endothelial abnormalities in women with gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Although some abnormalities persist beyond delivery and may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk, evidence remains insufficient to support their use as independent predictors of future cardiovascular events. Further standardized, prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine their prognostic and clinical value.

Title: Volumetric Quantification of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs) in Coronary Artery Disease.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) have been reported as correlates of several systemic conditions. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, number, area, and volume of RIPLs and to evaluate their association with coronary artery disease (CAD) using a contemporary imaged coronary angiography (CA) cohort.
METHODS: CA patients were imaged using an SS-OCTA device during the same visit. Structural volumes comprising 500 B-scans were pixel-wise annotated by three graders. RIPLs were quantified by presence, count, area and volume for the first time. CAD severity was assessed using the Gensini score (GS). Associations between RIPL metrics and CAD were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Multivariable and age and sex adjusted models were calculated. Multiple testing corrections were applied to primary analyses.
RESULTS: RIPLs were detected in 38.0% of eyes. In models with the Gensini score (GS) as outcome, RIPL metrics showed weak and inconsistent trends and were not statistically significant, especially after adjustment. The GS showed no significant associations with RIPL presence (β = 0.132, P = 0.102), area (β = 0.173, P = 0.093), count (β = 0.023, P = 0.165), or volume (β = 0.240, P = 0.085) either. Cardiovascular risk factors were not independently associated with RIPL metrics. Those negative findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses using the SYNTAX II and SCORE2.
CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary coronary angiography cohort with high-density OCT imaging, RIPL burden was not significantly associated with CAD and no robust or proportional association with CAD severity was found. In this work, no other disease specific associations could be established.

Title: Trends in Anti-Hyperglycemic Medicines Among US Adults With Diabetes and a History of Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes among adults with a history of stroke is associated with increased risks of recurrent vascular events and disability and greater healthcare costs. Contemporary glucose-lowering strategies now prioritize individualized therapy based on cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic factors over glycemic targets alone. However, national evidence on patterns of glucose-lowering medication use for this dual-diagnosis population is limited.
METHODS: We analyzed serial cross-sectional MEPS data from 2017 to 2023 to characterize glucose-lowering medication use among US civilian, noninstitutionalized adults aged ≥ 18 years with self-reported diabetes and a history of stroke. Medication classes were defined via Multum codes and standardized names. Weighted prevalence with 95% CIs and linear trends were estimated. Medication use was compared between adults with and without a history of stroke using base models adjusted for sociodemographic factors and expanded models additionally adjusted for coronary disease history, annual recorded chronic kidney disease, heart failure, obesity, and approximate diabetes duration. Additional analyses used an alternative ICD-based case definition requiring E11 and I63 records within the same survey year.
RESULTS: Among 2241 person-years (representing 3.05 million annually), 82.4% used any glucose-lowering agent. Metformin (52.2%), insulin (35.6%), sulfonylureas (23.1%), GLP-1RAs (10.5%), DPP-4is (10.5%), and SGLT2is (9.4%) were most common. GLP-1RA/SGLT2i use rose from 8.7% to 33.8% (OR per year, 1.36; p < 0.001), whereas the downward trend in DPP-4i use was not statistically significant (OR per year, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.83-1.01; p = 0.074). In the base models, stroke history was associated with higher odds of insulin use (OR, 1.57) and lower odds of metformin use (OR, 0.78). After additional clinical adjustment, these associations were attenuated (ORs, 1.26 and 0.86, respectively), and neither met the exploratory multiplicity-adjusted threshold. The alternative ICD-based cohort included 125 person-years; trend estimates were imprecise, and some adjusted associations differed from those in the primary analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Adoption of newer agents increased markedly, yet most stroke survivors with diabetes still did not receive GLP-1RAs or SGLT2is by 2023. The metformin and insulin associations were attenuated after additional clinical adjustment, and neither met the exploratory multiplicity-adjusted significance threshold. Medication-use patterns among adults with diabetes and a history of stroke warrant further investigation using data that capture clinical characteristics and treatment timing.

Title: The Effect of Shoulder Support on Shoulder Subluxation in Stroke Survivors Based on Ultrasonography Findings: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a standardized shoulder support in reducing shoulder subluxation, alleviating pain, and improving upper limb motor function and functional independence in stroke survivors using ultrasonography as the primary outcome measure for subluxation.
METHODS: In this single-blind randomized controlled trial, 40 stroke survivors with clinically confirmed shoulder subluxation were randomly allocated to either an intervention group (n = 20) or a control group (n = 20). Both groups received conventional rehabilitation consisting of 45-min sessions, 5 days per week, over a seven-week period. Participants in the intervention group additionally wore a standardized shoulder support during waking hours. Outcome evaluations were performed at baseline (before the intervention), week 3 (mid-intervention), and week 7 (end of the intervention) by independent assessors (physicians and rehabilitation therapists) who were blinded to group allocation. The primary and secondary endpoints included ultrasonographic measurement of the Acromion-Greater Tuberosity (AGT) distance, pain intensity assessed by the visual analog scale (VAS), upper extremity motor performance measured with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA), and functional independence evaluated using the Functional Independence Measure (FIM).
RESULTS: Within-group analyses revealed statistically significant changes in shoulder subluxation (p = 0.02), pain reduction (p < 0.001), upper limb function (p < 0.05), and functional independence (p = 0.001) in both groups over time. However, between-group comparisons showed no significant differences in any of the outcome measures (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Adding a standardized shoulder support to conventional rehabilitation did not produce a statistically significant additional benefit over 7 weeks in reducing shoulder subluxation, pain, or improving upper-limb motor function and functional independence. The observed changes over time should be interpreted in the context of rehabilitation received by both groups, spontaneous recovery, and other time-related factors cannot be distinguished.

Title: White Blood Cell Count Is Associated With Hospitalisation for Heart Failure in Patients With ATTR Cardiac Amyloidosis.
Abstract:
AIMS AND BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is the most common form of cardiac amyloidosis leading to restrictive cardiomyopathy and progressive heart failure. The prognostic relevance of inflammatory biomarkers is unknown so far. This study aims to evaluate an association of white blood cell (WBC) count and clinical outcome in form of hospitalisation for heart failure in ATTR-CM patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: WBC count was assessed in 150 patients (median age 80 [76-82] years; 13.3% female) with ATTR-CM from the West German Amyloidosis Center. Most patients (95.3%) received transthyretin stabilizer therapy. The cohort was divided into patients with low and high WBC count by median split. Hospitalisation for heart failure was defined as primary endpoint. The median follow-up time was 825 (728-932) days. ATTR-CM patients with high WBC count showed higher prevalence of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) at baseline assessment. High WBC count was mainly driven by a relative increase in neutrophils. During follow-up incidence of hospitalisation for heart failure was higher in patients with high WBC count (log-rank p = 0.035). Cox regression confirmed an association between WBC count and occurrence of hospitalisation due to heart failure (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.130; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.015-1.257; p = 0.025), which was unaffected after adjustment for further confounders.
CONCLUSIONS: Increased WBC count was associated with incidence of hospitalisation for heart failure in ATTR-CM patients, indicating a potential for inflammatory biomarkers in disease monitoring.

Title: Adoption of ESC Guideline-Directed Heart Failure Pharmacotherapy and Outcomes: A Nationwide Claims-Based Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: The actual European heart failure (HF) guidelines recommend the combination of four drugs as a standard therapy (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEI)/angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB)/angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI); beta-blocker (BB); mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA); sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT-2i)) in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). We investigated the current use of this combined treatment in comparison to partly using these drugs in routine data with respect to outcomes of mortality and readmission.
METHODS: We included anonymized data from all patients who were insured with Germany's largest health insurer and had a claims record for hospitalization (2021-2023, follow-up in 2024) with a primary hospital diagnosis of HF. The use of different combinations of the four drug classes and their association with mortality and readmission within 91-365 days following the index stay were analysed (n = 307,755). Data were adjusted for a large set of potential confounders including age, sex, and comorbidities. In addition, the frequency of different 2-, 3-, and 4-drug heart failure medications was assessed from 2019 to 2023.
RESULTS: In 2019 the dominant combination of drugs was ACEI/ARB and BB in nearly 37.84% of all cases. By 2023, the dominating combination was ACEI/ARB/ARNI, BB and SGLT-2i with or without an additional MRA (40.85%). The complete four-pillar therapy was prescribed in 21.81% of cases, while the old combination of ACEI/ARB and BB declined to 21.07%. Outcomes were assessed in 307,755 cases. In total, 55,985 of 298,535 (18.8%) included HF patients died 91-365 days after hospital discharge. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models indicated a significantly lower mortality risk when patients had a combined treatment of all four drugs compared to a two-drug therapy (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.86-0.92). The four-drug therapy was more effective with respect to mortality compared to the three-drug combination with an MRA (0.85, 95% CI 0.82-0.89). The comparison with a three-drug combination including an SGLT-2i performed equally (0.99, CI 0.95-1.03). Female sex was an independent negative predictor of four-drug therapy prescription after multivariable adjustment (AOR 0.62, 95% CI 0.60-0.63).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that the comprehensive four-drug therapy for heart failure is increasingly implemented in routine care and is independently associated with lower mortality and readmission rates. A three-drug combination including an SGLT-2i may be equivalent in selected cases. Female sex is associated with a lower likelihood of four-drug therapy prescription. These hypothesis-generating results underscore the necessity of investigating sex-specific clinical phenotypes and prescribing patterns in heart failure populations.

Title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing.
METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases.
CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

Title: Blood cell aggregation as a hemorheological marker of long-term clinical outcome after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with coronary artery disease.
Abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated serial blood cell aggregation changes after PCI in CAD patients and their 12-month outcomes.MethodsWe prospectively enrolled 120 elective PCI CAD patients and 50 frequency-matched controls. Blood was collected pre-PCI, on Days 3, 8, and Month 3. Erythrocyte aggregation index (EAI) was assessed by TAS-plus aggregometry. Patients were grouped into Group I (favorable, n = 106) and Group II (repeat PCI, n = 14).ResultsCAD patients showed higher baseline EAI (0.43 ± 0.06vs.0.29 ± 0.04, p < 0.001), fibrinogen (4.1 ± 0.6vs.2.9 ± 0.4 g/L, p < 0.001), and leukocyte aggregation (32.4 ± 5.8%vs.21.4 ± 4.2%, p < 0.001) than controls. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed a significant group-by-time interaction for EAI (F(3, 354) = 5.12, p = 0.002). Over 3 months, Group I showed progressive EAI normalization (0.42 ± 0.05 to 0.31 ± 0.03, p < 0.001), whereas Group II maintained elevated EAI (0.46 ± 0.07 to 0.44 ± 0.06, p = 0.245). Leukocyte aggregation increased transiently at Day 3 in both CAD groups (39.8 ± 6.7%vs.40.1 ± 6.5%) and returned to baseline by Month 3 (31.8 ± 5.4% vs. 32.1 ± 5.5%, p = 0.842), showing no persistent between-group differences in this cohort. ADP-induced platelet aggregation was significantly suppressed post-PCI at Day 3 (50.2 ± 7.6%vs.50.7 ± 7.4%, p < 0.001) without between-group differences.ConclusionsPersistent erythrocyte hyperaggregation post-PCI is associated with recurrent ischemia and repeat revascularization and may represent a potential biomarker for clinical risk stratification, pending validation in larger, multicenter prospective studies.

Title: Code Blue Awareness: System Changes to Improve Code Blue Chain of Survival in a Hospital.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Speed of code blue response is vital in intrahospital cardiac arrests. Correct activation of the dedicated team is the first step of the chain of survival. We describe an improvement implementation strategy to improve knowledge of code blue activation in a newly opened community hospital.
METHODS: Staff from various domains were randomly invited to participate in a baseline anonymous survey on knowledge and awareness of how to activate code blue. A comprehensive root cause analysis using the Ishikawa Diagram and Human Factors Analysis and Classification System was performed by the Code Blue Committee members. Four interventions targeting the root causes were instituted. Following the interventions, another anonymous survey was performed a few months later to measure the proportion of staff who correctly activated code blue. The respondents were also asked which intervention aided them the most.
RESULTS: The proportion of staff with correct code blue activation in Outram Community Hospital increased more than 4-fold from 19.3% to 88.4%. The intervention in which staff cards were affixed with the code blue telephone number may have the greatest likelihood for successful recall.
CONCLUSION: We successfully improved code blue activation awareness in a new hospital through our improvement initiatives. Further work is ongoing with looking at improving the end-to-end process of the code blue response.

Title: Inflammatory biomarkers as predictors of complications after endovascular aneurysm repair in patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm: a focused narrative review.
Abstract: Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) reduces early morbidity and mortality in anatomically suitable patients with infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm, but long-term durability is limited by endoleaks, adverse aneurysm sac remodeling, and the need for reinterventions. This focused narrative review examines whether inflammatory biomarkers can help predict these complications. The evidence supports two biologically related but clinically distinct settings. First, post-implantation syndrome (PIS) is an early sterile inflammatory response. Higher preoperative white blood cell (WBC) count, C-reactive protein (CRP), and systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI), along with greater new-onset thrombus, have been associated with its occurrence. Postoperative CRP, interleukin-6 (IL-6), and leukocyte changes reflect its intensity. Second, persistent type II endoleak and adverse sac behavior have been linked to systemic inflammatory disease, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), cytokines including interleukin-1, interleukin-8, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, and dynamic matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) profiles. Serial CRP changes and higher preoperative NLR and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) have also been associated with sac expansion or failure to regress. However, acute PIS does not consistently predict late endoleak or sac expansion, and most biomarker studies are small, single-center, and heterogeneous. Biomarkers may therefore complement, but cannot replace, imaging surveillance. Standardized prospective studies are needed to validate temporal biomarker panels and determine whether they improve clinical decision-making.

Title: Impact of Opioid Exposure on the Coronary Microvasculature in ANOCA: A Coronary Microvascular Disease Registry Analysis.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA) accounts for up to 50% of patients undergoing angiography for chest pain, with many cases due to coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD). Opioids are often prescribed to patients for multiple indications, and their effects on coronary microcirculation are unclear.
AIMS: To investigate the association between opioid exposure and coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients with ANOCA, focusing on differences in CMD prevalence, CFR, IMR, and MRR between opioid users and non-users, and whether opioid exposure independently predicts impaired microvascular vasodilatory function.
METHODS: A total of 367 ANOCA patients from the Coronary Microvascular Disease Registry (NCT05960474) who underwent invasive coronary function testing (August 2021 to March 2025) were analyzed. CMD was defined by coronary flow reserve (CFR) < 2.5 and index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) ≥ 25; microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) < 3.0 indicated impaired vasodilatory capacity. All indices were measured by bolus thermodilution. Opioid exposure during the 12 months preceding testing was obtained from the electronic health record and Surescripts database. Patients were categorized as opioid users (≥ 1 prescription > 3 days) or non-users, and stratified as short-term (< 90 days) or long-term (≥ 90 days). The primary outcome was the comparison of CMD prevalence and physiologic parameters (CFR, IMR, MRR) between exposure groups. Because groups differed at baseline, unadjusted comparisons were descriptive; the primary interpretation used a multivariable model of log-transformed MRR adjusted for hypertension, hemoglobin, and chronic kidney disease.
RESULTS: Opioid users had more hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and CCS class IV angina, and lower hemoglobin (12.38 ± 1.60 vs. 13.32 ± 1.58 g/dL; all p < 0.05). CMD prevalence was numerically higher among opioid users (19/55; 34.5%) versus non-users (85/312; 27.2%), but not significantly (p = 0.27). Mean CFR was lower in opioid users (2.84 ± 1.65 vs. 3.32 ± 1.80; p = 0.06), suggesting a trend toward impaired coronary flow. In unadjusted analysis, mean MRR was lower in opioid users (3.27 ± 1.78 vs. 4.02 ± 2.32; p = 0.01). Mean of IMR was similar between groups (18.51 ± 10.58 vs. 18.60 ± 12.24; p = 0.96). After adjustment, the MRR difference was no longer significant (β = -0.11 on the log scale, an estimated 10.5% lower MRR; 95% CI -0.30 to 0.08; p = 0.25); hemoglobin was the only independent correlate (p = 0.011).
CONCLUSIONS: In ANOCA, opioid users represented a distinct clinical phenotype with greater comorbidity, lower hemoglobin, and more severe angina. Their lower unadjusted MRR did not persist after adjustment, and CMD prevalence, CFR, and IMR were similar between groups, suggesting that opioid exposure marks a more complex clinical state rather than independently impairing microvascular vasodilatory function. Residual confounding cannot be excluded, and these exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Coronary Microvascular Disease Registry, clinicaltrials.gov, NCT05960474.

Title: New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Incidence, Outcomes, and Treatment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is the recommended treatment in advanced coronary heart disease. More than 28 000 isolated CABG procedures are performed each year in Germany: almost one-third of patients have transient, new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) before they are discharged from the hospital. In this narrative review, we outline the detection, incidence, outcomes, and treatment of POAF after CABG on the basis of current evidence.
METHODS: This narrative review is based on guidelines and pertinent publications that were retrieved by a selective search in PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov. In the analysis, randomized controlled trials concerning CABG patients were given priority over observational studies and those involving mixed cardiac surgical cohorts.
RESULTS: Nationwide registries have documented a 30-31% incidence of POAF after CABG, but recent data obtained by continuous monitoring indicate a cumulative 1-year incidence of 48% (95% confidence interval [41; 55]). The atrial fibrillation (AF) burden (time in AF divided by the duration of monitoring) after CABG is low (0.07%), and episodes most commonly arise in the first month after surgery. POAF can be treated acutely with either rate or rhythm control, depending on physician preference. The evidence on long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) for patients with POAF after CABG is mixed; current data suggest it may not be indicated.
CONCLUSION: POAF often arises shortly after CABG and mainly consists of brief episodes with a low overall atrial fibrillation burden. The role of long-term OAC remains unclear. The guideline recommendations for CABG patients should be reassessed in the light of current evidence.

Title: Off-Pump versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated.
RESULTS: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099).
CONCLUSION: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

Title: Hemorrhagic Cardiac Tamponade in an End-Stage Renal Disease Patient on Apixaban.
Abstract: Direct oral anticoagulants are used for stroke prevention in selected patients with atrial fibrillation who receive hemodialysis. Randomized trial data remain limited in this population, and the anticoagulant effect of a given dose may vary considerably between patients. We report a 56-year-old man receiving hemodialysis three times weekly who was taking apixaban 5 mg twice daily and developed persistent hypotension and abdominal pain during dialysis. The early findings suggested dialysis-associated hypotension or sepsis. Emergency department point-of-care cardiac ultrasound showed a large circumferential pericardial effusion, leading to urgent cardiology evaluation for obstructive shock. Computed tomography obtained during the same evaluation described the effusion as large and possibly hemorrhagic. Pericardiocentesis was unsuccessful because most of the fluid was posterior. Shortly after transfer to the intensive care unit, the patient developed pulseless electrical activity arrest and underwent an emergent subxiphoid pericardial window. Approximately 450 mL of bloody fluid was drained, followed by hemodynamic improvement. Cytology showed no malignant cells, and fluid cultures were negative. This case also highlights the uncertainty surrounding the use of full-dose apixaban in patients receiving hemodialysis, particularly after a major bleeding event.

Title: Hyperacute total and item-level NIHSS evolution after intravenous thrombolysis in anterior-circulation ischemic stroke: a Romanian tertiary stroke center cohort.
Abstract: Hyperacute neurological change after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is commonly summarized using the total National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, which may obscure changes in individual deficits. This study aimed to describe total and item-level NIHSS evolution during the first 2 hours after IVT in anterior-circulation acute ischemic stroke. We retrospectively analyzed prospectively recorded data from 124 eligible IVT-treated patients at a Romanian tertiary stroke center in 2024-2025. Median age was 67 years, and 62.1% were male. The NIHSS was assessed at baseline, 1 hour, 2 hours, and discharge. Hyperacute total-score changes were analyzed descriptively and with Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, while item-level recovery and recovered and worsened NIHSS item-points were summarized descriptively. Median NIHSS decreased from 6 (interquartile range [IQR] 5-9) at baseline to 4 (IQR 3-7) at 1 hour and 4 (IQR 2-5) at 2 hours. Improvement relative to baseline occurred in 72.6% of patients at 1 hour and 79.8% at 2 hours. Between 1 and 2 hours, 42.7% improved further, 53.2% remained unchanged, and 4.0% worsened, despite an unchanged group median. The NIHSS differed significantly across baseline, 1 hour, and 2 hours (Friedman χ2(2) = 152; P < 0.001). By 2 hours, improvement proportions were numerically higher than at 1 hour for 14 of 15 NIHSS components, and 353 item-points had been recovered among baseline-positive deficits. Hyperacute neurological evolution after IVT was heterogeneous across individual deficits. Item-level analysis characterized the neurological profile underlying aggregate change and may help contextualize subsequent monitoring, assistance, and rehabilitation needs.

Title: Stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation: radiobiology, clinical evidence, and emerging applications.
Abstract: STereotactic Arrhythmia Radioablation (STAR) has emerged as a promising non-invasive treatment for patients with refractory cardiac arrhythmias who are unsuitable for or have failed conventional catheter ablation. Initially developed for ventricular tachycardia (VT), STAR has demonstrated encouraging efficacy in reducing arrhythmia burden while avoiding the risks associated with invasive procedures. More recently, limited and early clinical experience has explored the potential application of STAR in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), including the feasibility of non-invasive pulmonary vein isolation; however, clinical evidence in AF remains anecdotal and investigational. Despite these advances, the biological mechanisms underlying STAR remain incompletely understood. While early hypotheses attributed its therapeutic effects primarily to radiation-induced fibrosis, accumulating evidence suggests that rapid anti-arrhythmic effects are mediated by early electrophysiological reprogramming and conduction remodeling, whereas delayed vascular injury, inflammation, and fibrosis may contribute to durable substrate modification and long-term toxicity. This evolving paradigm has important implications for optimizing radiation dose, fractionation strategies, and minimizing cardiac toxicity. Advances in imaging, electroanatomical mapping, and treatment planning are further improving treatment precision. Ongoing prospective clinical trials and international collaborative initiatives are expected to provide robust evidence regarding efficacy, safety, and long-term outcomes. This review summarizes current knowledge on the radiobiological mechanisms, clinical applications, and future perspectives of STAR, highlighting the key challenges for its integration into contemporary cardiac electrophysiology, as well as describing our current clinical trial investigating the role of dose and fractionation for this technique.

Title: Non-atherosclerotic vasculopathies in stroke: a pathobiology-based framework.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-atherosclerotic vasculopathies (NAV) are important causes of stroke, particularly in younger adults, but remain difficult to classify due to overlapping mechanisms and imaging features.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to propose a three-compartment framework that organises NAV according to the dominant biological process underlying the observed vascular phenotype: structural arterial abnormalities, functional dysregulation of vascular tone or autoregulation, and immune- or infection-mediated vascular injury.
METHODS: We conducted a clinically oriented narrative review of PubMed and Embase, focusing on publications from 2015 onwards and prioritising guidelines, systematic reviews, major observational studies, and randomised trials where available. For this review, NAV were defined as selected cerebrovascular disorders in which a non-atherosclerotic abnormality of arterial structure, vascular tone or autoregulation, or immune- or infection-mediated vascular injury is central to the neurological phenotype.
RESULTS: NAV can be conceptualised into structural, functional, and inflammatory compartments. Structural disorders involve arterial wall pathologies, functional disorders reflect dysregulation of vascular tone, and inflammatory disorders involve immune-mediated vascular injury. Imaging, particularly vessel wall magnetic resonance imaging, provides supportive differentiation, although interpretation requires clinical correlation. The framework is intended to complement, rather than replace, aetiological and imaging-based classifications by linking vascular phenotypes to mechanism-directed diagnostic testing and initial management.
CONCLUSION: A dominant-mechanism framework may help clinicians structure the evaluation of NAV and align diagnostic work-up and early management with the most likely underlying biology.

Title: OCT angiography characterizes time- and diameter-dependent intestinal microvascular alterations in acute mesenteric ischemia.
Abstract:
