SIGNIFICANCE: Acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) is associated with high mortality, and accurate assessment of intestinal viability and the extent of ischemic injury remains challenging. Microvascular alterations may precede overt mucosal structural damage but are difficult to monitor dynamically.
AIM: We aim to investigate the ability of OCT/OCTA to dynamically quantify intestinal mucosal microvascular alterations during AMI and to determine their temporal and vessel-diameter-dependent associations with histological injury.
APPROACH: AMI was induced in mice by mesenteric artery ligation. In a longitudinal cohort ( n = 8  ), OCT was performed at baseline and 0.5, 1, 2, and 4 h after ischemia to quantify vessel length and vessel perfused density (VPD) in three diameter categories ( < 20    μ m  , 20 to 50    μ m  , and > 50    μ m  ). In a separate cross-sectional cohort ( n = 40  ), mice were randomly assigned to sham or ischemia groups ( n = 8  each). OCT was also used to detect the vascular parameters of intestinal mucosal microcirculation. Histological injury was assessed by villus height, crypt depth, and Chiu's score. Correlations between microvascular and histological parameters were analyzed. Receiver operating characteristic curve was used to assess vascular parameters for discriminating severe intestinal injury.
RESULTS: Ischemia induced time- and diameter-dependent microvascular impairment. With the prolongation of ischemia, both vessel length and VPD decreased significantly across all vessel diameter categories ( P < 0.05  ). The length and VPD of vessels > 50    μ m  decreased significantly faster than those of vessels < 20    μ m  ( P < 0.05  ). Notably, reductions in the vascular parameters of 20 to 50    μ m  and > 50    μ m  vessels were observed as early as 0.5 h after ischemia and preceded significant elevation of Chiu's score. Villus height and crypt depth progressively decreased, whereas Chiu's score increased with prolonged ischemia. OCT-derived vascular parameters across all diameter categories were positively correlated with villus height and crypt depth and negatively correlated with Chiu's score (all P < 0.05  ). In addition, OCT-derived vascular parameters had significant diagnostic performance for severe mucosal injury (  Chiu ' s   score ≥ 3  ).
CONCLUSIONS: OCT enables real-time and quantitative assessment of intestinal mucosal microvascular alterations in AMI. Diameter-dependent microvascular impairment precedes overt histological injury and is associated with the severity of mucosal damage. These findings support the potential use of OCTA for intraoperative assessment of intestinal viability and provide a basis for future identification of ischemic transition zones and optimization of bowel resection boundaries.

Title: Preventive Linear Ablation Strategy for Intra-Atrial Reentrant Tachycardia Following Cardiac Surgery.
Abstract:
AIMS: Intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia (IART) frequently occurs following cardiac surgery due to scar-related conduction abnormalities. While advances in mapping technologies have improved the acute success rate of catheter ablation, arrhythmia recurrence remains a significant clinical concern. This study aimed to evaluate whether a preventive linear ablation strategy guided by voltage mapping improves the long-term success rate of catheter ablation in patients with IART post-cardiac surgery.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 46 consecutive patients following cardiac surgery who underwent atrial tachycardia ablation between 2022 and 2024 were enrolled in the study group. After activation mapping-guided ablation for ongoing IART, preventive linear ablation was performed based on voltage mapping. Fifty consecutive sex- and age-matched patients with cardiac surgery undergoing activation mapping-guided ablation alone served as the historical control group between 2018 and 2021. At a mean follow-up of 21 ± 4.9 months, the rate of freedom from atrial arrhythmias was significantly higher in the study group compared to the control group (82.6% vs. 64.0%; p = 0.019). Despite the improved outcomes, the study group had significantly longer total procedure times (192 ± 37 vs. 126 ± 25 min; p < 0.001) and radiofrequency ablation durations (29 ± 5 vs. 20 ± 6 min; p < 0.001). However, there were no significant differences in complication rates between the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Preventive linear ablation strategy was associated with improved arrhythmia-free survival in patients with IART post cardiac surgery, but these exploratory findings require confirmation in future prospective studies.

Title: The GIPMER 3-Method (Blood-Hegar-Silk) Approach for intraoperative localization of apical muscular ventricular septal defects via limited right ventricular apical ventriculotomy: a five-patient case series.
Journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Apical muscular ventricular septal defects (VSDs) are surgically challenging because of their deep location within the trabeculated right ventricle, often resulting in difficult intraoperative localization and residual shunting.
AIM: This study reports the early feasibility of a structured three-step intraoperative localization strategy, termed the GIPMER 3-Method Approach (Govind Ballabh Pant Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education & Research), developed to assist in identifying apical muscular VSDs during surgical repair.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single-center prospective feasibility case series included 5 pediatric patients with apical muscular VSDs who underwent surgical closure over a one-year period following standard preoperative evaluation. A structured three-step intraoperative localization strategy (the GIPMER 3-Method) was applied via a limited right ventricular apical ventriculotomy. Outcomes were assessed using intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and postoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) at 48 hours and at 1 month.
RESULTS: Complete closure was achieved in all 5 patients, with no residual VSD detected on intraoperative or early postoperative imaging. Median cardiopulmonary bypass time was 78 minutes (range: 70-90), and median aortic cross-clamp time was 42 minutes (range: 35-50). No major early postoperative complications, including arrhythmias or low cardiac output, were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small prospective case series, the GIPMER 3-Method Approach demonstrated technical feasibility for early localization of apical muscular VSDs. While early outcomes were favorable, these results should be interpreted as preliminary, and larger studies with longer follow-up are required to evaluate safety, durability, and comparative effectiveness against established techniques.

Title: A combination of melatonin and nicotinamide mononucleotide alleviates inflammation and enhances isolated heart function in aged rats following ischemia-reperfusion injury.
Journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
Abstract: Aging markedly increases vulnerability to cardiovascular disorders, including acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery disease. Although melatonin (M) and nicotinamide mono-nucleotide (N) have each shown cardioprotective properties, their combined effects on ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury in the aged heart remain unclear. This study investigated co-administration of M and N enhances cardiac functional recovery and reduces inflammatory responses following myocardial IR injury in aged rats. Forty adult male Wistar rats (n = 8/group) were randomly assigned to five groups: Sham, IR, M (IR + M), N (IR + N), and N + M (IR + N + M). Cardiac function was evaluated after IR by measuring coronary flow, heart rate, left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and left ventricular developed pressure. Melatonin was administered at 50.00 µM in the reperfusion solution for 15 min after 30 min of ischemia, N was administered intraperitoneally at 100 mg kg-1 every other day for 28 days. Creatine kinase and inflammatory markers, including interleukin IL-1β, IL-6, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and nuclear factor kappa B, were also assessed. IR significantly impaired coronary flow and heart rate, both of which were improved by M and N treatment. These agents also reduced left ventricular end-diastolic pressure and improved left ventricular developed pressure recovery, with the combined therapy producing the greatest effect. Likewise, creatine kinase and inflammatory marker levels were significantly elevated in the IR group but markedly reduced by treatment, especially by combined administration. These findings suggest that M and N exert additive cardioprotective effects against IR injury in aged rats.

Title: Archiving of Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory Procedures and Records of Radiation Exposure: A Single-Center Experience.
Abstract: Background and objective Cardiac catheterization laboratories (Cath Labs) increasingly perform fluoroscopy-guided diagnostic and interventional procedures, making systematic monitoring of radiation exposure important. Structured archiving can support radiation surveillance, quality assurance, and procedural evaluation. This study aimed to examine dose-area product/kerma-area product (DAP/KAP), cumulative air kerma (CAK/Ka,r), and fluoroscopy time, with particular attention to variation by procedure type and the influence of BMI. Methods A hospital-based retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory of Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. A total of 190 archived patient records were analyzed. Demographic variables, procedure category, fluoroscopy time, DAP/KAP, and CAK were evaluated. The association between BMI and radiation exposure was also examined. Results The mean age of the cohort was 55.88 ± 11.04 years and mean BMI was 26.78 ± 3.87 kg/m². Coronary angiography (CAG) + percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA) was the most frequently performed procedure (70.5%). Median DAP/KAP and CAK were lowest for diagnostic CAG and substantially higher for CAG + PTCA. The median fluoroscopy time was 1.9 minutes for CAG, 8.3 minutes for CAG + PTCA, and 13.1 minutes for other procedures. BMI demonstrated a significant positive correlation with DAP/KAP (r = 0.470, p < 0.001) and CAK (r = 0.469, p < 0.001). DAP/KAP and CAK demonstrated a very strong positive correlation (r = 0.941, p < 0.001). No radiation-related complications or dose alerts were documented. Conclusions Radiation exposure varied by procedure type and BMI. Systematic Cath Lab archiving and continuous monitoring of DAP/KAP, CAK, and fluoroscopy time can provide useful baseline data for radiation safety, quality assurance, and dose optimization.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Hemoglobin Improvement in Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Myeloproliferative Neoplasms: Mechanistic Rationale and Emerging Clinical Evidence.
Abstract: Anemia represents one of the most clinically significant and therapeutically challenging complications in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN), particularly in myelofibrosis. It is associated with increased symptom burden, transfusion dependence, and reduced overall survival. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have consistently demonstrated increases in hemoglobin levels across multiple large randomized clinical trials in cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic diseases, raising interest in their potential role as modulators of erythropoiesis. This narrative review aimed to provide a comprehensive and mechanistically grounded overview of the role of SGLT2 inhibitors in improving hemoglobin levels in patients with MDS and MPN. A literature review was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar, focusing on the database from inception to June 2026. Studies evaluating SGLT2 inhibitors and hematologic outcomes in MDS, MDS/MPN overlap syndromes, myelofibrosis, or other MPNs were included. Both clinical and mechanistic studies were included. Current evidence in MDS and MPN remains limited to small observational cohorts, retrospective studies, and case reports. Across the available clinical studies in patients with MDS and MPN, SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with increases in hemoglobin, generally ranging from 1.0 to 1.6 g/dL. Specifically, a median peak hemoglobin increase of approximately 1.2 g/dL was reported among non-transfusion-dependent patients with MDS/MDS-MPN overlap receiving SGLT2 inhibitors, while patients with myelofibrosis receiving predominantly empagliflozin or dapagliflozin had a median increase of 1.0 g/dL. In MDS and myelofibrosis, these findings may reflect improvement in ineffective erythropoiesis, whereas in non-anemic MPN subtypes, the observed changes may instead represent erythrocytosis. Preliminary observational findings suggest a potential erythropoietic effect of SGLT2 inhibitors; however, whether this translates into a therapeutic benefit in MDS or MPN remains uncertain and requires prospective and mechanistic validation.

Title: Limb Salvage Outcomes Following Endovascular Revascularization for Peripheral Artery Disease in a Southern Indian Population: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Background Peripheral artery disease (PAD), particularly chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), is associated with a high risk of limb loss and significant morbidity. Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population. Materials and methods This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary vascular care center and included 142 patients with symptomatic PAD who underwent endovascular intervention between July 2023 and June 2025. Clinical severity and lesion complexity were assessed using the Rutherford classification and the TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) classification, respectively. The primary endpoint was limb salvage at one year, defined as freedom from major amputation. Secondary endpoints included technical success, restenosis, and procedure-related complications. Results The study population was predominantly male (87.3%) with a mean age of 61.11 ± 12.90 years. Most patients (78.1%) presented with CLTI. Technical success was achieved in 87.3% of procedures. At one-year follow-up, limb salvage was achieved in 95.8% of patients, with major amputation occurring in 4.2% and minor amputation in 9.1%. Restenosis was observed in 14.7% of cases. Procedure-related complications were infrequent and mostly minor, with one all-cause death during follow-up. Conclusions ET is a safe and effective modality for limb salvage in PAD patients, particularly in populations with a high prevalence of diabetes and advanced disease at presentation. High limb salvage rates can be achieved even in cohorts predominantly comprising patients with CLTI, supporting an endovascular-first approach in appropriately selected patients.

Title: The uric acid-to-homocysteine ratio as a prognostic marker for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: A national population-based study.
Journal: Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The homocysteine (Hcy) paradox, the failure of Hcy-lowering therapies to consistently reduce cardiovascular events, remains a major challenge in metabolic medicine. We hypothesize that adenosine (Ado), a stoichiometric byproduct of Hcy production with vascular protective effects, may be relevant to this paradox.
OBJECTIVES: Because circulating Ado is difficult to measure at scale, uric acid (UA) is a downstream end product of adenosine catabolism, we evaluated the UA-to-Hcy ratio as an exploratory composite index that may capture aspects of Hcy-related purine/adenosine metabolism.
DESIGN: A nationally representative, population-based prospective cohort study.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2006 cycles, including 17,180 participants for all-cause and 14,667 participants for cardiovascular mortality. Survey-weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed non-linearity, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves (timeROC) evaluated predictive performance, and generalized additive models (GAMs) examined associations between B-vitamins and the UA-to-Hcy ratio.
RESULTS: The UA-to-Hcy ratio was inversely associated with all-cause mortality (HR = 0.989 per unit increase; 95% CI, 0.986-0.993) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 0.987 per unit increase; 95% CI, 0.980-0.995), exhibiting nonlinear relationships (P < 0.001). The ratio showed moderate discriminatory performance, with the highest AUCs observed for 5-year all-cause mortality (AUC = 0.691, 95% CI: 0.666-0.716) and cardiovascular mortality (AUC = 0.712, 95% CI: 0.677-0.749). Additionally, vitamin B12 and folate showed an inverted L-shaped association with the ratio (P < 0.001), indicating a saturation effect in their ability to modulate this metabolic balance.
CONCLUSIONS: The UA-to-Hcy ratio was independently associated with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality and showed stable discriminatory performance for mortality prediction in this cohort. Together with the observed B-vitamin saturation pattern, these findings warrant further investigation of Hcy-related purine/adenosine metabolism as a potential contributor to cardiovascular risk.

Title: Evaluation of Neointimal Coverage After Guiding De-escalation of Antiplatelet Treatment in Patients with ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention by Optical Coherence Tomography or Angiography: Rationale and Design of the DAPT-OCT Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) de-escalation strategies including early switching from a potent P2Y12 inhibitor to clopidogrel become attractive for patients with ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI). It is unclear whether DAPT de-escalation after optical coherence tomography (OCT)- or angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves neointimal coverage in STEMI patients who have completed 1-month DAPT with aspirin plus ticagrelor.
METHODS: This report describes the design of a randomized study evaluating the neointimal coverage in STEMI patients after guiding de-escalation of DAPT from aspirin plus ticagrelor to aspirin plus clopidogrel at 1 month after PCI with drug eluting stent implantation by OCT or angiography and 1-month DAPT with aspirin plus ticagrelor. Eighty patients who meet the inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 fashion to the OCT- or angiography-guided group (first randomization). All patients will receive open label ticagrelor plus aspirin for 1 month after the index PCI. At 30 ± 7 days after the index PCI, patients with no major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) or major bleeding (⩾Bleeding Academic Research Consortium [BARC] 3a) will be randomized in a 1:1 fashion to either the ticagrelor plus aspirin group or clopidogrel plus aspirin group for an additional 11 months (second randomization). The primary endpoint is the stent-strut neointimal thickness by OCT assessment at 12-month follow up.
DISCUSSION: The data obtained from DAPT-OCT study will explore the neointimal coverage after guiding de-escalation of antiplatelet treatment in STEMI patients undergoing PCI by OCT.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06339021.

Title: MACS: mild by definition, challenging by nature.
Abstract: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is the most frequent form of cortisol excess in patients with adrenal incidentalomas. Although it lacks the classical phenotype of overt Cushing's syndrome, MACS is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant condition associated with multisystem complications rather than a benign biochemical finding. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, diagnostic limitations, and management of MACS, with particular focus on cardiometabolic, skeletal, muscular, neuropsychiatric, frailty-related, reproductive, and emerging microbiome-related consequences. Chronic exposure to low-grade cortisol excess is being recognized as a factor associated with hypertension, disorders of glucose metabolism, dyslipidemia, increased cardiovascular risk, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, skeletal fragility, impaired muscle function, frailty, sleep and circadian disturbances, cognitive and mood alterations, hypogonadism, and possible changes in gut microbiota. The 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, but its interpretation is limited by assay variability, medication interference, comorbidities, and imperfect reflection of long-term tissue glucocorticoid exposure. Emerging approaches, including steroid profiling, hair cortisol/cortisone, salivary cortisone, inflammatory indices, metabolomic tools, and exploratory biomarkers related to microbial metabolites, may improve risk stratification in the future but remain investigational. Management should be individualized. Adrenalectomy may benefit selected patients with unilateral disease and clinically relevant cortisol-related comorbidities, whereas evidence supporting pharmacological therapy remains limited. MACS should be regarded as a heterogeneous multisystem condition requiring structured clinical assessment and individualized management. Prospective studies are needed to define clinically meaningful endpoints, refine diagnostic thresholds, and identify patients most likely to benefit from intervention.

Title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator.
RESULTS: Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73, p = 0.001; Gray's test p < 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98, p = 0.17; Gray's test p = 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68, p = 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86, p = 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not.
CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.

Title: Peri-procedural immune blood cell count changes and pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory study.
Journal: Kardiochirurgia i torakochirurgia polska = Polish journal of cardio-thoracic surgery
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a minimally invasive treatment for aortic stenosis. Although significant advancements in the TAVI technique have been made, the risk of requiring a permanent pacemaker remains clinically relevant.
AIM: The aim of the study was to analyze the relationship between peri-procedural blood count parameters and the risk of pacemaker implantation after TAVI.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The retrospective study analyzed 115 patients (median (Q1-Q3) age of 76.7 (73.5-81.9) years). Demographic and clinical data were collected. The counts of leukocytes, neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets were assessed before the procedure, on the day of the procedure (8 hours after the procedure), 24, 48, and 72 hours after the procedure, and at hospital discharge. Pre-procedural and post-procedural heart rhythm disturbances have been recorded.
RESULTS: The analysis showed a predominant increase in neutrophil and monocyte counts after the procedure, without differences between subgroups. Moreover, a decrease in lymphocyte counts was observed after TAVI; however, it was less pronounced in patients who required pacemaker implantation. Patients without heart rhythm disturbances experienced a greater decrease in their lymphocyte count. In the multivariable analysis, an increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was an independent factor for pacemaker implantation (OR = 5.2, 95% CI: 1.6-16.3, p = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: After TAVI, increases in neutrophil and monocyte counts and decreases in lymphocyte counts are observed; however, the lymphocyte count decrease is less pronounced in patients with heart rhythm disturbances requiring pacemaker implantation. An increase in lymphocyte count after the procedure was independently associated with pacemaker implantation.

Title: Effects of high-intensity treadmill training on intestinal permeability and myocardial autophagy in rats.
Abstract: In this study, we investigated whether gut microbiota-derived factors contribute to the increase in intestinal permeability and the activation of left ventricular autophagy-related signaling induced by high-intensity treadmill exercise, using an antibiotic-treated rat model. Serum levels of lipopolysaccharide (LPS), LPS-binding protein (LBP), colonic occludin, zonulin, and myocardial autophagy-related signaling were analyzed. A total of 38 specific pathogen-free male Sprague-Dawley rats aged 8 weeks were randomly assigned to four groups: control (n=9), antibiotic control (n=9), exercise (n=10), and antibiotic plus exercise (n=10). Treadmill exercise was performed for 60 min per session, 4 times per week, for 8 weeks. Eight weeks of high-intensity treadmill exercise increased intestinal permeability and elevated circulating levels of gut-derived LPS and LBP. Increased LPS and LBP levels were associated with the activation of adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and upregulation of myocardial autophagy-related markers, including microtubule-associated protein light chain 3 and B-cell lymphoma-2-interacting myosin-like coiled-coil protein. Although increased intestinal permeability was also observed in the antibiotic-treated exercise group, circulating LPS and LBP levels did not increase significantly, nor did AMPK activation or the expression of autophagy-related markers. Prolonged high-intensity treadmill exercise may be associated with increased intestinal permeability and activation of myocardial autophagy-related signaling. The attenuation of the increases in circulating LPS/LBP levels and in myocardial autophagy-related signaling after antibiotic treatment suggests that gut microbiota-derived factors may mediate these gut-heart responses. Optimizing exercise benefits while minimizing risks may require considering both training intensity and gut health in the exercise program design.

Title: Biomarkers for differential diagnosis of myocarditis, acute coronary syndrome, and sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Diagnosing acute myocardial injury remains a significant challenge in contemporary cardiovascular and critical care medicine. Myocarditis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) frequently present with overlapping features, chest pain, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and electrocardiographic abnormalities, yet require divergent management, making rapid and accurate etiological diagnosis essential for optimal patient outcomes.
METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the pathophysiology and biomarker signatures of myocarditis, ACS, and SICM, and examines how these signatures can be integrated into a practical diagnostic approach for the emergency department and intensive care unit.
RESULTS: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) remains the central biomarker of acute myocardial injury, but its kinetics differ across the three conditions. A steep rise and fall in ACS, a sustained moderate elevation in myocarditis, and a gradual, severity-parallel course in sepsis. Among complementary biomarkers, C-reactive protein lacks specificity, whereas procalcitonin supports the recognition of bacterial sepsis in SICM, and natriuretic peptides reflect myocardial wall stress, disproportionately elevated relative to troponin in SICM. Emerging molecular biomarkers, circulating microRNAs (like miR-4763-3p and miR-155) and extracellular matrix remodeling markers, show promise for distinguishing inflammatory from ischemic myocardial injury, but remain investigational owing to the lack of standardized assays and practical constraints on acute bedside use. Therefore diagnosis rests on an integrated, multimodal assessment.
CONCLUSION: The differential diagnosis of acute myocardial injury requires a systematic, biomarker-centered multimodal approach. Future research should prioritize the prospective validation of multi-biomarker panels and the development of rapid non-invasive tools to reduce reliance on emergency coronary angiography.

Title: Impedance-Based Contact Visualization for PulseSelect Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Single-Center Feasibility Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: PulseSelect pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lacks a dedicated contact indicator.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared 63 patients undergoing PVI before and after EnSite Contact Index (CI) implementation. Because electrical isolation does not confirm lesion transmurality, post-procedural unipolar electrograms (u-EGMs) were assessed as acute surrogate markers.
RESULTS: CI guidance was associated with more applications, shorter fluoroscopy, and in an exploratory analysis of analyzable patients, fewer residual high-voltage u-EGMs (1/20 vs. 8/24; p = 0.027). No complications occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: CI-guided PVI was feasible; these procedural and acute electrophysiological associations require prospective validation.

Title: Association between chronic sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors use and right ventricular function in hemodynamically stable patients with acute pulmonary embolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a common cardiovascular disorder associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with prognosis largely determined by the extent of right ventricular (RV) involvement. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF) and exert favorable effects on left ventricular (LV) remodeling; however, their effects on RV function in acute PE remain largely unexplored. We hypothesized that chronic treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors would be associated with a lower incidence of clinical congestion and a more favorable clinical course in patients with acute PE.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared 30 patients receiving chronic SGLT2 inhibitor therapy with 90 controls following 1:3 matching for multiple variables, including age, sex, comorbidities, and background medical therapy. Echocardiographic and clinical outcomes were compared between the groups, including tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), systolic pulmonary artery pressure (SPAP), and clinical congestion.
RESULTS: Patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors had higher TAPSE values (19.4 ± 2.7 vs. 17.3 ± 5, 95% Confidence interval (CI) 0.7-3.5, p = 0.004), fewer signs of clinical congestion [6.7% vs. 25.6%, Odds ratio (OR) 0.21, 95% CI 0.05-0.94, p = 0.03], lower troponin, [14.5 (5.3-51), vs. 64.5 (20-177), 95% CI (33-108), p < 0.001], and lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels, [158 (96-443) vs. 1000 (333-3433), 95% CI (467-1153) pg/mL, p < 0.001]. No significant between-group difference was observed in 1-year readmissions due to dyspnea or clinical congestion [OR 0.34, 95% CI (0.1-1.2), p = 0.13].
CONCLUSIONS: Among hemodynamically stable patients with acute PE, chronic SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with more favorable RV function during the index event; however, this association did not translate into improved long-term clinical outcomes. These findings warrant confirmation in prospective studies.

Title: Physical activity phenotypes from volume-based versus intensity-based wearable metrics: discordant classification and divergent metabolomic, body composition, and cardiac magnetic resonance associations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Consumer wearables report direct volume-based metrics (steps, distance, floors climbed) alongside device-derived metrics generated by manufacturer algorithms (activity-intensity minutes, energy expenditure). Both are widely used to characterize individuals into activity phenotypes, yet whether these representations yield concordant activity phenotypes and biological associations is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To compare activity phenotypes derived from direct accelerometry with those derived from device-derived intensity metrics, and to evaluate each against metabolomic, body composition, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) phenotypes.
METHODS: Using the SingHEART cohort, two hierarchical cluster analyses using Ward linkage yielded five phenotypes each for volume-based and intensity-based metrics. Agreement was quantified by the adjusted Rand index. For analyses, the two high-variability phenotypes were combined, giving four groups: sedentary, average movers, regular exercisers, and high-variability movers. Serum ¹H-NMR metabolomics was analyzed by PERMANOVA with Holm adjustment across pairwise contrasts. Body and CMR associations were assessed using linear regression with false discovery rate correction.
RESULTS: In total, 984 adults (mean age 45.6 years, 48.3% male) wore accelerometers for a mean of 7.1 valid days. The two classifications agreed poorly: adjusted Rand index was 0.18, with only 46.2% assigned identically. Volume-based phenotypes differed in metabolomic profiles (P < .001). Active participants (high-variability movers plus regular exercisers) differed from sedentary participants across 106 of 250 biomarkers (FDR q < 0.05), including higher HDL, lower VLDL, LDL and lower GlycA. Conversely, although intensity-based phenotypes showed a nominally significant omnibus metabolomic association (P = .003), no metabolomic difference was observed between active and sedentary groups defined by intensity-based phenotyping (P = .29). Across 16 body composition and CMR outcomes, volume-based phenotypes were associated with 11 and intensity-based phenotypes with 6, in divergent directions: volume-based high-variability movers showed lower body fat, higher skeletal muscle, and larger ventricular volumes and mass, whereas intensity-based high-variability movers showed higher body mass index and waist circumference.
CONCLUSIONS: Volume-based metrics and intensity-based metrics assign the same individuals to discordant activity phenotypes. Volume-based phenotypes showed more consistent associations across metabolomic, body composition, and cardiac imaging measures. These findings suggest that the choice of wearable-derived metrics substantially influences digital activity phenotyping and its biological interpretation.

Title: Systemic coagulation inflammation index and risk of mortality in peritoneal dialysis patients: a multicenter cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The systemic coagulation inflammation (SCI) index has been investigated as a prognostic marker in several diseases. The aim of this study was to investigate the association of SCI with mortality in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD).
METHODS: A total of 324 incident PD patients who initiated treatment between January 2011 and December 2020 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were stratified using the previously selected outcome-specific SCI cutoffs. Mortality associations were assessed using Cox regression and, for cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality, competing-risk methods.
RESULTS: Patients were stratified with three groups based on the optimal cutoff value of SCI index. In the primary model (Model 2), lower SCI was associated with increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 9.32; 95% CI, 4.55-19.08, P < 0.001). For CVD mortality, the corresponding HR was 7.03 (95% CI, 3.83-12.92, P < 0.001). SCI areas under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were 0.681 and 0.688 for all-cause and CVD mortality, respectively. Significant differences in overall survival were observed in older and hypertension population.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower SCI index was associated with higher mortality in this PD cohort. Discrimination was modest, and the data-derived cutoffs require independent validation before clinical use.

Title: Metabolomic signatures associated with muscle dysfunction during the SIRIUS-21 space analog mission.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is growing interest in exploring outer space to expand scientific knowledge and access valuable material resources. However, progress is limited by the harsh space environment, including microgravity, ionizing radiation, isolation and confinement (IC), disrupted circadian rhythms, and nutritional challenges. These stressors contribute to health problems across multiple organ systems, particularly the musculoskeletal, immune, renal/urinary, and cardiovascular systems. Although we have extensive insight into skeletal muscle pathophysiological changes induced by these spaceflight-related stressors, the molecular mechanisms underlying functional alterations caused by prolonged IC in skeletal muscle remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: During the 8-month SIRIUS-21 space analog mission, five participants (3 males, 2 females) underwent plasma and saliva sampling and electromyography (EMG) assessment at five time points: baseline (Ingress), early, mid, and late isolation and confinement (IC), and 14 days post-mission (Egress). Metabolites were analyzed by LC-MS/MS. Longitudinal metabolite changes were assessed using repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey HSD post hoc testing, and direct metabolite-EMG relationships were explored using Spearman rank correlations.
RESULTS: Metabolomic profiling identified 45 skeletal muscle-related metabolites with nominally significant longitudinal changes (p < 0.0001-0.05): 8 were detected in both plasma and saliva, 26 only in plasma, and 11 only in saliva. Direct exploratory Spearman correlations with EMG metrics were identified for a subset of metabolites, including pipecolic acid, phenylacetic acid, L-phenylalanine, L-acetylcarnitine, L-glutamine, and pyruvaldehyde. EMG findings showed a progressive decline in muscle activation and fatigue resistance during prolonged IC, with partial recovery after egress. Exploratory sex-related analyses were interpreted descriptively because the cohort included only two females and three males.
CONCLUSION: Prolonged IC was accompanied by coordinated changes in muscle function and circulating or salivary metabolites. The identified metabolites represent candidate metabolic signatures associated with muscle dysfunction and require validation in larger independent cohorts before diagnostic or therapeutic utility can be established.

Title: Early postoperative ipsilateral middle cerebral artery pulsatility index is associated with cerebral hemorrhage after endovascular treatment in anterior circulation large vessel occlusion.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the predictive value of the early postoperative ipsilateral middle cerebral artery pulsatility index (PI) for cerebral hemorrhage after endovascular treatment in patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke.
METHODS: A total of 120 patients were divided into a cerebral hemorrhage group (n = 17) and a non-hemorrhage group (n = 103). Multivariable logistic regression and Firth penalized likelihood regression were used to identify independent predictors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the predictive performance of individual indicators and a combined model. Bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations) was performed for internal validation.
RESULTS: Multivariable logistic regression showed that diabetes mellitus (OR = 4.154, 95% CI: 1.255-13.756, p = 0.020), ASPECTS >8 (OR = 0.115, 95% CI: 0.014-0.942, p = 0.044), and elevated ipsilateral PI (OR = 11.355, 95% CI: 1.267-101.761, p = 0.030) were associated with cerebral hemorrhage. Firth regression confirmed these results. The ipsilateral PI predicted cerebral hemorrhage with an AUC of 0.716 (95% CI: 0.597-0.835), an optimal cutoff of 0.735, a sensitivity of 0.882, and a specificity of 0.505. The combined model (diabetes, ASPECTS >8, PI) achieved an AUC of 0.808 (95% CI: 0.718-0.899), with a sensitivity of 0.882 and a specificity of 0.650. Bootstrap internal validation showed a bias-corrected AUC of 0.810 (95% CI: 0.717-0.896) and an optimism of -0.0022.
CONCLUSION: The early postoperative ipsilateral middle cerebral artery PI is a potential prognostic marker for any radiographic intracranial hemorrhage after endovascular treatment in anterior circulation large vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke, with an optimal cutoff of 0.735. In this cohort, adding PI to diabetes mellitus and ASPECTS was associated with a modest improvement in discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.088, p = 0.011) and continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI = 0.594, p = 0.020), whereas categorical NRI was not significant. These findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts.

Title: Dosimetric impact of target volume anatomical parameters on radiotherapy after right-sided breast-conserving surgery.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the dosimetric effects of target volume Anatomical Parameters on organ at risk (OAR) following breast-conserving surgery and subsequent radiotherapy in patients with right-sided breast cancer.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on 33 patients who underwent post-breast-conserving surgery radiotherapy. The transverse diameter (TD), oblique diameter (OD), and the ratio of transverse diameter to oblique diameter (TOR) were measured at the nipple-center plane for all patients. Bivariate Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the effects of TD, OD, and TOR on V20Gy, V5Gy, Dmean of the affected lung; Dmean and V5Gy of heart; Dmean of the right coronary artery (RCA); Dmean of the left anterior descending artery (LAD); V5Gy of the contralateral lung; and Dmean of the contralateral breast.
RESULTS: OD and TD showed significant correlations with V20Gy, V5Gy, and Dmean of the affected lung (0.5 < R < 0.7, P < 0.01); The TD was significantly correlated with Heart_Dmean (R = 0.58, P < 0.01), strongly correlated with RCA_Dmean (R = 0.45, P < 0.01), and strongly correlated with LAD_Dmean (R = 0.42, P < 0.05); The TOR was significantly correlated with Heart_Dmean (R = 0.47, P < 0.01), strongly correlated with LAD_Dmean (R = 0.47, P < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Exploratory observational thresholds from our cohort: target volume with TD >8.00 cm or OD >19.56 cm indicates higher lung dose risk; TD >8.00 cm or TOR >0.47 indicates higher cardiac dose risk. These thresholds were not optimized by ROC analysis and cannot be directly used for clinical risk stratification; prospective validation is needed. Clinical planning should minimize heart and lung radiation.

Title: ECG Holter-based screening for sleep-disordered breathing in post-stroke patients: a large monocentric cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is highly prevalent after stroke and is associated with poor functional outcomes and increased mortality, yet systematic screening remains challenging because of limited polysomnography accessibility. We evaluated three electrocardiogram (ECG)-based indices for SDB screening in a large consecutive post-stroke cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 1,929 consecutive patients hospitalised for stroke or transient ischaemic attack at Saint-Étienne University Hospital (2010-2021) who were in sinus rhythm with ECG signal quality adequate for ECG-derived respiration (EDR) analysis; patients with atrial fibrillation, pacemaker rhythm, or severe ectopy (>10% of beats) were excluded a priori. EDR, the Thoracic Impedance Disturbance Index (TIDI) and the Very Low Frequency Increment (VLFI) were compared with the simultaneous oxygen desaturation index (ODI) as reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and predictive values were calculated at ODI thresholds of 15/h and 30/h; a combined TIDI+EDR concordant rule was assessed as a post-hoc exploratory analysis.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 61% males (mean age 65.9 years). Suspected SDB (ODI ≥ 5/h) was present in 74.6% of patients, moderate-to-severe SDB (ODI ≥ 15/h) in 38.9% and severe SDB (ODI ≥ 30/h) in 17.1%. For ODI ≥ 15/h (n = 750), TIDI had the highest sensitivity (93.3%) and negative predictive value (90.8%), whereas EDR had higher specificity (80.2%) and accuracy (74.2%); the combined rule reached 85.2% specificity and 72.9% positive predictive value. For ODI ≥ 30/h (n = 330), EDR showed specificity of 92.4% and accuracy of 85.2%, and the combined rule 95.4% and 86.9%, respectively. VLFI performed poorly across all metrics.
DISCUSSION: ECG-based tools can identify post-stroke patients at high risk of SDB using routine cardiac monitoring. The complementary profiles of TIDI (rule-out) and EDR (rule-in) support a sequential screening approach, which requires prospective validation against polysomnography. VLFI is unsuitable for elderly stroke populations because of age-related autonomic dysfunction. Because patients with atrial fibrillation, pacemaker rhythm or severe arrhythmia were excluded, the findings may not generalise to this higher-arrhythmia-burden subgroup, who may also be at higher risk of SDB.

Title: Clinical outcomes and safety of finerenone in patients with heart failure: a real-world observational study in China.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Finerenone is a highly selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, but data on its use in patients with heart failure (HF) in real-world clinical practice remain limited. This study evaluated longitudinal clinical changes and safety outcomes observed during finerenone treatment in patients with HF.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective observational study included consecutive patients diagnosed with HF and treated with add-on finerenone between August 2023 and May 2024 at Tongji Hospital, Shanghai, China. All patients received finerenone add-on to standard treatment. Subgroup analyses were performed in patients with HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF), and HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Adverse events were recorded, including HF readmission, outpatient visits for acute HF, and diuretic dosage escalation. Laboratory and cardiac function markers were also collected.
RESULTS: Seventy-three patients were included. Favorable longitudinal changes were observed in cardiac structure, diastolic function, biomarker levels, and symptom status during follow-up. Left atrial diameter decreased from 50 to 48 mm, the E/e' ratio decreased from 10.65 to 8.20, and NT-proBNP decreased by 67.47% at 12 months (P < 0.001). NYHA functional class distribution also shifted toward lower symptom burden over time, and LVEF showed a modest increase. No patients discontinued finerenone because of adverse events.
CONCLUSION: In real-world clinical practice, finerenone was associated with a favorable clinical and safety profile in patients with HF, with profiles similar across the HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF subgroups. Future larger-sample, multicenter randomized controlled trials are warranted to validate these observations.

Title: A novel nutritional index is associated with adverse outcomes in patients with acute heart failure: insights beyond traditional risk markers.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutritional status is closely associated with clinical outcomes in patients with acute heart failure (AHF). However, the value of simple and comprehensive nutritional indicators in this population remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between the triglyceride-total cholesterol-body weight index (TCBI) and adverse outcomes in patients with AHF.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study consecutively included patients with AHF admitted between April 2022 and April 2024. TCBI and conventional nutritional indices, including prognostic nutritional index (PNI), geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI), and controlling nutritional status (CONUT), were calculated at admission. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint of heart failure rehospitalization or all-cause mortality within 1 year after discharge. Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, threshold effect analysis, ROC analysis, subgroup analyses, and incremental model analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among 1,898 patients with AHF, 557 experienced composite events during follow-up. After multivariable adjustment, higher TCBI was independently associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (HR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.60-0.81, p < 0.001). TCBI showed the highest discriminatory ability among nutritional indicators (AUC = 0.627). Restricted cubic spline and threshold effect analyses demonstrated a nonlinear association between TCBI and adverse outcomes. After adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors and NT-proBNP, TCBI remained independently associated with outcomes. Compared with the base model including traditional cardiovascular risk factors and NT-proBNP, the addition of TCBI improved model performance, with the C-index increasing from 0.676 to 0.686 and the AUC from 0.703 to 0.716. The association between TCBI and outcomes remained consistent across HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF phenotypes.
CONCLUSION: TCBI was independently associated with heart failure rehospitalization or all-cause mortality in patients with AHF and provided additional prognostic information beyond conventional nutritional indices and NT-proBNP.

Title: Adherence-related factors associated with weight reduction: clinical outcomes of telerehabilitation in patients with metabolic syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a major contributor to cardiovascular morbidity, yet our healthcare system is underdeveloped in terms of effective lifestyle interventions. Telemedicine-based programs may offer a scalable option, but evidence on their effectiveness in MetS populations is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a combined telemedicine-supported lifestyle program compared to non-randomized controls in adults with MetS and identify adherence-related factors associated with weight loss.
METHODS: In this prospective, non-randomized controlled intervention study (2021-2023, Hungary), 133 adults with MetS were enrolled and 111 completed a 90-day lifestyle program. All participants received an initial dietetic consultation; the intervention group additionally used smartphone-based dietary logging, remote exercise monitoring, and biweekly teleconsultations with dietitians and physiotherapists. Primary outcome was waist circumference at the standardized day-90 follow-up; secondary outcomes included body weight, body composition, exercise capacity, metabolic parameters, and adherence indicators. Outcomes were analyzed by baseline-, age-, and sex-adjusted ANCOVA with HC3-robust standard errors; the primary model included a group-by-baseline waist circumference interaction, and exploratory adherence analyses assessed linear trends across ordered weight-loss subgroups.
RESULTS: A significant group-by-baseline waist circumference interaction was observed (p = 0.029), with a greater adjusted intervention-control difference at higher baseline waist circumference. The intervention group also showed descriptive reductions in body weight (-5.23 ± 5.16 kg), BMI, skinfold thicknesses, body fat mass, and visceral fat. HbA1c declined by 0.41 ± 0.60 percentage points (p < 0.001), and HDL-cholesterol increased significantly, while other laboratory parameters changed modestly. After Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within the respective outcome families, the adjusted between-group differences in abdominal circumference, HbA1c, and skeletal muscle mass remained statistically significant. Exploratory adherence analyses showed significant trends toward more frequent body-weight logging and lower relative energy intake with greater weight loss, but not for the other adherence measures.
CONCLUSIONS: A telemedical lifestyle program was associated with favorable short-term changes in abdominal obesity, body composition, and metabolic control in adults with MetS, although skeletal muscle mass loss was also observed. Regular self-weighing and maintaining a lower relative energy intake were associated with greater weight loss. Telemedicine-supported lifestyle management may represent a promising approach for MetS care.

Title: Safety, effectiveness and healthcare resource implications of an early discharge pathway for cryoballoon ablation: real-world evidence from China.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Same-day discharge after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation has been increasingly adopted in Western healthcare systems. However, its applicability in China remains uncertain because of differences in healthcare delivery, peri-procedural management, and hospitalization practices. Meanwhile, real-world evidence on early discharge pathways for AF ablation in the Chinese setting remains limited. This study evaluated the clinical and economic outcomes of an early discharge pathway for patients undergoing cryoballoon ablation in China.
METHODS: A retrospective real-world study was conducted using data from the institutional atrial fibrillation database at Fuzhou University Affiliated Provincial Hospital. Consecutive patients who underwent cryoballoon ablation between January 2021 and December 2023 were included. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on post-operative length of stay: the early discharge (ED) group (discharged within 48 h) and the conventional inpatient (CI) group (discharged after 48 h). Propensity score matching was performed to minimize baseline imbalances between groups. The outcomes were atrial fibrillation recurrence, post-procedural complications and hospitalization cost.
RESULTS: A total of 327 patients were included in the final analysis, with 151 in the ED group and 176 in the CI group. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 80 patients remained in each group, and baseline comparability was substantially improved after matching, although a small residual imbalance remained for stroke/TIA history. During 12 months of follow-up, the recurrence rate of AF was similar between the two groups (8.75% vs. 10.00%, P = 0.786). No major in-hospital complications occurred in the ED group, whereas one case of pericardial effusion was reported in the CI group. Subgroup analyses showed no significant difference in recurrence among patients aged 65 years or older or among those with persistent atrial fibrillation. The ED group incurred significantly lower medical service costs (P = 0.0003) and medication costs (P = 0.035) than the CI group. However, no significant difference was observed in total hospitalization costs between the two groups (P = 0.957).
DISCUSSION: In this real-world Chinese cohort, a structured early discharge pathway for cryoballoon ablation appeared to be feasible and was not associated with a higher AF recurrence rate, while reducing medical service-related costs. However, because this was a retrospective single-center study with a limited sample size and no systematic post-discharge surveillance for all potential events, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Larger prospective studies are needed to further confirm the safety, effectiveness, and economic implications of this model.

Title: Tacrolimus ameliorates pulmonary hypertension associated with pulmonary fibrosis via modulation of vascular remodeling.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is frequently complicated by pulmonary hypertension (IPF-PH), a severe condition that worsens symptoms, reduces exercise capacity, and shortens survival. Current anti-fibrotic and PH-targeted therapies show limited efficacy in IPF-PH, and the therapeutic role of tacrolimus in this composite disease remains underexplored.
METHODS: A bleomycin-induced IPF-PH rat model was established. Rats were randomized into control, bleomycin model, treprostinil (positive control), and tacrolimus (0.05 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous, 21 days) groups. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), echocardiography, right ventricular and lung histology, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were assessed. In vitro, C166 endothelial cells and primary rat pulmonary arterial endothelial cells were stimulated with bleomycin with or without tacrolimus; MOVAS smooth muscle cells were stimulated with TGF-β1 with or without tacrolimus. Endpoints included cell viability, tube formation, ROS, SOD/GSH, apoptosis, proliferation/migration, and MAPK/PI3K/AKT signaling.
RESULTS: Tacrolimus reduced RVSP, improved PAT/PET and right heart function, attenuated right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary fibrosis, and decreased vascular wall thickness and α-SMA expression. It also downregulated fibrosis markers Fn1 and Col1a1. In endothelial cells, tacrolimus restored P-VEGFR2/VEGFR2 and VE-cadherin expression, promoted tube formation, reduced apoptosis (Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-9/3), and alleviated oxidative stress (ROS, SOD/GSH, Keap1/HO-1). In smooth muscle cells, tacrolimus inhibited TGF-β1-induced proliferation and migration and reduced Ki67 expression. Mechanistically, tacrolimus suppressed MAPK (JNK, ERK, p38) and PI3K/AKT pathway activation in vivo and in vitro.
DISCUSSION: Tacrolimus ameliorates bleomycin-induced IPF-PH through vascular remodeling-oriented, multi-target effects, including endothelial protection, suppression of oxidative stress and apoptosis, and inhibition of smooth muscle proliferation, partly via MAPK and PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings support tacrolimus as a potential therapeutic candidate for IPF-PH, especially in patients with prominent vascular remodeling, while highlighting the need for further dose-response, target-specific, immunomodulatory, and delivery optimization studies before clinical translation.

Title: Analysis of risk factors for kinesiophobia after coronary artery bypass grafting and construction of a nomogram prediction model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kinesiophobia, or the irrational fear of movement, is a significant barrier to effective cardiac rehabilitation and recovery in patients after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). This study sought to identify the risk factors for kinesiophobia in post-CABG patients and to develop and validate a nomogram prediction model to estimate individual risk.
METHODS: A retrospective case-control study was conducted on 138 patients who underwent CABG in the Cardiovascular ICU between February 2023 and November 2024. Using the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia-Heart (TSK-Heart), patients were categorized into a kinesiophobia group (TSK-Heart >37, n = 95) and a non-kinesiophobia group (n = 43). Risk Factors were identified with multivariable logistic regression. The resulting coefficients furnished a nomogram for individual risk estimation. Calibration was evaluated with the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and a bootstrap-corrected calibration plot; discrimination was quantified by the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and calibration curve.
RESULTS: The incidence of kinesiophobia in this cohort was 68.84%. The logistic regression analysis identified six risk factors: advanced age (OR = 1.127, P = 0.003), lower educational level (OR = 0.246, P = 0.001), higher degree of disability in activities of daily living (ADL) (OR = 3.880, P = 0.007), lower self-efficacy in cardiac rehabilitation exercise (OR = 0.898, P = 0.024), pain catastrophizing (OR = 4.513, P = 0.023), and fear of falling (OR = 1.212, P = 0.004). The constructed nomogram demonstrated excellent discrimination, with an AUC of 0.939 (95% CI: 0.898-0.981), and high sensitivity (93.7%) and specificity (83.7%). Calibration was confirmed by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (χ 2 = 5.97, P = 0.65) and a bootstrap-corrected calibration plot showing close agreement between predicted and observed probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced age, low educational attainment, ADL dependency, poor cardiac rehabilitation self-efficacy, pain catastrophizing, and fear of falling were significant risk factors for kinesiophobia after CABG. The developed nomogram was a reliable and accurate tool for early identification of high-risk patients, enabling clinicians to implement individualized preventative strategies and optimize postoperative recovery.

Title: Habitual sleep duration and spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a prospective UK Biobank cohort study with supporting hospital-based neurosurgical data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abnormal sleep duration has been associated with stroke, but evidence specific to spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a two-part observational study. The prospective UK Biobank analysis included 314,236 participants free of sICH at baseline, among whom 1,387 developed incident sICH. The supporting cross-sectional hospital analysis included 312 patients with imaging-confirmed sICH and 515 non-ICH neurosurgical controls from Jinjiang Municipal Hospital. Habitual sleep duration was categorized as short (<7 h/day), normal (7-9 h/day), or long (>9 h/day). Cox proportional hazards models [hazard ratios (HRs)] and logistic regression [odds ratios (ORs)] were used, together with restricted cubic splines, additional adjustment for medications, blood pressure, and indicators of prevalent ill health, and multiple imputation of missing data. A systemic inflammatory marker score and interaction analyses with false-discovery-rate correction were examined as secondary, exploratory analyses.
RESULTS: Compared with normal sleep, short and long sleep were associated with higher incident sICH risk in the UK Biobank [adjusted HRs 1.14 (95% CI 1.03-1.26) and 1.55 (1.15-2.09)]; the short-sleep association was modest and less robust in sensitivity analyses. Corresponding cross-sectional ORs in the hospital dataset were 1.49 (1.04-2.13) and 2.05 (1.17-3.59), respectively. Restricted cubic splines suggested U-shaped associations in both datasets, with the lowest estimated hazard or odds at approximately 7-8 h/day. Estimates were similar after additional confounder adjustment (HRs 1.10 and 1.43 for short and long sleep, respectively) and multiple imputation (HRs 1.13 and 1.50, respectively). No interaction, including with inflammatory marker burden, remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction, and adjustment for the marker score changed the estimates only modestly.
CONCLUSION: Both short and long sleep duration were associated with higher incident sICH risk in the UK Biobank and higher odds of sICH in the hospital dataset, with stronger and more consistent associations observed for long sleep. Systemic inflammatory markers neither explained nor reliably modified these associations, and because long sleep may partly reflect prevalent ill health, the long-sleep association warrants cautious interpretation. Sleep duration may be a useful marker of sICH susceptibility.

Title: Blood flow restriction training for lower-limb function, walking and functional recovery after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) is increasingly used as a low-load rehabilitation strategy after stroke, but the magnitude, clinical relevance, and certainty of its effects remain uncertain. We evaluated the effects and safety of BFRT on lower-limb function and mobility after stroke.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, CENTRAL, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed were searched from inception to June 10, 2026. Randomized controlled trials evaluating lower-limb BFRT in adults after stroke were included. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, certainty using GRADE, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Nineteen randomized controlled trials were included. BFRT improved Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Lower Extremity scores (10 studies, 646 participants; MD = 2.14 points, 95% CI 0.74 to 3.54) and Berg Balance Scale scores (8 studies, 581 participants; MD = 4.72 points, 95% CI 1.62 to 7.82). The 10-meter walk test analysis showed higher walking speed (4 studies, 322 participants; MD = 0.14 m/s, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.25), but the estimate attenuated after eligible grey literature was included (6 studies, 410 participants; MD = 0.09 m/s, 95% CI - 0.03 to 0.21). Six-minute walk distance increased by 8.01 m (5 studies, 271 participants; 95% CI 2.31 to 13.71). No clear pooled effects were observed for Timed Up and Go, sit-to-stand performance, cadence, or standard full-scale Barthel Index/Modified Barthel Index scores. FMA-LE and 6MWT effects were below reported clinically important thresholds; the BBS estimate was close to an approximately 5-point reference, with its confidence interval spanning effects below and above that threshold. Certainty was moderate for 6MWT, low for FMA-LE, and very low for BBS and 10MWT walking speed. No BFRT-related serious adverse or thrombotic events were reported among studies with explicit safety information, although reporting was limited.
CONCLUSION: BFRT may improve selected lower-limb outcomes after stroke, but clinical importance remains uncertain for several outcomes and certainty ranges from moderate to very low. Better-designed trials with standardized BFRT protocols and more complete safety reporting are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261477739, PROSPERO CRD420261477739.

Title: Fatigue after transient ischemic attack: cross-sectional associations with comorbidities, activities of daily living and social participation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Fatigue is a common symptom during the first year after transient ischemic attack (TIA), but its long-term persistence remain unclear. This study aim to assessed long-term perceived fatigue after TIA and to evaluated associated comorbidities and functional consequences.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational and cross-sectional study included 431 community-dwelling adults assessed 1-13 years after TIA in an outpatient setting, with a 25% response rate. Fatigue was measured using the Fatigue Assessment Scale in three subgroups: first-ever TIA (n = 299), recurrent TIA (n = 54), and TIA with stroke (n = 78). Depression and anxiety were evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, and. An activities of daily living and social participation using were determined using the Stroke Impact Scale. Multivariable ordinal linear regression analyses were performed in the first-ever TIA group to examine associations between fatigue, comorbidities and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: In the first-ever TIA group, fatigue levels were similar across time-since-TIA strata up to 13 years (mean 21.8, standard deviation [SD] 5.2); 35% exceeded the fatigue cut-off. Fatigue in the first-ever TIA group was lower than in the recurrent TIA group (mean 23.9, SD 5.7; p < 0.05) and TIA with stroke group (mean 23.8, SD 6.5; p < 0.05). Amon participants with first-ever TIA, depression (β = 6.8, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.5-10.1; p < 0.001), severe sleep problem (category 4: β = 3.9, 95% CI 0.9-6.8; p = 0.010) and (category 5: β = 5.9, 95% CI 2.2-9.6; p = 0.002), atrial fibrillation (β = 2.1, 95% CI 0.3-3.9; p = 0.02) and heart disease (β = 1.8, 95% CI 0.2-3.4; p = 0.03) were associated with higher fatigue. Higher fatigue was also associated with reduced activities of daily living (β = 0.15, 95% CI 0.07-0.22, p < 0.001) and lower social participation (β = 0.06, 95% CI 0.02-0.10; p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: Fatigue affected more than one-third of first-ever TIA survivors and did not differ materially across cross-sectional time-since-TIA strata up to 13 years. Greater fatigue was associated with depressive symptoms, severe sleep problems, atrial fibrillation, heart disease, and reduced daily activity and social participation. Early identification and management of fatigue and related comorbidities may improve functioning. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine temporal relationships and whether targeted management improves outcomes.

Title: Beyond the numbers: understanding inter-center variation in recanalization therapy rates.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to investigate the inter-center differences in recanalization therapy (RT) utilization between Estonia's two largest comprehensive stroke centers and to assess whether variation in the management of patient subgroups is associated with differences in short-term neurological and functional outcomes.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective two-center study including all acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients admitted between January-June 2021. Mild AIS or mild stroke was defined as National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) ≤ 5. Demographic, treatment, NIHSS, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) data were analyzed using nonparametric and categorical tests. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated predictors of RT use in AIS and predictors of stroke outcome.
RESULTS: Among 635 AIS patients, RT was administered more frequently at Tartu University Hospital (TUH) than at North Estonia Medical Centre (NEMC) (45.2% vs. 30.7%, p < 0.001; aOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.33-0.74). A total of 301 (47.5%) patients had mild stroke. RT use in mild stroke was substantially higher at TUH (33.1% vs. 10.0%, p < 0.001). Descriptive analysis showed greater neurological improvement in RT-treated mild stroke patients than non-RT-treated patients [median NIHSS reduction 2.0 (IQR 0.8-3.0) vs. 1.0 (IQR 0.0-2.0), respectively; Wilcoxon rank-sum test, p < 0.001], whereas good functional outcome did not differ by RT exposure. After adjustment, neurological improvement was independently associated with treatment center and baseline NIHSS category but not with RT exposure (aOR 0.94, 95% CI 0.43-2.06).
DISCUSSION: RT was also not independently associated with good functional outcome. Inter-center variation in RT utilization was primarily driven by the management of mild stroke patients. Comparable stroke-care infrastructure did not ensure uniform RT utilization.

Title: Estradiol via GPER Maintains Protection Against Arterial Stiffening During Midlife Hypertension in a Mouse Model of Menopause.
Journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
Abstract: Endogenous estradiol is associated with cardiovascular protection, but whether menopausal hormone therapy provides protection in aging women with underlying cardiometabolic disease is still not known. Our previous work has shown that the membrane-bound G protein-coupled estrogen receptor (GPER) plays a crucial role in estradiol's protective vascular effects by promoting vasodilation, attenuating oxidative stress, and reducing arterial stiffness. In the current study, we designed a midlife mouse model of menopause with induced hypertension to more closely mimic the conditions of postmenopausal women in randomized clinical trials. We hypothesized that estradiol's vascular protection would be reduced in the presence of cardiovascular disease, especially when the disease was established before menopause, and that vascular GPER plays a role in the response. Middle-aged female C57Bl/6J mice, wildtype and global GPER knockout mice, and smooth muscle-specific GPER knockout mice were ovariectomized at 46 weeks of age and infused with Ang II to induce hypertension in combination with either estradiol or vehicle treatment. Estradiol did not significantly impact blood pressure but reduced arterial stiffness independent of the timing of hypertension. Either global or smooth muscle cell GPER deletion abrogated estradiol's protection from arterial stiffening. These studies are important for determining whether cardiovascular status should be a factor when considering menopausal hormone therapy and underscores GPER as an important mediator of estradiol's protective vascular effects, particularly with regards to arterial stiffness.

Title: Clinical and Invasive Hemodynamic Correlates of the TAPSE/sPAP Ratio in Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) adaptation to increased pulmonary afterload is a major determinant of prognosis in pulmonary hypertension (PH), yet comprehensive validation of simple noninvasive markers against invasive hemodynamic parameters remains limited. We investigated whether the tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to systolic pulmonary artery pressure (TAPSE/sPAP) ratio reflects the clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic spectrum of PH.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 209 consecutive patients with right heart catheterization-confirmed PH who underwent comprehensive clinical assessment, transthoracic echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamic evaluation between 2016 and 2024. Patients were stratified into quartiles according to the TAPSE/sPAP ratio, and clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic characteristics were compared.
RESULTS: The mean age was 58.8 ± 16.5 years, and 61% of patients were female. Lower TAPSE/sPAP ratios were associated with older age, higher NT-proBNP and serum uric acid levels, and lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (all p < 0.05). Decreasing TAPSE/sPAP ratios were also associated with larger right atrial and right ventricular dimensions, lower TAPSE, and higher tricuspid regurgitation velocity and estimated sPAP (all p < 0.001). Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated progressively higher right ventricular systolic pressure, mean pulmonary artery pressure, and pulmonary vascular resistance (all p < 0.001), whereas mixed venous oxygen saturation increased across quartiles (p = 0.036).
CONCLUSIONS: The TAPSE/sPAP ratio is a practical, noninvasive marker that closely reflects right ventricular remodeling and invasive hemodynamic impairment in pulmonary hypertension. Lower TAPSE/sPAP ratios identify patients with more advanced RV-pulmonary arterial uncoupling and may improve bedside hemodynamic risk stratification.

Title: False-Positive Hepatitis C Virus Serology Following HeartMate 3 Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: False-positive hepatitis C virus (HCV) (FPHC) serology has been reported with earlier-generation axial-flow left ventricular assist devices (LVADs), but its frequency with the magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 and its implications for heart transplant pathways remain unknown. This study describes FPHC serology in HeartMate 3 LVAD recipients and explores associated clinical and immunological features.
METHODS: A retrospective, single-center study was conducted at a specialist cardiothoracic center. All adults implanted with a HeartMate 3 LVAD between March 2018 and July 2025 with complete HCV serology before and after implantation were included. Patients developing HCV antibody positivity with negative confirmatory testing were classified as having FPHC serology. Patient demographics, blood product transfusions, liver function tests, lactate dehydrogenase, and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) sensitization were compared between groups.
RESULTS: Among 54 HeartMate 3 LVAD recipients, 10 (18.5%) developed FPHC serology after implantation. There were no significant differences between groups in age, sex, liver function tests, or lactate dehydrogenase. The number of fresh frozen plasma units transfused at implantation and the development of anti-HLA Class I antibodies were associated with FPHC serology (p = 0.039, p = 0.04, respectively). No significant associations were observed with red blood cell or platelet transfusions.
CONCLUSION: FPHC serology is a clinically important phenomenon in HeartMate 3 LVAD recipients. Clinicians and patients should be aware of this phenomenon to minimize unnecessary investigations and delays to transplant candidacy assessment. Standardized confirmatory testing protocols and multicenter studies are needed to clarify the underlying immune mechanisms and their impact on post-transplant outcomes.

Title: Reducing Patient Radiation Skin Dose in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Using a Dedicated Protocol: A Single-Center Experience.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) expose patients and operators to ionizing radiation, posing risks of deterministic effects such as skin injury and stochastic effects including malignancy. Although real-time dosimetry and dose alerts have been associated with radiation-dose reductions in prior reports, the level of patient radiation reduction associated with implementing a formal, multifaceted radiation reduction program has not previously been reported in a high-volume catheterization laboratory.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of a substantial radiation dose level (SRDL) protocol on patient radiation exposure during PCI.
METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 19,249 PCI procedures at a tertiary center from July 2012 to December 2021. Patients were stratified into a pre-protocol cohort (Phase 1: 17,332 procedures) and a post-protocol cohort (Phase 2: 1917 procedures following implementation in November 2019). The SRDL protocol included real-time radiation monitoring, alert thresholds at 5 Gy air kerma, and structured follow-up for high-dose cases. Study outcomes included air kerma (Ka,r) dose-area product (DAP), contrast volume, and fluoroscopy time.
