RESULTS: The study cohort (mean age 66.3 years; 28.5% female) demonstrated significant reductions in radiation exposure after implementing the protocol. Median air kerma declined from 2.6 to 2.0 Gy (23% reduction; p < 0.0001), and median DAP decreased from 158 to 125 Gy·cm2 (20.8% reduction; p < 0.0001). Contrast volume was reduced by 15 mL (11.1% reduction; p < 0.0001), while fluoroscopy time remained unchanged (18.1 vs. 18.3 min; p = 0.094). Despite increased procedural complexity in Phase 2 (multivessel PCI: 69.5% vs. 65.2%; p < 0.001), radiation reduction remained significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of an SRDL protocol was associated with significant reductions in patient radiation exposure during PCI without increasing procedure time, supporting its use as a safety intervention in high-volume catheterization laboratories.

Title: Development and Preliminary Validation of a Male-Oriented Fertility Index in Infertile Men With Varicocele.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Male infertility is usually assessed using separate parameters, while a simple integrated male-oriented tool is lacking.
OBJECTIVES: To develop a Male Fertility Index (MFI), assess its association with natural conception after varicocelectomy, and perform preliminary external validation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This two-center cohort study included 149 infertile men with clinical varicocele: 99 in the development cohort and 50 in the validation cohort. Preoperative variables were analyzed against natural conception within 12 months. ROC-derived AUCs for total progressively motile sperm count, total motility, male age, and infertility duration were used to construct the MFI.
RESULTS: Natural conception occurred in 30/99 couples (30.3%). MFI values were higher in men whose partners conceived (1.44 [0.87-2.15] vs. 0.64 [0.25-1.31], p < 0.001). Conception was more frequent with MFI > 0.8 than with MFI ≤ 0.8 (44.4% vs. 13.3%, p = 0.0017). In validation, corresponding rates were 40.0% and 14.3%; AUC was 0.795 (95% CI 0.650-0.911).
DISCUSSION: The MFI showed a similar association with natural conception in both cohorts, although validation was limited by sample size and incomplete assessment of female factors.
CONCLUSION: The MFI may summarize male reproductive status in infertile men with clinical varicocele. Its weighting and cut-off require confirmation in larger cohorts, and its usefulness in other infertility settings remains to be established.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Validation Study; Multicenter Study

Title: ALDH2 Deficiency Promotes Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress and Adverse Limb Outcomes via VDAC-HSP60 Signaling.
Abstract: The ALDH2 rs671 variant, which is frequent in East Asian populations, markedly reduces mitochondrial aldehyde-detoxifying capacity and thereby increases vulnerability to reactive aldehydes, including 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), during ischemic stress. We show that impaired ALDH2 activity perturbs endothelial mitochondrial proteostasis through an ALDH2-4-HNE-HSP60-VDAC1 pathway. In Aldh2 knock-in mice and endothelial cells exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation, ALDH2 deficiency was accompanied by 4-HNE accumulation, mitochondrial DNA injury, loss of membrane potential, increased mitochondrial ROS, mitochondrial fragmentation, and apoptosis. Analysis of transcriptomic data highlighted HSP60 (HSPD1) as a downstream candidate. LC-MS/MS, covalent docking, co-immunoprecipitation, and proximity ligation analyses supported 4-HNE modification of HSP60, while native electrophoresis indicated disruption of higher-order HSP60 assembly. HSP60 redistribution to the cytosol was predominantly dependent on VDAC1. Activating ALDH2 with AD-5591, or suppressing VDAC1 genetically or pharmacologically, preserved HSP60 homeostasis, mitochondrial integrity, and endothelial function. In a prospective cohort of 227 patients with peripheral artery disease, the rs671 variant was associated with a higher incidence of major adverse limb events. These data position HSP60 proteostasis downstream of ALDH2-dependent aldehyde detoxification and identify the ALDH2-4-HNE-HSP60-VDAC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target in ischemic vascular disease.

Title: Cardiac Endothelial Enhancer RNA Tek-e1 Restores Microvascular Homeostasis After Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Microvascular repair after myocardial infarction involves both angiogenesis and re-establishment of vascular homeostasis. Here, we identify a distinct transcriptionally active state in hypoxic border-zone endothelial cells driven by KDM5A downregulation and biased towards endothelial stabilization and microvascular homeostatic repair. KDM5A loss increases H3K4me3 enrichment at the Tek promoter and an intronic enhancer, enabling ISL1 to coordinately activate transcription of Tek and the enhancer RNA Tek-e1. Tek-e1 acts as an essential cis-regulatory RNA that further amplifies Tek/TIE2 expression through R-loop formation and reinforced enhancer-promoter communication, thereby converting Kdm5a-loss-induced epigenetic activation into persistent transcriptional reinforcement. In mice with endothelial-specific deletion of Kdm5a, this mechanism promotes the maturation and stabilization of nascent-microvascular networks after myocardial infarction. In a clinical cohort, serum soluble TIE2 independently stratified collateral status in 402 patients with chronic total occlusion. To further enable translation, we developed LNP@Tek-e1 modified with a VCAM-1-targeting peptide, combining VCAM-1-directed endothelial enrichment with enhancer-dependent Tek-e1 activity to selectively enhance Tek/TIE2 expression in border-zone endothelium, improving microvascular function and limiting adverse left ventricular remodelling. Together, these findings define KDM5A downregulation as a hypoxia-triggered endothelial repair programme and establish Tek-e1 as an essential cis-regulatory amplifier that can be delivered in vivo to restore post-infarction microvascular homeostasis.

Title: Which Anthropometric Index Best Signals 10‑Year Cardiovascular Risk? A Sex‑Stratified Analysis From the Shiraz Heart Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality, with obesity as a critical contributor. Traditional measures like body mass index (BMI) do not fully capture fat distribution or composition. Anthropometric and fat indices such as body fat (BF), may offer greater precision in ASCVD risk assessment.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 1106 university individuals (26-72 years). The primary analysis included adults 40-70 years (n = 761), for whom 10-year ASCVD risk was estimated using the 2019 ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE). We modeled continuous risk using sex-adjusted linear regression with each index entered separately and We tested Index × Sex interactions. Discrimination for elevated risk (≥7.5%) was assessed with ROC/AUC. A secondary analysis in participants <40 years assessed discrimination for a composite high risk-factor burden endpoint (≥2 abnormalities among BP, lipids, smoking, diabetes, BMI).
RESULTS: The median (IQR) of ASCVD risk score was 1.33 (0.55-3.77), significantly higher in men than women (2.67 vs. 0.65; p < 0.001). Most participants (73.1%) were classified as low-risk, though men had greater representation in higher-risk categories. Furthermore, BF, Waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and Waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) showed the strongest positive associations with continuous PCE risk, whereas Fat-free mass (FFM) was inversely associated (p < 0.001). For discriminating ≥7.5% risk, WHR performed best, BF and WC were modest and WHtR and BMI provided little to no discriminative ability.
CONCLUSION: Anthropometric indices such as WC, WHR, and BF are valuable discriminators of ASCVD risk, surpassing BMI in risk assessment and stratification.

Title: Long-Term Prognostic Value of Angiography-Derived Quantitative Flow Ratio and Radial Wall Strain in Untreated Intermediate Coronary Stenoses: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative flow ratio (QFR) measures angiography-derived coronary physiology, whereas radial wall strain (RWS) characterizes cyclic lumen deformation. We investigated their complementary long-term prognostic information in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model.
AIMS: We investigated the complementary long-term prognostic information of QFR and RWS in untreated intermediate coronary stenoses, and assessed the internal validity of their combined prediction model.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 236 patients with 236 untreated index vessels and 50%-90% diameter stenosis. QFR and maximum RWS (RWSmax) were calculated offline and were unavailable to treating clinicians. Target vessel failure (TVF) comprised cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization (TVR). Prespecified Cox models used multiple imputation, and four nested models underwent 1000-bootstrap validation with repeat imputation and fitting. Fixed 3-year analyses, calibration, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Over a median potential follow-up of 66.8 months, 55 patients experienced TVF, including 40 TVR events. TVF occurred in 37/108 patients (34.3%) with RWSmax > 12% and 18/128 (14.1%) with RWSmax ≤12%. In the primary model, the adjusted hazard ratio was 1.14 (95% CI: 1.06-1.23; p = 0.001) per 1% increase in RWSmax and 1.34 (95% CI: 1.08-1.67; p = 0.010) per 0.05 decrease in QFR. The combined model had an apparent C-index of 0.733 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.704, compared with 0.597 for the clinical model. Its corrected 3-year AUC was 0.733, and its corrected calibration slope was 0.90.
CONCLUSIONS: Joint assessment of coronary physiology and wall strain provided incremental long-term prognostic information beyond clinical and angiographic characteristics in untreated intermediate lesions. Lower QFR and higher RWSmax were independently associated with TVF, and each added prognostic information beyond the other. The signal predominantly concerned subsequent revascularization. External validation is needed before clinical application.

Title: External Validation of the UK-BCIS CHIP Score to Predict 1-Year Outcomes in Patients Undergoing IVL-Assisted PCI: Insights From the International BENELUX-IVL Registry.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The United Kingdom-British Cardiovascular Intervention Society complex high-risk indicated percutaneous coronary intervention (UK-BCIS CHIP) score was developed to identify patient- and procedural factors to predict short-term adverse outcomes in patients undergoing high risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The performance of the UK-BCIS CHIP score in a patient population treated with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) for severe coronary calcification remains unknown.
AIMS: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the UK-BCIS CHIP score in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI for severe coronary calcification, and to assess procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes across CHIP score categories.
METHODS: This international, multicenter, prospective study included consecutive patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI between May 2019 and December 2025 from the BENELUX-IVL registry. Patients were stratified according to UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥ 5). The primary endpoint was 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target vessel revascularization. Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality, procedural outcomes, and periprocedural complications. Discrimination of the UK-BCIS CHIP score was assessed using the AUC for in-hospital events and the Harrell's C-index for 1-year outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 911 patients were included. Higher UK-BCIS CHIP scores were associated with increased clinical comorbidity, lesion complexity, and procedural intensity. Procedural, device, and technical success rates were comparable across UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (85.1%, 94.4%, and 85.7% overall; p = 0.850, p = 0.813, and p = 0.781, respectively). Complications requiring intervention occurred in 5.5% of patients and did not differ significantly across CHIP score categories (p = 0.347). The 1-year cumulative incidence of MACE, accounting for all-cause death as a competing risk, did not differ significantly across UK-BCIS CHIP score categories (Gray's test p = 0.53).
CONCLUSION: In IVL-assisted PCI, the UK-BCIS CHIP score effectively identifies patients with increased clinical and procedural complexity but shows limited discrimination for mid-term ischemic outcomes. IVL-assisted PCI is safe and effective across the full spectrum of CHIP risk, while long-term prognosis appears primarily driven by underlying comorbidity burden.

Title: Sacubitril/valsartan for radiation-induced heart disease in children: preclinical and clinical findings.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Radiation-induced heart disease (RIHD) is a life-threatening sequela for cancer survivors. A proactive preventive strategy is urgently needed but remains elusive, particularly for the vulnerable paediatric population where prospective data are scarce. To address this gap, this study aimed to evaluate the prophylactic efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan against RIHD in children through a comprehensive translational research pipeline.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was first conducted in 40 paediatric solid tumour patients, comparing cardiac function before and 1 week after radiotherapy, with 80 healthy controls. A juvenile rat RIHD model was then established, in which the efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan was assessed and validated through longitudinal echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, histopathology, bulk RNA-seq, and single-nucleus RNA-seq. Finally, a prospective clinical cohort (n = 15 sacubitril/valsartan, n = 15 control) was conducted in paediatric patients post-radiotherapy, with a 12-month follow-up for efficacy and safety.
RESULTS: In paediatric patients, radiotherapy significantly impaired biventricular function, notably reducing left ventricular global longitudinal strain, and mean heart radiation dose was significantly correlated with cardiac function impairment. In juvenile rats, sacubitril/valsartan attenuated pathological ventricular wall thickening, myocardial fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and perfusion deficits. Mechanistically, it mitigated endothelial cell damage and immune cell activation, promoted a macrophage phenotypic shift from M1 to M2, suppressed fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, and broadly attenuated pro-fibrotic and inflammatory cell-cell communication. In the clinical cohort, sacubitril/valsartan significantly improved left ventricular global longitudinal strain and aortic compliance vs controls, with a favourable safety profile.
CONCLUSIONS: This first-in-kind translational study demonstrates that early prophylaxis with sacubitril/valsartan is a feasible and effective strategy to mitigate radiation-induced cardiotoxicity in children. These findings, underpinned by multi-modal validation from bench to bedside, challenge the reactive management paradigm in paediatric cardio-oncology and establish a foundational evidence base for a new standard of proactive heart care in childhood cancer survivors.

Title: Hand Microcirculatory Perfusion During Simulated Simultaneous Proximal or Distal Radial and Ulnar Artery Occlusion: A Laser Doppler Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The distal radial artery access has been proposed as an alternative route to overcome some limitations and to reduce complications of conventional radial acces.
AIMS: This study aimed to compare hand microcirculatory perfusion during two experimentally induced combined-compression conditions: combined proximal radial and ulnar artery compression and combined distal radial and ulnar artery compression.
METHODS: A prospective, nonrandomized, fixed-sequence, within-participant physiological study was conducted on 50 healthy volunteers. Laser Doppler perfusion imaging with PeriScan PIM III device (Perimed AB, Järfälla, Sweden) was employed to quantify palmar microvascular flux during three prespecified sequential conditions: baseline assessment, combined proximal radial and ulnar artery compression, and combined distal radial and ulnar artery compression. Ulnar-flow cessation was confirmed by Doppler ultrasound before each compressed acquisition. The primary endpoint was the within-subject difference in palmar perfusion, expressed in terms of perfusion units (PU) in the different experimental conditions. Exploratory subgroup analyses by sex and weight status (normal weight vs. overweight/obese) were performed.
RESULTS: Mean palmar cutaneous microvascular flux was 58.18 ± 23.18 PU at baseline, 5.91 ± 4.48 PU during proximal combined compression, and 28.46 ± 12.69 PU during distal combined compression. At the individual-participant level, residual flux corresponded to 10.9 ± 8.5% and 50.4 ± 15.8% of baseline during proximal and distal combined compression, respectively. In the primary paired comparison, residual palmar cutaneous microvascular flux was significantly higher during distal than during proximal combined-compression condition (mean paired difference, 22.56 PU; Bonferroni-adjusted 95% CI, 18.58-26.53 PU; adjusted p < 0.001). Exploratory condition-by-sex (p = 0.265) and condition-by-weight-status (p = 0.642) interactions were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to directly compare palmar perfusion during combined proximal versus distal radial and ulnar artery compression using laser Doppler perfusion imaging. The less impaired perfusion during simulated distal radial and ulnar artery occlusion supports a physiological hypothesis regarding the influence of radial compression level on residual cutaneous microvascular flux, particularly when ulnar flow is compromised. However, confirmation in randomized, counterbalanced studies and in patients undergoing coronary procedures is required.

Title: Complications in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation: an analysis of the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Difficult tracheal intubation is associated with serious complications, including hypoxia, bradycardia and cardiac arrest. Neonates have increased physiologic vulnerability compared with older children, yet detailed data on management strategies and outcomes in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation remain limited. We hypothesised that clinicians have lower first-attempt tracheal intubation success and higher complication rates for neonates compared with older children with difficult tracheal intubation.
METHODS: We analysed the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry to determine tracheal intubation first attempt success and incidence of complications. We used logistic regression to identify variables associated with complications in neonates.
RESULTS: During the study period, 6283 paediatric difficult tracheal intubations were recorded, including 420 neonates. First attempt success was lower for neonates (139/420, 33.1%) than older children (2394/4683, 51.1%). Complications occurred more frequently in neonates (123/420, 29.3%) than older children (637/4683, 13.6%). Hypoxia occurred in 92/420 (21.9%) neonates and 269/4683 (5.7%) older children. Severe complications were more frequent in neonates vs. older children (12/420, 2.9% vs. 30/4683, 0.6%, respectively), with cardiac arrests occurring in 4/420 (1.0%) neonates and 11/4683 (0.2%) older children. Difficult mask ventilation occurred more frequently in neonates (60/420, 14.3%) than older children (353/4681, 7.5%). In neonates, increased number of tracheal intubation attempts (aOR 1.61 per attempt, 95%CI 1.30-2.00, p < 0.001) and difficult facemask ventilation (aOR 3.17, 95%CI 1.38-7.30, p = 0.007) were associated with complications. Anticipated difficulty with airway management had a protective effect (aOR 0.37, 95%CI 0.16-0.88, p = 0.025).
DISCUSSION: Neonates with difficult tracheal intubation experience a substantially higher rate of complications than older children. Early recognition of risk is critical in order to enable careful planning to minimise tracheal intubation attempts in this vulnerable population.

Title: Inflammation and early atherosclerosis beyond traditional risk factors: an imaging study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Understanding how inflammation contributes to subclinical atherosclerosis (SA) plaque burden, beyond the impact of established cardiovascular risk factors, holds significant implications for the success of preventive strategies focused on the reduction of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The aim of this study was to investigate the relative contribution of inflammation, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDLc), and systolic blood pressure (SBP), as determinants of SA plaque burden in a cohort of middle-aged, asymptomatic individuals, using non-invasive imaging techniques.
METHODS: Participants from the Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis (PESA) study (median age 45 years) underwent longitudinal screening every 3 years (baseline, 3- and 6-year visits) involving serial blood testing [including white blood cell (WBC) count, fibrinogen, oxidized LDLc, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein], physical examinations and imaging assessments with three-dimensional vascular ultrasound of peripheral arteries, and coronary artery calcium quantification. Global plaque volume (GPV, mm3; bilateral carotid plus femoral plaque burden) at 6-year follow-up was the primary outcome. Multivariable linear regression and proportional odds models determined the link of GPV to both inflammatory markers and established cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: Of the 3471 participants, 58% had SA (GPV >0 mm3) at 6-year follow-up. WBC count had the strongest statistical associations with 6-year SA burden after adjusting for age, sex, baseline LDLc, and mean SBP, with an estimated 32.6% increase in GPV per one standard deviation (SD) increase in WBC (Z = 7.33, P < 1 × 10-10). GPV at 6 years increased 40.9% per one SD increase in baseline LDLc and 42.7% per one SD increase in mean SBP (Z = 8.80 and Z = 7.97, respectively, both P < 1 × 10-10; their SDs were 29.4 mg/dL and 11.5 mmHg, respectively), followed by fibrinogen (16.8% increase in GPV per one SD increase, Z = 3.91, P < .0001). High-sensitivity C-reactive protein was not predictive of greater GPV at 6 years (Z = 1.36, P = .174). For WBC, the marked trend in risk occurred only at levels above its median. Similar patterns were observed for separate analyses of carotid and femoral plaque volumes, and coronary artery calcium. Increasing levels of WBC and fibrinogen were also associated with a greater anatomical spread of disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Inflammation contributes to SA burden, as assessed by direct plaque quantification, beyond the effects of LDLc and SBP. These findings indicate that inflammation, captured through the use of systemic inflammatory markers, is a risk factor relevant across the entire continuum of atherosclerosis, exerting a deleterious impact comparable to that of LDLc and SBP.

Title: Different Clinical Profile of Cannabis Intoxication Cases: Children Versus Adults.
Journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
Abstract:
AIMS: This observational, descriptive, retrospective study aimed to evaluate whether cannabis exposure presents distinct clinical patterns between paediatric and adult populations.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Toxicological Information and Assistance Center of Santa Catarina (CIATox/SC), and analyses were performed using Microsoft Excel 365.
RESULTS: A total of 697 suspected cannabis intoxication cases were identified, including 112 paediatric and 585 adult cases. Male patients predominated (67%), and the most affected age group was 20-29 years (39.7%). Most cases were classified as mild (76.9%) and evolved favourably. In children aged 0-14 years, the most frequent clinical manifestations were drowsiness (64.2%), lethargy (19.7%) and altered level of consciousness (14.8%), indicating a clinical profile distinct from that observed in adults. Paediatric cases were mainly associated with oral ingestion and central nervous system depression, suggesting the need for prolonged observation and careful neurological monitoring. In adults, cardiovascular and neuropsychiatric manifestations were more common. Although most cases had low severity and favourable outcomes, greater severity was associated with high doses and polysubstance use. Seven deaths were recorded, all involving concomitant use of other substances, mainly cocaine.
CONCLUSION: These findings support the hypothesis that cannabis intoxication presents age-dependent clinical patterns, providing relevant information for risk assessment, clinical management and decision-making in poison centre and emergency care settings.

Title: The role of global longitudinal strain change in the assessment of early cardiotoxicity in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: a prospective pilot study of 30 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve survival in various malignancies but may cause immune-mediated cardiotoxicity. Because left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) typically declines late, more sensitive markers are needed for early detection of subclinical myocardial injury. This study investigated the association between changes in global longitudinal strain (GLS) and early cardiotoxicity in patients receiving ICIs.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center pilot study, 30 consecutive adult patients scheduled for ICI therapy were enrolled. Serial transthoracic echocardiography was performed at baseline, 6 to 8 weeks, and 12 weeks to measure LVEF using the biplane Simpson method and GLS using 2D speckle-tracking echocardiography. Cardiotoxicity was defined as a ≥ 10% absolute reduction in LVEF to < 50% and/or new-onset heart failure, suspected myocarditis, clinically significant arrhythmia, or major cardiovascular events. A relative GLS reduction ≥ 15% was considered indicative of subclinical dysfunction.
RESULTS: During a mean 12-week follow-up, cardiotoxicity occurred in six patients (20.0%). In affected patients, GLS significantly deteriorated early (from - 18.2% ± 2.5% to - 14.1% ± 2.8%, P < 0.001), preceding any significant decline in LVEF. Patients without cardiotoxicity showed stable GLS and LVEF values. A ≥ 15% GLS reduction was associated with cardiotoxicity and showed exploratory discriminatory ability, with 83.3% sensitivity and 91.7% specificity (area under the curve, 0.86; 95% confidence interval, 0.72-0.97).
CONCLUSIONS: Early GLS deterioration was associated with cardiotoxicity despite relatively preserved LVEF. Given the temporal overlap between GLS assessment and cardiotoxicity events in several patients, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Title: Association of hemoglobin glycation index with all-cause mortality in critically.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hemoglobin glycation index (HGI), which quantifies individual variation in the relationship between hemoglobin A1c and glucose levels, has been associated with adverse outcomes across various clinical populations. However, the prognostic significance of HGI in critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation remains unknown. We investigated the association between HGI and all-cause mortality in this population.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV databases. Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with atrial fibrillation during ICU admission were included. HGI was calculated as the difference between observed and predicted hemoglobin A1c values (predicted HbA1c = 0.013 × glucose + 4.804). Primary outcomes were in-hospital and 30-day mortality. Patients were stratified into HGI quartiles. Statistical analyses included Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, restricted cubic splines, and multivariable logistic and Cox regression models. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among 9,924 critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation (median age 72.3 years, 63.1% male), 714 (7.2%) died during hospitalization and 912 (9.2%) died within 30 days of ICU admission. Non-survivors had significantly lower HGI values than survivors (-2.1 vs. -2.0, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated markedly inferior survival in the lowest HGI quartile (P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed an L-shaped dose-response relationship with threshold effects. In fully adjusted models, each 1-unit HGI increase was associated with reduced mortality (in-hospital: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.97; 30-day: HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.97). These associations remained consistent across subgroups and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher HGI values are independently associated with reduced short-term mortality risk in critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation. HGI represents a valuable prognostic biomarker for risk stratification and clinical decision-making in this population.

Title: The relationship between 100 cases of severe and recurrent epistaxis and long-term oral anticoagulants, age and hypertension.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This single-center retrospective cohort study aimed to explore the risk factors for severe and recurrent spontaneous epistaxis, including long-term oral anticoagulants (OAC), age, and hypertension.
RESULTS: Among the 100 participants, 23% were patients who had been using OAC for a long time. Compared with non-OAC users, the incidence of severe epistaxis in OAC users was significantly higher (52.17% [12/23] vs. 23.38% [18/77], p = 0.003), and the incidence of recurrent epistaxis within 3 months was also higher (43.48% [10/23] vs. 19.48% [15/77], p = 0.008). Multivariate logistic regression analysis confirmed that long-term use of OAC (severe epistaxis: relative risk ratio [odds ratios (OR)] = 2.91, 95% confidence interval [confidence intervals (CI)] 1.34-6.32, p = 0.007; recurrent epistaxis: OR = 2.69, 95% CI 1.23-5.93, p = 0.013) and age ≥ 70 years (severe epistaxis: OR = 2.36, 95% CI 1.13-4.92, p = 0.022; recurrent epistaxis: OR = 2.07, 95% CI 1.03-4.15, p = 0.042) were highly correlated with the occurrence of severe/recurrent epistaxis. After adjusting for covariates, hypertension did not show an obviously association with severe or recurrent epistaxis (all p > 0.05). In this study, diabetes, coronary heart disease, and cerebral infarction did not show a significant increase in bleeding risk.

Title: Association of serum vitamin C and E levels with mortality in individuals with metabolic syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Existing evidence suggests the importance of oxidative stress in the etiology of metabolic syndrome (MetS), which is a growing global health problem. However, the impact of serum antioxidant vitamins (C and E) levels on the clinical outcomes of the MetS population is unknown.
METHODS: This cohort study included 2102 adults diagnosed with MetS, who participated in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey from 2003 to 2006. Serum levels of vitamin C, α-tocopherol, and γ-tocopherol were measured. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards models to analyze the association between serum levels of vitamins and the risk of mortality from all causes, CVD, and cancer. Analyses controlled for demographic characteristics, body mass index, smoking, drinking, diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia.
RESULTS: Among the 2102 participants, 731all-cause deaths were documented, including 270 CVD deaths and 52 cancer deaths. Compared to the reference group with serum vitamin C levels of 0.02-0.65 mg/dL, the multivariable-adjusted HRs for high vitamin C levels (1.08-4.26 mg/dL) were 0.65 (95% CI, 0.53-0.79) for all-cause mortality and 0.60 (95% CI, 0.42-0.85) for CVD mortality. Compared to the reference group with serum α-tocopherol levels of 354-1139 µg/dL, the adjusted HRs were 0.52 (95% CI, 0.33-0.83) for mid-range α-tocopherol levels (1140-1590 µg/dL) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25) for high-range levels (1591-6405 µg/dL) for cancer mortality. For serum γ-tocopherol, compared to the reference group (16-190 µg/dL), the HR for mid-range levels (191-315 µg/dL) was 1.79 (95% CI, 1.25-2.55) and for high-range levels (316-3122 µg/dL) was 1.74 (95% CI, 1.10-2.75) for CVD mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlights the clinical value of antioxidant vitamins in predicting the survival of the MetS population. Vitamin C are associated with a reduced risk of death from all causes and CVD in individuals with MetS. Mid-range α-tocopherol levels may decrease the risk of cancer mortality, while high-range γ-tocopherol levels could increase the risk of CVD mortality. Individuals with MetS may require more careful antioxidant vitamins supplement to prevent the development of other diseases and thereby reduce mortality.

Title: Associations of grip strength, muscle mass, and fat-to-muscle ratio with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in chinese community adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a global health challenge. However, few studies have explored the associations between muscle health and CKM syndrome. This study aimed to investigate the associations between appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM), grip strength, and fat-to-muscle ratio (FMR) and advanced CKM syndrome in a Chinese community-based population.
METHODS: We conducted an observational study involving 7,330 Chinese adults. CKM syndrome is categorized into five stages, with stages 3-4 defined as advanced CKM syndrome. An electronic dynamometer and bioelectrical impedance analysis were used to measure grip strength, ASM, and FMR. The FMR was calculated as fat mass divided by muscle mass, and ASM/BMI as ASM divided by body mass index (BMI). Associations of grip strength, ASM/BMI, and FMR with advanced CKM syndrome were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, with subgroup analyses by age and sex. Subgroup analyses were further conducted to explore potential interactions.
RESULTS: Advanced CKM syndrome was identified in 8.57% of participants. Higher ASM/BMI (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.15-0.45) and grip strength (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.30-0.59) were inversely linked to the likelihood of having advanced CKM syndrome (P-trend < 0.001). Conversely, a higher FMR was associated with higher odds of advanced CKM syndrome (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.26-3.89; P-trend < 0.05). Furthermore, subgroup analyses showed that the inverse association between grip strength and advanced CKM syndrome was stronger among females (P for interaction = 0.007). A nonlinear, L-shaped association was observed between grip strength and advanced CKM syndrome, with an inflection point at 26.2 kg in females.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower ASM/BMI and grip strength, and a higher FMR are associated with an increased likelihood of advanced CKM syndrome. Additionally, a plausible grip-strength threshold (~ 26.2 kg) was identified among females. These findings support evaluating muscle health for risk stratification in CKM syndrome.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registry http//www.chictr.org.cn/, TRN ChiCTR2100054130, Registration date 9 December, 2021.

Title: Efficacy and safety of haemopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) for mucopolysaccharidosis type I-Hurler syndrome (MPS-IH): a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mucopolysaccharidosis type I-Hurler's (MPS-IH) is the most severe form of MPS-I, with onset in infancy, followed by rapid neurodegeneration, and death typically within the first decade in untreated patients. A previous systematic review (SR) concluded that treatment with allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplant (allo-HSCT) offers a clear survival and neurocognitive advantage, but does not prevent residual somatic disease. That review was published 15 years ago, which implies a need for a new SR to capture long-term efficacy, as well as safety outcomes reported since.
METHODS: We conducted a SR following guidelines of the Cochrane Collaboration and the Centre for Reviews and Dissemination. The search strategy had no date limits and was applied to multiple databases including MEDLINE and EMBASE. Searches were completed on 17.12.24. Reference checking ensured inclusion of all papers. All studies of allo-HSCT in MPS-IH were included if there were any efficacy outcomes with at least 5-years of follow-up, or any safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Thirty-five studies were included, none of which were comparative, 28 were retrospective and three included enzyme replacement therapy. Twenty-seven reported > 5-year efficacy, which showed survival was at least 80% in many studies (median follow-up between 3.8 and 9 years), including up to 62% at 10 years in one study, and 73.7% at 20 years in another. Neurocognitive and ambulatory preservation was observed in some patients, but in others there was progressive decline. Skeletal disease, poor ophthalmological outcomes with corneal opacity, cardiovascular disease, particularly affecting the heart valves, and pulmonary disease were also common. Nineteen studies reported safety, showing that graft versus host disease and pulmonary infections were common.
CONCLUSION: Allo-HSCT appears to be an effective intervention for MPS-IH that can extend survival and preserve long-term neurological and physical function, particularly when administered early. However, although it remains the standard of care in modifying the disease course, skeletal, cardiovascular and sensory deficits often persist. The procedure also carries measurable risks, particularly related to mortality, GvHD and infection. Consequently, continued research and innovation are essential to improve long-term outcomes and quality of life for individuals with MPS‑IH.

Title: Joint association of the cholesterol-HDL-glucose index and frailty with new-onset cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older adults: evidence from the prospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death and disability among middle-aged and older adults. Metabolic burden and frailty frequently co-occur in this population. However, few quantitative indicators capture their combined contribution to cardiovascular risk. We examined the association between a composite indicator integrating the cholesterol-HDL-glucose (CHG) index and the frailty index (FI) and the risk of incident CVD.
METHODS: Using baseline data from 2011 and follow-up data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), we included participants aged ≥ 45 years without baseline CVD. CHG-FI was constructed by integrating CHG and FI in a multiplicative form; FI was derived using a cumulative deficit model. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate HRs and 95% CIs. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to assess dose-response relationships. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to examine the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: A total of 7,123 participants were included. During a median follow-up of 9 years, 1,655 participants developed incident CVD (23.2%), including 554 cases of stroke (7.8%) and 1,287 cases of heart disease (18.1%). In the fully adjusted model, each one-unit increase in CHG-FI was associated with a 61% higher risk of CVD (HR 1.61, 95% CI 1.48-1.75), a 56% higher risk of stroke (HR 1.56, 95% CI 1.35-1.80), and a 64% higher risk of heart disease (HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.49-1.80) (all P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, the risks of incident CVD, stroke, and heart disease generally increased across higher quartiles of CHG-FI. RCS analyses revealed a positive dose-response association of CHG-FI with incident CVD and heart disease, with significant nonlinearity for both outcomes (all P for non-linearity < 0.001). In contrast, stroke risk showed a more nearly linear pattern after full adjustment (P for non-linearity = 0.074). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses yielded findings broadly consistent with the primary analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher CHG-FI was independently associated with increased risks of incident CVD, stroke, and heart disease. CHG-FI may provide complementary information for early cardiovascular risk identification in middle-aged and older adults, although its incremental predictive value beyond FI alone appears modest. Further validation is needed before its clinical utility can be more firmly established.

Title: Associations of the triglyceride-glucose index, lipid-derived parameters, and their joint exposure with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a nationwide prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and non-traditional lipid parameters (nTLPs) are accessible markers of cardiometabolic risk; however, their joint association with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) and the incremental predictive value of adding nTLPs to the TyG index remain unclear.
METHODS: This investigation utilized longitudinal datasets sourced from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), encompassing 7159 eligible participants. Kaplan-Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and restricted cubic splines were used to evaluate associations between joint TyG-nTLP exposure and incident CMM. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. Model discrimination and incremental predictive value were examined using receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: The median follow-up duration was 9 years, during which 758 participants developed CMM, corresponding to a cumulative incidence of 10.59%. Compared with participants in the dual-low groups for the TyG index and nTLPs, those in the dual-high groups had a higher risk of developing CMM. The corresponding fully adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were 1.80 (95% CI 1.51-2.14) when both the TyG index and AIP were at high levels, 2.16 (95% CI 1.74-2.67) when both the TyG index and Non-HDL-C were at high levels, 2.10 (95% CI 1.72-2.57) when both the TyG index and CRI-I were at high levels, 2.05 (95% CI 1.66-2.53) when both the TyG index and CRI-II were at high levels, and 1.95 (95% CI 1.62-2.36) when both the TyG index and LCI were at high levels. Adding nTLPs to the TyG-based model resulted in only a modest incremental improvement in predictive performance.
CONCLUSION: Among middle-aged and older adults, jointly elevated TyG index and nTLPs were associated with a higher risk of incident CMM, with the associations being more evident for incident diabetes and stroke than for incident heart disease. The combined assessment of the TyG index and nTLPs may provide complementary information for the early identification and risk stratification of individuals at elevated risk of CMM.

Title: Construction and validation of a differential diagnosis model for multiple myeloma and lymphoma based on XGBoost machine learning: an explaining analysis study of SHAP.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple myeloma (MM) and lymphoma can share overlapping clinical features but require different diagnostic and treatment strategies. Machine learning (ML) may identify discriminative patterns from routinely available clinical data and support rapid triage.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients from the Third Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine between 2015 and 2025. Data from 2015 to 2024 (n = 2,759) were used for model development, and the 2025 cohort (n = 1,011) served as an independent temporal external validation set. Feature selection combined univariate analysis, collinearity assessment, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and Boruta, yielding 14 core features. Nine ML models were compared.
RESULTS: XGBoost showed the best validation performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.964, accuracy of 0.904, sensitivity of 0.913, specificity of 0.896, positive predictive value of 0.889, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.918. In the held-out internal test set, the final model achieved an AUC of 0.947 and an accuracy of 0.890. External validation yielded an AUC of 0.713, sensitivity of 0.400, specificity of 0.768, and NPV of 0.876. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) identified age, mean corpuscular hemoglobin, red cell distribution width coefficient of variation, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and mean corpuscular volume as the leading contributors to model predictions.
CONCLUSIONS: The XGBoost model demonstrated good discriminatory ability in distinguishing multiple myeloma from lymphoma by integrating 14 routinely available variables: age, WBC, MONO, EO, BASO%, RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, RDW-CV, PLT, LYMPH/MONO, and PLT/LYMPH. This multivariable framework may serve as an adjunctive tool to support the differential diagnosis of these two hematological malignancies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Validation Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: 27-gauge microincision vitrectomy for acute nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy with peripapillary wrinkles: a pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess the functional stabilizing potential and structural safety of 27-gauge microincision vitrectomy surgery (MIVS) in a targeted subgroup of patients with acute nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) presenting with peripapillary wrinkles (PPWs).
METHODS: In this prospective, nonrandomized, patient-choice controlled pilot study, 39 patients presenting with acute unilateral NAION and PPWs (within 21 days of onset) were allocated into a surgical group (27-gauge MIVS) and a medical control group (tapered oral prednisone). All participants additionally received oral methylcobalamin. Main outcome measures included changes from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), mean deviation (MD), and visual field index (VFI); clinically meaningful response rates (≥ 15-letter BCVA gain/loss, ≥ 10% VFI, ≥ 3 dB MD change); and structural integrity of the foveal cone mosaic and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) using AOSLO.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable. Changes from baseline in BCVA, MD, and VFI were significantly better in the PPWs+MIVS group across all follow-up intervals (P < 0.05). The rates of MD improvement (≥ 3 dB) and VFI improvement (≥ 10%) were higher in the PPWs+MIVS group at 3 months (55.56% vs. 18.75%; P = 0.04). No eyes in the PPWs+MIVS group experienced clinically meaningful decline, compared to 25-33% for BCVA and 38-44% for visual field in the PPWs+Prednisone group (all P < 0.05). Exploratory AOSLO and pRNFL assessments in a single representative case revealed no postoperative structural damage to photoreceptors or RNFLs.
CONCLUSIONS: 27-gauge MIVS may be associated with visual benefits for acute NAION patients with PPWs. The favorable short-term safety profile and exploratory structural observations, coupled with potential functional benefits, warrants further investigation in larger randomized trials to confirm the role of MIVS in this subgroup.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2200066515, December 7, 2022, retrospectively registered.

Title: Influence of diabetes mellitus on dapagliflozin response after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR): insights from the DAPA-TAVI trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The DAPA-TAVI trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin reduced the composite of all-cause mortality or worsening heart failure (HF) at 1 year in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with prior HF. Whether the magnitude of this benefit differs according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status remains uncertain.
METHODS: This pre-specified subgroup analysis of the multicenter randomized DAPA-TAVI trial conducted at 39 centers in Spain, which enrolled 1222 patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR with prior HF and at least one high-risk condition. Patients were stratified by the presence or absence of DM. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or worsening HF at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of the primary endpoint, cardiovascular death, and safety outcomes. Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for age, sex, coronary artery disease, baseline ejection fraction and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to estimate treatment effects.
RESULTS: Among 1222 patients, 537 (43.9%) had DM. In patients with DM, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the primary endpoint compared with standard care (15.2% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.580; 95% CI 0.389-0.866; p = 0.008; number needed to treat [NNT] = 11), driven primarily by fewer worsening HF events. In patients without DM, the reduction was numerically lower and non-significant (15.0% vs. 18.0%; HR 0.814; 95% CI 0.560-1.183; p = 0.280; NNT = 32). Genital infections were more frequent with dapagliflozin in patients with DM, whereas symptomatic hypotension was more common in those without DM. No significant differences in serious adverse events were observed in either subgroup. No statistically significant interactions between DM status and treatment effect were observed for the primary or secondary endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: In this pre-specified subanalysis of the DAPA-TAVI trial, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of death or worsening HF in patients with DM undergoing TAVR, with a favorable benefit-risk profile, whereas a more modest and non-significant effect was observed in non-DM patients. Although no statistically significant interaction according to diabetes status was observed, the apparently greater benefit among patients with DM warrants further investigation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: The relationship between high-risk obstructive sleep apnea as identified by STOP-BANG questionnaire and diabetic retinopathy: a case-control observational study at a tertiary center in Jordan.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of vision loss worldwide. While metabolic control of blood glucose is the standard of care, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has emerged as a potential systemic factor influencing retinal disease. This study investigated the association between OSA risk, as assessed by the STOP-BANG questionnaire, and the presence of DR in a Jordanian cohort.
METHODS: A case-control observational study was conducted at a tertiary center in Jordan, including 300 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Participants were divided into a disease group (moderate non-proliferative DR or worse and/or diabetic macular edema) and a control group (no DR). OSA risk was assessed using the STOP-BANG questionnaire. Clinical data were retrieved from electronic medical records. Multivariate logistic regression models were constructed with sequential adjustment for demographic, metabolic, and vascular factors.
RESULTS: High-risk OSA category (as identified by the STOP-BANG questionnaire) was more frequent in the DR group compared with controls (odds ratio [OR]: 2.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.12-4.24; p = 0.023). This association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, HbA1c, and duration of diabetes (adjusted OR: 2.12; 95% CI: 1.08-4.16; p = 0.029), and after further adjustment for hypertension and body mass index also (adjusted OR: 2.87; 95% CI: 1.10-7.50; p = 0.032).
CONCLUSION: High-risk OSA category (as identified by the STOP-BANG questionnaire) was associated with DR in unadjusted and partially adjusted analyses. These findings suggest that the relationship between OSA high-risk category and DR is present in our cohort. However, further studies using objective OSA diagnostic methods are warranted.

Title: Oral anticoagulation therapy in nonagenarian patients with atrial fibrillation: usage patterns, predictors, and in-hospital outcomes from a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is highly prevalent in nonagenarians (≥ 90 years). However, this group is often excluded from clinical trials, leaving limited real-world evidence on oral anticoagulant (OAC) use, safety, and efficacy. This study sought to investigate the usage patterns, predictors, and in-hospital outcomes of OAC therapy in nonagenarian patients with AF to provide real-world evidence to inform clinical decision-making.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center analysis was conducted on 290 nonagenarian AF patients (Beijing Hospital, 2018-2024). Patients were grouped as OAC (n = 89) or non-OAC (n = 201).
PRIMARY ENDPOINTS: In-hospital stroke/SE (efficacy) and major bleeding (ISTH criteria; safety). Secondary endpoints included in-hospital composite efficacy, net clinical benefit (stroke/SE/major bleeding/all-cause death), and all-cause death. Multivariate logistic regression identified OAC predictors; OAC temporal trends were analyzed.
RESULTS: The overall OAC utilization rate was 30.69% and showed a steady annual increase. Positive predictors of OAC use included a history of ischemic stroke (OR = 2.653) and heart failure (OR = 2.083), while negative predictors included bedridden status (OR = 0.134), and concomitant antiplatelet use (OR = 0.203). DOAC accounted for 82.02% of OAC prescription, and 63.01% of DOAC users were inappropriately underdosed. Compared with the non-OAC group, OAC use was significantly associated with a lower risk of in-hospital stroke/SE (6.74% vs. 15.42%, OR = 0.396, 95% CI = 0.159-0.987, p = 0.047) and improved secondary composite efficacy outcomes (OR = 0.491, p = 0.024). The OAC group also demonstrated a numerically lower incidence of net clinical benefit outcomes (20.22% vs. 30.85%), though it did not differ significantly between groups (2.25% vs. 0.50%, p = 0.215), though total bleeding events were higher in the OAC group (49.44% vs. 36.32%, p = 0.037).
CONCLUSIONS: Although the overall OAC utilization rate in AF patients aged ≥ 90 years remains relatively low, it has shown a steady annual increase, with DOACs emerging as the predominant choice. OAC therapy is significantly associated with a lower risk of in-hospital stroke and demonstrates favorable net clinical benefit, highlighting the potential value of the judicious use of OAC in this population.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, identifier ChiCTR2300076161.

Title: Association of sodium bicarbonate use during CPR with sustained return of spontaneous circulation in adult in-hospital cardiac arrest.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium bicarbonate (SB) is frequently administered during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) despite contemporary guidelines advising against routine use. Observational evaluation is challenging because SB is often given later in resuscitations, creating confounding by indication and resuscitation-time bias. We assessed the association between SB administration during CPR and sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC).
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult (≥ 18 years) in-hospital cardiac arrests from January 1, 2020, to January 2, 2025, at a single academic hospital (~ 1,000 beds). Arrests were documented in real time on standardized Code Blue forms with stopwatch timestamps and supplemented with electronic medical record data. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC (≥ 20 min). Crude associations were estimated using risk difference (RD), risk ratio (RR), and odds ratio (OR). To account for time-varying confounding, we implemented a marginal structural model (MSM) with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting using discrete 2-minute intervals from CPR initiation to sustained ROSC or termination. SB was modeled as a time-varying initiation exposure.
RESULTS: Among 1,301 events, 1,298 were included after excluding 3 with missing exposure/outcome. SB was administered in 565/1,298 (43.5%) cases; sustained ROSC occurred in 803/1,298 (61.9%) overall. In crude analysis, sustained ROSC occurred in 304/565 (53.8%) SB-exposed versus 499/733 (68.1%) unexposed cases (RD - 14.3%, 95% CI - 19.6 to - 9.0; OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.44-0.69; p < 0.0001). In the weighted MSM, SB initiation was not associated with higher sustained ROSC (aRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91-1.06; marginal risk difference - 1.2%, 95% CI - 4.7 to + 2.3). Exploratory timing and 15-minute landmark analyses did not identify a clear administration window associated with higher sustained ROSC.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, SB use during CPR was associated with lower sustained ROSC in crude analyses, but the association attenuated toward the null after adjustment for measured time-varying confounding. Exploratory analyses did not identify a clear timing-dependent association between SB initiation and sustained ROSC. Because downstream outcomes and specific guideline-supported indications were incompletely captured, these findings should be interpreted as limited to sustained ROSC in an unselected in-hospital cardiac arrest cohort.

Title: Effects of non-soy legume protein on lipid profile in hypercholesterolemic adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) continues to rank as the foremost cause of death globally, with dyslipidemia representing a major contributing risk factor. While soy legumes have been extensively studied for their lipid-lowering effects, the extent to which non-soy legume protein influences lipid profiles in hypercholesterolemic adults warrants investigation.
METHODS: Databases including PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were comprehensively searched through September 23, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the impact of non-soy legume protein intake on lipid profiles in adults were included. The primary outcomes encompassed alterations in total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Weighted mean differences (WMD) alongside 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were derived using random- or fixed-effects models contingent on heterogeneity assessment. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, body mass index (BMI), and intervention duration. Moreover, the certainty of evidence for each outcome was assessed using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Six RCTs comprising 297 hypercholesterolemic adults and eight treatment arms were included. Overall, non-soy legume protein intake yielded no statistically significant changes in lipid parameters (TG: 0.895 mg/dL; 95% CI: -1.980 to 3.769; TC: -2.251 mg/dL; 95% CI: -4.693 to 0.192; LDL-C: -1.533 mg/dL; 95% CI: -3.575 to 0.509; HDL-C: 0.187 mg/dL; 95% CI: -0.614 to 0.988). However, subgroup analyses disclosed a statistically significant TC reduction in participants older than 50 years (-8.27 mg/dL; 95% CI: -16.41 to -0.12) and those with a BMI below 28 kg/m² (-5.18 mg/dL; 95% CI: -9.28 to -1.08). Similarly, LDL-C was significantly associated with a reduction in participants with BMI < 28 kg/m² (-2.94 mg/dL; 95% CI: -5.87 to -0.01). The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was rated as very low according to the GRADE approach.
CONCLUSION: While non-soy legume protein consumption did not significantly impact overall lipid profiles, modest reductions in TC and LDL-C were observed in certain subgroups; however, these findings are based on a limited number of studies and should be interpreted cautiously as exploratory. These results indicate that the cholesterol-modulating capacity of non-soy legume proteins may be shaped by individual characteristics and warrant further investigation to identify optimal consumption parameters and mechanisms of action.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) and is accessible at: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ . The registration ID is CRD420251045801.

Title: Risk model prediction of ICU mortality in aortic dissection patients based on MIMIC-IV.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to explore risk factors derived from clinical characteristics that are associated with intensive care unit (ICU) outcomes in patients with aortic dissection (AD).
METHODS: Total 478 patients' data including demographic characteristics, vital signs, hematological parameters, and other laboratory tests, were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC‑IV) database. Five different machine-learning methods were used to construct the prediction models.
RESULTS: Patients with Stanford type B dissection exhibited significantly lower heart rate (P = 0.022), neutrophil count (P = 0.015), chloride level (P = 0.018), and SOFA score (P = 0.008), but higher red blood cell count (P = 0.003), white blood cell count (P = 0.02), monocyte count (P < 0.001), basophil count (P = 0.019), platelet count (P < 0.001), glucose (P = 0.003), sodium (P = 0.03), and total calcium (P < 0.001) compared with type A patients. Non‑survivors in the ICU had significantly higher body mass index (P = 0.042), anion gap (P = 0.004), urea nitrogen (P = 0.041), creatinine (P = 0.011), alanine aminotransferase (ALT, P < 0.001), aspartate aminotransferase (AST, P < 0.001), and SOFA score (P = 0.024), along with lower levels of SaO₂ (P = 0.005), SvO₂ (P = 0.002), red blood cell count (P = 0.006), mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (P = 0.001), white blood cell count (P = 0.029), eosinophils (P = 0.03), platelets (P = 0.004), and urine output (P = 0.02) compared with survivors. In predictive modelling, the random‑forest‑based approach achieved a higher area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.825, versus 0.678 for logistic regression and 0.553 for the neural network.
CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated predictive models of ICU mortality in AD patients. Risk factors for ICU mortality in AD patients include SvO₂, anion gap, and AST, among which SvO₂ appears to be a reliable predictor of clinical outcome.

Title: Interpretable machine learning reveals the association of metabolic, inflammatory, and nutritional indices with ischemic stroke complicated by metabolic abnormality clustering.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to explore correlations between metabolic, inflammatory and nutritional composite indices and metabolic abnormality clustering (MAC) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS), and build an interpretable Clinlabomics model to support early risk screening and stratified clinical management.
METHODS: This study retrospectively recruited 2,183 AIS patients from Suining Central Hospital between January 2023 and July 2025, who were divided into MAC (n = 621) and non-MAC (n = 1,562) groups. We included a panel of glucose and lipid metabolic parameters as well as their composite metabolic indices. The cohort was randomly split into a 7:3 training set (n = 1,529) and internal test set (n = 654), with an independent temporal validation set of 496 patients. In the training cohort, feature selection was performed via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Eleven machine learning algorithms were used to develop Clinlabomics models. The optimal algorithm was selected based on sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, F1-score, and AUC. Interpretability analysis was performed on the optimal Clinlabomics model using feature importance ranking and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify core features. Subsequently, univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify metabolic signatures significantly associated with the comorbidity of MAC and AIS.
RESULTS: A total of 22 feature variables were identified via LASSO analysis. Eleven machine learning algorithms were adopted to develop Clinlabomics models in the training cohort, among which the recursive partitioning and regression trees (rpart) algorithm was identified as the optimal machine learning algorithm. After hyperparameter tuning, the optimal complexity parameter (cp.) was 0.00015. Following tuning, the AUC values in the training, test, and temporal validation cohorts were as follows: 0.979 (95% CI: 0.970-0.988), 0.968 (95%CI: 0.951-0.985), and temporal validation cohort 0.974 (95% CI: 0.958-0.990). In the temporal validation cohort, this optimal Clinlabomics model correctly identified 129 (84.3%) MAC patients and 337 (98.3%) non-MAC patients. Finally, through integrated analyses, triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), Castelli risk index II (CRI-II), fasting blood glucose (FBG) and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) were recognized as key metabolic indicators for MAC.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on the rpart algorithm, this study developed the optimal clinlabomics model for MAC-AIS comorbidity with satisfactory discriminative ability. TyG, CRI-II, FBG, and AIP were recognized as key metabolic signatures of MAC-AIS comorbidity, providing a reliable tool for early clinical intervention and personalized management.

Title: Adoption and diffusion of SGLT2 inhibitors among cardiologists in medicare part D, 2019-2023: a provider-level observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are guideline-directed therapies for heart failure, yet real-world diffusion into cardiology practice remains incompletely characterized. This study evaluated adoption, prescribing intensity, subspecialty variation, geographic variation, and concentration of SGLT2 inhibitor use among cardiologists in Medicare Part D from 2019 to 2023.
METHODS: We conducted an observational, provider-level study using Medicare Part D Prescriber-Provider Public Use Files, including all clinicians with a primary specialty designation of cardiology. Primary analyses focused on empagliflozin and dapagliflozin. Outcomes included annual observable adoption (presence of a non-suppressed prescribing record), prescribing intensity among adopters, prescribing concentration (raw and normalized for overall Part D prescribing volume), adoption by cardiology subspecialty, total drug spending, and state-level variation with confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Among approximately 23,000 to 24,000 cardiologists annually, observable adoption increased from 4.5% in 2019 to 56.1% in 2023, with acceleration after 2021. Median prescribing intensity among adopters rose from 23 claims (interquartile range [IQR] 15-43) to 43 claims (IQR 21-90); early adopters prescribed nearly three times the intensity of late adopters after adjustment (incidence rate ratio, 2.96; 95% CI, 2.85-3.08). By 2023, adoption reached 91.6% among cardiologists with a subspecialty designation in advanced heart failure/transplant cardiology, compared with 56.4% among general cardiologists and 49.7% among interventional cardiologists (P < 0.001). Prescribing by raw claim volume remained concentrated, with the top 10% of prescribers accounting for 40.6% of total claims in 2023; this concentration was substantially attenuated, to 21.4%, after normalizing for each cardiologist's overall Part D prescribing volume. Crude adoption varied substantially by state (25.6%-75.0% in 2023), though low-denominator states showed considerable estimate instability after empirical Bayes adjustment. Total Medicare Part D spending increased from $33.2 million in 2019 to $1.1 billion in 2023 in nominal dollars (28-fold in inflation-adjusted terms).
CONCLUSIONS: Observable SGLT2 inhibitor adoption among cardiologists increased rapidly, but a substantial portion of apparent geographic heterogeneity and prescribing concentration reflects practice volume and subspecialty composition rather than adoption behavior alone. Adoption approached ceiling levels among advanced heart failure/transplant cardiologists, while general and interventional cardiologists lagged behind, identifying a specific target for future implementation efforts.

Title: Moderate aortic stenosis identified during intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis and 90-day mortality: a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV echocardiography database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis is associated with reduced survival in ambulatory cardiology populations, but its prognostic significance when identified during an intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis is unknown. We examined its association with 90-day mortality in this setting.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) version 3.1 and its echocardiogram-matched subset (MIMIC-IV-ECHO). We included each adult's first intensive care admission for a non-cardiac primary diagnosis with an interpretable baseline transthoracic echocardiogram recording peak aortic jet velocity. Stenosis was graded from the peak velocity (no stenosis < 2.0, sclerosis or mild 2.0-2.9, moderate 3.0-3.9, severe ≥ 4.0 m/s). The echocardiogram defined time zero; the primary outcome was all-cause mortality within a fixed 90-day window. Associations were estimated with multivariable Cox models adjusted for acute-illness severity and comorbidity, with propensity-score matching, velocity-gradient concordance grading, pre-specified ejection-fraction subgroups, and an E-value.
RESULTS: Of 12,878 patients (10,511 no stenosis, 1,797 sclerosis, 411 moderate, 159 severe), 3,605 died within 90 days. Crude 90-day mortality rose across grades (26.1%, 34.4%, 40.4%, 46.5%). After adjustment, the hazard increased monotonically: sclerosis 1.17 (95% CI 1.07-1.28), moderate 1.33 (1.13-1.56), severe 1.61 (1.27-2.03). The moderate-stenosis association was modest but consistent, attenuating slightly in the most conservative specifications (propensity-score matched 1.20 [1.02-1.40]; parsimonious 1.22 [1.05-1.43]); the E-value was 1.73 (lower limit 1.41). It was numerically concentrated in the first two weeks (1.58 [1.30-1.93], days 0-14) and numerically larger with reduced (1.47 [1.10-1.97]) than preserved ejection fraction (1.10 [0.87-1.39]); neither the proportional-hazards nor the grade-by-ejection-fraction interaction test was significant (interaction P = 0.21), and both are exploratory numerical patterns, not demonstrated effect modification.
CONCLUSIONS: In non-cardiac critical illness, velocity-defined moderate aortic stenosis identified during the intensive care admission was independently associated with higher 90-day mortality, with exploratory numerical patterns of greater early risk and of greater risk with reduced ejection fraction. These data identify a higher-risk phenotype; they do not establish a causal adverse effect of moderate valvular obstruction itself. It is best regarded as a prognostic marker warranting closer surveillance rather than, on current evidence, a target for valve intervention.

Title: Association between systemic immune-inflammation index and mortality in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic inflammation is common in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) and is closely related to adverse clinical outcomes. The clinical significance of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), a composite marker derived from routine blood cell counts, has not been fully characterized in dialysis populations.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 408 MHD patients with a median follow-up of 33 months. SII was calculated from baseline platelet, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts. Associations between SII and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess dose-response relationships. Kaplan-Meier analyses and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore the consistency of associations.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 91 patients died, including 39 cardiovascular deaths. Higher SII levels were associated with increased risks of both all-cause mortality (HR 1.89, 95% CI 1.29-2.77) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.21-3.57). Patients in the highest SII tertile had approximately two-fold higher risk of all-cause mortality compared with those in the lowest tertile. Kaplan-Meier analyses demonstrated significantly lower survival probabilities among patients with higher SII levels. Subgroup analyses showed generally consistent associations across most clinically relevant strata.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher SII levels were associated with increased risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. These findings suggest that SII, derived from routine blood cell counts, may reflect inflammatory processes linked to adverse outcomes in dialysis populations.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Clinical and organizational stroke care quality performance by sex and age among stroke patients in differently-designated Quebec hospital centers: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The quality of interdisciplinary care in the acute phase of ischemic stroke remains unexplored in Quebec and the rest of Canada. Clinical and organizational indicators across differently-designated hospital centers must be evaluated while considering individual patient characteristics in order to better understand and improve these care practices.
OBJECTIVE: To describe the performance of care and services based on measurement of clinical and organizational quality indicators in the acute ischemic stroke phase according to sex and age in differently-designated Quebec hospital centers.
METHOD: A retrospective descriptive study was conducted on patients' health records in three centers (levels 3, 4, and 5) using 29 clinical and organizational quality indicators. Differences based on age and sex were analyzed using Chi-square tests including bootstrapping techniques (x 5 000) with a 95% CI and MoE at 5%.
RESULTS: We studied 132 patients' health records (mean age, 73.5 years; 53% women). Examples of indicators whose results revealed disparities calling for improved practices include the assessment of stroke severity using the NIHSS, which was carried out for 32.6% of patients, fall risk screening for 51.2%, secondary prevention referral at discharge for 45.1%, and pre-discharge stroke education documented in patients' health records for less than 50.0% of patients. On the other hand, assessment of dysphagia (78.6%), investigation of cardiac arrhythmias (95.5%) and admission in a stroke unit (88.3%) are examples of indicators that performed favorably in relation to clinical and organizational practices. Antiplatelet prescription (p = 0.007) and secondary prevention referral (p = 0.003) at discharge decreased with age, while the use of social work resources was higher in the over-80s subgroup (p = 0.003). Arrhythmia screening was performed more frequently in men (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSION: This first Quebec multicentric study in Canada, presented by age and sex, will enable optimized health outcomes for vulnerable populations by reducing health disparities and lead to improved management of resources as needed while improving patient care.

Title: Beyond HAS-BLED in very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation treated with direct oral anticoagulants: predictors of major bleeding in a real-world cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bleeding risk assessment in very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) remains challenging. The HAS-BLED score is widely used but may have limited applicability in this population. We aimed to evaluate its performance and to identify clinical predictors of major bleeding beyond conventional risk scores.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective real-world cohort study including consecutive patients aged ≥ 90 years with AF treated with DOACs. The primary outcome was major bleeding. Discrimination was assessed using receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify predictors and assess incremental value.
RESULTS: A total of 487 patients (mean age 93.0 ± 2.6 years, 63.4% female) were included, with major bleeding occurring in 57 patients (11.7%). The HAS-BLED score was not associated with major bleeding (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.55-1.23; p = 0.34) and showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.46). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.14 per year, 95% CI 1.03-1.27; p = 0.014) and anticoagulant type were independently associated with bleeding. Compared with apixaban, rivaroxaban (OR 3.77, p = 0.002) and dabigatran (OR 3.34, p = 0.008) were associated with higher bleeding risk. A clinical model incorporating these factors modestly improved discrimination compared with HAS-BLED (AUC 0.69 vs. 0.46).
CONCLUSIONS: In very elderly patients with AF receiving DOAC therapy, HAS-BLED has limited predictive value. Bleeding risk appears to be influenced by treatment-related factors, particularly anticoagulant type. Incorporating these factors may improve risk stratification and support a more individualized approach to anticoagulation management in nonagenarians.

Title: Single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis identifies a putative Purkinje fiber-associated remodeling program after myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Purkinje fiber (PF) remodeling may contribute to post-infarction ventricular arrhythmia, but rare conduction-associated cardiomyocyte states in injured human myocardium remain incompletely characterized. We use TsPF to denote transitional PFs, a study-specific transitional Purkinje fiber subpopulation resolved by cardiomyocyte re-clustering and characterized by an intermediate transcriptional phenotype. In this study, transitional refers to the observed expression phenotype; temporal progression, lineage conversion, and anatomical Purkinje localization require separate evidence.
METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the human myocardial infarction atlas reported by Kuppe et al. The analyzed discovery matrix was derived from 29 single-nucleus RNA-sequencing libraries representing 28 tissue specimens from 20 individuals (4 donor controls and 16 individuals with myocardial infarction). After quality control and Seurat/Harmony integration, ventricular cardiomyocytes were re-clustered. PF/TsPF annotation, MiloR, high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), scMetabolism, PF-anchored pseudotime, and CellChat were evaluated with an explicit separation between abundance testing, descriptive molecular patterns, and model-derived hypotheses.
RESULTS: The quality-controlled matrix contained 172,522 nuclei and 28,122 genes. All MiloR neighborhoods had a spatial false discovery rate (SpatialFDR) of at least 0.05.
