A secondary tissue-sample-level TsPF: mature-PF ratio was lower in myocardial infarction than control in the displayed comparison (unadjusted Wilcoxon P = 0.0345); several tissues came from the same donors, and mature-PF denotes the PF-labeled denominator. Using β = 5, hdWGCNA resolved nine colored modules; the selected blue module contained 1,050 genes, including NT5C, ITPA, GUK1, and ADSS1. TsPF-labeled nuclei showed higher nucleotide-metabolism scores (average log2 fold change = 0.9982; Bonferroni-type adjusted P = 4.63 × 10 - 27; cell-level comparison). CellChat network summaries showed 1,191 versus 805 inferred interactions and aggregate strength 0.095 versus 0.027 in control versus myocardial infarction; these values are descriptive model outputs rather than donor-level differential tests.
CONCLUSIONS: This secondary analysis prioritizes a putative PF-associated transcriptional remodeling program for follow-up. The abundance result remained negative after SpatialFDR correction, while the co-expression, metabolic, ordering, and communication analyses provide candidates for hypothesis-driven work. Establishing a distinct TsPF state and its functional relevance will require independent donor-aware, spatial/histological, molecular, and electrophysiological validation.

Title: Impact of Guideline-Directed Medication Titration Velocity in Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Abstract: This study evaluated whether shorter time to achieving targeted guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) was associated with greater improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). GDMT reduces morbidity and mortality in HFrEF. It is unclear whether the speed of achieving target doses influences improvement in LVEF or related outcomes. This retrospective study included new HFrEF patients seen in a heart failure clinic between January 1st, 2021 and January 1st, 2023 that met study criteria. The primary outcome was improvement in LVEF. Secondary outcomes included reduction in mitral valve regurgitation (MVR) severity and differences in LVEF improvement by provider type. Titration velocity was defined as time from first heart failure visit to attainment of target or maximally tolerated GDMT doses. Eighty-seven patients were included in the study (mean age 61 years; 64.4% male; 58.6% white). After GDMT titration, 90.8% demonstrated improvement in LVEF. Mean time to full GDMT titration was 146.6 days (<6 months). Mean LVEF improvement was 19.5% (<3 months), 19.1% (3-6 months), 21.0% (6-9 months), and 17.3% (>9 months), with no significant difference among groups (P = 0.823). No significant differences were observed in MVR reduction (P = 0.523) or LVEF improvement by provider type (P = 0.703). GDMT titration velocity was not associated with significant differences in LVEF improvement. These findings support individualized GDMT optimization rather than emphasizing rapid dose escalation and suggest potential benefits of longer therapy duration allowing additional time for specialty evaluation and avoiding premature device implantation.

Title: Real-World Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor After Acute Coronary Syndrome and Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To compare the real-world effectiveness and safety of prasugrel versus ticagrelor among patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the United States.
DESIGN: Retrospective new-user cohort study.
DATA SOURCE: MarketScan Research Databases, 2017-2023.
PATIENTS: Patients aged 18 years or older with ACS and PCI initiated on either prasugrel or ticagrelor were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) diagnosis codes and prescription records. The prescription fill date was assigned as the index date. Patients were required to have continuous enrollment in their health care plan for 1 year prior to and including the index date.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Stabilized inverse probability treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline characteristics between treatment groups. Cox proportional hazards models with adherence adjustment were used to estimate 1 year risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of myocardial infarction [MI], ischemic stroke, or stent thrombosis), bleeding events, and individual MACE components. The study included 6662 prasugrel-treated and 25,452 ticagrelor-treated patients. Prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of MACE (3.83 vs. 5.61 events per 100 person-years; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65-0.92) and MI (3.43 vs. 4.73 events per 100 person-years; aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.97) compared with ticagrelor, respectively. Bleeding risk did not differ between prasugrel versus ticagrelor (2.85 vs. 3.89 events per 100 person-years, respectively; aHR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74-1.13). Sensitivity analyses restricted to patients with high medication adherence and without contraindications to prasugrel showed similar results.
CONCLUSION: Among commercially insured US patients with ACS undergoing PCI, prasugrel was associated with a lower risk of ischemic cardiovascular events compared with ticagrelor, without an increase in bleeding risk, including in patients with high medication adherence. These findings provide contemporary real-world evidence supporting the preferential use of prasugrel over ticagrelor following ACS and PCI in appropriately selected patients.

Title: SAK-YOLO: An Improved YOLOv11-Based Method for Coronary Artery Stenosis Segmentation and Grading Judgment.
Journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
Abstract: Exposure to low-temperature environments predisposes to coronary spasm and plaque rupture, raising acute myocardial infarction risk. Coronary angiography is the principal diagnostic modality, but image noise, low contrast and poor vessel visualisation frequently cause missed detection. Conventional segmentation approaches depend heavily on expert input, while existing deep learning models remain limited in extracting multi-scale stenotic features and in grading stenosis severity. This study proposes SAK-YOLO, built on YOLOv11-seg with Switchable Atrous Convolution (SAConv) and KernelWarehouse dynamic convolution. A four-tier stenosis grading dataset was established from 376 angiographic images of 122 patients, augmented by flipping, rotation and contrast adjustment. SAConv replaces the backbone's strided convolutions to adapt the receptive field to varying vessel calibres, while KWConv and KW3K2 replace the neck convolutions, assembling kernels from a small warehouse of candidates. SAK-YOLO attains a box precision of 0.946, a box recall of 0.853, box mAP50 and mAP50-95 of 92.7% and 75.3%, and mask mAP50 and mask mAP50-95 of 91.3% and 56.5%, achieving the best result among all evaluated models on every mAP-based metric. These results indicate that SAK-YOLO has potential for coronary stenosis image analysis; however, they are based on a relatively small single-centre dataset, and multi-centre validation and prospective clinical evaluation are still required to establish its generalizability and clinical value.

Title: Availability-Aware Prediction of CCTA Findings Using Opportunistic Low-Dose CT and Routine Health-Check Data.
Journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
Abstract: Laboratory and history data are inconsistently available in health-check records, complicating prediction from combined clinical and imaging inputs. We evaluated an availability-aware ensemble for predicting coronary CT angiography (CCTA) findings in 864 participants, including 221 with Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) category ≥ 3. Models used eight clinical and 31 low-dose CT (LDCT) inputs, with optional laboratory and history variables. Six learner families underwent fivefold outer and fivefold inner validation; preprocessing, model selection, and cross-fitted sigmoid calibration were confined to outer training data. Calibrated adaptive top-3 aggregation achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.808, average precision of 0.622, and Brier score of 0.14152. Compared with selection of one compatible model, the AUROC difference was + 0.0193 (conditional 95% confidence interval 0.0029-0.0358) and the Brier difference was - 0.01174 (- 0.01723 to - 0.00621). Comparisons with the expanded-pool imputation baseline and common-feature ensembles were inconclusive. Matched analyses supported adding laboratory variables to single-model selection; history increments were uncertain. At threshold 0.15, 29/221 positive cases were missed (13.1%; 95% Wilson interval 9.3-18.2%). Human reviewers considered the proxy measurements acceptable in all 864 analyzed participants. Aggregation improved AUROC and Brier score relative to compatible single-model selection in this cohort. Its additional value over simpler ensembles and its suitability for clinical triage require external and prospective evaluation.

Title: Baricitinib Ameliorates Cutaneous Leukocytoclastic Angiitis in Rats.
Abstract: Cutaneous leukocytoclastic angiitis (CLA) is a skin-limited, small-vessel vasculitis characterized by neutrophil infiltration with leukocytoclastosis. Inflammatory cytokines released from activated neutrophils play crucial roles in the pathogenesis. Glucocorticoids and immunosuppressive drugs are used for treatment. However, susceptibility to infections occurs due to the long-term administration of these drugs. Therefore, the development of new drugs is desired. A recent study suggested that Janus kinase (JAK)1 and JAK2 are involved in CLA pathogenesis. This pilot study aimed to demonstrate the efficacy of baricitinib that can inhibit both JAK1 and JAK2 on CLA using an animal model. CLA was induced in Wistar Kyoto rats (n = 7) on Day 0, and these rats were divided randomly into two groups: baricitinib group (n = 4) and vehicle group (n = 3). The baricitinib group received baricitinib (10 mg/kg) once daily orally from Days 0 to 6. Skin tissues (four sites/rat) were harvested on Day 7, and histopathological examinations were conducted. The phosphorylation of JAK1 and JAK2 in the inflammatory cells and the amount of IL-6 secreted in the skin lesion was suppressed by baricitinib. Correspondingly, baricitinib decreased histological scores of CLA represented by a sum of the inflammatory cell infiltration score (0-3) and the leukocytoclastosis score (0, 1) (Vehicle: 2.1 ± 0.4; Baricitinib: 1.5 ± 0.3; p < 0.05). Interestingly, baricitinib suppressed leukocytoclastosis particularly, suggesting that JAK1 or JAK2 might be implicated in the mechanism underlying leukocytoclastosis. This study could serve as a motivation to advance baricitinib to the next stage to examine its efficacy on CLA using a larger number of rats.

Title: Norwood procedure for hypoplastic left heart syndrome: a 14-year national experience, temporal trends, and implications for management in a middle-income country.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is a severe congenital cardiac defect associated with substantial neonatal morbidity and mortality. The Norwood procedure, the initial palliative operation for HLHS, is a technically demanding surgery that requires highly specialized centers and an experienced multidisciplinary team. In middle-income countries, outcome data following the Norwood procedure remains limited. To identify factors associated with in-hospital mortality and major postoperative complications and to report temporal trends in outcomes among neonates with HLHS undergoing the Norwood procedure between 2009 and 2023 at a single center in a Latin American country. A retrospective cohort study was conducted including all neonates with confirmed HLHS who underwent the Norwood procedure. Patients were excluded only for significant comorbidities precluding surgical candidacy (prematurity < 36 weeks, chromosomal abnormalities, heterotaxy syndrome, intact atrial septum, or anomalous pulmonary venous connection). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included occurrence of at least one major postoperative complication (per STS criteria), postoperative length of stay, and complication-specific mortality. Crude ORs with 95%CIs were estimated using univariable logistic regression. Multivariable analysis was performed using Firth penalized logistic regression. A total of 81 patients were included. In-hospital mortality was 35.8%, with a 19% reduction observed between the periods 2009-2014 and 2015-2023. Preoperative mechanical ventilation (aOR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.07-0.97) and higher weight at the time of surgery were protective factors. In contrast, intraoperative ECMO use (aOR, 5.49; 95% CI, 1.36-22.1) and the occurrence of major postoperative complications (aOR, 4.46; 95% CI, 1.11-17.8) were associated with increased mortality. The most frequent complication was the need for unplanned reintervention (37%).
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of neonates undergoing the Norwood procedure in a middle-income setting, in-hospital mortality decreased over time but remained higher than that reported in high-income countries. Higher surgical weight was protective, whereas ECMO use and major postoperative complications were associated with worse outcomes.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The Norwood procedure remains a high-risk surgical intervention for neonates with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, associated with substantial postoperative morbidity and mortality. • The management of hypoplastic left heart syndrome remains particularly challenging in low-income populations and resource-limited healthcare systems, where access to surgical palliation is often restricted.
WHAT IS NEW: • In this 14-year single-center cohort from Colombia, in-hospital mortality decreased from 44.4% to 25.0%, accompanied by a statistically signifi cant reduction in major postoperative complications. • Higher weight at surgery and preoperative mechanical ventilation were associated with lower in-hospital mortality, whereas intraoperative ECMO use and major postoperative complications were associated with increased mortality.

Title: Efficacy and safety of apixaban versus rivaroxaban in acute venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apixaban and rivaroxaban are used direct oral anticoagulants for acute venous thromboembolism (VTE), but their comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain. We compared outcomes with apixaban versus rivaroxaban in adults with acute VTE.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to April 2026 for comparative studies in adults with acute VTE. Random-effects meta-analyses generated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); heterogeneity was assessed using I2, and certainty using GRADE.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies involving 233,569 participants were included. Most evidence came from observational studies, with only one randomized clinical trial contributing to the evidence base. Apixaban showed a non-significant reduction in recurrent VTE (10 studies; 203,462 participants; RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.64-1.05). Recurrent DVT was lower with apixaban (2 studies; 37,941 participants; RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.79-0.98), whereas recurrent PE (3 studies; 45,561 participants; RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.09-6.53) and all-cause mortality (6 studies; 149,742 participants; RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.79-1.23) did not differ significantly. Apixaban was associated with lower major bleeding (13 studies; 221,840 participants; RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57-0.99), CRNMB (5 studies; 29,530 participants; RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.53-0.75), and gastrointestinal bleeding (4 studies; 56,160 participants; RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.62-0.75). Intracranial bleeding was not significantly different (3 studies; 55,470 participants; RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.24-2.13). Certainty ranged from low to very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban and rivaroxaban showed broadly comparable efficacy, while apixaban may offer a more favorable bleeding profile. Findings should be interpreted cautiously because of heterogeneity, observational evidence, and low-to-very-low certainty.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study

Title: Non-invasive assessment of postoperative revascularization using slab MIP images in 3D TOF MRA in pediatric moyamoya disease.
Journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Repeated assessment of postoperative revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease is clinically important, but digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is invasive. We aimed to develop a novel, non-invasive scoring method (moya-ASPECTS) that applies the six cortical MCA regions of ASPECTS to slab maximum intensity projection (MIP) images from three-dimensional time-of-flight (3D TOF) magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), and to examine its correlation with DSA findings and cerebral blood flow (CBF) changes after surgery.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 45 treated hemispheres in 28 pediatric patients who underwent revascularization between 2010 and 2023. Eight hemispheres underwent indirect revascularization alone and 37 underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization. We evaluated postoperative cortical revascularization using the moya-ASPECTS score based on slab MIP images derived from 3D TOF MRA, and examined its associations with Matsushima grade, resting cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), and regression of basal moyamoya vessels.
RESULTS: The moya-ASPECTS score showed a strong correlation with Matsushima grade (p < 0.001). Postoperative resting CBF increased by 2.27 ml/100 g/min for each point increase in moya-ASPECTS (95% CI 0.87-3.67, p = 0.003). While moya-ASPECTS was not associated with CVR change, it correlated significantly with regression of moyamoya vessels (RR 1.33, 95% CI 1.12-1.58, p < 0.001). Higher moya-ASPECTS scores were inversely associated with postoperative asymptomatic infarction, although the number of events was small.
CONCLUSION: The moya-ASPECTS score derived from slab MIP images provides a non-invasive, repeatable, and semi-quantitative method for evaluating postoperative cortical revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease. This method correlates well with DSA-based Matsushima grade and postoperative CBF improvement, supporting its potential use as a practical non-invasive adjunct for serial outpatient follow-up.

Title: CTA-defined calcified nodules as a predictor of adverse outcomes following carotid revascularization.
Abstract: Carotid calcification can complicate carotid artery stenting (CAS), but the clinical impact may depend on calcification morphology rather than calcification burden alone. We retrospectively evaluated 92 patients who underwent carotid revascularization with either carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or CAS and classified preoperative CTA findings as no/spotty calcification (Group 1), outer calcification (Group 2), or a calcified nodule (CN) pattern directly abutting the contrast-enhanced lumen (Group 3). The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis. The endpoint occurred in 4 of 83 patients (4.8%) in Groups 1/2 and in 5 of 9 patients (55.6%) in Group 3 (unadjusted OR, 24.69; 95% CI, 4.72-129.14; p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model including treatment modality and calcification pattern, Group 3 remained associated with the composite endpoint (adjusted OR, 49.05; 95% CI, 4.82-498.94; p = 0.001), whereas CEA was associated with lower risk (adjusted OR, 0.045; 95% CI, 0.003-0.664; p = 0.024). Among patients undergoing CAS, the endpoint occurred in 3 of 38 patients (7.9%) in Groups 1/2 and all 5 patients (100%) in Group 3 (p < 0.001). A CTA-defined CN pattern may identify lesions at particularly high risk for CAS-related technical failure or restenosis and may support consideration of CEA when surgically feasible.

Title: Association of coronary artery calcium with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation according to atrial fibrillation type.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) reflects systemic atherosclerosis and inflammation and may contribute to atrial remodeling. Although CAC has been associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), whether this association differs according to AF type remains unclear.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 202 consecutive patients who underwent first-time catheter ablation for AF and had coronary computed tomography between October 2019 and August 2024. CAC was quantified using the Agatston score. The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Patients were stratified by AF type, and associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Branch-specific CAC was also evaluated in exploratory analyses. During a median follow-up of 617 days (IQR, 457-808), atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 19 of 96 patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF; 19.8%) and 39 of 106 patients with non-PAF (36.8%). In the overall cohort, CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (adjusted HR, 2.03; 95% CI, 1.07-3.86; P=0.031). In age- and sex-adjusted analyses stratified by AF type, CAC ≥100 was associated with a higher risk of recurrence in patients with PAF (adjusted HR, 5.59; 95% CI, 2.05-15.27; P<0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in patients with non-PAF (adjusted HR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.56-2.52; P=0.647). The interaction between CAC ≥100 and AF type was statistically significant in the age- and sex-adjusted model (P for interaction=0.011) and remained significant in the expanded clinically adjusted model including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and left atrial volume index (P for interaction=0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: CAC ≥100 was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after AF ablation, and this association may differ according to AF type, with a stronger association observed in patients with PAF. Subgroup and interaction analyses were exploratory and limited by the small number of recurrence events. CAC may provide useful information for post-ablation recurrence risk stratification, although these findings require validation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Pulmonary artery to ascending aorta ratio on pre-procedural computed tomography and pulmonary hypertension after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Abstract: To investigate whether pre-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical metrics are associated with post-TAVR pulmonary hypertension (PH) with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). In this post-hoc analysis of a prospective single-center registry (Invasive PPM Registry; UMIN-CTR: 000054628), 97 patients undergoing TAVR with complete CT, echocardiography, and invasive hemodynamics were evaluated. Prespecified CT metrics included main, left and right pulmonary artery diameters, right ventricle/left ventricle ratio (RV/LV), right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness, septal deviation, and the pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio (P​A:​AA). The primary endpoint was post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR (mean pulmonary artery pressure > 20 mmHg and PVR > 2 Wood units). Incremental value beyond right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) was assessed. PH with elevated PVR occurred in 21 (21.6%) patients. Diastolic PA:​AA showed the best discrimination, although this was modest (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.526-0.798), other metrics performed less well (AUCs 0.46-0.60). At the Youden-optimal threshold of ≥ 0.90, sensitivity was 61.9%, specificity 72.4%, positive predictive value 38.2% and negative predictive value 87.3%. RVSP discriminated poorly (AUC 0.558); adding PA:​AA(d) improved discrimination (AUC 0.710; ΔAUC 0.152), model fit (p = 0.015), risk separation (IDI 0.066; p = 0.020) and reclassification (category-free NRI 0.690; p = 0.024). PA:​AA(d) correlated modestly with post-procedural mPAP (Spearman ρ = 0.247; p = 0.015). In this exploratory analysis, a larger pre-TAVR diastolic PA:AA ratio was associated with post-TAVR PH with elevated PVR and improved discrimination when combined with echocardiographic RV​SP.Trial registration: This study was registered with the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry and accepted by the International Committee of Medical Journal ​Editors (UMIN ID: 000054628).

Title: Clinical outcomes associated with angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors versus mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist initiation in patients with hypertension without heart failure: a propensity score-matched study.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: Angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) lower blood pressure, but evidence directly comparing their clinical outcomes in patients with hypertension without heart failure is limited. We compared long-term outcomes associated with ARNI versus MRA initiation in this population. Adults with essential hypertension without heart failure were included if they had documented use of an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor blocker plus at least one additional antihypertensive drug class. Patients receiving sacubitril or spironolactone or eplerenone after a 1-year washout period were assigned to the ARNI and MRA cohorts, respectively. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were a composite of acute myocardial infarction and stroke, acute kidney injury (AKI), acute myocardial infarction, and stroke. Outcomes were assessed for up to 1095 days. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 11,832 patients were included in each group. During follow-up, the rates of all-cause mortality in the ARNI and the MRA groups were 7.6% (894 patients) and 10.2% (1 201 patients), respectively. The ARNI group compared to MRA group was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality, stroke, and AKI, whereas no significant differences were observed in the composite cardiovascular outcome or acute myocardial infarction. Mean systolic blood pressure was modestly lower in the ARNI group, while diastolic blood pressure and the most recently recorded estimated glomerular filtration rate were similar between groups. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

Title: Baroreflex Activation Therapy in Patients With Resistant Hypertension: A Single-Center Real-World Analysis of Blood Pressure Response and Procedural Safety.
Abstract: Baroreflex activation therapy (BAT) has emerged as a treatment option for patients with resistant hypertension; however, real-world data on blood pressure response and procedural safety of the second-generation Barostim Neo system remain limited. In this single-center retrospective study, 37 patients with resistant hypertension who underwent BAT implantation between 2013 and 2024 were analyzed. Changes in systolic office blood pressure (OBP) and 24 h ambulatory blood pressure (ABP) were assessed. Patients were classified as responders if any reduction in systolic blood pressure from baseline was observed. Periprocedural safety and procedural characteristics were also evaluated. In the overall cohort, no statistically significant reduction in systolic blood pressure was observed (ABP: 159 ± 27 to 157 ± 24 mmHg; OBP: 172 ± 19 to 165 ± 29 mmHg; both p > 0.05). However, a substantial proportion of patients showed a clinically meaningful response. Among responders, systolic ABP decreased significantly from 170 ± 24 to 141 ± 15 mmHg and systolic OBP from 178 ± 16 to 146 ± 17 mmHg (both p < 0.0001). A combined improvement in ABP and OBP was observed in 48% of patients with complete data. The mean implantation time was 74 min, and periprocedural complications occurred in 13.5% of cases. Generator replacement procedures were shorter and associated with a low rate of transient complications. In this real-world cohort, BAT using the Barostim Neo system appears to be a safe therapeutic option, although not all patients benefit. Among responders, BAT is associated with substantial and clinically relevant blood pressure reduction. Further prospective studies are needed to improve patient selection and evaluate long-term outcomes.

Title: Impact of patient sex and dual antiplatelet therapy duration on 10-year mortality following percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents: A post-hoc analysis of the ISAR-SAFE trial.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women are underrepresented in cardiovascular clinical trials and evidence regarding sex-specific long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between patient sex and duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with the 10-year prognosis of patients enrolled in the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled ISAR-SAFE trial.
METHODS: This post-hoc analysis included 1,871 patients from centers that participated in the ISAR-SAFE trial and agreed to collect 10-year follow-up data. In the ISAR-SAFE trial, a 6-month DAPT duration was compared with a 12-month DAPT regimen in patients treated with drug-eluting stents (DES). The primary endpoint of the present study was all-cause death at 10 years.
RESULTS: Compared to men, women were older (69.0 ± 9.7 vs. 64.8 ± 10.4 years, P < 0.001), had lower body weight (72.1 ± 14.2 vs. 84.8 ± 13.5 Kg, P < 0.001) and a higher prevalence of arterial hypertension (93.2% vs. 89.3%, P = 0.031) and dyslipidemia (85.1% vs. 77.9%, P = 0.003). The 10-year mortality was 11.9% in women and 9.3% in men (hazard ratio [HR] 1.28 [95% confidence interval 0.91-1.81], P = 0.156). The 10-year mortality was 10.1% in the 6-month DAPT arm and 9.6% in the 12-month DAPT arm (HR 1.06 [0.79-1.42], P = 0.685). There was no significant interaction between sex and DAPT duration with respect to mortality. Age was the only independent predictor of mortality (adjusted HR per 1 year increase 1.08 [1.06-1.09]; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing PCI with DES implantation, neither patient sex nor duration of DAPT regimen were independently associated with 10-year all-cause mortality after adjustment for relevant clinical covariates.

Title: Robotic-assisted versus manual percutaneous coronary intervention after contemporary randomized evidence: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of patient-level procedural and radiation outcomes.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted PCI (R-PCI) reduces measured radiation exposure to the primary operator, but procedural and patient-radiation benefits over manual PCI (M-PCI) remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To compare procedural/PCI time, fluoroscopy time, contrast volume, air kerma, and dose-area product between R-PCI and M-PCI after incorporation of randomized evidence.
METHODS: Randomized and nonrandomized comparative studies of adults undergoing PCI were included. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Mean differences (MDs) were calculated as M-PCI minus R-PCI. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I; certainty was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Twelve studies, including 2 randomized trials, contributed data. No primary pooled outcome differed significantly: procedural/PCI time, MD -3.90 min (95% CI: -16.15 to 8.35); fluoroscopy time, 0.17 min (95% CI: -2.61 to 2.95); contrast volume, 7.79 mL (95% CI: -3.08 to 18.66); air kerma, 232.01 mGy (95% CI: -145.67 to 609.70); and dose-area product, 31.31 dGy·cm2 (95% CI: -49.45 to 112.07). Heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 72%-93%). A direct-report-only analysis favored R-PCI for contrast volume (MD: 17.76 mL; 95% CI: 4.62-30.90), but other sensitivity analyses did not materially change interpretation. Certainty was very low for all outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: R-PCI has not shown consistent patient procedural or radiation benefit. Operator protection is supported descriptively but was not pooled; contrast reduction appeared only in sensitivity analysis. Future trials should assess patient benefit and team-wide occupational exposure.

Title: The ECMO-PoCS Score: Derivation and Internal Validation of an Implantation-Time Model for In-Hospital Mortality in Postcardiotomy Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To derive and internally validate a mortality score (ECMO-PoCS) for use at venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) implantation for postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS), hypothesizing that a few implantation-time variables would discriminate in-hospital mortality better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II), Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II), or pre-ECMO lactate.
DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study.
SETTING: Tertiary cardiac surgical center.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 149 consecutive adults receiving VA-ECMO for PCS (2007-2024), excluding 7 bridged directly to transplantation.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Hospital mortality was 65.8% and 1-year survival 33.4%. A 4-variable logistic model (age, pre-ECMO lactate, peripheral artery disease [PAD], and any preoperative right ventricular [RV] dysfunction) was fitted in 133 complete cases; PAD (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 4.58; p = 0.022) and RV dysfunction (adjusted OR = 3.16; p = 0.020) were independently associated with mortality. In 130 patients with all comparators, ECMO-PoCS (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.715) discriminated better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) (0.583; DeLong p = 0.043) and lactate alone (0.601; p = 0.030) but not significantly better than APACHE II (0.610; p = 0.13); adding these variables to APACHE II increased its AUC to 0.727 (likelihood ratio p = 0.002). Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.687 and the shrinkage factor 0.82. A 0- to 5-point score defined low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (mortality 23.1%, 63.6%, and 86.0%, respectively; trend p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: ECMO-PoCS, based on 4 variables available at implantation, discriminated in-hospital mortality better than EuroSCORE II and lactate alone and added information to APACHE II. Internally validated only, it is intended for risk description, research stratification, and benchmarking, not for decisions to initiate or withdraw support, pending external validation.

Title: Integrating polygenic and classical risk factors for cardiovascular risk stratification in a polish primary-care cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) promise improved cardiovascular risk stratification, but most validation derives from UK or Nordic biobanks. The transferability of these scores to Central European populations and their incremental value over classical risk factors in routine care remain unestablished.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether a coronary PRS derived from external European data transfers to a Polish primary-care population and adds discrimination for prevalent cardiovascular disease beyond classical risk factors.
METHODS: In the nationwide Polish LIPIDOGEN2015 primary-care cohort, we derived PRS for coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke from FinnGen data with continuous shrinkage priors and applied them to imputed genotypes. We compared allele frequencies of 1397 unrelated participants with a non-Finnish European (NFE) reference and, in 1328 participants with clinical data, related the PRS to coronary artery disease (CAD), MI and stroke recorded at baseline and to a composite including death during follow-up, with and without classical risk factors or SCORE2.
RESULTS: Allele frequencies correlated with the NFE reference (r = 0.97). Per standard deviation (SD), the coronary PRS was associated with prevalent CAD (odds ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.67) and the composite endpoint (1.26, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.51), as were two validated genome-wide scores. Adding it to classical risk factors changed the area under the curve (AUC) for the composite endpoint by 0.0017 (95% CI -0.0005 to 0.0076), from 0.860 to 0.861; results with SCORE2 were similar. The study had 80% power for odds ratios per SD of 1.31 (CAD) and 1.27 (composite).
CONCLUSIONS: A coronary PRS derived from external European data retains its association with prevalent CAD without re-derivation in this Polish primary-care cohort but, in this cross-sectional, event-limited sample, adds little discrimination to classical risk factors. Its value for predicting future events in this setting remains to be tested against incident outcomes.

Title: Left atrial appendage closure, direct oral anticoagulants or warfarin in atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials.
Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.
RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

Title: Transcatheter vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement for Isolated Native Aortic Regurgitation: National Propensity-Matched Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is well established for aortic stenosis, while its application for isolated native aortic regurgitation (AR) was previously off label and technically challenging. Comparative data between TAVR and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient characteristics and outcomes of off-label TAVR vs SAVR among patients with isolated native AR.
METHODS: Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Provider Analysis and Review database, patients ≥65 years of age who underwent TAVR or SAVR for isolated native AR (2017-2023) were identified. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed to evaluate short- and long-term outcomes. Fine-Gray models accounted for death as a competing risk, reported as subdistribution HRs (SHRs).
RESULTS: Among 9,859 patients, 1,742 propensity score-matched pairs were included, with balanced baseline characteristics (mean age 75.8 years vs 75.7 years; female sex 517 of 1,742 [29.7%] vs 528 of 1,742 [30.3%]). In the matched cohort, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization (OR: 0.33; 95% CI: 0.28-0.39; P < 0.001) and lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-1.00; P = 0.048) but higher 30-day pacemaker implantation (OR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.33-2.25; P < 0.001). Through 5 years (median follow-up 2.58 years), TAVR was associated with increased repeat aortic valve replacement (SHR: 2.04; 95% CI: 1.13-3.66) but similar all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.98-1.31) and heart failure-related readmission (SHR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.98-1.21) between treatment strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis, TAVR was associated with shorter hospitalization and comparable 5-year survival as SAVR, although pacemaker and long-term reinterventions rates were higher.

Title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.
METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

Title: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.
METHODS: The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.
RESULTS: Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications.

Title: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline).
RESULTS: Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121).
CONCLUSIONS: Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

Title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension.
METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

Are pregnancy- and lactation-related eligibility criteria in cardiovascular clinical trials underpinned by drug safety data?
Abstract:
AIM: To quantify the prevalence of pregnancy-, lactation- and reproductive potential-related eligibility criteria in cardiovascular clinical trials and to evaluate whether they are supported by drug-specific safety data.
METHODS: We analysed randomized phase 3 and phase 4 cardiovascular clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023. We used a rule-based natural language processing approach to identify eligibility criteria related to pregnancy, lactation and reproductive potential. In trials evaluating antihypertensive and lipid-modifying drugs, criteria were assessed against human safety data.
RESULTS: Among 1346 trials (1 834 685 participants, 37% women), 64% contained pregnancy-, lactation- or reproductive potential-related eligibility criteria. Pregnancy-related criteria occurred in 59% of trials, lactation-related criteria in 41% and reproductive potential-related criteria in 35%. These criteria frequently overlapped. In the 166 trials evaluating antihypertensive and lipid-modifying drugs, 133 (80%) excluded pregnant women, with 62% of these exclusions being supported by safety data. The remaining 51 (38%) were unsupported because human safety data were insufficient. For lactation, 9 of 97 exclusions (9%) were supported by safety data, 23 (24%) were unsupported because the drug was considered safe and 65 (67%) were unsupported due to insufficient safety data.
CONCLUSION: Pregnancy-, lactation- and reproductive potential-related eligibility criteria are common in cardiovascular trials. Many exclusions of pregnant or lactating women were not supported by drug-specific safety data, particularly for lactation. Continued exclusion in the absence of sufficient safety data limits opportunities to generate evidence within the controlled setting of clinical trials, shifting evidence generation to routine clinical practice.

Title: Two-Year Trajectories of DIAL2-Predicted Cardiovascular Risk After Initiation of Semaglutide, Empagliflozin or Their Combination: The DIAL-STEP Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: To describe observed clinical changes and trajectories of DIAL2-predicted cardiovascular risk during 24 months of oral semaglutide, empagliflozin or combination treatment.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 332 adults without prior cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, 139; empagliflozin, 106; combination, 87). The primary endpoint was the investigator-defined HIGH category (calculated 1-year risk ≥ 3%); continuous risk was secondary. Generalized estimating equations and linear mixed models assessed trajectories. Sensitivity models added baseline age, sex and their time interactions or baseline predicted risk. Age-fixed and Shapley calculations were exploratory.
RESULTS: Paired 24-month changes included HbA1c -1.13 percentage points (95% CI: -1.27 to -1.00), systolic blood pressure -7.64 mmHg (-9.48 to -5.79), total cholesterol -20.28 mg/dL (-23.84 to -16.73) and weight -3.91 kg (-4.40 to -3.41). Standard DIAL2 was valid for 329, 327 and 325 participants across visits. HIGH prevalence was 24.6%, 23.2% and 23.7%, without a time-by-treatment interaction (p = 0.731). The continuous-risk interaction was significant (p = 0.002; demographic-time-adjusted p = 0.006). In 324 complete cases, standard predicted risk changed from 2.172% to 2.052% (relative change -5.5%); holding age fixed yielded 1.777% at 24 months (-18.2%). These relative changes concern calculated probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Glycaemia and several other measured risk factors improved during follow-up. Categorical DIAL2 status remained broadly stable, while continuous estimates varied with risk-factor changes and chronological age. Repeated DIAL2 and its explanatory decompositions do not establish fewer cardiovascular events or superiority of a treatment strategy.

Title: Longitudinal Associations of Changes in Body Mass Index and Waist-to-Height Ratio With Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: Sex-Specific Analyses in UK Biobank.
Abstract:
AIMS: To examine associations of within-person changes in body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) with cardiometabolic outcomes, characterise dose-response non-linearity and investigate effect modification by sex.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this observational UK Biobank cohort, participants had repeated anthropometric and biochemical measurements approximately 4 years apart. Those with baseline cardiovascular disease, renal failure or cancer were excluded. Associations of BMI and WHtR change with cardiometabolic outcomes were examined using multivariable analysis of covariance and restricted cubic splines, with multiple imputation for missing data.
RESULTS: Among 16 911 participants with a mean baseline BMI 26.8 kg/m2 (SD: 4.5), 679 experienced ≥ 10% BMI loss and 705 ≥ 10% gain over median 4.4 years. Compared with stable BMI (±5%), ≥ 10% loss was associated with lower systolic blood pressure (-6.11 mmHg; 95% CI: -7.14 to -5.07), triglycerides (-23.4%; -25.7 to -21.0) and C-reactive protein (-39.5%; -43.7 to -35.1), with lower DBP, total and LDL cholesterol, HbA1c and SCORE2 and higher HDL cholesterol. Conversely, ≥ 10% gain was associated with higher SBP (+4.23 mmHg; 3.22-5.23), triglycerides (+16.9%; 13.4-20.5) and C-reactive protein (+45.7%; 36.0-56.1), with adverse differences across most outcomes. Associations were broadly similar for BMI and WHtR, with non-linearity for selected outcomes. Sex modified associations with DBP, lipids and SCORE2, with larger triglyceride reductions accompanying BMI loss in men.
CONCLUSIONS: Adiposity reduction was associated with favourable cardiometabolic profiles, whereas gain was associated with adverse profiles. BMI and WHtR showed broadly similar directions and patterns of association, with some variation by outcome and sex. These observational associations support prevention of excess adiposity gain and sustained adiposity reduction where clinically appropriate.

Title: Development and Validation of 10-Year Prediction Models for Cardiovascular, Kidney and Metabolic Events Among Chinese Patients With Prediabetes in Hong Kong.
Abstract:
AIMS: Risk stratification can support frontline doctors and patients by enabling care and empowering early prevention of cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic disease. We aimed to develop and validate 10-year prediction models for seven major clinical events and mortality among Chinese patients with prediabetes in Hong Kong.
METHODS: This population-based, retrospective cohort study identified 129 834 adults with prediabetes in 2012 and followed them through 2022. Backward stepwise Cox regression was used to develop an office-based non-laboratory model and three extended models with laboratory results, transformations, interactions and medications. Outcomes included cardiovascular disease (CVD), hypertension, Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), chronic kidney disease (CKD), CVD subtypes and all-cause mortality. Four survival machine learning (ML) models were used for comparison. For each outcome, two models for haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) were developed. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 10.4 years, 19.4% of patients developed CVD. Key predictors included age, sex, smoking status, Charlson comorbidity index, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, lipid profiles, estimated glomerular filtration rate and medications. Our Cox models demonstrated moderate-to-good discrimination: CVD (C-index 0.702), hypertension (0.697), T2DM (0.704), CKD (0.790), mortality (0.816) and CVD subtypes (range: 0.673-0.830), with adequate calibration and positive net benefits. Four selected ML approaches showed comparable performance. HbA1c- and FPG-based models showed comparable performance.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed interpretable prediction models for clinically actionable events among Chinese patients with prediabetes in Hong Kong to inform clinical strategies and resource allocation.

Title: Migalastat Versus Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Treatment-Naïve Fabry Disease: Real-World Evidence From the followME Fabry Pathfinders Registry.
Abstract: Fabry disease is a rare, progressive, X-linked disease resulting from α-galactosidase A enzyme deficiency due to GLA gene variants. Current treatments include intravenous enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) and the oral pharmacologic chaperone migalastat. The followME Fabry Pathfinders registry (EUPAS20599) is an ongoing prospective patient registry evaluating outcomes for Fabry treatments. The present analyses compared the effectiveness of migalastat with ERT in treatment-naïve patients ≥ 16 years at enrollment. The prespecified primary outcome was Fabry-associated clinical event (FACE) rates/1000 person-years from treatment start. Secondary outcomes included estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) annualized rate of change, proportion of patients with FACEs, FACE incidence rates, and time to first FACE. The populations included 319 migalastat- and 140 ERT-treated patients for FACE analyses; 268 and 119, respectively, for eGFRCKD-EPI outcomes. Propensity score matching (1:1, nearest neighbor with replacement) balanced treatment groups with absolute standardized mean differences < 0.1 after matching for baseline age, sex and eGFR (matching for amenability status was not possible). Overall, patients experienced 55.3 FACEs/1000 patient-years (95% confidence interval [CI] 40.7, 75.3) with migalastat and 100.7 (53.7, 188.9) with ERT; the event-rate ratio was 0.55 (0.27, 1.11; p = 0.093). The event-rate ratio (95% CI) for cerebrovascular FACEs was 0.24 (0.06, 0.88; unadjusted p = 0.031; Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = 0.093), representing 4.7 (2.0, 11.2) FACEs/1000 patient-years with migalastat and 19.8 (7.5, 52.4) with ERT. eGFRCKD-EPI slope, mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI), was -1.47 (-2.17, -0.77) with migalastat and -2.50 (-3.53, -1.46) with ERT. Comparisons generally numerically favored migalastat over ERT, with cerebrovascular FACEs being statistically significant when not adjusting for multiple comparisons. These analyses support real-world multisystemic effectiveness of migalastat in Fabry disease.

Title: The Prognostic Implication of Preoperative Troponin Elevation at Hospital Admission in Hip Fracture Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The purpose of our study was to evaluate the prognostic significance of preoperative troponin elevation in patients who have hip fractures.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or observational studies published up to December 2025 comparing patients who have elevated cardiac troponin levels at hospital admission with those presenting normal troponin levels in patients who have hip fractures. Risk ratios (RR) were used to evaluate binary outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous endpoints, with 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: A total of five studies comprising 2,148 patients who had hip fractures were included. The group with normal troponin at admission had significantly lower overall mortality compared to the group with elevated troponin (RR 2.11; 95% CI 1.63 to 2.74; P < 0.01). In a subgroup analysis, mortality at one month (RR 3.65; 95% CI 1.59 to 8.39; P < 0.01) and three months (RR 1.98; 95% CI 1.51 to 2.60; P < 0.01) was also significantly lower in patients with normal troponin at hospital admission. However, there were no significant differences between groups for arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, or lengths of hospital stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative elevation of cardiac troponin at hospital admission was consistently associated with an increased risk of mortality, supported by low to moderate-certainty evidence. These findings support the potential role of admission troponin as an accessible prognostic biomarker for early risk stratification in this high-risk population.

Title: ICH S7A revision: Considerations for integrating safety pharmacology endpoints into repeat-dose toxicology studies.
Journal: Journal of pharmacological and toxicological methods
Abstract: The integration of safety pharmacology (SP) endpoints into toxicology studies has become an increasingly important topic in nonclinical drug development. Driven by the principles of Reduction, Refinement, and Replacement (3Rs), evolving regulatory guidances, and technology advances in devices, the pharmaceutical industry is actively exploring how to combine safety assessments with general toxicology evaluations without compromising scientific rigor. The ICH M3(R2) guideline encourages integration of SP endpoints into toxicology studies wherever feasible and when similar sensitivity can be achieved. However, for small molecules, standalone safety pharmacology studies remain the predominant practice, particularly for cardiovascular endpoints requiring high sensitivity for hemodynamic and/or QTc interval assessment. This manuscript examines the practical, scientific, and regulatory considerations surrounding the integration of cardiovascular, central nervous system, and respiratory safety pharmacology endpoints into toxicology studies. Drawing on recent industry surveys, retrospective analyses, and advances in telemetry monitoring technologies, the authors present a balanced assessment of the advantages and limitations of integration across each organ system. The paper also addresses the challenge of adversity determination for functional endpoints and the role of weight-of-evidence reasoning in shaping safety pharmacology strategy. Pathologist experience further indicates that pathology-associated with implanted telemetry devices, while generally predictable and manageable, can confound interpretation of test article-related effects in a subset of studies, underscoring the importance of pathologist familiarity with device-related background lesions when designing and interpreting telemetry-instrumented studies. This work is intended to serve as a practical resource for safety pharmacologists, toxicologists, and regulatory scientists navigating the evolving landscape of nonclinical safety assessment.

Title: Prognosis of Patients with Delayed Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Rupture after Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Multicentre Retrospective Study in France.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The majority of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) undergo endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Despite its high overall success rate, EVAR does not eliminate the risk of aneurysm rupture. This study aimed to evaluate the prognosis of patients undergoing surgical management for post-EVAR rupture.
METHODS: A multicentre retrospective study of patients who presented with ruptured AAA after successful EVAR between 2007 and 2022 at 22 academic hospitals was conducted. The index EVAR procedures were performed between 2002 and 2020. Data were extracted from electronic hospital records and computed tomography scans. Death during follow up was ascertained using the French register of deceased persons. Survival probabilities at 30, 90, and 365 days were estimated with Kaplan-Meier estimators. Cox proportional hazards survival regression was used to identify determinants associated with increased risk of death.
RESULTS: One hundred and nine patients (96 men) were included, with a mean age of 79.1 ± 9 years at the time of rupture. The median time from index EVAR to rupture was 50 months (range 0 - 179 months). Sixty-seven patients had open surgery (of which 37% underwent suprarenal cross clamping), 39 received endovascular treatment, and three underwent hybrid repair. Overall mortality was 26.6% at thirty days, increasing to 33.9% at ninety days, and 41.3% at 1 year. Neither the type of endoleak nor the type of repair was significantly associated with risk of death during follow up. Post-operative complications were frequent, including renal complications (44.0%), major haemorrhage (22.9%), respiratory distress (19.3%), and mesenteric ischaemia (6%).
CONCLUSION: This study presented a large multicentre series of patients treated for ruptured AAA after EVAR. Despite considerable progress in stent graft technology, EVAR offers little protection in the event of late rupture, even among patients with type II endoleak only. The mortality rate in this study is within the range of those published based on de novo AAA rupture.

Title: Post-approval study preliminary 1-month outcomes of the first 100 patients treated with an off-the-shelf multibranch aortic device.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To report the preliminary 1-month outcomes from the post-approval study of the first 100 patients treated with the GORE® EXCLUDER® Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE).
METHODS: This multicenter, nonrandomized, prospective study of the TAMBE aortic component included endovascular repair of an aortic disease involving the visceral vessels. Demographics, core-lab adjudicated imaging characteristics, perioperative metrics, and postoperative 1-month outcomes are reported.
RESULTS: The first 100 patients treated were 30% female, 81% white, and the median was age 74 years. Anatomic classifications included 48 patients (49.0%) with Extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA), 21 (21.4%) with pararenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), 12 (12.2%) with juxtarenal AAA, and 17 patients with post dissection pathology (n=11) or 'other' (n=6). Enrollment and treatment of 45.0% of the patients were at sites without prior TAMBE device experience. Prior aortic surgery was noted in 48.0% of patients treated. For patients with Extent I-III TAAA (n=22), staging of the TAMBE procedure was planned with initial proximal thoracic endovascular aortic repair in 7 patients (31.8%). Median aneurysm diameter was 6.2 cm. The GORE® VIABAHN® VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis was used in all patients, with additional use of a VIABAHN® self-expanding stent in six patients. Intentional non-use of one or more portals (with planned plug occlusion) was a strategy used in 15 (15.0%) patients. Median procedure time was 280 minutes, and median length of stay was four days with 83 patients (83.8%) discharged to home. Branch target vessel technical success rate was 98.9% (average of 1.39 stents into the celiac, 1.44 superior mesenteric artery, 1.62 right renal, and 1.59 left renal per portal). Three patients (3.0%) died, all were procedure related. Major adverse events in 8 patients (8.1%, 3 had ≥1 event) included 1 (1.0%) respiratory failure, 4 (4.0%) permanent paraplegia, 4 (4.0%) renal function decline, and 1 (1.0%) bowel ischemia. No patient experienced a major stroke, aneurysm rupture, or myocardial infarction. A total of eight Type 1c or Type IIIa/IIIc endoleaks were detected in 6 (6.1%) patients. No conversion to open-surgical repair, rupture, or device migration/integrity issues were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: The preliminary analysis of the FDA-mandated post-approval study 1-month outcomes in this prospective multicenter cohort treated with the TAMBE device demonstrates applicability to more extensive thoracoabdominal pathology with similar outcomes to the pivotal trial. Distinct findings for the TAMBE device in the real-world include successful treatment of post-dissection aneurysms, increased staging strategies for spinal cord protection with low paraplegia rates, and rapid adoption by many sites that did not participate in the pivotal trial.
