Title: Revascularization Outcomes in Patients with Femoropopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease Presenting with Claudication.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and optimal medical therapy (OMT), including smoking cessation, are first-line treatments for claudication. Revascularization is reserved for quality-of-life-limiting symptoms refractory to conservative management; however, the optimal revascularization strategy for femoropopliteal disease remains uncertain. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy (ET) and bypass strategies in patients undergoing revascularization for claudication.
METHODS: We analyzed Vascular Quality Initiative data (2016-2024) for patients undergoing first-time elective revascularization for femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease (PAD) presenting with claudication. Three 1:1 propensity score-matched cohorts were constructed: ET vs single-segment great saphenous vein (SSGSV) bypass, ET vs prosthetic graft (PG) bypass, and PG vs SSGSV bypass. The primary outcome was one-year freedom from persistent claudication. Secondary outcomes included one-year loss of patency, reintervention, and all-cause mortality. Outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression.
RESULTS: We identified 27,335 patients (30,483 limbs): ET 27,111 (88.9%), SSGSV 1,399 (4.6%), and PG 1,973 (6.5%). Matching yielded 1,294 ET-SSGSV pairs, 1,801 ET-PG pairs, and 1,242 PG-SSGSV pairs with well-balanced baseline characteristics. At one year, symptom-free rates were 92.0% for SSGSV, 90.0% for PG, and 89.6% for ET. Compared with SSGSV, ET was associated with a higher risk of persistent claudication at one-year (HR 1.48; 95% CI 1.10-2.00; P=0.010). No significant differences in one-year symptom relief were observed between ET and PG or between PG and SSGSV. Across all matched comparisons, loss of patency, reintervention, and mortality did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: SET and OMT should remain first-line therapy for claudication. Among patients proceeding to revascularization after unsuccessful conservative care, SSGSV bypass was associated with greater symptom relief than ET at one year, while all strategies achieved high symptom-free rates (≥89%). ET and PG demonstrated comparable outcomes across symptom relief, patency, reintervention, and survival. There were no significant differences between PG and SSGSV. Given vein-preservation considerations and procedural invasiveness in claudication, strategy selection should be individualized to anatomy, comorbidities and patient goals. Prospective studies are needed to clarify long-term durability, and quality-of-life effects.

Title: Transvenous Lead Extraction Using the PISA Approach: A Decade of Experience from a National Referral Centre.
Journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The widespread implantation of cardiovascular implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has led to a growing demand for safe and effective transvenous lead extraction (TLE), particularly concerning device-related infection, venous occlusions and lead dysfunction. As procedural complexity increases, so does the importance of adopting reliable and adaptable extraction strategies. We present a comprehensive, single referral centre experience using the PISA technique - a rotational sheath-based approach - to perform transvenous lead extraction over a 10-year period.
METHODS: This retrospective study included all patients undergoing TLE at a national referral centre between February 2013 and December 2024. Extractions were initially performed using simple traction as the first-line approach, and in all cases where simple traction was unsuccessful, the PISA approach for lead extraction was employed. Clinical and radiological success, complications, and mortality were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 283 patients underwent extraction of 530 leads, with a median lead dwell time of 96 months (IQR: 48-144). The majority of devices were pacemakers (62.9%), followed by cardiac resynchronisation devices (20.2%) and transvenous implanted cardioverter defibrillators (15.9%). Infection was the predominant indication (74.6%). The majority of procedures were performed via a superior approach. Clinical success was achieved in 97.5% of cases, whereas complete radiological success was achieved in 92.9% of patients. Major complications were observed in 2.8% of the procedures. In-hospital mortality rate was 3.9%, with only one death (0.4%) related to a major complication (not intra-procedure). During a median follow-up of 39 months (IQR: 17-74), all-cause mortality was 22.3%. Of these deaths, 3.9% occurred during the index hospitalization for TLE, 6.4% within the first year post-procedure, and 12.0% beyond the first year. Rehospitalisations due to cardiovascular or non-cardiovascular causes were observed in 19.8% of patients throughout the follow-up period.
CONCLUSION: TLE extraction with the PISA technique is a high effective methodology, with favourable complication and mortality rates in patients with CIED. The implementation of structured peri-procedural protocols and a growing team experience may contribute to support a high-successfully programme.

Title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and major cardiovascular events: Hospital resource use, survival and predictors of death in a retrospective cohort from the Brazilian private healthcare system.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brazilian data on the course of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) after a myocardial infarction or stroke are scarce.
OBJECTIVES: To estimate the association of myocardial infarction or stroke with death and hospital resource use in patients with COPD in a Brazilian private healthcare network.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort of patients aged 40 years or older with a COPD-specific ICD-10 code (J41 to J44) and a spirometry report, followed from the date both criteria were met. Myocardial infarction or stroke was a time-varying exposure: patients with a history at entry were exposed from entry, and those with a first event during follow-up were exposed from the event. Cox models with the time-varying exposure and negative binomial regression were used.
RESULTS: The 1257 patients were followed for 1368 person-years; 63 had a history of myocardial infarction or stroke at entry and 41 had a first event during follow-up. Sixty-two died, 3.8 per 100 person-years in unexposed and 15.4 in exposed person-time (adjusted HR 3.81; 95% CI 2.00 to 7.27; p < 0.001), with the highest hazard in the first 90 days after an incident event (HR 4.26). Exposed person-time had more hospital admissions (IRR 2.69; 95% CI 1.85 to 3.92) and intensive care unit admissions (IRR 3.77; 95% CI 2.25 to 6.33).
CONCLUSION: In patients with COPD, myocardial infarction or stroke was followed by a near fourfold increase in the hazard of death and a threefold increase in hospital admissions.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes with survodutide in adults with obesity at increased cardiovascular risk (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survodutide, a glucagon receptor and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, improved markers of cardiometabolic health in people with obesity, but cardiovascular safety for this new class remains to be established.
METHODS: SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT was a global, phase 3, randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicentre, event-driven, cardiovascular safety trial conducted at 524 clinical sites in 34 countries. We included participants aged 18 years or older with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater and established cardiovascular disease or at least two obesity complications or risk factors for cardiovascular disease; participants with chronic kidney disease were eligible if they also had a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater. Participants were randomly assigned by interactive response technology (1:1:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous survodutide (up-titrated to 3·6 mg or 6·0 mg) or placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event (targeting 189 primary endpoint events). We assessed the non-inferiority of pooled survodutide compared with placebo with a margin of 1·65 for the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI of the hazard ratio (HR). Efficacy and safety analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of survodutide or placebo. The primary analysis was performed according to the treatment-regimen estimand, which assessed treatment effects regardless of any early discontinuation of survodutide or placebo, temporary stop, the use of protocol-prohibited obesity medications, or a prolonged dose-escalation period. This completed trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06077864.
FINDINGS: From Nov 20, 2023, to Nov 8, 2024, we screened 7753 participants, of whom 5530 (71·3%) participants were recruited and randomly assigned to treatment. 23 (0·4%) participants were not treated; 1836 (33·3%) of 5507 participants received survodutide 3·6 mg, 1835 (33·3%) received 6·0 mg, and 1836 (33·3%) received placebo; 2194 (39·8%) were female, 3313 (60·2%) were male, and 4332 (78·7%) were White. Median time in study was 22·0 months (IQR 20·1-23·7). 1029 (56·0%) in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 1039 (56·6%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg group, and 1083 (59·0%) in the placebo group remained on treatment until study closeout. The primary endpoint occurred in 136 (3·7%) of 3671 participants in the survodutide group and in 76 (4·1%) 1836 participants in the placebo group (HR 0·89 [95% CI 0·67-1·18; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Adverse events occurred in 1708 (93·0%) of 1836 participants with survodutide 3·6 mg, 1708 (93·1%) of 1835 with survodutide 6·0 mg, and 1571 (85·6%) of 1836 with placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with survodutide than in the placebo group (nausea occurred in 882 [48·0%] of 1836 participants in the 3·6 mg group and 900 [49·0%] of 1835 in the 6·0 mg group vs 223 [12·1%] of 1836 in the placebo group, and vomiting occurred in 582 [31·7%] participants in the 3·6 mg group and 623 [34·0%] in the 6·0 mg group vs 89 [4·8%] in the placebo group). Gastrointestinal adverse events leading to treatment discontinuations occurred in 354 (19·3%) participants in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 (20·8%) in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 34 (1·9%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates across treatment groups (413 [22·5%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 381 [20·8%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 439 [23·9%] in the placebo group). Fatal adverse events were similar across treatment groups (16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, 16 [0·9%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and 11 [0·6%] in the placebo group) and were primarily due to cardiac disorders (six [0·3%] in the survodutide 3·6 mg group, seven [0·4%] in the survodutide 6·0 mg, and six [0·3%] in the placebo group).
INTERPRETATION: In participants with obesity with established cardiovascular disease or chronic kidney disease or at increased risk of cardiovascular disease, survodutide was not associated with increased risk for the primary composite endpoint of death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction, ischaemia-related coronary revascularisation, or heart failure event compared with placebo. This cardiovascular safety trial provides clinicians with reassuring data that treatment with survodutide, a novel glucagon receptor-GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk.
FUNDING: Boehringer Ingelheim.

Title: Triple-rule-out computed tomography (CT) angiography revisited: selective contemporary use enabled by sequential acquisition and modern cardiovascular computed tomography (CT).
Abstract: Triple-rule-out computed tomography angiography (TRO-CTA) was introduced to evaluate acute coronary syndrome (ACS), pulmonary embolism (PE), and acute aortic syndrome (AAS) in a single emergency department (ED) examination. Early single-pass protocols were limited by compromise bolus timing, retrospective gating over a long z-axis, high radiation and iodine burden, and inconsistent coronary image quality, and routine use appropriately declined as dedicated coronary CT angiography (CCTA) and high-sensitivity troponin algorithms matured. A subset of patients nevertheless remains difficult to triage: older or multimorbid patients with overlapping symptoms, nonspecific troponin or D-dimer elevation, or limited access to subspecialty interpretation. Wide-detector and high-pitch acquisition, low-tube-voltage imaging, iterative and deep-learning reconstruction, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based motion correction have reduced the penalties that constrained early protocols, and sequential multiphase acquisition images each territory within its own enhancement window from one coordinated injection. This review reappraises TRO-CTA from a contemporary cardiovascular CT perspective. Dedicated coronary, pulmonary, or aortic CTA remains preferred when one diagnosis is dominant, and selective TRO-CTA is confined to stable patients with persistent diagnostic ambiguity after first-tier evaluation. For contemporary sequential multiphase TRO-CTA, evidence remains largely limited to single-center feasibility and image-quality studies; robust prospective comparative data on diagnostic timeliness, missed diagnoses, downstream testing, and clinical outcomes remain lacking. Value is additionally context-dependent, varying with ED case-mix, scanner platform, availability of expert interpretation, local disease prevalence, and access to staged reassessment. Contemporary TRO-CTA is therefore a selective, institution-calibrated option requiring explicit activation criteria, demonstrated coronary image quality, and prospective multicenter evaluation.

Title: Salidroside regulates blood-brain barrier integrity via Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis inhibition for high-altitude hypoxic brain injury intervention.
Journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-altitude hypoxic brain injury (HHBI) is a central nervous system injury disease induced by high-altitude hypobaric and hypoxic environment, which disrupts normal cerebral metabolism and neurological function and triggers multi-dimensional pathological damage in brain tissues. Among these pathological events, blood-brain barrier (BBB) injury represents a critical initiating and aggravating facet of HHBI, which drives subsequent cerebral inflammation, cerebral edema and progressive brain tissue deterioration. Current clinically commonly used drugs can only relieve partial discomforts caused by high-altitude hypoxia, and fail to achieve precise prevention and treatment of HHBI as well as favorable safety profile prognosis. Salidroside (Sal), the core active ingredient of the classic Tibetan medicine Rhodiola crenulata, exerts prominent anti-hypoxia and neuroprotective effects, yet its specific molecular regulatory mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. Combining in vivo and in vitro experiments, this study aimed to explore the novel mechanism by which Sal alleviates BBB injury and thereby prevents and treats HHBI via regulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis.
METHODS: After acclimatization, mice were randomly assigned to control, model, dexamethasone (0.5 mg/kg), and Sal (50 and 100 mg/kg) groups, followed by 7-day consecutive administration of corresponding drugs. A low-pressure oxygen chamber was used to simulate high-altitude environments to establish the mouse HHBI model. The WBP respiratory detection system and Morris water maze test were employed to assess alterations in respiratory function and memory cognitive capacity of HHBI mice. A hematology analyzer and H&E staining were utilized to characterize systemic and cerebral inflammatory injury, whereas evans blue staining and brain water content measurement were performed to evaluate hypoxic impacts on BBB permeability. Super-resolution imaging (NIR-Ⅱ imaging and TEM) was adopted to detect cerebral microvascular blood circulation and ultrastructural alterations. Subsequently, RNA-seq was conducted to screen potential molecular targets mediating Sal conferred therapeutic effects against HHBI. Moreover, molecular docking, DFT calculation, alanine scanning and LSPR analysis were implemented to simulate the binding potential and stability between Sal and proteins of the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis, and protein-protein docking and Co-IP further verified the potential binding and regulatory interaction between Lcn2 and NLRP3. Western blot and multiplex immunofluorescence staining were used to demonstrate the molecular mechanism by which Sal alleviates hypoxic BBB injury via modulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. In vitro, a CoCl₂ induced hypoxic model was established in bEnd.3 cells. CCK-8 assay, EdU staining and LDH release assay were used to evaluate the effects of Sal on proliferative activity of hypoxic bEnd.3 cells. DCFH-DA and JC-1 staining were applied to detect intracellular ROS levels and mitochondrial membrane potential. Label-free cellular imaging enabled continuous monitoring of mitochondrial morphological changes under hypoxia, and TEM further observed mitochondrial ultrastructural damage. Mitochondrial superoxide, mPTP and mtDNA staining together with SOD, MDA, GSH-PX and ATP quantification were performed to analyze hypoxia and Sal mediated changes in mitochondrial function. Furthermore, cell scratch wound healing, tube-formation and cell migration assays examined hypoxic vascular functional changes, while TEER resistance and FITC-dextran permeability assays assessed paracellular permeability. Western blot combined with multiplex flow cytometry was used to analyze Sal regulated expression of Lcn2, NLRP3 and downstream inflammatory factors. In addition, the Lcn2 inhibitor ZINC00640089 and target specific siRNA were employed to validate the regulatory role of Lcn2 on NLRP3. Finally, CETSA was further performed to determine the binding stability of Sal to Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis proteins.
RESULTS: The results demonstrated that Sal exerted robust anti-hypoxic neuroprotective effects in HHBI mice by alleviating cerebral hypoxic stress, suppressing neuroinflammation, improving cerebral microcirculation, maintaining BBB integrity, and upregulating TJ proteins. In vivo data indicated that Sal intervention markedly improved basal respiratory function and alleviated cerebral memory and cognitive impairment in HHBI mice. Meanwhile, Sal effectively mitigated cerebral inflammatory injury induced by acute hypoxic stimulation and restored excessive BBB hyperpermeability. Mechanistically, acute endothelial inflammation and TJ disruption serve as key drivers of HHBI progression, which is predominantly modulated by aberrant activation of the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. Combined molecular docking, DFT calculation, LSPR detection and alanine scanning analyses confirmed the high-affinity and stable binding of Sal to core proteins of the Lcn2-NLRP3 axis. Western blot and immunofluorescence staining further revealed that Sal effectively alleviated BBB damage by negatively regulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling cascade, and verified the favorable colocalization of Lcn2 with cerebral vascular endothelium. In vitro experiments showed that Sal markedly reversed hypoxia-triggered mitochondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by reduced mitochondrial superoxide accumulation, inhibited mPTP opening and mtDNA leakage, as well as restored MMP, ATP synthesis, and balanced levels of SOD, MDA and GSH-PX, thereby suppressing apoptosis in hypoxic bEnd.3 cells. Furthermore, Sal stabilized endothelial vascular structure and barrier function, increased transepithelial electrical resistance and elevated TJ protein expression in hypoxic endothelial cells. Multiplex flow cytometry further validated the regulatory effect of Sal on hypoxic inflammatory responses. Moreover, intervention with the Lcn2 inhibitor ZINC00640089 and Lcn2-specific siRNA further confirmed that Lcn2 acts as an indispensable upstream regulator of NLRP3 inflammasome activation and subsequent inflammatory cascades.
CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, this study demonstrated that Sal ameliorates acute hypoxia‑induced mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby inhibiting excessive Lcn2 accumulation, suppressing subsequent NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and activation, and blocking downstream inflammatory cascade amplification. These effects ultimately alleviate vascular structural and functional damage, thereby exerting prominent preventive and therapeutic effects against HHBI.

Title: The joint association of cognitive function and sedentary time on mortality risk in older adults: National health and nutrition examination survey 2011-2014.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Examining the joint association of cognitive function and sedentary time may provide insight into the complex mechanisms underlying mortality risk within older adults. This longitudinal observational study examines the joint association of cognitive function and sedentary time on mortality risk in older adults.
METHODS: Sample included older adult participants from the 2011-2014 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. The Digit Symbol Substitution Test, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease subtests, and Animal Fluency were used to assess cognitive function. Average daily sitting and television time represented sedentary time. Cognitive function (lowest quartile) and sedentary time (above median) were combined for analysis.
RESULTS: Older adult participants (N = 2,230; ≥ 60 years; 49% male) were shown to have a significant (p < 0.05) increase in mortality within the lowest quartile of cognitive function and above-median sedentary time. A 2.8, 3.9, 2.8, and 2.5-fold increased risk for all-cause mortality for the Digit Symbol Substitution Test, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Immediate Learning, Delayed Learning, Animal Fluency test, respectively, were observed. Our analysis also revealed a 3.8, 3.2, 3.5, and 2.7-fold increased risk for cardiovascular disease-related mortality for the Digit Symbol Substitution Test, Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease Immediate Learning, Delayed Learning, and Animal Fluency test, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The combination of cognitive function scores with sedentary time has been shown to be strongly associated with increased risks of both all-cause and cardiovascular disease-related mortality.

Title: Immune mediators form stable clusters and associate with dendritic cell functioning and cardiovascular risk in first episode psychosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous research suggests a high-inflammation subtype of psychosis, based on different combinations of immune mediators. We examined clustering and longitudinal stability of circulating immune mediators in young adults with first-episode psychosis (FEP) and healthy controls. Because circulating mediators act on immune cells and chronic low-grade inflammation drives atherogenesis from young adulthood, we assessed the profiles' biological and clinical relevance using dendritic-cell transcriptomes and cardiovascular risk markers.
METHODS: Discovery and replication cohorts comprised 131 patients (82 male) and 130 controls (58 male), studied at baseline and one-year follow-up. Soluble immune mediators were measured from fasting serum samples using a 38-plex Luminex assay. Given their skewed distribution, mediator levels were converted to ranks. Their clustering and longitudinal stability were investigated using Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) and randomized references. Biological significance was evaluated using clinical data, cardiovascular risk markers, and dendritic-cell phenotypes isolated from simultaneous blood samples.
RESULTS: Relative mediator levels were stable over one year. LPA identified three groups with low, medium, and high mediator concentrations. Few individuals shifted groups at follow-up. FEP status was not associated with group membership, but serum low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol was associated with the "high" group in the discovery sample. Dendritic-cell transcriptomes clustered distinctly according to participants' LPA profiles.
CONCLUSION: In both patients and controls, immunological mediators formed distinct profiles with high intraindividual stability. Transcriptomic analysis of dendritic cells suggests these immune profiles have physiological relevance. In the discovery sample, the immunological mediator-profile was associated with higher serum LDL cholesterol.

Title: Predicting survival in pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: Development and internal validation of risk scores.
Journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) in the pediatric population is associated with poor survival and neurological outcomes. We aimed to develop and internally validate risk scores to predict survival to discharge in pediatric OHCA patients.
METHODS: We included pediatric OHCA patients in the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival from 2013 to 2023. We used logistic regression (LR) and classification and regression trees (CART) to develop risk scores using 70% of the data and validated them using the remaining 30% of the data. We used discrimination and predictive accuracy to evaluate model performance.
RESULTS: We included 26,895 pediatric patients, of whom 27.8% survived to hospital admission and 11.9% survived to hospital discharge. We developed three separate risk scores for i) infants ii) preschool and school-age children, and iii) adolescents. The most important predictor variables were gender, arrest location, witness status, etiology of arrest, bystander CPR, use of prehospital AED, and first rhythm. Models developed using both LR and CART approaches had good classification accuracy (AUROCC for LR: 0.81, 0.77 and 0.82, AUROCC for CART: 0.78, 0.76, 0.82 for the three age groups) However, we found CART models to be the most useful because they are simpler to follow, classified more patients in low and high survival categories using a smaller number of predictors. The average survival probability in infants for each risk group was 3%, 13%, and 33%, for preschool and school-age children it was 4%, 11%, and 29%, whereas for adolescents it was 4%, 13%, and 48% for the low, moderate, and high survival categories.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric patients experiencing OHCA can be classified into low, moderate, and high survival categories using a simple risk score and easily identified prehospital variables. These risk scores can facilitate research, monitor the quality of medical services and can potentially support clinical decision-making.

Title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear.
METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS).
RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory.
DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT.
TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

Title: Response by Al Said et al to Letter Regarding Article, "Systemic Embolic Events in Atrial Fibrillation: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of 71 683 Participants Randomized to NOAC Versus Warfarin".
Letter by Fan et al Regarding Article, "Systemic Embolic Events in Atrial Fibrillation: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of 71 683 Participants Randomized to NOAC Versus Warfarin".

Efficacy and Safety of Pelacarsen in Black/African American and Hispanic Participants with Elevated Lipoprotein(a) and Established Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: The Randomized Controlled Lp(a)FRONTIERS EXPANSION Study.
Abstract: Background: Black and Hispanic individuals may experience a disproportionate burden of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]-associated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk, and ASCVD-related mortality, yet remain underrepresented in cardiovascular (CV) clinical trials. Efficacy and safety data on Lp(a)-targeted therapies in these populations are limited. Methods: Lp(a)FRONTIERS EXPANSION was a randomized, double-blind, phase 3b, placebo-controlled trial assessing the efficacy and safety of pelacarsen, an Lp(a)-targeted therapy, in US Black/African American and Hispanic participants with elevated Lp(a) (≥125 nmol/L) and ASCVD. Eligible adults were randomized 2:1 to monthly subcutaneous pelacarsen 80 mg or placebo for 12 months, followed by 16 weeks of safety follow-up. Enrollment spanned May 2024-March 2025. The primary endpoint was change in log-transformed Lp(a) from baseline at Week 52, analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures. Results: Overall, 423 participants were randomized, with 422 analyzed (282 to pelacarsen; 140 to placebo). The population comprised 64.5% (n=272) Black/non-Hispanic, 30.1% (n=127) nonBlack/Hispanic, and 5.5% (n=23) Black/Hispanic. Trial completion rates were 90.1% and 91.4% for pelacarsen and placebo groups, respectively; median (Q1, Q3) baseline Lp(a) levels were 232.70 nmol/L (165.80, 301.50) and 219.25 nmol/L (166.95, 293.65). Geometric mean ratio (GMR) of Lp(a) to baseline at Week 52 was 0.14 (95% CI: 0.12, 0.16) with pelacarsen and 0.98 (95% CI: 0.80, 1.20) with placebo; GMR between groups (pelacarsen/placebo) was 0.14 (95% CI: 0.11, 0.18; P<0.0001), equivalent to an 86% placebo-adjusted reduction. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 66.0% (n=186) of participants receiving pelacarsen and 61.4% (n=86) receiving placebo; serious TEAEs occurred in 17.0% (n=48) and 15.0% (n=21), respectively. TEAE-related treatment discontinuations were 6.0% (n=17) with pelacarsen and 3.6% (n=5) with placebo. Conclusions: This study is the first to demonstrate robust Lp(a) lowering with pelacarsen, which was generally well tolerated, in US Black/African American and Hispanic participants, populations disproportionately impacted by Lp(a)-associated CV risk. Registration: URL:https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06267560.

Title: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in 2025: a year in review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome has emerged as an integrated clinical framework reflecting shared pathobiology and overlapping risk trajectories across cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic diseases. In 2025, this paradigm advanced from a conceptual construct toward an operational strategy, informed by randomized clinical trials, mechanistic studies, and implementation-focused analyses.
MAIN FINDINGS: This Year in Review synthesizes the major randomized clinical trials with prespecified analyses, secondary analyses, mechanistic studies, and trial design reports published during 2025 shaping contemporary CKM care. Evidence consolidated sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists as foundational therapies across heart failure (HF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) phenotypes, with expanding data on earlier initiation, combination strategies, and phenotype-guided application. Incretin-based therapies addressed obesity-driven CKM phenotypes, particularly HF with preserved ejection fraction, while mechanistic trials and biomarker analyses strengthened biological plausibility across inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic, and fibrotic pathways. Advances in vascular prevention highlighted the relevance of residual inflammatory and atherosclerotic risk beyond lipid lowering, and studies targeting anemia, congestion, and acute kidney injury expanded the operational scope of CKM management. Parallel developments in risk stratification incorporated frailty, adiposity, biomarker trajectories, and machine-learning tools, supporting a shift away from single-organ severity thresholds toward integrated, trajectory-based care.
CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 evidence base reinforces CKM syndrome as a systems-level disease state addressed through earlier intervention, rational pathway layering, and integrated care models. Future priorities include definitive outcomes trials of combination strategies, pragmatic implementation studies, and improved inclusion of advanced CKD and dialysis populations to ensure equitable translation of CKM advances into clinical practice.

Title: Renin Kinetics and Hemodynamic Response During Treatment of Vasoplegic Shock With Angiotensin II (TENSINTEST): Protocol for a Multicenter Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shock is a life-threatening condition that can lead to multiorgan failure and death. Vasopressors are needed for the treatment of vasoplegic (distributive) shock. Angiotensin II (AT II) is a novel vasopressor. Approximately two-thirds of patients respond to AT II, and one-third do not. AT II is part of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). Renin is the limiting enzyme of the RAAS, and among other mechanisms, its concentration is regulated by AT II concentration through a negative feedback loop. It might be an indicator of response to AT II therapy.
OBJECTIVE: We designed a study with a primary objective of developing and standardizing an AT II stress test, which could help predict the responsiveness to AT II in patients with distributive shock, regardless of its origin.
METHODS: This is an investigator-initiated, multicenter observational clinical study of renin kinetics before and 6 hours after starting an infusion of AT II in patients with vasoplegic shock and adequate fluid resuscitation who are severely ill. Prior to AT II, patients will receive an infusion of norepinephrine base of 0.3 mcg per kilogram per minute or higher, and vasopressin of 0.03 IU per minute according to institutional protocol. Blood samples for serum renin determination will be obtained immediately prior to and after 6 hours of AT II infusion. We hypothesize that patients who demonstrate a negative trend in relative renin ratio (defined as renin plasma concentration at baseline or at 6 hours after treatment with AT II divided by upper normal concentration of plasma renin [50 mU/L]) will have a greater number of 28-day organ failure-free days (days without vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, or renal replacement therapy). The primary analysis will assess the association between early renin reduction and organ failure-free days using an adjusted proportional odds ordinal regression model.
RESULTS: The research was funded in December 2024. After obtaining ethics approval in July 2025, data collection started on August 1, 2025. As of July 2026, a total of 70 patients had been enrolled. Data collection is expected to be completed in 2027, after which the results will be analyzed and published.
CONCLUSIONS: The goal of our study is to determine whether renin 0-6 h kinetics (difference between renin levels before and 6 hours after starting an AT II infusion) are associated with clinical outcomes in patients who require AT II. Our study could contribute to the development of a more individualized approach to vasopressor therapy and avoidance of inappropriate use of AT II in patients who are not responders, allowing earlier discontinuation of AT II and consideration of alternative therapies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Effects of advanced practice nurse-driven sedation weaning and early extubation after cardiac surgery amid health care disruption in South Korea.
Journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease has reached unprecedented levels, leading to a substantial increases in the number of cardiac surgeries. Despite the life-saving efforts of surgery, complications remain, including pulmonary complications, which can lead to death. To mitigate these complications, early extubation has emerged as an evidence-based practice for patients undergoing cardiac surgery. The physician shortages that occurred after the mass resignation of physician trainees in South Korea disrupted postoperative care provided in intensive care units (ICU) and impeded early extubation. Our institution accordingly expanded the advanced practice nurses' (APNs) scope of practice to include performing extubation when deemed clinically appropriate after cardiac surgery. This practice change led APNs to develop and implement a sedation weaning and early extubation protocol.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of an APN-driven protocol implemented in the cardiac ICU.
METHODOLOGY: This retrospective study compared two group outcomes: preimplementation and postimplementation groups.
RESULTS: This study revealed differences in health outcomes between the two groups of patients. Beneficial health outcomes were achieved due to this protocol in the opioid use and ventilator time of patients with low grade of heart failure in the postprotocol group, which were 16.7% lesser and 17.0% shorter than those in the preprotocol group.
CONCLUSION: This APN-driven protocol proves its effectiveness without causing compromised health outcomes during a health care crisis in South Korea.
IMPLICATIONS: This protocol incorporating nursing staff autonomy for both sedation and extubation can be implemented and tested for its usefulness for instances where gaps of care occur such as during physician shortages.

Title: Evaluation of a therapeutic education program for patients with coronary heart disease in a Tunisian university hospital: A quasi-experimental study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major public health concern globally, including Tunisia. Therapeutic Patient Education (TPE) plays a crucial role in managing CVD and improving patient outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a TPE program on the occurrence of major cardiovascular events in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) in a Tunisian university hospital.
METHODS: A quasi-experimental study was conducted over one year, involving 129 patients with CHD. The intervention group (n = 38) received a four-stage TPE program, while the control group (n = 91) received standard care. The control group met the same inclusion and non-inclusion criteria as the intervention group. It was constituted based on a 3:1 ratio. Patients in the intervention and control groups were recruited from the same department and during the same period to ensure comparability. The primary outcome was the occurrence of major cardiovascular events within one year. Secondary outcomes included knowledge, lipid profile, glycated hemoglobin levels, and quality of life.
RESULTS: The occurrence of major cardiovascular events was significantly lower in the intervention group compared to the control group (21.1% vs. 59.3%, p < 0.001). The TPE program was also associated with improvements in knowledge and biological parameters. Knowledge of cardiovascular risk factors increased from 71.1% at baseline to 78.9% immediately post-intervention (p = 0.039), with 60.5% retention at 3 months. The intervention group showed marked improvements in lipid profiles, with LDL cholesterol decreasing from 2.53 ± 1.45 to 1.88 ± 1.11 mmol/L (p < 0.001) and total cholesterol from 4.32 ± 1.47 to 3.75 ± 1.56 mmol/L (p = 0.002) at 3 months. In contrast, the control group demonstrated worsening lipid parameters (LDL: 2.50 ± 1.55 to 2.90 ± 1.60 mmol/L, p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: The TPE program was associated with a lower occurrence of major cardiovascular events and improvements in patients' knowledge and lipid profiles. These findings suggest a potential beneficial effect of structured therapeutic education in patients with CHD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was prospectively registered on the Pan African Clinical Trial Registry within the number PACTR202307694422939. The authors confirm that all ongoing and related trials for this intervention are registered.

Title: Thrombus stiffness depends on occlusion site and influences thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Only 60% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) achieve successful reperfusion after the first endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) attempt. In vitro studies have shown that thrombus stiffness influences thrombus-device interaction and retrieval efficacy. This prospective observational study investigates how thrombus stiffness relates to clinical factors, thrombus imaging characteristics and histological composition. It further explores the association between thrombus stiffness and EVT success, as measured by the modified first-pass reperfusion (mFPR).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 281 thrombus samples were collected from 51 AIS patients undergoing EVT. Thrombus stiffness was quantified using compressive mechanical testing, composition from histological staining and radiological characteristics from pre-interventional non-contrast computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography. Statistical analysis was performed using linear and logistic mixed-effects regression models.
RESULTS: Thrombi retrieved from the proximal M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery showed significant lower stiffness (0.236 kPa, 95% CI, 0.136-0.409) compared to those from the M1 segment (0.760 kPa, 95% CI, 0.492-1.174) and from the ICA (1.106 kPa, 95% CI, 0.558-2.192). Occlusion location was the strongest clinical marker of thrombus stiffness. Adjusted mFPR probability was 40.4% (95% CI, 24.5-67.0) for thrombi retrieved from the ICA, 89.7% (95% CI, 79.5-97.0) for M1 occlusions, and 53.0% (95% CI, 30.8-84.7) for M2 occlusions.
CONCLUSION: Thrombi in distal vessels of the anterior cerebral circulation are significantly softer than those in proximal intracranial arteries. First-pass EVT success is lower for the stiffest thrombi from the ICA and for the softest thrombi from M2, providing a foundation for future biomechanically informed thrombus removal strategies to optimise AIS treatment.

Title: Perioperative venous thromboembolism prophylaxis during penile prosthesis surgery without routine drain placement: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing penile prosthesis surgery are at elevated risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet perioperative thromboprophylaxis is not addressed in current urologic guidelines and the safety of subcutaneous heparin (SqH) without drain placement remains unclear. We aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of perioperative SqH for VTE prevention in penile prosthesis surgery performed without surgical drains.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all penile prosthesis surgeries performed at a single institution from January 2019 to January 2025 in which no drain was placed. Demographics, comorbidities, Caprini risk scores, VTE risk factors, hematoma incidence, and 90-day postoperative complications were compared between patients who did and did not receive perioperative SqH.
RESULTS: The primary outcome of our study was postoperative VTE, with secondary outcomes including hematoma formation and 90-day complications. Of 524 patients, 85% were classified as high risk for VTE (Caprini ≥ 5). A total of 246 (47%) received perioperative SqH. VTE occurred in 0.7% (2/278) of patients who did not receive SqH, while no VTE was observed in the SqH group. Hematoma rates were similar between groups (SqH 2.0% vs non-SqH 2.2%; P = .920). Caprini scores and most comorbidities were comparable, though smoking (P = .043) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (P = .025) were more common in the non-SqH cohort.
DISCUSSION: Implementation of VTE prophylaxis with SqH in penile prosthesis patients may reduce the risk of VTE in a high-risk population and is relatively cost effective and simple to implement. The main strength of this study is that it is the largest cohort of penile prosthesis patients receiving SqH to be analyzed. In addition, our patient population is unique in the lack of drain placement postoperatively. The study is limited by its retrospective nature and potential bias in reporting complications. The cohort of patients receiving SqH prophylaxis did not develop a VTE and adverse event rates were similar between groups suggesting a possible protective benefit without increasing postoperative complications.

Title: 18F-FAPI PET/CT and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance for Cardiac Fibrotic Process in End-stage Renal Disease: A Pilot Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) increases the risk of myocardial fibrosis. This study aimed to detect cardiac fibroblast activation and fibrosis in ESRD using 18F-labeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective clinical trial (NCT07107919) enrolled 33 ESRD patients who underwent 18F-FAPI PET/CT, with 19 patients undergoing CMR. Myocardial FAPI activity was quantified. Cardiac function [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF), left atrial ejection fraction (LAEF)] and tissue parameters [native T1, extracellular volume (ECV), late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)] were assessed by CMR. Spearman correlation analysis assessed correlations between 18F-FAPI uptake and CMR parameters.
RESULTS: A total of 75.76% (25/33) of ESRD patients showed myocardial FAPI uptake, significantly higher than the controls (P < 0.05). 18F-FAPI-42 PET identified more segments with evidence of fibroblast activation than CMR-late gadolinium enhancement detected fibrosis (82 vs. 71). Compared with FAPI-negative patients, FAPI-positive patients had increased native-T1, decreased LVEF, LAEF and RVEF (P < 0.05). FAPI-positive segments showed higher native-T1 and extracellular volume % than FAPI-negative segments (P < 0.05). FAPI activity correlated with LVEF, RVEF, LAEF and native-T1. Higher myocardial FAPI uptake was associated with lower LVEF and longer dialysis duration.
CONCLUSIONS: 18F-FAPI PET enables in vivo detection of cardiac fibroblast activation in ESRD and correlates with functional and tissue parameters by CMR. FAPI uptake may serve as an imaging biomarker for cardiac remodeling. Further studies are warranted to clarify the role of 18F-FAPI PET in evaluating the efficacy of anti-fibrotic treatment and in assisting cardiac risk stratification in ESRD patients.

Title: Cardiac Complications following Creation of Arteriovenous Access in Medicare Beneficiaries with ESKD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs) are the preferred long-term hemodialysis access for the majority of patients, but produce hemodynamic changes that contribute to cardiac complications including heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia. This cohort study leverages nationwide claims data to examine adverse cardiac events associated with AVGs and AVFs among patients with ESKD.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using 100% Medicare fee-for-service claims to identify adults with ESKD undergoing AVF or AVG creation from 2017-2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for a composite adverse cardiac event (heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or atrial fibrillation or flutter) within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the composite outcome through 5 years, its individual components, all-cause hospitalization, and flow-reduction procedures. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Independent variable analyses were conducted for the primary outcome.
RESULTS: We identified 210,002 accesses (mean age 66.3 years; 43% female) including 147,709 (70%) AVFs and 62,293 (30%) AVGs. AVG recipients had a greater burden of baseline comorbidity and cardiovascular disease. Through 1 year, the cumulative incidence of hospitalization for an adverse cardiac event was 40% (AVF 39%, AVG 44%, P < .001), constituting 61% of all-cause hospitalizations. Heart failure predominated (AVF 33%, AVG 37%, P < .001), followed by atrial fibrillation or flutter (AVF 19%, AVG 21%, P < .001), and pulmonary hypertension (AVF 8%, AVG 9%, P < .001). Older age (≥ 50 years), AVG creation, pre-existing pulmonary hypertension, and atrial arrhythmia were independently associated with a higher hazard of the primary outcome (P < .05).
CONCLUSIONS: The high rate of hospitalization for adverse cardiac events in the first year after arteriovenous access creation supports consideration of strategies (e.g., lower-flow forearm access, flow-volume surveillance) to mitigate the hemodynamic consequences of long-term arteriovenous access.

Title: Inforatio Technique and Foot Ulcer Closure Among Patients With Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are common complications of diabetes, a disease increasing in prevalence worldwide. Novel adjunctive treatments that are affordable and feasible to implement in both high- and low-income settings are urgently needed.
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether the inforatio technique promotes healing of DFUs compared with standard of care (SOC).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, evaluator-blinded randomized clinical trial was conducted at 4 outpatient clinics specializing in wound care in Denmark from February 15, 2022, to December 18, 2024. One-year medical record follow-up was completed August 14, 2025. Participants included patients with noninfected Wagner grade 1 DFUs.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive the inforatio technique every third week for 12 weeks with SOC or SOC only. The inforatio technique involved making incisions on wound beds with 2-mm biopsy punch tools.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the proportion of ulcers achieving closure within 20 weeks. Secondary outcomes were health-related and disease-specific quality of life. Safety outcomes included serious and target ulcer-related adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 101 patients were randomized, of whom 100 had DFUs and were included in the primary analysis (49 in the inforatio group and 51 in the SOC only group; 85 men; mean [SD] age, 64.4 [11.4] years; median ulcer size, 0.76 [range, 0.09-23.23] cm2). Twenty-four patients in the inforatio group (49.0%) vs 14 in the SOC-only group (27.5%) achieved ulcer closure within 20 weeks (adjusted odds ratio, 3.01 [95% CI, 1.20-7.58]; P = .02). No between-group difference was found in quality of life change from baseline to 20 weeks. Within 20 weeks, 7 patients in the inforatio group vs 13 in the SOC-only group experienced the serious adverse events, including death, amputation, or target ulcer-related hospitalization (relative risk, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.24-1.29]; P = .25), and 16 patients in the inforatio group vs 30 in the SOC-only group experienced target ulcer-related adverse events (relative risk, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.88]; P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, the inforatio technique improved DFU healing compared with SOC alone. Fewer ulcer-related adverse events were also observed with the inforatio technique, although this exploratory finding should be interpreted cautiously.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05189470.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR).
METHODS: This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable.
RESULTS: We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], -6.7 percentage points [ -8.7 to -4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( -25.9ms [-41.7 to -10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (-19.1g [-28.0 to -10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8-8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6-8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

Title: From Glycemic Control to Obesity Management: A 20-year Systematic Evidence Map of GLP-1 Trials and Their Relevance to Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery.
Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapeutics have evolved from glucose-lowering agents into a major component of obesity care, with increasing relevance to metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). However, the long-term evolution of the randomized trial ecosystem across the full incretin-agonist spectrum has not been systematically mapped. We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review, evidence map, and bibliometric analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating GLP-1-based therapeutics, including selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and GLP-1-based co-/tri-agonists. ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed/MEDLINE, and Scopus were searched for trials registered and/or published between July 1, 2005, and June 30, 2025. After deduplication and eligibility assessment, 517 unique randomized trials were included. Trial activity was more than threefold higher in the recent era, with 393 trials (76.0%) initiated during 2016-June 2025 compared with 124 trials (24.0%) during July 2005-2015. Early development was predominantly diabetes-centered, whereas the later era showed marked expansion into obesity and weight-management, cardiovascular and cardiorenal outcomes, and other emerging indications. Across the mapped corpus, later-phase and larger-enrollment studies became increasingly prominent, reflecting maturation into broader and more pragmatic cardiometabolic development programs. Bibliometric patterns paralleled these shifts, showing a mature diabetes-centered literature and a rapidly expanding obesity evidence community. Over two decades, GLP-1-based therapeutics have transitioned into a broad obesity and cardiometabolic trial ecosystem. These trends are increasingly relevant to bariatric surgeons, particularly in relation to preoperative optimization, postoperative adjunctive therapy, and recurrent weight gain after MBS, and highlight the need for more durable, comparative, and post-bariatric randomized trials.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Anthracycline-Related Cardiac Dysfunction: Critical Evidence Appraisal and State-Specific Pharmacotherapeutic Positioning.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiorenal outcomes, but their role in anthracycline-related cardiac dysfunction (ARCD) beyond established indications is uncertain. We appraised mechanistic and clinical evidence across pre-exposure prophylaxis (State A); an isolated surveillance abnormality or mild asymptomatic cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), both with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (State B); and symptomatic CTRCD/heart failure irrespective of ejection fraction or asymptomatic moderate/severe CTRCD (State C).
METHODS: This critical narrative review used structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov, supplemented by an Embase search during revision. Peer-reviewed literature through 15 August 2026 and registry status through 22 August 2026 were assessed by clinical state, evidentiary directness, endpoint relevance, and validity threats.
RESULTS: Human evidence was predominantly retrospective, and SGLT2i use usually reflected conventional indications. Small prospective nonrandomized studies focused on imaging or biomarkers. Favorable associations remain vulnerable to residual confounding, treatment selection, competing cancer mortality, exposure-timing bias, and source-cohort overlap. No peer-reviewed randomized between-group efficacy report was available by the literature cutoff. Experimental studies support biological plausibility but not direct myocardial target engagement, a uniform class effect, preserved anticancer activity, or clinical benefit.
CONCLUSION: State C warrants phenotype-appropriate guideline-based care, including SGLT2i when indicated; an incremental ARCD-specific benefit remains unproven. Without another indication, initiation in States A and B remains investigational. HFA-ICOS may guide surveillance and trial enrichment but is not a prescribing trigger.

Title: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for VEGF-pathway inhibitor-associated hypertension and proteinuria: biological rationale, clinical evidence, and a hypothesis-generating framework.
Abstract: In this narrative review, we integrate mechanistic, clinical, and cardiorenal evidence relevant to mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-pathway inhibitor-associated hypertension and proteinuria. VEGF-pathway inhibition can cause systemic endothelial dysfunction, altered nitric oxide and endothelin signaling, and heterogeneous glomerular injury, including thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) with VEGF-ligand blockade and podocytopathy with some VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) blockade, dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers, careful blood pressure control, quantitative proteinuria assessment, and recognition of structural kidney injury remain the established management foundation. MR blockade is biologically attractive because it can lower blood pressure and proteinuria and modulate inflammatory, vascular, and glomerular pathways; however, most supporting evidence is extrapolated from resistant hypertension and chronic kidney disease. Direct oncology evidence is limited to small, nonrandomized datasets and remains hypothesis-generating. Accordingly, MRAs should not be positioned as a preferred third-line antihypertensive class or as established prophylaxis for VEGF-pathway inhibitor-associated renal toxicity. They may be considered as a phenotype-selected option when hypertension and non-nephrotic proteinuria coexist, conventional diuretic escalation is clinically unattractive, product-specific kidney function and potassium criteria are met, and close monitoring is feasible. Prospective oncology studies using kidney-function, structural, and treatment-continuity endpoints are required before routine adoption can be recommended.

Title: Physical Performance After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Gait, Frailty, and Cardiovascular Prognosis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Physical performance and frailty have emerged as potential markers of physiological reserve and cardiovascular vulnerability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This review examines the prognostic significance of gait speed, lower-extremity physical performance, frailty, and sarcopenia after AMI and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and discusses their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical implications.
RECENT FINDINGS: Slow gait speed, impaired Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores, and frailty are associated with mortality, rehospitalization, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events after AMI or ACS. Gait speed and SPPB may provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional cardiovascular risk assessment and established risk scores. These associations may reflect an interconnected cardiac-vascular-muscle axis involving reduced cardiac reserve, vascular dysfunction, impaired skeletal muscle perfusion, sarcopenia, and physical deconditioning. Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that targeted cardiac rehabilitation may improve gait speed, muscle strength, and overall physical performance in vulnerable patients. Physical performance represents a clinically relevant and potentially modifiable dimension of post-AMI cardiovascular vulnerability. Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Neurological and Medical Complications in Brain Tumor Patients. 2026 Update.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Patients with brain tumors have a plethora of potential complications that arise from both the tumor and its therapeutic management. These complicate clinical management and produce morbidity and occasionally mortality. In this review we discuss the most common neurological and medical complications that include tumor-related epilepsy, vasogenic edema, infection, thromboembolism, endocrine abnormalities and cognitive impairment and its management. This review is an update to the 2020 article by Schiff and Alyahya.
RECENT FINDINGS: IDH mutant gliomas cause neuronal hyperexcitability via D-2 -hydroxyglutarate production; use of IDH inhibitors may lower the rate of seizures in this patient population. Pneumocystis prophylaxis with antibiotics has been traditionally recommended with radiation and concurrent temozolomide chemotherapy but newer data suggest no difference in hospitalization or survival. Podoplanin produced by tumor cell releases into the circulation, often via extracellular vesicles, activates platelets and may contribute to venous thrombus formation. Direct oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) are the treatment of choice for venous thromboembolism, with high quality of evidence and a strong recommendation in cancer-associated thrombosis. Though brain tumor patients were underrepresented in clinical trials, retrospective studies support its safety in this population. Brain tumor patients are prone to complications arising from both the tumor and the treatment strategies. Management requires a multidisciplinary strategy with supportive medications including antiseizure medications, corticosteroids, anticoagulants for thromboembolism, and neurocognitive rehabilitation. Early recognition and timely intervention can reduce the morbidity associated with these complications leading to better patient outcomes.

Title: Mitral annular calcification on routine Non-ECG Gated Chest CT Is associated with advanced atrioventricular block requiring permanent pacing: A case-control study.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine whether visual or quantitative mitral annular calcification (MAC) burden on routine non-contrast, non-ECG-gated chest computed tomography (CT) is associated with permanent pacemaker (PPM) implantation for advanced atrioventricular (AV) block. MAC has been linked to conduction disturbances after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Whether MAC visible on routine chest CT is associated with significant AV conduction disease in non-TAVI patients remains uncertain. In this retrospective single-center case-control study, 39 consecutive patients who underwent PPM implantation for symptomatic advanced AV block and had non-contrast chest CT were compared with 39 age- and sex-matched controls without AV block or prior PPM. MAC was graded visually by annular circumference involvement and quantified using an Agatston-based score. Visual MAC was more prevalent in the PPM (+) group than in the PPM (-) group (22 of 39 [56%] vs. 12 of 39 [31%]; P = 0.039). The prevalence of PPM implantation increased across visual MAC categories, from 39% with no MAC and 48% with MAC involving < 1/3 of the annular circumference to 80% with MAC involving 1/3 to 1/2 and 100% with MAC involving > 1/2 of the annular circumference (P = 0.007). Quantitative MAC categories also differed (44%, 33%, and 78% PPM implantation for MAC scores of 0, 1 to 400, and > 400, respectively; P = 0.022). In multivariable analysis, MAC score > 400 remained independently associated with PPM implantation (odds ratio: 24.6; 95% confidence interval: 1.63 to 370.96; P = 0.02).Visual and quantitative MAC burden on routine non-contrast chest CT were associated with PPM implantation for advanced AV block. Structured assessment and reporting of marked MAC may provide a clinically useful marker in patients with suspected AV conduction disease.

Title: Transmitral flow analysis via valve tracking 4D flow MRI detects age- and sex-related diastolic changes.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: To evaluate whether valve tracking 4D flow MRI can detect subtle age- and sex-related changes in left ventricular (LV) diastolic function in healthy adults. We retrospectively recruited healthy adults who had undergone cardiac MRI between October 2020 and March 2022, selecting those with whole-heart 4D flow MRI, 2D long-axis cine, and short-axis cine acquisitions. A dynamic plane at the mitral valve (MV) level was generated in 4D flow MRI using leaflet insertion points tracked on 2- and 4-chamber cine images. Through-plane velocities were computed from 4D flow data and corrected for MV motion. After contouring the transmitral region, early and late diastolic peak flow rates (Eflow, Aflow), peak velocities (Evel, Avel), and mitral forward flow volume (MFVol) were measured. Peak early LV relaxation velocity (EMV) was defined as the peak through-plane velocity of MV plane motion. A total of 39 adults (age range: 46 ± 13; 20 women) were included. With age, both Eflow/Aflow (r = - 0.79, p < 0.0001, adjusted for HR) and Evel/Avel (r = - 0.70, p < 0.0001, adjusted for HR) were significantly decreased, while Evel/EMV increased (r = 0.53, p < 0.001, adjusted for EDV). Early diastolic changes were sex-specific; women showed decreased Eflow and increased Evel/EMV with aging, whereas men showed no significant associations. Additionally, the normalized Eflow/MFVol decreased with aging, significantly in the sex-combined cohort (r = - 0.42, p = 0.008) and in women (r = - 0.68, p = 0.004), but not in men. Transmitral flow rates and peak velocities assessed by 4D flow MRI with cine-based valve tracking effectively detected physiologic age-related declines in diastolic function, exhibiting sex-specific differences.

Title: Regression patterns of giant coronary artery aneurysms in children with kawasaki disease: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: To characterise post-peak regression of giant coronary artery aneurysms (GCAA) across severity groups in children with Kawasaki disease (KD) and examine factors associated with regression. This retrospective cohort included 146 children with KD-associated GCAA admitted to Beijing Children's Hospital between April 2016 and September 2025. Serial echocardiographic measurements were used to identify the retrospectively observed peak patient-level coronary Z score. Cumulative regression from the observed peak to Z scores < 10, < 5 and < 2.5 was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox models examined factors associated with regression to Z < 5. Patients were grouped by peak Z score: 10 to < 20 (n = 104), 20 to < 30 (n = 24) and ≥ 30 (n = 18). The observed peak occurred at a median of 30.0 days after disease onset. Five-year cumulative regression estimates to Z < 10 were 81.2%, 56.5% and 0%, respectively; estimates to Z < 5 were 55.6%, 13.5% and 0%. Older age, higher peak Z score and more affected coronary segments were independently associated with a lower regression hazard to Z < 5.
CONCLUSION: Post-peak regression differed across GCAA severity groups. Older age, higher peak Z scores and greater coronary segment involvement were associated with a lower hazard of regression to Z < 5. No regression was observed during available follow-up in the small subgroup with peak Z scores ≥ 30.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Giant coronary artery aneurysms after Kawasaki disease regress less frequently than smaller aneurysms and require long-term surveillance. • Aneurysm severity is associated with subsequent coronary outcomes.
WHAT IS NEW: • Post-peak regression differed across peak Z-score groups and according to thresholds of  <10, <5 and <2.5. • Greater segment involvement was associated with less frequent regression to Z <5.

Title: Effects of Eplontersen on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CARDIO-TTRansform Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In CARDIO-TTRansform, the TTR (transthyretin) silencer eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary end point of cardiovascular death and recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, although treatment effects varied by baseline TTR stabilizer use. Whether eplontersen favorably affects cardiac structure and function is unknown.
METHODS: CARDIO-TTRansform randomized 1432 patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy to eplontersen (45 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks or placebo. Echocardiograms were performed at baseline and weeks 61, 97, and 140. Associations of baseline echocardiographic measures with all-cause mortality and the primary end point were evaluated using Cox and semiparametric proportional rates models. Between-group differences at week 140 were analyzed with mixed models for repeated measures.
RESULTS: Among 1426 participants with baseline echocardiograms (mean age, 76±7 years, 91% men, 85% wild type, 57% receiving stabilizers), baseline measures of left ventricular systolic function (LV ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, stroke volume, myocardial contraction fraction), diastolic function (E wave deceleration time, septal e', average E/e'), and right ventricular function and hemodynamics were independently associated with all-cause mortality or the primary end point. At week 140 (echocardiograms available in 554 patients in the eplontersen group and 506 in the placebo group), eplontersen attenuated increases in mean LV wall thickness (least-squares mean [LSM] difference, -0.24 mm [95% CI, -0.48 to -0.01]) and declines in LV stroke volume (LSM difference, 1.88 mL [95% CI, 0.07-3.69]), myocardial contraction fraction (LSM difference, 0.88% [95% CI, 0.25-1.57]), average E/e' (LSM difference, -0.71 [95% CI, -1.36 to -0.07]), and right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LSM difference, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.00-0.85]) versus placebo in the overall cohort. Beneficial effects were driven almost exclusively by patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. No significant treatment effects were observed in patients receiving stabilizers.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, eplontersen modestly attenuated deterioration in prognostically important measures of LV systolic, diastolic and right ventricular function, primarily among patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. These findings complement the clinical findings of CARDIO-TTRansform and suggest that TTR silencing may attenuate progression of cardiac dysfunction in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

Title: Association Between Postoperative Pneumonia and Prognosis in Patients With Non-Traumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: An Analysis of the MIMIC-IV Database.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between postoperative pneumonia (POP) and prognosis in patients with nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the MIMIC-IV database. Adult SAH patients who underwent surgical treatment with postoperative sedation were included, excluding traumatic SAH, nonsurgical cases, ICU stay ≤ 1 day, and those without sedative use. Patients were divided into the POP and non-POP groups. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors for POP, validated by LASSO regression and random forest analysis. A progressive adjustment strategy evaluated POP's association with in-hospital, 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year mortality, and length of stay (LOS). Sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW)/doubly robust analysis, short-stay exclusion, survivor-restricted analysis, and Fine-Gray competing risk models. Mortality at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year was ascertained only among patients who survived to hospital discharge and is therefore reported as post-discharge mortality.
RESULTS: Among 505 included patients, 189 (37.4%) developed POP. Factors independently associated with higher POP odds included WFNS Grades IV-V (OR = 2.373, p < 0.001), dexmedetomidine use (OR = 2.026, p = 0.001), and COPD (OR = 1.817, p = 0.039). Higher admission potassium (OR = 0.526, p = 0.010) and acetaminophen use (OR = 0.597, p = 0.012) were independently associated with lower POP odds. POP was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality (OR = 1.030, p = 0.908) but significantly prolonged ICU LOS (ratio = 1.651, p < 0.001) and total hospital LOS (ratio = 1.765, p < 0.001). LOS findings were consistent across all sensitivity analyses, while in-hospital mortality results were less stable across analytical frameworks and should be interpreted cautiously. Post-discharge mortality among patients who survived to hospital discharge was 7.5% versus 3.7% at 30 days, 11.6% versus 8.2% at 90 days, and 18.5% versus 11.0% at 1 year.
CONCLUSIONS: In surgical nontraumatic SAH patients, POP correlated with prolonged ICU and hospital LOS. High WFNS grade, dexmedetomidine use, and COPD were independently associated with increased POP odds. These findings highlight the potential value of POP prevention strategies to reduce LOS and healthcare resource consumption.

Title: Patient-Spouse Experiences of Post-Stroke Life Reconstruction: A Longitudinal Dyadic Journey Mapping Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young and middle-aged stroke survivors with residual limb motor impairment continue rehabilitation while resuming employment, family responsibilities, and social roles. Their spouses often provide care and rehabilitation support, yet little is known about how partners' experiences compare and change within dyads over time. This study aimed to examine the experiences of young and middle-aged stroke survivors with limb motor impairment and their spouses across inpatient recovery, early transition home, and longer-term home-based life reconstruction, and to synthesize the findings into a patient-spouse dual-line journey map.
METHODS: This longitudinal qualitative study recruited 18 patient-spouse dyads using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Patients and spouses were interviewed separately 1-3 days before discharge (T1), 4 weeks after discharge (T2), and 6 months after discharge (T3), yielding 108 interviews. Data were analyzed using the Framework Method adapted for longitudinal and dyadic qualitative data. Longitudinal matrices and within- and between-dyad comparisons informed the visual synthesis of findings.
RESULTS: Findings were synthesized across three phases: T1: Inpatient recovery and preparation for discharge; T2: Early transition home and emerging differences in independence and safety; and T3: Longer-term life reconstruction and varied dyadic adjustment. Five cross-cutting analytic domains informed this synthesis: patients' rehabilitation and everyday-life experiences; spouses' caregiving experiences; convergence and difference within dyads; emotional experiences; and stage-specific support needs and service gaps. At T1, professional guidance provided reassurance, while preparation for home remained incomplete. At T2, patients' attempts at independence coexisted with spouses' safety concerns and difficulties applying discharge guidance.
