At T3, negotiated goals and reassurance in some dyads contrasted with restricted participation, caregiving strain, or reduced communication in others. These findings informed a patient-spouse dual-line journey map.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients' rehabilitation and everyday-life experiences and spouses' caregiving experiences changed across the hospital-to-home transition, with differing priorities within dyads and varied longer-term adjustment. Findings support involving both partners in discharge preparation and providing individualized follow-up, rehabilitation, and caregiver support responsive to changing needs.

Title: Early Acupuncture Following Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials on Efficacy and Safety.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intravenous thrombolysis is standard for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but many patients still have poor outcomes. Acupuncture may confer additional neuroprotection, yet its safety and efficacy when initiated early post-thrombolysis remain unclear.
METHODS: A systematic search of databases and registries was conducted from inception to March 31, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing thrombolysis plus acupuncture with thrombolysis plus conventional post-thrombolytic care in AIS patients within 14 days of onset. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; publication bias was evaluated via Egger's test. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: Ten trials (1116 patients) were included. Adjunctive acupuncture reduced neurological deficit (NIHSS MD -2.90, 95% CI -3.62 to -2.17), improved activities of daily living (Barthel Index MD 12.07, 95% CI 8.10-16.03), and increased clinical response (RR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.21; all p < 0.001). Adverse events did not differ significantly (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.25-1.08). Only one study reported symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (zero acupuncture vs. six control). Benefits were consistent across subgroups.
CONCLUSION: In AIS patients receiving thrombolysis, acupuncture initiated early following thrombolysis improves neurological and functional outcomes. In available safety data, adverse events did not differ significantly between groups; however, systematic surveillance for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage was lacking in most trials. These findings support further rigorous evaluation of early post-thrombolysis acupuncture in adequately monitored randomized trials.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261358943.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Meta-Analysis; Systematic Review; Review

Title: Glycolipid metabolic changes during remission induction in ANCA-associated vasculitis: a retrospective study of the lipid paradox.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate dynamic changes in glycolipid metabolism in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) during remission induction and to explore their associations with inflammatory markers, treatment and ANCA antigen specificity.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of 973 patients with AAV, baseline glycolipid profiles and the prevalence of dyslipidaemia were assessed. Paired baseline and post-remission induction glycolipid parameters were compared in the longitudinal cohort. Multivariable models were used to evaluate factors associated with baseline dyslipidaemia and exploratory associations with metabolic changes. Additional analyses compared patients with and without longitudinal data and assessed the relationship between changes in inflammatory markers and metabolic parameters.
RESULTS: Dyslipidaemia was highly prevalent at baseline. Inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), were associated with dyslipidaemia. During remission induction, triglyceride, total cholesterol and LDL-C levels increased, whereas fasting glucose and the TC/HDL-C ratio decreased, consistent with a lipid-paradox pattern. Additional analyses suggested potential selection bias in the longitudinal cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with AAV show a high burden of baseline dyslipidaemia and dynamic glycolipid metabolic changes during remission induction. The observed increase in lipid concentrations together with decreases in fasting glucose and the TC/HDL-C ratio suggests a lipid-paradox pattern and a close relationship between inflammation and metabolic status. Further prospective studies with standardised treatment exposure and cardiovascular outcome assessment are needed to clarify the clinical significance of these metabolic trajectories.

Title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy.
RESULTS: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

Title: Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking.
METHODS: We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome).
RESULTS: From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80).
CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).

Title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown.
METHODS: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo. The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke.
RESULTS: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

Title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

Title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized.
METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks.
RESULTS: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

Title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure.
RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

Title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo.
CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

Title: Association of Perivascular Space Volume in Basal Ganglia Subfields With Cognitive Impairment in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease.
Abstract: Perivascular spaces (PVS) serve as essential elements of the glymphatic pathway, facilitating waste clearance and nutrient transport, and their impairment may underlie cognitive deficits in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). Here, we investigated associations between PVS characteristics, potential determinants, and cognitive impairment in CSVD. 132 individuals diagnosed with CSVD and 40 healthy controls (HCs) were recruited to participate in a series of thorough neuropsychological assessments and neuroimaging examinations. PVS volume fraction (VF) was quantified in basal ganglia (BG), thalamus, hippocampus, and white matter (WM) using an automated, multimodal image processing pipeline (Enhanced PVS Contrast, EPC) combined with the Frangi filter for robust segmentation. Partial correlation analyses, adjusted for covariates, were performed. CSVD patients exhibited significantly larger PVS VF in the BG and hippocampus, particularly in caudate and putamen subfields of BG (all p < 0.05). In CSVD group, advancing age correlated with elevated PVS VF in both BG and hippocampus, especially in males (all pFDR < 0.05). A main effect of sex on PVS VF was observed in this patient cohort across the BG, caudate, hippocampus and thalamus, where males exhibited larger PVS VF than females (all p < 0.05). In HC group, age correlated positively with PVS volume fraction in the BG (pFDR < 0.05), with no significant sex differences across regions. Enlarged BG-PVS was associated with worse global cognitive function (pr = -0.27, pFDR = 0.027) and processing speed (pr = -0.31, pFDR = 0.010), persisting after controlling for other neuroimaging markers (including WMHs, lacunes, and CMBs) and regional volume. Subfield analyses revealed the correlation mainly occurring in the putamen (pr = -0.31, pFDR = 0.010). Hippocampal PVS VF inversely correlated with hippocampal volume (pr = -0.26, pFDR = 0.043), more pronounced in females, and was significantly linked to worse visuospatial function (pr = -0.33, pFDR = 0.010). Regional PVS enlargement in CSVD, particularly in BG and hippocampus regions, reflects underlying glymphatic impairment related to age and sex. The prominence of this finding within BG subregions further underscores their role in the pathogenesis of neurocognitive decline.

Title: Clinical-Immunological Phenomapping in Recurrent Pericarditis: Disentangling Biological Traits, Inflammatory State and Treatment Exposure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phenotype-oriented management is increasingly advocated in recurrent pericarditis (RP), but it remains unclear whether clinically recognizable phenotypes reflect underlying disease biology or are shaped by current inflammation and treatment exposure. We used multidimensional phenomapping to investigate this heterogeneity.
METHODS: We analysed 101 patients with idiopathic RP from the multicenter PERIPLO cohort. Factor analysis of mixed data followed by hierarchical clustering defined the index solution. Robustness was assessed across alternative specifications and models excluding treatment, inflammatory state or the IL-1Ra axis.
RESULTS: Three clinical-immunological patterns emerged: a predominantly remission-state, anakinra-treated group; a predominantly remission-state group largely managed without IL-1 blockade; and an active inflammatory group enriched for anti-IL-1Ra autoantibodies and characterized by markedly reduced measured IL-1Ra. The two antibody-negative groups were extensively reorganized after treatment variables were removed, whereas exclusion of the IL-1Ra axis nearly abolished agreement with the original partition. In contrast, anti-IL-1Ra positivity remained consistently associated with active inflammation and very low measured IL-1Ra.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, the phenotypic heterogeneity of RP was better represented as a clinical-immunological spectrum shaped by inflammatory state and treatment exposure than as discrete, stable endotypes. The anti-IL-1Ra-associated inflammatory signature was the most internally consistent biological signal. These exploratory findings require external validation, and longitudinal multidimensional phenomapping should test whether this signature can inform patient management.

Title: Prognostic impact of the Mehran 2 risk score on 1-year mortality after acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Mehran 2 score was developed to predict contrast-associated acute kidney injury after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Its prognostic value beyond renal complications remains uncertain. We evaluated the association of preprocedural (model 1) and postprocedural (model 2) Mehran 2 scores with renal outcomes and 1-year mortality in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 1025 patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Both scores were calculated and categorized into four risk groups. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality, while secondary outcomes included contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) and dialysis requirement. Prognostic performance was assessed using multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.
RESULTS: CIN occurred in 105 patients (10.2%), dialysis was required in 21 (2.0%), and 102 (10.0%) died within 1 year. All outcomes increased progressively across Mehran 2 risk categories (P < 0.001). Both scores were independently associated with 1-year mortality [model 1: adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.59, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.37-1.84; model 2: adjusted OR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.41-1.83; both P < 0.001]. The area under the curves (AUCs) for mortality were 0.794 and 0.806, respectively, with a modest improvement for model 2 (ΔAUC: 0.012; P = 0.049). Higher scores were associated with significantly lower 365-day survival (log-rank P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Both Mehran 2 models were associated with renal complications and 1-year mortality in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. The preprocedural model may facilitate early cardiorenal risk stratification, whereas the postprocedural model provides only modest incremental discrimination. Further validation against established mortality risk scores is needed.

Title: Early allograft dysfunction after liver transplant: approach to diagnosis and management.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Early allograft dysfunction (EAD) is one of the most challenging complications following liver transplantation. With the shortage of deceased donor organs, living donor liver transplants are increasing, especially in the Asia Pacific region. With continuously evolving practices and literature, an overview of prevailing EAD definitions (including subtle differences between deceased and living donor-related EAD), donor-specific and recipient-specific risk factors, predictive scoring models, status of biomarkers, and current management practices, has become imperative.
RECENT FINDINGS: Post living donor liver transplantation (LDLT), EAD is a distinct clinicopathological entity from post deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) and is primarily characterized by functional graft insufficiency rather than ischaemia-reperfusion injury (IRI)-mediated necroinflammation of DDLT. A novel preoperative risk score (e-GLR) demonstrates excellent discriminative ability for predicting early graft loss secondary to graft dysfunction in LDLT. In a mixed DDLT-LDLT cohort, acute liver failure (ALF), donor age, and warm ischaemic time (WIT) are the principal determinants of EAD.
SUMMARY: There is also need for individualized risk stratification in EAD, including donor quality, graft volume, recipient disease severity, and intraoperative parameters. The increasing use of marginal grafts owing to organ scarcity has led to increase in its incidence. Preoperative scoring tools such as early graft loss score (e-GLR) can help guide donor-recipient matching and counsel families before live-donor hepatectomy.

Title: Tracheostomy and Home Invasive Ventilation in Severe Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia: A Scoping Review of Indications, Timing, Outcomes and Transitional Care.
Journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
Abstract:
AIM: To map the literature on tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in infants and children with severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), including indications, timing, respiratory outcomes, comorbidities, complications, growth, neurodevelopment, social determinants and transitional care.
METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL/EBSCO from inception to 30 June 2026. Search terms combined BPD or chronic lung disease of prematurity with tracheostomy or tracheotomy. Eligible studies included infants or children with BPD who underwent tracheostomy, received chronic invasive ventilation or were discharged on home mechanical ventilation. Conference abstracts without full-text articles, duplicate precursor abstracts, reviews and editorials were excluded from primary synthesis.
RESULTS: Forty-one studies were included. Evidence was mainly retrospective, including cohorts, administrative database studies, multicentre registries and single-centre observational studies. Tracheostomy was generally considered for persistent invasive ventilation, failed extubation, high respiratory support needs, pulmonary hypertension, airway malacia, growth failure, sedation burden or limited developmental progress. Timing varied widely across centres. Pulmonary hypertension was associated with illness severity and mortality risk, although many children receiving home ventilation improved over time. Among survivors, ventilator liberation and decannulation were common but often occurred over several years. Airway complications, readmissions and operative airway interventions were frequent. Evidence also highlighted centre-level variation, racial and social disparities and limited caregiver-centred data.
CONCLUSIONS: Tracheostomy and home invasive ventilation in severe BPD represent a prolonged care trajectory. Future work should define consensus indications, optimise timing, standardise transitional care and prioritise family-centred and equity-focused outcomes.

Title: Plasma metabolites in early adulthood are associated with midlife cognitive performance and brain tissue integrity in the CARDIA study.
Journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Circulating plasma metabolites may serve as early indicators of midlife cognitive performance, but whether these associations are also reflected in midlife brain structure or white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden remains unclear.
METHODS: In the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study, we examined 575 plasma metabolites in early adulthood (Year 7; age [mean ± SD] 32 ± 3.6 years, N = 1,736) in relation to brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cognitive performance 23 years later (Year 30; age [mean ± SD] 55 ± 3.6 years, N = 646).
RESULTS: Eleven metabolites were independently associated with cognition; five were also associated with total brain volume but none with WMH burden. In mediation analysis, total brain volume accounted for 8%-33% of metabolite-cognition associations.
DISCUSSION: Plasma metabolites measured in early adulthood are associated with midlife cognitive performance and a subset is also associated with total brain volume, whereas no associations were observed with WMH burden, highlighting early-adult metabolic signatures as markers of midlife brain structural health.

Title: A plasma proteomic frailty signature for cardiovascular risk stratification: A multi-cohort study.
Journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty predicts adverse health outcomes, but its relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires further validation across diverse populations. The value of a circulating protein signature for cardiovascular risk assessment remains uncertain.
METHODS: We examined frailty-CVD associations in the XiDu2017 cohort (n = 4323) and UK Biobank (UKB; n = 84,276) using logistic and Cox regression, respectively. XiDu longitudinal analyses included 844 participants without baseline CVD. In the UKB proteomic subset, a 20-protein frailty (PF) score was compared with clinical frailty and a model of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: Each higher frailty category was associated with prevalent CVD in XiDu (adjusted odds ratio, 1.120; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.004-1.251). In UKB, frail participants had a higher CVD hazard than robust participants (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.28-1.48). For heart failure, the 5-year area under the curve (AUC) was 0.756 for PF and 0.595 for clinical frailty. Adding PF to conventional risk factors increased the optimism-corrected heart failure AUC by 0.113 (95% CI, 0.077-0.142).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical frailty was associated with cardiovascular outcomes in both cohorts. PF showed incremental discrimination for selected outcomes, particularly heart failure. External validation and evaluation of clinical utility are needed before clinical application.

Title: Adiposity and glycemic patterns among adults meeting measured cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic stage 1 criteria: a multicohort study.
Journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN guideline defines cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stage 1 by excess or dysfunctional adiposity. Whether adiposity and glycemic patterns distinguish subsequent risk is uncertain.
METHODS: Adults aged 45-79 years meeting measured stage 1 criteria were studied in CHARLS and CHNS. Four patterns combined body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, and prediabetes. Modified Poisson models estimated risk ratios (RRs). Progression and hypertension models used censoring weights; cumulative self-reported cardiovascular disease (CVD) models used baseline-covariate imputation. The nonglycemic composite was a key secondary outcome. NHANES assessed reclassification with ancestry-appropriate thresholds and age-sex standardization. Chinese cohorts lacked albuminuria and subclinical CVD assessment.
RESULTS: In CHARLS (model n = 965), adiposity plus prediabetes was associated with metabolic progression versus prediabetes only (RR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.18-1.61). Corresponding RRs were 1.45 (1.21-1.74) for nonglycemic progression and 1.55 (1.21-1.98) for CHNS hypertension. Among 1824 participants, concordant BMI and waist adiposity was associated with cumulative reported CVD through 2020 (RR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.23-2.71). CVD associations attenuated in complete-case models and after additional adjustment for metabolic measures. Standardized NHANES reclassification ranged from 0.8% to 9.0%.
CONCLUSIONS: Adiposity and glycemic patterns identified prognostic heterogeneity among adults meeting measured CKM stage 1 criteria, supporting joint assessment of these features.

Title: Divergent roles of H3K18 lactylation in human diseases: metabolic-epigenetic circuits and translational challenges.
Abstract: Histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) links fluctuations in lactate metabolism with chromatin-dependent transcription. Promoter- and enhancer-level associations suggest that H3K18la can report local metabolic-chromatin coupling, but evidence for modification-specific causality remains uneven because the known writers and erasers are promiscuous, dedicated readers are poorly defined, and broad acyltransferase inhibitors perturb competing histone and non-histone marks. Across tumor, inflammatory, metabolic, cardiovascular, and degenerative-disease models, H3K18la participates in oncogenic, immunoregulatory, fibrotic, or reparative programs according to cell lineage, chromatin state, metabolic exposure, and disease stage. We synthesize these observations using a testable framework in which lactate and lactyl-CoA provide metabolic permission, whereas transcription factors, chromatin accessibility, histone chaperones, and candidate protein or RNA scaffolds provide locus selection; downstream readers or conventional transcriptional effectors then shape the biological output. Direct long non-coding RNA (lncRNA)-guided deposition and a universally validated H3K18la reader remain unproven. Human cohort data support exploratory, disease-specific associations, but assay heterogeneity and the lack of prospective external validation preclude current clinical use. Progress will require histone H3 lysine 18 acetylation (H3K18ac)-aware, inhibitor-independent causal tests, structural validation of readers, integrated chromatin-RNA profiling, and prospective multicenter cohorts.

Title: Mortality From Chronic Chagas Cardiomyopathy in Brazil: National and Regional Trends, 2000-2023.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy is the main cause of death from Trypanosoma cruzi infection. Nationwide analyses of its mortality in Brazil are either restricted to all forms of Chagas disease or end before 2020, and none has examined the cardiac form separately across regions, sexes, and age groups through 2023.
METHODS: This is a nationwide ecological time-trend study of all deaths registered in the Brazilian Mortality Information System with chronic Chagas disease with heart involvement (ICD-10 B57.2) as the underlying cause, 2000-2023. Age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR, direct method, Brazilian 2022 population as standard) were calculated for Brazil, its five macroregions, and each sex. Trends were estimated as annual percent change (APC) from age-adjusted quasi-Poisson regression and by joinpoint regression of the annual ASMR series, with the average APC (AAPC) for 2000-2023; sensitivity analyses used the World Health Organization (WHO) standard population and restricted windows (2006-2023; 2000-2019).
RESULTS: Eighty-nine thousand seventy-nine deaths were attributed to B57.2 in 2000-2023 (56.1% male; 68.3% aged ≥60 years). The national ASMR fell from 4.06 (95% confidence interval (CI) 3.94-4.18) to 1.29 (1.24-1.34) per 100,000 population between 2000 and 2023 (-68%), with an AAPC of -4.7% (95% CI -4.9 to -4.5) and a single joinpoint in 2020, after which the decline accelerated (APC -6.9%, -8.7 to -5.2). Rates fell in all macroregions (APC from -2.6% in the Northeast to -6.5% in the South) and in both sexes (men -5.1%, women -3.9%), yet the Central-West retained an ASMR 3.5 times the national value in 2020-2023 (5.18 vs 1.49 per 100,000). The decline was steepest below 40 years of age (APC -9.9%) and negligible at ≥80 years (-0.5%, -0.7 to -0.2), in whom the rate remained above 20 per 100,000.
CONCLUSIONS: Mortality attributed to chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy in Brazil has declined by about two-thirds since 2000, in every region and both sexes. The age pattern is consistent with the aging and extinction of cohorts infected before vector control rather than with improved survival of established cardiomyopathy, although this ecological design cannot separate age, period, and cohort effects; deaths are now concentrated in elderly residents of historically endemic areas, particularly the Central-West.

Title: Peripheral Nerve Alterations in Jawbone Cavitations: Histopathological Findings from a Retrospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatty degenerative osteonecrosis of the jawbone (FDOJ), also referred to as jawbone cavitations or bone marrow defects (BMD), is characterized by ischemic fatty degeneration, impaired bone remodeling, and chronic overexpression of inflammatory mediators, particularly the chemokine RANTES/CCL5. Emerging clinical observations suggest that FDOJ/Cavitations may exert systemic effects through neuroimmunological mechanisms, potentially influencing autonomic nervous system (ANS) regulation and cardiovascular function.
OBJECTIVE: This retrospective observational study explored whether postoperative patient-reported improvement in cardiovascular or autonomic symptoms was documented in a subset of patients following surgical debridement of FDOJ/Cavitations, while primarily characterizing histopathological evidence of peripheral nerve involvement in these lesions.
METHODS: In a retrospective cohort, 16 patients reported subjective improvement in cardiovascular symptoms and ANS symptoms following surgical debridement of FDOJ/Cavitations. However, these outcomes were based on non-standardized patient self-reports without systematic cardiological evaluation.
RESULTS: In an analysis of 1,958 histological reports from patients who had undergone FDOJ/cavitation surgery, collected between 2008 and 2020 at a surgical center in Munich, Germany, these findings revealed the presence of scar-associated nerves in 84 cases (=4%). From this cohort, 31 patients (age 53-81 years) were selected for further detailed evaluation based on consistent neural alterations within the lesions. In all 31 FDOJ/Cavitation samples, histological analysis revealed pathological alterations of peripheral nerves, including perineural fibrosis, irregular axonal sprouting, accessory or aberrant nerve formations, and scar neuromas. Conventional radiographic methods often failed to detect FDOJ/Cavitations, whereas trans alveolar ultrasound sonography showed higher diagnostic sensitivity.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that peripheral nerve alterations may represent a relevant component of the pathology of FDOJ/Cavitations and raise the hypothesis of potential neuroimmune-autonomic interactions. Due to methodological limitations, the observations remain hypothesis-generating and require confirmation through prospective interdisciplinary studies with objective cardiovascular and autonomic assessments.

Title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography for the Detection of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy in Athletes: A Systematic Review of Diagnostic Accuracy and External Validity.
Abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a clinically important inherited myocardial disorder in sports cardiology because affected athletes may remain asymptomatic while being at risk of ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac events. Cardiovascular screening, therefore, requires the identification of occult HCM while distinguishing pathological disease from physiological adaptations to training. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and external validity of artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography (AI-ECG) for detecting HCM in athletes and sports-screening populations. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science Science Citation Index Expanded, Europe PMC, IEEE Xplore, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP were searched from inception through June 2026, supplemented by reference lists and citation searching. The original June 2026 records formed the authoritative review corpus; no later search update was incorporated. Eligible studies evaluated AI or machine learning applied to ECG for the detection of current HCM in athletes against an imaging-supported reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. The searches identified 1,024 database and registry records. After the removal of 321 duplicate occurrences and the addition of 18 records identified through supplementary methods, 721 records were screened, and 58 reports underwent full-text assessment. Fifty-six reports were excluded, one directly relevant study was ongoing without available results, and one published report was included in the qualitative synthesis. The included study evaluated 845 collegiate or professional athletes, of whom 99 underwent echocardiography, and one was identified as having HCM. AI-ECG-derived HCM probability was not significantly associated with echocardiographically verified HCM status (r = 0.173, p = 0.086). No prespecified HCM positivity threshold, HCM-specific sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, or participant-level 2 × 2 diagnostic data were reported, and no study met the prespecified criteria for quantitative synthesis. Athlete-specific evidence, therefore, remains insufficient to establish the diagnostic accuracy of AI-ECG for HCM or to support its use as a stand-alone rule-in or rule-out screening test. Prospective, participant-independent, imaging-verified external validation in representative athlete cohorts, particularly studies designed to distinguish pathological HCM from physiological athlete's heart, is required before AI-ECG can be considered a validated component of pre-participation cardiovascular screening.

Title: The Gut Microbiota-Associated Metabolite Network in Ischemic Stroke: From Pathophysiological Imbalance to Potential Precision Intervention Strategies.
Abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains a leading cause of death and long-term neurological disability worldwide, and current treatment options are constrained by narrow therapeutic windows and limited neuroprotective efficacy. Accumulating evidence implicates the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) in the development and progression of IS. Following cerebral ischemia, bidirectional communication between the brain and gut is disrupted, resulting in gut microbial dysbiosis, impaired intestinal barrier function, and altered production of microbiota-associated metabolites that influence neuroinflammation, immune regulation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and post-stroke recovery. Among these molecules, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), bile acids (BAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) have attracted particular attention. Importantly, these molecules differ in origin: SCFAs and several tryptophan-derived indoles are direct microbial products; TMAO is a host-microbial co-metabolite; primary BAs are host-derived and subsequently modified by gut bacteria; and LPS is a bacterial structural component. Rather than acting in isolation, these metabolites form an interconnected network characterized by synergistic, antagonistic, compensatory, and feedback interactions; however, only a subset of these interactions has been directly demonstrated in patients with IS or in experimental stroke models, and many remain inferred from studies in other cardiovascular, metabolic, or inflammatory conditions. At present, the strongest human evidence concerns associations of individual metabolites with stroke risk and outcomes, whereas the proposed network-level interactions remain largely inferential. This review therefore proposes "gut microbiota-associated metabolite network imbalance" as a conceptual, integrative, and hypothesis-generating framework for understanding IS pathophysiology, and summarizes current evidence on protective and injurious metabolite pathways, their crosstalk, and emerging therapeutic strategies. Metabolite-guided precision intervention remains largely investigational and will require prospective validation before clinical translation.

Title: Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio and Preoperative Acute Heart Failure in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients with Chronic Cerebrovascular Diseases.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), calculated using admission blood glucose (ABG) and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), remains unclear in the context of perioperative complications associated with hip fractures. This study evaluates the association and predictive capability of the SHR for preoperative acute heart failure in hip fracture patients with chronic cerebrovascular disease.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 515 patients were analyzed, revealing a 16.8% incidence of preoperative HF. Significant intergroup differences in age (P < 0.001), ASA classification (P < 0.001), coronary heart disease (P=0.025), serum albumin level (P < 0.001), and admission SHR (P=0.033) were identified between patients with and without preoperative heart failure. Logistic regression identified SHR, CHD, ASA, neutrophils, and hypoproteinemia as independent predictors of preoperative HF, leading to the development of a nomogram that demonstrated good predictive performance (AUC 0.72). Calibration curves and decision curve analysis indicated the model's clinical utility. Machine learning algorithms, especially the XGBoost model, surpassed traditional models by achieving an AUC of 0.787, demonstrating excellent calibration and clinical applicability. SHAP analysis validated the stable contribution of SHR in risk prediction.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the SHR's strong predictive ability for preoperative HF in hip fracture patients with chronic cerebrovascular disease. The XGBoost machine learning model could improve risk stratification and clinical decision-making for this at-risk group.

Title: Saroglitazar Facilitates Insulin De-escalation and Improves Metabolic Parameters in Pioglitazone-Ineligible Non-metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) Type 2 Diabetes: Real-World Evidence From India.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major global health burden, particularly in India. Pioglitazone is an established thiazolidinedione insulin sensitizer. It is contraindicated in heart failure and is clinically unsuitable for many patients with edema, osteoporosis, or bladder cancer risk, creating a therapeutic gap. Saroglitazar, a dual peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-α/γ agonist approved in India for T2DM, diabetic dyslipidemia, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), has insulin-sensitizing properties, but evidence in non-MASLD T2DM patients remains limited.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, real-world study analyzed the medical records of adults with T2DM who were deemed ineligible for pioglitazone and were initiated on saroglitazar 4 mg once daily as add-on therapy between June 2025 and March 2026. All consecutive eligible patients with documented follow-up at approximately 12 and 24 weeks were included (n = 60). Data on demographics, comorbidities, concomitant antidiabetic therapy and its modifications, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting and postprandial blood glucose (FBG, PPBG), lipid profile, liver enzymes, serum creatinine, body weight, and adverse events were extracted from outpatient case records, electronic medical records, and laboratory reports using a standardized data collection form. Changes from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks were assessed using two-tailed paired t-tests with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Mean age was 56.15 ± 11.27 years, and 58.3% were female. HbA1c decreased significantly from 9.42 ± 1.53% at baseline to 8.21 ± 1.16% at 12 weeks and 7.06 ± 0.69% at 24 weeks (P < 0.001). Significant improvements occurred in FBG and PPBG, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol (TC), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) (all P < 0.001). Liver enzymes and serum creatinine stayed within normal ranges, and body weight remained stable. Dose reduction or discontinuation of concomitant antihyperglycemic therapy occurred in 36.7% of patients; among the 12 insulin-treated patients, insulin was discontinued in eight (66.7%) and down-titrated in 2 (16.7%) (combined, 83.3%). No documented adverse events were identified in the retrospective records.
CONCLUSION: Saroglitazar was associated with significant improvements in glycemic and lipid parameters without weight gain in non-MASLD T2DM patients ineligible for pioglitazone. Given the uncontrolled retrospective design and concurrent modification of background antihyperglycemic therapy, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective evaluation of saroglitazar as an insulin-sensitizing option in this population.

Title: Trends in acute myocardial infarction mortality with diabetes mellitus as a contributing cause of death in the United States, 1999-2025, with forecasts through 2030 and exploratory projections for 2031-2040.
Journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with increased mortality. Despite substantial advances in the management of both conditions, the population-level mortality burden involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate national trends and disparities in mortality involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2025 using CDC WONDER data, forecasts were generated through 2030, with exploratory projections extending through 2040, stratified by DM type, age, sex, and race and ethnicity.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of U.S. national mortality data from 1999 to 2025 was conducted to identify deaths among adults aged ≥ 25 years in which AMI; ICD-10 code I21 was the underlying cause and DM; ICD-10 codes E10-E14 was a contributing cause. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and crude mortality rates (CMRs) were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Time-series methods were used to forecast mortality through 2030, with exploratory projections through 2040 .
RESULTS: Trend analyses were conducted using observed mortality data from 1999 to 2025, whereas projections extended from 2026 to 2040. A total of 762,802 deaths were attributed to AMI, with DM documented as a contributing cause, among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2025. Overall mortality significantly declined (AAMR: 18.9 to 9.16; AAPC: -3.05; 95% CI: -3.3 to -2.9; P < 0.001). Males showed higher AAMRs (23.32 in 1999 to 12.72 in 2025) when compared to females (15.74 to 6.2). Older adults aged ≥ 65 years carried the greatest mortality burden, with CMR decreasing from 72.9 in 1999 to 32.4 in 2025. NH Blacks had the highest AAMR (29.95 to 12.68). Forecasts projected a decline in overall AAMR from 8.17 in 2026 to 6.72 in 2030. Exploratory projections suggested a further decline to 3.08 by 2040, although substantial uncertainty surrounded these long-term estimates. The AAMR for deaths involving AMI as the underlying cause and T2DM as a contributing cause increased from 3.34 in 1999 to 4.15 in 2025, whereas the corresponding AAMR for T1DM decreased from 1.90 to 0.23.
CONCLUSION: Mortality involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause has significantly declined and is projected to continue declining through 2040. Disparities among males, NH Blacks and older adults require refined strategies to improve outcomes.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02124-x.

Title: Dietary potassium intake from different food sources and mortality in maintenance haemodialysis patients: a multicentre prospective cohort study.
Abstract: The association between dietary potassium intake and mortality in maintenance haemodialysis (MHD) patients remains controversial, particularly regarding potassium from different dietary sources. In this multicentre prospective cohort study, dietary potassium intake was assessed using 24-hour dietary recalls. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate associations with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response relationships, and sensitivity analyses included adjustment for dietary quality indicators, exclusion of serum potassium, exclusion of deaths within the first year, and competing-risk models. The lowest tertile of total dietary potassium intake was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1·36, 95 % CI: 1·02-1·81). The lowest tertile of plant-based potassium intake was associated with increased all-cause mortality (aHR: 1·54, 95% CI: 1·19-1·99) and cardiovascular mortality (aHR: 1·50, 95% CI: 1·05-2·14). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated inverse dose-response relationships between total dietary potassium intake and both mortality outcomes and between plant-based potassium intake and all-cause mortality. Dietary potassium intake was not associated with serum potassium levels or hyperkalaemia risk, whereas severe hyperkalaemia (serum potassium ≥6·0 mmol/L) independently predicted cardiovascular mortality (aHR: 1·59, 95% CI: 1·06-2·38). Lower dietary potassium intake, particularly from plant sources, was associated with increased mortality risk among MHD patients. These findings support a more individualised approach to dietary potassium management in MHD patients.

Title: Preventive cardiovascular ultrasound imaging: a strategy for lifelong atherosclerosis control.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atherosclerosis develops silently over decades before manifesting as myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular (CV) death. Carotid and femoral ultrasound can identify subclinical atherosclerosis SA), quantify plaque burden, and refine cardiovascular risk assessment beyond traditional risk factors.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from population-based cohorts, longitudinal studies, clinical trials, and imaging investigations from 1987-2026 identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Carotid and femoral plaque prevalence, associated risk factors, vulnerability, natural history, prediction of CV events across the lifespan, serial ultrasound assessment of plaque progression and regression, including responses to lifestyle modification and lipid-lowering therapy are discussed. Comparisons with other imaging modalities and the importance of primordial prevention to reduce cumulative exposure to CV risk factors are addressed.
EXPERT OPINION: Carotid and femoral plaque ultrasound offers a practical, accessible, radiation-free approach to detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and supporting individualized prevention. Plaque assessment may inform risk discussions, reinforce lifestyle changes, and improve adherence to appropriate lipid-lowering therapy. Standardized acquisition, reproducible measurements, and validated thresholds are needed for broader implementation. Prospective trials should establish whether ultrasound-guided prevention improves clinical outcomes. Integrating plaque imaging with sustained risk factor control and primordial prevention may help reduce the lifetime burden of atherosclerotic CV disease.

Title: Dynamic machine learning models for the early prediction of acute kidney injury following left ventricular assist device implantation: An explainable AI approach.
Journal: The International journal of artificial organs
Abstract: The risk of developing acute kidney injury (AKI) following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation is high, making its prediction essential. Current tools are limited by relying on static, preoperative data and "black-box" models. Our aim was to create a transparent prediction tool for AKI that integrates dynamic postoperative laboratory results with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). In a cohort of 138 LVAD patients, AKI was defined using KDIGO criteria within 7 days post-surgery. We evaluated LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost models, using the SMOTE method to manage class imbalance within a stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The LASSO model achieved the best performance with a ROC-AUC of 0.755. SHAP analysis revealed that dynamic postoperative laboratory changes were as important as baseline renal function in predicting AKI. Using risk scores calculated 48 h post-surgery, the model successfully predicted whether day 7 AKI would be "persistent" or "transient." Accurately predicting post-LVAD AKI is feasible using an interpretable machine learning model that tracks dynamic data. This approach can serve as a reliable tool for early risk assessment, enabling physicians to identify high-risk patients earlier and implement proactive interventions.

Title: Plasma CAF22, a Biomarker of Neuromuscular Junction Integrity, is Associated with Risk and Earlier Onset of Statin-Associated Muscle Symptoms.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statin-associated muscle symptoms (SAMS) are a major limitation to effective lipid-lowering therapy. C-terminal agrin fragment 22 (CAF22) is a biomarker of neuromuscular junction degradation, but its role in predicting SAMS remains unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 383 adults aged 40-60 years initiating statin therapy were followed for 12 months. Baseline plasma CAF22 was measured prior to statin initiation. Statin intolerance was defined as clinically significant muscle symptoms leading to dose modification, discontinuation, or switching. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations with the occurrence and timing of statin intolerance, respectively.
RESULTS: Statin intolerance occurred in 17% of participants. Higher baseline CAF22 was associated with increased odds of statin intolerance (adjusted OR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.08-1.61, p = 0.006) and earlier onset (adjusted HR: 1.38, 95% CI: 1.15-1.63, p < 0.001). The association was consistent across unadjusted and age- and sex-adjusted models. Higher handgrip strength was associated with reduced odds (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.97, p = 0.018) and delayed onset (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.95, p = 0.011) of intolerance. Diabetes mellitus was independently associated with both increased odds and earlier onset, while lipophilic and high-intensity statin use were associated with earlier intolerance. Other demographic and biochemical variables were not significant predictors.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CAF22 is independently associated with the risk and timing of statin intolerance. These findings support a role for neuromuscular junction integrity in SAMS and suggest that CAF22 may represent a potential biomarker of vulnerability.

Title: Arterial thrombosis redirects the natural history of myeloproliferative neoplasms: A biological perspective.
Abstract: We reviewed the emerging clinical and biological evidence that supports the broader interpretation of arterial thrombosis as a biological turning point that identifies patients who are entering a more aggressive phase of classic myeloproliferative neoplasms. Findings from multistate analyses, international registry studies, nested case-control investigations, and recent translational research were integrated. We showed that arterial thrombosis is associated not only with recurrent vascular events but also with increased mortality, progression to myelofibrosis and blast phase, and, in selected patient populations, the subsequent development of solid cancers. We discuss the biological mechanisms that may underlie these associations, including persistent JAK2-driven inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, immune remodelling, and clonal evolution. Particular attention is given to emerging biomarkers, such as JAK2V617F variant allele frequency and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, which provide complementary information on clonal burden and inflammatory activity and may improve biological risk stratification. Finally, we discuss the clinical implications of this evolving paradigm, proposing that patients experiencing arterial thrombosis should undergo closer surveillance and be considered for biology-directed therapeutic strategies aimed at suppressing both clonal expansion and chronic thrombo-inflammation, rather than receiving secondary vascular prevention alone.

Title: Associations of PM2.5 Exposure and Solid Fuel Use With Incident Stroke: Evidence From a Longitudinal Chinese Cohort.
Journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outdoor and indoor air pollution often co-occur and may exert combined health effects, but their combined effect on incident stroke risk remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of ambient particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure and solid fuel use with incident stroke among Chinese middle-aged and elderly adults.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. One-year pre-baseline county-level PM2.5 exposure was assigned using the China High Air Pollutants dataset, and household solid fuel use was assessed at baseline according to participants' primary cooking and heating fuels. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for prespecified covariates were used to estimate the independent and joint associations of PM2.5 exposure and solid fuel use with incident stroke. The overall trend across combined exposure categories was evaluated using ordinal exposure scores.
RESULTS: Of 13,917 adults with a mean age of 58.90 years, 1,060 developed incident stroke during follow-up. Solid fuel users had a higher risk of incident stroke than nonusers [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.38, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.18-1.62]. High PM2.5 exposure was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke (HR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.04-1.51). The multiplicative interaction of PM2.5 exposure and solid fuel use was observed (P for interaction = 0.022). An overall positive trend was observed between the combined exposure to PM2.5 and solid fuel use and incident stroke (HR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.05-1.15, P for trend < 0.001). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed generally consistent patterns across sex, residence, and comorbidity status.
CONCLUSION: Combined exposure to ambient PM2.5 and household solid fuel use was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke, with a generally increasing pattern across combined exposure categories. These findings suggest that both indoor and outdoor air pollution should be considered in public health strategies for stroke prevention.

Title: Risk factors for the recurrence of chronic subdural hematomas in patients undergoing burr-hole drainage.
Abstract: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is a common neurosurgical disease, particularly in the elderly. The recurrence of cSDH remains a clinical challenge, with several risk factors postulated. Although adjunctive treatments to surgery exist, such as steroids, statins, and middle meningeal artery embolization, the number needed to treat is high, and patient selection remains unclear. This retrospective study aimed to identify risk factors for recurrence after burr hole drainage of cSDH. A single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients undergoing burr-hole drainage for cSDH between February 2012 and May 2023. The primary outcome was surgical recurrence, defined as cSDH recurrence requiring reoperation within six months. Clinical characteristics, preoperative radiological findings, comorbidities and medications, and postoperative findings were assessed as potential risk factors using univariate analysis and, after imputation, multivariable analysis.A total of 766 patients with a recurrence rate of 11.2% (86/766) were included. Significant preoperative risk factors for recurrence included subacute and separated hematoma types (p = 0.02), larger hematoma volume (p = 0.004), greater midline shift (MLS) (p = 0.006), lower Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) (p < 0.001) and higher Markwalder score (p = 0.012). Postoperative findings significantly associated with recurrence were larger cavity volume (p = 0.005), greater MLS (p = 0.01), a higher Markwalder score (p = 0.01) and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score (p < 0.001) at discharge. After multivariable logistic regression, subacute hematoma age (OR 2.097, p = 0.036), absence of hypertension (OR 1.937, p = 0.012), larger postoperative cavity volume (OR 1.012, p = 0.016), greater postoperative MLS (OR 1.179, p < 0.001), and higher mRS at discharge (OR 1.959, p = 0.002) remained independently associated with recurrence. We found subacute hematoma, larger postoperative subdural cavity volume, higher mRS at discharge, greater postoperative MLS, and the absence of hypertension as factors significantly associated with surgical recurrence within six months.

Title: Study protocol for Rule-Out Acute Myocardial Infarction Using Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiogram 2 (ROMIAE-2) in patients with chest pain: a multicenter randomized noninferiority trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) requires rapid identification in the emergency department (ED). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation systems have shown strong diagnostic accuracy, no multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) has evaluated their clinical impact. This protocol describes a RCT for assessing whether real-time AI-ECG can be safely integrated into routine emergency care for undifferentiated chest pain.
METHODS: ROMIAE-2 is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication conducted at 12 academic tertiary EDs in South Korea. A total of 4,670 adults with acute chest pain will be randomized 1:1 to AI-ECG-guided or standard care. In the intervention arm, a deep learning algorithm (AiTiAMI Ver 2.00.00) will analyze the initial 12- lead ECG and generate an AMI probability score, which is combined with the HEART score to classify patients into four integrated risk categories for clinical decision-making. The primary outcome is 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), assessed using a noninferiority framework with a 3.0% margin. The trial will be powered at 80% with a onesided significance level of 0.025. Secondary outcomes include missed AMI at the index visit, ED length of stay, early discharge, 7-day ED revisit, hospital admission, hospital length of stay, AI-ECG diagnostic performance, additional testing, and direct medical costs. Clinical endpoints, including MACE and AMI, will be adjudicated by two emergency medicine specialists blinded to the group allocation.
DISCUSSION: ROMIAE-2 will provide randomized evidence on whether integrating AI-ECG into routine emergency care can preserve patient safety while improving efficiency in patients with undifferentiated chest pain.

Title: Hemodynamic effects of semaglutide in individuals with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial.
Abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide improves symptoms in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) through unclear mechanisms. Here, in this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 81 patients (47 women) with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) or placebo for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in invasively measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), a direct measure of cardiac congestion, during low-intensity exercise. Additional mechanistic outcomes included other hemodynamic measures and hemodynamic HFpEF remission (defined as normal PAWP under conditions of both rest and exercise at 52 weeks). At baseline, PAWP was 17.5 ± 4.3 mmHg at rest and 31.7 ± 5.2 mmHg during exercise. After 52 weeks, the mean change in PAWP during exercise was -9.8 (95% confidence interval (CI): -11.3 to -8.2) mmHg with semaglutide and +0.9 (95% CI: -1.3 to 3.0) mmHg with placebo (estimated difference, -10.6 mmHg; 95% CI: -13.3 to -8.0; P < 0.0001). As compared to placebo, semaglutide also decreased resting PAWP (estimated difference, -7.1 mmHg; 95% CI: -9.8 to -4.4; P < 0.0001), and semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission (53.7% versus 7.4%, odds ratio = 14.1, 95% CI: 3.0-134.6, P < 0.001). The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05371496 .

Title: URBANOME: an exposome-based framework linking urban interventions to molecular, health, and policy-relevant outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urban environments expose residents to multiple simultaneous stressors that often act synergistically (e.g., air pollution and extreme heat amplifying cardiovascular and respiratory risks), contributing to a substantial public health burden. Environmental factors account for an estimated 13% of all deaths in the European Union, with ambient air pollution alone responsible for approximately 400,000 premature deaths per year. Most of this burden is mediated through chronic non-communicable diseases, including cardiovascular disease, stroke, cancer, respiratory disease, and mental health outcomes. Because these conditions are shaped by interacting environmental, social, and lifestyle determinants, traditional single-hazard approaches are insufficient, motivating adoption of an exposome paradigm.
OBJECTIVE: This paper presents the URBANOME methodological framework, an integrated exposome-based architecture for evaluating urban interventions across external exposures, internal biological responses, functional health outcomes, and policy-relevant indicators, and reports illustrative pilot findings from its first multi-site implementation.
METHODS: In a four-year Horizon 2020 study across nine European cities (Aarhus, Aberdeen, Athens, Ljubljana, Madrid, Milan, Montpellier, Stuttgart, and Thessaloniki), URBANOME implemented an integrated exposome framework through Urban Living Labs (ULLs). Co-created interventions (combining active mobility, urban greening, and traffic calming) were evaluated using a before-after design. Methods included ambient and personal exposure monitoring (wearable sensors, smartphone applications), agent-based population exposure modeling, validated health and well-being questionnaires, objective clinical measures (spirometry, blood pressure, heart rate variability), and multi-omics analyses (untargeted metabolomics and transcriptomics) on biological samples. A cost-benefit analysis quantified the economic return of interventions.
RESULTS: The framework was successfully implemented across the nine ULLs, although intervention type, comparator availability, sample size, and follow-up duration varied by site (Table 1). Across paired participants, self-reported air-pollution annoyance and sleep-related breathing problems decreased between baseline and follow-up assessments, and pollution-related differences in forced vital capacity (FVC) were attenuated in higher-exposure neighbourhoods. In an exploratory pilot omics sub-cohort with paired pre/post samples, a four-metabolite panel (L-tyrosine, ascorbic acid, choline, coenzyme Q10) showed apparent perfect internal separation of pre- and post-intervention samples (apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC ≈ 1.0); given the small sample size and absence of an independent held-out validation set, this result is preliminary and likely overoptimistic, and must be interpreted as a hypothesis-generating finding requiring external validation. Exploratory exposome-lifestyle analyses suggested that co-exposure to poor diet and higher pollution was associated with greater oxidative-stress-related metabolic signals, while combined healthy environments and lifestyles were associated with anti-inflammatory metabolite profiles. An exploratory cost-benefit analysis, based on value-transfer assumptions and standard health-economic unit costs, estimated benefit-cost ratios in the range of approximately €19-€143 per €1 invested across heterogeneous interventions; this range reflects substantial between-site variability and the assumptions detailed in the Methods, and should be interpreted as illustrative rather than as a precise return-on-investment estimate.
CONCLUSIONS: This paper presents the URBANOME exposome-based evaluation framework and reports illustrative pilot findings from its multi-site implementation. The framework is feasible to deploy across heterogeneous European urban contexts and links external exposure assessment, internal biological profiling, functional health outcomes, and economic appraisal within a single architecture. Observed pre/post changes in self-reported, functional, and molecular endpoints are consistent with potentially beneficial responses to bundled urban interventions, but should be considered preliminary given the heterogeneous before-after design, variable comparator availability, small omics sub-cohorts, and short follow-up. External validation of the candidate biomarker panel and replication in independent settings are required before the framework's outputs can support firm conclusions about intervention effectiveness or cost-effectiveness.

Title: The effect of tilt-table robot-assisted training on functional outcomes in people with stroke and sarcopenia: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared changes in physical function following tilt-table robot-assisted training between stroke patients with and without sarcopenia. The aim was to investigate whether sarcopenia influences functional recovery during rehabilitation.
METHODS: A total of 74 stroke patients who received tilt-table robot-assisted training at Gwangju G Rehabilitation Hospital between July 2022 and June 2024 were included. Participants were classified into sarcopenia (SRG, n = 45) and non-sarcopenia (NSRG, n = 29) groups according to the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. All participants underwent a 4-week tilt-table robot-assisted training program combined with the hospital's standard multidisciplinary convalescent rehabilitation program. Functional outcomes, including muscle strength (MMT), balance (BBS), gait (FAC), and activities of daily living (K-MBI), were assessed before and after the intervention. Within-group and between-group comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Mann-Whitney U test, respectively. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with post-intervention functional outcomes.
RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvements in muscle strength, balance, gait, and activities of daily living following the intervention (all p < .05). Participants without sarcopenia demonstrated significantly greater improvements in balance and activities of daily living than those with sarcopenia (both p < .05), whereas no between-group differences were observed for muscle strength or gait. Multivariable regression analysis demonstrated that sarcopenia remained independently associated with lower post-intervention K-MBI scores after adjustment for age, sex, baseline cognition, and baseline functional status.
CONCLUSIONS: Both groups demonstrated significant functional improvements during the intervention period. Although participants with sarcopenia showed relatively smaller improvements in balance and activities of daily living, they also achieved meaningful functional gains.
