These findings suggest that individualized rehabilitation strategies may be particularly important for stroke patients with sarcopenia. Further controlled prospective studies are needed to clarify the independent effects of tilt-table robot-assisted training.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial was approved by the Public Institutional Review Board of the Ministry of Health and Welfare (P01-202411-01-011) and registered in the Clinical Research Information Service of Korea (KCT0010038).

Title: Comparative associations of six dietary pattern indices with mortality among U.S. adults with sarcopenia: a nationally representative cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary patterns may influence survival among individuals with sarcopenia, but evidence comparing different dietary indices remains limited. This study examined the associations of six commonly used dietary pattern indices with all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality among U.S. adults with sarcopenia.
METHODS: This nationally representative cohort study included 1,774 adults with sarcopenia from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with linked mortality data. Sarcopenia was defined according to the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health criteria using DXA-derived appendicular skeletal muscle mass adjusted for body mass index. Dietary patterns were assessed using the alternate Mediterranean diet score (aMED), Healthy Eating Index-2020 (HEI-2020), Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension score (DASH), Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI), Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII), and Ketogenic Diet Ratio (KDR). Survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate associations with mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess dose-response patterns. False discovery rate correction and multiple sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate robustness.
RESULTS: Among 1,774 adults with sarcopenia, 545 all-cause deaths and 183 cardiovascular deaths occurred during follow-up. In fully adjusted survey-weighted Cox models, compared with the lowest quartile, higher aMED adherence was associated with lower all-cause mortality in Q3 (HR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.37-0.87) and Q4 (HR = 0.60, 95% CI: 0.39-0.92). Similar but less robust inverse associations were observed for PHDI in Q3 (HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.54-0.93) and Q4 (HR = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.54-0.89), whereas the highest DASH quartile showed a weaker inverse association (HR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97). HEI-2020, DII, and KDR did not show robust associations with all-cause mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested a nonlinear association for aMED and an overall association for DASH, whereas the spline-based overall association for PHDI was not statistically significant. After FDR correction based on spline overall tests, the associations for aMED and DASH remained statistically significant, whereas the PHDI finding was attenuated. No consistent associations with cardiovascular mortality were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In U.S. adults with sarcopenia, aMED showed the most consistent inverse association with all-cause mortality, with evidence suggesting a nonlinear dose-response pattern. DASH showed weaker supportive evidence based on spline analyses, whereas PHDI should be interpreted as exploratory after accounting for spline-based multiple testing. These findings support the potential relevance of dietary pattern quality, particularly Mediterranean-style adherence, in sarcopenia, while cause-specific mortality findings require cautious interpretation.

Title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and cardiorenal outcomes in type 2 diabetes with CKD stages 2-4: a target trial emulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) face compounded cardiorenal risk. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits in randomized trials, yet real-world evidence in populations with established CKD stages 2 through 4 remains limited. We aimed to compare cardiorenal outcomes between new users of GLP-1 RAs and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i) in this high-risk population.
METHODS: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a new-user, active-comparator cohort study emulating a target trial. Adults with T2DM and CKD stages 2-4 who initiated GLP-1 RA or DPP-4i between January 2017 and December 2021 were identified. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 40 covariates, 28,824 patients per group were retained. Three co-primary outcomes-MAKE, MACE, and all-cause mortality-were assessed at 1, 2, and 3 years from the same matched cohort. Secondary outcomes included a safety composite and hypoglycemia. Conjunctivitis served as a negative control outcome. Restricted mean survival time was calculated as a supplementary analysis.
RESULTS: At 3 years, GLP-1 RA initiation was associated with significantly lower risks of MAKE (hazard ratio [HR] 0.837; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.796-0.880; P < .001), MACE (HR 0.875; 95% CI 0.843-0.909; P < .001), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.787; 95% CI 0.743-0.834; P < .001) compared with DPP-4i. These associations were evident at 1 year and persisted through 3 years. The safety composite favored GLP-1 RAs (HR 0.905; 95% CI 0.877-0.934; P < .001), with comparable hypoglycemia rates between groups. The negative control outcome yielded null results (HR 0.959; 95% CI 0.865-1.065; P = .436), supporting the validity of the study design.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large, propensity score-matched, international real-world cohort, GLP-1 RA initiation was associated with significantly lower risks of adverse kidney events, cardiovascular events, and mortality compared with DPP-4i in patients with T2DM and CKD stages 2 through 4. Benefits emerged early and persisted over 3 years, providing supportive evidence for GLP-1 RAs to a population underrepresented in randomized trials.

Title: Reproductive factors and mortality risk: insights from the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study (TLGS).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While reproductive history is recognized as a determinant of women's long-term health, its impact on mortality risk remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to elucidate the association between key reproductive factors and subsequent all-cause and cause-specific mortality within the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study (TLGS) population.
METHODS: We analyzed data from a prospective cohort of 5,165 women (aged ≥ 20 years) with a history of at least one pregnancy. Associations between reproductive factors and mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression models, adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, education, physical activity levels, diabetes history, hypertension history, and dyslipidemia.
RESULTS: Over the follow-up period, 497 deaths were recorded, representing 9.6% of participants; 168 deaths were due to cardiovascular disease (CVD) and 96 to cancer, accounting for 33.8% and 19.4% of all deaths, respectively. Late menarche was associated with increased all-cause and cancer-related mortality, with adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.52 and 2.04, respectively. Recurrent abortion was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR = 1.41; 95% CI: 1.12-1.77). Women with parity ≥ 3 had higher risks of all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer-related mortality compared with those with parity 1-2.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive characteristics, particularly late menarche, recurrent abortion, and high parity, were associated with increased long-term mortality risk. These findings support further investigation of reproductive characteristics as potential markers of long-term mortality risk.

Title: Construction and internal validation of a predictive model for risk of severe gastrointestinal involvement in children with IgA vasculitis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of the severity of gastrointestinal (GI) involvement in children with IgA vasculitis (IgAV) is crucial for prognosis assessment and formulation of treatment plans. This study aimed to develop a risk predictive model for severe GI involvement in pediatric IgAV to assist clinicians in decision-making.
METHOD: In a single-center retrospective cohort study, 293 eligible children were divided into two cohorts based on the time of admission: a training set and a validation set. Candidate risk indicators were identified using binary logistic regression, and a predictive model was developed to predict severe GI involvement in pediatric IgAV based on training set. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was utilized as a tool to evaluate the performance of the logistic regression model. Furthermore, a nomogram model was developed, and its calibration curve was visualized using a 1000-time bootstrap resampling method. The validity of these results was verified on an independent validation set.
RESULTS: Vomiting, lymphocyte count, C-reactive protein and thickening of intestinal wall displayed on abdominal ultrasound were identified as the potentially predictors for severe GI involvement in pediatric IgAV. The predictive model had area under the ROC curve of 0.816 and 0.802 in the training and validation set, with a sensitivity and specificity of 80.0% and 72.4%, 82.8% and 69.8%, respectively. The calibration curve demonstrated favorable predictive accuracy of the predictive model. Decision curve analysis indicated that the predictive model possesses clinical applicability.
CONCLUSIONS: Our research has identified potentially predictive indicators for severe GI involvement in children with IgAV. The risk prediction model we established can assist pediatricians in early prediction and identification of high-risk children, especially those at high risk of severe GI bleeding.

Title: Echocardiography-led multimodal assessment for pulmonary hypertension in a right heart catheterization-referred cohort: incremental value of ECG and natriuretic peptides.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right heart catheterization (RHC) is the reference standard for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), whereas echocardiography is the primary noninvasive tool for identifying patients who require further evaluation. Whether electrocardiography (ECG) and natriuretic peptides provide incremental diagnostic information beyond echocardiographic assessment in patients referred for RHC remains uncertain.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 130 hospitalized patients with suspected PH who underwent echocardiography, 12-lead ECG, B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) testing, and RHC during the same admission. PH was defined as mean pulmonary arterial pressure > 20 mmHg on RHC. A temporal validation cohort of 42 consecutive eligible patients was used to evaluate the final model without refitting. To reduce collinearity, the final multimodal model included pulmonary artery systolic pressure estimated by echocardiography (PASP ECHO), ECG positivity, and BNP/NT-proBNP positivity. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using DeLong's test, calibration was assessed using calibration plots and calibration metrics, and internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Among 130 patients in the derivation cohort, 111 had PH and 19 did not. The final multimodal model showed higher discrimination than PASP ECHO alone in the derivation cohort (AUC 0.825, 95% CI 0.722-0.928 vs. 0.730, 95% CI 0.620-0.841; DeLong P = 0.008). At the Youden threshold, the final model showed high specificity but limited sensitivity, whereas a sensitivity-oriented threshold increased sensitivity at the expense of specificity. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. In the temporal validation cohort, the final model showed an AUC of 0.792, compared with 0.749 for PASP ECHO alone; this difference was not statistically significant. Bland-Altman analysis showed wide limits of agreement between PASP ECHO and invasive systolic pressure estimates, indicating that echocardiographic and invasive pressure estimates are associated but not interchangeable.
CONCLUSIONS: In this RHC-referred suspected PH cohort, ECG and natriuretic peptide positivity provided complementary information beyond PASP ECHO. However, because of the small sample size, marked class imbalance, and limited subtype characterization, the proposed multimodal approach should be considered exploratory. Larger prospective studies with subtype stratification and external validation are required before clinical implementation.

Title: Predicting long-term survival following lung cancer resection based on early perioperative immune-metabolic response patterns.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer resection is usually associated with surgical stress and systemic immune-metabolic shifts. Existing prognostic tools largely depend on static parameters. We aimed to characterize early perioperative Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) response patterns and construct a predictive nomogram to risk-stratify patients undergoing lung cancer resection.
METHODS: We selected patients with malignant lung neoplasms who underwent resection and had complete perioperative laboratory records from the INSPIRE database (2011-2020). Gaussian finite-mixture modeling within an LCGA framework was applied to classify early SII response patterns from baseline to 24 h postoperatively. Primary and secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, respectively. A perioperative immune-metabolic stress index (PIMSI) nomogram via multivariable logistic regression was established to predict the high-risk Severe Surge response pattern and was internally validated using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: A total of 2,186 patients were included and classified into three early perioperative SII response patterns: Class 1 (Stable; 57.4%), Class 2 (Moderate Increase; 35.8%), and Class 3 (Severe Surge; 6.8%). Compared with the Stable group, patients in the Severe Surge group had longer ICU stays and a higher risk of 5-year mortality (Hazard Ratio [HR] = 2.38, 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.69-3.35, p < 0.001). The PIMSI model, incorporating diabetes history, preoperative C-reactive protein, operative time, prognostic nutritional index, body weight, age, and ASA physical status, showed good discrimination for identifying patients at risk of a Severe Surge response pattern (apparent AUC, 0.828; optimism-corrected AUC, 0.820) and demonstrated clinical net benefit on decision curve analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Early perioperative SII trajectories were associated with ICU dependency and prognosis after lung cancer resection. The PIMSI nomogram may support early risk stratification and perioperative care escalation, but it needs further validation with oncological staging and histological adjustment.

Title: The diagnostic value of residual cholesterol inflammatory index for coronary artery disease severity in patients with premature coronary artery disease undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the diagnostic value of the Residual Cholesterol Inflammatory Index (RCII) for assessing coronary artery disease severity in patients with premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and to provide evidence for clinical risk stratification and individualized treatment.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on 351 patients diagnosed with PCAD who underwent PCI at Nantong First People's Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were divided into four groups (low, medium, high, and extremely high RCII) based on RCII quartiles. Baseline characteristics, laboratory parameters, and coronary angiography data were collected. Coronary lesion severity was evaluated using the Gensini score. Associations between RCII and coronary lesion severity were analyzed using the Kruskal‑Wallis H test, χ² test, multiple linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.
RESULTS: With the increase in RCII levels, the Gensini score, the rate of three-vessel coronary artery disease, and the incidence of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in PCAD patients undergoing PCI increased significantly (all P < 0.001). Multiple linear regression analysis, after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors, showed that RCII exhibited a significant non-linear (inverted U-shaped) association with Gensini score (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with a positive linear relationship predominantly observed in the low-to-moderate RCII range (≤ 40, accounting for 94% of the population) (unstandardized regression coefficient B = 0.52, 95% confidence interval 0.338-0.701, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis revealed a significant inverted U-shaped nonlinear association between RCII and Gensini score (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), with an inflection point threshold of approximately 40. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of RCII for assessing severe coronary artery disease (Gensini score ≥ 60) was 0.698, for three-vessel coronary artery disease was 0.723, and for AMI was 0.598, all of which were significantly higher than those of residual cholesterol (RC) alone (all P < 0.05 for DeLong test).
CONCLUSION: RCII demonstrates moderate predictive ability for coronary lesion severity in PCAD patients undergoing PCI, serving as an independently associated indicator for severe coronary lesions. Its predictive performance is superior to RC alone, making it a potential auxiliary biomarker for risk assessment. While its clinical application value still needs to be further verified in large-sample, multi-center, prospective cohort studies.

Title: Pirfenidone and pentoxifylline attenuate acute cavernosal ischaemia-reperfusion injury in an experimental model of ischaemic priapism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischaemic priapism is a urological emergency in which sustained cavernosal veno-occlusion produces progressive hypoxia, acidosis, smooth muscle compromise, and ultimately corporal fibrosis. Cavernosal injury is not confined to the ischaemic phase, as reperfusion following detumescence may further amplify tissue damage through oxidative stress, inflammatory activation, and endothelial dysfunction; adjunctive pharmacological strategies targeting this early reperfusion phase remain insufficiently characterised. This study was designed to evaluate and compare the acute effects of pirfenidone, pentoxifylline, dexpanthenol, and selected combination regimens on biochemical and histopathological markers of cavernosal injury in a rat model of ischaemic priapism-related ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
METHODS: Sixty-eight adult male Wistar albino rats were randomly allocated into seven groups: Sham, Control/IRI, pirfenidone, pentoxifylline, dexpanthenol, pirfenidone+dexpanthenol, and pentoxifylline+dexpanthenol. Ischaemic priapism was induced using a vacuum-assisted constriction-band model followed by a one-hour reperfusion period. Serum IL-1β, IL-10, malondialdehyde, and endothelial nitric oxide synthase levels were measured, and cavernosal tissues were evaluated by semi-quantitative histopathological scoring. Group comparisons used parametric or non-parametric tests with multiplicity adjustment. The study protocol was approved by the Animal Experiments Local Ethics Committee of Necmettin Erbakan University KONÜDAM Experimental Medicine Application and Research Center (22 December 2023; No. 2023-060). All procedures complied with institutional animal-care guidelines, and the study is reported in accordance with ARRIVE 2.0.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven animals were included in the final analysis. Relative to the Sham group, the Control/IRI group exhibited significantly elevated IL-1β, IL-10, malondialdehyde, and endothelial nitric oxide synthase levels alongside marked histopathological injury, confirming successful model induction. Pirfenidone significantly attenuated IL-1β and malondialdehyde levels and improved the composite pathology score. Pentoxifylline significantly reduced IL-1β, IL-10, malondialdehyde, and endothelial nitric oxide synthase levels and similarly improved the composite pathology score. Dexpanthenol attenuated malondialdehyde levels but did not consistently improve endothelial nitric oxide synthase or overall histopathological injury. Combination regimens produced endpoint-specific effects without consistently surpassing the corresponding monotherapies.
CONCLUSIONS: Pirfenidone and pentoxifylline attenuated selected biochemical and histopathological components of acute cavernosal ischaemia-reperfusion injury in this experimental model. These findings are hypothesis-generating; additional studies incorporating long-term erectile function assessment, fibrotic remodelling markers, and pharmacokinetic evaluation are warranted to clarify the translational relevance.

Title: The predictive performance of RDW for coronary artery lesions in children with Kawasaki disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Elevated red cell distribution width (RDW) may indicate an increased risk of coronary artery lesion (CAL) during the acute phase of Kawasaki disease (KD). This meta-analysis aimed to assess the predictive performance of RDW for CAL in children with KD.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for studies published until October 2025 that examined RDW's role in predicting CAL in KD. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and evaluated study quality using the QUADAS-2 tool. Statistical analysis was conducted with STATA 15.1. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, and meta-regression was performed to explore potential sources.
RESULTS: Eight retrospective studies involving 3,058 KD patients were included; among them, 1,126 (36.82%) developed CAL. The meta-analysis showed that RDW-CV had a sensitivity of 0.64 (95% CI: 0.55-0.73) and specificity of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.73-0.92); the DOR was 9.67 (95% CI: 3.67-24.81). The PLR and NLR were found to be 4.10 (95% CI: 2.11-7.94) and 0.42 (95% CI: 0.31-0.58), respectively; SROC analysis indicated an area under the curve of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.74-0.81).
CONCLUSION: RDW-CV demonstrates moderate diagnostic performance for predicting CAL in children with KD. It may serve as a complementary and readily available biomarker, particularly when used in combination with other clinical and laboratory parameters, rather than as a standalone predictor. Given the substantial heterogeneity across studies, future prospective research with standardized protocols is warranted.

Title: Patients with hypertension consistently showed earlier onset of diabetes: A UK Biobank survival analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes (T2D) frequently coexist, but whether hypertension independently contributes to earlier diabetes onset beyond shared metabolic and genetic susceptibility remains incompletely understood. This study investigates the longitudinal relationship between hypertension and subsequent T2D risk using survival analysis and survival machine learning approaches.
METHODS: A matched cohort analysis was conducted using UK Biobank participants free of diabetes at baseline, and a 6-month lag period was applied to reduce reverse causation. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Cox proportional hazards models. Genetic susceptibility was evaluated using both a genome-wide polygenic risk score (PRS) and a targeted multi-variant score (TMS). Survival machine learning models including XGBoost, Random Survival Forests, and ridge-penalized Cox regression were evalueted under identical train/test splits. Additional robustness analyses incorporated antihypertensive medication classes, genetic principal components, broader hypertension phenotype definitions integrating blood pressure measurements and medication use, stricter baseline diabetes exclusion criteria, extended lag-period analyses, and time-stratified sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The final multivariable matched analytic cohort included 76,439 participants (37,951 individuals with HTN and 38,488 matched controls). During follow-up, 4,315 incident T2D events occurred, including 3,571 among individuals with HTN and 744 among controls. Hypertension remained independently associated with T2D after adjustment for adiposity, lipid traits, statin use, antihypertensive medication classes, genetic principal components, and genetic susceptibility (HR 1.30, p < 0.001). Individuals with hypertension developed T2D earlier, with reduced diabetes-free survival over follow-up. Both PRS and TMS independently predicted T2D risk and demonstrated significant interactions with hypertension. Survival machine learning analyses showed progressive improvement in discrimination following incorporation of hypertension and genetic susceptibility, with XGBoost demonstrating the highest performance (C-index 0.823, 95% CI 0.812-0.833). Importantly, the observed association remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, demonstrating persistence of the association beyond the early post-index period.
CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension is associated with an increased and earlier T2D risk independent of metabolic risk factors and genetic susceptibility. Polygenic risk further stratifies diabetes risk but does not explain the relationship between hypertension and earlier T2D onset. The consistency of the findings across sensitivity analyses and survival-learning frameworks supports hypertension as an important component of the cardiometabolic trajectory preceding T2D development.

Title: Association between heart rate, metoprolol use, and clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated heart rate is a recognized prognostic marker in heart failure (HF), and beta‑blockers are recommended to control heart rate. However, real-world data on discharge heart rate, beta-blocker dosing, and their prognostic associations in patients with concomitant HF and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain limited.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from patients with HF (left ventricular ejection fraction < 50%) and COPD. Patients were categorized by discharge heart rate as low (< 70 beats/min) or high (≥ 70 beats/min). Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses were used to estimate associations with three‑year all‑cause mortality. Subgroup analyses were performed by HF phenotype, rhythm, and COPD status.
RESULTS: Among 611 patients (204 with low heart rate, 407 with high heart rate), those with high heart rate had significantly higher all‑cause mortality (log-rank p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, high heart rate remained independently associated with increased mortality (HR 1.86; 95%CI 1.22-2.84; p = 0.004). Higher metoprolol dose was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.80; 95%CI 0.69-0.92; p = 0.002). These associations were consistent across all subgroups, with no significant interactions (all interaction p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HF and COPD, elevated discharge heart rate was associated with higher all-cause mortality, and higher metoprolol dose was associated with better survival. However, given the observational design, these associations likely reflect underlying disease severity and treatment tolerance. Discharge heart rate may serve as an integrative risk marker. Randomized trials are warranted.

Title: Synergistic impact of insulin resistance and physical inactivity on cardiovascular disease: a cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) leads global mortality. Insulin resistance (IR) and physical activity (PA) are key cardiometabolic factors, yet their combined impact remains unclear. This study explores the independent and combined links of IR and PA to CVD incidence across diverse populations.
METHODS: This prospective analysis involved the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) was calculated via waist circumference, hypertension status, and Glycated Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c). PA was divided into ≥ 600 MET-minutes/week and < 600 MET-minutes/week. The main outcomes were new CVD cases (self-reported).
RESULTS: Lower eGDR and insufficient PA were independently tied to higher CVD incidence (eGDR: HR = 0.930, 95%CI = [0.886, 0.977]; PA: HR = 0.818, 95%CI = [0.699, 0.958]). A synergistic eGDR-PA interaction in cutting CVD risks emerged. Benefits occurred with/without diabetes (DM) or chronic kidney disease (CKD), without DM: OR = 0.412, 95%CI = [0.186, 0.890]; with DM: OR = 0.342, 95%CI = [0.112, 1.000]; without CKD: OR = 0.669, 95%CI = [0.502, 0.905]. Population-attributable fractions indicated optimizing eGDR and PA might prevent 19.6% of CVD cases. Mediation analyses found eGDR mediated PA's effect on CVD incidence, accounting for 25.723%.
CONCLUSION: Low eGDR and insufficient PA together hike CVD risk, especially in people without CKD or DM. The findings underscore the need to enhance metabolic health and PA adherence early to cut CVD burden.

Title: Transcriptome expression profiles and regulatory networks in patients with heart failure following myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The molecular mechanisms underlying heart failure (HF) following myocardial infarction (MI) (HF-MI) remain incompletely understood, and discoveries from whole-transcriptome profiling hold significant promise for disease prevention and treatment.
METHODS: Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on whole blood from post-MI patients with and without HF to analyze differentially expressed mRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, along with functional enrichment analysis. Co-expression networks linking lncRNA-mRNA and circRNA-mRNA pairs, as well as ceRNA networks involving lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA and circRNA-miRNA-mRNA interactions, were constructed for differentially expressed (DE) RNAs. Candidate lncRNAs were validated by RT-qPCR. Transcriptional factor-lncRNA networks were constructed, and candidate relationships were verified using RIP-PCR.
RESULTS: Patients with HF-MI exhibited marked elevation of NT-proBNP and significant reduction in LVEF%. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed 228 DE-mRNAs, 700 DE-lncRNAs, and 1188 DE-circRNAs in HF-MI compared to non-heart failure patients (NHF-MI). Construction of the ceRNA network identified hsa-miR-6089 and hsa-miR-6771-5p as candidate miRNAs in the lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network, while hsa-miR-1207-5p and hsa-miR-10392-3p were candidate miRNAs in the circRNA-miRNA-mRNA network. PVT1, SNHG5, TTN-AS1, HCP5, and OIP5-AS1 were identified as the five candidate DE-lncRNAs, with PVT1/SNHG5 showing upregulation and TTN-AS1/HCP5/OIP5-AS1 exhibiting downregulation. The transcription factor-lncRNA network primarily involves GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1, with validated associative interactions.
CONCLUSION: This study systematically mapped the regulatory network of HF-MI, suggesting potential involvement of the GLIS3-HCP5 and ZNF135-PVT1 axes in HF-MI, thereby providing a basis for exploring novel therapeutic strategies.

Title: Metabolic vulnerability index increased risk of all-cause mortality among individuals with stage 4 cardiovascular-renal-metabolic syndrome: a prospective cohort study in UK biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Metabolic Vulnerability Index (MVX), a novel composite marker of inflammation and malnutrition, has an undetermined prognostic value in stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between MVX and the risk of all-cause mortality among patients with stage 4 CKM syndrome.
METHODS: We included 20,927 participants with stage 4 CKM syndrome in the UK Biobank. Sex-specific MVX scores were calculated by aggregating six biomarkers (glycoprotein acetyls (GlycA), small high-density lipoprotein particles (sHDL), valine, leucine, isoleucine, and citrate). We applied Cox proportional-hazards models to investigate the association between MVX and all-cause mortality and evaluated the performance of MVX in predicting mortality.
RESULTS: During a median 13.45 years of follow-up (IQR:12.54-14.32 years), a total of 4,613 participants (22.04%) died. The fully adjusted Cox regression model indicated that a graded association between MVX quartiles and all-cause mortality, with the highest MVX quartile showing the greatest risk (HR = 1.67, 95% CI: 1.49-1.87, P < 0.001). A consistent positive association was observed between MVX score and mortality risk at 5, 10, and 15 years (P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses showed that females and individuals with cardiovascular disease (CVD) exhibited a higher mortality risk (P for interaction < 0.001). MVX significantly improved the predictive value of all-cause mortality beyond established risk factors (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), lipid accumulation Product (LAP)) (Uno's C-statistic: 0.713, 95% CI: 0.705-0.721, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated MVX scores were independently associated with higher all-cause mortality risk in stage 4 CKM syndrome, supporting its potential for risk stratification.

Title: Lactate-right ventricular discordance patterns and mortality in critical illness.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum lactate and echocardiographic assessment are both central to hemodynamic evaluation in the ICU, yet their combined phenotypic information remains unexplored. We hypothesized that cross-classifying patients by lactate level and right ventricular (RV) function identifies clinically coherent classification groups with differential outcomes.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV v2.2 linked with MIMIC-IV-ECHO v1.0, with supportive external assessment in the eICU Collaborative Research Database. Adult ICU patients with transthoracic echocardiography and lactate measured within ± 6 h were classified by lactate (< 2 vs. ≥ 2 mmol/L) and qualitative RV function. Logistic models used patient-clustered robust standard errors; a sensitivity analysis retained only the earliest eligible observation per patient. Incremental value was assessed by adding RV dysfunction to a clinical model containing continuous lactate.
RESULTS: Among 6,228 observations from 4,965 patients (median age 66 years; 57.8% male; 30.9% hospital mortality), mortality increased from 18.8% in Low-Lactate/Preserved-RV to 47.2% in High-Lactate/RV-Dysfunction. Associations persisted with patient-clustered inference, first-day SOFA adjustment, and restriction to one observation per patient. Adding RV dysfunction to a clinical model containing continuous lactate produced a small improvement in AUC (0.758 to 0.761; ΔAUC 0.003, patient-bootstrap 95% CI 0.001-0.006). RR-based RERI was 0.070 (95% CI - 0.177 to 0.284). In 43,466 eICU stays with observed hospital outcome, diagnosis-coded RV disease reproduced the mortality ordering; aligned adjusted ORs were 2.01, 3.01, and 5.87 across the non-reference groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Lactate-RV cross-classification identifies clinically coherent groups with graded mortality in ICU patients selected for echocardiography. RV assessment adds statistically detectable but modest prognostic information beyond continuous lactate and clinical covariates. The eICU findings support the prognostic pattern but do not constitute direct validation of the echocardiographic phenotype.

Title: Prehospital endotracheal intubation and return of spontaneous circulation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients: a retrospective cohort study based on prehospital emergency registry data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal airway strategy during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain. This study investigated the association between prehospital endotracheal intubation (ETI) and return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) using a regional emergency medical services registry.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 6,162 adult non-traumatic OHCA patients treated by emergency medical services between October 2023 and November 2024. Patients were categorized into an ETI group (n = 1,448) and a basic airway (BA) group (n = 4,714). The primary outcome was prehospital ROSC. Long-term survival and neurological outcomes were not available in the registry. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-matched sensitivity analysis were used to evaluate the association between ETI and ROSC while accounting for measured confounders. Airway strategy was selected by on-scene physicians during routine EMS care, and rhythm-stratified unadjusted analyses were performed to describe whether the ETI-ROSC association differed by initial rhythm category.
RESULTS: ROSC occurred more frequently in the ETI group than in the BA group (21.1% vs. 3.8%, P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, ETI was strongly associated with ROSC (OR = 7.61, 95% CI: 6.07-9.53, P < 0.001). Shockable initial rhythm (OR = 5.42, 95% CI: 3.80-7.74, P < 0.001) and defibrillation (OR = 1.82, 95% CI: 1.37-2.42, P < 0.001) were also positively associated with ROSC, whereas longer response time and epinephrine administration were negatively associated with ROSC. In 1:1 propensity score-matched analysis, the association between ETI and ROSC remained significant (OR = 6.33, 95% CI: 4.72-8.47, P < 0.001). Rhythm-stratified analyses showed that the unadjusted association was strongest in non-shockable and other/unknown rhythm strata and was not statistically significant in the shockable rhythm stratum.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective prehospital registry cohort, ETI during OHCA resuscitation was strongly associated with higher ROSC rates. Because airway timing relative to collapse and ROSC, survival to discharge, and neurological outcomes were not captured, these findings should be interpreted as an association with immediate resuscitation success rather than evidence of a causal survival benefit. The observed association may also reflect physician selection of airway strategy and other unmeasured resuscitation factors, and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Clinical outcomes of native vessel versus saphenous vein graft percutaneous coronary intervention in coronary artery bypass graft patients presenting with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) should target the saphenous vein graft (SVG) or the native coronary vessel in patients with prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) who present with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) is uncertain. We compared outcomes after culprit-lesion PCI of the SVG versus the native vessel in this population.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective analysis of a PCI database (January 2003-July 2025), we included patients with prior CABG presenting with NSTEMI whose culprit-lesion PCI was in an SVG or in a native vessel supplied by an SVG. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality at discharge and at 5 years.
RESULTS: Of 631 patients, 283 (44.8%) underwent native vessel PCI and 348 (55.2%) SVG PCI. SVG PCI patients had older grafts (13.5 vs 10.8 years, p < 0.001), more left main disease (29.9% vs 17.8%, p < 0.001), and more laser atherectomy (9.2% vs 1.8%, p < 0.001) and thrombectomy (10.4% vs 3.6%, p = 0.001); native vessel PCI more often involved bifurcation lesions (6.4% vs 0.6%, p < 0.001) and chronic total occlusions (3.6% vs 0%, p < 0.001). All-cause mortality did not differ significantly between SVG and native vessel PCI at discharge (6.9% vs 3.5%, p = 0.063) or at 5 years (47.5% [95% CI 40.3-54.3] vs 45.0% [95% CI 37.5-52.2]; log-rank p = 0.236), nor did in-hospital complications.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, in-hospital and long-term mortality did not differ significantly between SVG and native vessel PCI. Because target-vessel selection was not randomized and its rationale was not captured, these findings are hypothesis-generating and should not alone guide target-vessel choice.

Title: Achieved LDL-C Levels and Clinical Outcomes Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Drug-Coated Balloons for De Novo Coronary Lesions.
Abstract:
AIM: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with a drug-coated balloon (DCB) is a coronary revascularization strategy; however, the prognostic impact of achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels after intervention remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to understand the association between LDL-C and the clinical outcomes in patients undergoing PCI with DCB.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent PCI with DCB (April 2019-March 2023) and had available 6-month LDL-C data. The clinical outcomes were assessed using a 6-month landmark approach. Patients were stratified by LDL-C level (＜70, 70-＜100, and ≥ 100 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and target lesion revascularization (TLR).
RESULTS: Among 320 patients, 47.8% had LDL-C ＜70 mg/dL, 31.6% had 70-＜100 mg/dL, and 20.6% had LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL. The cumulative incidence of MACE and TLR was significantly higher with increasing LDL-C levels (log-rank P = 0.006 and P = 0.023, respectively), whereas all-cause mortality and myocardial infarction did not differ significantly. In a multivariate Cox regression analysis, LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL independently predicted TLR (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.31; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-4.61; P = 0.02). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower achieved LDL-C levels and reduced rates of MACE and TLR.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing PCI with DCB, higher achieved LDL-C levels, particularly LDL-C ≥ 100 mg/dL, were independently associated with an increased TLR risk, which primarily drove the observed difference in MACE. These findings highlight the importance of optimal LDL-C management following PCI with DCB.

Title: [Clinical outcomes of horse antithymocyte globulin-based immunosuppressive therapy for aplastic anemia at a single institution].
Journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Horse antithymocyte globulin (hATG) has been available for the treatment of aplastic anemia (AA) in Japan since 2023.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of combination therapy with hATG, cyclosporine, and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA), and determine the optimal steroid regimen for serum sickness prophylaxis.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed seven patients with AA who received hATG combined with cyclosporine and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA; eltrombopag or romiplostim).
RESULTS: The median age was 62 years. All patients achieved transfusion independence within 3 months (median day 35 for red blood cells and day 36 for platelets). Six patients remain alive and transfusion-independent, while one died of heart failure. The early dose-reduction regimen frequently failed because of serum sickness, necessitating a switch to the conventional method.
CONCLUSIONS: hATG-based triple therapy led to rapid transfusion independence. Switching TPO-RAs may be effective in patients with a suboptimal response. The conventional method of steroid prophylaxis may be preferable.

Title: Changes and trajectories in sleep duration and risk of premature all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality.
Abstract: BackgroundWhile substantial evidence indicates an association between sleep and a range of chronic conditions, the potential impact of longitudinal changes in sleep on the risk of premature mortality remains poorly characterized.MethodsWe conducted a population-based cohort study using data from The Rural Chinese Cohort Study. Baseline assessments were performed during 2007-2008, with two subsequent follow-up surveys conducted in 2013-2014 and 2018-2020. A total of 13621 adults aged ⩾18 years were included after excluding participants with missing sleep duration data at baseline or the first follow-up or aged ⩾70 years at baseline. Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations of relative changes and trajectories of sleep duration with premature all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 5.07 years, the relative change in sleep duration was significantly associated with the risks of premature all-cause and CVD mortality. Compared with participants with stable sleep duration (-15% to 15%), those with a ⩾30% increase in sleep duration had a higher risk of premature all-cause (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.28-2.47) and CVD mortality (HR 2.20, 95% CI 1.42-3.41). Sleep trajectory analyses suggested that transitions toward long sleep duration (>9 h/day) were associated with an increased risk of premature CVD mortality.ConclusionsMaintaining a stable healthy sleep duration might be important for reducing the risk of premature all-cause and CVD mortality. These findings highlight the potential value of monitoring dynamic changes in sleep duration as a modifiable target for health promotion.

Title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.
METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.
RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).
CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

Title: Effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a pre-specified cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of the CAMEO-SEMA trial.
Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05371496.

Title: Lifetime Oestrogen Exposure Indices in Relation to Biological Aging and Future Life Expectancy: A Prospective Study of Two Cohorts.
Journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations of lifetime oestrogen exposure indices with biological aging, mortality and life expectancy.
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.
SETTING: UK Biobank and the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).
POPULATION OR SAMPLE: 112 381 postmenopausal women, including 107 218 from UK Biobank and 5163 from US NHANES.
METHODS: Lifetime oestrogen exposure was assessed using three reproductive-history-based indices: reproductive lifespan (RLS), endogenous oestrogen exposure (EEE), and total oestrogen exposure (TEE). Biological aging was measured by phenotypic age (PA). Multivariable linear regression examined associations with PA acceleration, Cox models assessed mortality, and flexible parametric survival models estimated life expectancy, with covariate adjustment.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: PA acceleration, all-cause and cause-specific mortality, and estimated life expectancy.
RESULTS: In the UK Biobank, higher RLS, EEE, and TEE were inversely related to PA acceleration, with estimates generally strongest for RLS and TEE (e.g., highest quartile RLS: β = -0.31, 95% CI: -0.40 to -0.22). In the US NHANES, inverse associations were clearest for TEE. Higher RLS and TEE were generally associated with lower risks of all-cause, cardiovascular, and respiratory mortality across both cohorts. The highest quartile of TEE was associated with increase in life expectancy of 0.64 years (95% CI: 0.30 to 0.97) in the UK Biobank and 1.35 years (95% CI: 0.20 to 2.50) in the US NHANES at age 45. In UK Biobank, RLS and EEE were associated with higher endometrial cancer incidence, and all three indices with higher breast cancer incidence.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher lifetime oestrogen exposure indices, particularly TEE, were generally associated with delayed biological aging and longer estimated life expectancy.

Title: Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The COAST-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) for persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) has demonstrated modest success rates. Ablation of atrial low-voltage areas (LVA) has shown potential results, but more data are required.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PVI plus LVA ablation is superior to PVI alone in reducing atrial arrhythmia recurrence in patients with AF.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Single-blind randomized clinical trial in 14 AF ablation centers in Canada. Adults with persistent AF of more than 3 months were enrolled between August 2018 and September 2024 and followed up for 18 to 36 months through April 2026.
INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation or PVI alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond 90 days after a single catheter ablation procedure. Secondary outcomes included repeat ablation for AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia, emergency visits or hospitalization, arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months, procedure duration, total ablation delivery time, AF burden, and safety outcomes. The primary efficacy analysis was based on the modified intention-to-treat principle for patients who received the intervention.
RESULTS: Among 508 enrolled patients, 253 were randomized to PVI plus LVA ablation and 255 to PVI alone. Mean (SD) age was 65.2 (9.0) years, 386 (76%) were male and 268 (54%) had LVA. After a mean (SD) follow-up of 21 (15) months, 124 (49.4%) randomized to PVI plus LVA and 146 (57.5%) randomized to PVI reached the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82; 95% CI, 0.65-1.04; P = .11). In the prespecified principal subgroup analysis of 268 patients with LVA, arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 68 of 138 patients (49.3%) following PVI plus LVA ablation compared with 90 of 130 patients (69.2%) following PVI alone (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66-0.91; P = .002). Arrhythmia recurrence over 18 months (37.0% vs 56.2%; HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.92) and AF burden were lower after PVI plus LVA ablation in this group. Among patients without LVA, recurrence was similar between ablation groups (56 of 113 [49.6%] vs 51 of 113 [45.1%]; HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.90-1.32). Procedure duration and ablation delivery time were longer in the PVI plus LVA ablation group. Safety outcomes were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, among patients with persistent AF, adjunctive LVA ablation did not significantly reduce atrial arrhythmia recurrence in the overall population over a mean 21-month follow-up. A prespecified principal subgroup analysis of patients with LVA suggested that adjunctive LVA ablation was consistent with reduced recurrence of atrial arrhythmias in this group.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03347227.

Title: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes.
Abstract: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549.

Title: Variability of lipoprotein(a) levels in patients with acute myocardial infarction between admission, discharge, and follow-up.
Abstract:
AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Using Lp(a) concentrations measured during stable follow-up as the reference, we aimed to assess the temporal variability of Lp(a) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and to explore a pragmatic strategy for Lp(a) measurement.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The FRENCHIE-Lp(a) cohort enrolled consecutive adults hospitalized for AMI in 21 centres. Lp(a) mass concentration, measured at admission, hospital discharge, and 3-12 months follow-up, was analysed both as a continuous and predefined categorical variable (≤20, >20-≤50, >50-≤70, >70 mg/dL). Assuming follow-up Lp(a) as the reference, we aimed to identify the threshold values that would allow us to accurately identify patients with Lp(a) > 70mg/dL, the threshold mostly used for patient selection in phase III trials of targeted Lp(a) therapies. A cumulative threshold analysis was performed to identify the Lp(a) value below which the misclassification rate (i.e. % of patients with follow-up Lp(a) > 70 mg/dL) remained <1%. Among 1561 patients (aged 61 ± 12 years; 21.3% women), median Lp(a) was 13 mg/dL at admission and remained stable over time (median difference overtime = 0 mg/dL). However, only 68.5% of patients remained in the same Lp(a) category overtime. In patients with discharge-Lp(a) ≤37 mg/dL (72.5% of the population), only 0.97% had Lp(a) >70 mg/dL at follow-up compared to 39.9% of those with discharge-Lp(a) >37 mg/dL.
CONCLUSION: Although the median Lp(a) level remained stable between admission and follow-up, one-third of AMI patients shifted within Lp(a) categories over time. Pending external validation, an exploratory two-step strategy based on Lp(a) measurement at discharge, followed by repeat testing in patients with Lp(a) >37 mg/dL, showed a misclassification rate below 1% for identifying patients potentially needing intervention.
REGISTRATION: Clinical trial Number: NCT04050956.

Title: [Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation in Hungarian emergency departments].
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advanced airway management of patients with preserved circulation (not in cardiac arrest) is a critical, high-risk procedure in emergency care. Internationally, safety improves through standardized procedures, equipment, documentation, and training.
OBJECTIVE: To map current practice in Hungarian emergency departments regarding who performs the procedure, the degree of regulation, the available drugs and devices, documentation practices, and training.
METHOD: We conducted a cross-sectional online questionnaire survey. Based on the department-head registry of the Hungarian Society of Emergency Medicine, we sent the questionnaire to the heads of all 44 Hungarian emergency departments. Data were collected between May and July 2026 and analyzed using descriptive statistics.
RESULTS: The response rate was 52% (23/44). In 96% of the departments, the procedure was routinely performed by emergency care providers. A written protocol existed in 48% of the departments (mandatory in 17%). Propofol, a depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent, and a bougie were available in all departments. Non-invasive ventilation was available in 96% of departments, videolaryngoscopes in 74%, and capnographs in 78%; however, only 39% mandated capnography. In 52% of the responding departments, no dedicated procedural documentation was produced, and 57% had no regular topic-specific training.
DISCUSSION: In the responding departments, the procedure was performed predominantly by emergency clinicians, and the basic pharmacological and equipment requirements were largely met. However, organizational safeguards for patient safety - a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation, and regular training - were often lacking, indicating both deviations from international recommendations and clear targets for improvement.
CONCLUSION: In the responding Hungarian emergency departments, the airway management practice for patients with preserved circulation was highly heterogeneous and insufficiently standardized. Priorities for improvement include a uniform protocol, mandatory capnography, structured documentation and a national registry, and regular training. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(45): 1835-1842.

Title: Iron Repletion in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The IRONMET-HFpEF Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iron deficiency is present in >50% of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and is associated with reduced exercise capacity and survival. Whether iron repletion improves exercise capacity as objectively measured by peak oxygen uptake ([Formula: see text]) is unknown. The IRONMET-HFpEF trial (Impact of Intravenous Iron Repletion on Mechanisms of Exercise Intolerance in HFpEF) sought to determine whether ferric derisomaltose (FDI) compared with placebo improves peak [Formula: see text] in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency.
METHODS: This was a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and iron deficiency, defined as ferritin <100 ng/mL or <300 ng/mL with transferrin saturation <20%. Participants were enrolled between December 2021 and April 2026. Single-dose ferric derisomaltose (1000 mg; n=44) or placebo (n=21) was administered once intravenously. The primary end point was the change in peak [Formula: see text] from baseline to 12 weeks with an analysis of covariance model including terms for treatment group, baseline peak [Formula: see text], and sex. Secondary end points included changes in [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, New York Heart Association class, health status assessed by the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score, and iron biomarkers at 12 weeks.
RESULTS: Among 65 randomized participants (median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 58-76 years], 72% women, transferrin saturation 16.0±7.4%, ferritin 57.8±48.9 ng/mL), 64 (98.5%) completed the study. The median baseline peak [Formula: see text] was 12.7 mL·kg-1·min-1 (interquartile range, 10.6-15.8 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the FDI group and 12.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (11.6-14.6 mL·kg-1·min-1) in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, peak [Formula: see text] improved by 1.2 mL·kg-1·min-1 (95% CI, 0.6-1.7) in the FDI group and was unchanged (0.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, -0.7 to 0.9]) in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, 1.1 mL·kg-1·min-1 [95% CI, 0.2-1.9]; P=0.02). [Formula: see text] at the anaerobic threshold, 6-minute walk test distance, and New York Heart Association class also improved in the FDI compared with the placebo group (all P<0.05), whereas the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary Score did not differ significantly between groups (FDI group, +4.4 [95% CI, -2.4 to 11.2]; P=0.20). FDI increased transferrin saturation (9.4% [95% CI, 4.9%-13.9%]) and ferritin (183 ng/mL [95% CI, 128-238]) compared with the placebo group (PLSMD<0.001 for both). There were no serious adverse events related to FDI administration.
CONCLUSIONS: In the largest trial to date of iron repletion in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction with iron deficiency, FDI improved multiple measures of exercise capacity.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04945707.

Title: Early third-trimester maternal cardiac function and morphometry in high-risk pregnancies that subsequently developed fetal growth restriction and/or pre-eclampsia.
Journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate maternal cardiovascular function and cardiac morphology in early third-trimester pregnancies at high risk for fetal growth restriction (FGR) and compare findings between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or pre-eclampsia (PE) and uncomplicated pregnancies.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies at high risk for FGR referred to the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Department at the Hospital Clinic of Barcelona, Barcelona, Spain, between August 2022 and August 2024, for a routine second-trimester fetal anomaly scan. The patients were assessed between 27 + 0 and 28 + 6 weeks' gestation and were only included in the analysis if they did not have a diagnosis of FGR or PE at the time of evaluation; those who subsequently developed FGR and/or PE were identified during follow-up. Maternal echocardiography was performed to assess cardiac output (CO), stroke volume (SV), systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and structural parameters including left ventricular (LV) wall thickness and chamber volumes. Results were compared between pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR (with or without PE), pregnancies that subsequently developed isolated PE and uncomplicated pregnancies. Multivariable analysis was performed using quantile regression of the medians for CO and SVR, adjusted for body mass index (BMI), with FGR and PE assessed independently.
RESULTS: A total of 948 patients were included in the final analysis, of whom 129 developed FGR and/or PE (including 59 that developed FGR (with or without PE) and 70 that developed isolated PE) and 819 had uncomplicated pregnancies. Median mean arterial pressure (MAP) was higher in the FGR (with or without PE) group (82.0 mmHg) and the isolated-PE group (84.8 mmHg) than in the uncomplicated group (79.7 mmHg; P = 0.027 and P < 0.001, respectively), with the isolated-PE group showing the highest MAP values (isolated PE vs FGR (with or without PE), P = 0.047). Median heart rate was elevated in the isolated-PE group (82.5 bpm) compared with the FGR (with or without PE) group (77.0 bpm; P = 0.03). In the multivariable analysis, FGR and PE were associated independently with lower CO and higher SVR prior to their development. Median SV was reduced in the FGR (with or without PE) group (59.7 mL) and the isolated-PE group (61.1 mL) compared with the uncomplicated group (64.2 mL; P = 0.030 and P = 0.016, respectively). Median BMI-indexed CO was also lower in the FGR (with or without PE) group (0.18 (L/min)/(kg/m2)) and the isolated-PE group (0.17 (L/min)/(kg/m2)) compared with the uncomplicated group (0.19 (L/min)/(kg/m2); P = 0.005 and P = 0.001, respectively). Median SVR was elevated in the FGR (with or without PE) group (1393 dynes × s/cm5) and the isolated-PE group (1339 dynes × s/cm5) compared with the uncomplicated group (1252 dynes × s/cm5; P < 0.001 and P = 0.01, respectively). Compared with the uncomplicated group, the isolated-PE group showed greater median LV myocardial thickness at end diastole (0.50 vs 0.47 cm; P = 0.003), interventricular septal thickness at end diastole (0.92 vs 0.89 cm; P = 0.031), posterior wall thickness at end diastole (0.98 vs 0.94 cm; P = 0.013) and relative wall thickness (0.45 vs 0.42; P = 0.001). Moreover, the FGR (with or without PE) group had a smaller median LV end-diastolic diameter (4.27 cm) compared with the uncomplicated group (4.48 cm; P = 0.003), indicating that preload may be reduced in patients who developed FGR (with or without PE). LV mass indexed for BMI was similar across groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal cardiovascular alterations may precede the development of FGR and PE and differ by phenotype. Pregnancies that subsequently developed FGR and/or PE showed reduced CO, but those that developed FGR reflected lower preload without tachycardia, while those that developed isolated PE showed hypertensive features with a compensatory rise in heart rate. Maternal echocardiography may aid early risk stratification and guide tailored surveillance and therapy in pregnancies at high risk for FGR. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

Title: Cardiovascular diseases and guideline-directed medical therapy in low socio-economic status patients: A single center experience.
Journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with a low socio-economic status (SES) exhibit high cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs) and a high burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but they are under-recognized in clinical practice. In this study, we explored CVRFs and CVD in low-SES patients, and estimated the guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) prevalence for each CVD.
METHODS: Consecutive individuals with low-SES who attended the primary care and cardiology clinics within a single charitable medical center between 2024 and 2025 were retrospectively recruited. Data on SES, symptoms, CVRFs, CVDs, and treatment strategies were collected and analyzed descriptively. GDMT comprised class I medications reported by patients and documented in their medical records at the time of data collection for each CVD.
RESULTS: Among the 2374 patients, the mean age was 58.7 ± 6 years (57.2% females). Common CVRFs included hypertension (39.5%), diabetes (28.6%), and hyperlipidemia (27.4%). Common CVDs included coronary artery disease (CAD) (12.4%), heart failure (HF) (6%), and atrial fibrillation (AF) (1.7%) (mean ages: 55.79, 63.12, and 62.4 years, respectively). CAD patients had a high prevalence of acute coronary syndrome (74.2%), with most managed noninvasively (87%), but 38.5% received GDMT. HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) exceeded HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) (63.6% vs. 32.8%). Prevalent HF causes included CAD, hypertension, and valvular disease (33.6%, 27.3%, and 26.6%, respectively). GDMT rates for HFrEF and HFpEF were 18.7% and 34%, respectively. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 3.5 for AF patients, with 42.8% on GDMT (78% on warfarin).
CONCLUSIONS: Low-SES patients had a high prevalence of CVRF, where CAD, HF, and AF were most common. The patients were relatively young and managed conservatively, but GDMT rates were low. These findings may guide policymakers to improve cardiovascular care in low-SES individuals.

Title: Comment on "Health related quality of life and cardiac symptoms following admission for suspected MINOCA: A post-hoc analysis of the MINOCA-BAT randomized clinical trial".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Effects of a 4-week vinyasa yoga intervention on sleep and cardiovascular health in adults with insomnia symptoms: a pilot randomized controlled trial.
Journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Vinyasa yoga (VY) yields moderate-intensity physical activity that may improve sleep and cardiovascular health (CVH). However, evidence is scarce regarding the effects of VY on CVH. This study examined the effects of a 4-week VY intervention on sleep and CVH in adults with insomnia symptoms.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 33 insufficiently active adults (84.8 per cent female; 78.8 per cent White; 34.9 ± 10.6 y; 28.9 kg/m2) with insomnia symptoms (Insomnia Severity Index [ISI] ≥10) were randomized to a 4-week VY intervention (n = 17) or non-active control (CON; n = 16). VY participants practiced 3×/week following pre-recorded 60-minute videos and CON maintained their current lifestyle. Resting daytime blood pressure (BP), heart rate (HR), and HR variability (HRV) were obtained at baseline and post-intervention. Sleep was measured using the ISI, actigraphy, and a sleep diary. One night during sleep assessment, participants wore a chest HR monitor to assess HRV; primary HRV outcome was root mean square of successive differences. Analyses used linear mixed models and Cohen's d effect sizes.
RESULTS: Changes in ISI, actigraphy-, and diary-assessed sleep from baseline to post-intervention did not differ between groups (each p > .06). Changes in nocturnal HRV and daytime resting BP and HRV were not significant (each p ≥ .30). Resting HR decreased for VY (72.41 ± 2.92 to 69.50 ± 2.60 bpm) and increased for CON (70.47 ± 2.54 to 72.93 ± 2.60 bpm) (p = .047). Additionally, among highly adherent participants, VY reduced ISI scores more than CON (p = .002).
CONCLUSION: VY improves insomnia symptoms among those who practice regularly. It does not appear to improve nocturnal cardiovascular physiology, and shows modest benefits on daytime cardiac parasympathetic activity.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov; Name: Yoga for Insomnia Study; URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05723211; Registration ID: NCT0572321; Date of Registration: January 2, 2023.

Title: Outcomes of Patients With Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia Treated With Bruton Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (BTKi): A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Healthcare Center in North India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi) are a pivotal advancement in treating chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). However, their adoption faces challenges such as high discontinuation rates caused by adverse events like cardiac and hematologic toxicities and a significant financial burden. Our study aims to evaluate the clinical spectrum and outcomes of patients with CLL receiving BTKi therapy in India. The objectives are to evaluate progression-free survival and overall survival in CLL patients on BTKi and to assess the BTKi toxicity profile.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study analyzed data from 41 patients with CLL treated with BTKi between January 2019 and November 2024.
RESULTS: Twenty-five male patients and 16 female patients were evaluated, with a median age of 64 years (range 42-90). Twelve patients (29.2%) had no cytogenetic abnormalities, while 29 (70.7%) had at least one abnormality; 13q deletion was the most common. BTKi was used as first-line therapy in 29 patients (70.7%), with acalabrutinib being the most commonly used agent, administered to 17 (58.6%) patients. Cardiac events were observed in 8 (19.5%) patients, including hypertension in four (9.7%) and atrial fibrillation in two (4.9%). Gastrointestinal adverse events were noted in 7 (17%) patients. One patient had Richter transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. At a median follow-up of 24 months, progression-free survival was 80% and overall survival was 95%.
CONCLUSIONS: BTKi therapy is effective and well tolerated in Indian CLL patients, but early discontinuation highlights the need for improved adherence strategies.

Title: Cardioprotective Effects of Low-Dose Bisoprolol Against Anthracycline-Induced Subclinical Cardiotoxicity in Breast Cancer: A Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial Using Advanced Echocardiographic Parameters.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthracyclines are cornerstone agents in breast cancer chemotherapy. However, they can cause dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, potentially impairing long-term cardiac function. Beta-blockers have demonstrated cardioprotective effects. However, evidence regarding bisoprolol, particularly using comprehensive echocardiographic evaluations, remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of low-dose bisoprolol against anthracycline-induced subclinical cardiac dysfunction in patients with breast cancer.
METHODS: This triple-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted in Isfahan, Iran, between January and December 2023. Eligible women with locally advanced breast cancer receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy were randomized to bisoprolol (2.5 mg/day) or a placebo. Cardiac function was assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, and the end of treatment during a 6-month follow-up period. The evaluated echocardiographic parameters included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions (LVEDD, LVESD), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and tricuspid annular systolic excursion (TAPSE). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software (version 25.0). Continuous variables were analyzed using paired or independent-samples t tests, and categorical variables were analyzed using the Chi square test. Statistical significance was defined as P<0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 50 patients completed the trial (25 in the bisoprolol group and 25 in the placebo group). LVEF remained stable in both groups. Compared with the placebo group, bisoprolol demonstrated significantly more favorable structural and functional changes, including a reduction in LVEDD (mean change=-0.172 cm; 95% CI=-0.343 to -0.001; P=0.049), LVESD (mean change=-0.156 cm; 95% CI=-0.295 to -0.172; P=0.029), and LVEDV (mean change=-7.920 mL; 95% CI=-15.174 to -0.666; P=0.033); improved GLS (mean change=0.974; 95% CI=0.083 to 1.865; P=0.033); and better preserved TAPSE (mean change=0.168 cm; 95% CI=0.101 to 0.234; P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Prophylactic bisoprolol might attenuate early subclinical cardiotoxicity in patients with breast cancer receiving anthracyclines, primarily through the stabilization of LVEDV and a more favorable GLS trajectory.Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials: IRCT20130701013828N8.

Title: Prescribing, Medication Adherence, and Blood Pressure Goal Achievement Among Middle-to-Older Age Adults in a Primary Care Setting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood pressure (BP) control among hypertensive people remains inadequate. This study aims to assess BP goal achievement among people prescribed antihypertensives, to examine medication nonadherence, and to identify demographics associated with goal achievements and medication nonadherence in this population.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of the Mitchelstown Cohort Study Rescreen data. Goal achievement was assessed in accordance with the 2013 European guidelines, the guidelines in place during data collection. A validated, self-reported 3-item medication nonadherence questionnaire was used, with a mean score ranging from 1 (Perfect Adherence) to 5 (Perfect Nonadherence).
