Nonadherence was defined as mean score > 1. Multiple imputation was used to impute missing data on covariates and outcomes. A sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the consistency of results by applying the 2024 European guideline recommendations. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify the factors associated with BP goal achievements and medication nonadherence.
RESULTS: Antihypertensives were prescribed to 567 participants. Based on imputed data, 63.8% of these achieved 2013 BP goal. Mean medication nonadherence score was 1.6 (SE ± 0.06), with 34.8% participants being nonadherent. Having multiple antihypertensives pills was associated with lower likelihood of achieving BP goals. In the sensitivity analysis, 38.4% achieved 2024 BP goal and in multivariable analysis, being overweight or obese was associated with not achieving the 2024 goals.
CONCLUSION: The study highlights the gap between guideline BP goals and achieving these goals in real world practice. Key patient and medication factors were identified that could guide efforts to improve BP goal achievement. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03191227.

Title: Advances in Digital Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Digital health technologies have rapidly transformed physiotherapy rehabilitation by improving accessibility, patient engagement, remote monitoring, and continuity of care. Interventions such as telerehabilitation, wearable devices, artificial intelligence (AI), virtual reality (VR), smartphone-based applications, and remote monitoring systems are increasingly being integrated into musculoskeletal, neurological, and cardiovascular rehabilitation. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of these digital health technologies by synthesizing evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, PEDro, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar identified English-language RCTs published between January 2021 and July 2026. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, and the methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool. Owing to heterogeneity in interventions, outcome measures, and study populations, findings were synthesized narratively. Fourteen RCTs involving musculoskeletal, neurological, and cardiovascular populations met the eligibility criteria. Overall, digital health interventions significantly improved pain, physical function, mobility, range of motion, exercise adherence, functional independence, and quality of life. Telerehabilitation demonstrated outcomes comparable to conventional face-to-face physiotherapy for musculoskeletal disorders, wearable technologies enhanced motor recovery and functional performance in neurological rehabilitation, and remote cardiac rehabilitation improved exercise capacity, adherence, and health-related quality of life. Most included studies were judged to have some concerns about risk of bias, while one study demonstrated an overall low risk of bias. The findings suggest that digital health technologies are effective adjuncts or alternatives to conventional physiotherapy, enhancing accessibility, patient engagement, and rehabilitation outcomes. However, further high-quality multicenter RCTs with standardized intervention protocols and longer follow-up periods are required to strengthen the evidence base and support wider implementation in routine physiotherapy practice.

Title: Association Between Awareness of Dietary Intake Restriction at Two Time Points and Mortality Outcomes: A Cohort Study in Japan.
Abstract: Our previous study identified a modest association between awareness of dietary intake restriction and all-cause mortality. However, whether repeated awareness is associated with all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and cancer mortality remained unclear. We analyzed 14,060 participants from the Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Study. Participants reporting energy or fat intake restriction at two points in time, approximately 5 years apart, were classified as having both-survey energy or fat awareness, respectively. Multivariable and inverse probability-weighted (IPW) Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Over approximately 7 years, 374 deaths occurred. In the IPW model (Model 2), both-survey energy awareness was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.59-0.97) and CVD mortality (0.48; 0.24-0.97), although the latter was not significant in Model 1; the cancer association was significant in Model 1 but not in Model 2. It should be noted, however, that the number of CVD deaths was extremely low (n = 63) and that, of these, only 10 occurred among individuals with both-survey energy awareness. Both-survey fat awareness was not associated with mortality. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested inverse awareness-mortality associations. Overall, both-survey energy awareness was inversely associated with all-cause mortality, but cause-specific findings require caution.

Title: Preoperative CALLY Index and Quantitative Left Atrial Low-Voltage Burden are Associated with Documented Recurrence After First Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: We assessed whether preoperative C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index and intraoperative left atrial low-voltage area (LVA) burden provide complementary prognostic information after first ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 259 patients. The endpoint was first documented atrial fibrillation, flutter, or tachycardia lasting ≥30 s after a 60-day blanking period. ln(1/CALLY) and LVA burden were modeled with natural cubic splines in landmark Cox models; diagnostics prompted an extended model allowing LVA effects to vary with log time.
RESULTS: There were 114 recurrences. Both exposures showed nonlinear associations (overall P<0.001; P for nonlinearity=0.011 and 0.004). Relative to the median, the 75th percentile of ln(1/CALLY), where higher values correspond to lower CALLY and a less favorable systemic profile, had HR 1.99 (95% CI 1.47-2.70). Corresponding LVA HRs were 2.41, 4.78, 7.36, and 10.21 at days 90, 150, 240, and 364, although late high-LVA support was sparse. Harrell C increased from 0.648 to 0.819 after adding both markers. Near-12-month performance was similar across fixed Cox, time-varying Cox, and fixed-horizon logistic models.
CONCLUSION: CALLY and LVA burden provided complementary systemic-host and electroanatomic information. Findings are prognostic within the observed operator-directed pathway and require external validation.

Title: Segmental distribution of hepatic steatosis on opportunistic low-dose computed tomography: a Couinaud-based analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis is commonly and incidentally detected on nonenhanced computed tomography (CT) as areas of low attenuation. Hepatic steatosis is recognized as an independent predictor of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), underscoring the clinical significance of its detection and characterization. Low-dose CT (LDCT) performed for lung cancer screening offers a unique opportunity for opportunistic evaluation of hepatic steatosis. The objective of this study is to measure CT attenuation across all eight Couinaud liver segments in patients with incidentally detected hepatic steatosis on lung cancer screening LDCT, and to identify clinical correlates of steatosis.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study evaluated hepatic steatosis among patients who underwent LDCT for lung cancer screening between 2019 and 2024; patients with steatosis and available 1.5 mm soft-tissue reconstructions comprised the analytic cohort for segmental analysis. Steatosis was defined as mean liver attenuation <40 Hounsfield units (HU) on unenhanced CT. Mean CT attenuation (HU) was measured in each Couinaud segment on soft-tissue 1.5 mm unenhanced reconstructions and normalized to intrathoracic tracheal air to reduce interscan variability related to scanner calibration and acquisition parameters. Segmental differences were assessed by repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey-Kramer post-hoc correction. Associations between mean liver HU and clinical variables [age, gender, coronary artery calcification (CAC) score, body mass index, DM] were evaluated using t-tests, and multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,000 patients, steatosis was identified in 79 (7.9%); 68 with available 1.5 mm reconstructions (70.6% male) comprised the analytic cohort. Patients with steatosis were younger (median 61 vs. 63 years, P=0.005) and had higher BMI (mean 32.43 vs. 28.59 kg/m2, P=0.01). Mean liver attenuation was -30.9±30.5 HU (range, -109.2 to +27.6 HU). Segmental attenuation ranged from -27.1±30.8 HU in segment 1 (caudate lobe) to -34.0±30.9 HU in segment 7. Repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant segmental variation (P<0.001); segment 1 showed higher attenuation than segments 3, 4A, 4B, 6, 7, and 8 (all Tukey-adjusted P<0.05), indicating relative caudate sparing. Segments 7 and 8 had the lowest attenuation. Within-patient variability was modest (mean standard deviation: 4.91±1.94 HU), though a subset showed substantial heterogeneity. In multivariable linear regression, older age (β=+0.16/year, P=0.001) and female sex (β=+1.51, P=0.03) were independently associated with higher liver attenuation, while DM was associated with lower attenuation (β=-2.44, P=0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, single-center study, the mean attenuation of segments 7 and 8 combined correlated strongly with whole-liver attenuation and may represent a practical candidate proxy for opportunistic screening. Validation in a larger study is needed before this two-segment measurement approach is adopted for routine use.

Title: Renal Function, OCT-Defined Coronary Calcification and Stent Optimization in Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Single-Center Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced renal function is linked to coronary calcification, which can limit stent expansion, and to contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CI-AKI). We examined renal function, optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined calcification and OCT measures of stent optimization in a Vietnamese provincial hospital.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, cross-sectional study included consecutive patients undergoing OCT-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (December 2023 to January 2026). eGFR was calculated with the CKD-EPI 2021 equation and CI-AKI defined by KDIGO creatinine criteria. Lesion-level associations were estimated by logistic or linear regression with patient-clustered robust standard errors, before and after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, smoking and acute coronary syndrome.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 300 patients, 309 procedures and 356 lesions. Mean eGFR was 79.7 ± 20.7 mL/min/1.73 m2 and 60 procedures (19.4%) had eGFR <60. Calcification was present in 235 lesions (66.0%). Each 10 mL/min/1.73 m2 lower eGFR was associated with calcification in unadjusted analysis (OR 1.19; 95% CI 1.03-1.38), but not after adjustment including age (OR 1.04; 0.88-1.22), whereas age remained associated (OR 1.46 per 10 years; 1.09-1.95). Mean minimum stent area was 5.75 ± 2.26 mm2 and was not correlated with eGFR (ρ=0.05; P=0.36); stent expansion ≥80% (87.4%) and procedural success (88.7%) were not associated with eGFR in crude or adjusted models. CI-AKI occurred in 8 of 206 procedures with paired creatinine (3.9%). Subgroups with eGFR <45 (22 lesions) and <30 (7 lesions) were small, and these analyses were exploratory.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cross-sectional study, the crude association between lower eGFR and OCT-defined calcification was largely explained by age. Under OCT guidance, renal function was not associated with stent optimization, and CI-AKI was infrequent. Prospective studies with larger advanced-CKD populations and a comparator arm are needed to establish whether OCT guidance offsets renal-related procedural disadvantage.

Title: AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumes on non-contrast CT as predictors of mortality in pulmonary hypertension.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumetric measurements in pulmonary hypertension (PH) using non-gated, non-contrast CT.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with suspected PH who underwent non-gated, non-contrast chest CT and right heart catheterisation within one month were retrospectively identified from the Assessing the Spectrum of PH Identified at a Referral Centre (ASPIRE) registry. Two validated deep learning models were used to segment and measure the volumes of cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcifications. The prognostic value of AI-derived cardiothoracic structures and coronary artery calcification volumetric measurements was assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression adjusted for demographics and PH subgroups and REVEAL scores.
RESULTS: Six hundred twenty patients were included (mean age 64 ± 13 years; 62% female; 388 patients died during follow-up), comprising 202 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, 84 with PH-LHD, 112 with PH associated with lung disease, 65 with chronic thromboembolic PH, 9 with unclear PH, and 148 patients without PH. Calcifications were present in the right coronary artery (RCA), mainstem and left anterior descending artery (LAD), and left circumflex artery (LCX) in 45%, 67%, and 35% of patients, respectively. In multivariable Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, and PH subgroup, right atrial (RA) volume was independently associated with mortality (HR 1.024, 95% CI: 1.009-1.039, p = 0.001), as were coronary artery calcifications in the RCA (HR 1.378, 95% CI: 1.113-1.705, p = 0.003), mainstem and LAD (HR 1.868, 95% CI: 1.441-2.421, p < 0.001), and LCX (HR 1.342, 95% CI: 1.084-1.660, p = 0.007). After further adjustment for the REVEAL risk score, these associations remained significant (RA volume HR 1.026, RCA calcification HR 1.604, mainstem and LAD calcification HR 2.339, LCX calcification HR 1.576; all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcifications are independently associated with increased mortality in PH patients.
KEY POINTS: Question The prognostic significance of AI-derived cardiothoracic volumes and coronary artery calcification measured on routine non-gated, non-contrast chest CT in patients with PH remains uncertain. Findings AI-derived RA volume and coronary artery calcification volumes independently predicted mortality in PH patients, even after adjustment for demographics, PH subgroups, and REVEAL score. Relevance statement Automated CT-based AI measurements can provide additional prognostic biomarkers to improve risk stratification in PH beyond established clinical scores.

Title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients.
METHODS: In the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) <5%, MFR >2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders.
RESULTS: Of 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p≤0.009), with modest gains in discrimination (ΔC 0.007-0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow.
CLINICAL PERSPECTIVE: What Is New?: In 3,580 patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve and no coronary artery calcium on PET, more than one in three had ascending aortic calcification on the attenuation correction CT.Ascending aortic calcification was independently associated with cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission (adjusted hazard ratio per SD 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40), most strongly with heart failure admission.A fast, fully automated method scored ascending aortic calcification with agreement to expert readers similar to agreement between readers.What Are the Clinical Implications?: A normal perfusion PET with normal flow and no coronary calcium does not mean uniformly low risk when the ascending aorta is calcified.Because ascending aortic calcification is scored automatically from the CT acquired with every perfusion PET, it could be reported routinely without additional scanning, cost or radiation.Patients presumed low risk who have ascending aortic calcification may warrant heart failure-oriented prevention, such as natriuretic peptide screening, pending prospective validation.

Title: Population-based Ethnoracial Disparity in Life's Essential 8 Vascular Health, Cerebral Small Vessel Disease & Cognition.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether ethnoracial differences in cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) appear in multimarker burden, particular MRI manifestations, or both, and how they relate to Life's Essential 8 (LE8) cardiovascular health and cognition, is unclear.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 44,982 participants and an age- and sex-matched subsample of 1,426 with reviewed lacune and cerebral microbleed (CMB) ratings. White, South Asian, Black, Chinese and Mixed participants were compared on 0-2 (white matter hyperintensity [WMH]/enlarged perivascular space [ePVS]) and 0-4 (adding CMB and lacunes) composite scores and each marker. LE8 was related to WMH and composite burden, and cognitive means were compared by group. Models were age-, sex- and center-adjusted with false-discovery-rate correction.
RESULTS: Both composite scores differed across groups (0-2: P=0.00010; 0-4: P=0.0011), with greater burden in Black than South Asian (0-4: OR 1.66; 95% CI, 1.21-2.28) and Chinese participants (OR 2.36; 1.51-3.70), whereas Black-White contrasts were not detected. Black participants had higher WMH volume than White participants (β=0.209; 0.110-0.308), robust to deprivation adjustment and segmentation method; South Asian participants had fewer ePVS (0.82; 0.72-0.93). No ethnoracial-group differences in lacune or CMB counts were detected after correction. Higher LE8 was associated with lower WMH volume (β=-0.13 per SD; -0.17 to -0.09) and lower two-marker burden (OR 0.89 per SD; 0.87-0.91) without detected ethnoracial moderation. Black participants, who had the least favorable LE8 scores, and South Asian participants had lower global cognition than White participants (z -0.76 and -0.57 versus 0.24) despite differing WMH profiles; the pooled WMH-cognition association was null.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethnoracial differences in multimarker cSVD burden were evident but marker-dependent: WMH showed the clearest Black-White difference; focal-lesion contrasts were inconclusive. Better cardiovascular health related to lower WMH and aggregate cSVD burden across groups, whereas cognitive differences did not track cSVD burden, supporting prospective prevention and cognition studies.

Title: Association Between Colchicine Use and Clinical Outcomes Post Cardiac Surgery: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colchicine has been shown to mitigate inflammation and reduce adverse cardiovascular events. However, evidence from clinical trials has been mixed regarding its efficacy in cardiovascular prevention among patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic literature search on various electronic databases for relevant studies from their inception until July 15, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with two arms-one with colchicine as an intervention and the other with placebo-in patients undergoing cardiac surgery were included. Risk ratios (RRs) and weighted mean differences (WMDs), along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were pooled using a random-effects model. A p value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Nine RCTs with 2005 patients (990 in the colchicine group and 1015 in the placebo group) were included. The mean age was 62.8 years. Pooled analysis demonstrated that compared with placebo, colchicine was significantly associated with a reduction in the risk of postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) (RR 0.70 [95% CI 0.59-0.83], p < 0.001). However, between the groups, there was no statistically significant difference in the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) (RR 0.81 [95% CI 0.39-1.69], p = 0.57, I2 = 0%), stroke (RR 1.86 [95% CI 0.48-7.12], p = 0.37), and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPM) (RR 1.36 [95% CI 0.08-22.44], p = 0.83). Length of hospital stay, which was exploratory, was significantly shorter in the colchicine group (WMD - 1.16 [95% CI - 1.89 to - 0.44], p < 0.01) compared to placebo.
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis demonstrates that colchicine appears to reduce the risk of POAF. However, it does not significantly affect the risks in terms of PPM, ACM, or stroke.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420251117966.

Title: Body composition in octogenarians with chronic kidney disease. Role of gender.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The population with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is undergoing marked ageing, and octogenarian patients represent a growing group with distinctive clinical and functional characteristics. In this context, alterations in fluid status and body composition (BC) limit the usefulness of body mass index, necessitating a more accurate assessment with bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). The aim of this study was to evaluate gender-related differences in body composition in octogenarian patients with CKD in a prospective observational cohort study with a 14-year longitudinal follow-up of clinical events.
METHODS: A total of 724 patients were included (46.4% women), with a mean age of 84.7 years and a mean estimated glomerular filtration rate of 36.6 ml/min/1.73 m2. Vectorial tetrapolar BIA was used to analyse body composition parameters, hydration status, and bioelectrical variables, while muscle strength was assessed by handgrip dynamometry. In addition, risk of progression to kidney replacement therapy, fracture risk, cardiovascular risk, and age-adjusted comorbidity were evaluated.
RESULTS: The results revealed clinically relevant gender differences. Women exhibited lower comorbidity and a lower risk of initiating kidney replacement therapy, but a significantly higher risk of osteoporotic and hip fractures. From a BC perspective, women showed higher adiposity and a greater proportion of ECW, together with lower muscle mass, lower TBW and ICW, and reduced muscle strength. Men presented greater muscle mass and strength but a higher prevalence of dynapenia. Overall sarcopenia was infrequent in the cohort.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a marked sexual dimorphism in body composition and functional status among octogenarians with CKD, with important clinical implications for risk stratification and individualized management in this population.

Title: Air Embolism During Cryoballoon Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation Under Different Respiratory Management Strategies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary air embolism is a rare but potentially fatal complication during catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF). Use of large-bore sheaths, such as those required for balloon-based catheter ablation, in the setting of unstable respiratory control may increase the risk.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated consecutive patients who underwent first-time cryoballoon ablation (CBA) for AF from January 2017 to December 2024. Patients were divided into two groups according to respiratory management strategy: adaptive servo-ventilation (ASV, n = 266) and laryngeal mask with mechanical ventilation (LM, n = 225). The incidence of complications was compared, with a primary focus on air embolism.
RESULTS: A total of 491 patients (median age 68 years, 71.3% male) were included. Coronary air embolism occurred in 5 patients (1.9%) in the ASV group and in none of the patients in the LM group (absolute risk difference, 1.9%; 95% CI, -0.1% to 4.3%; p = 0.066). In one patient with coronary air embolism, brain MRI performed on the day of the procedure incidentally revealed an asymptomatic acute cerebral embolic lesion. Other complications included two cases of cardiac tamponade in the ASV group and two cases of transient phrenic nerve palsy in the LM group.
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary air embolism was numerically less frequent in patients undergoing cryoballoon ablation with laryngeal mask ventilation than in those managed with ASV, although the difference did not reach statistical significance. Further prospective studies are warranted to clarify the potential role of respiratory management in procedural safety.

Title: Home Blood Pressure-Guided Lifestyle Intervention for Elevated Blood Pressure Detected at Workplace Health Checkups: A Randomized Pilot Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Workplace health checkups may identify elevated blood pressure (BP), but a single measurement may not reflect usual BP. We evaluated home BP-guided lifestyle management after elevated BP was detected at a workplace health checkup.
METHODS: Fifty-eight municipal employees were randomized to home BP monitoring plus physician-led lifestyle counseling (n = 31) or the same counseling without home BP feedback (n = 27). Both groups received two scheduled counseling sessions. The primary outcome was change in systolic BP at the subsequent annual health checkup.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group had greater reductions in systolic BP (between-group difference, -9.9 mmHg; 95% CI, -17.0 to -2.8; p = 0.007). After excluding three participants who initiated antihypertensive medication, the systolic BP difference remained significant (-7.7 mmHg; 95% CI, -14.6 to -0.8; p = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: Home BP-guided lifestyle counseling may improve management of elevated BP detected at workplace health checkups.

Title: Prevalence and One-Year Incidence of Patient-Healthcare Professional Discussions About Sexual Health in Hypertensive Adults in France: A Cohort Study.
Abstract: The association between hypertension and sexual dysfunction is documented in both men and women. However, data about sexual health management in hypertensive adults is scarce internationally and non-existent in France. In this context, our study aimed to estimate the prevalence and the one-year incidence of discussions about sexual health between hypertensive adults and healthcare professionals in France. A cohort study was conducted among hypertensive adults over a one-year period. The prevalence and temporality of discussion prior to inclusion were estimated in the overall sample (N = 676) and the one-year incidence was estimated among those who declared never having discussed sexual health in their lifetime prior the inclusion and completed at least one follow-up questionnaire (n = 279). Missing data was handled using multiple imputation, and attrition bias during follow-up was corrected using inverse probability weighting. Almost half (44.2%) individuals reported having never discussed about sexual health prior to inclusion. The one-year incidence was estimated at 12.8% [8.7-17.0]. Around a quarter (23.3% [18.1-28.4]) declared they wanted to discuss about it at least once during the follow-up period but only 9.1% [1.97-16.2] of them finally had a discussion after having expressed this wish. Our results highlighted the low integration of sexuality into clinical care, and the extent of this communication gap. We are calling for increased awareness among healthcare professionals of the sexual aspects of cardiovascular health. Taking a more systematic approach to sexual health could improve quality of life, therapeutic alliance and adherence to treatment, all of which are essential for controlling hypertension.

Title: Blood Pressure Variability in Neurodegenerative Disease: Evidence From a Large-Scale Remote Patient Monitoring Program.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood pressure variability (BPV) is an established predictor of cardiovascular risk, yet its physiologic determinants in specific populations remain incompletely defined. Neurodegenerative diseases are associated with autonomic dysfunction that may alter blood pressure regulation.
METHODS: We compared day-to-day systolic blood pressure (SBP) variability between patients with neurodegenerative disease and matched controls in a retrospective analysis of de-identified home blood pressure data from a remote patient monitoring platform. Eligible patients transmitted readings on at least three days per week over a monitoring stretch of at least eight weeks. Patients with Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, or dementia were propensity-matched 1:3 to controls on age, mean SBP, mean diastolic blood pressure (DBP), stretch duration, and days per week with readings. The primary metric was average real variability (ARV), the mean absolute difference between consecutive values; standard deviation (SD) and variability independent of the mean (VIM) were secondary metrics.
RESULTS: The matched cohort included 49 neurodegenerative patients and 147 controls. SBP ARV was higher in the neurodegenerative group (median 12.92 [IQR 10.74-15.35] vs. 11.19 [9.46-12.99] mmHg; p = 0.003), as was DBP ARV (7.72 [6.34-8.87] vs. 6.76 [5.67-7.75] mmHg; p = 0.002). SD and VIM results were concordant (all p ≤ 0.001). Mean blood pressure, monitoring duration, measurement frequency, and reading timing were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Neurodegenerative disease is associated with elevated day-to-day BPV despite similar mean blood pressure and monitoring behavior, suggesting that routine home monitoring may reveal autonomic dysregulation and cardiovascular risk beyond mean blood pressure alone.

Title: Continuous Associations and Predictive Performance of Electrocardiographic Voltage- and Product-Based Indices for Incident Hypertension: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrocardiographic (ECG) indices-Sokolow-Lyon voltage (SLV), Cornell voltage (CV), and Cornell product (CP)-have traditionally been used to detect left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), including that associated with established hypertension. However, it remains unclear whether these ECG indices, including values below conventional LVH thresholds, provide predictive information for incident hypertension before overt blood pressure (BP) elevation.
METHODS: We included 2860 adults from a prospective cohort with a baseline BP < 130/80 mmHg, no antihypertensive therapy, and no prior cardiovascular disease. Associations of SLV, CV, and CP with incident hypertension-defined as BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or initiation of antihypertensive medication-were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression, and their predictive performance was assessed.
RESULTS: During follow-up (mean 6.2 ± 3.0 years), 943 participants (33.0%) developed hypertension. Each 1-SD increase in sex-specific standardized ECG indices was independently associated with a higher risk of incident hypertension, with multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) of 1.30 (1.22-1.38) for SLV, 1.15 (1.08-1.22) for CV, and 1.15 (1.08-1.22) for CP. Restricted cubic spline analyses showed predominantly linear associations, although modest non-linearity was observed for SLV (p = 0.047). The addition of SLV, CV, or CP to a conventional risk model improved discrimination and reclassification at 5 and 7 years (e.g., 5-year area under the curve: base model, 0.774 vs. base model + SLV, 0.787; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: SLV, CV, and CP provide complementary predictive information for incident hypertension beyond conventional risk factors, suggesting that the predictive utility of these ECG indices extends across their full range of values.

Title: Elevated plasma phenylacetylglutamine is independently associated with heart failure: A cross-sectional biomarker study.
Journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
Abstract: Phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a microbial metabolite generated from dietary phenylalanine, has emerged as a candidate mediator in cardiovascular disease, but whether it holds diagnostic value for heart failure (HF) is unclear. We designed a cross-sectional case-control study at Xiangya Hospital, enrolling 104 participants (65 stable HF patients and 39 non-HF controls), to address this question. Plasma PAGln was quantified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). Concentrations were significantly higher in the HF group than in controls (median 1.7 vs. 1.2 μM, P = 0.001). After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, lifestyle factors, comorbidities, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, every 1-SD increase in log-transformed PAGln raised HF odds by 95% (odds ratio [OR] 1.95, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-3.56, P = 0.030). The top tertile carried 4.57-fold greater odds than the bottom tertile (OR 4.57, 95% CI 1.08-19.45, P = 0.040). On receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, PAGln achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.658 (95% CI 0.551-0.764) with 46.2% sensitivity and 84.6% specificity. PAGln tracked positively with LDL-C, total cholesterol, and fasting glucose, and inversely with estimated glomerular filtration rate. Notably, the highest PAGln levels were seen in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), with a significant difference between non-HF and HFrEF subgroups (P = 0.01). Collectively, our results indicate that elevated plasma PAGln is independently linked to HF and may reflect disease severity, supporting its potential as a complementary metabolic biomarker for HF evaluation.

Title: Frailty Burden in Patients with HFrEF Undergoing Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: Clinical Outcomes and Readmissions.
Journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes across cardiovascular populations. However, its prognostic significance, particularly the impact of graded frailty burden, among patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia (VT) remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We evaluated the association between frailty burden and in-hospital outcomes among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation using the Nationwide Readmissions Database. Frailty was defined using the validated Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) frailty indicator. Cumulative frailty burden was quantified as the number of domains (range: 0-10). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations with outcomes, and in-hospital mortality probabilities were estimated across increasing frailty burden.
RESULTS: Among 17,367 hospitalizations for VT ablation in patients with HFrEF, 7.4% were classified as frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.59; 95% CI, 1.19-2.13; p<0.001), and increased complication rates. Frail patients had higher 30-day (13.6% vs. 9.1%) and 90-day (33.7% vs. 28.1%) readmission rates compared with non-frail patients. Frailty burden demonstrated a graded association with in-hospital mortality, with estimated mortality increasing progressively with each additional frailty domain.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes and higher readmission rates among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation, with a graded increase in risk across increasing frailty domains. These findings suggest that frailty burden may serve as a clinically relevant risk stratification marker in this vulnerable cohort.

Title: Prevalence of coronary artery disease on coronary CT angiography in asymptomatic, predominantly high-risk Indian adults: A single-centre cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) in South Asians often develops at a younger age and may not be adequately detected by conventional risk stratification or coronary artery calcium scoring (CACS). In this study we assessed the prevalence of CAD in asymptomatic, predominantly physician-referred individuals undergoing coronary CT angiography (CCTA).
METHODS: This single-centre cross-sectional study included 1750 asymptomatic individuals, predominantly physician-referred for cardiovascular risk assessment, who underwent CCTA between 2019 and 2024. Clinical risk factors, Framingham risk score (FRS), and CACS were recorded. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of CAD. Prevalence of CAD in low FRS and CACS was further analysed.
RESULTS: CAD was detected in 1084 individuals (62%), including 787 (45%) with non-obstructive and 297 (17%) with obstructive disease, while coronary calcification (CACS >0) was seen in 957 (54.6%) patients. Increasing FRS scores were associated with increased CAD prevalence (p < 0.001). Increasing CACS was also associated with CAD severity (p < 0.001). On multivariable logistic regression, independent predictors of CAD included age (OR 1.09 per year, 95%CI 1.08-1.11), male sex (OR 2.20, 95%CI 1.55-3.13), diabetes (OR 2.07, 95%CI 1.56-2.76), hypertension (OR 1.47, 95%CI 1.09-1.98), obesity (OR 1.45, 95%CI 1.00-2.10), and elevated LDL/HDL ratio>4 (OR 1.93, 95%CI 1.22-3.04).
CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort of asymptomatic, predominantly high-risk Indian adults referred for CCTA, subclinical coronary atherosclerosis was common, including among individuals with low Framingham risk or zero coronary calcium. Whether detecting such disease with CCTA improves outcomes or is cost-effective requires prospective, outcome-based evaluation.

Title: Segment and side specific determinants of carotid atherosclerotic burden: evidence for a distinct left internal carotid artery phenotype.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Carotid atherosclerosis is an important feature in patients with cerebrovascular events, but its determinants may vary across arterial segments and sides. We assessed segment- and side-specific determinants of carotid atherosclerotic burden.
METHODS: We studied 177 patients aged 18-65 years who were hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke or TIA and underwent carotid ultrasonography. Atherosclerotic involvement of bilateral common carotid arteries, carotid bifurcations and internal carotid arteries was assessed using a Burden of Disease (BoD) score. We examined segment-specific associations between BoD, stenosis severity and cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: Plaques were more frequent at the carotid bifurcation and in the internal carotid artery than in the common carotid artery. After Bonferroni correction, age and hypertension were associated with BoD in the carotid bifurcation and internal carotid segments bilaterally; hypertension was also associated with left common carotid BoD (p = 0.003). BMI was associated with right bifurcation and internal carotid BoD (p = 0.007 and p = 0.005), Lp(a) >30 mg/dL with left internal carotid BoD (p = 0.002), and fibrinogen with left common carotid BoD (p = 0.005). The multivariable model for the left internal carotid artery explained the largest proportion of variance (R2 = 0.274), with contributions from hypertension (0.092), Lp(a) >30 mg/dL (0.084), BMI (0.036), fibrinogen (0.035) and atrial fibrillation (0.027). Associations with stenosis severity were less consistent (n = 16-54).
CONCLUSIONS: In this symptomatic cohort, carotid atherosclerotic burden showed segment- and side-specific associations with cardiovascular risk factors. The broader range of associations in the left internal carotid artery is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

Title: Predicting prosthetic use and survival following transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine associations between BLARt, CFS, prosthetic use and 24-month survival after unilateral transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 168 adults aged ≥65 years who underwent unilateral transfemoral amputation between 2019 and 2023. BLARt was analysed as a continuous score and CFS as an ordinal measure grouped as ≤4, 5 and ≥6. Prosthetic-use analyses excluded participants who had died by the relevant time point. Logistic regression, exact tests, ROC analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis were used.
RESULTS: At discharge, 23 of 132 survivors (17.4%) were using a prosthesis; at 24 months, 17 of 80 survivors (21.3%) were using one. Higher BLARt scores were associated with lower odds of prosthetic use at discharge (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.33-0.60) and 24 months (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.69; both p<.001). Prosthetic use differed across CFS groups at both time points (p<.001), with no prosthetic users among participants with CFS ≥6. By 24 months, 88 participants (52.4%) had died. Compared with CFS ≤4, adjusted odds of death were higher for CFS 5 (OR 4.12, 95% CI 1.12-15.20) and CFS ≥6 (OR 8.40, 95% CI 1.97-35.80). CFS and the combined mortality model each had an AUC of approximately 0.71.
CONCLUSIONS: BLARt was associated with prosthetic use among survivors, while increasing frailty was strongly associated with both lower prosthetic use and higher 24-month mortality. These measures may support multidisciplinary prognostic discussion but should not be used as rigid thresholds for prosthetic rehabilitation.

Title: ACEs and CKL diseases in middle and old age: Multistate model and MR analysis of a national cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with chronic diseases, but evidence regarding their impact on cardiovascular, kidney, and liver (CKL) diseases and multimorbidity remains limited. This study examines the association between ACEs and the onset of CKL diseases, and explores the potential mediating role of depressive symptoms.
METHODS: The study included 7184 middle-aged and older adults aged ≥45 years without CKL disease at baseline from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2018). Cox models were used to assess the association between ACEs and new-onset disease; multistate models were employed to analyse the risk of disease transition; mediation analysis was conducted to examine the mediating role of depressive symptoms. Two-sample Mendelian randomization was further applied as an independent triangulation analysis of the association between genetic liability to depression and selected outcomes.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 84 months, there were 1428, 547, 379 and 300 new cases of CVD, CKD, CLD and CKL multimorbidity, respectively. The risk of CVD, CKD, CLD and CKL multimorbidity was increased by 30% [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.15, 1.45], 37% (95% CI: 1.13, 1.66), 35% (95% CI: 1.07, 1.70) and 46% (95% CI: 1.12, 1.89), respectively, with a graded association observed across ACE categories (all P-trend <0.05). ACEs were significantly associated with the initial transition from health to CKL disease. Depressive symptoms acted as a potential mediator, and Mendelian randomization provided genetic evidence on the association between depression and selected cardiovascular outcomes.
CONCLUSION: ACEs were associated with higher risks of CVD, CKD, CLD and CKL multimorbidity in middle-aged and older adults, with depressive symptoms as a potential mediator. ACE history and depressive symptoms may help identify high-risk individuals, supporting further exploration of integrated management strategies for chronic diseases.

Title: Extended Clopidogrel Monotherapy versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Coronary Syndrome Patients With and Without Heart Failure: A Prespecified Subgroup Analysis of the OPT-BIRISK Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal extended antiplatelet strategy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in patients with heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
METHODS: In OPT-BIRISK, patients at high ischemic and bleeding risk who completed 9-12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) were randomized to clopidogrel plus placebo or aspirin for 9 months. This analysis compared treatments by recorded HF history. The primary endpoint was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) types 2, 3, or 5 bleeding; the key secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebral events (MACCE).
RESULTS: Of 7,758 patients, 653 (8.4%) had HF history. Without HF, bleeding occurred in 83/3,565 (2.3%) monotherapy recipients and 118/3,540 (3.3%) DAPT recipients (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.53-0.92). With HF, bleeding occurred in 12/308 (3.9%) and 9/345 (2.6%), respectively (HR 1.49, 95% CI 0.63-3.53). MACCE occurred in 90/3,565 (2.5%) versus 120/3,540 (3.4%) patients without HF (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.98) and 11/308 (3.6%) versus 16/345 (4.6%) patients with HF (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.36-1.66). Interaction P values were 0.1021 for bleeding and 0.9345 for MACCE.
CONCLUSIONS: Extended clopidogrel monotherapy reduced clinically relevant bleeding in patients without a history of HF after PCI for ACS. No statistically significant treatment-by-HF interaction was observed for bleeding or MACCE, although HF-specific treatment effects remain inconclusive because of limited events.

Title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes.
Abstract:
TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between statin use and the prevalence, incidence, and progression of age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: AMD is a major cause of vision loss in older adults, many of whom receive statins for cardiovascular prevention.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through October 2025 for randomized trials and cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies with comparators. We assessed risk of bias with tools appropriate to each design and pooled effect measures separately using random-effects models. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies included 1,918,120 participants. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) for the prevalence of any, early, and late AMD were 1.03 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-1.24), 1.10 (95% CI, 0.92-1.31), and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.46-1.25), respectively. For incidence of any AMD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.82-1.31) and the OR was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.43-1.34), with substantial heterogeneity. For neovascular AMD incidence, different study subsets suggested lower hazard (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.60-0.85) and higher risk (risk ratio, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.44); the OR was inconclusive (0.93; 95% CI, 0.82-1.05). Progression evidence was limited and heterogeneous. Ten of 12 longitudinal nonrandomized studies had serious overall risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.

Title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS.
METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor.
INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS.
FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

Title: The prognostic role of echocardiographic parameters in ischemic stroke patients with atrial fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) in stroke patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with an unfavourable outcome, but the additional prognostic value of echocardiographic parameters remains unclear.
METHODS: We included consecutive patients with recent AF-associated ischemic stroke (IS) or transient ischemic attack (TIA) who underwent echocardiography and brain MRI from the prospective Novel Oral Anticoagulants in Ischemic Stroke Patients registry. We examined associations of left atrial and ventricular echocardiographic parameters with a primary composite outcome (recurrent IS; intracranial hemorrhage, all-cause death) and its components as secondary outcomes, using unadjusted and adjusted (age, sex, modified CHA2DS2VASc-Score, hyperlipidemia, oral anticoagulation before/after stroke, MRI markers of cSVD) Cox regression. Associations between echocardiographic parameters and MRI markers of cSVD were analyzed using logistic regression.
RESULTS: We included 690 patients (median age 80, 45% female) with a total follow-up of 1084 patient-years. In unadjusted analyses, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) was associated with the composite outcome (HR 1.44 [1.05-1.97]) and all-cause death (HR 1.95 [1.33-2.84]), neither association persisted after adjustment (aHR 1.04 [0.74-1.46]; aHR 1.29 [0.85-1.96]) Reduced ejection fraction and concentric/eccentric hypertrophy were associated with all-cause death in unadjusted analysis only. No echocardiographic parameter was associated with recurrent IS. Left atrial dilatation (OR 1.96 [1.32-2.91]) and concentric hypertrophy were associated (OR 1.68 [1.08-2.62]) with white matter hyperintensities extent in unadjusted but not in adjusted analyses.
CONCLUSION: In stroke patients with AF, structural changes of the left ventricle might be considered as indicator but not independent predictor of future cerebrovascular events or death.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03826927.

Title: Restrictive versus liberal red blood cell transfusion thresholds in haemodynamically stable adults: explaining variability in patient blood management guidelines.
Journal: Transfusion and apheresis science : official journal of the World Apheresis Association : official journal of the European Society for Haemapheresis
Abstract: Patient Blood Management (PBM) promotes strategies to avoid unnecessary red blood cell transfusion. Guidelines broadly support restrictive transfusion for haemodynamically stable adults who are not actively bleeding, yet thresholds differ for some patient groups despite resting on the same trials. This narrative review examines landmark randomised trials (TRICC, FOCUS, TITRe2, REALITY, MINT, HEMOTION and TRAIN) and how they were incorporated into recommendations from major societies, including the 2025 AABB and ACC/AHA recommendations for acute myocardial infarction. For most stable adults, restrictive thresholds of 7-8 g/dL reduce transfusion exposure without increasing major adverse outcomes. Recommendations diverge where the certainty of evidence is lower. In acute myocardial infarction, MINT reported death or recurrent myocardial infarction at 30 days in 16.9% of restrictive-strategy and 14.5% of liberal-strategy patients (risk ratio 1.15; 95% CI 0.99-1.34); the 2025 AABB guideline conditionally recommends a liberal strategy (haemoglobin <10 g/dL) and the 2025 ACC/AHA guideline states that transfusion to maintain haemoglobin of at least 10 g/dL may be reasonable (Class 2b). In acute brain injury, HEMOTION and TRAIN reached different conclusions. These differences reflect populations, evidence certainty and guideline methodology rather than disagreement about PBM principles. We also consider why threshold trials so often show no difference, why haemoglobin is an imperfect surrogate for tissue oxygenation, and why thresholds do not apply to active haemorrhage. Prehospital whole blood showed no advantage over components, and the optimal timing of red cell transfusion in bleeding remains unresolved.

Title: Impact of oral diuretic monitoring duration prior to discharge on 30-day heart failure readmission rates.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend transitioning patients with heart failure (HF) to oral diuretics prior to discharge, yet data guiding the optimal duration of oral diuretic monitoring remains limited. Prior retrospective studies assessed discharge-day oral diuretics or used a 24-hour monitoring cutoff.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate time on oral diuretic prior to discharge and 30-day HF readmission.
METHODS: This single center retrospective study included patients admitted for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) between 1/2020-9/2022. The primary end-point was 30-day HF readmission. Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds of readmission across varying durations of oral diuretic therapy (<24, 24-47, 48-71, and ≥72 h). Inverse propensity score weights (IPTW) were applied to control for confounder variables. Statistical significance was assessed using 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: A total of 466 patients were included (mean age 67.2 + 16.2 years; 56.2% male). IPTW results showed no significant difference in readmission rates for patients on diuretics < 24-hour group compared to 24-47 h (odds ratio (OR) 0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.36, 1.67], 48-71 h (OR 0.78 [CI 0.36, 1.69]), and ≥72 h (OR 0.99 [CI 0.45, 2.15]). There was no significant difference in readmission rates when comparing <24 h versus ≥24 h of oral diuretic therapy (OR 0.85 [CI 0.43, 1.68]).
CONCLUSION: In patients with ADHF, extending oral diuretic monitoring beyond 24 h before discharge was not associated with reduced 30-day HF readmissions. Future studies should investigate the relationship between time on oral diuretics and overall response prior to discharge.

Title: Association between biological age acceleration and the risk of aortic valve stenosis: An observational epidemiologic and Mendelian randomization study.
Journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Biological age acceleration (BAA) is thought to be a major risk factor for age-related diseases, but its role in aortic valve stenosis (AVS) remains uncertain. We aimed to assess the associations between biological aging and the risk of AVS.
METHODS: This study involved 4526 participants from the Real-world Data of Cardiometabolic Protection (RED-CARPET) study and 5114 participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study. BAA was assessed using clinical biomarkers through the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM) and the PhenoAge algorithm. We employed multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression to examine the association between BAA and AVS risk. Additionally, Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was conducted to assess causality.
RESULTS: In the RED-CARPET cohort of 4526 participants (mean age 60.93 years, 33.5% female), 113 AVS events were recorded. In the ARIC cohort of 5114 participants (mean age 51.94 years, 56.4% female, 82.3% White), there were 266 AVS events. After fully adjusting for confounding variables, each standard deviation increase in BAA was significantly associated with elevated AVS risk (RED-CARPET: KDM-BA acceleration: OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.07-1.55; PhenoAge acceleration: OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.24-1.77; ARIC: KDM-BA acceleration: OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.24-1.63; PhenoAge acceleration: OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11-1.51). The RCS regression model revealed significant linear relationships between BAA and the risk of AVS in both cohorts. MR analysis suggested a potential causal relationship between KDM-BA acceleration and AVS risk (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.21-1.57).
CONCLUSION: BAA, as derived from clinical biomarkers, is independently associated with an increased risk of AVS. This finding suggests that BAA, as a composite indicator of systemic biological aging, may complement traditional risk factors in the early identification of high-risk populations for AVS, and offer the possibility of early intervention for prevention.

Title: Evaluating the impact of hypoglossal nerve stimulator therapy on cardiovascular and metabolic outcomes in sleep apnea patients: A retrospective cohort analysis.
Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea is associated with comorbidities such as obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension. While continuous positive airway pressure therapy has been shown to improve these conditions, the impact of hypoglossal nerve stimulation remains less defined. This retrospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the effect of hypoglossal nerve stimulation on blood pressure, mean arterial pressure, hemoglobin A1c, and body mass index in patients with obstructive sleep apnea. Adult patients who underwent hypoglossal nerve stimulator implantation between February 2017 and June 2024 at a tertiary academic medical center were included. Exclusion criteria included device removal, transfer of care following activation, or loss to follow-up. Of 210 patients, 141 met inclusion criteria, with age ranging 18 to 87 years, and 60.3% male. Over a two-year follow-up, systolic and diastolic blood pressures fluctuated without reaching statistical significance, while mean arterial pressure demonstrated a downward trend that approached significance at the two-year time point. Hemoglobin A1c and body mass index also varied over time without significant change. The mean Apnea-Hypopnea Index improved substantially from 36.0 at baseline to 5.9 at titration follow-up, and overall institutional compliance with hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy was 83.5%. In this cohort, hypoglossal nerve stimulation significantly improved obstructive sleep apnea severity but did not result in significant changes in blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c, or body mass index. The observed trend toward lower mean arterial pressure suggests a potential cardiovascular benefit, warranting further investigation into the broader metabolic effects of hypoglossal nerve stimulation in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.

Title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Recurrent Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The definition of very high risk from the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology 2018 and 2026 cholesterol guidelines may oversimplify heterogeneity in recurrent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk.
OBJECTIVES: We developed a prediction model for recurrent ASCVD and compared its performance with the 2018 cholesterol guideline.
METHODS: We used electronic health records from Kaiser Permanente Southern California (KPSC) for model development and the REGARDS (Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke) cohort for external validation. We included adults with a prior ASCVD and followed them for recurrent ASCVD or up to 10 years. We used elastic net regularization for predictor selection and a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model for model development. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve, sensitivity, and specificity compared with the 2018 guideline.
RESULTS: Among 70,310 and 5,239 adults from KPSC and REGARDS, 17,344 and 1,185 experienced recurrent ASCVD during the median (Q1, Q3) follow-up of 6.1 (2.5, 10) and 8.3 (4.0, 10) years, respectively. Time-dependent area under the curves were 0.68 (95% CI: 0.66-0.69) in KPSC and 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65-0.69) in REGARDS. Compared with the 2018 guideline, using a 5-year 15% risk threshold, the model classified a similar proportion of patients as high risk and improved sensitivity from 64% (95% CI: 62%-66%) to 73% (95% CI: 71%-75%) in KPSC and from 69% (95% CI: 65%-72%) to 73% (95% CI: 69%-76%) in REGARDS; specificity remained similar in KPSC (51% and 52%) and improved in REGARDS (from 45% to 50%).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the 2018 cholesterol guideline, the new model improves identification of individuals at very high risk of recurrent ASCVD, supporting more personalized treatment decisions.

Title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In a target-directed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C)-lowering strategy, the impact of the initial treatment regimen has not been investigated in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We compared the efficacy and safety of initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy versus statin monotherapy within intensive or conventional LDL-C-targeting strategies.
METHODS: In this prespecified second randomization of the randomized Ez-PAVE trial (Effects of Ezetimibe Combination Therapy for Patients With Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Randomized Comparison of LDL Cholesterol Targeting <70 versus <55 mg/dL) conducted at 17 centers in South Korea, a total of 3048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled between January 2021 and July 2022. Following the first randomization to either an intensive (<55 mg/dL) or conventional (<70 mg/dL) LDL-C-targeting strategy, patients underwent subsequent randomization (initial statin-ezetimibe combination therapy [n=1525] versus statin monotherapy [n=1523]) and were followed up for 3 years. Lipid-lowering therapy was adjusted according to a predefined protocol to achieve LDL-C targets. The primary end point was a 3-year composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, any revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina.
RESULTS: The mean±SD age was 64.4±9.0 years, and 638 patients (20.9%) were female. The incidence of the primary end point did not differ between statin-ezetimibe combination therapy (128 patients [8.5%]) and statin monotherapy (119 patients [7.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.83-1.37]; P=0.596). Patients who received statin-ezetimibe combination therapy achieved lower median LDL-C levels during follow-up than those who received statin monotherapy in both the intensive-targeting (53 mg/dL [interquartile range, 45-62 mg/dL] versus 62 mg/dL [interquartile range, 53-74 mg/dL]) and conventional-targeting (63 mg/dL [interquartile range, 55-73 mg/dL] versus 70 mg/dL [interquartile range, 62-81 mg/dL]) strategies. During follow-up, ezetimibe was added to the treatment regimen of 241 patients (34.3%) and 177 patients (24.8%) who initially received statin monotherapy in the intensive- and conventional-targeting strategies, respectively. The treatment effect of intensive-targeting versus conventional-targeting strategies was consistent regardless of therapy regimens without significant heterogeneity (Pinteraction=0.583). The safety end points were similar between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Within a target-directed LDL-C-lowering strategy, cardiovascular efficacy and safety did not differ significantly, whether initiated as statin-ezetimibe combination therapy or as statin monotherapy, but combination therapy facilitated achievement of a lower LDL-C target.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04626973.

Title: Smart Alerting in Smartphone-Based First Responder Systems and Arrival Before Emergency Medical Services:The ALARM Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smartphone alerting systems (SAS) aim to increase the proportion of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) cases in which a community first responder (CFR) arrives before emergency medical services (EMS). Many use fixed-radius alerts and ignore estimated arrival times. We compared different alerting strategies to maximize CFR arrival before EMS.
METHODS: In a prospective, randomized three-arm trial, smart alerting (SMA) was compared with fixed-radius strategies (600 m and 2500 m). The primary endpoint was the rate of CFR arrival before EMS. In the SMA arm, responders were dispatched based on individually estimated travel times versus expected ambulance time. Binary endpoints were analyzed using chi-square tests, reporting risk differences and 95% confidence intervals; continuous endpoints used non-parametric tests.
RESULTS: Across 823 activations, 1482 CFR were dispatched. CFR arrived before EMS in 31%, 57%, and 58% of missions in the 600 m, 2500 m, and SMA groups, respectively. Compared with the 600 m strategy, SMA increased pre-EMS arrival (risk difference +26.8%, 95% CI 18.6-34.4; p < 0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed compared with the 2500 m strategy (risk difference +1.2%, 95% CI -7.0-+9.3; p = 0.80). Response rates were 56%, 83%, and 87%, respectively. In the SMA group, 31% of accepting CFR were excluded because predicted arrival exceeded EMS arrival. Response times were longer with smart alerting reflecting greater dispatch distances.
CONCLUSIONS: Smart alerting increased the likelihood of CFR arriving before EMS while reducing dispatches unlikely to achieve pre-EMS arrival. Further research should evaluate its impact on patient outcomes.

Title: Integrated Prenatal Cardiopulmonary Assessment Using Fetal Echocardiography in Isolated Left-Sided Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prenatal severity assessment in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) primarily relies on lung-based parameters such as the observed-to-expected lung-to-head ratio (o/eLHR) and liver position; however, these markers do not fully reflect fetal cardiopulmonary adaptation. We investigated the prognostic significance of fetal echocardiographic parameters and integrated these in prenatal prediction models in left-sided CDH.
METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective study included fetuses with prenatally diagnosed isolated left-sided CDH. Gestational age-adjusted Z-scores were generated for fetal cardiac dimensions. Receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance for survival.
RESULTS: A total of 363 fetuses were included, with an overall survival rate of 74.9%. Non-survivors demonstrated significantly smaller right pulmonary artery and mitral valve dimensions than survivors. Among fetal echocardiographic parameters, the mitral-to-tricuspid valve ratio (MTR) demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77. In fetuses evaluated at ≤ 29 weeks' gestation, an exploratory model combining MTR with o/eLHR and liver-up status achieved an apparent AUC of 0.827.
CONCLUSION: Fetal echocardiographic parameters were associated with survival in CDH. Integrated prenatal cardiopulmonary assessment incorporating MTR may provide complementary prognostic information although independent external validation is required.

Title: Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrocardiographic analysis aided by artificial intelligence (AI) may identify atrial electrical vulnerability during sinus rhythm. The objective of this study was to determine whether AI-enabled ECG (AI-ECG) is effective for detecting atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter (AFl), or prespecified pre-AF atrial findings in a randomized trial.
METHODS: In this single-center, open-label trial, 14 665 adults 40 to 85 years of age without previous AF/AFl were randomized to an AI-ECG-guided strategy or usual care. Participants randomized to AI-ECG who were then identified by AI as having a high-risk sinus-rhythm ECG in the preceding year were offered Holter monitoring for ≤7 days. Each monitored high-risk intervention participant was paired with an age- and sex-matched control selected before control ECGs underwent AI analysis. Matched controls received identical monitoring to reduce ascertainment bias. Reporting cardiologists were blinded to AI results and randomized assignment. The primary outcome was a composite of newly detected AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings within 90 days. Pre-AF atrial findings comprised frequent premature atrial complexes, short runs of premature atrial complexes, or nonsustained AF/AFl.
RESULTS: Among 7337 intervention and 7328 control participants, 84 (1.1%) and 78 (1.1%), respectively, were classified as high risk. Of the 84 high-risk intervention participants, 48 (57.1%) underwent monitoring, as did 48 matched controls. The primary outcome occurred in 54 intervention participants (0.74%) versus 35 control participants (0.48%; odds ratio, 1.54 [95% CI, 1.01-2.37]; P=0.046). Hypothetical reclassification of 1 intervention event to a nonevent changed the primary analysis P value to 0.057. The intervention effect on detection of the primary composite outcome differed by baseline AI-ECG risk (Pinteraction<0.001): 32.1% versus 2.6% among high-risk participants and 0.4% versus 0.5% among low-risk participants. AF/AFl detection (0.3% versus 0.2%) and antiarrhythmic therapy initiation at 180 days (2.3% versus 2.4%) did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups. Participant-reported monitoring-related adverse events, including skin reactions and discomfort, occurred in 22.9% of monitored intervention participants versus 18.8% of matched controls.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG-guided monitoring resulted in a modest increase in the detection of new AF, AFl, or pre-AF atrial findings. However, these findings were fragile statistically and sensitive to reclassification of 1 event. LATENT (Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development) demonstrates the clinical application of AI-ECG risk stratification to guide targeted rhythm surveillance, providing a foundation for larger trials evaluating its impact on patient outcomes.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06847932.

Title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), the myocardium sustains a dual injury: ischemia of the culprit territory and global hypoperfusion from low cardiac output. Whether platelet inhibition at reperfusion affects the microcirculation, the infarct, the noninfarcted myocardium, and ventricular function, and over what time course, has not been examined with serial imaging. The prespecified multimodality imaging substudy of the randomized DAPT-SHOCK-AMI trial (intravenous cangrelor versus crushed oral ticagrelor) addressed this question.
METHODS: Patients at prespecified imaging sites underwent serial echocardiography (208 enrolled; evaluable examinations in 175, 120, and 99 patients in the acute phase, at 1 month, and at 1 year) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR; 93 enrolled; 73, 68, and 63); 81 patients (40 and 41) underwent both modalities. Blinded core laboratories analyzed all studies. The primary imaging endpoint was microvascular obstruction (MVO) on acute CMR, evaluable in 60 patients; secondary endpoints were infarct size, native T1 of the global, infarcted, and remote myocardium, left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', and left atrial volume, and their changes. Comparisons between the cangrelor and crushed ticagrelor arms used covariate-adjusted logistic or linear regression; the substudy was not separately powered.
RESULTS: The odds of acute MVO were lower with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27 [95% CI 0.08 to 0.98]; P=0.023). Infarct size did not differ between the arms. At 1 year, native T1 of the remote myocardium was lower with cangrelor (adjusted mean 1114 [95% CI 1057 to 1171] versus 1171 [1115 to 1228] ms; P=0.005). Over 1 year, LVEF increased more with cangrelor on echocardiography (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value; adjusted P=0.046) and CMR (15.8% versus 2.1%; P=0.027), with greater improvement in GLS, lower E/e', and less left atrial enlargement; no parameter differed between the arms at 1 month.
CONCLUSIONS: In AMI-CS, serial multimodality imaging characterized microvascular, tissue-level, and functional injury over 1 year. Cangrelor was associated with less acute MVO, lower remote native T1, and more complete recovery of LV function than crushed ticagrelor, without a difference in infarct size; these hypothesis-generating findings suggest differences in the microcirculation and non-infarcted myocardial injury but do not establish a treatment mechanism.

Title: The trajectories of comprehensive capacity of bedridden older people based on latent growth mixture models: a longitudinal study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bedridden older people generally have poor comprehensive capacity and are prone to multi-system complications including pressure injuries and lower limb venous thrombosis, imposing heavy caregiving and financial burdens and severely affecting their health.
OBJECTIVE: To identify distinct trajectories of ability in bedridden older people and characteristics distinguishing the trajectories, while assessing the prognostic value of these trajectories for early risk identification of pressure injury and deep-vein thrombosis (DVT).
PARTICIPANTS: Two hundred twenty six bedridden older people aged 65 years and above from two nursing homes in China.
METHODS: Patients were required 5 assessments during 1-year follow-up period. Latent Growth Mixture Modelling identified distinct trajectories, multinomial logistic regression identified characteristics distinguishing the trajectories and generalised estimating equations evaluated associations between trajectories and pressure injury and DVT.
RESULTS: There are three distinct trajectories of comprehensive capacity among bedridden older people, including severe impairment with stable type (63.5%); moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type (16.3%); moderate-to-severe impairment with fluctuating type (20.2%). Characteristics distinguishing the trajectories were tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia. Compared with the severe impairment stable type, the other two groups had higher pressure injury risk; the moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type also had higher DVT risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Capacity trajectories of bedridden older people are heterogeneous. Nurses may want to focus on those with tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia to deliver targeted care. These trajectories are significantly associated with pressure injury and deep vein thrombosis risks. Their identification enables earlier risk stratification and more targeted prevention.

Title: Long Term Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Lymphoma: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with a history of lymphoma may develop significant coronary artery disease (CAD), which may be treated by percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet long term outcomes are not well characterized.
