METHODS: We reviewed patients with a history of lymphoma undergoing PCI from our institutional PCI database and compared characteristics and outcomes to a cohort without cancer. Long-term mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE) (cardiac death, myocardial infarction (MI), target vessel revascularization (TVR)) were assessed.
RESULTS: Of the 11,953 patients identified, 83 (0.7%) had past or current lymphoma. Most had Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) (n=23; 28.8%) or Hodgkin's Lymphoma (HL) (n=22; 27.%), and 31 (37.3%) presented with acute coronary syndrome. Lymphoma patients, as compared to non-lymphoma patients, were similar with respect to age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, prior MI, and prior PCI (all p=ns). The 1, 3, and 5-year survival rates were 90.5%, 69.5 %, and 52.5% in lymphoma patients as compared to 88.0%, 77.1%, and 66.7% in propensity matched non-lymphoma controls. Lymphoma was an independent predictor of mortality (OR 1.59; 95% CI 1.07-2.36, p=0.02) after multivariable adjustment. In propensity matched analysis over a median follow up of 4.2 years (IQR 1.28, 7.73), lymphoma was not independently associated with worse survival or MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with CAD undergoing PCI, <1% had previous or active lymphoma. Although lymphoma may appear predictive of mortality in regression models with multivariable adjustment, mortality and MACE rates are similar to propensity matched controls.

Title: Impact of Aspirin Use on Mortality and Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy After Heart Transplantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) remains a major cause of late graft failure and morbidity among heart transplant (HTx) recipients. Aspirin is currently assigned a Class IIb recommendation for CAV prevention, reflecting the limited evidence supporting its clinical benefit. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the association between aspirin use and clinical outcomes in HTx recipients (PROSPERO ID: CRD420261399873).
METHODS: Outcomes of interest included all-cause mortality and CAV-related clinical outcomes (graft dysfunction or CAV-related death). Literature searches were conducted through December 2025 in PubMed and EMBASE. Studies comparing HTx recipients treated with aspirin versus no aspirin were included. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were meta-analyzed across studies.
RESULTS: Five observational studies were included, comprising four adult cohorts and one pediatric cohort. Participants were predominantly male (66.6%), with a mean age of ≈50 years in the four adult studies and 7.4 years in the sole pediatric study. Aspirin use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (four studies, HR 0.31 [95% CI: 0.15-0.67]). No statistically significant association was observed with CAV-related clinical outcomes (HR 0.42 [95% CI: 0.10-1.77]).
CONCLUSIONS: In HTx recipients, aspirin use was associated with lower all-cause mortality, while no significant association was observed in the exploratory analysis of CAV-related clinical outcomes. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design, substantial heterogeneity, and potential residual and time-related biases. Prospective studies are needed to determine the efficacy and safety of aspirin after HTx.

Title: Initial Diabetes Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Long-Term Outcomes.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is common among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but optimal post-CABG glucose-lowering therapy remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the OptumLabs Data Warehouse of adults with T2D undergoing isolated CABG from 2012-2024. Follow-up began 30 days after discharge. Glucose-lowering therapy was modeled as a time-varying exposure with patients contributing no-observed-therapy person-time until the first qualifying post-discharge fill. Pairwise comparisons used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were heart failure hospitalization, stroke, and repeat coronary revascularization.
RESULTS: Among 19,237 patients, 24.9% had no observed post-discharge therapy, 42.8% received metformin, 22.9% received insulin, and 9.4% received GLP-1RA/SGLT2i therapy. All active therapies were associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy, including GLP-1RA/SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58-0.87), metformin (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55-0.66), and insulin (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.67-0.84). Among active therapies, metformin was associated with lower mortality than insulin (HR, 0.61 [0.54-0.70]); GLP-1RA/SGLT2i comparisons with metformin and insulin were less precise. Metformin was also associated with lower cumulative incidence of heart failure hospitalization than no observed therapy and insulin, and lower stroke incidence than insulin.
CONCLUSIONS: Observed glucose-lowering therapy initiation after CABG was associated with lower mortality compared with no observed therapy across all active treatment groups. These findings highlight a potential care gap and suggest that proper initiation of diabetes therapy after CABG represents an important opportunity to improve long-term outcomes following surgical revascularization.

Title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle.
INTERVENTION: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time.
RESULTS: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

Title: AI-Identified Reasons for Nonescalation of Lipid-Lowering Therapy for Secondary Prevention.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite guideline recommendations for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals in secondary prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) remains underused. Identifying treat-to-target strategy adoption and reasons for LLT nonescalation are critical to close guideline-discordant care gaps.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether large language models (LLMs) can identify a treat-to-target strategy use and extract reasons for LLT nonescalation from clinical notes when LDL-C concentration is above goal.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients from January 1, 2019, through May 15, 2025. Notes from most recent clinical encounters were retrieved and split into development, test, and inference sets. The setting was a large, integrated health system in Northern California. Adults aged 18 to 90 years with 2 or more clinician-billed encounters for ASCVD and with LDL-C level greater than or equal to 70 mg/dL at the most recent encounter were included in note-based analyses.
EXPOSURES: Documented LDL-C targets and LLT management decisions.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Model performance was evaluated on LDL-C target documentation, LDL-C target value, LLT adjustment, and reasons for nonescalation against clinical annotations. Outcome prevalence was assessed on the inference set.
RESULTS: A total of 28 113 unique patients with ASCVD-related encounters were identified, of whom 13 810 (49.1%; mean [SD] age, 70.9 [11.4] years; 7904 male [57.2%]) had above-goal LDL-C level. Model-annotator and interannotator reliability were not statistically different across outcomes, and micro-weighted F1 scores ranged from 0.80 to 0.98. Of the 13 394 patients with above-goal LDL-C level and 13 354 relevant notes in the inference set, a treat-to-target strategy was identified in 3756 (28.1%) of all relevant notes, most commonly targeting an LDL-C level less than 70 mg/dL (2280 [17.1%]). LLT was not escalated in 11 842 of all relevant notes (88.7%), with 4788 (40.4%) containing at least 1 LLT nonescalation reason, most often due to patient-reported adverse effects (1683 [12.6%]), LDL-C level close to goal (922 [6.9%]), patient preference to avoid LLT (914 [6.8%]), preference for lifestyle changes (811 [6.1%]), and deferral to repeat laboratory tests (617 [4.6%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this study show that after using a state-of-the art LLM, nearly 9 in 10 ASCVD encounters with above-goal LDL-C level did not have patient LLT escalated, most often because of adverse effects, patient preference, preference for lifestyle changes, therapeutic inertia (eg, repeat laboratory tests), and near-goal LDL-C level. These findings highlight an avenue for personalizing system-level digital health interventions to help discover and minimize guideline-discordant care gaps in secondary prevention of ASCVD.

Title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Long-Term Outcomes in Stable Coronary Artery Disease: Extended Follow-Up of the COURAGE Randomized Trial.
Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness With Medical and Invasive Approaches-Chronic Kidney Disease), at a median follow-up of 2.2 years, the primary composite outcome of death or nonfatal myocardial infarction was similar between an initial invasive strategy (INV) compared with an initial conservative strategy (CON) in patients with moderate or severe myocardial ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease. However, the long-term outcomes comparing the 2 strategies are unknown.
METHODS: Participants in the ISCHEMIA-CKD trial were randomly assigned to either INV, involving coronary angiography and revascularization when feasible, added to guideline-directed medical therapy or to CON with guideline-directed medical therapy alone and invasive procedures reserved for failure of guideline-directed medical therapy. After the active intervention trial phase, long-term vital status follow-up was conducted through participant contact by participating sites and by health record and centralized death database searches. The primary outcome for the extended follow-up phase was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cause-specific mortality, including cardiovascular and noncardiovascular mortality.
RESULTS: Among the 777 participants randomized (388 to INV and 389 to CON), over a median of 8 years of follow-up, vital status retention among survivors was 95%. There was a total of 429 deaths (55%). Cumulative all-cause mortality (57.4% versus 56.8%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.05 [95% CI, 0.87-1.28]) or cardiovascular mortality (40.3% versus 38.4%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.84-1.34]) at 8 years did not differ between INV and CON. The restricted mean survival time was 1941 days (1834-2047 days) for INV versus 1990 days (1885-2094 days) for CON, with an adjusted estimated difference of -99 days (-245 to 46). The posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher death with INV at the 8-year median follow-up was 28% and 52%, respectively. Similarly, the posterior probability of at least a 1 percentage point lower or higher cardiovascular mortality with INV was 23% and 56%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with at least moderate ischemia and advanced chronic kidney disease, there was no significant long-term benefit of an initial INV at reducing the risk of all-cause or cardiovascular mortality compared with an initial conservative strategy.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01985360.

Title: Long Non-Coding RNA HIF1A-AS2 Promotes the Progression of Acute Cerebral Infarction with Large Atherosclerosis and Has Clinical Value in Early Diagnosis and Prognosis Assessment.
Abstract: Acute cerebral infarction (ACI) with large atherosclerosis (LAA) has a poor prognosis. This study evaluated the clinical significance of the HIF1A-AS2/miR-129-5p/HMGB1 axis in diagnosing and assessing prognosis in LAA-type ACI. This study included 150 LAA-type ACI patients and 150 matched healthy controls. The clinical outcomes of the patients were assessed using the GOS score. An in vitro hypoxia model was established using HUVECs. The levels of HIF1A-AS2, miR-129-5p, and HMGB1 were quantified by RT-qPCR, and levels of inflammatory factors were measured by ELISA. Luciferase reporter assays confirmed direct interactions among HIF1A-AS2, miR-129-5p, and HMGB1. Cell viability was assessed using the CCK-8 assay, cell migration was evaluated through Transwell assays, and apoptosis was analyzed by flow cytometry. The diagnostic performance of HIF1A-AS2 was assessed using the ROC curve. Kaplan-Meier curves were used to analyze adverse outcomes in LAA-type ACI, and Cox regression models identified prognostic factors. HIF1A-AS2 expression was significantly upregulated in LAA-type ACI, showing high diagnostic value. Higher HIF1A-AS2 levels were correlated with increased adverse outcomes, elevated inflammatory factors, higher NIHSS scores, and lower GOS scores. Hypoxic conditions upregulated HIF1A-AS2 expression, inhibited cell proliferation and migration, while promoting apoptosis. Conversely, downregulating HIF1A-AS2 reversed these effects. In LAA-type ACI, miR-129-5p was downregulated while HMGB1 was upregulated. Significant negative correlations were observed between HIF1A-AS2 and miR-129-5p and between miR-129-5p and HMGB1. The miR-129-5p inhibitor partially reversed the effects of si-HIF1A-AS2 on cell proliferation, migration, and apoptosis under hypoxia. Functional rescue experiments revealed that miR-129-5p mimic partially reversed the detrimental effects of HIF1A-AS2 overexpression on endothelial cells, as evidenced by enhanced cell proliferation and migration, suppressed apoptosis, and downregulated HMGB1 expression. Conversely, overexpression of HMGB1 partially abrogated the effects induced by the miR‑129‑5p mimic. In human aortic endothelial cells (HAECs) and human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs), knockdown of HIF1A‑AS2 or overexpression of miR‑129‑5p both attenuated cell injury, further validating the extensive role of this regulatory axis in various vascular cell types. HIF1A-AS2 promoted the progression of LAA-type ACI and has clinical value in early diagnosis and prognosis assessment. The HIF1A-AS2/miR-129-5p/HMGB1 axis may serve as a vital factor in the early diagnosis and prognosis evaluation of LAA-type ACI.

Title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis.
RESULTS: Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897).
CONCLUSIONS: MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms.
KEY POINTS: Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

Title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use in patients with minor stroke is associated with lower risk of post-stroke dementia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor ischemic stroke is associated with increased risks of post-stroke dementia independent of stroke recurrence, yet there are no guideline-recommended therapies targeted at cognitive outcomes. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been shown to be associated with lower risk of dementia among diabetes patients; however, their effect on cognitive outcomes among minor stroke patients is largely unknown.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used de-identified electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2016-2025). Adult patients with minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS ≤ 5 and non-disabling) were included. Patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, cognitive impairment, or dementia were excluded. GLP-1RA use was defined as a prescription prior to or within 3 months of stroke diagnosis. After 1:1 propensity score matching on 75 baseline characteristics, outcomes were assessed over a 5 year follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 1,425 patients per group were analyzed. Mean age was 60.7 years, with diabetes present in 92.7% and mean HbA1c of 8.7%. GLP-1RA use was associated with a 48% lower hazard of post-stroke dementia (3.4% vs. 7.0%, HR 0.52 [95% CI 0.37-0.74]) and a 31% lower hazard of other neurocognitive complaints (17.2% vs 25.6%, HR 0.69 [95% CI 0.59-0.81]) over 5 years. GLP-1RA use was also associated with reduced mortality (4.4% vs. 8.8%; HR 0.57 [95% CI 0.42-0.77]) and major ischemic stroke (1.5% vs. 2.7%; HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.35-1.01]). No significant difference in intracranial hemorrhage rates was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Among this cohort of minor ischemic stroke patients mostly with concomitant diabetes, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced risks of post-stroke dementia and other neurocognitive complaints. These findings support prioritizing GLP-1RA use for diabetic patients who suffered minor ischemic stroke. Prospective trials are warranted to confirm causality and determine optimal implementation.

Title: Agreement between fully automated artificial intelligence and cardiac radiologists for coronary stenosis and plaque assessment in an asymptomatic screening cohort.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: This retrospective single-center study evaluated segment-level agreement between experienced cardiac radiologists and a research AI platform for coronary stenosis and plaque assessment on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Asymptomatic individuals undergoing CCTA at a health screening center were studied, excluding those with prior revascularization, coronary anomaly, or total occlusion. Stenosis grade and plaque composition were independently assessed by the AI platform and two cardiac radiologists at the segment level, with disagreements between the two radiologists resolved by consensus. Agreement was evaluated using Cohen's κ, quadratic weighted κ for ordinal grading, observed agreement, and positive and negative agreement for dichotomized significant stenosis. The cohort comprised 172 participants and 2,582 segments. Significant stenosis was uncommon (18/2,582, 0.7%), with moderate agreement (κ = 0.412; observed agreement 98.5%; positive agreement 0.418; negative agreement 0.992). Agreement was fair for ordinal stenosis grade (κ = 0.397; quadratic weighted κ = 0.573; observed agreement 84.0%) and plaque composition (κ = 0.330; observed agreement 81.8%). Stenosis-grade agreement was lower in plaque-containing than plaque-free segments, an exploratory finding given marked differences in subgroup size and prevalence. Myocardial bridging and image quality were not major descriptive determinants of discordance. In this low-prevalence cohort, AI-based CCTA analysis showed high negative agreement for radiologist-defined significant stenosis but limited concordance for grading and plaque characterization. Reflecting low prevalence and few positive cases, the findings do not establish independent rule-out performance but support prospective evaluation of AI as an expert-supervised pre-reading or triage adjunct, with positive, ambiguous, or plaque-containing findings requiring expert review.

Title: EMAIL-HF: Can Digital Strategies Shorten the Path from Scientific Evidence to Clinical Practice in Heart Failure?
Abstract: A substantial gap persists between scientific evidence and clinical practice in heart failure (HF). Digital solutions have emerged as promising strategies to accelerate the implementation of evidence-based therapies. This mini-review examines the results of the EMAIL-HF study, a registry-based, randomized, controlled, parallel-group clinical trial conducted in Denmark that included patients aged 20 years or older with a diagnosis of HF irrespective of left ventricular ejection fraction, who were not receiving SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i). Participants were randomized to usual care or a digital strategy consisting of an e-mailed letter with information on SGLT2i, followed by contact with an HF specialist. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients redeeming a prescription for dapagliflozin or empagliflozin within 6 months of randomization and the secondary endpoint was a composite of time to first HF hospitalization or death from any cause. The digital strategy significantly increased SGLT2i initiation within 6 months, although no difference in HF hospitalization or all-cause mortality was observed during the 24-month follow-up. Whether these strategies can translate modest improvements in treatment uptake into sustained, scalable, and cost-effective gains across diverse healthcare systems remains uncertain.

Title: Transcatheter Solution to Atypical Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Drainage in a Single Ventricle Patient.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Partial anomalous pulmonary venous drainage (PAPVD) is typically incompatible with single ventricle physiology if left unrepaired before cavopulmonary connection. This report describes a rare anatomical variant and novel interventional solution.
CASE SUMMARY: An 8-month-old female with hypoplastic left heart variant developed profound cyanosis following bidirectional Glenn because of unrepaired PAPVD of the right upper pulmonary vein to the superior vena cava (SVC). Retrospective 3-dimensional reconstruction of the patient's neonatal computed tomography angiogram revealed a small interlobar vessel between the anomalous pulmonary vein and the anatomically normal right lower pulmonary vein. This interlobar vessel's gross dilatation and anatomical features permitted percutaneous device occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the SVC, isolating SVC return to the cavopulmonary circulation while preserving unobstructed pulmonary venous return to the atrium.
DISCUSSION: Surgical and interventional solutions are reviewed in the context of this unusual anatomical variant.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In the uncommon circumstance of an unrecognized anomalous pulmonary vein with connections to both systemic and pulmonary venous circulations, consideration may be given to interventional occlusion of the PAPVD connection to the systemic vein. Retrospective application of contemporary 3-dimensional reconstruction tools can add great value in delineating complex or unusual anatomy.

Title: Live Versus Delayed Video-Based TEAM Assessment During Real-World Cardiac Arrest: Agreement and Exploratory Differences by Rater Experience.
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate agreement between immediate live and delayed video-based assessment of nontechnical skills during real-world adult cardiac arrest resuscitation, and whether agreement differed by rater experience.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study of adult cardiac arrest resuscitations in a tertiary emergency department in Taiwan in 2024. For each event, one trained physician or nurse who participated in the resuscitation completed the Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) immediately afterward and re-rated the same event from video approximately 30 days later. Live-video agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: Of 105 recorded resuscitations, 80 had complete paired assessments. Mean global ratings were similar between modalities (8.25 versus 8.22; mean paired difference, -0.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.25 to 0.20), whereas teamwork scores were modestly lower on video review (mean paired difference, -1.00; 95% CI -1.77 to -0.23). Event-level agreement was limited: intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.21 (95% CI 0.00 to 0.41) for total TEAM score and 0.16 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.37) for global rating. Total TEAM video ratings averaged 1.24 points lower than live ratings, with limits of agreement from -12.28 to 9.80. Agreement was higher among senior raters.
CONCLUSION: Delayed video-based TEAM assessment produced similar group-level scores but limited event-level agreement during real-world cardiac arrest. Agreement appeared higher among senior raters. Video review may support debriefing and monitoring, but appraisal of a specific resuscitation or other higher stakes use likely requires experienced raters and structured safeguards.

Title: Cardiac electrophysiology procedures must be performed exclusively by trained electrophysiologists: A statement from the Heart Rhythm Society and Heart Rhythm Advocates.
Abstract: The exponential growth of clinical cardiac electrophysiology (CCEP) as a subspecialty has created an important unresolved question in contemporary cardiovascular medicine: Who is qualified to perform electrophysiology (EP) procedures? As nonelectrophysiologists increasingly perform procedures that require the nuanced expertise of a trained or board-certified CCEP (eg, permanent pacemaker implantation, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation, cardiac resynchronization therapy, and transvenous lead extraction), the consequences for patient safety, procedural outcomes, and health system efficiency have become impossible to ignore. This article presents a comprehensive, evidence-based argument that cardiac EP procedures must be performed exclusively by physicians who have completed accredited fellowship training in CCEP. We draw upon peer-reviewed outcome data, guideline-derived training standards from the Heart Rhythm Society, the American College of Cardiology, and American Heart Association, including the newly published 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/Heart Rhythm Society Advanced Training Statement on Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology, as well as registry analyses spanning hundreds of thousands of patients to substantiate our position. The risks associated with suboptimal operator training are not theoretical; they are measurable, costly, and potentially fatal. The evidence presented demonstrates that operator specialization in EP is among the most powerful independent predictors of procedural safety and long-term outcomes and can be as important as institutional volume in many analyses. We call upon hospital credentialing committees, national medical societies, payers, regulatory bodies, and policymakers worldwide to establish and enforce a definitive standard: only trained CCEPs should implant and manage cardiac implantable electronic devices, perform catheter ablation procedures, execute transvenous lead extraction, and conduct formal EP studies.

Title: High Bleeding Risk and Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary PCI in STEMI: A Post Hoc Analysis of the PREMIUM Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) at high bleeding risk (HBR) are also at increased risk of ischemic events, making the optimal antiplatelet therapy challenging. Whether HBR identifies patients who may benefit from upfront aspirin omission at the time of primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: In this study, we sought to evaluate whether HBR modifies the effect of aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI.
METHODS: The PREMIUM trial randomized patients with STEMI before primary PCI to low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin plus prasugrel. In the DAPT group, patients meeting Academic Research Consortium (ARC) for HBR criteria were permitted to discontinue aspirin at 3 months, whereas non-HBR patients were intended to continue DAPT for 12 months. This post hoc analysis assessed the primary outcome of a 12-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, or myocardial infarction and the major secondary outcome of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5 bleeding according to HBR status.
RESULTS: Among 2,189 patients, 786 (35.9%) met ARC-HBR criteria. HBR patients had higher rates of the primary outcome (16.2% vs 6.2%; HR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.05-3.52) and the major secondary outcome (10.9% vs 4.9%; HR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.65-3.14). The primary outcome occurred with monotherapy vs DAPT in 18.0% vs 14.5% of HBR patients (HR: 1.29; 95% CI: 0.91-1.82) and 7.4% vs 5.0% of non-HBR patients (HR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.01-2.37; P for interaction = 0.51). The major secondary outcome occurred in 9.2% vs 12.5% of HBR patients (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.46-1.11) and 3.8% vs 6.1% of non-HBR patients (HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.38-1.00; P for interaction = 0.67).
CONCLUSIONS: ARC-HBR identified patients with a substantially higher overall risk after primary PCI for STEMI, but did not identify a subgroup with a more favorable treatment effect of upfront aspirin omission. Clinically meaningful treatment-effect modification cannot be excluded, owing to limited precision. These findings do not support using HBR status alone to guide upfront aspirin omission and should be interpreted in the context of the low-dose prasugrel regimen used in Japan. (Prasugrel Monotherapy Following Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction [PREMIUM; NCT05709626]).

Title: Reinitiation of Optimal Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy After Coronary Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen is an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). In a randomized placebo-controlled trial in patients with established cardiovascular disease, pelacarsen did not reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared to placebo. We further investigated the association of pelacarsen treatment with cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: We report the association of pelacarsen treatment with a primary composite end point of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. Analyses included on-treatment, uninterrupted treatment, total primary end point events (first and recurrent events), landmark analyses classified by changes in and achieved lipoprotein(a) at 3 months, and key subgroups including baseline lipoprotein(a), low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (CRP), and time from qualifying event to enrollment.
RESULTS: For participants on treatment, a primary end point occurred in 434 participants (10.4%) randomly assigned to placebo and 380 participants (9.1%) assigned to pelacarsen (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.12). When evaluating participants with uninterrupted treatment, a primary end point event occurred in 167 participants (11.0%) in the pelacarsen group and 204 participants (10.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.34). When evaluating total primary end point events, there were 644 events in the pelacarsen group and 646 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.14). In landmark analyses evaluating participants alive and free of the composite end point at 3 months, when compared to placebo there was no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point either in participants with reduction in lipoprotein(a) greater than or equal to the median (170 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 0.92 to 1.29) or in participants who achieved lipoprotein(a) lower than or equal to the median (69.5 nmol/l) (hazard ratio, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.29). There was also no association between pelacarsen treatment and the primary end point in any of the evaluated key subgroups including classification by median baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, high-sensitivity CRP, or time from qualifying cardiovascular disease to enrollment.
CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen was not associated with a reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when evaluated by treatment exposure, changes in or achieved lipoprotein(a) levels at 3 months, considering total events, or within subgroups of baseline lipoprotein(a), LDL cholesterol, or high-sensitivity CRP levels.

Title: Impact of Statin and Aspirin Use on Dementia Diagnosis Stratified by Cardiovascular Risk.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia share common risk factors. However, the role of ASCVD prevention therapies in AD dementia prevention is not fully understood. We examined the effect of LLT and antiplatelets with dementia and AD dementia diagnoses across ASCVD risk profiles.
METHODS: We used data from primary prevention registry derived from a large healthcare network. Multivariable Cox proportional models were generated to study dementia and AD dementia diagnoses, stratified by ASCVD risk profiles. Impact of aspirin and LLT use on dementia and AD dementia diagnoses was assessed in adjusted models.
RESULTS: Among n= 347,128, 2.4% developed dementia and 2.0% developed AD dementia over a median follow-up of 7.94 years. In adjusted models, dementia (HR, 2.59; 95% CI [2.29-2.92]) and AD dementia (HR, 2.85; 95% CI [2.49-3.25]) was higher in high risk patients. Low and high-dose aspirin among high ASCVD risk had lower dementia (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, [0.77-1.00] and HR, 0.83; 95% [CI 0.77-0.90]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.83; 95% CI [0.77-0.91] and HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.73-0.97]). Similarly, moderate- to high-dose LLT use among high ASCVD risk groups was associated with lower dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.79-0.93]) and AD dementia (HR, 0.85; 95% CI [0.78-0.93]).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline ASCVD risk was associated with increased risk of dementia and AD dementia diagnoses. Aspirin and moderate- to high-dose LLT use among patients with high ASCVD risk was associated with lower dementia and AD dementia risk.

Title: Treatment Patterns of Oral Glucocorticoids in Patients with IgG4-Related Disease: A Real-World Analysis based on a Japanese Claims Database.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the prescribing patterns of oral glucocorticoid and evaluate flares and glucocorticoid-related complications in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study used a Japanese hospital claims database. Patients with a prescription for oral glucocorticoids, a diagnosis of immunoglobulin G4-related disease, and having at least two immunoglobulin G4 measurement tests were included. The index date was defined as the first oral glucocorticoid prescription recorded in the database (Day 0). Patients were followed for up to Day 1460 (4 years).
RESULTS: The study included 3,167 patients. The mean dose of oral glucocorticoid was 28.76, 10.71, and 4.12 mg/day on Day 0, 90, and 1095, respectively. At Day 1460, 66.56% of the patients were still receiving oral glucocorticoid therapy and the dose exceeded 5 mg/day in 17.80% of patients. During the follow-up period, 453 patients (14.30%) experienced at least one flare. The incidence rates of hospitalized infections, osteoporotic fractures, and cardiovascular diseases, defined as serious glucocorticoid complications, were 7.46, 0.61, and 1.61 per 100 person-years, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Over half of the patients continued glucocorticoid therapy at 4 years. Glucocorticoid withdrawal strategies could be associated with reducing the long-term glucocorticoid-related toxicity in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease.

Title: From cancer prevention to survivorship: Comprehensive menopause management after risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.
Journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
Abstract: Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) is the cornerstone of ovarian cancer prevention for women with hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes. When performed before natural menopause, however, RRSO induces immediate surgical menopause, with vasomotor symptoms, sexual dysfunction, accelerated bone loss, and potential long-term cardiometabolic consequences. For eligible women, menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and prevents estrogen-deficiency bone loss. MHT should not be prescribed solely to prevent cardiovascular disease, and cardiometabolic risk requires standard preventive care. Concerns about breast cancer risk nevertheless limit its use. Recent observational evidence in BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers found that estrogen-only MHT was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence in one prospective matched analysis, whereas combined estrogen-progestogen therapy was not statistically associated with increased risk; residual confounding and limited treatment duration preclude causal conclusions. For women with a personal history of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, systemic MHT remains generally contraindicated, and non-hormonal options, including neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected antidepressants, gabapentin, and cognitive behavioral therapy, can reduce symptom burden. Genitourinary syndrome of menopause and sexual dysfunction require proactive, multidimensional management. This narrative review synthesizes international guidance, cohort studies, trials, and systematic reviews to provide a practical framework for preoperative counseling and long-term survivorship care after risk-reducing gynecologic surgery.

Title: Correlation between platelet-to-white blood cell ratio and left ventricular myocardial strain in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a cardiac magnetic resonance feature-tracking study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) myocardial strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) feature tracking enables sensitive detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, factors associated with early post-infarction LV myocardial function following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain incompletely understood, particularly in the context of inflammation-related myocardial injury. The platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR) which combines two routinely measured blood cell counts and may reflect the dynamic interplay between platelet recovery and inflammatory dynamics, has emerged as a potential biomarker of systemic inflammatory status. This study investigated the association between PWR and LV myocardial strain in patients with STEMI after PCI.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 222 patients with STEMI who underwent CMR imaging within 1 week after PCI. Demographic information, laboratory test results, and CMR parameters were collected. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup, sensitivity and nonlinear analyses were performed to investigate the association between post-PCI PWR and CMR-derived LV myocardial strain.
RESULTS: Patients in the highest PWR quartile had significantly higher LV ejection fraction (LVEF) (53.4% vs. 45.0%, P<0.001) and a smaller median infarct size (IS) (11.9% vs. 18.8%, P=0.006) than those in the lowest quartile (Q1). In the fully adjusted logistic model, higher PWR was independently associated with lower odds of impaired global longitudinal strain (GLS) [odds ratio (OR) 0.13, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.05-0.30, P<0.001] and impaired global circumferential strain (GCS) (OR 0.18; 95% CI: 0.06-0.49; P=0.001), and with higher odds of preserved global radial strain (GRS) (OR 5.57; 95% CI: 2.06-15.06; P=0.001). RCS analysis showed a linear association between PWR and the odds of LV myocardial strain impairment. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses yielded similar associations.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher post-PCI PWR was independently associated with more favorable LV myocardial strain after PCI in patients with STEMI. As a routinely available ratio, PWR may complement the early description of myocardial strain impairment.

Title: An optimized integrated ultrasound-cardiac magnetic resonance imaging strategy for accurate prenatal diagnosis of fetal aortic arch branch abnormalities: a prospective dual-center study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal aortic arch branch abnormalities (FAABAs) are characterized by complex classifications. Accurate prenatal identification and precise sub-typing are of great value for clinical counseling and pregnancy management. This study aimed to assess the diagnostic efficacy of a comprehensive prenatal ultrasound (US) protocol integrating three-vessel and trachea (3VT) view, aortic arch and descending aortic coronal sections (CSs), and four-dimensional (4D) spatiotemporal image correlation combined with high-definition (STIC-HD) live flow imaging. It also compared prenatal US, fetal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI), and combined US + cMRI for diagnosing FAABAs.
METHOD: This prospective dual-center study recruited 180 pregnant patients with suspected FAABAs from 2019 to 2021. All underwent three described US examinations, and 33 cases received supplementary fetal cMRI. Postpartum imaging, surgery, and autopsy results were defined as the gold standard. Diagnostic efficiency was validated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, F-score, Youden index, and Cohen's kappa analysis.
RESULTS: Gold standard verification identified 165 FAABAs cases (91.7%), including 55.8% left aortic arch, 32.1% right aortic arch, and 12.1% double aortic arch, plus 15 normal cases. The combined 3VT + CS view and comprehensive US protocol yielded a sensitivity of 98.2%, significantly higher than that of single 3VT view (73.5%, P<0.001). The US + cMRI combination achieved the optimal overall diagnostic efficacy (sensitivity: 97.0%, P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The comprehensive US protocol is the preferred prenatal imaging method for FAABAs diagnosis and classification. Fetal cMRI is a reliable complementary modality, particularly for cases with suboptimal acoustic windows.

Title: Quantitative coronary plaque characteristics on coronary computed tomography angiography and their prognostic value in patients with chronic kidney disease.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events. This study compared coronary plaque characteristics assessed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) between patients with and without CKD and evaluated their associations with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This secondary analysis of the multicenter CREATION-CHINA cohort included patients with suspected coronary artery disease who underwent CCTA during 2016-2020. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Propensity score matching (1:3) used age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, smoking, family history of coronary artery disease, and hyperlipidemia. Quantitative plaque characteristics and perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) were assessed. MACE comprised all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization >90 days after CCTA. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs); analyses of CCTA-derived predictors were adjusted for age, body mass index, and hypertension. High plaque burden was defined as total plaque burden in the highest quartile.
RESULTS: After matching, 2,267 patients were included (588 with CKD and 1,679 without CKD). During a median follow-up of 3.47 years (interquartile range, 2.36-4.10), MACE occurred in 30 patients with CKD (5.1%) and 52 without CKD (3.1%; P=0.035). Patients with CKD had higher median total plaque volume (39.90 vs. 0 mm3), median total plaque burden (8.83% vs. 0%), and prevalence of high-risk plaque (9.35% vs. 4.35%; all P<0.001). Among patients with CKD, lipid plaque burden (adjusted HR =1.107, 95% CI: 1.006-1.218; P=0.038) and high FAI (adjusted HR =4.027, 95% CI: 2.329-6.960; P<0.001) were independently associated with MACE. Compared with patients without CKD and with low plaque burden, those with CKD and high plaque burden had a higher risk of MACE (adjusted HR =6.153, 95% CI: 2.937-12.890; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CKD was associated with greater coronary plaque burden and a higher incidence of MACE. Lipid plaque burden and high FAI were independently associated with MACE after adjustment for age, body mass index, and hypertension, supporting their potential role in cardiovascular risk assessment in patients with CKD.

Title: Validation of fully automated myocardial T1 and synthetic hematocrit-based extracellular volume quantification on 3T cardiac MRI: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated post-processing software has been developed to quantify various cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameters, including native T1 and extracellular volume (ECV) using synthetic hematocrit (Hct). However, validation studies of these automated measurements remain limited. We aimed to validate a fully automated workflow integrating myocardial T1 analysis and synthetic Hct for ECV quantification on 3T CMR, using manual ECV calculation based on venous Hct as the reference method.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 65 adults with low-to-intermediate risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease who underwent stress 3T CMR. Manual ECV was calculated using manually contoured myocardial T1 values and venous Hct obtained within 7 days of CMR. Automated analysis used Myomics-T1 software (Phantomics, Korea) to automatically generate myocardial and blood-pool T1 values and contours, with synthetic Hct derived from a regression model developed in an independent cohort of 450 participants. Correlation and agreement were assessed using Pearson correlation, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: The mean age was 65.2±11.5 years, and 60% of participants were female. Automated myocardial native T1 and ECV showed excellent correlation with manual measurements (r=0.96 and 0.91, respectively) and excellent agreement (ICC =0.96 and 0.93, respectively). Automated myocardial native T1 was slightly higher than manual measurements (1,246±52 vs. 1,233±47 ms), whereas automated ECV was higher by 1.2 percentage points (29.0%±4.9% vs. 27.8%±4.6%). Synthetic Hct correlated with venous Hct (r=0.78; ICC =0.76) but demonstrated proportional bias. Agreement between synthetic Hct-derived and manual ECV was better within the normal Hct range (35-45%) but substantially reduced at Hct >45% (ICC =0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: Fully automated ECV quantification demonstrated strong correlation and agreement with the manual method within the normal Hct range. However, synthetic Hct-derived ECV was less reliable at abnormal Hct levels, particularly at Hct >45%. Further external validation and refinement of the synthetic Hct model are warranted to support broader clinical application.

Title: Mitral regurgitation and left atrial phasic function and atrioventricular coupling in patients with myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral regurgitation (MR) after myocardial infarction (MI) may increase left atrial (LA) pressure and contribute to cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated the incremental association of MR with LA phasic function and strain and identified independent factors associated with LA deformation in patients with MI.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 189 patients with MI (111 without MR and 78 with MR: mild, 27; moderate, 33; severe, 18) and 86 normal controls who underwent 3.0-T cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). MR severity was graded by the CMR-derived MR fraction: mild <30%, moderate 30% to <50%, and severe ≥50%. CMR-derived LA phasic function and strain (reservoir strain, epsilon-s; booster strain, epsilon-a; conduit strain, epsilon-e), left ventricular (LV) function and strain, infarct size, and MR fraction were measured. Between-group comparisons were performed using one-way analysis of variance or the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc correction, and multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent factors associated with LA strain. A two-sided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Patients with MI and MR had lower LA reservoir strains [22.14%±10.91% vs. 28.65% (22.78%, 38.30%) vs. 41.70% (36.15%, 53.15%)], booster strains [11.52%±6.19% vs. 13.80% (10.20%, 19.80%) vs. 19.25% (15.10%, 24.05%)], and conduit strains [9.40% (6.03%, 14.85%) vs. 14.60% (9.60%, 20.50%) vs. 22.55% (17.75%, 30.43%)] than patients with MI without MR and controls (all P<0.05). They also had higher LA maximum volume [68.43 (57.44, 91.51) mL] and minimum volume [35.93 (24.43, 61.15) mL] and lower LA total ejection fraction (45.39%±14.97%) than the other groups (all P<0.05). In multivariable analysis, MR degree was independently associated with reservoir strain (β=-0.194, P=0.048) and conduit strain (β=-0.208, P=0.038). Anterior wall MI (reservoir strain: β=-0.245, P=0.014; booster strain: β=-0.231, P=0.028; conduit strain: β=-0.224, P=0.027) and posteromedial papillary muscle infarction (reservoir strain: β=-0.329, P=0.004; booster strain: β=-0.370, P=0.003) were also independently associated with LA strain.
CONCLUSIONS: MR was associated with further deterioration of LA myocardial strain in patients with MI. Posteromedial papillary muscle infarction, anterior wall MI, beta-blocker use, and dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus clopidogrel were independently associated with LA strain. CMR-derived functional and strain parameters may help characterize LV-LA coupling and support risk stratification in this population.

Title: Residual CatLet score predicts the long-term prognosis in "all-comers" patients with coronary artery disease: a survival analysis study based on time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, the incidence and mortality rates of coronary artery disease (CAD) have been rising annually. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of the coronary artery tree description and lesion evaluation (CatLet) angiographic scoring system to stratify risk and to elucidate its independent prognostic value in "all-comers" patients with CAD.
METHODS: A total of 373 consecutive CAD patients were enrolled at The First People's Hospital of Hefei following coronary angiography. The residual CatLet (rCatLet) score was calculated based on the residual lesions after completion of required revascularization at physicians' discretion during this hospitalization for all enrolled patients, who subsequently underwent follow-ups. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Secondary endpoints included all-cause death and cardiac death. Survival rates were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent prognostic factors, while the prognostic value of the rCatLet score was evaluated by the time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC).
RESULTS: This was a single-center cohort study of 279 patients, including 56 (20.07%) with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and 223 (79.93%) with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed progressively worse prognosis across higher rCatLet score tertiles for all endpoints (all log-rank P<0.001). Cox regression revealed that, compared with the low tertile, the highest rCatLet tertile was associated with a significantly increased risk of MACCEs [hazard ratio (HR) =4.96; 95% confidence interval (CI): 3.03-8.12], and the medium tertile showed a non-significant trend toward higher risk (HR =1.39; 95% CI: 0.79-2.43). Time-dependent ROC analysis showed that the rCatLet model predicted 1-, 3-, and 6-year MACCEs with AUCs (95% CIs) of 0.85 (0.77-0.92), 0.73 (0.64-0.81), and 0.71 (0.64-0.77). The multivariable-adjusted models performed better, and their AUCs (95% CIs) at the three time points were 0.87 (0.83-0.92), 0.78 (0.72-0.86), and 0.78 (0.73-0.84), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Our exploratory findings suggest that the rCatLet score has predictive value for the short- and long-term clinical prognosis in "all-comers" patients with CAD. Furthermore, the rCatLet score adjusted for clinical variables showed improved prognostic predictive values. These findings require further validation in future studies.

Title: Artificial intelligence applications in photon-counting detector CT for coronary artery disease imaging: a narrative review.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a first-line non-invasive imaging modality for CAD evaluation, but conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) is often limited by blooming artifacts, noise, and partial-volume effects. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) provides superior spatial resolution, reduced blooming, and multi-energy spectral data, yet its ultra-high-resolution (UHR) datasets frequently suffer from increased noise and complex spectral information that require advanced processing. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising solution to fully exploit PCD-CT's advantages. This narrative review aims to synthesize the current evidence on AI applications in PCD-CT for CAD imaging, evaluate their technical performance and clinical potential, identify limitations, and propose future directions.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. Original English-language studies applying AI techniques to PCD-CT data for CAD imaging were included, and categorized using a 5-level translational framework.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Thirty single-center studies were identified and grouped into three main categories. In image quality improvement, denoising models achieved 60-96% noise reduction while preserving spatial and spectral fidelity. Radiomics studies (the largest group) identified specific texture features in myocardium, plaques, pericoronary, and epicardial adipose tissue associated with coronary artery calcium severity, hypercholesterolemia, aging, and CAD presence, although feature reproducibility was only moderate. Automated detection/quantification/segmentation tools demonstrated high reproducibility, improved stenosis quantification, substantial workflow benefits, and promising CT-fractional flow reserve (FFR) performance with strong intra-individual agreement to EID-CT.
CONCLUSIONS: AI has shown promising technical advancements when applied to PCD-CT for CAD imaging. However, the evidence base remains limited by small sample sizes, single-center and single-scanner designs, lack of external validation, and absence of outcome-driven studies. Future research should focus on multicenter prospective validation, standardized protocols, human-in-the-loop systems, and clinical impact assessment to support the safe and effective translation of AI-enhanced PCD-CT into routine clinical practice.

Title: Cardiac remodeling, autonomic parameters, and clinical factors associated with obstructive sleep apnea: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity through mechanisms involving intermittent hypoxia, sympathetic activation, oxidative stress, and progressive cardiac remodeling. The present study aimed to comprehensively evaluate clinical characteristics, echocardiographic abnormalities, autonomic function, and independent factors associated with OSA in a case-control population.
METHODS: This observational, case-control study included 108 adults recruited from a tertiary sleep laboratory, 54 patients with OSA and 54 controls selected using frequency matching for age and sex and considered at low risk for OSA based on STOP-Bang screening. Clinical characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, transthoracic echocardiographic parameters, structural cardiac abnormalities, and 24-hour Holter-derived autonomic indices were compared between groups. Continuous variables were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test, categorical variables using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test, and univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify variables independently associated with OSA.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with OSA had significantly higher prevalences of obesity, smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and ischemic heart disease (IHD). Echocardiography demonstrated larger left atrial and right ventricular diameters, higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), and increased frequencies of left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), diastolic dysfunction, and moderate tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Among the Holter-derived autonomic parameters, the root mean square of successive differences between adjacent normal-to-normal intervals (RMSSD) was significantly lower in patients with OSA in the unadjusted comparison. In multivariable linear regression analyses, the association between OSA and RMSSD was attenuated and did not reach statistical significance, while OSA was not independently associated with the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN). In univariable logistic regression analyses, obesity, smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, ischemic heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction were significantly associated with OSA. After multivariable adjustment, obesity [adjusted odds ratio (OR) 10.86, 95% confidence intervals (CI) 2.99-39.47], smoking (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.32-18.14), ischemic heart disease (adjusted OR 19.17, 95% CI 1.65-222.41), and left ventricular hypertrophy (adjusted OR 3.54, 95% CI 1.01-12.40) remained independently associated with OSA.
CONCLUSIONS: OSA was associated with structural cardiovascular abnormalities and an unadjusted difference in the Holter-derived autonomic parameter RMSSD, whereas neither RMSSD nor SDNN showed a statistically significant independent association with OSA after multivariable adjustment. Obesity, smoking, ischemic heart disease, and left ventricular hypertrophy were independently associated with the presence of OSA, underscoring the close relationship between sleep-disordered breathing and cardiovascular disease. Comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation may improve risk stratification and support earlier identification of patients at increased cardiovascular risk.

Title: Value of left atrial to left ventricular volume ratio in left heart remodeling classification and postoperative prognosis assessment in patients with rheumatic mitral stenosis.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) patients exhibit heterogeneous left heart remodeling, with unclear impacts on postoperative prognosis. This study aimed to classify left heart remodeling subtypes using the left atrial (LA) to left ventricular (LV) volume ratio, analyze subtype differences, and validate the ratio's predictive value for 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 350 RMS patients who underwent mitral valve surgery between February 2021 and October 2024. Preoperative LA end-systolic volume (LAESV) and LV end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) were measured by three-dimensional (3D) echocardiography to calculate the LA/LV volume ratio. The optimal cutoff value was determined by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Patients were divided into predominantly LV remodeling (PLVR) and predominantly LA remodeling (PLAR) groups. Clinical data, echocardiographic parameters, and 1-year adverse outcomes [a composite of heart failure (HF) rehospitalization and all-cause mortality] were compared. Risk factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: The LA/LV volume ratio yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.723 (P<0.001) for predicting 1-year adverse outcomes, with an optimal cutoff of 0.61. PLAR patients (LA/LV >0.61, n=168) were older, more frequently female, had a higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), more severe mitral stenosis, and larger right atrial volume (all P<0.001). PLVR patients (LA/LV ≤0.61, n=182) had a higher rate of ischemic heart disease, lower LV ejection fraction (LVEF), and a higher proportion of moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (all P<0.001). The 1-year composite adverse event rate was 20.6% overall, significantly higher in the PLAR group than in the PLVR group (34.3% vs. 15.1%, P<0.001). Multivariate Cox regression identified PLAR [hazard ratio (HR) =1.72, P=0.008], preoperative N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) >3,000 pg/mL (HR =1.91, P=0.002), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV (HR =2.15, P=0.002), moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (HR =1.58, P=0.036), and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (HR =1.63, P=0.029) as independent risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: The LA/LV volume ratio (optimal cutoff 0.61) effectively classifies RMS left heart remodeling subtypes. PLAR is associated with increased 1-year postoperative adverse outcomes, and integrating mitral/tricuspid regurgitation assessment and extended echocardiographic parameters enhances prognostic accuracy. This provides a robust tool for preoperative risk stratification and individualized treatment in RMS patients.

Title: Echocardiographic epicardial adipose tissue thickness and coronary artery disease: a population-specific analysis.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with coronary artery disease (CAD), but whether this relationship is linear and consistent across different demographic and metabolic subgroups remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to characterize the dose-response pattern of this association and to examine its variation across key demographic and metabolic subgroups.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we enrolled 1,021 consecutive symptomatic patients who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) and echocardiography. EAT thickness was measured at end-systole using transthoracic echocardiography. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the association between EAT thickness and CAD, and a trend analysis was performed by categorizing EAT thickness into quartiles. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to further characterize the dose-response relationship and test the linearity assumption. Interaction analyses were conducted to identify potential effect modifiers, and stratified analyses were additionally performed according to sex, age, hypertension, smoking status, HbA1c level, and HDL-C level.
RESULTS: Among the 1,021 patients, 646 were diagnosed with CAD and had higher EAT thickness than those without CAD. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-mm increase in EAT thickness was associated with a 16% higher odds of CAD [odds ratio (OR): 1.16; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-1.26]. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile showed a markedly increased odds of CAD (OR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.41-3.25), with a significant linear trend (P for trend =0.0024). RCS analysis further supported a linear dose-response relationship, showing no significant deviation from linearity (P for nonlinearity =0.544). Interaction analysis revealed a significant interaction between EAT thickness and BMI (P for interaction=0.017). In subgroup analyses, the association was stronger in individuals with a BMI <24 kg/m2, whereas no significant association was observed in those with a BMI ≥24 kg/m2. Descriptive findings also suggested that the association was stronger among males, older adults (≥55 years), individuals with hypertension, non-smokers, and those with HDL-C ≥1.04 mmol/L.
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic EAT thickness demonstrated a significant positive linear association with CAD, which was significantly modified by BMI, with a notably stronger effect observed in individuals with BMI <24 kg/m2. Routine echocardiographic assessment of EAT thickness may help identify individuals at higher CAD risk, particularly among those with a normal BMI.

Title: Ultrasonic texture features for assessing abnormal interventricular septum motion following cardiac surgery.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery alters cardiomyocyte geometry and architecture, leading to changes in the acoustic properties of the myocardium. This study investigated ultrasomics-a novel cardiac ultrasound-based radiomics technique that extracts high-throughput pixel-level information from images-to identify ultrasonic texture and morphological changes associated with abnormal motion of the interventricular septum (IVS) following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A total of 650 patients from two centers were included in the study. The 460 patients from Center A were randomly allocated to the training (n=322) and internal validation (n=138) sets at a 7:3 ratio, while the 190 patients from Center B constituted the independent external validation set. All patients underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) at two time points: 10 minutes after anesthesia induction (preoperative) and 10 minutes after chest closure (postoperative). Standard left ventricular long-axis and four-chamber views were acquired to visualize the IVS. The workflow consisted of IVS segmentation, radiomics feature extraction, and feature selection using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Three machine learning methods were compared: logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM). Model interpretability was evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis.
RESULTS: Twenty-six significant radiomics features, including shape, first-order, and texture features, were identified. The incidence of postoperative abnormal IVS motion was 50.93%, 46.38%, and 40.00% in the training, internal validation and external validation sets, respectively, with no significant intergroup difference (P>0.05). The SVM model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.943 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.925-0.961] in the training set, 0.948 (95% CI: 0.921-0.974) in the internal validation set, and 0.803 (95% CI: 0.772-0.834) in the external validation set. Postoperative analysis revealed significant changes in the core IVS radiomics features. Specifically, increased gray-scale heterogeneity and decreased texture correlation in the IVS were observed in patients with abnormal septal motion after cardiac surgery (all relevant P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the potential of cardiac ultrasomics to differentiate between normal and abnormal IVS motion in patients after cardiac surgery. A highly interpretable SVM ultrasomics model was developed based on texture and morphological features, providing quantitative characterization of microstructural changes in the IVS associated with abnormal motion following cardiac surgery and potentially supporting more precise perioperative clinical decision-making.

Title: Beta-blockers, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, and cardiovascular outcomes during trastuzumab therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trastuzumab has substantially improved clinical outcomes in patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer, but treatment-related cardiac dysfunction may compromise treatment continuity and long-term cardiovascular health. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether prophylactic beta-blockers or renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs) preserve left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and reduce cardiotoxicity during trastuzumab-based therapy.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 31, 2026. Randomized controlled trials enrolling adults with HER2-positive breast cancer receiving trastuzumab-based therapy were eligible. LVEF change was pooled as a mean difference (MD) in percentage points, and cardiotoxicity incidence was pooled as a risk ratio (RR), both with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by drug class, with formal interaction testing.
RESULTS: Five randomized controlled trials involving 848 patients were included. Four trials involving 358 participants contributed to the LVEF analysis. Overall, prophylactic cardioprotective therapy was not significantly associated with greater LVEF preservation (MD, 1.93 percentage points; 95% CI: -0.07 to 3.93; I2=67.4%), and the 95% prediction interval ranged from -4.34 to 8.19 percentage points. Within the drug-class subgroups, RASIs were associated with greater LVEF preservation (MD, 2.90 percentage points; 95% CI: 0.92 to 4.87), whereas the estimate for beta-blockers was not statistically significant (MD, 1.47 percentage points; 95% CI: -1.35 to 4.29). However, the interaction test showed no significant difference between drug classes (P for interaction =0.416). Five trials involving 821 participants reported cardiotoxicity incidence. Cardioprotective therapy did not significantly reduce cardiotoxicity overall (RR, 0.97; 95% CI: 0.66 to 1.41; I2=31.4%). Neither RASIs (RR, 0.97; 95% CI: 0.60 to 1.57) nor beta-blockers (RR, 0.97; 95% CI: 0.32 to 2.91) significantly reduced cardiotoxicity incidence, and the interaction test showed no significant difference between drug classes (P for interaction =0.995).
CONCLUSIONS: Current randomized evidence does not demonstrate a clear overall benefit of prophylactic beta-blockers or RASIs for preserving LVEF or preventing cardiotoxicity during trastuzumab-based therapy. Although RASIs showed a significant within-class association with LVEF preservation, the nonsignificant interaction test precludes conclusions regarding class superiority. Larger randomized trials with standardized cardiac outcomes and risk-stratified designs are required.

Title: Ankle Foot Orthosis Intervention Improves the Ground Reaction Forces During Walking in Patients with Peripheral Artery Disease (Randomized Clinical Trial).
Abstract: This study investigated the impact of walking with ankle-foot-orthoses (AFOs) and without AFOs (non-AFO) on ground reaction forces (GRFs) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Additionally, this study examined the effect of AFO intervention vs. no AFO intervention on GRFs while walking with and without AFOs. Fifty patients with PAD were randomly assigned to either a three-month intervention (AFO) or a control (standard-of-care) group. After three months, subjects crossed over to the alternate group and were evaluated after three additional months. GRF data (anterior-posterior, medial-lateral, and vertical) were collected during walking with and without AFOs at baseline, three, and six months. Peak discrete GRF points, braking and propulsion impulses were compared across conditions, groups, and time points using linear mixed models. The peak brake and propulsion GRF were significantly reduced while walking with AFOs versus non-AFO (p < 0.01). Compared to non-AFO, walking with AFOs significantly reduced lateral GRF magnitude (p = 0.03) and significantly increased medial GRF (p = 0.02). The first and second maximum (p < 0.01) vertical GRF were significantly increased with AFOs versus non-AFOs. Walking with AFOs helped patients with PAD achieve greater peak propulsion and vertical GRFs compared to non-AFO, with GRF values trending toward those previously reported in healthy individuals.

Title: Ultra-high-pitch photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) versus ultra-high-pitch dual-source computed tomography (DSCT) for coronary artery disease evaluation in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) patients.
Abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To compare radiation dose and image quality of coronary artery reconstructions obtained from non-coronary-dedicated transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) planning CT scans using ultra-high-pitch photon-counting CT (PCCT) and ultra-high-pitch energy-integrating detector dual-source CT (EID-DSCT; hereafter referred to as DSCT), including assessment of the feasibility of coronary artery evaluation according to the Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study on consecutive patients with aortic valve stenosis (AS) undergoing contrast-enhanced TAVI planning CT, either PCCT or DSCT between August 2021 and June 2023. CT dose index (CTDI) and dose length product (DLP) were used to calculate the effective radiation dose (eRD). Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were calculated using standardized region-of-interest (ROI) analysis. Coronary arteries were evaluated by three independent radiologists using 5-point Likert scales followed by a classification according to the CAD-RADS system.
RESULTS: 187 patients (83 female, median age 82, IQR: 76-84) underwent 190 CT-examinations, 103 PCCT (54.2%) and 87 (45.8%) DSCT. Three patients underwent both PCCT and DSCT for clinical reasons. Mean CTDI and DLP were significantly lower in PCCT compared to DSCT (21.9 vs. 52.8 and 607.9 vs. 906.8, respectively; both p < 0.001), with a correspondingly lower mean effective radiation dose (eRD) in PCCT compared to DSCT (10.3 ± 5.4 mSv vs. 15.4 ± 5.6 mSv, p < 0.001). While both SNR and CNR were lower in PCCT than in DSCT (SNR: 35.28 ± 11.63 in PCCT vs. 45.6 ± 16.3 in DSCT, p < 0.001; CNR: 49.25 ± 13.31 in PCCT vs. 57.42 v ± 22.55 in DSCT, p = 0.004), PCCT outperformed DSCT in every one of the eleven visual image categories. Overall image quality was rated as good or excellent in 71.8% (74/103) of PCCT vs. 19.5% (17/87) of DSCT scans. Coronary reconstructions were rated as good or excellent in 72.8% (75/103) of PCCT vs. 20.7% of DSCT datasets.
