CAD-RADS [1-5] rating was possible in 68.9% (71/103) of PCCT vs. 39.1% (34/87) of DSCT datasets.
CONCLUSION: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) allows for significantly improved assessability of the coronary arteries in TAVI planning CT compared with dual-source CT (DSCT), while achieving a substantially lower radiation dose.

Title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology for non-experts: decoding key terms and understanding machine learning methodologies. A Scientific Statement of the ESC Working Group on e-Cardiology, the European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA), the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC), the Heart Failure Association (HFA), the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI), the European Association of Preventive Cardiology (EAPC), and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC, the ESC Regulatory Affairs Committee, and the ESC Digital Cardiology and Artificial Intelligence Committee.
Abstract: Evidence-based medicine represents the systematic approach through which physicians today use the best available scientific evidence from clinical research to guide their clinical decision-making process. However, the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), with its diverse models and potential applications in medicine, is leading to a new form of research driven by 'big data' and heterogeneous datasets, extending beyond conventional statistical analysis and thereby making AI literacy an increasingly essential competence for clinicians. Artificial intelligence applications in cardiology have shown potential to support disease diagnosis, risk prediction, workflow efficiency, and therapeutic decision-making. However, despite these opportunities, AI may also represent a technological barrier for many physicians, due to its mathematical foundations and the speed at which models evolve. A solid understanding of AI concepts is therefore necessary for cardiologists to critically interpret results and engage with this new research landscape. This scientific statement explores AI in cardiology from an educational perspective, outlining the key knowledge required to build adequate AI literacy. The goal is to enable cardiologists not only to avoid reliance on external experts for methodological decisions, but also to collaborate with greater insight and informed judgment.

Title: Acute Myocardial Injury in Patients Presenting With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Prevalence, Predictors, Troponin Dynamics, and In-Hospital Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) may cause anemia, hypovolemia, and hemodynamic compromise, potentially contributing to myocardial injury during the acute illness. Troponin elevation in this setting requires careful interpretation because an isolated measurement cannot reliably distinguish acute injury from elevation without qualifying change or establish myocardial infarction. The frequency, temporal evolution, and clinical significance of acute myocardial injury in patients with UGIB remain incompletely characterized. This prospective multicenter study evaluated its prevalence, associated admission factors, serial troponin dynamics, and relationship with in-hospital outcomes, including subsequent mortality among patients surviving the first 24 hours.
METHODS: This prospective multicenter observational cohort study enrolled 1,000 adults at tertiary care hospitals in Punjab, Pakistan, between January 2025 and August 2026. Cardiac troponin I measurements were scheduled at presentation, 3-6 hours, and 20-24 hours. Acute injury required a concentration above the applicable 99th-percentile reference limit and a serial maximum-minimum range of ≥10 ng/L and ≥20% of the earliest observed concentration, using at least two measurements spanning ≥3 hours. Prevalence was estimated with Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression examined admission factors associated with injury. A 24-hour landmark analysis evaluated subsequent mortality among patients alive and still hospitalized with classifiable injury status.
RESULTS: Injury status was classifiable in 960 patients; 104 had acute injury, giving a prevalence of 10.8% (95% CI: 9.0-13.0%). A further 131 patients (13.6% of classifiable assessments) had troponin elevation without qualifying change, while 40 assessments were indeterminate. Older age (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per decade: 1.40; 95% CI: 1.21-1.63), coronary artery disease (aOR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.06-3.10), and lower hemoglobin (aOR per 1 g/dL decrease: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.06-1.51) were associated with acute injury. Fourteen acute-injury cases (13.5%) first met the classification criterion at the late measurement. Among 810 landmark patients with known outcomes, 34 died. Subsequent mortality was 15.2% with acute injury versus 2.8% without acute injury (aOR: 3.47; 95% CI: 1.58-7.62; p=0.002). An adverse differential assignment of unresolved mortality outcomes attenuated this association (aOR: 1.86; 95% CI: 0.94-3.69).
CONCLUSIONS: Acute myocardial injury affected approximately one in 10 classifiable patients with UGIB and was associated with older age, coronary artery disease, lower hemoglobin, and higher subsequent in-hospital mortality. Serial measurements distinguished acute changes from elevation without qualifying change. The mortality association requires cautious interpretation because of limited events, residual confounding, and incomplete follow-up.

Title: Association of Baseline Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index with 12-month Change in Arterial Stiffness in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease: An Exploratory Single-Center Longitudinal Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) reflects arterial stiffness and is associated with the severity of coronary artery disease (CAD). Short-term change in CAVI in patients with angiographically documented CAD is poorly described. We explored whether baseline CAVI was associated with its 12-month change.
METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis used data from a previously published single-center study, extended with 12-month follow-up. Clinically stable patients with at least 50% coronary stenosis on invasive angiography and paired CAVI measurements were included. Change in the mean of right and left CAVI (ΔCAVI-mean) was the 12-month value minus the baseline value; positive values indicate greater stiffness, and ΔCAVI-mean ≥ +0.5 defined worsening. Non-worsening was analyzed by logistic regression; post hoc analyses estimated the change expected from regression to the mean.
RESULTS: Of 157 patients, 33 (21.0%) worsened. CAVI-mean was 9.20 ± 0.80 at baseline and 9.15 ± 0.76 at 12 months (r = 0.43). Baseline CAVI-mean ≥9.0 was associated with non-worsening (odds ratio adjusted for age and sex 8.10, 95% CI 3.35-19.58). ΔCAVI-mean differed by -0.81 (95% CI -1.08 to -0.54) between patients with baseline CAVI-mean ≥9.0 and those below 9.0; regression to the mean alone predicted a difference of -0.74. ΔCAVI-mean was not related to the average of the two measurements (Oldham's method: r = -0.05; p = 0.54).
CONCLUSION: In this selected single-center CAD cohort, baseline CAVI-mean ≥9.0 was associated with lower odds of CAVI worsening over 12 months. The association was of the size expected from regression to the mean and should not be interpreted as a biological effect. The worsening threshold is not clinically validated and no clinical outcomes were assessed. Studies of change in CAVI need repeated measurements, continuous modeling, and validation in larger cohorts with clinical outcomes.

Title: Effects of probiotic or synbiotic supplementation on glycolipid metabolism in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis, combined with trial sequential analysis (TSA), evaluated the effects of probiotic/synbiotic supplementation on glycolipid metabolism in patients with coronary heart disease (CHD).
METHODS: Randomized controlled trials published up to May 1, 2026, were systematically searched across major databases, including PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and ClinicalTrials.gov. Pooled analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.3, and TSA was conducted to assess the conclusiveness of evidence. Mean difference (MD) and risk ratio (RR) were calculated for continuous and dichotomous outcomes, respectively.
RESULTS: Six trials involving 296 participants were included. Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation was associated with a reduction in fasting blood glucose (FBG) (MD - 19.25 mg/dL, 95% CI -32.28 to -6.22, p = 0.004) and an increase in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) (MD 3.70 mg/dL, 95% CI 1.65 to 5.74, p = 0.0004) based on four studies involving 192 participants. No significant effects were observed on low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, very low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol, triglycerides, insulin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance, quantitative insulin sensitivity check index, systolic blood pressure, or diastolic blood pressure (p ≥ 0.05). Although adverse event rates did not differ significantly (p ≥ 0.05), safety evidence was limited by few events and a wide confidence interval. TSA showed that the cumulative evidence for both HDL-C and FBG did not cross the prespecified monitoring boundaries or reach the required information sizes. The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was rated as low or very low.
CONCLUSION: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation may be associated with increased HDL-C and reduced FBG levels in patients with CHD. However, given the negative TSA findings, low certainty of evidence, and lack of hard cardiovascular outcomes, changes in HDL-C and FBG cannot be regarded as direct evidence of cardiovascular benefit. Furthermore, generalizability is limited, as five of the six studies were conducted in Iran and only one in China, which may limit applicability to populations with different dietary patterns, microbiome profiles, ethnic backgrounds, or healthcare systems. The substantial heterogeneity in probiotic strains, formulations, doses, and treatment durations also limits generalization to probiotics or synbiotics as a whole.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251178187; identifier: CRD420251178187.

Title: Cardiopulmonary Event Prevalence Before First Recorded COPD Diagnosis: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Post-COPD diagnosis, individuals have an increased risk of cardiopulmonary events, but little is known about the risk pre-diagnosis. This study extends previous evidence by investigating the prevalence of cardiopulmonary events before the first recorded COPD diagnosis, including within a standardised 3-year pre-diagnosis window, and compared cardiopulmonary risk with that of matched controls without COPD.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective, cohort study included patients with a diagnosis of COPD in the Clinical Practice Research Datalink. The overall cohort included patients aged ≥35 years with a COPD diagnosis prior to December 31, 2019, from which an incident COPD cohort was identified with first recorded diagnosis between January 1, 2018-December 31, 2019 (index date). Cardiopulmonary events of interest were quantified within 3 years pre-index among those with ≥3 years of pre-index data and during the full look-back period. Matched non-COPD patients served as controls (1:2 ratio).
RESULTS: Of 426,854 patients with COPD, 77,428 were incident and matched 1:2 to patients without COPD. Patients in the incident cohort (mean age 67.4 [SD 13.6] years, 52% male, 94% White) had a higher prevalence of pre-diagnosis cardiopulmonary events than controls (76.2% versus 45.6%; odds ratio (OR) 3.8, [95% CI: 3.8-3.9]). This association was consistent, with greater relative odds observed among those with ≥3 years pre-index data (n=70,062): 56.6% had a cardiopulmonary event vs 20.9% (OR 4.9, 95% CI: 4.8-5.0) within 3 years pre-index, including severe cardiovascular events in 16,679 (23.8%) and respiratory events in 32,293 (46.1%) patients. Most common severe cardiovascular events were atrial fibrillation (58.1%), heart failure (46.1%) and myocardial infarction (15.1%). Before diagnosis, patients with incident COPD also had substantially greater HCRU, including 4.3-fold higher inpatient costs than matched controls.
CONCLUSION: Cardiopulmonary events are frequent before COPD diagnosis, and signal elevated cardiopulmonary risk. Understanding the occurrence of antecedent cardiopulmonary events in COPD may enable earlier diagnosis and treatment.

Title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a well-established role in RA treatment and potential therapeutic value in several other rheumatic diseases; however, its use should be guided by disease-specific evidence, previous treatment exposure, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and individual safety risks. Further prospective and long-term studies are needed to better define its role in less well-established indications and special populations.

Title: Efficacy and safety of conscious/deep sedation versus general anesthesia in pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a promising therapy for atrial fibrillation. While general anesthesia (GA) is the standard to ensure catheter stability, using conscious or deep sedation (CS/DS) to streamline workflows is gaining interest. However, whether CS/DS provides comparable safety and efficacy to GA remains controversial and has lacked systematic evaluation.
OBJECTIVES: To compare the clinical efficacy and safety of PFA for atrial fibrillation under GA vs. CS/DS.
METHODS: A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase from inception to April 9, 2026. Studies were selected using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The comparison of GA and CS/DS during PFA focused on the following clinical outcomes: procedural time, left atrial dwell time, fluoroscopy time, pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) success rate, and adverse event incidence. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I² statistic and Cochran's Q test; sensitivity analysis was performed if heterogeneity was high. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test.
RESULTS: Ten studies involving 3,692 atrial fibrillation patients were included. Compared to GA, CS/DS significantly shortened overall procedural time (WMD: -7.73 min, random-effects; 95% CI: -14.17 to -1.29; P = 0.019). However, there were no significant differences between the groups in left atrial dwell time (WMD: -2.59 min, random-effects; 95% CI: -9.74 to 4.57), fluoroscopy time (WMD: -2.52 min, random-effects; 95% CI: -5.31 to 0.28), acute PVI success (RR: 1.00, fixed-effects; 95% CI: 0.98 to 1.03), or major adverse events (RR: 1.57, fixed-effects; 95% CI: 0.81 to 3.05). CS/DS showed a borderline trend toward fewer minor adverse events (RR: 0.61, fixed-effects; 95% CI: 0.37 to 1.01; P = 0.053).
CONCLUSION: In PFA for AF, CS/DS was associated with reduced overall procedural time compared with GA, while maintaining comparable acute PVI success rates and safety profiles. However, large-scale randomized controlled trials are still needed to confirm these findings.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251165071, identifier (CRD420251165071).

Title: Whippets have larger abdominal caudal vena cava to aorta ratios than other dogs on computed tomography.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whippets are sighthounds with distinct cardiovascular adaptations associated with athletic performance. The caudal vena cava to aorta ratio (CVC/Ao) is an established index of intravascular volume status, assessed ultrasonographically and on computed tomography (CT) at thoracic and abdominal sites, but breed-specific differences remain unreported. We compared thoracic and abdominal CVC/Ao in whippets and non-whippet controls, and with published reference values, and hypothesised that whippets would have higher ratios.
METHODS: Sixty-eight dogs without known cardiovascular disease (34 whippets, 34 non-whippet controls) were retrospectively reviewed. CTs were performed under general anaesthesia, with CVC/Ao measured at standardised abdominal and thoracic sites. Groups were compared with Welch's two-sample t-tests, sites within animals with paired t-tests, and analysis of covariance adjusted for weight and age. Significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Whippets had significantly higher abdominal CVC/Ao than controls (1.54 ± 0.29 vs. 1.28 ± 0.23; p < 0.001), whereas thoracic ratios did not differ (1.22 ± 0.23 vs. 1.28 ± 0.26; p = 0.29). The abdominal difference persisted after adjustment for weight and age (adjusted difference 0.29, 95% CI 0.15-0.42; p < 0.001). Within whippets, abdominal ratios exceeded thoracic ratios (p < 0.001), a difference not seen in controls (p = 0.99). The thoracic ratio declined with age independently of breed and weight (-0.023 per year; p = 0.002). Both groups exceeded published CT values at both sites, and a greater proportion of whippets than controls exceeded the ultrasonographic upper limit (73.5% vs. 41.2%; p = 0.007). Observed mean ± 2 SD limits were 0.96-2.13 (abdomen, whippets), 0.82-1.75 (abdomen, controls) and 0.76-1.74 (thorax, combined); these are cohort observations rather than breed-specific reference ranges.
DISCUSSION: Whippets had larger abdominal CVC/Ao than controls, with comparable thoracic ratios, indicating a site-specific increase not attributable to body size or age. Because both groups exceeded published values, reference values are not transferable across imaging modality irrespective of breed or anaesthetic status. Modality-, breed- and possibly age-specific ranges are needed, and we provide preliminary limits as a starting point.

Title: Exposure to Size-Fractioned Ambient Particles Associated with Alterations in Gut Microbiome and Pro-Atherosclerotic Biomarkers in Young Adults.
Abstract: Background: Ambient fine and ultrafine particles are linked to the progression of atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases, wherein gut microbiome may play a critical role. However, the underlying mechanisms and relevant metabolic pathways are not yet fully understood. Objectives: To identify the features and metabolic pathways of gut microbiome, and to explore their potential roles in the pro-inflammatory and pro-atherosclerotic effects of particles in size ranges of 5-560 nm (measured as number concentration, PNC5-560). Methods: We conducted a longitudinal panel study of 152 young adults in Beijing, China, with four monthly clinical examinations between September 2019 and January 2020. Gut microbiome, fecal metabolome, and circulating pro-inflammatory and pro-atherosclerotic biomarkers were measured. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations linking short-term PNC5-560 exposure to health indicators. We further evaluated whether gut microbiota could mediate changes in these biomarkers and identified the underlying metabolic pathways. Results: Major sources of PNC5-560 in the study area were identified as diesel vehicle emissions (37.9%), gasoline vehicle emissions (39.4%), nucleation (9.2%), and secondary aerosols (11.9%). Per interquartile range increment in PNC5-560 over the preceding 7 days was associated with significant elevations in circulating pro-inflammatory and pro-atherosclerotic biomarkers, with effect estimates ranging from 2.1% (95% CI: 0.4%, 3.8%) to 198.6% (95% CI: 29.3%, 365.8%). PNC5-560 exposure was also associated with decreased gut microbial α-diversity (e.g., Shannon, Simpson, and Chao1) and altered taxonomic composition. Several microbial species (e.g., Solibaculum mannosilyticum, Bacteroides stercoris, and Bifidobacterium longum) were identified as potential mediators of the effects of PNC5-560 on pro-inflammatory and pro-atherosclerotic responses, with mediation proportions up to 9.8% (95% CI: 0.8, 38.3) and 4.8% (95% CI: 0.09, 22.5), respectively. Functional analyses further revealed that these mediating effects involved perturbations in nucleotide and amino acid metabolism pathways. Conclusions: This study provides evidence suggesting that gut microbiome may regulate nucleotide and amino acid metabolism, thereby partially mediating the detrimental cardiovascular effects of size-fractioned ambient particles.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Radial Versus Femoral Access for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Study From Southern Puerto Rico.
Abstract: Background and aim Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) frequently undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using either radial or femoral arterial access. Prior studies have shown potential benefits of radial access; however, data are limited regarding these approaches in patients from Puerto Rico. This study aimed to compare bleeding, vascular complications, and 30-day all-cause mortality between radial and femoral access for PCI in patients with STEMI in southern Puerto Rico. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional review of medical records of patients aged 21-90 years admitted with STEMI at Centro Médico Episcopal San Lucas in southern Puerto Rico from 2021 to 2023. We excluded patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction or unstable angina. A total of 311 patients were identified and included in the study. Patients were stratified according to radial or femoral access on the first attempt. Outcomes included 30-day all-cause mortality, pseudoaneurysm, hematoma, and bleeding after thrombolysis in myocardial infarction. All statistical analyses were conducted using RStudio (Boston, MA: Posit, PBC). Results Among the study subjects, 90 patients had first-attempt radial access, while 221 patients had first-attempt femoral access. There were no major bleeding events in any of the groups. Minor bleeding events were reported for one out of 90 patients in the radial group compared to 21 patients out of 221 in the femoral group. This difference was statistically significant (p=0.01791). Pseudoaneurysm did not occur in the radial group, while seven occurred in the femoral group; however, this difference was not statistically significant. No hematoma was seen in any patient in the first-attempt radial access group, compared with 33 patients with hematoma in the femoral access group (p=0.001). Mortality within 30 days from all causes occurred in one of 90 patients in the radial group compared with 26 of 221 patients in the femoral group. The 30-day survival rate was 98.9% in the radial group and 88.2% in the femoral group, representing a statistically significant difference (p=0.0012). Conclusion Among patients with STEMI undergoing PCI in southern Puerto Rico, first-attempt radial access was associated with lower rates of minor bleeding, hematoma, and 30-day all-cause mortality compared with first-attempt femoral access. The results suggest potential clinical advantages of radial access when clinically appropriate. However, since the current study is of an observational design, it is not reasonable to claim a cause-and-effect relationship. Larger studies that control for clinical factors are needed.

Title: Distinct risk factors for thrombosis in systemic lupus erythematosus and primary Sjögren's syndrome: A large Chinese cohort study with arterial-venous distinction.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the overall incidence and arterial-venous distribution of thrombosis, identify independent predictors of total and subtype-specific events, develop a prediction model, and evaluate the discriminative performance of risk factors in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 955 SLE patients and 558 pSS patients from a single center. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to determine independent risk factors for thrombosis. Discriminative ability was assessed using the time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and Harrell's concordance index (C-index).
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 10 years (interquartile range [IQR] 8-12) for SLE and 9 years (IQR 7-12) for pSS. In multivariable analysis, independent risk factors for total thrombosis in SLE were hypertension (hazard ratio [HR] 1.523, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.213-2.135, P = 0.03), lupus nephritis (HR 1.822, 95% CI 1.225-2.883, P < 0.0001), smoking history (HR 3.613, 95% CI 2.426-4.631, P < 0.0001), and positive lupus anticoagulant (LA) (HR 3.213, 95% CI 2.311-4.157, P < 0.0001); for pSS, they were diabetes (HR 1.913, 95% CI 1.112-3.245, P = 0.023), elevated platelet count (HR 3.115, 95% CI 1.672-6.779, P = 0.006), and positive LA (HR 2.611, 95% CI 1.697-3.782, P < 0.0001). The SLE prediction model yielded a C-index of 0.752 (95% CI 0.71-0.79), with 3-, 5-, and 10-year time-dependent AUCs of 0.778, 0.761, and 0.755. Beyond conventional discriminative metrics, positive likelihood ratio (LR+) and negative likelihood ratio (LR-) were calculated to evaluate the clinical practicality of the prediction models. In pSS, the combined discriminative capacity was limited, with a C-index of 0.665 (95% CI 0.587-0.743) and corresponding AUCs of 0.600, 0.606, and 0.639.
CONCLUSION: The underlying risk-factor profiles differ fundamentally between SLE and pSS. The SLE prediction model demonstrates acceptable-good discriminative performance and may serve as a guide for thrombotic risk stratification. Routine LA screening, alongside standardized management of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, should be incorporated into long-term thromboprophylaxis strategies for both diseases.

Title: Heterogeneous competing causes of death and transportability of the PREVENT equations.
Abstract: The American Heart Association's PREVENT equations represent a major advance in cardiovascular risk prediction, in part because they account for the possibility that patients may die from non-cardiovascular causes before experiencing a cardiovascular event. Despite this advance, recent external validations have found that PREVENT systematically underestimates cardiovascular risk in Black patients, socioeconomically disadvantaged groups, veterans, and those with Medicaid or no insurance. We propose that one underrecognized contributor is how PREVENT handles non-cardiovascular death: by treating all such deaths from cancer, overdose, suicide, injury, and other causes as a single combined category. This aggregation is a problem because the mix of competing causes differs across populations. The direct consequence is that the model's competing-risk adjustment reflects the cause-of-death composition of its derivation cohort rather than that of the population being evaluated, and standard recalibration methods cannot correct this mismatch. The direction of the resulting error is predictable: populations with disproportionately high overdose, suicide, and injury mortality relative to the cancer-dominant pattern of general-population derivation cohorts will have their cardiovascular risk systematically underestimated. This problem is further obscured by a common methodological choice in validation studies: using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates rather than cause-specific competing-risk methods to measure observed event rates. This approach inflates apparent event rates in exactly the subgroups most affected, making miscalibration harder to interpret and potentially masking its true direction. Future cardiovascular risk prediction models should separate non-cardiovascular deaths into cause-specific competing processes. External validations should use cause-specific competing-risk estimation. Health systems considering adoption of PREVENT should validate it locally before implementation, with particular attention to calibration within subgroups defined by competing-mortality burden.

Title: Dyslipidemia management in athletes: A comparative commentary on the 2026 ACC/AHA/Multisociety Guideline and contemporary sports cardiology recommendations.
Abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of exercise-related sudden cardiac death in athletes older than 35 years, and dyslipidemia is one of its principal modifiable drivers. The 2026 ACC/AHA/Multisociety Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol introduces several advances directly relevant to athletes, including restored LDL-C treatment targets, universal lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] measurement, the PREVENT-ASCVD risk equations, expanded options for selective coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring, and a more aggressive approach to lipid-lowering therapy (LLT). However, sports cardiology guidelines and consensus statements offer important caveats that must be reconciled with these general-population recommendations: existing risk calculators, including PREVENT, do not reliably estimate cardiovascular risk in athletes, and routine CAC scoring is not recommended in athletes at low calculated risk. This commentary compares and contrasts general-population dyslipidemia recommendations with athlete-specific guidance from contemporary sports cardiology consensus documents, highlights recent evidence on Lp(a), wearable-derived training load, and risk score performance across the physical activity spectrum, and proposes a five-step clinical framework, refined to reflect athlete-specific risk stratification, for dyslipidemia evaluation and management in this population.

Title: WHO HEARTS programs in high-income countries: Implementation, outcomes, and implications for global hypertension control.
Abstract: Despite advanced healthcare systems and near-universal coverage, hypertension control rates have stagnated in many high-income countries (HICs), even as this condition remains the leading preventable cause of cardiovascular disease and premature mortality worldwide. The WHO HEARTS technical package, initially designed for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), offers a comprehensive framework for strengthening hypertension management through six core components: healthy lifestyle counseling, evidence-based protocols, access to essential medicines and technology, risk-based cardiovascular disease management, team-based care, and systems for monitoring. Modeled on prior global analyses of WHO HEARTS in LMICs, this structured program report synthesizes available evidence on HEARTS implementation and outcomes in HICs, drawing on national registry data, PAHO/WHO program reports, and pooled epidemiological surveys. Results demonstrate that HEARTS is both feasible and effective in high-resource settings, with early adopters achieving substantial improvements in hypertension control. This report also identifies key barriers to HEARTS implementation in HICs, including therapeutic inertia, physician resistance to standardized protocols, fragmented electronic health record systems, and persistent socioeconomic inequities. However, HICs possess distinct advantages including advanced monitoring infrastructure, trained multidisciplinary teams, reliable medication supply chains, and financing capacity. These findings demonstrate that HEARTS provides a relevant and necessary framework for HICs to overcome systemic barriers, close equity gaps, and achieve sustained improvements in hypertension control. Expanding HEARTS across high-resource settings represents a critical opportunity to reverse declining control trends and prevent avoidable cardiovascular disease globally.

Title: Correlation between chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and comorbidities-a systematic analysis integrating global burden of disease and mendelian randomization study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently coexists with multiple comorbidities. However, the long-term trends, regional disparities, and potential causal relationships in the global burden of these comorbidities remain to be systematically elucidated. This study aimed to characterize the disease burden of common comorbidities in patients with COPD and to assess the potential causal relationships between these comorbidities and COPD.
METHODS: This study integrated data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) and conducted two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses. Based on GBD data from 1990 to 2023, we performed descriptive burden assessment, Das Gupta decomposition, Bayesian age-period-cohort modelling, exploratory correlation analysis, and formal age-interaction regression. Using summary statistics from the FinnGen consortium, we evaluated bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and various comorbidities primarily via the inverse variance weighted (IVW) method with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. The comorbidities of focus included asthma, anxiety disorders, major depressive disorder, pulmonary hypertension, hypertensive heart disease, ischemic heart disease, musculoskeletal disorders, osteoporosis, and respiratory tract cancers.
RESULTS: The absolute burden of comorbidities in COPD continued to increase, albeit driven by distinct factors. Population aging and growth were identified as the primary drivers for the rising burden of several COPD comorbidities, such as ischemic heart disease and musculoskeletal disorders. Significant regional inequalities were observed in disease distribution: high Socio-demographic Index (SDI) regions bore a heavier burden of musculoskeletal and mental disorders, whereas middle and low SDI regions exhibited more pronounced mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to ischemic heart disease. Formal interaction models demonstrated significant age heterogeneity in the ecological associations between COPD prevalence and all eight comorbidities after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (all q ≤0.028). MR analyses provided evidence supporting bidirectional genetic associations between COPD and specific comorbidities. Genetically predicted COPD was significantly associated with an increased risk of asthma and depression (FDR <0.05), and conversely, genetic susceptibility to asthma and depression was associated with a higher risk of developing COPD (FDR <0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The comorbidity patterns between COPD and its key concomitant conditions are influenced by multiple factors, including demographic structure, regional development levels, and shared biological mechanisms. Our findings underscore the necessity of shifting from a single-disease management model towards integrated care strategies that emphasize comorbidity screening and holistic patient management.

Title: Clinical efficacy of minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery concomitant with radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) and valvular heart disease (VHD) present complex clinical challenges. Standard radiofrequency ablation (RFA) combined with valve surgery via median sternotomy offers robust rhythm correction but causes significant surgical trauma. Minimally invasive cardiac valve surgery with concomitant RFA (MICVS-RFA) is a promising strategy, but clinical data regarding its comprehensive safety, efficacy, and predictive risk factors for AF recurrence remain scarce. Thus, we aimed to evaluate the safety and clinical efficacy of MICVS-RFA and to develop an exploratory prognostic model for risk stratification.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 146 patients with concomitant VHD and AF who underwent MICVS-RFA between April 1, 2020, and August 1, 2025. Surgical cohorts included mitral valve replacement (MVR; n=34), mitral valve repair (MVr; n=19), MVR combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVR + TVr; n=57), and MVr combined with tricuspid valve repair (MVr + TVr; n=36). Pre-operative predictors for post-operative AF recurrence were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and elastic net regularization integrated within a multiple imputation framework to develop an exploratory model. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvements were assessed dynamically.
RESULTS: Procedural success was achieved in all 146 patients, with an overall 30-day freedom from recurrent AF (FFAF) rate of 89.7% and no observed major adverse events (stroke, bleeding, or thromboembolism) within the first post-operative month. Length of stay (LOS) showed no statistical differences among surgical cohorts (P=0.71). Logistic regression modeling identified pre-operative metoprolol usage as associated with lower odds of AF recurrence [odds ratio (OR) =0.17; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.04-0.62], while pre-operative pulmonary hypertension (PH) showed a non-significant association with higher odds of AF recurrence (OR =3.07; 95% CI: 0.67-14.10). The predictive model showed moderate discrimination [bootstrap-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) =0.773] and apparent calibration. Patients with baseline LVEF <55% experienced superior functional recovery compared to those with LVEF ≥55% (ΔLVEF: 13.07%±2.56% vs. 0.18%±0.80%, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: MICVS-RFA was a feasible "dual minimally invasive" strategy that permits concomitant treatment of valvular pathology and AF through a minimally invasive approach, minimizing perioperative trauma. Comparative and long-term effects require further study.

Title: Dose-response association between early postoperative serum magnesium and in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study in MIMIC-IV with external replication in the eICU-CRD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypomagnesemia is common following cardiac surgery and is associated with arrhythmias and adverse outcomes. In postoperative cardiac intensive care unit (ICU) patients, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), hemodilution, perioperative electrolyte administration, and acute changes in renal function may alter early serum magnesium concentrations and their clinical interpretation. However, the dose-response relationship between early postoperative serum magnesium levels and mortality in this setting remains unclear. We investigated this association and sought to characterize its dose-response pattern.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult cardiac surgery patients admitted to the ICU in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV; version 3.1; 2008-2022) who had an ICU stay of at least 24 hours and a serum magnesium measurement within 24 hours of ICU admission. The exposure was the first recorded serum magnesium concentration, modeled continuously for the principal dose-response analysis and secondarily categorized into quartiles. Baseline covariates were obtained from ICD-coded diagnoses and electronic health record data. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, ascertained from hospital discharge records in MIMIC-IV and unit or hospital discharge status in the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and piecewise regression were performed, with the threshold estimated from the data. The same eligibility criteria were applied in the eICU-CRD, and the replication analysis used a harmonized covariate set.
RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV cohort included 7,783 patients {median age 68 years [interquartile range (IQR), 60-75 years]; 27.9% women; 70.8% underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score 7}, with 130 in-hospital deaths (1.7%). RCS analysis showed an overall association (P=0.003) compatible with an L-shaped pattern, although the formal test for nonlinearity was not significant. Piecewise regression with a threshold of 2.5 mg/dL showed that each 1 mg/dL increase below this threshold was associated with lower odds of mortality [odds ratio (OR) =0.35; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.18-0.68; P=0.002], whereas no association was observed above the threshold (OR =0.97; P=0.89). In the fully adjusted model, compared with Q2 (2.1-2.3 mg/dL), Q3 (2.4-2.6 mg/dL) was associated with lower odds of mortality (OR =0.50; 95% CI: 0.26-0.95; P=0.03). Sensitivity analyses were broadly consistent, and exploratory subgroup estimates were directionally similar overall. The eICU-CRD cohort included 3,929 patients (median age 68 years; 31.1% women; median SOFA score 8), with 67 deaths (1.71%); the Q3 estimate was directionally consistent but imprecise (OR =0.64; 95% CI: 0.29-1.36).
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative serum magnesium was associated with in-hospital mortality after cardiac surgery, with a hypothesis-generating inflection near 2.5 mg/dL and an association concentrated in the lower magnesium range. Because this is an observational analysis, the findings do not establish a treatment target or demonstrate that increasing magnesium to a specific concentration improves outcomes. Prospective studies are needed to validate this pattern and assess its relevance to postoperative risk stratification.

Title: Clinical outcomes with initial oral triple and dual therapy in echocardiography-defined connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Connective tissue disease-associated pulmonary hypertension (CTD-PH) is a serious complication, but evidence on early oral treatment intensification in patients followed primarily by echocardiography is limited. We evaluated outcomes associated with initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy vs. dual therapy in echocardiography-defined CTD-PH.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included consecutive adults who initiated PH-targeted therapy between April 2020 and June 2025. Treatment was selected by treating physicians in routine care and was not randomized: dual therapy comprised macitentan plus tadalafil, whereas triple therapy additionally included selexipag. Baseline clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic variables were obtained from standardized institutional assessments and reassessed at week 26. The primary endpoint was the change in the number (0-3) of European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) noninvasive low-risk criteria met: World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC) I-II, 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) >440 m, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) <50 ng/L or N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) <300 ng/L. Complete cases with all three components available at both time points were analyzed without imputation. Disease-progression events were recorded through 30 weeks, and adverse events were assessed during follow-up.
RESULTS: Of 119 patients, 59 received triple therapy and 60 received dual therapy. The groups had similar baseline functional and biomarker profiles (6MWD, 290.0 vs. 286.9 m; NT-proBNP, 1,455 vs. 1,473 pg/mL); mean age was 45.5 vs. 47.2 years in the triple and dual therapy group respectively, and 93% vs. 83% were women. At week 26, the change in low-risk criteria differed between groups (P=0.003), with 57.6% vs. 33.3% meeting all the three criteria. Mean 6MWD increased by 156 vs. 104 m (adjusted difference, 52 m; 95% confidence interval (CI): 29-78; P<0.001), and WHO-FC distributions differed at week 26 (P=0.007). Exploratory analysis yielded an hazard ratio (HR) of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.39-1.43) for the first disease-progression event. At least one adverse event occurred in 53/59 (89.8%) vs. 47/60 (78.3%) patients; diarrhea occurred in 24/59 (40.7%) vs. 19/60 (31.7%), nausea in 21/59 (35.6%) vs. 16/60 (26.7%), and jaw pain in 16/59 (27.1%) vs. 11/60 (18.3%), with no significant between-group differences.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients with echocardiography-defined CTD-PH, initial selexipag-containing oral triple therapy was associated with greater improvement in noninvasive ESC/ERS risk status and functional outcomes than dual therapy over 26 weeks, supporting further evaluation of noninvasive risk-guided oral treatment intensification in CTD-associated pulmonary vascular disease. However, given the small, single-center, nonrandomized retrospective design, these findings cannot establish superior efficacy or safety and require prospective multicenter confirmation with systematic hemodynamic assessment.

Title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database.
METHODS: Patients who underwent AD surgery were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (MIMIC-IV; development cohort) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external evaluation cohort). The primary outcome was postoperative GIB within 30 days, defined using a composite database-derived algorithm requiring either (I) a hemoglobin (Hb) decrease of ≥2 g/dL accompanied by at least one supporting indicator, including a transfusion record, hemostatic medication use, or endoscopic examination; or (II) the combination of a transfusion record and a GIB diagnosis. An isolated Hb decrease or transfusion record was not sufficient for outcome classification. Routinely available demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and disease-severity variables were extracted. Records with missing values in variables required for the final analysis were excluded before model development. Multivariable logistic regression served as the baseline model, with XGB and random forest employed as comparator models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 935 patients (GIB incidence, 10.7%), whereas the eICU-CRD validation cohort comprised 542 patients (GIB incidence, 12.7%). In the development cohort, the AUCs were 0.887 for logistic regression, 0.962 for XGB, and 0.853 for random forest. In the eICU-CRD cohort, XGB yielded an AUC point estimate of 0.873.
CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective two-database analysis developed prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery. The models showed discrimination in the analyzed data; however, prospective validation using predictors measured within prespecified pre-event windows is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Association between early vein graft failure and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: an exploratory retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early vein graft failure (VGF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is far from rare and often clinically silent. While mid-to-late graft failure is established to predict adverse clinical events, the long-term prognostic impact of predischarge early VGF remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early VGF and 10-year clinical outcomes following off-pump CABG.
METHODS: In this exploratory retrospective cohort study, adult patients undergoing elective isolated off-pump CABG using vein grafts with early postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography between July 2014 and December 2015 were consecutively included. Baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected from electronic medical records. VGF was defined as Fitzgibbon grade B (≥50% stenosis) or O (occlusion). Patients were stratified into the early VGF group (with at least one failed vein graft) and non-early VGF group (without failed vein grafts). Clinical follow-up was conducted through routine outpatient visits or standardized telephone interviews in accordance with institutional protocol. Primary outcomes included 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization) and its individual components. Secondary outcomes included perioperative myocardial injury and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI). Propensity score overlap weighting was applied to adjust for baseline confounders. Exploratory post-hoc landmark and piecewise Cox analyses were performed to address non-proportional hazards.
RESULTS: A total of 233 patients were included in the analyses (mean age 64.3±7.5 years; 18.4% female). Among them, early VGF was identified in 33 (14.2%) patients and 41 (5.9%) vein grafts. Early VGF numerically increased the risk of perioperative myocardial injury [45.5% vs. 30.5%, odds ratio (OR) 1.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89-4.01; P=0.09] and PMI (12.1% vs. 6.0%, OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.57-6.69; P=0.21), though without statistical significance. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years, there was no statistically significant difference in 10-year MACE between the two groups [early VGF 51.5% vs. non-early VGF 48.2%; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.31, 95% CI: 0.76-2.24; P=0.33]. In exploratory landmark analyses addressing non-proportional hazards (P=0.03), early VGF was associated with a higher risk of MACE within the first 2 years post-surgery (aHR 2.18, 95% CI: 1.14-4.17; P=0.02), which attenuated beyond the 2-year landmark (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.22-1.46; P=0.24). Additionally, early VGF was associated with a higher risk of repeat revascularization (18.2% vs. 7.7%; aHR 3.06, 95% CI: 1.13-8.31; P=0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Predischarge early VGF was not significantly associated with the overall 10-year risk of MACE following off-pump CABG. Exploratory findings regarding early risk clustering within 2 years and an increased risk of repeat revascularization remain hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.

Title: Prognostic value of the apelin-12-to-white blood cell ratio for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), patients remain at risk for long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The apelin-12/white blood cell ratio (AWR), a ratio has never been studied before, may reflect the balance between cardioprotective apelin signaling and systemic inflammation. We examined the prognostic value of admission AWR for long-term MACEs in STEMI patients after primary PCI.
METHODS: This secondary analysis included 464 consecutive STEMI patients who underwent primary PCI at The First People's Hospital of Taizhou (Zhejiang, China) between January 2010 and October 2014. Blood samples were collected on admission, immediately before primary PCI, for apelin-12 measurement. Patients were followed for 30 months. MACE was defined as the composite of cardiac death, cardiogenic shock, congestive heart failure, recurrent target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target-lesion revascularization. AWR was analyzed as a continuous variable and by pre-specified tertiles (cut-points 6.48 and 10.49). Cox proportional-hazards (PH) regression with a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-derived minimal adjustment set (age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, serum creatinine, and Killip class) was used to estimate associations. Predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), C-index, bootstrap optimism correction, integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and net reclassification improvement (NRI).
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.0 months, 118 patients (25.4%) experienced MACEs. Patients in the highest AWR tertile were older and less likely to be male than those in the lowest tertile. Higher AWR was independently associated with lower MACE risk [per 1-standard deviation (1-SD) increase: hazard ratio (HR) 0.52, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.40-0.68, P<0.001; highest vs. lowest tertile: HR 0.40, 95% CI: 0.24-0.65, P<0.001]. The protective association strengthened after the first month. Adding AWR to the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) 2.0 and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) scores significantly improved reclassification (IDI and NRI both P<0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: A lower admission AWR is associated with an increased risk of long-term MACEs in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, supporting its potential as a prognostic biomarker.

Title: Surgical outcomes and long-term survival after repair of post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal defect: a 30-year single-center experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal defect (pMI-VSD) remains a catastrophic mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction despite advances in surgical management. We evaluated early and long-term outcomes after surgical repair of pMI-VSD at a tertiary referral center.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 80 consecutive patients who underwent surgical repair of pMI-VSD between January 1995 and November 2025. Early outcomes, postoperative complications including residual shunting, and long-term all-cause mortality were analyzed. Long-term survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, and a parsimonious Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify factors associated with all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: The mean age was 70.4±9.1 years, and 47.5% were male. The 30-day mortality rate was 7.5%. Residual shunts were detected in 35 patients (43.8%), of whom five (6.3% of the overall cohort) underwent reoperation. During a median observed follow-up of 58.5 months, 38 patients (47.5%) died. Estimated survival was 81.0% [95% confidence interval (CI): 72.8-90.1%] at 1 year, 70.5% (95% CI: 60.8-81.8%) at 5 years. In multivariable analysis, age and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD) were associated with all-cause mortality. Survival differed between patients operated on in ≤2015 and >2015 (log-rank P=0.03), although this unadjusted comparison may reflect concurrent changes in patient characteristics and management.
CONCLUSIONS: Favorable early and long-term outcomes were observed among selected patients who underwent surgical repair of pMI-VSD at an experienced center. Residual shunt status was not associated with a statistically detectable difference in long-term survival, although quantitative hemodynamic assessment was not uniformly available. Survival was better in the more recent era, although the contributions of changes in patient selection, surgical technique, and perioperative management cannot be distinguished in this observational cohort. However, this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature of the study.

Title: Beyond flow: a ventricular-load framework for VA-ECMO in cardiogenic shock.
Abstract: Cardiogenic shock still carries a 30-day mortality of approximately 40%-50% despite reperfusion, vasoactive support and modern intensive care. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) can rapidly restore systemic perfusion, but recent randomised evidence has reframed its role. In infarct-related shock, randomised trials have not shown a clear survival benefit from routine early VA-ECMO; ECLS-SHOCK and pooled analyses also found more bleeding and vascular complications. In the same period, DanGer Shock showed that a primary microaxial-pump (Impella CP) strategy improved survival in a carefully selected population with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock, although it was tested against standard care rather than head-to-head against VA-ECMO and does not isolate unloading as the causal mechanism. Read together, these data motivate the central argument of this review: peripheral VA-ECMO is usefully managed not only as a problem of circulatory flow, but also as a dynamic problem of ventricular loading. We advance this as an organising framework rather than as a demonstrated mechanism, since differences in patient selection between these trials offer a competing and equally tenable explanation. Retrograde aortic return increases effective LV afterload, while venous drainage reduces preload; the clinical result depends on the interaction between circuit flow, native contractility and biventricular loading conditions. This narrative, non-systematic review synthesises contemporary trial evidence, the physiology and treatment of LV loading, and approaches to serial assessment of the supported heart, from haemodynamics and bedside echocardiography to emerging deformation and advanced imaging tools. VA-ECMO should therefore be viewed as a time-limited bridge whose net benefit depends on reversible disease, early recognition of clinically relevant ventricular overload and repeated assessment of recovery, escalation options and futility.

Title: Changes in serum lipid profile after total thyroidectomy versus thyroid lobectomy for papillary thyroid cancer patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum lipids have been suggested to be associated with thyroid dysfunction in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) patients after thyroidectomy. However, the association of lipids with different surgeries remains unclear. This study aimed to examine lipids changes after different surgeries in PTC patients.
METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study enrolled 298 patients diagnosed with PTC who underwent surgery and were followed up routinely, from January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2023. Thyroid functions and fasting serum lipids were evaluated at baseline, 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 months of follow-up. A mixed-effect linear regression model was used to compare postoperative serum lipids with different surgery groups adjusted for baseline confounders.
RESULTS: A total of 435 postoperative measurements of serum lipids were included in the analysis. Compared with total thyroidectomy (TT) (n=144, 48.32%), thyroid lobectomy (TL) (n=154, 51.68%) was associated with decreased postoperative triglyceride [β=-0.255, 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.451 to -0.058] and increased high-density lipoprotein (HDL; β=0.098, 95% CI: 0.013 to 0.182), but not with total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein (LDL), lipoprotein(a) and small dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (sd-LDL-C). The association with triglyceride was more pronounced in shorter follow-up (≤12 months) (β=-0.266, 95% CI: -0.497 to -0.035) vs. longer follow-up (>12 months) (β=-0.155, 95% CI: -0.563 to 0.253). Association with HDL was more pronounced in longer follow-up (β=0.172, 95% CI: 0.003 to 0.341) vs. shorter follow-up (β=0.030, 95% CI: -0.050 to 0.110).
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that different surgeries can independently affect postoperative serum lipids in PTC patients. Patients who underwent TT had worse lipid changes than TL. These changes indicate an increased risk for cardiovascular outcomes among patients with TT, which calls for more postoperative monitoring.

Title: Association between age and in-hospital mortality and arch repair strategy in acute type A aortic dissection: a dose-response analysis of a retrospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced age is a recognized risk factor in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but its dose-response relationship with in-hospital mortality and the optimal extent of arch repair in elderly patients remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. The association between age (as a continuous variable) and in-hospital mortality was assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis. In a subgroup of elderly patients (≥60 years, n=115), perioperative outcomes between no/partial arch replacement and total arch replacement were compared after 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Among 1,042 included patients, overall in-hospital mortality was 3.7% (39/1,042), and median age was 51 (interquartile range, 40-59) years. Age was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.04 per year, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.07, P=0.01), and RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear association without evidence of a threshold effect (P overall =0.02; P for non-linearity =0.31). In the elderly subgroup (n=244), 115 patients met imaging eligibility criteria for PSM, yielding 30 matched pairs. In this small matched cohort, total arch replacement was associated with longer cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, with no statistically significant differences in mortality (6.7% vs. 3.3%) or major complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Age shows a continuous linear association with in-hospital mortality after ATAAD repair, without evidence of a threshold effect. In elderly patients, total arch replacement and limited arch repair showed no statistically significant differences in early outcomes in this small matched cohort, suggesting that operative strategy should be individualized based on anatomical and physiological risk rather than age alone-a finding that warrants validation in larger studies.

Title: The ligament of Marshall as a therapeutic target in atrial fibrillation: from anatomy to catheter-based and surgical management-a narrative review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Long regarded as an inconsequential embryological remnant, the ligament of Marshall (LOM) is now recognized as a treatable component of the atrial fibrillation (AF) substrate. This review synthesizes the anatomical, electrophysiological and clinical evidence behind that shift and compares the two routes to the LOM: percutaneous retrograde ethanol infusion into the vein of Marshall (EIVOM) during catheter ablation, and direct division during thoracoscopic surgery. Both act on the same epicardial structure; only the route of access differs.
METHODS: A structured literature search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science covered the embryology, anatomy, histology and electrophysiology of the LOM and clinical studies of both routes. Two authors screened and selected records independently. Given the heterogeneity of study designs, findings were synthesized narratively.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: The LOM is a neuro-muscular remnant of the embryonic left superior vena cava that contributes to AF through three mechanisms: triggers arising from insulated myocardial "Marshall bundles", autonomic modulation via adjacent ganglionated plexi, and preferential conduction across the mitral isthmus. Five randomized trials of EIVOM-based strategies have enrolled more than 1,100 patients; pooled analysis shows improved 12-month freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (risk ratio 1.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.04-1.29; number needed to treat 10) and less repeat ablation, without excess major complications (2.5% vs. 2.8%) but with more overall complications and longer fluoroscopy. Crucially, no trial has tested ethanol infusion in isolation; the observed benefit reflects composite lesion sets. Thoracoscopic division interrupts the entire ligament independent of venous anatomy but has never been a randomized variable; randomized evidence for thoracoscopic and hybrid strategies overall ranges from neutral (CASA-AF) to positive (CONVERGE, HARTCAP-AF). Guidelines recognize both as options in selected patients without mandating routine LOM division.
CONCLUSIONS: The LOM is a reproducible, anatomically defined target reachable percutaneously or by surgical division within a comprehensive AF ablation strategy. The supporting evidence is markedly asymmetric: randomized data exist for EIVOM-based strategies but never for ethanol infusion alone, none at all for surgical division, and the two routes have never been compared head-to-head. Its incremental benefit beyond pulmonary vein and posterior wall isolation remains undefined.

Title: Post-operative multi-organ dysfunction following heart transplantation and left ventricular assist device implantation: phenotypes, trajectories, and prognostic implications-a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multi-organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is a leading cause of mortality after heart transplantation (HTx) and left ventricular assist device (LVAD), yet its phenotypic heterogeneity remains poorly characterised. This study intends to identify and clinically validate distinct multi-organ dysfunction phenotypes following HTx and LVAD implantation, and to analyse their early prognosis using longitudinal biomarker trajectories and independent clinical adjudication.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 68 consecutive adult patients who underwent HTx or LVAD implantation in the Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery Department of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, between January 2020 and June 2025. The Institutional Review Board of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology approved this with a waiver of informed consent. We collected demographic, preoperative, and operative data from medical records. Postoperative MODS was defined by Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) criteria as dysfunction with ≥2 organ systems. Patients were followed up for inpatient, 1-, and 2-year mortality.
RESULTS: MODS occurred in 48 of 68 patients (70.6%). It was more frequent after HTx than LVAD (77.6% vs. 52.6%, P=0.08). The most common organ dysfunctions were cardiovascular (70.6%), hepatic (60.3%), and respiratory (50.0%). Patients with MODS had significantly longer cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) duration than those without MODS (183.11±57.42 vs. 138.28±29.83 min; P=0.003) and higher rates of respiratory (68.8% vs. 5.0%; P<0.001), cardiovascular (83.3% vs. 40.0%; P=0.001), and renal dysfunction (50.0% vs. 5.0%; P=0.001). After adjustment, MODS was independently associated with 2-year mortality [hazard ratio (HR) =5.47, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-27.9; P=0.04]. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified 2 MODS phenotypes: a high-severity/multi-system phenotype with high probabilities of renal (100%), hepatic (78%), and respiratory (72%) dysfunction, and a lower-severity/selective phenotype. The high-severity phenotype had significantly worse 2-year survival than the lower-severity phenotype (44.8% vs. 74.4%; log-rank P=0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: With regard to post-cardiac surgery MODS, we report a novel trajectory-based approach that holds promise for improving early risk stratification and guiding targeted management by distinguishing high-severity multisystem from low-severity selective trajectories following HTx and LVAD implantation.

Title: Delayed recognition of primary thyroid lymphoma with progressive thyroid enlargement and cardiopulmonary symptoms.
Abstract: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare thyroid malignancy that may present with respiratory symptoms overlapping with cardiopulmonary disease, contributing to delayed diagnosis. We report a 78-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, and prior lung cancer whose worsening dyspnea was repeatedly attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary conditions. She subsequently developed dysphonia and dysphagia with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass requiring tracheostomy for airway protection. Prior computed tomography imaging obtained during multiple evaluations for cardiopulmonary symptoms incidentally demonstrated subtle thyroid enlargement with progressive interval growth on retrospective review. Core biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and staging established stage IIIE disease. Given her age and comorbidities, a dose-reduced regimen of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was initiated. Despite treatment, her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly thereafter. This case underscores how overlapping comorbidities can obscure PTL presentation until advanced airway compromise develops. In patients with persistent respiratory symptoms despite appropriate cardiopulmonary management, careful review of prior imaging is critical because subtle thyroid enlargement may otherwise be overlooked.

Title: Altered gut microbiota composition in adults with chronic subdural hematoma: a case-control study.
Journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is increasingly recognized as a dynamic inflammatory and angiogenic disorder, but whether it is associated with alterations in the gut microbiota remains unclear. We therefore characterized the gut microbial profiles of adults with CSDH and healthy controls (HCs).
METHODS: We conducted an observational case-control study of 40 adults with CSDH and 96 HCs. Fecal bacterial communities were profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. We assessed alpha and beta diversity, identified differentially abundant genera using covariate-adjusted centered log-ratio models with false-discovery-rate correction, evaluated genus-level discrimination using a random forest classifier with repeated nested cross-validation, and examined associations with clinical characteristics using partial Spearman correlations.
RESULTS: There was no clear evidence of an alpha-diversity difference after covariate adjustment. Community structure differed across Bray-Curtis, weighted UniFrac, and unweighted UniFrac distances (all P = 0.001), with the largest explained variance for weighted UniFrac (R² = 0.106). Thirteen genera remained significant after adjustment and multiple-testing correction, including sensitivity analyses that additionally accounted for diabetes and recorded medication exposure. Collinsella and Dorea were more abundant in CSDH, whereas Bacteroides was more abundant in HCs. Across 10 repeated outer cross-validation partitions, the mean out-of-fold area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve was 0.938 ± 0.010; averaging participant-level out-of-fold probabilities yielded an area under the curve of 0.951. Dorea was positively associated with diabetes, and Bacteroides was inversely associated with cerebral infarction after false-discovery-rate correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with CSDH showed differences in gut microbial community structure and genus-level composition, without clear evidence of an alpha-diversity difference. These are exploratory associations in a selected case-control sample. The cross-sectional, single-center design precludes causal inference, and the classifier has not established calibration, external validity or clinical utility.

Title: Development and internal validation of CTA-based radiomics models for differentiating symptomatic from asymptomatic unruptured spontaneous intracranial vertebrobasilar artery dissection.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous intracranial vertebrobasilar artery dissection (sIVBD) has heterogeneous clinical presentations, and conventional clinical and morphologic assessment may not fully characterize lesion heterogeneity. We aimed to develop and internally validate CTA-based radiomics models for differentiating symptomatic from asymptomatic unruptured sIVBD and to evaluate the incremental contribution of radiomics beyond conventional clinical and CTA features.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 173 patients with unruptured sIVBD, comprising 56 symptomatic and 117 asymptomatic patients. Patients were stratified into a development cohort (n = 138) and an independent internal validation cohort (n = 35). Radiomic features were extracted from subtraction CTA images after three-dimensional lesion segmentation. Feature reproducibility was assessed using inter-reader intraclass correlation coefficients. Four models were developed: a conventional CTA model (M1), a clinical plus conventional CTA model (M2), a radiomics XGBoost model (M3), and a combined model integrating M2 predictors with a cross-fitted radiomics probability (M4). Primary development-cohort evaluation used five-times-repeated five-fold stratified nested cross-validation. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, and decision-curve analysis were assessed.
RESULTS: Of 851 radiomic features, 722 (84.8%) met the prespecified reproducibility criterion. In patient-averaged out-of-fold evaluation, AUCs were 0.630 for M1, 0.681 for M2, 0.676 for M3, and 0.723 for M4. Compared with M2, M4 increased AUC by 0.0416 (95% CI, -0.0130 to 0.0962; p = 0.136) and reduced the Brier score by 0.0101 (95% bootstrap CI, -0.0208 to 0.0006). Across 25 outer folds, M4 had the highest mean AUC (0.715) and the lowest between-fold variability. In the independent internal validation cohort, AUCs were 0.814, 0.807, 0.803, and 0.966 for M1 through M4, respectively.
CONCLUSION: A combined model integrating clinical variables, conventional CTA features, and cross-fitted radiomics information showed the best overall performance for differentiating symptomatic from asymptomatic unruptured sIVBD. Radiomics may provide complementary quantitative information beyond conventional assessment.

Title: Neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio and short-term mortality in heart failure: an exploratory association without demonstrated superiority over PNI, NLR, or SII.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammation and greater illness severity are associated with adverse short-term outcomes in heart failure (HF). The neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio (NPNR) combines neutrophil count with the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), a composite derived from serum albumin and lymphocyte count that is influenced by inflammation and acute illness. This study examined the association of NPNR with 28-day and 90-day all-cause mortality in hospitalized patients with HF and assessed its replication in MIMIC-IV.
METHODS: The analysis included 1,885 patients with calculable NPNR from the Zigong Heart Failure Database and 1,150 adult ICU patients with HF from MIMIC-IV. Log2-transformed NPNR was examined using Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and sensitivity analyses, including parsimonious and Firth-penalized Cox models. MIMIC-IV provided an independent clinical setting for assessing the direction of the association.
RESULTS: In Zigong, each doubling of NPNR was associated with higher 28-day mortality (HR 1.728, 95% CI 1.130-2.642, p = 0.012) and 90-day mortality (HR 1.684, 95% CI 1.124-2.524, p = 0.012). However, the expanded models included only 32 and 36 deaths, respectively, and the tertile-based estimates had wide confidence intervals. RCS analyses suggested nonlinearity at both time horizons. NPNR AUCs were 0.727 and 0.717, with no significant superiority over PNI, NLR, or SII in DeLong comparisons. In MIMIC-IV, the continuous association was borderline significant at 28 days (HR 1.112, p = 0.049) and not statistically significant at 90 days (HR 1.081, p = 0.096). Higher NPNR tertiles were associated with greater mortality, while RCS analyses showed no clear nonlinearity.
CONCLUSION: Higher NPNR was associated with short-term all-cause mortality in the Zigong HF cohort, with weaker evidence in the MIMIC-IV ICU cohort. NPNR may be considered an exploratory laboratory-derived marker associated with systemic inflammation and illness severity. It did not demonstrate superior discrimination over PNI, NLR, or SII, and its incremental prognostic value remains uncertain. These findings do not support its routine use as a clinical decision tool.

Title: Effects of respiratory muscle training on respiratory function, functional outcomes, and pulmonary complications in patients with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of respiratory muscle training on respiratory function, functional outcomes, and pulmonary complications in patients with subacute stroke.
METHOD: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to August 12, 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Pooled estimates were calculated using Hartung-Knapp-adjusted random-effects models. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (ROB2). Sensitivity and publication bias were evaluated via leave-one-out and trim-and-fill analyses.
RESULTS: Eleven RCTs (Final analysis sample:737 patients) were included.
