Despite 91% having normal BMI (≤30 kg/m2), DEXA-measured fat mass showed a dose-response gradient across all scores (CAIDE 4.36-6.26); HbA1c revealed a glycemic gradient invisible to self-reported diabetes.ConclusionsIn this high-socioeconomic cohort, the scores were moderately concordant and varied almost solely by cardiovascular components, protective factors being saturated. Whether this reflects uniformly low risk or reduced ability to separate individuals cannot be determined without a cognitive outcome. Complementary biological measurements added stratification, supporting augmented risk-assessment tools to be validated against cognitive endpoints.

Title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
Abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study; Clinical Trial, Phase III; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: The effect of maternal oxygenation on cardiopulmonary haemodynamics during the transition at birth in preterm lambs.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular transition at birth is a period of instability for preterm infants; however, the impact of fetal oxygen (PaO2) levels on this process is unclear. We hypothesized that increasing maternal, and subsequently, fetal oxygenation will increase pulmonary blood flow (PBF) and improve cardiovascular stability at birth.
METHODS: Preterm sheep fetuses (0.9 gestation) were delivered via cesarean section and instrumented to measure carotid pressure and flow, PBF, and cerebral (SctO2) and arterial (SaO2) oxygenation. Ewes were randomized to maternal oxygen supplementation (O2Supp; fetal PaO2 > 20 mmHg, n = 7) or reduction (O2Red; PaO2 < 20 mmHg, n = 8). After reaching target PaO2, lambs underwent immediate cord clamping, with ventilation withheld for 1 min, then maintained for 30 min.
RESULTS: O2Supp increased fetal pH, PaO2, SpO2, SctO2, and PBF (28.5 ± 7.8 vs 4.0 ± 3.2 mL/min/kg), which was maintained during the period between cord clamping and ventilation. Cord clamping increased blood pressure but reduced oxygenation in O2Supp lambs. Ventilation caused marked increases in carotid pressure and flow in O2Red lambs, which were attenuated by prior oxygen supplementation.
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal oxygen supplementation enhances fetal oxygenation and PBF before cord clamping and reduces cardiovascular instability, suggesting potential benefits for improving cardiovascular stability in preterm infants.
IMPACT: The impact of maternal and fetal oxygenation on the cardiovascular transition is not known. We found that maternal oxygen supplementation improves fetal oxygen and increases pulmonary blood flow prior to cord clamping. Maternal oxygen supplementation stabilizes carotid blood pressure and flow during cord clamping and ventilation onset. Our findings suggest that maternal oxygen supplementation may provide cardiovascular stability for preterm infants at birth.

Title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
Abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study; Clinical Trial, Phase II; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Association of pre-stroke blood pressure with functional outcome after stroke. The PRESS study.
Abstract: The aim of this study was to analyze the association between the mean of available outpatient blood pressure (BP) measurements recorded during the 12 months preceding stroke and functional outcome at 90 days in patients with stroke, adjusting for other established prognostic factors. This was a prospective, observational study including consecutive adult patients admitted with acute stroke between October 2022 and October 2023. Pre-stroke outpatient BP data were obtained from the shared electronic medical record system of Catalonia. All available outpatient systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) measurements recorded during the 12 months preceding stroke onset were collected. A total of 187 patients were included. Sixty patients (32.1%) had a poor functional outcome at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≥ 3 (>3 in those with a previous mRS = 3). In unadjusted models, mean pre-stroke outpatient SBP and DBP and the outpatient SBP measurement closest to stroke were associated with poor functional outcome at 90 days. In the multivariate analyses adjusted for age, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, pre-stroke mRS, mean in-hospital SBP or DBP, type of stroke and history of atrial fibrillation, pre-stroke SBP (OR 2.52, 95% CI 1.59-4.01, per 1 SD increase, p < 0.001), and pre-stroke DBP (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.60-4.84, p < 0.001) were associated with a poor outcome. In conclusion, higher mean outpatient BP levels during the year preceding stroke were independently associated with poor functional outcome at 90 days.

Title: [Hypercholesterolemia and lipid profile alterations in Moroccan patients with myocardial infarction: A case-control study].
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia, particularly elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), is a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, including myocardial infarction.
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate lipid profile alterations in Moroccan patients with myocardial infarction.
METHODS: This case-control study included 104 patients hospitalized for myocardial infarction at the Ibn Rochd University Hospital Center (mean age: 59±11 years; range: 30-82 years) and 79 apparently healthy controls recruited at the Pasteur Institute of Casablanca (mean age: 48±8 years; range: 23-57 years). Serum total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), LDL-C, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) were measured using standardized enzymatic methods.
RESULTS: Patients with myocardial infarction exhibited significantly higher levels of TC, TG, and LDL-C compared with controls, with increases of 17.5% (P<0.001), 78.2% (P<0.001), and 27.7% (P<0.001), respectively. In contrast, HDL-C levels were significantly reduced by 22.2% in patients with myocardial infarction (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a strong association between dyslipidemia and myocardial infarction in the Moroccan population, emphasizing the importance of lipid profile monitoring for cardiovascular risk prevention.

Title: Volume status of patients with hyponatremia across the age span - results from a large prospective international study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Hypotonic hyponatremia is the most common electrolyte disorder in hospitalized adults and becomes increasingly prevalent with age. However, age-related differences in volume status and underlying etiologies remain poorly characterized. We aimed to assess the distribution of volume status and etiologies of hypotonic hyponatremia across the adult age span.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of the prospective Hyponatremia Intervention Trial (NCT03557957), including hospitalized adults with chronic moderate-to-severe hypotonic hyponatremia. Patients were stratified into three age groups (<65, 65-79, ≥80 years). Final volume status (hypovolemic, euvolemic, or hypervolemic) was determined at the end of hospitalization based on the complete in-hospital clinical course.
RESULTS: Overall, 1992 patients (F/M 1050/942; median age 73 [63-81] years) were analyzed. Euvolemic hyponatremia (n = 1073) predominated across all age groups and sexes, mainly due to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (SIAD; n = 853). In adjusted analyses, patients aged 65-79 years (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.19-1.88) and ≥80 years (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.14-1.91) had higher odds of SIAD than patients aged <65 years. Volume status distribution differed across age groups (p = 0.007), driven by a higher prevalence of hypervolemic forms in patients aged ≥80 years; however, the association between age category and volume-status phenotype was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after multivariable adjustment. Hypovolemic hyponatremia (n = 613) was most commonly due to gastrointestinal sodium losses in younger patients, whereas diuretics accounted for nearly 50% of cases in those aged ≥80 years. Among patients with hypervolemic hyponatremia (n = 306), heart failure and liver insufficiency were the leading causes, with heart failure increasing and liver insufficiency decreasing across age groups.
CONCLUSION: Euvolemic hyponatremia was the predominant form across all age groups and was mainly due to SIAD, with both older age groups showing higher adjusted odds of SIAD compared with patients aged <65 years. Age-related differences were observed in the distribution of etiologies within hypovolemic and hypervolemic hyponatremia.

Title: Interaction between unhealthy sleep pattern and obesity on cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity and unhealthy sleep are established risk factors for cardiometabolic multimorbidity, but their joint effect remains unclear. This study aims to investigate their joint effect on cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk by analyzing data from 2 independent cohorts.
METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional (Fuqing Cohort, N = 34,703) and prospective data (UK Biobank, N = 362,474; 12.3-year median follow-up, 3980 incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity cases). We defined unhealthy sleep (≥3 of 5 traits: late chronotype, sleep <7 or >8 h/day, frequent insomnia symptoms, self-reported snoring, frequent daytime sleepiness), cardiometabolic multimorbidity (≥2 of type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, stroke), and obesity (general: BMI ≥25 kg/m²; central: waist circumference ≥80 cm in women, ≥94/90 cm in European/Asian men). The reference group had a sleep score <3 and no corresponding obesity. Logistic and Cox regressions evaluated associations and additive interaction was assessed.
RESULTS: Unhealthy sleep and both obesity types independently increased cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk in both populations. The joint effect was stronger for unhealthy sleep combined with central obesity (FQC adjusted OR = 3.46; UKB adjusted HR = 2.55) than general overweight/obesity (FQC adjusted OR = 2.61; UKB adjusted HR = 2.46). Additive interaction showed stronger effect for unhealthy sleep with central versus general overweight/obesity in Europeans (adjusted RERI: 0.61 vs. 0.32). A similar additive interaction in Asians turned non-significant after covariate adjustment. Insomnia and central obesity showed a significant additive interaction in both cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Unhealthy sleep and obesity jointly increase cardiometabolic multimorbidity risk, with central obesity having a stronger additive interaction than general overweight/obesity. Integrated public health strategies targeting sleep and weight are warranted.

Title: Silencing the fire alarm: responding to intraoperative blood pressure targets.
Abstract: A meta-analysis in a recent issue of the British Journal of Anaesthesia pools randomised evidence on intraoperative arterial blood pressure targets in nine trials in noncardiac surgery. With a total of 14 658 patients included in the analysis, the authors show that higher mean arterial pressure targets do not reduce 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, or myocardial injury. These findings reinforce the distinction between low blood pressure as a marker of perioperative vulnerability and low blood pressure as a modifiable therapeutic target. Correcting arterial pressure might normalise a number without removing the underlying physiological vulnerability that drives adverse postoperative outcomes. Therefore, this meta-analysis supports a shift from reflexive increases in blood pressure targets towards attention to the underlying cause of haemodynamic instability.

Title: The effect of evinacumab on the clinical outcomes of dyslipidemia: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk remains substantial despite optimal conventional lipid-lowering therapy, particularly in patients with persistently elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Evinacumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting angiopoietin-like protein 3, represents a novel therapeutic approach that lowers LDL-C, triglycerides, apolipoprotein B (ApoB), apolipoprotein C-III (ApoC-III), and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C).
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of Evinacumab, an ANGPTL3-targeting monoclonal antibody, in patients with dyslipidemia. This review and meta-analysis assesses its effects on lipid parameters, including LDL-C, triglycerides, ApoB, ApoC-III, and non-HDL-C. It also seeks to determine Evinacumab's potential role in reducing residual ASCVD risk across diverse dyslipidemic populations.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Embase, EBSCO, PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, the Cochrane Library, and gray literature sources were searched. Of 1718 identified records, 113 full-text articles were assessed, and 6 studies comprising 9 randomized clinical trials met the predefined eligibility criteria and were included.
RESULTS: Evinacumab demonstrated substantial lipid-lowering efficacy across doses ranging from 5 to 20 mg/kg. LDL-C reductions ranged from approximately 16% to 50% over follow-up periods of 16 to 24 weeks, with consistent efficacy observed in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, including pediatric populations, and in adults with refractory dyslipidemias. Clinically meaningful reductions were also reported for triglycerides, ApoB, ApoC-III, and non-HDL-C. Triglyceride lowering was particularly pronounced in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, supporting its potential role in reducing pancreatitis risk, although responses varied according to the underlying genetic etiology. Evinacumab was generally well tolerated, with no major treatment-related safety concerns. Some studies reported transient anti-drug antibodies, but they did not appear to compromise efficacy or safety.
CONCLUSION: Evinacumab is an effective lipid-lowering therapy that produces clinically meaningful reductions in LDL-C, triglycerides, and apolipoproteins across difficult-to-treat dyslipidemic populations. Its favorable safety profile supports its use in refractory hypercholesterolemia and severe hypertriglyceridemia. Larger randomized trials with longer follow-up and head-to-head comparisons with other emerging lipid-lowering therapies are warranted to further define its long-term clinical role.

Title: Pitfalls of M-mode echocardiography end-diastolic and end-systolic measurements: a study of 154 dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.
Journal: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Echocardiographic assessment of myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) includes measurement of the left ventricular internal dimension at the end-diastole (LVIDd) and at the end-systole (LVIDs), using established cardiac cycle markers. The LVIDd is measured at the QRS onset, which may not coincide with the maximal internal dimension. The LVIDs is obtained at maximum septal contraction, which in dogs with non-synchronous contraction (NSC) between the septal and free wall, may not correspond to the minimal internal dimension. This study investigates alternative measurement methods and their potential impact on MMVD staging.
ANIMALS, MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis of echocardiographic examinations from 154 dogs with MMVD was performed. Twenty-five dogs displayed NSC and were selected for LVIDs assessment. The LVIDd was measured at the onset of the QRS complex (method D1, recommended by the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine [ACVIM]) and at the largest chamber diameter (method D2). In dogs with NSC, the LVIDs was measured using maximum septal contraction point (method S1) and minimum septal-to-free wall distance (method S2).
RESULTS: The LVIDd values were significantly lower with method D1 in 152 dogs (P<0.001). Using method D2, 12 dogs exceeded the the body-weight-normalized LVIDd threshold of 1.7. In NSC dogs, LVIDs values were significantly higher with method S1 (P<0.001).
STUDY LIMITATIONS: Limitations included operator subjectivity and observational NSC.
CONCLUSIONS: The measurement method influences LVIDd and LVIDs values. Although method D2 is not ACVIM- recommended, its application could hypothetically alter staging outcomes, highlighting the effect of measurement timing.

Title: Burden and temporal trends of cardiovascular disease among medical inpatients and age-specific and sex-specific risk of CVD-related hospitalisation at a national referral hospital in Uganda: a retrospective cohort study.
Incremental value of renal, metabolic, and inflammatory markers for prevalent self-reported cardiovascular disease across NHANES cycles: A repeated cross-sectional validation study.
Abstract: Renal dysfunction, metabolic stress, and systemic inflammation are associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD), but their incremental value beyond routine clinical factors is uncertain. This repeated cross-sectional study used 7 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cycles (2005-2018) for development and leave-one-cycle-out validation. The primary outcome was prevalent self-reported CVD. A locked clinical core was extended with estimated glomerular filtration rate plus log2 urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (renal), triglyceride-glucose waist circumference index (TyG-WC; metabolic), systemic inflammation response index (inflammatory), or all markers. Elastic Net was primary and XGBoost secondary. Preprocessing, imputation, and full-grid tuning were confined to training cycles. Survey-aware 95% confidence intervals (CIs) used 2000 Rao-Wu bootstrap replicates. NHANES 2021-2023 underwent a separate temporal assessment, corrected after inspection of initial outputs, using development-trained pipelines without temporal tuning or recalibration. Development examination and fasting samples included 37,482 adults (4222 CVD events) and 15,956 adults (1813 events), respectively. The Elastic Net core area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.8490 (95% CI, 0.8410-0.8560). Renal markers improved AUROC by 0.0046 (0.0031-0.0062) and area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) by 0.0161 (0.0101-0.0223); the combined extension improved AUROC by 0.0072 (0.0039-0.0106). In the corrected 2021-2023 assessment, phlebotomy and fasting samples included 5755 adults (739 events) and 2940 adults (355 events). Core AUROC was 0.8533 (0.8313-0.8753). Renal incremental AUROC was 0.0041 (0.0001-0.0081) and PR-AUC was 0.0217 (0.0093-0.0310); combined incremental AUROC was 0.0074 (0.0016-0.0124). TyG-WC alone showed no clear increment. XGBoost gains were less consistent across cycles and temporal metrics. Renal and combined extensions showed modest, algorithm-dependent gains in classifying prevalent self-reported CVD. The corrected temporal assessment provided supportive evidence for Elastic Net. These findings describe cross-sectional association patterns; prospective studies with adjudicated outcomes and defined clinical decisions are needed to evaluate clinical utility.

Title: Association between triglyceride-glucose body mass index and future risk of arthritis in individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: A national prospective cohort study.
Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome encompasses interrelated cardiovascular, renal and metabolic disorders. Arthritis is linked to CKM multimorbidity, but the association between triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI), a surrogate marker of insulin resistance and incident arthritis across the CKM spectrum remains unclear. We analyzed data from the CHARLS cohort, including 5018 participants aged ≥45 years with CKM stages 0 to 3. Analytical approaches included multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, stratified and mediation analyses. Incident arthritis was defined by self-reported physician diagnosis, without confirmation via medical records. During follow-up, 2307 participants (45.97%) developed incident arthritis. Each one-standard-deviation increase in triglyceride-glucose body mass index (triglyceride-glucose body mass index) was associated with an 11% higher risk of arthritis (odds ratio [OR] = 1.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.04-1.19), with an approximately linear positive dose-response trend. The association appeared stronger in participants with sleep duration <7 hours (OR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.08-1.31) and those at CKM stage 1 (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.20-2.05). Exploratory mediation analyses suggested negative mediating roles of HDL-C and, marginally, BUN. Triglyceride-glucose body mass index exhibited an independent positive association with incident arthritis across CKM stages 0 to 3 and may serve as a practical indicator for early risk stratification.

Title: Association of SII and SIRI with anxiety and depression severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that inflammatory mechanisms may play a key role in linking psychological disorders to cardiovascular outcomes. This study aimed to explore the association between anxiety and depression levels and two inflammatory markers, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 1498 patients with ACS who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) in Rasht, Iran, between January 2022 and June 2023. SII and SIRI were calculated for all patients. Patients' psychological status regarding anxiety and depression was evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). All data analyses were conducted using SPSS version 22. The mean age of the patients was 58.49 ± 11.14 years, with males comprising 57.5% of the sample. Male participants exhibited significantly higher levels of anxiety and depression compared to females (P < .05). Individuals with comorbidities showed significantly lower anxiety scores (P < .05). Anxiety levels varied significantly based on CAG findings (P = .004). In multivariable ordinal logistic regression analyses, neither SII nor SIRI was significantly associated with depression severity (SII: OR = 1.029, 95% CI: 0.70-1.49; SIRI: OR = 1.012, 95% CI: 0.86-1.03) or anxiety severity (SII: OR = 0.906, 95% CI: 0.63-1.29; SIRI: OR = 1.005, 95% CI: 0.98-1.03). Systemic inflammation indices (SII and SIRI) did not show significant associations with anxiety or depression severity in cardiac patients, highlighting their limited utility as psychological predictors.

Title: Association between dietary thiamine intake and serum lipid profiles in U.S. adults: NHANES 2021-2023.
Abstract: Thiamine (vitamin B1) is an essential water-soluble vitamin involved in carbohydrate metabolism and energy production. Emerging evidence suggests that thiamin may influence lipid metabolism and cardiovascular risk, yet population-based data are limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to investigate the association between dietary thiamin intake and serum lipid profiles, including total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, and triglycerides, among U.S. adults. Data from 4986 fasting adults aged ≥ 18 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2021 to 2023 were analyzed. Dietary thiamin intake was assessed using the first 24-hour dietary recall and classified into four intake categories based on the distribution of thiamin intake. Linear regression models were used to examine the associations between dietary thiamin intake and serum lipid components, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, dietary, and health-related factors. A sensitivity analysis was additionally performed, adjusting for lipid-lowering medication use. In fully adjusted models, higher thiamin intake was associated with lower total cholesterol (β = -7.13, SE = 2.61, P = .007) and LDL-C (β = -6.72, SE = 3.27, P = .04). No significant associations were observed with HDL-C (β = -0.21, SE = 0.80, P = .79) or triglycerides (β = 13.82, SE = 10.37, P = .183). In the sensitivity analysis additionally adjusted for lipid-lowering medication use, the associations with total cholesterol and LDL-C remained significant, while those with HDL-C and triglycerides remained nonsignificant. These findings indicate an inverse association between dietary thiamin intake and selected atherogenic lipid fractions. Among U.S. adults, higher dietary thiamin intake is associated with lower total and LDL cholesterol levels. Higher thiamin intake may be associated with a more favorable lipid profile and may represent a potential dietary factor relevant to cardiovascular risk management. Given the cross-sectional design, causal relationships cannot be inferred, and further prospective and interventional studies are warranted to confirm these findings and elucidate underlying mechanisms.

Title: Central nervous system hemorrhage related to protein kinase inhibitors: A real-world pharmacovigilance case-control study and genetic correlation study.
Abstract: Despite the widespread clinical use of protein kinase inhibitors in oncology, evidence regarding their potential to induce central nervous system (CNS) hemorrhage remains limited. This study aims to investigate the occurrence and risk signals of CNS hemorrhagic events associated with different PKI subclasses, identify the most affected patient populations, and examine variations in risk profiles across demographic subgroups. We conducted disproportionality analyses using data from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System to detect CNS hemorrhage signals linked to 14 PKI classes. Subgroup analyses stratified by age, sex, and body weight were performed to explore differential risk patterns. Furthermore, Mendelian Randomization and genetic correlation analyses were utilized to evaluate potential causal relationships between PKI therapeutic indications and CNS hemorrhages. We analyzed 9215 CNS hemorrhage reports linked to 14 PKI classes. We identified 6 CNS hemorrhage related signal of disproportionate reporting significantly associated with PKI use. Both BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors and BTK inhibitors showed consistent positive signals across all 6 signal of disproportionate reportings, with BTK inhibitors presenting analysis the highest risks (e.g., cerebral hemorrhage reporting odds ratio = 3.30 [3.00-3.62], subdural hematoma reporting odds ratio = 5.90 [5.28-6.60]). Mendelian Randomization revealed no causal genetic relationship between PKI indications and CNS hemorrhage, suggesting the hemorrhagic risks are likely attributable to the drugs themselves rather than underlying diseases. Significant disproportionality signals of PKI-related CNS hemorrhage were identified, while causal links between indications and adverse events were excluded. These findings enhance understanding of PKI-associated bleeding risks and support early detection, targeted monitoring, and informed clinical decision-making.

Title: Association between early central venous pressure monitoring and 30-day mortality in critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: Central venous pressure (CVP) is widely used in the intensive care unit (ICU), but the optimal timing to initiate CVP monitoring remains unclear for patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis. We explored the association between time to initial CVP measurement and 30-day mortality in this high-risk population. This retrospective cohort study included 9246 critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis from the MIMIC-IV database. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis examined the relationship between time to initial CVP measurement and 30-day mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting followed by weighted logistic regression was used to assess the association between early CVP monitoring (≤6 hours after ICU admission) and 30-day mortality. A nonlinear J-shaped association emerged, with the lowest risk at 2.89 hours post-admission. Early CVP monitoring was associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR = 0.816, 95% CI: 0.688-0.967, P = .019). A landmark sensitivity analysis comparing no monitoring, early (≤6 hours), intermediate (6-86 hours), and late (>86 hours) monitoring showed a time-dependent relationship: intermediate (OR = 1.396, 95% CI: 1.194-1.632, P < .001) and late monitoring (OR = 3.141, 95% CI: 2.263-4.359, P < .001) were associated with progressively higher mortality. In critically ill patients with comorbid heart failure and sepsis, early CVP monitoring within 6 hours of ICU admission was associated with lower 30-day mortality, while delayed monitoring carried an elevated risk. Early integration of CVP within a multimodal hemodynamic assessment framework may be a prudent approach in this high-risk population.

Title: Joint associations of estimated glucose disposal rate and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with metabolic syndrome in Korean adults: A cross-sectional study.
Abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS), an important metabolic risk phenotype within the broader cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework, is characterized by insulin resistance and chronic low-grade inflammation; however, evidence regarding the joint relationship of these 2 biological dimensions with MetS remains limited. We analyzed cross-sectional data from 20,781 Korean adults aged ≥ 19 years who were enrolled in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) 2015-2018. MetS was classified using the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III framework with waist circumference thresholds adapted for the Korean/Asian populations. Weighted logistic regression was performed to examine the relationships between estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and MetS. Potential dose-response patterns were further explored using restricted cubic splines. Joint analyses, interaction analysis, and prespecified subgroup analyses were also performed. MetS was present in 29.4% of participants after weighting. In the fully adjusted model, higher eGDR was associated with lower odds of MetS per unit (OR 0.48, 95% CI: 0.47-0.49), whereas log-transformed hs-CRP showed a positive association with MetS, with higher levels corresponding to greater odds (OR 1.71, 95% CI: 1.64-1.79; both P < .001). Dose-response analyses revealed a decreasing pattern for eGDR and an increasing pattern for hs-CRP in relation to MetS. In joint analyses, progressively higher odds of MetS were observed across exposure categories, with the low-eGDR/high-hs-CRP profile corresponding to the greatest odds of MetS. No significant multiplicative interaction was detected (P for interaction = .064). The association of the joint high-risk profile with MetS was generally consistent across subgroups and appeared stronger among younger participants and those without diabetes. Lower eGDR and higher hs-CRP levels were independently associated with MetS in Korean adults, and the low-eGDR/high-hs-CRP profile was associated with the highest odds of MetS. Their joint assessment may provide complementary information for characterizing adverse metabolic profiles within the broader CKM framework, although prospective studies are needed to determine its predictive value.

Title: Comparison of anticoagulation efficacy and safety of different heparin dosages in cardiogenic shock patients supported by intra-aortic balloon pump: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: The study aimed to evaluate whether a half-dose heparin flush strategy during intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support improves safety compared with the standard-dose strategy in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 128 CS patients who received IABP support between January 2023 and December 2024 were included. Sixty-eight patients received a standard-dose heparin flush, and 60 received a half-dose flush. The primary endpoints were clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 2, 3, or 5) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100 × 109/L). Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, adjusting for dual antiplatelet therapy and renal dysfunction. The incidence of clinically significant bleeding events and thrombocytopenia was significantly lower in the half-dose group than in the standard-dose group (P < .05). Compared with the standard-dose group, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was significantly associated with a lower risk of clinically significant bleeding (odds ratio = 0.15; 95% confidence interval = 0.03-0.68). Among the secondary outcomes, the half-dose group had a significantly lower transfusion requirement than the standard-dose group (P < .001). No significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in activated partial thromboplastin time, activated clotting time, in-hospital mortality, or catheter-related occlusion events. In patients with CS receiving IABP support, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was associated with lower incidences of thrombocytopenia, clinical bleeding, and transfusion requirements. No device-related thrombotic events were observed in either group, suggesting that the half-dose heparin flush strategy may contribute to optimizing anticoagulation management during the peri-support period.

Title: Association between pre-stroke anemia and risk of acute kidney injury following ischemic stroke: A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: Although anemia is an established risk factor for acute kidney injury (AKI), its specific impact on post-stroke AKI remains inadequately explored. This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-stroke anemia and the risk of developing AKI after acute ischemic stroke. This retrospective study, using the TriNetX research network database, identified adult patients who experienced their 1st recorded ischemic stroke between January 2010 and December 2023. Patients were categorized based on hemoglobin levels within 3 months pre-stroke: anemia (hemoglobin ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL) versus control (hemoglobin ≥12.0 g/dL). After 1:1 propensity score matching, we analyzed the outcomes at 1-year follow-up. The primary endpoint was the development of AKI during the follow-up period. Secondary endpoints comprised all-cause mortality, pneumonia, and intensive care unit admission. After propensity score matching, 61,896 patients were included in each cohort. Patients with pre-stroke anemia had a significantly higher 1-year risk of AKI (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.83-1.96), mortality (HR: 1.86, 95% CI: 1.80-1.93), pneumonia (HR: 1.76, 95% CI: 1.69-1.84), and intensive care unit admission (HR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.55-1.65) compared to controls (all P < .001). A graded association was observed between increasing anemia severity and adverse outcomes. The findings remained robust across sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Pre-stroke anemia is associated with an increased risk of post-stroke AKI and other adverse outcomes. However, given the observational nature of this study, future prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Association of the triglyceride glucose-waist circumference index with hypertension among US adults: A cross-sectional study from NHANES.
Abstract: The triglyceride glucose-weight-adjusted waist index (TyG-WWI), integrating glycolipid metabolism and central obesity, may offer a novel approach to identifying metabolic dysregulation linked to hypertension, yet its association with hypertension among general adults remains inadequately characterized. In this cross-sectional analysis of 2716 adults (aged ≥ 20 years) from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2015 to 2018, hypertension was defined by self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and exploratory mediation analyses were applied, accounting for the complex survey design with fasting subsample weights. Of 2716 participants, 890 (32.8%) had hypertension. After full adjustment, each unit increase in TyG-WWI was associated with a 2% increase in the odds of hypertension (OR = 1.02, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.03, P < .001). A nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed (P for nonlinearity < .05), with risk accelerating at higher TyG-WWI levels; participants in the highest quartile had 72% higher odds than those in the lowest quartile (OR = 1.72, 95% confidence interval: 1.21-2.46; P for trend < .001). Subgroup analyses showed stronger associations in females and in normal-weight individuals. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that body mass index and uric acid may account for 30.49% and 7.95% of the association, respectively; these estimates are descriptive and should not be interpreted as evidence of biological mediation. Higher TyG-WWI was independently associated with a higher prevalence of self-reported hypertension among United States adults across all body mass index categories. These findings support TyG-WWI as a promising composite marker for hypertension risk stratification; the exploratory mediation estimates warrant confirmation in prospective studies.

Title: Towards Contact-Free Cardiac Magnetic Resonance: Feasibility of Remote Photoplethysmography for Cardiac Triggering and Gating.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences necessitate synchronisation with the cardiac cycle. This is routinely obtained through electrocardiographic (ECG) detection of the R-wave with subsequent triggering or gating of the acquisition, depending on the type of sequence. An accepted alternative is the use of transmissive photoplethysmography using a fingerclip (fPPG) to detect the peripheral pulse wave.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of contact-free remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) for CMR triggering/gating.
METHODS: In this prospective study (www.drks.de, DRKS00036686), CMR sequences were triggered/gated by ECG, fPPG and rPPG. The primary endpoint was trigger accuracy, measured by true positive rate (TPR), positive predictive value (PPV), beat detection error rate (BDER) and trigger-latency variability (TLV) in the rPPG and fPPG tracings compared to the ECG tracing. Secondary endpoints were technical success, image quality and quantitative CMR measurements of the acquired CMR sequences. Subsequently, the rPPG algorithm was adjusted to improve pulse wave detection in patients with skin type Fitzpatrick 5-6.
RESULTS: 64 subjects were included. rPPG initially provided comparable measures of trigger accuracy to fPPG, with worse performance in subjects with skin type Fitzpatrick 5-6. Adjusting the rPPG algorithm significantly improved trigger accuracy irrespective of skin type: BDER (%) for fPPG 8.5 (0.9-23.0), for rPPG 7.2 (0.3-49.1) and for the adjusted rPPG 1.3 (0.2-11.2). Image quality with both fPPG and rPPG were comparable to ECG. The differences observed in quantitative CMR measurements between fPPG, rPPG and ECG were in the order of inter-observer-variability.
CONCLUSIONS: Contact-free rPPG is a viable alternative to standard CMR triggering/gating using ECG or fPPG. Adjustment of our algorithm led to excellent trigger accuracy irrespective of skin type.

Title: A randomized trial to reduce heart disease risk among Yup'ik Alaska native people: the DAiLY study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart disease (HD) is a leading cause of mortality among Yup'ik Alaska Native people, whose prevalence of HD exceeds that of the U.S. population overall. Transition away from traditional subsistence foods and lifestyles toward processed market-food diets and reduced physical activity have contributed to increasing cardiometabolic risk. The Diet and Active Lifestyle-Yuuyaraq (DAiLY) Study was developed in partnership with Yup'ik communities to promote heart health through culturally grounded strategies that support traditional foods, healthy market food choices, and active lifestyles.
METHODS: DAiLY is a community-based, cluster-randomized trial conducted in four Yup'ik communities in southwest Alaska. Communities were randomized to immediate or delayed intervention conditions. The multilevel intervention integrates home-based workshops, a food store component, community-wide events, and community media messaging, guided by the Warnecke Transdisciplinary Model and community-based participatory research principles. Adults aged ≥18 years who self-identify as Yup'ik are eligible to participate in outcome assessments. The primary outcome is a change in continuous metabolic syndrome (cMS) score, a validated composite indicator of cardiometabolic risk. Secondary outcomes include self-reported dietary intake, physical activity, psychosocial measures, and stable isotope biomarkers of subsistence and market food intake. Process evaluation will assess reach, dose, fidelity, engagement, and implementation context.
DISCUSSION: DAiLY is the first multicomponent, multilevel intervention designed to reduce cardiometabolic risk among Yup'ik Alaska Native communities by integrating Indigenous knowledge, subsistence food practices, and community-driven health promotion strategies. Findings will inform culturally grounded approaches to cardiovascular disease prevention in Indigenous and other rural populations undergoing nutrition and lifestyle transitions.

Title: Association of pre-existing sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy with outcomes in cardiogenic shock: a multicentre cohort study.
Sudden Death in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Pooled Analysis of Five Randomized Trials.
Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF.
RESULTS: Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms.
CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

Title: Recommendations for the Examination, Processing, and Reporting of Non-neoplastic Pericardial Diseases: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
Journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Recent advances in the evaluation and management of pericardial diseases highlight the importance of accurate pathologic assessment. Despite these current developments, the handling, processing, and reporting of pericardial specimens have not been formally addressed in recent years. This consensus document is intended to enable the pathologist to evaluate the pericardium as a surgical specimen as well as at postmortem examination, with particular emphasis on standardized gross and microscopic assessment of the pericardium.
METHODS AND RESULTS: An international expert panel comprising volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology was convened to develop consensus recommendations. Strong agreement on best practices was achieved through a series of in-person and hybrid virtual meetings. The document outlines recommendations for the handling and processing of surgical pericardial specimens, including appropriate histochemical and immunohistochemical stains and ancillary diagnostic studies. Guidance for the systematic examination of the pericardium at autopsy is also provided. In addition, a nomenclature for common and well-defined pathologic processes is proposed, together with relevant differential diagnoses. The recommended terminology encompasses the predominant inflammatory cell infiltrates and the spectrum of organization from fibrinous pericarditis to established pericardial fibrosis.
CONCLUSION: This consensus document provides a standardized framework for the pathologic evaluation of the pericardium with the goal of improving diagnostic consistency, facilitating communication among clinicians and pathologists, and promoting uniformity in clinical practice and research.

Title: Pathology of the Parietal Pericardium: A Consensus Statement on Pericardial Disease from the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology.
Journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Pericardial diseases encompass a broad spectrum of infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, traumatic, iatrogenic, and neoplastic disorders occurring in the setting of both localized and systemic conditions. Advances in understanding of the pathogenesis and diagnosis of pericardial disease have been substantial. Despite extensive literature on the clinical aspects of pericardial disease, relatively few studies have focused on its pathologic features.
METHODS AND RESULTS: An international panel from volunteer members of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology conducted a comprehensive review of the literature to develop a consensus document on the recommendations for pathologic evaluation of the parietal pericardium. This first document summarizes our state-of-the-art understanding of the etiological and morphological aspects of pericardial diseases, including pericardial effusions, cardiac tamponade, infectious and non-infectious pericarditis, and constrictive pericarditis, and incorporates updated clinical definitions and diagnostic criteria.
CONCLUSION: This consensus review highlights the role of pathology in the diagnosis of pericardial disease. Future efforts should explore establishing contemporary reference ranges for normal pericardial fluid volume, refining the pathologic characterization of pericarditis, correlating histopathologic findings with advanced cardiac imaging, and elucidating the molecular mechanisms driving the progression of pericardial fibrosis to constrictive disease.

Title: Baseline circulating thrombospondin-1 is associated with recurrence after catheter ablation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation remains common in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), and clinically accessible biomarkers for pre-procedural risk stratification are limited. Thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1) is a circulating matricellular protein implicated in inflammatory and profibrotic pathways.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 211 patients with paroxysmal AF undergoing first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation. Baseline circulating TSP-1 was measured before ablation and analysed primarily as a continuous (log-transformed) variable, with a pre-specified 75th-percentile threshold used for exploratory subgroups. The primary endpoint was AF recurrence after a 3-month blanking period. Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, time-dependent discrimination with bootstrap optimism correction, and propensity score matching (sensitivity analysis) were performed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 700 days, 61 patients (28.9%) experienced AF recurrence. Higher baseline TSP-1 was independently associated with recurrence in the full cohort (adjusted HR per 1-SD of log-TSP-1, 1.54; 95% CI 1.26-1.88; p < 0.001) and persisted after propensity score matching (HR 4.73; 95% CI 2.18-10.29). Adding TSP-1 improved time-dependent discrimination at 700 days (AUC 0.62 to 0.70; optimism-corrected 0.66; Harrell's C 0.627 to 0.705), although reclassification metrics were mixed and the incremental value was exploratory.
CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline circulating TSP-1 was associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence after first-time radiofrequency catheter ablation in patients with paroxysmal AF. These findings support further evaluation of TSP-1 as a candidate biomarker for pre-procedural risk stratification.

Title: Antiplatelet pretreatment in acute coronary syndromes: Bridging the gap between guideline recommendations and clinical practice.
Cardiovascular risk stratification in patients undergoing liposomal anthracycline: Association with cardiovascular outcomes and overall survival.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and cardiovascular disease are frequently treated with regimens incorporating non-PEGylated liposomal anthracycline to mitigate cardiotoxicity while preserving antitumor efficacy. However, considering their unique pharmacokinetics, validation of a cardiovascular risk stratification tool for these patients is much needed.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with newly diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphoma treated with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, non-PEGylated liposomal doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-COMP) between 2014 and 2025. Baseline demographics, cardiovascular history and medications, echocardiographic and laboratory parameters were recorded. Patients were stratified into risk categories according to the Heart Failure Association International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) score. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS) and incidence of cardiovascular events defined as asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, new-onset or worsening heart failure and acute coronary syndrome.
RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 265 patients [median age 73 years (69-77); 51% males]; 41% were classified as moderate risk, 55% as high risk, and 4% as very high risk. During a median follow-up of 29 months, 38 patients (14%) died. OS and cardiovascular events occurrence significantly differed across the three HFA-ICOS risk categories; in particular, very high-risk patients exhibited substantially higher hazards of mortality (HR 5.8) and cardiovascular events (HR 40.4). Cardioprotective therapy at baseline appears not influence cardiovascular outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: The HFA-ICOS score effectively stratifies mortality and risk of cardiovascular events among patients treated with R-COMP. Despite the limited number of very-high risk patients and the heterogenous, non-randomized cardioprotective strategies at baseline, our findings may provide evidence supporting its integration into practice.

Title: Transfer of prehospital defibrillator recordings to receiving hospitals after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a 16-year retrospective study in Paris.
Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM.
METHODS: We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

Title: Left Subclavian Artery Revascularization and Early Neurological Outcomes After Zone 2 TEVAR.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: LSA revascularization is generally favored when intentional LSA coverage is planned during elective zone 2 TEVAR, whereas in urgent settings the decision is individualized according to anatomy, ischemic risk, and clinical urgency. This study evaluated the association between preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization and early neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 32 patients who underwent zone 2 TEVAR with intentional LSA coverage between January 2018 and December 2024. Patients were classified according to whether LSA revascularization was performed before or concomitantly with TEVAR (Rev+, n=21) or not (Rev-, n=11). The primary endpoint was any 30 day neurological complication, including ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), and spinal cord ischemia (SCI). Major neurological events, defined as stroke or SCI, were additionally evaluated.
RESULTS: Early neurological complications occurred in 4/21 patients (19.0%) in the Rev+ group and 3/11 (27.3%) in the Rev- group (p=.667), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of -8.2 percentage points (95% CI, -39.4 to 23.0) and a risk ratio of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.19-2.58). Major neurological events occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) and 2/11 (18.2%) patients, respectively (p=1.000). Stroke occurred in 3/21 (14.3%) Rev+ patients and 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients, while SCI occurred in no Rev+ patients and in 1/11 (9.1%) Rev- patients. LSA revascularization was not significantly associated with the primary endpoint (OR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.12-3.34; p=.582). Results remained similar after separate adjustment for age, dissection, urgency, coronary artery disease, and chronic kidney disease. Sensitivity analyses using major neurological events as the endpoint and including postoperative LSA revascularization in the exposure definition also yielded similar results.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative or concomitant LSA revascularization during zone 2 TEVAR was associated with a numerically lower rate of early neurological complications, although the difference was not statistically significant. Larger studies are needed to better define the association between LSA revascularization and neurological outcomes after zone 2 TEVAR.

Title: VOLUME ADJUSTED CALCIUM ANALYSIS OF AORTOILIAC ATHEROSCLEROSIS AS A PREDICTOR OF AMPUTATION FREE SURVIVAL.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes.
METHODS: This single-institution retrospective study included 187 patients over nine years who underwent peripheral vascular intervention. Using TeraRecon, calcium and patent lumen volumes were quantified along a contiguous aorto-iliac segment totaling 10 cm generating a VACS. An intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessed inter-rater reliability. Patients were stratified into two groups. Primary outcomes were death at one year and amputation-free survival. Secondary outcomes were re-interventions and number of arteries treated.
RESULTS: Intervention type did not differ between the two groups. Patients with higher VACS were more likely older, have CHF, COPD, or hypertension. Patient in the higher VACS group had greater number of arteries treated, subsequent vascular interventions, and one-year all-cause mortality. A Cox-regression model demonstrated a VACSgreater than 0.33 was independently associated with decreased amputation-free survival at one year (HR 2.24, p=0.019).
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing intervention for aortoiliac occlusive disease, higher VACS was independently associated with worse one-year amputation free survival. Incorporating patent lumen volume into VACS appears to capture a systemic atherosclerotic burden not fully reflected by traditional lesion-specific assessments.

Title: Prevalence of concomitant aneurysms in patients with thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms who underwent Fenestrated/Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair (F-BEVAR).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of synchronous ascending aortic and peripheral arterial aneurysms in patients with Crawford extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) undergoing fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (F/BEVAR).
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective review of prospectively collected data from patients with Crawford extent I-IV TAAA treated with F/BEVAR under a physician-sponsored investigational device exemption. The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction. Bilateral popliteal artery (PA) diameters were obtained from preoperative arterial duplex imaging. An aneurysm was defined as a vessel diameter >50% greater than the expected normal diameter for that arterial bed, using references available from literature. Multivariable logistic regression included sex, obesity, race/ethnicity, TAAA diameter ≥7 cm, and prior aortic dissection. A sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding patients with prior aortic dissection.
RESULTS: Among 249 patients (mean age, 70.8±8.6 years; 40.2% women), 177 (71.1%) had at least one concomitant aneurysm. Race/ethnicity was 75.1% NH-White, 21.7% NH-Black, 0.8% Hispanic, and 2.4% Other. Among evaluable patients, aneurysm prevalence was 12.0% in the ascending aorta (29/242), 62.8% in the CIA (140/223), 42.1% in the HA (98/233), 22.2% in the PA (51/230), and 9.6% in the CFA (22/228). On multivariable analysis, CIA aneurysm was associated with obesity, non-White race/ethnicity, and TAAA diameter ≥7 cm; HA aneurysm with male sex, obesity, and prior dissection; CFA aneurysm with male sex; PA aneurysm with male sex and prior dissection; and ascending aortic aneurysm with TAAA diameter ≥7 cm and prior dissection. After exclusion of 46 patients with prior dissection, concomitant aneurysms remained a common occurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant aneurysms are common in patients undergoing F/BEVAR for Crawford extent I-IV TAAA. Several associations remained significant after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be interpreted in the context of a single-center referral population, variable arterial-bed denominators, possible diffuse arteriomegaly, and residual confounding. The prevalence of PA aneurysm supports further evaluation of selective popliteal assessment; however, this study does not support a universal screening recommendation or establish an effect on management, outcomes, or cost.

Title: Posterior Transverse Plication of Tortuous Internal Carotid Arteries During Carotid Endarterectomy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Excessive tortuosity of the internal carotid artery (ICA) can create a risk of kinking after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) with patch angioplasty. Posterior transverse plication (PTP) shortens and straightens the ICA without arterial transection or resection. This study reviewed our outcomes with PTP followed by patch angioplasty during CEA.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study identified patients who underwent CEA between 2006 and 2023. Patients treated with PTP and patch angioplasty (PTP+P) were compared with a contemporaneous cohort undergoing CEA with Dacron patch closure alone (DP) for the same atherosclerotic carotid disease. Early and long-term outcomes included neurologic events, restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, and survival.
RESULTS: Of 168 carotid interventions, 116 met inclusion criteria: 16 PTP+P and 100 DP. Patients in the PTP+P cohort were older and had higher rates of chronic renal insufficiency and coronary artery disease. There was no 30-day mortality or postoperative TIA/stroke in either cohort. During follow-up, no ipsilateral ischemic neurologic event occurred, and there was no significant difference in restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, or overall survival. In adjusted analysis, increasing age was associated with worse survival, while PTP was not.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small series, adding PTP during CEA before patch angioplasty appeared safe for correcting ICA tortuosity. The complication profile was similar to that of patients with straighter ICAs who underwent DP closure alone. A wide patch and intraoperative duplex ultrasound are advisable to prevent and detect technical narrowing at the plication site.
MESHWORDS: Carotid endarterectomy; internal carotid artery tortuosity; posterior transverse plication; patch angioplasty; restenosis.

Title: Repair durability following fenestrated versus chimney endovascular repair for elective juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms: a multicenter cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare repair durability following elective fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) and chimney endovascular aneurysm repair (ChEVAR) for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms using complementary procedural, imaging, and clinical outcome measures.
METHODS: A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included. Baseline characteristics, technical success, endoleaks, secondary aortic intervention, aneurysm sac remodeling, and target vessel patency were compared. Repair durability was assessed by integrating proximal seal integrity, longitudinal aneurysm sac remodeling, and freedom from secondary aortic intervention. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using χ2 or Fisher's exact tests. Statistical significance was defined as P < .05.
RESULTS: A total of 130 patients underwent elective repair, including 77 treated with FEVAR and 53 with ChEVAR. Baseline demographic characteristics, aneurysm diameter, and duration of follow-up were similar between groups. Technical success was comparable (98.7% vs 98.1%; P = .76), and target vessel patency exceeded 95% in both cohorts (P = .38). Type Ia endoleak occurred less frequently following FEVAR than ChEVAR (1.3% vs 22.6%; P < .001), with a lower incidence of all Type I endoleaks (Types Ia, Ib, and Ic) (7.8% vs 26.4%; P = .006). Secondary aortic intervention was also less common following FEVAR (10.4% vs 30.2%; P = .006). Progressive aneurysm sac regression was observed following FEVAR, with a mean reduction of 11 mm at 24 months, whereas ChEVAR demonstrated limited early regression followed by late sac re-expansion, resulting in an overall 2-mm reduction. Mean aneurysm sac diameter was significantly smaller following FEVAR compared with ChEVAR at both 12 months (55 vs 59 mm; P = .01) and 24 months (51 vs 63 mm; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: Elective FEVAR and ChEVAR achieved similarly high technical success and target vessel patency for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms. During mid-term follow-up, FEVAR was associated with lower rates of proximal attachment-site failure, greater aneurysm sac regression, and fewer secondary aortic interventions. These concordant procedural, imaging, and clinical outcomes suggest that integrated longitudinal assessment provides a more comprehensive evaluation of repair durability following complex endovascular aneurysm repair than technical success alone.

Title: Risk Prediction With a Type Ia-Oriented Proximal Neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score After EVAR.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We developed an exploratory Type Ia-oriented proximal neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score (Type Ia-ASGS) and assessed its association with postoperative type Ia endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR).
METHODS: We analyzed 304 elective standard EVAR patients treated during 2016-April 2024 with an Ankura endograft (Lifetech). Neck measurements were proximal diameter (A), distal diameter (B), and centerline length (C). The score assigned 1 point each for C ≤15 mm, max(A, B) >28 mm, and B - A ≥3 mm, and 2 points each for angulation >60° and calcification. The theoretical range was 0-7; weights reflected observed univariable associations.
RESULTS: Mean clinical and imaging follow-up was 27.6 ± 3.2 months, with final follow-up in June 2026. Type Ia endoleak occurred in 14/304 patients (4.6%). Observed event proportions were 1.2%, 2.8%, and 28.1% in exploratory low (0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (≥4) score categories (p < 0.001). Each point was associated with greater odds of type Ia endoleak (odds ratio, 2.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.80-4.29). Apparent area under the curve was 0.859 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.750-0.943). Individual event and censoring dates were unavailable for time-to-event analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: The Type Ia-ASGS was associated with postoperative type Ia endoleak in this derivation cohort. Its heuristic weights and exploratory categories require independent validation before clinical use.

Title: Prognostic Value of Late Gadolinium Enhancement in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Observational Study from India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) represents a significant cause of heart failure and sudden cardiac death (SCD). Current risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which has limitations in predicting adverse outcomes. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may provide additional prognostic information.
METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 88 consecutive NIDCM patients who underwent CMR imaging at our institution. Patients were followed for a minimum of 6 months and thereafter until a common study closure date, giving a mean follow-up of 337±173 days. The primary endpoint was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE), defined as sudden cardiac death, heart failure death, aborted sudden cardiac death, sustained ventricular tachycardia, and heart failure hospitalization.
RESULTS: LGE was present in 44 patients (50%). The most common pattern was mid-myocardial enhancement (40.9%), followed by a combination of patterns (25.0%) and transmural enhancement (22.7%); the interventricular septum was the most frequently involved segment (81.8%). MACE occurred in 22.7% of LGE-positive patients versus 13.6% of LGE-negative patients. ROC curve analysis identified LGE extent >26% of LV volume as the optimal threshold for predicting MACE (sensitivity 70%, specificity 73.5%, AUC 0.75). Patients with LGE >26% had significantly higher event rates (43.7% vs 10.7%; unadjusted OR 6.48, 95% CI 1.45-28.9; p=0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Greater LGE extent was associated with adverse cardiac events in NIDCM patients. CMR-based risk stratification may help identify high-risk patients who could benefit from ICD, but external validation in larger cohorts is required before using this threshold clinically.

Title: Surgical outcomes of infective endocarditis in children and adults with congenital heart disease.
Journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Reports describing surgery for infective endocarditis (IE) in children and adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited. This study aimed to determine the patient characteristics, preoperative conditions, surgical outcomes, and risk factors in this cohort.
METHODS: All children and adults with CHD who underwent surgical treatment for IE between 2001 and 2024 were reviewed. Patient characteristics and surgical procedures were evaluated; survival, recurrent IE, and risk factors were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent surgical treatment for IE, including 52 children and 44 adults with CHD. Underlying CHD included ventricular septal defect in 31 patients, aortic stenosis/insufficiency in 26, and tetralogy of Fallot in 14. The most frequently infected lesion was the aortic valve in 40 patients, and the most frequently detected organism was Staphylococcus species in 34 patients. Vegetation was observed in 65 patients. Median age at surgery was 17.2 (IQR: 11.7-29.4) years. In-hospital mortality was 6.3%, and survival at 5, 10, and 20 years was 90.6, 88.1, and 80.5%, respectively. Freedom from recurrent IE was 96.4% at 20 years. Number of previous operations (hazard ratio (HR): 1.585, p=0.005), gram-negative bacteria (HR: 11.475, p<0.001), emergency operations (HR: 17.988, p=0.001), and longer aortic cross-clamp time (HR: 1.011, p=0.043) were risk factors for mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In children and adults with CHD, mortality following surgery for IE was low, and recurrent IE was rare. Individualized management based on the patient's preoperative condition and the causative organism appears to be important for improving survival.

Title: Aortic Root Abscess in Infective Endocarditis: Prognostic Impact and Outcomes of Patch Repair.
Journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Due to discrepancies between guidelines and expert consensus, we examined the perioperative and mid-term outcomes of aortic root abscesses to determine their prognostic significance and optimal surgical management.
METHODS: We completed a single-center retrospective study of patients surgically treated for aortic valve infective endocarditis (AV IE) from 2019 to 2024. We compared outcomes in patients with and without root abscess, and among abscess cases, between patch repair and extended surgery (root reconstruction or replacement). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE, composite of all-cause death, heart failure (HF) readmission, and stroke). Outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan Meier estimators and Cox proportional hazards.
RESULTS: Among 158 patients (57% with abscess) with a median follow-up of 1.22 years (IQR 0.13-2.53), root abscesses were associated with increased MACCE (adjusted HR 3.15 (1.51-6.59), p=0.002) and HF readmission (SHR 4.54 (1.55-13.30), p=0.006). In patients with aortic root abscess, 62 underwent patch repair and 21 underwent extended surgery. Patch repair was associated with decreased MACCE (adjusted HR 0.34 (0.15-0.74), p=0.006), all-cause mortality (p=0.002), and death at 30 days (13% vs 33%, p=0.035) compared to extended surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Aortic root abscess was associated with increased MACCE and HF readmissions compared to AV IE without abscess, identifying root abscess as a marker of adverse prognosis and supporting prompt recognition and referral in aortic valve endocarditis. Patch repair for aortic root abscesses is a safe and reasonable approach in patients with suitable anatomy compared to more extensive surgery.

Title: Comparative outcomes of monocusp valve versus conduit for pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect.
Journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated reoperation and long-term right ventricular (RV) function after RV outflow tract (RVOT) reconstruction in pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect (PA/VSD), comparing monocusp valve outflow patch (MVOP) and conduit placement.
METHODS: This retrospective review included 130 patients with PA/VSD who underwent MVOP with 0.1-mm expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (n=84) or conduit placement (n=46) between 1993 and 2025. The primary endpoint was RVOT-related reoperation; the secondary endpoint was long-term RV function measured by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
RESULTS: Median age at repair was higher with MVOP group (2.4 vs. 1.4 years, P=.001), and median follow-up was 11.9 years. Freedom from RVOT-related reoperation at 12 years was higher with MVOP (78.0% vs. 60.2%, P=.017). In a sensitivity analysis additionally adjusting for surgical era, the association between reconstruction type and reoperation was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (adjusted hazard ratio for conduit vs MVOP, 1.79; 95% confidence interval, 0.72-4.43; P=.208). Subgroup analysis showed greater freedom from reoperation with MVOP in patients without major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (82.9% vs. 59.1%, P=.005). Cardiac MRI at school age showed comparable RV volumes and function between groups (all P >.05).
CONCLUSIONS: MVOP demonstrated higher observed freedom from RVOT-related reoperation than conduit placement, although this association was attenuated after adjustment for surgical era, with comparable long-term RV function at school age. Surgical strategy should be individualized based on patient characteristics and RVOT anatomy.

Title: Phytocannabinoids in neurologic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, pain, cardiometabolic, hepatic, renal, and neoplastic disorders: Pharmacology, clinical evidence, and translational perspectives.
Abstract: Phytocannabinoids are pharmacologically diverse constituents of Cannabis sativa whose actions go beyond canonical cannabinoid receptors. Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) are best characterized, while cannabigerol, cannabidivarin, tetrahydrocannabivarin, cannabichromene, cannabinol, and related compounds are emerging candidates. This review integrates molecular pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, safety, and therapeutic evidence across neurologic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, pain, cardiovascular and metabolic, hepatic, renal, and neoplastic disorders. The strongest evidence supports pharmaceutical-grade oral CBD as adjunctive therapy for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex, and standardized THC-CBD formulations for selected patients with multiple sclerosis-associated spasticity. Emerging clinical signals in schizophrenia, pain, fibromyalgia, sleep disturbance, substance-use disorders, dermatologic conditions, sickle cell disease, and other symptom-focused indications support continued development. However, efficacy remains compound-, formulation-, exposure-, and indication-specific. In oncology, supportive-care applications must remain distinct from tumor-directed treatment, for which clinical efficacy has not been established.
