Preclinical studies show coherent effects on neuronal excitability, glial and immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, mitochondrial injury, fibrosis, and regulated cell death. These findings support further investigation in neurodegeneration, ischemia-reperfusion injury, diabetic cardiovascular disease, immune-mediated disorders, hepatic and renal injury, and selected cancers. Translation is constrained by product heterogeneity, variable exposure, uncertain target engagement, model differences, drug interactions, and underpowered trials. Standardized products, exposure-informed dosing, pharmacodynamic biomarkers, responder-enriched designs, and indication-specific randomized studies can address these barriers. Phytocannabinoids therefore represent a promising therapeutic platform whose potential will be best realized by matching defined compounds and formulations to biologically coherent diseases, mechanisms, treatment windows, and patient populations.

Title: Safety and efficacy of cerebral embolic protection devices during TAVI: a meta-analysis and sequence analysis of trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral embolic protection (CEP) devices have been developed to reduce postoperative neurological outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI); however, their effectiveness remains controversial.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of CEP use during TAVI on the occurrence in clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Databases were used to search for randomized clinical trials. The occurrence of all strokes, of disabling strokes specifically, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), all-cause mortality, and vascular complications were analyzed. Conventional meta-analysis was conducted using fixed-effects modeling and trial sequential analysis (TSA: type I error of 5%, power of 90%). The systematic review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420251081075).
RESULTS: In total, eight clinical trials were included, gathering 11,589 patients randomized between those who used the devices (5,943) and those who did not (5,646). The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between CEP use and reduced odds of all-cause stroke (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.73-1.15, p = 0.46) and disabling stroke (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.57-1.13, p = 0.20). The sequential analysis identified a lack of evidence for all strokes (required sample size [rSS] = 38,626; 10.53%), disabling strokes (rSS = 59,732; 17.05%). In terms of mortality, there was no significance in the use of devices (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.71-1.69, p = 0.69), reaching evidence for support (rSS = 7,053; 42.25%).
CONCLUSION: The data on the use of CEP is insufficient to support meta-analytic conclusions regarding cerebrovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, TSA demonstrated evidence supporting futility regarding mortality reduction.

Title: PCSK9 and Thrombo-inflammatory Pathways.
Abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) was characterized as a hepatic regulator of low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) degradation. Monoclonal antibodies directed at PCSK9 lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and reduce major adverse cardiovascular events; small interfering RNA directed at PCSK9 lowers LDL-C, and cardiovascular outcome testing is ongoing. A parallel body of work has since linked PCSK9 to thrombo-inflammatory processes. Experimental studies indicate that extracellular PCSK9 activates platelets through CD36, induces monocyte tissue factor expression via Toll-like receptor 4 and nuclear factor-κB, promotes release of procoagulant extracellular vesicles, and impairs endothelial homeostasis; PCSK9 may also raise factor VIII by accelerating turnover of LDLR family members. Clinical biomarker studies report lower platelet-activation markers, and fibrinogen and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 during treatment. However, randomized placebo-controlled studies using direct platelet-function assays, as well as their pooled analysis, have not demonstrated a consistent reduction in platelet reactivity with PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies. This review synthesizes and evaluates the evidence by cellular compartment, separating circulating, locally released and intracellular PCSK9, and by evidentiary level, separating preclinical mechanism, observational association, circulating biomarker, randomized pharmacodynamic endpoint, clinical outcome, and human genetics. It also examines why experimental findings may not translate into measurable platelet inhibition in treated patients, and how concomitant antithrombotic and statin therapy conditions any such measurement. Preclinical plausibility is substantial. A clinically measurable, LDL-independent antiplatelet effect of PCSK9 inhibition has not been established, and the randomized evidence is more precise against a large platelet effect than against a modest one.

Title: Predictors of incident potentially inappropriate medication exposure in dementia: a national Medicare claims study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: PIMs remain common among older adults with dementia despite substantial safety concerns. Limited evidence exists on the predictors of new PIM initiation post-diagnosis. This study examined factors associated with incident PIM exposure among individuals with newly diagnosed dementia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Merative MarketScan Medicare Supplemental Database (2017-2019). The cohort included adults aged ≥65 years newly diagnosed with dementia in 2018, PIM-naive at baseline, and continuously enrolled during 12-month baseline and follow-up periods. Dementia was identified using diagnostic codes, and incident PIM exposure was defined according to the 2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Among 12,935 older adults with incident dementia, 1146 (8.9%) developed incident PIM exposure. Neuropsychiatric symptoms demonstrated the strongest associations: multiple symptoms (aOR 4.31, 95% CI 2.18-8.54), agitation (aOR 4.08, 95% CI 2.28-7.28), psychosis (aOR 2.70, 95% CI 1.88-3.88), and delirium (aOR 1.90, 95% CI 1.21-2.97). Greater baseline medication burden (aOR 1.018, 95% CI 1.004-1.031) and Lewy body or frontotemporal dementia (aOR 1.79, 95% CI 1.07-2.99) were also associated with increased odds. Conversely, hypertension and congestive heart failure were inversely associated with incident PIM exposure.
CONCLUSIONS: Neuropsychiatric symptoms were the strongest predictors of incident PIM exposure in dementia, with greater medication burden and Lewy body or frontotemporal dementia conferring additional risk. These findings underscore the need for safer behavioral management and targeted deprescribing to reduce inappropriate medication exposure in this vulnerable population.

Title: Paradoxical ethnic differences in prevalence of vascular risk factors versus extracranial atherosclerotic disease in TIA/stroke patients in the United Kingdom: Population-based study and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies in Northern America report a lower prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) in Black than White people despite higher prevalence of vascular risk factors. However, it remains unclear to what extent these differences are driven by biology or reflect ethnic disparities in smoking, socioeconomic deprivation, healthcare access, and health-seeking behaviour. We aimed to determine if ethnic differences in coronary and peripheral artery disease persist in people with stroke living in the United Kingdom (UK), considering that most people with stroke seek medical attention and the National Health Service provides equitable access to care.
METHODS: In a prospective population-based cohort of all patients with suspected TIA or stroke in Oxfordshire, UK (Oxford Vascular Study, OxVasc, April 2002 to March 2023), we fitted multivariable logistic regression models to quantify the association of ethnicity and extracranial atherosclerotic disease (coronary or peripheral) while adjusting for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and socioeconomic deprivation. We verified our findings in a systematic review of UK-based studies reporting prevalence of extracranial atherosclerotic disease and associated vascular risk factors across ethnic groups. Prevalence estimates were pooled by random-effects meta-analysis.
RESULTS: In 7297 OxVasc participants (52.6% women, 71.0 ± 15.5 years), non-White people (n = 335) had a higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus (OR = 3.26, 2.55-4.16). However, Black people had a lower prevalence of CAD (OR = 0.31, 0.10-0.98, p = 0.046) or any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (OR = 0.42, 0.18-0.96, p = 0.04) than White people. After adjustment for age, sex, vascular risk factors, and deprivation, the difference was attenuated both for CAD (aOR = 0.50, 0.18-1.41, p = 0.19) and any extracranial atherosclerotic disease (aOR = 0.43, 0.18-1.04, p = 0.06). Asian and White people had similar prevalence of CAD and extracranial atherosclerotic disease. Among UK-based studies of patients with stroke, Black and Asian people were more likely than White people to have diabetes (pooled OR: 2.78, 2.40-3.22, n = 3 studies; 4.15, 3.11-5.53 n = 6), hypertension (1.95, 1.47-2.60, n = 3; 1.47, 1.02-2.12, n = 6), and obesity (1.52, 1.27-1.83, n = 1; 1.2, 0.66-2.29, n = 3) but less likely to be smoking (0.70, 0.50-0.97, n = 2; 0.57, 0.44-0.74, n = 5). Yet, Black people had less CAD than White (0.48, 0.31-0.76, n = 3) and Asian (0.30, 0.10-0.80, n = 2) people.
INTERPRETATION: We confirm the existence of a coronary artery disease paradox in Black but not Asian people with TIA or stroke, which is likely independent of biases in healthcare access or health-seeking behaviour, and may suggest different biological susceptibilities.

Title: Workforce and economic consequences of premature cancer and cardiovascular disease mortality in Europe: A comparative modelling study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature mortality from non-communicable diseases (NCDs), particularly cancer and cardiovascular disease (CVD), threatens population health, workforce participation, and economic sustainability across Europe. However, comparative evidence on their productivity loss across European regions remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate and compare productivity losses associated with premature cancer and CVD mortality among working-age populations across Europe and assess regional inequalities.
METHODS: A quantitative, retrospective, cross-sectional comparative modelling study was conducted using secondary data from 30 European countries. Mortality data for adults aged 15-74 years were obtained from the World Health Organization Mortality Database, and labour market and economic data from Eurostat. A lifecycle simulation model incorporating age-specific earnings, employment rates, and labour force participation was developed to estimate productivity losses associated with premature mortality. Productivity losses were expressed in 2023 Euros and as a proportion of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
RESULTS: Premature mortality from cancer and CVD generated productivity losses of €220.1 billion, equivalent to 1.18% of European GDP. Cancer accounted for €130.3 billion (59.2%) and CVD for €89.8 billion (40.8%). Productivity losses per death were €235,991 for cancer and €221,809 for CVD. Central-Eastern Europe experienced the highest relative economic burden. Premature mortality from cancer and CVD is associated with substantial and unequal productivity losses across Europe. The magnitude of the estimates depends on the productive-age horizon, earnings trajectory, discounting and labour-market assumptions of the model. Increasing investment in prevention and early detection, particularly in higher-burden Central and Eastern European countries, could reduce avoidable working-age mortality and support workforce sustainability and long-term economic resilience.

Title: Joint CTI-eGDR phenotypes and incident cardiovascular disease in CKM stages 0-3: A retrospective landmark analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The joint cardiometabolic phenotypes of inflammatory-metabolic burden and insulin sensitivity based on repeated measurements their associations with the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) among individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remain unclear. We aimed to identify joint phenotypes in relation to C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) based on repeated measurements and evaluate their associations with incident CVD.
METHODS: This retrospective landmark cohort analysis used prospectively collected CHARLS data from 4883 participants aged ≥45 years with CKM stages 0-3. CTI, eGDR, cumulative CTI (CuCTI), and cumulative eGDR were derived from measurements in 2011 and 2015. K-means clustering of repeated CTI and eGDR measurements was used to identify joint cardiometabolic phenotypes, and Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-response, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During a median post-landmark follow-up of 5.0 years, 1195 incident CVD events were identified. Three phenotypes were identified: low CTI-high eGDR (n = 2344), high CTI-intermediate eGDR (n = 1351), and intermediate CTI-low eGDR (n = 1188). The K = 3 solution showed high bootstrap reproducibility (median adjusted Rand index, 0.978), although cluster separation was modest. Compared with the first phenotype, the latter two were associated with higher CVD risk after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.08-1.46; and HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.86-2.42). Both CuCTI and cumulative low-eGDR burden were associated with CVD risk. Findings were generally robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Joint CTI-eGDR phenotypes based on repeated measurements were associated with incident CVD, with the intermediate CTI-low eGDR phenotype representing a higher-risk composite cardiometabolic profile.

Title: Premedication with medetomidine compared to acepromazine reduces the risk of hypotension and mild acute kidney injury in healthy dogs undergoing gonadectomy surgery: results of a randomized clinical trial.
Journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare premedication with medetomidine or acepromazine in regard to hypotension and acute kidney injury (AKI) in dogs undergoing elective gonadectomy.
METHODS: This randomized clinical trial included healthy dogs ≥ 6 months of age undergoing gonadectomy in a university teaching hospital. Exclusion criteria were weight < 4 kg, American Society of Anesthesiologists risk > 2, or cardiovascular/renal disease. Premedication consisted of methadone and medetomidine at 0.3 to 5 µg/kg or acepromazine at 0.01 to 0.05 mg/kg IM. Anesthesia was induced with alfaxalone and maintained with isoflurane. Hypotension (mean arterial pressure < 60 mm Hg) frequency, severity, and duration; recovery temperature; and vomiting and pain interventions were compared. Oliguria 24 hours postoperatively was defined as no urination with low-volume bladder. Serum creatinine was measured from blood before and 24 hours after surgery. Acute kidney injury was defined as an increase of > 26.5 µmol/L.
RESULTS: The medetomidine group included 51 dogs and the acepromazine group 43. There were no differences in preoperative characteristics, anesthetic doses, or time. Hypotension was significantly less frequent (51% vs 84%), had a shorter duration (14 ± 20.2 minutes vs 26 ± 24.2 minutes), and was less severe (lowest mean arterial pressure 60.0 ± 14.9 mm Hg vs 51 ± 10.3 mm Hg) following medetomidine. Acute kidney injury was less frequent in the medetomidine group (9.8% vs 20.9%), with no oliguric AKI cases compared to 4 following acepromazine. There were no differences in postoperative hypothermia or treatments for vomiting or pain.
CONCLUSIONS: Premedication with medetomidine results in a lower frequency and duration of hypotension and might reduce the risk of AKI.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: For healthy dogs undergoing elective surgery, premedication with medetomidine is preferable to acepromazine.

Title: Predictors of longer recognition time in acute aortic dissection: a retrospective observational study.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) carries a high mortality risk closely tied to diagnostic timeliness. Delays remain prevalent, driven by atypical presentations-particularly in patients without a chief complaint of pain. This study identified predictors of a longer recognition time, as indicated by prolonged door-to-CT times, and developed a cumulative prediction model for patients presenting without pain complaints.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 197 adult patients diagnosed with AAD at a tertiary emergency department (ED) from 2016 to 2023. Patients were classified as having a shorter (< 74 min) or longer (≥ 74 min; cohort median) door-to-CT completion time. Predictors were identified by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized logistic regression and decision tree analysis. A subgroup analysis characterized pain-complaint-free patients using a stepwise identification algorithm.
RESULTS: A longer door-to-CT time was associated with female sex, older age, and physiological instability. The strongest multivariable predictors were absence of abrupt pain (odds ratio [OR] 2.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-5.46) and non-severe triage classification (OR 4.70, 95% CI 1.71-15.29). Dyspnea (OR 2.14) and elevated diastolic blood pressure (OR 1.02/mmHg) also independently predicted a longer door-to-CT time. Among pain-complaint-free patients (n = 46), a stepwise combination of mediastinal widening on chest radiography, Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and Shock Index > 1.0 was present in all identified cases (cumulative case coverage 46/46; 95% CI 92.3%-100%).
CONCLUSION: This study identifies a high-risk profile for a longer recognition time of AAD, particularly in older female patients and those presenting without sudden pain. For patients unable to report pain, chest radiography, shock index, and comorbidity burden may be considered to help identify atypical presentations warranting urgent evaluation.

Title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA).
RESULTS: Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow.
CONCLUSIONS: Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.

Title: Calibration of a fully closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model with baroreflex in response to induced central hypovolemia.
Abstract: Calibration of cardiovascular models is essential to their clinical utility. We provide a full description of the calibration of a non-linear, dynamic model using global optimisation methods. Specifically, we consider an experimental cohort response in a closed-loop, baro-regulated cardiovascular model, in the setting of induced central hypovolemia.We propose a framework for simplifying calibration of dynamic, regulated models. We perform global sensitivity analysis and orthogonality analysis of a 58-parameter non-linear cardiovascular model including the baroreflex, to select an optimal subset of parameters for model calibration. We fit the model to relative Lower Body Negative Pressure data, using global optimisation (Differential Evolution method), searching a reduced input parameter space. Global sensitivity analysis and orthogonality analysis revealed multiple higher-order interactions within the model, as well as areas of similar influence of input parameters, on the components of the objective function. The model was fitted using only baroreflex parameters. Relative errors in the estimation of heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and stroke volume were reduced from -15.03%, 1.60% and 42.06% before calibration to 0.42%, -1.37% and 0.61% after the fitting, respectively.

Title: Blood serotonin, ionized magnesium, cardiac troponin I, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide concentrations, and mitral valve billowing in horses with mitral valve regurgitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serotonin, ionized magnesium (iMg), cardiac biomarkers, and mitral valve prolapse are extensively investigated in humans and dogs with mitral valve regurgitation (MR), but not in horses.
HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: To investigate serotonin, iMg, cardiac troponin I (cTnI), and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations and degree of mitral valve billowing (MVB) in horses with MR.
ANIMALS: Eighty controls (no/trivial MR), 122 horses with MR (92 mild, 24 moderate, 6 severe).
METHODS: Prospective cross-sectional observational study. All horses underwent echocardiography with MVB distance assessment and MR classification. Platelet-poor plasma serotonin and serum iMg, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were determined. Controls and horses with different MR grades, biomarker concentrations, and MVB distance were compared using (non-)parametric tests.
RESULTS: Ionized magnesium concentration was lower in MR compared to controls (mean difference, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; P = .01), but showed no correlation with billowing distance. The billowing distance was higher in horses with MR than in controls (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P < .001; parietal: median difference, 0.3 cm; 95% CI, 0.2-0.3; P < .001), and in horses with a crescendo compared to a holosystolic MR jet (septal: median difference, 0.2 cm; 95% CI, 0.1-0.3; P = .003; parietal: median difference, 0.1 cm; 95% CI, 0.0-0.2; P = .01). No differences in serotonin, cTnI, and NT-proBNP concentrations were detected.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: Mitral valve billowing is to some extent likely physiological. The association of serotonin and iMg in MVB and MR requires further investigation. Both cTnI and NT-proBNP showed limited use as biomarkers of MR severity.
ABSTRACT (DUTCH): Achtergrondinformatie: Serotonine, geïoniseerd magnesium (iMg), cardiale biomarkers en mitraalklep prolaps werden reeds uitgebreid onderzocht bij mensen en honden met mitraalklep regurgitatie (MR), in tegenstelling tot paarden met MR. Hypothese/Doelstelling: Het onderzoeken van de serotonine, iMg, cardiaal troponine I (cTnI) en N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentraties en de mate van bolling van de mitraalklep naar het linker atrium (MVB) bij paarden met MR. Studiepopulatie: Tachtig controle paarden (geen/triviaal MR), 122 paarden met MR (92 mild, 24 matig, 6 erg). Materiaal en methoden: Prospectieve cross-sectionele observationele studie. Alle paarden ondergingen echocardiografie, waarna de mate van MVB gemeten werd en MR classificatie uitgevoerd werd. De concentraties van serotonine in bloedplaatjesarm plasma en van iMg, cTnI en NT-proBNP in serum werden bepaald. Controle paarden en paarden met verschillende MR graden, biomarker concentraties en de mate van MVB werden onderling vergeleken aan de hand van (non-)parametrische testen. Resultaten: De concentratie iMg was lager bij paarden met MR in vergelijking met controle paarden (gemiddeld verschil, 0.03 mmol/L; 95% BI, 0.01-0.05; P = 0.01), maar vertoonde geen correlatie met de mate van MVB. De mate van MVB was hoger bij paarden met MR dan bij controle paarden (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P < 0.001; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.3 cm; 95% BI, 0.2-0.3; P < 0.001), en bij paarden met een crescendo MR jet in vergelijking met paarden met een holosystolische MR jet (septaal: mediaan verschil, 0.2 cm; 95% BI, 0.1-0.3; P = 0.003; pariëtaal: mediaan verschil, 0.1 cm; 95% BI, 0.0-0.2; P = 0.01). Er werden geen verschillen gedetecteerd in de concentraties van serotonine, cTnI en NT-proBNP. Conclusies en klinisch belang: De mate van MVB is tot op een bepaalde hoogte waarschijnlijk fysiologisch. De rol van serotonine en iMg in MVB en MR vergt verder onderzoek. Zowel cTnI als NT-proBNP vertoonden een beperkte meerwaarde als biomarkers bij het bepalen van de ernst van MR.

Title: Ethnic disparities in outcomes of coronary artery bypass grafting in Israel.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Ethnic disparities after cardiac surgery are well reported. Israeli Arabs have lower life expectancy and greater frequency of cardiovascular risk factors. We sought to compare long-term outcomes following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between Arab and Jewish patients in Israel.
METHODS: Retrospective study of adult patients with multivessel disease undergoing isolated CABG in three centers between January 1st, 2009, and December 31st, 2023. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). The cumulative incidence of MACCE was plotted using KM curves. The hazard ratio (HR) for Arabs vs. Jewish were calculated using multivariate Cox models.
RESULTS: Our cohort included 6,330 patients, 1,819 (28.74%) and 4,511 (71.26%) patients were Arabs and Jewish, respectively. Median follow-up time was 78.32 months. Arab patients had higher rate of the primary outcome at median follow-up (46.26% vs 40.90%, HR 1.184, 95%CI: 1.09-1.286, P < 0.001) and there was no difference in mortality between the two groups (26.44% vs 26.45%, HR 1.004, 95%CI: 0.901-1.118, P = 0.82). After multivariable adjustment, the risk of MACCE was similar between the groups (adjusted HR 1.073, 95%CI: 0.965-1.193, P = 0.19).
CONCLUSIONS: After multivariable adjustment for baseline and socioeconomic factors, ethnicity was not independently associated with worse long-term clinical outcomes in patients undergoing CABG in Israel, while unadjusted disparities remained evident.

Title: Assessment of the appropriateness of stress ulcer prophylaxis practice among hospitalized patients across Lebanese hospitals: A multicenter prospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP) is recommended for critically ill patients at high risk of stress-related gastrointestinal bleeding. Despite established guideline recommendations, inappropriate use of acid suppressant medications (ASMs), particularly proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), remains common worldwide and may expose patients to unnecessary adverse effects and increased healthcare costs. This study aimed to assess the appropriateness of SUP prescribing practices among hospitalized patients across Lebanese hospitals, focusing on indication, choice of pharmacologic agent, dosing regimen, route of administration, duration of therapy, discharge prescribing, and factors associated with inappropriate SUP practice.
METHODS: A multicenter prospective study was conducted between April 20 and May 22, 2026, across ten tertiary-care hospitals in different regions of Lebanon. Adult patients (≥18 years) admitted to Internal Medicine Unit, Intensive Care Unit (ICU), or Coronary Care Unit wards were assessed for the appropriateness of SUP, regardless of whether ASMs were prescribed. The appropriateness of SUP practice was evaluated according to the Society of Critical Care Medicine and American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (SCCM/ASHP) 2024 and ASHP 1999 guidelines. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with inappropriate SUP practice.
RESULTS: A total of 552 patients were enrolled, with a mean age of 64.3 ± 18.5 years, and 58.7% were male. According to the SCCM/ASHP 2024 and ASHP 1999 guidelines, 90.8% and 77.2% of patients, respectively, were not eligible for SUP. Omeprazole was the most frequently prescribed agent (75.4%), and PPIs were used in all SUP prescriptions. Among patients admitted to ICU, 11.2% continued receiving ASMs after the SUP indication had resolved or following ICU transfer without a persisting indication. Overall, SUP practice was inappropriate in 77.9% of patients. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that anticoagulant therapy was associated with higher odds of inappropriate SUP practice (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI = 1.35-5.74, P = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Inappropriate SUP practice is highly prevalent among hospitalized patients in Lebanon, largely due to prescribing without guideline-based indications. Inappropriate continuation after resolution of the SUP indication or ICU transfer was also observed. Strengthening adherence to evidence-based recommendations through stewardship programs, prescribing audits, standardized protocols, and updated national guidance may help optimize SUP use and improve patient care.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Rethinking hypertension in the brain: from blood pressure control to temporal blood pressure stability-a scoping review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporal blood pressure variability (BPV) may contribute to cerebrovascular injury beyond mean blood pressure (BP), yet the mechanisms linking antihypertensive treatment patterns to temporal BP instability remain incompletely understood. This scoping review synthesised evidence linking treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants of BP control, temporal BPV, and cerebrovascular vulnerability.
METHODS: PubMed and Embase were searched for studies evaluating antihypertensive medication adherence, pharmacodynamic persistence, BPV, and cerebrovascular outcomes. Data were charted using a standardised form and synthesised narratively according to predefined thematic domains.
RESULTS: The available evidence suggests that inconsistent antihypertensive exposure and reduced pharmacodynamic persistence may contribute to increased temporal BPV. Generally BP fluctuations are associated with cerebral small vessel disease, white matter injury, vascular cognitive impairment, and other manifestations of cerebrovascular vulnerability independent of mean BP. This review investigates the relationship between treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants, and temporal BPV and proposes a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to facilitate future individualised risk stratification and guide prospective investigation.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports expanding hypertension management beyond achieving mean BP targets to include optimisation of temporal BP stability. Recognising treatment persistence and pharmacodynamic coverage as determinants of BP stability provides a clinically relevant framework for improving cerebrovascular protection and individualised risk assessment. These findings support consideration of temporal BP stability as a potential complementary dimension of hypertension management for preventing chronic cerebrovascular injury and vascular cognitive dysfunction.

Title: Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke.
AIM: To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke.
METHODS: A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. An individual responder analysis will be performed to determine if participants exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 2.25 points on the WGS.
DISCUSSION: This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Effectiveness of dose-matched rehabilitation with immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): study protocol for a single-blind, randomized crossover trial. URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07529665. Date of registration: 2026-04-14. Version 1.

Title: Visual outcomes and headache in intracranial hypertension following cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: Intracranial hypertension is a frequent complication of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT), posing a risk for permanent visual impairment. However, long-term visual outcomes have not been systematically assessed using objective neuro-ophthalmic measures. We retrospectively evaluated consecutive adults presenting to a single-center tertiary intracranial hypertension clinic between 2019 and 2025 with intracranial hypertension following CVT. Visual outcomes were assessed using best-corrected visual acuity, automated perimetry, and optical coherence tomography measuring global peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. Headache phenotype and medication overuse were documented. Nineteen patients (11 female; mean age 33.4 ± 12.1 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 3.4 ± 2.4 years after diagnosis of CVT-related intracranial hypertension. The transverse sinus was involved in 78.9% of cases, and complete or near-complete recanalization was achieved in 68.4%. Although visual acuity remained normal in most patients (84.2%), 26.3% had severe visual field loss and 15.8% showed retinal nerve fiber layer thinning. Headache persisted in 94.7%, most commonly as tension-type headache (63.2%), and 26.3% fulfilled criteria for medication overuse headache. Despite generally preserved visual acuity, substantial visual field deficits and persistent headache were common in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. These findings support routine neuro-ophthalmic follow-up to facilitate early detection of visual deterioration in CVT-related intracranial hypertension. As this cohort was drawn from a specialized tertiary referral clinic, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than representative of the broader CVT population.

Title: Protocol for investigating the association between Helicobacter pylori exposure, antigen-specific serological responses, and resistant versus non-resistant hypertension in a South African cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, with poor control in low- and middle-income countries. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) has been associated with hypertension through inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and immune pathways, but data from sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in resistant hypertension, are limited.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study will enrol 200 adults aged ≥18 at a tertiary academic hospital in Cape Town, South Africa: 80 with resistant hypertension, 80 with non-resistant hypertension and 40 with normotension. Participants will undergo standardised clinical assessment, blood pressure measurement, and collection of blood, urine and saliva. H. pylori exposure will be assessed using the Pylori DuoTect® point-of-care assay, which detects antibodies to CagA and FliD. Laboratory analyses will include lipid profile, inflammatory and nitric oxide-related markers, homocysteine, insulin indices, complete blood count, ghrelin, multiplex cytokine profiling and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. PAXgene® blood RNA samples will be retained for future exploratory analyses. Saliva will undergo exploratory H. pylori antigen testing using CerTest® kits, which are validated for stool rather than saliva. Saliva analysis will be exploratory, and results will not define the primary H. pylori exposure variable. Remaining saliva will be kept for potential future oral microbiome analyses not defined in this protocol. Multivariable logistic regression will evaluate associations between H. pylori exposure and hypertension phenotype, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates.
DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this will be the first African study to integrate point-of-care H. pylori serology with detailed clinical, inflammatory, metabolic, and immunological profiling across resistant hypertension, non-resistant hypertension and normotension. Findings may clarify biological pathways linking H. pylori exposure to blood pressure dysregulation and inform future mechanistic and interventional studies.

Title: Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil.
METHODS: We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios.
RESULTS: Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings.

Title: Identifying Patients for Cardiovascular Evaluation Using Artificial Intelligence and Team-Based Care in Ghana: The H-TRIAGE Study.
Abstract: Background: Cardiovascular diagnostic capacity is limited in many low-resource settings. We evaluated the HeartLINK Triage for Risk-Informed Allocation and Guided Evaluation (H-TRIAGE) index, a prespecified strategy combining clinical information and AI-enabled digital auscultation to prioritize cardiovascular evaluation. Methods: In this prospective study in Ghana (February-July 2026), consecutively enrolled adults underwent a standardized assessment by trained frontline nurses and community health workers. H-TRIAGE used predefined additive symptom, vital-sign, and AI-stethoscope weights to assign Low (0-3), Intermediate (4-7), or High (≥8) Risk. Four cardiologists, blinded to H-TRIAGE, independently reviewed all participants; a fifth adjudicated disagreements. The reference standard (adjudicated indication) was a recommendation for further diagnostic testing, cardiologist-led evaluation, or both. The primary cohort comprised 5 facilities across 3 districts of the Ashanti Region; external validation used a held-out facility in a separate district of the Eastern Region. In a modeled allocation analysis, Intermediate- and High-Risk participants were considered prioritized; we calculated sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Results: Among 3,800 participants (primary, n=3,123; external validation, n=677; median age, 52 years [IQR, 39-64]; 77.7% women), 1,707 (44.9%) had an adjudicated indication. By H-TRIAGE category, the proportion with an indication was 2.5% (Low), 87.9% (Intermediate), and 100% (High) (P for trend<0.001). Prioritizing Intermediate- and High-Risk participants yielded 1,656 true positives, 142 false positives, 1,951 true negatives, and 51 false negatives: sensitivity, 97.0% (95% CI, 96.1%-97.8%); specificity, 93.2% (92.1%-94.3%); PPV, 92.1% (90.8%-93.3%); and NPV, 97.5% (96.7%-98.1%). This approach would prioritize 47.3% of participants for evaluation. Conclusions: H-TRIAGE accurately identified adults needing cardiologist-adjudicated evaluation, and sensitivity remained high at a geographically distinct site. Applied by frontline nurses and community health workers, it could focus scarce specialist and diagnostic capacity on the patients most likely to need it, deferring roughly half of those assessed.

Title: Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index is Associated With Tumor Size and Preoperative Cerebrovascular Events in Left Atrial Myxoma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac myxomas are benign tumors associated with potentially serious cerebrovascular complications. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a readily available inflammatory marker; however, its relationship with tumor burden and cerebrovascular events in patients with left atrial myxoma remains unclear. This study investigated the associations of SII with tumor size and preoperative stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA).
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective study included 120 patients who underwent surgical resection of histopathologically confirmed left atrial myxoma between May 2014 and December 2025. Tumor size was assessed as the largest cross-sectional area measured by transesophageal echocardiography. SII was calculated from preoperative neutrophil, platelet, and lymphocyte counts. Correlation, multivariable regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Preoperative stroke/TIA occurred in 17 patients (14.2%). SII was positively correlated with tumor size (ρ = 0.602, p < 0.001) and remained significantly associated with tumor area after multivariable adjustment (β = 0.100 cm2 per 100-unit increase, 95% CI: 0.078-0.123; p < 0.001). Patients with larger tumors had a higher prevalence of preoperative stroke/TIA (21.9% vs. 5.4%, p = 0.016). Similarly, cerebrovascular events were more frequent in patients with high SII (≥840) than in those with low SII (32.4% vs. 6.0%, p < 0.001). Both SII (adjusted OR = 1.05 per 100-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.01-1.09; p = 0.021) and tumor size (adjusted OR = 1.80, 95% CI: 1.05-3.09; p = 0.033) were associated with preoperative stroke/TIA in multivariable analysis. SII demonstrated the highest numerical ROC area (AUC = 0.782), compared with the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (0.746), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (0.710), and tumor size (0.682).
CONCLUSIONS: SII was significantly associated with tumor size and preoperative cerebrovascular events in patients with left atrial myxoma. As an inexpensive and readily accessible marker, SII may complement echocardiographic assessment, although prospective validation is required.

Title: Reproductive Health in Monogenic Kidney Disease: Practical Guidance for Fertility, Genetic Counseling, and Pregnancy Care.
Journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
Abstract: Monogenic kidney diseases, including autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), Alport spectrum disorders, Fabry disease, and monogenic podocytopathies presenting as focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), increasingly affect people of reproductive age. Reproductive care extends beyond pregnancy to fertility, menstrual and sexual health, contraception, assisted reproduction, inheritance counseling, and long-term shared decision-making. This review uses these four disease groups to illustrate distinct counseling challenges arising from autosomal dominant, X-linked, autosomal recessive, and genetically heterogenous inheritance, including the underrecognized disease burden in heterozygous women with X-linked Alport syndrome or Fabry's disease. Across diseases, adverse maternal and fetal outcomes are driven primarily by reduced kidney function, chronic hypertension, proteinuria, prior preeclampsia and major extrarenal disease, whereas genotype, inheritance pattern, and syndromic features further shape counseling and reproductive genetic decisions. Preconception counseling should integrate maternal risk stratification; discontinuation or planned transition of fetotoxic agents, such as renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, tolvaptan, SGLT2 inhibitors, mycophenolate, and migalastat; and genetic counseling that addresses recurrence risk, cascade testing, and reproductive options, including prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). During pregnancy, close co-management by nephrology, maternal-fetal medicine, and genetics is essential to control blood pressure, provide low-dose aspirin prophylaxis, monitor kidney function and proteinuria, distinguish preeclampsia from progressive glomerular disease, and anticipate disease-specific complications such as cyst infection, intracranial aneurysm, nephrotic syndrome, and cardiac arrhythmia. Postpartum care should include medication re-optimization, breastfeeding counseling, kidney and cardiovascular surveillance, and revisiting contraception and future reproductive goals. Reproductive decision-making should be nondirective and centered on patient values, access to care, and tolerance for uncertainty. Evidence remains limited, largely retrospective, and enriched for milder disease, particularly regarding fertility outcomes, male reproductive implications, the reproductive safety of emerging targeted therapies, and genotype-specific pregnancy risk, underscoring the need for prospective multicenter studies.

Title: Agentic AI-Generated vs. Clinician-Authored Hospital Course Narratives for Cardiology Hospitalizations: A Blinded Physician Evaluation.
Abstract: Background: Discharge summaries are essential for safe transitions of care, but writing the hospital course narrative is time intensive. Large language models can generate plausible clinical narratives, yet prior approaches often rely on static inputs and remain vulnerable to omissions and factual inconsistencies. Methods: We developed an electronic health record (EHR)-integrated agentic artificial intelligence (AI) system that uses Gemini 2.5 Pro and Model Context Protocol tools to retrieve clinical notes, diagnostic reports, diagnoses, medications, and appointments on demand. In this retrospective, blinded, paired study, 50 inpatient cardiology encounters were randomly selected from admissions July 13 to 27, 2024, at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota. Five physicians rated AI-generated and clinician-authored hospital course narratives for each encounter (250 ratings) on 0-to-10 scales for overall quality, clarity, completeness, accuracy, and readability and indicated a preference. The primary outcome was the paired difference in overall quality (linear mixed-effects model with crossed random intercepts for encounter and reviewer). Secondary domains were analyzed similarly with Bonferroni adjustment, and preference with a crossed random-effects logistic model. Results: Clinician-authored narratives were preferred in 132 ratings (52.8%) and AI-generated narratives in 118 (47.2%) (odds ratio for clinician-authored preference, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.71 to 1.78). Overall quality did not differ significantly (mean, 7.27 AI-generated versus 7.42 clinician-authored; difference, -0.15; 95% CI, -0.86 to 0.56; p=0.627). AI-generated narratives were rated higher for clarity (0.36; 95% CI, 0.07 to 0.65) and readability (0.72; 95% CI, 0.20 to 1.24) but lower for completeness (-0.84; 95% CI, -1.36 to -0.32) and accuracy (-0.35; 95% CI, -0.66 to -0.05). After Bonferroni correction, only lower completeness remained significant (adjusted p=0.012). Conclusions: Hospital course narratives generated by the EHR-integrated agentic AI system did not differ significantly from clinician-authored narratives in physician-rated overall quality or preference. Lower completeness supports continued clinician review before use in the medical record.

Title: Multimorbidity burden and high-cost status among patients with diabetes: evidence from longitudinal claims data in China.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Multimorbidity is common among people with diabetes and is associated with healthcare cost concentration. This study aims to quantify multimorbidity burden and evaluates the association between multimorbidity and high-cost (HC) status.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using longitudinal health insurance claims and chronic disease management data from 79,910 diabetic patients in eastern China. Patients in the top 10% of annual healthcare expenditures in 2019 were classified as HC. Multimorbidity was defined based on 29 chronic conditions identified through literature review and utilization thresholds. Descriptive analyses compared HC and non-high-cost (NHC) patients. Six machine learning models were developed to identify the contribution of multimorbidity to HC patients, using ROC-AUC and PR-AUC as the primary performance metrics. For the best-performing model, the Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) method was used to interpret the results.
RESULTS: A total of 7,991 (10.0%) patients were classified as HC. HC patients had a higher multimorbidity burden than NHC patients (mean number of conditions: 8.6 vs. 6.4). Mean annual expenditure was substantially higher among HC patients ($25,903 vs. $2,490). Multimorbidity-related care accounted for 33.6% of total expenditures and was over ten times higher in HC patients. Hypertension was the most prevalent condition among HC patients (91.3%), while cerebrovascular disease sequelae generated the highest per-patient costs ($8,869). The Extreme Gradient Boosting model achieved the best performance (ROC-AUC = 0.750, PR-AUC = 0.301). SHAP analysis identified cerebrovascular disease sequelae, renal failure, chronic ischemic heart disease, cerebral infarction and osteoporosis as the most influential predictors of multimorbidity affecting HC status.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimorbidity is associated with HC status of patients with diabetes. Strengthening risk stratification and integrated management for patients with cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, and skeletal diseases can help reduce healthcare costs and improve health outcomes.

Title: Preoperative SASP burden predicts perioperative vulnerability in older patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract: Cellular senescence and its associated secretory phenotype (SASP) represent a fundamental mechanism of biological aging. SASP-related inflammation has been implicated in cardiovascular disease. However, its role in perioperative risk in cardiac surgery remains largely unexplored, and established risk scores such as EuroSCORE II and the STS Score do not regard biological aging or senescence. In this prospective single-center cohort study, 131 patients aged ≥ 65 years undergoing elective cardiac surgery were enrolled. A panel of 19 preoperative SASP biomarkers was quantified by a multiplex immunoassay. Of those, 17 markers were evaluated as predictors of a composite adverse outcome, an adapted multimorbidity score with 21.4% event rate, with MACCE (36.6%) as a secondary endpoint. Logistic regression, false discovery rate correction, bootstrap validation, and incremental value analyses (DeLong test, IDI, NRI) were used. Five markers showed nominal univariable significance (IGFBP-1, GDF-15, TNF-RI, TNF-α, and IGFBP-4), though none survived FDR correction. Adjusted for procedure type, IGFBP-1 (OR = 1.675, 95% CI = 1.175-2.389, p = 0.004) and IGFBP-4 (OR = 1.432, 95% CI = 1.044-1.966, p = 0.026) emerged as independent predictors of the composite adverse outcome (Model M3, AUCcorrected = 0.746), numerically comparable to EuroSCORE II (AUC = 0.727). Model M3 improved net reclassification over EuroSCORE II (NRI + 0.528, p = 0.008) and the STS Score (NRI + 0.418, p = 0.040), with consistent estimates under Firth-penalized sensitivity analysis. Preoperative SASP biomarkers, particularly IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-4, independently predict adverse outcomes, namely multimorbidity, after elective cardiac surgery. They improve individual risk stratification beyond standard clinical scores in older patients, suggesting a measurable dimension of perioperative vulnerability that warrants external validation in larger cohorts.

Title: Resolving clinical Dilemmas in Hyperkalemia management for chronic heart failure: Current and emerging roles of sodium zirconium cyclosilicate.
Abstract: Hyperkalemia, commonly defined as a serum potassium concentration > 5.0 mEq/L, is a frequent and clinically important complication in patients with chronic heart failure (HF), particularly those with chronic kidney disease receiving guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Its impact extends beyond the electrolyte abnormality itself because recurrent hyperkalemia may lead to underuse, dose reduction, or discontinuation of prognostically important therapy. The risk is not uniform across GDMT classes: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists carry the greatest direct risk, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors also increase risk, whereas sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors may reduce serious hyperkalemia. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) effectively lowers serum potassium and randomized evidence supports its use to maintain normokalemia and facilitate spironolactone optimization. However, a reduction in mortality or HF hospitalization has not been established. Emerging observational data suggest additional potential roles in supporting individualized dietary liberalization, improving gastrointestinal tolerability relative to traditional resins, and preventing recurrent hyperkalemia after treatment withdrawal. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because several supporting studies are small, nonrandomized, and potentially affected by residual confounding. Long-term treatment also requires attention to sodium exposure and edema, particularly in patients with HF or advanced kidney disease. This review integrates class-specific hyperkalemia risk, practical potassium thresholds, efficacy and safety evidence, comparison with patiromer, health-economic considerations, and remaining evidence gaps to provide a clinically applicable framework for individualized potassium management in HF.

Title: Genetic and phenotypic landscape of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the MENA region: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common inherited cardiomyopathy, and it is a leading cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young people. Recessive genetic disorders are especially prevalent in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region due to consanguinity, which affects the genetic landscape of hereditary disorders. Here we conducted a systematic review of mutations in patients with HCM in the MENA and report genotype-phenotype associations to provide an evidence base for personalized diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.
METHODS: We systematically searched the PubMed, ProQuest, and Scopus databases from inception until October 2025 to collect all genetic data and phenotypes of patients with HCM in the MENA. Broad search terms were used to capture all relevant literature describing genetic variants associated with HCM in the MENA region including inheritance patterns and genotype-phenotype associations.
RESULTS: The database search returned 448 studies, with 17 meeting inclusion criteria. 14 studies were case series, 2 studies were case reports, and 1 was a case-control study. In 1323 HCM subjects in the MENA, there were 107 genetic variants in 21 genes. The majority of the variants occurred in MYBPC3 and MYH7, consistent with other populations. However, there were also homozygous variants in recessive genes, founder mutations, and novel variants in non-sarcomeric genes in the region, with patients experiencing more severe clinical phenotypes.
CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first systematic review on genetic variants associated with HCM in the MENA region. The genetic landscape of HCM is complex and unique in the MENA. The underrepresentation of MENA populations in global genomic resources remains a barrier to variant interpretation. Region-specific gene panels may be required to advance the diagnosis of HCM in the region.

Title: Minimally important change of the PROMIS Global Health in older stroke patients: a multicentre prospective cohort study.
Journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Interpretation of patient-reported outcome measures (PROM) score changes requires knowledge of the minimally important change (MIC). The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Global Health questionnaire (PROMIS-GH), which contains subscales assessing physical and mental health, is increasingly used in post-stroke care. However, the MIC of the PROMIS-GH subscales has not been estimated in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). This study aimed to estimate the MIC of PROMIS-GH subscales in older stroke and TIA patients.
METHODS: This Dutch multicentre prospective cohort study included adults aged ≥ 70 years with a recent ischemic stroke or TIA (May 2024-March 2026). The PROMIS-GH was administered at baseline and after 1 month of follow-up. The MIC of the PROMIS-GH subscales was primarily estimated using the predictive modelling approach. Two additional methods, the mean change method and receiver operating characteristic analysis, were performed as secondary analyses.
RESULTS: We included 125 patients. Ninety-five patients with a median age of 78 completed the study. Using predictive modelling, we estimated an MIC of 1.3 points for the global physical health (GPH) subscale. MIC for the global mental health (GMH) subscale could not be estimated.
CONCLUSION: The MIC for the GPH subscale in older patients with ischemic stroke or TIA was small, suggesting that even small score changes may be clinically relevant in this population. No reliable MIC could be estimated for the GMH subscale, highlighting the need for further research.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06495073, registered on 3 July 2024.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Acute effects of hibiscus tea versus coffee consumption before prolonged sitting on blood pressure and heart rate variability in adults: a randomized crossover trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare acute effects of consuming hibiscus tea and coffee before prolonged uninterrupted sitting on blood pressure (BP) and heart rate variability (HRV) in young, healthy adults.
METHODS: In a randomized crossover trial, participants (n = 24; 24.9 [4.9] years old; 50% women; 54.2% with overweight/obesity) completed two 3-hour prolonged uninterrupted sitting sessions after consuming hibiscus tea or coffee. A Polar H10 heart rate (HR) strap connected to a Polar V800 monitor evaluated HRV indices, including HR, standard deviation of normal R-R intervals (SDNN), root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), low-frequency power (LF), and high-frequency power (HF). A sphygmomanometer (Welch Allyn Connex) measured systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) BP, and mean arterial pressure (MAP) was calculated. HRV indices were natural log-transformed (ln) due to skewness. Generalized linear mixed models with random effects examined the influence of both beverages on BP and HRV while adjusting for baseline values.
RESULTS: SBP, DBP, and MAP were significantly lower (β = - 4.2, - 3.3, - 3.6 mmHg, respectively), and lnHF (β = 0.3) was significantly higher in the hibiscus tea condition compared with the coffee condition (p < 0.05 for all). No other significant differences were detected for other HRV indices (p > 0.05 for all). Sex- and BMI-stratified analyses suggested potential variation in cardiovascular responses across subgroups, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously as formal interaction tests were not performed.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that hibiscus tea may have potential to favorably modulate cardiovascular responses to prolonged uninterrupted sitting compared with coffee, although further controlled studies are needed to confirm these effects and establish their long-term implications.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Associations between biomarkers of vitamin K and cardiovascular disease risk factors: the role of lipids.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging evidence indicates that vitamin K is important not only for its role in blood coagulation activation, but also for cardiovascular health. However, the results are equivocal, and due to the lipophilic nature of vitamin K, adjustment for triglycerides may be important. We investigated the associations between levels of circulating vitamin K vitamers, phylloquinone (PK) and total menaquinones (MK), and dephospho-undercarboxylated matrix Gla protein (dp-ucMGP, a biomarker of functional vitamin K status), with multiple cardiovascular disease risk factors and adjusted for triglycerides.
METHODS: From the population-based Inter99 cohort, 2,195 participants had available fasting blood samples from which dp-ucMGP, PK, and MK-4 to MK-10 were analysed (mean age, ± SD: 68, ± 7 years, 48% female). Cross-sectional associations with cardiovascular disease risk factors were examined per doubling of vitamin K biomarkers using multivariable regression models.
RESULTS: Both PK and total MK were positively associated with hypertriglyceridemia: OR (95%CI) 1.91, (1.69, 2.18) and 13.1, (7.55, 23.4), respectively, but not measures of adiposity and diabetes. However, after triglyceride adjustment, higher PK and total MK were inversely associated with central obesity: 0.86, (0.79, 0.95) and 0.61, (0.37, 0.98), respectively, and diabetes: 0.81, (0.69, 0.95) and 0.33, (0.13, 0.81), respectively. Higher dp-ucMGP was associated with hypertriglyceridemia: 1.50, (1.08, 2.09). After adjustment for triglycerides, higher dp-ucMGP remained associated with central obesity: 2.81, (2.16, 3.70) and obesity: 3.31, (2.50, 4.42).
CONCLUSION: After accounting for triglycerides, both PK and total MK were inversely associated with measures of adiposity and diabetes, suggesting that blood triglyceride levels need to be accounted for when considering circulating vitamin K levels. Higher dp-ucMGP, reflecting reduced vitamin K-dependent MGP carboxylation, was associated with adiposity markers independent of triglycerides.

Title: Revisiting the role of sex in stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2024 European Society of Cardiology guidelines introduced the CHA2DS2-VA score, omitting female sex from stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF). However, evidence on the relative predictive performance of CHA2DS2-VA versus CHA2DS2-VASc across diverse populations remains inconsistent. We therefore conducted a systematic evaluation of their discrimination and reclassification performance.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational cohort studies comparing CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc for prediction of ischaemic stroke or thromboembolic events in patients with AF. Discrimination was evaluated using the difference in C-statistics (ΔAUC) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and reclassification using continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI). Pooled estimates were derived using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Seven studies including 250,112 patients were analysed. In the overall population, discriminative performance was comparable between the CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc scores (ΔAUC 0.00065, 95% CI -0.00288 to 0.00417; IDI 0.00010, 95% CI -0.00063 to 0.00083). Continuous NRI indicated a modest advantage for CHA2DS2-VASc (-0.05615; 95% CI: -0.10350 to -0.00880). Among patients not receiving oral anticoagulation, both discrimination and reclassification were similar between the two scores. Variability in reclassification performance was observed across regions and study periods.
CONCLUSIONS: The CHA2DS2-VA and CHA2DS2-VASc scores showed comparable discrimination for stroke risk prediction in patients with AF when evaluated as continuous scores, although reclassification modestly favoured the CHA2DS2-VASc score. The clinical contribution of female sex to risk prediction appears context-dependent and warrants further evaluation.

Title: Demographic, comorbidity, and temporal trends in anterior (ALIF) versus posterior (PLIF/TLIF) single-level lumbar interbody fusion: a retrospective analysis from 2015 to 2023.
Journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to characterize national demographic and comorbidity profiles associated with anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) versus posterior interbody fusion (PLIF/TLIF) and evaluate temporal utilization patterns.
METHODS: Using a commercial insurance database from 2015 to 2023, adults undergoing single-level ALIF or posterior interbody fusion were identified. Univariate tests compared baseline characteristics. Annual utilization trends were estimated with Poisson regression or negative binomial regression if overdispersion was present. Significance was set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: Among 407,319 patients, 133,323 underwent ALIF and 273,996 underwent posterior interbody fusion. Mean age was higher for posterior interbody fusion (61.8 vs. 59.5 years; P < 0.001), as was mean Elixhauser Comorbidity Index (5.3 ± 3.6 vs. 5.2 ± 3.6; P < 0.001). Sex distribution and rheumatoid arthritis were similar (P > 0.05 for all). Posterior interbody fusion patients more frequently had obesity, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, chronic kidney disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, osteoporosis, and tobacco use (P < 0.001 for all). ALIF procedures increased at an average annual rate of 6.66% (95% CI, 4.60-8.47; P < 0.001), whereas posterior interbody fusion increased 1.98% per year (95% CI, -0.19-4.19; P = 0.075); the annual growth-rate difference (ALIF - posterior interbody fusion) was 4.68% points (95% CI, 1.71-6.98; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this national sample, posterior interbody fusion was more commonly used in older, more medically complex patients, while both approaches grew over time with faster growth for ALIF and increasing ALIF share. These descriptive patterns outline contemporary selection of anterior versus posterior approaches and motivate outcome-focused, risk-adjusted studies in key subgroups.

Title: Imaging-based epicardial adipose tissue assessment and serum adipokines in postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common complication after cardiac surgery. We evaluated the associations of preoperative epicardial adipose tissue thickness (EATT), measured by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) and multislice computed tomography (MSCT), and circulating adipokines with POAF after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and compared the imaging methods. This prospective observational cohort included 96 consecutive eligible adults without prior atrial fibrillation who underwent elective isolated CABG. EATT was measured preoperatively by TTE and MSCT, and serum adiponectin, leptin, and resistin concentrations were determined. POAF was recorded during the first postoperative week. POAF occurred in 26 patients (27.1%). EATT measured by both methods was higher in patients who developed POAF. In multivariable analysis, EATT measured by TTE (odds ratio, 2.05; 95% confidence interval, 1.45-2.89; p < 0.001) and age (odds ratio, 1.08; 95% confidence interval, 1.00-1.156; p = 0.040) independently predicted POAF. The area under the curve was 0.818 for TTE (cutoff, 6.55 mm; sensitivity, 73.1%; specificity, 87.1%) and 0.787 for MSCT (cutoff, 6.22 mm; sensitivity, 80.8%; specificity, 75.7%), with no significant difference (p = 0.127). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of - 0.016 mm. Serum adipokine concentrations were not associated with POAF. Increased EATT and older age independently predicted POAF after isolated CABG. TTE showed performance comparable to MSCT and may provide a practical, radiation-free approach to preoperative EATT assessment. Larger multicenter studies are needed.

Title: Effects of angiotensin receptor blockers on aortic growth and clinical events in Marfan syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a major cause of aortic dissection and premature mortality in Marfan syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome. We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, and Web of Science through February 1, 2025. Acute aortic dissection and all-cause mortality were the primary outcomes. Binary outcomes were analyzed using both Mantel-Haenszel common-effect (MH-CE) and inverse-variance random-effects (IV-RE) models. For outcomes with an event incidence below 10% in every contributing study, the MH-CE estimate was emphasized and the IV-RE estimate was treated as a sensitivity analysis. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using IV-RE models. All analyses were conducted with the meta package in R (v4.3.2). Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1522 patients with Marfan syndrome were included in the main analysis. For acute aortic dissection, the MH-CE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·24-1·59) and the IV-RE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·20-1·92). For all-cause mortality, the corresponding estimates were RR 0·53 (95% CI 0·17-1·64) and RR 0·58 (95% CI 0·16-2·07). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. ARBs were associated with less aortic-root growth measured by MRI (MD - 0·48 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·89 to - 0·08) and by echocardiography over 3 years (MD - 0·51 mm/3 years, 95% CI - 0·85 to - 0·17), whereas annual echocardiographic measurement showed no significant difference (MD - 0·06 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·22 to 0·10). No significant effect was observed on ascending-aortic diameter, aortic Z-score at 3 years, aortic surgery, or serious adverse events. No statistically significant effect modification was detected in exploratory subgroup analyses. In patients with Marfan syndrome, ARB therapy was associated with small reductions in aortic-root growth in selected imaging analyses but did not significantly reduce acute aortic dissection or all-cause mortality. Sparse events, wide confidence intervals, and limited follow-up preclude firm conclusions regarding clinical benefit. Adequately powered, long-term trials with standardized imaging and clinical outcomes are required.

Title: Disproportionality analysis of ventricular extrasystoles reported with semaglutide in VigiBase and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System.
Abstract: Semaglutide is widely used to treat type 2 diabetes and obesity and to reduce cardiovascular risk. However, its association with cardiac rhythm-related adverse-event reporting in routine clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. To investigate cardiovascular and rhythm-related adverse-event reporting associated with semaglutide, with a focus on ventricular extrasystoles, we conducted a disproportionality analysis of individual case safety reports from VigiBase and the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS; formerly the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System [FAERS]). Reports were included when semaglutide was recorded as a suspected drug, according to database-specific criteria. Cardiovascular outcomes were identified using Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Preferred Terms. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. A cross-database reporting signal was defined as at least three semaglutide-associated reports and a lower 95% CI bound exceeding 1 in each database. After deduplication and application of the predefined inclusion criteria, 1980 semaglutide-associated cardiovascular reports from VigiBase and 1754 from AEMS were included. Among the screened cardiovascular and rhythm-related preferred terms, ventricular extrasystoles was the only term that met the prespecified signal criterion in both databases. Ventricular extrasystoles, clinically corresponding to premature ventricular contractions, showed disproportionate reporting in VigiBase (ROR 1.77, 95% CI 1.31-2.40) and AEMS (ROR 1.37, 95% CI 1.00-1.88; unrounded lower CI bound > 1). Ventricular extrasystoles showed a consistent disproportionality signal across VigiBase and AEMS. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish incidence, causality, or prognostic significance, this finding warrants prospective investigation using systematic electrocardiographic assessment and ambulatory rhythm monitoring.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Clustering of Clinical Phenotypes in Adults With Bicuspid Aortic Valve: A Large Single-Center Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is clinically heterogeneous, and the relationships among valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, and aortic involvement remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify clinical phenotypes of adults with BAV by clustering multidimensional clinical data, primarily echocardiographic parameters.
METHODS: We retrospectively included adults with echocardiographically confirmed BAV at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2016 and December 2024. Data from the first echocardiographic examination and contemporaneous clinical records were extracted, and nine continuous and three categorical variables were entered into a two-step clustering model. Continuous and categorical variables were compared across clusters using the Kruskal-Wallis H test and chi-square test, respectively, followed by pairwise comparisons. The stability of the four-cluster solution was assessed using 100 bootstrap resamples; agreement was quantified with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) and Jaccard coefficients.
