Clustering was also repeated after separately excluding sex and valve dysfunction to assess the influence of these key variables on cluster structure.
RESULTS: A total of 6977 patients with echocardiographically diagnosed BAV were included. The median age was 53.0 years (interquartile range, 40.0-61.0), and 70.0% were men. Two-step clustering identified four clinical phenotypes that differed significantly in valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, aortic dimensions, left-heart remodeling, cardiac function, and surgical interventions (all p < 0.001): Cluster 1, a predominantly male, regurgitation-predominant phenotype with left ventricular dilatation; Cluster 2, a predominantly male, stenosis-predominant phenotype with concentric hypertrophy; Cluster 3, a male phenotype with no or mild valve dysfunction; and Cluster 4, a female phenotype characterized mainly by no or mild valve dysfunction with a tendency toward stenosis. The proportion undergoing subsequent surgery after the baseline echocardiographic assessment was highest in Cluster 2 (40%) and lowest in Cluster 3 (14%). Left ventricular end-systolic diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, aortic root diameter, valve dysfunction, and sex were the principal drivers of clustering. Across bootstrap resamples, the mean ARI for the four-cluster solution was 0.696. In sensitivity analyses, exclusion of either sex or valve dysfunction reduced the optimal solution from four clusters to two.
CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning-based two-step clustering identified four baseline clinical phenotypes among adults with BAV, revealing multidimensional combinations of valve morphology, valvular function, aortic dimensions, and left-heart remodeling. This classification is intended primarily to characterize the clinical heterogeneity of adult BAV; its longitudinal clinical value requires confirmation in independent prospective cohorts.

Title: Comparison of Spinal Anesthesia Against General Anesthesia for Surgical Management of Hip Fracture Patients: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Journal: Journal of perianesthesia nursing : official journal of the American Society of PeriAnesthesia Nurses
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Hip fracture surgery in older adults is associated with substantial perioperative morbidity and functional decline. Whether spinal anesthesia offers advantages over general anesthesia for key perioperative complications and recovery outcomes remains uncertain. Hence, we conducted this review comparing spinal anesthesia versus general anesthesia for surgical management of hip fracture.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
METHODS: Databases [MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science, and clinical trial registries] were searched till January 2026. Primary outcomes were major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular complications, delirium, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), hypotension, pain score, and functional recovery. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) were performed using risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.
FINDINGS: Nineteen trials were included. Spinal anesthesia showed no significant difference versus general anesthesia for major cardiovascular/cerebrovascular complications (RR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.69 to 1.20), delirium (RR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.81 to 1.21), PONV (RR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.60 to 1.58), and hypotension (RR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.58 to 1.50), with substantial heterogeneity for hypotension. Spinal anesthesia was associated with improved functional recovery (SMD = -0.49, 95% CI: -0.76 to -0.22) and lower pain scores (SMD = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.68 to -0.38), though these outcomes were informed by few trials. Publication bias was suggested for cardiovascular/cerebrovascular complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, no clear superiority was observed between spinal and general anesthesia for hip fracture surgery. Limited evidence suggests potential improvements in short-term pain and functional recovery with spinal anesthesia; however, these findings are based on a small number of studies and require confirmation in future well-designed trials.

Title: Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients.
METHODS: This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP.
RESULTS: Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

Title: Characteristics and Thresholds of Coronary Lesions to Predict Acute Coronary Syndrome From Artificial Intelligence-Guided Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Characteristics of future culprit lesions according to artificial intelligence-guided quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to characterize and derive thresholds to predict future culprit lesions from coronary computed tomography angiography using AI-QCT.
METHODS: A total of 2,169 patients/13,772 lesions undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography at Turku University Hospital, Finland, (derivation) and 553 patients/3,948 lesions from Amsterdam University Medical Center, the Netherlands, (validation) were analyzed with AI-QCT. Lesions from vessels undergoing early revascularization were excluded. Lesion-level total plaque volume (TPV) and noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV) thresholds were derived and externally validated to predict lesion-level and patient-level acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
RESULTS: Future culprit lesions from both cohorts (n = 69 validation; n = 15 derivation) had consistently higher median TPV (101 mm3 validation; 115 mm3 derivation; P = 0.811) and NCPV (65 mm3 validation; 74 mm3 derivation; P = 0.709) compared with control lesions (P < 0.001) and were nonobstructive in 69.6% (derivation) and 40.0% (validation). Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived and associated with significantly higher adjusted rates of lesion-level (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 12.09; 95% CI: 6.95-21.04; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 10.82; 95% CI: 6.22-18.80; P < 0.001) and patient-level ACS (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 2.92; 95% CI: 1.65-5.16; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 5.11; 95% CI: 2.49-10.46; P < 0.001) with consistent results in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Future culprit lesions vs nonculprit lesions by AI-QCT demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes and were nonobstructive in 40% to 70%. Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived to predict future culprit lesions and associated with increased rates of lesion-level and patient-level ACS in 2 independent cohorts.

Title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.
METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.
RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

Title: Integrated Multidisciplinary Post-Discharge Follow-Up in a Colombian Cardiovascular Referral Center: Real-World Implementation and Outcomes.
Journal: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The post-discharge period is vulnerable because gaps in continuity of care may increase adverse outcomes. This study aimed to describe the implementation of a structured post-discharge follow-up program and the outcomes observed during follow-up at a specialised cardiovascular referral centre in Colombia.
METHODS: We conducted a cohort study of patients enrolled in an institutional prospective post-discharge follow-up program between 2023 and 2025. Trained personnel conducted standardized telephone follow-up at predefined intervals up to 12 months, assessing vital status, readmissions, post-discharge events, outpatient follow-up, and health-related quality of life. Outcomes were summarized descriptively.
RESULTS: Of 34,564 identified patients, we included 25,232 (73.0%). Men comprised 54.2% of the cohort. Follow-up completion was 18,876/19,086 (98.9%) at one month and 3,861/5,720 (67.5%) at 12 months. At the one-month follow-up, all-cause readmission to the study institution occurred in 2,141/25,232 patients (8.5%). Cumulative mortality was 191/19,086 (1.0%) at one month, 467/13,749 (3.4%) at six months, and 240/5,720 (4.2%) at 12 months. Median EQ-VAS increased from 70 (IQR 61-80) at baseline to 85 (IQR 75-90) at 12 months; worsening was most frequent in pain/discomfort [1,653/5,720 (28.9%)] and anxiety/depression [986/5,720 (17.2%)].
CONCLUSION: This large-scale program enabled structured post-discharge follow-up and systematic collection of clinically relevant outcomes, with high completion at early scheduled assessments and lower completion at longer-term assessments.

Title: Protective effects of pramipexole on testicular torsion and detorsion injury in rats.
Journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testicular torsion induces ischemia-reperfusion injury, which is predominantly mediated by oxidative stress and inflammatory cascades. Pramipexole, a pharmacological agent widely used in neurological practice, possesses potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties. The aim of this experimental study was to evaluate the potential protective effects of pramipexole on testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury using a rat model of testicular torsion-detorsion, through both biochemical and histopathological analyses.
METHODS: A total of 18 male rats were randomly divided into three groups. Group 1 was designated as the control group. In Group 2, only a testicular torsion-detorsion model was established to evaluate testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury. In Group 3, a similar torsion-detorsion model was created. In addition, rats in this group received intraperitoneal pramipexole (0.5 mg/kg) immediately after testicular detorsion. The aim was to assess the effects of pramipexole on testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury. At the end of the experiment, blood samples were collected for biochemical analyses, and orchiectomy was performed for histopathological evaluation of testicular tissues.
RESULTS: Biochemical analyses showed that malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were significantly increased in Group 2 compared with the other groups (p<0.001). Similarly, tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-1beta levels were significantly higher in Group 2 than in the other groups (p<0.001). In Group 3, both pro-inflammatory cytokine levels and MDA levels were significantly reduced compared with Group 2 (p<0.001). Furthermore, glutathione peroxidase and superoxide dismutase activities were significantly increased in Group 3 compared with Group 2 (p=0.002 and p<0.001, respectively). Histopathological evaluation revealed a significant improvement in all testicular damage scores, including vasocongestion, inflammation, and edema, in Group 3 compared with Group 2 (p<0.001). Likewise, the mean Johnsen score in Group 3 was calculated as 8.37±0.62, which was significantly higher than that observed in Group 2 (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Pramipexole appears to be an effective pharmacological agent in alleviating the effects of testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury.

Title: Transcatheter Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
NMR-Derived Metabolic Profiles Associated with Incident Acute Myocardial Infarction and Pre-Diagnostic Metabolic Trajectories in the UK Biobank.
Abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cardiovascular event, yet the metabolic signatures that precede its onset and their value for long-term risk prediction remain incompletely characterized. Using NMR metabolomics data from 271 430 UK Biobank participants without baseline AMI, this study evaluated 168 absolute metabolite measures in relation to incident AMI. Cox proportional hazards models identified 60 AMI-associated metabolites after adjustment for conventional risk factors, and CatBoost modeling with SHAP interpretation and forward selection further defined eight metabolite profiles, including glycine, albumin, glycoprotein acetyls, creatinine, triglycerides in large LDL, free cholesterol in chylomicrons and extremely large VLDL (XXL-VLDL-FC), cholesteryl esters in IDL, and cholesteryl esters in HDL. Integrating these metabolite profiles with conventional risk factors modestly improved 10-year AMI discrimination in both machine learning and survival models, with a CatBoost AUC of 0.741 and a Cox C index of 0.761 in validation analyses. SHAP analyses suggested sex- and age-related heterogeneity in metabolite contributions, particularly for HDL-related and inflammatory traits. A nested case-control trajectory analysis showed persistently lower levels of glycine and albumin, and higher levels of glycoprotein acetyls, large LDL triglycerides, and creatinine during the decade before diagnosis. This study identifies NMR-derived metabolic patterns associated with AMI risk and provides a basis for further investigation of their potential contributions to metabolomics-informed cardiovascular risk assessment.

Title: Development and Temporal Validation of a Thromboelastography-Based Nomogram for Queensland-Defined High Thrombotic Risk in Postpartum Women.
Abstract: This study developed and temporally validated a nomogram that integrates thromboelastography (TEG) and maternal clinical factors to identify women classified as having high thrombotic risk according to the 2020 Queensland Clinical Guideline at postpartum reassessment after 24 h. The derivation cohort included 447 women who delivered at Foshan Women and Children Hospital between January 1, 2021, and December 27, 2022; 346 had Queensland scores of 0-2 and 101 had scores of ≥3. A same-center temporal validation cohort included 207 women who delivered between December 28, 2022, and February 14, 2025. Candidate clinical and TEG variables were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, and model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, and decision curve analysis. The final model retained hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, maternal age, current body mass index, native-cup TEG reaction time (R), and 24-h postpartum blood loss. Discrimination was acceptable in the derivation cohort (area under the curve [AUC], 0.791; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.737-0.845; sensitivity, 70.3%; specificity, 77.2%) and good in the temporal validation cohort (AUC, 0.847; 95% CI, 0.771-0.923; sensitivity, 75.8%; specificity, 85.6%). The model estimates Queensland-defined high thrombotic risk rather than objectively confirmed venous thromboembolism. It may support simplified postpartum reassessment after the first 24 h, but multicenter validation against objectively confirmed thrombotic outcomes is required before claims regarding event prediction or clinical implementation can be made.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Video-Audio Media; Validation Study

Title: Network Pharmacology, Machine Learning, and Molecular Docking Analysis of Changluo Tiaogan Dinghun Decoction for Coronary Heart Disease with Anxiety.
Abstract: Coronary heart disease (CHD) and anxiety disorder frequently coexist, highlighting the need to investigate their potentially shared molecular mechanisms. Conventional therapeutic approaches have limitations, while traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a potential multitarget strategy. Changluo Tiaogan Dinghun decoction (CLTGDHD) was developed for qi stagnation and blood stasis. This computational study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking to investigate the potential compounds and molecular targets of CLTGDHD relevant to CHD with anxiety disorder. Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets GSE100927 and GSE61672 were analyzed separately to identify disease-associated genes. GSE100927 comprises peripheral-artery atherosclerosis samples and was used as a surrogate for atherosclerosis-related processes relevant to CHD, whereas GSE61672 represents an anxiety disorder cohort. The resulting candidate genes were evaluated using a machine-learning prioritization workflow, which identified protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type C (PTPRC) as the sole retained gene. Molecular docking using the AlphaFold-predicted PTPRC structure (AF-P08575-4-F1) yielded predicted binding affinities ranging from -5.985 to -6.827 kcal/mol for five selected compounds. These findings suggest potential molecular interactions relevant to the investigated disease processes but do not establish therapeutic efficacy or a CHD-specific mechanism. Because the transcriptomic datasets represent separate populations rather than a clinically defined cohort with both CHD and anxiety disorder, the findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Further validation using appropriately defined clinical datasets and experimental models is required.

Title: Coronary artery disease and cardiac pathology in cerebral small vessel disease and post-stroke dementia: Implications for Alzheimer's disease.
Journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationships between coronary or cardiac pathology, cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), Alzheimer's disease pathology, and vascular cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID) remain unclear.
METHODS: We performed a clinicopathological study in 75 stroke patients enrolled in the prospective Cognitive Function After Stroke (CogFAST) cohort. Comprehensive histopathological examination was performed to characterize the spectrum of pathologies in samples of the main coronary arteries (CorA), and cardiac and brain tissues from stroke survivors diagnosed with post-stroke dementia (PSD; mean age, standard deviation, range, % sex; 88 ± 8 years, 65-99, 55% female) or without dementia (PSND; 86 ± 4 years, 79-94, 45% female).
RESULTS: All subjects exhibited occult or obstructive CorA disease with > 50% clinically defined stenosis in at least one of the main coronary arteries. Linear correlation analysis showed that CorA stenosis was positively related to internal carotid artery stenosis (P < 0.03). CorA stenosis was not associated with pathological measures of cerebral SVD per se or neurodegenerative disorders. Cardiac pathology was highly prevalent, with ≈ 80% of the subjects having at least one feature of cardiac pathology including fibrosis, disarray, and myocyte damage and 62% exhibiting myocardial infarcts. CorA stenosis was associated with higher cardiac pathology score, which was also related to cardiac sympathetic denervation and α-synuclein accumulation in the stellate ganglia. We noted low heart weights (P < 0.001), greater myocardial infarcts (P < 0.001), and greater general cardiac atrophy (P = 0.024) in the PSD compared to the PSND group.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest there is a relationship between CorA disease and carotid artery disease and that cardiac pathology in elderly stroke survivors may be a factor in the development of delayed dementia after the stroke injury and VCID.

Title: Role of protein lactylation in pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases: Current research and future perspectives (Review).
Abstract: The cardiopulmonary system is highly coupled in structure and function. Metabolic and epigenetic disturbances constitute the common pathological basis for the progression of cardiopulmonary diseases and their comorbidities. Aberrant metabolic reprogramming triggers lactate accumulation. As a novel post-translational modification, protein lactylation participates in the regulation of inflammatory responses, cell death and fibrotic remodeling, thereby mediating cardiopulmonary dysfunction. Existing studies have separately illustrated the roles of lactylation in isolated pulmonary and cardiac disorders. Nevertheless, most investigations are confined to a single-organ perspective, lacking systematic summaries of common mechanisms for cardiopulmonary crosstalk and comorbidities. The present review summarized research advances of lactylation in various cardiopulmonary diseases, generalized its potential comorbid mechanisms, identified existing research gaps and translational obstacles for targeted therapy and collected lactylation-targeted intervention compounds with potential therapeutic effects reported in basic studies. The present review further outlined prospective research directions focused on spatiotemporal regulation of lactylation, metabolic-immune-epigenetic crosstalk that shapes disease progression, and the identification of specific targets in cardiopulmonary comorbidities, with the aim of providing a theoretical foundation for developing precise, broad-spectrum, co-targeted therapeutic strategies for cardiopulmonary diseases.

Title: Neurorehabilitation as an Opportunity for Structured Post-Stroke Lipid Management: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Background and PurposeIschemic stroke remains a major cause of death, disability, and recurrent vascular events worldwide. Although lipid-lowering therapy is central to secondary prevention, the transition between acute stroke care and long-term outpatient management remains a vulnerable period during which guideline-directed treatment is frequently delayed, undertitrated, or discontinued. Neurorehabilitation may provide an important opportunity to address this gap. This narrative review summarizes evidence supporting intensive low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction after ischemic stroke and examines how the neurorehabilitation setting may facilitate optimized lipid management.MethodsA literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through March 2026, combining terms across three domains: (1) ischemic stroke and secondary prevention, (2) lipid-lowering therapy, and (3) neurorehabilitation and functional recovery. Included study types encompassed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews with meta-analyses, clinical practice guidelines, observational cohort and preclinical studies addressing statin pleiotropic effects. Priority was given to landmark randomized trials, major society guidelines, and studies with direct relevance to recurrent stroke prevention, hemorrhagic risk stratification, and rehabilitation-based care delivery.ResultsEvidence from SPARCL, Treat Stroke to Target, FOURIER, and Ez PAVE shows that intensive LDL-C reduction improves secondary stroke prevention. Statins may also affect neuroinflammation, endothelial function, blood-brain barrier integrity, and neuroplasticity, with differences in hemorrhagic stroke risk and safety profiles compared with PCSK9 inhibitors.ConclusionAlthough direct rehabilitation-based randomized trials are lacking, integrating supervised medication titration, adherence monitoring, neuroimaging-guided risk stratification, and patient-centered secondary prevention strategies into neurorehabilitation may represent a practical approach for strengthening secondary stroke prevention and reducing recurrent vascular events.

Title: Early childhood blood pressure in relation to umbilical cord homocysteine and folate: insights from the ENVIRonmental influence ON AGEing birth cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High blood pressure (BP) tracks from childhood into adulthood, contributing to cardiovascular risk. How the prenatal one-carbon (1-C) metabolism, as reflected by umbilical cord homocysteine and folate, affects BP in early childhood is unknown.
METHODS: The prospective population-based birth cohort ENVIRonmental influence ON early﻿AGEing (ENVIRONAGE) comprised 500 mother-offspring pairs. Umbilical cord and maternal homocysteine and folate were measured by electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. The association of the offspring BP and risk of high BP was assessed by linear and logistic regression and by mediation analysis. Association sizes were expressed per doubling of the biomarkers and adjusted for the children's sex, age and weight and maternal age at delivery and parity.
RESULTS: At 4.5  years (median), cord homocysteine was associated with higher diastolic and mean BP (MBP), but not SBP with association sizes of 1.67  mmHg [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.36-2.99] and 1.19  mmHg (0.01-2.38), respectively. The odds ratio for high childhood DBP with normotension as reference was 2.22 (1.34-3.68). Associations of BP with cord folate were not significant. Cord folate had only an indirect effect on DBP and MBP with effect sizes amounting to -3.04 (P = 0.027) and -2.30 (P = 0.061)  mmHg. Maternal biomarkers were not associated with the offspring's BP.
CONCLUSION: In this prospective birth cohort study, higher cord plasma homocysteine was associated with higher DBP in early childhood, whereas cord folate was only via homocysteine associated with the offspring's BP. The 1-C metabolism provides a mechanism for preventing high BP in childhood, which is a forerunner of hypertension in adolescence and adulthood.

Title: Electrocardiographic markers of arrhythmic risk after renal sympathetic denervation in resistant hypertension.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Renal sympathetic denervation (RDN) has emerged as a device-based therapy for resistant hypertension; however, its effects on electrocardiographic (ECG) markers related to arrhythmic risk remain incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate changes in ECG indices reflecting atrial and ventricular electrical heterogeneity in patients undergoing RDN compared to medically treated controls.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 263 patients with resistant hypertension (RDN+, n = 120; RDN-, n = 143) with baseline and 6-month ECG recordings. ECG parameters included the P-wave dispersion, Tp-Te interval, and frontal QRS-T angle. To account for baseline differences, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPW) based on propensity scores was applied. Weighted linear regression models with doubly robust adjustment were used to estimate the independent association between RDN and follow-up ECG parameters after adjusting for baseline ECG values and change in SBP.
RESULTS: At 6 months, patients undergoing RDN demonstrated significantly lower P-wave dispersion (27.4 vs. 37.5 ms, P < 0.001), Tp-Te interval (80.3 vs. 84.7 ms, P = 0.028), and frontal QRS-T angle (26 vs. 37°, P = 0.026) compared with controls. In the weighted models, RDN remained independently associated with reductions in these parameters.
CONCLUSION: In patients with resistant hypertension, renal sympathetic denervation was associated with improvements in ECG markers related to arrhythmic risk at 6 months, which were not fully explained by changes in office SBP.

Title: Clinical Characteristics of Lymph-Node-First Presentation of Kawasaki Disease: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lymph-node-first presentation of Kawasaki disease (NFKD) initially manifests as fever and cervical lymphadenopathy, mimicking bacterial cervical lymphadenitis (BCL). However, studies of diagnostic markers have yielded inconsistent results, and data from Japanese cohorts remain limited.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 151 patients with Kawasaki disease (KD) (typical KD [tKD], n = 104; NFKD, n = 47) and 21 patients with BCL. We compared clinical characteristics, pretreatment laboratory values, and imaging findings among the tKD, NFKD, and BCL groups.
RESULTS: Compared with BCL, NFKD was associated with older age, higher C-reactive protein, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels, and lower albumin levels. Patients with BCL had higher white blood cell (WBC) and platelet counts and more frequent imaging findings suggestive of abscess formation. Multivariable analysis showed that older age, elevated AST levels, hypoalbuminemia, and lower WBC count were factors associated with NFKD. Receiver operating characteristic analysis yielded exploratory cutoff values of age ≥ 29 months, WBC ≤ 13.02 × 103/μL, AST ≥ 35 U/L, and albumin ≤ 3.8 g/dL. Compared with tKD, patients with NFKD were older, had a longer interval from symptom onset to diagnosis, and a higher rate of incomplete KD. Coronary artery involvement and intravenous immunoglobulin responsiveness were similar between the two KD groups.
CONCLUSIONS: NFKD is a KD phenotype that mimics BCL in its local presentation but shares clinical features with tKD. In children with fever and cervical lymphadenopathy, older age, modest leukocytosis, elevated AST levels, and hypoalbuminemia may help raise clinical suspicion for NFKD.

Title: Biomarker Testing, Imaging, and Outcomes in Cardiology-Referred Acute Breathlessness: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.
Abstract: Background Breathlessness is a leading cause of emergency hospital attendances, and its multifactorial nature often reflects overlapping cardiopulmonary pathologies such as pulmonary embolism (PE), heart failure (HF), and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is frequently used, often without documented pretest probability assessments. This audit primarily assessed the diagnostic yield of CTPA for suspected PE against the Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standard of ≥15% and secondarily described biomarker testing, imaging, and outcomes across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways in patients referred to cardiology with acute breathlessness. Methods We conducted a retrospective audit of 70 adults referred to cardiology with breathlessness through the electronic patient record or multiprofessional team list (MPTL) referral systems at a district general hospital in the United Kingdom between March 1 and June 30, 2025. Biomarker testing for D-dimer, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hs-TnI), together with imaging and outcomes, was reviewed and described across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways, with diagnostic yields restricted to CTPA for suspected PE and coronary angiography for suspected ACS. Yields were reported with Wilson 95% CIs and compared using exploratory Fisher's exact tests. Additional analyses examined biomarker concentrations by outcome and overlap in biomarker and imaging use. Results Seventy patients were included (median age, 69.5 years; 52.9% male). D-dimer, NT-proBNP, and hs-TnI were tested in 68.6%, 58.6%, and 81.4% of patients, respectively. Overall, seven of 54 CTPAs performed for suspected PE were positive (13.0%, 95% CI, 6.4-24.4), numerically below the RCR benchmark of ≥15%. A clinically relevant alternative diagnosis was reported in 44.4% (target, ≥50%), and pretest probability was documented in 22.2% (target, 100%). PE yield was 15.0% (6/40) among patients with an elevated D-dimer, 0% (0/4) among those with a normal D-dimer, and 10.0% (1/10) among those without D-dimer testing (p = 1.000 for both comparisons). Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) was found on transthoracic echocardiography in 40.0% (8/20) of patients with elevated NT-proBNP, 23.1% (3/13) of those with non-elevated NT-proBNP, and 26.3% (5/19) of those without testing (p = 0.456 and p = 0.501, respectively). Of 47 patients with elevated hs-TnI, 10 (21.3%) underwent coronary angiography for suspected ACS, with percutaneous coronary intervention performed in four (40.0%). Overall, 29 of 57 patients tested (50.9%) had hs-TnI levels above the sex-specific 99th-percentile upper reference limit. Conclusions Cardiology-referred breathlessness frequently involved multiple biomarker and imaging pathways during the same admission. CTPA yield, alternative diagnosis rates, and pretest probability documentation fell below RCR standards. LVSD was more frequent with elevated NT-proBNP, although differences were not statistically significant. No hs-TnI comparison was possible because all patients undergoing angiography for suspected ACS had elevated levels. Given the small, single-center sample and selective imaging, these findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy or pathway effectiveness. Larger multicenter studies are needed. The findings support reviewing pretest probability documentation and investigation decisions, followed by reaudit against RCR standards.

Title: Development and Validation of A Frusemide Card to Guide Self-Titration of Oral Frusemide in the Outpatient Setting.
Journal: The Malaysian journal of medical sciences : MJMS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) causes frequent hospitalisations due to fluid congestion. Patient-friendly self-titration tools are scarce. This study developed and validated a "Frusemide Card" to support safe outpatient dose adjustment.
METHODS: This cross-sectional development and validation study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 involved developing the Frusemide Card through evidence-based content construction and graphical design. Phase 2 included content validation by six experts (four cardiologists, two pharmacists) using the Content Validity Index (CVI) and Content Validity Ratio (CVR), followed by face validation among 20 HF patients in two sequential cohorts using the Face Validity Index (FVI). Content validity included four domains: relevance, clarity, essentiality, and patient instructions. Face validation assessed clarity and comprehension to determine overall acceptance.
RESULTS: Expert validation showed perfect agreement for relevance and essentiality (I-CVI, CVR, and S-CVI/UA = 1.00). Clarity for domains 2-4 was acceptable (I-CVI ≥ 0.83), but domain 1 scored lower (I-CVI = 0.50), reducing the universal agreement (S-CVI/UA = 0.25), though average clarity was acceptable (S-CVI/Ave = 0.79). The first patient cohort reported good average clarity (S-FVI/Ave = 0.90) but low universal agreement (S-FVI/UA = 0.25). Following revisions based on feedback, the second patient cohort confirmed excellent clarity and acceptance, achieving perfect validity across all domains (I-FVI and S-FVI = 1.00).
CONCLUSION: The Frusemide Card showed strong content and face validity, suggesting that it could be a useful tool for guiding the safe self-titration of oral frusemide in outpatient HF management.

Title: Heart Failure With Reduced and Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Review of Guideline Directed Medical Therapy.
Journal: The International journal of angiology : official publication of the International College of Angiology, Inc
Abstract: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) are prevalent clinical syndromes associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Although both diagnoses are part of the same spectrum, the underlying pathophysiology and responsiveness to medical therapies differ. HFrEF is characterized by a maladaptive neurohormonal response that results in ventricular remodeling, forming the basis of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) centered traditionally on the four pillars: renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibition, β-blockade, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism (MRA), and sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibition. GDMTs confer robust mortality benefit and heart failure hospitalizations and should be initiated early and in combination, when hemodynamics and end organ function permits. In contrast, HFpEF is driven largely by comorbid associated inflammation, diastolic dysfunction, and elevated ventricular filling pressures, with fewer therapies demonstrating clear mortality benefits. Recent research has established SGLT2 inhibitors as the most consistently effective therapy for HFpEF, with some emerging research on selective use of MRAs and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. This literature review summarizes the current evidence-based pharmacological management strategies for both HFrEF and HFpEF, highlighting differences in guideline recommendations, exploring the therapeutic overlap and ongoing uncertainty. As newer clinical trial data emerge, future guidelines may further refine optimal treatment strategies for the heterogeneity of the heart failure population.

Title: Adverse arrhythmia-related outcomes after catheter ablation in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: a nationwide propensity score-matched cohort study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) have been associated with an increased long-term risk of arrhythmia. However, clinical outcomes following catheter ablation in patients with IBD are unknown.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this nationwide Swiss cohort study of adults undergoing catheter ablation for arrhythmia between 2012 and 2022, patients with IBD were propensity score-matched 1:10 to comparators without IBD. The primary endpoint was a composite of the first occurrence of any of the following events: reablation, cardioversion, or hospitalization for arrhythmia. Secondary endpoints were each individual component of the primary endpoint. An additional win ratio-based hierarchical analysis was performed. Hazard ratios (HRs) and incidence rates (IRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards modelling. A total of 251 patients with IBD and 2429 matched comparators were included in the study. After a median follow-up time of 2.6 years (IQR 0.8-5.6), the primary endpoint occurred in 81 (32.3%, IR: 100.8/1000 person-years) patients with IBD and in 640 (26.3%, IR: 73.3/1000 person-years) matched comparators, yielding an HR of 1.30 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.03-1.64]. Among the individual components of the primary endpoint, hospitalization for arrhythmia was more frequent in patients with IBD (HR 1.29, 95% CI = 1.02-1.64), while the remaining components did not differ between groups. In hierarchical win ratio analysis, patients with IBD had worse composite outcomes than matched comparators (win ratio 0.80, 95% CI = 0.65-0.99, P = 0.04).
CONCLUSION: Patients with IBD undergoing catheter ablation exhibited 30% higher hazards of adverse arrhythmia-related outcomes.

Title: Chronic Chagas Cardiomyopathy at a Peruvian National Referral Hospital: A Case Series.
Journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the cardiovascular manifestations and clinical course of patients with chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy at a Peruvian national hospital.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Descriptive retrospective case series (2021-2025). Nine patients with serologically confirmed Trypanosoma cruzi infection were assessed by electrocardiography, echocardiography, and/or 24-hour Holter monitoring; a predominant cardiovascular phenotype was assigned to each.
RESULTS: The mean age was 50.1 ± 6.8 years; 55.6% were male, and 66.7% came from the Peruvian Amazon. The heart failure phenotype predominated (55.6%), with ejection fractions of 15-39%, followed by ventricular arrhythmias (22.2%) and conduction disorders (22.2%). Two patients (22.2%) received permanent pacemakers, one (11.1%) received an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, and two (22.2%) died.
CONCLUSIONS: The three classic phenotypes coexisted, with advanced disease at diagnosis. Chagas disease should be considered cases of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy or conduction disorders.

Title: Multimodality imaging for the detection of cardiotoxicity in cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Abstract:
AIMS: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) may cause cardiotoxicity, mainly myocarditis, with potential life-threatening consequences. To date, large-scale prospective data on cardiac imaging after ICI are still lacking. Thus, our primary aim was to assess the diagnostic value of speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) for ICI-related cardiotoxicity according to current international recommendations, while our secondary aims were to assess the prognostic value of STE for adverse clinical outcome and evaluate the agreement between STE and CMR in patients with ICI-related myocarditis.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective study, cancer patients referred for cardiologic evaluation before ICIs initiation were enrolled. Patients with known cardiac dysfunction (LV ejection fraction < 40%) were excluded. All patients underwent clinical, biohumoral and echocardiographic evaluation completed by STE at baseline and at ∼6 months after immunotherapy. Patients with suspected myocarditis underwent CMR. Then, over a longer follow up, the clinical events were registered: all-cause or cardiovascular death, acute myocarditis, acute heart failure, pulmonary embolisms, acute coronary syndromes, atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, extra-cardiac toxicity. We enrolled 122 patients (65 ± 14 years) referred for ICIs. Over 7 ± 6 months follow up, mean LV GLS showed a slight reduction after therapy with ICI (-20 ± 4% at baseline vs. -18 ± 7%), although remaining within the normal ranges. During 22 ± 17 months of follow up, 65 patients developed events. Among ICI-related myocarditis, 4 patients showed a significant reduction of GLS with a regional distribution similar to regional myocardial injury at CMR (97 ± 7% agreement), the fifth had a minimal involvement of the right ventricle, with normal LV GLS.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that multimodality imaging combining different techniques may optimize the subclinical diagnosis of cardiotoxicity and the overall management of cancer patients undergoing ICIs.

Title: [Not Available].
Abstract: The AIFA (Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco) monitoring registries represent one of the most distinctive regulatory tools within the Italian pharmaceutical governance framework. Initially introduced to support the appropriate use of reimbursed medicines and pharmaceutical expenditure control, they have progressively evolved into an infrastructure linking access to medicines, reimbursement governance, managed entry agreements (MEAs), and real-world data collection. This article examines the evolution and the policy relevance of AIFA monitoring registries within the Italian Health Technology Assessment framework. Firstly, it outlines the main legislative and regulatory milestones shaping the system, from the establishment of AIFA in 2003 to the publication of the 2024 guideline, which formally defined the criteria for registry activation. Secondly, it describes the main registry types, the criteria guiding their establishment, and the role of MEAs within the monitoring process. Thirdly, it provides an updated overview of the current registry landscape based on recent AIFA lists, identifying 340 closed registries (March 2026) and 366 active registries (April 2026), with “registri propriamente detti” (comprehensive registries) representing the predominant tool. Among those registries, MEAs were applied in nearly half of cases, with payment by result being the commonest scheme. The article also reviews the use of registry-derived data in peer-reviewed studies across hematology, oncology, cardiovascular diseases, and infectious diseases. Finally, it discusses key challenges, including duplication of information, limited interoperability with healthcare databases, administrative burden and residual discretion in registry activation despite recent transparency reforms. Overall, AIFA monitoring registries emerge as a strategic interface between pharmaceutical regulation, reimbursement governance, and evidence generation.

Title: Genotypic and phenotypic characterization of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy at the Sociedad de Cirugía de Bogotá - Hospital de San José, Bogotá, 2023-2025.
Journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterise the clinical, imaging, and genetic profile of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy treated at a university hospital in Bogotá between 2023 and 2025. To propose an institutional pathway for multimodal assessment and family screening, informed by the study findings and expert opinion.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional observational study of adults treated at a university hospital, reported in accordance with the STROBE guidelines. We reviewed 182 medical records identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes. After excluding 120 duplicate, repeated, incomplete, insufficient, or ineligible records, a convenience sample of 62 patients was included. Clinical, family history, imaging, and genetic variables were analysed using descriptive statistics and unadjusted exploratory comparisons according to genetic test results.
RESULTS: The median age was 69 years (interquartile range [IQR]: 46-75), and 50% of patients were women. Hypertension was the most common comorbidity (51.6%), and two patients had amyloidosis (3.2%). Asymmetrical septal hypertrophy was the predominant morphological pattern (27 of 46 patients; 58.7%). Both echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging were available for 46.8% of patients. Median late gadolinium enhancement was 12%, and extensive fibrosis was observed in 6.5%. Genetic testing results were available for 47 patients (75.8%), of whom 10.6% had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. A family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was more common in this group (p<0.001), which also had a higher left ventricular outflow tract gradient, a greater frequency of obstruction of 50 mmHg or more, systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve, and a higher left ventricular ejection fraction. Because only five patients had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, these comparisons were interpreted as exploratory.
CONCLUSIONS: . The cohort showed clinical, imaging, and genetic heterogeneity, with a high prevalence of hypertension and the presence of infiltrative phenocopies. These findings support the implementation of an institutional pathway integrating family pedigree assessment, echocardiography with strain imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging with fibrosis quantification, clinical genetic evaluation, and family screening.

Title: Bloodstream Infections After Cardiac Surgery: Pathogen Distribution, Antimicrobial Resistance, and a Nomogram Prediction Model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative bloodstream infection (BSI) is a severe complication following cardiac surgery, associated with significant mortality. This study aims to characterize pathogen profiles, antimicrobial resistance and independent risk factors for BSI in a Chinese cardiac surgery cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of postoperative BSI in patients who underwent cardiac surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from January 2019 to December 2024. Patients who developed postoperative BSI were identified and a 1:1 propensity score matched analysis were performed to adjust for baseline characteristics of patients. Univariate and multivariate analysis were applied to identify independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. R software was used to construct a prediction nomogram, followed by internal validation.
RESULTS: During the study, a total of 10,007 patients underwent heart surgery, and 164 pairs of patients were successfully matched using propensity score matching. Gram-negative bacteria were the most common pathogens (64.1%), followed by Fungi (18.2%) and Gram-positive bacteria (17.6%). Among Enterobacterales, 33.8% were carbapenem-resistant, with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) accounting for 63.6% of K. pneumoniae isolates. Meanwhile, 85.0% (17/20) of A. baumannii isolates were multidrug-resistant A. baumannii (MDRAB). The 90-day mortality rate in the BSI group was 39.0%, significantly higher than that in the non-BSI group (4.9%, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified impaired cardiac function (New York Heart Association II-IV, NYHA II-IV) (OR=5.583, 95% CI:2.681-11.627), pulmonary infection (OR =4.053, 95% CI:1.692-9.710), emergency surgery (OR=9.629, 95% CI:2.962-31.301), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (OR=2.796, 95% CI:1.096-7.134), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT Postoperative ICU stay ≥ 14 d) (OR=4.758, 95% CI:1.854-12.211) and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d (OR=14.616, 95% CI:6.765-31.577) as independent risk factors for postoperative BSI. The nomogram showed good discrimination and calibration after internal validation, with an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.913 and a mean absolute calibration error of 0.026.
CONCLUSION: Postoperative BSI in cardiac surgery patients is associated with high mortality. A nomogram based on impaired cardiac function (NYHA II-IV), pulmonary infection, emergency surgery, CABG, CRRT and postoperative ICU stay ≥14 d displayed high accuracy and consistency in predicting the risk of postoperative BSI. These results facilitate early risk stratification and guide preventive strategies in high-risk cardiac surgical patients.

Title: Pump-Predicted Ciprofol Ce50 for Suppressing the Cardiovascular Response to Tracheal Intubation During Fixed Sufentanil-Esketamine Induction: An Age-Stratified Dixon Up-and-Down Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the ciprofol pump-predicted effect-site target concentration associated with a 50% probability of suppressing the cardiovascular response to tracheal intubation (Ce50) during fixed sufentanil-esketamine induction in two age cohorts.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, age-stratified Dixon up-and-down study, 53 adults undergoing elective surgery received sufentanil 0.3 μg/kg, esketamine 0.3 mg/kg, and ciprofol effect-site target-controlled infusion (TCI). Independent cohorts aged 45-64 and 65-79 years started at a pump-predicted target concentration (Ce) of 1.10 μg/mL, adjusted in 0.05 μg/mL steps. Ce50 was estimated by reversal-pair midpoints and Probit analysis. The trial was registered on March 31, 2026 (ChiCTR2600121464).
RESULTS: Thirty-two middle-aged and 21 older adults were analyzed. Midpoint Ce50 was 0.975 μg/mL (approximate 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.910-1.040) and 1.096 μg/mL (1.072-1.121), respectively. Probit Ce50 was 0.991 μg/mL (95% CI, 0.773-1.103) and 1.112 μg/mL (1.078-1.152). At target Ce, mean arterial pressure fell by 19.2% ± 11.0% and 22.5% ± 12.5% from baseline. Hypotension occurred in 20/32 (62.5%) and 13/21 (61.9%) participants.
CONCLUSION: These exploratory Ce50 estimates are specific to the CONCERT-III pump model and the studied co-induction and rescue protocol in small, nonrandomized cohorts at a single center. Frequent hypotension and norepinephrine use accompanied induction. The estimates do not establish an independent age effect or individual dosing targets and require external validation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600121464; prospectively registered March 31, 2026.

Title: Neoadjuvant Nivolumab-Ipilimumab versus Platinum-Based Chemotherapy in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Single-Institution, Propensity-Weighted Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is standard for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), yet many patients are platinum-ineligible. We compared outcomes of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus platinum-based NAC.
METHODS: This single-institution comparative cohort study compared a prospective immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cohort (n=11) receiving nivolumab (1 mg/kg) plus ipilimumab (3 mg/kg) against a retrospective platinum-based NAC cohort (n=30). Propensity score-based overlap weighting was used to reduce measured confounding. Main outcomes included pathologic complete response (pCR), downstaging (<ypT2N0), and overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Among surgically evaluable patients (ICI n=9; NAC n=30), pCR rates were 22.2% and 26.7%, respectively (p=1.00), and downstaging rates were 44.4% and 50.0% (p=1.00). Propensity-weighted analyses likewise showed no statistically significant differences in pathologic response. In the total ICI cohort (n=11), four patients (36.4%) did not complete all four planned cycles, including three because of grade 3 immune-related toxicity and one who died following an on-treatment acute myocardial infarction. At a median follow-up of 58.3 months in the ICI cohort, no recurrences were observed among the nine surgically treated patients during the available follow-up, compared with nine recurrences (30.0%) in the NAC cohort. Two-year OS was 100% in the ICI group and approximately 80% in the NAC group (log-rank p=0.18).
CONCLUSION: Neoadjuvant dual ICI demonstrated pathologic activity, with response rates numerically within the range observed with standard NAC. Clinically meaningful immune-related adverse events were observed in the ICI cohort; however, no recurrences were observed among surgically treated ICI patients during the available follow-up. These findings support further investigation of dual ICI as a potential option when platinum-based NAC is not feasible or is declined.

Title: The gut microbiome and vascular disease - A systematic review of mechanistic insights and implications for vascular surgery.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Observational studies repeatedly linked gut microbial features and metabolites to vascular disease, but it is unclear which associations are reproducible, which remain significant after confounder adjustment, and how they relate to experimental evidence. This review aims to determine which taxa and metabolites are consistently associated across independent human studies; whether the population, phenotype, method, and sample type explain divergent findings; and where the human data converge with, diverge from, or remain untested with the animal and interventional literature.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched for human studies of the gut microbiome composition or gut-derived metabolites reporting atherosclerotic, aneurysmal, peripheral arterial, calcific, or arterial stiffness outcomes from database inception to December 31, 2025. Study screening and duplicate article extraction were conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. The study design was classified explicitly, the covariates in each primary analysis were extracted, and the risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. The findings were then compared with the animal and human interventional literature identified through targeted searching.
RESULTS: All the 29 included reports were observational (19 cross-sectional, 3 case-control, and 7 cohort) studies, and none was interventional. The reproducible findings were the enrichment of Proteobacteria-affiliated genera (5 reports) and of oral-origin organisms (3 reports), and the depletion of butyrate producers in carotid disease. The carnitine pathway intermediates gamma-butyrobetaine and trimethyllysine were independently associated with cardiovascular death and major adverse limb events (hazard ratio, 1.93; 95% confidence interval, 1.35-2.76) in two independent cohorts. Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) was outcome-specific; TMAO levels were associated with 5-year mortality in peripheral arterial disease (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.06; 95% confidence interval, 1.36-3.11) and with ankle-brachial-index-defined disease in diabetes (odds ratio, 1.051), but TMAO levels were lower in large-artery stroke than in controls and were unrelated to carotid or limb outcomes once renal function was modelled. In addition, 16 of 29 reports fitted a multivariable model, and only three included renal function; the compositional findings were almost exclusively unadjusted. The risk of bias was good in 11 reports, moderate in 16, and low in 2. Animal models causally implicate TMAO in atherogenesis and aneurysm formation and show butyrate and Roseburia intestinalis to be protective, but the results of germ-free experiments and the only human fecal transplantation trial are discordant.
CONCLUSIONS: A small number of gut microbial signals are reproducible, but most have not been adjusted for potential confounders, particularly renal function, which may partly explain the observed associations. The carnitine pathway metabolites with the strongest prognostic signal in surgical populations have never been tested in an animal vascular model. Microbiome profiling has no current role in vascular surgical practice.

Title: A transformer-based deep learning model for predicting the use of atherectomy devices during PCI from preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography.
Abstract:
AIMS: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), often necessitating atherectomy-based debulking devices that increase procedural complexity and risk. We aimed to develop and externally validate a Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) to predict atherectomy device use during PCI and compare its performance with that of blinded human readers, including general cardiologists and PCI experts.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective multicentre study included 498 calcified coronary lesions from 419 patients who underwent PCI after preprocedural CCTA. Data from 12 institutions were used for training and validation with four-fold cross-validation, and data from two independent institutions (97 lesions) served as an external test cohort. The model combined a convolutional neural network feature extractor with Transformer-based multiple instance learning, and clinical variables were evaluated for incremental value. In the external test cohort, the CCTA-only model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.788 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.691-0.873) for predicting atherectomy device use. Adding clinical variables resulted in an AUC of 0.805 (95% CI, 0.713-0.886), indicating limited incremental value. In the reader comparison, the model showed higher accuracy than general cardiologists (0.742 vs. 0.619; P = 0.029) and numerically similar accuracy to PCI experts (0.742 vs. 0.670; P = 0.230).
CONCLUSION: A Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural CCTA showed clinically relevant performance for predicting atherectomy device use during PCI in an independent external test cohort. These findings suggest that the model may support lesion assessment and procedural planning.

Title: Population-based screening for familial hypercholesterolaemia.
Journal: Medizinische Genetik : Mitteilungsblatt des Berufsverbandes Medizinische Genetik e.V
Abstract: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) is among the most common monogenic disorders, affecting at least 1 in 250 individuals. Lifelong elevation of LDL cholesterol from birth can cause accelerated atherosclerosis and premature cardiovascular disease. However, the vast majority of affected children (and adults) remain undiagnosed. Population-based childhood screening, combining LDL cholesterol measurement with genetic testing, enables early diagnosis and treatment. This review summarizes evidence on childhood FH screening, including disease burden, treatment efficacy, diagnostic performance, and economic considerations. Although no randomized trial has compared screened and unscreened populations, extensive indirect evidence supports the benefit of early detection and lipid-lowering therapy.

Title: Amelioration of diabetic autonomic neuropathy symptoms following a course of transcranial direct current stimulation.
Abstract: Cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (CAN) is a severe and potentially life-threatening complication of diabetes. This randomized, sham-controlled, three-arm trial evaluated the efficacy of anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex for improving CAN symptoms and glycaemic control in older patients with insulin-dependent diabetes. Seventy-two participants (aged 60-80 years) with symptomatic CAN were randomly allocated to active tDCS (n = 24), sham tDCS (n = 24) or routine care only (control group, n = 24). The primary outcome was CAN severity quantified by the ratio of the change in systolic blood pressure to the change in heart rate measured three minutes after standing from a supine position; the secondary outcome was long-term glycaemic control assessed by glycated haemoglobin. The active and sham groups received 30 sessions of tDCS (2 milliamperes for 20 min per session, anode at F3 and cathode at Fp2) over 6-8 weeks. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and one-month follow-up. Data were analysed with mixed-design ANOVA. A significant Time × Group interaction was found for CAN severity (P < 0.001, partial eta squared = 0.165). The active tDCS group demonstrated significantly greater improvement in CAN symptoms from baseline to post-intervention compared with both the sham tDCS and control groups (P < 0.001), with these improvements remaining evident at one-month follow-up despite a small, non-significant numerical increase from post-intervention. The active tDCS group also achieved superior glycaemic control at follow-up (mean glycated haemoglobin 7.92 ± 0.79%) relative to the sham group (8.78 ± 1.05%, P = 0.008) and control group (9.12 ± 1.18%, P = 0.001). Thirty sessions of left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex anodal tDCS was safe and well-tolerated. These findings indicate that left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex tDCS can improve cardiovascular autonomic function and glycaemic control in older adults with diabetic CAN and warrant larger, longer-term, multi-centre randomized controlled trials to confirm efficacy, durability and generalizability.

Title: Psychosocial symptom networks across atrial fibrillation subtypes: evidence from two waves of the ARENA cohort.
Abstract:
AIMS: Atrial fibrillation (AF) carries substantial psychosocial burden, but how psychosocial symptoms interrelate across AF subtypes and severities remains unclear. This study compared psychosocial symptom networks across time, AF type, and European Heart Rhythm Association (EHRA) class in the ARENA (Atrial Fibrillation Rhine-Neckar Region) cohort.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Adults with AF were assessed at baseline (T0) and follow-up (T1). Analytic samples included 996 patients with EHRA class [asymptomatic (EHRA 1) vs. symptomatic (EHRA ≥ 2)] and 924 with AF subtype (paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent) data. Measures included anxiety and worry (GAD-2), cardiac worry and avoidance (CAQ-2), health-related quality of life (HRQoL) (EQ-5D-5L), and psychosocial stressors. Gaussian graphical models were estimated and compared using network comparison test. Global network structures were stable across EHRA classes, AF subtypes, and time points, but specific edges and node centralities varied. The most robust edges linked anxiety with general worry and cardiac worry with avoidance. Anxiety, general worry, cardiac worry, and diminished HRQoL were consistently the most central nodes. Among symptomatic (EHRA ≥ 2) patients, loneliness emerged as an increasingly central node over time, whereas among asymptomatic patients (EHRA 1), sleep problems showed a stronger association with HRQoL at follow-up. Atrial fibrillation-type network structures were similar, although paroxysmal networks showed higher node centrality and stronger anxiety-worry coupling at T0; persistent or permanent AF showed a stress-at-home-cardiac worry edge at T1.
CONCLUSION: Psychosocial symptom networks in AF are comparable across subtypes and reveal intervention targets, particularly anxiety, cardiac worry with avoidance, loneliness, and sleep disturbance.

Title: Sickle Cell Trait and Incident Ischemic Stroke Risk: A Whole-Genome Sequencing Study in the All of Us Research Program.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sickle cell trait (SCT), the heterozygous hemoglobin variant (HbAS) genotype, affects approximately 300 million individuals worldwide and 8-10% of Black/African American individuals in the United States. Previous studies examining the association between SCT and ischemic stroke have yielded conflicting results, with effect estimates ranging from null to more than 2-fold increased risk. Interpretation of this literature has been limited by modest sample sizes, restricted ancestral diversity, and incomplete adjustment for genetic ancestry. We therefore evaluated whether whole-genome sequencing (WGS) confirmed SCT was independently associated with incident ischemic stroke after adjustment for genetic ancestry and vascular risk factors in the All of Us (AoU) cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using WGS-confirmed hemoglobin subunit beta (HBB) genotypes at rs334 (HBB NM_000518.5:c.20A > T [p.Glu7Val]) from 414,830 participants in the NIH AoU Controlled Tier data set Curated Data Repository version 8 (CDR v8, C2024Q3R9). After restricting to eligible participants with WGS data, available electronic health record data, age 18-75 years, at least 12 months of follow-up, and no prior stroke or TIA at cohort entry, 275,530 participants comprised the incident ischemic stroke cohort. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to compare incident ischemic stroke risk among participants with heterozygous HbAS SCT vs homozygous reference HbAA, adjusting for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, chronic kidney disease (CKD), body mass index (BMI), smoking, and genetic ancestry principal components 1-10 derived from AoU's precomputed WGS ancestry pipeline. Secondary analyses included competing risk modeling, multivariable logistic regression for prevalent stroke, Cox models for all secondary outcomes, 5 sensitivity analyses to test robustness of primary findings, and 12 prespecified subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Among 275,530 participants contributing 3,374,790 person-years of follow-up (mean follow-up, 12.25 years), 5,876 had heterozygous HbAS SCT, 269,404 had homozygous reference HbAA, and 144 had homozygous variant HbSS sickle cell disease. The crude ischemic stroke incidence rate was 1.15 vs 0.67 per 1,000 person-years in HbAS vs HbAA (crude rate ratio, 1.70). After multivariable adjustment, SCT was not significantly associated with incident ischemic stroke (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.06; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89-1.25; p = 0.53). The results were consistent across all 12 prespecified subgroups, the 5 sensitivity analyses, and additional missing data and time-varying covariate analyses assessing robustness to outcome definition, covariate timing, and ancestry restriction, including an African genetic ancestry subgroup analysis (HR = 0.97, 95% CI 0.81-1.16), a separate sensitivity analysis restricted to participants with African genetic ancestry (HR = 0.98, 95% CI 0.82-1.17), and strict baseline covariate definition (HR = 1.09, 95% CI 0.92-1.29). The results were also consistent in competing risk modeling (HR = 1.06), for hemorrhagic stroke (HR = 1.01), for TIA (TIA; HR = 1.06), and in the prespecified SCT × CKD interaction analysis (interaction HR = 1.13; p = 0.51). In contrast, HbSS was associated with a markedly elevated hazard of ischemic stroke (HR = 5.12, 95% CI 2.96-8.85; p < 0.001). The attenuation from the crude rate ratio to the ancestry-adjusted HR was consistent with substantial confounding by the higher proportion of African genetic ancestry among HbAS vs HbAA participants (88.1% vs 20.8%).
DISCUSSION: In a large WGS-confirmed, ancestry-adjusted cohort study, SCT was not significantly associated with incident ischemic stroke risk. The marked attenuation of the crude association after adjustment for genetic ancestry suggests that previously reported associations may, at least in part, reflect ancestry-related confounding and population structure rather than a strong independent effect of SCT. These findings do not support a clinically meaningful independent association between SCT and incident ischemic stroke in this cohort.

Title: Post-operative results of Bentall surgery at a national reference center in Peru.
Journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the mortality and postoperative complications of patients undergoing Bentall-DeBono surgery at the Cardiovascular Surgery Service of the National Cardiovascular Institute, EsSalud, Lima, Peru, between 2019 and 2024.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a single-center, retrospective, descriptive, case series observational study of patients undergoing composite valve-conduit replacement (Bentall-De Bono procedure) for aortic root pathology between January 2019 and December 2024. The primary objective was to determine all-cause mortality and major complications.
RESULTS: Sixty-three patients underwent Bentall-De Bono surgery. The median age was 58 years (IQR: 40-71), and 19% of patients had Marfan syndrome. The 30-day mortality rate was 7.9% (5 patients). The main complications were: stroke (6.3%), perioperative myocardial infarction (4.8%), permanent pacemaker implantation (11%), and excessive postoperative bleeding (6.3%). The median length of hospital stay was 17 days, and the median length of stay in the ICU was 4 days. In a median follow-up of 745 days (403-1060), the mortality rate was 14%, the stroke rate was 7.9%, the myocardial infarction rate was 4.8%, and the definitive pacemaker implantation rate was 14%.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results for the Bentall-De Bono procedure are acceptable and comparable to those reported in the international literature.

Title: Challenging the guidelines: longitudinal trends in left ventricular diameter and function in severe aortic regurgitation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend aortic valve replacement (AVR) in patients with severe aortic regurgitation (AR) based on progressive changes in left ventricular (LV) function or size. We aimed to reassess the clinical relevance of current guideline recommendations pertaining to traditional echocardiographic measurements in routine practice.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of patients with severe AR who underwent serial echocardiographic follow-up over at least 18 months. The composite outcome was symptom-driven AVR, acute heart failure hospitalization, or death. We used a joint modelling approach to handle within-subject correlation and censoring.
RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 140 patients, with a median follow-up of 93 months (interquartile range 58-130). LV end-systolic (LVESD) and fractional shortening (FS) showed a small but statistically significant longitudinal trend, while LVEDD did not. In three separate joint models adjusted for age at onset and sex, higher LVESD and LVEDD and lower FS were each associated with increased risk of the composite event. Each 1 mm increase in LVESD and LVEDD was associated with a 6% in risk; each 1% decrease in FS corresponded to a 12% increase in risk. Only 8 (5.7%) of patients were predicted to exceed the guideline-recommended LVEDD threshold of 65 mm over 10 years. Age at onset was also a significant risk factor, with each decade increasing risk by 65% for each of the three parallel joint models.
CONCLUSION: LV parameters show modest changes over time, despite holding strong prognostic value in patients with severe AR. LVEDD, while associated with overall risk, does not predictably or significantly dilate over time in most patients. AVR decisions should be based on comprehensive clinical and volumetric assessment rather than waiting for simple linear progression to guideline cutoffs.

Title: Joint Association of Parity and Spontaneous Miscarriage with Incident Cardiovascular Diseases.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To prospectively investigate the combined association of parity and spontaneous miscarriage in relation to cardiovascular diseases (CVD) risks.
METHODS: In this prospective UK Biobank cohort analysis, multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used in outcome-specific analytic cohorts: 219,422 participants free of prevalent CHD or stroke (CHD and stroke analyses) and 230,231, 230,589, and 229,123 participants free of the respective prevalent condition (PAD, HF, and AF analyses).
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 12.2 years, parity exhibited a significant positive linear association with CHD risk. Nonlinear U-shaped associations were observed with HF and AF risks, with two live births representing the lowest risk. Importantly, a history of spontaneous miscarriage did not modify these associations. Compared to participants with two live births and no history of spontaneous miscarriage, individuals without any live births and no history of spontaneous miscarriage had the lowest point estimate for CHD (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.68-0.95), whereas those with four or more live births and a history of spontaneous miscarriage exhibited the highest point estimate (HR = 1.43, 95% CI = 1.28-1.60). Participants with four or more live births and a history of spontaneous miscarriage had the highest point estimate for HF and AF.
CONCLUSION: The combined association of parity and spontaneous miscarriage and the risk for various CVDs exhibits outcome-specific patterns.

Title: Time-varying metoprolol exposure and the risk of acute kidney injury: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding the association between metoprolol use and acute kidney injury (AKI) remains limited, particularly because of time-varying exposure, cardiovascular confounding, and uncertain temporal ordering. We evaluated the association between recent metoprolol exposure and incident AKI using a longitudinal time-varying framework.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective longitudinal cohort study included adult inpatients from three Chinese hospitals between January 2020 and December 2024. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate ≥60 mL min-1·1.73 m-2 at cohort entry and sufficient serial serum creatinine (Scr) and medication execution records. Metoprolol was modeled as a lag-1 time-varying exposure, relating use on hospital day t to AKI risk on day t+1. Incident AKI was identified using rolling KDIGO Scr criteria. Time-varying Cox regression adjusted for demographic characteristics, baseline renal function, major comorbidities, baseline severity-related factors, and lagged concomitant medication exposures. Sensitivity and complementary analyses evaluated the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: Among 291,049 screened hospitalizations, 20,333 patients contributed 284,470 risk intervals, and 1,050 developed incident AKI. Lag-1 metoprolol exposure was associated with a higher AKI hazard in the unadjusted model (HR, 2.53; 95% CI, 2.13-3.00). The association was substantially attenuated after adjustment but remained statistically significant in the primary model (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.05-1.79; P = 0.022). Prespecified follow-up-time analyses suggested that the association was concentrated during the first 72 h after cohort entry. Sensitivity analyses generally yielded estimates in the same direction, although the magnitude and statistical significance varied across analytical specifications; the association was attenuated to non-significance in the 2-day lag analysis (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 0.96-1.68) and after additional adjustment for vasopressor use (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.98-1.70). No consistent monotonic dose-response relationship was observed.
CONCLUSION: Recent metoprolol exposure was associated with a modestly higher hazard of incident AKI in the primary adjusted analysis.
