However, attenuation after adjustment, temporal heterogeneity, sensitivity to exposure timing and confounding control, and the absence of a consistent monotonic dose-response pattern suggest that residual confounding and clinical treatment context may contribute to the observed association. These findings should be interpreted as a hypothesis-generating short-term AKI safety signal rather than evidence of direct metoprolol nephrotoxicity or causality.

Title: Deep learning for diagnostic and clinical decision support in companion animals: a systematic review of CNN- and LSTM-based approaches.
Abstract: Early disease detection prior to the onset of advanced clinical signs remains a critical imperative in veterinary medicine. This systematic review provides a methodological synthesis of Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks applied to diagnostic and clinical decision support in canine and feline patients, evaluating both algorithmic performance and clinical feasibility. Adhering to the PICO-CS framework and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we queried Scopus and Web of Science for peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2026, retrieving a final corpus of 57 primary studies. Eleven clinical domains were identified, with evidence heavily concentrated in Oncology (28.1%), Cardiology (15.8%), and Pulmonology (12.3%). CNN architectures predominated in spatial imaging modalities-including radiographs, clinical photography, ultrasonography, and microscopic imagery-whereas LSTM networks were deployed for temporal signals and sensor-derived telemetry. Binary classification tasks achieved the highest performance metrics (accuracy reaching up to 99%), whereas multi-class formulations exhibited broader variability due to dataset imbalance. Cross-study benchmarking revealed substantial heterogeneity in datasets, evaluation metrics, and validation protocols, while reliance on high-performance computational infrastructure poses a barrier to point-of-care deployment in resource-constrained clinics. We conclude that while deep learning architectures hold significant promise as clinical decision-support tools, transitioning to routine veterinary practice requires prospective external validation, representative open-access datasets, and lightweight models optimized for conventional clinical hardware.

Title: Real-Time Invasive Hemodynamic Changes During Endobronchial Valve Therapy in Advanced Emphysema: A Prospective Case Series.
Abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) in advanced emphysema is associated with worse outcomes and often prompts caution or exclusion from bronchoscopic lung volume reduction. The immediate pulmonary hemodynamic response to endobronchial valve (EBV) deployment has not been characterized using invasive measurements obtained during implantation. We performed a prospective single-center physiological case series of four consecutive patients undergoing clinically indicated EBV therapy with concurrent right heart catheterization and continuous systemic arterial pressure monitoring. Hemodynamics were sampled at end-expiration at four predefined timepoints: pre-general anesthesia (pre-GA), GA pre-valve, GA post-valve, and post-extubation once awake and hemodynamically stable. Cardiac output was estimated by the indirect Fick method using an assumed oxygen consumption. All patients met hemodynamic criteria for PH with a pre-capillary profile at baseline. In the prespecified GA comparison (pre-valve to post-valve), mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) decreased in all four patients (-10% to -61%). In the prespecified awake comparison (pre-GA to post-extubation), mPAP decreased in all four (-33% to -58%), with post-extubation mPAP < 20 mmHg in three patients. Estimated pulmonary vascular resistance decreased in three under GA (-42% to -90%) and in all four in the awake comparison (-47% to -96%); pulmonary arterial compliance increased in all four. Real-time invasive hemodynamic assessment during EBV implantation was feasible in this four-patient case series and showed descriptive, hypothesis-generating reductions in pulmonary vascular load in selected patients with advanced emphysema and baseline pre-capillary PH.

Title: Sex-specific association between body mass index and mortality after heart transplantation: A nationwide KOTRY Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body mass index has paradoxical associations with outcomes in advanced heart failure, but whether its relationship with survival after heart transplantation differs by sex remains uncertain.
METHODS: We analyzed 1059 adult heart transplant recipients enrolled in the Korean Organ Transplantation Registry from 2014 through 2023. Body mass index was assessed using Asian-specific BMI categories and 3-knot restricted cubic splines. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for prespecified clinical characteristics and pretransplant support. Sex differences in the body mass index-mortality association were evaluated using restricted cubic spline modeling.
RESULTS: The cohort included 304 female patients, and 217 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 3.6 years. The body mass index-mortality association differed by sex in the pooled spline model (P for interaction=0.041). In male patients, the association was nonlinear and U-shaped (P for overall association=0.031; P for nonlinearity=0.017). Underweight was associated with higher mortality than normal weight (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.97; 95% confidence interval, 1.17-3.33). In female patients, the fitted association was inverse, without evidence of nonlinearity (P for overall association=0.030; P for nonlinearity=0.302). Obesity class I was associated with lower mortality than normal weight (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% confidence interval, 0.08-0.73), although this estimate was based on few events.
CONCLUSIONS: The association between body mass index and mortality after heart transplantation may differ by sex. The apparent lower mortality among female patients with obesity class I is hypothesis-generating and requires external validation.

Title: A comparative study of the state-of-the-art artificial intelligence models for automated plaque measurement in a carotid ultrasound Japanese cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) measurement from B-mode ultrasound is important for cardiovascular risk stratification. Direct comparisons of deep learning architectures on the same cohort under controlled conditions remain limited. This study aimed to compare the accuracy and computational cost of three deep learning architectures with the commercial AtheroEdge™ 2.0 (AE 2.0) system for carotid ultrasound analysis.
METHODS: This study evaluated three deep learning architectures: carotid non-attention double-stage convolutional neural network (cNonAtt-dsCNN), carotid attention-based single-stage UNet (cAtt-ssUNet), and carotid attention-based double-stage UNet (cAtt-dsUNet) against the commercial AE 2.0 system on 400 carotid ultrasound images from 200 Japanese patients. All deep learning models were trained using identical preprocessing, augmentation, hyperparameters (Adam optimizer, learning rate =1e-4, batch =32), and 5-fold cross-validation. Evaluation metrics included Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Jaccard index, lumen-intima error (LIe), media-adventitia error (MAe), intima-media thickness error (IMTe), and computational cost.
RESULTS: Under identical conditions, cAtt-dsUNet achieved the highest accuracy [DSC: 91.2%, Jaccard index: 85.5%, correlation coefficient (CC): 0.98, LIe: 0.031 mm, IMTe: 0.022 mm], reaching commercial-grade overlap and correlation but at ~2.5× longer training (20.2 vs. 8 min) and ~1.7× more graphics processing unit (GPU) memory than cNonAtt-dsCNN (DSC: 81.5%, CC: 0.92, LIe: 0.09 mm, IMTe: 0.124 mm). cAtt-ssUNet was intermediate (DSC: 88.5%, CC: 0.95, LIe: 0.07 mm). AE 2.0 retained the lowest boundary errors (LIe: 0.012 mm, IMTe: 0.011 mm) with 6 ms inference.
CONCLUSIONS: A clear trade-off between accuracy-efficiency exists across the evaluated methods. cAtt-dsUNet is optimal for high-accuracy research settings with adequate GPU resources, while cNonAtt-dsCNN and AE 2.0 are preferable for speed-critical clinical screening. The single-cohort Japanese dataset limits generalizability; multi-center, multi-ethnic validation is recommended before clinical deployment.

Title: Prognostic significance of IgG-Kappa positivity detected by serum immunofixation during daratumumab therapy in multiple myeloma.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Daratumumab, an immunoglobulin G kappa (IgG-κ) monoclonal antibody, can co-migrate with endogenous M-protein on serum immunofixation (IF), producing IgG-κ bands that may be misinterpreted as residual disease. We therefore evaluated treatment responses and the prognostic impact of daratumumab-associated IgG-κ IF positivity on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in multiple myeloma (MM).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 108 patients with MM treated with daratumumab-containing regimens at any line of therapy between January 2014 and January 2024. Serum IF IgG-κ positivity was assessed both at the first response assessment and during continued treatment. Treatment responses were classified according to the International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) criteria, and PFS and OS were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, the log-rank test, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: IgG-κ IF positivity was detected in 85 patients (78.7%) at first response, and the overall response rate to daratumumab was 64.8%. Patients positive at first response had longer PFS (14.0 vs. 7.0 months; P = 0.048) and higher very good partial response/complete response rates (65.9% vs. 43.5%; P = 0.058). In non-IgG-κ myeloma, treatment-emergent positivity was associated with a markedly higher deep-response rate (88.5% vs. 44.2%; P < 0.001) and a reduced risk of progression (hazard ratio 0.17; 95% confidence interval 0.03-0.74; P = 0.018). On multivariable analysis, older age independently predicted mortality, whereas persistent IF positivity did not worsen survival.
CONCLUSIONS: IgG-κ IF positivity during daratumumab therapy should not be interpreted as residual disease in isolation; a substantial proportion likely reflects therapeutic antibody interference. Recognizing this interference is important to avoid overestimating residual disease and misclassifying treatment response, and confirmatory assays should be used where available.

Title: Comparison of Effects of Pulsed Field Ablation and Cryoablation on Left Atrial Stiffness Using Invasively Derived Pressure-Volume Relationship.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute effects of pulsed field ablation (PFA) on passive atrial mechanical properties have not hitherto been assessed by reconstruction of pressure-volume relationship using invasive intracavitary pressure measurements.
METHODS: In a cohort of 38 first-time atrial fibrillation ablation patients, submitted to pulmonary vein isolation, we studied the effects of PFA and cryoballoon ablation on the left atrial elastic constant and passive elastic chamber stiffness constant, expressing baseline left atrial conditions and quantifying passive left atrial stiffness, respectively. Left atrial pressure was invasively measured immediately pre- and post-procedurally, while volume values were obtained echocardiographically.
RESULTS: No differences were noted in passive elastic chamber stiffness constant values, pre- and post-procedurally in either group. No differences were noted between CBA and PFA groups. There were no observable associations between Δα and Δb and either AF duration or preprocedural left atrial volume.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on the above, CBA and PFA demonstrated comparable effects on left atrial mechanical properties in the acute post-ablation setting.

Title: Admission high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T and clinical outcomes after acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study with exploratory nonlinear analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) is frequently observed in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and has been associated with adverse outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the association of admission hs-cTnT with 90-day functional outcome and all-cause mortality during follow-up, with particular attention to potential nonlinear risk patterns across the biomarker range.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 564 patients with AIS admitted between January 2022 and October 2024. The primary outcomes were modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 90 days and long-term all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was used for poor 90-day functional outcome and Cox proportional hazards models were used for all-cause mortality during follow-up. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were performed to explore nonlinear dose-response relationships, and segmented regression models were used to estimate exploratory turning points.
RESULTS: Among 564 patients, 212 (37.6%) had elevated hs-cTnT (>14 ng/L). Elevated hs-cTnT was independently associated with poor 90-day mRS (adjusted OR 1.93, 95% CI, 1.22-3.05; p = 0.005) and all-cause mortality during follow-up (fully adjusted HR 4.12, 95% CI, 2.31-7.48; p < 0.001). During a median follow-up of 17 months (IQR 12-26 months), Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly lower overall survival in patients with elevated hs-cTnT (p < 0.001). RCS analysis revealed significant nonlinear associations between hs-cTnT and both endpoints (p < 0.001). Exploratory model-derived turning points were observed at 28.42 ng/L for functional outcome and 31.68 ng/L for mortality; these should be interpreted as exploratory rather than validated clinical cutoffs. Below these values, risk increased more steeply; above them, no statistically significant further increase in risk was observed.
CONCLUSION: Admission hs-cTnT was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome and all-cause mortality during follow-up in patients with AIS. The association appeared to be nonlinear, with model-derived turning points at approximately 28-32 ng/L that should be interpreted as exploratory rather than definitive clinical cutoffs. Clinically, hs-cTnT may be useful as a complementary marker for identifying patients at higher risk who may warrant closer neuro-cardiac evaluation, although its incremental predictive value has not been formally assessed.

Title: Association between short-term fine particulate matter exposure and hospital-acquired pneumonia risk in critically ill post-cardiac surgery patients: a 10-year cohort study using distributed lag non-linear models.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambient air pollution (AAP) exposure is a substantial health threat to humans globally. However, whether AAP could promote hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) onset in critically ill patients, a vulnerable population undergoing cardiac surgery in the intensive care unit (ICU), remains elusive. This study evaluated the correlation of HAP onset with fine particulate matter (PM2.5).
METHODS: In total, this study included 6,196 patients who underwent cardiovascular surgery at the ICU of a major hospital in Shandong province, China, over 10 years, from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2023. The daily mean levels of sulfur dioxide (SO2), PM2.5, carbon monoxide (CO), PM10, and ozone (O3) were assessed from publicly available data. The outcome was HAP, defined according to CDC/NHSN pneumonia criteria as pneumonia developing >48 h after hospital admission and not present or incubating at admission; VAP was not analyzed as a separate endpoint. The association between PM2.5 and HAP was estimated via a distributed lag non-linear model, adjusted for pollutants, time trends, and weather conditions.
RESULTS: This study analyzed 1938 (31.278%) HAP cases. The mean levels of PM10, O3, PM2.5, and SO2 were 120, 75, 59, and 25 μg/m3, respectively, and the mean CO level was 0.979 mg/m3. The association between PM2.5 and HAP was statistically significant at lag 1 day within the perioperative exposure window. At a PM2.5 concentration of 30 μg/m3 compared with the reference concentration of 10 μg/m3, 14.2% higher odds of HAP were observed (95% CI: 2.6-27%). The stratified analyses indicated stronger associations among elders aged ≥ 60 years, patients with body mass index (BMI) > 23.9 kg/m2 and patients with diabetes. Additional adjustment for clinical covariates, including duration of mechanical ventilation, confirmed the robustness of the observed exposure-response association.
CONCLUSION: These findings revealed a substantial and robust link between short-term PM2.5 exposure and elevated HAP incidence in the vulnerable population undergoing cardiovascular surgeries.

Title: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor across the kidney-cardiometabolic continuum: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR), a circulating marker of innate immune activation, has been proposed as a risk biomarker in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and related cardiometabolic conditions, but its clinical utility remains uncertain.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review according to PRISMA 2020 and the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline, searching PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, medRxiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP from inception to May 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, the JBI checklist, RoB 2, and QUADAS-2; certainty of evidence was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
RESULTS: Twenty studies comprising 31,416 participants were included. In adults with preserved kidney function, elevated suPAR predicted incident CKD (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 3.13 for the highest versus lowest quartile, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.11-4.65) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.53 for the highest versus lowest tertile, 95% CI 1.10-2.12), but the gain in discrimination was modest (absolute C-statistic increase 0.027-0.08) and no study performed decision curve analysis (DCA). suPAR did not distinguish focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) from other glomerular diseases, and prognostic evidence in FSGS rested on a single moderate-quality study. In pediatric CKD and in metabolic cohorts, suPAR lost independent association after adjustment for baseline kidney function or inflammatory markers. Associations with cardiovascular outcomes were directionally consistent but observational and of low certainty. No study reported sex-stratified analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine clinical measurement of suPAR is not currently supported; assay harmonization, sex-disaggregated analyses, prospective validation with decision curve analysis, and trials of suPAR-targeted therapy are needed first.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261320503, identifier CRD420261320503.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Trans-sinus fracture as the gatekeeper: a two-step clinical strategy to guide venous imaging in mild-to-moderate traumatic brain injury.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (tCVST) is an underrecognized complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI). Despite its potential for serious neurological sequelae, no consensus exists regarding indications for CT venography (CTV) or MR venography (MRV) in patients with mild-to-moderate TBI. Trans-sinus fracture has been identified as a risk factor for tCVST, yet its predictive value alone remains insufficient to guide clinical decision-making.
OBJECTIVE: To propose a two-step clinical decision strategy for guiding venous imaging selection in mild-to-moderate TBI, using trans-sinus fracture as a gatekeeper followed by D-dimer and headache visual analog scale (VAS) score stratification.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 528 patients with mild-to-moderate TBI (Glasgow Coma Scale score > 8) who underwent CTV, MRV, or digital subtraction angiography between January 2024 and January 2026. Firth penalized logistic regression was employed to identify tCVST predictors. A two-step strategy was derived: Step 1 screened for trans-sinus fracture; Step 2 applied D-dimer threshold ≥ 3.95 mg/L or headache VAS score ≥ 3 in trans-sinus fracture-positive patients.
RESULTS: Traumatic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis was diagnosed in 41 patients (7.8%). Trans-sinus fracture was independently associated with tCVST (odds ratio 8.44, 95% confidence interval 4.38-16.39; P < 0.0001). As a standalone gatekeeper, trans-sinus fracture yielded sensitivity 58.5%, specificity 89.1%, negative predictive value 96.3%, and positive likelihood ratio 3.96. Among trans-sinus fracture-positive patients, the high-risk subgroup (D-dimer ≥ 3.95 mg/L or VAS ≥ 3) exhibited a tCVST rate of 31.2%, compared with 4.3% in the low-risk subgroup. The two-step strategy achieved a number needed to image of 3, avoiding 85% of unnecessary venous examinations compared with universal screening, and reduced the number needed to image from 13 (universal approach) to 3 (two-step approach).
CONCLUSIONS: This two-step strategy represents a simple, bedside-ready exploratory tool that may help optimize CTV/MRV selection in mild-to-moderate TBI by identifying a high-yield subgroup for targeted imaging. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective external validation before clinical implementation.

Title: Association of aspartate aminotransferase to alanine aminotransferase ratio with hypertension in Chinese adults: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence has linked the aspartate aminotransferase to alanine aminotransferase (AST/ALT) ratio to insulin resistance and various metabolic disorders, yet its relationship with hypertension in the Chinese adult population has not been well characterized. The present study was designed to evaluate whether the AST/ALT ratio is independently associated with hypertension risk among Chinese adults.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using data obtained from the Dryad repository, originally collected through the Rich Healthcare Group Health screening program. A total of 87,869 participants were enrolled. The AST/ALT ratio was derived by dividing serum AST by ALT concentrations. Hypertension was identified when systolic blood pressure reached ≥140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure reached ≥90 mmHg. Multivariable logistic regression models with progressive covariate adjustment were employed to assess the AST/ALT ratio-hypertension relationship. Smooth curve fitting coupled with threshold analysis was applied to detect nonlinear patterns, while stratified analyses with multiplicative and additive interaction assessments were performed to examine effect modification. A sensitivity analysis excluding renal-function markers was performed to probe robustness.
RESULTS: A total of 87,869 participants (57.0% male) with a mean age of 42.1 ± 12.8 years were included. In a model adjusted for age, sex, and BMI, each unit increase in the AST/ALT ratio corresponded to a 20% reduction in hypertension odds (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.76-0.84, p < 0.001), and the estimate was essentially unchanged in the fully adjusted model (OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.78-0.87, p < 0.001). When stratified by quartiles, participants in higher AST/ALT ratio categories exhibited progressively lower hypertension risk relative to the lowest quartile (Q2: OR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.81-0.90; Q3: OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.83; Q4: OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.75-0.87). A nonlinear dose-response pattern was identified, with the inflection point occurring at an AST/ALT ratio of approximately 1.010. Stratified analyses demonstrated significant effect modification by age (P for interaction < 0.001) and BMI (P for interaction < 0.001), with stronger inverse associations among individuals younger than 60 years and those with BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2.
CONCLUSION: Among Chinese adults, an elevated AST/ALT ratio is independently and inversely associated with the risk of hypertension, following a nonlinear pattern. Because it is obtainable at no additional cost from routine liver function panels, the AST/ALT ratio may serve as a complementary indicator for flagging individuals who warrant closer blood pressure surveillance; however, the association is modest in size, and the ratio does not replace direct blood pressure measurement.

Title: Mechanism-based therapeutic strategies in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: integrating biological pathways with evidence from clinical trials.
Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome describes the close relationship between metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease, which share several biological pathways and frequently progress together. This review examines the mechanisms and clinical trial evidence supporting established and emerging therapies relevant to CKM syndrome. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and lipid-lowering therapies have shown cardiovascular, kidney, and metabolic benefits across several high-risk populations. However, most evidence comes from trials enrolling patients with individual conditions, such as type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, obesity, or atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, rather than populations defined by CKM stage or phenotype. Evidence for the added clinical benefit of specific treatment combinations also remains limited. Newer therapies targeting aldosterone synthesis, endothelin signaling, inflammation, incretin pathways, and lipid-related pathways may broaden treatment options. In clinical practice, CKM stage and the predominant clinical phenotype may help identify treatment priorities while accounting for coexisting conditions, safety, treatment burden, cost, and access. This approach may provide a practical basis for selecting therapies across the CKM spectrum, although prospective studies are needed to determine whether phenotype-directed treatment improves clinical outcomes.

Title: Association between bosentan and reduced detection of precapillary pulmonary hypertension in systemic sclerosis: evidence from a EUSTAR study.
Journal: Journal of scleroderma and related disorders
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether exposure to vasoactive-vasodilating drugs (VVDs), particularly bosentan, is associated with reduced detection of precapillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) in systemic sclerosis (SSc).
DESIGN: Post hoc retrospective case-control study.
SETTING: European Scleroderma Trials and Research database.
PARTICIPANTS: SSc patients who underwent their first right heart catheterisation (RHC); patients with postcapillary PH (pulmonary wedge pressure >15 mm Hg) were excluded.
INTERVENTIONS: Exposure to VVDs (endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs), phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, prostanoids) was defined as 'ever' before or 'ongoing' at the time of RHC.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Presence of precapillary PH at RHC.
RESULTS: Among the 944 patients included in the study, 498 (53%) were diagnosed with precapillary PH. Bosentan 'ever' was associated with a lower likelihood of a precapillary PH detection (OR 0.594, 95% CI 0.362 to 0.975) in the whole population. When considering 'ongoing' bosentan exposure, this result was confirmed only in patients with current DU (OR 0.230, 95% CI 0.081 to 0.652). ERAs in general showed a trend for protective effects towards detection of precapillary PH in patients with current DU ('ever': OR 0.636, 95% CI 0.349 to 1.158; 'ongoing': OR 0.435, 95% CI 0.193 to 1.064), while other VVD classes did not.
CONCLUSIONS: Bosentan, especially when employed in patients with current DU at the time of RHC, was associated with less detection of precapillary PH. These findings highlight the need for individualised treatment strategies and further research to optimise the timing and patient selection for VVD therapy in SSc.

Title: First-Line Antiretroviral Regimens and Risk of Incident Hypertension in People With HIV: A 15-Year Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with HIV (PWH) face a growing burden of cardiovascular disease. Integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs) have been linked to weight gain and possibly hypertension, but head-to-head data among contemporary regimens are scarce, and few studies analyze older and modern regimens together. We evaluated the incidence of hypertension in antiretroviral therapy (ART)-naive PWH initiating Spanish guidelines-recommended first-line regimens since 2009.
METHODS: This study evaluated a retrospective cohort of ART-naive adults initiating first-line regimens from 2009 to 2024, grouped into non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI), INSTI, and boosted protease inhibitor (PI)-based classes. Incident hypertension was defined by a composite of clinical diagnosis, antihypertensive initiation, or 2 consecutive measurements ≥ 140/90 mmHg. Time to hypertension was analyzed using Kaplan-Meir methods and Cox regression, with a prespecified INSTI subanalysis.
RESULTS: Among 1134 participants (median age 34.1 years; 89.8% male), 205 (18.1%) developed hypertension over a median of 135.9 weeks (incidence 4.9/100 person-years). Hypertension-free survival differed by class (log-rank P = .005); INSTI-based ART was independently associated with higher risk than NNRTIs (adjusted HR 1.61; 95% CI 1.20-2.17). Within the INSTI subgroup (n = 437; incidence 7/100 person-years), 5-year cumulative hypertension ranged from 9% (EVG/c/FTC/TAF) to 37% (dolutegravir-based); dolutegravir-based regimens carried a >2-fold adjusted hazard versus EVG/c/FTC/TAF. Higher body mass index was independently predictive but did not abolish this signal.
CONCLUSIONS: In ART-naive PWH, INSTI-based regimens were associated with a higher incidence of hypertension than NNRTI-based regimens, whereas the comparison with PI-based regimens was not statistically significant. Dolutegravir-containing regimens were independently associated with incident hypertension supporting systematic blood pressure surveillance and further comparative studies.

Title: Circulating osteocrin is associated with cardiac remodeling in canine myxomatous mitral valve disease and skeletal alterations in a rat pressure-overload model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cardiac disease in dogs and is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder associated with extracardiac remodeling. Osteocrin (OSTN), a secreted peptide implicated in natriuretic peptide biology and skeletal homeostasis, has emerged as a potential candidate biomarker of cardiovascular-skeletal interactions. However, circulating OSTN dynamics during cardiovascular disease progression remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We employed a translational study design integrating a clinical cohort of dogs with naturally occurring myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and an experimental rat pressure-overload remodeling model. Circulating OSTN concentrations were evaluated alongside cardiac biomarkers, echocardiographic indices, bone mineral density, skeletal mechanical properties, and tissue localization by immunohistochemistry.
RESULTS: In the canine cohort (n = 47), circulating OSTN concentrations demonstrated stage-dependent alterations and were significantly associated with echocardiographic indices of cardiac remodeling. In the rat pressure-overload model, circulating OSTN concentrations increased, whereas NT-proBNP did not show a significant pressure-overload-associated increase. In pooled analyses, circulating OSTN was inversely associated with bone mineral density and stiffness; however, these associations were substantially influenced by between-group separation, whereas no significant associations were observed between NT-proBNP and the skeletal parameters examined. Multivariable regression analysis demonstrated that ACVIM disease stage remained significantly associated with circulating OSTN concentrations after adjustment for age and body weight.
CONCLUSION: Circulating OSTN was associated with cardiac remodeling in dogs with MMVD and with skeletal alterations in an experimental rat pressure-overload model. These findings support further investigation of OSTN as a candidate biomarker at the interface between cardiovascular and skeletal remodeling.

Title: Comparative effectiveness of lipid-lowering therapies for primary cardiovascular prevention: a network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comparative effectiveness across lipid-lowering drug classes in primary prevention remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a random-effects network meta-analysis of randomised trials of lipid-lowering therapy in adults without a prior coronary event, stratified by baseline atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk. MEDLINE and EMBASE were searched from inception to July 25, 2026; included trials were published 1984-2026. Statin-containing regimens were classified by intensity, with no lipid-lowering therapy as reference.
FINDINGS: 29 trials (218,657 unique participants) were included; hazard ratios are shown with 95% CIs. At high ASCVD risk, evolocumab plus statin (0.59, 0.49-0.71), bempedoic acid (0.64, 0.48-0.85) and high-intensity statin (0.80, 0.69-0.92) reduced 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) vs. no lipid-lowering therapy. Against its statin comparator, evolocumab retained benefit (0.74, 0.65-0.83), whereas eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) (0.81, 0.62-1.06) and fibrates (4-point MACE, low-to-moderate risk; 1.04, 0.80-1.36) did not. At low-to-moderate risk, benefit was graded by statin intensity (high 0.53, 0.37-0.75; moderate 0.76, 0.64-0.91); for 4-point MACE, ezetimibe (0.66, 0.50-0.87) and fibrates (0.81, 0.70-0.94) also reduced events. Heterogeneity was moderate in the 2-point and 3-point networks (I2 59-62%) and no network contained a closed loop, precluding consistency testing. Two trials were at high risk of bias; certainty was low or very low for 23 of 27 comparisons. No comparison contained enough trials to test for small-study effects.
INTERPRETATION: Benefit in primary prevention tracked statin intensity rather than drug class. Evolocumab added to a statin conferred further benefit over that statin, whereas EPA and fibrates did not, and bempedoic acid is an option where statins are not tolerated.
FUNDING: None.

Title: Association of ticagrelor versus clopidogrel with in-hospital early outcomes in elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: findings from CCC-ACS project.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) have a markedly high mortality. Although ticagrelor has demonstrated superiority over clopidogrel in the AMI population, its efficacy and safety in elderly patients with AMI-CS remain uncertain. This study aimed to compare the associations of ticagrelor and clopidogrel with early in-hospital clinical outcomes in elderly patients with AMI-CS.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 839 patients aged ≥65 years with AMI-CS who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at participating hospitals in China within the Improving Care for Cardiovascular Disease in China-Acute Coronary Syndrome (CCC-ACS) project between November 2014 and December 2020. Patients with missing information on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), those who did not receive DAPT within 24 hours of first medical contact, and those with combined use of or switching between P2Y12 inhibitors during hospitalization were excluded. Patients were grouped according to the P2Y12 inhibitor received: ticagrelor (n=314) or clopidogrel (n=525). The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major bleeding during the first 15 days of hospitalization; major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching (PSM), and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Compared with clopidogrel, ticagrelor was associated with higher risk of all-cause mortality [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.52, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.05-2.21, P=0.03] and MACE (adjusted HR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.09-2.01, P=0.01) during the first 15 days of hospitalization, without a statistically significant difference in major bleeding (adjusted HR 1.76, 95% CI: 0.68-4.52, P=0.24). Subgroup analyses generally showed a similar direction of association for all-cause mortality. The associations with mortality and MACE remained statistically significant after PSM; the corresponding IPTW estimates were directionally similar but not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Among elderly AMI-CS patients undergoing PCI, ticagrelor did not confer a clinical benefit over clopidogrel and was associated with increased in-hospital mortality and MACE without a significant increase in major bleeding. These findings highlight the need for cautious selection of P2Y12 inhibitors in this high-risk population and further prospective studies to guide individualized therapy.

Title: Update in short-term mechanical circulatory support: indications, devices and complications.
Abstract: Despite advances in early recognition, aetiology-directed therapy, intensive cardiovascular care and short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS), cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high mortality and morbidity. MCS can restore systemic perfusion and stabilise patients as a bridge to recovery or advanced heart failure therapies, or as a bridge-to-decision when the final therapeutic destination remains uncertain. However, appropriate patient and device selection remains challenging. The optimal timing of support is uncertain, as both premature implantation and delayed use in advanced shock may limit benefit while increasing complications. Device selection should therefore be individualised according to the predominant patient phenotype, including left ventricular, right ventricular or biventricular failure, concomitant respiratory failure, vascular access and anatomical considerations. Randomised trials have focused predominantly on acute myocardial infarction-related CS, whereas data in heart failure-related and acute-on-chronic CS remain limited. Recent trials have also shown that greater haemodynamic support does not uniformly translate into improved survival, highlighting the importance of matching device physiology to shock phenotype and clinical trajectory. MCS is associated with clinically relevant complications, including major bleeding, haemolysis, limb ischaemia, stroke, thrombosis and vascular injury. Accordingly, its use should be considered within a strategy integrating reversibility, neurological prognosis, recovery potential, a realistic definitive therapeutic strategy, technical feasibility and anticipated complication risk. This Mini Review summarises contemporary indications, devices and complications of MCS in CS, with emphasis on phenotype-guided selection, timing, intensive care management and current evidence gaps.

Title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients.
METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution.
RESULTS: XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension.
CONCLUSIONS: In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

Title: Long-term outcomes of antithrombotic treatment for retinal vein occlusion.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a leading cause of visual impairment. Several cardiovascular and thrombotic predisposing factors have been linked to RVO. Antithrombotic agents are commonly prescribed, but their effectiveness for visual recovery and long-term outcomes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To study the course of long-term clinical outcomes in RVO patients.
METHODS: In this multicenter, retrospective, observational study of patients with an index RVO at 3 academic hospitals, we estimated the risk of recurrent RVO, cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolic events, bleeding complications, and death, reported as incidence rates per 100 person-years, and compared these rates between patients treated with antithrombotic drugs and those untreated.
RESULTS: Between 2004 and 2023, 198 patients were enrolled (median age, 65 years; IQR, 54-75; 105 females, 53.0%) and followed for a median of 2.6 years (IQR, 0.9-4.5); of these, 39.4% received antiplatelet therapy, 16.6% received anticoagulant therapy, and 44.0% received no antithrombotic treatment. The median duration of anticoagulant therapy was 46 days (IQR, 30-158), while that of antiplatelet therapy was 296 days (IQR, 124-947). The incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for cardiovascular events and mortality were higher in the untreated group (IRR, 6.04; 95% CI, 1.17-38.9 for cardiovascular events; IRR, 3.89; 95% CI, 1.29-12.3 for mortality) than in patients receiving antithrombotic treatment. For RVO recurrence and hemorrhagic complications, we found no differences between treated and untreated patients (IRR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.18-3.97 for recurrent RVO; IRR, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.4-2.76 for bleeding complications).
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort study of RVO, our data suggest that patients with RVO should undergo careful cardiovascular risk assessment. Antithrombotic therapy should not be used routinely after RVO, only when indicated by established cardiovascular prevention principles or specific clinical circumstances. Notably, rates of recurrent RVO and bleeding complications were similar between treated and untreated patients.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Comment on "Ticagrelor versus prasugrel following PCI in acute coronary syndromes and high-risk coronary artery disease: A meta-analysis of one-year randomized trial outcomes".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Patent foramen ovale and stroke: from diagnosis to treatment-a clinical practice review.
Abstract: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is present in 25% of the general population. However, its prevalence increases to 50-60% in young cryptogenic stroke patients. Early randomized trials of PFO closure shows no significant improvement in future stroke risk, largely owing to suboptimal patient selection and limited power. With careful case selection and longer follow-up time, PFO closure has been shown to improve future stroke events in multiple landmark trials. Therefore, current practice of PFO closure in young stroke patients emphasizes on diagnostic workup and risk stratification, to better classify which PFOs are likely contributing to the stroke etiology. The PFO-associated stroke causal likelihood (PASCAL) risk stratification system combines patient underlying demographics with PFO anatomy to determine the PFO-stroke causal relationship. It has been shown to be effective in distinguishing patients who are likely to benefit from PFO closure. In borderline cases, a heart-brain team approach is advocated to further identify patients whose stroke is likely caused by PFO. Current success rate of PFO closure is nearly 100% with high safety profile. Careful device sizing and selection minimizes residual shunt. Atrial fibrillation after PFO closure is mostly transient and occurs in the first 3 months after the procedure. Anticoagulation is generally not necessary. Future studies should focus on bioresorbable or suture-based device would further improve outcome, and whether PFO closure could benefit elderly cryptogenic stroke patients after comprehensive evaluation.

Title: Echocardiographic response and predictors of reverse remodeling after sacubitril/valsartan in de novo heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sacubitril/valsartan (angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, ARNI) improves outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet treatment response varies and predictors of response remain incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate real-world echocardiographic responses to ARNI and identify predictors of favorable response in patients with newly diagnosed HFrEF.
METHODS: Consecutive patients who initiated ARNI at Uijeongbu Eulji University Hospital between March 2021 and August 2024 were prospectively enrolled. Echocardiographic reverse remodeling was assessed by changes in left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF). Based on the degree of echocardiographic response, patients were categorized as nonresponders [follow-up left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <40% and an absolute increased in LVEF <10%], partial responders (follow-up LVEF ≥40% and <50%, or an absolute increase in LVEF ≥10% with follow-up LVEF <50%), or super responders (follow-up LVEF ≥50%). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and predictors of response were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 392 patients who completed follow-up echocardiography (median follow-up interval, 11.0 months), 116 (29.6%) were nonresponders, 110 (28.0%) were partial responders, and 166 (42.3%) were super responders with a recovery of LVEF ≥50%. During a median follow-up of 708 days, nonresponders experienced significantly higher rates of clinical events, including death or heart failure rehospitalization, compared with responders (P<0.001). In multivariable analysis, higher baseline systolic blood pressure [SBP; odds ratio (OR), 1.249; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.120-1.400] and smaller LV end-diastolic volume (OR 0.919; 95% CI: 0.869-0.970) were independently associated with favorable echocardiographic response. Although a substantial proportion of patients did not achieve ARNI doses ≥200 mg/day, exploratory analysis did not demonstrate a significant association between ARNI dose and echocardiographic response or clinical outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort study, ARNI therapy was associated with substantial reverse remodeling and improved clinical outcomes despite low rates of target-dose attainment. Baseline SBP and LV remodeling parameters were associated with treatment response, supporting individualized ARNI titration strategies in clinical practice.

Title: Impact of super resolution deep learning reconstruction with a 1024 matrix on CAD-RADS classification of intermediate coronary stenosis: A bicentric retrospective study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Moderate coronary stenosis (CAD-RADS 3) is a diagnostic gray zone in coronary CT angiography (CCTA). We evaluated whether super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR), particularly with a 1024 matrix, modifies CAD-RADS classification and inter-reader agreement. Materials and methods: Thirty-nine CCTA examinations from two centers, each containing at least one 50-69% stenosis identified on the routine normal-resolution deep learning reconstruction (NR-DLR), were reconstructed with NR-DLR and SR-DLR (512 and 1024 matrices). Five experienced readers blindly assigned CAD-RADS categories. Agreement was assessed with Gwet's AC2 and paired reclassification with exact McNemar tests. Subgroup analyses (plaque composition, initial image quality) were exploratory.
RESULTS: Forty-six lesions were analyzed (19 calcified, 16 mixed, 10 non-calcified, one in-stent). Agreement remained excellent (AC2 0.89 [0.86-0.92], 0.87 [0.83-0.90] and 0.84 [0.81-0.88] for NR-DLR, SR-DLR-512 and SR-DLR-1024). Consensus CAD-RADS 2 rose from 6.5% to 21.7% with SR-DLR-1024 (p = 0.016; 10 lesions downgraded, 2 upgraded), predominantly in lesions with non-calcified components. Per-reader CAD-RADS 2 rates ranged from 13% to 30%, increasing significantly for two of five readers (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: SR-DLR-1024 modified CAD-RADS classification in about one fifth of intermediate lesions while preserving excellent agreement. Without an invasive reference standard, these reclassifications reflect a change in reader interpretation rather than a proven gain in accuracy.

Title: Association of carotid atherosclerotic disease on ultrasound with functionally relevant coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study, a subanalysis of BASEL VIII.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis is a systemic disease underlying coronary artery disease (CAD), and carotid atherosclerosis may serve as an accessible marker of systemic atherosclerotic burden. However, the diagnostic and prognostic relevance of carotid plaque characteristics in patients with suspected functionally relevant coronary artery disease (fCAD) remains uncertain. We aimed to investigate the association of carotid atherosclerotic plaque burden and morphology with fCAD and to evaluate the prognostic value of carotid plaque characteristics for future cardiovascular events.
METHODS: This prospective diagnostic subanalysis of the BASEL VIII cohort included 430 consecutive patients evaluated for suspected fCAD at the University Hospital Basel, Switzerland, between October 2011 and February 2016. fCAD was determined by myocardial perfusion imaging using single-photon emission computed tomography, supplemented by coronary angiography and fractional flow reserve measurements when available. Carotid ultrasound and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) were performed at enrollment to assess plaque presence, burden, stenosis severity, echogenicity, and intraplaque neovascularization. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death, were assessed during long-term follow-up using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: The study included 430 patients with suspected fCAD, of whom 105 (24.4%) were women. fCAD was confirmed in 136 patients (31.6%). Patients with fCAD more frequently exhibited carotid plaques than those without fCAD (78.7% vs. 68.0%, P=0.02). However, plaque burden, stenosis severity, plaque echogenicity, and intraplaque neovascularization were not significantly associated with fCAD. During 8 years of follow-up, 30 patients (7.0%) experienced non-fatal myocardial infarction, 17 (4.0%) suffered stroke, and 34 (7.9%) died from cardiovascular causes. The presence of carotid atherosclerotic disease was significantly associated with a higher risk of MACE [hazard ratio (HR) 2.69, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.33-5.45]. This association remained significant after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors and fCAD (HR 2.14, 95% CI: 1.09-4.42). In contrast, plaque morphology characteristics, including echogenicity and intraplaque neovascularization, did not provide additional diagnostic or prognostic value.
CONCLUSIONS: The presence of carotid atherosclerotic plaques was associated with fCAD and with an increased risk of future cardiovascular events in patients evaluated for suspected fCAD. However, carotid plaque burden, stenosis severity, echogenicity, and intraplaque neovascularization do not appear to improve the identification of fCAD or the prediction of long-term cardiovascular outcomes. In clinical practice, carotid plaque presence may provide complementary information on systemic atherosclerotic burden, whereas advanced carotid plaque characterization does not appear to add clinically relevant diagnostic or prognostic information in this patient population.

Title: Physical activity trajectories after mild ischemic stroke and their association with 6-month functional outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether post-stroke physical activity (PA) patterns are associated with stroke prognosis remains unclear. We aimed to examine the association between post-stroke PA trajectories and 6-month functional outcomes in patients with mild ischemic stroke.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included patients with mild ischemic stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score ≤ 5) admitted to a teaching hospital between July 2024 and March 2025. PA was assessed using the Saltin-Grimby Physical Activity Level Scale at pre-stroke, 1, and 3 months. PA trajectories from pre-stroke to 3 months post-stroke were identified using growth mixture modeling, yielding three PA trajectories: stable low, increased, and decreased. The primary outcome was functional independence (defined as a score of 0-2 on the modified Rankin Scale; range, 0-6, with higher scores indicating more severe disability) at six months. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between PA trajectories and the primary outcome, adjusted for prespecified baseline covariates (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, and atrial fibrillation).
RESULTS: Among 502 patients (median age, 66 years [IQR 57-72]; 354 males [70.52%]), functional independence at 6 months was achieved in 166 patients with stable low PA (80.58%), 177 with increased PA (88.06%), and 74 with decreased PA (77.89%). The overall three-level test for the trajectory variable was not statistically significant (P = 0.086). In an exploratory pairwise comparison, compared with decreased PA, the odds of functional independence were 2.03 (95% CI 1.05-3.90; P = 0.034) for increased PA and 1.29 (95% CI 0.70-2.36; P = 0.418) for stable low PA.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the overall trajectory test was not significant, an exploratory pairwise comparison suggested that an increased PA trajectory was associated with better functional independence compared with a decreased trajectory. These findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation; causality cannot be inferred.

Title: Frontal QRS-T angle in patients with Graves' disease: association with thyroid function and cardiovascular parameters.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thyroid hormone excess may alter ventricular electrophysiology, affecting both depolarization and repolarization. The frontal QRS-T (fQRS-T) angle reflects the directional relationship between these processes and may provide information on ventricular electrical heterogeneity. However, data on the fQRS-T angle in overt hyperthyroidism (OHT) remain limited. We evaluated the fQRS-T angle in patients with Graves' disease presenting with OHT compared with euthyroid controls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 55 patients with Graves' disease and biochemically confirmed OHT and 42 euthyroid controls. Frontal QRS and T axes were calculated from ECG measurements in leads I and aVF. Between-group comparisons, multivariable regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and heart rate, sensitivity analyses, ROC analysis, and correlations with thyroid function parameters were performed. Results: The median fQRS-T angle was greater in patients with OHT than in controls (21.89° [12.37-44.09] vs. 17.36° [9.02-27.29], p = 0.006), with a rank-biserial correlation of 0.328 (95% CI 0.106-0.535). An fQRS-T angle >45° occurred in 23.6% of patients with OHT and in none of the controls (p < 0.001), whereas the QRS and T axes did not differ significantly between groups. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and heart rate, OHT remained associated with a greater fQRS-T angle (β = 9.00°, 95% CI 1.77-16.22; p = 0.015), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses. Discriminatory performance was modest (AUC 0.664, 95% CI 0.552-0.768). No significant associations were observed between fQRS-T angle and FT3, FT4, TSH, or heart rate.
DISCUSSION: Patients with Graves' disease and OHT exhibited greater discordance between ventricular depolarization and repolarization despite similar individual QRS and T axes. This association persisted after adjustment for heart rate and other potential confounders, suggesting that fQRS-T widening may reflect electrophysiological alterations associated with OHT rather than tachycardia alone.
CONCLUSION: Overt hyperthyroidism due to Graves' disease is associated with a wider fQRS-T angle independently of age, sex, body mass index, and heart rate. Larger prospective, multicenter studies with longitudinal ECG assessment are needed to determine the reversibility and prognostic significance of these alterations.

Title: Diagnostic delay and predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely diagnosis is essential for acute treatment of in-hospital stroke. We aimed to investigate factors associated with diagnostic delay and clinical predictors of true stroke among patients with suspected in-hospital stroke.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we screened head computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging orders between Jan 2023 and Jan 2026 for patients hospitalized outside the Departments of Neurology and Neurosurgery who developed new neurological symptoms within 24 h of symptom onset or last known well and were clinically suspected of having in-hospital stroke. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify factors associated with diagnostic delay and true stroke.
RESULTS: A total of 183 patients (110 men, median age 77 years) were included. Median time from last known well to imaging-based final diagnosis was 292 min. Overall, 77 patients (42.1%) had true stroke, including 70 ischemic strokes, 5 intracerebral hemorrhages, and 2 subarachnoid hemorrhages. Wake-up symptom onset [Exp (β) 3.34, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.61-4.28] and initial medical emergency team activation [Exp (β) 0.71, 95% CI 0.56-0.91] were associated with diagnostic delay. Persistent neurological symptoms [odds ratio (OR) 1.44, 95% CI 1.24-1.68] and FAST-positive symptoms (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.12-1.46) were associated with true stroke. Among the 70 patients with ischemic stroke, 17 (24.3%) underwent reperfusion therapy.
CONCLUSION: Wake-up symptom onset and medical emergency team activation were associated with diagnostic delay, whereas persistent and FAST-positive symptoms were associated with true stroke. These findings may facilitate earlier recognition and improve triaging patients with suspected in-hospital stroke.

Title: Brachial artery flow-mediated dilation and mean platelet volume in relation to diabetic retinopathy severity in type 2 diabetes: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the cross-sectional associations of brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and mean platelet volume (MPV) with diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes duration, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and systolic blood pressure; carotid ultrasound measures were examined secondarily.
METHODS: This single-center, hospital-based cross-sectional study retrospectively analyzed clinical and imaging data obtained during routine inpatient care through a standardized multidisciplinary assessment pathway from 109 hospitalized adults with T2DM between June 2015 and December 2019: 46 with no DR (NDR), 36 with non-proliferative DR (NPDR), and 27 with proliferative DR (PDR). The main exploratory complete-case proportional-odds model included 86 participants (36 NDR, 30 NPDR, and 20 PDR) and simultaneously included age, sex, diabetes duration, HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, FMD, and MPV; a nephropathy-adjusted model and a ridge-penalized model were examined as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Median FMD was 6.9%, 6.1%, and 5.3% in the NDR, NPDR, and PDR groups (Kruskal-Wallis P = .025), and median MPV was 9.30, 9.60, and 10.00 fL (P = .012). In the main exploratory complete-case model (N = 86), lower FMD (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per 1-percentage-point increase, 0.831; 95% CI, 0.713-0.968; P = .018) and higher MPV (adjusted OR per 1-fL increase, 1.898; 95% CI, 1.238-2.912; P = .003) were associated with greater DR severity. After additional adjustment for recorded diabetic nephropathy, the FMD estimate was attenuated (OR, 0.855; 95% CI, 0.732-0.998), whereas the MPV estimate was preserved (OR, 2.166; 95% CI, 1.356-3.458). In a ridge-penalized sensitivity model, both estimates were attenuated (FMD OR, 0.899 and 0.919; MPV OR, 1.388 and 1.289 at the minimum-loss and one-standard-error penalties, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower brachial FMD and higher MPV were associated with greater DR severity in this selected hospital-based cross-sectional sample; the FMD association was sensitive to renal adjustment, and both associations, particularly that for MPV, were noticeably attenuated under penalization. These exploratory findings do not establish temporal sequence, causality, predictive performance, or clinical utility and require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

Title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Regional Myocardial Flow Reserve Beyond Global Flow and Perfusion: REFINE PET.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incremental prognostic value of regional myocardial flow reserve (MFR) assessed by positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) beyond global MFR remains unclear. We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of regional MFR in the international multicenter REFINE PET registry.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 35,391 patients from 13 sites in the international REFINE PET registry who underwent rubidium-82 ( 82 Rb) and 13 N-ammonia ( 13 NH 3 ) PET MPI. Abnormal MFR was defined as <2.0. Patients were classified into three groups: MFR-Group 1 (normal global and regional MFR; n=19,744), MFR-Group 2 (normal global MFR but abnormal regional MFR; n=3,184), and MFR-Group 3 (abnormal global and regional MFR; n=12,463). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) included all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, late revascularization (>90 days), and hospital admission for unstable angina.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 4.0 ± 2.9 years, 9,903 patients (28.0%) experienced MACE. Annualized MACE rates increased stepwise across MFR-Groups 1-3 (4.0%/year, 7.5%/year, and 11.8%/year, respectively; p <0.001). Abnormal regional MFR independently predicted MACE after adjustment for clinical risk factors, global MFR, and stress total perfusion deficit (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.25-1.43). Adding regional MFR to a model including global MFR significantly improved model fit (χ² 4,784 to 4,871; p <0.001), discrimination (AUC 0.710 to 0.729; p <0.001), and reclassification (NRI 41.9%). Among patients with normal perfusion and preserved global MFR, abnormal regional MFR identified higher risk (5.0%/year vs. 2.8%/year; p <0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Regional MFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional PET MPI findings, including global MFR, and may refine risk stratification, particularly when global MFR is preserved.
CLINICAL PERSPECTIVES: Global myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is widely used for risk stratification in patients undergoing positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). However, regional abnormalities in MFR may be overlooked when global MFR is preserved. In this international multicenter study of 35,391 patients, abnormal regional MFR was independently associated with major adverse cardiovascular events and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical and PET-MPI findings, including global MFR and myocardial perfusion abnormalities. Importantly, even among patients with normal perfusion and preserved global MFR, those with abnormal regional MFR had a substantially higher annualized event rate than those with normal regional MFR (5.0% versus 2.8%). These findings highlight the importance of assessing regional MFR in addition to global MFR during routine PET-MPI interpretation.

Title: Impact of sampling site on Activated Clotting Time (ACT) during cryoballoon ablation: Left atrium vs femoral sheath.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Activated clotting time (ACT) is used to monitor unfractionated heparin (UFH) during left atrial (LA) ablation procedures. Inadequate anticoagulation increases thromboembolic risk, while excessive UFH may increase bleeding. ACT can be sampled from a femoral venous sheath (ACTFV) or from oxygenated blood within the LA (ACTLA). The influence of sampling site on ACT values during atrial fibrillation ablation is unknown.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, consecutive patients undergoing cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation received intravenous UFH. ACT was sampled sequentially from the LA and from a femoral venous sheath. All samples were analyzed on the same point-of-care ACT machine. Non-inferiority of LA relative to femoral venous sampling was tested against a 30-s margin, with agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa at 300 s and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: Sixty-two patients were recruited (42% female; CHA2DS2-VASc 3.1 ± 1.8); 61 had paired samples. Mean ACTLA was 365 ± 83 and ACTFV was 359 ± 65 s (p = 0.455). The mean paired difference (ACTLA - ACTFV) was +6.1 s (upper one-sided 97.5% confidence limit +22.4 s), below the 30-s non-inferiority margin (p = 0.002). Bland-Altman limits of agreement were - 119 to +131 s, with significant proportional bias (β = 0.288, p = 0.017). Dichotomized at 300 s, Cohen's kappa was 0.586 (moderate concordance).
CONCLUSIONS: ACT sampling from the LA was non-inferior to femoral venous sampling within a 30-s margin, supporting the use of either sampling site during LA ablation. Despite notable variability between paired measurements, unexpected ACT values should prompt repeat testing rather than be attributed to the sampling site.

Title: Detection of Spreading Depolarization with Noninvasive Electroencephalography.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Spreading depolarizations (SDs) are waves of near-complete breakdown of the transmembrane ion gradients that underlie migraine aura and occur in patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic, ischemic or hemorrhagic brain injury. SDs are involved in primary and secondary brain injury. They are associated with poor neurological outcome and represent a modifiable therapeutic target. However, despite decades of investigation, SD detection still requires invasive subdural electrocorticography (ECoG) using an implanted subdural electrode strip, restricting monitoring to a small subset of neurosurgical patients.
METHODS: We developed WAVEFRONT, a noninvasive scalp electroencephalography (EEG) biomarker of SD based on spatiotemporal propagation characteristics of delta-band EEG activity. The biomarker was trained and validated using concurrent, multi-day scalp EEG and invasive subdural electrocorticography recordings from patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), or malignant hemispheric stroke (MHS) across three institutions. We assessed out-of-sample performance across institutions, diagnosis, and surgical approaches, as well as calibration, temporal synchrony, and spatial specificity relative to gold-standard SDs annotated on ECoG. Clinical utility was further evaluated in 607 patients comatose after cardiac arrest from the multicenter International Cardiac Arrest REsearch (I-CARE) consortium, a population in whom invasive monitoring is not performed. Outcome analyses excluded patients who died (Cerebral Performance Category [CPC] 5) because death may reflect decisions to withdraw life-sustaining treatment in addition to neurological injury.
RESULTS: A total of 1,119 gold-standard SDs were annotated in 32 patients (TBI, n=17; SAH, n=12; MHS, n=3; range 0-187 SDs per patient). Across exhaustive cross-validation and institution-, diagnosis-, and surgical approach-based hold-out analyses, WAVEFRONT models trained on one set of patients consistently maintained high performance when evaluated in previously unseen out-of-group cohorts. At the optimal operating point, WAVEFRONT achieved a mean cross-validated true positive rate of 97.3±1% with a false positive rate of 6.0±0.5%, calculated over 2-min sliding windows with 30-s overlaps. The cumulative duration of WAVEFRONT detections within 30-hour windows strongly correlated with the number of SDs measured by invasive ECoG (R 2 =0.7411). Scalp-detected depressions were spatially consistent with the location of the invasive recording strip, and visual inspection demonstrated close temporal correspondence with invasive detections, including during SD clusters. External validation in the independent I-CARE cohort using WAVEFRONT trained on the invasive-monitoring cohort demonstrated significantly greater SD burden on day 3 of post-arrest EEG monitoring among patients with poor neurological outcome (CPC 3-4, n=29) than those with good outcome (CPC 1-2, n=225; p=0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: Eight decades after Leão's description of SD in 1944, we propose and validate a noninvasive scalp EEG biomarker of SD. Consistent performance across institution-, diagnosis-, and surgical approach-based hold-out analyses, together with burden calibration, spatial specificity, and temporal synchrony with ECoG detections, supports the validity of the WAVEFRONT framework. The association of biomarker burden with neurologic outcome after cardiac arrest suggests that noninvasive monitoring may enable investigation of spreading depolarizations in populations where invasive monitoring is not feasible. Future studies should evaluate prospective performance, treatment responsiveness, and disease-specific associations of the SD biomarker with clinical outcome.

Title: Gastrointestinal medication use patterns and incident depressive symptoms among adults aged 50 years or older: a prospective multicohort study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive symptoms contribute substantially to disability and loss of independence in later life, and gastrointestinal illness frequently co-occurs with affective vulnerability. However, evidence linking gastrointestinal medication use to subsequent depressive symptoms remains largely confined to single countries and cross-sectional assessments. We investigated whether baseline gastrointestinal medication use and longitudinal two-wave medication-use patterns are associated with incident depressive symptoms across three prospective ageing cohorts.
METHODS: We analysed community-dwelling adults aged 50 years or older from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS), and the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) who scored below cohort-specific depressive-symptom thresholds at baseline, followed for a median of 8-11 years. Baseline medication use was compared with non-use; two-wave patterns comprised continued non-use (reference), initiation, discontinuation, and persistent use at both waves. Cohort-specific Cox proportional hazards models with cluster-robust standard errors adjusted for sociodemographic, behavioural, and chronic health covariates (multiple imputation for missing data); estimates were synthesised using random-effects meta-analysis. Negative- and positive-control medications and Fine-Gray competing-risk regression models evaluated specificity and survival bias.
RESULTS: The baseline analysis included 50,467 participants (median age 59-65 years; 44.4%-56.8% female) with 16,896 incident depressive events; the two-wave analysis included 32,686 participants with 8,069 events. Pooled adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were 1.31 (95% CI 1.21-1.41; I ² = 29%) for baseline use and 1.34 (95% CI 1.22-1.47; I ² = 0%) for persistent use; initiation (1.27, 1.13-1.43) and discontinuation (1.25, 1.11-1.40) showed consistent risk elevations across cohorts. Antihypertensive and lipid-lowering medications (negative controls) showed null associations with incident depression, whereas psychiatric medications (positive control) showed the expected strong relationship (pooled HR 1.99, 95% CI 1.79-2.22). The association remained robust after further adjusting for continuous baseline subthreshold depressive symptoms (pooled HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.14-1.27; I ² = 0%), and medicated digestive disease carried higher risk than untreated digestive disease (pooled HR 1.18, 95% CI 1.05-1.32; I ² = 0%). Accounting for competing mortality did not alter the estimates.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline and persistent gastrointestinal medication use were consistently associated with increased risk of incident depressive symptoms across three cross-national ageing cohorts with negligible heterogeneity. These findings support integrating routine affective screening into medication reviews for older adults receiving gastrointestinal pharmacotherapy, while maintaining guideline-directed management of digestive conditions.

Title: Genetics in Context: Social Factors Modify Polygenic Risk Across Multiple Cardiometabolic Diseases.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) are increasingly used for disease prediction, but whether their associations vary across social contexts remains poorly understood. Here, we leveraged the large and diverse All of Us cohort to examine interactions between PRS and social determinants of health (SDoH) across eight prevalent chronic diseases and developed disease-specific polysocial risk scores (PsRS). We found consistent evidence of SDoH modification of PRS- disease associations for cardiometabolic diseases, including type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease and chronic kidney disease, with PRS associations attenuated among more socially vulnerable populations. Joint modeling of PsRS and PRS significantly improved case status prediction across all eight diseases and PsRS were predictive for most diseases in external cohorts. These findings demonstrate that social context modifies associations between genetic risk and disease and suggest that integrating genetic and social information can refine disease prediction across diverse populations.
TEASER: Both genetics and the environment influence chronic disease, but whether and how they interact remains understudied. We find evidence of genetic effect modification of polygenic risk scores (PRS) by social factors for multiple cardiometabolic traits and that jointly modeling social risk improves disease prediction across a range of chronic diseases.

Title: A Local Enrichment Computational Framework to Identify Disease-Enriched Physical Activity Patterns.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract: Wearable accelerometers enable continuous monitoring of physical activity (PA), yet conventional summary measures and population-wide clustering approaches may overlook disease-associated behavioral heterogeneity. Here we introduce LocPA, a computational framework that identifies disease-enriched PA patterns through confounder-adjusted activity profiling, similarity network construction, local disease-enrichment testing and community detection. Applying LocPA to 24-hour accelerometry profiles from the UK Biobank, we identified two recurring PA phenotypes across six diseases spanning cardiometabolic, neurological, psychiatric, renal and cardiovascular conditions: a low-activity phenotype characterized by reduced daytime activity and a sleep-disrupted phenotype characterized by reduced daytime and elevated nocturnal activity. In hypertension and diabetes, the sleep-disrupted phenotype was associated with greater disease burden and less favorable clinical and metabolic profiles, differences not consistently captured by conventional PA summary measures. LocPA also identified disease-specific temporal patterns, particularly in Parkinsons disease. Analyses in an independent National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort supported the recurrence of hypertension- and diabetes-enriched patterns across populations and accelerometry measurements. LocPA provides a flexible, disease-driven approach for uncovering clinically relevant temporal PA patterns, with potential applications in disease risk characterization and personalized behavioral interventions.

Title: Polygenic Risk and Genomic Signals in Premature Coronary Artery Disease.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature coronary artery disease (pCAD) is a distinct presentation of CAD. Using the All of Us (AoU) Research Program data, we compared pCAD with later-onset CAD across cardiometabolic, polygenic, and genome-wide domains.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional case-case analysis of All of Us Research Program (AoU) participants with established CAD. pCAD was defined as first CAD event before age 55 years in males and before age 65 in females; later-onset CAD was defined as the first CAD event at or after age threshold. Pre-index cardiometabolic measures were extracted from electronic health records and modelled with logistic regression.
