Using 607,719 variants, a CAD polygenic risk score (PRS) was constructed using published summary statistics and short-read whole-genome sequencing data (srWGS). Results were standardized within self-reported race groups, and evaluated overall, by race, and with a PRS x race interaction. A case-case genome-wide association study (GWAS) compared pCAD with later-onset CAD.
RESULTS: The CAD cohort included 49,919 participants, including 18,455 with pCAD and 31,464 with later-onset CAD. Participants with pCAD had higher BMI, LDL cholesterol and diastolic blood pressure, and lower HDL cholesterol, serum calcium, and systolic blood pressure. Higher BMI and LDL cholesterol were positively associated with higher odds of pCAD, whereas higher HDL cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, and serum calcium were inversely associated. PRS was associated with greater odds of pCAD in the genomic models (OR per 1-SD higher PRS, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.12-1.17; P <0.001). Analyses stratified by race showed PRS association was present among White participants but was not observed among Black participants. In the case-case GWAS, one variant reached genome-wide significance at 2q24.3 (rs13383835; OR=1.20; 95% CI, 1.13-1.27; P =5.8x10 -9 ). A total of 137 variants met an exploratory threshold of P <1x10 -5 .
CONCLUSIONS: Premature onset of CAD is characterized by a distinct cardiometabolic profile driven by modifiable risk factors, greater polygenic burden, and genomic signals associated with earlier disease timing. A European-derived PRS did not transfer to Black participants, who were overrepresented in pCAD. Together, these findings support pCAD as a clinically and genetically distinct presentation of CAD and highlight the need for ancestry-specific validation of genomic risk tools in diverse cohorts.

Title: Routine Chest CTA Reliably Quantifies Left Ventricular Myocardial Mass.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine chest computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the primary imaging modality for thoracic aortic disease, yet cardiac information within these examinations remains underutilized. We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non-electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology.
METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection. LVMM was quantified using automated three-dimensional segmentation. In a separate 10-patient validation cohort, LVMM was compared across end-systolic, end-diastolic, and non-ECG-gated source reconstructions. CTA-derived LVMM was compared with published echocardiographic and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reference values using Cohen's d.
RESULTS: LVMM remained stable across cardiac phases and non-ECG-gated images (mean coefficient of variation, 2.4%), whereas left ventricular volume varied substantially (36.9%). CTA-derived LVMM demonstrated small effect sizes with the Penn method ( d = 0.22) and moderate effect sizes with ASE linear ( d = 0.67), area-length ( d = 0.68), and CMR ( d = 0.63). LVMM increased through young adulthood, with minimal association with age beyond 30 years. LVMM was comparable between patients with thoracic aneurysms and normal adults (140 ± 43 g vs. 141 ± 40 g; adjusted p = 1.0) but significantly greater in acute (199 ± 61 g) and chronic (191 ± 57 g) aortic dissection (both adjusted p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine non-ECG-gated chest CTA enables reliable automated LVMM quantification without additional imaging or radiation and may facilitate large-scale investigations of ventricular remodeling in thoracic aortic disease.

Title: The genetic, clinical and immune landscape of clonal hematopoiesis across adulthood in the multi-ancestry Mount Sinai Million cohort.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), the age-associated expansion of blood cell clones carrying acquired driver mutations, remains less well characterized in young adults, across genetic ancestries, and in clinical populations. We analyzed whole-exome sequencing and longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from 59,598 adults in the Mount Sinai Million Health Discoveries Program, an urban, multi-ancestry hospital-based cohort that includes substantial representation of African (∼35%) and Admixed American genetic ancestry (∼15%) and young adults aged 18-39 years (∼30%). After sample QC, separate analyses were performed in discovery (n = 28,051) and validation (n = 26,938) cohorts defined by sequencing platform and combined by meta-analysis. CHIP was detected in 8.5% of participants in each cohort and in 4.0% of young adults, with D NMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, and PPM1D the most frequently mutated genes. Prevalence and clone size increased with age across ancestry groups. After adjusting for age, participants of African ancestry had lower CHIP prevalence than those of European ancestry in both cohorts (discovery: OR=0.86, 95% CI = 0.78-0.95, p =0.002; validation: OR=0.84, 95% CI = 0.75-0.93, p =0.001). Participants of Admixed American ancestry showed a similar trend. Higher systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) was associated with CHIP after adjusting for age, sex and ancestry in both cohorts (pooled OR=1.30, 95% CI = 1.15-1.48, p =4.78e-5). Heterozygosity at an HLA class II locus HLA-DPA1 was associated with 7% lower odds of overall CHIP (pooled OR=0.93, 95% CI = 0.87-0.99, p =0.03). Driver-stratified analyses revealed distinct HLA class II nominal association patterns for DNMT3A - and TET2 -mutant CHIP. Particularly, HLA-DQB1 heterozygosity associated with lower odds of TET2 -mutant CHIP (pooled OR=0.84, 95% CI = 0.70-1.00, p =0.05), HLA-DQA1 and HLA-DOB heterozygosity associated with higher odds of DNMT3A -mutant CHIP (pooled OR=1.19, 95% CI = 1.00-1.42, p =0.05; pooled OR=1.12, 95% CI = 1.01-1.25, p =0.03 respectively). Longitudinal EHR analyses revealed CHIP associations with several incident diseases that varied by driver gene and clone size. The broadest pattern of associations involved high-risk CHIP genes and encompassed hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, cardiovascular outcomes, hypertension, and COPD. High-VAF clones were the main drivers of these associations. Among adults aged ≥40 years, phenome-wide analyses identified a Bonferroni-significant association with incident myeloproliferative disease and nominal associations with incident pancytopenia, anemia, cardiomegaly, and chronic renal failure. Young-adult CHIP was nominally associated with incident nodular goiter and esophageal disease. These findings characterize CHIP across adulthood and genetic ancestry and reveal inherited immune variation and systemic inflammation as correlates in a hospital-based population.

Title: Computational alternative to cardiac biopsy in multiple myeloma: utilizing the shape of routine laboratory data for the classification of AL cardiac amyloidosis.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with multiple myeloma (MM) are at increased risk for light chain cardiac amyloidosis (CA) due to high circulating levels of light chains. ALCA is a clinical diagnosis based on biopsy, cardiac imaging findings of restrictive cardiomyopathy, and serum monoclonal proteins. To overcome these challenges, we have developed machine learning models that accurately predict ALCA status while identifying key diagnostic features based on routine laboratory measurements and using limited data.
METHODS: Utilizing electronic medical data (EMR) data, we built support vector machine models (SVMs) using the MISTIC framework. Data including diagnosis history, treatment, and laboratory values for patients with MM or monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance (MGUS) were collected as a retrospective cohort study at Moffit Cancer Center and Research Institute between 2014 and 2019. To utilize the wealth of information in longitudinal EMR data, we fit regression models to the EMR data and used the parameters and characteristics of the fits as features for our SVMs. We tested three different sets of features: descriptive statistics alone, parameters and characteristics of fit only, and both the descriptive statistics and parameters of fit (DescFits). A classifier using raw data at a timepoint proximal to the date of ALCA diagnostic imaging (EchoAdj), as well as analogous random forest and XGBoost models were used for comparison.
FINDINGS: SVM classifiers trained on the DescFits feature set (AUC= 1·0) outperformed blind model predictions of the EchoAdj model (AUC = 0·36) and other conventional machine learning approaches in identifying which patients were diagnosed with ALCA. The DescFits model selected features describing the temporal relationship of physiologic parameters including hematologic state, and cardiac and renal function.
INTERPRETATION: We demonstrated that the MISTIC SVM framework and the shape of EMR data can aid in identifying patients with cardiac amyloidosis without cardiac biopsy or imaging.

Title: Stage-dependent associations of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Cognitive Decline, Depression, and Neuroimaging Signatures in multi-regional older adults.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a multisystem condition associated with adverse outcomes, yet its impact on age-related cognitive health remains understudied. We examined associations of CKM with neurocognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes, modifiable physical and psychosocial factors contributing to cognitive impairment across CKM stages, and neuroimaging correlates.
METHODS: Global aging cohorts (mean follow-up 6.5 years) and the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (5.4 years) were used. CKM stages (0-4) were defined according to AHA framework. Longitudinal domain-specific cognitive changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models, and depressive symptoms using generalized linear regression with individual participant data approach. Population-attributable fractions were estimated for six modifiable factors associated with cognitive impairment across CKM stages. Cross-sectional associations with 34 neuroimaging biomarkers were examined in UK Biobank.
RESULTS: Among 28,242 participants, advanced CKM stages (3-4) were associated with accelerated cognitive decline, particularly in attention, executive function, and language. Associations were stronger in younger individuals, men, and those with less education, but not modified by APOE ε4 status. Advanced CKM stages were associated with depressive symptoms among cognitively unimpaired individuals. Modifiable factors accounted for 24.8% of cognitive impairment risk across CKM stages, mainly social isolation (7.0%), depressive symptoms (5.2%), and physical inactivity (5.2%). Advanced CKM stages were linked to widespread MRI alterations (27 biomarkers), especially white matter hyperintensity.
CONCLUSION: Advanced CKM stages are associated with accelerated cognitive decline and greater cerebrovascular burden. Addressing psychosocial factors and physical inactivity, alongside management of CKM risk factors, may help reduce cognitive impairment.

Title: Multimodality imaging to enhance substrate characterization for ventricular tachycardia ablation: what's new?
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Image integration is now widely used to delineate the ventricular tachycardia substrate, and the first randomized data have appeared. We review developments of the past 18 months relevant to the practicing ablationist, with attention to what imaging-defined scar represents and how it should be applied at the bedside.
RECENT FINDINGS: Imaging-defined scar has been validated against co-registered whole-heart histology, confirming that most CMR channels correspond to bundles of surviving myocytes. Both commercially available platforms identify compact scar but underestimate nonconfluent scar, particularly in the epicardium. Intramyocardial fat rather than fibrosis alone distinguishes arrhythmogenic channel segments, making computed tomography complementary to cardiac magnetic resonance. The first randomized trial of image integration (InEurHeart) demonstrated that computed tomography-guided ablation shortened procedures without compromising safety. The landscape of image integration continues to evolve. Photon-counting detector computed tomography has entered clinical comparison, and digital twin-guided ablation has reached first clinical use.
SUMMARY: Imaging modality selection should follow aetiology, with intracardiac echocardiography used adjunctively wherever available. Advances in imaging protocols and integration offer novel toolkits for the clinician ablating ventricular tachycardia targets. Future studies should remember to validate image integration against mapped or surmised ventricular tachycardia circuits.

Title: The odyssey of inflammation: pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation as a dynamic marker of coronary-specific inflammation.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Inflammation drives atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, yet targeted therapies remain scarce, and identifying which patients benefit has been a central challenge. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), a systemic marker, has been used to select patients for anti-inflammatory trials but has proven neither sufficient nor necessary: the Ziltivekimab Cardiovascular Outcomes Trial (ZEUS), a recent phase 3 trial of an anti-interleukin-6 agent, lowered hsCRP yet did not reduce events, whereas colchicine reduced cardiovascular events in COLCOT and LoDoCo2 without hsCRP-based selection. Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) attenuation offers a novel, coronary-specific measure of inflammation; whether it translates into better patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy remains to be shown.
RECENT FINDINGS: Measured from routine coronary CT angiography (CCTA), PCAT attenuation reflects inflammation within the coronary wall and, in large observational cohorts, predicts cardiac events independent of plaque burden, traditional risk factors, and hsCRP. Early interventional studies suggest it may also serve as a dynamic endpoint, though this evidence remains preliminary.
SUMMARY: PCAT attenuation could enable precision anti-inflammatory prevention - selecting patients by coronary inflammatory risk rather than nonspecific systemic markers, and serving as a pharmacodynamic endpoint in mechanistic trials. Key gaps remain: randomized evidence that PCAT-guided care improves outcomes, treatment thresholds, longitudinal stability, reproducibility, and contrast-free validation.

Title: HDL and apoB: physiological and pathophysiological intersections and interactions.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To reexamine why high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) has been widely dismissed as a causal factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and to point to evidence of interactions between HDL particles and apolipoprotein B (apoB) that may modify risk.
RECENT FINDINGS: Notwithstanding the epidemiological evidence of a potent inverse relation between HDL-C and ASCVD risk, neither Mendelian randomization analyses nor randomized clinical trials with multiple classes of agents have confirmed a causal connection. However, this assumes HDL-C is a valid physiological entity, which it is not. HDL-C is a construct, the arithmetic sum of the cholesterol within the HDL particles. Cholesterol is only one constituent of these particles and, at most, cholesterol is a physiological product whereas other elements in the particle would be the physiological actors. HDL-C is only a surrogate for HDL particles. The relation of HDL-C to ASCVD risk persists after triglycerides are accounted for. Evidence of a potentially positive clinical interaction between HDL-C and apoB will be identified.
SUMMARY: HDL-C is a useful clinical and research tool but not a biological entity. Any putative biological property of HDL must relate to a specific class or classes of HDL particles. However, HDL-C remains a valid tool to assess the risk of ASCVD.

Title: Cessation of oral anticoagulation after atrial fibrillation ablation: who and when?
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The ideal long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC) management strategy for patients who have undergone successful catheter-based atrial fibrillation ablation is not well defined. Over the past 20  years, observational studies suggested that OAC could be safely discontinued for patients with intermediate thromboembolic risk, but randomized trial data were lacking to inform clinical practice.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recently, two randomized clinical trials on this topic have been published: The Optimal Anticoagulation for Enhanced Risk Patients Post-Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (OCEAN) and Anticoagulation One Year after Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF). These trials showed that OAC cessation at 1 year after successful atrial fibrillation ablation was not associated with increased thromboembolic risk for patients with an intermediate stroke risk profile (i.e. CHA2DS2-VASc 1-3 points). In both trials, the annualized rate of thromboembolism was below 1%. Patients with higher thromboembolic risk (i.e. CHA2DS2-VASc ≥4 points or history of stroke/transient ischemic attack) were minimally represented in these trials.
SUMMARY: For patients without high-risk features for thromboembolism, the OCEAN and ALONE-AF trials showed that OAC cessation is a viable option at 1 year after ablation if no atrial fibrillation is documented by routine rhythm monitoring modalities.

Title: Differential Effects of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing on Myocardial Work Indices, Transmural Strain Gradient, and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Right ventricular pacing (RVP) may impair myocardial mechanics even when ejection fraction (EF) is preserved, whereas left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) recruits the His-Purkinje system and may mitigate this. We compared these modalities for myocardial work indices, peak systolic dispersion (PSD) and transmural strain gradient.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 118 patients with preserved EF (≥50%; 58 RVP, 60 LBBAP) underwent speckle-tracking echocardiography before implantation and at 6 months. Pressure-strain loop-derived global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work (GWW), global work efficiency (GWE) and PSD were compared at both visits, and layer-specific global longitudinal strain (GLS) and transmural strain gradient (ΔGLS) at 6 months. The primary mechanistic outcome was the change in PSD (ΔPSD); the primary clinical outcome was a composite of heart failure hospitalisation, new loop diuretic initiation or device-detected atrial fibrillation. Clinical events were monitored for 6 months.
RESULTS: At 6 months, RVP showed higher GWW (242.5 vs. 152.5 mmHg·%), lower GWE (88.8% vs. 93.3%), greater PSD (58.5 vs. 40.0 ms) and greater ΔGLS (4.4% vs. 3.2%; all p<0.001). Within-patient changes diverged (ΔPSD +20.5 vs. -17.5 ms; ΔGWE -5.9 vs. -2.5 points; both p<0.001). The composite endpoint occurred in 31.0% vs. 8.3% (hazard ratio [HR], 0.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.09 to 0.65; adjusted HR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.11 to 0.84).
CONCLUSIONS: LBBAP was associated with more synchronous and efficient myocardial mechanics than RVP, and a 70% lower adjusted hazard of the composite endpoint. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant randomised confirmation.

Title: Left Atrial Functional Parameters and Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling After Aortic Valve Replacement in Severe Aortic Stenosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) after aortic valve replacement (AVR) varies in severe aortic stenosis (AS). We evaluated whether preoperative left atrial (LA)-derived functional indices were associated with structural LVRR (S-LVRR) and functional LVRR (F-LVRR).
METHODS: This retrospective 2-center study included 139 adults with severe AS undergoing surgical or transcatheter AVR and follow-up echocardiography after a median of 6.1 months. S-LVRR was defined as normalization of left ventricular (LV) mass index, and F-LVRR as sex-specific recovery of absolute LV global longitudinal strain. Separate adjusted logistic models assessed LA reservoir strain (LASr), LA stiffness index (LASI), LA reservoir work, and LA volumetric/mechanical coupling index, with supportive sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: S-LVRR and F-LVRR occurred in 58 (41.7%) and 42 (30.2%) patients, respectively. Higher LASr and lower LASI were independently associated with S-LVRR (odds ratio [OR] per 1-standard deviation increase, 2.48; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37-4.49 and OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.13-0.79) and F-LVRR (OR, 7.41; 95% CI, 2.70-20.32 and OR, 0.01; 95% CI, 0.00-0.15). LASr remained robust across sensitivity analyses, whereas LASI was attenuated in change-based analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: In severe AS, preserved preoperative LASr and lower LASI were associated with postoperative LVRR after AVR. LASr was the most consistent LA-derived marker and may complement conventional LV assessment pending prospective validation.

Title: Long-term Outcomes of the Cox-Maze Procedure in Patients With Atrial Septal Defect and Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Atrial septal defect (ASD) is often complicated by atrial fibrillation (AF). Although biatrial Cox-Maze procedures are more effective than right-sided ablations in restoring normal sinus rhythm (NSR), long-term outcomes in ASD remain underreported. We evaluated long-term outcomes and predictors of NSR restoration after biatrial Cox-Maze across ASD types.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with ASD and AF who underwent biatrial Cox-Maze between 2000 and 2023. Patients were stratified by preoperative fibrillatory wave amplitude into coarse (group C) and fine (group F), with fine defined as <1 mm. The primary endpoint was NSR restoration at discharge; secondary endpoints were 15-year survival, stroke, heart failure readmission, and pacemaker implantation.
RESULTS: Among 89 patients (mean age 56.5±10.4 years; 49.4% male), NSR was restored in 84.3% at discharge and maintained in 65.8% at 7 years. Fifteen-year survival was 74.4% (95% confidence interval [CI], 55.9-86.0%), vs. an expected 86.0% for the general population (p=0.159). Pacemaker implantation was required in 4.7%. Group C showed higher NSR maintenance (92% at discharge, 85.7% at 7 years) than group F (68.2% at discharge, 20.0% at 7 years; p=0.012). Preoperative coarse fibrillatory wave independently predicted NSR restoration (Firth odds ratio, 5.04; 95% CI, 1.39-20.38; p=0.014). All non-secundum ASD patients initially achieved NSR.
CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant biatrial Cox-Maze with ASD closure achieves durable NSR maintenance and favorable long-term outcomes. Preoperative fibrillatory wave amplitude predicts maze success. The Cox-Maze procedure is safe and effective across ASD subtypes.

Title: Association between Body Mass Index and Mortality From Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The association between obesity and aortic diseases remains uncertain. We investigated the relationship between body mass index (BMI) and mortality from aortic aneurysm and dissection.
METHODS: This population-based prospective cohort study used National Health Insurance Service health examination data from 15,146,946 Korean adults aged ≥18 years who underwent health screening between 2003 and 2006, with follow-up for mortality from aortic aneurysm and dissection through national death registry linkage until 2018. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 14.3 years, 4,299 deaths from aortic disease were identified. A J-shaped association was observed between BMI and aortic disease mortality. Underweight (BMI <18.5 kg/m²: HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.04-1.45; p=0.013) and higher BMI categories, including upper-normal, overweight, and obese groups (e.g., BMI ≥35 kg/m²: HR, 3.40; 95% CI, 2.10-5.49; p<0.001), were associated with increased mortality compared with BMI 21-22.9 kg/m². The association was more pronounced in younger individuals. The excess risk associated with underweight was more prominent in women, whereas the association with higher BMI was steeper in men.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large nationwide general population cohort, BMI showed a J-shaped association with mortality from aortic aneurysm and dissection. Further studies are needed to determine whether maintaining BMI within a healthy range is associated with lower risk of mortality from aortic aneurysm and dissection.

Title: High-Intensity Lipid-Lowering Therapy After Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate the association between high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy (HILLT) and long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) across procedural complexity.
METHODS: Post hoc observational cohort analysis of 3 drug-eluting stent registries (HOST-Onyx, HOST-Synergy, HOST-Alpine) was conducted. A total of 1,750 patients underwent PCI; 691 (39.5%) met criteria for complex PCI, defined as treatment of ≥3 stents implanted, ≥3 lesions treated, total stent length ≥60 mm, left main PCI, bifurcation PCI, or heavy calcification. The HILLT group was defined as those prescribed either high-intensity statins with or without ezetimibe, or moderate-intensity statins with ezetimibe. The primary outcome was major adverse cardio-cerebrovascular events (MACCE), composite of cardiac death, myocardial infarct, and stroke at 3 years. Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score (PS) matching, and inverse probability treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding.
RESULTS: Patients receiving HILLT exhibited a lower risk of MACCE (PS-matched hazard ratio [HR], 0.508; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.260-0.994; p=0.048). Subgroup analysis revealed that this benefit was significant among patients undergoing complex PCI (HR, 0.292; 95% CI, 0.107-0.797; p=0.017) compared with the noncomplex PCI group (HR, 0.896; 95% CI, 0.346-2.322; p=0.822; p-for-interaction=0.107). Sensitivity analyses in the complex PCI subgroup demonstrated consistent results, with lower risk of MACCE in patients receiving HILLT (PS-matched HR, 0.320; 95% CI, 0.116-0.881; p=0.027; IPTW-adjusted HR, 0.246; 95% CI, 0.093-0.647; p=0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing PCI, HILLT was associated with a lower 3-year risk of MACCE, with no significant interaction across procedural complexity.

Title: Organ Dysfunction in Neonates with Perinatal Asphyxia in a Tertiary Care Hospital of Nepal.
Abstract: Background Perinatal asphyxia is one of the commonest causes of neonatal mortality and morbidity. Multiple organ dysfunction is an important complication. The adaptive mechanisms triggered are overwhelmed in prolonged or severe asphyxia leading to dysfunction of multiple vital organs. Objective To find the prevalence of organ dysfunction among neonates admitted with perinatal asphyxia in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Bharatpur Hospital. Method We conducted a prospective, cross-sectional study in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of a tertiary hospital from January to December 2023 after obtaining ethical approval from Institutional Review Committee. Neonates admitted to Neonatal Intensive Care Unit with asphyxia were enrolled in the study. The basic information regarding period of gestation, sex, Apgar score, birth weight and birth events were collected. Neonates were investigated and managed as per Neonatal Intensive Care Unit protocol. Enrolled neonates were assessed for central nervous system, renal, respiratory, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, metabolic and hematologic dysfunction, the number of systems involved and the immediate outcomes. Result All 108 enrolled neonates had at least one organ dysfunction. Cardiovascular dysfunction (83.33%) was the most common followed by respiratory dysfunction (79.62%). The Central nervous system, hematologic, renal, gastrointestinal and metabolic dysfunction were seen in 28.70%, 20.37%, 8.33%, 8.33% and 6.48% of neonates respectively. Multiorgan dysfunction was found in 85.19% of neonates. Among the enrolled neonates, 93.52% were discharged, 4.63% left against medical advice while 1.85% died during hospital stay. Conclusion Organ dysfunction is seen in all neonates with asphyxia commonly involving cardiovascular and respiratory system. Multiorgan dysfunction is a frequent complication of perinatal asphyxia.

Title: Establishment and Validation of a Model of Indwelling Nasogastric Tube in Patients After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysphagia is common after stroke, and accurately predicting its duration is essential for guiding therapeutic decisions. Timely indwelling nasogastric tube (NGT) placement is critical for patient prognosis. The purpose of this study was to develop and validate a predictive model for indwelling NGT requirements in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: From 2020 to 2022, we retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 553 patients with AIS. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariate logistic regression were employed to identify predictors. Multiple machine learning (ML) classifiers were integrated to identify the optimal model, followed by validation. Finally, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was applied for model interpretation and personalized risk assessment.
RESULTS: A total of five variables-patient's National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, age, free thyroxine (fT4), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and stroke location, were derived from Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression and logistic regression as independent predictors associated with indwelling NGT requirement in AIS patients. Among nine machine learning classifiers, random forest demonstrated optimal performance. The model achieved an AUC of 0.850 in fivefold cross-validation within the training cohort and 0.853 in the independent testing cohort.
CONCLUSION: The proposed model serves as a user-friendly prognostic tool for reliably predicting swallowing dysfunction while offering interpretable results. It may assist clinicians in making NGT placement decisions for AIS patients, facilitating personalized care.

Title: Association of Homocysteine With All-Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality in Individuals With Advanced Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
Abstract: BACKGROUND Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects the overlap of cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. The prognostic relevance of homocysteine (Hcy) in advanced CKM syndrome remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of serum Hcy levels with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in adults with advanced CKM syndrome. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective cohort study included 3658 adults with advanced CKM syndrome from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2006. Hcy was analyzed continuously and by tertiles. The primary analyses used survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Restricted cubic splines assessed potential nonlinear associations. RESULTS During a mean follow-up of 153.4 months, 2008 all-cause deaths and 686 cardiovascular deaths occurred. After full adjustment, each 1-unit increase in Hcy was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02; P=0.014), and the highest vs lowest Hcy tertile was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.19-1.72; P<0.001). For cardiovascular mortality, associations were directionally positive but not statistically significant after full multivariable adjustment for either continuous Hcy (HR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02; P=0.053) or the highest vs lowest tertile (HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.96-1.86; P=0.082). Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested nonlinear associations. CONCLUSIONS Higher Hcy was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality in adults with advanced CKM syndrome. The association with cardiovascular mortality was directionally positive but did not reach statistical significance after full multivariable adjustment.

Title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
Journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

Title: Technical Feasibility and Outcomes of t-Branch Proximal Shortening in Urgent Complex Aortic Repair.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Branched endovascular repair has shown consistently good outcomes, being sometimes the only available endovascular solution for aortic emergencies. However, in cases of limited proximal extension of the disease, such as juxtarenal or pararenal aneurysms, branched endografts usually cover a greater extent of the aorta than needed to establish a seal zone, thus increasing the risk for spinal cord ischemia (SCI) by unnecessarily covering segmental arteries.Our objective is to analyze a series of patients who underwent proximal shortening of an off-the-shelf (OTS) branched endograft to limit aortic coverage and preserve segmental arteries.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) with a shortened t-Branch, through the removal of the first stent row, from April 2020 to March 2026.Perioperative technical success and complications were evaluated. Primary endpoints were technical success. Secondary endpoints were 30-day mortality, SCI, assessment of number of saved segmental arteries, and endograft migration at follow-up.
RESULTS: Fifteen patients underwent BEVAR with a shortened t-Branch endograft. All were urgencies, 60% being ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs). Thirteen (86%) cases were juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysms, and 3 (20%) had a previous endovascular aortic repair. In all cases, the proximal sealing stent of the t-Branch was removed, whereas in 2 cases, an additional large posterior fenestration at the second sealing stent was created. Technical success was 93%, with 1 severely stenotic renal artery not able to be catheterized and left unbridged. No endograft deployment complication (migration or malrotation) were experienced. There was 1 postoperative mortality in a patient with a ruptured AAA. Major complication rate was 27%, including 2 patients having SCI (one grade 2, one grade 3). A median of 2 segmental arteries were saved through the endograft modification.At a median follow-up of 1 year no endograft migration was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In urgent complex aortic repair for circumscribed anatomies such as juxta/pararenal aneurysms, the use of a modified OTS branched endograft proved to be a reproducible and safe technique, allowing the preservation of segmental arteries and possibly affecting favorably the spinal cord ischemic rates.Clinical ImpactOn-table shortening of the t-Branch endograft, optionally creating a big fenestration at the second sealing stent, is a feasible and reproducible option for urgent juxta/pararenal aortic aneurysm repair when custom-made devices are not available. The modification allowed sparing a median of two segmental arteries otherwise covered with a standard t-Branch, which might help mitigating the risk of spinal cord ischemia.

Title: Validation of Diagnosis Code for Cardiogenic Shock in an Integrated Healthcare System.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Many modern studies of cardiogenic shock rely on retrospective administrative datasets or electronic medical records. This makes determination of coding accuracy of International Classification of Diseases, 10 Revision (ICD-10-CM) critically important for valid case identification. This study aimed to determine positive predictive value and sensitivity of ICD-10-CM coding of cardiogenic shock.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study identified all encounters admitted with cardiogenic shock between January 1, 2016 and Dec 31, 2022. Two non-overlapping cohorts were analyzed: those identified by ICD-10-CM code for cardiogenic shock and those who did not have an ICD-10-CM code but did have a primary diagnosis of heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, and in whom either inotropes, pressors, or mechanical circulatory support devices were utilized. Based on chart review, the positive predictive value (PPV) as well as sensitivity for the ICD-10-CM code was calculated.
RESULTS: There were 4473 individual encounters with an ICD-10-CM code for cardiogenic shock. Review of 100 charts by a cardiologist showed PPV of 88% (95% CI: 80%-93.6%). The cohort identified with clinical criteria without ICD-10-CM code consisted of 1022 patients. After review of all the patients in this cohort, the calculated PPV was 69.8% (95% CI 66.8%-72.6%). Utilizing this set as a false negative cohort, the sensitivity of ICD-10-CM code for cardiogenic shock was 84.7% (95% CI:83.4%-85.5%). The two cohorts were similar in age and sex. Race/ethnicity differed modestly while discharge disposition differed substantially.
CONCLUSION: In this large, single health system validation study of 5495 patients, the ICD-10-CM code for cardiogenic shock demonstrated a high PPV of 88%. This supports the use of the ICD-10-CM code for administrative and retrospective research purposes. The calculated sensitivity of 84.7% shows that there is a meaningful proportion of patients with cardiogenic shock that are missed when utilizing only ICD-10-CM codes. Patients with and without the ICD-10-CM code differed in discharge outcomes. Future strategies should evaluate whether combining both ICD-10-CM codes and clinical criteria can improve cardiogenic shock case identification.

Title: Elevated Neutrophil Percentage-to-Albumin Ratio Is Associated With Stroke-Associated Pneumonia in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is a common and serious complication of acute ischemic stroke (AIS). The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) is a composite inflammatory and nutritional marker derived from routine blood tests. This study investigated the association between NPAR and SAP and evaluated its functional form and incremental discriminatory value.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This secondary analysis used a single-center AIS registry that screened 2150 consecutive admissions between September 2016 and September 2022; 1766 patients comprised the NPAR analytic cohort. Associations between log2-transformed NPAR and SAP were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, generalized additive models (GAM), and two-piecewise logistic regression.
RESULTS: SAP developed in 376 patients (21.3%). NPAR was independently associated with SAP after adjustment for the 18 prespecified covariates in Model 3 (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per doubling of NPAR = 6.14; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.19-11.82; p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest quartile, the adjusted ORs for SAP were 1.16 (95% CI, 0.68-1.99), 1.72 (95% CI, 1.04-2.83), and 3.48 (95% CI, 2.08-5.83) across increasing NPAR quartiles (p for trend < 0.001). Generalized additive and piecewise models indicated an exploratory non-linear, threshold-associated pattern, with a data-derived inflection point at approximately NPAR = 1.758. In ROC analysis, NPAR showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.785; 95% CI, 0.756-0.814), higher than the A2DS2 score alone (AUC = 0.758; p = 0.120) and lower than CRP alone (AUC = 0.826; p = 0.019). Adding NPAR to A2DS2 increased the apparent in-sample AUC to 0.821 (p < 0.001), whereas adding NPAR to CRP increased it to 0.842 without a statistically significant increment over CRP alone (p = 0.213); these combination models were not internally validated.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective secondary analysis, NPAR was independently and non-linearly associated with SAP after acute ischemic stroke. Multiple-imputation analyses supported the robustness of these findings. NPAR provided complementary discriminatory information, particularly when added to A2DS2; however, independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Predictive Value of Early Functional Improvement During Hospitalization for Intermediate-Term Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether early functional improvement status is associated with 3-month functional outcomes after stroke and to develop and internally validate a preliminary prediction model for poor outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 150 patients with stroke who were hospitalized in the Department of Neurology and the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine at our hospital between March 2021 and December 2024 and who completed the 3-month post-discharge follow-up. Early functional improvement was defined by changes in the Barthel Index and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores from admission to discharge. The cohort-specific median values of ΔBarthel and ΔNIHSS were used as exploratory thresholds to classify patients into the functional improvement group and the insufficient functional improvement group. Baseline characteristics, early functional changes during hospitalization, and functional outcomes at 3 months after discharge were compared between the two groups. Poor functional outcome at 3 months after discharge, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score ≥3, was used as the dependent variable. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between early functional improvement status and poor functional outcome and its incremental prognostic contribution beyond baseline clinical variables. A nomogram was constructed based on the extended model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration assessment, and decision curve analysis, and internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples. In a sensitivity analysis, the categorized early functional improvement status variable was replaced by continuous ΔBarthel and ΔNIHSS values while retaining the same baseline covariates.
RESULTS: The functional improvement group was slightly younger than the insufficient functional improvement group. During hospitalization, the functional improvement group had lower NIHSS scores, higher Barthel Index scores at discharge, and greater changes in both functional measures from admission to discharge. At the 3-month follow-up, the functional improvement group had significantly higher Barthel Index scores, a higher rate of functional independence, and a lower incidence of poor functional outcomes (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis showed that age, admission blood glucose, and admission NIHSS score were inde-pendently associated with higher odds of poor functional outcome, whereas admission Barthel Index and early functional improvement status were independently associated with lower odds of poor functional outcome. In the sensitivity analysis, each 1-point increase in ΔBarthel was associated with lower odds of poor functional outcome (OR = 0.936, 95% CI: 0.898-0.977, p = 0.002), as was each 1-point increase in ΔNIHSS (OR = 0.678, 95% CI: 0.524-0.878, p = 0.003). Adding early functional improvement status to the baseline clinical model modestly improved discrimination, with the apparent area under the curve (AUC) increasing from 0.809 to 0.852 (ΔAUC = 0.043, p = 0.037). After bootstrap correction, the AUC of the extended model was 0.827. These findings indicate modest incremental prognostic value within the present cohort, but external validation is required.
CONCLUSION: Early functional improvement status during hospitalization after stroke was independently associated with intermediate-term functional outcomes and may provide additional prognostic information beyond baseline clinical characteristics. The prediction model incorporating early functional improvement status and baseline clinical variables showed preliminary predictive performance within the present cohort but should not yet be regarded as a clinically validated risk-stratification tool. External validation is required before its use in rehabilitation planning or clinical decision-making.

Title: Angiotensin receptor blockers and nontraditional health outcomes: an umbrella review of meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
AIM: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) are prescribed for cardiovascular and renal protection, but their effects on nontraditional health outcomes remain unclear. With the increasing use of ARBs in diverse populations, clarifying their broader impact has important clinical implications.
METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed ARBs and nontraditional health outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 2026. Methodological quality was appraised using AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Where trial-level data were available, we re-analysed outcomes using random-effects models and evaluated heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, and small-study effects.
RESULTS: Fifteen systematic reviews and meta-analyses of RCTs were included, covering 35 unique nontraditional outcomes. Nine outcomes reached nominal statistical significance, but only a few met more stringent credibility criteria. The most credible associations were lower risks of headache and new-onset diabetes, and lower fasting plasma insulin levels with ARB therapy. Associations with migraine severity, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and insulin resistance were suggestive or exploratory because of prediction intervals crossing the null, sparse data, heterogeneity, or limited certainty. No convincing evidence supported associations with oncological, infectious, or transplant-related outcomes. Most included reviews were rated as low or critically low-quality using AMSTAR 2, warranting cautious interpretation.
CONCLUSION: ARBs appear to provide therapeutic benefits beyond traditional indications, particularly in metabolic and neurological domains, without evidence of excess harm. These findings may inform clinical decision-making in patients at risk of diabetes or with comorbid pain conditions.

Title: Efficacy of Nutritional Intervention in Adult Patients With Heart Failure: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Approximately 50% of heart failure (HF) patients are malnourished, doubling mortality risk; however, interventional evidence remains limited. A previously published meta-analysis found modest weight improvements only in malnourished/cachectic patients (5 studies, n = 275). This review updates the evidence in a broader HF population to evaluate the effect of nutritional interventions on all-cause mortality, hospital readmissions, and body mass index (BMI) in HF, determine whether intervention type moderates effect size, and identify sources of heterogeneity via meta-regression. This PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261445761) systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, and Embase for randomized controlled trials, quasi-randomized, and observational studies evaluating nutritional interventions (supplements, fortification, enteral/parenteral nutrition, counseling, with or without exercise) to increase protein/energy intake in HF, updating a 2021 search. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (RoB 2.0 for randomized controlled trials; ROBINS-I for observational studies). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs), with subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses. Of 7190 records screened, 23 studies (n = 2240) were included; 18 contributed to meta-analysis. Risk of bias was predominantly low. Nutritional intervention significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.43, 95% confidence interval: 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), with no significant effect on readmission or BMI. Exercise capacity improved significantly (6-minute walk distance mean difference 25.01, 95% confidence interval: 5.26-44.76, P = 0.013), while quality of life, creatinine, and B-type natriuretic peptide showed no significant change. Nutritional intervention was associated with reduced mortality and improved exercise capacity in HF, though effects on hospitalization, BMI, and biomarkers were nonsignificant, warranting cautious interpretation.

Title: Atrial fibrillation care in internal medicine: a multicenter survey of screening, anticoagulation responses, and clinical support needs.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Internal medicine physicians frequently encounter atrial fibrillation (AF) and anticoagulation-related problems before or alongside cardiology input. We described internal medicine residents' and specialists' first-choice method for confirming suspected AF, how often they reported screening for AF in four prespecified risk-enriched patient groups (screening method and interval were not specified), their responses to common anticoagulation scenarios, and their preferences for practical clinical support.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional online survey in nine hospitals in Türkiye. All 549 eligible internal medicine physicians listed on institutional staffing rosters were invited; 327 completed a 34-item questionnaire (response rate 59.6%). Item-level response distributions were the primary outcomes; resident-specialist comparisons were exploratory.
RESULTS: Twelve-lead electrocardiography was selected for diagnostic confirmation by 88.4%. Always/often screening was reported by 19.9%-38.8% of respondents across four prespecified risk-enriched groups: patients aged ≥ 65 years, those with heart failure, those with a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack, and those with diabetes or chronic kidney disease. Fewer than half selected the prespecified reference response in five selected scenarios: stable coronary disease (47.7%), the direct oral anticoagulant-unsuitable option of a mechanical prosthetic valve or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis (46.5%), apixaban dose reduction (38.5%), minor bleeding (37.9%), and an international normalized ratio outside the target range (34.3%). A practical algorithm was considered useful by 94.5%, structured internal medicine-cardiology collaboration by 86.5%, and 75.5% requested further education.
CONCLUSIONS: Although most respondents selected electrocardiography for AF confirmation, always/often screening was reported by fewer than 40% in each assessed risk-enriched group, and responses to anticoagulation scenarios varied, including among specialists. These findings support prospective evaluation of a locally adapted, internist-led pathway integrating opportunistic screening prompts, a defined initial assessment, and clear criteria for timely cardiology input.

Title: Smoking behavior and frailty: joint impact on incident cardiovascular disease in a prospective cohort study.
Journal: Archives of public health = Archives belges de sante publique
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the joint associations of smoking behaviors and frailty phenotype with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD), and to examine how associations of smoking cessation duration with CVD vary across different frailty states.
METHODS: We included 297,340 UK Biobank participants free of baseline CVD, with baseline assessment of smoking behaviors (including smoking status and years since quitting for former smokers) and frailty phenotypes (i.e., nonfrail, prefrail, and frail). Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations of combined frailty-smoking categories with coronary artery disease (CAD), stroke, and four secondary cardiovascular outcomes. Both additive and multiplicative interactions between frailty and smoking were evaluated using relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI), attributable proportion, synergy index, and interaction terms in Cox models.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up period of 13.5 (IQR: 12.7-14.2) years, 20,621 participants (6.9%) developed incident CAD and 5,696 (1.9%) experienced stroke. Joint analyses demonstrated that current smokers with frailty consistently exhibited the highest cardiovascular risk across outcomes, with the strongest joint associations observed for peripheral artery disease (PAD) and heart failure (HF). Significant positive additive interactions between frailty and smoking were also identified for CAD (RERI = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.004-0.39) and PAD (RERI = 1.43, 95% CI: 0.70-2.20), indicating that the coexistence of smoking and frailty was associated with excess cardiovascular risk beyond the sum of their individual associations. Longer cessation duration was consistently associated with progressively lower cardiovascular risk across frailty categories. Significant multiplicative interactions between frailty and smoking were observed for CAD, PAD, and cardiovascular mortality. Nonfrail and prefrail individuals showed lower CAD and PAD risk within 5 years after smoking cessation, whereas frail individuals had persistently elevated risk during 5-15 years before approaching that of never smokers. No multiplicative interaction was observed for stroke, HF, or atrial fibrillation (AF), although longer smoking cessation duration remained associated with lower cardiovascular risk across all frailty strata. Finally, smoking-related cardiovascular risk varied across specific frailty components, particularly exhaustion, low physical activity, and slow gait speed.
CONCLUSION: Frailty may increase susceptibility to smoking-related cardiovascular harm, particularly for CAD and PAD. Frail smokers may represent a particularly vulnerable population that warrants earlier smoking cessation support and more intensive cardiovascular prevention strategies to mitigate long-term cardiovascular risk. Joint consideration of smoking exposure and frailty status may therefore have greater public health relevance for reducing absolute cardiovascular risk burden than addressing either risk factor alone.

Title: The association between stress hyperglycemia ratio and adverse outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases risks of cardiovascular events and mortality, so reliable biomarkers are needed to improve risk stratification. Stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), which adjusts acute glucose levels for chronic glycemia using glycated hemoglobin, has shown prognostic value in various settings, but its role in predicting outcomes in CKD is still unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between SHR and adverse outcomes in patients with CKD.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched up to March 15, 2025, for studies reporting the association between SHR and outcomes in patients with CKD. Observational studies and clinical trials were eligible if they reported SHR and at least one adverse outcomes. Data extraction and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale were performed independently by two reviewers. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I² statistic, publication bias with Egger's and Begg's tests, and sensitivity analyses with a leave-one-out approach.
RESULTS: Out of 307 records initially identified, eight studies involving 19,740 patients with CKD were included. Most were cohort studies conducted in the United States or China. Four studies with 12,324 participants reported all-cause mortality, showing a non-significant association between higher SHR and risk of death (pooled OR: 1.39; 95% CI: 0.85-2.27). Three studies with 11,035 participants assessed cardiovascular mortality, also yielding a non-significant result (pooled OR: 1.50; 95% CI: 0.86-2.62). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that the pooled estimates were sensitive to the exclusion of a single influential study, indicating limited robustness of the current evidence rather than confirming a prognostic effect of SHR. No publication bias was detected, and overall study quality was rated as good.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher SHR was not consistently associated with all-cause or cardiovascular mortality in patients with CKD, although sensitivity analyses suggested SHR may have prognostic potential. These findings highlight the need for larger, well-designed studies with standardized SHR assessment to clarify its role as a prognostic marker in CKD.

Title: Association of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy with atrial fibrillation recurrence after catheter ablation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide, with a rising global prevalence. Post-ablation AF recurrence remains frequent, particularly among patients with obesity and metabolic syndrome. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated favorable cardiometabolic and cardiovascular effects, but their association with AF recurrence after ablation remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through June 18, 2026. Cohort studies evaluating GLP-1RA therapy in adults with atrial fibrillation undergoing catheter ablation were included. The primary outcome was post-ablation atrial fibrillation recurrence (or recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmia, as defined by the individual studies). Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Six cohort studies (three prospective and three retrospective), comprising 14,278 patients (7,065 GLP-1RA users and 7,213 controls), met the inclusion criteria. Follow-up duration ranged from 12 to 24 months across studies. The pooled mean age was approximately 64 years in both the GLP-1RA and control groups. GLP-1RA therapy was associated with a lower hazard of AF recurrence compared with the respective comparator groups (HR = 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.87; I² = 50.5%). However, the certainty of the evidence was low because the findings were derived predominantly from observational studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Observational evidence suggests that GLP-1RA use is associated with a lower hazard of AF recurrence following catheter ablation. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously, and further high-quality randomized controlled trials are required to confirm this association.

Title: Hypoxia and right ventricular dysfunction in patients with acute pulmonary embolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE), hypoxia may increase pulmonary vascular resistance and worsen right ventricular dysfunction (RVD), which is a key prognostic factor. However, associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes have not been well described.
AIM: To describe associations between hypoxia, RVD and clinical outcomes in patients with PE.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of patients treated by the Massachusetts General Hospital Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) from 10/2012 to 08/2021. Inclusion criteria included confirmed PE, recorded oxygen saturation prior to PERT activation, and echocardiogram within three days of PERT activation. Patients were categorized into four subgroups based on (1) hypoxia status (SaO₂ below vs. above 95%) and, (2) oxygen support (below vs. above 3 L/min). Our primary outcome was the presence of RVD on echocardiogram. Our secondary outcome was clinical deterioration within 7 days.
RESULTS: We included 894 PE patients. The mean age was 61 (± 16 SD), 614/894 (69%) were hypoxic, and 624/894 (70%) had RVD on echocardiogram. Overall, hypoxic patients were more likely to have RVD than non-hypoxic patients (467/614 [76%] vs. 157/280 [56%], p < 0.0001). On subgroup analysis, RVD prevalence was highest in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group (n = 216/266, 81%) followed by the "not hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" group 53/70 (76%); 198/278 (71%) in the "hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" and 157/280 (56%) in the "not hypoxic with oxygen support <3L" groups. Clinical deterioration occurred in 199/894 (22%) patients and was more common in hypoxic patients than non-hypoxic patients (157/614 [26%] vs. 42/280 [15%], p < 0.0001), and most common in the "hypoxic with oxygen support ≥3L" subgroup 88/266 (33%).
CONCLUSIONS: Hypoxia is associated with RVD and clinical deterioration in patients with PE. More research is needed to understand the risk associated with hypoxia and the physiology of supplemental oxygen support in PE.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in pediatric cardiac surgery: retrospective survival analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-saving therapeutic modality in children. Outcome is multifactorial with debates regarding predictors of weaning success and mortality.
OBJECTIVE: To explore predictors of ECMO outcome in children with surgically corrected congenital heart disease (CHD).
METHOD: This single-center retrospective cohort study included children with operated CHD who were admitted to a tertiary-care cardiac center in Saudi Arabia during 2022-2025. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, as well as operative and ECMO details were recorded. Predictors of weaning failure and overall mortality during follow-up were analyzed.
RESULTS: Thirty children aged 15 days to 12.8 years were included. ECMO connection was applied in day zero in 23 patients (76.6%). ECMO duration ranged between 1 and 15 days. Successful ECMO weaning was achieved in 56.7%. ECMO complication included renal injury in 36.7%, neurological complications in 16.7% and wound infection in 10%. The overall mortality rate was 46.7%. Residual cardiac lesions (OR 20; 95%CI:2.037-196.37 and OR 25.6; 95%CI:2.544-257.566) and ECMO complication (OR 5.4; 95%CI:1.12-26.044 and OR 7.5.6; 95%CI:1.484-37.905) were associated with ECMO failure and mortality during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Residual cardiac lesions and ECMO-related complications were associated with poor outcome in children with surgically corrected CHD who require ECMO. The complexity of cardiac surgery and delayed initiation of ECMO are associated with prolonged ECMO stay duration. Proper timing of ECMO Initiation may reduce complications and improve survival.

Title: Lipid-metabolic risk stratification for carotid plaque in adults under 50 years undergoing health examinations: cross-sectional modeling and same-center longitudinal validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid plaque is an imaging marker of early subclinical atherosclerosis. Adults under 50 years of age undergoing health examinations often have low short-term absolute cardiovascular risk, yet adverse lipid-metabolic profiles may already be associated with early plaque formation. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a parsimonious lipid-metabolic risk stratification model for carotid plaque risk using routinely available health-examination variables.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study constructed two related cohorts from a health management center. The cross-sectional modeling cohort included 30,557 adults under 50 years of age examined between 2018 and 2023, of whom 1277 had prevalent carotid plaque, and was used for model development and internal validation. The same-center longitudinal validation cohort included 1679 baseline plaque-free participants with classifiable longitudinal plaque trajectories from repeated examinations between January 2020 and December 2024; 105 developed the primary incident carotid plaque outcome. Thirteen routine health-examination variables were considered. Variable selection and model development were performed only in the training set. The final multivariable logistic regression model included age, male sex, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and fasting glucose. Performance was assessed using AUROC and PR-AUC. Low-, intermediate-, and high-risk strata were defined using tertiles of predicted probability in the training set.
RESULTS: In the internal validation set, the final multivariable logistic regression model achieved an AUROC of 0.807 and a PR-AUC of 0.168, higher than those of the age- and sex-only model. In the same-center longitudinal validation cohort, the final model achieved an AUROC of 0.795 and a PR-AUC of 0.216 for the primary incident carotid plaque outcome. The observed outcome rates increased across low-, intermediate-, and high-risk strata: 0.75%, 3.41%, and 13.9%, respectively. The high-risk stratum included 82 of 105 primary incident carotid plaque outcomes. Sensitivity analysis using Firth penalized logistic regression showed directionally consistent associations.
CONCLUSIONS: Among adults under 50 years of age undergoing routine health examinations, a parsimonious lipid-metabolic model incorporating age, male sex, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and fasting glucose provided discrimination for prevalent carotid plaque status and stratified longitudinal incident plaque outcomes in a same-center repeated-examination cohort. This model provides an interpretable framework for early subclinical atherosclerosis risk communication and cardiometabolic risk management in health-examination settings.

Title: Non-RA screening for systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases using a machine learning model based on physical findings and blood test data.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), particularly patients with non-rheumatoid arthritis (non-RA), the incidence of severe conditions such as interstitial pneumonia and pulmonary arterial hypertension is high. Therefore, early referral of these patients to university hospitals or other institutions capable of comprehensive medical care is desirable. However, the substantial overlap in clinical presentations across SARDs makes differentiation challenging, and objective tools to support disease classification in routine clinical practice remain limited. In this study, a machine learning based classifier was developed to distinguish Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) from non‑RA conditions using general physical findings and routine blood test data, focusing on patients who were diagnosed with a predefined set of SARDs from a secondary‑care teaching hospital.
METHODS: An observational retrospective study was conducted on 571 patients initially diagnosed with SARDs. From the hospital's clinical information database, patients' diagnoses, blood test results, and physical findings were extracted from the hospital's clinical information database to create the dataset. Physical findings were extracted as structured data using natural language processing from medical records written in a free description format by the attending physicians. For patient classification, some non-RA screening model using three classification algorithms were developed: Naive Bayes, Linear Support Vector Machines, and Random Forest.
RESULTS: RA and non-RA diseases share common clinical symptoms, with joint symptoms observed in over 40% of patients with the target diseases. Of the screening models, the random forest model performed the best, achieving a sensitivity of 77.3% and a specificity of 72.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with confirmed SARDs, a machine learning-based classifier using routinely available clinical symptoms and blood test results demonstrated promising internal performance for differentiating RA from non-RA conditions. These findings support the feasibility of machine learning-based classification within this secondary-care setting. Future studies are needed to validate the model in broader clinical populations, including primary care settings, and to evaluate its potential role in supporting referral decision-making.

Title: Clinical outcomes of rivaroxaban and warfarin for anticoagulation in children with giant coronary artery aneurysms after Kawasaki disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with giant coronary artery aneurysms (gCAA) after Kawasaki disease (KD) are at high risk of coronary artery thrombosis (CAT), associated with adverse cardiovascular events (ACEs). Long-term anticoagulation is the standard regimen, but evidence comparing rivaroxaban with warfarin in gCAA after KD remains limited.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational study at 2 pediatric centers from 2020 to 2025, enrolling children with gCAA after KD. Participants received rivaroxaban or warfarin. The primary efficacy assessment included ACEs and CAT outcomes within 6 months. CAA changes and safety outcomes were assessed.
RESULTS: The final cohort included 30 patients, 14 treated with rivaroxaban and 16 with warfarin. ACEs were infrequent, occurring in 1 patient (7.1%) receiving rivaroxaban and 2 patients (12.5%) receiving warfarin. Among patients without CAT at baseline, new-onset CAT occurred in 1 of 10 patients (10.0%) receiving rivaroxaban and 1 of 12 patients (8.3%) receiving warfarin. Among patients with CAT at baseline, CAT resolved in 2 of 4 patients in each group. CAA progression was observed in 7 patients (50.0%) in the rivaroxaban group and 10 patients (62.5%) in the warfarin group, whereas CAA regression occurred in 6 patients (42.9%) and 5 patients (31.2%), respectively. No major bleeding or prespecified severe hypersensitivity events were observed in either group.
CONCLUSIONS: Over the 6-month follow-up, ACEs, CAT outcomes, CAA changes, and safety outcomes were descriptively similar among children receiving rivaroxaban or warfarin. These descriptive findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Association between preoperative monocyte-to-HDL cholesterol ratio and postoperative atrial fibrillation after esophagectomy for ESCC: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a frequent complication after esophagectomy. The monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) integrates monocyte-related inflammatory burden with HDL-C-related anti-inflammatory and antioxidative capacity. We examined the association between preoperative MHR and POAF after radical esophagectomy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).
METHODS: Consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent radical esophagectomy from January 2022 to December 2024 were screened, and 413 patients were included. MHR was calculated as monocyte count divided by HDL-C measured within 7 days before surgery. POAF was defined as new-onset atrial fibrillation lasting ≥ 30 s within 7 postoperative days. ROC/Youden analysis was used to derive an exploratory cut-off. Primary propensity score matching (PSM) based on sex, BMI, smoking, drinking, and diabetes mellitus yielded 147 matched pairs. An expanded PSM analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis. The primary inferential analyses modeled MHR continuously, with additional exploratory categorical, quartile-based, restricted cubic spline, and Firth penalized logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: POAF occurred in 48 of 413 patients (11.6%). ROC analysis showed moderate discrimination for MHR (AUC 0.765). The exploratory Youden-derived cut-off was 0.355, with sensitivity of 0.92 and specificity of 0.53. POAF was more frequent in the high-MHR group than in the low-MHR group before matching (20.3% vs. 2.0%) and after primary PSM (21.1% vs. 2.0%). In age/sex-adjusted models, each 0.1 increase in MHR was associated with higher odds of POAF in the full cohort (OR 3.05, 95% CI 2.10-4.42), the primary PSM cohort (OR 3.01, 95% CI 1.88-4.82), and the expanded PSM cohort (OR 2.52, 95% CI 1.60-3.96; all P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant overall association (P for overall < 0.001), without evidence of non-linearity (P = 0.746).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated preoperative MHR was consistently associated with higher odds of POAF after radical esophagectomy for ESCC. Because the cut-off was data-derived and the study was retrospective, MHR should be considered a candidate biomarker requiring prospective multicenter validation before clinical implementation.

Title: Activation of the phenylalanine metabolic axis is associated with adverse clinical outcomes and mitochondria-dependent bioenergetic deficiency in ischemic cardiomyocytes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated plasma phenylalanine (PHE) is associated with adverse outcomes in heart failure (HF), but whether PHE is only a marker of systemic severity or can modify ischemic vulnerability remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the prognostic value of the PHE-phenylpyruvate (PPA) axis and examined how PHE affects mitochondrial stress responses after ischemic injury and whether 5-methoxytryptophan (5-MTP) mitigates these effects.
METHODS: Plasma levels of PHE and PPA were analyzed in 191 patients with ischemic HF from the cardiac intensive care unit to assess 90-day mortality. A rat myocardial infarction (MI) model was used to assess PHE-related metabolites in infarct and peri-infarct-enriched left ventricular tissue during chronic post-MI remodeling. HL-1 cardiomyocytes were subjected to oxygen-serum-glucose deprivation (OSGD) with or without PHE and 5-MTP. Cell metabolic activity, ATP levels, mitochondrial respiration, extracellular acidification rate-defined glycolytic function, pyruvate supplementation, dichloroacetate response, cell-death patterns, intracellular PHE-related metabolites, and quantitative proteomics were analyzed.
RESULTS: In the clinical cohort, elevated PHE was independently associated with 90-day mortality after adjustment for estimated glomerular filtration rate, C-reactive protein, and albumin, supporting PHE as a short-term prognostic and candidate risk-stratification biomarker. Post-MI myocardium showed tissue-level accumulation of PHE-related metabolites. In HL-1 cells, 20 mM PHE exacerbated OSGD-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, ATP reduction, glycolytic reserve exhaustion, and mixed cell-death signaling. Pyruvate failed to rescue ATP, while dichloroacetate partially restored ATP, suggesting pyruvate dehydrogenase-sensitive vulnerability. Proteomics revealed pathway-level suppression of oxidative phosphorylation; 5-MTP partially shifted mitochondrial and metabolic signatures toward recovery without uniformly lowering intracellular PHE.
CONCLUSIONS: PHE is a short-term prognostic marker and, under high-dose experimental stress, a potential modifier of ischemic bioenergetic vulnerability. 5-MTP appears to act mainly through downstream mitochondrial stress resilience. These findings support PHE-related metabolic stress as a clinically relevant risk signal and experimental modifier of ischemic myocardial vulnerability, while further validation is required before PHE-guided therapeutic strategies can be proposed.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Infant-onset mevalonate kinase deficiency with a previously unreported MVK c.827 A > G (p.Glu276Gly) variant presenting as suspected incomplete kawasaki disease with marked hyperinflammation: clinical response to firsekibart and systematic evidence synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD) is an autosomal-recessive autoinflammatory disorder spanning a clinical continuum from the hyperimmunoglobulin-D syndrome/recurrent-fever phenotype to severe mevalonic aciduria. In infants, the first attacks can resemble infection, incomplete Kawasaki disease, or other forms of systemic hyperinflammation. Comparative evidence to guide treatment choice and dose adjustment remains limited.
CASE PRESENTATION AND METHODS: We describe a female infant with recurrent high fever and a generalized erythematous rash beginning at 1 month and 23 days of age. She was initially treated for suspected incomplete Kawasaki disease because fever, rash, leukocytosis, elevated C-reactive protein, and qualitatively reported mild coronary-artery dilatation were present; segment-specific coronary measurements and z scores were not available.
