Ferritin 1101.72 ng/mL, soluble CD25 34,200 pg/mL, reduced natural-killer-cell activity, cervical lymphadenopathy, and mild splenomegaly indicated marked hyperinflammation, but the available data were insufficient to diagnose hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis or macrophage activation syndrome. Trio whole-exome sequencing identified MVK c.439G > A (p.Ala147Thr), maternally inherited, and c.827 A > G (p.Glu276Gly), paternally inherited. The second variant was not listed in Infevers and was not identified in ClinVar or the peer-reviewed MKD literature searched on 13 July 2026. It was classified as likely pathogenic by the reporting laboratory, but laboratory-specific ACMG/AMP evidence codes and biochemical confirmation were unavailable. We also updated a systematic review of IL-1-targeted treatment in systemic MKD.
RESULTS: Intravenous immunoglobulin and systemic corticosteroids produced transient improvement. An etanercept biosimilar provided only temporary control. Tocilizumab prolonged attack intervals but was discontinued after likely treatment-associated secondary hypogammaglobulinemia requiring intravenous immunoglobulin and subsequent relapse. Firsekibart (Jin Beixin; Changchun GeneScience Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Changchun, China), a fully human IgG4λ monoclonal antibody that selectively neutralizes IL-1β, was then given off-label at 40 mg subcutaneously (approximately 4 mg/kg) every 4 weeks; after the second dose, the interval was extended to 40 days. At the latest documented follow-up, five doses had been given and no typical fever-rash attacks or new treatment-related adverse events had been reported. The original database search identified 876 records and 7 eligible reports; a targeted update added 3 full-text studies, including the RELIANCE registry, for 10 reports in the final descriptive synthesis. Trial, extension, cohort, post-marketing, registry, and case-based evidence consistently supported IL-1 pathway inhibition. Dose escalation, interval modification, and individualized treat-to-target adjustment were frequent across the published reports.
CONCLUSIONS: This case supports early MVK testing when recurrent infantile inflammation persists after treatment for suspected incomplete Kawasaki disease. The patient had marked hyperinflammation with several HLH-associated abnormalities, but not enough evidence for a formal HLH/MAS diagnosis. Her response is consistent with the established therapeutic rationale for IL-1 blockade in systemic MKD; however, the c.827 A > G variant requires fuller laboratory documentation, and the firsekibart observation remains a single-patient, short-term, agent-specific experience.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Case Reports; Systematic Review

Title: Higher lipoprotein(a) burden in women undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High lipoprotein (a) is a risk factor for the development of cardiovascular disease. Lp(a) lowering medications are under investigation in clinical trials. We aimed to assess sex/gender-specific differences in the distribution of Lp(a) levels in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: This is a prospective, cross-sectional observational trial including patients undergoing CABG. Patients were classified into Lp(a) categories (Lp(a) (nmol/l) < 62, > 105; ≥ 150; ≥ 175; ≥ 200). Univariate and multivariate analyses were used to test for sex/gender-specific differences in Lp(a) distribution.
RESULTS: Out of all 413 patients undergoing CABG between 11/2024 and 02/2026, 300 patients signed informed consent and 404 had available Lp(a) values. Women were significantly older (p < 0.001), more often never smokers (p = 0.001) and more frequently had a positive family history (p = 0.001). Median Lp(a) levels did not significantly differ between male and female patients in all 404 patients with available Lp(a) levels (27.8 (IQR 118) versus 37.4 (IQR 206.4); p = 0.165). Female patients were significantly more often distributed in Lp(a) categories > 105 nmol/l, ≥ 150 nmol/l, ≥ 175 nmol/l and ≥ 200 nmol/l, also after adjustment in multivariate analysis.
CONCLUSION: A sex/gender-specific difference in Lp(a) distribution was observed. Female patients were more often distributed in higher Lp(a) categories than men, especially in Lp(a) categories > 105, ≥ 150, ≥ 175 and ≥ 200 nmol/l. If Lp(a) lowering agents prove to be effective in clinical trials and currently investigated Lp(a) thresholds are adopted, female patients undergoing CABG may represent a subgroup more likely meeting future treatment eligibility criteria for Lp(a) lowering therapies. The observed difference in Lp(a) distribution may yield a potential contributor to the consistently reported poorer clinical outcomes in women after CABG and warrants further investigation.

Title: Impact of timing on outcomes following redo-sternotomy after initial CABG or valvular surgery.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The optimal timing of reoperation for those who need repeat coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and valve surgery is not well established. Early re-entries may be technically challenging due to adhesions and incomplete healing, while delayed interventions may expose patients to progressive cardiac disease.
METHODS: Patients undergoing redo-sternotomy for CABG and valve surgery were identified from the TriNetX database and categorized into three cohorts based on the interval from their initial sternotomy: <1 year, 1-5 years, and > 5 years. Redo-sternotomies performed < 30 days after the initial procedure were excluded, as these typically represent early interventions for acute complications rather than planned reoperations. Two independent propensity score-matched analyses compared < 1 year vs. 1-5 years and 1-5 years vs. > 5 years, with separately matched 1-5 years cohorts for each comparison. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on demographics, comorbidities, prior cardiac procedures, medications, and laboratory parameters including BMI. Primary outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and emergency department or hospital readmissions. Secondary outcomes included postoperative infection, atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury, dialysis, cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure, and cerebrovascular events.
RESULTS: After PSM in the < 1 year vs. 1-5 years analysis (N = 305 in each group), redo-sternotomy within 1 year showed no significant differences in mortality, MACCE or readmissions. Combined cerebrovascular events were significantly reduced in the < 1 year group. In the 1-5 years vs. > 5 years analysis (N = 439 in each group), outcomes were similar between groups, with no significant differences in mortality, MACCE, or readmissions. Atrial fibrillation was significantly higher in the 1-5 years group. All other secondary outcomes, including combined cerebrovascular events, were comparable.
CONCLUSION: Redo-sternotomy within 1 year appears to be equally safe compared to later intervals, with comparable rates of adverse events, including mortality, MACCE, readmissions, postoperative infection, or AKI.

Title: Long-term treatment with sirolimus for pediatric vascular anomalies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although sirolimus has emerged as a safe and effective treatment modality for unresectable vascular anomalies, comprehensive long-term follow-up data remain scarce in the current literature. This study aims to evaluate the long-term clinical experience of pediatric patients with vascular anomalies who received sirolimus treatment over five years.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 17 pediatric patients with vascular anomalies treated with sirolimus over five years in Asan Medical Center. Lesion volumes were measured via 3D volumetric MRI and normalized to body surface area (BSA). Adverse drug effects and therapeutic responses were periodically assessed. Longitudinal response was modeled using generalized additive mixed-effects models (GAMM). Tapering protocols were initiated after 24 months of stability, and alpelisib switch was considered for sirolimus-refractory cases with documented PIK3CA mutations.
RESULTS: With a median follow-up of 78 months, the overall response rate was 81.3%. GAMM analysis demonstrated a significant non-linear volume reduction (p < 0.0001), characterized by a rapid initial response within 12-24 months followed by a sustained plateau. Tapering was successful in 70.6% of patients without disease progression. Three patients with suboptimal responses transitioned to alpelisib; those with sufficient follow-up achieved additional volume reduction within 12 months. Long-term sirolimus use was well-tolerated, with no Grade ≥ 3 adverse events reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Sirolimus provides sustained long-term efficacy and safety in pediatric vascular anomalies. The observed treatment plateau suggests that dose tapering is a viable strategy for sustained responders. Furthermore, genotype-guided transition to alpelisib offers an effective alternative for refractory PIK3CA-mutant cases.

Title: A novel glyco-inflammatory healing index for risk prediction after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Glyco-Inflammatory Healing Index (GIHI), calculated as HbA1c × C-reactive protein / albumin, integrates measures of glycemic control, systemic inflammation, and nutritional status. Its association with postoperative outcomes after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) has not been fully established, particularly according to diabetes status.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, international, multicenter cohort study of 6,262 adults who underwent isolated CABG between 2010 and 2025. Patients were stratified by diabetes status. GIHI was analyzed as a standardized continuous variable and descriptively categorized as high or low based on subgroup medians. The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, or repeat revascularization. The secondary outcome was long-term all-cause mortality. Associations were evaluated using Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and receiver operating characteristic curves.
RESULTS: Among 6,262 patients, 2,783 (44.5%) had diabetes. In diabetic patients, higher GIHI was associated with 30-day MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.28-1.65), 30-day myocardial infarction (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.00-1.60), 30-day mortality (HR 2.56, 95% CI 2.06-3.18), and long-term mortality (HR 2.57, 95% CI 2.33-2.83). In non-diabetic patients, GIHI was not associated with 30-day MACE but remained associated with 30-day and long-term mortality. Adding GIHI modestly improved discrimination for 30-day MACE in diabetic patients (AUC 0.65 to 0.69; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher GIHI was associated with adverse postoperative outcomes after isolated CABG, particularly in patients with diabetes. These findings suggest GIHI may provide incremental prognostic information, but prospective validation is needed before its routine clinical application.

Title: Metabolic and urological outcomes following sleeve gastrectomy: a prospective surgical cohort study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the incidence of urolithiasis and associated alterations in 24-hour urinary biochemistry in patients undergoing sleeve gastrectomy (SG).
METHODS: This prospective single-center study included patients undergoing sleeve gastrectomy between January 2020 and June 2023. Ultrasonography and a 24-hour urine collection were performed one week preoperatively. Postoperative ultrasonography was conducted every 6 months through 24 months, with repeat 24-hour urine analysis at 24 months. Urinary volume, pH, calcium, oxalate, citrate, uric acid, sodium, potassium, and magnesium were measured. All ultrasonographic evaluations were performed by a single radiologist, and all surgical procedures were conducted by a single experienced surgeon.
RESULTS: Of 94 analyzed patients, 12 (12.8%) developed urolithiasis over a median 18-month follow-up. Postoperatively, mean urine volume decreased (2248 to 1518 mL) and mean uric acid declined (623 to 541 mg), whereas mean calcium (170 to 242 mg) and mean urinary pH (5.5 to 5.9) increased (all p < 0.001). Significant postoperative reductions were also observed in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, serum glucose, triglycerides, and LDL cholesterol, whereas HDL cholesterol significantly increased (all p < 0.05). Oxalate and citrate were unchanged overall. Among stone formers, calcium and citrate increased, while volume and magnesium decreased.
CONCLUSION: SG was associated with lower urine volume and uric acid and higher calcium and pH, alongside a 12.8% urolithiasis rate. These shifts underscore the lithogenic potential of SG despite its non-malabsorptive nature and support structured metabolic follow-up after surgery.

Title: Long-term mobile use and incident hypertension: findings from the Shahrekord PERSIAN cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The widespread and increasing mobile use has raised concerns about hypertension risk; therefore, this study investigates the association between long-term use (> 10 years) and hypertension in adults aged 35-70 years.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 7,490 adults aged 35-70 years from the Shahrekord PERSIAN Cohort Study who were free of hypertension at baseline. Mobile use duration was categorized as < 5, 5-10, and ≥ 10 years. Incident hypertension was identified during follow-up, and hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression after adjustment for potential confounders.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 47.55 ± 8.33 years. During 61,895.9 person-years of follow-up, 236 participants developed incident hypertension, yielding an incidence rate of 3.81 per 1,000 person-years. In the multivariable Cox proportional hazards model, compared with participants with < 5 years of mobile use, those with 5-10 years (aHR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.05, 2.43) and ≥ 10 years (aHR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.03, 1.96) had significantly higher hazards of incident hypertension. Older age, obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²), depression, hypertriglyceridemia, and alcohol non-use were also independently associated with incident hypertension.
CONCLUSION: Long-term mobile use was independently associated with an increased risk of incident hypertension in this prospective cohort. These findings highlight the need to incorporate digital technology-related behaviors into cardiovascular prevention strategies.

Title: Preliminary experience of mechanical thrombectomy treatment in pediatric arterial ischemic stroke: a retrospective case series.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy in the treatment of pediatric acute ischemic stroke (AIS).
METHODS: The clinical data, radiographic results and management outcomes of children diagnosed with AIS and treated at our hospital between 2016 and 2021 were retrospectively analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 8 patients (4 male and 4 female) were included, with a mean age of 7.8 ± 2.8 years. All patients presented with focal neurological deficits at onset, including hemiplegia, facial deviation, mild limb weakness, dizziness, and headache, with Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (PedNIHSS) scores ranging from 4 to 12 on presentation. Six patients had isolated middle cerebral artery occlusion, one bilateral posterior cerebral artery occlusion, and one had combined middle cerebral and anterior cerebral artery occlusion. Half of the patients underwent two mechanical thrombectomy procedures. After treatment, all patients achieved a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) score of ≥2b. The median follow up duration was 20.13 months (range, 6-32 months). At the 6-month follow-up, all patients had the pediatric modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores of 0 to 1.
CONCLUSION: Our preliminary experience suggests that mechanical thrombectomy is technically feasible and may be associated with favorable short- to medium-term functional outcomes in carefully selected pediatric patients with large vessel AIS. However, due to the retrospective design, small sample size, and lack of a control group, further multicenter prospective studies are warranted to better evaluate the safety and clinical outcomes of this procedure in pediatric patients.

Title: Are oral hygiene behaviors associated with lower stroke risk? A systematic review.
Abstract:
AIM: This study aims to systematically synthesize observational evidence on the association between oral hygiene behaviors, including tooth brushing, interdental cleaning, dental visits, and professional dental cleaning, and stroke risk in adults.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review was conducted by searching PubMed, Scopus, Embase and google scholar on November 26, 2025. Observational studies evaluating oral hygiene behaviors in relation to stroke or cerebrovascular outcomes were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS). Due to substantial heterogeneity in exposures, outcomes, and effect measures, findings were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies (9 cohort, 4 cross-sectional) involving over 1.1 million participants were included. Eleven studies evaluated tooth brushing; six out of eight cohort studies and one of three cross sectional ones reported significant inverse associations. Interdental cleaning generally demonstrated a protective directional association with stroke risk; however, several studies reported non-significant associations following multivariable adjustment. Regular dental visits and professional dental cleaning were associated with reductions in stroke risk across cohort studies. Cross-sectional evidence for brushing alone and dental visit frequency was less consistent.
CONCLUSIONS: Observational evidence supports an association between favorable oral hygiene behaviors, particularly frequent tooth brushing and professional dental cleaning, and reduced stroke risk. Oral hygiene may represent an underrecognized component of vascular prevention strategies.

Title: Association of structured out-of-hospital continuity of care with wound healing and quality of life in severe diabetic foot ulcer: a retrospective exploratory study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the association of a structured out-of-hospital continuity of care intervention with diabetic ulcer healing and patient-reported outcomes in individuals with severe diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), and to identify prognostic factors influencing healing.
METHODS: This retrospective comparative study included 91 inpatients with severe DFUs (Wagner grades 4-5). The intervention group (n = 45) received a structured out-of-hospital care protocol comprising domiciliary visits, remote monitoring, and access to specialized care as needed. The control group (n = 46) was provided with standard post-discharge follow-up. Outcomes included ulcer healing status, time to complete wound closure, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Factors related to wound healing were assessed using Fine-Gray competing risks regression, with major amputation and death treated as competing events.
RESULTS: Over a mean follow-up of 10.74 ± 9.05 months, the intervention group showed a higher ulcer healing rate compared to the control group (82.22% vs. 63.04%; difference 19.20%, 95% CI: 0.80% - 37.50%, p = 0.060). In the Fine-Gray competing risks analysis, the intervention group was associated with a significantly higher probability of healing (subdistribution hazard ratio = 1.74, 95% CI: 1.08-2.83, p = 0.024). Regarding HRQoL, a transient between-group difference in EQ-5D-5L was observed at 6 months (p = 0.029), but the group-by-time interaction was not significant (p = 0.220), indicating no sustained improvement.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory retrospective study, structured out-of-hospital continuity of care was associated with a statistically non-significant increase in crude healing rates. After accounting for competing risks, a significant association was observed in the primary analysis. However, this effect was attenuated and no longer significant in additional baseline severity factors (ABI and ulcer location). A transient improvement in quality of life at 6 months was not sustained. Ulcer severity and peripheral artery disease were identified as independent prognostic factors. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these exploratory findings.

Title: Changing trends in the clinical characteristics of gastrointestinal bleeding among hospitalized patients from 2012-2024 in China: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) remains a critical medical emergency with rising healthcare burdens in China. This study aimed to analyze its epidemiological shifts and risk factors over the past decade.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis included 3,523 inpatients with GIB at Renji Hospital (2012-2024), stratified into two periods: 2012-2019 (n = 2,024) and 2020-2024 (n = 1,499). Temporal trends were assessed with Student's t-tests, Mann-Whitney U test and Pearson's χ² tests and further verified by Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling.
RESULTS: The mean age increased from 56.35 to 58.05 years (P < 0.01), while the median of hospital stay decreased from 9 to 7 days (P < 0.01). The age distribution shifted toward older population, with a decline in the 40-59 years group (from 30.09% to 26.68%; P = 0.03) and a rise in the 60-79 years group (from 41.50% to 46.96%; P < 0.01). Etiologies of GIB also evolved: the proportions of peptic ulcer disease and variceal bleeding decreased significantly, whereas cases of inflammatory bowel disease and post-endoscopic bleeding increased (all P < 0.01). Concurrently, antithrombotic use rose from 13.29% to 20.08% (P < 0.01), accompanied by higher prevalence of comorbidities such as cerebral infarction and coronary heart disease (P < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings illustrate a rapidly evolving GIB landscape in China, characterized by an aging patient profile, changing etiology, and rising antithrombotic use. These changes, likely driven by demographic aging and evolving clinical practices, underscore the need for updated management protocols-including enhanced bleeding risk assessment in elderly patients, standardized peri‑endoscopic care, and dynamic resource allocation-to address the growing complexity of GIB cases.

Title: Papillomacular bundle thickness is associated with visual acuity in proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether the papillomacular bundle thickness (PBT), measured as the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness at a point halfway between the fovea and the optic disc, is significantly associated with best-corrected visual acuity in eyes with proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted on patients with a history of proliferative diabetic retinopathy who presented to the Ambulatory Care Network Vitreoretinal Clinic at New York-Presbyterian Hospital at Columbia University Irving Medical Center between January and December 2023. One eye per patient was eligible for inclusion. The PBT was measured using pre-existing Cirrus OCT 512 × 128 macular cube scans. The ETDRS central subfield thickness (CST) was recorded from the Cirrus review software. Best-corrected visual acuity was obtained from the medical record and converted into an ETDRS letter score.
RESULTS: Forty-five patients were included. The mean ± SD ETDRS letter score, PBT, and CST were 58.6 ± 16.1 letters, 34.3 ± 13.9 μm, and 293.6 ± 107.0 μm, respectively. PBT was significantly correlated with visual acuity (r = 0.47; p = 0.001), while CST was not (p = 0.52). Linear regression of visual acuity on PBT yielded a coefficient of 0.55 (p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Thinning of the PBT is associated with decreased visual acuity in eyes with proliferative diabetic retinopathy. For every 2 micrometers of PBT thinning, there is an expected loss of approximately 1 ETDRS letter.

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of machine-learning models for detecting pulmonary embolism in patients with pneumonia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients with pneumonia presents a major diagnostic challenge because of overlapping clinical features and the limited specificity of conventional tools. Machine learning (ML)-based models have been proposed to improve diagnostic accuracy by integrating clinical, laboratory, and imaging data.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to May 2026. Fifteen studies met inclusion criteria, of which ten provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. The primary meta-analysis was restricted to studies reporting patient- or examination-level binary PE detection against an imaging or adjudicated reference standard; clinical prediction, segmentation/localization, thrombosis, and mortality outcomes were analyzed separately, and overlapping public-dataset studies were reduced to one estimate per dataset. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and summary receiver operating characteristic estimates were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model. Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses explored sources of heterogeneity. Study quality was evaluated using the PROBAST + AI tool, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Across included studies, ML-based models showed high overall diagnostic discrimination for PE detection in pneumonia. The primary analysis of six patient/examination-level studies yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.91 (95% CI 0.76-0.97; 95% prediction interval 0.16-0.99), specificity of 0.92 (95% CI 0.68-0.98; 95% prediction interval 0.02-1.00), and a summary AUROC of 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.98). However, substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8% overall; sensitivity I² = 76.0%, specificity I² = 85.3%) was observed across pooled estimates. Image-based deep-learning models applied to CTPA generally showed higher accuracy than clinical or hybrid approaches. According to GRADE, the overall certainty of evidence was rated as very low. Prediction intervals were wide, and the pooled operating point should not be read as the expected performance of a deployable model. Differences by reference standard and clinical setting were examined descriptively and are hypothesis-generating only.
CONCLUSIONS: ML-based models show promise as adjunctive tools for PE detection in pneumonia, but current evidence is limited by heterogeneity and low certainty. Prospective, multicenter validation and standardized evaluation are required before clinical implementation. The current evidence is heterogeneous, indirect, and insufficient to establish the performance of a deployable tool in any individual clinical setting.

Title: Clinical features of acute and chronic abdominal pain in children admitted to gastroenterology unit.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of abdominal pain in children has been gradually rising. The study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics of hospitalized children with abdominal pain for making the accurate diagnosis and treatment.
METHODS: This study collected the clinical data from a pediatric institution between January 2023 and January 2026. The data primarily included gender, age, body mass index (BMI), intensity, duration of pain, site of pain, common associated symptoms, diagnoses and surgical interventions.
RESULTS: A total of 1025 patients presenting with abdominal pain were analyzed. Among them, there were 625 boys (60.98%) and 400 girls (39.02%), with a median age of this cohort was 8.0 years (5.00, 11.00). The primary diagnoses were chronic gastritis (n = 458, 44.68%), acute gastroenteritis (n = 321, 31.32%), Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) (n = 100, 9.76%), and chronic enteritis (n = 44, 4.29%). Most patients (76.39%) had acute pain, and the median duration of pain was 2 months (0.1, 10.00). The pain in most patients localized in the periumbilical region (54.63%). In addition, The most common concomitant symptoms were vomiting (53.46%), diarrhea (22.63%), and fever (22.44%). 668 (65.17%) patients received gastrointestinal endoscope examination. Moreover, subgroup analyses were conducted based on disease types, intensity, gender and age. Statistical differences were found in some variables including age, gender, intensity, duration of pain, site of pain and concomitant symptoms (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Chronic gastritis was the most common disease in children, followed by acute gastroenteritis, HSP and chronic enteritis. Most children suffered from acute periumbilical pain, with vomiting as the most frequent concomitant symptom. Furthermore, significant differences were observed in some clinical characteristics of different subgroup analyses.

Title: Characteristics and outcomes of implantable cardioverter defibrillator therapy in patients with cardiac amyloidosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is associated with symptomatic heart failure and high morbidity and mortality. There is conflicting data on the benefits of implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICD) in patients with CA.
OBJECTIVES: To characterize CA patients undergoing ICD therapy and assess long term outcomes and ICD shocks as both a cohort of CA stratified subtype of amyloid light chain (AL) versus transthyretin (TTR).
METHODS: We studied all patients undergoing ICD implantation for a diagnosis of CA as either primary or secondary prevention between 1997 and 2019 in our health system. Baseline characteristics and outcomes were reviewed.
RESULTS: There were 62 patients with CA that underwent ICD implantation. Baseline characteristics included diabetes (30.6%), hypertension (72.6%), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (12.9%), and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III/IV (54.8%). Over a mean follow-up of 4.9 years (SD 4.0 years), the mortality rate was 62.1% in AL as compared to 69.7% in TTR CA patients (p = 0.53). First appropriate ICD shock occurred in 60% of AL patients compared to 54.5% of TTR patients, with no statistically significant difference observed between the two cohorts (p = 0.78). Inappropriate second ICD shock occurred in 71.4% of AL amyloid patients compared to 80% of TTR patients, with no significant difference observed between the two cohorts (p = 0.74). Competing risk analysis for the occurrence of ICD shock demonstrated a non-significantly higher incidence of shock for AL CA patients as compared to TTR CA patients (p = 0.20). Finally, multivariate cox regression demonstrated that TTR amyloid, advanced age, male sex, LVEF, andNYHA class III/IV were not independent predictors for the combined outcome of ICD shock, death, or heart failure hospitalization post-ICD placement.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with CA undergoing ICD therapy have high rates of mortality, with similar outcomes irrespective of amyloid subtype. The high rates of inappropriate shocks for both AL and TTR CA patients are relevant factors to consider during ICD counseling.

Title: Dental pulp stones as an independent predictor for extracranial carotid artery calcification: a cross-sectional cone-beam computed tomography analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular calcification is a key indicator of cardiovascular risk, and dental imaging allows its visualization. Dental pulp calcifications (pulp stones) have been suggested as markers of systemic mineralization. This study aimed to assess the association between pulp stones and extracranial carotid artery calcification (ECAC) using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, CBCT scans of 250 adults (124 men, 126 women; aged 20-81 years) from a university dental radiology department were evaluated. ECAC were bilaterally graded (0-4), and pulp stones were recorded as present or absent. Images were standardized to the Frankfurt horizontal plane and examined by a blinded observer. Descriptive statistics summarized demographics, while Chi-square and regression analyses explored associations.
RESULTS: ECAC was detected in 53 participants (21.2%), with prevalence increasing with age (p ≤ 0.008). Women showed higher rates than men (27.0% vs. 15.3%, p = 0.036). Pulp stones were more frequent in women (41.3% vs. 20.2%, p < 0.001) and older individuals (p = 0.001). Multivariable analysis indicated pulp stones as an independent predictor of ECAC (OR = 5.94; 95% CI: 2.97-11.85, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Pulp stones detected on CBCT were significantly associated with ECAC, suggesting their potential as adjunctive indicators of cardiovascular risk.

Title: Clinical study on the combined predictive value of admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and stress hyperglycemia ratio for early neurological deterioration in acute ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early neurological deterioration (END) affects short-term prognosis in acute ischemic stroke. Inflammation and stress-related glucose dysregulation may contribute to END, but their incremental predictive value remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations of admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) with END and assess whether adding these biomarkers to clinical variables improves risk discrimination.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 180 patients with acute ischemic stroke admitted between January 2021 and December 2024. NLR was calculated as neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio. SHR was calculated as admission glucose/estimated average glucose and rescaled as SHR_0.1 = SHR/0.1 before regression, so that the OR represented each 0.1-unit increase. END was defined as an NIHSS increase ≥ 2 within 72 h. Multivariate logistic regression and ROC analysis were performed.
RESULTS: END occurred in 38 patients (21.1%). NLR was independently associated with END per 1-unit increase (OR = 1.193, 95% CI 1.071-1.328, P = 0.001). Rescaled SHR was independently associated with END per 0.1-unit increase (OR = 1.241, 95% CI 1.082-1.424, P = 0.002). The basic clinical model had an AUC of 0.793, whereas adding NLR and SHR increased the AUC to 0.884.
CONCLUSION: Admission NLR and rescaled SHR were independently associated with END. Adding these routine biomarkers to clinical variables may improve early END risk stratification, pending external validation.

Title: Evaluation of the relationship between cardiac remodeling and serum FABP3 in hypertensive patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading cause of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality. In addition, owing to the pathological processes it causes in the vascular bed, it leads to end-organ damage, thereby contributing to morbidity. FABP3 (fatty acid binding protein 3) is a protein primarily expressed in the cardiac muscle, skeletal muscle, and kidney, and plays an important role in cardiomyocyte homeostasis.
METHODS: Echocardiographic evaluation was performed in 41 normotensive controls and 120 patients with hypertension. Patients with cardiac remodelling (n = 50) and hypertrophy (n = 33) were identified by calculating the left ventricular mass and relative wall thickness. FABP3 levels were measured in serum samples using ELISA.
RESULTS: FABP3 levels demonstrated an increasing trend (p < 0.0001) across the control, non-remodelled hypertensive, remodelling, and hypertrophy groups (1.27 ± 0.81, 1.85 ± 0.75, 2.31 ± 1.06, and 2.85 ± 1.71 ng/ml, respectively). FABP3 levels were significantly but weakly correlated with posterior wall thickness (ρ = 0.29), relative wall thickness (ρ = 0.23), and troponin levels (ρ = 0.2).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that FABP3 may be associated with hypertension-mediated cardiac remodelling and left ventricular hypertrophy. FABP3 may have potential as a supportive biomarker reflecting subclinical cardiac involvement in patients with hypertension.

Title: Effects of 8-week brisk walking combined with table tennis exercise on cardiovascular function in middle-aged and elderly individuals.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore the effects and the underlying mechanisms of an 8-week brisk walking combined with table tennis exercise on the cardiovascular function of the middle-aged and elderly individuals.
METHODS: Forty-eight middle-aged and elderly individuals were randomly divided into the brisk walking (BW) group, table tennis (TT) group, brisk walking combined with table tennis (BT) group, and the control group. Body composition parameters were assessed using a body composition analyzer. Cardiovascular function was analyzed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), flow-mediated dilation (FMD), and heart rate variability (HRV) assessment. Plasma biomarkers levels were detected by ELISA. We also analyzed 8-week changes in a composite CVD-Z score based on established cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: The BT group showed a significant increase in muscle mass (37.85 ± 7.26 to 39.01 ± 6.67). However, all three exercise modalities exhibited a significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (SBP) and central systolic blood pressure (CSBP), with a decrease of diastolic blood pressure (CDBP) observed exclusively in the BT group (75.82 ± 7.96 to 71.00 ± 6.53). The PWV analysis revealed significant decrease of the carotid-femoral Pulse Wave Velocity (cfPWV), augmentation index (AIx) and augmentation index normalized to a heart rate of 75 beats per minute (AIx@75) in BT group. While both TT and BT improved FMD (5.78 ± 0.87 to 7.30 ± 1.76 and 6.02 ± 0.95 to 8.06 ± 1.45). The HRV analysis showed BT decreased heart rate (HR), increased percent of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 ms (PNN50), standard deviation of all normal-to-normal RR intervals (SDNN), and high-frequency power (HF). An Increase in total power (TP) was detected in all the three exercise modalities. Furthermore, only BT upregulated serum levels of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), and downregulated intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1(VCAM-1) levels. All exercise groups had reduced composite CVD-Z score after 8 weeks, with the BT group showing the largest numerical reduction.
CONCLUSION: Collectively, the BT intervention elicited the numerically greater cardiovascular function benefits, independent of weight loss, potentially via reducing arterial stiffness, enhancing parasympathetic activity, and modulating key cardiovascular biomarkers. However, the majority of these favorable numerical changes did not reach statistical significance when compared with standalone brisk walking (BW) or table tennis (TT). Meanwhile, several limitations of this trial should be noted, including its small sample size, passive control design and potential selective outcome reporting.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was retrospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) on 28 May 2025, registration number: ChiCTR2500103378, available at: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=268481 .

Title: Association between hemoglobin A1c levels and coronary flow reserve in angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries: a retrospective observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) measures chronic glycemic levels, and its elevation is associated with vascular endothelial dysfunction and microcirculatory impairment, contributing to increased cardiovascular risk. In the assessment of angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA), coronary flow reserve (CFR) reflects vasodilatory capacity of the coronary microvasculature and is associated with adverse cardiovascular events, whereas IMR quantifies microvascular resistance during hyperemia. However, the association between HbA1c levels and invasive microvascular indices in ANOCA remains unclear.
METHODS: This study included 104 patients with ANOCA who underwent invasive coronary physiological assessment. CFR and IMR were measured using the thermodilution method. Associations between admission clinical parameters, including demographic characteristics and laboratory variables (particularly HbA1c), and CFR or IMR were examined using univariate and multivariate analyses.
RESULTS: The study population had a mean age of 65.8 ± 13.0 years, 50.0% were male, mean HbA1c was 6.0 ± 0.7%, mean CFR was 4.3 ± 2.4, and mean IMR was 14.2 ± 8.8. Multivariate analysis demonstrated a significant negative association between HbA1c and CFR (β = -0.250, 95% CI: -1.619 to - 0.155, P = 0.018). In contrast, no significant association was observed between HbA1c and IMR.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with ANOCA, higher HbA1c levels were independently associated with reduced CFR but not with IMR. These findings suggest a potential association between chronic glycemic status and coronary vasodilatory function in ANOCA.

Title: AI-Based Low-Dose Chest CT Assessment of Coronary Artery Calcification Score: An Analysis of Accuracy-Relating Factors.
Journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
Abstract: This study evaluates the accuracy of AI-based coronary artery calcium scoring on nongated low-dose chest CT and identifies factors affecting calcium risk classification, using ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT as the reference standard. This prospective study included 312 patients with chest pain who underwent ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT and additional low-dose chest CT (LDCT). LDCT images were reconstructed using pulmonary and standard kernels. AI software automatically quantified Agatston, mass, volume, and total coronary artery calcium scores (CACSs). Patients were stratified by Agatston-based risk category, heart rate (≤ 65 vs. > 65 bpm), and BMI (< 25 vs. ≥ 25 kg/m2). Agreement, systematic bias, and risk classification performance were assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, ICC analysis, Friedman tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, linear regression, and confusion matrices. Pulmonary kernel LDCT produced Agatston scores comparable to ECG-gated CT, with no significant differences across heart rate, BMI, or calcium severity subgroups. Under this kernel, measurement bias showed weak but significant correlations with heart rate and BMI (r = 0.145 and r = 0.131, respectively; both P < 0.05). Overall, nongated LDCT-derived CACS correlated strongly with reference CACS (r > 0.94). The low heart rate/low-BMI subgroup showed the best risk stratification performance, with 80% accuracy and good agreement (κ = 0.72). AI-assisted CACS assessment on nongated low-dose chest CT may serve as an adjunctive tool for opportunistic coronary artery calcification screening and preliminary cardiovascular risk stratification. Its accuracy may be influenced by reconstruction kernel and calcification burden, whereas heart rate and BMI may not be significant influencing factors.Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100073,2 April 2025, the study was retrospectively registered).

Title: Expression of herpes simplex virus-related genes in peripheral blood leukocytes of patients with behçet's disease: a case-control study.
Abstract: Behçet's disease is a chronic, relapsing multisystem inflammatory disorder characterized by recurrent oral and genital ulcerations, ocular inflammation, cutaneous lesions, and variable involvement of the vascular, neurological, and gastrointestinal systems. Although its precise etiology remains incompletely understood, accumulating evidence indicates that the disease arises from a complex interplay between genetic susceptibility, immune dysregulation, and environmental triggers. Among the proposed infectious agents, herpes simplex virus (HSV) has attracted considerable attention because of its capacity to induce persistent immune activation, molecular mimicry, and chronic inflammatory responses. Accordingly, the present study aimed to evaluate the expression profiles of HSV-related genes (UL29, UL18, UL46, and UL47) in peripheral blood leukocytes of patients with Behçet's disease to clarify the potential contribution of HSV infection to disease pathogenesis and immune-mediated inflammatory mechanisms. In this case-control study, 40 patients with BD and 40 healthy individuals were included as the control group. Blood samples were collected from all participants. Total RNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes, followed by cDNA synthesis. The expression levels of UL29, UL18, UL46, and UL47 genes were quantified using RT-qPCR. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to assess the diagnostic potential of the studied genes. Statistical analyses were conducted using GraphPad Prism and SPSS software (P-value ≤ 0.05). The expression of HSV-related genes was significantly higher in BD patients compared to healthy controls. After Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, UL29 remained significantly upregulated (4.5-fold, adjusted p = 0.012), while UL46 (3.7-fold, adjusted p = 0.060), UL18 (2.0-fold, adjusted p = 0.152), and UL47 (2.25-fold, p = 0.12) did not reach statistical significance. ROC curve analysis demonstrated strong diagnostic potential for UL29 (AUC = 0.90, sensitivity 80%, specificity 92.5%), UL46 (AUC = 0.86, sensitivity 87%, specificity 77.5%), and UL18 (AUC = 0.80, sensitivity 85%, specificity 72.5%). Overall, UL29, UL46, and UL18 showed promising potential as biomarkers for distinguishing BD patients from healthy individuals. Increased expression of UL29, UL46, and UL18 is associated with BD, and these genes, particularly UL29, show promising potential as diagnostic biomarkers. Further validation studies are needed.

Title: Spontaneous recanalization of pediatric internal carotid artery dissection during aspirin monotherapy: a retrospective case series.
Journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Internal carotid artery (ICA) dissection is an increasingly recognized cause of arterial ischemic stroke (AIS) in children, but optimal management strategies remain uncertain. While anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy is commonly employed, data on radiographic outcomes and vessel recanalization rates are limited. The objective of this study was to describe the clinical and radiographic outcomes of children with ICA dissection-related AIS who received aspirin monotherapy for secondary prevention.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed five consecutive pediatric patients with acute AIS secondary to ICA dissection treated at our institution between 2018 and 2025. All patients received aspirin monotherapy (3-5 mg/kg/day) initiated at diagnosis. Clinical presentations, neuroimaging findings (MRI/MRA, DSA, vessel wall imaging), laboratory evaluations, and follow-up imaging were analyzed. The primary outcome was angiographic vessel recanalization on follow-up imaging.
RESULTS: Three patients had right-sided and two had left-sided intracranial ICA dissections. Two cases were associated with definite trauma, while three cases were spontaneous. All patients presented with acute hemiparesis, and two presented with seizures. Laboratory findings ruled out the diagnosis of large-vessel vasculitis. Follow-up vascular imaging (MRI/MRA) performed at discharge demonstrated complete recanalization of the affected ICA in all five patients. All patients achieved favorable neurological outcomes with resolution or significant improvement of deficits.
CONCLUSION: This case series demonstrates that aspirin monotherapy may be associated with complete vascular recanalization and favorable clinical outcomes in pediatric ICA dissection, including both traumatic and spontaneous cases. It suggests that complete vessel recanalization may be more common in children than previously recognized.

Title: Evaluation of the NORPACS risk score in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The no-reflow prediction in acute coronary syndrome (NORPACS) risk score was developed to predict the risk of no reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate whether the NORPACS risk score predicts the outcome of patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) treated with primary PCI (pPCI).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 1725 patients. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed 6 as the optimal NORPACS risk score cut-off value. Patients were thus dichotomized into two groups: high (≥ 6) NORPACS risk score (n = 765) and low (< 6) NORPACS risk score (n = 960).
RESULTS: The frequency of in-hospital and all-cause mortality was significantly higher in the high NORPACS risk score group than in the low NORPACS risk score group. Compared with the baseline model, in the full model of binary logistic regression, the NORPACS risk score as both a continuous and a categorical variable emerged as an independent predictor of in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.31-1.99, p < 0.001; OR: 4.96, 95% CI: 2.13-11.54, p < 0.001; respectively). Compared with the baseline model, in the full model of multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analysis, the NORPACS risk score as both a continuous and a categorical variable emerged as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.22, 95% CI: 1.07-1.38, p = 0.004; HR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.27-3.06, p = 0.003; respectively).
CONCLUSION: The NORPACS risk score can be used for prognostication of patients with STEMI treated with pPCI. It predicts in-hospital and long-term all-cause mortality and may serve as a practical tool for risk stratification in this patient population.

Title: [Prolonged mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting].
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following coronary bypass surgery, postoperative intensive care plays a central role in the subsequent course of the illness. It is well known that patients with prolonged mechanical ventilation have an increased risk of developing numerous secondary organ complications and consequently have higher morbidity and mortality. The objective of this study was to validate established risk factors for prolonged postoperative mechanical ventilation after isolated coronary bypass surgery in a recent, representative patient collective.
METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study, all patients who underwent isolated coronary bypass surgery in 2024 and subsequently received interdisciplinary intensive care at the Ulm University Clinic were included.
RESULTS: The 312 patients included in the study were between 45 and 85 years old; 84% (n = 262) were male. The median ventilation time for all patients was 15 h (Q1 = 11 h; Q3 = 21 h), whereby 19.5% (n = 61) required prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV). In the multiple logistic regression analysis, intraoperative perfusion time (OR = 1.01; 95% CI 1.0-1.02; p = 0.04) and postoperative peak lactate (OR = 1.26; 95% CI 1.12-1.41; p < 0.001) were significant independent risk factors for PMV. The PMV group also had significantly lower oxygenation indices (Horovitz index = paO2/FiO2), more positive fluid balances on the first and cumulatively on the second postoperative day, longer ischemia and surgical times, and higher European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) scores. Hospital mortality was significantly higher at 8.2% (n = 5) in the PMV group than in the non-PMV group at 0.8% (n = 2).
CONCLUSION: A comprehensive risk profile for prolonged mechanical ventilation is an essential component of intensive care risk stratification and treatment planning. It enables a differentiated assessment of severity and complexity of underlying diseases and thereby associated organ dysfunction. Against this backdrop, necessary intensive care interventions can be initiated early and potentially contribute to improve treatment outcomes.

Title: Sleep duration: a neglected factor in stroke prevention among individuals with dysglycemia.
Journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
Abstract:
AIM: Stroke imposes a staggering and escalating disease burden in China. Individuals with dysglycemia face a markedly elevated risk of incident cerebrovascular events. This study aimed to characterize global and Chinese trends in stroke burden and examine the association between sleep duration and stroke among individuals with dysglycemia, with a particular focus on the potential utility of sleep duration as an behavioral marker for cerebrovascular risk assessment.
METHODS: This study utilized the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database to assess the trends of stroke burden globally and in China(1990-2023). In addition, the study was conducted using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), encompassing participants aged ≥ 45 with baseline dysglycemia and no prior stroke. Sleep duration was obtained from the 2020 survey, while incident stroke status was ascertained across the 2013, 2015, 2018, and 2020 follow-up waves. Stepwise logistic regression models were employed to evaluate the independent association between baseline sleep duration and new-onset stroke. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) with four knots were applied to explore non-linear dose-response relationships. Additionally, subgroup analyses were conducted to identify effect modifications, and receiver operating characteristic curves evaluated the discriminatory performance of the prediction model including sleep factors.
RESULTS: Despite declining global age-standardized rate, the absolute stroke burden in China significantly increased from 1990 to 2023, particularly among males and older adults. In the CHARLS cohort, 7,274 patients with dysglycemia were included in 2011. After a ten-year follow-up, 694 participants (9.54%) developed new strokes. Notably, the sleep duration was significantly longer (9.95 ± 1.74 h hours, P < 0.0001) in the new stroke group. The model after including covariates showed that for every additional hour of sleep, the risk of stroke increased by 22% (OR = 1.22, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.32). Crucially, RCS analysis uncovered a non-linear inflection point at 7.5-8 h, demonstrating that cerebrovascular risk accelerated rapidly beyond this threshold. The fully adjusted model showed the highest discriminatory performance among the evaluated models, although the overall discrimination remained modest (AUC = 0.666).
CONCLUSIONS: China's absolute stroke burden continued to surge. Sleep duration may serve as an easily obtainable behavioral marker that complements conventional factors in stroke risk assessment among individuals with dysglycemia.A non-linear association was observed, with stroke risk increasing more rapidly beyond approximately 7.5-8 h of sleep. These findings suggest that sleep duration may provide complementary information for identifying metabolically vulnerable individuals at elevated cerebrovascular risk, although further prospective validation is required. By synergizing human epidemiological expertise with data-driven modeling, this study may provide a feasible approach to complement stroke risk stratification in metabolically vulnerable populations.

Title: The impact of pomalidomide-containing induction on stem cell mobilization and engraftment in multiple myeloma: a single-center experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) is the standard intensification therapy for eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM) patients. While lenalidomide impairs hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) mobilization, data regarding pomalidomide (POM)-containing induction remain extremely limited.
METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study analyzed NDMM patients undergoing HSC mobilization with high-dose cyclophosphamide (CTX) plus pegylated granulocyte colony-stimulating factor between 2023 and 2025. A 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline characteristics.
RESULTS: From 111 patients initially included, 33 matched pairs (n = 66) were analyzed. The incidence of poor mobilization was similar between the POM and control groups (36.4% vs. 30.3%, P = 0.602). However, the POM group exhibited a marginally lower total CD34 + cell yield (median: 5.81 vs. 7.21 × 10⁶/kg, P = 0.059) and a significantly lower proportion of patients achieving the optimal target of ≥ 6 × 10⁶ cells/kg (45.5% vs. 72.7%, P = 0.024). Borderline increases in plerixafor (PXF) requirements (87.9% vs. 69.7%, P = 0.071) were observed with POM. Within the POM cohort, concomitant daratumumab (Dara) exposure significantly reduced total CD34 + yields (median: 5.19 vs. 8.24 × 10⁶/kg, P = 0.014) and increased PXF requirements (100.0% vs. 66.7%, P = 0.012). Post-ASCT engraftment kinetics were comparable (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: POM-containing induction reduces the likelihood of achieving optimal HSC collection targets and increases reliance on on-demand PXF, a negative impact further compounded by concomitant Dara use. Nonetheless, it does not preclude minimum dose collection or compromise long-term engraftment.

Title: Late Discordance Between Right Ventricular Fractional Area Change and Free-Wall Longitudinal Strain After Cardiac Surgery Including Tricuspid Annuloplasty.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This single-center retrospective study assessed preoperative-to-late postoperative changes in right ventricular (RV) indices in patients undergoing cardiac surgery including tricuspid annuloplasty, predominantly with concomitant mitral valve surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed 63 patients with paired preoperative and late postoperative echocardiography after tricuspid annuloplasty. RV fractional area change (RVFAC), RV free-wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and tissue Doppler tricuspid annular peak systolic velocity (S') were compared over time. RVFAC >35% and absolute RVFWLS >20% were classified as preserved.
RESULTS: Late echocardiography was performed at a median of 47 months. No statistically significant within-patient change in RVFAC was detected (37.9% to 37.4%; Hodges-Lehmann estimate, -1.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.0 to +0.7; p = 0.231), whereas RVFWLS decreased from 19.2% to 15.7% (median within-patient change, -3.1 percentage points; Hodges-Lehmann estimate, -3.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -5.3 to -2.3; p < 0.001); TAPSE and S' were also lower at late follow-up (both p < 0.001). At follow-up, 30 of 37 patients with preserved RVFAC had reduced RVFWLS.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing tricuspid annuloplasty, predominantly with concomitant mitral valve surgery, preserved RVFAC at late follow-up does not necessarily indicate preserved RV free-wall longitudinal deformation. RVFAC alone may be insufficient to characterize RV function at late postoperative follow-up in this setting.

Title: Cumulative Triglyceride-Glucose-Related Metabolic Burden and Incident Cardiovascular Disease Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults With Low Handgrip Strength.
Abstract:
AIM: To examine associations of cumulative triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) and obesity-related derivatives, and their two-point change patterns, with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) among middle-aged and older adults with low handgrip strength.
METHODS: This study included 607 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study participants with low handgrip strength at least once during 2011-2015, defined by the 2019 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia criteria. Cumulative TyG and five derivatives were calculated from Waves 1 and 3. Change patterns were classified by values below or above the population median at both waves. Incident CVD was identified at Waves 4 and 5. Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic splines, and subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed for incident CVD, with additional component-specific analyses conducted separately for heart disease and stroke. Incremental predictive performance was evaluated using changes in the C-index, continuous NRI, and IDI.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 130 participants developed CVD. Each 1-standard deviation increase in cumulative TyG and its derivatives was associated with a 22%-40% higher CVD hazard. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartiles of all indicators except TyG-a body shape index were associated with higher risk (hazard ratios 1.62-2.71). High-high patterns of several indicators were associated with increased risk; high-low patterns of TyG-WC and TyG-body roundness index were also associated with higher risk. Restricted cubic splines suggested linear associations for five indicators, without evidence of nonlinearity. Associations were significant in several female and older-age strata, although interaction tests were not significant. Adding cumulative TyG-related indices to traditional CVD risk factors modestly improved apparent model discrimination (C-index: 0.623-0.646 vs. 0.606). Sensitivity analyses yielded generally consistent findings, and component-specific analyses showed broadly similar positive associations for heart disease and stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher cumulative TyG-related metabolic burden was associated with incident CVD. Adding cumulative TyG-related indices to traditional risk factor models modestly improved apparent predictive performance. Repeated assessment may aid cardiovascular risk stratification, but validation in larger, diverse cohorts is needed.

Title: Variations in Access to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement by Socioeconomic Factors: A Retrospective Population-Level Study in New South Wales, Australia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite increasing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) activity in Australia in recent years, patient access to TAVI remains limited and is often more complex than access to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). The aim of this study was to identify socioeconomic factors associated with the likelihood of receiving TAVI versus SAVR in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.
METHODS: Data from the NSW Admitted Patient Data Collection were used to compare the clinical and socioeconomic profiles of patients aged ≥65 years who underwent either TAVI or SAVR between 1 November 2017 and 28 February 2022. Multiple logistic regression analyses were performed on the overall patient cohort and on subgroups defined by age groups, hospital type and funding type.
RESULTS: The study included 6,493 patients (mean age: 79.1 years, 35.5% female) who underwent aortic valve replacement (SAVR=3,294; TAVI=3,199). The odds of receiving TAVI versus SAVR increased significantly with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] for patients aged 85 years and older versus those aged 75-84 years: 12.3, 95% CI: 9.99-15.2). Patients from the most disadvantaged socioeconomic areas had lower odds of receiving TAVI than those from the least disadvantaged areas (aOR:0.58, 95% CI: 0.47-0.73). Patients with private health insurance/Department of Veterans Affairs (PHI/DVA) funding were more likely to receive TAVI than SAVR (aOR: 3.29, 95% CI: 2.61-4.14), with this finding consistent across age groups and even more pronounced in patients treated in public hospitals (aOR: 5.82, 95% CI: 4.40-7.70).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlights significant variations in TAVI access based on age, socioeconomic status of area of residence, and funding type. These findings underscore the need for policy settings that promote equitable access and ensure that procedural choices for aortic valve replacement reflect clinical needs.

Title: Female Sex and Ventilatory Recovery After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated whether female sex is associated with postoperative mechanical ventilation duration and prolonged ventilation >24 hours after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study.
SETTING: Four German academic centers, 2017-2023.
PARTICIPANTS: Five hundred seventy-four adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%; 70 (12.2%) were women.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Primary outcomes were postoperative mechanical ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay. The primary models were adjusted for baseline/preoperative covariates without CPB. Female sex corresponded to +30.2% longer ventilation (95% CI -3.6% to +75.8%; p = 0.086), which did not reach conventional statistical significance, and higher odds of ventilation >24 hours (aOR 1.82, 95% CI 1.01-3.26; p = 0.045). Adding CPB strengthened the estimates, whereas extracorporeal life support exclusion and center fixed-effects adjustment attenuated them. In 69 matched pairs, women had longer ventilation (16.0 [8.0-33.2] v 11.0 [5.8-18.0] hours; p = 0.021) and more ventilation >24 hours (30.9% v 13.2%; p = 0.029). No clear association was observed with acute kidney injury or 30-day mortality.
CONCLUSION: Female sex showed a model-dependent association with prolonged postoperative ventilation in this HFrEF CABG cohort. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation with standardized perioperative and extubation protocols.

Title: Occlusion myocardial infarction without ST-elevation is associated with delayed angiography and a higher risk of cardiovascular events.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation decides who undergoes immediate angiography, yet a quarter to a third of patients without it have an occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) and follow the slower non-ST-elevation pathway. Their outcome over extended follow-up compared with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), including non-fatal events, is poorly defined.
METHODS: In a retrospective single-centre cohort, we reclassified 313 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing angiography as STEMI, NSTEMI-OMI, or NSTEMI-non-OMI. OMI was pre-specified as culprit TIMI flow ≤2, and/or markedly elevated peak troponin with a new wall-motion abnormality. The composite of death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular readmission was assessed at 12 months and over a median follow-up of 26.2 months.
RESULTS: Of 313 patients, 177 had STEMI and 136 had no ST-elevation, of whom 54 (39.7%) fulfilled OMI criteria. Median time to angiography was 10.1 h in NSTEMI-OMI versus 1.0 h in STEMI (p < 0.001) and 15.9 h in NSTEMI-non-OMI (p = 0.140). The 12-month composite occurred in 16.7% of NSTEMI-OMI, 3.4% of STEMI, and 2.4% of NSTEMI-non-OMI (p = 0.001). The adjusted hazard ratio for NSTEMI-OMI was 3.46 (95% CI 1.70-7.02) versus STEMI and 3.31 (1.43-7.63) versus NSTEMI-non-OMI. In patients event-free at 12 months, the unadjusted hazard ratio versus STEMI was 3.56 (1.40-9.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with OMI but no ST-segment elevation waited longer for angiography than STEMI and had a higher hazard of the composite outcome than both other groups, an excess persisting beyond the first year.

Title: Does Implant Choice Matter? Clinical and Radiological Outcomes of 3-Level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion With Standalone Anchored Cage vs Plate-Cage System.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) remains the gold-standard surgical treatment for multilevel degenerative cervical myelopathy. While anterior plate-cage (PC) constructs have traditionally been used to enhance stability and lordosis, they are associated with increased soft-tissue dissection and plate-related complications. Standalone anchored cage (SAAC) systems have emerged as a lower-profile alternative with proven efficacy in single- and 2-level disease; however, evidence supporting their use in 3-level contiguous ACDF remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical, radiological, and perioperative outcomes of 3-level ACDF performed using SAAC vs conventional PC constructs.
METHODS: A retrospective comparative study was conducted on 50 patients who underwent 3-level contiguous ACDF between 2017 and 2024 at 2 tertiary centers. Twenty-five patients received SAAC, and 25 received PC constructs. Clinical outcomes (visual analog scale, Neck Disability Index, and modified Japanese Orthopedic Association) and radiological parameters (segmental alignment, C2-C7 lordosis, segmental height, and fusion rates) were assessed preoperatively and up to 24 months postoperatively. Mixed-effects modeling was used to adjust for baseline differences.
RESULTS: Patients in the SAAC group were significantly older and had higher cardiovascular comorbidity. Despite this, SAAC was associated with shorter operative time and lower blood loss (both P < 0.05). Both groups achieved comparable and clinically meaningful improvements in pain, neurological function, and disability at 2 years. Radiological outcomes, including alignment correction, height maintenance, subsidence, and fusion rates, were similar after adjustment for baseline factors. Complication profiles, including dysphagia and implant-related events, did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In 3-level ACDF, SAAC constructs provide clinical and radiological outcomes comparable to PC systems at 2 years while offering significant perioperative advantages. SAAC performed robustly even in older, more comorbid patients, supporting its role as a safe and effective alternative for multilevel cervical degenerative disease.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Standalone anchored cages may be considered an alternative to plate-cage constructs for 3-level ACDF, offering shorter operative time and lower blood loss with similar clinical and radiological outcomes at 2 years.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3.

Title: Prognostic Value and Population Attributable Fraction of Cardio-Ankle Vascular Index for Mortality in the General Population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) is a blood pressure-independent measure of arterial stiffness. While its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD) is well established, its prognostic value for non-CVD mortality and its overall public health impact in the general population remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate CAVI as a comprehensive predictor of cause-specific mortality and to quantify its population attributable fraction (PAF).
METHODS: In this 12.7-year prospective cohort study, we examined 5994 community-dwelling adults (aged 35-69 years) from the Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Study. Baseline data (2005-2012) and mortality outcomes through December 2021 were analyzed. Participants were categorized into three groups: CAVI 1 (< 8.0), CAVI 2 (8.0-8.9), and CAVI 3 (≥ 9.0). Adjusted hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. PAF was used to quantify the impact of elevated CAVI.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 295 deaths occurred. Compared with the CAVI 1 group, the CAVI 3 group showed increased risks of all-cause (hazard ratio: 1.38, 95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.90), CVD (hazard ratio: 2.17, 95% confidence interval: 0.97-4.86), and non-CVD mortality (hazard ratio: 1.26, 95% confidence interval: 0.88-1.79). PAFs were 8.9%, 23.4%, and 6.2% for all-cause, CVD, and non-CVD mortality, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Elevated arterial stiffness (CAVI ≥ 9.0) is an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in the general Japanese population. Furthermore, a substantial proportion of CVD deaths (approximately 23.4%) could potentially be prevented by maintaining a CAVI below 9.0, highlighting the clinical utility of CAVI screening in primary prevention and nursing management.

Title: Epidemiology and outcome of sudden cardiac arrest in elderly Nigerians: a prospective multicentre observational survey.
[Analysis of inflnencing factors for muscular calf vein thrombosis after hip fracture surgery and creation of Nomogram prediction model].
Journal: Zhongguo gu shang = China journal of orthopaedics and traumatology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a nomogram for predicting muscular calf vein thrombosis (MCVT) after hip fracture surgery and to evaluate its clinical utility.
METHODS: A total of 1, 600 patients who underwent surgery for hip fracture between February 2013 and February 2023 were enrolled, including 1, 028 men and 572 women, aged from 57 to 83 with a mean age of (68.96±10.19) years. Patients were assigned to a derivation cohort (1, 120 patients) and a validation cohort (480 patients). The derivation cohort was further divided into an MCVT group (210 patients) and a non-MCVT group (910 patients). Logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors for MCVT in the derivation cohort, and a nomogram was constructed using the rms package in R version 4.0. Internal validation was performed using calibration and decision curves, and external validation was performed using receiver operating characteristic(ROC) curves and the area under the curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Sex, D-dimer level, Waterlow pressure injury score(Ws), and Caprini thrombosis risk score differed significantly between the MCVT and non-MCVT groups(all P<0.05). Male sex[OR=1.654, 95%CI(1.083, 3.551)], D-dimer level[OR=3.320, 95%CI (1.734, 5.452)], Ws[OR=2.243, 95%CI(1.345, 4.901)], and Caprini thrombosis risk score[OR=5.013, 95%CI (2.014, 8.934)] were independent risk factors for MCVT. The nomogram showed good consistency, with a C-index of 0.827[95%CI(0.680, 0.901)], and provided clinical net benefit;the internal validation results met clinical requirements. Model fit was satisfactory(χ2=6.435, P=0.146). The AUCs were 0.851 in the derivation cohort and 0.844 in the validation cohort, with no significant difference between them (P=0.238);the external validation results also met clinical requirements.
CONCLUSION: The nomogram showed clinical value for predicting MCVT and may inform the treatment and management of patients after hip fracture surgery.

Title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch.
Abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

Title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF.
RESEARCH QUESTION: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations?
STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence.
RESULTS: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD.
INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

Title: EUK-134, a superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic, inhibits inflammatory cytokines, reduces myocyte necroptosis and improves left ventricular remodeling and function in heart failure after myocardial infarction in mice.
Abstract: Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a crucial role in heart failure after myocardial infarction (MI), but the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated whether EUK-134, a synthetic superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic, reduces myocardial oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines and myocyte necroptosis and apoptosis, leading to the improvement of left ventricular (LV) remodeling and function in heart failure after MI. Eight-week old C57BL/6J mice underwent MI or sham operation. The animals were randomized to receive EUK-134 (25 mg/kg, every other day, i.p.) or placebo for four weeks.
