In the MI placebo group, LV end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions were increased, LV fractional shortening and LV ejection fraction were decreased, and these alterations were attenuated by the treatment of EUK-134. In the MI placebo group, myocardial expression of 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine, a marker of oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β and interleukin-6, and phosphorylated RIP1 (p-RIP1), p-RIP3 and p-MLKL, reflective of their respect kinase activities, markers of necroptosis, pro-apoptotic Bax protein, phosphorylated JNK (p-JNK) protein, cleaved caspase protein and myocyte apoptosis were markedly increased, and the increases were prevented by the treatment of EUK-134. Similarly, intracellular levels of ROS, necroptosis and apoptosis were increased in H9C2 cardiomyocytes under mimic ischemia and the increases were prevented by the EUK-134 treatment. These findings suggest that the superoxide dismutase and catalase mimetic EUK-134 prevents RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated myocyte necroptosis and Bax/JNK-mediated myocyte apoptosis through inhibition of myocardial oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokines, leading to the improvement of post-MI LV remodeling and failure.

Title: HFpEF-ABA Score Can Predict Long-Term Mortality Across All Heart Failure Categories in Acute Heart Failure.
Abstract: HFpEF-ABA score, based on age, body mass index, and history of atrial fibrillation, was initially developed as a diagnostic screening tool for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). This study evaluated the prognostic significance of HFpEF-ABA score for all-cause mortality across HF phenotypes in patients hospitalized for acute HF (AHF). We analyzed 3,974 admitted patients in the STRATS-AHF registry (Korea, 2009-2016), classified into HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%; n=2,094), HFmrEF (LVEF 41-49%; n=609), and HFpEF (LVEF ≥50%; n=1,271). The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Over a median follow-up of 51.4 months, 1,642 patients (41.3%) died. HFpEF-ABA score was significantly higher in nonsurvivors than survivors (61.0±23.2 vs. 54.6±25.9; P<0.001), with a univariate hazard ratio (HR) of 1.009 per point (95% CI: 1.007-1.011; P<0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a monotonically increasing, non-linear association between the score and mortality risk, and patients with a score <45 had much better 6-year survival compared to those with a score ≥45 in the overall group and in each HF phenotype (all P≤0.005). Adding HFpEF-ABA score to clinical, pharmacological, and echocardiographic variables produced a modest but significant improvement in individual risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement 0.198; integrated discrimination improvement 0.013), despite only a marginal increase in discrimination (C-index from 0.696 to 0.700, P<0.001), with an independent HR of 1.008 per point (95% CI: 1.005-1.012; P<0.001) and preserved calibration. HFpEF-ABA score independently predicted long-term all-cause mortality across HF phenotypes in AHF patients, offering modest incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical, echocardiographic, and therapeutic predictors.

Title: Concomitant Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair and Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and High Bleeding Risk.
Abstract: Evidence on concomitant mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is limited. This retrospective registry compared 216 isolated M-TEER procedures with 133 concomitant procedures at 13 centers. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or site-reported major bleeding through 24 months. Analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimates, center-clustered Cox models, and overlap weighting. Median follow-up was 21.5 months after isolated and 9.2 months after concomitant treatment. The primary endpoint occurred in 41 (19.0%) and 16 (12.0%) patients, respectively; 24-month event-free survival was 73.8% and 80.1%. The adjusted hazard ratio was 0.79 (95% confidence interval 0.50-1.25), and the expanded overlap-weighted estimate was 0.79 (0.49-1.28). Overlap-weighted estimates with follow-up truncated at 9 and 12 months were 1.02 (0.56-1.83) and 0.91 (0.50-1.63). Results were sensitive to exclusion of patients with reconstructed event dates. Oral anticoagulation at discharge was prescribed in 187/202 (92.6%) evaluable isolated-procedure patients and 20/133 (15.0%) concomitant-procedure patients; standardized longitudinal medication assessments were unavailable. In conclusion, concomitant M-TEER and LAAC was feasible and associated with less anticoagulant prescription at discharge, but nonrandom allocation, unequal follow-up, incomplete bleeding classification, and uncertain event timing prevent conclusions regarding comparative clinical benefit.

Title: The atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment: cellular plasticity, extracellular matrix remodeling, and plaque stability.
Abstract: The plaque microenvironment (PME) integrates systemic lipid exposure with local vascular, immune and stromal responses. Vascular smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, fibroblast-like cells and lymphocytes interact within a continuously remodeled extracellular matrix. Their context-dependent states influence inflammation, lipid handling, matrix organization and the balance between plaque stability and vulnerability. This narrative review examines these cellular and extracellular components, with particular attention to phenotypic modulation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and the limitations of inferring cellular origin from shared markers. Human single-cell findings expand the conventional M1/M2 view of macrophages. Therapeutic evidence is considered across experimental models, human pathology, intravascular imaging and randomized clinical outcome trials. Systemic lipid lowering and selected anti-inflammatory interventions can modify atherosclerotic disease, but changes in plaque composition do not by themselves establish reductions in myocardial infarction or stroke. Carotid and coronary findings also require site-specific interpretation. Integrating mechanistic observations with the level and anatomical setting of the evidence provides a framework for evaluating established therapies and developing selective PME-directed strategies.

Title: Semaglutide versus diet-based weight loss in obesity and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (FIT-HF): Protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Obesity is common in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but the functional, mechanistic, and safety consequences of intentional weight loss remain uncertain. Incretin-based therapies improve symptoms and functional capacity in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, whereas evidence in HFrEF is limited, and prior glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist trials have raised safety concerns. The FIT-HF trial tests whether semaglutide-based weight loss is superior to intensive diet-based weight loss for improving exercise capacity in adults with obesity and stable HFrEF.
METHODS: FIT-HF is an investigator-initiated, randomized, parallel-group, open-label, assessor-blinded, active-comparator superiority trial enrolling 100 adults with body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40%, New York Heart Association class I-III symptoms, and stable guideline-directed heart failure therapy. Participants are randomized 1:1 to once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, titrated to a target dose of 2.4 mg, or low-calorie total dietary replacement of approximately 800 kcal/day for 8 weeks followed by a dietitian-led weight-maintenance program. Both groups receive lifestyle counseling, heart failure care, and structured physical training from week 16. Follow-up is 52 weeks. The primary endpoint is the adjusted between-group difference in change in weight-indexed peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) from baseline to week 52, assessed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Supportive secondary endpoints include Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, 6-min walk distance, left ventricular end-systolic volume assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Exploratory work packages assess safety, cardiac/pulmonary physiology, body composition, physical activity, and metabolic/biomarker responses.
DISCUSSION: FIT-HF is the first direct comparison of these weight-loss strategies in obesity and HFrEF, integrating VO2peak with multimodal phenotyping to interpret physiological profiles alongside achieved weight loss and body composition.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Clinical Trials Information System: European Union trial number: CT-2023-503753-35-01; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06423599.

Title: Early hypoxemia and hypocapnia burdens and 28-day mortality in ICU patients with cardiac arrest: A retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association of cumulative oxygen and carbon dioxide deficits with mortality in patients with cardiac arrest remains uncertain. We examined hypoxemia and hypocapnia burdens during the first 24 h of ICU care.
METHODS: This retrospective MIMIC-IV study included adult ICU patients with cardiac arrest identified using hospital diagnosis codes, eligible arterial blood gas measurements, and confirmed survival to 24 h after ICU admission. Burdens were calculated as the integrated deficits below PaO2 75 mmHg or PaCO2 35 mmHg divided by 24 h. Multivariable logistic regression assessed mortality within 28 days of ICU admission. Restricted cubic splines assessed nonlinear associations.
RESULTS: The cohort included 1028 ICU patients with cardiac arrest, of whom 487 (47.4%) died within 28 days; complete-case models included 972 patients. In the joint model, the adjusted odds ratio was 1.71 (95% CI 1.20-2.45) per 10 mmHg higher hypoxemia burden and 1.88 (1.42-2.47) per 5 mmHg higher hypocapnia burden. For hypoxemia, the high-exposure group had higher adjusted odds of death than the no-exposure group (1.95, 1.33-2.85), but the low-exposure group had lower odds (0.68, 0.47-0.98). Hypocapnia showed evidence of nonlinearity (P = 0.014); its low-exposure group had lower odds than the no-exposure group, while the difference between the high-exposure and no-exposure groups was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Among ICU patients with cardiac arrest who survived the first 24 h after ICU admission, greater hypoxemia burden was associated with higher 28-day mortality in continuous analyses. In categorical analyses, the high-exposure group had higher adjusted odds of death than the no-exposure group, whereas the low-exposure group had lower adjusted odds. Hypocapnia burden showed a nonlinear association with mortality. These findings warrant prospective validation.

Title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance findings in His-bundle pacing: Insights to pacing threshold rise.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The mechanisms underlying pacing threshold elevation in His bundle pacing (HBP) despite an electrically intact lead remain poorly understood. This can compromise long-term battery life and increase the need for generator replacement or lead revision, adding procedural risk for patients and costs for healthcare systems. Using multiparametric cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), this proof-of-concept study examined whether the myocardium at the lead tip can be visualised with conventional CMR sequences, whether imaging remains safe despite elevated pacing thresholds, and whether fibrosis at the implantation site can be identified.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 16 patients with HBP systems, of whom 9 had an increased pacing threshold. A significant increase was defined as a rise of ≥1.0V/1.0 ms. All scans were performed on a 1.5T scanner using standard bSSFP cine imaging and IR TFE late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging in atrial-focused short-axis, long-axis, and modified aortic valve (AV) views to optimally visualise the HBP insertion site. LGE was assessed visually in different views.
RESULTS: All MRI images were evaluable and showed no visual artefacts. The tip of the HBP lead was best visible on short-axis and AV planes. No periprocedural safety issues occurred, in particular pacing thresholds remained unaffected, demonstrating that CMR is feasible even in patients with elevated pacing thresholds, a scenario often considered a relative contraindication. In the case-control comparison, the presence of LGE at the His lead implantation site was associated with increased pacing thresholds, although our small cohort showed no association with clinical markers. Given the limited sample size, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study shows that the HBP lead implantation site can be visualized with conventional CMR sequences, and that MRI can be performed safely even in patients with elevated pacing thresholds. Pacing threshold rises were associated with LGE at the implant site, suggesting a mechanistic link and traction-related micro-injury. These findings highlight that local tissue remodeling should be considered when selecting and optimizing His-bundle implantation techniques.

Title: Transthoracic Echocardiographic Reference Values in Male Professional Major League Soccer Players Under 21 Years of Age.
Journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To define sport-specific echocardiographic reference values in elite male soccer players <21 years of age.
BACKGROUND: Exercise-induced cardiac remodeling varies by sport and demographic factors. The use of general population reference values may lead to misclassification of physiological remodeling as pathology, particularly in young athletes. Normative echocardiographic data in elite adolescent soccer players remain limited.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional echocardiographic analysis of 430 male Major League Soccer athletes on active rosters from 2018 to 2023. Standard echocardiographic parameters were assessed and compared with American Society of Echocardiography reference values.
RESULTS: Athlete age ranged from 14 to 21 years (mean 18.8 years). The cohort was racially and ethnically diverse (28.6% Black, 33.0% Hispanic, 37.0% White). 29% of athletes had dilated left ventricular end-diastolic volume (> 74mL/m2), while right ventricular enlargement (>41 mm) was observed in 27.2%. Maximal left ventricular wall thickness ranged from 5.5 to 12.9 mm (mean 9.79 mm), with 43.0% of athletes demonstrating wall thickness >10 mm. Mean left ventricular mass index was 92.8 g/m2, with 9.7% meeting criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. Eccentric hypertrophy was present in 5.8%, concentric hypertrophy in 3.9%, and concentric remodeling in 18.8%, while 71.5% demonstrated normal geometry.
CONCLUSION: In this large, racially diverse cohort of elite male soccer players under 21 years of age, we provide comprehensive sport-specific echocardiographic reference values that address critical gaps in adolescent and young adult male soccer players.

Title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Before Minimally Invasive Repair of Pectus Excavatum and After Bar Removal.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum (MIRPE) is associated with favorable outcomes, it remains generally unknown whether cardiac compression persists after bar removal. We therefore explored cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) outcomes after bar removal.
METHODS: We evaluated a retrospective cohort of patients with diagnosis of isolated pectus excavatum (PEX) who underwent CMR before MIRPE and after bar removal. We evaluated the effect of MIRPE on CMR outcomes including the presence of cardiac compression, pericardial effusion, abnormal septal motion, inspiratory septal flattening, and left ventricular eccentricity.
RESULTS: We included 60 patients who underwent CMR before repair and after bar removal. Before surgery, the mean Haller index was 5.9±3.0. All patients had baseline cardiac compression and 24 (40%) patients referred exercise intolerance. After bar removal, none of the patients reported exercise intolerance and we identified a significant decrease in the presence of cardiac compression [from 100% to 33%, mean difference -66.7 (95%CI -78.6; -54.7)]. With regard to RV inflow and septal wall kinetics, we identified a significant increase in the tricuspid to mitral annulus ratio [0.86±0.16 vs. 0.92±0.06, mean difference 0.06 (95%CI 0.02; 0.10)], and significantly reduced rates of abnormal septal motion [60.0%, vs 33.3%, mean difference -26.7 (95%CI -43.2; -10.1)], and a change in the rates of inspiratory septal flattening from 22% to 10% (mean difference -11.9 (95%CI -22.5; -1.3). Furthermore, we found a significant reduction in left ventricular eccentricity indexes after bar removal, particularly during inspiration [before MIRPE 1.61±0.2 vs. after removal 1.45±0.1, mean difference -0.16 (95%CI -0.23; -0.09)]. Finally, we also found a significant decline in the rates of pericardial effusion [25% vs. 5%, mean difference -20.0 (95%CI -30.1; -9.9)].
CONCLUSIONS: CMR assessment before MIRPE and after bar removal demonstrated persistent anatomical decompression, with a significant decrease in the presence and severity of cardiac compression, enhanced right ventricular inflow geometry, and favorable changes of septal wall kinetics. These structural modifications reflect mechanical relief of the right ventricle following bar removal.
TYPE OF STUDY: Retrospective before and after study LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

Title: Associations between Antidiabetic Drug Classes and Aortic Aneurysm Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a potentially life threatening condition that often remains asymptomatic for prolonged periods. Although type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases cardiovascular risk, epidemiological studies have paradoxically reported a lower incidence of AA in patients with T2DM. Antidiabetic therapies may contribute to this inverse association, but class specific effects remain unclear. This study evaluated associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA.
METHODS: This was a nationwide, population based, retrospective cohort study of adults with T2DM in Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database between 2009 and 2022. Associations between antidiabetic drug classes and incident AA were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models with time varying medication exposure, adjusted for demographic characteristics, diabetes severity, comorbidities, tobacco related diagnoses, and concomitant medications. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: Among 3 295 564 adults with T2DM (mean age 60.0 years; 52.8% men) followed for 8.5 ± 4.7 years, 45.5% received at least three antidiabetic drug classes. In multivariable time varying Cox models, metformin (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.78, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.82), thiazolidinediones (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.65 - 0.77), sulfonylureas/meglitinides (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 - 0.85), and α-glucosidase inhibitors (aHR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77 - 0.89) were associated with lower AA risk. DPP-4 inhibitors (aHR 0.95, 95% CI 0.90 - 1.00), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors (aHR 0.90, 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), and glucagon like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) (aHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 - 0.95) also showed inverse associations, whereas insulin use was associated with higher AA risk (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08 - 1.20). The inverse associations of conventional oral antidiabetic agents remained robust across sensitivity analyses. In contrast, the inverse associations for DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, and GLP-1RAs were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in patients with an index date from 2011 onward.
CONCLUSION: In this nationwide T2DM cohort, conventional oral antidiabetic agents were consistently associated with a lower observed AA risk. Although newer glucose lowering therapies showed similar inverse associations, these findings were less robust and warrant cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

Title: Modifiable cardiovascular health, inflammatory biomarkers, and risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality among Cancer survivors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, but the roles of modifiable cardiovascular health (CVH) and systemic inflammation remain incompletely understood. We examined the associations of CVH with incident CVD and mortality and assessed potential mediation by inflammatory biomarkers.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 11,825 cancer survivors free of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at baseline. CVH was assessed using the Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score and the number of LE8 components meeting guideline-based thresholds. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for cardiovascular events and mortality. Mediation analyses evaluated the contributions of inflammatory biomarkers.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.5 years, 1923 MACE events and 2082 deaths occurred. Compared with the lowest CVH tertile, the highest tertile was associated with lower risks of MACE (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.54-0.68), coronary heart disease (0.56; 0.48-0.65), heart failure (0.65; 0.52-0.81), stroke (0.60; 0.45-0.80), all-cause mortality (0.72; 0.64-0.80), CVD mortality (0.48; 0.32-0.72), and cancer mortality (0.74; 0.66-0.85). Each additional LE8 component under control was associated with 7%-20% lower risks across outcomes. Among significant mediation effects, C-reactive protein and the INFLA score mediated 9.7%-48.7% and 6.8%-17.9% of the associations, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Favorable modifiable CVH is consistently associated with substantially lower risks of cardiovascular events and mortality among cancer survivors. Inflammation biomarkers partially mediated these associations, implicating inflammation as a key biological pathway.

Title: Association of preoperative quantitative flow ratio with 1-year graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A two-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) targets are selected by angiographic stenosis, whereas percutaneous coronary intervention increasingly relies on functional assessment. Whether quantitative flow ratio (QFR), a wire-free angiography-derived index, relates to graft outcomes is unclear. We examined preoperative QFR and 1-year graft patency.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 491 patients undergoing isolated CABG at two heart centers, 2006-2019. Investigators blinded to bypass design and outcome measured preoperative QFR in all analyzable major vessels. Protocol angiography assessed 1-year graft status. Generalized estimating equations accounting for within-patient clustering related QFR (per 0.1-unit increment) to graft occlusion, unadjusted and adjusted for target vessel, graft type, age, sex, diabetes, and ejection fraction. Linearity and effect modification by graft type and target territory were assessed.
RESULTS: Median QFR among 1161 analyzable vessels was 0.66 (interquartile range, 0.48-0.80); among 1036 bypassed vessels, higher QFR was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk (unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-1.42; adjusted OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.27; p = 0.008). The association was linear (standardized occlusion probability, 8.2% at QFR 0.50; 13.1% at 0.90). Effect modification by target territory was borderline (joint interaction p = 0.025; Holm-adjusted p = 0.050); this exploratory finding requires confirmation. Graft type did not modify the association (p = 0.28).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative QFR, indicating functionally less significant stenosis, was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk. This hypothesis-generating, group-level association establishes neither causation nor predictive utility for individual grafts. Prospective validation is needed.

Title: Practice Patterns and Outcomes of Women Interventional Cardiologists in Treatment of STEMI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women are known to have worse outcomes than men in acute myocardial infarction. There is increasing evidence that gender discordance between patients and physicians may be a contributing factor to poor outcomes. Whether the gender of the interventional cardiologist influences outcomes in STEMI and whether this varies based on patient gender is unknown. We sought to ascertain whether the gender of the interventional cardiologist has an association with patient outcome.
METHODS: The NCDR CathPCI registry was queried for cases coded as "Primary PCI for STEMI" between April 2018 and March 2025. These cases were stratified by both patient and cardiologist gender. Logistic regression models were performed and sequentially adjusted for patient and hospital characteristics. Outcomes of interest were door to balloon time (DTB), in-hospital mortality, documented non-system reasons for delay, and door-to-door time (DTD) among transferred- in patients.
RESULTS: Among 834,465 primary PCI procedures for STEMI, only 44,335 (5.3%) were performed by female interventionalists. Male interventionalists were more likely to meet DTB standards. Female interventionalists were more likely to document non-system reasons for delay. There was no evidence of influence of operator gender on the outcomes of patients, when stratified by patient gender.
CONCLUSIONS: Female interventionalists performed a small proportion of primary STEMI PCI procedures. Although female interventionalists had lower adjusted odds of achieving DTB < 90 minutes, interventionalist gender was not associated with adjusted in-hospital mortality. These findings were consistent across male and female patient subgroups and highlight persistent differences in selected care-process measures without a corresponding detectable difference in mortality.

Title: Circulating miRNAs associated with frailty in old people with cardiovascular diseases promote cellular senescence and inflammation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have been suggested as candidate biomarkers of frailty, a complex multidomain geriatric syndrome associated with a high risk of poor outcomes. However, few studies have adopted an unbiased approach to screen for plasma miRNAs associated with frailty independently of common risk factors and little is known relatively to their putative pathogenic role.
METHODS: Leveraging a cohort recruited for a randomized trial testing the effect a remote rehabilitation intervention on frailty in elderlies with cardiovascular diseases (CVD), we tested plasma samples from 24 people, 12 frail and 12 not frail according to the EFT scale and matched for all the other clinical characteristics, to search for miRNAs associated with frailty through small RNA-Sequencing. From this analysis, we selected 11 of the 12 most significantly deregulated miRNAs (the probe of one miRNAs did not pass quality check), i.e. those with the lowest nominal p values, and quantified them in the entire cohort (n = 197) through quantitative RT-PCR. Then, we explored the candidate pathways targeted by miRNAs significantly deregulated in frailty through bioinformatics analyses and tested the effect of miR-181b-3p and miR-490-5p overexpression on cellular senescence and inflammation in endothelial cells.
RESULTS: We found that plasma levels of miR-181b-3p, miR-490-5p, and miR-500a-5p were increased, while miR-511-5p was reduced, in people with frailty compared with non-frail individuals, also after adjustment for age or multiple testing, a result corroborated by two sensitivity analyses. In a multivariate logistic regression adjusted for multiple risk factors, miR-181b-3p, miR-490-5p, and miR-511-5p levels were associated with the prevalence of frailty. Bioinformatics analysis of the frailty-upregulated miRNAs suggested cell cycle and cellular response to DNA damage, two recognized drivers of aging, as regulated biological processes for both miR-181b-3p and miR-490-5p. Overexpression of these two miRNAs through transient transfection in endothelial cells promoted a prototypical cellular senescence response accompanied by a pro-inflammatory phenotype, as assessed through SA-Beta Gal staining and increased expression of multiple senescence and inflammatory markers at both mRNA and protein levels.
CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that circulating levels of miR-181b-3p, miR-490-5p, and miR-511-5p might serve as markers of frailty in old people with CVD and that miR-181b-3p and miR-490-5p might be functionally linked to the pathophysiology of the syndrome through their effects on cellular senescence and inflammation.

Title: The effect of subcutaneous semaglutide injection on blood pressure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract: Hypertension remains a leading contributor to cardiovascular disease globally. Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), reduces blood pressure in clinical trials, but the consistency and magnitude of this effect across populations is unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo-controlled randomized trials reporting blood pressure changes in patients receiving subcutaneous semaglutide. MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Embase were searched through December 2025. Pooled weighted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were calculated using random-effects inverse-variance models. Cochrane's RoB 2.0 assessed risk of bias, and the Grading of recommendations Assessment Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was used to evaluate the certainty of the evidence. Our meta-analysis included seven trials with approximately 20,000 patients. Semaglutide reduced systolic blood pressure (SBP) significantly compared with placebo across 11 arms (20,011 participants): weighted mean difference -3.46 mmHg (95% CI: -4.44 to -2.49; I2 = 29.5%; high certainty of evidence). A modest reduction in diastolic blood pressure (DBP) was also observed (-0.56 mmHg, 95% CI: -0.82 to -0.29; I2 = 0.0%; moderate certainty of evidence). However, sensitivity analysis revealed that the DBP effect was dependent on a single large study, with loss of significance upon its exclusion. Subcutaneous semaglutide produces meaningful SBP reduction across diverse patient populations, with minimal DBP changes. Blood pressure improvement represents one component of semaglutide's cardiometabolic benefits.

Title: [Onlay Patch Repair Using the Internal Thoracic Artery for Diffuse Left Anterior Descending Artery Disease With In-stent Restenosis].
Journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
Abstract: Among 187 patients who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between January 2016 and August 2022, 7 patients who received concomitant stent removal and coronary endarterectomy followed by internal thoracic artery (ITA) onlay patch repair were retrospectively reviewed. Six patients were male, with a mean age of 60±12 years;six had diabetes mellitus, and two were on maintenance hemodialysis. All procedures were performed under cardiopulmonary bypass with cardioplegic arrest. The mean number of distal anastomoses was 3.6±1.7, and the mean onlay patch length was 51±13 mm. There was no in-hospital mortality. During a mean follow-up of 52±21 months, one patient died of unknown cause, while no ITA graft occlusion or no new wall motion abnormalities in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory were observed. These results suggest that ITA onlay patch repair after long-segment stent removal may be an effective revascularization strategy for diffuse LAD disease with in-stent restenosis.

Title: [Outcomes of Robotic Mitral Valve Repair in Patients Aged 80 Years and Older with Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation].
Journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
Abstract: Robotic mitral valve repair (RMVr) may offer a durable and less invasive treatment option for elderly patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation in the era of expanding transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). We retrospectively reviewed 42 consecutive octogenarians who underwent RMVr for degenerative mitral regurgitation between June 2018 and May 2025. Mean age was 83.0±2.5 years, and 38.1% had preoperative atrial fibrillation. Hospital mortality was 2.4%, and symptomatic stroke occurred in 2.4%. There were no conversions to sternotomy, re-explorations for bleeding, valve reinterventions, or new renal replacement therapy. At discharge, mitral regurgitation was none or trivial in 90.5% of patients, and only one patient had moderate residual regurgitation. Estimated 5-year overall survival was 80.3%, freedom from reoperation was 100%, and freedom from recurrent moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 89.3%. RMVr was feasible and provided acceptable midterm durability in carefully selected octogenarians. RMVr should remain an important treatment option within multidisciplinary heart team decision-making.

Title: Treatment of a concealed accessory pathway by radiofrequency catheter ablation in a horse.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accessory pathways (APs) are myocardial bundles directly connecting the atria and the ventricles, bypassing the atrioventricular node-His-Purkinje system. Retrograde AP conduction in horses can result in orthodromic atrioventricular re-entry tachycardia or bradycardia. Radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) can provide a permanent treatment by eliminating the retrograde conducting AP, but was previously unsuccessful in one case.
OBJECTIVES: To report the use of three-dimensional electro-anatomical mapping (3D EAM) to identify a concealed AP and treatment by RFCA in a horse.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective case report.
CASE DESCRIPTION: An irregular heart rhythm was detected in a 4-year-old, 518 kg Paint mare as an incidental finding. Frequent atrial depolarisations were identified in the ST segment with a fixed coupling interval to the preceding QRS complex on the ECG. A differential diagnosis of frequent premature atrial complexes displayed as bigeminy or a retrograde conduction along an AP was made. The presence of a retrograde conducting AP was confirmed by ventricular pacing, which resulted in 1:1 ventriculo-atrial activation. Three-dimensional EAM revealed the earliest atrial activation and thereby the atrial insertion of the AP in the caudal left atrium. Subsequent RFCA at 40 W eliminated AP conduction.
MAIN LIMITATIONS: Single case report.
CONCLUSIONS: This case report describes the identification of an AP by 3D EAM and the first successful permanent treatment of a retrograde conducting AP by RFCA in an adult horse.

Title: Patching up the heart: Electroconductive cardiac repair.
Abstract: Cardiac patches implanted onto the heart surface are a prospective treatment for myocardial infarction. In this issue of Cell Stem Cell, Xie et al. provide evidence that patches matching myocardial electroconductivity not only reestablish cardiac conduction after injury but also induce endothelial differentiation of epicardial cells to promote heart repair.

Title: Postmortem CT interpretation of hemopericardium and associated signs.
Abstract: Hemopericardium (HP) may result from natural cardiovascular disease or traumatic mechanisms, and distinguishing these etiologies is important in forensic practice. Postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) can characterize the morphology of pericardial blood, but the discriminatory value of specific PMCT features for natural versus traumatic HP remains incompletely defined. This retrospective observational study evaluated 53 autopsy-confirmed cases of HP identified from 4903 medicolegal autopsies performed between January 2022 and December 2024. PMCT was assessed for hyperdense armored heart (HAH), fluid-fluid level (FFL), and flattened heart sign (FHS), with inter-observer agreement evaluated using Cohen's κ. Exploratory quantitative attenuation analysis and multivariable logistic regression were also performed. HAH and FHS were significantly associated with natural HP (p < 0.001 for both), whereas FFL was not significantly associated with HP type (p = 0.090). Inter-observer agreement was perfect for all three features (κ = 1.00; 95% CI, 1.00-1.00). Mean attenuation did not differ significantly between natural and traumatic HP (67.13 ± 10.62 vs 71.43 ± 8.26 HU, p = 0.148). FHS remained significantly associated with HP type in exploratory multivariable analysis (adjusted OR, 0.11; 95% CI, 0.02-0.69; p = 0.018). PMCT identified HP in 49 of 53 autopsy-confirmed cases. These findings suggest that selected PMCT morphological features may provide complementary information for differentiating natural from traumatic HP, but should not be interpreted as evidence of antemortem hemorrhage or fatal tamponade in isolation.

Title: AI-enabled Vectorcardiography (AI-VCG) combined with cardiac magnetic resonance for the mechanism of left bundle branch block in patients undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch block (LBBB) is a heterogeneous conduction disorder with major implications for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Conventional ECG criteria incompletely distinguish intact Purkinje activation (IPA-LBBB) from complete conduction block (CCB-LBBB), limiting precision pacing decisions.
OBJECTIVE: To develop an AI-based, patient-specific vectorcardiographic (AI-VCG) framework that integrates ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) to noninvasively identify LBBB mechanisms.
METHODS: A patient-specific AI-VCG model was constructed using individualized ECG-to-VCG transformations derived from cardiac-torso geometry and expressed in cardiac-centric coordinates. Performance was evaluated using in-silico electrophysiology simulations (n = 48 hearts) and a clinical CRT cohort (n = 38). A physiologically interpretable AI-VCG feature-the integral of the left-right cardiac vector (IcX)-was assessed for mechanism classification.
RESULTS: In-silico validation demonstrated strong discrimination of IPA-LBBB versus CCB-LBBB (AUROC 0.96). The clinical IcX analysis separated IPA-LBBB and CCB-LBBB with 100% accuracy in the LBBB subset (n = 25), with a 22.4 μWb gap between the highest IPA and lowest CCB IcX values. Direct comparator analyses showed 100% accuracy for Kors-derived QRS area (but with a narrower gap), 76% accuracy for Strauss criteria, and 68% accuracy for sex-specific QRS duration alone.
CONCLUSIONS: A patient-specific AI-VCG framework provides an explainable, noninvasive and anatomically grounded representation of LBBB mechanisms. These preliminary results support further validation against conventional ECG and VCG metrics in larger multicenter cohorts.

Title: Androgen Imbalance, Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages, and Mortality in Men.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Androgen measures reflect adiposity, metabolic health, and systemic illness, but their associations with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and mortality may differ across measures and combined profiles.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to examine associations of total testosterone (TT), sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), calculated free testosterone (cFT), and joint TT-SHBG phenotypes with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome and mortality.
METHODS: We analyzed men aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013 to 2016 using survey-weighted logistic (odds ratio [OR]) and Cox (hazard ratio [HR]) regression models. Advanced CKM syndrome comprised determinate National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey-adapted stages 3 to 4; cFT was calculated using the Vermeulen equation. Analyses assessed adiposity adjustment and mortality robustness.
RESULTS: Among 5,505 men, 4,005 had determinate CKM status. Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome (OR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.31-2.42), but the association was attenuated after adjustment for body mass index (OR: 1.27; 95% CI: 0.90-1.79) or waist circumference (OR: 1.22; 95% CI: 0.85-1.75), suggesting that adiposity may partly account for this association. Low TT and cFT measures showed no consistent association with all-cause mortality. In exploratory analyses, the low-TT/high-SHBG phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR: 2.06; 95% CI: 1.18-3.58).
CONCLUSIONS: Low measured TT was associated with prevalent advanced CKM syndrome, but this association was strongly adiposity-dependent. The low-TT/high-SHBG profile showed an exploratory mortality association not observed for TT or cFT alone and may represent a distinct systemic-vulnerability phenotype. These findings underscore the noninterchangeability of androgen measures and support prospective evaluation of combined TT-SHBG profiles.

Title: Vascular Phenotypes and Recurrent Arterial Events After Nontraumatic Cervical Artery Dissection.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic cervical artery dissection (CeAD) is often approached as a localized cervicocranial vascular disorder, although overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) and other arteriopathies suggests broader vascular disease.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to determine whether head-to-pelvis imaging identifies clinically meaningful vascular phenotypes after nontraumatic CeAD and whether these phenotypes are associated with recurrent arterial events.
METHODS: Consecutive adults with CeAD evaluated in an institutional vascular medicine clinic underwent head-to-pelvis computed tomography and/or magnetic resonance angiography. Patients were classified as isolated CeAD, FMD-associated CeAD (FMD-CeAD), or multiple artery aneurysm and dissection without FMD (MAAD). Outcomes were recurrent CeAD and incident extracervical artery dissection.
RESULTS: Among 315 patients, 136 (43.2%) had isolated CeAD, 100 (31.7%) had FMD-CeAD, and 79 (25.1%) had MAAD-CeAD. Overall, 179 patients (56.8%) had systemic vascular abnormalities, and 125 (39.7%) had findings below the neck. Recurrent CeAD was most frequent in isolated CeAD. Incident extracervical artery dissection occurred most frequently in MAAD-CeAD. Isolated CeAD was associated with recurrent CeAD compared with FMD-CeAD (HR: 3.26; 95% CI: 1.43 to 7.43). Among patients with FMD-CeAD or MAAD-CeAD, MAAD-CeAD was associated with incident extracervical artery dissection after adjustment for age at index CeAD (HR: 3.75; 95% CI: 1.17-12.00; P = 0.026), with similar results after additional adjustment for baseline aneurysm.
CONCLUSIONS: Head-to-pelvis imaging identified frequent extracervical vascular abnormalities in patients with CeAD and phenotypes with distinct recurrent-event patterns. These findings support a cardiovascular arteriopathy framework for CeAD and provide a rationale for prospective studies of phenotype-guided imaging, genetic evaluation, counseling, and surveillance.

Title: Femoral venous stasis index improves risk classification in patients with pulmonary hypertension: a post-hoc analysis of the CODOVEIN study.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) requires accurate risk stratification to guide management. Although current ESC/ERS three-strata model is widely used, most patients remain classified at intermediate risk, limiting clinical decision-making. The femoral venous stasis index (FVSI), a Doppler-derived marker of venous congestion, has been associated with elevated right atrial pressure. We evaluated whether FVSI improves 1-year prognostic classification beyond the ESC/ERS 2022 model.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from the CODOVEIN study, including patients with confirmed PH. The primary composite endpoint was 1-year morbidity-mortality: escalation of PH-specific therapy, hospitalization for right-heart failure, or PH-related death. Patients were classified using ESC/ERS 2022 criteria. FVSI was categorized using predefined thresholds (<0.18, 0.18-0.45, >0.45). Risk improvement was assessed using the Net Reclassification Index (NRI). Survival was analyzed with log-rank tests.
RESULTS: Ninety-one patients were included (62.2% precapillary PH). The global NRI was 0.736, with event and non-event components of 0.333 and 0.403, respectively. Among intermediate-risk patients, 1-year event rates increased across FVSI categories (16.7%, 43.5%, 66.7%; p = 0.027). Survival differed significantly across FVSI-based subgroups (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: FVSI significantly improves 1-year risk classification in PH patients, particularly within the intermediate-risk category. As a simple, non-invasive marker of venous congestion, FVSI may refine prognostication and deserve evaluation in prospective multicenter studies.

Title: Pulmonary artery pulsatility index and adverse outcomes in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary hypertension (pH) is a recognized complication of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), in which right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is associated with worse outcomes. The prognostic value of the pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi), a load-dependent surrogate of RV performance, remains unclear in COPD.
METHOD: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients with COPD who underwent right heart catheterization (RHC) between January 2018 and December 2023. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalizations. Data were stratified into PAPi tertiles, and outcomes were compared using Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and surrogates of COPD and pH severity.
RESULTS: Among 224 patients, 50% were female, 75% African American, and 81% had pH. Median (ranges) PAPi values in the high, intermediate, and low tertiles were 8.1 (4.7-90), 3 (2.3-4.7), and 1.6 (0.5-2.3), respectively. Patients with low PAPi had higher mean and diastolic pulmonary artery pressures, as well as left- and right-sided filling pressures on RHC. On echocardiography, those with low PAPi had lower left ventricular systolic function and more RV strain. Compared with high PAPi, low PAPi was associated with higher risk of the composite outcome (unadjusted model: hazard ratio [HR]=2.36 [95% CI 1.34-4.17], p-value=0.003; adjusted model: HR=2.65 [95% CI 1.42-4.92]; p-value=0.002).
CONCLUSION: Lower PAPi may identify patients with COPD at increased risk of adverse outcomes. Future studies are needed to validate our study findings in different COPD cohorts and explore optimal PAPi cutoffs.

Title: Incidence, risk factors, and clinical features of postoperative new-onset atrial fibrillation in dogs undergoing mitral valve repair surgery.
Journal: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a potential complication following cardiac surgery. This study aims to identify POAF risk factors and describe its clinical features following mitral valve repair (MVR) in dogs.
ANIMALS, MATERIALS AND METHODS: Dogs that underwent MVR between January 2020 and December 2023 were included in the study. Dogs with pre-operative atrial fibrillation or those that died intra-operatively were excluded. Potential risk factors for new-onset POAF were assessed based on selected parameters, and POAF duration was documented.
RESULTS: Postoperative atrial fibrillation occurred in 100 of 1,577 dogs. Possible independent risk factors included male sex (vs. female sex; risk ratio [RR], 1.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.22-2.78), body weight (per 1.0 kg; RR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.30), left ventricular end-diastolic internal diameter normalized to body weight (per 0.1 unit; RR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.11-1.47), and left ventricular systolic internal diameter normalized to body weight (per 0.1 unit; RR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.56-0.94). Postoperative atrial fibrillation lasted <24 h in 88 of 100 dogs and returned to sinus rhythm between 24 h and 7 days in eight dogs and between 7 days and 1 month in one dog. Postoperative atrial fibrillation persisted for >1 month in three dogs.
STUDY LIMITATIONS: The retrospective design and predominance of small-breed dogs may limit generalizability.
CONCLUSIONS: New-onset POAF occurred in 6.3% of dogs undergoing MVR at our institution. Male sex, greater body weight, and pre-operative left ventricular remodeling may be associated with onset of POAF. The majority of POAF returned to sinus rhythm within 24 h postoperatively.

Title: Elevated remnant cholesterol and risk of heart failure in the general population.
Abstract:
AIMS: Elevated remnant cholesterol is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Here, we tested the hypothesis that high levels of remnant cholesterol are observationally associated with increased risk of heart failure in individuals in the general population with and without statin therapy.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We included 108,500 and 428,922 individuals free of baseline heart failure from the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and the UK Biobank, two cohort studies of the adult Danish and UK general populations started in 2003-2015 and 2006-2010. During median 9.2 and 13.7 years of follow-up, 5321(4.9%) and 21,428(4.3%) developed heart failure in the two studies. Diagnoses of heart failure were retrieved from Danish and UK national health registers. For individuals with and without statin therapy and in both the CGPS and the UK Biobank, stepwise higher remnant cholesterol were associated with stepwise increasing risk of a diagnosis of heart failure. For individuals without statin therapy, those with remnant cholesterol ≥1.5 mmol/L(≥59 mg/dL) compared to those with remnant cholesterol <0.5 mmol/L(<19 mg/dL), the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for risk of heart failure were 1.40(95% confidence interval: 1.19-1.63) in the CGPS and 1.61(1.38-1.89) in the UK Biobank. Corresponding hazard ratios for individuals with statin therapy were 1.63(1.29-2.07) and 1.60(1.24-2.07), respectively.
CONCLUSION: In 108,500 and 428,922 individuals from the general populations of Denmark and the UK, stepwise higher levels of remnant cholesterol were associated with stepwise increasing risk of heart failure in individuals with and without statin therapy.

Title: Motion-guided semi-supervised learning with dynamic kernels for cardiac cine segmentation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accurate segmentation of full cardiac cine magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences is crucial for clinical diagnosis. Although deep learning models have become the standard for this task, they typically require exhaustive frame-by-frame supervision, making manual data annotation prohibitively time-consuming.
APPROACH: To address this, we propose a novel motion-guided semi-supervised spatiotemporal framework that propagates sparse supervision from the label of the end-diastolic (ED) frame to the entire sequence. Our framework jointly optimizes motion estimation and segmentation. First, a motion decoder estimates dense displacement fields to warp the ED label, generating high-fidelity pseudo-labels for unannotated frames. Concurrently, the segmentation network employs a Temporal Kernel Segmentation (TKS) module with dynamic convolutions to adaptively capture rapid cardiac deformations, alongside a Multi-Scale Spatial Propagator (MSP) to recover fine anatomical boundaries. The motion-derived pseudo-labels directly supervise the segmentation network, ensuring temporal coherence.
MAIN RESULTS: Extensive experiments on a multi-center cohort from three clinical centers demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the compared methods, achieving superior segmentation accuracy and robust generalization capabilities.
SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed framework effectively mitigates the burden of manual data annotation while providing temporally coherent full-cycle cardiac analysis, holding significant potential for efficient and reliable clinical assessment of cardiovascular diseases.

Title: Thoracolumbar versus lumbosacral epidural anaesthesia in dogs: a single-centre retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare both vasopressor and intraoperative rescue fentanyl administration after thoracolumbar (TL) and lumbosacral (LS) epidural (extradural) anaesthesia in dogs undergoing cranial abdominal surgery.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort, single-centre, observational study.
ANIMALS: Eighty-nine client-owned dogs undergoing cranial abdominal surgery.
METHODS: Medical records of dogs undergoing TL or LS epidural anaesthesia for cranial abdominal surgery between 2014 and 2021 were retrieved. Selected demographic variables, mean arterial blood pressure, anaesthetic and epidural drugs and their dosage, volume and injection site, vasopressor and intraoperative rescue fentanyl administration were compared between groups. Intraoperative haemodynamic stability was assessed using generalised average real variability (GenARV). Univariate analysis was used to compare groups.
RESULTS: Forty-three dogs were enrolled in the TL group and 46 in the LS group. Vasopressors were required more frequently [p = 0.030; odds ratio 2.67 (1.09-6.53)] in the LS group, but GenARV was not different (p = 0.706; 1.51 ± 0.60 and 1.46 ± 0.68 mmHg minute-1 in the LS and TL groups, respectively]. The number of dogs requiring intraoperative rescue fentanyl did not differ between groups (p = 0.992); however, the median (range) amount of fentanyl per hour of surgery was lower in the TL group [1.31 (0.75-7) and 2.87 (0.75-14) μg kg-1 hour-1 in the TL and LS groups, respectively; p = 0.019]. The volume of epidural injectate was lower in group TL (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: In dogs undergoing cranial abdominal surgery, TL epidural anaesthesia was associated with reduced vasopressor use compared to LS epidural anaesthesia, while providing comparable intraoperative analgesia with a reduced volume of injectate. Thoracolumbar epidural anaesthesia may result in a more targeted neuraxial blockade with fewer cardiovascular adverse effects, supporting its use for cranial abdominal surgeries.

Title: Association between mechanical ventilation with positive end-expiratory pressure and outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
Journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
AIM: The effect of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) during intermittent positive pressure ventilation in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on outcome is unknown. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between the use of PEEP during cardiopulmonary resuscitation and clinical outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre observational cohort study using a retrospective analysis of data collected prospectively within a dedicated research registry of adult OHCA patients managed by a physician-staffed prehospital emergency medical team. All included patients were intubated and ventilated either with mechanical ventilation using PEEP or with manual ventilation without PEEP. Intratracheal pressure was continuously recorded via a catheter connected to a portable device, allowing objective verification of PEEP application and ventilation rate. The association between mechanical ventilation with PEEP use and clinical outcomes was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for relevant confounders.
RESULTS: 362 patients were included, with a median age of 65 years (54-79), of whom 250 (69.1%) were male. Median ventilation rate was 15 breaths/min (10-19). Of all patients, 149 (41.2%) achieved Return Of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC) and 31 (8.6%) survived to hospital discharge. The adjusted odds ratio (OR) of mechanical ventilation with PEEP for achieving ROSC was 1.58 (95% CI 1.01-2.50, p = 0.048). The unadjusted OR of mechanical ventilation with PEEP for survival to hospital discharge was 2.22 (95% CI 1.03-4.78; p = 0.037).
CONCLUSION: The use of mechanical ventilation with PEEP during CPR in OHCA patients was associated with higher likelihood of ROSC.

Title: Effects of Weight-Loss Diets on Circulating MicroRNA Profiles in Overweight and Obese Adults: Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Obesity, particularly visceral adiposity, is associated with metabolic inflammation and increased cardiometabolic risk. Dietary interventions are essential for weight loss and improved metabolic health; however, individual responses vary widely. Circulating microRNAs are key epigenetic mediators of metabolic adaptation, although their variable expression patterns often preclude a unified biological interpretation.
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aims to synthesize evidence on how weight-loss diets affect the circulating microRNA profile in adults with overweight or obesity.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed Central, LILACS, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched without language or publication date restrictions through May 2026.
DATA EXTRACTION: Of 4383 records identified, 12 articles representing 9 independent randomized clinical trials met the eligibility criteria. Data on study characteristics, dietary interventions, and circulating microRNA expression profiles were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool.
DATA ANALYSIS: The included studies were conducted in 6 countries and evaluated dietary interventions lasting 2-18 months. A total of 32 distinct circulating microRNAs were differentially expressed, with miR-221-3p, miR-223, miR-99b, miR-122, and miR-128 reported in more than one study. Considerable heterogeneity was observed among the dietary protocols, particularly regarding macronutrient composition. Alterations in microRNA expression were associated with weight loss, adiposity, glycemic parameters, lipid profile, inflammation, and cardiovascular risk. Bioinformatic analyses indicated enrichment of pathways related to inflammation, insulin signaling, and lipid metabolism, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK pathways, suggesting an integrated role for these microRNAs in metabolic regulation.
CONCLUSION: Weight-loss diets modulate the circulating miRNA profile, potentially influencing glycolipid metabolism and inflammation, supporting their role as candidate biomarkers.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD42024580048.

Title: Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis.
Journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
Abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m2; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.

Title: Generation of 12-Lead Electrocardiogram Using Smartwatches in Patients With Cardiac Conditions: Clinical Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smartwatches have significantly expanded personal health monitoring capabilities; however, their application in comprehensive cardiac assessment remains limited by single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) acquisition. The inability to directly obtain augmented limb leads represents a major limitation for the evaluation of ischemic and arrhythmogenic conditions.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to present and preliminarily evaluate a methodology for generating augmented limb leads (augmented voltage right [aVR], augmented voltage left [aVL], and augmented voltage foot [aVF]) from sequential smartwatch recordings through signal synchronization and RR interval alignment, and to combine this approach with precordial smartwatch recordings to reconstruct a full 12-lead ECG in a proof-of-concept setting.
METHODS: A signal-processing framework was developed to preserve ECG morphology across sequential smartwatch lead recordings. The method is based on RR interval-guided temporal resampling, enabling interlead synchronization and analytical reconstruction of augmented limb leads. A prospective proof-of-concept clinical validation was conducted in 20 cases with diverse cardiac pathologies, including 1 healthy control. Smartwatch-derived ECGs were compared with standard 12-lead ECGs. Evaluation included expert-based clinical interpretation by 85 health care professionals and objective quantitative analysis of key electrocardiographic parameters, including heart rate, PR interval, QRS duration, QT interval, QTc, RR interval, P-wave duration, and PP interval. Mean values, SDs, and intermethod differences were calculated to assess agreement and variability.
RESULTS: Reconstruction of a 12-lead ECG from smartwatch-acquired signals was successfully achieved in all cases. Visual correlation scores between smartwatch-derived and conventional ECGs ranged from 78.1% to 91.3% across specialty-level means (mean 81.1, SD 22.7), indicating high perceived concordance; individual case-level scores ranged more widely, from 47.0% to 96.3%. Evaluator-perceived axis agreement reached 95.4% across all cases, while the investigators' direct axis measurements showed complete concordance in all cases. Quantitative analysis demonstrated small mean differences between modalities, with particularly high agreement observed in structurally stable parameters such as heart rate (mean 77.2, SD 22.3 vs mean 75.9, SD 23.1 bpm; Δ=1.3 bpm) and PR interval (mean 176.2, SD 29.1 vs mean 180.8, SD 19.8 ms; Δ=-4.6 ms). Greater variability was observed in atrial activation parameters such as P-wave duration (Δ=-13.3 ms) and time-dependent parameters such as QT (Δ=-19.2 ms) and QTc (Δ=-12.7 ms).
CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of reconstructing a full 12-lead ECG from smartwatch-derived signals using a synchronization-based approach. The results demonstrated generally small mean differences between conventional and smartwatch-derived ECG measurements, although larger interval differences were observed in some individual cases. Importantly, due to the sequential nature of signal acquisition, the proposed methodology does not aim to achieve direct waveform equivalence but rather clinically meaningful agreement in electrocardiographic parameters. These findings support the potential of smartwatches as accessible tools for advanced cardiac monitoring and broaden their applicability beyond single-lead screening.

Title: A Retrospective Study on the Evolution of Complex Chronic Conditions Over a Decade in a Large Swiss Tertiary PICU.
Journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine, over a 10-year period, changes in the prevalence of complex chronic conditions (CCCs) and in the distribution of underlying chronic health categories within a large Swiss PICU, and to compare patient characteristics and PICU mortality between children with CCCs and those without.
DESIGN: Single-center retrospective observational study of two cohorts (2007 vs. 2017).
SETTING: Large academic tertiary referral PICU.
PATIENTS: Overall, 1867 children were included (0-16 years old): 981 admitted between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2007, and 886 admitted between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2017.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The prevalence of children with CCCs increased from 61% in 2007 to 70% in 2017. The most common conditions were cardiovascular (55% in 2007 vs. 52% in 2017), congenital/genetic defects (36% vs. 38%), and neurologic/neuromuscular (25% vs. 34%). The proportion of children with 3 or more chronic conditions rose from 16% to 25%. Children with CCCs had longer PICU stays than children without, with length of stay increasing significantly with the number of CCCs. Most children who died during the two study periods had a chronic condition (2007: 61%; 2017: 66%), with a significant increase in the proportion of deaths following intensive care treatment withdrawal (8% in 2007 vs. 48% in 2017).
CONCLUSIONS: Over a decade, the proportion of children with CCCs needing PICU care has grown, with trends toward increasing prevalence in the clinically dominant categories of respiratory and hematology, immunodeficiency, and immunology, and the subcategories respiratory malformations, hereditary hemostasis anomalies, and home ventilation, and trends toward higher mortality rates following treatment withdrawal.

Title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Pediatric Lung Transplantation: An Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry Study, 2000-2022.
Journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to identify factors associated with greater odds of survival, as well as odds of successful lung transplantation (LTx) in pediatric patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) as a bridge-to-LTx (BTT) or supported with ECMO after LTx.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry.
SETTING: International ECMO centers submitting data to the ELSO registry.
PATIENTS: Pediatric patients younger than 19 years old who were supported with ECMO before or after LTx between 2000 and 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We identified 194 pediatric patients who used ECMO as a bridge to LTx, and 63% survived to hospital discharge. We failed to identify an association between ECMO modality (i.e., venovenous vs. venoarterial) and odds of survival. Central venoarterial ECMO cannulation was associated with greater odds of receiving a LTx compared with not receiving a LTx (30/85 [35%] vs. 15/109 [14%]; odds ratio [OR], 3.42; 95% CI, 1.69-6.91). In the 109 patients who did not receive a LTx, ECMO cannulation delayed after hospital day 7 was associated with lower odds of survival (OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.15-0.75). ECMO post-LTx occurred in 95 patients, 62% received venoarterial or veno-venoarterial ECMO, and 48 of 95 (51%) survived to hospital discharge. In patients requiring ECMO post-LTx, cystic fibrosis was associated with lower odds of survival (OR, 0.31; 95% CI, 0.12-0.79) and pulmonary hypertension was associated with greater odds of survival (OR, 5.04; 95% CI, 1.68-15.1).
CONCLUSIONS: Our data show that ECMO was used to support children as a BTT and for stabilization of postoperative LTx recipients. Early initiation of ECMO was associated with greater odds of survival in patients undergoing BTT who did not receive LTx. Further studies, including additional patients and focused LTx-related data, are needed to better characterize and delineate treatment options in this population.

Title: Sex-related disparities in perception of health status, access to healthcare, and health literacy among patients with heart failure in the NIH all of us research program.
Abstract: BackgroundDespite ongoing advancements in heart failure care, sex-related disparities continue to be a major challenge in healthcare.ObjectivesWe aimed to describe sex-related differences in self-reported perceived health status, healthcare access, and health-literacy-related items among All of Us participants with an EHR-recorded diagnosis of heart failure.DesignCross-sectional secondary analysis of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) All of Us Research Program.MethodsThis cross-sectional secondary analysis used linked EHR and survey data from the NIH All of Us Research Program. Survey responses were used to describe sociodemographic characteristics, self-perceived health status, health-literacy-related items, and healthcare access among participants with an EHR-recorded diagnosis of heart failure. Participants were grouped according to self-reported sex assigned at birth. Analyses were descriptive and unadjusted; item-specific denominators were used because survey completion varied across modules and questions.ResultsThe cohort included 28,465 participants, comprising 14,496 females and 13,969 males. Female participants more frequently reported lower educational attainment, unemployment, lower annual income, and non-homeownership. The distributions of general, physical, and mental health, quality of life, functional limitations, fatigue, emotional problems, social satisfaction, and pain differed between female and male respondents. Female respondents also more frequently reported several financial and transportation-related barriers to care, including delayed care because of transportation or costs and inability to afford medications or clinical care. Responses to the three health-literacy-related items also differed by sex, with female respondents more frequently reporting no need for assistance with health materials, greater confidence completing medical forms, and no difficulty understanding health information. These findings represent unadjusted descriptive differences and should not be interpreted as independent effects of sex.ConclusionAmong All of Us participants with an EHR-recorded diagnosis of heart failure, female and male respondents differed across several self-reported measures of socioeconomic circumstances, perceived health and quality of life, healthcare access, and health-literacy-related items.

Title: Global Trends in Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy for Patients With Heart Failure: A Bibliometric and Thematic Analysis of Articles Indexed in Scopus (2013-2025).
Journal: Journal of primary care & community health
Abstract: Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) is still a major cause of mortality and morbidity all over the world. This study uses bibliometric analysis to trace global publication trends and evaluate the scientific production, citation impact, contributions of authors, institutions and countries, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy (GDMT) research in patients with HFrEF. We analyzed the data using Bibliometrix (R package) and VOSviewer v.16.21 to map collaboration networks, citation patterns, and emerging research themes. The analysis indicated a significant increase in academic interest after 2021, with the principal areas of focus being heart failure (HF), HFrEF, chronic kidney disease, Sacubitril/Valsartan, diabetes, and ivabradine; this trend shows that the emphasis is on existing treatments for HF and its major comorbidities. Researchers identified 693 peer-reviewed academic sources authored by 20,686 people. McMurray JJV of the Glasgow had the highest h-index, the most citations, and the most publications. Most top authors in GDMT and HFrEF were affiliated with institutions in the United States and Europe. The United States had the greatest research productivity. Although the United States produced the most research, the European countries showed comparatively higher levels of international collaboration. The European Journal of Heart Failure was the most influential journal, having the highest h-index (59) and highest total citation score (11,795). The results show that research into GDMT-HFrEF is highly concentrated in the major cardiovascular and heart failure journals. The thematic analysis of Authors keywords shows that in 2021 heart failure and HFrEF were still the main topics. Between 2023 and 2024, Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists became important themes, showing a move towards modern GDMT. By 2025 the subjects of the research had become more diverse and now included HFrEF, SGLT2 inhibitors, Dapagliflozin, pharmacotherapy and other heart failure phenotypes. The results show that research into GDMT-HFrEF is increasingly multidisciplinary and involves greater international cooperation, especially between the United States and Europe. Future studies are expected to concentrate on SGLT2 inhibitors such as dapagliflozin; combination therapies; drug optimization; personalized care; better implementation strategies; and team-based care models.

Title: NT-proBNP levels and arrhythmias in adolescents with chronic upper gastrointestinal diseases.
Journal: Revista paulista de pediatria : orgao oficial da Sociedade de Pediatria de Sao Paulo
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess plasma N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels in adolescents with chronic upper gastrointestinal diseases and investigate their association with 24-hour Holter electrocardiographic findings.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 104 adolescents with endoscopically-verified chronic upper gastrointestinal diseases and 58 comparison adolescents without clinically-documented chronic gastrointestinal or cardiovascular disease. Both groups underwent 24-hour Holter electrocardiographic monitoring. NT-proBNP was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 60 patients and 28 controls. Receiver operating characteristic analysis explored the ability of this biomarker to identify positive Holter findings, defined as rhythm, conduction, or repolarization abnormalities exceeding age-related physiological limits or requiring further cardiological evaluation.
RESULTS: Positive Holter findings were observed in 71 patients (68.3%). Most findings were benign; potentially clinically significant abnormalities occurred in 11 patients (10.6% of all patients; 15.5% of those with positive Holter findings). Median NT-proBNP levels did not significantly differ between patients and controls but were higher in patients with cardiovascular complaints (53.0 42.5-85.0 versus 22.6 12.4-41.4 pg/mL; p=0.001) and positive Holter findings (50.0 32.2-70.5 versus 27.8 10.7-41.4 pg/mL; p<0.05). According to the receiver operating characteristic analysis for identifying positive Holter findings, we observed an area under the curve of 0.779 (95% confidence interval 95%CI: 0.726-0.833; p<0.001). An NT-proBNP cutoff value of ≥43.2 pg/mL showed 66.7% sensitivity and 90.9% specificity for identifying positive Holter findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher NT-proBNP levels were associated with positive Holter findings. Given the cross-sectional design and limited monitoring period, this association requires prospective validation.

Title: Analysis of hospitalizations and deaths due to stroke in different regions of Brazil before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Abstract: Stroke, the second leading cause of death globally and a significant source of disability, has been impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, which may increase the risks of cerebrovascular events. This observational and ecological time-series study sought to analyze hospitalizations and deaths due to stroke, covering the period from 2008 to 2022, using data from the Hospital Information System of the unified health system. The data were filtered by the code, which includes cerebrovascular accidents not specified as hemorrhagic or ischemic. The research resulted in a significant increase in hospitalization rates (R2=0.9437, p≤0.0001) and mortality (R2=0.8894, p≤0.0001) over the years. A drop was noted during the peak of the pandemic, followed by a rebound in the indices. The results indicate the urgency of reviewing and adapting public health strategies to prevent and treat stroke in post-pandemic Brazil, highlighting the increase in hospitalizations and deaths.

Title: Completeness of care provision and inequalities in care for people with hypertension, diabetes, and obesity: an analysis of the Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census.
Abstract: This study aimed to identify patterns and inequalities in the completeness of care provision for people with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity in Brazilian primary health care (PHC), drawing on the 2024 Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census (BHU Census). This was a cross-sectional online survey covering 44,938 BHUs registered in the Brazilian National Registry of Health Establishments and validated by municipal health managers. Variables related to geographic region, municipal characteristics, and health service characteristics were analyzed. Care provision was considered complete when the response was positive for all 14 actions related to hypertension, 15 for diabetes, and 10 for obesity. A low proportion of BHUs demonstrated complete provision of care for people with hypertension (15.3%), diabetes (15.6%), and obesity (13.4%), across all regions and municipality profiles. Completeness was higher in the Southeast and Northeast and lower in the South. Large municipalities, municipalities with high or very high social vulnerability, and municipalities with 100% family health coverage also showed higher completeness levels. After adjusting for contextual and BHU characteristics, the family health was associated with 70% higher completeness of care provision. Although access to consultations is well established, weaknesses persist in comprehensiveness and care coordination for chronic diseases, highlighting the need for structural policies that strengthen the capacity of PHC to effectively address health needs.

Title: Natriuretic Peptides as Adjunctive Biomarkers for the Detection of Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation in Patients With Cryptogenic Stroke: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) is a common cause of cryptogenic stroke (CS). It is often asymptomatic, and prolonged electrocardiographic monitoring is not widely available. Natriuretic peptides (NPs) have emerged as potentially adjunctive biomarkers to support risk stratification.
