Title: DCB vs. DES in aorto-ostial lesions- clinical outcomes and QCA insights from SPARTAN registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aorto-ostial de novo coronary lesions (AOL) represent a technically challenging subset of coronary artery disease with historically high restenosis rates, even with contemporary drug-eluting stent (DES) platforms. Drug-coated balloons (DCB) offer a stent-less alternative strategy; however, data on their use in AOL are limited. We aimed to compare long-term clinical outcomes of DCB vs. DES in de novo AOL.
METHODS: We identified all patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with either DCB or DES for de novo AOL as their first procedure between January 2015 and November 2019. The primary endpoint was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of target lesion revascularisation (TLR), target lesion myocardial infarction (TLMI), and cardiovascular death. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of TLF, target vessel revascularisation and all-cause mortality. Exploratory quantitative coronary angiography (QCA) analysis was performed on any follow up angiograms obtained that were technically feasible. Clinical outcomes were obtained using national outcome datasets.
RESULTS: A total of 197 patients with aorto-ostial lesions were included (DES n = 140; DCB n = 57). Over a median follow-up of 3.7 years, TLF occurred in 17.1% of DES-treated lesions and 14.0% of DCB-treated lesions (HR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.35-1.76; p = 0.563). Rates of TLR, TVR, TLMI, cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Severe calcification and creatinine independently predicted TLF. Follow-up QCA was available in 59 lesions over varying time intervals and demonstrated lower late lumen loss (LLL) following DCB treatment, compared with DES-treated lesions.
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort with aorto-ostial coronary lesions, a DCB-only strategy was feasible and associated with similar long-term outcomes to DES. Exploratory angiographic analyses demonstrated significant late lumen gain following DCB treatment. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further prospective evaluation of a DCB approach in aorto-ostial coronary disease.

Title: Outpatient Initiation of Sotalol: Reappraising Risk, Monitoring, and Modern Care Pathways.
Abstract: Sotalol remains an important antiarrhythmic drug for rhythm control in atrial fibrillation and other supraventricular arrhythmias. However, sotalol is traditionally initiated in the inpatient setting because of concerns regarding QT prolongation and torsades de pointes. This practice is based on early observational data collected before the availability of contemporary risk stratification, standardized protocols, and modern rhythm monitoring technologies. Over the past two decades, evidence from observational studies using device-based monitoring, protocolized outpatient clinics, and remote electrocardiographic technologies has demonstrated low rates of malignant ventricular arrhythmias in carefully selected patients. These data also highlight the importance of longitudinal surveillance, as clinically relevant QT prolongation may occur beyond the conventional inpatient monitoring window. Thus, this review examines the pharmacologic basis of sotalol-related proarrhythmia, critically reassesses the rationale for inpatient initiation, synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting outpatient strategies in carefully selected patients with protocolized monitoring, and proposes a practical, risk-stratified framework for outpatient sotalol initiation while identifying key knowledge gaps that still require prospective validation.

Title: Current European landscape of in-hospital cardiac arrest registries mapped by a cross-sectional survey including barriers and enablers setting up a registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) has a high mortality rate. To measure and improve resuscitation outcomes, data collection through registries plays a key role. This study aims to evaluate the current landscape of IHCA registries across national resuscitation councils affiliated with the European Resuscitation Council.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was distributed among national resuscitation councils collecting data on the presence and type of IHCA registries, registry coverage and data variables collected. Findings informed an expert discussion on barriers and enablers establishing such registries and potential next steps.
RESULTS: 30/34 (88%) national resuscitation councils replied to the survey. Seven have no IHCA registry (23%), 11 a local registry (37%), two a local and regional registry (7%), five a national registry (17%), and two countries participate in a national registry in another country (7%). Of the included registries 17 (94%) are collecting cardiac arrests in adults, 13 (72%) in children, and four (22%) in neonates. Most registries are collecting location of cardiac arrest (95%), the initial rhythm (95%), and if return of spontaneous circulation is achieved (100%), while long term neurological outcome is only collected by four registries (21%). Overall, the AI-assisted descriptive content analysis demonstrated broad consensus regarding the value of registries, while highlighting substantial logistical, legal, and financial barriers.
CONCLUSION: Our survey demonstrates considerable variation in the existence, population coverage, and data collection practices of IHCA registries. While core cardiac arrest variables are collected by most registries, data on long-term outcomes remain limited.

Title: Cardioplegia Strategies in Aortic Stenosis: A Focused Review of Current Evidence for Surgical Considerations.
Abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) exposes the hypertrophied myocardium to cardioplegic arrest in the setting of increased left ventricle (LV) mass, interstitial fibrosis, impaired relaxation, coronary microvascular dysfunction, and reduced perfusion reserve. These abnormalities may increase susceptibility to ischemic injury and complicate homogeneous cardioplegic delivery. This focused narrative review synthesizes physiological and clinical evidence on cardioplegia composition, temperature, delivery route, dosing, redosing, and myocardial protection during prolonged aortic cross-clamping in adults undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement. AS-specific comparative studies remain limited, generally small, and frequently reliant on biochemical markers; meanwhile, larger observational cohorts and contemporary randomized aortic valve replacement (AVR) trials also vary substantially in patient selection and myocardial protection protocols. Although some studies have associated cold blood cardioplegia with lower biomarker release than cold crystalloid cardioplegia, and cold maintenance strategies with less biochemical injury than warm cardioplegia, no formulation, temperature, or delivery route has demonstrated consistent superiority in clinically important outcomes. Limited historical evidence also suggests that body weight-based dosing may inadequately reflect myocardial requirements in marked LV hypertrophy, but no validated LV mass-based regimen currently exists. Therefore, cardioplegia in severe AS should be considered within a comprehensive myocardial protection protocol incorporating composition, temperature, dose, delivery route, redosing strategy, myocardial phenotype, associated valve or coronary disease, and anticipated cross-clamp duration. Prospective AS-specific studies using standardized protocols, LV mass stratification, and clinically meaningful outcomes are required.

Title: Integrated management of acute pulmonary embolism and the post-pulmonary embolism syndrome: risk stratification, modern therapies, and long-term follow-up.
Abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is increasingly recognized as an episode of care that extends well beyond hospital discharge. Current guidance is distributed across several documents: the 2019 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines; the 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology (AHA/ACC) multisociety guideline, which replaced the massive/submassive terminology with clinical categories A-E; and separate position papers on catheter-directed intervention (CDI) and on follow-up. This narrative review (i) provides a side-by-side comparison of the ESC and AHA/ACC risk frameworks and their therapeutic implications; (ii) updates the evidence on reperfusion, including the recent randomized trials HI-PEITHO, PEERLESS and STORM-PE; and (iii) focuses on transitions of care and long-term follow-up, which guidelines address less comprehensively. Anticoagulation, preferably with a direct oral anticoagulant, remains the treatment for most patients. Systemic thrombolysis is reserved for high-risk (ESC) or category E (AHA/ACC) PE, because in intermediate-risk disease it halves hemodynamic decompensation at the cost of a several-fold increase in major and intracranial bleeding, without long-term functional benefit. In HI-PEITHO, ultrasound-facilitated catheter-directed thrombolysis reduced a 7-day composite outcome driven by cardiorespiratory decompensation (4.0% vs. 10.3%) in intermediate-high-risk patients with additional markers of physiological stress, without intracranial hemorrhage; a survival benefit of CDI has not been demonstrated. At discharge, a minimum bundle should specify the drug, dose, anticipated duration, provoking context, bleeding mitigation and follow-up ownership, followed by early contact within one week and a structured review at approximately three months. Up to half of survivors report persistent dyspnea or exercise limitation, whereas chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) develops in approximately 2%-3%. Persistent symptoms should prompt phenotype-directed evaluation with echocardiography, ventilation/perfusion scintigraphy, cardiopulmonary exercise testing and, when indicated, right-heart catheterization interpreted with the 2022 hemodynamic definitions, followed by early referral to an expert center where pulmonary endarterectomy, balloon pulmonary angioplasty and medical therapy can be combined. We state the type of evidence underpinning each key recommendation, propose a discharge bundle, a structured follow-up algorithm and episode-wide quality indicators, and identify the evidence gaps that should guide future trials.

Title: Performance, Recalibration, and Implementation of In-Hospital Mortality Prediction Models for Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Acute myocardial infarction remains a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality worldwide. Although reperfusion therapy has improved short-term outcomes, in-hospital mortality remains high, particularly among patients with complex conditions. Therefore, accurate mortality prediction models are essential for optimizing clinical decision-making and individualized management. This review summarizes the evolution of these models over the past two decades, from traditional statistical methods to machine learning. Indeed, machine-learning models may achieve slightly higher discrimination than traditional statistical models in selected datasets, particularly when high-dimensional and nonlinear clinical information is available. However, the magnitude of improvement is often incremental rather than transformative, and higher area under the curve (AUC) values do not necessarily indicate better calibration, interpretability, transportability, or clinical utility. Multicenter external validation studies indicate that performance is influenced by population heterogeneity, evolving treatment strategies, and data quality, with notable variation across subgroups, including Asian patients, women, and patients with diabetes. Recalibration is key to improving transportability and can be achieved through intercept adjustment, slope calibration, or model reconstruction; dynamic updating may help maintain long-term performance. Inadequate data standardization, concerns regarding black-box models, workflow misalignment, and limited policy support can all constrain clinical implementation. Therefore, this study proposes a technology-clinical-management pathway: promoting standardized data and federated learning, building lightweight interpretable embedded decision support, establishing model registration/certification and reimbursement linkages, and strengthening multidisciplinary training. Future work should prioritize multimodal data fusion, real-time prediction, improved interpretability, multicenter prospective validation, and cost-effectiveness assessment to support safe implementation across diverse healthcare systems. Notably, China represents an important regional context for evaluating these strategies.

Title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived hemodynamics predict adverse outcomes after Fontan palliation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term outcomes following the Fontan procedure remain heterogeneous, and robust imaging-based predictors of adverse events are limited. Patients residing at moderate-altitude may experience additional pulmonary vascular stress; however, the prognostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived flow parameters in this population are not well defined.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of Fontan patients followed at a single moderate-altitude center who were ≥5 years post-Fontan and had undergone comprehensive CMR exams. Demographic, anatomic, and surgical data were collected. CMR-derived variables included indexed ventricular volumes and function, systemic arterial dimensions, and flow indices in the ascending and descending aorta, superior vena cava (SVC), inferior vena cava, and branch pulmonary arteries.The primary composite outcome was death or referral/listing for heart transplantation. Time-to-event analyses from the time of CMR were performed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: A total of 182 Fontan patients were included (median age at Fontan 3.2 years [interquartile range (IQR) 2.6-3.9]; median time from Fontan to CMR 10.9 years [IQR 7.7-14.2]). Over a median follow-up of 4.7 years following CMR (IQR 3.1-6.6), 14 patients (7.7%) experienced the primary outcome. In univariable Cox regression, a higher SVC flow index was significantly associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome [hazard ratio [HR] 0.70 per 0.1 L/min/m2 increase; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.50-0.92; p = 0.008].
CONCLUSIONS: In this moderate-altitude Fontan cohort, reduced CMR-derived SVC flow index was significantly associated with the primary outcome. This finding suggests that systemic venous flow merits further investigation as a prognostic marker in the Fontan population.

Title: The Aortic Watershed Phenomenon and Differential Hypoxemia During Peripheral Venoarterial ECMO: A Scoping Review of Clinical and Experimental Evidence.
Abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a widely used technology in cardiac surgery practice. A clinically significant yet underexplored presentation that occurs during peripheral femoro-femoral venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) is differential hypoxemia (DH) or Harlequin syndrome. This phenomenon may occur when the aortic mixing interface shifts distally, and the coronary and supra-aortic circulations receive predominantly hypoxemic native blood. DH may reduce cerebral and myocardial oxygen delivery and produce clinically meaningful arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO2) gradients. This scoping review aimed to synthesize clinical and experimental evidence on the mechanisms, detection, management, and outcomes of DH during peripheral VA-ECMO. A scoping review of the watershed phenomenon during peripheral VA-ECMO was conducted using MEDLINE and EMBASE in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. The initial search identified 245 records. After screening, 16 studies were included. DH frequency ranged from 1.5% to 13.3%, but estimates varied substantially across case definitions, diagnostic thresholds, and cohort compositions. Regarding management, configuration-targeted strategies improved surrogates of upper-body oxygenation and perfusion, which included shifting venous drainage toward the superior vena cava/upper right atrium, in turn converting to veno-arteriovenous ECMO with internal jugular return (with flow-splitting control) and relocating arterial return to more proximal/antegrade sites. Detection extended beyond paired upper- and lower-body oximetry/arterial blood gases; reported approaches included contrast-enhanced ultrasound, Doppler mapping, and positional computed tomography angiography (CTA). Experimental models described why DH may persist despite higher ECMO flow as native output increases, and they highlight anatomy- and cannulation-dependent cerebral and coronary vulnerability. DH appears to be a predictable, physiology-driven complication best mitigated by modifying drainage position and/or circuit configuration rather than increasing ECMO flow. To further explore this phenomenon, adopting standardized definitions, investigating bedside localization tools, and conducting prospective comparative studies could be considered.

Title: Clinical Correlates and Prognostic Value of Low QRS Voltages in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on the prognostic significance of low QRS voltage (LQRSV) in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to determine whether LQRSV is associated with a composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or heart failure (HF) re-hospitalization in patients with NIDCM.
METHODS: Patients with NIDCM who met predefined criteria were retrospectively enrolled and divided into LQRSV and non-LQRSV groups based on electrocardiographic findings. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality or HF re-hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiovascular (CV) death, and HF re-hospitalization. The prognostic significance of LQRSV was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) functions were applied to examine potential nonlinear relationships between continuous QRS voltage and the primary outcome. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to assess predictive performance. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline characteristics, and sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted to test the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: The overall cohort included 784 consecutive patients with NIDCM (median age 56 years; 30% female). During a median follow-up of 1079 days, 335 primary outcome events occurred. After PSM, 463 patients were matched, with 186 in the LQRSV group and 277 in the non-LQRSV group. In the matched cohort, Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test showed that the LQRSV group had a significantly worse long-term prognosis than the non-LQRSV group (p < 0.001). Multivariable Cox analyses demonstrated that LQRSV was significantly associated with the composite of all-cause mortality or HF re-hospitalization (hazard ratio, (HR) 2.048, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.519-2.760; p < 0.001), all-cause mortality (HR 2.526, 95% CI 1.660-3.844; p < 0.001), and CV death (HR 2.820, 95% CI 1.776-4.476; p < 0.001). RCS analyses showed a linear association (p for nonlinearity > 0.05), with the highest risk observed at the lowest QRS voltage amplitudes. ROC analysis revealed that incorporating LQRSV into the clinical model significantly increased the area under the curve (0.808 vs. 0.723; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: LQRSV is associated with poor prognosis in NIDCM. Routine electrocardiographic assessment of QRS voltage may provide valuable information for risk stratification.

Title: Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) is the most common acute coronary syndrome presentation and represents a heterogeneous clinical entity with distinct mechanisms and distinct diagnostic and therapeutic implications. This narrative review summarizes contemporary concepts in NSTEMI pathophysiology, classification, angiographic phenotypes, and treatment strategies, with an emphasis on differentiating Type 1 from Type 2 myocardial infarction (MI) and the implications for revascularization decisions. The PubMed/MEDLINE database was searched for English-language publications addressing NSTEMI pathophysiology, classification, diagnosis, and management, supplemented by the most recent American and European acute coronary syndrome guidelines, the Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, landmark randomized controlled trials, and pivotal mechanistic and intravascular imaging studies, with priority given to contemporary and high-impact sources. NSTEMI emerges as a heterogeneous syndrome rather than a single disease, and optimal care depends on identifying the underlying mechanism. This requires distinguishing myocardial infarction from myocardial injury, separating Type 1 atherothrombosis from Type 2 supply-demand mismatch, and recognizing entities such as myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries and spontaneous coronary artery dissection. A mechanism-specific approach should guide antithrombotic therapy and revascularization decisions, and the transition from a syndromic label to an individualized, mechanism-based diagnosis is essential for optimizing patient outcomes.

Title: Risk of Short-Term Stroke in Non-High-Risk Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement vs Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the incidence of stroke at 1 and 2 years following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) versus surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), aiming to inform clinical decision-making regarding the safety and effectiveness of these interventions.
METHODS: A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted including 9 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with a total of 9865 patients. The primary endpoint was the incidence of stroke at 1 and 2 years post-procedure.
RESULTS: At 1 year, TAVR was associated with a lower incidence of stroke compared with SAVR (odds ratio (OR), 0.77; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.98; p = 0.03). No significant difference was observed at 2 years (OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.65-1.17; p = 0.37).
CONCLUSIONS: TAVR significantly reduces the risk of stroke within 1 year post-procedure compared with SAVR; however, this effect was not maintained at 2 years. These findings highlight the early benefit of TAVR, while the long-term advantage requires further investigation.
THE PROSPERO REGISTRATION: This study has been registered with PROSPERO, registration number: CRD42025636191, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42025636191.

Title: Artificial intelligence versus physician decision-making in acute heart failure: a comparative evaluation of four contemporary AI systems.
Abstract:
AIMS: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by the public and healthcare professionals for clinical reasoning. However, they were developed as general-purpose language models rather than dedicated clinical decision-support tools, and their performance in real-world acute heart failure (AHF) management remains insufficiently evaluated. We compared four contemporary AI models with physician decision-making.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This single-centre retrospective observational study incorporated a cross-sectional AI evaluation of consecutive patients treated at Sotiria General Hospital between July and November 2025, excluding acute coronary syndrome. ChatGPT, ChatGPT Plus, DeepSeek, and an ESC guideline-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) model independently assessed identical standardized cases. Recommendations were compared with physician decisions on diagnosis, treatment, guideline-directed medical therapy, timing, and prognosis using Cohen's kappa, McNemar's test, Cochran's Q, Wilcoxon signed-rank testing, and multivariable logistic regression. Diagnostic performance differed significantly across systems (Cochran's Q = 8.477, P = 0.037). In the balanced diagnostic cohort, ChatGPT Plus achieved the highest heart failure (HF) accuracy (accuracy 86.5%, sensitivity 87.0%, and specificity 86.0%), followed by RAG (accuracy 77.5%), ChatGPT (accuracy 77.0%), and DeepSeek (accuracy 69.0%). For HF within the top three differential diagnoses, sensitivity was 90.0-97.0%; specificity was 70.0% for ChatGPT Plus, 68.0% for RAG, 19.0% for DeepSeek, and 15.0% for ChatGPT. Physician agreement was highest for guideline-directed therapies, with greater variability in prognosis and escalation of care. RAG more closely matched physician therapeutic timing but did not consistently outperform general-purpose models.
CONCLUSION: Contemporary AI models show promise in AHF decision support but substantial task-specific variability, supporting use as complements rather than replacements for physician judgement.

Title: Artificial intelligence in cardiovascular medicine: systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
AIMS: Artificial intelligence (AI) holds considerable promise for improving cardiovascular care, but prior to widespread adoption, AI-powered tools require evaluation in randomized trials. We systematically reviewed the current evidence from randomized trials of AI tools in cardiovascular medicine.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a systematic review of randomized trials comparing AI tools vs. standard care in cardiovascular medicine. PubMed, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform were searched from 1 January 2018, to 10 April 2026. Screening and full-text review were performed by three independent reviewers and risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 criteria. Of 11 151 identified records, 8599 remained after removal of duplicates. Following screening and full-text review, 25 trials met the eligibility criteria. These trials evaluated AI tools in acute cardiovascular care (n = 3), cardiac imaging (n = 6), decision support for medical therapy (n = 6), electrophysiology (n = 8), and interventional cardiology (n = 2). Nine trials were single-centre, and two were international. Seventeen trials (68%) reported positive results, defined by non-inferiority or superiority of the AI-based strategy. Overall risk of bias was rated as high or with some concerns in 84% of the included trials, and only 36% explicitly reported following the CONSORT-/SPIRIT-AI reporting guidelines.
CONCLUSION: Evidence from randomized trials evaluating AI tools in cardiovascular medicine is limited, and most trials have a high risk of bias. Wider implementation of AI tools into practice requires robust, international, multi-centre randomized trials that evaluate patient-relevant outcomes, ensure external validity, and adhere to reporting guidelines.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: PROSPERO CRD420251019264.

Title: Association of coffee and tea consumption with the risk of atrial fibrillation: a prospective cohort study from the UK Biobank.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Atrial fibrillation (AF) has a high prevalence and a heavy healthcare burden, making prevention of AF essential. Coffee and tea are popular beverages around the world, and they may have a relationship with AF, but the results are controversial. This study aimed to investigate the relationship of coffee and tea intake with the risk of AF.
METHODS: This study included 495,269 participants without AF at baseline from the UK Biobank. Coffee and tea intake was self-reported (0, 0.5-1, 2-3, ≥ 4 cups/day). Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.04 ± 2.26 years, 37,261 participants developed AF. The associations of coffee and tea with AF were non-linear (P for non-linear < 0.001). Compared with non-drinkers, drinking 0.5-1, 2-3, and ≥ 4 cups of coffee per day was associated with a protective effect against AF, corresponding to a 7, 11, and 9% lower risk, respectively. For tea, only consumption of 2-3 cups per day was associated with a modestly lower risk of AF, whereas no significant associations were observed for other intake categories.
CONCLUSIONS: We found that coffee intake was inversely associated with incident AF across multiple intake categories, whereas for tea, a modest inverse association was observed only at 2-3 cups per day, with no statistically significant associations for other intake categories. Further studies are warranted to confirm our findings and clarify the potential mechanism.

Title: Positron Emission Tomography Versus Coronary Angiography for Initial Cardiac Screening in Kidney Transplant Candidates: Waitlisting and Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract: Background Cardiac evaluation is an important component of kidney transplant evaluation, but the optimal initial testing approach remains uncertain. Methods Because the initial test was clinician-selected rather than randomized, this retrospective cohort study examined associations between the initial cardiac testing pathway (PET versus coronary angiography) and transplant listing status among 116 kidney transplant candidates (57 PET, 59 coronary angiography). Because many candidates had already been listed before the index cardiac test, binary analyses were interpreted as associations between clinician-selected testing pathways and listing status rather than post-testing effects on waitlisting. A test-date-anchored landmark analysis, restricted to candidates not yet listed for testing, was used to evaluate subsequent time to listing. Firth-penalized logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were performed as complementary analyses. Results Known coronary artery disease (CAD) differed markedly by testing modality, consistent with confounding by indication and clinician-directed test selection. Overall, 99/116 patients (85.3%) were listed, with no statistically significant difference between groups. Because 31/57 (54.4%) PET patients and 24/59 (40.7%) angiography patients were already listed before testing, the unadjusted evaluation-to-listing timeline could not be attributed to testing modality. The landmark analysis included 58 patients not yet listed at testing, with 55 complete cases in the adjusted model; coronary angiography versus PET was not significantly associated with subsequent time to listing (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.76; 95% CI, 0.76-4.07). In an exploratory subgroup of patients without known CAD (n=30), the estimated rate of subsequent listing was higher with coronary angiography than with PET (HR, 2.58; 95% CI, 1.08-6.16); however, the small subgroup and wide confidence interval warrant caution, and this finding should not be interpreted as evidence of effect modification in the absence of a reproducible formal interaction test. The Firth model showed no significant association between testing pathway and listing status (OR, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.51-4.72), consistent with IPTW (OR, 1.62; 95% CI, 0.54-4.83). Only eight one-year major adverse cardiovascular events occurred, precluding conclusions regarding comparative cardiovascular safety. Conclusions Initial cardiac testing was clinician-selected and strongly related to known CAD status; therefore, these findings primarily describe associations between clinically selected testing pathways rather than causal effects of interchangeable testing strategies. After accounting for temporal ordering, no statistically significant overall association between modality and subsequent time to listing was identified. The finding among patients without known CAD was exploratory and requires confirmation. Given the observational design, modest sample size, residual confounding, and limited number of cardiovascular events, these results do not establish the superiority or equivalent safety of either PET or coronary angiography.

Title: Exposure to guideline-recommended quadruple therapy after first hospitalization for HFrEF in France.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In 2021, the European Society of Cardiology updated its guidelines for managing heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (HFrEF), recommending a four-drug regimen combining a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, a beta-blocker, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and a renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitor. This study assessed, 6 months after guideline publication, the exposure of this quadruple therapy in patients newly hospitalized for HFrEF and identified associated factors.
METHODS AND RESULTS: First-time hospitalizations for HFrEF in France in 2022 were identified using the French National Health Data System. Treatment exposure during the year following discharge was described. Logistic regression was used to assess factors associated with receiving quadruple therapy within 30 days, including socio-demographic characteristics, healthcare utilization, and comorbidities. A total of 22 990 patients were included (65.1% men; mean age 74 years, SD 13.5). At 30 days, 26.3% of patients received quadruple therapy (22.5% at 1 year). Exposure rates were 76% for beta-blockers, 70% for renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitor, 58% for SGLT2 inhibitors, and 47% for mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. Advanced age, female sex, and certain comorbidities were associated with a lower likelihood of receiving quadruple therapy, while early follow-up with a general practitioner or cardiologist increased this likelihood.
DISCUSSION: Exposure of quadruple therapy remains limited, with challenges in both initiation and persistence over time. Older age and comorbidities would appear to constitute barriers. Further studies with longer follow-up after guideline publication are needed to assess temporal trends and the impact of strategies aimed at improving care.

Title: Does Hospital Accreditation Increase Inpatient Expenditure and Improve Quality of Care? Evidence from Heart Failure Admissions in County-Level Public Hospitals in China.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital accreditation aims to strengthen hospital capacity and improve quality of care, but its effects on inpatient expenditure, patient cost sharing and quality remain unclear. We estimate these effects in county-level public hospitals in China.
METHODS: We use administrative claims data from Zunyi, China. Four county-level public hospitals that passed tertiary hospital accreditation in 2021 comprise the treatment group. The control group comprises 17 hospitals that remained at the secondary level. We analyse 6844 heart failure admissions among adults aged 18 years or older from December 2020 to November 2022. The eligible cohort comprised 6,844 admissions; after matching, the analytical cohort comprised 3,920 admissions, and 3,874 were eligible for the readmission analysis. We combine propensity score matching with a difference-in-differences model to estimate the effects on total health expenditures per inpatient case, out-of-pocket costs per inpatient case, the patient cost-sharing rate and the 30-day all-cause readmission rate.
RESULTS: Hospital accreditation increased total health expenditures per inpatient case by 3.99% (P = 0.046). It did not significantly change out-of-pocket costs (-8.00%, P = 0.304), the patient cost-sharing rate (-2.12 percentage points, P = 0.143) or the 30-day all-cause readmission rate (+3.96 percentage points, P = 0.117). In subgroup analyses, total health expenditures increased significantly among both URRBMI and UEBMI inpatients and among inpatients admitted to Traditional Chinese Medicine hospitals. No subgroup showed a significant reduction in the 30-day all-cause readmission rate.
CONCLUSION: Our estimates indicate that tertiary hospital accreditation increased total health expenditures per inpatient case but did not significantly alter patient cost sharing or the 30-day all-cause readmission rate. Post-accreditation evaluation should jointly assess expenditures across the episode of care, financial protection and quality of care.

Title: Real-World Effectiveness of Budesonide/Glycopyrronium/Formoterol (BGF) Fixed-Dose Combination in Patients with COPD (RECORD Study): A Prospective Observational Study.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness of budesonide/glycopyrronium/formoterol (BGF) fixed-dose combination regarding clinical and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) in patients with moderate-to-severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in routine care.
METHODS: This prospective, single-arm observational, multi-center study collected data via electronic forms and PRO questionnaires. The primary outcome evaluated change in COPD assessment test (CAT) scores from baseline to 3 months of therapy. Secondary outcomes included change in the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ), Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire for Medication (TSQM-9), and annualized exacerbation rates (AER) over 12 months.
RESULTS: The study enrolled 571 patients with COPD from Germany (n=441) and the United Kingdom (UK, n=130) prescribed BGF fixed-dose combination per routine care. Overall, the mean age was 65.5 years (Germany 64.8; UK 68.1), 55.9% were male (Germany 56.5%; UK 53.8%). Baseline CAT was 20.4 (Germany 19.5; UK 23.6), and the SGRQ score was 49.7 (Germany 47.3; UK 58.1). Prior 12-month exacerbations were reported by 35.6% overall (Germany 28.9%; UK 58.6%). Overall, 60.6% had cardiovascular comorbidities, including 46.2% with hypertension; cardiovascular disease rates were similar across countries, but asthma, depression, chronic kidney disease, and osteoarthritis were higher in the UK. At 3 months, CAT improved by -3.28 overall (95% confidence interval [CI] -4.31 to -2.26; Germany -3.49; UK -2.38); minimum clinically important difference was achieved in 58.2% (Germany 58.7%; UK 56.3%); SGRQ improved -7.04 overall (95% CI -9.09 to -5.00; Germany -7.57; UK -4.76); and TSQM-9 Global satisfaction increased 14.7 at 12 months (95% CI 10.61 to 18.85). AER fell from 0.74 to 0.45 (rate ratio 0.60; 95% CI 0.51 to 0.72).
CONCLUSION: BGF fixed-dose combination improved health status, quality of life, and reduced exacerbations in patients in this observational descriptive study. These findings complement evidence from clinical trials and suggest BGF fixed-dose combination has benefits for patients with moderate-to-severe COPD in routine care.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Across the Coronary Disease Continuum in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Ischemic Events, Revascularization, and Stent Healing.
Abstract: Type 2 diabetes is associated with accelerated coronary atherosclerosis, recurrent ischemic events, and impaired vascular healing after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, the effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists across these distinct coronary outcomes remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review synthesized randomized evidence on myocardial infarction (MI), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), coronary revascularization, post-PCI healing, and mechanistic markers of coronary disease. MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were initially searched for eligible reports published from January 1, 2020, through December 31, 2025. All four database searches were updated on August 31, 2026, extending publication eligibility through that date; no additional eligible reports were identified. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Seven eligible reports derived from seven parent randomized trials, involving 37,033 participants, were included. Two presented primary findings from independent randomized trials, three were prespecified analyses of parent randomized trials, and two were post hoc analyses. Owing to substantial clinical and outcome heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized narratively. Albiglutide reduced first and recurrent MI, including type 1 and type 2 events, whereas higher-dose efpeglenatide yielded more favorable cardiovascular effect estimates than the lower dose. Across separate reports, semaglutide favorably modified epicardial adipose tissue, a surrogate imaging measure, and reduced the composite of cardiovascular death, MI, or stroke in patients with diabetic kidney disease. Liraglutide was associated with lower risks of broader cardiovascular composites compared with the other glucose-lowering therapies combined, although individual MI and revascularization outcomes were not significantly reduced. Exenatide did not significantly reduce the composite of hospitalization for ACS or coronary revascularization, and the only PCI-specific trial demonstrated no significant improvement in early stent coverage, neointimal thickness, or in-stent obstruction. Of the seven included reports, one was judged to have a low risk of bias, whereas six raised some concerns, primarily because of post hoc analyses, open-label treatment, incomplete methodological reporting, or limited imaging follow-up. Across the included reports, findings were more favorable for MI and broader cardiovascular events than for coronary revascularization or post-stent healing. However, the small number of heterogeneous reports, reliance on several secondary or post hoc analyses, and absence of quantitative meta-analysis limit firm conclusions and do not establish a definitive class-wide coronary effect. Potential differences by agent, dose, and patient phenotype require further investigation, while treatment-initiation timing remains largely untested.

Title: Biomarkers for the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: recent advances and prospects for clinical application.
Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome describes a multidirectional network linking dysfunctional adiposity, metabolic risk factors, kidney disease and cardiovascular injury. Its early stages are often clinically silent, while obesity, impaired kidney function, multimorbidity and recent exercise can alter the concentrations and interpretation of commonly used biomarkers. This narrative review, informed by a structured literature search, evaluates biomarkers across screening, risk stratification, treatment monitoring and precision phenotyping, while distinguishing CKM-specific evidence from evidence extrapolated from chronic kidney disease, diabetes, obesity and heart-failure populations. Established clinical biomarkers, including estimated glomerular filtration rate, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, B-type natriuretic peptide/N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin, remain the foundation of clinical assessment. Emerging evidence spans directly measured markers of inflammation, oxidative stress and organ injury; indices derived from routine clinical variables; and metabolomic, lipidomic and other multi-omics platforms. Most of these measures provide biological or prognostic information but remain investigational because prospective external validation, analytical standardisation, actionable thresholds, incremental net benefit and biomarker-guided intervention evidence are limited. Lifestyle and exercise act both as upstream modifiers of CKM biology and as interpretive factors for several biomarkers. A clinically useful CKM biomarker framework should therefore integrate evidence maturity, population relevance, cross-organ specificity, serial trajectories, cost and equity. Emerging biomarkers should complement rather than replace established assessment until prospective studies demonstrate that their use changes treatment decisions and improves patient outcomes.

Title: Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells: Isolation, Origin, Phenotype Applications, and Challenges.
Abstract: Traditional adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (AD-MSCs) research has relied on unfractionated bulk populations, whose therapeutic efficacy is constrained by cellular heterogeneity, culture-induced phenotypic drift, and rapid postengraftment functional exhaustion, resulting in inconsistent outcomes and impeding clinical translation. This review systematically examines AD-MSC developmental origins, tissue niches, isolation and purification strategies, functional phenotypes, and biomanufacturing bottlenecks. It integrates preclinical and clinical evidence for AD-MSCs and their extracellular vesicles (EVs) in bone and cartilage regeneration, chronic cutaneous diseases, neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and other conditions. These therapies remodel injured microenvironments through immunometabolic reprogramming, antifibrotic signaling, angiogenesis, mitochondrial transfer, and paracrine regulation rather than direct tissue replacement. Major translational barriers include cellular heterogeneity, safety concerns, the transdifferentiation controversy, nonstandardized preconditioning, culture-induced phenotypic drift, and low cell retention after transplantation. We propose that clinical translation should be based on prospective isolation of functional subpopulations, coupled with tailored preconditioning, precision gene editing, three-dimensional biomaterials, EV engineering, and automated closed-system biomanufacturing. This framework aims to preserve potency, phenotypic stability, and paracrine function, transforming AD-MSCs and their bioactive derivatives from variable, unfractionated preparations into well-characterized, standardized, highly potent precision biologics. More broadly, it offers a mechanism-driven, function-defined, engineering-enabled, and clinically accessible roadmap for next-generation regenerative medicine.

Title: Associations of mortality and sepsis after GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation versus SGLT2 inhibitor or metformin initiation in people with HIV, overweight or obesity, and type 2 diabetes: A target trial emulation.
Journal: Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) carry elevated cardiometabolic and infectious morbidity. Comparative effectiveness data for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs)against active comparators are scarce in this population.
OBJECTIVES: To estimate associations between GLP-1 RA initiation andclinical outcomes compared withsodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) or metformin.
DESIGN: Target trial emulation of new-user, active-comparator cohorts in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (2017 to 2025), with pre-specified replication in the Global Collaborative Network.
METHODS: Adults with HIV, overweight or obesity (ICD-10-CM E66 or body mass index 27 kg/m2 or higher), and T2D newly starting a GLP-1 RA, SGLT2i, or metformin after a 6-month washout were eligible. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality within 3 years of the index date; secondary endpoints were A41.9-coded sepsis, candidiasis, major adverse cardiovascular events, major adverse kidney events, other or unspecified encephalopathy, and three nested exploratory code-based neurocognitive definitions (definitions 1, 1 to 2, and 1 to 3). We built 1:1 propensity score matched cohorts and fitted Cox models with Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each comparator stratum.
RESULTS: Analyses included 2,720 matched pairs vs SGLT2i and 4,604 vs metformin. GLP-1 RA initiation was associated with a lower estimated hazard of all-cause mortality during up to 3 years of follow-up vs SGLT2i (hazard ratio [HR] 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.49-0.81) and vs metformin (HR 0.65, 0.53-0.81). Kaplan-Meier estimated 3-year mortality risk was 6.7% versus 9.4% against SGLT2i and 5.4% versus 7.4% against metformin. A41.9-coded sepsis showed a lower hazard vs SGLT2i (HR 0.71, 0.53-0.94) and metformin (HR 0.75, 0.60-0.94). Cardiovascular and kidney composites differed less clearly, with renal outcomes directionally favoring SGLT2i. Code-based neurocognitive endpoints were lower vs metformin, but were exploratory and limited by administrative coding; reported significance reflects adjusted P values.
CONCLUSION: GLP-1 RA initiation was associated with a lower observed hazard of all-cause mortality and of A41.9-coded sepsis than SGLT2i or metformin in PLWH with overweight or obesity and T2D. These associations remainvulnerable to residual confounding and require prospective confirmation. Emulation is not equivalent to randomization.

Title: Authors' reply to "Comment on Prospective randomized clinical trial on comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation combined with individualized cognitive training in older adults with heart failure and mild cognitive impairment".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Association between platelet indices and VCAM-1 levels in patients with coronary artery disease.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine platelet indices reflect platelet size and turnover, whereas soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) reflects endothelial activation. Whether these inexpensive indices relate to circulating VCAM-1 in coronary artery disease (CAD) is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between platelet indices and sVCAM-1 in patients with CAD.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study consecutively enrolled 80 patients with stable, angiographically confirmed CAD (>50% stenosis in at least one major coronary artery) at Dr. Kariadi General Hospital, Semarang, Indonesia. Platelet count, mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet large cell ratio (P-LCR) and large-platelet count were measured with a Sysmex XN-1000 analyser, and serum sVCAM-1 by sandwich ELISA (Elabscience). Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression were used.
RESULTS: Platelet count (ρ = 0.24, p = 0.036) and large-platelet count (ρ = 0.35, p = 0.002) were weakly correlated with sVCAM-1 (344.23 ± 144.98 ng/mL), whereas MPV (ρ = 0.10, p = 0.387) and P-LCR (ρ = 0.11, p = 0.336) were not. After adjustment for clinical covariates, only large-platelet count remained associated with sVCAM-1 (β = 58.7 ng/mL per SD; 95% CI 23.4-94.1; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: In stable CAD, large-platelet count and, less robustly, platelet count, but not MPV or P-LCR, were weakly associated with sVCAM-1. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Association of Cardiovascular Disease with Exacerbations, Longitudinal Lung Function Changes, and Spirometric Transitions in Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm), defined as a post-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1)/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio ≥0.70 with a post-bronchodilator FEV1 <80% predicted, is a heterogeneous spirometric pattern associated with adverse clinical outcomes and progression to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a common comorbidity in PRISm, but its prognostic relevance for subsequent respiratory outcomes remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between baseline CVD and the longitudinal course of PRISm.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 521 participants with PRISm identified between 2021 and 2023 and followed through 2025, with a mean follow-up duration of 2.59 ± 1.58 years. Participants were grouped according to baseline CVD status. Exacerbations, longitudinal lung function changes, spirometric transitions, and incident COPD were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, linear mixed-effects models, and Cox proportional hazards models, as appropriate. Subgroup analyses were performed in restrictive and non-restrictive PRISm, with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) used for sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 521 participants with PRISm, 166 had CVD. Compared with participants without CVD, those with CVD had a greater burden of severe and moderate-to-severe exacerbations, and a higher risk of frequent exacerbations (adjusted OR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.13-5.47). Participants with CVD also experienced accelerated declines in FEV1, FVC, and their percent predicted values. They were more likely to progress to COPD and less likely to recover to normal spirometry. In the Cox proportional hazards analysis, baseline CVD was independently associated with incident COPD (adjusted HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.07-2.48). No significant interaction was observed between CVD status and PRISm subtype, and IPTW sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary findings.
CONCLUSION: CVD was associated with greater exacerbation burden, faster lung function decline, and a higher risk of progression to COPD in individuals with PRISm. Assessment of CVD may provide additional information for risk stratification in PRISm; however, these observational findings require validation in prospective studies. Whether cardiovascular assessment can improve clinical outcomes in PRISm requires further investigation.

Title: A Prediction Model for Heart Failure with Improved Ejection Fraction Phenotype Based on Electrocardiogram Images and Clinical Baseline Features.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally evaluate machine learning models for predicting the heart failure with improved ejection fraction (HFimpEF) phenotype in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy, using electrocardiogram (ECG) image features, all eligible clinical baseline features, and their combination.
METHODS: This two-center retrospective study included patients hospitalized between March 2018 and February 2025 with baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. HFimpEF was defined as an increase in LVEF of at least 10 percentage points and a follow-up LVEF >40%, with at least three months between echocardiograms. The development cohort comprised 415 patients (194 with HFimpEF and 221 with persistent HFrEF); an independent cohort of 100 patients (55 and 45, respectively) was used for external validation. Four classifiers were evaluated using ECG image features alone, all eligible clinical baseline features alone, and their combination. LASSO was used separately to rank clinical variables.
RESULTS: In the reported internal evaluation, the combined random forest model achieved an AUC of 0.825, accuracy of 0.747, precision of 0.753, specificity of 0.791, and F1 score of 0.721. In external validation, the combined-model AUCs (95% confidence intervals) were 0.624 (0.513-0.734) for random forest, 0.607 (0.496-0.718) for logistic regression, 0.653 (0.545-0.761) for SVC-RBF, and 0.565 (0.454-0.676) for k-nearest neighbors. β-Blocker use ranked highest in the exploratory LASSO analysis. Combined models did not consistently outperform single-feature-set models externally.
CONCLUSION: Models combining ECG image features and clinical baseline features showed promising internal discrimination for identifying subsequent HFimpEF in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy. However, external discrimination was modest, and the combined models did not consistently outperform single-source models. Further model refinement and validation in larger, independent cohorts are needed before clinical application.

Title: Penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) versus separate needling for post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction: an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial protocol.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction limits mobility, balance, and independence and remains a major target of neurorehabilitation. Acupuncture is widely used as an adjunctive intervention after stroke, but direct randomized evidence comparing penetrating needling with conventional separate needling at the same acupoints is limited. This protocol describes an active-comparator randomized controlled trial comparing penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) with separate needling for post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction, with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and surface electromyography (sEMG) included as exploratory mechanistic outcomes. This single-center, prospective, assessor-blinded, parallel-group superiority trial will enroll 130 participants with subacute post-stroke lower-limb motor dysfunction. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to penetrating needling from Qiuxu (GB40) to Zhaohai (KI6) or to separate needling at the same acupoints. Both groups will receive 12 acupuncture sessions over 2 weeks, delivered 6 times per week, with 30 min of needle retention per session, together with the same total rehabilitation dose of 30 min/day, 5 days/week. The primary outcome is the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Lower Extremity (FMA-LE) score at the end of treatment (T1). The primary analysis will use analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline FMA-LE. Secondary clinical outcomes include the Berg Balance Scale, Manual Muscle Testing, and Modified Ashworth Scale. Registered secondary neurophysiological assessments include fNIRS and sEMG; their derived measures will be analyzed exploratorily.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/mgt/project/view/2037483478790045696, ITMCTR2026000773.

Title: Carotid Plaque Score: A Useful Tool or Futile Gadget for Risk Assessment? An Update.
Abstract: Conventional cardiovascular risk scores estimate the probability of future events; however, these risk scores do not directly quantify the presence or extent of subclinical atherosclerosis. This narrative review critically evaluates the current evidence on the carotid plaque score (CPS), a semiquantitative ultrasound-based measure of carotid atherosclerotic burden across predefined arterial segments. Population-based cohorts have consistently shown that carotid plaque presence and burden are independently associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Studies specifically evaluating CPS have further suggested an incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk models, particularly for ischemic stroke and major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). However, CPS does not represent a single standardized metric. Therefore, proposed thresholds, including CPS ≥2 and CPS >3, were derived using different plaque definitions, arterial segments, scoring methods, and study populations and are not directly interchangeable. Meanwhile, CPS is more accessible, non-ionizing, and relatively inexpensive compared with coronary artery calcium (CAC), but it is less extensively validated and less standardized. Nonetheless, available comparative evidence indicates that CAC provides superior discrimination for coronary outcomes. In contrast, carotid plaque assessment may offer complementary information for cerebrovascular risk and in selected individuals with discordant estimated risk or no detectable coronary calcification. No randomized trial has demonstrated that treatment decisions guided by CPS improve clinical outcomes. Accordingly, current guidelines generally position carotid plaque imaging as a selective risk modifier rather than a routine screening or stand-alone treatment-allocation tool. Thus, broader clinical implementation will require standardized acquisition and reporting protocols, external validation across diverse populations, integration with established risk models, and prospective studies evaluating whether CPS-guided preventive strategies improve patient outcomes.

Title: Outcomes of Drug-Coated Balloon Versus Drug-Eluting Stent for the Treatment of Large De Novo Coronary Lesions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although drug-coated balloons (DCBs) outperform drug-eluting stents (DESs) in the treatment of de novo small-vessel coronary lesions, no comparable studies are available for de novo large-vessel coronary lesions.
METHODS: This retrospective study examined 960 patients with de novo large-vessel coronary lesions (reference vessel diameter ≥3.0 mm) who underwent paclitaxel DCB angioplasty or DES implantation at Beijing Anzhen Hospital. The study endpoints included all-cause death, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and target vessel revascularization (TVR). Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves and Cox regression analysis were used to investigate the clinical outcomes of patients in the DCB and DES groups.
RESULTS: The overall incidence rates of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), all-cause death, MI, stroke, and TVR were 9.27% (89/960), 1.5% (14 patients), 0.9% (9 patients), 0.6% (6 patients), and 6.8% (65 patients), respectively. No significant differences were observed between the DCB and DES groups in MACCEs (13.2% vs. 5.6%; p = 0.511), all-cause death (1.9% vs. 1.0%; p = 0.763), MI (0.6% vs. 1.2%; p = 0.239), or stroke (0.6% vs. 0.6%; p = 0.361). However, the TVR rate was significantly higher in the DCB group than in the DES group (10.1% vs. 3.6%; p = 0.028), and this difference persisted after multivariate adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: For patients with de novo lesions in target vessels with diameters ≥3.0 mm, the safety and efficacy of DCB therapy were comparable to those of DES therapy, except for target vessel revascularization.

Title: Absence of Documented Standard Modifiable Cardiovascular Risk Factors Among Catheterized Admissions in Bangladesh: Frequency and Coronary Angiographic Phenotype in a 20-Year Registry Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Coronary artery disease may occur without standard modifiable cardiovascular risk factors (SMuRFs), but the frequency and angiographic phenotype of such presentations in South Asian catheterization cohorts remain uncertain. We estimated registry-defined SMuRF-less frequency, tested alternative dyslipidaemia definitions, and compared angiographic phenotypes by SMuRF status.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, registry-based cross-sectional analysis of 51,864 admissions with matched catheterization records at a Bangladeshi tertiary cardiac centre from 2005 to 2024. Admissions were classified as SMuRF-less when no qualifying hypertension, diabetes, smoking, or dyslipidaemia was documented or identified; dyslipidaemia reflected a documented diagnosis or qualifying lipid measurement. Documented-only and statin-inclusive definitions were sensitivity analyses. We calculated unadjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Under the primary definition, 3172 admissions (6.1%) were SMuRF-less, compared with 6.5% under the documented-only definition and 1.6% under the statin-inclusive definition. Among admissions with a classifiable angiographic phenotype, SMuRF-less admissions more frequently had normal coronary arteries (24.9% vs. 10.7%; PR, 2.34; 95% CI, 2.18-2.50) and less frequently had obstructive coronary artery disease (56.6% vs. 71.2%; PR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.77-0.82). Among admissions with obstructive disease, multivessel disease was less frequent (49.6% vs. 57.8%; PR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.82-0.90), whereas recorded intracoronary thrombus was more frequent (5.3% vs. 3.2%; PR, 1.65; 95% CI, 1.33-2.04). Of 6635 ST-elevation myocardial infarction admissions, 355 (5.4%) were SMuRF-less; 318 (89.6%) had obstructive disease.
CONCLUSION: Registry-defined SMuRF-less admissions, reflecting absence of documented qualifying factors rather than prospectively verified biological absence, were uncommon, and their estimated frequency depended on risk-factor ascertainment. Although their recorded angiographic burden was generally lower, obstructive disease remained common, particularly in ST-elevation myocardial infarction. The absence of documented SMuRFs should not provide clinical reassurance. Prospective patient-level studies with standardized risk-factor assessment and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

Title: A whole-blood transcriptomic analysis of shared molecular mechanisms between subclinical atherosclerosis and hypothyroidism in women.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypothyroidism (HT) is clinically associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, yet the shared molecular mechanisms underlying subclinical atherosclerosis (sAS) in hypothyroid patients remain poorly understood. This study aims to identify common transcriptomic signatures and regulatory axes between these two conditions.
METHODS: We performed an integrated transcriptomic analysis of peripheral whole-blood datasets retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE176153 and GSE221615). To minimize sex-based biological bias, the analysis was restricted to female samples. Differential expression, functional enrichment, network topology, and transcription factor prediction were performed to identify shared differentially expressed genes (SDEGs) and candidate transcriptional regulators. The classification performance of selected pivotal SDEGs and predicted transcription factors was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Public transcriptomic data from myeloid-specific Tshr-knockout murine macrophages (GSE275079) were additionally examined to explore the myeloid context of TSH-TSHR signaling, followed by in vitro RT-qPCR validation in human THP-1 macrophages exposed to TSH and LPS.
RESULTS: We identified 20 female-restricted SDEGs enriched in pathways related to B-cell proliferation and activation. Integration of functional enrichment, functional network analysis, and PPI topology highlighted six pivotal genes: BLK, CD19, CD180, TNFRSF13C, SPIB, and FCRLA. SPI1 and MEF2A were identified as key candidate regulators collectively targeting this gene set. Exploratory ROC analyses showed discriminatory capacity for several pivotal SDEGs and candidate transcription factors across the study cohorts, with some of these findings also observed in an external cohort of advanced atherosclerotic disease. Analysis of Tshr-knockout murine macrophage data revealed enrichment in lymphocyte and mononuclear cell proliferation pathways, alongside downregulation of Ifrd1. In human THP-1 macrophages, TSH alone and in combination with LPS were associated with a significant downregulation of IFRD1 expression.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest a potential sex-specific immune-endocrine link between thyroid dysfunction and atherosclerotic disease, characterized by a shared transcriptomic axis converging on B-cell-associated pivotal genes and candidate transcriptional regulators. Exploratory myeloid analyses further identified TSH-associated downregulation of IFRD1.

Title: Age-stratified analysis reveals heterogeneity in factors associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in IgA vasculitis: a retrospective study in a large volume center.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding represents a severe complication of IgA vasculitis (IgAV). Most current analyses of risk factors aggregate patients across all ages, potentially obscuring critical age-specific differences. This study aimed to delineate factors independently associated with GI bleeding in IgAV across distinct age groups.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study involving 964 IgAV patients stratified into four age cohorts: preschool (3-6 years, n=192), school-age (7-12 years, n=313), adolescent (13-17 years, n=202), and adult (>18 years, n=257). Univariable analyses were followed by Firth's penalized logistic regression within each age cohort to evaluate factors associated with GI bleeding. Model discrimination was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with optimism correction performed via 1,000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: The pattern of factors associated with GI bleeding differed across age strata. In preschool children, NAR was significantly associated with GI bleeding (OR = 5.88). In school-age children, NAR (OR = 2.02), summer onset (OR = 2.47), and medium and high SII (OR = 2.72/3.70) were associated with GI bleeding. In adolescents, high SII (OR = 6.22) and log(FIB/GLO) (OR = 4.57) remained significant, while in adults, high SII was the predominant associated factor (OR = 9.53). These principal associations remained significant after FDR correction for multiple comparisons. The optimism-corrected AUC values of the age-specific models ranged from 0.686 in preschool children to 0.784 in adults.
CONCLUSION: The factors associated with GI bleeding in IgAV showed heterogeneous patterns across age strata, with neutrophil-related inflammatory markers more prominent in younger children and systemic inflammatory and coagulation-related markers more prominent in older groups. These exploratory findings support further investigation of age-specific risk assessment in IgAV.

Title: Management of cardiometabolic risk in prostate cancer: expert consensus from Singapore and Malaysia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer is one of the most diagnosed malignancies among men globally, with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and androgen receptor-targeted therapy remaining central to the management of advanced disease. Despite their proven efficacy in controlling tumour progression, these therapies are associated with significant cardiovascular and metabolic risks. The authors aimed to develop a set of evidence-based recommendations for the assessment, monitoring, and management of cardiometabolic risks associated with ADT and androgen receptor-targeted therapy in patients with prostate cancer.
METHODS: A panel of 12 clinicians from Malaysia and Singapore, with expertise in prostate cancer and cardiovascular disease management, developed consensus statements using a modified Delphi method. Statements were informed by a literature review and refined through structured discussions and anonymous voting until consensus was achieved.
RESULTS: A total of 13 statements were developed, of which 12 achieved consensus. Key recommendations include conducting a baseline evaluation of lifestyle risk factors and comorbidities, implementing a simplified cardiovascular disease risk assessment checklist, and tailoring treatment plans and structured management protocols according to individual cardiovascular disease risk categories. The panel also recommended referring high-risk or symptomatic patients for appropriate care (if not already on follow-up) and initiating cardiometabolic monitoring post-treatment with frequency adjusted based on patient-specific risk profiles. Additional endorsed strategies included incorporating lifestyle modification counselling during follow-up, applying the modified ABCDE Cardio-Oncology framework, and involving multidisciplinary teams in managing patients with elevated cardiovascular risk. The rejected statement, which proposed routine baseline electrocardiograms for all patients, lacked support owing to limited evidence, logistical and interpretative challenges, and concerns over delaying cancer treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: This consensus document offers practical, evidence-based guidance for minimising cardiometabolic risks in patients with prostate cancer on ADT or androgen receptor-targeted therapy. These recommendations support individualised care, balancing oncological efficacy with cardiovascular safety to improve patient outcomes.

Title: Long-Term Effects of Myocardial Injury on 1-Year Outcomes in Hospital Survivors With COVID-19: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Myocardial injury is both a common complication among hospitalized coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients and a major predictor of adverse clinical outcomes. However, its long-term effects remain poorly defined. In this prospective cohort study of 2185 COVID-19 survivors (531 with myocardial injury), we assessed 1-year post-discharge outcomes using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression before and after propensity score matching. Myocardial injury was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 3.14) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (aHR 5.22). Long-term use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin II receptor blockers (ACEI/ARB) was associated with reduced mortality (aHR 0.44) and MACE (aHR 0.58) in the myocardial injury group. At 1 year, 71.5% of survivors reported persistent symptoms-most commonly fatigue and sleep difficulties-and those with myocardial injury had poorer quality of life. This study provides the prospective evidence from China's Omicron era on the prognostic value of myocardial injury, combining hard clinical endpoints with patient-reported outcomes and the first analysis of the ACEI/ARB association in this population. These findings highlight the prognostic importance of myocardial injury and the potential role of ACEI/ARB therapy in post-discharge management, supporting targeted follow-up strategies for this high-risk population.

Title: Beta-blockers after acute coronary syndrome: insights across the ejection fraction spectrum.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association between beta-blocker (BB) prescription and long-term all-cause mortality after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and to assess whether this varies across the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) spectrum.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed ACS patients from the retrospective multicentre CardioMining study (NCT05176769). The primary analysis used inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and restricted mean survival time (RMST) derived from weighted Kaplan-Meier curves. RMST and survival differences were estimated at 1 and 5 years. A landmark analysis evaluated survival between years 1 and 5 among first-year survivors. Among 6049 ACS patients (age 66.8 ± 13.2 years; 74.9% male), 5107 (84.4%) were discharged on BBs. During a median 4.6-year follow-up, 1912 deaths (31.6%) occurred. Overall, the 1-year RMST difference associated with BBs was 6.3 days (95%CI 0.0 to 13.2), which attenuated further by 5 years (11.3 days, 95%CI -30.7 to 63.9). The largest 1-year RMST difference was observed among patients with LVEF ≤40% (18.8 days, 95%CI 1.1 to 37.4), whereas associations were smaller and non-significant among patients with LVEF 41-49% and LVEF ≥50%. At 5 years, confidence intervals crossed the null across all LVEF categories. Continuous LVEF analyses suggested greater short-term benefit at lower values, with progressive attenuation across the LVEF spectrum. Among 1-year survivors, no significant RMST differences were observed between years 1 and 5.
CONCLUSION: Discharge BB prescription was not associated with a clear long-term survival advantage after ACS in this large real-world cohort. Apparent associations were strongest at lower LVEF values and attenuated during longer follow-up.

Title: Inflammatory Biomarkers with Overall Cancer Prevalence in the MIDUS II Population: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The correlation between chronic systemic inflammation and cancer has been inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the associations between circulating inflammatory biomarker concentrations and overall cancer prevalence in the adult general population.
METHODS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of 961 participants from the MIDUS II Biomarker Project (2004-2009) with complete measurements of interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), fibrinogen, C-reactive protein (CRP), soluble E-selectin, and soluble ICAM-1. Cancer history was defined as self-reported physician-diagnosed cancer at the time of biomarker assessment. Associations were analyzed using generalized additive models and multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, BMI, smoking, drinking, and exercise.
RESULTS: Cancer history was present in 127 participants (13.2%). In the adjusted model, IL-6 was nominally associated with cancer history (OR = 1.2, 95% CI: 1.0-1.4, P = 0.035).. The other seven biomarkers were not significantly associated with cancer history. A subgroup analysis suggested an interaction with cholesterol problems (P for interaction = 0.0435). A combined ROC model including IL-6 showed moderate cross-sectional discrimination for cancer history (AUC = 0.708, sensitivity 75.59%, specificity 59.95%).
CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional analysis, IL-6 was nominally associated with cancer history. Because biomarker measurement and cancer history were assessed in the cross-sectional analysis, reverse causation and residual confounding cannot be excluded. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of prediction or causation. Larger prospective studies with repeated measurements are needed.

Title: Acute study of the glycemic, insulinemic and triglyceride responses on white bread with peanuts and cashews in different forms (whole nut, nut butter and nut milk).
Abstract: Frequent nut consumption is associated with reduced cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk and mortality, particularly in individuals with diabetes, highlighting their potential health benefits. This study investigated the acute postprandial glycemic, insulinemic, and triglyceride responses to white bread consumed with peanuts and cashews in three forms: whole nuts, nut butter, and nut milk. Given that particle size and food form influence postprandial responses, it was hypothesized that nut milk would significantly modulate these metabolic parameters compared to whole nuts and nut butter. Fifteen healthy participants completed a randomized crossover study. Participants consumed a standardized serving of 42.5 g of peanuts or cashews in each form alongside two slices of white bread. Compared to white bread alone, all nut forms significantly attenuated postprandial glucose peaks and reduced glycemic responses, with a slight increase in insulin responses. Notably, nut butter and nut milk elicited 52 and 44% higher triglyceride responses, respectively, compared to whole nuts. Furthermore, peanuts resulted in a lower glucose incremental area under the curve (iAUC, 2 h) and a higher triglyceride response than cashews. However, these differences were not statistically significant. The incorporation of peanuts and cashews into white bread demonstrated improved glycemic control. While nut form primarily impacted triglyceride responses, suggesting a critical role for lipid bioaccessibility in modulating postprandial lipid metabolism, it did not significantly influence glucose or acute insulin responses. These findings suggest that prioritizing whole nuts over highly processed forms in a high-carbohydrate meal could be a beneficial dietary strategy for individuals managing diabetes or cardiovascular disease risk.

Title: Which score best predicts new-onset AF after primary PCI in STEMI? Head-to-head assessment of four algorithms.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is a frequent and clinically significant comorbidity following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), associated with increased mortality, stroke risk, and healthcare costs. Predicting NOAF in this setting remains challenging. This study aimed to compare the predictive performance of four risk scores-CHA2DS2-VASc-60, mC2HEST, Mayo-AF, and HATCH-in identifying patients at high risk of NOAF after primary PCI in STEMI.
