METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study at Shaoxing Central Hospital, including consecutive adults with STEMI who underwent primary PCI within 12 h of symptom onset between February 2020 and June 2025. Patients with a history of atrial fibrillation or other exclusions were excluded. The endpoint was NOAF within 1 year after PCI, documented by continuous inpatient telemetry, 12-lead ECG at discharge, and routine follow-up ECGs at 1, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. We compared the discriminative ability of the four scores using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and assessed their clinical utility through net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: A total of 1,175 patients were included in the final analysis. The incidence of NOAF within 1 year was 8.2% (n = 96). The mC2HEST score demonstrated the highest area under the ROC curve (AUC) for predicting NOAF (AUC = 0.786), followed by HATCH (AUC = 0.746) and CHA2DS2-VASc-60 (AUC = 0.739), while Mayo-AF had the lowest AUC (AUC = 0.736).Pairwise comparisons showed that mC2HEST significantly outperformed CHA2DS2-VASc-60 (ΔAUC = 0.046, p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Among the four risk scores evaluated, mC2HEST provided the best predictive performance for NOAF after primary PCI in STEMI patients. Its superior discriminative ability and significant integrated discrimination improvement suggest that mC2HEST could be a valuable tool for identifying high-risk patients who may benefit from intensified monitoring and early interventions. Future prospective, multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

Title: Beyond solute clearance: the kidney-gut-immune-nutrition axis in hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis and a proposed framework for integrated risk stratification.
Abstract: Kidney disease affects approximately ~850 million people globally, with millions dependent on dialysis as life-sustaining renal replacement therapy. While dialysis corrects solute accumulation and fluid overload, it incompletely replicates normal renal physiology and introduces its own biological stressors, perpetuating a cycle of systemic dysfunction that extends well beyond the kidney. Central to this dysfunction is the kidney-gut-immune-nutrition (KGIN) axis: a bidirectional network linking renal clearance, intestinal microbial homeostasis, immune regulation, and nutritional metabolism. In end-stage renal disease, each component of this axis is simultaneously disrupted and becomes a driver of further deterioration. Uremic toxin accumulation remodels the gut microbiome toward a dysbiotic state, characterized by depletion of short-chain fatty acid-producing organisms and expansion of pathobionts. The resulting compromise of intestinal barrier integrity permits systemic translocation of lipopolysaccharide and other microbial products, sustaining chronic low-grade inflammation and a paradoxical state of immune dysfunction marked by heightened inflammatory signaling alongside impaired pathogen defense. These perturbations converge on nutritional status, driving protein-energy wasting through catabolic cytokine signaling, anorexia, and suppression of anabolic pathways, with sarcopenia reported in several dialysis cohorts to progress at two to three fold faster than age related muscle loss. Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis produce distinct patterns of axis disruption: hemodialysis is characterized by intermittent toxin peaks, bioincompatible membrane-driven complement activation, and more severe dysbiosis, whereas peritoneal dialysis introduces continuous peritoneal glucose exposure and a unique local immune microenvironment, with generally slower decline in residual kidney function. These modality-specific differences translate into divergent cardiovascular, infectious, and nutritional risk profiles that are incompletely explained by traditional clinical variables. Emerging multi-omics approaches, including metagenomics, metabolomics, and high-throughput immune profiling, are beginning to characterize axis disruption with unprecedented resolution, enabling in-depth characterization of host-microbiome-immune identification of patient subgroups with distinct mechanistic signatures that cannot be captured by single domain analysis alone. To bridge this analytical capability with clinical practice, we propose the Microbiome-Immune-Nutrition (MIN) Index, a conceptual, hypothesis generating composite biomarker framework designed to synthesize data across all three axis domains and stratify patients by the severity of disruption to guide targeted, personalized interventions, which remain to be demonstrated through prospective validation studies. Therapeutic strategies targeting the axis, including dietary fiber and plant-based approaches, synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, advanced dialysis modalities, and omega-3 and polyphenol supplementation, show mechanistic promise but require larger, better-designed trials with hard clinical endpoints before routine clinical adoption. Standardization of microbiome research methodology, investment in longitudinal multi-omics cohorts, and development of international collaborative consortia are research priorities that will be essential to translate mechanistic insights into improvements in survival and quality of life for patients on maintenance dialysis.

Title: Efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors on functional mitral regurgitation associated with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) commonly complicates heart failure (HF) and portends a poor prognosis. While sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve clinical outcomes and induce cardiac reverse remodeling in HF, their specific effect on FMR associated with HF severity remains uncertain.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to 21 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating SGLT2i in adult patients with HF and chronic FMR on background guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Primary outcomes were changes from baseline in effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) and regurgitant volume (RV). Secondary clinical outcomes included HF hospitalization and cardiovascular (CVS) death. Random-effects models were used. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Three RCTs involving 455patients were included. SGLT2i therapy was associated with a statistically significant reduction in EROA (MD -0.086 cm2, 95% CI -0.150 to -0.022) and RV (MD -10.87 mL, 95% CI -17.32 to -4.43), but substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 72.5% and I2 = 63.5%, respectively). On leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, statistical significance for both primary valvular outcomes was lost after omitting the EFFORT trial. The certainty of evidence was rated as low.
CONCLUSION: Addition of SGLT2i to GDMT was associated with reductions in FMR severity in pooled analyses; however, these findings were not robust in sensitivity analyses and are limited by low certainty of evidence. The apparent reduction in clinical events requires cautious interpretation due to event sparsity. These results should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory, warranting further validation in large-scale, prospective trials.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261462002, PROSPERO CRD420261385207.

Title: Explainable machine learning for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute heart failure: a prospective single-center cohort study from Vietnam.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate risk stratification is essential in acute heart failure (AHF), which carries substantial in-hospital mortality. The Get With The Guidelines-Heart Failure (GWTG-HF) score is widely used, but its performance may vary across populations, and prospective data from Southeast Asia are scarce. We developed and internally validated explainable machine-learning (ML) models for in-hospital mortality in a Vietnamese AHF cohort and compared them with the GWTG-HF score.
METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 572 consecutive patients admitted with AHF (October 2024-June 2025). Missing data were imputed with a random forest-based algorithm, and class imbalance handled with SMOTE within training folds. Six algorithms (logistic regression, elastic net, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) were trained with stratified cross-validation, with optimism correction, and evaluated on an independent 25% test set. We assessed discrimination (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC), calibration (calibration slope/intercept, Brier and scaled Brier scores), classification, and clinical utility (decision-curve analysis); thresholds were derived from training data only. Pairwise AUC comparisons used the DeLong test, and interpretation used SHAP. Reporting followed TRIPOD + AI.
RESULTS: Fifty-three patients (9.3%) died in hospital. Random forest had the highest discrimination (AUC 0.846, 95% CI 0.757-0.922), followed by the GWTG-HF score (0.817), logistic regression (0.795), elastic net (0.794), CatBoost (0.786), XGBoost (0.763), and LightGBM (0.694). No ML model significantly outperformed the GWTG-HF score (all DeLong p > 0.05), a comparison limited by only 13 test-set events. Although CatBoost had the numerically lowest Brier score (0.085), scaled Brier scores were low for all models and calibration intercepts were uniformly negative, indicating over-estimation of risk from aggressive imbalance correction; predicted probabilities therefore require recalibration. SHAP identified respiratory failure, NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity troponin I (risk-increasing) and an ADHF phenotype and left ventricular dilation (associated with lower predicted risk) as the most influential features.
CONCLUSIONS: Explainable ML, led by random forest, achieved good discrimination but did not significantly outperform the GWTG-HF score, most plausibly reflecting limited statistical power rather than true equivalence. With miscalibrated probabilities requiring recalibration, explainable ML is best viewed as a complementary risk-ranking tool; external, multicenter, and temporal validation are required before clinical use.

Title: Prognostic model integrating the blood urea nitrogen-to-serum albumin ratio and radiological features for poor functional outcome in cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The blood urea nitrogen-to-serum albumin ratio (BAR) is a novel composite biomarker. This study investigated whether BAR could reliably predict poor functional outcomes in patients with cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST).
METHODS: All patients with CVST enrolled in this observational study between January 2011 and December 2025 were identified. The study population was randomly divided into a derivation cohort comprising 70% of the patients and a validation cohort comprising the remaining 30%. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of poor functional outcomes. A prognostic nomogram was developed using data from the derivation cohort, and its predictive performance was assessed in the validation cohort.
RESULTS: A total of 803 patients were included in this study. In the derivation cohort, coma, older age, intracerebral hemorrhage, straight sinus thrombosis, and higher BAR were independently associated with poor functional outcomes and were incorporated into the nomogram. Straight sinus thrombosis was independently associated with higher odds of poor functional outcome (odds ratio [OR], 4.525; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.267-9.031), whereas each one-unit increase in BAR was associated with an OR of 1.411 (95% CI, 1.226-1.625). In the derivation cohort, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.900, compared with 0.893 in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSION: Higher admission BAR was independently associated with poor functional outcomes in patients with CVST. The nomogram incorporating BAR and radiologically confirmed straight sinus thrombosis may facilitate early individualized risk stratification.

Title: Adversarial domain adaptation for false-positive reduction in hospital-to-robotic echocardiographic screening under limited target-domain data.
Abstract: Hospital-trained deep learning models for echocardiographic wall motion abnormality detection achieve strong performance under standard clinical acquisition conditions but often degrade substantially when deployed on autonomous robotic acquisition systems. Most existing models are developed and validated under controlled clinical acquisition conditions, limiting their robustness when deployed in emerging autonomous imaging systems. A hospital-trained wall motion abnormality detection model trained on 10,000 hospital echocardiograms achieved 92.3% accuracy (94.0% sensitivity, 90.6% specificity) when applied to an independent hospital test data set of 500 studies. However, direct deployment on 150 robotic echocardiograms from 15 healthy subjects reduced the normal-case specificity to 65.7%, representing a 24.9 percentage-point drop compared to the performance when applied to the hospital-acquired data. No statistically significant difference in SNR was observed between domains (p = 0.31; d = 0.12), with similarly small standardized differences in contrast and sharpness, although formal equivalence was not established. Acquisition-geometry measures differed descriptively between domains, suggesting that geometry-associated factors may contribute to the observed domain shift. We propose an adversarial domain adaptation framework built upon a 3D ResNet-18 backbone with a gradient-reversal domain discriminator for aligning hospital and robotic feature representations while retaining the hospital-trained classification objective. This design enables adaptation to the robotic domain without requiring labeled robot-acquired pathological cases, which are particularly difficult to obtain during early-stage robotic system development. Under leave-one-subject-out validation across robotic subjects, Mixed-DANN improved specificity to 86.1% ± 4.3%, while Normal-only DANN improved specificity to 89.3% ± 4.8% (p < 0.001 versus direct transfer), recovering 94.8% of the hospital-to-robot specificity gap. Because the robotic cohort comprises only healthy subjects, evaluation is appropriately restricted to specificity and false-positive rate; sensitivity evaluation requires future acquisition of robot-acquired pathological cases. These findings suggest that acquisition-associated domain shift substantially impacts cross-platform deployment. The proposed adversarial domain adaptation framework provides a potential pathway for adapting hospital-trained cardiac AI models to autonomous robotic ultrasound under conditions of limited target-domain data, although validation using robot-acquired pathological cases remains necessary before clinical translation.

Title: Perioperative safety profile of robotic versus laparoscopic hiatal hernia repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic hiatal hernia repair (RHHR) is increasingly used, but whether its technical advantages improve perioperative safety compared with laparoscopic hiatal hernia repair (LHHR) remains uncertain. We compared the short-term safety profiles of RHHR and LHHR, with particular attention to organ-specific postoperative complications.
METHODS: MEDLINE (via PubMed), Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 15 July 2025 for comparative studies of RHHR and LHHR in adults. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. The primary outcome was overall postoperative complications; secondary outcomes included cardiovascular, respiratory, and urological complications, dysphagia, operative time, intraoperative complications, 30-day readmission, mortality, and length of stay. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled as appropriate.
RESULTS: Eleven comparative studies (10 retrospective and one prospective) involving 696,886 patients were included. Overall postoperative complications did not differ significantly between RHHR and LHHR (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.98-1.33). RHHR was associated with fewer intraoperative complications (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.24-0.73) and a modestly shorter hospital stay (MD -0.40 days, 95% CI -0.78--0.02). In contrast, RHHR was associated with higher odds of cardiovascular events (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.31), respiratory complications (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.59-1.71), 30-day readmission (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.19-1.27), and mortality (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.11-1.43). No significant differences were observed for urological complications, postoperative dysphagia, or overall operative time. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low.
CONCLUSIONS: Comparative evidence identified through 15 July 2025 suggests broadly similar overall postoperative morbidity after RHHR and LHHR. RHHR may be associated with fewer intraoperative complications and a shorter hospital stay, but observed associations with higher odds of cardiopulmonary events, readmission, and mortality should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence is predominantly observational and susceptible to residual confounding, case-mix differences, and database-related bias.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251102047, PROSPERO identifier CRD420251102047.

Title: Biomarkers associated with admission rupture status of intracranial aneurysms: a combined analysis of morphological, inflammatory and coagulation indicators.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is predominantly caused by intracranial aneurysm (IA) rupture. As a critical neurological emergency with rapid clinical deterioration, SAH is life-threatening and associated with high mortality and disability rates. Early and accurate discrimination of ruptured status is essential for the emergency management of intracranial aneurysms.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to screen admission inflammatory and coagulation biomarkers associated with IA rupture status and construct a comprehensive diagnostic model to distinguish ruptured from unruptured intracranial aneurysms.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis was conducted on 167 patients with intracranial aneurysms admitted to the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2020 to September 2025. Patients were divided into a ruptured group (119 cases) and an unruptured group (48 cases) based on intraoperative and imaging findings. Baseline clinical, morphological, hematological and coagulation data were collected. LASSO regression was used for preliminary variable screening. Firth-penalized multivariate logistic regression was further applied to screen independent correlates of aneurysm rupture status and eliminate collinear and insignificant indicators. Finally, a three-variable combined model incorporating aneurysm morphology, white blood cell count, and D-dimer level was established. ROC curve analysis, 1,000-bootstrap calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were performed to evaluate the discriminative ability, calibration consistency, and clinical net benefit of the model.
RESULTS: Irregular aneurysm morphology (OR = 37.13, 95%CI:7.26-189.75, p < 0.001), elevated white blood cell count (OR = 15.34, 95%CI:2.12-110.94, p < 0.001), and increased D-dimer level (OR = 12.27, 95%CI:2.26-66.70, p < 0.001) were independent biomarkers associated with ruptured IA status. After excluding collinear neutrophil counts, the final combined model achieved an AUC of 0.96. Bootstrap internal validation demonstrated excellent calibration with a mean absolute error of 0.017. DCA verified that the model yielded favorable clinical net benefit within a reasonable threshold probability range.
CONCLUSION: Irregular aneurysm morphology, elevated white blood cell count, and increased D-dimer level at admission are independent biomarkers distinguishing ruptured from unruptured intracranial aneurysms. The multi-index combined model shows good discriminative performance, stable calibration, and promising clinical utility, which can provide objective auxiliary evidence for the rapid identification of aneurysm rupture status in neurosurgical emergency settings.

Title: Cost-Related Medication Underuse and Coping Behaviors in Breast Cancer Survivors Taking Cardiovascular Risk Reduction Medication Enrolled in the National Institutes of Health All of us Research Program.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease throughout survivorship. Recent studies documented suboptimal adherence to cardiovascular risk reduction medications, but studies identifying contributors to this behavior are lacking. The association between sociodemographic characteristics, social drivers of health factors, and cost-related medication behaviors in survivors who were taking antihyperlipidemics or antihypertensives was evaluated.
METHODS: These cross-sectional analyses utilized data from the National Institutes of Health All of Us Research Program from May 31, 2017 to October 1, 2023. Cohort eligibility included identifying as Black/African American or White, being at least 18 years old, and having a diagnosis of breast cancer. The outcome, cost-related medication underuse and coping behaviors, was assessed using a seven-item scale. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate the associations of covariates and the outcome for each of the cardiovascular risk medication classes.
RESULTS: Compared to Black survivors, White survivors had higher odds of asking for lower-cost medications among antihyperlipidemics users (pooled adjusted OR = 1.69; 95% CI: 1.18-2.40; FDR-adjusted p = 0.012) and antihypertensives users (pooled adjusted OR = 2.03; 95% CI: 1.50-2.76; FDR-adjusted p = 0.004). Survivors who reported greater social support were less likely to delay filling their prescription to save money when compared to survivors who reported lower social support.
CONCLUSIONS: Some survivors are more likely to engage in cost-related coping and underuse behaviors than others. Clinicians, including primary care providers, should include discussions and resources about non-cancer therapy adherence-related financial challenges with their patients who are cancer survivors.

Title: Percutaneous tandem modified plastic stenting for post-transplant duct-to-duct biliary anastomotic strictures: long-term outcomes from a single-center cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and long-term outcomes of a percutaneous technique using tandem modified plastic biliary stents (MPBSs) for benign duct-to-duct biliary anastomotic strictures after liver transplantation (LT).
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 48 recipients who underwent treatment between January 2011 and January 2025 after failure or ineligibility for endoscopic therapy. All patients underwent percutaneous placement of two MPBSs through a single transhepatic access. Technical success, symptomatic and biochemical response, procedure-related complications classified according to the Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe system, and patency were evaluated. Patency was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and laboratory parameters were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
RESULTS: Patients' mean age was 33.3 ± 22.0 years. Technical success was achieved in all patients (100%), and symptomatic and biochemical improvement was documented in 46 of 48 patients (95.8%); assessment timing was not standardized. The mean stent indwelling time was 159 ± 42.9 days. Stent migration occurred in 3 patients (6.2%), and cholangitis in 5 patients (10.4%), with no major complications observed. The median primary patency was 1,689 days (95% confidence interval: 311-3,067 days). During follow-up, 29 of 48 patients (60.4%) required at least one additional biliary intervention. Total bilirubin levels decreased after the procedure (3.3 ± 1.9 vs. 0.8 ± 0.5 mg/dL, P < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Percutaneous tandem MPBS placement is a reversible, metal-free salvage option for duct-to-duct biliary anastomotic strictures after LT. However, 60.4% of patients required additional biliary interventions during follow-up, underscoring the substantial reintervention burden associated with this approach. Its comparative efficacy relative to established alternatives, including biodegradable and removable covered metallic stents, remains undetermined.
CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Percutaneous tandem modified plastic biliary stenting is a feasible metal-free salvage option for post-transplant anastomotic strictures when endoscopic treatment fails or is unfeasible. Further studies are needed to establish its efficacy relative to biodegradable and removable covered metallic stents.

Title: Distinct phenotypes associated with the same homozygous ENPP1 c.26dup variant.
Journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ENPP1 pathogenic variants have been associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum, ranging from generalized arterial calcification of infancy to vascular stenoses and autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets.
CASE PRESENTATION: This study presents two cases of cousins who are homozygous for the c.26dup (p.Gly10ArgfsTer67) variant in the ENPP1 gene, but who exhibit distinct clinical features. The first patient developed hypophosphatemic rickets in early childhood. He was subsequently diagnosed with hypertension due to multiple arterial stenoses. In the second case, prenatal monitoring revealed generalized vascular calcification of intrauterine onset. Postnatally, the patient was diagnosed with heart failure, for which medical therapy was initiated, and early parenteral pamidronate was administered. However, the infant died during infancy due to a respiratory infection.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ENPP1 variants may manifest with heterogeneous phenotypes and modifying factors may influence the variant's clinical expression. Case 1 was previously reported with limited clinical information as part of a national Turkish cohort of patients with autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 caused by ENPP1 deficiency. However, as the study was a cohort analysis, it did not comprehensively describe the patient's clinical course, cardiovascular involvement, long-term follow-up, or the intrafamilial phenotypic variability observed within the affected family. Our report contributes to a better understanding of this rare genetic disorder's clinical spectrum and to clarifying the genotype-phenotype correlation.

Title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.
RESULTS: Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

Title: Outcomes after lung transplantation for connective tissue disease-related interstitial lung disease: single center in South Korea.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary involvement is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in connective tissue diseases (CTDs), particularly in the form of CTD-related interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD), and patients with severe CTD-ILD may eventually require lung transplantation (LT). However, post-transplant outcomes specific to CTD-ILD remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult patients who underwent LT for ILD between 2008 and 2025 at a single tertiary center. Patients were classified into CTD-ILD and non-CTD-ILD groups. Clinical and perioperative data were obtained through chart review. Overall survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: A total of 170 patients were included; 39 had CTD-ILD and 131 had non-CTD-ILD. CTD-ILD recipients were more often female (22/39, 56.4% vs. 32/131, 24.4%; P<0.001) and had a numerically higher prevalence of preoperative pulmonary hypertension (7/39, 17.9% vs. 12/131, 9.2%; P=0.094). Overall survival did not differ significantly between the CTD-ILD and non-CTD-ILD groups (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.923; 95% CI, 0.383-2.229; P=0.859; log-rank P=0.334). CTD-ILD recipients had a longer postoperative intensive care unit stay (median [interquartile range], 23.0 days [13.0-35.0] vs. 17.0 days [11.0-28.0]; P=0.026), a longer duration of mechanical ventilation (17.0 days [8.0-32.0] vs. 8.0 days [5.0-18.0]; P=0.009), fewer ventilator-free days (8.0 [0.0-19.0] vs. 11.0 [0.0-22.0]; P=0.002), and a higher incidence of postoperative thromboembolic events (10/39, 25.6% vs. 6/131, 4.6%; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Although survival did not differ significantly in the present study, CTD-ILD recipients had a greater perioperative burden, including higher rates of thromboembolic events and greater use of intensive care resources.

Title: Comparative effects of glucagon-like peptide-1-based regimens on peripheral arterial and limb events in type 2 diabetes: a network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a disabling condition in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet lower-extremity outcomes are rarely prespecified in trials of GLP-1-based therapies. We compared individual GLP-1-based regimens for PAD-related vascular and limb events.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), ProQuest, medRxiv, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO ICTRP from inception through June 3, 2025, and updated the search on July 16, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults with T2DM were eligible. Events from trial reports and registries were harmonized using MedDRA v26.0. Bayesian random-effects network meta-analyses were the primary analyses, frequentist models assessed robustness, and confidence was evaluated with CINeMA. Treatment effects were reported as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs).
RESULTS: Forty-five RCTs involving 110,333 participants were included. For PAOD (33 RCTs; 90,742 participants; 572 events), subcutaneous semaglutide was associated with a lower risk than placebo (RR: 0.37; 95% CrI: 0.14-0.86), with low confidence; the finding was supported by frequentist and sensitivity analyses. In direct placebo-controlled trials, PAOD occurred in 18/4,088 participants receiving subcutaneous semaglutide (4.4 per 1,000) and 33/3,650 receiving placebo (9.0 per 1,000). For PVD (18 RCTs; 69,809 participants; 111 events), albiglutide (RR: 0.11; 95% CrI: 0.01-0.50) and efpeglenatide (RR: 0.09; 95% CrI: 0.01-0.57) were associated with lower risks than placebo, with high confidence for both comparisons. Insulin also showed a favorable Bayesian estimate versus placebo (RR: 0.06; 95% CrI: <0.01-0.49; moderate confidence). No credible Bayesian differences were identified for amputation, necrosis, or peripheral embolism and thrombosis; confidence was predominantly low or very low.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest agent- and outcome-specific signals rather than a class-wide limb benefit. Because events were rare and usually derived from adverse-event reporting, the results do not establish clinical superiority or support treatment selection based on limb protection alone. Dedicated PAD-focused trials with standardized adjudicated outcomes are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251244166.

Title: Hyperinsulinemia and its associations with arterial stiffness and myocardial injury: a real-world cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperinsulinemia is an early metabolic abnormality commonly associated with insulin resistance, but its relationship with cardiovascular injury in real-world populations remains incompletely understood. We examined whether fasting insulin is related to arterial stiffening and early myocardial biomarker abnormalities in a large health-examination population.
METHODS: This real-world retrospective analysis enrolled 30,343 adults who received routine health examinations from January 2017 to November 2021. For individuals with multiple visits, the earliest examination was used as the baseline record. Fasting insulin was evaluated in quartile categories, a log-transformed continuous exposure, and a hyperinsulinemia indicator based on the cohort-specific 75th percentile. The binary arterial-stiffness endpoint was defined using a mean baPWV (brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity) threshold of 1400 cm/s or higher. Myocardial injury was evaluated by cardiac troponin I or T. Logistic regression models were fitted to quantify the relationships of fasting insulin and HOMA-IR (homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance) with baPWV-related outcomes and myocardial injury markers. Dose-response patterns were explored using restricted cubic spline modeling. Subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis were performed. Python (3.13.0) was used for statistical analysis.
RESULTS: Higher insulin categories were accompanied by greater adiposity, blood pressure, glucose, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, baPWV, and arterial-stiffness. Hyperinsulinemia was correlated with arterial stiffness in the unadjusted model and adjusted model (OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.22-1.40, P < 0.001). Compared with the lowest insulin quartile, the highest quartile was associated with markedly increased odds of arterial stiffness (OR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.41-1.74, P < 0.001). Spline curves indicated that fasting insulin and HOMA-IR were positively and non-linearly related to mean baPWV. In contrast, the association between hyperinsulinemia and composite myocardial injury was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large real-world health examination cohort, hyperinsulinemia was independently and consistently associated with increased arterial stiffness. However, its association with subclinical myocardial injury was weaker. These results support fasting insulin as a potential early metabolic indicator of vascular stiffening, whereas its relationship with myocardial injury requires further longitudinal investigation.

Title: Effects of vegetarian or vegan diets on cardiovascular metabolic health in patients with cardiovascular disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vegetarian or vegan diets have been associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in the general population; however, their effects on cardiometabolic risk factors in patients with established cardiovascular disease (CVD) remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of vegetarian or vegan dietary interventions on cardiometabolic risk factors in patients with CVD.
METHODS: A systematic search of five electronic databases was conducted from inception to January 1, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing vegetarian or vegan diets with omnivorous diets in adult patients with CVD were included. Outcomes of interest included systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and triglycerides (TG). Pooled mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models according to heterogeneity. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to explore potential sources of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Six RCTs involving 325 patients with CVD were included. Compared with omnivorous diets, vegetarian or vegan diets were associated with significant reductions in TC [MD = -0.63 mmol/L (95%CI [-1.20, -0.05], P = 0.030)] and LDL-C [MD = -0.56 mmol/L (95%CI [-1.09, -0.02], P = 0.041)], but also with a modest reduction in HDL-C [MD = -0.05 mmol/L (95%CI [-0.10, -0.01], P = 0.023)]. No significant effects were observed on SBP, DBP, or TG levels. Subgroup analyses indicated that low-fat vegan diets, intervention duration, age, and BMI influenced lipid outcomes. Greater reductions in TC were observed in patients aged ≤ 60 years and those with BMI < 30, whereas LDL-C reductions were more pronounced in patients aged ≤ 60 years and those with BMI ≥ 30.
CONCLUSIONS: Vegetarian or vegan diets, particularly low-fat vegan diets, may improve lipid profiles by reducing TC and LDL-C in patients with established CVD. No significant benefits were observed for blood pressure or triglycerides. These findings suggest that plant-based dietary interventions may serve as a complementary strategy for the management of cardiometabolic risk factors in CVD patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol has been registered with PROSPERO under the registration number: CRD420261283606.

Title: Risk factors for post-extubation stridor in pediatric cardiac intensive care unit: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-extubation stridor (PES) is a frequent and clinically significant complication among pediatric cardiac intensive care unit (PCICU) patients, particularly those with congenital heart disease (CHD). This study aimed to determine the incidence, associated risk factors, and outcomes of PES in this population.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included children aged 1 month to 18 years who underwent planned extubation after more than 24 h of mechanical ventilation in the PCICU at Chiang Mai University Hospital between July 2016 and June 2024. Demographic, clinical, and ventilatory variables were retrieved from electronic medical records. Univariable and multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of PES.
RESULTS: Among 494 extubation episodes from 380 children, PES occurred in 25.5% of attempts. Patients who developed PES were younger, low body weight, and had longer ventilation duration compared with those without PES. In multivariable analysis, lower body weight (OR 0.84; 95% CI, 0.73-0.97) and mechanical ventilation exceeding 7 days (OR 1.83; 95% CI, 1.04-3.23) remained significant independent predictors.
CONCLUSIONS: PES was common among pediatric cardiac patients and was independently associated with lower body weight at extubation and prolonged mechanical ventilation. Recognition of children at higher risk may support targeted preventive strategies and improve post-extubation outcomes.

Title: Coronavirus disease 2019 vaccination and reduced severity-related outcomes in high-risk groups in Thailand during the Omicron period.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) booster vaccination, individuals with comorbidities continue to experience disproportionately severe COVID-19 disease and adverse outcomes. Evidence on associations between vaccination status and clinical outcomes among high-risk group during period of Omicron predominance in low- and middle-income countries remains scarce.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Bangkok, Thailand. It aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of COVID-19 infection in high-risk individuals and assess the association between vaccination status and severity-related outcomes, including hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, need for oxygen therapy, and survival at discharge.
RESULTS: Of the 1,379 patients, 1,241 (90.0%) received at least two vaccine doses, mainly AZD1222 for the first 1,105 (87.9%) and second 1,073 (86.5%) doses; BNT162b was the most frequently administered booster with 697 (76.7%) doses. Overall, 725 (52.6%) patients were hospitalized, and 585 (80.7%), 286 (39.4%), and 116 (16%) of whom developed pneumonia, required oxygen therapy, and necessitated ICU admission, respectively. Unvaccinated patients demonstrated higher odds of hospitalization (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 6.9; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.0-11.8; p < 0.001), oxygen therapy (aOR = 6.6; 95% CI: 4.2-10.5; p < 0.001), and ICU admission (aOR = 4.6; 95% CI: 2.5-8.4; p < 0.001). Similarly, patients with 1-2 doses exhibited increased odds of hospitalization (aOR = 3.2; 95% CI: 2.4-4·3; p < 0.001, oxygen therapy (aOR = 2.4; 95% CI: 1.6-3.4; p < 0.001), and ICU admission (aOR = 2.9; 95% CI: 1.7-4.8; p < 0.001) compared with those receiving three doses. Patients with chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease were strongly associated with adverse outcomes and ICU admission.
CONCLUSION: During the Omicron period predominance in Thailand, high-risk patients who received two doses of a viral vector vaccine followed by an mRNA booster remained vulnerable to severe COVID-19 infection; receipt of at least three COVID-19 vaccine doses was associated with significantly lower odds of severe outcomes. These findings highlight the significance of continued vaccination strategies, targeted prevention, and timely clinical management in medically vulnerable populations.

Title: How is the relationship between life style and cardiovascular diseases? A case- control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Considering the high prevalence of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) in most countries of the world and in Iran, lifestyle modification is emphasized as one of the effective factors for the prevention and control of these diseases. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the association between lifestyle and CVDs.
METHODS: This study utilized a case-control design, involving 99 individuals with CVDs such as hypertension, angina, heart attack, coronary artery disease, heart failure, arrhythmia, and valve diseases as the case group. The control group consisted of 396 participants without CVDs, all of whom were patients at Imam Ali and Imam Reza hospitals in Kermanshah in 2023. Inclusion criteria for the case group included a confirmed diagnosis by a physician, ages 18-65, use of at least one cardiac medication, no sensory or cognitive impairments, and the ability to communicate in Farsi or Kurdish. Additionally, participants could not have serious underlying conditions like metastatic cancer or kidney failure, nor could they be hemodynamically unstable. Data collection was conducted through convenience sampling and involved a questionnaire developed by Eshaghi et al., which included 46 questions across five domains: preventive measures, physical activity, nutrition, stress management, and social relationships. Trained interviewers worked with hospital administration to identify eligible participants in inpatient wards. Statistical analyses, including Chi-square tests, independent t-tests, and one-way ANOVA, were performed using Stata software. factors, including age, education, income, job, marital status, knowledge of computer, source of received health information, were adjusted during statistical analysis. The logistic regression model was used to determine the relationship between lifestyle and its dimensions and CVDs with the control of confounding variables, and adjusted odds ratio was reported with a confidence level of 95%.
RESULTS: Based on the results the mean score of lifestyle in CVDs patients was 146.66 ± 23.87 and in the control group was 169.4 ± 25.86 and it means moderate level of lifestyle. There was significant relationship between life style and CVDs, so that with increasing one unit in the mean score of life style, the odds of CVDs significantly decreased by 6% (OR = 0.94, CI: [0.93, 0.96], p < 0.001). Although, a significantly relationship was found between the mean score of each dimention of life style (including prevention, physical activity, sports, …, healthy diet, stress management, social and interpersonal relationships) and CVDs. In other words, with increasing one unit in the mean score of the each dimention of life style, the odds of CVDs significantly decreased by at least 12% (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: According to the correlation between lifestyle and cardiovascular diseases, it is imperative to implement appropriate interventions. The enhancement of nutritional status, social connections, and stress management, alongside social and community-centered interventions to facilitate physical activity and healthy leisure activities, as well as individual coaching to enhance lifestyle, can contribute to the prevention and mitigation of CVDs prevalence. Therefore, it is advisable for policymakers in the health sector to prioritize these aspects in their intervention strategies.

Title: The influence of maternal complications on small for gestational age in very preterm, late preterm and term pregnancies: a Chinese study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to assess the association between single or combined maternal complications and small-for-gestational-age (SGA) birth among very preterm, late preterm, and term births and to evaluate whether this association varied across gestational periods.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 46,829 singleton pregnancies. The maternal complications considered were gestational hypertension (GH), preeclampsia (PE), and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). The potential nonlinear association between gestational age and the risk of SGA birth was assessed using restricted cubic spline analysis. Binary logistic regression models were used to assess the associations between single or combined maternal complications and SGA birth within the very preterm, late preterm, and term groups. Results were reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additionally, effect modification by gestational age was assessed by incorporating interaction terms into the regression models.
RESULTS: Among the 46,829 women with singleton pregnancies, the mean maternal age was 31.7 years (SD, 3.8 years). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear inverse association between gestational age and SGA risk, with the odds of SGA being higher at earlier gestational ages and gradually decreasing toward term. PE showed the strongest association with SGA across all gestational periods, particularly in the very preterm group. In contrast, GDM was associated with lower odds of SGA, although the co-occurrence of PE and GDM was associated with an increased risk of SGA. GH was associated with an increased risk of SGA in the very preterm group (OR = 2.430; 95% CI, 1.156-5.111) but not in the late preterm or term groups. Interaction analysis indicated that the association between maternal complications and SGA weakened with advancing gestational age, with substantially weaker associations observed in term pregnancies.
CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to GDM, PE and GH were associated with an increased risk of SGA, particularly in preterm pregnancies. These findings underscore the importance of early identification, close monitoring, and individualized management of women with PE or GH, particularly among pregnancies resulting in preterm birth.

Title: Real-world hospitalization and readmission trajectory after Guillain-Barré syndrome in the United States.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy associated with substantial morbidity, but contemporary data on post-discharge readmission remain limited. We characterized 90-day readmission timing, causes, associated factors, and procedure coding after GBS.
METHODS: We analyzed an unweighted cohort of adults with a principal diagnosis of GBS in the 2020 Nationwide Readmissions Database. The primary outcome was all-cause readmission within 90 days after discharge. Readmission causes were classified using principal readmission diagnoses mapped to Clinical Classifications Software Refined categories, and procedure coding was descriptively assessed using ICD-10 procedure codes and procedure-day variables. Logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with readmission.
RESULTS: Among 2,587 adults eligible for 90-day follow-up, 364 (14.1%) were readmitted. Readmissions clustered early, with 170 (46.7%) occurring within 15 days and 241 (66.2%) within 30 days. Separately, GBS was the principal diagnosis in 170 of 364 readmissions (46.7%), representing the largest grouped cause followed by septicemia (9.6%) and cardiovascular or thromboembolic conditions (6.9%). In adjusted analyses, discharge disposition was the most consistent marker of readmission risk: compared with routine home discharge, facility discharge was associated with higher odds of 90-day readmission (odds ratio 1.70, 95% confidence interval 1.27-2.28). Procedure-code timing suggested that diagnostic evaluation and immunotherapy were administered early, whereas plasma exchange, tracheostomy, gastrostomy, and rehabilitation-related procedures were performed at later stages.
CONCLUSIONS: Readmission after GBS is frequent, early, and clinically heterogeneous, supporting its interpretation as a marker of residual neurological disability, systemic complications, and care-transition vulnerability rather than recurrent GBS alone.

Title: Acute profound thrombocytopenia associated with glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor after percutaneous coronary intervention: a single-center 6-year case series and therapy insights.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute profound thrombocytopenia is a rare, yet potentially life-threatening complication associated with intravenous glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitors (GPI), which are widely used in the management of acute coronary syndrome and during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Treatments with steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) are recommended for GPI-induced thrombocytopenia; however, evidence regarding their efficacy remains limited.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 21 patients who developed acute profound thrombocytopenia (defined as a platelet count < 20 × 109/L) following PCI and GPI treatment were enrolled. Patients' clinical characteristics, the timing of detection of thrombocytopenia, the administration of steroids and IVIg therapy, and subsequent changes in platelet counts and clinical outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Among the 21 patients, 7 were females, and the median age was 63 years. Tirofiban and eptifibatide were administered to 12 and 9 patients, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was detected on the day of PCI in 9 patients. Among the remaining 12 patients, one was found to have a profound decline in platelets only after the onset of intracerebral hemorrhage and coma, whereas the other 11 patients were diagnosed during routine blood testing on the first day after PCI. The median nadir platelet count was 4 × 109/L among all patients. 11 patients received both steroids and IVIg, 6 received steroids alone, and 4 did not receive any intervention. To evaluate the potential effect of steroids and IVIg therapy on platelet recovery, patients were categorized into three treatment groups: Steroids plus IVIg, steroids alone, and no intervention. No statistical difference was observed among the treatment groups. A separate analysis was performed by categorizing patients according to whether thrombocytopenia was detected on the day of PCI (early detection group) or on the first day after PCI (late detection group). Patients with early diagnosis who underwent prompt GPI withdrawal demonstrated significantly faster platelet recovery. The median time to platelet recovery above 20 × 109/L was significantly shorter in the early detection group (24 h) than in the late detection group (72 h), with a p-value of 0.017.
CONCLUSIONS: GPI-induced thrombocytopenia progresses rapidly following GPI exposure and is marked by an abrupt onset. Timely detection of thrombocytopenia and prompt GPI withdrawal are critical for platelet recovery. In our study, neither steroids nor IVIg improved platelet recovery.

Title: Association between the red blood cell distribution width to albumin ratio and cardiovascular outcomes in MASLD patients: a national cohort study integrating machine learning.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The red blood cell distribution width to albumin ratio (RAR) is a novel biomarker reflecting systemic inflammation and metabolic status. This study investigated the association between RAR and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
METHODS: This cohort study analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). MASLD participants were categorized by RAR levels. Regression models and restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed the relationships of RAR with life's crucial 9 (LC9), cardiovascular disease (CVD), all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 4,419 participants with MASLD were included in our study. Multivariable analysis showed higher RAR was significantly associated with lower LC9 (β = - 3.59, 95% CI: - 4.46 to - 2.73) and with higher odds of prevalent CVD (OR = 1.88, 95% CI: 1.34 to 2.64). Cox regression analysis revealed significant positive associations between RAR and all-cause mortality (HR = 2.13, 95% CI: 1.69 to 2.69) as well as cardiovascular mortality (HR = 3.05, 95% CI: 1.71 to 5.42). Nonlinear relationships were identified between RAR and cardiovascular outcomes. Machine learning revealed RAR as a key determinant of cardiovascular risk in MASLD patients.
CONCLUSION: RAR is a simple and reliable indicator associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes in MASLD patients.

Title: A multimodal Vision-Mamba model based on non-contrast CT hematoma and shell features predicts early hematoma expansion in hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage: a multicenter study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a multimodal Vision-Mamba deep learning (DL) model integrating clinical data, noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) hematoma features, and shell features to predict early hematoma expansion (EHE) in hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (HICH).
METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, a total of 676 patients diagnosed with HICH who received baseline NCCT within 6 hours and subsequent imaging within 24 hours were included. Patients were categorized as EHE-positive and EHE-negative and divided by center into training (n = 361), validation (n = 188), and test (n = 127) sets. Hematoma regions were automatically segmented using No new U-Net (nnU-Net), and a perihematomal shell feature map was derived. Four Vision-Mamba models were constructed: hematoma, shell, hematoma_shell, and Combined model (a combined model integrating hematoma, shell, and clinical data). For comparison, we also constructed conventional DL architectures including DenseNet121, EfficientNet, ResNet18, and Transformer. All baseline comparison models shared an identical structure (hematoma and shell), incorporating clinical feature fusion. The assessment of model performance was conducted through the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), along with DeLong's test, calibration curves, and decision curve analyses.
RESULTS: Within the test set, the AUCs for the hematoma, shell, and hematoma_shell models were recorded as 0.779, 0.812, and 0.832, respectively. The Combined model demonstrated the best performance in predicting EHE, achieving AUCs of 0.966 (95% CI: 0.949-0.980) in the training set, 0.938 (95% CI: 0.902-0.968) in the validation set, and 0.941 (95% CI: 0.899-0.973) in the test set. DeLong's test in the test set (n = 127) confirmed that the Combined model (AUC = 0.941) was significantly superior to all DL baselines: DenseNet121 (AUC = 0.851, p = 0.018), EfficientNet (AUC = 0.769, p < 0.001), ResNet18 (AUC = 0.778, p < 0.001), and Transformer (AUC = 0.804, p < 0.001). Decision curve analysis indicated a higher net benefit than treat-all and treat-none strategies across an observed threshold range of approximately 0.35-0.80.
CONCLUSION: The multimodal Vision-Mamba DL model based on clinical variables, NCCT hematoma features, and shell features showed predictive performance for EHE risk stratification in patients with HICH. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the use of imaging biomarkers for EHE risk assessment.

Title: Magnesium levels and short- to medium-term cardiovascular events after percutaneous coronary intervention: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnesium (Mg) is an essential electrolyte that plays a critical role in cardiovascular physiology. Several studies have investigated the relationship between Mg levels and cardiovascular outcomes; however, the findings have been inconsistent. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the association between serum magnesium levels and short- to medium-term cardiovascular events in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted at the Isfahan Cardiovascular Research Institute, Isfahan, Iran, between October 2018 and September 2023, within the framework of the Persian Cardiovascular Disease Registry. Patients were followed for short-term (1-month and 6-month) and medium-term (12-month) major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after PCI and were categorized into three groups according to their admission serum magnesium levels: < 1.8 mg/dL, 1.8-2.2 mg/dL, and > 2.2 mg/dL.
RESULTS: A total of 3,640 of the 5,300 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of AMI who underwent PCI met the eligibility criteria and were included in the final analysis. The mean age of the study population was 64.70 ± 12.07 years, and 80.3% of participants were male. At the 6-month follow-up, mortality was significantly higher among patients with serum Mg levels > 2.2 mg/dL (odds ratio [OR] = 1.45, P = 0.02). In contrast, at the 12-month follow-up, mortality was significantly higher among patients with serum Mg levels < 1.8 mg/dL (OR = 1.59, P < 0.01). The incidence of MACE was significantly higher among patients with serum Mg levels < 1.8 mg/dL at the 12-month follow-up (OR = 1.61, P < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with AMI undergoing PCI, both hypomagnesemia and hypermagnesemia were associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes during follow-up. Hypomagnesemia was associated with an increased risk of medium-term mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events, whereas hypermagnesemia was associated with increased short-term mortality. These findings suggest a potential U-shaped association between serum magnesium levels and cardiovascular outcomes in this high-risk population. As this was an observational study, these findings reflect associations rather than causal relationships. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these associations before any clinical application is considered.

Title: Front-loaded and mixed delivery models in hybrid cardiac rehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional centre-based cardiac rehabilitation (CBCR) reduces cardiovascular mortality but suffers from suboptimal participation due to logistical barriers. Hybrid cardiac rehabilitation (Hybrid CR) has emerged as a flexible alternative, yet previous reviews have treated it as a monolithic intervention. This study evaluated the comparative effectiveness of Hybrid CR versus CBCR, stratified by delivery model structure: "front-loaded" (initial intensive centre-based block) versus "mixed" (concurrent alternating sessions).
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing Hybrid CR with CBCR. PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, CINAHL, and EMBASE were searched through October 2025. Outcomes included functional capacity (peak exercise oxygen uptake, VO₂peak; metabolic equivalents, METs; 6-minute walk distance), Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL), program attrition, and cardiovascular risk factors. Data were pooled using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs (n = 1,383) met the inclusion criteria. Hybrid CR showed no statistically significant difference compared with CBCR for functional capacity (Hedges' g = 0.13, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.27; p = 0.09). Subgroup analysis showed no statistically significant differences for both front-loaded (g = 0.16) and mixed (g = 0.07) models. Program attrition did not differ significantly between groups (log RR = 0.03, p = 0.44). No significant differences were observed for lipid profiles or blood pressure. While overall HRQoL was similar between hybrid CR and CBCR, a mixed-model subgroup represented by a single study showed lower HRQoL compared with CBCR (g = - 0.86), identifying a potentially important outcome pattern that requires confirmation in additional studies. The certainty of evidence varied by outcome and was high for 6-minute walk distance, low for peak oxygen uptake, and very low for HRQoL and cardiometabolic outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid CR showed functional-capacity outcomes comparable to traditional CBCR, with no statistically significant differences observed between front-loaded and mixed delivery structures. However, certainty of evidence varied across outcomes and was limited for several secondary outcomes, particularly HRQoL and cardiometabolic measures. Further high-quality trials are needed to confirm whether specific hybrid delivery structures offer differential benefits.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251170627.

Title: Association of MTHFR C677T polymorphism with risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although several meta-analyses have examined the association between MTHFR C677T and specific cardiovascular outcomes, a comprehensive evaluation focusing on atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) as a unified outcome, incorporating recently published studies (January 2016-March 2026), remains limited.
METHODS: Potential studies were selected from Embase, Web of Science, and PubMed databases. Pooled effect size was evaluated by odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models where significant heterogeneity was present.
RESULTS: Twenty-three case-control studies (including 6693 patients and 7692 controls) from January 2016 to March 2026 were enrolled in this study. Significant heterogeneity was observed across models (I² > 50%, all phet < 0.001), and random-effects models were applied. MTHFR C677T was positively correlated to ASCVD risk under the dominant model (OR = 1.71, 95%CI = 1.35-2.16), the recessive model (OR = 1.73, 95%CI = 1.35-2.23), and the allelic model (OR = 1.55, 95%CI = 1.30-1.84). Supplementary genotype-specific comparisons also showed significant associations. Subgroup analysis identified a significant correlation in studies of East Asian and North African populations, younger individuals, and healthy controls. The association was significant in coronary artery disease (CAD) and ischemic stroke (IS) patients. Region, age, control type, and disease type are the sources of heterogeneity.
CONCLUSIONS: MTHFR C677T was positively correlated with ASCVD risk across multiple genetic models.

Title: Final Analysis of the BRUIN Phase 1/2 Study Assessing the Safety and Efficacy of Pirtobrutinib Monotherapy in Patients With MCL.
Abstract: Pirtobrutinib, a highly selective, non-covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor (BTKi) previously demonstrated durable efficacy and tolerable safety following covalent (c) BTKi therapy in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). Here, we report final results from the global Phase 1/2 BRUIN trial evaluating pirtobrutinib in patients with R/R MCL, with and without prior cBTKi exposure. Endpoints included overall response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. BRUIN enrolled 166 patients with R/R MCL (data cutoff: 27Jan2025). In the cBTKi-exposed cohort (n = 152), median study follow-up time was 16.1 months (range, 0.5-69.6). The ORR was 49.3% (95% CI, 41.1-57.6). Median DOR was 21.6 months (95% CI, 9.2-27.2). Median PFS was 5.6 months (95% CI, 5.3-9.2; 36-month rate, 19.9%). Median OS was 23.9 months (95% CI, 17.3-51.5; 36-month rate, 43.2%). In the cBTKi-naïve cohort (n = 14), median study follow-up time was 44.5 months (range, 1.6-67.1). The ORR was 85.7% (95% CI, 57.2-98.2). Median DOR was 42.7 months (95% CI, 25.8-not estimable [NE]). Median PFS was 44.6 months (95% CI, 16.7-NE; 36-month rate, 58.7%). Median OS was NE (36-month rate, 76.2%). The most frequent any-grade treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were infections (44.0%), fatigue (31.9%), and diarrhea (22.9%); the most frequent grade ≥ 3 TEAEs were infections (21.1%) and neutropenia (15.1%). Grade ≥ 3 hemorrhage (3.0%) and any-grade atrial fibrillation/flutter (3.6%) were infrequent. With extended follow-up, pirtobrutinib continued to demonstrate efficacy and favorable safety in cBTKi-exposed and -naïve R/R MCL. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03740529.

Title: Reported cardiovascular events and cardiometabolic risk markers with orforglipron and danuglipron in adults with type 2 diabetes or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of orforglipron and danuglipron on cardiovascular events and cardiometabolic risk markers in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and/or obesity.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov through May 5, 2026. Two authors independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. Meta-analyses estimated pooled risk ratios (RRs), least-squares mean differences (LSMDs), and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Thirteen randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 9,076 participants were included. Compared with controls, orforglipron/danuglipron showed no statistically significant difference in extended major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (RR = 1.10, 95% CI [0.59 to 2.05], I² = 0.0%, P = 0.760, 6 studies; intervention: 32/4741, control: 13/1928) or myocardial infarction (MI) (RR = 0.54, 95% CI [0.06 to 4.60], I² = 0.0%, P = 0.576, 2 studies; intervention: 2/881, control: 0/156). Extended MACE and MI were mainly derived from adverse event reports. Given sparse, indirect event data and low GRADE certainty, these findings warrant caution. In contrast, orforglipron and danuglipron reduced several cardiometabolic risk markers, including HbA1c (LSMD = - 1.07%, 95% CI [- 1.49 to - 0.64], I² = 99.1%, P < 0.001), fasting plasma glucose (LSMD = - 27.75 mg/dL, 95% CI [- 37.99 to - 17.50], I² = 98.2%, P < 0.001), and body weight (LSMD = - 4.68 kg, 95% CI [- 6.26 to - 3.10], I² = 95.4%, P < 0.001). These estimates showed substantial between-study heterogeneity, warranting cautious interpretation. Current randomized evidence supports changes in cardiometabolic risk markers, but uncertainty remains regarding the effects on hard cardiovascular events.
CONCLUSIONS: Current randomized evidence suggests that orforglipron and danuglipron reduce short- to medium-term cardiometabolic risk markers in patients with T2DM or obesity. However, no significant differences in extended MACE or MI were observed; the point estimates were imprecise, and cardiovascular effects remain unconfirmed. These findings are limited by sparse events, low-certainty evidence, and the lack of dedicated cardiovascular outcome trial (CVOT) designs; therefore, definitive conclusions regarding cardiovascular effects cannot be drawn.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was pre-registered and published on PROSPERO (CRD420251067874; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/ ).

Title: Assessing the prevalence of risk factors not included in the EuroSCORE II and their impact on hospital benchmarking in cardiac surgery: using the Netherlands Heart Registration as an example.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Quality registries often use risk-adjusted benchmarking of mortality to assess hospital performance. The Netherlands Heart Registration (NHR) uses the EuroSCOREII to adjust for hospital differences. However, EuroSCOREII does not include all risk factors that increase mortality risk. Suboptimal benchmarking may have significant negative consequences for all stakeholders. This study aims to assess risk factors not included in EuroSCOREII and their impact on risk-adjusted benchmarking in the Netherlands.
METHODS: This retrospective nationwide cohort study used data from the NHR. Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting and/or surgical aortic valve replacement were included. Patients with surgical mortality were assessed for any additional risk factor not included in the EuroSCOREII by a cardiothoracic surgeon and marked as additional high-risk or not. Risk-adjusted benchmarking was performed using EuroSCOREII. The influence of additional high-risk on benchmarking was assessed through exclusion of additional high-risk patients and through correction for additional high-risk.
RESULTS: 8,480 patients were included of which 156 died within 30-days, 60 out of 156 (38.5%) patients with surgical mortality were classified as additional high-risk. Most frequently mentioned non-cardiac risk factor was high body mass index, cardiac risk factors were ongoing acute myocardial infarction, porcelain aorta and previous unsuccessful revascularization. Both exclusion and correction for additional high-risk led to altered benchmarking positions of hospitals, both improving and degrading hospital rankings.
CONCLUSION: 38.5% of patients suffer from risk factors not covered in EuroSCOREII, including cardiac, non-cardiac and life-style factors. Including these factors as additional high-risk in the benchmarking process alters the hospital benchmarking positions, indicating that this process may be improved.

Title: Associations of cumulative exposure and dynamic trajectories of the combined estimated glucose disposal rate and frailty index with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity comprising diabetes, heart disease, and stroke: a longitudinal analysis based on the China health and retirement longitudinal study (CHARLS).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), encompassing the co-occurrence of major cardiometabolic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, is a growing clinical and public-health challenge associated with adverse functional outcomes and high long-term care needs. Insulin resistance and frailty are plausible, potentially interrelated determinants of CMM, including cerebrovascular complications, but their joint longitudinal contribution has not been fully characterized. We investigated whether estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR), frailty index (FI), and FI-to-eGDR ratio (FI/eGDR), assessed as baseline values, time-weighted cumulative exposure, and two-wave repeated-exposure patterns, were associated with incident CMM.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 5171 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study who were free of CMM at baseline. Baseline eGDR, FI, and FI/eGDR were evaluated as standardized continuous variables and tertiles. Time-weighted cumulative exposures were calculated from Wave 1 and Wave 3 values, and two-wave repeated-exposure patterns were identified using K-means clustering. Cox regression models with sequential covariate adjustment were used to estimate associations with incident CMM, with diabetes, heart disease, and stroke incorporated as components of the cardiometabolic disease burden within the outcome framework. Restricted cubic splines, exploratory subgroup analyses, conventional receiver operating characteristic and decision curve analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed. A Wave 3 landmark cohort included 5052 participants who remained free of CMM through Wave 3.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 441 participants developed CMM. In fully adjusted models, per-SD increases in baseline eGDR, FI, and FI/eGDR were associated with HRs of 0.57 (95% CI, 0.51-0.64), 1.29 (95% CI, 1.19-1.40), and 1.39 (95% CI, 1.29-1.48), respectively; corresponding HRs for cumulative measures were 0.52 (95% CI, 0.46-0.59), 1.51 (95% CI, 1.40-1.64), and 1.52 (95% CI, 1.43-1.60). Compared with T1, the fully adjusted HR for T3 of cumulative FI/eGDR was 6.52 (95% CI, 4.55-9.35). Compared with FI/eGDR repeated-exposure pattern class 1, HRs were 3.87 (95% CI, 3.03-4.93) for class 2 and 9.45 (95% CI, 6.95-12.86) for class 3. In the Wave 3 landmark cohort, FI/eGDR pattern class 2 and class 3 remained associated with higher risk (HR, 3.45 [95% CI, 2.62-4.54] and 6.38 [95% CI, 4.39-9.27], respectively). Spline analyses supported nonlinear associations. Cumulative FI/eGDR had the highest observed AUC among individual measures (0.742; 95% CI, 0.718-0.766), whereas the cumulative FI plus eGDR model had an AUC of 0.758 (95% CI, 0.735-0.781); in the landmark analysis, the corresponding AUCs were 0.731 (95% CI, 0.704-0.759) and 0.740 (95% CI, 0.714-0.767), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower eGDR, higher FI, and higher FI/eGDR were associated with incident CMM after multivariable adjustment. Cumulative and repeated-exposure pattern analyses provided complementary information beyond a single baseline measurement. Longitudinal integration of metabolic insulin-resistance and frailty measures may help characterize adults at increased risk of CMM, although the exploratory discrimination results require internal and external validation before any clinical application.

Title: Stress-hyperglycemia ratio, frailty index, and their product in relation to incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity comprising diabetes, heart disease, and stroke: a longitudinal analysis of CHARLS.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), encompassing the co-occurrence of major cardiometabolic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, is a major source of disability and premature mortality in ageing populations. The stress-hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) captures glycemic dysregulation relative to long-term glycemic exposure, whereas the frailty index (FI) quantifies accumulated health deficits. We evaluated whether SHR, FI, and their composite product (SHR-FI), assessed at baseline and across two survey waves, were associated with incident CMM.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis of 6,096 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study who were free of CMM at baseline. SHR, FI, and SHR-FI were assessed at Waves 1 and 3. Time-weighted two-wave summaries and data-derived two-time-point longitudinal patterns were evaluated; cumulative and pattern analyses used Wave 3 as a landmark. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Restricted cubic spline, subgroup, receiver operating characteristic, decision-curve, joint-model, landmark, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During the Wave 1-anchored follow-up, 527 participants developed CMM. In fully adjusted models, each SD increase in baseline SHR, FI, and SHR-FI was associated with HRs of 1.09 (95% CI, 1.01-1.18), 1.36 (1.26-1.48), and 1.35 (1.26-1.45), respectively. Associations were stronger for cumulative FI and cumulative SHR-FI: the HRs per SD increase were 1.60 (1.48-1.73) and 1.55 (1.44-1.66). The AUCs were 0.68 for baseline FI and SHR-FI and 0.72 and 0.73 for cumulative FI and SHR-FI, respectively. FI accounted for most of the observed discrimination, while SHR-FI showed a modest complementary signal. Landmark analyses beginning at Wave 3 produced directionally consistent cumulative FI and SHR-FI associations.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher SHR, greater FI, and a higher SHR-FI product were associated with incident CMM. FI provided most of the observed discrimination, and SHR-FI offered limited additional information in this cohort. Two-wave cumulative summaries and longitudinal patterns may support research-oriented risk stratification, but their clinical value requires calibration, internal validation, and external validation.

Title: The effect of social support on physical activity of hemodialysis patients : the chain mediating role of exercise self-efficacy and barriers to exercise benefits.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maintenance hemodialysis patients exhibit low physical activity, which is associated with sarcopenia, increased risk of cardiovascular events, and elevated all-cause mortality. Social support is an important resource for promoting healthy behaviors. But the mechanisms of influencing these patients' intrinsic psychological processes to raise physical activity levels are unclear.
METHODS: This study was a cross-sectional observational study from September 2021 to February 2022, enrolling 460 hemodialysis patients from four tertiary hospitals in Xi'an City. We assessed social support, exercise self-efficacy, and exercise benefits and barriers perceptions with the Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS), the Self-Efficacy for Exercise Scale (SEE), and the Dialysis Patient-perceived Exercise Benefits and Barriers Scale (DPEBBS) respectively. Daily total step count was measured using an Omron electronic pedometer (model HJ-321) worn continuously for seven days.
