Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and chain mediation analysis using the PROCESS macro developed by Hayes (Model 6) were performed; the significance of mediation effects was tested via bootstrapping.
RESULTS: Pearson correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations among social support, exercise self-efficacy, perceived exercise benefits and barriers, and total daily steps (r = 0.289-0.507; all P < 0.01). Chain mediation model analysis indicated social support's total effect on daily steps was 0.289. Specific mediation pathways included: (1) social support → exercise self-efficacy → total daily steps; (2) social support → perceived barriers to exercise benefits → total daily steps; (3) social support → exercise self-efficacy → perceived barriers to exercise benefits → total daily steps. Significant positive correlations were observed among social support, exercise self-efficacy, perceived exercise benefits and barriers, and total daily steps (all P < 0.01). Chain mediation analysis revealed that social support's total effect on daily steps was 0.289 (95% CI: 0.201-0.377). Three significant mediation pathways were identified: social support → exercise self-efficacy → daily steps; social support → perceived barriers to exercise benefits → daily steps; and the chain mediation pathway social support → exercise self-efficacy → perceived barriers to exercise benefits → daily steps.
CONCLUSION: Social support not only directly and positively influences physical activity levels among patients undergoing hemodialysis but also indirectly promotes physical activity by enhancing exercise self-efficacy and improving perceptions of barriers to exercise benefits. A chain mediation pathway "social support → exercise self-efficacy → perception of barriers to exercise benefits → physical activity "was identified.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of Xi'an Jiaotong University (approval number: 20211575).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Estimated glucose disposal rate outperforms other insulin resistance surrogate indices in predicting cardiometabolic disease and major adverse cardiovascular events in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: insights from UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has rapidly evolved into a pressing global health issue, exacting a formidable and escalating toll on public disease burden. Insulin resistance (IR) serves as a shared pathophysiological pathway for MASLD and cardiometabolic dysfunction. However, the associations between IR surrogate indices, cardiometabolic disease (CMD) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in MASLD, particularly the comparative predictive performance of these indicators, have yet to be fully elucidated.
METHODS: This large-scale prospective study incorporated 127,195 and 149,402 individuals with MASLD from UK Biobank in CMD and MACE cohort, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis was employed to estimate CMD and MACE risks across different IR indices quartiles. Cox regression model and restricted cubic splines (RCS) curve were performed to investigate the associations between IR-related indices, CMD and MACE in MASLD, with threshold effect analysis detecting potential inflection points upon observed nonlinear relationships. Additionally, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Harrell's C-index, along with net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), were utilized to compare the predictive capability of estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) and other IR indices. Furthermore, subgroup and sensitivity analysis were conducted to validate the robustness of primary findings.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up time of 13.67 and 13.92 years, 29,089 CMD (22.87%) and 15,445 (10.34%) MACE occurred, respectively. Kaplan-Meier curves indicated the risks of CMD and MACE increased progressively in parallel with descending eGDR quartiles (log-rank test, P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, eGDR was significantly associated with incident CMD (per 1 SD, HR = 0.70, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.69-0.72) and MACE (per 1 SD, HR = 0.82, 95% CI 0.80-0.84), which held true across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. RCS analysis revealed the nonlinear associations between eGDR, CMD and MACE, while turning points were identified at 5.377 and 5.215. Notably, eGDR outperformed other IR surrogate indices in predictions for CMD and MACE overall, as corroborated by all evaluation metrics (AUC, Harrell's C-index, NRI and IDI).
CONCLUSIONS: eGDR demonstrated significant relationships with CMD and MACE in MASLD, yielding comparatively better predictive performance across diverse IR surrogate indices, which suggested its potential clinical utility.

Title: New ESC/EACTS guidelines for the management of aortic valve disease: key takeaways and implications of long-term TAVR results based on recent explant and redo-TAVR registry outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines for valvular heart disease represent a pivotal update, emphasizing earlier intervention for aortic stenosis (AS) and broader indications for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). These changes are driven by randomized trial data demonstrating TAVR's safety in lower-risk patients. However, as TAVR expands to younger cohorts, long-term durability remains a concern.
MAIN BODY: This narrative review examines key guideline updates for aortic valve disease, focusing on aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), and integrates insights from recent registries (2020-2025) on TAVR explantation and redo-TAVR outcomes. Data from the EXPLANT-TAVR, EXPLANTORREDO-TAVR and FRANCE 2/FRANCE TAVI registries reveal reintervention rates of 0.3-1.7% at 8 years, with redo-TAVR offering superior short-term survival (30-day mortality 1.5-6.2%) compared to explantation (11.9-13.6%). Structural valve deterioration (SVD), leaflet thrombosis, and endocarditis predominate failure causes, underscoring the need for lifetime management strategies.
CONCLUSION: Implications include refined patient selection, enhanced imaging surveillance, and Heart Team-driven decisions to balance procedural benefits against reintervention risks.

Title: Effect of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential on long-term survival in patients with arrhythmias.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential(CHIP), defined by somatic mutations within hematopoietic clones, has emerged as a novel risk factor for cardiovascular disease. While cardiac arrhythmias are a major global health concern, the factors contributing to outcome variability remain unclear. The study aimed to investigate the association between CHIP and mortality in patients with arrhythmias.
METHODS: This study analyzed UK Biobank participants hospitalized with arrhythmias who had whole-exome sequencing data. Arrhythmia subtypes were classified using ICD-10 codes. Outcomes, including all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer-related mortality, were obtained from national registries. CHIP was defined as any CHIP as variant allele fraction(VAF) ≥ 2%, large CHIP as VAF ≥ 10%. Cox regression models adjusted for confounders were used.
RESULTS: Among 53,149 individuals (median age 69 years), 3,315 carried CHIP mutations. Both any and large CHIP were independently associated with higher mortality: adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality were 1.26 (1.19-1.34) and 1.44 (1.33-1.55), respectively; for cardiovascular mortality, 1.14 (1.02-1.27) and 1.31 (1.14-1.52); and for cancer-related mortality, 1.36 (1.23-1.51) and 1.65 (1.45-1.87). Associations persisted across arrhythmia subtypes, with the strongest effects in ventricular arrhythmias. In gene-specific analyses, TET2, TP53 and spliceosome genes appeared to be the strongest deleterious genes for all-cause mortality [large TET2 CHIP: HR 1.63 (1.40-1.90); large TP53 CHIP: 1.83 (1.18-2.84); large spliceosome CHIP: HR 1.85 (1.32-2.59)].
CONCLUSIONS: CHIP is independently associated with increased mortality in patients with arrhythmias across different subtypes. These findings suggest that CHIP may serve as a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic target.

Title: Cost-effectiveness of statin-based primary prevention of cardiovascular disease with electronic pillboxes for people with HIV in China.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading non-AIDS cause of death among people with HIV (PWH). Although statins reduce CVD risk by over one-third, poor adherence limits real-world effectiveness. Electronic pillboxes may bridge this gap, but their cost-effectiveness for CVD primary prevention in PWH remains unclear.
METHODS: We developed a Markov cohort model simulating 100,000 Chinese PWH (aged 40-75 years) over a lifetime horizon from a healthcare system perspective. Strategies varied by CVD screening frequency (every 6/12/24 months), lipid-lowering regimens (pitavastatin alone, or combined with ezetimibe or PCSK9 inhibitor), and electronic pillbox adherence support for high-risk individuals. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were calculated as cost per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained versus status quo at willingness-to-pay thresholds of 1 × and 3 × GDP per capita ($13,445 and $40,335) in China.
RESULTS: Risk-stratified screening every 24 months with pitavastatin alone (without pillboxes) was optimal at 1×GDP per capita (ICER $8,269/QALY), averting 4,298 major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and gaining 28,570 QALYs versus status quo. At 3×GDP per capita, 6-monthly screening with risk-tailored therapy (pitavastatin ± ezetimibe) plus electronic pillboxes was optimal (ICER $16,799/QALY), averting 10,169 MACE and gaining 59,125 QALYs. Statin adherence and ezetimibe cost were key drivers of cost-effectiveness.
CONCLUSIONS: Risk-stratified CVD prevention integrating periodic screening and tailored pharmacotherapy is cost-effective for PWH in China. Electronic pillboxes become cost-effective when greater healthcare investment is available, supporting a threshold-dependent approach to translating statin efficacy into population-level impact.

Title: Reducing pre-operative delays in urgent cardiac surgery: evidence for waiting-time effect on post-operative length of stay.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: According to the National Institute of Cardiovascular Outcomes Research (NICOR) report in 2022, the mean waiting time for urgent coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery in the United Kingdom is 10 days, rather than the recommended 7 days. We conducted a service evaluation of the acute cardiac pathway in our hospital.
METHODS: All patients who received cardiac surgery in 2022 were considered. 611 patients had cardiac surgery; 585 had elective or acute cardiac surgery; 580 had complete data for analysis. Data were reported in counts and percentages. We determined the associations between pre-operative length of stay and post-operative outcomes using negative binomial analysis. Fine-Gray model was used to address survival bias.
RESULTS: Median pre-operative LOS for urgent patients referred directly to CHH was 12 days (IQR 8.0-16.5, p < 0.001). Each additional pre-operative day were associated with an increase of stay (LOS) by 3.2%. Sensitivity analysis on the pre-operative LOS rate ratio shows that this effect is purely confined to the urgent population; RR 1.030, p < 0.001 and absent in elective patients; RR 0.976, p 0.3966. The effect is enhanced in patients presenting to Castle Hill Hospital (CHH) directly as we were able to capture the full duration of their in-hospital LOS; RR 1.035, p < 0.001. Other factors that impact post-operative LOS were presenting ejection fraction (EF), type of surgery and age.
CONCLUSION: Pre-operative LOS was independently associated with prolonged post-operative stay. This effect is confined to the urgent population supporting a service improvement focus on reducing in-hospital delays for the urgent pathway.

Title: Effects of Acepromazine-Xylazine-Ketamine combination on physiological and clinical parameters in somali goats (Capra hircus).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Somaliland, veterinary surgical interventions are often constrained by the lack of inhalation anesthesia. Total Intravenous Anesthesia (TIVA) offers a portable alternative. This study evaluated the physiological and clinical effects of an Acepromazine (ACP), Xylazine (XY), and Ketamine (KT) protocol in Somali goats, a breed adapted to arid environments.
METHODS: Twelve healthy Somali goats (9 females, 3 males; 15-25 kg) were used in a prospective study. Animals were premedicated with Xylazine (0.1 mg/kg) and Acepromazine (0.05 mg/kg) intravenously (IV), followed 10 min later by Ketamine (4 mg/kg) IV. Heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), and rectal temperature (RT) were monitored at 10-minute intervals. Clinical parameters (pedal, corneal, jaw, and tongue reflexes) were assessed for duration of suppression.
RESULTS: HR and RT showed gradual, non-significant declines (P > 0.05). RR exhibited significant variation (P = 0.034), with a transient increase at 10 and 20 min. Duration of pedal reflex suppression was 20.7 ± 0.7 min. Ptyalism (hypersalivation) was observed in 75% of subjects, and labored breathing in 50%.
CONCLUSIONS: The ACP-XY-KT combination provides approximately 20 min of surgical recumbency. While cardiovascular trends remained stable, ptyalism and respiratory shifts necessitate vigilant airway management.

Title: Joint association of five insulin resistance indices and frailty index with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity in individuals with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance and frailty are closely related to cardiometabolic deterioration, yet their joint contribution to the development of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) among individuals with early-to-intermediate cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. This study examined the associations of five insulin resistance-frailty composite indices and the joint status of insulin resistance indices and frailty index with incident CMM in Chinese middle-aged and older adults with CKM stages 0-3.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 6023 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study who had CKM stages 0-3 and were free of CMM at baseline. Insulin resistance was assessed using the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index (CTI), cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose index (CHG), stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), and estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR). Frailty was evaluated using a 32-item frailty index (FI). Composite indices included TyG-FI, CTI-FI, CHG-FI, SHR-FI, and eGDR/FI. Participants were also cross-classified into joint exposure groups according to baseline median-derived cutoff values of each insulin resistance index and FI. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Restricted cubic spline, subgroup, additive interaction, ROC, decision curve, NRI, IDI, and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 9.0 years, 399 participants developed incident CMM. In fully adjusted models, each 1-SD increment in TyG-FI, CTI-FI, CHG-FI, and SHR-FI was associated with a 29%, 30%, 31%, and 27% higher risk of incident CMM, respectively (TyG-FI: HR 1.29, 95% CI 1.18-1.41; CTI-FI: HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.19-1.41; CHG-FI: HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.20-1.43; SHR-FI: HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.17-1.39). Conversely, each 1-SD increment in eGDR/FI was associated with a 39% lower CMM risk (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.48-0.78). Restricted cubic spline analyses showed significant nonlinear dose-response relationships. The threshold points were 1.18 for TyG-FI, 1.17 for CTI-FI, 0.87 for CHG-FI, 0.13 for SHR-FI, and 337.74 for eGDR/FI; risks increased with higher TyG-FI, CTI-FI, CHG-FI, and SHR-FI, particularly before the thresholds, whereas CMM risk declined as eGDR/FI increased and then tended to plateau. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartiles of TyG-FI, CTI-FI, CHG-FI, and SHR-FI were associated with markedly higher risks of incident CMM, whereas the highest quartile of eGDR/FI was associated with lower risk. Joint analyses showed that participants with both high insulin resistance indices and high FI had the greatest CMM risk, particularly for CHG and FI (HR 6.47, 95% CI 4.15-10.10) and CTI and FI (HR 6.27, 95% CI 4.01-9.81). Adding FI increased the AUCs of the TyG, CTI, CHG, SHR, and eGDR models from 0.668 to 0.708, 0.683 to 0.718, 0.709 to 0.742, 0.547 to 0.654, and 0.702 to 0.723, respectively. NRI estimates ranged from 3.89 to 16.01% and IDI estimates from 0.73 to 1.40%, with all corresponding P values < 0.01; decision curve analyses generally showed greater or comparable standardized net benefit for the IR-plus-FI models. Additive interaction analysis showed a positive additive interaction between CHG and FI, with a relative excess risk due to interaction of 1.47 (95% CI 0.08-2.87) and an attributable proportion of 0.23 (95% CI 0.03-0.42).
CONCLUSION: Among Chinese middle-aged and older adults with CKM stages 0-3, insulin resistance-frailty composite indices were independently associated with incident CMM. Joint analyses revealed that individuals with concurrent insulin resistance and greater frailty exhibited the highest risk, suggesting that metabolic dysfunction combined with frailty constitutes a high‑risk CKM phenotype predisposed to progression toward CMM. Adding FI improved the exploratory discrimination and decision-analytic performance of individual insulin-resistance indices. These findings support the integrated assessment of insulin resistance and frailty for early‑stage risk stratification and prevention of CMM among individuals within the CKM spectrum.

Title: Fatty liver index-defined hepatic steatosis and impaired fasting glucose differentially associate with incident diabetes and cardiovascular events in older adults: a nationwide cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis and prediabetes are increasingly prevalent among older adults; however, their respective impacts on cardiometabolic outcomes remain unclear. We aimed to evaluate the associations of hepatic steatosis and prediabetes with incident diabetes and cardiovascular outcomes in this population.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study included 142,518 adults aged ≥ 65 years without diabetes. Hepatic steatosis was defined using the fatty liver index (FLI ≥ 60), and impaired fasting glucose (IFG) was defined by fasting glucose levels of 100-125 mg/dL. Outcomes included incident diabetes and composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death, which were analyzed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models.
RESULTS: At baseline, FLI-defined hepatic steatosis was identified in 6.6% of participants, while 30.6% had IFG. After multivariable adjustment, FLI-defined hepatic steatosis was associated with incident diabetes (SHR 1.67; 95% CI 1.59-1.76; P < 0.001) and composite MACE (SHR 1.21; 95% CI 1.15-1.29; P < 0.001). IFG was associated with an increased risk of incident diabetes (SHR 2.54; 95% CI 2.47-2.62; P < 0.001) but was not independently associated with composite MACE. In joint analyses, FLI-defined hepatic steatosis was consistently associated with an elevated risk of composite MACE regardless of glycemic status, with SHRs of 1.23 (95% CI 1.14-1.32; P < 0.001) among normoglycemic individuals and 1.20 (95% CI 1.11-1.31; P < 0.001) among those with IFG. In contrast, IFG without FLI-defined hepatic steatosis was not associated with an increased risk of composite MACE compared with normoglycemic individuals without FLI-defined hepatic steatosis.
CONCLUSION: In older adults, FLI-defined hepatic steatosis is a strong predictor of both incident diabetes and cardiovascular events, whereas IFG shows no independent association with cardiovascular outcomes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable (retrospectively registered).

Title: Assessment of end-tidal CO₂ levels in the diagnosis and management of patients with pulmonary embolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a life-threatening emergency associated with acute cardiopulmonary deterioration. This study evaluated the clinical utility of end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO₂) for assessing disease severity and monitoring treatment response in high- and intermediate-high-risk PE.
METHODS: This prospective study (registry ID: NCT07241130) included 120 individuals presenting between February and July 2025, categorized into four groups: high-risk PE with thrombolysis, intermediate-high-risk PE with thrombolysis, intermediate-high-risk PE without thrombolysis, and healthy controls. Physiological parameters were measured using the Rad-97 monitor under standardized conditions.
RESULTS: Baseline EtCO₂ levels differed significantly among the groups (p < 0.001). The lowest mean EtCO₂ value was observed in the high-risk PE group (15.2 ± 1.9 mmHg) and the highest in the control group (31.8 ± 3.1 mmHg). After 24 h of treatment, there were no significant differences among the groups in terms of EtCO₂, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂), or perfusion index (PI) values (p > 0.05). EtCO₂ was negatively correlated with pulmonary artery obstruction index (r = - 0.358, p = 0.01) and positively correlated with SpO₂ (r = 0.594, p < 0.001) and PI (r = 0.431, p < 0.001). ROC analysis identified an optimum EtCO₂ cutoff of 17.5 mmHg to discriminate between patients with and without thrombolytic therapy (97% sensitivity, 85% specificity).
CONCLUSION: EtCO₂ is a simple, noninvasive physiological marker associated with thrombus burden and treatment-related changes in PE. Rather than determining therapeutic decisions, EtCO₂ may complement established clinical and imaging parameters by providing supportive physiological information in acute settings.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07241130. Retrospectively registered.

Title: Cardiovascular effects of methylphenidate, risperidone, and their combination in children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a prospective 3-month observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to evaluate changes in hemodynamic parameters and electrocardiographic (ECG) indices related to ventricular arrhythmia risk after three months of treatment with methylphenidate (MPH), risperidone (RIS), or their combination in children and adolescents with ADHD.
METHODS: A total of 150 children and adolescents with DSM-5-diagnosed ADHD were prospectively enrolled at Qods Hospital. Participants received methylphenidate (n = 50), risperidone (n = 50), or combination therapy (n = 50). Cardiovascular outcomes were assessed using age- and weight-adjusted two-way repeated-measures ANCOVA to evaluate changes over time and differences among treatment groups.
RESULTS: Significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate, and QTc interval after adjustment for baseline age and weight. After three months, systolic and diastolic blood pressure increased in the methylphenidate and combination therapy groups, while heart rate showed an overall increase, with the greatest rise observed in the methylphenidate group. QTc interval increased over time across all treatment groups, with the largest prolongation observed in the combination therapy group (377.9 ± 25.4 to 424.5 ± 24.9 ms). However, mean QTc values remained below commonly accepted thresholds for clinically significant QT prolongation, and no significant longitudinal changes were observed in QRS duration or PR intervals.
CONCLUSION: Treatment with methylphenidate, risperidone, and combination therapy was associated with modest changes in heart rate, blood pressure, and QTc interval over three months. These findings highlight the importance of baseline and follow-up cardiovascular monitoring in children and adolescents receiving ADHD medications.

Title: Biomarker-dependent detection of contrast-associated acute kidney injury after intra-arterial contrast procedures: an exploratory randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) remains a controversial clinical entity, partly because incidence estimates vary according to the diagnostic criteria and biomarkers used. Serum creatinine-based definitions may underestimate early functional renal impairment after contrast exposure, whereas cystatin C has emerged as a more sensitive early biomarker of glomerular filtration changes. This study aimed to evaluate how biomarker selection influences CA-AKI detection and interpretation of preventive strategies after intra-arterial contrast procedures.
METHODS: This prospective, randomized, single-blind exploratory trial included 76 patients with peripheral arterial disease undergoing elective intra-arterial contrast-enhanced vascular procedures, most of which were diagnostic angiographic examinations. Participants were stratified according to baseline renal function and randomized to receive either standardized hydration alone or hydration plus high-dose atorvastatin and N-acetylcysteine. CA-AKI was assessed using two predefined definitions: historical creatinine-based criteria (≥ 25% or ≥ 0.5 mg/dL increase within 72 h) and cystatin C-based criteria (≥ 10% increase within 24 h). Diagnostic concordance and biomarker-dependent differences in event ascertainment were evaluated.
RESULTS: Substantial diagnostic discordance was observed between creatinine- and cystatin C-defined CA-AKI, with no overlapping cases and poor agreement between biomarkers (κ = 0.07). Creatinine-based criteria identified 4 CA-AKI events, whereas cystatin C identified 7 additional early functional injury cases. Biomarker-dependent differences in event detection varied across renal function strata, particularly among patients with preserved baseline renal function. Low event rates using creatinine-based criteria limited definitive assessment of preventive efficacy. Exploratory analyses suggested that biomarker selection influenced the apparent magnitude and direction of treatment-effect estimates.
CONCLUSIONS: CA-AKI ascertainment after intra-arterial contrast exposure is strongly biomarker-dependent. Historical creatinine-based definitions may underestimate early functional renal impairment and influence interpretation of preventive strategies. These findings highlight the importance of endpoint selection in CA-AKI clinical trials and support further investigation of sensitive functional biomarkers in larger prospective studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC), RBR3h2gv8r (Universal Trial Number U1111-1277-3145), registered on 31 March 2023 retrospectively registered.

Title: Assessment of intravenous thrombolytic therapy response in acute ischemic stroke using NIHSS changes and laboratory parameters.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ischemic stroke is one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in adults. Although intravenous thrombolytic therapy (IVTT) can improve neurological recovery in appropriate patients, the treatment response shows variability among individuals. Although the NIHSS score is widely used to monitor clinical response, it should be evaluated together with laboratory parameters to more accurately predict prognosis. In this study, the relationship between NIHSS score change and laboratory parameters in acute ischemic stroke patients treated with IVTT was investigated.
METHODS: Thirty-three acute ischemic stroke patients who presented to the emergency department in 2024 and received IVTT were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline and 24-hour NIHSS scores were recorded. Hemogram and biochemical parameters were analyzed. Clinical response was defined as a ≥ 4-point reduction in NIHSS score at 24 h after IVTT, and its associations with mortality and hemorrhagic complications were statistically evaluated.
RESULTS: Three-month mortality was 15.2%, and the hemorrhage rate was 9.1%. Platelet levels were found to be significantly lower in patients who died. The second NIHSS score was significantly associated with mortality and hemorrhage. Serum calcium and basophil levels were associated with clinical improvement. In ROC analysis, basophil showed a relatively higher discriminative ability than calcium in predicting clinical improvement; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and the exploratory nature of the analysis.

Title: A novel distal radial artery compression device versus elastic bandage compression after coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention via distal transradial access: a prospective randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal transradial artery access (dTRA) is increasingly used for coronary interventions because it preserves proximal radial artery patency. However, effective hemostasis at the distal puncture site remains challenging due to the superficial vessel location and limited soft-tissue support. This study evaluated the hemostatic performance, local safety, patient-reported outcomes, and early radial artery patency of a novel distal radial artery compression device compared with conventional elastic bandage compression.
METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 148 patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) via dTRA were randomized (1:1) to device-based or conventional compression. The primary outcome was first-attempt hemostasis success after compression release. Secondary outcomes included total hemostasis duration, operation time, access-site complications, pain, comfort, and ultrasound-assessed radial artery outcomes.
RESULTS: First-attempt hemostasis success was achieved in 74 patients (100.0%) in the device group and 70 patients (94.6%) in the elastic bandage group. Compared with elastic bandage compression, the novel device significantly shortened total hemostasis duration and operation time (both P < 0.001). Postoperative hand swelling was significantly less frequent and less severe in the device group (P < 0.001), while bleeding or hematoma formation was descriptively less frequent. No radial artery occlusion was detected by Doppler ultrasound before discharge in either group. Overall repeated-measures analysis showed no significant group effect or group-by-time interaction for pain or comfort scores.
CONCLUSIONS: The novel dTRA compression device achieved a high first-attempt hemostasis success rate and significantly shortened operation time and total hemostasis duration compared with conventional elastic bandage compression after CAG or PCI via dTRA. The device was associated with less postoperative hand swelling, while bleeding or hematoma formation was infrequent and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support the short-term feasibility and procedural hemostatic efficiency of the device compared with conventional elastic bandage compression. Further multicenter studies incorporating standardized patent-hemostasis assessment, longer vascular follow-up, and comparisons with currently available dedicated distal radial compression devices are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500105403. Registered 2 July 2025.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: First case series to describe clinical infections with Fusobacterium gonidiaformans.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fusobacterium species are anaerobic Gram-negative bacilli. Infections with F. necrophorum and the associated Lemierre's syndrome are the most commonly described in the literature, however the role of F. gonidiaformans in disease is less well characterised. We present the first case series to describe infections with F. gonidiaformans.
METHODS: The laboratory database for a Scottish health board was searched to identify samples in which F. gonidiaformans had been isolated between 2019 and 2022. Clinical and laboratory documentation was reviewed.
RESULTS: 26 isolates were identified in the time period studied corresponding to 25 cases. Most samples were polymicrobial (85%). No beta-lactam, metronidazole or clindamycin resistance was detected. 17 of the 25 cases were found to have clinical infection. Median age was 37 years with interquartile range (IQR) 33-50, 11 cases (65%) were female. The most common clinical syndrome was abscess (59%) followed by infected thrombophlebitis (18%). Median duration of antibiotic therapy was 14 days (IQR: 11-16). The majority of cases with abscess underwent source control (90%). Five cases were managed as outpatients only, median hospital stay for admitted cases was 7 days (IQR 5-15), and 2 cases required ICU admission. There was no mortality among the cases found to have clinical infection. Fusobacterium gonidiaformans was isolated from blood cultures in 4 cases, 3 of which were cases with infected thrombophlebitis in patients who injected drugs.
CONCLUSIONS: This series summarises 17 cases of F. gonidiaformans infection. Clinical abscess was found in the majority of cases, and thrombophlebitis in most cases of bacteraemia. Further studies will be required to establish clinical and epidemiological risk factors for clinical disease.

Title: Comparison of treatment delays and in-hospital outcomes between self-transported and EMS-transported patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing PCI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of reperfusion therapy in patients with myocardial infarction (MI) depends largely on timely treatment. This study aimed to compare treatment delays and in-hospital outcomes between self-transported and EMS-transported patients with STEMI.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included 208 patients with AMI who underwent PCI between March 2022 and June 2023. Of these, 92 patients arrived at the hospital by self-transport and 116 were transported by EMS. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The study population was predominantly male (78.4%), with a mean age of 58.05 ± 12.06 years. Significant differences were observed between self-transported and EMS-transported patients in onset-to-door time (P < 0.001) and door-to-balloon time (P = 0.001). However, no significant differences were found in AMI-related complications, including stroke, cardiogenic shock, heart failure, pericarditis, and dysrhythmias. Likewise, in-hospital outcomes, including left ventricular ejection fraction, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, and mortality, did not differ significantly between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: Although EMS transport was associated with acceptably shorter treatment delays in patients with STEMI, total treatment times remained longer than recommended guideline targets. Our findings suggest that improving EMS utilization alone may be insufficient to improve clinical outcomes when overall system delays remain prolonged. However, given the limited sample size and low event rates, the results should be interpreted with caution. Patient-related factors may also influence treatment outcomes. Future large-scale studies are warranted to identify modifiable factors associated with treatment delays throughout the STEMI care pathway and to determine whether addressing these factors improves clinical outcomes.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Routine metabolic-adiposity indices and incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity among adults with CKM stages 0-3: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is an increasing burden in ageing populations. Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stages 0-3 provide an upstream framework for identifying metabolic, renal, and cardiovascular vulnerability before overt multimorbidity. We evaluated whether routinely derived metabolic-adiposity indices add useful risk-phenotype information beyond established clinical factors.
METHODS: This prospective CHARLS cohort included 7,062 adults aged ≥ 45 years who were free of CMM and had CKM stages 0-3 at baseline. Twenty-nine cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose (CHG)-derived, triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-derived, and adiposity/body-shape indices were evaluated; the main text focused on RFM, CHG-RFM, TyG-RFM, BMI, and WC. Model 3 was used to anchor the primary association interpretation, while Model 4 was retained as an extended clinical-adjustment model to assess robustness after broader adjustment. Benjamini-Hochberg correction, inter-index correlations, paired CHG-TyG models, proportional-hazards diagnostics, prediction analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among 7,062 participants, 613 developed incident CMM (8.7%). In Model 3, the per-SD HRs (95% CIs) were 1.85 (1.52-2.25) for RFM, 1.72 (1.47-2.03) for CHG-RFM, 1.67 (1.41-1.98) for TyG-RFM, 1.30 (1.20-1.41) for BMI, and 1.34 (1.23-1.46) for WC. The corresponding estimates remained broadly consistent in Model 4. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, 28 of 29 Model 3 per-SD associations remained supported; ABSI was the exception. Correlations were substantial among structurally related indices, and paired CHG-TyG models showed marked mutual attenuation. The clinical baseline AUC was 0.787, whereas selected index-extended models achieved AUCs of approximately 0.799-0.800, indicating modest absolute improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: Selected routine metabolic-adiposity indices were associated with incident CMM among adults with CKM stages 0-3. RFM-related indices showed stronger association signals, whereas BMI and WC remain more accessible measures. The broadly consistent Model 3 and Model 4 estimates supported the overall association pattern. However, because inter-index overlap was substantial and incremental predictive gains were modest, these indices should be viewed as candidate adjunctive risk markers rather than independent biomarkers or clinically validated decision tools.

Title: Risk factors for acute ischemic stroke of small vessel occlusion in elderly patients with cerebral small vessel disease and establishment of a prediction model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) accounts for 25% of ischemic stroke causes, yet risk factors for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in elderly CSVD patients remain unclear. This study aimed to identify these risk factors and establish a prediction model.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 452 elderly CSVD patients (training cohort) and 59 patients (validation cohort). The total CSVD burden score was calculated based on MRI features. Logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors and develop prediction models.
RESULTS: Among 452 patients, 52 (11.5%) developed AIS. The total CSVD burden score (OR = 3.718, 95% CI: 1.971-7.011) was an independent risk factor. Carotid plaque thickness was significantly greater in AIS patients (1.879 ± 1.543 mm vs. 1.237 ± 1.246 mm, P = 0.006). In the training set, the parsimonious Model 2 achieved an apparent AUC of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.812 -0.938 ), with a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.867, sensitivity of 92.7%, and specificity of 84.2%. In the validation set, Model 2 exhibited excellent performance with an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI: 0.917-1.000), sensitivity of 100%, and specificity of 85.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: The total CSVD burden score, smoking and carotid plaque thickness are independent predictors of AIS in elderly CSVD patients. Integrating imaging burden with modifiable risk factors provides excellent predictive accuracy for early identification of high-risk individuals.

Title: Relationship between intraoperative hypotension and postoperative venous thromboembolism in elderly patients undergoing hip surgery and construction of a risk prediction model.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the dose-response correlation between intraoperative hypotension (IOH) and postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) among elderly patients receiving hip surgery under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia. It also sought to develop and validate a VTE risk prediction nomogram tailored to this patient population, providing evidence-based support for targeted perioperative VTE prophylaxis and individualized intraoperative blood pressure management.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort analysis enrolling 680 patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent primary hip procedures (periacetabular fracture internal fixation, total hip arthroplasty) with combined spinal-epidural anesthesia at our institution between January 2020 and December 2025. Minute-by-minute intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) recordings were extracted from the hospital's anesthesia information system. Using MAP < 65 mmHg as the hypotension cutoff, three quantitative IOH metrics were calculated: time-weighted average hypotension amplitude (TWA), hypotension area under the curve (AUC), and cumulative IOH duration. Variance inflation factor (VIF) testing was first performed to quantify multicollinearity across TWA, AUC, and cumulative hypotension duration prior to multivariable regression modeling. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized regression was applied for variable screening to mitigate collinearity and reduce predictor counts, lowering the risk of model overfitting. The primary study endpoint was incident VTE diagnosed within 14 days postoperatively. Electronic medical records were reviewed to collect clinical data including demographic profiles, comorbidities, surgical parameters, and perioperative thromboprophylaxis protocols. Multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was implemented to handle incomplete hemodynamic and clinical datasets; sample size justification was supplemented with detailed calculation logic to meet standard event-per-predictor ratios for regression modeling. Univariate Logistic regression identified candidate VTE risk factors with P < 0.1, which were subsequently entered into multivariable Logistic regression to screen independent risk correlates. A nomogram predicting postoperative VTE risk was built using these independent correlates. The model's discriminative performance, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). One-thousand-fold bootstrap resampling internal validation was conducted to compute optimism-corrected AUC and calibration metrics, minimizing overfitting bias. Risk stratification was performed based on total nomogram scores.
RESULTS: The 14-day postoperative VTE incidence across the full cohort of 680 elderly hip surgery patients was 4.20% (28/680). VIF values for TWA, AUC, and cumulative IOH duration ranged from 2.14 to 3.07, indicating mild multicollinearity. LASSO regression retained all three IOH metrics after penalty adjustment, which suggests each carries independent predictive value for postoperative VTE. The event-to-predictor ratio reached 4.0 (28 VTE events /7 predictors), nearly satisfying the widely accepted threshold of 10 events per 3 predictors required for stable Logistic regression modeling. Bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.792, slightly lower than the uncorrected original AUC of 0.816, implying mild overfitting. Multivariable Logistic regression indicated the following factors were independently associated with elevated postoperative VTE risk in elderly hip surgery patients: TWA (OR=1.125, 95%CI: 1.058-1.196, P<0.001), AUC (OR=1.098, 95%CI: 1.045-1.154, P<0.001), cumulative IOH duration (OR=1.036, 95%CI: 1.012-1.061, P=0.003), age ≥ 75 years (OR=2.895, 95%CI: 1.216-6.887, P=0.016), diabetes history (OR=2.563, 95%CI: 1.082-6.079, P=0.032), operative time ≥ 120 min (OR=3.102, 95%CI: 1.305-7.376, P=0.010), and non-standard postoperative mechanical thromboprophylaxis (OR=4.018, 95%CI: 1.695-9.523, P=0.001). All three quantitative IOH metrics displayed a graded positive correlation with VTE risk (P for trend <0.001), consistent with a dose-response pattern. For the nomogram constructed from the seven independent correlates above, ROC analysis yielded an uncorrected AUC of 0.816 (95%CI: 0.725-0.907), which suggests satisfactory discriminative capacity; bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC = 0.792 (95%CI: 0.701-0.883). Calibration curves revealed strong alignment between model-predicted VTE probabilities and actual observed event rates (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, χ²=6.895, P=0.542; bootstrap-corrected Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.517). DCA demonstrated that the model generated meaningful net clinical benefit within a threshold probability range of 5%-40%. Patients were stratified by nomogram total score into three risk tiers: low-risk (≤ 100 points), moderate-risk (101-150 points), and high-risk (> 150 points). Corresponding VTE incidences were 1.1% (3/325), 7.6% (22/286), and 22.7% (15/69), with statistically significant intergroup differences (χ²=45.865, P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Among elderly hip surgery patients under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia, the severity, cumulative load, and total duration of IOH appear to follow a dose-response pattern with postoperative VTE risk, and IOH metrics are independently correlated with VTE occurrence. The nomogram integrating quantitative IOH indicators and clinical patient characteristics exhibits favorable predictive performance and clinical applicability. It enables precise VTE risk stratification for this elderly surgical population and may serve as a quantitative reference for developing individualized perioperative VTE prophylaxis and refined intraoperative blood pressure management protocols.

Title: Stage-dependent predictors of atrial fibrillation recurrence after catheter ablation: a proof-of-concept analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk models for atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation apply the same predictor structure to every patient. This overlooks the biological differences between early and advanced disease. We examined whether the clinical predictors of 12-month recurrence differ across four disease-stage phenotypes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 419 consecutive patients who underwent first-time radiofrequency ablation at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, between October 2021 and June 2024. The institutional protocol was pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) alone, and patients undergoing concurrent left atrial appendage occlusion were excluded. Patients were classified by AF type and duration into four groups: early paroxysmal (Phenotype 1, ≤ 12 months, n = 225), long-standing paroxysmal (Phenotype 2, > 12 months, n = 86), recent-onset persistent (Phenotype 3, ≤ 18 months, n = 62), and long-duration persistent AF (Phenotype 4, > 18 months, n = 46). We performed phenotype-specific logistic regression, predictor × phenotype interaction testing, Kaplan-Meier and restricted mean survival analysis, and ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Twelve-month recurrence occurred in 88 patients (21.0%) and differed significantly across phenotypes (17.3%, 20.9%, 16.1%, and 45.7% in P1-P4; p < 0.001). Recurrence-free survival was worst in P4 (log-rank p < 0.001). In the overall model (AUC 0.672), the independent predictors were persistent AF type, longer duration, and hypertension, the last associated with lower recurrence. Phenotype-specific models revealed distinct profiles, and the sex × phenotype interaction was formally significant (p = 0.0042). In P1, younger age was the only predictor (AUC 0.701). In P3, female sex and hypertension were apparent predictors (apparent AUC 0.862; recurrence 43.8% in women vs. 6.5% in men), although this estimate is subject to optimism given only 10 events. In P4, no clinical variable was associated with recurrence despite its 45.7% rate, though power was insufficient to exclude moderate associations. The protective direction of hypertension strengthened across P1-P3 before disappearing in P4.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, single-center analysis, the clinical predictors of post-ablation AF recurrence appeared to shift across the four disease-stage phenotypes, with formal statistical support for sex. We propose the Predictor Lifecycle as a testable hypothesis for prospective, multicenter validation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not constitute a validated risk-stratification framework for clinical use.

Title: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy for Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine

Title: A Simplified Modification of the Transseptal Puncture Technique to Optimize Percutaneous Mitral Balloon Commissurotomy in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transseptal catheterization is a critical step in percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy (PMBC), yet conventional techniques can be technically challenging and sometimes lead to procedural risks. Our study aimed to use a simplified modification to improve anatomical guidance and reduce complications.
METHODS: This prospective multicenter study was conducted over one-year and included 161 patients with severe mitral stenosis who underwent PMBC using a modified septal puncture technique in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Data were entered and analyzed using SPSS version 25. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and procedural outcomes. Continuous variables were expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD) or median with range, as appropriate. Paired t-tests were used to compare pre- and post-procedural parameters, with a pvalue < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Our findings showed that the technique used was successful in all patients, with optimal results achieved in 160 (99.4%). Nonetheless, four patients developed new-onset atrial fibrillation during catheterization that resolved before discharge. The increase in mean mitral valve area and the reduction in transmitral mean gradient were statistically significant. The mean safety distance from the puncture site to the left atrial border was 24.8 mm (range 13 to 48 mm), while the average vertebral body height (VBH) was 17.3 mm (range 12 to 23 mm). The ratio of safety distance to VBH was 1.4 (range 1.0 to 2.4; SD = 0.26).
DISCUSSION: Our study introduces a novel modification of the atrial septal puncture technique, simplifying the conventional approaches described by Inoue and Hung. The left atrial shadow, carinal angle, and VBH were identified as important radiographic landmarks for atrial septal puncture.
CONCLUSION: The innovative modified transseptal puncture approach demonstrated a safe and effective technique, with a high success rate for mitral valve balloon commissurotomy.

Title: Comparative cardiovascular outcomes of IL-6 inhibitors versus rituximab in rheumatoid arthritis: a claims-based observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interleukin-6 receptor inhibitors (IL-6i), tocilizumab and sarilumab, are FDA-approved therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Beyond their efficacy in controlling systemic inflammation, growing evidence suggests that IL-6 inhibition may confer cardioprotective effects. This study investigates the long-term cardiovascular outcomes associated with IL-6i in RA patients, comparing IL-6 inhibitors with rituximab and evaluating differences between individual IL-6 inhibitor agents.
METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study using the TriNetX Linked Network (2010-2025) including adults with RA initiating an IL-6 inhibitor or rituximab and ≥ 2 prescriptions for a drug of interest ≥ 6 months apart. Comparisons were as follows: (1) IL-6 inhibitors (sarilumab, tocilizumab) versus rituximab, and (2) tocilizumab versus sarilumab. Patients receiving both IL-6 inhibitors simultaneously or a non-FDA-approved IL-6 blocker (e.g., siltuximab) were excluded. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, heart failure (HF), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) over 5 years. We calculated propensity scores using demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, inflammatory markers, prior TNFi exposure, systemic glucocorticoid use, and conventional DMARDs, and used scores to match exposed individuals 1:1 with comparators. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality and cardiovascular outcomes individually. All analyses were conducted using the TriNetX platform.
RESULTS: After matching, 4288 RA patients per group were included for IL-6i versus rituximab and 605 per group for sarilumab versus tocilizumab. Compared to rituximab, IL-6i was associated with lower hazards of mortality (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.82), MACE (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.64-0.85), and HF risk (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.94), with no significant difference in MI, stroke, or VTE. Amongst IL-6 inhibitors, sarilumab was associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality compared to tocilizumab (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.29-0.94), but no significant differences were identified for other cardiovascular outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with RA, IL-6i use was associated with lower rates of all-cause mortality, MACE, and heart failure compared to rituximab, while risks of stroke, MI, and VTE were similar. A lower risk of all-cause mortality was observed with sarilumab compared to tocilizumab. These findings support a potential survival and cardiovascular benefit of IL-6i and highlight the need for larger studies to further distinguish the cardiovascular outcomes with IL-6i agents. Such evidence could inform personalized treatment decisions based on cardiovascular risk factors. Key Points • This study provides long-term real-world evidence that IL-6 inhibitors may offer superior cardiovascular outcomes compared with rituximab in RA patients previously managed with TNFi, an important evidence gap in biologic choice after TNFi failure. • This study directly compares cardiovascular outcomes between sarilumab and tocilizumab, identifying a potential lower myocardial infarction risk with sarilumab.

Title: Age-specific prognostic value of 1-year changes in cardio-ankle vascular index.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: The prognostic significance of longitudinal changes in the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI) remains unclear. We investigated the association between 1-year changes in CAVI and subsequent cardiovascular events according to age. A total of 4032 participants with cardiovascular risk factors who were enrolled in the prospective multicenter Coupling Registry and had undergone CAVI measurements at baseline and 1 year were classified into four groups using a CAVI cutoff of 9: good ( < 9 at both time points, n = 1841), improved ( ≥ 9 to <9, n = 268), worsened ( < 9 to ≥9, n = 408), and persistently high ( ≥ 9 at both time points, n = 1515). The primary outcome was a composite of stroke, coronary artery disease, sudden cardiac death, heart failure, and aortic dissection. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations between CAVI changes and outcomes. CAVI increased from 8.80 ± 1.34 at baseline to 8.88 ± 1.35 at 1 year (P < 0.001). During a median 60-month follow-up (49-63 months), 155 cardiovascular events occurred. In the overall cohort, neither the worsened group (HR, 1.56; 95% CI, 0.93-2.62) nor the persistently high group (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.72-1.68) was significantly associated with cardiovascular events compared with the good group. Among participants aged <65 years, the worsened group (HR, 3.36; 95% CI, 1.18-9.58) and persistently high group (HR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.11-6.50) had higher cardiovascular risk. No significant associations were observed among participants aged ≥65 years. In conclusion, among patients aged <65 years with cardiovascular risk factors, both worsening and persistently elevated CAVI were independently associated with increased cardiovascular risk.

Title: The hidden burden of cardiovascular risk in working women : A preventive cardiology and gender-sensitive analysis in a hospital workforce.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among women, yet female-specific and psychosocial risk determinants are inconsistently integrated into preventive strategies. We describe traditional and female-specific risk factors in female hospital employees.
METHODS: In this single-centre, cross-sectional, exploratory study, 111 women aged 34-70 years (nursing, administrative, medical staff) underwent standardised occupational health assessment of lipids, lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)], glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NTproBNP), reproductive history and well-being (WHO-5 Well-Being Index). Voluntary participation may have caused selection bias.
RESULTS: Dyslipidemia was present in 58.6%, hypertension and prediabetes each in 15.3%, and obesity in 14.4%. Median Lp(a) was 20 mg/dl (interquartile range, IQR, 20-65 mg/dl), with 27.9% showing values ≥50 mg/dl. NT-proBNP exceeded 125 pg/ml in 11.7% and correlated with age (ρ = 0.23, p = 0.015). Of 90 participants with at least one pregnancy, 25.3% reported complications. Body mass index (BMI) correlated with HbA1c (r = 0.33, p < 0.001; a possible non-linear BMI-well-being association was non-significant. Among 103 women aged 40-65 years with coronary artery calcium (CAC) data, 22 (21.4%) had CAC > 0 and were older, more often postmenopausal and hypertensive, with higher NT-proBNP.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory cohort, traditional and female-specific risk factors were prevalent, and a substantial minority already showed subclinical coronary calcification. These findings support prospective evaluation of whether integrating reproductive history, female-specific biomarkers and psychosocial assessment improves risk stratification; causal or predictive conclusions cannot be drawn.

Title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) for detecting haemodynamically significant coronary disease in patients with anatomically long-segment lesions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and invasive pressure-wire FFR within 30 days. Anatomically long-segment disease was defined as lesion length ≥ 20 mm. Invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 was the reference standard. CT-FFR was assessed at vessel and patient levels, with patient-level CT-FFR defined as the minimum value per patient and patient-level disease as any invasive FFR ≤ 0.80. Diagnostic discrimination, threshold-based classification, and Bland-Altman agreement were evaluated.
RESULTS: The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant.
CONCLUSION: CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment.
KEY POINTS: Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

Title: Intergenerational educational attainment and risk for incident dementia in a U.S. community-based cohort study: Findings from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Neurocognitive Study.
Abstract: BackgroundIndividuals with higher educational attainment have a lower risk for dementia, including Alzheimer's disease, but it is less clear how the educational attainment of an individual's parents may influence dementia risk, particularly in diverse populations.ObjectiveThis study examined whether intergenerational educational attainment for two adjacent generations was associated with incident dementia risk.MethodsIndividuals from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study were asked about their own educational level (at study baseline, 1987-1989; ages 44-66 years) and, several years later, that of each parent. Dementia status was ascertained from baseline through 2020 using expert committee diagnoses from in-person and telephonic neuropsychological assessments, informant interviews, hospitalization codes, and death certificates. Individuals without dementia at baseline, and with non-missing covariates/ educational history, were included. Educational level was classified (for individuals and the highest-educated parent) as less than high school, completed high school or GED, or more than high school. Cox proportional-hazard models were used to evaluate the association between intergenerational educational attainment and incident dementia risk.ResultsAmong 10,626 individuals (21.8% Black; 55.9% female), models showed that high parental education level and individual education level were each significantly and independently associated with a lower hazard of dementia, although associations were strongest and most consistent for individual education. Individuals whose educational attainment surpassed that of their parents, compared to those with comparable levels, exhibited a significantly lower dementia risk.ConclusionsAn individual's own educational attainment may exert a more significant influence in lowering dementia risk, even when parental education is considered.

Title: Low-dose colchicine for the prevention of postoperative atrial fibrillation after bypass surgery: Results from the COLPOAF study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse outcomes. Standard-dose colchicine could reduce POAF incidence but is limited by poor tolerability. Low-dose colchicine (0.5mg daily) is recommended for secondary prevention in coronary artery disease with a favourable safety profile.
AIMS: To compare the incidence of POAF following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between patients who received low-dose colchicine and those managed with standard care.
METHODS: COLPOAF is an observational, retrospective, before-after, single-centre study conducted in a tertiary care hospital in France. A total of 206 patients who underwent CABG between November 2024 and January 2026 (treated with low-dose colchicine) were compared with a historical control group of 244 patients operated on between May 2023 and July 2024 (without colchicine). The primary efficacy endpoint was the incidence of POAF between postoperative day 3 and hospital discharge.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. POAF occurred in 23 patients (11.2%) in the colchicine group and 29 patients (11.9%) in the standard care group, with a hazard ratio of 0.92 (95% confidence interval 0.53-1.59; P=0.76). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with colchicine (7.8 vs. 2.5%), leading to drug discontinuation in 12 patients (5.8%). No major adverse events were attributed to colchicine. C-reactive protein levels were significantly lower in the colchicine group.
CONCLUSION: Low-dose colchicine was not significantly associated with a reduction in POAF after CABG. The overall safety profile remained acceptable with no severe treatment-related complications.

Title: The use of platelet function testing to guide antithrombotic regimens post-percutaneous coronary intervention in patients requiring therapeutic anticoagulation.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Platelet reactivity testing may help tailor antithrombotic regimens after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We sought to describe antithrombotic practices and assess 30-day outcomes in patients treated at an academic cardiac catheterization laboratory who underwent platelet reactivity testing following PCI while concurrently on oral anticoagulation (AC).
METHODS: Patients on oral AC who underwent PCI and received platelet reactivity testing at an academic medical center between 1/2012 and 9/2022 were reviewed. Patients were grouped by high on-treatment platelet reactivity (PRU ≥208) and a low on-treatment platelet reactivity (PRU <208) status and then analyzed based on whether they were continued on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) or de-escalated to single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT). Rates of major bleeding and stent thrombosis up to 30 days post-PCI were compared using univariate and multivariate analyses.
RESULTS: 156 patients were included (mean age 74, 72% male). Post-PCI, platelet reactivity testing revealed adequate platelet inhibition (PRU < 208) in 120 patients (77%) and inadequate inhibition (PRU≥208) in 36 patients (23%). In the group with adequate inhibition, 78 patients (65%) were de-escalated to SAPT. Compared to individuals with adequate inhibition that were continued on DAPT, patients in the SAPT group had a lower rate of major bleeding 30 days post-PCI (1.3% vs. 9.5%, p = 0.05) and with no increase in stent thrombosis rates. In the group with inadequate inhibition, 53% of patients were de-escalated to SAPT, most often with an alternative P2Y12 inhibitor. Compared to individuals with inadequate inhibition that were continued on DAPT, these patients had lower rates of major bleeding at 30 days (0% vs. 12%, p = 0.23) and similar rates of stent thrombosis.
DISCUSSION: In this analysis of a high bleeding and ischemic risk cohort of patients on concurrent AC undergoing PCI at a high-volume academic medical center, patients managed with SAPT post-PCI experienced lower rates of bleeding without a clear increase in ischemic events compared to those continued on DAPT. Antiplatelet de-escalation was left to the treating physician's discretion, and larger prospective studies are needed to corroborate the safety and utility of this strategy in clinical practice.

Title: Mentorship as infrastructure: Building the future cardiovascular CT workforce.
Abstract: Cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) continues to expand, creating a parallel need to develop the clinicians, educators, investigators, and leaders who will advance the field. This opinion paper frames mentorship and sponsorship as essential professional infrastructure rather than episodic networking. Using the Fellow and Resident Leaders of the Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography (FiRST) Committee and the SCCT Future Leaders Program (FLP) as complementary models, we describe five interconnected domains: connection, education, scholarship, visibility, and leadership. Activities include speed mentoring, educational resource development, mentored writing, scientific communication, and Society service. A retrospective descriptive evaluation of 73 FiRST alumni and 15 FLP alumni who completed participation by December 31, 2025 documented subsequent SCCT committee service in 43.8% and 80.0%, committee chair or vice-chair roles in 16.4% and 20.0%, and Board membership in 9.6% and 13.3%, respectively. Median publication counts were 48 (interquartile range [IQR], 18-131) for FiRST and 57 (IQR, 45-78.5) for FLP; median h-indices were 13 (IQR, 6-28) and 13 (IQR, 10.5-19). These findings describe recorded career achievements and cumulative scholarship, not effects attributable to program participation. We propose prospective evaluation of mentorship continuity, scholarly contributions, leadership, retention, and barriers to participation. Intentional investment in mentorship, sponsorship, and inclusive opportunities can help professional societies connect early engagement with sustained contribution and prepare the future CCT workforce.

Title: Is There a Role for Renal Revascularization in Atherosclerotic Renal Artery Stenosis?
Journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
Abstract: Atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis is a prevalent cause of secondary hypertension and ischemic nephropathy, particularly in older adults with generalized atherosclerosis. While randomized controlled trials have generally failed to show benefit from renal artery revascularization over optimal medical therapy in unselected populations, observational data highlight subgroups that may derive meaningful improvement. This review synthesizes evidence on patient selection, diagnostic strategies, and revascularization outcomes. High-risk clinical profiles-including recurrent flash pulmonary edema, rapidly progressive kidney dysfunction, global renal ischemia or resistant hypertension-consistently predict greater benefit, particularly with hemodynamically significant lesions. Functional assessments, including trans-lesional pressure gradients, may outperform anatomical severity alone in predicting blood pressure response. Kidney function improvement after revascularization is more likely in patients with rapidly declining kidney function and bilateral ≥70% stenosis or a solitary kidney. Cardiovascular benefit appears greatest in recurrent flash pulmonary edema or congestive heart failure, preserved kidney function, and low albuminuria. Patients with moderate stenosis, controlled blood pressure, and stable kidney function generally show no added benefit from revascularization. Integrating anatomical imaging, physiological measurements, and clinical risk factors may optimize patient selection. Future prospective trials should target high-risk phenotypes excluded from prior studies, with standardized endpoints including ambulatory blood pressure, objective medication adherence, and clinically meaningful kidney and cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Renal Denervation in Modern Hypertension Care: From Early Promise to Evidence-Based Clinical Integration.
Journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
Abstract: Hypertension remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. However, rates of global blood pressure (BP) control remain suboptimal, despite effective pharmacologic therapies and clear guideline targets. Persistent gaps in control are multifactorial, including poor adherence, complex treatment regimens, and health care system limitations. Renal denervation (RDN), a device-based therapy, is an emerging treatment which may overcome barriers for hypertension control. RDN targets renal sympathetic nerve activity, a key contributor to hypertension pathophysiology. Early studies of RDN, using catheter-based ablation techniques, suggested substantial BP reductions (∼10-30 mmHg reduction in office systolic BP). However, initial enthusiasm was tempered by neutral findings in sham-controlled trials. Recent advances in device technology, procedural optimization, technique, and patient selection have been central to improving reproducibility and redemonstrating efficacy (office and ambulatory BP) and safety of RDN in contemporary randomized studies. Current evidence supports RDN as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected patients with resistant or uncontrolled primary hypertension, particularly in those with preserved renal function and evidence of sympathetic overactivity. As the field evolves, ongoing research focusing on precision phenotyping, noncatheter-based techniques, long-term clinical outcomes, and cost-effectiveness will be critical in defining the role of RDN within contemporary hypertension management strategies.

Title: Hypertension in Patients Receiving Maintenance Hemodialysis: Beyond Sodium and Dry Weight.
Journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
Abstract: Hypertension is highly prevalent in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis and is strongly associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Optimal strategies for diagnosis and management of hypertension are uncertain. Peridialysis blood pressure (BP) measurements, although critical for safety monitoring, are increasingly recognized as being unreliable for diagnosing hypertension or guiding therapy. Current evidence supports the use of 44-h ambulatory BP monitoring as the preferred diagnostic method, with home BP monitoring as a practical alternative. Out-of-office measurements correlate more closely with cardiovascular outcomes, left ventricular hypertrophy, and mortality than peridialysis readings. Despite observational data suggesting a linear association between higher out-of-dialysis BP and adverse outcomes, randomized controlled trials establishing definitive BP targets in dialysis patients are lacking. Both extremes of BP may confer harm, and aggressive BP lowering increases the risk of intradialytic hypotension and vascular access complications. Management should prioritize the optimization of volume status by attainment of dry weight and sodium restriction. If BP remains high, pharmacotherapy is indicated. Beta-blockers are generally favored as first-line agents given their antihypertensive efficacy and potential cardiovascular benefits. Future research should focus on the role of emerging cardiovascular therapies, large-scale clinical trials to establish appropriate BP targets, and real-world implementation of out-of-office BP measurements.

Title: Hypertension in Children With Chronic Kidney Disease and Dialysis: State of the Art.
Journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
Abstract: Hypertension is a highly prevalent and clinically significant complication in childhood chronic kidney disease (CKD), contributing substantially to cardiovascular morbidity, progression of kidney dysfunction, and long-term health risks extending into adulthood. Management of hypertension remains suboptimal with missed opportunities in its accurate detection, monitoring, and subsequent risk stratification to improve clinical outcomes. Evidence consistently demonstrates that sustained hypertension accelerates decline in glomerular filtration rate and increases the risk of left ventricular hypertrophy and other forms of target organ injury. Early and effective intervention, therefore, is essential. Nonpharmacological strategies, including dietary sodium restriction, optimization of fluid balance, and promotion of healthy lifestyle habits, form the foundation of management. Pharmacological therapy, particularly with agents that block the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, remains the cornerstone of treatment due to their dual antihypertensive and renoprotective effects. Randomized controlled trials have informed treatment thresholds and targets for those with predialysis CKD. Several knowledge gaps remain including blood pressure targets for earlier stages of CKD especially in those with non-proteinuric kidney disease, longer term safety data for antihypertensive medications, and studies highlighting successful implementation treatment strategies that improve achievement of tretament targets and outcomes require further investigation. Early recognition, routine use of ambulatory monitoring, and comprehensive, individualized management are essential to slow kidney disease progression and reduce cardiovascular risk, ultimately improving long-term outcomes for this vulnerable population.

Title: Impact of environmental factors on cardiovascular health in Castilla-La Mancha: the CarVasCLiMa cohort study protocol.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: The CarVasCLiMa project aims to investigate the associations between environmental factors and cardiovascular health outcomes in the population of Castilla-La Mancha.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The study will include a representative cohort of residents from urban, semiurban and rural areas, followed over a 2-year period. Environmental exposure variables, including air pollution and climate conditions, will be assessed using high-resolution satellite data complemented by data from local monitoring stations. Proximity to green spaces will be estimated using the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index and geospatial data. Cardiovascular outcomes will include measurements of blood pressure, arterial stiffness and circulating biomarkers such as C-reactive protein. In addition, validated questionnaires will be administered to assess quality of life, emotional well-being and lifestyle factors. Data analysis will involve advanced statistical modelling to examine longitudinal associations between environmental and lifestyle factors and cardiovascular outcomes, including sex-stratified analyses and specific evaluations of vulnerable population subgroups.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This protocol was previously approved by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee of the Health Area in the city of Cuenca (REG: 2025/PI1625). This approach will enable the identification of differential susceptibility to environmental and lifestyle factors and support the development of targeted prevention strategies. Finally, the findings of this study are expected to inform the development of public health policies tailored to the regional context, contributing to the mitigation of environmental risks and the improvement of cardiovascular health and overall quality of life in Castilla-La Mancha.

Title: Integrated community-based HIV+NCD care in microfinance groups in Kenya: results from the Harambee cluster randomised trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Harambee randomised trial tested the extent to which integrating community-based care with microfinance improves viral suppression and retention in care among people with HIV in Kenya.
METHODS: Using a two-arm parallel-cluster randomised controlled trial, we randomised 57 microfinance groups (29 to intervention, 28 to usual (facility-based) care) with 855 members living with HIV (407 in intervention, 448 in usual care). We enrolled n=300 frequency-matched, prospectively followed usual HIV care patients without microfinance. Delivered quarterly during community-based microfinance meetings, the intervention included clinical consultations, diabetes and/or hypertension management, distribution of antiretroviral therapy and non-communicable diseases medications, health education and facility referrals. The primary outcome was viral suppression (<400 HIV-RNA/mL before 1 January 2023; <200 HIV-RNA/mL on or after 1 January 2023) at 18 months.
