The secondary outcome was retention-in-care (attending >1 scheduled HIV care visit/quarter over 18 months). Between-arm comparisons were done using doubly-robust generalised estimating equations accounting for dropout and confounding (for comparisons to the non-randomised arm).
RESULTS: At enrolment, 94% of participants were virally suppressed. Viral suppression at 18 months was not significantly different between microfinance group members receiving community care versus facility care (OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.51 to 2.95, p=0.64). Viral suppression at 18 months was higher among community-care microfinance members (OR 2.16, 1.48 to 3.19, p<0.001) and facility-care microfinance members (OR 1.42, 1.05 to 1.92, p=0.023), compared with matched facility-care patients not engaged in microfinance. There was evidence of better quarterly retention comparing microfinance group members receiving community care versus facility care (OR 3.79, 2.96 to 4.86, p<0.001). Retention was higher among community-care microfinance members (OR 9.13, 7.13 to 11.70, p<0.001) and facility-care microfinance members (OR 2.40, 2.03 to 2.85, p<0.001), compared with matched facility-care patients.
CONCLUSION: More convenient services can improve retention in HIV care, while economic strengthening likely helps improve clinical HIV outcomes. Research to identify impact mechanisms and scale-up potential is needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04417127.

Title: LIPOPROTEIN LIPASE GENE POLYMORPHISMS AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH APOLIPOPROTEIN A-I AND B-100 CONCENTRATIONS IN PATIENTS WITH CORONARY HEART DISEASE: A CROSS-SECTIONAL GENETIC ASSOCIATION STUDY.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interindividual variation in lipid and lipoprotein profiles is linked to polymorphisms in the gene encoding lipoprotein lipase (LPL), an enzyme central to lipoprotein metabolism. However, the relationship between common LPL variants and circulating apolipoprotein A-I (apoA-I) and apolipoprotein B-100 (apoB-100) concentrations in coronary heart disease (CHD) remains incompletely characterized. This study examined the Ser447Ter (rs328), HindIII (rs320), and PvuII (rs285) LPL polymorphisms in relation to apoA-I and apoB-100 concentrations among Sudanese patients with CHD and Sudanese controls without a history of coronary artery disease.
METHODS: A cross-sectional genetic association study enrolled 100 patients with angiographically verified CHD from the Sudan Heart Centre, Khartoum, Sudan, and 50 Sudanese controls recruited separately from the general population, without a personal history of coronary artery disease as confirmed by a Medical History and Symptom Questionnaire, and broadly matched to cases by age and sex in an approximate 2:1 case-to-control design. Genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP. Serum apoA-I and apoB-100 concentrations were determined by immunoturbidimetry. Inter-genotype differences in apolipoprotein concentrations among CHD cases were assessed by one-way ANOVA (HindIII, PvuII) or independent-samples t-test (Ser447Ter); Cohen's d effect sizes and point-biserial correlations were also calculated. Because several genotype cells contained zero or very small counts, genotype-frequency comparisons between cases and controls, and tests of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE), were performed using exact methods rather than chi-squared approximations.
RESULTS: CHD patients (54% male; mean age 51.7 ± 16.7 years) had significantly higher body mass index, apoA-I, and apoB-100 concentrations than controls (all p<0.001). Among CHD cases, inter-genotype differences in apoA-I and apoB-100 were not statistically significant for any of the three polymorphisms (all p>0.05), although HindIII H+H- heterozygotes showed numerically higher concentrations of both apolipoproteins than H+H+ homozygotes, corresponding to moderate effect sizes (apoA-I d=0.55; apoB-100 d=0.58). All three loci were monomorphic (0% variant carriers) among the 50 controls. Using Fisher's exact test, variant carriage was more frequent among cases than controls for HindIII (11% vs. 0%, p=0.016) and PvuII (12% vs. 0%, p=0.009) but not for Ser447Ter (5% vs. 0%, p=0.17); odds ratios calculated with the Haldane-Anscombe correction for zero-cell counts were imprecise, with wide confidence intervals. Exact tests for deviation from HWE among cases indicated significant deviation for HindIII (p=0.005) and PvuII (p=0.009) but not Ser447Ter (p=1.00).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, underpowered Sudanese cohort, LPL genotype was not significantly associated with apoA-I or apoB-100 concentrations, although a moderate, hypothesis-generating effect was observed for the HindIII polymorphism among heterozygous carriers. Variant carriage of HindIII and PvuII was more frequent among CHD cases than controls, but the zero-cell counts in controls, the imprecise odds ratio estimates, and the significant HWE deviation observed for these two loci among cases warrant cautious interpretation and independent replication.

Title: ASSOCIATION OF SER447TER, HINDIII AND PVUII LIPOPROTEIN LIPASE GENE POLYMORPHISMS WITH LIPID PROFILE IN CORONARY HEART DISEASE.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary heart disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and dyslipidaemia is one of its most important modifiable drivers. Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) is the rate-limiting enzyme for the intravascular hydrolysis of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, and common polymorphisms in the LPL gene on chromosome 8p22, Ser447Ter (rs328), HindIII (rs320) and PvuII (rs285), have been variably linked to circulating lipid levels and CHD susceptibility, with results that differ across populations.
AIM: To determine the distribution of the Ser447Ter, HindIII and PvuII LPL polymorphisms in patients with CHD compared with healthy controls, and to examine the relationship between each polymorphism and the lipid profile after adjustment for adiposity and other cardiovascular risk factors.
METHODS: A cross-sectional case-control study was conducted in 100 patients with established CHD (angiographically documented coronary stenosis ≥ 50%, prior myocardial infarction, or prior coronary revascularisation) and 50 apparently healthy, age- and sex-matched controls. Fasting venous blood was collected after a minimum 12-hour fast; serum lipid parameters were measured by standard enzymatic colorimetric methods, and LDL-C was calculated using the Friedewald equation when triglycerides were below 400 mg/dL and measured directly otherwise. Genomic DNA was extracted using the DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen, Cat. No. 69504). Genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP, with NlaIII, HindIII and PvuII used to digest the Ser447Ter, HindIII and PvuII amplicons, respectively. Because expected cell counts were below five, genotype distributions were compared using Fisher's exact test. Between-group lipid comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test and were repeated as analysis of covariance adjusted for BMI, age and sex. Genotype lipid relationships within the patient group were examined by multivariable linear regression adjusted for BMI, age, sex, diabetes, hypertension and smoking. Analyses were performed in IBM SPSS Statistics v26.
RESULTS: Patients and controls did not differ in total cholesterol (median 166.5 vs 165.5 mg/dL, p=0.485) or triglycerides (123.0 vs 129.0 mg/dL, p=0.624). HDL-C was markedly lower in patients (39.0 vs 62.0 mg/dL, p<0.001) and LDL-C, ApoA-I and ApoB-100 were higher (all p<0.001); these differences persisted after adjustment for BMI, age and sex. Variant alleles were detected in 5%, 11% and 12% of patients and in 0%, 0% and 4% of controls at Ser447Ter, HindIII and PvuII respectively. On Fisher's exact testing only HindIII was associated with CHD status (p=0.016); Ser447Ter (p=0.170) and PvuII (p=0.143) were not, and all odds ratio confidence intervals included unity. Within the patient group, HindIII variant carriage was independently associated with higher total cholesterol (adjusted β=+57.3 mg/dL, 95% CI 25.7 to 88.9, p<0.001) and LDL-C (adjusted β=+62.1 mg/dL, 95% CI 35.1 to 89.2, p<0.001) after adjustment for BMI, age, sex, diabetes, hypertension and smoking. No independent association was found for Ser447Ter or PvuII.
CONCLUSION: Of the three loci examined, only HindIII showed a relationship with the lipid profile that was independent of adiposity and conventional risk factors, and the association ran through total and LDL cholesterol rather than through triglycerides and HDL-C. Ser447Ter and PvuII showed no independent association. Because variant alleles were not detected in any control at two of the three loci, which is not consistent with published regional allele frequencies, the case-control genotype comparison is presented as hypothesis generating and requires confirmation with sequencing verified genotyping in a larger cohort.

Title: MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS AFTER ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME: DEFINITION, TIMING, RATES, MAIN RISK FACTORS, AND WAYS TO IMPROVE.
Abstract:
AIM OF STUDY: This review summarizes current evidence on MACE definitions, the timing and magnitude of post-ACS risk, its main drivers, and evidence-based risk-reduction strategies, and identifies key methodological gaps.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This narrative synthesis includes randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, large registries, and observational studies reporting MACE after ACS, identified through PubMed and cross-referenced guideline documents. No systematic search protocol or quantitative synthesis was performed; priority was given to peer-reviewed publications, current guidelines, and high-impact meta-analyses, with sources cited for pooled estimates.
RESULTS: MACE definitions are heterogeneous. The classical 3-point composite (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke) is the regulatory standard, but 4- and 5-point versions incorporating revascularization, unstable angina, or heart-failure hospitalization are common, and administrative datasets often substitute all-cause mortality. Broader definitions inflate event rates and can affect interpretation of treatment effects. Data from one of the largest meta-analyses indicate that nearly half of the adverse events during the first year occur within 90 days, with an overall 90-day MACE rate of 4.1%. However, it should be noted that one-year rates range from 3.6% in a small cohort of lower-risk patients to 34.4% in a large national registry, reflecting differences in patient composition, the completeness of revascularization performed, and definitions of MACE components. The strongest predictors of post-ACS MACE were clinical severity (Killip class >II, cardiogenic shock/arrest, LVEF ≤40%), comorbidity burden (chronic kidney disease, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, smoking, age/frailty), and anatomical/procedural factors (multivessel disease, incomplete revascularization, suboptimal TIMI flow). Complete revascularization, high-intensity statin therapy, individualized dual antiplatelet duration, and structured secondary prevention were each associated with reduced MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Post-ACS MACE clusters within 90 days after discharge. However, reported incidence varies widely due to heterogeneous endpoint definitions and population differences. Standardizing MACE definition and adjudication reporting, and designing trials powered for early endpoints, would meaningfully improve evidence synthesis. Clinicians should prioritize complete revascularization, optimized lipid-lowering, individualized antithrombotic therapy, and early, intensive secondary prevention.

Title: INDEPENDENT PREDICTORS OF SHORT-TERM MORTALITY IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC HEART FAILURE AND ANEMIA.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia is a common comorbidity in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) and is associated with an unfavorable prognosis. However, the prognostic value of various laboratory biomarkers in patients with CHF and anemia, as well as the contribution of inflammatory mechanisms to adverse clinical outcomes, remains insufficiently understood.
AIM: To identify independent clinical and laboratory predictors of three-month mortality in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) and anemia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 162 patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) and anemia. The type of anemia was determined based on a comprehensive assessment of laboratory parameters. Patients were followed for 3 months. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software (version 22.0).
RESULTS: Anemia of chronic disease was the most common type of anemia, identified in 104 (64.2%) patients, followed by iron deficiency anemia in 53 (32.7%) patients and macrocytic anemia in 5 (3.1%) patients. Signs of hemodilutional anemia were observed in 89 (54.9%) patients. During the follow-up period, 14 deaths (8.6%) were recorded. In the univariable analysis, hemoglobin level, hematocrit, red blood cell count, white blood cell count, ferritin level, C-reactive protein, and left ventricular ejection fraction were significantly associated with three-month mortality (p<0.05). Multivariable analysis identified elevated white blood cell count (OR 1.238, 95% CI 1.094-1.401; p=0.001) and ferritin level (OR 1.003, 95% CI 1.001-1.005; p=0.002) as independent predictors of three-month mortality.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with CHF and anemia, anemia of chronic disease was the most common type of anemia, while signs of hemodilution were observed in more than half of the study population. Elevated white blood cell count and ferritin levels were identified as independent predictors of three-month mortality. These findings suggest that inflammation-associated laboratory markers may play an important role in determining adverse short-term outcomes in patients with CHF and anemia.

Title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury Following Recanalization Of Chronic Total Coronary Occlusions In A Large Multi-Center Registry.
Abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a risk of percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) for chronic total coronary occlusions (CTO), and complex interventional procedures in general. The incidence and temporal changes of CA-AKI with contemporary CTO techniques had not been evaluated before in a large registry. Therefore, we analyzed 12911 CTO procedures by 27 operators between 2015 and 2024 with pre and postprocedural serum creatinine (SCr) assessment. CA-AKI was defined as an increase in SCr ≥0.3 mg/dl or ≥50% from baseline SCr. In addition, an older definition was applied as CIN (Contrast induced nephropathy: SCr increase ≥0.5 mg/dl or ≥25% of baseline). The incidence of CA-AKI was 3.91% with a slight temporal decrease from 5.0% in 2015 to 3.7% in 2024. CIN was 5.96%, however, the operator-reported CIN was only 1.68%. The major determinants of CA-AKI were age, diabetes, peripheral disease, reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease stage ≥2, and fluoroscopy time. The highest impact had the incidence of pericardial tamponade. Procedural perforations were more frequent in CA-AKI patients (10.3 vs 3.3%; p<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (0.9 vs 0.2%; p<0.001) was increased. Contrast volume (CV) was one of the determinants of CA-AKI. No CA-AKI occurred in procedures with <50ml, which was achieved in only 0.5%. In conclusion, CA-AKI remains a relevant procedural complication of CTO PCI even with modern techniques with a slight decrease during the past decade and reduced CV use. Pericardial tamponade had the strongest association with CA-AKI. Ultra-low contrast PCI may not be feasible in an all-comer cohort.

Title: Impact of Infarct Type on Serious Arrhythmic Event Detection and Cardiovascular Outcomes During Telemedical Monitoring After Myocardial Infarction: A SMART-MI substudy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction remain at risk after myocardial infarction (MI) despite not qualifying for primary-preventive defibrillator therapy. Implantable cardiac monitor (ICM)-based telemonitoring facilitates early detection of serious arrhythmic events (SArE), however it remains unclear whether infarct type modifies the detection and prognostic significance of SArE.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effect of ICM monitoring on SArE detection by infarct type and explore associations with subsequent major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE).
METHODS: SMART-MI randomized MI survivors with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction to ICM-based telemonitoring or conventional follow-up. Cox models assessed effects on SArE detection and treatment-by-infarct-type interaction. Exploratory analyses modeled detected SArE as a time-dependent covariate, stratified by arm, for subsequent MACCE.
RESULTS: 400 patients were randomized to ICM implantation (n=201, 122 STEMI) or conventional follow-up (n=199, 114 STEMI). Telemedical monitoring increased SArE detection in STEMI (HR 11.99, 95% CI 3.67-39.17) and NSTEMI (HR 4.44, 95% CI 2.09-9.43; both p<0.001). Although the effect was numerically greater in STEMI, clinically relevant effect modification cannot be excluded (p for interaction=0.154). Detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both, STEMI and NSTEMI with HR of 7.77 (95% CI 3.20-18.86) and 4.26 (95% CI 1.44-12.58), respectively.
CONCLUSION: ICM-based telemonitoring increased SArE detection in both STEMI and NSTEMI patients and detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both infarct types. These findings support further investigation of intensified rhythm-surveillance strategies in high-risk STEMI and NSTEMI patients.

Title: Local Conformal Auditing Exposes and Restores Reliability of AI-ECG Atrial Fibrillation Detection Under External Deployment Shift.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can detect atrial fibrillation (AF), but safe deployment depends on calibration, subgroup reliability, and explicit error guarantees, not on discrimination alone.
OBJECTIVE: To test whether the conformal-prediction coverage guarantee of an AF ECG classifier survives external deployment shift, and whether a small local labeled audit restores it without retraining.
METHODS: A four-class 12-lead rhythm classifier trained on PTB-XL (Germany; 7,831 ECGs, 7,164 patients) was evaluated unchanged on Chinese (Chapman-Shaoxing; n=2,289) and US (Georgia; n=1,990) cohorts. We measured discrimination, expected calibration error (ECE), 90%-target split-conformal coverage, subgroup coverage, label-free shift corrections, local recalibration across audit sizes, and an AF auto-clear policy with finite-sample risk control.
RESULTS: AF AUC remained 0.998 (95% CI 0.997-0.999) in China but fell to 0.936 (0.919-0.952) in the US cohort. ECE rose from 0.051 to 0.197 and 0.237, and source-calibrated coverage fell from 0.901 to 0.758 and 0.722 (both P<0.001). Coverage was lower in Chinese men than women (0.707 vs 0.822; difference 0.115, 95% CI 0.081-0.148). Label-free corrections failed. Local recalibration restored mean coverage to 0.90 with 50 labeled ECGs but with wide variability (95% simulation interval 0.82-0.97), narrowing to 0.86-0.94 at 200 ECGs. Local AF risk control certified auto-clearing of 68% of held-out ECGs in China but abstained in the US cohort.
CONCLUSION: AI-ECG uncertainty can fail silently despite high AUC. A local conformal audit detects when uncertainty estimates are untrustworthy and recalibrates the uncertainty layer without changing the classifier, converting trust into a measurable, subgroup-aware, task-specific guarantee.

Title: Characteristics and Mechanisms of Septal Myocardial Injury and Repair Following Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) requires screwing the lead deep into the interventricular septum. Multiple attempts are often required to achieve proper capture of the conduction system.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of deep screwing attempts on septal myocardial injury and repair and to explore the underlying mechanisms.
METHODS: Prospective LBBAP implantation was performed in 41 patients with bradycardia. Serum creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) and left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (GLS) were used to evaluate myocardial damage. Mechanisms of septal damage were explored in 24 LBBAP canines using histopathological and molecular changes.
RESULTS: Compared to patients with ≤ 3 attempts, those with >3 attempts had a higher incidence of CK-MB elevation (6 vs. 44%, P=0.004), a less negative LV endocardial (-17.9 vs. -13.6 %, P<0.001), and mid-myocardial GLS (-15.3 vs. -12.4 %, P<0.001). In animal study, molecular changes associated with >3 attempts featured amplified HMGB1-centered sterile inflammation and enhanced CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic remodeling. Canines with >3 attempts were characterized by three markedly thickened concentric reparative layers around the lead-inner thrombus layer, middle fibrous sheath layer, and outer reactive fibrotic layer. Interestingly, removal of the pacing lead after >3 attempts resulted in only mild scattered fibrosis, with markedly attenuated CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: LBBAP with >3 deep septal screwing attempts was associated with a higher risk of septal myocardial injury and markedly thickened concentric reparative layers, underpinned by more pronounced sterile inflammation, profibrotic remodeling, and foreign body reaction.

Title: Echocardiographic altered left atrial volume index associated to serum inflammatory biomarkers in patients with autoimmune diseases.
Journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Autoimmune diseases (AD) have significant cardiovascular impact in clinical outcome. Elevated levels of Endothelin-1 (ET-1) and Vascular cell adhesion molecule (VCAM-1) were shown in AD. Given that AD patients often present with altered left atrial volume index (LAVI), we hypothesized a correlation with inflammatory biomarkers.
METHODS: In this prospective, cross-sectional study, we evaluated patients with AD, and compared them to control subjects. The measurements of left atrial dimensions, volume, and LAVI were analyzed. Altered LAVI was defined as ˃34 ml/m2. Measurements of VCAM-1 and ET-1 serum levels were performed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits (ELISA).
RESULTS: A total of 246 AD patients, and 44 control subjects were evaluated. The altered LAVI was observed in 3 (6.8%) controls vs 55 (22.4%) AD patients (p ˂ 0.009). The value of Endothelin-1 in AD patients without altered LAVI was 1.7 ± 1.3 ng/ml vs 2.4 ± 1.8 ng/ml in those with altered LAVI (p < 0.003). There were 3 (6.2%) subjects with elevated levels of VCAM-1 in controls vs 67 (27.2%) AD patients (p ˂ 0.001). The value of VCAM-1 in AD patients without altered LAVI was 600.5 ± 281.1 ng/ml vs 709.8 ± 329.8 ng/ml in AD patients with altered LAVI (P < 0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: AD patients who possess altered LAVI have significantly higher levels of Endothelin-1 and VCAM-1. These biomarkers demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity, and high negative predictive accuracy of the existence of altered LAVI in AD patients. Elevated levels of ET-1 and VCAM-1 are associated to altered atrial structure and may improve risk stratification and clinical assessment of AD patients with subclinical heart involvement.

Title: Perioperative Outcomes After Open Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Tissue-Loss Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia in Patients Aged 80 Years or Older: An NSQIP Analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We compared 30-day outcomes of open bypass versus endovascular intervention in patients aged ≥80 years with tissue-loss chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), in whom trial evidence from younger populations may not apply.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing infrainguinal revascularization for tissue-loss CLTI in the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program vascular-targeted modules (2014-2024) were classified as open bypass with single-segment saphenous vein (OPEN-GSV) or alternative conduit (OPEN-Other), or endovascular intervention (ENDO). Doubly-robust inverse-probability weighting with regression adjustment estimated 30-day risks of the co-primary outcomes, major adverse limb events (MALE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 4,415 patients (2,573 ENDO; 1,124 OPEN-GSV; 718 OPEN-Other). Adjusted MACE risk was 2.9% after ENDO versus 6.5% after OPEN-GSV (risk ratio [RR] 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.61) and 6.0% after OPEN-Other (RR 0.48, 0.33-0.79). MALE did not differ significantly (RR 0.85 and 0.86), with CIs spanning clinically important differences in both directions. Serious complication, any complication, and non-home discharge were lower after ENDO (RR 0.41-0.56); major amputation did not differ. Mortality was lower after ENDO than OPEN-GSV (4.7% vs 6.9%; RR 0.68) but not OPEN-Other (RR 0.87).
CONCLUSIONS: In this population, endovascular intervention was associated with substantially lower 30-day cardiovascular events and systemic morbidity than open bypass, with no significant difference - though not established equivalence - in early limb outcomes. These findings support weighing perioperative physiologic risk in individualized treatment selection; data beyond 30 days are needed to address durability and limb salvage.

Title: Workflow-friendly free-breathing whole-chest cardiovascular MRI using inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Free-breathing cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) may provide useful volumetric information. This study evaluated acquisition time and the feasibility of incorporating highly accelerated free-breathing inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state (bT1RESS) imaging into a standard CMR protocol during the post-contrast interval before late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).
METHODS: A prototype ECG-gated, navigator-gated inner-volume bT1RESS sequence was added to 1.5T CMR examinations in 45 patients; 30 were included in the paired comparison with breath-hold bT1RESS. Series-start timing was assessed in 14 of the 45 patients. Three readers assessed image quality. Aortic diameters were compared between bT1RESS protocols and, in an additional cohort of 15 subjects, with CEMRA. Agreement was assessed separately at five aortic levels using Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: Median inner-volume bT1RESS acquisition time was 1.82minutes (range, 0.78-3.72). In the series-start timing subset, median intervals from perfusion/CEMRA start to TI scout and first LGE series were 6.49minutes (n=13) and 8.46minutes (n=14), respectively. Reader preferences favored the inner-volume over breath-hold bT1RESS protocol. In the CEMRA comparison, mean differences (inner-volume bT1RESS minus CEMRA) ranged from 0.00 to 0.93mm; the lower and upper 95% limits of agreement ranged from -2.47 to -1.16mm and from 2.06 to 3.02mm, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Inner-volume bT1RESS provided rapid volumetric cardiovascular imaging within the evaluated post-contrast workflow. A primary benefit is the capability for 3D vessel measurement without a separate first-pass CEMRA acquisition. The technique may also help identify coronary artery origins, characterize morphological abnormalities in congenital heart disease and other cardiovascular disorders, and help to detect and characterize extracardiac lesions. Larger studies are needed to establish reproducibility and diagnostic performance.

Title: Intravascular Lithotripsy versus Rotational Atherectomy for Calcified Coronary Lesions: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Unintentional 1-Year BMI Decrease After HeartMate 3 Implantation is Associated with Higher Early Morbidity.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight loss after HeartMate 3 (HM3) implantation is desired to decrease the risk of adverse events in obese patients. The implications of longitudinal body mass index (BMI) fluctuations and visceral protein (albumin, prealbumin) kinetics following HM3 implantation remain poorly characterized. We aimed to investigate the association of 1-year BMI, albumin, and prealbumin trends with clinical outcomes to differentiate healthy metabolic improvement from pathological failure to thrive after HM3 implantation.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 168 patients who underwent HM3 implantation at a large academic center between May 2015 and July 2020 and survived for at least 12 months. Patients were stratified by 12-month BMI changes: BMI-Gain (>10% increase), BMI-Similar (<10% change), and BMI-Loss (>10% decrease). Serial BMI, albumin, and prealbumin levels were analyzed for 12 months alongside postoperative adverse events and survival.
RESULTS: At 12 months post-implantation, 58 patients (34.5%) had BMI-Gain, 94 (56.0%) were BMI-Similar, and 16 (10.1%) experienced BMI-Loss. The BMI-Loss cohort exhibited a more profound 1-month nadir in both prealbumin and albumin. BMI-Loss was associated with early morbidity, including longer ICU stay (11.5 vs. 7 days; p=0.027), higher rates of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy tube placement (12.5% vs. 1.7%; p=0.010), and a trend toward increased mortality beyond 1 year (p=0.058). A subgroup of obese patients who successfully achieved a BMI <35 kg/m² had severe early hypoalbuminemia and clinical decompensation rather than physiological optimization.
CONCLUSION: Unintentional weight loss 1-year post-HM3 implantation is uncommon, and these patients tended to have higher early morbidity, lower nadirs of albumin and prealbumin early post-HM3 implantation, and a trend towards higher mortality after 1 year.

Title: Functioning in persons with Spinal Cord Injury compared with the general population.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a harmonized functioning metric enabling direct comparison between persons with spinal cord injury or disease (SCI/D) and the Swiss general population, and to quantify differences in functioning across population and chronic-condition groups.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional comparative analysis using data from the Swiss Spinal Cord Injury Cohort Study (SwiSCI) and the Swiss Health Survey (SHS). Functioning items from the 2012, 2017, and 2022 waves of both surveys were linked to International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) categories to identify items measuring comparable aspects of functioning, which were then psychometrically evaluated using the Partial Credit Model. Suitable anchor items were identified based on item fit, local dependence, and differential item functioning, and used to derive a common 0-100 functioning metric. Epidemiological comparisons were restricted to the 2022 wave, the most recent wave available in both surveys, after exact matching of SHS participants to SwiSCI participants on age, sex, and language region.
RESULTS: The metric-development sample included 1,773 participants from each survey. The matched 2022 comparison included 1,311 SwiSCI participants and 11,836 SHS participants. Combining complete and incomplete injuries within each group, mean functioning was 53.6 (SD 8.8) among participants with paraplegia and 52.0 (SD 9.4) among those with tetraplegia, compared with 74.7 (SD 10.2) among SHS participants without a history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or cancer. Mean functioning was also higher among SHS participants with cancer, 71.6 (SD 12.0), stroke, 69.2 (SD 15.0), or myocardial infarction, 72.4 (SD 12.4), than among participants with SCI/D. Functioning decreased with age in the SHS and paraplegia groups, but no clear age association was observed in the tetraplegia group.
CONCLUSION: This study developed a harmonized functioning metric that enabled direct comparison between persons with SCI/D and the Swiss general population. Persons with SCI/D showed substantially lower functioning than Swiss general-population participants, both with and without major chronic conditions, even after demographic matching. These findings support the use of functioning as a distinct population health outcome that complements mortality and morbidity in health surveillance and health-system planning.

Title: A pathway-level analysis reveals oxidative and inflammatory vascular stress signatures associated with VEGF inhibition.
Abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors (VEGFi) are widely used in the treatment of advanced malignancies, including clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but are frequently associated with cardiovascular toxicities such as hypertension and endothelial dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms underlying these adverse effects remain incompletely understood. In this study, we performed an integrated transcriptomic and functional analysis to characterise vascular stress responses associated with VEGFi. Pre-treatment tumour RNA sequencing data from a public cancer cohort were analysed using Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) to identify pathway-level signatures associated with subsequent VEGFi treatment. No individual genes remained significant after multiple testing correction; therefore, emphasis was placed on coordinated biological responses. Functional validation was conducted in human vascular cells treated with a VEGFi to assess reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, cytokine levels and expression, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) release. Pathway analysis revealed significant baseline enrichment of oxidative stress, inflammatory response, and nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signalling pathways in tumours of patients who subsequently received VEGFi. These baseline associations were complemented by increased vascular cell ROS production and enhanced EVs release in vitro. Inflammatory activation was further confirmed by increased cytokine secretion, despite unchanged messenger RNA expression, indicating regulation at post-transcriptional and secretory levels. Collectively, these baseline tumour signatures and the in vitro vascular findings are consistent with a model in which VEGF inhibition induces a coordinated redox-inflammatory response, which may involve EV-mediated intercellular communication. This mechanism may contribute to vascular dysfunction and cardiovascular toxicity associated with VEGFi-targeted therapies.

Title: Index of microcirculatory resistance-guided management in angina: design and rationale of the DECISIONING trial.
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction may contribute to persistent angina after fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary management. Whether disclosure of the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) and personalized management improve angina-related health status remains unknown.
PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS: Among participants with initial IMR ≥25, disclosure of IMR with protocol-guided personalized management will improve the baseline-adjusted 12-month Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) Summary Score compared with concealed IMR and usual care.
DESIGN: DECISIONING is an investigator-initiated, 16-center French randomized trial (planned n=280). All participants have angina and at least one angiographic lesion ≥50%; FFR and initial IMR are measured before randomization. FFR ≤0.80 guides percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PCI is deferred when FFR >0.80. Participants are randomized 1:1, stratified by center and initial IMR (<25 or ≥25), to IMR disclosure with individualized treatment or IMR-concealed usual care. Participants and treating clinicians are aware of allocation; the initial IMR value remains concealed from control participants and their treating clinicians. Centralized follow-up and outcome assessment are blinded. Coronary flow reserve (CFR) is collected for exploratory secondary physiologic characterization but does not guide randomization or treatment. Enrollment and status Enrollment began on March 31, 2022. As of September 19, 2026, 275 participants had been randomized; enrollment toward 280 was ongoing, with final follow-up expected in october 2028.
CONCLUSIONS: DECISIONING will test the clinical benefit of IMR-informed management while characterizing complementary CFR/IMR physiology in exploratory analyses. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT05178914; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05178914.

Title: Ophthalmic Artery versus Uterine Artery Doppler in the prediction of preterm pre-eclampsia at 11-13 weeks' gestation.
Journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm pre-eclampsia (PE) is a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. First-trimester screening using maternal factors (MF), mean arterial pressure (MAP), uterine artery pulsatility index (UtPI), and placental growth factor (PlGF) allows early risk stratification and effective prevention with aspirin. However, UtPI measurement is technically demanding and operator dependent. Maternal ophthalmic artery Doppler, expressed as the ophthalmic artery peak ratio (Oph-PR), reflects early maternal cardiovascular changes and may serve as an alternative or complementary marker for PE prediction.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the predictive performance of adding maternal Oph-PR versus uterine UtPI to the first-trimester prediction model for preterm PE that uses MF, MAP, and, PlGF.
STUDY DESIGN: This was a prospective observational study involving women attending first-trimester screening at 11+2 to 14+2 weeks of gestation. Maternal factors, measurement of MAP, serum PlGF collection, ultrasound examination for UtPI and Oph-PR measurement, were performed during the visit. Receiver-operating characteristics (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine the area under the curve (AUC), detection rates (DR), and positive screening cut-off from the Bayesian Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) survival models in predicting the occurrence of preterm PE (<37 weeks of gestation). De Long's test was performed to compare the superiority of the AUCs among models.
RESULTS: Of 946 eligible participants, 71 (7.49%) were affected by PE, and 21 (2.2%) had preterm PE. The predictive performance of the UtPI-based model (MF + MAP + UtPI and MF + MAP + UtPI + PlGF) was similar to that of the Oph-PR-based models (MF + MAP + Oph-PR and MF + MAP + Oph-PR + PlGF) in the prediction of preterm PE (AUC 0.805 and 0.837 vs 0.789 and 0.830; p=0.584 and 0.687, respectively). The combination of MF, MAP, UtPI, Oph-PR, and PlGF in predicting preterm PE demonstrated the highest AUC compared to the other prediction models (AUC 0.919, 95% CI 0.875-0.963).
CONCLUSION: UtPI and Oph-PR are comparable for first-trimester prediction of preterm PE. Combining both Doppler indices in a prediction algorithm may improve predictive performance for preterm PE.

Title: Preoperative C-reactive protein/Albumin Ratio and Outcomes After Isolated CABG.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation plays an important role in the development of complications following coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. C-reactive protein-to-albumin (CRP/Alb) ratio is a novel biomarker that reflects the inflammatory burden and nutritional status. The present study aimed to investigate the utility of preoperative CRP/Alb ratio in predicting postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 179 patients who underwent isolated CABG surgery between January 2019 and December 2023. Demographic characteristics, laboratory findings, surgical data, and postoperative outcomes were obtained from hospital records. Preoperative CRP/Alb ratios were calculated using serum CRP and albumin levels. The relationship of the CRP/Alb ratio with POAF development and ICU length of stay was evaluated.
RESULTS: During the study period, 26 patients (14.5%) experienced POAF. The preoperative CRP/Alb ratio was significantly associated with POAF development (p = 0.043), and patients who did not develop POAF had higher CRP/Alb ratios. Additionally, the CRP/Alb ratio exhibited a weak, albeit statistically significant, positive correlation with ICU length of stay (Spearman's r = 0.186, p = 0.013).
CONCLUSIONS: The preoperative CRP/Alb ratio was associated with the development of POAF and ICU length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG surgery. As an easily available, low-cost, and widely available biomarker, the CRP/Alb ratio may be useful for preoperative risk assessment in these patients.
KEY WORDS: atrial fibrillation; C-reactive protein/albumin ratio; coronary artery bypass grafting; inflammation; intensive care unit; length of stay; postoperative .

Title: Perinatal multidisciplinary management for neonates with prenatally-diagnosed congenital complete heart block undergoing early epicardial pacemaker implantation: a retrospective single-center case series.
Journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report our single-center multidisciplinary perinatal experience for neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated congenital complete heart block (CCHB) requiring early epicardial pacemaker implantation.
METHODS: This retrospective case series included four consecutive neonates with prenatally diagnosed isolated CCHB (2016-2020). A multidisciplinary team coordinated perinatal planning. Maternal data, fetal echocardiography, delivery-room resuscitation, vasoactive support, and short-term neonatal outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Four neonates (gestation 35 + 6-37 + 6 weeks; birth weight 2270-2500 g) were delivered by cesarean section. Umbilical vein catheterization was achieved rapidly in all. All neonates had a heart rate <50 bpm at birth and received immediate vasoactive resuscitation. All neonates underwent successful epicardial permanent pacemaker implantation within 10 days after birth with improved cardiac function and were discharged home. One infant was readmitted 8 days after discharge due to pocket infection and ultimately died on postnatal day 46.
CONCLUSIONS: Multidisciplinary coordination, early umbilical-vein access, and individualized vasoactive support are critical for managing these high-risk neonates. Our findings provide practical guidance but require validation in larger cohorts.

Title: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: Evidence from NHANES and mechanistic insights into MECPP-related macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phthalates are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their relevance to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. We examined the associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and advanced CKM syndrome, and explored the potential mechanisms linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-related exposure to macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
METHODS: We analyzed 4236 adults from seven cycles (2005-2018) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A total of ten urinary phthalate metabolites were quantified, and advanced CKM syndrome was defined as CKM stages 3-4 using an NHANES-adapted American Heart Association framework. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess single-metabolite, dose-response, and mixture associations. Mono(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP) was further evaluated using network toxicology, molecular docking, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and macrophage reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).
RESULTS: Among 4236 participants, 648 had advanced CKM syndrome. In fully adjusted models, oxidative DEHP metabolites were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher odds for mono(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP; odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-2.42), mono(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP; OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05-2.42), and MECPP (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68), with significant trends. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations. WQS regression indicated a positive mixture association, with MECPP receiving the highest weight. Network toxicology identified 33 overlapping genes enriched in pathways related to the renin-angiotensin system, insulin resistance, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling, and diabetic cardiomyopathy. Among the candidate hub genes, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) were further examined using molecular docking and Mendelian randomization. Single-cell analyses of public mouse heart and kidney datasets localized Tnf mainly to macrophages and Pparg to cardiac endothelial cells and renal monocytes. In RAW 264.7 macrophages, MECPP potentiated palmitic acid-induced expression of inflammatory and glycolysis-related genes.
CONCLUSIONS: Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites, particularly MECPP, were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome in US adults. These findings support MECPP as a potential biomarker of DEHP-related exposure and generate mechanistic hypotheses involving macrophage-centered inflammatory and glycolytic transcriptional activation. Prospective and experimental studies are warranted to clarify causality and to determine whether DEHP-related exposure contributes to the development and progression of CKM syndrome.

Title: Early-life neighborhood resources and adulthood mortality.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The current study investigated whether early-life walkability and park access were associated with lower mortality risk into later adulthood.
METHODS: Using data from the prospective St. Louis Baby Tooth Study cohort, we linked childhood residential addresses to environmental features on a historical street map. Mortality cases and causes of death were identified through a National Death Index search.
RESULTS: After adjusting for demographics and neighborhood socioeconomic factors, living in areas with higher park density during childhood was associated with a lower risk of non-accidental (HR = 0.95, 95% CI = 0.92, 0.98) and cardiovascular (CVD) mortality (HR = 0.92, 95% CI = 0.87,0.97). Growing up in areas with higher walkability was associated with a somewhat higher non-accidental (HR = 1.04, 95% CI = 0.98, 1.10) and CVD (HR = 1.09, 95% CI = 0.99, 1.20) mortality. Findings were consistent across strata based on sex, year of birth, and neighborhood socioeconomic status.
IMPLICATIONS: Early-life neighborhood resources such as walkability and park access have been hypothesized to be protective against long-term mortality risk; however, findings from this prospective study, while suggestive, only provided mixed support for these relationships. Studies with highly precise measures of greenspace and walkability, as well as key socioeconomic covariates, at various points in the life-course are needed to further investigate the associations identified in this study.

Title: Early post-resuscitation profiles after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A latent class analysis.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early cardiopulmonary heterogeneity after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) may be associated with prognosis and treatment response.
OBJECTIVES: To identify early post-resuscitation profiles and explore their associations with outcomes and randomized treatment effects.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the BOX pulmonary artery catheter substudy, latent class analysis (LCA) was applied to early clinical, echocardiographic, and invasive hemodynamic variables. The primary outcome was 365-day all-cause mortality. Exploratory cross-cohort replication used a separately fitted LCA in the Targeted Temperature Management (TTM) cohort, with 180-day mortality.
RESULTS: Among 700 BOX patients, a two-class model was selected. Class 2 (n = 352) showed longer time to return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), higher lactate, greater cardiopulmonary dysfunction, higher filling pressures, and greater noradrenaline requirements. Mortality was 48% in Class 2 versus 21% in Class 1. No treatment interaction was detected for mean arterial pressure (MAP; P = 0.606), oxygenation (P = 0.483), or fever-control duration (P = 0.946). Mortality discrimination was not superior to time to ROSC alone. In 152 TTM patients, mortality was 38% versus 24% (P = 0.057), with less pronounced hemodynamic separation.
CONCLUSION: Two early post-resuscitation profiles were identified after OHCA, with more pronounced separation in filling pressures than cardiac output in BOX. The profiles were associated with prognosis but did not identify differential responses to the randomized interventions.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: BOX trial, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT03141099; TTM trial, ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01020916.

Title: Efficacy and safety of add-on sotatercept therapy for pulmonary arterial hypertension. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sotatercept is an FDA first-in-class activin signaling inhibitor for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of add-on sotatercept in PAH.
METHODS: Public databases were searched from inception to May 15, 2026 for RCTs and cohort studies of adult PAH patients receiving add-on sotatercept. Primary outcomes included 6-minute walking distance (6MWD), all-cause mortality, hospitalization, NT-proBNP, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), and WHO-Functional Class. Secondary outcomes comprised adverse events, bleeding events, cardiometabolic outcomes, and other tolerability outcomes.
RESULTS: Six studies comprising 2769 patients were included. Sotatercept significantly improved 6MWD (MD: 25.15 m; 95% CI: 7.86 to 42.44) and WHO-FC (OR: 2.34; 95% CI: 1.78 to 3.18) and reduced PVR (MD: -254.23 dyn·sec·cm⁻⁵; 95% CI: -334.46 to -174.00), NT-proBNP (-540.21 pg/mL; 95% CI; -871.47 to -208.96), right ventricular failure (OR: 0.22; 95% CI: 0.09 to 0.51), peripheral edema (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.28 to 0.78) The pooled analyses also suggested reductions in hospitalization (OR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.20 to 0.84; P = 0.01) and all-cause mortality (OR:0.50; 95% CI: 0.36 to 0.70), although the certainty was limited by the available evidence. Most safety outcomes were comparable to placebo; however, bleeding events were more frequent with sotatercept.
CONCLUSION: Add-on sotatercept significantly improved exercise capacity, functional status, biomarker profiles, hemodynamic parameters and clinical profiles, with side effects being generally comparable with control. These findings support the use of sotatercept as an effective targeted add-on therapy to background treatment. (PROSPERO; CRD420261415041).

Title: Remimazolam versus propofol for sedation in mechanically ventilated ICU patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Propofol is widely used for sedation in the intensive care unit (ICU), but its use may be limited by cardiovascular depression, hypertriglyceridemia, and propofol infusion syndrome. Remimazolam has emerged as a potential alternative to propofol, with rapid metabolism, predictable recovery, and flumazenil reversibility. However, evidence regarding its use in mechanically ventilated ICU patients remains limited.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrial.gov databases were reviewed for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing remimazolam with propofol in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. The primary outcome was percentage of time within the target sedation range. Secondary outcomes included sedation success rate, 28-day mortality, ICU mortality, length of ICU stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation. Safety outcomes including adverse events leading to dose reduction, hypotension, and delirium were evaluated. Continuous endpoints were reported using mean differences (MDs), and dichotomous outcomes were analyzed using risk ratios (RRs), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Six RCTs including 705 patients were analyzed. No statistically significant difference was detected in the percentage of time within the target sedation range (MD, -0.45%; 95% CI, -2.46 to 1.55; p = 0.56; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were detected in sedation success rate, 28-day mortality, ICU mortality, ICU length of stay, and duration of mechanical ventilation, or safety outcomes, although several estimates were imprecise.
CONCLUSION: Remimazolam probably results in little to no difference in sedation efficacy compared with propofol in mechanically ventilated ICU patients. However, uncertainty remains regarding clinical and safety outcomes. Larger multinational RCTs are warranted to clarify these effects.

Title: Impact of the updated SOFA-2 score on organ dysfunction assessment and trial outcomes in Sepsis: A reanalysis of two randomized trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score is the standard tool for quantifying organ dysfunction in sepsis. The updated SOFA-2 score may alter interpretation of prior trials. We reanalyzed two adult sepsis randomized trials, Ascorbic Acid, Corticosteroids, and Thiamine in Sepsis (ACTS) and Thiamine for Renal Protection in Septic Shock (TRPSS), to evaluate the impact of SOFA-2 on organ-specific scoring and trial interpretation.
METHODS: Patient data were rescored using a best available SOFA-2 reconstruction. Subscores were compared between SOFA-1 and SOFA-2 at baseline, 24, 48, and 72 h using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Gwet's AC2. Trial outcomes were reanalyzed using linear mixed-effects models with SOFA-2. A post hoc, exploratory sensitivity analysis incorporated approximated urine output into the renal subscore.
RESULTS: SOFA-2 produced lower total scores than SOFA-1 in both cohorts (ACTS 9 vs. 7; TRPSS 11 vs. 10; both p < 0.001), with lower respiratory and cardiovascular and higher coagulation subscores. For the ACTS primary outcome, SOFA-2 (mean difference [MD] -0.8, 95% CI -1.6 to 0.0, p = 0.06) was similar to SOFA-1 (MD -0.8, 95% CI -1.7 to 0.2, p = 0.12) but became significant in the post hoc, exploratory urine-output analysis (MD -0.84, 95% CI -1.64 to -0.05, p = 0.04). In TRPSS, SOFA-2 did not change overall interpretation but attenuated the treatment effect at all timepoints.
CONCLUSIONS: SOFA-2 changes how organ dysfunction is defined and may influence interpretation of prior trials, particularly when urine output is included. These findings support SOFA-version transparency and prospective SOFA-2 validation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTS: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03389555), registered December 28, 2017; TRPSS: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03550794), registered May 25, 2018.

Title: A graph attention and SAINT-inspired transformer model for predicting postoperative atrial fibrillation: A bidirectional external validation study.
Journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common surgical complication. We tested whether a two-stage within-patient architecture-graph attention followed by a SAINT-inspired feature Transformer-adds information beyond strong tabular models and transports across healthcare systems.
METHODS: We used the independent MIMIC-IV and INSPIRE databases. Sixty leakage-controlled scalar features were encoded as tokens for piecewise-linear encoding, graph attention, feature-wise Transformer blocks, and learned pooling. Reciprocal external validation was performed in both directions. Comparators were logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and a baseline-only stack. Component ablations, dense versus training-derived sparse graphs, paired bootstrap differences, and efficiency were evaluated.
RESULTS: In Experiment 1 (MIMIC-IV development, INSPIRE external), GAT-SAINT had an external AUC of 0.844 (95% CI, 0.829-0.858), versus 0.839 for logistic regression; the paired difference was 0.005 (95% CI, -0.001 to 0.011). In Experiment 2 (INSPIRE development, MIMIC-IV external), its AUC was 0.791 (95% CI, 0.768-0.813), versus 0.788 for random forest (paired difference, 0.003; 95% CI, -0.008 to 0.014) and 0.797 for the baseline-only stack. External Brier scores were 0.096 and 0.162. The Experiment 2 validation-locked threshold transported poorly (sensitivity, 0.025; specificity, 0.999). Component and graph-sensitivity effects were direction-dependent, and removal of some modules was compatible with little or no external AUC loss.
CONCLUSIONS: Reciprocal external validation showed transportable rank discrimination but did not establish a consistent advantage over simpler tabular models or a transportable operating threshold. The architecture warrants further methodological study, but prospective validation, recalibration, and clinical-impact assessment are required before deployment.

Title: Reproductive Lifespan and Hormonal Therapy in Relation to Later-Life Neurovascular Health in Community-Dwelling Older Women.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Women are disproportionately affected by Alzheimer disease (AD), a vulnerability that may relate to estrogen fluctuations across the lifespan. Estrogen has neuroprotective and vasoprotective effects, suggesting that lifetime estrogen exposure may influence both AD-related neurodegeneration and cerebrovascular health. However, its association with late-life vascular and neurodegenerative brain changes remains unclear. We aimed to examine the associations of lifelong estrogen exposure-endogenous (reproductive span) and exogenous (oral contraceptives [OCs], menopausal hormone therapy [MHT])-with late-life vascular brain injury and AD-related atrophy and explore apolipoprotein-ε4 (APOE-ε4) effects.
METHODS: This population-based study included cognitively unimpaired women from the Gothenburg H70-1944 Birth Cohort who underwent brain MRI at age 70 and again 5 years later. Reproductive lifespan was calculated as age at menopause or oophorectomy minus age at menarche. OC and MHT use were categorized as ever vs never users. Outcomes included cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), AD-related cortical thickness, and white matter integrity (fractional anisotropy). SVD burden was a composite score derived from white matter hyperintensities (WMHs), lacunes, cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and perivascular spaces (PVSs) (range 0-4). Linear, multinomial, and mixed-effects regression models were adjusted for relevant confounders and stratified by APOE-ε4.
RESULTS: Among 352 women (mean age 70 years), longer reproductive span was associated with lower SVD burden (OR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.86-0.99). MHT use was associated with fewer PVSs and CMBs. OC and MHT use were associated with greater white matter integrity, with combined use showing the highest fractional anisotropy compared with nonusers (β = 0.45, 95% CI 0.12-0.78). No multiplicative interaction between OCs and MHT was observed, although joint exposure analyses suggested cumulative effects. MHT use was associated with greater AD-related cortical thickness among APOE-ε4 carriers only (β = 0.38, 95% CI 0.01-0.76). Longer estrogen exposure was associated with stable cortical thickness and WMH trajectories over time.
DISCUSSION: Greater lifetime estrogen exposure, both endogenous and exogenous, was associated with lower cerebrovascular pathology in women and, among APOE-ε4 carriers, greater cortical thickness in AD-vulnerable regions. These findings support the potential role of cerebrovascular mechanisms linking estrogen exposure to brain aging. Limitations included observational design and self-reported, binary estrogen exposure. Potential cognitive effects require further studies.

Title: Prevalence, clinical characteristics, and etiologic spectrum of extremely low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in Thai patients: a single-center study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extremely low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) is uncommon and may result from secondary conditions or rare genetic disorders. Data on persistently low HDL-C in Southeast Asians remain limited. We aim to determine the prevalence, clinical characteristics, underlying etiologies, and clinical outcomes of patients with persistent low HDL-C.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated adults with persistently low HDL-C (<30 mg/dL) identified via laboratory and electronic medical records between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients were stratified into two phenotypes based on baseline HDL-C severity: markedly low (20-29 mg/dL) or extremely low (<20 mg/dL).
RESULTS: Among 217,481 individuals undergoing lipid testing (1,053,662 HDL-C measurements), 164 patients had persistently low HDL-C (mean age, 56.9 years; 68.9% male). The prevalence of persistently low and extremely low HDL-C was 0.08% and 0.008%, respectively. Concomitant hypertriglyceridemia affected ∼75% of patients. Most cases were associated with secondary conditions. Extremely low HDL-C was more frequently associated with liver disease (41.2%) and active malignancy (29.4%), whereas metabolic syndrome predominated among patients with markedly low HDL-C (42.2%). During a median follow-up of 2.57 years, all-cause mortality was higher in the extremely low HDL-C group (29.4% vs. 11.6%; hazard ratio, 4.33; 95% CI, 1.58-11.91; p = 0.004), while atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease rates were similar between groups (35.3% vs. 32.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Persistently low HDL-C is an exceedingly rare phenotype driven primarily by secondary systemic conditions. An extremely low HDL-C level appears to be a marker of severe underlying systemic illness and was associated with higher short-term mortality.

Title: Prevalence and Incidental Detection Rates of Thoracic Aortic Dilation and Aneurysm Across Computed Tomography Imaging Modalities in a Veteran Population.
Journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence and incidental detection rates of thoracic aortic dilation (TAD) and thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) in computed tomography (CT)-based screening programs (eg, low-dose CT for lung cancer screening) are poorly characterized but could inform opportunistic screening strategies.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort analysis, 9409 consecutive chest CT studies for 6795 unique patients at the Milwaukee Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, were evaluated between January 2023 and January 2025. Radiology reports were reviewed manually. Incidental cases were defined as findings not previously documented in clinical notes or prior imaging. Point prevalence and incidental rates were calculated.
RESULTS: The overall prevalence of TAD and TAA across CT cohorts was 6.1% (95% CI, 5.5%-6.6%) and 1.2% (95% CI, 0.95%-1.5%), respectively. The prevalence of TAD was 8.1% for low-dose CT (95% CI, 7.1%-9.1%), 8.3% for CT without contrast (95% CI, 6.5%-10.1%), and 3.2% for CT with contrast (95% CI, 2.6%-3.9%). The incidental detection rate of TAD was higher for low-dose CT (3.7%) than for CT without contrast (1.9%) and CT with contrast (1.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: Thoracic aortic dilation and thoracic aortic aneurysm are common among veterans undergoing clinically indicated chest CT imaging. Integrating opportunistic aortic assessment into existing CT screening programs deserves prospective evaluation to determine its clinical relevance and impact on downstream management.

Title: Utilizing Coronary Artery Calcification and the COVID-GRAM Score to Predict Critical Illness in COVID-19 Patients.
Journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery calcification (CAC), identified on routine chest computed tomography (CT), has been associated with worse outcomes in hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The COVID-GRAM Score is a risk stratification tool developed to predict critical illness in this population. This study compared the predictive performance of CAC identified on chest CT with that of the COVID-GRAM Score for intensive care unit (ICU) admission among hospitalized patients with COVID-19 and evaluated whether combining these measures improved identification of high-risk patients. We hypothesized that CAC would outperform the COVID-GRAM Score.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study includes 238 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 at a large academic medical center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, between July 1, 2020, and July 1, 2021. Data were obtained through electronic medical record database queries and chart review. Eligible patients had confirmed COVID-19 infection and no prior history of coronary artery disease.
RESULTS: Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, sensitivity and specificity analyses, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The mean age was 64  [SD, 15] years, and 46.2% of patients were women. Patients admitted to the ICU had higher mean COVID-GRAM Scores than those not admitted to the ICU (mean [SD], 168 [45.4] vs 150 [44); P = .01). Any CAC was present in 54.2% of ICU-admitted patients compared with 39.1% of patients not admitted to the ICU, and severe CAC was more common among ICU-admitted patients (18.6% vs 5.6%). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.61 for illness risk score derived from the COVID-GRAM model, compared with 0.58 for any CAC and 0.57 for severe CAC. Composite measures combining CAC and illness risk score did not improve discriminatory performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Neither the COVID-GRAM Score nor CAC effectively predicted ICU admission among hospitalized patients with COVID-19. Combining CAC with the illness risk score did not significantly improve predictive performance, highlighting the need for more robust risk stratification tools.

Title: Vitamin D Supplementation During COVID-19 Infection Is Associated With an Unfavorable Impact of Increased Total Number of Organ Systems Involved.
Journal: WMJ : official publication of the State Medical Society of Wisconsin
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Introduction: COVID-19 is a systemic disease that affects multiple organ systems. We investigated the association between vitamin D supplementation and the number of organ systems involved in hospitalized patients with COVID-19.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 808 consecutive patients with COVID-19 treated at a tertiary care hospital in the metropolitan New York City area between March 2020 and May 2020. The outcome variable was the total number of involved organ systems, defined as a score reflecting involvement of the respiratory, neurologic, renal, cardiovascular, hepatic, endocrine, musculoskeletal, and hematologic organ systems.
RESULTS: Overall, 249 patients (30.8%) received vitamin D supplementation. The number of organ systems involved was significantly greater among patients who received vitamin D supplementation (mean [SD], 4.7 [1.82]) than among those who did not (mean [SD], 3.5 [1.93]; P < .001). Vitamin D supplementation was significantly associated with an increased number of organ systems involved (B,0.30; SE, 0.11; P = .01).
CONCLUSIONS: Vitamin D supplementation was associated with a greater number of involved organ systems among hospitalized patients with COVID-19. Prospective studies, including randomized clinical trials, are needed to confirm this association.

Title: Cardiometabolic dysfunction and age at natural menopause: a prospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Menopause marks a key reproductive milestone with significant implications for women's long-term cardiometabolic health. However, the influence of cardiometabolic health during the reproductive years on the timing of menopause remains poorly understood. We prospectively examined the association between cardiometabolic health profiles and menopause onset in South Asian women, a population at high risk of early cardiometabolic dysfunction.
METHODS: We analyzed longitudinal data from menstruating women aged 30-50 years in the CARRS cohort from 2010 to 2024. Baseline cardiometabolic measures included overweight/obesity (body mass index ≥25 kg/m2), hypertension (systolic blood pressure ≥140 or diastolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg, prior history, or medication use), diabetes (hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%, physician diagnosis, or use of glucose-lowering medication), and non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C ≥ 130 mg/dl). Using Cox proportional hazards models, we examined associations between baseline cardiometabolic status and time to natural menopause, adjusting for sociodemographic and reproductive factors.
RESULTS: Among 2225 women (median age 37 years; IQR: 33, 40), 44% reached natural menopause at a median age of 46 (IQR: 43, 49) years. Women with hypertension reached natural menopause approximately 1 year earlier than those without hypertension. In adjusted models, women with hypertension experienced relatively earlier natural menopause over follow-up (HR 1.34, 95% CI: 1.19-1.52). In contrast, the timing of natural menopause did not differ by baseline diabetes, weight, or non-HDL-C status.
CONCLUSION: Hypertension was associated with earlier timing of menopause in South Asian women. Further research is needed to explore underlying mechanisms and long-term health implications.

Title: Disease burden of rotavirus infection and its complications among children under 14 years old with acute gastroenteritis in China: a multicentre and retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the positivity rate, disease burden, and complications of rotavirus gastroenteritis (RVGE) among Chinese children under 14 years of age presenting with acute gastroenteritis (AGE).
METHODS: A multicentre, observational, and retrospective study was conducted at 11 centres across China (July 2013 - June 2023). Data on RVGE prevalence, direct medical costs, and complications were analyzed, with projections of direct economic burden for 2025 - 2034.
RESULTS: Out of 505,987 AGE visits, the rotavirus positivity rate was 15.70%, peaked at 26.41% in the 12-month period from July 2016 to June 2017, and the annual positivity rate declined by 19.63% between 2017 and 2023. Among 7,113 RVGE cases, 28.57% of inpatients had recorded complications, and the estimated rate of recorded complications among all RVGE patients was 8.29%, most commonly recorded complications being myocardial damage, dehydration, respiratory infection, convulsion, and metabolic acidosis. The median cost of RVGE was CNY 272.80 (USD 40.68) for outpatients and CNY 5336.60 (USD 795.69) for inpatients, respectively. Projected economic burden is estimated to decrease from CNY 8.55 billion (USD 1.21 billion) in 2025 to CNY 3.96 billion (USD 559 million) in 2034.
CONCLUSIONS: RVGE was associated with high complication rates. The decrease in rotavirus prevalence since 2018, highlighting the public health value of a series of preventive measures during this period, including vaccination.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Treadmill prehabilitation attenuates jejunal inflammation and enhances cytoprotective protein expression in murine gut ischemia-reperfusion.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether preoperative exercise protects the intestine itself is unclear. We hypothesized that treadmill prehabilitation acts on the intestine as ischemic preconditioning, and examined intestinal injury and cytokine responses after gut ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) and jejunal cytoprotective protein expression before ischemia.
METHODS: Two experiments were conducted in male C57BL/6J mice. In Experiment 1, mice were randomly allocated to a sedentary or an exercise group; exercised mice completed 1 week of acclimation and 3 weeks of treadmill running. One day after the final session, the superior mesenteric artery was occluded for 45 min. Jejunal and ileal cytokines were measured in 24 mice, and mucosal injury was graded by the Chiu classification in 22 mice, at 3 or 6 h after reperfusion. In Experiment 2, separate cohorts completed 0 (SED, n = 5), 1 (EX1, n = 5), 2 (EX2, n = 4) or 3 (EX3, n = 5) weeks of running, and jejunal HSP70, Bcl-2 and p62 were quantified by western blotting without I/R.
RESULTS: Injury scores were lower in exercised mice (jejunum at 3 h, 1.10 ± 0.22 vs 2.60 ± 0.50; main effect of exercise, P = 0.0025 [jejunum] and P < 0.0001 [ileum]). Jejunal IL-12 at 3 h (adjusted P = 0.042) and IL-6 at 6 h (adjusted P = 0.015) were lower in exercised mice, whereas in the ileum a main effect of exercise was found for IL-12 (P = 0.037) without adjusted between-group differences. HSP70/β-actin was higher in EX1-EX3, and p62/β-actin lower in EX2-EX3, than in SED (Bonferroni-corrected threshold, P < 0.017). Training duration was associated positively with HSP70/β-actin (R² = 0.55, P = 0.0003) and Bcl-2/β-actin (R² = 0.31, P = 0.014) and negatively with p62/β-actin (R² = 0.31, P = 0.014); group comparisons for Bcl-2 were not significant.
CONCLUSION: Treadmill prehabilitation was accompanied by less mucosal injury and a smaller early jejunal inflammatory response after gut I/R, and the jejunum before ischemia differed in cytoprotective and autophagy-related protein expression according to training duration, consistent with ischemic preconditioning of the intestine.

Title: Impact of cardiometabolic and renal phenotypes on the prevalence of type 2 diabetes in the geriatric population of Añisok, Equatorial Guinea: A prospective cohort study (2024-2025).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) represents a growing global health challenge, with management increasingly focused on organ protection and mitigating cardiometabolic-renal risk. In sub-Saharan African geriatric populations, the interplay between frailty, hypertension, and obesity presents critical diagnostic and management challenges. This prospective cohort study evaluated the baseline prevalence of T2D and the prospective risk of major adverse clinical outcomes associated with a concomitant high-risk cardiometabolic phenotype among older adults in Añisok, Equatorial Guinea.
METHODS: A total of 1,702 older adults (aged 60-100 years) were enrolled and followed prospectively from July 2024 to December 2025 (median follow-up: 18.6 months). Participants were stratified at baseline into a High Cardiometabolic Risk Cohort (n = 1,500; concomitant presence of obesity [BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2] AND hypertension [BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or active antihypertensive treatment]) and a Low-Risk / Control Cohort (n = 202; normotensive and BMI < 30 kg/m2). Baseline prevalent T2D, prospective incident T2D (among baseline non-diabetics, n = 612), composite Major Adverse Cardiometabolic and Renal Events (MACRE), acute renal function decline, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and peripheral vascular complications were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance and logistic regression models.
RESULTS: The overall baseline prevalence of T2D across the entire cohort was 64.0% (n = 1,090; 95% CI: 61.7%-66.3%). Among baseline non-diabetic participants (n = 612), the prospective 18-month incidence of T2D was 31.4% (n = 192). Over follow-up, composite MACRE occurred in 17.5% (263/1,500) of the high-risk cohort versus 4.5% (9/202) in the control cohort (adjusted Relative Risk [aRR] = 3.41, 95% CI: 1.75-6.66; p < 0.001). The high-risk phenotype was also independently associated with prospective peripheral vascular necrosis (aRR = 5.82, 95% CI: 1.44-23.51; p = 0.013) and baseline target-organ damage (aOR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.84-2.58; p < 0.001). The prospective absolute risk difference (ARD) for composite MACRE between primary exposure cohorts was 13.0% (95% CI: 9.8%-16.2%), while the overall cumulative target-organ complication ARD was 18.8% (95% CI: 15.2%-22.4%). In secondary subgroup analysis stratified by baseline prevalent diabetes status, diabetic participants (n = 1,090) accumulated 263 composite MACRE events (24.1%) compared to 9 events (1.5%) in non-diabetic participants (n = 612; ARD = 22.6%, 95% CI: 19.8%-25.4%; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant obesity and hypertension are independently associated with a significantly higher prevalence of target-organ involvement and prospective risk of cardiorenal and vascular complications in older adults in rural Equatorial Guinea. These findings highlight the need for early multi-organ risk screening in primary care settings across resource-limited central African populations.

Title: Circulating biomarkers for diagnosis of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in breast cancer patients: A prospective observational study.
Journal: The Indian journal of medical research
Abstract: Background and objectives Doxorubicin is an effective chemotherapeutic agent, whose clinical use is limited by cumulative doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity. Early identification of myocardial injury is essential to prevent irreversible cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated changes in cardiac function and circulating biomarkers associated with early doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity. Methods Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were assessed before and after chemotherapy. Circulating biomarkers, including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), high-sensitivity troponin I (hs-Troponin I), Interleukin-33 (IL-33), and miR126-3p, were analysed. Associations between biomarkers and echocardiographic indicators of subclinical cardiac dysfunction were evaluated. Results Significant reductions in LVEF (65.00±2.17% to 59.50±5.47%) and GLS (-19.04±1.87% to -15.37±1.79%), increased hs-CRP, and moderate elevations in IL-33 and significant reduction of miR126-3p were observed following doxorubicin therapy. There was a significant association between LVEF with hs-Troponin I (P=0.03) and IL-33 (P=0.04), whereas between GLS with hs-Troponin I (P=0.04), IL-33 (P=0.04), and miR126-3p (P=0.006). Among biomarker inter-association, hs-Troponin I was highly significantly associated with IL-33 (P<0.01), whereas no significant associations were observed between hs-CRP and other biomarkers. Interpretation and conclusions Early alterations in left ventricular function and circulating biomarkers were associated with doxorubicin chemotherapy; GLS and hs-Troponin I were associated with myocardial dysfunction, while IL-33 and miR126-3p showed additional associations with strain parameters.

Title: Operationalizing independent oversight in large-scale public health cohorts: Monitoring protocol for the NIMHANS-NH-SKAN Stroke project.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: onitoring the implementation of observational studies are rare, unlike experimental studies. This article aims to describe the development and implementation of a monitoring plan and framework for a large-scale cohort and quasi-experimental study: the NIMHANS-NH-SKAN Stroke project.
METHODS: The monitoring framework was developed through a systematic, stepwise process involving expert consultation workshops conducted by an Independent Monitoring Team in collaboration with the study team.
