A logical framework approach was used to identify key processes throughout the study implementation. These processes were then disaggregated into critical activities (sub-processes) to generate an initial list of monitoring items. These items were prioritized using the Vital-Essential-Desirable (VED) strategy through consensus building. The shortlisted items were further refined using SMART criteria (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound) to finalize checklist components. Key Performance Indicators were subsequently derived from the finalized checklist items. The framework emphasized usability, feasibility, and relevance to implementation, enabling systematic monitoring of critical study processes.
RESULTS: A total of 89 activities were identified and consolidated into 10 checklists, from which 16 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) were derived. The monitoring framework primarily emphasized indicator-based assessment of project outputs and outcomes while ensuring adherence to key processes and quality standards. KPIs were expressed as proportions to facilitate standardized performance assessment across sites and time periods. The checklists comprised a combination of in-person observations and record reviews. Monitoring findings were synthesized into periodic reports based on KPI proportions, enabling objective evaluation of implementation performance and identification of areas requiring corrective action.
CONCLUSIONS: Timely and systematic monitoring is critical to ensure rigor in large-scale projects, and the approach described in this study provides a replicable framework for the development of robust monitoring systems in similar community-based large-scale observational studies in India and similar countries.

Title: Pharmacogenomics-guided cardiovascular therapy in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review of barriers, equity gaps, and pathways to personalized medicine.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease causes more deaths than any other condition worldwide, and four in five of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Pharmacogenomics (PGx) uses genetic testing to guide drug selection and administration, which can reduce adverse drug reactions and enhance treatment response; however, LMIC groups are significantly underrepresented in the evidence base, limiting equitable clinical translation. A systematic review was conducted, following PRISMA 2020 guidance, mapping PGx-guided cardiovascular therapy, implementation barriers, and equity gaps in LMICs. PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies published between January 2020 and December 2025 and included 24 studies (one randomized controlled trial, 19 observational studies, and four economic models); because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were combined through SWIM guidelines, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Genotype-guided warfarin dosing nearly quintupled the time patients spent in the therapeutic INR range compared with standard care, and decision-analytic models supported the cost-effectiveness of genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy. Ancestry-specific genetic variants relevant to heart-failure drug response, statin-induced myotoxicity, and resistant hypertension were identified, yet African-ancestry individuals made up less than 1% of global PGx study participants. The certainty of evidence varied from very low to moderate across outcomes, indicating a near-total dependence on observational designs and small sample sizes. High testing prices, workforce shortages, low physician genetic knowledge, and the lack of locally appropriate prescribing recommendations all remain obstacles to implementation. Based on these findings, a four-tiered, health-system-focused implementation approach is proposed that spans primary care to national policy. To create regionally calibrated prescribing guidelines in LMICs, multi-site randomized trials, ancestry-informed genomic data, and coordinated policy investment are required.

Title: Obesity, frail obesity, and outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation: a pooled analysis of the MOMENTUM 3 trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obesity in patients supported by left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) is linked to excess mortality and haemocompatibility-related events. Whether this association persists with the fully magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 (HM3) pump is unknown. This analysis tested outcomes with obesity and the additive influence of co-existing frailty ('frail obesity') in the contemporary era.
METHODS: The study pooled 2200 HM3 recipients from the MOMENTUM 3 pivotal randomized trial (n = 515) and Continued Access Protocol (n = 1685). Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 and frailty by a 40-item Rockwood cumulative-deficit frailty index (FI), with clinically relevant frailty defined as FI ≥0.325 (moderate-severe frailty); BMI was excluded from the FI to avoid mathematical coupling. The primary endpoint was survival to transplant, recovery, or 24 months of support free of disabling stroke (modified Rankin score >3) or pump replacement reoperation.
RESULTS: Obese patients (n = 887, 40.3%) were younger, less often with ischaemic aetiology, and more frequently women, but more often had diabetes and hypertension, than non-obese patients. Unadjusted 2-year outcomes were similar between groups (freedom from the primary endpoint: 75.1% vs 77.1%, log-rank P = .34; survival: 79.9% vs 81.2%, P = .57). After covariate adjustment, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.58) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.67), as well as heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia, but not stroke, bleeding, or early right heart failure. Frailty affected 67.3% of obese recipients (571/849) and was associated with a higher adjusted risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10), overall mortality and non-haemocompatibilty-related morbidity endpoints. The obesity-by-frailty interaction was not significant for either the primary endpoint (P = .436) or mortality (P = .215), indicating additive rather than synergistic risk; frail-obese patients nonetheless carried the highest absolute risk of any subgroup. Frailty improved by at least one severity class by 6 months in 75.9% of frail-obese patients, and improvement was associated with better survival (adjusted HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.26).
CONCLUSIONS: In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia. Frailty was independently associated with adverse outcomes across nearly all endpoints and was highly prevalent among obese recipients; the combination of obesity and frailty was additive but not synergistic, with frail-obese patients carrying the highest absolute risk. Frailty, however, proved substantially reversible after LVAD support, and its improvement was associated with markedly better survival. Obesity and frailty should therefore be assessed together, rather than through BMI thresholds alone, with recognition that frailty status is dynamic after implantation and that improvement in frailty is associated with markedly better survival.

Title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

Title: The Effect of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Modified Del Nido Cardioplegia Solution on Myocardial Protection in Children Undergoing Congenital Heart Defect Surgery - A Prospective, Randomized, Triple-Blind, Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is an indispensable factor in pediatric congenital heart defect (CHD) surgery. Although effective myocardial protection strategies are crucial, the issue remains a dilemma. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia on myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery.
METHODS: This was a prospective, randomized, triple-blind, controlled clinical trial. A total of 60 pediatric patients were enrolled and randomized 1:1 into two groups - an intervention group that received dexmedetomidine-enriched modified Del Nido cardioplegia and a control group that received standard modified Del Nido cardioplegia with normal saline. Primary outcomes included serum troponin I and creatine kinase-MB levels, as well as coronary sinus lactate levels. Secondary outcomes were the vasoactive-inotropic score, weaning time from mechanical ventilation, and intensive care unit length of stay.
RESULTS: Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing CHD surgery. The intervention group showed significantly lower troponin I levels at all postoperative time points compared to the control group (P < 0.001). Similarly, the dexmedetomidine group had significantly lower vasoactive-inotropic score at all time points (P < 0.001). Patients in the intervention group also experienced a significantly shorter mean ventilator weaning time (P < 0.001) and intensive care unit stay duration (P < 0.001). The overall distribution of postoperative morbidities did not differ significantly between the groups (P = 0.059).
CONCLUSION: Adding dexmedetomidine to modified Del Nido cardioplegia significantly improved myocardial protection in children undergoing corrective CHD surgery.

Title: Feasibility and Early Outcomes of Intraoperative Extubation in Pediatric Atrial and Ventricular Septal Defect Repair via Axillary Thoracotomy.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and early recovery outcomes of intraoperative extubation combined with minimally invasive axillary thoracotomy for atrial septal defect (ASD) and ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair in pediatric patients.
METHODS: Sixty-one consecutive pediatric patients who underwent ASD (n = 43) or VSD (n = 18) repair via axillary thoracotomy between March 2017 and December 2023 were included. Patients were categorized by extubation timing into intraoperative (operating room [OR] group) and postoperative (intensive care unit [ICU] group). Baseline characteristics, operative variables, and postoperative outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: In the ASD cohort, patients extubated intraoperatively had a shorter hospital stay compared with those extubated in the ICU (2.78 ± 1.24 vs. 3.60 ± 0.99 days, P < 0.001). In the VSD cohort, the OR group included younger and lower-weight patients yet demonstrated a significantly shorter hospital stay (3.56 ± 0.73 vs. 5.78 ± 3.35 days, P = 0.013). Across the entire cohort, on-table extubation was associated with reduced hospital stay (P < 0.001), with no increase in reintubation or major complications.
CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative extubation following axillary thoracotomy for ASD and VSD repair in pediatric patients appears safe and feasible and was associated with a significantly shorter hospital stay, even in lower-weight patients. These findings suggest that intraoperative extubation may be considered as part of enhanced recovery strategies in pediatric congenital heart surgery.

Title: A Study of the Relationship Between Postoperative Complications of Acute Kidney Injury After Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and the Control of Patients' Blood Glucose Levels.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the relationship between admission blood glucose and postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) after off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG).
METHODS: One hundred seventy-seven patients who underwent OPCABG in the Cardiac Surgery Department of our hospital were selected for a retrospective study and were divided into 41 patients in the AKI group and 136 patients in the non-AKI group according to the occurrence of AKI in their postoperative period; the indexes of the patients at the time of admission were statistically analyzed using Student's t-test for continuous variables and χ test for categorical variables; and the relationship between preoperative fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and the occurrence of AKI was explored by multivariable logistic regression analysis. Normality of continuous variables was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test.
RESULTS: The preoperative FPG and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) measurements of patients in the AKI group were higher than those in the non-AKI group, and the difference was statistically significant (P < 0.05); the results of the logistic regression model showed that elevated preoperative blood creatinine, elevated preoperative uric acid, elevated preoperative hyperglycemia, elevated preoperative HbA1c level, and elevated preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio value were the OPCABG surgery patients' independent risk factors for postoperative AKI (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative hyperglycemia - assessed by both FPG and HbA1c - is an independent risk factor for AKI after OPCABG. Clinicians should prioritize glycemic control before surgery to reduce AKI risk.

Title: Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events Following Vaginal Estrogen Therapy 2004-2023.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: This study reports on prescription patterns during years when estrogen use may have been influenced by a U.S. Food and Drug Administration black box warning.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate whether vaginal estrogen prescription for genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort analysis using the TriNetX database of women with GSM. MACE was evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional hazard models. High-risk patients had MACE 91 days to 2 years before the index; low-risk patients had no MACE during this period. Comparisons were made between women with and without vaginal estrogen prescription within 1 year of GSM diagnosis.
RESULTS: Between January 1, 2004, and May 16, 2023, 301,701 women were included in the analysis. Of these, 6,152 (2.0%) had a history of recent MACE. Overall, 159,776 (53%) received at least 1 estrogen (estradiol or conjugated estrogens) prescription following GSM diagnosis, of whom 81,446 (51%) only received vaginal estrogen. Compared with controls, the vaginal estrogen cohort had lower odds of MACE (odds ratio [OR]: 0.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84-0.89) and no significant difference in MACE hazard (hazard ratio: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.95-1.01). Recent MACE history (OR: 12.3, 95% CI: 11.7-13.0) and obesity (OR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.21-1.29; hazard ratio: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.19-1.27) were strongly associated with MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Recent MACE history was strongly associated with subsequent MACE. Vaginal estrogen prescription was associated with lower odds of MACE and no increase in MACE hazard.

Title: Telemedicine and Cardiac Service Utilization After the COVID-19 Pandemic.
Reduced desaturation-based detection of sleep apnea events in self-identified Black individuals across two cohorts.
Journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Pulse oximetry may overestimate oxygen saturation in individuals with darker skin pigmentation, potentially reducing detection of desaturation during sleep-disordered breathing.
OBJECTIVES: To assess racial/ethnic differences in desaturation-based obstructive event detection and cardiovascular risk, and evaluate heart-rate response as an oximetry-independent marker for risk stratification.
METHODS: We analyzed participants without cardiovascular disease in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis(MESA) and Sleep Heart Health Study(SHHS). We modeled desaturation-based AHI relative to airflow-defined AHI and examined AHI-ΔHR6, defined by respiratory events with a heart-rate increase ≥6 beats/min. Adjusted Cox models evaluated associations with a composite outcome, major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality(MACE/mortality).
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Black participants had 21% and 20% lower proportions of airflow-defined events meeting the ≥4% desaturation criterion than White participants in MESA (ratio 0.79[95% CI,0.68-0.93]; p = 0.003) and SHHS (0.80[0.68-0.94]; p = 0.008), respectively. No other racial/ethnic group showed a lower proportion of airflow-defined events meeting desaturation criteria than White participants. AHI-ΔHR6 event detection was similar between Black and White participants in both cohorts. In Whites participants, desaturation-based events were associated with MACE/mortality in MESA but not in SHHS, while desaturation-based AHI measures were not significantly associated with MACE/mortality in Black individuals in either cohort. In contrast, AHI-ΔHR6 was associated with MACE/mortality in MESA (HR 1.33[1.09-1.63];p=0.006) and SHHS (1.26[1.02-1.55]; p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: Desaturation-based scoring identified a lower proportion of reduced flow events in Black than White participants, whereas heart-rate-response-based event detection was similar across groups, suggesting oximetry-related under-detection in individuals with darker pigment.

Title: The prognostic impact of cardioselectivity of beta-blockers prescribed during hospitalization for decompensated heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers (BBs) show considerable variation in cardioselectivity (i.e., the relative affinity to the β1 receptor), even among those with evidence of benefit in the treatment of chronic heart failure (HF). We aimed to evaluate whether the cardioselectivity of BBs prescribed during hospitalization for decompensated HF will affect the long-term prognosis of patients.
METHODS: In the prospective study, we followed 4053 patients hospitalized for decompensated HF. The entire cohort was divided into subgroups based on the cardioselectivity of recommended BBs (as stated in discharge summary).
RESULTS: After complex adjustment, patients treated with a highly selective BB (bisoprolol) showed significantly lower five-year cardiovascular mortality than those with a lesser degree of cardioselectivity (mainly metoprolol) [hazard ratio (HR) 0.69 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.52-0.92), p = 0.011]. This difference remained in patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) [HR 0.58 (95% CI: 0.37-0.89), p = 0.013], but was not yet significant in HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) [HR 0.66 (95% CI: 0.43-1.02), p = 0.063]. In HFrEF patients only, highly cardioselective BBs also showed a lower risk of cardiovascular mortality than nonselective BBs with vasodilatory properties (mainly carvedilol) [HR 0.55 (95% CI: 0.33-0.93), p = 0.025].
CONCLUSION: The choice of a BB regarding the degree of its cardioselectivity may have a prognostic impact in chronic HF patients.

Title: Evaluating the Cross-sectional Temporal Trends, Diagnostic and Clinical Relevance of Cell Free DNA in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a potential biomarker for cardiovascular injury, yet its clinical relevance in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains underexplored. cfDNA from 107 AMI patients and 32 healthy controls were isolated and its associations with clinical, demographic and biochemical profiling were explored. Patients were stratified by chest pain duration (0-24 h) to assess cross-sectional temporal trends. cfDNA levels showed six-fold elevation in AMI patients compared to controls and were associated with adverse cardiometabolic and lifestyle risk factors. cfDNA levels increased progressively with chest pain duration, peaking for 18-24 h (median:55.31 ng/mL), and strongly correlated with hs-cTnT (rho = 0.535) and NT-proBNP (rho = 0.615) during this phase. Overall diagnostic performance of cfDNA was good (AUC = 0.858), which further improved in late-phase AMI (AUC = 0.904). Strong diagnostic performance of cfDNA, particularly in the late phase AMI, suggests its potential as a complementary tool to existing cardiac biomarkers.

Title: External validation of the Shankar-Krings angioarchitecture score for discrimination of seizure presentation in brain arteriovenous malformations.
Abstract: About 20-30% of patients with newly diagnosed unruptured arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) present with seizures. However, the mechanisms and AVM-related factors predisposing to seizure onset remain incompletely understood. To address this gap, a score to discriminate seizure presentation based on AVM haemodynamic characteristics (including venous outflow restriction, nidus location, and presence of a long pial draining vein) was recently proposed. Despite its potential clinical utility, the Shankar-Krings AVM seizure score has not yet been externally validated, thus limiting its generalizability. Herein, we aimed to validate the Shankar-Krings score in an independent patient cohort. We conducted an ambispective, single-centre cohort study including patients diagnosed with unruptured brain AVMs. Angiographic features were systematically evaluated, and variables associated with seizure presentation were assessed using multivariable analysis. The three components of the Shankar-Krings AVM seizure score were assigned values of 0 or 1 as originally described. Model discrimination was assessed by calculating the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Of 118 AVMs identified between 2013 and 2024, 45 unruptured AVMs were included in the final analysis, of which 19 (42%) presented with seizures. On multivariable analyses, location in frontal, parietal or temporal lobes remained independently associated with seizure presentation (p < 0.05). Seizure prevalence increased stepwise with increasing score values (0%, 25%, 47%, and 100%; p < 0.001). The score showed good discrimination, with an AUC of 0.845. Seizures are a frequently unrecognized presentation in unruptured AVMs, despite their substantial impact on patient's health and quality of life. As such, they may justify an active interventional treatment. In this study we externally validated a previously proposed score for seizure association in unruptured AVMs. While the three-point score appeared to be a robust and practical tool for estimating seizure risk in this patient population, its role in supporting treatment decision-making requires further prospective evaluation.

Title: Transapical mitral valve-in-ring implantation: Results of the real-world European Tendyne valve-in-ring registry.
Journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is commonly treated with ring-based annuloplasty. In case of recurrent MR, re-do operations are often denied due to high risk. Transcatheter valve-in-ring (V-i-R) procedures offer an alternative. This study assessed the feasibility and outcomes of using the transapical, repositionable Tendyne valve for off-label mitral V-i-R procedures, as an alternative to balloon-expandable valves like SAPIEN, which face limitations such as paravalvular leakage and LVOT obstruction.
METHODS: The TEND-RING registry is a retrospective, international study with prospective follow-up, including 16 high-risk patients from eight European centers who underwent Tendyne V-i-R procedures between 2017 and 2024. Procedural, 30-day, and long-term outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Patients were elderly (median age 79.5), predominantly male (81%), with significant comorbidities (STS Risk of Mortality 5.6%, 4.4-7.2%) and severe MR (3 + /4 +). Procedural success was 100%, with no LVOT obstruction or device embolization. MR was reduced to mild or none in all patients. 30-day mortality was 6.3%. Over a median 11-month follow-up, five deaths occurred (31.3%), three from cardiovascular causes (18.75%). Surviving patients showed sustained MR reduction and improved symptoms (89% in NYHA I/II). Ring size analysis suggested a minimum of 36 mm for rigid/semi-rigid rings, while flexible bands allowed successful implantation in sizes as small as 30 mm.
CONCLUSIONS: Tendyne V-i-R procedures are technically feasible, effective, and safe in selected high-risk patients with recurrent MR. Ring size thresholds identified may guide patient selection and procedural planning in future interventions.

Title: Aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular mortality: smoking exposure as a potential effect modifier-a cotinine‑based observational analysis.
Abstract: Serum cotinine, an objective biomarker of tobacco smoke exposure, may modify the association between regular aspirin use and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) mortality in primary prevention, but this hypothesis has not been adequately tested. We analyzed nationally representative data from NHANES 2011-2018, including 6732 adults aged ≥ 40 years without prior cardiovascular events. Regular aspirin use was defined as ≥ 15 days/month, serum cotinine was measured by mass spectrometry, and the primary outcome was ASCVD mortality. Weighted Cox models assessed associations with interaction terms for aspirin use × smoking status and aspirin use × log‑cotinine. Aspirin use was associated with improved survival in current smokers (fully adjusted HR = 0.15, 95% CI 0.03-0.76), but with worse survival in never smokers (HR = 1.86, 95% CI 1.12-3.10), and a null association in former smokers (HR = 1.65, 95% CI 0.75-3.65). A graded risk attenuation was observed across increasing cotinine tertiles (p for linear interaction = 0.013). Significant interactions were found for both smoking status (p < 0.05) and continuous log‑cotinine (p = 0.009), and sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness. In conclusion, smoking exposure objectively quantified by serum cotinine significantly modifies the observed aspirin-ASCVD mortality association in this observational analysis; biomarker‑informed stratification may offer a framework for hypothesis generation, but prospective validation in randomized trials is essential before any clinical application can be considered.

Title: From a Team of Experts to an Expert Team in Congenital Cardiology: Making Distributed Expertise Usable.
Abstract: Congenital heart disease care depends on specialised expertise distributed across clinicians, disciplines, patients and families. But bringing knowledgeable individuals together does not guarantee that their distinct contributions shape a decision. In complex congenital heart disease, multidisciplinary deliberation must reconcile anatomy, physiology, procedural feasibility, longitudinal risk and patient priorities, often amid uncertainty. We distinguish a team's possession of expertise from its collective capability to make that expertise usable. This distinction affirms, rather than questions, individual clinical judgement, professional responsibility and shared accountability for patients. We propose a testable conceptual framework in which relevant expertise becomes accessible, is expressed and understood, receives appropriate weight, and can revise the team's understanding or decision. Congenital cardiology examples include choices between catheter-based and surgical intervention, anticipation of intensive-care needs, and consideration of treatment burden and family goals. Constructive disagreement may reveal overlooked information or competing interpretations, while patients and families contribute essential knowledge about daily life and acceptable trade-offs. Existing team-science research supports the framework's rationale, but its ability to improve congenital heart outcomes has not been demonstrated. We outline a developmental cycle-map, observe, practise, review, adapt and re-map-through which programmes might examine how expertise enters decisions, identify missed contributions and learn across changing membership. Evaluation should combine prospective measures of decision quality and implementation with appropriately risk-adjusted clinical outcomes, patient and family experience, and longer-term trajectories. The objective is not consensus for its own sake, but better use of knowledge already available to care teams.

Title: Effect of high-power radiofrequency combined with a hypocaloric diet on abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat: a preliminary randomized pilot study.
Abstract: Visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat are associated with metabolic and cardiovascular risk. This preliminary randomized pilot study evaluated a high-power radiofrequency energy-based device (EBD) treatment, alone or combined with a hypocaloric dietary intervention, for visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat reduction. Twenty middle-aged participants were randomly allocated to one of two parallel groups: EBD combined with dietary intervention (7 males, 3 females; mean age 58.2 ± 8.89 years) and EBD alone (5 males, 5 females; mean age 54.4 ± 12.5 years). Both groups received 12 EBD sessions over 6 weeks using a four-channel high-power radiofrequency device. Anthropometric, biochemical, and volumetric abdominal fat measurements were assessed at baseline and post-treatment, with visceral fat additionally evaluated at the 3-month follow-up. Both groups demonstrated reductions in abdominal fat volume. The EBD + diet group showed greater reductions in visceral fat (15.0%) and subcutaneous fat (18.6%) than the EBD-only group, which showed reductions of approximately 9.1% and 9.2%, respectively. Between-group change-score analyses favored the EBD + Diet group for weight and BMI, while differences in visceral and subcutaneous fat did not reach statistical significance. Most biochemical variables showed no clear between-group differences, although exploratory between-group differences were observed for triglycerides, insulin, and HOMA-IR. At the 3-month follow-up, mean visceral fat remained below baseline in both groups. Reductions in visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat were observed in both treated groups. These findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the exploratory design and small sample size. Larger studies are required to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

Title: Early echocardiographic changes during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
Abstract: Patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) are exposed to intensive conditioning regimens that may impose substantial cardiac stress during the peri-transplant period; however, early cardiac functional changes during this phase remain poorly characterized, particularly under protective isolation conditions that limit routine imaging. In this prospective observational study, 56 adult HSCT recipients underwent serial bedside transthoracic echocardiography performed before conditioning (pre), on the day of transplantation (t0), 5 days post-transplantation (t5), and at engraftment (eng). Early cardiac functional decline was defined as a ≥ 10% reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) from baseline. LVEF showed a modest but significant transient decline during the early post-transplant period, reaching a nadir at day 5, with partial recovery thereafter. In multivariable analyses, higher baseline cardiac troponin I (cTnI) levels were associated with greater early LVEF decline. An exploratory model incorporating baseline cTnI, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and age demonstrated moderate discrimination for early LVEF decline (AUC = 0.741) and a high negative predictive value (90.9%). These findings suggest that early transient cardiac functional alterations may occur during HSCT, and that baseline cTnI may help identify patients at low risk for early functional impairment. Validation in larger cohorts is warranted.

Title: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.
Journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
AIMS: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).
CONCLUSION: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Carbapenemase-Producing Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Among Children in the United States, 2019-2024.
Journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current epidemiology of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) among pediatric patients in the United States is poorly described. We assessed trends in pediatric CRE and carbapenemase-producing-CRE (CP-CRE) incidence in the U.S. and characterized recent pediatric CP-CRE cases.
METHODS: We analyzed CRE clinical isolates from patients <18 years submitted to CDC's Antimicrobial Resistance Laboratory Network from January 2019 through December 2024. Annual unadjusted incidence rates for CRE and CP-CRE were estimated overall and by age group for a national convenience sample and an open cohort of 29 states with required CRE isolate submission. Trends were assessed using Poisson regression. For pediatric patients with incident CP-CRE identified from January 2023 through March 2024, medical chart reviews were performed.
RESULTS: From 2019-2024, the estimated national pediatric CRE and CP-CRE incidence increased 51% (IRR:1.51; 95% CI:1.22, 1.88) and 92% (IRR:1.92; 95% CI:1.25, 2.99), respectively; increases were similar in the open cohort. Infants had the highest incidence rates. Overall, NDM-CRE incidence increased (IRR: 4.24; 95% CI: 2.07, 9.16), surpassing KPC-CRE as the most prominent carbapenemase. Chart reviews were completed for 109 of 129 pediatric patients with CP-CRE; 14% were in patients without healthcare risk factors. Among patients with healthcare risk factors, 75% had an underlying medical condition; the most common underlying condition among infants and toddlers was cardiovascular disease (64%) and among older children was neurocognitive conditions (49%) and malignancies (41%). Common exposures across all age groups included intensive care unit hospitalization (40%) and healthcare outside the United States (37%).
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric CP-CRE incidence is increasing, driven by NDM-CRE for which there are few treatment options. Most cases occurred among children with serious underlying conditions receiving high-acuity care. Prevention opportunities may include admission screening for patients with prior healthcare exposure outside the United States and strengthening infection prevention practices.

Title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial.
OBJECTIVES: This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.
METHODS: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.
RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

Title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year.
OBJECTIVES: We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial.
METHODS: Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246).
CONCLUSIONS: The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).

Title: Defining the Substrate in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia: A Hierarchy of Evidence for Arrhythmogenicity.
Abstract: Scar-related monomorphic ventricular tachycardia is sustained by a limited re-entry circuit within a much larger field of diseased myocardium. Late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac computed tomography define scar distribution, channel architecture, wall thickness, and tissue composition, but cannot demonstrate conduction or circuit participation. Voltage mapping and abnormal electrograms identify electrically abnormal myocardium, although their appearance depends on activation sequence, catheter geometry, contact, and annotation. Functional mapping reveals rate-dependent slowing, decrement, and block that may be concealed during baseline rhythm. Mapping during ventricular tachycardia (VT) provides the most direct evidence of circuit participation, but is often limited by hemodynamic instability, noninducibility, or incomplete surface representation of a 3-dimensional circuit. This review examines how to weight these findings when defining the arrhythmogenic substrate. Structural imaging establishes where a circuit could reside and how it may be accessed. Baseline electroanatomic mapping characterizes the electrical expression of surviving myocardium, while functional mapping tests whether conduction deteriorates with changes in wave front or coupling interval. Activation and entrainment provide the strongest evidence that a region participates in a specific VT. These findings should be integrated hierarchically rather than by simple spatial overlap, adjusting interpretation for disease phenotype, substrate depth, mapped surface, and recording conditions. The arrhythmogenic substrate is best understood as surviving myocardium within scar whose 3-dimensional architecture and electrophysiological behavior permit re-entry. A reproducible definition will require standardized acquisition and annotation, explicit reporting of the evidence linking a region to VT, and prospective validation using mapped circuits.

Title: Delays From Clinical Manifestations to Diagnosis of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A National Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, life-threatening condition. Timely and accurate diagnosis remains a challenge. We assessed time from first recorded clinical manifestation to ATTR-CM diagnosis in the United States and characterized manifestations associated with diagnostic delays.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of US claims data (Komodo Healthcare Map, July 1, 2016-June 30, 2024). Patients were required to have ≥3 years of continuous enrollment before diagnosis.
RESULTS: Among 7509 patients, mean age 75.9 years, 63.2% male, 54.5% White, and 28.6% Black. Patients had a median of 8 manifestations before diagnosis; median observed time from first recorded manifestation to diagnosis was 5.2 years, shorter for variant versus wild-type ATTR-CM (4.4 versus 5.2 years). Within 3 years before diagnosis, patients had a mean of 12.04 (95% CI, 11.75-12.35) primary care physician visits and 14.45 (95% CI, 14.10-14.80) specialists of interest visits, most commonly with cardiologists and ophthalmologists. In adjusted analyses, variant ATTR-CM was associated with shorter time to diagnosis (β, -0.41 years [95% CI, -0.56 to -0.26]), whereas comorbidities, including hypertension (β, 0.46 years [95% CI, 0.27-0.64]), were associated with longer delays.
CONCLUSIONS: The diagnostic trajectory for ATTR-CM can be prolonged and challenging, leading to more advanced disease at diagnosis and increased burden. Raising awareness may provide an opportunity for earlier diagnosis.

Title: Incretin-Based Therapies in Prostate Cancer: From Metabolic Protection to Potential Antitumour Activity - A Narrative Review.
Abstract: This narrative review evaluates the clinical rationale for integrating incretin-based therapies as therapeutic adjuncts for men with advanced prostate cancer undergoing androgen axis suppression. Androgen deprivation therapy combined with potent androgen receptor pathway inhibitors significantly prolongs survival but induces severe, progressive metabolic toxicities, including sarcopenic obesity, profound insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and heightened cardiovascular mortality. To address this unmet need, this study reviews published preclinical mechanisms, epidemiological data, and emerging clinical datasets examining glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. The compiled evidence indicates that these agents provide robust metabolic protection by counteracting treatment-induced metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular risk. Furthermore, incretins may exert indirect antitumor effects by attenuating systemic hyperinsulinemia and visceral adiposity-driven chronic inflammation. Direct antitumor activity is also supported by preclinical evidence demonstrating that receptor engagement on malignant cells downregulates oncogenic signaling pathways, which correlates with recent retrospective clinical database trends showing a numerical reduction in metastatic stage migration among men with localized disease. However, dual receptor agonism introduces mechanistic uncertainty due to potential proliferative signaling cascades in neuroendocrine tumor phenotypes. In conclusion, incretin-based therapies offer a highly rational dual-action strategy for metabolic rescue and potential tumor suppression in advanced prostate cancer. Although several early-phase prospective clinical trials are currently underway to evaluate safety and metabolic efficacy, routine clinical implementation cannot be recommended until rigorously designed randomized controlled trials definitively establish long-term safety, optimal patient selection, and durable oncological outcomes.

Title: Effects of a Smartphone-Enabled, Physician-Supervised Treat-to-Target Model for Gout Management: A 12-Month Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether an integrated, smartphone-enabled, physician-supervised treat-to-target (T2T) care model improves serum urate (SUA) target attainment compared with usual care, and to explore its effects on gout flares and systemic metabolic parameters.
METHODS: This 12-month, single-center, open-label, superiority randomized controlled trial enrolled 280 men with gout. Participants were randomized (1:1) to an integrated digitally supported care model (the "1CARE" platform combining automated behavioral reminders, tiered education, remote SUA monitoring, and weekly physician review) or Usual Care. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving serum urate (SUA) <360μmol/L. Secondary outcomes included gout flares and metabolic parameters.
RESULTS: At 12 months, 85.0% (119/140) of participants in the App-Led group achieved the primary therapeutic target of SUA<360μmol/L, compared with 48.6% (68/140) in the Usual Care group (risk ratio 1.75 [95% CI 1.46 to 2.10]; P < 0.0001). The App-Led Care group also showed a significantly lower annualized gout flare frequency (0.02 vs 0.10 flares/year; P < 0.01). Exploratory metabolic outcomes favored the App-Led Care group, with greater reductions in fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol (all P < 0.05), alongside higher medication adherence. Adverse event rates were comparable between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: An integrated, physician-supervised, digitally supported T2T care model significantly improved SUA target attainment and reduced gout flares compared with usual care over 12 months. Multi-center trials will be needed to fully evaluate the generalizability, cost-effectiveness, and optimal configuration of this approach.

Title: miR-200c-3p: An Adjunct Chronic Heart Failure Risk Marker Modulating Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophic Transcription and Cardiac Fibroblast Fibrosis.
Abstract: This study evaluated circulating microRNA-200c-3p (miR-200c-3p) for diagnosis and prognosis in chronic heart failure (CHF) and its regulatory roles in cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis in vitro. A single-center prospective cohort included 150 CHF patients and 80 healthy controls, with CHF stratified into heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF), and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) subgroups. Serum miR‑200c‑3p was quantified by quantitative real‑time polymerase chain reaction (qRT‑PCR), N‑terminal pro‑B‑type natriuretic peptide (NT‑proBNP) and inflammatory markers were measured with a fully automated analyzer, and all subjects underwent a 1‑year follow‑up, with correlation, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Kaplan-Meier, and multivariate Cox regression analyses evaluating its clinical associations and diagnostic and prognostic performance. Gain‑ and loss‑of‑function tests and cell counting kit‑8 (CCK‑8) assays were performed in primary neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) and primary-derived immortalized human cardiac fibroblasts (HCFs). Serum miR‑200c‑3p was significantly elevated in CHF and increased with higher New York Heart Association (NYHA) class, yielding a diagnostic area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 that improved to 0.90 when combined with NT‑proBNP (DeLong test, p < 0.05); it showed numerically higher AUC and specificity but lower sensitivity than NT‑proBNP in the HFpEF subgroup, and correlated with heart failure and inflammatory markers rather than demographic factors. In NRVMs, angiotensin II (Ang II) upregulates miR‑200c‑3p and hypertrophic marker transcription with its overexpression enhancing the hypertrophic transcriptional program, while in HCFs, transforming growth factor‑β1 (TGF‑β1) upregulates miR‑200c‑3p and profibrotic marker transcription with its overexpression further boosting fibrotic transcription and cell proliferation, and miR‑200c‑3p inhibition attenuates all resulting transcriptional and proliferative abnormalities. miR‑200c‑3p is a potential adjunct biomarker for CHF, offering high‑specificity auxiliary value for HFpEF verification, predicting poor prognosis, and modulating transcriptional and cellular phenotypes linked to cardiac remodeling.

Title: Targeting Accelerated Aging in COPD: The AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COpd) Trial Design.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD.
METHODS: AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous. A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV1 decline (>40 mL·year-1) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study; Clinical Trial, Phase III

Title: Prevalence of Transthyretin Amyloidosis Among Older Taiwanese Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The PATCH-HFpEF Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) has emerged as an important but frequently under-recognized cause, particularly in older patients. Prior studies have suggested that left ventricular (LV) wall thickness ≥12 mm in HFpEF warrants further evaluation; however, whether this applies to Asian patients with smaller body size remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: The authors sought to determine the prevalence of ATTR-CM and identify clinical predictors in older Asian patients with HFpEF.
METHODS: In this prospective multicenter study, patients aged ≥60 years with HFpEF underwent evaluation including echocardiography, laboratory tests, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy. ATTR-CM was diagnosed by multidisciplinary discussion integrating clinical presentation, laboratory evaluation, and multimodality imaging.
RESULTS: Among 205 patients, 4.4% (9/205; 95% CI: 2.0%-8.2%) were diagnosed with ATTR-CM, all with wild-type. The prevalence of ATTR-CM increased to 10.2% (9/88; 95% CI: 4.8%-18.7%) among patients with LV posterior wall thickness ≥12 mm, whereas no patient with LV wall thickness <12 mm had ATTR-CM. Higher visual score on technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy was more common with advancing age. In multivariable logistic regression, LV posterior wall thickness (OR: 2.50 per 1 mm increase; 95% CI: 1.54-4.06) and troponin T (OR: 1.15 per 10 ng/L increase; 95% CI: 1.01-1.31) were independently associated with ATTR-CM.
CONCLUSIONS: ATTR-CM is a clinically relevant contributor to HFpEF in older Asian patients, with prevalence markedly enriched among those with increased LV wall thickness. Age, LV wall thickness, and troponin T may facilitate targeted screening and improve recognition of ATTR-CM in older patients with HFpEF.

Title: Management of Coronary Calcified Nodules: A Position Statement.
Abstract: Coronary calcified nodules are an uncommon but important substrate for acute coronary syndromes, stent underexpansion, and recurrent target lesion revascularization. This consensus integrates pathologic, imaging, prognostic, and interventional evidence to guide practical decision-making. Intravascular imaging is essential for diagnosis, mechanism definition, and procedural optimization. Optical coherence tomography provides superior assessment of cap disruption and thrombus, whereas intravascular ultrasound remains valuable when contrast exposure or lesion crossing limits optical coherence tomography. Treatment should be tailored to lesion crossability, calcium distribution, and the need for mechanical scaffolding. No calcium-modification device or drug-eluting stent vs drug-coated balloon strategy has demonstrated consistent superiority. The proposed type IIa/IIb framework is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation. Calcified nodule-related target lesion failure should be managed by correcting the dominant mechanical mechanism before antiproliferative therapy. These recommendations emphasize individualized, imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention and identify priorities for prospective comparative research.

Title: Association of HIV infection with short-term major adverse cardiovascular events among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) suffer accelerated atherosclerotic injury, but real-world Chinese cohort data excluding patients with pre-existing cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases remain scarce regarding HIV-related incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study aimed to explore the independent associations between HIV infection and 2-year incident MACE among Chinese patients with carotid atherosclerosis free of prior cardiovascular events, and identify correlated metabolic and renal factors.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort design was adopted. We enrolled patients with ultrasound-confirmed carotid atherosclerosis from January 2020 to June 2023, excluded individuals with prior coronary heart disease, ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, and conducted standardized 2-year follow-up for all eligible participants. Univariate statistical tests screened variables correlated with MACE; variables with univariate p < 0.05 plus core clinical confounders (age, sex, hypertension, diabetes) were incorporated into multivariate binary logistic regression to identify independent correlates of new-onset MACE.
RESULTS: Patients with HIV infection showed significantly younger age compared with HIV-negative counterparts (63.55 ± 10.81 years vs 70.61 ± 9.75 years, p < 0.001). The cumulative 2-year occurrence rate of MACE was markedly higher in the HIV-positive group (40.4% versus 22.9%, p = 0.023). Multivariate regression analysis verified four independent risk markers for incident MACE: HIV seropositivity (OR = 2.24, 95%CI 1.19-4.22, p = 0.012), baseline active smoking (OR = 1.98, 95%CI 1.07-3.66, p = 0.028), reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (OR = 2.15, 95%CI 1.15-4.02, p = 0.017) and hyperuricemia (OR = 1.89, 95%CI 1.02-3.51, p = 0.043).
CONCLUSION: Chinese people living with HIV (PLWH) combined with carotid atherosclerosis develop atherosclerotic lesions at an earlier age and carry elevated short-term MACE risk. Integrated intervention strategies covering HIV viral control, smoking cessation, renal function protection and serum uric acid management can effectively improve cardiovascular long-term prognosis for this special population.

Title: Factors Associated With Short-Term Neurological Improvement Following Perforating Artery Disease-Related Infarction: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
Abstract:
AIMS/BACKGROUND: Perforating artery disease (PAD) is a common yet heterogeneous stroke subtype with variable short-term recovery patterns. Identifying early predictors of neurological improvement may facilitate the development of individualized treatment strategies. This study aimed to investigate the independent factors influencing short-term neurological improvement in patients with acute infarction due to PAD.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 243 inpatients diagnosed with PAD-related acute ischemic stroke between January 2020 and June 2025. PAD was diagnosed based on isolated infarcts within perforating artery territories on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), after excluding large-artery stenosis and other definite etiologies. Demographic characteristics, clinical features, laboratory results, and imaging data were collected. The degree of short-term neurological improvement (ΔNIHSS), defined as the difference between admission and day-14 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores, was used as the dependent variable. These variables were initially screened using univariate linear regression (p < 0.05), followed by bidirectional stepwise regression based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to construct a multivariable linear regression model. Subgroup analyses were performed according to infarct location (anterior vs. posterior circulation), and interaction tests were performed to assess the modifying effect of infarct location on individual factors.
RESULTS: Multivariable stepwise regression identified fasting glucose (β = -0.205, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.364 to -0.046, p = 0.012), diabetes mellitus (β = -0.180, -0.339 to -0.022, p = 0.026), total cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) burden score (β = -0.255, -0.365 to -0.145, p < 0.001), early neurological deterioration (END; β = -0.238, -0.347 to -0.128, p < 0.001), and baseline NIHSS score (β = -0.158, -0.265 to -0.050, p = 0.004) as independent factors associated with ΔNIHSS (adjusted R2 = 0.283). In patients with anterior circulation infarction, diabetes mellitus, total CSVD burden, END, and baseline NIHSS score were independently associated with ΔNIHSS (adjusted R2 = 0.355). In patients with posterior circulation infarction, only total CSVD burden score and END remained significant, while fasting glucose, diabetes mellitus, and baseline NIHSS score did not reach statistical significance (all p > 0.05; adjusted R2 = 0.290). Interaction analysis revealed no significant effect modification by infarct location (all p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that early glycemic monitoring, CSVD burden assessment, and END surveillance may facilitate risk stratification, and that underlying microvascular pathology may impair neurorepair capacity in PAD patients. Total CSVD burden and END exhibited the largest effect sizes, followed by fasting glucose, diabetes mellitus, and baseline NIHSS score, all of which are independent predictors. The effects of these factors do not differ significantly between anterior and posterior circulation infarctions.

Title: A Machine Learning-Based Predictive Model for One-Year All-Cause Readmission in Chronic Heart Failure: Implications for Precision Nursing Interventions.
Journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
Abstract:
AIMS/BACKGROUND: This study aims to develop and validate a machine learning model for predicting 1-year all-cause readmission in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF), and to assess its clinical utility in early risk stratification and targeted nursing interventions.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 293 patients with chronic heart failure (CHF) who were consecutively admitted to Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between January 2023 and May 2024. Participants were randomly allocated into a training cohort (n = 205) and a validation cohort (n = 88). Multidimensional clinical variables were extracted from the electronic medical record system of the hospital. Feature selection was performed using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression (with 10-fold cross-validation and the minimum lambda plus one standard deviation criterion to select λ to prevent overfitting). Five machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, ElasticNet, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT), were developed, and their predictive performance was compared. The hyperparameters of the model were optimized with grid search combined with 10-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, and F1 score. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were applied to interpret the optimal model.
RESULTS: The GBDT-based model demonstrated the strongest predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.969 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.950-0.988), a sensitivity of 0.896, and a specificity of 0.922 in the internal validation set. SHAP analysis identified N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class, respiratory infection, hyponatremia, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 as the top five predictors associated with readmission risk.
CONCLUSION: The GBDT-based machine learning model effectively predicts 1-year all-cause readmission in CHF patients, demonstrating superior discriminative accuracy and interpretability via SHAP analysis, offering a clinically practical tool for management. Given the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size, future validation in larger multicenter studies is warranted before broader clinical application.

Title: The Effect of Repetitive Facilitative Exercise Combined With Electromyography Biofeedback in Promoting Limb Function Rehabilitation in Patients With Post-Stroke Hemiplegia.
Journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
Abstract:
AIMS/BACKGROUND: Hemiplegia is a common complication following a stroke, resulting in decreased motor function. Although various treatment options are available, there is currently insufficient evidence to determine the definitive superiority of any single treatment modality, and the effectiveness of using a single therapy remains limited. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the efficacy and safety of combining repetitive facilitative exercise (RFE) with electromyography (EMG) biofeedback in managing patients with post-stroke hemiplegia.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 106 patients with post-stroke hemiplegia who were treated at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Qiqihar Medical University, China, between January 2022 and January 2024. Patients who received RFE alone were included in the RFE group (n = 51), while those who received the combination of RFE and EMG biofeedback treatment were included in the RFE+EMG group (n = 55). Both groups were treated continuously for 12 weeks. The limb function (Fugl-Meyer Assessment [FMA]), balance ability (Berg Balance Scale [BBS], Timed Up and Go Test [TUGT], 10-Meter Walk Test [10MWT]), and quality of life (Stroke Specific Quality of Life Scale [SS-QOL]) were comparatively assessed between the two groups before treatment and 12 weeks after treatment. Additionally, the incidence of adverse events throughout the treatment period was recorded for both groups.
RESULTS: After treatment, the FMA scores showed significant improvements in both groups compared to their pre-treatment values (p < 0.05). Notably, the RFE+EMG group exhibited significantly higher improvements in upper extremity, lower extremity and overall scores compared to the RFE group after treatment (p < 0.05). Following the intervention, both groups demonstrated a substantial increase in the BBS score compared to their scores before treatment (p < 0.05). In contrast, the TUGT and 10MWT were significantly shortened in both groups compared to their times before treatment (p < 0.05). Notably, the RFE+EMG group exhibited significantly higher BBS scores (p < 0.05) and significantly shorter TUGT and 10MWT times compared to the RFE group after treatment (p < 0.05). After treatment, the SS-QOL scores increased significantly in both groups compared to their scores before treatment (p < 0.05). Notably, the RFE+EMG group exhibited significantly higher scores in energy, family roles, language, mobility, mood, personality, self-care, social roles, thinking, upper extremity function, vision and work/productivity compared to the RFE group after treatment (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The combination of RFE and EMG biofeedback shows promising effects in limb functional recovery, improving balance ability, and enhancing quality of life in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia, while also demonstrating a favourable safety profile, with no severe adverse events reported.

Title: Effects of Different Stimulation Parameters on the Efficacy of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Post-Stroke Dysphagia: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
Abstract:
AIMS/BACKGROUND: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a promising intervention for post-stroke dysphagia (PSD). However, no consensus has been reached regarding the optimal stimulation parameters. This study aimed to identify the optimal tDCS stimulation protocol for patients with PSD.
METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, we systematically searched seven databases (Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, WanFang, CNKI, and VIP) for relevant trials, covering the period from database inception to 1 January 2025. Statistical analyses were performed with Review Manager 5.40, with the choice of fixed- or random-effects model guided by I2 values.
RESULTS: Overall, tDCS significantly improved swallowing function compared with control conditions for both outcome measures in which higher scores indicate better swallowing function (standardized mean difference (SMD) = 1.16, p < 0.001) and those in which lower scores indicate better swallowing function (SMD = -0.85, p < 0.001). In the subgroup analysis by stimulation intensity, 1.4 mA yielded the largest point estimate among positive-direction outcomes (SMD = 1.91, p = 0.04), whereas 1.8 mA yielded the largest effect estimate among negative-direction outcomes (SMD = -0.82, p = 0.04). Both single-session tDCS lasting 20 minutes and 30 minutes significantly improved swallowing function in patients with PSD (positive outcome indicators, 20 min: SMD = 1.18, p < 0.001; 30 min: SMD = 1.28, p = 0.02, subgroup difference: p = 0.86; negative outcome indicators, 20 min: SMD = -0.69, p < 0.001; 30 min, SMD = -0.70, p = 0.005, subgroup difference, p = 0.89). However, prolonging single-session duration to 30 minutes did not confer superior therapeutic efficacy relative to 20 minutes. tDCS was effective for both supratentorial and infratentorial lesions (positive outcome indicators, SMD = 1.57, p < 0.001; negative outcome indicators, SMD = -0.73, p < 0.001). Compared with the control group, swallowing function was improved in acute, sub-acute and chronic stroke patients treated with tDCS intervention (positive outcome indicators, Acute: SMD = 1.17, p < 0.0001; Subacute: SMD = 1.72, p < 0.0001; Chronic: SMD = 0.59, p = 0.0004; negative outcome indicators, Acute: SMD = -0.78, p < 0.0001; Sub-acute: SMD = -0.91, p = 0.0001; Chronic: SMD = -0.77, p = 0.001). tDCS significantly improved swallowing function in patients with pseudobulbar palsy (SMD = -0.86, p = 0.001), whereas it showed no obvious therapeutic effect on patients with bulbar palsy (SMD = -0.48, p = 0.07).
CONCLUSION: tDCS yields favorable effects on swallowing function in patients with PSD when administered to the lesional hemisphere, the contralesional hemisphere, or bilaterally, and there are no differences in efficacy among the three stimulation modes. An intensity of 1.8 mA represents a potential optimal "sweet spot", suggesting that higher intensities (2.0 mA) do not necessarily translate to better clinical outcomes. A 20-minute session duration is sufficient for therapeutic effect.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD42022344115).

Title: Prevalence and clinical associations of age-related clonal haematopoiesis in SSc.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: SSc is an autoimmune disease involving both innate and adaptive immunity, characterized by progressive organ fibrosis. Age-related clonal haematopoiesis (ARCH) results from somatic mutations in haematopoietic progenitors and is increasingly implicated in inflammation and autoimmunity. We aimed to assess the prevalence of ARCH in patients with SSc and its association with disease characteristics.
METHODS: Targeted myeloid next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed in 196 patients with SSc and 392 age- and gender-matched individuals without SSc and referred for NGS without a final diagnosis myelodysplastic syndrome. Variants with variant allele frequency (VAF) ≥ 0.8% were considered for ARCH analysis. Clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) was defined as ARCH with a VAF ≥2%.
RESULTS: The prevalence of ARCH and CHIP was similar between SSc patients and the control group: 32.7% vs 37.2% (P = 0.25) and 23.5% vs 28.8% (P = 0.15), respectively. Among patients with SSc, ARCH was associated with higher NT-proBNP levels and higher prevalence of progressive interstitial lung disease (39.1% vs 15.7%, P = 0.026), pulmonary hypertension (23.4% vs 11.4%, P = 0.028), valvular heart disease (23.4% vs 11.4%, P = 0.028), ACAs (65.1% vs 49.6%, P = 0.043) in our cohort. After adjustment to age and gender, only NT-proBNP levels remain significantly higher in SSc patients with ARCH. These associations were not observed when restricting the analysis to CHIP except for valvular heart disease (26.1% vs 11.4%, P = 0.019) and higher NT-proBNP levels.
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of ARCH and CHIP was 32.7% and 23.5%, respectively, in our cohort of patients with SSc presence of ARCH was associated with more severe pulmonary involvement, a higher frequency of pulmonary hypertension, valvular heart disease and ACAs. After adjustment to age and sex, ARCH was associated with a higher NT-pro BNP levels.

Title: Multi-Omics Analysis Uncovers a Link Between Dysregulated Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis and Pediatric IgA Vasculitis Nephritis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: IgA vasculitis (IgAV) is a systemic vasculitis with variable clinical manifestations, ranging from self-limiting cutaneous purpura and joint pain to severe gastrointestinal and renal involvement. However, whether specific metabolites are associated with these heterogeneous clinical manifestations remains unclear. This study aimed to identify metabolic and proteomic signatures associated with distinct clinical manifestations of IgAV, particularly IgAV nephritis (IgAVN), and to identify molecular features potentially associated with disease pathogenesis.
METHODS: We performed liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based metabolomic and exploratory proteomic analyses of plasma samples from patients with IgAV with isolated cutaneous purpura or additional joint, gastrointestinal, or renal involvement and from healthy controls.
RESULTS: Metabolomic analysis revealed significant differences between patients with IgAV, including those with IgAVN, and healthy controls. A total of 65 differentially abundant metabolites were identified, with the steroid hormone biosynthesis pathway among the most prominently altered pathways. Notably, patients with IgAVN exhibited a distinct metabolomic profile compared with patients without renal involvement. Levels of six steroids and steroid metabolites, including tetrahydrocorticosterone, tetrahydrocortisone, cortisone, aldosterone, androsterone glucuronide, and progesterone, decreased in patients with IgAVN compared with healthy controls. Proteomic profiling identified 50 upregulated and 12 downregulated proteins in patients with IgAV compared with healthy controls, with enrichment of pathways related to platelet activation and complement and coagulation cascades. Compared with healthy controls, 33 upregulated and 154 downregulated proteins were identified in the IgAVN group. Additionally, IgAVN was associated with a distinct proteomic signature involving the intestinal immune network, B cell receptor signaling, and cholesterol metabolism. Decreased levels of steroids and steroid metabolites were significantly associated with alterations in immunoglobulins and coagulation factors identified by exploratory proteomic analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Integrated metabolomic and proteomic analyses identified distinct molecular signatures associated with IgAV and IgAVN. Decreased levels of steroids and steroid metabolites and alterations in immune response, coagulation, and lipid metabolic pathways were particularly associated with IgAVN. These findings provide insights into the molecular features associated with IgAV and identify candidate biomarkers of disease severity and potential therapeutic targets that warrant further investigation.

Title: Trajectories of a Composite Lipid, Glucose, and Refined Obesity Index Predict Cardiovascular Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance and central adiposity are key drivers of cardiovascular disease (CVD).
