Although the CHG index and obesity-related indicators can separately predict metabolic risks, this study explored the predictive value of their composite indices and longitudinal trajectories for incident CVD.
METHODS: Based on 4164 middle-aged and elderly participants from a national prospective cohort, we analyzed baseline levels, cumulative exposures and K-means-defined longitudinal trajectories of CHG-related composite indices. Cox regression, ROC analysis, and weighted quantile sum regression were adopted to explore CVD associations and predictive efficiency.
RESULTS: During an 8-year median follow-up, 22.14% of participants developed CVD. Elevated baseline values, increased cumulative exposure, and unfavorable trajectories of composite indices were linked to higher CVD risk. Per 1-SD rise in baseline CHG-WC and CHG-CVAI corresponded to 19% and 17% higher CVD risk, respectively. Their addition produced statistically significant improvements in predictive performance and risk stratifying capacity of the Framingham Risk Score, as further supported by NRI and IDI analyses.
CONCLUSION: Longitudinal trajectories and cumulative exposures of CHG-obesity composite indices serve as reliable independent predictors of CVD. Dynamic monitoring of these indicators facilitates early CVD risk stratification.

Title: Psychosocial stressors at work and hypertension incidence: a prospective cohort study of multiple exposures.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain and effort-reward imbalance (ERI) models are frequent and modifiable exposures associated with increased blood pressure levels. The adverse effect of combined exposure to both work stressors on hypertension incidence remains unknown. This study aimed to examine this association in a long-term prospective cohort.
METHODS: The study included 9188 white-collar workers recruited at T1 (1991-1993), with follow-ups at T2 (1999-2001) and T3 (2015-2018). Exposures to psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain (T1 and T2) and ERI (T2) models were measured using validated instruments. Incident hypertension cases were identified using medico-administrative databases and automated office blood pressure measurements. Semi-parametric proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR). Analyses included normotensive workers at baseline: N = 6732 over 24 years (T1 to T3) and N = 4516 over 18 years (T2 to T3).
RESULTS: Over 24 years, workers exposed to passive jobs [low psychological demands and low decision latitude; HR = 1.19 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.05-1.34)], active jobs [high psychological demands and high decision latitude; HR = 1.23 (95% CI: 1.08-1.40)], and high strain [high psychological demands and low decision latitude; HR = 1.26 (95% CI: 1.11-1.44)] had an increased risk of hypertension. Over 18 years, workers exposed to active jobs [HR = 1.20 (95% CI: 1.03-1.39)], ERI [HR = 1.19 (95% CI: 1.06-1.33)], and both [HR = 1.34 (95% CI: 1.14-1.56)] had an increased risk of hypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: Psychosocial stressors at work from the job strain and ERI models were associated, separately and in combination, with an increased risk of hypertension.

Title: [Not Available].
Abstract: FitPreV assessed the feasibility of integrating polygenic risk scores and wearable health devices into cardiovascular primary prevention in general practice. In this four-arm pilot randomized trial, 120 adults with metabolic syndrome were followed for 12 months. Recruitment was high and acceptability was favourable, with low anxiety after polygenic risk score (Prs) disclosure. However, 12-month follow-up completeness and GP willingness to implement the intervention require improvement.
Publication Types: Randomized Controlled Trial; Journal Article; English Abstract

Title: Tirzepatide for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea: from apnea-hypopnea index reduction to cardiometabolic risk mitigation-a narrative review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a chronic respiratory disorder with nocturnal oxygen desaturation that is often associated with multisystemic sequelae such as hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, and increased morbidity and mortality. Obesity has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor; hence, the recent shift in focus to investigating anti-obesity medications for the management of OSA. Tirzepatide is the first U.S. FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for the treatment of moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity to be utilized in combination with low caloric intake and physical activity, given its prior success in managing type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity.
METHODS: This narrative review evaluates tirzepatide and the SURMOUNT-OSA trial program as the key contemporary anchors for the pharmacological treatment of OSA in adults with concurrent obesity. Because the randomized evidence base currently comprises a single pivotal trial program, the review centers on SURMOUNT-OSA and its prespecified endpoints along with post hoc analyses, supplemented by observational, modeling, and mechanistic studies.
RESULTS: In the SURMOUNT-OSA program, tirzepatide produced randomized, placebo-controlled reductions in the apnea-hypopnea index, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, and systemic inflammation. The program was designed around respiratory and metabolic endpoints rather than clinical events, so it cannot support conclusions about mortality, cardiovascular, or renal outcomes. Favorable signals for those events, including all-cause mortality, major adverse kidney events, and major adverse cardiovascular events, come only from nonrandomized observational cohorts and are best regarded as directional and exploratory rather than definitive.
CONCLUSIONS: Tirzepatide may help frame OSA as a multifactorial and partially metabolically treatable disease and may represent a clinically meaningful expansion of treatment options alongside, rather than as a replacement for, established mechanical and procedural therapies. The available evidence is anchored in a single phase 3 trial program and limited by short follow-up and the absence of definitive comparative and long-term outcome data. Long-term durability of effect after discontinuation, generalizability beyond the SURMOUNT-OSA-eligible population, OSA-specific economic analysis, and head-to-head comparisons against CPAP remain the principal unsettled questions requiring dedicated long-term studies before firm clinical recommendations can be made.

Title: All-cause and cause-specific mortality in people with rare autoimmune rheumatic diseases in England using whole population data.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: People with rare autoimmune rheumatic diseases (RAIRD) experience morbidity and premature mortality due to disease activity and immunosuppression. We conducted a nationwide, whole-population retrospective cohort study using linked routinely collected healthcare data in England.
METHODS: All individuals in England with a RAIRD diagnosis recorded in hospital admissions data and alive in 2013 were included. Linked demographic and death certificate data were used to calculate crude and age-sex-standardised mortality rates for all causes and leading causes of death from 2013 to 2020. Rates were compared with Office for National Statistics data for the general population of England.
RESULTS: There were 53,237 deaths among people with RAIRD. The cohort was 69.9% female, median age rose from 61.5 to 62.5 years during the study. All-cause mortality declined between 2013 and 2019 but rose in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. The age-sex-standardised mortality rate ratio versus the general population decreased from 2.6 (95% CI 2.6-2.7) in 2013 to 2.3 (2.2-2.3) in 2020. Mortality was particularly elevated for infection (rate ratio 4.10, 3.81-4.39), cardiovascular disease (2.50, 2.45-2.55), COVID-19 (2.74, 2.59-2.89) and respiratory disease (2.90, 2.82-2.98). Highest all-cause mortality occurred in systemic sclerosis, polymyositis/dermatomyositis, microscopic polyangiitis and unspecified arteritis. Deaths from opportunistic infections were rare.
CONCLUSIONS: Mortality in RAIRD remains more than twice that of the general population despite modest improvement over time. Infection, respiratory disease and COVID-19 remain major contributors, highlighting the need for targeted infection prevention and cardiovascular risk management.

Title: Association of platelet level and white blood cell level with coronary artery lesions persistence among patients with Kawasaki disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute febrile multisystem vasculitis with the most serious complication being coronary artery lesions (CALs). However, factors related to CALs persistence remain unclear. This study investigated the association between platelet (PLT) level and CALs persistence at one month in KD patients who had CALs before intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment, and explored potential interaction factors.
METHODS: We conducted a study of 170 KD patients with CALs prior to IVIG treatment. CALs persistence was defined as an increase or no decrease in coronary artery Z-scores at one-month follow-up. Using logistic regression, we assessed the independent association of PLT level (categorized as < 300 × 10^9/L, 300-450 × 10^9/L and ≥450 × 10^9/L) and their interaction with WBC level on CALs persistence.
RESULTS: Among the patients, 74 (43.5%) had CAL persistence at one month. A dose-response relationship was observed between higher PLT level and CALs persistence at one month. Patients with PLT ≥450 × 10^9/L had increased odds of CAL persistence at one month (adjusted OR = 4.860, 95% CI: 1.278, 18.487). We observed a nominally significant interaction between PLT and WBC level (P = 0.049). Exploratory analysis suggested higher odds in patients with both PLT ≥450 × 10^9/L and WBC >15 × 10^9/L (adjusted OR = 6.101, 95% CI: 0.620, 60.012).
CONCLUSION: A high PLT level (≥450 × 10^9/L) is independently associated with CAL persistence at one month in KD patients with pre-IVIG CALs. The coexistence of high PLT and high WBC level may be associated with increased odds of CALs persistence at one month, requiring confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 emerge as a novel antigenic axis linked to atherosclerosis in rheumatoid arthritis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular risk excess in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) cannot be explained by traditional risk factors alone. Recent experimental data have identified ALDH4A1 as a mitochondrial self-antigen implicated in atherosclerosis, yet its clinical significance in human autoimmunity remains unexplored. We aimed to characterize ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 antibody levels in early RA, and evaluate their associations with atherosclerosis burden and lipoprotein traits.
METHODS: ALDH4A1 and anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies (IgM, IgG, IgA, and IgG subclasses) were measured in early RA (n = 82), clinically suspect arthralgia (n = 14), healthy controls (n = 70), and a validation cohort of established RA. A prospective cohort (n = 13) explored therapeutic modulation under TNF blockade. Associations with atherosclerosis burden, lipid/lipoprotein profiles, oxylipin signatures, proteomics, and cell-free DNA were assessed.
RESULTS: ALDH4A1 serum levels were associated with apoptotic-related proteomic pathways, cell-free DNA and lipidomic signatures in early RA. Reduced anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies were found, although divergent patters were noted across isotypes. These differences were confirmed in a validation cohort. IgG (predominantly IgG3) anti-ALDH4A1 correlated with favourable lipoprotein traits and cardiometabolic risk factors. Increased ALDH4A1 and reduced IgM/IgG anti-ALDH4A1 antibodies independently predicted atherosclerosis and improved risk stratification beyond mSCORE, most notably for IgG. ALDH4A1 tracked with TNF dynamics under TNF blockade, whereas increases in IgG antibodies occurred in responders and paralleled changes in lipoprotein features.
CONCLUSIONS: The ALDH4A1/anti-ALDH4A1 axis emerges as a novel player bridging lipid disturbances and atherosclerosis along the whole RA continuum, hence highlighting the involvement of mitochondrial targets. These components hold promise as functional players, clinical tools and therapeutic targets.

Title: Association between preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and left internal mammary artery end-diastolic velocity in patients undergoing CABG.
Journal: Turk gogus kalp damar cerrahisi dergisi
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammation has been implicated in endothelial dysfunction and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is a readily available marker of systemic inflammation; however, its relationship with preoperative left internal mammary artery (LIMA) end-diastolic velocity (EDV) remains poorly understood. We evaluated the association between preoperative NLR and native LIMA EDV in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 150 consecutive patients undergoing isolated CABG. Patients were categorized by preoperative NLR as low (<2), intermediate (2-4), or high (>4). Preoperative LIMA Doppler ultrasonography assessed vessel diameter, flow volume, peak systolic velocity (PSV), and EDV. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlation and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses.
RESULTS: Of 150 patients, 40 (26.7%), 104 (69.3%), and 6 (4.0%) were classified into the low, intermediate, and high NLR groups, respectively. C-reactive protein (CRP) differed significantly across all three groups (all adjusted p≤0.029), while fibrinogen and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) were higher in the intermediate and high groups than in the low group. Among LIMA Doppler parameters, only EDV showed a graded decrease across NLR categories (median 35, 27, and 20 cm/s, respectively; all pairwise adjusted p≤0.014); diameter, flow volume, and PSV did not differ significantly. NLR was strongly inversely correlated with LIMA EDV (Spearman's rho=-0.885, p<0.001), while CRP, fibrinogen, and ESR also showed significant inverse correlations. In multivariable analysis, higher NLR remained independently associated with lower LIMA EDV after adjustment for demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, and left ventricular ejection fraction (B=-6.298, 95% confidence inter val: -7.071 to -5.524; p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Higher preoperative NLR was independently associated with lower native LIMA EDV, while other inflammatory markers were also inversely associated with EDV. These findings indicate an association between systemic inflammatory status and native LIMA diastolic hemodynamics but do not establish causality or clinical prognostic significance. Prospective studies incorporating postoperative graft assessment and clinical follow-up are warranted.

Title: [Diagnosis of amyloidosis].
Abstract: Given the availability of highly effective treatment options, early diagnosis of cardiac amyloidosis is more important than ever. In many cases, the diagnosis can now be made non-invasively, provided that clinical suspicion is raised in a timely manner. Warning signs such as heart failure, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, spinal stenosis, or an abnormal voltage-to-mass ratio on the ECG should prompt further investigation. Echocardiography allows for the detection of typical morphological and functional changes, while the simultaneous exclusion of monoclonal gammopathy via three simple laboratory tests determines the subsequent diagnostic pathway. If the laboratory findings are normal, SPECT/CT enables a non-invasive diagnosis of ATTR cardiomyopathy; however, if the imaging is negative and suspicion persists, a biopsy remains indicated. A cardiac MRI is particularly valuable when echocardiographic findings are inconclusive or there is suspicion of AL cardiomyopathy. New diagnostic approaches based on extracardiac manifestations and incidental findings on MRI also open the possibility of identifying affected individuals even before the onset of cardiac symptoms. Amyloid-binding PET tracers show promise for the future non-invasive diagnosis of both forms of amyloidosis, but still require prospective validation studies.

Title: [Specific treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy: established disease-modifying agents and emerging mechanisms].
Abstract: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), in which fibrillary protein deposits accumulate in the cardiac extracellular space, has changed within a few years from a rare condition regarded as therapeutically futile into a causally treatable and increasingly recognised cause of heart failure. Every specific therapy requires a secure diagnosis, with prior exclusion of alternative causes such as light-chain (AL) amyloidosis. Two mechanistic principles are central to the approved treatment options: stabilisation of the transthyretin (TTR) tetramer (Vyndaqel®, Beyonttra®) and reduction of hepatic production through TTR gene silencing (Amvuttra®). For the stabilisers and the siRNA agent vutrisiran, randomised trials demonstrate a reduction in all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events; the survival benefit typically becomes apparent months after commencing treatment thus, arguing for the earliest possible initiation of treatment. Two further promising approaches are currently under investigation in phase III trials: antibody-mediated depletion of already deposited amyloid (so-called «depleters») and one-time gene editing (using CRISPR-Cas9). Both offer, for the first time, the prospect of a meaningful regression of amyloid burden and thus of a degree of regression in disease stage. This article classifies the approved agents by mechanism in a practice-oriented manner, discusses the selection, sequencing and combination of therapies as well as the monitoring of treatment response, and provides an outlook on agents in development.

Title: Risk Factors and Subtype-Specific Prediction Models for Arterial versus Venous Thrombotic Events in Chinese Patients with Lupus Nephritis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Autoimmune diseases heighten thrombosis risk, yet large-scale studies that systematically profile risk factors while simultaneously distinguishing arterial from venous events in lupus nephritis (LN) remain lacking. This study aimed to determine the incidence and arterial-venous distribution of thrombosis in LN, identify independent risk factors for overall, arterial, and venous thrombosis, and construct separate prediction models for each subtype.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 348 patients with biopsy-confirmed LN from 2017 to 2023. Over a median follow-up period of 4 years (with a maximum of 8 years), all thrombotic events were verified through imaging. Cox regression analysis was employed to identify independent risk factors, while time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and Harrell's C-index were utilized to assess model discrimination.
RESULTS: The overall incidence of thrombosis was 14.1% (49/348), with arterial events being more prevalent (55.1% arterial and 40.8% venous). Independent risk factors for overall thrombosis included age at diagnosis (HR=1.036, P<0.0001), hypertension (HR=2.097, P=0.011), smoking (HR=3.155, P<0.0001), and the positive lupus anticoagulant (LA) (HR=3.266, P<0.0001). Arterial thrombosis was independently associated with age, hypertension, smoking, and the Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index (SLE-DAI), while venous thrombosis was associated with age and positive LA. The arterial model exhibited excellent discrimination (3-year AUC=0.909, C-index=0.884), whereas the venous model demonstrated moderate discrimination (3-year AUC=0.766, C-index=0.752).
CONCLUSION: This study provides the first systematic characterization of thrombosis in Chinese LN patients with a specific focus on arterial-venous heterogeneity, and constructs separate risk prediction models. The arterial prediction model demonstrates excellent discriminative performance and may serve as a guide for thrombotic risk stratification. Venous prediction model demonstrated moderate discrimination. Both models rely on routinely available clinical variables. Routine LA screening, alongside standardized management of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, should be incorporated into long-term thromboprophylaxis strategies for LN.

Title: Development and Validation of a Logistic-Bayes Method for In-Hospital Mortality Discrimination in Neonatal Heart Failure: A Real-World Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal heart failure is a severe condition with high mortality, posing a significant burden on families and healthcare systems. Accurately discriminating whether a neonate with heart failure will die in hospital is essential for improving outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a discriminant model for identifying neonates with heart failure who will experience in-hospital death.
METHODS: This real-world study included 600 neonates with heart failure treated at the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between 2012 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, perinatal, laboratory, and first-24-hour medication data were extracted. Candidate variables were screened by LASSO regression and between-group comparisons; eight discriminators retained by multivariable logistic regression were used to construct the Logistic-Bayes model, and the cohort was randomly split in a 7:3 ratio into training and internal validation sets.
RESULTS: The final discriminators were urea, fibrinogen, poor postnatal response, oliguria, cedilanid use, dopamine use, epinephrine use, and digoxin use. The model achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.87 (95% CI 0.82-0.91) in the training set and 0.86 (95% CI 0.78-0.92) in the internal validation set, with accuracy of 0.87 in both.
CONCLUSION: On internal validation, the model demonstrated high specificity and high negative predictive value, supporting early identification of low-risk neonates with heart failure; prospective multicenter validation is required before routine clinical use.

Title: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test-Derived Functional Indices Associated with Moderate-to-Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Young and Middle-Aged Adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with cardiovascular morbidity. However, exercise-related functional responses remain incompletely characterized in adults undergoing cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) for exercise prescription without established diseases affecting exercise capacity. We examined associations between CPET-derived indices and moderate-to-severe OSA, defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15 events/h.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 104 adults aged 18-65 years who underwent overnight sleep monitoring with electroencephalographic recording and CPET for exercise prescription. Participants were classified into AHI ≥15 and AHI <15 events/h groups. Demographic characteristics, clinical variables, and CPET-derived indices were compared between groups. Heart rate recovery (HRR), peak oxygen pulse, and peak breathing reserve (BR) were examined in separate logistic regression models. Models were sequentially adjusted for sex, age, and body mass index (BMI).
RESULTS: Among the 104 participants, 59 participants had AHI ≥15 events/h and 45 had AHI <15 events/h. The AHI ≥15 group had higher BMI and lower HRR, peak oxygen pulse (% predicted), and BR (all p < 0.001). After adjustment for sex, age, and BMI, higher HRR was associated with lower odds of AHI ≥15 events/h (OR = 0.745, 95% CI 0.640-0.867, p < 0.001). Higher BR was also associated with lower odds (OR = 0.923, 95% CI 0.878-0.971, p = 0.002). The adjusted association for peak oxygen pulse was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Lower HRR and BR were associated with moderate-to-severe OSA after adjustment for sex, age, and BMI in this selected cohort of young and middle-aged adults. Further prospective studies in independent cohorts are warranted to confirm these findings and clarify their potential clinical relevance.

Title: Acute and 6-month vascular effects of a multi-component nutritional supplement: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate 6-month effects of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation targeting complementary pathways relevant to vascular ageing on endothelial function and other vascular ageing markers in apparently healthy adults.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The effects of a supplement to target ageing mechanisms on vascular function study was a double-blind, randomized, controlled trial. Participants received a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation comprising vitamins/minerals, amino acids, and plant-derived bioactives, or control for 6 months. Vascular assessments were performed at baseline and after 6 months (with an acute post-dose assessment). The primary outcome was change in brachial artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD). Secondary outcomes included pulse wave velocity (PWV), peripheral and central blood pressure, augmentation index, lipid profile, and estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk (SCORE2/SCORE2-OP). Sixty-one participants (baseline SCORE2/SCORE2-OP 3.6 ± 2.9%) were randomized (33 actives; 28 controls); 43 completed both visits (24 vs. 19). Compared with control, the supplement improved endothelial function (ΔΔFMD at 6 months +2.9% [95% CI 2.1-3.8]) and reduced arterial stiffness (ΔΔPWV -1.18 m/s [95% CI -2.00 to -0.36]). Peripheral systolic blood pressure (SBP) decreased (ΔΔSBP -6.1 mmHg [95% CI -10.9 to -1.3]). Lipids were unchanged. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk decreased (ΔΔSCORE2/SCORE2-OP -0.45% [95% CI -0.86 to -0.03]).
CONCLUSION: Daily intake of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation was associated with sustained improvements in endothelial function, arterial stiffness, and systolic blood pressure, with a modest reduction in estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk primarily attributable to lower systolic blood pressure rather than lipid change.
REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov NCT06145087.

Title: Multi-omics in coronary atherosclerosis: mechanistic insights and advances in precision diagnosis and treatment.
Abstract: Coronary atherosclerosis, driven by the interplay of lipid metabolic derangements and chronic inflammation, constitutes the pathological basis of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and has emerged as the leading cause of mortality among Chinese residents. In patients with acute coronary syndrome, subsequent events may arise from initially nonculprit coronary lesions that appear angiographically mild. Invasive coronary angiography, the conventional diagnostic reference standard, is inherently invasive and incapable of characterizing plaque biological properties. Meanwhile, traditional risk factors only enable crude risk stratification, resulting in a critical shortage of precise early clinical screening modalities. Multi-omics technologies enable comprehensive molecular profiling of the human organism and effectively address the limitations of conventional detection approaches. Nevertheless, existing investigations remain largely confined to single-omics analyses; candidate biomarkers lack validation in large independent cohorts, and substantial bottlenecks persist in clinical translation. This review evaluates the respective advantages and limitations of genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and gut metagenomics in coronary atherosclerosis research. It elucidates the scientific value of integrated multi-omics analysis in dissecting pathogenic regulatory networks, unraveling gut-heart axis mechanisms, and identifying targets for precision therapy. Furthermore, it summarizes cutting-edge technological advances including single-cell multi-omics, spatial multi-omics, liquid biopsy, and AI-powered multi-omics integration, and compiles multi-omics risk prediction models developed on the basis of large-scale population cohorts. By bridging genetic susceptibility, cellular remodeling, peripheral molecular signatures, and plaque phenotypes, multi-omics integration can underpin early risk warning for high-risk populations, plaque subtyping, and therapeutic efficacy monitoring. Looking ahead, the establishment of standardized, multicenter prospective cohorts and the application of Mendelian randomization to infer causal relationships will be pivotal. These efforts are essential to translate multi-omics into a practical framework for comprehensive precision medicine across the entire continuum of coronary atherosclerosis.

Title: Differential Associations of Seven Circulating Complement Proteins with Heart Failure: A Single-Center Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The complement system is associated with heart failure (HF), but patterns across circulating complement proteins and their sensitivity to covariate adjustment remain unclear.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 392 participants (164 chronic HF: 128 HFpEF, 14 HFmrEF, 22 HFrEF; 228 non-HF controls) were enrolled, and seven circulating complement proteins were measured. Spearman correlations with NT-proBNP and LVEF, sequential multivariable logistic regression, and restricted cubic splines were assessed for each protein. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to fully adjusted models. Subgroup and restricted-sample sensitivity analyses were performed. Exploratory quasi-Bayesian statistical decomposition assessed whether the C8-HF and CD55-HF associations overlapped with CRP, eGFR, and hemoglobin.
RESULTS: C7 and CD55 showed the strongest positive correlations with NT-proBNP (ρ≈0.32) and weak negative correlations with LVEF. After full adjustment, odds ratios for prevalent HF per 1-SD increase were 1.39 (95% CI 1.06-1.84) for C1r, 1.72 (1.29-2.29) for C7, and 1.47 (1.13-1.92) for C9; FDR-adjusted P values were 0.045, 0.0017, and 0.014. C1s and CD46 were not significant; C8 and CD55 associations attenuated after adjustment. No non-linear associations were found. C1r, C7, and C9 remained significant when restricting to eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or CRP ≤10 mg/L, but attenuated to non-significance when HF cases were restricted to LVEF ≥50%. Exploratory statistical decomposition suggested that the CD55-HF association partly overlapped with eGFR and hemoglobin, but not CRP; no corresponding overlap was observed for C8.
CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional sample, C1r, C7, and C9 were associated with prevalent chronic HF after full adjustment and FDR correction, but estimates attenuated in the LVEF-preserved restricted sample. C8 and CD55 associations attenuated after adjustment, while C1s and CD46 were not significant. These associations require prospective validation and should not be interpreted as causal.

Title: Risk Factor Profiles and Clinical Outcomes: A 6-Month Longitudinal Study on Rehospitalization Rates in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate rehospitalization rates and identify modifiable risk factors in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients enrolled in an optimal management and treatment program.
METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study with longitudinal follow-up was conducted on 163 patients diagnosed with CHF patients (Framingham criteria) at an international hospital model in Vietnam from January 2022 to November 2023. Clinical, behavioral, and comorbid factors were analyzed over 6 months.
RESULTS: The program demonstrated high efficacy with a low 6-month rehospitalization rate of 9.82%. Statistical analysis revealed significant correlations between rehospitalization and male gender (p<0.01), alcohol consumption (p<0.05), smoking (p<0.05), elevated heart rate (p<0.001), and NYHA functional class (p<0.05). Key comorbidities including coronary heart disease (p<0.01), sinus tachycardia (p < 0.001), atrial fibrillation (p<0.01), and sleep disorders were also significantly associated with readmission (p<0.05).
CONCLUSION: Optimizing CHF outcomes requires a comprehensive intervention strategy targeting both modifiable lifestyle factors and underlying clinical comorbidities like sleep disorders.

Title: hsa-miR-155-5p concentration as a determinant of leptinemia in umbilical cord plasma.
Abstract: Childhood obesity, which is reaching alarming prevalence worldwide, is associated with long-term adverse metabolic and cardiovascular health outcomes and often persists into adulthood. Investigating the mechanisms responsible for weight gain in early life is essential to better understand and prevent obesity and its related comorbidities. Leptin is a hormone primarily secreted by adipocytes. It suppresses appetite and increases energy expenditure through neonatal programming of the hypothalamic neural circuits responsible for regulation of food intake. The mechanisms regulating leptinemia are not fully understood. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), short RNA molecules repressing protein synthesis of their target genes and secreted in bloodstream, may play a role. To identify circulating miRNAs whose levels are associated with leptinemia in umbilical cord plasma (UCP), the present study quantified the miRNAs from 273 newborns in the Gen3G prospective birth cohort using next-generation sequencing (NGS). A total of 73 miRNAs were associated with leptinemia (P≤0.05) in UCP. Of these, miR-183-5p and miR-155-5p were selected to be requantified by digital PCR for 201 of these newborns based on the strength of their association [Log2(fold-change)=0.22, P=0.0007 and Log2(fold-change)=-0.14, P=0.005, respectively]. Association with leptinemia was replicated for miR-155-5p (Pearson correlations: NGS, r=-0.13, P=0.03; dPCR, r=-0.12, P=0.04). Biological pathways analysis showed that miR-155-5p is predicted to target the leptin receptor mRNA. These findings suggest miR-155-5p may influence leptinemia in UCP and contribute to early-life adiposity programming.

Title: Five Trials, Five Different Questions: Design Heterogeneity Among Lipoprotein(a)-Lowering Cardiovascular Outcomes Trials After Lp(a)HORIZON.
Abstract: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), widely regarded as causal on the basis of genetic and epidemiological evidence, for which no approved Lp(a)-lowering therapy exists. In September 2026, Novartis announced that Lp(a)HORIZON, evaluating the antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) pelacarsen and the most clinically advanced of five phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trials (CVOTs) targeting Lp(a), had not met its primary composite endpoint. Key details, including the magnitude of Lp(a) lowering achieved, the result in the pre-specified higher-Lp(a) subpopulation, the effect estimate, and the safety profile, remain unpublished pending congress presentation. This review compares the design of all five phase 3 Lp(a)-lowering CVOTs, identified through a curated bibliography, a PubMed search for design and rationale publications, and searches of the ClinicalTrials.gov registry, and situates them within the wider landscape of Lp(a)-directed therapy. The four trials still running are not replications of the first. They differ from Lp(a)HORIZON and from one another in mechanism (ASO, small interfering RNA (siRNA), or oral small molecule), dosing interval, Lp(a) eligibility threshold, sample size, stage of disease at which they intervene, and, critically, in the composition of the primary endpoint: the two olpasiran trials use a coronary-only composite that excludes stroke, whereas Lp(a)HORIZON and, by its own nomenclature, MOVE-Lp(a) include it. A coronary-only composite and a stroke-inclusive composite do not estimate the same quantity, so effect estimates from these trials cannot be directly compared without accounting for endpoint composition, population, and follow-up. Five non-exclusive explanations for the neutral result are set out, together with the evidence bearing on each and what would distinguish them. A single neutral trial does not resolve the Lp(a) question, and the readouts expected between 2027 and 2031 will not resolve it jointly unless these design differences are held in view when the results are compared.

Title: OVER-TIME II trial: design and rationale of a multicentre randomized study evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery ectasia.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is characterized by diffuse coronary dilatation and increased thrombotic risk. In patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and CAE, the optimal antithrombotic strategy remains unclear. Previously, an exploratory trial suggested that the combination of antiplatelet monotherapy plus oral anticoagulation may reduce ischaemic events without increasing bleeding risk compared to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), although it was underpowered for definitive conclusions.
AIMS: The aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of antiplatelet monotherapy plus direct oral anticoagulation compared with DAPT in patients with ACS and culprit-vessel CAE in a multicentre randomized setting.
METHODS AND RESULTS: OVER-TIME II is a multicentre, multinational, randomized, open-label clinical trial with 1:1 allocation comparing acetylsalicylic acid 100 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg vs. clopidogrel 75 mg plus rivaroxaban 15 mg daily. The study will include 326 patients with ACS and culprit-vessel CAE. Patients will be followed for 12 months. The co-primary efficacy endpoint is the time to first occurrence of a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or repeat revascularization. The co-primary safety endpoint is the time to first occurrence of major or minor bleeding defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium criteria. Secondary endpoints include individual components of the primary outcomes. Exploratory analyses will include genomic and transcriptomic profiling through DNA and RNA sampling to identify molecular signatures associated with thrombotic risk, treatment response, and clinical outcomes.
CONCLUSION: OVER-TIME II is designed to provide robust multicentre randomized evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of an anticoagulation-based strategy in patients with ACS and CAE, with the potential to contribute to future clinical research and guideline development.
REGISTRATION: NCT07511257. The trial is registered and publicly available on ClinicalTrials.gov and is currently actively recruiting patients.

Title: Efficacy and safety of traditional Chinese medicine kidney-tonifying and blood-activating therapy in the treatment of vascular dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of Kidney-tonifying and Blood-activating Therapy (KTBAT) for vascular dementia (VaD).
METHODS: Eight electronic databases were systematically searched from inception to January 12, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Primary endpoints included clinical effectiveness and cognitive scores (MMSE, HDS, CDR). Secondary outcomes focused on neurotrophic factors (BDNF, NGF, GDNF). Study quality was assessed via RoB 1, with data synthesis performed using RevMan 5.4.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight RCTs involving 3,357 participants were identified. KTBAT, whether administered as monotherapy or combined with Western medicine (WMT), significantly increased the clinical effectiveness rate compared to WMT (RR = 1.25, 95% CI: [1.20, 1.31]). Regarding cognition, KTBAT significantly improved MMSE (MD = 3.71, 95% CI: [2.96, 4.47]) and HDS scores (MD = 4.07, 95% CI: [2.63, 5.52]). CDR scores were also lower after intervention (SMD = -0.87, 95% CI: [-1.26, -0.47]). Additionally, KTBAT was associated with higher serum levels of BDNF (SMD = 1.02, 95% CI: [0.13, 1.90]) and NGF (SMD = 0.69, 95% CI: [0.27, 1.12]). GDNF was assessed in only one trial, and its level was also higher in the intervention group. Adverse events (AEs) rates did not differ significantly between KTBAT and WMT (RR = 0.71, 95% CI: [0.32, 1.57], p = 0.40), with no serious AEs or deaths reported.
CONCLUSION: KTBAT appears to be a potentially effective intervention for improving clinical effectiveness and cognitive function in VaD; however, its safety profile remains uncertain. While these findings support KTBAT as a promising candidate for VaD management, further high-quality, multicenter trials are warranted to strengthen the evidence base.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/search, identifier CRD420251272344.

Title: Sex differences in the diabetes-related risk of incident myocardial infarction and relationship to established coronary heart disease risk factors: the Tromsø Study (1979-2016).
Abstract:
AIMS: To examine whether the adverse effect of diabetes on the risk of incident myocardial infarction (MI) differs between sexes and assess to what extent established coronary heart disease (CHD) risk factors contribute to the elevated risk.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Prospective study of 42 907 Tromsø Study participants (51.5% women) with 3942 incident MI (357 with diabetes) at ages 35-104 years. Relative risks [incidence rate ratio (IRR)] were estimated in Poisson regression analyses. Impact of CHD risk factors was quantified as a percentage change in the regression coefficient for diabetes. A contrast in risk of MI by diabetes status was seen from age 45 years in men and 55 years in women. Adjusted for age and birth cohort, the IRR was 2.26 in women and 1.84 in men (P = 0.12, test for interaction). In a mutually adjusted model, adjustment for the triglyceride-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio weakened the association with diabetes similarly in women (-19.0%) and men (-17.0%); systolic blood pressure had a larger impact in women (-10.3% vs. +2.2%), whereas smoking strengthened the association more in men (+23.1% vs. +7.1%). Body mass index had a minor impact. A larger joint impact of adjustment factors in women (-33.6% vs. -15.9%) narrowed the initial gender gap (adjusted IRR of 1.72 and 1.67, respectively). Adverse lipid levels and increasing systolic blood pressure emerged already during the pre-diabetic phase.
CONCLUSION: Traditional CHD risk factors contributed substantially to the diabetes-related risk of incident MI. A larger joint impact of these factors in women reduced the initial observed sex difference in the adverse effect of diabetes.

Title: Dressler syndrome and post-cardiac injury syndrome: an autoinflammatory framework for reappraising a seventy-year-old diagnosis: a state-of-the-art review.
Abstract: Dressler syndrome, the delayed pericarditis after myocardial infarction remains firmly established in cardiological teaching, yet contemporary direct evidence specific to it is sparse. Its reported incidence has fallen markedly in the reperfusion era, while post-cardiac injury syndrome (PCIS) is now encountered chiefly after cardiac surgery and catheter-based procedures. These trends reflect a change in the clinical settings in which delayed post-injury pericardial inflammation is recognised, rather than evidence of a transfer of the same biological disease burden; incidence estimates across eras and procedures are not directly comparable. The historical anti-heart antibody framework does not, on its own, account for current observations. Randomised trials in predominantly idiopathic recurrent pericarditis show that colchicine and interleukin-1 (IL-1)-directed agents (anakinra, rilonacept, goflikicept) reduce recurrence, and experimental and human pericardial tissue data implicate the NLRP3 inflammasome. These data support an important role for innate immune signalling in pericarditis, but they do not establish IL-1 dependency in late post-infarction Dressler syndrome, and they do not exclude a contribution of adaptive immunity to amplification, persistence or recurrence. We grade the evidence at three levels-direct human PCIS data, data from other human pericarditis phenotypes, and experimental data-and stratify therapeutic evidence by phenotype and drug class, distinguishing colchicine, for which randomised prevention data exist in post-pericardiotomy syndrome, from IL-1 blockade, for which no PCIS-specific trial exists. We propose a pericardial injury-threshold model as a testable hypothesis in which clinical expression reflects the interaction of damage-associated molecular pattern load, the directness of pericardial and mesothelial exposure, and host inflammatory susceptibility, with adaptive responses acting as potential amplifiers. The model yields falsifiable predictions and identifies a key unanswered question: whether IL-1 inhibition during infarct healing is safe and effective. We outline a staged research programme, including a candidate two-tier research case definition requiring prospective validation, registry-based ascertainment, pericardial fluid immunophenotyping, inflammasome genetics, and phenotype-specific trials, including of emerging direct NLRP3 inhibitors.

Title: Beyond disease counts: multimorbidity patterns and self-rated health in South African adults-a network analysis of the 2016 demographic and health survey.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multimorbidity is rising rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa, where infectious and non-communicable disease burdens overlap. Whether the pattern of co-occurring conditions carries information beyond a simple disease count is unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To map patterns of co-occurring chronic conditions in South African adults, test for additive interactions between condition pairs, and compare network-derived measures with the disease count as correlates of poor self-rated health.
METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of the nationally representative 2016 South Africa Demographic and Health Survey. The analytic sample comprised 5,650 adults aged 18 years and older with complete data on 12 chronic conditions ascertained by self-report and biomarker measurement. The outcome was self-rated health, dichotomised as poor vs. average, good or excellent. Disease networks were constructed from phi coefficients with Louvain community detection; cluster stability used 1,000 design-consistent bootstrap replicates. Survey-weighted logistic regression adjusted for age, sex and residence compared the disease count with network-based measures (per 1-SD increase), using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), DeLong tests and cross-validation.
RESULTS: Three disease clusters emerged: infectious (tuberculosis, HIV, anemia), cardiometabolic and pain (hypertension, diabetes, chronic pain), and cardiovascular-respiratory-neoplastic (stroke, heart attack, high cholesterol, chronic bronchitis, asthma, cancer). The infectious cluster co-clustered in 100% of bootstrap replicates, and network structure differed by sex (permutation p = 0.001) and residence (p = 0.031). Adjusted odds ratios for poor self-rated health were 1.66 (95% CI 1.41-1.95) per SD of disease count, 1.55 (1.31-1.82) per SD of network score and 1.24 (1.03-1.49) per SD of max centrality; the network measures were highly correlated with disease count (r = 0.96) and did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.756 vs. 0.758; DeLong p = 0.26), a finding confirmed by cross-validation. One additive interaction remained after false-discovery-rate correction: stroke with anemia (+0.55 on the risk-difference scale, 95% CI 0.24-0.86).
CONCLUSIONS: Network analysis revealed robust disease clustering, most notably a stable infectious cluster, and subgroup-specific patterns relevant to integrated care planning. Individual-level network measures did not outperform a simple disease count. Disease counts remain a pragmatic risk marker; pattern-based measures merit prospective evaluation before clinical adoption.

Title: Atrial fibrillation phenotypes derived from multimodal data exhibit distinct electrophysiological substrate characteristics, symptom trajectories, and ablation outcomes.
Abstract:
AIMS: The heterogeneity in response to catheter ablation amongst atrial fibrillation (AF) patients classified according to arrhythmia duration highlights the need for improved phenotyping. Multimodal assessment may better characterize the spectrum of pathophysiology present amongst patients classified as having paroxysmal or persistent AF. This study aimed to perform comprehensive multimodal pre-ablation phenotyping in patients undergoing AF ablation and evaluate associations with post-ablation arrhythmia recurrence, symptom burden, and bi-atrial substrate remodelling.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this multicentre prospective cohort study, 86 patients referred for first-time AF ablation (42% persistent AF) underwent pre-ablation phenotyping beyond usual care, incorporating patch-based ambulatory rhythm monitoring, atrial structural and functional MRI assessment, and formal symptom evaluation. Unsupervised K-means clustering was used to derive phenotypes. The primary outcome was 12-month arrhythmia recurrence; secondary analyses assessed symptom trajectories and bi-atrial substrate characteristics. Four AF phenotypes were identified. Arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 56.0%, 42.9%, 22.2%, and 19.0% of patients in Phenotypes 1-4, respectively (log-rank P = 0.032). Symptom trajectories differed across phenotypes, with the greatest improvements observed in Phenotypes 3 and 4. Exploratory electroanatomic mapping analyses demonstrated significant between-phenotype differences in bi-atrial bipolar voltage aligned with clinical trajectories. Importantly, phenotypes were not fully explained by conventional classification: Phenotype 2 experienced relatively high recurrence despite comprising predominantly paroxysmal AF patients whilst Phenotype 3 demonstrated favourable outcomes despite a high prevalence of persistent AF.
CONCLUSION: Multimodal phenotyping identified distinct AF subgroups associated with differences in post-ablation recurrence, symptom trajectories, and electrophysiological substrate. This approach could improve pre-ablation risk stratification and shared decision-making.
REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05057507.

Title: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors initiation and mortality in non-proteinuric chronic kidney disease: a target trial emulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment options for nonproteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. While renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs) are cornerstone therapies for proteinuric CKD, evidence supporting the clinical benefit of RASIs initiation in nonproteinuric CKD is lacking.
METHODS: We emulated sequential target trials using a retrospective cohort from the China Renal Data System. Adults with nonproteinuric CKD (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio <30 mg/g) were included to assess the intention-to-treat effect of initiating RASIs on all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The primary estimate was the 3-year risk difference. A composite kidney outcome (>25% eGFR decline with stage deterioration or kidney replacement therapy) was also explored.
RESULTS: A total of 17 382 eligible person-trials (10 101 unique persons) were included. The 3-year cumulative incidence of all-cause mortality was 14.88% (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.65% to 16.51%) and 18.26% (95% CI, 17.67% to 19.42%) in the RASIs initiation group and the control group, respectively, corresponding to a risk difference of -3.39% (95% CI, -4.71% to -2.07%). A significant association favoring RASIs initiation was also observed in terms of cardiovascular mortality, with a 3-year risk difference of -1.46% (95%CI, -2.57% to -0.52%). Estimates from the subgroup and the sensitivity analyses were consistent with the primary analysis. A similar trend of association was observed for composite kidney outcomes, though the 3-year cumulative risk difference between groups did not reach statistical significance (risk difference, -0.88%; 95% CI, -2.42%-1.40%).
CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of RASIs may be associated with lower risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with nonproteinuric CKD.

Title: Improvement in pulmonary vascular resistance with IMPELLA 5.5 as a bridge to orthotopic heart transplantation.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The Impella 5.5 is a temporary micro-axial mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) device used for left ventricular (LV) support and unloading as a bridge to advanced therapies. However, the short-term impact of LV unloading on pulmonary hypertension (PH) has not been clearly defined. This study explored whether Impella 5.5 support results in a reduction in PH in patients bridged to orthotopic heart transplantation (OHT).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study examined 75 patients from two tertiary cardiac centers who had an Impella 5.5 placed during an admission (2018-2025) that culminated in OHT. Right heart catheterization (RHC) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) data were collected, including studies obtained before and after Impella placement. The primary outcomes were changes in pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), and pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP). Secondary outcomes included changes in qualitative right ventricular (RV) systolic function, transpulmonary gradient (TPG), and pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi). Paired and unpaired analyses were conducted. For the primary unpaired analysis, differences between the pre-Impella and during-Impella time points were assessed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test for continuous variables and chi-square or Fisher's exact test for categorical variables.
RESULTS: Following Impella 5.5 placement, median PVR by Fick and Thermodilution decreased from 2.8 (IQR, 2.1-3.8) to 1.5 (1.2-2.1) Wood Units (WU) (p < 0.001) and from 2.4 (1.9-2.8) to 1.3 (1.0-1.5) WU (p < 0.001), respectively. Median mPAP and PASP decreased from 35.5 (31.0-41.8) to 24.5 (20.2-32.0) mmHg (p < 0.001) and from 48 (42.0-55.8) to 37.5 (27.5-42.0) mmHg (p < 0.001), respectively. Secondary outcomes showed an increase in PAPi from 1.9 (1.3-3.0) to 3.4 (2.0-5.6; p = 0.002). The median duration of Impella 5.5 support was 19.0 (10.0-31.0) days, and the median time from Impella to RHC was 14 (12.0-17.0) days.
CONCLUSION: Temporary mechanical circulatory support with the Impella 5.5 device led to rapid and significant reduction in PVR, mPAP and PASP in patients being bridged to OHT. These findings support the use of the Impella 5.5 for optimizing pre-transplant hemodynamics and suggest a potential role for tMCS in improving transplant candidacy among patients previously excluded due to PH.

Title: Combination finerenone and empagliflozin for chronic kidney disease with type 2 diabetes: a target trial emulation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to emulate the CONFIDENCE trial and compare combination finerenone plus empagliflozin with each monotherapy for albuminuria reduction in Chinese patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D).
DESIGN: This study employed modified target trial emulation. The primary contrast was the per-protocol effect, estimated by cloning, censoring, and inverse probability of censoring weighting, which is not susceptible to grace-period immortal time bias; a propensity-score-matched assignment analysis, the observational analogue of intention-to-treat, was secondary.
SETTING: Electronic health records from three Chinese tertiary (Grade A) hospitals, from January 2023 to September 2025, were utilized.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 2,895 adults (965 per strategy) with CKD and T2D met the CONFIDENCE eligibility criteria, selected by 1:1:1 propensity score matching from 3,822 eligible patients.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Relative change in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) from baseline to day 180 was the main outcome measure (co-primary comparisons with Holm-Bonferroni correction).
RESULTS: At day 180, the median UACR reduction was 52.0% in the combination strategy, 32.1% with finerenone, and 28.9% with empagliflozin. In the per-protocol analysis the difference was -19.5 percentage points (95% confidence interval -20.5 to -18.5) versus finerenone and -22.8 (-23.8 to -21.8) versus empagliflozin. The secondary assignment analysis gave -19.6 (-20.5 to -18.7) and -22.9 (-23.8 to -22.0), respectively (both P < 0.001); this is not a true intention-to-treat effect and is supportive only. Hyperkalemia occurred in 12.7%, 12.8%, and 3.5%, respectively, acute kidney injury in 4.9%, 2.8%, and 2.3%, respectively, and symptomatic hypotension in 1.9%, 0.6%, and 0.4%, respectively. The findings were consistent across 10 sensitivity analyses and six subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: Combination finerenone and empagliflozin was associated with greater albuminuria reduction than either monotherapy, directionally consistent with CONFIDENCE. Because the emulated strategy permitted sequential initiation within 90 days whereas CONFIDENCE randomized simultaneous initiation, this is a modified emulation rather than a direct replication. Albuminuria is a surrogate endpoint and follow-up was 180 days, so hard kidney and cardiovascular outcomes remain unstudied. Despite loss to follow-up of 29.6% to 32.7%, the finding was robust in a tipping-point analysis. Hyperkalemia was frequent with finerenone, so biochemical monitoring remains necessary. Findings apply to comparable Chinese tertiary-care populations.

Title: Longitudinal joint trajectories of the dietary inflammatory index and physical activity and risk of incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity among women: evidence from the China Health and Nutrition Survey.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between long-term joint trajectories of the dietary inflammatory index (DII) and physical activity (PA) and the risk of incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) among Chinese women.
METHODS: Data were drawn from the China Health and Nutrition Survey 2004-2015. A total of 3,970 adult women without CMM at baseline were included. DII and PA were repeatedly assessed from 2004 to 2011, and joint trajectories were identified via group-based trajectory modeling. CMM was defined as the first co-occurrence of ≥2 of hypertension, diabetes, stroke, and heart disease. Cox models evaluated associations between trajectory and incident CMM, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses performed.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 400 participants (10.1%) developed incident CMM. Three joint trajectories were identified: lower DII + moderately active (n = 559, 14.1%), moderate DII + highly active (n = 541, 13.6%), and higher DII + inactive (n = 2,870, 72.3%). Compared with the lower DII + moderately active group, higher DII + inactive group showed significantly higher CMM risk (HR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.14-2.31; p = 0.007), whereas the moderate DII + highly active group did not. No significant effect modification was observed across subgroups. The association persisted in sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: A sustained pattern of higher dietary inflammation with lower physical activity was associated with elevated incident CMM risk in Chinese women, providing longitudinal evidence for earlier risk identification based on behavioral exposures.

Title: Elevated C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio is associated with early neurological deterioration in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early neurological deterioration (END) is a frequent complication of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) that contributes to poor clinical outcomes. The C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) reflects systemic inflammation relative to albumin levels and may be associated with END. We evaluated the association between log2-transformed CAR and END in patients with AIS.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,766 patients with AIS admitted between September 2016 to September 2022. END was defined as an increase of ≥2 points in the NIHSS motor item or total score within 72 h of admission. Associations between log₂-CAR and END were assessed using a multivariable logistic regression analysis. Generalized additive and two-piecewise regression models were used as exploratory analyses to assess potential non-linearity. ROC curves were used to compare CAR with established biomarkers and the A2DS2 score.
CONCLUSION: Higher CAR was independently associated with END in this cohort. CAR's strongest predictive advantage was observed when compared with the A2DS2 clinical score, whereas superiority over CRP alone was not demonstrated. The possible threshold at a raw CAR of approximately 0.020 is exploratory and requires independent validation.

Title: Distinct monocyte phenotypes are associated with peri-coronary inflammation in persons with and without HIV and without cardiovascular disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Chronic inflammation in persons with (PWH) and without HIV (PWoH) is linked to cardiovascular disease (CVD). The fat attenuation index (FAI), a marker of peri-coronary inflammation, predicts CVD risk. The relationship between FAI and monocyte phenotypes remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between monocyte subsets-classical (CD16dim intermediate/inflammatory monocytes and CD16neg), intermediate, and non-classical- and surface markers of activation and chemokine expression, and FAI in a cohort of PWH and PWoH, and compare relative differences by HIV serostatus.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional of a prospective observational cohort study, 58 virologically suppressed PWH and 16 PWoH without known CVD underwent coronary computed tomography angiography to measure FAI. Peripheral blood monocyte subsets and activation/homing phenotypes were analyzed via flow cytometry. Multivariable regression models assessed correlations between monocyte markers and FAI in the LAD and RCA, with interaction terms testing effects of HIV serostatus.
RESULTS: Frequency and expression of CD40 were elevated in PWH, while HLA-DR expression was lower across all monocyte subsets compared to PWoH. CD38+ intermediate monocytes were linked to worsened LAD FAI. CD38+ non-classical monocytes were correlated with worsened RCA FAI. CCR2 expression on total classical, and CD16dim, and CD16neg monocytes correlated with worsened RCA and LAD FAI, while CX3CR1+ monocytes and CD40+ subsets correlated with improved RCA FAI in adjusted analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: FAI demonstrates strong correlations with monocyte phenotypes with relationships influenced by HIV serostatus, highlighting activation markers and chemokine receptor profiles as plausible drivers of vascular inflammation and FAI as a tool for detecting early immune-mediated vascular inflammation.

Title: Diabesity: an old term, a modern challenge - multi-omics and precision anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in type 2 diabetes.
Journal: Journal of pharmacy & pharmaceutical sciences : a publication of the Canadian Society for Pharmaceutical Sciences, Societe canadienne des sciences pharmaceutiques
Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity are closely interconnected but heterogeneous conditions in which treatment response, safety, body weight, glycemic control, and long-term clinical outcomes vary substantially between individuals. This narrative review evaluates emerging anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with coexisting T2DM and obesity and examines the translational role of multi-omics in future precision treatment selection. Distinct from reviews focused primarily on obesity pharmacotherapy or omics-based disease stratification, the present review emphasizes the interface between contemporary drug mechanisms, T2DM-associated metabolic heterogeneity, candidate molecular signatures, and the level of evidence required for clinically actionable prescribing. We summarize evidence for approved and investigational oral incretin therapies, dual and triple receptor agonists, amylin-based strategies, established antidiabetic drugs, and adjunctive approaches targeting body composition. Throughout the review, we distinguish established clinical evidence from mechanistic rationale, candidate biomarkers, exploratory associations, and hypothetical future precision applications. We also separate metabolic efficacy endpoints, such as body weight and HbA1c, from intermediate cardiometabolic risk markers and from cardiovascular or kidney outcomes demonstrated in dedicated outcome trials. At present, no genomic, metabolomic, lipidomic, proteomic, microbiome, or integrated multi-omics signature has been clinically validated to select a specific anti-obesity medication for patients with T2DM and obesity. Major unresolved issues include the need for prospective biomarker validation, direct comparative trials, standardized assays, externally validated and calibrated prediction models, preservation of skeletal muscle health and physical function, long-term safety, treatment durability, affordability, and equitable implementation. Multi-omics should therefore be viewed as an investigational framework for generating and testing precision-treatment hypotheses rather than as a basis for routine prescribing.

Title: Association between estimated glucose disposal rate and subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden in non-diabetic middle-aged and older adults.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association and dose-response relationship between estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR), a surrogate marker of insulin resistance, and subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden in non-diabetic middle-aged and older adults.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis used data from a prospective registry and included 604 adults aged ≥45 years without diabetes. Participants with symptomatic cerebrovascular disease, including prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack attributable to cerebrovascular stenosis, were excluded. Cerebrovascular atherosclerosis was assessed using carotid duplex ultrasonography, head and neck magnetic resonance angiography, or head and neck computed tomography angiography. Based on neuroimaging results, participants were classified into three categories: no atherosclerosis, single vascular bed involvement, and dual vascular bed involvement. Associations between eGDR and atherosclerotic burden were evaluated using ordinal logistic regression models, including unadjusted, age- and sex-adjusted, and fully adjusted models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to examine the dose-response relationship.
RESULTS: All 604 participants were community-dwelling adults without symptomatic cerebrovascular disease. The mean age was 64 ± 11 years, and 220 (36.4%) were male. Participants with a higher subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden were older, had a higher prevalence of hypertension, and had lower eGDR levels (p < 0.001). The prevalence of single and dual vascular bed involvement decreased progressively across eGDR quartiles, from the lowest (Q1) to the highest (Q4) quartile (single bed: 33.1% vs. 19.2%; dual beds: 13.2% vs. 2.0%). In the fully adjusted ordinal logistic regression model, each 1-SD increase in eGDR was associated with lower odds of being in a higher atherosclerotic burden category (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.62-0.89, p = 0.001). Compared with Q1, participants in Q4 had lower odds of being in a higher burden category (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.24-0.72, p = 0.001; P for trend = 0.002). The RCS analysis showed a linear correlation between eGDR and atherosclerotic burden (overall p = 0.002, non-linear p = 0.322).
CONCLUSION: Among middle-aged and older adults without diabetes, lower eGDR was independently associated with a higher subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden, with a linear pattern. These findings warrant further investigation in prospective studies.

Title: Analysis of risk factors for venous thromboembolism in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia and construction of a predictive nomogram model.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the risk factors for venous thromboembolism (VTE) in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia (AHN) and to construct a VTE prediction model based on clinical indicators to help clinicians better identify high-risk patients and develop prevention and treatment strategies.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study retrospectively included 327 patients diagnosed with AHN who were hospitalized in the Pain Department of Hengshui People's Hospital between December 2020 and December 2023, of whom 26 developed VTE during hospitalization. The basic clinical data of the patients were collected, and the independent risk factors for VTE were screened by LASSO regression and multifactorial Logistic regression analysis, and the VTE prediction model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated by ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curves, and internal validation was performed using ten-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: The incidence of VTE in AHN patients was 7.95%. LASSO regression screened for 10 relevant variables, and final multifactor logistic regression analysis identified FIB (fibrinogen), FDP (fibrin degradation products), NRS (Numerical Rating Scale) score, and thrombotic risk score as independent predictors. Among them, FIB was a protective factor for VTE (OR = 0.477, P = 0.006), while FDP (OR = 1.48, P < 0.001), NRS score (OR = 1.584, P = 0.039), and thrombotic risk score (OR = 2.05, P < 0.001) were risk factors. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.853 (95% CI: 0.764-0.941), and the bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index was 0.834. At the optimal cutoff, the sensitivity and specificity were 0.731 and 0.877, respectively, with good calibration and clinical applicability.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, a VTE prediction model was constructed for patients with AHN. The model can accurately predict the risk of VTE in patients with AHN and provide a reference for clinical prevention and intervention; however, external validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

Title: CT-derived subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness and circulating adipokines in relation to neurological outcome after in-hospital cardiac arrest: two parallel cohort analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury is a major determinant of outcome after in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA). Adipose tissue may be relevant to post-arrest outcomes through its anatomical and endocrine characteristics. We conducted two parallel exploratory analyses to examine the associations of thoracic subcutaneous adipose tissue depth and circulating adipokines with neurological outcome after IHCA.
METHOD: We employed a dual-cohort design. The CT Imaging Cohort included patients with pre-arrest and post-arrest thoracic CT examinations. Associations of anterior and posterior subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness with survival and neurological outcome at hospital discharge were evaluated. In the Biochemical Cohort, plasma concentrations of 12 adipokines measured during cardiac arrest were compared between neurological outcome groups. Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. Exploratory logistic regression models were evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and Firth regression sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: In the CT Imaging Cohort, several unadjusted differences in post-arrest posterior subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness were observed between neurological outcome groups, but none remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction in the overall analysis. In the ventilation-matched sensitivity analysis, greater pSAT thickness at selected thoracic levels remained associated with favorable neurological outcome after correction for multiple comparisons. In the Biochemical Cohort, CTRP6, CTRP9, Omentin-1, and Vaspin concentrations were higher and Chemerin concentration was lower in patients with favorable neurological outcomes after false discovery rate correction. The apparent AUC was 0.876 (95% CI, 0.795-0.957) for the clinical model and 0.938 (95% CI, 0.882-0.993) for the exploratory model adding CTRP6. The AUC difference was not statistically significant (ΔAUC, 0.062; 95% CI, -0.003 to 0.126; P = 0.062). The optimism-corrected AUC of the extended model was 0.930.
CONCLUSION: CT-derived posterior subcutaneous adipose tissue thickness and circulating adipokines showed exploratory associations with neurological outcome in two independent IHCA cohorts. The addition of CTRP6 to CPR duration and lactate numerically improved model discrimination, but the incremental AUC was not statistically significant. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation. Because CT measurements and adipokines were obtained from different patients, the study does not establish a direct anatomical-biochemical relationship.

Title: CMR-derived left atrial reservoir strain and the LAVI/LVEF ratio are associated with 30-day readmission in atrial fibrillation: the CMRRADAR-AF retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging allows simultaneous evaluation of cardiac structure, function, and tissue composition. Whether CMR-derived left atrial (LA) reservoir strain, the left atrial volume index-left ventricular ejection fraction (LAVI/LVEF) ratio, and atrial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) can identify patients at risk for 30-day readmission after atrial fibrillation (AF)-related hospitalisation has not been investigated.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the association between CMR parameters and 30-day unplanned readmission following an AF-related index admission and to describe CMR differences across three clinical groups using a three-group cohort design.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study at Chulabhorn Hospital, Bangkok (IRB005/2569), enrolled 43 patients with AF who underwent CMR on 1.5 T or 3 T Philips scanners: 25 outpatients (OPD), 10 index-admitted patients without readmission (Adm-NoReadmit), and 8 index-admitted patients with 30-day unplanned readmission (Readmit). A CMR analysis was performed using CVI42 version 6.4. LA reservoir strain was derived by feature tracking from standard cine images.
RESULTS: Among the admitted patients (n = 18), LA reservoir strain showed the highest apparent discrimination for readmission [area under the curve (AUC), 0.963; p < 0.001; exploratory internally derived cutpoint <11.1%: sensitivity, 88%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 47%-100%; specificity, 100%; 95% CI, 69%-100%]. Correcting for predictor selection, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.919. The LAVI/LVEF ratio was also associated with readmission (AUC, 0.913; p = 0.002). Qualitative atrial hyperenhancement on non-dedicated LGE imaging completely separated readmitted from non-readmitted admitted patients (8/8 vs. 0/10); however, because it was assessed on an LV-optimised protocol not validated for atrial tissue, we report it only as an exploratory qualitative finding and do not interpret it as evidence of a fibrosis mechanism. The LACE score (length of stay, acuity of admission, Charlson comorbidity index, and emergency department visits) achieved an AUC of 0.719 (95% CI, 0.44-0.95; p = 0.125); an exploratory combined LACE+ LA reservoir strain model produced a numerically higher apparent AUC, but with only eight events, this estimate is unstable and likely overfitted and is not interpreted as evidence of incremental value. A three-group analysis revealed a non-monotonic pattern: The Adm-NoReadmit patient group had the highest LA reservoir strain (15.4%), exceeding the OPD group (8.5%), whereas the Readmit group had the lowest (6.6%).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory feasibility analysis, CMR-derived LA reservoir strain and the LAVI/LVEF ratio were associated with 30-day unplanned readmission following an AF-related index admission. Because readmitted patients had a substantially higher prevalence of heart-failure history, these associations may reflect a shared structural-functional substrate rather than independent, AF-specific effects. Descriptive comparison across the three clinical groups showed a non-monotonic LA functional pattern, suggesting that CMR may aid risk stratification at discharge. However, prospective validation is needed.

Title: Stroke-associated pneumonia after acute ischemic stroke: early temporal dynamics, nonlinear risk factors, and time-dependent prognostic impact.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is a common complication following acute ischemic stroke, yet its early occurrence patterns, nonlinear risk factors, and time-dependent prognostic impact remain incompletely characterized. We investigated SAP incidence, temporal distribution, risk factors, and independent impact on in-hospital outcomes.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 3,347 consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke (2019-2025). SAP was diagnosed within 7 days after admission using consensus criteria. Cox models with restricted cubic splines identified risk factors and nonlinear relationships. Time-dependent Cox models, Gamma generalized linear models, and logistic regression were used to assess associations between SAP and in-hospital outcomes. Multiple imputation, complete-case, and landmark analyses verified robustness.
RESULTS: SAP developed in 428 patients (12.8%), with 55.1% occurring within 72 h (peak day 3). Independent risk factors included older age (HR 1.02), pre-stroke mRS 3-5 (HR 1.39), COPD (HR 1.69), cardioembolism (HR 1.71), dysphagia (HR 2.02), and nasogastric tube insertion within 48 h (HR 2.31) (all p < 0.05). Admission NIHSS, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio, and albumin showed nonlinear associations with SAP risk (all P-nonlinear <0.05). Time-dependent analyses revealed SAP independently associated with in-hospital death (HR 2.34), ICU transfer (HR 2.81), invasive mechanical ventilation (HR 3.47), prolonged length of stay (RoM 1.35), and poor functional outcome (OR 1.90) (all p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness.
CONCLUSION: SAP occurs early after acute ischemic stroke, with identifiable risk factors exhibiting nonlinear relationships, and independently predicts adverse in-hospital outcomes. Findings support forward-shifted preventive strategies, including early swallowing assessment, feeding pathway optimization, airway protection, and nutritional support, in high-risk patients during the first days of hospitalization.

Title: Mechanisms and clinical outcomes of sacubitril-valsartan and SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure patients: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure represents a challenging cardiovascular disorder among the elderly, repeatedly exacerbating cardiac dysfunction and a reduced capacity for activity, thereby presenting significant therapeutic challenge.
OBJECTIVE: To analyse mechanisms of action and outcomes of combined therapy with sacubitril-valsartan and SGLT2 inhibitors for heart failure patients.
METHOD: From October 2023 to October 2025, 150 heart failure patients were recruited and categorized them to the SV group (sacubitril-valsartan) and the SS group (sacubitril-valsartan and SGLT2 inhibitor) according to their treatment regimens. Both groups of patients received treatment with sacubitril-valsartan; the SS group additionally received SGLT2 inhibitor supplementation.
