The main parameters pre- and post- treatment were assessed and analyzed among both groups, including changes in cardiac function related indicators [left ventricle ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricle end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricle end-systolic diameter (LVESD), and cardiac output (CO)], serum indicators [β-endorphin (β-EP), cardiotrophin-1 (CT-1), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) changes], inflammatory indicators (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factors-α (TNF-α), and clinical efficacy. Secondary indicators include heart failure quality of life scale scores, complication incidences, and adverse events incidences.
RESULT: No marked discrepancy existed in the baseline clinical data among both groups (P > 0.05). Post-treatment, the indicators in both groups demonstrated remarkable improvement (P < 0.05). The LVEDD, LVESD, serum markers, inflammatory markers and MLHFQ scores in SS group were markedly below those in the SV group, whilst LVEF, CO and the overall clinical response rate were markedly increased (P < 0.05). The complications and adverse reactions incidences were markedly reduced in SS group vs. SV group (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The combined use sacubitril-valsartan and SGLT2 inhibitors demonstrates efficacy in improving cardiac function indicators, downregulate neuroendocrine and inflammatory factor levels, enhance clinical efficacy in heart failure patients, and can serve as an important reference for comprehensive treatment of such patients.

Title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Eleven studies (total N = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853-0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity (I 2 = 29.0%, p = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578-0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842-0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups.
CONCLUSION: AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

Title: Adjunctive extracorporeal shock wave therapy after botulinum toxin type A injection for post-stroke spasticity: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke spasticity is a common rehabilitation problem, and botulinum toxin type A (BTX-A) is a standard focal treatment. Whether extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) provides clinically relevant additional benefit after BTX-A remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and three-level meta-analysis evaluated the add-on effect of ESWT after BTX-A for post-stroke spasticity, with particular attention to impairment-level and activities-of-daily-living outcomes. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP, and CBM were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials of BTX-A plus ESWT in adult post-stroke spasticity were included. The primary quantitative synthesis was restricted to BTX-A-based comparators. Hedges' g was pooled with three-level random-effects models to account for dependent effect sizes.
RESULTS: Seven randomized controlled trials with 377 participants met the qualitative criteria, and six trials with 242 participants contributed to the primary quantitative synthesis. Adjunctive ESWT was associated with greater reduction in Modified Ashworth Scale scores (g = 0.87, 95% CI 0.41 to 1.34; p < 0.001) and greater improvement in Fugl-Meyer Assessment scores (g = 1.11, 95% CI 0.45 to 1.76; p < 0.001). Activities-of-daily-living estimates favored the combined intervention but did not reach conventional statistical significance (g = 1.15, 95% CI -0.03 to 2.32; p = 0.056). Two participants developed transient erythema after ESWT, but adverse-event reporting was too incomplete for a comparative safety estimate.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive ESWT may improve short-term impairment-level outcomes after BTX-A, but certainty is limited and evidence for reliable functional independence gains is very uncertain. Modality-, target-, timing-, and dose-specific findings remain exploratory.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: Identifier INPLASY202630010; https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2026.3.0010.

Title: Associations of insulin resistance surrogates with cardiovascular disease in early stage cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The early stages 0-3 of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represent a critical window for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention. Although insulin resistance (IR) is a key driver of CVD risk, systematic comparisons of IR surrogates in CVD remain limited. This study examined the associations of 12 IR surrogates with CVD in participants with stages 0-3 CKM syndrome.
METHODS: This prospective study included 5,625 participants with stages 0-3 CKM syndrome from the Qingdao Diabetes Program. Twelve IR surrogates related to CVD were evaluated using multivariable-adjusted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, sensitivity analyses, and predictive performance analyses, such as triglyceride-glucose index, atherogenic index of plasma, cardiometabolic index, metabolic score for IR (METS-IR), cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose (CHG) index, CHG plus body mass index, CHG plus waist circumference, CHG plus waist-to-height ratio, CHG plus body roundness index, CHG plus weight-adjusted waist index, CHG plus A body shape index, and CHG plus Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI).
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 15.2 years, 1,407 incident CVD events occurred. In multivariable-adjusted analyses, all 12 IR surrogates were significantly associated with CVD risk (all P < 0.05), of CHG-CVAI showing the best performance (Q4 vs. Q1: HR = 2.10, 95% CI = 1.74-2.52). Most indices showed nonlinear dose-response relationships. The associations were higher risk for adults aged <60 years and urban residents as compared with counterparts, and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings. Furthermore, addition of each IR surrogate improved CVD risk prediction: C-index ranging from 0.669 to 0.674, NRI ranging from 0.089 to 0.205 and IDI ranging from 0.0004 to 0.0032 (all P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: All IR surrogates, particularly CHG-CVAI were independently associated with incident CVD in early-stages CKM syndrome. These simple, low-cost indices improved risk stratification and moderately identify CVD individuals in high risk population.

Title: Sex differences in clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a real-world cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases in the ageing population, and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an effective and less invasive therapeutic alternative. Anatomical, pathophysiological, and clinical differences between women and men may influence outcomes following the procedure. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sex and mortality and procedure-related complications after TAVI in a real-world cohort from the Vigo Health Area.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including 1,065 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent transfemoral TAVI between 2010 and 2023. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included bleeding, vascular complications, and new permanent pacemaker implantation. Time-to-event analyses were censored at 365 days; multivariable models used complete-case analysis.
RESULTS: Women were older and had greater frailty and higher surgical risk scores than men. In-hospital and 1-year mortality were similar between sexes. Date-based 30-day mortality was 2.4% in men and 3.7% in women (p = 0.225), and female sex was not independently associated with 30-day mortality after adjustment for age and STS score (adjusted OR 1.79, 95% CI 0.80-3.98; p = 0.154). Female sex was not independently associated with 1-year mortality (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.69-1.66; p = 0.772). Women had more bleeding in unadjusted analyses, but female sex was not significantly associated with any bleeding after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.92-2.81; p = 0.093). Male sex remained associated with higher odds of new permanent pacemaker implantation (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.03-2.17; p = 0.036).
CONCLUSIONS: Sex was not independently associated with short- or 1-year mortality after TAVI. Women had a higher unadjusted incidence of bleeding, whereas men had a higher incidence of new permanent pacemaker implantation that persisted after adjustment. These findings describe sex-related differences in procedural risk profiles but should be interpreted in the context of the observational design and the long study period.

Title: Effects of synchronous versus sequential scalp acupuncture and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on post-stroke cognitive impairment based on multimodal assessments: a single-center randomized controlled trial protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) significantly burdens individuals and society. While scalp acupuncture and transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) show promise for alleviating cognitive deficits, the optimal temporal sequence of their combined delivery remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of synchronous versus sequential delivery of scalp acupuncture and taVNS for PSCI, and explore central-peripheral neuromodulatory responses associated with intervention timing via multimodal assessment.
METHODS: This prospective, randomized controlled trial will allocate 96 eligible PSCI patients equally into three groups. All receive conventional treatment alongside scalp acupuncture and taVNS. The synchronous group undergoes concurrent acupuncture and taVNS. Control Group 1 receives acupuncture followed by taVNS, while Control Group 2 receives taVNS followed by acupuncture. Treatments are administered once daily, 5 days per week, for 4 weeks. To assess the impact of temporal sequencing, multimodal data will be compared at baseline, week 4, and week 8 follow-up. Assessments encompass cognitive function (MoCA, MMSE), activities of daily living (MBI), neuroimaging (rs-fMRI), neuroelectrophysiology (ERP-P300), cerebral hemodynamics (TCD), and adverse events.
DISCUSSION: Results are expected to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and safety of synchronous versus sequential scalp acupuncture-taVNS delivery for PSCI. Furthermore, findings may help explore the temporal dynamics of neuromodulation across brain networks, neural electrical activity, and cerebral hemodynamics, contributing to the evidence base for standardizing integrative Chinese-western cognitive rehabilitation protocols.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, Identifier [ChiCTR2600125558].

Title: Preliminary exploration of the pathogenesis of patent foramen ovale-related migraine and efficacy analysis of PFO closure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patent foramen ovale (PFO), a common congenital atrial septal abnormality, can induce intracardiac right-to-left shunt (RLS) and is a potential risk factor for migraine. Currently, there is no unified consensus regarding the therapeutic efficacy and specific molecular mechanisms of PFO closure in the treatment of migraine.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted, enrolling 107 patients with PFO and migraine, of whom 58 underwent transcatheter PFO closure (observation group) and 49 received standard medical therapy (control group). All patients underwent cardiac imaging and contrast-enhanced transthoracic echocardiography before treatment, with follow-up assessments of headache episodes and scale scores at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post-treatment. Simultaneously, peripheral arterial blood samples were collected from 5 PFO patients before and after surgery and from 5 healthy controls for plasma proteomic analysis, and changes in arterial partial pressure of oxygen and oxygen saturation were monitored.
RESULTS: The improvements in Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), Headache Impact Test (HIT-6), Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS), and Migraine-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MSQ v2.1) scores at each follow-up time point were greater in the observation group than in the control group (all P < 0.05). At the 12-month follow-up, the overall treatment effective rate was 94.83% in the observation group, higher than 73.47% in the control group, with a statistically intergroup difference (P = 0.003). Stratified efficacy analysis revealed a higher proportion of markedly effective cases and a lower proportion of ineffective cases in the observation group, with statistically differences in the distribution of markedly effective and ineffective cases between groups (P < 0.05). Postoperative arterial partial pressure of oxygen and oxygen saturation were markedly improved compared with preoperative levels. Proteomic analysis suggested that the expression levels of inflammation-oxidative stress-related proteins, represented by myeloperoxidase (MPO), lysozyme C (LYZ), and heat shock protein 60 (HSPD1), were downregulated after surgery, and these changes appeared to be associated with the alleviation of hypoxia after elimination of intracardiac shunting.
CONCLUSIONS: PFO closure improved migraine symptoms in appropriately selected patients and was associated with downregulation of inflammation-oxidative stress proteins (MPO, LYZ, HSPD1). These findings provide preliminary molecular insights warranting further validation in larger cohorts.

Title: HalluciGuard-eye: knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation for hallucination detection and mitigation in ophthalmic multimodal large language models.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of preventable blindness in working-age adults, yet scalable early detection is limited by the unreliability of AI-assisted screening. Multimodal large language models can interpret fundus photographs and support DR grading, but they frequently hallucinate - fabricating lesions or misclassifying referable DR - which directly threatens timely treatment and prevention of vision loss. We developed HalluciGuard-Eye to make AI-assisted DR assessment trustworthy.
METHODS: HalluciGuard-Eye combines knowledge graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation with hierarchical hallucination detection. An Ophthalmic Clinical Knowledge Graph containing 47,832 medical entities and 156,294 semantic relationships was constructed from clinical guidelines and published literature. A dual-stream architecture uses a Visual-Semantic Alignment Module to verify cross-modal consistency and a Clinical Factuality Grounding Network to anchor generated content to reranked evidence. The Hierarchical Factuality Score assesses anatomical, pathological, and clinical-recommendation accuracy. The framework was evaluated on four public ophthalmic imaging benchmarks.
RESULTS: HalluciGuard-Eye reduced hallucination rates by 42.2% compared with state-of-the-art medical multimodal large language models and achieved 91.6% factual accuracy for clinical entity recognition on EyePACS. For diabetic retinopathy grading, sensitivity was 89.6% and specificity was 92.1%, representing improvements of 2.4% and 2.7%, respectively, over MedRAG. In the component ablation, removing knowledge-graph retrieval lowered EyePACS HFS by 9.4 percentage points. Additional analyses yielded 87.6% critical-evidence recall@20, 89.2% lesion-location accuracy, and 88.9% sensitivity in a patient-clustered cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that knowledge-grounded retrieval and hierarchical factuality assessment can reduce hallucinations while preserving diagnostic performance in ophthalmic multimodal language models.

Title: Association of perivascular fat density with vulnerable plaque and recent symptomatic cerebrovascular events.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate the association between perivascular fat density (PFD) and carotid plaque characteristics and to evaluate the discriminative ability of PFD and lipid-rich necrotic core plaques in relation to symptomatic status of cerebrovascular events.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was conducted in 119 patients with unilateral carotid atherosclerosis. Patients were classified into symptomatic and asymptomatic groups based on the occurrence of acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack within the preceding two weeks. Differences in plaque characteristics, PFD, lipid-rich core plaques, and geometric parameters between the two groups were compared using non-parametric statistical tests. Spearman rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate the association between PFD and plaque characteristics. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors and develop discriminative models. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap-derived optimism-corrected AUC.
RESULTS: Statistically significant differences in plaque characteristics, PFD, lipid-rich necrotic core plaques, and geometric parameters were observed between the symptomatic and asymptomatic groups (p < 0.001). PFD was positively correlated with plaque characteristics (p < 0.001). PFD, degree of stenosis, and the presence of lipid-rich core plaques were identified as independent correlates of cerebrovascular events. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated that the combined model improved the area under the curve from 0.885 for the stenosis-only model to 0.972. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement between model-estimated probabilities and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis indicated greater net clinical benefit for the combined model than for the stenosis-only model.
CONCLUSION: PFD is positively associated with carotid plaque characteristics and may serve as an imaging marker for assessing the perivascular inflammatory state. Combining PFD with stenosis severity and LRNC plaques demonstrated high discriminative value in assessing the symptomatic status of recent cerebrovascular events.

Title: Effect of combat gear and body armor on ventilatory thresholds and muscle oxygenation during graded treadmill exercise in female and male soldiers.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to determine how combat gear and body armor (CB) affect the relationship between treadmill setting and internal physiological responses at ventilatory transitions, and to characterize right vastus lateralis muscle oxygen saturation (SmO2) and exploratory early reoxygenation in female and male soldiers.
METHODS: Nine female and nine male soldiers completed randomized no-load (NL) and CB graded treadmill tests to volitional exhaustion. Heart rate and pulmonary gas exchange were measured, and right vastus lateralis SmO2 was assessed using near-infrared spectroscopy. VT1 was identified using the V-slope method and VT2 using ventilatory-equivalent criteria. SmO2 outcomes were referenced to a 30-s standing value.
RESULTS: VT1 was identified at a lower treadmill stage in CB than in NL in men (5.2 ± 0.8 vs. 6.4 ± 1.7; p = 0.02) and women (5.1 ± 0.6 vs. 7.1 ± 1.5; p <0.01). Absolute V̇O2 at VT1 changed little, whereas HR was higher in CB in men (p <0.01) and women (p = 0.04). VT2 was also identified at a lower stage in CB in both groups (p <0.01). Baseline-referenced right vastus lateralis desaturation amplitude during CB was greater in men than women (39.0% ± 23.9% vs. 17.1 ± 14.5%; p <0.01), although adipose-tissue thickness at the sensor site was not measured. No statistically significant effects were detected for the early post-exercise indices.
DISCUSSION: CB altered the treadmill setting at which ventilatory transitions were observed and increased cardiovascular demand at VT1 without essentially changing absolute V̇O2 at VT1. This indicates a changed relationship between treadmill task, transported mass, and internal physiological response rather than demonstrated displacement of the underlying metabolic threshold. The site-specific SmO2 and early reoxygenation findings were exploratory, and between-sex interpretation was limited by the small sample and unmeasured adipose-tissue thickness.

Title: Early antiplatelet therapy after intravenous thrombolysis in acute non-cardiogenic ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is a cornerstone of acute ischemic stroke management; however, early neurological deterioration due to reocclusion remains a concern, particularly in non-cardiogenic stroke where platelet-rich thrombi predominate. The safety and efficacy of early antiplatelet therapy (APT) initiated within 24 h after IVT in this specific population remain controversial. This meta-analysis evaluates the available evidence on early APT versus standard delayed APT, with particular attention to the type of antiplatelet agent used.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between January 2021 and March 2026, with a supplementary search conducted on May 15, 2026, evaluating early APT (≤24 h after IVT) versus standard APT (>24 h) in non-cardiogenic ischemic stroke. The primary efficacy outcome was favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1 at 90 days). The primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Pre-specified RCT-only analyses were conducted as the primary analytic strategy, with observational studies included as supportive evidence.
RESULTS: Four studies comprising 1,394 patients were included in the quantitative synthesis. In the two RCTs (ASSET-IT and INSTANT, n = 1,191), early tirofiban was associated with significantly higher odds of favorable functional outcome compared with standard APT (OR 1.78, 95% CI 1.38-2.30, p < 0.001, I 2 = 42%). We did not detect a statistically significant increase in sICH (OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.64-2.21, p = 0.59, I 2 = 0%) or 90-day mortality (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.61-1.16, p = 0.29, I 2 = 0%). The combined analysis including observational studies yielded consistent results (favorable outcome: OR 1.72, 95% CI 1.38-2.15; sICH: OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.71-2.18; mortality: OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.64-1.16). Subgroup analysis suggested numerically greater efficacy with tirofiban-based regimens (OR 1.81) compared with aspirin (OR 1.35), though the interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.11). The evidence base predominantly concerns tirofiban, with only one small study evaluating aspirin.
CONCLUSION: In patients with acute non-cardiogenic ischemic stroke, early tirofiban administration within 24 h after intravenous thrombolysis significantly improves functional outcomes. We did not detect a statistically significant increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or mortality. However, the confidence intervals do not exclude a clinically meaningful increase in sICH risk, and the small number of hemorrhagic events limits the precision of these safety estimates. The evidence for aspirin and other antiplatelet agents remains very limited and requires further investigation. These findings support reconsideration of current guideline restrictions for selected patients, particularly regarding tirofiban-based regimens. Large-scale randomized controlled trials with standardized protocols are warranted to establish optimal timing, agent selection, dosing, and patient selection criteria.

Title: Association of the prognostic nutritional index with in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events among emergency department patients with acute heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute heart failure (AHF) is prone to early clinical deterioration. The prognostic nutritional index (PNI), derived from serum albumin and lymphocyte count, is readily available. We evaluated the association of early PNI with incident in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events and its incremental prognostic value.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included consecutive adults presenting to the emergency department with AHF from March 2022 through March 2026. PNI was calculated from measurements obtained within 24 h and classified as low (<45) or high (≥45). The primary outcome was a post-index composite of all-cause death, cardiogenic shock, sustained ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, acute myocardial infarction, or worsening AHF requiring treatment escalation. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations; missing covariates were handled using multiple imputation. Discrimination was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Of 367 patients (156 low PNI; 211 high PNI), 112 (30.5%) experienced the primary outcome. Events occurred in 43.6% and 20.9%, respectively (P < 0.001). After adjustment, low PNI remained associated with higher odds of the primary outcome (odds ratio [OR], 1.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10-3.35; P = 0.022). Each 5-point PNI increase was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.56-0.90; P = 0.003). PNI alone yielded an AUC of 0.714. Adding PNI increased the conventional model AUC from 0.776 to 0.829 (increase, 0.053; 95% CI, 0.021-0.085; P = 0.001); bootstrap-corrected AUCs were 0.752 and 0.803, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Low PNI was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital adverse cardiovascular events. PNI provided modest incremental prognostic information and may serve as a complementary marker for early risk stratification.

Title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment.
METHODS: The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome.
RESULTS: Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50).
CONCLUSIONS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

Title: Primary Prevention ICD in a Contemporary Underserved Population: Factors Associated With Underutilization and Mortality.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Registry studies from 2000-2010 demonstrated underutilization of primary prevention ICD therapy. As heart failure therapies have reduced sudden cardiac death, investigators have questioned guidelines derived from trials conducted two decades prior, particularly in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) and elderly subgroups. We characterized contemporary referral determinants, decision-making processes, and outcomes of primary prevention ICD therapy in a diverse, under-represented population.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we reviewed records of all patients meeting Class I criteria for primary prevention ICD in 2019. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with ICD referral, and time-varying Cox models compared all-cause mortality by implantation status through 2022.
RESULTS: Of 559 eligible patients, 345 (62%) were referred and 227 (41%) underwent implantation. Referral was associated with male gender, care coordination by a cardiologist rather than a generalist, and lower social vulnerability index (SVI) score. No decision-making rationale was documented for a plurality of non-referred and non-implanted patients; documented rationales identified potential intervention targets. ICD implantation was not associated with all-cause mortality (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.49-1.12). In exploratory analyses stratified by cardiomyopathy type, implantation was associated with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy (aHR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95) but not in NICM (aHR 1.11, 95% CI 0.63-1.95).
CONCLUSION: Many eligible patients are never referred for ICD therapy. Female gender, generalist care coordination, and high SVI were associated with non-referral. The exploratory association of implantation with lower mortality in ischemic cardiomyopathy was not significant in propensity score overlap-weighted analyses. The NICM estimate was imprecise.

Title: Safety of Bioelectric Impedance Analysis Testing in Pediatric Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bioelectric impedance analysis (BIA) is a useful clinical tool in pediatric heart disease, but concerns regarding cardiac implanted electronic devices (CIEDs) limit its use. This study's goal was to assess the impact of BIA on CIED settings in pediatric patients.
METHODS: This single-center cohort study included two groups: a retrospective cohort of patients under 21 years old who had CIED interrogation within 12 months before and after BIA use, and a smaller prospective cohort who had CIED interrogation immediately before and after BIA use. The prospective group also underwent real-time monitoring for electrical interference during BIA. Exclusion criteria included age, implanted loop recorders, and incomplete data. Analysis used either a paired t-test or a Wilcoxon signed-rank test as appropriate, with p-value < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The retrospective cohort included 55 patients with 80 total tests. A statistically but not clinically significant difference in lead impedance was observed (513 [456, 627] v 513 [399, 593] ohms, p < 0.0001), though no differences were found in electrogram amplitudes, thresholds, or programmed output. When patients with multiple tests were analyzed, there remained a statistically significant difference in lead impedance (513 [399, 614] v 513 [375, 592] ohms, p = 0.0002) but not in other CIED parameters. In the prospective cohort (n = 10), no electrical interference was appreciated during BIA, and there were no before-and-after differences in CIED sensing amplitudes. No inappropriate shocks or premature device failures occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: BIA was not associated with adverse events or meaningful changes in CIED function in this pediatric cohort.

Title: An anatomy-aware spatio-temporal generative extrapolation network for distal ascending aorta restoration in standard echocardiographic views.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), the standard parasternal long-axis (PLAX) view enables reliable evaluation of the aortic valve and aortic root. Owing to the limited field of view of the ultrasound probe and rib-window occlusion, the distal ascending aorta (AA) is frequently truncated, compromising the diagnosis of aortic aneurysm and dilation.
PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views. By aggregating fragmented anatomical features intermittently visible in adjacent frames, we enhance the clarity of vessel wall edges and generate the distal AA structure, thereby completing the missing AA imagery in standard PLAX views.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively collected 1160 TTE videos from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2022 - December 2024), all showing complete AA anatomy. After de-identification, 1059 cases were randomly split into training/validation/test sets (6:2:2), and 101 cases were reserved for observer agreement experiments. An additional 152 videos from three different device models (EPIQ CVX, GE Voluson E10, Resona A20T) formed an external validation set. Two training data types were constructed: (i) dual-view synchronous data - a standard PLAX sequence and an AO-PLAX sequence acquired after a cranial probe shift, phase-matched at end diastole (ED); and (ii) locally masked data - the distal AA region was masked, forcing the model to infer missing anatomy from left-side context. Input sequences of five frames (ED ± 2) were extracted. The proposed Spatio-Temporal Ascending-Aorta generative adversarial network (STAA-GAN) first aligns adjacent frames using an Edge Boosted Feature Alignment (EBFA) module with multi-stage modulated deformable convolutions. A channel-wise fusion strategy then aggregates temporally aligned features. The fused representation is fed into a Swin-UNet generator enhanced with a Strip based Cross window Prediction (SCP) module to capture long-range structural dependencies. Training employs a composite loss including pixel reconstruction, feature reconstruction, texture consistency, relativistic average least-squares GAN (RaLSGAN), temporal coherence, and structure-aware terms, with data-dependent weighting. Statistical analyzes included Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok regression, paired t-tests with Cohen's d, Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and two one-sided tests (TOST, Δ = 0.2  cm  ).
RESULTS: STAA-GAN achieved the best image-quality values among the compared methods, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) = 22.51 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) = 0.7574, multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) = 0.8598, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) = 0.1758. All 12 pairwise comparisons (SRN, IOH, and U-Transformer versus STAA-GAN, designated as the reference group) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (  α 1 = 0.00417  ), with absolute effect sizes ranging from 0.255 to 3.439. The per-frame inference time was 203 ms. In clinical consistency validation, the mean difference between measurements on generated and original images was ≤ 0.01   cm with 95% limits of agreement within ± 0.13   cm; TOST with Δ = 0.2   cm confirmed clinical equivalence for all comparisons ( p < 0.001  ). The segmentation Dice coefficient on generated images averaged 0.913 ± 0.045  across five cross-validation folds. External validation on three different ultrasound devices (Philips, GE, Mindray) maintained consistent equivalence (TOST p < 0.001  , Cohen's d < 0.2  ). These results demonstrate that STAA-GAN produces clinically interchangeable distal ascending aorta images with high fidelity and real-time feasibility.
CONCLUSIONS: STAA-GAN enables extrapolation of the missing distal ascending aorta in standard PLAX views, achieving improved image quality and clinically equivalent diameter measurements on both internal and external validation datasets. These findings support its potential for assisting distal ascending aorta assessment in routine echocardiography.

Title: Bare-Metal vs Covered Balloon-Expandable Stents for Transplant Renal Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare short- and long-term outcomes of bare-metal (BMS) vs covered (CS) balloon-expandable stents in transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure. Long-term outcomes included Doppler ultrasound parameters - peak systolic velocity (PSV), acceleration time (AT) and resistive index (RI) - and restenosis/occlusion rates requiring or not intervention. Graft survival at the latest follow-up was recorded.
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients (mean age 58 ± 13 years, 68% male) were treated with BMS (n = 31) or CS (n = 9). Clinical improvement was observed in 71% of BMS and 83% of CS patients (P = 1.00). Median sCr decreased by 26% and 33% in BMS and CS patients, respectively (P = .30). At a median follow-up of 29 months, there were no statistically significant differences between groups in median PSV reduction (47% BMS vs 47% CS; P = .44), AT improvement (36% BMS vs 25% CS; P = .38) or RI increase (15% BMS vs 33% CS; P = .12). In the BMS group, 2 cases of in-stent restenosis occurred (6.5%). In the CS group, 1 stent occlusion occurred (11%), resulting in graft loss. At final follow-up, overall graft survival was 85%.
CONCLUSION: In this pilot study, BMS and CS showed no significant differences in TRAS outcomes. Further studies are warranted to better guide stent selection.Clinical ImpactIn transplant renal artery stenosis, balloon-expandable covered stents achieved clinical, biochemical and Doppler outcomes comparable to bare-metal stents, despite being used in more complex, atherosclerotic and longer lesions. This first direct comparison suggests that covered stents may be a reasonable option when heavy calcification, a friable wall or mural thrombus raise concern for embolisation or rupture, while bare-metal stents remain appropriate for most lesions. The single late covered-stent occlusion with graft loss highlights the need for careful platform selection and antiplatelet management. These pilot data should inform adequately powered multicentre registries rather than directly change practice.

Title: Comparison of different transplantation routes and timing for stem cell therapy in stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stem cell transplantation holds therapeutic promise for stroke, yet its clinical translation is hindered by unresolved challenges in administration routes, timing, and poor cell engraftment and survival.
METHODS: This is a narrative (non-systematic) review. Registered clinical studies were identified in ClinicalTrials.gov, the European Union Clinical Trials Register and the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, and were supplemented by targeted PubMed searches for the preclinical and mechanistic literature. Records were eligible if they evaluated stem cell transplantation for ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke and reported the delivery route and/or the transplantation time window; records reporting neither were excluded. Because direct head-to-head clinical comparisons of routes and time windows are scarce, registry data and selected preclinical studies were synthesised descriptively rather than pooled, and no meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Each administration route presents a distinct profile. Intravenous injection is minimally invasive and simple but limited by pulmonary sequestration, low cerebral engraftment, and high cell dose requirements. Intra-arterial infusion offers improved targeting but shares similar limitations. Intrathecal delivery allows direct central nervous system access with concentrated doses but carries risks of cerebrospinal fluid leakage and an inflammatory microenvironment. Intracerebral implantation ensures high local engraftment and long-term survival with minimal cell numbers but is invasive and poses risks of hemorrhage and further tissue injury. Intranasal administration is non-invasive with a wide therapeutic window yet exhibits extremely low delivery efficiency. Regarding timing, intravenous and intra-arterial routes are primary in the acute phase; in the subacute phase these routes remain common, alongside intrathecal administration; for chronic stroke, intracerebral and intrathecal transplantation are the predominant strategies in clinical trials.
CONCLUSION: This review synthesizes two decades of progress and persisting challenges in stem cell therapy for stroke, focusing on delivery strategies and timing. Successful clinical translation will require further large-scale, multicenter prospective studies to optimize these critical parameters.

Title: A Pharmacist-Led Antiplatelet Therapy Stewardship Initiative in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Receiving Concomitant Oral Anticoagulants and Single Antiplatelet Therapy.
Abstract: Concomitant therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelets in patients with atrial fibrillation and chronic coronary syndrome significantly increases the risk of bleeding with no added reduction in cardiovascular disease risk over anticoagulation alone. The primary objective was to evaluate an evidence-based antiplatelet stewardship service designed to deprescribe single antiplatelet therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation receiving oral anticoagulants and a single antiplatelet therapy for both primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease. This retrospective study included adult patients aged older than 18 years with atrial fibrillation who were seen at a tertiary academic heart failure center and received therapeutic oral anticoagulants and single antiplatelet therapy for any cardiovascular secondary or primary prevention. The primary outcome was the acceptance of the antiplatelet deprescribing intervention by both providers and patients. The secondary outcomes included provider- or patient-accepted antiplatelet deprescribing intervention. A total of 71 patients were included in the final cohort of this study. The most common indication for the antiplatelet therapy was chronic coronary disease at 69.0 % followed by primary prevention at 14.1% and stroke at 11.3%. The most common antiplatelet therapy was aspirin 81 mg once daily (83.1%), followed by clopidogrel 75 mg once daily(16.9%). Among the 71 patients, 54 (76.1%) were on non-guideline directed antiplatelet therapy. Of the 54 recommendations, 50 (92.6%) were accepted by the providers, and 43 of the 50 provider-accepted recommendations (86.0%) were accepted by the patients. Conclusion: A pharmacist-led antiplatelet deprescribing service is feasible in a tertiary heart failure cardiology outpatient setting. Most recommendations were accepted by the providers and patients.

Title: Cardiometabolic, Physiological and Objective-Sleep Responses to Transcendental Meditation: Secondary Analysis of a Randomised Controlled Trial Among University Staff.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic stress contributes to cardiometabolic risk, and stress-reduction interventions have been proposed to improve stress-sensitive physiology and cardiometabolic health, though evidence remains inconsistent. This study examined the effects of a Transcendental Meditation (TM) intervention on cardiometabolic health and upstream physiological outcomes.
METHODS: This two-arm, open-label RCT compared TM (n = 65) with control (access to university well-being resource, n = 64) among Australian university staff. Secondary outcomes included blood pressure (BP), fasting glucose, HOMA insulin resistance (IR), lipids, C-reactive protein, salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), sympathetic arousal, and a post hoc composite cardiometabolic risk (CMR) score. Post hoc exploratory analyses tested whether burnout, sex and baseline metabolic risk moderated TM effects on HRV, total cholesterol, cortisol slope and IR. Primary analyses were intention-to-treat.
RESULTS: TM was associated with a small diastolic BP reduction (-1.18 mmHg [95% CI: -2.35, -0.01], interaction p = 0.036), with a non-significant trend in the endpoint-only analysis (p = 0.064); no other outcomes differed between groups. Burnout moderated the HRV response (p = 0.02), favouring higher-burnout participants and sex moderated the cholesterol response (p = 0.011), with TM attenuating the control-group rise in females, with uncertainty on LDL and HDL. Interactions for cortisol slope (by sex) and HOMA-IR (by metabolic risk) were non-significant; stratified comparisons suggested numerically greater improvement in TM males and higher-risk participants, respectively. Given no multiplicity correction, all findings are hypothesis-generating only.
CONCLUSION: TM was associated with small, non-robust diastolic BP reduction with no effect on other outcomes. Burnout may modify HRV response, but this finding requires confirmation in adequately powered trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTRN12625000134426.

Title: Association Between Weight Loss on Incretin-Based Therapy and Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Regression.
Abstract:
AIMS: The primary aim was to evaluate, using aggregate-data meta-regression, whether body weight loss induced by incretin mimetic therapy is associated with reductions in three-point major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-MACE), individual cardiovascular outcomes and mortality. A secondary aim was to estimate the overall cardiovascular effects of incretin mimetics compared with placebo.
METHODS: A systematic review of placebo-controlled randomized trials was conducted using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible trials reported cardiovascular hazard ratios (HRs) and weight changes. The primary analysis was an aggregate-data meta-regression, with the prespecified moderator defined as the placebo-adjusted percentage weight difference at the latest reported follow-up time point. Standard meta-analysis was performed to estimate overall treatment effects.
RESULTS: Sixteen randomized trials including 97 199 participants with and without diabetes were analysed. Meta-regression showed no statistically significant association between greater body weight loss and treatment HRs for 3P-MACE, cardiovascular or all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). These findings do not establish an individual-level or causal relationship. Meta-analysis showed significant reductions in 3P-MACE (15%), cardiovascular mortality (13%), all-cause mortality (12%), myocardial infarction (14%), stroke (13%) and HHF (10%).
CONCLUSION: Greater trial-level placebo-adjusted body weight loss was not significantly associated with lower treatment HRs for the cardiovascular and mortality outcomes examined, including 3P-MACE and HHF. These findings do not exclude an individual-level contribution of weight loss to cardiovascular benefit or establish causality. Individual-participant-level analyses are needed to clarify the relationship between weight loss and cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Tibial Periosteal Distraction Technique Promotes Diabetic Foot Ulcer Healing and Improves Limb Preservation Rates: A Multicentre Cohort Study.
Journal: Wound repair and regeneration : official publication of the Wound Healing Society [and] the European Tissue Repair Society
Abstract: Tibial periosteal distraction has emerged as a potential surgical approach for ischemic diabetic foot ulcers, but evidence from large multicentre cohorts remains limited. This multicentre retrospective cohort study aimed to evaluate whether tibial periosteal distraction improves limb-related outcomes compared with standard treatment in patients with advanced ischemic diabetic foot ulcers. Between January 2023 and June 2025, 340 patients with diabetic foot ulcers were treated at three centres. After applying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 249 patients were eligible for analysis: 107 underwent tibial periosteal distraction and 142 received standard wound care and revascularization procedures. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. Primary outcomes were ulcer healing time, major amputation, and recurrence. Computed tomography angiography and histopathology were used to evaluate vascular and tissue changes. Tibial periosteal distraction was associated with significantly shorter median healing time (26 vs. 45 days; p < 0.001), lower major amputation rate (35.5% vs. 64.8%; RR 0.55 [95% CI 0.41-0.74]; p < 0.001), and lower recurrence rate (2.8% vs. 20.4%; RR 0.14 [95% CI 0.04-0.43]; p < 0.001) compared with standard treatment. TPD significantly shortened ulcer healing time (B = 36.485, p < 0.001) and reduced amputation risk (OR = 0.291, p < 0.001) in patients with diabetic foot ulcers. Computed tomography angiography revealed enhanced collateral formation, and histopathologic examination showed morphological changes suggestive of increased vascularity in limbs treated with tibial periosteal distraction. In this multicentre retrospective cohort, tibial periosteal distraction was associated with improved limb-related outcomes compared with standard treatment. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Next-generation incretin therapeutics for polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: navigating current pipeline and clinical considerations.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a complex metabolic-reproductive disorder managed with lifestyle interventions, metformin, and symptom-directed therapies. Incretin-based therapies offer substantial metabolic benefits, but their reproductive efficacy, durability, and phenotypic safety remain incompletely defined.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines the therapeutic evolution from single glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists to dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonism with tirzepatide and triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonism with retatrutide. A structured PubMed search of studies published from January 2023 to October 2026 was supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and reference-list screening. Evidence was evaluated across metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive outcomes.
EXPERT OPINION: Single GLP-1 receptor agonists, particularly semaglutide, improve weight, adiposity, and insulin resistance, with emerging evidence of reproductive benefits. Multi-incretin therapies may provide greater reductions in body weight, visceral and ectopic fat, and insulin resistance. However, PMOS-specific reproductive evidence remains limited. Whether reproductive benefits are independent of weight loss, persist after treatment withdrawal, or differ across PMOS phenotypes is uncertain. Phenotype-stratified randomized trials with standardized reproductive, metabolic, cardiovascular and safety endpoints are needed to determine whether multi-incretins provide durable benefits beyond weight control while maintaining reproductive safety and accessibility.

Title: Remnant Cholesterol Inflammatory Index and its Association With Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity in Middle-Aged and Advanced-Aged Individuals: Evidence From the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
Journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
Abstract: BACKGROUND The association between remnant cholesterol inflammatory index (RCII) and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. RCII is defined as: {Total Cholesterol - (High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol + Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol)] × High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein/10}. This study examined the association between baseline RCII and CMM among middle-aged and older adults in China. MATERIAL AND METHODS This study analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), including 6173 participants. CMM was defined as the coexistence of at least 2 of 4 conditions: hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, or stroke. Participants were grouped according to the quartiles of natural log-transformed RCII (lnRCII) values. Modified Poisson regression models, restricted cubic splines, and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to examine the relationship between lnRCII and CMM outcomes. RESULTS In the cohort, 1832 cases of CMM occurred, and the incidence of CMM was highest in the lnRCII highest-quartile group (P<0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each unit of increase in lnRCII was associated with a higher risk of CMM (RR=1.13, 95% CI: 1.09-1.16), and participants in the highest quartile had a higher risk than those in the lowest quartile (RR=1.69, 95% CI: 1.50-1.90). The area under the curve for lnRCII was 0.607 (95% CI: 0.592-0.622), indicating modest discriminatory ability. CONCLUSIONS Higher baseline lnRCII was associated with an increased risk of incident CMM in middle-aged and older Chinese adults. Although RCII may capture combined information on remnant cholesterol and inflammation, its clinical predictive value requires further validation.

Title: Bachmann Bundle Pacing and Acute Changes in Left Atrial Mechanical Function in Patients With Interatrial Block: A Within-Subject Echocardiography Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial block (IAB) is associated with atrial electromechanical dysfunction and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) has emerged as a physiological atrial pacing strategy capable of restoring interatrial conduction synchrony. However, its impact on left atrial (LA) mechanical function and hemodynamics remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the acute effects of BBP on atrial mechanical parameters in patients with IAB.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 31 patients with IAB who underwent successful BBP implantation were enrolled. A standardized postoperative evaluation protocol was performed under intrinsic sinus rhythm (SR), right atrial septal pacing (RASP) at atrial lead threshold +0.5 V/0.4 ms, and BBP at 5 V/0.4 ms using a within-subject repeated-measures design. Electrocardiographic and echocardiographic parameters were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, with additional adjustment for heart rate.
RESULTS: BBP produced significantly greater P wave duration (PWD) shortening than RASP (p < 0.001). Compared with SR, BBP was associated with lower LA volume indices and higher LA emptying fraction and LA expansion index (all p < 0.001), with consistent superiority over RASP at acute postoperative phase. These associations remained significant after heart rate adjustment. The observed acute changes were consistent across partial and advanced IAB subgroups without significant interaction effects.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with IAB, electrical resynchronization during BBP was accompanied by acute changes in LA mechanical parameters compared with SR and RASP. These findings suggest that BBP may represent a promising physiological pacing strategy for patients with atrial conduction disease.

Title: Haemorrhagic Transformation in Breakthrough Ischemic Stroke: Clinical Characteristics, Outcomes, and Anticoagulation Resumption Timing-Insights from the ASPERA-R Study.
Journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The timing of anticoagulation resumption in patients who experience ischemic stroke despite ongoing anticoagulation and develop haemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains uncertain. We aimed to describe the characteristics and outcomes of patients with HT after a breakthrough ischemic stroke and to explore the association between anticoagulation resumption timing and the model-predicted balance of recurrent ischemic and bleeding risks in this high-risk population.
METHODS: We analysed data from patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke receiving anticoagulation therapy from the multicentre ASPERA-R registry. Analyses focused on patients with HT. HT was defined according to the Heidelberg Bleeding Classification based on brain imaging within 24 hours and categorized as haemorrhagic infarction (HI) or parenchymal hematoma (PH). Anticoagulation resumption and its timing were determined by treating clinicians and were not randomized. Landmark Cox regression models were used to evaluate recurrent ischemic events and moderate-to-severe bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Restricted cubic spline models and exploratory net clinical benefit analyses integrating ischemic and bleeding risks were used to assess the relationship between anticoagulation resumption timing and model-predicted combined risk, overall and across clinically relevant subgroups.
RESULTS: Among 1,555 patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, 269 (17.3%) developed HT, of whom 170 (63.2%) resumed anticoagulation and contributed to the restart-timing analyses. At 90 days, patients with HT had higher crude rates of recurrent ischemic events (27.1% vs 13.8%), moderate-to-severe bleeding (7.4% vs 2.8%), and mortality (34.2% vs 17.7%) compared with patients without HT. In landmark analyses, HT was not associated with recurrent ischemic events (HR 1.42, 95% CI 0.85-2.37) but remained strongly associated with moderate-to-severe bleeding (HR 3.39, 95% CI 1.61-7.13). Exploratory net clinical benefit analyses showed that the model-predicted combined risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke in the overall HT population, with substantial uncertainty around this estimate.
CONCLUSIONS: HT is a marker of poor prognosis in patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke, with an increased risk of bleeding after anticoagulation resumption. Among selected patients who resumed anticoagulation, exploratory modelling suggested that the combined predicted ischemic and bleeding risk reached its nadir at approximately 10 days after stroke. Given the non-randomized treatment timing and potential for treatment-selection bias, this estimate is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

Title: Long-term Prognostic Value of Sequential Coronary CT Angiography and Quantitative PET in Suspected Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Multicentre study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The long-term prognostic value of a guideline-recommended selective sequential anatomical-functional imaging strategy using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) followed by quantitative [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) remains uncertain. We evaluated its long-term prognostic value in patients with first symptoms suggestive of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).
METHODS: In this multicentre European cohort, symptomatic patients first underwent CCTA and were selectively referred to quantitative [15O]H2O PET in case of suspected obstructive stenosis (≥50%). Patients were stratified according to CCTA findings and PET-derived ischaemia (normal CCTA; non-obstructive CAD on CCTA; obstructive CAD on CCTA without ischaemia; obstructive CAD on CCTA with ischaemia). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for unstable angina (UA). Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated.
RESULTS: Among 3,918 patients (61.0±9.8 years; 54.3% female) with a median follow-up of 5.1 [3.8-8.0] years, 278 (7.1%) experienced the primary endpoint. aHRs increased stepwise across CCTA-PET categories. Compared to normal CCTA, non-obstructive CAD and obstructive CAD without ischaemia were associated with a higher risk of the combined primary endpoint (aHR 1.89, [95%CI: 1.23-2.91], p=0.004; aHR 3.20, [95%CI: 1.95-5.25], p<0.001). Among patients with obstructive CAD on CCTA, PET-derived ischaemia further increased the risk of the primary endpoint (aHR 1.55, [95%CI: 1.05-2.30]; p=0.029), but not when excluding UA from the composite endpoint (aHR 1.37, [95%CI 0.90-2.07]; p=0.141). PET-derived ischaemia primarily predicted events within the first year, while obstructive CCTA findings remained associated with long-term hard outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: A sequential strategy combining CCTA and quantitative [15O]H2O PET provides robust and incremental long-term risk stratification. While PET-derived ischaemia refines prediction of short-term and symptom-driven events, CCTA-derived CAD remains the principal determinant of long-term hard outcomes.

Title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Eye: Ocular Safety, Retinal Outcomes, and Clinical Implications.
Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but rapidly expanding use has generated concern about ocular adverse events. In Korea, newly established national health insurance reimbursement criteria for injectable semaglutide (Ozempic prefilled pen) took effect on February 1, 2026; as use among eligible patients may expand, proportionate ophthalmic preparedness is timely. This structured narrative review evaluates randomized trials, systematic reviews, large pharmacoepidemiologic studies, mechanistic investigations, and regulatory assessments through June 30, 2026. The evidence does not support a single class-wide syndrome of ocular toxicity. The most coherent retinal signal is early worsening of diabetic retinopathy during rapid glycemic improvement, particularly in eyes with substantial pre-existing disease; available trial and real-world evidence does not demonstrate a uniform sustained toxic effect. Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is a rare but clinically important semaglutide safety signal. Multiple observational studies and regulatory action justify vigilance, although effect estimates remain heterogeneous and the absolute risk is low. Evidence for neovascular age-related macular degeneration is conflicting, whereas reported associations with retinal vein occlusion and glaucoma remain exploratory. For retina specialists, management should be phenotype based: identify active or advanced diabetic retinopathy, avoid delaying indicated retinal treatment, document the timing and trajectory of metabolic change, and urgently evaluate sudden painless visual loss or field defects. This approach preserves the substantial systemic benefits of incretin therapy while improving recognition of uncommon but consequential ocular events.

Title: EXPRESS: Age, Insurance, and Social Vulnerability as Determinants of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor After New-Onset Heart Failure: Insights from Epic Cosmos.
Journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social determinants of health contribute to inequities in heart failure (HF) management, yet how age, insurance status, and social vulnerability index (SVI) jointly influence sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate how SVI and key demographic and system-level factors impact SGLT2i initiation following new-onset HF.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Epic Cosmos, a national, de-identified electronic health record repository. Adults aged ≥18 years hospitalized with a new HF diagnosis between 2021 and 2024 were included, excluding those with prior SGLT2i use, dialysis-dependent kidney disease, or hospice enrollment. SVI was categorized into quartiles from least vulnerable (Q1) to most vulnerable (Q4). The primary outcome was SGLT2i initiation following index HF hospitalization stratified by SVI, age, and insurance types. Secondary outcomes included crude and age-adjusted mortality.
RESULTS: Among 389,986 patients hospitalized with new HF, 81,387 patients (20.9%) were started on SGLT2i. Higher social vulnerability was inversely associated with initiation (Q4 vs Q1 adjusted OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.98). Younger age was the strongest predictor of initiation (<45 vs 65-74 years: adjusted OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.48-1.59). Commercial insurance was independently associated with higher initiation odds (adjusted OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.18-1.22; p<0.001), as was Medicaid beneficiaries (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.11; p=0.006).
CONCLUSION: In patients with new HF diagnosis, a persistent disadvantage in SGLT2i initiation exists in high-SVI communities. Age and insurance, not social vulnerability alone, are the dominant determinants, highlighting the need for targeted strategies in older adults and payer-level reform.

Title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity.
RESULTS: A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%. Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; P = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; P = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

Title: Outcomes of AngioJet™ Rheolytic Thrombectomy for Occluded Lower-Extremity Bypass Grafts: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower-extremity bypass graft occlusion is associated with recurrent ischemia and potential limb loss. This study evaluated the technical and clinical outcomes of AngioJet™ rheolytic thrombectomy for occluded bypass grafts in a single-center retrospective cohort.
METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing AngioJet™ thrombectomy as the primary strategy for occluded bypass grafts (2014-2024) were reviewed. Technical success was defined as <30% residual stenosis. Outcomes included Rutherford category improvement, complications, 30-day mortality, major amputation, target lesion revascularization, and primary patency. Follow-up was available for 38/40 (95.0%) 30-day survivors.
RESULTS: Forty-one procedures were analyzed. Technical success was achieved in 38/41 (92.7%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 80.1%-98.5%). Periprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients (9.8%; 95% CI: 2.7%-23.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 2.4% (1/41; 95% CI: 0.1%-12.9%) and major amputation was 4.9% (2/41; 95% CI: 0.6%-16.5%). Rutherford category improvement at 30 days was 43.9% (18/41; 95% CI: 28.5%-60.3%). Primary patency at final follow-up was 63.4% (26/41; 95% CI: 46.9%-77.9%) in the overall cohort (intent-to-treat) and 68.4% (26/38; 95% CI: 51.3%-82.5%) among technically successful cases.
CONCLUSION: AngioJet™ thrombectomy is a technically feasible endovascular option for occluded bypass grafts with low 30-day mortality (2.4%) and amputation rates (4.9%). Prospective comparative studies are needed to define its role relative to surgical and alternative endovascular approaches.Clinical ImpactOccluded lower-extremity bypass grafts often cause limb-threatening ischemia in patients at high surgical risk. In this single-center cohort, AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy achieved technical success in 92.7% of procedures, with 30-day mortality of 2.4% and major amputation of 4.9%. These findings support AngioJet-assisted thrombectomy as a minimally invasive option for carefully selected patients with crossable grafts and treatable inflow or outflow disease. Clinicians should anticipate adjunctive interventions, monitor for compartment syndrome, and provide structured surveillance because reintervention remains common. Prospective comparative studies are needed before routine first-line use.

Title: Sex-based differences in the atrial fibrillation care pathway and outcomes: an ITHACA-database analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: To characterize sex-specific differences in clinical presentation, evaluate progression through the atrial fibrillation (AF) care pathway from diagnosis to catheter ablation (CA) and assess long-term outcomes.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with incident AF at Northwell Health between 2015 and 2024 from the ITHACA-database. Sex-specific differences in clinical presentation were examined. The AF care pathway was operationalized as a stepwise cascade, modelling conditional drop-off to identify care gaps. Sex-specific CA risk ratios were assessed via Poisson regression. Incident AF was identified among 165 563/655 459 patients (71.4 ± 11.6 years, 32% non-white, 45% female) with a recorded diagnosis of AF. Women were older (73.3 ± 10.6 vs. 69.8 ± 12.1 years, P < 0.001), had higher rates of dementia (9.1% vs. 5.2%), stroke (8.6% vs. 7.4%) and congestive heart failure (21.5% vs. 20.8%) at diagnosis. Transfer-of-care gaps [median 3.6 years follow-up, 96% retention] were identified at every level: 31.5% of women vs. 35.3% of men were evaluated by cardiology, 16.2% vs. 21.6% by electrophysiology, and 3.5% vs. 5.7% underwent CA (all P < 0.001). Women were 16% less likely to receive CA (RR 0.84 95% CI 0.77-0.91). In cause-specific Cox models, female sex was associated with incident stroke (aHR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.30) and dementia (aHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.24-1.35), but modestly lower mortality after adjustment (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99).
CONCLUSION: In this real-world analysis, significant sex-specific differences in clinical phenotype at presentation, progression through the AF care pathway and clinical outcomes were observed.

Title: Examining Racial Disparities in Lower Extremity Amputation Outcomes Among Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers in North America: A Multicohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Racial and ethnic disparities in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) outcomes are well described. We examined whether differences in major and minor lower extremity amputation (LEA) persist after matching for comorbidities, and whether the level of amputation identifies opportunities for earlier limb-preservation intervention.
APPROACH: In this retrospective, propensity-matched cohort study using the TriNetX network (2002-2019), reported in accordance with Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology, adults with DFU were identified by diagnostic codes and stratified by race/ethnicity. Minor and major LEA risks were compared with a matched White (non-Hispanic) reference, reporting both relative and absolute risks. We also calculated the high-to-low (Hi-Lo) ratio (major:minor).
RESULTS: Among 388,371 adults with DFU and after matching, Hispanic and African American patients had higher minor, major, and overall LEA risk than White patients (major-LEA absolute risk 3.0-4.7% vs. ∼2.7%; relative risks up to 1.89). Asian patients had the lowest risk. Native American patients had the highest Hi-Lo (major-to-minor amputation) ratio despite no significant increase in major-LEA risk, suggesting potential differences in disease presentation or access to limb-preservation care that warrant further study. Disparities persisted after adjustment for diabetes-related comorbidities and peripheral arterial disease.
INNOVATION: Applied to a multiethnic DFU cohort, the Hi-Lo ratio gave a descriptive view of major- versus minor-amputation burden, most notably in Native American patients.
CONCLUSION: The Hi-Lo amputation ratio may identify populations experiencing disproportionate major limb loss and help prioritize earlier vascular assessment, multidisciplinary limb-preservation referral, and posthealing surveillance. Persistent racial and ethnic differences after matching warrant further study of disease severity, access, and care delivery.[Figure: see text].

Title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiovascular Health Behavior Change: A Narrative Review of Patient-Facing Tools.
Journal: Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States and disproportionately affects racial/ethnic minoritized populations, low-income communities, older adults, and rural residents. Behavioral interventions can reduce cardiovascular risk, yet traditional programs face scalability barriers, including high costs and limited reach. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the efficacy and equity of patient-directed AI tools that support health education and behavior change for cardiovascular health. Using PRISMA-ScR elements, we searched 10 databases (January 2010 to December 2025), yielding 19 empirical studies evaluating Generation 2.0 AI systems aligned with the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. Of these, five were randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and 14 were nonrandomized (quasi-experimental, observational, or early-stage) studies. AI-enabled interventions such as conversational agents, machine-learning models, and reinforcement-learning systems addressed hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, and related conditions. Among the RCTs, one demonstrated superiority of an AI-powered program over usual care (AI-delivered Diabetes Prevention Program), whereas the remaining four reported outcomes equivalent or non-inferior to standard behavioral care. Effects were most apparent in high-intensity interventions that paired machine learning-based personalization with structured behavioral curricula, although the multi-component nature of these programs limits inference about AI-specific contributions. Across nonrandomized studies, greater engagement intensity was consistently associated with improved cardiometabolic outcomes, although causal attribution to AI-specific mechanisms remains limited. Most studies had small samples, short follow-up, and limited reporting on safety and equity. Technology-intensive interventions were concentrated in higher-resourced settings, and populations with limited health literacy showed reduced engagement. Overall, evidence supports cautious optimism that AI can meaningfully scale personalized cardiovascular prevention; however, realizing that equitable and clinically meaningful impact will require rigorous trials with longer follow-up, explicit behavioral science integration, safety-conscious governance, and equity-centered strategies addressing digital determinants of health.

Title: Body Mass Index, Cardiometabolic Treatment Patterns and Multifactorial Risk-Factor Control in Chinese Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To examine medication use and simultaneous achievement of glycemic, blood pressure and lipid targets across body mass index (BMI) categories in Chinese adults with Type 2 diabetes.
METHODS: This BMI-focused secondary cross-sectional analysis included 8590 adults with evaluable BMI recruited from 60 hospitals in the iCaReMe China Registry. The primary comparison was obesity versus normal weight for simultaneous achievement of HbA1c < 7.0%, blood pressure < 130/80 mmHg and LDL cholesterol < 2.6 mmol/L.
