Missing data were handled by multiple imputation (20 datasets; 20 iterations per chain), and associations were estimated with center-clustered generalized estimating equations (GEE).
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 99 (1.2%) adults with underweight, 2725 (31.7%) normal weight, 3663 (42.6%) overweight, and 2103 (24.5%) obesity. Among 6683 with all three observed components, 332 (5.0%) achieved the composite. Compared with normal weight, the pooled adjusted OR for obesity was 0.55 (95% CI 0.39-0.78); each 1-kg/m2 higher BMI was associated with an OR of 0.93 (0.90-0.96). For obesity, component-specific ORs were 0.72 (0.61-0.85) for HbA1c, 0.47 (0.40-0.55) for blood pressure and 1.05 (0.91-1.22) for LDL-C. Sensitivity analyses supported the composite finding, with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.904).
CONCLUSIONS: Obesity was associated with lower odds of simultaneous target attainment, with component-specific associations for glycemia and blood pressure but not LDL-C. GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors were used more often at higher BMI; these prescribing patterns do not establish treatment effectiveness.

Title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50).
CONCLUSION: The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

Title: Complication Prevention Beyond Glycaemic Control in Type 2 Diabetes: Cumulative Metabolic Exposure, Organ Vulnerability and Treatment Durability.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Type 2 diabetes is a progressive multisystem disorder in which long-term complication burden reflects more than contemporaneous glycaemic control. Age at onset, previous metabolic exposure, obesity-related risk, organ injury, treatment safety and the capacity to sustain effective care interact across the disease course.
METHODS: This critical narrative review synthesised targeted PubMed/MEDLINE searches, international guidance, landmark and contemporary randomised trials, longitudinal cohorts, validated risk models and clinically influential reviews. A targeted update search was completed through 22 September 2026.
RESULTS: The evidence supports a clinically ordered approach in which immediate treatment-related hazards are considered first, followed by established organ disease or a dominant preventable outcome, residual modifiable cardiometabolic exposure, treatment durability and the care systems required to translate evidence into sustained benefit. Historical trials established the importance of glycaemic, blood-pressure and lipid management and coordinated multifactorial intervention. Contemporary SGLT2 inhibitor and incretin-based trials add direct cardiovascular, heart-failure and kidney outcome evidence in defined populations, while MASH trials provide emerging histological evidence. HbA1c, validated risk equations and organ-specific pathways retain their established roles.
CONCLUSIONS: The proposed framework is interpretive rather than predictive. It does not assign numerical weights or treatment thresholds but aims to identify the preventable outcome that should take priority, the intervention supported by the most relevant evidence and whether that intervention can be implemented safely and durably.

Title: Stroke and cognitive decline: associations of social support and family connections in CHARLS and ELSA cohorts.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is associated with accelerated cognitive decline in older adults, but whether social support and family connections statistically moderate this association has rarely been tested formally in longitudinal, cross-national data.
METHODS: We analyzed the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; N = 11,569; Wave 1 [2011] baseline to Wave 4 [2018], up to 7.2 years) and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; N = 5,713; Wave 3 [2006-2007] baseline to Wave 9 [2019], up to 13.0 years). Cognitive function was assessed with a harmonized composite (orientation, immediate and delayed word recall, plus pentagon drawing in CHARLS). Linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts and slopes estimated the incident-stroke × time interaction (annual cognitive decline, points/year), adjusting for age, sex, BMI, education, marital status, smoking, drinking, comorbidity count, and residence (CHARLS only). A three-way interaction (stroke × social support/family connection × time) formally tested moderation. Propensity-score matching (1:2 nearest-neighbor) and subgroup analyses (age, sex, education) served as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Incident stroke occurred in 770 CHARLS (6.6%) and 347 ELSA (6.1%) participants. In fully adjusted models, stroke was associated with significantly faster cognitive decline in both cohorts (CHARLS: β = -0.068 points/year, 95% CI - 0.123 to - 0.013, p = 0.016; ELSA: β = -0.190, 95% CI - 0.229 to - 0.152, p < 0.001); after propensity-score matching, the ELSA association remained robust (β = -0.150, p < 0.001) while the CHARLS estimate was attenuated and no longer significant (β = -0.029, p = 0.386). The formal three-way interaction showed that higher family connection significantly attenuated stroke-related decline in ELSA ; the corresponding interaction for social support in CHARLS was directionally consistent but not significant (β = +0.082, 95% CI - 0.037 to 0.202, p = 0.177). Subgroup analyses showed a significant stroke-decline association across all age, sex, and education strata in ELSA, and only among male and less-educated participants in CHARLS.
CONCLUSION: Incident stroke was associated with faster cognitive decline in both a Chinese and an English cohort of middle-aged and older adults. A formal statistical test indicated that family connections significantly moderated this association in ELSA, whereas a similar but non-significant pattern was observed for social support in CHARLS. These associations warrant further investigation of social relationships as a potentially modifiable factor in post-stroke cognitive health; the observational design precludes causal conclusions.

Title: Joint effects of air pollution and compound dry-hot extremes on cardiovascular disease risk across adults: a cohort study in China.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Compound dry-hot extremes (CDHEs) and ambient air pollution are growing public health threats under global climate change, yet their joint impacts on cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk remain poorly understood.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide longitudinal cohort study using data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), including 9,265 Chinese adults aged ≥ 18 years with 69,297 repeated observations between 2010 and 2018. We evaluated the independent, joint and heterogeneous effects of multi-dimensional CDHE metrics (accumulated days, frequency and average severity) and key air pollutants (e.g., PM2.5) on incident CVD. Mixed-effects Cox models, interaction analyses and stratified analyses were performed to examine the study objectives.
RESULTS: Per interquartile range (IQR) increment in CDHE cumulative days and PM2.5 concentration were associated with 30% (HR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.20-1.41) and 54% (HR = 1.54, 95% CI: 1.42-1.67) higher CVD risk, respectively, with CDHE accumulated days rather than event frequency or intensity driving the long-term cardiovascular damage. Both exposures showed the strongest risk elevations for coronary heart disease, with 72% (HR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.44-2.07) and 75% (HR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.46-2.11) risk increments per IQR for CDHE cumulative days and PM2.5, respectively. Critically, concurrent high exposure to CDHEs and PM2.5 induced synergistic elevated CVD risk, with the joint hazard ratio reaching 1.92 (95% CI: 1.67-2.21), and this synergistic pattern was consistent across PM1, PM10, NO2 and O3. Stratified analyses further revealed that older adults, males, urban residents, smokers, drinkers, physically inactive and overweight individuals were more susceptible to these environmental risks.
CONCLUSIONS: Compound dry-hot extremes and ambient air pollution are independent risk factors for incident CVD in Chinese adults. Concurrent exposure to these two environmental stressors induces synergistic cardiovascular damage, with CDHE accumulated days being the primary driver. These findings pointing to the necessity for integrated public health strategies that simultaneously target air quality improvement and climate resilience.

Title: Admission cardiac and renal biomarkers for early identification of type 1 cardiorenal syndrome after acute myocardial infarction.
Abstract: This retrospective study evaluated the diagnostic screening and early identification value of admission baseline cardiac and renal biomarkers for newly developed in-hospital type 1 cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Baseline samples were collected at emergency admission before the documented onset of renal injury. A total of 150 AMI patients were included, comprising 60 patients who developed incident CRS and 90 AMI controls without renal impairment. Laboratory indicators included cardiac markers (cardiac troponin I [cTnI] and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP]) and renal-related markers including retinol-binding protein (RBP), urea, serum creatinine and spot urinary microalbumin. Multivariate logistic regression adjusted for infarct size, haemodynamic status, baseline renal function, comorbidities and guideline-directed cardiovascular medications, and ROC analysis assessed discriminatory performance. Baseline urea, urinary microalbumin and NT-proBNP were higher, while RBP was lower, in patients who developed CRS (all P < 0.0001). Independently associated indicators included cTnI (OR = 0.628, 95% CI: 0.436-0.903, P = 0.012), RBP (OR = 0.931, 95% CI: 0.883-0.981, P = 0.008), urea (OR = 1.226, 95% CI: 1.039-1.446, P = 0.016) and urinary microalbumin (OR = 1.017, 95% CI: 1.004-1.031, P = 0.013). Urea showed the highest AUC (0.914; sensitivity, 78.5%; specificity, 83.4%). Raw urinary microalbumin showed an AUC of 0.747, and urinary microalbumin showed improved discriminatory performance after urine creatinine calibration and covariate adjustment (AUC = 0.883). Combined assessment of these biomarkers may support diagnostic screening of AMI patients at increased risk of in-hospital CRS.

Title: Impact of preprocedural frailty on long-term mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the association between preprocedural frailty and long-term all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from database inception to 15 February 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to pool adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) with their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Thirteen cohort studies involving 429,827 patients were included in the systematic review. Of these, 8 studies (4,726 patients) reporting comparable adjusted effect estimates were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. Preprocedural frailty was associated with a higher risk of long-term all-cause mortality after TAVR (HR = 1.85, 95% CI 1.51-2.25; I² = 39.4%). The association was generally consistent across subgroup analyses stratified by follow-up duration and frailty assessment methodology. Five studies that were not amenable to quantitative pooling because of non-comparable effect formats or data structures showed a concordant direction of effect, with some studies demonstrating a graded relationship between increasing frailty burden and mortality risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Preprocedural frailty is significantly associated with increased long-term all-cause mortality in older adults undergoing TAVR. These findings support the incorporation of frailty assessment into routine preprocedural geriatric risk stratification and multidisciplinary decision-making.

Title: Prognostic value of OCT biomarkers and systemic factors for early and long term anatomical treatment response in diabetic macular edema.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the prognostic value of baseline optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers and systemic factors for early and long-term anatomical response to anti-VEGF therapy in diabetic macular edema (DME).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 164 eyes from 105 patients with type 2 diabetes and DME who received three monthly loading doses of intravitreal bevacizumab (January 2013 to April 2024) and were subsequently managed with a pro re nata (PRN) regimen using standard retreatment criteria. Completion of the loading phase (minimum follow-up, 3 months) was required for inclusion. Anatomical response was assessed after the loading phase (early response) and at final follow-up (long-term response); eyes were classified as full, partial, or non-responders based on CMT and OCT morphology. Baseline demographic, systemic, and OCT characteristics were analyzed using generalized estimating equation (GEE) logistic regression to account for inter-eye correlation, followed by one-eye-per-patient sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: After loading, 10 eyes (6.1%) were full responders, 72 (43.9%) partial responders, and 82 (50.0%) non-responders; 90% of early full responders maintained full response at final follow-up. In multivariable GEE analyses, higher baseline CMT, higher hyperreflective foci (HRF) count, and hyperreflective intraretinal material were independently associated with early anatomical response under the original percentage-reduction outcome definition; for long-term response, baseline CMT was only nominally associated and did not survive correction for multiple testing, and DRIL, EZ/ELM defect, and intraretinal cyst size were not significant. Both models showed moderate discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (AUC 0.751 and 0.757, respectively). Sensitivity analyses across eye-selection strategies were consistent for baseline CMT, DRIL, EZ/ELM defect, and hyperreflective material, but intraretinal cyst size was unstable; all associations were sensitive to how anatomical response was defined.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline OCT biomarkers showed candidate associations with anatomical response, but several, including the hyperreflective-material association, were not reproduced when the outcome was redefined using continuous final CMT or an absolute CMT threshold, despite robustness within the primary model. Discrimination was moderate (optimism-corrected AUC 0.75-0.76). These findings identify candidate prognostic OCT biomarkers requiring external validation before clinical application.

Title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.
METHODS: Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared.
RESULTS: A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV patients demonstrated greater improvements in left ventricular function and transvalvular hemodynamics, suggesting that bicuspid morphology itself does not confer an adverse long-term prognostic effect in appropriately selected patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR.

Title: Habitual sodium intake and metabolic abnormalities in Korean adults with obesity: a cross-sectional analysis of a prospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium intake is well recognized for its contribution to hypertension, but growing evidence suggests broader metabolic effects, particularly among individuals with obesity who are vulnerable to metabolic disturbances. This study investigated the cross-sectional associations between habitual sodium intake and metabolic diseases and related markers using baseline data from a prospective cohort of Korean adults with obesity.
METHODS: Participants with obesity (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2) and at least one metabolic condition were recruited from Severance Hospital, Seoul, Republic of Korea. Sodium intake was assessed using a food frequency questionnaire, and associations with diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease were evaluated using multivariable regression models. Mean differences in metabolic markers across sodium tertiles were examined using analysis of covariance with sex stratification.
RESULTS: Of the 633 individuals enrolled, 487 with obesity were included in the final analysis after excluding non-obese participants and those with implausible energy intake. No statistically significant associations were observed between sodium intake and the prevalence of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, or cardiovascular disease. In sex-stratified biomarker analyses, LDL-C, non-HDL-C, CRI-I, and CRI-II differed across sodium tertiles among women, whereas no such differences were observed in men.
CONCLUSIONS: In Korean adults with obesity and pre-existing metabolic conditions, increasing sodium intake was not significantly associated with higher prevalence of major metabolic diseases. In exploratory sex-stratified analyses, several atherogenic lipid markers differed across sodium intake tertiles among women only. This within-women pattern should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in future longitudinal analyses of this cohort.

Title: Linking serum lipid profiles to carotid artery calcifications: a computed tomography based investigation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the association between serum lipid parameters and carotid artery calcifications (CACs) detected on non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scans and to assess potential predictors of calcification severity.
METHODS: A total of 197 patients (mean age = 61.98 ± 16.63 years) who underwent head and neck CT and had corresponding serum lipid data were retrospectively analyzed. CACs were graded on a six-point scale (0-5). Serum lipid profiles, including total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL, HDL, and VLDL, were compared between patients with and without CAC. Logistic regression analysis was used to determine independent predictors of calcification.
RESULTS: CACs were identified in 33 patients (16.8%), with 7 right-sided, 12 left-sided, and 14 bilateral cases. The mean triglyceride level was higher in patients with CACs (184.18 mg/dL) than in those without (144.44 mg/dL). A moderate but nonsignificant difference (p = 0.106; Cohen's d = 0.36) was found. Age was the only independent predictor of CAC presence (p < 0.001; OR = 1.081) with an 8.1% increase in odds per year. No significant associations were found for total cholesterol, LDL, or HDL.
CONCLUSIONS: Age was found to be the only independent predictor of CAC. Although triglyceride levels were higher in patients with CAC, this difference was not statistically significant and should be interpreted with caution. Incidental detection of CAC on head and neck imaging may support interdisciplinary referral and cardiovascular risk assessment, particularly in older patients and in cases with more extensive calcification.

Title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the incidence and mortality of Takotsubo syndrome in Sweden, a report from the SWEDEHEART registry.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is often triggered by intense emotional or physical stress, with symptoms closely resembling those of acute myocardial infarction and heart failure. The COVID-19 pandemic caused unprecedented psychological, social, and economic stress, with TTS incidence and mortality either increasing or remaining stable. Previous studies have relied on single- or multicenter data, lacking the scope to provide national-level insights. This study aimed to fill the gap by investigating the incidence and outcomes of TTS across Sweden during two distinct periods: the pre-pandemic period (January 2015 to March 2020) and the pandemic period (April 2020 to December 2022).
METHODS: Using the nationwide Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry, we assessed the incidence rate (IR) for all patients with TTS referred for coronary angiography in Sweden. We calculated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) both before and during the pandemic using quasi-Poisson regression, adjusted for age and sex. We evaluated 30-day and 1-year mortality using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, accounting for clustering within hospitals.
RESULTS: We identified 3,180 patients hospitalized with TTS during the study period: 69% (2,189) pre-pandemic and 31% (991) during the pandemic. The incidence of TTS was 10% lower during the pandemic compared to the pre-pandemic period (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84-0.97, P = 0.008). The cohort's crude all-cause mortality rate was 2.73% at 30 days and 6.10% at 1 year, with no significant difference at 30 days (adjusted HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.69-1.78, P = 0.642) or one year (adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.75-1.46, P = 0.780). Compared with studies in other countries where incidence increased or remained unchanged, COVID-19 incidence was similar across the matching periods.
CONCLUSIONS: This nationwide observational study found a lower incidence of TTS during the pandemic compared to the pre-pandemic period, while mortality rates remained unchanged. The reduced incidence of TTS in Sweden may reflect the country's comparatively milder pandemic control measures and more robust social security infrastructure relative to other nations.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Evaluation of renal parenchymal stiffness using shear wave elastography in Behçet's disease without clinical renal involvement.
Abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Renal involvement in Behçet's disease is uncommon but clinically relevant and may remain subclinical in the absence of abnormal renal function tests or urinalysis findings. Shear wave elastography (SWE) may provide quantitative information on renal parenchymal stiffness beyond conventional ultrasonographic parameters. To evaluate renal parenchymal stiffness using SWE in patients with Behçet's disease without clinical, biochemical, or urinalysis evidence of renal involvement.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective case-control study included 29 patients with Behçet's disease and 40 healthy controls. All participants underwent conventional renal ultrasonography and renal SWE using a standardized protocol. Renal length, width, cortical thickness, and right and left renal parenchymal stiffness values were recorded. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, disease activity scores, organ involvement, and treatment status were analyzed in the Behçet's disease group.
RESULTS: Patients with Behçet's disease had significantly higher right, left, and mean renal parenchymal stiffness values than healthy controls. Mean renal stiffness was 6.87 ± 1.39 kPa in the Behçet's disease group and 4.87 ± 0.39 kPa in controls (p < 0.001). In contrast, renal length, width, and cortical thickness did not differ significantly between groups. Mean renal stiffness showed a positive correlation with erythrocyte sedimentation rate (r = 0.675, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression analysis, erythrocyte sedimentation rate remained independently associated with mean renal stiffness, while composite immunosuppressive treatment was associated with lower stiffness values. Exploratory ROC analysis showed good discriminatory performance of mean renal stiffness for differentiating patients with Behçet's disease from controls.
CONCLUSION: Renal parenchymal stiffness is increased in patients with Behçet's disease despite normal renal function, normal urinalysis, and preserved conventional ultrasonographic parameters. As a pilot study, these findings suggest that SWE may provide additional quantitative information on subclinical renal parenchymal alterations in Behçet's disease; however, larger longitudinal studies are required to validate its clinical significance.

Title: Age-stratified clinical phenotypes of cardiac implantable electronic device infections: a 20-year retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The widespread adoption of cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been accompanied by a parallel increase in severe CIED infections. Traditional risk stratification frequently relies on binary age cutoffs, which can obscure how infection phenotypes evolve across a patient's lifespan. This study evaluated how advancing age-analyzed across ordered chronological strata-correlates with anatomical infection site, device hardware type, microbiology, and in-hospital mortality in patients with CIED infections.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of 383 patients treated for CIED infections between 2002 and 2022, patients were categorized into five sequential age brackets (< 50 to 80-90 years). Age was modeled both categorically across these strata and continuously to estimate per-decade odds ratios (ORs) for clinical presentation, hardware type, and microbiological findings.
RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (75.2%) with a mean age of 67.4 years. Pacemaker involvement increased significantly with age (p < 0.001), whereas implantable cardioverter-defibrillator use declined (p = 0.036). Localized generator pocket infections demonstrated a pronounced age-dependent gradient, rising from 19.4% in patients under 50 years to 73.0% in octogenarians (p < 0.001; OR 1.43 per decade, 95% CI: 1.21-1.69). Conversely, systemic presentations-including bacteremia and lead endocarditis-showed no age-dependent trend. In-hospital mortality remained low and stable across age groups (p = 0.452) but was markedly higher in patients presenting with bacteremia or sepsis compared to those without systemic involvement (16.7% vs. 1.6%, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Analyzing age as a continuous spectrum reveals a distinct clinical phenotype dominated by localized pocket infections and low-power devices, an insight obscured by standard binary age cutoffs. Crucially, mortality risk was driven by systemic bloodstream infection rather than patient age itself, emphasizing that clinical surveillance should prioritize infection phenotype over chronological age alone.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Emotional distress in patients before first-time and redo catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is frequently accompanied by anxiety and depressive symptoms, which may affect quality of life. While catheter ablation (CA) is an established therapy for AF, data comparing emotional distress burden prior to first-time vs. redo CA procedures remain limited.
AIM: To compare pre-procedural anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients undergoing first-time AF/atypical atrial flutter CA vs. those undergoing redo AF/atypical atrial flutter CA.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients with AF or atypical atrial flutter scheduled for CA (first-time or redo) between January 2024 and May 2025. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed one day prior to the CA using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).
RESULTS: Overall, 112 patients who underwent first-time CA and 49 patients who underwent redo CA were included. Most baseline characteristics were similar between groups; however, redo CA patients had a higher prevalence of persistent AF and prior stroke and higher CHA₂DS₂-VA scores. Patients scheduled for first-time (vs. redo) CA had significantly higher emotional distress. Median HADS depression and anxiety scores were significantly higher in the first-time CA group compared with the redo CA group (10 [9-11] vs. 2 [1-5], p < 0.001 and 13 [11.5-14] vs. 5 [2-9], p < 0.001; respectively. Distributional analyses demonstrated a consistent shift of the HADS-A and HADS-D score distributions toward higher values in the first-time CA group, supported by large non-parametric effect sizes. After adjustment for persistent AF, diabetes mellitus, and prior stroke, first-time CA remained associated with a higher burden of anxiety and depressive symptoms compared with redo CA patients. Persistent AF was associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing first-time AF CA experience higher anxiety and depressive symptom burden than those undergoing redo CA.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Mechanical thrombectomy in nonagenarians: real-world outcomes from a highly selected cohort treated at a comprehensive stroke center.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence supporting mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in very elderly patients remains limited, as nonagenarians are underrepresented in randomized trials and frequently excluded from MT in routine practice. We evaluated the effectiveness and safety of MT in carefully selected patients aged ≥ 90 years treated at a comprehensive stroke center.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study including consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion treated with MT. Fifty nonagenarians treated between 2017 and 2025 were compared with 100 younger patients treated in 2023. In both groups, only patients with preserved pre-stroke functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) were included. Nonagenarians underwent detailed pre-treatment clinical assessment prior to treatment. Primary outcomes were functional independence (mRS 0-2) and all-cause mortality at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3), neurological status at discharge, and hemorrhagic complications. Multivariable regression models were used to adjust for baseline imbalances and clinically relevant prognostic factors.
RESULTS: Nonagenarians had a substantially higher burden of comorbidities and worse pre-stroke functional status than younger patients. Successful reperfusion rates were similar between groups (92% vs. 90%). Functional independence at 90 days was achieved in 18% of nonagenarians and 50% of younger patients, while 90-day mortality was 52% and 20%, respectively. In unadjusted analyses, nonagenarians had lower odds of functional independence and higher odds of mortality. After adjustment for baseline clinical and prognostic factors, the estimated associations were attenuated, although confidence intervals remained wide and the study could not exclude a clinically relevant age-associated effect. Parenchymal hematoma occurred more frequently among nonagenarians, whereas rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this highly selected real-world cohort, MT achieved high rates of successful reperfusion in nonagenarians, but functional outcomes and mortality were substantially less favorable than in younger patients. Adjustment for baseline clinical and prognostic factors attenuated the estimated associations, although clinically relevant age-associated differences could not be excluded. These findings support cautious, individualized treatment decisions incorporating chronological age, pre-stroke function, comorbidity burden, imaging findings, and the overall clinical profile.

Title: Unsupervised learning based on CT imaging in identifying subtypes of acute ischemic stroke severity.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore unsupervised learning based on CT imaging for identifying severity subtypes of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) in the middle cerebral artery territory.
METHODS: One hundred seventy-three AIS patients were retrospectively enrolled. K-means clustering was performed on clinical and CT features to identify severity subtypes. NIHSS scores were compared between subtypes. Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) served as an adverse outcome to compare associations of cluster subtypes versus NIHSS scores.
RESULTS: Two subtypes were identified. Subtype 1 (severe) showed larger infarct volumes, higher rates of basal ganglia involvement and dense middle cerebral artery sign, longer onset time, and younger age than Subtype 2 (non-severe) (all p < 0.001). Median NIHSS score was higher in Subtype 1 [17.0 (14.0,19.0) vs. 12.0 (8.0,17.0), p < 0.001]. HT identification accuracy was 70% for cluster subtypes vs. 67% for NIHSS scores. AUC for HT was 0.692 (subtypes), 0.679 (NIHSS), and 0.741 (combined). For poor 90-day functional outcome (mRS ≥ 3), AUC was 0.71 (subtypes), 0.69 (NIHSS), and 0.76 (combined).
CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised learning based on CT imaging effectively identifies AIS severity subtypes and may serve as an objective method for assessing post-stroke neurological damage.

Title: Baseline atherogenic coefficient and risk of incident chronic liver disease: a prospective cohort study from the CHARLS.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is a major public health burden, particularly among middle-aged and older adults. The atherogenic coefficient [(TC - HDL-C)/HDL-C]is a simple lipid-derived index widely used in metabolic risk assessment, but its longitudinal association with incident CLD remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the longitudinal association between the atherogenic coefficient [(TC - HDL-C)/HDL-C]and the risk of incident chronic liver disease among middle-aged and older adults using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).
METHODS: This prospective cohort study used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 6,721 participants aged ≥ 45 years without CLD at baseline (2011) were followed through 2020. The atherogenic coefficient was analyzed as both a continuous and categorical variable. Cox proportional hazards models were applied to assess associations with incident CLD, and restricted cubic spline models were used to explore nonlinear dose-response relationships.
RESULTS: Among the 6721 participants, 552 participants (8.2%) developed chronic liver disease. Higher baseline atherogenic coefficient was associated with an increased risk of incident CLD. In fully adjusted Cox models, participants in the high atherogenic coefficient group had a significantly higher risk of CLD compared with those in the low-risk group (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.56, 95%CI-1.17-2.06; p = 0.002). Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested an overall positive association between the atherogenic coefficient and incident CLD, with the lowest estimated risk observed around an atherogenic coefficient of approximately 3 and a tendency toward higher risk at higher atherogenic coefficient levels (p for overall < 0.001). Subgroup analyses showed broadly consistent associations across examined subpopulations.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher baseline atherogenic coefficient may be associated with an increased risk of incident chronic liver disease among middle-aged and older Chinese adults.

Title: Safety and Tolerability of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors: A State-of-the-Art Narrative Review.
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) have evolved from glucose-lowering agents to foundational therapies for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, with substantial benefits for cardiovascular, kidney, and survival outcomes. As their indications continue to expand, a comprehensive understanding of their safety and tolerability has become increasingly important for optimizing patient care. Building on our recent state-of-the-art review of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, this review provides a contemporary synthesis of the evidence on the safety and tolerability of SGLT-2is. We critically appraise data from randomized controlled trials, cardiovascular and kidney outcome trials, pharmacovigilance databases, large observational studies, and systematic reviews and meta-analyses. The available evidence demonstrates that SGLT-2is have a favorable overall safety profile, with genital mycotic infections representing the most consistently observed adverse event. Volume depletion and euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis remain clinically important but are uncommon and are largely preventable through appropriate patient selection, patient education, and temporary treatment interruption during high-risk clinical situations. Fournier's gangrene should be regarded as a very rare but serious complication requiring prompt recognition and treatment. In contrast, randomized trials and meta-analyses generally indicate a reduced risk of acute kidney injury, while evidence concerning fracture, lower-limb amputation, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and cancer is less definitive. Although consistent class-wide increases in these latter outcomes have not been established, uncommon or agent-specific risks cannot be excluded, particularly where event numbers are small or follow-up is limited. Overall, treatment discontinuation because of adverse events is low across major cardiovascular, heart failure, and kidney outcome trials, supporting the excellent tolerability of this therapeutic class. Comparative evidence suggests only modest differences among individual SGLT-2is, although definitive conclusions remain limited by the absence of direct, large, randomized head-to-head trials. We also summarize practical strategies for adverse-event mitigation, monitoring, temporary treatment interruption, and individualized patient selection. As the clinical applications of SGLT-2is continue to broaden, ongoing pharmacovigilance, inclusive clinical trials, and comparative safety studies will be essential to further refine their benefit-risk profile and optimize their safe use across diverse patient populations.

Title: Markers of early cardiac dysfunction in young adults with insomnia disorder: a case-control study.
Journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Insomnia is a highly prevalent, chronic disorder that is a modifiable novel risk factor for cardiovascular disease. However, there are fewer physiological data available suggesting that insomnia may be related to early cardiac disease and atherosclerotic progression among young adults (ages 21-44 years). In this case-control study, we investigated the association between insomnia and subclinical cardiovascular disease risk markers in a sample of young adults with ICSD-3-diagnosed insomnia compared to healthy good sleepers.
METHODS: Among a sample of 43 community-based, healthy young adults (18 individuals with insomnia disorder, 25 good sleeping controls; Mage = 28.7 years, range 21-42), we compared indices of cardiac function with 2D echocardiography, endothelial dysfunction with flow-mediated endothelial dilation, and arterial stiffness with carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, adjusted for body mass index.
RESULTS: The insomnia group had worse left ventricular global longitudinal strain in comparison to the good sleeping controls (insomnia M(SD) - 22.8 (2.2), good sleeping controls - 24.3 (1.5), F[1, 39] = 7.42, p = 0.01, ηp2 = 0.16, estimated marginal mean difference = 1.47%, adjusted R2 = 0.18), but no differences in endothelial function, arterial stiffness, or other cardiac function parameters.
CONCLUSION: Young adults with well-defined insomnia disorder and few confounding comorbidities demonstrated worse left ventricular strain than good sleepers. Worse left ventricular strain may reflect subtle, subclinical myocardial dysfunction that could precede changes in other cardiac function parameters or overt cardiovascular disease. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate whether this finding heralds future cardiovascular risk.
CURRENT STUDY/STUDY RATIONALE: Insomnia disorder is linked to cardiovascular disease, but this connection is rarely explored with markers of cardiac and vascular function in young adults.
STUDY IMPACT: Young adults with insomnia disorder had worse left ventricular strain, as measured by left ventricular global longitudinal strain, than well-defined good sleeping controls, suggesting early cardiac risk in patients with insomnia disorder.

Title: Management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia after 36 weeks' postmenstrual age: an evidence-informed review.
Journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
Abstract: To review available evidence in the management of established bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). We conducted a structured, domain-specific narrative review of PubMed (MEDLINE) from 2000 to 2025, including randomized trials, cohort studies, systematic reviews, and clinical guidelines in preterm infants with established BPD, with qualitative synthesis across predefined management domains. Published studies support oxygen saturation targets of 90-95% for most infants, with slightly higher targets used for those with pulmonary hypertension. Chronic-phase ventilation strategies accommodating heterogeneous lung mechanics are associated with improved synchrony and gas exchange. Diuretics provide only a transient benefit and are associated with growth and electrolyte disturbances. Systemic corticosteroids may facilitate extubation in selected infants, while inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators lack evidence for routine use. Chronic management of established BPD is supported by limited data. Current evidence for infants after 36 weeks' PMA favors careful oxygen titration, chronic-phase ventilation strategies, and selective pharmacologic therapy.

Title: Low-dose versus regular-dose paclitaxel-coated balloons for de novo coronary lesions: the ALLIANCE registry.
Abstract: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are widely used in clinical practice; however, the clinical impact of differences between DCB platforms, including paclitaxel dose, remains uncertain. This study compared the clinical efficacy and safety of low-dose (LD) versus regular-dose (RD) paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs) for de novo coronary lesions using data from the ALLIANCE registry, a prospective, multicenter, all-comers study. Patients treated with an LD-PCB (AGENT) or RD-PCB (SeQuent Please Neo) were compared using propensity score matching at a target LD-to-RD ratio of 2:1. The primary endpoint was 1-year target lesion failure (TLF), defined as a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (cd-TLR). Among 1,568 patients included in this analysis, propensity score matching yielded 784 patients in the LD-PCB group and 419 in the RD-PCB group. At 1 year, the incidence of TLF was 5.1% in the LD-PCB group and 3.8% in the RD-PCB group (p = 0.33). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed no significant between-group differences in TLF or its individual components. In this propensity score-matched registry analysis, LD-PCBs and RD-PCBs were associated with no statistically significant difference in 1-year TLF. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and do not establish equivalence between the two platforms.

Title: Body-Size Indexation of Left Atrial Volume in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: Retrospective Reclassification and E/e' Concordance.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether associations between body mass index (BMI) and left atrial (LA) size differ when LA volume is expressed as absolute volume, indexed to body surface area (BSA), or indexed to height squared, and whether discordant classification is associated with E/e' in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study linked MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-IV-ECHO. The complete-indexation cohort comprised 1663 adults with a documented heart failure diagnosis, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%, and required body-size and LA measurements. Multivariable models evaluated BMI associations with absolute LA volume, LAV/BSA, and LAV/height2. Discordance was defined as BSA-normal but height2-enlarged; adjusted E/e' was compared with the group normal by both methods.
RESULTS: BMI was positively associated with absolute LA volume (β = 0.345; 95% CI, 0.124-0.567), inversely associated with LAV/BSA (β = -0.329; 95% CI, -0.456 to -0.203), and positively associated with LAV/height2 (β = 0.156; 95% CI, 0.077-0.236). Discordant classification occurred in 389 of 1663 participants (23.4%). Adjusted E/e' was 1.630 higher (95% CI, 0.738-2.522) than in participants normal by both methods. The absolute reclassification proportion decreased to 9.6% with an alternative published height2 threshold.
CONCLUSION: Body-size normalization materially changed apparent LA enlargement in this selected HFpEF population. BSA-normal/height2-enlarged classification was associated with higher E/e', a noninvasive filling-related marker, but was threshold-dependent. These findings do not establish diagnostic superiority or prognostic benefit.

Title: Longitudinal Remodeling and Network Architecture of the Proximal Aorta in Children and Adolescents With Marfan Syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortopathy is the main cardiovascular manifestation of Marfan syndrome, but the joint evolution of the different segments of the proximal aorta during pediatric growth remains insufficiently characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate longitudinal remodeling and the interindividual and intraindividual architecture of the proximal aorta in children and adolescents with Marfan syndrome.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of data from the Pediatric Heart Network Marfan trial. Participants aged <18 years at randomization with acceptable echocardiograms obtained at baseline and at 6, 12, 24, and 36 months were included. The aortic annulus, sinuses of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, and ascending aorta were analyzed using absolute diameters and Z-scores. Partial correlation networks were estimated, separating interindividual and intraindividual components. Uncertainty was assessed using participant-level bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: A total of 515 participants were included; 445 (86.4%) had five acceptable visits. From baseline to 36 months, all absolute diameters increased, whereas Z-scores decreased (-0.688 to -0.454; all p < 0.001). Exploratory age-stratified analyses showed larger decreases among participants aged 6-11 years. The interindividual network was stronger than the intraindividual network (global strength 1.783 vs 1.020; difference 0.763; 95% CI 0.526-1.101; p < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses using inverse-probability weighting and an alternative Pediatric Heart Network Z-score system showed the same overall pattern of declining Z-scores.
CONCLUSIONS: The proximal aorta shows a multisegment architecture in which organization across patients is stronger than within-patient coordination of change. Network findings complement, but do not replace, serial measurement of individual aortic levels, and their prognostic value requires independent validation.

Title: Dapagliflozin vs. Acetazolamide in Patients With Acute Heart Failure: A Randomized Controlled Trial (CHOICE-AHF).
Abstract: Early adjunctive therapies may improve decongestion and symptoms in acute heart failure. This trial compared dapagliflozin with acetazolamide when initiated early, focusing on dyspnea relief as the primary outcome and decongestive, diuretic, natriuretic, and safety outcomes. In this randomized, active-controlled trial, 108 adults hospitalized with acute heart failure, dyspnea, and objective evidence of congestion requiring intravenous loop diuretics were randomized to receive dapagliflozin 10 mg (N = 55) or acetazolamide 500 mg (N = 53) once daily for 3 days alongside standard care. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in 72-hour dyspnea visual analog scale area under the curve. Secondary endpoints included successful decongestion within 3 days, diuretic and natriuretic responses, the relative change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels from baseline to day 3, and safety. Acetazolamide produced a significantly lower 72-hour dyspnea area under the curve than dapagliflozin (2647.9 ± 1213.8 vs. 2988.7 ± 1196.7 mm × hour; P = 0.048). It increased cumulative urine output over 72 hours (12,200 vs. 10,000 mL; P = 0.019) and total natriuresis over 48 hours (824.7 vs. 547.9 mmol; P = 0.001). Dapagliflozin achieved a larger reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide at 72 hours (-34.2% vs. -25.0%; P = 0.003). Safety events were infrequent and similar. In conclusion, acetazolamide provided greater dyspnea relief, diuresis, and natriuresis, whereas dapagliflozin produced a larger short-term reduction in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide. Further studies are needed to validate these findings. Trial registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06783166.

Title: Left Atrial Strain and Left Atrio-Ventricular Coupling in Heart Failure Patients with Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Wild-Type Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTRwt-CA) is a cardiomyopathy characterized by myocardial and atrial stiffening.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess left atrial (LA) function and left atrio-ventricular coupling index (LACI) in heart failure (HF) patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and evaluate their ability to discriminate ATTRwt-CA from non-amyloid LVH.
METHODS: We conducted a case-control study including 50 patients with ATTRwt-CA and 50 HF patients with hypertensive heart disease. LA reservoir strain (LARS), LA contraction strain (PACS), LA stiffness index (LASI), LA reservoir work (LAWr) and LACI have been measured. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for interventricular septal thickness (IVS), relative wall thickness (RWT), age, sex, coronary heart disease (CAD) to mitigate confounding.
RESULTS: Before matching,  significant differences in IVS, RWT, age, sex, and CAD rates were observed between cases and controls. After PSM, LA functional indices remained significantly impaired in CA patients compared to controls. In the multivariate analysis, only LARS and LASI were independently associated with ATTRwt-CA. A LASI > 1.57 (AUC 0.87) and a PACS  ≤  6.0% (AUC 0.79) demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for identifying ATTRwt-CA, with reduced LARS ( ≤  14.0%) also providing significant discrimination. Incorporating LASI  into the AMYLI (AUC 0.91) and IWT scores (AUC 0.89)  significantly enhances overall diagnostic accuracy for ATTRwt-CA detection.
CONCLUSION: LA function and the atrio-ventricular coupling are more impaired in ATTRwt-CA patients compared to patients with HF alone; especially LARS and LASI are independent predictor for ATTRwt-CA and should be assessed in HF patients with LVH to detect CA.

Title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve With Preserved Ejection Fraction: One-Year Changes in Ventricular and Atrial Mechanics.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) disease may precede ejection fraction (EF) decline. We assessed 1-year changes in LV global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial (LA) strain and myocardial work in BAV with preserved EF.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 82 adults with BAV and sinus rhythm who had preserved LVEF (≥50%) at two echocardiograms 363 ± 15 days apart without interim surgery; 40 age- and sex-matched controls with tricuspid aortic valves were imaged once. Primary outcomes were changes in absolute GLS and LA reservoir strain (LASr); myocardial work, corrected for the transaortic gradient in aortic stenosis, was exploratory. Reader reproducibility was tested on stored images.
RESULTS: At baseline, patients had lower absolute GLS (17.8 ± 2.8% vs. 21.8 ± 1.0%) and LASr (38.5 ± 5.2% vs. 40.8 ± 3.4%) than controls (p < 0.001 and p = 0.004). At 1 year, mean LVEF and LV volumes did not change significantly, whereas absolute GLS decreased by 0.8% points (95% CI 0.5-1.1) and LASr by 2.4 points (1.7-3.0; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Gradient-corrected global work index decreased by 47 mmHg% (27-68). The GLS decrease exceeded the intra-observer minimal detectable change in 22 patients (27%), versus an increase in 4 (5%). The GLS change was not significantly associated with valve lesion type or severity.
CONCLUSION: In selected patients with BAV who maintained preserved LVEF without valve or aortic surgery, LV GLS and LA reservoir strain decreased slightly over 1 year. Their clinical significance requires validation with longitudinal controls and test-retest data.

Title: Association Between Cholesterol-HDL-Glucose (CHG) Index and New-Onset Hypertension Across Different Sex and Glycemic Status: A Longitudinal Study With 9-Year Follow-Up.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major global public health issue, and the continuous search for new biomarkers to optimize risk stratification is crucial. This study aims to investigate the relationship between a novel metabolic disorder diagnostic tool-cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose (CHG) index-and the incidence of hypertension in populations with different sexes and glycemic statuses.
METHODS: This study utilized 9 years of follow-up data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Logistic regression models were employed to examine the association between the CHG index and new-onset hypertension across different sex and glycemic statuses. Additionally, the net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement indices were calculated to estimate the additional predictive value beyond the basic model.
RESULTS: A total of 6555 participants were included in the study. A significant association between CHG index and new-onset hypertension was observed in the total, male, female, prediabetic, and diabetic populations, with adjusted OR (95% CI) of 1.16 (1.10-1.24), 1.23 (1.12-1.36), 1.12 (1.02-1.22), 1.14 (1.01-1.29), and 1.19 (1.03-1.36) respectively. Restricted Cubic Spline (RCS) analysis revealed a positive linear relationship between the CHG index and new-onset hypertension. The addition of either the CHG index or the Triglyceride-Glucose (TyG) index significantly improved the predictive performance of the basic model for hypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: An elevated CHG index is significantly associated with new-onset hypertension.

Title: Can artificial intelligence add diagnostic value for human readers in detecting coronary artery stenosis on coronary CT angiography? A Bayesian network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: The incremental diagnostic value of artificial intelligence (AI) in coronary CT angiography (CCTA) remains uncertain. We compared five CCTA strategies: automated stenosis assessment software (COR Analyzer), stand-alone CCTA-based deep learning (DL), junior readers, senior readers, and AI-assisted readers, for detecting anatomical coronary artery stenosis against invasive coronary angiography.
METHODS AND RESULTS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through July 9, 2026. Twenty-two observational diagnostic accuracy studies were included (19 retrospective and three prospective; 21 for ≥50% stenosis and six for ≥70% stenosis). In the primary patient-level analysis at ≥50% stenosis, pooled sensitivity for DL and AI-assisted readers was 0.91 each (95% credible interval, 0.87 to 0.94 and 0.86 to 0.94), versus 0.80 (0.73-0.87) for junior and 0.87 (0.82-0.91) for senior readers; AI assistance increased sensitivity by 0.10 versus junior readers (0.06-0.15) and 0.03 versus senior readers (0.01-0.06). Specificity was similar across DL and reader strategies (0.64-0.67) but markedly lower for COR Analyzer (0.25 [0.15 to 0.38]). In the smaller ≥70% network, AI-assisted reading showed the highest estimated sensitivity (0.80 [0.70 to 0.88]). Findings were robust to outlier exclusion; certainty was low to very low for most ≥50% outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Stand-alone DL and AI-assisted reading had similar estimated diagnostic performance. AI assistance improved sensitivity most clearly for less-experienced readers. These accuracy comparisons did not establish formal equivalence or determine whether stand-alone DL could replace human interpretation in clinical practice.

Title: Dose-Exposure-Response Analysis of Finerenone on Serum Potassium and Cardiovascular Outcomes Among Patients With Heart Failure: Insights From FINEARTS-HF.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Finerenone reduces the risk of heart failure and cardiovascular (CV) death among patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF). Whether the effects of finerenone to reduce CV risk are dose/exposure dependent is not clear.
METHODS: In FINEARTS-HF, 6001 participants were randomized to finerenone or placebo, where the initial and target dose of finerenone was titrated according to the baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR; 10- > 20 mg if baseline eGFR ≤ 60; 20- > 40 mg if > 60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and by serum potassium and changes in eGFR during the trial. We fitted non-linear mixed-effects population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic and parametric repeated time-to-event models to explore the effect of finerenone dose on exposure (n = 6658 plasma concentration measurements) and exposure on serum potassium (n = 123 720 measurements), NT-proBNP (n = 16 971 measurements) and the primary composite outcome of total heart failure events and CV death (n = 2366 events).
RESULTS: The mean eGFR in those with an initial dose of 10 mg and 20 mg was 46 ± 12 and 76 ± 14 mL/min/1.73 m2, respectively. The frequency of hyperkalemia (> 5.5 mmol/L) was 4.3% in patients taking 10 mg finerenone, 2.7% among those taking 20 mg and 1.5% among those taking 40 mg. Simulated PK/PD data produced higher serum potassium with higher finerenone exposure in a hypothetical scenario without dose titration; however, when simulating the protocol-guided dose titration strategy implemented in the trial, the lower observed frequency of hyperkalemia at higher finerenone exposure was explained. For the efficacy exposure-response analyses, while higher finerenone exposure was non-significantly related to a lower frequency of CV composite events (p = 0.55), higher exposure did result in a significantly greater reduction in NT-proBNP concentrations (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among participants of FINEARTS-HF, finerenone dose titration was effective in managing serum potassium concentration. Although FINEARTS-HF was not designed to test a randomized comparison of dose or exposure, the PK/PD model suggests that higher achieved exposure is associated with improved CV efficacy.

Title: Catastrophic fetal-neonatal thrombosis: a thromboinflammatory concept and the role of antiphospholipid antibodies.
Journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fetal and neonatal thrombosis comprises a heterogeneous spectrum of disorders ranging from localized vascular events to rapidly progressive systemic thrombosis involving multiple vascular beds and organs. This review examines thromboinflammation and antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) in severe fetal-neonatal thrombosis.
METHODS: This narrative, hypothesis-generating review draws on a structured, non-systematic literature search through August 31, 2026, distinguishing direct fetal and neonatal evidence from adult and experimental findings.
RESULTS: Neonatal hemostasis is characterized by a physiologically balanced but vulnerable state that may become destabilized by infection, hypoxia, endothelial injury, inflammation, and genetic or immune-mediated factors. Current evidence suggests that interactions between endothelial dysfunction, innate immune activation, platelets, coagulation, neutrophil extracellular traps, and the complement system may promote a transition from localized thrombosis to a self-amplifying thromboinflammatory process. However, a common mechanism of such progression has not been established across different fetal and neonatal thrombotic disorders. Maternal IgG aPL may cross the placenta, whereas aPL detected in some neonates may reflect presumed de novo production. The presence of aPL does not necessarily result in neonatal thrombosis, and additional prothrombotic factors reported in selected cases are consistent with, but do not establish, a "second-hit" or "multiple-hit" model.
CONCLUSION: We propose catastrophic fetal-neonatal thrombosis as an unvalidated clinical and pathogenetic framework rather than a distinct disease entity. Paired maternal-neonatal testing and longitudinal antibody assessment may help clarify antibody origin, although delayed testing limits causal interpretation. Its potential value for earlier recognition and etiologically directed diagnostic evaluation requires prospective assessment.

Title: Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Pulmonary Embolism.
Abstract: This article highlights the limitations of thrombolysis in high-risk pulmonary embolism and the emerging role of temporary mechanical circulatory support, especially venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, as a bridge to recovery or definitive therapy. The pathophysiology of right ventricular failure in pulmonary embolism, risk stratification strategies, and decision-making frameworks for initiating mechanical circulatory support are reviewed. Further, we cover practical considerations, including device selection, circuit management during thrombectomy, and the imperative for preanesthesia planning in risk mitigation. Finally, this article highlights the importance of conducting prospective and randomized studies on device choice, timing, and integration with reperfusion strategies.

Title: Clot in Transit.
Abstract: Clot in transit, defined as a mobile right heart thrombus, is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of venous thromboembolism. Its presence in acute pulmonary embolism is associated with high mortality and hemodynamic instability. Diagnosis relies primarily on echocardiography, with adjunctive roles for computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance. Management remains challenging due to the absence of randomized trials. Treatment options include anticoagulation alone, systemic thrombolysis, surgical embolectomy, and catheter-based interventions, with outcomes favoring active reperfusion in unstable patients. Multidisciplinary decision-making is essential, and ongoing research aims to clarify optimal strategies to improve survival in this high-risk population.

Title: Catheter-directed Treatment of Pulmonary Embolism.
Abstract: Catheter-directed therapies, including catheter-directed thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy, are increasingly used in patients with intermediate and high-risk pulmonary embolism. Complications, such as bleeding, vascular injury, and hemodynamic instability, require diligent preprocedural planning involving bailout strategies and the potential for extracorporeal support. We provide a pragmatic framework for appropriate patient selection of catheter-directed treatment. Although randomized data remain limited, ongoing pivotal trials will help clarify appropriate patient selection and clinical efficacy compared to anticoagulation and systemic thrombolysis alone.

Title: Positive Airway Pressure Therapy: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve Adherence and Outcomes?
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in medicine, with growing evidence supporting its role in screening, phenotyping, risk stratification, and personalized treatment. In sleep medicine, AI shows significant potential in the management of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). While algorithm-based support for continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) use is not new, AI-driven personalized approaches aimed at improving adherence, patient satisfaction, and OSA-related outcomes are still emerging. Observational studies suggest promising applications of AI in CPAP management; however, independent randomized trials are needed to validate these approaches and determine their impact on neurologic, cardiovascular, and metabolic outcomes compared with traditional methods.

Title: Evolving indications for metabolic and bariatric surgery.
Abstract: This chapter addresses patient selection for metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) in the modern obesity care landscape, where anti-obesity medications (AOMs) such as semaglutide and tirzepatide have changed the clinical decision-making framework. We organize the evidence around four questions a clinician actually asks: who qualifies under current guidelines, who benefits most and from which procedure, who is poorly served by surgery, and when pharmacotherapy is the better answer. We review the evolution of indications from the 1991 NIH Consensus Conference through the 2022 ASMBS/IFSO joint guidelines, with attention to the randomized evidence supporting expanded indications at BMI 30-34.9 kg/m² with type 2 diabetes. We then examine outcomes by patient phenotype, including type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, obstructive sleep apnea, heart failure, transplant candidacy, polycystic ovary syndrome, pregnancy planning, and elevated cancer risk. We identify populations for whom surgery carries an unfavorable risk-benefit profile, including patients with advanced perioperative risk, decompensated cirrhosis, untreated psychiatric illness, active substance use, or inability to maintain long-term nutritional follow-up. Finally, we provide a comparative analysis of MBS and modern AOMs across cardiometabolic outcomes, with attention to the methodological limitations of current cohort comparisons and the role of combination and sequential strategies. The chapter concludes that the two modalities are converging on a complementary framework in which patient phenotype, not BMI alone, determines the right intervention.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and an aggressive coronary disease phenotype: Association with multivessel disease and recurrent coronary events in the CERES study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established genetically determined risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Whether elevated Lp(a) identifies a broader phenotype of aggressive coronary disease, integrating anatomical disease burden and recurrent clinical manifestations, remains incompletely characterised.
METHODS: We analysed 1892 patients with coronary artery disease from the multicentre CERES cohort after exclusion of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). Lp(a) was analysed continuously, after natural-log transformation, and categorically using >50 mg/dL. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, and historical maximum LDL cholesterol (LDL-C).
RESULTS: Lp(a) was available in 1833 patients; median concentration was 24.7 [9.1-63.7] mg/dL, and 33.2% had Lp(a) >50 mg/dL. Multivessel disease was present in 50.4% and recurrent coronary events in 19.5%. Lp(a) was independently associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.002) and recurrent coronary events (OR, 1.004; 95% CI, 1.001-1.006; p = 0.003). Lp(a) >50 mg/dL was associated with multivessel disease (OR, 1.406; 95% CI, 1.144-1.730; p = 0.001) and recurrent events (OR, 1.504; 95% CI, 1.166-1.942; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with greater anatomical coronary disease burden and recurrent coronary events, supporting its role as a marker of an aggressive coronary disease phenotype.

Title: Early and six-month ventricular remodeling after aortic valve surgery for aortic regurgitation: Predictive value of preoperative static exercise cardiovascular magnetic resonance. A prospective pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Little is known about the timing and trajectory of reverse remodeling after aortic valve surgery (AVS) in severe aortic regurgitation (AR), and better predictors of postoperative ventricular function are needed. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) with static exercise (SE) testing may help anticipate the ventricular response to AVS, but its predictive value has not been established.
METHODS: In this prospective pilot study, 20 patients with severe AR referred for AVS underwent CMR, including assessment during SE, with follow-up CMR at 14 days and 6 months. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) characterized the time course of each parameter, decomposing the time effect into linear and quadratic components.
RESULTS: Left ventricular (LV) end-diastolic volume decreased progressively, mainly following a linear pattern (η2 0.795), with most of the reduction by 14 days. LV end-systolic volume declined continuously through 6 months (linear component only, η2 0.711). LV ejection fraction (LVEF) described a V-shaped curve, falling at 14 days before recovering above baseline by 6 months (quadratic component predominant, η2 0.358). Right ventricular parameters remained stable. SE-induced changes mirrored the early postoperative response and correlated strongly with 14-day LVEF (r up to 0.87), with good agreement between SE-LVEF and 14-day LVEF (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] 0.76-0.86); no baseline or SE parameter predicted LVEF at 6 months.
CONCLUSIONS: AVS for severe AR induces early, heterogeneous LV reverse remodeling, with an initial LVEF dip followed by recovery by 6 months. Preoperative CMR with SE reproduces the early postoperative hemodynamic response and predicts short-term but not mid-term ventricular recovery.

Title: Transcarotid Artery Stenting Using Flow Reversal for Non-Atherosclerotic Carotid Artery Disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the use of transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) in non-atherosclerotic carotid disease and compared outcomes with transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS).
METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for all TCAR and TFCAS procedures performed from 2017-2024. Patients with lesion types categorized as atherosclerosis or restenosis were excluded. The study cohort included dissection, trauma, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), and other non-atherosclerotic etiologies. Primary outcomes included major adverse events, including stroke, death, and composite endpoints. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.
RESULTS: A total of 541 TCAR and 2,348 TFCAS patients met inclusion criteria. TCAR was associated with lower contrast usage and fluoroscopy time across all lesion types. In unadjusted analyses, stroke or death rates were higher with TFCAS than TCAR for dissection (7.1% vs 1.9%, p=0.006), other lesions (8.7% vs 2.1%, p<0.001), and symptomatic (8.1% vs 2.2%, p=0.001) and asymptomatic patients (6.4% vs 1.6%, p<0.001). After propensity matching (527 pairs), TCAR was associated with significantly lower rates of stroke (4.4% vs 1.7%, p=0.0118), death (4.4% vs 0.4%, p<0.001), stroke or death (7.6% vs 1.9%, p<0.001), and stroke, death, or MI (8.0% vs 2.7%, p<0.001) compared with TFCAS (TFCAS vs TCAR, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: This study supports consideration of TCAR for non-atherosclerotic carotid pathology when carotid stenting is indicated and suggests that TCAR may offer important advantages over TFCAS, particularly in reducing the risk of perioperative stroke or death.

Title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile.
METHODS: Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context.
RESULTS: Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

Title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral valve regurgitation: insights from a 5-year prospective multicenter registry.
Abstract: Long-term data on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for significant mitral regurgitation (MR) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes and functional and echocardiographic findings during follow-up after MitraClip in a long-term subanalysis of the prospective multicenter GIOTTO registry. We included 406 consecutive patients undergoing MitraClip implantation for significant MR from 6 Italian centers contributing long-term follow-up. Baseline, procedural, in-hospital, and long-term follow-up data were compared according to MR etiology. Predictors of all-cause death were assessed using Cox regression analysis. Mean follow-up was 56.4±27.2 months. The cohort included 257 (63.3%) patients with functional or mixed MR and 149 (36.7%) with degenerative MR, who were older, more often female, and had smaller ventricles and higher LVEF, whereas functional or mixed MR patients had greater ischemic burden, conduction disease, prior revascularization, pacemaker implantation, and ventricular remodeling. During the overall observation period, crude all-cause death occurred in 161 patients (39.7%) and MVARC-style cardiovascular death in 98 (24.1%), without significant differences between groups. Mitral surgery, repeat TEER, endocarditis, and stroke occurred in 2.2%, 0.7%, 1.5%, and 3.5%, respectively. Among patients with available follow-up assessment, 77.5% were in NYHA class I/II. At the actual 5-year landmark echocardiographic assessment, 82.9% had none or mild MR and 97.1% had no more than moderate MR.
