Independent mortality predictors were older age, lower body mass index, right bundle branch block, MR etiology, larger LV end-systolic diameter, higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure, and longer index hospitalization (all p <0.05). In conclusion, in this prospective multicenter cohort, TEER with MitraClip in high-risk patients was associated with high procedural success and favorable long-term clinical and echocardiographic findings among patients with available follow-up. Mortality appeared to be associated with patient vulnerability, MR etiology, ventricular remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, and the early post-procedural course.

Title: Polygenic susceptibility modifies the association between long-term physical activity patterns and major adverse cardiovascular events: Insights from a target trial emulation study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Physical activity is a key modifiable lifestyle factor for cardiovascular prevention. However, precise prevention strategies regarding long-term physical activity are lacking, particularly concerning whether genetic susceptibility modifies the association between long-term physical activity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Most previous cohort studies rely on a single assessment of physical activity, which may not capture long-term behavior. To address these gaps, we used repeated assessments and a target trial emulation framework in UK Biobank.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We studied 27,459 UK Biobank participants with repeat physical activity assessments. A target trial emulation framework defined eligibility, time zero, exposure groups, and follow-up. The prespecified primary contrast compared increased physical activity with sustained low activity after 1:1 propensity score matching. Secondary full-cohort models examined four physical activity change patterns. Cardiovascular polygenic risk strata were evaluated exploratorily.
KEY FINDINGS: In 4401 matched pairs, increased physical activity was not significantly associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) compared with sustained low activity (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.90-1.58). In full-cohort models, sustained high physical activity was associated with higher MACE risk (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.03-1.56). This signal was more apparent among participants with intermediate or high cardiovascular polygenic risk.
SIGNIFICANCE: In this UK Biobank target trial emulation, increasing physical activity from low levels did not clearly reduce MACE, whereas sustained high activity showed an unexpected higher-risk signal, particularly among genetically susceptible participants. These findings support the potential value of genetic risk assessment in cardiovascular risk evaluation for highly active individuals and provide new evidence for precision exercise prescriptions.

Title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).
FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.
INTERPRETATION: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.
FUNDING: The CardioVascular Research Foundation (South Korea).

Title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality.
METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods.
FINDINGS: Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality.
INTERPRETATION: Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency.
FUNDING: Mayo Clinic.

Title: Clinical Diagnosis Versus Plain Radiography for Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Prospective Study of Diagnostic Agreement in a Resource-Limited Settings.
Abstract: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers, particularly in advanced infections. In low-resource settings, access to medical imaging may be limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic agreement between a composite clinical approach (clinical assessment plus probe-to-bone test) compared with plain radiography for diagnosing DFO, including performance across ulcer categories. A prospective cohort study was conducted from December 2021 to January 2025 among patients with suspected DFO. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, risk factor assessment, ulcer history, SINBAD classification, probe-to-bone testing and plain radiography. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated. Given the absence of a gold standard reference test (bone biopsy) in this low-resource setting, performance measures represent comparative diagnostic agreement with plain radiography rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. A total of 166 patients with deep foot ulcers were enrolled. Composite clinical diagnosis identified osteomyelitis in 117 patients and excluded it in 49. Plain radiography was positive in 96 of 117 composite positive cases, while 21 were discordant; all 49 composite negative cases were radiographically negative. The composite approach showed 100% sensitivity, 70% specificity and 87.3% overall agreement. Sensitivity remained 100% across ulcer categories, while specificity increased significantly from 63.8% in SINBAD-4 ulcers to 77.8% in SINBAD-5 ulcers, improving agreement from 86.1% to 89.7%. In conclusion, composite clinical diagnosis demonstrates substantial agreement with plain radiography in this cohort of patients with suspected DFO. This can provide a practical adjunct for clinical assessment in resource-limited settings where imaging is unavailable or difficult to interpret but should not be considered a definitive diagnostic test in the absence of an independent reference standard.

Title: Clinical value of a five-predictor nomogram for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after orthopaedic surgery in ICU patients.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the predictive value of a five-predictor nomogram for postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in orthopedic patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).MethodsClinical data from 224 postoperative orthopedic ICU patients admitted between March 2022 and March 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into a DVT group (n = 73) and a non-DVT group (n = 151). Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors, and a predictive nomogram was constructed based on these variables. The performance of the model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.ResultsThe incidence of postoperative DVT was 32.59%. Patients in the DVT group had significantly higher age, D-dimer, prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), and a higher prevalence of diabetes, preoperative heart failure, and postoperative infection compared with the non-DVT group (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified age, diabetes, preoperative heart failure, PT, and APTT as independent risk factors for DVT. The nomogram demonstrated good predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.877. The sensitivity and specificity were 82.47% and 76.68%, respectively.ConclusionThe five-predictor nomogram provides individualized estimates of postoperative DVT probability in orthopedic ICU patients and may support risk stratification and targeted prevention.

Title: Diffuse adverse coronary hemodynamics associated with type 2 diabetes: A CCTA-CFD phenotyping study.
Abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) have a disproportionately high risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, which is not fully explained by the degree of coronary stenosis alone. In this retrospective study, patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models were reconstructed from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) data obtained from 53 individuals (26 non-T2DM and 27 T2DM). Time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), and relative residence time (RRT) were calculated to characterize the hemodynamic environment. Plaque composition and cardiac chamber dimensions were also analyzed. Results show patients with T2DM had significantly greater proportions of coronary surface area meeting the prespecified criteria for low TAWSS, high OSI, and high RRT than patients without T2DM (all P < 0.05) despite similar percent diameter stenosis. In plaque-level mixed-effects analyses accounting for within-patient clustering and clinical covariates, T2DM remained associated with lower TAWSS across all plaques (all P < 0.05). In plaque-type-stratified analyses, the most consistent adjusted differences were observed in non-calcified plaques. Longer diabetes duration was significantly associated with higher RRT (β = 0.0738, 95% CI: 0.0153 to 0.1324, P = 0.0135). These findings suggest that under standardized CCTA-CFD modeling assumptions, T2DM was associated with a greater patient-level burden of adverse simulated coronary hemodynamic regions. Plaque-level associations varied according to plaque composition and remained most evident in non-calcified plaques after multivariable adjustment. These findings suggest that CFD-derived hemodynamic assessment may provide information complementary to conventional anatomical measurements.

Title: Stellate ganglion block in contemporary anesthesia practice: perioperative applications, emerging indications, and risk management.
Abstract: Stellate ganglion block (SGB), an interventional technique that modulates sympathetic activity, has been increasingly investigated beyond traditional pain management in cardiology, neuropsychiatry, and perioperative medicine. This narrative review examines the evolving role of SGB in contemporary anesthesia practice, emphasizing that its effects may extend beyond immediate peripheral sympatholysis to longer-lasting central neural modulation. Technically, ultrasound guidance facilitates precise needle placement and low-volume injection, with improved visualization of relevant anatomy and injectate spread. Dose-finding studies have refined local-anesthetic volume and concentration, whereas continuous blockade may extend sympatholysis in selected refractory conditions. Clinically, SGB has been used in selected pain conditions, including complex regional pain syndrome and herpes zoster-related pain, and has been investigated for non-pain indications such as post-traumatic stress disorder, refractory ventricular arrhythmias, and menopausal vasomotor symptoms. In perioperative settings, SGB has been evaluated for postoperative analgesia, modulation of inflammatory responses, and potential neuroprotective effects. Risk mitigation relies on real-time ultrasound visualization of the needle tip, adjacent vascular structures, and injectate spread, together with predefined management protocols for major complications. Future research should prioritize multicenter prospective studies, standardized procedural parameters, and individualized treatment pathways to support the safe, precise, and evidence-based use of SGB across clinical settings.

Title: Clinical outcomes and coronary complication risk after transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with cardioband: a 12-month single-center cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system in a single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation.
METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort study included 64 consecutive patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation undergoing transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty with the Cardioband system. Clinical and echocardiographic data were collected at baseline, discharge, 6-months, and 12-months. Primary endpoints included changes in tricuspid regurgitation severity, annular dimensions, and clinical status, as well as all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Outcomes were analyzed using available-case data.
RESULTS: At 12-months, among patients with available echocardiographic data (n = 44), tricuspid regurgitation severity was reduced compared with baseline (p < 0.001); 15.9% had trace or mild TR, 45.5% had moderate TR, 27.3% had severe TR, and 11.4% had massive or torrential TR. All-cause mortality at 12-months was 6.3% (4/64 patients). According to TVARC criteria, intraprocedural success was achieved in 81.3% of patients, while a more stringent definition yielded a success rate of 65.6%.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort of high-risk patients with severe functional tricuspid regurgitation, transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty using the Cardioband system was associated with reductions in tricuspid regurgitation severity and improvements in selected clinical parameters at 12-months. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution given the observational design, incomplete follow-up, and the absence of a control group, as well as the observed rate of procedural complications. Further studies, ideally including larger multicenter cohorts and controlled comparisons, are needed to better define the role of this therapy in the management of tricuspid regurgitation.

Title: Preoperative lipid concentrations and 28-day mortality after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low cholesterol is associated with poor outcomes in acute illness, although low LDL-Cholesterol (LDL-C) is a therapeutic target in cardiovascular disease. We assessed whether preoperative lipid concentrations were associated with 28-day mortality after cardiac surgery with Cardiopulmonary Bypass (CPB).
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed a prospectively maintained single-centre registry of cardiac surgery with CPB (April 2013-December 2023), linked to preoperative lipid measurements and national death records. LDL-C was the primary exposure. Models were adjusted for EuroSCORE 2, statin use, infective endocarditis, urgent surgery, and critical preoperative state. Secondary analyses were corrected for multiplicity (Benjamini-Hochberg).
RESULTS: Of 10,088 patients, 71 were excluded (reoperation within one year or duplicate record) and 1,986 of the remaining 10,017 had a preoperative lipid panel; 64 (3.2%) died within 28-days. In unadjusted analyses, lower Total Cholesterol (TC), HDL-C and LDL-C were associated with mortality. After adjustment, LDL-C was no longer associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio = 0.803, 95% CI 0.595-1.084; p = 0.152). TC retained a borderline association (0.777, 0.607-0.994; p = 0.045), not surviving correction (q = 0.173). Lipid parameters discriminated poorly (areas under the curve 0.57-0.62) and added nothing to EuroSCORE 2.
CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment for illness severity, preoperative LDL-C was not associated with 28-day mortality, and lipids provided no prognostic information beyond EuroSCORE 2. Very low TC may primarily reflect illness severity rather than an independent causal risk factor, and these data provide no basis for modifying perioperative lipid-lowering therapy.

Title: The healthcare cost of multimorbidity in older patients with atrial fibrillation: A retrospective cohort study in an Italian local health unit.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults often coexists with comorbidities, increasing healthcare costs. Understanding the economic impact of different comorbidity patterns is essential for optimising care and resource allocation.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the economic burden of older adults with AF based on the number of comorbidities and multimorbidity classes, using data from an Italian hospital-based cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 4602 patients aged ≥65 years with AF, residing in a Local Health Authority of Veneto Region (Italy). Comorbidities were identified using the Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) System. Multimorbidity classes were derived through Latent Class Analysis. Total healthcare and pharmaceutical costs were estimated using ACG-based predictive models, stratified by comorbidity count and multimorbidity class.
RESULTS: Among AF patients (median age 82; 53.7% female), 98% had at least two additional comorbidities. Annual estimated healthcare costs rose from €1049 for AF only to €21,746 for patients with ≥14 comorbidities. Seven multimorbidity classes emerged: Respiratory, Gastro-intestinal, Neurological, Multisystem, Cardio-metabolic, Dementia and Functional Impairment, and Mild Comorbidity. Mean total costs ranged from €5721 (Mild) to €17,338 (Multisystem). Multisystem, Dementia (€15,107), and Neurological (€13,943) classes had the highest costs. Pharmaceutical costs were highest in Respiratory (€1780) and Multisystem (€1769) classes.
CONCLUSIONS: We present a novel approach to understanding the heterogeneity of comorbidity patterns and their costs in the AF population. Tailored, multidisciplinary care strategies considering comorbidity profiles may improve care quality and optimise resource use. Prevention should address cumulative cost burden of AF and associated comorbidities.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.
INTERVENTION: Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.
RESULTS: Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07477002.

Title: Integrating Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Score with NIHSS for Improved Prognostic Evaluation in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: AimTo investigate whether the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) heat syndrome score (HSS), alone or in interaction with the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), provides additional prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes in patients with large-artery atherosclerotic acute ischemic stroke (AIS).MethodsA total of 149 patients with large-artery atherosclerotic AIS admitted to Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, between December 2017 and December 2023 were retrospectively included. Demographic characteristics, medical history, laboratory parameters, clinical scores, and inflammatory indices, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), were collected or calculated. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with poor 90-day functional outcome (mRS ≥3). An interaction term (NH), defined as the product of mean-centered NIHSS and HSS, was evaluated in the prognostic model. Firth penalized logistic regression, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, ROC analysis, bootstrap internal validation, and restricted cubic spline analysis were additionally performed.ResultsAmong 149 patients, 55 (36.9%) had a poor functional outcome at 90 days. HSS alone was not independently associated with poor outcome, whereas lnNLR remained independently associated with outcome after multivariable adjustment. NH was significantly associated with poor functional outcome in the primary model (OR = 1.072, P = 0.005), and the association remained robust in Firth penalized regression and sensitivity analyses. Adding NH to the Base model resulted in a modest numerical increase in discrimination (AUC = 0.795 vs. 0.760), although the difference was not statistically significant by DeLong's test (P = 0.098). Exploratory mediation analysis provided no evidence that C-reactive protein (CRP) mediated the association between NH and poor functional outcome.ConclusionThe interaction between NIHSS and HSS was associated with 90-day functional outcome in patients with large-artery atherosclerotic AIS and may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional clinical factors. However, its incremental predictive value was modest and requires confirmation in larger independent external validation cohorts before clinical implementation.

Title: Transcutaneous Pacing in the Prehospital Setting - A Retrospective Cohort Study of Electrical Capture.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transcutaneous pacing (TCP) treats hemodynamically unstable bradycardia refractory to pharmacologic management. Effective TCP requires electrical and mechanical capture to augment perfusion. Little is known about prehospital TCP and capture incidence.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients treated with prehospital TCP by an emergency medical services agency between 2017 and 2024. Continuous ECG recordings from cardiac monitors were reviewed. Electrical capture was the primary outcome, defined as a widened QRS with a distinct T wave following a TCP spike. Secondary measures included capture duration, clinician-verbalized pulse during pacing, plethysmograph waveform alignment, and changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse oximetry, and end-tidal carbon dioxide.
RESULTS: Fifty-six patients received attempted TCP. Median age was 70 years (interquartile range [IQR] 58-85), and 34% were female. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was administered in 59% of patients. Electrical capture was achieved in 18 patients (32%). Among patients who achieved electrical capture, complete capture occurred a mean of 27.2% (standard deviation 30.5%) of attempted pacing duration. The median SBP change was +22.0 (IQR: -2-82) mmHg in patients with electrical capture and 0.0 (IQR: -29-7) mmHg in those with only rare-to-absent capture (p = 0.031). During TCP, clinicians verbalized a palpable pulse 26 times across 19 patients. Only 4 instances (15%) coincided with electrical capture.
CONCLUSIONS: Electrical capture during prehospital TCP occurred in a minority of patients and was often intermittent. Prehospital identification of mechanical capture using routine clinical indicators was difficult and unreliable. Future work should standardize capture definitions and physiologic measurements to determine when TCP produces clinically meaningful perfusion.

Title: Risk of cardiovascular events and mortality associated with LDL and non-HDL cholesterol levels after statin initiation for primary prevention: A multiregional cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular and mortality benefits of achieving guideline-recommended concentrations of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and non-high-density lipoprotein (non-HDL) cholesterol with statins in primary prevention remain uncertain.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: In this new-user cohort study, we used electronic healthcare databases from Hong Kong (HK), New Zealand (NZ) and the United Kingdom (UK) to identify 185,237 patients initiating statins between 1 January 2007 and 31 December 2012 (with follow-up to 31 December 2017) without atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease. Associations between LDL and non-HDL cholesterol measured within 2 years post-initiation with the outcomes of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) or all-cause mortality were assessed in landmark analyses using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia, obesity, smoking, alcohol misuse, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and connective tissue disorders, severe mental illness, antihypertensive drugs, antidiabetic drugs, antiplatelet drugs, and anticoagulant drugs. Estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. At 2 years, LDL cholesterol was <1.4 mmol/L in 7,084 (3.8%), 1.4-1.7 mmol/L in 21,893 (11.8%), 1.8-2.5 mmol/L in 81,941 (44.2%) and ≥2.6 mmol/L in 74,294 (40.1%) patients. Mean duration of follow-up for the primary outcome of MACE was 6.5 years in HK, 5.6 years in NZ and 5.4 years in UK. versus an LDL cholesterol ≥2.6 mmol/L, adjusted hazard ratios (HR) for MACE were 0.80 (95% CI [0.77,0.83]) for 1.8-2.5 mmol/L, 0.79 (0.66,0.94) for 1.4-1.7 mmol/L and 0.82 (0.60,1.12) for <1.4 mmol/L. Non-HDL cholesterol showed similar estimates for MACE (e.g., HR 0.75, [0.72,0.79] for 2.6-3.3 mmol/L versus ≥3.4 mmol/L). In continuous analysis, the association with MACE was approximately log-linear across achieved LDL and non-HDL cholesterol in HK and the UK, whereas in NZ estimates were less consistent and imprecise at the lowest concentrations. After adjustment for confounding factors, very low LDL (HR 1.06, [0.96,1.16]) and non-HDL cholesterol (HR 0.98, [0.84,1.14]) were not associated with all-cause mortality. Limitations include heterogeneity across cohorts, which may reflect confounding by indication where treatment intensity was guided by cardiovascular risk, and residual confounding from comorbidities, lifestyle interventions and disease severity. Estimates are also conditional on patients having initiated statins, survived to the landmark, and undergone follow-up lipid testing.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower achieved LDL and non-HDL cholesterol after statin initiation was associated with a reduction in MACE, with limited evidence of an increase in all-cause mortality at very low concentrations after adjustment for confounding. Additional reductions in cardiovascular events could be obtained by achieving guideline-recommended non-HDL cholesterol levels of at least <3.4 mmol/L after statin initiation for primary prevention.

Title: BAG3 genetic variant is associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction phenotypes.
Abstract: Genetic variations are involved in determining heart failure (HF) phenotypes. While variants within the BAG3 gene have been associated with HF in European populations, the impact of specific single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the BAG3 gene in determining phenotypes of HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in Southeast Asian populations is unknown. Therefore, in this study, we identified BAG3 SNPs and investigated their biological and clinical relevance in determining HFpEF phenotypes among an Indonesian HFpEF cohort. We conducted a study involving 36 patients with HFpEF and 30 healthy individuals. We detected the presence of rs196326 and rs2240777 SNPs in our cohort. However, the rs2234962 polymorphism, which has been associated with HF and cardiomyopathy in Western populations, was absent in our Indonesian cohort. We found that the rs196326 SNP was significantly associated with relative wall thickness (RWT), with patients carrying the CG genotype displayed significantly lower RWT. Additionally, the rs196326 CG/GG genotypes were correlated with higher serum N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and lower Caspase-3 levels. Our study showed that the BAG3 rs196326 polymorphism was significantly associated with HFpEF phenotypes in the Indonesian population. This highlights the importance of identifying population-specific as genetic markers of disease severity.

Title: Effects of Dialysis Room Noise Exposure on Plasma Renin Activity, Angiotensin II, and Blood Pressure Fluctuations in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of environmental dialysis room noise exposure on plasma renin activity (PRA), angiotensin II (Ang II) levels, and blood pressure fluctuations in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 100 patients receiving MHD at Cixi People's Hospital, Wenzhou Medical University, between May 2020 and November 2022. According to the average noise level of their dialysis shifts, patients were divided into a high-exposure group (>55 dB(A)) and a low-exposure group (≤55 dB(A)), with 50 cases each. Repeated-measures analysis of variance and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: At 3 and 6 months, the high-exposure group had significantly higher PRA and Ang II levels, greater systolic and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) fluctuation ranges, and a higher incidence of intradialytic hypertension compared with those in the low-exposure group (all P < 0.05). Multivariable linear regression showed that noise exposure level was independently positively associated with PRA ( β  = 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.41-0.86), Ang II ( β  = 13.35, 95% CI: 9.10-17.59), systolic blood pressure fluctuation range ( β  = 7.03, 95% CI: 5.06-9.01), and DBP fluctuation range ( β  = 3.49, 95% CI: 2.24-4.74), all P < 0.001.
CONCLUSION: Higher dialysis room noise exposure was associated with activation of the renin-angiotensin system, increased blood pressure fluctuations, and higher risk of intradialytic hypertension. Optimizing the acoustic environment may improve hemodynamic stability in patients undergoing MHD.

Title: Nonauditory Effects of Infrasound and Low-Frequency Noise in Humans: A Systematic Literature Review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to assess the quality of evidence across studies on the nonauditory effects of infrasound (IS) and low-frequency noise (LFN) in adults, investigating physiological and psychological outcomes associated with such exposures.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Studies were searched in eight databases from their earliest records up to March 2026. Outcomes assessed included annoyance and noise sensitivity, sleep disturbances, cardiovascular diseases, cognitive and mental health impairments, and other health-related disturbances. The quality of evidence for each outcome was assessed using an adapted Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.
RESULTS: The review included 39 papers, predominantly cross-sectional designs (laboratory-based and real-life), with fewer cohort studies and only three randomized controlled trials. Exposure scenarios varied widely, encompassing wind turbine noise, traffic and community noise, occupational noise, and experimentally generated IS and/or LFN stimuli. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate for annoyance/sensitivity to very low for sleep disturbance, cardiovascular outcomes, cognitive performance, mental health, and general health disturbances. These ratings were influenced by the predominance of cross-sectional studies, high overall risk of bias, methodological heterogeneity, inconsistent findings, and indirectness across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: The findings showed that annoyance and sensitivity were the only outcomes associated with exposure to IS/LFN, supported by moderate-quality evidence, suggesting that these subjective responses should be included in health impact assessments. For all other outcomes, the certainty of the evidence remains very low, highlighting the urgent need for well-designed longitudinal and experimental studies.

Title: Choosing Between On-Pump and Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Contemporary Evidence for Patient Selection and Clinical Decision-Making.
Abstract: On-pump (ONCAB) and off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) remain established approaches to surgical myocardial revascularization, but contemporary evidence does not support a universal preference for either technique. The clinically relevant question is which patient and operative setting are most likely to benefit from each strategy. We performed a contemporary narrative evidence synthesis of landmark randomized trials, long-term follow-up studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, observational cohorts, graft-patency studies, and major coronary revascularization guidelines. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched for studies published from 2009 through 2025. Evidence was organized around perioperative neurologic, renal, bleeding, and respiratory outcomes; completeness of revascularization; graft patency; conversion to cardiopulmonary bypass; surgical experience; and long-term survival. No de novo meta-analysis was performed, and all pooled estimates reported in this review are explicitly attributed to previously published evidence syntheses. Randomized evidence indicates broadly similar long-term mortality between OPCAB and ONCAB, whereas OPCAB may reduce selected perioperative complications, particularly stroke, transfusion, acute kidney injury, and respiratory morbidity in appropriately selected patients. Conversely, complex coronary anatomy may favor ONCAB because a stable operative field can facilitate complete revascularization. Conversion from OPCAB to cardiopulmonary bypass is consistently associated with worse outcomes, underscoring the importance of surgeon and institutional experience. Graft-patency differences are most evident for saphenous vein grafts and technically challenging territories. Anaortic or no-touch OPCAB may be particularly valuable in patients with extensive ascending-aortic atherosclerosis. ONCAB and OPCAB should therefore be viewed as complementary strategies. Selection should integrate aortic pathology, ventricular function, renal and bleeding risk, coronary complexity, the probability of complete revascularization, and local OPCAB expertise. A patient-tailored framework can help translate heterogeneous comparative evidence into practical clinical decision-making.

Title: Prior Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Its Impact on Lesion Complexity, Procedural Characteristics, and Outcomes in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is associated with accelerated native vessel atherosclerosis and more complex chronic total occlusion (CTO) anatomy, rendering CTO-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) more challenging despite contemporary technical advances. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare CTO lesion characteristics, procedural demands, and in-hospital outcomes according to prior CABG status. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were systematically searched from inception through May 15, 2026, for studies comparing CTO-PCI outcomes in patients with and without prior CABG. Data were pooled using odds ratios (ORs) and standardized mean differences (SMDs). Twelve studies enrolling 47,434 patients, including 10,354 with prior CABG, were included. Compared with patients without prior CABG, those with prior CABG had higher rates of blunt stump morphology (OR 1.51 [1.42-1.61]), proximal cap ambiguity (OR 1.55 [1.45-1.66]), calcification (OR 2.49 [2.22-2.79]), vessel bending (OR 2.27 [1.27-4.05]), distal cap bifurcation (OR 1.73 [1.51-1.98]), and higher Multicenter CTO Registry of Japan scores (SMD 0.48 [0.40-0.56]). Procedural burden was greater, with higher contrast use, longer fluoroscopy time and procedure duration, and greater stent use. Technical success (OR 0.63 [0.43-0.92]) and procedural success (OR 0.60 [0.53-0.69]) were lower in the prior CABG group. In-hospital mortality (OR 2.19), myocardial infarction (OR 2.29), and contrast-induced nephropathy (OR 1.97) were higher, whereas cardiac tamponade was less frequent (OR 0.37). Prior CABG is associated with substantially greater CTO complexity, procedural burden, and in-hospital risk, underscoring the need for careful procedural planning and individualized risk stratification in this population.

Title: Comparative Analysis of Arc Geometrical Configurations and Jaw Tracking for Peripheral Low-Dose Bath in Whole Breast VMAT.
Abstract: IntroductionMinimizing low-dose radiation spillage to surrounding organs at risk (OARs) is a critical consideration in whole breast irradiation (WBI) using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). While VMAT improves dose conformity and delivery efficiency, its continuous arc delivery may increase the "low-dose bath" in normal tissues. This study compared the dosimetric impact of arc geometry and jaw tracking under controlled planning conditions to characterize their effects on low-dose exposure.MethodsIn this retrospective dosimetric study, VMAT plans were generated for 30 breast cancer patients (15 left-sided and 15 right-sided). Four arc configurations were evaluated: conventional-arc VMAT (two and four arcs), tangential-arc VMAT (TA-VMAT), and hybrid-arc VMAT (HA-VMAT). Each configuration was planned with and without jaw tracking using identical objectives. Dose-volume histogram (DVH) parameters were analyzed for the planning target volume (PTV) and OARs, including the ipsilateral/contralateral lungs, heart, left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD), liver, and contralateral breast.ResultsAll techniques achieved comparable target coverage. Arc configuration substantially affected OAR dose distribution. Compared with conventional-arc VMAT, TA-VMAT reduced contralateral lung and breast exposure by 60-70%, while HA-VMAT yielded intermediate results. Notably, tangential arc restriction increased ipsilateral lung dose, particularly in right-sided cases, and increased LAD dose in left-sided cases. Jaw tracking provided additional dose reductions in selected OAR metrics, although the magnitude and statistical significance of these changes varied across arc configurations.ConclusionsThe findings suggest that peripheral low-dose exposure in whole-breast VMAT is influenced by arc configuration, while jaw tracking may provide additional dose reduction in selected OAR metrics. Considering both beam geometry and delivery-level leakage control may help reduce unnecessary OAR exposure.

Title: Genomics-Guided Risk Stratification in Myeloma Precursor Conditions: Converging Frameworks From Whole-Genome Sequencing.
Abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) remains incurable despite major therapeutic advances, underscoring the unmet need for earlier and genetically informed intervention. The rationale for such intervention lies in the stepwise evolution of MM from precursor states, including monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM), during which genetic alterations accumulate and drive the emergence, expansion, and evolution of malignant clones. In 2025, three landmark cohort studies using whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing (WES/WGS) proposed distinct but relevant genomic frameworks for reclassifying disease risk in MGUS and SMM. Despite differences in design and analyses, these frameworks converge on several principles: (i) the malignant genomic architecture of myeloma is established well before clinical progression; (ii) a substantial fraction of clinically defined precursor disease already harbors the hallmarks of overt myeloma; and (iii) WES/WGS-derived features meaningfully improve clinical risk models. In this perspective, we critically reviewed these three contemporaneous frameworks and synthesize their convergent implications, not previously consolidated for clinical use, into a practical approach toward genomics-guided management of myeloma precursor conditions.

Title: Spousal Traumatic Brain Injury and Risk of Mortality, Dementia, and Cardiovascular Events.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is highly prevalent in older adults. While there is strong and growing evidence that TBI is associated with caregiver burden and psychological health, it remains unclear whether a spouse's TBI is associated with the long-term health of the uninjured partner.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether having a spouse who sustains an incident TBI is associated with risk of mortality, dementia, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and to assess whether associations differ by sex or survival of the injured spouse after TBI.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective community-based cohort of married couples was performed at 4 US centers in North Carolina, Mississippi, Minnesota, and Maryland as part of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study. Of 4506 baseline spousal pairs, 3281 were retained for mortality and dementia analyses and 2740 of these for MACE analyses. Participants contributed person-time from baseline (1987-1989) until incident outcome, death, loss to follow-up, divorce or separation, or administrative censoring on December 31, 2022. Analyses were conducted from November 24, 2025, through August 25, 2026.
EXPOSURE: Incident spousal TBI (ascertained using self-report, hospitalization surveillance, and linked Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services data), modeled as a 2-category time-varying exposure (spousal TBI vs no spousal TBI) and 4-category exposure incorporating spousal death.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Incident all-cause mortality, dementia, and MACE. Cox proportional hazards regression shared frailty models were used to estimate associations adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioral characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 3281 married pairs included in mortality and dementia analyses (among whom, 2740 pairs were included in MACE analyses), the mean (SD) age at baseline was 54.5 (5.5) years, with 3281 female and 3281 male spouses (for a total of 6562 participants). The median follow-up was 19.5 (IQR, 10.6-29.0) years. Spousal TBI was associated with increased risk of mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.24 [95% CI, 1.07-1.43]; P = .004) but not dementia (HR, 1.17 [95% CI, 0.88-1.56]; P = .28) or MACE (HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.84-1.57]; P = .40). In sex-stratified analyses, associations were similar among males and females. In models incorporating spousal death, mortality risk was higher among individuals whose spouse was alive with a TBI (HR, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.05-1.41]; P = .008), higher among those whose spouse was deceased without a TBI (HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.36-1.61]; P < .001), and higher among those whose spouse was deceased with a TBI (HR, 1.27 [95% CI, 1.07-1.52]; P = .006) compared with those whose spouse was alive without a TBI. Results were similar, but less precise, for dementia and MACE.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of married pairs of participants in the ARIC Study, having a spouse who sustained a TBI was associated with a modest but significantly higher risk of mortality in the uninjured partner, whereas findings for dementia and major adverse cardiovascular events were less consistent. These findings suggest that the consequences of TBI may extend beyond injured individuals and support family- and care partner-centered approaches to care.

Title: Noninpatient Alternative Treatment Venues for Acute Care Needs.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Hospitalizations are costly and may lead to adverse events. Some health systems offer treatment in alternative venues of care for select patients.
OBJECTIVE: To describe use and short-term outcomes of emergency department (ED) patients transitioned to noninpatient care settings (ambulatory treatment center [ATC], advanced care at home [ACAH], or emergency department observation unit [EDOU]) compared with inpatient care.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study of ED patients aged 19 years or older was conducted from January 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025, at multisite community ED and inpatient medical centers within an integrated delivery system (Kaiser Permanente Northern California). Included patients had active health plan membership; had an ED visit for heart failure, pneumonia, cellulitis, urinary tract infection, COVID-19, or anemia; and had their care transitioned to an ATC, ACAH program (Kaiser Permanente Advanced Care at Home), EDOU, or inpatient bed.
EXPOSURE: Treatment venue.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were care escalation (inpatient admission) for patients treated in an ATC, ACAH program, or EDOU, as well as 7-day ED return visits, 30-day hospitalizations, and 30-day mortality following care completion across all venues. Unadjusted outcome rates are reported.
RESULTS: This study included 26 618 ED encounters (median patient age, 77 years [IQR, 65-85 years]; 52.6% female). Among 22 755 unique patients, 87.4% had 1 encounter, 9.8% had 2 encounters, and 2.8% had more than 2 encounters. There were 728 (2.7%), 880 (3.3%), 5133 (19.3%), and 19 877 (74.7%) encounters in ATC, ACAH, EDOU, and hospital settings, respectively. One-quarter of patients (25.3%) received care in an ATC, ACAH program, or EDOU. Inpatient admission rates were lower for ATC and ACAH encounters than for EDOU encounters (4.3% [95% CI, 2.7%-5.8%], 5.3% [3.8%-6.8%], and 28.0% [26.8%-29.2%], respectively). Rates of 7-day ED visits were similar across venues (ATC: 10.4% [95% CI, 7.8%-12.9%]; ACAH: 5.3% [3.8%-6.8%]; EDOU: 9.2% [8.4%-10.0%]; and hospital: 8.5% [8.1%-8.9%]). In contrast, 30-day mortality and hospitalization rates were lower among ATC, ACAH, and EDOU encounters than in hospital encounters (30-day mortality: 2.1% [95% CI, 1.0%-3.2%], 1.7% [0.8%-2.6%], 2.8% [2.3%-3.2%], and 5.3% [5.0%-5.6%]; and 30-day hospitalization: 11.4% [95% CI, 8.8%-14.1%], 8.3% [6.3%-10.2%], 12.7% [11.7%-13.7%], and 15.3% [14.7%-15.8%], respectively).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients treated in alternative venues of care, one-quarter received care in an ATC, ACAH program, or EDOU. These findings suggest that adoption of novel treatment spaces for appropriately selected patients may allow health systems to focus hospital resources on the patients with the most complex needs.

Title: Case Report: A Perioperative Buprenorphine/Naloxone Microinduction to Reduce the Harms Associated With Long-Term High-Dose Intravenous Opioid Infusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with complex chronic bowel conditions and Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome requiring multimodal analgesia regimens often require significant doses of opioids. Prolonged exposure to opioids can lead to opioid dependence and opioid misuse, requiring its own management. While the role of buprenorphine/naloxone as part of a multimodal pain management and opioid harm reduction strategy has been well described, its application following cardiac surgery in patients who also have Ehlers-Danlos disease remains limited. Historically, buprenorphine/naloxone induction has required patients to experience withdrawal symptoms and can result in patients experiencing emotional distress.
AIMS: Our aim was to review the outcomes of using a modified Bernese method microinduction strategy to help transition a patient from intravenous hydromorphone to buprenorphine/naloxone. This transition took place during hospitalization, approximately 2 weeks following cardiac surgery in a patient with significant opioid dependence, a relevant medical history of scoliosis, chronic pain of the, back, and abdomen, and significant gastric dysmotility requiring gastric tube feeding. The patient required a wheelchair for mobility. Before hospital discharge, the patient was successfully transitioned from approximately 1,300 mg oral morphine equivalents per 24-hour period to a stable dose of buprenorphine and naloxone and remained on the latter in the long term.
METHODS: Retrospective chart review was used for data collection to understand outcomes of the microinduction strategy. This case was undertaken on an inpatient cardiovascular surgical recovery ward in a Quaternary Care Facility in Ontario. The patient provided consent for chart review and publication of the case report as well as inclusion of her reported experience.
RESULTS: Review of the clinical records suggests that using the microinduction strategy of buprenorphine/naloxone to gradually transition from high-dose intravenous opioid to a stable dose of buprenorphine/naloxone was successful and sustained in the long term.
CONCLUSIONS: Microinduction of sublingual buprenorphine/naloxone was successful in a patient who was clinically stable postoperatively, presented with significant psychological distress given pending discharge on high-dose opioids and wanting to change the recovery trajectory related to opioid requirement. Precipitated withdrawal with buprenorphine/naloxone could have worsened psychological distress, and thus, a microinduction technique was successful.

Title: Sex-Specific Mediators of Serum Uric Acid Reduction Following Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy: A Retrospective Longitudinal Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperuricemia is highly prevalent among individuals with obesity and is associated with insulin resistance, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular risk. Although laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) reduces serum uric acid (SUA), the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Emerging evidence suggests that sex differences influence metabolic regulation, including insulin secretion and renal urate handling. This study investigates one-year changes in SUA following LSG and explores sex-specific determinants.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 268 patients (96 males, 172 females) undergoing LSG between 2014 and 2025. Clinical and laboratory parameters were collected at baseline and 12 months, with changes defined as baseline minus postoperative values. Sex-stratified univariate screening (P < 0.10) and backward multivariate regression identified independent predictors of SUA reduction. In females, bootstrap mediation analysis (5,000 resamples) assessed whether C-peptide and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) mediated the relationship between weight loss and SUA reduction.
RESULTS: Baseline SUA was higher in males than females (479.8 vs. 406.9 µmol/L, P < 0.001). At 12 months, females exhibited greater absolute and relative SUA reductions (both P < 0.001). Baseline SUA and percent total weight loss (%TWL) were independent predictors in both sexes. In females, ΔeGFR remained significant (P = 0.007), while ΔC-peptide showed a trend (P = 0.063). Mediation analysis demonstrated that %TWL indirectly reduced SUA via ΔC-peptide (β = 0.251, 95% CI: 0.009-0.562), accounting for 9.2% of the total effect.
CONCLUSION: SUA reduction following LSG exhibits sex-specific patterns. In females, the association between weight loss and SUA reduction was partially mediated by reductions in C-peptide, while changes in eGFR were independently associated with SUA reduction.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04548232.

Title: Directional Brain Connectivity Changes Induced by Heart Rate Variability Biofeedback: A Spectral Dynamic Causal Modeling Study.
Abstract: Heart rate variability biofeedback (HRVB) is a non-pharmacological intervention that trains individuals to breathe at their cardiovascular resonance frequency to enhance autonomic regulation. While HRVB improves cardiovascular function across clinical conditions, the directional neural pathways through which it modulates the central autonomic network (CAN) remain poorly understood. Using a publicly available open-access dataset, we conducted a secondary analysis of effective (directional) neural connectivity (EC) data from 32 healthy participants randomized to an 8-week HRVB intervention (n = 15) or a video game Control intervention (n = 17). Pre- and post-intervention resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were analyzed using spectral dynamic causal modeling (DCM) combined with parametric empirical Bayes to examine group differences in EC changes (ΔEC). We also evaluated whether connectivity changes correlated with changes in peripheral autonomic regulation, indexed by the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (ΔSDNN). Compared with the Control group, HRVB showed strong evidence (posterior-probability = 1) of increased ΔEC from the medial prefrontal cortex to the anterior cingulate cortex and bilateral thalamus post-treatment, along with reduced ΔEC from the right hippocampus to the right ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (VLPFC). Furthermore, the regression coefficient linking hippocampus-to-VLPFC ΔEC with ΔSDNN was more (posterior-probability = 1) negative in the HRVB group than in Controls, indicating an intervention-dependent association between autonomic changes and effective connectivity. These findings indicate that HRVB may alter directional fronto-limbic communication within the CAN. Given the relatively small sample sizes, these findings need replication, but provide preliminary understanding about the neural circuitry through which resonance breathing may modulate central autonomic control.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and chronic kidney disease: reciprocal associations, potential causal pathways, and clinical implications.
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) leads to multiple metabolic disorders which raise both the cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality, especially in end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) patients. Among the dysmetabolic CKD-associated patterns, dyslipidemia shows a wide spectrum of clinical concurrent presentations, involving high serum levels of triglycerides, cholesterol, and lipoproteins such as Lp(a). International consensus statements and guidelines have highlighted the increased cardiovascular risk associated with higher serum Lp(a) levels > 105 nmol/L due to its pro-atherosclerotic and pro-thrombotic effects. Therefore, its assessment should be recommended at least once in a lifetime, due to the relative stability of Lp(a) serum levels over time. CKD is associated with increased Lp(a) concentrations, which rise as the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and/or urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) worsen. Consequently, Lp(a) levels may be five-to-tenfold higher in patients with ESKD than in those with mild-to-moderate CKD. This alteration is mainly attributable to impaired renal clearance of Lp(a) and apolipoprotein(a) [Apo(a)] particles and, under specific conditions, to increased hepatic Lp(a) production, as observed in severe proteinuric diseases. Conversely, Lp(a) genetic determinants of elevated Lp(a) levels and increased serum Lp(a) concentrations have been investigated as potential causes of CKD onset, through Mendelian randomization (MR) and prospective studies, respectively. However, uncertainty and important gaps in the available evidence still remain. The aim of this review is to summarize and discuss the most recent and relevant clinical and experimental evidence on this topic through a defined research among the scientific literature.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Geriatric Heart Failure: Evidence, Safety, and Clinical Implementation.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes the rationale, efficacy, safety, and implementation of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in older adults with heart failure (HF).
RECENT FINDINGS: SGLT2i have become an integral part of contemporary HF therapy, with benefits demonstrated across the ejection fraction spectrum. Age subgroup analyses from randomized trials, frailty analyses, meta-analyses, and real-world cohorts suggest that benefits on HF hospitalization and cardiovascular outcomes are largely preserved in older and frail patients. Observational data in patients aged  ≥ 75 and > 80 years further support potential effectiveness in very old and multimorbid populations. However, geriatric vulnerability modifies clinical implementation, particularly regarding volume status, renal function, risk of falling, genitourinary infections, nutritional status, cognition, polypharmacy, and self-care capacity. Available evidence suggests that SGLT2i remain effective and are generally well tolerated in older patients with HF. Older age alone should therefore not preclude SGLT2i therapy. In geriatric HF, treatment decisions should be individualized according to frailty, comorbidity burden, safety risks, functional status, self-care capacity, and goals of care.

Title: Prosthetic valve endocarditis: valve type, microbiological patterns, and mortality-a nationwide multicenter cohort study.
Journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) carries high mortality. The impact of prosthetic valve type on outcomes remains unclear, particularly with the increasing use of transcatheter valves. We aimed to identify predictors of 30-day and 1-year mortality in PVE and assess the association between valve type and outcomes.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients aged ≥ 18 years with definite or possible PVE from the Türkiye Endocarditis Group registry between January 2016 and December 2025 were included. Valve type was evaluated across three groups: mechanical PVE (mPVE), surgical bioprosthetic PVE (bPVE), and percutaneous bPVE. Cox proportional hazards models were used.
RESULTS: A total of 261 patients were included (median age 63 years [IQR 49-71], 37.9% female). Among patients with available follow-up data, the 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 23.1% (58/251) and 46.3% (100/216), respectively. In multivariable analysis, age (HR 1.027 per year; 95% CI 1.006-1.049), creatinine level on admission (HR 1.154 per mg/dL; 95% CI 1.019-1.306), and cardiac complications (HR 3.589; 95% CI 2.080-6.193) were independently associated with 30-day mortality and remained significant for 1-year mortality. Valve type was not independently associated with mortality after adjustment for measured confounders. Enterococcus spp. were more frequent in percutaneous bPVE.
CONCLUSION: In this national multicenter cohort, PVE carried high mortality regardless of valve type. Older age, higher creatinine levels, and cardiac complications-but not valve type-were the strongest predictors of short- and long-term mortality. The higher frequency of Enterococcus spp. in percutaneous bPVE suggests that valve type may be more closely related to microbiological profile than prognosis.

Title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
Abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.
Publication Types: Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention.
KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

Title: Genotype and pulmonary function in children with primary ciliary dyskinesia: a cross-sectional cohort study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder with variable clinical severity. Genotype-associated differences in pulmonary function remain incompletely characterized, particularly in exclusively pediatric cohorts. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 44 children with molecularly confirmed PCD based on biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. Clinical characteristics and spirometric parameters were compared across genotype-based groups. Exploratory gene-level comparisons were performed for the most frequently represented genotypes. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations between DNAH5, DNAH11, and CCDC39/CCDC40 and FEV1 z-score after adjustment for age at diagnosis, BMI z-score, and bronchiectasis. The median age at diagnosis was 8.7 years (IQR 6-13), and parental consanguinity was present in 59.1% of patients. DNAH5 was the most frequently identified gene (22.7%), followed by DNAH11 and CCNO (13.6% each). FEV1% predicted, FEV1 Z-score, FVC Z-score, FEF25-75, FEF25-75% predicted, and FEV1/FVC differed significantly across the genotype-based groups (all p < 0.05), with the DNAH11 group showing the most preserved pulmonary function profile. In exploratory gene-level analyses, patients with CCNO and CCDC39/CCDC40 variants demonstrated numerically lower spirometric values, whereas DNAH11 showed the most preserved values and DNAH5 an intermediate profile. In exploratory adjusted analyses, CCDC39/CCDC40 was associated with lower FEV1 z-scores (B =- 1.55, p = 0.002), whereas DNAH11 was associated with higher FEV1 z-scores (B = 1.19, p = 0.023). Neither DNAH5 nor CCNO was independently associated with FEV1 z-score.
CONCLUSION: Pulmonary function showed genotype-associated heterogeneity in this exclusively pediatric cohort with molecularly confirmed PCD. However, the gene-level findings remain exploratory because of the small subgroup sizes. Larger longitudinal multicenter studies are needed to confirm these associations.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Primary ciliary dyskinesia is genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous, and previous large cohorts have demonstrated genotype-associated differences in pulmonary function, with poorer lung function reported particularly in CCNO and CCDC39/CCDC40 and relatively preserved function in DNAH11.
WHAT IS NEW: • This is one of the few exclusively pediatric cohorts to link PCD genotype with spirometric phenotype using molecularly confirmed diagnoses. • In exploratory adjusted analyses, CCDC39/CCDC40 was associated with lower FEV1 z-scores and DNAH11 with higher FEV1 z-scores, whereas DNAH5 was not independently associated with FEV1 z-score. • These findings are consistent with previously reported genotype-phenotype patterns in a pediatric population, butrequire confi rmation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

Title: Temporal fluctuations in retinal artery occlusions: an 11-year German cohort study.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiovascular events have been shown to follow seasonal and monthly distributions. It is unclear whether this applies to retinal vascular diseases. This study aims to determine the existence of seasonal variations in the onset of retinal artery occlusions (RAO) in a European population.
METHODS: This retrospective, monocentric study included 646 eyes of 646 patients who were treated for RAO at the University Hospital Münster, Germany, between 2014 and 2024. Data on the exact diagnosis, day of presentation, intake of anticoagulation (AC) and general patient characteristics were collected. To determine seasonal variations in the presentation of RAO Chi-Square Test for specified proportions and Poisson regression were applied. Additional subgroup analyses further distinguished between central retinal artery occlusions (CRAO) and branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO) and assessed whether pre-existing AC or antiplatelet (AP) medication status was associated with the temporal distribution of RAO presentations.
RESULTS: No significant seasonal variation in the occurrence of RAO was observed (χ² p = 0.11; Poisson regression p = 0.24). Monthly analysis revealed significant variation according to the chi-square test (p = 0.03), which was not confirmed by Poisson regression (p = 0.07). In the CRAO subgroup, no significant seasonal variation was observed (χ² p = 0.22; Poisson regression p = 0.22), whereas monthly variation was significant in both the chi-square analysis (p = 0.03) and Poisson regression (p = 0.01). No significant seasonal or monthly variation was observed for BRAO. Pre-existing AC/AP medication status was not significantly associated with the seasonal distribution of RAO presentations in any of the analyzed groups.
CONCLUSION: This study characterizes temporal fluctuations in RAO presentations and highlights the necessity for further investigations into potential underlying pathophysiological mechanisms, in order to better understand patterns of RAO presentations and their potential clinical relevance.

Title: Clinical phenotype and predictors of recurrence in childhood IgA vasculitis.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: IgA vasculitis (IgAV) is generally considered a self-limited disease in childhood; however, recurrent episodes may occur during the disease course. The clinical phenotype and associated factors of recurrent disease remain to be clearly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics of recurrent IgAV and compare patients with and without recurrence to identify potential predictors of recurrence.This retrospective medical record review study included children diagnosed with IgAV between 2015 and 2025 according to the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES classification criteria. Patients with incomplete data, follow-up duration < 6 months, or alternative diagnoses were excluded. Clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, treatment characteristics, and recurrence patterns were compared between patients with and without recurrence. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of recurrence.A total of 417 children with IgAV were included, of whom 50 (12.0%) developed recurrence. Recurrent disease was characterized by more severe cutaneous involvement, with significantly higher frequencies of widespread or bullous cutaneous manifestations, as well as higher frequencies of arthritis and microscopic hematuria at presentation. Preceding infection was significantly more common among recurrent patients and independently increased relapse risk (HR: 2.33, 95% CI: 1.20-4.51). Microscopic hematuria (HR: 3.00, 95% CI: 1.62-5.57), widespread/bullous cutaneous involvement (HR: 2.65, 95% CI: 1.47-4.80), and joint involvement (HR: 2.98, 95% CI: 1.55-5.73) also emerged as independent predictors of recurrence. In addition, lower monocyte counts were independently associated with relapse risk (HR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.71-0.95). Colchicine use was significantly more frequent among recurrent patients, likely reflecting therapeutic preferences related to recurrent cutaneous involvement.
CONCLUSIONS: Preceding infection, microscopic hematuria, extensive or bullous skin involvement, joint involvement, and lower monocyte counts may help identify patients at higher risk of recurrence.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • IgA vasculitis (IgAV) is the most common childhood vasculitis, and recurrence may occur during follow-up. • Renal and gastrointestinal involvement have previously been associated with recurrent disease; however, reported risk factors remain inconsistent across studies. • Data regarding the clinical phenotype and predictors of recurrent childhood IgAV are still limited.
WHAT IS NEW: • Recurrent childhood IgAV was associated with more severe cutaneous manifestations and more frequent joint involvement at presentation, with arthritis identified as a predictor of recurrence. • Lower monocyte counts were independently associated with recurrence, suggesting that readily accessible hematological parameters may contribute to early risk stratification in childhood IgAV. • Recurrent episodes were predominantly cutaneous, and the increased use of colchicine appeared to reflect therapeutic preferences related to recurrent cutaneous manifestations rather than increased systemic disease severity.

Title: Effectiveness of home-based exercise interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
