PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of home-based exercise (HBE) interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) in cancer survivors.
METHODS: A comprehensive search of seven electronic databases was conducted for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published from January 2000 to October 2025. The participants were cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic therapies. The interventions were structured HBE programmes. Eligible studies were those that reported on any outcomes related to CTR-CVT. The primary outcomes included direct cardiotoxicity parameters (e.g., left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] and global longitudinal strain [GLS]) and cardiac biomarkers (e.g., troponins and B-type natriuretic peptide); clinical cardiovascular events (e.g., heart failure and arrhythmias); cardiorespiratory fitness (e.g., peak oxygen uptake [VO2 peak]); and (d) functional capacity (e.g., the six-minute walk test [6MWT]). Two researchers independently performed the study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment. Meta-analyses were conducted using R software.
RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 851 participants were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that the HBE interventions significantly improved VO2 peak (MD = 2.35 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: 1.26 to 3.43, p < 0.001), which indicated improved cardiorespiratory fitness. Subgroup analysis found larger effects for longer-duration interventions (24 to 52 weeks), mHealth use, and cancer Stage III/IV. Evidence on direct cardiotoxicity parameters and biomarkers was limited, as only one study assessed these outcomes. No significant improvements were found in the 6MWT or health-related quality of life (HRQoL).
CONCLUSION: While HBE improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak) and mitigated functional decline in cancer survivors, its ability to prevent CTR-CVT was unproven. Future adequately powered trials should incorporate direct cardiotoxicity assessments to establish true cardioprotective efficacy and implementation studies to optimise real-world delivery.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting inflammation and oxidative stress in PCOS-associated insulin resistance.
Abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It is commonly associated with insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, chronic low-grade inflammation, and oxidative stress. These factors contribute to metabolic dysfunction and increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular complications. This narrative review critically evaluates the available evidence regarding nutraceutical and herbal interventions targeting insulin resistance, inflammation, and oxidative stress associated with PCOS. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Scopus, and CNKI databases, covering studies from database inception through 12 July to 21 November 2025 with keywords including PCOS, insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, oxidative stress, diabetes mellitus, nutritional supplements, and herbs. Relevant original research articles, randomized clinical trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses were considered, and the available evidence was interpreted according to study design and evidence level. Evidence from preclinical studies and human clinical investigations indicates that selected nutraceutical and herbal interventions may influence metabolic, inflammatory, oxidative stress-related, hormonal, and reproductive parameters in PCOS. However, the magnitude and consistency of these effects vary substantially depending on the intervention, formulation, dose, treatment duration, participant characteristics, and the outcome assessed. Improvements in surrogate biochemical measures, such as HOMA-IR or inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, should not be interpreted as direct evidence of improved fertility, reduced cardiovascular risk, or prevention of long-term diabetes. Therefore, the available evidence should be interpreted according to study design and evidence level, with greater weight given to findings from well-designed randomized clinical trials and systematic reviews or meta-analyses than to isolated preclinical or small clinical studies.

Title: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.
Journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer.
METHODS: CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality.
RESULTS: The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses.
CONCLUSION: CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Clinical Trial, Phase III

Title: Gout as a risk factor for lower-extremity amputation in diabetes: a nationwide, register-based case-control study.
Abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Non-healing diabetic foot ulcers are a major precursor to lower-extremity amputation (LEA) in diabetes, and gout may be an overlooked contributor. We hypothesised that individuals with both diabetes and gout have a higher risk of LEA than those with diabetes alone, with the strongest effect at more distal amputation levels.
METHODS: In a nationwide case-control study of 601,541 individuals with type 2 diabetes, we identified 4912 cases with LEA and 39,101 age- and sex-matched control participants. Gout exposure was determined using ICD-10 diagnoses and Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical codes for urate-lowering therapy. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression, adjusting for diabetes duration, peripheral arterial disease, acute myocardial infarction and late diabetes complications.
RESULTS: Gout was associated with an increased risk of LEA (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.69, 2.02) in unadjusted analyses, and the association remained significant after full adjustment (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.37, 1.69). A significant trend (p=0.03) was observed across amputation levels, with potentially higher risk at more anatomically distal sites although no statistically significant differences were observed between individual amputation levels: OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.12, 1.68) for above-knee amputations, increasing to OR 1.65 (95% CI 1.32, 2.05) for toe amputations.
CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Co-existing gout is an independent risk factor for LEA in individuals with type 2 diabetes. The risk is elevated across all amputation levels, with the most pronounced effect potentially being at distal anatomical sites. These findings highlight the need for increased awareness of gout when managing individuals with type 2 diabetes at risk of LEA.

Title: A Mortality Risk Prediction Score for Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a leading cause of pediatric heart failure and carries a substantial risk of death or heart transplantation. In low- and middle-income countries, limited access to advanced heart failure therapies and transplantation highlights the need for simple, reliable tools to identify children at highest risk. Therefore, this study aimed to identify independent predictors of mortality and develop a practical bedside risk score for mortality prediction in children with DCM. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children with DCM treated at Dr. Sardjito Hospital, Indonesia, between 2016 and 2025. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic variables were evaluated for association with mortality. Independent predictors were incorporated into a point-based risk score using the Spiegelhalter-Knill-Jones method. Discriminative performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internal validation. Among 109 children with DCM, mortality was 33.9%. Seven independent predictors of mortality were identified: age ≥ 2 years at diagnosis, New York Heart Association/Ross functional class IV heart failure, malnutrition, requirement for vasoactive support, low-voltage electrocardiography, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter z-score > + 4, and left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 30%. The derived score ranged from - 25 to + 28 points. A threshold score ≥ 11 accurately identified high-risk patients, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.932 (95% CI 0.886-0.977), with 73.0% sensitivity and 95.8% specificity. Internal validation demonstrated sustained performance (AUC 0.921). We developed and validated a simple, bedside mortality risk score with excellent discriminative ability for children with DCM. By relying on routinely available clinical and echocardiographic parameters, this tool enables early identification of high-risk patients and may support timely clinical decision-making and resource allocation, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

Title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).
RESULTS: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).
CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

Title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.
METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.
RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).

Title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score.
Abstract: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

Title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The virtual circle method is currently used in preprocedural computed tomography planning for Redo-transcatheter aortic valve (TAV) replacement to simulate the predicted outer boundary of the index TAV and the valve-to-aorta distance for coronary risk assessment, yet its accuracy against postprocedural observations has not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of the virtual circle method in predicting index TAV expansion and coronary risk following a second TAV implantation using paired preprocedural and postprocedural computed tomography in patients undergoing Redo-TAV replacement.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 58 patients who underwent Redo-TAV replacement at 5 sites with paired preprocedural and postprocedural cardiac computed tomography. Three valve combinations were analyzed: Evolut-in-SAPIEN (n=17), SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN (n=13), and SAPIEN-in-Evolut (n=28). Index TAV frame expansion was quantified by area- or perimeter-derived diameter change. Accuracy of the virtual circle method was defined as a diameter difference within ±1 mm between predicted and observed index TAV frame diameter.
RESULTS: In the Evolut-in-SAPIEN combination, meaningful index SAPIEN frame expansion occurred only with effective pre/postdilatation, whereas in both the SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, consistent frame expansion was observed regardless of dilatation. Changes in index frame diameter corresponded inversely to changes in valve-to-aorta distance. In the SAPIEN-in-Evolut combination, expansion was governed chiefly by implant position and sizing strategy. Across all combinations in which the virtual circle method was applicable (n=53), accurate prediction was achieved in 31 patients (58.5%), with overestimation in 14 (26.4%) and underestimation in 8 (15.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: The virtual circle method provided an accurate or conservative (overestimating) estimate of index TAV expansion and coronary risk in the majority of patients (85%), supporting its clinical utility for Redo-TAVR planning. The remaining 15% showed underestimation of modest magnitude (median, 1.3 mm), occurring predominantly in patients who underwent predilatation and postdilatation, warranting heightened caution in borderline coronary anatomy when dilatation strategies are employed.

Title: Risk of Postoperative Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events After Dermatologic Surgery After Recent Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dermatologic surgery is classified as very low risk by the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association. Limited evidence evaluates the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events after dermatologic surgery within 1 year of myocardial infarction.
OBJECTIVE: To determine major adverse cardiovascular event risk after dermatologic surgery within 1 year of myocardial infarction. Outcomes were compared with cataract surgery and endoscopies, which are also considered very low risk procedures.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the All of Us Research Program V8, nationwide database of 633,000 patients, the authors performed a retrospective study from 2018 to 2023. CPT and ICD-10 codes were used to retrieve data.
RESULTS: Out of 308 procedures, 3 (0.97%) major adverse cardiovascular events were observed within the 30-day postoperative window in patients with or without a history of myocardial infarction. Patients undergoing procedures postmyocardial infarction appeared more likely to experience major adverse cardiovascular events than those without prior myocardial infarction (4.9% vs 0%), although not significantly more so than patients with myocardial infarction without procedures.
CONCLUSION: The authors' findings are consistent with the low risk of dermatologic procedures in patients with myocardial infarction, although they are limited by the low number of major adverse cardiovascular events.

Title: Leadless Cardiac Resynchronization Results in Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling: A Randomized Substudy of the SOLVE-CRT Study.
3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease.
METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival.
RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ.
CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

Title: Phase 2 Trial of 89Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
Abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) imaging is currently suboptimal, which may limit patient care. Zirconium 89 (89Zr) deferoxamine (DFO)-daratumumab is a novel CD38-targeted immuno-PET tracer. Purpose To compare 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT against standard-of-care fluorine 18 (18F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT for detection of MM. Materials and Methods Participants with MM were accrued to this prospective phase 2 trial between March 2022 and July 2025. Standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT and bone marrow biopsy were performed, along with research 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT. If there were discrepant lesions between the two scans, image-guided biopsy was considered as the reference standard. The McNemar test was used to compare disease detection between the two imaging modalities. Results This study included 60 participants (median age, 63 years [IQR, 57-71 years]; 32 women). 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 43% (26 of 60; 95% CI: 31, 57) of participants, and 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 47% (28 of 60; 95% CI: 33, 60) of participants. While there was no overall difference in disease detection between the two imaging modalities (P = .81), MM was demonstrated only with 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT in 13% (eight of 60) of participants, with subsequent biopsy confirmation of active myeloma. Conclusion In participants with MM, CD38-targeted 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab immuno-PET helped detect active myeloma in some participants with no signs of disease at 18F-FDG PET/CT. Clinical trial registration no. NCT04814615 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Choyke in this issue.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Clinical Trial, Phase II

Title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis at Diagnosis is Associated With Adverse Long-Term Glycaemic Trajectories and Retinopathy in Adult-Onset Type 1 Diabetes. A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: The long-term significance of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) at the diagnosis of adult-onset type 1 diabetes (T1D) is poorly understood. We investigated the association between DKA at diagnosis and long-term outcomes.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analysed adults with T1D diagnosed at age ≥ 18 years who attended a single tertiary diabetes centre between 2000 and 2025. Participants were classified according to the presence or absence of DKA at diagnosis. Longitudinal changes in HbA1c were analysed using mixed models. Incident chronic complications were evaluated using Cox regression models.
RESULTS: Among 517 adults with T1D (47.2% women), 112 (21.7%) presented with DKA at diagnosis. The frequency of DKA at diagnosis increased from 13.2% in 2000-2008 to 34.6% after 2016 (p < 0.001). During a median (IQR) follow-up of 9.3 (3.5-15.5) years after cohort entry, individuals presenting with DKA had persistently higher HbA1c levels than those without DKA, with an adjusted between-group difference of 0.37% (95% CI 0.20, 0.53; p < 0.001). When data were aligned to the diabetes onset date, the estimated mean difference was 0.66% (p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, DKA at diagnosis was associated with a higher incidence of retinopathy (HR 1.61; 95% CI 1.02-2.55; p = 0.041). The association was confirmed after accounting for delayed cohort entry and was attenuated by adjusting for mean HbA1c during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Among individuals with adult-onset T1D attending a tertiary diabetes clinic, DKA at diagnosis was associated with persistently less favourable glycaemic control during long-term follow-up. Interpretation is limited by the single-centre retrospective design and delayed cohort entry.

Title: Transvenous Cardiac Pacing: 12-year Experience in Lagos, Nigeria.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The advent of cardiac pacemaker insertion has revolutionised the treatment of symptomatic bradycardia. As is often the case with low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), the entry of new technology, pacemakers included, lagged-behind those of their high-income counterparts. Access to pacemaker devices and the required expertise in LMICs has, however, increased over the last decade.
AIM: The aim is to review the outcome of pacemaker implantation in our city, increase awareness and advocate for an upgrade of the current standard.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who had permanent pacemaker insertion (PPI) for symptomatic bradycardia records in three centres over 12 years spanning from January 2011 to December 2022. Data on patients' demographics, clinical presentation, indications for pacemaker insertion and treatment outcomes were extracted. The data were analysed using the SPSS version 24 software.
RESULTS: A total of 133 patients (68 males, 67 females) had PPI at three hospitals during the study period. Their age range was 26-99 years, with median and mean ages of 70 and 67.72 ± 13.97 years, respectively. There was equal gender distribution. The mean pulse rate at presentation was 38.70 ± 6.56 per minute. The most frequent indication for PPI was complete heart block ( n = 117, 88%). Single-chamber pacemaker (VVIR) was inserted in 95.5%. Acute lead dislodgement was the most frequent complication.
CONCLUSION: PPI has revolutionised the treatment of symptomatic bradycardia, contributing to increased life expectancy. Upgrading and increased affordability will benefit more patients with indications for PPI, and extend life expectancy.

Title: Impact of Medication Therapy Management on Patient Knowledge and Adherence in Oral Anticoagulant Use.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The deficiencies in patient knowledge and adherence constitute a significant obstacle to optimal utilisation of oral anticoagulants, resulting in diminished safety and effectiveness.
AIM: The aim of the study was to assess the impact of pharmacist-led medication therapy management (MTM) on knowledge and adherence outcomes in patients on oral anticoagulants.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: An observational-cohort study was conducted in the surgery, cardiology and cardiothoracic surgery departments. A clinical pharmacist trained in MTM services conducted the MTM sessions according to the guidelines. The follow-up of the patients was conducted at scheduled visits to the hospital at 0, 4 and 8 months. The knowledge and adherence outcomes were assessed through a repeated measures analysis of variance, with P < 0.05 was statistically significant.
RESULTS: Out of 100 patients, 94 patients were followed up on, and their data were analysed. The commonly prescribed oral anticoagulants were acenocoumarol (34%) and warfarin (29%). The baseline knowledge and adherence scores on oral anticoagulant medications were 43.40 ± 19.37 and 51.59 ± 25.34. The MTM services were provided after 4-month and 8-month intervals, knowledge scores were 71.38 ± 14.99 and 82.97 ± 9.92, and the adherence scores were 80.45 ± 11.95 and 88.56 ± 9.64, respectively. Thirty-four adverse drug reactions were reported, with an International Normalized Ratio range >6 for which anticoagulation reversal agents were used.
CONCLUSION: The clinical pharmacist-led MTM services significantly improved knowledge ( P < 0.001) and adherence ( P < 0.001) of patients treated with oral anticoagulants at different time intervals. The pharmacist's role in anticoagulation management service will be helpful for physicians to optimise and maintain the dose.

Title: Cardiovascular and diabetes outcomes after metabolic bariatric surgery versus obesity management medications: nationwide overlap-weighted cohort study of 379 858 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) and incretin-based therapy (IBT) are effective treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, their comparative effectiveness in current practice remains incompletely defined.
METHODS: Adults aged ≥18 years with obesity and T2D who underwent MBS or initiated obesity management medications (OMMs) were identified. The median follow-up was 4.9 (interquartile range (i.q.r.) 3.6-6.7) years for MBS and 4.3 (i.q.r. 3.4-5.8) years for IBT. Overlap weighting balanced baseline covariates between groups. Five-year outcomes included nephropathy, retinopathy, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and all-cause mortality. One-year outcomes included percentage total weight loss (%TWL) and rates of haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) <6.5%.
RESULTS: In total, 379 858 adults met the inclusion criteria (32 401 underwent MBS and 347 457 initiated OMMs). After overlap weighting, baseline covariates were well balanced. Compared with OMMs, MBS was associated with lower 5-year cumulative incidences of nephropathy (4.5% versus 8.3%; -3.8% points; HR 0.55 (95% c.i. 0.52 to 0.60)), retinopathy (3.6% versus 7.4%; -3.8% points; HR 0.60 (95% c.i. 0.55 to 0.65)), MACE (6.1% versus 8.1%; -2.0% points; HR 0.78 (95% c.i. 0.73 to 0.84)), and all-cause mortality (2.1% versus 3.7%; -1.6% points; HR 0.61 (95% c.i. 0.55 to 0.69)). At 1 year, the mean %TWL was greater after MBS (25.4% (95% c.i. 25.3% to 25.5%)) than after OMMs (6.4% (95% c.i. 6.3% to 6.5%)). Among patients with baseline HbA1c ≥6.5%, the proportion achieving HbA1c <6.5% at 1 year was higher after MBS (76.7% (95% c.i. 75.3% to 78.0%)) than after OMMs (47.2% (95% c.i. 46.2% to 48.1%); P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across agent-stratified, competing-risk, landmark, and no-censoring sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Among adults with obesity and T2D, MBS was associated with greater %TWL, higher glycaemic normalization, and lower 5-year risks of nephropathy, retinopathy, MACE, and all-cause mortality compared with real-world initiation of OMMs among patients in clinical equipoise, supporting the role of MBS as a durable therapy in multimodal obesity management.

Title: Early and persistent blood pressure dysregulation in individuals with subacute motor incomplete spinal cord injury.
Journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Blood pressure (BP) dysregulation after spinal cord injury (SCI) may disrupt circadian BP rhythms, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and hypertension. These disturbances are independent predictors of cardiovascular disease, yet evidence in older adults with subacute motor incomplete SCI is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize nocturnal dipping status, BP variability, and daytime and nighttime hypertension at admission to inpatient rehabilitation, and to assess changes during rehabilitation.
UNLABELLED: Observational cohort study.
SETTING: Primary inpatient rehabilitation center.
PARTICIPANTS: Individuals with motor incomplete SCI who completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring shortly after admission and before discharge.
INTERVENTIONS: Not applicable.
OUTCOME MEASURES: Nocturnal dipping (% reduction from nighttime to daytime systolic BP), BP variability, and hypertension defined using general population thresholds.
RESULTS: Participants with motor incomplete SCI were included (n = 34, mean age 61 years, 82% male, 44% cervical injury). At admission, 82% were classified as non-dippers or reverse dippers. High BP variability was present in 59% for systolic BP and 29% for diastolic BP. Hypertension occurred in 21% during daytime and 59% during nighttime. All but one participant exhibited at least one BP-related risk factor. No changes were observed in dipping status, BP variability, and mean BP levels between admission and discharge (all p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Marked BP dysregulation is evident early after motor incomplete SCI, including absent nocturnal dipping, high BP variability, and nocturnal hypertension, despite daytime BP appearing within normal limits in most participants. These disturbances persisted throughout rehabilitation, indicating ongoing autonomic dysregulation that may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk.

Title: Bexagliflozin: pharmacological profile and clinical applications of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor.
Journal: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Bexagliflozin, approved in the United States in 2023, is the fifth selective sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Unlike other class members, it lacks an event-driven cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) and trials with hard kidney or heart failure endpoints. This narrative mini-review separates bexagliflozin-specific evidence from class benefits. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles (January 2009-June 2026) using "bexagliflozin," "Brenzavvy," and "SGLT2 inhibitor," plus prescribing information and pivotal class trials. Randomized trials and meta-analyses were prioritized. Bexagliflozin reduced glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight, and systolic blood pressure vs. placebo and was noninferior to sitagliptin, glimepiride, and, in one 24-week trial, dapagliflozin for HbA1c. In stage 3a/3b chronic kidney disease, it reduced albuminuria by 20.1 % vs. placebo, a surrogate finding. A cardiovascular safety trial and meta-analysis excluded excess cardiovascular risk but were not powered for benefit. Adverse events were consistent with the class. Bexagliflozin is an effective glucose-lowering drug, but its cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure benefits remain unproven and cannot be assumed from class data. Outcome-proven agents are preferred for cardiorenal protection. An adequately powered CVOT and hard kidney endpoint trials are the key research priorities.

Title: Visual Perceptual Learning Based on Adaptive Contrast Detection Training Enhances Vision and Contrast Sensitivity in Diabetic Retinopathy.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy of home-based visual perceptual learning (VPL) on visual function and explore the residual visual plasticity in diabetic retinopathy (DR).
METHODS: Thirty-six DR patients following routine therapies were randomized (1:1). Twenty-eight completed the study (VPL, n = 12; control, n = 16) after excluding eight for poor adherence or incomplete follow-up. The VPL group underwent 3-month home-based grating detection training at individual cutoff spatial frequencies. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), grating acuity (GA), contrast sensitivity to first-order motion stimuli (1stM), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), and Low Vision Quality-of-Life (LVQOL) questionnaire were assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months for the VPL group and at baseline and 3 months for the control group.
RESULTS: BCVA improved from 0.36 to 0.26 logMAR (P = 0.003), GA improved from 12.42 to 17.47 cycles per degree (2.96 dB) and 1stM increased from 64.26 to 83.42 (2.27 dB) in the VPL group. A significant group × time interaction was found for GA (F1, 26 = 63.595, P < 0.001, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.710), 1stM (F1, 26 = 32.663, P < 0.001, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.557), and BCVA (F1, 26 = 10.872, P = 0.003, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.295). The LVQOL score increased (+4.33; P < 0.001) and correlated with ΔGA (r = 0.671, P = 0.017). OCTA parameters remained stable in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: The results reveal significant plasticity in the visual system in DR and suggest that contrast detection training may extend to motion perception tasks. Our study provides additional support for VPL as a potential treatment for DR.

Title: Short 3-month telemedical monitoring is associated only with partial maintenance of functional performance 12 months later: a single-arm study in patients with heart failure in underserved areas.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A 3-month telemedical care model under specialist supervision was associated with an improvement in New York Heart Association (NYHA) class and quality of life in heart failure (HF) population from underserved areas.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate whether the effects of a 3-month telemonitoring intervention (3m-INT) were maintained 12 months later.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, HF patients were enrolled in 5 rural voivodeships and were evaluated after completion of a 3m-INT and 12 months later using the NYHA scale, the Chronic Heart Failure Questionnaire (CHFQ) and the EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale. The clinical composite endpoint (CCE) was death, hospitalization for HF decompensation, stroke, or myocardial infarction.
RESULTS: Of 429 HF patients who completed 3m-INT, 320 (74.6%) were reevaluated 12 months later. Within the 3m-INT, 1 patient died and 6 more during the following 12 months. After 12 months follow-up, CCE occurred in 23 (7.2%) patients while the NYHA class improved in 42 (13.4%) patients, remained unchanged in 131 (41.7%), and deteriorated in 141 (44.9%). Finally, the distribution of NYHA classes at 12 months remained significantly better than at baseline (P <0.001). Atrial fibrillation was independently associated with the occurrence of CCE (P = 0.005). EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale-assessed quality of life did not change (P = 0.36), while CHFQ-measured dyspnea measured by CHFQ deteriorated (P <0.001) after a 1-year observation.
CONCLUSIONS: After 3m-INT followed by 12 months of observation, only partial maintenance of functional performance of HF patients in underserved areas was observed. Atrial fibrillation was associated with an unfavorable clinical effect.

Title: Cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual agonists: from obesity and diabetes to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of all heart failure hospitalisations and is increasing in prevalence, largely driven by obesity and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). Glucagon-like-peptide receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and the dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, tirzepatide, have been shown to be safe and effective medications in the treatment of T2DM and obesity as well as in obesity-related HFpEF.
AREAS COVERED: This review summarises the pathophysiology of obesity-related HFpEF, mechanisms by which GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide may improve symptoms and outcomes, and summarise evidence from recent randomised controlled and observational trials across the disease spectrum they have been studied in. Therapeutic implications and future research directions are also discussed. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) up to August 2025.
EXPERT OPINION: GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide represent a promising therapeutic advance for obesity-related HFpEF. Benefits are likely mediated through weight loss dependent and weight-loss independent mechanisms. Important uncertainties remain regarding their role in non-obese HFpEF, optimal patient selection, and their safety in HFrEF.

Title: Translating microRNAs into clinical laboratory medicine: A critical review of biomarker potential, methodological barriers and implementation pathways.
Journal: Biomedical papers of the Medical Faculty of the University Palacky, Olomouc, Czechoslovakia
Abstract: This critical translational review evaluates the clinical significance of circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) across a broad spectrum of medical disciplines, identifies the main barriers to routine laboratory implementation and proposes a practical roadmap toward clinical use. A structured literature search of PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus covered English-language publications through May 2026. Evidence on preanalytical factors, analytical platforms, absolute quantification, reference interval derivation, clinical validation and translational feasibility of miRNA diagnostics was reviewed across oncology, neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, atherosclerosis, ophthalmology, acute kidney injury, sepsis, metabolic disease, liver disease, autoimmune disease, infectious disease, transplantation, reproductive medicine and toxicology. In multiple clinical domains, miRNAs may reflect pathophysiological processes earlier than established laboratory biomarkers; however, single miRNAs rarely offer disease-specific information. Multimarker panels combined with established biochemical markers demonstrate superior diagnostic and prognostic performance, whereas preanalytical standardization, absolute quantification and prospective clinical validation remain critical unmet needs. Reference intervals for eight cardiovascularly relevant miRNAs, determined in whole blood by the miREIA immunoassay, provide a first step toward routine implementation. Routine implementation of miRNA diagnostics therefore requires a five-stage laboratory medicine framework: preanalytical standardization, analytical validation with absolute quantification, biological reference data, prospective clinical validation and demonstration of clinical and economic utility beyond existing biomarkers.

Title: Comparison of modeling strategies to study the effect of an exposure on changes in continuous outcomes: evaluating the impact of alcohol consumption on changes in cardiometabolic health markers based on the German National Cohort (NAKO).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: When investigating effects of baseline exposures on changes in continuous outcomes in longitudinal studies, the change-score model is increasingly recommended, while baseline adjustment is debated. Limited empirical evidence exists on the extent to which these choices matter. We examined how different modeling strategies influence estimated effects using alcohol and prospective changes in cardiometabolic health markers as an example.
METHODS: We used data from the German National Cohort (NAKO; ∼205 000 participants at baseline, ∼140 000 at 4-5-year follow-up). Participants reported alcohol consumption at baseline (2014-19) and were classified as light, moderate, heavy, former, or never drinkers. Triglycerides (TG), systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP and DBP), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and glycated hemoglobin were measured at baseline and 5 years later. Longitudinal effects were estimated using a change-score model informed by directed acyclic graphs without baseline adjustment, and compared to a baseline-adjusted model and a model that adjusted for the average of baseline and follow-up (Oldham's). Statistical tests assessed whether changes in the outcome depended on baseline levels.
RESULTS: Change-score and Oldham's models produced highly consistent results across all five cardiometabolic markers, whereas baseline-adjusted change-score models yielded different results for all. Statistical tests assessing the relationship between baseline levels and subsequent change did not indicate whether baseline adjustment would materially alter the results. Based on the change-score models, former drinkers had lower 5-year TG change and higher SBP, DBP, and HDL-C changes compared with light drinkers, while heavy drinkers had lower DBP change.
CONCLUSION: When exposure precedes the baseline outcome, baseline adjustment in change-score analyses may substantially alter effect estimates.

Title: Subcutaneous Furosemide for Ambulatory Decongestion in Heart Failure: Outcomes From a High-Risk Real-World Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Volume overload remains a primary driver of heart failure hospitalization (HFH). Diuretic resistance limits the efficacy of oral loop diuretics during decompensation, often necessitating intravenous therapy. Subcutaneous (SC) furosemide (Furoscix, 80 mg/10 mL) represents a novel outpatient alternative for patients who remain symptomatic despite oral diuretic therapy.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical outcomes of SC furosemide in ambulatory heart failure (HF) patients inadequately managed with oral loop diuretics.
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of HF patients prescribed SC furosemide as an adjunct to oral loop diuretics between May 2023 and 2025. The primary outcome was HFH within 30 days of initiation. Secondary outcomes included a composite of HFH or urgent care or emergency department visits requiring intravenous diuresis, change in body weight, and New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class.
RESULTS: Fifty patients met the inclusion criteria; one was excluded for incomplete follow-up. SC furosemide was prescribed as two to three doses per week. Within 30 days, 10 patients (20.4%) experienced HFH; six had been hospitalized in the preceding 30 days, suggesting a high-risk baseline cohort. The composite endpoint occurred in 16 patients (32.7%). Among patients who avoided hospitalization, median NYHA class improved from III to II, and mean body weight decreased by 2.6 kg (5.7 lbs). Adverse events were infrequent; no deaths occurred within the 30-day follow-up period.
CONCLUSION: In ambulatory HF patients with persistent congestion despite oral diuretic therapy, SC furosemide was well tolerated and associated with improvements in functional status and volume burden.

Title: Joint Associations of Cumulative Triglyceride-Glucose-A Body Shape Index and Frailty Trajectories With Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Middle-Aged and Older Chinese Adults.
Abstract:
AIM: To examine the independent and joint associations of cumulative triglyceride-glucose-a body shape index (TyG-ABSI) and frailty trajectories with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) in middle-aged and older Chinese adults.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. We calculated cumulative TyG-ABSI as the mean of fasting measurements in 2011 and 2015; we identified frailty trajectories from frailty-index measurements in 2011, 2013, and 2015 using latent class linear mixed models. Survey-ascertained incident CVD was a newly reported physician diagnosis of heart disease or stroke in 2018 or 2020. We used complementary log-log discrete-time survival models with cluster-robust standard errors because exact onset dates were unavailable.
RESULTS: Among 3026 participants, 606 met the study definition of incident CVD. Each 1-SD increase in cumulative TyG-ABSI was associated with higher CVD risk (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.06-1.26), and the higher frailty trajectory was associated with greater risk (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.53-2.39). Relative to low TyG-ABSI/lower frailty, HRs were 1.26 (95% CI 1.04-1.53), 1.87 (1.34-2.61), and 2.43 (1.79-3.29) for high/lower, low/higher, and high/higher groups. Multiplicative and additive interactions were not significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative TyG-ABSI and frailty trajectory were independently associated with survey-ascertained incident CVD. Their joint distribution showed a cumulative risk gradient without statistical synergy. These observational findings support complementary risk stratification, not a validated clinical threshold or causal effect.

Title: The interplay of fibrinogen and lipoprotein(a) with 20-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk: a path analysis within the ATTICA study (2002-2022).
Abstract:
AIMS: Elevated levels of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and fibrinogen are known risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and their combined elevation in high-risk individuals may amplify risk. However, the long-term impact of this combination on ASCVD incidence in a primary prevention setting remains unclear. This study sought to examine the association between the combination of Lp(a) and fibrinogen with long-term ASCVD risk, in apparently healthy adults from the general population.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A cohort of 3042 CVD-free adults residing in greater Athens, Greece, was recruited in 2002. A 20-year follow-up was conducted in 2022, comprising n = 2169 participants, of which n = 1988 had complete data for cardiovascular disease incidence. Participants were divided into four groups, using a recommended threshold of 30 mg/dL for Lp(a) and the median value of 303 mg/dL for fibrinogen. In the overall cohort, fibrinogen was associated with higher ASCVD risk [hazard ratio (HR) per 10 mg/dL: 1.040, 95%CI:1.009-1.072]. Upon stratification by Lp(a) levels, the significant association was retained and amplified only in individuals with elevated Lp(a) levels (HR 1.083, 95%CI:1.009-1.162) (P for interaction=0.041). Participants with both elevated Lp(a) and fibrinogen levels demonstrated the highest 20-year ASCVD risk (HR 1.904, 95%CI [1.023, 3.547]). Path analysis revealed a mediating role of fibrinogen in the inflammation [i.e. interleukin-6 (IL-6)]-ASCVD risk association, which become more pronounced at higher Lp(a) concentrations.
CONCLUSION: In this general population study, elevated levels of Lp(a) and fibrinogen jointly conferred a higher long-term risk of ASCVD than either marker alone, potentially through the complex involvement of inflammation.

Title: Management of aspirin in lumbar fusion: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The perioperative management of acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) in spine surgery remains a daily clinical dilemma. While ASA discontinuation is traditionally recommended to minimize bleeding risk, cessation may expose patients with cardiovascular comorbidities to thromboembolic complications. In the absence of clear evidence-based guidelines, neurosurgeons frequently rely on institutional practices or personal judgment.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were searched for studies published from January 2000 to September 2025 comparing perioperative ASA use versus no ASA in adult lumbar fusion surgery. Random-effects models calculated mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I.
RESULTS: Four observational studies including 700 patients (316 ASA, 384 controls) were analyzed. ASA continuation or discontinuation did not significantly affect intraoperative blood loss (MD 31.29 mL; 95% CI -2.89 to 65.47; P=0.07), postoperative drainage, operative time, or hospital stay. Subgroup analysis stratified by timing of ASA discontinuation (≤3 days vs. ≥7 days) revealed no significant differences within or between subgroups. Complication rates, morbidity, and mortality were comparable across treatment arms.
CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of low-dose ASA during lumbar fusion does not appear to increase perioperative bleeding, complications, or mortality. Given the potential cardiovascular risks of interruption, discontinuation should be reserved for carefully selected patients following multidisciplinary evaluation and individualized risk assessment. However, the available evidence in this field is limited by retrospective designs and small sample sizes, requiring further high-quality prospective trials to confirm these findings.

Title: Nomogram to predict aneurysmal origin of intracranial subarachnoid hemorrhage: suggesting a user-friendly tool for clinical decision making.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While aneurysm rupture is the most common etiology of intracranial subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH), up to about 20% of cases are reported to be of non-aneurysmal origin or angiogram negative (anSAH). There currently is lack of practical prediction systems to aid in clinical decision making after initial negative angiogram to optimize patient disposition and clinical management. Our objective was to develop a predictive nomogram tool incorporating significant clinical and radiographic predictors of aSAH.
METHODS: Demographic, clinical, and radiographic data from sequential non-traumatic SAH patients from institutional database were retrospectively collected and analyzed. Univariate and multivariable statistical analyses were performed yielding significant SAH origin predictors that were incorporated into a predictive nomogram.
RESULTS: A total of 167 SAH subjects were identified and randomly split into the training and validation cohorts. Five models were generated to predict aneurysmal origin of SAH. The model including Hunt and Hess grade, modified Fisher grade, and hemorrhage presence/absence in the prepontine cistern, suprasellar cistern, interhemispheric fissure and foramen magnum demonstrated the highest predictive value (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.843, pseudo-R2=0.222). A corresponding graphical nomogram was developed with C-Index of 0.843.
CONCLUSIONS: Our nomogram tool incorporates easily identifiable factors assessing the risk of aneurysmal origin of SAH upon patient's initial presentation. The nomogram can be easily implemented in large, multicenter studies as a point-of-care setting tool aiding in clinical decision making in cases of anSAH.

Title: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol above 1 mmol/L is associated with 50% higher risk of coronary artery disease.
Abstract:
AIMS: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) leads to lifelong elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and increased risk of coronary artery disease. We tested the hypothesis that elevated remnant cholesterol additionally increases cardiovascular risk in FH.
METHODS: In the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and UK Biobank, 108,751 and 428,625 individuals were classified as with or without FH according to clinical scores and genetic mutations. In the two cohorts, 7,708 and 50,997 experienced coronary artery disease, respectively.
RESULTS: In CGPS and UK Biobank, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) was observed in 12% and 11% of individuals without FH (N = 104,226 and 403,172), in 33% and 40% with Simon Broome FH (N = 3,923 and 23,860), in 44% and 78% with MEDPED FH (N = 1,005 and 2,465), in 33% and 34% with DLCN FH (N = 744 and 1,207), and in 12% and 21% of individuals with genetic FH (N = 188 and 875). Likewise in the CGPS and UK Biobank, the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for coronary artery disease by remnant cholesterol ≥1 vs. < 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) were 1.49 (95% CI: 1.39-1.59) and 1.47 (1.43-1.52) in individuals without FH, 1.59 (1.31-1.93) and 1.18 (1.10-1.27) in Simon Broome FH, 1.50 (1.08-2.08) and 1.14 (0.89-1.45) in MEDPED FH, 1.60 (1.17-2.21) and 1.59 (1.20-2.09) in DLCN FH, and 1.48 (0.59-3.69) and 1.39 (0.88-2.19) in genetic FH.
CONCLUSION: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) vs below is associated with ≈50% higher risk of coronary artery disease, that is, above the already high risk due to lifelong genetically elevated LDL cholesterol.

Title: Distinct Doppler echocardiographic patterns of elevated left ventricular filling pressure in acute decompensated heart failure and AMI-related cardiogenic shock: a simultaneous Doppler-hemodynamic study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Doppler echocardiography supports noninvasive hemodynamic assessment, but its interpretation may vary across acute heart failure syndromes. We compared Doppler filling patterns and their relationship with pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) and acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS).
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single-center observational study included 61 patients with ADHF (n = 34) or AMI-CS (n = 27) who underwent contemporaneous echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic assessment. Transmitral inflow, pulmonary venous flow, and tissue Doppler indices were compared between groups and analyzed in relation to PCWP. Exploratory ROC analyses assessed discrimination of PCWP ≥ 18 mmHg.
RESULTS: Patients with ADHF had greater cardiac chamber enlargement and higher mean PCWP than those with AMI-CS (24.7 ± 8.4 vs. 18.0 ± 5.4 mmHg; p < 0.001). ADHF was characterized by higher E/A (2.8 ± 1.2 vs. 1.3 ± 1.2; p < 0.001), lower pulmonary venous S/D (0.7 ± 0.5 vs. 1.1 ± 0.5; p < 0.01), and higher average E/e' (21.0 ± 7.3 vs. 12.5 ± 4.7; p < 0.001). Deceleration time did not differ significantly. Average and septal E/e' correlated with PCWP in the pooled cohort but not within either group separately. Septal E/e' yielded AUCs of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.722-1.000) in ADHF and 0.762 (95% CI, 0.511-1.000) in AMI-CS.
CONCLUSIONS: ADHF and AMI-CS exhibit distinct Doppler filling profiles alongside differences in invasive filling pressure and cardiac remodeling. These findings support contextual interpretation of Doppler indices during bedside hemodynamic assessment of critically ill patients. The diagnostic value of syndrome-specific interpretation requires independent validation.

Title: The American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association classification of chronic hypertension in pregnancy has better clinical applicability and risk assessment than the traditional severe and mild hypertension approach - lessons from a population-based study.
Journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hypertension (CHTN) increases the risk of superimposed preeclampsia, contributing to maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. Accurate hypertension classification is therefore essential for risk stratification, antenatal surveillance, prevention, and outcomes. The clinical impact of applying the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) classification, compared with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) criteria, in pregnancy remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the impact of ACC/AHA versus ACOG hypertension classifications on the prevalence of CHTN and pregnancy outcomes.
STUDY DESIGN: This population-based retrospective cohort study used a computerized maternity database from a tertiary hospital. All parturients with singleton gestations initiating prenatal care in the first trimester were included (n = 136,606). CHTN was categorized according to ACOG and ACC/AHA criteria. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed using R-Studio, with ANOVA and Poisson regression models evaluating associations between CHTN severity and outcomes.
RESULTS: The prevalence of CHTN was 2.9% (4,127/137,606) by ACOG criteria and 3.9% (5,424/137,606) by ACC/AHA criteria (p < 0.001). Under ACOG classification, both mild and severe range CHTN were independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (RR 4.15, 95% CI 3.69-4.65; and RR 3.19, 95% CI 2.82-3.59, respectively). Using ACC/AHA criteria, elevated blood pressure (EBP), stage 1 CHTN (S1CHTN), and stage 2 CHTN (S2CHTN) were each independently associated with preeclampsia or eclampsia (EBP: RR 2.34, 95% CI 2.04-2.65; S1CHTN: RR 4.00, 95% CI 3.56-4.50; S2CHTN: RR 3.32, 95% CI 2.88-3.80). Mild CHTN, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were independently associated with small-for-gestational-age neonates, while both ACOG-defined CHTN and ACC/AHA-defined EBP, S1CHTN, and S2CHTN were associated with preterm birth.
CONCLUSION: Application of the ACC/AHA classification identifies a larger proportion of pregnant individuals as having CHTN. Notably, even those with elevated blood pressure had a two-fold increased risk of preeclampsia compared with the general obstetric population. These findings support the clinical relevance of the ACC/AHA classification in pregnancy and suggest that its implementation may improve identification of patients who may benefit from targeted preeclampsia prevention strategies.

Title: Cross-Ancestry Portability of a Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Polygenic Score in a Diverse US Cohort.
The triglyceride-glucose index in decompensated heart failure: A marker of insulin resistance or reverse lipid epidemiology? Insights from the HEROES registry.
Drug acquisition accounts for a minor share of the costs associated with dobutamine-milrinone escalation in cardiogenic shock: a propensity-weighted cost analysis from Indonesia.
Journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adding milrinone to dobutamine (dobutamine-milrinone escalation) in cardiogenic shock (CS) is reimbursed for a limited duration under Indonesia's national health insurance, but its cost structure is poorly characterized. This study quantified direct medical charges associated with escalation and the contribution of drug acquisition.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort of 76 adult CS survivors (20 escalation, 56 dobutamine monotherapy) at Indonesia's national cardiovascular referral center, 2020-2024. Covariate Balancing Propensity Score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting, using pre-treatment covariates, estimated adjusted cost ratios (CR) for intensive cardiovascular care unit (ICVCU) and total hospital costs from institutional billing records.
RESULTS: Escalation was associated with higher ICVCU costs (CR 2.711; 95% CI 1.912-3.844; p<0.001) and total hospital costs (CR 2.321; 95% CI 1.372-3.929; p= 0.002). Combined inotrope costs represented 4.3% of ICVCU expenditure in the escalation group, versus 30.9% for therapeutic and interventional procedures. Baseline vasoactive-inotropic score correlated with total hospital cost (ρ=0.597; p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Drug acquisition represented a minor share of costs associated with escalation. The findings support consideration of severity- and resource-based reimbursement approaches rather than focusing solely on duration limits for individual inotropes. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective, single-center, survivor-only design.

Title: Effectiveness of a physical literacy intervention program for young and middle-aged adults with hypertension: a mixed-methods quasi-experimental study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether a theoretically grounded, 8-week physical literacy intervention incorporating salutogenic model components (sense of coherence, social support, and self-efficacy) could improve physical activity levels and clinical outcomes in young and middle-aged adults with Grade 1 hypertension, and to explore participants' subjective experiences of the program.
METHODS: A mixed-methods quasi-experimental study was conducted between August and October 2024. Forty patients aged 18-59 years were recruited from a community healthcare center and allocated to the intervention group (n = 20) or control group (n = 20). The intervention group received a multidimensional physical-literacy program, while the control group received usual care. Five participants were lost to follow-up; 35 (intervention: n = 17; control: n = 18) completed all three assessments: baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1), and one-month follow-up (T2). Quantitative outcomes (SBP, BMI, physical-literacy scores, social support, sense of coherence, self-efficacy, and physical activity) were analyzed using independent t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for between-group comparisons and paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for within-group changes, with significance set at α = 0.05 (two-tailed). Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews were analyzed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 40 recruited participants, 35 (87.5%) completed the study. Post-intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (SBP), body weight, and BMI compared to baseline (all P < 0.05). Significant improvements were also observed in PL scores, social support, sense of coherence, and self-efficacy (P < 0.05). Qualitative findings corroborated these results, highlighting enhanced health literacy and stress alleviation, despite some logistical challenges.
CONCLUSION: The PL intervention is a feasible and effective strategy to improve health outcomes and psychosocial resilience in hypertensive adults, offering a promising approach for community-based chronic disease management.

Title: Extended-release guanfacine overdose in a pediatric emergency department: a systematic review and a 10-year retrospective chart review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize clinical presentations, management strategies and outcomes associated with extended-release guanfacine (ER guanfacine) overdose in pediatric patients presenting to a tertiary care pediatric emergency department (ED) supplemented with a systematic review of published pediatric cases.
METHODS: A retrospective chart review included patients aged 0 to 18 years presenting with guanfacine overdose to a tertiary pediatric ED between August 2013 and July 2023. Data were extracted on demographics, cause of overdose, clinical features, management and outcomes. Concurrently, a systematic review using the population, exposure, and outcome approach searched MEDLINE and Embase (1974-November 2025) to consolidate existing case-report evidence on emergent management of guanfacine overdose in pediatric patients.
RESULTS: Ten studies met inclusion criteria, describing eleven pediatric cases, mostly accidental with ingestions in younger children, with bradycardia and hypotension reported frequently.Management was supportive; naloxone produced variable benefit, and when used no deaths occurred. For the retrospective cohort, (n = 15; median age 14), 73% involved intentional ingestions and were frequently associated with psychiatric comorbidities. Bradycardia and hypotension were nearly universal; with some patients demonstrating transient hypertension. Treatment included intravenous fluids (87%) and atropine for symptomatic bradycardia (20%). Three patients required pediatric intensive care unit admission; none received naloxone. All patients recovered fully without mortality.
CONCLUSION: ER guanfacine overdose most commonly affects adolescents with underlying mental health conditions and presents with clinically significant cardiovascular depression. Management is supportive, emphasizing fluid resuscitation and cardiac monitoring. Findings support the need for standardized ED care pathways and integrated mental-health interventions.

Title: Cirrhotic Cardiomyopathy and Related Cardiocirculatory Dysfunction: A Systematic Review of Therapeutic Responses and Cardiorenal Outcomes.
Abstract: Cardiocirculatory dysfunction in cirrhosis encompasses impaired cardiac reserve, diastolic dysfunction, systemic vasodilation, neurohormonal activation, and progressive reliance on compensatory cardiac activity. This systematic review evaluated how pharmacological interventions affecting cardiac function, vascular tone, effective circulating volume, or natriuretic signaling influence cardiovascular, renal, and clinical outcomes in adults with cirrhosis. MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched for clinical studies published from August 1, 2016, through July 31, 2026. Eligibility was structured according to the Population, Intervention, Comparator, and Outcomes (PICO) framework, and study selection followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Five studies involving 465 participants were included in a narrative synthesis. Metoprolol did not restore impaired cardiac reserve or improve cardiac morphology in established cirrhotic cardiomyopathy. In refractory ascites, propranolol suppressed sympathetic support of systolic function, reduced renal perfusion pressure, and impaired renal function. Conversely, carvedilol-based targeted heart-rate reduction, with ivabradine added when required, improved left ventricular diastolic function and was associated with fewer episodes of acute kidney injury and hepatic encephalopathy, although mortality was not significantly reduced in the randomized comparison. Ularitide caused clinically important reductions in blood pressure, decreased urine output, and increased adverse reactions, while targeted albumin therapy did not improve cardiovascular biomarkers, renal dysfunction, or survival. The four randomized study results raised some concerns about bias, while the nonrandomized study had moderate risk of bias. These findings indicate that cardiovascular interventions in cirrhosis cannot be characterized as uniformly beneficial or harmful. Their effects may depend on disease severity, cardiac phenotype, and the extent to which sympathetic and hemodynamic compensation is required to preserve systemic and renal perfusion. Prospective, phenotype-stratified trials integrating cardiac, systemic, and renal endpoints are needed before individualized treatment strategies can be recommended.

Title: Plasma Osteoprotegerin and Cardiovascular Mortality During the First Two Years of Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Prospective Observational Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIM: We performed this study to determine the cardiovascular-cause mortality rate and the predictive value of the plasma osteoprotegerin (OPG) concentration for cardiovascular-cause mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) during the first 2 years.
METHODS: We performed a prospective observational cohort study of 218 ESKD patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis from September 2021 to September 2025. Plasma OPG concentrations were quantified using a colorimetric measurement method based on ELISA method. Cardiovascular-cause mortality data were collected over 2 years of follow-up. All patients were divided into 2 groups: the survival group (n = 187) and the mortality group (n = 31).
RESULTS: The incidence of cardiovascular-cause mortality was 14.2% over 2 years of follow-up. Compared with survivors, patients who died from cardiovascular causes had significantly lower HDL-C levels and higher PTH, hs-CRP, and OPG levels (p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, higher OPG levels were independently associated with increased cardiovascular mortality (HR = 1.050, p < 0.001). OPG showed good discriminatory performance for cardiovascular mortality (AUC = 0.828, p < 0.001), and Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly higher mortality among patients with OPG levels > 47.95 pmol/L (log-rank p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The cardiovascular-cause mortality rate during the first 2 years of maintenance hemodialysis was 14.2%. Plasma OPG levels are associated with cardiovascular mortality, suggesting its potential as a useful biomarker for risk stratification in ESKD patients.

Title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.

Title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Analysis and Interpretation of Intravascular Ultrasound in Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) leads to considerable morbidity and mortality worldwide. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is an imaging modality to guide percutaneous coronary intervention; however, it requires time-consuming, expert-dependent manual analysis. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly used for IVUS analysis, but there is limited evidence on its diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility. This review aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical usefulness of AI for automated IVUS analysis of coronary arteries. The research protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO, CRD420261454806) and followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines for systematic reviews. PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through July 23, 2026, and July 26, 2026, respectively, for publications assessing AI, machine learning, or deep learning algorithms for the automated analysis of coronary IVUS, including segmentation of structures, identification of plaque types, and quantitative measurements.
