Two reviewers independently screened and selected eligible studies and extracted the data. The risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 (Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2) and visualized using robvis, and the GRADE approach was used to rate the certainty of evidence. Of the 802 records identified (PubMed, n = 216; Cochrane CENTRAL, n = 586), eight studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in this review. They reported on the performance of convolutional neural networks, U-Net/U-Net++, Efficient-UNet, DeepLabv3+-based models, and gradient boosting in segmenting lumen, vessel, plaque, and stent in coronary IVUS. The Dice similarity coefficient ranged from 0.67 to 0.97, and the intersection over union for segmentation (including Jaccard similarity) ranged from 0.66 to 0.97, with the best performance for lumen and vessel segmentation and the poorest for stent and calcium. The sensitivity and specificity ranged from 62% to 90% and 88% to 99%, respectively, with the correlation to expert assessment generally above 0.9. Overall, the risk of bias was mainly related to patient selection (five out of eight studies) and the reference standard (three out of eight studies), and none of the studies was rated as having a high risk of bias. Due to between-study heterogeneity in the tasks, reference standards, and outcome measures, a meta-analysis was not performed, and the certainty of evidence was rated as low. The current evidence suggests that AI-based methods have good potential for analyzing coronary IVUS with acceptable accuracy, which could be helpful for high-throughput IVUS interpretation in clinical practice. They appear to perform best at segmenting lumen and vessel structures and worst at segmenting stent and calcium. However, due to the overall low certainty of evidence from these mostly retrospective studies, their use should be limited to complementing the work of experts in cardiovascular medicine.

Title: Endovascular Therapy in Intracranial Atherosclerotic Stenosis-Related Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Brief Practice Update and Consensus Statement From the SVIN.
Abstract: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis-related large vessel occlusion (ICAS-LVO) represents a distinct subset of acute ischemic stroke with unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges during endovascular therapy. Compared with embolic LVO, ICAS-LVO is associated with higher rates of reocclusion and the frequent use of adjunctive interventions. This Brief Practice Update summarizes current evidence and expert consensus to guide the identification and management of ICAS-LVO during endovascular therapy. The Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards committee convened a multidisciplinary writing group of neurointerventionalists to review available literature and define key clinical questions on ICAS-LVO and endovascular therapy. Evidence was appraised using the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology framework for Class of Recommendation and Level of Evidence, adapted from the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association. Draft statements were iteratively refined and approved by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Guidelines and Practice Standards Quality Committee for adherence to internal standards and endorsed by the Society of Vascular and Interventional Neurology Board of Directors. Evidence was derived from randomized trials, multicenter registries, cohort studies, post hoc analyses, and meta-analyses addressing diagnostic features, first-line thrombectomy strategies, and adjunctive therapies in ICAS-LVO. Both stent retriever and direct aspiration approaches are acceptable initial strategies; however, durable recanalization is only achieved in about half of patients. Adjunctive use of intravenous or intra-arterial glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors, balloon angioplasty, and rescue stenting has demonstrated improved recanalization rates and favorable functional outcomes in observational studies, without increased hemorrhagic complications. However, the quality of evidence remains weak. A summary of recommendations is provided to guide practice in common procedural scenarios. This Brief Practice Update provides evidence-based and expert consensus recommendations for the diagnosis and endovascular treatment of ICAS-LVO. Management should be individualized by incorporating the clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and operator expertise. While adjunctive therapy may be beneficial in select cases, high-quality randomized trials are needed to define optimal strategies and establish standardized algorithms for this challenging stroke subtype.
Category: Randomized Controlled Trials; Observational Studies; Guidelines & Statements

Title: Predictive Value of P-Wave Dispersion Combined with Left Atrial Reservoir Strain for Incident Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). This study aimed to investigate the associations of P-wave dispersion (PD) and left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) with incident AF.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 165 consecutive patients with HCM who were diagnosed at Liaoning Provincial People's Hospital from January 2018 to January 2026. Independent predictors of incident AF were identified using multivariable Cox regression. Model performance was assessed using a nomogram, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1.79 years, 56 (33.9%) patients developed incident AF. PD (P=0.025) and LASr (P=0.028) were independently associated with incident AF. The combined PD + LASr model showed AUCs of 0.766, 0.764, and 0.823 at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. The model showed good calibration at 3 years and positive net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a significantly higher cumulative incidence of AF in the high-risk group than in the low-risk group (log-rank P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: PD and LASr are independently associated with AF risk in patients with HCM, and their combination may improve AF risk assessment.

Title: MHR and AIP as Differential Predictors of 1-Year Major Adverse Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events After Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Combined Model Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the predictive value of monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR), plasma atherogenic index (AIP), and baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score for 1-year major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) after acute ischemic stroke, and to explore potential differences in their predictive patterns across endpoint subtypes.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 429 elderly patients (≥65 years) with acute ischemic stroke admitted to Lu'an People's Hospital (Anhui, China) between January 2020 and September 2023. Clinical and laboratory data were collected; MHR and AIP were Z-standardized. Patients were followed for 1 year for MACCE (stroke recurrence, all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction/angina). Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression (Enter method: full model, then parsimonious model). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong tests compared individual and combined (MHR+AIP+baseline NIHSS) models. Endpoint-specific analyses were exploratory. Bootstrap resampling was performed for internal validation.
RESULTS: MACCE occurred in 115 patients (26.8%), comprising 58 stroke recurrences, 41 deaths, and 17 coronary events. MHR (per 1-SD increase: OR=2.765, 95% CI: 2.062-3.707, P<0.001), AIP (per 1-SD increase: OR=1.682, 95% CI: 1.289-2.193, P<0.001), and Baseline NIHSS score (OR=1.170, 95% CI: 1.108-1.235, P<0.001) were independent predictors of MACCE. In exploratory endpoint-specific analyses, MHR was associated with all three subtypes, while AIP was associated with stroke recurrence and coronary events but not all-cause mortality. However, formal interaction tests were underpowered. AUCs were 0.731 (MHR), 0.628 (AIP), 0.646 (NIHSS), and 0.810 (combined); the combined model outperformed all individual markers (all P<0.05 by DeLong test).
CONCLUSION: MHR and AIP independently predict 1-year MACCE in elderly stroke patients. The observed differences in their associations across endpoint subtypes are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; formal interaction tests or adequately powered prospective studies are required. The combined model may improve risk stratification, but requires prospective validation.

Title: Cardiovascular Events Among Female Users of Osteoporosis Treatments: A Cohort Study in United Kingdom Primary Care Data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Information on cardiovascular disease (CVD) safety of osteoporosis treatments is important for patients and clinicians choosing between treatment options.
METHODS: We conducted a cohort study in the United Kingdom Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and linked inpatient data (2000-2020). We selected two cohorts of female patients aged 40-89 with no history of CVD: (1) treated cohort: new users of study drugs (alendronate, ibandronate, risedronate, zoledronic acid, etidronate, denosumab, raloxifene, teriparatide, and calcitonin); (2) common reference cohort: prescription vitamin D users with a diagnosis or monitoring for osteoporotic disease. We followed patients from first prescription through censor date (event, major comorbidity, age 90, or end of record) and estimated adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRRs) of atrial fibrillation (AFib), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and fatal stroke, by study drug compared to vitamin D-only. We assessed aIRRs compared to the common referent across all osteoporosis treatments.
RESULTS: Among 226,484 (74%) patients in the treated cohort and 79,973 (26%) in the vitamin D-only referent cohort, there were 4313 AFib, 7312 stroke, and 3846 MI outcomes. AFib rates were highest in zoledronic acid users (13 outcomes; aIRR 1.87; 95% CI 1.08-3.24). MI incidence was highest among ibandronate users (63 outcomes; aIRR 1.50; 95% CI 1.16-1.95). There were no differences in rates of AFib or MI across other study drugs or for stroke or fatal stroke for any study drug.
CONCLUSION: Rates of AFib, MI and stroke were similar across most osteoporosis treatments, including between various types of bisphosphonates. However, the rate of AFib was increased among zoledronic acid users and rate of MI was somewhat increased among ibandronate users. However, findings were generally limited by small numbers of exposed outcomes.

Title: D-dimer/NT-proBNP ratio in acute pulmonary embolism patients stratifies risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are ongoing efforts to identify patients at risk of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during acute pulmonary embolism (APE). Lower D-dimer levels and right heart overload at APE diagnosis were reported to predict CTEPH. We hypothesised that plasma D-dimer to N-terminal pro-B type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ratio assessed during APE may be useful for early CTEPH screening.
METHODS: We followed 342 APE survivors (median age 64.5 years, female 56.1%), for a median of 39 (25-64) months.
RESULTS: Despite ≥3 months anticoagulation CTEPH was diagnosed in 22 (6.4%) patients (CTEPH(+)). At APE diagnosis, CTEPH(+) compared with subjects without this sequela (CTEPH(-)) presented with advanced right ventricular overload: increased tricuspid regurgitation peak gradient (TRPG) (46.5 mmHg versus 32.0 mmHg; p<0.001) and NT-proBNP (1860 ng·L-1 versus 515 ng·L-1; p=0.02). Despite no differences in plasma D-dimer (4210 μg·L-1 versus 5330 μg·L-1; p=0.10), the ratio of D-dimer to NT-proBNP (DD/NT-proBNP) was significantly lower in the CTEPH(+) cohort versus the CTEPH(-) cohort (2.89 μg·ng-1 versus 12.0 μg·ng-1; p<0.001). In patients with DD/NT-proBNP≤10 CTEPH was diagnosed in 20 cases (11.7%), whereas in the group with DD/NT-proBNP> 10 CTEPH could only be detected in 2 of 171 cases (1.2%) with an OR 0.09 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.38; p=0.0013), a sensitivity of 90.9% (95% CI 70.8-98.9%), a specificity 52.8% (95% CI 47.2-58.4%), a negative predictive value 98.8% (95% CI 95.8-99.9%), a and positive predictive value of 11.7% (95% CI 7.3-17.5%). Combination of DD/NT-proBNP≤10 with TRPG≥36 mmHg detected in 87 patients, including 17 patients with CTEPH (19.5% CTEPH incidence).
CONCLUSION: DD/NT-proBNP>10 μg·ng-1 identifies patients with a low risk of subsequent CTEPH diagnosis, whereas DD/NT-proBNP≤10, especially presenting TRPG≥36 mmHg at echocardiography, forms a high risk group at follow-up.

Title: Strategies to reduce microvascular obstruction and infarct size in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Abstract: Microvascular obstruction (MVO) remains a major challenge in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), as adequate myocardial reperfusion may not be achieved despite successful epicardial recanalization with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI). MVO results from multiple interacting mechanisms, including distal embolization, ischemia-reperfusion injury, inflammation, oxidative stress, and microvascular dysfunction, and is associated with larger infarct size and worse clinical outcomes. This review summarizes current and emerging strategies for the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of MVO in STEMI. Advances in cardiac imaging and invasive or angiography-derived assessment of the coronary microcirculation may improve early identification and risk stratification. Therapeutic approaches include pharmacological and device-based strategies targeting thrombotic burden and distal embolization, reperfusion injury, inflammation, and oxidative stress. However, despite encouraging results for selected interventions, available evidence remains heterogeneous and no specific therapy has become standard of care for MVO. These findings highlight the need to move beyond a uniform approach to MVO. Integration of early diagnosis with identification of the predominant pathophysiological mechanism may provide a framework for future phenotype- and endotype-guided therapeutic strategies delivered within the appropriate therapeutic window. Whether such an approach can improve myocardial reperfusion and clinical outcomes after STEMI requires evaluation in adequately powered prospective trials.

Title: A multimodal optimisation framework for cardiac electrophysiology model personalisation using computed tomography and 12-lead electrocardiogram: Algorithm development and validation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Accurate parameterisation of cardiac patient-specific models is a major challenge. Here we aimed to test the feasibility of an optimised multimodal personalisation framework that combines structural information from computed tomography (CT) and 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) features, for high-fidelity simulations of ventricular tachycardia (VT).
METHODS: We studied a small cohort of six patients who had CT images and sinus-rhythm 12-lead ECGs available prior to VT ablation. The CT images were used to construct patient-specific biventricular simulation domains and to estimate ECG lead positions. We implemented a graphics processing unit-based computational pipeline and a two-stage optimisation framework consisting of: (i) an early activation onset estimation; and, (ii) the optimisation of conductivity parameter. For validation, the simulation outcomes were compared to clinical VT patterns and cycle lengths.
RESULTS: Following early onset estimations, simulated 12-lead ECG signals achieved a 91.20 % mean Q wave, R wave, and S wave (QRS) peak accuracy. Using the optimised parameters, average QRS duration error was reduced to 3.94 ms, compared to 37.42 ms for baseline parameters. Notably, in four patients with available electro-anatomical VT maps, simulations reproduced the clinical VT patterns and cycle length closer to recordings than those obtained with baseline parameterisation.
CONCLUSION: Our pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of a robust electrophysiology modelling framework able to perform multimodal personalisation by integrating sinus-rhythm ECGs and cardiac CT images for VT simulations with tractable computational time, paving the way for its clinical translation and a less invasive scar-related VT risk assessment.

Title: Factors associated with in-hospital mortality after stroke at a tertiary hospital in Angola.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most Angolan patients with stroke reach hospital beyond the thrombolysis window, and many deaths occur within 72 h of admission. We investigated routinely recorded variables associated with in-hospital mortality at Hospital do Prenda.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study at Hospital do Prenda, a public tertiary hospital in Luanda, from January 2023 to December 2025. The unit of analysis was the hospitalisation episode; four episodes ending in transfer were excluded. Hypertension and type 2 diabetes were extracted from free-text fields using predefined string rules. Univariable analyses used Pearson chi-square, crude odds ratios (OR; 95% CI), and Mann-Whitney tests. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, year, stroke subtype, recorded comorbidities, and head-CT status. Given the low events-per-variable ratio (~7) and poor calibration in some models, adjusted estimates were considered exploratory associations rather than independent prognostic effects.
RESULTS: Among 479 episodes, 75 patients died (15.7%; 95% CI 12.7-19.2). Median age was 58.5 years among decedents versus 52.0 among survivors (p = 0.049). Median length of stay was 3 versus 6 days (p < 0.0001), reflecting early mortality rather than a prognostic exposure. Mortality increased from 6.7% at age 45-54 years to 28.0% at ≥75 years and remained graded after adjustment (≥75 years: adjusted OR 5.92, 95% CI 2.28-15.38; p = 0.0003). Mortality among patients <45 years was also elevated (17.2%; adjusted OR 2.97, 95% CI 1.28-6.87), predominantly among haemorrhagic strokes (22.2% versus 10.8% for ischaemic stroke; age-by-subtype interaction p = 0.0009). Sex, year, stroke subtype, recorded hypertension, and diabetes were not associated with mortality. Absence of head CT showed higher crude mortality (30.0% versus 15.0%; OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.90-6.52). Recorded hypertension prevalence was only 19.8%, indicating substantial under-ascertainment.
CONCLUSION: Older age was the strongest admission-available correlate of in-hospital mortality, while elevated mortality among younger patients was concentrated in haemorrhagic stroke. Under-ascertainment limits interpretation of comorbidities. Absence of stroke-severity, functional-status, ICU, ventilation, and reperfusion data further limits causal or independent prognostic inference.

Title: The application of brain-computer interface on cognitive function and activities of daily living in stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Nonmotor dysfunction is a common sequela of stroke, affecting patients across acute, subacute, and chronic recovery stages and significantly impairing their functional independence, psychosocial adjustment, and overall Activities of Daily Living (ADL). Brain-computer interface (BCI) technology has demonstrated effectiveness in motor function rehabilitation. The primary objective of this study was to assess the efficacy of BCI technology on cognitive function (as the primary indicator of nonmotor dysfunction) and ADL in stroke patients through a systematic review and meta-analysis.
METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261453809). Systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, CNKI, and Wanfang Data up to March 2026. Statistical analyses and the risk of bias were assessed using Review Manager 5.3. The quantitative synthesis focused on the effects of BCI on the cognitive function and ADL of patients with stroke.
RESULTS: The meta-analysis reviewed 11 randomized controlled studies (RCTs) involving a total of 559 participants. Compared with conventional rehabilitation, BCI-based training significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.634, 95% CI: 0.214, 1.055; p = 0.003) and ADL (SMD = 1.198, 95% CI: 0.079, 2.316; p = 0.036). Subgroup analyses suggested exploratory patterns of benefit in certain strata. However, subgroup analysis revealed no significant differences for most comparisons (including scale type, region, sample size, stroke type, BCI type, intervention intensity, and intervention duration; all p > 0.05), except for first-episode stroke in the ADL analysis (p = 0.001).
CONCLUSION: BCI-based training shows preliminary promise for improving cognitive function and ADL in stroke patients. Current evidence remains insufficient to recommend BCI for emotion or speech rehabilitation. However, the GRADE certainty of evidence was rated as low for cognitive function and very low for ADL, indicating that further high-quality research is warranted.

Title: Sex-Based Differences in Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in Patients with Acute Pulmonary Embolism. An Analysis of 1000 Pulmonary Embolism Response Team Activations.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular death, with prior studies suggesting differences in clinical characteristics and risk factors between males and females.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all 1,000 adult patients with confirmed PE evaluated by the Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) at Corewell Health West from November 2019 to March 2024 to describe sex-based differences in presentation, management, and outcomes. Based on sex, patients were classified by differences in demographic, clinical, biomarker, treatment, and outcome measures, including 30-day and one-year survival.
RESULTS: Among 1,000 patients, 480 (48%) were female. Females were older (64 vs. 62.4 years; p = 0.028), had higher body mass index (35.5 vs. 32.2; p < 0.001), and more frequently reported hormone use (21% vs. 5%; p < 0.001). Troponin and Pro-BNP elevations were higher in proportion in females, while males were more likely to smoke (26% vs. 15%; p < 0.001) and present with cough (31% vs. 23%; p = 0.005). No significant sex differences were observed in PE severity, catheter-based interventions, inferior vena cava filter placement, or 30-day (females 8.7%, males 5.8%; p = 0.064) and one-year survival (females 85.4%, males 87.9%; p = 0.217).
CONCLUSION: Despite differences in baseline characteristics and certain clinical features, PE severity, interventions, and outcomes were similar between sexes in this PERT-managed cohort. This highlights sex-specific variations in presentation without differences in management or outcomes within a standardized multidisciplinary pathway such as PERT.

Title: Effects of combined non-invasive brain stimulation and brain-computer interface on upper extremity motor function after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) and brain-computer interface (BCI) training are both promising approaches for post-stroke upper extremity rehabilitation, and their combination has been hypothesized to produce synergistic effects. However, the efficacy of this combined strategy has not been systematically evaluated.
METHODS: We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to October 2025 for randomized controlled trials evaluating NIBS combined with BCI in stroke rehabilitation. Mean differences (MDs) in pre- to post-intervention change scores and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted to examine potential moderators.
RESULTS: Seven randomized controlled trials were included. Pooled analysis showed that NIBS combined with BCI did not provide superior immediate upper extremity motor recovery compared with BCI alone and was associated with lower FMA-UE improvement (MD = -3.67, 95% CI -5.32 to -2.01; I2 = 0%). Subgroup analysis suggested that this effect was mainly driven by studies of tDCS plus BCI, while no significant difference was observed for rTMS plus BCI. No significant long-term effect of tDCS plus BCI or stimulation-site difference for rTMS plus BCI was identified. However, the certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low, and sensitivity analyses suggested that the findings were unstable.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear additional benefit of NIBS as an adjunct to BCI for upper extremity rehabilitation after stroke. Given the limited number of studies and the instability of the pooled result in sensitivity analysis, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. More rigorous and adequately powered trials are needed to determine whether optimized stimulation protocols or specific patient subgroups may benefit from this combined strategy.

Title: Evaluation of a mobile health-enabled hierarchical care model for hypertension management and health-related quality of life among older adults: a prospective pre-post intervention study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a major public health challenge among older adults, particularly in the context of population ageing and increasing demand for long-term chronic disease management. Although mobile health (mHealth) technologies have demonstrated potential in supporting hypertension self-management, evidence regarding their integration with hierarchical healthcare delivery systems and their association with patient-reported health outcomes remains limited. This study evaluated changes in blood pressure control and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) following implementation of a mHealth-enabled hierarchical care model within regional medical consortia.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess changes in blood pressure indicators and HRQoL following implementation of a mobile health-enabled hierarchical diagnosis and treatment education program (mHealth-HDTEP) among older adults with hypertension.
METHODS: A prospective, single-arm, pre-post evaluation study was conducted from January to December 2025 among older adults with hypertension recruited from regional medical consortia in Shenzhen, China. Participants received a 12-month mHealth-HDTEP program delivered through the Shekangtong WeChat mini program, integrating blood pressure self-monitoring, health education, family doctor follow-up, and specialist consultation pathways. The primary outcome was HRQoL measured using the EQ-5D-5L, while secondary outcomes included systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Continuous pre-post changes were assessed using paired t-tests when normality assumptions were satisfied, and changes in EQ-5D-5L dimension levels were assessed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons. Pearson correlation analyses were used to examine associations between changes in blood pressure and HRQoL measures.
RESULTS: Among 225 enrolled participants, 210 completed the 12-month follow-up. Compared with baseline, statistically significant improvements were observed in both blood pressure and HRQoL outcomes. Mean SBP decreased from 145.35 ± 4.18 mmHg to 130.64 ± 5.62 mmHg (mean difference: 14.71 mmHg, 95% CI: 13.68 to 15.74; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 2.043), and mean DBP decreased from 68.93 ± 4.85 mmHg to 60.73 ± 4.31 mmHg (mean difference: 8.20 mmHg, 95% CI: 7.28 to 9.12; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.262). EQ-5D-5L utility values increased from 0.82 ± 0.13 to 0.94 ± 0.06 (mean difference, 0.12; 95% CI, 0.10 to 0.14; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 0.850), and EQ-VAS scores increased from 74.16 ± 11.07 to 80.93 ± 8.03 (mean difference, 6.77; 95% CI, 6.18 to 7.36; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.536). The anxiety/depression dimension showed the most pronounced improvement among the five EQ-5D-5L dimensions (FDR-adjusted p < 0.001). Changes in blood pressure indicators were positively associated with changes in HRQoL measures (p < 0.001). Reductions in blood pressure were positively correlated with improvements in HRQoL parameters (r = 0.22 to 0.32, all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: A mHealth-enabled hierarchical care model integrated within regional healthcare networks was associated with improvements in blood pressure indicators and HRQoL among older adults with hypertension. The findings suggest that combining digital self-management support with primary care coordination may represent a feasible strategy for supporting chronic disease management. Further controlled studies are required to determine effectiveness, sustainability, and scalability across diverse healthcare settings.

Title: Recreational football as medicine? A meta-analysis of its effects and feasibility in patients with chronic diseases.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantitatively synthesise the effects of recreational football interventions on physiological and feasibility-related outcomes in people with chronic diseases.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 6 February 2026, and additional searches of Scopus and Embase were conducted on 17 August 2026. Controlled trials of recreational football in adolescents and adults with selected chronic disease populations were eligible. Three-level random-effects meta-analyses were performed, with cluster-robust (CR2) variance estimation, clustering on the independent trial, applied to every outcome as a robustness check, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.
RESULTS: Twenty-two study reports representing 17 unique trials (15 randomised and 2 non-randomised controlled trials; 588 unique participants) were included. Recreational football was associated with significant improvements in body fat percentage (k = 13; SMD = -0.36, 95% CI - 0.57 to -0.14; p < 0.01), muscle mass (k = 12; SMD = 0.22, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.44; p = 0.05), diastolic blood pressure (k = 12; SMD = -0.53, 95% CI - 0.96 to -0.09; p = 0.02), mean arterial pressure (k = 7; SMD = -0.89, 95% CI - 1.48 to -0.29; p = 0.01), resting heart rate (k = 10; SMD = -1.01, 95% CI - 1.72 to -0.31; p = 0.01), VO₂peak (k = 16; SMD = 0.70, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.03; p < 0.01), Yo-Yo Intermittent Endurance Test level 1 performance (k = 4; SMD = 1.43, 95% CI 0.83 to 2.03; p < 0.01), triglycerides (k = 11; SMD = -0.56, 95% CI - 0.91 to -0.22; p < 0.01), total cholesterol (k = 11; SMD = -0.69, 95% CI - 1.08 to -0.30; p < 0.01), plasma osteocalcin (k = 4; SMD = 1.07, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.60; p < 0.01), and P1NP (k = 4; SMD = 1.28, 95% CI 0.22 to 2.34; p = 0.03). Borderline effects that were not retained under cluster-robust inference were observed for fat mass (SMD = -0.30; p = 0.05), systolic blood pressure (SMD = -0.60; p = 0.05) and LDL (SMD = -0.50; p = 0.05). No statistically significant pooled effects were observed for body weight (SMD = -0.29; p = 0.05), BMI (SMD = -0.06; p = 0.71), waist circumference (SMD = -0.48; p = 0.18), HbA1c (SMD = -0.28; p = 0.10), fasting glucose (SMD = -0.11; p = 0.48), fasting insulin (SMD = 0.07; p = 0.73), HDL (SMD = 0.10; p = 0.70), CRP (SMD = -0.88; p = 0.13), DXA-derived leg and whole-body bone mineral density or content (all p ≥ 0.11), or CTX-1 (SMD = 0.54; p = 0.19). Effects on body fat percentage, fat mass, muscle mass, SBP and LDL were sensitive to the assumed pre-post correlation. Under cluster-robust (CR2) inference the statistical interpretation was unchanged for 22 of the 27 outcomes; fat mass, SBP, LDL and P1NP were no longer significant (all p between 0.05 and 0.07) and whole-body bone mineral density became significant (p = 0.03). Certainty of evidence was low to very low for most outcomes, and adverse events were summarized narratively because quantitative synthesis was not possible. Mean attendance was 82.7% across 13 independent trials, and mean attrition was 15.6% across 14 independent trials.
CONCLUSION: Across the selected chronic disease populations represented in the current evidence base, recreational football showed signals of potential benefit for cardiorespiratory fitness and selected cardiovascular, lipid, and bone-related outcomes, although adiposity- and bone-formation-related effects were less robust in sensitivity analyses. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to heterogeneity and generally low or very low certainty of evidence. Recreational football may be considered a supervised adjunctive exercise option.

Title: Cross-cohort blood transcriptome analysis identifies an eight-gene diagnostic index and inflammatory programs in acute myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is the foremost cause of cardiovascular fatality, with dysregulated immune-inflammatory cascades serving as master regulators of both acute cardiomyocyte necrosis and subsequent maladaptive remodeling. Despite the prognostic potential of individual immune biomarkers, no multi-omics machine learning (ML)-derived immune gene signature has been established for predicting AMI outcome.
METHODS: Peripheral blood transcriptomes from four Gene Expression Omnibus datasets (GSE59867 as the discovery cohort; GSE48060, GSE60993, and GSE66360 as independent validation cohorts; total 348 participants) were subjected to study-wise differential expression analysis and marker-based immune scoring without cross-platform batch harmonization. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and nested machine learning (L2-regularized logistic regression, linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and gradient boosting) were used to derive an eight-gene diagnostic index. Signature performance was evaluated in three independent validation cohorts, contextualized at the single-cell resolution (GSE121893), and experimentally supported by in vitro reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) using American Type Culture Collection (ATCC)-authenticated cell lines (THP-1 TIB-202 and EA.hy926 CRL-2922).
RESULTS: AMI specimens showed marked enrichment of pro-inflammatory M1-like macrophages, neutrophils, and exhausted CD8+ T cells compared to healthy donors. The WGCNA turquoise module exhibited the strongest phenotypic correlation (r = 0.78, p < 0.001). Convergent machine learning analysis yielded an eight-gene diagnostic index (BAX, EDA2R, MCEMP1, SOCS3, ASGR2, RNASE1, ADM, and KPNA5) with a repeated out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.984 in the discovery cohort and independent validation AUCs of 0.863, 0.655, and 0.876. Two exploratory binary-outcome analyses (6-month heart failure progression and 18-month recurrent events) yielded AUCs of 0.819 and 0.569, respectively; these small-sample results are descriptive only and do not support Kaplan-Meier or hazard ratio claims. In vitro RT-qPCR in ATCC-authenticated THP-1-derived macrophages (lipopolysaccharide/ATP stimulation) and EA.hy926 cells (hypoxia/reoxygenation) confirmed elevated levels of CXCL10 (3.82 ± 0.31-fold), IL6 (4.15 ± 0.44-fold), NLRP3 (2.94 ± 0.28-fold), and CASP1 (3.47 ± 0.38-fold) under AMI-relevant stimulation conditions (n = 3 independent biological replicates).
CONCLUSIONS: An eight-gene diagnostic index (BAX, EDA2R, MCEMP1, SOCS3, ASGR2, RNASE1, ADM, and KPNA5), derived using nested machine learning and validated in three independent cohorts, achieved robust discriminative accuracy for AMI diagnosis. Elevated inflammatory transcripts (CXCL10, IL6, NLRP3, and CASP1) confirmed by in vitro RT-qPCR in ATCC cell lines reflect concurrent inflammasome activation and immune dysregulation, offering a mechanistic rationale for precision immune-targeted intervention strategies.

Title: Assessment of QT Dispersion in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Background Acute myocardial infarction is associated with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly due to ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. QT dispersion (QTd), reflecting heterogeneity of ventricular repolarization, may provide useful information regarding ventricular electrical instability in patients with acute myocardial infarction. This study assessed QT dispersion and evaluated its association with clinical characteristics, ventricular arrhythmias, and in-hospital outcome. Methodology This prospective observational study was conducted in a tertiary care hospital from June 2025 to June 2026. A total of 100 patients diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction were enrolled after obtaining written informed consent and Institutional Ethics Committee approval. A standard 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) was recorded at presentation, and QTd was calculated as the difference between the maximum and minimum QT intervals. A QTd value >42 ms was considered abnormal. Associations between QTd and clinical characteristics, ventricular arrhythmias, and in-hospital outcome were evaluated using chi-square and independent-samples t-tests, as appropriate. Results The study included 100 patients. The mean QTd was 80.71 ± 18.2 ms, with QTd >42 ms observed in 88 (88.0%) patients. Ventricular arrhythmias occurred in 30 (30.0%) patients, and mean QTd was significantly higher among patients with ventricular arrhythmias than among those without (94.9 ± 17.5 vs. 70.4 ± 9.82 ms; p < 0.001). Ventricular premature contractions were observed in 20 (20.0%) patients, while ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation occurred in 5 (5.0%) patients each. Patients who died during hospitalization had significantly higher mean QTd than survivors (121.0 ± 22.0 vs. 70.64 ± 9.82 ms; p < 0.001). Conclusions Increased QTd was frequently observed in patients with acute myocardial infarction and was significantly associated with ventricular arrhythmias and in-hospital mortality. These findings represent associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of independent prognostic prediction or causality. Larger multicenter studies with standardized ECG assessment and appropriate adjustment for potential confounders are warranted to determine the independent prognostic significance of QTd in acute myocardial infarction.

Title: Case Report: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis presenting as a multiple sclerosis mimic.
Abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) rarely involves the central nervous system and may closely resemble inflammatory demyelinating disease. We report a 32-year-old woman with adult-onset asthma and recurrent sinusitis who presented with bilateral lower-extremity sensory symptoms and neuropathic pain. Brain and spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multifocal T2-hyperintense lesions fulfilling dissemination in space and time according to the 2017 McDonald criteria. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed mild pleocytosis, CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands, and eosinophils on qualitative cytological examination. Multiple sclerosis (MS) was initially suspected and intravenous methylprednisolone resulted in partial improvement. Three weeks later, the patient developed palpable purpura, inflammatory arthralgia, and left foot-elevating paresis. Follow-up MRI demonstrated a new enhancing lesion and electrophysiological studies revealed axonal neuropathy. Retrospective review of the initial laboratory results showed that peripheral eosinophilia was already present at baseline, while subsequent evaluation identified eosinophilic gastritis on gastroscopic biopsy and eosinophilic bone marrow infiltration. The diagnosis of EGPA was established based on the clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and histopathological evidence of eosinophilic inflammation, and the patient fulfilled the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for EGPA. Treatment with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide followed by maintenance mepolizumab resulted in sustained clinical stability. This case highlights that EGPA may present with radiological and CSF-findings suggestive of MS and emphasizes the importance of integrating systemic manifestations to avoid diagnostic delay.

Title: Association between maternal antimony exposure and offspring congenital heart defects: findings from a large birth cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This nested case-control study aimed to investigate the association between maternal blood antimony concentrations and the risk of congenital heart defects (CHDs) in offspring, identify potential risk factors for CHDs, and inform prevention strategies.
METHOD: The study was conducted within a birth cohort established jointly by Gansu Provincial Maternity and Child Care Hospital and Yale University. A total of 291 women were enrolled, including 97 women who gave birth to infants with CHDs (case group) and 194 controls. Controls were selected from the same cohort using a 1:2 matching ratio and matched to cases by age and community. Maternal whole blood samples were collected during prenatal hospitalization before delivery, and antimony concentrations were measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to determine an antimony exposure cutoff and classify participants into high and low exposure groups. Conditional multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between maternal blood antimony concentrations and the risk of CHDs in offspring.
RESULTS: The mean maternal blood antimony concentration was 13.05 μg/L in the control group and 20.30 μg/L in the CHDs group, and the difference between the two groups was statistically significant. Compared with the low exposure group, the high exposure group was associated with a significantly higher risk of CHDs in offspring (OR = 4.455, 95% CI: 2.029-9.782). Similar associations were observed for the subgroups of isolated CHDs, great arteries malformation, septal defects, and atrial septal defects (ASDs). For each 6 μg/L increment in maternal blood antimony, a 38.9% higher risk of CHDs in offspring (OR = 1.389, 95% CI: 1.110-1.735), with consistent findings in the isolated CHDs, septal defects, and ASDs subgroups. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis showed that when maternal blood antimony exceeded 18.409 μg/L, CHDs risk in offspring increased with rising antimony levels.
CONCLUSION: Higher maternal blood antimony concentrations were associated with an increased risk of CHDs in offspring. These findings suggest that the prenatal living environment may be a modifiable target for CHD prevention and warrant efforts to minimize exposure to potential environmental sources of antimony.

Title: Association of Platelet-to-White Blood Cell Ratio With All-Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality in Hypertensive Patients.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study investigates the prognostic value of the platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR), a composite inflammatory indicator derived from routine complete blood count parameters, for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in hypertensive populations.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) database spanning 1999-2018. The study included 21,608 hypertensive participants aged ≥ 20 years with complete PWR measurements and mortality follow-up data. Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to assess associations between PWR and mortality. Restricted cubic splines identified nonlinear relationships, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated predictive performance.
RESULTS: An inverse association was observed between PWR and mortality risk in hypertensive patients. Each standard deviation increase in PWR was associated with a 10.0% reduction in all-cause mortality (HR = 0.900, 95% CI: 0.873-0.927, p < 0.001) and a 12.3% reduction in cardiovascular mortality (HR = 0.877, 95% CI: 0.828-0.930, p < 0.001) in fully adjusted models. A characteristic L-shaped nonlinear relationship was identified, with inflection points at PWR 45.22 for all-cause mortality and PWR 50.59 for cardiovascular mortality. Time-dependent ROC analysis also demonstrated modest discriminatory capacity.
CONCLUSION: This study suggests that PWR might be a potential biomarker for stratifying risk and predicting mortality in hypertensive patients.

Title: Pretreatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio is associated with clinical phenotypes and infection-related mortality in microscopic polyangiitis: the multicentre REVEAL cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) remains associated with substantial early mortality despite advances in immunosuppressive therapy, highlighting the need for simple biomarkers that facilitate LR) has been associated with disease activity and prognosis in antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV), its phenotype-specific significance in newly diagnosed MPA remains unclear. We investigated whether pretreatment NLR is associated with clinical phenotype, disease course, and long-term outcomes in MPA.
METHODS: Among 418 patients with MPA enrolled in the multicentre REVEAL cohort between 2005 and 2025, 340 newly diagnosed treatment-naïve patients fulfilling the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria were included. Patients were stratified into tertiles according to pretreatment NLR. Baseline characteristics, temporal outcomes, and survival were compared. Infection-related mortality was further evaluated after stabilised inverse probability weighting (IPW).
RESULTS: Higher pretreatment NLR was associated with greater disease severity, including higher Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (P < 0.001) and Five-Factor Score (P = 0.03), more frequent diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (P = 0.015), poorer renal function (P = 0.003), and more intensive remission-induction therapy, including methylprednisolone pulse therapy and rituximab. In contrast, interstitial lung disease was more common in patients with lower NLR (P = 0.001). Despite these baseline differences, disease activity, glucocorticoid tapering, and cumulative organ damage became comparable after treatment initiation. Pretreatment NLR was not associated with relapse-free survival (P = 0.44) but was associated with poorer overall survival (P = 0.012) and higher infection-related mortality (P = 0.002). After adjustment using IPW, the association with overall survival was no longer statistically significant, whereas the increased risk of infection-related mortality remained significant (HR 3.47, 95% CI 1.32-9.09, P = 0.034).
CONCLUSION: Pretreatment NLR reflected distinct inflammatory phenotypes and was independently associated with infection-related mortality in patients with newly diagnosed MPA. As an inexpensive and widely available marker, pretreatment NLR may have potential as a prognostic biomarker, although further validation is required to establish its clinical utility.

Title: Ultrasound-detected renal surface nodularity and renal damage in hypertensive adults undergoing routine health screening: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop an ultrasound-based grading system for renal surface nodularity (RSN), assess its reproducibility, and evaluate its association with renal damage in hypertensive adults undergoing routine health screening.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 871 hypertensive adults who underwent renal ultrasound during routine health screening between October 2025 and March 2026. RSN was graded from stored standardized coronal-plane images on a three-point scale: grade 0 (smooth), grade 1 (mild, undulating), and grade 2 (severe, serrated). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with RSN and to evaluate the association between RSN grade and renal damage, defined as eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m² or proteinuria (≥ 1+), with sequential adjustment that included eGFR as a continuous variable in the final model.
RESULTS: RSN was detected in 410 of 871 patients (47.1%): 226 (25.9%) had grade 1 and 184 (21.1%) had grade 2 RSN. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement for image interpretation showed weighted κ values of 0.798 and 0.888, respectively (n = 80). In multivariable analysis, hypertension grade (OR, 2.40; P <.001), hypertension duration (OR, 1.62; P <.001), cortical echo intensity (OR, 1.63; P <.001), and lower eGFR (OR, 0.625 per 10 mL/min/1.73 m² increase; 95% CI: 0.53-0.74; P <.001) were independently associated with RSN (AUC = 0.815). Renal damage was present in 5.2%, 8.0%, and 27.2% of patients with RSN grades 0, 1, and 2, respectively (P for trend <.001). Grade 2 RSN remained associated with renal damage after adjustment for age, sex, hypertension grade, and diabetes (OR, 8.77; 95% CI: 4.49-17.13; P <.001) and after further adjustment for eGFR as a continuous variable (OR, 2.88; 95% CI: 1.26-6.61; P = .012). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to the non-eGFR components of the endpoint and adjusted for continuous eGFR, the association was attenuated and no longer significant (OR, 1.55; P = .30). Among the 779 patients without threshold-defined renal damage, grade 2 RSN was present in 134 (17.2%), and eGFR declined progressively across RSN grades (medians, 98.8, 93.1, and 87.4 mL/min/1.73 m²; P <.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound can detect and grade RSN, and RSN grade shows a dose-response association with renal damage in hypertensive adults. RSN was frequently present in patients whose eGFR and urinalysis remained within normal limits, suggesting that it may reflect structural change accompanying subclinical decline in renal function.

Title: Routine cine cardiovascular magnetic resonance for clinical phenotyping and serial assessment of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a retrospective single-center clinical analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to confirm because symptoms are non-specific, comorbidities are prevalent, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is normal by definition. We evaluated whether markers from routine cine cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) improved phenotyping and diagnostic discrimination in HFpEF and whether they changed after treatment optimization.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center, observational analysis, 126 adults evaluated between January 2023 and December 2025 were included: 72 with adjudicated HFpEF, 27 hypertensive controls without heart failure, and 27 healthy volunteers. All had available 1.5-T cine CMR studies that underwent blinded analysis of LV volumes, LVEF, left ventricular mass index (LVMI), left atrial volume index (LAVI), right ventricular ejection fraction, and feature-tracking global longitudinal strain (GLS). Interobserver reproducibility was quantified. The primary analysis estimated the discrimination of LAVI, LVMI, and GLS for HFpEF; a multiparametric model was developed using Firth-penalized logistic regression with bootstrap optimism correction. Forty-six patients with HFpEF had repeat CMR available at approximately 6 months after individualized treatment optimization and were included in the serial analysis.
RESULTS: LVEF was preserved and similar across groups. HFpEF was associated with higher LVMI, marked LAVI enlargement, and less negative GLS, with large effect sizes for LAVI and GLS. LAVI and GLS were the strongest single discriminators [apparent area under the curve (AUC) 0.83 and 0.85, respectively]; the multiparametric model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.87 that fell to 0.84 after optimism correction and did not exceed GLS alone. LAVI and less negative GLS remained independent predictors after adjustment. At 6 months, LAVI decreased (mean change -4.8 mL/m2), and GLS became more negative (-1.3 percentage points), exceeding measurement variability, whereas LVEF was unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine cine CMR identified atrial remodeling, ventricular hypertrophy, and impaired longitudinal deformation despite preserved LVEF, and appeared capable of detecting selective short-term temporal changes rather than definitive treatment-induced reverse remodeling. It is a practical adjunct for phenotyping and hypothesis-generating serial assessment, pending external validation.

Title: Effects of different weekly frequencies of combined training on blood pressure variability in aging adults with hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated blood pressure (BP) variability is associated with cardiovascular mortality, independent of mean BP levels. While exercise may influence short-term BP variability, evidence remains inconclusive, and the impact of different weekly training frequencies is unknown.
PURPOSE: To compare the effects of a pragmatic combined training (CT) intervention performed twice vs. four times per week on short-term BP variability in older adults with hypertension.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, men and women aged 50-80 years were assigned to CT twice (CT-2) or four (CT-4) times per week for 12 weeks. The protocol adopted a pragmatic approach, utilizing a weekly exercise dosage: 120-160 min/week and intensity by perceived exertion (4-6). Total volume and overload were matched between groups. Short-term BP variability was assessed via average real variability (ARV) and standard deviation (SD) for 24-hour, daytime, and nighttime periods.
RESULTS: Forty-seven participants (CT-2: n = 27; CT-4: n = 20) with ≥80% attendance were analyzed. No significant group × time interactions were observed. However, both CT-4 and CT-2 significantly reduced 24-hour systolic ARV (CT-4: -2 ± 1 mmHg, P = 0.003; CT-2: -1 ± 1 mmHg, P = 0.032) and daytime systolic ARV (CT-4: -3 ± 1 mmHg, P = 0.008; CT-2: -2 ± 1 mmHg, P = 0.019). Only CT-2 showed reduced daytime diastolic ARV (-1 ± 1 mmHg; P = 0.016). SD-based indices remained unchanged.
CONCLUSION: Twelve weeks of combined training was not associated with statistically significant differences in short-term BP variability between training frequency groups (2 vs. 4) among aging adults with hypertension. Reductions in short-term systolic BP variability were observed over time in both training groups.Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04218903, NCT04218903.

Title: Cross-cohort single-nucleus transcriptomic identification of a MEOX1+FAP+ACTA2-low extracellular matrix-remodeling fibroblast state in dilated cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac fibrosis is a major determinant of adverse remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), but the human disease-associated fibroblast state is incompletely resolved. We tested whether a non-classical MEOX1+FAP + ACTA2-low extracellular matrix (ECM)-remodeling state could be reproduced across independent human cardiac single-nucleus RNA-sequencing cohorts.
METHODS: Public GSE183852 data (25 non-failing donor and 13 DCM hearts) were used for discovery, and SCP1303 (16 normal and 11 DCM hearts) for external validation. Fibroblasts were independently reclustered. All inferential analyses used donors as the statistical unit. State abundance was assessed with Wilcoxon tests, 10,000-iteration donor bootstrap confidence intervals, leave-one-donor-out analyses, and heteroscedasticity-robust covariate models. Raw fibroblast counts were aggregated by donor for pseudobulk differential expression with age-tertile and sex adjustment. ECM activity was compared using pseudobulk and cell-derived donor summaries.
RESULTS: Discovery cluster two showed a MEOX1+FAP + ACTA2-low profile distinct from an ACTA2-high state and was enriched in DCM. Its mean abundance difference was 0.165 of fibroblasts (bootstrap 95% confidence interval 0.035-0.349), with a positive effect after omission of every donor. Age-tertile and sex adjustment preserved the effect magnitude, although the robust confidence interval marginally crossed zero. In SCP1303, the corresponding activated-fibroblast state was enriched in DCM (mean difference 0.192, bootstrap 95% confidence interval 0.144-0.256) and remained associated after sex adjustment. Donor-pseudobulk models identified higher DDAH1, MEOX1 and FAP expression in DCM after false-discovery-rate correction. Two ECM summaries were strongly correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.891), although group significance was method dependent.
CONCLUSION: A reproducible MEOX1+FAP+, relatively ACTA2-low fibroblast state is associated with ECM remodeling in the analyzed human DCM cohorts. DDAH1 is a prioritized state-associated candidate, not an established causal regulator. Spatial and perturbation studies are required for mechanistic validation.

Title: Dosimetric benefits of deep inspiration breath-hold in postoperative radiotherapy for left-sided breast cancer after breast-conserving surgery: an anatomical parameter-based analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the dosimetric impact of deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) technique on radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for left-sided breast cancer, and to explore the relationship between patient anatomical characteristics and dosimetric benefits of DIBH, providing preliminary evidence for understanding individual differences in DIBH related dosimetric gains and their personalized application.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 17 patients who underwent postoperative radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery for left-sided breast cancer. All patients underwent computed tomography (CT) simulation under both DIBH and free-breathing (FB) conditions, and intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) plans were generated from both image sets. With identical prescription doses and planning optimization objectives, dosimetric parameters for the left lung, heart, and cardiac substructures were compared between the two respiratory conditions. Correlations of the maximum cardiac margin distance (MCMD), cardiac displacement, cardiac displacement volume, heart-to-breast distance (HBD), and changes in lung volume with dosimetric parameters were also analyzed.
RESULTS: Compared with FB, DIBH significantly reduced the mean dose (Dmean), V20, and V30 of the left lung, as well as the cardiac Dmean, V20, V30, and V40 (all P < 0.05). In addition, DIBH significantly reduced the mean doses to of the right ventricle (RV), left ventricle (LV), and left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) compared with FB (all P < 0.05). Correlation analysis demonstrated that MCMD under the DIBH condition was positively correlated with cardiac Dmean. The change in MCMD between DIBH and FB was negatively correlated with cardiac and ventricular dose parameters. Cardiac displacement volume between the two respiratory states was positively correlated with changes in mean heart dose. Further analysis revealed that changes in lung volume were positively correlated with cardiac displacement along the Z-axis and changes in HBD while negatively correlated with LAD Dmean under the DIBH condition.
CONCLUSION: DIBH can reduce radiation exposure to the left lung, heart, and selected cardiac substructures while satisfying target-dose requirements. Exploratory analyses indicated that cardiac geometric parameters and changes in lung volume were associated with selected dosimetric parameters, suggesting that dynamic anatomical changes during DIBH may help explain interindividual differences in dosimetric benefit. These findings require further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

Title: Machine learning-based models to predict 90-day non-excellent functional outcomes among patients with mild acute ischemic stroke after intravenous thrombolysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite intravenous thrombolysis, a substantial proportion of patients with mild acute ischemic stroke fail to achieve an excellent functional outcome. Prediction models specifically developed for these patients remain limited. We aimed to construct and evaluate a machine learning model for identifying 90-day non-excellent functional outcomes.
METHODS: We retrospectively collected data from patients with mild acute ischemic stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis at Tianjin Fourth Central Hospital between January 2024 and June 2025. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and neuroimaging variables were extracted from electronic medical records. LASSO regression was applied for feature selection, followed by the development of seven machine learning models. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and classification metrics. We conducted SHAP analysis to elucidate the relative importance and direction of association of individual predictors with model predictions.
RESULTS: A total of 507 patients with mild acute ischemic stroke undergoing intravenous thrombolysis were included, of whom 136 (26.8%) experienced a non-excellent functional outcome at 90 days. LASSO regression identified six predictors, including age, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, platelet count, monocyte count, blood glucose level, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. In the validation cohort, XGBoost achieved the highest numerical AUC of 0.753 (95% CI, 0.660-0.840) and demonstrated adequate calibration and clinical usefulness.
CONCLUSION: A machine learning model was developed and internally validated to predict 90-day non-excellent functional outcomes in patients with mild acute ischemic stroke after intravenous thrombolysis. The XGBoost model showed promising predictive performance and potential utility for early risk stratification.

Title: Qili Qiangxin capsule as adjunctive therapy for heart failure after acute myocardial infarction: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality despite advances in conventional therapy. Qili Qiangxin Capsule (QLQX) has been widely used as an adjunctive treatment for HF in China, but its efficacy and safety in patients with HF after AMI require further evaluation.
METHODS: Seven databases were searched from their inception to January 2026. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing QLQX plus conventional Western medicine (WM) with WM alone were included. The primary outcome was N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), clinical response rate, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), quality of life, all-cause mortality, heart failure-related hospitalisation, and adverse events. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.
RESULTS: A total of 16 RCTs involving 1391 participants were included. Compared with WM alone, QLQX plus WM was associated with greater reductions in NT-proBNP, BNP, LVEDD, LVESD, and hs-CRP, and improving LVEF, quality of life and the clinical response rate. No statistical differences were observed in LVEDV, all-cause mortality, and adverse events. Heart failure-related hospitalisation was not reported in any included study. The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was rated as low or very low according to the GRADE approach.
CONCLUSION: QLQX plus conventional WM was associated with improvements in several surrogate and short-term clinical outcomes in patients with HF after AMI. However, the certainty of evidence was low or very low, and data on mortality and heart failure-related hospitalisation were insufficient. The current evidence is therefore inadequate to determine whether QLQX improves long-term clinical prognosis. Further high-quality RCTs with longer follow-up and clinically important endpoints are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261277047, identifier CRD420261277047.

Title: Rethinking favorable outcomes: "return to baseline" as an additional outcome in ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke outcomes are commonly assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), dichotomized into "favorable" (0-2) and "unfavorable" (3-6). Many elderly patients present with pre-stroke mRS scores of 3-5, making "favorable" outcomes unattainable and complicating treatment evaluation.
METHODS: This is a monocentric, retrospective analysis of ischemic stroke patients in our prospective registry (2010-2022). Outcomes include mRS scores at discharge and 90 days post-stroke. Descriptive and inferential statistics were applied with appropriate tests for categorical and ordinal variables. Multivariable logistic regression was used to model return to pre-stroke mRS and death by 90 days, adjusted for pre-stroke mRS group, age, sex, NIHSS on admission, treatment modality and vascular territory. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Of 3,724 ischemic stroke patients admitted, 2,070 met inclusion criteria (median age 75.7). Among those with favorable pre-stroke mRS (0-2, n = 1,827), 47.6% achieved favorable outcomes at discharge and 47.5% at 90 days. By definition, none with unfavorable pre-stroke mRS achieved favorable outcomes. At discharge, return to baseline mRS occurred in 16.2% with favorable pre-stroke mRS, compared to 19.3% with unfavorable (p = 0.216). 90 days post-stroke, return to baseline occurred in 21.8% with favorable pre-stroke mRS, compared to 11.9% with unfavorable (p < 0.001). Redefining favorable outcome to include return to pre-stroke mRS increased rates from 42.0 to 44.3% at discharge and from 41.9 to 43.3% 90 days post-stroke (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis a pre-stroke mRS of 3-5 was associated with death by 90 days (OR 4.40, 95% CI 3.18-6.10) but not with return to baseline in all patients (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.65-1.58); among survivors it was associated with a higher probability of return to baseline (OR 2.34, 95% CI 1.40-3.91).
CONCLUSION: The traditional dichotomization of mRS does not reflect the wide range of pre-stroke status. Incorporating "return to pre-stroke mRS score" as a favorable outcome metric alongside the conventional dichotomy provides a more individualized measure, improving treatment evaluation and supporting tailored care strategies, particularly for patients with higher pre-stroke mRS scores.

Title: NLR-TyG index and prevalent chronic kidney disease in hypertension: a cross-population study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation and metabolic dysfunction are interrelated in chronic kidney disease (CKD). The NLR-TyG index (NTI), calculated from the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, summarizes concurrent inflammatory and metabolic burden. We examined its association with prevalent CKD in hypertensive adults from a Chinese cardiology inpatient population and the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included hypertensive adults from the Department of Cardiology, First Affiliated Hospital of Dali University, and NHANES. NTI was analyzed continuously and by cohort-specific quartiles. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines assessed associations. Subgroup, sensitivity, and incremental discrimination analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: The analysis included 8,358 hospital participants (1,800 with CKD) and 9,182 NHANES participants (2,751 with CKD). In fully adjusted models, each 1-unit increase in NTI was associated with higher odds of CKD in the hospital population [odds ratio (OR), 1.012; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.010-1.014] and NHANES (OR, 1.021; 95% CI, 1.013-1.029; both p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest NTI quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher CKD odds in the hospital population (OR, 2.85; 95% CI, 2.38-3.40) and NHANES (OR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.56-2.38; both P for trend <0.001). Significant nonlinearity was detected only in the hospital population. Associations persisted among participants with known non-use of lipid-lowering therapy. Adding NTI increased the C statistic from 0.769 to 0.778 in the hospital population and from 0.772 to 0.778 in NHANES; discrimination was similar when NLR and TyG were entered separately.
CONCLUSION: Higher NTI was independently associated with prevalent CKD in both hypertensive populations and provided modest incremental discrimination. NTI may offer a simple summary of inflammatory-metabolic burden, but prospective prediction and clinical utility require further validation.

Title: Comparative outcomes of middle meningeal artery embolization, burr hole drainage, and neuroendoscopic-assisted evacuation with MMA disconnection for chronic subdural haematoma: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy, safety, and resource utilization of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE), burr hole drainage (BHD), and neuroendoscopic-assisted evacuation with middle meningeal artery disconnection (NE-MMAD) for chronic subdural haematoma (CSDH).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 265 patients with CSDH, divided into MMAE (n = 46), BHD (n = 152), and NE-MMAD (n = 67) groups. The primary outcome was the 6-month recurrence rate. Secondary outcomes included neurological improvement rate, reoperation rate, operation time, hospital stay, number of imaging follow-ups, and complications.
RESULTS: The recurrence rates for MMAE and NE-MMAD (4.35 and 4.48%, respectively) were significantly lower than that for BHD (19.74%, p = 0.001). The neurological improvement rate was highest in the NE-MMAD group (88.06%, p = 0.003). The reoperation rates for MMAE and NE-MMAD were both lower than that for BHD (p = 0.002). In the MMAE group, 5 patients (10.87%) underwent salvage BHD due to delayed resolution of mass effect. MMAE had the shortest operation time (31 min) and hospital stay (7 days), while NE-MMAD had the longest operation time (70 min); both MMAE and NE-MMAD required fewer imaging follow-ups than BHD (all p < 0.05). No significant difference in complication rates was observed among the three groups; however, one patient in the MMAE group experienced permanent blindness due to inadvertent embolization through a dangerous anastomosis.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, MMAE and NE-MMAD were associated with lower recurrence compared with BHD, and NE-MMAD was associated with the greatest neurological improvement. BHD may be preferred for first-onset, non-septated haematomas; MMAE may be preferred for older patients or those with coagulopathy, but the risk of blindness warrants caution; NE-MMAD may be preferred for septated, organized, recurrent, and markedly space-occupying haematomas. Clinical decision-making should integrate haematoma characteristics, patient status, and available medical resources to guide individualized stratified treatment.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Association of physical frailty with cardiac conduction disorder events in the UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Practical markers for identifying individuals at risk of cardiac conduction disorders (CCDs) before overt disease are limited. Physical frailty reflects reduced physiological reserve and may capture vulnerability beyond chronological age and individual cardiometabolic factors. Herein, we investigated the association of physical frailty with incident CCD in the UK Biobank cohort.
METHODS: We included 423,162 participants with data for a modified Fried frailty phenotype and linked health-record follow-up after excluding those with cardiovascular disease, CCDs, or pacemaker implantation at baseline. Participants were classified as non-frail, prefrail, or frail. The primary outcome was incident CCD, and the secondary outcomes were severe conduction block and left bundle branch or fascicular block. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Overall, 58.2% of participants were non-frail, 38.5% were prefrail, and 3.3% were frail; 18,067 incident CCD events occurred during the follow-up. Compared with participants who were non-frail, participants who were prefrail and frail were at higher risks of CCDs after multivariable adjustment [HR, 1.23 (95% CI, 1.19-1.27) and HR, 1.71 (95% CI, 1.60-1.83), respectively; P for trend <0.01]. The corresponding HRs were 1.13 (95% CI, 1.09-1.18) and 1.44 (95% CI, 1.32-1.59) for severe conduction block and were 1.24 (95% CI, 1.17-1.32) and 1.61 (95% CI, 1.43-1.81) for left bundle branch or fascicular block.
CONCLUSIONS: Physical frailty was associated with graded increases in incident CCD and related conduction outcomes, with excess risk evident at the prefrailty stage. Frailty assessment may help identify individuals with increased susceptibility, although the observational design does not establish causality or demonstrate that modifying frailty would reduce risk.

Title: Association of liberal versus restrictive oxygen saturation targets with mortality in mechanically ventilated stroke patients: a multicenter retrospective propensity-matched analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal oxygen saturation targets in mechanically ventilated stroke patients remain uncertain. While restrictive oxygen strategies are increasingly adopted in general critical care, their impact in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) are unclear. We evaluated the association between restrictive versus liberal oxygen saturation targets during the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation and short-term mortality in stroke patients.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX database (2006-2026). Adult patients (≥18 years) with a stroke diagnosis who required invasive mechanical ventilation and had documented peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) values within the first 48 h of ventilation were included. Patients were stratified according to early oxygen saturation targets: restrictive (SpO₂ 92-96%) versus liberal (SpO₂ ≥ 97%). Propensity score matching (PSM) by demographics, comorbidities, and stroke severity was performed separately within the combined stroke cohort and prespecified AIS and ICH subgroups to balance demographic and clinical covariates. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality at 30 and 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 30-day tracheostomy and ventilator-associated pneumonia. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. p-value was set at 0.05.
RESULTS: Among 17,207 mechanically ventilated stroke patients, 2,366 received restrictive and 14,841 liberal oxygen saturation targets prior to matching. After PSM, 2,350 patients remained in each group. Restrictive oxygenation during the first 48 h was associated with higher mortality at 1 month (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.03-1.23; p = 0.008) and 3 months (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02-1.20; p = 0.014). In AIS, restrictive oxygenation was similarly associated with increased mortality at 1 month (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.11-1.43) and 3 months (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.37). No statistically significant mortality difference was observed in ICH. Restrictive oxygenation was associated with lower 30-day tracheostomy rates (8.5% vs. 13.1%; RR 0.653, p < 0.001), with no difference in VAP.
CONCLUSION: Restrictive oxygen saturation targets during the first 48 h of mechanical ventilation may be associated with higher short-term mortality in stroke, driven primarily by the AIS group. These findings suggest that early oxygenation strategy may have subtype-specific implications and warrant prospective evaluation in stroke focused randomized trials.

Title: Association between prognostic nutritional index and mortality in older Japanese patients with severe post-stroke dysphagia requiring nutritional support: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic nutritional index (PNI), calculated from serum albumin and lymphocyte count, has remained insufficiently investigated in older patients with post-stroke dysphagia (PSD). We investigated whether PNI was associated with all-cause mortality in older Japanese patients with PSD and compared its prognostic performance with that of the C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 132 older Japanese patients with severe PSD requiring PEG or TPN between January 2014 and January 2017. Multivariable Cox regression analysis and Kaplan-Meier curves were used to estimate the associations of PNI and CAR with all-cause mortality. We assessed robustness through subgroup and sensitivity analyses. To evaluate the prognostic discrimination for 1-year mortality, we used time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and assessed incremental predictive value using integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and net reclassification improvement (NRI).
RESULTS: The mean age of the cohort was 80.7 years (78 women, 54 men). In fully adjusted models, multivariable Cox regression showed that each 1-point increment in PNI was associated with a 7% reduction in all-cause mortality (HR = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.97). Compared with the lowest PNI tertile (T1), the highest tertile (T3) showed a 75% risk reduction (HR = 0.25; 95% CI: 0.10-0.60). For 1-year mortality, the time-dependent AUC was numerically higher for PNI than for CAR (0.771 vs. 0.712; p = 0.16). Adding PNI to a clinical baseline model significantly improved discrimination (IDI = 0.055, 95% CI 0.010-0.104, p < 0.001; NRI = 0.471, 95% CI 0.126-0.957), whereas adding CAR did not (IDI = 0.015, p = 0.31).
CONCLUSION: PNI was inversely associated with mortality in older Japanese patients with severe post-stroke dysphagia requiring PEG or TPN and provided incremental prognostic information beyond standard clinical variables. Whether PNI may be useful for risk stratification in this population requires prospective and external validation.

Title: Perioperative prothrombin time activity trajectories and subsequent mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative prothrombin time activity (PTA) changes rapidly during surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but single measurements do not capture heterogeneous longitudinal patterns. We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023. Group-based trajectory modeling used the last preoperative and observed postoperative day (POD) 1-7 PTA measurements. Patients required at least three observed PTA measurements for trajectory modeling. Mortality analyses began immediately after POD7. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and sex; Firth regression addressed sparse events. Incremental information beyond last preoperative PTA was evaluated by a prespecified likelihood-ratio comparison.
RESULTS: The trajectory cohort comprised 268 patients with 1,895 observations and 27 deaths after POD7.
