Four perioperative PTA trajectory groups were identified: moderate-stable [87 (32.5%)], low-declining [50 (18.7%)], preserved-rapidly-declining [61 (22.8%)], and high-preserved [70 (26.1%)]. Cumulative mortality differed globally (log-rank P = 0.00210), and trajectory group remained associated with subsequent mortality in the age- and sex-adjusted Cox model (global P = 0.0322) and Firth sensitivity analysis (global P = 0.0481). The prespecified direct low-declining-versus-preserved-rapidly-declining comparison did not demonstrate a clear difference. Adding trajectory group to age, sex, and last preoperative PTA did not show clear incremental information (likelihood-ratio P = 0.304; Firth P = 0.380). After exclusion of mechanical-valve recipients, the principal trajectory structure was largely preserved, although this sensitivity analysis did not exclude treatment-related effects on PTA.
CONCLUSION: Four reproducible perioperative PTA trajectories characterized distinct longitudinal patterns and were associated with mortality after the POD7 landmark. These trajectories should be interpreted as composite perioperative patterns reflecting both disease and treatment context rather than as intrinsic coagulation states. They were not ordered mortality-risk tiers and did not show clear incremental prognostic information beyond last preoperative PTA. External validation is required.

Title: Association between the perivascular fat attenuation index and CCTA-defined anatomically significant left anterior descending coronary artery stenosis: relationship with serum inflammatory biomarkers.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether lesion-specific perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI) is associated with CCTA-defined anatomically significant (≥50%) left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) stenosis and to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a composite model integrating serum inflammatory biomarkers.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 160 patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Patients receiving anti-inflammatory medications were excluded. Lesion-specific perivascular FAI was measured around the LAD. The prespecified primary outcome was CCTA-defined anatomically significant LAD stenosis (≥50%), analysed as a binary variable. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors, and the final model was internally evaluated with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, 10-fold cross-validation, and 1,000-bootstrap resampling. Model building was repeated within each resample. Calibration (slope, calibration-in-the-large, Brier score) and incremental discrimination (DeLong test) were assessed.
RESULTS: Patients with CCTA-defined anatomically significant stenosis (≥50%) had higher, less negative FAI values, higher hs-CRP and LDH levels, and a lower ApoA1/ApoB ratio than those with stenosis <50% (all P < 0.05). FAI correlated with stenosis both as a continuous percentage (ρ = 0.54, P < 0.001) and as a binary ≥50% variable (ρ = 0.64, P < 0.001), with less negative FAI values accompanying more severe stenosis. The final model identified FAI (OR = 1.055, 95% CI: 1.014-1.098), hs-CRP (OR = 1.063, 95% CI: 1.005-1.125), LDH (OR = 1.014, 95% CI: 1.005-1.023), and the ApoA1/ApoB ratio (OR = 0.209, 95% CI: 0.070-0.624) as independent predictors. The composite model achieved an AUC of 0.915 (95% CI: 0.865-0.965); internal validation yielded AUCs of 0.872 (5-fold), 0.881 (95% CI: 0.826-0.936; 10-fold), and 0.895 (95% CI: 0.848-0.942; bootstrap). On formal DeLong testing for correlated ROC curves, the composite model showed significantly better discrimination than hs-CRP alone (P  =  0.020) and than FAI alone (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher, less negative perivascular FAI values were associated with CCTA-defined anatomically significant LAD stenosis. A composite model integrating FAI, hs-CRP, LDH, and the ApoA1/ApoB ratio showed high apparent diagnostic accuracy and remained stable across multiple internal validation strategies. Because this was a single-centre retrospective study without external validation or outcome data, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and hypothesis-generating; the model is not ready for clinical use.

Title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Three-Month Unplanned Readmission in Patients with Moderate-to-Severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with moderate-to-severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) face a high risk of three-month unplanned readmission after discharge, yet early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging in clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting the risk and providing a reference for the subsequent development and updating of predictive tools.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study involved individuals with moderate-to-severe COPD from Tianjin Chest Hospital (January 2023 to January 2026). Participants were randomly split into a 70% training set and a 30% validation set. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression identified candidate predictors for model development. Six models were constructed: logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Naive Bayes (NB). Model performance was assessed through the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), sensitivity (SEN), and specificity (SPE). Calibration was evaluated through calibration curves, and clinical utility via decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: 299 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD were enrolled, and 59 (20%) experienced unplanned readmission within three months after discharge. Six ML models were compared, and the XGBoost model exhibited the best performance in the validation cohort, with an AUC of 0.809 (95% CI: 0.690-0.927), SEN of 0.750, and SPE of 0.826. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranked the key predictive factors in descending order: history of hospitalization in the past year, FEV1, history of coronary heart disease, and smoking history.
CONCLUSION: XGBoost model showed promising performance in internal validation for predicting the risk of unplanned readmission among patients with moderate-to-severe COPD. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size, single-center design. Future studies should use prospective, multicenter data from diverse geographic regions to externally validate and update the model.

Title: Forgotten electrolytes: magnesium and calcium flux during dialysis.
Journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Calcium and magnesium remain incompletely individualized in contemporary dialysis prescriptions despite growing evidence linking their concentrations to cardiovascular outcomes, vascular calcification, mineral metabolism, and mortality. The 2025 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Controversies Conference report on chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder (MBD) and recent kinetic studies of intradialytic ion fluxes make a focused review of these "forgotten" divalent cations timely.
RECENT FINDINGS: Intradialytic calcium mass transfer is influenced by patient- and prescription-level factors, and total serum calcium incompletely reflects biologically relevant calcium flux; ionized calcium may decline during dialysis as hemoconcentration increases albumin concentration and alkalosis increases albumin-bound calcium. Small randomized trials show that raising dialysate magnesium improves serum resistance to calcification, but whether higher dialysate magnesium improves clinical outcomes remains unknown. The 2025 KDIGO report retains the 1.25-1.50 mmol/l dialysate calcium range and identifies individualized calcium mass-transfer assessment as a research priority. Dial-Mag, a large pragmatic trial comparing higher versus conventional dialysate magnesium concentrations, is ongoing.
SUMMARY: Recent evidence challenges the assumption that standardized dialysate calcium and magnesium prescriptions are optimal for all patients. Future studies should define patient-specific targets, validate practical methods to assess peridialytic calcium and magnesium levels and intradialytic flux, and determine whether individualized dialysate prescriptions improve clinical outcomes.

Title: Association between carotid intima-media thickness and preeclampsia: Prospective observational comparative study.
Journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia is associated with widespread endothelial dysfunction and shares several pathophysiological mechanisms with atherosclerosis. Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) is a well-established marker of subclinical atherosclerosis and may reflect early maternal vascular remodeling. This study aimed to compare CIMT between pregnant women with and without preeclampsia and to evaluate the association between CIMT and preeclampsia.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort study, pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who attended the outpatient obstetrics clinic between 24 and 37 weeks of gestation and met the eligibility criteria were prospectively enrolled. Participants diagnosed with preeclampsia formed the study group, and pregnant women who were not diagnosed with preeclampsia during the evaluation phase and during pregnancy formed the control group. CIMT measurements were performed at the time of evaluation for all patients, concurrently with the clinical and laboratory assessment used for diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, routine laboratory parameters, and CIMT measurements were compared between groups. Correlation analyses and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed to evaluate the association between CIMT and preeclampsia.
RESULTS: Women with preeclampsia had significantly greater CIMT than pregnant women without preeclampsia. Maternal age, body mass index, serum uric acid, urea, and creatinine levels were significantly higher, whereas serum albumin levels were significantly lower in the preeclampsia group. CIMT demonstrated significant correlations with several biochemical parameters related to renal function and systemic vascular involvement. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, median CIMT remained independently associated with preeclampsia after adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at CIMT measurement (adjusted odds ratio 2.53 per 0.1 mm increase; 95% confidence interval 1.36-4.71; P = 0.003). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that CIMT had a moderate ability to discriminate women with and without preeclampsia (area under the curve 0.75).
CONCLUSION: Women with preeclampsia exhibited significantly increased CIMT compared with pregnant women without preeclampsia. Median CIMT demonstrated moderate discriminatory performance for distinguishing women with and without established preeclampsia; however, the clinical utility of CIMT for preeclampsia screening remains to be established. Larger prospective studies are required to validate the observed association and determine the clinical utility of CIMT in preeclampsia assessment.

Title: SDHC Gene is a Potential Player in the Pathogenesis of Congenital Heart Disease and Neurodevelopmental Disorder by Promoting eNOS Signaling, Suppressing Inflammation and Improving Angiogenic Endothelial Function.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) and Neurodevelopmental Disorders (NDD) frequently co-occur due to shared genetic defects in embryonic angiogenesis and mitochondrial metabolism; however, the regulatory mechanisms linking these pathways remain poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To identify pathogenic genes underlying CHD-NDD co-development and investigate the regulatory role of Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Subunit C (SDHC) in endothelial angiogenesis.
METHODS: Blood samples from 70 children (13 CHD+NDD, 33 CHD, 24 NDD) were analyzed by Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) and Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS). Candidate genes were identified through bidirectional deduplication, multi-library comparison, PPI network analysis, and functional enrichment analysis. SDHC expression was examined by immunofluorescence in the developing mouse heart and brain. In Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells (HUVECs) with SDHC overexpression or knockdown, eNOS and TNF-α protein levels were measured by Western blot. Cell migration and tube formation were quantified by scratch and Matrigel assays.
RESULTS: WES identified high-frequency SDHC mutations, including T→TTA (Chr1:161293485, 33.33%) and C→CT (Chr1:161332091, 55.56%) in CHD+NDD. Bioinformatics suggested SDHC involvement in cardiac and neural development. In mice, cardiac SDHC increased age-dependently by 71.83% (P < 0.05), 100.21% (P < 0.01), and 239.89% (P < 0.0001) from 1 to 8 weeks. In HUVECs, SDHC overexpression upregulated eNOS by 103.25% (P < 0.001) and downregulated TNF-α by 45.16% (P < 0.01); knockdown downregulated eNOS by 43.37% (P < 0.05). SDHC overexpression increased migration by 42.96% (P < 0.0001), while its knockdown decreased it by 34.02% (P < 0.001). Tube formation nodes increased by 130.24% (P < 0.0001) and mesh area by 111.82% (P < 0.0001); knockdown reduced mesh area by 80.81% (P < 0.0001).
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest SDHC dysregulation may affect CHD-NDD comorbidity through eNOS modulation and inflammatory responses in HUVECs. The presence of SDHC variants in 7 of 13 patients (53.8%) and functional data indicate SDHC may serve as a candidate angiogenesis regulator linking cardiovascular and neurodevelopmental abnormalities. However, the small cohort (n = 13 CHD + NDD), absence of healthy controls, and lack of patient-derived variant validation limit definitive conclusions. The biological consequences of the identified variants remain unknown because variant-specific functional analyses were not performed. Future studies require expanded cohorts and in vivo SDHC- specific models to investigate potential associations.
CONCLUSION: SDHC may play potential roles in eNOS signaling, inflammation suppression, and endothelial angiogenic function. These findings suggest SDHC as a candidate gene associated with CHD-NDD comorbidity.

Title: Uncovering cardiac molecular remodelling in racing Thoroughbreds with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in both humans and horses, with a comparable prevalence of ~2%. In horses, AF is a major cause of poor athletic performance and linked to sudden cardiac death, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate transcriptomic remodelling associated with spontaneous paroxysmal AF (PAF).
STUDY DESIGN: Case-control study.
METHODS: We performed RNA sequencing on left atrial (LA) tissue from three Thoroughbred racehorses with PAF and four matched controls. All horses were euthanised due to musculoskeletal reasons. Cell type deconvolution was performed with BayesPrism. The differential expression analysis was performed with EdgeR. Alternative splicing analysis was performed with SUPPA2.
RESULTS: Cell-type deconvolution revealed a modest, non-significant shift towards increased fibroblast and immune cell proportions in PAF, but not enough to account for widespread transcriptional changes. 1400 of the 12,012 included genes were considered significantly differentially expressed (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value <0.05). These genes included ion channels, calcium-handling proteins, and conduction-related genes. In addition, several genes directly involved in cardiac muscle contraction and mitochondrial energy metabolism were differentially expressed. Alternative splicing analysis revealed over 20 significantly altered events, including skipped exons in genes with potential relevance to cardiac function and remodelling.
MAIN LIMITATIONS: The number of biological replicates was modest.
CONCLUSIONS: Overall, despite no major changes in cell composition, the findings highlight intrinsic structural and molecular changes in the LA of PAF-affected horses. This study provides the first transcriptomic and splicing analysis of atrial tissue in racehorses with PAF, revealing molecular remodelling consistent with mechanisms of arrhythmia maintenance and suggesting potential targets for further functional investigation.

Title: [Infectious complications in young patients with acute ischemic stroke].
Journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the prevalence of infectious complications (ICs) during the acute phase of ischemic stroke (IS) in young patients and to identify potential biomarkers for early diagnosis.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective and retrospective study included 150 patients diagnosed with acute IS at the Buyanov Moscow City Hospital, from 2023 to 2025. The cohort was divided into two groups: Group 1 comprised patients aged between 20 and 45 years (n=80; 19 females, 23.75%; mean age: 40.2±8.1 years), while Group 2 included 70 patients over 45 years (25 females, 35.71%; age range: 46-87 years, mean age: 66.4±10.1 years). The study assessed the incidence of ICs, the factors associated with their emergence, and the prognostic implications of ratios of blood cell counts as early markers for ICs.
RESULTS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus was statistically more prevalent in elderly patients with ICs (p<0.05). Conversely, in younger patients with an elevated risk of ICs, only a prior history of IS showed a significant association (p<0.05). The occurrence of ICs was significantly lower in younger patients compared to older patients (12.5% vs. 22.8%; p<0.05). However, ICs were correlated with more pronounced neurological deficits at discharge (mean NIHSS scores of 9.1±5.9 vs. 6.3±2.9, respectively; p<0.05). The earliest changes in the CRP/albumin ratio (p<0.001), D-dimer/albumin (p=0.015), and fibrinogen/albumin (p=0.022) were identified as the most significant predictors. A CRP/albumin ratio >0.3 indicates a high risk of ICs in young patients.
CONCLUSION: In young patients, the presence of ICs complicates recovery of neurological function, underscoring the need for reliable markers for early detection.

Title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or medical therapy alone before transcatheter aortic valve replacement: insights from a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.
METHODS: We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

Title: Resuscitation and 30-day postoperative mortality in acute type A aortic dissection: A cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with acute type A aortic dissection who experience cardiopulmonary arrest require cardiopulmonary resuscitation before definitive repair, but the prognostic relevance of its duration is unclear. We evaluated the association between resuscitation duration and early mortality after emergency surgery.
METHODS: In this retrospective two-centre study, we included all adults who underwent emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection. The exposure was the combined preoperative and intraoperative duration of resuscitation until return of spontaneous circulation or initiation of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or cardiopulmonary bypass, categorised a priori as none, <15 min or ≥ 15 min. Multilevel proportional hazards models and competing-risks regression, with multiple imputation of missing covariates, were used.
RESULTS: Of 880 patients, 815 (92.6%), 13 (1.5%), and 52 (5.9%) received no resuscitation, resuscitation for <15 min and resuscitation for ≥15 min, respectively (median recorded duration 29 min, interquartile range 15-43). Thirty-day mortality was 81/815 (9.9%), 3/13 (23.1%) and 42/52 (80.8%), respectively. Resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 9.59, 95% confidence interval 4.28-21.45; P < 0.001), whereas the estimate for resuscitation for <15 min was imprecise (adjusted hazard ratio 1.68, 95% confidence interval 0.46-6.13; P = 0.43).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection, combined preoperative and intraoperative resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality, and the risk increased with resuscitation duration. These findings provide prognostic information rather than a criterion for withholding surgery.

Title: [Expert consensus on multidisciplinary sequential diagnosis and treatment of sleep-disordered breathing in children].
Journal: Lin chuang er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Journal of clinical otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
Abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing（SDB） has a relatively high prevalence in children, and its pathogenesis is complex, involving interdisciplinary issues. Among its subtypes, obstructive sleep apnea （OSA） is the most common, accounting for approximately 90% of cases. Untreated SDB can impair growth and development, cognitive function, and cardiovascular health in affected children. At present, its diagnosis and treatment remain constrained by inadequate multidisciplinary collaboration, single-dimensional assessment, fragmented care, and the lack of a sequential care concept. This consensus was jointly developed by a multidisciplinary panel of experts in otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, orthodontics and stomatology, pediatrics, endocrinology, and psychiatry and psychology. In accordance with the principles of relevant guidelines issued by the World Health Organization （WHO） and the Chinese Medical Association, the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation （GRADE） system was adopted to assess the quality of evidence and grade the strength of recommendations. Recommendations were formulated covering diagnostic assessment, multidisciplinary collaboration, sequential treatment, management of special populations, follow-up and health education, and future research directions, and a child-centered, stage-based, and dynamically adjusted multidisciplinary framework for sequential diagnosis and treatment was established, with the aim of standardizing clinical practice, enhancing comprehensive management, and improving the quality of life and long-term prognosis of affected children.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Consensus Statement; English Abstract

Title: Cardiovascular Disease in Women the Two Decades Following Uteroplacental Disorders: A Population-Based Data-Linkage Study.
Journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Uniform recommendations on cardiovascular follow-up after complicated pregnancies are lacking, partly due to limited evidence. This study aimed to investigate the incidence and timing of premature cardiovascular disease (CVD) after different uteroplacental disorders, to inform the timing and content of cardiovascular follow-up.
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study, linking data from the Dutch perinatal registry with national hospital admissions data.
SETTING: Netherlands, 2000-2022.
POPULATION: 1 669 681 nulliparous women, with a singleton pregnancy.
METHODS: Cox regression was used to estimate hazard ratios for overall CVD and specific cardiovascular conditions after uteroplacental disorders, adjusted for confounders. Time-dependent Cox regression and interaction analyses for education attainment, income, and migration background were performed.
RESULTS: Risks of premature hypertension, atherosclerosis, ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrest, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease were significantly increased among women with a history of a uteroplacental disorder, adjusted for confounders (overall CVD: aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.67-1.74; median follow-up time 11 years, IQR 6-17 years). Hazard ratios were similar after pregnancy induced hypertension (PIH), preeclampsia (PE), fetal growth restriction (FGR), or fetal death, while risks after spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) were less elevated. Most relative CVD risks were highest shortly after pregnancy but remained elevated more than 10 years postpartum. After hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), hypertension risk was most pronounced, whereas after FGR the increased risk of atherosclerosis was most notable. Socioeconomic factors had limited impact on these associations.
CONCLUSIONS: All uteroplacental disorders-not only PE-serve as women-specific markers of CVD risk, shortly after pregnancy and later in life, highlighting the need for early cardiovascular screening. Pathological processes contributing to the increased CVD risk might differ across uteroplacental disorders.

Title: Predictors of Malnutrition in Patients With Multiple Myeloma: A Review of the Literature.
Journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
Abstract: Multiple myeloma is the second most common hematological malignancy, and malnutrition and cancer cachexia represent clinically relevant complications associated with impaired treatment tolerance and unfavorable outcomes. Their pathogenesis involves systemic inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, treatment-related toxicity, and genetic and epigenetic mechanisms. Among inflammation-related biomarkers, C-reactive protein (CRP) and interleukin-1b (IL-1ß) currently have the strongest evidence for direct predictive potential. CRP concentrations >54 mg/L are associated with an increased likelihood of cachexia (OR=5.94), and IL-1ß >6.7 pg/mL demonstrated predictive performance for cachexia (AUC=0.788). This association strengthened when IL-1ß was combined with CRP (AUC=0.956). Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) and soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR) have also been associated with hypoalbuminemia and disease-related characteristics, although their predictive utility remains less extensively validated. Emerging genetic and epigenetic candidates include the IL1B rs1143634 polymorphism and dysregulated non-coding RNAs, including miR-192-5p, miR-1271-5p, MALAT1, and TUG1. Current evidence therefore supports a clearer near-term clinical potential for inflammation-related biomarkers, whereas molecular predictors remain predominantly investigational and require prospective validation. This narrative review aims to critically summarize and compare current evidence on inflammatory and genetic predictors of malnutrition and cancer cachexia in multiple myeloma, with particular emphasis on the strength of evidence, clinical applicability, and future translational potential.

Title: Development and internal validation of a serum ferritin-based prediction model for coronary artery aneurysms in Kawasaki disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease is the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, and coronary artery aneurysms represent its most important cardiovascular complication. Identifying children at risk for coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset is clinically important. Serum ferritin may reflect systemic inflammation in Kawasaki disease, but its incremental predictive value remains uncertain. This study developed a ferritin-based model for predicting coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks.
METHODS: Patients with Kawasaki disease were retrospectively identified at a single centre and randomly divided into training and internal validation cohorts in a 6:4 ratio. Predictors were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and reclassification metrics.
RESULTS: Among 378 patients, 98 (25.9%) had coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after disease onset. The ferritin-based model included male sex, platelet count, serum ferritin, albumin ≤ 31.5 g/L, and baseline maximum coronary artery Z score ≥ 2.5. Adding serum ferritin increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.853 to 0.899 in the training cohort and from 0.842 to 0.868 in the internal validation cohort, with good calibration, greater decision-curve net benefit, and improved risk reclassification.
CONCLUSIONS: Serum ferritin provided incremental predictive value for coronary artery aneurysms at 4 to 8 weeks after the onset of Kawasaki disease. The ferritin-based model improved predictive performance in internal validation and warrants multicentre external validation to assess its generalisability and clinical applicability.

Title: Three-dimensional-printed heart models as medical educational tools in cardiac catheterisation: randomised controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Simulation-based tools are increasingly used to improve procedural training in medical education. However, access to affordable and anatomically accurate models for teaching cardiac catheterisation remains limited. This study aimed to enhance medical education by developing a cost-effective three-dimensional-printed heart model for teaching basic cardiac catheterisation to medical students.
METHODS: This open-label, single-site randomised controlled trial was conducted at Fu Jen Catholic University. Undergraduate and postgraduate medical students were recruited and randomly assigned to either a three-dimensional model group with hands-on practice or a control group receiving slide-based instruction. The effectiveness of a custom-made three-dimensional-printed heart model in teaching cardiac catheterisation was evaluated. A total of 35 participants were enrolled, including 18 in the three-dimensional model group and 17 in the control group.
RESULTS: Overall posttest scores were comparable between groups. However, among undergraduate medical students, posttest scores were significantly higher in the three-dimensional model group than in the control group (P = 0.03). The production cost of each three-dimensional-printed heart model was capped at US＄200, indicating that the model is a cost-effective educational tool.
CONCLUSION: Three-dimensional-printed heart models provide a feasible and cost-effective approach for teaching cardiac catheterisation in medical education. Their educational benefits appeared more evident among undergraduate medical students. Integrating such models according to learners' training stages and procedural complexity may further enhance training effectiveness.

Title: The role of T-peak to T-end, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance in the differential diagnosis of myocarditis.
Abstract:
AIM: Paediatric myocarditis, a rare inflammatory cardiomyopathy (incidence 1-2/100,000 annually), challenges emergency diagnosis due to nonspecific symptoms mimicking common illnesses. This study assessed electrocardiographic markers of ventricular repolarisation heterogeneity-T-peak to T-end interval, T-peak to T-end/QT, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratios, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance-for diagnosing myocarditis and predicting ventricular arrhythmia risk in children aged 0-18 years.
METHODS: Retrospective case-control study of 76 myocarditis patients (diagnosed by clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and cardiac MRI criteria) presenting to our paediatric emergency department from January 1, 2024, to May 30, 2025, versus 75 age-matched healthy controls. Electrocardiographic parameters were measured in leads DII and V5. Receiver operating characteristic analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of T-peak to T-end and T peak-to-end/corrected QT (Lead II (Derivation II)). Myocarditis cases stratified by arrhythmia development (with: n = 28; without: n = 48); groups compared via t-tests, Mann-Whitney U, and chi-square (p < 0.05 significant).
RESULTS: Myocarditis group: 23 females (30.2%) and 53 males (69.8%); mean age 12.0 ± 4.7 years. Controls: 39 females (52.0%), 36 males (48.0%); mean age 10.3 ± 4.9 years (p = 0.03). Receiver operating characteristic (Lead II (Derivation II)): T-peak to T-end cut-off 62 ms (sensitivity 69.3%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.725, p < 0.001); T peak-to-end/corrected QT cut-off 0.19 (sensitivity 50.7%, specificity 78.9%, area under the curve 0.625, p < 0.05).The arrhythmia subgroup showed corrected QT prolongation (470 vs. 435 ms, V5; p < 0.001), T-peak to T-end (110 vs. 90 ms, V5; p < 0.001), higher T peak-to-end/corrected QT, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance (both p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The T-peak to T-end interval, T peak-to-end/corrected QT ratio, and index of cardiac electrophysiological balance provide high-specificity, noninvasive electrocardiographic biomarkers for paediatric myocarditis diagnosis in the ED. Corrected QT and T-peak to T-end prolongation signals repolarisation heterogeneity and arrhythmia risk, supporting routine triage integration for early risk stratification.

Title: Real-World Comparison of Cardiorenal Outcomes With SGLT-2 Inhibitors Versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes.
Abstract:
AIMS: To compare cardiorenal outcomes, mortality and safety between sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) in adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, new-user cohort study using the TriNetX global federated health research network. We identified 249 237 propensity score-matched pairs (498 474 total patients) who initiated SGLT-2i or GLP-1 RA between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was a kidney failure/death composite, defined as kidney failure, dialysis, kidney transplantation or all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included composite cardiovascular events, mortality and safety profiles.
RESULTS: SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of the kidney failure/death composite compared with GLP-1 RA (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). For the kidney-specific component, SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of kidney failure, dialysis or kidney transplantation (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.71-0.78), while all-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.88-0.93). The composite cardiovascular outcome (myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest or death) was broadly comparable between groups (HR: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-1.00).
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT-2i initiation was associated with lower risks of kidney failure-related outcomes and all-cause mortality compared with GLP-1 RA initiation, while cardiovascular outcomes were broadly comparable. These findings may inform individualized treatment selection in adults with T2D.

Title: Intensive pharmacist-led guideline-directed medical therapy for hospitalized heart failure patients: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of pharmaceutical health care and sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) improves outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). However, implementation remains suboptimal, and evidence for inpatient pharmacist-led interventions is limited. We evaluated the association between a pharmacist-led electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded checklist and GDMT use in hospitalized patients with acute heart failure.
METHODS: A single-center, retrospective, non-randomized study with a historical control group was conducted. Adult patients hospitalized with acute heart failure from October 2021 to March 2023 were enrolled. Patients admitted between October 2022 and March 2023 formed the pharmacist-led GDMT checklist intervention group, whereas those admitted between October 2021 and March 2022 served as historical controls. Primary outcomes were discharge implementation and new initiation rates of individual GDMT agents (renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, beta-blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [MRA], sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors [SGLT2i]) and quadruple therapy. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression was performed for quadruple therapy use at discharge in patients with HFrEF. Secondary outcomes included target-dose achievement, exploratory 90-day heart failure readmission, and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 103 patients were included (49 controls, 54 intervention). Among patients with HFrEF (22 controls, 23 intervention), the intervention group had higher prescription rates of MRA (87.0% vs. 59.1%, p = 0.047) and SGLT2i (95.7% vs. 72.7%, p = 0.047). Quadruple therapy was achieved in 78.3% vs. 40.9% (p = 0.016). The proportion of patients who newly achieved quadruple therapy during hospitalization was also higher in the intervention group (83.3% vs. 35.0%, p = 0.038). In the exploratory multivariable model, the intervention remained associated with higher odds of quadruple therapy use at discharge. Target-dose achievement was similar between groups. In mildly reduced/preserved EF, discharge SGLT2i use tended to be higher in the intervention group (p = 0.062). Exploratory 90-day outcomes showed no clear between-group differences and were limited by incomplete follow-up and insufficient statistical power.
CONCLUSIONS: The pharmacist-led EMR-embedded checklist intervention was associated with higher discharge implementation and in-hospital initiation of HFrEF-directed GDMT, particularly MRA, SGLT2i, and quadruple therapy. This simple checklist-based approach may support evidence-based pharmacotherapy optimization and warrants confirmation in larger multicenter studies with long-term follow-up.
Category: Randomized Controlled Trials; Observational Studies; Guidelines & Statements

Title: Temporal associations between severe infection and long-term risk of incident arrhythmias: a population-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The long-term impact of severe infection on arrhythmia risk across the cardiac rhythm spectrum remains incompletely characterized. We investigated the association between hospital-treated infection and incident arrhythmias, examining temporal patterns, pathogen and site specificity, and cumulative effects.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective analysis of 465,374 UK Biobank participants. Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models were adjusted for sociodemographic factors, lifestyle behaviors, clinical comorbidities, and biochemical parameters. Comprehensive analyses assessed infection timing (1-30, 31-365, ≥366 days), type (bacterial, viral, sepsis), site, and recurrence. Findings were validated in ARIC and CHS cohorts.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 14.2 years, 70,527 (15.2%) participants had a severe infection. Infection was associated with a significantly increased risk of any incident arrhythmia (adjusted HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.80-1.90). Risks were elevated across all specific arrhythmias, being particularly pronounced for sudden cardiac arrest (HR 2.79, 2.54-3.07), ventricular arrhythmias (HR 3.11, 2.80-3.45), and AV block (HR 3.03, 2.83-3.25). Risk demonstrated temporal gradient, peaking at 1-30 days (HR 11.40, 10.44-12.47 for any arrhythmia) and remaining elevated long-term (HR 1.58, 1.53-1.63 at ≥366 days). Sepsis posed the highest risk among infection types, while pneumonia was most hazardous among sites. Recurrent infections showed a dose-response relationship, with second infections conferring greater risk than first infections (HR 2.51 vs 1.85). Population attributable fractions for infection reached 16.6% for AV block, comparable to traditional risk factors. External validation confirmed these associations.
CONCLUSION: Severe infection is associated with increased long-term risks of various arrhythmias, with variations by time since infection, infection characteristics, and recurrence history. These observations suggest that a history of severe infection may provide modest additional information for arrhythmia risk assessment, though its contribution is substantially smaller than that of traditional risk factors such as hypertension.

Title: Effectiveness, safety and persistence of filgotinib in rheumatoid arthritis with a specific focus on difficult-to-treat patients: results from a multicentre observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Filgotinib, a preferential JAK1 inhibitor, is among the most recently approved therapies for rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Real-world evidence remains limited, particularly for difficult-to-treat RA (D2T) patients, who are underrepresented in clinical trials. We therefore evaluated the efficacy, safety, and treatment persistence of filgotinib in a large cohort of patients with RA, with a specific focus on those with D2T RA.
METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included patients with RA (ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria) treated with filgotinib across nine Italian centres. Patients were followed every 3-6 months for up to 3 years, with collection of clinical variables, laboratory data, and adverse events (AEs).
RESULTS: A total of 254 patients were included (mean age 58 ± 12 years; 85% female), of whom 47% had D2T disease. Disease activity indices (CDAI, DAS28-CRP, PGA, PhGA) improved significantly from baseline (p < 0.001), with remission rates reaching 41.3% (CDAI) and 70.5% (DAS28-CRP). Glucocorticoid (GC) use decreased from 64.4% to 32.6%. Improvements in disease activity and the GC-sparing effect were comparable between D2T RA and non-D2T RA patients. During follow-up, 153 AEs were reported, including 13 serious AEs and one infection-related death; non-serious infections were the most frequent events. Lipid profile remained stable throughout the study period, and two major cardiovascular events were reported. Treatment persistence was 88.4% at 6 months and 68% at 24 months, with no significant differences between D2T RA and non-D2T RA patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Filgotinib demonstrated effective disease control, good safety and high treatment persistence in a real-world RA population, including a high proportion of D2T patients.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Pregnancy loss and prevalent cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a two-stage individual participant data analysis of CHARLS, ELSA, and HRS.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is associated with substantially higher mortality and reduced life expectancy. Pregnancy loss is common and has been linked to later cardiovascular risk, but multinational evidence using harmonized individual participant data and CMM as the outcome remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the cross-sectional association between self-reported pregnancy loss and prevalent cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) among middle-aged and older women in three nationally representative ageing cohorts, and to evaluate the consistency of findings across countries.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional analysis using the last valid observation for each woman as the individual-level main analysis, with person-wave analyses as sensitivity analyses. The study did not model incident CMM or CMM progression. Country-specific estimates were combined using a two-stage individual participant data approach.
DATA SOURCES: The China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2018), the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA, 2002-2018), and the Health and Retirement Study (HRS, 2017/2019 Life History Mail Survey).
PARTICIPANTS: Women aged 45 years or older with available pregnancy history and cardiometabolic outcome data (CHARLS: n = 7,514; ELSA: n = 3,773; HRS: n = 1,630; total N = 12,917).
EXPOSURE: Self-reported history of pregnancy loss. In CHARLS and HRS, pregnancy loss corresponded to miscarriage or stillbirth; in ELSA, the available variable combined miscarriage, stillbirth, and induced abortion and could not be disaggregated.
MAIN OUTCOME: CMM, defined as the coexistence of at least two of five self-reported physician-diagnosed conditions: hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, heart disease, and stroke.
RESULTS: The prevalence of pregnancy loss was 25.2% in CHARLS, 24.9% in ELSA, and 35.3% in HRS; the individual-level prevalence of CMM was 30.1%, 46.6%, and 36.9%, respectively. In the fully adjusted individual-level model (M3), pregnancy loss was associated with higher odds of prevalent CMM in CHARLS (OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.20-1.75, p < 0.001), but not in ELSA (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.90-1.29, p = 0.424) or HRS (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 0.71-2.17, p = 0.455). The DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooled OR was 1.24 (95% CI: 0.99-1.56, p = 0.062; HKSJ 95% CI: 0.82-1.89). In the person-wave M3 sensitivity analysis, the pooled OR was 1.15 (95% CI: 0.98-1.34, p = 0.083; HKSJ 95% CI: 0.77-1.72). In parity-adjusted person-wave analyses restricted to ELSA and HRS, the pooled OR was 1.02 (95% CI: 0.81-1.29, p = 0.849).
CONCLUSIONS: The individual-level main analysis suggested that the association between pregnancy loss and prevalent CMM was primarily observed in CHARLS, whereas no statistically significant association was observed in ELSA or HRS. The three-country pooled estimate did not reach statistical significance and was attenuated after parity adjustment in ELSA and HRS. Given the cross-sectional design, the heterogeneous exposure definition in ELSA, sample reduction in HRS, and sensitivity of estimates to analytic choices, the findings should be interpreted as exploratory evidence rather than evidence of a temporal or causal association.

Title: Differentiated effect of hypothermia versus normothermia after cardiac arrest by neurological status and clinical correlates of ischemic burden.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The optimal temperature target after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain, as major randomized trials have not demonstrated a clear benefit of lower-target hypothermia compared with normothermia. Despite this, patients with differing degrees of ischemic burden or early neurological injury may hypothetically respond differently to temperature targets, raising the possibility of heterogeneous treatment effects. This study aimed to determine whether outcomes differ after OHCA with 33 °C versus controlled normothermia (36.0-37.7 °C) according to correlates of ischemic burden and neurological findings at hospital admission.
METHODS: This secondary analysis of the TTM and TTM2 trials employed effect-based machine learning to probe for heterogeneous treatment effects. Causal forests and Bayesian additive regression trees (BART) estimated individualized treatment effects (ITE) based on ischemia duration, prehospital factors, and neurological examination findings at hospital admission. Treatment effect modifier variable importance parameter (TEM-VIP) analysis ranked the baseline variables most likely to modify effect. The primary outcome was six-month all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was poor functional outcome (modified Rankin scale score 4-6). Primary analyses evaluated potential heterogeneity within each trial, while secondary analyses pooled all participants.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: All 2789 adult OHCA patients from the trials' primary analyses were included (median age 65 years (IQR 56-73), 79.9% male). Death occurred in 49.4% of patients in the 33 °C group, and in 47.9% in the controlled normothermia group. Variation in six-month mortality ITEs estimated from ischemic burden correlates and initial neurological findings was minimal, and no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was identified across all methods and analysis populations. In the pooled analysis, estimated conditional mean mortality risk difference ranged from - 1.2% to 2.1% in causal forest (p = 0.99), and from - 0.5% to 1.5% in BART, with posterior probabilities for hypothermia benefit ranging from 42% to 53%. Absolute subgroup estimates in TEM-VIP analysis were small and non-significant. Results were consistent for the six-month functional outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Among TTM and TTM2 participants randomized to 33 °C versus controlled normothermia post-OHCA, no evidence of detectable heterogeneity of treatment effect based on available clinical correlates of ischemic burden or initial neurological findings was identified, with minimal estimated variation in treatment effect.

Title: Transcutaneous low-level vagus nerve stimulation for the prevention of postoperative atrial fibrillation after cardiac valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common complications following cardiac surgery, with reported incidence rates reaching up to 44%. Transcutaneous low-level vagus nerve stimulation (TLL-VNS) has shown potential in reducing the risk of postoperative AF by modulating autonomic nervous system activity, suppressing inflammation, and regulating atrial ganglionic function.
METHODS: The Vagus-Heart Trial is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled study designed to evaluate the efficacy of TLL-VNS in preventing postoperative AF. A total of 140 patients undergoing elective cardiac valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) are randomly assigned to receive either active TLL-VNS or sham stimulation. The primary endpoint is the incidence of AF within the first week after surgery. Secondary endpoints include the duration of AF within the first week after surgery, surgical parameters, vital signs, inflammatory markers, renal function, surgical prognosis, and stress response biomarkers.
DISCUSSION: This trial is the first large-scale, randomized, sham-controlled study to evaluate TLL-VNS for the prevention of postoperative AF in patients undergoing cardiac valve surgery with CPB. If proven effective, TLL-VNS could represent a novel, non-invasive, and cost-effective strategy to enhance postoperative recovery and reduce the burden of AF in this high-risk population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chictr.org.cn Identifer: ChiCTR2400080750. Registered on 6 February 2024.

Title: A structured progressive training intervention for chest compressions among primary health care personnel: a multicentre pilot non-randomised quasi-experimental study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-quality chest compressions are a key component of effective cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). Retention of CPR skills among healthcare personnel remains limited over time, particularly in settings with low exposure to cardiac arrest. This study assessed whether a brief, 25-min structured progressive training intervention was associated with improved chest compression quality among primary health care (PHC) personnel and whether skills were retained after three months.
METHODS: A multicentre, quasi-experimental, non-randomised, single-group pre-post study was conducted in 16 PHC clinics. Chest compression quality was assessed at baseline (T0), immediately after training (T1), and at three-month follow-up (T2) using a manikin-based feedback system. The primary outcome was the overall compression score. Secondary outcomes included compression depth, hand position, chest recoil, adequate depth, and compression rate. Within-subject changes over time were analysed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
RESULTS: A total of 152 participants completed the baseline and immediate post-training practical assessments, and 125 completed the three-month follow-up. The median overall compression score increased from 19 at baseline to 84 immediately after training and remained above baseline at three months (73; T0-T1 and T0-T2, both p < 0.001). All compression parameters improved immediately after training. At three months, some parameters had declined, but all remained above baseline values.
CONCLUSIONS: The intervention was associated with improved simulated chest-compression performance among personnel working in settings with low exposure to cardiac arrest, with partial retention at three months.

Title: Application of bronchoscopy in children with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the value of bronchoscopy in the clinical diagnosis and management of primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on six genetically confirmed PCD children admitted to the Department of Respiratory Intervention at Jinan Children's Hospital between October 2020 and August 2024. Bronchoscopic procedures were performed, including collection of specimens for microbiological testing, bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) for cytological analysis, and interventional therapies such as local drug/saline lavage and forceps-assisted clearance. Mucosal biopsies were attempted in selected cases, but ultrastructural analysis was not consistently reliable.
RESULTS: Bronchoscopy revealed copious secretions and a characteristic fish-bone appearance (defined as tortuous, dilated segmental bronchi with prominent transverse ridging of the mucosa, resembling the spine of a fish) in the airways of all six PCD patients. Based on endoscopic assessment and microbiological results from BAL fluid, the anti-infective treatment regimen was adjusted for one patient. All patients underwent forceps-assisted clearance and lavage therapy, with two patients requiring two lavage sessions due to severe infection. BALF cytology revealed a predominantly neutrophilic and lymphocytic inflammation. No severe complications occurred during or after the procedures.
CONCLUSION: In this small cohort of six pediatric PCD patients, bronchoscopy appeared to be a safe and potentially useful integrated approach, combining disease assessment, and therapeutic intervention (airway clearance). The procedure also provided valuable insights into the airway inflammatory and microbiological phenotype. However, given the preliminary nature of these findings and the limited sample size, larger prospective studies are needed to confirm the role of bronchoscopy in routine PCD management.

Title: Associations of anthropometric indices with all-cause and cause-specific mortality among US adults with a self-reported history of cancer: a population-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for cancer incidence and mortality. Body mass index (BMI) does not adequately characterize body shape or fat distribution. Whether a body shape index (ABSI) and body roundness index (BRI) are associated with mortality among adults with a history of cancer remains uncertain.
METHODS: We analyzed 3,230 NHANES participants (2003-2018) using survey-weighted Cox models adjusted for sociodemographic, behavioral, and cancer-related factors. Nonlinear and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During a survey-weighted median potential follow-up of 7.9 years, 937 all-cause, 315 cancer, and 197 CVD deaths occurred. In the primary model, each 1-SD higher ABSI was associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.11-1.38) and CVD mortality (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.26-1.90), but not cancer mortality (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.96-1.29). Continuous BRI and BMI were not independently associated with the outcomes. Underweight BMI was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.46-4.08). BMI had a nonlinear association with all-cause mortality (P for nonlinearity = 0.002). ABSI findings remained similar across sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Higher ABSI was associated with higher all-cause and CVD mortality among U.S. adults with a self-reported history of cancer. Further studies are needed to confirm these associations.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Association between glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio and risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio has been proposed as a potential marker reflecting metabolic stress and immune-inflammatory status. This retrospective cohort study investigated the association between glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio and in-hospital mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke using the MIMIC-IV database from 2008 to 2019.
METHODS: The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. The glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio was analyzed as both a continuous variable and a categorical variable according to quartiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals, with adjustment for potential confounders. Restricted cubic spline analysis was performed to assess potential nonlinearity. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: Among 7,659 screened patients, 2,565 met the inclusion criteria. The overall in-hospital mortality rate was 18.4% (473/2,565). Patients in the highest glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio quartile (Q4, ≥ 9.4) had a significantly higher risk of in-hospital mortality than those in the lowest quartile (Q1, < 3.4) in the fully adjusted model (hazard ratio = 1.54, 95% confidence interval: 1.12-2.14, P = 0.009). When analyzed as a continuous variable, each 10-unit increase in the glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio was independently associated with a 14% higher risk of in-hospital mortality (hazard ratio = 1.14, 95% confidence interval: 1.05-1.25, P = 0.003). Restricted cubic spline modeling indicated a linear relationship (P for nonlinearity = 0.584). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations. A higher glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio was also associated with increased 90-day mortality (hazard ratio = 1.13, 95% confidence interval: 1.04-1.22, P = 0.005).
CONCLUSIONS: An elevated glucose-to-lymphocyte ratio was independently and linearly associated with increased in-hospital mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke, suggesting that it may serve as a practical prognostic marker. Further prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

Title: Prognostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance in acute myocarditis: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of late gadolinium enhancement and narrative literature review of parametric mapping.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Limited data exist on the prognostic value of parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) in patients with acute myocarditis (AM). This meta-analysis aimed to investigate the prognostic value of LGE as assessed by using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with AM, including more recent evidence. Additionally, the prognostic value of CMR parametric mapping was narratively reviewed.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The systematic search was conducted in the PubMed and Scopus databases from inception to January 17, 2026 (PubMed) and January 20th 2026 (Scopus). 1296 records were found through the search. Finally, sixteen studies were included in this systematic review. Thirteen studies were included in the meta-analysis on association between LGE and clinical outcomes in AM. The composite endpoint was defined as MACE and/or one of the following endpoints: all-cause death, heart failure decompensation requiring hospitalization, heart transplantation, and recurrent AM. MACE was defined as a composite of cardiovascular death (including sudden death), sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, complete atrioventricular heart block requiring a pacemaker, and cardiogenic shock. Five studies were reviewed for the prognostic value of parametric mapping parameters. After initial calculations, it appeared that studies using broader composite endpoints than only MACE introduced substantial heterogeneity. Therefore, we have additionally conducted analysis incorporating only eight studies with MACE as the endpoint.
RESULTS: The presence of LGE was associated with higher odds of the composite endpoint. The unadjusted pooled OR demonstrated a significant relationship between the presence of LGE and higher chances of the composite endpoint (ORLGE(+) vs. LGE(-)[95% CI] = 3.02 [1.40, 6.51], p < 0.001) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 81.98%, p < 0.0001) On the qualitative level, results obtained in the MACE studies subgroup remained the same (ORLGE(+) vs. LGE(-)[95% CI] = 2.88 [2.01, 4.13], p < 0.0001). No clear evidence of publication bias was detected; however, power to detect small-study effects is limited and results should be interpreted cautiously. The prognostic value of parametric mapping parameters did not undergo meta-analysis and was reviewed narratively due to the shortage of the respective data. The data on the prognostic value of native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) are controversial and limited.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on the findings, the presence of LGE appears to be associated with an adverse prognosis in patients with AM. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of substantial heterogeneity among studies and the unadjusted effect estimations. Evidence regarding the prognostic value of CMR-derived parametric mapping remains limited. Large, prospective, well-designed studies are needed to determine the incremental prognostic value of parametric mapping beyond LGE for risk stratification and outcome prediction in patients with AM.

Title: Platelet trajectory patterns and 28-day mortality in ICU stroke patients: a retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Platelet abnormalities are common in critically ill patients, but dynamic trajectory patterns and their prognostic value in intensive care unit (ICU) stroke patients remain unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,562 ICU stroke patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database (version 3.1). Latent class trajectory models (LCTM) were used to identify platelet trajectory patterns during the first 5 days of ICU admission. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to assess the association between trajectory groups and 28-day mortality. Exploratory effect decomposition analysis was conducted to explore the relative contribution of baseline platelet levels and subsequent platelet decline to prognosis.
RESULTS: Four distinct platelet trajectory groups were identified: High-Declining (14.7%), Moderate-Low Stable (52.4%), Low-Rising (4.5%), and Moderate-High Stable (28.4%). The High-Declining group had the highest 28-day mortality (34.1% vs. 20.4% in the Moderate-Low Stable group, P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, the High-Declining group was associated with a 56% increase in mortality risk compared with the Moderate-Low Stable group (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.56, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.17-2.07, P = 0.002). Exploratory effect decomposition analysis revealed a suppression pattern: the direct protective effect of higher Day 2 platelet was offset by an indirect harmful effect mediated through greater subsequent platelet decline (Average Component Mediation Effect [ACME] = 0.017 on the probability-difference scale, 95% CI: 0.010-0.026, P < 0.001), suggesting that rapid platelet decline may reflect a high-risk phenotypic pattern associated with this trajectory group.
CONCLUSIONS: Platelet trajectory patterns are associated with 28-day mortality and may serve as prognostic indicators in ICU stroke patients. A high baseline platelet level with rapid decline represents the highest-risk phenotype and, if confirmed in future prospective studies, may help identify patients requiring closer clinical evaluation to screen for underlying deteriorating conditions.

Title: Low-kV high-pitch one-scan aortic and coronary CT angiography using dual-source photon-counting CT: comparison with separate acquisition strategies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with aortic diseases, coronary CT angiography (CCTA) is performed for preoperative evaluation of coronary artery disease, often in combination with CT angiography of thoracic and abdominal aorta (CTAO) within the same examination. A dual-source photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) offers advantages including improved dose efficiency and reduction of electronic noise, which might help maintain image quality even at low tube voltages. This study aimed to compare a low-kV one-scan CCTA/CTAO protocol with a low-kV dedicated CCTA followed by a higher-kV CTAO acquisition (separate-scan) regarding radiation dose and image quality.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 42 patients who underwent CCTA and CTAO using PCD-CT for preoperative CAD screening for aortic disease: 19 had separate-scan, 23 had one-scan CCTA and CTAO. Image quality for CCTA was assessed using a four-point scale (excellent, good, fair, non-diagnostic). Image quality for CTAO was assessed using a five-point scale (excellent, good, moderate, poor, non-diagnostic).
RESULTS: Radiation dose was significantly lower in the one-scan group compared to the separate-scan group (mean total dose-length product, 175.8 ± 71.1 vs. 769.4 ± 212.1 mGy·cm; P < 0.001). For CCTA, subjective image quality scores were comparable between the two groups (P = 0.537), although the separate-scan group showed significantly higher objective CNR compared to the one-scan group (P =0.025). For CTAO, the subjective image quality was significantly superior in the one-scan group (P < 0.01), despite comparable CNR between the groups (P = 0.13). The proportions of good or excellent ratings were 97.1% and 98.4% for CCTA, and 85.1% and 91.3% for CTAO in the separate-scan and one-scan groups, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The low-kV one-scan strategy using PCD-CT substantially reduced radiation dose while maintaining comparable subjective CCTA quality and superior subjective CTAO quality. This approach may provide a dose-efficient option in selected patients requiring primary aortic assessment with concomitant coronary screening; however, its adequacy for preoperative CAD screening remains to be established.

Title: Association between the time window of rash recurrence and the risk of renal involvement within 6 months in children with immunoglobulin A vasculitis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal involvement is a major determinant of long-term outcome in childhood immunoglobulin A vasculitis (IgAV). We examined whether the timing of the initial rash recurrence was associated with renal involvement within 180 days, while accounting for temporal ordering, rash phenotype, and surveillance intensity.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 302 children with newly diagnosed IgAV from 2020 to 2024. Rash recurrence was modeled as a time-varying exposure: all children entered a not-yet-recurrent state and, at the initial recurrence, moved to the ≤ 14-, 15-30-, 31-60-, or 61-180-day state. The primary outcome was the initial confirmed renal event within 180 days. Multivariable time-varying Cox regression, Simon-Makuch curves with the Mantel-Byar test, and prespecified sensitivity analyses were used.
RESULTS: Ninety-four children (31.1%) developed renal involvement. Seventy events occurred after documented recurrence and 24 while children remained in the not-yet-recurrent state; eight of the latter recurred only after the renal event and were not retrospectively reclassified. Compared with the not-yet-recurrent state, recurrence at 15-30 days (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-3.37; P = 0.040), at 31-60 days (aHR, 3.18; 95% CI, 1.73-5.83; P < 0.001), and at 61-180 days (aHR, 2.72; 95% CI, 1.25-5.90; P = 0.011) were associated with higher renal-event hazards, whereas recurrence within 14 days was not significantly associated. Extensive and bullous skin involvement was more frequent in unadjusted comparisons but was not independently associated in separate exploratory models. Children with recurrence recorded before event or censoring had more clinical-contact and urine-assessment days. In the surveillance-complete subset, associations persisted for 31-60 and 61-180 days, whereas the 15-30-day estimate was attenuated. Simon-Makuch curves differed (Mantel-Byar P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Delayed rash recurrence, particularly at 31-60 days, was associated with renal involvement within 6 months. Standard renal surveillance remains necessary for every child with IgAV; recurrence timing may provide additional information for identifying children who warrant closer vigilance. Residual surveillance bias and the observational design limit causal interpretation.

Title: The severity of immediate hepatocellular damage in the first two days after liver transplantation predicts long-term graft survival.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early allograft dysfunction (EAD) is associated with graft loss up to 5-years after liver transplantation (LT), but longer follow-up data are not available. We investigated which laboratory tests used in the diagnosis of EAD were most strongly associated with long-term LT outcome.
METHODS: We enrolled 101 consecutive HCV-negative adult patients, who underwent their first non-urgent LT between 2001 and 2011. Demographic and clinical data, including graft steatosis on pre-ischemia protocol biopsy, were collected for both recipient and donor.
RESULTS: The median follow-up was 13.7 years. Among the laboratory tests used for the diagnosis of EAD, graft loss was more strongly associated with serum aminotransferase on the first two postoperative days (POD) than with INR and total bilirubin on POD7. In multivariate Cox analysis, graft loss was associated with a new index of immediate hepatocellular damage (IHD), calculated as the sum of AST and ALT on POD1 and POD2 (HR = 3.27, CI: 1.51-7.08, p = 0.0001), outperforming EAD (HR = 2.27, CI: 1.11-4.62, p = 0.020). Risk factors for IHD were older transplant era, recipient obesity, and graft large droplet steatosis (15%).
CONCLUSIONS: IHD is a strong predictor of long-term graft loss after LT and outperform traditional EAD criteria. Steatotic grafts should increasingly be subjected to defatting methods, and their use should be limited in obese recipients.

Title: The relationship between endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in acute myocardial infarction patients admitted in emergency department.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In this study, we aimed to explore the relationship between endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients.
METHOD: This retrospective study was based on the clinical data of the AMI patients admitted in emergency department of Changsha Central Hospital from August 2020 to January 2023. Different models were constructed by multivariable regression analysis for investigating the relationship between EASIX index and MACE risk. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was utilized for further validating the potential nonlinear relationship. The receiver-operator characteristic (ROC) analysis of EASIX index for predicting MACE risk in AMI was done.
RESULTS: 805 AMI patients with 193 individuals in MACE group were included. After adjusting potential confounders, with per unit increasement in EASIX index, the risk of MACE increased by 16% (OR = 1.16, 95%CI: 1.04-1.29, p = 0.0054). The RCS showed the nonlinear relationship between EASIX index and the incidence of MACE was not significant. The predictive performances of EASIX index were showed as follow: an AUC of 0.687 (95%CI:0.642-0.732) and a cut-off value of 2.42.
CONCLUSION: A significant relationship between EASIX index and the incidence of MACE in AMI was identified.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Validation of the BREST score for diagnosing acute heart failure in emergency department patients with dyspnea: added value of NT-proBNP and biomarkers.
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a leading cause of dyspnea among patients presenting to the emergency department (ED), necessitating timely diagnostic approaches. The BREST score is a pragmatic bedside tool developed to support the early identification of AHF using clinical and electrocardiographic findings. This study aimed to prospectively validate the diagnostic performance of the BREST score and assess the incremental diagnostic value of NT-proBNP and selected inflammatory biomarkers.
METHODS: This study prospectively enrolled consecutive adult patients presenting with dyspnea to the ED of Gaziantep City Hospital between January 2024 and May 2025. At presentation, BREST score components were recorded using standardized clinical forms. Biomarker levels, including NT-proBNP, C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), were collected during routine diagnostic evaluation. The diagnosis of AHF was established by board-certified cardiologists, blinded to the BREST score, through adjudication of echocardiographic findings, laboratory data (including NT-proBNP), and clinical documentation. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Among 1215 screened patients, 1000 were included in the final analysis. The median age was 68 years (IQR: 59-76), and 48% were male. AHF was diagnosed in 736 patients (73.6%) based on the reference standard. At the optimal BREST cut-off (≥ 5), the score yielded an AUC of 0.874 (95% CI: 0.849-0.900), with 93.8% sensitivity and 69.3% specificity. The addition of NT-proBNP improved the AUC to 0.895 (95% CI: 0.873-0.917), while the full biomarker panel provided no significant additional benefit (AUC: 0.898). In subgroup analysis, the BREST score retained good discrimination in de novo heart failure (AUC 0.824) and performed strongly in known chronic heart failure (AUC 0.943); this difference indicates that its diagnostic performance is not identical across presentation types.
CONCLUSION: This prospective validation demonstrated that the BREST score is an accurate and efficient diagnostic tool for AHF in ED patients presenting with dyspnea. Its reliance on readily available clinical and ECG data supports its integration into routine ED workflows. Adding NT-proBNP produced a modest, non-significant numerical increase in discrimination, which may still be clinically useful in cases of intermediate clinical probability, while other inflammatory biomarkers added no further value.

Title: Revalidation of the M-DIRECT scale in prehospital identification of acute stroke patients for endovascular treatment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The M-DIRECT scale was implemented for prehospital triage of acute stroke, such that patients with an M-DIRECT score ≥ 2 are transferred directly to an endovascular treatment (EVT)-ready center (EVT-C) instead of a nearer stroke unit (SU). Our aim is to evaluate the performance of M-DIRECT at five years post-implementation.
METHODS: A prospective observational study of consecutive prehospital code stroke patients attended by regional emergency medical services during 2022 in an urban network of 6.75 million inhabitants. Basal characteristics, time metrics, presence of large or medium vessel occlusion (LVO/MeVO), and treatments were compared between EVT-C and non-EVT-ready SU groups according to the M-DIRECT score.
RESULTS: A total of 1950 patients were included. Of these, 992 (51%) were first attended at an EVT-C and 958 at a nearer SU (49%). Furthermore, 706 (36%) patients were M-DIRECT positive, of which 413 (58%) had an LVO/MeVO, and 354 (50%) underwent EVT. Of 1244 M-DIRECT negative patients, 204 (16%) had an LVO/MeVO and 105 (8%) underwent EVT. M-DIRECT showed 77% sensitivity, 76% specificity, and 77% diagnostic accuracy for EVT from prehospital triage, with an AUC (95% CI) of 0.768 (0.742-0.793). A positive M-DIRECT score was independently associated with EVT adjusted for age, sex, NIHSS, and unknown onset, with aOR (95% CI) 3.05 (1.65-5.68), and consistently across every arterial segment. Only 46 out of 459 (10%) EVT required a secondary transfer.
CONCLUSIONS: M-DIRECT scale accurately identifies EVT candidates prehospital, reduces secondary transfers, and independently predicts EVT likelihood across different vessel occlusions.

Title: A Low HALP score is an independent predictor of coronary artery ectasia: a retrospective comparative study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine whether the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score is independently associated with the presence and angiographic severity of coronary artery ectasia (CAE), and to assess its potential role as a diagnostic inflammatory-nutritional biomarker in this population.
METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study, the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) scores were calculated using routine laboratory parameters obtained at admission. Logistic regression models were constructed to identify independent predictors of CAE. Furthermore, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine the diagnostic performance of the HALP score, and the association between the HALP score and the angiographic extent of CAE was evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 628 patients (290 CAE, 338 controls), the median HALP score was significantly lower in the CAE group (4.14 vs. 4.99, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis identified a lower HALP score as an independent predictor of CAE (OR: 0.752, 95% CI: 0.655-0.865, p < 0.001).
