A HALP score of 4.569 predicted CAE with 60.1% sensitivity and 57.2% specificity (AUC: 0.650). The score was not associated with the angiographic extent of CAE (p = 0.461).
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, a low HALP score is significantly and independently associated with the presence of coronary artery ectasia in patients without obstructive coronary artery disease, reflecting the underlying systemic inflammatory and nutritional milieu. This easily obtainable index may serve as a useful complementary biomarker for assessing inflammatory burden in CAE patients, although further large-scale prospective studies are warranted to confirm its prognostic and clinical utility.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study is a retrospective observational analysis and does not report the results of a health care intervention.

Title: Serial cardiac ultrasound in acutely ill adults: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary symptoms frequently prompt emergency department (ED) visits. Serial as-sessment of dynamic cardiac ultrasound parameters may support monitoring, but their asso-ciation with patient outcomes and role in guiding management is uncertain. This systematic review evaluated whether serial changes in ejection fraction (EF), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), and the right ventricular-to-left ventricular (RV/LV) ratio are associated with mortality, readmissions, length of stay, or intensive care unit trans-fer in acutely ill patients.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase (Ovid), CENTRAL (Wiley), Scopus (Elsevier), Web of Science (Clarivate), Google Scholar, ProQuest, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the International Clini-cal Trials Registry Platform. The initial search was conducted on 16 April 2024 and updated on 31 October 2025. We included randomized and non-randomized trials and observational stud-ies of adults (≥18 years) undergoing at least two in-hospital cardiac ultrasound assessments and reported mortality, readmission, length of stay, and/or intensive care unit transfer. Risk of bias was assessed with study design-specific tools. Results were summarized using synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM).
RESULTS: Of 15,174 screened records, 11 studies with a total of 941 patients were included. Study popu-lations were defined by presenting symptoms (dyspnea, hypotension) or by clinical conditions (toxicological, infectious, and cardiopulmonary diseases). Echocardiography was most used, and patients underwent 3-4 scans during admission. Overall risk of bias was moderate to high. Four studies compared serial changes in EF, TAPSE, and/or the RV/LV ratio with outcomes and found no consistent pattern. One randomized study evaluated ultrasound-guided treatment and found no difference compared with usual care. Across studies, EF, TAPSE, and RV/LV ratio were generally stable or improved over time.
CONCLUSION: Available evidence is limited and does not demonstrate a consistent association between serial cardiac ultrasound parameters and outcomes in acutely ill adults. However, serial changes are frequently observed, highlighting the need for trials evaluating whether decision-linked, ultrasound-guided management strategies can improve outcomes.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION NUMBER: PROSPERO, CRD42024524740.

Title: Predictive value of plasma soluble thrombomodulin for new-onset carotid plaque in adults with carotid intima-media thickening.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endothelial damage constitutes the initial phase in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis, and plasma soluble thrombomodulin (sTM) is a sensitive biomarker of endothelial injury. However, the association between plasma sTM and new-onset carotid plaque development remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate whether plasma sTM can predict new-onset carotid plaque and identify factors associated with plaque formation in adults with carotid intima-media thickening (cIMT).
METHODS: Carotid ultrasonography performed during health examinations was retrospectively analyzed to evaluate carotid plaque status. Participants with carotid plaques at baseline were excluded from the study. Baseline plasma sTM levels were quantified using a chemiluminescence immunoassay. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to evaluate factors associated with new-onset carotid plaques and to develop an exploratory prediction model.
RESULTS: A total of 2,607 adults with cIMT and no carotid plaque at baseline were included in the study. The median baseline plasma sTM level was 10.0 TU/mL (interquartile range [IQR]: 6.8-12.9 TU/mL). Baseline plasma sTM levels were significantly correlated with multiple clinical factors. During a median follow-up of 13.2 months, 488 participants (18.72%) developed carotid plaque. Multivariable logistic regression analyses showed that baseline plasma sTM was independently associated with new-onset carotid plaque formation, together with fasting blood glucose, body mass index (BMI), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), low-density lipoprotein, uric acid, hypertension, and smoking (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated baseline plasma sTM levels were independently associated with new-onset carotid plaque formation in individuals with cIMT. These findings suggest that plasma sTM may have potential as an exploratory risk-stratification biomarker to assist in clinical monitoring.

Title: Comparative efficacy of esophageal protection strategies during radiofrequency atrial fibrillation ablation: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal thermal injury remains a clinically significant complication of radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), with endoscopically detected esophageal lesions (EDELs) occurring in up to 10-15% of cases and atrio-esophageal fistula carrying high mortality. Multiple protective strategies have been proposed; however, their comparative efficacy remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating esophageal protection strategies during AF ablation. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through August 7, 2026. Parallel-group randomized trials in adult patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation were included. The primary outcome was incidence of EDEL. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was performed, with treatment hierarchy assessed using P-scores. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 and CINeMA frameworks, respectively.
RESULTS: Twenty-five randomized controlled trials involving approximately 2,500 patients were included in the systematic review. Twelve trials involving 1,077 patients contributed to the connected network meta-analysis. Mechanical esophageal deviation combined with luminal esophageal temperature monitoring (LET) had the most favorable point estimate compared with no dedicated protection (OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.02-3.05) and achieved the highest P-score (0.861). The rankogram estimated a 58% probability of ranking first. Visualization-guided strategies also showed a favorable point estimate (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.08-3.09), whereas LET alone and active cooling did not demonstrate significant reductions in EDEL. Directly, mechanical deviation plus LET significantly reduced the odds of EDEL compared with single-sensor LET (OR, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.04-0.41). Seven randomized trials involving 990 patients showed no significant association between higher- versus standard-power ablation and EDEL (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.56-2.54), with no observed heterogeneity (I² = 0%). Network heterogeneity was moderate (I² = 46.9%), with no significant evidence of network inconsistency or publication bias.
CONCLUSIONS: No single esophageal protection strategy completely eliminates the risk of thermal injury during AF ablation. Mechanical esophageal deviation combined with LET demonstrated the most favorable overall ranking, while visualization-guided strategies also showed a potentially beneficial signal. In contrast, LET or cooling alone did not reliably reduce EDEL incidence. However, overall confidence in the evidence is constrained by small trial samples and reliance on surrogate outcomes. Larger, contemporary trials are needed to confirm clinical benefits and assess the impact on rare but catastrophic complications.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not Applicable.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis

Title: Association Between Triglyceride-glucose Index, Neutrophil to High-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Ratio and Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Study in China.
Journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common arrhythmia and the major cause of morbidity and mortality in cardiovascular disease. Although the pathogenesis of AF is unclear, insulin resistance and inflammation have been recognized to be strongly associated with AF. This study aimed to investigate the association between triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, neutrophil to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (NHR) and AF.
METHODS: A total of 1468 subjects from a single center were used in the retrospective study, and logistic regression analysis was used to determine the association between the TyG index, NHR and AF. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to assess the predictive ability of these independent associated with AF.
RESULTS: AF patients exhibited higher levels of TyG index and NHR than non-AF patients. The TyG index (OR = 2.79, 95% CI 1.07-7.26, P = 0.029) and NHR (OR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.47-1.81, P < 0.001) were significantly associated with AF. The TyG index and NHR remained significantly associated with AF across the subgroups analyzed and were consistent with the trend in overall outcome (P < 0.05). ROC analysis confirmed the combination of the TyG index and NHR demonstrated moderate potential predictive ability, with improved sensitivity for the occurrence of AF (AUC = 0.762, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: High TyG index and NHR were independently associated with AF. The combination of the TyG index and NHR showed potential predictive ability for the occurrence of AF.

Title: Disease Burden and Mortality of Ischemic Heart Disease in China from 2008 to 2036.
Journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: To examine long-term trends and population subgroup differences in ischemic heart disease (IHD) mortality and disease burden in China from 2008 to 2021, and to project future trends to inform targeted prevention.
METHODS: Using the China Cause-of-Death Surveillance Dataset (2008-2021), we calculated crude mortality rate (CMR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), potential years of life lost (PYLL), and potential years of life lost rate (PYLLR). Temporal trends were quantified using Joinpoint regression, with results expressed as the average annual percentage change (AAPC). Age, period, and cohort effects were assessed with an age-period-cohort (APC) model. ASMR from 2022 to 2036 were forecasted by ARIMA model.
RESULTS: In 2008, the CMR and ASMR for IHD in China was 70.98/100,000 and 79.32/100,000; In 2021, the CMR and ASMR was 143.70/100,000 and 89.12/100,000. From 2008 to 2021, the overall ASMR trend showed no statistically significant change (AAPC = 0.75%, P = 0.63), whereas PYLLR rose significantly (AAPC = 2.01, P < 0.001). IHD ASMR and PYLLR were higher in males than females (P < 0.001), in rural than urban (P < 0.001), and in the central region than eastern region and western region (P < 0.001). APC analysis identified age effect as the predominant driver of IHD mortality risk. ARIMA projections indicated that IHD ASMR would remain largely stable through 2036.
CONCLUSION: China's substantial IHD burden demands prioritized primary prevention targeting younger populations, older adults, males, and rural residents. Multisectoral IHD risk-factor interventions should be integrated into national health policy to curb the rising burden.

Title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
Abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

Title: High-flow versus standard nasal cannula oxygenation during prone-position ERCP under nurse-administered propofol sedation: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxemia affects up to 23% of patients undergoing ERCP under nurse-administered propofol sedation (NAPS) with a standard nasal cannula (SNC). High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) provides heated, humidified oxygen at high gas flow with more controlled inspired oxygen delivery than conventional low-flow oxygen and may reduce hypoxemic events during sedation. We compared HFNC with SNC during ERCP under NAPS.
METHODS: In this two-center, prospective, randomized trial, 300 adults undergoing ERCP between October 2025 and June 2026 were allocated 1:1 to HFNC (flow 50 L/min; FiO2 0.50) or SNC (5 L/min). All procedures were performed in the prone position under propofol-based NAPS. The primary outcome was hypoxemia (SpO2 < 92% for > 10 s). Secondary outcomes included airway interventions and cardiovascular events.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, procedural factors, and sedation dosages were comparable. Hypoxemia occurred in 2 of 150 patients (1.3%) with HFNC versus 21 of 150 (14.0%) with SNC (RR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02-0.36; P < 0.001). Jaw-thrust maneuvers (1.3 vs. 12.0%; P < 0.001) and nasopharyngeal airway insertion (0 vs. 9.3%; P < 0.001) were also less frequent with HFNC. No patient required emergency intubation. Hypotension was more frequent with HFNC (16.7 vs. 8.0%; P = 0.02), but no episode required vasopressors or procedure termination. In post hoc analyses, HFNC reduced hypoxemic events in both BMI subgroups; however, the treatment-by-BMI interaction was not significant (P for interaction = 0.65).
CONCLUSIONS: HFNC oxygenation strategy reduced hypoxemic events and rescue airway interventions during ERCP under NAPS, although transient hypotension occurred more frequently. No significant treatment-by-BMI interaction was observed.
TRIAL REGISTRY: Thai Clinical Trials Registry, TCTR20250901001.

Title: Long-term follow-up of adolescents with white coat hypertension: a preliminary exploratory study.
Abstract: White coat hypertension (WCH) in youth has traditionally been considered benign, but it may precede sustained hypertension (SH) and cardiovascular remodelling. We evaluated long-term blood pressure (BP) outcomes and hypertension-mediated organ damage in adolescents with WCH. This preliminary exploratory cohort study included 34 adolescents with WCH and 24 normotensive controls followed for median periods of 8.5 and 7.7 years. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, vascular, and ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) assessments were performed at baseline and follow-up. At follow-up, 13 participants with WCH (38.2%) progressed to SH, 2 (5.9%) maintained WCH, and 19 (55.9%) became normotensive; no control developed SH. Participants who progressed had higher baseline ambulatory systolic BP (SBP; 124 vs 119 mmHg, p = 0.004) and pulse pressure (PP; 55 vs 49 mmHg, p = 0.01), while office BP was similar. At follow-up, office BP, ambulatory SBP (131 vs 118 mmHg, p = 0.001), PP (60 vs 45 mmHg, p = 0.003), central SBP (126 vs 121 mmHg, p = 0.032), and augmentation pressure (7 vs 4 mmHg, p = 0.009) were higher in the SH group. Most biochemical parameters, carotid intima-media thickness, and pulse wave velocity were similar between groups. More than one-third of adolescents with WCH progressed to SH. Higher baseline ambulatory SBP and PP may identify those at greater risk. These preliminary findings support individualized, risk-stratified surveillance, with closer ABPM follow-up for adolescents with higher-normal ambulatory BP, wider PP, excess adiposity, persistent office BP elevation, or other cardiovascular risk factors.

Title: Real-time XR-based 6-DOF catheter tracking enhances cardiac intervention navigation efficiency and depth perception.
Abstract: Despite advances in 3D ultrasound, most percutaneous cardiac interventions still rely on 2D visualization, limiting depth perception and spatial understanding. To address this challenge, we developed an Extended Reality (XR)-based platform that enables real-time six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) catheter tracking and visualization within a patient-specific 3D heart model. The system combines a custom machine-vision algorithm for 5-DOF catheter tracking with a 3D-printed electromechanical encoder that measures catheter roll, providing complete 6-DOF motion reconstruction. In a proof-of-concept study, 20 novice medical students navigated an intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) catheter to six anatomical targets using either immersive 3D visualization or a conventional 2D cathlab-style view. Participants in the 3D condition completed the task in 54.6 seconds and traveled 1939 mm on average, compared with 263.5 seconds and 7854 mm in the 2D condition. The ratio of cohort means was 4.8× for completion time and 4.1× for travel length (means of subject-level ratios: 5.1× and 4.9×). The 3D mode also produced more direct and less variable approach trajectories. Participants consistently rated immersive visualization higher for accuracy, speed, usability, and clinical value. Exploratory kinematic analysis suggested that 3D users distributed motion more evenly along the depth axis, whereas 2D users relied more on lateral and vertical adjustments. These findings demonstrate that XR-based visualization can substantially improve procedural training efficiency and motor control.

Title: Postdischarge continuity of care and cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome.
Journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite the availability of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), postdischarge continuity of care (CoC) remains suboptimal, and evidence from Asian health-care systems remains limited. The present study examined the association between CoC and clinical outcomes in Taiwanese patients with ACS.
METHODS: This nationwide observational cohort study was conducted using data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. It included patients who had their first ACS-related hospitalization between 2012 and 2020 and excluded those who died during the index hospitalization or experienced study outcomes within 1 month after discharge. CoC was assessed in terms of physician, specialty, and GDMT continuity. Study outcomes were all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and major bleeding.
RESULTS: This study included 140 214 patients with ACS. Patients with low physician continuity had significantly higher risks of all-cause mortality (adjusted risk ratio [aRR]: 2.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.09 to 2.31), cardiovascular death (aRR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.81 to 2.15), MACEs (aRR: 1.78, 95% CI: 1.66 to 1.90), HHF (aRR: 1.66, 95% CI: 1.54 to 1.78), and major bleeding (aRR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.26 to 1.66) than did those with high physician continuity. Low specialty continuity was associated with a 1.28-to-1.95-fold increase in the risk of adverse outcomes. Furthermore, low GDMT continuity was significantly associated with elevated risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, and MACEs but not HHF or major bleeding.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that lower CoC during the first year after ACS-related hospitalization is associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Future studies should explore strategies to improve CoC.

Title: Discordance Between Height- and BMI-Adjusted AWGS 2025 Definitions of Confirmed Sarcopenia After Stroke.
Abstract:
AIM: The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 allows height- or body mass index (BMI)-adjusted muscle mass in diagnosing confirmed sarcopenia. We evaluated classification discordance and associated clinical characteristics after stroke.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 864 patients undergoing post-acute stroke rehabilitation. Confirmed sarcopenia was defined using low handgrip strength combined with either height- or BMI-adjusted muscle mass. Patients were classified into four groups: Neither, Height-only, BMI-only, and Both. Agreement between definitions was quantified, and the two discordant groups were compared using multivariable logistic regression. Model robustness and discharge outcomes were examined in sensitivity and exploratory analyses, respectively.
RESULTS: Discordant classification occurred in 183 patients (21.2%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 18.6%-24.0%), with moderate agreement between definitions (κ = 0.578). Compared with the Height-only group, the BMI-only group had higher BMI, serum albumin, and phase angle. In adjusted analyses of 182 patients, higher albumin (odds ratio [OR] per 0.5 g/dL, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.10-2.64), phase angle (OR per degree, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.23-3.04), and medication count (OR per drug, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32) were associated with BMI-only classification. Firth estimates were similar, but internal validation indicated overfitting. Adjusted discharge outcomes did not clearly differ between discordant groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Height- and BMI-adjusted AWGS 2025 criteria classified approximately one in five patients differently after stroke. Beyond expected body-size differences, discordant groups exhibited distinct clinical characteristics, highlighting the importance of considering the indexing method when interpreting sarcopenia classifications.

Title: Plasma short-chain fatty acids and risk of cardiovascular events and recurrent stroke after ischemic stroke.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) serve as important mediators linking the gut microbiome to ischemic stroke and are associated with poststroke recovery and neuronal plasticity. However, population-based prognostic evidence for circulating SCFAs after ischemic stroke is scarce. We aimed to evaluate the relationships between multiple SCFAs and cardiovascular events in patients with ischemic stroke.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a nested case-control study within the China Antihypertensive Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke with 328 cardiovascular events and 328 controls, matched for age, sex and treatment group. The primary outcome was cardiovascular events after ischemic stroke. Nine plasma SCFAs were determined by ultra-high-performance LC-MS/MS. Logistic regression models were applied to incremental predictive value of SCFAs were evaluated. We identified 6 SCFAs (acetate, isobutyrate, isovalerate, caproate, isocaproate and 3-hydroxyisovalerate) that were inversely associated with cardiovascular events, with multivariable-adjusted ORs per 1 log-SD increment ranging from 0.31 to 0.53 (all P values < 0.05). Acetate, caproate and 3-hydroxyisovalerate were also associated with recurrent stroke, with the multivariable-adjusted ORs ranging from 0.30 to 0.37. The SCFAs score constructed by 6 identified SCFAs was associated with both cardiovascular events and recurrent stroke, ORs (95% CIs) for the highest versus lowest tertile were 0.49 (0.32-0.77) and 0.49 (0.30-0.80), respectively. Furthermore, the SCFAs score offered substantially predictive capability for cardiovascular events and recurrent stroke, beyond traditional risk factors and clinical features.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher SCFAs were associated with lower risks of cardiovascular events and recurrent stroke after ischemic stroke, and provided incremental value for risk discrimination and reclassification after ischemic stroke.

Title: Performance of artificial intelligence versus clinician left-ventricular segmentation of cardiac MRI for mortality prediction: a retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ejection fraction, a key measure of cardiac function, is used in health care for clinical decision making and risk stratification. We hypothesised that a deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) segmentation of ejection fraction obtained from cardiac MRI (CMR) outperforms expert clinician segmentation for the prediction of all-cause mortality.
METHODS: In this retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study, we studied a cohort of 27 382 consecutive patients who underwent cardiac MRI (CMR) in the UK and the USA. Patients were referred for CMR from nine hospitals to Barts Heart Centre (BHC), London. Patients were identified from the reporting archive at BHC as having undergone a CMR between Oct 1, 2014 and Dec 31, 2019. A further cohort of patients was also identified from University of Pittsburgh Medical Centre (UPMC), Pittsburgh, PA, USA, as having undergone a CMR between June 1, 2010 and March 31, 2016. Mortality data were obtained from national and local databases. AI segmentation was done on all CMR studies, and Cox proportional hazards models were fitted to compare the prognostic value of AI-measured versus clinician-measured left-ventricular volume metrics. Model fit was compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), discrimination using C indices and the incremental value of AI over clinician segmentation using likelihood-ratio tests of nested models.
FINDINGS: 27 382 patients received a baseline CMR (26 106 patients from BHC and 1276 from UPMC). The median follow-up was 5·6 years (IQR 4·4-6·9), during which 3458 (13%) of 27 382 patients died. AI ejection fraction showed better model fit (AIC 57 936 vs 58 097, ΔAIC 161 favouring AI) and marginally better discrimination (C index 0·669 vs 0·637; ΔC 0·033 [95% CI 0·026-0·041]). AI ejection fraction significantly improved model fit when added to clinician ejection fraction (χ2=168, p<0·0001), with only slight improvement when clinician ejection fraction was added to AI (χ2=7·5, p=0·023). After adjustment for age and sex, AI-derived ejection fraction showed better model fit (AIC 55 684 vs 55 742; ΔAIC 59) and had marginally better discrimination (C index of 0·781 vs 0·777; ΔC=0·004 [95% CI 0·002-0·006]).
INTERPRETATION: AI-derived ejection fraction shows marginally superior prediction for mortality than clinician-derived ejection fraction in patients who had CMR. Findings support the potential utility of AI for first-line ejection-fraction measurement with clinician oversight, although this should be investigated in prospective studies.
FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research Clinical Lectureship and the British Heart Foundation Accelerator Award.

Title: Influence of the PROFUND index on the effectiveness of SGLT2 inhibitors in elderly pluripathological patients with acute heart failure: PROFUND-IC registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The PROFUND index is a useful tool for estimating one-year mortality in pluripathological patients with heart failure, although its influence on the treatments administered remains unknown. The objectives of the present study were to evaluate whether the PROFUND index influences the effectiveness of sodium-glucose cotransporter type II inhibitors (SGLT2i), and to describe the differential characteristics of pluripathological patients with acute heart failure (AHF) according to this scale.
METHODS: Retrospective study of 880 pluripathological patients with AHF from the PROFUND-IC registry, divided into three groups according to PROFUND index: low (0-2 points), medium (3-6) and high/very high mortality risk (≥7). A descriptive and comparative analysis was performed using the Chi-square test for qualitative variables and ANOVA for quantitative ones, (Fisher and Kruskal-Wallis, when indicated). Propensity Score Matching (PSM) was applied to minimize confounding factors. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed analysing readmissions and mortality according to SGLT2i administration.
RESULTS: 880 patients were included, 16.3% with low risk; 39.7% with medium risk and 44.1% with high/very high risk. Those with PROFUND index≥7 were predominantly women (61.3%, p=0.006), older, with worse functional class, lower Barthel index, and higher one-year mortality (p<0.001). SGLT2i administration appears to reduce readmissions among patients with PROFUND index between 3 and 6 (25.5% vs. 38.3%, p=0.02). After PSM, this trend persisted (24.1% versus 36.1%), without reaching statistical significance (p=0.065).
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i appear beneficial in pluripathological patients with AHF, although the greatest impact is observed in PROFUND 3-6. Further studies are needed to clarify how comorbidity and functionality influence the effectiveness of these drugs.

Title: Translating the familial hypercholesterolemia pediatric diagnostic score (FH-PeDS) into clinical practice: Development of an open-access online tool.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: More than 90% of children with familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) remain undiagnosed. Although genetic testing is the diagnostic gold standard, limited availability necessitates the use of clinical diagnostic criteria, which have suboptimal performance in children.
OBJECTIVE: To introduce the recently developed familial hypercholesterolemia pediatric diagnostic score (FH-PeDS) and its online implementation.
METHODS: FH-PeDS was developed using real-world data from Slovenian children identified through universal cholesterol screening and externally validated in an independent Portuguese pediatric cohort.
RESULTS: FH-PeDS demonstrated improved diagnostic accuracy compared with traditional clinical scoring systems and was recently recognized as promising tool in the European Atherosclerosis Society consensus statement on FH in children and adolescents. It is now freely available at https://fh-peds.eu in two versions: a semi-quantitative clinical scoring system and a machine learning model.
CONCLUSION: The online FH-PeDS provides healthcare professionals with an accessible tool to estimate the likelihood of pediatric FH, potentially facilitating earlier diagnosis and treatment. Further external validation is warranted before widespread implementation.

Title: Complementary Yield of Gene Panel Testing and ACMG SF v3.3 Screening for Cardiovascular Disease in a Korean Cohort.
Abstract: Inherited arrhythmia syndromes and cardiomyopathies are genetically heterogeneous, and clinical exome sequencing (CES) for unrelated indications increasingly yields cardiovascular secondary findings (SFs) under the ACMG SF v3.3 list. We compared, at a single Korean centre, phenotype-directed cardiac gene panel testing with opportunistically ascertained cardiovascular SFs. Forty patients with suspected inherited arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy underwent a 19-gene arrhythmia or 173-gene cardiomyopathy panel with AI-assisted, manually reviewed variant classification; separately, 288 patients undergoing CES for unrelated indications were screened for ACMG SF v3.3 cardiovascular pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants. A phenotype-concordant pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant was found in 8/40 patients (20.0%), including a recurrent KCNQ1 p.Arg231His variant in two unrelated infants and a MYBPC3 variant upgraded to pathogenic by co-segregation in a mother-son pair. Among the 288 exome-sequenced patients, 17 reportable cardiovascular SFs occurred in 16 (5.6%), predominantly dilated cardiomyopathy (n = 7, mostly TTN) and familial hypercholesterolaemia (n = 6, including a recurrent PCSK9 p.Glu32Lys variant in three patients). The two approaches sampled largely non-overlapping gene categories and are complementary rather than competing; recurrent, population-specific variants underscore the need for population-informed interpretation and structured counselling in cardiovascular genetic diagnosis.

Title: Sex-associated territory-specific vascular phenotypes in genetically confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise territory-specific sex-associated vascular phenotypes in genetically confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and assess whether associations persisted after accounting for COL3A1 molecular mechanism.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicentre cohort, clinical-genomics review identified 95 eligible patients from 110 source records. 18 prespecified vascular outcomes were evaluated using Firth bias-reduced logistic regression adjusted for completed age per 10-year increment. Sensitivity analyses among 75 patients with classifiable dominant-negative or haploinsufficient mechanisms additionally adjusted for molecular mechanism.
RESULTS: The cohort included 34 male and 61 female patients. Male sex was associated with ascending aortic dilation or aneurysm (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.68 to 15.41), iliac/femoral aneurysm (4.61, 95% CI 1.79 to 12.52), extra-aortic dissection (3.93, 95% CI 1.61 to 10.24), renal dissection (10.08, 95% CI 3.08 to 42.11) and splanchnic dissection (5.84, 95% CI 2.27 to 15.90). Aortic dissection and cervical aneurysm or dissection were not associated with male sex. In the imaging-restricted unadjusted comparison, head and neck tortuosity, ectasia or dilation was present in 23/44 (52.3%) female and 7/29 (24.1%) male patients (p=0.028). In genotype sensitivity analyses, associations remained for iliac/femoral, renal and splanchnic aneurysms and for extra-aortic, renal, splanchnic and iliac dissections, whereas several broader aneurysm and intervention estimates became less precise.
CONCLUSIONS: Male sex was associated with a territory-specific vascular phenotype, with the most consistent genotype-adjusted associations involving renal, splanchnic, iliac/femoral and broader extra-aortic dissection territories. Surveillance should remain comprehensive rather than sex restricted.

Title: Effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity in patients with diabetes mellitus and coronary artery disease receiving aspirin and clopidogrel: a randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial (POC-DM).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors are often prescribed with aspirin and clopidogrel to reduce gastrointestinal bleeding risk. However, the European Society of Cardiology diabetes guidelines recommend avoiding concomitant use of omeprazole and clopidogrel due to potential drug–drug interactions. Evidence in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), who have a higher prevalence of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, remains limited. In Thailand, where omeprazole is the only reimbursed PPI, this potential interaction has important clinical implications. We aimed to evaluate the effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity, measured as P2Y12 reaction units (PRU), in patients with DM and coronary artery disease (CAD) receiving aspirin and clopidogrel.
METHODS: This double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial enrolled patients with DM and CAD receiving aspirin 81 mg/day and clopidogrel 75 mg/day. Participants received omeprazole 20 mg or a matching placebo for 2 weeks, followed by crossover to the alternate treatment. Platelet reactivity was assessed using the VerifyNow P2Y12 assay. The primary outcome was the change in PRU following omeprazole coadministration compared with both baseline and placebo. Secondary outcomes included changes in clopidogrel responder status (PRU >208) before and after omeprazole treatment and PRU values in each treatment period.
RESULTS: 50 patients were enrolled (median age 67 years; 58% male). Omeprazole significantly increased PRU by a mean difference of 20.57 units versus baseline (p=0.002) and 16.14 units versus placebo (p=0.006). The proportion of clopidogrel non-responders increased from 44% to 56%, with 25% of baseline responders converting to non-responders.
CONCLUSIONS: Omeprazole significantly attenuated clopidogrel’s antiplatelet effect in patients with diabetes and CAD. Concomitant use may be avoided, especially in those with high thrombotic risk.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: TCTR20260714003.

Title: China-PAR-based cardiovascular risk assessment in East Shenzhen using Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays: A prospective cross-sectional and retrospective study.
Journal: The Journal of international medical research
Abstract: ObjectiveHypertension and dyslipidemia are two well-established risk factors for cardiovascular disease. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical performance of homocysteine and lipid assays, estimate the 10-year cardiovascular disease risk among individuals with hypertension, and determine the proportions of hyperhomocysteinemia-type hypertension and dyslipidemia in a hospital-based population in East Shenzhen, China.MethodsThe analytical performances of the Biossays homocysteine, total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol assays were evaluated according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute documents. A cross-sectional hypertension cohort comprising 400 eligible participants was recruited from Pingshan People's Hospital between April 2024 and April 2025 to assess the risk of cardiovascular disease and prevalence of hyperhomocysteinemia-type hypertension. Additionally, a retrospective analysis was performed involving 55,575 unique individuals with complete lipid data identified from the hospital laboratory database in 2024, following the exclusion of participants with incomplete and duplicate records, to assess the proportion of participants with dyslipidemia.ResultsThe Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays demonstrated satisfactory precision, trueness, sensitivity, and linearity. The 10-year cardiovascular disease risk, based in the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China, differed across ages but not across sexes. The proportions of individuals with hypertension and hyperhomocysteinemia, defined as homocysteine levels ≥10 μmol/L and ≥15 μmol/L, were 85.50% (342) and 33.75% (135), respectively, with no difference in the risk distribution between the two criteria. At least one abnormal lipid parameter was observed in 68.00% (272) of the participants in the hypertension cohort and in 62.35% (34,651) of individuals from the annual laboratory dataset.ConclusionsThe Biossays homocysteine and lipid assays demonstrated satisfactory analytical performance. Among individuals with hypertension, the estimated 10-year cardiovascular disease risk differed across ages but not between sexes, and hyperhomocysteinemia was frequently observed. Lipid abnormalities were also common in the hospital-based population. These findings may support cardiovascular risk assessment and preventive management in similar clinical populations.

Title: Genetic testing considerations for hereditary duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
Abstract: The incidence of duodenal and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (dpNETs) has increased substantially in recent years. These tumors may be due to syndromic hereditary predisposition syndromes: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) or 4 (MEN4), Von Hippel-Lindau disease (VHL), neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), or tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). Because a dpNET may be the first MEN1 sign, recent guidelines recommend MEN1 genetic testing in selected patients with an isolated dpNET. Whether similar genetic testing strategies should be extended to other hereditary syndromes remains unknown. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the genetic and clinical data of patients who underwent genetic testing for isolated or syndromic dpNETs. We assessed the presence of (likely) pathogenic variants ((L)PVs) in MEN1, NF1, VHL, CDKN1B, TSC1, and TSC2. 410 patients were included: 301 with isolated (=non syndromic) dpNETs and 109 with syndromic dpNETs. Among them, 38 carried a (L)PV, most frequently in MEN1 (n = 27 patients), followed by NF1 (n = 8) and VHL (n = 3). No TSC1, TSC2, or CDKN1B (L)PVs were found. Patients with syndromic dpNETs exhibited significantly higher positive rates (29.4%) compared to isolated dpNETs (<2%). We confirm that MEN1 is the predominant gene underlying predisposition to dpNETs. The low diagnostic yield in isolated dpNETs supports a clinically stratified genetic testing strategy. Clinical evaluation should systematically assess for signs of MEN1, MEN4, VHL, NF1, or TSC to inform appropriate genetic testing and maximize diagnostic yield. Concerning MEN1, we propose limiting extended genetic testing in patients with isolated dpNETs to those with (i) gastrinoma, (ii) multiple dpNETs, or (iii) diagnosis before 40 years of age.

Title: Predicting the persistence of Long COVID 36 months after hospitalisation: a prospective Ukrainian cohort study.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVE: To determine early predictive markers and to develop prognostic models for self-reported persistence of Long COVID syndrome at 36 months after hospitalisation.
DESIGN: A prospective observational study with cross-sectional analyses at predefined follow-up points.
SETTING: A tertiary care hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: 221 patients hospitalised for COVID-19 underwent detailed clinical, functional, imaging and survey-based symptom assessment prior to discharge and at 1 month, followed by a 3-year longitudinal follow-up on symptoms. 159 patients (mean age 53.1±13.6 years, 55% female) completed the 36-month assessment and were included in the final analysis.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Self-reported persistence of Long COVID symptoms at 36 months after hospital discharge.
RESULTS: At 36 months after discharge, 66 (41%) patients reported persistent Long COVID symptoms. This group did not differ in age or sex structure, more frequently reported ongoing symptoms at 3 months (91% vs 59%, p<0.001) and 12 months (77% vs 13%, p<0.001), had longer time to hospitalisation (10.2±3.4 vs 5.2±3.9 days, p<0.001) and higher Charlson comorbidity index (0.61±0.96 vs 0.33±0.56, p=0.022), higher in-hospital creatinine (109 (100–119) vs 96 (85–105) µmol/L, p<0.001), aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (43 (37–55) vs 32 (21–47) IU/L, p=0.003), and alanine aminotransferase (47 (30–128) vs 42 (26–62) IU/L, p=0.011) and paradoxically lower Galectin-3 (8.6±0.7 vs 9.0±0.5 ng/mL, p<0.001) and sST2 (23.2±13.7 vs 29.7±15.8 ng/mL, p=0.012). No significant differences were found in inflammatory markers, minimal in-hospital peripheral capillary oxygen saturation, need for oxygen supplementation, pulmonary involvement on CT or lung ultrasound, and clinically negligible differences detected in cardiovascular evaluation, with a baseline tendency to minimal hypercontractility and lower flow-mediated dilation (10.1±5.1 vs 12.9%±5.9%, p=0.006) and marginally worse early dynamics of diastolic indices in Long COVID group. In 6-Minute Walking Test, no differences were observed at baseline but patients with Long COVID reported higher postexertional fatigue (3.3±2.1 vs 1.9±1.6, p<0.001) and dyspnoea (3.4±1.7 vs 2.5±1.8, p=0.027) despite lower blood oxygen desaturation (1.7±1.7 vs 2.8%±2.4%, p=0.014) at 1 month. In symptom assessment, longitudinal trajectories differed significantly for Medical Research Council Dyspnoea (p=0.004), post-COVID functional scale (p<0.001), EFTER-COVID study physical symptoms (p<0.001) and Symptom Burden Questionnaire for Long COVID Memory, Thinking and Communication (p<0.001) scores, reaching maximal differences by 3–12 months, while respiratory scores showed no sustained differences. A simple artificial neural network model combining predischarge variables (sex, age, creatinine, AST, weight loss, duration of hospitalisation and 6-Minute Walk Distance) with 3-month multidimensional symptom assessment achieved a 92% accuracy (area under the receiver operating characteristic, AUROC 0.902), consistently outperforming other machine learning classifiers. A simplified model using only 3-month survey data, age, sex and hospitalisation duration retained high discrimination accuracy (88%, AUROC 0.850).
CONCLUSIONS: 41% of hospitalised COVID-19 patients reported persistent symptoms at 36 months, preceded by early divergence in patient-reported symptoms despite comparable recovery of objective functional parameters. Predictive models incorporating 3-month multidimensional symptom assessment and routine clinical variables accurately identified patients at risk, outperforming later reassessment strategies and supporting early risk stratification.

Title: Impact of CKD and Hemodialysis on Treatment of Severely Calcified Lesions: The ECLIPSE Trial.
Abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and coronary calcification increase risk for adverse events following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. We evaluated whether outcomes following vessel preparation with orbital atherectomy (OA) versus balloon angioplasty (BA) vary according to CKD. Methods: This pre-specified CKD sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter ECLIPSE trial evaluated 2,001 patients with severely calcified lesions randomized to OA versus BA prior to DES. Independent predictors of two-year target-vessel failure (TVF)-a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (ID-TVR)-were determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² or hemodialysis) was present in 694 (34.7%) patients; 112 required hemodialysis. Two-year TVF was significantly higher with versus without CKD (21.2% vs. 11.6%; p<0.001), driven by increased cardiac death and ID-TVR. Hemodialysis independently predicted TVF (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.30-3.53; p=0.003), whereas reduced eGFR alone did not (p=0.070). In patients on hemodialysis, OA versus BA was associated with higher rates of TVF (52.3% vs. 30.7%; adjusted HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.16-5.41; P=0.020), driven by higher rates of TV-MI and ID-TVR, whereas TVF was similar after OA versus BA in patients not on hemodialysis (13.5% vs. 13.1%; adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.81-1.35; P=0.730); however, the interaction between treatment assignment and hemodialysis status was not significant (Pint=0.244). Conclusions: CKD remains a major predictor of adverse outcomes after DES implantation in severely calcified lesions, with the highest risks in patients on hemodialysis. In the ECLIPSE trial, higher two-year rates of TVF were observed after vessel preparation with OA compared with BA in patients on hemodialysis but not in patients with CKD not on hemodialysis or in those without CKD. Given the modest hemodialysis subgroup size and non-significant interaction testing, confirmation of these findings in additional studies is warranted.

Title: Global burden of chronic kidney disease attributable to hypertension due to high body mass index: projections to 2050.
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects approximately 9.1% of the global population, equivalent to approximately 843 million individuals as of 2021, with hypertension (HTN) as a major contributor. High body mass index (BMI) exacerbates HTN-related kidney injury, but the global burden of HTN-related CKD attributable to high BMI remains poorly characterized. Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study for 1990-2021, we estimated attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and the age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rate (ASDR). Temporal trends were assessed using the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was used to project rates to 2050. Attributable deaths increased from 36,476 in 1990 to 179,788 in 2021, and DALYs increased from 1.01 million to 4.26 million. ASMR increased from 1.09 to 2.19 per 100,000 (EAPC, 4.22%), and ASDR increased from 26.04 to 50.11 per 100,000 (EAPC, 3.63%). Central Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest ASMR (7.66 per 100,000), whereas High-income North America had the fastest increase in ASMR (EAPC, 5.63%). ASMR and ASDR were higher in men than in women. Death counts peaked at ages 85-89 years in both sexes, whereas DALYs peaked at ages 60-64 years in men and 65-69 years in women. Crude rates were higher in populations with a higher sociodemographic index (SDI), whereas the relative burden became more concentrated in lower-SDI populations; concentration indices changed from -0.10 to -0.17 for deaths and from -0.06 to -0.08 for DALYs. By 2050, ASMR is projected to reach 4.44 per 100,000 (95% credible interval [CI], 3.70-5.20), and ASDR is projected to reach 77.15 per 100,000 (95% CI, 1.81-152.49). The high BMI-attributable burden of HTN-related CKD is increasing and remains unequally distributed. These findings support integrated obesity prevention and hypertension control, with priority given to high-risk regions and older adults.

Title: The lipoprotein-immune checkpoint axis: Linking cardiovascular toxicity and antitumor immunity during immune checkpoint therapy.
Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors(ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but may also perturb vascular immune homeostasis and increase atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk. Clinical cohorts and imaging studies associate ICI exposure with atherosclerotic events, plaque progression, and arterial inflammatory changes, although causality and the relevant vascular phenotype remain incompletely defined. This Review examines a lipoprotein-immune checkpoint interface linking plaque inflammation with antitumor immunity. We focus on low-density lipoprotein(LDL) and oxidized LDL(oxLDL), lipoprotein(a)[Lp(a)] and oxidized phospholipids (OxPLs), statin-related regulation of ubiquitin-like 3(UBL3)-dependent programmed death-ligand 1(PD-L1) sorting into small extracellular vesicles(sEVs), and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9(PCSK9). Lp(a) and OxPLs are established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease(ASCVD) mediators but unvalidated ICI-specific biomarkers. Statins have proven cardiovascular benefit and emerging mechanistic links to PD-L1 trafficking, whereas oncologic associations remain observational. PCSK9 inhibition combines established lipid lowering with preclinical enhancement of antigen presentation and checkpoint response, but randomized ICI-specific evidence is lacking. Current evidence therefore supports a testable translational framework rather than a validated causal axis. Guideline-directed cardiovascular prevention remains the clinical standard while biomarker and therapeutic hypotheses require prospective validation.

Title: Evaluating the SVS 90-Minute Door-to-Intervention Target for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (rAAAs) are a life-threatening condition requiring rapid surgical intervention for survival. Guidelines from the Society of Vascular Surgery in 2018 advised a door-to-intervention time of ≤90 minutes. We hypothesised that door-to-intervention time would not predict outcomes following rAAA repair, as treatment timelines may reflect differences in physiological severity, diagnostic assessment and operative modality, including the use of EVAR.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 29 patients presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth (UHP) who underwent surgical intervention for rAAA between February 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving the SVS-recommended door-to-intervention time of ≤90 minutes. Secondary outcomes were the rates of endovascular repair (EVAR) compared to open repair and the associated mortality and morbidity.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were included, of whom only three (10.3%) met the SVS target. Median door-to-intervention time was 182 minutes. Arrival-to-diagnosis time was associated with the greatest delay, with a median time of 84 minutes. Twenty-three patients (79.3%) underwent open repair, with a 60.9% (14/23) mortality rate compared to 16.7% (1/6) for EVAR cases. Shorter door-to-intervention time was associated with higher 30-day mortality, although no association was observed with overall mortality. Morbidity rates were 95.6% (22/23) for open cases and 50.0% (3/6) for EVAR cases. No statistically significant association was identified between overall morbidity rates and door-to-intervention time. However, higher grade complications were statistically significantly associated with both shorter arrival to diagnosis time (p=0.011) and shorter arrival to knife-to-skin time (p=0.039).
CONCLUSIONS: 89.7% (26/29) of rAAAs presenting to UHP between February 2018 and December 2024 exceeded the recommended SVS door-to-intervention target of <90 minutes. Shorter timelines were observed among patients with higher grade complications and who subsequently died. Mortality was higher following open repair.

Title: Heart Failure Care in Greece: A Call for Action.
Journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major public health challenge in Greece, affecting an estimated 300,000 individuals and imposing a substantial burden through high mortality, recurrent hospitalizations, impaired quality of life, and escalating healthcare costs. Although significant advances in pharmacological therapies, device-based interventions, and multidisciplinary care have improved outcomes in recent years, important gaps persist in the implementation of evidence-based HF care across the country. This viewpoint from the Heart Failure Working Group of the Hellenic Society of Cardiology (HCS) highlights five strategic priorities for the development of a comprehensive national HF strategy. First, improving the recognition and diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), an increasingly prevalent and frequently underdiagnosed condition, through greater awareness, structured diagnostic pathways, and the adoption of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. Second, strengthening the national advanced HF network by establishing coordinated referral pathways and equitable access to advanced therapies such as heart transplantation and durable left ventricular assist devices. Third, integrating palliative care into routine HF management to address symptom burden, psychosocial needs, and advance care planning throughout the disease trajectory. Fourth, expanding access to cardiac rehabilitation through hospital-based, community-based, and home-based programs capable of overcoming geographical disparities and improving functional outcomes. Fifth, developing a specialized HF nursing workforce through structured education and certification programs aligned with European standards. Collectively, these interconnected priorities provide a framework for advancing and modernizing HF care in Greece. A national HF registry is proposed as the foundational infrastructure supporting all five priorities.

Title: Saturated and Trans Fatty Acids Were Not Associated with All-Cause or Cause-Specific Mortality in a Japanese Population with Relatively Low Intakes: The Japan Public Health Center-Based Prospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines recommend that saturated fatty acids (SFAs) and trans fatty acids (TFAs) should comprise ≤10% and ≤1% of total energy intake, respectively. However, evidence of the mortality risk associated with increased TFA and SFA intake in populations with a relatively low fat intake is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between total fat, SFA, TFA, monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA), and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) intake and all-cause and cause-specific mortality in a Japanese population.
METHODS: We included 90,807 participants aged 45-74 years with no history of cancer or cardiovascular disease (CVD). Dietary assessment was performed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models for each quintile of dietary fat intake: total fat, SFA, MUFA, PUFA, TFA, industrially-derived TFA (i-TFAs), and ruminant-derived TFA (r-TFA).
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 18.9 years, 22,618 deaths occurred. None of the analyses of fat intakes in quintiles showed a positive association with all-cause mortality for higher intakes of all fats, even for i-TF. In females, a nominally significant association was observed for all-cause mortality with PUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.92 [0.84-0.997]) and cancer mortality with MUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.84 [0.73-0.97]).In females, higher intakes of total fat and MUFA were nominally associated with higher respiratory disease mortality, whereas a higher SFA intake showed a suggestive association (P for trend <0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, neither SFA nor TFA intake was positively associated with all-cause mortality, and higher PUFA intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality in females.

Title: Eicosapentaenoic acid in adipose tissue is associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke: A Danish case-cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have been linked to a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, however, their association with hemorrhagic stroke remains uncertain. We investigated associations between adipose tissue content of individual omega-3 PUFAs (α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the sum of EPA+DHA), and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke and its subtypes intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage.
METHODS: This case-cohort study based on the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort included 54,546 men and women aged 50 to 65 years at baseline (1993-1997). Adipose tissue composition of omega-3 PUFAs was determined by gas chromatography for all hemorrhagic stroke cases and within a randomly drawn subcohort of 4,615 participants. Cases were identified by linkage to the Danish National Patient Register. Hazard ratios (HR) were obtained by weighted Cox regression.
RESULTS: During a median of 21 years follow-up, we identified 729 hemorrhagic stroke cases. In multivariable analyses, a significant inverse association between the content of EPA in adipose tissue and the risk of total hemorrhagic stroke was found. Thus, the HR for hemorrhagic stroke was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.50-0.82) when comparing the highest quintile of EPA content in adipose tissue with the lowest. Associations were similar when stratified according to sex and when investigating subtypes of hemorrhagic stroke, although findings were not statistically significant for subarachnoid hemorrhages. No statistically significant associations were observed between adipose tissue content of DHA, DPA and EPA+DHA and hemorrhagic strokes. A high content of ALA in adipose tissue was associated with a higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke (HR for quintile 5 vs. 1: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72).
CONCLUSION: A high content of EPA in adipose tissue was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke, while a high content of ALA was associated with a higher risk in this cohort.

Title: Residual physiological profiles in patients with CABG- or PCI-Favored coronary anatomy: A post hoc analysis of the PANDA III randomized clinical trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with anatomically complex coronary artery disease may be considered more suitable for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) than percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but some undergo PCI because of clinical constraints and experience higher long-term cardiovascular risk. The physiological rationale underlying this excess post-PCI risk remains unclear. From the perspective of post-PCI revascularization completeness and physiological results, we sought to explain the drivers of excess long-term adverse risk among patients with Favor CABG anatomy undergoing PCI.
METHODS: Coronary physiology based on quantitative flow ratio (QFR) was retrospectively evaluated in the randomized PANDA III trial in which all patients underwent PCI. Patients were stratified into 2 predefined groups by baseline SYNTAX score: Favor PCI or Favor CABG. Functional revascularization completeness was assessed using classic residual functional SYNTAX score (c-rFSS). Final physiological results were quantified by post-PCI QFR. Causal mediation analyses used 2-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) excluding periprocedural MI as the outcome to estimate the proportion of the group-outcome association statistically accounted for by residual coronary physiological profiles. The primary endpoint was 2-year MACE, defined as the composite of all-cause death, all MI, or any ischemia-driven revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 1555 patients with complete post-PCI physiological assessment constituted the final study cohort, among whom 269 (17.3%) individuals were stratified to Favor CABG group by baseline SYNTAX score. The 2-year MACE rate was significantly higher in the Favor CABG than the Favor PCI group (18.6% vs 9.2%; adjusted HR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.27-2.50). Functional incomplete revascularization (c-rFSS >0) was substantially more prevalent among patients in the Favor CABG group (53.2% vs. 15.1%, P < 0.001). Suboptimal post-PCI physiology defined by QFR <0.90 was more frequent in Favor CABG cohort (32.0% vs 11.8%, P < 0.001). In analyses using MACE excluding periprocedural MI, the estimated proportions mediated by functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology were 49.4% and 47.8%, respectively, and their estimated joint proportion mediated was 79.8%. Integrating c-rFSS or post-PCI QFR into clinical-anatomic risk models significantly improved discrimination and reclassification capacity for 2-year MACE (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this post hoc analysis of an all-comers PCI trial, approximately one-fifth of patients presented with anatomic complexity warranting CABG as the preferred revascularization strategy. Favor CABG anatomy was associated with higher 2-year MACE than Favor PCI anatomy. This association may be partly explained by the higher prevalence of residual functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology. These findings between Favor CABG and Favor PCI anatomy do not represent a head-to-head comparison and should not be interpreted as a direct comparison of revascularization modalities.
