Model performance was evaluated using discrimination (area under the curve, AUC), calibration, classification metrics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) and decision curve analysis.ResultsOf 486 enrolled patients, 79 (16.3%) developed preoperative VTE. Among the ML models, LASSO-LR and multilayer perceptron (MLP) achieved the highest validation AUCs (0.709 each), the best calibration and highest net benefit. The traditional LR nomogram showed an identical AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.691-0.718), with superior calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.738, calibration intercept = -0.109, slope = 0.921) and better stability. Therefore, this simple five-predictor traditional LR nomogram, incorporating age ≥ 65 years, hemoglobin, glucose, external immobilization, and pre-injury anticoagulant or antiplatelet use, was selected as the optimal model.ConclusionThe traditional LR nomogram appears promising for preoperative VTE risk prediction in LEF patients. External validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

Title: Clinical predictive modeling of CK-MB using troponin I/T and CPK in patients post myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Myocardial infarction (MI) continues to be a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. This study evaluated the predictive relationships between Creatine Kinase-MB (CK-MB) and Troponin I/T (cTnI/T), creatine phosphokinase (CPK), and C-reactive protein (CRP) markers to improve clinical interpretation where CK-MB assays are unavailable.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 102 first-time MI patients from multiple Saudi hospitals was analyzed. Demographic, biochemical, and clinical data were extracted, and univariable and multivariable linear regressions were performed via R (v4.4.2). Subgroup analyses by age, sex, and body mass index were conducted to explore demographic variations.
RESULTS: Mean CK-MB levels were 60.85 ± 51.69 U/L in males and 53.71 ± 45.44 U/L in females. cTnI/T, averaged 7.87 ± 12.65 ng/mL, total CPK 370.85 ± 466.99 U/L, and CRP 22.09 ± 14.12 mg/L. Univariable regression revealed strong positive association of CK-MB with cTnI/T, (estimate = 2.98, P < 0.0001, R2 = 0.583), CPK (estimate = 0.082, P < 0.0001, R2 = 0.468), and CRP (estimate = 1.67, P < 0.0001, R2 = 0.202). In the multivariable model, cTnI/T (estimate = 2.33, P < 0.0001) and CPK (estimate = 0.047, P < 0.0001) remained independent predictors, while CRP lost significance (P = 0.192).
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: These findings support using cTnI/T and CPK as reliable clinical correlates for CK-MB estimation in post MI evaluation, especially when laboratory access is limited.

Title: Physiological Adaptations to Controlled Work Rate Heat Acclimation Do Not Differ Between Highly Trained Male and Female Endurance Runners.
Abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine whether the trajectory and magnitude of physiological adaptation to controlled work rate heat acclimation (HEAT) differ between male and female highly trained endurance runners, while comparing adaptations with work rate matched temperate exercise training (TEMP). Eighteen highly trained endurance runners (8 males, 10 females) completed two seven-session interventions consisting of HEAT (40°C, 35% relative humidity [RH]) and TEMP (22°C, 35% RH) in a randomized, counterbalanced crossover design. Each session consisted of 60 min of running at 50% of velocity at maximal oxygen uptake. Physiological adaptation was quantified as the change (Δ) relative to session 1 for core temperature (Tc), skin temperature, heart rate (HR), whole-body sweat rate (WBSR), and plasma volume (PV). No intervention × sex × session interactions were observed for Tc, HR, or WBSR (p > 0.05), indicating that the trajectory of adaptation did not differ between sexes or interventions. Likewise, no sex differences in the overall magnitude of adaptation were observed for any HEAT outcome. Significant main effects of intervention demonstrated greater reductions in mean and peak Tc; baseline, mean, and peak HR; as well as greater increases in WBSR during HEAT compared with TEMP (p < 0.05). PV did not change following either intervention. Male and female highly trained endurance runners exhibited comparable thermoregulatory and cardiovascular adaptation to controlled work rate heat acclimation. Although work rate matched temperate exercise induced partial physiological adaptation, environmental heat stress enhanced the overall adaptation magnitude without altering the adaptation trajectory between sexes.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.
Abstract: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05143177.

Title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules: The NODULE-SHOCK Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B.
RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm2; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm2; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873).
CONCLUSIONS: RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).

Title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year.
METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT).
RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days).
CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

Title: TECTONIC CAD: Pivotal IDE Evaluation of Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Lesions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.
METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S.
CENTERS: The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion.
RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included in the full analysis set, with 330 and 334 as the evaluable populations for the primary safety and primary effectiveness endpoints, respectively, and a median follow-up duration of 36 days (Q1-Q3: 28-37 days). Thirty-day target lesion failure was 0.3% (1 of 330; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 0.0%-1.7%); the upper 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 1.7%, below the 12.9% performance goal (P < 0.0001). Procedural success was 97.0% (324 of 334; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 94.6%-98.6%); the lower 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 94.6%, above the 87.1% performance goal (P < 0.0001). In the OCT substudy, mean calcium length was 22.2 ± 10.3 mm, and the maximum contiguous calcium site had a calcium arc of 247.3 ± 99.0° and a thickness of 0.90 ± 0.25 mm at baseline. At this site, final stent area was 7.1 ± 1.9 mm2, with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting.
CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.

Title: Early Increases in GDF-15 Are Associated With Declines in Cardiac Function With Breast Cancer Therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 is a stress-responsive cytokine induced by mitochondrial dysfunction and genotoxic stress, mechanisms central to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Whether early changes in GDF-15 following cancer therapy relate to subsequent cardiac dysfunction is not established.
OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the longitudinal trajectory of GDF-15 and its associations with changes in cardiac function and structure following cardiotoxic cancer therapy in women with breast cancer.
METHODS: In 366 women receiving anthracyclines and/or trastuzumab from the Penn Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy prospective cohort study, associations between baseline, early-peak (maximum 0-6-month change), and longitudinal GDF-15 concentrations with quantitative echocardiographic measures of systolic, diastolic, and structural function over 36 months were evaluated using multivariable linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: GDF-15 rose from a median baseline of 662 to an early-peak of 1,412 pg/mL, with trajectories differing across regimens (P = 0.004). Each doubling of the early-peak-to-baseline GDF-15 ratio was associated with a subsequent 1.5 percentage point decline in left ventricular ejection fraction (β -1.5%; 95% CI: -2.5 to -0.6; P = 0.002) and a 0.9-unit worsening in longitudinal strain (β 0.9; 95% CI: 0.4-1.4; P = 0.001). GDF-15 was not associated with diastolic outcomes, incident diastolic dysfunction, or incident cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: In women receiving anthracycline- and/or trastuzumab-based breast cancer therapy, early increases in GDF-15 were associated with modest declines in left ventricular ejection fraction and worsening of longitudinal strain, without associations with diastolic measures. These findings support mechanistic investigation of GDF-15 in anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity. (Cardiotoxicity of Cancer Therapy [CCT]; NCT01173341).

Title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.
Journal: The New England journal of medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.
RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.
CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

Title: A Virtual Pulmonary Rehabilitation Program to Address Gaps in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Retrospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional brick-and-mortar pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) programs remain substantially underused, with only 2.7% of Medicare beneficiaries completing PR within 12 months following hospitalization for a COPD exacerbation. Given the critical role of PR in improving exercise tolerance, quality of life, and reducing readmissions, innovative delivery models are needed to address this massive utilization gap. Virtual PR platforms have emerged as a potential solution, offering scalable, and home-based rehabilitation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a novel virtual PR program on functional, psychosocial, and cardiometabolic outcomes among adults with COPD.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed outcomes among patients enrolled in a structured, multidisciplinary virtual PR program between 2022 and 2024. Participants completed individualized exercise and education sessions remotely, supported by a multidisciplinary team including Physicians and Clinical Exercise Physiologists. Baseline and postprogram measures were compared using Cohen d to assess effect sizes across clinical domains. Primary outcomes included changes in maximum metabolic equivalents (METs), Duke Activity Status Index (DASI), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores. Other measures included changes in blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), smoking status, and prevalence of hypertension.
RESULTS: Among 2444 patients completing the program, the largest effect size improvements were observed in maximum METs achieved, DASI, and PHQ-9 scores. The program was also associated with decreased smoking rates and a lower prevalence of hypertension post intervention. Notably, 91% of the studied population self-identified as having a "fixed income," underscoring the potential for virtual PR to extend access to patients with lower incomes in the United States.
CONCLUSIONS: Virtual PR appears to be a promising and potentially more scalable alternative to traditional facility-based PR for patients with COPD. Significant improvements in exercise capacity, mood, and cardiovascular parameters suggest clinical benefit, while reductions in smoking and hypertension further highlight potential for broader health impact. Given the high proportion of participants on fixed incomes, virtual PR may represent an effective strategy to expand access and equity in chronic respiratory care delivery across the United States.

Title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition.
RESULTS: Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411).
DISCUSSION: An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected.
CONCLUSION: An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Serum brain-derived tau in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Brain-derived tau (BD-tau) selectively quantifies tau of central nervous system origin in blood and has demonstrated strong correlations with infarct volume and functional outcome in general ischaemic stroke, but data in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are lacking.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In a prospectively collected cohort of 101 lacunar stroke patients with an MRI-confirmed recent small subcortical infarct (RSSI) and 47 controls, we measured serum BD-tau using the HD-X SIMOA platform at baseline and 3 and 15 months after stroke. We examined associations of BD-tau with infarct size, chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (white matter hyperintensities [WMHs], lacunes, microbleeds, total SVD score), CSVD progression on follow-up MRI and functional outcome.
RESULTS: Baseline serum BD-tau was higher in RSSI patients than controls (median 9.54 [7.32-12.20] vs 7.75 [6.18-9.44] pg/mL; P = .003) and correlated with infarct diameter (rs = 0.222, P = 0.039). Brain-derived tau did not correlate with time from stroke symptom onset to blood sampling (rs = 0.150, P = .179). Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (WMHs, lacunes, microbleeds, SVD score; all P > .05) at any timepoint. Longitudinally, BD-tau returned to control levels by 3 months (P = .374) and remained stable at 15 months (P = .985). Brain-derived tau was neither associated with new vascular MRI lesions on follow-up nor functional neurological outcome.
CONCLUSION: Serum BD-tau is elevated acutely in CSVD-related RSSI, correlates with infarct size and normalises by 3 months. Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features or disease progression, suggesting sensitivity to acute neuronal injury rather than chronic or progressive CSVD.

Title: Patient-centred outcomes with incretin-based therapies and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a programme-level systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is characterised by symptom burden, impaired mobility, and reduced health status. Direct comparative evidence between incretin-based therapies and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors is lacking.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and programme-level meta-analysis, using the independent parent randomised trial programme as the unit of analysis to avoid double-counting linked reports. The primary endpoint was the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score, and the secondary endpoint was the six-minute walk distance. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood estimation with Knapp-Hartung inference.
RESULTS: Six parent programmes were included: STEP-heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, STEP-heart failure with preserved ejection fraction DM, SUMMIT, PRESERVED-HF, EMPEROR-Preserved, and DELIVER. In obesity-focused incretin programmes, pooled mean differences were 7.38 Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score points (95% confidence interval, 6.29 to 8.48; I2 = 0.00%) and 17.60 m for six-minute walk distance (95% confidence interval, 10.69 to 24.52; I2 = 0.00%). The secondary sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score synthesis showed a pooled mean difference of 2.53 points (95% confidence interval, −1.97 to 7.03; I2 = 82.21%). No parent programme was judged to be at high risk of bias.
CONCLUSIONS: Incretin-based therapies showed consistent patient-centred improvements in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, whereas sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor evidence was derived from broader heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction populations and was more heterogeneous. Cross-class comparisons remain exploratory because of population differences, follow-up differences, limited six-minute walk distance availability, and the absence of direct comparative trials; these findings do not establish class superiority.

Title: Troponin Thresholds for Risk Stratification of Chest Pain Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department: Alternatives to the 99th Percentile.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Two methods are used to determine cardiac troponin (cTn) thresholds for high-risk stratification for myocardial infarction (MI), namely the assay's healthy population 99th percentiles and a threshold that has a positive predictive value (PPV) of about 70%. We hypothesized that these methods may produce inconsistent prediction of MI risk.
METHODS: We compared the positive likelihood ratio (LR+), sensitivity, and specificity at 99th percentiles and published high-risk thresholds for a high-sensitivity (hs) cTnI (Abbott) and cTnT (Roche) assay. We simulated the high-risk threshold derivation methodology that derives thresholds with 70% PPV as a function of prevalence and sample size. We derived and validated thresholds based on LR+ = 20 and specificity = 95%.
RESULTS: In 2584 patients there was an almost 2-fold difference in LR+ between males and females at the sex-specific 99th percentiles, and a 2- to 3-fold difference between assays. Thresholds giving 70% PPV were much higher in lower-prevalence cohorts for both assays, being 3- to 10-fold lower at 5% than 20% prevalence. Thresholds derived using a LR+ or specificity had similar performance in a validation cohort between sexes but had a 2-fold difference in LR+ in a validation cohort between assays.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients presenting to the emergency department with possible MI, sex-specific 99th percentile thresholds convey lower risk of MI for females than males. Risks also differed between assays. Risk thresholds derived using the PPV vary considerably with the prevalence and size of cohort. Thresholds derived with specificity or positive likelihood ratio had more consistent risk-prediction.

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Empagliflozin or Dapagliflozin in the MASLD-Heart Failure Phenotype: An Exploratory Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment selection may confound observational comparisons of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and heart failure (HF).
AIMS: To compare recorded outcomes between treatment groups and examine whether the associations persisted after restricting the analysis by agent and diabetes status and separating early and later outcome windows.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective, initiation-based, active-comparator cohort study (new-user design not verified).
METHODS: We used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network and a common index eligibility period from January 1, 2018, through June 2, 2026. The revised analyses were performed on September 12, 2026. An additional sensitivity analysis of acute HF excluded patients with this outcome before the start of the day 1-1825 window. The primary analysis compared semaglutide, liraglutide, or dulaglutide with empagliflozin or dapagliflozin using 1:1 propensity score matching and assessed outcomes during days 1-1825. Separate analyses of the broader GLP-1 RA group examined outcomes during days 1-90 and 91-1825 and among patients with type 2 diabetes and no recorded type 1 diabetes. We report endpoint-specific event proportions, risk differences, hazard ratios (HRs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and proportionality test results.
RESULTS: The primary analysis included 8,550 patients per group after matching. Mortality occurred in 599/8,514 (7.0%) versus 861/8,509 (10.1%); the HR was 0.607 (95% CI, 0.546-0.673). Coded acute HF diagnoses occurred in 1,217/8,550 (14.2%) versus 2,525/8,550 (29.5%); the HR was 0.398 (95% CI, 0.372-0.427), with evidence of non-proportional hazards. In separately matched descriptive interval analyses (8,489 patients per group), the HR for coded acute HF was 0.262 (95% CI, 0.236-0.291) during days 1-90 and 0.507 (95% CI, 0.469-0.548) during days 91-1825. The HR for acute kidney injury during the later interval was 0.740 (95% CI, 0.650-0.842). Among 5,709 matched pairs with type 2 diabetes and no recorded type 1 diabetes, the HR for coded acute HF was 0.431 (95% CI, 0.397-0.468), whereas the HR for ketoacidosis was 0.683 (95% CI, 0.455-1.025). No advantage was observed for acute pancreatitis in any analysis. In a separate analysis excluding patients with prior acute HF, the HR was 0.421 (95% CI, 0.362-0.489), with evidence of non-proportional hazards. Albumin and bilirubin remained imbalanced in a direction favoring the GLP-1 RA group; body mass index also remained imbalanced.
CONCLUSION: GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with lower observed hazards for several outcomes, and the association with coded acute HF was weaker after day 90. The early concentration and magnitude of this association make treatment channeling a plausible explanation, although this analysis cannot establish that explanation. These exploratory findings do not support causal inferences or treatment-preference conclusions and do not challenge randomized evidence supporting SGLT2i use in HF.

Title: Ultrasonographic assessment of diaphragmatic functions in relation to obstructive sleep apnea severity.
Journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects 9-38% of adults and is associated with intermittent hypoxia, sleep fragmentation, and increased cardiovascular risk. Although the diaphragm contributes 60-80% of ventilatory effort, diaphragmatic functional changes in OSA remain inadequately characterized. Diaphragmatic ultrasonography offers a noninvasive, bedside method for functional assessment, but evidence in OSA is limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate diaphragmatic function using ultrasonography in patients evaluated for suspected OSA and to determine its association with disease severity.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 62 patients evaluated for suspected OSA attending inpatient and outpatient services at a tertiary care center between January 2024 and April 2025. OSA severity was classified using polysomnography-derived Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) as per American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) guidelines. Blinded ultrasonographic assessment measured right and left hemidiaphragm thickness, thickening fraction, and diaphragmatic excursion. Statistical analysis included Spearman's correlation, Kruskal-Wallis test, ordinal logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: The mean age was 51 years, with male predominance (72.6%). Most participants were overweight or obese. The median AHI was 25.6 events/hour, and severe OSA was present in 41.9% of participants, while mild OSA constituted 37.1%, reflecting referral-based nature of the cohort. None of the enrolled patients had AHI < 5. Left diaphragmatic excursion showed a weak positive correlation with AHI (ρ = 0.274; P = 0.031) and a multivariable-adjusted association with OSA severity (OR 1.125; 95% CI 1.026-1.249; P = 0.017). For identifying moderate-to-severe OSA, diaphragmatic ultrasonography demonstrated an AUC of 0.72 (95% CI 0.59-0.85; P = 0.002), with 66.1% accuracy, 59.0% sensitivity, and 78.3% specificity.
CONCLUSION: Diaphragmatic function assessed by ultrasonography is largely preserved in OSA, with left diaphragmatic excursion showing a multivariable-adjusted association with disease severity, these findings primarily reflect a mixed-severity population with a substantial proportion of mild OSA. Bedside diaphragmatic ultrasound may serve as an exploratory adjunct for OSA risk stratification, particularly in resource-limited settings, pending external validation.

Title: Welcoming Novelty in the Treatment of Coronary Artery Disease: FDA Approves the Use of Drug-Coated Balloon for Angioplasty.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, with in-stent restenosis (ISR) posing a significant challenge following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Drug-eluting stents (DES) have been widely used to mitigate ISR; however, until recently, no drug-coated balloon (DCB) catheter had been approved for use in the United States. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has now approved AGENT DCB, a paclitaxel-coated balloon catheter, offering a novel approach to treating ISR.
HYPOTHESIS: The approval of AGENT DCB represents a pivotal advancement in PCI, providing an effective alternative to traditional balloon angioplasty for ISR.
METHODS: This article is an editorial review and does not involve original research, statistical analysis, or software-based evaluations. The findings and discussion are based on the results of the AGENT IDE trial and related literature on the efficacy of DCB catheters in the treatment of ISR.
RESULTS: The AGENT IDE trial, a randomized, multicenter study involving 600 participants across 40 US sites, demonstrated that the paclitaxel-coated balloon group had a significantly lower target lesion failure rate at 12 months compared to the uncoated balloon group (17.9% vs. 28.6%, p = 0.003). The reduction was primarily driven by a lower incidence of target lesion revascularization (13.0% vs. 24.7%, p = 0.001) and myocardial infarction related to the target vessel (5.8% vs. 11.1%, p = 0.02). Additionally, no cases of stent thrombosis were observed in the DCB group compared to 3.2% in the control group (p = 0.001), reinforcing the device's safety and efficacy.
CONCLUSIONS: The FDA approval of AGENT DCB marks a significant milestone in the management of ISR, offering a promising alternative to conventional interventions. With its ability to deliver antiproliferative therapy while avoiding the complications associated with permanent stents, DCB may revolutionize PCI strategies in the United States. Further studies assessing the long-term impact of this technology, as well as its application in broader patient populations, will be essential to solidify its role in clinical practice.

Title: A Large Multicenter Cohort of Ataxia-Telangiectasia: Clinical, Immunologic, Genetic, and Survival Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ataxia telangiectasia (AT) is a life-threatening multisystem disorder characterized mainly by neurologic manifestations, infections, and malignancy. We aimed to present a comprehensive analysis of demographic, clinical, immunologic, and genetic features and outcomes of patients with AT in Iran.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 305 registered patients with AT enrolled through a national referral network (2002-2025). Diagnosis was established according to the European Society for Immunodeficiencies criteria.
RESULTS: Mean age at diagnosis and mean age at onset were 72.0 (±46.0) and 25.2 (±35.57) months, respectively. A substantial proportion of patients presented with non-neurological manifestations as their first clinical feature (43.9%). Among non-neurological manifestations, pneumonia was the second most common initial manifestation (13%) and the most frequent infectious complication (30.2%). Variants classified as severe under the predicted loss-of-function (PVS1) criteria were identified in 104 patients, representing 83.8% of those who underwent genetic evaluation. Immunoglobulin abnormalities were detected in 84.7% of patients. A notable proportion of patients showed class switching recombination defects (45.6%), which were associated with a higher burden of clinical morbidity. Median age at death was 12.8 years (95% CI, 11.0-15.0), and the estimated overall survival rates at 5 and 10 years were 81.6% and 60.2%, respectively. Malignancy (28.9%) and respiratory tract infections (20.0%) were the most common causes of death, respectively.
CONCLUSION: This large national cohort provides a comprehensive characterization of the clinical, immunologic, and genetic landscape of AT and its determinants of outcome, thereby improving diagnostic recognition, risk stratification, and patient management.

Title: Early psychosocial-behavioral phenotypes associated with subsequent engagement and longitudinal outcomes in a digital health intervention for heart failure.
Journal: Annals of behavioral medicine : a publication of the Society of Behavioral Medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of digital interventions for heart failure (HF) is limited by variable engagement. Psychosocial phenotyping can characterize engagement heterogeneity, but it remains unclear whether early phenotypes are associated with subsequent engagement and HF outcomes.
PURPOSE: To identify early psychosocial-behavioral phenotypes and examine associations with longitudinal affective and motivational states, digital engagement, and HF outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of a 6-month decentralized randomized controlled trial, using k-medoids clustering of baseline psychosocial characteristics and the first 4 weeks of device engagement among 175 adults with HF. Kruskal-Wallis tests examined phenotype differences in engagement during weeks 5-24. Linear mixed-effects models tested differences in anxiety, depressed mood, motivation, and patient-reported outcomes across 24 weeks.
RESULTS: Three phenotypes emerged: Engaged Self-Regulators (42%), Activated Learners (31%), and Challenged Survivors (26%), characterized by psychological profiles, social and structural resources, and early engagement patterns. Phenotypes differed in subsequent device engagement (all P values less than or equal to .03), with Engaged maintaining the highest use. Differences in anxiety, depressed mood, and motivation persisted over time (P < .001). All phenotypes improved in functional status, quality of life, and self-care; however, Engaged maintained functional status and quality of life scores 20-23 points higher than both other phenotypes (P < .001). Heart failure knowledge trajectories diverged; Engaged and Challenged improved comparably, while Activated showed no gains (P = .008).
CONCLUSIONS: Psychosocial-behavioral phenotypes identified early in a digital intervention were associated with engagement and HF outcomes. Early phenotyping may provide a foundation for prospectively testing phenotype-informed tailoring of digital interventions.
PARENT TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05056129.

Title: Semaglutide and Cardiovascular Death: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Cardioprotective Efficacy of Semaglutide.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular death (CVD) remains a leading cause of global mortality. Although semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), the consistency and exact magnitude of its standalone effect on CVD across various patient phenotypes require comprehensive evaluation. This meta-analysis systematically evaluated the clinical efficacy of semaglutide on CVD risk across randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 to identify RCTs comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), overweight or obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or chronic kidney disease, reporting CVD as a primary, secondary or exploratory outcome. Pooled hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model. Publication bias and study robustness were assessed via Egger's test, Begg's test, and trim-and-fill analysis.
RESULTS: Seven high-quality RCTs comprising 38412 patients were included. Semaglutide significantly reduced the risk of CVD by 17% compared with placebo (pooled HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.72-0.95; P = 0.01). Inter-study heterogeneity was low-to-moderate (I 2= 27.44%, P = 0.18). Subgroup analyses confirmed uniform benefits across different clinical phenotypes (T2DM; overweight or obesity without diabetes; and obesity-related HFpEF, with or without T2DM; P = 0.63) and administration routes (oral versus subcutaneous; P = 0.74). Meta-regression identified trial duration as a key moderator (R 2 = 85.27%, P = 0.089), whereas sex, age, BMI, HbA1c and concomitant SGLT2i therapy did not modify the treatment effect. Publication bias tests were non-significant, and trim-and-fill simulations confirmed the stability of the primary pooled estimate.
CONCLUSION: Semaglutide delivers a robust and consistent 17% reduction in CVD across diverse cardiometabolic populations, including patients with T2DM, overweight or obesity without diabetes, and obesity-related HFpEF. These findings strongly support its role as a foundational cardioprotective intervention, independent of baseline glycemic status or the administration route.

Title: Tricuspid valve repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis of different surgical techniques and their long-term results.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The degree of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is related to mortality. The majority of TR is secondary, and surgery consists mainly of annuloplasty repair (TVr), but repair durability is a prerequisite for a lasting treatment effect. We performed a systematic assessment of TVr durability.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed (MEDLINE, Cochrane Library and Web of Science). Follow-up of TVr techniques and TR recurrence rates were used to estimate incidence rates which were then meta-analyzed using a single-arm meta-analysis model with random-effects. Comparisons between techniques were performed to obtain incidence rate ratios (IRR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 50 studies met the criteria for inclusion (5 randomized and 45 observational), with 15,563 patients, representing 79,763 patient-years (mean follow-up: 3.9 years). Overall recurrence rate was 2.73 per 100 person-years (95% CI 2.15-3.47). Ring annuloplasty had lowest rates (1.81; 95% CI 1.17-2.79), followed by band (2.58; 95% CI 1.66-4.00) and suture (4.06; 95% CI 2.93-5.64). There was a large difference in treatment effects within and between groups (P for interaction=0.011). Compared to suture, ring annuloplasty was associated with lower TR recurrence (IRR 0.45; P = 0.003), but not versus band (IRR 0.71; P = 0.26). There was no difference between band and suture (IRR 0.63; P = 0.12).
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term durability of TVr techniques is extremely heterogeneous. We identified the use of rigid rings and flexible bands as being associated with lower recurrence rates compared to suture techniques.

Title: Interactive Acupuncture for Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poststroke dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) is a common disabling complication of stroke and is associated with malnutrition, aspiration pneumonia, impaired quality of life, and mortality. Conventional swallowing rehabilitation and instrumental assessment are useful but may be limited by equipment dependence and inconsistent accessibility. Interactive acupuncture is a dynamic acupuncture procedure in which short needling stimulation at selected nape acupoints is synchronized with active swallowing tasks.
OBJECTIVE: This protocol describes a multicenter, parallel-group randomized controlled trial that will evaluate whether interactive acupuncture improves swallowing function in patients with poststroke dysphagia compared with conventional acupuncture at the same acupoints.
METHODS: A total of 100 participants with poststroke dysphagia will be randomized 1:1 to an interactive acupuncture group or a conventional acupuncture control group. Both groups will receive routine conventional medical care and standardized acupuncture therapy for stroke. The intervention course comprises 14 sessions delivered 6 times per week followed by a 1-month follow-up. The registered primary outcome is the water swallowing test (WST) grade; the primary efficacy comparison is the change in WST grade from baseline to immediately after the 14th treatment session. Secondary outcomes include the Standardized Swallowing Assessment, Functional Oral Intake Scale, Swallowing Quality of Life Questionnaire, instrumental and physiological assessments, inflammatory markers, safety outcomes, and a supportive WST responder analysis. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline; after sessions 3, 7, and 14; and at 1 month after treatment completion, where applicable.
RESULTS: The current amended protocol was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Hengshui Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine on August 25, 2026 (approval 2026-KY-09), and separate institutional ethics approval was obtained from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (approval Y2025-053-01). The study was funded in June 2025. The trial was registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry on December 30, 2025. Recruitment began on January 1, 2026; as of July 6, 2026, a total of 36 participants had been enrolled. Primary outcome data analysis has not yet begun. Recruitment is expected to continue until June 1, 2027, with final follow-up anticipated by July 2027 and submission of the primary results planned for September 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: This trial will clarify whether adding a task-synchronized interactive acupuncture procedure to the same acupoint prescription provides incremental benefit over conventional acupuncture for poststroke dysphagia and will provide a manualized, fidelity-monitored protocol for future clinical implementation.

Title: Carotid Intima-Media Thickness and Plaque Burden in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Hospital-based Case-Control Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) accelerates atherosclerosis, and carotid ultrasonographic assessment of intima-media thickness (IMT) and plaque offers a noninvasive method to detect subclinical vascular disease and stratify cardiovascular risk.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the IMT of the common and internal carotid arteries between patients with T2DM and age- and sex-matched healthy individuals.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center, hospital-based analytical case-control study included 40 patients with T2DM and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Participants underwent clinical and biochemical assessment, and carotid IMT (common and internal carotid arteries) and plaque were measured using high-resolution B-mode ultrasonography.
RESULTS: Among 80 participants (40 T2DM cases and 40 controls), the groups were comparable in age (52.4 ± 14.9 vs. 51.7 ± 18.7 years; P = 0.843), sex and lifestyle factors. Body mass index was slightly higher in cases (26.9 ± 4.9 vs. 25.1 ± 3.0 kg/m2; P = 0.052). Cases had significantly higher systolic blood pressure/diastolic blood pressure (142.6 ± 11.4/87.3 ± 4.6 vs. 127.4 ± 7.2/84.1 ± 5.6 mmHg) and markedly higher glycemic indices (fasting blood sugar 160.9 vs. 90.1; postprandial blood sugar 224.9 vs. 109.9 mg/dL; all P ≤ 0.006). Triglycerides, very-low-density lipoprotein and total cholesterol were higher in cases, while high-density lipoprotein and low-density lipoprotein were similar. Mean carotid IMT was greater in cases (0.72 ± 0.17 vs. 0.61 ± 0.19 mm; P = 0.006) and plaque was more frequent (50% vs. 17.5%; P = 0.002). IMT was not significantly associated with age or lifestyle factors. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed fair discrimination (area under the curve 0.686; P = 0.004); IMT >0.62 mm yielded 70% sensitivity and 65% specificity.
CONCLUSION: Patients with T2DM had significantly higher carotid IMT and plaque prevalence than controls, supporting carotid ultrasonography as a useful tool for detecting subclinical atherosclerosis and aiding cardiovascular risk stratification.

Title: Perimenopause and cardiometabolic risk: emerging evidence, therapeutic opportunities and unanswered questions.
Journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
Abstract: Perimenopause is increasingly recognized as a critical period for cardiometabolic health. During the years surrounding the final menstrual period, adverse changes in lipid profiles, insulin sensitivity, body composition and vascular function accelerate beyond those expected from aging alone, concurrent with the emergence and peak severity of menopause symptoms. Accumulating evidence suggests that vasomotor symptoms and sleep disturbance are associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Mechanistic data indicate that autonomic dysregulation, inflammation and neuroendocrine systems may represent shared pathways linking symptom burden and cardiometabolic dysfunction. Complementing these findings, prospective studies demonstrate that poor cardiovascular health and metabolic dysfunction may predict subsequent symptom development, suggesting that cardiometabolic health influences the menopause transition experience itself. Together, these findings support a model in which perimenopause represents a physiologic convergence point where symptom burden and cardiometabolic risk intersect, with implications for symptom management and primary prevention. However, major evidence gaps remain, including the absence of interventional studies during perimenopause and uncertainty regarding whether these relationships are causal or therapeutically modifiable. Future research should determine whether targeting cardiometabolic health during this window can improve both cardiovascular outcomes and the symptom experience of the menopause transition.

Title: Integrating SERPINE1 Genotype With Clinical Indicators Improves Venous Thromboembolism Risk Prediction in Cancer Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study From Xinjiang.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk prediction model integrating genetic polymorphisms and routine clinical indicators in a cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang, China.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted on 1135 cancer patients (179 with VTE, 956 without) at Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between March 2024 and May 2025. Six gene polymorphisms (SERPINE1, SERPINC1, PROC, MTHFR, F5, F2) and clinical predictors were assessed. Chi-square tests and logistic regression identified independent predictors for model construction. Model performance was evaluated using ROC analysis, and three clinically optimized cut-off values were defined.ResultsThe SERPINE1 4G allele was identified as a strong genetic risk factor for VTE (4G/4G genotype: OR=2.330, 95%CI: 1.378-3.942; 4G/5G genotype: OR=2.399, 95%CI: 1.411-4.078). No significant associations were found for the other five genes. Age (OR=1.022, 95%CI: 1.008-1.037), D-dimer level (OR=1.288, 95%CI: 1.186-1.399), and hemoglobin level (OR=0.987, 95%CI: 0.979-0.995) were independent clinical predictors (P<0.01). The combined model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.769 (95%CI: 0.731-0.807). Three optimized cut-off values were derived for different clinical contexts: high-sensitivity (90.5%), balanced (Youden index 0.434), and high-specificity (90.1%).ConclusionThe SERPINE1 4G allele independently predicts VTE risk in this cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang. A prediction model integrating this genetic marker with age, D-dimer, and hemoglobin demonstrates good discriminatory performance. The three derived cut-off values may facilitate risk-stratified thromboprophylaxis in clinical practice; however, these findings are based on a retrospective, single-center cohort and internally validated only by ROC analysis.

Title: Identification and risk stratification of chronic kidney disease in primary care.
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD), defined as a reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate and/or increased albuminuria, is a common disease in primary care. CKD is more common in individuals with diabetes and hypertension, as well as older adults and those from minoritized racial-ethnic groups. Although CKD can be diagnosed through blood and urine tests, screening is under-utilized, in part, because there are no clear screening frequency guidelines outside of diabetic kidney disease. Many individuals with diabetes do not receive annual guideline-recommended CKD screening, particularly yearly urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. In primary care, physicians may miss the opportunity to identify, treat, and risk stratify patients with CKD. Early CKD identification and treatment are important because new therapeutics can delay CKD progression to end-stage kidney disease and reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Identifying patients at high risk of CKD progression and complications can guide patient and clinician action. Equations such as the Pooled Cohort Equation, the PREVENT equation, and QRISK® risk score have been validated in predicting the risk of a cardiovascular event in patients with CKD. Furthermore, the Kidney Failure Risk Equation and the Kaiser Permanente Northwest equation have also been validated tools in being able to predict risk of end-stage kidney disease in patients with CKD. Although there have been no validated equations to predict death in patients with CKD, the REIN, and Charlson Comorbidity Indices have been used to predict mortality in patients starting on dialysis to help frame prognostication with patients and their families. These risk equations help to quantify risks for CKD-related outcomes for physicians and patients to aid in deciding therapeutics, understanding prognosis, and instituting timely referral to nephrology.

Title: Dapagliflozin attenuates progression from prefrailty to frailty in patients with hypertension and chronic kidney disease.
Abstract: BACKGROUNDChronic kidney disease (CKD) and hypertension share common pathophysiological pathways contributing to vascular damage, endothelial dysfunction, and physical decline, particularly in older adults with prefrailty. To evaluate the relationship among renal injury, physical performance, and frailty progression in hypertensive older adults with CKD and assess whether dapagliflozin associates with reduced frailty progression, we designed the study DAPA-FORTRESS (DAPAgliflozin and Frailty prOgression in hypeRTension and chRonic kidnEy diSeaSe).METHODSWe enrolled 135 prefrail hypertensive patients with CKD aged >65 years and followed them for 1 year. After coarsened exact matching, our balanced cohort had 105 patients (52 dapagliflozin). Associations between albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and physical performance were analyzed using correlation and regression models. Effect of dapagliflozin on frailty progression was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.RESULTSA significant inverse association between gait speed and albuminuria (r2 = 0.48, P < 0.0001) and significant positive linear association between gait speed and eGFR (r2 = 0.18; P < 0.0001) were observed. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 exhibited significantly worse physical performance than those with higher eGFR (P = 0.0003). In adjusted analyses, receiving dapagliflozin was independently associated with lower odds of progressing to frailty at 1 year (OR = 0.130; CI 0.045-0.381; P < 0.001).CONCLUSIONIn older hypertensive patients with CKD, greater renal injury is associated with worse physical performance, while dapagliflozin use reduces the risk of frailty progression. These findings indicate a potential protective role of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition in mitigating functional decline in this high-risk population.FUNDINGNIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (R01-HL146691), National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (R01-DK123259); American Heart Association (AHA- 24IPA1268813, AHA-22-915561, AHA-24-1195524).

Title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
Abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

Title: Statin Intolerance, Treatment Gaps, and Cardiovascular Outcomes: A 24-Year Health System Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statin intolerance may disrupt lipid-lowering therapy (LLT). We characterized clinician-documented intolerance and assessed whether cardiovascular risk was concentrated among patients who discontinued all LLT.
METHODS: We studied new statin users at Mass General Brigham using medication records dated 1987 through November 2025. Temporal trend analyses were restricted to 2001 through 2024. We characterized postintolerance management and examined cardiovascular outcomes using time-varying Cox models. Within the intolerance cohort, we compared patients who discontinued all LLT with those who continued any LLT.
RESULTS: Among 254 035 new statin users, 10 644 (4.2%) developed documented intolerance after a median of 3.1 years. Musculoskeletal symptoms were documented in 68.1%. Within 90 days, 39.9% discontinued all LLT and fewer than 10% received a nonstatin-based strategy. At 3 to 6 months, mean low-density lipoprotein cholesterol increased by 6.8 mg/dL among discontinuers and decreased by 4.9 mg/dL among continuers. Compared with statin-tolerant patients, intolerance was associated with higher risks of coronary artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke (hazard ratios, 1.12-1.55). Within the intolerance cohort, discontinuing all LLT was associated with higher risk across all outcomes, with hazard ratios ranging from 1.38 for mortality to 2.14 for venous thromboembolism.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinician-documented statin intolerance was frequently followed by complete LLT discontinuation and limited use of nonstatin therapy. Complete discontinuation identified a high-risk subgroup with worsening lipid trajectories, supporting systematic reassessment and restoration of statin or nonstatin therapy.

Title: Association between urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and postpartum resistant hypertension in patients with severe preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
Journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to investigate the association between elevated urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia at a tertiary care center in Colombia.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted in Medellín, Colombia. Patients aged >18 years diagnosed with severe preeclampsia who underwent UPCR assessment were included. Associations between elevated UPCR (≥0.3) and resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization were evaluated using robust Poisson regression models.
RESULTS: A total of 261 patients were included in the study. Bivariate analysis showed that resistant hypertension in the postpartum period was more frequent in the UPCR ≥0.3 group than in the UPCR <0.3 group (43.2% vs. 12.7%; risk ratio 3.69; 95% confidence interval 1.92-7.07). After adjustment for maternal age, body mass index, and gestational age at diagnosis, elevated UPCR remained independently associated with resistant hypertension (adjusted risk ratio 4.87; 95% confidence interval 1.86-12.76). Earlier gestational age at diagnosis was also independently associated with resistant hypertension.
CONCLUSION: The UPCR is independently associated with the development of resistant hypertension during postpartum hospitalization in patients with severe preeclampsia.

Title: Extended Wearable ECG Monitoring Detects Unrecognised Arrhythmias After COPD Exacerbation: The PRECURSOR Pilot Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The period after hospitalisation for an acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with cardiovascular vulnerability. Clinically important rhythm disturbances may be intermittent or asymptomatic and escape routine postdischarge assessment; however, the diagnostic yield of prolonged monitoring is intrinsically influenced by monitoring duration.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre observational pilot, 18 adults recently hospitalised for COPD exacerbation underwent continuous remote monitoring for 21 days between September 2019 and February 2020. The three-lead ZENSOR wearable recorded electrocardiographic rhythm, heart rate and respiratory rate and transmitted full-disclosure data and predefined alerts for clinician review. The primary outcome was participant-level detection of previously unrecognised, cardiologist-confirmed arrhythmias warranting therapeutic evaluation or intervention. Outcomes were analysed descriptively with exact 95% binomial confidence intervals.
RESULTS: Participants were predominantly male (15/18; 83.3%), with a mean age of 73 ± 6 years. Seven had GOLD grade 3-4 airflow limitation, seven received long-term oxygen therapy, five had coronary artery disease and four had chronic atrial fibrillation. During the planned 21-day monitoring period, previously unrecognized clinically actionable arrhythmias were detected in 9/18 participants (50.0%; 95% CI: 26.0-74.0). Nonmutually exclusive findings included trigeminy (2/18), third-degree atrioventricular block (2/18), bradycardia (5/18), newly detected atrial fibrillation (1/18), supraventricular tachycardia (2/18) and nocturnal atrial or ventricular ectopy (8/18). Sixteen participants (88.9%; 95% CI: 65.3-98.6) reported satisfaction with monitoring.
CONCLUSIONS: Extended wearable electrocardiographic monitoring produced a high participant-level detection yield of previously unrecognised arrhythmias during early recovery from hospitalised COPD exacerbation. This finding supports targeted postdischarge rhythm surveillance but does not distinguish biological post-exacerbation vulnerability from the greater ascertainment achieved by prolonged monitoring. Confirmation requires larger controlled studies with comprehensive cardiopulmonary phenotyping, standardised monitoring-performance metrics and comparative clinical outcomes.

Title: Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.
RESULTS: Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

Title: Sleep and Cardiometabolic Disease: A Wearable-Electronic Health Record Study in the US All of Us Research Program.
Abstract: Background: Sleep health spans duration, quality, regularity, and timing, yet Life's Essential 8 scores sleep by duration alone, and regularity studies used about 1 week of data. How these dimensions, measured over months, relate to incident cardiometabolic disease is unknown, as is whether nightly sleep-cycle structure adds information. Methods: This cohort study included US adults in the All of Us Research Program with linked Fitbit and electronic health records (2009-2023). We derived 11 sleep metrics over a 180-day baseline (≥90 valid nights). Incident diagnoses, grouped into phecodes, were counted after a 180-day washout to limit reverse causation. Primary analyses related these metrics to prespecified endpoints, including a CVD composite (myocardial infarction, heart failure, cardiomyopathy, or ischemic stroke), heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. Cox models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, and comorbidity factors. Exploratory analyses examined wearable-estimated sleep cycles (7,199 participants; 1,017,812 sleep-stage nights). Results: Among 10,362 participants (median age, 53 years; 70% female), 230 developed the CVD composite (median follow-up, 3.7 years). Each 1-SD (29-minute) higher night-to-night variability in sleep duration was associated with higher CVD composite risk (hazard ratio, 1.24 [95% CI, 1.09-1.41]), as was higher variability in bedtime (1.23 [1.10-1.37]), waketime (1.20 [1.09-1.32]), and midpoint (1.21 [1.09-1.35]); mean sleep duration was not (0.96 [0.85-1.08]). Variability in sleep duration was also associated with heart failure (1.32 [1.13-1.55]), hypertension (1.16 [1.08-1.25]), and type 2 diabetes (1.20 [1.07-1.35]). More sleep cycles were associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk (0.72 [0.58-0.89]), independent of sleep duration, regularity, and timing (0.58 [0.44-0.77]). Conclusions: Night-to-night irregularity in sleep duration and timing was associated with the CVD composite, heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes; mean duration was not associated with the CVD composite. More wearable-estimated sleep cycles were associated with lower atrial arrhythmia risk beyond conventional sleep metrics, a novel finding requiring confirmation.

Title: Albumin/Neutrophil-Lymphocyte Ratios and All-Cause and Cardiovascular Mortality in Atherosclerotic Patients.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: BackgroundSerum albumin (ALB) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) are linked to adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but few studies have used ALB/NLR (ANLR) to assess mortality risk in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). This study evaluated the nonlinear association between ANLR and all-cause mortality (ACM) and cardiovascular mortality (CVM) in ASCVD patients.MethodsThis study was grounded in data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey spanning 1999 to 2018.ResultsThe study cohort comprised 2,918 participants. During the follow-up period, 1,231 all-cause deaths and 454 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed that a lower ANLR (Q1) was associated with worse survival outcomes (ACM and CVM: log-rank test P < 0.001). Multivariate Cox regression showed a significant inverse association between ANLR and the risk of ACM (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.883, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.810-0.964, P = 0.005). After ANLR was grouped according to quartiles, the risk of CVM in the Q2-Q4 groups was significantly lower than that in the Q1 group. Restricted cubic spline analysis further revealed a nonlinear negative link between ANLR and the risk of ACM (P for nonlinear < 0.001), and the risk rose sharply when ANLR < 1.8, suggesting this value may be a practical cutoff for identifying high-risk individuals. Additionally, the elevated risk observed at ANLR > 3.816 may reflect a U-shaped association rather than measurement error alone.ConclusionsANLR was significantly and negatively associated with the risk of ACM and CVM in ASCVD, and there was a nonlinear threshold effect. This finding provides an economical biomarker for identifying high-risk individuals and assessing the prognosis of ASCVD. Nonetheless, longitudinal studies are needed to verify these findings.

Title: Long-Term Outcomes of Endoscopic or Open Vein Harvesting for Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A 10-Year Follow-Up of the REGROUP Randomized Clinical Trial.
Sustained Improvement in Interstage Survival and Outcomes Within the National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborative.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infants with hypoplastic left heart syndrome remain at high risk during the interstage between stage 1 and stage 2 surgical palliations. As a multicenter Learning Health Network, the National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborate uses collaborative research and improvement to improve hypoplastic left heart syndrome outcomes for infants. We evaluated whether our previously reported improvement in interstage survival from 90.5% to 94.8% was sustained over time.
METHODS: Infants enrolled in the National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborate clinical registry who underwent stage 1 surgical palliation and were discharged home during the interstage period were included. Patient demographics, hypoplastic left heart syndrome anatomic type, and neonatal hospitalization data in phase 1 (2008-2016) and phase 2 (2016-2025) were compared. Statistical process control was used to analyze rates of interstage survival, major adverse event readmissions, and growth failure.
RESULTS: A total of 5495 patients (phase 1-2199, phase 2-3296) were enrolled from 77 centers, of which 38.7% were female and 11.2% had a major syndrome. The phase 2 cohort had a higher prevalence of RV-PA conduit (phase 1: 55.2% versus phase 2: 64.3%; P<0.001), lower median NEONATE score (9 versus 3; P<0.001), higher digoxin prescription (28.9% versus 74.7%; P<0.001), and longer median length of stay compared with phase 1 (28 versus 34 days; P<0.001). Improvement in interstage survival noted in phase 1 was sustained throughout phase 2 at 94.8%. Major adverse event readmissions declined early in phase 2 and were maintained (1.74 versus 0.9/100 interstage patients). Adequate growth was statistically different but clinically stable over time (mean weight Z score at stage 2 admission -1.5 versus -1.42; P<0.019).
CONCLUSIONS: National Pediatric Cardiology Quality Improvement Collaborate sustained significant improvements in interstage outcomes through continued adherence to improvement processes, collaborative learning, and promoting best practices over time, including utilization of digoxin and NEONATE score.

Title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment.
METHODS: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF.
RESULTS: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040).
CONCLUSIONS: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

Title: Performance of the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway prehospital triage system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates: a quality-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Accurate identification is one of the cornerstones of prehospital care for patients with suspected acute ischaemic stroke (AIS). In the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway triage system, emergency medical service (EMS) providers use dedicated criteria to identify acute reperfusion candidates and call a coordinated medical team (CMT, including a neurologist and an emergency physician), which can activate the stroke code pathway. The objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of the system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates.
METHODS: This was a retrospective single-centre quality-control study conducted in a Swiss university-based stroke centre, from 1 January 2019 to 31 May 2022. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥18 years, for whom the EMS called the CMT or patients with AIS eligible for acute reperfusion managed by the EMS. The main outcomes were the performance of both the EMS and the CMT in detecting AIS patients eligible for acute reperfusion, as assessed through their respective under- and overtriage rates. A secondary outcome was the identification of alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients.
RESULTS: Of 1071 patients included, the EMS phone-contacted the CMT for 937 (87.5%) of them. Among the 1071 patients, 440 (41%) had an AIS eligible for reperfusion. The system's undertriage rate was 30% (133 patients without stroke pathway activation among the 440 patients with an AIS eligible for acute reperfusion).
