The undertriage rates were 21% for the EMS and 11% for the CMT. The overtriage rates were 63% for the EMS and 57% for the CMT. The main alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients were seizures (14%), intracranial haemorrhages (9.9%) and functional disorders (6.5%).
CONCLUSION: Undertriage and overtriage rates were relatively high, but both were reduced by the CMT call, highlighting the added value of a second expert assessment step, with a higher level of expertise. Concerning overtriage, a better prehospital identification of alternative diagnoses, such as seizures or functional disorders, could help to better classify our patients.

Title: Electrocardiographic screening in paediatric and adolescent athletes: a 6-year prospective observational study from a Swiss mass-participation race.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pre-participation cardiovascular screening with resting 12-lead electrocardiography (ECG) is recommended by most sports societies to detect conditions associated with sudden cardiac death. While the ideal age to initiate screening remains controversial, an expert consensus paper written in Switzerland suggested starting ECG screening at 15 years of age. As part of the Swiss multicentre prospective ECG screening study (Swiss PAED), we initiated an ECG screening programme in 2018 in conjunction with the Course de l'Escalade, a popular Geneva running event attracting over 10,000 children and adolescents annually.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted between 2018 and 2024 (excluding 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic) during the Course de l'Escalade in Geneva, Switzerland. Competitive athletes aged 8-17 years training ≥6 hours per week in organised sport and without known cardiac disease were invited to undergo pre-participation cardiovascular evaluation including medical history, physical examination and resting 12-lead ECG. ECGs were interpreted according to the 2017 international criteria for athlete ECG interpretation and classified as normal, borderline or abnormal. Abnormal ECGs were referred for specialist cardiology evaluation.
RESULTS: A total of 428 athletes (239 boys; mean age 12.9 [2.7] years) were enrolled. Normal variants were observed in 298/428 athletes (69.6%), most frequently sinus arrhythmia (183/428, 42.8%). Borderline findings in isolation occurred in 30/428 athletes (7.0%), most often right atrial enlargement (16/30, 3.7%). Abnormal findings were detected in 7/428 (1.6%) athletes, among whom 2/7 were subsequently found to have a condition associated with sudden cardiac death: Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern.
CONCLUSION: ECG-based screening during the Course de l'Escalade identified abnormal findings in 1.6% of young athletes among whom 2/7 were found to harbour a disease associated with sudden cardiac death. Current international interpretation criteria performed well in this population of young competitive athletes.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Physical Activity, and Diet in Law Enforcement Officers: A 6-Year Prospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Law enforcement officers (LEOs) often display poor cardiovascular health, which can impair job performance and increase cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. While many cross-sectional studies have documented these issues, few have examined the progression of CVD risk factors over time, and none appear to have used a longitudinal design assessing incidence in relation to healthy lifestyle behaviors within a sex-representative sample of this occupation.
METHODS: This prospective study followed 228 LEOs (28% women) over 6 years using online questionnaires assessing CVD risk factors, physical activity, and fruit and vegetable intake. Incidence of CVD risk factors was analyzed according to baseline physical activity (active vs. inactive), fruit and vegetable intake (≥5 vs. <5 servings/day), and their combined adherence.
FINDINGS: Over time, participants showed significant increases in weight (p < .001, Cohen's d = .49), body mass index (p < .001, Cohen's d = .53), and prevalence of most CVD risk factors. Physically inactive LEOs demonstrated higher incidence of dyslipidemia (7% vs. 0%, p = .04, Cramer's V = .15) compared to active counterparts. Those consuming <5 daily servings of fruits and vegetables were more likely to develop hypertension (7% vs. 0%, p < .01, Cramer's V = .19) and dyslipidemia (8% vs. 1%, p = .01, Cramer's V = .18). The lowest cumulative incidence was observed among participants meeting both lifestyle recommendations.
CONCLUSIONS/APPLICATION TO PRACTICE: CVD risk factors increased over time in this LEO sample, with baseline physical inactivity and poor diet tending to predict greater incidence. These findings suggest the need for workplace health promotion programs targeting physical activity and healthy eating to reduce long-term CVD risk in this population.

Title: Blood and urinary NT-proBNP: atrial fibrillation-associated patterns and cardiac dysfunction in acute chest pain.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: NT-proBNP is the gold-standard biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring congestive heart failure (CHF); however, its role in detecting atrial fibrillation (AFib) is gaining attention. This study assessed the influence of aberrant cardiac rhythms on plasma NT-proBNP (pNT) considering urinary NT-proBNP (uNT) as a noninvasive alternative in selected clinical scenarios.
METHODS: In 824 patients presenting with chest pain at the emergency department of the University Hospital of Regensburg, pNT was assessed. A subset of 355 patients additionally provided uNT.
RESULTS: Both pNT and uNT were significantly increased in AFib, and lesser in atrial flutter (AFlut) and right ventricular (RV) pacing compared to SR (each p < 0.05). A pNT cutoff of 900 pg/mL yielded 74% sensitivity and 83% specificity for discriminating AFib from SR (AUC = 0.85). In multivariate regression, pNT or uNT and history of AFib were independent predictors of AFib (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Both pNT and uNT are significantly elevated in AFib, and to a lesser extent AFlut, and RV pacing independently of heart failure. These findings align with prior observations and provide further evidence supporting adequately powered prospective studies to evaluate rhythm-adjusted diagnostic thresholds for CHF in AFib. In addition, uNT may complement pNT when venous access is difficult or serial remote monitoring is required.

Title: Double Consecutive Electrical Countershock for Atrial and Ventricular Fibrillation: A Narrative Critical Review.
Journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent strategies for refractory ventricular fibrillation (VF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) employ two consecutive, biphasic shocks with varying evidence of success. Due to their electrophysiological similarities, the strategies used for VF and AF can be collectively referred to as double consecutive electrical countershock (DCEC). This review aims to identify and synthesize outcome data on the effectiveness of DCEC across both VF and AF.
METHODS: This narrative critical review with systematic search methods was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA checklist where applicable. From 672 identified articles, 262 duplicates were removed and 410 screened; 316 articles irrelevant to the study were excluded. Of 94 sought for retrieval, 8 were unavailable and 67 failed full-text screening, leaving 19 included articles (16 VF, 3 AF). All 19 underwent risk-of-bias assessment (RoB2, ROBINS-I, or AMSTAR-2) and data extraction.
RESULTS: Full-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) showed low risk of bias, pilot RCTs had "some concerns," observational studies carried serious risk of bias, and meta-analyses showed "low confidence." High-quality randomized evidence showed improved primary outcomes for DCEC in both refractory VF (survival to discharge, return of spontaneous circulation, good neurological outcome) and high-BMI AF (arrhythmia termination). Non-randomized observational studies predominantly showed non-statistically significant differences.
CONCLUSIONS: DCEC shows potential to improve arrhythmia termination in refractory VF and high-BMI AF. Randomized evidence supports its efficacy, while observational findings remain neutral due to confounding. Success in high-BMI AF supports elevated BMI as a hypothetical indication for DCEC in VF.

Title: The Many Faces of Familial Mediterranean Fever in Children: Lessons From a Moroccan Cohort and Four Diagnostic Pitfalls.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is the prototypical hereditary autoinflammatory disease. Inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, it is associated with mutations in the MEditerranean FeVer (MEFV) gene. Its clinical heterogeneity poses a major diagnostic challenge in pediatrics, particularly in developing countries where access to genetic testing remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical, epidemiological, biological, and genetic characteristics of pediatric FMF in the Oriental region of Morocco and to document diagnostic pitfalls through illustrative case reports.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study including 14 children followed for FMF in the Pediatrics Department of the Mohammed VI University Hospital in Oujda over an 11.5-year period (January 2015 to June 2026). The diagnosis was based on the Yalçınkaya-Özen pediatric criteria and/or genetic confirmation via MEFV gene sequencing.
RESULTS: The mean age at diagnosis was 6.5 years (range: 2-14 years). A marked male predominance was observed in 12 (85.7%); sex ratio (6:1). Parental consanguinity was present in 5/14 (35.7%) of cases. All patients were from the Oriental region 14/14 (100.0%). The predominant clinical manifestations were recurrent fever in 14 (100.0%), abdominal pain in 12/14 (85.7%), and arthralgia/arthritis in 11/14 (78.6%). MEFV gene sequencing was positive in 9/14 (64.3%) of patients, with a predominance of the M694V mutation in 5/14 (35.7%), of whom 3/5 (60.0%) were homozygous. Four illustrative case reports document atypical presentations that resulted in a diagnostic delay of more than two years: a polyarticular form mimicking juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), a coronary aneurysm mistaken for Kawasaki disease, recurrent febrile seizures, and predominantly erysipelas-like erythema. Colchicine was effective in all 14/14 (100.0%) treated cases. No amyloid amyloidosis (AA) was detected during follow-up.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric FMF is underdiagnosed in the Oriental region of Morocco. Its clinical polymorphism leads to diagnostic delays with harmful consequences. A rigorous clinical evaluation supported by targeted genetic sequencing is essential for early diagnosis and prompt initiation of colchicine therapy.

Title: Underuse of Intramuscular Adrenaline in Pediatric Anaphylaxis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anaphylaxis is a potentially life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction for which prompt intramuscular adrenaline is the recommended first-line treatment.
PURPOSE: We aimed to describe the triggers, clinical characteristics, severity, and treatment patterns of pediatric anaphylaxis in children at a single tertiary allergy center, with particular focus on adherence to guideline-recommended adrenaline use.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 51 children aged 0-18 years diagnosed with anaphylaxis at the Pediatric Allergy and Immunology Clinic, Alanya Alaaddin Keykubat University, between 2020 and 2025. Severity was graded using the 2024 World Allergy Organization (WAO) classification. Associations between demographic, clinical, and treatment variables were assessed using appropriate non-parametric tests.
RESULTS: Fifty-one children were included (32 male [62.7%] and 19 female [37.3%]; mean age 6.38 ± 5.16 years). Food was the leading trigger (52.9%), followed by Hymenoptera venom (17.6%), drugs (13.7%), and idiopathic reactions (13.7%), with a significant age gradient across trigger categories (food-induced reactions occurring in younger children; p<0.001). Cutaneous (92.2%) and respiratory (82.4%) symptoms predominated. Adrenaline was administered in only 49.0% of reactions overall and was markedly less frequent in food-induced (25.9%) than in drug- (100%) or venom-induced (77.8%) anaphylaxis (p=0.001). Increasing WAO severity grade was significantly associated with cardiovascular involvement (p=0.016) and inversely associated with the use of antihistamines as the initial treatment (p=0.013). Sixteen patients (31.4%) were hospitalized and only 14 (27.5%) were prescribed an adrenaline auto-injector at discharge.
CONCLUSION: In this pediatric cohort, anaphylaxis triggers and treatment patterns showed clear age-related differences. Adrenaline was underused, particularly in food-induced reactions among young children, potentially reflecting difficulties in early symptom recognition. These findings highlight the need for improved anaphylaxis recognition and timely adrenaline use, particularly in young children, as well as appropriate adrenaline auto-injector prescription at discharge, accompanied by training in its use and reinforcement of the importance of carrying the prescribed device.

Title: Evaluation of devices used for endovascular repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in the international consortium of vascular registries: an international, retrospective, multicentre, single-arm, open-label performance goal study.
Abstract:
IINTRODUCTION: The purpose of this study was to pilot a new concept for device appraisal-leveraging international real-world data (RWD) from the International Consortium of Vascular Registries (ICVRs) to assess aggregate endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) performance against a conservative performance goal (PG) derived from open surgical repair (OSR), with the intention of helping refine device labelling in collaboration with industry and the US Food and Drug Administration.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: International retrospective, multicentre, single-arm cohort, open-label clinical PG-based study within the ICVRs. Because OSR patients may not have been anatomically EVAR-eligible, the OSR cohort used for PG derivation was restricted to smaller diameters (<6.5 cm men; <5.5 cm women) to include patients eligible for EVAR. Analyses performed at Weill Cornell Medicine (MDEpiNet Center).
RESULTS: OSR PG cohort: 932 patients (72±9 years average; 83.8% men) with 30% in-hospital mortality. EVAR cohort: 219 patients (75±10 years average, 83.1% men) with larger aneurysms (EVAR 7.3±2.0 cm vs OSR 5.3±1.3 cm; p<0.001). In-hospital mortality after EVAR was 18% (upper 95% CI 13% to 23%), exceeding the PG (p<0.001). EVAR showed lower dialysis (10.6% vs 15.7%; p=0.02), bowel ischaemia (1.8% vs 7.5%; p<0.001) and reoperation for bleeding (2.7% vs 7.1%; p=0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: This proof-of-concept study shows harmonised international RWD can evaluate device performance in ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. Despite a comparator biased to favour OSR, EVAR met/exceeded the PG and reduced complications, supporting regulatory discussions to align instructions for use with guideline-endorsed EVAR-first strategies.

Title: Maternal Mortality Across a Multi-Hospital Health System in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study (2016-2024).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains a pressing global health challenge and is a vital indicator of healthcare quality. Despite improvements in Saudi Arabia, preventable maternal fatalities continue to occur, with insufficient research on regional disparities.
OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to assess the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and its causes across five hospitals within the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs in Saudi Arabia and evaluate it is main causes,thereby addressing a gap in maternal mortality data in the Gulf region.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, descriptive study included all maternal deaths occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days postpartum between 2016 and 2024 across five National Guard hospitals in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam. Data were extracted from hospital records and analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 28.
RESULTS: Eighteen maternal deaths were identified over the nine-year period, yielding an overall MMR of 6.2 per 100,000 live births (mean age at death 29.8 ± 6.3 years). MMR varied considerably by year, from 0.00/100,000 in 2017 to 37.5/100,000 in 2020. Pregnancy-related complications accounted for 50% of deaths (9/18), most commonly venous thromboembolism (66.7%). Non-obstetric causes included COVID-19 (16.7%), unknown cause (16.7%), brain tumor (5.6%), and myocarditis (5.6%). Most deaths occurred in women with parity 1-3 (61.1%), split evenly between vaginal and caesarean delivery (50% each). Geographic variation was marked: Riyadh recorded deaths in most years with a peak in 2020; Dammam and Al-Ahsa each showed sporadic extreme spikes; Jeddah showed intermittent elevations; no deaths occurred in Madinah.
CONCLUSION: The overall MMR at these hospitals is comparatively low to global figures, significant variations across different cities and years, alongside a notable number of deaths with unspecified causes, underscore the need for standardized mortality reviews, autopsy confirmations for suspected embolic deaths, and continuous targeted monitoring.

Title: Serum Lipid Abnormalities and Age-Related Cataract: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in North India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dyslipidaemia may contribute to age-related cataract through altered lens membrane homeostasis, oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation, but clinical evidence remains inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: To compare serum lipid profiles in adults with and without age-related cataract and quantify the independent associations of specific lipid abnormalities with cataract.
METHODS: This hospital-based case-control study included 300 adults aged 50 years or older at a tertiary care centre in Kanpur, India, from April 2024 to October 2025. Cases were 150 patients with age-related cataract, and controls were 150 participants without cataract. Patients with diabetes, secondary cataract or lipid-lowering therapy were excluded. Fasting total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), very-low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (VLDL-C) and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) were measured by enzymatic colourimetry. Separate multivariable logistic regression models adjusted each lipid abnormality for age, sex, education, occupation, smoking, alcohol use and socioeconomic status.
RESULTS: Cases were older than controls (63.07 ± 6.14 vs 60.70 ± 6.67 years; p = 0.002). Compared with controls, cases had higher total cholesterol (209.62 ± 33.23 vs 183.10 ± 28.08 mg/dL), triglycerides (169.42 ± 34.47 vs 146.65 ± 27.12 mg/dL), LDL-C (138.69 ± 30.45 vs 119.17 ± 21.27 mg/dL) and VLDL-C (33.89 ± 6.89 vs 29.33 ± 5.42 mg/dL), and lower HDL-C (39.49 ± 5.90 vs 45.95 ± 6.75 mg/dL; all p < 0.001). Adjusted odds of cataract were higher with low HDL-C (adjusted odds ratio {aOR} 3.91, 95% confidence interval {CI} 2.22-6.89), high LDL-C (aOR 3.06, 95% CI 1.86-5.04), high VLDL-C (aOR 3.03, 95% CI 1.84-5.00), high triglycerides (aOR 2.69, 95% CI 1.64-4.43) and high total cholesterol (aOR 2.49, 95% CI 1.54-4.05). Lipid distributions did not differ significantly across the 15 recorded cataract morphology categories.
CONCLUSION: Dyslipidaemia, particularly low HDL-C and elevated atherogenic lipids, was independently associated with age-related cataract in this hospital population. These findings identify a clinically relevant metabolic correlate but do not establish causality. Prospective population-based studies should determine whether lipid abnormalities predict cataract onset or progression.

Title: Efficacy and safety of semaglutide versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes: updated meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity poses significant challenges for those seeking long-term weight loss through diet and exercise alone. Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for chronic weight management in eligible adults.
METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of semaglutide for treating obesity in adults without diabetes. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261338170). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through February 28, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing semaglutide with placebo in adults without diabetes with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2 or ≥ 27 kg/m2 and at least one obesity-related comorbidity. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 Tool, GRADE methodology, RevMan v5.4, and CMA v3 were used for risk-of-bias assessment, certainty-of-evidence assessment, data analyses, and meta-regression analyses respectively.
RESULTS: We included 10 RCTs with a total of 7,131 participants. Risk-of-bias was judged at the level of each outcome: all included trials were at low risk-of-bias for the efficacy outcomes and the prespecified safety outcomes, while cardiovascular and psychiatric disorders raised some concerns. Compared to placebo, semaglutide produced significantly greater reductions in percentage change in body weight (WMD -12.29%, 95% CI -13.38 to -11.20, I2 88%, 95% PI -16.06 to -8.52; 10 studies, n = 6975), absolute change in body weight from baseline (WMD -12.67 kg, 95% CI -13.53 to -11.81, I2 77%, 95% PI -15.36 to -9.98; 10 studies, n = 6975), BMI (WMD -4.55 kg/m2, 95% CI -5.08 to -4.03, I2 86%, 95% PI -6.33 to -2.78; 8 studies, n = 6573), and waist circumference (WMD -9.42 cm, 95% CI -10.27 to -8.56, I2 79%, 95% PI -12.12 to -6.71; 10 studies, n = 6970). Participants assigned to semaglutide also had a higher probability of reaching a ≥ 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% loss of body weight (9 studies, n = 6103). However, substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed for efficacy outcomes, indicating that the magnitude of benefit varied across trials. With semaglutide, individuals experienced a greater number of total adverse events (aggregate proportions 90.0% vs. 85.0%; RR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.10, I2 72%; 9 studies, n = 6922) and discontinuation due to adverse events (aggregate proportions 6.0% vs. 3.0%; RR 1.86, 95% CI 1.41 to 2.45, I2 0%; 10 studies, n = 7129) than did individuals taking the placebo; while for serious adverse events (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.51, I2 40%; 10 studies, n = 7129) the estimate was imprecise, did not establish a clear difference and the interval remains compatible with a potentially important increase in risk. These pooled figures represent average effects and may not apply equally across different semaglutide doses, formulations, treatment duration, or patient populations. Certainty-of-evidence was low for the primary outcome of percentage change in body weight and for absolute change in body weight and change in BMI, and very low for change in waist circumference.
CONCLUSION: Semaglutide was associated with clinically meaningful weight loss during trial treatment periods in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes; however, low-certainty evidence and substantial between-study heterogeneity warrant cautious interpretation of the magnitude of benefit.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02108-x.

Title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke-Pro and Contra.
Journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

Title: Remote activity and rhythm monitoring using patient-owned consumer devices after first-time pulmonary vein isolation.
Journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Passively collected physical activity data from consumer devices could provide a scalable, objective measure of functional status in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study assessed the feasibility of remotely collecting activity and rhythm data from patients undergoing index pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).
METHODS: AF patients enrolled in the prospective TRUST registry who underwent index PVI and reported owning an eligible smartphone were re-contacted to provide informed consent and share their smartphone- and smartwatch-generated data. Pre-specified feasibility criteria were participation rate, technical success, and temporal data coverage. The primary functional outcome was the mean daily step-count change between the one-year pre-PVI and two-year post-PVI windows. Exploratory analyses examined associations of daily activity with AF recurrence and AF burden.
RESULTS: Of 280 eligible patients, 172 (61%) attempted and 154/172 (90%) completed data transfer, of whom 123 met pre-specified completeness criteria. Median monitoring duration was 6.0 [3.6, 6.6] years, with 98% [77, 100] coverage. Mean daily step count increased from 5731±2808 to 6220±2816 steps/day after PVI (+488 steps/day [187, 789]; p=0.002). In 35 smartwatch users, AF burden decreased from 3.6% [1.6, 10.8] to 0.0% [0.0, 0.3] after PVI (p<0.001). Baseline AF burden was inversely correlated with daily step count (ρ=-0.36, p=0.035).
CONCLUSION: Remote collection of activity and rhythm data from consumer smartphones and smartwatches is feasible, yielding high-coverage, multi-year research data. This enables scalable, objective quantification of longitudinal functional outcomes. Daily step count increased after PVI in this exploratory cohort and was inversely related to baseline AF burden.

Title: Microbiological profiles, antimicrobial resistance patterns and mortality-associated factors in necrotizing soft tissue infections: a 16-year retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Necrotizing soft tissue infections (NSTIs) are rapidly progressive, life-threatening infections requiring prompt surgical and antimicrobial treatment. We aimed to characterize the microbiological profiles and antimicrobial resistance patterns of NSTIs and to assess their associations with 90-day mortality.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 212 adults with NSTIs admitted from December 2008 to May 2025. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, pathogen groups and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns were compared between survivors and non-survivors. All 40 candidate factors were jointly included in ridge-penalized logistic regression, and estimation stability was assessed using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Overall 90-day mortality was 29.7% (63/212), and Gram-negative infections predominated (43.9%, 93/212). Mortality was 40.0% (12/30), 33.3% (31/93), and 66.7% (2/3) in Gram-positive, Gram-negative and fungal infections, respectively. Resistance analysis included 127 bacterial isolates from nine predominant taxa. Penicillin G resistance in Staphylococcus aureus and oxacillin resistance in coagulase-negative staphylococci were both 80.0%. Streptococcus pyogenes showed resistance to erythromycin and clindamycin in 75.0% and 62.5% of isolates, respectively. Among Escherichia coli isolates, ESBL positivity and resistance to levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin each occurred in 66.7%. Cefepime resistance was detected in 5.88% of Vibrio vulnificus isolates. In the jointly fitted ridge model, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, shock within 24h, coagulation measures, bilirubin, creatine kinase, potassium and lactate showed positive associations with mortality, whereas white blood cell count, albumin, CRP and PaCO2 showed inverse associations.
CONCLUSIONS: This long-term NSTI cohort showed Gram-negative predominance and species-specific heterogeneity in antimicrobial resistance. The ridge-penalized multivariable analysis characterized associations of microbiological categories and clinical indicators with 90-day mortality. These findings support locally tailored empirical therapy and the assessment of mortality risk.

Title: Final 5-Year Results of Abluminal Groove-Filled Biodegradable-Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stent Versus Durable-Polymer Everolimus-Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM.
AIMS: In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5-year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus-eluting stent (EES).
METHODS: TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non-stratified outcomes in DM versus non-DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia-driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis.
RESULTS: Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non-DM patients, TLF (p < 0.001), cardiac death (p < 0.001), TVMI (p = 0.002), ischemia-driven TLR (p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis (p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM.
CONCLUSION: This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.

Title: Heart Failure Outcomes in Primary Care: The Role of Primary Care Practice Assistants (VERAH) in German General Practice.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Germany's GP-centred care (GPCC) model aims to strengthen coordinated primary care and incorporates delegated case management delivered by Primary Care Practice Assistants (VERAH). While previous studies have demonstrated beneficial effects for patients with heart failure, the additional long-term impact of multidisciplinary primary care incorporating VERAH support compared with GPCC alone remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using German statutory health insurance claims data from 2011 to 2022. Patients with heart failure were identified using validated ICD-10 codes from inpatient and outpatient care records and assigned to three groups: usual care, GPCC and GP-centred care with extended multidisciplinary team involvement (GPCC-Plus). GPCC-Plus was defined as a study-specific category based on predefined VERAH-related service codes and lump-sum payments documented in AOK Baden-Württemberg claims data. Outcomes included all-cause hospitalisation, ambulatory care-sensitive condition (ACSC) hospitalisations and all-cause mortality. Multivariable regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic factors, comorbidities and healthcare utilisation, with time-varying covariates included where applicable. Direct comparisons between GPCC and GPCC-Plus were performed, and longitudinal trends were assessed over the 12-year observation period.
RESULTS: Both GPCC models were associated with reduced hospitalisations compared with usual care, with consistently stronger effects observed in GPCC-Plus practices involving multidisciplinary team care including Primary Care Practice Assistants (VERAH). GPCC-Plus demonstrated the lowest odds of all-cause hospitalisation and mortality across the study period. ACSC hospitalisations showed modest declines in both GPCC groups. Longitudinal analyses indicated sustained benefits over time, with more pronounced and consistent improvements in the GPCC-Plus group.
CONCLUSIONS: A coordinated, integrated, multidisciplinary primary care programme including delegated case management by Primary Care Practice Assistants (VERAH) is associated with sustained long-term reductions in hospitalisations and mortality among patients with heart failure over 12 years. These findings suggest that integrating structured nonphysician workforce roles may enhance the effectiveness of GPCC beyond GP coordination alone.
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT: Structured delegated case management and multidisciplinary teamwork can support continuity of care for patients with heart failure. Clear roles and communication pathways facilitate the integration of nursing and practice-based care into GPCC.

Title: EUS-PPG Measured Distal to the Thrombus: A Reliable Way to Detect the Pressure Gradient in Patients With Cirrhosis and Portal Vein Thrombosis.
Journal: Digestive endoscopy : official journal of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In patients with portal vein thrombosis (PVT), hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) does not accurately reflect portal pressure. This study aimed to evaluate the application of endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided portal pressure gradient (PPG) in cirrhotic patients with PVT.
METHODS: In patients with cirrhosis who had gastroesophageal varices (GEV) and PVT were included. The PPG proximal to the PVT (Pro-PVT PPG), PPG distal to the PVT (Dis-PVT PPG), and gastric variceal pressure gradient (GVPG) were measured by puncturing the target vessels under the guidance of EUS. The pressure gradients measured using different methods were compared and correlated with clinical characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 51 patients with GEV and PVT were included in the final analysis. There was a substantial agreement between Dis-PVT PPG and GVPG, with an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of 0.693 (0.514-0.813). Dis-PVT PPG and GVPG were significantly higher in the patients with bleeding history than in those without (17.0 mmHg vs. 11.3 mmHg, and 18.0 mmHg vs. 7.0 mmHg, p < 0.01 for both). In addition, patients with a Dis-PVT PPG ≥ 12 mmHg had a higher incidence of red sign (odds ratio [OR] = 5.6, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.6-20.2) and bleeding history (OR = 7.0, 95% CI = 2.0-26.4).
CONCLUSIONS: Dis-PVT PPG may be a preferred index that reflects the status of portal hypertension in cirrhotic patients with PVT and is associated with a bleeding history of GEV.

Title: Senescence Biomarkers Predict Physical Function and Clinical Outcomes After Heart Failure Hospitalization: Insights From REHAB-HF.
Journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is the most common cause of hospitalization in older adults. Cellular senescence, a hallmark of aging biology, has been implicated in heart failure pathophysiology and functional decline via the pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). We evaluated the association between SASP and physical function in older adults hospitalized for ADHF.
METHODS: REHAB-HF was a trial of older adults hospitalized for ADHF randomized to a novel physical rehabilitation intervention or attention control. We measured a panel of 18-SASP analytes at in-hospital baseline and at 3-month follow-up. Outcomes included short physical performance battery (SPPB) and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD). Statistical analysis included principal component analysis (PCA) of log- and z-transformed SASP values. Associations were evaluated with multivariable regression models adjusted for age, sex, and intervention arm.
RESULTS: Samples were available for 226 (65%) of the REHAB-HF participants with mean age (SD) 72.3 (8), 53% female, 52% HFpEF, and 53% assigned to rehab intervention. Principal Component 1 (PC1) reflected a coordinated signal across biomarkers of inflammation and immune signaling. PC1 was associated with poorer function at baseline [(SPPB -0.46 [-0.77, -0.14]; p = 0.004 and 6MWD -19.7 meters [-32.7, -6.7]; p = 0.003)]. Increasing SASP over time was associated with clinically significant reduced physical function improvement (ΔSPPB -1.80 [-2.58, -1.03]; p < 0.001 and Δ6MWD -49.7 meters [-77.2, -22.1]; p = 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Higher SASP levels were associated with poorer physical function recovery in older patients hospitalized for ADHF. These findings suggest that inflammatory SASP biomarkers may improve risk stratification and potentially guide therapeutic strategies.
REHAB-HF TRIAL IS REGISTERED AT CLINICALTRIALS.GOV CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY: NCT02196038.

Title: Ventilation strategies in reconstructive surgery of the tracheal bifurcation and bronchi: a 40-year retrospective institutional experience of 1,345 procedures.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes of differentiated intraoperative ventilation strategies tailored to the level and complexity of reconstructive surgery on the tracheal bifurcation and bronchi.
METHODS: A retrospective descriptive institutional study of 1,345 consecutive reconstructive procedures performed between 1986 and 2025 across four specialized thoracic centers by a single surgical team was conducted. Surgeries were categorized into five procedural groups: circumferential carinal resection (n = 142), partial carinal resection (n = 5), bronchial sleeve resection (n = 231), pneumonectomy with stump-less carinal closure (n = 815), and bronchopleural/tracheopleural fistula repair (n = 152). Intraoperative airway management included selective one-lung volume-controlled ventilation (OLV), catheter-based high-frequency jet ventilation (HFJV), and combined/apnoeic techniques.
RESULTS: No intraoperative deaths occurred, and no complications were directly attributable to ventilation failure. Five transient intraoperative anesthetic incidents occurred in patients with severe cardiopulmonary comorbidities: arterial hypotension (n = 1), supraventricular arrhythmias (n = 2), and asystole/cardiac arrest (n = 2), all successfully resolved. Major postoperative complications occurred in 109 patients (8.1%); 18 patients (1.3%) had complications potentially related to airway management (atelectasis, n = 4; pneumonia, n = 6; acute respiratory distress syndrome, n = 8). Overall 30-day mortality was 0.9% (13/1,345). Mortality was 0% in isolated bronchial resections (0/231), 2.1% after circumferential carinal resection (3/142), 1.3% in post-pneumonectomy fistula repairs (2/152), and 0.98% in stump-less carinal closures (8/815).
CONCLUSIONS: A procedure-tailored ventilation strategy provides safe and reliable intraoperative gas exchange. For carinal reconstructions, catheter-based HFJV is technically advantageous by avoiding bulky tubes in the operative field. For isolated bronchial sleeve resections, conventional selective OLV is sufficient. Managing post-pneumonectomy fistulas requires adaptable maneuvers to maintain gas exchange during induction and airway transection.

Title: Rethinking the role of sex and body size in mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Female sex and smaller body size have been associated with increased mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting. Whether these factors represent independent determinants or markers of correlated vulnerability remains uncertain.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-centre cohort study of adults undergoing non-emergent isolated coronary artery bypass grafting at Amsterdam UMC between January 2000 and April 2021. We examined whether body surface area explained the association between sex and all-cause mortality within one year by sequentially adding body surface area and other clinical covariates to Cox proportional hazards regression models.
RESULTS: Among 6,411 patients, 1,261 (20%) were female, and 192 patients (3.0%) died within one year. Female patients and patients with lower body surface area were older and had lower haemoglobin levels. Crude 1-year mortality was numerically higher in female patients than male patients (3.4% vs 2.9%) and in lower versus higher body surface area patients (3.6% versus 2.4%). After adjustment for age, estimated glomerular filtration rate and haemoglobin level, female sex and increasing body surface area were associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Crude one-year mortality was higher in female patients and in patients with lower body surface area. After adjustment, female sex and increasing body surface area were both associated with a lower mortality hazard, suggesting that the crude sex difference partly reflects differences in body size and clinical risk profile.

Title: Incidence and Risk Factors for Early Major Neurologic Complications in Lung Transplantation: From Restrictive Cardiopulmonary Bypass to ECMO by Criteria.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative hemodynamic instability and hypoxemia may contribute to early major neurologic complications (EMNC) following lung transplantation. Mechanical circulatory support can mitigate cerebral hypoperfusion, but cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is an independent risk factor for EMNC. This study examines the incidence of EMNC transitioning from a restrictive CPB strategy to criteria-based use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO-BC).
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study on 389 lung transplant recipients comparing patients managed with restrictive CPB (PRE-ECMO, 2012-2017, n = 288) to those managed with criteria-based ECMO (ECMO-BC, 2022-2024, n = 101). The incidence of EMNC was compared between groups.
RESULTS: EMNC occurred in 29 of 280 patients in the PRE-ECMO group and in 5 of 101 patients in the ECMO-BC group (10% versus 5%; P = 0.152), with 78 versus 8 total events, corresponding to an incidence rate ratio of 3.5 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.7-7.4, P < 0.001). Ischemic stroke was significantly less frequent in the ECMO-BC group (2% versus 9%; P = 0.022). Intraoperative mechanical circulatory support was used in 20% of PRE-ECMO and 43% of ECMO-BC cases (P < 0.001). Patients in the ECMO-BC group were older, had more cardiopulmonary comorbidities, greater intraoperative blood loss (2489 versus 1861 cc; P < 0.001), and more severe primary graft dysfunction at 24 and 72 h (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Transition to ECMO-BC was associated with lower EMNC events and fewer ischemic strokes, but increased intraoperative blood loss and worse early graft function, generating hypotheses for prospective studies that define optimal ECMO indications in lung transplantation.

Title: PCSK9-Targeting Therapies and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria.
RESULTS: Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent.
CONCLUSION: PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

Title: Pulsed Field Versus Contact Force Radiofrequency Ablation in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) remains a challenging arrhythmia to manage, and catheter ablation is a cornerstone therapy. Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) has recently emerged as a novel non-thermal alternative to Contact Force Radiofrequency (CF-RF) ablation. This meta-analysis compares the efficacy, safety, and procedural efficiency of PFA versus CF-RF in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using randomized controlled trials and cohort studies identified from MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases. Primary outcomes included 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia (AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia), procedure duration, fluoroscopy time, and major complications. Subgroup analyses were performed based on PFA device type (Farapulse vs. HT-9000Pro) and patient characteristics, including left atrial size and AF duration.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies met inclusion criteria. PFA was associated with significantly higher 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia compared with CF-RF (OR = 1.36, 95% CI 1.26-1.47, p < 0.001). Procedure time was markedly shorter with PFA (MD = -40.5 minutes, p < 0.001), while fluoroscopy time also showed a significant reduction (MD = -1.8 minutes, p = 0.001). Major complications were significantly lower with PFA (1.2% vs. 2.8%; OR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.35-0.57, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In persistent AF, PFA, demonstrates superior efficacy, safety, and procedural efficiency compared with CF-RFA, supporting its role as a potential first-line ablation strategy. Larger multicenter trials with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm durability and device-specific outcomes.

Title: Cardiometabolic and Nutritional Parameters in Patients with Primary Sjögren Syndrome.
Journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology
Abstract: Primary Sjögren syndrome (pSS) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease of the exocrine glands that may contribute to altered nutritional status. The aim of this study was to investigate the association between pSS and various nutritional and cardiometabolic parameters. This retrospective, cross-sectional study included 91 patients with pSS and 100 healthy controls. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed, including serum levels of albumin, glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), lipids, 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], and other biomarkers. Principal component analysis was applied to reduce the number of variables and identify key factors associated with pSS. Body mass index (BMI) and serum concentrations of albumin, glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol were significantly lower in patients with pSS than in controls (p=0.001, p<0.001, p=0.013, p=0.035, p=0.010, and p=0.001, respectively). Serum 25(OH)D levels were significantly higher in the pSS group compared with controls (p<0.001). Multivariable binary logistic regression analysis showed that BMI and 25(OH)D levels were independently associated with pSS (p=0.013 and p<0.001, respectively). Of the five factors extracted by factor analysis, three were significantly associated with pSS. The factor including CRP, HbA1c, and BMI and the factor including albumin and LDL cholesterol were negatively associated with pSS, whereas the factor comprising 25(OH)D and vitamin B12 was positively associated with pSS. Lower BMI and higher serum 25(OH)D levels were independently associated with pSS. Combined factors related to inflammation, glycemic status, lipid metabolism, and nutritional markers showed distinct associations with pSS, highlighting the importance of nutritional status screening in these patients.

Title: Remnant cholesterol-incorporating dual-axis lipid risk stratification using apolipoprotein B and the LDL-C to total cholesterol ratio: a prospective cohort study from the UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherogenic lipid-related risk may not be fully characterized by a single lipid measure. A dual-axis framework combining apolipoprotein B (ApoB), a measure of atherogenic particle number, with the LDL-C to total cholesterol ratio (LDL-C/TC), a derived measure of cholesterol partitioning, has been proposed to characterize lipid-related risk heterogeneity. The position of remnant cholesterol (RC) within this framework remains uncertain.
METHODS: We analyzed 288,257 UK Biobank participants free of cardiovascular disease and lipid-lowering therapy. Participants were classified using dual-axis framework. Associations with incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) were assessed using Cox models. RC was evaluated in combination with these axes across strata, including SCORE2-defined low-to-intermediate risk populations.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.9 years, the dual-axis framework differentiated ASCVD risk, with the dual-elevated phenotype (ApoB ≥ 90 mg/dL and LDL-C/TC ≥ 0.60) showing the highest risk (adjusted hazard ratio 1.23; 95% CI, 1.17-1.29). RC did not modify associations across dual-axis categories (P for interaction = 0.44), and higher RC levels were associated with attenuation of risk gradients across categories. In low-to-intermediate SCORE2 risk individuals, increasing numbers of elevated markers (ApoB, LDL-C/TC ratio, and RC) were associated with stepwise increases in risk, with absolute risk differences reaching 1.49% at 10 years for individuals with all three markers elevated versus those with none elevated. ApoB and the LDL-C/TC ratio produced small C-index increases (ΔC, 0.0013 and 0.0012), whereas RC produced no further improvement (ΔC, - 0.0001; P = 0.364).
CONCLUSIONS: RC did not materially modify associations across ApoB-LDL-C/TC phenotypes but identified absolute-risk heterogeneity within ApoB strata. Co-occurring marker elevations characterized higher-risk lipid phenotypes, although gains in discrimination were small and require external validation.

Title: Cumulative non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol exposure and residual cardiovascular mortality risk in patients with peripheral artery disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with peripheral artery disease (PAD) face substantial residual cardiovascular risk despite lipid-lowering therapy. Non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C) has been recognized as a more comprehensive marker of cardiovascular risk than low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), but its prognostic value in PAD and the relevance of cumulative exposure remain unclear. This study investigated whether early cumulative non-HDL-C exposure is associated with cardiovascular death (CV death) in PAD and whether the same association is observed among individuals whose LDL-C is already well controlled.
METHODS: A territory-wide PAD cohort in Hong Kong was analyzed. Early cumulative non-HDL-C and LDL-C exposures were defined as the lipid burden during the first 2 years after PAD diagnosis and were estimated using spline models. In the overall cohort, Fine-Gray competing-risk models were applied to assess the associations between tertiles of cumulative non-HDL-C exposure and CV death, with non-cardiovascular mortality treated as a competing event. Discordance analyses compared CV death risk across nine strata defined by cross-classified tertiles of cumulative LDL-C and non-HDL-C, with the low-LDL-C/low-non-HDL-C stratum as the reference. In the well-controlled LDL-C subgroup, the same competing risk framework was used to assess the residual risk of CV death across cumulative non-HDL-C categories.
RESULTS: Among 3,847 patients, 637 CV deaths occurred during a mean follow-up of 7.30 ± 3.92 years. Higher cumulative non-HDL-C exposure was associated with a higher risk of CV death (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.11-1.65; P = 0.002). Notably, patients with high non-HDL-C despite low LDL-C showed higher CV death risk (SHR, 2.00; 95% CI, 1.12-3.57; P = 0.018). In the 516 individuals with well-controlled LDL-C, higher cumulative exposure of non-HDL-C remained significantly related to CV death risk (SHR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.39-5.16; P = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher early cumulative non-HDL-C exposure was associated with a higher risk of CV death in PAD, including individuals who had attained the LDL-C target. Incorporating non-HDL-C into routine lipid follow-up may help identify residual cardiovascular risk, improve risk stratification, and support secondary prevention in patients with PAD, thereby addressing the long-term cardiovascular burden in this population.

Title: A multifunctional biomimetic nanoplatform targeting mitochondrial dynamics and oxidative stress for heart failure therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) presents a significant global health challenge, caused by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation, all of which impair cardiac function. This investigation introduces a new nanoplatform, PCM-refined M2 macrophage membrane-coated CeO2 nanozyme loaded with PGAM5 siRNA (P-MM@Ps-CeO2), that can target these interconnected disease pathways.
RESULTS: Mechanistically, silencing PGAM5 with this nanoplatform precludes the dephosphorylation of Drp1 at Ser637, thereby lessening excessive mitochondrial fission. Yet, it restores the DDX17- BCL6 control mechanism to decrease Drp1 levels, ultimately maintaining mitochondrial balance. CeO2 nanozymes break down reactive oxygen species (ROS), Attenuating cellular oxidative imbalance, while M2 macrophage membranes improve anti-inflammatory targeting to inflamed heart tissue, with PCM ensuring delivery precisely to the heart. In vitro, P-MM@Ps-CeO2 re-established baseline 90% of the viability in lipopolysaccharide- worsened HL-1 cardiomyocytes, attenuated ROS by 70%, and lowered Pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α) by up to 67%. It also preserved mitochondrial integrity, increased ATP production, and lowered apoptosis by 70%. In vivo, in a doxorubicin-induced HF mouse model, the nanoplatform improved ejection fraction to 65% and fractional shortening to 35%, reduced myocardial fibrosis by 30% and apoptosis by 70%, and increased cardiac accumulation by 2.5 times.
CONCLUSIONS: These outcomes indicate that P-MM@Ps-CeO₂ transcends conventional HF interventions, which typically fail to address mitochondrial abnormalities. The nanoplatform showed excellent biocompatibility, with minimal hemolytic activity and no detectable organ toxicity, supporting its potential for clinical use. By simultaneously targeting mitochondrial turnover, reactive oxygen species (ROS) stress, and inflammation, P-MM@Ps-CeO2 yields an advantageous pioneering treatment modality, HF, highly capable of improving analysis outcomes for the worldwide HF cohort.

Title: Implementing high intensity home-based rehabilitation for patients following stroke: a mixed methods study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Facility-based rehabilitation following stroke is costly and yields inconsistent outcomes. A high intensity home-based rehabilitation (HIHR) model may improve value and support patient-centered care. Studies are needed to assess contextual factors influencing adoption of HIHR models. The purpose of this study was to examine how clinical adoption of HIHR influenced its reach, maintenance, and fidelity, as well as therapists' perceptions of its acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility.
METHODS: HIHR was implemented as a standard-of-care pathway for patients with stroke at one academic hospital and its integrated home health agency. Data were examined for its first two years of implementation guided by the RE-AIM QuEST mixed methods approach. Quantitative data included retrospective clinical data for patients who met HIHR eligibility criteria at hospital discharge (used to measure reach, maintenance, and fidelity) and clinicians' ratings on the Acceptability of Intervention, Intervention Appropriateness, and Feasibility of Intervention Measures. Qualitative data were collected in three focus groups with medical, rehabilitation, and case management clinicians who were potential adopters of HIHR. These qualitative data were analyzed for adoption, fidelity, acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. We used a triangulation mixed methods analytic approach, collecting quantitative and qualitative data concurrently, and integrating the data at the interpretation phase.
RESULTS: Clinicians rated acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility of HIHR highly, with mean (SD) scores of 4.35 (0.64), 4.24 (0.56), and 4.00 (0.58), out of 5, respectively. HIHR's reach was 15.0% (49 of 327 eligible patients discharged to HIHR). Maintenance (reach over time) diminished in year 2 compared to year 1 (8.8% vs. 19.4%). Fidelity was poor (only 1 of 49 [2.0%] patients received all HIHR services). Four barriers related to adoption emerged to explain the quantitative findings: clinician education, in-hospital communication, patient eligibility, and service shortfalls.
CONCLUSIONS: While the HIHR model implemented in one health system was viewed as acceptable, appropriate, and feasible by clinicians, several barriers limited its adoption, undermining reach, maintenance, and fidelity. Key challenges included inconsistent education and in-hospital communication, overly restrictive eligibility criteria, and service delivery gaps. The findings offer valuable insight into how clinical contextual factors influence HIHR adoption, which can inform the model's evolution as it is scaled.

Title: The prescription profiles of Chinese patent medicine in Internet hospitals in China: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chinese patent medicine (CPM) is widely used in China's rapidly expanding Internet hospital system, yet its prescribing profiles in this setting remain uncharacterized.
METHODS: Prescription data were collected from 87 enterprise-led Internet hospitals between January 1, 2018, and March 31, 2021. Visits involving at least one prescribed CPM were included. Descriptive analyses characterized the top 20 most frequently prescribed CPMs overall, with stratification by gender and age groups. The top three CPMs for diseases with over 20,000 visits were identified, and the results were visualized using a sunburst chart.
RESULTS: Among 2,065,486 eligible visits, the respiratory diseases category was the most prevalent (26.29%), with acute upper respiratory tract infection (n = 319,772) as the top diagnosis, commonly treated with CPMs like Niuhuang Jiedu Tablet. Genitourinary diseases (23.43%) were also prominent, with Honghe Fujie Cleansing Lotion being the most prescribed CPM overall (3.77%), accounting for 15.2% of prescriptions for adult females. For chronic disease management, digestive (19.12%) and circulatory system (13.14%) diseases were common. Elderly patients (≥ 60 years) frequently received CPMs for cardiovascular conditions (18.9%, e.g., Wenxin Granule, Suxiao Jiuxin Pill). Age stratification showed pediatric patients (< 18 years) were primarily prescribed CPMs for respiratory infections (48.0%), while patients in the 18-44 years age group commonly used CPMs for gynecological and dermatological conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: Among visits that included at least one CPM prescription, CPM was extensively prescribed via Internet hospitals in China for acute respiratory infections, urogenital, and chronic conditions, with notable coverage also observed among pediatric and elderly populations. Our findings suggest that this model may enable contactless care, provide discreet consultation channels for urogenital conditions, and facilitate medication access for patients with stable chronic diseases.

Title: Lentinan alleviates autoimmune myocarditis via inhibiting CD40 expression and GSDMD-mediated cardiomyocyte pyroptosis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanism and regulatory effect by which lentinan (LNT) alleviates autoimmune myocarditis via suppressing CD40 expression and GSDMD-mediated cardiomyocyte pyroptosis.
METHODS: Fifty 8-week-old male BALB/c mice were randomly divided into 5 groups (n = 10): Control, experimental autoimmune myocarditis (EAM) model, EAM + low-dose LNT (5 mg/kg), EAM + high-dose LNT (20 mg/kg), and EAM + dexamethasone (DEX, 2.5 mg/kg). EAM was established by immunization with cardiac myosin on D0 and D7 using ‌α-MyHC. LNT and DEX were administered intraperitoneally from D8. Additionally, 40 CD40fl/flLysMCre+/- (CD40mye-KO) mice and 16 CD40WT littermates were used. CD40mye-KO mice were divided into 4 groups (n = 10): CD40mye-KO, CD40mye-KO EAM model, CD40mye-KO EAM model + High-dose LNT (20 mg/kg), CD40mye-KO EAM model + DEX (2.5 mg/kg). CD40WT mice divided into 2 groups (n = 10): CD40WT, CD40WT EAM model. The HW/BW ratio was measured, and LVEF, LVFS, LVESD, and LVEDD were assessed by echocardiography. Cardiac histopathological changes were evaluated using inflammatory scoring after H&E staining. Bone marrow-derived macrophages were pre-treated with 0.1 µg/mL LPS to induce cell damage, followed by treatment with 5 µg/mL LNT, 20 µg/mL LNT, 100 nM DEX, or 100 ng/mL CD40 activator (anti-mouse CD40 antibody fgk4.5/fgk45) for 24 h. Primary mouse cardiomyocytes were isolated from hearts, and supernatants from pyroptotic macrophages were used to treat cardiomyocytes for 24 h. Cell viability was measured using CCK-8 assay. LDH content in culture supernatant was detected to evaluate cell membrane damage. Serum and cell culture supernatants were analyzed for cTnT, CK-MB, IL-1β and IL-18 using ELISA. Protein expression of CD40, TRAF6, NF-κB p65, p-NF-κB p65, cleaved caspase-1, NLRP3, and GSDMD-N was assessed by WB. The spatial distribution of CD40 and GSDMD-N fluorescent signals and the expression of GSDMD-N in cardiomyocytes were analyzed by IF.
RESULTS: LNT significantly improved LVEF and LVFS while reducing LVESD and LVEDD in EAM mice. Both LNT doses reduced serum levels of cTnT, CK-MB, IL-1β and IL-18, with low-dose LNT exerting beneficial effects less pronounced than high-dose LNT and DEX. H&E staining demonstrated increased cardiac inflammation and immune cell infiltration in EAM mice, which was significantly alleviated by LNT and DEX treatment. WB analysis showed that LNT significantly downregulated protein expression of CD40, TRAF6, p-NF-κB p65/NF-κB p65, cleaved caspase-1, NLRP3, and GSDMD-N in myocardial tissues of EAM mice. IF staining showed that the spatial overlap and distribution of CD40 and GSDMD-N fluorescent signals was significantly reduced after LNT treatment. Reversal experiments demonstrated that LNT counteracted the effects of CD40 activator on cardiomyocyte pyroptosis. Experiments in CD40mye-KO mice confirmed that CD40 is a critical target for LNT-mediated cardiac protection. In vitro studies demonstrated that LNT regulates CD40 expression and downstream GSDMD-related pyroptosis signaling in macrophages, while a CD40 activator could partially counteract its protective effect against cardiomyocyte pyroptosis, further highlighting the central role of CD40 in LNT-regulated pyroptosis.
CONCLUSION: Lentinan alleviates autoimmune myocarditis, and its protective effect is closely related to the inhibition of CD40 expression and the subsequent suppression of GSDMD-mediated cardiomyocyte pyroptosis.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Association between PCSK9 and post-stroke cognitive impairment: a retrospective cohort study and predictive models establishment based on machine learning.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) has gained increasing attention due to its involvement in lipid metabolism and neuroinflammation regulation. High PCSK9 levels are linked to an elevated risk of cerebrovascular events and small vessel diseases. However, systematic research exploring the association between PCSK9 and post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains scarce. This study investigated the link between PCSK9 and PSCI.
METHODS: A cohort of 354 patients with PSCI was enrolled in this investigation. The link between PCSK9 and PSCI occurrence was evaluated through multivariate logistic regression analysis. Restricted cubic spline methodology was employed to examine the non-linear association between PCSK9 levels and PSCI risk. Prediction models were developed using machine learning algorithms.
RESULTS: After adjusting for confounders, elevated PCSK9 levels were identified as an independent predictor of PSCI. Including PCSK9 in prediction models alongside traditional risk factors significantly improved the accuracy of PSCI predictions. Feature importance rankings from the SVM model highlighted the significance of PCSK9, with the SVM-based model yielding the highest performance (AUC = 0.895).
CONCLUSION: PCSK9 blood levels in individuals after acute ischemic stroke function as an independent predictor for PSCI and improve the precision of machine learning-based predictive models.

Title: Predictive value of C-reactive protein for progression from prehypertension to hypertension: a prospective cohort study based on the CHARLS database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The key to preventing and treating hypertension is predicting the progression of prehypertension and implementing preventive and control measures. Whether C-reactive protein (CRP) can predict the progression from prehypertension to hypertension remains to be confirmed.
METHODS: Based on prospective data from CHARLS from 2011 to 2015, 1,236 middle-aged and elderly individuals with prehypertension were enrolled and stratified into three groups according to their baseline CRP levels using predefined CRP categories. We employed interval-censored Cox models and restricted cubic spline analysis to assess the association between CRP level and hypertension risk, as well as model improvement metrics after incorporating CRP.
RESULTS: During the 4-year follow-up period, 269 participants developed incident hypertension, accounting for 21.8% of the study population. In the adjusted interval-censored Cox model, higher log-transformed CRP was associated with a higher risk of hypertension (HR = 1.34; 95% CI: 1.07-1.68). Because the restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a nonlinear pattern (P for nonlinearity = 0.040), this estimate should be interpreted as an overall summary rather than a constant risk increase across the full CRP range. In the analysis based on clinical CRP categories, participants with CRP > 3 mg/L had a higher risk than those with CRP < 1 mg/L (HR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.15-2.26). Subgroup analyses showed no significant interactions across age, sex, BMI, systolic blood pressure, or remnant cholesterol groups. After adding CRP to the conventional risk model, the C-index increased from 0.626 to 0.634.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated CRP levels were associated with the progression from prehypertension to hypertension among middle-aged and elderly adults. Adding CRP to conventional risk factors provided modest additional predictive information. CRP may serve as a supplementary indicator for identifying individuals who need closer follow-up, but it should not be used alone for risk assessment.

Title: Association between the uric acid to high‑density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio and H‑type hypertension: a cross‑sectional study in Chinese adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The uric acid to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) is a novel inflammatory and metabolic biomarker. Studies have confirmed that it is closely associated with the onset and progression of various metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between UHR and H-type hypertension (HTH) remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the association between the UHR and HTH.
METHODS: This study was conducted as a cross-sectional analysis. The study population consisted of adults aged over 30 years from six randomly selected regions in Hunan Province, China, among whom 1,835 eligible participants were included in the analysis.Data were collected through questionnaire surveys, physical examinations, and laboratory tests. Logistic regression model was used to analyze the association between the UHR index and HTH. RCS were used to assess the potential nonlinear relationship between the two variables. Subgroup analyses were conducted to explore the interaction effects of different subgroups on the association between UHR and HTH. ROC curves were applied to evaluate the discriminatory ability of UHR for HTH.
RESULTS: The analysis included 1835 participants, of whom 1026 had HTH, and 1,069 participants (58.3%) were female. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that, each one‑standard‑deviation increase in the UHR index was associated with a 40% increase in the risk of HTH (OR = 1.41, 95%CI: 1.24-1.60, P < 0.001). RCS analysis indicated a nonlinear dose-response relationship between the UHR index and the risk of HTH (P for nonlinear = 0.045). We further identified an inflection point of the threshold effect of UHR, above and below which the prevalence of HTH exhibited distinct increasing trends.Subgroup analysis showed that the association between UHR and HTH was more pronounced in females and the Han Chinese population. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that UHR had moderate discriminatory ability for HTH, with AUC of 0.618 (95%CI: 0.592-0.644, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: UHR is independently associated with HTH and exhibits a positive nonlinear association with the condition, with an inflection point at 0.09.

Title: The prognostic value of inflammatory prognostic index in patients with chronic total occlusion undergoing successful PCI: a single-center prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests that inflammatory and nutritional status play key roles in the prognosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVD). The Inflammatory Prognostic Index (IPI), integrating both inflammatory and nutritional metrics, has been linked to multiple subtypes of coronary artery disease (CAD). However, the association between IPI and long-term prognosis in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) after successful PCI remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the prognostic role of IPI in patients with CTO who underwent successful PCI.
METHODS: A total of 525 patients with CTO who underwent successful PCI were enrolled in this study. Participants were stratified into a MACE group and a control group, as well as three subgroups (T1, T2, T3) by IPI tertiles. Baseline characteristics were compared, and Cox regression analysis were performed. The receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) was used to determine the predictive value of IPI for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
RESULTS: A total of 76 patients with 82 MACE were recorded during the follow-up. Patients with MACE exhibited significantly higher C-reactive protein (CRP) and IPI levels (p < 0.05). Patients in T3 (high IPI group) had higher white blood cell count, neutrophil count, CRP, creatinine, and IPI, while they had lower lymphocyte count, albumin (ALB), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (p < 0.05). In addition, patients in the highest IPI tertile exhibited a higher risk of target vessel revascularization (TVR) and composite MACE (p < 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that IPI was an independent predictor of MACE in patients with CTO who underwent successful PCI (p < 0.05). Moreover, patients in the highest IPI tertile had a 2.484-fold higher risk of MACE (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: IPI may serve as a supplementary prognostic tool due to its simplicity and low cost. However, given its modest predictive performance, it should be combined with existing risk models to improve predictive value and facilitate clinical decision-making.

Title: Hotspot mutations and tumour spectrum in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome: genotype-phenotype analysis of a large Chinese cohort.
Journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem tumour syndrome caused by germline VHL mutations. The traditional classification of VHL syndrome, which is largely based on pheochromocytoma penetrance, is insufficient for individualised surveillance and management. This study aimed to improve mutation-specific risk stratification and define genotype-phenotype correlations of recurrent hotspot mutations in a large Chinese cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 674 patients with VHL disease from 283 unrelated families. Four recurrent hotspot mutation subtypes were analysed: codon 65 missense mutations, exon 2 deletion, c.481C > T, and c.224_226del. Kaplan-Meier analysis and univariate and multivariate Cox regression models were used to assess age-related tumour risks and survival outcomes.
RESULTS: Codon 65 missense mutations were associated with a lower risk of retinal angioma and pheochromocytoma, indicating a relatively mild phenotype. Exon 2 deletion was characterised by a higher prevalence, earlier onset, and increased age-related risk of retinal angioma and worse renal cell carcinoma (RCC)-specific survival. Increased prevalences and age-related risks of central nervous system hemangioblastoma (CHB), RCC, and pancreatic cysts or tumours were associated with c.481C > T mutations. The c.224_226del subtype showed a distinct CHB-predominant phenotype, with higher CHB incidence, earlier onset, lower pancreatic lesion risk, and higher overall mortality.
CONCLUSION: Recurrent hotspot VHL mutation subtypes were associated with distinct clinical phenotypes and prognostic patterns. Mutation subtype-based classification (covering 19.6% of patients with VHL syndrome) may provide more precise guidance for surveillance, clinical decision-making, and genetic counselling than traditional broad classification models.

Title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Hypokalemia in Patients With Multiple Myeloma Undergoing Autologous Peripheral Blood Stem Cell Collection.
Abstract: Autologous peripheral blood stem cell (APBSC) collection is a standard procedure for patients with multiple myeloma (MM) undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Hypokalemia is a frequently observed but underappreciated complication during apheresis, with limited evidence on its incidence and risk factors. To determine the incidence of hypokalemia following APBSC collection in MM patients and to identify independent risk factors. This retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 109 MM patients who underwent their first APBSC collection at Union Hospital, Fujian Medical University, between January 2018 and December 2022. All patients received prophylactic potassium supplementation during collection. Patients were stratified by serum potassium measured 2 h postprocedure: hypokalemia (< 3.5 mmol/L; n = 59) and normokalemia (3.5-5.0 mmol/L; n = 50). Variables with p < 0.10 in univariate analysis were entered into multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination. Post-APBSC serum potassium was significantly lower than baseline (3.46 ± 0.43 vs. 3.85 ± 0.22 mmol/L; p < 0.001). Hypokalemia developed in 59 patients (54.1%): 48 mild (81.4%), nine moderate (15.3%), and two severe (3.4%). Three independent predictors were identified by multivariable analysis: higher body mass index (BMI) (OR 1.217; 95% CI 1.030-1.439; p = 0.021), higher hematocrit (OR 1.119; 95% CI 1.032-1.213; p = 0.006), and lower preprocedure serum potassium (OR 1.43 per 0.1 mmol/L decrease; 95% CI 1.15-1.78; p = 0.001). The model demonstrated adequate calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.635) and explained 24.6% of variance (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.246). Hypokalemia affects over half of MM patients undergoing APBSC collection. Preprocedure risk factors (BMI, hematocrit, baseline potassium) may help identify high-risk patients for whom intensified electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation strategies are warranted.

Title: The Effect of Perioperative Video Interventions on Postoperative Pain Control: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative pain is a major cause of suffering and is linked to serious complications, including delayed wound healing, increased cardiovascular risk, delayed rehabilitation, and chronic postsurgical pain. Modifiable psychological factors influence pain outcomes, and preliminary evidence suggests video interventions can reduce preoperative anxiety and improve patient satisfaction. We hypothesized that video interventions could improve postoperative pain control. Therefore, the aim of the current systematic review was to summarize all previous research and investigate the effects of perioperative video interventions on pain levels and/or analgesic consumption.
METHODS: The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024596389) and followed the PRISMA Guidelines.
