We searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Academic Search, and the Cochrane Central register of controlled trials from inception to October 2025 for randomized controlled trials in adult surgical patients. Trials assessing any perioperative video interventions reporting on postoperative pain intensity and/or analgesic consumption were included. Data was extracted independently by two authors, and data synthesis was qualitative due to significant heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).
RESULTS: Forty-four trials were included. Of the 42 trials assessing pain, 11 (26%) reported significantly lower pain in the intervention group. Of the 19 trials measuring analgesic consumption, eight (42%) reported significantly lower consumption in the intervention group. Only two trials demonstrated a benefit for both co-primary outcomes. Significant improvements in secondary outcomes, including anxiety, physical function, and satisfaction, were reported in 26 trials. Most trials were judged as having a high risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: The current systematic review suggests that perioperative video interventions may improve acute postoperative pain control, although effects are inconsistent across trials. Future research should focus on identifying patient and intervention characteristics that predict efficacy to guide clinical implementation.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This trustworthy systematic review presents an overview of current research findings for application of perioperative video-based treatments as part of managing postoperative pain. While this approach shows promise, more definitive evidence may be needed to justify more widespread implementation.

Title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included.
EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores.
RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

Title: Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
Journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs.
RESULTS: Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%).
CONCLUSION: Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

Title: Prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction measured by cardiac magnetic resonance in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an important role in both the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), as it provides information on cardiac function, structure, and tissue characterization. Moreover, it is the gold standard for right ventricular (RV) assessment. However, evidence regarding the prognostic value of RV systolic dysfunction in this population remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic value of right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) measured by CMR in patients with ATTR-CM. MéTODOS: This was a single-center, observational, retrospective cohort study. We included patients from an institutional ATTR-CM registry who underwent CMR within 6 months of diagnosis between 2011 and 2025. Patients with other types of amyloidosis were excluded. Clinical, biochemical, echocardiographic, and CMR variables were collected. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves were constructed according to the presence or absence of RV dysfunction on CMR, defined as RVEF <50%. Univariate and multivariable Cox regression models were performed to identify predictors of the primary endpoint. TAPSE was not included in the multivariable models to avoid collinearity.
RESULTADOS: A total of 100 patients were included, with a median age of 79 years [IQR 73-84]; 84% were men. Median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% [IQR 42-62], and median RVEF was 48% [IQR 38-57]. Patients with lower RVEF had higher all-cause mortality (log-rank p = 0.008, Figure). In the multivariable model including age, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP, RVEF was independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98; p = 0.002, Table).
CONCLUSIONES: In our cohort of patients with ATTR-CM, RVEF assessed by CMR was independently associated with all-cause mortality. These findings suggest that RV assessment may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.

Title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist and SGLT2 inhibitor use with outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes undergoing pacemaker implantation.
Abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure (HF) remains prevalent following pacemaker implantation, with patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) representing a particularly vulnerable population. Whether use of contemporary glucose-lowering therapies is associated with subsequent clinical outcomes has not been well characterized. We investigated the associations of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) therapy, individually and in combination, with post-implantation clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Electronic health records identified 3,609 patients with T2DM who underwent pacemaker implantation from 2016-2023. Based on peri-implantation medication dispensing, patients were classified as SGLT2i (n = 438), GLP-1RA (n = 193), combined therapy (n = 231), or neither (n = 2,747). Following a 90-day landmark period, three-year risks of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization were evaluated using multinomial propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting and Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Overall, 463 patients (12.8%) died. All treatment groups showed lower all-cause mortality than controls, with the greatest reduction observed in the combination therapy group (HR 0.41; 95% CI, 0.22-0.77; P = 0.006). HF hospitalization occurred in 295 patients (8.2%), significantly reduced in combination therapy (HR 0.35; 95% CI, 0.17-0.74; P = 0.006), with trends toward benefit in monotherapy groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with T2DM undergoing permanent pacemaker implantation, SGLT2i and GLP-1RA therapy were associated with lower all-cause mortality, while combined therapy was additionally associated with fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support further evaluation of cardiometabolic therapies after pacemaker implantation in randomized trials.

Title: Positive-call rates and agreement of two artificial intelligence electrocardiogram models for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and cardiac amyloidosis in competitive athletes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) models detect hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and cardiac amyloidosis in clinical populations; whether two independently developed models agree in athletes is unknown.
METHODS: We applied two independently developed AI-ECG models to the screening electrocardiograms (ECGs) of 716 competitive athletes aged 40 years or younger, screened by ECG alone and presumed free of structural heart disease. The RST algorithms return per-condition probabilities dichotomized at published operating points; the AZ model, a four-class ECG-image classifier, assigns one class per ECG. The primary outcome was each model's positive-call rate (proportion of athletes flagged) for HCM and cardiac amyloidosis; agreement was described with Cohen kappa and positive agreement. Because the cohort was presumed disease-free, sensitivity was not assessed.
RESULTS: Median age was 22.1 years; 86.0% were men. The RST algorithms flagged HCM in 13 athletes (1.8%; 95% CI, 1.0-3.1) and cardiac amyloidosis in 2 (0.3%; 0.0-1.0); the AZ model flagged HCM in 29 (4.1%; 2.7-5.8) and cardiac amyloidosis in 18 (2.5%; 1.5-3.9). Of 60 athletes flagged by either model, 2 were flagged by both (kappa 0.07 and - 0.01; positive agreement 0.10 and 0.00); continuous outputs were uncorrelated for HCM (Spearman rho 0.00). Of 59 flagged athletes with a stored cardiologist interpretation under the international criteria, 39 had a normal ECG. All 18 AZ amyloidosis calls occurred in men.
CONCLUSIONS: The two models flagged different athletes at different rates. Without verified cases these rates describe referral burden, not accuracy; whether either detects disease requires validation against verified diagnoses.

Title: Updated Staging System to Define Cardiogenic Shock Severity A Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) severity is defined by the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions stages and modifications from the Cardiogenic Shock Working Group (CSWG). Lactate thresholds, treatment intensity, and cardiac arrest modifiers remain incompletely defined. We aimed to refine the 2022 CSWG staging criteria using contemporary data.
METHODS: Patients with CS from heart failure (HF-CS) or myocardial infarction (MI-CS) enrolled in the multicenter CSWG registry (2021-2025) were analyzed. Associations between systolic blood pressure (SBP), lactate, treatment intensity, and in-hospital mortality, which is considered a surrogate for CS severity, were examined. External application of the updated system was performed in an independent US health system.
RESULTS: Among 11,640 patients (60.5% HF-CS, 26.1% MI-CS), SBP and lactate demonstrated graded relationships with mortality across thresholds (SBP <60, 60-<90, ≥90 mm Hg; lactate 0-2, >2-5, >5-10, >10 mmol/L). Mortality increased incrementally with treatment intensity. The 2026 staging system, incorporating these thresholds and the number of vasoactive drugs and temporary mechanical circulatory support devices (stage C: 1-2, D: 3-4, E: ≥5), demonstrated progressive mortality across stages. Compared with previous CSWG staging, 28.4% of patients classified as stage D and 56.4% of patients classified as stage E were reclassified, with lower mortality among those reclassified to less-severe stages. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest functioned best as a stage modifier, whereas in-hospital cardiac arrest corresponded to stage E. Findings were consistent across HF-CS and MI-CS. The 2026 CS staging system was evaluated in 1,417,637 patients in a geographically and structurally diverse health care system and demonstrated a graded, monotonic increase in mortality across stages A-E.
CONCLUSIONS: Using fewer clinical variables, the 2026 CSWG criteria provide a simple framework for CS severity staging that is applicable among patients with HF-CS and MI-CS and can be standardized across clinical trials and health care settings.

Title: Potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: Rationale and design of the STARS DAPT randomized pilot trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 12 months is the current standard of care for patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Recent evidence indicates that potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) after 1 to 3 months of DAPT following drug-eluting-stent (DES) implantation reduces major bleeding events without increasing the risk of major ischemic outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome. However, the optimal timing of aspirin discontinuation in STEMI patients treated with P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT remains uncertain.
DESIGN: STARS DAPT is an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, open-label, precision-based, randomized controlled pilot trial with a blinded outcome assessment. Patients with STEMI who underwent successful primary PCI of the culprit lesion with a newer-generation polymer-free DES will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT (with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge) for 12 months vs. standard DAPT for 12 months. The primary efficacy endpoint is the rate of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as the composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial re-infarction, non-fatal stroke, urgent target vessel revascularization, or definite/probable stent thrombosis, at 12 months. The primary safety endpoint is Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) class 3 or 5 major bleeding at 12 months. The study is designed to provide estimates of treatment effects and their precision to inform the design of a subsequent larger randomized trial.
ENROLMENT STATUS: The trial aims to recruit a total of 350 patients. The first patient was enrolled on December 1, 2025.
CONCLUSION: STARS DAPT is a randomized pilot study assessing the safety and efficacy of a potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT strategy, with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge, following primary PCI with a newer-generation polymer-free DES in patients with STEMI. The findings will inform future large-scale trial design and may help optimize antiplatelet strategies and guide clinical decision-making after primary PCI.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: Identifier, NCT05785897.
FUNDING SOURCE: Unrestricted research grant from Concept Medical (Tampa, FL, USA) to Geneva University Hospitals, Switzerland.

Title: Systematic Development of a Training Intervention to Support General Practitioners' Very Brief Physical Activity Advice for Patients With Coronary Heart Disease: Formative Intervention Development Study From the OptiCor Project.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite strong evidence supporting the benefits of regular physical activity (PA) for managing coronary heart disease (CHD), PA advice remains infrequent in general practice. Barriers include the limited familiarity of general practitioners (GPs) with current PA guidelines and their application to CHD patients, their insufficient skills for delivering very brief advice, and time constraints. To our knowledge, no structured, theory-informed training has been reported in Germany to support GPs in delivering very brief PA advice in routine CHD care.
OBJECTIVE: This intervention development study aimed to systematically develop and specify a training intervention to strengthen GPs' delivery of very brief PA advice to patients with CHD in routine primary care.
METHODS: Guided by the behavior change wheel (BCW), we conducted a formative intervention development study informed by preceding empirical studies from the OptiCor project, including a cross-sectional survey, interviews, and focus groups with GPs and patients, alongside guideline recommendations and behavior change theory. These sources identified needs, barriers, and preferences related to PA advice. Findings were mapped onto COM-B (capability, opportunity, motivation-behavior) components to identify determinants of GP behavior and were specified using the theoretical domains framework (TDF). The BCW intervention function matrix informed discussions of suitable intervention functions and training components. Intervention components were specified using the behavior change technique (BCT) taxonomy, and GPs were involved throughout to ensure relevance, feasibility, and acceptability.
RESULTS: The development process resulted in a fully specified intervention: a structured, 3.5-hour, small-group training for GPs focusing on the very brief 3As method (ask/assess, advise, and assist). The training comprises theoretical input on PA and CHD, guided self-reflection and group discussions, moderated role-plays with simulated patients, experiential learning using PA stimuli, practical consultation materials, and short on-demand good practice videos. Outputs included a refined behavioral specification of GP-delivered PA advice, a COM-B/TDF-based behavioral diagnosis, BCT-specified training components, minor refinements after a preimplementation training rehearsal, and fidelity procedures to support standardized delivery.
CONCLUSIONS: This study resulted in a fully specified GP training intervention to strengthen very brief PA advice in routine CHD care. By integrating empirical findings, guideline recommendations, behavior change theory, and GP and patient input, the intervention targets the determinants of GP advising behavior and is described transparently to support evaluation and replication. Following this development work, the training and evaluation procedures were examined in a pragmatic pilot cluster randomized controlled trial (cRCT), which has been reported separately, before proceeding to an ongoing full-scale pragmatic cRCT evaluating the effects on GP behavior.

Title: Validation of a patient-specific virtual reality preoperative clip planning environment for microsurgical clipping of unruptured anterior circulation aneurysms: a blinded comparison between operative selection and postoperative imaging.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Virtual reality (VR)-based platforms for aneurysm clipping are increasingly used for preoperative visualization, but objective validation against the final clip construct and postoperative imaging remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the implementation of a patient-specific VR preoperative clip planning environment by comparing blinded simulated clip selections with operative clip choice and postoperative day 1 CTA in patients undergoing microsurgical clipping of unruptured anterior circulation aneurysms.
METHODS: The authors conducted a single-center retrospective validation study that included 10 patients who underwent elective clipping for an unruptured anterior circulation aneurysm between 2021 and 2025. Three vascular neurosurgeons independently performed 1 anonymized VR planning session per case at least 6 months postoperatively and were blinded to clinical data, operative documentation, clip records, and postoperative imaging. Life-size Yasargil clip models mirrored the institutional tray. Raters selected primary clip type, primary blade length, single- versus multiple-clip strategy, and anticipated dog-ear remnant; planning time was recorded. The operative reference standard was derived from operative documentation and clip records. Aneurysm occlusion, remnant status, and clip pose validation were based on postoperative day 1 CTA. The primary endpoint was a 4-point VR-Clip Concordance Index (VCCI).
RESULTS: Ten patients (6 female, median age 63.5 years [IQR 60.0-69.0 years]) who underwent clipping for an unruptured anterior circulation aneurysm and 30 corresponding VR simulations were included in this analysis. The mean VCCI was 2.00 ± 1.11 on a 4-point scale, and 10 of 30 simulations (33.3%) achieved VCCI ≥ 3 using exact primary blade-length agreement. Of 30 simulations, agreement was 17 (56.7%) for primary clip type, 21 (70.0%) for single- versus multiple-clip strategy, 18 (60.0%) for remnant expectation, and 4 (13.3%) for exact primary blade length. Blade-length agreement increased to 5 of 30 simulations (16.7%) with a ±0.5-mm tolerance and to 10 of 30 simulations (33.3%) with an exploratory ±1.0-mm tolerance. The mean VR planning time was 2.23 ± 1.57 minutes. The median positional deviation between simulated and postoperative clip poses was 2.41 mm (IQR 1.67-3.70 mm); rotational deviation was larger and more variable (median 44.42°, IQR 31.13°-64.95°). On postoperative day 1 CTA, 9 of 10 patients had aneurysms were that were completely occluded and 1 had a small dog-ear remnant.
CONCLUSIONS: This patient-specific VR environment for clip planning was feasible and fast; however, it was only partially concordant with the operative clip construct. There was stronger agreement for broad clip strategy than exact blade length, recognition of nonstraight clip geometries, multiclip reconstruction, or remnant prediction, which were identified as priority engineering targets before prospective clinical implementation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Validation Study

Title: Sequential arterial feeder targeting with microscope-based augmented reality and multimodal navigation for brain arteriovenous malformation resection: an integrated operative workflow in 158 cases.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early proximal arterial control is an established principle of brain arteriovenous malformation (bAVM) microsurgery but remains difficult to execute when feeding arteries are deep, obscured, or not apparent at the cortical surface. Herein, the authors describe the longitudinal clinical implementation of a workflow using multimodal navigation and microscope-based augmented reality (AR) to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection in bAVM resections.
METHODS: Case-specific multimodal datasets were assembled according to clinical relevance and availability from CTA, high-resolution structural MRI with thin-slice T2-weighted imaging, MRA, and 3D rotational DSA studies and were fused within standard clinical neuronavigation platforms. All angiographically identifiable arterial feeders were segmented along their surgically relevant courses, prioritized as operative targets, and incorporated into exposure and corridor planning. Targets were displayed intraoperatively using the available navigation configuration, including microscope-based AR as the technology evolved. Functional MRI (fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) were coregistered selectively to provide cortical and tractographic context. Consecutive navigation-assisted bAVM resections performed by a single neurosurgeon from 2013 to 2025 were analyzed. Outcomes included angiographic obliteration, perioperative morbidity, mortality, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score change relative to baseline.
RESULTS: Of 192 bAVM resections performed during the study period, 158 consecutive navigation-assisted resections comprised the analytical cohort and included Spetzler-Martin (SM) grades I-V. Complete obliteration on initial angiography after microsurgery was observed in 97.5% of cases (154/158). At a median follow-up of 15 months, 93.0% of patients were functionally independent (mRS score 0-2). An increase in the mRS score relative to baseline occurred in 18.4% of patients, most commonly reflecting minor, nondisabling deficits with preserved independence. Loss of independence attributable to surgery occurred in 3.1% of patients, and the mortality rate was 1.3%.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal navigation with microscope-based AR was implemented longitudinally to identify and target arterial feeders before substantial nidal dissection, with selective integration of fMRI and DTI providing cortical and tractographic context for lesions near eloquent anatomy. Across SM grade I-V bAVMs, the workflow was feasible and was associated with high rates of angiographic obliteration and functional independence. By translating preoperative angioarchitecture into a planned sequence of discrete intraoperative arterial targets within their structural and functional context, the featured workflow provides a structured framework for operative planning, execution, and teaching in feeder-directed bAVM microsurgery.

Title: Electrophysiological Characteristics of Fasciculoventricular Pathways.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fasciculoventricular (FV) accessory pathways are rare variants of pre-excitation, connecting the His-Purkinje system to ventricular myocardium. Though typically benign and not participating in tachycardia circuits, they can mimic septal accessory pathways on ECG, creating diagnostic challenges.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence, ECG characteristics, electrophysiological features, and atypical properties of FV pathways in patients undergoing EP study at a tertiary center.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed all patients undergoing EP study from 2010 to 2024. FV pathways were diagnosed by subtle pre-excitation, short and fixed HV interval, and lack of change in pre-excitation during atrial pacing.
RESULTS: Of 2836 patients undergoing EP study for supraventricular tachycardia, 668 had accessory pathways; 15 (2.2%) had FV pathways. The mean age was 26.5 years, with 53% male. Four patients (27%) were asymptomatic. Coexisting arrhythmias included AV accessory pathways (40%), AVNRT (20%), and atrial arrhythmias (15%). All patients showed subtle pre-excitation (mean PR 101 ± 18.7 ms, QRS 105 ± 14.4 ms). EP study revealed a short fixed HV interval (mean 17.6 ± 5.85 ms) with persistent pre-excitation during atrial pacing. Atypical features included intermittent FV conduction (13%), gap phenomenon (7%), and retrograde conduction (20%). FV pathways were not involved in any tachycardia circuit.
CONCLUSION: FV pathways are uncommon (2.2% of accessory pathways) with characteristic ECG and EP findings. The presence of gap phenomenon, intermittent antegrade conduction, and retrograde conduction suggests that a subset of these pathways may possess functional, discrete myocardial properties rather than passive insulation defects; however, further structural and electroanatomical studies are needed to confirm this hypothesis.

Title: Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Coronary Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
Serum sclerostin in relation to insulin resistance and epicardial fat thickness in obese women.
Journal: Hormone molecular biology and clinical investigation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Visceral obesity is closely linked to insulin resistance and cardiometabolic risk. Epicardial adipose tissue, commonly assessed by epicardial fat thickness (EFT), is a clinically relevant fat depot associated with early cardiac remodelling. Sclerostin, a bone-derived protein, may play a role in crosstalk between the skeleton and adipose tissue. However, its relationship with insulin resistance and cardiac visceral fat remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate serum sclerostin levels and their association with insulin resistance and EFT in obese women.
METHODS: This case-control study included 90 women (55 obese and 35 age-matched controls). Participants underwent anthropometric and metabolic assessment, including serum sclerostin measurement. Insulin resistance was evaluated using HOMA-IR, and EFT was assessed by echocardiography. Correlation, ROC, and regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Serum sclerostin levels were significantly higher in obese women than in controls (p<0.001). Sclerostin was positively correlated with fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and EFT. Levels were higher in insulin-resistant obese participants than in metabolically healthier obese individuals. ROC analysis showed good discriminative ability for insulin resistance (AUC=0.89) and moderate accuracy for identifying increased EFT (AUC=0.80). In multivariate analysis, BMI, but not sclerostin, remained an independent predictor of increased EFT.
CONCLUSIONS: Serum sclerostin is elevated in obese women and is associated with insulin resistance and adverse metabolic profiles. Although not independently associated with epicardial fat thickness, it reflects metabolic dysfunction related to visceral adiposity and may serve as an indicator of metabolically unhealthy obesity within this cohort.

Title: The Steroid Symptom Questionnaire Multiple Myeloma (SSQ-MM): translation and cross-cultural adaptation into Danish and Norwegian and initial psychometric evaluation of the Norwegian version.
Journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The Steroid Symptom Questionnaire - Multiple Myeloma (SSQ-MM) was developed to assess patient-reported side effects of corticosteroid treatment in multiple myeloma (MM) patients. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the SSQ-MM into Danish and Norwegian, and to provide an initial evaluation of the psychometric properties of the Norwegian version.
METHODS: Translation and cultural adaptation followed ISPOR good practice guidelines, including forward-backward translation and cognitive debriefing interviews with patients and clinicians. Psychometric evaluation was conducted in newly diagnosed Norwegian MM patients receiving weekly dexamethasone. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha. Construct validity was explored through correlations with EORTC QLQ-C30 constructs and known-groups comparisons based on ECOG performance status. Responsiveness was evaluated across three time points.
RESULTS: The Danish and Norwegian translations were considered relevant and acceptable by patients and clinicians. The Norwegian version demonstrated acceptable internal consistency for the total score (α = 0.74) and psychological subscale (α = 0.81). Correlation patterns were generally consistent with predefined hypotheses and known-groups validity was supported by differences in symptom scores according to ECOG performance status. Responsiveness analyses demonstrated significant increases in the total score and several steroid-related symptoms during treatment, whereas fewer changes were observed following treatment discontinuation. Overall, symptom levels were lower than those reported in the original Australian validation study.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings from the Norwegian cohort provide preliminary evidence supporting the reliability, construct validity, known-groups validity, and responsiveness of the Norwegian SSQ-MM. Further studies in larger, diverse MM populations are needed to further evaluate its measurement properties.

Title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc).
METHODS: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

Title: Diagnostic Performance of Corrected Carotid Flow Time for Assessing Fluid Responsiveness in Patients With Septic or Hypovolemic Shock: A Prospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
Abstract: Background Predicting fluid responsiveness in patients with hemodynamic instability remains challenging. Corrected carotid flow time (CFTc) is a non-invasive bedside Doppler measure proposed to identify fluid responsiveness, but its reported performance is inconsistent. We evaluated baseline CFTc as a predictor of fluid responsiveness and assessed whether the post-bolus percentage change in CFTc corresponded with the echocardiographic change in stroke volume. Materials and methods This prospective diagnostic accuracy study included 80 adult patients presenting with new-onset shock of presumed septic and/or hypovolemic origin. All received a clinically indicated first bolus of 10 mL/kg Ringer's lactate. Stroke volume (SV) measured by transthoracic echocardiography and CFTc by carotid Doppler were obtained at baseline (T1) and 20 minutes after the bolus (T2). Responders were defined by a ≥15% rise in SV. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to assess the diagnostic performance of CFTc and its percentage change. Results An infective focus was identified in 61 patients (76.2%), with no source documented in 19 patients (23.8%). Thirty-two patients (40.0%) were responders. A baseline CFTc cut-off of ≤324.03 ms predicted responders with 71.9% sensitivity and 47.9% specificity (AUROC 0.563, 95% CI 0.435-0.691; p = 0.343). The percentage change in CFTc showed poor discrimination for fluid responsiveness (AUROC 0.568, 95% CI 0.436-0.700; p = 0.305) and corresponded weakly with the percentage change in SV (Spearman rho = 0.141; p = 0.213). Non-responders experienced recurrent hypotension more often and required earlier initiation of vasopressors. Conclusion In adults with new-onset shock, baseline CFTc did not usefully discriminate echocardiography-defined fluid responders, and the post-fluid change in CFTc showed weak correspondence with the change in stroke volume. CFTc should not be relied on alone to guide fluid resuscitation in this population.

Title: Clinical Symptom Burden and Its Association With Echocardiographic Parameters and Comorbidities in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which substantial symptoms may occur despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Echocardiographic abnormalities involving ventricular filling, left atrial remodeling, diastolic function, and pulmonary pressures may contribute to symptom burden. This study evaluated the association between clinical symptom severity, echocardiographic parameters, and comorbidities in patients with HFpEF.
STUDY: This retrospective observational cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Peripheral Hospital, Periyar Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, from March 2025 to March 2026. A total of 216 patients aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and LVEF ≥50% were included. Clinical symptom burden was assessed using New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and categorized as I-II or III-IV. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and echocardiographic parameters, including LVEF, left ventricular mass, left atrial volume index (LAVI), E/e' ratio, diastolic dysfunction grade, and estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with NYHA III-IV symptoms.
RESULTS: The mean age was 67.8 ± 10.4 years, and 53.7% were female. Hypertension was the most prevalent comorbidity (80.6%), while 76.9% had ≥2 major comorbidities. Fifty-five patients (25.5%) had NYHA III-IV symptoms. Compared with NYHA I-II, the severe symptom group had higher E/e' (17.4 ± 5.0 vs. 12.6 ± 4.0), LAVI (44.5 ± 12.1 vs. 34.2 ± 9.1 mL/m²), LV mass, and PASP (43.9 ± 12.4 vs. 36.8 ± 8.7 mmHg), with significantly more advanced diastolic dysfunction. On multivariable analysis, E/e' (adjusted OR 1.18), LAVI (adjusted OR 1.05), and PASP (adjusted OR 1.04) were independently associated with severe symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Symptom severity in HFpEF was associated more strongly with abnormal filling pressures, left atrial remodeling, and pulmonary hemodynamics than with preserved systolic function alone. E/e', LAVI, and PASP may provide useful complementary markers of symptomatic burden and support a multidimensional echocardiographic assessment of HFpEF.

Title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events.
RESULTS: For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.

Title: Circulating Biomarkers with Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Risk Assessment and Therapeutic Monitoring: Evidence, Limitations, and Translation.
Abstract: Circulating biomarkers, particularly cell-free DNA (cfDNA), are transforming contemporary medicine through their capacity to provide dynamic, minimally invasive assessments of disease dynamics. Their clinical utility has broadened substantially to include oncology, cardiovascular conditions, transplant monitoring, infectious diseases, and persistent inflammatory disorders. Nevertheless, the increasing complexity and volume of biomarker-related data pose substantial challenges, necessitating the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning methodologies for improved data interpretation, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. This review presents a thorough examination of recent progress in the integration of circulating biomarkers with AI within therapeutic contexts and clinical risk management. It outlines the translational trajectory from molecular signatures to precision medicine, addresses present constraints, and explores prospective developments. The objective of this review is to serve as a systematic resource for both clinical practice and research, thereby promoting the evolution of personalized medicine through innovative, biomarker-driven strategies supported by AI.

Title: Stage 1 Registered Report: sex differences in anticoagulation and stroke outcomes among patients with atrial fibrillation: a registry-based cohort study.
Abstract: Women with atrial fibrillation have a higher risk of ischaemic stroke and worse functional outcomes than men but may be less likely to receive adequate anticoagulation. Preliminary single-centre findings in patients treated with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion suggest that women may be under-anticoagulated prior to stroke onset. This Stage 1 Registered Report outlines a prespecified analysis plan to test sex-based differences in anticoagulation, stroke characteristics, treatment and outcomes in a prespecified confirmatory population and to explore whether similar patterns are observed at the national level. Using a retrospective cohort design, we will analyse local data from Stavanger University Hospital (2009-22) and national data from the Norwegian Stroke Registry. Confirmatory analyses will include patients with atrial fibrillation and large vessel occlusion treated with endovascular thrombectomy. Sex differences in anticoagulation, stroke severity, treatments and outcomes will be examined using chi-square tests and prespecified regression models; equivalence testing will be applied where appropriate. Exploratory analyses will assess age, comorbidity and healthcare delivery as potential mediators and moderators. No confirmatory analyses have been conducted.

Title: Clinical Evaluation of Patients With Premature Canities and Its Association With Metabolic Syndrome.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Premature canities (early hair graying) are no longer just a cosmetic concern; they are visible markers of systemic oxidative stress. The underlying depletion of follicular melanocytes mirrors the physiological aging associated with metabolic syndrome. Consequently, early graying can serve as a crucial preclinical warning sign for underlying cardiovascular risks, including central obesity, hypertension, and dyslipidemia.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the clinico-epidemiological profile of patients with premature canities and to assess the prevalence of metabolic syndrome in these individuals compared with healthy controls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An observational case-control study, conducted at a tertiary care center, included 240 age- and sex-matched participants (120 cases and 120 controls). After collecting comprehensive demographic data, subjects were divided into mild, moderate, or severe categories based on the extent of hair graying at presentation. Metabolic syndrome parameters were subsequently evaluated using the NCEP ATP III (National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III) criteria, which included waist circumference, blood pressure, fasting triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein, and fasting blood sugar.
RESULTS: The study identified a highly significant male predominance among the participants (n=85, 70.8%). The mean age of onset for premature graying was notably early, at 16.58 ± 4.20 years. A positive family history was reported by 38.3% (n=46) of the participants. Anthropometric and biochemical evaluations revealed that cases exhibited a significantly higher mean waist circumference compared with controls (84.44 cm vs. 81.75 cm; p=0.020) and a higher mean systolic blood pressure (123.63 mmHg vs. 119.35 mmHg; p=0.001). Furthermore, lipid profiles in cases demonstrated significantly lower protective HDL cholesterol (50.10 mg/dL vs. 53.34 mg/dL; p=0.045) and elevated triglycerides (115.98 mg/dL vs. 103.40 mg/dL; p=0.023) compared with controls.

Title: Management of bleeding and nonelective invasive procedures in patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs): a 5-year single-center observational study.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines exist for managing bleeding or nonelective invasive procedures in patients on direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), but their clinical impact remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the management of patients who had DOAC concentrations measured for bleeding or nonelective invasive procedures and to assess associations between guideline compliance, outcomes, and DOAC concentrations.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study (2014-2018) included adult patients receiving dabigatran etexilate, rivaroxaban, or apixaban who required hospital care for bleeding or nonelective invasive procedures and had DOAC concentrations measured at the time of the event. Compliance with French and European guidelines was assessed. Adverse outcomes-a composite of all-cause mortality, worsening or new bleeding, and thrombotic events-were recorded until discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 584 events (432 procedures and 152 bleeding episodes) in 547 patients were analyzed. Guideline compliance was 79% and showed no association with outcomes. Among 95 events treated with prothrombin complex concentrates, one thrombotic event occurred. DOAC concentrations were higher in the bleeding group than in the procedural group (122 [IQR, 57-219] vs 55 [IQR, 25-127] ng/mL), but bleeding severity was not associated with drug levels. In bleeding patients, rivaroxaban concentrations were higher in those with adverse outcomes compared with those without (243 [IQR, 74-367] vs 88 [IQR, 35-199] ng/mL).
CONCLUSION: In a large cohort of patients who had DOAC concentrations measured at the time of a bleeding or a nonelective invasive procedure, compliance with guidelines was high and not associated with outcomes. In bleeding patients, rivaroxaban concentrations were higher in those with vs without adverse events.

Title: Cutaneous Adverse Events With Semaglutide: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Semaglutide is widely used for metabolic disease, but cutaneous adverse events are inconsistently reported. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated randomized comparisons of semaglutide with placebo, usual care, or non-semaglutide active treatment. The protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261464289). PubMed, Europe PubMed Central, trial registers, sponsor reports, and regulatory sources were examined through September 9, 2026; source verification was completed on September 21, 2026. Meta-analysis required directly available, source-verified participant event counts and denominators in both groups. Reported alopecia or hair loss and source-defined participant-level injection-site reactions were analyzed separately using common-effect Mantel-Haenszel odds ratios (ORs) without continuity correction. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed for the primary syntheses. Thirty-one trials contributed verified outcome data. Twenty trials formed the primary placebo/common-control evidence set, of which 19 contributed relative-effect estimates and one reported zero injection-site reactions in both groups. Eleven additional trials provided active-comparator or design-specific evidence. Across nine comparisons, alopecia or hair loss was reported in 191/11,564 semaglutide recipients and 36/9,799 comparators (OR: 2.92, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.99-4.27; p < 0.001; low-certainty evidence). The association persisted after exclusion of the largest cardiovascular outcomes trial with restricted ascertainment; random-effects analyses supported the primary interpretations. Eleven informative comparisons reported injection-site reactions in 156/5,066 semaglutide recipients and 114/3,483 comparators (OR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.67-1.11; p = 0.256; very-low-certainty evidence). Active comparators and design-specific results were described separately. Semaglutide may increase reports of alopecia or hair loss; its comparative effect on injection-site reactions remains uncertain. Available-count synthesis does not resolve selective non-reporting or incomplete event ascertainment. The findings do not establish a hair-loss mechanism or injection-site safety equivalence.

Title: Nurse-Led Longitudinal Screening and Care Transitions for Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A 12-Month Retrospective Longitudinal Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify longitudinal trajectories of post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and to examine baseline and time-varying psychological factors associated with subsequent symptom burden in a nurse-led follow-up cohort.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 278 ATAAD survivors discharged from Henan Provincial Chest Hospital between 1 August 2023 and 30 July 2024. Clinical and nurse-led follow-up records through 1 August 2025 were reviewed for assessments at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary trajectory analysis used PCL-5 scores from 1 to 12 months among participants with at least two valid assessments. One- through four-class latent class mixed models were compared according to convergence, Bayesian information criterion, classification quality, and minimum class size. Baseline correlates were examined with multinomial regression. Lagged models separated between-person means from within-person changes in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking; social support was examined across the 3-to-6-month interval.
RESULTS: A three-class solution was selected: low-decreasing (n=153, 55.0%), recovering (n=77, 27.7%), and persistent-high (n=48, 17.3%). Within-person increases in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking were associated with higher subsequent PCL-5 scores, whereas higher social support was associated with a lower subsequent score. Baseline associations were attenuated after multiplicity correction.
CONCLUSION: The model identified three PTSS trajectories during the first year after ATAAD discharge. Repeated nurse-led assessment may help identify survivors with a persistent symptom burden, and changes in illness threat, insomnia, repetitive negative thinking, and social support may inform the timing and focus of transitional care. The effectiveness of screening or targeted care was not tested.

Title: Improvement in mitral regurgitation after alcohol septal ablation in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The primary mechanism of mitral regurgitation (MR) in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral leaflets due to septal hypertrophy narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), influencing leaflet movement and closure. Among patients undergoing alcohol septal ablation (ASA), the impact on- and underlying mechanism of MR remains less studied. The aim was to determine the prevalence of MR and changes in MR severity after ASA and analyze echocardiographic (ECHO) parameters associated with MR changes.
METHODS: All patients who underwent ASA at Karolinska University Hospital in Sweden, 2009-2021 (follow-up until 2025), were included in this retrospective cohort study. ECHO parameters were collected before ASA, at 1-year follow-up and at the latest follow-up registered. To evaluate differences in continuous values, Kruskal-Wallis test was used, and for categorical values, Fischer's exact test was used.
RESULTS: 154 patients were included (mean follow-up 4.0 ± 3.9 years). 14% (n = 21) had at least moderate MR at baseline, of which 90% (n = 19) improved to mild MR or less. The patients with improved (n = 19, 12%) or unchanged (n = 128, 83%) grade of MR showed greater reduction of LVOT peak pressure gradients (improved MR: 137.5 to 4.8 mmHg, unchanged MR: 57.0 to 25.0 mmHg) between baseline and last follow-up, compared with patients with increased MR grade (n = 7, 4.5%, 57.0 to 51.0 mmHg, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with at least moderate MR before ASA, MR severity generally improved at follow-up, potentially due to septal reduction and LVOT enlargement, which may have reduced SAM.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Cumulative estimated glucose disposal rate and longitudinal eGDR patterns in relation to incident cardiovascular disease among middle-aged and older adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) is a surrogate measure of insulin sensitivity derived from routinely available clinical variables. However, whether repeated eGDR measurements provide additional information for cardiovascular risk assessment among individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains unclear. We examined the associations of cumulative eGDR and longitudinal eGDR patterns with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) and evaluated their incremental risk-discrimination value.
METHODS: Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we conducted a prospective cohort analysis with 2015 specified as the landmark. Participants were aged ≥ 45 years in 2011, met an operational TyG-WC-based definition of MASLD in 2011, had calculable eGDR in both 2011 and 2015, were alive and free of CVD at the 2015 landmark, and had valid post-2015 outcome and follow-up data. Cumulative eGDR was calculated from the 2011 and 2015 measurements and, because all participants shared the same four-year interval, was mathematically proportional to the mean of the two measurements; K-means clustering was used exploratorily to identify longitudinal eGDR patterns, operationally characterised as two-wave eGDR level-change patterns based on the two observed measurements. Participants were followed from 2015 to 2020, and incident CVD was defined as the first report of physician-diagnosed heart disease or stroke. Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines were used to estimate associations and dose-response relationships. Competing-risk, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses, including alternative handling of CVD event times, were performed to assess robustness. Incremental predictive performance was evaluated using conventional and internally validated discrimination measures, including paired out-of-bag C-index comparisons.
RESULTS: A total of 2,059 participants were included, of whom 457 developed incident CVD during follow-up. Each 1-SD lower cumulative eGDR was associated with a 39% higher risk of CVD after full adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 1.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.26-1.55). Compared with participants in the highest cumulative eGDR quartile (Q1), those in the lowest quartile (Q4) had an HR of 2.40 (95% CI 1.77-3.25; P for trend < 0.001). The dose-response relationship was approximately linear (P for non-linearity = 0.915). K-means clustering identified four exploratory longitudinal eGDR patterns based on the two observed measurements. Using the high eGDR-slight decline pattern as the reference, the moderate-low eGDR-slight rise, high eGDR-marked decline, and low eGDR-slight decline patterns were associated with HRs of 1.43 (95% CI 1.07-1.90), 1.64 (1.20-2.23), and 2.14 (1.67-2.74), respectively. Lower cumulative eGDR was also associated with higher risks of heart disease and stroke, and the main findings remained stable across multiple sensitivity analyses, including alternative handling of event times. Adding cumulative eGDR to the conventional risk-factor model increased the paired out-of-bag C-index by 0.033 (95% CI 0.009-0.056); however, when 2015 eGDR was already included, adding cumulative eGDR produced essentially no further improvement (ΔC-index - 0.001, 95% CI - 0.007 to 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: Among middle-aged and older Chinese adults meeting an operational TyG-WC-based MASLD definition, lower cumulative eGDR and longitudinal eGDR patterns characterised by low levels at both observed measurements or a marked decline between measurements were associated with a higher risk of incident CVD. Cumulative eGDR provided modest incremental discrimination beyond conventional risk factors but essentially no additional discrimination beyond the 2015 eGDR measurement, indicating substantial overlap with the most recent eGDR value.

Title: Associations Between Self-Reported Experiences of Racial Discrimination and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy among Black and White Women in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study.
Journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are major contributors to maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Perceived experiences of racial discrimination (EORD) have been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. This study investigates the association between EORD and incident HDP among Black and White women.
METHODS: The Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study is a prospective cohort of 5,115 Black and White adults aged 18 to 30 years at baseline (1985-1986), followed for over 30 years. EORD was analyzed as a continuous proportion, a three-category variable (no discrimination, overall proportion < 33%, and 33% or greater), and dichotomously (none vs. ever). HDP was self-reported in pregnancies lasting at least 23 weeks. Logistic regression assessed the association between EORD and HDP among 1,184 parous women, adjusting for age, race, education, income, cardiovascular risk factors, and parity.
RESULTS: At baseline, the mean age was 24.1 years; 48.1% were Black, 72.3% were nulliparous, and 19.7% had an income less than $16,000. Overall, 60.6% reported EORD (86.0% of Black and 37.1% of White women). Those reporting EORD were more likely to be Black, unmarried, have higher BMI, and have had one birth at baseline (p < 0.001). EORD was associated with increased odds of HDP (OR: 1.73 [1.20-2.48]) among both Black and White women. EORD < 33% (OR: 1.75 [1.20-2.55]) and 33% or greater (OR: 1.65 [1.04-2.64]) were significantly associated with HDP.
CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS: EORD, regardless of race, is significantly associated with increased odds of HDP. The disproportionate burden among Black women highlights the need for targeted interventions.

Title: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors and arterial stiffness in chronic kidney disease: results from the chronic renal insufficiency cohort.
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with accelerated arterial stiffness, which contributes to its high burden cardiovascular disease. There is conflicting evidence on whether renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs) prevent arterial stiffness. We investigated the association between RASIs versus non-RASI antihypertensive medications and yearly changes in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) - a measure of arterial stiffness -using a linear mixed-effects model among participants in the Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) Study. As a secondary analysis, we restricted the cohort to participants on one antihypertensive medication at baseline. Lastly, we used a linear mixed-effects model to evaluate the relationship between RASI use and systolic blood pressure over time. Of the 1 201 participants who met inclusion criteria, 982 were on RASI and 219 were on a non-RASI medication. Individuals on RASI had a non-significant increase in cfPWV (adjusted cfPWV 0.19 m/s per year, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.25) compared to non-RASI users (adjusted cfPWV 0.15 m/s per year, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.30; p = 0.61). In the monotherapy cohort (N = 283), there was no difference in adjusted yearly change in cfPWV between RASI (0.11 m/s per year, 95% CI 0.02 to 0.21) and non-RASI users (0.03 m/s per year, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.20; p = 0.41). In both cohorts, there was no significant difference in systolic blood pressure over time between RASI and non-RASI users. Future research to mitigate the accelerated large artery stiffness in patients with CKD should focus on targetable mechanisms beyond the renin-angiotensin system.

Title: Updates in cardiovascular CT imaging in 2025: A year in review.
Abstract: The year 2025 brought long-term outcome data supporting coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-guided management of stable chest pain, a proposed reframing of coronary artery disease around atherosclerosis rather than ischemia, and the first large-scale real-world evaluation of a national artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled CT-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) program. This review summarizes selected advances in cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) published in print or online during 2025. The studies span coronary artery disease outcomes and prevention, quantitative plaque analysis, photon-counting detector CT, coronary artery calcium scoring, pericoronary inflammation imaging, AI and machine learning, structural and congenital heart disease, and consensus and training documents. For each study we summarize the design, principal findings, limitations, and likely clinical implications, and we close with the barriers, including technical standardization, vendor-specific thresholds, equitable access, and the need for randomized outcome trials, that must be addressed before many of these advances can be implemented broadly.

Title: A Multidimensional Weight-Time-Frequency Score for Quantifying Intraoperative Hypotensive Burden During Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a multidimensional weight-time-frequency (WTF) score for quantifying cumulative intraoperative hypotensive burden during off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) and to evaluate its association with postoperative outcomes.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: A tertiary cardiac surgery center.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing OPCABG with continuous intraoperative arterial pressure monitoring.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A qualifying hypotensive episode was defined as mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg sustained for at least 1 minute. The WTF score integrated hypotension depth, duration, and frequency, and outcome-specific cohorts were used for 30-day all-cause mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF). Among 2,070 patients undergoing OPCABG, each 10-point increase in WTF was associated with higher adjusted odds of AF (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.155; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.001-1.333), AKI (adjusted OR, 1.216; 95% CI, 1.001-1.478), and 30-day all-cause mortality (adjusted OR, 2.346; 95% CI, 1.332-4.130). Restricted cubic spline analyses showed generally increasing adjusted odds across the WTF range without significant nonlinearity. In test-set analyses, adding WTF yielded significant integrated discrimination improvement for AKI and significant IDI and continuous net reclassification improvement for 30-day mortality, whereas incremental gains for AF were minimal. Mortality findings should be interpreted cautiously because only 31 deaths occurred. WTF met the prespecified noninferiority criterion in 14 of 15 comparisons with conventional MAP-based metrics, including all comparisons for AF and AKI.
CONCLUSION: The WTF score provides an interpretable cumulative measure of intraoperative hypotensive burden during OPCABG, shows adjusted associations with postoperative AF, AKI, and 30-day all-cause mortality and generally preserves discrimination comparable to conventional mean arterial pressure‒based metrics.

Title: Cerebral Embolization During Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation is Linked to Early Right Ventricular Failure.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of air introduction into the left ventricular (LV) cavity and right coronary artery (RCA) during durable left ventricular assist device (dLVAD) implantation on the incidence of early right heart failure (RHF) within 7 postoperative days, specifically to investigate whether the quantity of air emboli, as detected by transcranial Doppler (TCD) monitoring, correlates with an increased risk of early RHF.
DESIGN: This single-center retrospective analysis involved intraoperative TCD monitoring of the middle cerebral arteries. Between January 2021 and April 2024, 62 cases of dLVAD implantations (all of them HeartMate3) were performed, 59 of which were eligible for inclusion in the statistical analysis. TCD recorded high-intensity transient signals (HITS), indicative of emboli. Based on the number of intraoperative HITS, 2 categories were created: minimal-mild (<2,500 HITS; group A) and moderate-severe (>2,500 HITS; group B).
SETTING: A single-center retrospective chart review.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients who received dLVAD implantation under TCD surveillance.
INTERVENTIONS: A retrospective chart review of patients receiving standard of care; no study interventions were performed.
MEASUREMENTS & MAIN RESULTS: In group A, 9 out of 40 patients (22.5%) experienced early postoperative RHF. In contrast, 14 out of 19 patients (73.7%) in Group B developed early RHF, indicating a strong statistical significance (P < .001). A statistically significant difference was also demonstrated in postoperative 30-day all-cause mortality; there were no deaths (0% mortality) in group A, whereas in group B, 4 out of 19 patients (21.1%) died within 30 days (p = 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: The presence of >2,500 intraoperative HITS was correlated with a higher incidence of complications in the postoperative period. TCD monitoring during dLVAD implantation may be a potential tool to monitor for RV dysfunction.

Title: Social and Environmental Exposures and the Developing Gut of Newborns With Congenital Heart Disease.
Journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysbiotic gut microbiomes are linked to morbidity, mortality, and poor outcomes, so it is critical to understand their influencing factors.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of nosocomial and socioecological factors on the gut microbiome in newborns with congenital heart disease (CHD).
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort of newborns with CHD matched to healthy newborns by age, sex, and race and ethnicity. Data on feeding type and routes and disease-related factors were collected from electronic medical records. Stool samples were collected at 3 perioperative time points. Gut microbiome diversity and abundance were analyzed using QIIME 2.
RESULTS: Newborns with CHD (n = 41) showed higher alpha diversity (P = .007) and dissimilar beta diversity (P = .001) versus controls (n = 40). Beta diversity was dissimilar between those receiving human milk versus formula (P = .05), between those receiving fortified versus nonfortified human milk (P = .04), and between those receiving naso-orogastric tube feeds versus other routes (P = .02). Newborns with CHD fed only human milk had higher relative abundance of Haemophilus (P = .04), those with longer duration of aortic cross-clamping had lower relative abundance of Streptococcus (P = .10), and those of higher socioeconomic deprivation had higher relative abundance of Enterococcus (P = .03).
CONCLUSIONS: Feeding tubes, formula exposure, aortic cross-clamp, and socioeconomic status were associated with altered gut microbiome diversity. Further study is needed to determine the causal relationships leading to gut microbial dysbiosis in newborns in the cardiac intensive care unit.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Versus Standard-Dose Alteplase to Treat High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.
Journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal dosing of alteplase in patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism is widely debated.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate outcomes in patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism who received alteplase at a low dose or a standard dose.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort analysis of 65 patients who received alteplase for high-risk pulmonary embolism at a large academic medical center between June 1, 2011, and August 31, 2022. Patients were placed in 2 cohorts according to initial dose: low-dose alteplase (50 mg) and standard-dose alteplase (100 mg). The primary outcome was sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours of the start of alteplase infusion. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, hospital and intensive care unit length of stay, and major bleeding.
RESULTS: The primary outcome of sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours did not differ significantly between the 2 cohorts (achieved in 32% of patients in the low-dose group and 38% in the standard-dose group; P = .65). In-hospital mortality did not differ significantly between groups (48% in the low-dose group vs 45% in the standard-dose group; P = .81). Patients in the low-dose group had fewer days of mechanical ventilation than patients in the standard-dose group (1.5 vs 6 days; P = .03) and a smaller percentage had major bleeding (12% vs 25%; P = .34).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism, sustained hemodynamic stability within 24 hours did not differ significantly between low-dose and standard-dose alteplase treatment strategies. Low-dose alteplase may be an appropriate alternative dosing strategy for patients with high-risk pulmonary embolism.

Title: Imaging-Based Assessment of Plaque Modification Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Femoropopliteal Disease: A Prospective Single-Centre Observational Study.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is designed to treat calcified peripheral arteries with steno-occlusive disease; however, its effect on plaque morphology remains incompletely understood in vivo. This study evaluated plaque modification and luminal changes following IVL in femoropopliteal disease using computed tomography angiography (CTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS).
METHODS: This was a prospective single centre observational study. Consecutive patients with symptomatic femoropopliteal disease undergoing IVL between December 2024 and October 2025 underwent pre- and post-procedural (within five days) CTA with quantitative plaque analysis. IVUS was performed before and immediately after IVL, prior to drug coated balloon angioplasty (applied in all patients) or stenting (used only as bailout). The primary endpoint was change in calcified plaque volume on CTA. Secondary endpoints included luminal gain, haemodynamic changes, procedural success, and 6 month clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Thirty nine patients were included; median age was 71 years. Calcified plaque volume showed a modest reduction (median proportional reduction 12.2%, p < .001) on post-procedural CTA. IVL resulted in luminal expansion, with IVUS measured lumen area increasing from 5.78 to 16.11 mm2 (p < .001) immediately after IVL alone and CTA intraluminal volume increasing 52.7% (median). Haemodynamic improvement was observed (ankle brachial index: 0.80 to 1.00 (median); toe brachial index: 0.40 to 0.62 (median); p <.001) between baseline and 30 days. Intra-procedural dissections were detected in 18% of cases on IVUS; only two lesions (5%) were flow limiting and required stenting. At 30 days, no mortality or target lesion revascularisations were observed, while restenosis at 6 months occurred in 5% of cases. Chronic total occlusion was associated with residual stenosis in multivariable analysis (OR 6.2, 95% CI 1.11 - 34.48, p = .038).
CONCLUSIONS: IVL was associated with modest apparent plaque modification and significant luminal gain in calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Combined CTA and IVUS imaging suggest luminal expansion is primarily driven by plaque fracture, altered vessel compliance, and remodelling rather than debulking.

Title: Carotid and femoral plaque burden in patients with early coronary artery disease events: Prevalence, extent and relationship to risk phenotypes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early coronary artery disease events (eCAD) are increasing, occasionally occurring in individuals with minimal atherosclerosis, suggesting heterogeneous underlying mechanisms. We report, for the first time, carotid and femoral plaque burden in eCAD patients, relate it to underlying phenotypes, and compare it with the PESA reference cohort to explore preventive implications.
METHODS: eCAD patients (<60 years) were consecutively and prospectively enrolled at a tertiary hospital. Conventional and non-conventional cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and blood biomarkers were assessed, and global atherosclerosis plaque burden (GPB) was quantified as total carotid and femoral plaque volume by 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound (3DVUS).
RESULTS: Among 231 eCAD patients (53 ± 5 years old; 14% women; 23% with a prior event; 52% presented with STEMI) conventional CVRF were frequent but prevalence of non-conventional CVRF was high (28% elevated lipoprotein a, 25% family history of premature CVD, 25% hyperuricemia, and 14% hyperhomocysteinemia). Underlying GPB was high (268.7 mm3 [IQR75.2-509.9]), being higher in the femoral than the carotid territory (200.6 mm3 [IQR51.7-420.7] vs 35.2 mm3 [IQR7.9-96.2], p < 0.001), and increased with age. Compared with age-matched asymptomatic individuals (PESA study), eCAD patients had markedly higher GPB (284.1 mm3 [IQR110-546.8] vs 50.8 mm3 [18.7-121.5]). However, GPB in eCAD patients varied widely. Severe GBP (percentile≥75th) identified a subgroup with predominantly conventional CVRF and prior CVD, with marginal presence of non-conventional factors, compared with those with no-or-mild GPB (percentile≤25th).
CONCLUSION: Carotid and femoral PB by 3DVUS identifies distinct pathophysiological phenotypes in eCAD, underscoring the value of atherosclerosis assessment for individualized management and prevention.

Title: Title: Impact of Coexisting Gout on Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Data from the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative (OBRI).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with coexisting gout in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and evaluate whether concomitant gout is associated with worse RA disease activity.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of RA patients enrolled in the Ontario Best Practices Research Initiative, a multicentre real-world cohort across Ontario, Canada. Coexisting gout was defined by patient- or physician-reported diagnosis or xanthine oxidase inhibitor use. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with coexisting gout and the impact of gout on oral glucocorticoid (GC) use. The association between baseline gout and longitudinal RA disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index, CDAI ≤10) was examined using mixed-effects logistic regression at 24-months, adjusting for prespecified confounders.
RESULTS: Among 3,703 RA patients, 113 (3.1%) had coexisting gout with mean (SD) age of 66.1 (8.7) years and 52.2% were female. Coexisting gout was associated with older age (OR 1.05 per year), obesity (OR 1.67), cardiovascular disease or hypertension (OR 1.95) and diuretic use (OR 1.68), while female sex was inversely associated (OR 0.31).
