CDAI scores were similar between patients with and without gout at baseline (18.3±12.5 vs 20.2±13.5) and at 12-months (10.9±9.8 vs 11.0±10.4). After adjustment, baseline coexisting gout was neither significantly associated with oral GC use at 12-months (OR 1.73, 95% CI: 0.96-3.13) or the attainment of CDAI low disease activity/remission by 24-months (OR 1.19, 95% CI: 0.72-1.97).
CONCLUSION: In this large real-world RA cohort, coexisting gout was uncommon and associated with traditional gout risk factors but did not statistically influence oral GC use or RA treatment target attainment.

Title: Stent Configurations in Aortoiliac Occlusive disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate which endovascular stent configuration at the aortic bifurcation offers superior outcomes for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD).
METHODS: Studies reporting outcomes for endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, for TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C and D lesions were included in the review. Data for primary, primary-assisted and secondary patency were extracted (full-text articles or reconstructed from published Kaplan Meier curves).
RESULTS: This review included 12 studies, including 1027 patients (177 Covered Endovascular Reconstruction of the Aortic Bifurcation (CERAB), 850 kissing stent). Most studies were retrospective cohort studies with moderate methodological quality. Median follow-up was 20 months for primary patency, and 48 months for assisted and secondary patency. CERAB and kissing stent techniques showed similar primary patency (p=0.24). Primary-assisted patency was slightly lower for CERAB but not statistically significant (p=0.051). Secondary patency favored CERAB (p=0.045). At two years, CERAB had primary patency of 90%, primary-assisted patency of 87%, and secondary patency of 100%. Kissing stents showed primary patency of 91%, primary-assisted patency of 92%, and secondary patency of 96%.
CONCLUSION: Both stent types yielded positive results, but current data does not favor one configuration. Current studies on this topic are low quality. At present, the method of endovascular intervention for AIOD could be left to clinical expertise, although hemodynamic studies may provide insights. Randomized trial data or post-market registries are needed to ascertain superiority of any stent configuration in this disease process.

Title: SGLT2 inhibitor-induced genitourinary infections and the consequent antimicrobial-antidiabetic drug interactions: A narrative review of clinical and pharmacovigilance concern.
Abstract: Sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular and renal benefits in type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure, but their use is associated with genitourinary (GU) infections and medication-safety concerns during antimicrobial treatment. This narrative review integrate evidence regarding SGLT2 inhibitor-associated GU infections, antimicrobial-antidiabetic drug interactions, pharmacovigilance, clinical management, and antimicrobial stewardship. Evidence from randomized controlled trials, meta-analysis, observational studies, pharmacokinetic studies and pharmacovigilance databases were used to synthesise on infection risk, drug interactions, management and safety issues in vulnerable populations. To identify relevant evidence narrative review was completed with evidence found in Pubmed, Google scholar, Clinical trial gov between 2020 and 2026. A purposive selection of literature was conducted to identify studies relevant to the article with a methodological strength, and not a systematic search was used.SGLT2 inhibitors demonstrate a more consistent association with genital mycotic infections than urinary tract infections (UTIs). Most GU infections are mild to moderate and can be treated with standard antimicrobial or antifungal therapy without routine discontinuation of SGLT2 inhibitors. SGLT2 inhibitors have low potential for drug-drug interactions, however, exposure to other agents can altered by strong enzyme inducers like rifampin, and this effect varies by SGLT2 inhibitor. Pharmacovigilance complements trial evidence by identifying safety signals, although disproportionality signals require clinical validation. Antimicrobial stewardship also enables treatment, avoidance of unnecessary prophylaxis, evaluation of risk factors, and assessment of concomitant medications and interactions.

Title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA).
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study

Title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with MASLD: A translational study.
Abstract: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, potentially involving systemic metabolic dysfunction and cardiac remodeling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve metabolic dysfunction in MASLD; however, their associations with cardiovascular outcomes and effects on MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. In this translational study, we integrated a real-world TriNetX cohort of patients with MASLD and T2D with complementary experimental studies in a mouse model of MASLD. Following propensity score matching, 42,910 patients were included in each treatment group. GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite cardiovascular outcome compared with sulfonylurea therapy (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% confidence interval 0.84-0.91; P < 0.001), although this association was not statistically significant in 90-day and 180-day landmark analyses. In Western diet-fed mice, GLP-1 RA treatment improved selected indices of cardiac function and attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Although myocardial fibrosis was numerically reduced, the difference compared with vehicle-treated mice was not statistically significant (P = 0.28). Molecular analyses showed reduced expression of fibrosis- and extracellular matrix remodeling-related markers, including CTGF, TGF-β1, and vimentin. Collectively, GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the primary observational analysis, although this finding was not consistently supported by sensitivity analyses. Complementary experimental findings suggest improvements in selected cardiac functional indices and changes in fibrosis-associated molecular remodeling, warranting further investigation.

Title: Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE) in adults with chronic stroke: a randomized controlled trial.
Journal: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke rehabilitation guidelines recommend goal-oriented, task-specific, intensive interventions. Yet most programs emphasize upper extremity (UE) recovery, overlooking lower extremities (LEs) and trunk, which are essential for activities of daily living. Consequently, Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including LEs (HABIT-ILE) represents a promising approach for stroke rehabilitation.
OBJECTIVE: This randomized controlled trial aimed to determine the effect of HABIT-ILE and to compare its efficacy with a control group in adults with chronic hemiparetic stroke by promoting greater improvements across the body functions, activity, and participation domains of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health.
METHODS: Forty-six adults with hemiparetic chronic stroke were randomized to either a 2-week (50 h, 5 h/day) HABIT-ILE camp-setting program in Brussels, Belgium, or to continue their usual neurorehabilitation (mean = 4 h 36 min) for over the same period. Participants were assessed before, immediately, and at 3 months after intervention using the Adult Assisting Hand Assessment Stroke (Ad-AHA Stroke, primary outcome), the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM), the Fugl Meyer Assessment for UEs (FMA-UE), the Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT), the ABILHAND-CS and ACTIVLIM-CS questionnaires, the six-minute walk test, the modified Rankin Scale and the Stroke Impact Scale (SIS).
RESULTS: The ANCOVA revealed a significant between-groups difference favoring the HABIT-ILE group (TG), with a time effect observed for the Ad-AHA Stroke (TG: at 2 weeks = +6.24% of logits; at 3 months = +7.05% of logits), WMFT (Functional Ability Scale, all P ≤ 0.041), and COPM (P < 0.001, performance and satisfaction) at both 2 weeks and 3 months. We found a similar significant effect for the SIS (hand function, P = 0.003) at 2 weeks and the FMA-UE and ABILHAND-CS at 3 months (all P ≤ 0.033). We observed no significant between-group differences for the other outcomes, including LEs measures.
CONCLUSION: In adults with chronic stroke, HABIT-ILE intervention significantly improved spontaneous bimanual use, motor function, and ability of the paretic UE (both externally rated and self-perceived) and reduced participation restrictions compared with the control group.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This randomized controlled trial was registered on December 11th, 2020, on ClinicalTrials.gov as "HABIT-ILE in Adults With Chronic Stroke (HABIT-ILE Stroke)", with the registration number NCT04664673 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04664673?cond=NCT04664673&rank=).

Title: Social participation after community stroke rehabilitation: individual and intervention factors in a retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improving social participation is a key objective of poststroke rehabilitation, yet determinants of successful outcomes in Community Stroke Rehabilitation Teams (CSRT) remain poorly understood. In particular, the respective contributions of person-related and intervention-related factors need clarification.
OBJECTIVE: To identify person-related and intervention-related factors associated with improvement in social participation following a home-based CSRT rehabilitation program.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 534 patients with stroke managed by a CSRT between 2019 and 2024. Social participation was assessed using the Frenchay Activities Index (FAI) at baseline and after intervention. Responders were defined as a FAI score increase ≥7 points. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors among patient characteristics and intervention components.
RESULTS: Seventeen percent of participants achieved an improvement in FAI ≥7 points. Independent person-related factors included younger age (OR 0.975; P = 0.010) and higher baseline functional status (Barthel Index) (OR 1.027; P = 0.005). Regarding intervention-related factors, programs including adapted physical activity (OR 2.01; P = 0.023), mobility-focused interventions (OR 3.21; P = 0.043), communication (OR 2.15; P = 0.035), and work reintegration support (OR 2.17; P = 0.015) were significantly associated with FAI improvement. Participation in therapeutic education workshops was more frequent among Responders (88%vs 60%, P < 0.001), particularly those focused on adapted physical activity, mobility retraining, and communication. Responders also showed greater improvement in quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Personal and stroke-related factors show limited ability to predict improvement in social participation. In contrast, key interventions targeting mobility, physical activity, communication, and work reintegration are significantly associated with an improvement in social participation.
DATA REGISTRATION: This study was a retrospective observational study based on routine clinical care and was not prospectively registered in an international trial registry.

Title: A latent ODE approach to full-cycle biventricular cardiac motion modeling from cine MRI.
Abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) captures rich spatiotemporal information about ventricular structure and motion, but conventional risk models use only a few image-derived indices from selected cardiac phases. We present a latent dynamical model that encodes bi-ventricular anatomy and full-cycle cine motion as a continuous latent trajectory, using heart-rate-aware neural ordinary differential equation (ODE) dynamics and a graph-based mesh autoencoder to reconstruct anatomically consistent 3D+t ventricular motion. A covariate-conditioned prior defines the expected end-diastolic latent state, and a Cox proportional hazards model tests whether deviations from this prior predict incident heart failure. We studied 72,386 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease, including 367 incident heart failure events. In a held-out evaluation subset, adding the latent score to refitted pooled cohort equations improved the stratified C-index from 0.704 to 0.785, compared with 0.764 for seven established cardiac markers. Compared with non-graph and non-ODE approaches, the proposed model gave the best trade-off between reconstruction fidelity, generative realism, and downstream prognostic performance. These results suggest that continuous full-cycle modeling of ventricular motion provides informative cardiac phenotypes beyond conventional CMR summaries, while external validation in more representative patient cohorts is required before clinical risk-prediction use.

Title: Exercise capacity in patients with psoriasis assessed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psoriasis is a systemic inflammatory disease associated with cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities. Although reduced physical activity is frequently reported in these patients, objective data on physiological exercise capacity remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate exercise capacity in patients with psoriasis using Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), the gold standard method, and compare the results with those of healthy controls.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 32 patients with psoriasis (off systemic therapy for ≥6-months) and 33 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Participants underwent symptom-limited CPET on a cycle ergometer. Disease severity was assessed using the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI), and Physician Global Assessment (PGA).
RESULTS: Patients with psoriasis demonstrated significantly lower exercise capacity compared to controls. Peak VO₂, percentage of predicted peak VO₂, VO₂ at AT, and work rate were all significantly lower (all p < 0.01). Peak VO₂ showed significant negative correlations with BMI, PASI, and PGA (all p ≤ 0.001). In multiple linear regression analysis, age (β = -0.17, p = 0.017), BMI (β = -0.30, p = 0.007), and PASI score (β = -0.47, p = 0.001) were identified as independent predictors of peak VO₂, explaining 63.4% of its variance (R² = 0.634, p < 0.001).
STUDY LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design and relatively small single-center sample limit causal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with psoriasis demonstrated reduced exercise capacity compared with healthy controls, and disease severity was independently associated with lower peak VO₂. However, due to the cross-sectional design and the potential influence of unmeasured cardiometabolic and lifestyle-related confounders, causality cannot be established, and further prospective studies are required.

Title: Temporal trends and projections of hypertension with hyperlipidemia-related mortality among US adults, 2000-2035: Insights from CDC WONDER database.
Journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and hyperlipidemia are highly prevalent cardiometabolic disorders and major contributors to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. These conditions frequently coexist and synergistically increase cardiovascular risk through mechanisms including endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, and atherosclerosis. Despite advances in treatment, many individuals remain inadequately controlled. This study evaluated temporal trends in mortality associated with hypertension and hyperlipidemia in the United States from 2000 to 2035.
METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database. Adults aged ≥25 years with hypertension (ICD-10: I10-I15) or hyperlipidemia (ICD-10: E78) listed on death certificates were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated using the 2000 U.S. standard population. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent change (APC) and average annual percent change (AAPC). Analyses were stratified by sex, age, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization.
RESULTS: From 2000 to 2023, 1,156,335 deaths were recorded. AAMRs increased from 5.86 (95% CI: 5.74-5.97) to 37.28 (95% CI: 37.05-37.51), with a significant overall rise (AAPC: 8.34; p < 0.001). Mortality was consistently higher in males than females (AAPC: 8.50 vs. 7.93; both p < 0.001). All racial and ethnic groups showed increasing trends, with the highest mean AAMR among non-Hispanic Black individuals (AAPC: 8.21; p < 0.001). Older adults (≥65 years) had the greatest mortality burden (AAPC: 8.82; p < 0.001). The South (AAPC: 8.84; p<0.001) and non-metropolitan areas (AAPC: 9.76; p < 0.001) demonstrated the fastest-rising mortality rates.
CONCLUSION: Hypertension- and hyperlipidemia-related mortality rose substantially with marked disparities, highlighting the need for improved prevention and equitable care.

Title: Screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in adults using ECG-derived frontal QRS-T angle.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common inherited cardiac disorder associated with increased risk of arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. While the spatial QRS-T angle has shown strong performance for detecting HCM retrospectively, its widespread clinical utility is limited by a need for specific equipment or dense computations. The frontal QRS-T angle can easily be derived from any 12‑lead electrocardiogram (ECG) and may offer a practical screening alternative.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 3133 adults over the age of 30 who participated in the Heartfelt community cardiovascular screening program, including 3124 controls and 9 HCM cases. In the primary analysis, HCM was defined as septal or posterior left ventricular wall thickness ≥15 mm in the absence of hypertension. In a secondary analysis, the definition of HCM was expanded to include patients with hypertension. Frontal QRS-T angle was derived from standard 12‑lead ECGs by calculating the absolute difference between frontal plane QRS axis and the T axis. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the diagnostic performance of frontal QRS-T angle in predicting HCM. In addition, logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between the frontal QRS-T angle and HCM.
RESULTS: In the primary analysis, the frontal QRS-T angle demonstrated fair discriminatory ability for HCM detection, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.711 (95% CI 0.520-0.901). At a cutoff threshold of 44.5°, sensitivity was 67% and specificity was 86%. In the secondary ROC analysis, which included patients with underlying hypertension in the HCM group, the AUC was 0.806 (95% CI 0.676-0.935). At a threshold of 46.5°, sensitivity was 44% and specificity was 87%. In multivariate logistic regression, frontal QRS-T angle was independently associated with HCM (adjusted OR per 1° increase 1.023; 95% CI 1.008-1.039; p = 0.003).
CONCLUSIONS: The ECG-derived frontal QRS-T angle showed fair to good diagnostic performance as a screening tool for HCM in a healthy adult screening cohort. A higher frontal QRS-T angle was also independently associated with greater odds of HCM in a logistic regression analysis. These findings suggest that the QRS-T angle may serve as a useful, noninvasive adjunct for identifying individuals at risk for HCM in broader clinical populations. Further studies with larger and more balanced cohorts are warranted to validate these findings.

Title: Poor R-wave progression and long-term outcomes in the multi-ethnic study of atherosclerosis (MESA).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor R-wave progression (PRWP) has been interpreted as a marker of anterior myocardial injury since the 1970s, but its temporal stability, substrate, and independent prognostic value in a CAD-free cohort remain uncertain.
METHODS: We studied 6323 MESA participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease with standardized 12‑lead ECGs at baseline (Exam 1, 2000-02) and after a median of 10 years (Exam 5, 2010-12). PRWP was defined as R-wave amplitude ≤3 mm in V3 with RV3 > RV2. We assessed 10-year test-retest stability (Cohen's κ), pulmonary/thoracic correlates, mechanistic substrate via cardiac magnetic resonance, high-sensitivity troponin T, NT-proBNP, and polysomnography, and long-term outcomes (all-cause death, cardiovascular death, MACE) over median 14 years using Cox and Fine-Gray models.
RESULTS: PRWP prevalence was 3.2% at Exam 1 and 6.2% at Exam 5. Binary test-retest agreement was limited (κ = 0.344; 95% CI 0.283-0.406) despite good continuous R-V3 reliability (ICC = 0.73); only 52% of baseline PRWP persisted at 10 years. Self-reported emphysema (OR 4.48; 2.30-8.22) and current smoking (OR 1.77; 1.14-2.73) were the strongest PRWP predictors. PRWP was not associated with RV volumes, RV ejection fraction, NT-proBNP, or sleep apnea. After adjustment for smoking and emphysema, PRWP was not independently associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.19; 0.90-1.58), cardiovascular death (HR 1.02; 0.67-1.57), or MACE (HR 0.89; 0.54-1.47). Time-updated and Fine-Gray models confirmed null associations.
CONCLUSIONS: In a CAD-free multi-ethnic cohort, isolated PRWP is an ECG pattern with limited binary reproducibility, linked to pulmonary exposure and thoracic habitus rather than myocardial substrate, and carries no independent cardiovascular prognostic value.

Title: Hemodynamic Effects of Reducing LV Afterload With Impella or Intra-Aortic Balloon Counterpulsation During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock: HERACLES Trial.
Abstract: Background: Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides organ support in cardiogenic shock but increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, potentially impairing cardiac recovery. LV unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or micro-axial flow pump (mAFP) may mitigate this effect. HERACLES compared their effects on myocardial oxygen supply and demand. Methods: Patients receiving VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock were randomized to LV unloading with IABP or mAFP, stratified by ischemic/non-ischemic etiology. Distal coronary, aortic and LV pressures and coronary flow (inverse mean transit time, Tmn) were measured with and without unloading. Myocardial oxygen demand was estimated as the area under the LV pressure curve in systole (TTI) x heart rate (HR). The primary endpoint was the change in myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio calculated as [(Tmn * TTI*HR)off / (Tmn * TTI *HR)unload]. Secondary endpoints included changes in coronary flow [device flow ratio (DFR) =(Tmn)off/ (Tmn)unload], oxygen demand per beat (DTTI), contractility (DdP/dtmax) and filling pressure (DLVEDP). Results: Twenty-four patients were enrolled (age 51 [46-57]; 46% male; 96% SCAI D/E; 38% ischemic). At randomization, lactate was 4.3 mmol/L [IQR 2.5 to 8.4], LV ejection fraction 10% [10 to 17], LVEDP 18 mmHg [14 to 24]. The myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio improved with IABP but not mAFP (1.48 [1.23 to 2.10] vs 0.97 [0.92 to 1.39]; P=0.036), driven predominantly by differential reduction of TTI. Coronary pressure increased but flow was unchanged with mAFP (DFR 1.00 [0.86 to 1.13]). Coronary flow increased marginally with IABP (DFR 1.16 [1.00 to 1.51]). LV pressures decreased with both devices and contractility with IABP only, with no between-group differences. Thirty-day mortality was similar (38% vs 45%, p=0.84). Conclusions: In VA-ECMO supported SCAI D/E cardiogenic shock, IABP improved myocardial oxygen supply-demand balance, whereas mAFP did not. Further research is needed to determine whether these mechanistic differences translate to clinical outcomes.

Title: Bivalirudin With a High-Dose Post-PCI Infusion Versus Heparin During Primary PCI in STEMI: One-Year Results From the BRIGHT-4 Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The BRIGHT-4 trial (Bivalirudin With Prolonged Full-Dose Infusion During Primary PCI Versus Heparin Trial-4) demonstrated that procedural anticoagulation with bivalirudin plus a high-dose postprocedure infusion reduced the 30-day composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding compared with heparin monotherapy in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with radial artery access. We now report the 12-month follow-up results to evaluate the long-term outcomes of primary PCI with these 2 anticoagulation regimens.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 6016 patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion for 2 to 4 hours (n=3009) or heparin monotherapy (n=3007). The primary outcome of interest was the composite of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 12 months.
RESULTS: At 12 months, the primary outcome occurred in 124 (4.1%) patients in the bivalirudin group and 169 (5.6%) patients in the heparin group (hazard ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.58-0.92]; P=0.007). Bivalirudin resulted in lower 12-month rates of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding (0.6% versus 1.2%; hazard ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.28-0.87]; P=0.01) and stent thrombosis (0.8% versus 1.3%; hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.36-0.99]; P=0.045), with nonsignificant differences in all-cause death (3.8% versus 4.8%; hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.63-1.02]; P=0.08), cardiovascular death, reinfarction, ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization, and stroke between the 2 groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access, the benefits of bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion in reducing the composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 30 days compared with heparin monotherapy are maintained through 12-month follow-up. These findings support the use of bivalirudin with a post-PCI high-dose infusion as an alternative to heparin to reduce mortality and major bleeding in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03822975.

Title: Beyond the heart: a large-cohort study of 11C-PiB PET revealing organ-specific uptake patterns and diagnostic thresholds in systemic AL amyloidosis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Systemic AL amyloidosis frequently involves multiple organs, yet non‑invasive imaging for early and comprehensive multi‑organ assessment remains limited. The diagnostic role of 11C-PiB PET beyond the heart-particularly its organ‑specific uptake patterns and clinically applicable thresholds-has not been systematically defined in a large cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 80 participants (60 ± 10 years, 55 males) undergoing Whole-body 11C-PiB PET/MR or PET/CT from 2018 to Sep 2024. Final diagnoses were as follows: AL group (n = 65), non‑AL group (n = 10), control group (n = 5). PET indices (SUVmax, SUVRmax, ASUVRmax, ASUVRmean) were quantified for 15 organs. Optimal diagnostic cutoffs were derived using ROC analysis or quartiles. Correlations with clinical and morphofunctional markers were assessed.
RESULTS: Organ-specific uptake patterns differed across tissues, with clear disease-related accumulation observed in the myocardium, spleen, bone marrow, and tongue, whereas interpretation was limited in organs affected by physiological tracer kinetics, such as the kidney. Myocardial PiB uptake correlated significantly with NT‑proBNP, native T1, and ventricular wall thickness; hepatic uptake was paradoxically reduced, with negative correlations with ALP and projected liver area; renal uptake correlated positively with eGFR and negatively with β2‑microglobulin. Organ-specific diagnostic thresholds were established using the optimal-performing semiquantitative parameters: myocardium SUVmax 2.20 (sensitivity 90%, specificity 100%, AUC 0.995); tongue SUVmax 2.05 (86%, 100%, AUC 0.971); bone marrow SUVRmax 2.05 (70%, 100%, AUC 0.880); liver SUVmax 7.95 (88%, 80%, AUC 0.900). Quartile‑based thresholds further defined involvement in the spleen, thyroid, and salivary glands.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, 11C-PiB PET revealed distinct organ-specific uptake patterns and diagnostic thresholds for systemic AL amyloidosis across multiple organs were preliminarily established. It provides a non-invasive, biopsy‑sparing assessment of multi-organ involvement while highlighting organ-specific limitations, particularly related to renal uptake interpretation and the need for further validation in selected tissues.

Title: Pharmacological Interventions for Neurological Manifestations of Ataxia-Telangiectasia: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T) causes progressive neurological disability. Following two phase III trials published in 2026, this study is an updated randomized evidence for pharmacological interventions targeting neurological manifestations of A-T. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library were searched. Eligible studies were RCTs in children or adults with A-T. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2. N-acetyl-L-leucine/levacetylleucine SARA treatment effects were pooled using a random-effects generic inverse-variance model with restricted maximum likelihood (REML), with common-effect and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman sensitivity analyses. Secondary analyses pooled full-ICARS efficacy and safety outcomes from the two eDSP trials. Six RCTs evaluated oral betamethasone, N-acetyl-L-leucine/levacetylleucine, erythrocyte-encapsulated dexamethasone sodium phosphate (eDSP), and triheptanoin. Two crossover trials contributed to the SARA meta-analysis. The pooled REML effect was not significant (MD -0.90, 95% CI -3.20 to 1.40; p = 0.443; I²=75.8%). Two eDSP trials contributed comparable full-ICARS estimates in children aged 6-9 years; the conventional pooled result favored eDSP (MD -4.03, 95% CI -6.78 to -1.29). Neither eDSP trial met its prespecified primary neurological endpoint. Pooled eDSP risk ratios were 1.05 (0.94 to 1.17) for any treatment-emergent adverse event, 1.45 (0.995 to 2.12) for treatment-related events, and 0.94 (0.40 to 2.22) for serious adverse events. Betamethasone and triheptanoin were each represented by one RCT. Despite FDA approval of levacetylleucine for ataxia in A-T, pooled SARA effects remain inconsistent. The favorable secondary eDSP full-ICARS estimate does not supersede the unsuccessful primary trial analyses. Harmonized, feasible neurological outcome measures are needed.PROSPERO Registration NumberCRD420261474940.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Image guidance is associated with lower rates of pseudoarthrosis diagnosis after long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation: a propensity-matched cohort study.
Journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to assess the association between intra-operative navigation and short- and long-term outcomes following long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation.
METHODS: This was a retrospective propensity-matched cohort study of adults undergoing long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation utilizing a multi-institutional electronic health record database. Inclusion criteria were patients undergoing thoracolumbar posterior spinal instrumentation greater than seven levels with and without intra-operative navigation. Exclusion criteria were < 18 years old, spinal neoplasms, trauma, inflammatory, or infectious bone conditions. The index surgery date range was restricted a priori to 2015 through 2020 to reduce era-related confounding in navigation exposure and outcome ascertainment and to allow adequate observation time for each outcome window. Cohorts were matched 1:1 on 40 covariates, with balance assessed by standardized mean differences. Categorical outcomes were compared with Chi-squared tests and time-to-event outcomes with Kaplan-Meier estimation, log-rank testing, and Cox proportional-hazards models. Because multiple outcomes were tested within each time window, the Holm-Bonferroni procedure was applied to control the family-wise error rate.
RESULTS: Propensity score matching resulted in 1,646 patients in each cohort. At thirty days, the navigated cohort had a higher rate of blood transfusion (12.4% versus 9.2%; OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.12-1.75; P = 0.003), which remained significant after Holm-Bonferroni correction. Higher observed rates of acute kidney injury and myocardial infarction in the navigated cohort were nominal only and did not survive correction, and there was no significant difference in deep venous thrombosis or sepsis. At one, two, and five years, patients in the non-navigated cohort demonstrated a significantly higher risk of pseudoarthrosis diagnosis than patients in the navigated cohort (one year OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.10-1.82, P = 0.006; two years OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.15-1.81, P = 0.001; five years OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.13-1.69, P = 0.002), each surviving Holm-Bonferroni correction. However, there were similar rates of reoperation at five-years between the two cohorts (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.75-1.18; P = 0.465) with similar rates of adjacent segment disease (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.77-1.24; P = 0.820).
CONCLUSION: Image guidance was associated with a lower rate of pseudoarthrosis diagnosis through five years following long-segment posterior spinal instrumentation. This was not accompanied by a reduction in reoperation, and short-term medical outcomes were largely similar with mixed differences in selected complications.

Title: Clinical patterns and major organ involvement in Behçet's syndrome: a latent class analysis of a regional cohort.
Abstract: Behçet's syndrome is a heterogeneous disease with diverse patterns of organ involvement. We aimed to identify clinical subgroups using latent class analysis and evaluate clinical characteristics and treatment patterns across the identified subgroups and sex. We retrospectively evaluated 136 patients fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease. Latent class analysis (LCA) based on six clinical indicators was used to identify clinical subgroups. Clinical manifestations, major organ involvement, and current treatments were compared between the identified latent classes and by sex. Major organ involvement occurred in 79 patients (58.1%). Among the standard LCA models, the two-class solution had the lowest BIC. Class 1 (40.4%) was characterized by absence of pathergy positivity and a very low probability of papulopustular lesions (1.3%), but a higher probability of ocular involvement (60.0%). Class 2 (59.6%) showed high probabilities of pathergy positivity (90.7%) and papulopustular lesions (57.7%). Major organ involvement was more frequent in Class 1 than in Class 2 (70.9% vs. 49.4%, p = 0.020). Male patients had significantly higher rates of ocular (52.7% vs. 35.5%, p = 0.044), vascular (28.4% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.003), and major organ involvement (73.0% vs. 40.3%, p < 0.001), as well as current anti-TNF therapy (23.0% vs. 8.1%, p = 0.019), than female patients. Patients with major organ involvement had significantly lower rates of genital ulcer history (51.9% vs. 84.2%, p < 0.001), pathergy positivity (45.6% vs. 70.2%, p = 0.004), and joint involvement (11.4% vs. 28.1%, p = 0.013). The BIC-selected solution identified two main patient groups, but the class structure was highly sensitive to indicator selection. Overall, our findings support exploratory clinical patterns rather than fixed Behçet phenotypes, with major organ involvement being significantly more frequent among men.

Title: Cellular senescence in calcific aortic valve disease: are we ready for senolytic therapy?
Abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the Western countries and carries significant morbidity and mortality, yet no pharmacological therapy has demonstrated efficacy in modifying its natural history. Once regarded as a passive degenerative process, CAVD is now recognized as an actively regulated disease driven by endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, dysregulated mineral metabolism, and cellular senescence, which collectively drive progressive fibrotic remodeling and calcification of the valve leaflets through both dystrophic and osteogenic mechanisms. This review examines the pharmacological strategies that have been investigated or are currently under evaluation to slow CAVD progression, encompassing lipid-lowering agents, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, bone resorption inhibitors, vitamin K supplementation, and nitric oxide pathway modulators. Despite strong biological rationale and encouraging observational or preclinical data, each of these approaches has thus far failed to demonstrate consistent disease, modifying efficacy in prospective randomized trials, reflecting the complexity of CAVD pathophysiology and the historical lack of mechanistic precision in patient selection and trial design. Emerging evidence suggests that cellular senescence may represent a unifying and potentially actionable therapeutic target, bridging endothelial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and active calcification within a single pathophysiological framework. Preclinical studies demonstrate that senolytic clearance of senescent cells reduces calcification in atherosclerosic and hypercholesterolemic vascular models provide a compelling rationale for extending this approach to valvular targets.

Title: Colchicine and Perioperative Acute Kidney Injury: A Substudy of the COP-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Perioperative inflammation may result in organ injury, including acute kidney injury (AKI). Colchicine, an anti-inflammatory drug, may help protect the organs from inflammation. This clinical trial substudy examined whether colchicine reduced the risk of perioperative AKI compared with placebo.
STUDY DESIGN: Prespecified substudy of a placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged 55 years or older undergoing major noncardiac thoracic surgery enrolled in the Colchicine for the Prevention of Perioperative Atrial Fibrillation (COP-AF) trial from 45 centers in 11 countries (2018-2023). Patients were excluded for a history of atrial fibrillation, for taking antiarrhythmic medication, or for a preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min per 1.73 m2.
EXPOSURE: Participants were randomized 1:1 to 0.5 mg oral colchicine or placebo, given twice daily for a total of 10 days. Patients, health care providers, data collectors, and outcome adjudicators were masked to the treatment assignment.
OUTCOME: Perioperative AKI, defined as an increase in serum creatinine concentration of either ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours of surgery or ≥50% within 7 days of surgery. Alternative definitions of AKI were examined, as was effect modification by pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD).
RESULTS: Among 3,209 patients enrolled in the main trial, 2,947 were included in this substudy (mean age, 68 years; mean eGFR, 83 mL/min/1.73 m2) and were randomly allocated to receive colchicine (n = 1,476) or placebo (n = 1,471). Perioperative AKI occurred in 67 participants (4.7%) in the colchicine group and in 63 participants (4.4%) in the placebo group (risk ratio [RR], 1.07 [95% CI, 0.76-1.50], P = 0.72; risk difference [RD], 0.3% [95% CI, -1.2% to 1.8%]). The RD of AKI in patients with CKD treated with colchicine versus placebo was -0.9%, and it was 0.5% in those without CKD (interaction P = 0.62).
LIMITATIONS: Limited statistical power to detect small clinically important effects on AKI treated with dialysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing noncardiac thoracic surgery, the risk of perioperative AKI did not differ between patients allocated to receive colchicine versus placebo.
FUNDING: Grants from academic (Department of Medicine, Western University; Division of Cardiology, McMaster University), government (Canadian Institutes of Health Research; General Research Fund, Research Grants Council, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China), and not-for-profit (Accelerating Clinical Trials Consortium; Innovation Fund of the Alternative Funding Plan for the Academic Health Sciences Centres of Ontario; Population Health Research Institute; Hamilton Health Sciences; Hanela Foundation) sources.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov with study number NCT03310125.
PLAIN-LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Inflammation during and after surgery can lead to organ injury, including acute kidney injury (AKI). Colchicine, an anti-inflammatory drug, may help protect the organs from inflammation. This prespecified kidney substudy of the COP-AF trial (a placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial of 3,209 patients aged 55 years and older having major noncardiac thoracic surgery), examined the effect of oral colchicine (0.5 mg tablet, taken twice daily starting within 4 hours before surgery for a total of 10 days) on the risk of perioperative AKI. The study found that the risk of perioperative AKI did not differ between patients assigned to receive colchicine versus placebo. The results were consistent for multiple definitions of AKI and in patients with pre-existing chronic kidney disease.

Title: A Mobile Application for STEMI Care Optimization in a Multicenter Health System.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interhospital transfer logistics and fragmented coordination among care team members may cause delays in treating ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients. We developed a secure mobile application, STEMIcathAID (App), to streamline STEMI activation, transfer coordination, and allow time-stamp data capture.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to assess the effect of App implementation on time measures in a multicenter health care system.
METHODS: We conducted an observational comparison of STEMI activations managed through the App vs the traditional workflow across 2 interfacility transfer routes (pathways 1 and 2), and 1 percutaneous coronary intervention-capable local pathway. The primary analyses were the composite door-to-device (D2D) and combined transfer pathway door-in-door-out (DIDO) comparisons, reported as median (IQR).
RESULTS: Composite D2D time decreased from 92 min (IQR: 63-110) to 71 min (IQR: 60-85; Hodges-Lehmann reduction: 16 min; 95% CI: 8-24; P < 0.001). Combined transfer pathway DIDO decreased from 57.5 min (IQR: 48.3-70.8) to 46.0 min (IQR: 39.5-57.5; Hodges-Lehmann reduction: 12 min; 95% CI: 6-19; P < 0.001). D2D and DIDO improved in both interhospital transfer pathways, whereas the local pathway showed no significant improvement. D2D target attainment according to pathway-specific registry benchmarks improved from 84.9% (79/93) to 100% (123/123; P < 0.001). The proportion of transfer cases achieving DIDO ≤45 min increased from 20.4% (11/54) to 46.0% (29/63; P = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: In this observational multicenter implementation study, App-managed STEMI activations were associated with shorter transfer-related time metrics and higher attainment of guideline-relevant time thresholds across 2 interfacility pathways.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Detection of Aortic Valve Calcification on Routine Noncontrast Chest CT: A Real-World Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine noncontrast chest computed tomography (CT) may reveal aortic valve calcification (AVC) outside aortic stenosis evaluation. Its prevalence, burden, and documentation remain uncertain. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enable systematic detection.
OBJECTIVES: The study aims to evaluate AVC prevalence and burden, clinical correlates, radiology documentation, and AI-assisted case finding.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study screened 511 consecutive noncontrast, non-electrocardiographically gated chest CT examinations in adults aged ≥50 years. After 15 protocol exclusions and 56 software-designated nonevaluable examinations, 440 underwent quantification by 2 blinded readers. AVC was defined as >10 AU using a 130-Hounsfield-unit threshold adjusted for blood-pool attenuation and image noise when needed. Locked HealthAVC V1.0 was a secondary comparator.
RESULTS: Manual quantification identified AVC in 172 of 440 scans (39.1%; 95% CI: 34.6%-43.7%); 97 of 440 (22.0%) had ≥100 AU. Inter-reader agreement at >10 AU was 99.5% (kappa = 0.990). Age (adjusted OR: 1.92 per 5 years; 95% CI: 1.63-2.26) and male sex (adjusted OR: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.32-3.30) were associated with AVC. Reports documented 27 of 172 positive scans (15.7%; 95% CI: 11.0%-21.9%). AI detected 169 of 172 manually confirmed cases (98.3%) among 440 evaluable scans, including 142 of 145 undocumented cases. Of 496 submitted scans, 56 (11.3%) were nonevaluable. End-to-end sensitivity counting positive rejected scans as missed was 89.9%. Among 86 AI-positive patients with echocardiography, 10 (11.6%) had mild-or-greater aortic stenosis.
CONCLUSIONS: AVC was common but infrequently documented on routine chest CT. AI detected most cases among evaluable scans; 11.3% were nonevaluable, yielding 89.9% end-to-end sensitivity. Prospective studies should assess clinical pathways.

Title: Procedural Volume and Outcomes After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty for Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is an established treatment for inoperable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension; however, volume-outcome relationships remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined the relationship between hospital and operator volume and BPA-related complications using a nationwide registry.
METHODS: The authors analyzed 5,403 BPA sessions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension in the Japanese Structural Heart Diseases registry between 2021 and 2024. Procedural volume was defined as BPA sessions performed during the preceding 3 years. The primary outcome was a composite of BPA-related complications. Mixed-effects logistic regression models accounted for hospital and operator clustering.
RESULTS: BPA-related complications occurred in 751 sessions (13.9%). Severe complications were uncommon, with 3 periprocedural deaths, 6 requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, and 7 requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. The main categorical analysis revealed that hospital BPA volume ≥150 sessions/3 years was associated with higher odds of BPA-related complications (adjusted OR: 1.60; 95% CI: 1.08-2.36; P = 0.019), whereas operator volume was not independently associated. When hospital and operator volumes were modeled separately as continuous variables, each was associated with complications. However, neither remained independently associated after mutual adjustment. In an analysis restricted to 135 complications considered less susceptible to differences in ascertainment, no statistically significant association was detected for either volume measure, although the smaller number of events limited statistical precision.
CONCLUSIONS: BPA-related complications demonstrated a complex relationship with procedural volume, while severe complications remained uncommon. The attenuation of hospital- and operator-level associations after mutual adjustment suggests that procedural volume alone may not adequately characterize BPA safety. Further studies incorporating lesion- and procedural-level characteristics and standardized complication ascertainment are warranted.

Title: Angiography-Derived Radial Wall Strain Across All Epicardial Vessels Before Acute Coronary Syndrome: The CULPRIT-STRAIN Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiography-derived radial wall strain (RWS) is a biomechanical index associated with plaque vulnerability. Whether elevated RWS demonstrates culprit-vessel predominance or broader multivessel distribution within the same patient is unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare maximal RWS (RWSmax) in the future culprit vessel with nonculprit vessels within the same patient and assess its association with time to acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
METHODS: In the multicenter CULPRIT-STRAIN study, consecutive ACS patients with a prior coronary angiogram (≥3 months before event) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry (NCT04185285). RWSmax was measured in all 3 epicardial coronary arteries at the index angiogram. The primary endpoint was within-patient comparison of culprit vs nonculprit RWSmax; secondary endpoints included its association with index-to-ACS interval and the prevalence of multivessel biomechanical elevation.
RESULTS: Among 101 patients (303 vessels; median index-to-ACS interval, 35 months), culprit-vessel RWSmax was higher than nonculprit-vessel RWSmax (19.7% vs 11.3%; P < 0.001). The culprit vessel had the highest RWSmax in 96 patients (95.0%; P < 0.001), with a median within-patient ΔRWS of 7.0% (IQR: 3.6%-13.2%). In exploratory analysis, higher culprit-vessel RWSmax was associated with a shorter index-to-ACS interval (ρ = -0.34; P < 0.001). Overall, 60.4% of patients had ≥2 vessels with RWSmax >12%.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who developed ACS, RWSmax demonstrated marked culprit-vessel predominance despite frequent multivessel elevation, indicating a graded distribution across vessels. These retrospective findings do not establish prospective risk prediction and require validation in unselected populations with event-free controls.

Title: Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement: The TRIPLACE Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transprosthetic gradients are established prognostic markers after left-sided valve interventions, the prognostic significance of discharge tricuspid gradient (dTVG) after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between dTVG and clinical outcomes after TTVR and identify high dTVG determinants.
METHODS: TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement) is an international, multicenter TTVR registry. A discharge landmark analysis was performed, excluding patients with in-hospital mortality, lack of TTVR technical success, missing dTVG, or unavailable follow-up at any time point. Endpoints included all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. The optimal dTVG cutoff was identified through quartile-based survival analysis and confirmed by log-rank maximization. Multivariable Cox models were developed using cross-validated candidate variable selection.
RESULTS: Among 526 patients, 474 were included. Median follow-up was 208.5 days (Q1-Q3: 54-474 days). A data-driven dTVG cutoff of 3.5 mm Hg identified 122 of 474 patients (25.7%) with high dTVG. dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg was associated with higher 1- and 3-year mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.14-3.75; P = 0.017 and HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.24-3.48; P = 0.006, respectively) and composite endpoint events (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.31-3.03; P = 0.001 and HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.33-2.88; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg remained associated with 3-year mortality (adjusted HR: 1.84; 95% CI: 1.09-3.10; P = 0.022) and the composite endpoint at 1 and 3 years (adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.16-2.70; P = 0.009 and adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.20-2.60; P = 0.004, respectively). Indexed inner transcatheter tricuspid valve diameter was the only potentially modifiable independent predictor of high dTVG (OR: 0.79 per 1 mm/m2 increase; 95% CI: 0.71-0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

Title: Incident Acute Myocardial Infarction and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Cancer: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although cancer and acute myocardial infarction (MI) often coexist, the prognostic impact of revascularization for MI in patients with cancer remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aim to evaluate the incidence of MI among patients with cancer and the prognostic impact of revascularization for MI in patients with cancer compared with medical treatment.
METHODS: A retrospective, nationwide, cohort study was conducted using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. A total of 682,030 patients newly diagnosed with cancer from 2016 to 2018 and 682,030 propensity score-matched individuals without cancer were included. The primary outcome was cardiovascular death. The median follow-up was 6 years.
RESULTS: The incidence rates of cardiovascular death were 1,692.4 (95% CI: 1,678.3-1,706.5) per 100,000 person-years in patients with cancer and 796.3 (95% CI: 788.2-804.5) in controls (HRadj: 2.50; 95% CI: 2.47-2.54; P < 0.001). The incidence rates of MI were 156.5 (95% CI: 152.2-160.9) and 191.7 (95% CI: 187.7-195.8) per 100,000 person-years, respectively (HRadj: 0.93; 95% CI: 0.90-0.96; P < 0.001). Cardiovascular outcomes varied across cancer types. Pancreatic, hepatic, lung, and hematologic malignancies were associated with the highest risks of cardiovascular death, whereas an increased risk of acute MI was observed in lung cancer and hematologic malignancy. Among patients with cancer who developed MI, revascularization was associated with lower cardiovascular death than medical treatment alone (HRadj: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.73-0.92; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Although patients with cancer had a higher risk of cardiovascular death than the general population, the observed incidence rate of MI was lower. Even among patients with cancer, revascularization for MI was associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular death than medical treatment alone.

Title: Evaluation of an Echocardiography-Based Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Early HFpEF Detection: A HeartShare/AMP-HF Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to identify because of nonspecific symptoms and subtle echocardiographic abnormalities. EchoGo HF, an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) model, estimates HFpEF probability from a single apical 4-chamber echocardiographic clip, but has been validated only in patients with clinically adjudicated HFpEF.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether AI-HFpEF can detect early HFpEF in community-dwelling adults without a clinical heart failure (HF) diagnosis and predict incident clinical HFpEF in patients within a health system.
METHODS: The authors included 2 community cohorts (the MESA [Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis] Early HF study and the DHMS [Dallas Hearts and Minds Study]). Early HFpEF was defined by impaired exercise capacity or health-related quality of life with objective evidence of elevated cardiac filling pressures in patients without clinically diagnosed HF. The AI-HFpEF model was applied to resting echocardiograms, and the diagnostic performance was assessed. Multivariable models examined associations between AI-HFpEF output and early HFpEF phenotype. Separately, we included adults in the UTSW (University of Texas Southwestern) Health System with structurally normal echocardiograms and no prior HF (2018-2024) and assessed the association of AI-HFpEF output with incident HFpEF (adjudicated using a validated registry) using Cox regression.
RESULTS: In MESA (N = 2,544; 8.3% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF for detecting early HFpEF (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve [AUROC]: 0.77 vs 0.70). AI-HFpEF diagnostic positivity was associated with higher odds of early HFpEF (OR: 3.26; P < 0.001), lower 6-minute walk distance, and lower Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12-Clinical Summary Score. Similarly, in DHMS (N = 624; 18.6% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF (AUROC: 0.83 vs 0.77), and diagnostic positivity was associated with early HFpEF (OR: 6.76; P < 0.001), shorter exercise duration, and lower peak oxygen uptake. In the UTSW cohort (N = 6,876; median follow-up = 33 months; incident HFpEF = 3.4%), an AI-HFpEF diagnostic positive result was associated with >2-fold higher incident HFpEF risk (aHR: 2.08; P < 0.001). This association persisted across all conventional diastolic dysfunction grades.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-HFpEF identified the early HFpEF phenotype in community-dwelling adults and independently predicted incident clinical HFpEF among patients in a health system.

Title: 5.0 T Coronary Magnetic Resonance Angiography in Calcified Coronary Arteries: Diagnostic Performance Compared With Computed Tomography Using Invasive Angiography as Reference.
Journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) often overestimates stenosis in calcified plaques due to blooming artifacts. The performance of 5.0 T Coronary MR angiography (CMRA) in calcified arteries remains unclear.
PURPOSE: To assess plaque effects on 5.0 T CMRA image quality and compare diagnostic performance with CCTA.
STUDY TYPE: Prospective.
POPULATION: Forty-six patients with suspected coronary artery disease.
FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 5.0 T; free-breathing, non-contrast 3D gradient-echo sequence, Dixon water-fat separation, artificial intelligence-assisted compressed sensing.
ASSESSMENT: Three blinded radiologists with 6, 8, and 12 years' experience independently evaluated all datasets. Obstructive stenosis was defined as ≥ 50%; CMRA and CCTA image quality used a 4-point scale; quantitative CMRA measures included vessel edge sharpness (VES), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR). CCTA assessed plaque composition, calcium burden, and calcification length. Invasive angiography was the reference.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Diagnostic metrics and generalized estimating equations evaluated performance and plaque-image-quality associations. Wilcoxon tests compared visual scores. Agreements used Cohen's κ, Fleiss' κ, and intraclass correlation coefficients.
RESULTS: 5.0 T CMRA showed higher specificity (90.1% vs. 77.7%, p < 0.001) and accuracy (89.4% vs. 82.8%, p = 0.006) than CCTA, with similar sensitivity (88.7% vs. 87.7%, p = 0.740). For CMRA, VES was lower in segments containing mixed plaques than in noncalcified or calcified plaques (16.0 ± 0.8 vs. 18.2 ± 0.8 and 18.3 ± 1.0; p < 0.001). Visual scores differed across calcium-burden categories (3.35 ± 0.07, 3.16 ± 0.09, 2.96 ± 0.09, and 2.79 ± 0.09; p < 0.001). Greater calcification length was associated with lower VES (B = -0.152, p = 0.008) and visual scores (B = -0.019, p = 0.019).
DATA CONCLUSION: In this cohort, 5.0 T CMRA showed higher specificity and accuracy than CCTA, with similar sensitivity. Plaque characteristics were associated with selected CMRA image-quality measures.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

Title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year.
RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04864145.

Title: LOW-FLOW NOCTURNAL OXYGEN THERAPY FOR THE TREATMENT OF CENTRAL SLEEP APNEA IN CHRONIC HEART FAILURE: THE PAST, the PRESENT, and the FUTURE.
Abstract: Central sleep apnea (CSA), commonly seen in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fractions (HFrEF), is associated with hypoxia, heightened sympathetic activity, and poor clinical outcomes. While several CSA therapies reduce the apnea-hypopnea index, none have been shown to improve long-term important clinical outcomes. Nocturnal oxygen therapy (NOT) represents a physiologically sound approach to the treatment of CSA. Evidence supports the potential benefits of NOT in such patients, but no proof of its effectiveness on hard outcomes exists. Thus, there has been a longstanding need for a randomized controlled trial of NOT for CSA in HFrEF patients. The ideal trial would establish the rationale for NOT by measuring clinically meaningful outcomes, use rigorous methodologies such as double-blinding and a sham control, and optimize safety by delivering oxygen at doses that ameliorate hypoxemia and avoid hyperoxia. Such a trial (LOFT-HF NCT03745898) was indeed eventually sponsored by the National Institute of Heath and was initiated in 2018-2019. However, the trial was halted during the COVID-19 pandemic due to slow enrollment. Findings were recently published and did not provide a firm conclusion but suggested potential harm in the NOT arm based on a very small number of participants. Meanwhile, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) published recently new treatment guidelines for CSA, suggesting use NOT in CSA. In this article, we attempt to reconcile the LOFT-HF trial findings with existing literature and the new AASM CSA management guidelines and discuss future research needs.

Title: Timing of Cardiac Contractility Modulation Therapy Implementation.
Abstract:
AIMS: Symptomatic chronic heart failure (HF) despite medical treatment can be addressed with cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) therapy, which has yet to have been investigated regarding outcome differences between early versus late implementation.
METHODS AND RESULTS: CCM recipients from the Mannheim Cardiac Contractility Modulation Observational Registry (MAINTAINED) aged ≤ 70 years at implantation were grouped with regard to implantation time after the first diagnosis of CCM indicating HF (New York Heart Association classification (NYHA) ≥ 2 and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) = 25%-45%) into either Early- (EC, n = 50, implantation < 13 months after diagnosis) or Late-Implantation Group (LC, n = 81, implantation ≥ 13 months after diagnosis). Both groups were compared regarding survival, NYHA, LVEF, and HF-related hospitalizations for up to 60 months. The mean implantation time after the first diagnosis were 5.85 ± 3.1 versus 92 ± 70.2 months (first values EC, p < 0.05). Mean survival was better for EC (55.2 ± 1.7 vs. 52.8 ± 1.6 months, p < 0.05). Improvements in NYHA (2.98 ± 0.47 to 2.0 ± 0.73 vs. 3.01 ± 0.46 to 2.25 ± 0.8, both p < 0.05) and LVEF (23.2 ± 7.5 to ± 38.82 ± 12.85 vs. 23.9 ± 7 to 29.92 ± 8.9%, each p < 0.05) were comparable, with differences in terms of grouping. Hospitalizations due to HF were more frequent to LC patients (39 vs. 110 events, Odds Ratio 2.1).
CONCLUSIONS: Heart failure patients might experience improvements in functional status and left ventricular reverse remodeling following CCM therapy, regardless of the timing of implantation. Early implementation of CCM within the first year of CCM suitable HF might provide additional benefits regarding survival, left ventricular systolic recovery and protection against heart failure hospitalizations.

Title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Predicts Recurrent Myocardial Infarction in Diabetic Patients Following Acute Coronary Syndromes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who experience acute coronary syndromes (ACS) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events despite secondary prevention. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] contributes to residual cardiovascular risk, but its prognostic impact on recurrent myocardial infarction (MI) and repeat revascularization in diabetic patients after ACS or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that elevated Lp(a) is associated with increased risk of recurrent MI and repeat coronary revascularization in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, EBSCOhost, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies evaluating Lp(a) and recurrent cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI. Observational studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were included. Pooled HRs were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Seven studies comprising 7887 patients with diabetes and prior ACS or PCI were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with increased risk of recurrent MI (pooled HR 2.17, 95% CI 1.02-4.62; I2 = 75%) but not repeat coronary revascularization (pooled HR 1.68, 95% CI 0.79-3.57; I2 = 78%).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with increased risk of recurrent MI in patients with diabetes after ACS or PCI. Findings should be interpreted considering the observational study designs, substantial heterogeneity, and limited evidence for repeat revascularization. These findings support Lp(a) as a contributor to residual cardiovascular risk and its potential role in post-ACS risk stratification.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420261296821).

Title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Model Integrating Chest CT and Cardiac Ultrasound for the Auxiliary Diagnosis of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by elevated pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular dysfunction. Conventional imaging modalities, chest computed tomography (CT) and cardiac ultrasound (echocardiography), provide complementary structural and functional information but exhibit incomplete sensitivity and specificity when used alone. This study aimed to evaluate a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model integrating chest CT and cardiac ultrasound for auxiliary PAH diagnosis, benchmarked against right heart catheterization (RHC) as the reference standard. A retrospective observational study was conducted on 100 patients (mean age 52.6 ± 15.2 years; 56% female) with suspected PAH between January 2020 and December 2024. Each underwent high-resolution chest CT, transthoracic echocardiography, and RHC within a 2-week interval. Imaging-derived structural and functional features were integrated within an attention-based multimodal AI framework. Diagnostic metrics were calculated for chest CT, cardiac ultrasound, and multimodal AI against the archived RHC clinical classification. The multimodal AI system achieved sensitivity of 92.2%, specificity of 88.9%, accuracy of 91.0%, and AUC of 0.930, compared with CT (sensitivity 84.4%, specificity 80.6%, accuracy 83.0%, AUC 0.860) and echocardiography (sensitivity 79.7%, specificity 77.8%, accuracy 79.0%, AUC 0.840). McNemar tests of paired binary classifications favored AI over CT (p = 0.0078) and echocardiography (p = 0.00049). Exploratory subgroup analyses were performed for borderline pulmonary artery diameter and connective tissue disease. The multimodal approach showed improved overall discrimination in this internal retrospective evaluation and should be considered an auxiliary, noninvasive tool that requires external prospective validation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Video-Audio Media; Observational Study

Title: A Pilot Retrospective Electronic Health Record Workflow for Evaluating Adjunctive Danshen Injection After Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Danshen injection is used as an adjunctive cardiovascular therapy in some Chinese hospitals, but retrospective evaluations are vulnerable to exposure misclassification, nonuniform measurement timing, baseline imbalance, complete-case selection, and time-related bias. This article presents an audit-ready electronic health record workflow for adults with acute myocardial infarction who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention and received inpatient aspirin plus clopidogrel. The workflow adds TCM-specific fields for syndrome differentiation, indication, prescriber specialty, product formulation, and administration timing; separates outcome-specific analysis sets; and defines propensity-score overlap weighting for the population with clinical equipoise. An archived 89-patient cohort (45 with documented Danshen administration and 44 controls) illustrates the analytical sequence. In the archived file, only analysis-file checks, model fitting, balance diagnostics, bootstrap estimation, and visualization could be executed. Source-record steps requiring unrecovered treatment timestamps, echocardiographic metadata, assay boundaries, exact exclusion variables, or adjudicated events are presented as workflow specifications and were not treated as completed procedures. The groups were strongly imbalanced at baseline. In the primary ANCOVA using HC3 standard errors, the adjusted between-group difference in pre-discharge left ventricular ejection fraction was 6.82 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 4.54-9.10). The separate overlap-weighted estimate was 6.95 percentage points (patient-level bootstrap standard error: 1.08; 95% percentile confidence interval: 4.90-9.07; 2,000 resamples). These estimates are numerical demonstrations rather than causal treatment effects. Database-coded cardiovascular and bleeding indicators were excluded because component events, dates, follow-up completeness, and a common time origin could not be verified. The workflow has not been externally validated and should be considered a pilot demonstration.

Title: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomics with Tissue Validation Prioritizes MMP1 in Diabetic Foot Ulcer.
Abstract: Cellular sources of reproducible transcriptomic changes in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated differential-expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) gene screening, exploratory machine-learning feature selection, two external bulk-transcriptomic datasets, single-cell analysis, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) network analysis, and patient-tissue quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and western blotting. In GSE199939 (10 DFU and 11 control samples), 3,691 differentially expressed genes were identified, and the WGCNA blue module was strongly associated with DFU (r = 0.97, p = 5 × 10-13). Intersecting the differentially expressed genes, blue-module hub genes, and 1,062 DPN-related genes yielded 77 candidates. CCL7, CHEK1, MKI67, MMP1, MMP13, and TRPV2 were supported by at least two feature-selection methods; complete separation in support vector machine recursive feature elimination raised concerns about discovery-cohort overfitting. MMP1 showed the largest discovery-cohort expression change (log2 fold change = 9.854; adjusted p = 1.24 × 10-29). In the merged GSE68183/GSE80178 matrix, MMP1 had an adjusted p of 0.0159 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.981. In GSE134431, MMP1 expression was nominally higher in DFU than in non-ulcerated diabetic foot skin (p = 0.0225; adjusted p = 0.135; AUC = 0.808). Analysis of 69,944 cells from 24 samples showed the highest mean MMP1 expression in fibroblasts, with higher sample-level expression in DFU fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and endothelial cells. Patient-tissue assays showed higher MMP1 mRNA abundance in four matched pairs (paired test on ΔCq, p = 3.04 × 10-5) and higher protein abundance in three matched pairs (paired p = 0.0107). Statistical replication was incomplete. Findings suggest a fibroblast-centered matrix-remodeling association, subject to limitations from transcripts per million (TPM) input in count-based discovery analysis, incomplete single-cell preprocessing records, and small tissue-assay cohorts. Causality and clinical utility remain unestablished.

Title: CPR training, educational attitudes, and resuscitation ethics in northern Greece: a cross-sectional questionnaire study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bystander response to cardiac arrest is linked to cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, confidence and access to education. Resuscitation also raises ethical questions about when CPR should be withheld and how new treatments should be studied.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study in Thessaloniki, Greece, from January to March 2026. The questionnaire was administered electronically and on paper to health-sciences students/professionals and non-health-sciences respondents. Descriptive, comparative and multivariable regression analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among 1,271 respondents, 1,264 had known health-sciences status; 89.8% reported CPR awareness and 33.6% previous training. Health-sciences status was associated with training (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 5.15, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.95-6.76). Among trained respondents, 345/418 (82.5%) answered all three basic-response items correctly; higher confidence was associated with this endpoint (aOR 1.47, 95% CI 1.08-2.00). Among untrained respondents, 509/775 (65.7%) intended training and 440/746 (59.0%) both intended training and reported access barriers. Greater perceived ethical acceptability was associated with willingness to be randomized (aOR 5.98, 95% CI 4.69-7.61).
CONCLUSIONS: In this regional sample, high CPR awareness contrasted with less frequent training. Varied ethical attitudes suggest communication priorities.

Title: Standalone Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization Versus Surgical Evacuation for Nontraumatic Subdural Hematoma: A Propensity-Matched Multicenter Real-World Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to compare real-world outcomes after standalone middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) versus surgical evacuation among adults with inpatient International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM)-coded nontraumatic subdural hematoma.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective propensity-matched cohort study using TriNetX Global Collaborative Network reports. Adults aged 18 years or older with inpatient ICD-10-CM-coded nontraumatic subdural hemorrhage were assigned to standalone MMAE or surgical evacuation if the qualifying procedure occurred within one month of diagnosis. Patients were matched 1:1 on demographic, cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, hepatic, metabolic, substance use, medication, and laboratory variables. For outcome analyses, the qualifying intervention served as the analytic index event, with follow-up beginning on day 1 after the procedure. Outcomes were all-cause mortality, incident seizure disorder, and ischemic stroke assessed through 3, 6, and 12 months after the qualifying intervention.
RESULTS: After matching, 2,156 patients were included in each cohort.
