All-cause mortality did not differ significantly at 3 months (245/2,156 (11.4%) vs 283/2,156 (13.1%); risk difference (RD), -1.8%; p=0.08), 6 months (308/2,156 (14.3%) vs 327/2,156 (15.2%); RD, -0.9%; p=0.41), or 12 months (354/2,156 (16.4%) vs 377/2,156 (17.5%); RD, -1.1%; p=0.35). Incident seizures were less frequent after MMAE at 3 months (63/1,888 (3.3%) vs 106/1,798 (5.9%)), 6 months (79/1,888 (4.2%) vs 136/1,798 (7.6%)), and 12 months (97/1,888 (5.1%) vs 157/1,798 (8.7%); all p<0.001); however, this association was not statistically significant in the age >65 years sensitivity analysis. Ischemic stroke risk did not differ significantly at 3 months (90/1,692 (5.3%) vs 81/1,731 (4.7%)), 6 months (103/1,692 (6.1%) vs 97/1,731 (5.6%)), or 12 months (115/1,692 (6.8%) vs 111/1,731 (6.4%)).
CONCLUSIONS: In this propensity-matched real-world cohort, standalone MMAE was associated with similar mortality and ischemic stroke risk compared with surgical evacuation. Lower incident seizure risk was observed after MMAE in the primary analysis, but this association was not preserved in the age >65 years sensitivity analysis and should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating. These findings support prospective evaluation in selected patients and should not be interpreted as evidence that MMAE replaces urgent surgical decompression.

Title: Discriminatory power of organ-specific Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores: Predictors of maternal mortality in obstetric intensive care units (ICU).
Journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critically ill obstetric patients in intensive care units (ICUs) present unique challenges, and maternal mortality remains a major concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, though widely used in general ICUs, has not been adequately studied for its organ-specific discriminatory power in predicting maternal mortality. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic accuracy of individual organ SOFA sub-scores to improve risk stratification in obstetric critical care.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted over one year in the obstetric ICU of a tertiary center in Northern India. A total of 125 obstetric patients (pregnant or within 42 days postpartum) were enrolled. SOFA sub-scores for respiratory, cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, coagulation, and neurological systems were calculated on admission and throughout ICU stay. Patients were classified into survivors and non-survivors. Associations between individual organ dysfunction and maternal mortality were assessed. Discriminatory accuracy of organ-specific SOFA scores was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
RESULTS: Mortality increased proportionally with the number of dysfunctional organs (χ² =39.693; P < 0.001). Escalating organ-specific SOFA scores were significantly associated with maternal mortality. ROC analysis revealed that cardiovascular dysfunction had the highest predictive accuracy (area under the curve [AUC] =0.875), followed by hepatic (AUC = 0.808), respiratory (AUC = 0.804), hematological (AUC = 0.763), and renal (AUC = 0.757) dysfunction.
CONCLUSION: Cardiovascular, hepatic, and respiratory SOFA sub-scores provide strong discriminatory power for predicting maternal mortality in Obstetric ICU patients. Incorporating organ-specific SOFA assessments may enhance early risk stratification and guide life-saving interventions in resource-limited settings.

Title: Tissue Doppler S wave velocities are associated with changes in pro-brain natriuretic peptide levels following transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an effective treatment for severe aortic stenosis. Despite its efficacy, TAVI carries risks of complications in elderly patients. Prior research indicates that failure to reduce NTproBNP levels post-TAVI increases the risk of mortality and recurrent hospitalizations. The tissue Doppler S wave is an index of longitudinal left ventricular function which may predict poor outcomes following TAVI.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to examine whether pre-TAVI S wave velocities are associated with hemodynamic response to TAVI as assessed by changes in NTproBNP levels.
METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled patients scheduled for elective TAVI who underwent echocardiographic evaluation including TDI S wave measurements. Blood levels of NTproBNP were assessed both before and 3 months after the procedure. Subjects were defined as responders or non-responders (NR) with response defined as a ≥ 30% reduction in NTproBNP levels post-procedure.
RESULTS: 185 subjects (mean age 79 ± 9 yrs., 47% male) were included in the study. Response to TAVI was observed in 78 (42%) of the cohort. The NR group had a significantly higher incidence of hypertension (62.3% vs. 37.7%, P = 0.017). Median S wave was 6.96 (3.8-13.7) cm/s in the responders and 5.88 (3.77-12.1) cm/s in the NR (p = 0.001), a finding which remained significant on multivariate analysis (p = 0.004; OR 1.31 95%CI 1.09-1.59).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that for the first time that the TDI S wave is a significant predictor of NTproBNP reduction following TAVI. Further research is needed to validate these results in larger populations.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and statin indications in low-risk patients based on the 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Though elevated lipoprotein (a) (Lp[a]) is associated with ASCVD and testing is recommended for all adults, how to use Lp(a) for decision-making in low-risk patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: We studied low-risk adults in a large healthcare system, excluding those on statins or with statin indications in the 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline. ASCVD risk and statin eligibility were estimated using the PREVENT equations, incorporating Lp(a) using a calculation proposed by the AHA: ASCVD risk x (1.11^[(Lp[a] in nmol/L)/50]). Measured Lp(a) was used when available, and imputed values were used for all other adults.
RESULTS: The cohort included 124 low-risk patients with measured Lp(a) (median [25th-75th percentile] age 44 [38-50] years; 64.5% women) and 28,527 without Lp(a) (median age 42 [36-49] years, 73.3% women). Adding Lp(a) to 10-year risk equations made 3.3% of patients with measured Lp(a) ≥125 nmol/L and 0.1% with imputed Lp(a) of 125 nmol/L newly statin eligible. Eligibility rose with older age, higher Lp(a), and higher ASCVD risk. When Lp(a) was added to 30-year risk in exploratory analyses, 20.2% with measured Lp(a) and 19.6% with imputed Lp(a) of 125 nmol/L met statin eligibility, and 70.0-84.6% (measured cohort) and 33.1-54.2% (imputed cohort) at the highest Lp(a) quintile met eligibility as age increased.
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating Lp(a) into ASCVD risk equations changes predicted risk and potential statin eligibility in low-risk adults not indicated for therapy under current guidelines. Including Lp(a) in risk estimation and clinical decision-making, particularly for patients with elevated levels, could be considered in patients with low ASCVD risk.

Title: Heart Failure Care and Post-Hospital Outcomes in Northwestern Tanzania.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Africa, heart failure (HF) mortality is the highest in the world; approximately 50% of patients die within one year of HF hospitalization. Little is known about the quality of inpatient and post-discharge care and its association with patient outcomes. The purpose of this study is to describe HF outcomes for patients admitted in Northwestern Tanzania and evaluate associations between gaps in quality care and post-hospital survival.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of all adult patients admitted with HF at Bugando Medical Centre in 2023. We abstracted data from the index hospitalization and subsequent encounters until August 31, 2025. Vital status was ascertained by telephone. We characterized post-discharge outcomes and adherence to guideline recommendations for HF care. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations between gaps in quality measures and mortality.
RESULTS: Among 177 patients admitted with HF, 23 (13%) died during the index hospitalization. Of the 154 patients alive at discharge, 63 (40.9%) died within six months and 86 (56%) within a year. Among patients alive at discharge, 79% received indicated testing, 50% were on guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) at discharge, 68% attended the first post-discharge appointment, 53% received ongoing care three months post-discharge, and 39% were on GDMT three months post-discharge. Attending the first post-discharge visit (aHR 0.32 [95% CI: 0.17, 0.63]) and remaining in care three months after discharge (aHR 0.36 [95% CI: 0.16, 0.81]) were both independently associated with improved survival. GDMT use was low across outpatient visits (47%), with frequent medication changes and de-escalation over time.
CONCLUSIONS: Mortality following HF admission in Northwestern Tanzania remains high. Factors associated with post-hospital mortality may include poor linkage to post-discharge care and low sustained care engagement. Implementation research is needed to develop strategies to improve post-discharge HF outcomes in East Africa, focusing on optimizing GDMT before discharge and improving early post-hospital linkage to care.
LAY SUMMARY: Heart failure (HF) mortality in sub-Saharan Africa is the highest in the world, yet little is known about the quality of HF care provided during and after HF hospitalization and its relationship to post-hospital outcomes. This study seeks to understand the quality of care provided to patients admitted with HF in Northwestern Tanzania and its association with post-hospital outcomes.This study took place at Bugando Medical Centre, a large academic regional referral hospital in Mwanza, Tanzania that serves a catchment population of ~22 million people. Among 177 patients admitted with HF in 2023, there was a trend of high, early mortality following hospital discharge. Among the 154 patients who survived and were discharged, we found significant gaps in linkage to care after hospitalization, sustained retention in care, and utilization of guideline-directed medical therapy at discharge and in the outpatient setting. Linkage to care and retention in care were each independently associated with significant improvements in survival.There is a pressing need for future studies focused on understanding and addressing factors associated with post-hospital care engagement and utilization of guideline-directed medical therapy after HF hospitalization in East Africa.

Title: Barriers and Enablers to Guideline-Directed Prescribing for Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multi-Stakeholder Qualitative Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality despite effective treatments. Guideline-directed medical therapy, commonly referred to as quadruple therapy, reduces mortality and hospitalisation; however, uptake and dose optimisation remain suboptimal across Asia, including Singapore. This study explores barriers and enablers influencing prescribing and titration practices in a multi-ethnic Asian setting.
METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 38 healthcare providers from seven public healthcare institutions in Singapore, including cardiologists, clinicians from relevant subspecialties, nurses, and pharmacists. The study was informed by the Cabana framework, and data were analysed using an inductive-deductive approach.
RESULTS: Guideline awareness was generally high, but confidence in initiating and up-titrating therapy varied. Attitudinal barriers included perceived gaps between clinical trial evidence and the realities of managing diverse patient populations, safety concerns in multi-morbid patients, clinical inertia, challenges related to professional boundaries, and limited confidence among junior staff. Nonetheless, guidelines were perceived as enablers, providing a shared framework that promotes standardised care. Prescribing behaviour was shaped by patient-related factors including financial constraints, limited health literacy, cultural preferences for traditional medicines, and treatment outcomes. Organisational barriers included limited access to specialist follow-up, rotating inpatient teams, formulary gaps in primary care, and fragmented medical records. Multidisciplinary nurse- or pharmacist-led titration clinics with specialist support were a key institutional enabler.
CONCLUSIONS: To narrow the guideline-practice gap, targeted toolkits and specialist support are needed to address concerns and build staff confidence. A culture of reviewing quadruple therapy prescription at discharge and during follow-up should be supported. Prescribing patterns should be monitored and reflected in real-time, and patient adherence strengthened through dedicated heart failure nurses or case managers. Telehealth or primary care-based services, increased government support for healthcare information integration, and increased financial support for patients are necessary.
LAY SUMMARY: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is a serious medical condition that can lead to frequent hospital admissions and premature death. Clinical guidelines strongly recommend the use of four classes of evidence-based medicines, commonly known as quadruple therapy, because they can significantly improve survival and reduce hospitalisation. Despite guideline endorsement, real-world uptake and dose optimisation of quadruple therapy remains suboptimal globally.Studies on implementation barriers in adhering to the guideline recommendations for quadruple therapy have focused mainly on physicians. This study provides one of the first multi-institutional qualitative accounts of barriers and enablers in prescribing quadruple therapy or guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure patients in Singapore, exploring the views of all three frontline healthcare professional groups-doctors, nurses, and pharmacists.We found that the prescription of quadruple therapy was negatively influenced by a perceived gap between clinical trial evidence and the realities of managing diverse patient populations-particularly older and multimorbid patients-alongside interprofessional relationships and limited confidence among junior staff. Health care providers' prescribing behaviour was shaped by patient-related factors, including financial constraints, limited health literacy, and cultural preferences for traditional medicines.Limited specialist follow-up, fragmented health records, and formulary gaps in primary care hinder implementation, while positive patient outcomes and multidisciplinary care models act as enablers in adhering to guideline recommendations.The study adds context-specific implementation insights by identifying individual, organisational, and system-level factors. Specialist-supported nurse- or pharmacist-led services, primary care-based medication titration, clearer task-sharing pathways, improved decision tools, and better health information integration may enhance guideline implementation.

Title: The associations between healthful and unhealthful plant-based dietary patterns and all-cause mortality among older Chinese adults with data-adapted early-stage cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (stages 0-2): a prospective cohort study from the CLHLS.
Abstract:
AIMS: To examine the associations of the overall plant-based diet index (PDI), healthful plant-based diet index (hPDI), and unhealthful plant-based diet index (uPDI) with all-cause mortality in older Chinese adults with data-adapted early-stage cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome (stages 0-2).
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed data from 5,872 participants aged ≥65 years from the 2008 wave of the China Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) with data-adapted CKM stages 0-2 and no prevalent cardiovascular disease. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Mortality was ascertained through March 2019. Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analyses were used. During a median follow-up of 108 months, 2,870 deaths occurred. In multivariable-adjusted models, each 1-point increase in hPDI was associated with a 1.1% lower mortality risk (HR = 0.989, 95% CI: 0.982-0.995; p < 0.001), whereas each 1-point increase in uPDI was associated with a 1.2% higher mortality risk (HR = 1.012, 95% CI: 1.006-1.019; p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest hPDI quartile had a 13.2% lower mortality risk (HR = 0.868, 95% CI: 0.783-0.961), and the highest uPDI quartile had a 19.2% higher risk (HR = 1.192, 95% CI: 1.060-1.340). Stratified estimates suggested numerically stronger associations in CKM stages 1-2 than in stage 0; however, formal interaction tests did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.062 for hPDI and p = 0.824 for uPDI), indicating limited evidence of effect modification.
CONCLUSION: Higher adherence to a healthful plant-based diet was associated with lower all-cause mortality, whereas higher adherence to an unhealthful plant-based diet was associated with higher mortality among older Chinese adults with data-adapted early-stage CKM syndrome. The overall PDI was not independently associated with mortality after adjustment, underscoring that plant-based dietary quality, rather than plant-based eating per se, is the relevant exposure.

Title: Prognostic value of pre- and post-procedural TAPSE/PASP ratio for long-term mortality in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction < 50% undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE)/pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) ratio reflects right ventricular-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) coupling and has prognostic value in heart failure and pulmonary hypertension. Its significance in patients with low ejection fraction (LVEF < 50%) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains unclear.
AIM: This study aimed to investigate the association between pre-procedural TAPSE/PASP ratio and long-term all-cause mortality and to determine whether post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP ratio assessed at discharge was associated with subsequent mortality in patients with severe AS and LVEF < 50%.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 225 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI (2015-2025). TAPSE/PASP was measured at baseline and discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality, analyzed using multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1161 days, 102 (45.3%) patients died. Post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP was significantly higher in survivors (0.56 ±0.20 vs. 0.48 ±0.16 mm/mm Hg, p = 0.005) and was independently associated with long-term mortality (HR = 0.74 per 0.1 mm/mm Hg increase; 95% CI: 0.55-0.99; p = 0.04). Pre-TAVI TAPSE/PASP showed a borderline, non-significant association with mortality. Patients with post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP < 0.514 mm/mm Hg had significantly worse 5-year survival (log-rank p = 0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: In severe aortic stenosis with LVEF < 50%, post-TAVI TAPSE/PASP at discharge was independently associated with long-term mortality. The findings suggest that assessment of RV-PA coupling after TAVI may provide additional prognostic information, although the clinical utility of the proposed threshold requires prospective validation.

Title: Changes in the institutional treatment of severe aortic stenosis following the introduction of transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has transformed the treatment of severe aortic stenosis.
AIM: To investigate the association of TAVI introduction on institutional volume and characteristics of patients treated for aortic stenosis either by surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) or TAVI.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A single-centre retrospective observational study of consecutive patients treated only with SAVR (SAVR-only period, 2004-2017) and with either SAVR or TAVI (SAVR + TAVI period, 2017-2025).
RESULTS: During the SAVR-only period, 1011 patients underwent SAVR, and during the SAVR + TAVI period, 685 patients underwent SAVR and 824 underwent TAVI. The total number of aortic valve interventions increased annually by 9% (95% CI: 1.08-1.10; p < 0.001), while SAVR decreased by 15% during the SAVR + TAVI period (95% CI: 0.82-0.89; p < 0.001). Cumulative 30-day mortality was 2.8% during the SAVR-only period and 1.5% during the SAVR + TAVI period (p = 0.021). Patients undergoing SAVR during the SAVR + TAVI period were younger (68 vs. 70 years; p < 0.001), had a lower Logistic EuroSCORE (4.52 vs. 6.33; p < 0.001) and less often underwent concomitant revascularization (29% vs. 35%; p = 0.013). Patients undergoing TAVI compared to SAVR were older (80 vs. 68 years; p < 0.001), had a higher Logistic EuroSCORE (11.39 vs. 4.52; p < 0.001), and had comparable 30-day mortality (1.0% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.083). The difference in 5-year mortality in favour of SAVR (13.8% vs. 27.4%) was not significant after adjustment for age, sex and Logistic EuroSCORE (HR = 0.794; 95% CI: 0.550-1.147; p = 0.22).
CONCLUSIONS: Introduction of TAVI was associated with increased institutional volume of aortic valve interventions despite a concomitant decrease in the number of SAVR procedures. TAVI appears to have expanded treatment to previously undertreated high-risk elderly patients while also being used in a sizable proportion of patients who previously underwent SAVR.

Title: Prognostic value of preprocedural neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio for in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced ejection fraction undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) represent a particularly vulnerable subgroup with elevated perioperative and long-term mortality. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), an integrated marker of systemic inflammation and nutritional status, has not been specifically evaluated as a prognostic marker in this population.
AIM: To examine the prognostic value of preprocedural NPAR for in-hospital and overall (all-cause) mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study enrolled 169 consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis and LVEF < 50% undergoing TAVI between June 2020 and January 2026. Preprocedural NPAR was derived from blood samples obtained within 24 h before the procedure. In-hospital and overall mortality were assessed using logistic and Cox regression models with limited covariate adjustment.
RESULTS: Using an NPAR cut-off of 20.74, patients with elevated NPAR exhibited higher rates of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and both in-hospital and overall mortality, along with higher C-reactive protein and BNP levels and lower haemoglobin, albumin, postprocedural LVEF, and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) values. NPAR remained associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for chronic kidney disease or TAPSE and was also associated with overall mortality in multivariable Cox regression analyses. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly reduced survival among patients with elevated NPAR.
CONCLUSIONS: After limited multivariable adjustment, preprocedural NPAR was associated with both in-hospital and overall mortality in patients with reduced LVEF undergoing TAVI. As a simple marker of inflammatory and nutritional burden, NPAR may provide additional prognostic information and complement preprocedural risk assessment, although its incremental value beyond established risk models and other biomarkers remains uncertain.

Title: Sex- and age-specific trends in prescription medication use, 2005-2025: a nationwide repeated cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have documented higher medication consumption among females than males; however contemporary sex-based differences across age and therapeutic classes remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We used the Danish National Prescription Registry to identify all prescriptions redeemed by Danish adults in 2005, 2015 and 2025, assessing overall medication use by sex and age. For the 30 most prescribed therapeutic classes, age-adjusted rate ratios (aRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated to compare use between sexes. Polypharmacy (≥ five medications redeemed within a calendar year) was also assessed by sex and age groups.
FINDINGS: In 2025, females accounted for 52% of total medication consumption (1.98 billion Defined Daily Doses (DDDs) among females vs. 3.82 billion DDDs overall), down from 60% (1.17 billion vs. 1.96 billion DDDs) in 2005. This female excess was confined to early adulthood; from age 55 onward, male consumption exceeded that of females. While some of the higher medication use reflected a higher prevalence of certain conditions among females (e.g., thyroid disorders, osteoporosis, depression), females also exhibited a higher use of mental health medications, including antipsychotics, and, newly in 2025, ADHD medications (aRR 1.25; 95%CI 1.16-1.34). Males more frequently used cardiovascular therapies (antithrombotic agents (0.64; 0.62-0.66), insulins (0.67; 0.65-0.69)). However, the historical male cardiovascular predominance was challenged in 2025: thiazide diuretics (1.19; 1.16-1.22) and non-insulin glucose-lowering drugs were more prescribed to females (1.08; 1.01-1.16). Polypharmacy was more common among females in early adulthood but converged after age 65.
INTERPRETATION: Sex-based differences in overall medication use have narrowed over time. There is a need for continued monitoring of persistent and emerging sex differences in prescribing.
FUNDING: No specific funding.

Title: Non-inferiority of a paclitaxel-coated balloon versus a rapamycin-eluting metal stent for de novo non-complex small coronary vessel disease: a prospective randomized controlled trial.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While drug-coated balloons (DCB) have demonstrated efficacy for coronary small vessel disease, comparative data between DCB and drug-eluting stents (DES) in de novo coronary lesions remain limited.
AIM: This study hypothesized that a DCB-only strategy would be non-inferior to DES for angiographic outcomes in de novo small vessel coronary lesions.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 228 patients with de novo (≥ 70% stenosis), non-complex coronary lesions from January 2022 to January 2024. Participants were randomized 1 : 1 to paclitaxel-coated balloon or rapamycin-eluting stent (DES). The primary endpoint was late lumen loss (LLL) at 6 and 12 months post-procedure, with a non-inferiority margin of 0.15 mm. Baseline clinical characteristics were compared between groups, with 12-month follow-up assessments including cardiac function, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), post-procedural angina, and bleeding events. Quantitative coronary angiography was used to evaluate minimal lumen diameter, percent stenosis, and LLL. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to assess cumulative survival rates.
RESULTS: Baseline clinical characteristics were similar between groups (p > 0.05). The DCB group had more Mehran Type I lesions (p < 0.05). Both groups reduced thrombogenic potential (p < 0.05). There were no significant differences in angiographic outcomes, MACE, or BARC ≥ 3 bleeding (p > 0.05). At 6 and 12 months, the 95% CI upper limits for LLL difference were below 0.15 mm (p for non-inferiority < 0.001). DCB had lower post-procedural angina frequency (p < 0.05) but similar episode duration. Survival rates did not differ significantly (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: For de novo, non-complex small coronary vessel disease, DCB monotherapy demonstrates comparable long-term efficacy to DES, meeting non-inferiority criteria.

Title: Real-world comparative effectiveness and safety of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation.
Journal: International journal of cardiology. Cardiovascular risk and prevention
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs), either vitamin K antagonists or direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), are essential for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF). However, comparative real-world evidence among DOACs in upper-middle-income settings remains inconsistent. This study compared the effectiveness and safety of DOACs with warfarin in reducing stroke or systemic embolism (SSE), major bleeding, and all-cause mortality in patients with AF.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with non-valvular AF newly prescribed OACs between 2010 and 2021 using the Ramathibodi Hospital database. Inverse probability weighting (IPW) was applied to balance baseline covariates and emulate a RCT. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using IPW-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among 5580 patients, 4237 received warfarin, 414 dabigatran, 428 rivaroxaban, 413 apixaban, and 88 edoxaban. Compared with warfarin, apixaban (HR 0.35; 95% CI 0.18, 0.67) was associated with significantly lower risks of SSE. Dabigatran (HR 0.43; 95% CI 0.23, 0.81) and rivaroxaban (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.25, 0.90) significantly reduced the major bleeding risk. No DOAC was associated with reduced all-cause mortality. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings.
CONCLUSION: Apixaban showed the most favorable profile with significant reductions in SSE and trend toward lower major bleeding compared with warfarin, supporting its preferential use for stroke prevention in this setting.

Title: Technical failure patterns during chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention: a multicenter registry analysis.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Technical failure during chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is usually reported as a binary outcome, although failed procedures may follow different procedural courses.
AIM: To describe procedural patterns of technical failure during CTO PCI and assess their association with conventional CTO complexity scores.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We analyzed 2,375 CTO PCI procedures from a multicenter registry. Technical failure was classified as Pattern A (crossing- or device-delivery failure) or Pattern B (dissection- or flow-related failure). Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine correlates of overall and pattern-specific failure.
RESULTS: Technical failure occurred in 192 (8.1%) procedures: 148 (77.1%) were Pattern A and 44 (22.9%) were Pattern B. J-CTO and CASTLE/EuroCTO scores were higher in Pattern A than in Pattern B. Overall technical failure was associated with blunt/absent proximal cap, CTO length ≥ 30 mm, moderate/severe calcification, previous coronary artery bypass grafting, and proximal tortuosity. In the exploratory Pattern B model, CTO length ≥ 30 mm, moderate/severe calcification, and left anterior descending versus right coronary artery target vessel were associated with Pattern B versus technical success. However, target vessel did not differentiate Pattern B from Pattern A after adjustment for J-CTO or CASTLE/EuroCTO score. Pattern B consisted mainly of persistent dissection and no/slow flow.
CONCLUSIONS: Technical failure during CTO PCI is heterogeneous. Conventional CTO complexity scores appeared to align more closely with crossing- or device-delivery failure, while dissection- or flow-related failure remained a smaller exploratory subgroup requiring external validation.

Title: Association between fibrosis-4 index and 30-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients hospitalised with acute heart failure: a retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Fibrosis-4 index (Fib-4), a non-invasive liver fibrosis biomarker, is increasingly linked to cardiovascular risk, but its role in acute heart failure (AHF) remains unclear.
AIM: We evaluated its association with 30-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with AHF.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled 1535 ICU patients with AHF from the MIMIC-IV database. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality within 30 days from the date of hospital admission. Baseline characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory data, and clinical information were extracted. Patients were divided into survival and mortality groups, and baseline differences were compared. Lasso regression identified variables influencing prognosis, which were then included in a restricted cubic splines (RCS) model. Three multivariable logistic regression models (Model 1 unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for INR, age, BUN, and potassium; Model 3 fully adjusted for pO2 max, WBC, lymphocytes, BUN, calcium, glucose, anion gap, potassium, INR, ALP, CRRT, CK-MB, age, peripheral vascular disease, and CHA2DS2-VASc score) were constructed. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis assessed the predictive performance of Fib-4. Subgroup analysis evaluated potential differences across population subgroups. Sensitivity analyses using complete-case analysis and multiple imputation were performed to address missing data.
RESULTS: The mortality group (n = 219, 14.3%) exhibited significantly higher Fib-4 values than the survival group (n = 1316). Lasso regression identified 16 variables influencing prognosis, including Fib-4. RCS analysis showed a positive correlation between Fib-4 and 30-day mortality risk (p-overall = 0.006, p-nonlinear = 0.330). After adjustment for confounders, logistic regression demonstrated that Fib-4 was an independent risk factor (Model 1: OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.07-1.13, p < 0.001; Model 2: OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.05-1.11, p < 0.001; Model 3: OR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.09, p = 0.002). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for Fib-4 predicting 30-day mortality was 0.665, indicating modest predictive value. The optimal cutoff was 2.25 (sensitivity 74.0%, specificity 51.4%). Quartile analysis showed a dose-response relationship (Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.28-4.92, p = 0.007 in Model 3). Subgroup analyses revealed no significant interaction. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings.
CONCLUSIONS: In critically ill patients with AHF, the Fib-4 index is independently associated with 30-day mortality but provides only modest predictive discrimination. This readily available, cost-effective marker may offer adjunctive information for early risk stratification, but its clinical utility should be interpreted with caution given the limited AUC.

Title: Identifying Iron Deficiency and Opportunities for IV Iron Supplementation in Patients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: The Canadian journal of hospital pharmacy
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the AFFIRM-AHF trial, IV administration of iron reduced total hospitalizations due to heart failure in patients with acute heart failure and iron deficiency.
OBJECTIVES: To identify what proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) had iron deficiency and to compare their rate of hospitalization due to heart failure with that of patients in the AFFIRM-AHF trial.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study involved patients with HFrEF seen at a specialized heart failure clinic. Data were collected between February 2021 and August 2022. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with iron deficiency, with comparison of the rate of hospitalization due to heart failure in this study relative to the AFFIRM-AHF trial.
RESULTS: A total of 284 patients were screened to generate the pre-specified sample of 100. Of these, 73% had iron deficiency. After clinic attachment, the rate of hospitalization due to heart failure among patients with iron deficiency was 21.6 per 100 patient-years, compared with 43.2 in the AFFIRM-AHF trial.
CONCLUSIONS: Although more than two-thirds of patients with HFrEF in the study clinic had iron deficiency, their rate of hospitalization due to heart failure was markedly lower than that reported in the AFFIRM-AHF trial. Therefore, the need for routine IV iron repletion in these patients is questionable.

Title: Scoping Review of Predictors and Risk Factors for Acute Myocardial Infarction in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease : Short title: Acute Myocardial Infarction in Patients with CKD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) significantly elevates the risk of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and associated mortality, with cardiovascular disease accounting for approximately 40% of deaths in CKD patients. Diagnostic and therapeutic challenges arise due to altered biomarker profiles and underutilization of interventions like percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This systematic review aims to identify and evaluate predictors of AMI in CKD patients, focusing on clinical, biochemical, demographic, and lifestyle-related risk factors to inform targeted prevention strategies.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library up to August 14, 2025, using MeSH terms like "chronic kidney disease" and "myocardial infarction." Included studies involved adult CKD patients, assessing predictors through observational designs or relevant randomized controlled trial subgroup analyses. Data were extracted by two independent reviewers, with study quality assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Narrative synthesis was employed due to heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Twenty studies (54-911,360 participants) identified dyslipidemia, inflammatory (CRP, IL-6) and cardiac biomarkers (NT-proBNP, hs-cTnT), lower eGFR, albuminuria, advanced CKD stage, hypertension, prior AMI, and older age as key AMI predictors. Risk scores (GRACE, PRECISE-DAPT) and novel indices (TyG, TyG-BMI) showed high predictive accuracy.
CONCLUSION: Comprehensive risk assessment integrating biomarkers, clinical factors, and novel indices can enhance AMI prediction and guide interventions in CKD patients, addressing therapeutic underutilization.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Wearable ECG and PPG Devices for Arrhythmia Detection: A Narrative Review : Short title: Artificial Intelligence in Wearable Devices for Arrhythmia Detection.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the world's top cause of death. Short recording times and a dependence on clinical settings are two practical drawbacks of traditional methods like Holter monitoring and standard 12-lead ECG. Two significant trends have come together in recent years: the broad availability of consumer-grade wearable technology, including smartwatches and adhesive ambulatory ECG patches, and the quick advancement of deep learning and artificial intelligence. Four main themes currently dominate research in this field: diagnostic accuracy under controlled conditions, algorithmic innovation for real-time and on-device analysis, real-world implementation and performance in large prospective studies, and the persistent technical, clinical, and regulatory challenges that limit widespread deployment.AI-based systems have shown consistently high performance in controlled environments and curated datasets, with reported sensitivities and specificities commonly ranging between 92% and 99%.However, performance, especially specificity and generalizability, frequently declines significantly if these algorithms are exposed to the messiness of daily movement, a variety of patient demographics, fluctuating skin contact, and hardware limitations outside of the lab. More advanced transformer architectures and multimodal techniques that combine ECG signals with photoplethysmography (PPG) waveforms, as well as lightweight convolutional neural networks that can operate directly on the device itself and provide true real-time detection, have been the focus of recent algorithmic work. The present status of wearable ECG and PPG technology for AI-enabled arrhythmia detection is examined in this narrative review. It critically evaluates diagnostic performance, translational gaps that still exist and paying special attention to the major prospective studies that have shaped the field. All things considered, the data indicates that wearables driven by AI have real potential for screening for arrhythmias at the population level and have already shown promising signs of clinical utility. The field will require larger, longer, and more diversified prospective trials that are sufficiently powered to identify significant differences in hard clinical outcomes.

Title: Emergency medicine literature in the Web of Science category "emergency medicine": A bibliometric analysis (1980-2024).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The objective is to describe long-term trends in emergency medicine (EM) research output from 1980 to 2024 and to map study designs, conceptual domains, and collaboration structures within the Web of Science (WoS) Category "EM."
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective bibliometric analysis of records indexed in the WoS Core Collection from January 1, 1980, to December 31, 2024, using the WoS Categories filter "EM." The search was performed on October 3, 2025. Only records with WoS document type "Article" were included. Bibliographic data, including publication year, journal, country, institutions, citations, and indexed keywords/metadata, were extracted. A rule-based text-mining algorithm classified study designs and conceptual domains and was internally validated against a manually reviewed sample of 240 records, showing 75.8% agreement (κ = 0.638) for study design and 86.3% agreement (κ = 0.828) for conceptual domain. Descriptive statistics and VOSviewer-based co-authorship, co-citation, and keyword co-occurrence analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Of 161,842 records initially identified, 102,561 articles met eligibility criteria. Annual EM publication counts increased after 2000. Health services and systems research and observational clinical studies predominated, whereas randomized controlled trials and qualitative or mixed-methods studies remained uncommon. Trauma, resuscitation, cardiovascular emergencies, and sepsis were longstanding core domains, while digital health, artificial intelligence, point-of-care ultrasound, disaster medicine, and global EM gained prominence after 2010. Collaboration expanded over time, but multinational co-authorship remained limited, and affiliations from low- and middle-income countries were underrepresented.
CONCLUSIONS: EM has evolved into a high-volume, thematically diverse field, but its evidence base remains predominantly observational and geographically imbalanced.

Title: Benefit take-up in the last year of life: a population-based study using linked data for England and Wales.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: In the UK, and in other countries, people living with a terminal illness are eligible for financial support to help with the costs of serious illness and to support their dignity and independence. This study investigates the take-up of benefits in the last year of life and identifies sociodemographic, clinical, and geographical factors associated with underclaiming.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using linked mortality, Census and benefits data for all people who died aged 16+ from chronic illnesses in England and Wales between 1 May 2018 and 30 April 2021. Outcome was receipt of non-means tested disability benefits in the last 12 months of life. We describe geographical variation in take up, and association with sociodemographic, clinical and geographical exposures using Poisson models.
FINDINGS: Our population included 1,049,493 people who died from an expected, non-sudden, cause with an overall take-up rate of 65.9%. After adjusting for sociodemographic factors, variation in take-up by cause of death was wide: liver disease 44% (95% CI 43-45%), heart failure 52% (51-52%), cancer 62% (61-62%), dementia 75% (74-75%), and neurodegenerative diseases 90% (88-91%). Across Local Authorities, the age-and-sex-standardised take-up varied from 53% to 78%; rates were generally higher in more deprived areas, but not uniformly.
CONCLUSIONS: In England and Wales, 1 in 3 people who die from expected causes (120,000 each year) do not receive the benefits for which they are eligible. Our analysis uses novel data linkages and highlights clinical and sociodemographic groups and geographical areas that could be targeted with proactive take-up initiatives.

Title: Brain and Cardiometabolic Effects of Major Weight Loss in People With Obesity: Preliminary Cohort Findings.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Given the overlap between obesity-related metabolic and vascular abnormalities and Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk factors, it is critical to determine whether weight loss improves brain and cardiovascular health. This study examined whether ≥ 40% excess-weight loss is associated with improvements in cardiometabolic risk, brain structure, and cognition.
METHODS: The study was a longitudinal study of individuals with obesity undergoing metabolic and bariatric surgery or medical/behavioral weight-loss treatment. Participants were classified at follow-up as weight-loss (WL; ≥ 40% excess-weight loss) or non-weight-loss (nWL; < 40%). All completed medical evaluations, structural MRI, and cognitive testing at baseline and 1 year.
RESULTS: At 1 year, the WL group exhibited improvements in BMI, HbA1C, inflammatory, metabolic, and lipid profiles. MRI-based volumetrics revealed increases in subcortical gray-matter volume and preservation of AD-vulnerable regions. Cognitive performance remained unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: Achieving ≥ 40% excess-weight loss was associated with improvements in metabolic health and brain structure, including favorable subcortical volume increases. These findings underscore the potential of sustained weight reduction to mitigate risks linked to metabolic syndromes and neurodegeneration. Longer-term follow-up is warranted to determine whether continued metabolic improvements lead to detectable cognitive gains and additional brain-health benefits beyond 1 year.

Title: Medication non-adherence and its associated factors among heart failure patients in Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medication non-adherence is a critical determinant of poor outcomes in heart failure, a condition posing a significant public health burden across Africa. Unique regional challenges such as healthcare resource constraints, economic disparities, and diverse healthcare systems exacerbate this issue. However, a consolidated estimate of non-adherence prevalence and its associated factors across the continent remains unknown.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251139486). A comprehensive search of databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, African Journal Online, and Google Scholar) was conducted for studies published between 2000 and 2025. Observational studies reporting non-adherence prevalence or associated factors among African heart failure patients were included. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklists for cross-sectional and cohort studies. Data were extracted and pooled using a random-effects model in STATA 17.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies (n = 6276 patients) from multiple African regions were included. The pooled prevalence of medication non-adherence among heart failure patients in Africa was 41.88% (95% CI: 25.43-58.34). Extreme heterogeneity (I² = 99.7%) was explored via subgroup analyses, revealing significant regional variation with Western Africa showing the highest prevalence (77.59%). Meta-analysis of associated factors identified lack of health insurance as the strongest predictor (OR = 4.27, 95% CI: 1.62-11.26). Other significant factors included polypharmacy (OR = 2.58, 95% CI: 2.00-3.33) and presence of comorbidities (OR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.31-2.35). No publication bias was detected (Egger's test: p = 0.267).
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately two in five heart failure patients in Africa are non-adherent to their medication, with prevalence rates varying significantly by region. This rate is exacerbated by financial, clinical, and therapy-related factors. Concerted multi-faceted interventions are urgently needed across the continent. Recommendations include expanding health insurance coverage, implementing medication subsidy programs, strengthening therapy simplification strategies, and developing context-specific adherence support strategies tailored to regional healthcare contexts and patient populations.

Title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment.
Abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommendations and consensus-based practice from technical feasibility and demonstrated comparative patient benefit, while identifying unresolved questions concerning AMI reperfusion strategies and device selection, in addition to antithrombotic therapy and restenosis management in CMI.

Title: High Rates of Atrial Fibrillation among Inpatients with Heart Failure or Ischemic Stroke in Southwestern Uganda.
Abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) affects over 37 million people worldwide, and its prevalence is projected to increase by 60% by 2050. Addressing AF is critical in Uganda and elsewhere in sub-Saharan Africa, where data are lacking despite the high prevalence of AF risk factors, comorbidities, and sequelae. Objectives: To evaluate AF prevalence among inpatients with acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke in Uganda. Methods: Between November 4, 2024 and November 30, 2025, we recruited a cohort of inpatients at the Regional Referral Hospital in Mbarara, Uganda with either acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke. We collected baseline clinical data and hospital outcomes, performed a transthoracic echocardiogram, and equipped participants with a 24-hour Holter monitor. A multivariable logistic regression model was fitted for a primary outcome of AF detection. Results: Among 250 individuals, mean age was 61.7 years (SD 20.5), of whom 175 (70.0%) were women. 123 (49.2%) had acute heart failure; 127 (50.8%) had acute ischemic stroke. Holter monitors detected AF in 105 (42.0%), with a mean AF duration of 11.0 hours (IQR 1.0-21.9) with a bimodal distribution. Mean stroke risk (CHA2DS2VA) was 3.5 (SD 1.6). Factors associated with AF included increasing age in years (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.02-1.06) and left atrial volume index (mL/m2) (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.01-1.03). Conclusions: We found high rates of AF among inpatients with acute heart failure or acute ischemic stroke, comparable to studies from the United States and Europe. These findings highlight the need to address AF in Uganda, with improved screening using long-term monitors, updated treatment protocols, and broadened access to cardiac care.

Title: Deciphering Kawasaki disease genetics through next-generation sequencing: A scoping review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute self-limiting childhood vasculitis. KD is considered the most common cause of acquired heart disease in children worldwide. Despite being the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, its etiology remains poorly understood. Several epidemiological studies reveal a strong genetic predisposition to KD susceptibility, underlying coronary artery abnormalities (CAAs) and treatment resistance to intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG).
AIM: To evaluate the current literature on the roles of targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS), whole-exome sequencing (WES) and/or whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in identifying genetic susceptibility loci, immunopathogenic pathways, and mechanisms of IVIG resistance in KD.
METHODS: We performed a literature search to identify key genes and pathways associated with genetic susceptibility, IVIG resistance, and CAAs development in KD. Our search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Studies investigating these features using targeted NGS, WES or WGS were included in this review. Studies employing other methods to investigate genetic susceptibility, IVIG resistance, and CAA among KD patients were excluded.
RESULTS: Targeted NGS, WES and WGS studies of the KD cohort across different regions have identified both rare and common variants associated with KD-related phenotypes. Genes with these variants were linked to immune regulation and vascular biology. Genes linked with innate and adaptive immune responses included TLR6, MEF2A, HLA-DRB1, IL6ST, MYH14, RBP3, EFCC1, FCRLA, PTGER4, IL17F, CARD11, and SIGLEC10. Studies have also revealed genes associated with CAA. These genes were IL17RC, FGFR4, IL31RA, FNDC1, MMP8, and FOXN1, all of which were implicated in inflammatory and vascular remodelling processes. WGS studies also identified novel loci associated with IVIG resistance. These were FANK1, MAP2K3, KCNJ12, CA10, CWH43, EDN1, PPP2R5E, and SFMBT2, as well as previously established genes such as ITPKC, CASP3, FCGR2A, CD40, and IL1B. Many of these genes have known or proposed functions in biological pathways potentially relevant to KD, including TLR and NF-κB signalling, IL-17-mediated cytokine pathways, calcium/NFAT signalling, MAPK signalling, vascular remodelling, and endothelial dysfunction. Moreover, sex-biased variants (EFCC1, LMO7, CEMIP, and USH2A) also revealed gender-based differences in KD susceptibility, indicating a higher risk of KD in boys.
CONCLUSION: Studies using NGS-based approaches have significantly advanced understanding of KD by identifying key candidate genes and pathways associated with disease susceptibility, CAAs, and IVIG response, and IVIG resistance. These findings support a multi-pathway immunovascular model of KD. Future studies involving larger, ethnically diverse cohorts and functional validation are essential for clinical translation.

Title: Strengthening stroke registries for trial readiness and research equity in Sub-Saharan Africa.
Abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa carries one of the highest stroke burden globally, yet contributes fewer than 6% of participants to trials to inform international secondary stroke prevention guidelines. Although stroke registries across the region have expanded in numbers, they have not yet provided the trial-ready infrastructure required to support clinical research, quality improvement, and policy-relevant evidence generation. This commentary examines how existing stroke registries can evolve into platforms capable of supporting locally relevant clinical research and participation in multinational clinical studies. Recent studies identified more than 40 stroke registries across sub-Saharan Africa; however, most are characterised by heterogeneous data elements, variable follow-up, limited alignment with international standards, and incomplete population coverage. These structural limitations restrict comparability across sites, impede regional data pooling, and constrain participation in collaborative research. We propose a three-pillar pathway toward trial readiness comprising harmonised core data standards, operational capacity development through regional mentorship networks, and sustainable funding supported by coordinated national and international leadership. Harmonisation should be accompanied by broader registry coverage to improve representativeness and trial recruitment. Beyond supporting research participation, mature registries can also facilitate quality improvement, benchmarking, and health-system planning alongside clinical research. Transforming stroke registries into trial-ready platforms is both feasible and necessary to strengthen secondary prevention, improve research equity, and ensure that international stroke guidelines better reflect the epidemiological realities and research priorities of sub-Saharan Africa.

Title: Alterations in oral microbiome and salivary metabolome profiles associated with myocardial infarction: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few studies have comprehensively profiled both the salivary microbiome and metabolome in myocardial infarction (MI). This case-control study therefore characterized microbial and metabolic alterations in MI patients and identified potential diagnostic signatures.
METHODS: Seventy participants (35 MI patients and 35 matched healthy controls) were enrolled. Salivary microbiota were profiled via 16S rRNA (V3-V4) sequencing, and metabolites were analyzed using untargeted LC-MS. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and predicted functional pathways were assessed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by ROC analysis, and microbiota-metabolite correlations.
RESULTS: Significant differences in oral microbial diversity were observed between MI patients and controls. MI patients exhibited significantly higher alpha diversity and a distinct community structure, with beta diversity separating between groups. Enriched taxa included Bacteroidota, Veillonella, and Prevotella_7, while Streptococcus and Porphyromonas were depleted in MI patients. A four-metabolite panel comprising elevated L-2-aminoadipic acid and reduced thromboxane B2, 4-oxo-2-nonenal, and arginyl-glutamate distinguished MI from controls with high diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.92-0.94). Pathway analysis implicated ferroptosis and arginine/proline metabolism as candidate mechanisms. Correlation analysis revealed a significant positive association between Streptococcus and L-2-aminoadipic acid.
CONCLUSION: MI is associated with distinct oral microbial and salivary metabolomic signatures. A four-metabolite panel shows promise as a potential non-invasive biomarker signature, though external validation is required. Given the cross-sectional design, causality cannot be established.

Title: Sex-related differences in long-term outcomes of drug-coated balloons versus thin-strut drug-eluting stents in the treatment of in-stent restenosis (DCB-DRAGON Registry).
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Drug-coated balloons (DCB) and drug-eluting stents (DES) are established options for coronary in-stent restenosis (ISR); evidence on sex-specific outcomes remains limited.
AIM: To determine whether sex modifies the comparative effectiveness of DCB versus thin-strut, second-generation DES in ISR.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of 1,317 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for ISR, 2008-2021. Because 57.6% were censored before 3 years, the primary estimand is the difference in restricted mean survival time (RMST) over 0-3 years for the device-oriented composite endpoint (DOCE). Counterfactual survival was estimated by weighted Kaplan-Meier estimation with entropy-balancing weights within each sex stratum; variance was estimated using bootstrap resampling pooled across 20 imputed datasets by Rubin's rules.
RESULTS: Among 395 (30.0%) women and 922 (70.0%) men, 209 DOCE events accrued. Median observation time differed approximately twofold between arms (20.6 vs. 38.7 months in women; 19.7 vs. 39.4 months in men). The RMST difference was -0.047 years (95% CI: -0.579 to +0.486) in women and +0.036 (-0.186 to +0.259) in men, a sex difference of -0.083 years (-0.661 to +0.495; p = 0.78); weighted HRs were 0.76 (0.43-1.34) and 0.73 (0.50-1.07), respectively. No secondary endpoint showed heterogeneity: every uncorrected p exceeded 0.5 and every false-discovery-rate-adjusted value equalled 0.82. Cardiovascular deaths were similar between arms in women (5 vs. 5) and men (16 vs. 15); weighted HRs for all-cause mortality were 1.03 (0.39-2.72) and 0.78 (0.42-1.46), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Sex did not modify the comparative effectiveness of DCB versus thin-strut DES for ISR, on the composite endpoint or on any component; these data do not support sex-based device selection. Wide intervals and differential follow-up establish the absence of detectable heterogeneity rather than equivalence.

Title: Inflammatory burden index and contrast-associated acute kidney injury after iliac artery endovascular intervention: association with renal injury and lesion complexity.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a complication after peripheral endovascular interventions, but the value of the inflammatory burden index (IBI) in this setting is unknown.
AIM: To evaluate the association between pre-procedural IBI and CA-AKI after iliac artery intervention, compare its performance with other inflammatory indices, and examine its relationship with TASC II lesion complexity.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 417 patients treated between January 2020 and December 2025. IBI was calculated as C-reactive protein multiplied by the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. CA-AKI was defined as a serum creatinine increase of ≥ 0.5 mg/dl or ≥ 25% within 72 h. Receiver operating characteristic analysis, DeLong testing, multivariable logistic regression with multiple imputation, restricted cubic splines, and bootstrap validation were performed.
RESULTS: CA-AKI occurred in 70 (16.8%) patients. IBI showed the highest discrimination for CA-AKI (AUC = 0.857, 95% CI: 0.810-0.904), outperforming C-reactive protein, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (all p < 0.001). At a cutoff of 40.6, sensitivity and specificity were 80.0% and 80.2%, respectively. Each doubling of IBI was independently associated with CA-AKI (adjusted OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 2.22-4.59; p < 0.001). The association was nonlinear (p for nonlinearity < 0.001). IBI was also independently associated with TASC II C-D lesions (adjusted OR per doubling 2.91, 95% CI: 2.29-3.71; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Pre-procedural IBI was independently associated with CA-AKI and complex iliac lesion morphology and outperformed the other evaluated inflammatory indices. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Prognostic value of chronic total occlusion complexity scoring systems beyond procedural planning: a comparative analysis of five contemporary scores in patients undergoing chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic total occlusion (CTO) complexity scores were developed to predict procedural difficulty during CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO-PCI). Their value for predicting long-term clinical outcomes remains uncertain.
AIM: We investigated the association between commonly used CTO complexity scores and adverse outcomes after CTO-PCI and compared their prognostic performance.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 149 consecutive patients undergoing CTO-PCI. Five CTO complexity scores (J-CTO, RECHARGE, PROGRESS-CTO, CL, and CASTLE) were calculated. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or urgent coronary revascularization. Multivariable Cox regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis were performed.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 17.1 ±10.6 months, the composite endpoint occurred in 30 (20.1%) patients. After adjustment for age, left ventricular ejection fraction, serum creatinine, and albumin, all five CTO scores remained independently associated with the composite outcome. The J-CTO score showed the strongest association (adjusted HR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.38-3.45; p = 0.001). The CASTLE score had the highest observed ROC-AUC (0.726, p < 0.001), although its discriminatory performance did not differ significantly from that of the J-CTO score. Harrell's C-index also demonstrated comparable discrimination between the CASTLE and J-CTO scores (both C-index 0.697), indicating modest-to-moderate discriminatory ability. Patients with J-CTO ≥ 2 or CASTLE ≥ 2 had significantly worse event-free survival (log-rank p = 0.013 and p = 0.004, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: CTO complexity scores were independently associated with long-term adverse outcomes after CTO-PCI and may have prognostic relevance in addition to their established role in procedural planning. These findings should be confirmed in larger prospective studies.

Title: Comparison of transcatheter aortic valve replacement performed in a hybrid operating room versus a catheterization laboratory.
Journal: Postepy w kardiologii interwencyjnej = Advances in interventional cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) can be performed in a catheterization laboratory (cath lab) or in a hybrid operating room (hybrid OR).
AIM: The objective of this study was to compare the safety of patients undergoing TAVR in a hybrid OR with those undergoing TAVR in a cath lab.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: The primary endpoint was a composite safety endpoint, which includes freedom from all-cause in-hospital mortality, stroke, major vascular complications (VARC ≥ 2), aortic regurgitation (grade ≥ 2), new pacemaker implantation, emergent surgery, annulus rupture, tamponade, or stent femoral implantation. The two secondary endpoints consisted of technical failure criteria and device failure criteria, at hospital discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 286 patients were included, 143 undergoing TF TAVR in the cath lab and 143 in a hybrid OR. Regarding the safety primary endpoint, there was no significant difference between the groups: 75.3% in the cath lab group versus 71.1% in the hybrid OR group (p = 0.421). There was also no significant difference in the technical failure criteria (3.5% in the cath lab group versus 4.2% in the hybrid OR group; p = 0.758) and device failure criteria (20.6% in the cath lab group versus 17.6% in the hybrid OR group; p = 0.526).
CONCLUSIONS: Regarding the composite safety and efficacy endpoints, no statistically significant between-group differences were detected in this unadjusted single-center cohort between patients undergoing TF-TAVR in a cath lab and those treated in a hybrid OR. These data suggest that performing TF TAVR in the cath lab can achieve high safety and effectiveness outcomes.

Title: Health-Related Quality of Life and Psychiatric Morbidity at Follow-up After Catheter Ablation in Children with Supraventricular Tachycardia.
Abstract: Background: This study aimed to evaluate health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and psychiatric outcomes in children and adolescents with supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) during the post-ablation follow-up period. Methods: This retrospective-prospective observational cohort study included pediatric patients who underwent successful catheter ablation for supraventricular tachycardia. Clinical and procedural data were collected retrospectively. Pre-ablation HRQoL data were obtained from either documented pre-procedural assessments or caregiver recall when records were unavailable. Psychiatric interviews and post-ablation HRQoL assessments were conducted prospectively during a single follow-up evaluation. Results: A total of 59 pediatric patients participated in the follow-up evaluation and were included in the study; the median age was 13.0 years (Q1-Q3, 10.0-15.0). Depending on the HRQoL domain, paired pre- and post-ablation data were available for 53 or 54 participants. Follow-up scores for physical, emotional, social, and school functioning were higher than the retrospectively obtained pre-ablation reference scores (all p < .001; Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold, p < .0125). At follow-up, at least 1 DSM-5 psychiatric diagnosis was identified in 18 participants (30.5%), most commonly anxiety and depressive disorders. Seven of these participants had 2 or more concurrent psychiatric diagnoses. Conclusion: Pediatric patients had higher HRQoL scores at post-ablation follow-up, and 30.5% met criteria for at least 1 psychiatric diagnosis. The HRQoL comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because baseline data were obtained from a combination of medical records and caregiver recall, informants were not fully standardized across assessment periods, and the exact interval between ablation and follow-up could not be reliably reconstructed.

Title: The lungs in Alström syndrome: a retrospective analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alström syndrome (AS) is a rare multisystemic disorder frequently associated with respiratory complications, which are a major cause of premature death. While fibrosis in multiple organs has been historically suggested as a hallmark of AS, including the lungs, definitive evidence in adult patients remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients diagnosed as AS seen in our National Multidisciplianry AS clinic from 2010 to 2024. Lung function test and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the thorax was performed in a subset of patients. Postmortem lung tissue analysis was available from four patients.
FINDINGS: A total of 25/41 (61%) of the patients were unable to complete full lung function testing. Among those who did, 67% exhibited reduced lung volumes, with 47% showing decreased diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide but normal or elevated transfer coefficient for carbon monoxide, indicating extrapulmonary restrictive physiology. HRCT scans in 39 patients showed no evidence of diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis; however, breathing artefacts were common. Historical infantile cardiomyopathy was identified as a risk factor for adult pulmonary dysfunction. Post-mortem pathology reports were obtained from four patients and no diffuse fibrosis in the lung tissue was identified in any of the patients. Pulmonary hypertension and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome were identified as potential causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality, despite the absence of intrinsic interstitial lung disease.
INTERPRETATION: This is the first large cohort study to depict the lung in adult patients with AS. This study provides no evidence for diffuse interstitial lung fibrosis in adult patients with AS, challenging prior assumptions. Pulmonary dysfunction appears mainly due to extrapulmonary restrictive physiology, with infantile cardiomyopathy as a possible risk factor. Pulmonary hypertension and acute respiratory distress syndrome, rather than intrinsic lung disease, likely underlie respiratory morbidity and mortality, highlighting the need for focused cardiopulmonary care. Although this study represents one of the largest single-centre cohorts of patients with AS reported to date, the overall sample size remains limited due to the ultra-rare nature of the disease and findings should be interpreted with caution.
FUNDING: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

Title: Beyond glycemic control: cardiovascular and kidney benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists and the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide: a narrative review.
Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome reflects the complex interplay among cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide have emerged as important therapeutic options within CKM syndrome, although the strength and maturity of evidence differ across individual agents and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the cardiovascular and kidney effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists and the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide. Large randomized controlled trials have established reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events with several GLP-1 receptor agonists, while dedicated evidence for clinically meaningful chronic kidney disease progression is currently strongest for semaglutide. Cardiovascular benefits of semaglutide have also been demonstrated in individuals with overweight or obesity without type 2 diabetes, supporting effects beyond glucose lowering. Tirzepatide provides substantial improvements in glycemic control and body weight, with expanding evidence supporting cardiovascular benefit, including particularly encouraging findings in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. In contrast, its kidney evidence remains less mature and is derived predominantly from secondary and post-hoc analyses rather than from a dedicated kidney outcome trial. Collectively, these findings support a phenotype-oriented and multimodal role for incretin-based therapies in CKM syndrome management while highlighting important differences in the maturity of outcome evidence.

Title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism.
Abstract: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal-fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Adjunctive Corticosteroids in Children With Kawasaki Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease is an acute pediatric vasculitis and a major cause of acquired heart disease in children. Although intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) with aspirin remains the standard treatment, some patients have persistent inflammation, IVIG resistance, or coronary complications. The role of adjunctive corticosteroids remains debated, particularly across different risk populations and corticosteroid regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of adjunctive corticosteroid therapy in children with Kawasaki disease.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science was conducted to identify randomized controlled trials comparing corticosteroid-containing treatment strategies with non-corticosteroid comparators, including standard IVIG-based initial treatment or additional IVIG in IVIG-resistant disease. The primary outcome was the change in C-reactive protein levels. Secondary outcomes included fever duration, IVIG resistance, laboratory markers, coronary outcomes, and adverse events. Pooled estimates were calculated using random-effects models and reported as mean differences (MD) or risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Ten randomized controlled trials, including 5,796 unique children, were included. Adjunctive corticosteroid therapy was associated with a greater reduction in C-reactive protein levels compared with usual care alone (MD, -11.05; 95% CI, -18.27 to -3.84; P = 0.0027; I2 = 34.3%, P = 0.179). Corticosteroid therapy also reduced fever duration (MD, -1.03; 95% CI, -1.70 to -0.36; P = 0.0025; I2 = 85.2%, P < 0.001) and white blood cell count (MD, -1.07; 95% CI, -1.98 to -0.17; P = 0.020; I2 = 0.0%, P = 0.887). No significant differences were observed in IVIG resistance, coronary artery lesions, large/giant aneurysms, any adverse event, or adverse events leading to discontinuation.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive corticosteroids were associated with improved inflammatory and early clinical response in Kawasaki disease, mainly through greater C-reactive protein reduction and shorter fever duration.
