However, corticosteroids did not significantly reduce overall coronary outcomes, and no statistically significant increase in the pooled adverse-event outcomes was detected. These findings support selective, risk-based use rather than routine universal administration.

Title: Virtual Assessment of Coronary Microcirculation Before and After Rotational Atherectomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcified coronary lesions remain a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Rotational atherectomy (RA) (Boston Scientific) is a well-established tool used to modify calcified plaques and facilitate stent delivery. Despite its mechanical benefits, RA may adversely affect coronary microcirculation through distal plaque debris embolization. Angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR) (Pulse Medical) is a wire-free index correlated with invasive indices such as the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR), which allows assessment of microcirculatory resistance directly from angiographic images, without a pressure wire or adenosine. The objective of this study is to evaluate changes in AMR before and after RA and to identify clinical, angiographic, and procedural predictors of postprocedural coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD).
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center observational study including all patients who underwent RA between January 2023 and December 2024 at Clinique Saint-Hilaire in Rouen, France. AMR was measured before and after RA using the AngioPlus software (Pulse Medical). CMD was defined as postprocedural AMR > 250 mm Hg·s/m.
RESULTS: Of 49 RA procedures, 40 patients were included. AMR increased in all cases but CMD occurred in 42.5% of patients (n=17). Diabetes mellitus and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were significantly more prevalent in the CMD group. Long coronary artery lesions (> 20 mm), larger plaque burden, and prolonged burr run time were associated with higher AMR values. Mean AMR rose from 176 to 315 mm Hg·s/m in the CMD group, versus 177 to 201 mm Hg·s/m in the non-CMD group.
CONCLUSIONS: Performing RA affects the coronary microcirculation, especially in cases of diabetes mellitus and reduced LVEF.

Title: Personalized Prevention of Cardiovascular Diseases Through Measurement of Plaque Burden in the Carotid Artery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study provides an overview of the results of carotid screening for the prevention of cardiovascular disease.
METHODS: Between 2009 and 2026, 11,540 individuals, 45% of whom were women, aged 20-65 years without clinical signs of cardiovascular disease, underwent carotid ultrasound examinations. Over 8,800 follow-up examinations were also performed. The total plaque area (TPA) and maximum plaque thickness were measured.
RESULTS: TPA was presented as percentile curves according to age and sex. In a second cohort, age-related TPA thresholds for coronary stenosis ≥ 50% were determined. Advanced atherosclerosis (type III/IVb) is associated with a high risk of cardiovascular disease. Early treatment with statins improves the prognosis of these patients. The individual course of the disease with rapid progression of plaque burden could not be predicted based on classic risk factors. Of 75 patients with advanced atherosclerosis who suffered a myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke, 35% had a low PROCAM risk (< 10%) and only 27% had a high PROCAM risk. Mortality (from any cause) was significantly lower in men treated with statins.
CONCLUSIONS: Measuring plaque burden in the carotid artery allows for a good estimation of an individual's risk of a cardiovascular event. In this non-randomized observational study, statin treatment significantly improved the prognosis in subjects with advanced carotid artery atherosclerosis (type III-IVb findings on ultrasound).

Title: Vein of Galen malformation in newborns and children: contemporary advances and future directions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vein of Galen malformation is a rare and complex cerebrovascular disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality from the fetal period through childhood. Advances in perinatal care, neuroimaging, endovascular therapy, and multidisciplinary management have improved survival and expanded therapeutic options, while generating new challenges in clinical strategies and long-term outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This review integrates evidence and expert perspectives presented during the II International Meeting on Vein of Galen Malformation in Newborns and Children, held in Camogli, Italy, in October 2025 and summarizes current advances, emerging developments, and priorities for research and clinical innovation.
RECENT ADVANCES: Current developments include improved fetal and neonatal imaging, emerging prognostic biomarkers, fetal intervention, advances in endovascular treatment, and increasing understanding of underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms. Contemporary management increasingly integrates cardiovascular and neurological assessment, advanced neuroimaging, individualized endovascular strategies, and structured long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up. The development of a disease-specific registry reflects the growing impact of international collaboration.
FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Major priorities include validation of risk-stratification tools, development of standardized imaging and neurodevelopmental biomarkers, refinement of fetal and neonatal interventions, improved understanding of disease biology, and multicenter data sharing. Family-centered care and standardized long-term outcome assessment should remain integral components of future VOGM research and clinical practice.
CONCLUSIONS: VOGM management is rapidly evolving from survival-focused treatment toward individualized, multidisciplinary care extending from fetal diagnosis through childhood and adulthood. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge and emerging developments in this field, while defining a multidisciplinary, internationally informed roadmap for future research.

Title: Digoxin Revisited: An Updated Review in the Light of Recent Trials.
Abstract: Isolated from Digitalis species following William Withering's 1785 work on foxglove, digoxin inhibits myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and vagal tone to produce inotropic, rate-controlling, and neurohormonal-deactivating effects. The foundational DIG trial (1997) showed no mortality benefit but reduced heart failure hospitalizations, prompting a progressive guideline downgrade. Three decades later, DIGIT-HF (2025, digitoxin) and DECISION (2026, low dose digoxin) retested cardiac glycosides atop modern four pillar guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). DIGIT-HF significantly reduced the composite of death or worsening heart failure (hazard ratio (HR), 0.82), while DECISION showed a numerical but nonsignificant benefit. A pooled meta-analysis of DIG, DIGIT-HF, and DECISION (9,013 patients) confirmed a consistent 15% reduction in worsening heart failure events across three decades of changing background therapy, without a significant mortality effect. The Dig-RHD trial addressed an unstudied population: symptomatic rheumatic heart disease (RHD), a chronic valvular heart disease that results from permanent damage to cardiac valves due to group A streptococcal infection. RHD affects roughly 40 million people and causes approximately 300,000 deaths annually, disproportionately in low- and middle-income countries. In 1,769 patients randomized across 12 Indian centers, digoxin significantly reduced the composite of death or new-onset/worsening heart failure (31.4% vs. 35.5%; HR, 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.70 to 0.97; P = 0.02), with greater benefit in atrial fibrillation, women, and patients with low body mass index (BMI), and a number needed to treat of approximately 14 over 2 years. Digoxin is not a mortality-reducing drug, but pooled contemporary evidence establishes it as a reproducible, low-cost tool for reducing heart failure events, now supported for the first time by high-quality randomized data in RHD, a population with substantial global burden and no prior evidence-based medical therapy. These findings warrant reconsideration of digoxin's guideline status and development of RHD-specific recommendations.

Title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases.
Abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.

Title: Development and internal validation of a parsimonious model for neurological deterioration at 48 h after endovascular thrombectomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incremental value of routine admission measurements for predicting early neurological deterioration after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains unclear.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) points from admission to the fixed 48-h postoperative assessment. The conservative primary cohort excluded an unresolved longitudinal data segment. A revision-stage locked five-predictor logistic regression model included admission NIHSS scores, age, glucose levels, white blood cell count, and ln triglyceride value, with the NIHSS-only model serving as the comparator. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap samples and paired nested intervals of 1,000 outer × 100 inner samples.
RESULTS: Of the 253 records representing 251 unique patients, 214 adults entered the primary cohort; 51 (23.8%) had END48. The primary model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.651 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.601 (0.511 to 0.723). The corrected AUC difference vs. the NIHSS-only model was 0.038 (-0.025 to 0.171). The corrected Brier score was 0.180, compared to a prevalence-only reference of 0.182, resulting in a Brier skill score of 0.9%. The corrected primary calibration slope was 0.731 (0.519 to 0.892). Incremental net benefit was -0.015, 0.036, and 0.013 at 10%, 20%, and 30% thresholds, respectively; all corresponding 95% confidence intervals crossed zero. Post-hoc Riley assessments across plausible model-fit assumptions indicated that the available cohort was below the sample size desirable for model development. The reconstructed cohort sensitivity analysis did not change the overall interpretation.
CONCLUSION: Discrimination was limited, improvement in probability accuracy was marginal, and incremental discrimination and net benefit were uncertain. The model should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically implementable; independent validation and improved outcome ascertainment are required.

Title: Hyperdominant Left Circumflex Artery Challenging Conventional Paradigms and Current Guideline Recommendations: A Comprehensive Literature Review and Case Series.
Abstract: Despite its rarity in the general population, left dominant coronary circulation with a hyperdominant left circumflex artery (LCx) has been associated with a more severe risk for ischemic and coronary artery disease. The concealment of an isolated posterior myocardial infarction (IPMI) on a standard 12-lead ECG among these patients with distinctive coronary anatomy can be concerning, especially when clinicians become trapped within conventional guideline-based diagnostic criteria, a circumstance that may ultimately be linked to a poorer prognosis. We present two cases that posed unique diagnostic challenges in this specific anatomical context. Case 1: A 63-year-old man presented to the emergency department (ED) with typical anginal chest pain and severe fatigue. Although the patient was initially diagnosed with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), eventually a catastrophic occlusion of the left posterior descending artery (PDA) in the setting of a hyperdominant LCx was seen during coronary angiography (CAG). Case 2: A 69-year-old man arrived at the ED with typical angina, described as pressure-like. Although the serial 12-lead ECGs were completely normal, given the clinical context, the patient underwent an immediate invasive strategy in < 2 h. CAG revealed complete occlusion of the ostio-proximal segment of the left PDA. In both cases, hyperdominant LCx anatomy created a diagnostic blind spot within the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI paradigm, because the infarct territory was insufficiently captured by standard ECG criteria and failed to trigger guideline-based use of posterior leads or adjunctive imaging, thereby obscuring the diagnosis of IPMI. These cases warn clinicians about the diagnostic complexity of IPMI in a hyperdominant LCx setting. In such cases, ECG findings can be ambiguous or even completely absent, and the clinical presentation may not meet current unclear guideline-based indications for adjunctive diagnostic assessment, leading to delayed recognition of high-risk ischemia, particularly IPMI.

Title: PFOCUS study protocol: a prospective case-control study investigating genetic, haemodynamic, and platelet function in migraine with aura with or without patent foramen ovale.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migraine with aura (MA) is associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke, particularly in young individuals without conventional vascular risk factors. A growing body of evidence indicates a strong association between MA and patent foramen ovale (PFO), the prevalence of which is up to three times higher in patients with MA than in the general population. The mechanisms underlying this association remain incompletely understood and are likely to extend beyond paradoxical embolism.
METHODS AND DESIGN: PFOCUS is a prospective, monocentric, observational case-control study designed to investigate the genetic, neurosonological, and hematological determinants linking MA and PFO. Specifically, the study evaluates whether genetic variants, particularly within the Notch signaling pathway, contribute to the coexistence of PFO and MA, and whether these patients display distinct cerebrovascular and prothrombotic profiles. As exploratory aims, the study will assess whether aura phenotypes and the distribution of MRI lesions are associated with different haemodynamic and prothrombotic profiles, potentially identifying clinically relevant subgroups within MA.A total of 240 patients with MA will be enrolled and classified as right-to-left shunt (RLS)-positive or RLS-negative on the basis of contrast-enhanced transcranial Doppler (TCD), used as a surrogate marker of PFO. Participants will undergo comprehensive phenotyping including genetic testing by whole-exome sequencing, neurosonological assessment of right-to-left shunt, cerebral microemboli detection, dynamic cerebral autoregulation and cerebral vasomotor reactivity (VMR), and platelet function testing. The primary endpoint is the difference in the frequency of NOTCH3 gene variants between groups. Secondary endpoints include associations with other panel genes, correlation with shunt size, and differences in haemodynamic and platelet function parameters. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07349004.
DISCUSSION: PFOCUS aims to identify a biologically distinct phenotype of MA associated with PFO, potentially driven by genetic predisposition and vascular dysfunction. Its findings may inform stroke risk stratification and open new avenues for personalized preventive strategies in patients with MA.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT07349004 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07349004).

Title: Cognitive impairment profiles in patients with cerebrovascular diseases: a latent profile analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is an increasingly recognized condition predominantly attributable to cerebrovascular diseases (CVDs). It substantially diminishes patients' quality of life and imposes considerable burdens on caregivers and healthcare systems. However, how cognitive impairment manifest across multiple functional domains in individuals with CVDs remains poorly understood, often resulting in generalized care plans that fail to meet patients' specific rehabilitation needs. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of cognitive impairment and their associated factors in patients with CVDs using latent profile analysis (LPA).
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted using convenience sampling in a tertiary hospital in southwestern China from November 2023 to September 2025. LPA was employed to identify distinct cognitive impairment profiles among patients with CVDs. Multinomial logistic regression was subsequently performed to examine factors associated with profile categories.
RESULTS: The final three-profile model classified 474 participants into three groups: a mild impairment group (82.5%), a moderate impairment group (11.4%), and a severe impairment group (6.1%). The three profiles reflected increasing severity of cognitive impairment among patients with CVDs. Compared with the mild impairment group, higher NIHSS scores (OR = 1.222, 95 %CI = 1.126-1.326, p < 0.001) were associated with higher odds of membership in the moderate impairment profile. Male gender and lower NIHSS scores were associated with lower odds of membership in the severe impairment profile (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In this predominantly hemorrhagic and neurosurgical cohort, the retained three-profile model represented different levels of MMSE-based global cognitive severity among patients with CVDs. NIHSS score and gender showed exploratory associations with profile membership. The applicability of these findings to broader CVD populations requires further validation.

Title: Effects of wearable lower-limb robotic exoskeleton-assisted gait training on balance, walking, and activities of daily living after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wearable lower-limb robotic exoskeleton-assisted gait training encompasses heterogeneous overground and treadmill/platform-based implementations. Comparative effects remain uncertain. We synthesised evidence from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on walking, balance, lower-limb motor function, and activities of daily living (ADL).
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science Core Collection, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure from inception to February 26, 2026. We included RCTs comparing wearable lower-limb robotic exoskeleton-assisted gait training (overground and/or treadmill/platform-based) with usual rehabilitation or other controls. Effects were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment; 95% prediction intervals were reported when applicable. Certainty was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and publication bias was evaluated for outcomes with ≥10 studies.
RESULTS: Fourteen RCTs (n = 565) were included. Pooled between-group estimates favoured intervention groups for walking independence measured by the Functional Ambulation Category (FAC; mean difference [MD] = 0.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.15-0.63), balance measured by the Berg Balance Scale (BBS; MD = 1.66, 95% CI 0.52-2.81), and lower-limb motor function measured by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Lower Extremity (FMA-LE; MD = 2.40, 95% CI 1.63-3.16). The 6-Minute Walk Test estimate favoured intervention groups (MD = 19.83, 95% CI 2.21-37.45), although its prediction interval crossed the null. No between-group differences emerged for walking speed, mobility, or ADL. Certainty was moderate for FAC, BBS, and FMA-LE and low to very low for other outcomes. No small-study effects were detected for BBS (k = 11; p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Across heterogeneous exoskeleton-assisted gait-training interventions, pooled estimates favoured intervention groups for walking independence, balance, and lower-limb motor function. However, most prediction intervals crossed the null, certainty for other outcomes was low to very low, and inconsistent reporting limited analyses of training environment and precluded granular analyses of body-weight support, assistance strategy, patient engagement, comparator content, dose, and patient selection. These estimates reflect heterogeneous intervention-comparator packages and cannot determine whether differences are attributable to the robotic device category itself or support specific prescribing recommendations. Larger, stratified RCTs with standardised reporting and longer follow-up are needed to identify influential intervention and patient characteristics.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261327255.

Title: Efficacy of Melatonin in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) represents the leading cause of chronic liver disease globally. Oxidative stress, inflammation, and hepatocellular necrosis play central roles in its pathogenesis. Emerging evidence highlights melatonin as a promising therapeutic agent for MASLD. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy of melatonin in MASLD management.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception through December 2025 for randomized and non-randomized controlled clinical trials comparing melatonin supplementation with placebo, no treatment, or an active comparator in adults with MASLD. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using the Mantel-Haenszel method and continuous outcomes as mean differences (MDs) using the inverse-variance method, both under random-effects models. In every trial the control arm received the same background management as the melatonin arm (placebo, essential phospholipids, statin therapy, or lifestyle advice) without melatonin; no trial compared melatonin with an active pharmacological comparator.
RESULTS: Eleven controlled trials (nine randomized, two non-randomized; 548 participants: 300 melatonin, 248 control) were included. In the primary analyses, melatonin was associated with reductions in total cholesterol (MD: -16.80 mg/dL, 95% confidence interval (CI): -29.13 to -4.47, P = 0.008; I2 = 76%) and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol (MD: -52.4 mg/dL, 95% CI: -100.52 to -4.27, P = 0.03; I2 = 96%), in interleukin-1 (IL-1), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and in body weight and waist circumference, and with a lower proportion of participants with grade III steatosis at follow-up (RR: 0.23, 95% CI: 0.07-0.77; two trials). No significant differences were found for grade I or II steatosis, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein (HDL), fasting blood sugar, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, or high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). Reductions in ALT, AST, GGT, and triglycerides were observed only in exploratory sensitivity analyses after exclusion of individual trials. Heterogeneity was high (I2 > 75%) for several outcomes, and nine of the 11 trials were placebo-controlled.
CONCLUSION: Melatonin supplementation was associated with modest improvements in total and LDL cholesterol, selected inflammatory markers, and anthropometric measures, but not in liver enzymes or grade I-II steatosis. Given the small number of trials, the inclusion of non-randomized designs, high heterogeneity, heterogeneous comparators, and the exploratory nature of the sensitivity analyses, these findings are preliminary. Melatonin may merit evaluation as an adjunctive therapy in MASLD, but larger, well-designed randomized trials with standardized comparators and systematic safety reporting are required.

Title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice.
METHODS: Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80-86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73-84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria.
RESULTS: The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6-25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5-5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36-54) mm Hg and 72 (60-87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5-9) mm Hg and 12 (9-15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27-43) mm Hg and 59 (44-70) mm Hg to 9 (7-11) mm Hg and 16 (14-23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

Title: Association between statin intensity and adherence, and MACE in post-STEMI patients: A cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statins are among secondary preventive cardiovascular medications that adherence is critical to their effectiveness. Although, the management of cardiovascular diseases emphasize both intensity and patient adherence, observations show that statin adherence and intensity is not adequate. This study aimed to measure statin adherence and intensity in post-ST elevated myocardial infarction patients and its association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: Of 867 patients in the ST-elevated myocardial infarction cohort study in Isfahan, 549 individuals had data on the intensity of statin therapy. 455 of these patients tended to fill out the adherence questionnaire. Morisky Medication Adherence questionnaire and a checklist consisting potential adherence, and intensity-associated factors were filled out.
RESULTS: In the age group of 50-70 years, increasing age (P = 0.014), receiving physician's support on the consequences of statin discontinuation (P = 0.019), taking lower number of medications (P = 0.045) were significantly associated with statin adherence. Besides, the experience of side effects (P = 0.028) and depressed mood (P ≤ 0.0001) were negatively associated with adherence. None of the measured factors were associated with statin intensity. Statin adherence and statin intensity independently affect MACE, such that even after full adjustment, the chance of experiencing MACE increases 8% (95% CI = 1.02, 1.20) for low-statin adherents and 12% (1.04, 1.28) for patients on non-high statin intensity.
CONCLUSION: Statins have a significant role in the prediction of MACE, based on their intensity and adherence. Educational support from the physician, considering patients' mood and number of medications could improve patients' adherence.

Title: K-CVD as the Best-Calibrated ASCVD Risk Equation Among Three Country-Specific Equations in 9,532 Chinese Adults: A 9-Year Real-World Validation From CHARLS With Decision Curve Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Precise 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk prediction matters for Chinese primary prevention, while domestic risk equations have not been validated in 9-year real-world cohorts, and the Korean K-CVD model has never been validated locally.
METHODS: This study enrolled 9,532 ASCVD-free Chinese adults aged 45-79 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2020) with a 9-year follow-up (114 ASCVD events, incidence 1.20%). Three risk tools (pooled cohort equation (PCE)-US, China-PAR, and K-CVD-Korea) were compared regarding discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC)), calibration, and clinical utility via decision curve analysis (DCA); MICE was adopted to impute missing systolic blood pressure data.
RESULTS: K-CVD presented optimal calibration (predicted/observed ratio = 0.97). PCE overestimated risk by 17%, and China-PAR underestimated risk by 10%. The three models had comparable AUCs (0.775-0.777, P > 0.05). Post logit recalibration yielded identical Brier score (0.0116) for all models. DCA showed negative net benefit at thresholds ≥ 5%; PCE and K-CVD gained slight superiority over China-PAR at 1-2% thresholds matching the low actual event rate.
CONCLUSIONS: K-CVD has the best native calibration in this Chinese cohort. All three equations need formal recalibration for clinical use, and low cut-offs (1-2%) are more suitable for low-risk Chinese adults instead of Western standard thresholds.

Title: Association Between Hepatitis C Virus Infection and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its relationship with coronary artery disease (CAD) remains uncertain.
METHODS: This systematic review included observational studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for CAD outcomes among HCV-infected and HCV-uninfected adults. Adjusted hazard ratios, risk ratios, and odds ratios were combined on the logarithmic scale using a random-effects model and are presented as a summary relative association estimate with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by study design, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection status, and CAD outcome type; meta-regression evaluated follow-up duration, mean age, and the proportion of male participants.
RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included, representing diverse populations including veterans, people living with HIV, dialysis patients, and community-based cohorts. Fifteen studies contributed adjusted estimates to the quantitative synthesis. HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD (summary estimate 1.21; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40; P = 0.007), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 72.1%). The association was statistically significant in cohort studies and in both HIV-specific and non-HIV-specific subgroups, although the HIV-specific subgroup was based on four studies. The myocardial infarction (MI)-specific subgroup was not statistically significant, whereas studies using broader CAD outcomes showed a significant association.
CONCLUSIONS: Chronic HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD. However, substantial heterogeneity, differences in endpoint definitions and populations, residual confounding, and the combination of different effect measures limit causal interpretation and make the clinical importance uncertain. The nonsignificant MI-specific analysis further supports a cautious interpretation. These findings do not establish a cardiovascular benefit of antiviral therapy; prospective studies with standardized CAD endpoints and detailed data on renal disease, antiviral exposure, and lipid-lowering therapy are needed.

Title: Prognostic Value of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index and Controlling Nutritional Status Score in Patients Aged ≥ 75 Years With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malnutrition is common in elderly patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but its prognostic significance and the optimal screening tool remain unclear. This retrospective, single-center study aimed to compare the application of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score in assessing nutritional status in very elderly patients with HFpEF, and to evaluate the association between nutritional status and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: A total of 196 patients aged ≥ 75 years (mean age 92.12 ± 4.28 years, 86.2% male) with HFpEF were enrolled. Nutritional status was categorized using CONUT and GNRI according to standard cut-offs.
RESULTS: Patients with higher CONUT scores or lower GNRI scores (indicating worse nutritional status) had significantly longer hospital stays, lower levels of nutrition-related indices (albumin, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), serum ferritin, transferrin saturation), lower lymphocyte counts, and higher NT-pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), interleukin-6 (IL-6)) (all P < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 11.5 months, 83 patients (42.3%) died. In unadjusted analyses, patients with worse nutritional status had significantly higher rates of all-cause death, all-cause readmission, and heart failure-related readmission (all P < 0.05). Multivariable Cox regression revealed that CONUT (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.366, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.181-1.579, P < 0.001) was an independent risk factor for all-cause mortality, while GNRI (HR = 0.962, 95% CI: 0.927-0.999, P = 0.043) was a protective factor. The CONUT and GNRI showed poor consistency (κ = 0.235, P < 0.01). Using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis based on vital status at the end of follow-up, the area under the curve (AUC) for predicting all-cause mortality was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.80-0.91) for CONUT, 0.79 (95% CI: 0.73-0.86) for GNRI, and 0.87 (95% CI: 0.82-0.92) for a combined model incorporating both scores via logistic regression. Net reclassification improvement (NRI) analysis showed that compared with the GNRI score, the NRI of the CONUT score was 0.580 (95% CI: 0.309-0.852), and the NRI of the combined score was 0.760 (95% CI: 0.499-1.022), both reaching statistical significance (P < 0.01). By contrast, the NRI was 0.083 (95% CI: -0.197 to 0.363, P = 0.560) for the combined score versus the CONUT score.
CONCLUSIONS: Malnutrition is common in elderly patients with HFpEF. CONUT and GNRI scores are associated with adverse outcomes. Compared with GNRI alone, the combined assessment of the two scores improves predictive performance for adverse prognosis in elderly patients with HFpEF, while no incremental benefit is observed over CONUT alone.

Title: Study on the correlation between SPISE-IR, METs-IR, TyG and short-term adverse cardiovascular events in patients with heart failure and diabetes mellitus.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Heart failure (HF) patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at high risk of short-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Insulin resistance (IR) is a key shared mechanism, yet simple prognostic markers remain limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort study compared three IR surrogate indices (SPISE-IR, METs-IR, and TyG) for predicting 18-month post-discharge MACE in hospitalized HF-T2DM patients, aiming to identify practical tools for risk stratification.
METHODS: A total of 477 hospitalized HF-T2DM patients from two tertiary hospitals in Zhejiang (2018-2024) were enrolled according to unified criteria. Baseline clinical, laboratory, echocardiographic, and medication data were collected to calculate SPISE-IR, METs-IR, and TyG. The primary outcome was 18-month post-discharge composite MACE. Associations were evaluated using Cox regression and RCS, while predictive performance was assessed by ROC and PR curves, DCA, NRI, IDI, and subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Of 477 patients, 191 (40.04%) experienced MACE over 18 months, including 3 cardiovascular deaths. Patients with MACE were older, had lower LVEF, worse renal function, and higher NT-proBNP (all p < 0.05). On multivariable analysis, SPISE-IR (HR 9.31, 95% CI 5.96-14.55, p < 0.001) and METs-IR (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.05-1.09, p < 0.001) were associated with MACE, whereas TyG was not (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.95-1.49, p = 0.127). SPISE-IR and METs-IR showed significant nonlinear dose-response relationships and yielded AUCs of 0.790 and 0.801, respectively, versus 0.539 for TyG. Higher SPISE-IR and METs-IR quartiles were associated with progressively higher cumulative event risk (log-rank p < 0.001), whereas no significant between-quartile difference was observed for TyG. Adding either index to the baseline model significantly improved NRI and IDI (all p < 0.05); SPISE-IR showed numerically larger NRI and IDI improvements than METs-IR. Subgroup analyses showed a consistent SPISE-IR association, whereas METs-IR exhibited effect modification by age, sex, smoking status, and hypertension; TyG remained largely non-significant. Heart failure rehospitalization accounted for 138 of 191 MACE (72.3%). After exclusion of 24 recurrent-angina events, SPISE-IR (HR 10.83, 95% CI 6.71-17.45) and METs-IR (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.06-1.09) remained associated with the strict MACE endpoint (both p < 0.001). After 1,000 bootstrap resamples, optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.818 for the clinical + SPISE-IR model and 0.806 for the clinical + METs-IR model. In center-based external validation, their AUCs were 0.804 and 0.806, respectively.
CONCLUSION: SPISE-IR and METs-IR are associated with 18-month MACE risk in hospitalized HF-T2DM patients and show better predictive performance than TyG. These indices may provide additional value for risk stratification in this population.

Title: Coronary plaque characteristics of acute myocardial infarction patients with and without previous ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) occurring after ischemic cerebral stroke leads to substantially worse short- and long-term outcomes, as indicated by emerging evidence. Few studies explore possible plaque features.
METHODS: From September 2019 to December 2021, 1050 AMI patients were enrolled. The individuals were divided into two groups based on whether they had suffered an ischemic stroke before percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Patients from both groups underwent 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) with a caliper width of 0.02. Ultimately, the final study cohort comprised 386 patients.
RESULTS: Regarding culprit lesions, patients in the stroke group exhibited a greater prevalence of thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFA, 70.0% vs. 55.4%, p = 0.003), macrophage accumulation (52.3% vs. 39.4%, p = 0.011), a longer lipid core length (15.3 ± 7.4 mm vs. 13.5 ± 6.4 mm, p = 0.013), and a higher lipid index (3,465.0 ± 2,135.8 vs. 2,946.4 ± 1,784.4, p = 0.011), compared to non-stroke patients. Concerning non-culprit plaques, prior stroke was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of TCFA (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.15-3.74, p = 0.014). The clinical follow-up results revealed a significantly higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in the stroke group (8.9% vs. 4.2%, p = 0.009, HR 2.61, 95% CI 1.28-5.34), along with a greater frequency of recurrent stroke (4.2% vs. 1.6%, p = 0.019, HR 3.78, 95% CI 1.23-9.30) and a higher cardiac mortality rate (5.8% vs. 1.6%, p = 0.011, HR 3.55, 95% CI 1.33-9.47) than the non-stroke group.
CONCLUSION: In stroke patients, coronary multivessel disease is common and characterized by high-risk plaque features and increased cardiovascular event susceptibility, with prior ischemic stroke being associated with a higher prevalence of these OCT-defined high-risk features.

Title: Thrombectomy improves functional outcome in large core stroke partly by preventing severe cerebral edema: a real-world mediation analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is effective in large infarct core (LIC) stroke, but mortality and severe disability remain high when cerebral edema (CED) develops. We assessed the effect of EVT on CED and outcomes in LIC patients within 24 h of stroke onset.
METHODS: In a prospective observational cohort study, we enrolled patients with large-vessel occlusion in the anterior circulation, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score ≥ 6, Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) ≤ 5, and admission within 24 h of onset. The primary outcome was mass effect (ME) due to severe cerebral edema, defined as a maximum midline shift (MLS) ≥ 5 mm on follow-up imaging within 72 h. The secondary outcome was favorable outcome, defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Safety outcomes were determined by death at 90 days, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) according to SITS-MOST criteria. Treatment effects were estimated using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with doubly robust adjustment. Mediation analysis assessed whether ME contributed to the association between EVT and favorable outcome.
RESULTS: Of 202 patients (EVT group: 119; medical management group: 83), after IPTW adjustment, EVT was associated with lower odds of ME [31.1% vs. 51.8%; IPTW-adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 0.28; 95% CI, 0.12-0.67], higher odds of favorable outcome (aOR, 2.32; 95% CI, 1.01-5.31), and lower mortality (aOR 0.45; 95% CI, 0.21-0.97) with no excess sICH. ME independently predicted poor outcome (aOR for mRS 4-6, 7.7; 95% CI, 3.01-19.69), and approximately 29.5% of the association between EVT and favorable outcome was statistically mediated by ME attenuation. Two admission variables-lower baseline ASPECTS and higher admission glucose-independently predicted ME (optimism-corrected AUC 0.82).
CONCLUSION: In large-core stroke, EVT was associated with better functional outcome and lower odds of mass effect. Approximately one-third of EVT's functional benefit was statistically mediated by attenuation of severe CED. ME independently predicted poor outcome, whereas lower ASPECTS and higher admission glucose identified patients at greater risk of severe swelling, supporting bedside risk stratification to guide intensified monitoring and edema-targeted management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier [NCT06016348].

Title: Incidence of dysphagia in acute stroke patients-a prospective multicentre cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of dysphagia after stroke remains uncertain in the context of contemporary stroke care. Reported estimates vary widely due to heterogenous assessment methods and limited use of standardized and validated evaluations. Dysphagia is also frequently underestimated despite its strong associations with increased mortality, morbidity, and pneumonia-related hospitalisation. Reliable estimates on incidence based on standardized swallowing assessments are therefore needed to improve identification of dysphagia and to improve clinical management. This study was conducted within the framework of the large prospective multicenter study Dysphagia Evaluation after Stroke (DESIRE) to address these knowledge gaps. Thus, the objective was to determine the incidence of dysphagia in the acute phase following stroke in patients receiving current stroke care using standardized assessment methods, and to identify factors independently associated with post-stroke dysphagia.
METHODS: Consecutive acute stroke patients admitted to four Swedish stroke units were assessed within 96 h after stroke onset using the Gugging Swallowing Screen (GUSS) administered by a speech-language pathologist. Clinical data on stroke characteristics, dysphagia risk factors, pneumonia incidence, and discharge destination were prospectively collected. Multivariable regression models were used to identify factors associated with dysphagia.
RESULTS: Of 1,093 patients (468 women, 42.8%; median age 75 years), the incidence of dysphagia was 38.8%. Independent predictors of dysphagia included dysarthria (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.85, CI = 1.32-2.59, p = <0.001), greater stroke severity (aOR: 1.16, CI = 1.12-1.19, p = <0.001), female sex (aOR: 1.39, CI = 1.00-1.92, p = <0.047), infratentorial lesions (aOR: 2.01, CI = 1.10-3.69, p = 0.024) and older age (p = <0.001). Dysphagia was significantly associated with longer hospital stay (ratio of mean: 1.64, CI = 1.36-1.98, p = <0.001), and with increased odds of discharge to nursing homes (aOR: 4.84, CI = 2.46-9.56, p = <0.001), short-term care facilities (aOR: 4.69, CI = 1.87-11.76, p = <0.001) or in-hospital death (aOR: 16.67, CI = 2.10-132.05, p = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: Dysphagia affected more than one third of acute stroke patients, and was associated with greater stroke severity, extended hospitalisation, and adverse discharge outcomes. These findings underscore the need for early identification and targeted management of dysphagia to reduce complications and improve patients' outcomes.

Title: Asymmetric biphasic pulsed field ablation of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: clinical assessment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is a non-thermal, tissue-selective therapy for atrial fibrillation. In this study, we evaluated the safety and efficacy of a novel asymmetric biphasic PFA system, which combines a unique pulse-parameter configuration with a dedicated, adjustable six-spline catheter.
METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, single-arm study was conducted in China. Patients with drug-refractory paroxysmal AF underwent pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using a 1,000 V asymmetric biphasic PFA system with a novel parameter configuration. The primary effectiveness endpoint was freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence through 12 months post-blanking. The primary safety endpoint was predefined serious adverse events. The secondary safety endpoint was hemolysis and silent cerebral lesions (SCLs).
RESULTS: Among 120 enrolled patients, 105 underwent ablation and completed the 12-month follow-up, while 15 patients withdrew before the PFA operation. Acute PVI was successfully achieved in all 420 targeted veins. At 12 months, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of freedom from atrial arrhythmia recurrence was 69.5% (95% CI, 60.1-77.5%). The observed 12-month effectiveness was within the range reported in previous studies of PFA technologies. Regarding safety, major procedural complications-including pulmonary vein stenosis, phrenic nerve injury, atrioesophageal fistula, stroke, and acute kidney injury (AKI)-were entirely absent. However, one patient (0.95%) experienced a transient coronary vasospasm that was successfully resolved with an intracoronary vasodilator. Additionally, SCLs were detected in two patients (1.9%). While laboratory hemolysis was a common finding, it did not lead to renal impairment.
CONCLUSIONS: This asymmetric biphasic PFA system achieved complete acute PVI and 12-month effectiveness was within the range reported in previous studies of PFA technologies. It showed a favorable safety profile, with few SCLs and no hemolysis-related AKI.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=134973, identifier ChiCTR2200062157.

Title: The ipsilesional DTI-ALPS index provides modest incremental prognostic value beyond clinical models for 90-day outcome in patients with acute MCA occlusion treated with intravenous thrombolysis: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Impaired perivascular fluid dynamics may contribute to secondary brain injury after acute ischemic stroke, yet its prognostic relevance remains uncertain. We investigated whether the Diffusion Tensor Image Analysis along the Perivascular Space (ALPS) index-a quantitative MRI marker of perivascular fluid dynamics-provides incremental predictive value for long-term functional outcomes in patients with acute middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) treated with intravenous thrombolysis.
METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort study, 128 patients underwent multimodal brain MRI within 24 h of admission, and the ALPS index was calculated in the hemisphere ipsilateral to the occlusion (ipsilesional ALPS). Favorable outcome at 90 days was defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors, with covariates (admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score, LDL cholesterol, and smoking status) prespecified on clinical grounds rather than selected by univariate screening. Incremental discriminative value was assessed by comparing nested models using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and the likelihood-ratio test (LRT), which is preferable to DeLong's test for nested models. Calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, Nagelkerke R2) and internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples (optimism-corrected AUC) were performed.
INTERPRETATION: Lower admission NIHSS score [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) per 1-point increase: 0.890, 95% CI: 0.813-0.976; p = 0.013] and lower LDL cholesterol (aOR per 1 mmol/L: 0.660, 95% CI: 0.472-0.923; p = 0.015) were independently associated with favorable outcome, whereas the ipsilesional ALPS index showed a directionally consistent, non-significant association (aOR per 0.1-unit increase: 1.525, 95% CI: 0.948-2.454; p = 0.082). Adding the ALPS index to a base model containing NIHSS and LDL yielded a modest but significant improvement in discrimination (AUC 0.681 to 0.699; ΔAUC = 0.018; LRT p = 0.042); calibration was adequate (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.31 and 0.28), and the gain persisted after bootstrap optimism correction (ΔAUC = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory cohort, the ipsilesional ALPS index showed a consistent directional association with 90-day functional outcome and provided a modest but significant incremental improvement in discrimination beyond NIHSS and LDL cholesterol; the magnitude of this gain is small and requires external validation.

Title: Dose-response association and predictive value of plasma aldosterone concentration for cardiometabolic multimorbidity in patients with hypertension: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to investigate the relationship between cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) and plasma aldosterone concentration (PAC) among patients with hypertension, to characterize the potential dose-response pattern, and to assess whether the inclusion of PAC into a conventional risk model improves risk reclassification and clinical utility.
METHODS: Between January 2010 and January 2026, 7,677 hospitalized hypertensive patients without CMM at baseline were included in this retrospective cohort analysis. The follow-up period was 3.52 years on average. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were performed to examine the association between PAC and the risk of incident CMM. The incremental predictive value of PAC was evaluated for 3-year risk prediction using time-dependent ROC analysis with inverse probability of censoring weighting (IPCW), survival-based net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), calibration assessment, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Based on the potential interaction observed in the subgroup analysis, RCS analyses stratified by serum potassium level and a bivariate penalized spline model were used to characterize the joint nonlinear associations of serum potassium and PAC with the risk of CMM. The Boruta algorithm was additionally applied for feature selection and assessment of variable importance.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 1,949 incident cases of CMM were documented. Patients in the highest quartile of baseline PAC (Q4) had a considerably greater cumulative likelihood of CMM than those in the other quartiles, according to Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank P < 0.05). In the multivariable Cox regression analysis, each 1-ng/dL increment in PAC was associated with a 2% higher hazard of incident CMM (hazard ratio [HR], 1.02; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02-1.03). Compared with the lowest quartile (Q1), the adjusted HRs were 1.19 (95% CI, 1.04-1.36) for Q2, 1.32 (95% CI, 1.16-1.52) for Q3, and 1.65 (95% CI, 1.45-1.87) for Q4, with a significant trend across quartiles (P for trend<0.001). RCS analysis demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between PAC and the risk of CMM (P for nonlinearity < 0.001), identifying an estimated inflection point at approximately 15.34 ng/dL, above which the risk curve showed an upward trend. Subgroup analyses indicated that the PAC-CMM association may differ by serum potassium status (P for interaction < 0.05). After PAC was added to the baseline prediction model, the time-dependent AUC increased from 0.678 to 0.735 (P < 0.001), with a net reclassification improvement of 0.372 and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.038 (P < 0.05). DCA suggested that incorporating PAC may provide additional estimated net benefit across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. The Boruta feature-selection algorithm identified PAC as an important predictor, and the overall findings remained consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: The possibility of a CMM incident was positively correlated with PAC in a nonlinear fashion, and this correlation differed depending on serum potassium levels. Incorporating PAC into a conventional risk model was associated with improved predictive performance and greater net clinical benefit, suggesting that PAC may provide additional prognostic information for cardiometabolic risk stratification among patients with hypertension.

Title: Robot-assisted training for post-stroke lower-limb dysfunction: an umbrella review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to reappraise published systematic reviews and meta-analyses on robot-assisted training for lower-limb motor dysfunction after stroke and evaluate their methodological quality, reporting completeness, and certainty of evidence.
METHODS: Seven databases were searched, including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science, from inception to January 15, 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses that were based on randomized controlled trials. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal. The methodological quality of the included reviews was assessed using A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews (AMSTAR) 2, and the reporting of this umbrella review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews (PRIOR) guideline. The reporting completeness of the included systematic reviews and meta-analyses was evaluated using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 checklist. The certainty of evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.
RESULTS: Nineteen reviews were included, comprising eight Chinese and 11 English publications. Primary-study overlap across reviews was moderate (CCA = 7.44%). According to AMSTAR 2, three reviews were rated as high quality, six as moderate quality, six as low quality, and four as critically low quality. PRISMA completeness scores ranged from 14.5 to 23.5 out of a maximum possible score of 27. Among the 70 extracted outcomes, none was rated as high-certainty evidence, 20 were of moderate certainty, 32 were of low certainty, and 18 were of very low certainty. Overall, robot-assisted training showed potential benefits for balance and lower-extremity motor function, whereas evidence for walking-related outcomes remained less consistent.
CONCLUSION: Evidence was most consistent for balance and lower-extremity motor impairment, whereas findings for walking independence, endurance, functional mobility, and gait speed were less consistent and generally supported by low-to-moderate certainty evidence. More rigorously designed primary trials and better-conducted systematic reviews are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The review protocol was registered under Prospero, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/home (Registration No: CRD420261419692).

Title: The snake-head sign on MRI in craniocervical junction dural arteriovenous fistulas: a novel imaging feature and a hypothesis of venous remodeling and congestion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Craniocervical junction (CCJ)-region dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs) are rare but potentially reversible causes of venous congestive myelopathy, often difficult to recognize due to non-specific presentation. We observed a characteristic pattern of intramedullary T2 hyperintensity on sagittal MRI, involving the medulla and upper cervical cord with a rostral end divided into ventral and dorsal limbs, which we termed the "snake-head sign." This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of this feature among reported CCJ-region dAVF cases and explore its clinical and anatomical correlates.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed published cases of CCJ-region or adjacent dAVFs reported between 1996 and 2026 that included retrievable sagittal T2-weighted or FLAIR images. The presence of the snake-head sign was assessed, and clinical, angiographic, and treatment-related variables were extracted, including fistula location, feeding artery, draining vein direction, treatment modality, and outcome. Associations with the sign were evaluated using univariate analyses. Given the retrospective, literature-based design and limited sample size, findings were considered hypothesis-generating.
RESULTS: Among 64 reported cases, the snake-head sign was identified in 31 (48.4%). No significant associations were found between the sign and age, sex, symptom duration, feeding artery, treatment modality, or outcome. However, a non-significant trend was observed for venous drainage configuration: cases with cranial convergence of the draining vein toward the CCJ more frequently demonstrated the sign, whereas purely caudal drainage patterns showed it less often. Fistulas at lower cervical nerve-root sleeves, requiring a longer cranial venous course, also showed higher sign frequency. These findings suggest the sign may reflect venous outflow geometry rather than arterial source or fistula location.
CONCLUSION: The snake-head sign is a recognizable MRI feature present in roughly half of reported CCJ-region dAVF cases. Its identification may raise clinical suspicion for CCJ-related dAVF, particularly in unexplained venous congestive myelopathy. The trend toward a higher frequency of the sign in cases with cranially convergent venous drainage raises the hypothesis that it reflects concentrated venous congestion at this anatomical transition zone. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized imaging review and angiographic correlation are needed to confirm its diagnostic value and clarify the underlying mechanism.

Title: Effects of morning versus evening exercise on vascular function in older adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is a common complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), with increased risk closely associated with vascular dysfunction. Exercise is an effective strategy for improving vascular health, but whether exercise timing influences long-term vascular adaptations in patients with T2DM remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of morning versus evening exercise on vascular function in older adults with T2DM.
METHODS: Sixty-six older adults with T2DM were randomised to morning exercise, evening exercise, or control (n = 22 each). The exercise groups received 12 weeks of online moderate-intensity aerobic and resistance exercises, three times per week. The morning group exercised from 9:00 to 10:10, and the evening group from 19:00 to 20:10. The control group maintained their usual lifestyle and attended weekly health education sessions without structured exercise. Blood pressure, brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) and plasma nitric oxide (NO) levels were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Outcomes were analysed using two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance, with exploratory analyses directly comparing the two exercise groups.
RESULTS: Fifty-eight participants were included in the final analysis (morning, n = 20; evening, n = 19; control, n = 19). Significant group × time interactions were observed for FMD, baPWV, systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and plasma NO (all p < 0.05). Both exercise groups increased FMD and reduced SBP, MAP, and baPWV from baseline (all p < 0.05). Plasma NO increased significantly following the evening exercise (p = 0.003), whereas no significant changes were observed following the morning exercise (p = 0.722). At post-intervention, the evening group exhibited lower MAP (p = 0.012) and higher FMD (p = 0.019) and NO levels (p = 0.012) than controls. Exploratory analyses showed a greater baPWV reduction with evening exercise (group × time interaction, p = 0.034). The increase in plasma NO was numerically greater with evening exercise, although the interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.051).
CONCLUSIONS: Exercise timing may influence vascular adaptations in older adults with T2DM, with evening exercise potentially offering additional benefits, particularly for arterial stiffness.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=200163, identifier ChiCTR2300073737.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Clinical Trial

Title: Serial urinary NGAL and CK20 for dynamic cardiovascular risk stratification in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a retrospective clinical cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is commonly managed with intravesical BCG, whereas pembrolizumab is reserved for selected BCG-unresponsive high-risk disease. Cardiovascular adverse events (CVAEs) may occur during cancer therapy, but BCG-related systemic inflammatory effects and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-mediated cardiovascular immune-related adverse events have distinct pathophysiology and clinical kinetics. We evaluated serial urinary NGAL and CK20 as non-invasive candidate biomarkers for dynamic CVAE risk stratification.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort of 215 NMIBC patients (2021-2023) underwent serial urinary NGAL (ELISA) and CK20 mRNA (qRT-PCR) assessment at baseline and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after TURBT. Biomarker cutoffs were derived in a 70% training split and evaluated in the remaining 30% internal validation split. Cardiovascular surveillance included echocardiography, ECG, BNP, and high-sensitivity troponin I. The primary endpoint was CTCAE-graded CVAE; Cox regression evaluated associations with cardiovascular event-free survival (CVEFS).
RESULTS: CVAEs occurred in 74/215 patients (34.4%). The BCG cohort comprised 112 patients; the pembrolizumab subgroup comprised only 25 patients and is therefore interpreted exploratorily. Four ICI-associated myocarditis cases occurred in the pembrolizumab subgroup (16.0%; exact 95% CI 4.5-36.1%). Baseline urinary NGAL was higher in patients with subsequent CVAEs (128.7 ± 38.9 vs. 69.3 ± 33.7 ng/mL, p < 0.001). Combined NGAL + CK20 yielded an internally validated 6-month AUC of 0.913 (95% CI 0.866-0.960), and dual positivity was associated with CVAE risk (aHR=4.12, 95% CI 2.71-6.26). The reported lead-time analysis suggested earlier NGAL change before echocardiographic LVEF decline; this finding requires prospective confirmation.
CONCLUSIONS: Serial urinary NGAL and CK20 are promising candidate markers for CVAE risk stratification in this retrospective NMIBC cohort. The findings are driven principally by the overall cohort and the larger BCG-treated group; ICI-specific observations are hypothesis-generating because only 25 patients received pembrolizumab. The proposed biomarker thresholds and surveillance framework require prospective, multicenter external validation before clinical implementation.

Title: Prevalence of many comorbidities is similar irrespective of the time since HIV diagnosis in persons ageing with HIV who have survived to age 65 years.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the prevalence of comorbidity in persons with HIV ≥65 years of age based on the time from HIV diagnosis.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational cohort study.
METHODS: Data was collected from 540 participants in the CHANGE HIV (Correlates of Healthy Aging in Geriatric HIV) study, a longitudinal study of HIV in persons aged 65 years and older from seven primary and tertiary care centres in Canada between 2019 and 2026. We compared the baseline prevalence of comorbidities stratified by the cumulative time since known HIV diagnosis (<20 years, 20-30 years and >30 years) and controlled for demographic, HIV and lifestyle factors.
RESULTS: The cohort was 90% male, median age 69 years, 76% white, median CD4 561 cells/mm3 and 92% with an undetectable viral load. They had a median of 3 (range 0-12) comorbid conditions. There was no difference in prevalence of coronary artery disease, dyslipidaemia, peripheral artery disease, stroke, chronic obstructive lung disease, asthma, arthritis, Parkinson's disease, HIV-associated neurocognitive dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, diabetes or liver disease based on time since HIV diagnosis. After accounting for confounders, longer time since HIV diagnosis was associated with higher prevalence of cancer, diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Of the comorbidities only peripheral neuropathy, dyslipidaemia and Kaposi's sarcoma occurred at a younger age.
CONCLUSIONS: Prevalence of many comorbidities was not increased in those with longer time since HIV diagnosis. Lifestyle factors (smoking, substance use and diet) are important contributors to non-infectious comorbidities in this population, and increased prevalence of cancer reinforces the importance of preventative screening.

Title: Subcutaneous Defibrillator for Primary Prevention in Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3-5: The Single-Arm STEADIED Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prospective data on the subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) in chronic kidney disease (CKD) are lacking. We estimated the rate of appropriate ICD therapy with the S-ICD in CKD stage 3-5 with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 35%.
METHODS: In this single-arm exploratory study, adults with CKD stage 3-5 and a guideline-based primary-prevention indication received an EMBLEM MRI S-ICD at eight Korean centers. The primary endpoint, appropriate ICD therapy, was hypothesized at 18% versus a historical rate of 7.8% (α = 0.05, 80% power, planned N = 77; exact binomial test).
RESULTS: The study was terminated early after 39 patients (51% of target; achieved power ≈61%). Mean LVEF was 27.8% and median eGFR 11.7 mL/min/1.73 m2; 71.8% had CKD stage 5 and 69.2% were on hemodialysis. Over a median follow-up of 361 days, appropriate ICD therapy occurred in 2 patients (5.1%; 95% CI, 1.4-16.9), significantly below the hypothesized 18% (p = 0.036). Inappropriate shocks occurred in 5 patients (12.8%; 95% CI, 5.6-26.7; 8 shocks), a proportion 2.5 times that of appropriate therapy, from external electromagnetic interference (2 patients), multiple counting after automatic SMART Pass deactivation (2), and supraventricular misclassification (1). Three deaths (7.7%) occurred, none device-related or documented as arrhythmic (one undetermined); all hospitalizations were for heart failure, and no systemic device infection occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single-arm study, appropriate ICD therapy was infrequent and exceeded by inappropriate shocks, while non-arrhythmic competing mortality dominated the clinical course. These hypothesis-generating findings support cautious patient selection, verification of filter status during follow-up, and larger comparative studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS), Republic of Korea; identifier KCT0005596.

Title: Comparative treatment effects of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation in clinical practice vary over time due to channelling.
Abstract:
AIM: Temporal shifts in patient characteristics can influence comparative treatment effects within a certain indication. We investigated patient characteristics and comparative effectiveness and safety for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and warfarin over the time period where DOACs replaced warfarin as preferred stroke prophylaxis in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF).
METHODS: We applied the cohort design to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and created 12 sequential subcohorts of patients with NVAF between 2011 and 2023. Patients with a DOAC or warfarin prescription following a 1-year prescription-free period were included. Baseline characteristics were compared between subcohorts. Survival analysis was used to evaluate the risk of ischaemic stroke (effectiveness outcome) and major bleeds (safety outcome).
RESULTS: We included 207 393 patients with NVAF (45% women, 77% DOAC users, mean age 76 years). In early subcohorts, a history of stroke/transient ischaemic attack was more common among DOAC users. In later subcohorts, diabetes, deep venous thrombosis/pulmonary embolism and antihypertensive use were more common among warfarin users. History of other cardiovascular disease, renal failure and diuretic use were consistently higher among warfarin users. Over time, the crude stroke hazard ratio for DOAC users compared with warfarin users shifted from 2.66 (95% CI 2.00-3.52) to 0.62 (0.23-1.67). This trend was attenuated in adjusted analyses. No such trends were seen for major bleeds.
CONCLUSION: DOACs had unfavourable effectiveness estimates in earlier subcohorts, potentially due to preferential prescribing to higher risk patients. Early observational studies may encounter initial biases, underscoring the need for robust methodological approaches when evaluating newly introduced medicines.

Title: The interconnections between novel adiposity indices and cardiometabolic multimorbidity in Chinese adults: a population-based cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) poses a major public health challenge. This study aimed to investigate the associations between seven novel adiposity indices and CMM prevalence in Chinese adults.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis, we included 10,383 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). CMM was defined as the presence of at least two of the following: hypertension, diabetes, coronary heart disease, or stroke. We assessed the Lipid Accumulation Product (LAP), Visceral Adiposity Index (VAI), Body Roundness Index (BRI), Atherogenic Index of Plasma (AIP), C-reactive protein triglyceride glucose index (CTI), Conicity Index (CI), and Residual Cholesterol (RC). Associations were examined using multivariable logistic regression and non-linear association analysis.
RESULTS: All indices showed significant positive associations with CMM in the fully adjusted model. After standardization to a per-1-SD increase, CTI showed the strongest association (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.49-1.65), followed by LAP (OR = 1.49) and AIP (OR = 1.44). Significant non-linear relationships with inflection points were identified for LAP, VAI, BRI, AIP, RC, and CI, whereas CTI showed a linear association. In an exploratory variance decomposition analysis, CTI accounted for 26.50% to 43.13% of the statistical variance shared among LAP, CI, BRI, and CMM. This estimate is purely descriptive of shared statistical variance and reflects only the associations observed in this cross-sectional sample. CTI and LAP showed the highest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.669 and 0.668, respectively), though still modest, and significantly outperformed most other indices (DeLong P < 0.01). All AUCs were below 0.70, suggesting limited utility as standalone screening tools.
CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional study, several novel adiposity indices-particularly CTI, LAP, and AIP-were significantly associated with prevalent CMM in Chinese adults, with evidence of non-linear relationships. In the variance decomposition analysis, CTI statistically accounted for a substantial portion of the shared variance between other adiposity indices and CMM. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not support immediate clinical translation. They suggest that these indices may warrant further investigation in prospective cohorts to evaluate their predictive utility. However, they are purely associational findings, and validation in independent studies is required before any clinical use can be considered.

Title: Enhancing team process improvement through the implementation of the Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM): the case of medication reconciliation at hospital discharge.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare professionals working in complex dynamic work systems are often forced to adjust their behaviour to changing conditions, possibly causing practice variation. Teams can analyse the (un)desirability of those variations by conducting team process improvement. This refers to a learning process in which teams reflect on past performances and formulate improvement strategies. The objective of this study was to identify barriers and facilitators for team process improvement when applying the Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM).
METHODS: This study entails a multicentre prospective study. Nine cardiology and orthopaedic wards from eight Dutch hospitals participated in this study. For each ward, team process improvement consisted of four phases: 1) Constructing FRAM, 2) Discussing differences between protocols and daily practice, 3) Reflecting on intended improvements, 4) Evaluating team reflection process.
RESULTS: On all wards, we identified several discrepancies between protocol and daily practice. After sharing and discussing these results, most wards proposed improvements aimed at making the process safer and more efficient. Facilitators for team process improvement included: team composition (dedicated task forces and multidisciplinary teams) and being familiar with the analysed process. Identified barriers included a lacking motivation and limited involvement from the ward's contact person in the study.
CONCLUSIONS: This study showed that FRAM can provide valuable input to initiate team process improvement. The reflection process helped healthcare professionals to decide whether adjustments are needed to keep patients safe or if they introduced risks that were meant to be reduced by implementing protocols. To undertake successful team reflection, we suggest assembling dedicated task forces that regularly evaluate the process. The task force should consist of healthcare professionals from different disciplines.

Title: Self-management of blood pressure following hypertensive pregnancy (the SNAP2 trial): a prospective, multi-centre, unblinded, randomised controlled trial protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy affect around 10% of pregnant women and can continue following childbirth. Such hypertension that persists postnatally can be unpredictable and may have long-term health consequences but care can be sub-optimal with poor support as women transition from maternity to community services. However, there is little evidence to guide best practice for managing postnatal hypertension, and these gaps in evidence and care disproportionately affect women from minoritised ethnic and socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds. Previous work suggests self-management where women self-monitor blood pressure (BP) and self-titrate medication, overseen by clinicians, could improve BP control in the short and long term but has been limited to single geographical areas. The aim of the SNAP2 trial is to evaluate the clinical and cost effectiveness of a self-management intervention at scale.
METHODS: SNAP2 is a multi-centre unblinded randomised controlled trial. A planned sample of at least 628 participants across England with any pregnancy hypertension will be randomised within 7 days post birth to a digitally-supported self-management intervention, including self-monitoring of BP and clinician-guided titration of anti-hypertensive medication, or usual care. A cross-cutting theme is evaluating how health equity can best be ensured in postnatal hypertension management. The primary outcome is the difference in mean daytime ambulatory diastolic BP between intervention and usual care, measured between 22 to 39 weeks postpartum. Secondary outcomes include other measures of BP, maternal quality-of-life, medication adherence, adverse outcomes and readmission to hospital up to one year after birth. A qualitative process evaluation will explore how the intervention is implemented and integrated into women's lives and clinical pathways. An economic analysis will evaluate within-trial cost and outcomes and long-term economic modelling.
DISCUSSION: The SNAP2 trial will provide essential data on the clinical and cost-effectiveness of a self-management intervention that, if proven effective, could improve current sub-optimal postnatal care for BP management.
