In-depth qualitative and equity data will provide important insight to inform potential implementation. Throughout the manuscript, in our references to women, we encompass all birthing people. CLINICAL TRAIL NUMBER: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN11042045 .

Title: The effect of early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
Journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
Abstract:
OBJECT: This study aimed to investigate the effect of implementing early rehabilitation nursing on the recovery of cardiac function indices and prognosis after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) treatment in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: Patients diagnosed with AMI and treated with PCI between March 2020 and May 2024 were selected as the study participants. This was a prospective randomised controlled trial; patients were randomly allocated to an observation group and a control group using a random number table method (157 cases per group). The control group received routine nursing after surgery, whereas the observation group received structured early rehabilitation nursing. After 6 months of intervention, cardiac function indices, the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and quality of life were compared between the two groups. Cardiac function indices included stroke volume (SV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) and 6-minute walking distance (6MWD). The World Health Organization Quality of Life Measurement Brief Form was used to evaluate quality of life.
RESULTS: After nursing intervention, the levels of SV, LVEF and 6MWD in the cardiac function indices of the observation group were higher than those of the control group, whereas the levels of LVEDV were lower than those of the control group; the differences between the two groups were significant (p < 0.05). The total incidence of MACE in the observation group was lower than that in the control group (p < 0.05). In the comparison of quality-of-life scores, the observation group scored higher than the control group in five domains (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Early rehabilitation nursing for patients with AMI can effectively improve patients' cardiac function indices and reduce the risk of MACE, thereby improving their quality of life.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: ISRCTN18094960.

Title: Escitalopram for psychological symptoms and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) often have comorbid depression and anxiety, which worsen prognosis. Escitalopram, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, is used for these symptoms, but evidence on its psychological and cardiovascular effects in CHD is limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated its effects on psychological symptoms and cardiovascular outcomes in CHD.
METHODS: We systematically searched five databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of escitalopram vs. control in adults with CHD. Data were extracted to avoid double counting; extended follow-up data were analyzed separately. Outcomes included depression/anxiety scale changes, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and revascularization. Random-effects models and sensitivity analyses were used.
RESULTS: Five RCTs were included. Overall depression score change was not significant (SMD = -0.70, 95% CI -1.57 to 0.18), but medium-term (12-24 weeks) follow-up showed improvement (SMD = -0.39, 95% CI -0.58 to -0.20). Anxiety scores significantly decreased with escitalopram (SMD = -0.64, 95% CI -1.12 to -0.17). Pooled data from two studies were compatible with reductions in MACE (RR = 0.74, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.94) and myocardial infarction (RR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.96), however, approximately 90% of the pooled weight came from the post-treatment follow-up of a single trial, so these findings are hypothesis-generating. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for all-cause mortality or revascularization.
CONCLUSION: Escitalopram appears effective for selected psychological symptoms in CHD without evidence of major cardiovascular harm; current evidence is insufficient to establish a cardiovascular benefit, and the observed MACE and myocardial infarction reductions are hypothesis-generating. Treatment should aim primarily to improve psychological well-being and quality of life.

Title: Monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio and carotid atherosclerosis in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a comparative analysis of systemic inflammatory indices.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic inflammation indices have been linked to carotid atherosclerosis (CAS); however, their comparative performance and relative independence within the metabolic-inflammatory milieu of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear. We aimed to identify the inflammatory index showing the strongest and most consistent association with CAS and to exploratorily assess potential mediating pathways.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study of 24,683 adults with MASLD, eight systemic inflammation indices were calculated. Associations with ultrasonography-defined CAS were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. All indices were entered into a mutually adjusted model to identify the most independent marker. Dose-response relationships, subgroup analyses, and exploratory mediation analyses were performed.
RESULTS: After full adjustment, the monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) showed the strongest association with CAS (odds ratio [OR] per 1-standard deviation increase: 1.092, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.054-1.132). In the mutually adjusted model including all eight indices, only MHR remained independently associated with CAS (OR: 1.062, 95% CI 1.005-1.123). The MHR-CAS association was linear (P for nonlinearity = 0.416) and stronger among individuals without hypertension (P for interaction = 0.027). Exploratory mediation analysis suggested that approximately 4.0% of the association was statistically mediated by fasting plasma glucose (FPG)-related pathways, observed exclusively in non-lean MASLD.
CONCLUSION: Among commonly used systemic inflammation indices, MHR appears to be a robust and independent marker associated with carotid atherosclerosis in MASLD. Its association is linear, modified by hypertension status, and modestly linked to glucose-related pathways in a phenotype-specific manner, supporting its potential role as a complementary biomarker for vascular risk stratification in MASLD.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Types of adult intensive care units and admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023: a nationwide cohort study.
Journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Türkiye has one of the highest intensive care unit (ICU) bed capacities among middle-income countries but also globally. Nevertheless, little is known about the characteristics of ICUs in Türkiye, their temporal trends, and ICU admissions and readmissions. We sought to analyze the structural characteristics of all adult ICUs and the clinical profiles of ICU admissions across Türkiye.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using data from the Turkish Ministry of Health National Electronic Database. We analyzed adult ICU admissions across all levels and types over 6 years (2018-2023) and documented patient demographics, comorbidities, admission diagnoses, and ICU outcomes.
RESULTS: We retrieved data on 3,362,539 ICU admissions. Among 22 ICU types, mixed ICUs accounted for the highest proportion of admissions (31.4%), followed by coronary (23.7%), anesthesiology (14.3%), medical (6.1%), and surgical (6.0%) ICUs. The proportion of mixed ICU beds decreased from 44.0% in 2018 to 25.1% in 2023. Most ICU beds were in state (public) hospitals (50.8%), followed by private hospitals (34.8%). The number of ICU beds increased from 2019, with a notable rise in state hospitals after 2020. The average number of ICU admissions was 659 per 100,000 population annually. The median patient age was 65 [interquartile range, 39-91] yr, and the ICU mortality was 15.5%. The leading admission diagnoses were respiratory failure (10.1%), cerebrovascular disease (7.1%), and acute kidney injury (5.2%). Hypertension (67.5%) and coronary artery disease (44.8%) were common comorbidities, particularly in nonsurvivors. The 7-day ICU readmission rate was 3.0%.
CONCLUSIONS: The present comprehensive analysis of ICU admissions in Türkiye between 2018 and 2023 highlights a shift toward specialization with a decrease in mixed ICUs. The impact of ICU diversity on resource use and patient outcomes requires further evaluation.

Title: JAK inhibitor retention and adverse event-related discontinuation in elderly patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a real-world cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in elderly patients poses management challenges due to comorbidities and polypharmacy. JAK inhibitors offer oral-administration advantages, but their safety in the elderly remains uncertain.
METHOD: We compared the retention and discontinuation reasons of JAK inhibitors in patients with RA who initiated therapy at age ≥ 65 versus < 65 years in a real-world setting. We included 317 patients with RA treated with JAK inhibitors at a single tertiary center (2000-2025), classified as ≥ 65 years (H65Y, n = 97) or < 65 years (L65Y, n = 220). The outcomes were retention and cause-specific discontinuation, with a single primary reason per patient. Drug retention was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis and compared using the log-rank test; factors associated with discontinuation were assessed by multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: No statistically significant difference in overall retention was detected between the groups (HR [95% CI] 1.18 [0.419, 1.714], log-rank p = 0.680). However, discontinuation due to adverse effects was significantly more frequent in the H65Y group (10/20 [50.0%] vs. 6/52 [11.5%]). No cardiovascular- or malignancy-related discontinuations were observed in the H65Y group; however, given the limited cohort size and follow-up, the study was underpowered to detect these infrequent outcomes. Concomitant methotrexate (HR 2.94) or glucocorticoid (HR 3.73) use was associated with subsequent discontinuation. Herpes zoster incidence was significantly higher in the H65Y group (adjusted HR 1.94 [95% CI] 1.02-3.71; p = 0.044), with approximately half of the cases occurring within the first treatment year.
CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant difference in JAK inhibitor retention between the elderly and younger groups was detected. Because this study assessed reasons for discontinuation rather than systematically ascertained safety events, it does not permit conclusions regarding cardiovascular or malignancy safety. Herpes zoster, particularly during the early treatment phase, warrants heightened vigilance in elderly patients initiating JAK inhibitor therapy. Key Points • No significant difference in JAK inhibitor retention between the elderly and younger groups was detected. • As only the primary reason for discontinuation was recorded, this study does not assess cardiovascular or malignancy safety; its findings pertain to drug retention and adverse event-related discontinuation. • Herpes zoster risk was significantly higher in elderly patients, mostly within the first treatment year, warranting early vigilance.

Title: Prognostic significance of ejection fraction derived from prospectively ECG-triggered coronary CT angiography.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prospective electrocardiogram (ECG)-triggered coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography is widely used for noninvasive evaluation of coronary artery disease, with relatively low radiation exposure. However, its limited temporal sampling restricts comprehensive assessment of left ventricular (LV) systolic function. Therefore, novel functional parameters derived from restricted acquisition windows may provide additional prognostic information without increasing radiation dose.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prognostic significance of LVEF120ms, a novel systolic functional parameter derived from LV volume change over a 120-ms systolic acquisition window.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 356 patients who underwent prospectively ECG-triggered coronary CT angiography between 2021 and 2023. We calculated LVEF120ms from three systolic phases using semi-automated volumetric analysis. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis determined the optimal cut-off value, and Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses were used to assess outcomes.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 36 months, 31 patients (8.7%) experienced MACE. Median LVEF120ms was significantly lower in patients with MACE (5.6% vs. 10.2%, p < 0.001). The optimal cut-off was 7.2% (area under the ROC curve [AUC]: 0.712). Patients with LVEF120ms ≤ 7.2% had significantly reduced MACE-free survival (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, LVEF120ms ≤ 7.2% remained an independent predictor of MACE (hazard ratio [HR]: 3.42; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: The parameter LVEF120ms derived from prospectively ECG-triggered cardiac CT independently predicts adverse cardiovascular events and may improve risk stratification without additional radiation.

Title: Association Between Exercise Adherence and Long-Term Quality of Life in Ischemic Stroke Survivors: A 2-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to investigate factors associated with quality of life within 2 years post-discharge, with a particular focus on exercise adherence.
DESIGN: A prospective observational cohort study.
METHODS: Participants were enrolled during hospitalisation and followed up at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months post-discharge via questionnaires. Linear mixed-effects models were used to identify factors associated with quality of life.
DATA SOURCES: Data were collected from ischemic stroke patients (discharged from The First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College, January to August 2021) using structured questionnaires, medical records and validated scales.
RESULTS: Of 355 enrolled stroke survivors, 242 (68.2%) completed the two-year follow-up. Functional disability, exercise adherence, family history of stroke and prior stroke were independently associated with long-term quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Greater exercise adherence is independently associated with better quality of life on average over the 24-month follow-up period among stroke survivors.
IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurses and rehabilitation guidelines should prioritise exercise adherence support during long-term follow-up to sustain post-stroke quality of life.

Title: Safety and Outcomes of Prone Positioning in the Early Postoperative Period following Cardiac Surgery.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate prone positioning (PP) safety and its respiratory and hemodynamic effects in patients with moderate-to-severe respiratory failure after cardiac surgery via median sternotomy.
DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center, observational cohort study.
SETTING: Cardiovascular intensive care unit at a tertiary academic hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Thirty-eight consecutive adult patients undergoing PP for acute respiratory failure within 30 days of median sternotomy cardiac surgery between 2004 and 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: Protocolized PP sessions under deep sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and advanced hemodynamic monitoring. Median PP duration was 24 hours (IQR 16-26); 47.4% underwent their first session within 5 postoperative days.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary endpoint was PP-related complications (mediastinitis/sternal dehiscence). Secondary endpoints included gas exchange, vasoactive requirements, and in-hospital mortality. Mediastinitis occurred in one patient (2.6%), comparable to non-proned populations. PP significantly improved oxygenation, with the PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio increasing from 82.8 ± 26.1 mmHg at baseline to 177.5 ± 68.9 mmHg at 4 hours into the maneuver and to 175.0 ± 70.8 mmHg at PP completion (both p < 0.001). No significant hemodynamic deterioration or increased vasoactive support occurred. Overall mortality was 44.7%. Advanced age (≥75 years) and baseline hypercapnia (PaCO₂ ≥50 mmHg) were independent predictors of mortality.
CONCLUSION: PP was safe after recent median sternotomy and elicited a marked improvement in oxygenation without increasing sternal complications. These findings support considering PP for selected patients with moderate-to-severe postoperative adult respiratory distress syndrome following cardiac surgery.

Title: Estimated pulse wave velocity and 20-year cumulative incidence of type 2 diabetes: The ATTICA cohort study (2002-2022).
Abstract:
AIMS: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV), a composite marker derived from age and mean blood pressure, reflects integrated vascular ageing and haemodynamic load. This study aimed to investigate the association between baseline ePWV and the 20-year cumulative incidence of type 2 diabetes (T2D) in a population-based cohort of initially healthy adults.
METHODS: A total of 2000 adults from the ATTICA cohort (2002-2022), free of cardiovascular disease and T2D at baseline, were included and followed-up for 20-years (2002-2022). Incidence of T2D was the outcome of interest; ePWV was derived using a validated equation based on age and mean blood pressure.
RESULTS: Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with 22% higher odds of T2D over 20 years (OR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.03-1.44; p = 0.017). In sex-stratified analyses, the association was significant in men (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.01-1.60), although no significant interaction with sex was observed (p for interaction = 0.453). A significant interaction was observed between ePWV and physical activity trajectories (p for interaction < 0.001); no significant association was observed among consistently active participants (OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 0.83-1.24). No significant interactions were observed for smoking (p for interaction = 0.752), various food groups, or MedDietScore (all remaining p for interaction > 0.500).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline ePWV was associated with increased odds of T2D over 20-year observation. Exploratory analyses suggested potential effect modification by physical activity trajectories; however, these findings require independent confirmation.

Title: Associations of weekend warrior and regularly active physical activity patterns with mortality and cardiometabolic outcomes in middle-aged and older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Journal of science and medicine in sport
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Whether within-week distribution of physical activity is associated with mortality and cardiometabolic outcomes beyond activity status remains unclear. We compared weekend warrior (WW) and regularly active (RA) patterns in adults with a mean age ≥40 years.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
METHODS: PRISMA-compliant review (PROSPERO CRD420251026061). Five databases were searched from inception to 1 April 2025; targeted forward-citation and hand-search checks were conducted to 31 October 2025 and on 8 March 2026, without a complete database rerun. Parent-cohort overlap was adjudicated. Direct WW-RA mortality estimates were primary; reconstructed contrasts were analysed separately across specified covariance assumptions. Heterogeneous non-fatal outcomes were synthesised narratively.
RESULTS: Forty-six registered-core reports were retained. Three independent reports provided direct WW-RA all-cause mortality estimates (N = 452,513); the exploratory random-effects summary was hazard ratio (HR) 1.019 (95% confidence interval 0.851-1.221; Q-based I2 = 27.6%). Six compatible reconstructed contrasts (N = 527,963) remained compatible with no clear difference across assumed correlation values (ρ = 0, 0.50, and 0.75). Direct cause-specific, non-fatal, safety, and adherence evidence was sparse. Certainty for the direct and reconstructed mortality evidence was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: No clear difference in all-cause mortality was identified between WW and RA patterns in middle-aged and older adults. This finding does not establish equivalence because direct evidence was limited, reconstructed contrasts required additional assumptions, and actual weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) volume was not uniformly matched. Evidence for other outcomes, safety, and adherence remained sparse.

Title: Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
Abstract:
AIM: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107).
RESULTS: Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

Title: Cardiac Arrhythmias and Sleep Disorders.
Abstract: Sleep disordered breathing (SDB), periodic limb movements of sleep, insomnia, sleep curtailment, and sleep architectural changes are associated with cardiac arrhythmias in community-based and clinical cohort studies. Findings appear to be strongest in magnitude and most consistent for SDB and atrial fibrillation (AF). The mechanisms most consistently identified in animal experimental models include autonomic nervous system fluctuations and intrathoracic pressure alterations, the latter resulting in direct mechanical effects on the thin-walled atria. Other studies point toward intermittent hypoxia. Nonrandomized interventional studies suggest that the treatment of SDB reduces AF recurrence after ablation or cardioversion.

Title: Baseline gradient, valve morphology and left ventricular recovery and survival after TAVR in reduced-ejection-fraction aortic stenosis: a retrospective cohort study.
Haematological and iron-handling effects of SGLT2 inhibitors: a meta-analysis of randomised trials.
What is known about the impact of animated video-based interventions on patient outcomes? A scoping review.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review examined the impact of animated video interventions on health-related outcomes among adults living with health conditions.
DESIGN: Scoping review based on the methodological framework by Arksey and O’Malley, refined by the Joanna Briggs Institute and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).
DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, PsycINFO and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature were searched, with an initial search in March 2021 and an updated search in August 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: English-language studies published since 1996, and of any design using animated videos targeting adults with any health condition and reported clinical, cognitive, behavioural, psychosocial or patient-reported outcomes.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two independent reviewers screened and charted data on study characteristics, intervention features, development processes and outcomes, and synthesised using numerical and thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Of 4163 records screened, 154 full-text articles were assessed and 49 studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 44 full-text papers (90%) and five conference abstracts (10%). Most were single-arm pre-post designs (n=21, 42.8%) or randomised controlled trials (n=18, 36.7%), with videos ranging from 50 s to 60 min and applied mainly to chronic conditions, including cancer (n=13, 26.5%), kidney disease (n=9, 18.4%) and stroke or cardiovascular disease (n=9, 18.4%). Thematic synthesis identified six domains: application across conditions and contexts, targeted outcomes, design and development processes, integration into rehabilitation, implementation strategies and accessibility. Reported benefits included improved health literacy, adherence, anxiety reduction, empowerment and symptom management. Only 15 studies (30.6%) described their video development process and two studies (4%) addressed rehabilitation content.
CONCLUSION: Animated videos show promise for enhancing patient knowledge, engagement and emotional well-being, but more rigorous, theory-informed research is needed.
INNOVATION: Unlike prior reviews focused on estimating the effectiveness of animated videos on defined outcomes, this scoping review maps the breadth of animated video interventions for adults with health conditions, charting the frameworks guiding video development, implementation strategies, accessibility considerations and integration within rehabilitation. This identifies priority areas for advancing theory-informed, equitable design of animation-based interventions.

Title: Serious Adverse Events in Adult ICU Patients: A Substudy of the PATIENCE Cohort.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prokinetic agents are used to enhance upper gastrointestinal motility, but adverse events related to these agents are poorly described. We aimed to provide detailed epidemiological data on predefined serious adverse events (SAEs) in a cohort of adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with and without prokinetic treatment. We hypothesised that all predefined SAEs would occur in both patients treated and those not treated with prokinetic agents, and that a higher number of SAEs would occur among patients treated with prokinetic agents for more than three consecutive days.
METHODS: This substudy of the inception cohort study "Prokinetic agents in adult intensive care unit patients" included acutely admitted adult ICU patients. The prokinetic agents assessed (exposures) were erythromycin, metoclopramide, domperidone, and prucalopride. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients experiencing at least one episode of five pre-specified SAEs during ICU stay (cardiac arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, vomiting with aspiration, diarrhoea, extrapyramidal symptoms). Secondary outcomes were (1) proportion of patients experiencing each SAE, (2) the proportion of patients experiencing any of the SAEs after prokinetic treatment stratified by longest consecutive treatment duration, (3) time from index ICU admission to first SAE and (4) time from prokinetic initiation to first SAE. All analyses were descriptive, summarising SAE proportions and timing overall and according to prokinetic exposure.
RESULTS: Among 1440 adult ICU patients, 710 SAEs occurred in 354 patients (24.6%), most commonly cardiac arrhythmias (199/1440, 13.8%). Across the exposure groups, the proportion of patients experiencing one or more SAEs ranged from 23.0% to 42.5%. Among patients treated with prokinetic agents for > 3 consecutive days, 14/59 (23.7%) experienced a SAE, which was similar to the proportion observed among patients not receiving prokinetic agents (291/1.253, 23.2%). Most SAEs occurred on median Day 2 after ICU admission and on median Day 3 after prokinetic initiation.
CONCLUSION: One in four adult ICU patients experienced at least one SAE, with cardiac arrhythmias being the most frequent. Among patients receiving prokinetic agents, the proportion experiencing one or more SAEs ranged from 23.0% to 42.5% across treatment groups. The findings from this study may help inform the design of a future clinical trial.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This analysis presents reported serious adverse event observed in an ICU trial cohort assessing gastrointestinal prokinetic drug effects. Serious adverse events were reported frequently in both the drug treatment groups and the comparison (no prokinetic drug) group. Types of serious adverse events reported are presented.

Title: Impact of diabetes mellitus on aortic valve calcification: a cross-sectional study of two large multicentre cohorts.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, but its relationship with aortic valve calcification (AVC) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to investigate whether the presence of DM is associated with a higher prevalence of AVC.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study combines two large multicentre cohorts: Steno INTEN-CT (EUCT2022-500143-21-01) and DANCAVAS (NCT03946410). Participants with available AVC scores assessed by cardiac CT were included in the present study. Propensity score matching was performed to compare participants with DM to those without DM. AVC was analysed as a binary outcome (0 vs >0) using logistic regression with clustering by matched pairs.
RESULTS: After propensity matching of participants with and without DM, 14 182 participants (7091 matched pairs) were included. Mean age was 67±4 years in the no-DM group compared with 66±4 years in the DM group, p<0.001. AVC was present in 54% and 52% of individuals without and with DM, respectively (p=0.003). In a multivariate logistic regression analysis, DM was not associated with higher AVC prevalence (OR=0.88, 95%CI 0.80–0.96, p=0.004) while male sex, older age, higher body mass index, hypertension, smoking, higher low density lipoprotein cholesterol and statin use remained independently associated with higher prevalence of AVC. An interaction between statin use and DM was found in the association with AVC (p for interaction 0.018), suggesting a potentially stronger association between statin use and AVC among individuals without DM.
CONCLUSION: In this large cross-sectional cohort of 14,182 individuals without known cardiovascular disease, the presence of DM was not associated with higher prevalence of AVC. Instead, higher prevalence of AVC was independently associated with cardiovascular risk factors that frequently coexist with DM. These findings suggest that the previously reported relationship between DM and AVC may, at least partly, be related to accompanying cardiovascular risk factors rather than DM per se.

Title: Development and external validation of a preprocedural prediction model for 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a well-established treatment for severe aortic stenosis but not recommended for patients with a life-expectancy below 1 year. Nevertheless, 1 year mortality after TAVI is around 15% in current reports. Accurate prediction models are thus needed to prevent futile interventions.
METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI were prospectively recruited between 2008 and 2021 from a single-centre registry in Zurich, Switzerland and data split into derivation and validation datasets. Four expert cardiologists defined relevant candidate predictors. A prediction model was developed using multiple logistic regression after imputation of missing data. An independent cohort undergoing TAVI from 2008 to 2018 in London, UK served as an external validation dataset. Performance of the prediction model was assessed through internal and external validation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and calibration plots were used for discrimination and calibration.
RESULTS: A total of 1702 patients were included from the Swiss cohort. Among these 1278 were used for model development and 424 for validation. 12 predictors were incorporated including age, male sex, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, haemoglobin, creatinine, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, troponin, left ventricular ejection fraction, mean transaortic pressure gradient and severe mitral regurgitation. The prediction model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.72 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.81) in internal validation and showed optimal sensitivity and specificity for 1-year mortality prediction at a probability threshold of 20%, outperforming European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II and Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM) score. In the external validation dataset consisting of 851 patients from the UK cohort, the AUC was 0.64 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.70).
CONCLUSION: The TAVI-specific risk model demonstrated acceptable performance for prediction of 1-year mortality after TAVI across two contemporary real-world cohorts, highlighting its potential for clinical application instead of EuroSCORE II or STS-PROM.

Title: Temporal responses of plasma and urinary nitrate and nitrite to acute and 14-day beetroot powder supplementation and associated exercise responses under normoxia and normobaric hypoxia.
Abstract: This study aimed to characterize the temporal responses of plasma and urinary nitrate (NO3-) and nitrite (NO2-) during acute ingestion and 14 days of beetroot powder supplementation, and to compare exercise performance and physiological responses under normoxia and normobaric hypoxia before and after supplementation. Twenty-four healthy male university students consumed 40 g of beetroot powder (approximately 11.2 mmol NO3-) once daily for 14 doses. Plasma and urine were sampled at multiple time points over 24 h after the first dose and in the fasting state on the mornings after the 7th and 14th doses (Days 8 and 15). NO3- and NO2- were quantified by UPLC-MS/MS, and urinary measures were normalized to urinary creatinine. Participants completed incremental cycling tests under normoxia and normobaric hypoxia (FiO2 = 13.5%) before and after supplementation; countermovement jump performance was assessed only under normoxia. Plasma NO3- and urinary NO3-/Cr showed significant time effects (both P < 0.001), reaching their highest observed levels at 1 and 2 h, respectively, and remaining above baseline at 24 h and on the mornings after the 7th and 14th doses. Plasma NO2- did not change significantly over time (P = 0.444). Urinary NO2- was summarized as the proportion of quantifiable samples because some results were below the lower limit of quantification. After 14 days of supplementation, time to exhaustion increased under both normoxic and normobaric hypoxic conditions (P = 0.018 and P = 0.014, respectively), with moderate effect sizes; countermovement jump performance, maximal heart rate, and most cardiovascular measures did not change significantly. Beetroot powder elicited clear temporal responses in plasma and urinary NO3-, whereas NO2- responses were inconsistent. After 14 days of supplementation, incremental exercise tolerance improved under both normoxic and normobaric hypoxic conditions, whereas countermovement jump performance and most cardiovascular measures did not change significantly. Given the single-group pre-post design, these findings require confirmation in randomized, placebo-controlled studies.

Title: Heterogeneity of Treatment Effect of ABC Pathway-Based Care in Older Atrial Fibrillation: Insights from the mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF Trials Using a Causal Machine Learning Approach.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrated care based on the Atrial fibrillation Better Care (ABC) pathway improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but whether treatment effects differ across older patients remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate heterogeneity of treatment effect (HTE) of ABC pathway-based care and assess its transportability across healthcare settings using causal machine learning (ML).
METHODS: Individual participant data from the cluster-randomised mAFA-II and MIRACLE-AF trials were analysed, including 3,209 patients aged ≥65 years. Three causal ML models were developed in mAFA-II and externally validated in MIRACLE-AF. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, ischaemic stroke, intracranial haemorrhage, heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, or major bleeding.
RESULTS: The uplift random forest demonstrated the best performance and identified meaningful HTE. In the mAFA-II testing cohort, ABC pathway-based care was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome in patients predicted to benefit, whereas no benefit and possible harm were observed in those predicted to derive harm (P-interaction=0.002). In external validation, benefit was preserved in the predicted benefit group but not in the predicted harm group, although treatment discrimination was attenuated. Patients predicted to derive limited benefit had greater clinical complexity, including higher comorbidity burden and CHA2DS2-VASc scores. Sex, heart failure, and hypertension were the strongest predictors of treatment effect.
CONCLUSIONS: ABC pathway-based integrated care demonstrates clinically meaningful treatment heterogeneity among older patients with AF. These findings support more personalised implementation of integrated care and highlight the potential of causal ML to guide precision management in AF.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: MAFA-II trial (ChiCTR-OOC-17014138 || http://www.chictr.org.cn/, registered on 26 December 2017), MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514 || https://clinicaltrials.gov/, registered on 10 November 2020).

Title: Guideline-directed medical therapy implementation and its association with cardiac adverse events across cardiac and noncardiac risk domains.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) improves prognosis in heart failure (HF), but its implementation remains suboptimal, particularly in patients with multiple risk domains.
METHODS: We analyzed the association between GDMT achievement and the 2-year composite endpoint of cardiac death or HF hospitalization across cardiac and noncardiac risk domains using the WET-HF2 registry, a prospective multicenter Japanese registry. GDMT achievement was quantified using a dose-weighted GDMT score (0-12). Cardiac and noncardiac risk domains were assessed using MAGGIC risk score components.
RESULTS: Among 2,702 patients, median GDMT and MAGGIC risk scores were 5 (3-6) and 23 (18-27), respectively. Each 1-point increase in noncardiac risk domain was associated with lower GDMT achievement (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.93; 95% CI 0.90-0.95), whereas each 1-point increase in cardiac risk domain was associated with greater GDMT achievement (aOR, 1.08; 95% CI 1.06-1.10). Among patients in the highest tertile of noncardiac risk, no documented reason for non-prescription of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists was identified in 11% and 16%, respectively. During 2-year follow-up, 652 patients (24%) experienced the composite endpoint. A higher GDMT score was associated with lower risk of the composite endpoint (adjusted hazard ratio per point, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.91-0.98), consistently across tertiles of cardiac and noncardiac risk (P for interaction=0.784 and 0.359).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher cardiac risk was associated with greater GDMT achievement, while higher noncardiac risk was associated with lower achievement. The favorable association between GDMT achievement and clinical outcomes was observed across both risk domains.

Title: Ticagrelor pretreatment and angiographic no-reflow in STEMI: a multicentre observational study.
Abstract:
AIMS: We examined the association between ticagrelor pretreatment and angiographic no-reflow in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), with in-hospital mortality as a secondary outcome and clinical phenotyping as an exploratory objective.
METHODS: In a retrospective multicentre registry (2018-2021), 623 patients referred for percutaneous coronary intervention were compared by loading strategy: pretreatment at first medical contact or deferred before PCI. Cohort-wide inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), using a clinical covariate-balancing propensity model and 50 imputations, estimated adjusted risk ratios (RRs). Outcome-blind latent class analysis preceded a treatment-weighted comparison of class-specific no-reflow risks.
RESULTS: No-reflow occurred in 28/464 pretreated patients versus 27/159 comparators (6.0% versus 17.0%); the crude RR was 0.36 (95% CI 0.22-0.58), and the IPTW-adjusted RR was 0.43 (95% CI 0.24-0.74; P = 0.003). Ten patients died (adjusted RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.13-1.67). Three classes comprised 328, 231 and 64 patients, but their pretreatment-standardised no-reflow risks did not establish prognostic separation.
CONCLUSIONS: Ticagrelor pretreatment was associated with lower angiographic no-reflow after propensity weighting. The adjusted mortality and exploratory class-risk findings did not reach statistical significance. Residual confounding and uncertain covariate timing limit causal interpretation, and prospective validation is required.

Title: Association of Long-acting Bronchodilator Use with Cardiovascular Adverse Events in Patients with Asthma: A Population-based Cohort Study.
Journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: A recent meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with cardiovascular adverse events (AEs) leading to treatment discontinuation in asthma, although the certainty of evidence was low.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cardiovascular safety of long-acting bronchodilators in a real-world asthma population.
METHODS: This population-based cohort study used UK Biobank data from patients with asthma (2006-2010). Exposure was categorized into three mutually exclusive groups: LABA alone, LAMA alone, or combined LABA/LAMA therapy. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular AEs, including coronary heart disease, arrhythmia, hypertension, heart failure, and cerebrovascular disease. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Pre-specified subgroup analyses and interaction tests were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 14,677 patients were included (median follow-up 14.68 years). Long-acting bronchodilator use was associated with an increased risk of total cardiovascular AEs (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.15). This was primarily driven by arrhythmia (HR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.06-1.42), heart failure (HR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.02-1.65), and cerebrovascular disease (HR: 1.35, 95% CI: 1.02-1.79). When stratified by regimen, the association was confined to the LABA group (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.001-1.13) and the combined group (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.09-1.59). The association was more pronounced in patients using short-acting bronchodilators (HR: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.07-1.23; interaction P = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: The observed positive associations are more plausibly attributable to confounding rather than to a causal drug effect. Future research should prioritize new-user designs to clarify whether these signals are drug-specific or confounded by disease severity.

Title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.
METHODS: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

Title: Fibroblast Growth Factor-23 as a biomarker to refine cardiovascular risk identification: A cross-sectional study in postmenopausal osteoporosis.
Journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Postmenopausal osteoporosis presents with heterogeneous comorbidities including cardiovascular disease. Objectives of this study were the identification of clusters of osteoporotic patients in relation to the cardiovascular risk, comorbidities, and levels of intact Fibroblast Growth Factor (iFGF23), a key player of the bone-cardiovascular axis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis took place in the Rheumatology Department, University Hospital Clermont-Ferrand, France. Twelve variables representative of comorbidities were selected according to their associations and clinical relevance: age, bone mineral density, flow-mediated dilation, cardiovascular risk (SCORE2/2OP), muscle mass, handgrip, sleep, quality of life, pain and plasma iFGF23. Multiple correspondence analysis followed by hierarchical clustering was used to propose profiles of patients and associations related to iFGF23 and cardiovascular risk.
RESULTS: Three comorbidity clusters were identified in 102 women (69.1 ± 7.7 years old): clusters of older age with worse outcomes, of younger age with better results and an intermediate cluster. iFGF23 is unveiled as a marker of the cardiovascular risk even in patients with normal renal function, with a threshold of 94.14 ng/L, and is significantly associated with age, fat mass, poor handgrip, poor quality of life, pain and impaired sleep.
CONCLUSIONS: Comorbidity clusters of post-menopausal osteoporosis based on the severity of health impairment highlight in this exploratory study iFGF23 as a possible biomarker of the cardiovascular risk. We suggest that iFGF23 measurement may complement SCORE2/2OP calculation to better predict the cardiovascular risk of osteoporosis patients. A suggested hypothesis-generating algorithm is proposed and future validation in a larger prospective study is warranted.

Title: Dementia, Treatment Intensity, and Outcomes in Acute Myocardial Infarction with Cardiogenic Shock.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia is associated with lower use of invasive therapies and poorer outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). However, its impact in AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMICS), where timely invasive management is critical for survival, remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the association between dementia, treatment intensity, and in-hospital outcomes in AMICS.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2019). Adults hospitalized with AMICS were identified using ICD-10-CM codes and stratified according to pre-existing dementia. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and use of invasive and supportive therapies. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, hospital, socioeconomic, presentation, and comorbidity characteristics estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We additionally performed 1:1 propensity score matching.
RESULTS: Among 226,570 patients with AMICS, 10,895 (4.8%) had dementia. Patients with dementia were older, more frequently female, had greater comorbidity burden, and fewer markers of acute disease severity. They underwent coronary angiography (50.2% vs. 70.4%), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (39.3% vs. 55.0%), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (5.2% vs. 17.5%), mechanical ventilation (34.1% vs. 45.5%), and circulatory support (23.7% vs. 46.4%) less frequently than those without dementia (all p < 0.001). Dementia was independently associated with lower odds of coronary angiography (aOR 0.50, 95% CI 0.48-0.52), PCI (aOR 0.58, 95% CI 0.55-0.61), CABG (aOR 0.31, 95% CI 0.28-0.34), and circulatory support (aOR 0.49, 95% CI 0.46-0.51), as well as higher odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.12-1.22) and MACCE (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.09-1.18). Results were consistent in the propensity-matched pairs.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalized with AMICS, dementia was independently associated with lower treatment intensity and worse in-hospital outcomes despite fewer markers of acute clinical severity. These findings highlight the importance of individualized, goal-concordant decision-making while avoiding unwarranted limitation of potentially life-saving therapies.

Title: Pulmonary function impairment, exercise intolerance, and clinical outcomes in symptomatic patients with HFpEF undergoing exercise stress echocardiography.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary function impairment is common in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). However, its relationships with exercise capacity, cardiovascular reserve capacity, and prognosis in HFpEF remain uncertain.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied symptomatic patients undergoing exercise stress echocardiography with simultaneous expired gas analysis. Cross-sectional analyses were performed to compare pulmonary function in patients with HFpEF and symptomatic controls in the cohort with available data on percent predicted vital capacity (%VC) and forced expiratory volume in 1 s (%FEV1). Outcome assessment was also performed in a subset of patients.
RESULTS: Among 486 patients in the cross-sectional cohort, 178 had HFpEF and 308 were symptomatic controls. Patients with HFpEF had lower %VC and %FEV1 than controls. After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index, lower %VC and %FEV1 were consistently associated with reduced exercise capacity, higher echocardiographic estimates of left ventricular filling pressure (E/e') and reduced right ventricular systolic function during exercise. Prognostic analyses were performed in the HFpEF cohort with follow-up data (N = 148). There were 37 primary composite events of all-cause death or worsening heart failure over a median follow-up of 935 days. Lower %VC was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint and remained associated in multivariable models. The %FEV1 showed a weaker but concordant association.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower %VC and %FEV1 were associated with reduced exercise capacity and hemodynamic derangements in the overall cohort and with worse clinical outcomes in patients with HFpEF.

Title: Association of cognitive frailty and its changes with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic multimorbidity: Findings from the CHARLS study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical frailty has been linked to cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) multimorbidity, but the role of cognitive frailty and its dynamic changes in CKM progression remains unclear. We investigated the associations of baseline cognitive frailty and changes in cognitive frailty status with incident CKM multimorbidity.
METHODS: This cohort study included participants aged ≥ 45 years from the CHARLS (2011-2018). Cognitive frailty was classified as Robust, reversible cognitive frailty (RCF), or potentially reversible cognitive frailty (PRCF). A five-level score quantified the magnitude of cognitive change (Δscore). CKM multimorbidity was defined as ≥ 2 of cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disease. Cox models and trend tests estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.
RESULTS: Among 9816 participants, 3836 were included in baseline CKM analysis and 1891 in transition analysis. Both RCF (HR=2.74, 95%CI:2.25-3.34) and PRCF (HR=2.51, 95%CI:1.96-3.21) were associated with increased CKM risk (both P < 0.001). Cognitive status provided additional risk stratification beyond physical frailty. RCF-to-Robust improvement reduced CKM risk by 56% (HR=0.44, 95%CI:0.23-0.85, P = 0.015), while deterioration markedly increased risk (HR≈5.3, P < 0.001). The Δscore trend test showed a significant dose-response relationship (P < 0.001). Substantial improvement (Δscore=-3) significantly reduced risk, whereas minor improvements showed protective trends without statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Cognitive frailty is independently associated with CKM multimorbidity progression. Within each direction of cognitive change, the magnitude of change provided additional prognostic information beyond direction alone. These findings support the brain-CKM interconnection framework and suggest cognitive screening should be considered in CKM prevention strategies.
LAY SUMMARY: Cognitive frailty-a condition where physical decline and memory problems occur together-is common in older adults. In this study, we analysed data from nearly 10,000 middle-aged and older adults in China to understand whether cognitive frailty increases the risk of developing cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) multimorbidity, a cluster of conditions including heart disease, kidney disease, and diabetes. We found that people with cognitive frailty had significantly higher risks of developing CKM multimorbidity. More importantly, we found that the magnitude of change in cognitive function added prognostic information on top of its direction-greater worsening tracked with higher CKM risk. These findings suggest that monitoring changes in cognitive function over time could help identify individuals at high risk of CKM multimorbidity, and that interventions aimed at improving cognitive health may need to achieve meaningful improvement to reduce this risk.

Title: Cardiometabolic abnormalities among normal-weight adults: Prevalence and associated sociodemographic and lifestyle factors in a large Spanish cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although body mass index (BMI) is widely used to assess obesity-related health risks, it may fail to detect individuals with normal weight who present with significant cardiometabolic abnormalities. This phenotype, often overlooked in clinical practice, is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence and determinants of cardiometabolic abnormalities in a large cohort of Spanish adults with normal BMI and to explore their associations with sociodemographic and lifestyle variables.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 163,254 workers aged 18-69 years who underwent occupational health examinations between 2021 and 2024. Only individuals with a BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 kg/m² were included. Cardiometabolic abnormalities were defined as the presence of hypertension, dyslipidemia, or hyperglycemia. Sociodemographic data, smoking status, alcohol intake (measured in standard drinking units), physical activity (assessed with the IPAQ), and Mediterranean diet adherence (assessed using the MEDAS-14 questionnaire) were collected. Multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with the presence of one or more cardiometabolic abnormalities.
RESULTS: Among normal-weight adults, 49.0% presented at least one cardiometabolic abnormality. The prevalence was higher in men (54.3%) than in women (44.5%). Cardiometabolic risk was significantly higher among men, older individuals, smokers, those with low physical activity, poor adherence to the Mediterranean diet, and high alcohol consumption. Lower occupational social class was also associated with greater risk. The likelihood of presenting ≥1 cardiometabolic abnormality increased progressively with the accumulation of unhealthy lifestyle habits.
CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of normal-weight individuals exhibit cardiometabolic abnormalities, underscoring the need to move beyond BMI in clinical risk stratification. Preventive strategies should incorporate metabolic screening and lifestyle assessments for all individuals, regardless of weight status, to identify those at silent cardiometabolic risk.

Title: Effects of an opioid-free versus two opioid-based anesthetic protocols on intraoperative cardiovascular variables and postoperative pain in rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus) undergoing elective ovariohysterectomy: A prospective, randomized, blinded clinical study.
Abstract: This prospective, randomized, blinded clinical study compared intraoperative cardiovascular variables and postoperative pain in rabbits undergoing elective ovariohysterectomy under an opioid-free anesthetic protocol or the same protocol supplemented with tramadol or morphine. Rabbits were assigned to three groups (n = 13/group): CONTROL (dexmedetomidine 50 µg/kg), MOR (dexmedetomidine 50 µg/kg plus morphine 2 mg/kg) and TRA (dexmedetomidine 50 µg/kg plus tramadol 10 mg/kg), administered as premedication. All rabbits received intravenous meloxicam (0.6 mg/kg). Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane under mechanical ventilation; norepinephrine infusion was initiated when arterial hypotension occurred. Heart rate, arterial blood pressure, capnography and expired sevoflurane were recorded intraoperatively. Postoperative pain and rescue analgesia were assessed using the Rabbit Pain Behaviour Scale (RPBS) from two to six hours after anesthetic recovery (T2-T6); sedation was scored from one to six hours (T1-T6). Intraoperatively, CONTROL showed higher blood pressure and required less norepinephrine than MOR. Postoperatively, MOR had higher sedation scores, differing from the other groups at T2 and T4 and from CONTROL at T5 and T6. Rescue analgesia was required in 12 MOR rabbits (92.3%) and seven TRA and CONTROL rabbits (53.8%). MOR also presented higher pain scores, differing from the other groups at T2 and from CONTROL at T3. In conclusion, all protocols allowed completion of the surgical procedure without an intraoperative exacerbated cardiovascular response. However, none of the protocols provided adequate postoperative pain control after ovariohysterectomy, as most rabbits required postoperative rescue analgesia. Sedation appears to have influenced postoperative pain scoring, particularly in the MOR group.

Title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]).
FINDINGS: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups.
INTERPRETATION: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes.
FUNDING: BreakthroughT1D, German Research Foundation (DFG), German Center for Diabetes Research (DZD), Schmutzler Stiftung, German Federal Ministry of Health, Ministry of Culture and Science of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia, and German Federal Ministry of Education and Research.
TRANSLATION: For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes and safety of SGLT2 inhibitors in rheumatic diseases: a systematic review of evidence predominantly from systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rheumatic immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) are associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiometabolic outcomes in high-risk populations, but IMID patients were largely excluded from major trials. It remains unclear to what extent these benefits extend to IMIDs.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidance, MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, Cochrane Library and Web of Science Core Collection databases were searched (PROSPERO: CRD420261289071). Observational and interventional adult IMID studies reporting all cause-mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; cardiovascular mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure), safety or IMID disease activity with SGLT2i were included.
RESULTS: Five studies including 11,190 IMID participants were identified: systemic sclerosis (SSc; 25.4%), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE; 70.9%) and other IMIDs (3.9%). Across three studies reporting MACE, SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality and heart failure risk, with no clear effect on myocardial infarction. Safety data were variably reported, with infections, particularly genitourinary infections, were most frequently reported. Evidence on hospitalisation, treatment discontinuation and IMID flare was limited and inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: Predominantly observational data suggest a potential cardiovascular benefit of SGLT2 inhibitors in rheumatic IMIDs, but the available evidence is confined largely to SLE and SSc populations. Whilst SGLT2 inhibitors should be used in established indications of type 2 diabetes mellitus, heart failure and chronic kidney disease, prospective and controlled studies in IMID populations are needed to establish their cardiovascular benefit, clarify safety and evaluate for effect on disease activity.

Title: Awake intubation in a Japanese tertiary emergency department: a single-center retrospective descriptive study.
Journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on awake intubation in emergency departments (EDs) is limited. We aimed to describe patient characteristics, intubation indications, procedural practices, and outcomes for awake intubation in the ED.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective descriptive study included consecutive adult patients who underwent tracheal intubation at a tertiary ED in Japan from April 2020 through December 2025. Patients intubated during cardiac arrest were excluded. Operational definition for awake tracheal intubation required topical upper airway anesthesia, no neuromuscular blockers before or during the initial attempt, and documented preservation of consciousness and spontaneous ventilation throughout that attempt. Outcomes included first-pass success, adverse events related to airway management, and definitive airway management, including rescue.
RESULTS: Eighty-four patients underwent awake tracheal intubation, representing 5.5% of intubations in patients without cardiac arrest (84/1531). Upper airway infectious diseases were present in 54 patients (64.3%); airway-related indications accounted for 63 cases (75.0%). Emergency physicians performed 79 initial attempts (94.0%); a flexible bronchoscope was used initially in 49 patients (58.3%). First-pass success occurred in 63 patients (75.0%; 95% confidence interval, 64.4%-83.8%). Seven patients (8.3%) experienced adverse events related to airway management. Eighty patients (95.2%) achieved definitive airway management without a surgical airway. Four patients (4.8%) required a surgical airway, all after first-pass failure.
CONCLUSIONS: Awake intubation, performed primarily by emergency physicians, was used to manage upper airway infectious diseases with actual or impending obstruction in a tertiary ED. A flexible bronchoscope was used initially in over half of cases and most patients were intubated without a surgical airway.

Title: Depressive Symptoms and 6-Year KCCQ Health Status in Chronic Heart Failure: Findings From the Cognition.Matters-HF Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term disease-specific health status trajectories in ambulatory chronic heart failure (HF) are incompletely characterized, and the contribution of depressive symptoms remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize 6-year Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OSS) trajectories and distinguish persistent and visit-specific depressive symptom associations with health status.
METHODS: In the prospective Cognition.Matters-HF cohort, 148 patients with HF underwent assessments at baseline and 6, 12, 36, and 69 months. Linear mixed-effects models estimated KCCQ-OSS trajectories and prespecified correlates. Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores were decomposed into between-person and within-person components. Sensitivity analyses addressed missingness, and exploratory lagged analyses assessed whether recent PHQ-9 worsening predicted subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.
RESULTS: KCCQ-OSS remained stable over 69 months (78.0-76.6; change: -1.4; 95% CI: -4.6 to 1.8; P for time = 0.065), despite substantial individual variation. Higher between-person PHQ-9 burden (β: -3.44 per point; 95% CI: -4.00 to -2.88; P < 0.001) and within-person PHQ-9 worsening (β: -1.80; 95% CI: -2.50 to -1.11; P < 0.001) were associated with lower concurrent KCCQ-OSS. Recent PHQ-9 worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ-OSS, a ≥5-point KCCQ decline, or all-cause death/HF hospitalization. NYHA functional class and 6-min walking distance, but not N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, left ventricular ejection fraction, or executive function, were independently associated with KCCQ-OSS.
CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory chronic HF, average KCCQ-based health status remained stable over 6 years despite substantial individual variation. Depressive symptoms were strongly associated with concurrent health status, but recent worsening did not predict subsequent KCCQ deterioration or adverse clinical events.

Title: Systematic validation of BACH1 antibodies enables the identification of BACH1 localisation as predictor of prognosis in early-stage lung cancer.
Abstract: The transcription factor BACH1 is a key regulator of cellular stress responses, metabolism, and tumour progression, and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in several diseases, particularly metastatic cancer, inflammatory disease and cardiovascular conditions. As interest in BACH1 biology and its clinical relevance grows, the field would benefit from robust, well-characterised reagents enabling reliable detection of BACH1 across diverse experimental platforms, including analysis of human tissue. Establishing such tools is essential for advancing mechanistic studies and recognising the potential of BACH1 as a prognostic biomarker. We performed the first systematic validation of commercially available antibodies against human BACH1 across multiple experimental platforms, including western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. To ensure robustness, we validated antibodies using complementary approaches, including BACH1-knockout and knockdown cell lines, pharmacological modulators of BACH1 stability and localisation, and multiple extraction conditions. Their performance in immunohistochemistry was further tested using fixed cell pellets from wild-type and BACH1-deficient cells. Validated antibodies were subsequently applied to normal human tissues and lung cancer tissue microarrays to investigate BACH1 expression and subcellular localisation, and quantitative multiplex single-cell immunofluorescence analysis was performed in a cohort of early-stage lung adenocarcinoma patients with clinical follow-up. We demonstrate that subcellular localisation of BACH1 in early-stage lung adenocarcinoma correlates with patient prognosis, underscoring its clinical and translational significance. Our study delivers a rigorously validated toolkit for the BACH1 research community, removes a major barrier to progress in the field, and highlights the potential of BACH1 localisation as a biomarker in early-stage lung adenocarcinoma.

Title: Urinary tract and genital infections with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin across type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease: An indication- and sex-stratified disproportionality analysis of eudravigilance reports.
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), chronic heart failure (CHF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although their cardiovascular and renal benefits are well established, urogenital infections remain a relevant safety concern. Comparative post-marketing data on dapagliflozin (DAPA) and empagliflozin (EMPA) across therapeutic indications are limited. A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis of the EudraVigilance database (January 2021-July 2025) was conducted using a case/non-case approach. Cases were defined as individual case safety reports (ICSRs) containing at least one urogenital infection-coded reaction and a confirmed indication (T2DM, CHF, or CKD). The primary analysis was restricted to reports originating from the European Economic Area (EEA), where reporting rules are identical for both drugs; reports with unspecified patient age were excluded. Among 16,102 EEA ICSRs, 8156 adult reports with a confirmed indication were analyzed, of which 1109 met the case definition. Non-EEA reports were analyzed separately as a sensitivity analysis. Urogenital infection reporting did not differ between DAPA and EMPA, overall (ROR 0.91; 95% CI 0.80-1.03) or within any indication (T2DM: 13.9% vs 14.9%, ROR 0.92; 95% CI 0.79-1.07; CHF: 11.5% vs 12.6%, ROR 0.90; 95% CI 0.69-1.18; CKD: 11.0% vs 6.7%, ROR 1.73; 95% CI 0.75-3.99). For both drugs, reporting was higher in T2DM than in CHF (DAPA ROR 1.25; 95% CI 1.00-1.56; EMPA ROR 1.22; 95% CI 0.99-1.51), a difference confined to female patients (DAPA 1.38; EMPA 1.56) and, in the endpoint disaggregation, to genital mycotic infections (DAPA 2.24; EMPA 1.79) rather than non-mycotic urogenital infections. Female sex was the strongest determinant of urogenital infection reporting for both drugs (ROR female/male 1.85 for DAPA and 1.58 for EMPA). In non-EEA reports, an apparent excess of urogenital infection reporting with DAPA over EMPA (ROR 1.85; 95% CI 1.59-2.16) was explained by a different composition of the reports forwarded for the two drugs rather than by a drug effect. Urogenital infection reporting with SGLT2 inhibitors depends on indication and sex rather than on the molecule, and between-drug comparisons in EudraVigilance are sensitive to the geographic origin of reports.

Title: Outcomes and Complications of Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Single-Center Experience.
Journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
Abstract: Axillary intra-aortic balloon pump (axi-IABP) support has emerged as an alternative to femoral access for patients with advanced heart failure, offering improved mobility and potential benefits in pretransplant conditioning; however, data on associated complications remain limited. We conducted a retrospective study of 55 patients who underwent axi-IABP placement between January 2019 and July 2025 at our institution. The cohort had a median age of 59 (interquartile range [IQR], 52-65) years and presented with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Axi-IABP successfully bridged 87.3% of patients to advanced therapies. A total of 83 complications were identified in 60.0% of patients, most commonly malposition in 23.6% of patients, gas leak alarms in 16.4% of patients, and kinking in 16.4% of patients. Serious vascular complications were infrequent. The median time to first complication was 10.5 (IQR, 2.75-25.5) days. Female sex was associated with a higher hazard of first complication when controlled for height (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04-7.27; p = 0.041). In conclusion, axi-IABP is an effective bridging strategy that enhances patient mobility but is associated with a high rate of device-related complications, predominantly mechanical in nature, underscoring the importance of careful patient selection and monitoring.

Title: Iliohypogastric and Ilioinguinal Nerve Block for Awake ECPella Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Nonpostcardiotomy Cardiogenic Shock.
Journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
Abstract: In pediatric cardiogenic shock, endotracheal intubation may carry a high risk of cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction. This single-center retrospective case series (2020-2025) evaluated the feasibility, safety, and outcomes of ultrasound (US)-guided ilioinguinal-iliohypogastric (IhIG) nerve blocks (0.05-0.1 ml/kg of 0.25% ropivacaine) under light sedation to facilitate awake venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella (ECPella) surgical cannulation. Five adolescents (median age: 13 years, range: 7-17; median weight: 45 kg, range: 21-58) with nonpostcardiotomy cardiogenic shock underwent successful IhIG block placement in the pediatric intensive care unit by anesthesia-trained intensivists, followed by surgical cannulation in the catheterization laboratory. Intubation and mechanical ventilation were avoided during initial cannulation and throughout ECPella duration. Three patients required a modified chimney Y-graft for cannula placement, and two experienced local surgical bleeding. All five patients survived to hospital discharge, with three achieving direct biventricular recovery. Based on these preliminary data, US-guided IhIG nerve block seems a feasible and safe strategy for awake ECPella cannulation in selected pediatric patients, successfully avoiding high-risk invasive ventilation and general anesthesia.

Title: Collateral channel crossing failure during retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention: predictors and associated procedural outcomes from a multicenter registry.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Retrograde chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO PCI) may fail at several stages. The authors evaluated factors associated with collateral channel crossing failure during retrograde CTO PCI and its associations with technical success and procedural complications.
METHODS: The authors analyzed procedures from a multicenter CTO PCI registry with attempted retrograde or retrograde-assisted strategies and recorded the retrograde result. The primary endpoint was collateral channel crossing failure. Secondary endpoints included retrograde success, overall technical success, collateral/coronary perforation, donor-vessel injury, vascular complications, and an extended complication composite.
RESULTS: Among 577 retrograde CTO PCI procedures with recorded retrograde result, retrograde success was achieved in 375 (65.0%), and collateral channel crossing failure occurred in 135 (23.4%). Overall technical success was lower with collateral crossing failure than without it (51.9% vs 88.7%), with higher rates of collateral and coronary perforation, vascular complications, and the extended complication composite.
