In the primary adjusted model restricted to procedures with known collateral connection (CC) grade, corkscrew collateral morphology (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.85; 95% CI, 3.63-12.91) and CC0 grade (adjusted OR, 4.70; 95% CI, 1.97-11.26) were associated with higher odds of crossing failure, whereas CC2/CC3 grade was associated with lower odds (adjusted OR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.22-0.92).
CONCLUSIONS: Collateral channel crossing failure was common in retrograde CTO PCI and was associated with lower technical success and greater complication burden. Unfavorable collateral morphology was associated with a higher risk of crossing failure; repeated collateral attempts may indicate escalating procedural difficulty and may warrant strategy reassessment.

Title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes of Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.
Abstract: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), particularly among individuals at increased risk of bleeding. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and safety of LAAC versus OAC in AF. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) was conducted to evaluate the sufficiency of cumulative evidence. Six randomized trials involving 7,004 patients were included. Compared with OAC, LAAC demonstrated similar risks of stroke, systemic embolism, cardiovascular death, all-cause mortality, and transient ischemic attack. LAAC showed a nominally higher risk of ischemic stroke or systemic embolization (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.04-1.79), although this finding was not robust to sensitivity analysis, with a borderline increase in ischemic stroke. In contrast, LAAC significantly reduced non-procedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.42-0.58), while major bleeding and hemorrhagic stroke were comparable between groups. TSA confirmed sufficient evidence supporting the reduction in bleeding outcomes but indicated that current evidence remains insufficient to establish definitive conclusions regarding thromboembolic efficacy. Overall, LAAC was not associated with statistically significant differences in several thromboembolic and mortality outcomes compared with OAC, while providing a substantial reduction in non-procedural clinically relevant bleeding. However, the potential signal toward increased ischemic events warrants further investigation in adequately powered randomized trials, particularly against contemporary DOAC-based therapy.

Title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.
METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination.
RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%).
DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

Title: An integrated machine learning framework for cerebral aneurysm rupture status classification using clinical, morphological, and hemodynamic features.
Abstract: Accurate assessment of cerebral aneurysm rupture status remains a critical challenge in neurovascular research due to the complex interplay between geometric, hemodynamic, and clinical factors. In this study, we developed and evaluated a machine-learning framework for retrospective rupture-status classification in 708 patient-specific aneurysms by integrating 55 predictors: three clinical variables, 35 morphological descriptors, and 17 hemodynamic parameters derived from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Blood flow was modeled as incompressible laminar flow with a non-Newtonian Carreau-Yasuda viscosity model to capture shear-thinning behavior in cerebral arteries. We compared 13 supervised classifiers, 10 unsupervised clustering approaches, and two neural-network models. Model training and hyperparameter optimization were performed using stratified five-fold cross-validation within a 90/10 training-testing split, with performance evaluated using ROC-AUC, precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score. Among the evaluated models, BaggingSVM achieved the strongest discrimination on the independent test set (ROC-AUC = 0.78), followed by SVM (0.75) and Gaussian Process (0.75). A scenario comparison using BaggingSVM showed that the combined feature set improved classification performance (AUC = 0.78) compared with clinical+morphological features (AUC = 0.76) and clinical+hemodynamical features (AUC = 0.71) settings. Sensitivity-oriented threshold tuning increased recall for ruptured aneurysm detection, reaching values up to 0.96 for BaggingSVM. Permutation feature importance analysis revealed consistent dominance of ellipticity index, low shear area ratio (LSAR), aneurysm location, irregularity and aneurysm angle across models. a small subset of variables contributes disproportionately to rupture-status classification, although the reduced-feature analysis indicates that lower-ranked predictors collectively provide additional discriminatory information. The proposed framework demonstrates the value of integrating physiologically informed hemodynamic modeling with machine learning to improve data-driven rupture status assessment and provides a scalable foundation for future clinical decision-support studies in cerebrovascular diagnostics.

Title: Association between coronary artery calcium score and myocardial ischemia assessed by stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring effectively stratifies cardiovascular risk, and stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) accurately detects myocardial ischemia. We aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with myocardial ischemia on CMR in patients with CAC, and to assess the clinical impact of myocardial ischemia following CMR.
METHODS: This study included 215 patients aged ≥18 years who underwent CAC scoring for risk stratification, followed by stress CMR between 2013 and 2026. The prevalence and predictors of myocardial ischemia were investigated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the association between CAC scores and myocardial ischemia. Additionally, subsequent clinical management following CMR was determined.
RESULTS: The mean age was 69.3 ± 9.1 years (60.9% male). The average 10-year PREVENT risk score was 18.6 ± 8.7%. Overall, myocardial ischemia was present in 26.0% of patients (56/215): 17.1% in the CAC 300-999 Agatston units (AU) group (14/82) and 41.6% in the CAC ≥ 1,000 AU group (42/101). CAC score was the only independent predictor of myocardial ischemia (adjusted OR 1.07, 95%CI 1.03 - 1.10; p < 0.001 per 100 AU). Across clinical risk score categories and diabetes status, CAC score was consistently associated with myocardial ischemia, with no significant interactions observed (all p for interaction >0.05).The number of ischemic segments increased with increasing CAC scores (p < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an optimal cutoff threshold of CAC ≥ 1,093 AU for detecting myocardial ischemia (AUC 0.75, p < 0.001). The clinical impact of stress CMR included medication changes in 37.2% of patients, while 18.1% underwent invasive procedures.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CAC scores undergoing stress CMR, the prevalence of myocardial ischemia was approximately one-fourth and was associated with higher CAC scores. Stress CMR may influence clinical management in this population. Larger or prospective studies validating these findings and evaluating prognosis are warranted.

Title: Sex-Specific Prognostic Significance of Interventricular Septal Thickness in Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interventricular septal (IVS) thickness is routinely measured by echocardiography, yet its prognostic significance in heart failure (HF), and whether it differs by sex, remains uncertain.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with HF from the SHEBAHEART registry (2009-2025). IVS thickness was classified as normal (<1.1 cm), mildly thickened (≥1.1 to ≤1.3 cm), or severely thickened (>1.3 cm), using identical thresholds by sex. Associations with all-cause mortality were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, comorbidities, and left ventricular ejection fraction, with formal testing for sex-by-IVS interaction.
RESULTS: Among 20,836 patients (median age, 74 years; 39% women), 41% had mild and 18% had severe IVS thickening. During a median follow-up of 4 years, 11,930 patients (57%) died; 4-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative mortality increased across IVS categories (35%, 39%, and 42%; P < 0.001). In primary complete-case analysis (n = 13,902), the sex-by-IVS interaction was significant (P = 0.030). Adjusted hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) for mild and severe thickening were 1.16 (1.07-1.26) and 1.19 (1.08-1.32) in women, compared with 1.02 (0.96-1.09) and 1.07 (0.99-1.16) in men. The sex-by-IVS interaction remained significant in multiple-imputation and time-varying Cox analyses, but not with sex-specific IVS reference partitions.
CONCLUSIONS: With common absolute IVS thresholds, increased septal thickness was more strongly associated with all-cause mortality in women than in men with HF. These findings support evaluation of IVS thickness as a potential component of sex-specific risk stratification in HF.

Title: Cognitive frailty in patients with acute coronary syndromes: A scoping review.
Abstract:
AIMS: To address a critical knowledge gap, this is the first scoping review to systematically map and describe the evidence on cognitive frailty in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS), including its prevalence, assessment tools, associated factors, and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: The Joanna Briggs Institute methodology guided the conduct of this scoping review, which has been reported in line with the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Following the PCC framework, a systematic search was conducted across five databases: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science. The search was performed up to August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality.
RESULTS: A total of 9 studies were included. The prevalence of cognitive frailty ranged from 8% to 55%, the differences attributed to the heterogeneity of assessment tools and diagnostic criteria. Regarding assessment tools, the FRAIL scale combined with the Short Portable Mental Status Questionnaire was the most commonly used combinations. Risk factors covered sociodemographic, physical health, and clinical domains. Prognostically, cognitive frailty was linked to higher composite short‑term (in‑hospital complications, prolonged stay, 30‑day events) and medium‑term (6‑month MACCE) risks, and also to elevated long‑term mortality and readmission.
CONCLUSION: Cognitive frailty is commonly reported in patients with ACS, with considerable variation across studies, and an association with adverse outcomes has been noted in multiple reports. However, the lack of standardized assessment tools and criteria makes results difficult to compare and synthesize. Existing prospective studies have primarily relied on baseline measurements of cognitive frailty to predict subsequent outcomes, without repeated assessments over time. This limits the ability to characterise the dynamic trajectory of cognitive frailty during the ACS course. Future research should focus on longitudinal studies, the development of rapid screening tools, and the exploration of multidisciplinary interventions.

Title: Correction to: Pathophysiology, prevention, and management of coronary microvascular obstruction: A clinical consensus statement of the ESC Working Group on Coronary Pathophysiology & Microcirculation, the ESC Working Group on Thrombosis, and the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC.
Remodeling of Failed Pulmonary Valve Autografts After the Ross Procedure.
Abstract: The Ross procedure utilizes a pulmonary autograft for aortic valve replacement, but late autograft failure remains a clinical challenge. In this exploratory study, we characterized structural alterations in failed pulmonary autografts using digital morphometric analysis. Five autografts explanted because of regurgitation were compared with six autopsy control pulmonary valves using special stains and alpha-smooth muscle actin immunohistochemistry. One histologically most affected section per valve was evaluated using QuPath. Failed autografts showed leaflet thickening, elastosis, fibrosis, and myxomatous matrix accumulation. Compared with controls, autografts had greater maximum leaflet thickness (1.540 vs. 0.447 mm; P = 0.004), cross-sectional area (8.730 vs. 3.045 mm²; P = 0.004), α-SMA-positive area (0.707 vs. 0.046 mm²; P = 0.008), and α-SMA-positive area fraction (0.069 vs. 0.016; P = 0.017). The findings demonstrate extracellular matrix alterations and increased α-SMA immunoreactivity in hotspot regions, suggesting a myxomatous-like remodeling pattern.

Title: The impact of leaflet thrombosis on transcatheter aortic valve degeneration: a narrative review.
Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has expanded into younger and lower-risk patients, making long-term valve durability increasingly important. Leaflet thrombosis, most commonly identified on computed tomography as hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), is common after TAVI. Whether leaflet thrombosis contributes to structural valve deterioration (SVD) remains incompletely understood. To summarize the current evidence on the relationship between leaflet thrombosis and SVD after TAVI, with a focus on clinical outcomes, imaging findings, antithrombotic therapy, and pathophysiological mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes available clinical, imaging, mechanistic, histopathological and antithrombotic literature addressing leaflet thrombosis and valve durability after TAVI. CT studies show that leaflet thrombosis occurs in 13-32% of patients within the first post-procedural year. Although some lesions resolve spontaneously, longitudinal imaging studies demonstrate persistence in a substantial proportion of patients, supporting the presence of an underlying valve-related substrate. HALT has not consistently been associated with adverse valve hemodynamics during the first year after implantation. Long-term TAVI durability studies report low rates of severe SVD (0.8-1.5% up to 10 years), although outcomes vary according to valve generation and study population. The 10-year NOTION and PARTNER 2A data provide important long-term durability information, but neither study included systematic longitudinal CT assessment of leaflet thrombosis. Observational studies linking early HALT to subsequent hemodynamic valve deterioration have yielded conflicting results. Indirect evidence from anticoagulation studies and histopathological investigations supports biological plausibility for a relationship between leaflet thrombosis and progressive leaflet injury, but does not establish causality. Leaflet thrombosis is a frequent imaging finding after TAVI and may persist over time, but its contribution to long-term SVD remains uncertain. Current evidence supports a potential biological relationship between leaflet thrombosis and valve degeneration but does not demonstrate that HALT is a causal precursor of clinically relevant SVD. Prospective studies combining serial CT imaging with long-term, standardized assessment of structural valve outcomes are required to resolve this question.

Title: Anticoagulation stewardship quality improvement project to decrease incidence of supratherapeutic activated partial thromboplastic time in overweight cancer patients on unfractionated heparin infusions.
Abstract: Unfractionated Heparin (UFH) is widely used to treat multiple conditions in hospitalized patients. Standard dosing based on actual body weight (ABW) may lead to over-anticoagulation in overweight patients due to the limited vascularity of adipose tissue. Historically, ABW was used when BMI ≤ 40 kg/m2, and adjusted body weight (AdjBW) when BMI > 40 kg/m2. However, patients with ABW >130% of ideal body weight (IBW) and BMI ≤ 40 kg/m2 experienced increased rates of supratherapeutic activated partial thromboplastin times (aPTTs). The objective of this project was to evaluate whether use of AdjBW for initial UFH dosing reduces supratherapeutic aPTTs in cancer patients with ABW >130% of IBW and BMI ≤ 40 kg/m2. A new high intensity UFH protocol utilizing AdjBW UFH dosing was implemented on July 9, 2024. This single-center quality improvement study compared the pre- and post-intervention aPTTs in hospitalized cancer patients. In the bolus/transition cohort the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs decreased by 37% (RR 0.63; 95% CI: [0.46-0.86], p = 0.004 and the percentage of first therapeutic aPTTs increased by 82.1% (RR 1.82; 95% CI: [1.12-2.97], p = 0.03. In the no bolus cohort, the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs decreased by 39.2% (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.38-0.97, p = 0.04). Time to therapeutic aPTT was shorter in the post-implementation arm compared to pre-implementation. In conclusion, AdjBW-based UFH dosing significantly reduced the percentage of first supratherapeutic aPTTs and decreased the time to first therapeutic aPTT in obese cancer patients on the high-intensity UFH protocol.

Title: Cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1 is a novel prognostic biomarker in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) exhibits great prognostic heterogeneity, necessitating the identification of high-risk patients for timely treatment. This study aimed to find novel prognostic biomarkers directly from diseased cardiac tissue to improve risk stratification of HCM. We utilized a myocardial transcriptome discovery cohort (n = 246; median follow-up 6.8 years) alongside two independent plasma validation cohorts (Beijing, n = 1,238; follow-up 2.5 years; Xi'an, n = 402; follow-up 4.8 years). The primary and secondary endpoints were cardiovascular death and sudden cardiac death (SCD), respectively. In the discovery cohort, myocardial expression of CECR1 (cat eye syndrome chromosome region, candidate 1, also known as ADA2, Adenosine Deaminase 2) demonstrated the strongest association with cardiovascular death (P = 9.6 × 10-5). Plasma CECR1 levels correlated modestly but significantly with myocardial expression. In the Beijing validation cohort, decreased plasma CECR1 predicted increased risks of cardiovascular death (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 3.731, P < 0.001) and SCD (adjusted HR 7.398, P < 0.001), with areas under the curves (AUCs) of 0.720 and 0.798, respectively. These findings were replicated in the Xi'an validation cohort. Integrating plasma CECR1 into the HCM Risk-SCD model significantly enhanced its predictive performance, increasing the AUC from 0.723 to 0.845 (P = 0.031) in the Beijing validation cohort and consistently improving it from 0.600 to 0.781 (P = 0.018) in the Xi'an validation cohort. In conclusion, CECR1 represents a novel prognostic biomarker of HCM. Measurement of CECR1 may improve risk stratification by facilitating the identification of individuals at higher risk of cardiovascular mortality. CECR1 assessment may provide additional information for SCD risk evaluation and support clinical decision-making regarding implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy.

Title: Predictive and risk stratification performance of CCTA-derived pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events: retrospective development and prospective validation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the predictive efficacy and risk stratification potential of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent CCTA at our hospital between June 2017 and June 2020, with 5-year follow-up for MACE occurrence. Patients were grouped by MACE status. Machine learning was applied to construct and compare three models: PCAT radiomics model, fat attenuation index (FAI) model, and clinical model. Prospective validation was conducted in 578 patients with suspected CAD undergoing CCTA, who were stratified into high- and low-risk groups by the optimal cutoff of the PCAT radiomics model. The predictive and risk stratification performance of all models was assessed.
RESULTS: Fourteen PCAT radiomics features (5 first-order and 9 texture features) were finally screened. The PCAT radiomics model showed significantly superior MACE predictive performance over the FAI and clinical models (P < 0.001). Only the PCAT radiomics model identified significantly higher MACE risk in the high-risk versus low-risk group (HR=2.611, 95% CI: 1.806-3.775, P < 0.001), with progressively reduced MACE-free survival in the high-risk group during follow-up (P < 0.001). No such significant between-group differences were found in the FAI and clinical models (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The PCAT radiomics model showed favorable performance for predicting the composite MACE endpoint, which was predominantly driven by worsening stable or unstable angina, and provided better risk stratification than the FAI and clinical models.

Title: AI-Enabled Digital Stethoscope for Early Detection of Congenital Heart Disease: Prospective Study.
Abstract: Early detection of congenital heart disease (CHD) is critical, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to congenital cardiac services is limited. While auscultation remains a first-line screening tool, its accuracy is operator dependent. Advances in digital stethoscopes and artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance diagnostic performance. To evaluate the accuracy of an AI-based algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope for detecting CHD in children and young adults, using echocardiography as the reference standard. In this prospective single centre study, heart sounds were recorded from 721 subjects (382 with CHD, 339 controls) using the digital stethoscope at four standard auscultatory sites. Of these, 301 recordings were used for algorithm training and 420 for blinded forward testing, which was divided temporally with the data collected in first 5 months used for training and the data collected after that used for forward testing. Recordings were denoised, transformed into mel-spectrograms, and analyzed using a convolutional neural network (CovNN) to classify CHD probability. A threshold probability of > 0.5 across > 2 sites was used to predict CHD. Performance was compared against echocardiography. In forward testing, the AI algorithm correctly identified 222 of 233 CHD cases and 171 of 187 controls, yielding a sensitivity of 95.2% and specificity of 91.4%. The algorithm remained effective in noisy environments and in uncooperative children, where conventional auscultation is challenging. An AI algorithm integrated with a digital stethoscope demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for CHD detection in children and young adults. By leveraging mel-spectrogram features, it overcomes key limitations of isolated time-domain or frequency domain analysis and shows promise as a scalable, non-invasive screening tool for early CHD detection, particularly in resource-limited settings.

Title: Beyond LDL-C reduction: molecular pleiotropy and emerging therapeutic roles of statins.
Abstract: Statins rank among the most prevalent pharmacological treatments for the prevention and management of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chiefly by inhibiting 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase and consequently reducing low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels. In addition to their recognized lipid-lowering properties, experimental, translational, and clinical research has uncovered various possible pleiotropic effects. These cholesterol-independent effects relate to the modulation of the mevalonate pathway and subsequent signaling molecules, which may affect endothelial function, nitric oxide availability, oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, atherosclerotic plaque stability, and thrombotic mechanisms. Nonetheless, the degree to which these processes yield clinically significant advantages apart from LDL-C lowering is still ambiguous. The clinical pharmacology of statins is examined, encompassing their pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic characteristics, molecular mechanisms of action, and novel therapeutic applications. Particular attention is directed at the molecular foundation and clinical relevance of statin pleiotropy in neurological conditions, metabolic disorders, inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, infectious illnesses, and cancer. The advantages and drawbacks of these prospective indications are rigorously assessed utilizing data from preclinical investigations, observational studies, randomized controlled trials, and meta-analyses. The evaluation additionally discusses safety factors, clinically significant drug-drug interactions, and the influence of pharmacogenomics in formulating individualized treatment approaches. Overall, statins have well-established cardiovascular benefits, whereas the clinical significance of their proposed pleiotropic effects and potential applications beyond cardiovascular disease varies across indications and remains incompletely established. Further high-quality, indication-specific clinical trials are needed to determine whether these effects provide additional therapeutic benefits and to define their appropriate clinical roles.

Title: Effect of Intravenous Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide on Left Ventricular Function After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Journal: American journal of cardiovascular drugs : drugs, devices, and other interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite timely reperfusion and guideline-directed therapies, the recovery of left ventricular function after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains suboptimal. Adjunctive metabolic therapy may enhance post-infarction cardiac repair. Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺), a key regulator of cellular bioenergetics and redox homeostasis, has cardioprotective effects in experimental ischemia-reperfusion injury. However, its clinical impact in patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 120 patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI were assigned to receive intravenous NAD⁺ (10 mg/day) or placebo for 7 days, in addition to standard medical therapy. The primary endpoint was the left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) at 30 days. The secondary endpoints included N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels at 7 and 30 days, echocardiographic parameters at 30 days, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) at 6 months.
RESULTS: At 30 days, the NAD⁺ group demonstrated a modest but significant improvement in LVEF compared with the placebo group (56.32 ± 8.04% vs. 53.37 ± 8.12%, p = 0.048). NT-proBNP levels were lower in the NAD⁺ group at follow-up. However, findings for LV remodeling parameters were mixed, and no significant between-group difference was observed in 6-month MACCE rates.
CONCLUSIONS: Short-term intravenous NAD⁺ therapy following primary PCI improved left ventricular systolic function and reduced NT-proBNP levels in patients with STEMI. These findings suggest that restoring NAD⁺ availability may facilitate post-ischemic cardiac recovery, potentially through mechanisms related to mitochondrial energy metabolism and NAD⁺-dependent stress-response signaling. Larger trials are required to confirm its long-term clinical benefits and elucidate the underlying biological pathways.
REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier number ChiCTR2200059333.

Title: Diagnostic performance of the Normandy score for infective endocarditis in native bone and joint infections.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The Normandy score was developed to estimate the risk of typical cardiac lesions of infective endocarditis (IE) among patients with native bone and joint infections (NBJI). The aim of this study was to externally validate the Normandy score for the prediction typical cardiac lesions and IE in patients with NBJI.
METHODS: Retrospective study.
SETTING: This study included adult patients with NBJI (2014-2025). Typical cardiac lesions included vegetations, abscess, leaflet perforation, prosthetic valve dehiscence, aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, or fistula identified by echocardiography or cardiac CT, and abnormal metabolic activity on [18F]FDG-PET/CT. IE was diagnosed according to the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria. The primary outcome was the negative likelihood ratio (NLR), with a threshold of < 0.10 to safely rule out IE or typical cardiac lesions.
RESULTS: Among 462 NBJI episodes, typical cardiac lesions were identified in 101 (22%) and IE was diagnosed in 151 (33%). The Normandy score classified 415 (90%) episodes as high risk compared to 450 (97%) that actually had echocardiography. Against the typical cardiac lesion reference standard, the NLR was 0.08 (95% CI 0.01-0.56). Against the IE reference standard, the NLR was 0.14 (0.04-0.44).
CONCLUSIONS: In this highly selected population (89% bacteremic, 33% with IE), the Normandy score met the prespecified NLR threshold for typical cardiac lesions, but not for IE overall. Because it classified 90% of episodes as high risk, it would have reduced echocardiography by only 7 percentage points A more discriminatory prediction tool is needed to meaningfully optimize resource utilization in this population.

Title: Risk of Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Psoriasis, Psoriatic Arthritis, and/or Other Forms of Spondyloarthritis: A Cohort of 72,291 Biologic New Users.
Journal: BioDrugs : clinical immunotherapeutics, biopharmaceuticals and gene therapy
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of biologic therapies (biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs [bDMARD]) used in psoriasis (Pso), psoriatic arthritis (PsA), and other forms of spondyloarthritis (SpA) on the risk of major cardiovascular events (MACE) remains controversial.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the risk of MACE after initiation of a bDMARD among patients with Pso, PsA, or SpA, in a real-world clinical setting.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults with Pso, PsA, or SpA who initiated a bDMARD (tumor necrosis factor inhibitors [TNFi]; interleukin [IL] inhibitors: IL-12/23i, IL-23i, IL-17i) between 1 July, 2016, and 31 July, 2023 were eligible for inclusion. The primary outcome was incident MACE, defined as cardiovascular death and/or hospitalization for acute myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke. Inverse probability-weighted Cox models were used to estimate weighted hazard ratios and their confidence intervals. Models were further adjusted for time-varying concomitant treatments, treatment indication, year of initiation, and prior non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. An interaction term between bDMARD exposure and history of cardiovascular disease was included.
RESULTS: A total of 72,291 patients were included (mean age 46.1 ± 14.2 years, 49.4% female): 10,703 IL-17i (14.8%), 7952 IL-23i (11.0%), 5962 IL-12/23i (8.2%), and 47,674TNFi (66.0%). Compared with initiators of other bDMARDs, TNFi initiators were younger and had fewer comorbidities and cardiovascular risk factors at baseline. During follow-up, 438 patients (0.6%) experienced a MACE, including 107 (0.1%) cardiovascular deaths. The median time to event was 13.5 months (interquartile range, 5.1-30.4). In crude analyses, initiation of IL-17i, IL-23i, and IL-12/23i was associated with a higher risk of MACE compared withTNFi drugs. However, among patients without a history of cardiovascular disease, after inverse probability of treatment weighting and adjustment, no significant association was observed (weighted hazard ratio [95% confidence interval]: 0.90 [0.57-1.43] for IL-12/23i, 1.12 [0.66-1.88] for IL-23i, and 1.07 [0.74-1.55] for IL-17i). Findings held across most sensitivity analyses, except for the short-term analysis restricted to the first 6 months after treatment initiation, in which a trend toward a higher MACE risk with IL-17i was observed. A trend toward a higher MACE risk with IL-17i was also observed among men, patients aged ≥ 50 years, and those with a history of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use. However, the number of events was low, and the results did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: No significant increase in MACE risk was observed with IL-12/23i, IL-23i, or IL-17i compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors. However, the study lacked sufficient power to draw definitive conclusions regarding a possible increased risk associated with IL-17i in patients with a high baseline cardiovascular risk profile, or the potentiation of this risk by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use.

Title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of SHR-2004, a Novel Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: An Open-Label Phase 1b Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: SHR-2004, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting factor XI (FXI), demonstrates potential for preventing and treating thrombotic events with reduced bleeding risk. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of SHR-2004 in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).
METHODS: In this open-label dose-escalation phase 1b study, patients with AF aged ≥ 40 and < 80 years with a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥ 1 (male) or ≥ 2 (female) were enrolled to receive six doses of SHR-2004. The primary endpoints were safety and tolerability. PK and PD parameters, including activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and FXI activity, were also assessed.
RESULTS: From 10 April 2024 to 6 May 2024, ten patients were enrolled to receive SHR-2004 (180 mg subcutaneously, every 2 weeks), with a median age of 68.0 years, and male being in the majority (9/10). The median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 2.5 (range 1-6). The trial was terminated after completion of the 180 mg cohort. SHR-2004 was well tolerated. Treatment-emergent adverse events (AEs) occurred in eight (80.0%) patients, and treatment-related AEs were reported in six (60.0%) patients. All AEs were mild or moderate. Notably, no major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events were reported. Plasma exposure of SHR-2004 increased rapidly after administration and reached steady state by day 57 with the geometric mean (CV%) plasma concentration of 24,000 (26.4) ng/mL. This exposure resulted in median FXI activity after the first dose of 1.40% (IQR 1.40-1.40%). The outcomes of PD effects, FXI activity and aPTT prolongation, reached a plateau during the treatment period from day 3 to day 85 indicating that the 180 mg dosage regimen achieved and maintained therapeutic pharmacodynamic steady state.
CONCLUSIONS: Multiple subcutaneous doses of SHR-2004 were generally well tolerated in patients with AF. These preliminary findings support further clinical development of SHR-2004 in this population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT06280768. Trial registration date: 28 February 2024.

Title: The effect of acupuncture-rehabilitation therapy on brain functional plasticity in motor aphasia after ischemic stroke: a randomized clinical neuroimaging trial.
Abstract: Motor aphasia is the most prevalent type of aphasia following ischemic stroke (IS). This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and underlying neural mechanisms of acupuncture-rehabilitation (A-R) therapy on motor aphasia after IS. Twenty-six patients with post-IS motor aphasia were randomly assigned to either the A-R group or the Conventional Rehabilitation (CR) group in a 1:1 ratio, and matched by age and gender with 26 healthy controls (HCs). The CR group received standard treatment and language training, while the A-R group additionally underwent scalp acupoint cluster acupuncture. Behavioral assessments and Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (BOLD-fMRI) scans were conducted before and after the four-week intervention to evaluate therapeutic outcomes and underlying mechanisms. Compared to HCs, patients exhibited decreased Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations (ALFF) in the right precuneus (p < 0.05) and reduced Regional Homogeneity (ReHo) in the left precuneus/postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). Enhanced functional connectivity (FC) was observed in regions including the left Broca's area and right superior temporal gyrus, left Broca's area and right inferior frontal orbitalis gyrus, left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus, left Broca's area and right postcentral gyrus (p < 0.05). After intervention, significant improvements were observed in Aphasia Quotient (AQ) scores and sub-item performance in both patient groups (p < 0.05), with the A-R group showing greater gains in AQ and spontaneous speech scores compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FMRI results indicated a significant increase in mean ALFF (mALFF) in the left inferior temporal gyrus after A-R treatment (p < 0.05) compared to before, and higher szReHo in the left anterior central gyrus compared to the CR group (p < 0.05). FC between the left Broca's area and right precentral gyrus decreased in the A-R group (p < 0.05). Additionally, a negative correlation was observed between the right anterior central gyrus and listening comprehension (r = -0.574, p = 0.020). The findings suggest that both A-R and CR therapies enhance language function in patients with motor aphasia post-IS, with A-R therapy demonstrating superior efficacy. The therapeutic mechanism of A-R likely involves activating left hemisphere brain regions, suppressing right hemisphere activity, and restoring hemispheric balance to facilitate functional recovery.

Title: Cigarette smoking and circulating androgens in women from the Epic Florence cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The harmful effects of smoking on health include respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, adverse reproductive outcomes, and an increased risk of several cancers, including breast cancer. While the effect of circulating estrogens on breast cancer development is well established, recent studies suggest androgen involvement, but little is known about lifestyle factors influencing their levels. We investigated the relationship between smoking habits and circulating androgen levels in pre- and postmenopausal women.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study on 867 women randomly selected from participants enrolled in the EPIC Florence study between 1993 and 1998. At enrollment, participants provided data on diet, lifestyle, reproductive history, and anthropometry. Blood samples were collected, aliquoted, and stored in liquid nitrogen. To assess the association between active smoking and circulating androgens, we used linear regression models adjusted for age, body mass index, waist circumference, education level, physical activity level, alcohol consumption, caloric intake, and reproductive history, separately for pre- and postmenopausal women.
RESULTS: In pre- and postmenopausal women, current smokers had higher testosterone (premenopause: exp(β) 1.13; 95% CI 1.01-1.26 and postmenopause: exp(β) 1.13; 95% CI 1.00-0.26) and androstenedione levels (premenopause: exp(β) 1.14; 95% CI 1.04-1.26 and postmenopause: exp(β) 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.28) compared to never smokers. A significant trend toward increasing androstenedione with increasing pack-years of smoking was observed in postmenopausal women.
CONCLUSIONS: Our analysis revealed a direct association between circulating levels of testosterone and androstenedione and smoking habit, and a dose-response effect for androstenedione in postmenopausal women. This association could provide insights into the mechanisms linking smoking to breast cancer risk.

Title: Outcome-Blind EEG Microstate Topography After Cardiac Arrest: Spatial Expression of a Lateralized Microstate and Association with Neurological Outcome.
Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is central to neurological assessment after cardiac arrest, yet conventional approaches predominantly characterize amplitude, frequency content, continuity, suppression, reactivity, or predefined pathological patterns. EEG microstates provide a complementary framework by describing quasi-stable configurations of the global scalp electric field. We investigated whether an outcome-blind microstate decomposition of EEG from comatose survivors of cardiac arrest identifies reproducible spatial states associated with neurological outcome. We performed a secondary analysis of the multicenter I-CARE/PhysioNet database. Following prespecified EEG screening requiring continuous 19-channel recordings of at least 300 s, 567 subjects were included (34 excluded at preflight). Microstate reconstruction was performed outcome-blind using a fixed 300-s continuous baseline analysis window, GFP-peak sampling capped at 500 peaks per patient, and polarity-invariant clustering across K = 2-10. After model-order evaluation, the K = 4 solution was frozen and backfitted at the patient level. Associations between microstate metrics and neurological outcome were evaluated using unadjusted, multivariable, dose-response, ROC discrimination, and extensive resampling analyses. The primary outcome analysis included 567 patients: 209 with favorable (CPC 1-2) and 358 with unfavorable (CPC 3-5) neurological outcomes. M2 global explained variance (GEV) was higher in patients with favorable outcome (median 0.0852 vs. 0.0564; rank-biserial correlation = 0.185; p = 0.000243; false-discovery-rate [FDR]-adjusted p = 0.000568 within the four-state GEV family). M2 GEV was inversely associated with CPC severity (Spearman rho = -0.144; p = 0.000583; FDR-adjusted p = 0.001419). Standalone ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.59 (95% CI 0.54-0.64). After adjustment for age, sex, and shockable rhythm in the extended cohort without return-of-spontaneous-circulation (ROSC) time (N = 535), each 1-SD increase in M2 GEV was associated with greater odds of favorable outcome (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.58; p = 0.0092). In the complete-case model additionally adjusted for ROSC time (N = 292), the association remained significant (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.10-1.97; p = 0.0087). A graded association was observed across M2 GEV quartiles without evidence of nonlinearity. Results remained directionally stable under winsorization, exclusion of distributional extremes, heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors, bootstrap resampling, leave-one-out analysis, repeated leave-five-out perturbations, and accounting for recording-center clustering. By contrast, M2 coverage, mean duration, and occurrence were not significantly associated with outcome after multiplicity correction. An outcome-blind decomposition of EEG after cardiac arrest identified a frozen microstate, M2, whose GEV was reproducibly associated with neurological outcome. The prognostic information associated with M2 was related primarily to the degree to which this spatial configuration explained the global EEG field rather than to its conventional temporal parameters. EEG microstate architecture may provide a complementary description of residual large-scale electrophysiological organization after hypoxic-ischemic brain injury. Rather than functioning as a standalone prognostic test, M2 GEV reflects residual spatial organization that complements established clinical and background EEG markers.

Title: Patient-Reported Outcomes with High-Volume Hemodiafiltration Versus High-Flux Hemodialysis Across Clinical Subgroups: Results from the CONVINCE Trial.
Journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-volume hemodiafiltration (HDF) improves survival and attenuates decline in selected patient-reported outcome (PRO) domains versus high-flux hemodialysis (HD). Whether benefits differ across clinically relevant subgroups remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a prespecified subgroup analysis of the multicenter CONVINCE randomized controlled trial comparing high-volume post-dilution HDF (≥23 L/session) with high-flux HD in adults receiving maintenance dialysis. Eight PROMIS domains were assessed quarterly over a median follow-up of 30 months. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated longitudinal PRO changes and treatment-by-subgroup interactions by prespecified baseline characteristics: age, sex, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, dialysis vintage, vascular access type, and residual urine volume. Joint-model sensitivity analyses of all eight longitudinal PROMIS trajectories and time to death assessed informative dropout due to death.
RESULTS: Of 1360 randomized participants, 1211 with baseline and follow-up PRO assessments were included. PRO treatment effects were broadly consistent across prespecified clinical subgroups, without evidence of clinically meaningful heterogeneity. Models adjusted for baseline sociodemographic and clinical characteristics showed nominal treatment-by-subgroup interactions for dialysis vintage and physical function (P = 0.03), age and pain interference (P = 0.02), and dialysis vintage and sleep disturbance (P = 0.04). Joint-model sensitivity analyses accounting for informative dropout due to mortality reproduced the first two interactions and identified nominal interactions for vascular access type and sleep disturbance (P = 0.03) and cardiovascular disease status and cognitive function (P = 0.05). Interactions were modest in magnitude, exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and not consistently observed across related PROMIS domains.
CONCLUSIONS: This prespecified exploratory subgroup analysis found no convincing evidence of clinically meaningful treatment-effect heterogeneity across baseline characteristics examined. Nominal interactions were unadjusted for multiple comparisons and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. Findings should not guide selection or exclusion of patients for high-volume HDF based on patient-reported outcomes.

Title: Safety and patient comfort after coronary artery bypass surgery: Conventional versus single-drain - a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate whether on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) using the left internal mammary artery can be safely performed without pleural drain placement and whether this approach improves postoperative comfort by reducing pain and pulmonary complications.
METHODS: A total of 207 patients who underwent elective on-pump CABG between January 2016 and December 2020 were retrospectively analysed. Patients were divided into two groups: Group 1 (n = 100) received a mediastinal drain only, and Group 2 (n = 107) received both a mediastinal and an intercostal pleural drain. Preoperative characteristics, operative variables, postoperative complications, analgesic requirements, pulmonary outcomes, and mortality were compared.
RESULTS: Preoperative and operative variables were similar between the groups. Analgesic consumption was significantly lower in Group 1 compared to Group 2 (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: 3.04 ± 1.25 versus 3.95 ± 1.50 doses, respectively; opioids: 1.33 ± 1.29 versus 2.23 ± 1.45 doses, respectively; p < 0.001). Pulmonary complications and mortality rates were comparable between the cohorts.
CONCLUSION: On-pump CABG performed without pleural drain placement appears to be safe and does not increase postoperative complications, while significantly reducing analgesic requirements and improving patient comfort.

Title: Cardiovascular safety of romosozumab versus alendronate in postmenopausal women with severe osteoporosis: a propensity-matched real-world study.
Journal: Journal of bone and mineral metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Romosozumab is highly effective for severe osteoporosis, but its cardiovascular safety is debated. The ARCH trial found more major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) with romosozumab than with alendronate, whereas the placebo-controlled FRAME trial found no signal. Real-world head-to-head data against alendronate are lacking.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network, we identified women aged ≥55 years with severe osteoporosis (pathological, lumbar vertebral, or hip fracture within 2 years) who initiated romosozumab or alendronate, excluding those with any MACE in the prior 12 months. Cohorts were matched 1:1 by propensity score on demographics, cardiovascular comorbidities, medications, and laboratory parameters, and followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was a composite of MACE; secondary outcomes were myocardial infarction (MI), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and ischemic stroke. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models.
RESULTS: After matching, 5930 women remained per group (mean age 72 years; median follow-up 365 days). Romosozumab was not associated with an increased risk of MACE (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.70-1.07), MI (HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.67-1.28), or ACS (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.72-1.32). Ischemic stroke was significantly lower with romosozumab (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.46-0.89; P=0.008). Findings were consistent in event-naïve analyses and across subgroups, including chronic kidney disease and diabetes; however, the advanced-CKD stratum (stage 4-5 or end-stage renal disease) could not be analyzed because event counts were too small for estimation.
CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women with severe osteoporosis, romosozumab was not associated with higher 12-month cardiovascular risk than alendronate. These findings are reassuring in the populations that could be evaluated, although cardiovascular safety in advanced CKD remains uncertain and prospective confirmation is warranted.

Title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Pulmonary hypertension (PH), a progressive and life-threatening condition with rising prevalence among older adults, frequently coexists with systemic hypertension, the prognostic impact of which is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between systemic hypertension and survival in patients with PH.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter cohort study analyzed data from the Pulmonary Vascular Research Institute GoDeep meta-registry, integrating global retrospective and prospective PH cohorts (n = 3238 in Europe, n = 3014 in North America, n = 96 in Africa, n = 802 in Asia, and n = 851 in Oceania). Survival was assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and adjusted for key confounders, with sensitivity analyses to validate robustness. Independent external validation was performed in a cohort in the UK. A total of 12 771 patients with incident PH (median [IQR] age, 65 [53-73] years; 7372 [58%] female) were diagnosed via right heart catheterization and comprehensive clinical data, encompassing PH groups 1-5 and all age categories. The study spans diagnosis decades from 1980 to 2020. Data were analyzed from February 2025 until September 2026.
EXPOSURES: Center-reported diagnosis of systemic hypertension, baseline systolic systemic arterial pressure (sSAP), and heart rate as well as longitudinal sSAP and heart rate trajectories.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause mortality, adjusted for confounding variables, including age, PH group, antihypertensive and PH-specific medications, and cardiac index.
RESULTS: Higher baseline sSAP and preexisting systemic hypertension were independently associated with improved survival. Patients with hypertension exhibited a 26% reduced mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74; 95% CI, 0.68-0.79) compared to their counterparts without hypertension. Survival benefits correlated positively with increasing sSAP (80-180 mm Hg), remained consistent across PH groups and age groups, and were independent of antihypertensive and PH-specific medications. Elevated heart rate was associated with higher mortality. sSAP increments correlated with improved cardiac index and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion. Decreased sSAP and higher heart rate during follow-up correlated with higher mortality. External validation in a separate UK cohort confirmed these findings.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this global PH cohort, higher sSAP was associated with enhanced survival, while a higher baseline heart rate and declining systemic blood pressure during follow-up were significantly associated with increased mortality risk.

Title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Angiotensinogen (AGT) is the precursor of angiotensin peptides and a key determinant of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity. ART101 is an investigational N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA (GalNAc-siRNA) designed to durably suppress hepatic AGT synthesis.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of single ascending doses of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA in healthy volunteers and to provide an initial exploratory assessment of blood pressure effects in patients with hypertension.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase I study was conducted from January 2025 to April 2026 with 24-week follow-up. Part A was a double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending-dose trial; part B was an open-label, single-dose study. The study took place at Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China. Part A enrolled 40 healthy adults randomized 6:2 to receive the GalNAc-siRNA (25-600 mg) or placebo; 39 completed the study. Part B enrolled 8 patients with hypertension receiving the GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg; all completed the study.
INTERVENTIONS: A single subcutaneous injection of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA (25, 75, 150, 300, or 600 mg) or placebo in part A; a single open-label subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siRNA, 600 mg, in part B.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was safety and tolerability; secondary outcomes included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, exploratory blood pressure assessments, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system biomarkers.
RESULTS: Among 40 healthy volunteers (27 [67.5%] male; mean [SD] age, 40.4 [7.8] years) and 8 patients (6 [75.0%] male; mean [SD] age, 47.3 [10.3] years) with hypertension, the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA was well tolerated. In part A, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 23 of 30 active-treatment participants (76.7%) vs 7 of 10 placebo recipients (70.0%); in part B, 6 of 8 patients (75.0%) had TEAEs. No serious adverse events, injection site reactions, or hyperkalemia were observed; all TEAEs were mild to moderate. Plasma exposure (maximum plasma concentration [Cmax] and area under the plasma concentration-time curve [AUC]) increased with dose over the wide dose range from 25 mg to 600 mg. Mean maximum serum AGT reductions of 93% (at 600 mg) in healthy volunteers and 90% (at 600 mg) in patients with hypertension were observed. At 24 weeks after a single 600-mg dose, the placebo-corrected 24-hour ambulatory systolic blood pressure decreased by 12.9 mm Hg in healthy participants.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this phase I study, no serious treatment-related safety signals were identified. Sustained, dose-dependent AGT reductions and exploratory blood pressure lowering were observed. These findings support further investigation of the AGT-targeting GalNAc-siRNA as a potential long-acting therapeutic for hypertension.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: China Drug Clinical Registry Identifiers: CTR20250041 (part A) and CTR20253973 (part B).

Title: Intensive vs More Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Plaque Regression in Statin-Naive Patients: Prespecified Analyses From the FLOWPROMOTE Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Prior imaging studies (predominantly using intravascular ultrasound) have demonstrated modest plaque regression with lipid-lowering therapy in stable coronary artery disease (CAD). The effect of initiating intensive lipid-lowering therapy on coronary plaque regression across the entire coronary tree in treatment-naive patients remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To report the prespecified secondary imaging end points of the FLOWPROMOTE trial by comparing the effects of intensive vs more intensive lipid-lowering therapy on plaque regression in statin-naive patients with stable CAD and to assess the association between achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and plaque regression.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: FLOWPROMOTE was a multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolling statin-naive patients with newly diagnosed stable CAD, defined by a coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) stenosis greater than 50% and fractional flow reserve CT less than or equal to 0.80. Coronary CTA was performed at baseline and repeated at 9 and 18 months. Study data were analyzed from February 2025 to January 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to intensive lipid-lowering therapy (atorvastatin 40 mg) or more intensive lipid-lowering therapy (rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg) for 18 months.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Prespecified secondary end points included changes in total plaque volume (TPV), noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV), and calcified plaque volume (CPV) across all coronary vessels at 9 and 18 months compared with baseline.
RESULTS: A total of 104 patients (mean [SD] age, 64 [9] years; 82 male [79%]) were included in this analysis, with 52 patients in the intensive group and 52 patients in the more intensive group. LDL-C levels decreased from 119.7 to 69.5 mg/dL (-38%) with intensive therapy and from 127.4 to 42.5 mg/dL (-65%) with more intensive therapy (between-group P < .001). At 18 months, both TPV and NCPV decreased in both groups, with significantly greater regression in the more intensive-therapy group. TPV was reduced by -69.8 mm3 (-21.1%) with more intensive therapy vs -39.0 mm3 (-13.6%) with intensive therapy (between-group difference, -30.9 mm3; 95% CI, -57.2 to -4.5 mm3; P = .02), and NCPV was reduced by -82.3 mm3 (-28.2%) vs -53.5 mm3 (-20.0%), respectively (between-group difference, -28.9 mm3; 95% CI, -53.2 to -4.6 mm3; P = .02). CPV increased similarly in both groups. Regression of TPV occurred in 90% of patients receiving more intensive therapy compared with 76% receiving intensive therapy (47 of 52 [90%] vs 38 of 51 [75%]; P = .05), and regression of NCPV was observed in 98% vs 77% (51 of 52 [98%] vs 39 of 51 [77%]; P =.001). Lower achieved LDL-C levels were linearly associated with greater regression of TPV and NCPV.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This secondary analysis of the FLOWPROMOTE randomized clinical trial demonstrated that in statin-naive patients with CAD, more intensive lipid-lowering therapy was associated with significantly greater regression of total and noncalcified coronary plaque burden compared with intensive therapy. The extent of plaque regression was related to achieved LDL-C levels, supporting the potential for partial reversal of coronary atherosclerosis with intensive lipid reduction.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04737408.

Title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Concern for ototoxicity hinders loop diuretic (LD) dosing in heart failure (HF); given the mechanism by which LDs affect the ear, high-dose LDs should produce transient, not permanent, hearing changes.
OBJECTIVE: To measure the association of LD dose with permanent and temporary ototoxicity.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cohort 1 received a randomized sequence of LD doses (bumetanide, 1.25-10 mg) across study visits with serial audiometry assessments. Cohort 2 received serial LD up to furosemide 500-mg doses during a HF hospitalization with audiometry at baseline and prior to discharge. Cohort 3 retrospectively characterized clinically diagnosed ototoxicity in HF hospitalizations was defined using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. Cohorts 1 and 2 were single center, while cohort 3 was multicenter. Cohort 1 studied outpatient participants with stable HF, while cohort 2 (n = 40) and cohort 3 studied hospitalized patients with acute HF.
EXPOSURE: Intravenous LD.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were clinically diagnosed ototoxicity and hearing changes via audiometry.
RESULTS: Cohort 1 contained 50 participants, cohort 2 contained 40 participants, and cohort 3 contained 22 656 participants. In cohort 1, mean (SD) participant age was 63.2 (10.4) years, and 21 of 50 participants (42%) were women. In cohorts 1 and 2, clinically diagnosed ototoxicity was not observed. In cohort 1, at peak diuretic concentration, worsening hearing shifts were infrequent (24 ears of 400 doses [6%]) but were more common with higher doses (odds ratio [OR], 1.99; 95% CI, 1.21-3.28 per doubling dose; P = .007). Within hours, hearing shifts largely resolved and were absent in 98% of measurements (393 ears of 400 doses). No significant association between LD dose and hearing shifts was present at any time aside from peak LD concentration. In cohort 2, hearing shifts were not different across groups divided by the median daily LD dose and were not associated with LD dose (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.71-1.98 per doubling dose; P = .52). In cohort 3, 608 HF hospitalizations (2.7%) had clinically diagnosed ototoxicity. In multivariable analyses, peak dose of 160 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.52-1.31; P = .43) and 400 mg furosemide equivalents or greater (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.71-2.31; P = .41) were not associated with greater clinically diagnosed ototoxicity risk relative to less than 160 mg.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this analysis of 2 small HF cohorts, short-term exposure to high-dose LD was not associated with permanent ototoxicity, although concomitant ototoxin use was excluded. Future studies are needed to understand the risk of ototoxicity with repeated LD exposure and in broader HF populations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT04481919 and NCT05323487.

Title: Intersection of Patient and Hospital Rurality in Heart Failure Care and Outcomes.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Rural-urban disparities in heart failure (HF) care delivery and outcomes are well documented. However, it remains unclear if differences in outcomes after HF hospitalization are primarily driven by patient rural residence, hospital resources, or both.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of patient and hospital rurality with quality of care and postdischarge outcomes after hospitalization for HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries in US hospitals with HFrEF with an index hospitalization from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2021. Included were Medicare beneficiaries discharged alive after an index hospitalization for HFrEF. Participants were classified as rural patients hospitalized in rural hospitals (rural-rural), rural patients in urban hospitals (rural-urban), urban patients in urban hospitals (urban-urban), and urban patients in rural hospitals (urban-rural). Study data were analyzed from July to September 2026.
EXPOSURES: Patient rural residence and hospital rurality.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality after hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included inpatient cardiology consultation, 90-day postdischarge guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) use based on prescription fills, and HF readmission at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year.
RESULTS: Among 735 460 beneficiaries (median [IQR] age, 77 [70-85] years; 415 077 male [56.4%]), 69 061 (9.4%) were rural-rural, 65 510 (8.9%) rural-urban, 582 947 (79.3%) urban-urban, and 17 942 (2.4%) urban-rural. Compared with rural patients treated in rural hospitals, rural patients treated in urban hospitals were more likely to receive inpatient cardiology consultation (odds ratio [OR], 2.02; 95% CI, 1.84-2.22) and initiation of several GDMT classes, including β-blockers (OR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.16-1.25), ARNIs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.13-1.34), MRAs (OR, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.15-1.31), and SGLT2Is (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.32-1.67). They also had lower rates of HF readmission and mortality at all time points (HF readmission 1-year: OR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.88; mortality 1-year: OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.89-0.94) than rural-rural patients. Compared with urban patients hospitalized at urban hospitals, rural patients hospitalized at urban hospitals more often received inpatient cardiology consultation (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.31-1.44), whereas postdischarge GDMT differences were modest (absolute difference in GDMT score 0.09 points; 95% CI, 0.05-0.14). Rural patients also had lower HF readmission (1-year OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79-0.82) but higher 30- and 90-day mortality than urban patients (30-day OR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; 90-day OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results suggest that hospital rurality was associated with lower odds of GDMT use and higher rates of all-cause mortality, whereas rural residence was associated with mortality differences despite treatment in urban hospitals. Interventions addressing both inpatient resource disparities and postdischarge transitions of care may reduce rural-urban inequities in HF outcomes.

Title: Posterior Mitral Leaflet Length and Outcomes After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: From The OCEAN-Mitral Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: A short posterior mitral leaflet (PML) length is challenging anatomy for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER); however, its prognostic impact remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the association between PML length and M-TEER outcomes.
METHODS: A total of 2,441 patients with functional mitral regurgitation (MR) were stratified by preprocedural PML length: very short (7 mm or less, n = 82), short (>7-10 mm, n = 736), and adequate (>10 mm, n = 1,623) groups. Procedural outcomes, echocardiographic data, and all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization were compared.
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 14.4 months [Q1-Q3: 10.2-27.5]. At discharge, MR grade 1+ or less was comparable among the 3 groups (very short: n = 63/82, 77% vs short: n = 598/736, 81% vs adequate: n = 1,259/1,623, 78%; P = 0.129). At 1 year, MR grade numerically worsened in the very short group (MR grade 1+ or less, n = 31/52, 60%). The rate of achieving both MR grade 1+ or less and transmitral mean pressure gradient <5 mm Hg was similar among groups at discharge, but it was significantly lower in the very short group (n = 14/39, 36%) than in the short (n = 201/306, 66%) and adequate (n = 440/665, 66%) groups (P < 0.001) at 1 year. Although the incidence of the composite outcome was higher in shorter groups (P = 0.018), the PML length was not an independent risk factor in the multivariate analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: M-TEER may be feasible in selected patients with shorter PML; however, very short PML might have less favorable echocardiographic durability, warranting anatomical assessment and follow-up. Given the small subgroup and limited follow-up, these findings require cautious interpretation and validation.
CLINICAL TRIALS: OCEAN-Mitral registry (UMIN000023653).

Title: Low-Intensity Focused Ultrasound Modulation of Stellate Ganglion Attenuates Post-STEMI Ventricular Arrhythmias: First-in-Human Feasibility Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sympathetic overactivation contributes to ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Preclinical study demonstrated that low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) modulation of the left stellate ganglion (LSG) reduced post-STEMI VAs.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate whether LIFU modulation of LSG reduces VAs following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with STEMI.
METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled exploratory study, 41 STEMI undergoing primary PCI were assigned to LIFU modulation (n = 20) or sham stimulation (n = 21). LIFU was initiated in the catheterization laboratory and continued in the ward. All patients were followed up for 7 days and underwent Holter monitoring, serum biomarker assessment, echocardiographic evaluation, and safety assessment.
RESULTS: LIFU significantly reduced VA burden within 72 hours after PCI. Heart rate variability analysis indicated reduced low-frequency power and a decreased low-frequency/high-frequency ratio. Exploratory analyses also showed lower levels of proinflammatory cytokines and sympathetic neurotransmitters. Myocardial injury markers did not differ significantly between groups, whereas left ventricular ejection fraction was higher in the LIFU group on day 7. Furthermore, no significant organ dysfunction or thermal injury was observed following LIFU intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: LIFU modulation of LSG might attenuate sympathetic activity and reduce VAs in patients with STEMI undergoing PCI. This study provides the first clinical evidence supporting LIFU as a promising noninvasive neuromodulatory strategy for VA prevention in the STEMI setting. Larger multicenter trials (NCT07587294/ChiCTR2600122798, ongoing) are warranted to confirm these findings. This study offers a novel strategy for the management of VAs following STEMI.

Title: Healthy Dietary Patterns and Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Cancer Survivors: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of noncancer mortality among cancer survivors. The potential influence of healthy dietary patterns on CVD risk among cancer survivors remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to investigate the association between healthy dietary patterns and incident CVD among cancer survivors.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 8,716 cancer survivors initially free of CVD in the UK Biobank cohort. We used 24-hour dietary recall data to calculate 8 dietary pattern scores. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risks models were used to investigate the association between dietary patterns and incident CVD.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 12.3 (Q1-Q3: 11.6-13.0) years, 1,116 individuals experienced incident CVD events. When comparing the top quintile with the bottom quintile, HRs (95% CI) for total CVD were 0.72 (0.58-0.88) for Mediterranean diet score, 0.74 (0.61-0.89) for Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to stop Hypertension Diet Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay score, 0.63 (0.52-0.76) for Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010, 0.65 (0.53-0.79) for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension score, 0.82 (0.68-0.99) for healthful Plant-Based Diet Index, 0.67 (0.55-0.80) for reversed energy-adjusted diet inflammatory index, and 0.80 (0.67-0.96) for healthy low-fat diet score. The findings remain robust after fitting the generalized propensity score model. At age 45, participants with the highest adherence to healthy dietary patterns gained an estimated life expectancy of 1.66 to 3.32 years more than those with the lowest adherence.
CONCLUSIONS: Adherence to healthy dietary patterns is associated with reduced CVD risk among cancer survivors, underscoring the potential for diet to support cardio-oncology care.

Title: Exploratory Associations Between Retinal Parameters and Selected Systemic Markers in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to explore associations between retinal parameters and selected systemic markers in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
METHODS: Retinal imaging was used to measure vessel diameter/tortuosity and thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) and retina in participants. Uric acid (UA), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), 24-hour urine protein levels, and mean ocular perfusion pressure (MOPP) were assessed. Intergroup comparisons were performed using 1-way analysis of variance/nonparametric tests; correlations were analyzed using linear regression.
RESULTS: In total, 150 pregnant women were included: 87 normotensive controls, 32 with gestational hypertension (GH), and 31 with preeclampsia (PE). Across groups, arteriolar diameter decreased, temporal venular diameter and inferonasal arteriolar tortuosity increased (P < 0.001), and inferotemporal venular tortuosity decreased (P = 0.017). Nasal RNFL thickness increased (P < 0.001), with nonsignificant changes in other quadrants. No significant trends were noted for retinal thickness. MOPP interacted with nasal RNFL thickness (P < 0.05), but not with retinal thickness. The 24-hour urine protein and UA were associated with superotemporal venular and arteriolar diameters, respectively. MOPP was associated with inferotemporal, superonasal, and inferonasal arteriolar diameters, inferonasal arteriolar tortuosity, and central retinal arteriolar equivalent (P < 0.05). AST was not significantly associated with any retinal parameter.
CONCLUSIONS: UA and 24-hour urine protein were associated with retinal vascular parameters, whereas AST was not significantly associated with any retinal parameter. These exploratory associations warrant prospective validation.

Title: Individual Effects of Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) antagonize the AT1 receptor and are effective antihypertensives. Modest differences in blood pressure-lowering efficacy have been reported, reflecting variations in pharmacokinetics, receptor binding, duration of action, and potential pleiotropic effects. However, data on their comparative effects on cardiovascular outcomes in patients are scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effects of ARBs on MACE, hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and all-cause mortality in randomized trials not primarily designed to evaluate heart failure (HF).
METHODS: MEDLINE/PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ClinicalTrials.gov databases were searched until May 2025. Published RCTs reporting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), HHF or all-cause death, involving ARBs, with at least 100 individuals per arm and ≥12 months of follow-up, were included. Studies focusing primarily on patients with existing HF were excluded. Incidence rates of HHF, MACE, and all-cause death. A random-effects network meta-analysis including 27 RCTs and 702,584 patient-years was performed.
RESULTS: Candesartan reduced MACE versus placebo (OR 0.79; 95% CI, 0.63-0.97; SUCRA=0.85), ranking highest among ARBs, while telmisartan showed a smaller but significant reduction (OR 0.90; 95% CI, 0.80-0.99; SUCRA=0.61). The analysis relied on study-level data; included moderately sparse treatment networks with predominantly indirect comparisons between ARBs.
CONCLUSION: This network meta-analysis in patients without baseline HF indicates that candesartan and telmisartan reduce MACE, suggesting clinically meaningful differences among ARBs. Given the predominantly indirect nature of several comparisons, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis

Title: Association between the Inflammatory Atherosclerosis Index and Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease: NHANES 2017-2020.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) prevalence is increasing globally and is closely associated with dysregulated lipid metabolism and inflammation. However, the relationship between NAFLD and the inflammatory atherosclerosis index (IAI), which reflects these processes, is unclear.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between IAI and NAFLD in a representative sample of U.S. adults.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 5,309 adults from the U.S. NHANES database. Multivariate weighted logistic regression was used to assess the association between IAI and NAFLD. Restricted cubic splines explored nonlinear relationships, and ROC analysis evaluated diagnostic performance.
RESULTS: A total of 5,309 participants were included, of whom 37.6% had NAFLD. Obesity and metabolic abnormalities were more pronounced in the NAFLD group, and IAI levels were significantly higher (P < 0.001). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that IAI was independently and positively associated with NAFLD (OR = 1.538, 95% CI: 1.421-1.665). RCS analysis indicated a nonlinear relationship (P for nonlinearity = 0.0473), with an inflection point at IAI = 0.145.
