When IAI < 0.145, the risk increased steeply (OR = 2.341, 95% CI: 2.037-2.690), whereas when IAI ≥ 0.145, the increase was attenuated (OR = 1.399, 95% CI: 1.263-1.548). Subgroup analyses showed consistent results, with no significant interactions across subgroups. ROC analysis showed that IAI exhibited the best diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.722), significantly outperforming other indicators (all P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among U.S. adults, IAI demonstrates a strong, positive, and nonlinear association with NAFLD. These findings suggest IAI is a promising population-level marker for NAFLD, though prospective studies are required for validation.

Title: Effectiveness of Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Therapy for Primary Prevention in Patients with Nonischemic Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary prevention with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) has become an increasingly debated strategy, with its role in patients with nonischemic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing continued reassessment.
OBJECTIVE: To summarize the available scientific evidence on the effectiveness of ICD therapy for primary prevention in patients with nonischemic HFrEF.
METHODS: A rapid systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the recommendations of the Cochrane Rapid Reviews Methods Group and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p-value < 0.05. Searches were performed in the MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL databases. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating ICD implantation for primary prevention were included, with sudden cardiac death (SCD), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality as the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 18 publications reporting daata from six pivotal RCTs were included. ICD therapy was associated with a statistically significant reduction in SCD (relative risk [RR] 0.41; 95%CI 0.26-0.65; high-certainty evidence) and cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.75; 95%CI 0.59-0.95; high-certainty evidence). For all-cause mortality, the primary analysis showed no statistically significant difference between groups (RR 0.88; 95%CI 0.72-1.07; moderate-certainty evidence). In the subgroup analysis, studies with shorter follow-up (< 6.8 years) demonstrated a significant reduction in all-cause mortality (RR 0.69; 95%CI 0.52-0.92).
CONCLUSION: In patients with nonischemic HFrEF, ICD therapy reduced SCD and cardiovascular mortality but did not significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the primary analysis. These findings support the use of ICD therapy when guided by individualized clinical assessment.

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in emergency settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of emergency clinician-performed ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and explore variation by scan protocol and operator group.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis included studies of adults with suspected DVT in emergency settings. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 8 April 2026, and a targeted literature update was conducted through 20 September 2026 during revision. A bivariate binomial random-effects model jointly estimated sensitivity and specificity. The primary analysis included one dataset per study to avoid duplicate weighting of paired cohorts. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with QUADAS-2. Protocol and operator subgroup analyses were exploratory. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261361599).ResultsSixteen studies contributed quantitative data, providing 17 protocol datasets because one paired cohort was evaluated with both two-point and three-point protocols. Selecting the three-point result from that paired cohort for the primary overall model yielded 16 independent study datasets comprising 2,781 patient or limb/examination units. Pooled sensitivity was 0.91 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.85-0.95), and specificity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Sensitivity estimates for two-point and three-point/extended protocols were 0.87 and 0.92, respectively. Source-data uncertainties, including a reconstructed diagnostic-analysis table in Jahanian 2019 and a provisional Crowhurst input, were examined in sensitivity analyses. Koylu 2026 was added during the revision-stage targeted literature update.ConclusionsEmergency clinician-performed ultrasound may support proximal DVT assessment within a defined diagnostic pathway. Negative limited examinations require interpretation alongside clinical probability and examination adequacy. Heterogeneity and unresolved source data limit confidence in the pooled estimates. Exploratory subgroup findings do not establish the superiority of any protocol or operator group.

Title: Cryofibrinogenemia - an often-neglected rare disease: a case series.
Journal: European review for medical and pharmacological sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryofibrinogenemia (CF) is a rare systemic condition characterized by reversible precipitation of circulating plasma components such as fibrinogen, fibrin, or fibronectin at cold temperatures that resuspend upon rewarming to body temperature. It is crucial to consider the possibility of CF in the differential diagnosis of patients with purpura or ischemic skin lesions. PLEX may serve as an effective salvage treatment for severe CF manifestations, such as refractory skin ulcers or limb digital ischemia that do not respond to conventional immunosuppressive treatment. Unfortunately, randomized controlled trials are lacking, and no guidelines exist. Our current knowledge is based on case reports and case series.
CASE SERIES: We report a case series of three patients treated at IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo, Pavia, Italy, who presented with different clinical manifestations of CF refractory to conventional immunosuppressive therapies and were successfully treated with plasmapheresis (PLEX).
CONCLUSIONS: Management of CF includes glucocorticoids, whereas azathioprine, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, anticoagulants, and intravenous fibrinolysis have been reported to be effective in more severe cases. The proposed maintenance therapy for moderate disease is corticosteroids and low-dose aspirin or stanozolol. Treatment of refractory symptomatic CF remains challenging. Plasmapheresis (PLEX) has been reported in a few cases in the literature as a useful treatment for CF. The contribution of our cases highlights the importance of considering CF in the differential diagnosis among patients with purpura or ischemic skin lesions and PLEX as an effective salvage treatment for severe CF manifestations, such as refractory skin ulcers or limb/digital ischemia that do not respond to conventional immunosuppressive treatment.

Title: Five-Year Prognostic Outcomes After Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Treatment According to Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia Status: Insights From the BIOLUX P-III Registry.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of death, limb loss, and impaired functional recovery despite revascularisation. Drug-coated balloons may reduce restenosis and repeat intervention after infrainguinal endovascular therapy, but long-term safety and effectiveness data in patients with CLTI remain limited.
METHODS: We performed a prespecified subgroup analysis of BIOLUX P-III, a prospective international post-market all-comers registry evaluating the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon for infrainguinal peripheral artery disease. Outcomes were compared between patients with and without CLTI through 60 months. Endpoints included freedom from major adverse events, clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation, major target-limb amputation, amputation-free survival and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Because follow-up completeness declined substantially by 60 months, late estimates were interpreted in the context of censoring, attrition and competing mortality.
RESULTS: Among 877 treated patients, 328 (37.4%) had CLTI. Technical success exceeded 98% in both groups. Patients with CLTI had greater baseline comorbidity, more advanced limb threat and more frequent below-the-knee disease. At 60 months, freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation was 85.3% in patients with CLTI and 78.3% in those without CLTI (P = .59), and freedom from major adverse events was similar (76.5% vs 74.3%; P = .13). In contrast, 5-year survival was substantially lower in patients with CLTI (47.9% vs 76.7%; P < .001). Freedom from major target-limb amputation was lower (93.3% vs 99.3%; P < .001), and amputation-free survival was reduced (47.1% vs 75.7%; P < .001). Patients with CLTI received a lower cumulative paclitaxel dose despite higher mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Passeo-18 Lux treatment was associated with preserved lesion-level durability through 5 years, but CLTI identified a high-risk prognostic phenotype with poor survival and limb outcomes. These findings suggest that long-term outcomes in CLTI are influenced by systemic comorbidity, early limb vulnerability, competing mortality and wound-related factors beyond lesion-level device performance alone.Clinical ImpactThis study provides clinically relevant insights into the long-term outcomes of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) undergoing endovascular revascularisation with drug-coated balloons. Despite high procedural success, patients with CLTI experience substantially greater long-term mortality and adverse limb outcomes than those with intermittent claudication. These findings highlight the importance of recognising CLTI as a high-risk clinical phenotype requiring comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction, multidisciplinary management, and structured postprocedural surveillance. The study's principal contribution is its evaluation of five-year outcomes in a real-world, all-comers population, providing valuable evidence to inform patient counselling, individualised treatment strategies, and long-term clinical decision-making.

Title: Joint Expert Consensus Report on the Diagnosis and Management of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Türkiye In collaboration with Turkish Society of Cardiology, Turkish Thoracic Society and Pulmonary Vascular Disease Research Association (ADHAD).
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive and life-threatening disease characterized by increased pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular (RV) dysfunction, requiring early diagnosis and timely management. This joint expert consensus report, developed in collaboration with the Turkish Society of Cardiology, Turkish Thoracic Society, and Pulmonary Vascular Disease Research Association (ADHAD), provides a practical, real-world framework for the diagnosis and management of PAH in Türkiye. The document presents updated, practice-oriented diagnostic algorithms designed to facilitate early recognition and accurate classification of PAH. A key objective is the standardization of data collection across centers; therefore, recommended echocardiographic and hemodynamic parameters, along with their normal and pathological ranges, are clearly defined to improve consistency in clinical evaluation and reporting. Risk assessment remains a cornerstone of patient evaluation; however, current guideline-based models have important limitations. In a disease with high mortality such as PAH, greater emphasis should be placed on dynamic risk evaluation at follow-up, incorporating detailed RV assessment through imaging and hemodynamic parameters, and enabling more timely treatment escalation when needed. Accordingly, treatment algorithms have been updated to reflect contemporary therapeutic strategies, emphasizing early combination therapy, individualized management, and prompt escalation in patients who fail to achieve or maintain a low-risk profile with particular attention to RV performance. Overall, this consensus aims to harmonize clinical practice, enhance data quality, and support more proactive and standardized management of PAH across Türkiye.

Title: Clinical and toxicological factors associated with pediatric intensive care unit admission in pediatric acute poisoning: a 10-year retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute poisoning is an important cause of emergency department visits among children and adolescents. Early identification of patients requiring escalation-of-care or pediatric intensive care unit-level monitoring remains clinically challenging. The purpose of this study is to evaluate clinical and toxicological factors associated with pediatric intensive care unit admission in pediatric acute poisoning.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 652 patients younger than 18 years managed for acute poisoning between 2015 and 2024 at a tertiary university hospital. Demographic, exposure-related, toxicological, clinical, and laboratory variables were analyzed. Pediatric intensive care unit admission was evaluated as an escalation-of-care and healthcare utilization outcome. Three multivariable logistic regression models were constructed, including models excluding variables closely related to admission decisions to reduce potential incorporation bias.
RESULTS: Of 652 patients, 99 (15.2%) were admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit. Across the primary and sensitivity models, delayed presentation, psychiatric disorder history, and multiple-drug ingestion remained independently associated with admission. Lower Glasgow Coma Scale score and cardiovascular findings were associated with admission in models including clinical severity variables. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses demonstrated poor discriminatory performance of individual parameters, indicating that none were suitable as stand-alone triage tools. No deaths occurred, invasive mechanical ventilation was required in one patient, and advanced organ-support interventions were uncommon.
DISCUSSION: Pediatric intensive care unit admission appeared to reflect both observed clinical instability and anticipated toxicological risk rather than poisoning severity alone. The poor discriminatory performance of individual parameters suggests that admission decisions are multifactorial and should not rely on a single clinical or laboratory variable.
CONCLUSION: Delayed presentation, multiple-drug ingestion, psychiatric disorder history, and clinical severity indicators were associated with pediatric intensive care unit admission. These findings should be interpreted as observational evidence regarding escalation-of-care decisions rather than as a validated prediction model or triage tool in this single-center pediatric poisoning cohort.

Title: Angiographic findings, revascularisations and mortality in childhood cancer survivors with ischaemic heart disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of childhood cancer (CCS) have higher risk of developing ischaemic heart disease (IHD), however, data on coronary anatomy, revascularisations, and prognosis remain limited. The objective was to investigate angiographic findings, invasive treatment patterns and mortality in CCS with IHD compared with controls without a history of childhood cancer.
METHODS: This was a nationwide retrospective cohort-study of all 5-year survivors of leukaemia, lymphoma, or central nervous system cancer who subsequently developed IHD, with index cancer between 1958-2021. CCS were compared with population-based controls with IHD matched on cancer date by age, sex and residence.
RESULTS: 136 CCS and 667 controls with IHD were included. CCS were a median of 5.2 years younger than controls at diagnosis of IHD. CCS had a higher prevalence of left main coronary artery (LMCA) stenosis (25.0% vs. 6.5%; p < 0.001) and multivessel disease (51.2% vs. 39.4%; p = 0.043). Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) was more frequently performed in CCS (22.8% vs. 11.4%; p < 0.001), although after adjusting for relevant covariates the difference was attenuated. After a median follow-up of 5.4 years following IHD diagnosis, CCS had higher hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 1.83, 95% CI 1.31-2.54; p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.42-2.95; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CCS who developed IHD demonstrate a higher burden of extensive coronary artery disease, characterized by increased prevalence of LMCA stenosis and multivessel disease. Although overall revascularisation rates were similar, CCS experienced significantly higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality following IHD-diagnosis compared with controls.

Title: Apixaban Versus Rivaroxaban After Spontaneous Intracranial Hemorrhage in Atrial Fibrillation: A Propensity Score-Matched TriNetX Study.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: BackgroundSurvivors of spontaneous intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) with atrial fibrillation (AF) face competing risks of thromboembolism and recurrent bleeding. Evidence directly comparing individual direct oral anticoagulants after resumption is limited.MethodsUsing the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with AF who restarted apixaban or rivaroxaban after spontaneous ICH. The index date was DOAC resumption, and cohorts were matched 1:1 using propensity scores. Recurrent spontaneous ICH was assessed at 30, 90, 180, and 365 days. One-year secondary outcomes were ischemic stroke, all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Cox models produced hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals, with log-rank testing.ResultsAt 1 year, recurrent spontaneous ICH occurred in 141 (34.9%) apixaban-treated and 135 (33.4%) rivaroxaban-treated patients (HR 1.076, 95% CI 0.850-1.363; P = 0.542). No significant differences were detected at 30, 90, or 180 days. One-year ischemic stroke (HR 1.109, 95% CI 0.863-1.424), all-cause mortality (HR 1.336, 95% CI 0.937-1.903), major bleeding (HR 1.074, 95% CI 0.861-1.339), and gastrointestinal bleeding (HR 1.480, 95% CI 0.844-2.597) also did not differ. A day 31-365 sensitivity analysis was consistent (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.77-1.36; P = 0.868).ConclusionsIn this propensity score-matched real-world cohort, no statistically significant differences were detected between apixaban and rivaroxaban for recurrent spontaneous ICH or major clinical outcomes after anticoagulation resumption. These findings concern the choice of agent among patients in whom resumption has already been decided; anticoagulation after spontaneous ICH remains an unproven strategy, and enrolment in randomized trials is preferred where available.

Title: Plasma magnesium levels and postoperative atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery: a cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is common after cardiac surgery, and hypomagnesemia has been proposed as a modifiable risk factor. In centers with active magnesium repletion protocols, however, overt hypomagnesemia has become uncommon. We aimed to determine whether postoperative plasma magnesium concentration is independently associated with POAF.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 435 adults undergoing cardiac surgery at a hospital specializing in cardiovascular disease. Postoperative plasma magnesium concentration, assessed at intensive care unit admission, as the mean value, and as the lowest value, was evaluated as the primary exposure in multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for relevant preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative covariates.
RESULTS: Isolated coronary artery bypass grafting was the most frequent procedure (46.6%). Overall mortality was 3.2%, and POAF incidence was 16.8%. Under active repletion, hypomagnesemia occurred in only 3.4% of patients. None of the three magnesium measures was independently associated with POAF. In contrast, age, type of surgical procedure, severe left ventricular dysfunction, and postoperative acute kidney injury were independently associated with POAF.
CONCLUSIONS: Under a protocol of active postoperative magnesium repletion, we did not detect an independent association between plasma magnesium concentration-within the observed normal-to-high range-and POAF. This complication was primarily related to age, type of surgery, and severe ventricular dysfunction, factors that should guide postoperative risk stratification; acute kidney injury showed a concurrent association with POAF and may act as a marker of shared postoperative risk factors rather than a causal factor.

Title: Clinical and psychosocial factors associated with clinician-driven allocation to hybrid versus in-person care in chronic disease management: a Colombian retrospective cohort.
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Hybrid care is increasingly used for chronic disease management, yet how patients are allocated to these modalities in routine practice remains poorly understood.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To characterize baseline factors associated with physician-driven allocation to hybrid versus in-person care and examine three-year clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort included adults with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and/or dyslipidemia enrolled in a programme in Alma Mater Hospital of Antioquia, Medellín, Colombia (2019-2025). Care modality was determined by treating physicians. Associations between baseline clinical, functional-behavioural, and psychosocial characteristics, care allocation, and follow-up outcomes were examined using logistic regression and interpreted as associational rather than causal.
RESULTS: Among 638 participants (319 hybrid; 319 in-person), higher baseline glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.68 per 1% increase; 95% CI 2.17-3.31) and inadequate medication adherence (aOR 1.96; 95% CI 1.17-3.28) were associated with hybrid care allocation, whereas higher educational attainment was inversely associated (middle vs low: aOR 0.43; 95% CI 0.25-0.72; high vs low: aOR 0.19; 95% CI 0.10-0.33). A strong gradient was observed in the secondary complexity analysis. Hybrid care was associated with higher three-year therapeutic goal attainment (OR 7.34; 95% CI 4.96-10.86) and lower chronic disease-related emergency department utilization (OR 0.53; 95% CI 0.36-0.79).
CONCLUSION: Hybrid care allocation was systematically associated with baseline clinical and contextual characteristics. Outcome differences should be interpreted cautiously given clinician-driven allocation and baseline differences.

Title: Clinical Impact of Multiple-Clip Implantation for Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual moderate or greater mitral regurgitation (MR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is strongly associated with adverse clinical outcomes. However, the prognostic impact of implanting additional clips in patients with significant residual MR after the first clip remains uncertain. We evaluated the clinical and echocardiographic outcomes of multiple-clip implantation for significant residual MR following placement of the initial clip.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 826 patients with moderate or greater residual MR on intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiography after placement of the first clip during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center from 2014 to 2023. Patients were categorized into single-clip (n=113) and multiple-clip (n=713) groups. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization at 1 year.
RESULTS: Procedural technical success and complication rates were comparable between groups. The multiple-clip group demonstrated greater MR reduction and higher transmitral pressure gradients at discharge, 30 days, and 1 year. At 1 year, the composite end point occurred less frequently in the multiple-clip group than in the single-clip group (16.8% versus 29.2%; P=0.002), along with greater and more sustained improvement in New York Heart Association functional class. In subgroup analyses, multiple-clip implantation consistently reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with moderate as well as moderate-severe/severe residual MR.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with significant residual MR after implanting the first clip, multiple-clip implantation improved MR reduction and 1-year outcomes without increasing complications. Even in moderate residual MR, additional clips were associated with more favorable clinical outcomes.

Title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate whether GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), compared with DPP4 (dipeptidyl peptidase-4) inhibitors or sulfonylureas, are associated with reduced all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalizations in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
METHODS: PRAISE-HFpEF (Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist in Obese Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction) was a nationwide multicenter cohort study using a new-user, active-comparator design within the national Veterans Affairs Health System (170 US hospitals). Adults with type 2 diabetes between January 1, 2000 and December 31, 2021, were identified from centralized electronic health records. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 were selected using a validated diagnostic algorithm. Exposure was initiation of a GLP-1RA versus DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea from January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2021. The primary outcome was time to all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on the propensity score was used to balanced baseline characteristics.
RESULTS: Among 179 288 patients with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, 1024 GLP-1RA users and 796 DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea users met inclusion criteria. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.64-0.95], P=0.01). Weight loss was modestly greater with GLP-1RAs compared with DPP4 inhibitors/sulfonylurea (-12.9% versus -10.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with obese heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA initiation was associated with a lower incidence of death or heart failure hospitalization compared with alternative oral agents.

Title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]).
CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.

Title: National Use Patterns and Comparative Effectiveness of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Myocardial Infarction-Related Cardiogenic Shock.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) provides bi-ventricular support for patients with myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (MI-CS); comparative effectiveness data relative to other mechanical circulatory support remain limited. We characterize contemporary ECMO utilization for MI-CS and compare short-term mortality across ECMO and non-ECMO treatment strategies.
METHODS: We compared baseline characteristics and temporal trends in mechanical circulatory support utilization among Medicare beneficiaries hospitalized with MI-CS from 2016 to 2023 and treated with ECMO, Impella, intra-aortic balloon pump, or medical management alone. Patient outcomes for each group were evaluated using inverse probability of treatment weighting, G-formula approach, and grace period analysis. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: The cohort included 102 718 patients: 1165 (1.1%) treated with ECMO, 10 064 (9.8%) Impella, 24 631 (24.0%) intra-aortic balloon pump, and 66 858 (65.1%) medical management alone. From 2016 to 2023, ECMO use for MI-CS increased from 0.8% to 1.8%. The percentage of hospitals using ECMO increased from 9.2% to 17.1%. Unadjusted 30-day mortality was higher for ECMO (69%) compared with Impella (60%), intra-aortic balloon pump (39%), and medical management (46%) (all P<0.0001). Adjusted inverse probability of treatment weighting and G-formula analyses revealed a 30-day mortality rate of 68%-70% for ECMO, which was higher than that for other therapies. The grace period analysis revealed similar mortality between patients treated with ECMO (54%) and Impella (54%).
CONCLUSIONS: ECMO use in a contemporary Medicare cohort of patients with MI-CS was infrequent (1.1%) and associated with high 30-day mortality. Despite use of complementary causal inference methods, we were unable to establish valid causal inferences on ECMO use and patient survival.

Title: Oral Potassium Supplementation Lowers Clinic Blood Pressure in Untreated Primary Hypertension-Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Potassium may lower blood pressure (BP), but its effect in untreated primary hypertension remains uncertain.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized parallel or crossover trials in adults with untreated primary hypertension comparing oral potassium supplementation with placebo, sodium chloride, or no treatment. The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews; CRD42024621287). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, and trial registries were searched through January 31, 2025 and updated October 1, 2025. End-of-treatment between-group mean differences were pooled using inverse-variance common-effect models; random-effects models were sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias, missing-evidence bias, and certainty were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, Risk of Bias Due to Missing Evidence, and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Nineteen trials (803 participants; 14 crossover, 5 parallel; median duration, 4 weeks) were included. Potassium reduced clinic systolic BP by 5.3 mm Hg (95% CI, 4.4-6.3) and diastolic BP by 4.5 mm Hg (95% CI, 3.9-5.1). Reductions in 24-hour ambulatory BP were smaller: 2.8 mm Hg (95% CI, 1.3-4.3) systolic and 3.2 mm Hg (95% CI, 2.2-4.2) diastolic. Adverse events were more frequent with potassium (12.8% versus 3.2%), whereas withdrawals and adverse-event withdrawals were uncommon. Heterogeneity was substantial, and ambulatory BP evidence was limited.
CONCLUSIONS: In untreated primary hypertension, oral potassium supplementation modestly reduces clinic BP and may produce smaller reductions in 24-hour ambulatory BP. Heterogeneity, short follow-up, and limited ambulatory and safety data warrant cautious interpretation.
REGISTRATION: URL: PROSPERO; Unique Identifier: CRD42024621287.

Title: Efficacy of Stellate Ganglion Block for Preventing Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) may reduce postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) by modulating the autonomic nervous system. This study evaluated the efficacy of preoperative SGB in preventing POAF following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: In this single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 140 patients undergoing valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned (1:1) to ultrasound-guided right SGB with 7 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine or 7 mL of normal saline. The primary outcome was the incidence of POAF from postoperative day 0 to day 7 or until discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 132 patients completed the study and were included in the modified intention-to-treat population (SGB group: n=65; saline group: n=67). POAF occurred in 43% of the SGB group and 40% of the saline group (odds ratio [OR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.46-2.15], adjusted P=0.989). The SGB group demonstrated a lower incidence of intraoperative ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia requiring defibrillation after aortic cross-clamp release (6% versus 19%; OR, 0.21 [95% CI, 0.06-0.80]; adjusted P=0.022), lower postoperative high-sensitivity troponin I levels (median difference: -2562 ng/L [95% CI, -4301 to -45]; P=0.045), and a reduced risk of postoperative acute kidney injury (5% versus 18%; OR, 0.24 [95% CI, 0.06-0.98]; adjusted P=0.046).
CONCLUSIONS: While preoperative SGB did not reduce the incidence of POAF, it was associated with potential benefits, including a lower requirement for intraoperative defibrillation attributable to ventricular arrhythmias, attenuated myocardial injury (as indicated by lower high-sensitivity troponin I levels), and a decreased risk of postoperative acute kidney injury.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn; URL Identifier: ChiCTR2300068572.

Title: Rationale and Design of a Parallel Randomized Trial of a DASH-Enhanced Portfolio Diet With or Without Ultra-Processed Plant Proteins for Blood Pressure and Other Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Adults With Hypertension and Obesity: The Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention on Cardiometabolic Health Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death and hospitalization globally. Clinical practice guidelines recommend various plant-based dietary patterns that target specific cardiometabolic risk factors, including the Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet for blood pressure and the Portfolio diet for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Combining key elements of these patterns may enhance cardiovascular disease risk reduction. However, many soy-based products, a key Portfolio component, are classified as ultra-processed foods (UPFs). This trial will answer 2 questions: (1) Does a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet result in clinically meaningful reductions in blood pressure compared with standard of care and (2) Is a high-UPF noninferior to a low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet for blood pressure reduction?
METHODS: The SWITCH (Substitution of High With Low Ultra-Processed Soy Protein Foods in a Guideline-Based Diet Intervention for Cardiometabolic Health) trial is a parallel, randomized, 3-arm, open-label, superiority-noninferiority trial. Three hundred adults with hypertension and obesity, including 50% with type 2 diabetes, will be randomized to a high-UPF or low-UPF soy protein-containing DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet or standard of care for 12 weeks. The primary outcome is systolic blood pressure. Key secondary outcomes are non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and body weight. Other outcomes include cardiometabolic risk factors.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings will provide high-quality evidence on the use of a DASH-enhanced Portfolio diet and the role of nutrient-dense soy foods classified as UPFs within the combination of the 2 guideline-based dietary patterns to support dietary strategies for cardiometabolic risk reduction.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique identifier: NCT06907862.

Title: Correlation of the Distressed Communities Index Score With Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Disease in the United States.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and death worldwide. Risk scores such as the pooled cohort equations often underpredict risk in individuals with low socioeconomic status.
METHODS: We used the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Population Level Analysis and Community Estimates data set to obtain zip code-level prevalence of hypertension, obesity, stroke, diabetes, and coronary artery disease. The Distressed Communities Index (DCI) collates community socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health metrics into a numerical score. Linear regression adjusted for region and rurality assessed associations between DCI and CVD prevalence.
RESULTS: We included 26 058 US zip codes (2016-2020). The median DCI was 50.9 (interquartile range, 25.4-75.9). Each 1-unit increase in DCI was associated with increased prevalence of obesity (β=0.10 [95% CI, 0.09-0.10]), hypertension (β=0.08 [95% CI, 0.08-0.09]), diabetes (β=0.06 [95% CI, 0.06-0.06]), coronary artery disease (β=0.03 [95% CI, 0.03-0.03]), and stroke (β=0.02 [95% CI, 0.02-0.02]; all P<0.001). Rurality and region were independently associated with CVD and risk factor prevalence, with rural and southern zip codes having the highest prevalence.
CONCLUSIONS: DCI, geographic region, and rurality are independently associated with greater prevalence of CVD and its risk factors in the United States. The DCI is a practical, scalable surrogate for socioeconomic status and social determinants/drivers of health that may enhance CVD risk stratification on the basis of an area's economic resilience or disadvantage. Using DCI with the Preventing Cardiovascular Events score may capture economic and social challenges it omits, warranting further study.

Title: Sudden Cardiac Death in Firefighters From the United States: A 16-Year Postmortem Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is the leading cause of duty-related death among firefighters. Understanding postmortem cardiovascular abnormalities associated with SCD is critical to guiding fire service cardiovascular disease screening and prevention programs.
METHODS: This study included US firefighters who had a duty-related death over a 16-year period (1999-2014) with available postmortem reports (autopsy/medical examiner reports). Cases were systematically reviewed to identify cases of SCD. For each SCD case, the primary etiology of SCD was adjudicated by experts in sports cardiology and cardiovascular pathology.
RESULTS: Postmortem evaluations were available for 794 of 2100 (37.8%) on-duty firefighter deaths over the study period (average age, 44±13 years; age range, 17-82 years; 4.0% women). A total of 312 of 794 (39.3%) firefighter deaths were adjudicated as SCD. A total of 255 of 312 (81.8%) SCD events were attributable to coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease or hypertensive heart disease, which both are associated with traditional cardiovascular risk factors. The leading etiology of SCD among young firefighters (aged <40 years) was also coronary artery disease/ischemic heart disease (24/50 [48.0%]). Of firefighters who had an exertional SCD event thought to be secondary to coronary artery disease (n=97), a total of 62 of 91 (68.1%) had severe fixed coronary stenosis, while 29 of 91 (31.9%) demonstrated acute plaque rupture/thrombosis.
CONCLUSIONS: More than 80% of on-duty SCD events among US firefighters are due to coronary artery disease and hypertensive heart disease that may be prevented by early disease identification and risk factor modification. Future studies should assess the efficacy of more rigorous firefighter cardiovascular disease screening and management practices.

Title: Association of APOA5 rs3135506 and CETP rs708272 Polymorphisms with Metabolic Syndrome in a Moroccan Population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a multifactorial condition and a major public health concern due to its strong association with cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes. Genetic factors contribute to its development. This study aims to evaluate the association between polymorphisms in genes APOA5 and CETP and susceptibility to MetS and its components in a Moroccan population.
METHODS: A case-control study was conducted, including 136 MetS patients and 138 controls recruited from the Doukkala region (Morocco). The APOA5 rs3135506 (C>G) and CETP rs708272 (G>A) polymorphisms were genotyped using PCR-RFLP.
RESULTS: The APOA5 rs3135506 polymorphism was significantly associated with increased MetS risk. The CG and GG genotypes conferred 2.39-fold (OR = 2.39; p = 0.0008) and 7.17-fold (OR = 7.17; p = 0.0007) higher risks, respectively, with significant associations also observed under dominant (OR = 2.76; p < 0.0001), recessive (OR = 4.79; p = 0.006), and allelic (OR = 2.36; p < 0.0001) models. The GG genotype was also associated with general and abdominal obesity, hypertension, and hyperglycemia, whereas the CG genotype was associated with dyslipidemia. For CETP rs708272, the AA genotype was associated with increased MetS risk (OR = 3.31; p = 0.0078), with significant associations under dominant (OR = 1.81; p = 0.0160), recessive (OR = 2.80; p = 0.0185), and allelic (OR = 1.81; p = 0.0023) models. However, these associations were no longer significant after adjustment for age and sex. Combined genotype analysis revealed increased MetS risk for the CG-GG, CG-GA, and GG-AA combinations (OR = 4.64, 2.98, and 7.35, respectively).
CONCLUSION: The APOA5 rs3135506 and CETP rs708272 polymorphisms may contribute to MetS susceptibility in the Moroccan population, with certain combined genotypes associated with increased risk. These findings support their potential as genetic biomarkers for early risk assessment but require confirmation in larger studies.

Title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Determinants of Bowel Ischemia and Associated Risk After Elective Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Bowel ischemia (BI) is an uncommon but devastating complication of elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify patient- and procedure-related risk factors for BI after elective EVAR.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Cochrane Library, Scielo, and Lilacs from database inception through March 31, 2024, without language or date restrictions. We included observational studies of adults who underwent elective EVAR and reported postoperative BI and extractable risk-factor data. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, extracted data, and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For factors reported in multiple sufficiently homogeneous studies, random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs), with heterogeneity assessed using I2.
RESULTS: Twenty-three retrospective cohort studies, including 306 344 elective EVAR procedures, met the inclusion criteria, and 10 provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. Across all studies, 1535 patients developed postoperative BI, corresponding to an overall incidence of approximately 0.5%. Female sex was associated with increased BI risk (RR, 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.06-3.43; I2 = 0%). Larger aneurysm diameter was also associated with increased risk (MD, 4.05 mm; 95% CI, 0.09-8.02; I2 = 0%). Renal dysfunction was a consistent predictor, with chronic kidney disease (RR, 2.93; 95% CI, 1.01-8.47; I2 = 29%) and dialysis dependence (RR, 5.35; 95% CI, 2.38-12.05; I2 = 0%) associated with BI. Major intraoperative blood loss >1 L conferred the highest relative risk among pooled factors (RR, 7.45; 95% CI, 2.80-19.85; I2 = 0%). Age, systemic arterial hypertension, and active smoking were not significantly associated with BI in pooled analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Bowel ischemia after elective EVAR is uncommon but clinically important because delayed recognition carries substantial morbidity and mortality. Female sex, larger aneurysm diameter, chronic kidney disease, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss identify patients who may warrant heightened perioperative vigilance. The certainty of evidence remains very low, and future studies should standardize reporting of bowel segment, mesenteric vessel involvement, inferior mesenteric artery and internal iliac artery status, endograft configuration, and overlapping registry populations.Clinical RelevanceBowel ischemia after elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare, but its low incidence should not be interpreted as low clinical importance because delayed diagnosis is often catastrophic. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes the largest available elective EVAR evidence focused on bowel ischemia and identifies reproducible risk signals, including female sex, aneurysm size, renal dysfunction, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss. The practical gain for readers is not a definitive prediction score, but a clearer framework for perioperative judgment: recognize vulnerable patients, avoid overinterpreting weak or non-poolable associations, and apply heightened postoperative vigilance when embolic, hypoperfusion, pelvic collateral, or renal-risk features coexist.

Title: 15O-water PET-detected myocardial ischaemia and CT-derived FFR: Predicting the functional significance of anatomical stenosis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical assessment of coronary stenoses, its ability to determine their functional significance is limited. Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) has emerged as a non-invasive method for lesion-specific ischaemia assessment. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR using 15O-water positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging as the reference standard.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively reviewed 193 patients who underwent hybrid CCTA and 15O-water PET at Kuopio University Hospital between 2017 and 2022. Patients with low-to-moderate pretest probability of CAD in whom CAD could not be ruled out by CCTA were eligible. After exclusions, 165 patients were included. CT-FFR values were calculated using a research prototype algorithm and compared with PET-derived perfusion abnormalities. In the overall cohort, CT-FFR showed moderate diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.672-0.740. In a subgroup of 83 patients with high-quality CCTA and stenosis >50%, diagnostic performance improved substantially (AUC 0.836). Using a CT-FFR threshold of 0.80, sensitivity and specificity were 85% and 87%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: In an unselected clinical population referred for PET perfusion imaging after CCTA, CT-FFR did not significantly improve diagnostic performance compared with CCTA alone. However, in patients with high-quality CCTA and obstructive coronary stenoses, CT-FFR demonstrated good accuracy for identifying functionally significant disease, supporting its role as a complementary non-invasive diagnostic tool.

Title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown.
METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR.
RESULTS: 3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804).
CONCLUSIONS: In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

Title: S100 proteins in kidney disease: Inflammatory biomarkers, pathogenic mechanisms and therapeutic prospects (Review).
Abstract: The S100 protein family, particularly the calprotectin heterodimer S100A8/A9, is increasingly recognized as both an inflammatory readout and a context‑dependent mediator of kidney injury. Selected extracellular S100 proteins function as damage‑associated molecular patterns released during cellular stress, leukocyte activation and tissue injury. They can amplify sterile inflammation through the receptor for advanced glycation end‑products (RAGE), Toll‑like receptor 4 (TLR4) and related downstream pathways, although receptor usage and biological effects vary by cell type and disease setting. The present review examines S100 proteins in kidney disease across three related domains: Clinical biomarkers, disease mechanisms and therapeutic translation. Current evidence most strongly supports urinary S100A8/A9 for distinguishing intrinsic from pre‑renal acute kidney injury; circulating S100A8/A9 and S100A12 have mainly been studied as markers of inflammatory and cardiovascular risk in chronic kidney disease. S100‑associated signaling has been implicated in leukocyte recruitment, mesangial and macrophage activation, podocyte injury, tubular stress, tubulointerstitial fibrosis and uremia‑associated vascular calcification. Emerging studies also describe stress‑regulated and intracellular S100 functions, including gasdermin E (GSDME)‑regulated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling that controls S100A7A, S100‑annexin complexes and S100A16‑driven Wnt/β‑catenin or endoplasmic reticulum stress. However, therapeutic evidence remains largely preclinical, and clinical translation is constrained by ligand redundancy, disease heterogeneity and incomplete prospective validation. S100 proteins may therefore contribute to biomarker panels and targeted interventions, but their clinical utility requires prospective validation and clear separation of receptor‑mediated from intracellular effects.

Title: Associations of Coexisting Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Sarcopenia-Related Abnormalities With Adverse Clinical Outcomes Across Obesity States.
Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with adverse liver and non-liver outcomes, but the impact of coexisting sarcopenia-related abnormalities (e.g., low muscle strength [MS], muscle mass, and physical performance) remains unclear. In a prospective UK Biobank cohort (n = 438,748), we evaluated their joint associations with incidence and risks of all-cause mortality, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), non-liver cancers, and obesity-related cancers across MASLD and sarcopenia-related abnormality status. Over a median follow-up of 13.8 years, 401 HCC, 1714 cirrhosis, 39,534 CVD, 19,637 CKD, 38,240 non-liver cancers, 12,536 obesity-related cancers, and 34,801 deaths occurred. A stepwise increase in both incidence and adjusted risk of liver and non-liver outcomes was observed across MASLD and sarcopenia strata. Within the coexistence group, the obesity (vs. non-obesity) subgroup generally had higher risks. For example, for cirrhosis, adjusted hazard ratios increased from 3.93 to 7.36 then 8.48 with MASLD alone, coexisting MASLD with low MS overall and coexisting MASLD, low MS and obesity, respectively. Similar findings were observed in external validation analyses using the 2011-2018 US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort. Together, these observations inform risk stratification strategy and management of MASLD to include sarcopenia assessment.

Title: Pre-emptive Circulatory Support Before Emergency Tracheal Intubation: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Emergency tracheal intubation is associated with peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse, and pre-emptive circulatory support is frequently used to mitigate this risk despite uncertain evidence. We conducted a systematic review of randomised and comparative non-randomised studies evaluating pre-emptive circulatory support initiated before or at induction in adults undergoing emergency or urgent tracheal intubation. Eligible interventions included prophylactic vasopressors, intravenous fluid boluses, hypertonic saline, blood products, deliberate circulation-first strategies, and multi-component care bundles. The primary outcome was peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse within 30 minutes of induction, defined according to individual study criteria. MEDLINE via PubMed, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 30 August 2026, with additional searches of ClinicalTrials.gov and citation lists. Risk of bias (RoB) was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool for randomised trials and the Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool for non-randomised studies. Fourteen independent cohorts comprising two randomised trials and 12 comparative non-randomised studies, with more than 7,400 participants overall, were included. Two randomised trials evaluated a pre-emptive 500 mL crystalloid bolus and found no reduction in peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse. Observational evidence for prophylactic vasopressors was inconsistent, with substantial changes between crude and adjusted estimates and substantial concerns regarding confounding. Studies evaluating circulation-first strategies or pre-intubation blood products generally reported associations favouring earlier circulatory resuscitation, but these findings were strongly influenced by confounding and treatment selection. Multi-component care bundles were also associated with fewer peri-intubation complications, but the independent contribution of their circulatory components could not be determined. Overall, the available evidence indicates that pre-emptive crystalloid administration does not reduce peri-intubation cardiovascular collapse, while evidence for prophylactic vasopressors, circulation-first strategies, and multi-component interventions remains insufficient to support routine use. Further randomised trials are needed, particularly among physiologically high-risk adults.

Title: Clustering of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Midlife Forms Trajectories That Affect Heart Aging Biomarker and Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To (1) identify multivariable longitudinal midlife patterns of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body mass index, and non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol and (2) assess whether electrocardiogram derived heart age acceleration (δ-age) mediates their associations with incident myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and all-cause mortality.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed 5244 participants from the observational cohort study, the Tromsø Study, who were free of MI or stroke at baseline (Tromsø7, 2015-2016) and attended at least 3 surveys (Tromsø3-7, 1986-2016). Age-standardized risk factor z-scores were modeled with quadratic B-splines and grouped using K-means clustering to identify joint multivariable life-course risk profiles. δ-Age was derived from 12-lead electrocardiograms using a validated neural network. Natural-effects models decomposed hazard ratios between clusters and clinical events (follow-up to 2021) into direct and δ-age mediated components.
RESULTS: Four distinct clusters were identified: stable low-risk (cluster 1, n=1604, 30.6%), dyslipidemia (cluster 2, n=1340, 25.6%), hypertension (cluster 3, n=1476, 28.1%), and high-risk trajectory (cluster 4, n=824, 15.7%). Each 1-SD increment in δ-age was associated with 27% to 30% of excess MI, stroke, and death, independent of age and sex. Clusters 3 and 4 carried the greatest excess risk of clinical events, whereas mediation by δ-age was modest (4%-8% of total effect for MI and stroke) and not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Joint multivariable life-course clustering of conventional risk factors identified clinically distinct long-term cardiovascular risk phenotypes. Although δ-age adds independent prognostic information, it explained little of the excess risk associated with chronic hypertension, dyslipidemia, or obesity, indicating it functions primarily as a parallel marker and not a causal mediator.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors in World Health Organization Group 1 Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A REVEAL Lite 2-Matched Cohort With Time-Varying Exposure Analysis.
Journal: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes across several cardiometabolic conditions, but their role in World Health Organization group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of adults with group 1 PAH. Patients prescribed SGLT2i were compared with patients without exposure. Propensity-score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events. Associations were evaluated using fixed-exposure and start-stop time-varying Cox models. The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 (33%) receiving SGLT2i and 244 (67%) controls. Most patients were classified as high risk by REVEAL Lite 2 (106 SGLT2i recipients (87%) and 215 controls (88%), respectively). In the fixed-exposure analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=.018), without a significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=.14). In the time-varying analysis, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=.57). The apparent survival association was attenuated after accounting for treatment timing, demonstrating the sensitivity of observational PAH estimates to exposure classification and supporting prospective randomized trials.

Title: AI-enabled OPM-magnetocardiography for pre-angiography infarct-related artery probability estimation in NSTEMI: a two-campus prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Identifying the infarct-related artery (IRA) before coronary angiography in non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) is difficult because current approaches have limited sensitivity. We evaluated whether a non-invasive 90-s optically pumped magnetometer magnetocardiography (OPM-MCG) recording can estimate pre-angiography IRA probabilities in these patients and provide information beyond standard-care variables.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This prospective two-campus study within one hospital system included a Campus 1 development cohort (n = 493) and a geographically separate Campus 2 test cohort (n = 118). All patients underwent OPM-MCG before angiography. An XGBoost model using 65 prespecified OPM-MCG features was developed with nested cross-validation, locked, and evaluated once in Campus 2. IRA adjudication followed a core-laboratory hierarchy. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were compared with ECG and TTE. Among 611 patients, 43% had LAD, 23% LCx, and 34% RCA IRA. In Campus 2, overall accuracy was 63.6%, macro-F1 was 60.0%; LAD/LCx/RCA vessel-specific areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.87/0.79/0.79 and top-1 sensitivity was 76.6%/34.5%/69.0%. Accuracy was 51.7% for matched ECG-only XGBoost and 55.9% for integrated standard care. In an exploratory stacked analysis, adding locked OPM-MCG probabilities to standard care increased accuracy to 67.8% (paired difference 11.9%, 95% CI 4.2-19.5; P = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: In haemodynamically stable patients with NSTEMI already selected for invasive management, a locked OPM-MCG model provided informative vessel-level probabilities in Campus 2 and complementary signal with standard care. Performance was strongest for LAD and RCA. Prospective multicentre, cross-platform testing is needed before clinical use.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2300070211.

Title: Uric acid-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio and incident carotid atherosclerosis: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The uric acid-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio (UHR) has been proposed as a composite cardiometabolic biomarker, but prospective evidence linking UHR to incident carotid atherosclerosis remains limited.
METHODS: In a retrospective cohort of 16,572 adults from a tertiary health examination center in Zhejiang, China, we examined the association between baseline UHR and incident carotid artery lesions using Cox proportional hazards regression. Incremental predictive performance was evaluated using C-statistic, integrated discrimination improvement, continuous net reclassification improvement, median improvement in individual predicted event probabilities, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Over a mean follow-up of 2.7 years, 4,454 incident events occurred. Each 1-SD increment in baseline UHR was independently associated with a 6% higher hazard of incident carotid artery lesions (HR 1.06, 95% CI 1.01-1.11; p = 0.015). In exploratory sex-stratified analyses, the association was statistically significant in males (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.02-1.12; p = 0.010) but not in females (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.93-1.04; p = 0.524), though the formal interaction test was not significant (p = 0.261). UHR did not improve discrimination (ΔC = 0.0003) or net clinical benefit despite significant changes in individual predicted event probabilities in males (p = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: Higher baseline UHR was independently associated with short-term carotid atherosclerotic progression. Exploratory analyses suggested a possible sex difference, but this requires confirmation in adequately powered studies. While UHR provides independent prognostic information, it does not meaningfully improve risk stratification beyond traditional cardiovascular risk factors in health examination populations.

Title: Comment on "Nationwide trends and disparities in deaths from second- or third-degree atrioventricular block (1999-2022): A 24-year retrospective analysis of CDC WONDER data".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Factors Associated With Uncontrolled Blood Pressure and Its Association With Cardiovascular and All-Cause Mortality Among Adults Receiving Antihypertensive Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using NHANES 2013-2018 Linked Mortality Data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncontrolled blood pressure remains common among adults in the United States receiving antihypertensive therapy. However, contemporary nationally representative evidence examining associated factors and subsequent mortality within the same treated population remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with uncontrolled blood pressure and examine its association with all-cause and heart disease mortality.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2013-2018 data linked to mortality through 2019. Adults receiving antihypertensive therapy with complete data were included. Uncontrolled blood pressure was defined as mean systolic pressure of at least 130 mmHg or diastolic pressure of at least 80 mmHg. Survey-weighted logistic and Cox regression were performed.
RESULTS: The sample included 3,311 adults, representing an estimated 42,895,551 US adults after application of the NHANES examination weights. Uncontrolled blood pressure affected 56.9%. Higher odds were found among other Hispanic adults (adjusted odds ratio (AOR) 1.50, 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.08-2.07), non-Hispanic Black adults (AOR 1.63, 95% CI, 1.29-2.05), and non-Hispanic Asian adults (AOR 1.68, 95% CI, 1.15-2.45). Uncontrolled blood pressure was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.24, 95% CI, 0.87-1.78) or heart disease mortality (adjusted HR 0.97, 95% CI, 0.51-1.84).
CONCLUSION: Uncontrolled blood pressure remained common and differed across population groups. Future studies should use repeated measurements, objective treatment data, and longer follow-up.

Title: Histopathological Analysis of the Spectrum of Forensic Pathology Lesions Over Two Years From a Tertiary Care Centre in Kerala: A Descriptive Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Medicolegal autopsies provide key insights into the causes of death and disease evolution. This study analyzes the spectrum and frequency of histopathological alterations across major organ systems in medicolegal autopsies over two years at Government Medical College, Thrissur, a tertiary care center in South India.
METHODS: This descriptive retrospective study included details of 831 autopsy cases. Histopathological findings from cardiovascular, respiratory, hepatobiliary, renal, central nervous, and accessory visceral systems were systematically categorized.
RESULTS: Male predominance was observed (594 cases, 71.5%). The 50-59 (21.1%) and 40-49 (19.3%) age groups were most represented. Evaluated left anterior descending (LAD) arteries (N = 388) frequently showed advanced atherosclerosis (AHA type V: 38.9%, 151 cases). In evaluated hearts (N = 628), hypertrophy was present in 19.1% (120 cases) and healed infarcts in 9.6% (60 cases). Evaluated lungs (N = 676) mostly showed congestion with edema (20.1%, 136 cases), isolated congestion (18.8%, 127 cases), and isolated edema (12.9%, 87 cases). Evaluated livers (N = 476) showed congestion (37.4%, 178 cases) and macrovesicular steatosis (21%, 100 cases). Evaluated kidneys (N = 445) demonstrated congestion (40.2%, 179 cases) and chronic kidney disease (18%, 80 cases).
CONCLUSION: Histopathological evaluation revealed a significant subclinical burden of chronic cardiovascular, respiratory, and metabolic conditions. Targeted histopathological examination in forensic autopsies enhances diagnostic precision and informs public health statistics.

Title: Comparing two distinct costing models for health economics of heart failure within a Swedish population-based cohort.
Abstract:
AIMS: To compare two healthcare costing models, Cost Per Patient and Patient Encounter Costing, in patients with heart failure, quantify differences in estimated healthcare costs, and identify factors associated with discrepancies between the models.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A retrospective register study was conducted in Region Halland, southwest Sweden, including 3230 patients aged 40-90 years with heart failure diagnosed at least twice between 2013 and 2018 and alive during 2019. Healthcare utilization costs during 2019 were estimated using the Cost Per Patient and Patient Encounter Costing models. Linear regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with costs and differences between the models. The Cost Per Patient model estimated a mean annual cost of €10 341 compared with €9538 for the Patient Encounter Costing model. Hospital care accounted for 73% of total costs in both models. Although overall cost estimates were similar, differences in outpatient and primary care costs reached 22%. Higher costs in both models were associated with diabetes, elevated N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide levels, and impaired kidney function. Differences between the models were primarily explained by primary care visits, inpatient care days, and N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide levels. Sensitivity analyses using log-transformed costs yielded similar results.
CONCLUSION: Both Cost Per Patient and Patient Encounter Costing methodologies were useful for estimating healthcare costs in heart failure. The models provide different perspectives on healthcare costs because they use different cost-allocation principles. These differences should be considered when selecting a costing methodology for healthcare evaluations.

Title: Comparing perioperative complications and recovery outcomes of neuraxial versus general anesthesia in hip fracture surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: To compare perioperative complications and recovery outcomes between neuraxial and general anesthesia in adult patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched from 2000 to April 25, 2026. Studies comparing neuraxial and general anesthesia were included. Outcomes included mortality (in-hospital, 30-day, 90-day, 1-year), intraoperative hypotension, postoperative delirium, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), pneumonia, acute kidney injury (AKI), length of hospital stay, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV). Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled effect estimates. Nineteen RCTs (n = 4,742) were included. No significant differences were observed between neuraxial and general anesthesia for mortality at any time point, postoperative delirium, ACS, pneumonia, or PONV. Neuraxial anesthesia was associated with a lower risk of intraoperative hypotension (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.40-0.77) and AKI (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.84), and shorter length of hospital stay (MD - 0.58 days, 95% CI - 1.08 to - 0.07). Heterogeneity was substantial for some outcomes. Neuraxial anesthesia decreases the risk of intraoperative hypertension and acute kidney injury in comparison to general anesthesia in patients undergoing hip fracture repair.

Title: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease/Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and the Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cohort Studies.
Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), has been inconsistently linked to incident atrial fibrillation (AF) across observational cohorts. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies, following the Meta-analysis Of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) guidelines, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through July 25, 2026, for studies comparing incident AF risk in adults with versus without NAFLD/MASLD. Adjusted effect estimates were pooled using a random-effects model, with heterogeneity assessed via the I² statistic and explored through subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses. Eighteen cohort studies comprising over 15 million participants from Asia, Europe, and North America met inclusion criteria. Pooling all studies demonstrated a significantly increased risk of incident AF among individuals with NAFLD/MASLD compared with those without (pooled risk ratio (RR) 1.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-1.34, p < 0.001), with substantial statistical heterogeneity (I² = 99.4%). In an exploratory analysis of three studies, advanced disease with hepatic fibrosis was also associated with increased AF risk (RR 1.19, 95% CI 1.11-1.28). In the present meta-analysis, NAFLD/MASLD was associated with a modestly higher risk of incident AF after adjustment for conventional cardiometabolic risk factors, although heterogeneity was very high. These findings support attention to AF risk in this population and the use of standardized diagnostic approaches in future research.

Title: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes for non-prescription drug-associated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-prescription drug toxicity contributes to a substantial proportion of out-of-hospital cardiac arrests (OHCAs). Among OHCAs overall, previous reports have shown lower survival among females, compared to males. We examined sex-based differences in outcomes among non-prescription drug-associated OHCA (DA-OHCA).
METHODS: In this population-based observational cohort study using data from the BC Cardiac Arrest Registry (2019-24), we included emergency medical services (EMS)-treated OHCAs that had evidence of recent non-prescription drug use. The primary outcome was favorable neurological outcome, and secondary outcomes included survival at hospital discharge, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), and ROSC at emergency department (ED) arrival. We assessed the association between female sex (vs male) and outcomes using multivariable logistic regression models, adjusted for Utstein variables.
RESULTS: Among 47,051 EMS-Assessed OHCA, there were 4926 adult EMS-assessed DA-OHCA. We included 3133 adult EMS-treated DA-OHCAs, of whom 864 (28%) were female and 2269 (72%) were male, with a median age of 38 (interquartile range [IQR] 30-49) and 40 (IQR 32-52) years, respectively. Favorable neurological outcomes occurred in 108 (13%) females and 212 (9.6%) males. Female sex was not associated with favorable neurological outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.32, 95% CI 0.97, 1.79), prehospital ROSC (aOR 1.00, 95% CI 0.83, 1.19), or ROSC at ED arrival (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.84, 1.22), but was associated with an increased odds survival to hospital discharge (aOR 1.34; 95% CI 1.01, 1.77).
CONCLUSIONS: Among DA-OHCA, female sex was not independently associated with favorable neurological outcomes, but was associated with a higher odds of survival to hospital discharge.

Title: Progression rates of aortic stenosis in patients with calcific and rheumatic heart disease in Saudi Arabia.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is the most prevalent type of AS in developed countries. However, in developing countries, rheumatic heart disease (RHD), which has a low progression rate, remains the prevalent type. This study compared the progression rates of AS between the National Guard cohort and Western populations.
DESIGN: This was a retrospective single-center cohort study.
PARTICIPANTS: Involving patients who underwent two echocardiographic examinations within an interval of at least 2 years.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Progression of aortic valve stenosis was assessed by measuring changes in the aortic valve area (AVA), peak aortic velocity, and mean aortic valve gradient.
RESULTS: In total, 1669 patients (median follow-up: 6.9 years) were included in the analysis. The overall annual AVA progression rate was 0.074 ± 0.1 cm2/year (median: -0.061 cm2/year). Patients with RHD had lower progression rates than those without RHD (25%-35%; AVA: -0.036 [-0.042, -0.030] cm2/year). Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) who exhibited calcific AS had the highest progression rate (AVA: -0.102 ± 0.096 cm2/year). The overall progression rate of AS for the National Guard cohort was lower across all groups compared with that in Western populations (AVA: -0.08 to 0.12 cm2/year).
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ESRD who had calcific AS had the highest progression rate. Meanwhile, patients with RHD exhibited the lowest progression rate. The high prevalence of calcific AS in our study shows the importance of adherence to the American College of Cardiology/European Society of Cardiology guidelines for disease management.

Title: Feature-token clinical transformer for 24-h landmark mortality risk stratification in critically ill patients with heart failure: development and multicenter external validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The first 24 h after ICU admission in critically ill patients with heart failure yield heterogeneous EHR evidence across vital signs, laboratory tests, treatments, organ support, and nurse-charted monitoring. Conventional scores and flat-vector ML models may not preserve individual variable identity or context.
METHODS: We developed FTCT, encoding each predictor recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission as a clinically tagged token (value, missingness, identity, group).
