MIMIC-IV (2008-2019) served for development, validation, and internal testing; eICU-CRD (2014-2015) served for external validation. Included were adults with heart failure, a complete 24-h ICU observation window, and known discharge status. The endpoint was in-hospital all-cause death.
RESULTS: MIMIC-IV included 11,156 stays and 1,484 deaths, partitioned into training (n = 7,809), validation (n = 1,673), and internal test (n = 1,674) sets. eICU-CRD included 9,837 stays and 1,319 deaths. FTCT achieved an AUROC of 0.849 (95% CI, 0.835-0.863) internally and 0.804 (0.788-0.820) externally. Patient-paired AUROC differences vs. XGBoost were 0.027 (0.011-0.043) internally and 0.032 (0.014-0.050) externally. A matched FT-Transformer-style baseline achieved an external AUROC of 0.781 (0.760-0.801). In eICU-CRD, FTCT achieved an AUPRC of 0.296 (0.278-0.314), Brier score of 0.091 (0.085-0.097), and expected calibration error of 0.036 (0.030-0.042). In a post hoc cohort-specific descriptive operating analysis targeting approximately 85% specificity, external sensitivity was 0.662 (0.636-0.687), positive predictive value 0.406 (0.385-0.427), negative predictive value 0.942 (0.937-0.947), and F1 score 0.503. Removing feature-token encoding produced the largest ablation loss in external AUROC (-0.031).
CONCLUSIONS: FTCT combines established feature-token Transformer modeling with clinical-group embeddings, explicit missingness representation, and group-aware pooling for 24-h landmark mortality risk stratification from structured EHR data recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Its external validation and ablation results support prospective investigation, but do not yet demonstrate clinical utility, workflow integration, admission-time applicability, or autonomous use.

Title: Baseline Characteristics and Physical Activity Patterns of Participants Enrolled in the Team Lifestyle Immersion Program (TLIP) study.
Journal: International journal of sciences, basic and applied research
Abstract: Hypertension remains a global cause of chronic illnesses, morbidity, and mortality. According to the CDC data (2024), about 120 million Americans have hypertension, and about a billion people globally, when defined by a systolic blood pressure greater than 140 mm Hg and at least a diastolic pressure of 80 mm Hg. Even more provocative are the suggestions that most people may develop hypertension if they live long enough. The unsatisfactory rates of hypertension control with only drug therapies emphasize the potential benefits of including lifestyle modifications for better control. Lifestyle intervention has been proposed to complement drug management of hypertension for decades. Regarding physical activity behavior, motivational messages could be tailored to focus on instrumental exercise goals for younger adults and meaningful relationships for older adults. This study aims to evaluate the baseline characteristics and physical activity patterns of participants enrolled in the team lifestyle immersion program (TLIP) study. To address these questions, this study leverages an existing TLIP P-50 project (5P50MD01347-04) at Meharry Medical College in Nashville, TN. The funding authority is NIH. Project number: 5P50MD01347-04. This study examines the baseline characteristics and physical activity patterns of participants enrolled in the team Lifestyle immersion program (TLIP) and followed at 6 and 12 months. To evaluate and analyze differences at baseline and in the prospective rate of change of physical activity patterns and progression of hypertension, and follow-up at 6 and 12 months. This study highlights distinct sex- and age-specific patterns in exercise behaviors among individuals enrolled in a hypertension research protocol. Despite high physical access to fitness resources (66.7% overall living close to a gym), physical activity engagement varied markedly by demographic subgroup. Interventions aiming to improve cardiovascular risk profiles in hypertensive populations should focus on targeted strategies for middle-aged women, prioritizing habit formation to reduce total inactivity rather than exclusively emphasizing high exercise intensity.

Title: Electrophysiology Team-Administered Conscious Sedation for Pulsed-Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation in Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) is emerging as a novel nonthermal alternative. However, PFA is commonly performed under general anesthesia or deep sedation requiring anesthesiologists, which increases resource utilization and limits its widespread application. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of conscious sedation for PFA administered by the electrophysiology (EP) team, using radiofrequency ablation (RFA) as a comparator.
METHODS: A total of 120 patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory atrial fibrillation were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the PFA group or the RFA group. We evaluated three key outcomes: (1) intraoperative patient tolerance, assessed using validated scales (Faces Pain Scale-Revised [FPS-R], Likert Scale Questionnaire [LSQ]) combined with intraoperative body movement and cough reactions; (2) procedural efficiency; and (3) procedural safety.
RESULTS: The incidence of pain during pulmonary vein isolation was comparable between the two groups (all p > 0.05), whereas FPS-R scores were significantly lower in the PFA group (p < 0.05). No significant difference was observed in movement scores between the two groups (p = 0.452). According to the LSQ analysis, only 1 patient (1.7%) in the RFA group reported dissatisfaction with intraoperative pain management. Cough incidence during PVI was higher with PFA (21.7% [13/60] vs 6.7% [4/60]; p = 0.018). Both total procedure time and left atrial dwell time were shorter in the PFA group. Furthermore, no serious complications were directly related to conscious sedation.
CONCLUSION: In selected low-risk patients, EP team-administered conscious sedation is feasible for PFA, with acceptable intraoperative tolerance and safety while preserving procedural efficiency.

Title: Rationale and design of RECOVER - a prospective, longitudinal cardiac rehabilitation registry.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) has been performed in a structured manner since the 1970s, supported by a substantial body of evidence demonstrating its benefits across the heterogeneous pool of cardiac patients. Although therapeutic interventions, pharmacological options, and patient-centered recommendations keep emerging, the majority of CR programs have not changed accordingly. Hence, they are becoming less capable of accounting for an increasingly diverse patient cohort. With a prospective long-term cohort, we aim to achieve an in-depth characterization of CR patients, enabling the delivery of more personalized care in the contemporary era.
METHODS: In this non-interventional, monocentric, prospective cohort study named RECOVER (Cardiac REhabilitation COhort at the Medicine Campus DaVos to invEstigate Recovery), we plan to include 10,000 patients over 10 years across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular conditions (e.g., cardiac surgery, myocardial infarction, heart failure) with data collected across the full spectrum of inpatient CR. Data acquisition is complemented through extensive biobanking allowing detailed phenotyping and biomarker profiling of patients. Follow-up assessments are conducted at 3 and 6 months, and yearly thereafter, up to 10 years. By harnessing novel devices, digital monitoring is employed to continuously capture a wealth of health-related parameters, such as blood pressure and accelerometry-based physical activity.
ADDITION TO THE FIELD AND LIMITATIONS: Given the substantial research gap in personalized CR, the RECOVER study provides the opportunity to systematically evaluate recovery patterns and treatment response across distinct cardiovascular subgroups. Due to the unique and highly innovative infrastructure available at the recruiting site, the monocentric design enables performance of an extensive standardized assessment. By incorporating digital technologies in conjunction with deep phenotypic and biomarker data, RECOVER holds promise to enable tailored CR strategies.

Title: The effect of vitamin C supplementation additive to the priming solution on postoperative bleeding in coronary artery bypass grafting: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing cardiac surgery often experience bleeding during and after the procedure. Antioxidants such as Vitamin C (VC) are used to manage postoperative bleeding and inflammation after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A total of 110 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) were enrolled. Patients were randomly assigned into two groups of 55 participants each. In the intervention group, 25 mg/kg of VC was added to the CPB priming solution. In the control group, 25 mg/kg of normal saline was added instead. Nurse recorded the amount of chest tube drainage on intensive care unit (ICU) entry, and 2, 4, 6, 12, and 24 hours. They also documented the amount of blood product transfusion required during surgery and in the ICU.
RESULTS: The amount of chest tube drainage in the control group was higher than the intervention group, but this difference was not statistically significant between the two groups (P > 0.05). The amount transfused blood in the operating room and in the ICU in the intervention group was 1.64±0.79 and 2.14±1.17 ml, respectively, and in the control group it was 1.69±0.84 and 2.52±1.68 ml, which was not statistically significant between the two groups (P > 0.05). There was no significant difference in duration of ICU and hospital stay between the two groups (P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Adding VC to the CPB prime showed a non-significant trend toward reduced postoperative bleeding after CABG. Current evidence from this study is insufficient to recommend routine use; further larger trials are needed.

Title: Comment on "Differential effects of pre-procedural atorvastatin versus rosuvastatin on hematologic and inflammatory markers in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: A randomized controlled trial".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Intravascular imaging-guided versus angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention: a reconstructed individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of intravascular ultrasound- and optical coherence tomography-guided strategies.
Abstract:
AIMS: Uncertainty persists regarding the comparative efficacy of intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) and optical coherence tomography (OCT) vs. angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We synthesized randomized evidence using reconstructed individual participant data (IPD) and compared the two modalities indirectly.
METHODS AND RESULTS: MEDLINE and CENTRAL were searched up to 31 March 2026. IPD were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Primary analyses used one-stage stratified Cox models; secondary analyses included random-effects and Bayesian hierarchical models. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Twenty-three randomized controlled trials enrolling 21 176 patients were included (16 IVUS, N = 15 209; 7 OCT, N = 5967). IVUS-guided PCI reduced MACE [hazard ratio (HR) 0.74; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-0.83; P < 0.001], target-vessel revascularization (TVR; HR 0.70; 0.60-0.82), and stent thrombosis (ST; HR 0.54; 0.37-0.78). OCT-guided PCI reduced MACE (HR 0.75; 0.63-0.91; P = 0.003), cardiac death (HR 0.48; 0.27-0.83), myocardial infarction (HR 0.79; 0.63-0.99), ST (HR 0.40; 0.22-0.74), and TVR (HR 0.74; 0.57-0.97). Bayesian posterior probabilities of benefit exceeded 82% for all IVUS and 94% for all OCT endpoints. Indirect comparison detected no significant between-modality difference. Meta-regression of IVUS trials revealed heterogeneity by geographic region (P < 0.001) and attenuation of benefit over time (β = +0.034/year; P = 0.004); OCT analyses were non-significant.
CONCLUSION: Both IVUS and OCT reduced MACE, revascularization, and ST compared with angiography-guided PCI. These findings support intravascular imaging as a routine adjunct to PCI in the populations studied.

Title: Left atrial appendage occlusion: an alternative to anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia. Global Burden of Disease estimates indicate that 52.6 million individuals were living with AF or atrial flutter in 2021, and one in three to one in five persons are expected to develop AF during their lifetime. AF is associated with an increased risk of stroke, systemic thromboembolism, and death. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) is the first-line strategy for preventing AF-associated embolism. However, embolic events still occur in 1%-4% of anticoagulated patients per year, major bleeding occurs in 2%-4% per year, and long-term adherence to direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) is incomplete. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) was developed as a mechanical alternative to address these unmet needs. The evidence base has changed substantially over the last 2 years: three randomized controlled trials comparing LAAO with DOAC-OPTION, CHAMPION-AF, and CLOSURE-AF-have now reported. In this update, we summarize the pathophysiological rationale, the technical aspects of the procedure, and the totality of the randomized and observational evidence, including a 2026 meta-analysis of 5,890 randomized patients. Taken together, these data indicate that LAAO reduces non-procedure-related bleeding but does not decrease all-cause major bleeding, intracranial haemorrhage, or mortality, and may carry a higher risk of ischaemic stroke than DOAC. LAAO remains an established option for patients with contraindications to or intolerance of long-term OAC. In DOAC-eligible patients, it has become a randomized-tested alternative, but current evidence supports an individualized, shared decision rather than a universal offer. We outline the remaining controversies-patient selection, device-related thrombus, peri-device leak, post-procedural antithrombotic therapy, and the interpretation of observational data-and the trials designed to resolve them.

Title: The association of left atrial volume index and coronary artery disease in type 2 diabetic patients without a history of hypertension and valvular heart disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial volume index (LAVI) evaluated using echocardiography serves a powerful predictor of cardiovascular outcomes. Since type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a main risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD), the present investigation was conducted to examine the association between LAVI and incidence of CAD in diabetic patients.
METHODS: In this case-control study, 90 type 2 diabetic patients aged 18-70 years who underwent coronary angiography at Imam Hossein Hospital, Tehran, between 2023 and 2024 were consecutively enrolled. Patients with hypertension, valvular heart disease, heart failure, or respiratory diseases were excluded. Cases (n = 45) had coronary artery disease (≥ 50% stenosis on angiography), while controls (n = 45) had no significant stenosis. Left atrial volume index (LAVI) was measured by echocardiography and classified as abnormal if ≥ 34 mL/m². All variables including LAVI were compared between two groups. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to investigate the role of variables in predicting CAD incidence in diabetic patients.
RESULTS: A total of 90 patients with type 2 diabetes were included (45 with CAD and 45 without CAD); the mean age was 51.48±5.68 years, and 60% were male. Analyses revealed that LAVI values were significantly higher in patients with CAD compared to those without (P = 0.018), while there were no significant differences between two groups regarding gender, age, smoking, insulin dependence, diabetes duration, HbA1c, FBS, EF. also, no significant differences were observed in other echocardiographic measures including mild LVH, mild diastolic dysfunction, heart rate. Multivariate logistic regression identified LAVI as an independent predictor of CAD (OR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.06-1.45), P = 0.006. ROC curve analysis showed that a LAVI cut-off of 28 mL/m² predicted CAD with 71% sensitivity and 51% specificity (P = 0.016).
CONCLUSION: LAVI could be a potentially useful, accessible and practical index for screening CAD in diabetic patients. It may be proposed as part of the workup for the diagnosis and management of CAD in type 2 diabetic patients.

Title: Serum magnesium levels and the risk of acute viral cardiomyopathy in children: A case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute viral cardiomyopathy is a leading cause of heart failure in children. Although magnesium is essential for myocardial electrophysiology, its potential association with pediatric viral cardiomyopathy remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: This hospital-based frequency-matched case-control study (1:1 ratio, balanced for age) included 73 children with confirmed acute viral cardiomyopathy and 73 non-cardiac hospitalized controls at Afzalipour Hospital, Kerman, Iran (2023-2024). Serum total magnesium was measured on admission (reference 1.7-2.3 mg/dL); hypomagnesemia was defined as <1.7 mg/dL. Groups were compared using an independent-samples t-test and a χ² test. Multivariable logistic regression has been used to assess associated factors for acute viral cardiomyopathy.
RESULTS: Mean serum magnesium level was significantly lower in the cardiomyopathy group than the control group (1.80 ± 0.31 vs. 1.98 ± 0.31 mg/dL; P = 0.003). Hypomagnesemia prevalence was significantly higher in the cardiomyopathy group (39.7% vs. 9.6%; unadjusted OR (95% CI): 5.80 (2.28-14.75); P < 0.001). After adjustment for sex, BMI, fever, and underlying chronic disease, each 0.1 mg/dL decrease in serum magnesium was associated with 1.38-fold higher odds of cardiomyopathy (adjusted OR (95% CI): 1.38 (1.11-1.72); P = 0.004). Hospital stay was longer in cases (7.77 ± 2.42 vs. 5.39 ± 2.20 days; P < 0.001). In-hospital mortality was higher among the cardiomyopathy group (6.8% vs. 1.4%), though the difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.209).
CONCLUSION: Children with acute viral cardiomyopathy seem to have significantly lower serum magnesium compared with matched controls. Routine admission magnesium screening could be considered in management protocols.

Title: Pulmonary Endarterectomy After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty: A Single-Center USA Experience.
Abstract: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) is the treatment of choice for operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), while balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) is reserved for inoperable disease. However, operability is subjective and there are patients who may undergo BPA prior to PEA. It is not clear if prior BPA affects PEA outcomes. We present a series of patients from a single, high-volume, referral center who underwent PEA after prior BPA. CTEPH patients who underwent BPA prior to undergoing PEA at the University of California, San Diego between January 2013 and July 2025 were included. Post-PEA outcomes were compared to all PEA patients who did not have prior BPA from the year 2022. Twenty-one patients were identified. Average number of BPA sessions prior to PEA was 3.4 ± 2.1. The most common reason for initial BPA was distal disease deemed inoperable (43%). Average total circulatory arrest time was 61.5 ± 21.8 min, compared to 47.9 ± 19.3 min (p = 0.003) in the control PEA cases (n = 188). Post-operatively, the PEA after BPA cohort had longer ventilator days (p < 0.001), ICU days (p = 0.022) and post-operative length of stay (LOS) (p < 0.001); there were also higher rates of post-operative bleeding (p < 0.001) requiring transfusions (p = 0.033) and return to the operating room (p = 0.008). There was one death related to prior BPA complications despite adequate endarterectomy with improved hemodynamics. There was similar hemodynamic improvement post-operatively in both cohorts. Although prior BPA made PEA more challenging and increased select post-operative complications, it is not a contraindication for successful PEA.

Title: Characteristics of Patients Involved With the Kidney Supportive Care Program: A Cohort Study of Routinely Collected Data.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: People with kidney failure face a significantly higher risk of death and symptom burden. We sought insights into the survival and symptom burden of people receiving medical management of kidney failure without dialysis.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: People with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≤ 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 receiving nondialytic/conservative/palliative management and known to the Kidney Supportive Care Team in a tertiary care hospital.
PREDICTORS: eGFR at cohort entry, living arrangement, and history of ischemic heart disease, heart failure, or stroke, according to routine care databases.
OUTCOMES: Primary: median survival. Secondary: number of hospitalizations and symptom burden assessed through the Integrated Palliative Care Outcome Scale-Renal score.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cox regression survival modeling and descriptive statistics for hospitalizations and symptom burden.
RESULTS: The cohort included 223 people receiving care between January 2016 and April 2023, with a median age of 84 (interquartile range, 77-87) years. Median survival was 452 days (95% CI, 351-552). People with an eGFR of 11-15 mL/min/1.73 m2 at cohort entry had a median survival of 517 days (95% CI, 406-623); those with an eGFR of 6-10 mL/min/1.73 m2 had a median survival of 260 days (95% CI, 138-382), whereas people with an eGFR of < 5 mL/min/1.73 m2 had a median survival of 61 days (95% CI, 46-107). People living independently at home had significantly higher median survival (538 days), compared with assisted living at home (356 days) or living in a nursing home (232 days) (P < 0.05). The studied comorbidities were not predictive of survival. At year 1, the most prevalent symptom was weakness (60%) with median "moderate" severity, with similar findings at year 2.
LIMITATIONS: Single-center, retrospective study with univariable analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: The study provided valuable insights into life expectancy and symptom burden with kidney failure managed without dialysis, including the prognostic value of considering the baseline living situation in anticipating survival, to help guide clinicians facing the uncertainty of this clinical scenario.

Title: Low-Sodium Peritoneal Dialysis Solution (Na 126 mmol/L) for Enhanced Sodium Removal: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Fluid overload is a major cause of treatment failure in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD), and insufficient sodium removal is involved with this condition. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of a novel low-sodium (LS) PD solution (Na 126 mmol/L, glucose 1.6%) combined with standard-sodium (SS) PD solutions as a new approach to enhance sodium removal.
STUDY DESIGN & PARTICIPANTS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group study, outpatient PD patients at 20 facilities in Japan were randomly assigned (2:1) to the LS PD solution group or the SS PD solution group (Na 135 mmol/L, glucose 1.35%).
EXPOSURE: The test solution replaced 1 daily exchange and was combined with at least 1 standard PD solution. Patients who met dose-escalation criteria at week 4 switched to twice-daily dosing.
OUTCOMES: The primary outcome was the change in daily peritoneal sodium removal from baseline to week 8. Secondary outcomes included peritoneal sodium removal per bag exchange, total daily (peritoneal and urinary) sodium, water removal, and dialysis adequacy.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Efficacy, including sodium removal in PD treatment, was analyzed in the full analysis set; safety was assessed in all patients.
RESULTS: The mean change in daily peritoneal sodium removal was significantly higher in the LS PD solution group (n = 51, 28.7 ± 36.2 mmol/d) than in the SS PD solution group (n = 27, -6.3 ± 26.2 mmol/d; P < 0.001). Other outcomes showed no significant differences. Drug-related adverse events (mainly hyponatremia) were observed in the LS PD solution group; however, they were generally mild and completely reversible.
LIMITATIONS: Participants with relatively preserved residual kidney function and incremental PD were overrepresented.
CONCLUSIONS: The LS PD solution, when combined with standard PD solutions, increased sodium removal without compromising dialysis adequacy or residual kidney function.

Title: Protein-bound Uremic Toxin Lowering Effects of Sevelamer in Hyperphosphatemic Hemodialysis Patients: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: p-Cresyl sulfate (pCS) is an important protein-bound uremic toxin associated with high cardiovascular mortality in patients receiving long-term hemodialysis (HD). Data regarding pCS lowering and the pleiotropic effects of sevelamer are limited in patients receiving long-term HD.
STUDY DESIGN: Open-label, multicenter randomized controlled trial.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Patients with hyperphosphatemia receiving long-term HD.
EXPOSURES: Patients were randomly assigned to receive either sevelamer or calcium carbonate as phosphate binders for 24 weeks.
OUTCOMES: The primary outcome was the between-group difference in pCS change over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels, intact parathyroid hormone levels, cardio-ankle vascular index, and adverse event rates.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Mean differences between groups were analyzed using a linear mixed model. Multivariate logistic regression was used to determine factors associated with decreased pCS levels.
RESULTS: A total of 128 patients were enrolled, 4 dropped out, and 124 were analyzed. Residual kidney function (RKF) ≥100 mL/day was present in 47.7%. Both groups achieved significant phosphate reduction. Mean changes in pCS did not differ significantly between groups: 0.70 mg/L (95% CI, -1.04 to 2.44) in the sevelamer group versus -0.09 mg/L (95% CI, -1.70 to 1.51) in the calcium carbonate group (P = 0.07). However, sevelamer was associated with a smaller increase in cardio-ankle vascular index than calcium carbonate (adjusted mean change difference -0.63 [95% CI, -1.22 to -0.04]; P = 0.04). Preserved RKF and high-dose phosphate binders were independently associated with decreased pCS levels.
LIMITATIONS: Change in pCS is only a surrogate marker for cardiovascular events. The study may have been underpowered, or the sevelamer dose and treatment duration may have been insufficient.
CONCLUSIONS: pCS levels were not significantly changed in both groups. However, the increase in cardio-ankle vascular index was smaller with sevelamer than with calcium carbonate, independent of pCS change. Further trials with larger samples and longer treatment durations are warranted.

Title: Protective effects of vanillic acid against isoprenaline-induced heart failure in Wistar rats: A biochemical and histological investigation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) continues to pose a major health concern worldwide, frequently arising from ongoing myocardial damage driven by oxidative stress, inflammatory processes, and programmed cell death. While synthetic medications are widely used, natural compounds with multi-targeted actions are gaining attention. Vanillic acid (VA), a plant-derived phenolic compound, is suggested to possess cardioprotective properties; yet, its effects in experimental HF models remain underexplored.
METHODS: This study evaluated the impact of VA pretreatment on isoprenaline (ISO)-induced HF in male Wistar rats. A total of forty animals were randomly allocated into four distinct groups: sham, VA, ISO, and ISO + VA. ISO was administered subcutaneously to induce cardiac injury, while VA was given orally for 10 days prior to ISO exposure. Biochemical markers of myocardial damage, oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, infarct size, and apoptotic gene expression (Bax, Bcl-2) were assessed through ELISA, histological staining, and real-time PCR.
RESULTS: ISO administration caused significant elevation in cardiac enzymes (LDH, CK-MB, cTn-I), pro-inflammatory markers (IL-1β, TNF-α), lipid peroxidation (MDA), and Bax expression, along with reduced antioxidant enzyme activity (CAT, SOD, GPx), IL-10, and Bcl-2 levels. VA pretreatment mitigated these alterations, demonstrating a notable decrease in infarct size, oxidative damage, inflammation, and apoptosis. No adverse effects were observed in the VA-only group.
CONCLUSION: VA exhibited substantial cardioprotective effects against ISO-induced myocardial injury, likely through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic mechanisms. The results indicate that VA could be a valuable natural adjunct in the management of HF.

Title: Cardiovascular Risk of Conventional Synthetic, Biologic and Targeted Synthetic Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs in Common Rheumatic Diseases: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence.
Abstract: Rheumatic diseases, including those with an autoimmune etiology (including rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, spondyloarthropathies and systemic vasculitis) represent an independent risk factor for coronary atherosclerosis and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Systemic inflammation plays a multidimensional role in cardiovascular disease (CVD) pathogenesis, and patients with rheumatic diseases face elevated CVD risk and mortality compared with the general population, driven by both traditional cardiovascular risk factors and systemic immune dysregulation. Adequate management of inflammation will be accompanied by improved cardiovascular risk. In 2010, rheumatology introduced the "targeted therapy" strategy, and around the same time, cohort studies showed a significant decrease in cardiovascular mortality. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to June 2026. Studies were included if they evaluated the cardiovascular effects of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) in patients with the aforementioned rheumatic diseases. These diseases were selected based on their high prevalence, well-established cardiovascular risk, and availability of comparative evidence across DMARD classes; systemic sclerosis was excluded due to its distinct pathophysiology and limited published data on DMARD-related cardiovascular outcomes. We still need to deepen our understanding of the precise pathophysiological mechanism of autoimmune mediated acceleration of atherosclerosis and its clinical manifestations, to enable more appropriate selection of immunotherapies and biological agents for patients with rheumatic diseases, including those with an autoimmune etiology, and ultimately reduce the cardiovascular risk of this population, thereby improving prognosis and quality of life. The aim of this narrative review was to synthesize available evidence regarding the cardiovascular effects of three major classes of DMARDs: conventional synthetic disease‑modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs), biologic disease‑modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs), and targeted synthetic disease‑modifying antirheumatic drugs (tsDMARDs), across a stratified spectrum of cardiovascular endpoints ranging from hard clinical outcomes to subclinical surrogate markers. The main findings indicate that different DMARDs classes exhibit heterogeneous effects on cardiovascular outcomes, with csDMARDs such as methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine generally associated with favorable cardiovascular profiles, whereas the cardiovascular safety of certain biologic and targeted synthetic agents remains a subject of ongoing investigation. Limitations of this review include the observational nature of most included studies, heterogeneity across study designs and populations, and the lack of head-to-head randomized trials comparing different DMARDs classes with respect to cardiovascular outcomes. Collectively, these findings underscore the need for individualized cardiovascular risk assessment and tailored DMARDs selection in patients with rheumatic diseases, thereby optimizing both rheumatic and cardiovascular prognosis.

Title: Short-Term Effects of Golden Rice Cookies Enriched With Piper crocatum Extract on Lipid Profiles in Adults With Diabetes: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) commonly coexists with dyslipidemia and elevated cardiovascular risk. Food-based interventions containing antioxidants and polyphenols may support lipid metabolism. This study evaluated the short-term effects of Golden Rice cookies enriched with active Piper crocatum extract on lipid profiles in adults with DM.
METHODS: This quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group study included 102 adults with DM assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received Golden Rice cookies enriched with P. crocatum extract, while the control group received similar cookies without the extract for 28 days. Total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and triglycerides were measured before and after the intervention. Bivariate analyses were performed in the full sample, whereas analysis of covariance was performed among non-statin participants, adjusting for baseline lipid values, age, body mass index, diabetes duration, carbohydrate intake, and protein intake.
RESULTS: In the unadjusted analysis, total cholesterol and LDL-C increased significantly in the intervention group, whereas total cholesterol decreased significantly in the control group. Between-group analysis showed a significant difference only in total cholesterol. Among non-statin participants, an exploratory adjusted analysis showed a significant between-group difference in total cholesterol (p = 0.016; adjusted mean difference = -12.55 mg/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI] = -22.74 to -2.36). No significant adjusted differences were observed for LDL-C, HDL-C, or triglycerides.
CONCLUSION: A 28-day intervention with Golden Rice cookies enriched with active P. crocatum extract was associated with a limited exploratory adjusted between-group difference in total cholesterol among non-statin adults with DM. These preliminary findings require confirmation in longer randomized controlled trials with stronger dietary control and mechanistic biomarker assessment.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT07268781.

Title: Thrombophilia-Related Gene Polymorphisms and Recurrent Miscarriages in Lebanese Population: A Case-Control Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genes associated with cardiovascular diseases are strongly linked to idiopathic recurrent pregnancy loss. Because these genetic mutations often involve coagulation factors, anticoagulant therapy, particularly low-molecular-weight heparin, is increasingly encountered in obstetric practice in Lebanon for selected maternal and pregnancy-related indications. However, data describing the prevalence and prescribing patterns of anticoagulant use among Lebanese obstetricians remain limited. In this multicenter retrospective case-control study, 12 mutations within 10 CVD-related genes in Lebanese women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss were assessed to uncover further potential genetic links between these two conditions.
METHODS: Data were collected from a total of 117 women with recurrent pregnancy loss (≥ 2 pregnancy losses with the same partner before the 22nd week of gestation) and 38 women with a history of at least one successful pregnancy. Data were collected from two independent medical centers in Lebanon, Abou Jaoude Hospital and the Lebanese Diagnostic Medical Center, through medical-record review and participant interviews. Twelve mutations were covered employing polymerase chain reaction and reverse-hybridization techniques. Because of the variation in genotyping completeness across assays, the effective sample size for individual polymorphisms ranged from 27 to 38 controls and 78 to 117 cases.
RESULTS: Genetic analysis revealed a significant association between Factor V Leiden (OR = 0.31; p = 0.017), Factor XIII: V34L (OR = 0.3; p = 0.009), plasminogen activator inhibitor-1: 4G/5G (OR = 0.3; p = 0.034), and lower odds of recurrent pregnancy loss. However, these associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing and should therefore be considered exploratory. No significant associations were observed for other evaluated polymorphisms, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase C677T and A1298C.
CONCLUSION: Repeated pregnancy loss is multifaceted and not necessarily linked to coagulopathy-related mutations; in the Lebanese population, certain polymorphisms showed nominal associations with lower odds of recurrent pregnancy loss that require confirmation in larger, independent studies, and no statistically significant association was observed between methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase mutations and recurrent pregnancy loss in the present study. These findings suggest that the routine presumption of a thrombophilic etiology in recurrent pregnancy loss may not be universally applicable. Future research should prioritize validating these genetic associations in larger, adequately powered cohorts and exploring the underlying biological mechanisms before any therapeutic implications are considered.

Title: Post-stroke sequelae risk score (PSSRS): a 16-year retrospective study developing an internally validated multi-algorithm model for post-stroke sequelae.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Post-stroke sequelae (PSS) encompass persistent functional impairments after stroke and may benefit from early risk stratification. We developed and internally validated a time-to-event prediction model based on routinely available clinical and biochemical variables.
METHOD: This retrospective single-center cohort included 2,095 patients hospitalized with acute stroke at Zhujiang Hospital between 2008 and 2024. Thirty-seven candidate variables were assessed. The cohort was split 7:3 into training (n = 1,467) and internal test (n = 628) sets before preprocessing, feature selection, tuning, and model comparison. Univariate Cox, multivariable Cox, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and random survival forest (RSF) analyses identified eight intersection variables. A total of 101 survival-model pipelines were compared using training-set resampling; the selected model was then evaluated in the internal test set.
RESULT: The StepCox (forward) + RSF pipeline showed the highest prespecified training-resampling performance. Its Harrell C-index was 0.87 in the training set and 0.85 in the internal test set. Test-set time-dependent AUROCs at 1, 3, and 5 years were 0.800 (95% CI, 0.760-0.840), 0.830 (0.790-0.870), and 0.820 (0.780-0.860), respectively; corresponding AUPRCs were 0.748, 0.772, and 0.761, and Brier scores were 0.140, 0.170, and 0.180. Calibration slopes were 0.96, 0.93, and 0.90. LDH, CK-MB, and DBIL were among the leading contributors in the model-interpretation analyses.
CONCLUSION: PSSRS provides an internally validated framework for estimating individualized risk of post-stroke sequelae. External temporal and multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Latent class analysis identifies three biologically distinct phenotypes among patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy: a derivation and temporal validation study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite successful vascular recanalization, approximately half of patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) fail to achieve functional independence at 3 months. The biological determinants of this heterogeneity remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: Latent class analysis (LCA) was applied to 825 consecutive EVT-treated patients (development cohort, January 2021-December 2024) using 12 routine post-procedural clinical and laboratory indicators. Phenotype associations with favorable 3-month outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Reproducibility was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 211).
RESULTS: LCA identified three phenotypes. The Low-burden phenotype (Class 1, 44.4%) had the lowest inflammatory and coagulatory burden and achieved favorable outcome in 70.8% of patients. The Metabolic phenotype (Class 2, 42.7%), characterized by hyperglycemia and elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, had a favorable outcome rate of 44.9% and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) rate of 7.1%. The hypercoagulable phenotype (Class 3, 13.0%), defined by markedly elevated D-dimer and atrial fibrillation, had a favorable outcome rate of 40.2% and sICH rate of 8.4%. After multivariable adjustment, both Class 2 (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.35-0.69) and Class 3 (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.25-0.67) were independently associated with unfavorable outcome (both p < 0.001). Class distribution and outcome associations were reproduced in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSION: LCA identified three biologically distinct phenotypes among EVT-treated patients with divergent functional outcomes. Multicenter prospective validation is needed before these findings can inform clinical practice.

Title: A buffer-positive serotonin release assay pattern is associated with increased mortality in HIT: a retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HIT is an anti-platelet factor 4 (PF4) disorder characterized by thrombocytopenia and increased thrombosis risk. The serotonin release assay (SRA) is the gold standard test for diagnosing HIT. The clinical significance of a buffer-positive SRA pattern remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study compared characteristics and outcomes between patients with HIT with buffer-negative and buffer-positive SRA patterns.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania and affiliated hospitals. Consecutive patients with confirmed HIT, defined as a positive PF4/heparin enzyme-linked immunoassay and platelet-rich plasma-based SRA without a high-heparin inhibition step, were classified by an SRA pattern (buffer-negative vs buffer-positive) and followed for 30 days. The primary outcome was cumulative incidence of thrombosis; secondary outcomes included mortality, major bleeding, and platelet recovery.
RESULTS: Of 207 HIT-positive patients, 190 (91.8%) had a buffer-negative and 17 (8.2%) had a buffer-positive SRA pattern. Median anti-PF4/heparin enzyme-linked immunoassay optical density was significantly lower in the buffer-positive group (0.8 vs 2.3; P < .001). Thrombosis incidence was similar between groups (64.7% vs 50.2%; P = .28). The buffer-positive pattern was independently associated with longer time to platelet recovery (9.0 vs 5.0 days; P = .03) and higher 30-day cumulative incidence of death (47.4% vs 17.1%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.74; P = .03).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with HIT, a buffer-positive SRA pattern was associated with more prolonged thrombocytopenia and increased mortality. Given that our assay used platelet-rich plasma, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation with the classical washed-platelet SRA.

Title: Association between preoperative E/e' and early left ventricular systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, the degree of systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is heterogeneous. We assessed whether routine preoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) indices-particularly E/e'-are associated with early postoperative improvement in left ventricular function.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing isolated CABG at a single tertiary center (April 2019 to July 2025). Eligibility required a preoperative left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of <50%. Emergency/salvage operations, 30-day deaths, and patients without an evaluable early postoperative TTE were excluded. The primary outcome was an absolute increase in the LVEF of ≥10 percentage points. Because of the limited number of outcome events, the primary association analysis used a single-predictor logistic regression model with preoperative E/e'. Sensitivity analyses excluded patients with preoperative atrial fibrillation (AF) and modeled postoperative LVEF as a continuous outcome adjusted for baseline LVEF.
RESULTS: Of 75 otherwise clinically eligible patients, three lacked an evaluable early postoperative TTE, leaving 72 patients for outcome analysis; 17 (23.6%) achieved an LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. A higher preoperative E/e' was associated with early LVEF improvement (OR 1.155 per 1-unit increase; 95% CI 1.04-1.28; p = 0.005; N = 66; 16 events). The apparent AUC was 0.700; after 1,000-resample bootstrap internal validation, the estimated optimism was 0.004 and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.696 (95% bootstrap CI 0.526-0.885). The association persisted after excluding patients with AF (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.27; p = 0.025). In a sensitivity analysis using postoperative LVEF as a continuous outcome, E/e' remained associated with postoperative LVEF after adjustment for baseline LVEF (β = 0.31 percentage points per 1-unit increase; 95% CI 0.01-0.61; p = 0.042).
CONCLUSION: A higher preoperative E/e' was associated with early improvement in LV systolic function after CABG among patients with a preoperative LVEF of <50% who survived to undergo early postoperative echocardiographic assessment. Given the small number of events and the single-center retrospective design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation.

Title: Rethinking immunotherapy sequencing in multiple myeloma: a conceptual adaptive immunotherapy sequencing model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy and bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) have transformed treatment for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). Contemporary guidelines increasingly incorporate prior antigen-directed exposure, disease kinetics, patient fitness, toxicity, access, and patient preference. However, a prospectively validated framework that jointly operationalizes immune fitness, tumor antigen status, and treatment feasibility for sequencing T-cell-redirecting therapies is not available.
MAIN BODY: This Perspective introduces the Adaptive Immunotherapy Sequencing Model (AISM), an author-proposed framework for research and multidisciplinary discussion. AISM proposes that sequencing should be studied in relation to two evolving biological domains: the capacity of the host T-cell compartment to support therapy and the probability that the relevant tumor antigen remains therapeutically actionable. The model uses provisional 0-10 research constructs for T-cell fitness and antigen-escape risk to make these domains explicit. AISM hypothesizes that, for eligible patients with early RRMM and feasible access, referral for BCMA-directed CAR-T before prolonged exposure to T-cell-redirecting BsAbs may preserve a potentially favorable treatment option. It also recognizes that off-the-shelf BsAbs may be necessary when disease tempo, frailty, access, or patient preference make CAR-T impracticable. After prior BCMA-directed therapy, an antigen-switching approach is biologically plausible, but antigen loss is not universal and other mechanisms of resistance must be considered.
CONCLUSIONS: AISM provides a testable framework for prospective comparative studies. Such studies should evaluate whether biologically informed sequencing improves progression-free survival (PFS), while also assessing overall survival, toxicity, infections, treatment-free time, feasibility, and patient-reported outcomes.

Title: Remimazolam for Procedural Sedation During Synchronized Electrical Cardioversion in the Emergency Department.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
Abstract: Synchronized electrical cardioversion necessitates procedural sedation to ensure patient comfort and amnesia. Remimazolam is a novel, ultrashort-acting intravenous benzodiazepine with organ-independent esterase metabolism, a favorable safety profile, and flumazenil reversibility. Although, previously described in the electrophysiology laboratory, use of remimazolam has not been reported for electrical cardioversion in the emergency department. In this case, a 67-year-old man with sudden-onset paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented in symptomatic atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Following rate and rhythm optimization, the decision was made to proceed with synchronized electrical cardioversion under procedural sedation. After consent was obtained, remimazolam (5 mg intravenously) was administered as a single bolus. Sedation onset occurred at 49 seconds, with adequate depth achieved at 1 minute 37 seconds. A single synchronized biphasic 200 joule electric shock was successfully delivered at 2 minutes 20 seconds, converting the patient to normal sinus rhythm. Eye opening occurred at 3 minutes 50 seconds, with return to baseline orientation at 4 minutes 30 seconds. No apnea, hypoxia, hemodynamic instability, or procedural recall was observed. Continuous end-tidal carbon dioxide monitoring confirmed uninterrupted spontaneous ventilation throughout. The rapid onset, hemodynamic stability, and remarkably brief recovery time observed support its potential as a first-line sedative for emergency department cardioversion. Further prospective study in this setting is warranted.

Title: Association of estimated plasma volume status with progression from stage 2 to stage 4 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: a cohort from the Tianjin region of China.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKM) is a systemicdisorder linked to insulin resistance. The association between estimated plasmavolume status (ePVS) and progression from CKM stage 2 (CKM2) to stage 4(CKM4) remains poorly understood. This study assessed the association betweenePVS and CKM2-to-CKM4 progression.
METHODS: A total of 36,505 hospitalized CKM2 patients from the TJHFIT cohortwere followed for 10 years, with 15,495 incident CKM4 events. Cox proportionalhazards models, restricted cubic splines, and SHAP analyses were applied toestimate hazard ratios, nonlinear associations, and variable importance, adjustedfor demographics, medical history, laboratory parameters, and medications.
RESULTS: CKM4 patients had significantly higher admission and discharge ePVS thancontrols (all P < 0.05). In quartile-stratified analyses, elevated risk of CKM4progression was independently observed only in the upper admission ePVS strata(Q3 and Q4), with no significant risk in the moderate stratum (Q2). For dischargeePVS, a significant risk signal emerged starting from Q2. The highest admission ePVSquartile was associated with 43%, 88%, and 76% higher risks of CKM4, CKM4b, andheart failure versus Q1. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a spoon-shapednonlinear association between admission ePVS and CKM4, with an inflection point atapproximately 5.14. The association was stronger in patients aged >60 years.
DISCUSSION: Higher admission ePVS (Q3/Q4) is independently associated with CKM2-to-CKM4 progression and may serve as a noninvasive risk biomarker particularly in older high-risk populations. External cohort validation is requiredbefore clinical application.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The research has been registered (ChiCTR2300077220) with ethics approval (TYLL2023-K-016).

Title: Hemodynamic biomarkers in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis: evidence boundaries and research pathways from prognostic stratification to treatment-effect prediction.
Abstract: Symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (sICAS) has traditionally been stratified primarily according to angiographic stenosis severity. However, this anatomical approach does not adequately capture the heterogeneity of ischemic mechanisms, distal hemodynamic compromise, or treatment response, prompting increasing interest in hemodynamic biomarkers for mechanism-based risk stratification. In this review, we propose an evidence framework that evaluates these biomarkers across measurement validity, mechanistic coherence, prognostic association, treatment-effect prediction, external validation, and clinical utility, while integrating lesion function, distal perfusion, compensatory capacity, and parallel embolic and perforator pathways. Although several measures, particularly distal hypoperfusion and borderzone infarction, have shown prognostic value, the evidence identified in this review remains dominated by single-center studies, platform-specific definitions, and incompletely validated thresholds. Among the completed direct sICAS studies identified, we found no prospective validation of a hemodynamic biomarker as a treatment-effect modifier. Translation requires standardized measurement, prespecified biomarker definitions, and external validation. Claims of treatment-effect modification additionally require prespecified interaction analyses within appropriate treatment comparisons, preferably randomized. Biomarker-guided treatment selection should be supported by reliable estimates of absolute benefits and harms and evidence of clinical utility.

Title: AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy under superior vena cava filter protection for acute upper extremity deep vein thrombosis in patients with cancer: a single-center, retrospective analysis.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The incidence of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) is increasing, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy (PMT) is receiving more attention as a treatment option. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT.
METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025. The evaluation indicators included technical success rate (defined as a thrombus clearance rate >80%), intraoperative adverse events, degree of limb swelling relief, incidence of pulmonary embolism, and thrombus recurrence during follow-up.
RESULTS: A total of 19 patients (10 female; mean age 60.84 ± 11.30 years) were included. All patients had secondary UEDVT and a history of malignant tumors, with 14 cases (73.7%) having a history of central venous catheterization. All procedures achieved technical success, with no severe adverse events such as major bleeding occurring intraoperatively, nor were there any new symptomatic pulmonary embolisms. The average circumference of the affected limb 10 cm above the elbow before surgery was 29.83 ± 2.20 cm, which decreased to 26.98 ± 2.0 cm on the second postoperative day. During the 6-month follow-up, one patient with advanced lung cancer developed swelling of the upper limb on postoperative day 136, confirmed by ultrasound to be a recurrence of deep vein thrombosis; another patient was found to have an asymptomatic mural thrombus on ultrasound examination on postoperative day 28.
CONCLUSION: PMT with the 8-Fr AngioJet system and SVC filter protection appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for cancer patients with acute UEDVT.

Title: Among rural older adults, an apparent physical-activity contrast in nonblank medication-field presence was markedly attenuated when chronic-disease management registration was incorporated into the analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medication fields created for chronic-disease management may mislead when reused as medication-exposure measures in broader older-adult populations. Using routine exercise-frequency as routine-recorded physical activity (PA), we compared PA + records (daily, at least weekly, or occasional exercise) with PA- records (no exercise) and examined how nonblank medication-field presence changed after management-registration context was incorporated.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study used 2,270 examination records from a 2025 rural primary-care program in northeastern China; PA was available for 2,226 records. The outcome was any nonblank text in the main-medication field. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) with small-sample-adjusted cluster-robust inference across 20 sites. Sequential models incorporated demographics, site, and four hypertension/diabetes management-registration categories. Logistic regression estimated standardized proportions and absolute differences. Medication text underwent secondary audit, including 200 randomly sampled retained entries independently reviewed by two pharmacists.
RESULTS: Nonblank medication fields occurred in 1,114/1,157 (96.3%) records with hypertension and/or diabetes management registration versus 27/1,113 (2.4%) with neither registration. Field presence was low without registration and near-complete with hypertension-only or dual registration; the diabetes-only stratum was small (n = 37). Overall field presence was 56.4% in PA+ and 42.8% in PA- records (PR 1.317, 95% CI 1.076-1.612). After registration context was incorporated, the PR was 1.001 (95% CI 0.960-1.043); full adjustment yielded 1.002 (95% CI 0.959-1.046). Standardized proportions were 51.26% and 51.14%, a difference of 0.12 percentage points (95% CI -2.07 to 2.30). Among 1,368 retained entries, archived labels classified 75.9% as antihypertensive, 14.5% as glucose-lowering, 0.5% as other cardiovascular, 1.7% as other medications, and 7.4% as unresolved. Inter-reviewer agreement for broad therapeutic class was 99.5% (κ = 0.982), and parser-manual-reference concordance was 99.0%; these assessments did not verify medication exposure.
CONCLUSION: Nonblank main-medication-field recording was strongly patterned by chronic-disease management registration, and the apparent overall PA-related contrast was markedly attenuated after this context was incorporated. Blank fields cannot establish medication nonuse, and nonblank or consistently parsed text cannot establish complete, current medication exposure.

Title: Real-world discrimination and incremental value of first-trimester placental growth factor for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a retrospective Chinese cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Placental growth factor (PlGF) contributes to first-trimester screening algorithms for preeclampsia, but its prognostic performance as an isolated biomarker in routine Chinese care is uncertain.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-centre cohort study among pregnancy episodes recorded in a hospital PlGF workbook. Pregnancy episodes were deduplicated, PlGF values were traced to source laboratory cells, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) were ascertained using unvalidated free-text discharge-diagnosis keywords. The primary operational window was 9 + 0 to 13 + 6 weeks; 11 + 0 to 13 + 6 weeks was evaluated separately. We compared PlGF with a parsimonious maternal-characteristics model containing age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI), and nulliparity.
RESULTS: From 405 source rows, 380 pregnancy episodes were resolved; 310 met the primary criteria, including 27 HDP events (11 cases of preeclampsia and 16 of gestational hypertension). PlGF alone had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.633 (95% bootstrap CI 0.523-0.738), and internally derived PlGF multiple of the median (MoM) had an AUC of 0.636 (0.533-0.740). In 308 complete records, the maternal-characteristics model had an apparent AUC of 0.740 (0.635-0.837), while adding log10(PlGF) yielded an AUC of 0.748 (0.638-0.849); paired ΔAUC was 0.009 (95% CI -0.019 to 0.037).
CONCLUSION: The findings are consistent with a modest association between lower first-trimester PlGF and subsequent HDP, but they do not support isolated clinical use or a deployable prediction model.

Title: Cardiovascular complications as a consequence of coronavirus infection in pregnant women managed in ambulatory settings.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 has been linked to cardiovascular complications in the general population. However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. In this retrospective population-based matched cohort study, we evaluated whether COVID-19 infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular complications among pregnant women managed predominantly in outpatient settings.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based matched cohort study using electronic health record data from pregnant women between 2020 and 2025. Women with COVID-19 during pregnancy were matched 1:1 to women without documented COVID-19 during pregnancy according to demographic, obstetric, and clinical characteristics. The final analytical cohort included 4,068 women in each group. Cardiovascular outcomes during pregnancy and within a year since last menstrual period were assessed. Baseline demographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the COVID-19 and control groups. No significant differences were observed between the groups in the incidence of major cardiovascular complications, either when analyzed individually or as a composite endpoint (0.15% vs. 0.15%; OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.27-3.74). Specifically, there were no significant differences in the occurrence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, or deep venous thrombosis. In contrast, cough and backache were significantly more frequent among women with COVID-19 than among matched controls (6.88% vs. 4.87%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.19-1.75; 13.8% vs. 11.8%; OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05-1.37; p = 0.007 respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that among pregnant women in ambulatory community settings, COVID-19 infection is not associated with an increased risk of major cardiovascular complications.

Title: Magnetocardiographic characteristics in patients with varying severity of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) is an established risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Magnetocardiography (MCG) is an emerging non-invasive electrophysiological technique with potential value in cardiovascular assessment; however, its utility in evaluating OSAS severity remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize MCG features across different severities of OSAS and to evaluate their predictive performance for moderate-to-severe disease.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled OSAS patients between June 2023 and October 2024, all of whom underwent MCG examination. Patients were stratified by OSAS severity, and MCG parameters were compared between the normal-to-mild and moderate-to-severe groups. Baseline data, complete blood count, serum biochemical indicators, and MCG parameters were collected along with relevant clinical and laboratory data. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of moderate-to-severe OSAS, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to evaluate the predictive performance of each parameter and the combined model.
RESULTS: Group comparisons revealed significant differences in traditional OSAS severity risk factors (sex, body mass index, etc.). Diastolic function indicators, including E/A ratio and left atrial size, also showed marked differences between groups, with the moderate-to-severe subgroup exhibiting larger left atria and a higher proportion of E/A ratio values below 1. Univariate analysis identified 35 MCG parameters that differed between groups, while multivariate regression retained four independent predictors (htrt, tmdf, RS-didma, and qr_rela_dist_neg_mode). ROC analysis indicated that T-wave- and QRS-wave-related indices had moderate predictive value; a combined model incorporating htrt, tmdf, and RS-didma showed superior area under the curve compared to any single parameter.
CONCLUSION: MCG parameters demonstrate distinct characteristics across OSAS severity levels and yield favorable predictive performance for moderate-to-severe OSAS, positioning MCG as a promising non-invasive tool for early diagnosis. The observed changes in diastolic function markers may suggest underlying coronary microcirculatory alterations in patients with moderate-to-severe OSAS. Rigorously designed prospective studies are warranted to validate MCG as a standardized diagnostic modality for OSAS-related coronary microcirculation disorder.

Title: Association of the red cell distribution width/albumin ratio with 6-month readmission risk in heart failure patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Readmission due to heart failure (HF) remains a major clinical and economic challenge. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been proposed as a novel biomarker reflecting chronic inflammation, nutritional status, and multi-organ involvement in cardiovascular diseases. However, the association between RAR and readmission risk, particularly in Asian populations with HF, remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between RAR levels and the 6-month readmission risk among Chinese patients with heart failure.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the Zigong Heart Failure Database, which included 2008 patients hospitalized for HF between December 2016 and June 2019. After excluding patients with missing RDW, albumin, or readmission data, 1854 patients were included in the final analytical cohort. Based on RAR values, patients were divided into four quartiles. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to assess the association between RAR and 6-month readmission risk, adjusting for demographics, clinical parameters, comorbidities, and medications. Subgroup analyses were performed to examine the consistency of associations across different patient characteristics.
RESULTS: The overall 6-month readmission rate was 38.5% (714/1854). Patients in higher RAR quartiles had a significantly greater risk of readmission than those in lower quartiles (P = 0.0025). In unadjusted analyses, each unit increase in RAR was associated with a 57% higher risk of 6-month readmission (HR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.27-1.93, P < 0.001). This association remained significant after adjusting for confounding variables (HR 1.52, 95% CI: 1.21-1.92, P < 0.001). After full adjustment, patients in the highest quartile (Q4) had a 39% higher risk of readmission compared with those in the lowest quartile (Q1) (HR 1.39, 95% CI: 1.10-1.76, P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across sex, age, BMI, NYHA classification, and medication use, with no significant interactions observed.
CONCLUSION: Elevated RAR was independently associated with an increased 6-month readmission risk among Chinese patients with HF. As a simple and cost-effective biomarker, RAR may enhance risk stratification and inform clinical decision-making in HF management, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare burden.

Title: Angiography-derived fractional flow and clinical outcomes in symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To explore the association between fractional flow (FF) and clinical outcomes in patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS), and to evaluate its potential role in patient stratification.
METHODS: This retrospective exploratory study included symptomatic ICAS patients hospitalized between March 2019 and May 2024. FF values were derived from digital subtraction angiography using an angiography-based computational method. Patients were stratified according to a pre-specified FF threshold of 0.76 and treatment modality (interventional vs. conservative). Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) at discharge and 12 months.
RESULTS: Among patients with FF ≤ 0.76, no worsening in mRS between discharge and 12 months was observed in 96.3% of the interventional group and 78.6% of the conservative group (p = 0.017). In a post hoc analysis, improvement of at least one mRS point occurred in 46.3 and 17.9%, respectively; however, discharge mRS scores differed between groups, and the difference in improvement was not statistically significant when the analysis was restricted to patients with discharge mRS ≥ 1. No significant differences in mRS or NIHSS improvement were observed between treatment strategies in patients with FF > 0.76 (p > 0.05). In contrast, stratification based on degree of stenosis (DS% ≥ 70%) did not differentiate clinical outcomes between treatment groups. These findings suggest that FF-based stratification may be associated with differences in functional outcomes across treatment strategies.
CONCLUSION: FF may provide additional information for risk stratification in symptomatic ICAS patients and may help identify clinically relevant subgroups for further evaluation. However, these findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Integrated multi-omics reveals plasma biomarkers of fatigue in HIV immunological non-responders.
Journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the metabolic and inflammatory signatures distinguishing fatigued from non-fatigued HIV immunological non-responders (INRs) and to explore candidate biomarkers and potential mechanistic pathways underlying HIV-associated fatigue.
METHODS: We performed untargeted metabolomics and cytokinomics on plasma obtained from 18 fatigued and 17 non-fatigued HIV-INRs. Mechanistic insights were explored via Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) networks and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses.
RESULTS: Compared to non-fatigued controls, the fatigued cohort showed significant up-regulation of 4-ketopimelic acid, cholesterol, and 1-hexadecyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine, with concurrent down-regulation of DL-arginine and D-pipecolic acid (P < 0.05). Immunologically, the fatigued group displayed elevated macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) but reduced interferon-induced protein 10 (IP-10/CXCL10) and interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels (P < 0.05). Functional enrichment analysis suggested the involvement of necroptosis, lipid metabolism, and atherosclerosis signaling pathways.
CONCLUSION: Fatigue in HIV-INRs receiving long-term antiretroviral therapy was associated with distinct lipidomic and cytokinomic alterations. These results underscore the potential roles of dysregulated fatty acid metabolism, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation in the pathophysiology of fatigue. Cholesterol and IL-18 emerged as candidate biomarkers associated with HIV-associated fatigue; however, their combined discriminatory performance was not statistically validated in this exploratory study and requires confirmation in larger, independent cohorts.

Title: A cross-sectional study on anthropometric indices and hypertension in Chinese adults: comparison of discriminatory power and age-stratified analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension imposes a heavy public health burden in China. Simple anthropometric indicators help screen hypertension risk, yet the optimal index differs by age. This study compares five adiposity indices including WC, BMI, WHtR, ABSI, and BRI and their age-specific discriminatory ability among Chinese adults.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of 104,248 adults from a health check-up cohort in Southwest China, hypertension was defined as blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg, a self-reported diagnosis, or current antihypertensive medication use. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were employed to examine the associations between a one-standard-deviation increase in the Z-score of each index and hypertension prevalence or blood pressure levels. Discriminatory power was compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) overall and within age groups.
RESULTS: Per standard deviation increase, WC, BMI, WHtR, ABSI, and BRI were associated with a 61% (OR 1.61, 95% CI: 1.58-1.64), 61% (1.61, 1.58-1.64), 60% (1.60, 1.57-1.63), 9% (1.09, 1.07-1.11), and 56% (1.56, 1.54-1.59) higher hypertension risk, respectively. WHtR and BRI showed the highest and identical AUC (both 0.676), followed by WC (0.653). ABSI had the lowest AUC (0.612). Discriminatory ability was strongest in adults aged 18-35 years, with WC performing best (AUC = 0.763). The associations for all indices significantly weakened with age (P for interaction < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: WHtR and BRI demonstrated the strongest overall associations with hypertension, whereas WC was the best indicator in young adults. The performance of anthropometric indices varied by age, suggesting that age-specific considerations may enhance their utility for preliminary hypertension risk screening in practice.

Title: Routine laboratory biomarker signature combined with machine learning for rapid differentiation of intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid and reliable differentiation between intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (IS) is essential for appropriate triage and treatment. We aimed to develop and validate a laboratory-based machine learning model using routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to discriminate ICH from IS.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical and laboratory data of 12,213 hospitalized stroke patients (including 3,251 with ICH and 8,962 with IS) and 2,893 hypertensive controls at Xijing Hospital between 2013 and 2023. A temporal validation cohort comprising 153 ICH and 342 IS patients admitted from January to December 2024 was also established. To address class imbalance, BorderlineSMOTE-2 (BS2) was applied. Candidate variables were screened using three feature selection strategies, including RFECV-ADA, Lasso, and Boruta. Six supervised machine learning models were trained using ten-fold cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Feature importance was interpreted using SHAP analysis. Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses were performed as exploratory complementary analyses.
RESULTS: Ten routine laboratory parameters were retained for model construction: white blood cell count, neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, uric acid, total protein, potassium, sodium, chloride, fibrinogen degradation product, and D-Dimer. In the test cohort, the final model (BS2_LightGBM_V10) achieved AUCs of 0.926 for discriminating ICH from IS, 0.979 for discriminating ICH from controls, and 0.923 for discriminating IS from controls. For the three-class classification task (ICH, IS, and controls), the overall accuracy reached 79.07%. SHAP analysis indicated that neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, D-Dimer, and total protein were the most influential predictors. Mendelian randomization analysis suggested that uric acid had a potential causal association with the risk of ICH (OR = 1.309), whereas uric acid (OR = 1.0008), cystatin C (OR = 1.0011), and potassium (OR = 1.0040) had potential causal associations with the risk of IS. Colocalization analysis identified 18 genes linked to uric acid in the context of ICH.
CONCLUSION: A diagnostic model based on ten routine laboratory indicators accurately differentiated ICH from IS. Uric acid may also play a causal role in the pathogenesis of both disorders.

Title: A multicohort proteomics-based machine learning score (MASHPredict) for noninvasive diagnosis and long-term prognostication of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) can progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet the invasiveness of liver biopsy limits its clinical utility. Accurate noninvasive diagnostic tools are essential for improved patient risk stratification.
METHODS: A machine learning study was conducted using plasma proteomics from 142 participants (83 MASH cases, 59 controls) recruited from a Chinese hospital, randomly divided into training and validation cohorts (7:3 ratio). Key proteins were identified via feature selection using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression and the Boruta algorithm. Ten machine learning models were developed to create the MASHPredict score, with external validation in two test cohorts. Prognostic evaluation focused on liver-related events, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)-related mortality, and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: MASHPredict demonstrated robust diagnostic performance, with Area Under the Curve (AUC) values of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.74-0.92) in the training cohort, 0.80 (0.66-0.94) in the validation cohort, 0.79 (0.67-0.91) in test cohort 1, and 0.79 (0.76-0.83) in test cohort 2. It outperformed established noninvasive tests, including the Fibrosis-4 Index, AST to Platelet Ratio Index, AST/ALT Ratio, and NAFLD Fibrosis Score. High-risk individuals exhibited significantly increased hazards for liver-related mortality (HR = 8.18), MASH (HR = 12.07), cirrhosis (HR = 3.37), liver cancer (HR = 3.11), ASCVD-related mortality (HR = 1.64), and all-cause mortality (HR = 1.42) (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The MASHPredict score is a validated, noninvasive diagnostic tool with broad applicability. Its superior performance in diagnosing MASH and prognosticating liver-related outcomes supports its potential role in early detection, risk stratification, and clinical decision-making.

Title: Machine learning predictors of cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy in type 2 diabetes: insights from a prospectively collected single-center registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac autonomic neuropathy (CAN) is a severe complication of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Machine learning (ML) can integrate multidimensional clinical data and identify features associated with CAN. We aimed to characterize predictors of CAN categories using ML.
METHODS: Data were obtained from a prospective single-center observational registry of patients with T2DM undergoing standardized cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (CARTs) based on Ewing's protocol. Demographic, anthropometric, clinical, laboratory, and medication data were analyzed. Patients were classified as CAN0 (no or borderline CAN), CAN1 (early CAN), or CAN2 (definite or severe CAN).
