Three extreme gradient boosting models were evaluated: a CART-inclusive model, a CART-excluded model restricted to patients with T2DM, and a CART-excluded model supplemented with non-diabetic controls without abnormal CART results. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and feature contributions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations values.
RESULTS: Among 693 patients with T2DM, 19 (2.7%) had completely normal autonomic function, whereas 674 (97.3%) exhibited at least one borderline or abnormal CART result. Greater CAN severity was associated with older age, longer diabetes duration, higher systolic blood pressure, and poorer renal function. The CART-inclusive model achieved perfect discrimination in the best iteration (weighted AUC, 1.00; accuracy, 100%), with all five CARTs ranking among the leading predictors. After CART exclusion, performance declined markedly (weighted AUC, 0.64), with class-specific AUCs of 0.59 for CAN0, 0.59 for CAN1, and 0.68 for CAN2. Inclusion of non-diabetic controls improved the weighted AUC to 0.78, with the greatest improvement for CAN0 (AUC, 0.85), followed by CAN2 (0.78) and CAN1 (0.70). Age, diabetes duration, and renal function markers were recurrent non-CART predictors, while anthropometric, hematological, metabolic, and treatment-related features showed category- and model-specific contributions. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection demonstrated substantial overlap among CAN categories, particularly for CAN1.
CONCLUSIONS: CARTs remained essential for accurate CAN classification and staging. Routinely available clinical variables provided complementary phenotypic information but were insufficient to robustly distinguish CAN categories without CART data, particularly CAN0 and CAN1. ML may support multidimensional phenotyping and hypothesis generation but cannot replace standardized autonomic testing.

Title: Atrial Fibrillation in Tribal and Non-tribal Populations: A Comparative Analysis From Eastern India.
Abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasingly prevalent arrhythmia in India, where rheumatic heart disease and cardiometabolic etiologies coexist. This study compared the demographic profile, clinical presentation, associated clinical conditions, echocardiographic characteristics, thromboembolic risk, and anticoagulation practices between tribal patients and non-tribal patients in Eastern India. Methods This retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study included 364 consecutive adult patients with AF (106 tribal and 258 non-tribal patients) admitted between January 2022 and December 2024. Clinical, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and treatment data were extracted from hospital records. Continuous variables were compared using Welch's t-test and categorical variables using Pearson's chi-square test. Results Tribal patients more frequently presented with first-diagnosed AF (81/106, 76.4% vs. 153/258, 59.3%; p = 0.002), higher ventricular rates (112.6 ± 25.1 vs. 102.3 ± 19.6 beats/min; p < 0.001), lower left ventricular ejection fraction (46.0 ± 11.7% vs. 51.0 ± 10.5%; p < 0.001), and more heart failure symptoms at presentation (27/106, 25.4% vs. 41/258, 15.9%; p = 0.033). Lifestyle-related risk factors were significantly more prevalent among tribal patients (79/106, 74.5% vs. 137/258, 53.1%; p < 0.001). Conversely, non-tribal patients had a higher prevalence of cardiometabolic disorders (168/258, 65.1% vs. 43/106, 40.6%; p < 0.001), ischemic cardiovascular disease (69/258, 26.7% vs. 18/106, 17.0%; p = 0.047), chronic kidney disease (93/258, 36.0% vs. 25/106, 23.6%; p = 0.021), higher CHA₂DS₂-VASc scores (2.38 ± 1.66 vs. 1.86 ± 1.45; p = 0.004), and a greater proportion meeting criteria for long-term oral anticoagulation (192/258, 74.4% vs. 67/106, 63.2%; p = 0.032). Rheumatic heart disease, heart failure, left atrial thrombus, ischemic stroke, and anticoagulant prescribing patterns were comparable between the two groups. Conclusions Tribal patients with AF had more first-diagnosed AF, higher ventricular rates, lower left ventricular systolic function, and greater lifestyle-related risk factors, whereas non-tribal patients had greater cardiometabolic and thromboembolic risk. These findings demonstrate differences in the clinical presentation and risk profile of AF within this hospital-based cohort and highlight the need for population-specific strategies to improve AF detection, prevention, and management in Eastern India.

Title: A predictive model for osteoporosis in frail elderly patients with cerebral infarction: an integrated analysis based on machine learning and care-sensitive indicators.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify key risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly patients with frailty and cerebral infarction using three machine learning algorithms-Least Absolute and Selective Operator (LASSO) regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Random Forest (RF)-and establish a risk prediction model to provide data support for clinical prevention.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted using clinical data from 120 elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction admitted to our hospital between April 2024 and October 2025. Patients were categorized into an osteoporosis occurrence group (n=41) and a non-occurrence group (n=79) based on medical records indicating osteoporosis development. Clinical data were collected and compared. Risk factors were screened using "overlap-covering" screening with three machine learning methods: LASSO regression, XGBoost, and RF. The intersecting variables were incorporated into a logistic regression model to analyze risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction. Data analysis was performed using R software. RF to screen risk factors using "overlap coverage." Intersecting variables were incorporated into logistic regression to analyze factors influencing osteoporosis in elderly patients with frailty and cerebral infarction. A nomogram prediction model was developed using R software, internally validated via Bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations), and its predictive accuracy assessed through calibration curves. Clinical utility was evaluated using decision curves.
RESULTS: Significant differences (P < 0.05) were observed between the occurrence and non-occurrence groups in gender, age, affected circulatory system, disease severity, Tilburg Frailty Inventory (TFI) score, Global Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI), Barthel Index, and Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) score. Through machine learning screening using LASSO regression, XGBoost, and RF, five common risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction were identified: age, TFI score, GNRI, Barthel Index, and SAS score as five common risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction. These were incorporated into a logistic regression model. Analysis revealed that age, TFI score, and SAS score were risk factors for osteoporosis in this population (OR = 1.102, 2.876, 1.177, P<0.05). GNRI and Barthel Index were protective factors (OR = 0.913, 0.838, P<0.05). The Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test yielded χ²=2.345, P = 0.969>0.05, indicating acceptable model fit. Based on the logistic regression results, a risk prediction model for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction was constructed using a nomogram. The AUC was 0.955 (95% CI: 0.920-0.991). Calibration curves showed Cox-Snell R² = 0.755 and Nagelkerke R² = 0.546, indicating strong explanatory power and high calibration of the model. The clinical decision curve generally exceeded both extreme curves, demonstrating that the nomogram effectively captured the risk distribution. Nagelkerke R²: 0.546, indicating strong explanatory power and high calibration for the dependent variable. The clinical decision curve generally exceeded both extreme curves, demonstrating that the factors included in the nomogram provide high net benefit for predicting osteoporosis in patients.
CONCLUSION: Key factors influencing osteoporosis development in frail elderly patients with cerebral infarction include age, TFI score, GNRI, Barthel Index, and SAS score. The risk prediction model constructed using these factors demonstrates predictive value, high calibration accuracy, and clinical utility, providing theoretical guidance for clinical practice.

Title: Home-based telerehabilitation after CABG: higher objectively verified adherence and 12-week functional outcomes in a single-center observational cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Home-based telerehabilitation (HBTCR) may address access barriers to center-based cardiac rehabilitation (CBCR) after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, real-world comparative evidence on objectively verified adherence and functional recovery, with careful confounding control, remains sparse. This observational cohort study compared session completion and 12-week functional outcomes between HBTCR and CBCR in post-CABG patients using routine clinical data.
METHODS: This single-center observational cohort screened 288 patients and identified 195 potentially eligible post-CABG patients (February 2024-February 2025). After excluding 28 patients with unresolved rehabilitation exposure, 167 patients (56 HBTCR, 54 CBCR, 57 usual care) formed the propensity-score estimation cohort, adjusted for 25 baseline covariates with generalized propensity scores and overlap weighting. The primary complete-case analysis included 105 patients (35 per group) with complete 12-week follow-up. The primary outcome was objectively verified session completion (% of 36 prescribed sessions). The key clinical outcome was 12-week VO2peak, analyzed via weighted ANCOVA. Results are reported as adjusted differences with 95% CIs.
RESULTS: After weighting, covariates were well balanced (all SMDs <0.10). HBTCR showed significantly higher objectively verified session completion than CBCR (87.7% vs. 78.5%; overlap-weighted difference 9.1 percentage points, 95% CI: 4.4 to 13.7; P < 0.001). The adjusted HBTCR-CBCR difference in 12-week VO2peak was small and not statistically significant (0.17 mL/kg/min, 95% CI: -0.50 to 0.84; P = 0.616). Both active rehabilitation groups showed substantially larger 12-week VO2peak gains than usual care (adjusted differences >4.0 mL/kg/min).
CONCLUSION: Among post-CABG patients who chose HBTCR or CBCR in routine practice, those choosing HBTCR had higher objectively verified session completion and comparable observed 12-week improvement in VO2peak. These findings support HBTCR as a feasible option for patients who prefer or require home-based rehabilitation because of work, travel, or scheduling constraints. Formal equivalence was not tested, and the clinical meaningfulness and cost-effectiveness of this delivery model warrant further evaluation.

Title: Serial fibrosis-4 variability and longitudinal patterns are associated with incident heart failure in type 2 diabetes: a 24-month landmark cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic relevance of serial Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) changes for incident heart failure (HF) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains unclear. We examined whether within-person FIB-4 variability and longitudinal patterns were associated with HF after explicit adjustment for chronological age.
METHODS: Routinely collected clinical data from 2000 to 2025 were analyzed using a 24-month landmark design. FIB-4 measurements from months 0 to 18 defined the exposure, followed by a 6-month lag before HF follow-up. Variability was calculated as the within-person standard deviation of log2-transformed FIB-4. Using a threshold of 2.67, patients were classified as never high, improving from high, worsening to high, or persistently high. Associations with incident HF were estimated using multivariable Cox regression.
RESULTS: Among 8,221 patients, 1,811 developed HF during 50,640 person-years. Greater FIB-4 variability was associated with a higher HF hazard (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.43-2.09). Compared with the never-high pattern, persistent-high FIB-4 (HR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.35-2.20) and worsening to high (HR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.01-1.62) were associated with higher HF hazards, whereas improving from high was not (HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.70-1.28). Adding serial FIB-4 features resulted in a small, statistically uncertain improvement in temporal-validation discrimination (ΔC-index, 0.0069; 95% CI, -0.0043 to 0.0190).
DISCUSSION: Serial FIB-4 variability and persistent elevation were associated with incident HF independently of chronological age. These measures may characterize longitudinal multisystem cardiometabolic burden, but their incremental predictive value was limited. External validation is required before clinical application.

Title: Citrulline Supplementation Improves Aortic Vasodilation and Prevents Aortic Thickening Only in Female Rats.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aging is associated with endothelial dysfunction and vascular remodeling, partly due to reduced nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. l-citrulline, a precursor of l-arginine and NO synthesis, has been proposed as a therapeutic strategy to improve vascular function. This study evaluated the effects of chronic citrulline supplementation on aortic structure and vasodilatory function in adult male and female rats.
METHODS: Eight-month-old male and female Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control or treatment groups. The treated animals received oral malate citrulline (1 g/kg/d) for 12 weeks. We isolated thoracic aortas for histological and morphometric analyses, including tunica media thickness and intima/media ratio. We assessed vascular reactivity in vitro using isolated aortic rings in an organ bath system, measuring acetylcholine (ACh)-induced relaxation following phenylephrine-induced contraction.
RESULTS: Citrulline supplementation significantly improved ACh-induced vasorelaxation in female rats compared with female controls (55.14% ± 4.8% vs 42.4% ± 4.3%, P < .05. No differences in vasorelaxation were observed in males between the treated and control groups. Histological analyses showed that treated females had less disruption of elastic fibers and a thinner minimal intima than controls, whereas males showed no structural differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Citrulline supplementation improves endothelium-dependent vasodilation and may preserve aortic structural integrity in female rats but not in males. These findings suggest a sex-dependent vascular response to citrulline, potentially mediated by differences in NO signaling and hormonal regulation. Citrulline may represent a therapeutic strategy to improve vascular function during aging, particularly in females.
CLINICAL IMPACT: The findings may guide clinical trials investigating how hormonal status and nitric oxide signaling affect the efficacy of citrulline supplementation in female patients. Ultimately, these insights could establish citrulline as a targeted, preventive intervention to preserve aortic structural integrity and reduce cardiovascular disease risk in the aging female population.

Title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
Journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited.
METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.
RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68).
DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

Title: Left ventricular geometry as a risk factor for recurrent subaortic stenosis after primary resection.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discrete subaortic stenosis is a progressive cause of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in children, and recurrence after surgical resection is not uncommon. We evaluated echocardiographic and morphologic factors associated with reintervention after primary subaortic membrane resection.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of paediatric patients (0-14 years) who underwent primary surgical resection of subaortic membrane stenosis between 2002 and 2019. Demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic variables were compared between patients requiring reintervention and those requiring a single operation. Independent predictors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Seventy-seven patients were included; 16 required reintervention and 61 did not. On univariate analysis, the reintervention group had higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak and mean gradients and shorter membrane length. In multivariable analysis, shorter membrane length independently predicted reintervention (adjusted odds ratio 0.677 per 1-mm increase, 95% confidence interval 0.487-0.941; p = 0.020), as did higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient (adjusted odds ratio 1.066 per 1-mmHg increase, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.111; p = 0.002). A smaller aorto-septal angle showed a trend towards increased risk but did not reach statistical significance (adjusted odds ratio 0.933, 95% confidence interval 0.866-1.005; p = 0.067). Aortic regurgitation was significantly worse at follow-up in patients requiring reintervention.
CONCLUSION: Shorter subaortic membrane length and higher preoperative left ventricular outflow tract peak gradient were independent predictors of reintervention after primary resection. These findings may improve risk stratification and support closer echocardiographic surveillance of patients at increased risk of recurrence.

Title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
Abstract: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

Title: The impact of defects of the atrial septum on procedural complexity, complications, and outcomes of transvenous lead extraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with defects of the atrial septum (DAS) undergoing transvenous lead extraction (TLE) may be at increased risk of systemic embolism due to transient right-to-left shunting. However, data on the prevalence and clinical relevance of DAS in patients undergoing TLE remain limited.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 3637 patients undergoing TLE between 2006 and 2024 with complete preprocedural assessment of the atrial septum and at least 3 years of follow-up. We evaluated the prevalence of DAS and its association with procedural complexity, major complications, and survival.
RESULTS: DAS was identified in 3.71% of patients. Patent foramen ovale was present in 2.45%, secundum atrial septal defect in 1.15%, and both defects in 0.08%. Most defects were small, with predominant left-to-right shunting. Patients with DAS more frequently had lead-related infective endocarditis and vegetations on transesophageal echocardiography (p < 0.001). TLE procedures in patients with DAS were more complex, with longer extraction times and more frequent use of advanced extraction tools. Despite higher predicted procedural risk, the incidence of major complications, including stroke, was low. DAS was not associated with increased in-hospital, 30-day, 1-year, or 3-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large TLE cohort, DAS was uncommon and associated with greater procedural complexity, but not with a higher incidence of major complications or worse long-term survival. Clinically apparent systemic embolic events were rare.

Title: Does thrombocytopenia predict short-term mortality after transcatheter and surgical aortic valve replacement?
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postprocedural thrombocytopenia is frequently observed after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and surgical aortic valve replacement (sAVR), but its independent prognostic value remains unclear. We investigated whether platelet reduction after TAVI and sAVR independently predicts short-term mortality beyond baseline procedural risk.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients who underwent aortic valve replacement between 2015 and 2020. Sixty-seven patients underwent TAVI and 149 underwent sAVR. Mechanical valve recipients were retained in the overall cohort but excluded from the primary TAVI-sAVR comparison. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to reduce baseline differences between groups. Longitudinal changes in platelet count (PLT), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) were evaluated using generalized estimating equation models, and factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using Firth penalized logistic regression.
RESULTS: The primary comparative cohort included 67 TAVI and 93 sAVR patients. After overlap weighting, adequate balance was achieved for all measured baseline covariates. Significant treatment × time interactions were observed for PLT (p = 0.001), NLR (p < 0.001), and PLR (p = 0.002). On postprocedural day 3, moderate thrombocytopenia was more frequent after sAVR than TAVI (33.5% vs. 8.3%), whereas normal platelet levels were more frequent after TAVI (45.6% vs. 8.2%; overall p < 0.001). Weighted 90-day mortality did not differ significantly between TAVI and sAVR (12.6% vs. 17.5%, p = 0.487). In Firth regression models, only EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with 90-day mortality.
CONCLUSION: Postprocedural platelet and inflammatory responses showed different temporal patterns after TAVI and sAVR. However, these biomarker changes were not independently associated with 90-day mortality after adjustment, whereas EuroSCORE II remained independently associated with mortality. Serial hematological changes should therefore be interpreted together with baseline clinical risk rather than as isolated prognostic markers.

Title: In Situ Fenestration-Assisted TEVAR in Patients With Complex Pathology Involving the Aortic Arch.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the feasibility, safety, and short-term clinical outcomes of in situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (ISF-TEVAR) employing an electrocautery-connected guidewire combined with a novel, pump-less, extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass for cerebral perfusion in patients with complex aortic arch pathology.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration. Fenestrations were performed with an electrocautery-connected 0.018-inch chronic total occlusion-dedicated guidewire. Patients' demographics, procedural details, perioperative outcomes, and early follow-up data were analyzed, with stratification according to the number of fenestrated supra-aortic branches.
RESULTS: A total of 37 supra-aortic branches were targeted: 3-branch fenestrations in 6 patients (31.6%), 2-branch in 6 patients (31.6%), and single-branch in 7 patients (36.8%). Technical success, defined as successful graft fenestration with patent branches on completion angiography, was achieved in 94.5% (35/37). One failed innominate artery fenestration was managed with chimney-assisted TEVAR, and 1 left subclavian artery fenestration was successfully completed in a subsequent procedure. Operative time increased with procedural complexity (140 ± 12 minutes for 1 branch, 152 ± 10 minutes for 2 branches, and 162 ± 13 minutes for 3 branches; P = .004). No intraprocedural mortality occurred. Two perioperative strokes (10.5%) and 2 in-hospital deaths (10.5%) were recorded, 1 death was due to vertebrobasilar stroke and the other due to retrograde type A aortic dissection with rupture. Median hospital stay was 8 days. During a mean follow-up of 9.2 months, there was no aorta-related mortality, with an overall survival rate of 89.5%. All stented branches remained patent, and 2 endoleaks (10.5%) were successfully treated endovascularly.
CONCLUSION: In situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair using an electrocautery-connected wire combined with a temporary, pressure gradient-driven extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass is a feasible, reproducible, and safe technique for complex aortic arch repair. This fully percutaneous approach ensures continuous cerebral perfusion, demonstrates efficient procedural metrics, and yields favorable short-term outcomes, representing a practical alternative when custom-made devices or hybrid surgical procedures are not available.Clinical ImpactIn situ fenestration-assisted TEVAR combined with a temporary pumpless extracorporeal femoral-carotid bypass enables continuous cerebral perfusion during complex aortic arch interventions without the need for cardiopulmonary bypass or surgical debranching. This technique expands the feasibility of fully endovascular multibranch arch repair in urgent or anatomically challenging cases where custom-made devices are unavailable. For clinicians, this approach offers a practical and reproducible strategy to mitigate cerebral ischemic risk while maintaining procedural efficiency and percutaneous access. This technique may facilitate broader adoption of in situ fenestration by providing a cerebral protection strategy using readily available endovascular equipment.

Title: Determinants of MASLD and liver fibrosis in maintenance hemodialysis: a prospective evaluation of metabolic, nutritional, and volume-related factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is underrecognized in hemodialysis (HD) patients, yet its evaluation is confounded by volume fluctuations. We aimed to determine the prevalence of MASLD and advanced fibrosis using transient elastography (TE), identify their metabolic, nutritional, and volume-related determinants, and assess the impact of a single HD session on controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM).
METHODS: Forty adult patients on maintenance HD for ≥ 3 months were enrolled in this prospective cross-sectional study. TE was performed immediately before and after a midweek dialysis session. Steatosis was defined as CAP > 257 dB/m and advanced fibrosis as LSM ≥ 8 kPa. Volume status was assessed by interdialytic weight gain (IDWG) and ultrafiltration (UF) volume. Associations with clinical, biochemical, and dialysis-related variables were analyzed.
RESULTS: The study cohort had a mean age of 63.5 ± 17.3 years, with males comprising 70% and diabetic patients accounting for 30% of the population. MASLD prevalence was 25% pre-HD and 22.5% post-HD; advanced fibrosis prevalence was 17.5% pre-HD and 10% post-HD. CAP and LSM did not change significantly with fluid removal (p = 0.877 and p = 0.962, respectively). CAP correlated positively with body mass index, IDWG, UF volume, and triglycerides, and negatively with serum albumin. Post-HD LSM showed a strong inverse association with serum albumin and positive associations with alanine aminotransferase, total cholesterol, and LDL-cholesterol, whereas pre-HD LSM was predominantly linked to age and bilirubin. The FIB-4 index did not correlate with LSM.
CONCLUSIONS: MASLD and advanced fibrosis are highly prevalent in maintenance HD patients. TE provides a clinically valuable, volume-independent assessment of liver disease, outperforming FIB-4 in this setting. Low albumin and dyslipidemia emerge as key correlates of fibrosis, highlighting the interplay between malnutrition, metabolic risk, and liver stiffness in end-stage renal disease.

Title: Preoperative empagliflozin and ventricular remodeling after coronary artery bypass grafting in type 2 diabetes: a prespecified analysis of the POST-CABGDM randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and coronary artery disease (CAD) are associated with adverse ventricular remodeling. Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) may further contribute to myocardial injury through inflammatory and ischemia-reperfusion mechanisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardioprotective effects, including reduction in left ventricular mass, but their impact in the perioperative setting of cardiac surgery remains unclear.
METHODS: This study is a prespecified secondary analysis of the open-label randomized POST-CABGDM trial (NCT04523064). Patients with T2DM and multivessel CAD undergoing CABG with CPB were randomized to receive empagliflozin 25 mg once daily or standard antidiabetic therapy. SGLT2i were discontinued 3 days before surgery and were not protocol-mandated postoperatively. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively and at 1-6 months postoperatively. The primary endpoint was the change in left ventricular mass index (ΔLVMI). Secondary endpoints included changes in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF) and ventricular dimensions.
RESULTS: A total of 118 patients were included (53 in the intervention group and 65 in the control group). Baseline characteristics were well balanced. No significant difference was observed in ΔLVMI between groups (- 1.39 ± 18.7 vs. -4.55 ± 16.8 g/m²; p = 0.337), and this finding remained unchanged after adjustment for baseline LVMI. Similarly, no differences were found in ΔLVEF or ventricular dimensions. Surgical characteristics and postoperative complications were comparable. In a separate exploratory, non-randomized multivariable analysis, continued use of SGLT2i during follow-up was associated with a higher likelihood of LVMI reduction (OR 4.69; 95% CI 1.20-18.40; p = 0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative empagliflozin use was not associated with significant short-term changes in LVMI, LVEF, or ventricular dimensions after CABG with CPB. Exploratory, non-randomized analyses suggested an association between continued SGLT2i use during follow-up and LVMI reduction, but these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies designed to evaluate sustained perioperative and postoperative therapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04523064.

Title: The cardiac intervention imaging clinical trial of an intracardiac ultrasound catheter and ultrasound system: the multicenter, randomized, INTELICE trial protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) plays an increasingly important role in guiding cardiac interventional procedures. However, evidence from randomized studies comparing different ICE catheter systems is limited, and standardized criteria for ICE image quality assessment are lacking. The INTELICE trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a novel Arch Echo™ intracardiac ultrasound catheter and ultrasound system compared with a commercially available ICE system.
METHODS: INTELICE is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label, non-inferiority clinical trial with blinded outcome evaluation. Adult patients undergoing cardiac interventional procedures requiring ICE guidance are eligible for enrollment. Participants are randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either the Arch Echo™ ICE catheter with its dedicated ultrasound system or the ACUSON AcuNav catheter paired with the P500 ultrasound system. A standardized ICE imaging protocol is applied across all participating centers. The primary endpoint is ICE image quality, assessed using a predefined 1-5 scoring system by independent core-laboratory sonographers who are blinded to device allocation. Secondary endpoints include operator-assessed image quality, procedural success, catheter delivery to target positions, procedure duration, and safety outcomes.
DISCUSSION: The INTELICE trial will provide high-quality comparative evidence on ICE image performance and procedural safety between a novel ICE catheter system and an established commercial device. In addition, this study aims to establish standardized criteria for ICE image quality assessment and to explore differences between operator-based and sonographer-based evaluations, which may improve the consistency and reliability of ICE-guided cardiac interventions.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06344494.

Title: Bilateral cortical network disruptions in the rat caudal forelimb area after unilateral stroke.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate how ischemic stroke alters neural activity in the caudal forelimb area (CFA) and identify electrophysiological mechanisms underlying post-stroke motor deficits.
METHODS: Local field potentials were recorded bilaterally from ipsilateral and contralateral CFA in rats under anesthesia and during a single-pellet retrieval task. Analyses included spectral power across canonical frequency bands, aperiodic 1/f slope characterization of excitation-inhibition balance, and cross-frequency coupling assessment of interhemispheric coordination.
RESULTS: Stroke induced widespread bilateral disruptions in oscillatory dynamics across delta, theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands. The aperiodic 1/f slope shifted, reflecting altered excitation-inhibition balance. Cross-frequency coupling between hemispheres, particularly low-frequency phase to gamma amplitude, was reorganized, indicating impaired interhemispheric coordination and bilateral motor network imbalance. Notably, the main experimental cohort did not include a sham-operated control group; however, a pilot experiment with three sham and three MCAO animals, conducted using identical procedures, provided supportive evidence for the stability of key measures under sham conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that ischemic stroke induces coordinated alterations in spectral organization, excitation-inhibition balance, and cross-frequency interactions within the bilateral caudal forelimb cortex. These findings indicate that post-stroke motor dysfunction arises from disrupted, state-dependent dynamics of distributed motor networks rather than isolated changes within the lesioned hemisphere.

Title: Circulating sphingomyelins and mortality in a community-based Korean cohort: the Korean Genome and epidemiology study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating sphingomyelins (SMs) have been proposed as biomarkers of mortality and cardiovascular risk, but findings have varied across populations. We aimed to evaluate the associations in a community-based Korean cohort.
METHODS: This cohort study included 2,434 participants from the Ansan-Ansung cohort of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study. Seven SM species were measured at the 2005-2006 examination, and mortality data were linked through December 2024. Associations with all-cause, cardiovascular, and non-cardiovascular mortality and the composite cardiovascular outcome were examined using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, clinical and laboratory factors. Multiple testing was addressed using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure across 28 tests within each adjustment model.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 18.5 years, 426 deaths occurred, including 79 cardiovascular deaths. In the fully adjusted model, higher SM 16:0 levels were nominally associated with all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.70; 95% CI, 1.07-2.70; P = 0.025), but the association was not statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. None of the seven SM species were significantly associated with all-cause, cardiovascular, or non-cardiovascular mortality or with the composite cardiovascular outcome after correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: In this community-based Korean cohort, circulating SMs were not significantly associated with mortality or cardiovascular outcomes. This suggests that the prognostic relevance of circulating SMs may be limited and may vary according to population characteristics.

Title: Early outcomes of switching from bevacizumab to aflibercept-jbvf in exudative macular diseases: a real-world study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate very early anatomical and functional outcomes following a switch from intravitreal bevacizumab to aflibercept-jbvf in patients with exudative macular diseases.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, single-arm interventional cohort study included 53 eyes of 41 patients with diabetic macular edema (DME), macular neovascularization (MNV) secondary to neovascular age-related macular degeneration, or retinal vein occlusion (RVO). This heterogeneous cohort comprised biologically distinct disease entities; therefore, diagnosis-specific analyses were considered exploratory. All eyes received three monthly intravitreal bevacizumab injections followed by a single aflibercept-jbvf injection. Primary outcomes were changes in BCVA and CST from the post-bevacizumab preswitch baseline, assessed immediately before aflibercept-jbvf administration, to 4 weeks after the injection. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for paired comparisons, and generalized estimating equation models accounted for within-patient intereye correlation in bilateral cases.
RESULTS: Among 53 eyes, 30 (56.6%) had DME, 18 (34.0%) had MNV, and five (9.4%) had RVO. Median CST decreased from 312 μm (IQR, 275-354 μm) at preswitch baseline to 291 μm (IQR, 255-322 μm) at week 4. The mean CST change was - 22.6 ± 68.1 μm (95% CI, - 40.9 to - 4.2; p = 0.001). Median BCVA was 0.699 logMAR at both the post-bevacizumab preswitch baseline (IQR, 0.495-1.000) and week 4 (IQR, 0.398-1.000). The mean BCVA change was - 0.051 ± 0.230 logMAR (95% CI, - 0.114 to + 0.013; p = 0.129). In the GEE analyses, CST reduction remained statistically significant (p = 0.005), whereas BCVA change was not significant after adjustment for within-patient intereye correlation (β = -0.051; p = 0.065). No serious adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSION: Administration of aflibercept-jbvf following three monthly bevacizumab injections was temporally associated with a statistically significant but modest very early reduction in CST at 4 weeks in this heterogeneous cohort of exudative macular diseases. Because DME, neovascular AMD-related MNV, and RVO represent biologically and clinically distinct disease entities, the pooled findings should be interpreted as descriptive cohort-level estimates within this shared treatment pathway rather than as evidence of a uniform treatment effect across these conditions. A small numerical trend toward BCVA improvement was observed, but the change was not statistically significant in either the unadjusted or GEE-adjusted analysis. Because this was a single-arm study without a comparator group, the observed anatomical change cannot be attributed specifically to aflibercept-jbvf and may partly reflect a delayed or cumulative response to prior bevacizumab, regression to the mean, or natural variability in retinal thickness. Diagnosis-specific findings were exploratory, and the 4-week endpoint does not provide information regarding durability of response or longer-term treatment burden.

Title: Risk factors of recurrent hemorrhage following minimally invasive transcranial puncture and drainage in patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the risk factors for recurrent hemorrhage in patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) following minimally invasive transcranial puncture and drainage using a YL-1 hard-channel approach.
METHODS: Clinical data, CT imaging data, and follow-up information for patients with sICH who were continuously admitted to the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2021 to June 2025 were extracted from our hospital information system. All patients underwent minimally invasive transcranial puncture and drainage using a YL-1 hard-channel approach under CT guidance. Patients were categorized according to the occurrence of recurrent hemorrhage following surgery. Statistical analyses were conducted on the patients' general clinical data, CT imaging data, and follow-up data. Univariate analysis and stepwise multivariate regression analysis were employed to identify relevant risk factors for postoperative recurrent hemorrhage (PRH). Additionally, the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) was utilized to further examine the independent risk factors and determine the cut-off value for predicting outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 159 patients was included in this study. Among them, 24 (15.1%) patients experienced recurrent hemorrhage after surgery. Univariate analysis indicated that a higher preoperative body mass index (BMI) (P = 0.049), a larger postoperative dosage of urokinase (UK) (P = 0.026), and a shorter time from onset to puncture (OPT) (P = 0.001) were statistically associated with PRH. Among the preoperative CT imaging parameters, irregular hematoma shape (P = 0.002) and the blend sign (P = 0.001) were also statistically correlated with PRH. Multivariate binary logistic stepwise regression analysis revealed that a shorter OPT (OR = 1.223, 95% CI = 1.080-1.386, P = 0.002) and irregular hematoma shape (OR = 7.110, 95% CI = 1.840-17.473, P = 0.004) were independent risk factors for PRH. Conversely, the blend sign was associated with a reduced risk for PRH. (OR = 0.073, 95% CI = 0.012-0.108, P < 0.001). Additionally, plotting the ROC curve for OPT yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.840, with an exploratory threshold of 10.5 h, corresponding to a sensitivity of 0.958 and a specificity of 0.778.
CONCLUSION: A shorter OPT and an irregular hematoma shape are independent risk factors for recurrent hemorrhage following minimally invasive transcranial puncture and drainage using a YL-1 hard-channel approach in patients with sICH. In contrast, the blend sign may be associated to a lower risk of PRH. And these findings warrant further validation through external studies.

Title: Metabolic score for visceral fat as a predictor of new-onset cardiovascular disease in patients with metabolic syndrome: a validation study in two prospective cohorts (UK Biobank and CHARLS).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) substantially increases cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. The metabolism score for visceral fat (METS-VF) is a novel assessment tool that may substitute visceral adipose tissue measurement. This study investigated the association between METS-VF and new-onset CVD in MetS patients.
METHODS: The data from two prospective cohorts: UK Biobank (UKB) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Multivariate Cox regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses assessed the association between METS-VF and new-onset CVD. The interaction between METS-VF and the CVD polygenic risk score (PRS) was analyzed in the UKB to assess genetic contributions. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to evaluate the discriminative capability of METS-VF for new-onset CVD. Subgroup analyses were performed to confirm the robustness of the results.
RESULTS: A total of 101,292 individuals from the UK Biobank and 1,680 individuals from CHARLS were included. The median follow-up periods were 14.6 years in UKB and 5.0 years in CHARLS. High METS-VF was significantly associated with an increased risk of new-onset CVD in both UKB (HR = 1.63, 95% CI: 1.56-1.71) and CHARLS (HR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.52-2.94) compared with low METS-VF. Individuals with the highest METS-VF and high genetic risk exhibited the highest risk of new-onset CVD (HR = 2.36, 95% CI: 2.14-2.61).
CONCLUSIONS: METS-VF is a valuable indicator for predicting new-onset CVD in individuals with MetS, providing new insights into the prevention and management of CVD in high-risk populations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

Title: Time to diabetic retinopathy and its prognostic factors among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Johor, Malaysia from 2015 to 2019: a retrospective cohort study using surveillance data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy is a major microvascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus and remains a leading cause of preventable visual impairment worldwide. Understanding the time to onset of diabetic retinopathy and its prognostic factors is essential to optimise screening strategies and guide early intervention. This study aimed to determine the time to development of diabetic retinopathy and identify its associated prognostic factors among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Johor, Malaysia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using secondary data from the National Diabetes Registry in Johor, Malaysia. Adults aged ≥ 18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus who had no documented diabetic retinopathy DR at cohort entry were included. Cohort entry was defined as the first eligible National Diabetes Registry registration/assessment date between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2019. Participants were followed until first documented diabetic retinopathy, death, loss to follow-up, transfer out, or 31 December 2019, whichever occurred first. Baseline sociodemographic, clinical, treatment-related and complication variables were evaluated. Kaplan-Meier methods, Log-rank test, and Cox regression analyses were used to evaluate time to first documented diabetic retinopathy and its prognostic factors.
RESULTS: Of 50,457 registry records initially identified, 1,056 duplicate records were removed. After excluding 1,448 records with incomplete eligibility, outcome or key baseline information, 47,953 participants were included in the original analytic dataset. Of these, 6,402 (13.3%) had a diabetic retinopathy diagnosis recorded in the registry and 41,551 (86.7%) were censored. Following verification of temporal eligibility and exclusion of 6,401 prevalent diabetic retinopathy records recorded before or at cohort entry, 41,552 participants contributed 64,551.7 person-years of follow-up, during which one incident diabetic retinopathy event occurred. Median follow-up estimated using the reverse Kaplan-Meier method was 6.1 months (IQR 5.3-29.0; range 3.2-113.4 months). duration of diabetes greater than 10 years (AHR = 1.96, 95% CI: 1.79-2.14), hypertension (AHR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.10-1.31), dyslipidaemia (AHR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.16-1.34), high waist circumference (AHR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.02-1.14), positive urine protein (AHR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.04-1.15), poor glycaemic control (AHR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.03-1.20), and complications such as nephropathy (AHR = 1.78, 95% CI: 1.69-1.88) and diabetic foot ulcer (AHR = 1.92, 95% CI: 1.67-2.20) were independently associated with an increased risk of diabetic retinopathy.
CONCLUSIONS: Diabetic retinopathy develops within a relatively short duration following type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosis and is influenced by a combination of metabolic, clinical, and complication-related factors. Early risk stratification and integrated management of modifiable risk factors are essential to delay the onset of diabetic retinopathy. These findings provide important real-world evidence to support targeted screening and public health strategies in Malaysia.

Title: Association of medical visit frequency with cardiovascular events and mortality in patients with dyslipidaemia: a cohort study using a Japanese claims database.
Journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dyslipidaemia is a major risk factor for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases; however, the optimal frequency of medical visits remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether medical visit frequency is associated with the incidence of cardiac events, cerebrovascular events, and mortality among patients initiating lipid-lowering therapy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the Shizuoka Kokuho Database between April 1, 2012, and September 30, 2021. Patients initiating lipid-lowering therapy were classified into high-frequency (≥ 22 visits in 2 years) and low-frequency (8-12 visits in 2 years) groups. After 1:3 propensity score matching and exclusion of patients with events within 2 years, 1,435 patients in the low-frequency group and 4,412 in the high-frequency group were analysed.
RESULTS: Over a mean follow-up of 5.3 years, composite outcomes occurred in 5.6% of both groups (hazard ratio [HR] 1.08; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84-1.38; p = 0.571). No significant differences were observed for cardiac events (HR 1.13; 95% CI 0.83-1.54), cerebrovascular events (HR 1.13; 95% CI 0.67-1.90), or mortality (HR 0.94; 95% CI 0.60-1.48).
CONCLUSION: Less frequent visits were not associated with increased risks of cardiovascular events or mortality. Extending visit intervals may therefore be a reasonable option for selected stable patients receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention.

Title: Pharmacologic prevention of cardiotoxicity in breast cancer: a Bayesian network meta-analysis and meta-regression.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer therapy related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is a major concern in breast cancer patients, often reducing left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and causing symptomatic heart failure. This study assessed the comparative effectiveness and safety of cardioprotective drugs in preserving LVEF during chemotherapy.
METHODS: Our database search, included Cochrane, PubMed, WOS, and SCOPUS, from inception to May 1st, 2024, to find randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that assessed the effectiveness and safety of cardioprotective drugs in breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy. Bayesian network meta-analysis and meta-regression were performed using the BUGSnet package in R studio version 4.4.2, applying a random-effects model, and mean differences (MD) with 95% credible intervals (CrI) were calculated.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs involving 2,223 patients, met the inclusion criteria. Participants had a mean age was 48.78 (SD: 9.7). Spironolactone provided the greatest improvement in LVEF compared to placebo MD: 12.80; 95% CrI: 5.99 to 19.60, with the highest SUCRA value (97.84). Nebivolol ranked second (MD: 7.30; 95% CrI: 0.34 to 14.25; SUCRA: 81.67), while lisinopril + bisoprolol showed modest benefit (MD: 5.25; 95% CrI: -1.57 to 12.06; SUCRA: 69.43). Other agents, including rosuvastatin, bisoprolol, and candesartan, had variable effects with wide CrIs, and carvedilol and metoprolol showed limited efficacy. Model diagnostics confirmed stable convergence, good model fit, and no significant inconsistency across comparisons. Covariate-adjusted effect size from Bayesian network meta-regression identified hypertension prevalence and sample size as significant positive modifiers of treatment effect. Sensitivity analyses using a leave-one-out approach confirmed the robustness of the findings.
CONCLUSION: Spironolactone and nebivolol are promising candidates for preserving LVEF in breast cancer patients undergoing cardiotoxic chemotherapy, while metoprolol showed minimal benefit. However, further studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up are essential to validate these results and assess long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Neuropathological and vascular determinants of cerebral amyloid angiopathy risk: evidence from the NACC cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is strongly associated with Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic changes (ADNC), but its links with other brain pathologies remain unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a clinicopathological study of 3,267 participants from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) cohort. Neuropathological evaluations included potential risk factors for CAA, such as ADNC, Lewy body pathology (LBP), frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), and other neuropathologies.
RESULTS: We found that ADNC and LBP were associated with increased odds of CAA, with the risk increasing according to ADNC severity and in cases of limbic/amygdala-predominant LBP. In contrast, FTLD, particularly the FTLD-TDP subtype, was inversely associated with CAA. Among other neuropathologies, CAA was positively associated with microinfarcts, arteriolosclerosis, white matter rarefaction, and hippocampus/cortical atrophy, but inversely associated with lobar atrophy and higher brain weight. In addition, APOE ε4 carriers with mixed ADNC, LBP, and FTLD exhibited the highest risk. Stronger associations between ADNC and CAA were observed in participants aged < 80 years and in males, whereas females demonstrated greater vulnerability to vascular- and atrophy-related correlates. Several neuropathology-CAA associations were also more pronounced among APOE ε4 carriers.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the interplay of neurodegenerative, vascular, sex, and APOE ε4 in CAA susceptibility, with implications for risk stratification.

Title: B‑lines on lung ultrasound: a non‑invasive marker for short‑term outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications increase morbidity and mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Lung ultrasound detection of B-lines is an established method to quantify pulmonary congestion, and while B-lines have been studied as predictive markers in heart failure and general critical care settings, their role in predicting outcomes specifically for post-CABG patients remains inadequately defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between B-lines detected on postoperative lung ultrasound and 30-day mortality and hospital length of stay in patients undergoing isolated CABG.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted in a single-center intensive care unit between 2023 and 2024. A total of 148 adult patients scheduled for elective CABG were enrolled. Lung ultrasound was performed on postoperative days 1 (POD1) and 3 (POD3) using a standardized 8-zone protocol to quantify B-lines. The primary outcomes were all-cause 30-day mortality, assessed via hospital records and telephone follow-up, and total hospital length of stay. Univariate and multivariate logistic and linear regression analyses were used to identify predictors.
RESULTS: The mean patient age was 60.15 ± 9.8 years, and 57% were male. Within 30 days, 22 patients (15%) died. In the multivariate logistic regression, the number of B-lines on POD1 was an independent predictor of 30-day mortality (Adjusted Odds Ratio: 1.090, 95% CI: 1.018-1.167, p = 0.013), indicating a 9% increase in the odds of death for each additional B-line. In contrast, the B-line count on POD3 was not significantly associated with mortality. B-line counts on both days were also not associated with hospital length of stay. Instead, higher body mass index (β = 0.22, p = 0.022) and a history of smoking (β = 2.20, p = 0.020) were independently associated with longer hospitalization.
CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative pulmonary congestion, as quantified by B-lines on POD1 lung ultrasound, is an independent predictor of 30-day mortality after CABG. Routine bedside lung ultrasound on the first day after surgery can serve as a non-invasive tool to stratify high-risk patients, potentially allowing for earlier intervention to optimize fluid status and improve outcomes.

Title: Cerebrovascular stenosis and mortality after isolated off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebrovascular atherosclerosis is common in patients undergoing coronary revascularization. Although carotid artery disease has been extensively studied, the association between vertebral artery stenosis and long-term outcomes after isolated off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) remains uncertain.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing isolated OPCABG at a tertiary cardiac center between January 2018 and July 2021. Preoperative bilateral carotid and vertebral artery duplex ultrasonography was reviewed. Severe cerebrovascular stenosis was defined as 70%-99% luminal narrowing or complete occlusion involving at least one extracranial carotid or vertebral artery. The primary outcome was long-term all-cause mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate associations with mortality. In-hospital postoperative cerebral infarction and 30-day all-cause mortality were additionally summarized.
RESULTS: Among 1,277 patients, 186 (14.6%) had severe cerebrovascular stenosis, including 100 with severe carotid disease and 109 with severe vertebral disease; 23 patients had both. During a median follow-up of 4.79 years, 87 deaths occurred. Severe carotid stenosis was associated with worse unadjusted survival (log-rank P = 0.028) but was not independently associated with mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR], 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-2.13; P = 0.196). Severe vertebral stenosis (HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.22-2.84; P = 0.004) and any severe cerebrovascular stenosis (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.21-2.37; P = 0.002) were independently associated with mortality. In-hospital postoperative cerebral infarction (5.91% vs. 0.55%; P < 0.001) and 30-day mortality (4.84% vs. 1.65%; P = 0.011) were more frequent among patients with severe cerebrovascular stenosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Severe cerebrovascular stenosis was associated with increased long-term mortality after isolated OPCABG. Severe vertebral artery stenosis showed the strongest association and may represent a marker of more extensive systemic atherosclerotic disease. These findings support consideration of both carotid and vertebral territories during preoperative vascular assessment, while prospective studies are needed to determine clinical utility.

Title: Improvement in naming with tDCS and alteration of functional connectivity in post-stroke aphasia: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the effects of anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (A-tDCS) over the left Sylvian parietal temporal region (SPT) on picture naming and auditory comprehension, as well as changes in brain functional connectivity in post-stroke aphasic patients.
METHODS: This is a double-blind, sham-controlled, randomized controlled study. Sixty aphasic patients were randomly assigned to receive either active or sham tDCS over the SPT as well as speech-language therapy for four weeks. Standardized aphasia assessments and electroencephalogram (EEG) examinations were conducted before and after the treatment. The EEG nonlinear index of cross approximate entropy (C-ApEn) was used to assess brain functional connectivity.
RESULTS: The tDCS group demonstrated significantly greater improvements than the control group in both picture naming and auditory word-picture identification scores (p < 0.001). Regression analysis revealed that the group (tDCS/control) was the primary factor associated with improving picture naming. The functional connectivity of F3-P3, F7-P3, T3-T5, T5-P3, T5-C3, T4-T6, T3-T4, and T5-T6 significantly increased following tDCS.
CONCLUSIONS: Anodal tDCS over the left SPT can improve picture naming and auditory comprehension in subacute post-stroke aphasia. Potential mechanisms include enhanced connectivity within the left-hemisphere dorsal/ventral streams, the executive control network, and between the bilateral temporal lobes. These functional connectivity changes provide neural evidence for the effect of tDCS on naming improvement. Clinical trial registry number ChiCTR-TRC-14005072.

Title: Self-care recovery after ischemic stroke: a quasi-experimental comparison of two psychological interventions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke patients often experience cognitive, psychological, and self-care impairments. Comparative evidence on mindfulness-based interventions and cognitive rehabilitation interventions remains limited. This study compared two psychological interventions (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) and Cognitive Rehabilitation Therapy (CRT)) on post-stroke recovery outcomes.
METHOD: In this quasi-experimental study, 61 ischemic stroke patients were allocated to MBSR, CRT, or control groups. Outcomes included self-care, psychological status, and cognitive function assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up. Data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Both MBSR and CRT were associated with significant improvements in psychological and self-care outcomes compared with the control group (p < 0.05). MBSR was associated with greater improvement in cognitive outcomes compared to CRT (p < 0.05). Clinically meaningful improvements were observed in intervention groups based on MCID thresholds.
CONCLUSION: Both interventions were associated with improved psychological and self-care outcomes after stroke, while MBSR was associated with greater improvements in cognitive function. Further randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these findings.

Title: Joint association of LDL cholesterol and inflammation with mortality and the modifying effect of physical activity: findings from two population-based cohort studies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and inflammation are two main factors contributing to risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. However, their joint associations remain controversial, and it is unknown whether physical activity (PA) can modify these associations.
METHODS: A total of 18,416 US adults with a total of 150047.8 person-years follow-up from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) including general population, patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and individuals at extreme risk, and 2575 Chinese adults with a total of 10736.8 person-years follow-up from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) including general population and patients with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) were analyzed. Restricted cubic spline, Cox regression models, and mediation analyses were employed to estimate associations between PA, LDL-C, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in the NHANES/platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) in the CLHLS, and the risk of mortality from all-cause and CVD.
RESULTS: The combined effects were significant, which included LDL-C with SII on mortality from all-cause and CVD among the general population and ASCVD patients in the NHANES, and LDL-C with PLR on all-cause mortality among NCDs patients in the CLHLS. Compared with participants with LDL-C in tertile 2 (T2) and SII/PLR in T2, the hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs) for all-cause/CVD mortality in participants with LDL-C in T1/T3 and SII/PLR in T1/T3 were 1.47 (1.23-1.76)/1.36 (1.01-1.84), 1.40 (1.06-1.86)/1.67 (1.01-2.75) in the NHANES, and 1.22 (0.96-1.55) for all-cause mortality in the CLHLS, respectively. PA significantly reduced the above-mentioned risks: compared with participants who did not engage in PA, the HRs (95%CIs) for those who engaged in PA were 0.56 (0.48-0.67)/0.54 (0.41-0.71), 0.62 (0.45-0.86)/0.78 (0.50-1.20) in the NHANES, and 0.67 (0.51-0.87) for all-cause mortality in the CLHLS, respectively. LDL-C and inflammation mediated 4.99%-20.01% of the association between PA and mortality from all-cause/CVD.
CONCLUSIONS: Either low LDL-C level or high inflammation level was associated with increased risk of mortality from all-cause and CVD. Engagement in PA can reduce the above mortality risks related to abnormal levels of LDL-C and inflammation, providing practical implications for public health interventions.

Title: Single-center clinical analysis of anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) in children: a multimodal imaging approach to risk stratification.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics of pediatric patients with Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA), explore the application of multimodal imaging in risk stratification, and establish individualized diagnosis and treatment protocols for this population.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was performed on children diagnosed with AAOCA at Wuhan Children's Hospital between January 2015 and April 2026. Clinical manifestations, multimodal imaging findings, therapeutic strategies, and long-term outcomes were comprehensively analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 58 AAOCA patients confirmed by coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled. Initial transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) yielded false-negative results in 24 patients (41.4%). Twenty-seven patients underwent single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT-MPI, MPS), among whom 6 had normal perfusion and 21 showed perfusion defects. Seven patients with positive MPS findings received surgical correction, including 2 patients with L-AAOCA( 1 coronary angioplasty and 1 coronary unroofing) and 5 patients with R-AAOCA; all treated with coronary unroofing. No patients with negative MPS results underwent surgery, indicating that negative MPS findings perhaps provide limited valuable evidence to avoid unnecessary coronary revascularization. Two patients developed massive postoperative pericardial effusion and recovered after pericardiotomy and drainage; the remaining 5 surgical patients experienced no perioperative complications. All surgical patients were discharged after full recovery and received 3 months of aspirin antiplatelet therapy. Non-surgical patients were instructed to restrict strenuous physical activity and followed up for 3 months to 3 years. Follow-up CCTA or TTE revealed normal coronary ostia without stenosis in all patients.
CONCLUSION: Clinical manifestations of pediatric AAOCA vary widely across age groups, ranging from asymptomatic presentation to sudden cardiac arrest (SCA), leading to marked discrepancies in risk evaluation and therapeutic decision-making. Multimodal imaging including TTE, CCTA and SPECT-MPI facilitates risk stratification and guides personalized clinical management of children with AAOCA.

Title: Associations between glycolysis related metabolites and short-term mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior studies found that glycolysis-related metabolic markers-particularly lactate and glucose-are associated with short-term mortality after myocardial infarction (MI). However, information on glycolysis-wide metabolite alterations and short-term post-MI mortality remains insufficient. Therefore, this study investigated the associations of glucose, lactate, pyruvate, and citrate with short-term mortality after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
METHODS: This study was based on data from 724 STEMI patients enrolled in the population-based Augsburg Myocardial Infarction Registry. Arterial EDTA blood samples were drawn at the start of the catheterization procedure and plasma concentrations of the metabolites were quantified using a high-throughput nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy platform developed by Nightingale Health (Finland). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess the associations between glycolysis-related metabolites and 28-day mortality. P values were adjusted for multiple testing using the false discovery rate (FDR) method.
RESULTS: Overall, 677 patients survived the first 28 days after hospitalization, whereas 47 died within this period. Elevated plasma levels of glucose, lactate, pyruvate, and citrate were each significantly associated with an increased risk of short-term mortality. In the multivariable logistic regression models, the strongest association was observed for glucose (OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.53-2.88, padj ≤ 0.001) and the weakest association for pyruvate (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.22-2.10, padj = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that metabolic disturbances, reflected by glycolysis-related metabolites, are associated with short-term mortality in STEMI patients, suggesting their potential prognostic value.

Title: Effects of mechanical thrombectomy combined with anticoagulation vs anticoagulation monotherapy for acute intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial (CAPE study, ChiCTR2500095253, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn/clinicalResearch/researchInfo?id=c57630b7-51ec-4b24-83e1-85b9c0a835d6).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism is still debated. Interventional therapy is being increasingly widely applied in clinical practice. Numerous studies have confirmed that interventional therapy is effective. Both catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT) showed improvement in some efficacy outcomes compared with anticoagulation monotherapy. A recent study showed that MT has lower rates of clinical deterioration and/or bailout and postprocedural intensive care unit use compared with CDT, with no difference in mortality or bleeding, which makes the application of MT in clinical practice increasingly widespread. Recently, STORM-PE, the first randomized controlled trial to test the efficacy and evaluate the safety of MT combined with anticoagulation compared with anticoagulation monotherapy for the treatment of intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, showed that treatment with MT combined with anticoagulation resulted in a significantly greater reduction in right ventricular/left ventricular (RV/LV) diameter ratio at 48 h versus anticoagulation monotherapy, with comparably low rates of major adverse events in both treatment arms. However, whether MT combined with anticoagulation is more effective than anticoagulation monotherapy needs more evidence, especially in Asian populations.
METHODS: The CAPE study is a currently enrolling national multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing MT with MPA 8F guiding catheter [Cordis (Shanghai) Medical Device Co., Ltd] combined with anticoagulation vs anticoagulation monotherapy. A total of 156 patients with acute intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism stratified by the classification of the latest guideline of European Society of Cardiology (ESC) will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio. The primary efficacy endpoint was reduction of RV/LV diameter ratio assessed by computed tomographic angiography (CTPA) at 48 h. The secondary efficacy endpoint was the incidence of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary disease including chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. The primary safety endpoint was serious adverse events including major bleeding through 3 months visit.
DISCUSSION: CAPE is a RCT to compare the short and long efficacy of MT combined with anticoagulation and anticoagulation monotherapy for acute intermediate-high pulmonary embolism. The result will give more evidence for selection of different strategies for physicians.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: CAPE study is registered in Chinese Clinical Trial Registry identifier (ChiCTR2500095253,  https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn/clinicalResearch/researchInfo?id=c57630b7-51ec-4b24-83e1-85b9c0a835d6 ). Registered on November 26 2024.

Title: Mortality-related predictors in patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate in-hospital mortality and to identify predictors of mortality in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) patients receiving veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed data from adult patients who received VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock after CABG at our centre between 2014 and 2025. Among the 10,256 patients who underwent CABG, 74 received ECMO postoperatively. Among these, 33 patients (44.6%) died during ECMO support, 15 patients (20.3%) died after ECMO removal, and 26 patients (35.1%) survived to hospital discharge. For distinguishing hospital mortality, the lactate level at 24 h after ECMO initiation (LAC-T24) (> 4.35 mmol/L, AUROC: 0.916) performed the best, followed by the lactate clearance at 24 h (LC-T24) (< 55.73%, AUROC: 0.915). Other predictive factors included CKMB activity at 24 h (CKMB-T24) (> 157 U/L; AUROC: 0.848), mean arterial pressure at 24 h (MAP-T24) (< 77.5 mmHg; AUROC: 0.844), SOFA-2 scores (> 11.5; AUROC: 0.835), and the pre-ECMO Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (SOFA-1) (> 10.5; AUROC: 0.815). The best model revealed the pre-ECMO updated SOFA-2 scores (P < 0.001) (OR: 1.793, 95% CI: 1.029-3.124, P = 0.039), LAC-T24 (OR: 1.395, 95% CI: 1.045-1.861, P = 0.024), CKMB-T24 (OR: 1.015, 95% CI: 1.003-1.026, P = 0.013), and MAP-T24 (OR: 0.895, 95% CI: 0.809-0.989, P = 0.029) as independent predictors of hospital mortality after VA-ECMO.
CONCLUSION: In patients receiving ECMO treatment after CABG, in-hospital mortality rates remains high. In this study, LAC-T24, LC-T24, CKMB-T24, pre-ECMO SOFA-1 and SOFA-2 scores were identified as predictors of mortality.

Title: Echocardiographic markers for left atrial stiffness and left atrial conduction delay in patients with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation compared to age-matched controls.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To study left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and left atrial activation time (LA-AT) changes in an older population with silent paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF) compared to age-matched control.
METHODS: Individuals with newly diagnosed PAF and a randomly selected age-matched control group without AF were enrolled from STROKESTOP2-study. All participants had NT-proBNP levels 125-900 ng/L. TTE examinations were analyzed retrospectively offline using dedicated software. Besides conventional echocardiographic measurements, LA-AT was obtained by measuring the time delay between the onset of the P-wave on ECG and tissue Doppler Á peak wave in lateral LA wall. LASI was calculated as the ratio of left ventricular filling (E/é) to peak atrial longitudinal strain (PALS).
RESULTS: Mean age was 76 ± 0.3 years. The PAF group (n = 67) presented significant increase of LASI (0.41 (0.29-0.60) vs. 0.32 (0.29-0.43), P = 0.001) and prolonged LA-AT (170 (140-180) ms vs. 140 (120-144) ms, P < 0.001) compared to controls (n = 94). Subgroup analysis in participants with normal LA volume index (LAVI) ≤ 34 ml/m2, LASI and LA-AT remained significantly increased/prolonged in PAF (N = 27) compared to controls (N = 72). NT-proBNP-levels did not differ between PAF (228 (181-348) ng/L) and controls (216 (156-317) ng/L) (P = 0.18). ROC curve analysis identified thresholds LASI > 0.54 and LA-AT > 139 msec for discrimination of silent PAF.
CONCLUSION: Indices reflecting LA stiffness and atrial conduction delay were significantly elevated in recently diagnosed PAF patients. LASI and LA-AT thresholds might non-invasively detect early atrial remodeling without structural enlargement in elderly patients with high risk of PAF and mildly increased NT-proBNP levels.

Title: Associations of baseline levels, cumulative exposure, and two-wave patterns of the combined triglyceride-glucose index and frailty index with progression from cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-2 to stages 3-4 and stage 4: a prospective cohort study from CHARLS.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) and frailty index (FI) reflect metabolic dysregulation and multisystem vulnerability, respectively. However, the associations of the combined triglyceride-glucose index and frailty index (TyG-FI), its cumulative exposure, and two-wave patterns with progression from cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-2 to stages 3-4 and stage 4 remain unclear.
METHODS: This CHARLS cohort study included 3,473 adults with CKM stages 0-2 at Wave 1 and repeat exposure and outcome assessments at Wave 3. TyG-FI was calculated as TyG × FI. Estimated cumulative TyG-FI combined the two measurements and their time interval; K-means clustering identified three two-wave patterns. Cox regression evaluated baseline TyG-FI, and logistic regression evaluated cumulative exposure and two-wave patterns. Discrimination, internal K-fold cross-validation, and sensitivity analyses were assessed.
RESULTS: At Wave 3, 319 participants met CKM stage 4 criteria and 975 met CKM stages 3-4 criteria. In fully adjusted models, baseline TyG-FI was associated with stage 4 (HR per SD, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.20-1.47) and stages 3-4 (HR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.03-1.18). The corresponding ORs for estimated cumulative TyG-FI were 1.83 (95% CI, 1.62-2.06) and 1.42 (95% CI, 1.29-1.56); highest-versus-lowest-tertile ORs were 12.40 (95% CI, 7.43-20.67) and 2.38 (95% CI, 1.86-3.04).
