MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the occurrence of extracorporeal circuit coagulation. The secondary outcome was extracorporeal circulation lifespan (filter lifespan).
RESULTS: intracatheter Ca2+ trajectories were categorised into three types: low baseline with stable trend, moderate baseline with slow decline and high baseline with rapid decline. Fibrinogen, lactic acid and nurses’ professional titles showed significant differences among the three trajectory groups. Cox regression revealed that the high baseline with rapid decline type was the high-risk group for coagulation-induced filter lifespan reduction (HR=1.0), with the moderate baseline with slow decline type (HR=0.633 (95% CI 0.425 to 0.942), p=0.024) and low baseline with stable trend type (HR=0.534 (95% CI 0.289 to 0.986), p=0.045) having lower hazards. Multivariable analysis identified factors associated with circuit coagulation, including Body Mass Index, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) score, use of lipid-lowering drugs and blood-product transfusion. Higher citrate flow rate and lower transmembrane pressure were variables associated with a lower hazard of coagulation-driven filter failure. Several of these variables were measured during ongoing CRRT and may reflect downstream changes related to evolving circuit status rather than baseline causal determinants.
CONCLUSIONS: Heterogeneous intracatheter Ca2+ trajectories exist in patients receiving CRRT with unplanned early withdrawal due to circuit coagulation, and the high baseline with rapid decline trajectory is an independently associated factor for coagulation-induced filter lifespan reduction. These hypothesis-generating findings provide preliminary observational insights for optimising citrate anticoagulation management in CRRT; the observed intracatheter Ca2+ range among low-risk patients requires prospective external validation before any clinical implementation.

Title: High-density lipoprotein (HDL) dysfunctionality in autoimmune connective tissue diseases: protocol for a systematic review.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: Autoimmune connective tissue diseases (AICTDs) are associated with both chronic inflammation and an increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease beyond that conferred by traditional risk factors. High-density lipoprotein (HDL) exerts anti-atherogenic effects through its cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC), which inflammation may impair. Although HDL dysfunction has been reported in AICTDs, the role of this dysfunction in connective tissue diseases has not yet been systematically evaluated.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The study protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251183500). From inception, the Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online, Excerpta Medica database and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials will be searched. The review is scheduled to run from October 2026 to August 2027. Observational and interventional studies in adults with AICTDs reporting quantitative measures of HDL functionality, including CEC, antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory function and endothelial protective function, will be included. The study will be independently conducted by two reviewers.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Because this study will be a systematic review based on previously published data and will not involve individual patient data, ethical approval is not required. The findings will be disseminated through publication in a peer-reviewed journal and will be presented at a conference.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251183500.

Title: Sustained Tocilizumab and Adjunctive HydroBox Therapy in Refractory Takayasu Arteritis: An 11-year Case Report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Takayasu arteritis (TAK) is a rare, chronic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly affecting young women, characterized by progressive stenosis and occlusion of the aorta and its major branches. Despite advances in biologic therapy, refractory disease with recurrent vascular complications remains a significant clinical challenge. Molecular hydrogen-based adjuvant (HydroBox) therapy has emerged as a promising adjuvant approach owing to its antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties. This report aims to describe the long-term clinical course and therapeutic outcomes of a patient with refractory TAK managed with sustained tocilizumab and HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy over 11 years.
CASE REPORT: We report the case of a 25-year-old female with refractory TAK first diagnosed at age 13, presenting with sudden vision loss, dizziness, and pulseless upper extremities. Disease course was complicated by extensive great-vessel involvement, multiple cerebral infarctions, and recurrent in-stent restenosis despite ongoing interleukin-6 (IL-6) blockade. Over 50 courses of tocilizumab (Actemra) were administered from 2014 onward, combined with multiple percutaneous transluminal angioplasty and stenting procedures. HydroBox-assisted immunomodulatory therapy was subsequently introduced as an adjunctive treatment. During continued follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable with sustained suppression of inflammatory markers and favorable cerebrovascular findings on serial imaging.
CONCLUSION: This 11-year case report documents the feasibility of sustained long-term tocilizumab therapy combined with adjunctive HydroBox therapy in a patient with refractory TAK. Despite extensive multi-vessel involvement, recurrent in-stent restenosis, and prior cerebrovascular ischemia, the patient achieved progressive hemodynamic stabilization, durable suppression of inflammatory markers, and continued disease control. The potential immunomodulatory and antioxidant properties of HydroBox-assisted therapy warrant further prospective investigation to establish standardized protocols and confirm efficacy in larger cohorts.

Title: Predictors of Cardiovascular Events in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis for Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Two-year Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis (HD) for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) have a high risk of cardiovascular (CV) events. This study aimed to identify predictors of CV events in these patients, focusing on the prognostic significance of plasma docosapentaenoic acid (DPA).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 255 patients on maintenance HD between May 2019 and May 2020. Of these, 123 patients whose underlying disease was DKD were analyzed in this study. Baseline clinical parameters, lipid profiles, plasma fatty acids, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) were measured. Patients were followed for two years to monitor CV events.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 28 CV events occurred. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that a history of CV disease, high hs-CRP, and low plasma DPA levels were significantly associated with CV events. Multivariable Cox regression identified a history of CV disease [hazard ratio (HR)=4.86, p<0.001] and elevated hs-CRP (HR=2.80, p=0.035) as independent predictors of CV events. The association of lower DPA with CV events in univariate analysis was not retained after multivariable adjustment.
CONCLUSION: A history of CV disease and elevated hs-CRP are independent predictors of future CV events in patients on maintenance HD for DKD. While lower DPA levels were associated with CV risk in univariate analysis, larger multicenter studies are needed to fully clarify its prognostic significance.

Title: A Comparative Exploratory Study of Cognitive and Functional Outcomes by Sex and Age in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIM: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are associated with cognitive decline, but possible sex-related differences in cognitive and functional outcomes remain uncertain. This exploratory study evaluated sex-stratified associations of clinical factors, depressive symptoms, and functional independence with severe cognitive impairment in patients with T2DM, AF, and newly identified cognitive decline.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The study included 140 patients with T2DM, AF, and a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score <27, comprising 68 men and 72 women. Cognitive performance, depressive symptoms, and functional status were assessed using the MMSE, Montreal Cognitive Assessment, 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), Activities of Daily Living (ADL), and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living scales. Logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with severe cognitive impairment, defined as MMSE <24, in the overall cohort and separately in male and female patients.
RESULTS: Severe cognitive impairment was present in 32/68 men (47.06%) and 36/72 women (50.00%), with no significant difference between sexes. Increasing age and higher diastolic blood pressure were associated with higher odds of MMSE <24 in the overall cohort and in sex-stratified analyses. Higher GDS-15 scores were associated with increased odds of severe cognitive impairment in both sexes, whereas greater functional independence, reflected by higher ADL scores, was associated with lower odds of MMSE <24.
CONCLUSION: Age, higher diastolic blood pressure, and greater depressive symptom burden in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus were associated with increased odds of severe cognitive impairment, whereas greater functional independence was associated with lower odds in both sexes. These exploratory findings support cognitive, cardiovascular, psychological, and functional assessment in patients with T2DM and AF.

Title: The Effects of Cannabinoids in Cardiovascular Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
Abstract: Expanded Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) use have prompted increasing interest in their risk for cardiovascular complications. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, experimental, and epidemiologic evidence on the relationships between cannabinoid exposure and cardiovascular disease, summarizes acute and chronic outcomes, evaluates therapeutic potential of non-psychoactive cannabinoids, and identifies future research priorities. Cannabinoid type 1 receptors in cardiovascular tissues promote sympathetic activation, tachycardia, and endothelial dysfunction, while cannabinoid type 2 receptor activation exerts anti-inflammatory and athero-protective effects. Acute THC exposure in humans produces tachycardia, increased myocardial oxygen demand, vascular stiffness, and transient blood-pressure alterations. Recent large observational studies and meta-analyses suggest associations between cannabis/cannabinoid use and increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events. While causality has not yet been definitively established, the accumulation of in vitro and in vivo evidence indicates potentially significant cardiovascular risks associated with frequent and/or heavy cannabinoid use, particularly in individuals with underlying cardiovascular disease or other risk factors. In the future, clinicians should screen for cannabinoid use, and standardized exposure metrics, longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials are urgently needed.

Title: A Branch-Specific Combined Fenestration Strategy for Chronic Aortic Dissection With Severe Paravisceral True Lumen Compression.
Journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate a branch-specific combined fenestration strategy to address the technical challenges of severe true lumen (TL) compression during physician-modified fenestration (PMF)-based four-vessel visceral reconstruction in chronic aortic dissection (CAD).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled twenty-three consecutive patients with aneurysmal CAD and severe paravisceral TL compression (minimum functional TL diameter ≤10 mm) treated between January 2020 and December 2024. All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion. Endpoints included technical success (complete four-vessel reconstruction), 30-day mortality, target-vessel patency, and TL expansion.
RESULTS: Complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction was achieved in all 23 patients (92/92 target vessels). Renal ISLF was successful in all 46 renal arteries, with first-attempt success in 44 (96%). Distal aortic exclusion was required in 20 patients; one interval infrarenal rupture in the staged group was managed with emergency repair. Over a median follow-up of 17.0 months, primary target-vessel patency was 99% (91/92). The median minimum functional TL diameter increased from 8.0 mm preoperatively to 15.9 mm at one-year follow-up. No type I or III endoleak was identified. Thirty-day mortality was 0%. Transient spinal cord ischaemia occurred in one patient (4%), and acute kidney injury (KDIGO Stage 1) in two patients (9%), all resolving before discharge.
CONCLUSION: In highly selected CAD patients with severe TL compression, this combined fenestration strategy enabled complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction with satisfactory early target-vessel patency and no target-vessel loss, though longer follow-up in larger cohorts is required.

Title: Clinical factors and the non-linear relationship between age and neurological outcome in comatose patients following cardiac arrest.
Journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Age is often incorporated as a linear or categorical predictor after cardiac arrest, which may obscure variations in its association with neurological outcome.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate clinical factors associated with good neurological outcome and explore its nonlinear relationship with age in comatose patients after return of spontaneous circulation.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of 508 patients from the I-CARE cohort. The outcome was Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) 1-2 versus CPC 3-5, based on the best CPC recorded between 3 and 6 months. Age was modelled using restricted cubic splines with four knots. Discrimination, calibration, and optimism were assessed using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Time to return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), missing in 51.8%, was examined in sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: CPC 1-2 occurred in 38.2%. Age was associated with outcome (χ² = 29.16; p < 0.001) and showed nonlinearity (χ² = 7.79; p = 0.020). A shockable rhythm was associated with a higher probability of good outcome (adjusted OR = 6.68; 95% CI: 4.19-10.66). The AUC was 0.775 for the spline model and 0.767 for the linear model, with no significant difference (p = 0.179); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.764. In multiple imputation, each additional five minutes to ROSC was associated with a lower probability of good outcome (OR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.77-0.97).
CONCLUSIONS: Age showed a nonlinear association with neurological outcome, and flexible modelling improved model fit, although not discrimination. Shockable rhythm was the factor most strongly associated with good outcome.

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA.
METHODS: Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate.
RESULTS: We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years.
CONCLUSIONS: The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

Title: Serum proteomic correlates of arts and cultural engagement and their associations with health outcomes: cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses in the UK Household Longitudinal Study.
Abstract: Understanding of the biological mechanisms underpinning associations between arts and cultural engagement (ACEng) and health outcomes remains embryonic. This study aimed to characterize serum proteomic signatures of ACEng, investigate the relationships between ACEng and health conditions, and undertake preliminary analyses to explore whether these proteins may mediate the associations. We analysed prospective cohort data from 6,180 participants in the UK Household Longitudinal Study who had cardiometabolic protein data and/or neurology protein data. Two indices of arts engagement were generated by summing metrics of frequency and diversity of arts participation, cultural attendance, and library, archives, museum, and heritage visits. Geater ACEng was found to be consistently associated across models with differences in 17 proteins after adjusting for sociodemographic confounders and multiple testing. The enriched biological pathways identified involved cell proliferation, receptor-mediated signaling, immune regulation and inflammatory signaling. We then explored longitudinal associations between ACEng and incidence of 15 chronic diseases. ACEng was consistently associated with lower prospective risk of asthma, COPD, CVD, IHD, stroke, arthritis, hyperthyroidism, hypertension, diabetes, clinical depression, and dementia (but not with cancer, heart failure, liver disease or epilepsy). In exploratory analyses, the identified significant proteins mediated 15.95-37.70% of the associations between ACEng and cardiometabolic and respiratory diseases, arthritis, and depression, although as ACEng and proteins were measured near contemporaneously, this does not establish a causal protein pathway. Instead, these findings present, for the first time, proteomic signatures of ACEng and provide preliminary data to help generate hypotheses about potential mediation pathways to health conditions. Future longitudinal research is encouraged to test whether proteins provide causal mechanistic pathways linking ACEng to human health and disease.

Title: Early Cardiac Dysfunction in Pediatric Becker Muscular Dystrophy: A Prospective Cross-sectional Echocardiographic Study.
Journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) is an X-linked disorder characterized by progressive muscle weakness and cardiac involvement, with cardiomyopathy being the leading cause of mortality. While cardiac dysfunction in adult BMD patients is well documented, the early cardiac phenotype in pediatric populations remains poorly understood. This prospective cross-sectional study aimed to characterize age-stratified differences in cardiac function among children with BMD, children with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), and healthy controls.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included male children aged 3-18 years who were enrolled from June 2020 to December 2023 and met strict inclusion criteria: genetically confirmed BMD or DMD diagnosis, no prior cardiac medications, and absence of comorbid conditions affecting cardiac function. Participants were stratified into three age-matched groups: 3 to under 7 years (youngest group), 7 to under 10 years (middle group), and 10 to under 18 years (oldest group), with comparable mean ages across BMD, DMD, and healthy controls within each age stratum. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessments were performed, including conventional parameters, tissue Doppler imaging, and speckle-tracking echocardiography. Statistical comparisons were made between groups within each age range.
RESULT: The study comprised 86 BMD patients, 86 DMD patients, and 74 controls across three age groups. After normality testing and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc comparisons, BMD patients showed early left ventricular involvement, including lower LVEF (60.54±8.09% vs 65.56±3.04%, p<0.01) and GLS (18.06±2.10 vs 20.66±1.42, p<0.01) than healthy controls from the Younger group onward. Right ventricular enlargement (RV GLS 22.99±3.26 vs 25.58±2.37, p<0.01) and reduced FAC (40.35±6.01% vs 47.8±17.08%, p<0.01) were also evident in BMD, with age-dependent RV strain abnormalities. Compared with DMD, BMD showed larger LVEDV across age groups and relatively preserved GCS, whereas GLS abnormalities (18.06±2.10 vs 20.66±1.42, p<0.01) were still present compared with healthy controls. Left atrial reservoir/conduit indices were better preserved in BMD than DMD in the Older group. In a short-term longitudinal subsample (16 BMD and 19 DMD patients; mean follow-up ∼0.9 years), BMD patients showed a modest decline in LVEF (annualized change 2.01%/year, P = 0.050), while LV-GLS remained stable in both groups.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric BMD patients exhibit subclinical, age-associated cardiac dysfunction detectable across pediatric age groups. Because abnormalities in LVEF, LV GLS, RV FAC, and RV GLS were already present in the youngest group, the findings support early and regular cardiac surveillance incorporating advanced echocardiographic techniques from preschool age. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these subclinical differences predict clinically overt cardiomyopathy or treatment response.

Title: Atrial fibrillation recurrence pattern and subsequent heart failure hospitalization after ablation in left ventricular systolic dysfunction: A time-dependent analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, but the prognostic significance of postablation recurrence pattern and its evolution remains unclear. We investigated whether evolving postablation recurrence pattern was associated with subsequent heart failure (HF) hospitalization.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 381 of 5535 consecutive patients who underwent first-time AF ablation between 2012 and 2024 and had baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50%. Recurrence was defined as any atrial tachyarrhythmia lasting >30 s beyond the 3-month blanking period and classified as paroxysmal or persistent (lasting >7 days). Recurrence pattern was modeled as a time-dependent variable and updated upon documentation of paroxysmal or persistent recurrence during follow-up.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 49 months, 140 patients experienced recurrence (71 paroxysmal only and 69 persistent, including 21 who progressed from paroxysmal to persistent recurrence) and 61 experienced HF hospitalization. In a multivariable time-dependent Cox model adjusted for age, sex, baseline LVEF, prior myocardial infarction, prior HF hospitalization, and baseline AF type, both paroxysmal recurrence [hazard ratio (HR), 2.38; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.15-4.90; p = 0.019] and persistent recurrence (HR, 5.45; 95% CI, 2.59-11.46; p < 0.001) were associated with HF hospitalization compared with no recurrence. Persistent recurrence was also associated with a higher risk than paroxysmal recurrence (HR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.00-5.25; p = 0.049).
CONCLUSIONS: Time-updated assessment of postablation AF recurrence pattern revealed differential risks of subsequent HF hospitalization among patients with LV systolic dysfunction. Both paroxysmal and persistent recurrence were associated with HF hospitalization, with persistent recurrence representing a particularly high-risk state that may warrant closer HF surveillance and reassessment of rhythm-control strategies.

Title: Artificial intelligence-assisted, electrocardiogram-derived, sequential rule-based decision tree for exclusion of acute coronary syndrome as the etiology of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: After out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), deciding which patients without ST-segment elevation warrant emergency coronary angiography is difficult, as standard electrocardiogram (ECG), troponin, and echocardiography are limited in the early post-arrest window. We aimed to develop a sequential rule-based decision tree to identify post-ROSC patients in whom acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is unlikely to be the arrest etiology.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with OHCA were divided into development (2020-2024; n = 329) and temporal validation (2025; n = 71) cohorts. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECGs were analyzed by a deep-learning platform generating ten digital biomarkers. Five candidate biomarkers were combined into a rhythm-stratified sequential decision tree under a zero false-negative constraint; its performance was compared with that of individual biomarkers and validated in the temporal cohort.
RESULTS: The tree classified 171/329 (52.0%) and 32/71 (45.1%) patients in the development and validation cohorts, respectively, as "ACS not likely," with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified at any node. Yield concentrated in the non-shockable subgroup, in which the model excluded 169/261 (64.8%) non-ACS cases (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], 0.824), outperforming each individual biomarker. In the shockable subgroup, which carries a high pretest probability of ACS, 38/40 patients (95.0%) were retained as "ACS not excluded."
CONCLUSIONS: A rhythm-stratified, rule-based decision tree combining AI-assisted ECG-derived biomarkers classified approximately half of post-OHCA patients as "ACS not likely" with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified, principally in the non-shockable subgroup. This transparent, bedside-deployable framework warrants prospective multicenter evaluation.

Title: Ventilation monitoring in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest care.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adherence to American Heart Association (AHA) ventilation guidelines during cardiac arrest is challenging.
METHODS: Prospective, Before/After quality assurance study determining adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by Milwaukee County Emergency Medical Services and Kenosha Fire in Wisconsin using (Before) end tidal carbon dioxide [ETCO2] to monitor ventilations - Real BVM Help® applied but blinded versus (After) Real BVM Help®.
PRIMARY ENDPOINTS: mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in-target for rate, tidal volume, and both rate and tidal volume. AHA 2020 guidelines were followed.
RESULTS: From 9/29/22-12/22/23, 278 patients were entered (148 Before/130 After). Average age: 62.3 ± 16.7 years; 185 (67%) male. Mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in Before/After Groups in-target for rate (47.7 ± 25.1% vs 74.4 ± 24.1% respectively, p < 0.0001), tidal volume (15.3 ± 15.4% vs 45.4 ± 23.8% respectively, p < 0.0001), and rate and tidal volume (7.5 ± 9.6% vs 39.0 ± 23.3% respectively, p < 0.0001) were significantly higher in the After Group. In the Before Group, using ETCO2 to monitor all ventilations (N = 22,037 ventilations), only 43.8% were in-target for rate, 13.5% in-target for tidal volume, and 6.8% in-target for rate and tidal volume with a lower-than-target tidal volume delivered in 58.2% of all ventilations.
CONCLUSION: Real BVM Help® was associated with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines. ETCO2 monitoring failed to approach both rate and tidal volume guideline adherence with a lower-than-target tidal volume being the most common parameter delivered out-of-target (58.2%). Ventilation rate and tidal volume monitoring with real-time feedback should be considered during treatment of cardiac arrest.

Title: Early identification of recurrent out-of-hospital cardiac arrest using clinical ECG features.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent cardiac arrest (rearrest) after initial return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is associated with relatively poor outcomes. Early identification of rearrest might enable intervention to prevent rearrest. In this study, we sought to determine whether clinical ECG features can predict rearrest.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients who achieved ROSC between 2018 and 2024. We evaluated the association of ECG features (QRS width, standard deviation of Normal-to-Normal intervals, root mean square of successive NN interval differences, and percentage of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 ms) within individual 15-s segments throughout a 5-min window prior to rearrest as well as their temporal trends over the 5-min analytic window.
RESULTS: Of the 1489 OHCA patients achieving ROSC, 1298 were analyzed; 528 (40.7%) experienced rearrest. Rearrest patients were older, less likely to receive bystander CPR (48.7% vs. 61.9%), and had lower survival (20.4% vs. 43.1%) and favorable neurologic outcomes (7.8% vs. 21.2%; all p < 0.001). We found lower heart rate, wider QRS, and higher HR variability in those with rearrest. Identification was highest 1  min prior to rearrest (AUROC 0.74), declining beyond 3  min. Models using temporal trends achieved AUROC 0.67; strongest predictors were heart rate variability measures and QRS width.
CONCLUSION: Established ECG features achieved good prediction for rearrest with identification improving closer to time of rearrest. Future work leveraging novel features or more advanced artificial intelligence models may further improve prediction.

Title: Aging in cardio-oncology: Pathophysiology, clinical implications and future directions.
Abstract: Population aging is changing the needs of patients seen in cardio-oncology. Older adults with cancer often have cardiovascular disease, multimorbidity, and reduced physiological reserve, which can complicate treatment and recovery. Patients of the same chronological age may differ considerably in cardiovascular health, functional capacity, and treatment tolerance. Frailty and geriatric assessment can help characterize these differences and inform care. This review examines the biological mechanisms linking aging, cancer, and cardiovascular disease and discusses their implications for cardiovascular risk assessment, cancer treatment decisions, and long-term survivorship. Treatment decisions require consideration of the expected oncological benefit, cardiovascular risk, physiological reserve, life expectancy, and patient preferences. Identifying and addressing reversible vulnerabilities may help patients tolerate effective anticancer therapy while preserving function and quality of life. During survivorship, cardiovascular care should account for previous treatment exposure, changing health status, and adherence to preventive therapies. Closer collaboration between cardio-oncology and geriatric medicine may improve the assessment and management of older patients. Evidence specific to frail and very old adults remains limited. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether geriatric and biological aging measures improve cardiovascular risk prediction, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

Title: Semaglutide versus other GLP-1 RAs and cardiovascular risk in obesity-related cancer survivors.
Abstract:
AIMS: Obesity-related cancer (ORCa) survivors are a unique population often excluded from landmark GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) trials. Given their cardiovascular risks, we investigated whether semaglutide initiation, compared with other GLP-1 RA, was associated with modified 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among ORCa survivors with type 2 diabetes (T2D).
METHODS: We emulated a target trial using PCORnet-UTSW electronic health records (2016-2025). Adults with ORCa and T2D initiating semaglutide versus other GLP-1 RA were included. The primary outcome was modified 3-point MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, or all-cause mortality). Cumulative incidence risk (CIR), risk difference (RD), and hazard ratio (HR) were estimated in 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort.
RESULTS: Among 918 matched patients (semaglutide, n = 459; other GLP-1 RA, n = 459), 124 modified 3-point MACE occurred. The 5-year CIR% was 17.6 (95% CI, 12.3-22.9) for semaglutide and 26.6 (95% CI, 20.7-32.6) for other GLP-1 RA. Semaglutide was associated with lower modified 3-point MACE risk (RD%, -7.41 [95% CI, -11.83 to - 2.98];HR, 0.65 [95% CI, 0.44-0.94]) than other GLP-1 RA. Findings were largely consistent across high-risk subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide was associated with a lower modified 3-point MACE risk than other GLP-1 RA. These findings suggest potential heterogeneity in cardioprotective effects and warrant confirmation.

Title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials.
METHODS: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452).
FINDINGS: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156).
INTERPRETATION: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.
FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

Title: Long-term evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for systemic sclerosis (NISSC1-LTE): a cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis is a rare and heterogeneous chronic autoimmune disease. It has the highest mortality of the rheumatic diseases and few treatment options exist. Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) is an effective and established therapeutic option in selected patients with early severe systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis in real-life clinical practice.
METHODS: This cohort study (NISSC1-LTE) followed up patients with systemic sclerosis included in the prospective European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation NISSC1 study who had undergone their first autologous HSCT for severe progressive systemic sclerosis. Follow-up data were collected from 13 participating centres in France, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and Brazil. Participating centres completed a yearly case report form for each patient alive after 2 years and up to 10 years after autologous HSCT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as survival from baseline without evidence of systemic sclerosis progression. Late complications after autologous HSCT, including malignancies, secondary autoimmune diseases, infections, and major adverse cardiovascular events were also analysed. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were involved in the design and conduct of this study. The NISSC1 study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02516124) and is complete.
FINDINGS: All 80 patients with systemic sclerosis who had an autologous HSCT between Dec 4, 2012, and Jan 19, 2016, were included in this long-term extension study. 12 patients were lost to follow-up, including five patients with a follow-up less than 5 years. Median age at autologous HSCT was 43 years (IQR 33-51), 57 (71%) of 80 patients were female, 23 (29%) were male, and median follow-up was 9·2 years (IQR 8·9-9·6) after autologous HSCT. Progression-free survival was 81% (95% CI 71-88) at 2 years, 72% (61-81) at 5 years, and 60% (47-71) at 10 years. 18 patients died during the study; causes of death were autologous HSCT-related in five (6%) of 80 patients, disease progression in nine (11%) patients, post-autologous HSCT malignancy in two (3%) patients, and late serious infection in two (3%) patients. 34 (43%) of 80 patients maintained remission without immunosuppressive treatment over 10 years.
INTERPRETATION: This study provides long-term follow-up data after autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis allowing robust assessment of response rate, late complications, and sustained treatment benefit. The extended timeframe might serve as an important comparator for all upcoming, cellular treatment options.
FUNDING: None.

Title: TAILORing ibrutinib dose and plasma levels in the real-life patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
Journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics
Abstract: Ibrutinib is the cornerstone of treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL); however, cardiovascular adverse events (AE) may limit its long-term use. We performed a prospective, multicenter, real-life study that investigated the relationships between ibrutinib steady-state trough plasma concentrations (Cmin), the risk of development of AE, and the effects of dose reduction. Forty-eight patients with CLL treated with 420 mg/day ibrutinib were enrolled. Thirteen patients developed AE and exhibited significantly higher Cmin (geometric mean of 18.3 ng/mL) than patients without AE (geometric mean of 2.6 ng/mL, P < .0001). Logistic regression analyses showed that age and ibrutinib plasma levels were independent predictors of AE. Following temporary ibrutinib discontinuation, leading to resolution or mitigation of AE, ibrutinib was resumed at 280 mg/day, which lowered Cmin to a geometric mean of 3.4 ng/mL, similar to the Cmin measured in patients without AE. Adverse events did not recur in patients managed by DR. These real-life data show that dose reduction helps to normalize ibrutinib plasma exposure in CLL patients at risk of AE. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: In patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) treated with the Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor ibrutinib, development of cardiovascular adverse events (AE) seems to associate with increased ibrutinib plasma levels compared with patients without AE. Dose reduction from 420 to 280 mg/day effectively reduces ibrutinib plasma levels and helps to resolve or mitigate AE. These findings call for reconsidering the ibrutinib dose in CLL patients and provide clinical pharmacology evidence that individualized dose reduction may improve the therapeutic index of ibrutinib.

Title: Tongue capillary refill time and imaging parameters for acute coronary syndrome identification: A prospective ED study.
Journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid identification of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain remains challenging. Tongue capillary refill time (CRT) and tongue imaging may reflect systemic perfusion, but their value in ACS is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of standardized tongue-derived perfusion, macroscopic, and imaging parameters for identifying ACS.
METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 208 consecutive adult ED patients presenting with chest pain. Standardized tongue imaging and tongue CRT were assessed. A separate 20-patient pilot assessed interobserver reliability using ICC and kappa coefficients. Blinded ACS adjudication used clinical findings, serial high-sensitivity troponin measurements, electrocardiography, imaging studies, specialist consultations, and follow-up data. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed.
RESULTS: Among 208 patients, 61 (29.3%) had ACS: 16 STEMI, 41 NSTEMI, and four unstable angina cases. Tongue CRT was significantly prolonged in ACS patients (2.6 [2.2-2.9] vs. 1.3 [1.1-1.6] seconds; p<0.001). Tongue CRT demonstrated excellent discrimination for ACS (AUC 0.941, 95% CI 0.903-0.980), outperforming the HEART score (0.860), admission troponin (0.831), and TIMI score (0.788). A CRT threshold ≥2s yielded 86.9% sensitivity and 93.2% specificity. Tongue CRT and macroscopically dry tongue remained associated with ACS after adjustment (both p<0.001). Quantitative RGB and HSV parameters showed no significant between-group differences.
CONCLUSIONS: Standardized tongue CRT showed excellent discrimination for ACS in this cohort, in which most ACS cases were myocardial infarction. Its diagnostic value in unstable angina and incremental clinical utility remain unestablished. External validation is required before routine clinical use.

Title: Deep learning and dual-domain fusion of temporal and spectrotemporal SCG for valvular heart disease classification.
Abstract: Heart valve disease (HVD) is a growing cause of cardiovascular morbidity, yet accessible screening tools remain limited. Tri-axial seismocardiogram (SCG) signals capture mechanical signatures of both stenosis and regurgitation, but their non-stationary nature and subtle inter-lesion morphological differences challenge robust classification from a single representation. This study proposes an electrocardiogram (ECG)-free dual-domain deep learning framework that combines a 1D convolutional-recurrent encoder of raw SCG waveforms with a 2D EfficientNet encoder of continuous wavelet transform scalograms, integrating temporal and spectrotemporal representations through feature-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on primary valve lesion classification in 94 patients, with an additional exploratory analysis of multi-valvular, aortic-stenosis-dominant disease. Under patient-level stratified group cross-validation, the fused model achieved the highest mean accuracy (65.3%; 95% CI, 59.8%-70.7%), exceeding both unimodal encoders and the majority-class (35.2%) and covariate-only (39.1%) baselines. The same mean performance ordering was preserved when the image backbone was replaced, although the confidence intervals overlap at this cohort size. Under the segment-level protocol used in prior studies, the framework achieved 99.63% accuracy, with faster training convergence and more compact, separable feature clusters than either unimodal encoder. These findings support the value of combining temporal and spectrotemporal SCG representations and demonstrate its potential for ECG-free HVD classification under patient-independent evaluation.

Title: Exclusion of Arteriovenous Shunts in Intracerebral Hemorrhage Using MRI Arterial Spin Labeling: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Identifying intracranial arteriovenous shunts (AVSs), chiefly arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) and dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), after nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is critical to guide management and prevent recurrence. AVSs are the leading secondary causes of ICH but typically require digital subtraction angiography (DSA) for diagnosis, an invasive, ionizing radiation-based procedure that carries a non-negligible risk of complications and is not readily available in many centers. We assessed the diagnostic accuracy of arterial spin labeling (ASL), a noninvasive MRI technique for detecting AVSs during the etiologic workup of acute ICH.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study, across 3 French tertiary hospitals within the ongoing OPTICH cohort (October 2022-October 2025). Consecutive adults with nontraumatic ICH who underwent standardized MRI including ASL within the first week were included. ASL perfusion maps were independently evaluated by 2 blinded neuroradiologists and rated positive when focal hyperperfusion was observed adjacent to the hematoma. Final ICH etiology was adjudicated using all available imaging and follow-up data, with DSA confirmation for all AVSs. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and overall accuracy were calculated, using the final etiologic diagnosis as the reference standard.
RESULTS: Among 537 enrolled patients, 277 met inclusion criteria (median age 71 years [interquartile range 60-80]; 163 (58.8%) men). An AVS was confirmed in 24 patients (8.7%; 23 AVMs and 1 dAVFs). Interobserver agreement for ASL rating was excellent (κ = 0.88). ASL demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.8% (95% CI 79.8-99.3), specificity of 94.5% (90.9-96.7), PPV of 62.2% (46.1-75.9), and NPV of 99.6% (98.1-99.9), with an overall accuracy of 94.6% (91.3-96.7). All AVSs identified on initial DSA were detected by ASL; 3 ASL-positive AVSs were occult on initial DSA.
DISCUSSION: In an unselected, low-prevalence adult ICH population, ASL demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy and a near-perfect NPV, indicating that a negative ASL reliably excludes AVS. Main limitations include selective DSA use, few non-AVM shunts, and modest scanner heterogeneity. Pending external validation, these findings support systematic incorporation of ASL as a gatekeeper to DSA into standard MRI protocols during ICH etiologic workup.

Title: Resting-State Functional MRI and Clinical Outcomes After Acute Disorders of Consciousness: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate assessment and prognostication of patients with acute disorders of consciousness (DoC) after severe brain injury remain a substantial clinical challenge. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) measures spontaneous, temporally correlated brain activity in the absence of external stimulation and provides objective insight into the integrity of large-scale neural networks that support brain function. Emerging evidence suggests that assessing neural integrity using rs-fMRI may improve outcome prediction in patients with acute DoC. This review summarizes the current evidence of rs-fMRI as an assessment tool during the acute phase of severe brain injury.
METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature search using MEDLINE and Embase databases from January 2006 to March 2026. Eligible studies included peer-reviewed empirical investigations of adult patients with acute DoC (<28 days postinjury) that examined associations between rs-fMRI measures and clinical outcomes. The systematic review protocol was registered in the PROSPERO International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251085923).
RESULTS: Of 396 studies screened, 30 met eligibility criteria. Across these studies, a total of 800 patients (mean age = 48, 69% male) were scanned at a weighted average of 9.31 days after intensive care unit admission. Ten studies included patients exclusively with traumatic brain injury, 8 with cardiac arrest, 2 with encephalopathy, and 10 included mixed etiologies. The most frequently assessed resting-state networks were the default mode (n = 20) and executive control networks (n = 11), followed by visual (n = 6), salience (n = 6), sensorimotor (n = 6), and auditory (n = 5) networks. Across studies, significant associations between rs-fMRI measures and outcome were consistently reported, despite heterogeneity in methodology. The most commonly reported patient outcomes were functional or neurologic status, assessed at hospital discharge or between 3 and 12 months postinjury.
DISCUSSION: Current evidence consistently demonstrates that rs-fMRI acquired during the acute phase of brain injury is associated with neurologic and functional outcomes in patients with DoC. In addition, rs-fMRI may help identify patients more likely to recover consciousness and achieve favorable functional outcomes by characterizing the integrity of large-scale brain networks. However, substantial heterogeneity and small sample sizes limit comparability across studies. Standardized acquisition and analysis frameworks, along with larger prospective studies, are needed to validate the clinical utility of rs-fMRI and support translation into an assessment tool after brain injury.

Title: Transient Lung-Volume Reduction Improves First-Shock Cardioversion Success by Reducing Transthoracic Impedance in Patients With Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthoracic impedance (TTI) is an important determinant of the efficacy of direct-current cardioversion (DCCV), as increased impedance may reduce myocardial current delivery. Because lung volume influences thoracic electrical properties, transient lung-volume reduction (TLVR) may represent a simple strategy for acutely lowering TTI and improving cardioversion efficacy. This study evaluated the effect of a standardized TLVR maneuver on TTI and first-shock cardioversion success in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF).
METHODS: This prospective, randomized study included 116 patients with persistent AF scheduled for first-time radiofrequency ablation. Patients were randomized 1:1 to conventional mechanical ventilation (standard CV group, n = 58) or a standardized TLVR maneuver immediately before cardioversion (TLVR CV group, n = 58). Baseline TTI was measured before the intervention, and post-TLVR TTI was additionally measured in the TLVR group. All patients underwent anterior-posterior cardioversion with an initial 200 J shock. First-shock success was defined as maintenance of sinus rhythm for at least 1 min. Multivariable linear and hierarchical logistic regression analyses were performed to investigate determinants of impedance reduction and first-shock success.
RESULTS: First-shock cardioversion success was significantly higher in the TLVR CV group than in the standard CV group (53.4% vs. 29.3%, p = 0.008), whereas cumulative success after up to three shocks was similar (96.6% vs. 91.4%, p = 0.242). The impedance reduction rate was significantly higher among patients with successful first-shock cardioversion (9.09% vs. 5.00%, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, TLVR independently increased the impedance reduction rate by 1.75 percentage points (B = 1.751, p = 0.001), while a higher Body Roundness Index was associated with a lower reduction (β = -0.468, p < 0.001). In the mechanistic logistic regression model, each 1% increase in impedance reduction was associated with a 2.23-fold higher likelihood of first-shock success (OR = 2.226, p < 0.001). Model explanatory power increased from 56.3% to 74.9% after the incorporation of impedance reduction.
CONCLUSION: A standardized TLVR maneuver immediately before cardioversion was associated with greater TTI reduction and an approximately twofold increase in first-shock cardioversion success in patients with persistent AF. The impedance reduction rate emerged as a strong independent predictor of successful initial cardioversion, supporting a potential physiological mechanism linking acute lung-volume reduction to improved electrical cardioversion efficacy.

Title: Association Between Cumulative Social Determinants of Health and Mortality Among Stroke Survivors.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Social determinants of health (SDoH) are well-established contributors to health disparities. Whether cumulative SDoH burden is associated with long-term mortality among stroke survivors remains poorly understood.
METHODS: We extracted data of 1,404 stroke survivors from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018. Cumulative SDoH burden was calculated incorporating eight individual SDoH indicators across multiple domains: employment status, poverty-income ratio (PIR), food security, education level, healthcare access, health insurance, housing status, and marital status. Survey-weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations of individual SDoH indicators and cumulative SDoH burden with all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD) and non-CVD mortality outcomes.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 72 months, 604 deaths were documented, including 237 CVD deaths and 367 non-CVD deaths. Among the eight SDoH indicators, being unemployed, having lower PIR and having government insurance only or being uninsured were significantly associated with all-cause mortality. Looking at cause-specific mortality, having lower PIR was significantly associated with CVD mortality, whereas being unemployed was significantly associated with non-CVD mortality. The risk of mortality from all-cause (p for trend <0.001), CVD (p for trend =0.026) and non-CVD (p for trend <0.001) increased with the increasing SDoH burden.
CONCLUSION: In this nationally representative cohort of stroke survivors, increasing cumulative SDoH burden was significantly associated with higher risks of mortality.

Title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference.
DISCUSSION: Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8+ cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

Title: Factors associated with loss to follow-up after point-of-care diabetic retinopathy examination in a teleophthalmology program: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify patient-, clinical-, and system-level factors associated with loss to follow-up after point-of-care diabetic retinopathy examination (DRE).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults ≥18 years undergoing DREs at 75 primary care clinics in Pennsylvania, USA (2017-2019), restricted to examinations with recommended follow-up. The unit of analysis was the DRE. Electronic medical records were used to obtain six-month follow‑up outcomes and patient-, clinical-, and system-level variables. Loss to follow-up was defined as failure to attend an eye care visit within 180 days of DRE. Examinations with duplicate results, those from patients who died within six months, or from sites where the program was discontinued were excluded. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models with random intercepts for patient and clinic were used. Analyses were conducted in the full cohort and separately for gradable and indeterminate exams (ungradable/no image).
RESULTS: Among 3,121 DREs from 2,959 patients, 32.3% completed follow-up. In the full cohort, higher odds of loss to follow-up were associated with increasing age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=1.02, 95% confidence interval [95%CI]=1.00-1.03, p = 0.019), not being married (aOR=1.36, 95%CI = 1.04-1.77, p = 0.03), findings suggestive of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) on DRE (aOR=1.80, 95%CI = 1.14-2.85, p = 0.012), and higher no-show rates (aOR=1.04, 95%CI = 1.02-1.05, p < 0.0001). History of eye disease (aOR=0.50, 95%CI = 0.37-0.69, p < 0.0001) and patient contact within 30 days (e.g., same/next day: aOR=0.37, 95%CI = 0.20-0.67, p = 0.001) were associated with lower odds of loss to follow-up; contact at 31-60 days was not significantly associated. Findings were consistent across full and gradable models; only no-show rate remained significant in the indeterminate model. Socioeconomic variables, comorbidities, and diabetic retinopathy severity were not independently associated with loss to follow-up after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Adherence was associated with patient (sociodemographic: age, marital status), clinical (AMD on DRE, prior eye disease), and system-level factors (no-show rates, patient contact within 30 days), supporting targeted, multifactorial interventions.

Title: Integration of radiobiological modeling with clinical outcomes for optimizing carotid-sparing treatment planning in head and neck cancers.
Journal: Journal of cancer research and therapeutics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) can deliver significant incidental doses to the carotid arteries, increasing the risk of late vascular events. Carotid-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) with radiobiological modelling may reduce these risks without compromising tumour control.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the predictive accuracy of normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) modelling for carotid stenosis and its association with tumour control, vascular events, and quality of life in HNSCC patients treated with carotid-sparing IMRT.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 120 patients with HNSCC underwent carotid-sparing IMRT. Dose-volume histograms were used to calculate NTCP for carotid stenosis using the Lyman-Kutcher-Burman model, and tumour control probability (TCP) from target coverage. Patients were followed for ≥5 years with Doppler ultrasonography, MRI angiography when indicated, neurocognitive testing, and EORTC QLQ-H and N35 questionnaires. The primary endpoint was correlation between NTCP and ≥50% radiographically confirmed carotid stenosis. Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, and ROC analyses were performed.
RESULTS: At 5 years, high NTCP (>8%) was associated with reduced stenosis-free survival compared to low NTCP (≤5%) (HR = 5.62; 95% CI: 2.1-14.8; P < 0.001). NTCP correlated with incidence of ≥50% stenosis ( r = 0.78; P < 0.001) and cerebrovascular events ( P = 0.002). ROC analysis demonstrated good predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.84). TCP remained >90% across all NTCP quartiles. Low NTCP was associated with slower intima-media thickness progression and better neurocognitive and quality-of-life scores.
CONCLUSION: NTCP modelling reliably predicts late carotid stenosis and vascular outcomes in HNSCC patients receiving IMRT and supports patient-specific carotid-sparing strategies.

Title: Digital and technology‑enabled approaches for post‑stroke fatigue: A scoping review protocol.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post‑stroke fatigue (PSF) affects approximately 50% of stroke survivors and is one of the most common and disabling post‑stroke sequelae. Digital and technology‑enabled approaches have attracted increasing attention in the field of stroke rehabilitation, including mobile health applications (mHealth), wearable devices, virtual reality (VR), remote rehabilitation, artificial intelligence (AI), and neuromodulation technologies. However, no comprehensive scoping review has systematically mapped the full spectrum of evidence on digital and technology‑enabled approaches for PSF.
METHODS: This scoping review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews, be guided by the Population, Concept, Context (PCC) framework, and be reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta‑Analysis Protocols (PRISMA‑P) and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta‑Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA‑ScR). Eight electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PsycINFO) and five gray literature sources (OpenGrey, ProQuest Dissertations and Theses Global, ClinicalTrials.gov, the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, and Google Scholar) will be searched. Two reviewers will use NoteExpress to remove duplicates and manage references, and will independently screen titles, abstracts, and full texts. After pilot testing, data will be extracted independently by the two reviewers. Synthesis will involve descriptive numerical summaries and inductive qualitative content analysis. Inter‑rater agreement will be assessed during a calibration phase. The expected output is an evidence map organized by approach category and purpose (assessment, monitoring, prevention, and treatment), which will identify knowledge gaps and guide future research.
REGISTRATION: This protocol has been registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). Registration DOI (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/4WMEK).

Title: Medication background of Japanese men undergoing prostate needle biopsy: A medication profile based on the number of medications and drug classes.
Abstract: Prostate cancer is common in older men, and the treatment decision depends strongly on the patient's general condition and comorbidities. However, the medication background of men who reach prostate biopsy has rarely been described. We used a large Japanese administrative claims database (Medical Data Vision) to profile the medications of men who underwent prostate needle biopsy between April 2008 and June 2019. We examined the number of medications and the drug classes in relation to body mass index (BMI) and age. We identified 67,812 men, all aged 60 years or older. The mean number of medications was lowest at BMI 20-25 and increased toward both low and high BMI, showing a U-shaped pattern (minimum 1.44 drugs at BMI 22.0-22.5); the increase was driven mainly by high BMI. This pattern was consistent across age strata, and in a negative binomial regression adjusted for age the quadratic term of BMI remained significant (p < 0.001), with an adjusted minimum at BMI 20.5. The composition of drug classes differed by body size: metabolic drugs (antihypertensive/cardiovascular, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and hyperuricemia drugs) were more common at high BMI, whereas gastrointestinal and analgesic drugs were relatively more common at low BMI, and all classes increased with age. In conclusion, among men undergoing prostate biopsy, the number of medications was lowest at BMI 20-25 and the qualitative medication profile differed by BMI. These findings describe the medication background of this population and may inform the design of future risk-stratified or prospective studies.

Title: Infective endocarditis in children: a 23-year experience at a Southern African tertiary institution.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a paucity of data regarding infective endocarditis (IE) in children, particularly in low-to-middle-income settings, with minimal recent data from Sub-Saharan Africa.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the demographic and clinical profiles of paediatric patients with IE at the Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital (CHBAH), Johannesburg, South Africa.
METHODS: A retrospective descriptive study of all paediatric patients diagnosed with IE between 1993 and 2015. Demographic data, the presence of congenital or acquired structural heart disease and other risk factors, blood culture results and complications were recorded and analysed using basic statistical methods.
RESULTS: 183 patients were included (median age 31.2 months). Ninety-seven patients (53%) had underlying congenital heart disease (CHD), 26 had rheumatic heart disease (14.2%), and 45 (24%) were identified with structurally normal hearts. Underlying sepsis (37.8%), central venous catheters (CVC) (31.2%), prematurity (15.6%) and human immunodeficiency virus (13.3%) were found to be risk factors in the group with normal hearts. Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus viridans were the most common pathogens. Complications were documented in 103 (56.3%) patients. These included cardiac failure (CF), worsening valve lesions, vascular complications (embolisation and mycotic aneurysm formation), other manifestations of sepsis, surgery required to treat complications and death. The overall mortality rate was 23.5%. CF and vascular complications were associated with a high risk of mortality.
CONCLUSION: CHD is the most common association with IE, followed by structurally normal hearts in premature infants and patients with CVC. The complication rate of 56% and 24% mortality rate highlight the devastating outcomes of IE.

Title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-23 concentration in dogs with myxomatous mitral valve disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF-23) is primarily a kidney-related biomarker, but also may be influenced by cardiovascular remodeling and hemodynamic load.
HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: Verify whether serum FGF-23 concentration increases with myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) severity.
ANIMALS: Forty-two client-owned dogs with MMVD without overt kidney disease.
METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional study to evaluate serum FGF-23, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), creatinine (Cr), and symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) concentrations. Imaging variables included vertebral heart score (VHS), vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), left atrial-to-aortic root ratio (LA/Ao), normalized left-ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN), and diastolic transmitral E-wave velocity (E-vel). Differences among American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine stages were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Correlations were analyzed using Spearman's correlation. Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with serum FGF-23 concentration.
RESULTS: Dogs with ACVIM stages C and D had higher serum FGF-23 concentrations than those with stages B1 and B2 (P < .05). Serum FGF-23 concentrations were positively correlated with VLAS (rs = 0.500, P < .01), ANP (rs = 0.455, P < .01), LA/Ao (rs = 0.384, P < .05), E-vel (rs = 0.372, P < .05), and NT-proBNP (rs = 0.366, P < .05). ACVIM stage was significantly associated with serum FGF-23 concentration after adjustment for serum Cr concentration and loop diuretic use.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: The potential influence of MMVD should be considered when interpreting increased circulating FGF-23 concentrations in dogs with MMVD.

Title: Inflammation and thrombosis: from pathophysiology to future treatments.
Abstract: Inflammation and coagulation are tightly interconnected host-defense systems that, when dysregulated, promote pathological thrombosis. This narrative review examines mechanisms, clinical settings, and therapeutic implications of thromboinflammation (TI) across venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, with particular attention to the differences in clinical translation among vascular territories. Endothelial activation, tissue factor expression, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil extracellular traps, complement activation, inflammasome signalling, and impaired fibrinolysis converge to generate a procoagulant phenotype. These mechanisms modify Virchow's triad and contribute to venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, although their relative importance varies across vascular territories. Clinically, TI is relevant in inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatologic and other immune-mediated disorders, sepsis, coronavirus disease 2019, clonal haematopoiesis, complement-mediated diseases, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. TI offers a unifying framework for mechanistic risk assessment and therapeutic development. In atherothrombosis, randomised trials have demonstrated that selective modulation of inflammatory pathways, particularly the NLRP3-interleukin-1β-interleukin-6 axis and colchicine-sensitive pathways, can reduce recurrent cardiovascular events. By contrast, the role of inflammation-targeted therapies for primary or secondary prevention of VTE remains uncertain. Future studies should identify disease-specific biomarkers and test targeted anti-inflammatory or immunothrombotic strategies, alone or alongside anticoagulation, to prevent thrombosis without compromising haemostasis effectively.

Title: Comparative Effects of Pharmacological Treatment on Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The comparative efficacy and safety of the new drugs (including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors [SGLT-2Is], glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists [GLP-1RAs], non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists [nsMRAs], and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators [sGCs]) for heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved (HFmrEF/HFpEF) ejection fraction remains largely unclear. We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate their comparative effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF, aiming to provide evidence-based guidance for treatment selection.
METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were comprehensively searched. We included randomized controlled trials that compared nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA with placebo for patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Primary efficacy outcomes were cardiovascular (CV) death, hospitalization for heart failure (HF hospitalization), and all-cause mortality, while primary safety outcomes were adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs). The main analysis was conducted to compare the effects on HFmrEF/HFpEF between individual drugs. A frequentist network meta-analysis with random-effects models was used to calculate risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes and standardized mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 20 randomized controlled trials (RCTs, including 10 drugs from 35 publications) were included for analyses, but none provided head-to-head direct comparisons. No significant differences among all the individual drugs were found in risks of CV death or all-cause mortality. Compared with exenatide, low or moderate certainty evidence showed that dapagliflozin (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.36-0.91), empagliflozin (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.34-0.86), and semaglutide (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20-0.91) were related to decreased risk of HF hospitalization. No significant differences in the risk of SAEs were found among the individual drugs. Compared with empagliflozin, very low certainty evidence showed that tirzepatide (RR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32) was related to increased risk of AEs. When comparing the four drug classes (nsMRA, sGC, SGLT-2I, and GLP-1RA), no significant differences in efficacy outcomes were found, while SGLT-2I (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.96) was associated with a decreased risk of AEs compared with GLP-1RA.
CONCLUSIONS: No significant differences among the individual SGLT-2I, GLP-1RA, nsMRA, and sGC drugs were found in risks of CV death, all-cause mortality or SAEs in patients with HFmrEF/HFpEF. Further evidence is needed to support these comparative effects and update guidance on medication choice for HFmrEF/HFpEF.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier number CRD420251143542.

Title: Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.
Abstract: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion.
