REGISTRATION: Protocol available via https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD013416.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Prognostic Impact of Late Gadolinium Enhancement on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events and Time-Varying Attenuation of Risk in Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prognostic value of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) patients and characterize the dynamic pattern of its risk effect over time.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients who underwent Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) between 2020 and 2024, with MACE (cardiac death, heart failure re-hospitalization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmia) as the endpoint. Patients were stratified by MACE occurrence. Schoenfeld residual testing showed borderline deviation of the proportional hazards (PH) assumption for LGE extent (LV mass percentage). Thus, a time-dependent Cox model (Extended Cox PHs Model) with an LGE extent × follow-up time interaction term was built to assess dynamic hazard ratio changes, and independent MACE risk factors were identified.
RESULTS: Among 173 DCM patients (age 47 ± 15 years, 105 males), 46 (26.6%) experienced MACE after a mean follow-up of 27 ± 16 months. The time-dependent Cox model identified LGE extent (baseline HR: 1.243, 95% CI: 1.162-1.329, p < 0.001), the LGE extent × time interaction (HR: 0.993, 95% CI: 0.989-0.997, p = 0.001), and LV end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi; HR = 1.008, 95% CI: 1.003-1.014, p = 0.001) as independent MACE predictors. Notably, the risk effect of LGE extent demonstrated time-dependent attenuation.
CONCLUSION: LV LGE extent and LVEDVi independently predict MACE in DCM patients. The early prognostic value of LGE extent suggests a critical time window for early fibrosis intervention.

Title: Prevalence and prognostic impact of valvular heart disease in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
Journal: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Significant valvular heart disease (VHD) is associated with adverse prognosis in transthyretin amyloidosis cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, data is limited to isolated VHD. We aimed at evaluating the difference in outcome between isolated and multiple VHD, and particularly with and without aortic stenosis (AS).
METHODS: Patients with ATTR-CM were retrospectively included in a multicentric registry. The endpoint was a composite of heart failure hospitalizations and all-cause death.
RESULTS: Of the 694 patients (mean age 75 ± 13 years,74%male), 302(44%) presented with significant VHD. Of these, 98 had VHD including AS (isolated AS in 45%;multiple VHD with AS in 55%), while 204 had VHD without AS (isolated in 64%, multiple VHD in 36%). During a median follow-up of 22(8-38) months, 217(31%) patients reached the endpoint. Significant VHD was associated with worse outcomes than no-VHD (log-rank p < 0.001; HR:3.275; 95%CI (2.472-4.337), remaining significant after adjustment (HR2.006 (1.193-3.047);p = 0.007). Stratification by the presence of AS, and according to isolated or multiple VHD, revealed that isolated significant AS ((HR: 2.462; 95%CI (1.233-4.917); p = 0.011), and multiple VHD including significant AS, had the highest risk for adverse outcomes ((HR: 3.385; 95%CI (1.744-6.573);p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In ATTR-CM, significant VHD is strongly associated with poor prognosis, with the highest risk for adverse events in significant multiple VHD including AS.

Title: Machine learning improves 10-year prediction of atherosclerotic plaque progression and cardiovascular events in systemic lupus erythematosus.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance of generic and disease-adapted tools in predicting 10-year cardiovascular disease (CVD) events and atherosclerotic plaque progression risk in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and develop a machine learning-based model to improve cardiovascular risk stratification.
METHODS: In a prospective 10-year follow-up carotid and femoral ultrasound study of patients with SLE without prior CVD events, we assessed the performance of 11 CVD risk scores (7 conventional, 4 SLE-adapted) to predict atherosclerotic plaque progression and incident CVD events. We used discrimination (sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve [AUC], Youden index), calibration (Brier Score [BS]) and classification (Matthews correlation coefficient, F1 score) metrics, and logistic regression and time-to-event analyses. A machine learning-based gradient boosting model was developed and internally validated.
RESULTS: Among 111 patients (91% female, median age: 43.0 years) with 10-year ultrasonography follow-up, 53 (47.7%) developed new plaques, and 8 (7.2%) had incident CVD events. All scores demonstrated suboptimal performance; sensitivity: 0.00-0.44, AUC 0.58-0.79, and BS: 0.44-0.71. In multivariable analysis, QRISK3 was the only tool independently associated with CVD events and/or plaque progression (HR:1.87, p = 0.027). A machine learning-based score that integrates QRISK3 with disease-related risk factors (disease duration, cumulative glucocorticoid dose, DORIS achievement, antiphospholipid antibodies, hydroxychloroquine) and additional traditional CVD risk factors (physical activity, waist circumference), demonstrated significantly better performance compared to all evaluated scores.
CONCLUSION: Conventional and SLE-adapted tools underestimate CVD events and atherosclerosis progression risk in SLE. A machine learning-based model incorporating disease-specific and traditional cardiovascular risk factors into QRISK3 improves CVD risk stratification.

Title: Performance of the recent Duke criteria versions in patients with suspected infective endocarditis and sufficient cardiac imaging: The more things change, the more they remain the same.
Journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Even after the major revisions incorporated into the International Society for Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases (ISCVID) and 2023 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Duke criteria, approximately one third of cases remain categorized as "possible" IE. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Duke criteria in a cohort of patients who underwent guideline-concordant multimodality cardiac imaging.
METHODS: This retrospective study at two Swiss university hospitals (2014-2025), included adult patients with suspected IE who underwent guideline-concordant cardiac imaging. The reference standard was the final diagnosis established by the Endocarditis Team. Each episode was classified according to 2015 Duke-ESC, 2023 Duke-ISCVID, and 2023 Duke-ESC clinical criteria as definite, possible, and rejected IE. Diagnostic performance was assessed using two approaches: (1) definite IE versus possible/rejected IE, and (2) definite/possible IE versus rejected IE.
RESULTS: Among 3,448 of suspected IE, 1,302 (38%) were adjudicated as IE. The proportion of episodes classified as possible IE remained high: 2015 Duke-ESC: 29%; 2023 Duke-ISCVID: 33%; and 2023 Duke-ESC: 29%. Sensitivity (definite IE vs possible/rejected IE) increased from 63% (95% CI 60-66%) with the 2015 Duke-ESC criteria to 74% (71-76%) with the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria and 71% (68-73%) with the 2023 Duke-ESC criteria. Specificity (definite/possible IE versus rejected IE) declined from 72% (70-74%) to 59% (57-61%) and 66% (64-68%), respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort of patients who underwent guideline-concordant imaging, both 2023 Duke criteria increased sensitivity but failed to reduce the persistent diagnostic gray-zone of "possible" IE, highlighting an ongoing limitation with direct clinical and research implications.

Title: Left ventricular assessment using speckle-tracking echocardiography in Behçet's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory disorder associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity. Conventional echocardiography often fails to detect early myocardial involvement. Speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) allows sensitive assessment of left ventricular (LV) myocardial deformation, particularly global longitudinal strain (GLS). The aim of this study is to systematically evaluate LV systolic function assessed by STE in BD patients and to compare GLS differences with healthy controls.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science databases were searched for studies assessing LV strain by STE in BD. Studies using two- or four-dimensional STE were included. Pooled standardised mean differences (SMD) in LV GLS between BD patients and controls were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochrane Q test and was further explored using Baujat plot and leave-one-out analysis. PROSPERO registry number: CRD420251251109.
RESULTS: Eight studies including 373 BD patients and 402 controls were included. LV GLS was not significantly reduced in BD compared to controls (SMD -0.59; 95% CI -1.21 to 0.04; p=0.06). Subgroup analyses showed that GLS impairment was more pronounced in patients with non-active disease (SMD -0.9; 95% CI -1.71 to -0.08), while no significant difference was observed in patients with no cardiovascular risk factors (p=0.20).
CONCLUSIONS: BD patients do not exhibit consistent subclinical LV systolic dysfunction in strain echocardiography. Further studies are required to optimise the use of STE in this population.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Behçet's disease and pregnancy: retrospective study and updated review of the literature.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Behçet's disease (BD) is a rare, chronic-relapsing multisystem vasculitis of unknown aetiology, typically presenting with bipolar aphthosis (oral and genital), cutaneous lesions, and ocular involvement. It is most often diagnosed during reproductive age and its coexistence with pregnancy is therefore not uncommon. The interaction between BD and pregnancy is complex and bidirectional: pregnancy can modulate disease activity, while the disease itself may influence maternal, foetal, and neonatal outcomes. Current literature remains limited and frequently yields inconsistent conclusions regarding this relationship. In light of these considerations, this study aims to evaluate the impact of BD on pregnancy outcomes and to characterise the disease course during pregnancy in a cohort of affected patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively analysed data from 25 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of BD and a total of 48 pregnancies, followed at the outpatient clinics of Policlinico Umberto I, Rome, Italy. Clinical records were reviewed and supplemented with telephone interviews to ensure accuracy and completeness of information. Additionally, a literature review wasconducted using major databases such as PubMed, Cochrane and Google Scholar to provide context and comparison with previously published findings.
RESULTS: Contrary to the prevailing consensus in the literature, which often reports increased disease activity during pregnancy, our findings indicate that in 80% of cases it remained stable, with no significant differences compared to the pre-pregnancy period. When flares did occur, they primarily involved oral aphthosis, aligning with previously reported patterns. Pregnancy outcomes were generally favourable, with an overall live birth rate of 89.58%. Complications were observed in 13 pregnancies (27.08%), mostly in pregnancies that occurred before BD diagnosis (21%). The most common were spontaneous miscarriage and deep vein thrombosis. Other complications, each occurring in one case, included threatened miscarriage, preterm delivery, low birth weight, gestational diabetes, gestational hypertension, and premature rupture of membranes.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that Behçet's disease does not usually worsen during pregnancy and that favourable pregnancy outcomes are achievable. Nonetheless, the risk of complications, although relatively low, supports the need for preconception counselling and close multidisciplinary monitoring. This study contributes new insights from a specialised referral centre to the limited body of evidence available on this topic.

Title: [The method of counter differentiation in analysis of co-morbid relationships of arterial hypertension].

Title: Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting Major Adverse Renal and Cardiovascular Events in Acute Myocardial Infarction With Chronic Kidney Disease: Algorithm Development and Validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major adverse renal and cardiovascular events (MARCE) have been proposed as a comprehensive end point reflecting both cardiac and renal outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, existing prediction tools lack accuracy and generalizability for this high-risk population.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and externally validate explainable machine learning models and a nomogram for predicting in-hospital MARCE among patients with AMI and CKD.
METHODS: We enrolled patients with AMI and CKD who underwent emergency treatment at the First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University as the discovery cohort and those at Wenzhou TCM (traditional Chinese medicine) Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University as the external validation cohort. Clinical features, including demographic details, comorbidities, laboratory results, echocardiography measurements, procedural details, and medication parameters, were collected for all participants. Important variables were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression in the training set. We developed extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest, decision tree, and logistic regression (LR) models and evaluated their discrimination, calibration, and classification metrics in the hold-out test set and external cohort.
RESULTS: In the training set, we identified 6 important variables (Killip class, lactate, estimated glomerular filtration rate, use of diuretics, use of beta-blockers, and use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors). In the test set, model discrimination was comparable across XGBoost (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.882, 95% CI 0.816-0.947), LR (AUC 0.875, 95% CI 0.799-0.950), and random forest (AUC 0.870, 95% CI 0.800-0.940), while decision tree showed lower performance (AUC 0.814, 95% CI 0.720-0.886). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values illustrated both global and individual feature contributions in the XGBoost model. A nomogram based on LR achieved an AUC of 0.873 (95% CI 0.714-0.926) in external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study identified 6 important predictors and provided a series of prediction models to enhance risk stratification of MARCE for patients with AMI and CKD. These models might aid in stratifying risk and choosing appropriate therapeutic strategies in the management of patients with AMI and CKD.

Title: Divergent epidemiologic, shared risks: a comparative global analysis of COPD, ischemic stroke, and intracerebral hemorrhage.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although COPD and stroke share pathological mechanisms and risk factors, their epidemiological patterns differ significantly. This study investigates the global burden of COPD and stroke, analyzing their shared risk factors and epidemiological disparities to inform targeted prevention strategies.
METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 estimates, we conducted a repeated cross-sectional comparison of COPD, IS, and ICH from 1990 to 2021. Historical age-standardized rates were taken directly from archived GBD records labelled 'Age-standardized', whereas age-specific analyses used groups aged ≥20 years. We examined temporal, geographical, age-specific, sex-specific, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI) patterns, shared risk-attributable DALY rates, and exploratory Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) projections through 2050.
RESULTS: From 1990 to 2021, absolute incident cases for all three conditions increased, while age-standardized incidence rates declined. In 2021, COPD had the highest global ASIR, ASMR, and ASDR among the three diseases. Country-level first-place counts differed by metric: COPD had the highest ASIR in 187 countries and territories, IS the highest ASMR in 110, and ICH the highest ASDR in 95. Air pollution accounted for the largest global attributable DALY burden among the shared Level 2 categories, whereas tobacco predominated in high-SDI settings. Exploratory BAPC projections suggested continued ASDR declines through 2050, with IS potentially having the highest projected ASDR, while age-specific burden increasingly shifted toward older populations.
CONCLUSION: Prevention priorities should reflect disease burden and local resources, with sustained attention to tobacco exposure and air pollution. The observed geographical overlap supports population-level planning and motivates individual-level research, but it does not establish COPD-stroke comorbidity, causality, or clinical predictive value.

Title: Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery in Patients on Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Prisma Guided Systematic Review and Propensity Score Matched Cohort Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (HD) have limited physiologic reserve and high competing cardiometabolic risk, yet surgery remains central to cure for many gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies. Evidence describing oncologic surgery in this population is fragmented across cancer sites and data sources.
METHODS: A PRISMA guided systematic review of adult patients on maintenance HD undergoing resection for GI malignancy was performed. The review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL through March 2026 and included comparative observational studies reporting perioperative or long-term outcomes. In parallel, a propensity-score matched TriNetX cohort of adults undergoing major GI cancer surgery between 2010 and 2025. HD was defined by preoperative ESRD and dialysis dependence codes. Patients were matched 1:1 on age, sex, race, and ethnicity. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes were 30-day sepsis, pneumonia, and acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
RESULTS: The review included 20 studies after screening 1,744 deduplicated records and 83 full texts. Colorectal surgery provided the most robust evidence: dialysis was associated with markedly higher mortality and serious morbidity, and a published meta-analysis of colorectal surgery estimated a pooled mortality odds ratio (OR) of 4.12. Gastric, pancreatic, and hepatobiliary reports were smaller but showed the same direction of effect, with frequent infectious and cardiovascular complications and substantial competing non-cancer mortality. In the current TriNetX analysis, 3,757 HD patients were matched to 3757 non-HD controls. Thirty-day mortality was 11.4% in HD patients versus 3.0% in controls (OR: 4.21, 95% CI: 3.40-5.22). HD patients also had higher rates of sepsis (14.1% vs. 3.9%; OR 4.06), pneumonia (8.1% vs. 2.2%; OR: 4.02), and AMI (4.3% vs. 0.9%; OR: 5.18).
CONCLUSIONS: Across GI cancer operations, maintenance HD identifies a very high-risk surgical phenotype. The dominant short-term pattern is excess death, infection, and cardiopulmonary morbidity; the dominant long-term pattern is competing non-cancer mortality. Surgery remains appropriate for selected patients with resectable disease, but perioperative dialysis timing, multidisciplinary optimization, and treatment in experienced centers are critical.

Title: Alzheimer's pathology mediates arteriolosclerosis and cerebral amyloid angiopathy associations with cognition.
Abstract: Vascular and neurodegenerative pathologies frequently co-occur in aging brains, yet the mechanisms linking vascular neuropathologies to cognitive impairment remain incompletely understood. We examined whether Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic change (ADNC) and Lewy body disease (LBD) mediate or modify associations between vascular neuropathologies and domain-specific cognitive performance. The analytic sample included 1,269 decedents (mean age at death, 84.3 ± 9.1 years; 43.3% female; 94.7% White). At the last evaluation prior to death, 22.5% were cognitively normal, 2.4% were impaired but not mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 14.9% had MCI, and 60.2% had dementia. Vascular neuropathologies included arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis of the circle of Willis, cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), gross infarcts/lacunes, and microinfarcts. Multivariable linear regression models evaluated associations with harmonized memory, executive function, and language z-scores adjusting for age at death, sex, education, and apolipoprotein E ε4 status. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was tested. Mediation models estimated indirect and direct effects of vascular neuropathologies on cognition through ADNC or LBD using 5,000 bootstrap samples. Greater arteriolosclerosis severity was associated with worse memory (β=-0.16, 95% CI -0.23 to -0.09), executive function (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.11), and language (β=-0.18, 95% CI -0.24 to -0.12; all p<0.001). CAA was strongly associated with poorer cognition across domains, including memory (β=-0.26, 95% CI -0.33 to -0.19; p<0.001). Atherosclerosis and infarcts showed more limited associations, while microinfarcts were not significantly associated with cognition. Mediation analyses indicated that ADNC statistically accounted for approximately 13-29% of the associations between arteriolosclerosis and cognition across domains and 64-91% of the associations between CAA and cognition. Direct effects of arteriolosclerosis remained significant, whereas CAA effects were largely explained by ADNC. Effect modification by ADNC and LBD was limited, although LBD attenuated associations of arteriolosclerosis and CAA with executive function. Mediation through LBD was not observed. This novel evidence shows that vascular neuropathologies influence cognition through defined pathways with statistically significant patterns of associations. In this autopsy-confirmed cohort, vascular neuropathologies showed different patterns of association with domain-specific cognitive performance and ADNC. A larger proportion of the association involving CAA was statistically accounted for by ADNC, whereas direct associations remained more apparent for arteriolosclerosis. This study clarifies how vascular and neurodegenerative processes interact to shape cognitive impact and inform mechanistic preventions.

Title: Clopidogrel Versus Aspirin Monotherapy According to Atherothrombotic Risk Profile.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel monotherapy has shown superior efficacy compared with aspirin after completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, whether treatment effects differ according to overall atherothrombotic risk integrating clinical and angiographic factors remains unclear.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the SMART-CHOICE 3 (Smart Angioplasty Research Team: Choice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) randomized trial included patients who completed guideline-directed dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI. Atherothrombotic risk was defined using the a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention and complex PCI. Patients with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention ≥3 or complex PCI were classified as higher risk, and those with a Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction Risk Score for Secondary Prevention <3 without complex PCI were classified as lower risk. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke). Bleeding was defined as Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2, 3, or 5.
RESULTS: Among 5506 patients, 4486 (81.5%) were at higher risk and 1020 (18.5%) were at lower risk. Over a median 2.3 years, the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events was higher in the higher-risk group (6.1% versus 3.1%; hazard ratio, 1.83 [95% CI, 1.17-2.78]; P=0.007). In higher-risk patients, clopidogrel reduced major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events compared with aspirin (4.6% versus 7.4%; hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.50-0.89]; P=0.006), with no difference in lower-risk patients (3.0% versus 3.2%; hazard ratio, 1.03; P=0.945; interaction P=0.242). Bleeding was similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: After completion of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with lower ischemic risk than aspirin in patients with higher atherothrombotic risk, without increased bleeding.

Title: Comparative Safety and Efficacy of Oral Anticoagulants in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Prior Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized-Controlled Clinical Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and prior ischemic stroke represent a high-risk population facing competing risks of recurrent thromboembolism and hemorrhagic complications. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended over vitamin K antagonists for stroke prevention in AF, no randomized controlled clinical trial has directly compared individual DOACs to each other in this population.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized-controlled clinical trials enrolling patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack. MEDLINE, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception until May 2026. The primary outcome was any stroke. Secondary outcomes included ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), cardiovascular mortality, and all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs.
RESULTS: The evidence network comprised 6 trials (18 395 patients) in a star-shaped structure. Each DOAC was informed by a single warfarin-controlled trial, and 2 trials used aspirin as the comparator. All between-DOAC comparisons were indirect. In the network meta-analysis, compared with warfarin, apixaban was the only agent to significantly reduce both any stroke (RR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.53-0.97]) and major bleeding (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]). Dabigatran, apixaban, and edoxaban each significantly reduced hemorrhagic stroke and ICH versus warfarin, whereas rivaroxaban did not reach significance for any bleeding outcome. Edoxaban was the only agent associated with significantly lower cardiovascular (RR, 0.79 [95% CI, 0.65-0.97]) and all-cause mortality (RR, 0.84 [95% CI, 0.72-0.99]). Based on indirect comparisons only, no differences between individual DOACs were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AF and prior ischemic stroke, individual DOACs reduced intracranial and systemic bleeding relative to warfarin, although not uniformly across agents. Apixaban alone significantly reduced both any stroke and major bleeding versus warfarin, but differences between individual DOACs could not be established given the small number of trials.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/; Unique identifier: CRD420261404062.

Title: Impact of Inflammatory Burden on Outcomes After Breakthrough Ischemic Stroke: Insights From the ASPERA-R Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with atrial fibrillation who experience ischemic stroke despite oral anticoagulation (breakthrough stroke) remain at high risk of recurrent vascular events and death. Although inflammation has been associated with thromboembolic risk, its prognostic role in breakthrough stroke remains unclear. We investigated whether a composite inflammatory burden index was associated with adverse outcomes after breakthrough ischemic stroke.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with breakthrough ischemic stroke from the ASPERA-R registry. Inflammatory burden was assessed using admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and C-reactive protein. Biomarkers were log-transformed, standardized using Z scores, and combined into a composite inflammatory burden index. Patients were classified as having high (upper tertile) or lower inflammatory burden (lower 2 tertiles). Outcomes included new 90-day ischemic events (recurrent ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, or systemic embolism), 24-hour hemorrhagic transformation, and 90-day moderate-to-severe bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, and mortality. Inverse probability of treatment weighting accounted for center, demographics, vascular risk factors and comorbidities, anticoagulation, competing stroke causes, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, prestroke modified Rankin Scale, and time to blood collection.
RESULTS: Among 1649 patients enrolled in ASPERA-R, 671 patients from 14 centers had complete biomarker data (median age, 80.1 years [interquartile range, 73.5-85.5]; 52.3% female). Of these, 223 (33.2%) had high inflammatory burden, and 448 (66.8%) had lower inflammatory burden. After weighting, high inflammatory burden was associated with increased risks of ischemic events at 90 days (hazard ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.02-2.30]), all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.70 [95% CI, 1.17-2.47]), moderate-to-severe bleeding (hazard ratio, 2.92 [95% CI, 1.04-8.17]), and hemorrhagic transformation at 24 hours (odds ratio, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.43-3.33]).
CONCLUSIONS: In breakthrough ischemic stroke, high inflammatory burden was associated with increased risks of recurrent ischemic events, mortality, hemorrhagic transformation, and major bleeding. A composite of routinely available inflammatory biomarkers may help identify patients with higher residual vascular risk.

Title: VSMC DDR1 Mechanosensation Aggravates Atherosclerosis via Paracrine Signaling.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases cardiovascular risk and is linked to arterial stiffening and atherosclerosis. How stiffness promotes atherogenesis remains unclear. DDR1 (discoidin domain receptor 1), a mechanosensory tyrosine kinase receptor, has been implicated in force-regulated arterial remodeling. We investigated whether DDR1-mediated mechanosensation links arterial stiffness to vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC)-endothelial paracrine communication in CKD-related atherosclerosis.
METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, secretome proteomics, and bulk RNA sequencing were integrated with stiffness-controlled models, endothelial assays, and a CKD-hyperlipidemia mouse model. SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion and a DDR1 dephosphorylation-targeting chimera (DEPTAC) were evaluated in vivo. Plasma TSP-1 (thrombospondin-1) levels were quantified in a CKD clinical cohort and analyzed in relation to renal function and atherosclerosis severity.
RESULTS: CKD-associated vascular stiffening coincided with SMC phenotypic switching and enhanced THBS signaling. Multiomics integration identified THBS1 as a stiffness-induced SMC secretory effector. Stiff matrices increased SMC THBS1 secretion, promoting endothelial proliferation, migration, and leukocyte adhesion; these effects were attenuated by THBS1 knockdown. DDR1 coupled matrix stiffness cues to THBS1 expression by regulating its transcription via a tyrosine 3-monooxygenase/tryptophan 5-monooxygenase activation protein epsilon-FOXO3 (forkhead box O3) axis. Vascular SMC-specific Ddr1 deletion reduced aortic THBS1 levels, vascular stiffening, and atherosclerotic burden. DEPTAC suppressed aberrant DDR1 phosphorylation, reduced THBS1, and ameliorated vascular stiffening and atherosclerosis. Plasma THBS1 increased with CKD severity and correlated with atherosclerosis.
CONCLUSIONS: DDR1-dependent mechanosensing in SMCs drives stiffness-induced paracrine signaling to endothelium via THBS1, promoting CKD-accelerated atherosclerosis. Targeting mechanical DDR1 activation may be therapeutic.

Title: F2R Polymorphisms and Efficacy of Clopidogrel Initiated Within 72 Hours for Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to investigate the association between PAR-1 (protease-activated receptor-1) gene F2R polymorphisms and the efficacy of clopidogrel therapy initiated within a time window extended to 72 hours for mild ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack with intracranial or extracranial atherosclerosis.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of the INSPIRES trial (Intensive Statin and Antiplatelet Therapy for Acute High-Risk Intracranial or Extracranial Atherosclerosis), a randomized clinical trial conducted at 222 centers across China between September 2018 and October 2022. Four single-nucleotide polymorphisms (F2R [IVSn-14 A/T, rs168753], CYP2C19*2 [681G>A, rs4244285], CYP2C19*3 [636G>A, rs4986893], and CYP2C19*17 [-806C>T, rs12248560]) were genotyped among 5791 patients treated with clopidogrel plus aspirin (n=2894) or aspirin alone (n=2897). The primary efficacy outcome was new stroke, and the safety outcome was moderate-to-severe bleeding within 90 days. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate the interaction between treatment assignment and F2R polymorphisms for the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 5791 patients, 1698 (29.3%) were AA homozygotes, and 4093 (70.7%) were the T-allele carriers (AT/TT) for F2R IVSn-14 polymorphisms. Compared with aspirin alone, clopidogrel-aspirin reduced the rate of new stroke in patients with AT/TT genotype (7.1% versus 9.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.77 [95% CI, 0.62-0.95]; P=0.02) but not in carriers of the AA genotype (7.7% versus 8.1%; HR, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.67-1.33]; P=0.75; P=0.30 for interaction). For the safety outcome, the risk of moderate-to-severe bleeding between the clopidogrel plus aspirin group and aspirin group was not significant in patients with AT/TT genotype (HR, 1.91 [95% CI, 0.85-4.29]; P=0.12) or AA genotype (HR, 1.97 [95% CI, 0.59-6.55]; P=0.27; P=0.97 for interaction). Moreover, the presence of CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele carrier status did not alter the effect of the F2R polymorphisms on clinical outcomes, although a marginally reduced risk of stroke with clopidogrel-aspirin versus aspirin alone was observed only among carriers of at least 1 F2R IVSn-14 T allele without CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.52-1.01]; P=0.06).
CONCLUSIONS: With the treatment initiated within a time window extended to 72 hours after mild ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack onset, we found that clopidogrel plus aspirin may reduce the occurrence of new stroke specifically in F2R IVSn-14 T-allele carriers. This finding suggests that the clopidogrel-aspirin treatment may appear more beneficial among carriers of the F2R IVSn-14 T allele.

Title: Lithium Concentrations After Initiation or Discontinuation of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Psychiatric Inpatients: A Case Series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce cardiovascular and renal risk, but coprescription with lithium raises concern because lithium elimination is linked to renal sodium handling. Prescribing information recommends lithium monitoring after SGLT2i initiation or dose changes, although clinical evidence remains limited, particularly after discontinuation. We describe lithium concentrations and clinical evolution after SGLT2i initiation or discontinuation in lithium-treated psychiatric inpatients.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series at a psychiatric hospital. Pharmacy records identified patients who received lithium and an SGLT2i between January 1, 2014 and March 31, 2026. Patients were included if the SGLT2i was initiated or discontinued while lithium was continued and ≥1 lithium concentration was available before and after modification. Clinical pharmacists reviewed records for lithium dose and concentrations, SGLT2i exposure, renal function, interacting medications, acute illness, hydration status, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Six cases were identified: 3 initiations and 3 discontinuations. Lithium concentrations showed no consistent directional change. After initiation, concentrations remained stable or changed minimally in 2 cases and increased slightly in one. After discontinuation, lithium remained stable in an older patient with chronic kidney disease, increased slightly in 1 case confounded by lithium dose escalation, and increased from 0.6 to 0.8 mmol/l in 1 case complicated by pneumonia, diarrhea, and dehydration. No case required urgent lithium discontinuation, toxicity treatment, or prolonged hospitalization attributed to lithium.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i initiation or discontinuation was not associated with consistent or clinically concerning lithium changes. These observations suggest coprescription may be manageable with individualized monitoring when clinically indicated.

Title: Comprehensive Clinical, Neuroradiologic, and Oral Health of 23 Individuals With MOPDII: Molecular Spectrum and Phenotypic Features.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type II (MOPDII; MIM #210720) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by severe growth failure and microcephaly, frequently complicated by central nervous system (CNS) anomalies and early-onset cerebrovascular disease. This study aimed to define the neurologic, radiologic, molecular, and oral-dental features of a MOPDII cohort, with particular emphasis on cerebrovascular involvement, and to assess genotype-phenotype correlations.
METHODS: Molecular diagnosis was established using next-generation sequencing, including targeted gene panel sequencing (n = 11) and exome sequencing (n = 1), or Sanger sequencing (n = 11). Clinical data, neuroimaging and vascular findings, systematic oral-dental examinations, and molecular results were retrospectively reviewed.
RESULTS: Twenty-three patients from 18 unrelated consanguineous families were included. Seventeen distinct homozygous PCNT variants were identified, including 5 splice-site, 5 frameshift, and 7 nonsense variants; of these, 12 were novel. Structural CNS anomalies were common, with the thin corpus callosum being the most frequent finding, observed in 14 of 17 patients (82%) who underwent cranial imaging. Moyamoya disease was identified in 12 patients (70.5%), of whom 7 experienced chronic or acute cerebral infarctions and/or intracranial hemorrhage. Three patients with moyamoya disease died of complications related to vascular involvement. The 2 oldest patients developed severe peripheral arterial and coronary artery occlusions, leading to spontaneous limb amputation and acute myocardial infarction. Oral-dental evaluation, performed in 14 patients (61%), revealed microdontia, malformed teeth, and root shortening. No consistent genotype-phenotype correlation was identified for cerebrovascular or orodental manifestations.
DISCUSSION: MOPDII is strongly associated with moyamoya disease and represents a major cause of neurologic morbidity and mortality. Early and longitudinal neuroimaging, including brain MRI and angiographic assessment, should be integral to patient management. Oral-dental abnormalities are common and merit routine evaluation.

Title: The quality and reliability of short videos about Marfan syndrome on Bilibili and Douyin: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome (MS) is a rare, life-threatening connective tissue disorder. Short video platforms are now key health-information sources, yet the quality and reliability of MS-related content remain unclear.
METHODS: In a cross-sectional study, Marfan syndrome videos were retrieved from Bilibili and Douyin on 25 April 2026 using the Chinese keyword "," from new accounts under anonymous browsing. After screening, data on video characteristics, uploader type, and publicly displayed likes, comments, shares, and collections were extracted. Two reviewers independently scored all eligible videos with Global Quality Scale (GQS), modified Decision-making Information Support Criteria for Evaluating the Reliability of Non-randomised Studies (mDISCERN), Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) criteria, and Content Completeness Score (CCS). Descriptive statistics, non-parametric tests, Spearman correlations, and weighted Cohen's kappa were used.
RESULTS: 185 videos (103 from Douyin and 82 from Bilibili) were analyzed. The median video duration was significantly longer on Bilibili than on Douyin (126.00 (IQR: 59.00-377.00) vs. 64.00 (IQR: 45.50-103.50) seconds; P < 0.001). Douyin videos had been available for a significantly shorter time since publication (median: 275.00 vs. 747.50 days; P < 0.001), yet their per-day interaction counts remained significantly higher after this adjustment (all P < 0.001). Douyin videos demonstrated significantly higher absolute interaction counts, including likes (median: 2,214.00 vs. 48.00; P < 0.001), comments (240.00 vs. 0.00; P < 0.001), shares (606.00 vs. 5.50; P < 0.001), and collections (475.00 vs. 24.00; P < 0.001). In terms of quality, Douyin videos had higher GQS scores than Bilibili (median: 4.00 vs. 3.00; P < 0.001), whereas Bilibili videos showed higher mDISCERN scores (median: 3.00 vs. 2.00; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in JAMA scores (P = 0.245) or CCS (P = 0.274). Healthcare professionals accounted for the majority of Douyin content (78.6%), while institutional sources predominated on Bilibili (53.7%) (P < 0.001). Videos produced by professionals and institutions achieved significantly higher quality and reliability scores compared to individual uploaders. Spearman correlation analysis revealed strong correlations among engagement metrics (r = 0.84-0.94), but weak or negligible correlations between absolute interaction counts and quality scores (r = -0.16 to 0.17).
CONCLUSION: Marfan syndrome-related videos on Bilibili and Douyin varied considerably in educational quality and reliability; those by healthcare professionals were generally higher quality. Within this sample, observed interaction counts showed weak or negligible associations with quality measures.

Title: Risankizumab in Psoriasis: Real-World Effectiveness, Safety, and Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risankizumab (anti-IL-23 p19) is an established therapy for moderate-to-severe psoriasis, with strong trial efficacy and growing real-world evidence. However, long-duration outcomes and treatment-spacing patterns from the Gulf region remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term effectiveness, safety, and treatment patterns-including extended-interval dosing-of Risankizumab in a real-world tertiary center.
METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort of adults treated with Risankizumab between January 2020 and January 2025. Primary outcome: Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) 100 on last visit. Secondary outcomes: changes in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI), body surface area (BSA), and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) and Nail Psoriasis Severity Index (NAPSI); adverse events; treatment persistence and dosing intervals. Non-parametric tests were used; predictors of PASI 100 were explored with multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: We included 144 patients (mean age 39.3±14.9 years; 55.6% male; mean BMI 29.0±6.5). At last visit, 61.1% achieved PASI 100. Mean scores improved from baseline to last visit: PASI 7.24→0.34, BSA 9.81%→0.26%, DLQI 7.64→0.68, NAPSI 9.56→2.94 (all p<0.001). Adverse events were infrequent (3.5%), all mild; no major adverse cardiovascular events or deaths occurred. A single case of lung cancer was reported and considered unlikely to be treatment related. A quarter of patients transitioned to extended intervals (most commonly every 4-6 months), with the majority maintaining disease control and relapse occurring infrequently and only after ≥6 months. Longer treatment duration and maintenance of standard dosing frequency were associated with achieving PASI 100, while positive family history was associated with lower odds of complete clearance.
CONCLUSION: In routine practice, Risankizumab achieved high complete-clearance rates with excellent tolerability over ~31 months' mean exposure. Extended-interval dosing was feasible in selected stable responders. These findings align with trial durability and regional registry signals and support individualized long-term strategies.

Title: The Rising Burden of Atrial Fibrillation and Respiratory Failure Mortality in the United States: A 25-Year Nationwide Retrospective Analysis of Death Certificate Data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and respiratory failure (RF) frequently co-occur in critically ill patients, but long-term national trends in deaths recording both remain unknown.
METHODS: CDC WONDER multiple-cause-of-death data identified U.S. adults aged ≥ 55 years with both AF (including atrial flutter) and RF listed on death certificates from 1999 to 2024. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were estimated using joinpoint regression. Sensitivity analyses included adults aged ≥ 25 years, exclusion of COVID-19-related deaths, and stratification by co-listed heart failure (HF).
RESULTS: A total of 462 284 deaths listed both AF and RF. The AAMR increased roughly five-fold (7.84 to 41.76 per 100 000), rising steadily through 2018 (APC 7.81), accelerating through 2021 (APC 18.78), and declining thereafter (APC -5.90). Excluding deaths listing COVID-19, the 2018-2021 acceleration was not detected, and AAMRs rose through 2024 (2017-2024 APC 5.25). AAMRs for deaths without HF recorded rose over fourfold. Mean AAMRs were higher in males (26.19) than in females (19.04) and in non-Hispanic (NH) White adults (24.06) than in other groups. The West and nonmetropolitan areas had the highest rates. The 2018-2021 surge was steepest among Hispanic (APC 25.62) and NH Black adults (APC 24.06).
CONCLUSIONS: Population mortality rates for deaths recording both AF and RF increased substantially over 25 years, beginning before the COVID-19 pandemic, persisting after excluding deaths listing COVID-19, and occurring with and without HF recorded. These data cannot separate changes in disease occurrence from changes in diagnosis or coding.

Title: Posterior Pulmonary Vein Isolation Lesion Spacing and Left Atrial Posterior Wall Narrowing During Pulsed Field Ablation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial posterior wall (LAPW) narrowing after excessive extension of bilateral pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) lines during pulsed field ablation (PFA) may create a proarrhythmic substrate. The CARTO 3-integrated variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC) provides real-time tissue proximity indication (TPI) and ablation-tag location, but their relationship with LAPW narrowing remains unclear. Therefore, we evaluated associations of TPI status and inter-tag distance (ITD) with acute LAPW narrowing and whether an ITD-guided workflow was associated with LAPW preservation.
METHODS: Fifty-two retrospective and 27 prospective atrial fibrillation patients underwent PFA using a VLCC. In the retrospective phase, we evaluated the association between ITD, measured using TPI-positive tags and all tags, and LAPW narrowing (< 10 mm) and derived a cutoff. In the prospective phase, the ITD-guided workflow was applied, and we assessed residual LAPW band width.
RESULTS: In the retrospective phase, both TPI-positive-tag ITD and all-tag ITD correlated with LAPW band width (r = 0.63 and 0.70, respectively; both p < 0.001). All-tag ITD showed a numerically higher AUC for LAPW narrowing than TPI-positive-tag ITD (0.869 vs. 0.795; p = 0.099), with an optimal all-tag ITD cutoff of 16.5 mm. In the prospective phase incorporating the all-tag ITD cutoff, residual LAPW band widths were wider at the roof (19.4 ± 7.9 vs. 25.1 ± 7.1 mm; p = 0.002) and carina (13.6 ± 7.1 vs. 20.8 ± 8.0 mm; p < 0.001) than in the retrospective phase.
CONCLUSIONS: An all-tag ITD-guided workflow was associated with greater preservation of the residual LAPW band width.

Title: Clinical Utility of Serum Neuropeptide Q in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Case-Control Observational Pilot Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Current cardiac biomarkers lack specificity and are limited by instrumental constraints in diagnosing acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Therefore, research has focused on identifying new cardiac biomarkers, e.g., neuropeptide Q (NPQ), associated with the pathophysiological response to myocardial injury. NPQ plays an important role in metabolic regulation and cardiac protection. As there are limited studies on the role of NPQ in ACS, we assessed serum NPQ levels in ACS patients and healthy populations to evaluate serum NPQ's clinical utility in ACS.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We recruited ACS patients (n = 120) and non-hospitalized healthy participants (n = 40). The baseline characteristics and history were recorded. Biochemical investigations, including serum NPQ and heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), were measured using blood samples collected at a mean of 24 hours after the onset of chest pain in ACS patients and at the time of enrolment of healthy participants. Appropriate statistical tests were performed.
RESULTS: ACS patients had significantly higher serum NPQ and H-FABP levels as compared to healthy participants. Serum NPQ levels showed a significant positive correlation with weight, waist circumference, creatine kinase-total, creatine kinase-MB, and H-FABP levels and showed a significant negative correlation with white blood cells (WBCs) and serum high-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-C) levels. In univariate logistic regression, weight, WBC, HDL-C, and NPQ levels were linked with ACS outcome in study participants. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, after adjusting for potential confounders, WBC and NPQ were independently linked with ACS outcome in the study population. Receiver operating characteristic curve evaluation showed that the cut-off value of serum NPQ level for prediction of ACS was 2.53 ng/mL, with a specificity of 67.5%, sensitivity of 71%, and an area under the curve of 0.808 (95% CI: 0.731-0.886).
CONCLUSION: The study showed that the reported performance characteristics of serum NPQ levels strictly differentiate between established ACS patients and apparently healthy participants. Its diagnostic utility when facing a standard chest-pain differential diagnosis remains completely unknown. However, our findings should be confirmed by further studies.

Title: Predicting 365-Day Lower-Limb Amputation at Discharge After Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Hospitalization: Development and Temporal Validation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients discharged after diabetes-related foot ulcer hospitalization remain at risk of limb loss. We developed and temporally validated discharge-time models for 365-day amputation, comparing clinical-plus-discharge predictors with a fuller set including contextual information.
METHODS: Epic Cosmos provided 431 493 development patients discharged in 2016-2024 and 36 823 temporal-validation patients discharged in January-June 2025. Cause-specific Cox models estimated any and major amputation with death as a competing event. Model C included clinical, contextual, and discharge variables; Model D omitted contextual variables. Models were compared using discrimination, calibration, and decision curves.
RESULTS: Observed 365-day cumulative incidences were 19.3% for any amputation and 6.4% for major amputation. Model C areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.710 and 0.737, compared with 0.711 and 0.736 for Model D. Corresponding calibration slopes were 1.003 and 1.026 for Model C and 1.010 and 1.025 for Model D. Brier scores were similar. Gangrene and peripheral artery disease had the largest joint Wald statistics in Model C. Its highest-risk quintile contained 40.6% of any-amputation and 49.6% of major-amputation events.
CONCLUSIONS: Models C and D showed similar performance, with moderate discrimination and risk enrichment. These findings do not establish superiority of the fuller model, irrelevance of contextual factors, or improved patient outcomes. Independent validation, local recalibration, and prospective impact evaluation are required before clinical use.

Title: 1-Methylhistidine attenuates early myocardial inflammation in type 3 cardiorenal syndrome through modulation of the p105/p50 NF-κB axis.
Abstract: Type 3 cardiorenal syndrome (CRS3) is characterized by cardiac injury or dysfunction secondary to acute kidney injury (AKI), yet the contribution of AKI-associated metabolic remodeling to early myocardial inflammation remains poorly understood. Here, paired serum and myocardial untargeted metabolomics identified 1-methylhistidine (1-MH) as a metabolite elevated in both compartments, with the highest variable importance in projection score in serum. Exogenous 1-MH improved the E/A ratio and attenuated myocardial inflammation and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) positivity in rats with CRS3. Similar protective effects were observed in a separate post-ischemic cohort in which 1-MH was administered immediately after renal reperfusion. In CRS serum-exposed H9c2 cells, 1-MH reduced reactive oxygen species-associated fluorescence, malondialdehyde content, and intracellular Fe2+ levels. Transcriptomic profiling showed that 1-MH suppressed inflammatory signaling, accompanied by changes in oxidative metabolism. Integration of these transcriptomic signatures with target prediction prioritized NFKB1/p105, while ensemble docking identified recurrent candidate interaction regions within p105. Cellular thermal shift assays showed a concentration-related increase in p105 thermal stability following 1-MH treatment. 1-MH increased p105 abundance while reducing total p50 abundance and nuclear p50 accumulation. p105 overexpression increased p50 abundance and the expression of inflammatory transcripts and proteins suppressed by 1-MH. These findings demonstrate that 1-MH attenuates early myocardial inflammation in CRS3 and reduces oxidative stress-related changes in CRS serum-exposed H9c2 cells. These functional results support modulation of the p105/p50 NF-κB axis and identify p105 as a molecular link between AKI-associated metabolic remodeling and myocardial inflammatory signaling.

Title: Diuretics for Management of Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Associated Pulmonary Hypertension in Preterm Infants-A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia associated pulmonary hypertension (BPD-PH) in preterm infants results from impaired pulmonary vascular development and contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality. Diuretics are commonly used to reduce pulmonary vascular congestion and improve oxygenation, but their efficacy and safety remain unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of diuretic use in preterm infants with BPD-PH. Primary outcomes were mortality and need for home respiratory support; secondary outcomes were echocardiographic and clinical parameters, and adverse effects such as hyponatremia, nephrocalcinosis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to October 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized studies of interventions (NRSI) evaluating diuretics in preterm infants (< 32 weeks' gestation) with BPD-PH diagnosed by echocardiography at 36 weeks postmenstrual age. Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment (ROBINS-I). Outcomes were synthesized narratively, and a meta-analysis was performed where sufficient data were available. Of 492 studies identified, 2 NRSI (n = 49) met inclusion criteria, both were at serious risk of bias. No RCTs exist on diuretics for BPD-PH in preterm infants. Mortality, respiratory, discharge outcomes and adverse effects were reported inconsistently. Meta-analysis of limited data demonstrated small improvements in echocardiographic markers, but the certainty of evidence was very low due to heterogeneity between the two included studies. To conclude, evidence supporting the use of diuretics in BPD-PH in preterm infants remains limited and of low certainty. High quality studies are needed to better define their safety and efficacy.

Title: Developing proficiency in a transcatheter aortic valve replacement program: lessons from a single academic center's learning curve.
Journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a prevalent and high-mortality valve disease. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is a minimally invasive treatment with outcomes often better than surgery, requiring a multidisciplinary team. This study analyzes outcomes and trends from a high-volume TAVR program in an urban, low-income setting since 2017 to guide future practices.
METHODS: Medical records of patients that underwent TAVR were analyzed retrospectively from 2018 to 2023, dividing them into two cohorts to analyze trends in operative details, complications, length of stay (LOS), and readmission/mortality rates. The learning curve (LC) was assessed by operative time.
RESULTS: Risk-adjusted cumulative sum (RA-CUSUM) analysis identified the transition point at case 76, dividing the cohort into early LC phase group (n = 76) and post-LC phase group (n = 190). Median operative time decreased from 106 to 80 minutes. After adjustment, operative time was 14% shorter in the post-learning-curve cohort (GMR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.96; p = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: Operative time serves as a useful benchmark for institutional maturation. In our program, reaching 76 cases represented a key transition point toward optimized workflows, enhanced efficiency, and improved resource utilization.

Title: Testosterone replacement therapy and aneurysm biology: current evidence and clinical implications.
Journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is increasingly used to treat male hypogonadism, but its role in aneurysm biology remains unclear. Because aneurysm formation is driven by inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation, and vascular remodeling, testosterone may influence disease progression through androgen receptor-mediated pathways.
METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Google Scholar (August-September 2025). Studies examining testosterone, TRT, vascular inflammation, and aneurysm-related outcomes, including experimental, preclinical, and clinical studies, were included.
EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Available evidence is mostly mechanistic and preclinical. Animal studies indicate vascular bed-specific effects: physiological androgen signaling seems protective in abdominal aortic aneurysm models by reducing macrophage infiltration and inflammatory cytokine signaling, whereas exogenous or supraphysiologic testosterone may exacerbate oxidative stress and vascular injury in intracranial aneurysm models. Human data remain indirect, with no prospective studies specifically assessing aneurysm formation, growth, or rupture in TRT users. Large randomized trials and meta-analyses indicate cardiovascular safety comparable to placebo in appropriately selected patients, though higher rates of atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, and erythrocytosis have been reported.
CONCLUSION: Testosterone has context-, dose-, and vascular bed-specific effects on aneurysm biology. Until clinical studies on aneurysm outcomes are available, TRT should be individualized, dosed to meet physiological needs, and closely monitored for cardiovascular and vascular health. No evidence-based recommendation can currently be made to initiate, withhold, or modify TRT solely on the basis of aneurysm status. Multidisciplinary discussion and continued standard aneurysm surveillance are advisable for hypogonadal patients with known aneurysmal disease.

Title: Pulmonary vasoreactive reserve in patients with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension: characteristics and clinical significance.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We hypothesized that differences in pulmonary hemodynamics during acute vasoreactive testing (AVT), beyond the conventional Sitbon criteria, may be described as pulmonary vasoreactive reserve (VRR) that could be used to assess disease severity and prognosis in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) patients. The study aimed to evaluate the clinical significance of VRR in patients with IPAH.
METHODS: Ninety adult IPAH patients (40.4 ± 14.6 years, 14.3% males) from a prospective single-center PAH registry were divided into three groups based on mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) decrease during AVT: Group I (n = 25): ΔmPAP > 30%; Group II (n = 13): ΔmPAP 15%-30%; and Group III (n = 52): ΔmPAP < 15%. A comparison was performed between the standard model of survival prediction using the 2022 European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) three-strata risk stratification scale and the experimental model with ΔmPAP grading.
RESULTS: The absolute value of ΔmPAP was 21 mmHg (14; 28) in Group I, 11 mmHg (10; 12) in Group II, and only 2.5 mm Hg (1; 4.5) in Group III. The Δ%mPAP significantly differed in low-, intermediate-, and high-risk 2022 ESC/ERS three-strata categories (32.4 (12.3; 42.2) vs. 12.9 (3.01; 28.2) vs. 4.8% (1.8; 8.9), p = 0.0009). Significant association was revealed between the Δ%mPAP and pulmonary artery compliance (r = 0.30; p = 0.0045), pulmonary artery distensibility (r = 0.37, p = 0.0058), and cardiopulmonary exercise test parameters. During a follow-up of 2.32 years (1.04; 4.06), 17 (18.8%) patients died. The survival rate was 93%, 83%, 78%, 62%, and 55% at 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10 years, respectively. The degree of Δ%mPAP [heart rate (HR) 5.99 (1.37-26.2), p = 0.017], N-terminal pro-brain-type natriuretic peptide > 1,100 pg/mL [HR 8.1 (1.67-39.2), p = 0.009], and the number of PAH-specific drugs [HR 0.07 (0.018-0.3), p = 0.0003] were considered independent predictors of survival. The inclusion of Δ%mPAP slightly improved prognostic value for the 2022 ESC/ERS three-strata risk stratification scale in comparison with the standard 2022 ESC/ERS three-strata approach (mean absolute percentage error, MAPE = 9.66%; C-index = 0.7552742616033755 vs. MAPE = 9.82%; C-index = 0.7510548523206751).
CONCLUSION: The assessment of VRR may warrant further investigation as an additional marker of the disease severity and prognosis in IPAH patients.

Title: Optimization of direct oral anticoagulant prescribing in primary care: a pharmacotherapeutic review in real-world clinical practice and therapeutic efficiency.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants are among the first-line treatments for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment and secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism. The increasing use of these agents poses challenges related to prescribing appropriateness, clinical safety. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, quasi-experimental before-and-after study was conducted in the healthcare area of Xarxa Santa Tecla (Tarragonès and Baix Penedès, Spain). 791 patients receiving DOAC therapy were included. The intervention comprised multidisciplinary educational activities, individualized pharmacotherapeutic review, and communication of recommendations to prescribers.
RESULTS: The mean age was 78.2 years, and 43.2% of patients had moderate or severe renal impairment. The pharmacotherapeutic review identified 527 patients (66.6%) as candidates for treatment optimization, through a proposed switch from apixaban to dabigatran. The pharmacist intervention was associated with changes in prescribing patterns among newly initiated patients, increasing the use of dabigatran. The economic analysis estimated savings of €75,508.81 from new treatment initiations and €31,288.25 from therapeutic switches, resulting in total savings of €106,797.06 in 2025. The overall bleeding rate remained stable (5.3% in 2024% vs. 5.2% in 2025), with no deterioration in clinical safety. In conclusion, a structured, multidisciplinary, and coordinated primary care pharmacist-led intervention promoted a more efficient use of healthcare resources, while no deterioration in population-level safety indicators was observed. These findings reinforce the role of primary care pharmacists in optimizing anticoagulant therapy.

Title: Gut microbiome and gut-derived metabolites to identify the transition from metabolically healthy to unhealthy obesity: a mini review.
Abstract: Obesity is a metabolically heterogeneous condition with distinct metabolic phenotypes, ranging from metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) to metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). Although individuals with MHO initially lack cardiometabolic dysfunction, many transition to MUO over time, exponentially increasing their risk for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. In this mini-review, we synthesize recent evidence from multi-omic cohort studies evaluating gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites as functional biomarkers of obesity heterogeneity and drivers of metabolic decline. While microbial diversity yields inconsistent signatures across cohorts, MHO is generally characterized by higher relative abundance of Ruminococcaceae, Oscillospira, Akkermansia, and Bifidobacterium and enrichment of other taxa predicted to be short-chain fatty acid-producers. Conversely, circulating gut-derived metabolomic signatures including altered secondary bile acid pools, elevated branched-chain amino acids, and trimethylamine N-oxide more reliably discriminate MUO from MHO than traditional measures, and correlate strongly with visceral adiposity, insulin resistance, and systemic inflammation. Furthermore, new systems biology approaches, such as integrating high-dimensional metagenomics and metabolomics via machine learning models, offer a potentially superior early indicators tool in precision medicine for identifying obesity phenotypes compared with traditional metrics (e.g., body mass index, fasting glucose). Overall, current evidence remains predominantly cross-sectional and based on secondary analyses of large cohort studies, underscoring the need for prospective longitudinal studies to validate these multi-omic biomarkers for precise phenotype identification and clinical risk assessment.

Title: Teaching AI, teaching bias: addressing gender inequality in public health education.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly shapes healthcare, public health and health professions education. However, predictive and generative systems can reproduce or amplify longstanding inequalities embedded in data, institutions and established knowledge structures. Public health education therefore needs to connect technical approaches to identifying and mitigating algorithmic bias with their broader social, population health and institutional contexts. This conceptual article presents the sociotechnical Bias literacy for public health education framework (SBL-PHE), developed through a theory-informed conceptual synthesis drawing on conceptual framework analysis. A focused supplementary literature search in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ERIC and the ACM digital library was conducted to examine and refine its theoretical foundations. An evidence-informed composite case of AI-supported cardiovascular risk assessment traces algorithmic gender bias from knowledge production and data representation through modeling and implementation to monitoring. The framework comprises five interconnected competency dimensions concerned with recognizing, explaining, evaluating, addressing and reflecting on algorithmic bias. For master's-level public health education, these dimensions are linked to learning objectives, learning activities, assessment methods and a prospective evaluation strategy. Sociotechnical Bias literacy is proposed as a foundational competency for public health professionals who use or interpret AI. Sociotechnical fluency describes an advanced, role-dependent capability, particularly for responsibilities in implementation, evaluation, translation and governance. SBL-PHE provides a theoretically grounded framework for integrating technical understanding, health equity, professional judgment and institutional responsibility into public health education. The framework and its proposed educational application have not yet been empirically validated.

Title: External validation of the D-PACE score for predicting late high-grade atrioventricular block after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a Colombian cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries a clinically significant risk of late high-grade atrioventricular block (AVB), yet no validated tool exists to predict this complication in Latin-American populations. The D-PACE score was developed in European cohorts for this purpose.
METHODS: In a retrospective cohort of 175 consecutive TAVR procedures at a Colombian center (2012-2025), 141 patients met inclusion criteria for D-PACE validation. The primary outcome was late high-grade AVB (≥Mobitz type II) occurring between 24 h and 30 days post-TAVR. Discrimination, logistic-regression calibration, and decision curve analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Late AVB occurred in 31 patients (22.0%), with 80.6% of events within 72 h. The D-PACE score demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71-0.92; sensitivity 77.4%, specificity 86.4% at a cutoff of 5.5 points; NPV 93.1%). Late AVB rates rose progressively across strata: 5.9% (low-risk, score 0-3), 8.8% (intermediate, 4-5), and 61.5% (high-risk, ≥6), with the high-risk group concentrating 77.4% of all events. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities from 8% to 60%. All four low-risk events occurred among valve-in-valve patients assigned a score of 0 per the original algorithm; excluding this subgroup (N = 114), the AUC rose to 0.91 (95% CI 0.85-0.96) with zero low-risk events. In an exploratory analysis applying the full seven-variable scoring uniformly, including valve-in-valve cases, the AUC was 0.90 (95% CI 0.85-0.95; NPV 96.7%), and 0.91 (95% CI 0.78-1.00) within the valve-in-valve subgroup (N = 27, 4 events).
CONCLUSIONS: Applied as originally specified, the D-PACE score showed good discrimination for late high-grade AVB in this cohort (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71-0.92). The algorithm's automatic low-risk classification of valve-in-valve patients was not supported (14.8% AVB rate). Discrimination was higher both in the sensitivity analysis excluding valve-in-valve cases and in the exploratory analysis applying the seven-variable scoring uniformly, indicating that the scoring variables transfer well while the valve-in-valve exemption warrants reconsideration. These findings provide the first external validation of D-PACE in Latin America.

Title: [Clinical characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of patients receiving antithrombotic therapy in a cardiac intensive care unit in sub-Saharan Africa: a retrospective comparative study at the Cardiology Institute of Abidjan].
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: antithrombotic therapies are essential in the management of cardiovascular diseases but carry a risk of bleeding complications. This study aimed to describe the use of antithrombotic agents and associated complications in a Cardiac Intensive Care Unit, and to analyse trends in their prescription over time.
METHODS: we conducted a retrospective, observational, descriptive, and analytical study including 1,000 patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit of the Institute of Cardiology of Abidjan who received at least one antithrombotic therapy over 12 years. Data were collected in two phases, from 2013 to 2017 and from 2018 to 2024, allowing for the analysis of temporal trends.
RESULTS: the mean age was 59.5 ± 14.1 years. Hypertension was the most prevalent cardiovascular risk factor, and acute coronary syndrome was the main indication for antithrombotic therapy. The proportion of patients receiving antithrombotic treatment increased significantly between the two study periods (76.5% vs 78.7%, p = 0.004). The use of fibrinolytic agents also increased significantly (2.6% vs 6.6%). Adverse events related to antithrombotic therapy were predominantly hemorrhagic, with independent risk factors including advanced age (>65 years), use of fibrinolytics, and concomitant use of multiple antithrombotic agents. In-hospital mortality was higher in patients with hemorrhagic events, with no significant difference between the two periods.
CONCLUSION: antithrombotic therapies remain widely used in Cardiac Intensive Care Units in sub-Saharan Africa, with an increasing trend in prescriptions. Rigorous clinical and laboratory monitoring is essential to improve patient outcomes.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study; English Abstract

Title: Gastrointestinal manifestations in adult IgA vasculitis over 8.5 years: severity assessment and therapeutic outcomes.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: IgA vasculitis (IgAV), formerly known as Henoch-Schönlein purpura, is a small-vessel systemic vasculitis predominantly affecting children. In adults, IgAV is a rare disease; gastrointestinal (GI) involvement is nonetheless more frequent and severe than in the pediatric population, significantly impacting short-term prognosis. Data on GI manifestations in adult IgAV remain limited, and therapeutic management is not well codified.
METHODS: we conducted a descriptive observational study of adult patients (≥16 years) diagnosed with IgAV according to the 1990 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) or the 2012 Chapel Hill Consensus Conference (CHCC) criteria, admitted to the Internal Medicine Department of Farhat Hached University Hospital, Sousse, over the years. Gastrointestinal involvement was defined by clinical manifestations combined with at least one objective criterion (imaging or endoscopic/histological findings). Clinical and radiological severity were assessed using the Trouillier scoring system. Prolonged remission was defined as the absence of GI symptoms for at least six months after completion of corticosteroid therapy.
RESULTS: among 30 patients diagnosed with IgAV, twenty-nine patients were included in the primary analysis (mean age: 45.6±18.1 years; gender ratio: 0.87) and one patient with concurrent gastric MALT lymphoma was analyzed separately. Gastrointestinal involvement occurred in 20 patients (66.7%). The most common symptom was abdominal pain (100%), followed by vomiting (70%) and GI bleeding (40%). Severe disease was identified in 45% by clinical scoring and in 39% by radiological assessment. Corticosteroid therapy achieved prolonged remission in 63% of patients. Male gender showed a non-significant trend toward increased GI involvement (p=0.058).
CONCLUSION: gastrointestinal manifestations in adult IgAV are frequent and often severe. The low patient accrual rate (3.5 cases/year) reflects the rarity of IgAV in adults, a disease predominantly affecting children.

Title: Mechanism-defined secondary hypertension enables precision diagnosis and treatment: an evidence review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary hypertension is under-recognised despite the availability of mechanism-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause-directed treatment.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically synthesise evidence across the principal causes of secondary hypertension using a mechanism → diagnosis → therapy framework; to compare diagnostic performance and cause-directed treatment effects; and to examine concordance between contemporary society guidelines and real-world implementation.
METHODS: This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, with diagnostic accuracy reporting informed by PRISMA-DTA. MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO ICTRP were searched from inception to 30 June 2025, supplemented by citation searching. The formal search identified 580 records; after removal of 168 duplicates, 412 records were screened, 106 full-text reports were assessed, and 58 included evidence records were represented across 63 publications. The review was not prospectively registered in PROSPERO. Screening, extraction and structured appraisal were performed by a single reviewer (the first author); therefore, no dual-reviewer agreement statistic was applicable. Risk of bias was appraised with RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUADAS-2, and AMSTAR 2 as appropriate, and certainty was summarised using GRADE. A targeted post-search surveillance update through 31 July 2026 was used only to contextualise major newly available guidelines and Phase 3 trial reports and did not alter the original PRISMA counts.
RESULTS: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is best understood as a continuum of renin-independent aldosterone excess: in Brown et al. [The unrecognized prevalence of primary aldosteronism: a cross-sectional study. Ann Intern Med. (2020) 173:10-20], biochemically overt autonomous aldosterone production was present in 11.3%, 15.7%, 21.6%, and 22.0% across normotensive, stage 1, stage 2, and resistant-hypertension strata, respectively. In unilateral PA, the PASO cohort distinguished complete biochemical success after adrenalectomy (94%; 656/699) from complete clinical success (37%; 259/705), with partial clinical improvement in a further 47%. PATHWAY-2 established spironolactone as the most effective fourth-line drug in resistant hypertension; CORAL, ASTRAL, STAR, and DRASTIC did not support routine revascularisation for stable atherosclerotic renal-artery stenosis; plasma-free metanephrines remained highly sensitive for phaeochromocytoma/paraganglioma; and PA testing in eligible patients with resistant hypertension remained only 1.6%-2.1%. Post-search Phase 3 trials of selective aldosterone synthase inhibition showed approximately 9 mm Hg placebo-corrected office systolic blood pressure reductions, but cardiovascular-outcome benefit has not been established, and electrolyte/renal monitoring remains necessary.
CONCLUSIONS: Across secondary hypertension, a limited set of pathophysiological effector pathways maps to specific diagnostic tests and cause-directed treatments. The strongest opportunities for clinical gain are earlier recognition of high-yield phenotypes, accurate aetiological subtyping, and implementation of established testing pathways; emerging aldosterone synthase inhibitors expand blood-pressure-lowering options but should not yet be interpreted as proven cardiovascular-outcome therapies.

Title: Endoscopic intervention is associated with a lower risk of in-hospital mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by gastrointestinal bleeding.
Abstract:
