INTRODUCTION: It remains unclear whether endoscopic intervention affects the prognosis of patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) complicated by gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB). This study aimed to evaluate the association between endoscopic intervention and the risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality in patients with AMI complicated by GIB.
METHODS: The study had a single-center retrospective cohort design and included consecutive adult patients with AMI complicated by GIB who were hospitalized at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2020 and February 2026. The patients were divided into an endoscopic intervention group and a no-endoscopic intervention group according to whether or not they underwent endoscopic intervention during hospitalization. Baseline differences between the two groups were further addressed using propensity score methods. The primary outcome was in-hospital all-cause mortality. For the primary survival analysis, follow-up began at recognition of GIB, and endoscopic intervention was modeled as a time-varying exposure in Cox regression. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used as a sensitivity analysis to address measured baseline confounding. The secondary outcome was serious in-hospital clinical adverse events after GIB.
RESULTS: A total of 155 hospitalized patients with AMI complicated by GIB were included in the study (endoscopy group, n = 57; non-endoscopy group, n = 98). In the adjusted time-varying Cox regression model using the recorded intraday times, endoscopic intervention was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 0.478, 95% confidence interval 0.240-0.951, P = 0.035). In the adjusted 24-hour landmark analysis, the association was directionally similar but did not reach statistical significance (hazard ratio 0.433, 95% confidence interval 0.184-1.020, P = 0.056). In the propensity-score-matched cohort, endoscopic intervention remained associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality after further adjustment for residual imbalance (adjusted hazard ratio 0.346, 95% confidence interval 0.152-0.786, P = 0.011). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed in serious in-hospital clinical adverse events after GIB (odds ratio 1.340, 95% confidence interval 0.660-2.724, P = 0.406).
DISCUSSION: In this retrospective cohort, endoscopic intervention was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital all-cause mortality in patients with AMI complicated by GIB, although residual confounding and the uncertainty observed across complementary analyses should be considered when interpreting this association.

Title: Prevalence and Clinical Characteristics of Myocardial Infarction With Non-obstructive Coronary Arteries Compared With Obstructive Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Tertiary-Centre Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a working diagnosis in patients who fulfil the diagnostic criteria for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) but have no coronary artery stenosis ≥50% and no clinically evident alternative diagnosis that adequately explains the presentation. It encompasses heterogeneous coronary mechanisms.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence and clinical characteristics of MINOCA at a tertiary cardiac centre in Bosnia and Herzegovina and to compare demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, electrocardiographic presentation, laboratory parameters and echocardiographic findings with those of patients with obstructive myocardial infarction (OMI).
METHODS: This retrospective single-centre observational study comprised a prevalence analysis and a comparative analysis. For the prevalence analysis, medical records of 2,341 patients admitted to the Intensive Cardiac Care Unit between April 2022 and February 2024 were reviewed, of whom 1,104 fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for AMI. For the comparative analysis, 40 patients with MINOCA identified between January 2020 and February 2024 were compared with a simple random sample of 155 eligible patients with OMI. Demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, electrocardiographic presentation, laboratory parameters and echocardiographic variables were analysed.
RESULTS: MINOCA accounted for 32 (2.9%) MIs in the prevalence analysis. Patients with MINOCA (N = 40) were younger than patients with OMI (N = 155) (52.1 ± 15.2 vs. 59.8 ± 11.7 years; p = 0.005). Among patients with available sex data, female sex was more frequent in the MINOCA group (19 {47.5%}) than in the OMI group (43 {29.9%}; p = 0.037). The MINOCA group had a shorter hospital stay and a lower prevalence of hypertension, dyslipidaemia and active smoking. Diabetes mellitus was numerically less frequent, but the difference was not statistically significant. MINOCA more frequently presented as non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI; 19 {51.4%} vs. 20 {13.9%}; p < 0.001) and was characterised by lower peak troponin T and CK-MB concentrations, higher left ventricular ejection fraction and a lower wall motion score index.
CONCLUSION: MINOCA should be approached as a heterogeneous working diagnosis rather than a uniform final diagnosis. The absence of obstructive coronary artery disease should prompt continued clinical evaluation and a structured, individualised diagnostic approach. Standardised diagnostic pathways and prospective multicentre studies incorporating comprehensive imaging and long-term clinical follow-up are needed to refine risk assessment and guide management.

Title: Beneficial effects of cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome and coronary artery bypass grafting: Real-world evidence from the Cardiac Rehabilitation Outcome Study update (CROS-III).
Abstract:
AIMS: To review the effects of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and in mixed populations treated with contemporary interventional, surgical and pharmacological therapy.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42025630588) including randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective/retrospective controlled cohort studies (pCCS/rCCS) was performed with total mortality as main endpoint. Additional endpoints were cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal cardiovascular events, and hospital readmissions. Subgroup analysis was performed for age and sex. From 40 included studies, 29 studies encompassing 308 514 patients were eligible for this meta-analysis, including 5 newly identified (published between 11/2018-09/2025) studies with 92 571 patients. In pCCS and rCCS, CR-participation was associated with significantly reduced total mortality in patients with ACS (n = 41 740; pCCS: HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.15-0.69; rCCS: HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.55-0.75) and with CABG (n = 17 998; rCCS: HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.56-0.76). The effects regarding total mortality were similar in sex and age subgroups. Cardiovascular mortality and non-fatal stroke were decreased in ACS and CABG patients. In mixed populations, CR was associated with reduced hospital readmissions for any reason and for any cardiovascular event. Methodological and structural heterogeneity and low patient numbers prevented robust results.
CONCLUSION: Based on observational data, participation in CR is associated with an improved prognosis in current patients after ACS, CABG and mixed populations, similarly for sex and age subgroups. Hence, CR should be an integral part of secondary prevention in those patients. Nevertheless, high-quality studies are needed to increase the CR evidence base further.

Title: The frequency and risk factors of deep vein thrombosis among surgical patients receiving thromboprophylaxis at Oshakati Intermediate Hospital: a six-year retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: venous thromboembolism (VTE) is the formation of clots in the deep veins. This is due to three main risk factors, namely: endothelial damage, hypercoagulability, and venous stasis. These may lead to complications affecting patient morbidity and mortality, as well as causing high healthcare costs. Prophylaxis and treatment are imperative to prevent recurrence and complications. There is, however, limited data, especially in the African context, on the efficacy of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis and its outcomes.
METHODS: ethical approval from the Ministry of Health and Social Services and the University of Namibia was obtained, and a retrospective review of 42 inpatient records that met the inclusion criteria from the targeted surgical departments from January 2017 to December 2022 was conducted.
RESULTS: despite prophylaxis, 44% of patients developed VTE, with the majority being from orthopedic surgery (50%). Most patients requiring prophylaxis were from orthopedic surgery, and among all patients requiring prophylaxis, 77% didn't receive any. The most common risk factors and complications were previous malignancy (28.6%) and pulmonary embolism (50%), respectively, and HIV infection correlated with VTE development (p=0.000147). The treatment for DVT followed the Namibian Standard Treatment Guidelines.
CONCLUSION: these findings highlight the need to improve prophylactic treatment and the use of VTE prophylaxis tools, which are known to reduce VTE-related morbidity and mortality. Future research could explore the impact of inadequate VTE prophylaxis and the relationship between common comorbidities in sub-Saharan Africa and VTE prophylaxis.

Title: Deep learning analysis of sinus-rhythm echocardiography for the identification of patients with atrial fibrillation.
Abstract:
AIMS: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) is underdiagnosed due to its intermittent and asymptomatic nature. We evaluated whether a deep neural network (DNN) applied to transthoracic echocardiograms (TTEs) acquired in sinus rhythm can discriminate between patients with and without documented AF and identify individuals at increased risk for subsequent AF documentation and adverse outcomes.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed 85 686 TTE studies (2009-21). A DNN was applied to apical four-chamber and parasternal long-axis videos without Doppler. AF ground truth was based on International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes, electrocardiogram, Holter, or prior echocardiographic documentation of AF. The dataset was split into training (60%), validation (20%), and an independent test set (20%). In the test cohort, we assessed discrimination performance. Among patients without prior AF, we evaluated associations between model classification and subsequent AF documentation and a composite outcome of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or stroke. The test set included 17 121 patients (median age 66 years [interquartile range, IQR 54-75]; 57.6% male), of whom 3449 (20.1%) had prior AF. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.85, with sensitivity 0.80 and specificity 0.72. At the selected threshold, 6581 patients (38.4%) were classified as model-positive, including 3832 (58.2%) without prior AF. Among patients without prior AF, model-positive classification was associated with subsequent AF documentation [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.64; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.33-2.04] and with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 1.24; 95% CI 1.13-1.35).
CONCLUSION: Deep learning applied to sinus-rhythm TTE demonstrates discrimination for AF and identifies an imaging-derived signal associated with subsequent AF documentation and adverse outcomes.

Title: Association between a stepwise health education model based on evidence-based practice and self-care behaviors of patients with chronic heart failure: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the association between a stepwise health education model based on evidence-based practice (EBP) and self-care behaviors, cardiac function improvement, and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF).
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 120 patients with CHF admitted to our hospital from January 2023 to December 2024. The patients were divided into a control group (CG, n = 62, receiving routine health education) and an intervention group (IG, n = 58, receiving stepwise health education based on EBP in addition to routine care) according to the health education strategy received. The 6-month total score of the EHFScB-9 was defined as the primary outcome. Cardiac function indicators (LVEF, BNP, and 6MWD), biochemical indicators, clinical outcomes, individual scale items, and hospitalization-related indicators were considered exploratory outcomes. Factors associated with the occurrence of composite endpoint events were analyzed.
RESULTS: After 6 months of intervention, the IG exhibited significantly higher LVEF and 6MWD and significantly lower BNP level than the CG (P < 0.05). The serum sodium level in the IG was significantly higher than that in the CG (P < 0.05). Exploratory analyses showed that the nominal P values for the 30-day, 90-day, and 6-month readmission rates, as well as the incidence of composite endpoint events, were all <0.05 in the IG. The average length of stay and total hospitalization costs in the IG were significantly lower than those in the CG (P < 0.05); however, these findings were interpreted as exploratory. At the 6-month follow-up, the IG exhibited lower total EHFScB-9 scores and lower scores for individual items than the CG (P < 0.05), indicating better self-care behaviors. Comparisons of individual items were exploratory findings. Multivariable analysis revealed that NYHA class III-IV (OR = 3.765), concomitant atrial fibrillation (OR = 2.440), LVEF < 40% (OR = 3.184), and lack of stepwise health education based on EBP (OR = 2.607) were associated with the composite endpoints.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, analyses without adjustment for multiple comparisons suggested that a step health education model based on evidence-based practice was associated with better self-care behaviors, improved cardiac function, and lower rates of readmission and composite endpoint events.

Title: Letter to the editor: "No-touch technique for saphenous vein graft harvesting in coronary artery bypass surgery safely improves graft patency: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials".
Journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery

Title: Longitudinal relationships between anxiety and fear of progression in post-CABG patients: a cross-sectional and cross-lagged panel network analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) frequently experience elevated anxiety and fear of progression (FoP), which has a high comorbidity and significantly increases adverse postoperative event risks. This prospective study explored the dynamic longitudinal associations between anxiety and FoP in post-CABG patients using network analysis methods.
METHODS: A prospective longitudinal design enrolled first-time CABG patients from three tertiary hospitals in Urumqi, China. Anxiety and FoP were assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF) at three time points: hospital discharge (T1), 1 month (T2), and 3 months (T3) post-discharge. Cross-sectional Gaussian Graphical Models were constructed at each time point, and cross-lagged panel network (CLPN) analysis was performed to examine longitudinal symptom associations. Six a priori selected covariates (age, gender, educational level, duration of CHD, chronic comorbidities, and NYHA functional classification) were residualized prior to network estimation.
RESULTS: A total of 343 patients were included in the network analysis. From T1 to T3, total GAD-7 scores demonstrated a notable downward trend, whereas FoP-Q-SF scores exhibited a continuous upward trend. The core node at both T1 and T2 was FoP11 "Worrying about what will become of the family if something should happen to the patient, " which shifted to FoP2 "Being nervous prior to doctors' appointments or periodic examinations" at T3. In the T1-T2 CLPN, the strongest cross-lagged edge was from GAD7 "Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen" to FoP2 "Being nervous prior to doctors' appointments or periodic examinations". In the T2-T3 CLPN, the strongest cross-lagged edge was from GAD2 "Not being able to stop or control worrying" to FoP6 "Being afraid of the possibility that the children could contract disease". In the T1-T3 network, the strongest cross-lagged edge was from GAD4 "Trouble relaxing" to FoP3 "Being afraid of pain". Anxiety nodes generally exhibited higher Out-Expected Influence, while FoP nodes showed higher In-Expected Influence.
CONCLUSION: Anxiety levels gradually decreased during early rehabilitation, whereas fear of progression increased over time. Early anxiety symptoms showed positive cross-lagged associations with later fear of progression. These findings suggest that clinical nurses should consider phased, precision-based psychological interventions targeting stage-specific symptoms during different rehabilitation stages.

Title: Cardiometabolic biomarker profiles associated with estimated 10-year ASCVD risk by the China-PAR model in an older adult health examination cohort: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the associations between cardiometabolic biomarker profiles and estimated 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk calculated using the China-PAR (Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China) equation in adults aged ≥60 years undergoing routine physical examinations.
METHODS: Participants aged ≥60 years were recruited from a hospital health examination center. Ten-year ASCVD risk was calculated using the China-PAR equation and classified as low-to-intermediate (<10%) or high (≥10%). Associations between continuous biomarkers and the risk score were assessed using Spearman correlation with false discovery rate correction. Exploratory LASSO logistic regression was used for feature selection for China-PAR-defined high-risk status, followed by mutually adjusted logistic regression and quartile-stratified analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 511 participants were included (median age 67 years; 62.8% male), and 191 (37.4%) were classified as high risk by China-PAR. Waist-to-hip ratio (WHR; rho = 0.43), fasting plasma glucose (FPG; rho = 0.40), and cystatin C (CysC; rho = 0.39) showed the strongest correlations with the calculated risk score. Exploratory LASSO feature selection retained CysC, FPG, atherogenic coefficient (AC), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Per one-standard-deviation increase, FPG [adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.772, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.047-3.753] and CysC (aOR = 2.731, 95% CI: 1.881-3.964) showed the strongest associations with China-PAR-defined high-risk status. All four biomarkers showed graded trends across quartiles in the overall population and in descriptive sex-stratified analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: CysC, FPG, AC, and NT-proBNP were associated with higher estimated China-PAR risk. Because FPG and AC overlap clinically or mathematically with variables used to construct China-PAR, their associations should be interpreted partly in the context of score construction. CysC and NT-proBNP are not components of the China-PAR equation and warrant prospective evaluation. These findings characterize biomarker profiles associated with higher estimated cardiovascular risk and may help increase clinical awareness of unfavorable cardiometabolic and cardiorenal features during routine health examinations.

Title: Efficacy and safety of Yangxin Dingji capsule as an adjunctive therapy for atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Yangxin Dingji Capsule (YXDJ), a modern Chinese patent medicine derived from the classic Zhigancao Decoction, is commonly used as an adjuvant therapy for atrial fibrillation (AF). This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy and safety of YXDJ as an adjuvant therapy in AF patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China Biology Medicine, Wanfang, VIP Chinese Journal Service Platform, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure from inception to 1 April 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing YXDJ plus conventional therapy versus conventional therapy alone in patients with AF. Meta-analyses were performed using RevMan with fixed- or random-effects models based on heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and the overall quality of evidence for each outcome was evaluated using the GRADE framework. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261286691).
RESULTS: Ten RCTs involving 872 patients were included. All studies were Chinese-language publications with methodological limitations. According to the RoB 2 assessment, most studies were rated as having some concerns or high risk of bias, mainly due to inadequate allocation concealment, lack of blinding for subjective outcomes, and absence of publicly available trial registrations or protocols. In terms of clinical symptoms, YXDJ was associated with improvements in the overall clinical response rate [RR = 1.27, P < 0.00001, very low], reductions in EHRA symptom scores [MD = -0.47, P = 0.0009, very low], and reductions in postoperative AF recurrence at 6 months [RR = 0.43, P = 0.03, moderate]. For cardiac function, YXDJ was associated with increases in left atrial ejection fraction (LAEF) [MD = 2.11%, P = 0.003, low] and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) [MD = 4.39%, P < 0.00001, moderate], whereas no significant changes were observed in left atrial diameter (LAD) [MD = -1.97 mm, P = 0.07, very low] and mitral E/A ratio [MD = 0.12, P = 0.06, very low]; subgroup analysis revealed that YXDJ reduced LAD in postoperative patients [MD = -2.70 mm, P = 0.02, low]. In terms of inflammatory biomarkers, YXDJ was associated with reductions in hs-CRP [MD = -1.21 mg/L, P < 0.00001, low], TNF-α [SMD = -0.44, P = 0.0009, low], and IL-6 [MD = -10.42 ng/L, P < 0.00001, low]; subgroup analysis further showed a greater reduction in hs-CRP in postoperative patients [MD = -1.42 mg/L, P < 0.00001, low]. For safety, no clear increase in the overall incidence of adverse events was observed [RR = 0.58, P = 0.07, low]. Exploratory analyses from single studies suggested possible long-term benefits, including a lower reported risk of ischemic stroke and sustained reductions in AF recurrence and symptom scores at 9 months post-ablation; however, these findings are preliminary and require confirmation.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence, derived exclusively from methodologically limited, small, single-center Chinese studies, provides only preliminary signals that YXDJ may offer possible additional benefits as an adjunct to conventional therapy for symptom control and postoperative management in AF. Most efficacy outcomes were supported by low- or very-low-certainty evidence, with only LVEF and postoperative AF recurrence at 6 months rated as moderate certainty. These findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. YXDJ should not replace guideline-directed anticoagulation, rate or rhythm control, or catheter ablation. Rigorously designed trials are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW: Identifier CRD420261286691.

Title: Beyond the clinic: a six-month home-based exercise and respiratory rehabilitation program improves functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, and fatigue in chronic heart failure.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Optimal models of rehabilitation dedicated for patients with heart failure (HF) remain under investigation. The aim of this study was to assess the safety and effectiveness of a 6-month home-based rehabilitation program in patients with HF.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 63 patients with stable HF were randomized, 28 patients from intervention group completed the study and were included in the analysis. Assessments including the 6-minute walk test, respiratory muscle strength, and quality of life measures (SF-36 and Fatigue Severity Scale - FSS) were conducted at baseline and after 6 months. Additionally, adverse events and adherence to the training protocol were monitored.
RESULTS: Due to objective challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak, the course and final outcomes of the study differed from the original protocol; the control group was not assessed after 6 months. In the intervention group, 6 months of rehabilitation resulted in statistically significant improvements: the 6-minute walk distance increased by 37.86 meters (p = 0.001), maximal inspiratory pressure (PImax) improved by 20.21 cmH₂O, and maximal expiratory pressure (PEmax) by 20.75 cmH₂O (both p < 0.01). A significant reduction in fatigue was observed, as measured by FSS, with a mean decrease of 0.68 points (p = 0.029). Adherence to the exercise protocol averaged 91.5 ± 15.3%. No serious adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: The home-based rehabilitation program, including respiratory muscle training, is safe and effective for patients with chronic HF. It improves functional capacity and reduces fatigue levels.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03780803, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03780803. Registered 19/12/2018.

Title: Colchicine use and clinical outcomes in acute myocarditis: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocarditis (AM) is an inflammatory disease of the myocardium associated with ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, and progression to cardiomyopathy. Current management remains supportive, and no targeted anti-inflammatory therapy has demonstrated proven benefit on cardiovascular outcomes outside specific histological subtypes. Colchicine is an inexpensive, widely available anti-inflammatory agent with an established role in pericarditis, yet real-world data on its association with clinical outcomes in confirmed AM remain limited.
METHODS: Patients with cardiac magnetic resonance-confirmed AM were retrospectively included. The primary outcome was echocardiographic maintenance or recovery of LVEF to a follow-up of ≥50%. Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, absolute change in LVEF, and an absolute LVEF improvement of ≥10%.
RESULTS: A total of 243 patients with AM were included in the study, with 63 receiving colchicine and 178 not. Colchicine-treated patients were significantly younger (median 29 vs. 39 years; p < 0.001) with a similar sex distribution, although clinical presentation differed between groups. Follow-up LVEF of ≥50%, evaluable in 93 patients, was more frequent in colchicine-treated patients (95% vs. 70%; p = 0.035) and persisted after adjustment for age and sex (OR 5.10, 95% CI 1.14-48.7; p = 0.03), with directionally consistent results in a propensity score-matched sensitivity analysis. All-cause mortality occurred in 1 of 63 colchicine-treated patients (1.6%) and 12 of 178 untreated patients (6.7%), with no significant difference after age and sex adjustment (OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.06-2.76; p = 0.53). Absolute change in LVEF and improvement ≥ 10% did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Colchicine use was associated with more frequent maintenance or recovery of left ventricular function, although these findings are exploratory in the context of the limitations of this study. Further prospective evidence will highlight the efficacy and scope of colchicine in patients with AM.

Title: The correlation between epicardial adipose tissue thickness and left ventricular systolic function in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can cause myocardial damage and left ventricular dysfunction in patients. Abnormal deposition of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) can promote the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to investigate changes in EAT thickness in patients with SLE and apply two-dimensional speckle tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) to study the correlation between EAT and left ventricular systolic function.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This case-control study recruited a total of 67 SLE patients as the case group and 31 healthy individuals as the control group. Left ventricular systolic function parameters were measured using 2D-STE. Changes and correlations in laboratory indicators, EAT, and left ventricular systolic function parameters were compared between groups.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the case group showed significantly increased EAT and diastolic left ventricular posterior wall thickness (LVPWD) (P<0.05). High-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (AP2C LS), apical three-chamber longitudinal strain (AP3C LS), apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (AP4C LS), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were significantly reduced (P < 0.05). The 18-segment left ventricular longitudinal strain was further grouped according to coronary artery supply; the LAD, RCA, and LCX groups in the patient cohort all showed reductions compared with the healthy control group (P < 0.05). Spearman correlation analysis revealed that EAT was negatively correlated with GLS (r = -0.39, P < 0.05), LAD group (r = -0.26, P < 0.05), RCA group (r = -0.47, P < 0.05), and LCX group (r = -0.29, P < 0.05), and positively correlated with duration of illness (DT) (r = 0.41, P < 0.05) and age (r = 0.45, P < 0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis confirmed that EAT is an important influencing factor of left ventricular longitudinal strain function (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Increased epicardial adipose tissue thickness is negatively correlated with left ventricular systolic function. EAT can effectively reflect changes in left ventricular systolic function in SLE patients, providing a basis for clinical management and early intervention.

Title: Acupuncture attenuates hypertension-induced myocardial hypertrophy: role of the SIRT1/NF-κ B/MAPK signaling axis in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic hypertension is a major risk factor for cardiovascular complications and can induce pathological myocardial hypertrophy. The hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) is a key autonomic regulatory center involved in hypertension through sympathetic overactivation, neuroinflammation, and central renin-angiotensin system dysregulation. Although acupuncture exerts protective effects against hypertension-related target organ damage, its central mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether acupuncture was associated with the attenuation of hypertension-induced myocardial hypertrophy in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) and whether these effects may involve modulation of the sirtuin 1 (SIRT1)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling axis in the PVN.
METHODS: Twenty-seven SHRs were randomly assigned to Model, Acupuncture, and Losartan groups (n = 9 per group), while nine Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) rats served as Controls. Rats received acupuncture at Taichong (LR3), Baihui (GV20), and Sanyinjiao (SP6) or losartan treatment for 12 weeks. Blood pressure, plasma norepinephrine (NE), cardiac function, myocardial remodeling, fibrosis, and PVN-related molecular changes were assessed.
RESULTS: Acupuncture reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure and decreased plasma NE levels in SHRs. In the PVN, acupuncture increased SIRT1 expression and inhibited NF-κB p65 expression and MAPK phosphorylation. Moreover, acupuncture suppressed central renin-angiotensin system activation, neuroinflammation, and neurotransmitter imbalance by regulating ACE, AT1R, pro-inflammatory cytokines, GABA, and Glu levels. Echocardiographic and histological analyses demonstrated that acupuncture alleviated myocardial hypertrophy, improved cardiac function, and reduced fibrosis and structural remodeling.
CONCLUSION: Acupuncture was associated with the attenuation of hypertension-induced myocardial hypertrophy in SHRs, possibly involving modulation of the PVN SIRT1/NF-κB/MAPK signaling axis. These effects may involve suppression of neuroinflammation and sympathetic overactivation, regulation of the central renin-angiotensin system, and restoration of PVN neurotransmitter balance, providing new insights into the central neural mechanisms underlying acupuncture-mediated cardioprotection in hypertension.

Title: The prediagnostic period of Behçet's disease: a nationwide population-based study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched case-control study using the electronic health records of Leumit Health Services. Patients with BD fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease or International Study Group classification criteria were identified by manual chart review and matched 1:5 with controls by sex, age, socioeconomic category and year of first observation. Clinical diagnoses, diagnostic investigations and laboratory measurements and medication dispensing recorded during the five years preceding diagnosis were compared between groups. Early and late laboratory measurements within the prediagnostic period were analyzed to assess temporal trends. Manifestations documented over the entire available record were analyzed separately.
RESULTS: The study included 218 patients who subsequently developed BD and 1,090 matched controls. During the five years preceding diagnosis, future patients with BD more frequently exhibited oral aphthosis (36.2% vs 3.0%; OR 18.2), panuveitis (4.6% vs 0.1%; OR 52.4), inflammatory polyarthritis (7.3% vs 0.6%; OR 14.3), and venous thromboembolism (4.6% vs 0.2%; OR 26.2) (all P<0.001). Over the entire available record, oral aphthosis was documented in 61.0% of patients with BD and 11.8% of controls. Autoimmune serology was frequently requested but remained largely negative. Laboratory analyses demonstrated a biphasic trajectory. Absolute monocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were lower than in controls at the early assessment (0.40 vs 0.44 ×109/L, P = 0.009, and 1.45 vs 1.49, P = 0.023) but significantly higher near diagnosis (0.64 vs 0.58 ×109/L, P = 0.025, and 2.44 vs 2.09, P = 0.003). This transition was accompanied by rising CRP, ESR, platelet count and globulin levels, persistently lower mean corpuscular volume and consistently higher IgA at both assessments (247 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.009, and 256 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.012), whereas IgG and IgM remained comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: BD seems to be preceded by a clinically and biologically active prediagnostic phase characterized by a distinct inflammatory multisystem footprint.

Title: Development and multi-database validation of machine learning models for 28-day mortality prediction in ICU patients with COPD and pulmonary hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early mortality prediction in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) coexisting pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains challenging, particularly because prediction models developed in intensive care unit (ICU) database may not perform consistently across other healthcare systems.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study employed two large-scale databases to establish and validate ML models for predicting early mortality in ICU patients with COPD and PH. The MIMIC-IV database served as the model-development cohort (2555 patients), with external validation conducted on eICU CRD (292 patients) database. Six ML algorithms were adopted: Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Logistic Regression (LR), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN).The baseline variables were screened to identify potential predictors via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (Lasso) regression. Model interpretability was evaluated via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis.
RESULTS: The overall cohort consisted of 2,847 ICU patients with COPD and PH. Twelve consistently crucial clinical features were identified, including acute kidney injury, pneumonia, age, weight, heart rate, red blood cell distribution width (RDW), white blood cell (WBC), anion gap, chloride, creatinine, base excess, potential of hydrogen (pH). The Random Forest algorithm achieved the optimal performance, with a training Area Under Curve (AUC) of 0.938, internal validation AUC of 0.748, and eICU CRD external validation AUC of 0.800. SHAP analysis indicated that acute kidney injury was the most influential predictor, followed by base excess and RDW. Additionally, a web tool was developed in this study to facilitate the application of early death risk prediction in clinical practice.
CONCLUSIONS: This study is the multi-database validation of ML models for early mortality prediction in ICU patients with COPD and PH. The Random Forest model integrated with SHAP interpretability offers a reliable tool for clinical decision-making support, with consistent validity verified across two databases, including our internal validation cohort. This work provides a decision support tool to assist in identifying high-risk individuals within this complex comorbid population, and establishes a foundation for future studies with a more dynamic and personalized prognostic approach.

Title: Glomerular diseases associated with multiple myeloma: renal pathology and survival outcomes in a retrospective study at Charles Nicolle Hospital, Tunis, Tunisia.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Multiple myeloma (MM) is frequently complicated by renal involvement, which represents a major prognostic factor included in the Durie-Salmon staging system. In contrast, glomerular diseases associated with MM are rare and have been reported mainly in small case series. This study aimed to describe the clinical and histopathological characteristics of MM-associated glomerular diseases and to identify factors associated with renal and overall survival.
METHODS: we conducted a retrospective hospital-based study over 33 years, including patients with MM and biopsy-proven glomerular disease. Clinical, biological, and histopathological data were collected. Renal and overall survival were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and multivariable Cox regression analysis. Factors associated with the presence of glomerular disease were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, by comparison with patients with MM without renal involvement.
RESULTS: a total of 22 patients (100%, n=22) with MM-associated glomerular disease were included. The mean age was 55.5 ± X years, and males represented Y% (n=Z). Proteinuria was present in 86.4% (n=19) and hematuria in 63.6% (n=14). The mean creatinine clearance was 25.6 ± 28.3 mL/min, and renal impairment was observed in 72.7% (n=16). According to the Durie-Salmon classification, 13.6% (n=3) were stage I, 22.7% (n=5) stage II, and 63.6% (n=14) stage III. Histopathological findings showed amyloidosis in 72.7% (n=16), monoclonal immunoglobulin deposition disease in 22.7% (n=5), and membranous glomerulonephritis in 4.5% (n=1). Renal survival at 12 months was 54% (n=12). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, independent predictors of worse renal survival were smoking (aHR: 3.10, 95% CI 1.30-7.40; p=0.01), baseline renal impairment (serum creatinine >177 μmol/L) (aHR: 2.85, 95% CI 1.20-6.80; p=0.02), plasma uric acid >600 µmol/L (aHR: 3.95, 95% CI 1.60-9.70; p=0.003), and disease progression despite therapy (aHR: 2.70, 95% CI 1.15-6.30; p=0.02). For overall survival, serum calcium >2.8 mmol/L (aHR: 4.20, 95% CI 1.70-10.3; p=0.002), serum phosphorus >2 mmol/L (aHR: 3.80, 95% CI 1.60-9.00; p=0.001), and Durie-Salmon stage III (aHR: 2.40, 95% CI 1.10-5.40; p=0.03) remained independently associated with mortality. Compared with patients with MM without renal involvement, multivariable logistic regression showed that proteinuria (aOR: 5.10, 95% CI 1.10-23.5; p=0.04), elevated alkaline phosphatase (aOR: 4.30, 95% CI 1.30-14.2; p=0.02), and absence of IgG-kappa MM (aOR: 3.90, 95% CI 1.20-12.8; p=0.02) were independently associated with glomerular involvement.
CONCLUSION: in this retrospective study, glomerular diseases associated with MM were uncommon and predominantly represented by amyloidosis. Renal and overall survival were poor and were independently influenced by renal function, metabolic abnormalities, and advanced disease stage.

Title: Fatal plant poisoning cases in Tunisia: a retrospective series.
Abstract: Medicinal plants are widely used and commonly considered safe. However, certain species contain toxic compounds that may cause severe or fatal poisoning. This study aimed to describe fatal cases of plant poisoning reported to the toxicology laboratory of a Tunisian university hospital over a ten-year period. This retrospective study was conducted at the Toxicology Laboratory of Fattouma Bourguiba University Hospital in Monastir, Tunisia, over the period from 2014 to 2023. Data were collected from toxicological analysis reports and laboratory records. Only cases of suspected plant poisoning referred for medico-legal toxicological analysis and resulting in death were included. Data collected related to patient characteristics, plant species involved, circumstances of exposure, and clinical signs observed before death. Five fatal cases of plant poisoning were recorded. Most cases occurred in the context of medicinal use. In one case, the circumstances of exposure were uncertain but were reported to have followed advice from a spiritual healer. Three plant species were implicated: Peganum harmalaL., Ephedra alata Decne. subsp. alenda (Stapf) Trab and Ecballium elaterium (L.) A. Rich. Clinical manifestations ranged from gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms progressing to respiratory arrest, to cardiovascular complications and multiorgan failure, depending on the plant species. Fatal plant poisonings, although rare, highlight the potential toxicity of medicinal plants commonly perceived as safe, mainly due to the presence of toxic bioactive compounds. Increasing awareness among healthcare professionals and the general population is essential to prevent such outcomes.

Title: Network and pairwise meta-analysis of the effects of novel hypoglycemic agents on cardiorenal outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes and heart failure.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the cardiovascular and renal benefits of novel hypoglycemic agents, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is), sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is), and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 dual receptor agonists (GIP/GLP-1RAs) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and heart failure (HF).
METHODS: Systematic literature searches were conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to 30 April 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) for cardiovascular outcomes (CVOTs) or post hoc analyses of CVOTs comparing SGLT-2is, DPP-4is, GLP-1RAs, or GIP/GLP-1RAs in patients with T2DM and HF were selected. Network meta-analysis was used for indirect comparisons, with results presented as hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 10 RCTs and two post hoc analyses of CVOTs involving 13,886 patients were included. Compared with placebo, SGLT-2is (HR [95% CI]: 0.75 [0.68, 0.82]) and GLP-1RAs (HR [95% CI]: 0.77 [0.61, 0.97]) both significantly reduced the risk of HF-related composite endpoints in patients with T2DM and HF. No statistically significant difference was observed between SGLT-2is and GLP-1RAs (HR [95% CI]: 0.98 [0.76, 1.25]). SGLT-2is also reduced the risk of HF worsening (HR [95% CI]: 0.72 [0.53, 0.96]), HF hospitalization (HR [95% CI]: 0.74 [0.66, 0.83]), and cardiovascular (CV) death (HR [95% CI]: 0.87 [0.77, 0.98]). For all-cause death, SGLT-2is showed a trend toward reduced risk compared to placebo, but this difference did not reach statistical significance (HR [95% CI]: 0.83 [0.67, 1.02]). For the renal composite outcome, SGLT-2is did not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit (HR [95% CI]: 0.76 [0.51, 1.14]).
CONCLUSION: Optimal clinical management of T2DM requires a comprehensive assessment of cardiovascular and renal comorbidities. This network meta-analysis indicates that SGLT-2is significantly reduce the risk of HF-related composite endpoints and CV death in T2DM patients with HF, although their renoprotective effect does not reach statistical significance. GLP-1RAs also demonstrate beneficial effects on HF-related composite endpoints. These findings suggest that both SGLT-2is and GLP-1RAs are preferred glycemic control strategies for improving cardiovascular outcomes in T2DM patients with HF, while further evidence is needed to confirm their definitive renal benefits.

Title: Clinically low-risk features do not exclude diffusion-weighted imaging-positive lesions in suspected transient ischemic attack.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) is essential for distinguishing tissue-negative transient ischemic attack (TIA) from MRI-defined minor stroke. When MRI capacity is limited, clinical features could help estimate DWI lesion yield. While features associated with DWI positivity are well established, it remains uncertain whether clinically low-risk presentations identify patients with a sufficiently low probability of DWI-positive lesions. We investigated clinical features associated with DWI-positive lesions in patients presenting with suspected TIA and assessed whether clinically low-risk constellations reliably excluded DWI-positive lesions.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 418 patients presenting with suspected TIA who underwent a standardized MRI protocol within 6 h of admission. The study endpoint was an acute DWI-positive lesion, defined by DWI hyperintensity with corresponding apparent diffusion coefficient reduction. Univariate analyses and exploratory multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to examine clinical, neurological, and cardiovascular features associated with DWI positivity, with particular emphasis on clinically low-risk presentations.
RESULTS: DWI-positive lesions were detected in 118/418 patients (28.2%). Motor symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.683, p < 0.001), NIHSS 1-5 (aOR 1.940, p = 0.007), and acute symptom onset (aOR 1.999, p = 0.025) were associated with DWI positivity in the clinical-neurological analysis, while cardiovascular risk factors showed the strongest association in the extended analysis (aOR 3.959, p < 0.001). Conversely, subacute onset, non-specific accompanying symptoms, NIHSS 0, and dizziness were associated with lower odds of DWI positivity. Importantly, DWI-positive lesions remained present in 13/133 patients (9.8%) with ≥2 and 2/48 (4.2%) with ≥3 low-risk features.
DISCUSSION: Clinically low-risk presentations did not reliably exclude DWI-positive lesions, supporting MRI-based evaluation. Clinical and cardiovascular features may help estimate the likelihood of DWI positivity; whether they can inform MRI prioritization requires prospective validation.

Title: Serum β-defensin-3 and inflammatory markers for discriminating diabetic foot infection and infection severity: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human β-defensin-3 (hBD-3) is an epithelial-derived antimicrobial peptide involved in innate immunity and tissue repair, but its clinical association with diabetic foot infection (DFI) remains insufficiently characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations of serum hBD-3 with prevalent DFI and infection severity and to assess its discriminatory performance alone and in combination with conventional inflammatory markers.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 150 participants: 30 healthy controls, 30 patients with diabetes without foot disease, and 90 patients with diabetic foot disease, including 30 without infection and 60 with DFI. Logistic regression and LASSO penalized regression were used to identify factors associated with prevalent DFI and moderate/severe infection. Restricted cubic spline analyses explored nonlinear associations. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, and internal validation was performed with 1,000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: Serum hBD-3 was higher in patients with DFI than in those with non-infected diabetic foot disease [108.9 (86.3, 141.5) vs. 69.8 (56.1, 84.7) pg/mL, P < 0.001] and increased with infection severity. Higher hBD-3, CRP, PCT, and HbA1c and lower albumin were independently associated with prevalent DFI. The final prevalent-DFI model included HbA1c, albumin, hBD-3, CRP, and PCT and achieved an apparent AUC of 0.928, with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.895. The moderate/severe DFI model included hBD-3, CRP, and PCT and achieved an apparent AUC of 0.935 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.917. RCS analyses suggested nonlinear associations between hBD-3 and both prevalent DFI and infection severity.
CONCLUSION: Serum hBD-3 was associated with the presence and severity of DFI and provided complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional inflammatory markers. The combined models showed promising performance but remain exploratory and require prospective multicenter external validation before clinical application.

Title: A clinical and biomarker model for predicting post-stroke cognitive impairment: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is highly prevalent and substantially compromises functional recovery and quality of life; however, early identification remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate an early prediction model for PSCI by integrating routinely available blood biomarkers with clinical characteristics.
METHODS: Patients with acute ischemic stroke were prospectively enrolled at Shanghai Fourth People's Hospital between March and November 2024. Cognitive function was assessed 3 months after stroke using the Telephone Montreal Cognitive Assessment (T-MoCA), a telephone-based cognitive screening instrument, with PSCI defined as a corrected T-MoCA score <19. Univariable logistic regression, Spearman correlation analysis, and variance inflation factor analysis were performed to characterize associations and predictor redundancy. Bootstrap least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression with 1,000 resampling iterations was used to assess variable-selection stability, followed by multivariable logistic regression and nomogram construction. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration analysis, decision curve analysis (DCA), and clinical impact curves (CIC), with 1,000 bootstrap iterations used for internal validation.
RESULTS: A total of 198 patients were included, of whom 138 developed PSCI and 60 were classified as post-stroke cognitively normal (PSCN, non-PSCI group). The final prediction model incorporated age, prior stroke history, diabetes mellitus, small dense low-density lipoprotein (sdLDL), apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I), homocysteine, cystatin C, and D-dimer. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.798. Following 1,000 bootstrap resampling iterations, the mean AUC was 0.777 (95% CI, 0.733-0.802), and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.762. Calibration analysis suggested reasonable agreement between predicted and observed risks, while DCA and CIC analyses indicated potential utility for PSCI risk stratification.
CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and internally validated a multivariable model combining clinical characteristics and circulating biomarkers to estimate PSCI risk after acute ischemic stroke. The model showed acceptable predictive performance and may support early risk stratification.

Title: Tongxinluo is associated with neurovascular changes following rt-PA-treated ischemic stroke: associations with inflammation, vascular remodeling, and neural plasticity.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but is often limited by microvascular obstruction and reperfusion injury. Tongxinluo (TXL) has demonstrated neuroprotective potential, yet its association with neurovascular responses during rt-PA-associated reperfusion remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Because reperfusion was achieved by filament withdrawal before rt-PA administration, this model evaluates TXL-associated effects during mechanically induced reperfusion with rt-PA exposure rather than enhancement of rt-PA-mediated thrombolysis. Animals were randomized into Sham, MCAO, MCAO + rt-PA, and MCAO + rt-PA + TXL (low/high dose) groups. Neurological outcomes were assessed longitudinally. Cerebral perfusion was monitored using laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI). Mechanistic analyses included assessments of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, oxidative stress, microglial activation, angiogenesis, mitochondrial function, apoptosis, and synaptic plasticity markers (BDNF, GAP-43, and Synapsin I) using histological, biochemical, and molecular techniques.
RESULTS: Adjunctive TXL treatment was associated with improved neurological outcomes and reduced infarct volume compared with rt-PA alone, with dose-dependent trends observed. TXL was associated with improved cortical microvascular perfusion and reduced severity of the no-reflow phenomenon. Mechanistically, TXL suppressed microglia-mediated neuroinflammation (downregulating TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) and preserved BBB integrity. This anti-inflammatory environment facilitated angiogenic maturation, evidenced by increased microvessel density and lumen formation. Furthermore, TXL stabilized mitochondrial function, inhibited neuronal apoptosis, and upregulated BDNF, GAP-43, and Synapsin I, leading to significant restoration of dendritic spine density.
CONCLUSION: TXL may provide adjunctive neuroprotective effects in the context of rt-PA treatment by modulating inflammatory, vascular-associated, and neuronal recovery responses. These findings support further investigation of TXL as a complementary therapy following reperfusion. By concurrently suppressing neuroinflammation and promoting vascular and synaptic reconstruction, TXL translates multi-target modulation into robust functional recovery, supporting its potential as a strategic combination therapy for acute ischemic stroke.

Title: Acute cardiovascular responses to slow and deep breathing in normotensive non-pregnant and pregnant women.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the acute cardiovascular responses of non-pregnant and pregnant women to slow and deep breathing (SDB) at a range of breathing frequencies. Participants: Forty-one women (23 non-pregnant and 18 pregnant).
METHODS: Participants completed five different breathing conditions in a randomised order (5-min duration); spontaneous breathing (Sf r ), dynamic SDB breathing frequency (Df r ), and three fixed breathing frequencies of 4 breaths. min-1 (4Ff r ), 6 breaths. min-1 (6Ff r ), and 8 breaths. min-1 (8Ff r ). Main Outcome Measures: Non-invasive beat-to-beat arterial blood pressure, heart rate and respired airflow were monitored continuously.
RESULTS: The maximum amplitude of respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA) during SDB was 2.1 times higher than during spontaneous breathing (Sf r ) for both groups, maximising at 6 breaths. min-1 (0.25s ± 0.1 non-pregnant, 0.15s ± 0.1 pregnant). Although absolute RSA was significantly lower in pregnant women during spontaneous breathing (Sf r ; 0.07s vs. 0.12s non-pregnant), SDB increased RSA to the same level as non-pregnant women's spontaneous breathing levels. In both groups, the amplitude of blood pressure oscillations (both systolic and diastolic blood pressure) increased as breathing frequency declined, reaching a peak at 4 breaths. min-1 (4Ff r ), which was up to 4.5 times higher (14.3%, 10 mmHg) than during spontaneous breathing (Sf r ).
CONCLUSION: Cardiovascular responses maximised at ≤6 breaths. min-1 and acute haemodynamic responses to SDB are similar in pregnant and non-pregnant women, despite absolute differences under spontaneous breathing conditions. If blood pressure oscillations underpin the anti-hypertensive effect of SDB, the data indicate that these can be amplified in pregnant women at frequencies between 4 and 6 breaths. min-1.

Title: The platelet-to-high-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol ratio: a promising biomarker for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events in the Chinese community-based population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The platelet-to-high-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol ratio (PHR), a composite index integrating platelet count and HDL-C concentration, has recently attracted attention as a potential indicator of inflammatory and metabolic status. However, evidence regarding its relationship with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) is still limited. Therefore, using data from a prospective community-based cohort, we evaluated whether baseline PHR was associated with the occurrence of MACE during 10 years of follow-up.
METHODS: A total of 8,184 eligible subjects were included in our analysis. The primary outcome was MACE, and the secondary outcome was acute myocardial infarction (AMI), stroke, and CV mortality over 10 years. The PHR was calculated as the ratio of platelets to high-density-lipoprotein-cholesterol (HDL-C). Associations between baseline PHR and subsequent MACE were examined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, with effect estimates reported as hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Of all participants, the mean age was 56.4 ± 8.9 years, and 2,989 (36.5%) were men. During a mean 10-year follow-up, a total of 853 (10.4%) cases of MACE, 165 (2.0%) cases of AMI, 673 (8.2%) cases of stroke, and 143 (1.7%) cases of CV mortality were recorded. After multivariable adjustment, individuals in the highest PHR quartile showed a greater risk of MACE than those in the lowest quartile (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 1.12-1.69). A similar association was observed for AMI, with the highest quartile having more than twice the risk of the lowest quartile (HR: 2.44; 95% CI: 1.43-4.18). In contrast, the corresponding associations with stroke (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.00-1.60) and CV mortality (HR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.65-1.77) were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that higher PHR is associated with an increased long-term risk of MACE and AMI among Chinese community-dwelling adults, suggesting that PHR may serve as a potential biomarker associated with cardiovascular risk.

Title: Long-term quality of life, rehospitalization risks, and economic viability of remote cardiac rehabilitation: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although remote cardiac rehabilitation (RCR) is a promising alternative to traditional center-based care, evidence regarding its exact impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), cardiovascular safety, and economic viability remains fragmented, necessitating a comprehensive synthesis to guide clinical implementation.
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the HRQoL, cardiovascular safety, and economic viability of RCR versus standard center-based care in cardiovascular disease, with subgroup analyses based on follow-up duration and high-risk patient cohorts.
METHODS: Literature searches were conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by manual screening of relevant references to identify clinical studies on RCR up to July 2026. Two independent review teams performed data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the RevMan software. Meta-analyses were conducted employing random-effects models to calculate pooled effect sizes with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I 2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA).
RESULTS: A total of 45 randomized controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis. RCR significantly improved HRQoL across multiple scales (MacNew: MD = 0.17; MLHFQ: MD = -5.38; P < 0.05), while maintaining SF-36 and HADS outcomes comparable to standard care. Exploratory analyses indicated statistically significant improvements in mental health at 6 months (MD = 1.73, P = 0.03) and physical functioning at 12 months (MD = 1.48, P = 0.0002). Regarding cardiovascular safety, RCR was not associated with a statistically significant increase in the risk of MACEs, all-cause mortality, or adverse events (P > 0.05) compared to conventional care. RCR significantly reduced the risk of cardiac rehospitalization (RR = 0.70, P = 0.01), with exploratory stratified analyses indicating that this favorable association was evident in the hardware-integrated interventions subgroup (RR = 0.59, P = 0.02) and 6-month observation subgroup (RR = 0.38, P < 0.00001), alongside a non-significant numerical protective trend among high-risk patients (RR: 0.59 vs. 0.74, P = 0.15). The economic viability of RCR remains uncertain, critically depending on initial setup outlays, patient scaling, and subsequent healthcare utilization.
CONCLUSIONS: RCR may serve as an effective and safe alternative to conventional care that improves physical and psychological well-being, was associated with a lower risk of cardiac rehospitalization, and may provide economic value in certain healthcare systems.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261374977, PROSPERO CRD420261374977.

Title: Independent linear association between flow-mediated dilation and predicted intermediate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk in patients with type 2 diabetes: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular endothelial dysfunction precedes atherosclerosis in type 2 diabetes (T2DM). However, the specific nature of the association between flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and the intermediate-to-high 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk remains to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate this correlation in a large sample of Chinese patients with T2DM.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,272 T2DM patients managed at the National Metabolic Management Center (MMC) between March 2020 and March 2025. Endothelial function was assessed via brachial artery FMD (dysfunction: FMD < 6.5%). Multivariate linear and logistic regressions identified independent factors. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models assessed non-linear associations between FMD and the intermediate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk.
RESULTS: Overall, 78.9% (n=1,003) exhibited endothelial dysfunction. Multivariate analysis identified older age, higher systolic blood pressure, male sex, smoking, hypertension, and the intermediate-to-high ASCVD risk were independently associated with impaired FMD (all p < 0.05). FMD showed an independent inverse association with intermediate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk (OR = 0.90, 95% CI: 0.82-0.99, p < 0.05) and moderate discriminative ability (AUC = 0.700, 95% CI: 0.66-0.75). Crucially, RCS analysis confirmed a linear negative correlation between FMD and the intermediate-to-high ASCVD risk (p-overall = 0.004), with no evidence of non-linearity (p-non-linear = 0.653).
CONCLUSIONS: Endothelial dysfunction is highly prevalent in T2DM. FMD was independently, inversely and linearly associated with the intermediate-to-high calculated 10-year ASCVD risk.

Title: Developing and evaluating machine learning models in the prediction of recurrent sudden cardiac arrest.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) is a major killer of adults in the United States and has a significant recurrence rate. Predicting the risk of recurrent SCA has implications to patients' counseling and management.
OBJECTIVE: The goal of this study is to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict recurrent SCA in this high-risk population.
METHODS: Patients (n = 5,286) whose index arrest was coded as a primary diagnosis were selected and followed to the endpoint of second SCA. The cohort was divided into training (n = 3,382, 3.8% event rate), internal validation (n = 846, 3.8% event rate), and holdout test (1,058, 3.8% event rate) sets. External validation was performed using a cohort of 1,776 patients (2.3% event rate). Multiple ML discriminators were tested using model area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative (NPV) predictive values, and F1 scores. The model with highest AUROC was evaluated on a holdout test set and was externally validated.
RESULTS: The gradient boosting (GB) model outperformed other models with AUROC of 0.93 in the internal validation set. It also achieved high discrimination in the holdout (AUROC=0.92), and external validation (AUROC = 0.90, sensitivity = 0.92, specificity = 0.83, F1 score = 0.19) sets. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) demonstrated that a diagnostic code of shockable rhythm (ventricular tachycardia), evidence of structural heart disease, conduction abnormalities, and initial blood work results at the time of the index arrest were main contributors to model prediction. Low (NPV ≥ 99%), intermediate, and high (PPV≥25%) risk groups defined from the internal validation set were applied to the holdout and external validation sets with strong prediction of time to recurrent SCA (p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: Our ML prediction model demonstrates very good and stable discrimination in the prediction of recurrent SCA based on explainable clinical factors. External validation results confirm the generalizability of our findings. This model could support risk stratification and counseling for survivors of SCA.

Title: Rhythmic auditory stimulation combined with split-belt treadmill training improves spatiotemporal gait parameters in hemiparetic stroke patients: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Split-belt walking training (SWT) primarily ameliorates spatial gait asymmetry after stroke, yet its effect on temporal gait parameters remains limited. Rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) enhances cadence and rhythmicity via auditory-motor coupling. This study examined whether combining RAS with SWT yields greater walking benefits than SWT alone or conventional rehabilitation.
METHODS: Thirty patients with post-stroke hemiparesis were randomized to RAS+SWT (n = 11), SWT alone (n = 8), or conventional rehabilitation (control, n = 11). Interventions were delivered for three weeks (five sessions/week). Primary outcomes were spatiotemporal gait parameters: walking speed, cadence, step length, and limping index. Linear mixed-effects models were used, with Hedges' g for effect sizes.
RESULTS: No dropouts occurred. Significant time-group interactions were found for walking speed (F = 10.68, p < 0.001), cadence (F = 5.01, p = 0.014), and affected-side step length (F = 6.21, p = 0.006). The RAS+SWT group showed greater improvements than controls in walking speed (mean difference = 0.167, 95% CI [0.090, 0.245]), cadence (mean difference = 9.340, 95% CI [4.456, 14.223]), and step length (unaffected: mean difference = 0.077, 95% CI [0.039, 0.116]; affected: mean difference = 0.081, 95% CI [0.035, 0.127]), and greater walking speed improvements than the SWT group (mean difference = 0.110, 95% CI [0.022, 0.197]). For the limping index, a significant main effect of group was observed (F = 5.41, p = 0.011); however, the time-by-group interaction was not significant (F = 0.430, p = 0.655).
CONCLUSION: RAS combined with SWT is more effective than conventional rehabilitation in improving multidimensional spatiotemporal gait parameters-including walking speed, cadence, and affected-side step length-in patients with post-stroke hemiparesis. Compared with SWT alone, the combined intervention yielded greater improvements in walking speed, while no significant between-group differences were observed for cadence or step length. The combined protocol is feasible and safe.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2600121963.

Title: The HALF-IT score: proposing a simplified mechanical thrombectomy triage tool for basilar artery occlusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is a devastating subtype of stroke with poor prognosis. Current patient selection tools for endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) are multi-tiered with interrater variability and limited validation studies. The HALF-IT score is a novel, simplified, dichotomized triaging tool focusing solely on the brainstem level. This study investigated the utility of the HALF-IT score to predict functional outcomes of EVT in patients with BAO.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, cohort study including patients with acute BAO presenting to four comprehensive stroke centers between 2021-2025. Acute infarction of ≥50% of any brainstem section on any axial or coronal slice of MRI was considered HALF-IT positive, whereas < 50% was considered HALF-IT negative. The primary efficacy outcome was a favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days; functional independence (mRS 0-2) was analyzed as a secondary outcome. Reperfusion was graded with the modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) scale. Primary safety endpoints included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage at 24 h and all-cause mortality at 90 days. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of the primary efficacy outcome.
RESULTS: 37 patients (23 HALF-IT negative; 14 HALF-IT positive) met the inclusion criteria. The rate of 90-day mRS 0-3 was significantly lower in the HALF-IT positive compared with HALF-IT negative group [14.3% vs. 68.2%, OR 0.08 (0.01-0.45), p = 0.004]. HALF-IT positive status remained associated with a lower rate of 90-day mRS 0-3 after adjusting for age, initial NIHSS, onset-to-reperfusion time, intravenous thrombolysis administration complete reperfusion (final mTICI 3) [adjusted OR 0.02, 95% CI 0-0.84, p = 0.02]. Safety events were numerically higher in the HALF-IT positive group but the difference did not reach statistical significance. The two groups differed substantially at baseline in age, presenting NIHSS, and intravenous thrombolysis exposure, whereas stroke etiology (p = 0.28) and level of basilar occlusion (p = 0.63) were similarly distributed.
CONCLUSION: In this small, retrospective, hypothesis-generating cohort, HALF-IT positivity was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes after EVT for BAO. Further prospective validation in larger cohorts is required before the score can inform treatment decisions.

Title: Association of endovascular treatment versus intravenous thrombolysis in mild stroke across occlusion subgroups.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) vs. intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is uncertain in minor stroke patients (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] ≤ 5) with anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO).
METHODS: The pooled cohort consisted of patients with NIHSS ≤ 5 and internal carotid artery (ICA), M1 or M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery (MCA) from the DETECT2-China study and the Early antiplatelet for minor stroke following thrombolysis (EAST) trial. The primary efficacy outcome was excellent functional outcome, defined as a mRS 0-1 at 90 days. The primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). Subgroup analyses were performed using interaction terms in logistic regression models to assess effect modification by baseline variable. To further explore the subgroup findings, analyses were repeated separately in patients with ICA/MCA-M1 occlusion and those with MCA-M2 occlusion.
RESULTS: A total of 237 patients were enrolled, including 105 (44.3%) with the IVT group, 132 (55.7%) with the EVT group. Compared to the IVT group, the EVT group had a similar proportion of excellent functional outcome (73.5% vs. 75.2%, aOR = 0.749, 95% CI = 0.392-1.433, p = 0.383), a numerically higher proportion of sICH (1.9% vs. 6.1%, aOR = 4.158, 95% CI = 0.819-21.127, p = 0.086). Subgroup analysis revealed that a numerically increased odds of excellent functional outcome was found in patients with ICA or MCA-M1 occlusion who received EVT vs. IVT (79.4% vs. 67.2%, aOR = 1.491, 95% CI: 0.693-3.211; p = 0.307), whereas significantly less probability of excellent functional outcome in those with MCA-M2 occlusion who received EVT vs. IVT (53.3% vs. 86.4%, aOR = 0.250, 95% CI: 0.057-0.980, p = 0.050). A significant interaction effect was identified between treatment (EVT vs. IVT) and excellent functional outcome (p for interaction = 0.008).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, the association between reperfusion strategy and functional outcome differed according to occlusion site. Patients with proximal occlusions (ICA or MCA-M1) in the EVT cohort had numerically better outcomes, whereas those with M2 occlusions in the EVT cohort had worse outcomes compared with the IVT cohort.

Title: Glycemic biomarkers and cardiovascular disease in diabetes: a comparative analysis of population-based and clinical cohorts.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a major complication contributing to morbidity and mortality among individuals with diabetes. Different glycemic biomarkers reflect distinct aspects of glucose metabolism, but their associations with prevalent CVD across different diabetic populations remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of fasting blood glucose (FBG), glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and triglyceride-glucose index (TyG) with prevalent CVD among adults with diabetes.
METHODS: This study included adults with diabetes from two independent cross-sectional cohorts: a population-based cohort derived from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005-2020 (n = 3,418) and a Chinese clinical cohort of hospitalized patients with diabetes (n = 765). Multivariable logistic regression models, subgroup analyses, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were performed to evaluate the associations between glycemic biomarkers and prevalent CVD.
RESULTS: After adjustment for potential confounders, HbA1c was consistently associated with prevalent CVD in both cohorts. In the fully adjusted model, each unit increase in HbA1c was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD in the population-based cohort (OR = 1.097, 95% CI: 1.002-1.202, P = 0.045) and the clinical cohort (OR = 1.413, 95% CI: 1.280-1.564, P < 0.001). In contrast, FBG and TyG were not significantly associated with prevalent CVD in the fully adjusted models. RCS analyses showed a significant overall association between HbA1c and prevalent CVD without evidence of nonlinearity in the NHANES cohort, whereas a significant nonlinear association was observed in the clinical cohort. TyG also showed a significant nonlinear association with prevalent CVD in the NHANES cohort. Subgroup analyses did not show consistent evidence of effect modification across demographic and clinical characteristics.
CONCLUSION: Among adults with diabetes, HbA1c showed a consistent positive association with prevalent CVD across population-based and clinical cohorts, whereas the associations of FBG and TyG were less consistent. These findings support the relevance of HbA1c as a measure of long-term glycemic status in relation to prevalent CVD among individuals with diabetes. Further longitudinal studies are warranted to clarify the temporal relationship between HbA1c and cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Sphingolipid-renal interplay in coronary artery calcification: ceramide profiling and imaging validation from the CRUISE-MET study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) represents a distinct imaging phenotype reflecting advanced vascular remodeling, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, metabolic determinants linking renal dysfunction to CAC remain incompletely understood. Ceramides, bioactive sphingolipids involved in vascular inflammation and calcification, may represent potential mediators of this interaction.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis of 851 coronary artery disease (CAD) patients from the CRUISE-MET trial (NCT06383208), six plasma ceramide species [Cer(18:1/16:0), (18:1/18:0), (18:1/20:0), (18:1/22:0), (18:1/24:0), and (18:1/24:1)] were quantified by UHPLC-MS/MS. CAC severity was classified angiographically as absent, mild, moderate, or severe. Logistic regression, ROC analysis, and restricted cubic splines assessed associations. Joint and mediation analyses examined interactions with CKD. Sensitivity analyses evaluated consistency across subgroups and in a cohort with non-ECG-gated chest CT-derived CAC scores.
RESULTS: Patients with moderate-to-severe CAC had higher Cer(18:1/16:0), Cer(18:1/24:1), older age, higher SYNTAX scores, and lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (all p<0.05). Each SD increase in Cer(18:1/16:0) was associated with 59% higher odds of moderate-to-severe CAC (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.33-1.88, p<0.001); the highest tertile was associated with 151% higher odds (OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.68-3.75, p<0.001). CKD modified this association (p for interaction=0.032), with coexisting CKD and high ceramide exposure yielding nearly fourfold higher odds (OR = 3.94, 95% CI: 2.47-6.28, p<0.001). Mediation analysis indicated Cer(18:1/16:0) accounted for 15.6% of the CKD-CAC association. Associations remained directionally consistent across sensitivity analyses. In the CT subgroup, modest associations were observed between selected ceramide species and quantitative CACS.
CONCLUSION: Specific ceramides, particularly Cer(18:1/16:0), are independently associated with CAC severity, with stronger associations observed in patients with CKD.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Large-bore Mechanical Thrombectomy for Treatment of Intermediate-high Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Single-center Australian Experience.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy is an emerging treatment for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism. We report outcomes from an Australian cohort.
