MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis compared patients with intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, defined according to the 2019 European Society of Cardiology guidelines, who were managed before large-bore mechanical thrombectomy implementation (May 2023-April 2024) with those treated with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (May 2024-October 2025) at a teaching hospital within a multidisciplinary pulmonary embolism response team framework. The primary endpoint was procedural feasibility and safety. Secondary endpoints included hemodynamic changes, intensive care unit utilization and 30-day mortality.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients were included: 24 treated with large-bore mechanical thrombectomy (median age 66.5, interquartile range 51.8-73.0 years; 58.3% male) and 43 treated with anticoagulation and/or thrombolysis (median age 76.0, interquartile range 65.5-82.5 years; 34.9% male). Technical success was 100%. Mean pulmonary arterial pressure decreased from 28.5 ± 8.7 to 21.2 ± 5.6 mmHg (p < 0.001). Heart rate and respiratory rate improved at 24 hours (both p < 0.001), although adjusted analyses showed no significant between-group differences in hemodynamic changes. Intensive care unit length of stay was shorter in the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group (20.1 ± 7.9 vs 32.2 ± 17.3 hours, p = 0.003), with multivariable analysis confirming an independent 43% reduction (exp(β) = 0.57, 95% confidence interval 0.42-0.79, p = 0.001). No major bleeding events or deaths within 30-days occurred in the large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group, compared with two major bleeding events (4.7%) and three mortalities (7.0%) in the non-large-bore mechanical thrombectomy group.
CONCLUSIONS: Large-bore mechanical thrombectomy appears to be a safe and feasible treatment modality for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism and was associated with reduced intensive care unit utilization compared with conventional therapies. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies.

Title: Dissociation between structural reverse remodeling and clinical outcomes in ischemic cardiomyopathy undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy: a real-world analysis.
Journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
Abstract: Patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) generally exhibit better responses to cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) due to more pronounced reverse remodeling compared to ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) patients. However, the prognostic impact of CRT in ICM patients remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of heart failure (HF) etiology on reverse remodeling, clinical outcomes, and survival following CRT in a real-world population. We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients who underwent CRT-P (pacing)/CRT-D (defibrillator) implantation. Patients were stratified according to HF etiology (ICM vs. NICM). The primary composite endpoint was the occurrence of all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization. Secondary outcomes focused on echocardiographic measures of left ventricular reverse remodeling. Survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models. Of the 95 patients initially screened, 83 were included in the final analysis, of whom 38 (45.8%) had ICM. The mean age was 69.5±10.4 years, and 75.8% were male. Both groups received similar medical therapy. NICM patients demonstrated a significant improvement in reverse remodeling after CRT [left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF): 32.3±11.5% to 44.0±13.2%, p=0.001); end-diastolic volume (LVEDV): 189.6±74.3 mL to 143.9±48.9 mL, p=0.010] with post-CRT LVEF being higher than in ICM patients (44.0±13.2% vs. 35.5±13.5%, p=0.003). NICM patients were more likely to be super-responders (58.1% vs. 25.0%, p=0.014). No significant differences were observed between groups in the primary composite endpoint (27.3% vs. 42.1%, p=0.171) or overall survival over a mean follow-up of 35 months (log-rank p=0.733). Although ICM patients showed less pronounced reverse remodeling following CRT, long-term clinical outcomes and survival were comparable to those observed in NICM. These findings reinforce the role of CRT as a disease-modifying therapy that prevents disease progression irrespective of HF etiology and support its systematic use in all eligible patients.

Title: Next-Generation Sequencing in Pediatric Lipid Disorders: Expanding the Genetic Landscape and Clinical Understanding.
Journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to assess the utility of next-generation sequencing panels in the molecular evaluation of pediatric lipid metabolism disorders and identifying clinically relevant and novel genetic variants.
METHODS: Sixty-seven pediatric patients with clinical signs of dyslipidemia were valuated retrospectively. Lipid profiles, clinical findings, and family histories were recorded. Patients were referred for genetic evaluation because of dyslipidemia and/or clinical or familial features suggestive of an inherited lipid disorder. The criteria used for referral differed according to the lipid phenotype and included marked or persistent lipid abnormalities, relevant family history, and characteristic clinical findings. NGS was performed using a 25-gene custom panel related to lipid metabolism.
RESULTS: Genetic variants were identified in 44 patients (65.6%), with 33 distinct variants across multiple genes, including 13 novel variants. Six patients had multiple variants in different genes. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were significantly more common among patients with a positive family history (p = 0.002). Several novel variants showed a potential genotype-phenotype correlation, particularly in patients with severe manifestations such as xanthomas, hepatosteatosis, or atherosclerosis.
CONCLUSION: In children with clinically suspected inherited lipid disorders, multigene NGS testing may provide clinically useful molecular information and complement careful clinical phenotyping and family history assessment. Genetic testing may be particularly informative in children with a strong or suggestive family history or with phenotypes raising suspicion for a monogenic lipid disorder. However, a negative NGS result does not exclude a genetic etiology, and genetic findings should be interpreted in the context of the clinical phenotype.

Title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis.
METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors.
RESULTS: Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, p = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, p = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, p = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, p = .039).
CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

Title: Clinical Phenotypes, Machine-Learning Risk Stratification and Treatment Outcomes of Constipation in Stroke Patients Receiving Enteral Nutrition: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke-related complications and frequent feeding interruptions often compromise nutritional intake, making enteral nutrition (EN) a cornerstone therapy to improve nutritional status and support recovery. Nevertheless, constipation is highly prevalent and clinically consequential among stroke patients receiving EN, particularly in critically ill populations, where enteral nutrition-associated constipation can impede rehabilitation, increase complications and prolong intensive care unit (ICU) stay.
AIM: This study aimed to explore potentially important determinants of enteral nutrition-associated constipation (ENAC) in patients with stroke using artificial intelligence approaches, characterise relevant clinical subgroups, compare internally validated machine-learning models and examine how the temporal availability of candidate predictors may influence model performance.
STUDY DESIGN: Clinical data from patients admitted to a neurological intensive care unit between December 2019 and December 2023 were retrospectively analysed. K-means clustering was used to identify clinical subgroups. Six algorithms-logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting tree, XGBoost, LightGBM and Table PFN-3-were compared under temporally restricted and expanded retrospective feature frameworks using five repeats of nested five-fold cross-validation. Performance was assessed using ROC-AUC, average precision, Brier score, calibration and decision-curve analysis. Treatment outcomes were summarised descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 362 patients, 233 (64.4%) had documented constipation. Table PFN-3 achieved the highest discrimination in both frameworks. The temporally restricted model yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.629 (95% CI 0.567-0.689), whereas the expanded retrospective model achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.771 (95% CI 0.715-0.820), average precision of 0.857, Brier score of 0.177 and calibration slope of 0.965. The ROC-AUC increased by 0.142 (95% CI 0.090-0.201) after full-hospitalisation information was included. K-means clustering retained three subgroups (K = 3; silhouette coefficient = 0.108), with constipation frequencies of 67.35%, 56.98% and 88.89% in Clusters 0, 1 and 2, respectively. Among evaluable patients, observed relief was 80.3% with glycerin enema, 60.0% with lactulose, 72.7% with combination treatment and 65.7% with neither treatment; these treatment comparisons were descriptive.
CONCLUSIONS: Table PFN-3 achieved the strongest internally validated performance, with the expanded retrospective framework combining good discrimination, strong precision-recall performance and close calibration. The 0.142 increase in ROC-AUC after completed hospital-course variables were incorporated quantifies the substantial discriminative information that emerges as hospitalisation evolves. Together with the distinct clinical phenotypes and descriptive treatment findings, these results establish a clinically relevant framework for trajectory-aware bowel monitoring and provide a clear rationale for developing dynamic, time-updated prediction models.
RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: By integrating machine-learning benchmarking, clinical phenotyping and observed treatment outcomes, this study identifies prolonged, treatment-intensive hospital trajectories as a particularly high-burden constipation phenotype and demonstrates that classification performance changes materially as hospital-course information accumulates. These findings support structured reassessment of bowel risk during neurological intensive care rather than reliance on a single static evaluation and provide a practical rationale for future dynamic monitoring tools.

Title: International Collaboration in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
Abstract: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) exemplifies how international collaboration can transform the study of a rare disease. Since the identification of the first PCD-associated genes in 1999-2002, parallel developments in Europe and North America, driven by patient organizations, academic investigators, and coordinated funding initiatives, have progressively converged into a unified global research infrastructure. Early milestones included the founding of patient advocacy groups, the NIH-funded Genetic Disorders of Mucociliary Clearance Consortium, and European projects such as EUCILIA and SYSCILIA, which respectively established coordinated clinical research infrastructure and advanced ciliary systems biology. The 2012 EU-funded BESTCILIA project formalized transatlantic collaboration, establishing the International PCD Registry and iPCD Cohort, generating the first robust diagnostic evidence base, and enabling the first multinational randomized controlled trial in PCD. This infrastructure was subsequently sustained and expanded through the BEAT-PCD COST Action and its successor ERS Clinical Research Collaboration, the ERN-LUNG PCD Core Network, and the PCD Clinical Trial Network, alongside parallel North American developments including the PCD Foundation Clinical and Research Centers and PCDF Network for Clinical Trials. Together, these initiatives have harmonized diagnostic pathways, produced joint ERS/ATS diagnostic guidelines, and created durable platforms for multinational trials and registries. Dedicated scientific meetings, culminating in the planned 2026 Global PCD Congress, further embody this convergence. Despite this progress, disparities in global representation and diagnostic access remain, underscoring the need for continued international coordination as the field moves toward precision medicine approaches.

Title: Rapid Response System Escalation During Recovery of Hospital Bed Occupancy: An Observational Longitudinal Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early warning scores (EWS) identify patient deterioration, but their impact depends on how they are integrated into workflows and escalation culture, particularly as hospitals recover from pandemic-related bed pressures.
AIMS: To evaluate changes in rapid response system (RRS) escalation processes and rare safety outcomes after embedding an EWS within proactive Critical Care Outreach Team (CCOT) rounds as hospital bed occupancy recovered.
STUDY DESIGN: Observational longitudinal study at a single tertiary hospital in Japan comparing one pre-intervention year (2021) with three post-intervention years (2022-2024). In January 2022, a standardised EWS was embedded into proactive CCOT rounds and used as a prompt for shared clinical reasoning rather than a strict numeric trigger. Monthly aggregated ward-level data were analysed using Poisson regression, adjusting for seasonality, patient characteristics and bed occupancy.
RESULTS: Across 71 985 admissions and 692 942 general-ward patient-days, rates of nurse-initiated escalations, RRS activations and resuscitation-status updates per 1000 patient-days increased in post-intervention analyses, but these differences were attenuated after full adjustment. In fully adjusted models, post-intervention incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were close to 1.0 for all process outcomes. For nurse-initiated escalations, IRRs ranged from 0.94 to 1.14, and all 95% confidence intervals included 1.0. Rates of unexpected in-hospital cardiac arrest and unplanned ICU admission remained low and stable. Bed occupancy increased over the study period, but within-year associations with outcomes were weak.
CONCLUSIONS: After adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital bed occupancy, embedding an EWS within proactive CCOT rounds was associated with broadly stable escalation process indicators and no clear evidence of deterioration in rare safety outcomes.
RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: These findings suggest that approaches to the RRS afferent limb that embed EWS use within structured dialogue between ward nurses and outreach teams may provide one plausible mechanism for sustaining escalation behaviours under operational pressure.

Title: Energy Drink Consumption and Premature Coronary Events: Two Case Reports and a Systematic Patient-Level Review of 31 Published and Newly Reported Patients.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract: Energy drink (ED) consumption has been temporally associated with acute coronary events, particularly in young individuals; however, causality remains uncertain. We aimed to characterize coronary events reported following ED consumption and evaluate their clinical features, underlying mechanisms, and causal plausibility. Two new cases of premature myocardial infarction (MI) were combined with cases identified through a systematic review of the literature published through September 2026. Patient-level data on ED exposure, cardiovascular risk factors, coronary mechanisms, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Causality was assessed using an adapted World Health Organization-Uppsala Monitoring Centre (WHO-UMC) framework. The cohort comprised 31 male patients (29 previously published cases and two new cases; mean age, 25.6 +- 5.4 years). Twenty-eight patients (90.3%) met strict criteria for MI or acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and 25 (80.6%) presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Coronary thrombosis was documented in 13 patients (41.9%), coronary vasospasm in eight (25.8%), and spontaneous coronary artery dissection in three (9.7%). Additional exposures or physiological stressors were identified in 22 patients (71.0%). The initial left ventricular ejection fraction was below 50% in 10 of the 19 evaluable patients (52.6%). Cardiac arrest occurred in six patients (19.4%), and two patients died (6.5%). Causality was classified as probable/likely in five patients (16.1%), possible in 23 (74.2%), and unlikely in three (9.7%). Coronary events temporally associated with ED consumption predominantly affected young men, involved heterogeneous mechanisms, and were associated with potentially severe outcomes. The frequent presence of coexisting risk factors and limited causal evidence preclude definitive attribution of these events to ED consumption. Prospective controlled studies are needed to clarify the independent cardiovascular risks associated with ED consumption.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Case Reports; Review

Title: Prospective Associations of Diet Quality During Pregnancy With Cardiovascular Health (Life's Essential 8) Among Women in Midlife.
Journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular health (CVH) often declines in midlife. Diet during pregnancy, a similarly sensitive period involving physiological changes, may influence long-term CVH, but few studies have examined this relationship. We examined the associations between diet during pregnancy and CVH in midlife.
METHODS: Participants are 776 women enroled in Project Viva during early pregnancy (1999-2002, mean 32.7 years). Participants completed food frequency questionnaires during the first and second trimesters, from which we calculated three diet scores (higher scores = better diet): Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Mediterranean Diet (MD) and Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII × -1). We averaged scores across trimesters and generated internal z-scores. At the midlife visit (2017-2021, mean 51.1 y), we assessed CVH using the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (range 0-100; higher scores = better CVH), including behavioural (diet, physical activity, sleep, smoking) and biomedical (BMI, blood pressure, lipids, glucose) subscores. We assessed associations using linear regression adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, nativity, education, parity, marital status and income at enrolment.
RESULTS: Most participants were non-Hispanic White (70%) and college graduates (76%). Mean midlife CVH score was 76.3 points. Higher (per 1-SD) DASH z-scores were associated with better overall (β 3.3; 95% CI 2.2-4.3), behavioural (3.5; 2.5-4.4) and biomedical (3.1; 1.5-4.7) CVH scores. Higher MD z-scores were associated with better overall CVH (2.4; 1.4-3.4), behavioural (2.6; 1.6-3.5) and biomedical (2.6; 1.0-4.2) scores. Higher DII (× -1) z-scores were associated with better overall CVH (2.6; 1.6-3.7), behavioural (2.7; 1.7-3.7) and biomedical (2.5; 0.9-4.1) scores. A better pregnancy diet was associated with higher CVH scores for diet, physical activity and BMI, and both DASH and DII with blood pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: Women who consumed healthier diets during pregnancy had better CVH two decades later. Dietary assessment in pregnancy may identify women at risk for both short-term and long-term health problems.

Title: Comparison of cardiac magnetic resonance findings in idiopathipulmonary arterial hypertension and that associated with CHD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare cardiac MRI findings between children diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and those with pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with CHD, and to determine whether there are prognostic differences between these groups.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 paediatric patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, who underwent standardised cardiac MRI evaluation. Key functional and flow parameters were analysed and compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: There were no significant differences in right ventricular volume, mass, and function parameters, and right atrial volume index, or septal shift findings. However, left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, left ventricular end-systolic volume index, left ventricular ejection fraction, left ventricular mass index, and right-left ventricle volume ratios were significantly different between groups. A ventricular mass index ≥75% was more common in idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension patients.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac MRI-based assessment reveals meaningful differences in left ventricle volume and mass parameters between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with CHD patients. These findings may aid in follow-up strategies for paediatric pulmonary arterial hypertension.

Title: The Fibular Artery Communicating Branch and Fibular Artery Dominance: An Anatomical Hazard for Posterior Approaches to the Ankle.
Abstract: Open reduction of posterior malleolar fractures (PMFs) increasingly employs direct posterior approaches. The posterolateral and posteromedial approaches both develop the deep posterior compartment in the plane between the fibular and posterior tibial arteries, placing the fibular artery communicating branch (FACB) within the operative field; inadvertent injury to this branch has been associated with limb-threatening ischemia. This study quantified the prevalence of the FACB and of fibular artery dominance (FAD), a configuration in which the fibular artery provides the principal distal supply because the posterior tibial artery is atretic or absent, and considered the implications for surgical approach selection. In a single-center cross-sectional study, 916 consecutive lower-limb computed tomography angiograms performed over 1 year were screened; 726 met the inclusion criteria and were assessed by trained reviewers for the FACB, FAD, laterality and clinical indication. An FACB was identified in 280 patients (38.6%, 95% CI 35.1-42.2). Its prevalence varied with clinical indication (χ2 = 33.67, p < 0.001), being highest in peripheral vascular disease (45.1%) and lowest in other vascular referrals (16.4%). FAD occurred exclusively in FACB-positive limbs, in 28 patients (10.0% of FACB-positive limbs; 3.9% of the whole cohort, 95% CI 2.7-5.5), and its distribution did not differ by indication (Freeman-Halton exact p = 0.81). Because the FACB lies within the field of the posterolateral and posteromedial approaches but posterior and lateral to the medial-posteromedial (MPM) approach, the MPM approach avoids the at-risk plane. These findings support anatomically informed approach selection and caution when a posterolateral or posteromedial approach is planned, particularly in patients with peripheral vascular disease.

Title: Stroke-Heart Syndrome: Mechanisms, Temporal Phenotypes, and Diagnostic Reasoning.
Abstract: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) encompasses new or worsened cardiac abnormalities that arise after acute stroke, most often within the first 30 days and with an early peak. Its spectrum includes acute myocardial injury, electrocardiographic changes, arrhythmia, ventricular dysfunction, Takotsubo syndrome, and heart failure, but similar findings may reflect antecedent cardiac disease or systemic illness. This Review defines the accepted clinical boundaries of SHS and integrates central autonomic network disruption, neuroendocrine stress, inflammation, endothelial and microvascular dysfunction, oxygen supply-demand imbalance, and premorbid substrate into a time-resolved framework. Eight provisional, non-mutually-exclusive phenotypic domains are proposed to organize current evidence without implying validated endotypes. A diagnostic approach based on symptom chronology, prior cardiac data, serial troponin and electrocardiography, rhythm monitoring, echocardiography, selective coronary assessment, and cardiac magnetic resonance is presented to distinguish stroke-triggered injury from recent myocardial infarction, pre-existing atrial fibrillation, chronic myocardial injury, and established heart failure. No syndrome-specific treatment is validated; care should prioritize recognized cardiac emergencies, correction of reversible stressors, and coordinated stroke-cardiology decision-making. Prospective studies with documented premorbid status, standardized time points, and blinded adjudication are needed to validate the proposed phenotypes and determine whether they improve outcomes.

Title: Revisiting VACTERL Association in Patients With Esophageal Atresia With an Emphasis on Skeletal Anomalies.
Journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to characterize VACTERL-associated anomalies in patients with esophageal atresia (EA), with particular emphasis on skeletal anomalies.
METHODS: 168 EA patients were evaluated as those with a distal TEF (D-TEF) (86.9%), those without D-TEF (9.5%), and isolated TEF (3.6%). In the D-TEF subgroup, a gap length of ≥ 4 vertebral-body was defined as long-gap EA (15.8%). Baseline neonatal chest and spine radiographs were reviewed using a standardized protocol.
RESULTS: The mean gestational age was 36.41 ± 3.04 weeks. The mean birth weight was 2525.35 ± 728.52 g. Long-gap D-TEF patients had lower gestational age and birth weight (p = 0.014 and p = 0.001, respectively). Vertebral, rib, renal, limb, and cardiac anomalies and anorectal malformations (ARM) were present in 17.9%, 14.9%, 19.6%, 9.5%, 38.1%, and 12.5%, respectively. Vertebral and rib anomalies were significantly associated (p < 0.05). Exploratory analyses suggested differences in vertebral-anomaly location across EA subtypes (nominal p = 0.038) and in limb-anomaly frequency across anatomic EA subtypes (nominal p = 0.047). ARM was more frequent in long-gap than short-gap D-TEF (30.4% vs. 8.9%; p = 0.010). It remained significant across sensitivity analyses using alternative gap-length thresholds. VACTERL association was present in 25.0% of the cohort, without a significant association with anatomic subtype.
CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal anomalies were common across EA phenotypes with possible subtype-related differences in their distribution. A standardized assessment on baseline radiographs may improve VACTERL phenotyping and provide a more accurate description of the musculoskeletal burden in patients with EA. The association between ARM and greater gap length in D-TEF should be interpreted within the present cohort and the study-specific gap-length definition.

Title: Ex Vivo Thrombin Generation Assessment of Four Anticoagulants in Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
Abstract: Venous thromboembolic events (VTE) are a serious complication in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Currently, there is no consensus regarding anticoagulant treatment or prevention in this setting, and the role of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) has not been extensively studied. The recent approval of DOACs for the treatment of VTE in children supports their further evaluation in pediatric patients with ALL. We prospectively evaluated the effects of four anticoagulant agents in 67 pediatric patients with ALL, compared with healthy controls, using the global coagulation assay thrombin generation (TG). The first 21 patients formed the calibration cohort, and we performed the primary TG analysis in the subsequent 46 patients. Measurements were performed before and after asparaginase therapy, with and without ex vivo spiking of the different anticoagulants. Low-molecular-weight heparin demonstrated preserved anticoagulant activity both before and after asparaginase therapy, with reductions of 29% and 31% in thrombin peak height, respectively, similar to healthy controls. However, the direct factor Xa inhibitors apixaban and rivaroxaban showed minimal anticoagulant effect (7%-13% reduction in thrombin peak height compared with reductions of 48%-59%, in controls). Notably, dabigatran, an oral direct thrombin inhibitor, demonstrated substantial anticoagulant activity before and after asparaginase therapy, with 180% and 134% prolongation of lag time, respectively, comparable to controls. These ex vivo pharmacodynamics findings support the anticoagulant activity of LMWH and dabigatran. The clinical efficacy of dabigatran in pediatric patients with ALL should be further investigated and confirmed in prospective in vivo studies.

Title: Diagnosis-Intervention Packet (DIP) Payment Standard Versus Actual In-Hospital Cost: Insights From a Chinese County Hospital.
Journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Evaluate alignment between calculated Diagnosis-Intervention Packet (DIP) payment entitlements and observed inpatient costs and identify insurance, regional, and disease-group patterns in payment-cost misalignment.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational study of all inpatient final settlements (2023-2024).
METHODS: We analyzed 23,597 discharge settlements using linear mixed-effects models with DIP group as a random intercept and heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors to compare signed payment-cost gaps. Robustness was assessed with model diagnostics and 1st-99th percentile trimming; separate gamma-log mixed models evaluated total cost and calculated DIP payment. Analyses compared insurance type (UEBMI vs. URRBMI) and insured region (local vs. non-local); high-volume DIP groups were defined as those with at least 150 admissions, and groups with cost-to-calculated-payment ratios of at least 3.0 were profiled as descriptive outliers.
RESULTS: Mean total cost per admission was CNY 14,604 and mean calculated DIP payment was CNY 4865, equivalent to 33.3% of observed inpatient cost. The mean signed payment-cost gap was -CNY 9739. Adjusted gaps were more negative for UEBMI than URRBMI (-CNY 12,971 vs. -CNY 8936) and for non-local than local admissions (-CNY 11,796 vs. -CNY 9279); trimmed analyses were consistent. Ten high-volume cerebrovascular, oncologic, renal, cardiac, infectious, and pancreatic clusters accounted for 18.8% of episodes and 35.6% of the cohort's net payment-cost shortfall.
CONCLUSIONS: At this county hospital, calculated DIP payments were equivalent to about one-third of observed inpatient spending, with concentrated shortfalls in complex neurovascular and oncologic groups and larger adjusted gaps among UEBMI and non-local admissions. These associations should not be interpreted causally because detailed clinical severity and comorbidity were unavailable. Although site-specific, the findings suggest that case-based payment systems may require severity adjustment, outlier protection, and periodic recalibration to reduce systematic payment-cost misalignment while safeguarding access to complex care.

Title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been associated with cardiovascular complications including cardiac arrhythmias. However, the relative contributions of respiratory, oxygenation, and sleep architecture indices to composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index remain incompletely understood.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the sequential associations of sleep architecture, nocturnal oxygenation, and respiratory disturbance indices with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index in patients undergoing polysomnography (PSG).
METHODS: Demographic, respiratory, oxygenation and sleep-architecture variables were extracted from PSG records. The primary outcome was a composite PSG-derived rhythm-event count, estimated as round(arrhythmia index × TST_hours) from the PSG-exported arrhythmia index, which was calculated during total sleep time only. Negative binomial regression used an offset of log(TST_hours). Because the outcome demonstrated overdispersion, negative binomial regression with an offset of log(TST hours) was used. Because the original 14-predictor model was over-parameterized for the sample size, a six-predictor model (age, sex, BMI, AHI, T90, and sleep efficiency) was chosen post hoc. This reduced model was not prespecified before the original analysis. Sleep efficiency was retained because it showed a strong signal in the exploratory 14-predictor model. The resulting p-values should therefore be interpreted as optimistic and exploratory. A sequential model-building approach (Model 1: age, sex, BMI, AHI; Model 2: plus T90; Model 3: plus sleep efficiency) was used to document the incremental contribution of each domain. A fully adjusted 14-predictor model was fitted only as a supplementary analysis. Wald 95% CIs and bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (2000 resamples) are reported.
RESULTS: Forty-one participants were included (mean age 47.8 ± 13.5 years; median BMI 29.4 kg/m2). Severe OSA (AHI ≥ 30 events/hour) was present in 56.1%. Median arrhythmia index was 3.2 events/hour, with marked overdispersion. In the six-predictor model, only higher sleep efficiency was associated with lower arrhythmia rate (IRR = 0.946 per 1 percentage-point increase, 95% CI 0.921-0.972, p < 0.001; bootstrap 95% CI 0.888-0.984). T90 was associated in the Wald inference (IRR = 1.034, 95% CI 1.006-1.063, p = 0.016) but this association was not robust under bootstrap resampling (95% CI 0.979-1.067). AHI was not associated with arrhythmia rate (IRR = 1.000, 95% CI 0.987-1.014, p = 0.954). Age, sex and BMI were also not significant. A 14-predictor exploratory model had a marginally lower AIC (411.4) but a substantially higher BIC (438.8), consistent with overfitting.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory selected sleep-center cohort, AHI and other respiratory-event indices were not independently associated with the composite PSG-derived rhythm-event index. Only higher sleep efficiency showed a robust association with lower arrhythmia rate, but this finding is hypothesis-generating and may reflect unmeasured confounding. These results require confirmation in larger prospective studies and should not guide clinical risk stratification.

Title: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk.
AIM: The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups.
STUDY DESIGN: This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC).
RESULTS: This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons.
CONCLUSIONS: Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes.
RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

Title: Immediate drug hypersensitivity severity is associated with cardiovascular risk.
Abstract: Background: Drug hypersensitivity reactions (DHR) exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity. Although established cardiovascular disease is a known risk factor for severe anaphylaxis, the impact of subclinical cardiovascular risk on DHR severity remains poorly understood. Objective: This study investigated the association between Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2 (SCORE2) estimated cardiovascular risk and the severity of immediate-type DHRs. Methods: This retrospective study included 161 patients ages 40-69 years (median age, 49 years; 79.5% women) with immediate-type DHRs. To assess the subclinical risk, those with known cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease were excluded. Reaction severity was graded by using the Brown system, and SCORE2 was calculated by using clinical data from the 12 months preceding the reaction. Results: Reaction severity was graded as mild (35.4%), moderate (34.8%), or severe (29.8%). The median SCORE2 values were significantly higher in the severe group versus the mild group (4.10% versus 2.50%; p = 0.022). The proportion of patients in high or very high SCORE2 risk categories increased stepwise with reaction severity (35.1% in the mild group versus 64.6% in the severe group; p = 0.011). In an univariable ordinal logistic regression, each 1-point increase in SCORE2 percentage was associated with higher odds of greater reaction severity (odds ratio 1.144 [95% confidence interval, 1.041-1.257]; p = 0.005). This association remained significant after adjusting for the culprit drug class (p = 0.008). Conclusion: Higher subclinical cardiovascular risk, as estimated by SCORE2, is significantly associated with increased DHR severity. Analysis of these findings suggests that vascular reserve may modulate the clinical presentation of drug-induced allergic reactions, potentially aiding in clinical risk stratification.

Title: Weight, blood glucose and lipid changes in the course of long-acting cabotegravir + rilpivirine: A prospective two-year evaluation.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There are little real-world data from observational cohorts regarding the impact of long-acting (LA) cabotegravir (CAB) and rilpivirine (RPV) treatment on weight and blood lipids.
METHODS: This multicentre, prospective, observational study included people with human immunodeficiency virus initiating LA CAB+RPV within the Surveillance Cohort Long-Term Toxicity Antiretrovirals (SCOLTA) cohort. Weight and cholesterol levels (total, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL)) were collected at six-month intervals within two-year follow-ups. A multivariate mixed linear model was run to determine the association between change from baseline and participants' characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 671 participants were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 22 (interquartile range [IQR]: 13-29) months. The median age was 49 years (IQR 40-58) and median duration of antiretroviral therapy (ART) was 10.3 years (IQR 6.4-16.7). There was no significant change in mean weight after 1 year and 2 years, with differences of -0.25 kg (95% CI: -0.59 to +0.08, p = 0.14) and -0.18 kg (95% CI: -0.70 to +0.33, p = 0.48), respectively. The multivariable analysis revealed that weight change was significantly associated with baseline body mass index (BMI). People with obesity and overweight experienced a significantly greater reduction in weight, compared to those of normal weight (mean estimate -1.66 kg, 95% CI -2.69 to -0.64, and -0.72 kg, 95% CI: -1.24 to -0.19, respectively). Total cholesterol (+6 mg/dL, 95% CI: +1.4 to +10.7), HDL cholesterol (+2.9 mg/dL, 95% CI: +1.2 to +4.7) and LDL cholesterol (+2.4 mg/dL, 95% CI: -1.8 to +6.6) increased at 2 years, with no change in the total/HDL ratio.
CONCLUSIONS: Body weight remained stable in the SCOLTA cohort after switching to LA CAB+RPV for 2 years. There was a modest but significant increase in cholesterol levels, though the ratio of total to HDL cholesterol remained stable.

Title: Aspirin Use for the Prevention of Preeclampsia, an Evidence-Based Review.
Abstract: Preeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that is defined by new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation along with proteinuria or evidence of end-organ dysfunction. Affecting 2-8% of pregnancies worldwide, preeclampsia remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. This disorder originates secondary to defective placentation during the first trimester, causing incomplete remodeling of the uterine spiral arteries, resulting in placental hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and the release of anti-angiogenic factors into the maternal circulation. This pathophysiology provided researchers a rationale for the use of low-dose aspirin as a preventive strategy for preeclampsia. Early studies investigated low-dose aspirin initiated at variable gestational ages and failed to show significant reductions in the incidence of preeclampsia. However, over the years, multiple meta-analyses studying aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention revealed a consistent decrease in the incidence of preeclampsia with the use of low-dose aspirin initiated at or before 16 weeks of gestation, with the efficacy being largely dependent on the time of initiation. In 2017, a randomized controlled trial demonstrated a statistically and clinically significant reduction in the incidence of preeclampsia leading to preterm delivery with aspirin initiated before 16 weeks gestation in women identified as high risk by first-trimester algorithm-based screening. Based on the strong evidence in support of aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention, current guidelines recommend initiation of aspirin 81 mg after 12 weeks and ideally before 16 weeks for all pregnant women at increased risk for preeclampsia.

Title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Vitamin K Antagonists for Atrial Fibrillation After Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery is common and is associated with stroke, prolonged hospitalization, and mortality; yet, the optimal oral anticoagulant in this setting remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) in adults requiring oral anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation after cardiac surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials. The primary outcome was any bleeding; secondary outcomes were stroke or transient ischemic attack, systemic embolism, major bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, reoperation, and length of hospital stay. Odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences (MDs) were pooled with random-effects models, risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Five randomized trials including 302 patients (153 DOACs and 149 warfarin) were included; rivaroxaban was tested in 3 trials, and apixaban and dabigatran in 1 trial each. Any bleeding did not differ significantly between DOACs and VKAs (9.2% vs 8.1%; OR, 1.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39-3.99).

Title: "Life and Lower Limb Threatening Condition" Clinical Features, Management and Outcomes of Diabetic Foot Ulcers Complicated by Gas Gangrene: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a common complication of diabetes in low- and middle-income countries and may be complicated by gas gangrene (GG), a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection. This prospective study assessed whether GG can be diagnosed clinically in low-resource primary care and explored factors associated with wound-healing outcomes in DFU complicated by GG. From December 2021 to June 2025, consecutive patients with diabetic foot infection and clinically active GG were enrolled. Data included demographics, ulcer history and examination, SINBAD classification, GG signs, sepsis status, comorbidities, management, and outcomes. All participants had classical clinical features of GG and were admitted for urgent surgical treatment. Ninety-nine patients (58 male) with classical GG were admitted for urgent surgery. Initial amputation was required in 18% (major 12%, minor 6%). Ten patients were lost to follow-up; that included six who died from foot-ulcer-related causes. Of 89 followed, 30 (33.7%) healed in 225.5 ± 126.9 days, while 59 remained unhealed after 146.1 ± 175.4 days; major amputations during treatment were more frequent in the healed group. Having a previous history of ulcer showed to increase the time to heal by 136 days. A one-day increase in treatment duration was associated with a 1% decrease in both the chance of healing or risk of amputation. Early diagnosis, aggressive medical and surgical intervention are the keys to decreasing morbidity and mortality of diabetic patients with gas gangrene; and remain the mainstay treatment of this dangerous condition globally. Patient's with previous ulcer history were found to need longer time to heal. Increasing treatment duration seems to be a double-edged sword, as while it is associated with reduced risk of amputation, it also decreases the chance of ulcer healing.

Title: Beyond Blood Cultures and Echocardiography: Emerging Diagnostics for Infective Endocarditis.
Abstract: Management of infective endocarditis (IE) is often confounded by the presence of prosthetic valves, transcatheter prostheses, and cardiovascular implantable electronic devices, as well as by changing epidemiologic risks and antimicrobial resistance patterns. For the diagnosis of IE, blood cultures and echocardiography remain foundational, but important gaps persist, particularly in culture-negative and prosthetic/device-associated infections. Contemporary diagnostic criteria and guidelines now support a multimodality approach incorporating molecular microbiology and advanced imaging. This review summarizes emerging technologies including broad-range 16S/18S/28S rRNA polymerase chain reaction and sequencing, fluorescence in situ hybridization coupled with sequencing, targeted and shotgun metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), plasma microbial cell-free DNA, cardiac computed tomography, and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron-emission tomography/computed tomography. We also examine the potential role of artificial intelligence in echocardiographic interpretation and of large language models in multimodal data integration. Current evidence suggests that tissue-based molecular testing generally provides greater microbiologic yield than valve culture in culture-negative IE, while blood-based mNGS and microbial cell-free DNA may extend pathogen detection after antibiotic exposure and reduce reliance on tissue-based diagnosis. However, heterogeneity in specimen handling, sequencing pipelines, contamination control, reporting thresholds, and clinical interpretation remains a major barrier to implementation. Future progress should move beyond pathogen detection toward rapid, reproducible, clinically actionable diagnosis that integrates organism identification, anatomic localization, disseminated disease, and personalized treatment. Prospective outcome trials, standardized workflows, cost-effectiveness studies, and multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team integration can help determine whether these technologies translate into better antimicrobial stewardship, procedural decision-making, and patient outcomes.

Title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on 12-Lead Electrocardiograms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic detection of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but available studies address distinct diagnostic questions. We systematically reviewed studies evaluating AI-based STEMI detection from 12-lead electrocardiograms and separately synthesized AI performance against a clinical reference standard, AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, and AI agreement with physician electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2010 through March 10, 2025. Bivariate random-effects models generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (AUC). Twenty-six studies comprising 539,876 ECGs were included. In 20 studies comparing AI with a clinical reference standard, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.91-0.97), specificity 0.95 (0.90-0.98), AUC 0.98 (0.97-0.99), positive likelihood ratio 19.2 (9.3-39.5), and negative likelihood ratio 0.05 (0.03-0.10). In 8 studies reporting both AI and clinician performance against a clinical reference, separate syntheses showed sensitivity of 0.91 (0.86-0.94) for AI versus 0.78 (0.69-0.85) for clinicians, specificity of 0.91 (0.82-0.96) for both, and AUCs of 0.95 and 0.90, respectively. In 7 studies using physician ECG interpretation as the comparator, AI sensitivity was 0.85 (0.70-0.94), specificity 0.99 (0.96-1.00), and AUC 0.98 (0.96-0.99). Sensitivity analyses excluding case-control designs, influential studies, and restricting analyses to deep learning models or raw waveform ECGs produced similar findings.

Title: Social and clinical determinants of liver transplant evaluation in hepatocellular carcinoma: A multicenter cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver transplantation (LT) is curative for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) but requires timely referral. Comprehensive data on factors impacting LT referral and outcomes for HCC are limited. We evaluated social, system, and clinical factors associated with listing, LT, mortality, HCC stage at referral, and time from HCC diagnosis to referral.
METHODS: The California Liver Network is a consortium of 6 LT centers comprising >75% of adult LTs in California. Demographic, clinical, psychosocial, and social determinants of health and outcome data were collected for adults referred for LT. Multivariable regression identified factors associated with outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 9987 adults referred, 1573 (15.7%) had HCC. Median age was 63.3 years; 73% males, 40% Hispanic, and 26.1% Medicaid insurance. Median MELD was 12.7 (IQR 8-16), and median time from HCC diagnosis to LT referral was 124 days (IQR 32-410). In all, 10% were T1 and 70.5% were T2 at referral. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (OR 0.99), HCC stage, Medicaid insurance (OR 0.55), LT site, and marital status (OR 1.90) were associated with listing. Transplantation was associated with HCC stage (OR 0.42) and LT site. Mortality was associated with MELD (OR 1.02), hypertension (OR 1.44), dialysis (OR 2.48), hepatic encephalopathy (OR 1.54), and portal vein thrombosis (OR 1.44). Referral at more advanced HCC stage was associated with male sex (OR 1.55), AFP (OR 1.01), Medicaid insurance (OR 1.40), primary language (OR 0.70), and prior HCC treatment type. Longer time to referral was associated with HCV/alcohol liver disease and prior HCC treatment type.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter study of adults with HCC, Medicaid insurance, LT site, HCC treatment history, and psychosocial factors were key determinants of HCC care cascade progression, identifying targets to improve LT access.

Title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Screening for Detection of Low Ejection Fraction in Routine Care: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) is common and treatable but often undiagnosed, especially in early stages with non-specific symptoms. AI applied to standard ECGs offers low-cost screening for low ejection fraction (EF), yet its real-world impact on diagnosis remains unclear.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs assessed AI-ECG screening for low EF in clinical practice. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261287652). Databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central, Google Scholar) were searched from inception to January 18, 2026, for RCTs comparing AI-ECG screening to usual care in adults without known heart failure undergoing routine ECGs. The primary outcome was new low EF (≤ 50%) confirmed by echocardiography. Secondary outcomes included echocardiography referral rates, positive predictive value, and cardiology referral rates. Pooled risk ratios (RR) with 95% CIs were calculated using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Three RCTs were included (two individual and one cluster) with 37,467 participants. After adjusting for clustering, AI-ECG screening significantly improved detection of new low EF diagnoses compared to usual care (RR 1.36, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.64; p = 0.002; I2 = 0%), with a number needed to screen of 204. No significant difference was found in echocardiography referral rates (RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; p = 0.55; I2 = 36%). The PPV of the AI tool ranged from approximately 20% to 34% across studies.
CONCLUSION: AI-ECG screening added to routine care improves low EF detection without substantially increasing echocardiography referrals. These findings support AI-ECG for earlier LVSD detection in at-risk populations, though further validation across diverse AI platforms is warranted.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Variation in Pediatric Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Survival After In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Development and Validation of a Survival Model for Risk-Standardized Survival Rates: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate a multivariable prediction model for survival to hospital discharge after pediatric extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and to use this model to derive risk-standardized survival rates (RSSRs) and quantify between-hospital variation in outcomes.
DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study.
SETTING: Hospitals contributing to the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry between 2020 and 2023.
PATIENTS: Children (< 18 yr) treated with ECPR for IHCA.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Eligible patients were identified from the ELSO Registry and split into derivation (N = 1060) and validation (N = 317) cohorts using a hospital-stratified split to preserve within-hospital clustering. Survival prediction models were derived using penalized logistic regression with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. A full-event model incorporating 14 routinely available clinical variables demonstrated fair discrimination (area under the curve, 0.728 in the derivation cohort and 0.678 in the validation cohort) and good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, 0.995; Brier score, 0.222 in the validation cohort). This model was embedded in a multilevel logistic regression model to generate hospital-level RSSRs for centers reporting five or more ECPR cases. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio, which was 1.30 (95% CI, 1.11-1.93), indicating significant differences in survival likelihood between centers after adjusting for patient-level risk.
CONCLUSIONS: In a large, international cohort of pediatric ECPR patients, we developed and internally validated a clinically interpretable model for survival to hospital discharge. The model performance as a discriminator likely limits its use as a standalone tool for clinical decision-making. However, strong internal calibration allowed for determination of hospital-level RSSRs, which revealed significant inter-hospital variability. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of developing a risk-adjustment model capable of estimating hospital-level RSSRs. Additional external validation and evaluation of residual case-mix differences are needed before such models can be used for benchmarking across pediatric ECPR centers.

Title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Concomitant coronary artery disease affects 40-75% of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Three recent randomized trials yielded conflicting findings: NOTION-3 demonstrated reduced composite events with pre-TAVI percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PRO-TAVI showed non-inferiority of PCI deferral with less bleeding; neither demonstrated mortality benefit. No previous meta-analysis combined all 3 trials with observational evidence, applied design-stratified GRADE certainty, or explored cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (3 randomized trials, 13 observational cohorts; 8,207 patients). Ten prespecified outcomes were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); 30-day all-cause mortality was primary. GRADE certainty was assessed separately for randomized and observational evidence. Prespecified design-based subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Pre-TAVI PCI was not associated with significant differences in 30-day all-cause mortality (RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.90-1.77; I2 = 32%) or 1-year mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15; I2 = 0%). Major bleeding (RR 1.19, 95% CI 0.98-1.44) and major vascular complications (RR 1.48, 95% CI 0.95-2.30) showed borderline non-significant trends favoring PCI deferral (both I2 = 0%). Excluding Griese et al. 2014, the principal driver of harm and heterogeneity, reduced cardiovascular mortality heterogeneity (RR 0.91; I2 = 24%). No significant differences occurred in stroke, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, pacemaker implantation, or rehospitalization. Routine pre-TAVI PCI confers no mortality benefit and may increase bleeding and vascular complications; PCI should be individualized according to coronary complexity, lesion significance, and bleeding risk.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Recaticimab in Patients With Dyslipidemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With GRADE Assessment.
Abstract: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the principal target for preventing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, yet many patients do not reach treatment goals with statins, and established proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) antibodies require injections every 2-4 weeks. Recaticimab is a humanized anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibody designed for dosing intervals of up to 12 weeks. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library up to March 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing recaticimab with placebo in adults with dyslipidemia. Four double-blind trials (1657 randomized participants) were included. At week 12, recaticimab reduced LDL-C by 47.31 percentage points relative to placebo (95% confidence interval [CI], -49.87 to -44.75; I2 = 0%), with similar reductions for 150 mg every 4 weeks (-49.63), 300 mg every 8 weeks (-49.43), and 450 mg every 12 weeks (-45.50) (P for subgroup difference = 0.29). Recaticimab also reduced non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-45.17), apolipoprotein B (-42.31), lipoprotein(a) (-31.06), the total cholesterol/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (-36.94), and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 ratio (-45.28), whereas the change in triglycerides was not significant (-10.05; 95% CI, -20.18 to 0.08).

Title: Intravenous Tenecteplase for Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Recent or Concurrent Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) alongside a recent or concurrent non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) occupy one of the least evidence-supported decision points in acute stroke care, excluded from every pivotal thrombolysis trial. The recent approval and guideline endorsement of tenecteplase-an agent separately licensed for myocardial infarction at twice the cerebral dose-adds a dimension the alteplase-derived literature does not address. This narrative review synthesizes the evidence on intravenous thrombolysis, specifically tenecteplase, in this setting and distinguishes infarct-related from treatment-related barriers to eligibility. Concomitant NSTEMI complicates approximately 1.6% of acute ischemic stroke hospitalizations and carries an adjusted 3.6-fold increase in in-hospital mortality. The historical contraindication derives from mechanisms-myocardial hemorrhage with free-wall rupture, postinfarction pericarditis with hemopericardium, and left ventricular thrombus embolization-that scale with transmurality and are therefore largely ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction phenomena. Registry data from more than 40,000 thrombolyzed patients show no significant excess of thrombolysis-related complications with recent NSTEMI, and fatal ruptures cluster in subacute ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction; the excess mortality is of similar magnitude without thrombolysis, marking a sicker patient rather than a more dangerous drug.

Title: Complete necrosis of HCC improves recurrence-free and overall survival after transplantation independent of baseline risk.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete pathologic necrosis (CPN) is associated with improved outcomes after liver transplantation for HCC. Whether this association persists after accounting for hepatic reserve, tumor burden, locoregional therapy modality, and risk of waitlist dropout remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network Standard Transplant Analysis and Research database, comprising 16,955 adult recipients bridged with locoregional therapy and a comparator group of 5867 recipients with no evidence of pretransplant treatment. Multivariable models were adjusted for hepatic reserve, tumor burden at original presentation, alpha-fetoprotein, and transplant era.
RESULTS: CPN was achieved in 5,132 patients (30.3%) and was associated with improved survival (adjusted HR: 0.73, 95% CI: 0.68-0.78) and reduced recurrence (adjusted HR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.31-0.44). Outcomes were similar whether necrosis was absent or incomplete (adjusted HR: 1.39 and 1.37 vs. complete necrosis). Relative to the no treatment comparator, no adjusted survival advantage was detected for treatment without CPN (HR: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.89-1.01), whereas recurrence was higher (HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.25-1.66). Compared with transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization and percutaneous ablation were associated with higher odds of CPN (adjusted odds ratios 2.19 and 1.84; both p<0.001). This association was observed in both baseline waitlist-dropout risk groups.
CONCLUSIONS: CPN was strongly associated with reduced posttransplant tumor recurrence and improved overall survival. Radioembolization and thermal ablation were the locoregional therapy modalities most likely to achieve CPN. These findings further establish CPN as an important objective of bridging and downstaging therapy.

Title: Insertable Cardiac Monitoring in Pediatric Patients: A Real-World Single-Center Experience With a New-Generation Device.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insertable cardiac monitors (ICMs) are increasingly used in pediatric patients, yet data on new-generation devices remain limited. The aim of this retrospective study was to describe a single-center real-world experience with a new-generation ICM in pediatric patients, focusing on procedural feasibility, sensing performance, transmission burden, and user experience.
METHODS: Consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing LUX-Dx ICM implantation between 2023 and 2025 were included. Procedural characteristics, sensing parameters, transmission patterns, diagnostic yield, reprogramming strategies, and patient/caregiver-reported experience were analyzed. Data are reported as median (25th-75th percentile) or mean ± standard deviation.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients underwent ICM implantation. Procedures were brief (6 ± 2 min) and complication-free. Electrical parameters were satisfactory and stable at discharge. Follow-up was 18 (6-23) months. A median of 2.7 transmissions per patient-month were received, of which 55% were alerts. Time from arrhythmia detection to transmission was 15 (3-21) hours. The number of episodes per patient was 4.8 (3.1-15.9) per month, with substantial inter-patient variability and bradycardia being the most frequent detection (80%). A diagnostic conclusion was reached in 79% of patients (positive: 45%, negative: 34%) at a median of 3 months. Reprogramming was performed in 90% of patients, mainly remotely (77%), and was predominantly directed toward reducing detection sensitivity. Patient and caregiver acceptance of remote monitoring was high.
CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric patients, new-generation ICM implantation was safe, well tolerated, and associated with stable sensing performance. Remote monitoring and reprogramming enabled timely diagnosis and individualized optimization, supporting the clinical utility of contemporary ICMs in this population.

Title: Above-Threshold Ambulatory Systolic Pressure and Left Ventricular Mass in Chronic Kidney Disease: Does AUC Add Beyond Mean Pressure?
Abstract: Above-threshold ambulatory systolic blood pressure (SBP) area under the curve (AUC) captures both the magnitude and duration of SBP above daytime and nighttime reference values. We examined whether this measure provided information about left ventricular mass index (LVMI) beyond daytime and nighttime mean SBP. In this cross-sectional study, 212 Chinese adults with non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) underwent ambulatory blood pressure monitoring and echocardiography. Daytime AUC above 135 mmHg and nighttime AUC above 120 mmHg were entered jointly. Together, daytime and nighttime AUC were significantly associated with LVMI (P < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.345). From the 25th to the 75th percentile, adjusted LVMI was 3.46 g/m2·7 higher for daytime AUC and 5.56 g/m2·7 higher for nighttime AUC. AUC attributable to daytime and nighttime mean SBP accounted for 89.7% of the cohort-average above-threshold burden. The remaining AUC not captured by those period means was not significantly associated with LVMI after adjustment for daytime and nighttime mean SBP (0.69 g/m2·7 per interquartile range; 95% confidence interval, -2.00 to 3.37). Above-threshold AUC was associated with greater LVMI but added limited information beyond daytime and nighttime mean SBP in this cohort.

Title: Ischemic severity rather than ischemic time is associated with major limb complications in traumatic popliteal artery injury: A retrospective case series.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Although prolonged ischemic time is considered a key determinant of limb loss in traumatic popliteal artery injury (PAI), it does not fully explain the variability in clinical outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether ischemic severity at presentation is associated with major limb complications in PAI.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with blunt PAI treated at a single trauma center between 2013 and 2025. Ischemic severity was assessed using the Rutherford classification and the presence of collateral circulation on computed tomography angiography (CTA). Patients were categorized into mild ischemia (Rutherford grade I-II) and severe ischemia (Rutherford grade III). Outcomes included extensive soft tissue defects requiring reconstruction and amputation.
RESULTS: Twenty-one limbs were included. Thirteen limbs were classified as mild ischemia and eight as severe ischemia. Collateral circulation was preserved in 17 limbs and absent in 4 limbs. The time to arterial reconstruction was comparable between groups. No major soft tissue complications occurred in the mild ischemia group. In contrast, 5 of 8 limbs with Rutherford grade III developed extensive soft tissue defects (p = 0.006). Absence of collateral circulation was also strongly associated with adverse outcomes, with all limbs without collateral flow developing major soft tissue complications (p = 0.002), despite a shorter time to revascularization.
CONCLUSION: Ischemic severity at presentation, particularly Rutherford grade III and absence of collateral circulation on CTA, is associated with major limb complications in traumatic PAI, whereas ischemic time alone may be insufficient to predict outcomes.

Title: Effects of Base Excess Levels at the End of Anhepatic Stage on Early Hepatic and Renal Function After Liver Transplantation: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe metabolic acidosis commonly occurs during the anhepatic phase of liver transplantation. Intravenous sodium bicarbonate is routinely administered to regulate intraoperative base excess (BE), but the independent correlation between pre-reperfusion BE and early postoperative hepatic and renal function remains insufficiently clarified in real-world cohort studies. This study aimed to explore whether discretionary mild alkalization with BE ≥ 0 before portal reperfusion affects early hepatorenal recovery after liver transplantation.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational cohort enrolled 68 adult liver transplant recipients treated from January to December 2024. Patients were divided into a mild alkalization group (BE ≥ 0 mmol/L, n = 38) and routine acidosis correction group (BE < 0 mmol/L, n = 30). Serial serum creatinine on postoperative day (POD) 1, 3, 7 was set as the primary renal outcome; postoperative liver enzymes, procalcitonin and post-reperfusion blood gas parameters were secondary outcomes. Multivariate linear regression adjusted for recipient, donor and intraoperative confounders was used to analyze correlations between end-anhepatic BE and organ injury markers. Post-hoc power analysis was performed to interpret neutral study results.
RESULTS: No intergroup statistical differences were found in serum creatinine at POD 1, 3 and 7, and repeated-measures ANOVA revealed consistent longitudinal creatinine trends between 2 cohorts (all P > .05). After multivariate adjustment, end-anhepatic BE showed no independent correlation with postoperative creatinine, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Intraoperative total sodium bicarbonate dosage presented weak univariate positive correlations with early liver enzyme elevation, which disappeared after confounding factor adjustment. Post-reperfusion blood gas, postoperative procalcitonin and reperfusion syndrome incidence were comparable in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Short-term mild intraoperative alkalization targeting BE ≥ 0 at the end of the anhepatic phase has no significant correlation with early postoperative hepatic and renal function within one week after liver transplantation. Cumulative intraoperative sodium bicarbonate consumption can act as a preliminary auxiliary marker reflecting early graft ischemia-reperfusion injury. Large prospective trials are required to verify whether alkalization strategies reduce reperfusion syndrome. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size.

Title: 2,611 Liver Transplants: Indications and Survival Rates of a High-Volume Latin American Center.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: The liver transplantation program at the Centro de Transplante de Fígado do Ceará (CTFC), one of the largest centers in Northern and Northeastern Brazil, was evaluated over a 23-year period to describe indications, recipient characteristics, and survival outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 2611 liver transplants performed in 2491 patients between 2002 and 2025. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and laboratory data were collected from medical records and managed using REDCap. Survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: Most recipients were middle-aged men, predominantly from outside the state, and nearly all procedures were funded by the public health system. The main indications for transplantation were decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and alcohol-related liver disease, reflecting global epidemiological shifts. Overall survival rates were 88% at one month, 79% at one year, and 71% at 5 years, with progressive improvement over time. Donor characteristics and ischemia times were consistent with international standards.
CONCLUSIONS: These results show that a high-volume public transplant center can achieve outcomes comparable to major international programs while serving a socioeconomically diverse population.

Title: Cross-sectional study in a lipoprotein apheresis centre: a thirty-year history of Practice, Investigation and Struggle against Atherosclerotic disease (P.I.S.A.).
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Lipoprotein apheresis (LA) has a protective role for endothelium and microcirculation and is able to reduce the incidence of major cardiovascular events. Recent advances in lipid-lowering drug therapy (LLT) lead to an improvement in the pre-apheresis lipid profile.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This cross-sectional study with retrospective event collection evaluates patient's clinical characteristic, backbone lipid-lowering therapies (LLT), major cardiovascular events (MACE) rate and causes of LA discontinuation in subjects who do not reach LDL-Cl (Group A - 36/92 patients), Lp(a) target values (Group B - 24/92 patients) or both (Group C - 32/92 patients). The prevalence of pre-LA and post-LA MACEs was respectively 203 and 75 events with a significant lower observed MACE rates in all the groups, the Kaplan-Meier analysis of time to first MACE during LA showed no difference in the three groups. Moreover, PCSK9i contribute to overcome statin intolerance allowing, especially in patients on group A, to discontinue LA.
CONCLUSIONS: Currently, LA maintaining a therapeutic role in subjects who do not reach LDL-C and/or Lp(a) targets, have a history of multiple MACEs and/or polydistrict atherosclerotic vascular disease or pregnancy HoFH who transient discontinue LLT.

Title: Multidimensional sleep health and risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: A MAIHDA-based prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The combined and interactive effects of multiple sleep dimensions on mortality remain unclear. We applied Multilevel Analysis of Individual Heterogeneity and Discriminatory Accuracy (MAIHDA) to examine how multidimensional sleep health relates to all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.
METHODS: The analytic sample included 4340 adults for all‑cause mortality and 3790 for cardiovascular mortality from the Sleep Heart Health Study. Six sleep dimensions were dichotomized into healthy versus unhealthy categories and combined to form 64 unique strata representing all possible sleep health profiles. Individuals were nested within strata in multilevel Cox MAIHDA models. Three models were estimated: model 1 (null), model 2 (sleep-domain fixed effects), and model 3 (sleep-domain fixed effects plus covariates).
RESULTS: In null models, sleep‑health strata explained 8.51% of the variance in all‑cause mortality and 15.01% in cardiovascular mortality, indicating meaningful heterogeneity across sleep profiles. After accounting for sleep-domain main effects and covariates, most between‑strata variance was explained (PCV = 99.95% for all-cause mortality and 78.32% for cardiovascular mortality), indicating that mortality risk was predominantly additive rather than driven by unique non‑additive combinations. Healthier continuity and timing were associated with lower all-cause mortality, while timing was the most consistent sleep feature for cardiovascular mortality; absence of sleep disorders showed a weaker association mainly for all-cause mortality. Strata with multiple unhealthy sleep dimensions consistently had the highest marginal standardized predicted 10-year mortality risks.
