CONCLUSIONS: MAIHDA maps mortality risk across multidimensional sleep profiles and quantifies additive versus non-additive effects. Mortality risk was explained primarily by the additive accumulation of sleep-health attributes.

Title: Epicardial adipose tissue volumes improve prediction of myocardial infarction in women on top of SCORE2, CACS and plaque burden: Long-term follow-up of 25,000 individuals.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increased epicardial adipose tissue volume (EATV) is a risk marker for future myocardial infarction (MI), but its value beyond SCORE2 (Systemic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2), the coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and the coronary artery segment involvement score (SIS) remains poorly studied.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the incremental value of EATV normalized to heart volume (EATVh) on top of SCORE2, CACS and SIS in predicting future MI.
METHODS: We studied associations between EATVh, SCORE2, CACS, SIS and the risk of MI in a general population cohort of 25,155 participants (age 50-64, 50.7% women). Sex-stratified multivariable Cox-regression estimated hazard ratios (HR) and ROC-analysis with variables dichotomized at their 75th percentile assessed incremental predictive value.
RESULTS: A total of 304 MI (71 in women) occurred during follow-up (median: 7.8 years). In adjusted analysis, EATVh and SCORE2 were independently associated with MI in women, but only SIS and SCORE2 in men. The highest HR per EATVh IQR was found in women <55 years (1.89). ROC-analysis showed that adding EATVh to SCORE2, CACS and SIS improved MI prediction in women but not men (AUC: 0.681 vs. 0.667; p < 0.05 for both).
CONCLUSIONS: EATVh provides independent, modest incremental information on the risk of future MI in women on top of CACS and SIS, but not in men. Further studies in more diverse population segments including younger and symptomatic individuals are warranted.

Title: Peripheral Nerve Blocks for Postoperative Pain Management in Cardiothoracic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness, comparative effectiveness, and safety of peripheral nerve blocks for postoperative pain management after cardiothoracic surgery.
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, with strength of evidence rated using the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality methodology (PROSPERO CRD42024549561).
SETTING: Perioperative care settings in studies published between 2013 and 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing open or minimally invasive cardiothoracic surgery.
INTERVENTIONS: Peripheral nerve blocks, including chest wall blocks and erector spinae plane blocks, compared with sham, no block, local infiltration, or neuraxial techniques.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 104 randomized controlled trials were included. Chest wall blocks reduced 24-hour pain scores and opioid consumption compared with sham or no block in both open cardiac and minimally invasive thoracic surgery. Erector spinae plane blocks demonstrated similar effects, with no clinically meaningful differences compared with chest wall blocks. Peripheral nerve blocks provided analgesia comparable to neuraxial techniques across several outcomes. Reported adverse events were rare and inconsistently defined.
CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral nerve blocks provide some reductions in postoperative pain and opioid use after cardiothoracic surgery and appear to have a favorable safety profile. Chest wall blocks and erector spinae plane blocks were found not to differ in effectiveness, and both offer analgesia comparable to neuraxial techniques.

Title: Recovery of worsening renal function after acute heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Worsening renal function (WRF) is common during hospitalization for acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). However, the post-discharge trajectory of renal function in these patients remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the rate of WRF recovery after discharge and its prognostic significance.
METHODS: In a cohort of 2020 patients hospitalized for ADHF (TRI-AHF registry), serum creatinine was measured at admission, daily during hospitalization, and at 12 months after discharge. WRF was defined as a creatinine increase ≥0.3 mg/dL. Only patients who developed WRF during the index hospitalization were included. At the 12-month follow-up, WRF was classified as recovered if the change in creatinine from admission was <0.3 mg/dL, and persistent if ≥0.3 mg/dL. The primary endpoint was 5-year all-cause mortality after the 12-month creatinine reassessment.
RESULTS: During the study period, 331 patients (16%) experienced WRF. At 12 months, 157 (54%) had recovered WRF and 133 (46%) had persistent WRF. Older age, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and right ventricular dysfunction during hospitalization were independent predictors of persistent WRF. At 5-year follow-up after the 12-month assessment, recovered WRF was strongly associated with a lower risk of mortality compared with persistent WRF (adjusted HR=0.229, p < 0.001). The association between WRF recovery and improved survival was independent of prior chronic kidney disease and baseline creatinine, and appeared more pronounced in males than in females (p-int=0.034).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalized for ADHF who experienced WRF, 54% recovered renal function at 12 months. Recovery of WRF was associated with significantly better long-term survival compared with persistent WRF.

Title: Prevalence of Atrial Cardiopathy Biomarkers Across Ischemic Stroke Subtypes.
Journal: Journal of Nippon Medical School = Nippon Ika Daigaku zasshi
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial cardiopathy (AC) has been proposed as a potential embolic mechanism in embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS); however, the distribution of AC biomarkers across ischemic stroke subtypes remains unclear.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 533 consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke. Stroke subtypes were classified as small-vessel occlusion (SVO), branch atheromatous disease (BAD), large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA), ESUS, or cardioembolism (CE). AC was defined according to ARCADIA trial criteria as the presence of at least one of the following: P-wave terminal force in lead V1 (PTFV1) >5,000 μV·ms, N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) >250 pg/mL, or left atrial diameter index (LADI) ≥3 cm/m2. We evaluated the prevalence and overlap of these biomarkers across subtypes.
RESULTS: AC biomarkers were significantly more frequent in CE than in other subtypes. Using ≥1 biomarker, AC prevalence was 43% in SVO, 49% in BAD, 53% in LAA, 54% in ESUS, and 97% in CE. With ≥2 biomarkers, prevalence decreased to 8%, 7%, 13%, 19%, and 78%, respectively. NT-proBNP elevation was the most common biomarker across all groups. Left atrial enlargement was rare in non-CE subtypes (~5%) and showed no overlap with PTFV1 in SVO, BAD, or LAA.
CONCLUSIONS: While AC defined by ARCADIA criteria is highly prevalent in CE, it is also widely observed across other stroke subtypes. Refinement of AC definitions, including stricter thresholds and/or biomarker combinations, may better identify atrial dysfunction with causal relevance to stroke.

Title: Underlying Plaque Type and Neoatherosclerosis After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Substudy of the CONNECT Trial.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching. At the frame level, we compared post-procedural OCT findings in NALS to 2 comparators: non-NA-leading lesions (lesions without neoatherosclerosis); and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions. Of 144 lesions with serial OCT, neoatherosclerosis occurred in 17 (11.8%). In NA-leading segments, compared to non-NA-leading lesions and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions, the proportion of frames with lipid-rich plaque was higher (71% vs. 54% [odds ratio (OR) 2.72; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.23-6.01] and 58% [OR 2.62; 95% CI 0.99-6.96], respectively). Similarly, the mean (±SD) in-stent atherothrombotic material area was larger in NA-leading segments (0.41±0.39 vs. 0.24±0.31 [geometric mean ratio (GMR) 2.00; 95% CI 1.21-3.29] and 0.16±0.16 mm2[GMR 2.33; 95% CI 1.26-4.31], respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Underlying lipid-rich plaque and a higher burden of in-stent atherothrombotic material were associated with neoatherosclerosis at 3 years in STEMI patients, indicating that plaque composition at the time of DES implantation may critically influence neoatherosclerosis formation.

Title: Trough Rivaroxaban Plasma Concentrations and Early Thrombus Regression in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: A Sub-analysis of the SAKURA-PE/DVT REGISTRY.
Abstract: Objectives　To evaluate the association between trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations and early thrombus regression in patients with acute pulmonary embolism (PE).Methods　This study was a sub-analysis of the multicenter, prospective SAKURA PE/DVT REGISTRY. The thrombus regression rate was calculated using contrast-enhanced computed tomography performed at diagnosis and approximately two weeks after treatment initiation. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were measured using a chromogenic anti-factor Xa assay. Correlations between plasma concentrations, thrombus regression rates, and coagulation parameters were analyzed.Patients　Among 153 patients with acute PE treated with direct oral anticoagulants, 106 received rivaroxaban, and trough plasma concentrations were measured in 51 patients.Results　The median trough rivaroxaban plasma concentration was 120.0 (55.6-186.0) ng/mL, with substantial interindividual variability. Trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were positively correlated with the thrombus regression rate in all patients (ρ = 0.33, P = 0.018) and in the intensive therapy group (ρ = 0.41, P = 0.009). In the multivariable analysis, log-transformed rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were independently associated with the thrombus regression rate in the intensive therapy group (β = 9.79, 95% confidence interval 0.72-18.86; P = 0.035). Prothrombin time was strongly correlated with rivaroxaban plasma concentration (ρ = 0.85, P < 0.001). Plasma concentrations tended to increase with age and showed greater variability in elderly patients.Conclusion　Higher trough rivaroxaban plasma concentrations were associated with greater early thrombus regression in patients with acute PE. Prothrombin time may be a practical surrogate for rivaroxaban exposure and may support individualized anticoagulation strategies in selected patients.

Title: Digital health interventions and their effects on health beliefs and self-efficacy in adults with chronic conditions: a systematic review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review examined the impact of digital health interventions on health beliefs and self-efficacy among adults living with chronic conditions.
METHODS: Eight randomised controlled trials and one mixed-methods study involving adults aged 18 years or older with chronic conditions were included if they evaluated a digital health intervention and reported outcomes related to health beliefs and/or self-efficacy. PubMed, Embase and CINAHL were searched from database inception to 29 August 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.
RESULTS: Nine studies were included comprising over 1500 adults with conditions including diabetes, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and obesity. Most included studies reported improvements in self-efficacy following digital health interventions. Only two studies explicitly assessed health beliefs, both demonstrating favourable effects when interventions were theory informed. All randomised trials were rated as having a high risk of bias, primarily due to reliance on self-reported outcomes and lack of blinding.
DISCUSSION: Digital health may support self-efficacy and to a lesser extent health beliefs in adults with chronic conditions, particularly when grounded in behavioural theory and supported by clinician engagement. However, methodological limitations and the under-representation of health belief outcomes restrict the strength of conclusions.
CONCLUSION: This review highlights that digital health interventions have the potential to improve self-efficacy and health beliefs when they are grounded in behavioural theory, personalised to users’ needs and culturally responsive. However, the certainty of these findings is limited by the consistently high risk of bias across the included studies.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251031784.

Title: Estimated glucose disposal rate and mortality in patients with cardiovascular disease: findings from two large cohorts.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Insulin resistance contributes to adverse cardiovascular outcomes but conventional assessments are complex and not routinely available. The estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR), a simple surrogate of insulin resistance, may provide prognostic information in patients with established CVD.
METHODS: Adults with CVD were identified from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) (n=4283) as the primary cohort and from a predefined UK Biobank (UKB) subcohort (n=31 460) as the replication cohort. Cox models, restricted cubic splines, Kaplan-Meier curves and subgroup analyses were used to evaluate associations between eGDR and mortality.
RESULTS: During median follow-ups of 7.8 and 14.2 years, 1886 and 2218 deaths occurred in NHANES and the UKB, including 634 and 616 cardiovascular deaths, respectively. In fully adjusted models, higher continuous eGDR was associated with lower all-cause mortality in NHANES (HR, 0.859; 95% CI 0.800 to 0.923; p<0.001) and the UKB (HR, 0.792; 95% CI 0.743 to 0.844; p<0.001). Similar associations were observed for cardiovascular mortality in NHANES (HR, 0.844; 95% CI 0.736 to 0.969; p=0.016) and the UKB (HR, 0.737; 95% CI 0.656 to 0.828; p<0.001). Spline analyses showed non-linear inverse associations with both mortality outcomes in NHANES. In the UKB, the association with all-cause mortality became non-linear after multivariable adjustment, whereas the association with cardiovascular mortality was approximately linear.
CONCLUSION: Higher eGDR was independently associated with lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with CVD, supporting its potential as a simple marker for mortality risk stratification.

Title: Seasonal variation in cardiovascular mortality and hospitalisations and its implications for public health planning: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We characterised seasonal patterns in cardiovascular (CV) mortality and hospitalisations to understand how CV health might be affected by climate change.
METHODS: We analysed the UK Biobank cohort recruited from 22 centres between 2006 and 2010. Seasonal mortality rates and hospitalisation rates were determined for death (all cause, CV and non-CV death) and first recorded of CV hospitalisations (heart failure (HF), myocardial infarction (MI), stroke and peripheral vascular disease (PVD)). Seasonal trends were evaluated using a cosinor model with a binomial family and by sex, age, ethnicity and socioeconomic deprivation. Multivariable models were adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle and clinical covariates, and assessment centre was subsequently included as a random intercept to account for clustering within centres.
RESULTS: Data from 453 597 participants were included, 56% were women, with a mean age of 56 years (SD 8). There were 33 857 deaths (10 807 (31.9%) were CV and 23 050 (68.1%) non-CV deaths). All-cause mortality showed evidence of seasonal variation, and CV and non-CV deaths had significant seasonal variation (p<0.001), with the highest rates in winter. The maximum and minimum of all-cause mortality rates were 62.2 and 51.5 per 10 000 person-years in winter and summer respectively. There were 12 273, 9520, 7137, 14 492 hospitalisations for HF, MI, stroke and PVD. MI and stroke showed clear winter peaks (p<0.001), HF and PVD also displayed seasonal variation (p<0.001) with the highest hospitalisation rate in spring.
CONCLUSIONS: Rates of deaths, MI and stroke hospitalisations were highest during winter months. The findings imply that colder temperatures rather than warmer temperatures are a more significant driver of adverse outcomes.

Title: Tirzepatide Use Resulted in Clinically Meaningful Weight Reduction in Individuals With Obesity or Overweight: 12-Month Real-World Results.
Abstract:
AIMS: This study assessed the real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in commercially insured individuals without diabetes, eligible for obesity medications (OMs), including glucagon like-peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA)-naïve individuals (i.e., no GLP-1 RA prescription during the 12-month pre-index period) and GLP-1 RA-experienced individuals.
METHODS: This retrospective, observational cohort study used Optum's de-identified Market Clarity Data (Optum Market Clarity). Adults with ≥ 1 prescription claim for tirzepatide between November 2023 and March 2024, with continuous medical/pharmacy enrollment for ≥ 12 months pre-index and post-index and available pre- and post-index data were included. Baseline demographics, clinical characteristics, and treatment effectiveness (change from baseline in weight, body mass index, and cardiometabolic risk factors) were assessed among OM-eligible individuals who were persistent on tirzepatide for ≥ 12 months.
RESULTS: The GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced cohorts included 230 individuals (mean age: 49.5 years, 72.2% female) and 123 individuals (mean age: 48.9 years, 81.3% female), respectively, who were persistent on tirzepatide for 12 months with documented pre- and post-index weight measurements. At baseline, more than 85% of individuals in each cohort had ≥ 1 obesity-related complication, most commonly dyslipidemia, hypertension, and prediabetes. At 12 months post-index, the GLP-1 RA-naïve cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 19.3%, while the GLP-1 RA-experienced cohort achieved a mean weight reduction of 13.1%.
CONCLUSIONS: After 12 months of persistent tirzepatide use, individuals experienced clinically meaningful weight reduction, comparable to outcomes reported in clinical trials. These real-world findings were observed both in GLP-1 RA-naïve and experienced individuals.

Title: Harnessing Clinical Characteristics to Identify High-Risk of Drug-induced QTc Prolongation in Hospitalized Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-induced QTc-prolongation is a major concern for developing ventricular arrhythmias, which may eventually lead to sudden cardiac death. Identifying high-risk patients is essential to support healthcare providers in handling automatically generated alerts in clinical practice. The aim of study was to develop clinical data-driven machine learning methods to predict drug-induced QTc-prolongation.
METHODS: Inpatients with paired electrocardiograms were enrolled from Southwest Hospital (2015-2022). Six machine learning (ML) algorithms were developed to predict drug-induced QTc prolongation (ΔQTc > 60 ms). Model performance was evaluated using an internal test set and an independent external validation cohort. Model interpretations were recognized by feature importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) methods. Finally, we benchmarked the ML models against the traditional Tisdale risk score.
RESULTS: A total of 2451 participants were recruited, of whom 292 developed QTc-prolongation, while 150 patients from a separate center served as the external validation cohort. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model achieved the best performance with recall of 0.884 and AUC of 0.814 in internal test set. During external validation, the AUC remained robust at 0.864, although recall declined to 0.650. SHAP analysis identified baseline QTc and QT intervals, inflammation, high-risk drugs, and hypertension are the primary drivers of model predictions.
CONCLUSIONS: The XGBoost algorithm provides a highly sensitive framework for predicting drug-induced QTc prolongation. Integrating this ML tool with identified clinical drivers into hospital decision support systems would facilitate the optimization of treatment strategies and early ECG monitoring strategies.

Title: Towards a digital twin for precision diabetes care: a phenotypic mapping and virtual representation of a person living with type 1 diabetes in the SFDT1 study.
Abstract: T1D is clinically heterogeneous, yet its key parameters are still largely interpreted in isolation. As a first step towards developing a digital twin for T1D, we aimed to build a phenotypic mapping and virtual representation of a person living with T1D (PwT1D) usable at the individual level. We analysed baseline data from 2187 adults with T1D in the SFDT1 cohort using Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). Twenty-five sociodemographic, clinical, biochemical, and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) variables were used to construct a low-dimensional structure. Structural reproducibility and individual projection were assessed in an unseen set of 235 participants. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) risks were computed with the Steno T1 Risk Engine. We identified seven interpretable phenotypes, ranging from well-controlled profiles to profiles characterized by poor glycaemic control, metabolic abnormalities, social vulnerability and a high burden of micro- and macrovascular complications. An independently fitted map for the additional participants showed a similar overall branching structure and comparable clinical patterns, and individual projection was accurate (R² 0.85-0.98). A multilingual application enables exploration of the phenotypic map, individual projection, and estimation of Steno risk scores. This phenotypic mapping and virtual representation capture clinically meaningful heterogeneity and let care teams locate and explore individual profiles. It provides the foundation for an AI-enabled digital twin an interpretable virtual representation that integrates a person's clinical, biological, glycaemic, and social profile and supports individualized decisions - and a practical clinical decision-support tool for precision diabetes care.

Title: P2X7 receptor-mediated inflammatory and ionic remodeling promotes atrial fibrillation in diabetes.
Abstract:
AIMS: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet the mechanisms by which diabetic metabolic stress promotes atrial arrhythmogenesis remain incompletely understood. Recent evidence suggests that purinergic signaling-driven sterile inflammation plays an important role in cardiac remodeling. This study aimed to investigate the role of the ATP-gated purinergic P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) in DM-associated AF and to explore its underlying mechanisms.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Rats were randomly assigned to four groups: control (Con), diabetes mellitus (DM), P2X7R overexpression in controls (Con+P2X7), and P2X7R knockdown in diabetic rats (DM + P2X7 KD), with gene manipulation achieved using AAV9-cTnT vectors. AF susceptibility, atrial structural and electrical remodeling were systematically evaluated using electrophysiological studies, optical mapping, patch-clamp recordings, and molecular analyses. DM markedly increased AF inducibility and duration, accompanied by enhanced sympathetic nerve activity and activation of P2X7R-related inflammatory signaling. Compared with controls, DM atria exhibited pronounced interstitial fibrosis, connexin remodeling, delayed atrial activation, slowed conduction velocity, and increased conduction heterogeneity. Atrial P2X7R overexpression in control rats recapitulated key arrhythmogenic features, whereas P2X7R KD in diabetic rats significantly attenuated atrial remodeling and reduced AF susceptibility, without altering the diabetes-induced increase in sympathetic activity. At the cellular level, P2X7R selectively modulated INa, ICa,L, and IKur while relatively preserving Ito, and was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and disturbed Ca2+ homeostasis, characterized by increased mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, increased cytosolic Ca2+ signals, and reduced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake.
CONCLUSION: P2X7R-mediated inflammatory and mitochondrial signaling contribute to diabetic atrial remodeling and AF susceptibility. Targeting P2X7R may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for preventing AF in diabetes.

Title: Procedure-specific bleeding risk assessment: a multidisciplinary expert consensus companion to the 2026 periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprocedural anticoagulant management requires balancing thrombotic risk against procedure-specific bleeding risk. Existing procedure bleeding risk classifications are fragmented across specialties, inconsistent in methodology, and rarely extend beyond a few procedural domains, limiting their clinical applicability.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a comprehensive, standardized, procedure-specific bleeding risk classification to accompany the 2026 GIHP-SFAR periprocedural anticoagulant management guidelines.
METHODS: A formal multidisciplinary consensus was conducted under the auspices of GIHP and SFAR, in collaboration with 24 surgical and interventional specialty societies. For each procedural domain, a working group performed a systematic literature review. Procedures were classified into four tiers: no bleeding risk, low bleeding risk, high bleeding risk, and very high bleeding risk. A specific category was created for procedures carrying particular contextual risk (e.g., anatomical site, patient factors, or need for reversible anticoagulation). Consensus was reached by the full expert panel.
RESULTS: Twenty-four procedural domains were classified, ranging from regional anaesthesia and digestive endoscopy to cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, and ophthalmology. Each domain provides a procedure-specific bleeding risk table, with narrative supporting evidence. Procedures warranting delayed resumption of anticoagulation (≥72 hours) or use of short-acting/reversible anticoagulants are identified. The classification covers common and complex surgical scenarios, including those with limited published evidence where structured expert opinion was applied.
CONCLUSION: This companion document provides clinicians with a standardized, evidence-based, procedure-specific bleeding risk framework across 24 domains to support individualized periprocedural anticoagulant decisions in daily practice.

Title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults With Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: A NHANES Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90. A NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up ten steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment.
RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (OR 1.748, 95% CI 1.218-2.510; P=0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P=0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P=0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P=0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability.
CONCLUSIONS: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.

Title: Common Femoral Atherectomy yields safe results and low morbidity in the outpatient setting.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy is considered the gold standard for the treatment of CFA disease. Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted. This study aimed to describe our experience expanding the use of atherectomy in the outpatient setting for the treatment of CFA disease.
METHODS: This is a single-institution, retrospective review of 49 CFA atherectomy procedures performed from January 2017 to November 2022 at Trinity Health Ann Arbor. Primary outcomes included primary patency at 1 year and MALE-free survival. Secondary outcomes involved changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI), toe pressures, and morbidity at 90 days.
RESULTS: 49 CFA atherectomies were performed on 45 patients (73 yo ± 7 years), 45% with claudication and 55% with critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). TASC classification of the treated lesions was TASC A in 4%, TASC B in 29%, TASC C in 61%, and TASC D in 6%. Three patients also underwent superficial femoral artery (SFA) stenting; one had concomitant CFA stenting, and 24 (49%) underwent treatment distal to the CFA atherectomy site. We encountered three complications: one readmission for dehydration, one postoperative hematoma, and one focal SFA dissection requiring delayed secondary stent placement. There were no deaths within 90 days. Post-procedure, the average ABI increased from 0.59 to 0.80 (P<0.01), and toe pressure rose from 42 to 68 (P<0.01). Thirty-five cases had follow-up of at least one year, showing a primary patency rate of 86% and a 94% MALE-free at one year. Additionally, 71% reported symptom improvement or wound healing at their last follow-up.
CONCLUSION: When open surgery may be medically prohibited, CFA atherectomy combined with balloon angioplasty can be performed safely, yielding good clinical outcomes as a standalone procedure or with additional infrainguinal interventions. When applied in appropriate clinical and radiologic circumstances, patients experience favorable outcomes with low procedural morbidity. Due to its clinical benefits and low risk, this procedure can be a valuable addition to the modern vascular surgeon's treatment armamentarium.

Title: Acute Upper Limb Ischaemia: A 5-Year Prospective Single-Centre Experience from Northern Morocco.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute upper limb ischaemia (AULI) is an uncommon vascular emergency associated with a risk of limb loss and functional impairment. Contemporary data from North Africa remain scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, aetiological factors, management strategies, and outcomes of patients presenting with AULI in a tertiary vascular centre in Northern Morocco.
METHODS: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted including consecutive patients treated for acute non-traumatic upper limb ischaemia between January 2021 and May 2026. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, clinical presentation, imaging findings, aetiology, treatment strategies, and outcomes were prospectively recorded. The primary outcome was limb loss. Secondary outcomes included clinical improvement, reintervention, and mortality. All outcomes were assessed during the index hospitalisation and up to one month after discharge.
RESULTS: Forty-three patients were included (mean age 59.8 +/- 13.2 years; 76.7% women). Delayed presentation was common, with 53.5% of patients presenting more than 24 hours after symptom onset and 39.6% presenting after more than 72 hours. Rutherford class IIb and III ischaemia accounted for 41.9% and 11.6% of cases, respectively. Cardioembolic disease was the leading aetiology (34.9%), while cancer-associated thrombosis and thrombophilic or inflammatory disorders were important non-cardioembolic causes. The brachial artery was the most frequently involved vessel (74.4%). Thromboembolectomy was performed in 72.1% of patients. Clinical improvement was achieved in 81.4% of cases. Secondary intervention was required in 7.0%. Overall limb loss occurred in four patients (9.3%), and one patient died (2.3%). Rutherford III ischaemia was significantly associated with limb loss.
CONCLUSION: AULI in Northern Morocco is characterised by delayed presentation, advanced ischaemic severity, and a substantial burden of cancer-associated and thrombophilic disorders. Despite these challenges, surgical thromboembolectomy achieved satisfactory limb-salvage and functional outcomes. Early recognition and prompt referral remain essential to prevent irreversible ischaemic injury.

Title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD).
METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.
RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs 6.6% vs 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend= 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short- and long-term outcomes.

Title: Guideline-to-Practice Gap in Ankle-Brachial Index Screening Among Inpatients with Newly Documented Lower Extremity Wounds.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to two hospitals within a single urban academic health system in 2025 with a new lower extremity wound documented in nursing wound flowsheets. Recent screening was defined as ABI testing performed during the index hospitalization or within one year prior to admission. Patient and admission characteristics were compared by screening status, and logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with screening. Wound location and noninvasive vascular testing results were summarized descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 2244 inpatients with newly documented lower extremity wounds, 343 patients (15.3%) were screened with ABIs. Screened patients were younger (65 vs 69 years; P<.001) and had a higher burden of atherosclerotic or diabetic comorbidities. After multivariable adjustment, pre-existing PAD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.79; P<.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR, 2.72; P<.001), and end-stage renal disease (aOR, 1.60; P=.021) were independently associated with ABI screening. Female sex was associated with lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.73; P=.045). Compared with medicine or hospitalist services, admission to general surgery/acute care surgery (aOR, 2.15; P=.002) and vascular surgery (aOR, 4.29; P<.001) was associated with higher odds of screening. Screening proportions were 23.6% for toe wounds, 20.6% for ankle/Achilles wounds, 19.9% for foot/heel wounds, and 12.8% for lower leg wounds. Among screened patients with available measurements, 50.4% had an abnormal ABI, 63.8% had an abnormal TBI, and 69.0% had at least one abnormal ABI or TBI.
CONCLUSION: PAD screening was performed in a minority of hospitalized patients with newly documented lower extremity wounds and was associated with recognized vascular risk factors and admitting service. Abnormal physiologic testing was common among screened patients. Standardized wound-triggered screening pathways may reduce missed opportunities for vascular evaluation.

Title: Long-term Outcomes of Primary Femoropopliteal Stents: A Retrospective Multi-Centre Experience and the Role for a Doppler Ultrasound Surveillance Programme.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularisation is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating re-intervention, remains a challenge. This study performs a retrospective outcomes analysis to suggest which patient populations may benefit from a Doppler ultrasound (DUS) surveillance programme in improving primary patency and amputation-free survival following femoropopliteal stenting in patients with PAD.
METHODS: A multicentre, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients who underwent femoropopliteal stenting between January 2015 and April 2023 within a vascular network with six hospital sites. Data were collected from 238 stents in 220 patients. Demographics, stent characteristics, and surveillance protocols were analysed. Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models were used to identify risk factors for primary patency and amputation-free survival. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated for both outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to compare outcomes between supra-popliteal and infra-popliteal stents.
RESULTS: A total of 238 stents were inserted in a population comprised of 28.6% females, with the median age of 72.5 +/- 11.5 years. In 74.8% (178) of cases, patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Primary patency rates at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years were 90%, 67.7%, 51.2%, 26.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. The average amputation-free survival was 3.2 years. Cox regression identified CLTI (hazard ratio, 6.37, p = .001), type 1 diabetes mellitus (hazard ratio, 3.16, p = .006), and female sex (hazard ratio, 1.69, P = .037) as significant predictors of loss of primary patency. Drug-eluting stents and diabetes were associated with poorer amputation-free survival.
CONCLUSIONS: The study illustrates a cohort of high-risk patients, particularly those with CLTI and diabetes, who may benefit from future enrolment in an enhanced DUS surveillance programme targeted to improve long-term outcomes. However, further research is required to explore the clinical-effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and implementation feasibility of such programmes in clinical practice.

Title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: An Arterial-Wall Dimension Uncharacterized in Current Limb Staging.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on haemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging.
METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS).
RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis. An elevated ankle-brachial index is uninterpretable, and a reference-range value does not exclude peripheral artery disease. Across cohorts of differing design and definition, MAC has been consistently associated with major amputation, delayed wound healing and mortality, in line with a systematic review of 51 calcification-scoring studies; the five-point pedal score has been externally validated, and associations persisted after adjustment for WIfI stage. Model comparison in one cohort suggests incremental information, but discrimination, calibration and reclassification beyond established staging have not been reported. Neither WIfI nor GLASS characterizes arterial-wall phenotype.
CONCLUSIONS: The consistency and reproducibility of the prognostic evidence justify formal consideration of MAC in forthcoming revisions of limb-staging systems and guidelines. Incremental-value analyses should accompany that evaluation and inform the form of any modifier rather than delay it. One concrete route is to use MAC as a qualifier of the reliability of the WIfI ischaemia grade in the individual limb.

Title: Impact of Skin Color on the Clinical Diagnosis and Outcomes of Acute Limb Ischemia.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a time-sensitive vascular emergency with high rates of mortality and major limb amputation. Diagnosis relies on clinical signs, including pallor, which may be less apparent in patients with darker skin tones due to limited representation of ethnic skin variations in medical literature. This study investigates the influence of skin pigmentation on the clinical recognition, severity at presentation, and outcomes of ALI.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in adult patients diagnosed with ALI between 2022 and December 2025. Patient demographics, comorbidities, surgical intervention, and outcomes were collected. Skin pigmentation was categorized using the Fitzpatrick skin scale (I-VI) in the initial evaluation. The primary outcome was severity of initial ALI presentation, which was measured using the Rutherford classification. Secondary outcomes, such as time to intervention, surgical interventions, amputation-free survival, in-hospital mortality and length of stay were also collected. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models were used to evaluate independent associations.
RESULTS: Among 231 patients with ALI, higher Fitzpatrick skin types (V-VI), were significantly associated with more severe ischemic changes at presentation (p=0.014) and longer symptom-to-admission times (p=0.05). Longer utilization of thrombolytic therapy was observed in patients with darker skin tones (p<0.001) and Rutherford classification severity was strongly associated with major amputation rates (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Skin pigmentation may impact timely diagnosis and management outcomes of ALI. Improved clinical education and literature that reflect diverse skin tones are essential for equitable vascular care.

Title: A Scoping Review on Artificial Intelligence for Image-Based Analysis in Aortic Aneurysm Care.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance automated image analysis, quantitative assessment, and clinical decision-making in aortic aneurysm care. This scoping review aims to summarize the current cumulative body of evidence.
METHODS: A systematic PubMed search identified 661 records, with 59 studies ultimately included after de-duplication and multi-stage screening based on predefined eligibility criteria, focusing on original research applying artificial intelligence to medical imaging in aortic aneurysm care. Data were extracted on study design, imaging modality, AI methodology, validation, and dataset characteristics.
RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Deep learning approaches, particularly U-Net-based architectures, were the most frequently applied methods, with AI primarily used for automated segmentation and quantitative analysis of aortic pathology. AI models achieved high technical performance across applications, including vessel segmentation, aneurysm detection, endoleak identification, and risk prediction, with reported improvements in efficiency and diagnostic accuracy. However, external validation, multimodal data integration, and prospective clinical evaluation remained uncommon.
CONCLUSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential to enhance aortic aneurysm disease assessment through accurate image analysis, automated quantification, and improved procedural support. However, current limitations include lack of external validation, reporting transparency, and clinical integration.

Title: Impact of Angiographic Lesion Distribution on Walking Therapy Outcomes in Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
Abstract:
AIM: To investigate whether angiographic lesion distribution and disease severity influence outcomes of walking therapy in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) and intermittent claudication (IC).
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients with IC participated in a 12-week hybrid progressive walking program consisting of one supervised treadmill session and two home-based walking sessions per week. Baseline evaluation included assessment of ankle-brachial index (ABI), angiographic imaging (CTA or MRA), and functional exercise testing. Pain-free walking distance (PFWD) and maximal walking distance (MWD) were assessed using standardized treadmill protocols. Angiographic lesion distribution was classified according to lesion location, while disease severity was graded using the ANGIO score.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients (mean age 69.1 ± 9.4 years, 75.8% male) with available angiographic imaging were included in the present analysis. After three months, PFWD increased from 173 m to 304 m, an increase of 131 m (p < 0.001), and MWD increased from 448 m to 627 m, an increase of 179 m (p < 0.001). Lesion distribution was not significantly associated with changes in PFWD (p = 0.059), and no statistically significant differences were observed for MWD (p = 0.44). Disease severity, expressed by the ANGIO score, was not correlated with walking improvements (ρ = -0.10, p = 0.57 for PFWD; ρ = 0.10, p = 0.56 for MWD).
CONCLUSION: Walking therapy significantly improved walking capacity in patients with LEAD. In this exploratory cohort, no statistically significant associations were observed between angiographic lesion distribution or disease severity and improvements in walking distance. However, the small overall sample size and limited number of patients within several lesion distribution groups preclude firm conclusions regarding the influence of lesion characteristics on treatment response. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in larger studies.

Title: One-Year Sac Regression After Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated With Favorable Outcomes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after EVAR indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression.
METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent non-ruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5mm), stable sac (<5mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5mm). The primary outcome was late re-intervention, including endovascular re-intervention and open conversion.
RESULTS: A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow-up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late re-intervention compared to sac regression (HR, 2.335; 95% CI, 1.048 - 5.191; P=0.047). However, the rate of late re-intervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383 - 1.258; P=0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak, and 3.2% (4/126) needed open conversions.
CONCLUSION: Late re-intervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.

Title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins After Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors.
RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (IQR, 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap CI, 2.2-3.7; p<0.001). Completion DUS confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; p=0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

Title: Antiplatelet Therapy and Bleeding, Thrombosis, and Aneurysm Growth in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed. Demographics and outcomes were compared by antiplatelet status, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with mortality, MACE, bleeding, and AAA growth.
RESULTS: Among 886 (73% male) patients studied, 511 (57.7%) were prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Those prescribed antiplatelet therapy had higher rates of atherosclerotic disease than those not on antiplatelets. Patients not prescribed antiplatelet therapy were more likely to be female, have atrial fibrillation, and be prescribed anticoagulation. At a mean follow-up of 1.8 years, there were no differences in bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism events, or growth rate associated with antiplatelet prescription. Adjusted analyses showed statins (HR=0.73, p=0.02), but not antiplatelets or anticoagulants, were associated with reduced risk of mortality. Diabetes was associated with decreased AAA growth rate, while larger initial diameter was associated with increased growth rate as well as mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AAA, antiplatelet therapy was not observed to be associated with an increase in bleeding risk, but was also not associated with decreased mortality, thrombosis, or aneurysm growth. Statins were observed to be associated with reduced mortality. Aneurysmal growth rate was not associated with any medical therapies studied, including statins, and was only influenced by the presence of diabetes.

Title: Roles of one-carbon metabolism, folate and riboflavin in blood pressure: Can a precision nutrition approach reduce the risk of hypertension?
Abstract: Folate, along with the metabolically-related B vitamins (B12, B6 and riboflavin), play essential roles in human health throughout life. Notably, recent UK Biobank evidence implicates folate deficiency in hypertension, the major risk factor contributing to mortality worldwide. An estimated 15% of pregnancies are affected by hypertension, which contributes to serious adverse maternal and offspring outcomes, a greater risk of stroke later in life in the mother and long-term disease risk in the child. Clinical and genome-wide association studies link the C677T polymorphism in the gene encoding the folate-metabolizing enzyme methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) with an increased risk of hypertension. Riboflavin (as flavin adenine dinucleotide; FAD) is required as a cofactor for MTHFR, and randomized trials show that intervention with riboflavin lowers blood pressure, specifically in individuals with the MTHFR 677TT genotype, independently of antihypertensive medications. The health implications of this gene-nutrient interaction are important, especially for populations worldwide with the highest frequencies of the variant TT genotype in MTHFR, including Guatemala (up to 66%), Mexico (32-44%), and Northern China (24%). Further investigation is required to elucidate the mechanisms linking folate-mediated one-carbon metabolism with blood pressure and how riboflavin alleviates the excess genetic risk of hypertension in affected individuals. Riboflavin deficiency is highly prevalent worldwide, particularly in women, but is typically overlooked in health and research settings. This review highlights the roles of folate and riboflavin in blood pressure and the opportunity for a precision nutrition approach to reduce hypertension in at-risk individuals by addressing riboflavin deficiency and thus optimizing folate metabolism.

Title: Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry. 35th official report of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (1990-2025).
Abstract: Introduction and objectives This report presents the 2025 activity of the Interventional Cardiology Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (ACI-SEC). Methods All interventional cardiology laboratories in Spain were invited to complete an online survey. Data were analyzed by an external company and subsequently reviewed and presented by the ACI-SEC board. Results A total of 125 hospitals participated, compared with 118 in the previous year. The number of diagnostic procedures and coronary angiograms increased by 4% and 4.5%, respectively, both reaching record highs. Percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) increased by 3.3%. The trend toward lower relative stent use was confirmed, with a marked increase in the use of drug-coated balloons, both as a standalone strategy and as part of hybrid strategies. The use of intracoronary imaging and coronary physiology techniques increased, reaching record absolute numbers. Interventional treatment of myocardial infarction increased by 3.6%, with primary PCI accounting for 98% of procedures. Structural heart interventions continued to expand: transcatheter aortic valve implantation (+10.1%), percutaneous mitral interventions (+25.2%), tricuspid interventions (+7.9%), and left atrial appendage closure (+8.4%). Renal denervation procedures, interventional treatment of acute pulmonary embolism, and interventions for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension increased significantly. Conclusions The 2025 Spanish cardiac catheterization and interventional cardiology registry shows overall growth in both coronary and structural activity. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

Title: Transient immediate systemic side effects following long-acting cabotegravir and rilpivirine injections in people with HIV: a 5-year cohort study.
Journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterise transient immediate systemic side effects (TISSE) following long-acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine (CAB-RPV-LA) injections, estimate their incidence, assess treatment continuation, and investigate associated plasma drug concentrations.
METHODS: This prospective single-centre French cohort included adults with HIV receiving CAB-RPV-LA during 2021-2026. Nurses prospectively documented unexpected systemic symptoms. Treatment discontinuation was compared by TISSE status. Plasma concentrations were measured by LC-MS/MS after TISSE events and compared with post-injection concentrations in 24 matched asymptomatic controls and routine trough measurements.
RESULTS: Among 308 participants receiving 4,644 monitored on-site injection sessions, 24 experienced 28 TISSE episodes: 0.60% per session (exact Poisson 95% CI, 0.40-0.87%). Symptoms occurred during or shortly after injection, predominantly intense lumbar pain (18 episodes) and dyspnea/chest oppression (16), co-occurring in seven. All symptoms resolved within 15 minutes; none required hospitalisation. No difference in treatment discontinuation was detected (2/24 versus 38/284; Fisher's exact test, p=0.75). In all 17 sampled episodes, RPV and/or CAB concentrations were markedly elevated. RPV elevations occurred in 14 episodes, (up to 767-fold the upper concentration bound at trough), and CAB elevations in four, including one involving both drugs.
CONCLUSIONS: TISSE episodes were brief and self-limited but clinically striking, potentially mimicking cardiovascular emergencies. Post-event concentration elevations suggest inadvertent systemic passage, predominantly involving RPV, without establishing causality. Possible CAB involvement remains exploratory. Recognising TISSE is important, and healthcare professionals should be familiar with its clinical presentation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02898987.

Title: Community-engaged protocol for the modified B-SWELL program randomized control pilot trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Midlife Black women experience disproportionately high rates of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Evidence supports the use of culturally tailored interventions and community engagement to reduce health disparities in this population. In response, the Midlife Black Women's Stress Reduction and Wellness program (B-SWELL) was co-developed with midlife Black women to address cardiovascular risks and promote healthier lifestyle behaviors.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to: (1) Refine the B-SWELL program to enhance sustainability, update outcome metrics in alignment with American Heart Association guidelines, and integrate findings from a prior feasibility trial; and (2) Conduct a randomized controlled pilot trial of the modified B-SWELL program to assess trends in primary and secondary outcomes and explore the preferences of midlife Black women participating in clinical research.
METHODS: Program refinements were guided by a community-engaged approach. The randomized controlled pilot trial compares the modified B-SWELL intervention with an attention control condition. Midlife Black women from the community will be recruited for participation. The primary outcome is cardiovascular health; secondary outcomes include depressive symptoms, unhealthy days, sleep quality, perceived general health, and symptom burden.
STUDY PROGRESS: Objectives 1 and 2 have been completed. Although the final sample did not reach the target of 64 participants, five cohorts, each comprised of an intervention group and an attention control group, completed the trial with only 9% attrition.
CONCLUSIONS: The B-SWELL modifications highlight the value of culturally tailored, community-engaged approaches in addressing persistent cardiovascular health disparities among midlife Black women.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov Registration Number: NCT06707636.

Title: Long-term outcomes after angioarchitecture-based endovascular treatment of cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center cohort study from Germany.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Endovascular treatment is an established option for cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), and its efficacy has been demonstrated in single-center and multicenter cohorts. In this study, we critically evaluate our single-center experience with a standardized endovascular treatment strategy, assessing angiographic success, recurrence, safety, and long-term outcomes.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients treated endovascularly for cranial dAVFs from January 2014 to October 2019 at the Institute for Neuroradiology, University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany; direct carotid-cavernous fistulas were excluded. Fistulas were Cognard-classified, cavernous-sinus dAVFs additionally Barrow-classified. Treatment was based on angioarchitecture and accessibility, using transarterial liquid embolization and/or transvenous coils. Outcomes included angiographic success, complications, recurrence/retreatment, and symptom evolution from records, follow-up, and structured telephone interviews; median patient-reported clinical follow-up was 53 months.
RESULTS: Fifty-five patients were included. Cognard I/ IIa/ IIa + b/ IIb/ III/ IV/ V distribution was 6/10/1/13/16/8/1; 39/55 were high-grade. Definite venous/sinus thrombosis was documented in 22. Initial hemorrhage occurred in 9 and was associated with high-risk drainage (8/22 vs 1/33; p=0.0017) and high-grade Cognard lesions (9/39 vs 0/16; p=0.046). Embolization achieved complete occlusion in 49 cases; three additional patients had residual Cognard type I shunting, resulting in angiographic success in 52/55 patients. One recurrence, three clinical complications, and one technical complication occurred. Patient-reported improvement occurred in 46/50; tinnitus improved most, whereas diplopia persisted in 2/6 cases.
CONCLUSION: This single-center study provides a real-world evaluation of our institutional treatment strategy. Our findings support its feasibility, while the small, heterogeneous cohort limits broader conclusions regarding treatment efficacy and durability.

Title: Carotid arterial stiffness and strain after treatment in primary aldosteronism: A prospective follow-up study using speckle-tracking ultrasonography.
Abstract:
AIM: This study investigated vascular alterations in patients with primary aldosteronism (PA), using speckle-tracking carotid strain (STCS) ultrasonography, which allows simultaneous assessment of arterial structure and function. It also aimed to compare arterial stiffness and strain changes over follow-up between surgical and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) treatments.
METHODS: All patients underwent standardized diagnostic work-up for PA. STCS ultrasonography was performed at baseline and 6 months post-treatment. A 5-mm segment of the common carotid artery below the bulb was analyzed to quantify arterial compliance and distensibility (reflecting elasticity); elastic modulus, β-stiffness index and pulse wave velocity (PWV) (reflecting stiffness); and strain-related parameters: displacement, strain and strain rate.
RESULTS: Thirty patients were included. Arterial compliance increased in both transverse and longitudinal planes in the overall cohort (p<0.05). Between-group comparison revealed greater improvement in arterial compliance in the surgical than in the medical group (p=0.033). Arterial distensibility also increased in the transverse plane (p<0.05), whereas no significant changes were observed in β-stiffness index, elastic modulus, PWV, or strain parameters (p>0.05). Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) significantly decreased after treatment in the overall cohort and medical group (p<0.05). Multivariate linear regression identified younger age, shorter hypertension duration, male gender and surgical treatment as independent predictors of greater post-treatment improvement in arterial compliance (p<0.05).
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that STCS may be a feasible tool for assessing treatment-related vascular changes in PA. Arterial compliance improved following treatment, and more particularly after adrenalectomy, while structural stiffness was largely unchanged in this exploratory comparison.

Title: PROlonged posterior PERicardial chest tube treatment to reduce rates of postoperative atrial fibrillation following cardiac surgery (PROPER trial): Rationale and design of a prospective, multinational, randomized clinical trial.
Abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common complication after cardiac surgery and is associated with increased morbidity and prolonged hospitalization. Accumulation of pericardial blood after surgery triggers a localized inflammatory response that has been identified as a contributing factor in POAF development. The PROPER trial (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06800781) is a prospective, multinational, randomized, controlled clinical trial designed to determine whether evacuation of pericardial blood through prolonged drainage using a posterior pericardial chest tube reduces the incidence of POAF following elective cardiac surgery. In addition to routine surveillance, patients will be monitored using a wearable electrocardiographic patch monitor. Patients undergoing non-emergent, first-time coronary bypass grafting, aortic valve replacement, aortic surgery without circulatory arrest, or a combination of these procedures, are randomized 1:1 to either receive intraoperative placement of a posterior pericardial chest tube or standard care. A total of 624 patients will be enrolled across eight Nordic cardiac surgery centers. The primary endpoint is atrial fibrillation (AF) recorded within seven days after surgery. Secondary endpoints include AF recurrence, hospitalization due to bleeding or ischemic stroke, and all-cause mortality. Patients will be followed for five years. If effective, posterior pericardial drainage represents a readily available, low-risk strategy with the potential for rapid and broad adoption in clinical practice.

Title: Rationale for Early Discontinuation of Aspirin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Design of the SOLOTAVI Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trans-aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become the first line treatment of aortic stenosis, a condition predominantly affecting elderly patients. In absence of a specific indication for antithrombotic therapy, lifetime aspirin is recommended after TAVI while it may be discontinued 3 months after bioprosthetic surgical valve replacement. Primary prevention, using aspirin compared to placebo among elderly patients is associated with an increased risk of major bleeding and no reduction rates of thrombotic events. Hence, there is a gap of knowledge on whether aspirin should be continued >3 months after TAVI.
STUDY DESIGN: SOLOTAVI is a multicenter, open label, blinded endpoint assessment, 1:1 randomized, non-inferiority trial comparing aspirin discontinuation 3 months after TAVI (experimental) to long-term therapy (control). Adult patients with successful transfemoral TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis and no indication or contraindication for long-term antithrombotic therapy will be enrolled. Randomization is stratified on center and valve type. The primary endpoint is the 12-month composite of all cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, and non-procedure-related major or disabling bleeding. A hierarchical analysis is performed for the primary and 3 principal secondary endpoints. The sample size is computed for demonstrating the non-inferiority of the experimental strategy compared with the control strategy, with a conservative non-inferiority margin of 6.5%. A total of 1400 patients will be enrolled.
CONCLUSIONS: The SOLOTAVI trial will assess the non-inferiority of a 3-month duration of aspirin compared to the long-term therapy after successful transfemoral TAVI in terms of thrombotic and bleeding events. NCT06518317 clinicaltrials.org.

Title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.
RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.
CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

Title: Echocardiographic atrial and right heart to pulmonary circulation coupling indices identify high-risk patients in moderate aortic stenosis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging evidence points to an increased mortality risk associated to moderate aortic stenosis (AS), yet this population remains insufficiently characterized. We tested the prognostic value of two echocardiographic coupling indices reflecting right and left-sided cardiac function: the ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure (TAPSE/PASP) and the left atrial volumetric/mechanical coupling index (LACI).
METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study including 135 patients with moderate AS. TAPSE/PASP was used as a non-invasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary circulation (RV-Pc) coupling, and LACI was defined as the ratio of left atrial volume index to mitral a' velocity. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to assess the prognostic value of both indices.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 1.61 ± 0.79 years, 33 patients (24%) died. Reduced TAPSE/PASP (< 0.67 mm/mmHg) and elevated LACI (> 5.17) were independently associated with an increased mortality (HR: 3.05 and 3.17, respectively, p < 0.01). These associations remained significant even after adjusting for age. Stratification into three groups - preserved, single, or combined uncoupling -showed progressively lower 1-year survival rates, ranging from 95% to 49% (p < 0.0001). None of the coupling-derived variables was associated with hemodynamic progression or need for aortic valve replacement.
CONCLUSION: TAPSE/PASP and LACI are independently associated with mortality in patients with moderate AS. These parameters may provide incremental prognostic information in this often-overlooked population. These findings may prompt further studies evaluating the potential role of these parameters in helping to refine prognostic phenotyping.

Title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared.
RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002).
CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

Title: Comparing SGLT2 Inhibitors on Incident Major Adverse Kidney Events in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin differ in rates of major adverse kidney events (MAKE) in adults with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk and without stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Using target trial emulation and U.S. claims data from commercial, Medicare Advantage, and traditional Medicare plans, we compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin among adults ≥ 21years with T2D at moderate cardiovascular risk (1-5% annualized MACE or death risk), without insulin use or stage 3+ chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline, initiating treatment from January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2021. Propensity scores estimated via super learner ensemble were incorporated as inverse probability weights into Cox models examining major adverse kidney events (MAKE: stage 3+ CKD, kidney failure, kidney replacement therapy initiation) and all-cause death under intention-to-treat analysis through December 31, 2022.
RESULTS: The weighted cohort included 41,248, 17,548, and 72,638 adults initiating canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and empagliflozin, respectively. One-year post-initiation, rates of MAKE were 3.2% in the dapagliflozin and empagliflozin arms and 3.5% in the canagliflozin arm; by three years, 8.4%, 8.5%, and 9.1%. Compared to canagliflozin, MAKE risk was lower with dapagliflozin (HR 0.91; 95%CI 0.85-0.97) and empagliflozin (HR 0.93; 95%CI 0.88-0.97), with no difference between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin.
CONCLUSION: Empagliflozin and dapagliflozin were associated with modestly lower adverse kidney event rates compared to canagliflozin. These findings provide clinically actionable evidence to support selection of SGLT2i to reduce CKD risk in a highly prevalent subset of people with T2D.

Title: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse.
