Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings.
METHODS: Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks.
RESULTS: A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest.
CONCLUSION: In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

Title: Sex-specific associations between Mediterranean Diet Score and long-term risk of mortality, dementia and other chronic diseases. 20-year evidence from a Swedish population study of 70-year old individuals.
Journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between adherence to the Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS) and the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer, and dementia morbidity over 10- and 20-year follow-up periods in a population-based cohort of older adults.
DESIGN: A prospective population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Gothenburg, Sweden.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1298 participants (56.2% women) aged 70years at baseline from the general population and recruited from the Gothenburg H70 and Population Study of Women in Gothenburg (PSWG) birth cohorts.
MEASUREMENTS: Dietary intake was assessed via face-to-face, semi-structured diet history interviews. The MDS was calculated based on eight food groups (excluding alcohol). Outcomes were identified through linkage with national health and death registers. Cox proportional hazard models were used, adjusting for BMI, smoking, marital status, physical activity, and education.
RESULTS: A higher MDS was associated with a lower risk of 20-year dementia morbidity in men (multivariable-adjusted HR=0.83; 95% CI: 0.71-0.96), but not in women. This association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing, and the sex-by-MDS interaction (p=0.048) was nominally significant, but not robust to multiple testing. No statistically significant associations were found for CVD or cancer morbidity in either sex over the available follow-up (i.e., 10 and 20years, and up to 18years for cancer; 20-year CVD follow-up in men: HR=0.98; 95% CI: 0.88-1.08). For all-cause mortality, an initial association in men at 10years (HR=0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.99) was no longer significant after full adjustment (HR=0.92; 95% CI: 0.84-1.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher MDS levels were associated with lower dementia risk in men, but this finding was not robust to multiple testing correction and requires confirmation in larger studies. No association was found with all-cause mortality, CVD and cancer morbidity. A limitation of these findings is that dietary assessment was conducted at a single time point (age 70), and that dementia ascertainment relied on registers which are estimated to miss > 50% of cases, particularly among home-dwellers.

Title: Mediating role of frailty in the association between systolic blood pressure trajectories and catastrophic health expenditure among middle-aged and older adults: A longitudinal cohort study.
Journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine hypertension management primarily targets acute cardiovascular events, frequently overlooking progressive physiological decline (frailty) and its economic implications. This study aimed to identify systolic blood pressure (SBP) trajectories and evaluate the mediating role of frailty in their association with catastrophic health expenditure (CHE) among middle-aged and older adults.
METHODS: We analyzed 3996 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). Group-based trajectory modeling identified SBP evolution patterns (2011-2015). The 2015 Frailty Index (FI), based on a 27-item deficit accumulation model, served as the mediator. The primary outcome was CHE in 2018, defined as annual household healthcare expenditure exceeding 40% of the household's capacity to pay. Mediation analysis quantified total, direct, and indirect effects.
RESULTS: Three SBP trajectories emerged: "Low-stable" (50.0%), "Moderate-increasing" (41.3%), and "High-decreasing" (8.7%). Compared with the Low-stable group, the High-decreasing trajectory was significantly associated with higher 2015 FI scores (β=0.029, P<0.001). A statistically significant indirect effect through frailty was observed for the association between the High-decreasing trajectory and CHE in 2018 (ACME = 0.0084, 95% CI: 0.0031-0.0100, P < 0.001), although the direct and total effects were not statistically significant. Findings were similar in sensitivity analyses using alternative CHE definitions and BMI trajectories.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty may be one pathway linking the High-decreasing SBP trajectory with subsequent household CHE. These observational findings support considering functional health alongside blood pressure in middle-aged and older adults. Further prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal relationships and to assess whether incorporating frailty assessments into cardiovascular management improves clinical and socioeconomic outcomes.

Title: Assessing hemodynamic responses in patients undergoing oral surgery with vasoconstrictor-enhanced local anesthesia: a prospective comparative study between medically compromised and healthy participants.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The present study deals with hemodynamic responses between different types of patients along different stages of operations.
METHODS: In a prospective clinical trial,(approved by the IRB approval number 275-15-ASF) and patient informed consent for the procedure, hemodynamic responses were evaluated before and during minor oral surgical procedures performed under local anesthesia. The study encompassed both medically compromised patients (experimental group) and healthy individuals (control group). Hemodynamic parameters, including blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation, were monitored. Statistical analysis was conducted to compare parameter fluctuations within each group and patient. Additionally, clinical indicators were documented using a visual analogue scale. Table 1 presents the characteristics of each group regarding age,gender, medical situation and sort of surgical procedure.
RESULTS: The study findings revealed consistent hemodynamic stability across all stages of the procedures. Patients in both groups maintained stable blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygenation levels prior to and during all stages of surgery. Medically compromised patients showed hemodynamic trends comparable to healthy controls. Local anesthesia with vasoconstrictors demonstrated stable profiles and pain management was effective.
CONCLUSION: Local anesthesia containing adrenaline (1:100,000) demonstrated safety in hemodynamic parameters of healthy and medically compromised patients undergoing minor oral surgery. Overall, hemodynamic fluctuations were minimal, underscoring both the efficacy and safety of using vasoconstrictor-containing local anesthetics for pain management in a controlled hypertension and other well-managed chronic conditions.

Title: Self-reported disease management knowledge by cardiac rehabilitation use multinationally and its correlates.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To multinationally investigate: (1) CVD management knowledge following CR, including variations by region, country income classiﬁcation, as well as patient sociodemographic and clinical characteristics; (2) the association of post-CR knowledge with the number of CR sessions completed and setting of CR delivery; and (3) whether domain-speciﬁc knowledge post-CR is associated with corresponding health markers.
METHODS: Secondary analysis of the International Council of Cardiovascular Prevention and Rehabilitation's International Cardiac Rehabilitation Registry (ICRR) data to December 2024 was conducted for this prospective observational study. Eligible patients were those receiving phase II outpatient CR, with pre-program assessment completed ≥ 6 months prior. Knowledge was assessed via patient report at follow-up/post-program in 9 domains (yes/no), as well as heart-health behaviors and work status. Programs reported CR use, functional capacity, and risk factors.
RESULTS: 4309 patients from 17 programs in 11 countries were included, with 3359 (78.0%) having knowledge follow-up data. Total knowledge was high (8.1 ± 1.3), highest regarding return to life roles, cardiac medications, and care plans. In an adjusted regression model, knowledge varied by region, country income, work status, function, quality of life and CR completion. Knowledge in specific domains was associated with corresponding health markers, including nutrition (p < 0.001), medication adherence (p < 0.001), and stress (p = 0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: CR participants in diverse settings multinationally reported high disease management knowledge, with significant variation by regional, economic, and patient-level factors. Increased CR exposure, potentially in hybrid models, was associated with higher knowledge. This may be associated with improved health behaviors, and hence potentially better patient outcomes.
PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: There is a need for tailored, evidence-based education strategies that address specific knowledge gaps and accommodate diverse patient populations.

Title: Venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer: a comparison of primary cytoreductive surgery versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
Journal: International journal of gynecological cancer : official journal of the International Gynecological Cancer Society
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and temporal distribution of venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer treated with primary cytoreductive surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval cytoreductive surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program-Medicare data to identify women aged ≥65 years with Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program Summary Stage distant uterine cancer diagnosed from 2008 to 2017 who underwent both hysterectomy and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Treatment was classified by the sequence of surgery and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism, comprising pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis, was identified from claims. Patients with baseline venous thromboembolism (6 months before through the month of diagnosis) were excluded from the primary analysis. Cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was estimated using competing risk methods (death as a competing event) and compared via Gray's test. Multi-variable analysis evaluated factors associated with venous thromboembolism during the first 6 months after diagnosis, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and tumor characteristics. Landmark, time-varying treatment-phase, and first-treatment-anchored sensitivity analyses were performed to address immortal time and time-zero misalignment.
RESULTS: Of 1977 patients, 186 (9.4%) had venous thromboembolism prior to diagnosis and were excluded, leaving 1791 patients for analysis: 74.7% underwent primary cytoreductive surgery and 25.3% received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy use increased from 17.6% (2008) to 35.5% (2017). Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher baseline venous thromboembolism prevalence (14.7% vs 7.5%, p<.001) and comorbidity burden. Overall, 568 venous thromboembolism events occurred; cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 20.1% at 6 months, 33.6% at 24 months, and 49.3% at 60 months. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher early cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence (23.0% vs 19.1% at 6 months; 40.8% vs 31.5% at 24 months), with convergence by 60 months (46.5% vs 49.2%; Gray's test p=.054). In multi-variable analysis, the adjusted risk ratio for early venous thromboembolism with neoadjuvant chemotherapy versus primary cytoreductive surgery was 1.21 (95% confidence interval 0.97-1.51), an imprecise estimate that does not exclude a clinically meaningful increase in early risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Among older patients with distant-stage uterine cancer, venous thromboembolism was common, affecting approximately 1 in 5 patients within 6 months and nearly 1 in 2 within 5 years. The cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence did not differ significantly between primary cytoreductive surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Events occurred earlier in the neoadjuvant chemotherapy group, a pattern that may reflect baseline differences between the groups and differential ascertainment as much as treatment sequence. Our findings support the need for a prospective evaluation of treatment-phase-specific thromboprophylaxis.

Title: CT perfusion-derived arterial input function dispersal versus echocardiographic left atrial enlargement in acute stroke.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Arterial input function (AIF) dispersal on brain computed tomography (CT) perfusion reflects delayed cerebral contrast transit and is associated with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We hypothesized that delayed contrast transit through the LA due to LA enlargement may prolong AIF, independent of LVEF.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack from the prospective INSPIRE registry (December 2020-June 2024) who underwent multimodal CT including brain perfusion CT (CTP), as well as transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) within 90 days of stroke. On TTE, left atrial (LA) enlargement was defined as area ≥ 24 cm² and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) as < 50%. Prolonged AIF dispersal from CTP was defined as ≥ 29 s from scan onset to the end of AIF (return to baseline). Multivariable logistic regression was performed, adjusted for clinical and cardiac covariates.
RESULTS: Among 172 patients, prolonged AIF was observed in 50 (29.1%), LA enlargement in 52 (30.2%), and reduced LVEF in 28 (16.3%). In multivariate analysis including both variables, LA enlargement (≥24 cm²: OR 3.76, 95% CI 1.66-8.52, p = 0.002) and reduced LVEF (OR 3.35, 95% CI 1.21-9.27, p = 0.020) were independently associated with prolonged AIF dispersal.
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Both LA enlargement and reduced LVEF were associated with prolonged AIF dispersal, suggesting that AIF delay on CTP is a useful screening tool to identify stroke patients with cardiac dysfunction.

Title: Change in left atrioventricular coupling index from acute to chronic phases for prediction of major adverse cardiac events after myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
AIM: Previous studies confirmed the usability of the left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI) to enhance risk stratification of cardiovascular adverse events in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). We intend to study the prognostic value of the change in LACI (ΔLACI) from the acute to the chronic phases to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in an AMI patient cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 264 patients following AMI were included in a secondary analysis. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in the acute and chronic stages. LACI was defined by the ratio of left atrial to left ventricular end-diastolic volumes. MACE, including all-cause mortality, reinfarction, or heart failure after the follow-up examination (52 [interquartile range {IQR}: 47-61] months after AMI), was defined as the primary endpoint.
RESULTS: Among the 264 participants (median age, 59 years [IQR 50-66]; 229 men), MACE occurred in 41 patients over 52 months after the first imaging. LACI was higher in patients with MACE (P< 0.001). The Youden Index identified a LACI cut-off at 24% and a ΔLACI cut-off at 0.02%/month (both P < 0.001) to classify high-risk patients. After adjusting for multivariate models, ΔLACI (model 1, hazard ratio [HR]: 0.46, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-0.60; model 2, HR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.50-0.78; both P < 0.001) was an independent predictor of MACE. ΔLACI enabled further risk stratification in AMI (LACI > 24%, P < 0.001; LACI < 24%, P = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: LACI and ΔLACI provide superior prognostic value for MACE in AMI patients. ΔLACI provides incremental prognostic value beyond baseline LACI.

Title: Greenspace utilization and obesity burden in urban America: Multi-city analysis with validation in a clinical cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Greenspace engagement is a crucial environmental determinant of obesity, yet evidence remains mixed across urban contexts. Most studies use static measures of greenness, which may mischaracterize pathways through which greenspace influences obesity. This study explores how greenspaces affect obesity across major U.S. metropolitan areas (MSAs) and how these effects vary across cities.
STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional ecological analysis of census tract-level data across nine U.S. metropolitan areas, with validation using a clinical cohort from the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Disease Learning Health System Registry.
METHODS: Census tract-level data across nine U.S. MSAs were analyzed, integrating greenspace visits, adult obesity prevalence, vegetation (NDVI), demographics, food deserts, and health covariates. Linear models (OLS) estimated adjusted associations, while multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) models assessed neighborhood-level variation. Results were validated using patients' Body Mass Index (BMI) data from the Houston Methodist Registry.
RESULTS: The analytic sample included over 15,000 tracts across nine MSAs. In adjusted OLS models, seven MSAs demonstrated inverse associations, with Houston exhibiting the strongest. MGWR analyses revealed substantial within-metro heterogeneity across all MSAs, reflecting neighborhood context, particularly in relation to density, nutrition, and structural constraints. In the Houston Methodist cardiovascular cohort (n = 1,049,782), higher visitation was associated with lower obesity burden. Each additional visit was associated with lower odds of obesity across BMI levels, demonstrating a consistent association across increasing levels of severity.
CONCLUSIONS: Across U.S. metros, greater greenspace engagement was generally associated with lower obesity prevalence, though associations were not spatially uniform. These findings highlight the importance of actual greenspace use and local context in evaluating the role of urban environments in shaping obesity risk.

Title: Measured, not labeled: un-analyzable input versus misclassification in single-lead wearable ECG.
Abstract: Objective. Wearable single-lead ECG has expanded arrhythmia screening, but many recordings are inconclusive, and each corpus defines that word differently. We ask how much deployment error is un-analyzable input rather than misclassification when analyzability is measured with one instrument.Approach. We evaluate three diagnostic databases in-domain and leave-dataset-out under a strict loss counting windows carrying each corpus's inconclusive label as errors unless deferred. We score analyzability with an unsupervised morphological criterion calibrated against three experts on free-living ECG. Reference unreadability is sparse and imbalanced: only seven of 15 subjects contain an unreadable window and one supplies 88% of all unreadable windows. Thresholded sensitivity and every prevalence or true-share correction are therefore exploratory.Main results. The criterion flags almost all expert-unreadable windows but only subsets of the windows labeled inconclusive by their corpora: an inconclusive rate measures convention as much as signal. At, criterion-positive windows are 8.1%, 56.7% and 69.6% of the strict proxy loss on Holter, handheld and patch. The true-share point intervals lie below 50% on handheld and above it on patch, but joint calibration-and-sampling envelopes span 50% on both and still do at the Youden threshold 0.60. On handheld, the calibration-only envelope is more than twice as wide as the corpus-sampling-only envelope. Gate-versus-confidence ordering changes with the accounting and corpus; no general selective-risk advantage of the gate is established.Significance. Corpus labels, criterion flags and latent expert unreadability must not be conflated. A gate can win by predicting a labeling convention, and this retrospective study validates neither transfer to smartwatch dry electrodes nor improvement in patient outcomes. Measure the inconclusive rate with a stated criterion on the raw signal; do not inherit it from a corpus label.

Title: [Mild traumatic brain injury in prehospital primary care emergency services: care pathway and the opportunity of point-of-care biomarkers].
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the initial management of adult patients with mild traumatic brain injury attended by mobile primary care emergency units and to explore the potential role of point-of-care biomarkers of acute brain injury as a future support tool for risk stratification.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, observational, and descriptive study was conducted using clinical records from the mobile emergency units of Cádiz and San Fernando over the full period from January to December 2025. A total of 107 episodes coded as traumatic brain injury were reviewed. After excluding patients younger than 18 years and cases with an initial Glasgow Coma Scale score of ≤13, considered non-mild traumatic brain injury for the operational purposes of this analysis, 91 adult patients with mild traumatic brain injury, defined as a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 14-15, were included. Demographic variables, cardiovascular risk factors, antithrombotic treatment, prehospital disposition, hospital referral, cranial CT, traumatic findings, observation, admission, and final outcome were analyzed. No GFAP or UCH-L1 biomarker measurements were performed in any of the included patients.
RESULTS: The mean age was 71.1 years (SD 20.5) and the median age was 75 years; 46 patients were male (50.5%). Hypertension was present in 57 patients (62.6%), dyslipidemia in 37 (40.7%), and diabetes mellitus in 30 (33.0%). Thirty-three patients (36.3%) were receiving antithrombotic treatment. Hospital referral was the predominant decision, with an overall rate of approximately 88%. Among the 80 patients evaluated in hospital, cranial CT was performed in 61 cases (76.3%). Most patients were discharged after emergency assessment or brief observation. Three patients required admission for traumatic neurological pathology, without neurosurgical intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: In this series, hospital referral and cranial CT were frequent, whereas traumatic neurological admissions were uncommon. As no biomarker measurements were performed in this cohort, the potential role of GFAP and UCH-L1 should be interpreted in this study as a hypothesis for future prospective prehospital research rather than as a conclusion directly supported by the observed data.

Title: Innovative pharmacist-led hypertension management in urgent care: Bridging the gaps in cardiovascular disease.
Journal: Canadian pharmacists journal : CPJ = Revue des pharmaciens du Canada : RPC
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension control remains suboptimal, contributing to preventable cardiovascular disease events, particularly among patients with limited access to primary care. While pharmacist-led care has demonstrated benefit in primary care settings, its impact in urgent care is not well-studied. This study aimed to evaluate patient-centred outcomes of pharmacist-led interventions for hypertension management in urgent care.
METHODS: A pilot project was designed to integrate a pharmacist into a team-based care model to evaluate and intervene on hypertension and other cardiovascular risk factors among patients presenting to urgent care without a primary care provider and with hypertension (blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg). The project was performed at the Metrotown Urgent and Primary Care Centre in British Columbia. A retrospective chart review was performed to evaluate the effectiveness of this project.
RESULTS: A total of 62 patients were included (mean age 56 years; 56.5% male). Mean (standard deviation [SD]) baseline systolic/diastolic blood pressure was 178.4 (SD 21.7)/101.2 (SD 14.7) mmHg and decreased to 124.1 (SD 12.0)/77.4 (SD 9.9) mmHg following pharmacist-led care, representing a mean reduction (SD) of 54.3 (SD 19.7)/23.8 (SD 15.0) mmHg. Overall, 82% of patients were discharged from the program after achieving Hypertension Canada guideline-recommended blood pressure targets.
CONCLUSION: In an urgent care setting, pharmacist-led interventions achieved substantial reductions in blood pressure and high rates of guideline-recommended control, supporting this model as a strategy to address gaps in hypertension care for patients without primary care access.

Title: Pharmacist-led intervention for optimal heart failure medications: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
Journal: Canadian pharmacists journal : CPJ = Revue des pharmaciens du Canada : RPC
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) do not receive optimal pharmacotherapy. Several health systems have incorporated pharmacist-led medication optimization for HFrEF, but this has not been assessed in a randomized controlled trial (RCT). The aim of this pilot RCT was to determine the feasibility of conducting a larger, definitive RCT of pharmacist-led HFrEF medication optimization on top of usual multidisciplinary care.
METHODS: This was a single-centre, parallel-group, open-label, pilot RCT conducted within a heart function clinic. Eligible patients with New York Heart Association class I-III HFrEF were randomized to usual care with or without pharmacist-led HFrEF medication optimization. Primary feasibility outcomes were recruitment (proportion of eligible patients at screening and recruitment rate), retention, intervention fidelity, and patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) completion.
RESULTS: Between March 2023 and May 2024, we screened 423 patients to randomize 42 participants. Recruitment stopped before reaching the target sample size of 60 participants due to slow enrollment (2.2 versus ≥8 monthly anticipated), mainly due to low eligibility. Participants' mean age was 64.7 years, 24% were female, and baseline use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers/angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors, beta-blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors was each ≥90%. One of 11 feasibility outcomes (12-month follow-up ≥80%) met the pre-specified feasibility criteria, indicating a need to modify eligibility criteria, the recruitment strategy and setting, and the processes for collecting PROMs.
INTERPRETATION AND CONCLUSION: This pilot RCT identified several design modifications needed in terms of eligibility, recruitment, and PROM collection to ensure the feasibility of a future definitive trial of pharmacist-led heart failure medication optimization.

Title: Acute and Chronic Cardiovascular and Neuromuscular Effects of Blood Flow Restriction Resistance Training in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Low-load blood flow restriction resistance training (BFR-RT) may offer a lower-load alternative to conventional resistance training for older adults, but its cardiovascular responses and neuromuscular benefits remain incompletely characterized. To synthesize the acute cardiovascular responses and chronic cardiovascular and neuromuscular effects of low-load BFR-RT in older adults. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to July 15, 2026. Randomized controlled trials, including parallel-group and crossover designs, comparing low-load BFR-RT with no-exercise/passive control or conventional non-BFR resistance training were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Twenty-seven studies were included. Acutely, BFR-RT increased systolic blood pressure versus no exercise (MD, 5.30 mmHg; 95% CI, 0.48 to 10.12) and increased diastolic blood pressure (MD, 5.23 mmHg) and mean arterial pressure (MD, 5.81 mmHg) versus conventional resistance training, while heart rate, stroke volume, and cardiac output were not significantly different. Chronically, resting cardiovascular and endothelial outcomes were largely unchanged. Versus no exercise, BFR-RT significantly improved knee-extension, leg-extension, and leg-press 1RM and quadriceps cross-sectional area. Comparisons with conventional resistance training were mixed and outcome-specific. Low-load BFR-RT improves selected neuromuscular outcomes in older adults, particularly relative to no exercise, while cardiovascular responses are comparator-dependent and chronic vascular effects appear largely neutral. These findings support cautious, individualized application rather than assumptions of cardiovascular superiority or equivalence to conventional resistance training.

Title: Perceived Ratings of AI-Generated and Expert-Reviewed vs Clinician-Developed Virtual Cardiology Patient Scenarios Among Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Virtual patients (VPs) are widely used in medical education, but creating high-quality cases requires clinical expertise, iterative revision, and alignment with educational objectives. Generative AI may support VP authoring, but direct comparisons between AI-generated and clinician-developed cases delivered within the same educational setting remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare medical students' learner-perceived ratings of 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed virtual cardiology patient scenario with those of 1 clinician-developed virtual cardiology patient scenario delivered through the same mobile platform.
METHODS: A randomized, participant-blinded 2-arm controlled study was conducted in October 2025 during scheduled fifth-year emergency medicine course sessions. Eligible participants were fifth-year medical students who had completed the cardiology course. Students were assigned 1:1 to complete either a clinician-developed VP (CD-VP; n=64) or a ChatGPT-generated VP (GPT-VP; n=67). Both scenarios followed a shared acute coronary syndrome blueprint and were delivered through the same mobile-optimized app (mobile VPs app [MobiViP]) with identical interface structure and branching logic. The GPT-VP was generated using GPT-5 and refined through iterative follow-up prompting under expert review; direct manual rewriting was prohibited. After completion, students completed a mandatory 19-item questionnaire covering realism and validity, cognitive load, self-reported learning and reflection, and engagement and satisfaction. Analyses included reliability testing, 1-sample tests against a neutral midpoint, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Spearman correlations. Full scenario content and development details are provided as multimedia appendices.
RESULTS: A total of 131 complete questionnaires were analyzed, with no item-level missing data. Mean subscale scores in the CD-VP group were 3.81 (SD 0.64) for realism and validity, 3.67 (SD 0.74) for cognitive load, 3.64 (SD 0.73) for self-reported learning and reflection, and 4.16 (SD 0.64) for engagement and satisfaction; corresponding GPT-VP scores were 4.11 (SD 0.56), 3.03 (SD 0.76), 3.86 (SD 0.77), and 4.28 (SD 0.58), respectively. Compared with the CD-VP, the GPT-VP received higher ratings for realism and validity (Mann-Whitney U=1503.0; P=.003) and lower cognitive load ratings, indicating a lower perceived burden (Mann-Whitney U=1070.5; P<.001). Self-reported learning and reflection showed a marginal difference between groups, with a higher rating for the GPT-VP (Mann-Whitney U=1719.0; P=.05), whereas engagement and satisfaction did not differ significantly (Mann-Whitney U=1922.5; P=.31). Internal consistency was acceptable to good for most subscales, although internal consistency for the realism and validity subscale in the GPT-VP group was moderate (Cronbach α=0.67).
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center randomized study, 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed cardiology VP scenario was rated similarly to or more favorably than 1 clinician-developed scenario in selected learner-perceived domains. Future research should expand to objective learning, retention, development workload, and scalability outcomes.

Title: Mind Your Heart-A Web-Based Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet and Mindful Eating Intervention for Working Adults at Elevated Cardiovascular Risk: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Diet (DASH) diet supports heart health; yet, many find it difficult to follow in community settings. Mindful eating can improve adherence, but in-person programs are time-consuming and not always accessible. eHealth offers an accessible, scalable alternative that may increase engagement and compliance.
OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the feasibility of a DASH eHealth program focused on mindful eating and the preliminary changes in eating behaviors, diet quality, and health outcomes.
METHODS: Participants were recruited from a university workplace via email and flyers and randomly assigned to either a web-based DASH diet education program (Diet Only) or the Mind Your Heart (MYH) intervention. The MYH program included the same DASH curriculum plus additional mindful eating instruction, guided practice, and specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time frame (SMART) goal setting. Both interventions were fully asynchronous, self-guided, and lasted 6 weeks on the Desire2Learn (D2L) Brightspace platform, with no personalized coaching or counseling. Baseline and postintervention assessments involved in-person measurements of anthropometrics, blood pressure, and blood biomarkers. Participants recorded their diets electronically over 3 days using MyFitnessPal (MyFitnessPal, Inc) and completed validated questionnaires on mindful eating using the Mindful Eating Behaviors Scale (MEBS), eating behaviors using the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire Revised 21-item (TFEQ-R21), motivation for regulated eating using the Regulated Eating Behaviors Scale (REBS), and perceived stress using the Perceived Stress Scale 10-item (PSS-10). During the intervention, automated ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) were sent electronically 3 times weekly to monitor eating behaviors in real time.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven participants (mean BMI 31.93 SD 7.25, 34/37, 91.9% female, 31/37, 83.8% White) were randomized into groups. Among the 36 who remained enrolled, the mean curriculum completion was 85.9%, SD 21.4; 31 (86.1%) completed≥60% of assigned content, and 32 (88.9%) completed at least half of the scheduled EMA prompts. Thirty-four participants attended the postintervention assessment and completed the questionnaires and the blood pressure assessment, although paired baseline and postintervention data were not available for all anthropometric measures and biomarkers. Participants reported no adverse events, and research staff observed none. Although no significant between-group differences were observed for DASH adherence, anthropometric measures, blood pressure, or cardiometabolic biomarkers, participants in the MYH group showed greater improvements than the Diet Only group in TFEQ-cognitive restraint (mean difference in change 0.39, 95% CI 0.06-0.72; Hedges g=0.81; P=.02) and REBS-controlled regulation (mean difference in change 3.59, 95% CI 0.01-7.16; Hedges g=0.68; P=.05).
CONCLUSIONS: A fully asynchronous digital mindful eating plus DASH education intervention and associated research procedures were feasible among working adults at elevated cardiovascular risk. Preliminary changes in eating behaviors suggest that mindful eating warrants further evaluation, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample and feasibility design. Larger, adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed.

Title: Reader Response: Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Migraine: A Retrospective, Observational Cohort Study.
Reader Response: Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Migraine: A Retrospective, Observational Cohort Study.
Reader Response: Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Migraine: A Retrospective, Observational Cohort Study.
Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins.
Abstract: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

Title: Brief Mindfulness Training Influences Daily Life Stress Among Emerging Adults Exposed to Childhood Trauma: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Childhood trauma is thought to program biological adaptations to stress that confer lifelong health risk. Mindfulness interventions have improved mental health among adults exposed to childhood trauma, but whether they can offset physical health risk is unknown. This trial evaluated effects of mindfulness and coping interventions on daily life stress processes in this population.
METHODS: Eighty-one emerging adults who recalled physical, emotional, or sexual abuse in childhood were randomly assigned to a two-week remote mindfulness or coping comparison intervention. They provided daily life stress (momentary and day-level perceived stress and stressful events) and heart rate data for one week at pre-intervention, post-intervention, and one-month follow-up. Multilevel models tested for time × condition effects.
RESULTS: Across conditions, participants reported fewer stressful events over time (ps<.001), with larger effects following mindfulness training. Mindfulness participants reported higher stress perceptions from pre- to post-intervention relative to coping (momentary: d=.26, P=.002; daily: d=.44, P=.005), effects that were weaker at follow-up (momentary: d=.20, P=.015; daily: d=.19, P=.23). Increases in perceived stress following mindfulness training were more pronounced at higher levels of childhood abuse severity. In contrast, mindfulness participants showed relatively lower heart rate during moments of stress compared to coping participants from pre- to post-intervention (d=.62, P=.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Brief mindfulness training alters stress processes among adults who recall childhood trauma, reducing stressful events and physiological reactivity while intensifying stress perceptions. Results suggest the possibility that brief mindfulness training increases awareness and reduces emotional avoidance of stress experience. Further work is warranted to examine mindfulness intervention effects on stress-related health trajectories in trauma-exposed populations.

Title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Hepatic Artery Thrombosis and Stenosis After Pediatric Liver Transplantation: Results From the HEPATIC Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence and risk factors of hepatic artery complications (HACs), including thrombosis (HAT) and stenosis (HAS), after pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) are not well characterized. This study aimed to assess the incidence and risk factors of HACs after pLT and quantify the screening effort required to identify a single HAC.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter analysis using the HEPATIC registry, including pLTs from 32 centers over a 20-y period. HAC incidence was assessed across subgroups defined by pLT indication, recipient age, donor type, transplant era, and annual center volume. Timing of HAC occurrence and the number needed to screen were analyzed.
RESULTS: Among 11 443 pLTs, HACs occurred in 4.8% (HAT 3.6%; HAS 1.2%). Most HACs developed within the first-month posttransplant (82.4%), with HAT peaking in the first 2 wk, whereas HAS was more evenly distributed. The overall incidence increased in 2012-2021 (5.3%), with rising HAS and stable HAT rates. Modifiable factors included living donor transplantation (3.4%) and high-volume centers (3.8%), both associated with lower HAC rates, whereas whole grafts in infants <1 y with biliary atresia (15.3%) were associated with higher incidence (all P < 0.001). Patient-related risk factors included retransplantation following previous HACs (11.3%) and noncirrhotic metabolic diseases (7.6%, both P < 0.001). The number needed to screen ranged from 173 to 1907 and was lower in high-risk groups.
CONCLUSIONS: HACs occurred in 4.8% of pLTs, with recent increases driven by HAS. Infants <1 with biliary atresia receiving whole grafts and patients undergoing retransplantation after prior HACs were at the highest risk.

Title: Right Atrial Phasic Function Improves CMR-Based Prognostication in Patients with Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Multicenter Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: In multiple cardiovascular diseases, right atrial (RA) function can serve as an independent predictor for the clinical status and prognosis. However, the prognostic value of RA strain in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) remains considerably unknown. This study aims to explore the relationships between RA strain derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging-feature tracking (CMR-FT) and adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with HFmrEF who were referred for echocardiography and CMR at two tertiary medical centers from April 2016 to September 2024. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, HF-related hospitalization and cardiac transplantation. The findings were validated in a cohort of patients with HFmrEF enrolled from two additional tertiary care centers (January 2019 to January 2025). The development cohort included 1317 patients, and the validation cohort comprised 385 patients. During a median follow-up period of 2.8 years and 2.1 years, respectively, 243 and 72 patients in the development cohort and validation cohort reached the primary endpoint, respectively. Cox regression analysis showed that RA conduit strain was an independent predictor of the primary outcome (HR: 0.86 [0.82, 0.90]; P < .001). The full model integrating clinical variables, traditional imaging, and RA strain achieved the best predictive performance (C-index: 0.80 in development, 0.81 in validation cohorts).
CONCLUSION: RA conduit strain derived from CMR is an independent predictor of adverse outcomes in patients with HFmrEF, providing incremental prognostic value beyond traditional clinical and imaging-derived risk markers.​.

Title: Harnessing AI for Hypothyroidism Monitoring Using Wearable-Derived Heart Rate Data: Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypothyroidism is a prevalent endocrine disorder characterized by an insidious onset and nonspecific symptoms, often leading to significant diagnostic delays. While biochemical thyroid function tests (TFTs) are the gold standard, their invasive nature and cost make them impractical for continuous, proactive screening of at-risk populations. Thyroid hormones exert direct chronotropic effects on the cardiovascular system, and their levels are closely correlated with heart rate (HR). Wearable devices capable of continuous HR monitoring offer a novel opportunity for noninvasive, digital phenotype-based detection.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate an AI-assisted system that uses wearable-derived sleep HR data as a digital monitoring tool for individuals at risk of hypothyroidism, helping identify those who warrant further confirmatory thyroid testing.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used 1677 paired observations consisting of sleep HR data and serum TFT results, including free thyroxine (T4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone levels, from 413 participants (mean age 43.1, SD 9.7 y; women: n=314, 76%). Participants wore consumer-grade wearables (Fitbit) that recorded HR and sleep data. Each TFT result was paired with sleep HR data extracted from the 15 consecutive nights preceding the blood test. An AI system was developed using a gradient boosting algorithm (LightGBM) to classify thyroid status by integrating baseline TFT results with statistical and temporal HR features. The model's performance was evaluated using patient-level leave-one-out cross-validation. To examine the benefit of longitudinal data, performance was compared using 1, 2, or 3 prior paired observations as reference points.
RESULTS: To ensure clinical relevance and avoid performance inflation from hyperthyroid cases, we prioritized the analysis of a subset containing only euthyroid and hypothyroid data (n=744 paired observations). In this clinically challenging subset, the system achieved an accuracy of 74.6%, with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 73.5% using a single-reference data pair. Incorporating longitudinal HR patterns further enhanced performance; using 3 reference pairs improved accuracy to 78.1% (sensitivity 81.8% and specificity 77.7%). In the overall dataset (n=1677 paired observations), the system demonstrated an accuracy of 80.8%, with a sensitivity of 82% and a specificity of 80.8% using a single-reference pair. Notably, the system achieved high clinical safety by detecting 96.3% of severe overt hypothyroidism cases (free T4 <0.5 ng/dL).
CONCLUSIONS: This AI-assisted system demonstrates the feasibility of a sensitive, noninvasive longitudinal monitoring tool for hypothyroidism, robustly identifying a high proportion of hypothyroid cases-particularly severe ones-to prioritize at-risk individuals for confirmatory blood tests. Given the predominantly female iatrogenic-withdrawal cohort, prospective sex-balanced validation in primary hypothyroidism is warranted.

Title: Adjunctive Intracoronary rhTNK-tPA During Primary PCI and Early Regional Left Ventricular Function in STEMI Patients With High Thrombus Burden: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with high thrombus burden often shows impaired myocardial perfusion despite successful epicardial recanalization. Intracoronary recombinant human TNK tissue-type plasminogen activator (rhTNK-tPA) may reduce microvascular obstruction and preserve ventricular function, but evidence is limited.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 136 STEMI patients with high thrombus burden undergoing primary PCI between May 2022 and February 2025. Patients receiving intracoronary rhTNK-tPA (n=62) were compared with controls receiving standard PCI alone (n=74). The primary endpoint was left ventricular regional wall motion status within 7 days after PCI, assessed by WMSI and normal ventricular wall motion. Secondary endpoints included cTFC, ST-segment resolution, final TIMI flow grade, and clinical and safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally comparable. The rhTNK-tPA group had lower WMSI values (P<0.001) and a higher incidence of normal ventricular wall motion (41.7% vs. 19.6%; P=0.014). rhTNK-tPA was also associated with lower post-PCI cTFC (18.18 ± 6.91 vs. 21.24 ± 9.20; P=0.033) and higher ST-segment resolution (83.9% vs. 68.9%; P=0.043), while final TIMI grade 3 flow was similar. In multivariable analysis, rhTNK-tPA was independently associated with lower odds of ventricular wall motion abnormalities (OR=0.214; 95% CI, 0.106-0.433; P<0.001). MACE were infrequent, and no intracranial hemorrhage occurred.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive intracoronary rhTNK-tPA during primary PCI was associated with better early preservation of regional wall motion and improved reperfusion indices without an observed increase in major bleeding.

Title: Effects of Orthokeratology Versus Single-Vision Spectacles on Choroidal Structure and Microcirculation in Adolescents With Myopia.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the longitudinal effects of single-vision spectacles (SV) and orthokeratology (OK) lenses on choroidal structure and microcirculation in adolescents with myopia, and to analyze differences in responses between the two correction modalities.
METHODS: This prospective, nonrandomized cohort study enrolled myopic patients aged 8 to 15 years. Axial length (AL), spherical equivalent refraction (SE), choroidal thickness (ChT), and three-dimensional choroidal vascularity index (3D-CVI) in nine macular sectors within concentric rings of 1, 3, and 6 mm in diameter were measured at baseline and at 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year after lens wear. Within-group and between-group differences were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 116 myopic patients aged 8 to 15 years were enrolled, including 62 in the SV group and 54 in the OK group. After 1 year, AL elongation in the OK group (0.101±0.032 mm) was significantly smaller than that in the SV group (0.393±0.035 mm; P<0.001), and the change in SE (-0.444±0.251 D) was also significantly smaller than that in the SV group (-0.863±0.372 D; P<0.001). Between-group differences in AL emerged from 1 month (P<0.001), and differences in SE emerged from 3 months (P<0.001). In the OK group, ChT increased across sectors during the first 1 to 3 months, followed by partial fluctuation and regression thereafter, whereas 3D-CVI generally increased during months 3 to 6 with mild later fluctuation. In the SV group, most sectors showed statistically significant differences, except for the outer inferior sector, but changes lacked a consistent trend; for 3D-CVI, significant differences were observed in several sectors, likewise without a consistent trend. Except at 1 week, increases in ChT and 3D-CVI in almost all macular sectors at subsequent time points were significantly greater in the OK group than in the SV group (most P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with SV, OK lenses suppress AL elongation and SE progression. There are increases in ChT and 3D-CVI associated with this suppression, suggesting that ChT and 3D-CVI may serve as biomarkers for evaluating the efficacy of myopia-control interventions and supporting further investigation of their role in mechanism of myopia control.

Title: Peripheral perfusion index combined with end-tidal carbon dioxide in predicting sustained return of spontaneous circulation in adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest: A prospective observational study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations of peripheral perfusion index (PI) and end-tidal carbon dioxide (PETCO2), individually and in combination, with sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest, and to assess their predictive performance.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included 125 adults with in-hospital cardiac arrest, of whom 62 achieved sustained ROSC and 63 did not. Measurements obtained after ROSC or termination of resuscitation were excluded. Changes in PI and PETCO2 during resuscitation were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Event-average PI and PETCO2 were evaluated for their ability to predict sustained ROSC using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. The combined model was internally validated using 2,000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: The median time to ROSC was 11 min (IQR, 5-20). Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for both PI and PETCO2 (both P < 0.001). Event-average PI was higher in the ROSC group than in the non-ROSC group [0.62% (IQR, 0.42-0.90) vs. 0.37% (0.31-0.52)], as was event-average PETCO2 [15.5 mmHg (12.2-17.8) vs. 12.0 mmHg (10.4-13.7)] (both P < 0.001). The areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) were 0.756 (95% CI, 0.670-0.842) for PI, 0.753 (95% CI, 0.666-0.839) for PETCO2, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.731-0.886) for their combination. The optimism-corrected AUC for the combined model was 0.800. Pairwise comparisons showed no significant differences among the AUCs. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, PETCO2 remained independently associated with sustained ROSC (adjusted OR, 1.626; 95% CI, 1.148-2.302; P = 0.006), whereas PI was not statistically significant (adjusted OR, 1.359 per 0.1% increase; 95% CI, 0.962-1.920; P = 0.082).
CONCLUSION: Higher PI and PETCO2 during resuscitation were associated with sustained ROSC. Combining PI with PETCO2 yielded numerically better discrimination than either measure alone, although the differences in AUC were not statistically significant. External validation is needed before the combined model can be applied in clinical practice.

Title: Functional trajectories between 90 days and 1 year after intracerebral haemorrhage: a Swedish Stroke Register (Riksstroke) study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Functional outcome after ICH is commonly assessed at 90 days, although recovery and deterioration may continue beyond this conventional endpoint. Large-scale data describing within-patient functional trajectories beyond 90 days remain limited.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a register-based cohort study using the Swedish Stroke Register (Riksstroke), including adults with ICH between 2017 and 2021. Prestroke-independent 90-day survivors with available mRS data at both 90 days and 1 year were included. Functional trajectories were classified as improved, unchanged, worsened or died according to transitions across grouped mRS categories (0-2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 [death]). Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of worsening or death and improvement.
RESULTS: Among 13,574 patients with ICH, 8583 prestroke-independent patients fulfilled eligibility criteria. Of these, 4797 were alive with available 90-day mRS data, and 3030 had complete mRS assessments at both 90 days and 1 year and were included in the primary analysis. Between 90 days and 1 year, 21.5% improved, 67.6% remained unchanged, 5.2% worsened and 5.8% died. Recovery at 1 year was most frequent among patients with mRS 3 at 90 days, of whom 62.4% achieved mRS 0-2, whereas 92.8% of patients with mRS 0-2 remained in the same category. Among patients with mRS 4-5 at 90 days, 20.4% improved to mRS 0-3 by 1 year. Increasing age and higher 90-day disability were associated with less favourable trajectories, whereas male sex was associated with greater likelihood of improvement.
CONCLUSION: Among prestroke-independent 90-day survivors with complete functional follow-up, functional outcomes after ICH remained dynamic beyond 90 days, particularly among patients with moderate disability. Nearly two-thirds of patients with moderate disability at 90 days achieved mRS 0-2 by 1 year, whereas more than 9 in 10 patients who were already classified as mRS 0-2 remained so. These findings suggest that longer-term outcome assessment may provide additional clinically relevant information in future ICH studies and clinical trials.

Title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed.
OBJECTIVE: To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications.
RESULTS: The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921.

Title: Efficacy and Mechanism of Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients With Poststroke Dysphagia: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysphagia is a common complication following stroke. While current management strategies for poststroke dysphagia (PSD) range from nutritional support to neurostimulation techniques, an optimal treatment regimen remains elusive. As a promising noninvasive neuromodulation approach, transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) requires further validation in rigorously designed trials to establish robust evidence of its efficacy and mechanisms of action.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors.
METHODS: This study will use a prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial design. A total of 40 patients with PSD will be enrolled and randomly allocated to either a taVNS group or a sham taVNS group. Both groups will receive conventional swallowing rehabilitation therapy as the baseline intervention. The taVNS group will receive bilateral electrical stimulation at the cymba conchae and cavum conchae of the auricle. These sites correspond to the "Heart" and "Kidney" auricular acupoints, selected in accordance with traditional Chinese medicine theory. In contrast, the sham taVNS group will receive stimulation at regions of the auricle not innervated by the vagus nerve. The primary outcome measure will be the Penetration-Aspiration Scale score. Secondary outcomes will include the Yale Pharyngeal Residue Severity Rating Scale, hyoid bone displacement and hyoid-thyroid approximation distance assessed via B-mode ultrasonography, and motor-evoked potentials of the suprahyoid muscles elicited by transcranial magnetic stimulation. All outcome measures will be evaluated at baseline and after the 2-week intervention period.
RESULTS: This paper describes the protocol for a study evaluating the efficacy and mechanisms of taVNS in patients with PSD. The study was funded in January 2025. Participant recruitment began in March 2025 and is projected to conclude by October 2026. Data collection began in March 2025 and is projected to be completed by October 2026. Primary study results are expected to be submitted for publication in winter 2026.
CONCLUSIONS: This study aims to validate the efficacy of taVNS in treating PSD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms, thereby supporting the development of a novel, noninvasive therapeutic strategy for improving swallowing function in stroke survivors.

Title: Repositioning dislocated rigid C- loop intraocular lens using double rectangle prolene 10-0 sutures: A novel technique.
Abstract: PurposeTo describe a novel technique for repositioning dislocated rigid C-loop polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) intraocular lenses (IOLs) without eyelets using a double-rectangle 10-0 prolene suture configuration.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included six eyes of patients with dislocated rigid C-loop PMMA IOLs in the vitreous cavity. All eyes underwent pars plana vitrectomy and repositioning of the existing IOL using a double-rectangle 10-0 prolene suture configuration, securing the IOL between the suture and the iris. Postoperative evaluation included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), slit-lamp biomicroscopy, fundoscopy, anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), and posterior segment OCT. IOL tilt and postoperative complications were assessed during follow-up.ResultsAt 12 months follow up all six IOLs were successfully repositioned intraoperatively. No complete IOL redislocation occurred during the available follow-up. Final BCVA was 0.14 ± 0.08 logMAR, and the mean IOL tilt was 2.43° ± 1.58°. A myopic refractive shift of 1.75 ± 0.22 D was observed compared with the pre-dislocation refraction. One eye (16.7%) developed partial inferior IOL subluxation, without associated visual or refractive deterioration, and two eyes (33.3%) developed cystoid macular edema, resolved with treatment.ConclusionIn this small proof-of-concept series, the double-rectangle 10-0 prolene suture technique allowed repositioning of dislocated rigid C-loop PMMA IOLs while avoiding a large corneal incision and was associated with favorable short-term anatomical outcomes. The occurrence of CME and partial IOL subluxation highlights the need for careful postoperative monitoring. Larger studies with longer follow-up are required to determine the long-term stability, safety, and reproducibility of the technique.

Title: The effect of pregnancy and puerperium on haemorrhage risk in women with cerebral cavernous malformations: a case-crossover study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are lesions that may be incidental or present with haemorrhage or focal neurological deficits. Some authors have reported apparent lesion enlargement during pregnancy and hypothesised that hormonal fluctuations may promote CCM growth or haemorrhage. Whether pregnancy increases the risk of symptomatic haemorrhage (SH) from CCMs therefore represents an important clinical concern.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We collected prospective data from patients with CCMs. A case-crossover framework was used to compare the risk of SH during pregnancy-related and non-pregnant observation periods. Pregnancy-related observation periods included pregnancy and the 6-week puerperium, while all other follow-up time after CCM diagnosis was considered non-pregnant. Each woman served as her own control, with the risk of SH during pregnancy-related periods compared with that during her non-pregnant follow-up periods.
RESULTS: After screening, the final cohort included 42 women diagnosed with a CCM at 46 years of age or younger. Of these, 23 women experienced at least 1 pregnancy (30.4% familial CCM; 21.7% brainstem CCM) at or after CCM diagnosis, accounting for 40 pregnancies. Overall, 2 SHs occurred during 25.6 pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to an annual SH rate of 7.8% (95% CI, 0.9-28.3), compared with 42 SHs during 420.7 non-pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to an annual SH rate of 10.0% (95% CI, 7.2-13.5). No statistically significant difference was found in the haemorrhagic rates between pregnant vs non-pregnant periods (P = .751). When observation periods were stratified according to a history of prior haemorrhage, no SHs occurred during 10.3 pregnancy patient-years among periods with prior haemorrhage, whereas 8 SHs occurred during 12.7 non-pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to an annual SH rate of 63.0% (95% CI, 27.2-124.2). Among periods without prior haemorrhage, 2 SHs occurred during 15.2 pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to an annual SH rate of 13.1% (95% CI, 1.6-47.5), compared with 34 SHs during 408.0 non-pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to an annual SH rate of 8.3% (95% CI, 5.8-11.6). In this subgroup, generalised estimating equation (GEE)-Poisson analysis showed no significant difference in haemorrhage risk between pregnancy and non-pregnancy periods (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.64, 95% CI, 0.44-6.13; P = .462). When analysis was restricted to brainstem CCMs, GEE-Poisson analysis showed no significant difference between pregnancy and non-pregnancy periods (IRR 2.09; 95% CI, 0.36-12.14; P = .411). One SH occurred during 8.2 pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to an annual SH rate of 12.2% (95% CI, 0.3-67.9), vs 6 SHs during 91.6 non-pregnancy patient-years, corresponding to 6.6% (95% CI, 2.4-14.3). Among periods with prior haemorrhage, no SHs occurred during 1.5 pregnancy patient-years (0.0%; 95% CI, 0.0-194.7), vs 2 SHs during 4.4 non-pregnancy patient-years (45.2%; 95% CI, 5.5-163.4). Among periods without prior haemorrhage, 1 SH occurred during 6.7 pregnancy patient-years (15.0%; 95% CI, 0.4-83.6), vs 4 SHs during 87.2 non-pregnancy patient-years (4.6%; 95% CI, 1.3-11.7), with no significant difference on GEE-Poisson analysis (IRR 3.50; 95% CI, 0.62-19.78; P = .156).
CONCLUSION: Pregnancy was not associated with a significantly increased rate of SH in this cohort of women with CCMs. However, the limited number of events during pregnancy and the limited pregnant follow-up require cautious interpretation. Counselling should remain individualised according to lesion location, prior haemorrhagic history, neurological status and treatment history.

Title: Bronchoscopy in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery Patients: Airway Findings, Clinical Outcomes, and the Selective Role of Rigid Bronchoscopy.
Journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
Abstract: BackgroundThis study evaluated the indications, airway findings, therapeutic interventions, and clinical outcomes associated with bronchoscopy in pediatric cardiac surgery patients, including the selective role of rigid bronchoscopy.MethodsThis retrospective, single-center study included patients who underwent bronchoscopy between January 2019 and January 2025. Among 1840 surgical patients, 60 required bronchoscopy because of prolonged mechanical ventilation, extubation failure, difficulty weaning from ventilatory support, or suspected airway pathology.ResultsThe median age of the patients was 9 months, and the first bronchoscopy was performed at a median of 8.5 postoperative days (range, 5-24 days). Findings were normal in 32/60 patients (53.3%). The most common abnormalities were mucus plugging/secretion retention (20.0%, 12/60), blood clots (8.3%, 5/60), and tracheomalacia (8.3%, 5/60). Thirteen patients underwent 16 rigid bronchoscopic procedures. Bronchoscopy guided subsequent management, including diaphragmatic plication in four patients and surgery for bronchial compression in three. Among 17 patients with mucus plugging/secretion retention or blood clot, eight achieved successful extubation without tracheostomy. Tracheostomy was performed in 34/60 patients (56.7%), and in-hospital mortality in this group was 28.3% (17/60). Brief transient oxygen desaturation occurred occasionally, but no major procedure-related complications were observed.ConclusionsBronchoscopy provides clinically useful diagnostic and therapeutic information in selected pediatric cardiac surgery patients. Mucus plugging or retained secretions were the most common abnormal finding, while normal findings helped redirect evaluation toward alternative causes of ventilator dependence. Flexible bronchoscopy was adequate for most patients, whereas rigid bronchoscopy was reserved for selected cases of dense mucus plugs or organized blood clots that could not be adequately removed with flexible techniques.

Title: Ambient Heat Exposure Is Not Associated with Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction among Emergency Department Patients with Acute Chest Pain.
Abstract: BackgroundHeat exposure increases cardiovascular risk, but its relationship with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) in emergency department (ED) patients is unknown. This study examined whether heat exposure increases NSTEMI risk in ED patients with chest pain.MethodsThis observational cohort study of adults with chest pain from 5 US EDs (April 1, 2019-October 31, 2023) used the Wake Forest Chest Pain Registry. Heat data were collected from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Heat exposure was defined as maximum daily heat index ≥80°F, the National Weather Service's cautionary threshold. The primary outcome was index NSTEMI, determined using validated diagnosis codes. Logistic models assessed the association between heat and NSTEMI. Multivariable models were adjusted for common cardiovascular confounders, and pollution-given its potential to exacerbate cardiovascular disease. Lagged analysis evaluated heat exposure over 5-d lags. Unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) are reported with 95% confidence intervals.ResultsAmong 21,367 patients with chest pain, 52.7% (11,260/21,367) were female, the median age was 53.5 y (IQR 40-65), and 63.1% (13,486/21,367) had heat-exposed days. Index NSTEMI occurred in 5.9% of patients. NSTEMI rates were similar between those with and without heat exposure (5.8% [778/13,486] vs 6.2% [487/7881]; OR: 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.05). After adjustment, heat exposure remained unassociated with index NSTEMI (aOR: 0.91, 95% CI 0.80-1.03). Lagged analysis showed no association between NSTEMI and heat exposure in unadjusted (OR: 0.92, 95% CI 0.82-1.04) or adjusted (aOR: 0.94, 95% CI 0.82-1.07) models.ConclusionHeat exposure was not associated with NSTEMI in chest pain ED patients.

Title: Meta-Analysis: Potassium-Competitive Acid Blockers Versus Proton Pump Inhibitors for Gastroprotection in Patients Receiving Antiplatelet Therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPIs are standard for gastroprotection during antiplatelet therapy. However, certain PPIs, chiefly omeprazole and esomeprazole, inhibit cytochrome P450 2C19 (CYP2C19), which activates clopidogrel, whereas potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) are metabolised predominantly by CYP3A4.
AIMS: To compare the efficacy of P-CABs with PPIs in preventing gastrointestinal bleeding in adults receiving single or dual antiplatelet therapy.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to 31st May 2026 for randomised and comparative observational studies of P-CABs versus PPIs. Risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were pooled using random-effects models. The primary outcome was gastrointestinal bleeding; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, revascularisation, stroke, upper gastrointestinal bleeding and platelet reactivity.
RESULTS: We included nine studies (one randomised, eight observational; 34,123 patients). Gastrointestinal bleeding did not differ between groups (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.67-1.18). MACE (RR 0.80, 0.65-0.98); revascularisation (RR 0.77, 0.59-0.99) was less frequent with P-CABs (observational studies only). No differences were seen for all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, or platelet reactivity. Findings may be confounded by study origin, ulcerogenic and acid-suppressive agents, and outcome definitions.
CONCLUSIONS: P-CABs showed no statistically significant difference from PPIs in gastrointestinal bleeding. Lower rates of MACE and revascularisation were from observational studies. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted with caution, as they do not establish non-inferiority or a cardiovascular benefit. Randomised trials are needed to confirm these findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261372513 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews).

Title: A generalizable 3D dose prediction across heterogeneous cohorts: A framework developed for the 2025 AAPM GDP-HMM challenge.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Manual radiotherapy treatment planning is labor-intensive, subjective, and highly variable across planners and institutions. Deep learning has emerged as a promising approach for estimating achievable three-dimensional (3D) dose distributions for a given plan (hereafter: dose prediction) by directly mapping patient anatomy and beam geometry to voxel-wise dose. However, achieving robust generalization across diverse anatomical sites, prescriptions, and institutions remains a major challenge, particularly under computational constraints required for clinical deployment.
PURPOSE: We sought to develop and evaluate a generalizable, computationally efficient 3D dose prediction framework capable of spanning heterogeneous multi-site and multi-cohort datasets, as defined in the 2025 AAPM Generalizable Dose Prediction for Heterogeneous Multi-Cohort and Multi-Site (GDP-HMM) Grand Challenge. Our goal was to design a model that not only achieved state-of-the-art voxel-wise accuracy but also maintained clinically meaningful dose-volume and geometric characteristics across diverse cases.
METHODS: We implemented a fully convolutional 3D dose-prediction model adapted from the MedNeXt architecture, which was originally introduced as a high-capacity convolutional backbone for medical image segmentation and is well suited to volumetric dense prediction tasks. The network accepted multimodal inputs comprising CT, PTV/OAR masks, beam and angle plates, and scalar plan metadata. A composite loss function combined voxel-wise L1, body-masked weighted L1, structure-wise moment-matching, and gradient-based penalties to jointly preserve spatial fidelity and dosimetric accuracy. The model was trained on the fixed GDP-HMM dataset consisting of 2876 training plans, 356 validation plans, and a held-out test set of 498 plans using random 3D patches and evaluated by mean absolute error (MAE), homogeneity index (HI), and conformity indices (CI100%, CI50%). Ablation studies quantified the contribution of each loss component to overall performance. Statistical comparisons used paired Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction.
RESULTS: The proposed model achieved a mean voxel-wise MAE of 2.04 Gy on the validation set, outperforming the challenge baseline (2.54 Gy). An ensemble with the baseline further improved MAE to 1.94 Gy on the validation set and 2.071 Gy on the held-out test set, corresponding to the lowest test-set MAE and first-place overall ranking in the GDP-HMM Challenge. Predicted dose distributions preserved key plan characteristics, with ΔHI, ΔCI100%, and ΔCI50% narrowly centered around zero, indicating consistent target coverage and dose conformity. Protocol-specific evaluations for head-and-neck and lung cohorts demonstrated close alignment with reference plans, with no systematic degradation in OAR endpoints. Ablation experiments showed that removing gradient-based terms increased MAE by 0.50 Gy, while excluding the moment-matching term increased MAE by 0.06 Gy confirming that both gradient- and moment-based constraints enhanced spatial and dosimetric fidelity.
CONCLUSION: We present a generalizable 3D dose prediction framework that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while satisfying stringent runtime requirements (< 3s per case on < 24 GB GPU memory). By integrating gradient-aware and moment-based constraints within a MedNeXt backbone, the model preserved clinical DVH endpoints and geometric plan features. These findings demonstrate that carefully engineered loss formulations are pivotal for cross-institutional generalization. The framework offers a foundation for rapid dose prediction that could accelerate treatment planning, reduce inter-planner variability, and enable intelligent automation in radiotherapy workflows.

Title: Differentiating Coumadin Ridge From Thrombus in Dilated Left Atria: The Value of the Modified Apical 4-Chamber View.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: We read the study by Walczewski et al. The authors used the LATTEE registry to evaluate left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus predictors. They call for comprehensive echocardiographic evaluation. We agree. Their analysis covers both sexes. Building on this, we highlight a shared diagnostic pitfall.
