Freedom from death or HFH was significantly higher among patients with GLIDE scores ≤1 compared to those ≥2 (p = 0.032). Of the 251 1-year survivors, follow-up echocardiography was available in 170 (68%). The GLIDE score predicted 1-year TR severity (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.73; 95% CI 0.65-0.81), with moderate or less residual TR achieved in 80.6%, 54.9%, and 18.8% of patients with GLIDE scores of 0-1, 2-3, and ≥4, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The GLIDE score is associated with 1-year survival and HFH after T-TEER as well as ≤ moderate TR.

Title: Endoscopic versus open vein harvesting technique and 2-year saphenous vein graft patency: A subanalysis of the Newton-CABG CardioLink-5 randomized trial.
Machine Perfusion in Split Liver Transplantation: A Scoping Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Split liver transplantation (SLT) maximizes donor organ utilization but faces challenges with ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI). Machine perfusion techniques, including hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE), dual HOPE (DHOPE), and normothermic machine perfusion (NMP), may enhance graft viability and expand the donor pool. This scoping review maps existing clinical and experimental evidence on machine perfusion in SLT, examining benefits, feasibility, outcomes, and knowledge gaps.
METHODS: Following Joanna Briggs Institute manual guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through September 3, 2025, plus gray literature (ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform, Google Scholar). Studies exploring machine perfusion techniques in liver splitting of human or animal grafts, with or without transplantation, were included.
RESULTS: After screening 958 records, 38 studies were included (29 primary studies, 9 reviews). Among primary studies, 84 clinical transplant cases using machine perfusion were identified (including 2 cases with unspecified perfusion modality); however, this number may not represent unique patients because of possible overlap between same-center cohorts. HOPE (7 studies, 40 cases) was supported by preliminary comparative data suggesting reduced IRI versus static cold storage, with 1 cohort study showing lower postreperfusion syndrome rates (13.3% versus 47.1%, P = 0.04) and reduced IRI scores (3 versus 4, P = 0.03). NMP (16 studies, 34 cases) enabled extended preservation up to 25 h with 100% short-term graft survival in case series. DHOPE (4 studies, 8 cases) reported feasibility for complex full-left/full-right splitting. Evidence was limited by small sample sizes (median n = 2, range 1-26), short follow-up (maximum 18 mo, median 6 mo), absence of randomized trials, and potential publication bias.
CONCLUSIONS: Machine perfusion remains an investigational strategy in SLT. Preliminary evidence suggests HOPE may reduce IRI and NMP may provide logistical advantages through extended preservation. However, evidence derives entirely from small observational studies without randomization. Multicenter prospective studies with standardized protocols, longer follow-ups, and cost-effectiveness analyses are needed.

Title: Effects of exercise-related interventions on blood pressure and related variables among individuals with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a leading contributor to global cardiovascular disease burden and premature mortality. Although pharmacological treatment is effective, long-term Blood Pressure (BP) control remains suboptimal for many patients, highlighting the importance of non-pharmacological strategies such as physical exercise. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of exercise training interventions for improving BP outcomes among adults with hypertension. While a limited number of included randomized controlled trials involved participants with prehypertension, the review primary focus was hypertension management.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across five electronic databases (Scopus, AMED, MEDLINE, PUBMED, and CINAHL) to identify relevant clinical trials. A small number of trials involving participants with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension were retained where they met the predefined eligibility criteria and contributed to the overall evidence regarding elevated BP management. Methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the PEDro scale. Data were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis, and pooled effects were expressed as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical heterogeneity was evaluated using the I2 statistic. Meta-analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5. Structured Narrative synthesis was performed where meta-analysis was not feasible.
RESULTS: A total of 26 studies that recruited 1,576 participants met the inclusion criteria and were included in the review. Majority of the studies were of moderate-to-good methodological quality (∼70%). Aerobic training consistently produced statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in both SBP (SMD: -0.97; 95% CI -1.46 to -0.47; p = 0.0001) and DBP (SMD: -1.55; 95% CI -2.19 to -0.90; p < 0.00001). Combined aerobic and resistance training also resulted in significant reductions in SBP (SMD: -1.11; 95% CI: -2.11 to -0.11; p = 0.03) and DBP (SMD: -1.25; 95% CI: -2.24 to -0.27; p = 0.01), suggesting potential additive or complementary effects of multimodal exercise interventions. Resistance training alone demonstrated a significant and large reduction in DBP but showed inconsistent and non-significant effects on SBP. In addition to blood pressure reduction, several studies reported improvements in secondary outcomes, including cardiorespiratory fitness, heart rate variability, body composition, inflammatory markers, physical performance, and quality of life. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed across most pooled analyses, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests that aerobic exercise, either alone or combined with resistance training, is associated with some beneficial reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure among individuals with hypertension.

Title: A Comparative Review of Performance and Concurrent Cardiac Rhythm Assessment Across Home Sleep Apnea Testing Devices.
Abstract: Home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) is now widely used in place of in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) for the evaluation of sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), but published performance varies across FDA-cleared devices. This narrative review aimed to summarize the published performance of FDA-cleared Type III HSAT devices currently marketed in the United States and compare their labeled capabilities for assessing SDB over multiple nights and concurrently evaluating cardiac rhythm and atrial fibrillation (AF) burden. A search of the FDA 510(k) database identified 68 devices with MNR as the primary product code that were cleared after August 1, 2016, or were cleared earlier but released for sale after that date. There were 13 devices that met these criteria and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) criteria for a Type III HSAT. For each device, sensitivity and specificity against PSG, scored under American Academy of Sleep Medicine Rule 1B (4% oxygen desaturation), were obtained from the FDA 510(k) Summary or a peer-reviewed validation study. Balanced accuracy (the mean of sensitivity and specificity) was calculated at apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) thresholds of 5, 15, and 30 events per hour. Five devices were excluded from the comparison and are reported for information only because their performance data were not reported using a methodology consistent with that of the other devices: they used a different scoring rule or severity threshold, reported central apnea detection only, or relied on a less credible source for the reported data. Among the remaining eight devices, reported sample sizes ranged from 30 to 476 subjects. All eight reported performance at AHI ≥ 15, five at AHI ≥ 5, and three at AHI ≥ 30. At AHI ≥ 15, balanced accuracy was highest for AcuPebble Ox200 (Acurable Limited, London, UK) (96.5), followed by WatchPAT SW (Itamar Medical, Caesarea, Israel) (94.0) and RX-1 Sleep (Rhythm Express, St. Paul, MN) (92.2). RX-1 Sleep reported the highest balanced accuracy at AHI ≥ 5 (90.9) and AHI ≥ 30 (92.9). These comparisons are indirect and descriptive: each device was validated against PSG in a separate cohort, none was evaluated against another device in the same patients, and between-device differences were not statistically tested. Prospective head-to-head studies against a common reference standard would be needed to confirm differences in relative performance. Among the devices compared, RX-1 Sleep system provides an aid for concurrent assessment of SDB and AF burden in a single test. Other devices can flag or record rhythm information but cannot quantify AF burden. Together with its published performance and multi-night testing capability, this may offer clinical benefit given the severity-dependent association between SDB and AF burden and the elevated cardiovascular risk observed when the two conditions coexist.

Title: Saphenous vein grafts from thigh versus calf: Comparison of angiographic patency and clinical outcomes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study compared angiographic patency and clinical outcomes between patients who received saphenous vein (SV) grafts from the upper leg (UL) and those who received grafts from the lower leg (LL) for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: A total of 1630 patients who received primary isolated off-pump CABG using the SV harvested via the no-touch technique from the UL (UL group, n = 203) or the LL (LL group, n = 1427) were enrolled in this study. Propensity score matching was performed, and 202 pairs were matched. Early, 1-year, and 5-year graft angiograms were obtained for 99.5%, 85.7%, and 31.2% of the cohort, respectively. The median follow-up duration was 85.8 months. The primary outcome was midterm angiographic patency, and the secondary outcomes were midterm clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: There was no significant difference in baseline characteristics between the matched groups. Early clinical outcomes, including operative mortality (0.8%, 13 out of 1630), demonstrated no intergroup differences. Angiographic patency for SV grafts was not significantly different at early (98.3% vs 98.5% in the UL group vs the LL group, P = .80), 1-year (94.8% vs 95.4% in the UL group vs the LL group, P = .74), or 5-year evaluation (97.8% vs 96.0% in the UL group vs the LL group, P = .43). Midterm survival up to 7 years was comparable between the groups (P = .81).
CONCLUSIONS: SV grafts from the UL demonstrated comparable 5-year angiographic patency and 7-year clinical outcomes compared with those from the LL during off-pump CABG.

Title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns.
METHODS: GEO datasets for IPAH and MPM were analyzed. Overlapping DEGs and WGCNA modules were identified. PPI network analysis combined with LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE was used to identify candidate biomarker genes. A classification model was constructed and evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction. Immune infiltration was evaluated by ssGSEA. Molecular docking and MD simulations assessed drug binding to candidate target proteins. qRT-PCR validated candidate biomarker gene expression.
RESULTS: Six concordantly upregulated and eleven concordantly downregulated DEGs were shared between IPAH and MPM. Upregulated genes were enriched in cell cycle regulation, while downregulated genes were enriched in neutrophil chemotaxis. WGCNA identified 58 overlapping genes. CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 were identified as candidate biomarker genes. A ROTS sensitivity analysis confirmed that all 1710 MPM DEGs were reproducible and directionally concordant at the matching FDR <0.05 threshold despite the imbalanced case-control ratio. The classification model achieved AUCs of 0.909 and 0.875 in training and external validation sets, with a LOOCV AUC of 0.879 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.896. Immune infiltration revealed increased Th17 cells but decreased neutrophils in IPAH. CXCR2 and S100A9 expression correlated with neutrophil infiltration; LCN2 expression correlated with metabolic reprogramming. Navarixin showed the strongest binding affinity to CXCR2 (-10.1 kcal/mol). MD simulations confirmed stable binding of the CXCR2-Navarixin complex. qRT-PCR confirmed significant downregulation of all three genes in IPAH patients.
CONCLUSION: This hypothesis-generating study identifies shared transcriptomic signatures between IPAH and MPM, highlighting CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 as candidate biomarkers linked to immune dysregulation and metabolic reprogramming. The computational and correlative nature of these findings, together with the limited size of the external validation cohort, requires confirmation through functional experiments and validation in larger, independent, and multicentre cohorts before clinical translation can be considered.

Title: Prospective Randomized Evaluation of DIabetics for graft patency and outcomes following Coronary artery bypass grafting using one (single) versus two or More (mulTi) arterial grafts (PREDICT) trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: As the result of procedural complexity and risk of sternal wound infections, the adoption of multiarterial grafting (MAG) in coronary artery bypass surgery is lower in patients with diabetes despite a high prevalence of multivessel coronary artery disease. We conducted a randomized controlled study to evaluate the safety, graft patency at 1 year, and long-term survival at 5 years in MAG compared to single arterial grafting (SAG). This interim analysis reports 1-year mortality, morbidity, and graft patency.
METHODS: A total of 950 patients with diabetes and multivessel coronary artery disease were enrolled between February 2022 and January 2025 at 15 hospitals across 7 states in India and randomized to SAG (n = 477) or MAG (n = 473) groups in a multicenter, prospective, randomized trial. Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events and graft patency assessed by computed tomography coronary angiography at 1 year were analyzed (CTRI/2020/09/027692).
RESULTS: One-year composite outcome (SAG: n = 7 [1.5%] vs MAG: n = 7 [1.5%], P = .98) and mortality (SAG: n = 4 [0.8%] vs MAG: n = 6 [1.3%], P = .51) were low and comparable. Myocardial infarction occurred in 1 patient in each group. Stroke rates were comparable (SAG: n = 2 vs MAG: n = 1). One patient with SAG required repeat revascularization (percutaneous coronary intervention). Sternal wound infection occurred in 7 patients in the SAG group (1.5%) and 12 patients in the MAG group (2.6%) (P = .36). Sternal reconstruction was required in only 3 patients in the MAG group (0.6%). In total, 350 patients underwent protocol computed tomography graft angiography for graft assessment (SAG: n = 170, MAG: n = 180). Although overall graft patency did not differ between the SAG and MAG groups, vein graft patency was greater with MAG only after statistical adjustment for the effect of on-pump or off-pump status and involved coronary artery. Off-pump coronary artery bypass surgery, right internal mammary artery grafts, and right coronary artery and left circumflex coronary artery territory grafting were associated with lower overall graft patency.
CONCLUSIONS: Interim results from the trial demonstrate similar safety and 1-year clinical outcomes for SAG and MAG. We show superior venous graft patency with MAG after adjustment, but additional studies are required to validate this finding.

Title: Tricuspid valve leaflet multiplicity and Doppler-derived right-heart hemodynamic trajectories after surgical repair.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether tricuspid leaflet multiplicity is associated with divergent postoperative hemodynamic trajectories after surgical repair.
METHODS: One hundred seventeen patients undergoing tricuspid valve surgery (January 2023 to March 2025) were prospectively enrolled, with leaflet morphology classified by intraoperative visualization and serial echocardiography over 1 year. The prespecified primary end point was a Doppler-derived tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) increase, defined as a 5-mm Hg-or-greater increase in TRPG from discharge to 1 year.
RESULTS: Among 100 patients with paired data, the primary end point occurred more frequently in the 4/5-leaflet group despite similar residual tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and discharge TRPG (48.5% vs 26.9%; odds ratio, 2.56; 95% CI, 1.07-6.12; P = .034); the age-adjusted association was borderline (aOR, 2.39; P = .054) and the within-group rise significant only in that cohort (P = .024). Severe-or-greater TR recurrence was rare (3.0% vs 0.0%; P = .327). Discharge tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion was lower in the 4/5-leaflet group (0.96 ± 0.36 vs 1.15 ± 0.36 cm; P = .010) but converged by 1 year (P = .585).
CONCLUSIONS: Tricuspid leaflet multiplicity was associated with a subphenotype showing preserved early TR reduction, lower discharge tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, and a greater 1-year frequency of Doppler-derived TRPG increase. Morphology-based stratification may refine postoperative surveillance pending external validation.

Title: Low palmar arch velocity does not predict hand dysfunction after radial artery harvest: A prospective analysis of duplex ultrasonography.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Preoperative assessment of radial artery suitability commonly relies on the Allen test, a subjective bedside maneuver. We evaluated whether duplex ultrasonography flow metrics predict postoperative hand function after radial artery harvest for coronary artery bypass grafting.
METHODS: Patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting (October 2024 to February 2026) with an appropriate second arterial conduit target underwent preoperative Allen testing and upper-extremity duplex ultrasonography, including palmar arch velocity with radial artery occlusion (PAVRO) and ulnar augmentation (percentage increase in ulnar artery flow with radial occlusion). Hand function (grip and pinch strength, fatigue, and dexterity) and patient-reported symptoms were measured preoperatively and at 1 month. Analysis of covariance and logistic regression models were adjusted for baseline hand function, age, sex, and the presence of diabetes.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine patients underwent radial harvest with complete follow-up. Low PAVRO was not associated with postoperative change in any hand function metrics. Increased ulnar augmentation was associated with greater postoperative mean grip strength (P = .017) and fatigue resistance (P = .002); no patient with ulnar augmentation >40% had a clinically meaningful (>20%) decrease in grip strength. Allen test results had low concordance with duplex ultrasonography: 11 of 23 patients deemed unsuitable by duplex had a normal Allen test result at the 3-second threshold, and 13 of 47 harvested patients had an abnormal Allen test results.
CONCLUSIONS: Low PAVRO does not predict hand dysfunction after radial artery harvest, whereas lower ulnar augmentation may better identify patients at risk of grip strength decrease postoperatively. Duplex ultrasonography provides objective flow metric data and should be prioritized in preoperative assessment.

Title: Hypothermic fibrillatory arrest may not increase stroke risk in minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: A 13-year propensity score-matched experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Hypothermic fibrillatory arrest (HFA) has been associated with increased stroke risk in minimally invasive mitral valve surgery, although selection bias may confound this association.
METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective analysis of minimally invasive mitral valve surgeries (July 2011 to December 2024) stratified by myocardial protection strategy (HFA vs aortic crossclamping [ACC]), assessed using propensity-score matching and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of 1258 patients, 984 underwent HFA and 274 received ACC. The fibrillatory arrest group had more complex profiles and greater rates of previous myocardial infarction (14.2% vs 4.7%), previous cardiac surgery (12.8% vs 2.2%), and urgent/emergent status (18.8% vs 10.2% all P < .05). Despite these greater-risk profiles, postoperative stroke rates were comparable (3.1% vs 3.7%, P = .57). After propensity matching, stroke remained comparable (3.3% vs 3.7%), and fibrillatory arrest was not independently associated with increased stroke risk (odds ratio, 0.94; P = .91). In-hospital mortality was also comparable (HFA: 2.6% vs ACC: 1.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: HFA demonstrated noninferior stroke outcomes compared with ACC when performed with meticulous protocols at high-volume centers. These findings do not support HFA as a replacement for ACC but rather as a viable alternative when clinically and technically indicated.

Title: Pilot safety and efficacy trial of amiodarone-infused biologic acellular biatrial patches to prevent new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: New onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) occurs in approximately 25% to 40% of patients undergoing heart surgery and is associated with increased perioperative morbidity and mortality. We evaluated the safety and exploratory efficacy of amiodarone-infused CardiaMend (Helios Cardio) biatrial patches for POAF prevention.
METHODS: A single-center pilot clinical trial enrolled 40 patients after applying inclusions and exclusion criteria, randomized in 1:1 fashion. Patients in the treatment group received the CardiaMend patch, a porous acellular matrix derived from fetal bovine dermis, infused with 70 mg amiodarone, placed on both atria, whereas the control group received standard care. The primary end point was safety, defined as major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Secondary end points included POAF, length of hospital stay, 30-day readmission, and POAF duration.
RESULTS: The 2 randomized groups had similar baseline characteristics. There were 2 major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events: 1 patient in the control group experienced an embolic stroke with full recovery before discharge, and 1 patient in the treatment group died from an acute abdominal event following intra-aortic balloon pump removal, deemed unrelated to the study device. The incidence of POAF (4 patients [20%] vs 8 patients [40%]; P = .30) and mean atrial fibrillation duration (2.5 ± 2.4 days vs 3.8 ± 4.1 days) were lower in the treatment group. Mean length of hospital stay was shorter in the treatment group (5.8 ± 1.2 days vs 9.3 ± 7.5 days; P = .07). At 30-day follow-up, Holter monitoring revealed no atrial fibrillation in the treatment group and 3 (15%) patients in the control group (P = .23), and readmission rates were also lower in the treatment group (5% vs 15%; P = .6).
CONCLUSIONS: This pilot randomized clinical trial showed that amiodarone-infused CardiaMend biatrial patches were safe, with no evidence of systemic amiodarone toxicity. Treatment with amiodarone-infused CardiaMend patches was associated with a clinically noticeable reduction in POAF, length of stay, and postdischarge atrial fibrillation.

Title: Extracardiac conduit versus lateral tunnel: Exploring the optimal surgical approach in the EUROFONTAN experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The Fontan procedure is a crucial surgical intervention for single-ventricle physiology, with the extracardiac conduit (ECC) and lateral tunnel (LT) techniques being the predominant approaches. This study aimed to compare early and late clinical outcomes of ECC and LT, using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) to ensure robust assessments.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 3300 patients from the EUROFONTAN registry was conducted, with data collected from 21 European centers. The cohort included 3010 patients who underwent the ECC technique and 290 patients who underwent the LT technique. IPTW was used to balance baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were early and late mortality, Fontan failure, and adverse events. Secondary outcomes included postoperative complications and nonsurgical adverse events.
RESULTS: Propensity-matched analysis showed significantly better outcomes for ECC. Early mortality was lower for ECC (1.2% vs 3.9%, P = .003), whereas late mortality at 20-year follow-up was 8.6% in LT versus 3.2% in ECC after IPTW (P = .003). Patients who underwent the ECC technique experienced fewer postoperative complications (47% vs 66%, P = .025) and less frequent Fontan failure (12% vs 19%, P = .032). Kidney-related events were more frequent in patients who underwent the LT technique (3% vs 0.6%, P = .004). The development of arrhythmia initially appeared greater in the LT group but equalized after matching. Long-term complications, such as protein-losing enteropathy and hepatic issues, showed no significant differences.
CONCLUSIONS: ECC was associated with better early and intermediate outcomes than LT in this multicenter European registry. However, surgical era and hospital center explain a substantial part of the observed difference. Continued long-term surveillance of the Fontan pathway is essential to optimize lifelong outcomes.

Title: Waitlist mortality and post transplant survival amongst non-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation high-urgency heart transplant recipients before and after the 2018 policy change.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The adult heart allocation policy changed from a 3- to 6-tiered system in 2018, more precisely stratifying high-urgency patients. Many studies examined the effects on patients classified as Status 1 or those with implantable devices, especially extracorporeal membrane oxygentation (ECMO), however, few have analyzed other high-urgency cohorts. This study's purpose is to compare waitlist and midterm outcomes of non-ECMO high-urgency patients before and after the policy change.
METHODS: All high-risk (Status 1A, 1, 2, 3) non-ECMO adult patients listed for isolated heart transplantation were identified using the United Network for Organ Sharing database and split based on the October 18, 2018, policy change date into era 1 (7/2014-7/2018) and era 2 (1/2019-1/2023). Categorical and continuous variables were assessed using χ2 and t tests, respectively. Waitlist mortality was analyzed using competing risk regression whereas Kaplan-Meier curves assessed posttransplant survival.
RESULTS: Candidates from era 2 demonstrated greater rates of comorbidities like pulmonary hypertension (65% vs 67%, P = .007) and greater need for support with inotropes (39% vs 47%, P < .001) and intra-aortic balloon pump (12% vs 42%, P < .001). Yet, candidates from era 2 had significantly decreased waitlist time (71 vs 19 days, P < .001) and waitlist mortality (19% vs 7%, P < .001) whereas Kaplan-Meier 3-year survival (86% vs 85%, P = .42) remained similar.
CONCLUSIONS: Among non-ECMO high-urgency heart transplant recipients, candidates from era 2 demonstrated greater clinical acuity but improved waitlist mortality and equivalent midterm survival. These findings reassure that the 2018 policy change did not compromise outcomes amongst this high-urgency cohort, despite favoring patients bridged with ECMO.

Title: Quality of life after open descending thoracic and thoracoabdominal aortic repair: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To longitudinally evaluate health-related quality of life (HRQoL) following open descending thoracic or thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair, with validated patient-reported outcome measures.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients who underwent open descending thoracic or thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair between 2016 and 2023 were included. HRQoL was assessed preoperatively and at 3, 12, and 24 months postoperatively with the Short Form-12 physical component summary (PCS) and mental component summary (MCS) scores. Secondary quality-of-life scores were included as well. Additionally, complete-case analysis and the impact of baseline variables were assessed. Longitudinal changes were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: In total, 128 patients were included. PCS scores (95% CIs) decreased from 46.0 (44.1-48.0) preoperatively to 39.7 (37.6-41.7) at 3 months, with partial recovery to 42.2 (40.2-44.2) at 1 year and 41.0 (38.1-43.9) at 2 years (overall P < .001). MCS scores (95% CIs) decreased initially from 47.4 (44.9-49.8) to 44.3 (41.8-46.9) (3 months), with recovery to 49.2 (46.7-51.7) (1 year) and 48.4 (44.6-52.2) (2 years) (overall P = .01). Complete-case analysis showed comparable trajectories. Anxiety decreased and cognitive complaints increased but remained within normal ranges. No baseline variables were independently associated with PCS or MCS score trajectories.
CONCLUSIONS: Open descending thoracic and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair is associated with a sustained reduction in physical HRQoL, while mental HRQoL recovers. These findings underscore the multidimensional nature of recovery and the importance of integrating patient-reported outcomes into perioperative care.

Title: Prognostic Value of N-Terminal Pro-B-Type Natriuretic Peptide for Risk Stratification in Adults With Fontan Palliation.
Journal: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are limited data about the prognostic role of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in adults with Fontan palliation. The purpose of this study was to determine the correlates and the prognostic value of serial NT-proBNP assay for risk stratification in adults with Fontan palliation.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study of adults with Fontan palliation who had ≥1 NT-proBNP measurement in the outpatient clinic (2003-2023). In patients with ≥3 NT-proBNP measurements, serial NT-proBNP was calculated as the mean of the first 3 measurements. The study outcome was death/transplant.
RESULTS: Of 369 patients (age 27 ± 8 years; 55% male) with NT-proBNP, 214 (58%) had serial measurements. The baseline level was 217 (82, 562) pg/mL, whereas the serial value was 261 (98, 715) pg/mL. The correlates of higher NT-proBNP levels were older age, atriopulmonary connection, atrial fibrillation, hepatorenal dysfunction, systemic ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction, and higher Fontan pressures and pulmonary artery wedge pressure. Baseline and serial NT-proBNP levels were associated with death/transplant independent of anatomic indices, comorbidities, and hemodynamic indices. Serial NT-proBNP levels had superior prognostic value to single (baseline) NT-proBNP measurements, echocardiographic indices, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging indices, and cardiac catheterization indices.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings have important clinical implications in the management of adults with Fontan palliation because NT-proBNP assay is inexpensive, readily available, and noninvasive, and hence ideal for longitudinal assessment. Further studies are required to determine whether NT-proBNP can be used as a surrogate marker to monitor response to therapeutic interventions in this population.

Title: Psychological Impact of Fetal Echocardiography Referral on Pregnant Women With a Normal Routine Morphologic Ultrasound.
Journal: CJC pediatric and congenital heart disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal echocardiography (FE) is widely recommended in pregnancies at increased risk of congenital heart defects. Although FE is a safe diagnostic tool, its psychological impact on expectant pregnant women remains poorly understood.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study in 8 Canadian centers. Women aged ≥18 years with a normal second-trimester ultrasound between 18 and 26 weeks' gestation referred for an FE were compared with women who were not. Anxiety was assessed using the Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory. The primary outcome was the difference between state and trait anxiety (net situational anxiety) after morphologic ultrasound but before FE (T0). Secondary outcomes included the proportion of participants with significant anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory ≥40) and anxiety trajectories after FE among referred participants.
RESULTS: Eighty-four women were included, of whom 38 were referred for FE. At T0, women referred for FE showed slightly higher median net situational anxiety compared with controls. In multivariable analyses, FE referral was associated with a modest increase although estimates were imprecise. A higher proportion of referred women reached a state anxiety score ≥40, though this association was weak after adjustment. Among the 14 women who completed post-FE questionnaires, anxiety trajectories were heterogeneous, with both increases and decreases observed after FE.
CONCLUSIONS: Referral for FE after a normal second-trimester ultrasound is associated with a small and variable increase in maternal anxiety. These findings suggest that FE referral may not be psychologically neutral and highlight the importance of considering maternal psychological responses as referral criteria broaden.

Title: Clinical outcomes of primary Impella 5.5 versus transition from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in cardiogenic shock: A Spanish multicenter cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mechanical circulatory support strategies for cardiogenic shock have traditionally relied on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. However, newer high-flow ventricular support devices such as the Impella 5.5 device, capable of providing effective circulatory support, ventricular unloading, and early mobilization with fewer device-related complications, have begun to challenge the systematic use of an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-first approach. The clinical evolution of patients treated with the Impella 5.5 device and the impact of different support trajectories remain poorly characterized. We describe the clinical evolution of patients treated with the Impella 5.5 device according to initial support trajectory, distinguishing primary implantation from transition after venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
METHODS: This multicenter observational study included 114 consecutive patients with advanced heart failure or cardiogenic shock who underwent Impella 5.5 implantation in Spanish heart transplant centers. Patients were classified according to initial support trajectory: primary Impella 5.5 implantation (n = 72) or initial venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support followed by transition to Impella 5.5 (venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation to Impella 5.5 transition, n = 42). Baseline characteristics, clinical trajectories, complications, and in-hospital outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: All patients ultimately received Impella 5.5 device support. In-hospital mortality was 27.8% in the primary Impella group and 69.0% in the extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-Impella group (P < .001), with an overall mortality of 43.0%. Heart transplantation as definitive therapy was achieved in 76.4% and 31.0% of patients, respectively (P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: In transplant-oriented centers, outcomes among patients supported with the Impella 5.5 device appear to differ according to support trajectory. Primary implantation was associated with lower mortality and greater access to heart transplantation than transition from extracorporeal membrane oxygenation to the Impella 5.5 device.

Title: Diagnostic utility of transit time flow measurement for predicting early coronary bypass graft occlusion.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study objective was to evaluate the predictive value of intraoperative graft flow and pulsatility index for early in-hospital graft occlusion.
METHODS: We prospectively included 634 patients undergoing isolated coronary bypass grafting surgery between 2020 and 2025. To assess bypass flow, intraoperative transit-time flow measurements were performed. Graft patency was determined in all patients by coronary computed tomography angiography or coronary angiography at discharge. Receiver operating characteristic analysis using the Youden index identified optimal intraoperative flow and pulsatility index thresholds for predicting in-hospital graft occlusion. A logistic regression-based nomogram using flow and pulsatility index was constructed to estimate occlusion risk, and multilevel mixed-effects models were applied to assess independent predictors of graft failure.
RESULTS: The incidence of early graft occlusion was 7.9% (n = 50) and associated with female sex, hypercholesterolemia, longer surgery, reoperations, and prolonged hospital stay. Venous grafts were associated with higher occlusion rates at the patient level (6.5% vs 3.0%, P = .004), with a similar trend observed at the graft level (3.1% vs 1.8%, P = .07). In conduit-specific analysis, every 10 mL/min increase in venous graft flow was associated with a 38% reduction in occlusion (odds ratio, 0.62; P < .001), whereas arterial grafts showed no such association with intraoperative flow or the pulsatility index. Optimal prognostic thresholds for venous grafts were identified at a mean flow less than 50 mL/min and a pulsatility index greater than 1.7.
CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of early graft occlusion is significantly higher in venous conduits. Occlusion is associated with intraoperative graft flow, whereas no statistically significant relationship with these parameters was detectable in arterial grafts in this cohort.

Title: Aortic valve repair versus biological replacement for aortic regurgitation with or without ascending aortic aneurysm: Heart Valve Society Aortic Valve Database Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the long-term outcomes of aortic valve repair (AVr) (REPAIR group) with biological aortic valve replacement (bAVR group).
METHODS: Adults who underwent REPAIR or bAVR for aortic regurgitation (AR) +/- ascending aortic aneurysm (AscAA), recorded in the Heart Valve Society database until April 2024, were included. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for confounders. Differences in long-term survival, major adverse valve-related events (MAVRE), and other valve-related events were assessed.
RESULTS: In total, 7318 patients were included (REPAIR n = 6773, bAVR n = 545). Propensity score matching resulted in 1006 REPAIR patients matched to 530 bAVR patients (median age: 67 years [interquartile range, 59.0-73.0], 22% female). In the matched cohort, early mortality (≤30 days) was comparable between REPAIR and bAVR patients (1.2% vs 2.1%, P = .070). At 7.5 years, overall matched survival was lower in the bAVR group compared to the REPAIR group (73.9% [95% CI, 66.5%-82.1%] vs 85.6% [95% CI, 82.3%-89.3%], P < .001), with a higher proportion of valve-related deaths (bAVR 4.2% vs REPAIR 1.2%, P < .001). At 7.5 years, patients with bAVR had significantly lower freedom from MAVRE (P < .001) and more infective endocarditis (P = .006), and severe valve dysfunction (P < .001) compared to patients with REPAIR. The incidences of aortic valve reintervention (P = .388) and pacemaker implantation (P = .671) were comparable.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients in whom repair was deemed feasible and surgery was performed at mainly expert centers, repair was associated with more favorable long-term outcomes, including improved survival, compared with bAVR in an older propensity-matched cohort. These findings support the consideration of AVr when technically feasible in patients with AR, with or without AscAA.

Title: Tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/pulmonary vascular resistance index predicts right ventricular assist device requirement and mortality after magnetically levitated centrifugal-flow left ventricular assist device implantation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Right ventricular failure remains a major cause of perioperative morbidity and early mortality after left ventricular assist device implantation. We evaluated whether a novel and readily available echocardiographic-hemodynamic surrogate of right ventricular pulmonary vascular coupling predicts right ventricular assist device requirement and survival after magnetically levitated centrifugal flow left ventricular assist device.
METHODS: We performed a multicenter retrospective study of 202 HeartMate 3 recipients with preoperative right ventricular dysfunction. The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and pulmonary vascular resistance index ratio was derived. The primary end point was assessing its capacity to prognosticate the right ventricular assist device need in comparison with other established indices of right ventricular dysfunction. Multivariable logistic regression, calibration analysis, bootstrap validation, cross-validation, incremental-value modeling, and sensitivity analyses excluding venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and mechanically ventilated patients were performed. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses.
RESULTS: The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and pulmonary vascular resistance index ratio demonstrated strong discrimination for right ventricular assist device requirement and outperformed conventional predictors. Bootstrap validation confirmed model stability, and cross-validation demonstrated consistent discrimination. Sensitivity analysis showed that discrimination remained robust after excluding venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and mechanically ventilated patients. Multivariable logistic regression showed that the tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and pulmonary vascular resistance index ratio remained independently associated with overall 1-year survival age, body mass index, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes. Discrimination remained robust after excluding venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation placement before the left ventricular assist device. A tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and pulmonary vascular resistance index ratio threshold of 0.9 was able to stratify patient survival at 30 days, 100 days, and 1 year after left ventricular assist device placement.
CONCLUSIONS: The tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and pulmonary vascular resistance index ratio improves prediction of right ventricular assist device requirement and survival after HeartMate 3 implantation and may enhance perioperative right ventricular risk stratification.

Title: Influence of concomitant mitral valve intervention on late survival in patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing surgical revascularization.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation, the influence of concomitant mitral valve (MV) intervention at the time of revascularization on late survival remains unclear. The purpose of this study was to compare the lifetime survival of patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation who underwent revascularization alone versus concomitant MV repair or replacement.
METHODS: Retrospective review was performed for 776 consecutive patients, ages 65 years and older with coronary artery disease and moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation who underwent isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) (n = 372), CABG with MV repair (n = 131, CABG + MV repair), or CABG with MV replacement (n = 273, CABG + MV replacement) from 1976 to 2005. Propensity score matching, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox regression were used to compare perioperative and long-term survival. Cross-sectional follow-up utilized the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Death Index as well as government and genealogical internet sites, publicly available online obituaries, and death notices. Follow up was 98% complete.
RESULTS: The mean age of the cohort was 74.1 ± 5.8 years with 42.4% female patients. Preoperatively, 54.5% had prior myocardial infarction, 47.7% had a history of congestive heart failure, and 69.1% had an abnormal ejection fraction. Matched patients undergoing CABG or CABG + MV repair had similar incidence of major perioperative morbidity (29.0% vs 22.1%; P = .202) and operative mortality (8.4% vs 6.1%; P = .475). Late survival was similar between groups (P = .630). Among matched patients undergoing CABG versus CABG + MV replacement, those undergoing concomitant replacement had significantly increased perioperative major morbidity (35.2% vs 20.9%; P < .001) and operative mortality (16.9% vs 7.7%; P < .001). CABG + MV replacement patients experienced an increased risk of late mortality (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.01-1.49; P = .035), compared with those undergoing isolated CABG.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with moderate ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing surgical revascularization, concomitant MV repair did not demonstrate a clear late survival benefit over isolated CABG, whereas concomitant MV replacement was associated with increased early and late mortality risk.

Title: Minimally invasive mitral surgery in patients with high pulmonary artery pressure: Results of a multicenter observational study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary hypertension is diagnosed in 40% to 75% of patients affected by mitral valve diseases. Little is known regarding outcomes of patients with pulmonary hypertension undergoing mitral valve oeprations through minimally invasive approaches. This study compares the characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of patients undergoing minimally invasive mitral valve surgery, stratified by systolic pulmonary artery pressure.
METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective, prospective, observational study included adults undergoing mitral valve operations through a right minithoracotomy with or without tricuspid valve surgery and atrial fibrillation ablation between 2020 and 2024. Comparisons were performed between patients with systolic pulmonary artery pressure less than 31 mm Hg, systolic pulmonary artery pressure 31 to 55 mm Hg, and systolic pulmonary artery pressure more than 55 mm Hg based on European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II cutoffs for systolic pulmonary artery pressure categories.
RESULTS: This analysis included 1121 patients (female, 47.5%; median age, 69 years, interquartile range, 59-77). Median systolic pulmonary artery pressure was 38 mm Hg (interquartile range, 30-50; systolic pulmonary artery pressure <31 mm Hg: n = 307, 27.4%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure 31-55 mm Hg: n = 152, 55.3%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure >55 mm Hg: n = 194, 17.3%). Patients with higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure were older, mainly female, and characterized by more comorbidities including atrial fibrillation and renal disease. A critical perioperative state was diagnosed in 12% of patients with systolic pulmonary artery pressure more than 55 mm Hg (P < .001). Patients with higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure more frequently underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid annuloplasty and experienced more postoperative dialysis and pacemaker implantation but comparable rates of conversions to sternotomy, respiratory and bleeding complications, and in-hospital mortality (systolic pulmonary artery pressure <31 mm Hg: n = 3, 1%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure 31-55 mm Hg: n = 6, 1%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure >55 mm Hg: n = 5, 2.6%; P = .222) compared with patients with lower systolic pulmonary artery pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite a higher preoperative complexity, patients with high systolic pulmonary artery pressure could be considered for minimally invasive mitral valve surgery with acceptable rates of major intraoperative or postoperative complications regardless of their systolic pulmonary artery pressure values.

Title: Challenges in monitoring and titration of argatroban versus unfractionated heparin in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Anticoagulation during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) remains challenging. Direct thrombin inhibitors such as argatroban are increasingly proposed as alternatives to unfractionated heparin (UFH). We sought to characterize the dose titration and monitoring reliability of argatroban compared with UFH in adult patients who received ECMO.
METHODS: This prespecified subanalysis of a randomized controlled pilot trial (2021-2024) included 40 adults on venovenous or venoarterial ECMO randomized to argatroban (target diluted thrombin time 0.6-0.8 μg/mL; n = 20) or UFH (target anti-factor Xa 0.2-0.3 IU/mL; n = 20). The primary outcome was the pooled proportion of measurements within the therapeutic target range. Secondary outcomes included dose requirements, time to target, dose-assay correlations, and platelet count trajectories.
RESULTS: Patients who were treated with argatroban achieved therapeutic targets significantly less often than those receiving UFH (38% vs 51% of pooled active measurements; P < .001). The median argatroban dose required to reach the initial target was 0.40 μg/kg/min (interquartile range, 0.34-0.49). Correlations between anticoagulant dose and monitored effect were weak-to-moderate for both agents (repeated measures correlation coefficient = 0.29 for argatroban vs diluted thrombin time, and repeated measures correlation coefficient = 0.31 for UFH vs anti-Xa). Both groups experienced a comparable decrease in platelet counts.
CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating subanalysis, patients receiving argatroban achieved therapeutic targets less reliably than those receiving UFH. However, this variability likely reflects challenges in dosing strategy optimization and differing target stringencies rather than intrinsic pharmacokinetic instability of the drug.

Title: Neurocognitive dysfunction among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery-A prospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neurocognitive dysfunction (NCD) remains a common complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, the trajectory of cognitive recovery and associated risk factors remain incompletely understood. This study evaluated the prevalence, early postoperative course, and predictors of NCD among patients undergoing elective CABG.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 110 consecutive patients undergoing elective CABG between January 2025 and August 2025 at a tertiary care center were enrolled. Neurocognitive function was assessed using Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III preoperatively, at hospital discharge, and at postoperative day 10 follow-up. Changes in cognitive performance were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Transitions in categorical cognitive status were evaluated using the McNemar-Bowker test. Associations between patient characteristics and NCD were examined using multivariable analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 110 patients undergoing CABG were included in the study, with a mean age of 57.5 ± 8.5 years; 79.1% were male, and 85.5% underwent off-pump CABG. Mean Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III scores declined significantly from baseline (77.0 ± 9.1) to discharge (73.8 ± 9.9), followed by recovery at follow-up (77.1 ± 10.0) (P < .001). Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons demonstrated a significant decline from baseline to discharge (mean difference -3.2; 95% CI, -4.8 to -1.6; P = .001) and a significant improvement from discharge to follow-up (mean difference +3.3; 95% CI, 1.7-4.9; P = .001), whereas baseline and follow-up scores did not differ significantly (mean difference +0.1; 95% CI, -1.5 to 1.7; P = .865). NCD was present in 68.2% of patients preoperatively, increased to 80.0% at discharge, and decreased to 64.5% at follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified increasing age as independently associated with NCD at follow-up (adjusted odds ratio, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.14; P = .007).
CONCLUSIONS: In this group of patients undergoing CABG, cognitive impairment was often seen before surgery. There was a temporary decline right after the operation, followed by partial recovery by the early follow-up. The link between older age and early postoperative cognitive issues indicates that older patients may benefit from cognitive screening around the time of surgery. More research is needed to look at long-term cognitive changes and the effectiveness of specific interventions.

Title: Tricuspid aortic valve morphology predicts favorable midterm outcomes after aortic valve neocuspidization in children.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the midterm outcomes of the aortic valve neocuspidalization (AVNeo) procedure for aortic valve reconstruction in 83 pediatric patients with complex aortic valve disease and to identify risk factors associated with the outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on pediatric patients who underwent the AVNeo procedure between January 2017 and June 2025. The composite primary end point included all-cause mortality, reoperation, or moderate-to-severe aortic valve dysfunction (regurgitation or stenosis). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify risk factors.
RESULTS: Among the 83 patients (mean age 7.0 ± 3.7 years; 67.5% male) included in the analysis, the predominant preoperative pathology was moderate-to-severe aortic regurgitation (88.0%). Single-leaflet reconstruction (65.1%) using autologous pericardium (94.0%) was the most common surgical approach. Over a mean follow-up of 28.4 ± 23.9 months, 27 patients (32.5%) met the composite end point, including 2 late deaths, 18 cases of moderate-to-severe regurgitation, and 9 cases of moderate-to-severe stenosis; 10 patients underwent reoperation. The probability of freedom from the primary end point was 83.6%, 64.5%, and 54.4% at 1, 3, and 6 years, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified tricuspid aortic valve morphology as an independent protective factor against the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.408; 95% CI, 0.178-0.935, P = .034), whereas the use of autologous pericardium showed a strong protective trend (hazard ratio, 0.284; 95% CI, 0.078-1.037, P = .057).
CONCLUSIONS: AVNeo provides midterm outcomes that support its use as an alternative strategy. Tricuspid aortic valve morphology is a strong predictor of favorable outcomes, and the use of autologous pericardium demonstrates significant potential as a protective factor.

Title: Training pathway and early career trajectories in cardiothoracic surgery: A national cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study objective was to compare educational outcomes and early career practice patterns of cardiothoracic surgery graduates by training pathway: direct entry through the integrated thoracic surgery residency and the independent fellowship pathways comprising fast-track entry and the 2- and 3-year fellowship programs.
METHODS: We assembled a national cohort of graduates from Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education-accredited integrated thoracic surgery residencies and independent cardiothoracic surgery fellowships between 2013 and 2023. Graduates were identified using institutional alumni resources and self-identification in the Doximity Residency Navigator. Demographic, educational, and professional characteristics were abstracted from institutional websites, advertised professional profiles, and state and national provider databases.
RESULTS: Women were most represented among integrated thoracic surgery residency and fast-track graduates, whereas international medical graduates and osteopathic physicians were more common among 2- and 3-year independent graduates. Independent graduates had higher odds of thoracic subspecialization, but lower odds of adult cardiac subspecialization compared with integrated thoracic surgery residency graduates. Fast-track and 3-year independent graduates had similar odds of congenital cardiac subspecialization compared with integrated thoracic surgery graduates, whereas 2-year independent graduates had lower odds. Among adult subspecialists, only 3-year independent graduates had lower odds of superfellowship completion compared with integrated thoracic surgery residency graduates. Integrated thoracic surgery residency graduates completed fewer postgraduate training years than all independent-pathway groups regardless of subspecialization. Within subspecialties, integrated thoracic surgery and independent graduates had similar odds of entering academic practice.
CONCLUSIONS: Integrated thoracic surgery residency and independent pathways have attracted trainees with distinct demographic, educational, and subspecialization patterns. After accounting for subspecialization, graduates achieve comparable early career outcomes. Maintaining multiple entry pathways broadens access to cardiothoracic surgery and supports workforce diversity.

Title: Pericardial fluid cardiac troponin I predicts postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) is a sensitive biomarker of myocardial injury. We hypothesized that cTnI measured in pericardial drainage fluid (PCF), which reflects the cardiac microenvironment, may enhance risk stratification for postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after coronary artery bypass grafting.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 114 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting were enrolled. The primary end point was new-onset POAF within 7 days postoperatively. Blood and PCF cTnI at 6 hours postoperatively were measured. Variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and were then incorporated into multivariable logistic regression to construct a predictive model. A simplified risk score (CALT score) was developed. Model performance was compared with existing POAF tools, including the POAF score, CHA2DS2-VASc, and the atrial fibrillation risk index.
RESULTS: POAF occurred in 30.7% of the cohort. Postoperative 6-hour PCF-cTnI was an independent predictor of POAF (odds ratio, 5.502; 95% CI, 1.887-16.045; P = .002) and significantly enhanced continuous net reclassification improvement (0.562; 95% CI, 0.189-0.921; P = .002). The CALT score comprised left circumflex artery lesions, left atrial diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, postoperative 0-hour serum calcium, and postoperative 6-hour PCF-cTnI. The PCF-cTnI-based model demonstrated good discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.821), with favorable calibration and clinical utility. Compared with commonly used risk scores, the CALT score exhibited superior discrimination and calibration.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides novel evidence that PCF-cTnI is a strong predictor of POAF. The CALT score, integrating PCF-cTnI with clinical factors, provided superior predictive performance by capturing both the vulnerable atrial substrate and localized myocardial injury.

Title: Long-term outcomes of transcatheter versus surgical aortic valve replacement in patients aged 70 years and older: An overlap-weighted analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare long-term outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 70 to 89 years with aortic stenosis (AS).
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 1100 patients who underwent primary TAVR (n = 599) or SAVR (n = 501) between 2008 and 2023 were included. An overlap-weighted propensity-score analysis was conducted using 36 baseline variables, including age, procedural year, frailty scale, Society of Thoracic Surgeons risk score, New York Heart Association class, history of coronary artery and cerebrovascular disease, and AS severity. The primary end point was the composite of all-cause mortality or cerebrovascular events.
RESULTS: During long-term follow-up, the composite end point occurred more frequently after TAVR than after SAVR. In the overlap-weighted analysis, TAVR was associated with a greater risk of the composite outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 1.8; 95% CI, 1.1-3.0; P = .024), with Kaplan-Meier curves diverging early and remaining separated. All-cause mortality did not differ between the groups (HR, 1.2; 95% CI, 0.7-2.1; P = .426); however, cerebrovascular events occurred predominantly after TAVR and remained significantly more frequent after overlap weighting (HR, 15; 95% CI, 2.8-89; P = .002).
CONCLUSIONS: In the overlap-weighted population of patients aged 70 to 89 years with AS, SAVR and TAVR were associated with comparable all-cause mortality; however, cerebrovascular events occurred more frequently after TAVR.

Title: Evaluating preoperative imaging in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension: Is computed tomography pulmonary angiography a reliable alternative to pulmonary angiography?
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension is a potentially curable form of pulmonary hypertension, with pulmonary endarterectomy serving as a key surgical treatment option. Accurate preoperative imaging is critical for determining surgical candidacy and optimizing operative outcomes. Although digital subtraction pulmonary angiography remains the gold standard, computed tomography pulmonary angiography has emerged as a noninvasive alternative. This study compares the concordance of computed tomography pulmonary angiography and digital subtraction pulmonary angiography with intraoperative specimen findings to determine their diagnostic accuracy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent pulmonary endarterectomy for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension at a single Canadian center between 2014 and 2017. All patients underwent preoperative computed tomography pulmonary angiography and digital subtraction pulmonary angiography as part of their routine evaluation. Imaging findings were compared with operative findings using a territory-based anatomic assessment across major pulmonary artery segments. Functional and hemodynamic outcomes were also assessed before and after surgery.
RESULTS: Seventeen patients (mean age 52.8 years [±3.7]; 53% female) were included. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography demonstrated greater agreement with operative findings in the right main pulmonary artery, left upper lobe, and lingula. Digital subtraction pulmonary angiography demonstrated greater agreement in the right upper lobe, whereas both modalities showed similar agreement in the left main pulmonary artery and left lower lobe. Patients experienced postoperative improvements in New York Heart Association functional class, pulmonary artery pressures, and cardiac index. Despite overall agreement between imaging and operative findings, discrepancies persisted across several vascular territories.
CONCLUSIONS: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography demonstrated substantial agreement with operative findings in central and lobar pulmonary arterial territories, supporting its role as an important frontline imaging modality in the evaluation of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. However, persistent discrepancies between imaging and operative assessment, particularly in more distal territories, support the continued use of a multimodal approach integrating computed tomography pulmonary angiography, digital subtraction pulmonary angiography, hemodynamic assessment, and multidisciplinary evaluation when determining operability and treatment strategy.

Title: Weekend effect on operative mortality following coronary artery bypass grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) late in the workweek or on weekends experience excess mortality remains controversial.
METHODS: Medicare beneficiaries undergoing isolated CABG from 2008 to 2019 were stratified by day of surgery (DOS; Monday-Sunday). A flexible parametric model adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, surgeon/hospital volume, and procedural details was used to evaluate whether CABG-DOS was associated with 30-day mortality. Regression standardization was applied to estimate standardized survival probabilities (SSPs). SSPs for CABG performed on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday were compared to those for CABG performed on Monday to Thursday in the overall cohort and within cohorts defined by admission urgency (proxy for surgical urgency).
RESULTS: Among 735,603 beneficiaries undergoing CABG, surgery was performed on Friday in 144,220 (19.6%), Saturday in 18,568 (2.5%), and Sunday in 11,502 (1.6%). From Monday to Friday, approximately 50% of CABGs were elective; elective CABG composed 30% of Saturday cases and 22% of Sunday cases. Risk-adjusted 30-day SSPs were similar for CABGs performed on Monday to Thursday (97.0%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 96.9%-97.1%) and Friday (97.1%; 95% CI, 97.0%-97.2%) but were lower for CABGs performed on Saturday (96.2%; 95% CI, 95.9%-96.4%) and Sunday (95.4%; 95% CI, 95.0%-95.7%). A weekend effect on mortality was persistent across all admission urgency levels.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with weekday operations, weekend CABG was associated with 1 to 2 excess mortalities per 100 procedures. These findings suggest that environmental factors specific to DOS, unique to weekends, and present regardless of case urgency may adversely impact early post-CABG survival.

Title: Sex-specific impact of computed tomography-defined sarcopenia on postoperative complications following elective cardiac surgery in older patients.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sex-specific differences in sarcopenia-related prognosis after cardiac surgery are unclear. We aimed to investigate the association between preoperative computed tomography-defined sarcopenia and postoperative complications in older patients undergoing elective cardiac surgeries, focusing on sex-specific differences.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 133 patients aged 65 years or more who underwent elective open surgeries. Sarcopenia was assessed using the psoas muscle area index derived from preoperative computed tomography scans and defined using sex-specific cutoff values. The primary outcome was postoperative complication.
RESULTS: Forty-nine patients (36.8%) had sarcopenia. Although the incidence of complications was higher in this group, the difference was not statistically significant between the groups. Multivariate logistic regression analysis excluding patients with preexisting atrial fibrillation revealed that sarcopenia was independently associated with a higher risk of postoperative complications (odds ratio, 3.73, 95% CI, 1.49-9.84, P = .006). The male patients with sarcopenia showed a higher incidence of complications versus those without (56.8% vs 33.9%, P = .046), whereas no association was observed in the female patients. Sex-stratified analyses confirmed the independent prognostic value of sarcopenia in male patients only (odds ratio, 2.52, 95% CI, 1.08-6.01, P = .033).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative computed tomography-defined sarcopenia was independently associated with postoperative complications in older male patients undergoing elective cardiac surgeries, but not in female patients. These findings suggest that the prognostic significance of sarcopenia is sex-specific and highlight the importance of sex-specific risk stratification strategies in older patient populations undergoing cardiac surgeries.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Diagnosis of Coronary Heart Disease with Clinical and Biomarker Data.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a common condition associated with high disability and mortality. Although coronary angiography (CAG) remains the gold standard for diagnosis, its accessibility is limited in medically underserved regions or for patients who are ineligible for the procedure. The aim of this study was to develop a prediction model using machine learning algorithms that integrate clinical data and plasma biomarkers for timely and noninvasive CHD diagnosis.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 191 patients who underwent CAG at the First Affiliated Hospital of Henan University between March and October 2023, comprising 151 CHD patients and 40 non-CHD controls, were included. Clinical data and plasma samples were collected; the levels of eight biomarkers (LPA, MCP-1, TNF-α, IL-1β, NRG4, S100A8/A9, HMGB1, and cfDNA) were measured by ELISAs and fluorescence spectrophotometry. The dataset was split into training, test, and validation sets (8:1:1) and standardized. After the SMOTE was applied to the training set, key features were selected via recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV). Six machine learning algorithms were used to construct the models, and their performance was evaluated on the test set and via 10-fold cross-validation. SHAP was used to interpret the optimal model.
RESULTS: Eight important features were identified. Among the six models, the KNN model performed best on the test set, achieving an AUROC of 80.7%, accuracy of 82.7%, F1‑score of 89.5%, precision of 86.4%, and sensitivity of 92.7%.
CONCLUSION: A machine learning model integrating clinical and plasma biomarker data has potential for predicting CHD in patients who present with chest discomfort, offering a potential diagnostic aid when CAG is not readily accessible, pending validation in larger, multicenter studies. However, these findings are based on a single-center cohort of 191 patients and require external validation in larger, multicenter populations.

Title: Associations of reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent with erythrocyte indices and serum ferritin in anemic patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A retrospective study.
Abstract: Cancer-related anemia is common in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and its pathogenesis is complex due to the coexistence of chronic liver disease, portal hypertension, hypersplenism, inflammation, nutritional disorders and tumor-related factors. The present retrospective study characterized anemia morphology in 96 anemic patients with HCC before initiation of their first antitumor therapy, and examined the associations of reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (RET-He) with erythrocyte indices and serum ferritin (SF), with a focus on whether RET-He and SF displayed distinct patterns of association with hematological parameters. The data collected included sex, age, Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage, Child-Pugh grade, splenomegaly/hypersplenism, hemoglobin (Hb) concentration, mean corpuscular volume (MCV), mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH), MCH concentration (MCHC), absolute reticulocyte count (RET#), RET-He and SF. Patients were compared by anemia severity, morphological type and RET-He level, and Spearman'a correlation was used to assess relationships between RET-He and other parameters. Mild, moderate and severe anemia occurred in 41 (42.71%), 52 (54.17%) and 3 (3.13%) patients, respectively. Macrocytic, normocytic, simple microcytic and microcytic hypochromic anemia were found in 29 (30.21%), 40 (41.67%), 5 (5.21%) and 22 (22.92%) patients, respectively. A total of 26 patients (27.08%) had RET-He ≤29 pg, and the median SF was 248.5 ng/ml (interquartile range, 146.8-346.0 ng/ml). Compared with mild anemia, moderate-to-severe anemia was associated with lower MCV, MCH, MCHC and RET-He, and higher proportions of RET-He ≤29 pg and microcytic hypochromic anemia (all P<0.05). RET-He was lowest in the microcytic group (P<0.001). Patients with RET-He ≤29 pg had lower Hb concentration, MCV, MCH, MCHC and RET# (all P<0.05). Spearman's analysis indicated that RET-He was positively correlated with Hb concentration, MCV, MCH, MCHC and RET# (all P<0.05), but not with SF (P=0.408). In conclusion, anemia in patients with HCC demonstrated heterogeneous morphological patterns, and microcytic anemia was associated with lower RET-He levels. RET-He was associated with erythrocyte indices related to hemoglobinization, whereas no such association was observed with SF. The dissociation between RET-He and SF suggests that these markers may reflect different aspects of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis in HCC. RET-He may offer complementary information on erythroid hemoglobinization not directly captured by SF, but its clinical utility requires further validation. SF should be interpreted cautiously in the context of chronic liver disease, inflammation and tumor-related factors.

Title: Specialist-led community-based cardio-kidney-metabolic-pulmonary care in high-risk individuals: multi-centre pragmatic prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: Pharmacological therapies that treat cardiovascular, kidney, metabolic, and pulmonary (CKMP) risk factors reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events, but community-dwelling individuals may not receive all treatments to which they are eligible from non-specialists. This trial investigated if specialist-led care in the community increases the utilization of CKMP pharmacological interventions compared with usual care.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This pragmatic prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint trial included community-dwelling high-risk adults aged ≥30 years from 15 primary care sites in England. Participants were randomized 1:1 to an intervention of two clinic appointments (at baseline and ∼3 months) with a cardiology specialist at their primary care site to review and optimize CKMP risk factors in accordance with UK guidelines, or usual care. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with initiation and/or increase in the dose of guideline-directed CKMP pharmacological therapies at 6 months after date of randomization. Between March 2025 and July 2025, 138 participants were randomized (68 intervention, 70 control); the median age was 76.6 years, and 52.9% were women. At 6 months after randomization, in the intervention arm, 42 of 68 (61.8%) patients received a CKMP pharmacological intervention compared with 16 of 70 patients (22.9%) in the control arm (odds ratio 5.4, 95% CI 2.5-12.3, P < 0.0001, absolute risk difference 38.9%, 95% CI 23.7-54.1%).
CONCLUSION: Specialist-led care in the community for high-risk individuals increased the use of pharmacological interventions for CKMP risk factors compared to usual care.

Title: The lactate-to-albumin ratio as a novel predictor for post-stroke epilepsy: insights from a large cohort.
Abstract: Ischaemic stroke (IS) represents a leading cause of adult mortality and long-term disability globally, and post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) constitutes a severe complication that worsens neurological recovery and reduces quality of life, yet reliable early predictive biomarkers remain insufficient. The serum lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR, mmol/g), an integrated indicator reflecting hypoxic-ischaemic stress, energy metabolic disturbance, and systemic inflammation, has emerged as a promising prognostic marker but has not been investigated for predicting PSE risk. This multicentre retrospective cohort study enrolled 21 459 acute IS patients from four centres to examine the association between admission LAR and 1-year PSE incidence. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, subgroup stratification, and sensitivity testing were applied for statistical evaluation. Overall, 936 patients (4.36%) developed PSE within one year. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit increment in LAR was associated with an odds ratio (OR) of 1.13 (95% CI: 1.04-1.22, P = 0.003) for PSE. Compared with the lowest LAR quartile (Q1), the highest quartile (Q4) conferred a markedly elevated risk (OR = 12.02, 95% CI: 7.91-18.90, P < 0.001), with a significant non-linear dose-response relationship and an inflection point at LAR = 0.06. The association was stronger in patients with atrial fibrillation or cortical stroke lesions, and sensitivity analyses confirmed result robustness. Taken together, these data indicate that serum LAR measured at admission behaves as an independent, non-linear correlate of PSE risk after acute IS. As a readily available biomarker derived from routine serum laboratory tests, LAR may serve as a promising candidate for early risk stratification in IS patients, although prospective studies are warranted to confirm its clinical utility.

Title: Comparative Performance of Oxygenation Indices for Mortality Prediction in Patients With Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome at a Tertiary Care Intensive Care Unit in Bangladesh.
Abstract: Background Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a syndrome of acute inflammatory lung injury and impaired gas exchange, not hypoxemia alone, and carries high mortality. This study compared the discrimination of the partial pressure of arterial oxygen (PaO₂)/fraction of inspired oxygen (FiO₂) (PF) ratio, oxygenation index (OI), and oxygen saturation index (OSI), measured on the day of ARDS diagnosis, for intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in a Bangladeshi tertiary ICU. Methods This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 80 consecutive adults meeting the 2012 Berlin definition of ARDS and requiring invasive mechanical ventilation at Bangladesh Medical University between June 2024 and May 2025. Time zero (day 1) was the day the Berlin criteria were first met. Indices were calculated on days 1, 3, and 7 from simultaneous blood gas, oximetry, and ventilator data. Groups were compared by independent t- and chi-square tests, serial change by paired t-tests in survivors only, and discrimination by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with Youden cutoffs. Correlated areas under the curve (AUCs) were not formally compared, and no multivariable model was fitted. Results Forty-five of 80 patients (56.3%) died in the ICU, and 35 (43.8%) survived. Non-survivors had lower blood pressure, higher heart and respiratory rates, and greater ventilatory requirements (p<0.05). OI and OSI were higher and the PF ratio was lower among non-survivors (p<0.05). Discrimination was numerically highest for OSI (AUC=0.879; 95% CI: 0.786-0.977), followed by OI (AUC=0.867; 95% CI: 0.788-0.963) and the PF ratio (AUC=0.731; 95% CI: 0.612-0.881); as the intervals overlapped and no paired test was applied, this ordering is descriptive only. Specificity was 91.4% for both OSI and OI, and accuracy was 86.3% and 83.8% versus 70% for the PF ratio. Serial improvement among survivors was not statistically significant. Conclusions OI and OSI were higher among non-survivors and showed numerically higher discrimination for ICU mortality than the PF ratio, with OSI performing best. As the analysis was univariable and cutoffs were internally derived, these findings indicate discrimination and association rather than independent prognostic value, and the thresholds are exploratory. Larger multicenter studies with formal paired comparison of ROC curves, multivariable adjustment, and independent validation are warranted.

Title: Time to Discontinuation and Risk Factors for Outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy in Primary Care: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using Survival Analysis.
Journal: Journal of general and family medicine
Abstract:
