Title: Nonlinear association between perceived social support and fear of disease progression in stroke patients: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the nonlinear association between perceived social support and fear of disease progression in stroke patients.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 300 patients with stroke completed a general information questionnaire, the Fear of Progression Questionnaire-Short Form (FoP-Q-SF), the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS), and the Modified Barthel Index (MBI). Independent-samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, hierarchical linear regression, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis were used.
RESULTS: The mean FoP score was 30.34 ± 8.56. In the hierarchical regression model, higher PSS was associated with lower FoP (B = -0.223, P < 0.001). Compared with employed participants, unemployed participants had lower FoP scores (B = -3.188, P = 0.008), and severe ADL dependence was associated with higher FoP compared with independence (B = 4.921, P = 0.035). The restricted cubic spline analysis indicated evidence of nonlinearity (P foroverall < 0.001; P for nonlinear = 0.023). Exploratory piecewise linear regression identified an estimated change point at a PSS score of 67 (P = 0.011). Below 67, each one-point increase in PSS was associated with a 0.319-point lower FoP score (B = -0.319, 95% CI -0.396 to -0.241; P < 0.001). At PSS scores ≥ 67, the slope was not statistically significant and was imprecisely estimated (B = 0.304, 95% CI -0.142 to 0.751; P = 0.182).
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggested a nonlinear association between perceived social support and fear of disease progression, with a change point at a perceived social support score of 67. However, this change point requires validation in larger multicenter and prospective studies. In addition, unemployed and severely dependent were independently associated with fear of disease progression. These findings may help guide more comprehensive psychosocial assessment for stroke patients at risk of fear of disease progression.

Title: The predictive model of intra-arrest blood markers for the sustained return of spontaneous circulation in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of intra-arrest blood markers, including blood routine, blood biochemistry, and coagulation profile, during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for the return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of patients who experienced OHCA and admitted to the emergency department of a tertiary hospital in Zhejiang Province, China, between January 2021 and December 2025 was assembled. Their clinical and demographic data were collected, and missing values were addressed using multiple imputation. Physiologic laboratory markers obtained during resuscitation were compared between the sustained ROSC and non-ROSC groups. Candidate predictors were selected based on clinical relevance, previous literature, availability at the intended prediction time point, and univariable screening, with age and gender retained as prespecified demographic covariates. Model discrimination for the prediction of sustained ROSC was evaluated using a receiver operating characteristic analysis and the area under the curve (AUC). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling to assess model stability and quantify potential overfitting.
RESULTS: A total of 283 patients were included, and among them, 94 (33.22%) achieved sustained ROSC. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation (m = 20). In univariable analyses, the sustained ROSC group had higher PCO2, platelet count, white blood cell count, and absolute lymphocyte count; higher admission glucose, fibrinogen, and serum calcium levels; shorter chest compression duration and prothrombin time; and lower epinephrine dose, serum potassium level, and international normalized ratio than the non-sustained ROSC group (all P < 0.05). A multivariable logistic regression model incorporating age; gender; white blood cell count; platelet count; blood PCO2 measured during CPR; capillary blood glucose level on admission; and fibrinogen, serum potassium, and serum calcium levels yielded a mean apparent AUC of 0.832 across the imputed datasets. After internal validation with 500 bootstrap resamples, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.807 and the bootstrap-derived calibration slope was 0.853. The final model is given as follows: logit[P(ROSC=1)] = -2.65-0.002 × age-0.790 × gender + 0.076 × white blood cell count + 0.001 × platelet count + 0.010 × PCO2-0.011 × admission glucose + 0.145 × fibrinogen-0.247 × serum potassium+0.633 × serum calcium.
CONCLUSION: In patients who experienced OHCA, higher white blood cell count and lower serum potassium levels were associated with a higher incidence of sustained ROSC. Female patients were more likely to achieve sustained ROSC than male patients. Although the model showed certain predictive value for sustained ROSC, further multicenter, large-scale studies are needed in the future.

Title: High-sensitivity troponin T as a predictor of cardiovascular events in colorectal cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: results of the COLOVASC prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy is associated with cardiovascular events in patients with colorectal cancer, yet validated tools for pre-treatment cardiovascular risk stratification are lacking. Cardiac biomarkers are not routinely incorporated into baseline assessment and prospective evidence supporting their use remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to determine whether baseline high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) provides prognostic information for major adverse cardiovascular events during chemotherapy in patients with colorectal cancer.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Within a prospective single-center observational cohort study at the Department of Internal Medicine and Hematology, Semmelweis University, consecutive patients with histologically confirmed newly diagnosed or recurrent colorectal cancer scheduled to receive 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-based chemotherapy were enrolled between September 1, 2020, and June 2, 2024. Baseline hs-TnT concentrations were measured before treatment initiation, and patients were followed for the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Independent predictors of MACE were identified using penalized multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the discriminatory performance of baseline hs-TnT and determined the optimal cut-off value using the Youden index. Adequacy index analysis assessed the relative prognostic contribution of hs-TnT to the multivariable model.
RESULTS: 180 patients were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 185 days, 44 patients (24.4%) experienced MACE, more than half of them occurred within the first two cycles of chemotherapy. Baseline hs-TnT demonstrated modest discrimination for predicting MACE (AUC 0.628, 95% CI 0.513-0.742). The optimal hs-TnT cut-off was 14 ng/L. In a multivariable analysis, elevated baseline hs-TnT (OR 2.35 per +10 ng/L, 95% CI 1.37-4.05) and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF)-inhibitor therapy (OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.23-4.60) were associated with MACEs. In a sensitivity analysis, excluding treatment-related hypertension from the composite endpoints, elevated baseline hs-TnT remained the only independent predictor. According to the adequacy index analysis, hs-TnT contributed 38.3% of the total prognostic information provided by the multivariable model.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline hs-TnT was independently associated with MACEs in patients with colorectal cancer receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. Although its discriminatory performance as a standalone biomarker was modest, hs-TnT provided incremental prognostic information for baseline cardiovascular risk assessment and may help identify patients who warrant closer cardiovascular surveillance.

Title: Exercise capacity and handgrip strength following dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training in patients with bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a prospective single-arm study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) is a severe complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) and is associated with impaired exercise capacity. Feasible rehabilitation strategies for this population remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate changes in functional exercise capacity and handgrip strength following a 12-week dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training program in patients with BOS after allo-HSCT and to explore associations of these changes with selected baseline characteristics.
METHODS: This prospective, single-center, single-arm pre-post interventional study included 31 patients with BOS after allo-HSCT. Participants completed a 12-week dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training program. Six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and bilateral handgrip strength were assessed at baseline and week 12. Within-participant changes were evaluated using paired tests according to the distribution of change scores. Associations with selected baseline characteristics were examined in exploratory analyses.
RESULTS: Following the 12-week intervention, mean 6MWD increased from 406.3 m at baseline to 425.9 m at week 12, corresponding to a mean within-participant increase of 19.6 m (95% CI: 9.3-29.9 m; p < 0.001). Mean bilateral handgrip strength increased from 23.2 kg to 25.0 kg, corresponding to a mean increase of 1.8 kg (95% CI: 1.3-2.3 kg; p < 0.001). The change in 6MWD did not differ significantly between women and men (p = 0.282), whereas the increase in handgrip strength was greater in women than in men (p = 0.021). Baseline heart-rate response during the 6MWT and supplemental oxygen requirement were not clearly associated with the magnitude of functional change. No serious training-related adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Twelve weeks of dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training was associated with improvements in 6MWD and handgrip strength in patients with BOS after allo-HSCT. However, the single-arm design precludes causal attribution of these improvements to the intervention, and the exploratory subgroup findings should be interpreted cautiously. Larger controlled studies are needed to establish efficacy and characterize potential differences in response.

Title: Effects of exercise-based interventions on balance and functional mobility in adults with chronic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate, using the GRADE framework, the effects of exercise-based interventions on Berg Balance Scale, Timed Up and Go, and Functional Reach Test outcomes in adults with chronic stroke.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Physiotherapy Evidence Database from inception to 29 June 2025 for randomized controlled trials investigating structured exercise-based interventions in adults with chronic stroke. Eligible studies enrolled adults at least 6 months after stroke onset and reported at least one validated balance or functional mobility outcome. Methodological quality was assessed using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database scale, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models and expressed as mean differences (MDs) or standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); exploratory univariable random-effects meta-regression was used to examine intervention duration and training frequency.
RESULTS: Sixty-nine randomized controlled trials involving 2,314 adults with chronic stroke were included. Exercise-based interventions improved Berg Balance Scale scores [MD = 2.54, 95% CI (1.83-3.26)], reduced Timed Up and Go test completion time [MD = -2.68 s, 95% CI (-3.72 to -1.65)], and improved Functional Reach Test performance [SMD = 0.65, 95% CI (0.25-1.05)]. The certainty of evidence was moderate for BBS, high for TUG, and moderate for FRT, with the degree of heterogeneity differing across outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Exercise-based interventions were associated with improvements in BBS scores, TUG performance, and FRT outcomes in adults with chronic stroke, although the certainty and consistency of evidence varied across these measures. These findings support the potential role of exercise-based interventions in improving these selected outcomes. Larger pragmatic trials with standardized intervention reporting and longer follow-up are needed to clarify optimal training components, dose, delivery, and durability of effects.

Title: Factors associated with short- and long-term maintenance of sinus rhythm after successful elective electrical cardioversion.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electrical cardioversion (ECV) effectively restores sinus rhythm in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), although arrhythmia recurrence is common. We aimed to identify factors associated with a higher probability of maintaining sinus rhythm one month after successful ECV, and after one year in those who were arrhythmia-free after the first month.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included patients who underwent elective ECV for persistent AF or AFL between January 2011 and June 2023. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic characteristics were analyzed to identify parameters associated with the maintenance of sinus rhythm.
RESULTS: We included 297 ECV procedures. ECV was successful in 91.9% of patients and sinus rhythm was maintained in 89.7% of them at one month and in 40.3% at one year follow-up. Shorter arrhythmia duration (OR = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.76-0.98, p = 0.026) and ventricular pacing on the pre-procedural ECG (OR = 5.212, 95% CI: 1.16-23.48, p = 0.032) were associated with one-month success. Factors associated with one-year sinus rhythm maintenance in patients who were in sinus rhythm during monthly follow-up were smaller left atrial dimensions (OR = 0.817, 95%CI: 0.77-0.98, p = 0.022), the first-ever arrhythmia episode (OR = 3.320, 95%CI: 1.10-10.05, p = 0.034), lower CHA2DS2-VASc score (OR = 0.132, 95%CI: 0.03-0.54, p = 0.005), non-smoking status (OR = 0.120, 95%CI: 0.04-0.37, p < 0.001), no previous ECV (OR = 0.082, 95%CI: 0.01-0.47, p = 0.005), and antiarrhythmic therapy (OR = 2.486, 95%CI: 1.01-8.65, p = 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: ECV is a reasonable rhythm-control strategy in AF/AFL particularly when performed early after arrhythmia onset, in non-smokers and patients with fewer comorbidities, antiarrhythmic treatment, smaller left atrium and no prior ECV.

Title: Real-world safety of vericiguat as a fifth-line agent in heart failure: a pharmacovigilance study of quintuple therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vericiguat, a novel soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC) stimulator, is indicated for high-risk worsening heart failure (HF). However, its real-world reporting profile when added to contemporary quadruple guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT)-effectively creating a "quintuple" regimen-remains largely unexplored, particularly regarding cardiorenal and hematologic adverse-event reporting patterns.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database (2021 Q1-2025 Q4). HF reports were strictly stratified into an expanded quadruple GDMT cohort [renin-angiotensin system inhibitor + beta-blocker + mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist [MRA] + sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor [SGLT2i]] and a quintuple cohort (GDMT + vericiguat). Disproportionality analysis utilized a dual-algorithm approach: the frequentist Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) and the Bayesian Information Component (IC) derived from the Bayesian Confidence Propagation Neural Network (BCPNN). SGLT2i-stratified analyses and formal interaction testing were also performed.
RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 5,524 reports (5,459 quadruple; 65 quintuple). No ROR signals were identified for hypotension (ROR = 1.66, 95% CI: 0.90-3.06), syncope (ROR = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.21-3.49), or acute kidney injury (ROR = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.26-1.41). Anemia met the frequentist ROR signal criterion (ROR = 2.61, 95% CI: 1.03-6.58), but not the BCPNN criterion (IC = 0.96, IC-2SD = -0.29). The anemia ROR was 2.61 (95% CI: 1.03-6.58) with an SGLT2i background and 1.82 (95% CI: 0.42-7.88) without an SGLT2i background; formal interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification (P for interaction = 0.683). No statistically significant differences were detected in reported serious outcomes between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this FAERS analysis, no robust reporting signals were identified for hypotension, syncope, or acute kidney injury after vericiguat was added to contemporary quadruple GDMT. Although anemia met the frequentist ROR criterion, the finding was not supported by Bayesian signal detection, and formal analyses did not demonstrate significant effect modification by background SGLT2i use. Given the small vericiguat-exposed cohort, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger longitudinal studies.

Title: Annual variation and clinical characteristics of postoperative lower extremity venous thrombosis after urological surgery: a single-center real-world study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the annual variation and clinical characteristics of clinically detected postoperative lower extremity venous thrombosis (LEVT) during hospitalization in patients undergoing urological surgery at our institution from 2022 to 2025, providing reference for perioperative thrombosis risk assessment and preventive management.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective real-world study was conducted using the hospital electronic medical record system. Patients who developed LEVT for the first time during hospitalization following urological surgery between January 2022 and December 2025 were included. Lower-extremity ultrasonography was performed based on clinical indications rather than routine systematic screening. Detailed information was extracted for patients with thrombosis, including demographic characteristics, admission-related scores and laboratory tests, surgical details, and thrombosis-related outcomes. Descriptive statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software.
RESULTS: Between 2022 and 2025, a total of 12,313 urological surgical procedures were performed at our center, among which 57 patients were newly diagnosed with postoperative LEVT during hospitalization, corresponding to an overall procedure-based clinically detected LEVT rate of 0.46% (57/12,313). The corresponding annual procedure-based clinically detected LEVT rates were 0.63% (17/2,711) in 2022, 0.43% (13/3,005) in 2023, 0.25% (8/3,256) in 2024, and 0.57% (19/3,341) in 2025, showing annual variation over the four-year study period. One patient was excluded due to archived medical records, and two patients were excluded due to incomplete data, leaving 54 patients for detailed analysis. Among these, 45 were male (83.33%) with a median age of 69.0 years (interquartile range, 61.0-74.75). Benign prostatic hyperplasia constituted the largest subgroup by primary condition (29/54, 53.70%), and transurethral resection of the prostate was the most common surgical procedure among the identified LEVT cases (28/54, 51.85%). Thrombosis predominantly involved the intermuscular veins (62.96%), followed by deep veins (35.19%). The median time to LEVT detection was 7 days after admission (IQR, 6-8) and 4 days after surgery (IQR, 3-5). Clinical manifestations were mainly local symptoms such as limb swelling or pain (79.63%). Anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin was the primary treatment (70.37%), and most patients experienced no significant complications (92.59%).
CONCLUSION: The overall procedure-based clinically detected postoperative LEVT rate during hospitalization in urological surgery was low, with annual variation observed over the four-year study period. Among the identified LEVT cases, benign prostatic hyperplasia was the most common primary condition, with intermuscular vein thrombosis being the most common type, and most cases were detected in the early postoperative period. Clinical attention should focus on continued perioperative VTE risk assessment and early recognition of clinically suspected LEVT.

Title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation paired with a 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis for ankle-foot dysfunction among older adults following subacute stroke: clinical findings and exploratory neurophysiological analyses.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This work evaluated clinical effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) plus custom-made 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) for older adults living with post-stroke ankle-foot impairment. Neurophysiological assessments were also carried out for exploratory purposes, drawing exclusively on indirect physiological readouts.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty older participants with ankle-foot dysfunction after subacute stroke were randomized into three parallel groups: conventional-only rehabilitation, 3D-printed AFO therapy, and combined rTMS-AFO intervention (n = 20 per group). Evaluations including ankle active range-of-motion (AROM), resting motor threshold (RMT), integrated surface electromyography (iEMG), Clinical Spasticity Index (CSI), Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Lower Extremity (FMA-LE), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and 10-Metre Walking Test (10MWT) were performed at baseline and four-week post-intervention time-point.
RESULTS: Noticeable within-group functional improvements emerged in all three study arms upon completion of treatment (p < 0.001). Participants assigned to combined therapy achieved greater functional improvements compared with those receiving standalone 3D-printed-AFO or conventional rehabilitation (p < 0.05). The conventional rehabilitation group produced the weakest magnitude of functional recovery across measured endpoints.
CONCLUSION: Compared with single-modality rehabilitation approaches, adding rTMS to 3D-printed AFO therapy brought measurable improvements in ankle mobility, muscle recruitment, balance and walking performance. These clinical benefits occurred alongside elevated excitability within the ipsilesional corticospinal tract. Explanations regarding sensorimotor integration and afferent-efferent circuit regulation should be regarded as exploratory hypotheses because direct neural measurements were not obtained in this investigation. Further independent research is needed to test these mechanistic assumptions.

Title: Body mass index, diabetes, inflammation and survival in COVID-19: a retrospective study evaluating the obesity paradox in an urban hospital center.
Journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with increased morbidity and mortality, particularly among patients with comorbidities such as diabetes and obesity. The combined influence of glycemic control, hyperglycemia, and body mass index (BMI) on disease severity remains incompletely understood, particularly in underserved urban populations.
METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated 478 adults hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19 between March and May 2020 at an urban academic medical center to examine the impact of diabetes, glycemic control, and body mass index (BMI) on clinical outcomes. Data collected included demographics, comorbidities, BMI, diabetes type, baseline hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), inflammatory markers, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, mechanical ventilation, hyperglycemia, and glucocorticoid use.
RESULTS: Among patients with available HbA1c measurements, those with diabetes who developed cytokine storm had significantly higher mean HbA1c than those without cytokine storm. Obesity and overweight were highly prevalent, with 45% of patients classified as obese (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) and 29% classified as overweight (BMI 25-29 kg/m²). Diabetes was associated with increased ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and steroid-induced hyperglycemia. Mortality was higher among older patients, Black patients, and those with diabetes, hypertension, hyperglycemia, greater glucocorticoid use, or ICU admission. Notably, patients with overweight or obesity demonstrated improved survival compared with those of normal weight, consistent with an obesity paradox in this urban cohort. Multivariable analysis identified steroid-induced hyperglycemia, obstructive sleep apnea, and higher methylprednisolone use as independent predictors of ICU admission, whereas higher BMI was associated with a lower risk of adverse outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes and hyperglycemia were associated with greater COVID-19 severity, increased ICU utilization, and higher mortality, while higher BMI offered potential survival benefits. These findings highlight the complex interplay between metabolic dysfunction, obesity, and COVID-19 outcomes, suggesting the presence of an obesity paradox in hospitalized patients, and emphasize the importance of early recognition and management of diabetes and hyperglycemia to improve clinical outcomes.

Title: Lipid metabolism-related inflammatory indices and diabetic kidney disease in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improving the prognosis of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) requires early diagnosis and treatment. This study examined the associations of lipid metabolism-related inflammatory indices (LMIIs)-the platelet-, neutrophil-, monocyte-, and lymphocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratios (PHR, NHR, MHR, and LHR, respectively)-with DKD in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
METHODS: A total of 3,468 T2DM patients were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Logistic regression models were employed to assess the association between LMIIs and DKD. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to evaluate nonlinear relationships, and threshold effect analysis identified inflection points. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses, including inverse probability of treatment weighting, were performed to test the robustness of the findings. Mediation analysis was conducted to explore indirect associations through selected markers. The candidate mediator was not included as a conventional covariate in the corresponding model. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to evaluate the discriminative performance of models incorporating the four LMIIs.
RESULTS: After multivariate adjustment, all four LMIIs showed significant positive associations with DKD (P for overall < 0.05). RCS analysis revealed substantial nonlinear dose - response relationships for PHR, NHR, and MHR (P for nonlinear = 0.009, 0.014, and 0.030, respectively), with inflection points at 2.65, 4.78, and 6.07, respectively. Subgroup analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations. However, lipid-lowering agent use significantly attenuated the NHR - DKD and MHR - DKD relationships (P for interaction = 0.032 and 0.007, respectively). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. TG and ALB showed statistically significant indirect associations in exploratory mediation analyses. ROC analysis showed that the model incorporating NHR had a slightly higher area under the curve (AUC) than those incorporating PHR and LHR (P = 0.002 and 0.003, respectively).
CONCLUSION: LMIIs were significantly associated with DKD and exhibited distinct nonlinear dose-response relationships with threshold effects. Lipid-lowering agent use attenuated the associations of NHR and MHR with DKD. NHR may provide modestly improved discrimination compared with PHR and LHR, while showing comparable performance to MHR. These findings highlight the potential relevance of lipid-inflammation interactions in DKD and warrant further prospective studies to clarify the underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.

Title: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus And Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease In Children And Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Journal: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE), and to evaluate associated clinical and laboratory features.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 72 children with T1DM and 83 healthy controls who were comparable in age and sex. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using ultrasonography and VCTE. A controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) value >236 dB/m was used to define CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD in the T1DM group. Clinical, anthropometric, laboratory, and radiological characteristics were compared between groups. Correlations of CAP and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) with clinical and laboratory parameters were evaluated in the T1DM cohort. Stepwise multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify candidate factors independently associated with CAP and LSM values.
RESULTS: CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD was more frequent in children with T1DM than in controls (31.9% vs. 14.5%). Among children with T1DM, those with MASLD had higher body mass index, WHtR, diastolic blood pressure, and triglyceride levels than those without MASLD. In the multivariable CAP model, diabetes duration, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and WHtR were independently associated with higher CAP values. WHtR and alanine aminotransferase were independently associated with higher LSM values.
CONCLUSION: Children and adolescents with T1DM had a higher prevalence of CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD than healthy controls. Adiposity-related parameters and dyslipidemia appear to be important clinical features associated with hepatic steatosis in pediatric T1DM.

Title: Normal-BMI MASLD is Associated with Increased Mortality, Cardiovascular Events, Cancer and Lower GLP-1 Use.
Journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) can occur in individuals who are not overweight or have obesity (normal-BMI MASLD), yet disease burden and management remain poorly characterized. We compared long-term outcomes and incretin-based therapy use between normal-BMI MASLD (nbMASLD) and overweight/obesity-associated MASLD (obMASLD) across racial and ethnic groups.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, observational study using the TriNetX United States Network. Adults diagnosed with MASLD or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) from 2005-2025 were classified using ethnicity-informed normal-BMI thresholds: <23 kg/m2 for Asian, <27 kg/m2 for Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, and <25 kg/m2 for White/others. Propensity-score matching balanced demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models with obMASLD as the reference group.
RESULTS: Among 619,171 eligible patients, 51,940 matched pairs were identified. Nb-BMI MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality across grouped ethnic groups, with survival of 77.49% versus 83.93% in obMASLD (HR 1.735, CI 1.653-1.822). Ethnicity-specific risks included higher myocardial infarction risk in White and Black patients, higher stroke risk in White patients, higher ESRD risk in Black patients, and increased cancers (colorectal, pancreatic and multiple myeloma) among White patients. Incretin-based therapy (IBT) use was markedly lower in nbMASLD but was associated with improved survival.
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with nbMASLD demonstrated an increased mortality and ethnicity-specific clinical complications than obMASLD despite a more favorable metabolic profile. These findings demonstrate a potential treatment gap for nbMASLD patients and the shortcomings of BMI-based strategies to risk-stratify MASLD patients.

Title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Stroke Risk Decision System for Patients With Carotid Artery Plaque Based on AI-Powered Handheld Ultrasound and Laboratory Markers.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a fusion model combining portable artificial intelligence (AI) ultrasound imaging with multidimensional laboratory data to stratify risk and support decision-making in patients with carotid plaque-related anterior circulation stroke, and to assess its predictive performance and clinical utility.
METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded. All participants completed the 180-day follow-up. The primary outcome was new-onset anterior circulation stroke or TIA, defined as focal neurological deficit > 24 h with CT/MRI-confirmed infarction, or transient (< 24 h) deficit without evidence of acute infarction on neuroimaging. Outcomes were adjudicated by two neurologists (attending or above), with a third for disagreements. Participants were classified into ACS group (n = 140) and non-ACS group (n = 499). Ultrasound features of carotid plaques and clinical laboratory data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with ACS, and a nomogram was constructed based on the regression model. Internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap method. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (C-index and area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis [DCA] and clinical impact curves [CIC]).
RESULTS: (1) Significant differences were observed between the two groups in history of hypertension, smoking, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI), as well as plasma triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels, carotid plaque thickness, plaque area, plaque echogenicity percentage, degree of carotid stenosis, plaque continuity score, and plaque mutability score (p < 0.05). No significant differences were found in sex, history of diabetes, total cholesterol (TC), plaque location, or plaque fibrous cap continuity analysis score (p > 0.05) (2) Multivariable logistic regression identified history of stroke, history of myocardial infarction, plaque thickness, LDL, and HDL as independent predictors of stroke. A nomogram based on these factors demonstrated good discrimination (C-index/AUC = 0.884), with a sensitivity of 84.29% and specificity of 72.55%, along with excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.250). Decision curve analysis showed superior net benefit across a range of risk thresholds compared with the null model, supporting a multi-threshold stratified intervention strategy. Notably, when the predicted risk exceeded 75%, the model's predictions closely aligned with observed outcomes.
CONCLUSION: The stroke risk decision system developed using AI-powered handheld ultrasound and laboratory indicators demonstrates clinical applicability for early prediction of anterior circulation ischemic stroke and is particularly suitable for early screening and risk stratification of high-risk stroke populations in resource-limited settings.

Title: Low latency and generalizable dynamic MRI via L+S alternating gradient descent and minimization.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dynamic MRI reconstruction often requires accurate, fast, and low-latency algorithms that generalize across multiple applications, sampling schemes, and rates, without problem-specific parameter tuning. Existing methods either lack generalizability or require extensive parameter adjustment.
PURPOSE: To develop generalizable, low-latency MRI reconstruction algorithms based on low-rank (LR) and low-rank + sparse (L+S) models that are accurate, fast, and require minimal parameter tuning across diverse dynamic MRI settings.
METHODS: We propose a novel Alternating Gradient Descent and Minimization (AltGDmin) approach for L+S matrix recovery from column-wise undersampled measurements, and extend it to a 3-level hierarchical L+S model for dynamic MRI. A few-shot (FS) learning modification (AGM-L+S-FS) is introduced to enable near low-latency reconstruction with per-frame processing time comparable to or faster than scan time. A simpler LR-only variant is also evaluated.
RESULTS: The proposed algorithms were validated on 6 prospective and 12 retrospective dynamic MRI datasets, covering cardiac, speech, and abdominal applications, with Cartesian, pseudo-radial, radial, and spiral sampling schemes. Experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction, generalizability across datasets and sampling rates, and low-latency performance. Detailed comparisons with state-of-the-art LR, L+S, low-latency, and unsupervised deep learning methods show superior or comparable performance.
CONCLUSIONS: Our AGM-L+S-FS approach provide generalizable, fast, and low-latency MRI reconstruction across multiple dynamic MRI applications and sampling schemes, without the need for problem-specific parameter tuning.

Title: Pharmacological and Therapeutic Potential of Garlic (Allium sativum): Integrating Phytochemistry, Molecular Mechanisms, and Clinical and Preclinical Evidence.
Abstract: Garlic (Allium sativum) is a medicinal plant with diverse pharmacological properties and therapeutic potential in metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, immune, inflammatory, infectious, and neoplastic disorders. However, comprehensive integration of clinical and preclinical evidence remains limited. This review synthesized randomized controlled trials, crossover studies, therapeutic clinical investigations, and experimental animal studies evaluating garlic supplementation. Allicin was identified as the principal intermediate precursor generating numerous bioactive organosulfur compounds. Clinical evidence demonstrated reductions in systolic blood pressure of 5.2%-10.5% and diastolic blood pressure of 4.0%, decreases in LDL cholesterol of 11.8%-14.2% and total cholesterol of 7.6%-14.2%, and increases in HDL cholesterol of 11.5%. Fasting glucose decreased by 7.01 mg/dL, and HbA1c by 0.66%. Inflammatory markers, including TNF-α and C-reactive protein, declined by up to 24.7%, whereas antioxidant capacity increased. Preclinical studies demonstrated reduced tumor growth, improved renal function, enhanced epithelial regeneration, and increased survival in experimental infection models. Garlic demonstrates consistent therapeutic benefits across multiple conditions. Nevertheless, additional high-quality, large-scale clinical trials are required to establish optimal dosing, long-term safety, and clinical efficacy.

Title: Effects of Walnut Consumption on Inflammatory Cytokines and Adipokines in Adults: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation and dysregulation of adipokines play key roles in the development of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders. Walnuts (Juglans regia L.), rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, fiber, and antioxidants, may modulate inflammatory and metabolic pathways; however, evidence from interventional studies remains inconsistent. This systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis aimed to determine the effects of walnut consumption on inflammatory cytokines and adipokines in adults.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in databases through July 2026 to identify relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of walnut intake on C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), adiponectin, and leptin. Weighted mean differences (WMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Subgroup, sensitivity, and non-linear dose-response analyses were performed.
RESULTS: The pooled analysis of 24 RCTs (2068 participants) showed that Walnut intake was associated with a small reduction in CRP concentrations (WMD: -1.0 mg/dL; 95% CI: -1.9 to -0.1; p = 0.031) and IL-6 concentrations (WMD: -0.11 pg/mL; 95% CI: -0.20, -0.01; p = 0.028). However, sensitivity analyses indicated that this finding was not robust to the exclusion of several influential studies. No significant effects were observed for TNF-α (WMD: 0.21 pg/mL, p = 0.306), adiponectin (WMD: -0.17 ng/mL, p = 0.678), or leptin (WMD: 1.39 ng/mL, p = 0.314). Subgroup analyses revealed more potent anti-inflammatory effects with interventions lasting more than 12 weeks and doses above 50 g/day.
CONCLUSIONS: Walnut consumption may be associated with small reductions in CRP and IL-6 levels, without significant effects on TNF-α or adipokine concentrations. However, these effects are modest, and their clinical relevance remains uncertain.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Association of haematologic parameters with persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children: a pilot study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Rheumatic heart disease remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity in children. Although echocardiography is central to diagnosis and staging, it does not directly reflect inflammatory processes that may contribute to ongoing valvular damage. This study aimed to evaluate the association between baseline haematologic parameters and persistent rheumatic heart disease stage in children with prior acute rheumatic fever.
METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective pilot study, 45 children with persistent rheumatic heart disease were classified as Stage A (n = 23), Stage B (n = 14), or Stage C (n = 8) according to the 2023 World Heart Federation echocardiographic staging framework. Baseline laboratory values obtained during acute presentation were analysed. Clinical and laboratory variables were compared across stages using non-parametric tests. Binary logistic regression identified factors associated with advanced disease (Stage B-C vs Stage A).
RESULTS: Markers reflecting acute inflammatory activity, including leukocyte counts and derived indices, did not differ significantly among stages. In contrast, red cell distribution width, mean platelet volume, and platelet distribution width differed significantly. In multivariable analysis, red cell distribution width, and mean platelet volume were independently associated with advanced persistent rheumatic heart disease stage, with higher values linked to increased odds of Stage B-C disease.
CONCLUSION: Red cell distribution width and mean platelet volume were associated with advanced stages of persistent paediatric rheumatic heart disease. These widely available haematologic markers may complement echocardiographic assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed to define their clinical utility.Trial registration: Not applicable (retrospective study).

Title: Focused ultrasound versus LEEP for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions: a retrospective cohort study of long-term effectiveness and obstetric outcomes.
Journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To compare long-term effectiveness and obstetric outcomes of focused ultrasound (FU) ablation versus loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) for high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) in reproductive-aged women.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included women treated with FU (n = 29) or LEEP (n = 32) for HSIL who subsequently delivered (2017-2023). A control group (n = 61) comprised healthy women with negative preconception HR-HPV/cytology. Outcomes were cumulative HR-HPV clearance, cervical length, pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: Both FU and LEEP demonstrated comparable long-term effectiveness: cumulative HR-HPV clearance rates did not differ significantly at any time point (p > 0.05). Post-intervention cervical length was significantly shorter in the LEEP group (24.79 ± 3.98 mm) than in both the FU (27.63 ± 2.80 mm) and control (28.26 ± 3.92 mm) groups (p = 0.003). Cervical insufficiency was more frequent in the LEEP group (15.63%) than in the FU (3.45%) and control (1.64%) groups (p = 0.019). The LEEP group also had higher rates of preterm birth (18.75% vs 3.45% in FU and 4.92% in controls; p = 0.039) and lower rates of vaginal delivery (15.63% vs 44.83% in FU; p = 0.025).
CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort of women with successful live births, FU may have comparable long-term effectiveness to LEEP for HSIL while potentially preserving cervical length and reducing adverse obstetric risks. These preliminary findings suggest FU may be a fertility-sparing option for appropriately selected HSIL women who are planning pregnancy.

Title: Predicting cardiovascular disease in peritoneal dialysis patients using glycated proteomics and machine learning: A prospective multicentre study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients, yet PD-specific biomarkers and prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to identify glycated peptide biomarkers associated with CVD in PD patients and develop a prediction model integrating glycated proteomics and clinical indicators using machine learning.
METHODS: In Phase I, a matched discovery cohort (48 PD patients with CVD and 48 without CVD) was used to identify glycated peptides by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with glmnet used to prioritise candidate biomarkers. In Phase II, candidate biomarkers were quantified in a prospective internal derivation cohort (n = 240) and a multicentre external validation cohort (n = 102). The combined model was developed using F-test feature selection and elastic-net logistic regression. Its predictive performance was compared with three published cardiovascular risk models. Patients were stratified using a training-derived Youden cutoff.
RESULTS: In the discovery cohort, 257 glycated peptides were differentially abundant between groups. Four candidate biomarkers were prioritised, and two peptides, GEAFTLK(g)ATVLNYLPK and K(g)QHLFVK, were retained in the final model together with six clinical indicators: phosphate, diabetes, total Kt/V, albumin, cardiac troponin T, and glycated albumin. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.784 in the training set, 0.781 in the internal testing set, and 0.822 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Using the training-derived cutoff of 0.373, higher 1-year CVD incidence was observed in the high-risk group in both validation cohorts. The combined model also achieved higher ROC-AUCs than the published cardiovascular risk models.
CONCLUSION: We developed and externally validated a PD-specific CVD prediction model by integrating glycated peptide biomarkers with clinical indicators, which may facilitate earlier risk stratification and targeted prevention.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Validation Study

Title: Photobiomodulation Reduces Physiological Stress and Pain During Dental Diagnostic Procedures: The UM-DANE 1 Pediatric Clinical Trial.
Abstract: Purpose: To evaluate effectiveness of photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) in reducing physiological stress (as measured by heart rate [HR] change), self-reported pain, and anxiety during cold pulp testing and routine gingival probing in healthy school-aged children. Methods: This prospective, randomized, split-mouth clinical trial enrolled 30 children aged 7 to 12 years at the University of Maryland pediatric dental clinics from July 2025 to January 2026. Each participant received PBMT (multiwavelength LED device, Nuralyte™) on 1 primary molar and no treatment on the contralateral control tooth. Following a 2-minute waiting period, cold testing and gingival probing were performed. Primary outcomes were HR changes from baseline measured via pulse oximetry. Secondary outcomes included self-reported pain (Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale), anxiety (0 to 10 numeric rating scale), cold perception, cooperation level (Frankl scale), and duration of analgesia. Paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used for split-mouth comparisons. Results: PBMT significantly reduced HR changes during cold testing compared to control (2.23±8.95 versus 6.07±8.70 beats per minute [bpm]; mean difference=-3.83 bpm, 95% confidence interval=-6.89 to -0.77, P=0.016). For gingival probing, self-reported pain was significantly lower with PBMT (median within-subject difference -2.0 points, P=0.004). Sensory perception was preserved in both groups (93.3% positive cold response). Analgesic effects remained stable through 20 minutes post-application. No adverse events occurred. Conclusion: PBMT with a multi-wavelength near-infrared device reduced physiological stress and self-reported pain during pediatric dental diagnostic procedures while preserving sensory function, supporting its use as a promising nonpharmacological behavior guidance option.

Title: Acceptability, Feasibility, and Satisfaction of Buzzy®and VibradentTM for Pain and Anxiety Management in Children During Local Anesthesia Administration.
Abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the efficacy of 2 vibrotactile devices, Buzzy® and VibradentTM, in reducing pain and anxiety during local anesthesia (LA) administration for dental extractions in children. Methods: The study included 126 children aged 7 to 10 years, divided into 3 groups (N=42 each): Group 1 (conventional syringe), Group 2 (Vibradent TM), and Group 3 (Buzzy®). Pain was assessed using the Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale (WBFPS), Face-Legs-Activity-Cry-Consolability scale (FLACC), and Sound-Eye-Motor scale (SEM) at baseline (T0), needle insertion (Tn), and end of local anesthesia administration (Te). Anxiety was measured through the Facial-Image-Scale (FIS) and heart rate. Salivary cortisol was evaluated at T0 and T20 (20 minutes after needle insertion) to assess physiological stress. Parent and child satisfaction were also recorded. Results: Both Buzzy® and VibradentTM significantly reduced pain, anxiety, and salivary cortisol compared to the control group (P<0.001). Buzzy® showed more favorable outcomes in WBFPS, FLACC, SEM, heart rate, and FIS scores (P<0.05) and the highest satisfaction ratings. Both devices showed significantly lower salivary cortisol levels (P<0.05), with no significant difference between them. Conclusions: Buzzy® and Vibradent TM are effective, non-invasive techniques for reducing pain, anxiety, and physiological stress. Buzzy® demonstrated superior overall efficacy.

Title: Association between a novel four-location outer retinal morphology score and visual outcomes in full-thickness macular hole.
Journal: International journal of retina and vitreous
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between a novel four-location outer retinal score (OR score) and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in eyes with full-thickness macular hole.
METHODS: This retrospective study included eyes undergoing vitrectomy for full-thickness macular hole. Preoperative optical coherence tomography (OCT) was used to assess outer retinal morphology at the macular hole edge in four lacations (temporal, nasal, superior, and inferior) using horizontal and vertical scans. Each location was graded, and the sum was defined as the total OR score. Associations with postoperative BCVA at 3 months were evaluated using Spearman's correlation and multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: A total of 48 eyes from 48 patients were included in this study. Four eyes in which primary macular hole closure was not achieved after the initial surgery were excluded from the final analysis of postoperative BCVA at 3 months. The OR score was significantly correlated with postoperative BCVA (ρ = 0.458, p = 0.0018). However, after adjustment for minimum hole diameter, it was not an independent predictor. The OR score was significantly correlated with minimum hole diameter (ρ = 0.522, p < 0.001). Neither the Gass classification nor single cross-sectional OCT classification showed significant associations with postoperative BCVA.
CONCLUSIONS: The four-location OR score was associated with postoperative BCVA and may reflect the severity of outer retinal damage. Its lack of independent predictive value suggests that it captures morphological severity overlapping with minimum hole diameter.

Title: The effect of phytosterol supplementation on endothelial function in adults: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While the cholesterol-lowering properties of phytosterols are well established, their effects on cardiovascular health, particularly endothelial dysfunction and low-grade inflammation, remain insufficiently explored. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of phytosterol supplementation on endothelial function in adults using key vascular biomarkers.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A systematic search of major databases up to March 2026 identified randomized controlled trials comparing phytosterol supplementation with placebo or control. Eligible studies assessed endothelial function using flow-mediated dilation (FMD) or markers of endothelial activation, such as vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1). Random-effects models were applied to pool effect sizes, and subgroup and dose-response analyses were performed. Ten randomized controlled studies (14 effect sizes; 1,278 participants) were included, comprising six studies contributing eight effect sizes for FMD (n = 802) and four studies contributing six effect sizes for VCAM-1 (n = 476). Phytosterol supplementation showed no significant effect on FMD (mean difference: -0.05%, 95% CI: -0.61 to 0.51; P = 0.857) or VCAM-1 (standardized mean difference: -0.16, 95% CI: - 0.34 to 0.03; P = 0.098). Dose-response and meta-regression analyses indicated no significant association of either dose or treatment duration with endothelial outcomes (all P > 0.3).
CONCLUSION: Based on current evidence, no statistically significant effect of phytosterol supplementation on endothelial function was observed. Further long-term, well-designed randomized trials, particularly in high-risk populations, are required to better elucidate potential vascular effects.

Title: The impact of prior asymptomatic COVID-19 infection on outcomes following coronary bypass surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing and expected postoperative course of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) after asymptomatic coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remain uncertain. Evidence guiding cardiac surgical practice has largely been extrapolated from mixed surgical cohorts or broader cardiac surgery series rather than from isolated CABG populations.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults who underwent isolated CABG during 2021-2022. Patients with documented asymptomatic preoperative SARS-CoV-2 infection were compared with patients without documented prior COVID-19. Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables were extracted from institutional records. Outcomes included early clinical recovery, respiratory support, transfusion exposure, laboratory trajectories, and mortality. A timing subgroup analysis (< 4 weeks vs >= 4 weeks from infection to surgery) was prespecified as exploratory.
RESULTS: Seventy-six patients met eligibility criteria: 37 with prior asymptomatic COVID-19 and 39 without documented prior COVID-19. The cohort was predominantly male (81.6%), low risk by EuroSCORE II, and largely elective. Baseline demographics, major comorbidities, ventricular function, operative priority, number of grafted vessels, cardiopulmonary bypass time, cross-clamp time, extubation time, intensive care unit stay, hospital stay, oxygen requirement, and transfusion exposure were similar between groups. Postoperative complications were more frequent in the prior-COVID group (16.2% vs 0.0%; risk difference 16.2%, 95% CI 3.8-31.1%; P = 0.011), whereas mortality remained rare and not significantly different (2.7% vs 0.0%; P = 0.487). Longitudinal laboratory analyses showed expected perioperative inflammatory and hematologic changes within both groups, without consistent between-group separation. In the exploratory timing subgroup, no statistically significant differences were detected between earlier and later surgery, but this analysis was markedly underpowered.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center exploratory cohort of predominantly elective, low-risk CABG patients, prior asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection was not associated with a generalized worsening of early postoperative recovery, although postoperative complications were more frequent in the exposed group. These data are insufficient to inform CABG timing recommendations after asymptomatic infection and should not be extrapolated to unstable or higher-risk patients. Larger multicenter studies with better exposure characterization, vaccination data, and longer follow-up are required.

Title: Disease severity and lyso-Gb3 are associated with early echocardiographic markers of cardiac involvement in Fabry disease: a single-center observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac involvement in Fabry disease often begins with subtle functional abnormalities before overt hypertrophy or systolic dysfunction becomes evident. Identifying early echocardiographic markers associated with disease burden may improve risk stratification in this rare disorder.
METHODS: In this single-center cross-sectional observational study, 19 genetically confirmed Fabry disease patients receiving stable enzyme replacement therapy underwent comprehensive clinical, biochemical, and echocardiographic evaluation. Disease severity was assessed using the Mainz Severity Score Index (MSSI), and plasma lyso-globotriaosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb3) levels were measured by LC-MS/MS. Associations between MSSI, Lyso-Gb3, and echocardiographic parameters reflecting early cardiac dysfunction were analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean MSSI score was 26.1 ± 14.2, and plasma Lyso-Gb3 levels were markedly elevated. Higher MSSI scores were associated with increased E/e' septal (r = 0.52, p = 0.021), E/e' average (r = 0.51, p = 0.027), and tricuspid regurgitation velocity (r = 0.60, p = 0.006). Plasma Lyso-Gb3 levels correlated positively with left ventricular mass index (r = 0.60, p = 0.031), posterior wall thickness (r = 0.62, p = 0.023), and tricuspid regurgitation velocity (r = 0.80, p = 0.001), and negatively with left ventricular ejection fraction (r = - 0.72, p = 0.005). These associations were observed despite preserved systolic function in most patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Disease severity assessed by MSSI and circulating Lyso-Gb3 levels are associated with early functional and structural echocardiographic abnormalities in Fabry disease. Incorporating these measures into routine evaluation may facilitate earlier identification of cardiac involvement and support individualized monitoring strategies in this rare disease population.

Title: Machine learning‑based risk stratification for moderate‑to‑severe anxiety‑depression in patients with hypertension and/or coronary heart disease: a multicenter cross‑sectional study.
Journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depression in patients with hypertension and/or coronary heart disease (CHD) are associated with severe outcomes. However, there is a lack of objective risk stratification tools. This proof‑of‑concept study developed eight machine learning (ML) models to assess the feasibility of risk stratification for moderate‑to‑severe anxiety‑depression in this population and to identify key associated factors.
METHODS: The study retrospectively included patients with hypertension and/or CHD from the 2023 Psychology and Behavior Investigation of Chinese Residents (PBICR) database, a cross‑sectional, self‑report survey. Patients were randomly split into training (70%) and test (30%) sets for internal validation. In the training set, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with cross-validation was employed to select features for constructing the model. Eight ML models were developed for risk stratification of moderate‑to‑severe anxiety‑depression (PHQ‑9 ≥ 10 and/or GAD‑7 ≥ 10). Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 4,006 eligible patients, allocated to training (n = 2,805) and test (n = 1,201) sets. LASSO regression selected 15 predictors from 43 initial features. This study established eight ML models for risk stratification of moderate-to-severe anxiety-depression in patients with hypertension and/or CHD. Random Forest (RF) demonstrated optimal discrimination in the training set (AUROC = 0.837; 95% CI: 0.812-0.862). In the test set, it maintained acceptable discrimination (AUROC = 0.838; 95% CI: 0.814-0.862; Brier score = 0.134). Family health, risk taking, and quality of life (QoL) were identified as the strongest correlates via SHAP analysis. DCA suggested net benefit across risk thresholds of 10-40%.
CONCLUSIONS: The RF model achieved the best performance, with family health, risk taking, and QoL as the strongest correlates. The proposed two‑stage screening workflow is hypothetical and has not been prospectively validated. Due to a lack of external validation and the cross‑sectional, self‑report design, this study is hypothesis‑generating and proof‑of‑concept. Prospective validation in independent cohorts is required before any clinical application.

Title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolic events at 90 days in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Evidence regarding venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in palliative care populations remains scarce, and current thromboprophylaxis recommendations are largely extrapolated from non-palliative oncology cohorts. This study aimed to determine the 90-day incidence of VTE and associated clinical risk factors in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults with advanced cancer enrolled in a palliative care program who were hospitalized between 2018 and 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Bogotá, Colombia. VTE incidence was calculated, and clinical risk factors were identified using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: A total of 782 patients were included (mean age 61 years; 58.7% male). Withing 90 days of admission, 81 patients (10.3%) developed VTE, corresponding to an incidence density of 2.3 events per 1,000 patient-days. Pulmonary embolism accounted for 40.7% of VTE events. In the adjusted analysis, lung cancer was associated with an increased risk of VTE (HR 2.34; p = 0.010), whereas higher Karnofsky Performance Status was associated with a lower risk (HR 0.98; p = 0.020). Age, sex, body mass index, baseline hemoglobin, active anticancer treatment, and white blood cell count were not independently associated with VTE. Overall, 90-day mortality was 66.3%.
CONCLUSION: VTE was a frequent complication among hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. Lung cancer and poor functional status were independently associated with VTE, whereas traditional clinical predictors were not associated with VTE. These findings support individualized VTE risk assessment and highlight the need for future prospective studies evaluating thromboprophylaxis strategies in palliative care settings.

Title: CTC-AttnNet: development and validation of an attention-based neural network for staging gastrointestinal malignancies.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a noninvasive model for classifying T stage in gastrointestinal malignancies using circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and serum tumor markers and to compare the predictive value of CTCs with that of conventional tumor markers.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 328 patients with gastrointestinal malignancies from two hospitals in the same region. The internal modelling cohort comprised 214 patients (T1 + T2, n = 49; T3 + T4, n = 165), and the independent validation cohort comprised 114 patients (T1 + T2, n = 55; T3 + T4, n = 59). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify stage-related factors associated with CTCs. Three-dimensional-matched feature sets were constructed to minimize bias from unequal feature numbers. Repeated stratified fivefold cross-validation, the foldwise synthetic minority oversampling technique, and weighted cross-entropy loss were used to address severe class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, balanced accuracy, F1 score, and calibration metrics rather than overall accuracy. Logistic regression, decision tree, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, and the newly developed CTC-AttnNet were compared. K‒M and Cox analyses were performed as exploratory recurrence analyses.
RESULTS: CTC count alone moderately discriminated the overall TNM stage (AUC = 0.742) but poorly discriminated the T stage (AUC = 0.595); the AUCs of all four conventional tumor markers were < 0.60. Advanced overall TNM stage was independently associated with CTC positivity (OR = 1.844, 95% CI: 1.255-2.710; P = 0.002). Under dimension-matched conditions, the CTC-containing feature set achieved an external validation AUC of 0.76, outperforming the dimension-reduced conventional marker combination (AUC = 0.65). CTC-AttnNet achieved an external validation AUC of 0.82, a balanced accuracy of 0.78, and an F1 score of 0.76. Ablation analysis revealed that the attention module improved the recognition of minority class T1 + T2 cases. CTC positivity was also independently associated with recurrence (HR = 5.263, 95% CI 1.637-16.927; P = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: CTCs were significantly associated with gastrointestinal tumor stage and postoperative recurrence. Multivariable CTC-based models discriminated T stage better than models based on four conventional serum tumor markers did, although the CTC count alone had limited discriminatory ability. CTC-AttnNet represents an exploratory noninvasive stratification tool for this retrospective regional cohort and provides a methodological framework for developing liquid biopsy prediction models.

Title: Peripheral and cardiac determinants of exercise intolerance in classic Anderson-Fabry disease: insights from cardiopulmonary exercise testing and advanced echocardiography.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise intolerance is a common feature of Anderson-Fabry disease (AFD), but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied eighty-eight patients with classical AFD phenotype and preserved ejection fraction. Patients underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), lactate assessment, and advanced echocardiography including myocardial work and atrial strain analysis. Exercise tolerance was reduced across the cohort, with low peak VO2 measured as percent predicted (VO2%predicted) and early lactate accumulation. Peak VO2%predicted declined with worsening left ventricular geometry. Left ventricular diastolic parameters, myocardial work efficiency, and left atrial strain were associated with exercise capacity. In multivariable analysis, left atrial conduit strain emerged as a strong independent predictor.
CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal muscle energetic metabolism alterations primarily drive exercise intolerance in AFD and early cardiac dysfunction, assessed by advanced echocardiography further exacerbated it.

Title: Quantitative assessment of deformable image registration accuracy for cumulative dose estimation in multi-site stereotactic re-irradiation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Re-irradiation of previously treated anatomical sites requires precise cumulative dose estimation to balance tumor control with organ-at-risk (OAR) tolerance. Conventional physical dose summation fails to account for inter-treatment anatomical deformations, potentially leading to systematic over- or underestimation of OAR doses. This study evaluates intensity-based deformable image registration (DIR) for improving dose accumulation accuracy in multiple stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) re-irradiation across different anatomical sites.
METHODS: Sixty patients (226 lesions) who underwent robotic CyberKnife-based SABR re-irradiation (2-5 courses) to liver (36.7%), brain (36.7%), lung (10%), and spine (16.7%) metastases between 2016 and 2025 were analyzed. Cumulative OAR doses were calculated using both DIR-based approach and traditional physical summation. DIR registration accuracy was quantified using dice similarity coefficient (DSC), jaccard index (JI). Biologically effective dose (BED) and equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions (EQD2) conversions were evaluated for dose assessments across heterogeneous fractionation schedules.
RESULTS: DIR-based dose accumulation demonstrated significantly lower maximum doses compared with physical summation: liver maximum dose decreased from 123.8 ± 55.6 Gy to 83.2 ± 28.0 Gy (p < 0.001) and chest wall maximum dose reduced from 82.9 ± 22.4 Gy to 66.9 ± 18.6 Gy (p = 0.05). DIR yielded excellent spatial agreement for relatively rigid structures, including the heart, liver, kidneys, and brainstem (DSC > 0.90; JI > 0.84), whereas highly deformable organs such as the bowel and stomach demonstrated markedly inferior agreement (DSC < 0.50; JI < 0.35). Biological dose assessment revealed that DIR-guided workflow more accurately reflected cumulative dose patterns.
CONCLUSION: Deformable registration improves cumulative dose estimation accuracy for multiple SABR re-irradiation. Integration of validated DIR with quantitative quality assurance and biological dose modeling provides a robust framework for multiple re-irradiation workflows. Future prospective studies correlating DIR-derived doses with clinical toxicity are warranted to validate the clinical impact of improved dosimetric accuracy.

Title: Association of esketamine with acute lung injury and macrophage polarization-related markers after ATAAD surgery.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between perioperative esketamine use, postoperative acute lung injury (ALI), and macrophage polarization-related markers in patients undergoing acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) surgery.
METHODS: A total of 124 patients with ATAAD treated at our hospital between January 2022 and December 2024 were retrospectively included. Postoperative ALI was assessed within the first 24 h after ICU admission following ATAAD surgery, and patients were classified into the ALI group (n = 52) and non-ALI group (n = 72) accordingly. Univariate analysis and binary logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with postoperative ALI after ATAAD surgery. Patients were further analyzed according to perioperative esketamine use to evaluate differences in macrophage polarization-related markers and clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Binary logistic regression analysis showed that hypertension was independently associated with an increased risk of postoperative ALI (OR = 5.586, 95% CI: 1.832-17.034, P = 0.002), whereas perioperative esketamine use was independently associated with a reduced risk of postoperative ALI (OR = 0.155, 95% CI: 0.061-0.394, P < 0.001). After propensity score matching, 45 matched pairs were retained. In the matched cohort, postoperative ALI occurred in 11 patients in the esketamine group and 23 patients in the non-esketamine group (24.4% vs. 51.1%, P = 0.011). Perioperative esketamine use remained associated with a lower risk of postoperative ALI after matching (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.13-0.74, P = 0.008). Patients in the esketamine group also showed a lower postoperative M1-related index and M1/M2 ratio, a higher M2-related index, and a shorter hospital stay.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative esketamine use was associated with a lower risk of postoperative ALI after ATAAD surgery and was accompanied by favorable changes in macrophage polarization-related markers. Given the retrospective single-center design and limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger prospective studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This was a retrospective observational study and did not involve prospective assignment of participants to an intervention.

Title: Meal-induced changes in cardiometabolic peptides in the context of acute cardiovascular diseases and glucose metabolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natriuretic peptides (NPs) and copeptin are established cardiovascular biomarkers which can partly affect human metabolism. However, impact of human metabolism on their postprandial regulation in high-risk patients remains insufficiently understood. We aimed to characterize meal-induced changes in MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, and copeptin and to assess how these dynamics relate to acute cardiovascular (CV) events, type 2 diabetes (T2D) and insulin resistance (IR).
METHODS: Within the BeLOVE cohort, a subset of 373 participants with acute coronary syndrome, stroke or very high chronic CV risk underwent standardized study-specific mixed-meal testing approximately 3 months after the acute event or 1 month after enrollment for the chronic high-risk group. Fasting and 120-min postprandial concentrations of MR-proANP, NT-proBNP, copeptin, insulin and glucose were assessed. Structural equation models were used to evaluate direct and indirect associations of acute CV events, T2D, and IR (HOMA-IR) with fasting levels and postprandial changes, adjusted for age, sex and BMI.
RESULTS: MR-proANP showed the most pronounced meal-induced suppression. NT-proBNP demonstrated only minor and inconsistent postprandial changes. For all peptides, fasting concentrations were the main determinant of their postprandial changes. A recent acute CV event was associated with higher fasting NP levels (MR-proANP: standardized β = 0.22 [0.09; 0.34]; NT-proBNP: β = 0.28 [0.15; 0.41]), but not substantially with their postprandial changes after accounting for their baseline levels. T2D showed no consistent association with fasting or postprandial NP responses. In contrast, higher HOMA-IR was associated with lower fasting MR-proANP (β=-0.19 [-0.30; -0.07]) and a stronger postprandial decline (β=-0.18 [-0.33; -0.04]). Similarly, higher HOMA-IR was linked to lower fasting NT-proBNP (β=-0.15 [-0.28; -0.03]) but showed no clear association to its postprandial change. Copeptin dynamics were largely independent of acute CV disease and metabolic status.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients after a recent ACS or stroke, postprandial MR-proANP dynamics are linked to insulin resistance, rather than diabetes status. In contrast, the limited postprandial variability of NT-proBNP and the largely fasting-related changes of copeptin make these markers less suited for capturing short-term metabolic responses. Together, these findings highlight the value of postprandial phenotyping for understanding cardiometabolic regulation and support further evaluation of MR-proANP as a potential biomarker in future prospective studies with cardiovascular outcomes across subjects with and without acute CV event.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was approved by the institutional ethics committee (EA1/066/17) and registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00016852).

Title: Identification and validation of candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism in diabetic foot.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the precise regulatory mechanisms underlying diabetic foot (DF) remain incompletely understood, increasing evidence suggests that mitochondrial metabolism may be involved in DF progression. The study aimed to identify and validate candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism in DF.
METHODS: Transcriptome sequencing data from 12 DF and 18 control tissue samples were analyzed together with 1,234 mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MMRGs), which were obtained from MSigDB by integrating curated gene sets directly associated with mitochondrial metabolic processes. First, overlapping genes between MMRGs and DEGs between DF and control samples were used as candidate genes. Then, candidate biomarkers were identified using PPI network construction, two machine learning algorithms, and ROC curve analysis. Next, based on the candidate biomarkers, functional enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory network, compound prediction, as well as molecular docking analyses were undertaken. Finally, to explore the expression of candidate biomarkers in clinical samples, the reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was performed.
RESULTS: GPAT3 and PTGS2 were identified as mitochondrial metabolism-associated candidate biomarkers for DF, with area under the curve values of 0.963 and 0.958, respectively. Functional enrichment analysis showed that multiple pathways were significantly enriched by both GPAT3 and PTGS2, such as ribosome and Leishmania infection. GPAT3 had the strongest positive and negative correlations with neutrophils and resting CD4 memory T cells, respectively. In contrast, PTGS2 exhibited the strongest negative connection with M1 macrophages and the strongest positive correlation with neutrophils. Subsequently, multiple transcription factors (TFs) were found to co-target GPAT3 and PTGS2, such as BRD4 and NR0B1. Moreover, compound prediction analysis identified several compounds potentially associated with these biomarkers, such as lipopolysaccharides and cisplatin. The binding free energy between PTGS2 and tetradecanoylphorbol acetate was - 8.2 kcal/mol, while the binding free energy between GPAT3 and cyclosporine was - 10.4 kcal/mol, according to molecular docking data. Finally, the expression levels of GPAT3 and PTGS2 were significantly different in clinical samples.
CONCLUSION: GPAT3 and PTGS2 were identified as candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism in DF, providing molecular clues for further investigation of DF pathogenesis and potential intervention strategies.

Title: Multi-Backbone U-Net segmentation and interpretable hybrid deep learning classification for lung cancer detection in chest CT images.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its early and accurate diagnosis from chest CT imaging is complicated by overlapping radiological features between benign and malignant lesions, as well as by the limited cross-institution validation and interpretability reported in much of the existing computer-aided diagnosis literature.
