Given the increasing staffing shortages and the substantial heterogeneity of the population of primary care patients at increased risk of CVD, cardiovascular risk management strategies should be better tailored to individual patients’ needs and risk profiles. Therefore, we developed the PROSPERA programme, a population-level risk-based approach aimed at improving cardiovascular risk management in primary care.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The PROSPERA study is a pragmatic 1:1 cluster randomised controlled trial in 22 primary care practices in the greater Leiden and The Hague region in the Netherlands, investigating real-world effectiveness of usual care plus the PROSPERA programme with usual care alone. The PROSPERA programme consists of (1) a population-level risk stratification overview to anticipate care needs (empanelment), (2) training for healthcare professionals in cardiovascular risk communication, (3) a lifestyle questionnaire completed by patients before consultation (Lifestylecheck) and (4) a clinical decision support tool (U-Prevent). The programme aims to support a more targeted use of available resources by identifying patients at higher risk and tailoring preventive efforts to those who may benefit most, thereby potentially improving the efficiency and effectiveness of care. Patients between 40 and 90 years of age enrolled in integrated care programmes (programmes developed to ensure a continuum of care for patients with chronic conditions) for increased cardiovascular risk are included. The primary outcome is defined as the proportion of the participants with successful achievement of all protocol-defined cardiovascular preventive treatment goals at 18 months of follow-up. Secondary outcomes include implementation outcomes (penetration and fidelity), healthcare professionals’ satisfaction on usability of the PROSPERA programme, patient experience with shared decision-making and decisional conflict when making a healthcare decision and outcomes on cost-effectiveness.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Consent for the use of routine healthcare data are obtained through an opt-out procedure for participating practices. Digital informed consent will be obtained for the study questionnaires for patients and healthcare professionals. Main findings on effectivity, efficacy and implementation will be disseminated via peer-reviewed journals and via (inter)national conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06593704.

Title: Exploring patterns of acute and primary care utilisation before diagnosis, during treatment and for 3 years postcompletion of surgery and adjuvant treatment in women with endometrial cancer: a protocol for a Victorian data linkage study.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: Women with endometrial cancer have two to three times higher rate of pre-existing chronic cardiovascular risk factors including hypertension (59% vs 31%), obesity (34% vs 15%) and diabetes (26% vs 10%) compared with women without cancer. With a 5-year cancer-specific survival of 85%, these women are three times more likely to die of cardiovascular disease than they are to have a cancer recurrence. Surveillance for recurrence dominates post-treatment follow-up, a model misaligned with greatest health risks. Current approaches to endometrial cancer care may disrupt established management pathways for high-mortality risk chronic conditions and how best to manage chronic disease postcancer remains unclear. Women’s engagement with health services to manage chronic conditions before, during and after cancer treatment and what it means for long-term health is unknown. Linked data enables examination of healthcare utilisation across the care continuum.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This retrospective cohort study uses data accessed via the Victorian Comprehensive Cancer Centre (VCCC) Alliance Data Connect platform, an Australian platform that links Victorian general practice data: Primary Care Data Research Repository (PATRON); hospital data—Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED), Victorian Radiotherapy Minimum Dataset (VRMDS), Victorian Emergency Minimum Dataset (VEMD), Victorian Integrated Non-Admitted Health Dataset (VINAH); and clinical registry data—Victorian Cancer Registry (VCR) and Victorian Death Index (VDI), managed in the secure environment of the Centre for Victorian Data Linkage (CVDL). Data span 2008–2022. Healthcare utilisation across acute and primary care settings will be mapped across three phases: prediagnosis, during treatment and 3 years post-treatment. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics reporting frequency and percentage of encounters, mean and SD. Primary outcome is frequency and patterns of healthcare utilisation before, during and after endometrial cancer diagnosis and treatment. This includes frequency and type of cancer and non-cancer healthcare encounters, patterns of specialist versus general practice (GP) care, evidence of care associated with, or sought for, chronic diseases.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Study approved by the Office of Research Ethics and Integrity (Number 2025–23718-73133-20); Patron Data Governance (ID PAT 0001138), The University of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Results will be disseminated via funder reports, peer-reviewed publication, professional and consumer conferences.

Title: HFSA Scientific Statement on Right Heart Failure.
Abstract: Right heart failure (RHF), both acute and chronic is increasingly recognized as a distinct and clinically significant syndrome across the spectrum of cardiovascular disease. Estimates suggest RHF complicates >25-30% of hospitalizations for acute decompensated HF and is nearly universal in advanced pulmonary hypertension (PH) (1) Despite recent diagnostic and therapeutic advancements, RHF remains associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and impaired quality of life. Addressing RHF requires dedicated strategies tailored to its pathophysiology, including early identification, risk stratification, and novel therapies. (2) While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the topic remain limited, there has been increasing emphasis on early recognition and management of RHF (especially in the setting of left ventricular [LV] failure). In addition, there is an expanding role for temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in acute RHF and percutaneous tricuspid interventions in chronic RHF. Yet, the field remains limited by its under-recognition, lack of standardized definitions, and limited therapeutic options, which underscore the urgent need for consensus and guidance.

Title: Sex-Based Outcomes After Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a ten-year period in three stroke centers.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within six months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite endpoint. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging (MRA-VWI).
RESULTS: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs 23.5%, p=0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, p<0.01), HDL (56.8 ± 18.1 vs 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, p<0.01), and LDL (101.5 ± 45.4 vs 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, p<0.01); however, the LDL/HDL ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, p<0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs 48.6%, p=0.91), TIA (32.0% vs 33.5%, p=0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs 20.7%, p=0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs 4.0%, p=0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs 1.6%, p=0.61), TIA (0.7% vs 1.6%, p=0.23), MI (0.5% vs 0.0%, p=0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs 1.2%, p=0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs 24.3%, p=0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs 5.2%, p=0.32), TIA (5.1% vs 4.0%, p=0.50), MI (2.6% vs 3.6%, p=0.45), mortality (17.5% vs 19.1%, p=0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs 7.2%, p=0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs 4.8%, p=0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N=182), the 30-day (3.3% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs 31.9%, p=0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs 7.7%, p=0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs 6.6%, p=0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a ten-year period at three high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.

Title: Outcomes of single-branched TEVAR with cervical debranching for zone 0 and zone 1 aortic arch repair: A VQI analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).
METHODS: The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. Mean age was 73.8±8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7±12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. Median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion Type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair.
CONCLUSIONS: Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.

Title: Venous Thromboembolism Reporting in Fusion-Positive NSCLC Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Safety Reporting and Protocol-Level Provisions in Phase I-IV Clinical Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria.
RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods.
CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

Title: Waitlist Outcomes of Multiorgan Heart Transplant Candidates.
Journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, the number of patients undergoing simultaneous multiorgan heart transplant (MOT) has increased significantly. However, there is no unified policy for MOT allocation, allowing Organ Procurement Organizations to individually determine priority for match runs across all organ types. We evaluated if heart transplant (HT) candidates listed simultaneously for a kidney or liver are at a disadvantage on the waitlist.
METHODS: Adult HT candidates registered with the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients between 2019-2023 were included. Candidates were waitlisted statuses 1-6 within the heart allocation system in order of medical urgency. The primary outcomes were transplantation and removal from the waitlist for death or clinical deterioration, estimated with cumulative incidence functions for the first-year after listing, stratified by both waitlist status and type of organ listing. Rates of transplantation and removal from the waitlist at 1 year were reported. Using cox proportional hazards models, cause-specific hazards of transplantation and removal, holding waitlist status constant were estimated.
RESULTS: Of 20,588 HT candidates, 9.3% were heart kidney (HK) and 1.4% were heart liver (HL) candidates. Irrespective of status, heart-alone candidates had higher cumulative incidence of transplant (70.6% vs. 67.9% HK, p < 0.01; vs. 63.6% HL, p < 0.01), and lower cumulative incidence of removal from the waitlist for death or deterioration (5.3% vs. 10.3%, p < 0.01); vs. 10.4%, p < 0.01). In adjusted analysis and stratified by candidate listing center, MOT listing was significantly associated with lower likelihood of transplant (HK: HR 0.71, 0.68-0.75; HL: HR 1.13, 1.09-1.17), and a significantly higher risk of delisting due to death or deterioration (HK: HR 2.08, 1.81, 2.39; HL: HR 2.45, 1.75, 3.42). Hemodialysis-dependent HK candidates experienced the highest cumulative incidence of death or deterioration at 1 year (13%) compared to non-hemodialysis dependent (8.7%, p < 0.01) and heart-alone (5.3%, p < 0.01) candidates, but similar to HL candidates (10.4%, p = 0.32).
CONCLUSION: MOT candidates, especially HK, had worse waitlist outcomes with lower rates of transplantation and higher incidence of removal from the waitlist compared to heart-alone candidates. These outcomes demonstrate a need for MOT allocation based on criteria more reflective of medical urgency.

Title: Inferoseptal Recess Anatomy Predicts Conduction Disturbances After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Journal: Hellenic journal of cardiology : HJC = Hellenike kardiologike epitheorese
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: New-onset conduction disturbances (CDs) remain the most frequent and clinically relevant complications after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The anatomical mechanisms underlying conduction injury are not fully understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between inferoseptal recess (ISR) anatomy and post-TAVR conduction disturbances, and to validate its predictive value using an interpretable machine learning algorithm.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 307 patients who underwent TAVR between 2017 and 2024. Pre-procedural computed tomography (CT) was used to quantify ISR morphology and aortic root anatomy. The primary endpoint was new-onset CDs (bundle branch block, high-grade atrioventricular block, or need for permanent pacemaker implantation). Machine learning algorithms were applied to integrate CT-derived anatomical and clinical variables and to validate the predictive value of ISR metrics, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) applied for interpretability.
RESULTS: CDs occurred in 57 of 307 patients (18.6%). Wider WOISR (per 1-mm increment) was independently associated with reduced risk of CDs (OR: 0.76, 95% CI 0.66-0.89; P<0.001), along with counter-clockwise aortic root rotation (OR: 0.91, [95% CI, 0.87-0.95]; P<0.001), smaller ΔMSID (OR: 0.83, [95% CI, 0.76-0.91]; P<0.001), larger left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (P=0.004), with pre-existing right bundle-branch block (P<0.001). Among ML models, the RF model achieved an AUC of 0.91 in the temporal holdout cohort and showed favorable net benefit across a range of clinically relevant threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified non-coronary sinus calcification score, LVEDD, and WOISR as dominant contributors to model output.
CONCLUSIONS: WOISR (≤4 mm) is an anatomical predictor of CDs following TAVR. WOISR was independently associated with post-TAVR conduction disturbances and provided incremental discriminatory information beyond established clinical predictors. These findings support further prospective evaluation of ISR morphology as a complementary component of CT-based conduction-risk assessment before and after TAVR.

Title: Shock teams may improve outcomes of patients with cardiogenic shock (STOP-CS): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: A multidisciplinary team-based approach became one of the main paradigms in health care. Current evidence regarding the efficacy of Shock Teams and related advanced shock care models in cardiogenic shock (CS) comes from observational studies, with limited synthetic data available. We aimed to assess the association between advanced shock care models and short- and mid-term outcomes of CS patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO registration: CRD42024581904) were conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 Statement. We included observational studies of at least 25 adult CS patients managed with or without a Shock Team or related advanced shock care models. We searched Embase, Medline Ultimate, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 01.01.2016 to 13.08.2024. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Meta-analyses were performed with a random-effects model. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Nine studies with a total of 658,708 patients met the inclusion criteria. For medium-term mortality, follow-up ranged from 60 to 365 days. Treatment of patients within the included models was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.81, 95%CI: [0.74, 0.90], p < 0.0001, I2 = 58%), lower intensive care unit mortality (OR: 0.58, 95%CI: [0.43, 0.78], p = 0.0004, I2 = 45%), and lower medium-term mortality (HR: 0.59, 95%CI: [0.48, 0.72], p < 0.00001, I2 = 0%). These associations remained significant in sensitivity analyses, although clinical and methodological heterogeneity persisted.
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced shock care models may be associated with improved short- and mid-term outcomes in CS patients including lower in-hospital and medium-term mortality. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these results.

Title: Preoperative Predictors of Outcome for Adults Undergoing Congenital Cardiac Surgery: Multicenter Model Validation.
Journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) undergoing cardiac surgery represent a growing population in whom conventional surgical risk models perform suboptimally. We externally validated a previously described ACHD-specific preoperative risk model and evaluated whether performance could be improved through recalibration/model updating.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study of patients ≥16 years undergoing congenital cardiac surgery at four centers (March 2020-April 2023). The primary composite adverse outcome (CAO) comprised in-hospital death, prolonged ventilation >7 days, or new-onset dialysis. We evaluated discrimination and calibration of the original preoperative model (including MELD-XI, cognitive impairment, body-mass index [BMI], prior chest wall incisions, and complex anatomy) and then performed bootstrap-based model updating (200 resamples) to derive refined models with and without the Adult Congenital Heart Surgery (ACHS) procedural mortality score.
RESULTS: Among 538 patients, CAO occurred in 4.3% (n=23). In external validation (n=383 complete cases), the original model preserved discrimination (AUC=0.729, 95% confidence interval: 0.602-0.855) but systematically overestimated risk, indicating need for recalibration. The refined model retained BMI, prior chest incisions, cognitive impairment, age, serum albumin level, and ventricular systolic dysfunction. Discrimination was good without procedural complexity (AUC=0.799; 0.697-0.900) and improved with inclusion of the ACHS score (AUC=0.857; 0.779-0.935).
CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective multicenter external validation, an ACHD-specific preoperative risk model maintained discrimination but required recalibration. Incorporating procedural complexity enhanced discrimination, supporting a hybrid patient- and procedure-based approach to guide perioperative planning.

Title: Perivascular space imaging marker and glymphatic function in obstructive sleep apnea: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a recognized cardiovascular and dementia risk factor that has been previously reported in association with enlarged cerebral perivascular spaces (PVS) indicative of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and impaired glymphatic function. We aimed to evaluate associations between OSA and neuroimaging-visible PVS and Diffusion Tensor Imaging Analysis Along the Perivascular Space (DTI-ALPS), as a surrogate marker of glymphatic function.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase was conducted through Oct 11, 2026. The meta-analysis included observational studies exploring associations between OSA severity and PVS burden and DTI-ALPS. Reported effect estimates for PVS or glymphatic parameters across OSA disease severity were pooled using a random-effect model.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies (N = 2618) met the inclusion criteria. Results showed that patients with OSA had a significantly higher odds of documented PVS compared to those without OSA (OR = 4.97, 95% CI 2.51 to 9.82). Each per unit increase in apnea-hypopnea index corresponded to a 3% increase in the odds of PVS (OR = 1.03, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.04). OSA was linked to a significant decrease in glymphatic-related diffusion as indicated by DTI-ALPS index (mean difference = -0.2, 95% CI -0.35 to -0.06). This reduction persisted across all OSA severities, including mild (mean difference = -0.17, 95% CI -0.32 to -0.02), and moderate-to-severe (mean difference = -0.10, 95% CI -0.17 to -0.04) OSA.
CONCLUSIONS: Our meta-analysis demonstrated a strong link between OSA and both increased PVS burden and impaired surrogate of glymphatic function, potentially implicating OSA in the pathogenesis of both CSVD and dementia. Further prospective studies are necessary to confirm causality and direction of effect of the observed association. Registration PROSPERO registration number, CRD420261279540. ABBREVIATIONS AND ACRONYMS.

Title: Cardiovascular remodeling in spaceflight: Mechanotransduction, space radiation, and countermeasure strategies.
Journal: Progress in biophysics and molecular biology
Abstract: Protecting cardiovascular function during longer missions beyond low Earth orbit requires understanding how altered loading and radiation affect the heart and vasculature. Evidence spans astronaut physiology and experimental models, but the links between molecular responses, tissue remodeling and functional impairment remain incompletely resolved. This narrative review integrates human observations, unloading analogs, real-flight experiments and mechanistic studies to distinguish exposure-related responses from demonstrated cardiovascular remodeling and to assess their relevance to countermeasures. Human studies show reduced cardiac work with preserved structure under studied countermeasure regimens, variable recovery across endpoints and no persistent vascular abnormalities in a small long-term cohort. Experimental systems identify endothelial, vascular smooth muscle, and matrix mechanisms that can be tested against these physiological observations, although the contributions of these mechanisms to astronaut outcomes remain uncertain. For exploration beyond low Earth orbit, combined radiation-unloading studies further show that cardiovascular effects depend on the model, endpoint and recovery interval, limiting predictions from either stressor alone. Countermeasure studies likewise show that preserved fitness can coexist with impaired orthostatic tolerance. Together, these findings support the assessment of cardiovascular risk and protection through specific functional trajectories rather than molecular changes alone. Progress requires longitudinal human phenotyping, factorial exposure studies, and mechanistic perturbation in calibrated human tissue models, with countermeasure efficacy evaluated against the functions that missions require crews to maintain.

Title: Towards the diagnostic scores we need in ATTR-CM: Editorial for the article: Comparison of three scoring systems in the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in a HFpEF cohort.
Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis versus anticoagulation alone in intermediate-high risk pulmonary embolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USAT) may enhance right ventricular recovery in intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, but evidence is limited.
OBJECTIVES: We compared the safety, efficacy, and net benefit of USAT versus standard anticoagulation.
METHODS: We analysed a propensity-matched prospective cohort of 432 intermediate-high-risk patients (216 USAT vs 216 anticoagulation) from the Italian USAT-HI and OPTIRAPE registries. Outcomes included all- cause, cardiovascular (CV) and PE-related death, major bleedings, and a composite net clinical benefit (NCB), with a day-7 landmark analysis distinguishing early (0-7 days) from late (8-30 days) events. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression with Hazard ratios (HRs) and relative 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Baseline demographics (mean age 64 ± 12 years; 48% female) and comorbidities were balanced between cohorts. USAT was associated with lower all-cause (7.4% vs 13.9%; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.01), cardiovascular (3.2% vs 8.3%; HR 0.39; p < 0.001), and PE-related mortality (2.3% vs 6.5%; HR 0.34; p = 0.02) compared with anticoagulation. Major bleeding was similar (2.7% vs 1.9%; p = 0.56). USAT significantly improved net clinical benefit (13.4% vs 25.9%; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.001), mainly driven by reductions in early mortality and clinical deterioration. Landmark analysis indicated that benefits were largely confined to the first 7 days, with favourable but non-significant effects during days 8-30.
CONCLUSIONS: In intermediate-high-risk PE, USAT was associated with lower early mortality, improved net clinical outcomes, and a safety profile comparable to standard anticoagulation.

Title: Fundus torsion in strabismus: measurement, clinical interpretation, and emerging imaging approaches.
Abstract: Fundus torsion is an important but underused anatomical marker in strabismus evaluation, particularly for cyclovertical disorders. Unlike subjective cyclodeviation testing, fundus-based assessment provides an objective reference based on retinal landmarks, though it remains influenced by image acquisition, head position, ocular anatomy, and measurement conventions. We synthesize the anatomical basis of ocular and fundus torsion, contemporary qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, and disease-specific evidence across superior oblique palsy, pattern strabismus, pediatric and adult strabismus, and surgical follow-up. The review emphasizes 3 clinically important issues: the frequent dissociation between objective fundus torsion and subjective cyclodeviation, the need for method-specific interpretation using reproducibility and minimal-detectable-change data, and the importance of avoiding isolated treatment decisions based on anatomical torsion alone. Recent optical coherence tomography-based and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve measurement consistency and scalability, but current evidence supports their use as adjunctive tools rather than autonomous decision systems. Fundus torsion should therefore be interpreted within a multimodal clinical framework that integrates motility findings, sensory status, age, chronicity, fixation behavior, and surgical history. Treatment options include observation and symptom relief in selected patients, inferior oblique weakening for associated overaction, and torsion-directed surgery for persistent symptomatic excyclotorsion; comparative evidence remains limited. Prospective comparative treatment studies are a clinical research priority. Standardized acquisition protocols, explicit reporting conventions, age- and population-specific normative data, externally validated automated methods, and prospective studies linking torsional change to symptoms and functional outcomes are needed to strengthen the clinical utility of fundus torsion assessment.

Title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: a competing-risk analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray's test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P<.001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P<.001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P=.002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P=.030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 0.74-1.70), whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

Title: Insulin Dependence Erodes the Cardiac and Survival Advantage of Asymptomatic Status After Carotid Revascularization.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent (IDDM) and non-insulin-dependent DM (NIDDM) with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid artery stenting (CAS), stratified by symptom status.
METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed January 2005-January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. Endpoints were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs).
RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) NIDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days there were 1,645 MIs, 2,051 ipsilateral strokes, 1,806 deaths, 3,626 strokes or deaths, and 5,029 MACE; at 1 year, 2,378, 2,924, 8,269, 10,750, and 12,646, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR 1.24), mortality (OR 1.19), and MACE (OR 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE OR 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P<0.001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR 1.54, P<0.001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR 1.05, P=0.41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR 1.19, P<0.001). Relative to CEA, TCAR and CAS were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR 2.10 and 1.93, respectively, P≤0.01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every endpoint.
CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival endpoints, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable to symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

Title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly amid conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI.
METHODS: We utilized the NIS (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. Our outcomes evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs. endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. Mann-Kendal trend tested monotonic temporal trends.
RESULTS: An estimated 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations were included (mean age 69.7 years, 40.0% women, 69.5% White). Overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with reversal and steady rise thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations included revascularization (n=14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n=16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization decreased (ptrend=0.016), while endovascular remained stable (ptrend=0.368), and hospitalizations without revascularization increased (ptrend=0.016) over time. Endovascular revascularization rates did rise among females, non-frail patients, and those presenting with rest pain (all ptrend>0.05). Overall, in-hospital amputation (n=6,270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n=1,086 [2.3%]) remained stable (ptrend>0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased most substantially among hospitalizations without revascularization (ptrend=0.007).
CONCLUSION: We provide contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. Relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings underscore the need for further investigation into optimal CLTI patient selection and coordinated integration of non-operative care, such as medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

Title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the incidence of poor responsiveness to VEGF-A suppression in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) by evaluating the effect of continuous delivery of ranibizumab via the Port Delivery Platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in individual patients enrolled in the Pagoda clinical trial.
DESIGN: Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical trial data SUBJECTS: DME patients enrolled in Pagoda (NCT04108156).
METHODS: Change in central subfield thickness (CST) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over time was evaluated for the adjusted intent-to-treat (aITT) population in the Pagoda trial. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images obtained at each visit were analyzed for 56 PDS subjects from 8 sites to determine the time course of changes in intraretinal and subretinal fluid.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: CST, BCVA, and time to resolution of edema.
RESULTS: In the aITT population the mean duration of follow up was 107.7 weeks in the PDS arm (n=272) and 100.7 weeks the IVT-PDS arm (n=238). The percentage of eyes with CST improvement into the normal range (≤325 µm) by the last visit was 87.9% in the PDS group and 85.3% in the IVT-PDS arm with mean time to normalization of 21.3 weeks and 20.6 weeks, respectively. All eyes in both arms showed reduction in CST over time although some exhibited periods of CST fluctuation and a few in each arm showed initial improvement followed by worsening at last follow up. In the eyes of 56 PDS patients that had detailed analysis of OCTs, normalization of CST occurred in 93% at a median of 17 weeks and elimination of intraretinal fluid in the central 1mm occurred in 84% at a median of 68 weeks. Only 3 of 56 eyes had poorly controlled DME at last follow up.
CONCLUSIONS: Sustained suppression of VEGF-A is sufficient to effectively treat DME in the vast majority of patients, but edema resolution may be slow in some patients giving the false impression of poor response to anti-VEGF-A treatment. In DME, the term unresponsive to anti-VEGF-A treatment should be replaced by slowly responsive.

Title: Videolaryngoscopy versus direct laryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures (NasoVISI): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nasotracheal intubation is a common procedure for infants undergoing surgery, and successful intubation at first attempt reduces the risk of complications. First-attempt success is improved with videolaryngoscopy compared with direct laryngoscopy in infants requiring orotracheal intubation, but the value of videolaryngoscopy in infants requiring nasotracheal intubation is unknown. We aimed to compare first-attempt success of nasotracheal intubation by videolaryngoscopy and direct laryngoscopy in infants undergoing cardiac procedures.
METHODS: In this multicentre, parallel group, randomised controlled trial across eight paediatric cardiac centres in the USA, we enrolled infants aged 365 days or younger without anticipated difficult airways requiring nasotracheal intubation for elective cardiothoracic surgery or cardiac catheterisation. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy using permuted block randomisation stratified by site. The primary outcome was first-attempt intubation success rate. Analysis was by modified intention to treat using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering within intubating clinicians. Complications associated with first attempt and across all attempts were compared between groups with the same marginal models as the primary outcome analysis. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05433155) and is closed to new participants.
FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024, 684 infants were randomly assigned, of whom 673 were included in the primary outcome analysis: 340 in the videolaryngoscopy group and 333 in the direct laryngoscopy group. 311 (46%) participants were female, 362 (54%) were male, and 457 (68%) were White. The median age was 14·04 weeks (IQR 1·48-22·89) and the mean weight was 4·77 kg (SD 1·74). First-attempt success was higher in the videolaryngoscopy group than in the direct laryngoscopy group (281 [83%] vs 249 [75%]; adjusted risk difference 8·2% [95% CI 2·0-14·3], p=0·0093). First-attempt complications occurred in 85 (13%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (45 [13%] vs 40 [12%]; 0·4% [-3·5 to 4·3], p=0·83). Considering all attempts cumulatively, any complication occurred in 94 (14%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (46 [14%] vs 48 [14%]; -1·9% [-6·0 to 2·3], p=0·38). No cases of cardiac arrest or death occurred in either group.
INTERPRETATION: Improved first-attempt success rates with videolaryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures add to growing evidence favouring videolaryngoscopy as the first-line technique for tracheal intubation in infants. Key remaining questions for ongoing research include whether this benefit extends to infants with difficult airways and at non-specialist centres or urgent settings, and how clinician training should evolve as videolaryngoscopy becomes standard practice.
FUNDING: Anesthesia Patient Safety Foundation and The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

Title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.
METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.
FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.
INTERPRETATION: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings.
FUNDING: The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

Title: Reference ranges of the fetal ductus arteriosus area by Three-Dimensional ultrasonography.
Journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine reference values for the fetal ductus arteriosus (DA) area using three-dimensional (3D) ultrasonography with spatio-temporal image correlation (STIC) in the rendering and multiplanar modes.
METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted with 322 cardiac volumes from normal fetuses between 20 and 33 + 6 weeks. DA area measurements were performed in the multiplanar (sagittal B-plane) and rendering modes. Polynomial regression models were fitted and assessed using the coefficient of determination (R2). Reproducibility was assessed by the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman plots, and agreement between modes by Bland-Altman analysis and least products regression.
RESULTS: Patient age ranged from 18 to 45 years, with a median of 29.0 years. The median gestational age at the time of the ultrasound examination was 26.6 weeks (20.0-33.9 weeks). A linear relationship and a significant strong positive correlation were observed between gestational age and DA area measurements in the multiplanar and rendering modes (R2 = 0.54 and 0.53, respectively). Mean DA areas in the multiplanar and rendering modes ranged from 0.06 to 0.32 cm2 and 0.07 to 0.37 cm2, respectively. Intra- and interobserver reliability was good (CCC ≥ 0.72), but relative limits of agreement were wide. The rendering mode yielded larger areas (mean difference -0.028 cm2).
CONCLUSION: Reference curves for the fetal DA area by 3D ultrasonography with STIC in the multiplanar and rendering modes were determined and showed a strong correlation with gestational age. These measurements showed good reliability but wide limits of agreement; the two modes are not interchangeable, and their clinical usefulness remains to be established.

Title: Coronary artery anomalies in computed tomography of coronary arteries for symptomatic patients: Types, prevalence and association with atheromatous disease.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anomalous coronary arteries are rare but potentially dangerous. Early diagnosis and recognition can prevent serious outcomes. Our study aimed to determine the prevalence of coronary artery anomalies amongst symptomatic individuals who presented for computer tomography of coronary arteries (CTCA) and their trends with age and concurrent atherosclerotic disease.
METHODS: Retrospective study of all CTCAs for symptomatic patients was conducted over a 5-year period in a large healthcare network, including a dedicated heart hospital, to identify the types and prevalence of anomalous coronary arteries. Patients' age, symptomology and associated atherosclerotic burden represented by CAD-RADS and calcium scores were compared between the identified individuals with coronary artery anomalies.
RESULTS: A total of 13,596 patients were recruited. 296 (2.18%) patients had significant coronary anomalies. Mean age was 53.85 years. 211/296 (71.28%) patients had anomalous coronary artery origins. 180/296 (60.81%) patients had anomalous coronary artery courses in which 85/180 (47.22%) were potentially malignant (inter-arterial course). There were 25/296 (8.45%) patients with coronary artery fistulae and 12/296 (4.05%) patients with more complex coronary vascular malformations. There was statistical significance between potentially malignant coronary artery course and younger age and trend towards lower CAD-RADS score and Agatston calcium score.
CONCLUSION: Broad variability of incidence of coronary anomalies on imaging has been reported in the literature. To our knowledge, this study is amongst the first to demonstrate a statistically significant association between potentially malignant coronary artery course and younger age on CTCA, with a trend towards lower CAD-RADS score and Agatston calcium score also observed.

Title: Mid-pregnancy plasma environmental chemical exposures and maternal blood pressure in a pilot study of Black women.
Journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
Abstract: Epidemiological evidence suggests Black women experience disproportionate exposure to environmental chemicals and diagnoses of hypertension during pregnancy. We characterized environmental chemicals and determined their associations with blood pressure in a cross-sectional analysis of Black women in Philadelphia. We measured 32 plasma chemicals using non-targeted analysis in samples collected between the 16th and 24th weeks of gestation in the MOMENTUM cohort (n = 68). We assessed the association between log2-transformed chemical abundance and blood pressure, as well as preterm hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), using regression analysis. We categorized chemical abundances into tertiles and modelled them as ordinal variables; blood pressure as a continuous variable; and preterm HDP as a binary variable. We assessed the mixture effect with a Weight Quantile Sum regression constraint in the positive direction. Each increase in one tertile of 4-methylbenzophenone (β = 4.48 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.84, 7.12), 4-tert-Butylcatechol (β = 3.83 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.53, 6.14), benzophenone (β = 4.05 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.49, 6.61), carvone (β = 3.50 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.19, 5.81), and tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (β = 3.98 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.23, 6.74) was cross-sectionally associated with a statistically significant increase in diastolic blood pressure. A mixture of flavoring and fragrance agents also showed a positive association with diastolic blood pressure (β = 3.05 mmHg; 95%CI: 0.60, 4.67). Exposures were not significantly associated with systolic blood pressure and preterm HDP. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require replication in large-scale cohort studies.

Title: Metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, a fatty-liver proxy, inflammation, and apolipoproteins in relation to breast cancer risk in young Korean women: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Greater adiposity is associated with higher postmenopausal but lower premenopausal breast cancer risk; whether its metabolic consequences - insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and atherogenic lipoproteins - follow the same pattern is unresolved. Apolipoproteins, which track with adiposity, have not to our knowledge been evaluated prospectively for premenopausal breast cancer risk in East Asia. We examined these markers in relation to incident breast cancer in Korean women.
METHODS: We followed 99,648 Korean women (91.3% premenopausal) without prior breast cancer attending health screening during 2011-2024. Prespecified exposures were metabolic syndrome component count, the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), a fatty-liver proxy, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and the apolipoprotein B (ApoB) to apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) ratio. Incident breast cancer was ascertained by registry linkage (ICD-10 C50 plus D05). Age-stratified Cox models used sequential adjustment; the primary model included reproductive, anthropometric, and lifestyle covariates.
RESULTS: Over a median 7.75 years of follow-up, 1094 incident breast cancers occurred (28.1% in situ). In the primary model, metabolic syndrome component count (hazard ratio 1.05 per component, 95% CI 0.97-1.14), HOMA-IR (1.01 per log unit, 0.91-1.12), and hs-CRP (0.98 per log unit, 0.90-1.06) were not associated with breast cancer risk; the fatty-liver estimate was uninformative (38 exposed cases). The ApoB/ApoA1 ratio (0.94 per 1 SD, 0.88-1.00) and ApoB (0.94, 0.88-1.00) were inversely but not significantly associated, both attenuating to the null in a 3-year landmark analysis (0.99, 0.92-1.07). ApoB and LDL cholesterol were near-collinear (r = 0.944), precluding specificity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and apolipoprotein markers were not associated with breast cancer risk in this predominantly premenopausal Korean cohort. These sequelae therefore do not appear to share the inverse association adiposity shows before menopause. These are, to our knowledge, the first prospective apolipoprotein data on premenopausal breast cancer risk in East Asian women.

Title: Explainable artificial intelligence in clinical decision support systems: a systematic review of techniques, clinical applications, evaluation, and future directions.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has emerged as an important approach for improving the transparency and interpretability of artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinical decision support systems (CDSSs). However, evidence regarding the models and explainability techniques used in healthcare, their clinical evaluation, methodological quality, and progression toward real-world implementation remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and critically evaluate the current evidence on XAI-enabled CDSSs, with particular emphasis on AI and XAI methods, clinical applications, validation, explainability evaluation, implementation, and methodological limitations.
METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261449460). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from database inception through 30 June 2026 (searches run on 15 July 2026). Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles that applied artificial intelligence within healthcare clinical decision support systems, incorporated at least one explainability or interpretability technique, and demonstrated a direct role in clinical decision-making or decision support. Studies limited to prediction, classification, diagnosis, or prognostic modeling without a decision-support component were excluded. Two reviewers jointly screened titles and abstracts, independently assessed full texts, and independently extracted data using a standardized form informed by the CHARMS checklist. Risk of bias and applicability of prediction model studies were assessed using PROBAST, and reporting completeness was evaluated against relevant TRIPOD + AI recommendations where applicable. Due to substantial clinical, methodological, and statistical heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with SWiM guidance.
RESULTS: Of 2008 identified records, 68 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Publications increased substantially in 2025-2026, accounting for 47 of the 68 included studies. China and India contributed the largest number of studies (11 each), followed by the United States (10). Critical care/intensive care medicine and cardiology were the most frequently represented clinical specialties (13 studies each). Numeric patient-level sample size was reported in 35 studies. Among these, the median sample size was 973 (IQR 303-10,015; range 57-106,449), while the mean was 11,944, indicating a markedly right-skewed distribution. Internal validation was reported in 51 studies (75.0 %), whereas external validation was reported in 17 studies (25.0 %). Most systems remained at the research-prototype stage (n = 63, 92.6 %). One study (1.5 %) reported pilot testing in a clinical workflow, while only two studies (2.9 %) reported real-world or routine clinical deployment. Implementation status was unclear or not reported in two studies (2.9 %). Of the 63 studies for which PROBAST was applicable, 3 (4.8 %) were judged at low overall risk of bias and 3 (4.8 %) at high risk; the remainder were rated Unclear mainly because of incomplete reporting. Five studies describing non-prediction CDSS designs were classified as PROBAST not applicable. Clinician involvement was reported in 53 studies. Formal user studies with structured evaluation protocols were reported in 39 studies (57.4 %), but rigorous assessment of effects on decision quality or patient outcomes remained rare.
CONCLUSIONS: XAI-enabled CDSS research has expanded rapidly, yet remains largely confined to model development and technical explainability rather than rigorous clinical translation. Although SHAP and gradient-boosting methods currently predominate, external validation, real-world deployment, standardized evaluation of explanation quality, and meaningful human-centered assessment are still limited. Future work must prioritize multicenter external validation, transparent reporting, rigorous assessment of explanation fidelity and stability, active clinician and patient involvement, and prospective evaluation of effects on decision-making and patient outcomes. Closing the gap between algorithmic performance and clinically meaningful utility is essential for the safe, trustworthy, and responsible adoption of these systems.

Title: Pathogen identification by shotgun metagenomics in inflammatory myopathies: a prospective observational study reporting the first European case of Anncaliia algerae myositis.
Abstract: This study highlights the utility of shotgun metagenomics (SMg) in the diagnosis of infectious myositis, focusing on a rare case of Anncaliia algerae infection in an immunocompromised patient. This is among the first reports of SMg application in inflammatory myopathies. We conducted a monocentric prospective observational study at Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital (2021-2024), including patients with inflammatory myopathies and suspected infectious etiologies. Diagnosis was based on clinical symptoms, paraclinical findings, myopathological examination, and SMg performed using DNA/RNA sequencing with the Illumina NextSeq 500® sequencing system and the MetaMIC® bioinformatics pipeline. Among nine patients, SMg identified A. algerae in a kidney transplant recipient with severe myositis and myocarditis. Standard microbiological techniques, including blood tests and muscle biopsy staining, failed to accurately identify the pathogen. Despite specific therapy (albendazole), the infection was fatal, underscoring the pathogen's aggressiveness in immunocompromised hosts. Other patients either recovered spontaneously or with immunosuppressants. This study demonstrates the diagnostic advantage of SMg in infectious myopathies, especially for rare pathogens like A. algerae. The unbiased nature of SMg enables pathogen identification when conventional methods fail, guiding targeted treatments. Early SMg use could improve outcomes in immunocompromised patients and warrants integration into diagnostic workflows for inflammatory myopathies. As an unbiased and culture-free pan-pathogenic method, SMg enables the identification of pathogens, including unexpected ones, and can be used in addition to routine procedures for inflammatory myopathy diagnosis.

Title: Radiofrequency ablation for tongue lymphatic malformations in children: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the safety and clinical outcomes of radiofrequency ablation for tongue lymphatic malformations in a paediatric population and to explore predictors of symptom control.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of all paediatric patients who underwent transoral radiofrequency ablation to a tongue lymphatic malformation between 2018 and 2025. The primary outcome of interest was successful control of symptoms with radiofrequency ablation alone. Secondary outcomes of interest included the degree of symptom control, complications following surgery and additional treatment types required. Non-parametric data was analysed using Mann-Whitney U test. Statistical significance was defined as p value < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 44 children were included. Lesions were classified using the Wiegand system. Stage I in 12 patients (27.3%), IIa in 5 (11.4%), IIb in 4 (9.1%), III in 12 (27.3%), IV in 11 (25.0%). Mixed disease predominated at higher stages, with 10 of the 11 stage IV lesions being mixed. Twenty-five (56.8%) patients had mixed microcystic and macrocystic disease whereas 19 patients (43.2%) had isolated microcystic disease. Symptom control with radiofrequency ablation alone was achieved in 73.8% patients (n = 31/42), with 100% Wiegand I patients, 4/5 (80%) Wiegand IIa patients, 4/4 (75%) Wiegand IIb, 7/12 (58.3%) Wiegand III, and 6/10 (60%) Wiegand IV patients achieving symptom control. Older age of first treatment was predictive of symptom control with radiofrequency ablation alone (p = 0.005). No statistically clear associations were observed for sex, prior therapies, or individual pre-operative symptom categories. Symptom improvement was recorded in 93.2% of patients (41/44). No patients reported worsening of symptoms. Nine patients required alternative therapies mainly to treat residual tongue swelling.
CONCLUSIONS: Radiofrequency ablation appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for managing symptomatic microcystic and mixed tongue lymphatic malformations and is useful as part of a multimodal treatment strategy. It was favoured particularly for controlling bleeding and improving surface related symptoms.

Title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy.
STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

Title: Quantitative Measurement of White Matter Hyperintensities in Brain MRI using a Multimodal Boundary-Aware Dual-Task Segmentation Framework.
Abstract: White matter hyperintensity (WMH) subtype segmentation in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous lesion sizes, indistinct boundaries, and severe class imbalance. We propose a multimodal boundary-aware dual-task U-Net for segmenting periventricular (PVWMH), deep (DWMH), and subcortical (SWMH) lesions. The framework integrates FLAIR-T1-weighted feature fusion, Vision Mamba-based feature modeling, an SWMH-specific boundary loss, and auxiliary boundary detection. The method was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a private multicenter cohort (n = 75) and separately on 60 publicly annotated MICCAI WMH Challenge subjects for binary segmentation. On the private cohort, the proposed framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.6081 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 14.80 mm, compared with 0.5638 and 18.25 mm for the FLAIR-only ablation baseline. It also improved SWMH DSC from 0.4610 with nnU-Net to 0.5215 (p = 0.008). On the public dataset, the mean binary DSC and HD95 were 0.6812 and 12.91 mm, respectively.Given the relatively large through-plane voxel spacing (8.4 mm), the framework processes 2D axial slices independently and does not explicitly model inter-slice context, which may limit its ability to characterize lesions extending across adjacent slices.

Title: Second consensus statement on abdominal aortic aneurysms in Mexico.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive and life-threatening disease, with rupture-related mortality reaching up to 80% in Mexico. Limited national epidemiological data and the need to standardize diagnostic, therapeutic, and follow-up strategies prompted the development of the Second National Consensus on AAA in Mexico, coordinated by the Mexican Society of Angiology, Vascular and Endovascular Surgery (SMACVE), based on the Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines and adapted to local practice.
METHODS: The consensus was developed using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method and a modified Delphi process. A panel of national and international experts evaluated 116 statements derived from Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines. Statements were discussed, reformulated when necessary, and subjected to structured voting. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement among participants.
RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for the majority of the evaluated statements, including recommendations on screening, diagnosis, preoperative assessment, medical management, indications for endovascular and open repair, rupture management, perioperative care, follow-up, and organizational aspects. Recommendations were adapted to the clinical practice environment and healthcare resources available within the Mexican healthcare system.
CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides standardized definitions, diagnostic criteria, and management recommendations for AAA care in Mexico, aiming to promote evidence-based, uniform clinical practice adapted to local healthcare conditions.

Title: Estimating Functional Independence Measure Scores From Japanese Rehabilitation Notes Using a Large Language Model: Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Functional Independence Measure (FIM) is a standard functional assessment tool in rehabilitation medicine; however, formal assessments are often conducted only at limited intervals. Free-text clinical notes contain more frequent observations of patients' functional status and may complement these assessments.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate item-level FIM scores from Japanese free-text rehabilitation notes using a locally deployed large language model (LLM) and to evaluate estimation performance; item-level estimability; and differences across diseases, therapy types, and admission FIM severity groups.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed free-text notes from physical therapy (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) for patients hospitalized with cerebral infarction (CeI), hip fracture (HF), or vertebral fracture (VBF) at Saiseikai Moriyama Municipal Hospital between October 2019 and September 2024. Using zero-shot prompting, an LLM estimated all FIM items from each note. Estimated scores were matched to reference FIM scores recorded for the same patient on the same calendar date. Performance was evaluated using the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error, and quadratic weighted kappa. Estimation rates and comparisons with modal-score and last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) baselines were also examined.
RESULTS: Among 2,952,702 eligible note-item pairs from 164,039 retained rehabilitation-note-level outputs, the model produced 980,000 valid estimates, corresponding to an overall estimation rate of 33.2%. Among 170,744 note-item opportunities with an available same-day reference score, 57,246 (33.5%) were estimable, of which 77.7% (44,481/57,246) were within 1 point of the reference score. Estimates derived from OT notes had a lower MAE than those derived from PT notes in CeI and HF, whereas the difference was not significant in VBF. The LLM outperformed the modal-score baseline but had a higher MAE than the LOCF overall (0.825 vs 0.648).
CONCLUSIONS: The locally deployed LLM shows the potential to derive item-level FIM estimates from Japanese rehabilitation notes. Among estimable note-item pairs with a same-day reference FIM score, 77.7% were within 1 point of the reference score. These findings support the potential use of LLM-based estimation to structure functional information contained in routine rehabilitation notes and complement periodic FIM assessments. Further integration of multidisciplinary clinical records and external validation are needed to improve estimability and evaluate its value for longitudinal functional monitoring.

Title: Effectiveness of Wrist-Worn Wearable-Guided Cardiac Rehabilitation Delivered Through Fully Remote or Hybrid Programs in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) remains suboptimal. Wrist-worn wearables may support fully remote or hybrid CR through activity monitoring and individualized feedback, but the effectiveness and consistency of benefits remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs initiated during phase II or III CR in patients with CVD.
METHODS: A total of 8 databases were searched for randomized controlled trials published from January 1, 2015, through August 7, 2026. Eligible trials enrolled adults with CVD and integrated a wrist-worn wearable into fully remote or hybrid CR. Studies focused primarily on heart failure or using wearables only for outcome measurement were excluded. Primary outcomes were peak oxygen consumption (VO2), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), and daily steps. Random-effects meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs), except for quality of life, which used standardized MDs. Between-study variance was estimated using the DerSimonian-Laird method, pooled-effect CIs used the Knapp-Hartung adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) used the Nagashima-Noma-Furukawa parametric bootstrap method. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane Risk of Bias 2. Subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses explored study and intervention characteristics.
RESULTS: A total of 18 trials involving 1993 randomized participants, reported in 20 publications, were included; 17 contributed to meta-analysis. Pooled estimates favored wearable-guided CR for peak VO2 (10 studies; 591 participants; MD 1.69, 95% CI 0.46-2.92, 95% PI -2.21 to 5.39 mL/kg/min), 6MWD (9 studies; 1094 participants; MD 31.03, 95% CI 7.66-53.92, 95% PI -62.11 to 123.18 m), and daily steps (8 studies; 474 participants; MD 1062.8, 95% CI 383.5-1825.0, 95% PI -503.0 to 2860.0 steps/day). All 3 PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future comparable settings. No clear pooled effects were observed for anaerobic threshold, BMI, waist circumference, grip strength, or quality of life. Subgroup differences were not statistically significant. In univariable meta-regression, a higher proportion of female participants was associated with greater peak VO2 improvement, although this aggregate-level finding was exploratory.
CONCLUSIONS: Wrist-worn wearable-guided CR delivered through fully remote or hybrid programs may improve average exercise capacity and physical activity in patients with CVD. However, PIs included the null, indicating uncertainty about consistency across future settings. These programs may extend activity monitoring, individualized feedback, and behavioral support beyond center-based CR, but their multicomponent nature prevents attributing effects to wearables alone. Larger, rigorously designed trials with standardized protocols and outcomes should identify the patients and program components most likely to benefit. Future research should also evaluate long-term adherence, safety, equity, and implementation within routine multidisciplinary CR across diverse health systems.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Anti-Müllerian Hormone Trajectories Across the Menopause Transition.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the trajectory of anti-müllerian hormone (AMH) decline leading to the final menstrual period, identify distinct AMH patterns, and assess their association with unique participant characteristics.
METHODS: SWAN (Study of Women's Health Across the Nation), a multisite, multiethnic perimenopausal cohort, was analyzed. Included participants had an observed final menstrual period and three or more measurements of AMH levels taken during perimenopause. Statistical modeling was used to identify AMH trajectory classes; participants were placed into predicted class based on best fit. Differences in baseline demographic and health characteristics were assessed by analysis of variance or χ2.
