We used exploratory multivariable models to identify GP and FA-related features associated with the detected pathogenic LDLR variant status. The models showed within-cohort discrimination. However, these models were developed and evaluated in the same small cohort after data-driven variable selection. They were not externally validated. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and do not establish diagnostic performance, clinical utility, or functional pathway impairment. Further validation in larger cohorts using targeted lipidomics with chromatographic separation is necessary.

Title: Empagliflozin and Metformin Combination Therapy Attenuates Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Experimental Cardio-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome.
Abstract: This study evaluated the therapeutic effects of the empagliflozin+metformin (E+M) combination on cardio-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKMS) using an experimental model. Animals were fed a Paigen-type (high-fat) diet supplemented with sugar-sweetened beverages to induce the CKMS phenotype. After confirming metabolic, cardiovascular, and renal alterations, animals were randomized into untreated and E+M-treated groups for 30 days while continuing the diet. Cardiovascular risk factors, vasoactive substances in the heart and kidney, oxidative stress, and the expression of inflammatory markers and the lipogenic transcription factors ChREBP and SREBP1 were analyzed. The E+M combination reduced body weight, hyperglycemia, fasting glucose, and hypertension, while restoring the lipid profile and improving oral glucose tolerance and renal function (p < 0.05). It also reduced posterior wall and interventricular septal thickening, as well as the elevated septum/posterior wall (PP/PS) ratio observed in the CKMS group (p < 0.05). Likewise, the increases in angiotensin II and nitric oxide concentrations in the hearts and kidneys were attenuated (p < 0.05). The CKMS group exhibited glomerular hypertrophy and reduced total antioxidant capacity mitochondrial complex I and II activities, glutathione peroxidase, glutathione reductase, and superoxide dismutase activities, and Nrf2 and IL-10 expression, all of which were restored by combination therapy (p < 0.05). In contrast, the upregulation of IGF-1, aldose reductase, sorbitol dehydrogenase, ChREBP, IL-6, TNFα, and NF-κB observed in the CKMS group was reduced following E+M treatment (p < 0.05). Overall, the E+M combination attenuated metabolic alterations and suppressed renal oxidative stress and inflammation, providing cardiac and renal protection at both functional and structural levels. These effects appear to be mediated by the modulation of key proteins involved in vascular tone, uric acid metabolism, oxidative stress, inflammation, and regulation of transcription factors involved in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism.

Title: Nutritional Programming via Maternal Protein Restriction Mitigates Long-Term Consequences of Acute Kidney Injury.
Abstract: The kidney is highly sensitive to prenatal and early-life environmental influences. Maternal protein restriction (MPR) can alter renal development and may modify susceptibility to chronic kidney disease (CKD) following acute kidney injury (AKI). We investigated whether MPR during gestation and/or lactation influences the progression from AKI to CKD after renal ischemia-reperfusion (IR) in rat offspring. Fifty Wistar pregnant rats were fed a control (20% casein) or protein-restricted (10% casein) diet during gestation, with diets maintained or switched during lactation, generating four maternal nutritional groups (CC, CR, RC, and RR). At 280-330 g body weight, offspring from these groups were randomly assigned to left renal IR plus right nephrectomy (CC + IR, CR + IR, RC + IR, and RR + IR) or right nephrectomy alone (CC, CR, RC, and RR). Renal outcomes were assessed in two independent cohorts of rats at 7 days and 5 months after surgery. Offspring from MPR during gestation and/or lactation (CR + IR, RC + IR, and RR + IR) showed reduced susceptibility to AKI-to-CKD progression compared to the CC + IR group, characterized by attenuated proteinuria, absence of glomerular hypertrophy, and minimal renal fibrosis. This protective phenotype was associated with reduced oxidative stress and endoplasmic reticulum stress, as indicated by lower 4-HNE, CHOP, and BiP, together with enhanced post-ischemic repair reflected by lower urinary KIM-1 and Hsp72 excretion. MPR during gestation and/or lactation induces a persistent renal phenotype in the offspring that confers resistance to AKI-to-CKD progression, potentially through modulation of oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum stress. These findings highlight developmental nutritional programming as a previously underappreciated determinant of renal resilience in offspring after AKI and provide a basis for investigating nutritional and developmental mechanisms that may be targeted to prevent CKD after AKI.

Title: CYBA Gene Polymorphisms, Lipid Parameters and Atherogenic Indices: A Cohort Study of Healthy Individuals Without Prior Lipid-Lowering Therapy.
Abstract: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the CYBA gene, encoding the p22phox subunit of vascular NADPH oxidases, have been associated with atherosclerosis-related disorders. This association may partly reflect their involvement in lipid metabolism. We investigated the effects of seven CYBA SNPs (rs7195830, rs1049255, rs4673, rs13306296, rs72811418, rs16966671, and rs9932581) on systemic lipid profiles (total cholesterol, HDL-C, LDL-C, and triglycerides) and six lipid-derived atherogenic indices in 220 blood donors who had never received lipid-lowering therapy. Genotyping was performed using PCR-RFLP and TaqMan PCR. Serum lipid concentrations were determined by enzymatic colorimetric methods. For all SNPs, in silico analyses assessed allele-specific binding (ASB) of transcription factors (TFs) and gene expression in cardiovascular tissues. Statistically significant differences in lipid parameters were observed among the rs7195830, rs1049255, and rs13306296 variants. In silico analyses indicated ASB of TFs for rs1049255 and rs13306296 and genotype-dependent effects of rs13306296 and rs4673 on CYBA expression. Notably, the G allele/GG genotype of rs13306296 was associated with the least favorable lipid profile across multiple parameters, preferential binding of thirteen TFs, and increased CYBA expression in aorta and heart tissues. In conclusion, CYBA variants influence the systemic lipid profile and lipid-derived atherogenic markers in individuals untreated with lipid-lowering drugs, potentially through modulation of CYBA expression.

Title: Reversibility of Male Factor Infertility: Mechanisms and Evidence from the Literature.
Abstract: Male factor infertility contributes to approximately 50% of reproductive failure in couples worldwide. We conducted a narrative critical review synthesizing evidence from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, and clinical practice guidelines on reversible and irreversible causes of male infertility, examining hormonal, surgical, pharmacological, lifestyle, and drug-induced etiologies. The majority of identifiable etiologies demonstrate some degree of reversibility. Varicocele (prevalence 25-40% in infertile men) achieves natural pregnancy rates of 30-40% after varicocelectomy. Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism responds to gonadotropin therapy with spermatogenesis induction in 90-95% of cases. Obstructive azoospermia achieves ductal patency rates of 85-97% with microsurgical reconstruction. Male accessory gland inflammation is reversible with prompt antibiotic therapy. Spermiotoxic drug exposures-including anabolic-androgenic steroids, sulfasalazine, and chemotherapy-show variable reversibility depending on agent and duration of exposure. Normogonadotropic normotestosteronemic oligozoospermia represents a commonly encountered phenotype that may respond to empirical medical therapy. Lifestyle modifications demonstrate measurable benefits in selected patients. Irreversible causes include Klinefelter syndrome, Y-chromosome AZFa/b microdeletions, and severe post-chemotherapy damage. Systematic andrological evaluation, including comprehensive drug history, is essential to identify treatable causes and guide clinical management.

Title: The Impact of Vitamin E Intake on Cardiometabolic Outcomes of Testosterone Replacement Therapy in Men with Late-Onset Hypogonadism.
Abstract: Androgen deficiency is associated with an increased risk of cardiometabolic complications, whereas vitamin E may exert protective effects against cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. This pilot prospective cohort study examined whether cardiometabolic outcomes observed during exogenous testosterone therapy differed according to vitamin E intake in men with insufficient endogenous testosterone production. Three cohorts of men with late-onset hypogonadism (LOH) (n = 29 per group), matched for age, smoking status, body mass index, and baseline testosterone concentration, were classified according to vitamin E intake as low, adequate, or high; 29 men without LOH served as controls. Men with LOH received intramuscular testosterone injections every three weeks for six months. Cardiometabolic parameters were assessed before and after treatment, including biochemical markers, carotid intima-media thickness, retinal vascular sclerotic changes, and estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk. Compared with controls, men with LOH had higher HOMA-IR, LDL cholesterol, uric acid, fibrinogen, homocysteine, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), carotid intima-media thickness, and estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk. Elevations in homocysteine, hsCRP, and UACR were more pronounced in men with low or high vitamin E intake than in those with adequate intake. Testosterone levels increased during treatment in all groups. Improvements were observed in most cardiometabolic parameters in men with adequate vitamin E intake, whereas changes were limited to HOMA-IR in those with low intake. In men with high intake, no significant changes were observed except for a decrease in HDL cholesterol. At study completion, carotid intima-media thickness and retinal vascular sclerotic changes in men with adequate vitamin E intake did not differ significantly from those in controls. Changes in assessed risk factors correlated with increases in testosterone levels and mean daily vitamin E intake. These findings suggest an association between vitamin E intake and cardiometabolic outcomes observed during testosterone therapy in men with testosterone deficiency.

Title: The Prognostic Value of the Endothelial Activation and Stress Index in Stable Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
Abstract: Background: Endothelial dysfunction and chronic inflammation are central pathophysiological mechanisms in the development of idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH). EASIX, the endothelial activation and stress index, is a simple and recently introduced score that captures endothelial activation and systemic stress. EASIX has been shown to be associated with several cardiovascular conditions. We investigated the relationship between EASIX and clinical outcomes in stable patients with IPAH. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed a total of 256 stable patients with IPAH in this single-center prevalent cohort. EASIX was calculated from lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and platelet count. The optimal cut-off of EASIX was derived by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis in this cohort without external validation. Its association with all-cause mortality was assessed with ROC analysis, Kaplan-Meier estimates, and Cox regression models adjusted for age, sex, World Health Organization (WHO) functional class (WHO-FC), 6-min walking distance (6-MWD), and N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and its incremental value with Harrell's C-index. Results: Forty-one patients (16.0%) died during a median follow-up of 35 (interquartile range 21-46) months. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, EASIX was independently associated with all-cause mortality both as a continuous variable (Model 1; hazard ratio (HR) per 1-unit increase 1.528, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.255-1.860; p < 0.001) and when dichotomized at ≥1.23 (Model 2; HR 3.989, 95% CI 1.962-8.111; p < 0.001). Adding EASIX to a model with WHO-FC, 6-MWD, and NT-proBNP changed Harrell's C-index from 0.784 to 0.812 (likelihood-ratio test p < 0.001). The patients with higher EASIX had worse functional capacity, right ventricular function, and hemodynamics. WHO-FC III-IV and logNT-proBNP were also independently associated with all-cause mortality. Conclusions: In this single-center cohort of patients with IPAH, higher EASIX was associated with more advanced disease and was independently associated with long-term all-cause mortality. Its incremental value over established risk-stratification tools and the reproducibility of the data-derived cut-off require external validation.

Title: The Silent Face of Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review of Associated Factors, Clinical Phenotype, and Outcomes.
Abstract: Background: Asymptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) is increasingly recognized through incidental diagnosis and continuous rhythm monitoring, yet its clinical phenotype and prognostic significance remain incompletely characterized. We systematically evaluated factors associated with asymptomatic AF and its clinical outcomes. Methods: This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 recommendations. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and EMBASE were searched from inception through 1 September 2026. Studies reporting demographic, clinical, anthropometric, laboratory, electrocardiographic, imaging, or therapeutic correlates of asymptomatic AF and/or associated clinical outcomes were eligible. Given substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, evidence was synthesized using structured qualitative analyses and descriptive summaries of study-level data, without formal meta-analysis or inferential testing of aggregated between-group differences. Results: Twenty-three studies were included, comprising 47,456 patients with asymptomatic or subclinical AF and 126,894 participants in the corresponding comparator groups. Study-specific evidence identified male sex, lower ventricular rate, and long-standing persistent or permanent AF as relevant correlates of asymptomatic presentation. Greater left atrial remodeling, including larger atrial dimensions and impaired mechanical function, was also reported in selected studies of silent AF, whereas conventional left ventricular structure and systolic function showed relatively similar descriptive estimates across the available datasets. Selected studies identified metabolic biomarkers and thoracic morphology as additional potential correlates. Rhythm-control strategies and catheter ablation showed numerically lower utilization in descriptive summaries of asymptomatic AF, although the contributing populations were heterogeneous and not necessarily directly comparable. Prognostic findings were heterogeneous: mortality and thromboembolic outcomes were generally comparable between asymptomatic and symptomatic AF in several individual studies, whereas other investigations reported a greater burden of heart failure and heart failure-related events among symptomatic patients. Conclusions: Asymptomatic AF represents a heterogeneous clinical phenotype rather than a benign form of the arrhythmia. A lower ventricular response may attenuate symptom perception, while atrial remodeling and cardiovascular risk may progress despite the absence of symptoms. Symptom status should therefore not replace established cardiovascular risk assessment. Thoracic geometry may represent an additional determinant of symptom perception, although current evidence remains preliminary and requires prospective validation.

Title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Use in Confirmed Acute Aortic Syndrome: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study at the Ljubljana Emergency Medical Unit.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in emergency care, but data on its use in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) remains limited. This single-center retrospective cohort described POCUS use among patients with confirmed AAS and explored factors associated with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup. Methods: Records coded ICD10 I71.0-I71.8 from the Emergency Medical Unit, University Medical Centre Ljubljana (2019-2023) were reviewed. Clinical, imaging, and outcome data were extracted, and diagnoses were confirmed by two investigators through manual chart review of ED documentation, radiology reports, and specialist consultation notes. Fisher's exact and Wilcoxon rank sum tests were used for comparisons. Associations with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup (defined from arrival at triage to completion of the emergency department workup) were assessed with univariable logistic regression and linear regression models, respectively. Survival was explored using univariable Cox proportional-hazards models. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results: Among 120,109 emergency department visits, 73 patients had confirmed AAS (type A: 48; type B: 17; intramural hematoma: 8). POCUS was performed in 62% of patients, more often in those who were hemodynamically unstable (87.5% vs. 54.4%; p = 0.020) or had unclear presentations (40% vs. 7%; p = 0.003). Median time to completion of diagnostic workup was shorter with POCUS (110 vs. 213 min), though not statistically significant (p = 0.069). Hemodynamic instability was associated with higher odds of POCUS use (OR 5.87, 95% CI 1.22-28.2; p = 0.028), whereas a clear clinical presentation was associated with lower odds of POCUS use (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.55; p = 0.007). Lower triage level was associated with longer time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 5.43, 95% CI 2.21-13.4; p < 0.001 for urgent vs. immediate triage), whereas very high D-dimer levels were associated with shorter time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93; p = 0.031 for highest vs. lowest quartile). In-hospital mortality was 14%, with only age associated with mortality (HR 1.06 per year, 95% CI 1.02-1.11; p = 0.007). Conclusions: In this single-center retrospective AAS cohort, POCUS was used more frequently in unstable and diagnostically unclear patients but was not associated with time to completion of diagnostic workup. Findings are descriptive and exploratory; they do not establish that POCUS accelerates diagnosis or improves outcomes.

Title: A Self-Care Mobile Application for Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
Abstract: Background: Mobile health applications may support self-care following acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), particularly when conventional healthcare contact is limited. We evaluated the integration of the Aintree Heart Failure Passport (AHFP) application into a specialist ambulatory ADHF pathway and described self-care behaviour, medication adherence and 30-day heart failure rehospitalisation among app users. Methods: This prospective, single-centre observational study included consecutive patients treated with day-case intravenous diuretics in a consultant-led ambulatory heart failure unit at a UK university hospital between March 2020 and July 2021. Patients with access to a smartphone were offered the AHFP application. Self-care behaviour and medication adherence were assessed two weeks after presentation using the nine-item European Heart Failure Self-care Behaviour Scale (EHFScB-9) and five-item Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5), respectively. Thirty-day HF hospitalisation among application users was compared with a separate cohort of hospitalised HF patients recorded in the National Heart Failure Audit (73/382, 19.1%). This inpatient cohort was used as a contextual benchmark rather than a matched control group. Results: Of 221 consecutive patients treated for ADHF, 148 (67%) downloaded and registered with the AHFP application. Their mean age was 62 ± 6.1 years, and 45% were women. At two weeks, the mean EHFScB-9 score was 19.1 ± 6.7, and the mean MARS-5 score was 23.3 ± 1.0. Within 30 days, 16 patients (10.8%; 95% CI 6.8-16.8%) were hospitalised with HF, accounting for 73 inpatient bed-days. The corresponding 30-day readmission rate in the separate inpatient audit cohort was 19.1% (73/382). Conclusions: The AHFP application was downloaded and registered by 67% of patients treated within an ambulatory ADHF pathway. Self-care behaviour and medication adherence were assessed at two weeks. The observed 30-day HF hospitalisation rate was lower than that of a separate inpatient audit cohort, although differences in patient selection and care setting preclude attribution to the application. These findings support the feasibility of integrating a self-care application into specialist ambulatory HF care and warrant further evaluation in controlled studies.

Title: Impact of Chronic Heart Failure on Vascular Responsiveness: A Prospective Observational In Vivo and Ex Vivo Study in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
Abstract: Background: Patients with chronic heart failure (HF) are at increased risk of vasoplegia after cardiac surgery, potentially because neurohormonal activation in the context of HF alters vascular regulation. Methods: We compared perioperative vasoresponsiveness in patients with and without HF undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Patients were prospectively enrolled, and changes in systemic vascular resistance (ΔSVR) after phenylephrine and nitroglycerin were measured perioperatively (in vivo). Ex vivo vasoreactivity to phenylephrine and vasopressin was tested in 40 biopsies. Results: In vivo and ex vivo analyses included 36 and 13 patients (10 controls and 3 HF patients), respectively. At baseline, phenylephrine increased SVR by 26% in HF patients (estimated marginal mean, 95% CI 16-35%) versus 51% in controls (95% CI 38-64%; p = 0.002). This attenuated response persisted during CPB, and ex vivo observations suggested a similar pattern. Responsiveness to nitroglycerin was unchanged. Lower post-CPB ΔSVR was associated with greater norepinephrine use during the first postoperative day (β = -346.6, 95% CI -541.2 to -151.9; R2 = 0.291). Conversely, HF patients showed greater ex vivo responsiveness to vasopressin. Conclusions: HF is associated with marked impairment of α1-adrenergic vasoresponsiveness, indicating impaired α1-adrenergic signaling. Preserved vasopressin responsiveness may support its earlier use for postoperative hypotension in these patients.

Title: Initial Clip Selection and Outcomes After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Single-Center Experience.
Abstract: Background: Whether the initial clip type selected during transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) of the mitral valve-grasping width and arm length-independently influences procedural and echocardiographic outcomes remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 138 consecutive patients undergoing mitral TEER. The first implanted clip was classified as narrow standard-length (NT), long narrow-arm (XT), or long wide-arm (XTW). Determinants of initial clip selection and its association with procedural success (residual mitral regurgitation [MR] ≤ 1+), post-procedural transmitral gradient, and the need for ≥2 clips were assessed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Results: Median age was 74.0 (66.0-80.0), 74.5 (66.0-82.5), and 75.0 (70.0-79.0) years, and median LVEF was 35.0% (30.0-50.0), 30.0% (25.0-45.0), and 40.0% (25.0-45.0), for the NT, XT, and XTW groups, respectively; 66% of patients overall were male. An XTW clip was implanted first in 61.6% of patients. XTW selection was independently associated with larger effective regurgitant orifice area, lower LVEF, longer posterior leaflet length, and secondary MR (all p < 0.05), whereas NT selection favored younger age, smaller orifice, and higher LVEF. After adjustment for these factors, no statistically significant independent association was detected between initial clip type and residual MR ≥2+, post-procedural transmitral gradient, or the need for additional clips (all p > 0.05); however, confidence intervals were wide. On univariable analysis, larger left atrial size and moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation were associated with residual MR ≥ 2+, but neither remained significant after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions: Initial clip selection was associated with valve anatomy, LVEF and MR etiology. No statistically significant independent association between initial clip type and procedural or short-term echocardiographic outcomes was detected in this cohort. Given the observational design, confounding by indication, limited sample size and wide confidence intervals, clinically relevant effects cannot be excluded, and these findings do not establish the superiority or equivalence of any clip-selection strategy.

Title: Association of Anterior Ventricular Aneurysm and D-Dimer with Intracardiac Thrombus in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Retrospective Analysis.
Abstract: Background: Intracardiac thrombus is a clinically important complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), particularly in patients with ventricular aneurysm. We examined the contemporaneous associations of anterior ventricular involvement and D-dimer with echocardiographically documented intracardiac thrombus with incomplete chamber-specific localization among hospitalized AMI patients with ventricular aneurysm. Methods: This retrospective analysis included 1684 patients with documented ventricular aneurysm from a final cohort of 17,950 hospitalized AMI patients treated between January 2018 and October 2025. The first D-dimer measurement obtained at our hospital after AMI confirmation was used for D-dimer analyses. Ventricular aneurysm and intracardiac thrombus status were determined from the available echocardiographic documentation during the index hospitalization. Aneurysm locations were coded as linked patient-level, non-mutually exclusive indicators. Logistic regression evaluated anterior involvement; missing model covariates were multiply imputed and regression estimates were pooled using Rubin's rules. Collinearity diagnostics and sensitivity analyses restricted to patients with apical aneurysm, including a complete-case analysis, were performed. Model-performance measures were interpreted as exploratory apparent performance in the development dataset. Results: Intracardiac thrombus was documented in 211 of 1684 patients (12.5%). Anterior involvement was more frequent among patients with thrombus than among those without thrombus (57.3% vs. 45.0%; p < 0.001) and remained associated with thrombus in the primary anatomical and clinical model (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.20-2.21; p = 0.002). D-dimer was available in 1633 patients. On the log2-transformed scale, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with higher odds of echocardiographically documented intracardiac thrombus (adjusted OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.14-1.34; p < 0.001). As a complementary descriptive analysis, the observed thrombus proportion increased from 3.63% in Q1 to 22.30% in Q4; compared with Q1, the adjusted ORs were 3.71, 5.22, and 9.50 in Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. The combined model had a mean apparent AUC of 0.716, compared with 0.713 for the model containing D-dimer without anterior involvement; the mean absolute increment was approximately 0.003. Conclusions: Among hospitalized patients with AMI and ventricular aneurysm, higher D-dimer levels and anterior ventricular involvement were associated with echocardiographically documented intracardiac thrombus. Chamber-specific localization was incomplete, and these contemporaneous associations do not establish causality or prospective prediction. Anterior involvement provided minimal incremental discrimination beyond D-dimer.

Title: Takotsubo Syndrome in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: Current Evidence, Clinical Challenges, and Future Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute and usually reversible form of myocardial dysfunction associated with emotional or physical stress. Solid organ transplantation (SOT) combines several potential triggers, including major surgical stress, hemodynamic instability, systemic inflammation, and exposure to exogenous catecholamines. Respiratory failure, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and altered cardiac innervation may also contribute. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on organ-specific timing, potential triggers, diagnostic challenges, management, and outcomes of TTS in SOT recipients. Reported cases predominantly occur early after liver and kidney transplantation, whereas presentations after heart transplantation range from the immediate postoperative period to years later. After heart transplantation, distinguishing TTS from early graft dysfunction and considering donor-side TTS are particularly important. Diagnostic certainty varies among published cases because formal criteria and the exclusion of competing diagnoses are inconsistently documented. Management largely follows recommendations for the general TTS population, with temporary mechanical circulatory support used in selected severe cases. Although ventricular function usually recovers, cardiogenic shock, arrhythmias, and multiorgan dysfunction may complicate the acute course, and persistent ventricular impairment has been associated with poorer long-term outcomes after liver transplantation. Comparisons with the general TTS population suggest a high proportion of severe presentations among reported transplant-associated cases; however, publication and ascertainment bias preclude firm conclusions about differences in incidence or severity. Evidence remains dominated by case reports, small series, and retrospective studies, underscoring the need for standardized reporting and prospective multicenter research.

Title: Early Relative eGFR Decline After SGLT2 Inhibitor Initiation in Heart Failure: Clinical Correlates and Pretreatment-Anchored 12-Month Trajectories.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Early changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) after sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor initiation in heart failure (HF) are difficult to interpret in routine practice. We assessed the clinical correlates of >10% early relative eGFR decline and the subsequent trajectories relative to the pretreatment eGFR. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 295 patients with HF who remained on SGLT2 inhibitor treatment at their first eligible creatinine assessment on days 10-45 (median 25 days [IQR 21-30]; range 10-42). Multivariable regression, mixed-effects modeling, and within-patient paired analyses were used. Results: Among the 333 initiation episodes, 33 (9.9%) were excluded after early treatment discontinuation, and five repeat episodes were removed. Early decline >10% occurred in 110/295 patients (37.3%). Age ≥ 80 years (adjusted OR 2.14, 95% CI 1.21-3.81), female sex (2.51, 1.42-4.44), higher baseline eGFR per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2 (1.43, 1.21-1.69), and loop-diuretic use (1.82, 1.03-3.23) were associated with decline; the loop-diuretic association attenuated in an expanded model. Twelve-month eGFR was available for 195/295 patients (66.1%). Among the 71 with >10% early decline and paired 12-month data, the mean eGFR increased by 4.70 mL/min/1.73 m2 from the early assessment but remained 6.99 mL/min/1.73 m2 below the pretreatment (both p < 0.001). Conclusions: In this selected cohort, a mean increase after early decline did not indicate a return to the pretreatment mean. The interpretation of an isolated early eGFR value requires clinical context and subsequent measurements.

Title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis.
Abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04-2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03-0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

Title: Changes in Circulating Inflammatory and Cardiac Biomarkers at Three-Month Follow-Up After CABG.
Abstract: Background. Biomarkers associated with inflammation and the cardiovascular system are altered during the perioperative and immediate postoperative periods after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) but less is known about the changes occurring during the intermediate recovery phase. We measured levels of 7 inflammatory and cardiovascular biomarkers in CABG patients between the preoperative phase and follow-up three months after hospital discharge. We hypothesized that the circulating inflammatory and cardiac biomarker profile at three-month follow-up would differ from the preoperative profile. Methods. A prospective longitudinal observational cohort included 45 adults who underwent elective coronary artery bypass grafting between May 2025 and February 2026; 40 subjects had analyzable paired preoperative and three-month post-discharge biomarker samples. Plasma levels of the inflammatory and cardiovascular biomarkers, including high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-18 (IL-18), resistin, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and cardiac troponin I (cTnI) were measured on the day before surgery and at three-month follow-up after hospital discharge. Results. The analyzed cohort had a median age of 69.0 years and included 33 men (82.5%). Following correction for multiple testing, only IL-18 (from 119.6 [87.9-155.0] to 163.6 [111.9-228.0], p = 0.007 [adjusted p = 0.025]) and NT-proBNP (221.0 [135.3-424.8] to 372.6 [213.4-632.0], p = 0.001 [adjusted p = 0.007]) had statistically significant longitudinal increases. Secondary mixed-effects model analyses produced directionally consistent results, with follow-up-to-baseline ratios of 1.26 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.05-1.52; p = 0.015] for IL-18 and 1.48 [95% CI 1.15-1.90; p = 0.003] for NT-proBNP. The levels of hsCRP, TNF-α, IL-6, resistin and cTnI did not change significantly over time. Conclusions. At three months after discharge, significant increases were confined to IL-18 and NT-proBNP rather than occurring across the broader circulating biomarker panel. These findings extend the limited prospective evidence on intermediate post-CABG biomarker changes and support further evaluation of IL-18 and NT-proBNP as candidate markers of postoperative recovery.

Title: Procedural Efficiency of Direct Stenting Versus Predilatation in Type A and B1 Coronary Lesions.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The optimal stent deployment strategy for low-complexity Type A and B1 coronary lesions remains poorly defined. We compared direct stenting (DS) and predilatation followed by stenting (PS) in elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for these lesions. Methods: This single-center, retrospective study included adults undergoing elective PCI with drug-eluting stents for ACC/AHA Type A or B1 lesions between June 2020 and December 2025. Procedure duration, cumulative contrast volume, and cumulative reference air kerma were compared using generalized estimating equations accounting for within-patient clustering, adjusted for clinical, lesion-related, procedural, and operator-related factors. Results: In total, 324 patients contributed 334 PCI observations (PS: 239; DS: 95). After adjustment, DS was associated with lower contrast volume (-18.12 mL; 95% CI -28.08 to -8.17; p < 0.001) and lower cumulative reference air kerma (-223.54 mGy; 95% CI -259.98 to -187.11; p < 0.001), whereas procedure duration did not differ significantly (-0.92 min; 95% CI -4.56 to 2.71; p = 0.619). Findings were consistent when restricted to the first PCI per patient. Conclusions: In these lesions, DS was associated with lower contrast volume and cumulative reference air kerma, without a significant adjusted difference in procedure duration. As nonrandomized observations, these findings do not establish equivalence in clinical safety or effectiveness, nor do they demonstrate cost-effectiveness.

Title: Seasonal Initiation of Hemodialysis: A Single-Center Experience.
Abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the seasonal pattern of hemodialysis initiation in a warm/subtropical climate region (Adana) and its association with the mode of initiation, early complications, and mortality. Materials and Methods: A total of 319 patients who started chronic hemodialysis at Adana City Training and Research Hospital, Department of Nephrology, between 2022 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Chi-square/Fisher's exact and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used for seasonal comparisons. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease (coronary artery and/or valvular heart disease) were fitted for emergent initiation and for any early (30-day) complication, with a likelihood-ratio test of season as a whole; 3-month mortality (13 events) was described by season and analyzed with a season-only Firth model. Catheter dysfunction was analyzed among catheter-exposed patients, followed by sensitivity analyses. Results: A total of 58.3% of patients started dialysis emergently and 41.7% in a planned manner; only 11.3% had an arteriovenous fistula as initial vascular access. No significant seasonal differences were found in initiation type, indications, or the frequency of any early complication (161/314, 51.3%; p = 0.090). In the adjusted complication model, spring versus summer gave OR = 2.33 (95% CI: 1.23-4.41, p = 0.009; Holm-adjusted p = 0.028 across the three season contrasts), but the omnibus test of seasons was not significant (p = 0.069), and spring did not differ significantly from autumn or winter. Among catheter-exposed patients, catheter dysfunction occurred in 31.4% (22/70) in the spring and 16.5% (13/79) in the summer (p = 0.035; four-season omnibus p = 0.191); this contrast was not significant after excluding initiations from February to December 2023 (p = 0.111) or when the season was assigned at the midpoint of the risk window (p = 0.114). Season was not associated with emergent initiation (omnibus p = 0.230) or with 3-month mortality (Firth OR for spring versus summer 1.12, 95% CI: 0.28-4.48). Conclusions: Hemodialysis initiation in Adana was not associated with a winter-peak pattern in initiation counts or blood pressure. Spring initiation was associated with a higher frequency of early complications, mainly catheter dysfunction, but this exploratory single-center finding was not supported by the four-season omnibus tests and was sensitive to analytic choices, and none of the 33 seasonal omnibus tests remained significant after Holm correction. It is hypothesis-generating only and does not support a seasonal practice recommendation; confirmation in larger, multicenter, prospective studies is needed.

Title: Drug Therapies and Incident Heart Failure in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common cardiac arrhythmia, significantly elevates the risk of new-onset heart failure (HF). We aimed to systematically map and appraise available evidence on drug therapies and incident HF in patients with AF. Methods: We searched Medline, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Scopus up to 16 September 2026 for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs), sub-analyses of RCTs, and observational/cohort studies. Results: Seventeen studies (397,991 participants) were included. The only randomized signal came from a prespecified subgroup of the ACTIVE-I trial, in which irbesartan was associated with fewer first HF hospitalizations than the placebo (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.96; moderate certainty). Observational studies showed an association with lower first HF hospitalization for sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors in patients with type 2 diabetes (pooled HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.48-0.95; two studies; low certainty) and lower incident HF diagnosis in a larger cohort that included patients without diabetes (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.82-0.89). The remaining cohort evidence largely reflected prescribing patterns rather than drug effects. Statins showed an inconsistent association. The higher HF incidence among users of diuretics, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, digoxin and renin-angiotensin system inhibitors was consistent with confounding by indication (very low certainty). Conclusions: Evidence on drug therapies to prevent HF in AF is limited to one randomized subgroup signal for irbesartan. The remaining findings were associations rather than demonstrated treatment effects. High-quality research, including RCTs in broader AF populations, is needed. PROSPERO Registration: CRD42024587926.

Title: Coenzyme Q10 for Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection: Protocol for a Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Feasibility Trial.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency. Emergency surgery is the standard life-saving treatment, but some patients decline operative repair, and no established pharmacological therapy has been shown to stabilize acute TAAD. Preclinical work by our team implicates mitochondrial dysfunction and smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching in aortic dissection and suggests that coenzyme Q10 may reduce dissection-related injury. This study aims to determine the feasibility of a future definitive randomized trial and to obtain preliminary safety and exploratory efficacy information. Methods: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-center feasibility trial will enroll 60 adults with CTA-confirmed Stanford type A aortic dissection within 24 h of symptom onset who decline emergency surgical repair after standard surgical counseling. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to oral coenzyme Q10 100 mg three times daily or matched placebo for 14 days, in addition to the same guideline-directed supportive medical care. The primary feasibility outcome is recruitment feasibility, defined as randomization of 60 participants within 12 months after recruitment initiation. Secondary feasibility outcomes include treatment adherence, follow-up completion, dropout, missingness, outcome-assessment feasibility, and candidate endpoint event rates. The primary exploratory clinical outcome is 14-day all-cause mortality; additional exploratory outcomes include aortic rupture death, false-lumen thrombosis, cardiac tamponade, worsening pericardial effusion, and organ malperfusion syndromes. Safety outcomes include adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse drug reactions, suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, and prespecified laboratory indices. Results: The trial is designed to establish whether recruitment, blinded treatment delivery, follow-up, outcome collection, and safety monitoring are operationally feasible and to provide estimates for planning a larger confirmatory trial. Conclusions: This feasibility trial will inform the design and conduct of future definitive evaluation of coenzyme Q10 in acute TAAD. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600123230.

Title: Obesity and Atrial Fibrillation: Weighing the Evidence.
Abstract: Obesity is a major, modifiable risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF). Potential mechanisms include haemodynamic and metabolic changes, inflammation, changes in epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) composition and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. EAT is increasingly recognised as a dynamic, pro-arrhythmic fat depot with a possible bidirectional relationship with AF, whereby AF itself may modulate EAT independent of weight change. CKM syndrome also underlies the complex interplay between obesity and AF. Despite guideline recommendations for at least 10% weight reduction in obese patients with AF, recent randomised trials focusing on weight reduction have largely failed to demonstrate clinically meaningful improvements in AF outcomes compared with catheter ablation or usual care. Incretin-based therapies including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are a promising therapy offering sustained weight loss alongside broader cardiometabolic benefits, although randomised trials with AF as a primary endpoint are lacking. Comprehensive multidisciplinary lifestyle risk factor modification (LRFM) clinics that address cardiometabolic risk factors, AF education and medication adherence have shown benefit beyond weight reduction alone, although their delivery has been heterogeneous. This narrative review examines the evolving relationship between obesity and AF including a multidimensional cardiometabolic lens, EAT characterisation, contemporary randomised trials of weight reduction, and the emerging role of incretin-based therapies and LRFM clinics.

Title: Association Between Admission Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate and Long-Term Mortality in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Background: Reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and acute kidney injury (AKI) are common in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and adversely influence prognosis. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the association between admission eGFR and one-year mortality following STEMI, accounting for admission AKI and cardiovascular risk factors. Methods: Consecutive adults (n = 2903) admitted with STEMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at a tertiary center were analyzed, selected from 2949 initially screened patients after excluding those treated conservatively or with thrombolysis (n = 14), those with a final discharge diagnosis other than STEMI (n = 21), and early deaths within 24 h of presentation (n = 11). Admission eGFR was calculated using the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation and categorized into quintiles. The primary outcome was all-cause one-year mortality, assessed using multivariable logistic regression and secondary Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: Both one-year and 30-day crude mortality decreased markedly across increasing eGFR quintiles (p < 0.001), a pattern that was maintained among patients presenting without admission AKI (30-day mortality: Q5 4.4% vs. Q1 0.0%, p < 0.001). In crude analysis, 30-day mortality was 9.1% in the lowest eGFR quintile overall. Multivariable logistic regression identified advancing age (OR 1.05 per year, p < 0.001) and admission AKI (OR 7.07, p < 0.001) as the dominant independent predictors of one-year mortality, whereas individual eGFR quintiles were attenuated after adjustment (global Wald p = 0.047). Conclusions: Lower admission eGFR is significantly associated with one-year mortality after STEMI in crude and unadjusted analyses, but its predictive contribution is substantially attenuated following multivariable adjustment for advancing age and admission AKI, which serve as the dominant prognostic determinants. Rather than acting as a strong isolated independent predictor, admission renal function primarily serves as an indicator of baseline cardiorenal reserve and baseline patient vulnerability.

Title: Prognostic Value of the Atherogenic Index of Plasma for Severity and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Young Patients (≤35 Years) with Coronary Artery Disease: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Background: Rising coronary artery disease (CAD) in young adults calls for early risk stratification, yet the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) has been understudied in patients aged ≤35 years. We therefore assessed its association with coronary lesion severity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in this cohort. Methods: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 948 patients aged 18-35 years with angiographically confirmed CAD. Greater coronary lesion severity was defined as a Gensini score > 40. The association between AIP and MACE was explored. Results: During a median follow-up of 60 months, MACE occurred in 287 patients. After full adjustment, AIP as a continuous variable was independently associated with greater coronary lesion severity (OR = 1.761; 95% CI: 1.052-2.948; p = 0.031). Regarding prognosis, when AIP was dichotomized at 0.4, it was independently associated with MACE (HR = 1.350; 95% CI: 1.060-1.721; p = 0.015) in the fully adjusted model, whereas continuous AIP did not retain significance. Restricted cubic spline analysis suggested a possible U-shaped dose-response relationship between AIP and MACE (overall p < 0.001, nonlinear p = 0.051). Subgroup analyses showed that the association of AIP with MACE was generally consistent across all examined strata, with no significant interactions (all p for interaction >0.05). Conclusions: AIP was independently associated with greater coronary lesion severity and MACE in young CAD patients (≤35 years). These findings support AIP as a practical tool not only for early risk stratification but also for guiding intensive lipid-lowering therapy in this distinct population.

Title: Clinical Risk Factors and Inflammatory Markers as Predictors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients Undergoing Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery.
Abstract: Background: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious neurological complication following acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the critical role of systemic inflammation in POD pathogenesis, this study aimed to evaluate perioperative inflammatory profiles in patients undergoing ATAAD repair and to develop a predictive nomogram for early POD risk stratification. Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 355 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD. Serial inflammatory markers were assessed across multiple perioperative time points. A two-stage variable selection process, incorporating variance inflation factor (VIF) and the Boruta algorithm, was utilized to identify robust predictors. A predictive nomogram was constructed via multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results: POD occurred in 29.86% of the cohort. Patients who developed POD had higher inflammatory marker levels at several individual postoperative time points compared to the non-delirium group. The final predictive model integrated 11 key variables: age, EuroSCORE I, CPB time, SIRI_6h, PLR_6h, IL-10_6h, IL-8_6h, IL-8_pre, IL-6_6h, IL-6_pre, and PCT_6h. The nomogram demonstrated acceptable internal discrimination with an AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.794-0.876) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. Notably, IL-6_6h and PCT_6h emerged as strong independent risk factors, while SIRI_6h demonstrated an inverse association with POD. Calibration and DCA analyses confirmed the model's acceptable performance and potential clinical utility, though independent external validation remains essential prior to any clinical translation. An exploratory, web-based risk calculator was developed to facilitate bedside implementation. Conclusions: This study develops and internally validates an exploratory biomarker-based prediction model for POD in ATAAD patients. By integrating early inflammatory profiles with established clinical variables, this preliminary model provides a preliminary foundation for early risk stratification, though rigorous prospective multicenter external validation is required before real-world clinical implementation can be considered.

Title: Mid-Term and Long-Term Clinical Events with Conduction System Pacing Versus Biventricular Pacing in HFrEF with Wide QRS: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials with Trial Sequential Analysis.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Conduction system pacing (CSP) has emerged as a more physiological alternative to biventricular pacing (BiVP) in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and wide QRS, but recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded discordant results. This meta-analysis aimed to compare CSP with BiVP for clinical events and functional recovery in HFrEF. Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for RCTs through 15 April 2026. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality (ACM) and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at mid-term (6-12 months) and long-term (>12 months) follow-up. Random-effects meta-analyses and Trial Sequential Analysis (TSA) were performed. Results: Eleven RCTs comprising 12 reports and 1073 patients were included. CSP showed no significant difference in mid-term ACM (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.21 to 2.49; p = 0.605) or HFH (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.52 to 1.81; p = 0.918). At long-term follow-up (three RCTs; n = 312), CSP showed a non-significant trend toward ACM reduction (RR 0.34; 95% CI 0.11 to 1.06; p = 0.063; low-certainty evidence) and a significant, TSA-supported reduction in HFH (RR 0.30; 95% CI 0.16 to 0.58; p < 0.001; moderate-certainty evidence). At 6 months, CSP improved LVEF (MD 2.84%; 95% CI 0.74 to 4.93; p = 0.008) and reduced QRS duration (MD -9.97 ms; 95% CI -18.57 to -1.37; p = 0.023), with NYHA improvement at 12 months (MD -0.31; 95% CI -0.50 to -0.11; p = 0.002). Conclusions: In this meta-analysis of RCTs predominantly evaluating left bundle branch area pacing, CSP was associated with a lower risk of long-term HFH compared with BiVP in HFrEF with a wide QRS, although the evidence remains limited by the small number of available trials. The observed trend toward lower long-term ACM should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger, adequately powered RCTs with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings and determine whether CSP provides sustained clinical benefit over BiVP.

Title: Cognitive Impairment and Functional Independence in Hospitalized Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with cognitive decline even without clinically apparent stroke, but the relative contributions of demographic, vascular, inflammatory and therapeutic factors remain unclear. We aimed to explore clinical determinants of cognitive and functional performance in hospitalized patients with AF. Methods: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, 62 consecutive patients with documented AF admitted to an internal medicine department underwent assessment with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Activities of Daily Living (ADL) scale. Associations were examined with multivariable linear regression, with false-discovery-rate correction and sensitivity analyses. Results: Mean age was 75.3 ± 8.1 years; 17 patients (27.4%) had a previous ischemic stroke. Fifty-nine patients (95.2%) scored below the MoCA threshold of 26 and 35 (56.5%) below the MMSE threshold of 24. Patients with previous stroke scored lower on all three instruments (MoCA mean difference 4.13, 95% CI 0.75-7.51; MMSE 4.84, 1.67-8.01; ADL 1.69, 0.25-3.12). After correction for multiple testing, age remained associated with all three outcomes and previous stroke with MMSE score; no association was detected for sex, education, diabetes, C-reactive protein, LDL-cholesterol or anticoagulant type. Higher CHA2DS2-VAScscores were associated with poorer performance, though not independently of their own components. Conclusions: In this exploratory study, cognitive impairment was common among hospitalized patients with AF and was associated with age and previous stroke. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Autonomic Changes During an Adaptive Cognitive Task.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examined between-participant associations of task-minus-baseline heart rate (HR) and skin conductance (SC) changes with performance during the adaptive Determination Test (DT), in which performance influences subsequent task demand. Methods: This exploratory secondary analysis included 48 young adults. Accuracy was the study-defined proportion correct/(correct + incorrect + omitted), calculated from exported counts. Ten Pearson correlations formed the primary analytical family. Complementary fractional-logit and linear models included the corresponding baseline physiological value and the exported stimulus count (DT_Stimuli). Tonic skin conductance level and skin conductance response (SCR) frequency and amplitude were also examined. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment was applied separately to the defined analytical families. Results: Mean HR increased by 19.99 bpm and mean SC by 4.65 µS. The HR-accuracy Pearson estimate was r = 0.338 (95% CI 0.060 to 0.568; p = 0.019; BH q = 0.187), compared with Spearman ρ = 0.192. In the model including baseline HR and DT_Stimuli, the average marginal association was 1.42 percentage points per 10 bpm (95% bootstrap CI 0.13 to 2.65; p = 0.033; BH q = 0.306). Neither the primary correlation family nor the 15 complementary model tests met q < 0.05. Direct comparisons did not establish different HR and SC correlations. Conclusions: HR and SC increased during adaptive DT performance. A possible HR-accuracy association depended on analytical specification. Adjustment for aggregate stimulus count did not identify the direction of the performance-demand-physiology relationship. These findings support prospective testing with time-resolved task exposure.

Title: Cross-Dataset Generalization in Phonocardiogram Murmur Classification: A Benchmark Study of Domain-Conditional Performance and the Role of Multi-Representation Fusion.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Automated phonocardiogram (PCG) analysis is a candidate tool for scaling up cardiac auscultation, but the internal accuracy reported in many studies may not reflect performance when a model is applied to recordings from a different source. This study evaluated how a broad range of classifiers generalize across PCG datasets and examined whether a multi-representation architecture improves cross-dataset transfer. Methods: Eleven approaches were trained on the pediatric CirCor DigiScope dataset and evaluated, without target-domain fine-tuning, on two external datasets: a heterogeneous adult/mixed dataset (the PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2016 database) and a homogeneous five-class open-access heart sound dataset. The approaches spanned classical machine learning (spport vector machine, random forest), standard deep models (1D-CNN, 2D-CNN, ResNet1D, CNN-BiLSTM, and two hybrid networks), image-based backbones (EfficientNet-B0, MaxViT), and a proposed four-branch fusion model (PCG-MambaConformer) combining raw-signal, mel-spectrogram, and continuous wavelet transform (CWT) representations. Threshold-transfer and precision-recall analyses, adversarial domain adaptation, an uncertainty-quantification benchmark, a disease-specific transfer analysis, multi-architecture ensembling, a branch ablation, a label-grouping sensitivity analysis, a reciprocal (reverse-direction) transfer experiment and explainability analyses (feature-space t-SNE with class-separability metrics and Grad-CAM saliency) were also performed. Performance was summarized using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with sensitivity and specificity. Results: Internal AUROC was similar across deep models (approximately 0.82-0.90) and largely independent of parameter count, whereas classical models were lower (0.67-0.69). On the heterogeneous external dataset, the highest AUROC was 0.738 and none of the nine deep models reached a sensitivity and a specificity both of at least 0.80 at any of the three thresholds examined. On the homogeneous external dataset, PCG-MambaConformer reached an AUROC of 0.985 (sensitivity 0.718, specificity 0.995 at the 0.5 threshold), whereas other models tended to collapse toward either always-normal or always-abnormal predictions. Adversarial adaptation improved performance on the homogeneous target but reduced it on the heterogeneous target. On the heterogeneous target, even an oracle threshold raised balanced accuracy by only 0.022 on average, whereas on the homogeneous target a source-derived threshold produced a balanced operating point only for PCG-MambaConformer (sensitivity 0.863, specificity 0.980). Models trained in the reverse direction (PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2016 to CirCor) also transferred poorly (AUROC 0.612-0.677). Branch ablation showed that three of the four single-branch configurations collapsed to a one-class operating point and that the full fusion model achieved the highest AUROC, and a feature-space analysis showed that successful transfer was associated with the class-separability of the target domain (silhouette score highest for the homogeneous dataset) rather than with the proximity of dataset centroids. Conclusions: In the two external datasets evaluated, successful cross-dataset PCG transfer was associated with the homogeneity of the target domain; because these datasets also differed in population, recording protocol, disease spectrum, class distribution and signal quality, homogeneity cannot be isolated as the sole determinant of transferability. Internal accuracy was a weak indicator of external behavior, model complexity alone did not close the heterogeneous transfer gap, and balanced cross-dataset performance on a homogeneous target was associated with multi-representation fusion. The near-perfect result on the homogeneous target should be read as technical cross-dataset transfer under favorable, highly curated conditions rather than as clinical external validation, whereas the heterogeneous result is the more realistic indication of current limitations. These findings support multi-metric external evaluation on independent data, followed by prospective clinical validation, before any clinical use is considered.

Title: Atrial Septal Aneurysm and Anxiety: A Matched Cross-Sectional Study with Prospective Enrollment Exploring Clinical and Psychosomatic Associations.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: An isolated atrial septal aneurysm (ASA) represents a distinct structural anomaly defined by abnormal bulging of the interatrial tissue, affecting roughly three percent of the general public. Although routinely viewed as an accidental discovery during imaging, this condition carries recognized associations with adverse clinical events, notably cerebrovascular ischemia and rhythm disturbances. Because the interplay between cardiovascular diseases and psychological distress is well established, our primary goal was to determine if individuals harboring this septal anomaly display elevated symptoms of anxiety or depression relative to standard cardiology outpatients. Methods: For this comparative cross-sectional investigation, we recruited a total of one hundred and twenty adults from a dedicated cardiology clinic. The cohort consisted of sixty individuals diagnosed with the septal anomaly and sixty healthy control subjects, carefully paired according to age and gender. Every participant received a comprehensive clinical baseline assessment, which included a 12-lead electrocardiogram alongside a detailed two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiogram. Psychological status was assessed using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-1 for state anxiety and STAI-2 for trait anxiety) and the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI). Results: Initial physical and demographic profiling-specifically regarding patient age, gender distribution, and calculated body mass indices-revealed no significant statistical variances between the two study arms. The ASA group presented with a significantly higher prevalence of clinical palpitations (83.3% vs. 43.3%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the ASA group exhibited significantly higher scores on all psychometric measures (STAI-1: 44.97 ± 9.15 vs. 32.53 ± 8.24, p < 0.001; STAI-2: 49.37 ± 7.22 vs. 34.72 ± 10.55, p < 0.001; BDI: 19.66 ± 9.79 vs. 10.07 ± 6.81, p < 0.001). After confirming the absence of severe multicollinearity (Variance Inflation Factor < 5), exploratory logistic regression analysis demonstrated that clinical palpitations (odds ratio [OR]: 5.309; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.621-17.383; p = 0.006) and trait anxiety scores (STAI-2) (OR: 1.169 per one-point increment; 95% CI: 1.062-1.286; p = 0.001) were independently associated factors for the presence of ASA. Conclusions: This study demonstrates a significant clinical association between ASA, clinical palpitations, and persistent trait anxiety (STAI-2). While the cross-sectional design precludes causal inferences, the findings suggest a clinical clustering of anxiety and palpitations in patients diagnosed with ASA. This highlights the importance of recognizing potential psychosomatic overlaps in structural heart diseases.

Title: Association of Serum Visfatin Levels with Coronary Artery Disease and Biochemical Parameters in Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis.
Abstract: Background: Cardiovascular disease is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage kidney disease receiving maintenance hemodialysis. Visfatin is a pro-inflammatory adipokine involved in metabolic and inflammatory pathways; however, its relationship with established coronary artery disease (CAD) in hemodialysis patients remains uncertain. This study evaluated the associations of serum visfatin concentrations with hemodialysis status, clinically documented CAD, and selected metabolic and biochemical parameters. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 130 non-diabetic adults classified into four groups: healthy controls (n = 40), participants with preserved renal function and established CAD (n = 28), maintenance hemodialysis patients without CAD (n = 30), and maintenance hemodialysis patients with established CAD (n = 32). Demographic, anthropometric, and laboratory variables were recorded. Serum visfatin concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Between-group comparisons and exploratory correlation analyses were performed. Analysis of covariance was additionally used to assess between-group differences in visfatin after adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, and BMI, with body fat percentage substituted for BMI in a sensitivity analysis. Results: Median serum visfatin concentration was higher in the pooled hemodialysis groups than in the pooled non-hemodialysis groups (35.75 vs. 30.51 ng/mL, p = 0.014). In unadjusted pairwise comparisons, healthy controls had lower visfatin concentrations than participants with preserved renal function and CAD (p = 0.007), hemodialysis patients without CAD (p = 0.001), and hemodialysis patients with CAD (p = 0.004). However, visfatin concentrations did not differ between hemodialysis patients with and without established CAD (p = 0.972). After adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, and BMI, the overall between-group effect was no longer statistically significant (F(3, 122)= 2.054, p = 0.110, partial η2 = 0.048). The result was similar in the sensitivity analysis replacing BMI with body fat percentage (p = 0.060). In exploratory analyses of the pooled hemodialysis population, visfatin was positively correlated with fasting insulin (r = 0.269, p = 0.039), HOMA-IR (r = 0.277, p = 0.033), and serum uric acid (r = 0.263, p = 0.039). Conclusions: Higher serum visfatin concentrations were observed in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis in unadjusted analyses, but the overall between-group difference was attenuated after adjustment for demographic and body-composition variables. Visfatin did not distinguish hemodialysis patients according to established CAD status. These findings do not demonstrate an independent association of circulating visfatin with either hemodialysis status or clinically documented CAD. Given the cross-sectional design and exploratory nature of the correlation analyses, further prospective studies with larger samples and standardized assessment of coronary disease burden are warranted.

Title: Beyond the Apnoea-Hypopnoea Index: Towards Personalised Care of Patients with Suspected Obstructive Sleep Apnoea Through Clinical Phenotyping and Physiological Stratification.
Abstract: The apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) remains central to the diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), but it incompletely captures both clinical heterogeneity and the physiological burden of respiratory events. We propose a phenotype-guided framework with a common initial clinical assessment followed by two complementary pathways according to the patient's predominant clinical need: a symptom-oriented pathway based on pre-test clinical phenotyping, and a cardiovascular risk-oriented pathway in which directly measured hypoxic burden (HB), complemented by the respiratory event-related pulse-rate response, may eventually support physiological stratification. In our single-centre cohort of 5385 referrals, three predominantly symptomatic phenotypes accounted for 56.5% of patients and two paucisymptomatic phenotypes (A and E) for 43.5%; these groups had overlapping AHI distributions but different clinical profiles and needs. The reported AUC of 0.87-0.95 reflects supervised reproduction of internally derived cluster labels, not prediction of clinical outcomes or CPAP benefit. HB and pulse-rate response remain candidate physiological markers: evidence for treatment-effect modification derives from post hoc analyses and does not establish validated treatment-allocation criteria. Pre-test phenotyping is sufficiently developed to justify prospective, external, multicentre validation, whereas physiological integration requires methodological standardisation and prospective evaluation before individual treatment decisions can be guided by these markers.

Title: Heart Failure Is Associated with Limb-Related Adverse Events in Patients Hospitalized for Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
Abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the impact of heart failure (HF) on one-year outcomes in patients hospitalized for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs). Methods: A retrospective observational study including consecutive patients admitted in 2024 to a tertiary multidisciplinary diabetic foot service for DFUs. Patients were stratified according to the presence of HF (HF+ vs. HF-). One-year outcomes included wound healing, major amputation, non-fatal major adverse limb events (NF-MALCE), including myocardial infarction, stroke, recurrent chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) requiring revascularization, and mortality. Results: Overall, 270 patients were included (104 HF+ [38.5%] vs. 166 HF- [61.5%]). Patients with HF exhibited a more severe cardiorenal phenotype, with worse cardiac and renal biomarkers. At one-year follow-up, patients with HF showed lower wound healing rates than patients without HF (58.6% vs. 71.7%, p = 0.03), higher incidence of NF-MALCE (43.3% vs. 18.7%, p < 0.001), mainly driven by recurrent CLTI requiring revascularization (48.9% vs. 27.0%, p < 0.001), and higher mortality (21.1% vs. 7.2%, p = 0.001). Conversely, no differences were observed in major amputation, myocardial infarction, or stroke. After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, ischaemic heart disease, atrial fibrillation, dialysis, haemoglobin, albumin, foot infection and peripheral arterial disease (PAD), HF remained independently associated with NF-MALCE (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.38-6.09, p = 0.005) and recurrent CLTI requiring revascularization (aOR 2.43, 95% CI 1.11-5.32, p = 0.026); the association remained consistent in the subgroup with PAD. Conclusions: HF identifies a high-risk cardio-renal phenotype and is independently associated with increased limb-related adverse events in patients hospitalized for DFUs, supporting closer vascular surveillance and integrated multidisciplinary cardio-renal-foot care.

Title: Clinical Correlates of Cardiovascular Autonomic Measures in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction in type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) is heterogeneous, and individual autonomic measures may identify distinct clinical profiles. This study assessed the clinical, neuropathic, metabolic, and vascular correlates of three cardiovascular autonomic measures: the expiratory-to-inspiratory (E:I) R-R interval ratio, orthostatic blood pressure response, and corrected QT interval (QTc). Methods: This secondary cross-sectional analysis included 109 patients with T2DM from a previously characterized cohort. Cardiovagal function was assessed using the E:I R-R interval ratio during deep breathing. Orthostatic hypotension (OH) was defined according to systolic and diastolic blood pressure changes after standing, while QTc was calculated using Bazett's formula. Peripheral neuropathy was evaluated using the Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI) and Toronto Clinical Neuropathy Score (TCNS), and peripheral vascular status using the ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI). Group comparisons, chi-square or Fisher exact tests as appropriate, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Spearman correlation analyses, and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed. Exploratory families of comparisons and correlations were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. Results: A pathological E:I R-R interval ratio was identified in 90 patients (82.6%), prolonged QTc in 23 (21.1%), and orthostatic hypotension in 40 (36.7%). Categorical OH was not associated with the evaluated clinical, neuropathic, or vascular parameters. In contrast, continuous systolic blood pressure change after standing (ΔSBP) was independently associated with peripheral neuropathy severity, assessed using the MNSI and TCNS. The nominal univariable association between ΔSBP and HbA1c did not remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction or multivariable adjustment. QTc prolongation showed no consistent association pattern with the other evaluated autonomic-related measures. Conclusions: The evaluated cardiovascular autonomic measures showed partially distinct cross-sectional association patterns in patients with T2DM. Continuous ΔSBP was independently associated with peripheral neuropathy severity, whereas categorical orthostatic hypotension showed no significant associations. The E:I R-R interval ratio and QTc prolongation showed limited overlap with the other evaluated measures. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish the diagnostic utility of individual measures for cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy.

Title: Quantitative CT Geometry of the Patent Ductus Arteriosus in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease: Association with Aortic Arch Obstruction or Hypoplasia.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Quantitative patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) geometry in congenital heart disease (CHD), particularly in relation to aortic arch abnormalities, is incompletely characterized. We evaluated CT-derived PDA geometry. Methods: This retrospective exploratory single-center study included 168 infants with CHD and a PDA on cardiovascular CT. Aortic-end, pulmonary-end, and mid-duct diameters and ductal length were measured. The Ductal Length-to-Diameter Index (LDI), selected during exploratory analysis, was defined as ductal length divided by the mean end diameter. Seventy-three patients had CT-documented aortic arch obstruction or hypoplasia. Results: LDI was lower in patients with arch obstruction/hypoplasia than in those without these findings (2.04 [1.39-2.84] vs. 3.51 [2.23-4.89]; p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = -0.473) and remained associated after adjustment for age, weight, and sex (OR per +1 LDI, 0.534; 95% CI, 0.412-0.693; p < 0.001). The association remained robust with a conservative definition restricted to coarctation or interrupted aortic arch. LDI had an interobserver ICC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.685-0.954), with wide limits of agreement (-1.98 to +2.45). Conclusions: CT-documented aortic arch obstruction or hypoplasia is associated with lower LDI. This exploratory geometric association warrants prospective external validation before clinical use.

Title: Analgesic Prescribing in Medically Complex Adult Outpatients Aged ≥40 Years: A Hierarchical Analysis of Comorbidity-Associated Patterns.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Selecting appropriate analgesic therapy in patients with multimorbidity is increasingly challenging because clinicians must balance pain management against comorbidities, polypharmacy, and medication-related risks. However, evidence describing how analgesic prescribing patterns vary across patients with different multimorbidity profiles in routine outpatient practice remains limited. This retrospective cross-sectional study examined associations between multimorbidity and prescribing patterns across paracetamol, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and opioids, and identified clinical characteristics associated with different hierarchical analgesic exposure groups among adults aged ≥40 years in Saudi Arabia. Methods: Electronic health record data were analyzed for adults aged ≥40 years attending multiple clinics in the Eastern Region of Saudi Arabia between January 2020 and December 2021. Analgesic exposure at the index outpatient visit was classified using a hierarchical framework into mutually exclusive paracetamol-only, NSAID-priority, opioid-priority, or non-use groups.
