Participants completed the Transplant Effects Questionnaire (TxEQ), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES), Life Orientation Test-Revised (LOT-R), and SF-36. We performed univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses separately for heart and kidney transplant recipients to identify factors associated with transplant-specific psychological adaptation.
RESULTS: Overall psychological adaptation was favorable. Adherence demonstrated the highest TxEQ scores, whereas donor-related guilt and disclosure concerns were relatively low. Approximately 20.53% of participants reported clinically relevant anxiety symptoms and 14.2% reported depressive symptoms. In heart transplant recipients, better mental health-related quality of life was independently associated with greater adherence (β = 0.025, p = 0.003). Among kidney transplant recipients, higher donor-related guilt was associated with transplantation center, while greater disclosure was associated with male sex, transplantation center, and shorter time since transplantation (all p < 0.05). Several psychological variables were associated with selected domains of transplant-specific psychological adaptation, whereas demographic and clinical variables showed fewer significant associations.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that several psychological variables were associated with transplant-specific psychological adaptation in long-term heart and kidney transplant recipients. Routine assessment of anxiety, mental health-related quality of life, and transplant-specific emotional responses may facilitate identification of recipients who could benefit from further psychosocial evaluation. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether these associations translate into improved long-term outcomes.

Title: A Configurable Multi-Modal Clinical Time-Series Platform for Predictive Modeling in Cardiology.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Predictive models for cardiovascular disease rely predominantly on electronic health records (EHRs), whereas wearable devices, home monitoring, and patient-reported outcomes offer new opportunities for multimodal risk prediction; however, integrating these heterogeneous sources into a reproducible, clinically usable machine learning workflow remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an end-to-end architecture for explainable multimodal time-series prediction in patients with heart failure (HF), left ventricular assist device (LVAD) recipients, and heart transplant (HT) recipients.
METHODS: The modular architecture harmonizes Health Level Seven Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (HL7 FHIR) and non-FHIR telemonitoring data into a unified event log, which leakage-aware temporal preprocessing converts into patient-day feature matrices. Configurable adverse-event tasks (HF hospitalization, cardiac decompensation, transplant rejection, and mortality) are modeled using gradient-boosted trees or temporal neural networks, with optional probability calibration. Explanations combine SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for tabular models with temporal-perturbation attribution and integrated gradients for sequence models. The pipeline is declaratively configured, tracked with MLflow, and deployable via command-line and web interfaces. It was developed alongside the prospective multicenter RETENTION trial of a telemonitoring-based care pathway and was subsequently applied to data collected within the trial.
RESULTS: Applied to the RETENTION cohort, the framework executed the complete workflow, from heterogeneous source data to per-patient-day probability estimates for each prediction task, with feature- and time-level explanations presented as clinician-facing narratives. The cohort served to demonstrate the architecture, not to establish clinical predictive performance or prospective clinical validation.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a reproducible, end-to-end architecture that unifies data harmonization, temporal processing, machine learning orchestration, explainability, and deployment for multimodal clinical prediction. Its modular, disease-agnostic design supports adaptation to other diseases, settings, and data sources, laying a foundation for prospective validation and clinical translation.

Title: Etiology and Anatomical Level of Lower-Limb Amputations in Two Iranian Referral Hospitals: A Retrospective Record-Based Study.
Abstract: Background: Lower-limb amputation arises from heterogeneous pathways ranging from severe trauma to dysvascular disease and infection, yet comparative data across Iranian hospitals remain limited. We aimed to characterize demographic, etiologic, and anatomical patterns of lower-limb amputation and to evaluate between-hospital heterogeneity. Methods: This retrospective, two-hospital, record-based study included 229 eligible hospitalization records with lower-limb amputation at Al-Zahra and Kashani hospitals in Isfahan, Iran, from 13 April 2014 through 18 March 2020. Primary etiology was reconstructed from ordered diagnostic codes using a predefined hierarchical algorithm; external-cause codes were reviewed as supporting contextual information and to characterize documented traumatic mechanisms. Amputation level was derived from ICD-9-CM procedure codes. Analyses used Python 3.13.5 (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and statsmodels). Results: Trauma was the leading etiology (49.3%), followed by dysvascular disease (28.8%) and infection (10.5%). Age differed strongly across etiologies (H = 93.71; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; epsilon-squared = 0.398, 95% CI 0.307-0.509), with trauma-related hospitalizations occurring at younger ages. Toe (35.4%) and below-knee (34.5%) amputations were most frequent. Hospital was associated with both etiology and amputation level (both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; bias-corrected Cramer's V = 0.374 and 0.471, respectively). In an adjusted major-versus-minor model, older age and treatment at Al-Zahra Hospital were associated with major amputation, whereas female sex was not statistically significant. Conclusions: The hospitalizations showed marked descriptive differences by age, etiology, and hospital. Trauma-related hospitalizations occurred at younger ages, whereas dysvascular and infection-related hospitalizations occurred later in life. The substantial between-hospital differences indicate that pooled hospital-based estimates may obscure institutional case mix and should not be interpreted as population-level incidence.

Title: Complications and Hospital Resource Utilization Associated with ECMO in COVID-19 ARDS with Acute Kidney Injury: Insights from United States National Inpatient Sample, 2020-2022.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication of COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet the impact of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) on outcomes in this high-risk population remains unclear.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, survey-weighted study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2020-2022 to compare outcomes among adults hospitalized with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI managed with invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) alone versus IMV and ECMO. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, while secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT), complications, hospital length of stay (LOS), and healthcare utilization.
RESULTS: Among 198,395 hospitalizations with COVID-19 ARDS complicated by AKI, 4730 received IMV and ECMO. ECMO use was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.81-1.12). However, ECMO was associated with greater odds of RRT, intracranial hemorrhage, disseminated intravascular coagulation, cardiogenic shock, vasopressor use, tracheostomy, acute liver failure, deep vein thrombosis, ischemic stroke and ICU-acquired weakness. ECMO was also associated with longer LOS and higher hospitalization charges.
CONCLUSIONS: Among hospitalizations with COVID-19-associated ARDS and AKI, ECMO was not associated with statistically significantly lower adjusted in-hospital mortality but was associated with markedly higher complication burden, longer hospitalization, and substantially greater healthcare resource utilization.

Title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Dexamethasone in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery with Cardiopulmonary Bypass: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial of Inflammatory Biomarkers and Opioid Consumption.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) triggers a systemic inflammatory response in children undergoing congenital heart surgery. Although dexmedetomidine has been proposed as an alternative to corticosteroids, the two agents have not previously been directly compared in a pediatric randomized trial. This study aimed to compare the effects of dexmedetomidine and dexamethasone on inflammatory biomarkers and analgesic outcomes in children undergoing congenital heart surgery with CPB. Methods: In this prospective, randomized, controlled exploratory trial, 50 children aged 6 months to 18 years undergoing elective congenital heart surgery with CPB were randomized 1:1 to dexamethasone (n = 25) or dexmedetomidine (n = 25), using institutional regimens that were not equipotent anti-inflammatory doses. Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-8 (IL-8) were measured at baseline, immediately after separation from CPB (post-CPB), and 12 h postoperatively. The primary endpoint was IL-6 at the two postoperative time points; IL-8 was a secondary biomarker outcome. Secondary outcomes also included Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) pain scores, fentanyl consumption, and time to first rescue analgesia. Effect estimates included Hodges-Lehmann (HL) median differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); a post hoc baseline-adjusted mixed-effects model of log-transformed concentrations served as a sensitivity analysis. Secondary and exploratory analyses were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: All 50 randomized children were analyzed. Median IL-6 was lower in the dexmedetomidine group at 12 h (50 vs. 178 pg/mL; HL difference 86 pg/mL, 95% CI 59 to 144; p < 0.001); the post-CPB difference (46 vs. 77 pg/mL; HL difference 34 pg/mL, 95% CI 0 to 112; p = 0.045) was imprecise and not significant after post hoc Bonferroni correction for the two primary comparisons. In the post hoc baseline-adjusted sensitivity model, the ratio of geometric mean IL-6 concentrations (dexmedetomidine/dexamethasone) was 0.35 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.58; p < 0.001). Among secondary and exploratory outcomes, for which p-values are nominal, IL-8 was also lower post-CPB (159 vs. 381 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and at 12 h (120 vs. 311 pg/mL; p = 0.002). Dexmedetomidine was associated with lower intraoperative (83.0 ± 30.7 vs. 142.6 ± 51.7 µg; p < 0.001) and cumulative 24-h fentanyl consumption (53.8 ± 17.4 vs. 105.4 ± 32.8 µg; p < 0.001), analyzed in absolute units with incompletely documented intraoperative doses, and a longer time to first rescue analgesia (4.68 ± 0.73 vs. 1.84 ± 0.23 h; p < 0.001). Time to extubation did not differ significantly (median 2 vs. 1 h; p = 0.204). Intensive care unit length of stay, an exploratory outcome recorded in days, was distributed toward shorter stays with dexmedetomidine (median 2 [interquartile range 1-2] vs. 2 [2-3] days; p = 0.007). No pre-specified adverse events occurred in either group, although the trial was too small to exclude clinically important safety differences. Conclusions: In this exploratory trial of two non-equipotent institutional regimens, dexmedetomidine was associated with lower early postoperative IL-6 and IL-8 concentrations and lower opioid consumption than dexamethasone. These hypothesis-generating biomarker and analgesic signals do not demonstrate therapeutic superiority or patient-centered clinical benefit and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter trials.

Title: Guideline Concordance and Documentation of Allopurinol Initiation Across Clinical Specialties: A Three-Year Retrospective Evaluation.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: To assess guideline concordance and indication documentation of new allopurinol prescriptions and whether these differed across clinical specialties. Methods: A retrospective study at a tertiary academic center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, included adults with a first institutional allopurinol dispensation between January 2022 and November 2024. Prescriptions were guideline-concordant if issued for gout meeting 2020 American College of Rheumatology initiation criteria, tumor lysis syndrome management, or recurrent nephrolithiasis; documented non-guideline-concordant if another indication was recorded; and undocumented otherwise. Specialty associations were assessed using logistic regression, age- and sex-adjusted Firth models, and Fisher's exact tests. Results: Among 707 patients, 105 (14.9%) prescriptions were guideline-concordant, 452 (63.9%) were documented non-guideline-concordant, and 150 (21.2%) were undocumented; asymptomatic hyperuricemia accounted for 47.0%. Relative to Rheumatology, Primary Care (OR 92.57, 95% CI 32.89-260.57) and Nephrology (OR 24.69, 95% CI 7.01-86.90) had higher odds of documented non-concordance, persisting after adjustment. Cardiology had the highest undocumented rate (35.4%). Conclusions: Non-guideline-concordant initiation was common, and the type of quality gap differed by specialty. These observational associations may partly reflect case mix and should not be attributed to specialty alone, but they support specialty-tailored stewardship.

Title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Dual Physical and Cognitive Impairment Among Adults Aged 50 Years and Older with Cardiometabolic Conditions: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background: Dual impairment of physical and cognitive capacities is associated with adverse health outcomes in aging populations and may emerge during middle age. However, evidence on its prevalence and associated factors among adults with cardiometabolic conditions in primary care settings remains limited, particularly in Southeast Asia. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of dual impairment and identify factors associated with dual impairment among adults aged ≥50 years with cardiometabolic conditions. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among adults aged ≥50 years who had at least one cardiometabolic condition and attended a primary care clinic at a university-affiliated health center in Northern Thailand between March 2024 and July 2025. Dual impairment was defined as impaired cognitive function, assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), together with impaired physical function, defined as either slow gait speed or low handgrip strength. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to examine factors associated with dual impairment. Results: A total of 196 participants were included. The mean age was 69.08 ± 6.15 years, and 72.96% were female. The prevalence of dual impairment was 25.00%. In the primary fully adjusted model (Model 1), lower LDL-C was the only factor significantly associated with dual impairment (adjusted OR [aOR] = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-1.00, p = 0.021). In the secondary parsimonious model (Model 2), female sex was associated with higher odds of dual impairment (aOR = 2.48, 95% CI: 1.05-5.84, p = 0.038), whereas age was not statistically significant (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.99-1.10, p = 0.139). The inverse association between LDL-C and dual impairment remained significant in Model 2 (aOR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-0.99, p = 0.020). Conclusions: Dual impairment was identified in approximately one-quarter of participants, representing a substantial burden among individuals with cardiometabolic conditions. The observed inverse association between LDL-C and dual impairment should be interpreted cautiously given the potential for reverse causation and residual confounding, as well as the lack of information on lipid-lowering medication use. The identified associations are exploratory and warrant confirmation in larger prospective multicenter studies.

Title: Physical Performance Outcomes and Programme Delivery Costs of ELDERPLAY, a Community-Based Multicomponent Exercise and Recreational Intervention for Older Adults: A Non-Randomized Controlled Evaluation.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examined the association between participation in a community-based multicomponent physical and recreational programme (ELDERPLAY) and changes in physical performance and frailty-related outcomes in adults aged 65 years and older, and estimated programme delivery costs. The study was designed as a quasi-experimental, non-randomized controlled evaluation conducted in a community setting. Methods: Community-dwelling older adults (n = 184) were allocated to an intervention group (n = 103) or a control group (n = 81) through voluntary enrolment and geographic matching. Participant enrolment and data collection were carried out between July 2022 and December 2023, after ethics approval had been obtained. The intervention consisted of 20 supervised sessions (two per week) combining Vivifrail-based multicomponent exercises with simple recreational activities. Primary outcomes were physical performance and frailty-related function, assessed using the Short Physical Performance Battery and the Timed Up and Go test. Secondary exploratory outcomes included actigraphy-derived daily step count, heart rate, and sleep parameters, recorded over seven consecutive days at a single intermediate assessment point. Analyses were conducted using analysis of covariance and generalized estimating equations adjusted for cholesterol, COVID-19 vaccination and Barthel Index score. Programme costs were estimated using an activity-based costing approach. Results: Compared with the control group, participants in the intervention group showed greater improvement over time in balance, gait performance, chair-stand performance and overall physical performance (time × group interaction: gait performance p < 0.001, partial eta squared 0.450; chair-stand performance p < 0.001, 0.306; SPPB total score p < 0.001, 0.361; Timed Up and Go p < 0.001, 0.224). At 10 weeks, the adjusted mean SPPB total score was 9.62 (95% CI 9.25-10.00) in the intervention group and 7.80 (95% CI 7.37-8.23) in the control group, and the adjusted mean Timed Up and Go was 8.85 s (95% CI 8.08-9.62) versus 12.04 s (95% CI 11.15-12.92). Higher daily step counts were also observed in the intervention group; heart rate and sleep parameters were recorded cross-sectionally at a single intermediate assessment point that coincided with the delivery of the programme and are reported only as descriptive values. The programme was delivered at a mean cost of €92.3 per participant, or €62.3 per participant when the research monitoring devices are excluded. Conclusions: Participation in a community-based multicomponent exercise programme incorporating recreational activities was associated with improvements in clinically relevant physical performance outcomes in community-dwelling older adults. The programme was delivered in full at a mean delivery cost of €92.3 per participant in a real-world community setting. Because allocation was not randomized, the groups differed at baseline, and outcome assessment was carried out by a single unblinded assessor who designed and coordinated the programme but did not deliver the sessions, these findings are associative and require confirmation in a randomized trial. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07864831 (retrospectively registered).

Title: Weighted Blanket Load and Sleep Outcomes During Daytime Napping and Overnight Sleep: Two Randomized Crossover Studies.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Weighted blankets provide deep pressure stimulation and may support relaxation, sleep initiation, and sleep continuity. However, the optimal acute blanket load across different sleep contexts remains unclear. This study examined the acute effects of 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets on daytime napping and overnight home sleep in healthy adults. Methods: Two complementary randomized crossover protocols were integrated into one manuscript. In Protocol A, 20 healthy young adults completed four randomized 30-min laboratory nap conditions: control/sham blanket, 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets. In Protocol B, 20 healthy young adults completed four randomized overnight home sleep conditions: personal blanket control, 7 kg, 9 kg, and 14 kg weighted blankets. All conditions were separated by one-week washout intervals. Portable EEG/EOG polysomnography was used to assess nap and sleep architecture. Relaxation state, handgrip strength, blood pressure, heart rate, and skin/ambient temperature were also assessed where applicable. Results: During daytime napping, no statistically significant differences were observed across conditions for sleep outcomes. During overnight home sleep, the original gender-adjusted repeated-measures model indicated a significant condition effect on sustained sleep efficiency [F(1.929, 9.646) = 14.223, p = 0.001, η2p = 0.740], with higher values under the 9 kg and 14 kg conditions compared with control. However, a sensitivity analysis excluding gender, using the same seven complete cases, did not confirm a significant overall condition effect [F(3, 18) = 0.630, p = 0.605]. Systolic blood pressure decreased after overnight sleep with the 9 kg blanket, while skin and ambient temperatures remained unchanged. Conclusions: Weighted blankets did not significantly affect objective sleep outcomes during the daytime nap protocol. During overnight sleep, the original gender-adjusted model suggested a potential effect on sustained sleep efficiency; however, this finding was based on only seven participants with complete data and was not reproduced in either the sensitivity analysis excluding gender or the non-parametric Friedman analysis. The remaining objective sleep outcomes did not differ significantly across conditions. Accordingly, the sustained sleep efficiency finding should be considered exploratory and model-dependent rather than confirmatory evidence of an effect of weighted blanket load on overnight sleep. Larger and longer-term studies are needed before conclusions regarding the overall effectiveness of weighted blankets for sleep can be drawn.

Title: The Influence of Age and Comorbidities on Telehealth Usability Perceptions in Patients with Hypertension: A Cross-Sectional Study in Saudi Arabia.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Telehealth has promising opportunities for hypertension management through remote monitoring and enhanced patient-provider communication. However, the usability of these services may vary across patient populations, particularly with respect to age and clinical complexity. This study examined the association of age and specific comorbidity categories with perceived telehealth usability among patients with hypertension in Saudi Arabia. Methods: An analytical cross-sectional study using questionnaire data linked with retrospective electronic health-record information was conducted among adults with physician-diagnosed hypertension who received telehealth follow-up following hospital discharge. Participants completed the Arabic version of the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire (TUQ). Sociodemographic and clinical data were extracted from electronic health records. Age in years was entered as a continuous variable in the primary multivariable model, while age group was examined as a categorical sensitivity analysis. Comorbidity was entered as a nominal categorical variable using hypertension only/no additional comorbidity as the reference group. Because group variances were heterogeneous, Welch's ANOVA and Games-Howell post-hoc comparisons were used for group comparisons. Results: We included 266 adults with physician-diagnosed hypertension. Mean age among the 265 participants with valid age entries was 48.38 years (SD 18.80), and 56.0% were female. The mean total TUQ score was 93.11 ± 21.58, corresponding to a mean item score of 4.43 ± 1.03. According to the prespecified mean-item scoring framework, this represented moderate perceived usability. Significant differences were observed across age groups (Welch's F(5,46.07) = 8.96, p < 0.001; η2 ≈ 0.177), with the highest mean TUQ score among participants aged 20-30 years (110.75 ± 31.72) and the lowest among those aged >70 years (82.53 ± 7.33). In the corrected multivariable model, age was inversely associated with the TUQ score (B = -0.357, 95% CI -0.525 to -0.190; p < 0.001; β = -0.314). Compared with hypertension only/no additional comorbidity, the "other comorbidities" group had higher TUQ scores (B = 23.292, 95% CI 12.392-34.192; p < 0.001), whereas diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and respiratory conditions were not independently associated with the TUQ score. Conclusions: Perceived telehealth usability among patients with hypertension varied according to age and specific clinical characteristics. Older age was associated with less favorable usability perceptions, whereas the pattern across comorbidity categories was heterogeneous rather than uniformly positive or negative. These findings support age-sensitive, patient-centered telehealth design and targeted usability support for clinical subgroups experiencing greater barriers to digital care.

Title: Axillary Dacron Graft Versus Direct Femoral Arterial Cannulation for Peripheral VA-ECMO After Heart Transplantation: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) remains a major cause of early morbidity and mortality after heart transplantation, and peripheral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) represents an established rescue therapy for severe cases. Although direct femoral arterial cannulation is commonly used because of its rapid deployment, axillary artery cannulation through a Dacron graft provides antegrade arterial perfusion and may represent an alternative approach. This study compared early clinical outcomes and cannulation-related complications between these two arterial cannulation strategies. Methods: In this retrospective single-center observational study, 42 consecutive adult heart transplant recipients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for PGD were included. Patients were divided according to arterial cannulation strategy into direct femoral cannulation (DFC, n = 25) and axillary Dacron graft cannulation (ADG, n = 17). Baseline recipient and donor characteristics, perioperative variables, postoperative outcomes, vascular complications, successful VA-ECMO weaning, and survival to hospital discharge were compared. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for major clinical outcomes and cannulation-related complications. Results: The primary composite endpoint of cannulation-related complications occurred in 0/17 patients (0%) in the ADG group and 3/25 patients (12.0%) in the DFC group (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.01-3.80; p = 0.260). Successful VA-ECMO weaning was achieved in 94.1% versus 92.0% (p = 1.000), and survival to hospital discharge was 76.5% versus 64.0% (OR 1.83, 95% CI 0.46-7.32; p = 0.505). Stroke occurred in 5.9% versus 16.0% (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.03-3.23; p = 0.632), while renal replacement therapy was required in 35.3% versus 52.0% (OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.14-1.79; p = 0.353). No statistically significant differences were detected between groups. Conclusions: No statistically significant differences in successful VA-ECMO weaning or survival to hospital discharge were observed between axillary Dacron graft and direct femoral arterial cannulation. No statistically significant differences in neurological, vascular, or other major postoperative outcomes were detected. Although several complications occurred numerically less frequently with axillary cannulation, the limited sample size and wide confidence intervals preclude conclusions regarding comparative superiority. Axillary Dacron graft cannulation may therefore represent a feasible alternative in selected heart transplant recipients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for PGD. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted.

Title: Age-Normalized Baseline Renal Function: A Simple Risk Marker in Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
Abstract: Objective: Creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) equations incorporate age but do not normalize renal function to age-expected values. We evaluated whether the eGFR-to-Age ratio is associated with outcomes after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 1311 patients. Multivariable and Firth penalized logistic regression, DeLong receiver operating characteristic (ROC) comparisons, bootstrap internal validation, and outcome-specific Youden cut-offs were used. Results: Thirty-day mortality occurred in 19 (1.4%) and postoperative dialysis in 17 (1.3%) patients. After adjustment, each 0.1-unit increase in the ratio was associated with lower odds of mortality, with odds ratio (OR) 0.786, 95%; confidence interval (CI) 0.679-0.915, and dialysis (OR 0.735, 95% CI 0.633-0.851). For mortality, discrimination of the ratio (AUC 0.818) was comparable to that of eGFR and age entered separately (AUC 0.831, p = 0.195) and higher than that of eGFR alone (AUC 0.767, p = 0.005) and European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II (AUC 0.722, p = 0.018). Negative predictive values exceeded 99%, largely reflecting low event rates, whereas positive predictive values were below 5%. Conclusions: The eGFR-to-Age ratio is a simple single-parameter summary of eGFR and age, with discrimination comparable to that of its two components. It may serve as a supplementary bedside screening parameter rather than a replacement for comprehensive risk scores, pending external validation.

Title: Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Exploratory 12-Month Clinical Follow-Up of a Novel BIOtorcin™-Coated Balloon for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The BRight PK Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) provide local antiproliferative therapy during endovascular revascularization without leaving a permanent vascular scaffold. Sirolimus is an attractive cytostatic antiproliferative agent, although its relatively low lipophilicity creates challenges for rapid arterial uptake and sustained tissue residence following balloon delivery. The BRight DCB is a novel peripheral DCB coated with BIOtorcin™ (CRC-015), a highly lipophilic synthetic derivative of sirolimus. The BRight PK study primarily evaluated the systemic pharmacokinetics of BIOtorcin™ and its metabolite sirolimus following treatment of femoropopliteal disease and secondarily assessed procedural performance, safety, patency, and functional outcomes over 12 months. Methods: BRight PK was a prospective, single-center, non-randomized pharmacokinetic study involving six adults with symptomatic peripheral artery disease (PAD; Rutherford-Becker category 2-4) caused by de novo superficial femoral and/or proximal popliteal artery disease. Following mandatory predilatation, lesions were treated with one or two BRight DCBs. Whole-blood BIOtorcin™ and sirolimus concentrations were measured before treatment and serially from 5 min to 24 h after removal of the final DCB. Non-compartmental pharmacokinetic analysis was performed. Angiography and duplex ultrasound were independently assessed by a core laboratory, and endpoint-related clinical events were independently adjudicated. Results: All six participants completed 12-month follow-up. Mean age was 70.8 ± 7.4 years, and four (66.7%) were male. Seven BRight DCBs treated six lesions. Mean core-laboratory lesion length was 140.85 ± 136.23 mm, and baseline diameter stenosis was 78.50 ± 23.39%. Mean BIOtorcin™ exposure was 3976.8 ± 1665.7 µg (0.051 ± 0.0188 mg/kg). BIOtorcin™ Cmax was 23.60 ± 9.88 ng/mL at 5 min, terminal half-life was 21.87 ± 10.17 h, AUC0-t was 28.30 ± 12.19 h·ng/mL, and AUC0-∞ was 47.47 ± 18.27 h·ng/mL. Sirolimus Cmax was 0.692 ± 0.462 ng/mL at 24 h, when concentrations remained on the ascending portion of the concentration-time curve, indicating that the 24 h sampling window captured only early systemic sirolimus exposure rather than a complete pharmacokinetic profile. Device success was 100% (7/7); core-laboratory technical and procedural success were each 66.7% (4/6). No deaths, major or minor amputations, clinically driven target lesion revascularizations (cd-TLR), or clinically driven target vessel revascularizations (cd-TVRs) occurred. Visit-based 12-month primary patency was 83.3% (5/6); the single binary restenosis was detected at day 391, resulting in Kaplan-Meier primary patency of 100% at calendar day 365. The mean overall Walking Impairment Questionnaire (WIQ) score increased from 21.87 ± 19.16 at baseline to 62.28 ± 38.78 at 12 months. Conclusions: BIOtorcin™ demonstrated rapid systemic appearance following BRight DCB treatment, followed by a progressive decline in circulating parent drug concentrations and low systemic exposure to its metabolite, sirolimus. These pharmacokinetic findings, together with successful device delivery and the absence of major safety concerns over 12 months, demonstrate procedural feasibility and support continued clinical evaluation of the BRight DCB. Given the pharmacokinetic study design and small sample size (n = 6), the 12-month clinical, functional, and patency findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical efficacy.

Title: Postprocessing of Structural En Face OCT Images of the Choroidal Haller Layer for Quantitative Assessment: An Exploratory Pilot Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: To develop a binarization workflow for structural en face OCT images of the choroidal Haller layer and examine how postprocessing parameters affect measurements, using chronological age as an exploratory reference. Methods: We included 66 healthy volunteers (66 eyes; 22-73 years; three age groups). En face Haller layer images from swept-source OCT angiography scans (DRI OCT Triton; 6 × 6 mm) were binarized using retinal vessel masking and Phansalkar thresholding. Radius R (22 values) and coefficients k and r (24 combinations) were varied. Results: Measurements depended strongly on R; age-group separation was similar over R = 13-26 pixels; permutation testing gave p = 0.031 across radii and p = 0.115 across all 45 configurations. Using the representative working configurations (R = 17 pixels; default k = 0.25 and r = 0.50), vessel density (VD), vessel length density (VLD), and inter-vessel distance (IVD) showed modest, non-monotonic nominal age-group differences (η2 ≈ 0.10); those for VD and IVD were lost after accounting for masked regions. Adjusted for sex and spherical equivalent, VLD decreased and IVD increased with age, whereas VD did not. Conclusions: Measurements depend substantially on postprocessing parameters. The working configuration, selected and evaluated in one cohort, requires repeatability testing and independent validation.

Title: Cardiorenal Syndrome: From Hemodynamic and Humoral Pathophysiology to New Frontiers in Modulation and Enabling Therapy-Part 1.
Abstract: Cardiorenal syndrome (CRS) encompasses a spectrum of disorders in which acute or chronic dysfunction of the heart or the kidney induces dysfunction in the other. Although the five-subtype classification provides a useful conceptual framework, operational definitions remain heterogeneous and management requires an individualized approach. Traditionally attributed to reduced forward arterial perfusion, renal impairment in heart failure is increasingly associated with systemic venous congestion and renal venous hypertension, although most evidence is observational. At the humoral level, chronic activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system and the sympathetic nervous system sustains a cycle of oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibrosis. In this first part of a narrative review, we summarize these hemodynamic and humoral mechanisms and examine biomarkers that complement serum creatinine, including markers of filtration, tubular injury, and fibro-inflammatory activity, emphasizing that their interpretation depends on baseline renal function and congestion status. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to September 2026. The available evidence is mainly observational and heterogeneous; these biomarkers appear complementary rather than substitutive, and their incremental clinical value requires prospective validation. Therapeutic strategies will be addressed in Part 2.

Title: The Aldosterone-Immune Axis in Primary Aldosteronism: Linking Adrenal Pathogenesis to Systemic Inflammation and Target-Organ Damage.
Abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is the most common endocrine cause of secondary hypertension and is increasingly recognised as a systemic disorder extending beyond haemodynamic dysregulation. Accumulating evidence suggests that chronic autonomous aldosterone excess promotes maladaptive immune activation, establishing an aldosterone-immune axis that may contribute to cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic injury independently of blood pressure elevation. In some patients, glucocorticoid co-secretion may further amplify tissue-specific mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) signalling. Human and experimental studies indicate that aldosterone modulates both innate and adaptive immunity. Patients with PA demonstrate altered monocyte transcriptional profiles, enhanced vascular inflammatory activity, and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine signalling in monocyte-derived macrophages compared with blood-pressure-matched essential hypertension controls. Experimental models further show that sustained aldosterone exposure promotes macrophage M1 polarisation, dendritic cell activation, Th17 expansion, and regulatory T-cell suppression. These inflammatory changes are accompanied by oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, fibroblast activation, and extracellular matrix remodelling across cardiovascular and renal tissues. Emerging evidence is also consistent with a role for trained innate immunity, whereby prolonged aldosterone exposure may induce persistent epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming of monocytes and macrophages. Whether such reprogramming persists after biochemical correction by adrenalectomy or MR antagonism in human PA has not yet been directly demonstrated and remains an important open question. If confirmed, these mechanisms may help explain the partial irreversibility of target-organ damage despite successful treatment. This review synthesises current evidence linking adrenal somatic pathogenesis to systemic immune dysregulation and target-organ injury in PA. We propose that PA should be viewed not solely as a hypertensive disorder, but as a chronic fibro-inflammatory endocrine disease with important implications for early diagnosis, risk stratification, and targeted therapy. Future prospective human studies are needed to confirm the mechanistic hierarchy proposed and to identify the immunological targets most amenable to therapeutic intervention.

Title: Early Initiation of Dapagliflozin in Acute Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Dapagliflozin is a foundational chronic heart failure therapy, but whether it retains benefit when initiated early during hospitalization for acute heart failure (AHF) remains uncertain. Methods: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and CENTRAL from inception to 26 January 2026 for randomized trials comparing early initiation of dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily with standard therapy in adults hospitalized for AHF (PROSPERO CRD420261364466). Two reviewers independently performed screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Outcomes were pooled under random-effects models with Knapp-Hartung adjustment. Results: Ten trials enrolling 3507 participants (1769 in the dapagliflozin group and 1738 in the control group) were eligible. Dapagliflozin significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.52-0.86) and urinary tract infections (RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.35-0.76), while no significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death, MACEs, heart failure hospitalization, all-cause readmission, length of hospital stay, or body weight. Dapagliflozin was not associated with a significant increase in acute kidney injury, hypotension, or hypoglycemia, supporting a favorable safety profile. Conclusions: In adults hospitalized with acute heart failure (AHF), dapagliflozin significantly reduced all-cause mortality but not heart failure hospitalization during follow-up. Larger, adequately powered trials in patients with AHF, with prespecified analyses according to the timing of dapagliflozin initiation, are warranted.

Title: The Glymphatic System in Traumatic Brain Injury, Subarachnoid Hemorrhage, and Neurodegeneration: A Unifying Neurobiological Framework.
Abstract: Whether glymphatic dysfunction drives or merely follows brain injury and neurodegeneration remains unresolved. The glymphatic system mediates the transport, exchange, and clearance of solutes between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and interstitial fluid (ISF) through paravascular CSF influx, polarized aquaporin-4 (AQP4) at astrocytic endfeet, and meningeal lymphatic drainage. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on glymphatic regulation and its role in traumatic brain injury (TBI), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), and neurodegeneration, and appraises imaging, biomarker, and therapeutic approaches. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from inception to August 2026, and 128 sources were analyzed. In TBI, mechanical shear and NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)-dependent inflammation may alter AQP4 distribution and impair tau and amyloid-beta (Aβ) clearance; however, glymphatic failure has not been established as the causal mediator of later neurodegeneration, which is likely multifactorial. After SAH, blood and fibrin may obstruct perivascular pathways, and hemoglobin, heme, and iron toxicity may further disrupt CSF-ISF exchange; these changes are associated with delayed cerebral ischemia, cortical spreading depolarizations, and post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus. Impaired clearance of Aβ, phosphorylated tau, and α-synuclein may link glymphatic dysfunction to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, although causality is unproven. Current imaging tools, including diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), and biomarkers do not yet provide a validated measure of glymphatic function. Sleep optimization is a low-risk strategy, and controlled lumbar drainage has the strongest clinical evidence among CSF-dynamics approaches. Translation requires appropriate animal models and prospective TBI/SAH studies combining serial DTI-ALPS with cognitive follow-up.

Title: Physiological Basis of Skeletal Muscle Electrical Stimulation in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction: Established Mechanisms, Extrapolated Mechanisms and Translational Priorities.
Abstract: Skeletal muscle electrical stimulation, delivered as neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) or functional electrical stimulation (FES), is one of very few interventions in heart failure that produces sustained contractile work in the periphery without volitional effort and, in low-frequency configurations, without a measurable rise in cardiac output. Three decades of clinical evaluation have produced consistent signals of improved muscle strength, walking distance and quality of life. The physiological rationale that underpins these observations has advanced much less. This review separates what has been demonstrated in human skeletal muscle in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) from what has been extrapolated from healthy volunteers, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, critical illness and ageing muscle. We frame stimulation within the muscle hypothesis of chronic heart failure, in which peripheral myopathy drives ergoreflex overactivity, sympathetic excitation and exertional symptoms, and we show that the decisive mechanistic question, whether a programme of stimulation attenuates ergoreflex sensitivity, has never been tested, although two sham-controlled microneurographic studies indicate that stimulation acutely lowers muscle sympathetic nerve activity. Four further gaps are identified: a single biopsy-controlled randomised dataset in advanced heart failure, a single in vivo spectroscopic study in which muscle energetics did not change, absence of contemporary molecular phenotyping of anabolic and proteolytic signalling in stimulated HFrEF muscle, and drift of the recent evidence base towards decompensated, frail and older populations with mixed ejection fraction. Against the background of the 2026 European Society of Cardiology guidelines, which recommend exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation for all stable patients and mention electrical muscle stimulation only as an option for very weak patients, we propose a research agenda in which stimulation dose is reported as a biological variable and muscle afferent physiology becomes the primary mechanistic endpoint.

Title: Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Among Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Undergoing Clinically Indicated Echocardiography at a Saudi Cardiac Center: Prevalence and Associated Factors.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is an important cardiovascular complication, but regional data on this condition among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in Saudi Arabia remain limited. This study determined the prevalence of LVH and associated factors among adults with T2DM without documented cardiac disease undergoing clinically indicated echocardiography at a specialized cardiac center in Saudi Arabia. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 625 patients with T2DM who underwent clinically indicated echocardiography at Prince Sultan Cardiac Center, Qassim, between January 2023 and December 2025. Of 878 patients with T2DM and no documented cardiac disease assessed for eligibility, 253 (28.8%) were excluded because at least one required clinical variable was missing or unavailable, leaving 625 patients (71.2%) in the final analysis. LVH was assessed according to American Society of Echocardiography/European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging recommendations. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with LVH. Results: LVH was identified in 146/625 patients (23.4%; 95% CI, 20.0-26.7). After multivariable adjustment, male sex (aOR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.11-2.63; p = 0.015) and uncontrolled/elevated blood pressure (aOR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.26-3.80; p = 0.006) were associated with LVH. Diabetes duration showed a significant nonlinear association with LVH (overall p < 0.001; p for nonlinearity = 0.001). Conclusions: LVH was common among this clinically selected group of patients with T2DM undergoing clinically indicated echocardiography. Male sex and uncontrolled/elevated blood pressure were associated with LVH after adjustment, while diabetes duration showed a nonlinear association. Although causal relationships cannot be established, the observed association between uncontrolled/elevated blood pressure and LVH highlights the importance of optimal blood pressure management as part of comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction in patients with T2DM.

Title: Inflammatory Hematological Indices in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: Associations with Disease Severity and 12-Month Outcomes.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory syndrome with limited diagnostic and prognostic tools applicable in routine practice. Hematological indices derived from complete blood count, including neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), red cell distribution width (RDW), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), have emerged as potential markers of systemic inflammation and cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to compare these indices between patients with HFpEF and individuals without heart failure and to examine their associations with disease severity and 12-month clinical outcomes. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, 221 patients with confirmed HFpEF were compared with 143 control subjects without heart failure. NLR, RDW, and PLR were calculated from routine laboratory tests. Associations with echocardiographic parameters, NT-proBNP levels, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Patients were followed for 12 months to assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), all-cause mortality, and heart failure-related rehospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression models were used to evaluate independent prognostic value. Results: Patients with HFpEF exhibited significantly higher NLR (3.98 ± 0.98 vs. 2.72 ± 0.81), RDW (14.62 ± 1.09% vs. 13.48 ± 0.92%), and PLR (152.4 ± 38.7 vs. 131.9 ± 29.6) compared with controls (all p < 0.001). NLR and RDW correlated with NT-proBNP, E/e' ratio, left atrial volume index, and NYHA class. Higher tertiles of NLR and RDW were associated with progressively increased rates of MACEs and all-cause mortality, with statistically significant trends across tertiles (all p-trend ≤ 0.008). In multivariable analysis, NLR (HR 1.28, p = 0.001) and RDW (HR 1.32, p < 0.001) remained independently associated with 12-month MACEs, while PLR showed borderline significance. However, ROC analysis demonstrated limited discrimination, with AUC values ranging from approximately 0.55 to 0.61, indicating that none of the three indices reliably discriminated between patients with and without MACEs when considered individually. Conclusions: NLR and RDW were elevated in patients with HFpEF and were independently associated with disease severity and 12-month MACEs. However, all three indices showed limited individual discrimination and should not be considered standalone prognostic tools. Their potential clinical value, if any, requires evaluation as part of validated multivariable prediction models.

Title: Multi-Omics and Digital Biomarkers for Dynamic Cardiometabolic Risk Prediction.
Abstract: Cardiometabolic risk changes as metabolic state, vascular injury, behavior and treatment evolve. Multi-omics assays characterize the underlying molecular state, whereas wearable sensors and continuous glucose monitoring capture physiological responses during daily life. This review asks whether combining these measurements improves a defined clinical decision beyond established clinical information in type 2 diabetes, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and heart failure. We distinguish biological association, prediction and clinical utility, and define dynamic risk prediction as repeated estimation of future event probability over a specified horizon using only information available at each prediction time. Large cohorts link proteins and metabolites with future disease, and intensive studies connect molecular variation with activity, nutrition and glycemic responses. However, evidence for joint molecular-digital integration remains predominantly observational. Trials of glucose monitoring and structured telemanagement show that monitoring can improve outcomes when it is embedded in an effective care pathway, but they do not establish the incremental value of multi-omics. We therefore organize the evidence around three requirements: temporal alignment of stable genomic information, intermittent molecular assays and dense digital trajectories; validation against a strong clinical comparator; and prospective assessment of patient outcomes, cost and burden. Emerging sensors, dynamical network biomarkers and digital twins may eventually extend this framework, but they remain experimental or conceptual for integrated cardiometabolic event prediction.

Title: Comparative Associations of Inflammation and Nutrition-Based Indices with No-Reflow and Mortality After Primary PCI for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute myocardial infarction is accompanied by thromboinflammation, immune-cell redistribution and changes in nutritional reserve. We compared six routinely calculable indices under a common modelling strategy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Methods: This retrospective cohort included 2613 patients. The primary endpoint was long-term all-cause mortality, analysed with Cox regression; angiographic no-reflow, in-hospital mortality and 30-day mortality were analysed with logistic regression. The global immune-nutrition-inflammation index (GINI), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), controlling nutritional status (CONUT) score, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and Naples prognostic score (NAPLES) were evaluated in separate models. Continuous indices were modelled flexibly, and every effect estimate compared the 75th with the 25th percentile. Results: No-reflow occurred in 353 patients (13.5%), in-hospital death in 102 (3.9%), 30-day death in 157 (6.0%) and long-term death in 466 (17.8%). Median recorded follow-up was 34 [14-46] months. After clinical adjustment, the Q3-versus-Q1 hazard ratios for long-term mortality were 1.17 (95% CI 1.00-1.36) for GINI, 0.79 (0.68-0.91) for PNI, 1.19 (1.01-1.40) for CONUT, 1.20 (1.04-1.39) for SII, 1.24 (1.07-1.44) for NLR and 1.13 (0.98-1.31) for NAPLES. After Holm correction across the six primary tests, PNI, SII and NLR retained evidence of association. In angiographically expanded no-reflow models, GINI and NLR retained Q3-versus-Q1 associations. Conclusions: Admission inflammatory and immune-nutrition indices showed outcome-specific prognostic associations. PNI, SII and NLR had the most consistent multiplicity-sensitive long-term associations, whereas GINI and NLR retained associations with no-reflow after angiographic adjustment. These findings do not establish causal effects, predictive superiority or readiness for clinical decision-making.

Title: Chronic Proton Pump Inhibitor Use and Glycemic Control in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Evidence regarding the effects of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) on glucose metabolism is conflicting, and real-world data on the association between chronic PPI use and glycemic control in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are limited. This study aimed to evaluate the association between chronic PPI use and glycemic control in patients with T2DM aged 65 years or older. Methods: This single-center, retrospective cross-sectional study included 462 T2DM patients attending the Family Medicine Outpatient Clinic of Ankara Bilkent City Hospital between April 2025 and April 2026. Patients with regular PPI use for ≥6 months before the index HbA1c were classified as chronic PPI users. Suboptimal glycemic control was defined as HbA1c ≥ 8.0%. Associations were evaluated using logistic regression for suboptimal control and linear regression for HbA1c level. Results: Of the 462 patients, 316 (68.4%) were chronic PPI users. Mean HbA1c (7.11 ± 1.21% vs. 6.23 ± 0.99%; p < 0.001) and fasting plasma glucose (148.70 ± 64.87 vs. 116.23 ± 43.54 mg/dL; p < 0.001) were higher among PPI users. In multivariable logistic regression, chronic PPI use was independently associated with suboptimal glycemic control (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 3.416; 95% CI: 1.572-7.422; p = 0.002). This association remained significant in a sensitivity model additionally adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), smoking status, diabetes duration, insulin use, metformin use, and heart failure/coronary artery disease (aOR = 3.834; 95% CI: 1.734-8.478; p = 0.001). In multivariable linear regression, chronic PPI use was independently associated with a 0.793-percentage-point higher HbA1c level (95% CI: 0.570-1.016; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Chronic PPI use was independently associated with higher HbA1c levels and suboptimal glycemic control in older adults with T2DM. Because of the observational design, causality cannot be established. Prospective studies accounting for PPI indication, agent-specific effects, dose, and duration of exposure are needed to clarify the nature of this association.

Title: EASIX for Long-Term Prognostication in Hospitalized Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: Incremental Value Beyond Clinical Risk Markers.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous multisystem syndrome in which conventional cardiac measures may not fully capture systemic vulnerability. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) is prognostic in other cardiovascular populations, but evidence in HFpEF remains limited. We evaluated the association of EASIX with long-term mortality and compared its prognostic value with the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) and Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 79 adults hospitalized with HFpEF between 2019 and 2025. EASIX, PNI, and CONUT were calculated from admission laboratory values. The endpoint was all-cause mortality. EASIX was modeled using restricted cubic splines. Incremental value beyond age, serum sodium, and B-type natriuretic peptide was assessed using likelihood-ratio tests. Harrell's C-index was internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples; conventional and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analyses were also performed. Results: During a median follow-up of 27.6 months, 45 patients (57.0%) died. EASIX was nonlinearly associated with mortality (overall and nonlinearity p < 0.001) and improved clinical model fit (Δχ2 = 24.36; p < 0.001). PNI improved the clinical model without EASIX (Δχ2 = 8.74; p = 0.003), but its contribution after EASIX was attenuated (Δχ2 = 3.54; p = 0.060); CONUT did not improve model fit (p = 0.859). Optimism-corrected C-indices were 0.728 for clinical + EASIX and 0.732 after adding PNI. Conventional AUCs were 0.753, 0.782, and 0.661 for EASIX, PNI, and CONUT, respectively. Conclusions: In this selected hospitalized HFpEF cohort, EASIX provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical markers. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts with external validation.

Title: Leukocyte-to-HDL Ratios for Symptomatic Phenotyping in Heart Failure: Head-to-Head Comparison of Routine Inflammatory Indices and Benchmarking Against NT-proBNP.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Inflammatory indices are increasingly studied in heart failure (HF), but direct comparisons remain limited. We compared eight indices across New York Heart Association (NYHA) classes and assessed the leading indices against N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Methods: This analysis included 85 patients with established HF. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), neutrophil-to-HDL ratio (NHR), lymphocyte-to-HDL ratio (LHR), monocyte-to-HDL ratio (MHR), platelet-to-HDL ratio (PHR), and uric acid-to-HDL ratio (UHR) were evaluated using group comparisons, Spearman correlations, ordinal logistic regression, and multivariable models for NYHA III/IV versus I/II. Primary multivariable models used a parsimonious adjustment set comprising age, smoking status, and HF duration, while broader covariate adjustment was examined in sensitivity analyses. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results: NHR and PHR differed across NYHA classes after FDR correction. In parsimoniously adjusted ordinal models, SII, SIRI, NLR, NHR, MHR, and PHR were associated with increasing NYHA class after FDR correction. In the NYHA III/IV versus I/II analysis, only NHR (OR per doubling 2.01, 95% CI 1.19-3.39) and MHR (OR 1.96, 95% CI 1.17-3.25) remained significant after FDR correction (q = 0.022 for both). AUCs were 0.688 for the reference model, 0.775 with NHR, 0.777 with MHR, and 0.978 with NT-proBNP. Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.739 for NHR, 0.739 for MHR, and 0.969 for NT-proBNP. Neither ratio improved model fit beyond NT-proBNP. Conclusions: NHR and MHR showed the most consistent adjusted associations with NYHA-defined symptomatic severity and remained robust across sensitivity analyses. They should be viewed as compact routine inflammatory-metabolic indices rather than independent biomarkers or replacements for NT-proBNP. External and prospective longitudinal validation is warranted.

Title: Prehypertension and Endothelial Dysfunction: The Role of Oxidative Stress.
Abstract: Prehypertension, defined as blood pressure of 120-139/80-89 mmHg, affects approximately 36-38% of adults worldwide and is associated with a substantially increased risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and coronary heart disease. Beyond being a transitional stage toward overt hypertension, prehypertension represents a biologically active vascular state in which early vascular injury is already evident. Endothelial dysfunction is considered the earliest detectable vascular abnormality in prehypertension and is characterized by reduced nitric oxide bioavailability, endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) uncoupling, and increased asymmetric dimethylarginine levels. These alterations are accompanied by endothelial activation, reflected by enhanced expression of adhesion molecules and endothelin-1, as well as impaired endothelial progenitor cell function with a reported threshold effect at systolic blood pressure of 130 mmHg. In parallel, prehypertensive individuals exhibit increased arterial stiffness and microvascular abnormalities, including systemic capillary rarefaction and retinal microvascular alterations. Oxidative stress, driven mainly by NADPH oxidase activation and eNOS uncoupling, appears to be a central mechanism linking elevated blood pressure with endothelial dysfunction and progressive vascular damage. However, the temporal relationship between oxidative imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, and blood pressure progression remains unclear. It is still uncertain whether oxidative stress initiates vascular impairment or primarily accelerates already established endothelial injury. Further prospective studies are needed to define the vascular trajectory of prehypertension, clarify its prognostic relevance, and identify whether early vascular alterations represent therapeutic targets for cardiovascular prevention. By integrating current evidence, this review examines endothelial dysfunction in prehypertension, with particular attention to oxidative stress and its interactions with NO signaling, endothelial activation, and vascular remodeling.

Title: Incident Atrial Fibrillation Following Anthracycline-Based Adjuvant Chemotherapy in Women with Breast Cancer: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Anthracyclines carry considerable cardiotoxicity risk, and atrial fibrillation (AF) during cancer treatment adversely affects morbidity and mortality. We compared the incidence of clinically documented AF and explored its early clinical correlates between anthracycline-containing and non-anthracycline adjuvant regimens in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included consecutive women with stage II TNBC treated with breast-conserving surgery and adjuvant doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by docetaxel (AC-T) or docetaxel-cyclophosphamide (TC) between 2018 and 2023. ECG and echocardiography were performed at baseline, month one, and month six. Clinically documented AF was defined as AF documented on a scheduled or symptom-triggered 12-lead ECG or as AF lasting ≥30 s on symptom-triggered 72 h Holter monitoring. Patients with structural or coronary heart disease, complete bundle branch block, or non-sinus rhythm were excluded. Results: Among 140 women (mean age, 64 ± 12 years; 64 AC-T), 17 (12.1%) developed clinically documented AF within six months. AF was more frequent with AC-T (18.8% vs. 6.6%; absolute risk difference, 12.2% [95% CI, 1.1-23.3%]; risk ratio, 2.85 [1.07-7.58]; log-rank p = 0.030), and the association persisted after inverse probability of treatment weighting (OR, 3.28 [1.05-10.24]). At one month, PR prolongation > 20 ms was associated with incident AF (OR, 5.16 [1.79-14.89]), whereas conventional echocardiographic changes did not differ between regimens. Conclusions: The AC-T regimen was associated with more clinically documented incident AF than TC. Early PR prolongation, occurring without detectable changes in conventional echocardiographic parameters, may be an informative early electrical signal of AF risk, although prospective validation is required.

Title: Is the International Normalized Ratio (INR) Enough? Reevaluating INR-Based Decision-Making for Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate in Geriatric Warfarin-Associated Intracranial Hemorrhage: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Warfarin-associated intracranial hemorrhage (WA-ICH) remains one of the most devastating anticoagulant-related emergencies, particularly among older adults, with substantial morbidity and mortality. Although current guidelines recommend that reversal strategies should be guided primarily by bleeding severity and clinical presentation rather than the international normalized ratio (INR) alone, real-world treatment decisions often continue to rely on INR thresholds. This study investigated whether INR is an adequate determinant for four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) administration in geriatric patients with non-traumatic WA-ICH. Methods: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients aged ≥65 years presenting with non-traumatic WA-ICH to five tertiary-care centers in Turkey were evaluated. Patients were categorized according to reversal strategy into a 4F-PCC group (n = 30) and a heterogeneous non-PCC management group (n = 30), which included supportive care, intravenous vitamin K, FFP, combinations of these approaches, or no specific reversal treatment. Subgroup analyses were performed using multiple INR thresholds to examine the relationship between INR levels, treatment allocation, and in-hospital mortality. The primary outcome was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Results: Patients who received 4F-PCC had higher admission INR values than those managed without PCC, whereas admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) was similar between treatment groups. Admission GCS was substantially lower among non-survivors than survivors. In the revised Firth-penalized logistic regression model, higher admission GCS was independently associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.37 per 1-point increase; 95% CI 0.10-0.62; p < 0.001), whereas 4F-PCC administration and admission INR values were not independently associated with mortality. Conclusions: Higher admission INR was associated with 4F-PCC administration and was not independently associated with mortality, whereas admission GCS was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings support consideration of neurological, radiological, and laboratory information together rather than interpretation of admission INR in isolation. Given the retrospective design, small sample size, baseline differences in anticoagulation intensity, and potential residual confounding, the findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Title: Association of the Charlson Comorbidity Index and Age-Adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index with Clinical Course and Mortality in Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) frequently coexists with comorbidities that may influence clinical outcomes. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) quantifies the weighted comorbidity burden, whereas the age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (ACCI) additionally incorporates age. We evaluated the associations of CCI and ACCI with pulmonary function, disease severity, clinical course, and mortality in IPF. Methods: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 319 patients with IPF. Comorbidities present at diagnosis were scored using the CCI and ACCI. Associations with pulmonary function, GAP index, acute exacerbations, hospitalization, long-term oxygen therapy, echocardiographic findings suggestive of pulmonary hypertension, incident malignancy, antifibrotic treatment, and mortality were assessed. Correlation analyses were performed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, and Bonferroni correction was applied to account for multiple testing. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate whether the CCI or ACCI was independently associated with survival. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results: The mean age was 71 ± 8 years, 78.1% were male, and 75.5% had at least one comorbid condition among patients with available comorbidity data. The median CCI and ACCI scores were 2 (IQR, 0-4) and 5 (IQR, 4-7), respectively. Higher CCI and ACCI categories were associated with hospitalization (p = 0.006 and p = 0.011), echocardiographic findings suggestive of pulmonary hypertension (both p = 0.002), and incident malignancy (p < 0.001 and p = 0.005, respectively). After Bonferroni correction, higher CCI and ACCI categories remained significantly associated with echocardiographic findings suggestive of pulmonary hypertension (both p = 0.002) and incident malignancy (both p < 0.001), whereas the associations with hospitalization did not remain statistically significant. A nominal association between ACCI and mortality (p = 0.044) also did not remain significant after Bonferroni correction. In Spearman analyses, ACCI remained significantly correlated with current age, age at IPF diagnosis, and the GAP index after correction, whereas the correlations of CCI and ACCI with baseline DLCO did not. Neither CCI (HR = 1.029, 95% CI: 0.923-1.146; p = 0.610) nor ACCI (HR = 1.035, 95% CI: 0.936-1.144; p = 0.509) was independently associated with survival in multivariable Cox regression analyses. Lower baseline DLCO remained independently associated with survival in both Cox models (both p < 0.001).Kaplan-Meier survival curves were constructed according to the predefined CCI and ACCI score categories (0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥5), and survival distributions across categories were compared using the log-rank test. Conclusions: CCI and ACCI were associated with selected clinical characteristics in IPF, particularly echocardiographic findings suggestive of pulmonary hypertension and incident malignancy. However, neither index independently predicted survival after multivariable adjustment. These indices may complement, rather than replace, disease-specific physiological assessments in patients with IPF.

Title: Prevalence of Epiretinal Membrane and Macular Edema Across Uveitis Subtypes: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of epiretinal membrane (ERM) and macular edema (ME) at initial presentation across clinically defined uveitis subtypes. Methods: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, we reviewed clinical records from the initial visit and imaging from 3879 eyes of 2559 patients diagnosed with uveitis at Tokyo Medical University Hospital between 2011 and 2021. The prevalence of ERM and ME was estimated overall and by uveitis subtype, with additional descriptive age- and sex-stratified analyses. Results: ERM and ME were identified in 185/3879 eyes (4.8%) and 235/3879 eyes (6.1%), respectively. Rare subtypes with very small sample sizes showed the highest crude prevalences; however, among uveitis subtypes represented by at least 30 eyes, sarcoidosis had the highest ERM prevalence (50/363 eyes, 13.8%). By contrast, Behçet's disease had the highest ME prevalence (44/284 eyes, 15.5%). In descriptive subgroup analyses, Behçet's disease accounted for a greater proportion of ERM and ME in male and younger patients. By contrast, sarcoidosis accounted for a greater proportion in female and older patients. Conclusions: The prevalence of ERM and ME at presentation varied across uveitis subtypes; of those represented by at least 30 eyes, sarcoidosis showed the highest prevalence of ERM, whereas Behçet's disease showed the highest prevalence of ME.

Title: Serum Peroxides and Galectin-3 in Chronic Heart Failure: Cross-Sectional Associations with NT-proBNP and Cardiac Structure.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Oxidative stress and galectin-3-related fibro-inflammatory processes contribute to heart failure pathophysiology, but their concurrent relationships with natriuretic peptides and structural/cardiorenal parameters remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated baseline associations of serum peroxide burden and galectin-3 with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and related phenotypic parameters in chronic heart failure. Methods: This cross-sectional analysis included 57 patients from a prospective single-center cohort. Serum peroxides were quantified using the ferrous oxidation-xylenol orange assay and expressed as nmol H2O2 equivalents/mL. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and linear regression with ln-transformed NT-proBNP. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied to eight secondary/exploratory correlations. Results: Serum peroxide burden correlated with NT-proBNP (ρ = 0.387, p = 0.0095; n = 44) and remained significantly associated after adjustment for age, sex, and left ventricular ejection fraction (B = 0.1756, p = 0.0420; n = 43). After additional estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) adjustment, the effect estimate remained similar, although statistical significance was not reached (B = 0.1646, p = 0.0525; n = 39). Galectin-3 correlated with NT-proBNP, left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi), and serum uric acid; all associations remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Serum peroxide burden and galectin-3 were not significantly correlated. In an exploratory joint model (n = 29), both biomarkers remained significantly associated with ln(NT-proBNP) (adjusted R2 = 0.4294). Conclusions: Serum peroxide burden and galectin-3 showed different cross-sectional association patterns with NT-proBNP and selected structural/cardiorenal parameters. Given the limited sample size, missing data, and exploratory nature of the joint model, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and do not establish biological independence or incremental clinical value.

Title: Myocardial Work Index Dispersion as a Potential Predictor of Ventricular Arrhythmias in Patients with Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction.
Abstract: Background: Mechanical dispersion of left ventricular contraction reflects electromechanical heterogeneity and may contribute to arrhythmogenesis. We evaluated whether myocardial work dispersion is associated with ventricular arrhythmia (VA) risk in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods: Eighty-five patients with HFrEF and no history of atrial fibrillation of any type and with complete arrhythmia follow-up (mean age 65 ± 12 years, 83.5% male, mean LVEF 30.5 ± 6.6%) underwent echocardiography one day before elective implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) or cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT) implantation and were followed for one year. Results: VAs-sustained or non-sustained ventricular tachycardia, or ventricular fibrillation-occurred in 32.9% of patients. Myocardial work index (MWI) dispersion, expressed as standard deviation (SD) or Range, showed the highest single-parameter discrimination (AUC 0.848 and 0.859). Models combining MWI dispersion with right atrial (RA) area performed best (AUC 0.912 and 0.911). In multivariable logistic regression, both MWI dispersion and RA area were independently associated with VAs; odds ratios per 10-unit increase were 1.116 for MWI dispersion (SD), 1.030 for MWI dispersion (Range) and 1.276 per 1 cm2 of RA area. Conclusions: In this cohort, MWI dispersion showed the highest single-parameter discrimination for VAs among the echocardiographic variables tested, and its combination with RA area gave the best model. The two variables were independently associated with VAs in the same model. These exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation before clinical application.

Title: Comparative Prognostic Value of AFP, PIVKA-II, and GPC-3 in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Real-World Multicenter Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The current cornerstone for prognostic hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) stratification is the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) score, which integrates tumor and liver function staging but lacks tumor biology parameters. Serum tumor biomarkers, such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), protein induced by vitamin K absence-II (PIVKA-II), and glypican-3 (GPC-3), may improve prognostic assessment. We evaluated their prognostic value in this multicenter retrospective study. Methods: Serum AFP, PIVKA-II, and GPC-3 levels were measured (as continuous and categorical variables: >20 ng/mL, >200 mAU/mL, and >150 pg/mL, respectively) at baseline in 605 consecutive patients newly diagnosed with HCC at two tertiary Italian centers (2010-2024). The correlation between tumor stage, liver function, tumor marker levels, and overall survival (OS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models. Results: Tumor marker levels increased stepwise across BCLC stages. Median OS was 29.0 months, declining from 47.9 months (BCLC-0) to 10.7 months (BCLC-C; p < 0.001). In univariate analysis, shorter OS was significantly (p < 0.001) associated with elevated serum levels of all tumor markers, higher ALBI grade, presence of ascites, and portal hypertension. On multivariate analysis, BCLC stage, ascites (hazard ratio [HR] 2.19, p < 0.001), ALBI grade 2-3 (HR 1.36, p = 0.009), and PIVKA-II > 200 mAU/mL (HR 1.56, p < 0.001) were independently associated with OS, whereas GPC-3 showed a borderline association (HR 1.27, p = 0.058), but not AFP (HR 0.88; p = 0.306). Conclusions: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, PIVKA-II was the only serum biomarker independently associated with OS after adjusting for BCLC stage and liver function. These findings support further prospective evaluation of whether PIVKA-II provides clinically meaningful incremental prognostic information beyond established BCLC-based assessment.

Title: The Gut-Kidney Axis in Chronic Kidney Disease: Microbial Dysbiosis, Host-Microbial Metabolism, and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies.
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) appears linked to changes in the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier defects, and microbiota-driven changes in metabolite profiles. Experimental evidence links gut microbiota disturbances to kidney injury through pathways such as microbial metabolism, inflammation, immune signals, and epithelial barrier dysfunction. Still, applying this knowledge in clinical practice for patients with CKD remains difficult.
