For instance, one study on indoxyl sulfate and p-cresyl sulfate levels in a patient showed that, beyond being synthesized by the intestinal microbiota, the host can also metabolize or alter these metabolites. In addition, they undergo impaired renal clearance and can be secreted by the tubules. Moreover, most human microbiome-related studies are observational, making it difficult to determine the causal role of bacterial dysbiosis. Disease, dietary factors, medication, and other comorbid conditions are major confounders. Microbiota-directed means of altering the composition of the microbiota, such as changing diet, using prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics, oral adsorbents, and even fecal microbiota transplantation, have, to varying degrees, affected the composition of the gut microbiota, levels of uremic toxins, short-chain fatty acids, and markers of inflammation. They have also been connected to leaky gut syndrome. However, evidence that these actions delay eGFR decline or prevent kidney failure, cardiovascular events, hospitalization, or mortality remains limited. Postbiotics and microbiota-derived metabolites in pure form are distinct experimental therapies and need to be assessed independently. This article reviews the gut kidney axis at different levels of evidence and distinguishes preclinical mechanisms, human associations, surrogate biomarker responses, and clinical outcomes. It points out why impressive mechanistic and biomarker results have not translated into better kidney or cardiovascular outcomes. Future research should use standardized methodologies, provide more detail on microbial functions and host metabolite metabolism, and test microbiome-targeted therapies in sufficiently powered randomized controlled trials with meaningful endpoints.

Title: The Association of Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Disease Indices with Pro-Oxidant and Antioxidant Markers in CKD.
Abstract: Oxidative stress (OS) is highly prevalent in chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its clinical significance and association with cardiovascular disease (CVD) has not been yet clearly demonstrated. In this cohort study, 477 adults with CKD at various stages and 20 healthy controls were enrolled. In all participants, an extensive panel of OS biomarkers was measured. Malondialdehyde (MDA) was correlated with glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and carotid intima media thickness (cIMT) (p = 0.008 and p = 0.024, respectively, according to Spearman's rho). Advanced oxidation protein products (AOPPs) were correlated with the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (uPCR), parathormone (PTH) and eGFR (p = 0.048, p = 0.025 and p = 0.045 respectively, according to Spearman's rho) and oxidized albumin (oxALB) was correlated with PTH (p = 0.032) and pulse wave velocity (PWV) (p = 0.017). The antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase (SOD) was correlated with PWV (p = 0.042), urea (p < 0.001), uPCR (p = 0.024), and eGFR (p < 0.001). Meanwhile, catalase (CAT) was correlated with eGFR (p = 0.029) and indices of central pressure. Xanthine oxidase (XO) was correlated with the duration of CVD and PWV. Multivariate analysis showed that kidney function and/or arterial stiffness and CVD were independent predictors of all OS markers.

Title: Erythrocyte Glutathione Shows a Larger Case-Control Difference than Serum Thiol-Disulfide Homeostasis at Emergency Department Presentation with Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Clinical redox studies usually sample a single compartment. In a single-centre, cross-sectional case-control study, we measured serum thiol-disulfide homeostasis, a bulk extracellular thiol measure, and erythrocyte glutathione, an intracellular measure, in the same blood draw from 82 patients presenting to an emergency department with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction and 75 controls. Cases and controls differed substantially in sex and in cardiovascular risk profile. All nine redox indices differed between groups in the direction consistent with greater oxidation in patients. The standardized case-control difference was larger for erythrocyte reduced glutathione (Hedges g 1.14) than for serum native thiol (0.56). The post hoc bootstrap ratio of the two was 2.04 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.31 to 4.08) before adjustment and 1.60 (0.99 to 3.23) after adjustment for age, sex and smoking, and no asymmetry was seen in the small subgroup free of recorded risk factors. In exploratory analyses within patients, serum indices were associated with the Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score and reduced glutathione with ejection fraction. Each assay reports its own pool and is not a global measure of oxidative stress. In this sample, the compartment chosen determined the size of the observed case-control difference, a result that needs confirmation in a design with comparable groups.

Title: Circulating ELAFIN Is Associated with a Distinct Renal-Inflammatory Phenotype in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: ELAFIN (peptidase inhibitor 3, PI3) is an endogenous inhibitor of neutrophil elastase and proteinase 3, but its circulating profile in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and cardiovascular disease remains poorly characterized. We investigated circulating ELAFIN in patients undergoing elective coronary angiography and explored its associations with metabolic, inflammatory, renal, cardiac, and angiographic phenotypes.
METHODS: Forty-three consecutive clinically stable patients undergoing elective coronary angiography, including nine with T2DM, were prospectively enrolled. Plasma ELAFIN was quantified by ELISA. Associations with clinical and laboratory variables were assessed using non-parametric comparisons, correlation analyses, and parsimonious multivariable regression. Discrimination analyses were considered exploratory.
RESULTS: Median ELAFIN was 5.03-fold higher in patients with T2DM than in those without T2DM (31.2 [28.3-36.2] vs. 6.2 [5.5-7.0] ng/mL; p < 0.001; Cliff's δ = 0.85). The association remained pronounced after adjustment for age, sex, and renal function. ELAFIN was positively correlated with REG3A and creatinine, and inversely correlated with eGFR, whereas no significant associations were observed with angiographic coronary stenosis, LVEF, or NT-proBNP.
CONCLUSIONS: Circulating ELAFIN was markedly elevated in T2DM and associated predominantly with renal and inflammatory characteristics rather than anatomical coronary disease or left ventricular dysfunction. Because oxidative stress and protease activity were not directly measured, their relationship with ELAFIN remains hypothesis-generating. These findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

Title: Exogenous ATP Attenuates Biochemical and Histological Markers of Osimertinib-Associated Myocardial Injury in Rats.
Abstract: (1) Background: Osimertinib is an effective third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor, but its clinical use may be limited by cardiotoxicity. This study investigated the relationship between reduced measured cardiac ATP levels and osimertinib-associated cardiac injury and examined whether exogenous ATP administration attenuates the associated biochemical and histopathological alterations. (2) Methods: Twenty-four male Wistar rats were randomly allocated to healthy control (HG), osimertinib (OSM), ATP 5 mg/kg + osimertinib (AOSM-5), and ATP 10 mg/kg + osimertinib (AOSM-10) groups (n = 6). ATP was administered intraperitoneally once daily, followed 1 h later by osimertinib (50 mg/kg, oral gavage) for three weeks. Cardiac tissue ATP, MDA, and tGSH levels, SOD and CAT activities, and plasma TPI levels were measured, together with histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation of COX-1, COX-2, and 8-OHdG. (3) Results: Osimertinib significantly decreased ATP and tGSH levels and SOD and CAT activities, and increased MDA and TPI levels (p < 0.001), accompanied by increased COX-2 and 8-OHdG, reduced COX-1, hemorrhage, and mononuclear cell infiltration. Exogenous ATP attenuated these alterations, with generally greater effects observed at 10 mg/kg. (4) Conclusions: These findings indicate that ATP co-administration attenuated biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical alterations associated with osimertinib-induced myocardial injury in rats, with these effects being associated, at least in part, with reduced oxidative stress. However, the functional cardiac effects, underlying mechanisms, and potential influence of ATP administration on the antitumor efficacy of osimertinib require further investigation.

Title: Mesenchymal Stromal Cells for Heart Diseases: Current Perspective and Future Directions.
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide and continue to impose a substantial clinical burden despite major advances in pharmacological and interventional therapies. Because the adult myocardium has limited regenerative capacity, irreversible cardiomyocyte loss frequently leads to adverse remodeling and progressive heart failure (HF). Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are among the most extensively studied cell therapies for cardiac repair because of their immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic effects, mediated predominantly through paracrine signaling. This review summarizes the current evidence for MSC-based therapy in ischemic heart disease (IHD), coronary and microvascular disorders, myocardial infarction, HF, myocarditis, pulmonary arterial hypertension, and valvular heart disease (VHD). We discuss MSC sources, preclinical and clinical evidence, manufacturing and dosing, delivery routes, biomaterial-assisted transplantation, preconditioning, genetic modification, and imaging for cell tracking and treatment monitoring. Although MSC therapy has shown a favorable safety profile and regenerative potential, clinical efficacy remains variable because of limited cell survival, poor myocardial retention, and heterogeneous treatment protocols. Further optimization of manufacturing, delivery, and patient selection, together with well-designed randomized trials, is required to establish standardized protocols and support clinical translation.

Title: An Exploratory Randomized Clinical Trial to Assess the Effects of Vitamin D and Leucine-Enriched Whey Protein Supplementation on Inflammaging and Gut Eubacterial Biomass in Cardiac Rehabilitation Patients.
Abstract: Whey protein (WP) supplementation could affect low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) and gut microbiome dysbiosis, both of which play key roles in non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Twenty-seven cardiac rehabilitation patients were randomly allocated to two groups: the case group (CA) (n = 14) received 80 g/die vitamin D and leucine-enriched WP supplement, combined with a standard hospital diet, while the control group (CO, n = 13) received the standard hospital diet alone. Blood and stool samples were collected at baseline (T0) and after two weeks (T1). At T1, serum levels of interleukin 6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP) significantly decreased in the CA group. Ferritin levels significantly decreased within both groups and between the two groups. No significant differences were observed for IL-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), or IL-10. A clear difference in the bacterial intestinal microbiome composition between the case group at T1 (CAT1) and at T0 (CAT0), and control group at T0 (COT0) and at T1 (COT1), was observed. The eubacterial rpoB copy number, which was quantified by qPCR, significantly increased between CAT0 and CAT1, in contrast to the Lactobacillus spp. rpoB copy number. Our exploratory results showed that vitamin D and leucine-enriched WP supplementation could have a potential effect on chronic inflammation and gut microbiota composition in cardiac rehabilitation patients.

Title: α-Lipoic Acid, with or Without Ambrisentan, Attenuates Experimental Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Associations with AMPK/mTOR/NF-κB Signaling and Kallistatin.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling driven by excessive cellular proliferation and inflammation. Targeting both vasoconstriction and vascular remodeling represents a key therapeutic strategy. Alpha-lipoic acid (α-LA), a metabolic and anti-inflammatory modulator, is associated with modulation of AMPK/mTOR/NF-κB signaling, whereas ambrisentan (AMB) is an endothelin receptor antagonist with established vasodilatory effects. We investigated the beneficial effects of α-LA and AMB, administered alone or in combination, in a monocrotaline (MCT)-induced PAH rat model.
METHODS: Male rats were randomly assigned to control, MCT, α-LA, AMB, and α-LA + AMB groups. PAH was induced by a single subcutaneous injection of monocrotaline (60 mg/kg). Treatments were administered between days 22 and 35. Echocardiographic measurements were obtained, and histopathological, immunohistochemical, and biochemical analyses were performed in lung and cardiac tissues and in serum. Sample sizes analyzed per outcome were: echocardiography (Control: n = 10, MCT: n = 10, α-LA: n = 8, AMB: n = 9, α-LA + AMB: n = 10), histology (n = 10/group), RVSP (Control: n = 7, MCT: n = 8, α-LA: n = 8, AMB: n = 7, α-LA + AMB: n = 9), Fulton index (Control: n = 10, MCT: n = 10, α-LA: n = 12, AMB: n = 9, α-LA + AMB: n = 10), and ELISA (n = 8/group). Statistical analyses were performed using a web-based statistical software, applying one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test according to data distribution. Results were considered statistically significant at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: MCT administration caused pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular remodeling, evidenced by increased RVSP, Fulton index, medial wall thickness, cardiomyocyte diameter, PCNA, α-SMA, p-mTOR, and NF-κB, together with reduced PAT, TAPSE, kallistatin, and p-AMPK levels. α-LA and AMB monotherapy improved right ventricular function and inflammation. Combination therapy produced hemodynamic and structural improvements relative to MCT that were generally comparable to, rather than significantly greater than, either monotherapy, and showed attenuated antiproliferative effects, with higher cardiomyocyte diameter and PCNA levels than either monotherapy alone. All treatments suppressed mTOR activation and the NF-κB increase, accompanied by increased serum kallistatin levels, whereas a significant increase in p-AMPK relative to MCT was observed only with AMB monotherapy.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that α-LA exerts antiproliferative, anti-remodeling, and anti-inflammatory effects in experimental PAH, suggesting that the AMPK/mTOR/NF-κB signaling pathway and kallistatin may be potential therapeutic targets in pulmonary vascular disease.

Title: Heart Failure and Risk Assessment in Systemic Autoimmune Disease: Do Inflammation, Autoantibodies and Sex Matter?
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is increasingly recognized as an important cardiovascular complication of systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), which include rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, Sjögren's syndrome, and idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. Excess HF risk is only partly explained by conventional cardiovascular risk factors and ischemic heart disease. Chronic inflammation, endothelial and coronary microvascular dysfunction, immune-mediated myocardial injury, oxidative stress, fibrosis, and selected autoantibody-associated pathways may contribute to progressive myocardial dysfunction. Biological sex is also relevant because most SARDs predominantly affect women and sex influences immune regulation, vascular biology, myocardial remodeling, and HF phenotype. Current cardiovascular risk scores are primarily designed for atherosclerotic events and incompletely capture autoimmune disease-specific determinants of myocardial injury. This review summarizes HF across major SARDs and examines three interconnected modifiers of myocardial vulnerability-chronic inflammation, autoantibodies, and biological sex. We further discuss how disease activity and duration, biomarkers, global longitudinal strain, cardiovascular magnetic resonance, and conventional risk factors might be integrated into future risk assessment. A biology-centered approach may enable earlier recognition of subclinical myocardial involvement and individualized cardiovascular surveillance, but prospective validation is required before disease-specific HF-screening strategies can be recommended.

Title: Biochemical Endocrine and Skeletal Findings in Adults with Fabry Disease: A Descriptive Single-Center Study.
Abstract: Background: Endocrine and skeletal findings have previously been reported in Fabry disease (FD), but their interpretation alongside Fabry-specific biochemical markers and multiorgan disease burden remains uncertain. This study descriptively characterized biochemical endocrine findings, vitamin D status, and age-appropriate DXA measurements in adults with FD receiving enzyme replacement therapy (ERT). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study screened 29 patients evaluated between January 2020 and December 2025, of whom 21 adults with genetically and/or enzymatically confirmed FD were included. Biochemical thyroid findings and HbA1c-defined dysglycemia were summarized separately as descriptive measures; no prespecified primary endpoint, composite endocrine outcome, or confirmatory outcome hierarchy was defined. A post hoc exploratory comparison was performed between patients with HbA1c-defined dysglycemia (HbA1c ≥ 5.7%; n = 7) and those without HbA1c-defined dysglycemia (HbA1c < 5.7%; n = 14). Vitamin D status and DXA findings were evaluated using age-, sex-, and menopausal-status-appropriate criteria. Exploratory analyses incorporated effect sizes, bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation tests, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Results: The mean age was 40.7 ± 14.5 years, and nine patients (42.9%) were male. The cohort was genetically concentrated, with c.851T>C (p.M284T) identified in 12/21 patients (57.1%). An elevated-TSH/non-elevated-FT4 biochemical pattern was observed in 2/21 patients (9.5%), and HbA1c-defined dysglycemia in 7/21 (33.3%). Vitamin D concentrations were <20 ng/mL in 16/21 patients (76.2%). DXA data were available for 20 patients. Among four postmenopausal women and four men aged ≥50 years, 5/8 (62.5%) had a minimum T-score within the osteoporosis range. Among seven premenopausal women and five men aged <50 years, 7/12 (58.3%) had a minimum Z-score ≤ -2.0, indicating BMD below the expected range for age. None of the 14 post hoc subgroup comparisons or 48 exploratory correlations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Conclusions: Thyroid, glycemic, vitamin D, and age-appropriate DXA measurements were descriptively characterized in this small, ERT-treated FD cohort. In the absence of an age-, sex-, and clinically matched comparator, the observed distributions cannot be interpreted as abnormalities attributable specifically to FD or as occurring more frequently than in an appropriate reference population. Moreover, no subgroup comparison or correlation remained significant after multiplicity correction. The data therefore do not demonstrate independent endocrine or skeletal relationships with Fabry disease burden and should be considered cohort-specific, descriptive, and hypothesis-generating.

Title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants in the Cardiorenal Patient: Pharmacology, Kidney Function Estimation and Dose Selection Across the CKD Spectrum.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are not two coincident diseases but two expressions of the cardiorenal syndrome, the disorder in which dysfunction of the heart or the kidney induces dysfunction of the other. Their coexistence spans the chronic renocardiac and cardiorenal subtypes of that syndrome, and fits neither cleanly: the relationship is genuinely bidirectional, and each organ accelerates the deterioration of the other. Anticoagulation sits precisely at the point where this bidirectional relationship becomes a therapeutic dilemma: the same patient is simultaneously hypercoagulable and haemorrhagically fragile, and the drug intended to protect the brain is cleared by an organ whose function is both impaired and unstable. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have redefined therapeutic standards in AF and venous thromboembolism (VTE), offering predictable pharmacokinetics, fewer food and drug interactions and reduced monitoring requirements compared with vitamin K antagonists (VKAs). In the cardiorenal patient, however, these advantages are conditional. Renal elimination varies more than three-fold across the class-from approximately 27% for apixaban to approximately 80% for dabigatran-so that the choice of molecule, and not merely the decision to anticoagulate, becomes a kidney-related decision. The cardiorenal argument in favour of DOACs extends beyond bleeding: VKAs promote vascular calcification through inhibition of matrix Gla protein, are associated with calciphylaxis, and can cause anticoagulant-related nephropathy, an under-recognised cause of accelerated loss of glomerular filtration rate (GFR). Randomised and observational data indicate that GFR declines faster on VKAs than on DOACs, making the kidney an outcome of anticoagulation and not only a route of elimination. A second, largely unresolved problem is metrological rather than pharmacological. Dose thresholds for DOACs were derived from creatinine clearance (CrCl) estimated with the Cockcroft-Gault (CG) equation, whereas contemporary nephrology stages kidney disease with estimated GFR (eGFR) from the CKD-EPI or EKFC equations. The two quantities are not interchangeable, and the discordance between them translates directly into discordant doses in 4-34% of patients depending on the agent, with the largest discrepancies in the oldest patients and in those with the lowest measured function. This review reframes DOAC therapy as a cardiorenal problem. We examine the shared pathophysiological substrate of AF and CKD, the pharmacology of each agent through the lens of renal handling, the evidence across CKD stages G1-G5D including dialysis, the kidney as an outcome rather than only a covariate of anticoagulation, and the clinical consequences of the equation used to estimate kidney function at the point of prescription.

Title: Metformin, SGLT2 Inhibitors, and Intermittent Fasting: Convergent Pathways to Healthspan Extension, Cardiovascular Longevity, and Cancer Prevention-A Narrative Review.
Abstract: The biology of aging and the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease share a common molecular pathway expressed through nutrient-sensing kinases, mitochondrial redox state, and chronic inflammation. Three interventions have independently emerged as translators of that interconnection into clinical benefit: metformin, a biguanide that has evolved from a first-line anti-diabetic into the world's most extensively studied putative geroprotector; the sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), pharmacological generators of a fasting-mimetic state that has reshaped heart failure outcomes across the ejection-fraction spectrum; and intermittent fasting (IF), the evolutionary archetype from which both agents partially derive their effects on longevity. Based on the synthetized evidence, we propose a stage-stratified clinical framework for integrated deployment. To find the manuscripts relevant for our narrative review, we searched the medical literature by using key words ("metformin"; "SGLT2i"; "intermittent fasting"; "health span"; "cardiovascular longevity"; "cancer chemoprevention"; "gut microbiome"; "geroprotection"; "heart failure") combined through Boolean operators (AND/OR). This narrative review integrates preclinical mechanistic evidence, landmark randomized controlled trial data, and emerging data on cancer chemoprevention and gut microbiome remodeling to provide a rigorous, side-by-side analysis of all three strategies. We delineate molecular convergence on adenosine monophosphate kinase (AMPK) activation, mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) suppression, enhanced autophagy, mitochondrial renewal, inflammatory responses, and anti-cancer biology, while mapping critical divergences in specific populations, lifespan timing, combinability, and safety. Our proposed framework has to be treated with caution, as it is based on the current evidence base, which lacks dedicated outcome trials for IF and published randomized clinical trial data for metformin in non-diabetic adults.

Title: Integrative Multi-Omics Reveal the Molecular Architecture and Systemic Burden of Metabolic Syndrome in a Brazilian Cohort.
Abstract: Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) includes a complex cluster of metabolic disorders that significantly increases the risk for cardiovascular disease and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular architecture and systemic burden of MetS by integrating high-resolution plasma proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. A cohort of 60 adult volunteers (n = 37 controls; n = 23 MetS) from Brazil was subjected to comprehensive clinical evaluation and multi-omics profiling. Clinical analysis identified HOMA-IR and triglycerides as primary predictors of MetS. FDR was used for multiple testing correction for all data. Untargeted proteomics identified 589 proteins, with 26 showing significant differential abundance, including the upregulated Intercellular Adhesion Molecule-1 (ICAM-1) and Vanin-1 and the depleted protective Apolipoprotein D (ApoD) in MetS. Metabolomic analysis resulted in the identification of 410 metabolites, with 27 distinct features, revealing accumulation of branched-chain and aromatic amino acids, alongside a significant reduction in the signaling molecule 3-hydroxybutyrate, in the case group. Lipidomic profiling identified 1241 lipids, with 41 differentially abundant, highlighting the increase in Phosphatidylinositol (PI 40:5) and Phosphatidylcholine (PC) classes and the depletion of Sphingomyelins (SM). Integrative analysis demonstrated that MetS comprises a synchronized and multisystemic molecular disruption rather than a collection of independent risk factors. The homeostatic breakdown is characterized by the depletion of the body's antioxidant and anti-inflammatory defense, and the elevation of pro-inflammatory mediators like ICAM-1 and Vanin-1, the accumulation of lipotoxic drivers and a significant disruption in amino acid catabolism (BCAA) that overactivates the mTORC1 pathway. These findings provide a multifactorial metabolic dysregulation, offering putative signatures for future diagnoses and risk stratification.

Title: Beyond Hemorrhagic Fever: Hepatic and Endothelial Dysfunction in Ebola Virus Disease.
Abstract: Background: Ebola virus disease (EVD), caused by Ebola virus (Orthoebolavirus zairense), is one of the most lethal viral infections, with case fatality rates historically exceeding 80% in several outbreaks. Once classified as a viral hemorrhagic fever, EVD is now regarded as a systemic disorder with immune dysregulation, endothelial injury, metabolic impairment, and multiorgan dysfunction, in which hepatic involvement has been underappreciated. Objective: To synthesize the evidence on hepatic involvement in EVD (mechanisms of injury, clinical spectrum, prognostic significance, therapeutic implications, and long-term consequences in survivors) and to appraise its strength. Methods: Narrative review based on a structured, non-systematic PubMed search, with the search strategy reported in full and SANRA used as a reporting guide. Results: Hepatocytes and Kupffer cells are early targets of infection in human autopsy and animal studies. Hepatic injury reflects direct viral effects, macrophage activation, cytokine release, endothelial activation and barrier dysfunction, coagulopathy, and hypoperfusion, with mechanistic evidence largely derived from experimental models. Aminotransferase elevation, particularly of AST, is associated with severity and mortality but is not specific for liver injury (muscle injury, hemolysis, ischemia, and drugs also contribute). Monoclonal antibodies improve survival in disease caused by Ebola virus, whereas no approved specific therapy exists for Sudan or Bundibugyo virus disease. Subclinical hepatic and platelet abnormalities have been reported in survivors, but evidence for chronic liver disease is lacking. Conclusions: Hepatic dysfunction is an important, prognostically relevant component of EVD pathophysiology, interlinked with inflammatory and endothelial pathways. Whether it acts as a direct driver of disease progression, rather than a marker of systemic severity, remains to be established; prospective studies with systematic hepatological assessment are needed.

Title: Intraoperative Measurement of Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow Using Transit-Time Flowmetry After Carotid Endarterectomy: Results from 196 Consecutive Cases.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is a standard surgical treatment for high-grade symptomatic and asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis. The Transit Time Flowmeter (TTF) provides an easy-to-use tool to quantify intraoperative ICA blood flow in mL/min. This study aimed to (1) describe post-CEA ICA flow quantified with TTF, (2) identify predictors of post-CEA ICA flow, and (3) examine its association with contralateral steno-occlusive disease. Methods: We queried data from our prospective registry of patients who underwent a CEA between January 2019 and July 2024 and had intraoperative registered post-CEA ICA flow measurements using TTF. Preoperative ICA stenosis was graded according to the NASCET criteria. The clinical data was retrospectively collected. Results: Data from 196 CEAs in 190 patients (median age 74 [67-81]; 25% female) were included. Most patients (86%) had a symptomatic ICA stenosis. The median post-CEA ICA flow was 170 mL/min [IQR 140-242; range 40-800]. Post-CEA ICA flow was not associated with age, sex, comorbidities, symptomatic stenosis, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), or ipsilateral stenosis severity but was significantly higher in patients requiring intraluminal shunt placement during CEA (p = 0.010) as well as in those with contralateral steno-occlusive disease (p < 0.001). Conclusions: TTF is a practical intraoperative tool for quantitative flow assessment during CEA. Higher post-CEA ICA flow in patients with an intraoperative shunt placement or with contralateral steno-occlusive disease may reflect a compensatory hyperperfusion, as the ipsilateral ICA serves as a key supplier when collateral pathways are incomplete.

Title: Systemic Inflammatory Markers in Parkinson's Disease: Correlations with Disease Severity and Neuropsychiatric Symptoms.
Abstract: Objective: Chronic neuroinflammation is a recognized driver of Parkinson's disease (PD) pathophysiology, in which systemic inflammation may also participate. This study evaluated composite inflammatory indices in peripheral blood and investigated their associations with disease severity, motor symptoms, and non-motor symptoms. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted using routinely collected clinical and laboratory data. A total of 315 PD patients and 125 healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled. All PD patients underwent motor and non-motor symptom assessments. Differences in peripheral inflammatory indices were compared between the PD and HC groups, and across Hoehn-Yahr (H-Y) stages. Multinomial logistic regression was used for factors associated with disease severity. Multivariable linear regression examined correlations with clinical measures. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to PD vs. HC comparisons, H-Y group comparisons, and all symptom-related analyses. Results: Levels of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) were significantly elevated in PD after FDR correction. In the multinomial logistic regression model, disease duration was significantly associated with both H-Y < 3 vs. H-Y > 3 (OR = 0.940, 95% CI: 0.894, 0.989; p = 0.016) and H-Y = 3 vs. H-Y > 3 (OR = 0.961, 95% CI: 0.925, 0.999; p = 0.043). Hypertension was associated only with H-Y < 3 vs. H-Y > 3 (OR = 0.468, 95% CI: 0.226, 0.970; p = 0.041). Platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) was significantly associated with H-Y = 3 vs. H-Y > 3 (OR = 0.989, 95% CI: 0.980, 0.997; p = 0.012) but not with H-Y < 3 vs. H-Y > 3 (p = 0.167). Systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) was not significantly associated with either comparison. SII × sex (p = 0.496) and PLR × sex (p = 0.048, Bonferroni-corrected p > 0.025) interaction terms were not significant. After FDR correction, no inflammatory indices were significantly associated with motor or non-motor symptom (all q > 0.05). Conclusions: After rigorous adjustment, previously reported associations between peripheral inflammatory indices and PD severity were not replicated. Disease duration and hypertension were the primary correlates of higher H-Y staging. Elevated inflammatory indices should be interpreted with caution, as they may be associated with longer disease duration or vascular comorbidity.

Title: Acute Cervical Carotid Management During Thrombectomy for Tandem Occlusion: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The optimal cervical carotid strategy during thrombectomy for anterior-circulation tandem occlusion remains uncertain. We compared emergent carotid stenting, balloon angioplasty alone, and no targeted acute cervical revascularization.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Ovid Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus for comparative studies published from January 2015 to 25 August 2026. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with outcome-specific cohort-overlap auditing. The event-count network was exploratory; adjusted evidence was analyzed separately. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I-aligned domains; confidence was assessed with CINeMA. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261494924.
RESULTS: The review included 60 reports representing 49 cohort or report families. Fifteen cohorts contributed 1556 patients for functional independence and 15 contributed 1676 for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). Stenting was associated with greater 90-day functional independence than angioplasty alone (OR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.22-2.45), without a detected difference in sICH (OR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.60-1.67). All leave-one-cohort-out functional estimates remained above 1, with 95% CIs excluding 1. Evidence was predominantly nonrandomized.
CONCLUSIONS: Emergent carotid stenting was associated with greater 90-day functional independence than balloon angioplasty alone, with no detected difference in sICH. Serious or critical risk of bias in all studies in the strict network limits causal interpretation. Imprecision and heterogeneous antiplatelet protocols preclude establishing noninferiority or excluding increased hemorrhagic risk.

Title: Dynamic Evolution of Quantitative Electroencephalography During Graded Intracranial Hypertension and Screening of Candidate Early-Warning Features in a Rabbit Model.
Abstract: Background and Objectives: Elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) is common to many encephalopathies, but the evolution of quantitative electroencephalography (qEEG) indices along a pressure gradient-and their relative suitability for early warning-have not been systematically compared. In this exploratory study we established a stepwise, steady-state rabbit model of graded intracranial hypertension and screened candidate early-warning features against prespecified criteria. Materials and Methods: Eight male New Zealand rabbits were studied; two were excluded-one for circulatory failure during catheterization and one for refractory status epilepticus that reached a humane endpoint-leaving six that completed the protocol. Repeated small-volume inflation of a left parenchymal water balloon was used to define five windows: baseline (BL; ICP < 10 mmHg), 15-20, 25-30 and 35-40 mmHg, and an end stage (END). Eight-channel EEG was recorded synchronously, and δ, θ, α and β power, together with the amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) upper margin, lower margin and bandwidth, were computed. Seven candidate features and three criteria (evolution timing, individual consistency and strength of association with ICP) were fixed before analysis; selection stability was assessed by leave-one-rabbit-out (LORO) cross-validation. Results: ICP rose in a controlled manner from 5.43 ± 1.09 to 35.93 ± 1.48 mmHg (Kendall W = 0.96), without systematic changes in respiratory mechanics. As ICP increased, absolute θ and α power declined progressively (ρ = -0.77 and -0.53), whereas absolute δ power did not increase and its rising relative share merely reflected redistribution after the loss of faster activity. The three aEEG components changed asynchronously: the lower margin shifted downward early and persistently (ρ = -0.87 with ICP; W = 0.86), whereas the upper margin changed only terminally and bandwidth showed no consistent direction. Concurrently, MAP rose through the Cushing response, with heart-rate slowing, but the rise was insufficient and CPP fell from 64.78 to 41.24 mmHg, approaching the rabbit lower limit of autoregulation (~50 mmHg CPP) only in the later windows. Because ICP and CPP were tightly coupled within animals, their independent effects on the EEG could not be separated. In leave-one-rabbit-out cross-validation, the lower margin was selected in five of six folds, with a median out-of-sample ρ of -1.00 (a discrete value based on four windows per animal). Conclusions: In this exploratory study in a small cohort (n = 6), qEEG indices evolved asynchronously along the ICP gradient; the aEEG lower margin appeared earliest and remained relatively stable across leave-one-rabbit-out folds, making it a candidate early-warning feature worthy of priority validation. However, because rising ICP and falling CPP were tightly coupled and could not be separated in this model, its early decline cannot be uniquely attributed to either ICP elevation or hypoperfusion. Its alarm threshold and early-warning value still require confirmation in larger independent cohorts with simultaneous CPP and cerebral blood flow monitoring.

Title: The Effect of Different Auditory Conditions on Pattern-Reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (PVEPs) in Healthy Adults.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of different auditory conditions on pattern-reversal visual evoked potential (PVEP) responses among healthy adults. Methods: This repeated-measure design with a fixed baseline and randomized order of the two auditory conditions was conducted at the Retina Clinic, Ophthalmology Department, Tertiary Hospital in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Healthy adults with no systemic or ocular diseases aged 20-60 years were included. All participants underwent comprehensive visual and ocular assessment, including best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), slit-lamp examination, optical coherence tomography (OCT), screening audiometry, and a PVEP test conducted under three auditory conditions: silence, Quran recitation, and music exposure. P100 latency and amplitude were recorded using 1° and 0.25° stimulation sizes. Statistical analysis was performed using non-parametric statistics. A p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Significant differences in PVEP amplitude responses were observed across auditory conditions, particularly at the 1° stimulation size. The Friedman test demonstrated significant amplitude differences at the 1° stimulation size (χ2 = 16.379, p < 0.001), with silence producing adjusted significantly higher amplitudes compared with Quran recitation and music exposure (p = 0.001 and p = 0.003), respectively. Significant positive correlations were identified between BCVA and P100 amplitude at Quran exposure (r = 0.178, p < 0.05) only at the 0.25° stimulation size. Conclusions: The stimulus size can be sensitive in revealing auditory-related changes in different retinal areas of functional visual pathway alterations. In comparison to baseline (silence), which generally produces the highest amplitudes, both auditory conditions (Quran recitation and music) were associated with lower P100 amplitude, while no significant difference was observed between Quran recitation and music.

Title: Microsurgical Outcomes of Third-Ventricle Colloid Cysts Treated via an Interhemispheric Transcallosal Approach: A Single-Center Retrospective Series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Third-ventricle colloid cysts are benign but can cause obstructive hydrocephalus and sudden deterioration, and the role of microsurgical transcallosal resection in the endoscopic era remains debated. We evaluated clinical, radiological, and functional outcomes of microscope-assisted interhemispheric transcallosal resection and the effect of preoperative hydrocephalus on recovery.
METHODS: This retrospective, observational, single-center study analyzed 30 patients with symptomatic, histopathologically confirmed colloid cysts operated on between June 2015 and February 2021, divided into hydrocephalus (n = 16) and non-hydrocephalus (n = 14) groups. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) scale.
RESULTS: Mean KPS improved from 65.3 ± 21.0 to 92.0 ± 11.0 (p < 0.001). Patients with hydrocephalus had lower preoperative Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS; p = 0.022) and KPS (p = 0.048) scores, comparable postoperative KPS (p = 0.208), and greater KPS improvement (p = 0.012). Four patients (13.3%) needed external ventricular drainage; none required a permanent shunt. Four patients (13.3%) developed new persistent neurological events (seizures, n = 3; memory impairment, n = 1). No recurrence occurred over a median follow-up of 7.0 years.
CONCLUSIONS: Microscope-assisted interhemispheric transcallosal microsurgical resection was associated with significant KPS improvement, no permanent shunt requirement, and no recurrence. Despite the increasing use of endoscopic techniques, microsurgical approaches remain valuable due to direct visualization, bimanual dissection, and the potential for durable gross-total resection; however, neurocognitive outcomes were not assessed, and prospective studies are needed.

Title: Preoperative Antithrombotic Exposure and Postoperative Outcomes Following Nontraumatic Subdural Hematoma Evacuation: A Multicenter Electronic Health Record Analysis with Single-Center Context.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Preoperative antithrombotic therapy is common among patients undergoing subdural hematoma (SDH) evacuation. However, the association with postoperative outcomes remains uncertain. We evaluated this potential association using a multicenter electronic health record cohort and a single-center cohort. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using TriNetX, a multicenter electronic health record (EHR) database, and a single-center cohort. TriNetX was used to identify adults undergoing evacuation of nontraumatic subdural hematoma between 2005 and 2025. The exposed cohort was defined as documented oral anticoagulant or antiplatelet exposure within 7 days before surgery, after which patients were propensity-score matched 1:1. The single-center cohort included surgically treated subdural hematoma patients with clinical, radiographic, laboratory, and operative data. Postoperative outcomes included 30-day mortality, short-term thrombotic complications, and 90-day repeat subdural hematoma surgery. Results: In TriNetX, 15,651 eligible patients were identified. Matched cohorts included 1455 exposed and 1455 unexposed patients. Preoperative antithrombotic exposure was associated with higher 90-day repeat surgery (9.7% vs. 6.5%; hazard ratio [HR] 1.52; p = 0.001), whereas 30-day mortality and 14-day thrombotic complications did not differ significantly. The single-center cohort included 164 surgically treated patients, including 103 exposed and 61 unexposed patients. The reoperation association was not reproduced. However, exposed patients had higher unadjusted 30-day and overall mortality that attenuated after multivariable Cox adjustment. Conclusions: Preoperative antithrombotic exposure was associated with repeat surgery in the TriNetX cohort but not in the single-center cohort. Together, these findings suggest that antithrombotic exposure may identify a medically complex surgical SDH population requiring individualized postoperative surveillance.

Title: Multispectral PPG Sensing Framework for Noninvasive Glucose Prediction via Multi-Feature Fusion and Micro-Environmental Compensation.
Abstract: Noninvasive blood glucose prediction using near-infrared spectroscopy remains challenging due to weak glucose-specific absorption, tissue variability, and environmental interference. This study proposes a multispectral photoplethysmography (PPG)-based framework integrating multi-feature fusion, local temperature and humidity compensation, and machine learning regression. The system employs four near-infrared wavelengths (940, 1300, 1550, and 1650 nm) while simultaneously measuring finger contact-site temperature (T) and local relative humidity (H) within the finger clip. A 39-dimensional feature set incorporating optical ratios, pulse-wave morphology, frequency-domain descriptors, participant characteristics, and environmental parameters was constructed. Among six optimized regression models, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) achieved the best performance in group-isolated 10-fold cross-validation, with R2 = 0.9135, root mean square error (RMSE) = 0.2991, and mean absolute relative difference (MARD) = 2.71%. Clarke error grid analysis (CEGA) showed that 97% of predictions fell within zone A and 100% within zones A and B. Feature ablation demonstrated that local temperature and humidity measurements improved prediction accuracy, with humidity providing a greater improvement than temperature. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified the contributions of optical, environmental, and participant-level features. A separate session-holdout evaluation yielded R2 = 0.7261 and MARD = 6.07%. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed framework for noninvasive glucose prediction. However, the small, predominantly healthy cohort and limited glucose range constrain generalizability, necessitating validation in larger, more diverse populations to establish performance in previously unseen participants and assess clinical applicability.

Title: Multimodal Prodromal Patterns Associated with COPD Exacerbations in Home Telemonitoring: An Exploratory Observational Study.
Abstract: Characterizing multi-parameter physiological, acoustic, and environmental changes before acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations (AECOPD) is crucial for improving home telemonitoring and enabling timely clinical intervention. In a 12-month prospective observational exploratory pilot study (N=16), a multimodal Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem collected daily data on symptoms, lung function, cardiorespiratory dynamics, actigraphy, sleep, fine motor skills, bioacoustics, and indoor air quality. From 427 daily features across 4738 patient-days, collinearity mitigation retained 245 independent features. Linear mixed-effects models (LMM), nonparametric paired tests, and multi-timescale exponential moving average smoothing quantified prodromal trajectories and univariate discrimination during the 7-day pre-exacerbation window. Engagement analysis showed a dual hierarchy: passive background monitoring had high retention (>72 %), while demanding active tasks like peak flow spirometry dropped to 26.9 % compliance. Patients with frequent exacerbations showed higher reactive adherence. LMM frameworks identified a multisystem prodromal footprint marked by coordinated increases in cough frequency, sputum purulence, dyspnea, and resting heart rate. Acoustic measures showed notable pre-event changes in higher-order speech cepstral coefficients, voice-intensity variability, and cough spectral dispersion, providing objective proxies for airway limitation. Indoor environmental signals suggested domestic confinement but weakened after adjustment for macro-seasonal confounders. Multi-temporal kinetics demonstrated that acute physiological symptoms peaked within 72 h, whereas acoustic features required 3-to-7-day temporal smoothing (EMA3-EMA7) to optimize signal-to-noise ratios. In conclusion, these preliminary observations in the exploratory small cohort suggest that the transition from a stable baseline to the prodromal AECOPD phase is marked by a quantifiable, multi-systemic digital footprint across cardiorespiratory, bioacoustic, and symptom domains. Although requiring validation in broader populations, findings highlight the potential of multi-tiered digital health architectures that pair continuous passive sensing with low-friction active reporting to overcome task attrition and secure the uninterrupted longitudinal baselines needed for automated early-warning systems.

Title: A Fast and Generalizable Deep Neural Network for the Detection of Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AFib) is the most prevalent sustained cardiac arrhythmia, yet most deep learning detectors are validated on a single cohort and few report uncertainty. We developed a compact 14M-parameter convolutional neural network for binary AFib classification from 10 s, 12-lead ECG at 500 Hz, trained exclusively on the HDXML dataset (67,432 ECGs; 9628 AFib) with on-the-fly augmentation for noise, drift and missing channels. Using one unchanged checkpoint, we evaluated six independently sourced public cohorts totaling over 1.25 million recordings, including MIMIC-IV critical care and two ambulatory Holter cohorts. All metrics are reported with 95% confidence intervals from a cluster bootstrap at the patient, recording or subject levels. ROC-AUC exceeded 0.95 in every cohort, from 0.960 (95% CI 0.956-0.963) on CODE-15 to 0.999 (0.998-0.999) on SPH, including 0.966 (0.965-0.967) on MIMIC-IV with 75.3% sensitivity and 97.7% specificity, 0.963 (0.929-0.987) on CPSC 2021 and 0.995 (0.988-0.999) on MIT-BIH. Performance was stable under progressive lead masking without retraining, and median inference took 110 ms per segment on a server-class CPU without a GPU. A compact network trained on one curated source can therefore generalize across hospitals, countries and recording hardware. This study is retrospective; prospective validation is required before clinical use.

Title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence for Estimating Trabecular-Iris Angle from Slit-Lamp Images Developed Using Anterior-Segment Optical Coherence Tomography.
Abstract: Background: Narrowing of the trabecular-iris angle (TIA) is a key anatomical feature of primary angle-closure disease and contributes to impaired aqueous humor outflow; however, conventional angle assessment requires specialized expertise or costly imaging equipment. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence model for quantitative TIA estimation from anterior-segment images acquired with a smartphone-attached slit-lamp microscope. Methods: In this retrospective study, 127,512 candidate frames were extracted from anterior-segment videos obtained from 2654 eyes. After automated diagnosability filtering, 59,412 frames suitable for TIA500 estimation were retained and assigned to the training, validation, and test datasets using patient-level grouping. A ResNet50-based model was trained to estimate inferior, nasal, and temporal TIA500 values using the corresponding measurements obtained by anterior-segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) as the ground-truth reference. Model performance was evaluated by comparing the AI-predicted values with the AS-OCT measurements using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), Spearman's rank correlation coefficient, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: Per-eye MAEs were 7.01° ± 5.69°, 7.28° ± 5.80°, and 7.90° ± 6.37° for inferior, nasal, and temporal TIA, respectively. Corresponding correlations with reference measurements were 0.683, 0.696, and 0.646, while ICCs were 0.769, 0.764, and 0.743 (all p < 0.001). Conclusions: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of estimating TIA500 from smartphone-based slit-lamp images. However, the moderate correlations with AS-OCT measurements indicate that the present model is not yet sufficiently accurate for independent clinical diagnosis or screening, and further model improvement and external validation are required.

Title: An Interpretable Multimodal Machine-Learning Model for Predicting Cognitive Impairment from Routine MRI: A Study with External Validation.
Abstract: Existing MRI-based prediction models for cognitive impairment often rely on a single biomarker or simply compare algorithms, act as black boxes, and lack external validation, which limits their clinical translation. We developed and externally validated an interpretable multimodal machine-learning model that classifies a MoCA-defined screening outcome as a binary task: cognitive impairment (CI, MoCA < 26) versus no cognitive impairment (NCI, MoCA ≥ 26). Sixteen candidate features were considered, including AI-derived medial temporal atrophy (MTA), regional white matter hyperintensity (WMH) volumes and proportions, and Fazekas ratings from routine T1WI and T2-FLAIR, together with age and sex. In a single-center cohort of 433 subjects (302 CI, 131 NCI) with a 7:3 training/hold-out split, five algorithms were compared and Random Forest performed best; SHAP-guided recursive feature elimination within five-fold cross-validation then reduced the set from 16 to 11 features. The optimized 11-feature Random Forest reached a cross-validated AUC of 0.883 ± 0.024 on the training folds and an internal hold-out AUC of 0.966, and 0.860 in an independent ADNI cohort of 139 subjects (100 CI, 39 NCI). SHAP identified the left MTA score as the most influential feature, followed by near-ventricular (juxtaventricular and periventricular) WMH burden and the right MTA score. The left MTA score was most strongly correlated with MoCA (r = -0.481). The model may offer an objective, routine-MRI-based screening aid, pending prospective multicenter validation.

Title: Clonal Hematopoiesis Across the Cancer Treatment Continuum: A Scoping Review of Clonal Selection, Evolution, and Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) is characterized by the proliferation of blood cell clones that possess acquired genetic modifications. While therapy-related CH refers to CH detected in the setting of prior or current treatment in cancer populations, therapy-selected CH demands demonstration that treatment preferentially expanded or maintained an extant clone; therapy-induced CH requires evidence of de novo treatment-associated mutation supported by serial sampling and mutational-signature analyses.
OBJECTIVE: To map evidence distinguishing therapy-related, therapy-selected and therapy-induced CH across cancer treatment, including clonal dynamics, genomic features, clinical outcomes and surveillance gaps.
METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidance, PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched from inception through 1 June 2026, and updated on 15 September 2026. Primary evidence mapping was limited to original human studies. Reviews and conceptual sources were used only for context or reference tracking and were ineligible for the primary evidence map. Narrative synthesis was employed as critical variation existed in sequencing platforms, variant allele frequency thresholds, timepoints of sampling, filtering strategies, and outcome definitions.
RESULTS: Of 684 records identified, 213 duplicates were removed and 471 records were screened. Across both pathways, 121 full texts were assessed, 87 excluded and 34 primary reports mapped; contextual citations were outside the included set. Contextual references were used for definitions and interpretation and were excluded from the included-report count. Six domains were deductively established and inductively refined during charting: terminology; therapy-associated mechanisms of clonal selection/expansion; genomic architecture; longitudinal clonal dynamics; clinical consequences; and study design and methodological heterogeneity. Treatment-associated selection or expansion of pre-existing TP53 and PPM1D clones was the most consistently reported mechanism of therapy-related CH, while CHEK2 was inconsistently detected. Pediatric cohorts and mutational-signature analyses also supported de novo mutagenesis with therapy in select contexts. Progression to therapy-related myeloid neoplasm was the most consistent outcome across studies; however, cytopenia, CAR-T-therapy-associated toxicity, cardiovascular events and mortality were inconsistently reported.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports a spectrum of mechanisms ranging from selection of pre-existing clones to therapy-induced de novo mutation. Existing literature cannot support universal CH screening recommendations or guide treatment decisions. Prospective serial analyses harmonized on definition, employing sensitive baseline assays with paired germline controls and tumor-contamination checks, are needed to justify clinical implementation and assessment of fixed outcomes.

Title: Outcomes of Combined Hepatectomy and Intraoperative Ablation for Multiple Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Introduction: Radical hepatectomy is the standard curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs). However, extensive resection may be contraindicated in patients with insufficient liver reserve or anatomically complex disease. Although ablation therapy is generally not recommended as a primary curative modality in current guidelines, intraoperative ablation may facilitate parenchymal-sparing, curative-intent treatment in selected high-risk patients. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 118 patients who underwent curative-intent hepatectomy for multiple CRLM. Patients were categorized into hepatectomy-only (Hx) and hepatectomy plus intraoperative ablation (Hx + Abl) groups, and propensity score matching (PSM) generated 29 balanced pairs. Overall survival (OS) and hepatic progression-free survival (HPFS) were compared using a log-rank test. Cox regression identified predictors of OS, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated tumor size associated with local recurrence after ablation. Results: Before PSM, the HX + Abl group showed higher tumor burden and Beppu scores, and demonstrated inferior OS and HPFS. After PSM, oncological outcomes were comparable. Perioperative outcomes, including major complications and post-hepatectomy liver failure (PHLF), were similar. Preoperative chemotherapy was an independent predictor of OS. Among 99 ablated tumors, local recurrence occurred in 12 lesions, and ROC analysis identified tumor size ≤ 15mm as the optimal cutoff predicting local recurrence. Conclusions: In selected high-risk CRLM patients, hepatectomy with intraoperative ablation had no statistically significant difference in OS and HPFS compared with hepatectomy alone without increasing major complications or PHLF.

Title: Occult Malignancy Presenting as Pericardial Effusion: The Diagnostic Contribution of Pericardial Fluid Cytology.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Pericardial effusion may occur in patients with established cancer but may also represent the first manifestation of an occult malignancy. This study evaluated the diagnostic contribution of pericardial fluid cytology and pathological assessment according to previous oncological status, with particular emphasis on previously unrecognized malignancy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational study of patients hospitalized with pericardial disease between January 2021 and December 2025 at a tertiary cardiovascular center. The final cohort comprised 234 clinical episodes in 209 patients. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, procedural, cytological, and histopathological data were analyzed in relation to previous oncological status and malignant pericardial involvement. Results: Pathological assessment was available in 95/234 episodes (40.6%), with neoplastic involvement identified in 21/95 (22.1%). Neoplastic findings occurred in 13/33 (39.4%) evaluable episodes with known malignancy and 8/62 (12.9%) without a previous cancer diagnosis (odds ratio, 4.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.59-12.11; p = 0.004). Conversely, 20/33 (60.6%) evaluable episodes in patients with known cancer showed no neoplastic involvement. In all eight patients without previously known malignancy, pericardial fluid cytology provided the first pathological evidence of cancer; six (75%) had findings suggestive of a pulmonary origin. All presented with large effusions and hemodynamic compromise. Conclusions: Pericardial pathological assessment provides diagnostic information beyond previous oncological status. It can distinguish malignant from non-neoplastic pericardial involvement in patients with established cancer while also revealing occult malignancy when pericardial disease is its first presentation.

Title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for Early Detection of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction: From Multiparametric Tissue Signatures to Clinical Pathways.
Abstract: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) can compromise cardiovascular health and the delivery of anticancer treatment. Echocardiography and cardiac biomarkers remain the first-line surveillance tools; cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) provides complementary assessment of ventricular function and myocardial tissue when findings are inconclusive or additional characterization may change management. This narrative review examines multiparametric CMR across seven anticancer treatment groups and proposes a risk-adapted approach to its clinical use. Cine imaging, T1 and T2 mapping, extracellular volume fraction (ECV), late gadolinium enhancement, and feature-tracking strain provide different, partly overlapping information. Serial interpretation requires attention to local reference ranges, measurement reproducibility, hematocrit, and acquisition and analysis consistency. An absolute ECV increase of at least 3 percentage points is discussed as an observational risk signal, not proof of collagen deposition or a validated treatment threshold. The guideline threshold of a greater than 15% relative decline in global longitudinal strain derives from echocardiography and should not be assumed to apply directly to CMR feature tracking. We distinguish guideline-supported practice, randomized evidence, observational evidence, and mechanistic extrapolation from the authors' proposed surveillance and rechallenge framework. Suspected immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis requires urgent clinical evaluation even when CMR is negative. Prospective trials are needed to establish whether CMR-informed management improves cardiovascular outcomes, treatment completion, or survival.

Title: Radiofrequency Ablation for the Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Just Below the Hepatic Capsule.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: During radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), electrodes are generally inserted into the center of the tumor through the hepatic parenchyma under image guidance, including ultrasound or computed tomography (CT) guidance. However, tumors located just below the hepatic capsule require special puncture techniques. This retrospective study aimed to analyze the efficacy and outcomes of RFA for HCC located just below the subcapsular region of the liver. Methods: A total of 81 patients with 81 subcapsular HCC tumors underwent RFA. Baseline patient characteristics, treatment results, and adverse events were investigated. Factors associated with local recurrence were also examined. Results: Among the 81 patients, 59 (73%) were male, the median age was 74 years (range, 46-93 years), and 68 (84%) were classified as Child-Pugh class A. The median tumor size was 1.5 cm (range, 0.5-3.7 cm), and 56 of 81 tumors (69%) were <2.0 cm in diameter. 53 tumors were located in the right lobe of the liver (65%). Monopolar RFA was performed in 55 patients (68%), and no-touch multi-bipolar RFA was performed in 26 patients (32%). Treatment success was achieved in 75 tumors (93%), with inadequate ablative margins observed in 6 tumors (7%). Of these six tumors, five (83%) were treated with monopolar RFA; however, differences between the RFA devices were not statistically significant (p = 0.368). Local tumor progression (LTP) was observed in 19 patients (24%), with cumulative LTP rates of 13%, 29%, 33%, and 33% at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years, respectively. Multivariate analysis using a COX proportional hazards model identified insufficient ablative margins as a significant factor associated with LTP (hazard ratio, 4.64; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-14.9; p = 0.031). Adverse events occurred in 17 patients (21%), all of whom recovered with conservative treatment. Tumor seeding occurred in only one patient (1%). Conclusions: In the present study, achieving an adequate ablative margin using either monopolar or multi-bipolar RFA systems was associated with a reduced risk of local tumor recurrence in patients with subcapsular HCC.

Title: Incremental Value and Cross-Center Validation of Pretreatment Tri-Modal Ultrasound Deep Learning for Predicting Breast Pathologic Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy: A Multicenter Study.
Abstract: Objective: To evaluate the incremental predictive value of pretreatment tri-modal ultrasound deep learning integrating two-dimensional ultrasound (2DUS), color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI), and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) for predicting breast pathologic complete response (bpCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), and to assess performance stability across independent centers. Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included 1089 patients with primary invasive breast cancer. Center 1 provided the training cohort (n = 572) and internal validation cohort (n = 246), whereas centers 2 (n = 160) and 3 (n = 111) served as independent external validation cohorts. Using pretreatment 2DUS, CDFI, and CEUS within a standardized intratumoral and 10-mm peritumoral framework, single-modality, all three dual-modality combinations, and tri-modal models were developed. The best-performing dual-modality model was identified and locked during training as the primary imaging comparator. A Tri-modal + Clinical model further integrated pretreatment clinical and biomarker variables. Performance was assessed using AUC, Brier score, calibration, decision curve analysis, and ablation experiments. Results: Overall, 383 patients (35.2%) achieved bpCR. CEUS was the strongest single modality, and 2DUS + CEUS was the best-performing dual-modality model. Compared with 2DUS + CEUS, the tri-modal model increased the AUC from 0.895 to 0.919 in the combined external cohort (ΔAUC, +0.023; 95% CI, +0.010 to +0.038; p = 0.001), with corresponding improvements in Brier score (0.124 to 0.105) and F1 score (0.747 to 0.786). The AUC point estimate increased in both external centers, although the 95% CI for the incremental AUC included zero in external validation cohort 2. Despite modest standalone discrimination, CDFI provided measurable incremental information when added to 2DUS + CEUS. Further integration of pretreatment clinical and biomarker variables increased the combined external AUC to 0.935. Reduced-input retraining showed performance decreases after omission of any modality, with the largest reduction after CEUS omission. Conclusions: Pretreatment tri-modal ultrasound deep learning provided incremental predictive value for bpCR beyond the best dual-modality model, with a consistent direction of benefit across two independent external centers. Clinical and biomarker integration provided additional predictive information, supporting further evaluation of this multimodal framework for individualized pretreatment bpCR prediction.

Title: Advances in Interventional Oncology for Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract: Locoregional therapies are used across the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treatment spectrum, including for curative treatment of small tumors, as bridging or downstaging therapy before liver transplant, for treatment of intermediate-stage disease, and as part of combination treatment with systemic therapy in selected patients. This narrative review summarizes recent developments in transarterial radioembolization (TARE), transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and percutaneous ablation techniques and separates established clinical advances from early investigational work. The strongest evidence supports personalized TARE dosimetry and radiation segmentectomy, selective TACE with reassessment before repeat treatment, and image-guided thermal ablation with objective margin assessment. Phase 3 trials of TACE combined with antiangiogenic and immune checkpoint therapy demonstrated improved progression-free survival in selected patients with unresectable, nonmetastatic HCC, although the survival benefit of these combinations so far extends only to progression-free survival, and the best treatment sequence remains to be defined. Histotripsy, pulsed electric-field ablation, electrochemotherapy, cryoablation, high-intensity focused ultrasound, imageable or alternative radioembolic microspheres, new embolic agents, robotics, and artificial intelligence remain at different stages of clinical development. Most supporting data are derived from single-arm studies, retrospective cohort studies, trials in mixed liver-tumor populations, or studies in preclinical models. Treatment selection should account for tumor burden and location, liver function, portal hypertension, vascular invasion, transplant candidacy, available alternatives, local expertise, and patient preferences. Future studies should focus on durable local control, preservation of liver function, quality of life, transplant eligibility, overall survival, and cost.

Title: Baseline D-Dimer Predicts Subsequent Venous Thromboembolism in 23,505 Patients with One of 11 Solid Malignancies: An 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of cancer. The predictive performance of baseline D-dimer and factors influencing its levels among patients with cancer remain unclear. We aimed to identify predictors of subsequent VTE development and evaluate the cancer-specific predictive performance of baseline D-dimer. Methods: This retrospective study included 23,505 patients with any of 11 malignancies who underwent baseline D-dimer measurement at initial diagnosis at Gifu University Hospital between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients with pre-existing VTE were excluded. Predictors were identified using logistic regression analyses. Cancer-specific predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analyses, with optimal cutoff values determined by the Youden index. Factors associated with baseline D-dimer were also assessed. Results: The median follow-up was 45.3 months (30.4-59.1 months), during which VTE occurred in 784 (3.3%) patients. Higher baseline D-dimer levels and distant metastasis were independent predictors of subsequent VTE. Cancer type was significantly associated with VTE overall, and breast cancer was associated with lower odds than esophageal cancer. D-dimer performance varied among cancer types, with optimal cutoff values of 0.55-2.35 μg/mL. Older age and higher platelet counts were independently associated with elevated baseline D-dimer levels, whereas a higher cholesterol level was inversely associated. Conclusions: Baseline D-dimer level is an independent predictor of subsequent VTE in patients with cancer. Its predictive performance and exploratory thresholds vary among cancers, suggesting that cancer type should be considered when interpreting baseline D-dimer levels. External validation is required before these cancer-specific thresholds can be applied clinically.

Title: Historical Baseline Electrocardiogram Ascertainment Prior to Cancer Diagnosis and Cardiovascular Diagnosis Patterns in Cancer Survivors: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among cancer survivors. Contemporary cardio-oncology frameworks emphasize baseline cardiovascular risk assessment before potentially cardiotoxic cancer therapies. Historical real world implementation of baseline electrocardiography (ECG), however, remains incompletely characterized. The objective of this study was to characterize historical baseline ECG ascertainment before cancer diagnosis and examine its association with documented cardiovascular diagnosis patterns in cancer survivors.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 4592 adult cancer survivors within the Froedtert & Medical College of Wisconsin health system from 2000 to 2020. The analytic cohort was derived from a previously established longitudinal cancer survivor resource integrating demographic and cardiovascular clinical data, cancer treatment exposures, multimodality cardiac function ascertainment, and linked clinical, radiation oncology, and cancer registry information. Cardiac function ascertainment from an available cardiovascular imaging modality within three years before cancer diagnosis was one component of the analytic cohort definition. Patients were stratified by ascertainment of a 12-lead ECG within the same pre-diagnostic interval. Cardiovascular diagnoses documented before and after cancer diagnosis were characterized separately. For the newly documented diagnosis analyses, each cardiovascular outcome was evaluated among participants without a prior diagnosis of that same condition before cancer diagnosis. A multivariable logistic regression model evaluated the association between baseline ECG ascertainment and newly documented overall CVD diagnosis (including HF, AFIB, CAD, and stroke) while adjusting for age, sex, race, comorbidity count, and treatment count.
RESULTS: Among 4592 individuals, 3726 (81%) had a baseline ECG. ECG ascertainment was associated with older age and greater pre-existing cardiovascular and cardiometabolic burden. The available follow up distributions were similar between patients without and with baseline ECG ascertainment (748 [Q1 258, Q3 1781] vs. 767 [Q1 219, Q3 1822] days; p > 0.9). In multivariable analysis, baseline ECG ascertainment was associated with lower odds of a newly documented overall CVD diagnosis (OR 0.38, 95% CI 0.31-0.46); this odds ratio represents an association rather than a time-specific risk or protective effect.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline ECGs were commonly ascertainable within this longitudinal cancer survivor cohort and identified groups with different pre-existing cardiovascular burden and subsequent cardiovascular diagnosis patterns. These findings provide a historical benchmark for cardiovascular assessment in cancer care and support prospective patient-level studies integrating ECG findings with clinical and oncologic risk factors to refine cardiovascular surveillance strategies across cancer survivorship.

Title: Long-Term Outcomes of Cryoablation for Solitary De Novo T1a Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Tertiary Cancer Center Experience.
Abstract: Objective: To assess the long-term oncologic and survival outcomes of percutaneous cryoablation (PCA) for patients with solitary de novo T1a renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Methods: This retrospective study was conducted following the STROBE guidelines. We included patients with a single, biopsy-confirmed, treatment-naïve T1a RCC (<4 cm) who underwent PCA between January 2008 and December 2021. Patient demographics, tumor characteristics, and procedural details were collected. Survival analyses were performed using the Kaplan-Meier estimator. Results: Eighty-six patients (57 men and 29 women) with a median age of 69 years met the inclusion criteria. Fifty patients (58%) had a history of an additional non-renal malignancy. In total, 86 renal tumors were treated using PCA, with a median tumor diameter of 2.7 cm. Clear cell RCC accounted for 67.4% of the tumors. Procedural complications classified as Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher occurred in 4.6% of cases. Local tumor recurrence at the ablation site was observed in five patients (5.8%), and four patients (4.6%) developed new lesions elsewhere within the kidney. The estimated median overall survival was 10.34 years. The 10-year local recurrence-free and disease-free survival rates were 93.5% and 84.0%, respectively. Both metastasis-free survival and cancer-specific survival rates at 10 years were 100%. Conclusions: Percutaneous cryoablation provided durable local tumor control with low major morbidity and favorable long-term oncologic outcomes in this selected cohort of patients with solitary cT1a renal tumors.

Title: Dermoscopy at an Inflection Point: Sharper Criteria, New Optics, and the Arrival of Artificial Intelligence.
Abstract: Dermoscopy improves the diagnosis of melanoma and keratinocyte carcinoma, but its value depends on the observer, the lesion mix, the anatomic site, and the action taken after the examination. Recent reviews have mainly focused on one modality or image-classification accuracy. This narrative review follows the clinical pathway and compares five linked areas: defined diagnostic criteria, sequential digital monitoring, site- and skin-tone-specific interpretation, multimodal imaging, and artificial intelligence (AI). Melanoma and keratinocyte carcinoma are discussed separately because their criteria, diagnostic problems, imaging needs, and management differ. Meta-analyses support dermoscopy over naked-eye examination, although accuracy remains closely related to clinician experience. A randomized trial of three-dimensional total-body photography with sequential dermoscopy led to more procedures and higher costs without finding more malignant tumors over two years. Reflectance confocal microscopy can improve specificity in selected equivocal lesions, while optical coherence technologies add architectural and depth information that is most relevant to keratinocyte carcinoma. AI has moved from retrospective benchmarks to prospective multicenter studies, but false-positive burden, dataset shift, underrepresentation of darker skin tones, limited explainability, and uncertain workflow effects remain. The review also considers foundation models, regulation, and patient-facing tools and uses a SWOT analysis to define research priorities. The field is at an inflection point in evidence, not image quality. Progress should be judged by effects on biopsy decisions, missed-cancer rates, timeliness, cost, access, and patient outcomes in defined populations.
