CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

Title: Predicting spinal hypotension during cesarean delivery: what is being predicted, and when.
Abstract: Spinal hypotension during cesarean delivery has generated a large prediction literature, but the term "prediction" is applied to signals obtained at very different points in the peri-spinal course. Most reviews group predictors by physiology or device. Here we organize them by when the signal becomes available and which clinical decision remains open. This changes how reported performance should be interpreted. A preoperative low-frequency/high-frequency heart rate variability threshold of 2.5, for example, showed only 35% sensitivity and discrimination around 0.60 in an independent cohort, whereas small development studies of other preoperative tools have reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve approaching 0.9. Pre-spinal provocation may improve discrimination while preserving time to adjust prophylaxis. Measurements obtained after intrathecal injection, and real-time algorithms operating minutes before hypotension, answer a different question because sympathetic blockade is already evolving and the decision window is narrower. Variation in hypotension definitions, treatment background, case mix, and small development samples further limits direct comparison. Routine vasopressor prophylaxis also changes what a useful predictor should do: rather than decide who receives prevention, it should help identify who needs earlier, stronger, or differently titrated treatment. Two randomized cesarean trials now support Hypotension Prediction Index-guided management, while treatment-impact evidence for true preoperative prediction remains limited.

Title: Multi-omics insights into immune dysregulation and candidate biological programs in kawasaki disease: toward precision immunomodulation.
Abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an immune-mediated pediatric vasculitis characterized by dynamic interactions among genetic susceptibility, innate and adaptive immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular remodeling. Although intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) therapy substantially reduces coronary complications, 10%-20% of patients show persistent or recurrent fever after initial IVIG treatment, and reliable clinically validated molecular approaches for diagnosis, treatment-response prediction, and coronary-risk stratification remain unavailable. Recent advances in multi-omics technologies, including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, single-cell sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome profiling, have expanded our understanding of KD-associated immune dysregulation. However, the clinical interpretation of these molecular findings remains challenging because of limited cohort sizes, heterogeneous control populations, treatment-related confounding, and insufficient external validation. In this review, we integrate evidence across multiple molecular layers and propose a framework in which current KD multi-omics findings converge into candidate biological programs rather than fixed molecular subtypes. These programs may represent temporally dynamic biological states along a shared inflammatory trajectory, influenced by disease phase, cellular composition, genetic background, and treatment exposure. Synthesized from convergent multi-omics evidence rather than derived from formal molecular classification, these candidate biological programs include myeloid inflammatory activation characterized by S100A8/A9 and IL-1/NF-κB signaling, interferon-associated immune responses, and vascular injury/remodeling responses involving endothelial activation and extracellular matrix regulation. Current evidence supports biologically meaningful molecular programs that may contribute to clinical heterogeneity, but prospective validation is required before molecular signatures can be applied as clinical classifiers or treatment-selection tools. Integrating multi-omics approaches with functional validation, longitudinal sampling, and multicenter studies may facilitate the development of precision immunomodulation strategies for Kawasaki disease.

Title: Botulinum toxin type a within function-oriented management of post-stroke spasticity: a narrative review.
Abstract: Post-stroke spasticity (PSS) is a heterogeneous complication of stroke that affects motor recovery, care needs, pain, positioning, and participation in daily life. Current management frameworks commonly stratify patients by time since stroke, but disease duration alone does not capture differences in neural mechanisms, residual voluntary control, functional priorities, or response to intervention. This narrative review searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Wanfang databases from inception to May 2026, prioritizing randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, systematic reviews, real-world studies, Goal Attainment Scaling research, the Upper Limb International Spasticity cohort series, best-practice guidance, and clinical trials including BEST and InTENSE. We synthesize evidence that PSS heterogeneity can be understood across central and peripheral mechanisms, temporal trajectories, and active versus passive functional consequences. Available studies suggest that active and passive functional goals differ in baseline functional profiles, outcome assessment, treatment response, and intervention requirements. However, patients sharing a functional goal type may still differ in residual voluntary control, neural and non-neural contributors to movement restriction, pain, mobility, and care dependency. Botulinum toxin type A is well aligned with focal tone reduction and passive goals, including pain relief, hygiene, and limb positioning. It may also support contracture-prevention strategies when modifiable neural muscle overactivity remains, whereas active functional gains usually require preserved motor potential and integration with task-oriented training, rehabilitation, and adjunctive modalities. We propose that functional goal type should complement time-based staging as a decision dimension rather than serve as a complete clinical phenotype. This combined framework may better align patient selection, intervention matching, outcome assessment, and longitudinal treatment planning. Prospective goal-stratified studies and standardized assessment tools are needed to test its clinical utility.

Title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength.
OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional.
PARTICIPANTS: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728).
EXPOSURE: CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3).
OUTCOME MEASURES: Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis.
METHODS: Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated.
RESULTS: Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women.
CONCLUSION: In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

Title: Beyond the skin surface: untangling sensitive skin syndrome and peripheral neuropathy through an exploratory real-world data analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sensitive skin syndrome (SSS) is commonly reported despite its nonspecific definition, whereas peripheral neuropathy (PN) remains underrecognized in the general population. Because localized paresthesia and numbness-particularly in the hands and feet-may be perceived as skin problems, some patients reporting sensitive skin could have unrecognized neuropathy. This exploratory real-world evidence study investigated the potential overlap between SSS and PN.
METHODS: Patient-level real-world data from health records of individuals reporting sensitive skin were analyzed to characterize associated diagnoses, symptoms, comorbidities, and risk factors potentially related to PN.
RESULTS: Diagnoses among patients reporting sensitive skin included dermatitis (44%), altered skin sensation (33%), dry skin or urticaria (15%), and acne (13%). Within the group diagnosed with altered skin sensation, 18% reported paresthesia or tingling, 11% reported anesthesia or numbness, and 4% reported other symptoms. Documented comorbidities and risk factors included established contributors to PN, such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and smoking.
DISCUSSION: The findings suggest a potential diagnostic overlap between SSS and PN and raise the hypothesis that some patients with altered skin sensation may have unrecognized PN. They also demonstrate how real-world data can reveal symptom patterns that may be overlooked during routine clinical assessment. Because the hypothesis arose from the same dataset used to explore it, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation. Nevertheless, timely differentiation between SSS and PN could facilitate appropriate clinical evaluation and improve patient health and well-being.

Title: P2Y12 inhibition, adenosine signaling, and bone remodeling: differential skeletal pharmacology of antiplatelet agents.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, and fragility fractures frequently coexist in older adults, creating an important overlap between antiplatelet therapy and orthopedic care. This narrative review examines mechanistic, preclinical, observational, and perioperative evidence concerning the skeletal effects of aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors, and other clinically relevant antiplatelet agents. Purinergic signaling provides biological plausibility for interactions between platelet inhibition and bone remodeling because P2Y12, P2Y1, P2X7, adenosine receptors, and equilibrative nucleoside transporter 1 (ENT1) regulate osteoblast differentiation, osteoclast activity, inflammatory responses, and tissue repair. Aspirin shows dose- and context-dependent skeletal effects, whereas clopidogrel has been associated with impaired osteoblast mineralization in preclinical studies and conflicting fracture-risk estimates in observational cohorts. Direct skeletal evidence for prasugrel and other agents remains limited. Selected preclinical studies suggest that ticagrelor-associated ENT1 inhibition can enhance adenosine-dependent osteogenic signaling; however, clinical evidence is limited to one retrospective cohort in which ticagrelor-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was associated with lower fracture risk than clopidogrel-based DAPT, while prospective skeletal outcome data are lacking. Perioperative antiplatelet management in orthopedic surgery should remain guided by cardiovascular indications, thrombotic risk, and bleeding risk. A conceptual framework may help define priorities for evaluating skeletal outcomes during antiplatelet therapy. However, current evidence is insufficient to support antiplatelet selection or switching on the basis of presumed skeletal effects.

Title: Ostial vs Left Main Crossover Stenting in Isolated Ostial Left Anterior Descending Stenosis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited data exist on the optimal stenting strategy for isolated ostial left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) lesions. The aim of this study was to compare the outcomes in patients who had a significant isolated ostial LAD stenosis treated with either left main crossover stenting (LMCS) or focal ostial LAD stenting (FO-LAD).
METHODS: The primary end point of the study was target lesion failure (TLF), a composite of target lesion revascularization, target vessel myocardial infarction, and cardiac death at 2 years. Secondary end points included the individual components of the primary outcome. Additional secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events, which are a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, and any unplanned revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 522 patients were included in this study, of whom 382 underwent FO-LAD stenting and 140 underwent LMCS. The primary outcome occurred in 32 patients (22.9%) in the LMCS and in 44 patients (11.5%) in the FO-LAD group at a median follow-up of 730 days (IQR, 451-730). LMCS was associated with a higher risk of TLF compared with FO-LAD stenting (adjusted HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.16-2.98; P = .01).With regard to secondary outcomes, LMCS was associated with more major adverse cardiovascular events (31.4% vs 15.5%; adjusted HR, 2.11 [1.41-3.17]; P < .001) and cardiac death (17.1% vs 7.9%; adjusted HR, 2.05 [1.19-3.55]; P = .01]. No significant differences were observed for target lesion revascularization and target vessel myocardial infarction.
CONCLUSIONS: Left main crossover stenting was associated with a higher rate of TLF at a median follow-up of 2 years when compared with FO-LAD stenting in the treatment of patients with significant isolated ostial LAD disease.

Title: Outcomes of Surgical Versus Transcatheter Mitral Valve Repair or Replacement in Patients With Myocardial Infarction and Concomitant Mitral Regurgitation: A Retrospective Analysis of Real-World Data.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions

Title: Impact of a Continuous Quality Improvement Committee on Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous quality improvement (CQI) programs aim to enhance procedural safety and efficiency in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). This analysis evaluates changes in PCI practice patterns and outcomes after implementation of a multidisciplinary catheterization laboratory CQI committee at a large academic center.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted regarding PCI procedures from January 2018 to June 2024 using National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI data. Outcomes and practice patterns were compared before (pre-CQI: 2018-October 2022) versus after CQI implementation (post-CQI: November 2022-2024). Prespecified primary end points were post-PCI acute kidney injury, periprocedural hemoglobin change, and same-day discharge.
RESULTS: Among 2759 PCI cases (1783 pre-CQI; 976 post-CQI), monthly PCI volume increased (30.7-48.2 cases/mo, P < .001). Post-CQI, radial access use increased (33.4%-58.9%, P < .001) and mean contrast volume decreased (188-153 mL, P < .001). Primary outcomes improved post-CQI: acute kidney injury decreased (14.3%-9.7%, P = .01), mean periprocedural hemoglobin change decreased (0.65-0.54 g/dL, P = .004), and same-day discharge increased (13.0%-24.7%, P < .001). Overall complication rates and in-hospital mortality remained stable.
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a catheterization laboratory CQI committee was temporally associated with improved PCI safety and discharge efficiency alongside increased procedural volume and evolving case mix. These findings support CQI-driven approaches to optimize PCI care delivery.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Concurrent Impella-Assisted High-Risk PCI and TAVR in Patients With Complex Coronary Artery Disease and Severe Aortic Stenosis.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous management of high risk, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) needing mechanical support for complex coronary artery disease in patients needing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis remains incompletely defined. We report on the feasibility and safety of a single-session strategy using Impella-assisted complex high-risk PCI (IA-CHIP) followed by transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of consecutive patients undergoing simultaneous IA-CHIP and TAVR at 3 tertiary centers between January 2015 and March 2026. All patients received mechanical circulatory support with percutaneous microaxial flow pump Impella CP (Abiomed) during PCI, followed by transfemoral TAVR in the same session. Baseline demographics, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes were collected. The primary endpoint was in-hospital complications, including death, stroke, major bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 2, 3, or 5), acute kidney injury, permanent pacemaker implantation, and vascular complications.
RESULTS: A total of 12 patients were included (median age, 79.5 years [IQR, 77.0-81.2]; 91.7% male; median Charlson Comorbidity Index of 7 [IQR, 5.8-9]). Coronary lesions mainly involved left main disease in 66% of cases. Advanced calcium modification was required in 50% of cases. The median aortic valve area was 0.86 cm2, and median mean gradient was 38 mm Hg. Procedural success for IA-CHIP and TAVR was 100%. There were no in-hospital deaths, strokes, or major vascular complications. Conduction disturbances requiring permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 25%. An acute kidney injury occurred in 16.7% of cases, with no requirement for dialysis. The majority of patients (91.7%) were discharged home.
CONCLUSIONS: A single-session strategy of IA-CHIP followed by TAVR is feasible and safe in selected patients with complex coronary artery disease and severe aortic stenosis.

Title: Clinical Efficacy of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients With Diabetes: A Global Retrospective Study.
Journal: Journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), a standard therapy for aortic stenosis, is preferred for older or high-risk patients. Various complications, including heart failure (HF), resulting in increased mortality, have been reported in the literature. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are recommended in HF, irrespective of ejection fraction; however, their role in reducing post-TAVR cardiovascular complications remains underexplored. We conducted a retrospective study to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes associated with the use of SGLT2i in post-TAVR patients.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort was based on a global database of electronic health records of more than 160 million patients. After propensity-score matching, the study population included 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients divided into 2 cohorts based on their exposure to SGLT2i. Exposure to SGLT2i was defined as exposure after 1 day of TAVR.
RESULTS: In this study of 9930 post-TAVR diabetic patients, the primary outcome of major adverse cardiovascular events and secondary outcomes, ie, cardiovascular mortality, ischemic stroke, and HF exacerbation, were significantly reduced in SGLT2i-exposed post-TAVR patients at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up. Hemorrhagic stroke was comparable at the 1-month follow-up; however, it was significantly lower in SGLT2i-exposed cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. The risk of new-onset myocardial infarction was significantly reduced at 1 month; however, it was comparable between the 2 cohorts at the 1-year follow-up. Our study also demonstrated a significant reduction in the risk of end-stage renal disease in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort at the 1-year follow-up. The periprocedural risk of acute kidney injury (within 7 days of TAVR) as well as at the 1-month and 1-year follow-up was significantly lower in the SGLT2i-exposed cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In this study, post-TAVR SGLT2i use in diabetic patients was associated with reduced cardiovascular morbidity and mortality for up to 1 year.

Title: Health literacy and cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and postpartum.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Health literacy is a key social determinant of health. Adequate health literacy has been associated with better obstetric and general adult health outcomes. However, its relationship with cardiovascular health during and after pregnancy is not well known. We aimed to estimate associations between health literacy and cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and postpartum.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-be (nuMoM2b) study and its prospective follow-up phase, the nuMoM2b Heart Health Study. Participants who completed the Rapid Estimate of Adult Literacy in Medicine-Short Form (REALM-SF) in the second trimester (16-21 weeks of gestation) and a 2-7 year postpartum study visit were included. Health literacy was classified as inadequate (REALM-SF score <7) or adequate (≥7) using standard scoring procedures. The primary outcomes were cardiovascular health in early pregnancy and 2-7 years after the first birth, assessed using a modified Life's Essential 8 (LE8) score, which includes health behaviors (diet, physical activity, sleep health, and nicotine exposure) and health factors (body mass index, blood pressure, blood glucose, and lipid levels). Secondary outcomes included LE8 subcomponents. Multivariable linear regression models, which adjusted for maternal age, insurance type, and family income, were used to evaluate associations of health literacy with LE8 overall scores and its subcomponents.
RESULTS: Among 4424 participants eligible for analysis, 3599 (81.4%) had adequate health literacy. Those with adequate health literacy were older, more likely to identify as non-Hispanic White, and more likely to have higher income, higher education, and private insurance coverage. Participants with adequate health literacy had higher early pregnancy LE8 scores (79.9 ± 13.3 vs. 73.0 ± 14.2, p < 0.001), a relationship that persisted after adjustment (aβ 3.6, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.8-5.4). This association was driven by body mass index, diet, physical activity, and sleep subcomponents. Similarly, LE8 scores 2-7 years after birth were higher among those with adequate health literacy (80.1 ± 13.8 vs. 72.9 ± 14.6, p < 0.001; aβ 3.2, 95%, CI, 0.8-5.6), primarily due to healthier measures of body mass index, diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, and sleep.
CONCLUSION: Among nulliparous women, adequate health literacy scores in early pregnancy were associated with better cardiovascular health during pregnancy and several years after first birth.

Title: Associations of cardiac autonomic modulation and urinary adrenal hormones with marathon finishing time in middle-aged male athletes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The autonomic nervous and endocrine systems are involved in the physiological adaptation to exercise, and in experimental settings both the sympathovagal balance and the adrenal function are associated with athletic performance. In this real-life field study, the association between non-invasive markers of cardiac autonomic modulation, urinary adrenal hormone levels, and marathon finishing time in middle-aged Caucasian male athletes was investigated.
METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in male marathon runners aged ≥30 years. Continuous single-lead electrocardiographic (ECG) recordings were obtained using a wearable chest device from the day before the marathon until after its completion. Urinary adrenal hormone levels were measured before and after the race. Univariate linear regression analyses were performed to correlate general characteristics, nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV) parameters, and hormonal parameters with marathon finishing time. A multivariable model was then applied including age, body mass index (BMI), and training hours.
RESULTS: 104 athletes were enrolled in the study and 73 (median age 48 years, interquartile range = 16) had adequate data quality for the final analysis. Several HRV parameters correlated with better performance at univariate analysis; lower minimum nocturnal heart rate and vagal predominance, expressed as higher 2 Like Variations (2LV) values remained independently associated with shorter finishing time. Among hormonal variables, the post-/pre-race ratio of urinary normetanephrine hourly output and cortisol/cortisone ratio remained significant at multivariable analysis. Only BMI, but not age and training history, remained significant in a model integrating HRV and hormones.
CONCLUSIONS: Under real-world marathon conditions, specific HRV indices and endocrine markers showed promising value as indicators of physiological readiness with endurance exercise in male master athletes.

Title: Sex differences in electrocardiographic patterns among patients with acute coronary syndromes.
Abstract: Sex-based differences in ACS presentation and outcomes have been observed, but limited information is available on sex-specific electrocardiogram (ECG) features and their prevalence in this context. The aim of this study was to compare the prevalence of different ECG patterns between sexes and their prognostic roles for in-hospital mortality in ACS patients. This prospective single-center study (NCT02438085)° was conducted from June 2018 to December 2019, including 841 consecutive patients. Data on baseline characteristics, ECG findings, treatments, and outcomes were collected. Statistical analyses were performed to determine differences in the prevalence of various ECG patterns and identify independent predictors of in-hospital mortality. Males more frequently presented with ST-segment elevation (51% vs. 43%, p = 0.031) and hyperacute T waves (13% vs. 7%, p = 0.006) than females. Moreover, females more often had a normal ECG at admission (15% vs. 9%, p = 0.01). In female STEMI negative T waves (50% vs. 38%, p = 0.025) were more common than in males. Hyperacute T waves were linked to a higher risk of in-hospital death in female STEMI cases (OR=6.25, 95% CI: 1.0 -39.7, p = 0.048). Additionally the development of left bundle branch block during hospitalization (OR=14.4, 95% CI: 1.48-14 p = 0.02) was a significant predictor of in-hospital mortality in the female NSTEMI subgroup. No ECG features were found to predict in-hospital mortality in male patients. Compared to males, females with ACS often showed less frequent and less extensive ST-segment abnormalities and were more likely to have a normal initial ECG at admission. These differences could impact clinical evaluation and prognosis. Recognizing these sex-related ECG differences may help optimize the management of ACS patients. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT02438085.

Title: Inflammatory and cardiac-stress biomarkers in Moyamoya disease: the role of GDF-15.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is an uncommon cerebrovascular condition that requires the identification of easily measurable biomarkers to enable prompt diagnosis. This study aimed to: (1) compare clinical and laboratory parameters between individuals with MMD and control subjects; (2) examine the associations of these parameters with growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15); (3) evaluate the diagnostic effectiveness of potential biomarkers; and (4) identify independent risk factors for MMD.
METHODS: The study cohort comprised 265 participants, including 121 patients diagnosed with MMD and 144 healthy control subjects. The parameters measured included white blood cell count (WBC), neutrophil count (NEU), Glu, homocysteine (HCY), GDF-15, and soluble growth stimulation expressed gene 2 (ST-2) concentrations. The analyses conducted encompassed correlation assessments, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve evaluations, and multivariable logistic regression analyses.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups except for smoking status, which was significantly more frequent in the MMD group (p = 0.046). Patients diagnosed with MMD exhibited significantly elevated levels of WBC, NEU, HCY, GDF-15 and soluble ST-2. No significant differences were observed in Glu levels (p = 0.468). GDF-15 demonstrated a positive correlation with WBC (r = 0.53, p < 0.0001), NEU (r = 0.45, p = 0.026), but not with Glu or HCY (p > 0.05). ROC analysis revealed that GDF-15 had the highest area under the curve (AUC) (0.779), followed by NEU (0.668), Glu (0.590), and WBC (0.577). Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified Diabetes, NEU, and GDF-15 as independent risk factors (all p < 0.001). A 100 pg./mL increment in GDF-15 levels was correlated with an estimated 49% elevation in the odds of MMD occurrence.
CONCLUSION: Patients diagnosed with MMD exhibit a unique profile of inflammatory and cardiac-stress biomarkers. GDF-15 and NEU were independently correlated with MMD. Among these, GDF-15 demonstrated the highest diagnostic efficacy, suggesting its potential utility as a non-invasive adjunctive biomarker.

Title: Population aging and the spatial equity of prehospital emergency medical resources: evidence from Shanghai's five new towns.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: China is undergoing rapid urbanization and profound population aging, presenting the prehospital emergency medical system with the dual challenges of inadequate capacity and spatial mismatch. Shanghai's five new towns are strategic vehicles for the spatial restructuring of a megacity; however, evidence is still lacking as to whether their prehospital emergency systems can meet the aging-driven increase in demand.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the spatial equity of emergency medical resource allocation in the five new towns and to analyze its associations with population aging and future demand.
METHODS: Based on 2024 data, the Gini coefficient and Theil index were used to evaluate equity; population projections were performed using the cohort-component method in PADIS-INT (population analysis software); resource requirements were estimated in stages according to policy standards; and coverage gaps were identified through isochrone analysis in QGIS (open-source geographic information system).
RESULTS: The population-based Gini coefficients across the five districts ranged from 0.03 (substations) to 0.10 (physicians), indicating relatively equitable per capita allocation. However, after including all 16 districts of the municipality, the area-based Gini coefficient for substations reached 0.61, reflecting a gradient in substation density between the urban core and the suburbs. Under the medium scenario, the population aged 65 years and older in Jiading increases from 13.18% to 19.15% (2035), and the demand for R1 standard ambulances in Jiading New City is projected to rise from 24 vehicles in 2025 to 29 vehicles in 2035. In Fengxian, patients aged 60 years and above accounted for 48.49% of emergency calls. Highly aged subdistricts spatially overlapped with 8 min coverage blind spots. Notably, stratified emergency response time (ERT) analysis showed that in two of the three districts, the differences in ERT between cardiac arrest and non-emergency patients were not statistically significant (p > 0.05), suggesting limited implementation of dispatch prioritization.
CONCLUSION: The five new towns exhibit a dual-track pattern of equity in population terms but inequity in spatial terms. Population aging exacerbates inequity through demand expansion, changes in the disease spectrum, and spatial overlap.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitors for the Primary Prevention of CKD in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors slow the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), although their potential to prevent the development of CKD in type 2 diabetes needs to be examined.
PURPOSE: To evaluate SGLT2 inhibitors for the primary prevention of CKD in people with type 2 diabetes.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through October 2025.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of SGLT2 inhibitors compared with placebo or other glucose-lowering agents in people with type 2 diabetes without baseline CKD were included. Outcomes were estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline and incident albuminuria (i.e., urine albumin-to-creatine ratio [UACR] ≥30 mg/g). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, and heterogeneity was assessed with I 2. Certainty of evidence was evaluated with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).
RESULTS: Eight RCTs were included: five cardiovascular outcomes trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitors and placebo (24,072 participants) and three trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitors and sulfonylureas (2,889 participants). Compared with placebo, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of incident albuminuria (three trials; hazard ratio 0.82; 95% CI 0.77-0.88; I 2 = 0%, high certainty) and slowed eGFR decline based on the chronic eGFR slope (five trials; mean difference [MD] 0.95 [95% CI 0.84-1.07] mL/min/1.73 m2/year; I 2 = 19%, high certainty) and total eGFR slope (four trials; MD 0.76 [0.50-1.03] mL/min/1.73 m2/year; I 2 = 88%, moderate certainty). Compared with sulfonylureas, SGLT2 inhibitors slowed eGFR decline based on the chronic eGFR slope (three trials; MD 2.43 [1.72-3.13] mL/min/1.73 m2/year; I 2 = 55%, moderate certainty).
CONCLUSIONS: In people with type 2 diabetes without CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors slow eGFR decline compared with both placebo and sulfonylureas and prevent incident albuminuria compared with placebo.

Title: Diabetic Retinopathy Risk in SGLT2i vs GLP1RA Initiators With CKD Stages 3-4 and Type 2 Diabetes.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1RA) have demonstrated renal and cardiovascular benefits among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, their comparative effects on diabetic retinopathy (DR) outcomes in patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D remain unclear. This study aimed to demonstrate the effect of SGLT2i vs GLP1RA in this population.
STUDY DESIGN: Population-based, new-user, active comparator cohort study comparing SGLT2i versus GLP1RA initiators. Subjects were divided into 2 cohorts: (1) incident nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) and (2) DR progression cohort.
SETTING & STUDY POPULATION: Patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D across 3 US health care databases: Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database (2014-2024), Merative MarketScan (2014-2022), and Medicare Fee-for-Service (2014-2020).
SELECTION CRITERIA FOR STUDIES: Adults with a new prescription for either SGLT2i or GLP1RA without prior use in the preceding 365 days. The primary outcomes were incident NPDR and DR progression, identified through ICD-9/10 diagnosis codes and procedural codes for retinopathy treatments.
DATA EXTRACTION: Exposures, covariates, and outcomes were obtained from structured claims fields.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Both cohorts were analyzed using propensity score matching (1:1) to control for confounding. Incidence rates (IRs), rate differences, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated.
RESULTS: After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 20,135 matched patient pairs in the incident NPDR cohort and 7,763 matched pairs in the DR progression cohort. For incident NPDR, there was no difference between SGLT2i and GLP1RA groups (IR 29.55 vs 30.38 per 1,000 person-years, respectively; HR 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87-1.10]). Similarly, DR progression was not different between groups (IR 32.73 vs 35.24 per 1,000 person-years; HR 0.92 [95% CI, 0.76-1.12]). Subgroup analyses showed no differences in HRs for both incident NPDR and DR progression across multiple predefined subgroups.
LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding, outcome misclassification, and limited generalizability to non-U.S. populations.
CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of SGLT2i was not associated with a different risk of incident NPDR or DR progression compared with GLP1RA among patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D. Additional studies with extended follow-up are needed to better characterize long-term retinal safety profiles of these therapies.

Title: Heterogeneity in maternal perceptions of psychological birth trauma: a latent profile analysis and predictor study.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The heterogeneity in maternal childbirth trauma perception remains poorly understood, hindering the development of targeted prevention strategies. Identifying distinct risk subgroups and their associated modifiable factors is crucial for informing early interventions aimed at reducing the risk of Postpartum Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PP-PTSD).
OBJECTIVE: To identify heterogeneous classes of maternal perceived childbirth trauma and to examine their cross-sectional correlates and short-term longitudinal associations with the development of PP-PTSD symptoms from 3 to 42 days postpartum.
DESIGN SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective longitudinal study enrolled 300 women following vaginal delivery at a tertiary hospital in Chongqing between February and April 2024. Participants were assessed at two time points: 3 days and 42 days postpartum.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was childbirth trauma perception, measured using the Birth Trauma Perception Scale for Women During Vaginal Delivery (BTPS-WVD). PP-PTSD symptoms were assessed with the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) Checklist-Civilian Version (PCL-C). Associated factors examined included perineal pain, breast engorgement, mother-infant separation, and partner support, collected via structured questionnaires.
RESULTS: Latent profile analysis identified four trauma perception classes based on changes in perception scores between the two time points: severe (C1, 13.67%), high (C2, 20.67%), moderate (C3, 48.33%), and low (C4, 17.33%). Factors associated with a lower likelihood of belonging to the high-risk classes (C1/C2) included laboring in shared rooms (OR = 0.362), abnormal fetal heart rate during labor (OR = 0.314), and having the husband as the primary caregiver (OR = 0.410). Factors associated with a higher likelihood included severe breast engorgement affecting mood (OR = 7.084), perineal pain lasting >2 days (OR = 4.019), pain interfering with daily life (OR = 4.899), and mother-infant separation (OR = 4.600). Notably, PTSD symptom scores showed a significant increase from 3 to 42 days postpartum in the severe and high trauma perception classes (C1 and C2) compared to the moderate and low classes (C3 and C4; P < 0.05), suggesting that early trauma perception class membership is associated with subsequent symptom worsening.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Maternal childbirth trauma perception exhibits four distinct classes, characterized by different patterns of early postpartum change. Postpartum physical discomfort and mother-infant separation emerged as key modifiable associated factors, while a supportive intrapartum environment and partner involvement appeared protective. The observed association between high-risk trauma perception classes and subsequent worsening of PTSD symptoms highlights the potential value of early identification. Future targeted interventions focusing on pain management, lactation support, and enhanced partner engagement may be beneficial, though prospective validation of these factors as predictors is warranted.

Title: A 2-year prognostic assessment of patients with coronary borderline lesions based on three-vessel quantitative flow ratio and the development and internal validation of a risk prediction nomogram.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic value of three-vessel quantitative flow ratio (3V-QFR) in patients with borderline coronary lesions (QFR 0.75-0.80) over a 2-year period; to identify key variables using LASSO regression; and to construct and internally validate a personalized nomogram model for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) over 2 years.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with coronary artery disease who were treated at Ordos Central Hospital from January 2021 to December 2024, underwent coronary angiography revealing at least one borderline lesion in a major coronary artery, and received a QFR assessment. Patients were followed for up to 24 months after discharge through outpatient visits, telephone follow-up, and electronic medical-record review. The primary endpoint was defined as the occurrence of MACE during the 2-year follow-up period. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to explore the nonlinear relationship between 3V-QFR and the risk of MACE. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized regression evaluated 19 prespecified candidate predictors using 10-fold cross-validation and the one-standard-error rule. A nomogram was constructed based on the selected factors, and the model's discriminatory power, consistency, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap resamples that repeated the complete preprocessing, variable-selection, and model-refitting pipeline.
RESULTS: A total of 138 patients with borderline lesions were enrolled (33 in the MACE group and 105 in the non-MACE group). Among 33 first MACE events, 20 were ischemia-driven revascularizations, 9 were non-fatal myocardial infarctions, and 4 were all-cause deaths. RCS analysis showed an overall association between lower 3V-QFR and higher MACE risk, whereas evidence for nonlinearity was not statistically strong; multivariable regression supported 3V-QFR as an independent predictor. LASSO regression identified four optimal predictors of 2-year MACE through 10-fold cross-validation: 3V-QFR, age, diabetes, and NT-proBNP levels. The final model included 3V-QFR, age, diabetes, and NT-proBNP. The apparent AUC was 0.869 (95% CI 0.802-0.936), and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.842 (95% CI 0.771-0.913); calibration and decision-curve findings were considered exploratory.
CONCLUSION: Lower 3V-QFR was associated with higher 2-year MACE risk in this retrospective development cohort. The 3V-QFR-based nomogram showed promising internal performance and may support exploratory risk stratification; independent external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

Title: Synthesized cardiometabolic, pulmonary, and sleep outcomes after bariatric surgery in adolescents with severe obesity: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To synthesize cardiometabolic, pulmonary, sleep-related, anthropometric, and safety outcomes after metabolic and bariatric surgery in adolescents with severe obesity.
METHODS: This was a systematic review and meta-analysis conducted according to PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261354795). Five databases were searched for studies of adolescents aged approximately 10-19 years undergoing recognized metabolic or bariatric procedures. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis was used when studies were sufficiently comparable.
RESULTS: Of 5110 records, 147 reports representing 101 unique studies or cohorts published from 1995 to 2026 were included. Follow-up ranged from 30 days to approximately 15 years. Across three independent randomized cohorts, surgery reduced body mass index by 9.39 kg/m2 at 2 years versus non-surgical care (95% CI -13.90 to -4.89; I2 = 88%; low certainty). Randomized evidence indicated lower triglycerides (mean difference -0.36 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.57 to -0.14; low certainty), whereas blood-pressure effects were indeterminate (very low certainty). Observational cohorts reported improvement or remission of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea. Weight reduction was durable after gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy but smaller and less durable after gastric banding. Repeat objective sleep testing was reported in three studies and postoperative spirometry in one. No included report documented use of a validated asthma-control instrument, ambulatory blood-pressure monitoring, or vascular imaging as a pre- and postoperative outcome; diastolic function was reported once; diastolic function was reported once. Perioperative mortality and serious 30-day complications were uncommon, whereas reoperation and micronutrient deficiency remained important during extended follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and bariatric surgery produces large body mass index reductions and multisystem improvement in adolescents with severe obesity; serious short-term complications and perioperative mortality were uncommon, but lifelong nutritional and multidisciplinary surveillance remains important. Most effect estimates remain uncertain, particularly for objective long-term sleep and pulmonary outcomes.

Title: Efficacy of Huangbai liniment for diabetic foot ulcers with multidrug-resistant organism infection: a randomized controlled multicenter trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot infection, particularly with multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs), is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) that increases wound healing time and amputation risk. Prolonged use of broad-spectrum antibiotics can contribute to antibiotic resistance and limit future treatment options. Developing effective non-antibiotic antibacterial therapies is therefore urgently needed. Huangbai liniment (HB) is a standardized herbal product clinically used to treat diabetic foot infections, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureusStaphylococcus aureus (MRSA). This trial assessed the efficacy and safety of HB for DFUs with mild MDRO infection.
METHODS: This multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial was conducted in China. A total of 154 patients with DFUs and mild MDRO infection were randomly assigned to the HB group and the silver dressing (SD) group. Both groups received the same basic treatment for diabetic foot disease. The HB group received Tazi therapy (topical application of HB) for 2 weeks, while the control group was treated with SD. Primary outcome was the resolution of infection defined as a change from mild infection to no infection (using the Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Diabetic Foot Infections). Secondary outcomes included the MDRO conversion rate, rate of completing ulcer healing, and reduction in ulcer size.
RESULTS: A total of 74 patients in the HB group and 63 patients in the SD group were included. Infection was resolved in 35 patients (47.3%) in the HB group versus 13 patients (20.6%) in the SD group (p = 0.001). Mixed-level logistic regression analyses showed that the HB group was associated with resolution of infection [odds ratio (OR) = 4.81; 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.01-12.48; p < 0.001]. However, there was no difference in rate of completing ulcer healing and reduction of ulcer size.
CONCLUSION: Topical HB effectively facilitated mild infection resolution and MDRO conversion, with no adverse effects. HB is an effective and safe adjunctive therapy for short-term infection resolution in patients with DFU with mild MDRO infection. However, no evidence emerged for improved ulcer healing within 2 weeks. Longer follow-up is needed to assess wound healing outcomes.

Title: MammoDiff: weakly supervised mammographic anomaly detection via classifier-guided denoising diffusion models-a real-world clinical study on the KHCC mammography cohort.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early detection of malignant mammographic lesions is a critical clinical challenge, particularly where large annotated datasets are unavailable. Supervised deep learning achieves near-radiologist performance but requires large datasets with reliable labels and pixel/ROI annotations. Weakly supervised anomaly detection, requiring only image-level binary labels, offers an annotation-efficient alternative, yet prior GAN- and autoencoder-based methods have struggled to preserve fine anatomical detail in the mammographic domain.
METHODS: We present MammoDiff, to our knowledge the first application of classifier-guided denoising diffusion models to weakly supervised mammographic anomaly detection, trained and evaluated on 3,013 mammograms from 806 patients at King Hussein Cancer Center (KHCC), Jordan. MammoDiff encodes input anatomy through deterministic DDIM noise encoding and reconstructs a counterfactual healthy image guided by the gradient signal of a noise-conditioned binary classifier. The anomaly map is the pixel-wise absolute difference between input and reconstruction, and the image-level score is obtained by spatial mean pooling. A 3 × 3 ablation over noise level L ∈ {250, 500, 750} and gradient scale s ∈ {50, 100, 200} was performed on the validation set.
RESULTS: The optimal configuration (L = 750, s = 50) achieved AUROC = 0.7246 [95% CI: 0.6685, 0.7825] on the held-out test set (n = 304), compared with a simplified PatchCore-style baseline (AUROC = 0.6634) and a supervised ResNet-50 reference (AUROC = 0.8100), without pixel-level annotation. The proposed Healthy-Shift Index (HSI) was positive for 94.8% of malignant and 87.4% of normal cases, so it is the separation between the class distributions rather than the sign of the index that carries information.
DISCUSSION: This performance is not clinically deployable: at the Youden-optimal threshold the sensitivity is 0.6013, meaning that 61 of 153 malignant cases are missed, well below the approximately 87% targeted by FDA-cleared triage devices, and the study is single-centre without external validation. MammoDiff is therefore presented as a methodological proof-of-concept and a reproducible baseline for future work, not as a screening or triage tool..

Title: Treating a systemic disease as a local one: failure points of current pancreatic cancer management and a multimodal, biology-guided framework for redesign.
Abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the most lethal solid tumors, with 5-year survival near 13% despite decades of incremental change, and current management continues to be organized around anatomic resectability and a chemotherapy backbone applied largely without regard to tumor biology. This article advances the thesis that the dominant paradigm underperforms because it treats a systemic, molecularly convergent, multi-compartment disease as though it were a local one. We first summarize the real advances of the past decade-in surgery, systemic therapy, molecular profiling, and immunotherapy-and then identify five interlocking failure points that persist despite them: (i) selection by vessel anatomy, judged on imaging criteria that are read inconsistently and that classify inaccurately even where read consistently, and applied to splanchnic veins without accounting for their baseline variability and tumor-associated thrombosis; (ii) occult metastasis and the resulting limits of local cure for the systemic majority, evidenced by the gap between complete resection and durable survival and by early distant recurrence; (iii) the addition of radiotherapy, which improves local control without extending survival; (iv) chemotherapy chosen without reference to a validated prognostic classical/basal-like distinction, although prospective subtype-directed regimen selection has not yet improved outcomes in randomized testing; and (v) a sequential, non-integrated structure in which systemic and immune therapy are deferred and no definitive path exists for the roughly 80% who are not surgical candidates. We then propose a multimodal, biology-guided framework that answers each failure point, with every component graded on an explicit evidence scale: corrected tumor-suppressor gene therapy matched to lesion type, a systemic backbone combining renin-angiotensin system-pathway inhibition with immunogenically sequenced chemotherapy and personalized neoantigen vaccination, in-situ immune conversion of an accessible tumor by cryoablation with local priming and natural killer (NK) cell delivery, and front-end biological patient selection. The framework is conceptual rather than product-specific; we specify its rationale, its integration in time, a staged first-in-human development program, and the studies required to test it. The objective is to convert local disease into systemic benefit-a step the current paradigm is not designed to take.

Title: Strategies for defibrillation during out-of-hospital cardiac arrest - protocol for a randomised clinical trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a lack of evidence regarding which defibrillation strategy is the most effective during resuscitation. Anterior-posterior pad placement and double sequential defibrillation have been proposed as alternatives to standard anterior-lateral defibrillation for patients with refractory shockable rhythms, but evidence remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This trial will investigate whether there is a difference in 30-day survival when using anterior-posterior and double sequential defibrillation as compared to standard anterior-lateral defibrillation in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and a shockable rhythm.
METHODS: This trial is an investigator-initiated, individually randomised, 3-group, clinical trial enrolling adult patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with at least one emergency medical services defibrillation attempt and if the last known rhythm is shockable and two manual defibrillators are available. Participants are randomised 1:1:1 to anterior-lateral defibrillation, anterior-posterior defibrillation, or double sequential defibrillation. The trial is planned to be conducted in Denmark, Finland, Belgium, and Ireland.The primary outcome is 30-day survival, with key secondary outcomes of 90-day survival and neurological status at 30 and 90-days assessed using the modified Rankin Scale. Additional outcomes include return of spontaneous circulation, hospital disposition, health-related quality of life, and longer-term survival and neurological outcomes.The planned sample size is 909 participants. Enrollment began in March 2025. 320 patients have been enrolled by September 2026. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier: NCT06781892).

Title: Electroacupuncture pretreatment attenuates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury-induced ferroptosis via the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A major side effect of reperfusion therapy after myocardial infarction is myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI). Electroacupuncture (EA) preconditioning has a long history of application in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. This study aims to investigate whether EA preconditioning alleviates MIRI by regulating the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway to suppress the ferroptotic biochemical phenotype characterized by iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation.
METHODS: Healthy male SPF rats were randomly divided into nine groups: Ctrl, Sham, MIRI, EA, RSL-3+EA, COTI-2+EA, Erastin+EA, COTI-2+Erastin+EA, and COTI-2+Pantethine+EA. Before MIRI induction, EA pretreatment was applied daily at CV4, bilateral ST36, and bilateral PC6 for 20 min (2 Hz, 1 mA) for 7 consecutive days. Pharmacological interventions were administered intraperitoneally once daily for 7 consecutive days before EA stimulation. The MIRI model was established by ligating the left anterior descending coronary artery for 30 min followed by 2 h of reperfusion. Myocardial oxidative stress, ferroptosis-related markers, myocardial injury markers, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis were assessed using corresponding commercial kits, DCFH-DA probe combined with flow cytometry, RhoNox-6 fluorescent probe, Western blot, RT-PCR, ELISA, and TUNEL staining combined with flow cytometry.
RESULTS: EA preconditioning inhibited p53 expression, promoted the activation of the SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway, and thereby alleviated myocardial injury. The morphology of cardiomyocytes in EA-pretreated rats was altered, and the apoptosis rate of cardiomyocytes in these rats was also reduced. In addition, administration of Erastin (SLC7A11 inhibitor) showed effects similar to those of COTI-2 (p53 agonist) intervention, whereas pantethine (SLC7A11 agonist) reversed the effects of COTI-2, exerting anti-ferroptotic and cardioprotective effects.
DISCUSSION: As a proof‑of‑concept study with limited sample size per experimental group, our findings preliminarily suggest that EA preconditioning ameliorates MIRI by suppressing the ferroptotic biochemical signature characterized by myocardial iron overload and lipid peroxidation through the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway. Further studies with larger sample sizes are still needed for validation.

Title: Efficacy of digital interventions for patients with post-stroke aphasia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital interventions show potential for improving language function in post-stroke aphasia (PSA), but contradictory evidence leaves the optimal strategy unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effects of different digital interventions on language function and quality of life in patients with PSA, and to provide evidence-based support for clinical rehabilitation decisions.
METHODS: A systematic search across PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) (inception to May 2026) identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating digital interventions (e.g., virtual reality [VR], computer-assisted language therapy [CALT], telerehabilitation [TR]) for adults with PSA. Eligible studies reported Western Aphasia Battery or Stroke and Aphasia Quality of Life Scale-39 (SAQOL-39) outcomes. Data were extracted independently. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 1 (RoB 1) tool. Network meta-analysis was performed using R 4.5.2, incorporating a consistency model, a random-effects model, and I2statistics to assess heterogeneity. Sources of heterogeneity were analyzed through sensitivity analyses, subgroup analyses, and meta-regression. Intervention efficacy was ranked using Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve (SUCRA). Robustness was validated via the Egger test and sensitivity analyses. Evidence quality was assessed using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Twenty-five RCTs involving 1,069 participants were included. Compared to conventional therapy (C), VR showed significant superiority in aphasia quotient (mean difference [MD] = 10.77, 95% CI 9.48 to 12.06; SUCRA = 89.57%), spontaneous speech (MD = 2.35, 95% CI 1.71 to 2.99), auditory comprehension (MD = 1.47, 95% CI 0.81 to 2.13), and repetition (MD = 1.98, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.76); Ranking was VR > CALT>TR > C. For naming, CALT ranked highest (MD = 1.41, 95% CI 0.79 to 2.03; SUCRA = 89.87%); Ranking was CALT>VR > C > TR. For SAQOL-39, VR showed the best effect (MD = 0.51, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.70; SUCRA = 96.40%). Ranking was VR > TR > C > CALT.
CONCLUSION: Digital interventions effectively improve language function in PSA. VR demonstrated potential advantages for aphasia quotient, speech, comprehension, repetition, and SAQOL-39, whereas CALT provides targeted advantages for naming impairments. Caution is warranted due to study heterogeneity, bias risks, and limited sample sizes. Future research should optimize intervention protocols, integrate neuromodulation or traditional therapeutic techniques, and explore cost-effective implementation strategies.

Title: Histotripsy in tumor therapy: advances in non-thermal mechanical ablation, immune modulation, and clinical translation.
Abstract: Histotripsy is an emerging non-invasive focused-ultrasound technology that mechanically disrupts tissue through controlled bubble activity rather than sustained thermal coagulation. This review distinguishes shock-scattering cavitational histotripsy, intrinsic threshold histotripsy, and boiling histotripsy and relates their pulse regimes, bubble dynamics, tissue effects, monitoring strategies, and evidence maturity. Mechanical fractionation can expose tumor antigens and damage-associated molecular patterns, but immune outcomes vary by submodality, dose, tumor model, treated fraction, and sampling time; no standardized head-to-head evidence establishes a superior immunological approach. Early prospective liver studies demonstrate high technical feasibility and encouraging local control, whereas post-market cohorts also reveal targeting limitations and uncommon but clinically important vascular, thrombotic, and renal complications. Pancreatic investigation remains ongoing, while the renal CAIN study is completed with registry results and a peer-reviewed first-patient report. A clinically useful dosimetry framework should connect delivered acoustic parameters with in situ cavitation, tissue disruption, imaging or acoustic surrogates, and delayed oncologic and immune endpoints. Histotripsy should currently be viewed as a complementary local therapy with a distinctive mechanical mechanism rather than as a proven replacement for established ablation. Standardized reporting, independently adjudicated safety data, and prospective comparative trials are needed to define its durable oncologic and immunological value.

Title: Orthostatic Blood Pressure Changes and Associated Factors Among Adults With Diabetes in Cameroon: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orthostatic blood pressure abnormalities are common in people with diabetes mellitus (DM) and are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Data on orthostatic hypotension (OH), exaggerated orthostatic pressor response (EOPR), and orthostatic hypertension (OHTN) in patients with diabetes from sub-Saharan Africa are limited.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional study among 339 ambulatory adults with DM attending three referral hospitals in Cameroon between November 2023 and April 2024. OH, EOPR, and OHTN were defined according to the 2023 American Autonomic Society/Japanese Society of Hypertension consensus statement. Prespecified multivariable logistic regression models identified factors independently associated with OH and OHTN.
RESULTS: The mean age was 60.3 ± 11.3 years, and 66.1% of participants were female. The prevalence of OH was 13.3% (95% CI, 9.8-17.4), EOPR 8.9% (95% CI, 6.1-12.4), and OHTN 8.6% (95% CI, 5.8-12.1). A history of diabetes-related complications (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.47, 95% CI 1.05-5.81; p = 0.038) and ever smoking (aOR 2.85, 95% CI 1.09-7.44; p = 0.032) were independently associated with OH. Increasing age (aOR 1.08 per year, 95% CI 1.03-1.13; p = 0.002) and dyslipidemia (aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.11-7.06; p = 0.030) were independently associated with OHTN. Sensitivity analyses using the previous diagnostic criteria increased the estimated prevalence of EOPR to 16.5% and OHTN to 15.0.
CONCLUSIONS: Orthostatic blood pressure abnormalities were common among adults with DM in this hospital-based cohort in Cameroon. OH and OHTN were associated with different clinical factors, suggesting potentially distinct underlying mechanisms. Routine orthostatic blood pressure assessment may provide additional information for cardiovascular risk stratification in adults with diabetes, particularly in resource-limited settings.

Title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH.
METHODS: Publicly available single-cell RNA-seq data from PAH and control pulmonary vascular tissues were analyzed. A senescence-associated score was calculated for each cell based on MSigDB gene sets. Senescence-associated genes in monocytes/macrophages were identified through correlation and differential expression screening, and further examined in bulk transcriptomic datasets. Bulk transcriptomic discovery used GSE113439, GSE117261, and GSE254617. A sample-title audit identified 68 shared PHBI identifiers between GSE117261 and GSE254617; therefore, the merged data represented 257 expression profiles from 189 unique subjects. LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost were used as complementary feature-selection approaches, and genes jointly retained by the three algorithms were defined as candidates for evaluation in independent cohorts.
RESULTS: Single-cell RNA-seq identified 14 cell types in PAH pulmonary vascular tissues, with dendritic cells, T cells, and monocytes/macrophages exhibiting the highest senescence-associated scores. Integrative screening identified 405 senescence-associated genes enriched in monocytes/macrophages. Multi-algorithm screening prioritized 10 candidate genes for subsequent evaluation. After within-cohort multiple-testing correction, external cohort analyses reproduced the discovery-stage expression directions for RGS1, PHLDA1, MAFB, and RNF13 in lung tissue cohorts, and for MAFB in a PBMC cohort. With nominal P values, RGS1 was significantly upregulated in GSE48149 and GSE53408 (both lung), and PHLDA1 was upregulated in GSE48149 (lung). MAFB was significantly downregulated in GSE33463 (PBMC) and GSE48149 (lung), whereas RNF13 was downregulated in GSE15197 and GSE48149 (both lung). Functional analysis revealed significant enrichment of immune-inflammatory and phagocytosis-related pathways among the candidate genes. Consensus clustering based on the candidate genes classified PAH patients into two exploratory transcriptomic groups with distinct expression and pathway activity profiles. In vivo evaluation in an MCT-induced PAH rat model showed seven significant direction-consistent changes, two direction-consistent nonsignificant trends, and one discordant gene (PDE4B), supporting tissue-level expression concordance.
CONCLUSION: These analyses identify a Mono.Macs-associated senescence-related candidate gene set in PAH. Independent expression analyses provide additional support for RGS1, PHLDA1, MAFB, and RNF13 as candidate genes for subsequent mechanistic and functional validation.

Title: Conduit type is associated with distinct fibrin-mediated coagulation trajectories following lower extremity bypass.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prosthetic and autogenous vein conduits used in lower extremity bypass differ in biologic composition and thrombogenic potential, but their influence on postoperative coagulation remains poorly understood. Postoperative antithrombotic strategies following bypass remain largely empiric. We aimed to determine whether the choice of conduit is associated with distinct longitudinal postoperative coagulation trajectories that may inform conduit-specific antithrombotic strategies.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study evaluated patients undergoing lower extremity bypass with serial perioperative thromboelastography with platelet mapping assessment and stratified according to conduit type: prosthetic or autogenous vein conduit. Longitudinal coagulation trajectories were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts for patients. Fixed effects included postoperative time point, conduit type, antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulation regimen, and time-by-conduit interaction terms.
RESULTS: A total of 338 longitudinal thromboelastography with platelet mapping measurements were obtained from 81 patients undergoing lower extremity bypass, including 59 (72.8%) receiving prosthetic conduit and 22 (27.2%) receiving autogenous vein conduit. Adjusted mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant time-by-conduit interaction for citrated functional fibrinogen maximum amplitude (P = .048), indicating differing postoperative fibrin-mediated clot strength trajectories according to conduit type. Prosthetic conduit recipients demonstrated an earlier postoperative rise in citrated functional fibrinogen maximum amplitude, peaking around postoperative day 4, whereas vein conduit recipients demonstrated a later peak around postoperative day 5.
CONCLUSIONS: Conduit type was associated with distinct postoperative coagulation trajectories following lower extremity bypass, with the principal conduit-associated differences observed in fibrin-mediated clot-strength trajectories. These findings should be considered hypothesis generating and suggest that postoperative coagulation physiology may differ according to conduit type and support further investigation into whether conduit-specific coagulation phenotypes can inform individualized antithrombotic strategies.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Postoperative antithrombotic management following lower extremity bypass remains largely empirical despite well-recognized differences in thrombogenicity between prosthetic and autogenous vein conduits. In this prospective longitudinal study, conduit type was associated with distinct fibrin-mediated coagulation trajectories during early postoperative recovery, with prosthetic conduit recipients demonstrating an earlier rise in citrated functional fibrinogen maximum amplitude than autogenous vein conduit recipients. These findings suggest that postoperative coagulation physiology may differ according to conduit type and raise the possibility that the relative contributions of platelet- and fibrin-mediated coagulation differ across conduit types. They provide a biologic rationale for future studies evaluating whether conduit-specific coagulation phenotypes identified by serial thromboelastography with platelet mapping are associated with graft-related outcomes and can inform individualized antithrombotic strategies.

Title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR.
METHODS: A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regression identified five independent clinical predictors: age, hemoglobin, albumin, maximum aneurysm diameter, and diabetes. The clinical model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.917 in the internal cohort and 0.944 in the external cohort. From the 3D ResNet200 network, 32 DL features were extracted. LASSO regression further selected two of these features. The ensemble predictive model, which integrated the clinical predictors and DL features, demonstrated improved discrimination, with an AUC of 0.971 in the internal cohort and 0.958 in the external cohort. Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.911 for the clinical model and 0.966 for the ensemble model. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent model performance across age and diabetes strata, while performance in the female subgroup warrants further evaluation in larger cohorts.
CONCLUSION: This study developed an ensemble predictive model to predict PLOS following EVAR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination and provided significant prognostic value beyond clinical variables alone. This nomogram may serve as a preoperative tool for risk stratification and resource planning in this population. Future studies should focus on prospective validation and clinical integration.

Title: LDL-C target attainment and risk of revision following knee and hip replacements: real-world evidence from a target trial emulation study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hyperlipidaemia is common in knee and hip replacement patients, with nearly half untreated. Elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) has been associated with postoperative pain and prosthetic joint infections; however, the impact of LDL-C lowering on revision surgery remains unclear. We aimed to examine the association between pragmatic LDL-C management strategies, operationalized according to LDL-C target attainment during the 1-year grace period, and the risk of revision among patients with hyperlipidaemia undergoing knee and hip replacement.
METHODS: Using The Health Improvement Network database, we identified knee and hip replacement patients with hyperlipidaemia aged 40 years or older initiating LDL-C-lowering medications. We emulated a hypothetical target trial to compare the 5-year revision risk between pragmatic LDL-C management strategies, with adherence to the goal-based strategy operationalized as having an LDL-C level <3 mmol/L during the 1-year grace period.
RESULTS: Among 28,756 qualified participants, the 5-year revision risk was lower in those achieving the target LDL-C level (2.35%) compared to those not achieving it (2.76%), with a risk difference of -0.41% (95%CI: -0.72% to -0.09%), and a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.74 (95%CI: 0.61 to 0.90). For knee replacement revision, the 5-year risk difference was -0.47% (95%CI: -0.91% to -0.09%), with an HR of 0.69 (95%CI: 0.51 to 0.92). For hip replacement revision, the 5-year risk difference was -0.28% (95%CI: -0.80% to 0.20%), with an HR of 0.80 (95%CI: 0.63 to 1.01).
CONCLUSION: Adherence to a goal-based LDL-C management strategy, operationalized as having an LDL-C level <3 mmol/L during the 1-year grace period, was associated with a lower risk of revision surgery among patients with hyperlipidaemia undergoing joint replacement, especially after knee replacement.
THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS ARTICLE: This study highlights postoperative lipid management as a potentially modifiable component of joint replacement care. If confirmed in future prospective studies, strategies to achieve guideline-recommended LDL-C targets may be considered as part of routine postoperative management to potentially improve long-term outcomes following joint replacement.

Title: Association of hepatic steatosis with atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: A hospital-based case-control study from India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis, a recognised manifestation of systemic metabolic dysfunction, remains incompletely characterised in terms of its independent association with clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), particularly in South Asian populations where prior studies have relied on surrogate markers.
AIM: To evaluate the association of objectively quantified hepatic steatosis with clinical ASCVD events in an Indian cohort.
DESIGN: Hospital-based, frequency-matched (age, sex, BMI) case-control study.
METHODS: 165 ASCVD cases and 165 controls were evaluated. Hepatic steatosis was quantified by vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE; FibroScan®) and examined for its independent association with ASCVD using multivariable logistic regression after adjustment for established cardiovascular risk factors. Dose-response relationships and phenotype-specific associations were additionally assessed.
RESULTS: Hepatic steatosis, modelled as a continuous CAP exposure, was independently associated with ASCVD (aOR 2.02 per 1-SD increase; 95% CI 1.48-2.75; p < 0.001), an association concentrated above an empirically-identified threshold of 260 dB/m (no association below this level, p = 0.73; strong association above it, p < 0.0001). Consistent with this, only severe steatosis (S3, ≥280 dB/m) was independently significant on categorical analysis (aOR 5.13; 95% CI 2.45-10.73; p < 0.001); mild and moderate grades were not. The association was predominantly driven by acute coronary syndrome; analyses for cerebrovascular accident and peripheral artery disease were limited by sample size. Unmatched cardiometabolic risk factors - diabetes, hypertension, smoking, and dyslipidaemia - behaved as expected, supporting model validity; age, sex, and BMI, the matched variables, showed the attenuated associations expected under frequency matching.
CONCLUSION: VCTE-defined hepatic steatosis is independently associated with major ASCVD events in a severity-dependent manner in an Indian cohort. The observed association was primarily driven by ACS; CVA and PAD showed numerically elevated but non-significant associations and require validation in adequately powered cohorts. The association was concentrated at severe steatosis, consistent with a threshold rather than a linear dose-response effect. Given the cross-sectional design, temporal precedence between steatosis and ASCVD cannot be established. These findings suggest hepatic steatosis assessment may merit consideration within cardiovascular risk evaluation, particularly in high-risk South Asian populations, pending validation in prospective cohorts.

Title: Sex-based differences in the management and outcomes of oesophageal fistula following atrial fibrillation ablation: a subanalysis of the worldwide POTTER-AF study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Oesophageal fistula (OF) is a rare but life-threatening complication of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Data on sex-related differences in its management and outcomes are limited.
