METHODS AND RESULTS: The PrOgnosis following oesophageal fisTula formaTion in patients undergoing cathetER ablation for AF study is a global, multicentre study evaluating the incidence, management, and outcome of OF following AF ablation. Among 553 729 patients treated across 214 centres in 35 countries between 1996 and 2022, 138 developed OF. Sex-specific data on management and outcome were available in 117 cases and are analysed herein. Females comprised 47% of the analysed cohort. Baseline characteristics, ablation modality, and use of oesophageal temperature monitoring were not different between sexes in patients developing OF. Fewer women received proton pump inhibitors post-procedure (64.8% vs. 84.7%; P = 0.017). Among patients with OF, less women developed atrio-OF (90.9% vs. 100%; P = 0.021). Oesophageal perforation and oesophageal-pericardial fistula occurred exclusively in females. The median duration until symptoms onset was 20 days for women and 16.5 days for men (P = 0.14). Echocardiography was more frequently used in women (36.4% vs. 15%; P = 0.01). Stroke was more common in women (32.7% vs. 14.8%; P = 0.040), however only before adjusting for potential cofounders. Other complications were comparable. Women underwent endoscopic therapy more often (35.8% vs. 17.7%; P = 0.034) and surgical treatment alone less frequently (28.3% vs. 51.6%; P = 0.014). Fatality rates were high and not different (63.6% in women vs. 67.2% in men; P = 0.70).
CONCLUSION: While OF incidence for each sex could not be calculated, nearly half of all patients with OF were female. Women underwent more often endoscopic and less often surgical interventions; outcomes were comparable.

Title: Robot-assisted aspiration improves survival over conservative treatment in critical primary brainstem hemorrhage: a multicenter, volume-stratified cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal management of critical primary brainstem hemorrhage (PBSH, hematoma volume 5-15 mL) remains controversial. While minimally invasive surgery shows promise, multicenter evidence-particularly stratified by hematoma volume-is lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the survival benefit and safety of frameless robot-assisted aspiration compared to conservative treatment in patients with critical PBSH.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study involving 79 consecutive patients [Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) 3-8] admitted to three neurosurgical centers between May 2022 and October 2025. Patients were allocated to a robot-assisted aspiration group (n = 38) or a conservative care group (n = 41). Further stratification was performed based on initial hematoma volume (5-10 mL, n = 63; >10 mL, n = 16). Volumetric measurements were performed by two independent neurosurgeons blinded to outcomes, demonstrating excellent inter-rater reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.96). Primary outcomes included 30-day and 90-day survival rates, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards regression. To rigorously control for potential treatment selection bias inherent in a retrospective cohort design, a 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) sensitivity analysis was additionally performed.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, including age, GCS score, and hemorrhage location, were comparable between groups. Safety profiles, including rebleeding (7.89% vs. 4.88%) and intracranial infection rates, were similar (all p > 0.05). In the overall cohort, the robot-assisted aspiration group exhibited a significantly higher 30-day survival rate (76.3% vs. 43.9%, p = 0.006). Stratified analysis revealed that the survival benefit was confined to the 5-10 mL subgroup, where robot-assisted aspiration significantly improved 30-day (82.1% vs. 45.7%, p = 0.004) and 90-day survival (71.4% vs. 42.9%, p = 0.044), alongside improved discharge GCS scores. In the >10 mL subgroup (n = 16), 30-day survival was 60.0% (6/10) vs. 33.3% (2/6) - an absolute difference of +26.7 percentage points (95% CI: -19.9 to +59.8; Fisher's exact p = 0.61; post-hoc power 0.28). This subgroup was underpowered and the result is inconclusive rather than negative. Multivariable Cox regression confirmed robot-assisted aspiration as an independent protective factor (hazard ratio = 0.494, 95% CI: 0.245-0.997, p = 0.049), reducing mortality risk by 50.6%. In the PSM sensitivity cohort (34 matched pairs; 68 patients in total), robot-assisted aspiration still showed a significant survival benefit, reducing the risk of 90-day death by 60.0% (adjusted HR = 0.400, 95% CI: 0.195-0.822, p = 0.013). Volume stratification confirmed significant surgical benefits with respect to both survival and neurological function in the 5-10 mL subgroup (90-day survival rate: 73.1% vs. 32.1%, p = 0.003; distribution of mRS grades: p = 0.034), whereas the outcomes of the two treatment groups converged in the >10 mL subgroup (37.5% vs. 33.3%, p = 1.000).
CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted aspiration is a safe intervention for critical PBSH and is associated with improved survival over conservative care - an association that persisted after propensity score matching - particularly within the 5-10 mL volume window. In hematomas larger than 10 mL the study was inconclusive: the point estimates favored aspiration but the subgroup was underpowered (n = 16; n = 14 after propensity score matching) and the confidence intervals included no benefit. Long-term functional outcomes were dominated by severe disability or death in both treatment arms regardless of volume. These findings suggest-rather than prove-a volume-dependent therapeutic window, underscoring the need for prospective validation to guide stratified neurocritical care.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: RAAS Inhibitors for the Primary Prevention of CKD in Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefits of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors in people with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are well established, although their effects in people with diabetes without CKD have yet to be fully characterized.
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the effects of RAAS inhibitors on the development of CKD in people with diabetes without CKD.
DATA SOURCES: Searches were conducted in PubMed and Cochrane CENTRAL from inception through October 2025.
STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of RAAS inhibitors versus placebo in people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes without baseline CKD. Outcomes were incident albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio [UACR] ≥30 mg/g) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, slopes, and mean change).
DATA SYNTHESIS: Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and heterogeneity was assessed using I 2. Certainty of evidence was assessed following the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Fifteen RCTs were identified, nine for type 2 diabetes (majority of participants had hypertension) and six for type 1 diabetes (all participants were normotensive). RAAS inhibitors reduced the risk of incident albuminuria in type 2 diabetes (18,938 participants; risk ratio [RR] 0.83 [95% CI 0.76-0.91]; I 2 = 13%; high certainty) but not in type 1 diabetes (4,047 participants; RR 0.98 [95% CI 0.66-1.47]; I 2 = 50%; moderate certainty). Evidence on eGFR decline was limited, with no clear effects in type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
CONCLUSIONS: RAAS inhibitors prevent incident albuminuria in people with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, although effects on eGFR are unclear. No benefits were observed in people with type 1 diabetes and normotension.

Title: Comparative Effectiveness of Individual DPP-4 Inhibitors on Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes With Moderate Cardiovascular Risk: A Target Trial Emulation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine kidney disease outcomes associated with dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors (DPP-4i).
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this target trial emulation, claims data from enrollees in commercial, Medicare Advantage, and traditional Medicare health plans were used to identify adults ≥21 years old with type 2 diabetes, with moderate cardiovascular risk, and without stage 3 or worse chronic kidney disease (CKD) initiating alogliptin, linagliptin, saxagliptin, or sitagliptin between 2014 and 2021. The primary outcome was a composite of incident CKD stages 3-5, kidney failure, or kidney replacement therapy. Random treatment assignment was emulated using propensity scores, estimated using the super learner ensemble method and incorporated as inverse probability of treatment weights into proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: The weighted study cohort included 3,026 individuals starting alogliptin, 38,213 starting linagliptin, 14,934 starting saxagliptin, and 115,091 starting sitagliptin. One year after treatment initiation, the primary outcome occurred in 1.4%, 2.7%, 2.2%, and 2.4% of patients initiating alogliptin, linagliptin, saxagliptin, and sitagliptin, respectively, increasing to 3.2%, 6.2%, 5.0%, and 5.4%, respectively, at 3 years. Alogliptin was associated with lower risk of stage 3 or worse CKD than linagliptin (hazard ratio [HR] 0.50; 95% CI 0.37-0.69), saxagliptin (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.45-0.86), and sitagliptin (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.42-0.79), while saxagliptin was associated with lower risk than linagliptin (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.73-0.87). Conversely, linagliptin was associated with higher risk than sitagliptin (HR 1.15, 95% CI 1.10-1.21).
CONCLUSIONS: Alogliptin was associated with lower risk of moderate-to-severe kidney disease than other DPP-4i, while linagliptin was associated with higher risk. Limitations include lack of laboratory data and potential unmeasured confounding.

Title: The diagnostic value of admission myoglobin for sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is a frequent and under-recognized complication of sepsis. Early diagnosis remains challenging. We evaluated the diagnostic value of admission myoglobin (MYO), alone and combined with NT-proBNP and the SOFA score, for SICM in patients with sepsis.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study (April 2022 to May 2024), we enrolled 158 patients with sepsis diagnosed according to Sepsis-3 criteria. Blood samples for MYO and NT-proBNP were collected within 24 h of admission; admission echocardiography was performed as soon as feasible (within 24 h whenever possible, and within 72 h in all enrolled patients); follow-up echocardiography was performed between day 7 and day 14. SICM was defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below 50% with documented reversibility. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with SICM, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, and renal function. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, internal validation by 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were performed. Model calibration was assessed by a calibration plot, the calibration intercept and slope, and the Brier score, with bootstrap optimism-corrected estimates.
RESULTS: Of 158 patients, 63 (39.9%) were diagnosed with SICM. MYO levels were significantly higher in the SICM group than in the non-SICM group (median 395.7 vs. 97.3 ng/mL, P < 0.001). In multivariate analysis adjusting for age, sex, BMI, and renal function, MYO (OR 1.061 per 100 ng/mL, 95% CI 1.008-1.115; P = 0.023) and NT-proBNP (OR 1.087 per 1,000 pg/mL, 95% CI 1.025-1.153; P = 0.005) were independently associated with SICM. The combined model (MYO + NT-proBNP + SOFA) achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.750-0.892), outperforming SOFA alone (AUC 0.743; likelihood ratio test P < 0.001); the optimism-corrected AUC after bootstrap validation was 0.812. The model was well calibrated (calibration intercept 0.00, slope 1.00; Brier score 0.173). DCA suggested potential net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.1-0.7.
CONCLUSION: Admission MYO, particularly in combination with NT-proBNP and SOFA, may assist in the early identification and diagnosis of SICM.

Title: Effect of a potassium-competitive acid blocker on the gut microbiota in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomized pilot study.
Journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are routinely used in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to prevent gastrointestinal bleeding associated with dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). However, long-term PPI use has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis. Tegoprazan, a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), may exert distinct effects on the gut microbiome. This study compared the longitudinal effects of tegoprazan and pantoprazole on gut microbiota composition in patients with angina undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study randomized 38 patients 1:1:1 to tegoprazan 50 mg once daily, pantoprazole 40 mg once daily, or no acid-suppressive therapy for 24 weeks. Five participants did not provide baseline fecal samples, and nine discontinued participation before week 24. Thus, 24 participants with paired baseline and week-24 fecal samples were included in the final analysis. Fecal samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
RESULTS: No drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in any group. Observed amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness was significantly higher at week 24 than at baseline in the overall cohort (p = 0.003) and P-CAB group (p = 0.016), whereas the Shannon index showed no significant changes. Paired PERMANOVA with permutations restricted by patient ID revealed significant differences in Bray-Curtis beta diversity between baseline and week 24 in the P-CAB group (R² = 0.070, p = 0.031) and PPI group (R² = 0.059, p = 0.008), but not in the no acid-suppressive therapy group (R² = 0.021, p = 0.691). In the formal cross-arm analysis, the treatment group-by-visit interaction was not significant for Bray-Curtis beta diversity (R² = 0.021, pseudo-F = 0.505, p = 0.270). Although nominal within-arm taxonomic changes were observed, no treatment group-by-visit interaction survived Benjamini-Hochberg correction in ANCOM-BC2.
CONCLUSION: Tegoprazan was well tolerated, with no drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding during the 24-week follow-up. Both acid-suppressive treatment groups showed modest longitudinal microbiome changes. The taxon-level findings were exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of treatment-specific differential effects. Larger, adequately powered studies are required to confirm these observations.

Title: Associations of the triglyceride-glucose index and intracranial arterial stenosis with poor functional outcome after ischemic stroke: a retrospective observational study of 712 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While intracranial atherosclerosis (ICAS) and insulin resistance (IR) often co-occur in ischemic stroke, their combined prognostic impact is unclear; we hypothesized their synergy predisposes to worse short-term outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 712 consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke. The primary outcome was poor functional status, defined as modified Rankin Scale score > 2 at 90 days. Participants were categorized according to TyG index (as a surrogate for IR) and ICAS status. Subsequent stratification based on ICAS severity (none, moderate, severe) and number of affected vessels (none, single, multiple) enabled dose-response evaluation. Subgroup analyses and interaction analyses were further performed to assess the robustness of the associations and explore potential interactive effects between TyG index and ICAS. Exploratory mediation analysis quantified the proportion of ICAS's total statistical effect on functional outcomes that could be explained via the TyG index.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis demonstrated that both elevated TyG index (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.01-1.79) and presence of ICAS (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.56) were associated with poor outcomes. Although the combination of high TyG index and ICAS showed a non-significant trend (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 0.98-3.17, p = 0.057), high TyG index significantly increased poor outcome risk in patients with severe ICAS (OR = 2.15, 95% CI: 1.13-4.09) or multiple ICAS lesions (OR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.11-4.02). The exploratory mediation analysis showed that the mediated proportion of the TyG index in the association between ICAS and poor post-stroke functional outcome was approximately 9.0% (95% CI: -0.8% to 68.2%), and this mediated effect was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: The combined assessment of the TyG index and ICAS burden shows promise for identifying stroke patients at high risk of poor prognosis.

Title: Breaking limits: rapid sea-to-summit ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) in 3 days 23 hours following normobaric-hypoxic pre-acclimatization and staged supplemental oxygen in a non-elite athlete.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Traditional ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) typically requires 40-50 days of on-mountain acclimatization. Normobaric hypoxia (NH) pre-acclimatization is a practical home-based alternative; however, no peer-reviewed case report has described a sea-to-summit Everest ascent completed in under four days by a non-elite individual without prior on-mountain acclimatization rotations.
METHODS: A 40-year-old male recreational mountaineer (baseline VO2max 40.8 ml·kg-1·min-1; BMI 30.1 kg·m-2) completed an 18-week structured NH pre-acclimatization program comprising 48 nights of hypoxic sleep (~377 h at simulated altitudes of 1,850-5,486 m; FiO2 16.7-10.5%) and 16 hypoxic exercise sessions (34 h at 3,085-6,000 m; FiO2 14.3-9.8%). Hypoxic dose was calculated as Σ[(95/SpO2 - 1) × h × 100]. During the climb, peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) and heart rate (HR) were recorded at each camp, and acute mountain sickness (AMS) was assessed using the 2018 Lake Louise Score (LLS). Supplemental oxygen (O2) was initiated at 0.5 L·min-1 at the start of the ascent from Everest Base Camp (EBC, 5,360 m) and titrated to SpO2 and symptoms up to 3.0 L·min-1 during the summit push.
RESULTS: The program yielded a combined hypoxic exposure of 411 h and a cumulative hypoxic dose of 4,779%·h (sleep 4,353%·h; exercise 426%·h). VO2max increased from 40.8 to 51.0 ml·kg-1·min-1, and body mass decreased from 118.1 to 101.5 kg. The subject departed New York at 00:30 local time (EDT; 10:15 Nepal Standard Time, NST) on 15 May 2025 and reached the summit at 09:22 NST on 19 May 2025, a total sea-to-summit time of 3 days, 23 hours and 7 minutes; the ascent from EBC to the summit took 60 hours and 22 minutes. SpO2 was 75% at Camp 3 (7,100 m; HR 95 bpm) and 70% on arrival at Camp 4 (7,950 m; HR 105 bpm) and at the summit (HR 105 bpm). On descent, SpO2 recovered to 80% at Camp 4 and 85% at Camp 2 (6,750 m; HR 110 bpm), and was 85% on room air on return to EBC (HR 62 bpm). No AMS was diagnosed during the ascent (LLS 0-1 at all ascending checkpoints); mild AMS criteria were met on descent (LLS = 3), resolving by return to EBC. No high-altitude cerebral or pulmonary edema occurred.
DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this case documents the fastest recorded sea-to-summit ascent of Mount Everest by a non-professional athlete. The combination of a structured 18-week NH pre-acclimatization program, objective physiological monitoring, and staged supplemental oxygen, together with the absence of severe altitude-related complications, suggests that rapid ascent without traditional on-mountain acclimatization may be feasible in a well-prepared, closely supervised non-elite individual. Controlled prospective studies are required to quantify the relative contributions of hematological, ventilatory, and mitochondrial adaptations induced by high-dose NH exposure.

Title: Risk factors for invasive fungal infections after kidney transplantation and the construction of a predictive model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-transplant infection is one of the main complications in the early stage of kidney transplantation. However, there is a lack of risk prediction tools to identify those at high risk of infection.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the risk factors for invasive fungal infections (IFIs) after kidney transplantation in a single center in Guangxi region and to construct a predictive model.
METHODS: A total of 997 patients who underwent kidney transplantation were selected as the research subjects. Patients with IFIs after kidney transplantation were classified into the IFIs group (n = 125), while the remaining patients formed the control group (n = 872). The clinical data of the two groups were compared, and the risk factors for IFIs after kidney transplantation were analyzed using multivariate logistic stepwise forward regression. The 997 samples were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set in an 7:3 ratio. The training set was used to build the model, while the validation set was used to evaluate the model performance.
RESULTS: Heart failure (OR = 4.235), low EOS% level (OR = 0.825), high Cr level (OR = 1.003), and low Mg + level (OR = 0.198) are independent risk factors influencing the occurrence of IFIs after kidney transplantation (all P < 0.05). Based on these four risk factors, a nomogram prediction model was constructed. The AUC of the training set was 0.654 (95% CI: 0.591-0.717), with a specificity of 59.3% and a sensitivity of 65.3%. The AUC of the validation set was 0.677(95% CI: 0.583-0.770), with a specificity of 59.0% and a sensitivity of 76.6%.
CONCLUSION: Heart failure, low EOS%, high Cr level, and low Mg level are closely related to the occurrence of IFIs after kidney transplantation. The prediction model based on these risk factors has certain predictive value.

Title: Independent correlates of vancomycin steady-state trough concentration among patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery: observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump support.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) combined with valve surgery represent a high-risk surgical population with substantial perioperative hemodynamic disturbances and highly variable organ function, leading to high variability in vancomycin pharmacokinetics. Conventional vancomycin dosing solely on renal function frequently fails to achieve target trough concentrations in this complex subgroup. This study aimed to identify independent correlates c of vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations (Css-min), and to report observational findings for intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, to inform individualized therapeutic drug monitoring.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery from January 2018 to October 2024. Clinical data and vancomycin TDM records were extracted from electronic medical records. Vancomycin Css-min was detected by enzyme-multiplied immunoassay technique. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) accounting for within-patient repeated TDM measurements were used to identify clinical correlates of Css-min. IABP support was pre-specified and force-entered into the multivariable model based on clinical observations and pathophysiological reasoning, independent of univariate screening results. We performed a sensitivity analysis for patients with at least one TDM within postoperative day 7, prespecified interaction tests for effect modification, and binary logistic-GEE for the supratherapeutic endpoint (Css-min > 20 mg/L). A two-tailed P < 0.05 was set as statistical significance.
RESULTS: A total of 283 eligible patients with 473 valid Css-min measurements were included. Multivariate GEE demonstrated that categorical vancomycin dosing regimen, age, ventilator dependence ≥96 h, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), IABP support, serum creatinine (Scr), and serum urea nitrogen (SUN) were positively associated with higher geometric-mean Css-min. Associations remained largely consistent in the sensitivity-analysis subgroup of patients with at least one early-phase TDM within postoperative day 7. A significant CRRT-by-postoperative-time interaction was detected, indicating that the influence of CRRT on vancomycin exposure varied across different postoperative phases. Of note, the association signal linking IABP to supratherapeutic trough concentrations (Css-min>20 mg/L) was modest and requires cautious interpretation.
CONCLUSION: Multiple clinical factors jointly affect vancomycin steady-state trough concentrations in patients undergoing combined CABG and valve surgery, including dosing regimen, age, renal biomarkers, and critical-care supportive interventions such as IABP, CRRT and prolonged mechanical ventilation. IABP support represents an intriguing observational signal; this finding remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation before it can guide formal dose-adjustment strategies. Individualized vancomycin management for this population should comprehensively integrate hemodynamic support measures and laboratory indices rather than depend merely on renal-function markers. This study focuses on clinically accessible trough concentration monitoring rather than constructing complex pharmacokinetic models, which is more in line with real-world clinical practice.

Title: Reevaluating hypercoagulability in the portal vein and the impact of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt on platelet activation in cirrhosis.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In liver cirrhosis, dysregulated hemostasis predisposes patients to both hemorrhagic and thrombotic complications. The portal vein (PV) is a frequent site of thrombosis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Whether the PV constitutes a locally hypercoagulable environment remains controversial, as previous studies have reported conflicting findings regarding portal venous platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction, and coagulation factor alterations.
METHODS: We enrolled 34 patients with liver cirrhosis undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) implantation. Platelet count, activation, and reactivity were assessed by flow cytometry before and after TIPS, as well as across multiple vascular compartments, including the PV, superior mesenteric vein, hepatic vein, and peripheral vein. In addition, we measured key coagulation factors involved in secondary hemostasis in the indicated vessels.
RESULTS: Platelet counts declined with advancing liver disease, but no changes in platelet activation or reactivity were observed. Despite elevated platelet counts in the PV, we found no evidence of increased platelet activation or reactivity. Moreover, no compartment-specific differences were detected in the selected conventional coagulation parameters assessed, except for lower fibrinogen levels in the PV compared with the hepatic vein. TIPS implantation did not lead to a short-term increase in platelet activation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, we found no evidence of increased portal venous platelet activation or reactivity. Apart from lower fibrinogen levels in the PV compared with the hepatic vein, the selected conventional coagulation parameters assessed did not show consistent compartment-specific differences. These findings do not support the concept of a PV-specific hypercoagulable state as assessed by the present platelet activation and reactivity measures and selected coagulation assays. Rather, they suggest that relief of portal hypertension and reduction of venous stasis may be more relevant for thrombosis risk than changes in platelet activation alone.

Title: Admission-based predictors of in-hospital AKI in HFrEF: a single-centre retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct and internally validate a concise prediction model for in-hospital acute kidney injury (AKI) among patients admitted with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The model was limited to information available at hospital presentation.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,071 HFrEF hospitalizations at the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University from September 2020 to September 2022. The outcome was incident AKI during the index admission, defined using a modified KDIGO (48-h serum creatinine) criterion, based on an increase of ≥26.5 µmol/L within 48 h. Candidate variables measured at admission were screened with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression using the 1-SE rule. Bootstrap stability and clinical parsimony were then considered to preserve temporal validity and bedside usability. Internal validation was performed using 5-fold stratified out-of-fold cross-validation.
RESULTS: In-hospital AKI occurred in 118 of the 1,071 patients (11.0%). Five key on-admission clinical parameters were identified as the strongest predictors: age, furosemide-equivalent dose, hypotension on presentation, RDW, eGFR. In internal validation, the combination of these five strictly admission-based parameters achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.81 [95% bootstrap confidence interval (CI): 0.77-0.85], a precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC) of 0.47, a Brier score of 0.08, a calibration intercept of -0.02, and a calibration slope of 0.98. Decision curve analysis demonstrated clinical utility with a positive net benefit across most clinically plausible decision thresholds.
CONCLUSION: A five-predictor model based entirely on admission data can provide interpretable early risk stratification for in-hospital AKI in patients hospitalized with HFrEF. By excluding post-admission treatment responses and weight change, the model reduces reverse-causality bias and may support renal safety decisions at the time of presentation.

Title: Clinical study of isokinetic training with joint control tasks on lower limb function in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment: a preliminary randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of isokinetic training with joint control tasks on lower limb proprioceptive and motor function in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment.
METHODS: A randomized controlled trial design was adopted. Stroke patients with proprioceptive dysfunction who were admitted to the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University, between April 2025 and November 2025 were prospectively and consecutively enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to an experimental group or a control group using a random number table. Both groups received conventional rehabilitation for 4 weeks, while the experimental group additionally underwent isokinetic training with joint control tasks during the same intervention period. General demographic and clinical data were collected. Before and after intervention, proprioception, motor function, and activities of daily living (ADL) were assessed.
RESULTS: Based on the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 58 eligible patients were finally enrolled and randomly allocated into two groups (29 patients per group). Within-group comparisons showed that both groups exhibited significant post-intervention improvements in proprioceptive function, motor function, and activities of daily living (ADL) (all P < 0.05). In the control group, the Modified Nottingham Sensory Assessment (NSA), Joint Position Reproduction (JPR) tests at 30°, 45°, and 60°, Threshold to Detect Passive Motion (TTDPM), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the lower extremity (FMA-LE), and Modified Barthel Index (MBI) scores all improved significantly compared with baseline (P < 0.05). Similarly, in the experimental group, all aforementioned indicators demonstrated significant improvements after intervention (P < 0.05). Between-group comparisons revealed that improvements in proprioceptive, motor, and ADL functions were significantly greater in the experimental group than in the control group. Specifically, the changes in NSA, JPR (30°, 45°, 60°), and TTDPM scores were significantly higher in the experimental group (P < 0.05). Furthermore, the experimental group exhibited larger gains in BBS and FMA-LE scores (P < 0.05), as well as greater improvements in MBI scores (P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Isokinetic joint control training combined with conventional rehabilitation was associated with improvements in proprioceptive function, lower-limb motor performance, and activities of daily living in stroke patients with proprioceptive impairment. These findings suggest that this approach may serve as a useful adjunct to stroke rehabilitation; however, further studies with more rigorous designs are required to confirm these results.

Title: Effects of RhBNP combined with immune modulation on immune function and short-term clinical outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation and heart failure.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexist, sharing underlying pathophysiology and risk factors, which leads to high morbidity and complex clinical management. While recombinant human B-type natriuretic peptide (rhBNP) is used for acute HF, its combined effect with traditional Chinese medicine for immune regulation in HF patients with persistent AF remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and immunological impact of rhBNP combined with an immunomodulatory therapy in patients with HF and permanent AF.
METHODS: In this randomized, prospective, controlled trial, 40 hospitalized patients with HF (NYHA class II-III, LVEF ≤40%) and permanent AF were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to receive conventional therapy alone (Control group, n = 20) or conventional therapy plus intravenous rhBNP and oral Zhenqi Fuzheng Granules for 7 days (Treatment group, n = 20).
RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the treatment group showed significantly greater reductions in BNP levels and greater improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Immunophenotyping analysis revealed that the treatment group had significantly increased absolute counts of CD3+ and CD4+ T lymphocytes and a higher CD4+/CD8+ ratio.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive therapy combining rhBNP and immunomodulation in HF-AF patients significantly improves cardiac function, and is associated with improved short-term clinical outcomes. This suggests a promising multi-mechanistic therapeutic approach for this patient population.

Title: Comparative risk assessment of cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes using cystatin C and creatinine in DECLARE-TIMI 58.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between cystatin C and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes is not well explored in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and normal or mild kidney dysfunction.
METHODS: This nested prospective biomarker study included patients enrolled in DECLARE-TIMI 58. Participants were categorized into quartiles of CysC/creatinine and eGFRCysC/eGFRCr and classified according to Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) risk categories. Hazard ratios were estimated for a composite of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure (CVD/HHF), major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and a kidney-specific composite outcome (persistent ≥40% decrease in eGFR, end-stage renal disease, or renal death).
RESULTS: Among 1899 placebo-treated patients, higher baseline CysC was associated with higher risk for CVD/HHF, MACE, and the kidney-specific composite outcome. A gradient of risk across quartiles was observed for CVD/HHF [Q4 v Q1: 1.33 (0.98-1.80), p-trend = 0.016]; MACE [1.34 (1.06-1.69), p-trend = 0.013]; and kidney-specific composite outcome [1.95 (0.95-3.99), p-trend = 0.036]. When compared with creatinine, CysC showed more pronounced and statistically significant risk gradients (CVD/HHF: KDIGO-CysC p-trend < 0.001 vs. p-trend Cr 0.34; MACE: CysC p-trend < 0.001 vs. Cr p-trend 0.52). No heterogeneity was observed in the effect of dapagliflozin across CysC concentrations (p-interactions >0.05).
CONCLUSION: In patients with T2D and predominantly preserved Cr-based eGFR, CysC was associated with increased cardiovascular and kidney risk. Although discrimination assessed by c-statistic was similar for CysC and Cr, risk gradients seen with CysC became attenuated and no longer statistically significant when using Cr-based analogs. The effect of dapagliflozin was consistent irrespective of baseline CysC.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01730534.

Title: Wearable-derived sleep and circadian features associated with electronic health record-documented persistent postsurgical pain.
Abstract: A substantial percentage of surgical patients develop persistent postsurgical pain, and sleep disruption is an established, modifiable contributor. We examined temporal dynamics linking sleep and circadian rhythms to persistent postsurgical pain, using longitudinal Fitbit and electronic health record (EHR) data from the NIH All of Us Research Program to track sleep and circadian changes preceding EHR documentation of pain beyond expected surgical recovery. Patients later documented with persistent pain showed systematic shifts in wake timing and in heart rate circadian rhythms (elevated amplitude and mesor), with wake timing decoupled from heart rate circadian timing. These changes were absent in a comparison cohort without persistent pain documentation, indicating specificity to persistent postsurgical pain rather than a postoperative or clinical-encounter effect. Findings align with evidence linking altered sleep to pain outcomes and identify cardiac circadian disruption as a distinct marker, suggesting wearable-derived features could capture physiological changes before documentation and inform intervention.

Title: Oral Health-Related Adverse Events of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: As the clinical use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) continues to grow for the management of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal protection, noncirrhotic fatty liver disease, and weight management, their potential implications for oral health need to be considered.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined oral health-related adverse events (AEs) associated with GLP-1 RAs using postmarketing data from the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
METHODS: FAERS reports for available GLP-1 RAs, exenatide, liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide, and tirzepatide, were screened from their initial market introduction through December 2025, identifying 364,274 total AE reports, of which 31,195 (8.6%) involved oral, craniofacial, or dental manifestations.
RESULTS: Tirzepatide, despite being one of the most recently approved GLP-1 RAs, accounted for the highest overall AE volume, and semaglutide demonstrated the largest proportion of oral health-related AEs. A disproportionality analysis revealed a significant drug-specific signal for dry mouth of semaglutide, while vomiting, regurgitation, and reflux-related events produced a significant signal across all 5 drugs. Sensory disorders, including dysgeusia and taste disturbances, also demonstrated significant proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) and reporting odds ratios (RORs) for several GLP-1 RAs. Association analysis of AEs showed significant associations between vomiting and taste disturbances, as well as between dry mouth and dysgeusia, particularly with semaglutide and dulaglutide.
CONCLUSION: This analysis highlights emerging safety signals in oral health and underscores the need for heightened clinical awareness and prospective studies to characterize the incidence, timing, and mechanisms of oral AEs associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.Knowledge Transfer Statement:Understanding the oral adverse effects associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists allows clinicians and dental providers to more effectively counsel patients initiating or continuing these medications. By recognizing early symptoms such as dry mouth, dysgeusia, and reflux-related irritation, providers can implement targeted preventive strategies-including hydration guidance, salivary substitutes, dietary modifications, and closer oral health monitoring-to reduce complications and improve patient comfort, adherence, and overall treatment outcomes. This knowledge enhances interdisciplinary management of individuals using GLP-1 RAs.

Title: Genotype, Phenotypic Severity, and Survival in Pediatric Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Report From the Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) frequently presents with heart failure in children. Whether a genetic cause of DCM is associated with disease severity or eventual outcome in pediatric DCM is unclear.
METHODS: A multiinstitutional prospective pediatric cohort study (0-18 years) with nonsyndromic DCM was undertaken from 2013 to 2016. A panel of 37 cardiomyopathy-associated genes was interrogated by exome sequencing with analysis for pathogenic or likely pathogenic (LP) variants. Clinical severity and outcomes of death, cardiac transplant, and continuing left ventricular dysfunction versus echocardiographic normalization were assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 279 DCM probands (47% male) with a median (interquartile range) age at diagnosis of 1.6 (0.4-10.4) years were enrolled. Median follow-up was 1.1 (0.2-4.0) years. Gene variants designated as pathogenic/LP were identified in 18 of the 37 genes evaluated, and of all positive variants, TTN (17%), TNNT2 (15%), MYH7 (15%), RBM20 (9%), and LMNA (8%) were most frequently implicated. Only 19% of the overall cohort yielded an identifiable genetic cause, without any difference between ancestries. Children >12 years old had the highest genetic yield at 34% (P<0.05). Symptoms of heart failure occurred in 62% of patients who carried a pathogenic/LP gene variant, at or within 12 months of presentation, but neither heart failure symptoms, nor echocardiographic severity was associated with having a pathogenic/LP variant. The rate of death or cardiac transplant did not differ with the presence or absence of a pathogenic/LP variant and exceeded 60% by 10 years after diagnosis. On competing risks analysis, a trend (P=0.09) toward greater echo normalization, was noted in those without a pathogenic/LP variant by 10 years after diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: A genetic cause was detected in a minority of children and was not associated with the phenotypic severity of DCM at diagnosis. Echocardiographic normalization of left ventricular function over time was noted more frequently in patients who did not have an identified pathogenic/LP variant.

Title: [Total coronary revascularization in elderly and senile patients. Rationale for the surgical approach.].
Abstract: With increasing life expectancy and the rising prevalence of coronary artery disease among elderly and senile patients, the need to optimize surgical methods of myocardial revascularization is growing. Traditional coronary artery bypass grafting via median sternotomy remains the standard of care for multivessel coronary artery disease; however, in elderly and senile patients, it is often associated with an elevated risk of perioperative complications, including infectious complications, respiratory failure, stroke, cognitive dysfunction, and prolonged recovery time. In this context, minimally invasive myocardial revascularization techniques through a left anterolateral minithoracotomy are attracting increasing interest. This analytical review compares outcomes following minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting and sternotomy-based coronary artery bypass grafting with complete myocardial revascularization in elderly and senile patients. The technical features of the approach are discussed, and an analytical review of its efficacy, safety, advantages, and prospects for use in this patient cohort is provided.

Title: [Markers of metabolic and mitochondrial stress in atherosclerosis in elderly and senile individuals.].
Abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate the association between markers of metabolic stress (FGF21, GDF15, and lactate) and mitochondrial stress (p-AMPK, PGC-1α, and PINK1) and clinically significant atherosclerosis in elderly and senile individuals. This pilot comparative cross-sectional study included 310 patients aged 60-89 years. There were 162 patients with clinically verified atherosclerosis and 148 controls without clinically manifested or hemodynamically significant atherosclerotic lesions according to the available clinical and instrumental assessment. Serum levels of FGF21, GDF15, and lactate were measured using enzyme immunoassay and biochemical methods. The expression of p-AMPK, PGC-1α, and PINK1 was assessed by immunocytochemistry of buccal epithelial cells as a non-invasive model of the systemic cellular stress response. In patients with atherosclerosis, there were higher serum levels of FGF21, GDF15, and lactate, lower expression of p-AMPK and PGC-1α, and higher expression of PINK1 compared with age-matched control subgroups (p<0,001). There were the most pronounced changes in patients aged 75-89 years with atherosclerosis. In this subgroup, there were the strongest correlations between FGF21 and PINK1 (r=0,67), GDF15 and p-AMPK (r=-0,61), and FGF21 and PGC-1α (r=-0.63; p<0,001). In multivariable models, there was an independent association between reduced PGC-1α expression and increased FGF21 and GDF15 levels, older age, lower eGFR, type 2 diabetes, and higher BMI. There was also an independent association between increased PINK1 expression and GDF15, lactate, older age, lower eGFR, type 2 diabetes, and higher BMI. In elderly and senile individuals, clinically significant atherosclerosis is associated with a more pronounced profile of metabolic and mitochondrial stress. There are potential research indicators of vascular-metabolic aging among the studied markers; however, their clinical application requires further validation in prospective studies accounting for comorbidity, kidney function, inflammation, and pharmacotherapy.

Title: Long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes in type 2 diabetes: final results of the prospective DM-FibroScan Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: International guidelines recommend routine liver assessment in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), but the long-term clinical implications remain unclear. We aimed to characterise the long-term hepatic and extrahepatic outcomes across the vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) spectrum in T2D.
METHODS: The prospective DM-FibroScan Study consecutively enrolled adults with T2D in Hong Kong during 2013-2014. Baseline controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) were assessed.
RESULTS: 1,862 patients were followed for a median of 11.9 years (interquartile range 11.5-12.1). The 10-year cumulative incidence of liver-related events (LREs) was 1.1% (95% CI 0.7-1.7), lower than those of all cause mortality (21.1% [19.2-22.9]), cardiovascular events (12.5% [11.0-14.2]), malignancies (9.7% [8.3-11.1]), and end-stage kidney disease (9.0% [7.7-10.3]). Most participants (84.2%) had baseline LSM <10 kPa and a low LRE incidence (0.4 [0.1-0.8] per 1,000 person-years), with cardiovascular events predominated (14.1 [12.2-16.2] per 1,000 person-years). Patients with LSM >15 kPa (5.3%) exhibited a markedly higher LRE incidence (12.2 [6.1-21.8] per 1,000 person years), approaching the incidences of malignancies and ESKD. LRE incidence per 1,000 person-years was 1.9 in patients with LSM regression (≥10 to <10 kPa) and 28.0 in those with persistently elevated LSM. Patients with elevated baseline LSM also showed higher incidences of extrahepatic outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: LREs were relatively uncommon in the overall T2D population but increased substantially with advanced fibrosis. This study provides natural history data across the VCTE spectrum in a relatively unselected T2D cohort and supports integrating fibrosis assessment into routine T2D care.

Title: Catheter-related complications in children with burns: A retrospective clinical study on 103 central venous access devices.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Central venous access devices (CVADs) are often indispensable for treating burns in children. Early and late complications related to CVAD placement may result in prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity and mortality, and increased cost of care.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study describes catheter-related outcomes in children with burns who underwent CVAD insertion and were managed with standardized insertion and maintenance practices. The primary outcome was the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI), expressed per 1000 catheter days.
RESULTS: A total of 103 CVADs in 81 patients admitted to our pediatric burn unit (mean age 5.1 years, mean TBSA 22.3%) were analyzed: 39 centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs), 47 femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs), and 17 peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs). All CVADs were non-valved, non-cuffed, power-injectable polyurethane catheters; 84.5% were tunneled. The median dwell time was 18.3 days, for a total of 1883 catheter days. The incidence of CRBSI was 1.1 episodes per 1000 catheter days. Unscheduled removal due to catheter-related complications occurred in 11.7% of CVADs. No symptomatic catheter-related thrombosis was reported.
CONCLUSIONS: In children undergoing CVAD placement as a part of burn care, catheter-related complications were infrequent in this cohort managed with a standardized insertion and maintenance approach. These descriptive findings could serve as a basis for future prospective studies.

Title: Association between migraine and angiogenic biomarkers in women with suspected or confirmed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
Journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
Abstract: AimMigraine is associated with increased odds of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). Elevated soluble Fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1), decreased placental growth factor (PlGF), and upregulated sFlt-1/PlGF ratios are biomarkers of preeclampsia-related complications. Our primary objective was to examine the effect of migraine on sFlt-1, PlGF, and their ratio within subgroups of women with different HDP diagnoses. Our secondary objective was to evaluate the interrelationship between migraine and these biomarkers in the overall cohort with suspected or confirmed HDP.MethodsWe evaluated pregnant women with suspected or confirmed HDP in whom sFlt-1, PlGF and their ratio were measured during index pregnancy. Migraine diagnoses before/during index pregnancy were retrospectively assessed according to ICHD-3 criteria. Both, descriptive and adjusted analyses were performed, comparing women with and without migraine. For the latter analyses, linear regression analyses were conducted for the log-transformed sFlt-1 levels, PlGF levels and their ratio, while adjusting for gestational age, maternal age, and smoking status.ResultsAmong 234 women (mean age 32 years, SD = 5), 91 had (a history of) migraine. No significant association between migraine and the log-transformed biomarkers was observed in women with and without migraine across HDP groups, also when adjusting for confounding factors (adjusted estimates of the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio: β = -0.2 [95% CI: -1.0-0.6] for women with preeclampsia or hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme levels, and low platelet levels syndrome, β = -0.8 [95% CI: -2.0-0.4] for gestational hypertension, and β = -0.1 [95% CI: -0.7-0.4] for those without HDP). Secondary analyses showed that, when pooling the overall study population, women with migraine had lower sFlt-1 levels and sFlt-1/PlGF ratios compared to women without migraine. Adjusted analyses in the overall study population instead showed that migraine was not associated with significant changes in log sFlt-1 levels (β = -0.2 [95% CI: -0.5-0.04]), but rather with higher log PlGFs levels (β = 0.3 [95% CI: 0.03-0.6]) and lower log sFlt-1/PlGF ratios (β = -0.5 [95% CI: -1.0 - -0.08]).ConclusionsResults of this study do not support enhanced angiogenic imbalance by migraine status within HDP groups. As a consequence, interpretation of sFlt-1 and PlGF might not require modification according to migraine status within different HDP diagnoses. The findings observed in the overall cohort require cautious interpretation; whether migraine influences magnitude of angiogenic dysregulation warrants prospective investigation.

Title: Management strategies for right-to-left intraatrial shunt with thrombus in transit: a systematic review of 297 patients and associated mortality outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombus in transit (TIT) through a patent foramen ovale (PFO) or atrial septal defect (ASD) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition associated with paradoxical embolism. Despite advances in imaging and interventional techniques, optimal management strategies remain poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes of adult patients with TIT across right-to-left intra-atrial shunts.
DESIGN: Systematic review of published cases.
DATA SOURCES AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through March 2025 for case reports, case series, and letters describing adult patients with TIT visualized by transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography. After screening 1736 records, 278 studies reporting 297 patients were included. Two independent reviewers extracted demographic, clinical, imaging, treatment, and outcome data. Descriptive statistics were summarized, and treatment groups were compared using chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests. Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank testing assessed 120-day survival, and multivariable Cox regression was used to evaluate potential predictors of mortality.
RESULTS: A total of 297 patients from 278 studies were included. The mean age was 58.5 ± 15.8 years, and 50.2% were male. Respiratory symptoms predominated (77.7%), followed by cardiac (29.7%) and neurological (23.0%) manifestations. Provoked events accounted for 70.3% of cases, most commonly in the postoperative setting. Thrombi were detected by transthoracic echocardiography in 92.1% of cases and by transesophageal echocardiography in 100%. Management strategies included surgical embolectomy (57.8%), anticoagulation (36.5%), thrombolysis (13.5%), and percutaneous aspiration (2.7%); 61.1% underwent PFO/ASD closure. Overall mortality was 8.3%. Surgical management was associated with the lowest mortality (3.0%) and the highest short-term clinical improvement (90.5%; p < 0.001). Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality (16.6% and 25.0%, respectively). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated superior 120-day survival with surgical management compared with other treatment strategies (log-rank p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox models, no independent predictors of mortality were identified.
CONCLUSION: In this largest synthesis of TIT cases to date, surgical management and PFO/ASD closure were associated with favorable short-term outcomes. Surgical intervention demonstrated the lowest observed mortality, while anticoagulation provided acceptable outcomes in selected patients. Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality. These findings support the role of definitive management and shunt closure in selected patients, although prospective studies are needed to establish standardized treatment strategies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (INPLASY) (Registration number: INPLASY202630021).

Title: Background Histological Lesions in Aged African Green Monkeys (Chlorocebus sabaeus) From St. Kitts.
Abstract: The Caribbean African Green Monkey (Chlorocebus sabaeus) (AGM) represents a valuable nonhuman primate model for the study of age-related pathology, with an average lifespan of over 20 years. We describe histological background and common lesions in 44 aged AGMs, >15 years, 20 males and 24 females, 26 colony-born and 18 wild-caught from a primate research facility. The most frequent cardiovascular lesion was myocardial fibrosis (54.5%), characterized by multifocal myocardial fibrosis, cardiomyocyte degeneration/necrosis, lipofuscin accumulation, and frequent concurrent vascular hyalinization affecting small to medium-sized arteries across multiple organs. Chronic kidney disease was highly prevalent, marked by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, interstitial and glomerular fibrosis, tubular degeneration, mineralization, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition; unique renal findings included intratubular iron concretions with foreign body reactions. Hepatic lesions were dominated by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration and widespread hemosiderosis, indicating systemic iron overload. In the respiratory system, silica-laden macrophages (SLM) were the most common finding, alongside diverse forms of pneumonia and occasional cryptogenic organizing pneumonia. Additional aging-related changes included adrenal nodular hyperplasia, uterine pregnancy-associated vascular remodeling (PAVR) (uterine hyaline deposits), and Sarcocystis infection in skeletal muscle. This retrospective, descriptive study provides initial data on age-related background histopathology in the aged AGM.

Title: Risk Factors and Predictive Model for In-Stent Restenosis After PCI in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: A Retrospective Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in true bifurcation coronary lesions can lead to repeat revascularization and adverse outcomes.
AIMS: To identify independent risk factors for ISR in patients with coronary bifurcation lesions undergoing PCI and to develop a predictive model for ISR-free survival.
METHODS: Patients with coronary artery disease and Medina coronary bifurcation lesions was analyzed. Baseline characteristics, laboratory values, bifurcation anatomy, and PCI details were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify independent predictors of ISR and its performance was evaluated Model interpretability was explored with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and a nomogram was constructed for clinical use.
RESULTS: Univariate analysis showed lesion/procedural factors were strongly predictive. Multivariable Cox analysis identified use of a drug-coated balloon in the side branch and side-branch stenting with a drug-eluting stent as the top independent predictors of ISR. Lesion location in the left circumflex was associated with higher ISR risk The Cox model Calibration plots showed close agreement between predicted and observed ISR probabilities. A SHAP analysis confirmed the direction and relative importance of each predictor, enhancing the model's interpretability.
CONCLUSIONS: In true bifurcation PCI, Side-branch interventions are associated with higher ISR risk, whereas a simple single-stent approach confers lower risk. The developed Cox-based nomogram demonstrated robust ability to predict ISR, which can aid clinicians in risk stratification and personalized management. Early identification of high-risk patients may enable closer surveillance or preventive measures to improve long-term outcomes after bifurcation PCI.

Title: PCSK9 and Atrial Fibrillation: A New Perspective on an Old Problem.
Abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) has emerged as a novel contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF) pathophysiology. Recent studies suggest that elevated PCSK9 levels may promote AF through multiple mechanisms, including platelet activation, oxidative stress, vascular calcification, and structural atrial remodeling. PCSK9 inhibitors such as alirocumab, evolocumab, and newer agents like inclisiran have shown potential in reducing AF incidence and cardiovascular events, particularly in high-risk populations. However, evidence from randomized controlled trials with AF as a primary clinical endpoint is limited. Further mechanistic and interventional research is warranted to establish optimized therapeutic strategies targeting PCSK9 in AF prevention and management.

Title: Early Experience of Fiber Optic RealShape Technology in Endovascular Interventions for Peripheral Artery Disease: A Prospective Single-Center Study.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interventions in peripheral artery disease (PAD) have changed significantly over the past decades. Most centers have adopted an endovascular-first strategy resulting in an increased radiation exposure, especially for the treatment team. Fiber Optic RealShape (FORS) technology uses laser light instead of fluoroscopy to visualize the specially designed guidewire and catheters. The aim of this early experience overview was to evaluate feasibility and safety of FORS-guided navigation for endovascular interventions in PAD.
METHODS: This overview presents prospectively collected, single-center data of FORS-guided PAD interventions. Feasibility was evaluated through technical success in crossing stenotic lesion(s) or occlusion(s). Lesion characteristics were also recorded. Safety was assessed by scoring of intraoperative adverse events related to FORS. Secondary assessments included navigation time, and radiation exposure outcomes (cumulative air kerma [CAK], air kerma-area product [KAP], and fluoroscopy time [FT]) during crossing of the culprit lesion.
RESULTS: In 22 patients (31 lesions) selected for FORS-guided PAD interventions, 22 of 31 lesions (71.0%) were successfully crossed while using FORS-enabled devices, without adverse events. Median length of the treated lesions was 48.0 mm (23.0-87.0). Sixteen lesions (51.6%) had a severe degree of stenosis and 10 lesions (32.3%) had a moderate degree of stenosis, defined according to the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial criteria. Navigation times, CAK, and FT were highest during FORS-guided interventions of most complex stenotic lesions.
CONCLUSION: Fiber Optic RealShape-guided navigation and lesion crossing in PAD interventions is feasible and safe. Expansion of the FORS portfolio hypothetically in combination with other radiation-reducing technologies might enable a radiation-free interventional environment in the future.Clinical ImpactFiber Optic RealShape (FORS) represents a novel technology that enables visualization of specially designed endovascular devices by utilizing laser light instead of fluoroscopy. These devices facilitate real-time visualization with three-dimensional features to simplify endovascular navigation without the necessity of using fluoroscopy during navigation. This is the first single-center study that presents an overview of 31 peripheral arterial disease (PAD) lesions (in 22 patients) showing that using FORS guided navigation in PAD interventions is safe and feasible. Ultimately, the use of FORS in combination with other radiation reducing technologies might eventually enable a radiation-free interventional environment in the future.

Title: Multiple Myeloma in Iran: National Spatiotemporal Trends, Geographic Hotspots, and Projections to 2035.
Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a malignant plasma cell disorder with a rising global burden; however, comprehensive national analyses in Iran remain limited. This study evaluated the national and provincial burden of MM in Iran, identified spatial and temporal patterns, and forecasted trends through 2035.
METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, we conducted an ecological analysis of MM incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in Iran from 1990 to 2021, by sex and province. Spatial patterns were assessed using Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi* statistics in ArcGIS. Future trends were forecast using autoregressive integrated moving average models with exogenous variables (ARIMAX).
RESULTS: In 2021, Iran recorded 767 new MM cases (ASIR: 0.98 per 100,000), 2,006 prevalent cases (ASPR: 2.41 per 100,000), and 593 deaths (ASMR: 0.79), accounting for 15,873 DALYs (ASDR: 19.38 per 100,000). Men consistently showed higher rates than women. Spatial analyses identified central-western provinces, including Isfahan, Lorestan, Tehran, Alborz, and Qazvin, as incidence and prevalence hotspots, while Zanjan and Markazi were identified as coldspots. Mortality and DALY hotspots were concentrated in Isfahan, Hamedan, Alborz, and Qom, whereas Mazandaran and Ilam showed lower burdens. Forecasts indicate continued increases by 2035, with incidence projected to reach 1.30 per 100,000 and prevalence projected to reach 3.15 per 100,000. Temporary declines during 2020-2021 likely reflected COVID-19-related disruptions in diagnosis and reporting.
CONCLUSIONS: The burden of MM in Iran is increasing and geographically unequal. Strengthening early detection, diagnostic capacity, treatment access, and region-specific cancer control strategies is essential to reduce disparities and improve outcomes.

Title: Profiling Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Specific Signatures of Homocysteine Metabolism and Mineral Homeostasis in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia.
Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The application of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) has revolutionized the management of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), rendering it a controllable disease. However, long-term administration is associated with adverse metabolic effects, particularly disruptions in homocysteine metabolism and mineral balance. A comprehensive comparison across TKI types remains absent.
OBJECTIVE: This study systematically characterized and compared the metabolic signatures elicited by first- and second-generation TKIs Imatinib, Nilotinib, and Dasatinib on homocysteine and mineral parameters in chronic myeloid leukemia.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study involved 90 stable CML patients treated with TKI therapy for at least six months at Baghdad Oncology Teaching Hospital between March 2024 and April 2025. Patients were divided into three equal groups based on their medication: Imatinib, Nilotinib, or Dasatinib. Fasting blood samples were collected and analyzed for homocysteine, PTH, calcium, potassium, creatinine, vitamin B12, and ALP. Statistical methods, including ANOVA and correlation analyses, were used to compare groups and explore drug-specific effects.
RESULTS: The three TKI groups demonstrated distinct metabolic disturbance patterns. Nilotinib was associated with the highest homocysteine levels and showed strong positive correlations with PTH and ALP. Dasatinib caused a moderate elevation in homocysteine and uniquely correlated positively with potassium. Imatinib showed the most favorable homocysteine profile, which was primarily inversely correlated with calcium. Multivariate analysis confirmed that these metabolic profiles effectively distinguished the three TKI groups.
CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrates that Imatinib, Nilotinib, and Dasatinib elicit distinct and discernible metabolic signatures. These results support the adoption of personalized, TKI-specific monitoring approaches in the management of CML, aiming to proactively reduce long-term cardiovascular and skeletal adverse effects and thereby improve alignment between the quality and duration of survival.

Title: Association of Abdominal Aortic Calcification with Pathological Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Gastric Cancer: A Retrospective Exploratory Study.
Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy is an important prognostic determinant in patients with locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC). However, reliable pretreatment biomarkers for predicting treatment response remain limited. Abdominal aortic calcification (AAC), an imaging marker of systemic atherosclerosis, can be readily assessed on routine computed tomography (CT). This study investigated the association between baseline AAC and pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with LAGC.
METHODS: This retrospective exploratory study included patients with histologically confirmed LAGC who received neoadjuvant FLOT chemotherapy followed by curative-intent gastrectomy between January 2024 and January 2025. Pretreatment CT images were reviewed to quantify AAC using the abdominal aortic calcification index (ACI). Pathological response was evaluated according to the Mandard tumor regression grade (TRG) system. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ACI and pathological response.
RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included, with a median age of 64 years, and 70.2% were male. Patients with higher ACI values were significantly older than those with lower values. ROC analysis demonstrated limited discriminatory performance of ACI for predicting pathological response. Using an optimal cutoff value of 3.28, the sensitivity and specificity of ACI were 60.0% and 60.4%, respectively. Older age, hyperlipidemia, and clinical T stage were significantly associated with poorer pathological response in univariate analyses. However, ACI was not independently associated with pathological response in multivariable logistic regression analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline AAC was not independently associated with pathological response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with LAGC. AAC may reflect host-related vascular aging rather than tumor-specific treatment sensitivity and may contribute to future exploratory risk-stratification models.

Title: Ubiquitin Protease Levels and Mitochondrial DNA Synthesis in Multiple Myeloma.
Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The deregulation of the ubiquitin system is linked to several disorders, including cancer, and is implicated in MM. The study aimed to determine serum β-catenin and UCHL1 concentration and relate it to the risk of developing MM and to assess mitochondrial DNA by RT-qPCR.
METHODS: The study was conducted in October 2023 to February 2024. The study included 20 men and 20 women diagnosed with MM  by their physicians and a total of 40 individuals who were in good health and had no prior medical history of MM . A 5 mL of blood were withdrawn from patients and controls groups.  The serum beta-catenin protein (β-catenin) , ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCHL1) were measured by ELISA and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) was assessed by qPCR.
RESULT: The results clearly showed a significant decrease in level of UCHL1, β-catenin in MM patients compared to level in control group ( P = 0.00018) . The result also showed elevated level of mtDNA synthesis in patients with MM compared to control group (P = 0.00014). Based on the research data, the patient group exhibited a significantly increase in levels of mtDNA synthesis compared to the control group (P = 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Decreased serum β -catinine and UCHL1 levels, along with an increase in mtDNA synthesis seems to have significant role in the progress of MM.

Title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires effective sedation to ensure patient comfort while preserving gas exchange, hemodynamic stability, and predictable recovery. Remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, has emerged as a potential alternative to traditional sedatives. However, its safety and efficacy compared with those of other sedatives remain under investigation. This meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of remimazolam versus dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol in adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy.
METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted using 5 databases through January 2026. Outcomes included respiratory depression, hypotension, bradycardia, time to target sedation depth, procedure success rate, emergence time, and postanesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Relative risks (RR) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: Sixteen RCTs (2325 patients) were included. Remimazolam significantly reduced respiratory depression (RR: 0.51, 95% CI: 0.36-0.73, P<0.001), hypotension (RR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.34-0.73, P<0.001), and bradycardia (RR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.65, P=0.001) versus controls. Sedation onset was faster than dexmedetomidine (MD: -2.19 min), but slower than propofol (MD: 0.49 min). Success rates were comparable across groups (RR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.98-1.28, P=0.097). Compared with dexmedetomidine and midazolam, remimazolam shortened emergence (MD: -1.79 and -4.37 min, respectively) and PACU stay (MD: -3.58 and -6.70 min).
CONCLUSION: Remimazolam provides effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with advantages in terms of respiratory and hemodynamic safety, rapid recovery, and procedural efficiency.

Title: Multidomain Polysomnographic Abnormalities in Cervical Dystonia: REM Suppression, Respiratory Instability, and Sensorimotor Dysregulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical dystonia (CD) is considered a basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and brainstem network disorder rather than an isolated focal motor disease.
OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to analyze sleep architecture, REM physiology, respiratory patterns, and sensorimotor activity in CD using full-night PSG.
METHODS: We conducted a full-night PSG case-control analysis involving 33 CD patients and 20 matched controls. Clinical scales used were Toronto Western Spasmodic Torticollis Rating Scale (TWSTRS), Craniocervical Dystonia Questionnaire (CDQ-24), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), and Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS).
RESULTS: CD patients showed greater sleep disruption than controls with significantly decreased total sleep time (TST) and reduced sleep efficiency (SE). Wake after sleep onset (WASO) was considerably higher. >70% met criteria for a study-defined severe insomnia pattern (<25% of controls). REM was absent in 42% of patients and overall REM percentage was reduced by ~70%. CD showed nearly three-fold higher apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), a significantly higher obstructive apnea index, and prolonged respiratory event duration. Periodic limb movements (PLMS) index was ~14 times higher. Spontaneous arousal rates were significantly increased. Greater motor disability (TWSTRS) correlated with decreased N3 sleep. Higher Tsui severity correlated with increased N2 sleep, linking clinical severity to altered sleep architecture. BDI correlated with higher AHI, greater respiratory event burden and obstructive apnea index. PLMS index showed strong internal coupling with PLMS arousal index and correlated with cardiac parameters.
CONCLUSION: Sleep measures may offer a useful non-invasive perspective on distributed network features associated with CD. These findings are associative and require replication in larger cohorts.

Title: Focused Ultrasound for Essential Tremor in Denmark: Results After 1 Year of Follow-Up.
Journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Essential tremor (ET) is the most common hyperkinetic movement disorder. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy (MRgFUSTh) has become an established therapy in drug-refractory tremor as one treatment option. Here, we present the results of a large cohort of MRgFUSTh-treated ET patients followed-up 1 year post-ablation.
OBJECTIVE: The primary endpoint durability of tremor reduction at 12 months at this timepoint.
METHODS: This was a single-hospital cohort study. Prior to, and 12 months after, treatment, patients were rated according to the Fahn-Tolosa-Marin (FTM) scale, Quality of Life in Essential Tremor (QUEST) scale, Patient Global Assessment of Change (PGIC), as well as general health, well-being, and factors relating to social and everyday activities. Finally, side effects and adverse event data were collected at 12 months.
RESULTS: The current cohort comprised 111 patients. Patients showed good response to MRgFUSTh with a mean decrease of 29.5 points in the total FTM-score from pretreatment (95% CI: 26.3; 32.8, P < 0.0001) corresponding to 62.4% (95% CI: 56.4%; 68.5%). This meant a reduction in the FTM-score of 13.8 points (± 5.2 points, 95% CI: 12.79; 14.73, P < 0.00001) or 85.2% (±24.2%, 95% CI: 80.70%; 89.78%) in the treated limb. For QUEST, symptoms improved by 20.9 points (95% CI: 12.1; 29.6, P < 0.0001) corresponding to a relative improvement of 54% (95% CI: 33.2%; 75.5%).
CONCLUSION: Results showed clear and persistent tremor improvements as assessed by both clinicians and patients. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

Title: Increasing use of SGLT-2 inhibitors among patients with heart failure.
Journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this quality improvement project was to identify and address barriers contributing to the underutilization of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors in eligible patients with heart failure across the health system.
METHODS: The heart failure registry was used to identify the prescription percentage of SGLT-2 inhibitors pre- and postintervention. Interventions to increase prescribing included pharmacist education to primary care providers and use of a cost information handout.
RESULTS: Following the intervention, SGLT-2 inhibitor prescription for eligible patients improved from 7.1% (n = 630) to 9.0% (n = 814), representing a relative increase of 26.8% from baseline.
CONCLUSION: A multimodal approach involving pharmacy and primary care effectively increased SGLT-2 inhibitor prescribing in patients with heart failure. Physician associates, a key part of the primary care workforce, play an important role initiating guideline-directed medical therapy.

Title: Residual SYNTAX score and optical coherence tomography-derived thin-cap fibroatheroma in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: an exploratory descriptive pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality.
