Blood was sampled within 1 h of admission. We analyzed ascorbate by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry in light-protected heparin plasma. The endpoint was pre-discharge PICU mortality. We expressed differences as Hodges-Lehmann estimates with exact 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and discrimination as the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The five principal biomarker comparisons were subjected to Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) control. We fitted no multivariable model (11 events).
RESULTS: Of the 37 children enrolled, 33 (89.2%) had septic shock, and the mortality rate was 29.7%. Non-survivors had lower plasma vitamin C concentrations (51.1 vs. 73.8 umol/L; difference -17.0, 95% CI -28.4 to -5.7, p = 0.028, q = 0.141, AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.55-0.90), and mortality declined across ascending vitamin C tertiles, although the gradient was not statistically significant (p = 0.058). No patient had hypovitaminosis C (<23 umol/L). We did not detect an association between 25(OH)D, lactate, albumin, or the LAR and mortality (all p ≥ 0.18; AUC 0.50-0.64), and the LAR was collinear with lactate (rho = 0.95). The weight-for-age z-score correlated with vitamin C (rho = 0.39, p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: In this small cohort, non-survivors had lower plasma vitamin C concentrations within the replete range in unadjusted analysis; this difference did not persist after FDR control or in the subgroup with evaluable nutritional status, and nutritional confounding cannot be excluded. No association with mortality was detected for 25(OH)D, lactate, albumin, or the LAR. These findings are hypothesis-generating, do not establish prognostic value, and require multicenter confirmation.

Title: Emergency Department Pediatric Early Warning System for Identifying Resuscitation-Defined Critical Illness in Children: A Prospective Diagnostic Classification Study in Vietnam.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Early recognition of children with severe physiological illness is essential in emergency care. The Emergency Department Pediatric Early Warning System score (ED-PEWS) has not been evaluated in Vietnam. We assessed how well ED-PEWS recorded at presentation identifies children who meet criteria for resuscitation-defined critical illness in a high-acuity pediatric emergency setting.
METHODS: This prospective observational diagnostic classification study was conducted from August to October 2022 in the emergency and resuscitation department of a national tertiary children's hospital in Vietnam. Children aged 1 month to 15 years were enrolled according to a prespecified shift-based schedule. The outcome was resuscitation-defined critical illness within 24 h (cardiac arrest or bradycardia with poor perfusion requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation). Because the timing of scoring relative to interventions and outcome was not recorded, the analysis was interpreted as concurrent classification rather than prediction.
RESULTS: Of 805 children (median age 19 months; 65.3% male), 156 (19.4%) met the outcome criteria. The median ED-PEWS was 32 (interquartile range, 24-43) in children with the outcome and 10 (8-12) in those without (p < 0.001). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.952 (95% CI, 0.926-0.977). At the exploratory Youden-derived threshold of ED-PEWS ≥ 16, there were 143 true positives, 49 false positives, 13 false negatives, and 600 true negatives; sensitivity was 91.7% (95% CI, 86.2-95.5), specificity 92.4% (90.1-94.4), and negative predictive value 97.9% (96.4-98.9).
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected high-acuity cohort, ED-PEWS showed strong concurrent discrimination for resuscitation-defined critical illness. Because the score and the outcome share physiological components and the threshold was derived and evaluated in the same dataset, these findings are exploratory and require multicenter external validation and comparison with existing triage systems.

Title: Electrocardiographic Changes Following Pediatric Adenotonsillectomy for Obstructive Sleep-Disordered Breathing: A Pilot Prospective Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Adenotonsillar hypertrophy (ATH) is the primary driver of pediatric obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (OSDB), potentially leading to cardiac remodeling. This study evaluated the impact of adenotonsillectomy (AT) on electrocardiographic (ECG) parameters and correlated these changes with sleep metrics. Methods: This prospective study evaluated ECG parameters (P-wave and QRS morphology) in children (>3 years) with symptomatic ATH before and three months after AT. A subset underwent sleep analysis via Cardiopulmonary Coupling (CPC) at both time points. Pre- and postoperative data were compared using paired t-tests and Linear Mixed Models (LMMs). The link between ECG and sleep modifications was also analyzed using Pearson and Spearman correlations of their respective variations (Δ). Results: Significant reductions were observed in the maximum RR interval (p = 0.027). Mean P-wave duration significantly shortened (84.40 ± 6.51 ms to 81.20 ± 3.32 ms; p = 0.043) and mean amplitude increased (0.076 ± 0.008 mV to 0.080 ± 0.004 mV; p < 0.001). Mean, minimum, and maximum QRS amplitudes increased significantly (p ≤ 0.018). Exploratory LMM confirmed that these modifications remained significant after adjusting for age and sex. Furthermore, post hoc analyses revealed that Δ QRS maximum amplitude exhibited negative correlations that survived false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment with Δ AHI 4% max (r = -0.727, p = 0.045), Δ ODI 3% max (r = -0.765, p = 0.045), Δ ODI 4% mean (r = -0.819; p = 0.033), and Δ maximal hypoxic burden (r = -0.730; p = 0.045). Conclusions: AT may alter ECG parameters. QRS amplitude increments correlated well with a decrease in nocturnal respiratory events. These findings may represent preliminary ECG changes associated with postoperative respiratory improvement. Larger controlled studies are needed to determine whether these ECG parameters can serve as markers of post-operative cardiopulmonary recovery.

Title: To Tap or Not to Tap? A Still Unanswered Question for Lumbar Puncture and Treatment Strategies in Asymptomatic Pediatric Papilledema: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Papilledema is a potentially vision-threatening finding in children, often diagnosed during routine ophthalmological evaluation in asymptomatic subjects, which requires prompt diagnostic evaluation to exclude intracranial pathology. The available literature suggests that a significant proportion of cases with confirmed idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) may present without headache or other manifestations of increased intracranial pressure. Current diagnostic criteria for pediatric IIH include lumbar puncture (LP) as a mandatory step following neuroimaging. However, the invasive nature of this procedure raises critical questions regarding the identification of patients who truly require this investigation. Indeed, the challenge of distinguishing true papilledema from pseudopapilledema represents the critical diagnostic prerequisite, requiring an expert pediatric neuro-ophthalmologist to ensure appropriate patient selection and avoid unnecessary tests. Evidence regarding the management of asymptomatic IIH is limited. Most published cohorts report treatment with acetazolamide despite the absence of symptoms, probably based on concerns regarding potential visual deterioration rather than prospective data. Currently, data from pediatric populations characterizing the natural history of untreated patients are lacking, and there is no consensus regarding treatment duration, tapering strategies, or long-term follow-up for this group. This narrative review summarizes the current literature on the diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for asymptomatic pediatric papilledema. It focuses on the role of lumbar puncture, the importance of differentiating papilledema from pseudopapilledema, and the uncertainties surrounding treatment decisions. Nevertheless, significant knowledge gaps persist regarding the optimal management of these patients, highlighting the need for prospective studies.

Title: Thrombotic Complications in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies: Pathophysiology, Prevention, and Clinical Management-A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Thrombotic complications represent uncommon but potentially life-threatening adverse events associated with assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs), particularly in the setting of controlled ovarian stimulation and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). The relationship between thrombophilia, infertility, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains complex and only partially understood. While antiphospholipid syndrome is a well-established acquired thrombophilic disorder associated with recurrent pregnancy loss, the association between common inherited thrombophilias and recurrent pregnancy loss is less consistent, and their contribution to primary infertility and implantation failure remains uncertain. Conversely, severe OHSS is consistently recognized as the principal treatment-related determinant of thrombotic events during IVF because of profound endothelial activation, hemoconcentration, and hypercoagulability. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation of thrombotic complications associated with assisted reproductive technologies, including deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebral venous thrombosis, upper-extremity thrombosis, splanchnic vein thrombosis, and arterial thrombotic events. Current recommendations for thromboprophylaxis, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic management are critically discussed, with particular attention to individualized risk assessment and the role of low-molecular-weight heparin in high-risk patients. Although routine thromboprophylaxis is not recommended for all women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF), careful evaluation of patient-specific thrombotic risk factors remains essential. Future prospective studies are needed to improve risk prediction, optimize preventive strategies, and establish evidence-based recommendations for women undergoing assisted reproduction.

Title: Congenital Afibrinogenemia and Hypofibrinogenemia: Genetic Basis, Pathophysiology, Laboratory Diagnosis, and Management.
Abstract: Congenital fibrinogen disorders (CFDs) comprise quantitative deficiencies-afibrinogenemia and hypofibrinogenemia-and qualitative defects-dysfibrinogenemia and hypodysfibrinogenemia. This review is confined to the quantitative disorders, and the term quantitative CFDs is used throughout in preference to the wider umbrella term; qualitative defects are considered only insofar as they must be distinguished at the bench. Afibrinogenemia results from biallelic loss-of-function variants in FGA, FGB, or FGG, and is defined by fibrinogen activity below the analytical limit of detection with undetectable antigen; hypofibrinogenemia results from monoallelic variants and is defined by a proportionate reduction in activity and antigen. Several authoritative reviews of this field have appeared recently. The contribution intended here differs in emphasis. Rather than restate the stepwise diagnostic approach, we set out what actually goes wrong at the bench: the analytical variability among fibrinogen methods, the behavior of the Clauss assay near its limit of detection, and overestimation by prothrombin time-derived fibrinogen. We also address interference from anticoagulants and sample factors, the requirement for laboratory-specific reference intervals, the interpretation of discordant results, and the molecular workflow, including copy-number analysis and the handling of variants of uncertain significance. We also address a question that the descriptive literature largely leaves open: why patients carrying identical variants, sometimes within a single family, differ so markedly in phenotype. We propose a four-layer framework-cis-acting effects at the fibrinogen locus, hepatocyte proteostasis and endoplasmic reticulum quality control, trans-acting genetic modifiers, and acquired factors-and review the evidence supporting each. Population genomic data are reconsidered: current estimates derived from gnomAD suggest that predicted-deleterious fibrinogen genotypes are considerably more frequent than clinically ascertained disease, a discrepancy that reflects incomplete penetrance and the limits of in silico prediction rather than a hidden burden of undiagnosed severe disease. Management recommendations are presented with the strength of the supporting evidence made explicit. Fibrinogen concentrate is a first-line replacement. Widely accepted targets are a peak > 1.5 g/L before major surgery, and >1.0 g/L before minor procedures; >1.0 g/L postoperatively until hemostasis, and >0.5 g/L until wound healing; and a trough ≥ 1.0 g/L in pregnancy, rising to ≥1.5 g/L peripartum. All data are derived from expert consensus, registry data, and small interventional series rather than randomized trials, and are presented here as starting points for individualized care. Paradoxical thrombosis, its uncertain mechanism, and the possibility that replacement precipitates it are treated as an unresolved problem rather than a footnote.

Title: Declining Kidney Function Is Associated with Altered Erythrocyte Membrane Fatty Acid Profiles and Estimated Enzymatic Indices.
Abstract: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) face a substantial cardiovascular burden, with altered erythrocyte membrane fatty acids (FAs) representing potential markers of adverse outcomes. However, comprehensive evaluations according to varying levels of kidney function remain limited. This retrospective pooled analysis evaluated the association between kidney function decline, erythrocyte FA profiles, and estimated enzymatic indices (surrogate product-to-precursor ratios) across eight distinct cohorts (N = 282: 33 healthy controls, 131 non-dialysis CKD, 118 end-stage kidney disease). Generalized linear mixed models accounted for inter-cohort heterogeneity with study source as a random intercept, adjusting for age, sex, diabetes, and serum albumin. With declining kidney function, erythrocyte membrane oleic acid exhibited a stepwise increase alongside an elevated elongation of very long-chain fatty acids protein 6 index, whereas linoleic acid and the stearoyl-CoA desaturase 18 index progressively decreased. Multivariable models confirmed that estimated glomerular filtration rate was an independent predictor of oleic (β = -0.012, 95% CI: -0.024 to -0.0003, p = 0.044) and linoleic (β = 0.016, 95% CI: 0.004 to 0.028, p = 0.012) acid levels. In conclusion, kidney dysfunction is independently associated with an altered membrane FA composition, characterized by an increase in monounsaturated FAs and a decline in essential polyunsaturated FAs. These findings suggest a potential link between declining kidney function and altered lipid metabolism, providing a basis for further studies exploring targeted nutritional interventions in CKD.

Title: Effects of Acute Aerobic Exercise on Sequentially Administered Cognitive Tasks Reflecting Working Memory Subcomponents and Heart Rate Variability.
Abstract: Although acute aerobic exercise selectively influences specific subcomponents of working memory, whether such benefits transfer to a subsequent cognitive task engaging a different domain remains unclear. Forty-seven participants completed, in randomized order, an exercise condition (10 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise) and a control condition, each immediately followed by a visuospatial construction task (the Equilibrio game) and a 2-Back working memory task, with heart rate variability (HRV) recorded throughout. Completion time on the Equilibrio task was significantly shorter following exercise than following control, W = 292.5, z = -2.873, p = .004, rB = -0.481. In contrast, no significant between-condition differences emerged on any behavioral parameter of the 2-Back task, including completion time, accuracy, hit rate, discrimination sensitivity (d'), and response bias (c; all ps > 0.05). During the 2-Back task, however, sympathetic indices (SNS Index, Stress Index, LF/HF ratio) were significantly elevated and parasympathetic/vagal indices (RMSSD, SDNN, PNS Index, HF n.u.) were significantly suppressed following exercise, despite unchanged behavior. These findings indicate that exercise-induced cognitive benefit is task-specific and does not extend to a subsequent task engaging a different working memory subcomponent, even as autonomic activation persists. This dissociation challenges general-arousal accounts of exercise-cognition effects and supports a domain-specific, timing-sensitive framework.

Title: Primary cardiac tumours in contemporary clinical practice: A preliminary analysis of retrospective registry.
Genetic Insights into the Comorbidity of Congenital Heart Disease and Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Focus on Copy Number Variations.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) frequently co-occur, indicating that cardiac and neural phenotypes can arise from shared developmental disturbances rather than exclusively from the physiological consequences of heart disease. Copy number variations (CNVs) provide a major genomic basis for this overlap, but their effects extend beyond changes in protein-coding gene dosage. This review synthesizes evidence from recurrent CNV syndromes, genomic cohorts, developmental studies, and experimental models to define how CNVs jointly influence heart and brain development. We examine four interconnected mechanisms: dosage alteration of pleiotropic and multiple genes, disruption of non-coding regulatory elements, remodeling of non-coding RNA networks, and reorganization of three-dimensional chromatin architecture. We further describe how developmental timing, cell-type-specific regulatory context, additional genomic variants, cardiac physiology, and clinical exposures shape incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. Together, these findings support a layered model in which a primary CNV establishes cross-organ susceptibility, whereas genetic and developmental modifiers determine whether CHD, NDD, or both become clinically manifest. Clinically, CNV diagnosis can inform neurodevelopmental surveillance, multisystem management, and genetic counseling. Genotype-first longitudinal cohorts, developmental multi-omics, parallel cardiac and neural models, and prospective clinical studies will advance individualized risk prediction and intervention.

Title: Colchicine Use Is Associated with Shorter ICU Stay and Lower FFP Transfusion Requirements After CABG.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colchicine has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular benefits in patients with coronary heart disease. However, evidence regarding its effects on postoperative inflammation and early clinical outcomes following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to evaluate the association between perioperative low-dose colchicine use and postoperative clinical outcomes, transfusion requirements, complications, and inflammatory markers in patients undergoing elective on-pump CABG.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 151 patients who underwent elective on-pump CABG: 81 received colchicine (0.5 mg once daily for 3 days preoperatively and 10 days postoperatively) and 70 did not receive colchicine in the past period. The primary clinical outcomes included ICU and total hospital length of stay, erythrocyte and fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion requirements, wound complication, and surgical revision. Postoperative day 5 laboratory parameters included C-reactive protein, white blood cell (WBC) count, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and albumin. Between-group comparisons were performed using Student's or Welch's t tests and Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, as appropriate.
RESULTS: Baseline age and sex distribution were similar between the groups. The colchicine group had a significantly shorter ICU stay than the control group (4.28 ± 1.95 vs. 5.83 ± 3.04 days; mean difference, -1.54 days; 95% CI, -2.38 to -0.71; p < 0.001). FFP transfusion requirements were also significantly lower in the colchicine group (3.49 ± 1.24 vs. 8.13 ± 3.97 units; mean difference, -4.63 units; 95% CI, -5.62 to -3.65; p < 0.001). Postoperative WBC counts were lower with colchicine (9.44 ± 3.31 vs. 10.78 ± 4.04 × 109/L; p = 0.027). Total hospital stay, erythrocyte transfusion requirements, other inflammatory parameters, wound complication rates, and surgical revision rates did not differ significantly between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative low-dose colchicine was found to be in relation with shorter ICU stays, lower FFP transfusion requirements, and reduced postoperative WBC counts following elective on-pump CABG according to this retrospective study. Prospective randomized studies are required to confirm these findings and to determine whether colchicine improves early postoperative outcomes.

Title: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing in Preoperative Assessment: From Exercise Physiology to Personalized Perioperative Care.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Major surgery imposes physiological stress requiring coordinated adaptation of the cardiovascular, respiratory, hematological, and musculoskeletal systems. Conventional preoperative assessment remains essential but may underestimate heterogeneity in physiological reserve because resting measurements incompletely capture the response to increasing metabolic demand. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) provides an integrated assessment of oxygen transport and utilization, linking pulmonary ventilation and gas exchange to cardiovascular performance and peripheral oxygen extraction. This narrative review examines the role of CPET in preoperative assessment, from prognostic testing to physiological phenotyping and personalized perioperative care. We summarize the physiological basis of key variables, including peak oxygen uptake, anaerobic threshold, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency, end-tidal carbon dioxide, breathing reserve, and exercise kinetics, and discuss how integrated interpretation can identify patterns suggestive of haemodynamic, ventilatory, pulmonary vascular, or peripheral limitations. Evidence across major surgical populations is critically appraised, with attention to isolated thresholds and the distinction between prognostic association and clinical effectiveness. The current data support selective rather than universal use of CPET, particularly when functional capacity is uncertain or physiological information may alter management. We propose a phenotype-oriented framework in which CPET findings identify potentially modifiable impairments and inform cardiovascular optimization, respiratory treatment, nutritional support, exercise training, and prehabilitation. Emerging approaches combining complex CPET, non-invasive haemodynamic assessment, wearable technologies, and artificial intelligence may enable personalized profiling, although prospective validation remains necessary. CPET should therefore be considered not simply a risk-prediction tool, but an in vivo interrogation of physiological reserve that can contribute to mechanism-oriented perioperative assessment.

Title: Development and Population-Based Prognostic Utility Assessment of an ICD-10-CM-Based Prediction Model to Identify Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction: Discrimination Performance and Population-Based Evaluation in 83,357 Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Population-based studies of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) are often limited by the lack of structured left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) data in administrative registries. We developed a logistic regression model using ICD-10-CM diagnostic codes and two clinical variables to estimate the probability of reduced LVEF (<50%) at discharge after ACS, and examined the prognostic value of the resulting classification in a large population-based cohort. The model was derived from 1596 patients with pre-discharge echocardiographic LVEF. In a 10-fold cross-validation analysis that repeated predictor selection within each train-ing fold, the procedure yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.711 (95% CI, 0.680-0.741). The fixed 28-predictor model, subsequently applied to the population-based cohort, yielded a ROC-AUC of 0.738 in the corresponding cross-validation analysis. The fixed 28-predictor model was then applied to 83,357 patients from the population-based BEAT-HF cohort (Catalonia, 2011-2021), in whom reference LVEF was unavailable. Patients classified as having reduced LVEF had a less favourable clinical profile and significantly higher rates of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Predicted reduced LVEF was associated with higher observed rates of all-cause mortality (HR 2.45, 95% CI 2.35-2.55; p < 0.001), as well as higher risks of heart failure (HF) and major adverse cardiovascular events. The model should not guide individual clinical decisions but may support exploratory population-level characterization of patients in administrative data. Validation against measured LVEF is needed.

Title: Association of the Vasoactive-Inotropic Score with Postoperative Intensive Care Unit Stay Following Arterial Switch Operation.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transposition of the great arteries (TGA) is one of the most common cyanotic congenital heart diseases in the neonatal period, and arterial switch operation (ASO) is the standard surgical treatment. Postoperative low cardiac output syndrome remains an important cause of morbidity. This study evaluated the association between serial vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) measurements and postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay in neonates with TGA undergoing ASO.
METHODS: This retrospective study included neonates with TGA who underwent ASO and were followed in a tertiary Pediatric Cardiac Intensive Care Unit between 1 August 2020, and 1 August 2022. ICU length of stay was analyzed as a continuous primary outcome. Prolonged ICU stay, defined as the upper quartile of ICU length of stay in the study cohort (≥9 days), was evaluated as a secondary exploratory outcome. VIS values were recorded at ICU admission and at 24, 48, and 72 h after surgery. Associations between VIS parameters and continuous ICU length of stay were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. ROC analysis and logistic regression were performed for prolonged ICU stay.
RESULTS: A total of 60 neonates were included, and 15 patients (25%) had a prolonged ICU stay. Admission VIS values were similar between groups. However, VIS values at 24 and 48 h were significantly higher in the prolonged ICU stay group (p = 0.005 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas no significant difference was observed at 72 h. VIS at 48 h showed the strongest correlation with ICU length of stay (Spearman's r = 0.52, p < 0.001), followed by ΔVIS48 (r = 0.48, p = 0.001) and VIS at 24 h (r = 0.44, p = 0.002). In secondary exploratory analyses, VIS at 48 h demonstrated a numerically higher AUC than VIS at 24 h (0.82 vs. 0.74). ΔVIS48 was associated with prolonged ICU stay in multivariable logistic regression (OR, 1.18 per unit increase; 95% CI, 1.05-1.33; p = 0.006). Firth's penalized logistic regression yielded a similar estimate (OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.03-1.30; p = 0.012).
CONCLUSIONS: In neonates with TGA undergoing ASO, higher VIS during the first 24-48 postoperative hours, particularly an increase from admission to 48 h, was associated with longer ICU stay. These findings support serial VIS assessment as a marker of early postoperative clinical trajectory. Cohort-derived VIS thresholds should be considered exploratory and require external multicenter validation before clinical application.

Title: Invasive Complications and Infection-Related Reconstruction in Bicuspid Versus Tricuspid Native Aortic Valve Endocarditis: A 12-Year Surgical Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detailed operative evidence comparing invasive anatomy and reconstruction between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) cases of native-valve infective endocarditis is limited. We examined the association of BAV morphology with non-leaflet invasive complications and infection-related reconstruction.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 317 adults who underwent surgery for native aortic valve infective endocarditis from 2013 through 2025 (113 BAV; 204 TAV). The primary outcome was any non-leaflet invasive complication; infection-related reconstruction was a secondary operative outcome reflecting operative management of invasive anatomy. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs), corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and marginally standardized absolute differences. Site-specific and invasive-subgroup analyses were exploratory.
RESULTS: Patients with BAV were younger, more frequently male, and had a lower comorbidity burden. Non-leaflet invasive complications occurred in 44.2% of patients with BAV and 18.6% with TAV (aPR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.41-3.06; adjusted absolute difference, 21.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 9.6-32.6). Abscess involving non-leaflet structures was more frequent in BAV than in TAV (43.4% vs. 16.7%; p < 0.001). In the full cohort, aortic annular and left ventricular outflow tract involvement were more frequent in BAV. Infection-related reconstruction was performed in 31.9% of patients with BAV and 15.2% of those with TAV. Within the invasive subgroup, reconstruction was performed in 72.0% and 81.6% of BAV and TAV cases, respectively (unadjusted PR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.70-1.11). Early mortality was low in both groups, and the adjusted analysis did not identify a clear difference in long-term mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Bicuspid morphology was associated with a higher prevalence of non-leaflet invasive complications, predominantly abscess, and a higher overall frequency of infection-related reconstruction.

Title: Coexisting Moderate-to-Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation and Renal Dysfunction Identify a High-Risk Group After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and renal dysfunction are each associated with adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We investigated whether their coexistence identifies a clinically relevant high-risk group.
METHODS: In this retrospective two-centre cohort, patients undergoing TAVR were classified into four groups according to moderate-to-severe TR and preprocedural estimated glomerular filtration rate < 45 mL/min/1.73 m2. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified clinical covariates, and multiplicative interaction between TR and renal dysfunction was assessed.
RESULTS: Among 2227 patients, 1456 had neither condition, 324 isolated renal dysfunction, 315 isolated TR, and 132 both conditions. Patients with the combined phenotype had the highest rates of in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, and renal replacement therapy (all p < 0.001). One-year mortality increased progressively across groups (6.7%, 10.6%, 11.3%, and 22.9%; p < 0.001). After adjustment (n = 1704), the combined phenotype was associated with higher one-year mortality compared with neither condition (OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.62-5.23; p < 0.001), isolated TR (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.16-4.07; p = 0.015), and isolated renal dysfunction (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.16-4.61; p = 0.017). No significant multiplicative interaction was observed (p = 0.187).
CONCLUSIONS: Coexisting moderate-to-severe TR and renal dysfunction identify a clinically relevant high-risk group after TAVR, with higher adjusted one-year mortality than either condition alone. Combined assessment of TR and renal function may improve preprocedural risk stratification.

Title: Interatrial Shunt Devices in Heart Failure: A Therapy in Search of the Right Patient.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF/HFmrEF) accounts for approximately half of the global heart failure burden and remains a syndrome with limited device-based therapeutic options. It is often characterized by a disproportionate rise in left-sided filling pressure during exercise. Interatrial shunt devices (IASDs) aim to reduce left atrial pressure through controlled left-to-right atrial communication. We performed a structured narrative review of mechanistic studies, early feasibility cohorts, randomized trials, meta-analyses, and ongoing studies indexed through to August 2026. Early proof-of-concept studies consistently demonstrated technical feasibility, durable patency, and favorable hemodynamic effects, particularly through reductions in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), often accompanied by improved functional status. However, larger sham-controlled randomized trials failed to show consistent overall benefit in unselected populations. Recent mechanistic and observational data indicate that pulmonary vascular reserve, right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, rhythm-device status, and device design may affect benefits and harms. Latent pulmonary vascular disease and impaired right-heart reserve may identify patients poorly suited for shunt implantation, whereas carefully selected, promising phenotypes remain under prospective study. IASDs should therefore remain investigational. Future trials should use exercise hemodynamics and validated noninvasive markers to prospectively define responders, assess device-specific effects, and reconcile physiological unloading with clinical outcomes.

Title: Recurrence Rates and Outcomes After First Detected Atrial Fibrillation Episode in a Contemporary Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Center.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), occurring in 20-25% of patients and associated with increased morbidity, stroke risk, and symptom burden. Despite this substantial clinical impact, the understanding of the short-term natural history of AF, including recurrence and the effectiveness of treatment strategies in HCM, remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: We assessed 2016 patients referred to Lahey Hospital and Medical Center for the diagnosis and subspecialty management of HCM, of whom 341 (17%) had a remote history of AF (≥5 years), and 149 (7%) had AF episodes initially detected between January 2020 and June 2025. These 149 patients were included in this retrospective analysis to allow comprehensive short-term assessment of AF recurrence, treatment interventions, and clinical outcomes from first detected AF utilizing contemporary treatments.
RESULTS: AF was first detected at a median age of 63 years (IQR 54-70); 63% were male. Most AF episodes (87%) were symptomatic at presentation. Among 146 patients who converted to sinus rhythm, AF recurred in 80 (54%) at a median of 171 days (IQR 53-278; 29% at 6 months, 43% at 12 months). In patients not undergoing rhythm control after first detected AF episode, 60% had spontaneous recurrence (29% at 6 months, 48% at 1 year), while recurrence rates after antiarrhythmic drug (AAD) initiation were 44% (28% at 6 months, 37.5% at 1 year), and after catheter ablation were 27% (9.8% at 6 months, 18% at 1 year). At last follow-up, 1.9 years (IQR 1.2-2.6 years) from first detected AF episode, 133 of 149 patients (89%) were in sinus rhythm. Seven patients (4.7%) died at a median of 1.16 years (IQR 0.74-1.62) after their first detected AF; estimated survival was 98.6% at 1 year and 96.0% at 3 years.
CONCLUSIONS: AF recurrence occurs at high rates after the initial detected AF episode in HCM regardless of rhythm-control strategy or AAD use. Catheter ablation was associated with lower recurrence rates. These findings characterize the relapsing natural history of HCM-associated AF and underscore the need for further studies to optimize rhythm-control strategies in this population.

Title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Long-Term Mortality in Patients with Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Aims: Accurate prediction of the clinical course in implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) and cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator (CRT-D) patients is crucial, as their disease progression varies significantly due to comorbidities and individual characteristics. Methods: This retrospective study included 3321 patients from four hospitals in China, with 3207 for model development and internal validation and 114 for external testing. Five machine learning (ML) models were evaluated using the C-index, time-dependent AUROC, and Brier score. Decision curve analysis (DCA) assessed clinical utility, while Kaplan-Meier curves stratified patients into high-, intermediate-, and low-risk groups. SHAP analysis identified key predictors and explained model outputs. Results: The Random Survival Forest (RSF) model demonstrated favorable numerical performance across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving the highest time-dependent AUROC (0.74, 0.74) and C-index (0.71, 0.70) in internal and external test sets. It also had the lowest time-dependent Brier score (0.17) in the internal test and ranked second (0.13) in the external test. DCA demonstrated numerically higher net benefit for the RSF model across evaluated threshold probabilities. Kaplan-Meier curves revealed distinct survival trajectories, with high-risk patients showing significantly higher mortality than low-risk patients (HR: 4.50, 95% CI: 3.10-6.55, p < 0.0001), while intermediate-risk patients also had increased mortality (HR: 2.49, 95% CI: 1.69-3.68, p < 0.0001). LVEDD was the most influential predictor of mortality. Conclusions: The RSF survival model enables individualized, time-resolved prediction of all-cause mortality risk in ICD and CRT-D patients, supporting risk stratification and future evaluation of clinical utility, while requiring cautious interpretation of longer-term predictions due to limited numbers at risk.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and Triglycerides as Independent Predictors of Long-Term Aortoiliac Stent Failure After Endovascular Revascularisation.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restenosis and occlusion remain important after aortoiliac stenting, and device choice does not fully explain late patency loss. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is implicated in atherosclerotic progression and residual vascular risk.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether baseline Lp(a) is associated with long-term restenosis or occlusion after aortoiliac stenting.
METHODS: This post hoc biomarker analysis of COBEST included 125 patients and 168 treated iliac arteries randomised to the Advanta V12 covered stent (Atrium Medical Corporation, Hudson, NH, USA) or bare-metal stents for symptomatic aortoiliac occlusive disease. The primary outcome was loss of primary patency, defined as restenosis or occlusion during 5-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards modelling and cumulative failure curves were the main analyses.
RESULTS: In the Lp(a)-adjusted Cox model, covered stent use was associated with a lower hazard of restenosis or occlusion (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.31-0.97; p = 0.039), whereas each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration was associated with a higher hazard (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.06-1.10; p < 0.001; equivalent to HR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.79-2.59 per 10 mg/dL increase). In the biomarker-adjusted model, each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08; p < 0.001; HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.22-2.16 per 10 mg/dL increase) and each 1 mmol/L higher triglyceride concentration (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.34-2.68; p < 0.001) remained associated with restenosis or occlusion.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) and, to a lesser extent, triglycerides were independently associated with long-term aortoiliac stent failure after adjustment for stent type.

Title: Cardiometabolic Substrate Modification in Atrial Fibrillation: Obesity and Epicardial Adipose Tissue in the Era of Incretin-Based Therapies and Catheter Ablation.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is increasingly understood as the electrical expression of a systemic and atrial cardiometabolic disease rather than an isolated disorder of pulmonary-vein triggers. Obesity, insulin resistance, hypertension, sleep-disordered breathing, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and visceral adiposity promote atrial stretch, inflammation, fibrosis, autonomic imbalance, and conduction heterogeneity. Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), particularly the peri-left-atrial depot, may provide a local mechanistic bridge between systemic metabolic dysfunction and atrial cardiomyopathy through paracrine, inflammatory, fibrotic, and infiltrative pathways. This framework has direct therapeutic implications. Structured weight loss, cardiorespiratory fitness, alcohol reduction, and comprehensive risk-factor management can reduce AF burden and improve rhythm-control outcomes, although the magnitude of benefit varies across populations and trial designs. Incretin-based therapies have introduced a potentially important pharmacologic route to substrate modification. Semaglutide and tirzepatide produce substantial weight loss and favorable cardiovascular and heart-failure effects, while emerging observational and prospective data suggest lower AF incidence and post-ablation recurrence. However, evidence for reduced post-ablation recurrence remains predominantly non-randomized and is susceptible to residual confounding, treatment-selection effects, and healthy-user bias. Causality, weight-independent antiarrhythmic effects, optimal timing relative to ablation, and durability after treatment withdrawal remain unresolved. Observational sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor data support further investigation of cardiometabolic approaches to rhythm control, although randomized evidence has not consistently demonstrated benefit. Our review integrates mechanistic, imaging, lifestyle, pharmacologic, and electrophysiological evidence and proposes a practical model in which catheter ablation and cardiometabolic substrate modification are complementary strategies.

Title: Aortic Clamping Strategy During Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Partial or Single? A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between partial aortic clamping (PAC) and single aortic clamping (SAC) techniques during isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and their impact on clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Between 2022 and 2026, 974 patients who underwent isolated CABG were retrospectively evaluated. The study cohort was initially divided based on the operative technique into Group A (PAC, n = 626) and Group B (SAC, n = 348). To account for baseline clinical disparities, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed, yielding two balanced subgroups: Group C (PAC, n = 218) and Group D (SAC, n = 218).
RESULTS: Following propensity matching, the median cross-clamp (XCL) time was significantly lower in the PAC group compared to the SAC group (73 min vs. 100 min, p < 0.001). No statistically significant differences were observed between the balanced groups regarding postoperative exploration, cerebrovascular accidents, continuous renal replacement therapy requirements, or all-cause in-hospital mortality. The incidence of NOAF was significantly lower in the PAC group than in the SAC group [24 (11.0%) vs. 49 (22.5%), p = 0.001; absolute risk difference 11.5%, 95% CI 4.5-18.4%; number needed to treat ≈9]. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the SAC technique as an independent predictor of NOAF (p = 0.001, OR= 2.531 [95% CI, 1.442-4.441]).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated no significant differences between the PAC and SAC techniques regarding postoperative bleeding, blood product utilization, and major neurological or renal complications. However, the PAC strategy was associated with a significantly lower incidence of NOAF compared to the SAC technique.

Title: Safety and Cost-Analysis of Same-Day Versus Next-Day Discharge Following Complex Ablation Procedures: A Single-Centre Observational Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: (1) Introduction and objectives: The most common practice after a complex ablation procedure (CAP) is next-day discharge (NDD) following an appropriate observation period. However, the use of same-day discharge (SDD) has increased substantially since the COVID-19 pandemic. We aimed to evaluate the safety and cost-analysis of an SDD strategy for patients undergoing CAP. (2) Methods: This was a single-centre, retrospective observational study of patients undergoing CAP between January 2021 and July 2024, with intracardiac echocardiography used in all procedures. (3) Results: A total of 250 CAPs were performed, with a complication rate of 20.4% in the initial cohort. Forty-five patients were excluded, mainly because of significant procedural complications or severe pre-ablation medical conditions. The final analysis included 205 patients: 70 in the SDD group and 135 in the NDD group. Multiple patient and procedural characteristics were evaluated and compared between the groups. Among patients included in the final analysis, the overall complication rate was low (8.8%), with no differences between groups (early minor complications, 5.4%: 8.6% vs. 3.7% for SDD vs. NDD, p = 0.191; late major complications, 0.5%: 0% vs. 0.7%, p = 1; late minor complications, 3.4%: 2.9% vs. 3.7%, p = 1). There were five deaths (2.4%), none of which were procedure related. The SDD policy for CAP during this period would have saved €479.84 ± €248.09 per patient. (4) Conclusions: An SDD strategy was feasible and cost-saving and seemed to not increase periprocedural complications compared with an NDD strategy.

Title: Primary Non-Adherence and Associated Factors in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation in Germany: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary non-adherence (PNA)-failure to dispense a newly prescribed medication-is an early barrier to effective treatment. This study aimed to estimate PNA to oral anticoagulants in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) in Germany and to identify associated factors.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, first prescriptions of vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), direct thrombin inhibitors, or direct factor Xa inhibitors issued to AF patients between 2016 and 2025 in the IQVIA Disease Analyzer database were combined with pharmacy dispensing records in the Longitudinal Prescription (LRx) database. First prescriptions preceded by a dispensing of the same class within 365 days were excluded. PNA was defined as failure to dispense within 30 days; associated factors were assessed using logistic regression with generalized estimating equations.
RESULTS: The study included 57,290 first prescriptions in 53,815 patients (mean age 75.5 years; 49.7% women). PNA occurred in 10.6% (VKAs 14.4%, direct thrombin inhibitors 11.7%, direct factor Xa inhibitors 10.1%). Direct factor Xa inhibitors (odds ratio [OR] 0.67; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62-0.72), prior myocardial infarction (OR 0.79), and dementia (OR 0.85) were associated with lower odds of PNA, whereas ischemic heart disease (OR 1.18) and hypertension (OR 1.11) were associated with higher odds. Non-dispensing of the first prescription was strongly associated with non-dispensing of subsequent prescriptions.
CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in ten first oral anticoagulant prescriptions in AF was not dispensed within 30 days, most frequently for VKAs.

Title: Timing of Microaxial Flow Pump Support and In-Hospital Mortality in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock: The TIMING-CS Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: (1) Background: The association between microaxial flow pump (mAFP) timing and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains uncertain. (2) Methods: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of patients with AMI-CS admitted between January 2017 and July 2025. Prespecified 24 h landmark analyses included patients alive 24 h after intensive care unit (ICU) admission. The primary analysis compared patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) receiving mAFP within 6 h with STEMI patients managed without temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). Later STEMI implantation (>6-≤24 h) and both non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) timing cohorts were exploratory. The primary endpoint was subsequent in-hospital mortality from the landmark onward. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and propensity score-weighted models. (3) Results: In the primary STEMI cohort, 106 patients received mAFP within 6 h and 59 received no-tMCS. Subsequeunt in-hospital mortality was 17.0% versus 23.7%, respectively (p = 0.293). Early mAFP implantation was associated with lower mortality in the fully adjusted model (OR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.06-0.99]; p = 0.048). Propensity score-based estimates were directionally consistent, with significance in the doubly robust weighted model (OR, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.06-0.85]; p = 0.028) but not in all weighted models. Later-timing and NSTEMI estimates did not reach statistical significance and were imprecise. (4) Conclusions: Among patients with STEMI who survived the first 24 h after ICU admission, mAFP implantation within 6 h was associated with lower subsequent in-hospital mortality. Exploratory later-timing and NSTEMI estimates were inconclusive. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

Title: Sequential Arch-Tear Eligibility for Uncovered Aortic Arch Stent in Acute DeBakey Type I Aortic Dissection.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Because an uncovered arch scaffold does not provide a covered seal across an unresected arch tear, we evaluated a source-adjudicated sequential eligibility framework separating study-defined stop gates from residual-risk modifiers.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 266 patients with acute DeBakey type I dissection treated by hemiarch repair alone (No. = 160) or hemiarch plus AMDS (No. = 106). Blinded preoperative CT-scan re-review validated Gate 1 (visible arch tear), and operative-report review confirmed Gate 2 (tear directly observed at open inspection). Supra-aortic false-lumen communication was assessed only after both gates were negative.
RESULTS: Sixty-nine patients (25.9%) passed both study-defined gates (AMDS = 32; hemiarch = 37). Twelve-month CT-scan was available in 45/69 (65.2%; AMDS 24/32, hemiarch 21/37). Among imaged patients, complete zone 2-3 false-lumen exclusion occurred in 20/24 (83.3%) after AMDS and 0/21 after hemiarch (risk difference +83.3 percentage points, 95% CI +58.7 to +93.3; p < 0.001). DANE occurred in 4/32 (12.5%) and 16/37 (43.2%), respectively (p = 0.007). Under the adverse opposing missingness scenario, the exclusion risk difference narrowed to +19.3 percentage points (95% CI -4.2 to +39.9; p = 0.148).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings are hypothesis-generating and apply to a selected post hoc subgroup; treatment comparisons are non-causal. Prospective external validation of the study-defined hierarchy remains required.

Title: Feasibility of the Pleural Sliding Test for Detection and Management of Lung Adhesions During Robotic Cardiac Surgery.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Pleural adhesions can complicate access in robotic cardiac surgery, risking lung injury or conversion to sternotomy. The sliding test using thoracic ultrasound can predict thoracic adhesions and guide the surgeon during robotic set-up. We evaluated the utility of the sliding test in robotic cardiac surgery. The pleural sliding test was performed in 300 consecutive robotic cardiac surgery patients between August 2022 and September 2025. The test was performed by the surgeon using a linear probe at six intercostal sites after intubation. Intraoperative findings were used to validate the test. Tailored port placement and minithoracotomy strategies were used when adhesions were suspected. The mean age was 60.3 ± 13.7 years and 91 (30.3%) of the patients were female. Adhesions were encountered in 20 (6.7%) patients. Prior cardiothoracic surgery was associated with thoracic adhesions (p < 0.001). The pleural sliding test had a sensitivity of 95.0%, specificity of 97.9%, positive predictive value of 76.0%, negative predictive value of 99.6%. No pulmonary injuries occurred and no conversions to sternotomy were necessary in the cohort. Patients with adhesions had higher 24 h chest tube output (p = 0.006) but had similar mechanical ventilation times and intensive care unit stay durations. Pleural adhesions are not rare in patients undergoing robotic cardiac surgery, and their optimal management enhances the safety and efficiency of robotic cardiac procedures. The pleural sliding test offers high accuracy for preoperative detection, enabling tailored access strategies that enhance safety and maintain benefits of the robotic approach.

Title: Association Between Long-Term Blood Pressure Patterns and Onset of Stroke: A Nested Case-Control Study of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Elevated blood pressure (BP) and its variability are established stroke risk factors; however, whether long-term BP patterns are associated with stroke onset in patients with type 2 diabetes remains unclear. As a post hoc analysis, we conducted a nested case-control study among 2535 patients in the Japanese Primary Prevention of Atherosclerosis with Aspirin for Diabetes (JPAD) trial. During follow-up, 117 patients developed cerebral infarction (CI), and 35 developed intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Controls for these cases were matched for sex, aspirin allocation, age, and diabetes duration. Systolic, diastolic, and mean BP values were collected at baseline, annually during the trial, and every two years after the completion of the trial. Sequential BP levels and coefficient of variations (CVs) were compared between cases and controls. In both CI and ICH subsets, the median intervals from the most recent BP measurement to stroke onset were similar between cases and controls (CI: 300 vs. 288 days, p = 0.46; ICH: 481 vs. 448 days, p = 0.76). The most recent BP measurements before stroke were similar between cases and controls for both CI (systolic BP, 135 vs. 133 mmHg, p = 0.15; diastolic BP, 74 vs. 74 mmHg, p = 0.85) and ICH (systolic BP, 137 vs. 134 mmHg, p = 0.40; diastolic BP, 75 vs. 72 mmHg, p = 0.17). CVs were also comparable. Among patients with type 2 diabetes enrolled in a clinical trial, we found no clear evidence of an association between long-term BP patterns and subsequent stroke onset, suggesting that other factors triggering stroke onset warrant investigation.

Title: Preoperative Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index and Acute Kidney Injury After Adult Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common after cardiac surgery. We assessed the association between the preoperative advanced lung cancer inflammation index (ALI) and postoperative AKI. This retrospective cohort included adults undergoing cardiac surgery from 2 January 2019 to 16 March 2026. The primary outcome was the first in-hospital AKI recorded within 168 h using stored Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes creatinine and kidney-replacement-therapy classifications. Among 11,890 adults, AKI was recorded in 3380 (28.4%). Each ALI doubling was associated with a lower adjusted AKI rate (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval, 0.80-0.86; p < 0.001); the fixed-horizon risk ratio was 0.86 (95% confidence interval, 0.83-0.88; p < 0.001). Adjustment for available preoperative shock, resuscitation, intubation, infective endocarditis, acute aortic disease, and catecholamine indicators attenuated the hazard ratio to 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.87-0.94). Association magnitude differed across mutually exclusive procedure categories (interaction p < 0.001). The coefficient constraints imposed by ALI were rejected, and the positive BMI association persisted with flexible modeling. Lower ALI was associated with more recorded AKI, but differential monitoring, residual confounding, and unsupported component constraints limit interpretation of the composite.

Title: Evaluation of Clinical SYNTAX Score in Predicting New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation and Long-Term Prognosis in Patients Hospitalized with Non-ST Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) is a frequent complication among patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and is associated with adverse outcomes, making early identification of predictors essential for risk stratification and management. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the prognostic value of the Clinical SYNTAX score (CSS) compared with the anatomical SYNTAX score (SS), GRACE, and CHA2DS2-VASc scores in predicting in-hospital NOAF and long-term outcomes among 979 NSTEMI patients undergoing coronary angiography. Predictors of NOAF, all-cause mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs: death, myocardial infarction, stroke) were identified using logistic and Cox regression models, with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis used to compare the discriminative power of CSS against SS, GRACE, and CHA2DS2-VASc over a median follow-up of 86 months (IQR 36-100; range 0.1-144). NOAF developed in 80 patients (8.2%), with age, female gender, left atrial diameter, left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, and CSS (p = 0.014) identified as independent predictors. CSS's AUC for predicting NOAF (0.724; 95% CI: 0.673-0.775) was significantly higher than SS's (0.644; 95% CI: 0.588-0.699; DeLong p < 0.001) and comparable to that of the CHA2DS2-VASc and GRACE scores; a CSS threshold ≥ 17.77 predicted NOAF with 75% sensitivity and 65% specificity. In Cox regression analysis, in-hospital NOAF, age, hypertension, reduced ejection fraction (<60%), and CSS independently predicted long-term all-cause mortality, while NOAF, EF < 60%, age, early AF recurrence, hypertension, and CSS independently predicted MACEs; SS was not a significant predictor in either model. In non-overlapping multivariable models, this advantage reflected the contribution of CSS's clinical components rather than incremental value of the composite score; CSS nonetheless remained an independent predictor of NOAF and long-term outcomes and may serve as a practical single-score tool for risk-guided management.

Title: 5T Non-Contrast One-Stop MRA for Thoracic Aorta and Coronary Arteries: A Prospective Feasibility Study in Healthy Volunteers.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: This prospective study evaluated the feasibility of a non-contrast 5T one-stop MRA protocol for simultaneous assessment of the thoracic aorta and coronary arteries and examined the effect of heart rate (HR) on image quality.
METHODS: Thirty-four healthy volunteers underwent 5T MRA and were stratified by median HR into Low-HR (≤70 bpm, n = 17) and High-HR (>70 bpm, n = 17) groups. Subjective image quality was assessed using a 4-point scale, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and vessel edge sharpness (VES) were measured in predefined aortic and proximal coronary segments.
RESULTS: The protocol was successfully completed in all participants, and all evaluated segments were evaluable. Interobserver and intraobserver agreement was excellent (kappa ≥ 0.90; ICC ≥ 0.85). Subjective aortic scores did not differ between HR groups, whereas several coronary segments had lower scores in the High-HR group. SNR, CNR, and VES were higher in the Low-HR group across all objectively assessed segments.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings support the technical feasibility of integrated 5T non-contrast MRA in healthy volunteers and suggest that the subjective effect of higher HR is more evident in the coronary arteries than in the thoracic aorta, warranting further validation in patients with cardiovascular disease.

Title: Effects of Pulmonary Vein Isolation on Left Atrial Hemodynamic and Mechanical Function: Insights from Advanced and Emerging Echocardiographic Parameters in Responders and Non-Responders.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with progressive remodeling of the left atrium (LA). Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is an established rhythm-control strategy; however, its long-term impact on LA mechanical and hemodynamic function remains insufficiently defined.
OBJECTIVES: Our objective was to assess long-term changes in LA structure, mechanics, and hemodynamics after PVI, and to compare remodeling patterns between responders and non-responders.
METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 51 patients undergoing PVI were enrolled. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed before ablation and after 12 months. LA assessment included volumetric parameters, speckle-tracking-derived strain, and advanced functional indices (LA ejection fraction [LAEF], LA emptying fractions, LA function index [LAFI], and LA stiffness index [LAS-si]).
RESULTS: Forty-two patients (mean age 61 ± 9 years, 59.6% male) were included; a total of 32 (76.2%) were classified as responders and 10 (23.8%) as non-responders. Longitudinal differences between groups were tested using a Group × Time mixed-design ANOVA with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 19 echocardiographic parameters assessed. Non-responders showed a numerically greater decline in peak left atrial reservoir strain (PALS) than responders (95% CI 2.28-10.44; nominal p = 0.003), but this did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons (FDR-adjusted p = 0.06) and is therefore considered hypothesis-generating. Directionally consistent, non-significant trends toward greater adverse change among non-responders were also observed for LA volume index, LA ejection fraction, and LA stiffness index (all nominal p 0.07-0.13; all FDR-adjusted p ≥ 0.32). No parameter retained significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusions: In this hypothesis-generating, exploratory study, recurrent arrhythmia after PVI was associated with numerically greater adverse left atrial remodeling than freedom from recurrence, but between-group differences did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence that PVI itself caused the observed changes, particularly in the absence of a non-ablated control group, and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered prospective studies incorporating continuous rhythm monitoring.

Title: Predictors of Long-Term Clinical Outcomes of Perceval Aortic Valve Replacements in Females: A 9-Year Experience.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Females are at increased risk of patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM) following surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR) due to anatomical complexities. Whilst sutureless valves can reduce risk in smaller annuli, the literature lacks sex-specific outcome data pertaining to women. We evaluate long-term survival and durability outcomes pertaining to females.
METHODS: This is a retrospective analysis of demographic, clinical and outcome data in adults undergoing first-time isolated Perceval sutureless AVR between January 2017 and June 2025 at a tertiary centre. Subgroup analysis in females was also performed.
RESULTS: The number of patients N = 430 (178 males, 252 females). The median follow-up was 4.5 years. Females had higher Euroscores (p = 0.03) and smaller prosthetic valves (p = 0.01), but this group had fewer individuals with diabetes (p = 0.02) and fewer smokers (p < 0.01). Females had a higher 9-year survival (p = 0.02), where Euroscore (p = 0.02) and angina (p = 0.03) conferred a worse survival. No patients had PPM. FFR at 9 years was 97.3% in females (p = 0.61 compared to males); there were three reinterventions due to paravalvular leak. Of the females studied, 7.5% had permanent pacemakers at 9 years, with no significant predictors. At 9 years 2.4% of females had a stroke admission (mean time 1.4 ± 0.8 years), and female gender predicted stroke admission (p = 0.04). At 9 years, 3.1% had heart-failure admissions (mean time 1.8 ± 0.6 years), where angina (p = 0.02) predicted heart-failure admissions in females.
CONCLUSION: The findings in our single-centre retrospective cohort study suggest excellent long-term survival and durability outcomes in females, however, with a greater predisposition to stroke admissions after discharge. Whilst optimization of pre-operative symptoms can potentially reduce adverse events, further larger, non-inferiority studies with echocardiographic data are required to validate our findings.

Title: Lower Blood Pressure Extremes Precede the Recorded Diagnosis of Fibromyalgia by up to Two Decades: A Population-Based Matched Case-Control Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
Abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) has been linked to autonomic dysregulation, but population-level evidence on blood pressure (BP) in FM is sparse, and whether BP differences are present before diagnosis is unknown. We conducted a population-based case-control study within Leumit Health Services, Israel, comparing 15,869 adults with FM with 79,345 controls matched 5:1 on sex, birth year, and membership start. BP, heart rate (HR), and body temperature were summarized as each individual's minimum, mean, and maximum values over the full observation period and within a pre-diagnosis window extending up to 20 years before the index date with a 30-day blackout. Over the full period, FM patients had lower minimum systolic BP (99.1 ± 11.1 vs. 102.6 ± 12.3 mmHg; standardized mean difference [SMD] -0.29, 95% CI -0.31 to -0.27), lower minimum diastolic BP and pulse pressure, and higher maximum HR (SMD +0.22), whereas mean systolic BP differed little (SMD -0.08). The lower-tail BP difference was already present before diagnosis (minimum systolic BP -3.27 mmHg, 95% CI -3.51 to -3.04; SMD -0.24), in every interval from 20 years before the index date, and with 90-, 180-, and 365-day blackouts and across diagnostic-criteria eras. FM patients had more BP readings (22.1 vs. 15.3 per patient), and greater measurement intensity amplified the observed difference; nevertheless, the association persisted, attenuated, when measurement opportunity was standardized (first 3, 5, or 10 readings; measurement count strata; patient-level 10th percentile) and after multivariable adjustment for measurement intensity and cardiometabolic and cardiovascular covariates (-1.18 mmHg, 95% CI -1.37 to -0.99). The HR difference was small after adjustment (+0.25 bpm, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.48). Coded hypotensive, orthostatic, and autonomic diagnoses and dispensing of midodrine and fludrocortisone were more frequent in FM before diagnosis. A modest but reproducible lower-tail BP difference therefore precedes the recorded diagnosis of FM by many years. Because symptoms also antedate diagnosis, these data establish precedence over diagnosis rather than over disease onset, and they are compatible with, but do not prove, altered cardiovascular-autonomic regulation.

Title: Novel Techniques and Emerging Technologies in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Structured, Narrative Review.
Abstract: Chronic total occlusions (CTOs) represent one of the most technically demanding areas of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Despite advances in equipment and operator expertise, CTO PCI remains associated with lower procedural success rates and a higher risk of complications than non-CTO PCI. This review summarizes emerging techniques and technologies designed to improve procedural efficiency, safety, and outcomes in contemporary, personalized patient care. Recent innovations span multiple domains of CTO PCI. The minimalistic hybrid approach (MHA) aims to reduce vascular complications by minimizing the number of access sites and the sheath size. Novel perforation management strategies, including the cut balloon technique (CBT) and the condom technique, offer simple, low-cost options for distal vessel sealing, supported so far only by small series and technical reports. Advanced re-entry methods, such as tip-detection, antegrade dissection and re-entry (TD-ADR), integrate intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) to enhance precision. HydroDynamic contrast recanalization (HDR) revisits hydraulic dissection with a controlled, microcatheter-based contrast strategy whose safety profile remains to be established. The microcatheter anchor technique (MAT) has been proposed to facilitate retrograde CTO PCI in post-CABG anatomy. New plaque-modifying strategies, including RODIN-CUT and ORCAS, leverage high-pressure cutting balloon inflations under real-time IVUS guidance. Additional technologies, such as Plasmawire™, Shockwave Javelin®, and Hertz Contact intravascular lithotripsy (IVL), may expand the armamentarium for crossing and modifying complex CTO lesions, although CTO-specific clinical data are very limited (for Javelin, a 20-patient first-in-human coronary series). CT coronary angiography (CTCA) continues to improve pre-procedural planning, while drug-coated balloons (DCBs) show promise in selected de novo CTO lesions, although the evidence remains limited to retrospective series. Taken together, this rapid pace of innovation is steadily widening the procedural toolkit available for CTO PCI and may improve outcomes. Evidence for most of these techniques comes from case reports, small single-center series, and early-phase single-arm studies. It suggests feasibility in selected patients, but safety data are limited, and some reports signal concerns, including tamponade after the cut balloon technique and a higher perforation rate in a registry of the Carlino technique. The place of these techniques in routine practice will become clear only once larger, multicenter trials are completed.

Title: Beyond Mean Absolute Error: Ancestry-Stratified Calibration and Explainability for Warfarin Dosing Models.
Abstract: Background: Warfarin's narrow therapeutic index requires precise dose individualization, yet published machine-learning studies report accuracy that is inversely correlated with evaluation rigor: the field's best-reported mean absolute error (MAE) comes from an unreliably small test set. Methods: We present a reproducible, nine-phase ML pipeline on the public International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium (IWPC) dataset (n=6037 and n=1780) with fixed patient-level splits, strict leakage controls, and a nested clinical/genetic ablation across nine architectures. Results: AutoGluon with combined features achieves MAE =8.55 mg/week, R2=0.475, PW20 (percentage of predictions within 20% of the true dose) =0.466 on the larger cohort (MAE =7.96, R2=0.480, PW20 =0.497 on the smaller), exceeding prior rigorous benchmarks. A leave-one-ancestry-group-out evaluation, cross-checked across two model families, reproduces only part of an earlier analysis's known error concentration in Black/African-American patients: the Black label shows no penalty under either model, while Han Chinese and Caucasian show model-dependent penalties. A deep ensemble is badly miscalibrated (24.9%/21.6% coverage of a nominal 90% interval), while MAPIE (Model Agnostic Prediction Interval Estimator) conformal prediction on the same model achieves near-nominal coverage (89.8%/93.3%); per-ancestry coverage shows every Black/African-American label under-covered, a fairness gap the aggregate number hides. On IWPC-1780, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) attributes 64% of feature importance to genetics, confirming VKORC1 as the strongest predictor. Conclusions: To our knowledge, no previously published pipeline evaluated on the IWPC dataset jointly reports accuracy, ancestry-stratified fairness, calibration, and explainability on the same fixed splits.

Title: Association of the Red Cell Distribution Width-Albumin Ratio with Myocardial Strain, Mortality, and Heart Failure Hospitalization: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Aims: The aims of this study were to evaluate the association between the red cell distribution width (RDW)-albumin ratio (RAR) and subclinical myocardial impairment, as assessed by left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS), and to examine the relationships between the RAR, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study on adults who underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) with LVGLS assessment across three Mayo Clinic centers (2017-2024) and who had RDW and serum albumin measured on the same day or within seven days. The RAR was calculated as RDW/albumin and categorized into the following tertiles: <2.93, 2.93-3.48, and >3.48. Impaired LVGLS was defined as >-18%. Associations between the RAR and outcomes were assessed using multivariable logistic regression (LVGLS) and Cox models (HF and mortality), adjusting for demographics and comorbidities. Results: Among 5069 patients, 39.7% had impaired LVGLS, and its prevalence increased across RAR tertiles (26.8%, 41.9%, and 51.1%). Adjusted odds ratios for impaired LVGLS were 1.74 and 2.30 for tertiles 2 and 3, respectively. A higher RAR was associated with increased risk of HF hospitalization (aHR 2.54 and 4.48) and all-cause mortality (aHR 2.39 and 7.30). These associations persisted after adjusting for LVGLS. The effect of the RAR on mortality was stronger in patients with normal LVGLS compared to those with impaired LVGLS (p for interaction = 0.0004). Conclusions: A higher RAR was associated with abnormal LVGLS, HF hospitalization, and all-cause mortality after adjustment for clinical risk factors. However, the RAR did not provide discriminative value beyond its individual components.

Title: Renal Artery Occlusion After Standard Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: Incidence, Mechanisms, and Individualized Management.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Direct renal artery compromise after standard endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare and may result from mechanical ostial coverage or atheroembolism. We estimated its incidence and described mechanism-specific management and renal outcomes. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed all consecutive elective standard infrarenal EVAR procedures performed at a single center from March 2016 to June 2025, excluding repairs requiring planned renal incorporation. The primary event was complete renal artery occlusion or severe compromise requiring revascularization. We assessed mechanism, timing, management, renal function, dialysis, target-vessel patency, and survival. Results: Among 973 EVAR procedures, three patients developed renal artery compromise (0.31%; exact 95% confidence interval, 0.06-0.90%): inadvertent right ostial coverage, right atherothrombotic occlusion from a thrombus-bearing proximal aorta, and left occlusion with severe right compromise after proximal cuff deployment. Endovascular salvage succeeded in both attempted cases; the unilateral embolic occlusion was managed conservatively. All patients developed acute kidney injury, but none required dialysis. Median follow-up was 67.6 months. Conclusions: Recognized renal artery compromise after standard EVAR was uncommon in this cohort. These three cases illustrate a mechanism-informed approach to individualized assessment but cannot establish the superiority of any management strategy.

Title: MultiCaRe-Thorax: A Curated Benchmark Dataset and Reproducible Labeling Framework for Multi-Label Thoracic Disease Classification in Chest X-Ray Imaging.
Abstract: Chest X-ray (CXR) imaging remains a widely used diagnostic modality for the detection of thoracic diseases, including pneumonia, tuberculosis, pleural effusion, lung cancer and cardiomegaly. Despite the extensive use of CXR examinations in clinical practice, the development of robust multi-label artificial intelligence (AI) systems remains constrained by limitations in dataset availability, annotation consistency and reproducible labeling methodologies. Existing public datasets frequently rely on heterogeneous labeling protocols, limited pathology coverage or annotations that inadequately account for linguistic negation and uncertainty within radiology reports. In this paper, we introduce MultiCaRe-Thorax, a curated thoracic benchmark dataset derived from the publicly available MultiCaRe repository, with a reproducible negation-aware natural language processing (NLP) framework for automated generation of multi-label thoracic disease annotations. Unlike existing CXR benchmarks that are distributed in their pre-curated form, MultiCaRe-Thorax provides a fully reproducible pipeline from raw case reports to curated dataset, establishing a new resource that is both scalable and transparent. Our pipeline performs thoracic case identification, image-report matching, duplicate removal, data cleaning, disease-specific label extraction and quality-control verification to produce a curated cohort comprising 5252 chest radiographs from 3415 unique patients. Sixteen clinically relevant thoracic pathologies were automatically annotated using a dictionary- and pattern-based NLP framework incorporating explicit negation detection and n-gram mining, achieving 95% accuracy against 500 manually reviewed reports (Cohen's κ=0.89). Sixteen clinically relevant thoracic pathologies were automatically annotated using a dictionary- and pattern-based NLP framework incorporating explicit negation detection and n-gram mining, achieving 95% agreement against 500 manually reviewed reports. Five ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB0, EfficientNetB7 and InceptionV3) with two hybrid ensemble configurations were evaluated under a patient-level data partitioning protocol.
