Among individual architectures, DenseNet121 attains the best AUC on tuberculosis (0.757) and pleural effusion (0.767) with roughly one-third the parameters of ResNet50, while ResNet50 attains the higher mean AUC across all sixteen pathologies (0.688 vs. 0.682) and on interstitial lung disease (0.769) and lung mass/cancer (0.777); we report this as an accuracy-efficiency trade-off rather than a single best architecture. The DenseNet121-InceptionV3 ensemble achieves the highest reported AUC of 0.821 for lung mass/cancer detection. We report 95% confidence intervals for the evaluated ensemble and remaining backbones and note substantial estimation uncertainty for the rarest classes (e.g., congenital heart disease, n=8 test cases). Grad-CAM visualizations were also employed to provide clinically interpretable explanations of model predictions.

Title: Added Diagnostic Value of Stress CT Perfusion to Coronary CT Angiography Across Increasing Coronary Calcium Burden.
Abstract: Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) may show reduced specificity in patients with extensive coronary artery calcification (CAC). We evaluated the diagnostic performance of CCTA alone versus integrated CCTA-stress myocardial CT perfusion (CTP) across different CAC burdens. In this retrospective single-center study, 102 symptomatic patients with suspected coronary artery disease underwent CCTA with stress-only dynamic CTP and were stratified into CAC 0-400 (n = 38), 401-1000 (n = 43), and >1000 (n = 21). Stress-induced hypoperfusion was defined using a prespecified relative myocardial blood flow ratio ≤ 0.85. The primary diagnostic-accuracy analysis included 68 patients with an invasive reference standard (ICA/QCA ± FFR); FFR ≤ 0.80 was used when available, whereas QCA stenosis ≥ 50% defined reference-positive disease otherwise. The remaining 34 patients had complete event-free 12-month clinical follow-up and were included exclusively in a supportive exploratory analysis. In the primary cohort, CCTA alone showed a sensitivity of 89.8%, specificity of 36.8%, and accuracy of 75.0%, compared with 87.8%, 84.2%, and 86.8%, respectively, for integrated CCTA-CTP. The integrated strategy increased specificity by 47.4 percentage points (95% CI, 24.9-69.8) and accuracy by 11.8 percentage points (95% CI, 3.1-20.4), with a significant paired difference (McNemar p = 0.021) and an NRI of 0.45 (95% CI, 0.22-0.68). In the supportive exploratory full-cohort analysis, integrated CCTA-CTP showed numerically higher accuracy across all CAC strata; however, CAC-stratified comparisons were not individually significant and these findings should be considered descriptive. Mean total radiation dose was 7.0 ± 1.4 mSv. Integrated stress CTP was associated with higher specificity and diagnostic accuracy than CCTA alone, primarily by reducing false-positive anatomical classifications.

Title: Maternal Obesity and Outcomes During Pregnancy and the Puerperium: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Study.
Abstract: Background: Maternal obesity is associated with pregnancy complications and adverse perinatal outcomes, although observational associations may be influenced by confounding, exposure ascertainment, and missing data. This study investigated associations between recorded maternal body mass index (BMI) and maternal clinical conditions, obstetric complications, delivery characteristics, and perinatal outcomes in a referral center. Methods: A retrospective study was conducted using medical records of pregnant women at a referral center. Recorded maternal BMI categories were classified according to the World Health Organization. Database standardization harmonized equivalent diagnostic terms, preserved maternal clinical conditions and obstetric complications as separate domains, and grouped uncommon conditions for descriptive and exploratory analyses. Missing non-BMI variables underwent multiple imputation across 50 completed datasets; maternal BMI was not imputed. Twin pregnancies were excluded, and women with and without recorded BMI were compared before and after imputation. All singleton pregnancies with recorded BMI were included descriptively, whereas association analyses excluded women with underweight because of their small number and absence of recorded primary-outcome events. The primary composite perinatal outcome comprised neonatal intensive care unit admission, recorded fetal death or stillbirth, or a 5-min Apgar score <7 among liveborn infants. Logistic regression models compared overweight and obesity with normal weight, adjusting for maternal age and parity. Selected outcomes underwent additional adjustment for smoking, chronic hypertension, and pre-existing diabetes mellitus. Complete-case analyses assessed the sensitivity of the core findings. Results: The source database comprised 1012 records. After excluding 13 twin pregnancies, 999 singleton pregnancies remained; BMI was recorded for 787 women and missing for 212 (21.2%). Among women with recorded BMI, 27 (3.4%) had underweight, 282 (35.8%) normal weight, 210 (26.7%) overweight, and 268 (34.1%) obesity. Association analyses included 760 women. Compared with normal weight, obesity was associated with maternal clinical conditions (adjusted odds ratio, 3.04; 95% confidence interval, 2.06-4.49), chronic hypertension (8.96; 4.14-19.38), obstetric complications (4.12; 2.83-5.99), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (6.12; 3.60-10.40), gestational diabetes mellitus (2.43; 1.48-3.97), cesarean delivery (3.18; 2.12-4.75), and large-for-gestational-age birth (5.99; 2.74-13.13). Overweight was also associated with obstetric complications, gestational diabetes mellitus, cesarean delivery, and large-for-gestational-age birth. The associations between obesity and overall obstetric complications, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and large-for-gestational-age birth remained evident in expanded models. No statistically significant association was observed with the primary composite outcome for overweight (0.58; 0.21-1.57) or obesity (1.16; 0.54-2.53), and complete-case analyses were similarly inconclusive. Core models did not identify statistically significant associations with preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, or low birth weight. The exploratory association with perineal tears was attenuated after adjustment. Women without recorded BMI had fewer recorded maternal clinical conditions, obstetric complications, and cesarean deliveries, but more composite perinatal events; these differences persisted after imputation. Conclusions: Higher recorded maternal BMI was associated with maternal morbidity, cesarean delivery, and large-for-gestational-age birth after adjustment for age and parity. The composite perinatal findings remained inconclusive because of limited event frequency and imprecise estimates, rather than demonstrating absence of increased risk. Differences according to BMI availability indicate potential selection bias, while uncertain exposure timing and residual confounding further constrain interpretation. The findings support individualized preconception and antenatal assessment and standardized clinical documentation, without establishing causal relationships or the effectiveness of a specific intervention.

Title: Incremental Value of Cardiovascular CT in Neonates and Infants with Congenital Heart Disease: An Integrated Multimodality Imaging Approach.
Abstract: Background: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the first-line imaging modality in neonates and infants with congenital heart disease (CHD), whereas cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) is generally reserved for selected questions that remain unresolved after echocardiography. We evaluated the incremental diagnostic contribution of CCT within this multimodality imaging pathway. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients aged <1 year with CHD who underwent CCT after multidisciplinary review because TTE was inconclusive or additional anatomic definition was required for surgical planning. The primary endpoint was the incremental anatomic information provided by CCT beyond TTE. Secondary analyses included diagnostic performance against operative findings, acquisition characteristics, radiation exposure, contrast administration, and procedural safety. Results: Twenty-six patients were included; 14 (53.8%) were neonates. CCT was requested most frequently to assess coronary anatomy (9/26, 38.5%), followed by the pulmonary veins (4/26, 15.4%), aortic arch (3/26, 11.5%), and pulmonary arteries/MAPCAs (4/26, 15.4%). CCT provided additional anatomic characterization in 14/26 patients (53.8%), predominantly involving extracardiac vascular structures, and was discordant with TTE regarding the unresolved target anatomy in 12/26 (46.2%). Against the operative findings, TTE accuracy was 96.2% for intracardiac abnormalities, 41.2% for extracardiac abnormalities, and 11.1% for coronary abnormalities; corresponding CCT accuracy was 100%, 94.1%, and 100%. CCT directly informed the surgical approach in two patients with total anomalous pulmonary venous drainage. All examinations provided sufficient image quality to address the specific clinical question for which CCT was performed, and no contrast-related adverse events occurred. The median estimated effective dose was 3.62 mSv (IQR, 1.94-6.06). Conclusions: In a highly selected cohort of neonates and infants with CHD in whom expert TTE leaves a clinically relevant question unresolved, CCT may provide incremental information, particularly regarding coronary and extracardiac vascular anatomy. These findings support a targeted multimodality strategy in which CCT complements echocardiography and is tailored to the anatomic question relevant to surgical planning.

Title: Anabolic-Androgenic Steroid Use, All-Cause Mortality, and Major Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-medical anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with adverse cardiac remodelling, but the magnitude of excess all-cause mortality and the cardiac phenotype of former users remain incompletely defined. Methods: We systematically reviewed studies reporting mortality, major cardiovascular outcomes, or cardiac function after cessation in AAS-exposed individuals. All-cause mortality was pooled from comparative cohorts with individually ascertained exposure using random-effects models; global longitudinal strain (GLS) and left ventricular ejection fraction in former users were pooled as mean differences. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-E and certainty with GRADE. Results: Fifteen primary reports were included. Across three cohorts, AAS exposure was associated with higher all-cause mortality (risk ratio 2.57, 95% CI 1.98-3.33; I2 = 0%; 95% prediction interval 0.47-13.87), with consistent sensitivity analyses. In a single large matched cohort, adjusted hazard ratios for cardiovascular outcomes ranged from 2.26 to 8.90, highest for cardiomyopathy. Former users had worse GLS than AAS-naïve controls (3 studies; mean difference +0.90 percentage points, 95% CI +0.13 to +1.66), whereas the pooled ejection-fraction estimate was exploratory and highly heterogeneous. Conclusions: AAS exposure was associated with higher all-cause mortality in three observational cohorts, but residual confounding, differing follow-up, and the small evidence base preclude causal inference. Cardiovascular associations from a single cohort require independent replication, and evidence on residual myocardial dysfunction in former users is of very low certainty.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Deep-Learning-Based Assessment of Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography: Technical Validation, Cardiovascular Prognostic Value, and Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is a manifestation of medial arterial calcification frequently detected incidentally on screening mammography. Increasing evidence suggests that BAC may also serve as a marker of cardiovascular risk. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-based detection, segmentation, and quantification of BAC. It also evaluates the cardiovascular prognostic significance of automatically quantified BAC and examines the requirements for clinical translation. A targeted literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted for English-language publications available from database inception through 3 September 2026, with additional studies identified from reference lists. Deep-learning approaches included convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived segmentation architectures, transfer-learning models, and semi-supervised methods. Reported technical performance varied according to task and validation strategy. Representative segmentation models achieved Dice/F1 scores ranging from 0.666 to 0.756 and Jaccard indices from 0.581 to 0.614. Case-level BAC detection achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of up to 0.95-0.96 in selected test cohorts. However, external validation, learning-curve reporting, multivendor evaluation, and robustness assessment remained inconsistent. Prognostic studies demonstrated graded associations between automated BAC burden and cardiovascular outcomes. In a cohort of 21,514 women without known cardiovascular disease, age-adjusted BAC burden was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among women classified as low risk, with adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.66 and 2.31 for BAC below and above the age-specific median, respectively. In 123,762 women from two healthcare systems, MACE risk increased progressively with BAC burden after adjustment using the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs (PREVENT) equations, reaching approximately 2.8- to 3.3-fold higher risk with severe BAC. Nevertheless, incremental predictive improvement may be small-in one study, the addition of BAC changed the 5-year AUC from 0.645 to 0.646. Overall, available evidence supports the feasibility of scalable AI-based BAC assessment and demonstrates consistent associations between AI-quantified BAC and cardiovascular outcomes. However, technical performance and independent prognostic associations alone do not establish clinical utility. Standardized BAC definitions, genuinely independent external validation, and prospective implementation studies are required before BAC-guided cardiovascular management can be recommended.

Title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion with the Watchman FLX Device: A Single-Centre Retrospective Analysis of Procedural and One-Year Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an alternative approach to stroke prevention in selected patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. This single-centre retrospective study describes device implantation, peri-procedural complications and clinical outcomes during the first year after Watchman FLX implantation. Methods: We analysed 100 consecutive patients who underwent LAAO with the Watchman FLX device at Helios Frankenwaldklinik-Hospital, Kronach, Germany, between 2021 and 2024. The primary endpoint was device implantation success, defined as correct device deployment and implantation. The secondary safety endpoint was a composite of major peri-procedural complications within 72 h. Additional clinical outcomes were strokes and mortality at 30 days and one year. Results: The mean age was 70.7 ± 6.5 years, and 47% of patients were female. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.9 ± 1.4, and the mean HAS-BLED score was 4.1 ± 1.0. Device implantation was successful in 100% (95% CI 96.4-100%). The reported peri-procedural complication rate was 7% (95% CI 2.9-13.9%), including major bleeding in 6% (95% CI 2.2-12.6%) and pericardial tamponade in 1% (95% CI 0.0-5.4%). Thirty-day mortality was 2% (95% CI 0.2-7.0%), with no reported strokes (0%; 95% CI 0.0-3.6%). One-year mortality was 11% (95% CI 5.6-18.8%), with one reported stroke (1%; 95% CI 0.0-5.4%). Conclusions: Watchman FLX implantation was achieved in all patients in this cohort. Bleeding was the most frequently reported peri-procedural complication. The low observed stroke proportion should be interpreted alongside the 11% one-year mortality and incomplete imaging surveillance. This uncontrolled descriptive study cannot establish comparative efficacy or comprehensive device safety.

Title: Prognostic Impact of EASIX According to the Timing of Assessment in Newly Diagnosed Multiple Myeloma Undergoing Autologous Stem Cell Transplantation.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) is an easily accessible biomarker reflecting endothelial stress and has demonstrated prognostic value in several hematologic settings. However, its role in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM), particularly according to the timing of assessment, remains insufficiently characterized. We evaluated the prognostic value of EASIX measured at diagnosis and immediately before autologous stem cell transplantation (autoSCT) for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 99 transplant-eligible patients with NDMM who underwent autoSCT between 2017 and 2023. EASIX was calculated at diagnosis and pre-autoSCT and log2-transformed. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. Optimal EASIX thresholds were explored using maximally selected log-rank statistics. Model discrimination was evaluated using Harrell's concordance index and time-dependent area under the curve (AUC). Results: EASIX at diagnosis was available for 92 patients. Higher log2(EASIX) at diagnosis remained associated with inferior OS after adjustment for International Staging System (ISS) stage (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.11-1.71; p = 0.0035). It also remained associated with shorter PFS after adjustment for ISS stage, age, and sex (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.14-1.74; p = 0.001). Diagnosis EASIX demonstrated good discrimination for OS, with a C-index of 0.78 and sustained time-dependent AUC values. Conversely, pre-autoSCT EASIX was not significantly associated with OS or PFS when analyzed continuously, and cutoff-based analyses did not provide a consistent, robust prognostic signal. Conclusions: EASIX measured at diagnosis was associated with both OS and PFS in transplant-eligible NDMM, whereas continuous pre-autoSCT EASIX showed no consistent association with either outcome. A direct paired comparison demonstrated a significantly stronger prognostic association of diagnosis EASIX with PFS, while the corresponding between-timepoint difference for OS was not statistically significant. These findings support further evaluation of EASIX timing in larger independent cohorts.

Title: Residual Atherogenic Dyslipidemia in Normal-Weight Adults: The Role of Visceral Adiposity and Metabolic Dysfunction.
Abstract: Background. Body mass index (BMI) remains the most widely used tool for obesity classification and cardiometabolic risk stratification. However, increasing evidence suggests that normal BMI does not necessarily reflect metabolic health, particularly in individuals with hidden visceral adiposity and residual atherogenic dyslipidemia. The present study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of residual atherogenic dyslipidemia among normal-weight adults and to analyze its association with visceral adiposity, metabolic dysfunction, and lifestyle-related factors. Methods. A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 166,008 Spanish workers aged 18-69 years with normal BMI (18.5-24.9 kg/m2) who underwent standardized occupational health examinations between 2022 and 2024. Anthropometric, biochemical, vascular, and lifestyle-related variables were evaluated. Visceral adiposity was estimated using waist-to-height ratio (WtHR) and the Metabolic Score for Visceral Fat (METS-VF). Residual atherogenic dyslipidemia was primarily assessed using the triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio (TG/HDL-c). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent associations with elevated TG/HDL-c. Results. Despite normal BMI values, 8.0% of participants presented with an elevated TG/HDL-c ratio, 11.8% had central adiposity, 11.4% showed low HDL cholesterol, and 17.9% exhibited elevated blood pressure. Individuals with an elevated TG/HDL-c ratio demonstrated significantly higher waist circumference, WtHR, METS-VF, triglycerides, non-HDL cholesterol, fasting glucose, blood pressure, and TyG index values (all p < 0.001). A progressive worsening of lipid and metabolic parameters was observed across increasing METS-VF quartiles. Elevated TG/HDL-c ratio prevalence increased from 2.7% in the lowest METS-VF quartile to 15.8% in the highest quartile. Men showed a substantially higher prevalence of residual atherogenic dyslipidemia than women (12.2% vs. 3.9%, p < 0.001). Physical inactivity, smoking, poor Mediterranean diet adherence, and regular alcohol consumption were strongly associated with adverse lipid-metabolic profiles. In multivariable analyses using separate adiposity measures, BMI and METS-VF remained independently associated with elevated TG/HDL-c, whereas WtHR ≥ 0.50 was not independently associated after adjustment. Male sex, physical inactivity, smoking, impaired fasting glucose, elevated blood pressure, and low Mediterranean diet adherence showed consistent associations across models. Conclusions. Residual atherogenic dyslipidemia is highly prevalent among adults with normal BMI and is strongly associated with visceral adiposity, metabolic dysfunction, and unfavorable lifestyle-related behaviors. Conventional BMI classification alone substantially underestimates hidden cardiometabolic risk. These findings highlight the metabolic heterogeneity present among apparently healthy normal-weight individuals and the limitations of BMI as a sole marker of cardiometabolic health.

Title: Prognostic Value of Plaque Burden Beyond Stenosis Severity in Patients with Stable Chest Pain Undergoing Coronary CT Angiography.
Abstract: Introduction: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a noninvasive test for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), but the prognostic value of integrating plaque burden into CAD-RADS 2.0 has not been fully evaluated. We aimed to assess whether the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category, which combines stenosis severity and segment involvement score (SIS), provides prognostic information beyond stenosis severity in patients with stable chest pain. Methods: We retrospectively included 563 consecutive patients with stable chest pain who underwent CCTA between 2017 and 2022. CAD-RADS 1.0 categories and CAD-RADS 2.0 plaque burden grades were assigned by experienced radiologists. High-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 was defined as CAD-RADS ≥ 3 or any CAD-RADS with P-SIS ≥ 3. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was restricted to clinically justified parsimonious Cox proportional hazards models. A model including age, sex, and significant stenosis was compared with a model including age, sex, and the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category. A formally nested extended model additionally included severe-to-extensive plaque burden. Results: Over a median follow-up of 51.2 months, 41 patients (7.3%) experienced MACEs. Among patients with non-obstructive CAD (CAD-RADS 1-2), 29 of 477 (6.1%) experienced MACEs, and 85.4% of these events occurred in patients with severe or extensive plaque burden (P3-P4). After adjustment for age and sex, significant stenosis was not associated with MACEs, whereas the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category was independently associated with MACEs (HR 2.88, 95% CI 1.07-7.75; p = 0.036). Addition of plaque burden to a model including age, sex, and significant stenosis increased the Harrell C-index from 0.760 to 0.772 and significantly improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ2 = 5.41; p = 0.020). In the extended model, plaque burden remained independently associated with MACEs (HR 2.81, 95% CI 1.10-7.19; p = 0.031). Conclusions: In patients with stable chest pain undergoing CCTA, the high-risk CAD-RADS 2.0 category was independently associated with MACEs. Formal incremental analyses demonstrated that plaque burden provided prognostic information beyond age, sex, and significant stenosis. These findings support the prognostic relevance of integrating plaque burden into CCTA-based risk classification but require confirmation in larger prospective and externally validated cohorts.

Title: Acute Effects of Two Slow-Paced Breathing Protocols With and Without Inspiratory Breath-Holding on Heart Rate Variability: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Slow-paced breathing (SPB) is associated with changes in heart rate variability, although these responses are strongly influenced by respiratory patterns; the effects of incorporating an inspiratory breath-hold into an SPB protocol remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the immediate effects of two SPB protocols on heart rate variability (HRV) and cervical pressure pain thresholds (PPT). Methods: A single-blind, randomized, controlled trial was conducted with 60 healthy adults (aged 18-65) stratified by age and sex, and allocated equally (n = 20 per group) to: Protocol 1 (6 s inhalation, 6 s hold, 6 s exhalation), Protocol 2 (6 s inhalation, 6 s exhalation), or a sham control (general respiratory education). Interventions lasted 5 min. Primary outcomes were time-domain HRV indices, root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and standard deviation of normal-to-normal (SDNN), recorded using a Polar H10 chest strap. The secondary outcome was PPT at the fourth cervical vertebra (C4) measured via digital algometry. Results: Repeated measures ANOVA revealed a significant time-by-group interaction for heart rate, RMSSD, and SDNN. Both active breathing protocols significantly increased RMSSD and SDNN compared to control, with high effect sizes (η2). Notably, Protocol 1 (with inspiratory breath-holding) produced the largest changes in HRV, RMSSD, and SDNN. Conversely, changes in cervical PPT were modest and reached only borderline significance with small effect sizes. Conclusions: Both SPB protocols were associated with acute increases in time-domain HRV indices. Protocol 1 (combining inspiratory breath-holding and lower respiratory frequency) produced a larger acute autonomic response, suggesting its potential utility in non-pharmacological interventions for autonomic dysregulation. However, the isolated contribution of breath-holding cannot be separated from the lower respiratory frequency inherent to this protocol.

Title: Interleukin-Driven Inflammation and Cardiovascular Risk in People Living with HIV: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Emerging Preventive Strategies.
Abstract: Heart and vascular complications now rank among the leading health threats facing individuals with HIV, a reality that continues even when modern drug regimens successfully silence viral replication. Sustained immune system overdrive and persistent low-grade systemic inflammation appear central to this heightened vulnerability. This narrative review integrates current understanding of how inflammatory signaling molecules, particularly interleukins, connect to heightened cardiovascular danger in HIV-positive populations, while exploring mechanistic underpinnings, cohort-derived evidence, and prospective treatment possibilities. Elevated concentrations of proinflammatory messengers such as IL-6 and IL-18, alongside indicators of myeloid cell activation including sCD14 and sCD163, characterize the HIV-positive state and independently forecast arterial disease progression, clinical cardiac events, and shortened survival. Notably, this inflammatory signature endures despite pharmacologically induced viral quiescence. Disturbances in protective lipoprotein function, heightened clotting propensity, and leakage of gut-derived bacterial components into the bloodstream each amplify vascular injury. Inflammatory cytokines occupy a central position in HIV-associated cardiovascular pathobiology, serving dual roles as disease predictors and candidate treatment targets. Importantly, recent evidence from the REPRIEVE randomized clinical trial demonstrated that pitavastatin therapy reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by approximately 35% in people living with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy, highlighting inflammation-modulating strategies as a new foundation of cardiovascular prevention in this population.

Title: Prediction of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Machine Learning Approach.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: New-onset atrial fibrillation is a common complication of acute myocardial infarction and is associated with increased mortality, heart failure, and recurrent cardiovascular events. Prediction models for the occurrence of atrial fibrillation may facilitate early risk stratification, improve patient monitoring, and support personalized therapeutic decision-making in clinical practice. Methods: A prospective study included 150 patients with acute myocardial infarction admitted within 24 h of symptom onset. Clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic data were collected, and a machine learning model was developed to predict new-onset atrial fibrillation. Model performance was evaluated using ROC-AUC, while SHAP analysis was applied to identify and quantify the contribution of individual predictors. Results: The machine learning model demonstrated excellent predictive performance, achieving an accuracy of 97.0%, ROC-AUC of 0.991, and precision-recall AUC of 0.991 in the independent test set. SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and permutation importance analyses identified the E/e' ratio, left ventricular mass index, left ventricular ejection fraction, left atrial volume index, oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde and superoxide dismutase), NT-proBNP, and complete revascularization as the most influential predictors of new-onset atrial fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction. Conclusions: Machine learning combined with SHAP-based explainability showed high potential for predicting new-onset atrial fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction. This approach may improve individualized risk assessment and clinical decision-making, pending validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

Title: Early Recognition of Patients with Neuronopathic Forms of Mucopolysaccharidosis Type II in Clinical Practice.
Abstract: Background: Mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS II) is a progressive, rare, X-linked inherited disease with multi-organ involvement and a restricted life expectancy. The disease has two main forms: neuronopathic (severe) and non-neuronopathic (attenuated). Aim: To compare the two main forms of MPS II to identify signs for early recognition of severe disease forms in daily practice. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, clinical and laboratory data, as well as enzyme replacement therapy data, for approximately 162 patients were extracted and analyzed from the Russian MPS II registry. Patients with insufficient clinical information (23 patients) and children under 5 years of age (15 patients) were excluded. We compared patients with MPS II neuronopathic (n = 82, 66.1%) and non-neuronopathic forms (n = 42, 33.9%) based on the presence of cognitive deficits after age 6 years and on remaining committed to the phenotype throughout follow-up. Results: The patients with both forms had the following symptoms with similar frequency: Hurler phenotype, hernias, hepatosplenomegaly, short neck, orthopedic problems: spinal pathology (curvature), chest deformity, joint stiffness, deformity of the hand, hand contractures, wrist joint deformity and contractures, elbow joint deformity and contractures, shoulder and knee deformity and contractures, hip contractures, cardiomyopathy, obstructive respiratory tract diseases, noisy breathing, hearing loss, carpal tunnel syndrome. Highly specific symptoms (frequency of occurrence above 80%) for the diagnosis of the neuronopathic form of MPS II were: delayed intellectual disability at the age of 1-3 years, epilepsy, and the presence of gross rearrangements in the IDS gene. Highly sensitive symptoms (above 80%) were: psychomotor development delay of up to 1 year of age and delayed intellectual disability at the ages of 1-3 years, heart damage, and myxomatous degeneration of the valves (79.5%). A symptom with high sensitivity and specificity is delayed mental and speech development between the ages of one and three, with respective sensitivities and specificities of 94.8 and 86.5. Conclusions: Identifying symptoms characteristic of neuronopathic forms of MPS is important not only for determining the clinical form of the disease but also for developing various approaches to treating such patients. Early diagnosis of severe forms of MPS II will make it possible to use currently approved methods of intraventricular enzyme replacement therapy, or primarily use of ERT capable of crossing the brain-blood barrier which could improve the prognosis for such patients. Symptoms that predict the risk of developing the neuronopathic form can be used in clinical practice.

Title: Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Adding Trimetazidine to Standard Antianginal Therapy in Patients with Stable Angina: Egyptian Cohort Findings of the COMBINE Angina Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Stable angina is a significant health issue in Egypt, often showing poor responses to standard treatments. This study examines the effectiveness and safety of early combination therapy with trimetazidine and either a β-blocker or a calcium channel blocker (CCB) among Egyptian patients with stable angina. Methods: This sub-analysis of the Egyptian cohort from the COMBINE Angina study included patients with stable angina (CCS class II-III) who remained symptomatic after 2-4 weeks of β-blocker or CCB monotherapy. Patients received trimetazidine 35 mg modified-release twice daily as an add-on treatment for 4 months. The primary outcome was the Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) summary score, with secondary outcomes including SAQ-7 domain scores, CCS class, frequency of angina attacks, nitrate use, treatment satisfaction, adherence, and safety. Results: In the global COMBINE study involving 578 patients, the Egyptian cohort had 138 participants with an average age of 58.3 years. The SAQ-7 summary score improved from 42.2 at baseline to 76.8 at month 4 (mean change 34.6 points, 95% CI 31.3 to 38.0; p < 0.0001). All 138 patients contributed data at every visit for the SAQ-7 summary score. Patients in CCS class I increased from 0% to 56.5%, weekly angina attacks fell from 5.0 to 1.7 (p < 0.0001), and short-acting nitrate use decreased from 2.9 to 1.0 doses per week (p < 0.0001). Patient satisfaction was about 75%, and physician satisfaction reached 83% by month 4. Medication adherence also improved (MARS-5 score: 20.8 to 22.7), and two non-serious, treatment-related adverse events (nausea and somnolence) were reported in a single patient (0.7%), with no serious or fatal events. Conclusions: In Egyptian patients with stable angina, implementing an early combination strategy incorporating trimetazidine with first-line β-blocker or CCB therapy was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in angina symptoms, functional status, and quality of life, with good tolerability and high satisfaction. As the study was observational and single-arm, these findings are provisional and require confirmation in further long-term controlled studies.

Title: Anatomical Predictors of Endovascular Technical Success in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: The Role of GLASS and Diabetes.
Abstract: Background: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major adverse limb events and mortality, particularly in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) standardizes anatomical assessment and supports revascularization planning. This study evaluated the association of anatomical complexity and diabetes with immediate technical success after infrainguinal endovascular treatment. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 136 patients undergoing infrainguinal endovascular procedures for CLTI between May 2021 and May 2023, stratified into diabetic (n = 85) and non-diabetic (n = 51) groups. Anatomical complexity was assessed using GLASS. Technical success was defined as restoration of inline flow to the foot. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: Technical success was achieved in 74.3% of procedures, without significant differences between diabetic and non-diabetic patients (75.3% vs. 72.5%, p = 0.723). Success declined progressively from 86.3% in GLASS stage I to 75.5% in stage II and 53.1% in stage III (p = 0.003; trend p = 0.001). In multivariable analysis, GLASS FP (femoropopliteal) grade ≥2 (adjusted OR 8.068, 95% CI 3.018-21.562; p < 0.001) and tibioperoneal trunk occlusion (adjusted OR 4.874, 95% CI 1.271-18.687; p = 0.021) were independently associated with technical failure, whereas diabetes was not. The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.820, 95% CI 0.744-0.897; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Anatomical complexity was associated with immediate technical success in CLTI, whereas no independent association with diabetes was detected in this cohort. GLASS may provide clinically relevant preprocedural risk stratification and support endovascular planning.

Title: The Role of Interleukin 17 in Association with Systemic Parameters in Severity Stratification and Mortality Prediction in Moderate and Severe Acute Pancreatitis.
Abstract: Introduction: Acute pancreatitis is an inflammatory lesion that can lead to multiple organ dysfunctions and has an increased mortality rate. The pathogenic mechanisms are complex. A central element is represented by systemic inflammation. This exploratory study aims to identify parameters useful in stratifying the severity of moderate and severe acute pancreatitis and predicting mortality, as well as in evaluating the predictive value of IL-17 regarding disease severity. Material and Methods: A retrospective study was conducted during the period October 2024-August 2025 on an eligible group of 64 patients with moderate and severe acute pancreatitis. Demographic, etiological, and biological data were collected according to the observation sheets, anamnesis, and clinical examination. Also, the level of IL-17 was quantified by the ELISA technique. All data were appropriately analyzed statistically. Results: Of the 64 cases, 35 (54.69%) had severe acute pancreatitis. From the clinical-demographic data, we identified personal cardiovascular and renal pathological antecedents as independent risk factors for death (OR = 7.529 and OR = 24, respectively). Also, metabolic etiology represented a risk factor for death (OR = 5.625). From the biological parameters, erythrocyte sedimentation rate ≥ 41.29 mm/h and AISI score ≥ 1627.50 have a role in predicting severity with quite high sensitivity and specificity. Leukocytosis, C-reactive protein (CRP), IL-17, and hypocalcemia represent predictive risk factors for the occurrence of severe acute pancreatitis (OR = 3.733, OR = 1.136, OR = 1.068, and OR = 3.542, respectively). Of these, only CRP, IL-17, and hypocalcemia represent risk factors for death (OR = 1.051, OR = 1.080, OR = 6.771). Regarding the in-hospital management of intensive care days, complications and organ dysfunctions are risk factors for death. Conclusions: This study identified useful parameters adjunct to the current scoring systems to stratify patient severity in moderate and severe acute pancreatitis, as well as risk factors for mortality. In addition, IL-17 provides useful information involved in the pathogenesis, evolution of severity and survival in these patients. Despite the promising role of IL-17, these findings remain preliminary due to the small sample size and require external validation.

Title: Optimizing Cardiovascular Risk in PLWH: Real-World Efficacy and Lipid Kinetics of Fixed-Dose Combination Rosuvastatin Ezetimibe.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) have increased cardiovascular disease risk, and dyslipidemia remains a major modifiable factor. Achieving recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets can be challenging.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of fixed-dose low-dose rosuvastatin/ezetimibe in virologically stable PLWH and to describe lipid-lowering kinetics in comparison with an HIV-negative control cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 32 PLWH and 43 HIV-negative outpatients receiving rosuvastatin 5 mg plus ezetimibe 10 mg daily. Lipid parameters, cardiovascular risk scores, and safety markers were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months.
RESULTS: In PLWH, LDL-C decreased from 170.7 ± 35.1 to 87.8 ± 24.6 mg/dL at 6 months, corresponding to a mean reduction of 46.7% (p < 0.001). Total cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol also decreased significantly (p < 0.001 for both), while triglycerides decreased significantly at month 6 (p = 0.016). Overall, 53.1% of PLWH reached guideline-recommended LDL-C targets. Both the 5-year and 10-year D:A:D scores decreased significantly during follow-up (p < 0.001 for both). The exploratory comparison suggested a more rapid early lipid response among HIV-negative controls, with most of the reduction occurring by month 3. No treatment-limiting adverse events or viro-immunological deterioration occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose rosuvastatin combined with ezetimibe was associated with substantial improvement in atherogenic lipid parameters in virologically stable PLWH, while the exploratory finding of an earlier response among HIV-negative controls may support further investigation of treatment-response kinetics.

Title: Clinical Outcomes and Hospital Resource Utilization Among Patients with Sepsis and COVID-19 Infection: Insights from the United States National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2020-2022.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Clinical studies have shown that patients who had sepsis with COVID-19 infection had worse clinical outcomes; however, there is a paucity of data on the association between concurrent COVID-19 infection and outcomes among patients with sepsis. Hence, we conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database from 2020 through 2022 to evaluate the association between concurrent COVID-19 infection and outcomes among patients with sepsis.
METHODS: Adult hospitalizations with sepsis were identified using ICD-10-CM codes; hospitalizations with septic shock were excluded, and the remaining cohort was stratified by concurrent COVID-19 infection status. Survey-weighted multivariate regression analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Patients with sepsis with concurrent COVID-19 infection had worse outcomes with higher mortality rate (15.6% vs. 5.4%; aOR 3.70; 95% CI 3.62-3.79), higher need for invasive ventilation (13.1% vs. 6.5%) and NIV (non-invasive ventilation) (10.2% vs. 4.9%), higher incidence of acute kidney injury (37.6% vs. 36.7%), acute respiratory failure (57.5% vs. 20.3%), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) (0.4% vs. 0.3%), cardiac arrest (3.1% vs. 1.5%), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) (7.9% vs. 0.4%), higher need for renal replacement therapy (4.9% vs. 4.5%), tracheostomy (1.6% vs. 0.6%), extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) (0.2% vs. 0.04%), longer length of hospital stay (10.3 days vs. 7.6 days), and higher total charges ($127,632 vs. $93,735, respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: The results demonstrate that COVID-19 infection was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes among those hospitalized with sepsis. These results underscore the need for early recognition, aggressive treatment, and targeted therapy in this high-risk clinical group.

Title: Age-Driven Cardiovascular Risk Scores Differ Across Antiretroviral Regimens Among People Living with HIV in the Colombian Caribbean Region.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: People living with HIV (PLHIV) face an elevated burden of cardiovascular disease, and general-population and HIV-specific risk scores are commonly used for stratification, though data from Latin America, particularly Colombia's Caribbean region, remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the distribution of cardiovascular risk, assessed through the Framingham, ASCVD ACC/AHA, and D:A:D scores, and to compare these scores across antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens among PLHIV individuals in the Colombian Caribbean region.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 147 adult PLHIV patients receiving ART at care sites across the Colombian Caribbean. Sociodemographic, clinical, immunovirological, and treatment-related variables were compared across cardiovascular risk categories (low, moderate, high) using the Kruskal-Wallis test for continuous variables and Chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables, as appropriate to expected cell counts. Agreement between the three scores was assessed with weighted Cohen's kappa. Factors independently associated with high cardiovascular risk were evaluated using Bayesian multivariate logistic regression (full and parsimonious models).
RESULTS: All three cardiovascular risk scores differed significantly across ART regimen groups (p ≤ 0.005), with INSTI-containing regimens showing the highest scores. Agreement between scores was substantial between Framingham and ASCVD (κ = 0.717) and moderate between Framingham and D:A:D (κ = 0.534), and fair between ASCVD and D:A:D (κ = 0.321). Neither CD4+ count nor viral load status differed significantly by risk category. In multivariate analysis, age was the only variable independently associated with high cardiovascular risk (adjusted OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.18-1.53).
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular risk stratification in this Caribbean Colombian HIV cohort is driven primarily by chronological age; univariate differences by ART regimen group did not persist after formal comparison against an age-only model (likelihood-ratio p = 0.215), and are more consistent with channeling of older, higher-comorbidity patients toward INSTI-based regimens than with a direct pharmacological effect. Agreement between the three risk scores ranged from fair to substantial, indicating that scoring-system choice can meaningfully alter risk classification independently of virological or immunological control. These findings support age-focused cardiovascular monitoring in PLHIV individuals and caution against relying on a single, non-locally validated risk score in this population.

Title: Antiproteinuric Response to Finerenone in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Responder and Non-Responder Subgroup Analysis of the FINDKDLATAM Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Albuminuria is an early marker of kidney damage and an independent predictor of adverse outcomes, making its reduction a key therapeutic goal. Finerenone, a selective nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, has demonstrated renal and cardiovascular benefits in patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD), although the magnitude of the antiproteinuric response may vary in clinical practice. This post hoc analysis aimed to characterize the six-month antiproteinuric response to finerenone and to descriptively explore baseline clinical and treatment characteristics across response categories in the FINDKDLATAM cohort. Methods: A subgroup analysis was performed on a real-world, multicenter, retrospective, observational study that included patients from the FINDKDLATAM study who had urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) measurements taken at baseline and six months. Patients were classified as absolute responders (≥50% reduction in UACR), partial responders (30-49% reduction), and non-responders (<30% reduction or no reduction in UACR) at six months of follow-up. Sociodemographic, clinical, biochemical, therapeutic, and safety variables were analyzed. Results: Of the 347 patients included in the original cohort, 334 had complete UACR data at six months and were included in the analysis. Of these, 80.2% (n = 268) were absolute responders, 11.7% (n = 39) partial responders, and 8.1% (n = 27) non-responders. Median UACR decreased from 350.7 to 67.0 mg/g among absolute responders and from 240.5 to 143.0 mg/g among partial responders (both p < 0.0001), whereas no significant change was observed among non-responders. No baseline clinical characteristic consistently distinguished responders from non-responders. Serum potassium increased during follow-up, particularly among non-responders. Conclusions: In this retrospective Latin American cohort, most patients experienced a reduction in UACR after six months of finerenone treatment. However, the uncontrolled observational design, concomitant therapies, UACR variability, and regression to the mean preclude attributing these changes exclusively to finerenone. These exploratory findings do not support selecting patients according to a particular responder phenotype but rather support prescribing finerenone according to currently approved clinical criteria. Prospective studies with adjusted analyses are needed to identify independent predictors of response.

Title: Characteristics and Treatment Outcomes of Patients with Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis in Selected Facilities of O.R. Tambo District Municipality, Eastern Cape, South Africa: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, due to its high prevalence, mortality, and economic impact. The emergence of drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) has intensified this burden, posing significant challenges to disease control and management. Understanding the epidemiology of DR-TB is crucial for improving prevention strategies, guiding treatment interventions, and informing public health policies aimed at reducing its spread and impact. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using medical records of patients diagnosed with DR-TB between January 2020 and December 2024 at decentralized DR-TB clinics in the O.R. Tambo District Municipality, Eastern Cape, South Africa. Treatment outcomes were collected from available records through August 2025. Data on demographic, clinical, and treatment outcome variables were collected using a structured abstraction tool. Data was analyzed using SPSS version 30 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results: A total of 385 participants were included in the study, with a mean age of 38.6 years. Males accounted for 62.3% of cases. Most participants (94.3%) resided in rural areas, and 62% were HIV-coinfected. Rifampicin-resistant TB was the most common type (51%), followed by MDR-TB (38%). A significant association was observed between age and HIV status (p = 0.001). Treatment outcomes showed that 40.8% of patients were cured, while 11.7% died, with mortality highest among older and HIV-positive patients. Comorbidities reported included hypertension and diabetes mellitus. Conclusions: Most patients included in this facility-based cohort were males, aged 25-39 years, rural residents, living with HIV, with suboptimal treatment outcomes and a substantial comorbidity burden. Strengthened integrated TB/HIV care, early diagnosis, and targeted interventions are needed to improve DR-TB outcomes in this setting.

Title: Comparative Cardiovascular Outcomes in Acalabrutinib vs. Zanubrutinib in B-Cell Malignancies: A TriNetX Data Study.
Abstract: Next-generation Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) such as acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib have improved treatment outcomes in B-cell malignancies, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), and Waldenström macroglobulinemia (WM), while reducing off-target toxicities compared to ibrutinib. However, their comparative cardiovascular safety profiles remain poorly characterized. This study evaluates real-world cardiovascular and clinical outcomes between zanubrutinib and acalabrutinib using a large multi-center database. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (October 2017-December 2024) including adult patients with CLL, MCL, WM, or small B-cell lymphoma treated with zanubrutinib or acalabrutinib. Patients with prior exposure to other BTKis were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 2887 patients were included in each cohort. We assessed one-year outcomes including new-onset atrial fibrillation/flutter, cerebral infarction, hypertension, and all-cause mortality using Cox proportional hazards modeling. The rate of AF/flutter events observed in the zanubrutinib group (4.05%) was numerically lower compared to the acalabrutinib group (5.25%). Time-to-event analysis did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in AF risk over time (HR 0.777, 95% CI 0.597-1.012; p = 0.06), which was similar in binary analysis (OR 0.761, 95% CI 0.581-0.997; p = 0.05). Cerebral infarction rates were similar between groups (1.09% vs. 1.12%), with no significant difference in time-to-event analysis (HR 0.984, 95% CI 0.596-1.626; p = 0.95) or binary analysis (p = 0.91). There was no significant difference in onset of hypertension in the zanubrutinib cohort (HR 1.199, 95% CI 0.957-1.501; p = 0.11) All-cause mortality was not statistically significant between the two groups (HR 0.865, 95% CI 0.740-1.012; p = 0.07). In this large, real-world analysis, fewer AF/flutter events were observed with zanubrutinib at one year; however, time-to-event analysis did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in AF risk over time. Notably, hypertension, cerebral infarction, and all-cause mortality occurred at similar rates. This suggests zanubrutinib and acalabrutinib share similar cardiovascular safety profiles overall. However these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before definitive conclusions about cardiovascular risk can be drawn.

Title: Cancer Cachexia and the Heart: A Review with Focus on China.
Abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic, multifactorial syndrome characterized by progressive depletion of skeletal muscle, disruption of metabolic homeostasis, and reduced survival. In experimental models, cachexia-associated mediators, including inflammatory cytokines, myostatin-related signaling, and proteolytic activation, have been implicated in driving cardiac atrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and impaired myocardial function. Conversely, data from chronic heart failure suggest that reduced tissue perfusion, neurohormonal activation, and sustained inflammation secondary to cardiac dysfunction may further aggravate skeletal muscle wasting. These observations suggest a bidirectional relationship between cancer cachexia and cardiac dysfunction, which has not been tested in patients with cancer. Approximately 4.82 million new cancer cases occur in China annually, with a disease distribution predominated by gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, and thoracic malignancies, all of which carry high risks of cachexia. Among 710,170 Chinese patients with cancer, 5.0% had cardiovascular disease and 13.0% had at least one cardiovascular risk factor. These figures indicate a large population at risk, but they do not show that cardiac involvement in Chinese patients differs in frequency, phenotype, or clinical impact from that in other populations; to our knowledge, no prospective data on cancer-associated cardiac involvement have been reported for Chinese patients, and cachexia assessment does not include cardiac biomarkers or echocardiographic measures. This review summarizes cancer cachexia epidemiology in China, shows the evidence linking cachexia to cardiac wasting, and evaluates how cardiac dysfunction may in turn influence the cachectic trajectory. Accordingly, we outline the key clinical and mechanistic questions that remain unanswered in Chinese patients and propose a research agenda in which cardiac assessment is evaluated prospectively before it is considered for routine care.

Title: CBCT-Guided Online Adaptive Ultrahypofractionated Whole-Breast Radiotherapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer: Dosimetric Outcomes and Acute Toxicity.
Abstract: Ultrahypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy reduces treatment burden but increases the importance of accurate dose delivery at each fraction. This retrospective single-center study evaluated cone-beam computed tomography-guided online adaptive radiotherapy in 55 patients with early-stage breast cancer treated with 26 or 27 Gy in five fractions. Dosimetric analysis was available for 52 patients and 259 paired scheduled and adapted fractions. Linear mixed-effects models with a patient-specific random intercept were used to account for repeated fractions within individual patients. The adapted plan was selected for 242 out of 260 delivered fractions (93.1%). Mean planning target volume V95% increased from 93.52 ± 2.94% with the scheduled plan to 98.13 ± 1.04% with adaptation (p < 0.001), with reduced interfraction variability. Ipsilateral lung V30% increased modestly from 13.94% to 14.96% (p < 0.001). In left-sided cases, no significant differences were observed for heart V25% (1.400% vs. 1.395%; p = 0.3825) or left anterior descending coronary artery D0.03 cm3 (1.771 vs. 1.873 Gy; p = 0.1390). Acute grade 1 toxicity occurred in five patients (9.1%), with no grade ≥ 2 events. Mean treatment-session duration was 28 min. Online adaptation significantly improved daily target coverage and was technically feasible within a five-fraction whole-breast workflow. Acute toxicity was limited in this cohort, while longer follow-up and cumulative dose analyses are needed to further define its impact on organ-at-risk exposure and clinical outcomes.

Title: Challenges of Conducting a Feasibility Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial During COVID-19 Restrictions: Rivaroxaban Versus Acetyl Salicylic Acid in Patients with Multiple Myeloma on Lenalidomide-Based Therapy (RithMM).
Abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a serious medical complication with an increased risk in patients with multiple myeloma undergoing combination treatment regimens. Acetylsalicylic acid is routinely used as a method of thromboprophylaxis in multiple myeloma patients treated with lenalidomide, and rivaroxaban has been assessed in small-scale studies in multiple myeloma patients treated with immunomodulatory drugs; yet, no study has compared the two methods. In this pilot, we asked if a full-scale trial would be feasible to assess the benefits of rivaroxaban over acetylsalicylic acid as a thromboprophylactic approach. This pilot recruited patients with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide-based therapy and randomized them to either low-dose acetylsalicylic acid or rivaroxaban, then monitored bleeding and thrombotic events throughout lenalidomide-dexamethasone treatment. A total of 55 patients were recruited across three Canadian centres, with two venous thromboembolic events and two bleeding events, all in the acetylsalicylic acid arm. We conducted a post hoc analysis of active recruitment time as a definition of recruitment feasibility, as we did not achieve our pre-defined feasibility goals. Despite the challenges in enrollment, possibly due to social restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic, we maintain that a full-scale trial is feasible and offers insight into thromboprophylactic management in this population.

Title: Clinical and Laboratory Factors Associated with Serious Infections in Multiple Myeloma: A Real-World Study.
Abstract: Background: Serious infections remain a major cause of morbidity and treatment disruption in patients with multiple myeloma (MM). Identifying readily available clinical factors associated with infectious complications may facilitate risk-adapted supportive care. This study evaluated clinical and laboratory factors associated with serious infection in patients with MM, including the potential association of baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) with subsequent serious infectious complications. Methods: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 104 patients with MM. Baseline demographic, disease-related, treatment-related, and laboratory characteristics were evaluated. Serious infection was defined as an infectious episode requiring hospitalization. Infectious events were recorded throughout follow-up, including those occurring during second-line and subsequent therapies. Associations with serious infection were assessed using univariate and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses. The primary multivariable model included age, International Staging System (ISS) stage, dialysis requirement at diagnosis, treatment response, and baseline NLR. Results: Serious infections occurred in 39 patients (37.5%). Dialysis requirement at diagnosis (30.8% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.001), failure to achieve treatment response (51.3% vs. 7.7%, p < 0.001), hypogammaglobulinemia (48.7% vs. 29.2%, p = 0.046), and IVIG administration (76.9% vs. 46.2%, p = 0.002) were more frequent among patients with serious infection. Baseline NLR did not differ significantly between patients with and without serious infection. In the multivariable model, dialysis requirement at diagnosis (adjusted OR 8.26, 95% CI 1.81-37.68; p = 0.006) and failure to achieve treatment response (adjusted OR 16.77, 95% CI 4.37-64.31; p < 0.001) were independently associated with serious infection, whereas age, ISS stage, and baseline NLR were not. Conclusions: Serious infections were common in this real-world MM cohort. Dialysis requirement at diagnosis and failure to achieve treatment response were independently associated with serious infection, whereas baseline NLR was not independently associated with serious infectious complications. These findings suggest that clinical characteristics reflecting renal dysfunction and treatment response may be useful for identifying patients at increased risk of serious infection. The observed association between IVIG administration and serious infection should be interpreted cautiously because of potential confounding by indication and reverse causality.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Risk Stratification and Factors Associated with Heart Failure Hospitalization During Osimertinib Therapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is the standard of care for epidermal growth factor receptor mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer, but heart failure hospitalization (HFH) remains a concern, and no practical tool exists to stratify HFH risk during therapy.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study using a Japanese claims database, 5802 patients newly initiating osimertinib were followed for HFH during treatment. Baseline predictors assessed before the index date were selected by 10-fold cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression and internally validated by bootstrapping (B = 500), repeating predictor selection in each resample. Cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event; cause-specific Cox models served as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: HFH occurred in 169 patients (2.9%) during a median on-treatment follow-up of 9.3 months, with 268 competing deaths. LASSO retained seven predictors. The apparent concordance index (C-index) was 0.731 (95% confidence interval, 0.691-0.771) and the optimism-corrected C-index 0.718. Observed incidence increased 10.2-fold across predicted-risk deciles (1.03-10.50%). Fine-Gray and Cox estimates closely matched the logistic model.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline cardiovascular vulnerability stratifies HFH risk during osimertinib therapy. The nomogram, not externally validated, is best used as a screening aid to identify patients who may benefit from intensified cardiovascular monitoring.

Title: Machine Perfusion and Oncologic Outcomes After Liver Transplantation for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Machine perfusion has emerged as a promising strategy to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury during liver transplantation (LT). However, its impact on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence and post-transplant oncologic outcomes remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the association between machine perfusion and oncologic outcomes after LT for HCC.
METHODS: A systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to May 2026. Comparative clinical studies evaluating machine perfusion and oncologic outcomes after LT for HCC were included. The primary outcome was recurrence-free survival (RFS). Secondary outcomes included HCC recurrence, early recurrence, overall survival (OS), and graft-related outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed when appropriate.
RESULTS: Six comparative clinical studies involving HCC recipients undergoing LT were included. All studies were observational, and no randomized controlled trial was identified. Three studies were judged to have a moderate risk of bias and three were judged to have a serious risk of bias. In the primary RFS meta-analysis, machine perfusion was associated with a numerically lower risk of recurrence or death, although the pooled estimate did not reach statistical significance (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.07-1.77; p = 0.20). The binary recurrence analysis also demonstrated a numerically lower risk of HCC recurrence after machine perfusion (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.13-1.20; p = 0.10). Several studies reported favorable associations between machine perfusion and early recurrence, while large adjusted cohorts reported associations with improved RFS and OS. Machine perfusion was generally associated with lower markers of ischemia-reperfusion injury, including postoperative aminotransferase release.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests a potential favorable association between machine perfusion and oncologic outcomes after LT for HCC. However, the pooled estimates from the primary analyses were not statistically significant, and the evidence remains limited by the small number of studies, observational designs, heterogeneity, and potential cohort overlap. Further prospective studies are required before an oncologic benefit of machine perfusion can be established.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Cardiotoxicity of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors with Anthracycline Chemotherapy in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
Abstract: Background/Aim: The addition of an immune-checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) to chemotherapy improves outcomes in both early-stage and metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, ICIs are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs), such as cardiotoxicity, raising concerns for patients receiving both anthracyclines and ICIs. We sought to determine if combining anthracycline and ICI in TNBC is associated with greater cardiotoxicity than anthracycline alone. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a large academic center. Two cohorts were analyzed: anthracycline plus ICI and anthracycline alone. Demographics, comorbidities, medications, cardiac imaging, and outcomes were reviewed. Time to adverse cardiac events were compared. Results: A total of 382 patients were included: 297 received anthracyclines without ICI, and 85 received both. There were no major differences in baseline characteristics. The rate of acute cardiac events was 3.4% in the anthracycline-alone cohort and 3.5% in the anthracycline-plus-ICI cohort (p > 0.99) over a median of 1232 days of follow up (median of 1336 days in the anthracycline only group; median of 704 days in the ICI group). No significant differences in acute heart failure, acute coronary syndrome, myocarditis, or pericardial effusion were observed. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in cardiac event-free survival (p = 0.60). Furthermore, there was no significant difference in time to cardiac events between the two groups following competing risk analysis when accounting for both prior coronary artery disease (HR = 1.32, 95% CI: [0.42, 4.14], p = 0.64) and age (HR = 1.64, 95% CI: [0.52, 5.19], p = 0.40). Conclusions: This single-institution analysis did not identify a significant increase in cardiotoxicity with the addition of an ICI to anthracycline therapy in patients with TNBC. Active surveillance for cardiotoxicities should continue in patients receiving ICI in addition to anthracycline therapy.

Title: Analytical Characterization, Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Preliminary Immunogenicity of GNR-062, an Agalsidase Beta Biosimilar Candidate, in Healthy Male Volunteers.
Abstract: Fabry disease is a rare genetic multisystemic lysosomal disease characterized by progressive cellular accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) in various organs with specific cutaneous (angiokeratoma), neurological (pain), renal (proteinuria, chronic kidney failure), cardiovascular (cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia), cochleovestibular and cerebrovascular manifestations (transient ischemic attacks, strokes). The phenotypic expression depends on the age of onset and, in females, on the level of X-inactivation. Enzyme replacement therapy is currently the standard therapy for the disease. JSC GENERIUM recently developed a potential biosimilar of Fabrazyme®, GNR-062, and investigated its physicochemical and biological properties, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity to assess its bioequivalence to Fabrazyme®. Direct evaluation of the N-glycosylation profile by HPLC revealed differences mainly related to the distribution of complex sialylated glycans. The overall sialylation level was comparable between the two products. The same conclusion follows from the results of direct analysis of the sialic acid content. Despite a small difference of a few percent in biphosphorylated glycan content, the overall measured M6P values were comparable. Thus, the internalization of agalsidase β into the inner space of lysosomes by binding to key receptors appear to be the same for both products. In a single-blind, randomized comparative study of the pharmacokinetics and safety of a single intravenous infusion of GNR-062 (JSC GENERIUM, Russia) and Fabrazyme® (Genzyme Europe B.V., The Netherlands) in a crossover design in healthy volunteers, the ratio of geometric means (90% CI) of AUCinf and Cmax for GNR-062 to agalsidase β was 0.9736 (0.9413-1.0070) and 0.9867 (0.9546-1.0199), respectively. These studies demonstrated pharmacokinetic bioequivalence of GNR-062 to agalsidase β. Immunogenicity findings are preliminary, as the study was not powered for formal immunogenicity equivalence, and the single-dose design in healthy volunteers does not reflect repeated long-term administration in patients with Fabry disease. In conclusion, GNR-062 demonstrated acceptable short-term tolerability in healthy volunteers and warrants further investigation as a potential therapeutic option for patients with Fabry disease.

Title: Stroke Lesion Location Is Associated with Dynamic Inspiratory Performance: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: We examined whether respiratory performance differed among broad stroke lesion-location categories.
METHODS: This exploratory single-center cross-sectional analysis combined pre-intervention assessments from 20 participants in an earlier trial with 60 subsequently recruited participants. The 80 patients were classified into frontal lobe (n = 27), basal ganglia region (n = 26), or brainstem (n = 27) categories. Peak inspiratory flow (PIF), strength index (S-Index), and five conventional respiratory outcomes were assessed. Holm correction was applied across seven outcomes. Linear models used type 3 heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) robust standard errors and the original six clinical covariates. Additional PIF analyses incorporated time since stroke, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), or modified Barthel Index (MBI), and restricted the sample to ischemic or first-ever stroke.
RESULTS: Only PIF retained an unadjusted group association after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.008). The adjusted overall lesion-location association also survived correction (adjusted p = 0.009). PIF was 0.625 L/s higher in the basal ganglia region than in the brainstem group (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.282-0.967). This contrast persisted with additional clinical adjustment in the full cohort and in ischemic stroke. Evidence weakened in first-ever stroke; with MBI adjustment, the contrast was 0.381 L/s (95% CI, -0.067-0.829).
CONCLUSIONS: Broad lesion-location categories were associated with PIF in this selected cohort. The findings remain exploratory and cannot fully separate anatomical associations from stroke severity, disability, unmeasured clinical factors, or measurement limitations.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Inhaled Treprostinil in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic interstitial lung disease with high morbidity and mortality. Inhaled treprostinil showed pulmonary vascular and lung-function signals in pulmonary hypertension associated with Interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and was subsequently tested in IPF trials.
OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of inhaled treprostinil in adults with IPF.
METHODS: PubMed, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Library/CENTRAL were searched for records published from January 2000 to 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis used the DerSimonian-Laird tau squared and inverse-variance weighting methods. Continuous outcomes were pooled as generic inverse-variance effects from reported estimates and 95% confidence intervals. Hazard ratios were pooled on the log scale. Safety outcomes were pooled as risk ratios from event counts.
RESULTS: The searches identified 1552 records. After deduplication, 379 records were screened and 85 full-text reports were assessed. Eleven reports were included in the systematic review. TETON-1 and TETON-2 were the two direct-IPF randomized trials within the coordinated TETON program eligible for primary meta-analysis. Inhaled treprostinil improved absolute forced vital capacity (FVC) change at 52 weeks compared with placebo (MD 111.28 mL, 95% CI 77.61 to 144.95, p < 0.001; I squared 8.5%). Clinical worsening was reduced (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.84, p < 0.001; I squared 0.0%). Acute exacerbation was lower in pooled analysis (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.91, p = 0.022), while all-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.05, p = 0.086). Adverse-event discontinuation, cough and headache were more frequent with treprostinil.
CONCLUSIONS: In direct IPF randomized evidence, inhaled treprostinil preserved lung function and reduced clinical worsening at 52 weeks.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Deciphering the Benefits and Risks of Single-Inhaler Triple Therapy in COPD.
Abstract: Single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) combines an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS; for example, fluticasone furoate, budesonide, or beclometasone dipropionate), a long-acting β2-agonist (LABA; for example, vilanterol or formoterol fumarate), and a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA; for example, umeclidinium or glycopyrronium bromide) in one device. Triple pharmacological therapy reduces exacerbations in selected patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but its effects on mortality and cardiovascular outcomes remain uncertain. This structured narrative review summarizes randomized trials, observational comparative-effectiveness studies, target trial emulations, systematic reviews, and health technology assessments published between 2015 and 2026. We grouped the evidence by comparator: LABA/LAMA, ICS/LABA, multiple-inhaler triple therapy (MITT), and ICS continuation versus withdrawal, because each comparison addresses a different clinical question. Pivotal trials and evidence syntheses consistently showed fewer moderate-to-severe exacerbations with triple therapy, with reported rate ratios of approximately 0.69-0.93. Mortality signals from IMPACT and ETHOS are clinically important, but previous ICS use and ICS withdrawal among participants assigned to ICS-free comparators make these findings difficult to interpret. Observational cardiovascular findings are also uncertain because residual confounding, treatment selection, exposure misclassification, outcome misclassification, and differences in baseline disease severity limit causal interpretation. Compared with MITT, the main advantages of SITT are simpler treatment and possible improvements in adherence and persistence, not greater pharmacological potency. Treatment decisions should consider exacerbation history, repeated blood eosinophil counts, pneumonia risk, cardiovascular disease, previous ICS exposure and response, inhaler technique, device suitability, and patient preference. Trials in patients with documented absence of previous ICS use and well-designed target trial emulations are needed to determine whether the observed mortality and cardiovascular associations are causal.

Title: Patterns of Falls and Fractures Among Older Adults Undergoing Rehabilitation After Fall-Related Fractures: A Retrospective Study in Croatia.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: The injury patterns of older patients who reach rehabilitation after a fall-related fracture are rarely described. We aimed to describe these patients and to examine how age, sex, recorded chronic conditions, osteoporosis and previous fractures relate to the mechanism of injury and the fracture site. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, the records of 255 patients aged 65 years and over who entered a rehabilitation programme at a Croatian rehabilitation hospital after a fall-related fracture between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2025 were extracted from the hospital information system and analysed using the chi-square test, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis test and Spearman rank correlation. Results: Women accounted for 74.9% of the sample and hip fracture was the most frequent site (52.9%). Ground-level falls caused 78.8% of fractures overall, 95.2% of those in patients aged 85 years and over, and 86.7% of hip fractures; the mechanism of injury differed by sex, age group and fracture site (all p ≤ 0.005). Cardiovascular disease was recorded in 78.0% of patients but osteoporosis in only 19.2%. Both osteoporosis (p = 0.041) and having two or more recorded chronic conditions (p = 0.012) were associated with the mechanism of injury, but not with the fracture site. Conclusions: Hip fractures and ground-level falls predominated, particularly in the oldest patients. The findings support systematic nursing assessment of fall circumstances, chronic disease burden, bone health and fracture history after a fall.
