Title: Relationship Between Social Isolation, Loneliness, and Systemic Inflammation: A Scoping Review of Biological Signatures and Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social isolation and loneliness are established social determinants of health, associated with 25-30% higher mortality risk, yet their relationship with systemic inflammation and broader biological and clinical outcomes has not been comprehensively synthesized across life stages.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched (2015-2025), supplemented by citation searching and a targeted supplementary search, for human studies linking social isolation, loneliness, or social connectedness to inflammatory biomarkers or biological/clinical outcomes. PRISMA-ScR guidance was followed; findings were synthesized narratively across five thematic axes as an evidence map.
RESULTS: Of 3351 records identified, 73 studies were included. Isolation was most often associated with CRP and fibrinogen, and loneliness with IL-6. Isolation predicted sarcopenia, venous thromboembolism, pancreatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with inflammatory or metabolic markers mediating a modest (≈5-19%) share. Proteomic (n = 42,062) and epigenetic analyses linked loneliness to inflammatory, antiviral, and complement-pathway proteins and to accelerated epigenetic ageing; Mendelian randomization supported causal involvement of several proteins. Social connectedness and relationship quality tracked with lower IL-6 and better functional indices. Evidence was strongest in midlife and older cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Social disconnection shows biologically plausible but heterogeneous associations with inflammatory and molecular signatures; harmonized measurement and prospective, hypothesis-free omics designs are needed to clarify causality and inform targeted screening.

Title: Real-World Pharmacological Patterns and Residual Cardiometabolic Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes in Romania.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has shifted from a glucose-centered approach toward integrated cardio-renal-metabolic protection. Although sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and intensive lipid-lowering therapies have demonstrated substantial cardiovascular and renal benefits, implementation in routine outpatient care and the burden of persistent residual risk remain insufficiently characterized in Romania.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate routine-care pharmacological treatment patterns, identify residual cardio-renal-metabolic risk despite ongoing therapy, determine independent correlates of persistent adverse outcomes, and explore potential therapeutic gaps in adults with T2DM.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 232 unique adults with T2DM attending a specialized outpatient diabetes clinic in Romania between 1 October 2024 and 19 February 2026. One eligible outpatient record per participant was analyzed; when multiple records were available, the earliest eligible record in the exported dataset was used as the index visit. No a priori sample-size calculation was performed. Pharmacological therapies, cardiovascular and renal phenotypes, metabolic biomarkers, and clinical outcomes were extracted from routinely collected electronic medical records. Residual risk was evaluated using glycemic, lipid, renal, obesity, and blood-pressure targets. Multivariable logistic regression analyses identified independent correlates of persistent cardio-metabolic abnormalities. An exploratory cumulative residual-risk count was constructed by summing seven clinically relevant uncontrolled risk factors.
RESULTS: Biguanides were the most frequently prescribed glucose-lowering agents (53.0%), followed by SGLT2 inhibitors (44.8%), insulin (32.3% of the total cohort), GLP-1 receptor agonists (15.5%), and DPP-4 inhibitors (14.7%). Statins were prescribed to 48.7% of participants. SGLT2 inhibitor use did not differ significantly according to established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease phenotypes, whereas GLP-1 receptor agonists were prescribed more frequently in participants with obesity (22.0% vs. 7.6%, p = 0.003). Clinically important residual risk persisted across all treatment groups. Among SGLT2 inhibitor users, 57.3% had HbA1c ≥ 7%, while 27.9% remained albuminuric. Among insulin-treated participants, 84.0% had HbA1c ≥ 7%; reduced eGFR and albuminuria were also more frequent than among non-users. Despite statin therapy, 33.6% of treated participants continued to exhibit LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL. In multivariable logistic regression, insulin therapy was associated with higher odds of HbA1c ≥ 7% (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.50-15.65), while SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with lower odds of albuminuria (aOR 0.54, 95% CI 0.30-0.95). Absence of statin-containing therapy was associated with higher odds of LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL (aOR 6.01, 95% CI 3.38-10.66). Absence of statin-containing therapy was associated with higher odds of residual LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL (aOR 4.21, 95% CI 2.34-7.58). Seventy-two percent of participants presented at least three persistent cardio-renal-metabolic abnormalities, while 24.2% exhibited five or more. More than half of participants with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease were not receiving either an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist.
CONCLUSIONS: Significant residual cardio-renal-metabolic risk persists in adults with T2DM despite use of contemporary pharmacological therapies. Disease severity markers and treatment exposure were associated with persistent adverse outcomes, but the cross-sectional design does not establish causality. The study identified potentially modifiable therapeutic gaps among patients with established cardiovascular and renal disease. Comprehensive and repeatedly reassessed cardio-renal-metabolic management, integrating pharmacological optimization with individualized risk stratification, may improve implementation of guideline-directed therapy and reduce long-term complications in routine clinical practice.

Title: Cognitive-Affective Dimension After Virological Cure of Hepatitis C Virus Infection: WBSI Dynamics, Liver Status, and the Role of Comorbidities.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Virological cure in chronic infection with hepatitis C virus (HCV) is followed by important clinical and biological benefits, including psychological ones. The White Bear Suppression Inventory (WBSI) assesses the tendency to suppress intrusive thoughts and was used in this study as a tool to provide a cognitive-affective assessment of patients with chronic HCV infection-both at the start of antiviral therapy and five years after achieving virological cure.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize patients with HCV infection who received antiviral therapy and completed the WBSI, to assess longitudinal changes in WBSI scores, and to identify clinical, biological, and comorbidity-related factors associated with these changes.
METHODS: The study employed an ambispective observational longitudinal cohort study design conducted on a sample of 386 patients, of whom 81 completed the WBSI both at baseline and at follow-up.
RESULTS: The WBSI subsample did not differ significantly from the remainder of the cohort in terms of age, cytolysis markers, bilirubin, albumin, platelet count, or major comorbidities. The WBSI score decreased significantly from baseline to follow-up, from 61.36 to 54.16, with a mean difference of 7.20 points (t = 6.32; p < 0.001). The correlation between the baseline and follow-up scores was very strong (r = 0.899; p < 0.001), indicating substantial interindividual stability. ΔWBSI was weakly but significantly correlated with the change in total bilirubin (r = 0.254; p = 0.022), with no significant correlations with the other biological markers. In the multivariable model, cardiovascular comorbidities (B = -8.469; p < 0.001) and metabolic comorbidities (B = -9.869; p = 0.002) were independent negative predictors of WBSI scoring, whereas fibrosis evolution, age, sex, and baseline total bilirubin had no significant influence.
CONCLUSIONS: Improvements in WBSI scores observed only in specific patient subgroups, one year after achieving HCV virological cure, underscore the need to integrate psychological assessment into long-term monitoring, particularly for patients with cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities.

Title: Temporal Distribution of Elevated-HbA1c Records and a Young-Adult Multiorgan Biomarker Profile in Diabetes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Diabetes-related renal, lipid, and hepatic abnormalities are clinically important, but their distribution may be heterogeneous and is not fully represented by HbA1c alone. We characterized the temporal age and sex composition of elevated-HbA1c records and, separately, the multiorgan biomarker profile of a 2022 young-adult subcohort.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed 1160 patient-year records classified as having elevated HbA1c from 2019-2022. These were annual record strata rather than 1160 unique individuals or a cohort followed as participants aged. A separate cross-sectional biomarker subcohort comprised 49 adults aged 18-29 years in 2022, of whom 26 were source-classified as having elevated HbA1c. Annual age and sex distributions were assessed using chi-square tests. Biomarker abnormalities were summarized with biomarker-specific denominators and Wilson 95% confidence intervals; sex comparisons were exploratory and used Fisher's exact tests, odds ratios, φ coefficients, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction.
RESULTS: Age composition differed across calendar years (χ2[6] = 45.02, p < 0.001; Cramér's V = 0.139), with adults aged ≥60 years accounting for 50.0% of elevated-HbA1c records in 2022. Sex composition also varied (χ2[3] = 19.47, p < 0.001; Cramér's V = 0.130). In the young-adult biomarker subcohort, the most frequent abnormalities were total cholesterol (60.0%), triglycerides (53.8%), UACR (45.5%), urea (40.0%), uric acid (40.0%), and ALT (35.3%). Elevated urea showed the largest female-to-male odds ratio (17.50, 95% CI 1.22-250.37; p = 0.041), but no sex-biomarker association remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction (minimum q = 0.295).
CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrates temporal heterogeneity in elevated-HbA1c record composition and a descriptive young-adult biomarker profile dominated by dyslipidemia, albuminuria, selected renal-metabolic abnormalities, and ALT elevation. Because the archived dataset did not retain the paired continuous HbA1c-biomarker data or older-age biomarker data needed for dose-response or cross-age comparisons, the findings should not be interpreted as establishing an HbA1c-linked multiorgan causal relationship. They support the value of integrated organ-risk assessment and the need for prospective patient-level analyses across HbA1c and age strata.

Title: Role of Interleukin 17 in Severe Acute Pancreatitis: Human Retrospective Pilot Study.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Severe acute pancreatitis accounts for 20% of acute pancreatitis episodes and carries a substantial mortality risk. The systematic severity of the disease is driven by a massive cytokine release, with Interleukin-17 (IL-17) acting as a crucial modulator of the pro-inflammatory cascade. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of serum IL-17 at admission and correlate it with multi-organ dysfunctions and clinical-biological outcomes in patients with severe acute pancreatitis. Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a cohort of 35 patients with severe acute pancreatitis. Demographic, etiological, and clinical-biological baseline characteristics were extracted. Serum IL-17 levels were determined at admission using the ELISA method, and data were statistically analyzed. Results: Significantly higher levels of IL-17 were observed in patients who developed multi-organ failure. Prognostic thresholds were identified via ROC analysis to predict organ dysfunctions: ≥19.77 pg/mL for neurological dysfunction (AUC = 0.814, p = 0.003) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (AUC = 0.756, p = 0.024); ≥18.45 pg/mL for respiratory (p = 0.004) and cardiovascular dysfunctions (AUC = 0.820, p = 0.002); and ≥19.81 pg/mL for renal dysfunction (AUC = 0.735, p = 0.020). Furthermore, univariate binary logistic regression identified elevated serum IL-17 as a significant prognostic factor for mortality among patients admitted to the intensive care unit (OR = 1.062, p = 0.048). Conclusions: Serum IL-17 at admission functions as a significant prognostic biomarker that reflects the severe systemic pro-inflammatory status in severe acute pancreatitis and mirrors the risk of subsequent organ dysfunctions and mortality. Incorporating IL-17 into initial risk stratification protocols may assist clinicians in timely therapeutic escalation.

Title: Temporal Dynamics of Emerging Cardiovascular Biomarkers in the Early Phase After Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Prospective Single-Center Pilot Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Despite successful primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI), early myocardial injury and stress may contribute to left ventricular dysfunction. The optimal timing of biomarker assessment after STEMI remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the early kinetics of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity-2 (sST2), galectin-3 (Gal-3), mid-regional pro-adrenomedullin (MR-proADM), and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15) during the first 96 h after STEMI and identify potentially informative sampling time points for future prognostic assessment. Secondary, exploratory objectives were to evaluate differences in biomarker concentrations according to symptom duration, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and infarct-related artery.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center, exploratory pilot study, patients aged 18-75 years with first STEMI treated with pPCI within 6 h of symptom onset were enrolled between September 2024 and November 2025. Blood samples were collected at admission and 12 ± 4, 24 ± 4, 48 ± 8, and 96 ± 8 h after pPCI. Biomarkers were measured by ELISA, with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) as a reference marker of myocardial injury.
RESULTS: Of 46 enrolled patients, 16 were excluded, mostly due to early discharge, and 30 patients with complete samples at all five time points were included in the analysis (mean age 57.9 ± 11.1 years; 66.7% male). sST2, MR-proADM, and hs-cTnI showed significant temporal variation (all p < 0.001), with the highest measured concentrations of sST2 at 12 h and of MR-proADM at 24 h. No significant change over time was found for Gal-3 and GDF-15. In exploratory analyses, sST2 and MR-proADM concentrations were higher in patients with LVEF < 40%, and sST2 concentrations were higher in patients with left anterior descending artery (LAD) infarction. Symptom duration was not associated with biomarker concentrations.
CONCLUSIONS: sST2 and MR-proADM show distinct early post-STEMI kinetics, suggesting potentially informative sampling windows for future prognostic studies. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these kinetics and the exploratory differences according to left ventricular function and infarct location, and to evaluate the prognostic value of these sampling windows with echocardiographic and clinical follow-up.

Title: Can Thyroid Dysfunction Contribute to Infertility via Lipid Abnormalities?
Abstract: Thyroid dysfunction alters lipid metabolism and may impair reproduction, raising the possibility that lipid abnormalities contribute to thyroid-related infertility. This review evaluates dyslipidemia as a potential mechanistic link between these conditions. Thyroid hormones regulate hepatic LDL clearance, triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism and HDL remodeling. Overt hypothyroidism commonly increases total and LDL cholesterol, changes that are partly reversible with levothyroxine, whereas lipid abnormalities in subclinical and central hypothyroidism are smaller and less consistent; hyperthyroidism generally lowers total and LDL cholesterol. Independently, adverse circulating lipid profiles are associated with reduced natural fecundability and poorer outcomes in selected assisted-reproduction studies. Experimental evidence identifies biologically coherent pathways involving ovarian steroidogenesis, follicular HDL function, oocyte cholesterol efflux and membrane signaling, endometrial receptivity and sperm membrane integrity. Human evidence supports both the thyroid-lipid and lipid-fertility relationships, but does not establish that lipid abnormalities mediate thyroid-related infertility. Interpretation is complicated by direct thyroid hormone effects, thyroid autoimmunity and metabolic confounding. Taken together, current findings support dyslipidemia as a biologically plausible potential contributor to thyroid-related reproductive dysfunction. Clinically, they suggest considering integrated assessment of thyroid and lipid status in reproductive-age adults and reassessment of the lipid profile after restoration of euthyroidism. Prospective preconception studies incorporating functional lipid measurements and formal mediation analyses are needed.

Title: TMAO at the Crossroads of the Gut-Brain Axis: Emerging Mechanisms Linking Microbiota-Derived Metabolites to Neuroinflammation and Cognitive Dysfunction.
Abstract: Trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) is a gut microbiota-derived metabolite produced through the hepatic oxidation of trimethylamine. Although TMAO has been widely investigated as a therapeutic target in multiple cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, growing evidence suggests it may play a critical role in the neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction associated with the gut-brain axis. This narrative review summarizes the current literature to synthesize evidence on the mechanisms linking TMAO with neurological disorders; it discusses potential mechanisms contributing to this association, with particular focus on neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and activation of inflammatory pathways. Overall, this review also suggests the potential use of TMAO and its precursors as therapeutic targets for multiple neurodegenerative disorders. However, it emphasizes the need for conducting large, adequately powered randomized clinical studies to determine its therapeutic relevance.

Title: In Vivo Study of Topical Bimatoprost, Latanoprost, Travoprost in Comparison with Minoxidil on Hair Growth in C57BL/6 Mice.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alopecia significantly affects psychological well-being and social functioning. Standard treatments, like minoxidil and finasteride, are limited by delayed efficacy, need for lifelong use, and adverse effects. Prostaglandin analogs (PGAs), originally developed for ocular hypertension, have shown promise in promoting hair growth. This study compares their effects with minoxidil in a murine model.
AIM AND OBJECTIVES: To compare the effects of bimatoprost, latanoprost, and travoprost on hair growth in C57BL/6 mice, with evaluation of hair density, follicle diameter, and growth rate using minoxidil as the comparator.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: After Institutional Animal Ethics Committee approval, 40 male C57BL/6 mice (aged 6-7 weeks, weighing 20-25 g) were randomized into five groups ( n = 8 in each group): (1) vehicle control, (2) minoxidil 5%, (3) latanoprost 0.005%, (4) bimatoprost 0.03%, and (5) travoprost 0.004%. Drugs were applied topically to shaved dorsal skin daily for 28 days. Hair growth was assessed by follicle density, bulb diameter, and area of regrowth using ImageJ from photographs taken on days 1, 7, 15, and 28.
RESULTS: All PGAs significantly increased hair density compared to vehicle control (vehicle control: 1.50 ± 0.55 vs. latanoprost: 7.50 ± 1.69, bimatoprost: 7.75 ± 2.87, travoprost: 6.87 ± 3.40; P = 0.001). Latanoprost and bimatoprost showed higher hair density than minoxidil (3.75 ± 2.87; P = 0.038 and 0.010, respectively). Hair follicle diameter was greater with PGAs (latanoprost: 53.12 ± 5.30, bimatoprost: 51.87 ± 7.52, travoprost: 48.12 ± 3.47 μm) versus vehicle control (27.91 ± 5.57 μm, P = 0.001) and minoxidil (38.12 ± 5.46 μm, P = 0.001). Bimatoprost showed the greatest regrowth by day 28, while latanoprost demonstrated earlier onset by day 15. PGAs also caused darker pigmentation and longer hair.
LIMITATIONS: The present study duration was limited to 4 weeks. Minoxidil (positive control) did not show noticeable hair growth because its effects usually take 6-8 weeks to appear.
CONCLUSION: Topical PGAs improved key hair growth parameters. Bimatoprost and latanoprost showed early and superior efficacy by day 28.

Title: Characterizing hypertension in activated PI3K delta syndrome: Findings from Epic Cosmos.
Abstract: APDS is a rare inborn error of immunity with comorbidity patterns that have yet to be characterized at a large scale. Using Epic Cosmos, a de-identified electronic health record database, we conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 866 patients identified by structured diagnosis codes (ICD-10: D84.81; SNOMED: 793412000). Findings revealed that hypertension was coded as affecting 28.5% of the cohort, with age-stratified analyses demonstrating higher prevalence among younger APDS patients compared with age-matched non-APDS peers. Among patients aged ≤50 years, hypertension prevalence was 24.05% in the APDS group compared with 10.89% in the age-matched non-APDS population (prevalence ratio 2.21, 95% CI, 1.90-2.57, P < 0.0001). This association remained prominent in a more specific APDS sensitivity cohort in which the base population required an APDS diagnosis, alongside an allergy and immunology encounter. The findings of this paper provide large-scale characterization of APDS and identify hypertension, particularly among younger APDS patients, as a potentially underrecognized comorbidity that warrants further investigation.

Title: Foveal Avascular Zone and Its Associations - An Analysis Using OCTA: Results From the Gutenberg Health Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to describe the distribution and ocular and systemic associations of the foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area in Caucasians in a population-based setting.
METHODS: We included 1004 participants (aged 59.91 ± 9.39 years; 49.3% female) of the 10-year follow-up of the Gutenberg Health Study, a population-based, prospective cohort Study in Mainz, Germany, with gradable optical coherence tomography angiography of the macula. The FAZ area of the total retina was measured manually. Linear regression analysis was conducted to evaluate the associations of the FAZ area with ocular and systemic factors.
RESULTS: The mean FAZ area was 0.27 ± 0.12 mm2. It was associated with female sex (B-estimate 0.04; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.03-0.06; P < 0.001) and inversely with axial length (B-estimate -0.02; 95% CI, -0.03 to -0.01; P < 0.001). Multivariable analysis of the FAZ area confirmed the associations with sex and axial length. No association was found with age, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, chronic kidney disease, socioeconomic status, or best-corrected visual acuity.
CONCLUSIONS: The FAZ area was larger in females and in participants with a shorter axial length indicating that both ocular and anthropometric factors may influence FAZ size.
TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: This study provides normative data of the foveal avascular zone area in an adult Caucasian population and describes the ocular and systemic associations that have to be taken into account when interpreting optical coherence tomography angiography data in Caucasians.

Title: Association Between Systemic Arterial Stiffness and Choroidal Vascular Resistance Assessed by Laser Speckle Flowgraphy in Diabetic Retinopathy.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the association between peripapillary choroidal hemodynamics, as measured by laser speckle flowgraphy (LSFG), and systemic arterial stiffness, indicated by the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI), in patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR).
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 72 eyes from 72 patients with type 2 diabetes across DR stages were analyzed. Choroidal parameters, including mean blur rate (MBR; indicating blood flow), beat strength (BS; reflecting pulsatility), and the BS/MBR ratio (BOM; a resistance-related waveform index), were quantified in both temporal and nasal peripapillary regions. A stepwise multiple regression analysis was conducted to identify independent predictors of CAVI, considering age, sex, and LSFG parameters.
RESULTS: In univariate analyses, higher CAVI was significantly associated with increased choroidal pulsatility and resistance (P < 0.05). In the final exploratory stepwise multivariable model, age remained significantly associated with higher CAVI (β = 0.048, P = 0.020), while temporal BOM showed a borderline positive trend with CAVI (β = 2.719, P = 0.055). The model was statistically significant overall (adjusted R² = 0.326, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DR, age was the most robust determinant of CAVI. The retention of regional choroidal BOM parameters in the final exploratory stepwise model suggests a possible association whereby systemic pulsatile stress may influence choroidal hemodynamics, although these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: LSFG-derived choroidal resistance (BOM) may help explore the ocular-systemic vascular connection in diabetes management.

Title: Retinal Microvascular and Neuronal Alterations in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights From a Population-Based Screening Program (START2).
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore early microvascular and neuronal retinal alterations in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and their associations with lesion distribution, systemic factors, treatment exposure, and lifestyle variables in a real-world screening cohort.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 1978 eyes from 998 participants observed in a diabetic retinopathy screening program underwent ultra-widefield fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT-angiography (OCTA) (CIRRUS 5000 HD-OCT with AngioPlex). Ganglion cell layer and inner plexiform layer (GCL-IPL) thickness was measured by OCT, and OCTA assessed skeletonized vessel density (SVD) in the superficial capillary plexus (SCP) and deep capillary plexus (DCP). Retinal lesions were classified as not visible or as central or peripheral, or both. Mixed-effects models were used to compare lesion groups and assess associations with systemic and lifestyle factors.
RESULTS: Of 1978 eyes, 1468 (74%) had no visible lesions, and 510 (26%) showed lesions (229 peripheral only, 132 central only, 149 both). Eyes with both lesions exhibited significantly reduced SVD compared with eyes without lesions (SCP, P = 0.019; DCP, P = 0.035) and with peripheral-only lesions (SCP, P = 0.005; DCP, P = 0.019). No significant differences were found for GCL-IPL. GCL-IPL thickness was associated with older age (P < 0.001) and higher body mass index (P = 0.020), and reduced SVD-SCP was associated with older age (P < 0.001) and higher glycated hemoglobin (P = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: Combined central and peripheral lesions are associated with greater microvascular impairment. Age and glycemic control are key determinants of early retinal microvascular changes in T2DM, and age and body mass index relate to GCL-IPL thickness, highlighting the need for a multidisciplinary approach to improve early detection, risk stratification, and ocular and systemic management.

Title: AI-Based OCT Assessment of Anatomic Response During the Loading Phase of Anti-VEGF Therapy in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare functional and anatomic outcomes after the loading phase of intravitreal bevacizumab, aflibercept 2 mg, or faricimab in treatment-naive neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), using artificial intelligence (AI)-based optical coherence tomography (OCT) analysis.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 224 eyes. Patients received three monthly injections of bevacizumab (n = 80), aflibercept 2 mg (n = 78), or faricimab (n = 66). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and spectral-domain OCT were assessed at baseline and week 12. AI-based segmentation quantified volumetric measurements of intraretinal fluid (IRFv), subretinal fluid (SRFv), and pigment epithelial detachment. The primary outcome was qualitative dry macula (absence of intraretinal fluid and subretinal fluid). An exploratory composite OCT biomarker (ΔCOMBO), defined as the lesser percentage reduction between IRFv and SRFv, was evaluated as a hypothesis-generating metric using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Baseline-adjusted analyses and multivariable logistic regression were performed.
RESULTS: Descriptive within-group analyses showed improvement in BCVA and reduction in OCT parameters at week 12 in treatment groups. BCVA improvement was statistically significant in the bevacizumab and faricimab groups. In baseline-adjusted analyses, between-group differences emerged for OCT outcomes, whereas no significant between-group differences were observed for BCVA. Higher rates of dry macula were observed with faricimab (80.3%) and aflibercept 2 mg (67.9%) compared with bevacizumab (41.3%) (P < 0.001). The exploratory composite metric ΔCOMBO showed high discriminative performance (area under the curve = 0.959; 95% confidence interval, 0.907-0.999).
CONCLUSIONS: All agents improved functional and anatomic outcomes after the loading phase in treatment-naive nAMD. Baseline-adjusted analyses showed differences in anatomic response patterns across treatments. Exploratory AI-based OCT biomarkers may help characterize short-term anatomic response; however, these findings require external validation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Medical emergency response related to MedicAtion InciDents (MERRMAID): a case series and lessons to improve medication safety.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence suggests that some medical emergencies in hospital are associated with preventable medication errors or adverse reactions.
AIM: The purpose of this case series was to investigate and describe the proportion of Medical Emergency Response Team (MERT) activations that are medication-related, the degree of preventability and underlying contributing factors.
METHOD: This retrospective case series included a review of MERT activations collected from an Australian tertiary hospital by two separate multidisciplinary teams. Initial review by the research team identified those that were potentially medication-related; these cases were then reviewed by an expert panel to determine the degree of causation and preventability and to identify errors within the medication management cycle and their underlying factors. The main outcome measures were the proportion of preventable medication-related MERT activations. The secondary outcome included descriptions of medications, medication errors in the context of the medication management cycle and consideration of factors underlying the errors including pharmacy review contributing to these activations.
RESULTS: Fifteen per cent (17/117) of MERT activations reviewed were medication-related, and 65% (11/17) of those were deemed preventable. The omission of medications due to errors in prescribing, administration, pharmacy review or supply stage was the main contributor to preventable medication-related MERT activations (7/11, 64%). Cardiovascular medications, predominantly metoprolol, were most implicated in preventable medication-related MERT activations.
CONCLUSIONS: Medication adverse events due to potentially error-prone steps in medication management processes are a common cause of inpatient MERT activations, presenting a considerable preventable burden to patients and healthcare resources.

Title: Haemodynamic and Respiratory Effects of Dexmedetomidine as an Adjuvant to Oxycodone Patient-Controlled Analgesia After Lumbar Spinal Fusion: A Post Hoc Analysis of the DoseRespDex Randomised Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Dexmedetomidine has been studied as an adjunct to opioid patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) because of its opioid-sparing properties and limited respiratory depression. However, potential dose-dependent haemodynamic effects should be considered, and data on dexmedetomidine administered via PCA remain limited.
METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 98 adults undergoing lumbar spinal fusion were randomised 1:1:1:1 to 24-h PCA with oxycodone 1 mg/mL alone (D0; placebo referring to normal saline replacing dexmedetomidine in the PCA syringe) or combined with dexmedetomidine 2.5 μg/mL (D2), 5 μg/mL (D5) or 10 μg/mL (D10). Outcomes of interest for the present analysis included mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR), respiratory parameters and adverse events. Plasma dexmedetomidine concentrations were analysed as a pre-planned pharmacokinetic sub-analysis.
RESULTS: Mean changes over time differed significantly between groups for MAP (p = 0.005) and HR (p < 0.001). Plasma dexmedetomidine concentrations increased across the D2, D5 and D10 groups, with observed median peak concentrations of 0.15, 0.31 and 0.55 ng/mL in D2, D5 and D10. Over 72 h, MAP was lower in D5 versus D0 (-11.2 mmHg, 95% confidence interval [CI] -19.9 to -2.5, p = 0.004) and D10 versus D0 (-9.1 mmHg, 95% CI -17.4 to -0.8, p = 0.032). All dexmedetomidine doses reduced HR versus D0 (D2: -10.2; D5: -9.9; D10: -11.9 bpm; all p < 0.01), without differing from each other. Haemodynamic changes resolved by 48 h. No bradycardia occurred, and no between-group differences were detected in the measured respiratory variables.
CONCLUSION: Dexmedetomidine as an adjunct to oxycodone PCA produced transient haemodynamic effects without differences in bradycardia or in the measured respiratory variables. Although higher doses resulted in higher plasma concentrations, the magnitude of haemodynamic effects did not follow a clear dose-response pattern in the range studied. Dexmedetomidine 5 μg/mL combined with oxycodone 1 mg/mL may represent a reasonable candidate dose for further investigation.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: In this post hoc analysis of patients undergoing posterolateral spinal fusion, adjunctive dexamethasone (2.5, 5 or 10 mg/mL), administered alongside oxycodone PCA (1 mg/mL), resulted in a transient, minor decrease in mean arterial blood pressure and in heart rate at the highest doses, with no effect on respiratory parameters and with no adverse events. No correlation between plasma concentrations of dexmedetomidine and haemodynamic parameters was demonstrated.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02454881, EudraCT 2014-003252-31.
Publication Types: Clinical Trial, Phase IV; Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Temporal trends in oral anticoagulant prescribing in patients with atrial fibrillation and advanced chronic kidney disease: insights from the CRAFT registry.
Persistent Pelvic Adhesions and Fibrotic Remodeling Following Ectopic Lesion Ablation in a Mouse Model of Endometriosis.
Journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
Abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, estrogen-dependent inflammatory disorder characterized by ectopic endometrial-like lesions, fibrosis, and persistent pelvic pain. Although ectopic lesions are important contributors to pain, symptom severity often correlates poorly with lesion burden, suggesting lesion-independent mechanisms. Here, we investigated the contribution of ectopic lesion-derived cells to persistent pelvic adhesions, fibrotic remodeling, and endometriosis-associated behavioral alterations using a mouse model. A syngeneic model combined with inducible diphtheria toxin receptor (iDTR)-mediated cell ablation was used to selectively eliminate donor-derived progesterone receptor-expressing ectopic cells. Endometriosis was induced by transplantation of uterine tissue from Pgrcre/+Rosa26iDTR/mTmG donor mice into recipients, followed by diphtheria toxin-mediated lesion ablation. Lesion burden, pelvic adhesions, and fibrotic remodeling were assessed by imaging, histology, and molecular analyses, while behavioral outcomes were evaluated using non-evoked assays. Selective ablation eliminated detectable GFP-positive ectopic lesions. Histological and molecular analyses demonstrated significantly reduced collagen deposition and α-SMA-positive fibrotic remodeling within adhesion-associated tissues relative to established ectopic lesions, although these measures remained elevated above sham controls. However, despite lesion ablation, no statistically significant differences were detected between DT- and vehicle-treated mice in nesting or marble-burying performance, although the modest cohort size may have limited detection of partial behavioral effects. These findings indicate that, although fibrosis in adhesion-associated tissues was reduced relative to established ectopic lesions, residual fibrotic remodeling persisted above sham levels, whereas behavioral outcomes showed variable responses without a significant, uniform reversal, highlighting the potential importance of targeting fibrotic and adhesive remodeling in addition to ectopic lesions.

Title: Sedation Versus General Anesthesia During Pediatric Electrophysiology Studies: A Paired Comparison.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anesthetic strategy may influence tachycardia inducibility during pediatric electrophysiology studies, but direct paired comparisons between sedation and general anesthesia remain limited.
METHODS: This prospective paired-comparison study included 51 pediatric patients aged 5-21 years with supraventricular tachycardia undergoing electrophysiology study under both procedural sedation and general anesthesia during the same session. Procedural sedation consisted of midazolam, fentanyl, and supplemental propofol boluses as needed. General anesthesia was induced with propofol and fentanyl and maintained with sevoflurane. Tachycardia inducibility and electrophysiological parameters were compared between anesthetic conditions using paired analyses.
RESULTS: Overall tachycardia inducibility was higher during sedation than during general anesthesia (40/51 [78.4%] vs. 29/51 [56.9%], p = 0.007). No significant differences were observed in atrial effective refractory period, ventricular effective refractory period, atrioventricular nodal Wenckebach point, jump, echo interval, or ventriculoatrial block duration. In patients with atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, inducibility decreased from 84.0% during sedation to 60.0% during general anesthesia (p = 0.109). In the Wolff-Parkinson-White/atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia subgroup, inducibility decreased from 73.1% to 53.8% (p = 0.063), and the accessory pathway effective refractory period, measured by extrastimulus pacing, was prolonged under general anesthesia (p = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: Procedural sedation was associated with greater overall tachycardia inducibility than general anesthesia during pediatric electrophysiology studies. The AVNRT and WPW/AVRT subgroups showed numerically lower inducibility under general anesthesia in the same direction as the overall finding, although these subgroup differences did not reach statistical significance. These findings support individualized anesthetic planning that considers the arrhythmia substrate, the need to preserve inducibility for mapping and post-ablation validation, and patient-specific requirements for procedural stability.

Title: Association of MASLD With Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation: A Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation remains common. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a cardiometabolic condition and has been linked to incident AF, but its association with AF recurrence after catheter ablation remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to determine whether MASLD is associated with recurrent AF after catheter ablation METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus till July 2026 for studies that included adults with AF undergoing catheter ablation and compared the risk of AF recurrence between those with and without MASLD. A random-effects model was used to synthesize HRs and corresponding 95% CIs. Between-study variability was evaluated with the I2 measure, with additional subgroup analyses stratified by AF type and MASLD diagnostic method.
RESULTS: Six studies comprising 2921 patients (894 with MASLD) were included. MASLD was significantly associated with an increased risk of AF recurrence after ablation (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.39-2.64; p < 0.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 69.7%). The association remained significant in both paroxysmal (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.36-2.33) and persistent AF (HR 1.61, 95% CI 1.26-2.05), with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.58). Studies using imaging-based diagnosis of MASLD showed a significant association, whereas the association was not significant when the Fatty Liver Index was used, with no evidence of a difference between diagnostic-method subgroups (p = 0.47) CONCLUSION: MASLD is associated with a higher risk of AF recurrence after catheter ablation and may help identify patients at greater risk of recurrence. Further prospective studies are needed to provide a more comprehensive understanding of this association.

Title: Beyond Mean Blood Pressure Reduction: Distributional and Responder Effects of Bedtime Antihypertensive Dosing in Nondipping Hypertension. A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Study.
Abstract: Mean blood pressure (BP) differences do not fully characterize treatment response. We examined adjusted BP, target attainment and change distributions after morning versus bedtime antihypertensive dosing. This post hoc secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial included 60 patients with uncontrolled hypertension and a nondipping pattern, assigned to morning or bedtime dosing (30 per group). Two-month systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP) and mean arterial pressure (MAP) were compared using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. Secondary analyses assessed BP <140/90 mmHg and median and trimmed changes. Adjusted bedtime-minus-morning differences were -18.1 mmHg for SBP (95% CI -22.4 to -13.8), -11.6 mmHg for DBP (-14.5 to -8.8) and -13.9 mmHg for MAP (-16.7 to -11.0); all p < 0.001. Bootstrap intervals were similar. BP <140/90 mmHg was achieved by 29/30 (96.7%) versus 3/30 (10.0%) patients (risk ratio 9.67; 95% CI 3.30-28.34). Median SBP and DBP change differences were -9.5 and -3.0 mmHg, respectively, with confidence intervals including zero. Bedtime dosing was associated with lower adjusted two-month BP and greater target attainment. Change-based estimates were less precise, indicating uncertainty about the distribution of response. These exploratory findings from a small randomized trial warrant prospective confirmation.

Title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Atrial Fibrillation in Brugada Syndrome: A Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmogenic disorder responsible for approximately 4% of sudden cardiac deaths. Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists and increases the risk of inappropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) therapies. Antiarrhythmic drugs are often limited by proarrhythmic effects, creating an unmet therapeutic need.
PURPOSE: We evaluated whether pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) reduces AF recurrence and provides effective rhythm control in patients with BrS and AF.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception until February 14, 2026. We included studies reporting outcomes of PVI in patients with BrS and AF. The primary endpoint was freedom from AF after ablation. Secondary endpoints included AF recurrence, changes in inappropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator shocks before versus after ablation, and procedural complications. Pooled proportions and risk differences were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: A total of 2149 records were initially identified. After screening and eligibility assessment, Five studies comprising 214 participants overall, including 124 patients with BrS or Brugada-type ECG, were included in the final analysis. The mean age of participants ranged from 45.8 ± 15.5 to 57 ± 10 years, and the proportion of male patients ranged from 33.3% to 100% across studies. PVI significantly reduced inappropriate defibrillator shocks (pooled risk difference -0.35). Freedom from AF was achieved in 82% of patients. The pooled recurrence rate was 36%. A spontaneous type 1 electrocardiographic pattern was present in 10% of patients, and 32% had a family history of sudden cardiac death. Procedural complications were uncommon across studies.
CONCLUSION: PVI was associated with favorable rhythm-control outcomes and acceptable procedural safety in patients with BrS or Brugada-type ECG and AF. Inappropriate ICD shocks were less frequent after ablation, supporting PVI as a clinically relevant rhythm-control strategy in this challenging population. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings.

Title: Percutaneous mechanical aspiration versus medical management in tricuspid valve infective endocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous mechanical aspiration (PMA) has emerged as a treatment option for patients with tricuspid valve infective endocarditis (TVIE); however, comparative evidence on PMA versus medical management (MM) remains limited.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review and meta-analyze clinical outcomes among patients with TVIE treated with PMA versus MM alone.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, MEDLINE Ultimate, and Web of Science were searched following the PRISMA guidelines through December 17, 2025. Studies comparing PMA versus MM alone in adult patients with TVIE were included. The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality. Secondary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, 1-year mortality, and hospital length of stay. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I V2 (Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions, version 2) tool. Random-effects models were used for quantitative syntheses.
RESULTS: Four nonrandomized studies of intervention were included in the systematic review, and 3 studies involving 252 patients were eligible for quantitative synthesis. Pooled analysis showed no significant benefit of PMA over MM alone for 30-day mortality (risk ratio, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.29-2.08; P = 0.62) or 1-year mortality (risk ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.18-5.45; P = 0.99). There was no significant difference in hospital length of stay between the groups (mean difference, 2.40 days; 95% CI, -3.30 to 8.09; P = 0.41).
CONCLUSIONS: Current comparative evidence does not demonstrate a mortality benefit of PMA over MM in patients with TVIE; however, the available evidence is limited and of low to very low certainty. Prospective studies are warranted to establish the clinical indications and safety profile of PMA in patients with TVIE.

Title: The Effectiveness and Safety of Deep Sedation Protocols for Pulsed Field Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep sedation (DS) is increasingly utilized during pulsed field ablation (PFA) for atrial fibrillation (AF), but the optimal electrophysiologist-led sedation regimen remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To compare sedative effectiveness and safety of three electrophysiologist-led DS protocols.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center study, AF patients undergoing focal-form PFA received (1) midazolam + fentanyl (Midazolam group), (2) flurbiprofen axetil + midazolam + fentanyl (Flurbiprofen group), or (3) dexmedetomidine + fentanyl (Dexmedetomidine group). The primary endpoint was the achievement of the target sedation level at ablation initiation (Ramsay Sedation Score ≥3). Secondary endpoints included intraoperative pain, sedation difficulty, operator satisfaction, and sedation-related adverse events.
RESULTS: 166 patients (mean age, 62.2 ± 10.8 years; 62.7% male; 48.2% with paroxysmal AF) were enrolled, with 53, 67, and 46 patients included in the Midazolam, Flurbiprofen, and Dexmedetomidine groups, respectively. The primary outcome occurred more frequently in the Flurbiprofen (73.1%) and Dexmedetomidine (82.6%) groups compared to Midazolam (47.2%) (overall p < 0.001); Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine group did not differ significantly. Intraoperative pain scores were lowest with Dexmedetomidine (overall p < 0.001). Both Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine groups showed lower sedation difficulty and higher operator satisfaction than the Midazolam group (both overall p < 0.001). Dexmedetomidine was associated with more intraoperative hypotension (overall p = 0.047).
CONCLUSION: Electrophysiologist-led DS protocols with Flurbiprofen and Dexmedetomidine were associated with higher target sedation attainment than the specific low-dose Midazolam regimen during PFA, but Dexmedetomidine is linked to higher hypotension rates, warranting caution.

Title: Electrocardiographic screening for left atrial enlargement in dogs: derivation and validation of an algorithm combining lead II P-wave duration and the Morris index.
Journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Combining electrocardiographic measurements may improve identification of dogs requiring echocardiographic assessment. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study derived a three-category algorithm in 150 dogs and evaluated it in 50 separate validation dogs. Three observers independently measured lead II P-wave duration and the V1 Morris index, with observer A providing the primary analysis. Left atrium-to-aorta ratio (LA/Ao) ≥ 1.6 was the primary outcome; normalized left ventricular internal diameter in diastole (LVIDDN) ≥ 1.7 was evaluated independently as a secondary outcome. Thresholds from 114 reference dogs were 48 and 52 ms for P duration and 3.04 mV·ms for Morris. Positive triage comprised intermediate and high categories. Primary-outcome sensitivity and specificity were 90.6% and 50.0% in derivation and 100% and 85.7% in validation. Validation sensitivity had a 95% confidence interval of 88.1%-100%. The ordinal algorithm area under the curve was 0.961 in validation, compared with 0.868 for P and 0.844 for Morris; paired differences were not significant after Holm adjustment. Secondary-outcome validation sensitivity and specificity were 88.0% and 60.0%. The algorithm provided complementary detection of left atrial enlargement and reproducible measurements across observers, supporting further evaluation as an adjunct to echocardiographic triage.

Title: NLRC4 Acts as a Non-Canonical Tumour Suppressor in Lung Adenocarcinoma by Inhibiting PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signalling to Induce Protective Autophagy.
Journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
Abstract: Autophagy plays complex, context-dependent roles in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), but the upstream molecular drivers that govern this process remain elusive. NLRC4 is classically defined as a pyroptosis-inducing inflammasome sensor, yet its non-canonical, tumour-intrinsic function in LUAD progression remains largely unexplored. Through multi-omics screening and prognostic modelling across TCGA and GEO datasets, we identified NLRC4 as a critical autophagy-associated protective factor, which was validated in an institutional cohort of paired LUAD tissues. In vitro and in vivo assays, autophagic flux monitoring, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation and genetic rescue experiments were employed to elucidate the underlying mechanism. NLRC4 protein was markedly downregulated in LUAD tissues alongside the tumour suppressor PTEN, correlating with advanced TNM stage and poor overall survival. Functionally, restoring NLRC4 expression inhibited LUAD cell proliferation, motility, invasion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in vitro, whereas NLRC4 depletion accelerated xenograft tumour growth in vivo. Crucially, NLRC4 selectively stimulated complete autophagic flux without triggering Caspase-1/Gasdermin cleavage or lytic pyroptotic death. Mechanistically, NLRC4 physically interacted with NFKB1 (p105/p50) in a tumour-selective manner, relieving NF-κB-mediated transcriptional repression of PTEN. This restored PTEN expression, thereby tonically dampening the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling cascade. Genetic blockade of autophagy (siATG5) or PTEN ablation largely reversed the tumour-suppressive effects of NLRC4, confirming the functional dependency on the PTEN-autophagy axis. Our study establishes a non-canonical, tumour-intrinsic role for NLRC4 in restraining LUAD progression via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis to induce protective autophagy, positioning it as a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

Title: Associations between types of residential greenspace and depressive symptoms in older adults: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
Abstract: Residential greenspace may prevent older-adult depression, but it is unclear whether this depends on type of greenspace and population subgroup. We examined associations between six greenspace measures and depressive symptoms among 6,799 U.S. older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (1-3 observations per participant in 2000-2012). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression scale. Time-varying residential address-linked exposures included street-view-based vegetation (grass, trees, other, and total), satellite-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and park access. In fully adjusted mixed-effects Poisson models, overall associations were null (symptom count ratios [CRs], 0.98-1.03 per SD increase). Associations varied by site, race/ethnicity, neighborhood socioeconomic status, and population density. In site-stratified analyses, fewer symptoms were associated with NDVI in New York, NY (CR=0.96, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), park access in Winston-Salem, NC (CR=0.95, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), and grass in Minneapolis, MN (CR=0.87, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.97). The greenspace metric most strongly associated with fewer symptoms differed across racial/ethnic groups. Greater street-level greenspace was associated with more symptoms in high-density areas. Greenspace-depression associations may therefore depend on greenspace type and context, suggesting that mental-health-oriented greenspace interventions should be tailored to local populations and environments.

Title: Underrepresentation of women in U.S. occupational cohort mortality studies.
Abstract: Reviews of the occupational epidemiology literature between the 1970s and 2010s found that men were more likely than women to be included in studies of occupational exposures and chronic disease. Our objective was to examine a contemporary sample of occupational cohort mortality studies to determine the extent to which women are underrepresented, how sex is used in analyses, and if the representation of women has improved over time. We searched PubMed for U.S. occupational cohort mortality studies published between 2000 and 2022 with cancer or cardiovascular disease mortality outcomes. We identified 176 U.S. cohort analyses meeting inclusion criteria. Among the cohort analyses that reported the sex of participants, 57% included men and women, 42% included men only, and 1% included women only. Sex was most commonly used in statistical analyses to adjust for confounding (69%) and to exclude women from the study population (26%). Between 2000-2004 and 2015-2022, the proportion of cohort analyses including women increased from 48% to 69%. Women remain poorly represented in occupational cohort mortality studies, although over time fewer studies excluded women. Achieving appropriate representation of women in occupational epidemiology research is essential for fully understanding relationships between occupational exposures and health.

Title: Fasting triglyceride-glucose index and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: an observational study of metabolic risk in singleton pregnancies.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the fasting TyG index and gestational hypertension/preeclampsia (GH/PE) in singleton pregnancies.
METHODS: This observational study included 175 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies examined during routine antenatal care between 11 and 35 weeks of gestation from January 2023 to December 2024. Women with pre-existing hypertension, diabetes, renal disease, gestational diabetes mellitus or major systemic disorders were excluded. Clinical, anthropometric and fasting biochemical data were collected, and the TyG index was calculated as ln [fasting triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting glucose (mg/dL)/2]. Group comparisons, correlation analyses, logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Thirty-nine women (22.3 %) developed GH/PE. Compared with women with physiological pregnancies, women with GH/PE had higher pre-gestational BMI, gestational weight change, blood pressure, fasting glucose, triglycerides and TyG index values (all p≤0.018). The TyG index correlated positively with mean arterial pressure (r=0.20, p=0.027) and gestational week at assessment (r=0.35, p<0.001). Higher TyG index values were associated with increased odds of GH/PE (OR=3.75, 95 % CI 1.79-7.85). A TyG cut-off of 8.6 showed 58.97 % sensitivity and 69.85 % specificity, with an AUC of 0.69 (95 % CI 0.59-0.79).
CONCLUSIONS: In this antenatal cohort, the fasting TyG index was associated with GH/PE and showed moderate discriminatory ability. The TyG index should not be used as a stand-alone diagnostic test, but it may complement BMI and routine clinical assessment in identifying women with increased metabolic susceptibility to hypertensive pregnancy disorders.

Title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
Abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

Title: Impact of age and frailty on the effect of a multimodal individualized long-term intervention after stroke: the last-long trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The LAST-long randomized trial tested a multidimensional, stroke coordinator-led, community-based intervention and found no overall functional benefit. Because most participants had mild stroke symptoms, whether older or frailer subgroups benefited was examined.
METHODS: In this single-blinded RCT at 4 Norwegian hospitals (2019-2022), 301 participants were randomized 1:1 to monthly stroke-coordinator meetings for 18 months (structured risk assessment and individualized goals) or to standard care.
PRIMARY OUTCOME: modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 18 months.
SECONDARY OUTCOMES: mortality, cognition, ADLs, physical function, fatigue, and quality of life. Older age: ≥ 80 years; frailty: Frailty Index ≥ 0.2. Linear and logistic regression tested age- and frailty-intervention interactions.
RESULTS: mRS data were available for 268 participants (136 intervention, 132 control). Mean age 71.1 (SD 12.4); 66 (24.6%) ≥ 80; 89 (33.2%) frail. Age modified the intervention effect on mRS: among participants ≥ 80, favourable outcome was less likely with intervention vs control (23.4% vs 57.0%, p = 0.004). For secondary outcomes, the intervention improved Trail Making Test B in younger participants (-32.2 s, 95% CI -58.0 to -6.4, p = 0.015) with a significant age-intervention interaction (p = 0.019). No frailty-intervention interaction was found.
CONCLUSIONS: Age - but not frailty - modified response to the intervention, indicating differential effects in older participants.
CLINICAL TRIALS: gov identifier: NCT03859063.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Evaluation of Peripapillary Vitreous Dynamics in Patients with Acute Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate peripapillary and vitreomacular interface configurations using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) in patients with acute nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) and to compare findings with age-matched controls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, observational study included 60 patients with acute NAION and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer scans and macular SD-OCT images were analyzed. Assessed peripapillary vitreoretinal interface parameters included peripapillary vitreoretinal adhesion, vitreoretinal traction, complete peripapillary vitreous detachment, peripapillary folds, superficial vascular protrusions, and hyperreflective vitreous dots. Vitreomacular interface characteristics were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Peripapillary vitreoretinal adhesion was more frequently observed in NAION eyes compared with controls (50% vs. 25%, p=0.04). Hyperreflective vitreous dots were significantly more common in NAION eyes (68.3% vs. 8.3%; p<0.001), with a higher mean count (5.31±6.05 vs. 0.50±1.54; p<0.001). Peripapillary folds were also more prevalent in NAION (41.7% vs. 1.7%; p<0.001). Although peripapillary superficial vascular protrusions were common in both groups, mean counts differed significantly (p<0.001). Among 34 NAION eyes with longitudinal follow-up, 29.4% demonstrated interval changes in vitreoretinal interface configuration.
CONCLUSION: Acute NAION is associated with distinct peripapillary vitreoretinal interface characteristics detectable by SD-OCT. These findings highlight structural differences in vitreoretinal interface configuration in acute NAION. However, their temporal relationship to ischemic injury remains uncertain.

Title: Workroom contact networks: implications for COVID-19 and other respiratory infections.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how physician workroom size affects healthcare professional contact networks and the risk of respiratory virus transmission.
DESIGN: Prospective observational study with agent-based simulations.
SETTING: Two physician workrooms of differing size (internal medicine, 208.7 sq ft; cardiology, 112.6 sq ft) in a large academic hospital.
METHODS: We deployed wireless sensor networks over 18 days in internal medicine and 14 days in cardiology workrooms. Physicians, residents, and medical students wore proximity-sensing badges during work shifts. Contacts were defined as two healthcare professionals within six feet, based on calibrated received signal strength indicators. Contact networks were generated in one-minute intervals. We simulated respiratory disease spread using a Susceptible-Infected (SI) model across varying transmission probabilities and estimated infection risk at different room densities.
RESULTS: Average occupancy was 2.7 persons in internal medicine and 2.3 in cardiology. Despite lower occupancy, the smaller cardiology room exhibited greater contact density: healthcare professionals in the smaller room had higher mean and median numbers of contacts. SI simulations showed consistently higher risk of secondary infections in the cardiology room, even at lower transmission probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: Workroom size significantly affects healthcare professional contact density and infection risk. Smaller rooms increased opportunities for transmission despite lower average occupancy. Designing larger workrooms, limiting occupancy, or reconfiguring shared spaces may reduce infection transmission in healthcare facilities.

Title: Automated Cerebrospinal Fluid Flow Quantification in Hydrocephalus Using Phase-Contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
Abstract: Quantitative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow analysis with phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging depends on segmentation and is affected by operator variability. This cohort method-comparison study evaluated whether a flow-aware deep learning (DL) model provides reproducible C2-C3 CSF segmentation and flow quantification compared with repeated manual segmentation. Ten hydrocephalus patients underwent 3-T phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging at C2-C3, with 32 magnitude and phase frames across the cardiac cycle. Three experts and one novice segmented each case twice using semi-automatic software, generating 80 manual annotations. A pretrained flow-aware 2D-UNet generated one fixed automatic segmentation per case. The inference pipeline was deterministic, meaning that repeated processing of the same input with fixed model weights and settings produced identical masks. A multi-expert reference was defined as the arithmetic mean of the expert measurements. Region of interest (ROI) surface area, peak flow amplitude, and stroke volume were compared using mean difference, Bland-Altman 95% limits of agreement, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Expert ICC(1,1) was 0.88-0.97 for surface area, 0.97-1.00 for peak flow amplitude, and 0.97-0.99 for stroke volume; novice values were 0.63, 0.95, and 0.92, respectively. Compared with the multi-expert reference, model mean differences were -0.42 mm2 for surface area, -0.00 mL/s for peak flow amplitude, and -0.01 mL for stroke volume, with CCC values of 0.50, 0.87, and 0.86. Bland-Altman limits of agreement were -69.12 to 68.27 mm2, -1.47 to 1.46 mL/s, and -0.34 to 0.31 mL. The model provided rapid, deterministic CSF segmentation with small cohort-level mean differences in peak flow amplitude and stroke volume; however, individual-level agreement with the flow-derived multi-expert reference was lower than for expert and novice segmentations obtained using the semi-automatic workflow.

Title: Theranekron Attenuates Inflammation, Oxidative Stress Index, and Apoptosis in Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Cardiovascular Toxicity: Association With Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1 Alpha-Related Gene Expression.
Journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the possible protective effects of Theranekron, an extract derived from Tarantula cubensis venom, on cardiovascular damage induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in an experimental rat model. A total of 32 male Wistar Albino rats were randomly divided into 4 groups: Control, Lipopolysaccharide, Lipopolysaccharide plus Theranekron, and Theranekron alone. Lipopolysaccharide administration caused pronounced histopathological changes in the heart and aorta, including endothelial sloughing, hyperemia, hemorrhage, and infiltration of inflammatory cells. These pathological findings were accompanied by elevated oxidative stress markers, increased tumor necrosis factor-alpha and inducible nitric oxide synthase immunoreactivity, and increased caspase-3 immunoreactivity. Additionally, genes associated with the hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) pathway-such as interleukin 6, signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), and vascular endothelial growth factor-were significantly upregulated in the lipopolysaccharide group. Theranekron pretreatment was associated with partial attenuation of oxidative stress imbalance, of inflammatory and apoptotic immunoreactivity, and of the upregulation of HIF-1α-related transcripts. Overall, these findings suggest that Theranekron may offer partial protection against early LPS-induced cardiovascular injury.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors across the spectrum of myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) help in heart failure (HF), but their benefit after acute myocardial infarction is unclear. This meta-analysis assesses their impact on mortality and heart failure hospitalization post-acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and identifies which patients benefit most.
METHODS: Four databases were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and matched studies comparing SGLT2i with control post-AMI.
PRIMARY OUTCOMES: all-cause death and hospitalization for heart failure (HHF); secondary: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Subgroups and meta-regression examined timing, diabetes, follow-up, design, SGLT2i type and baseline HF/diabetes.
RESULTS: Fifteen studies including 117 096 patients (58 613 SGLT2i vs. 58 483 control) were included. A total of 117 096 patients contributed to the all-cause mortality analysis (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.90), whereas 116 992 patients across 14 studies contributed to the HHF analysis (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.88). All-cause mortality was significantly lower in PSM observational studies (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.61-0.67), whereas the reduction did not reach statistical significance in RCTs (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.01), with a significant interaction by study design. HHF reduction occurred with both early and delayed initiation; dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were similarly effective. MACE was significantly lower with SGLT2i, but CV death, recurrent MI and stroke did not differ. Baseline HF or diabetes showed no association with primary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i reduced HHF after MI, but this benefit should be interpreted cautiously because of small-study effects and possible publication bias. The all-cause mortality benefit is driven by observational studies; RCTs show a favourable but nonsignificant trend.

Title: Endohepatology in the Management of Portal Hypertension in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
Journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
Abstract: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. This biology is compounded by a diagnostic gap: non-invasive tests such as liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography, FIB-4, ANTICIPATE-NASH, spleen stiffness and the NICER model, are degraded by obesity through technical limitations and altered diagnostic thresholds, even when test discrimination is preserved. Moreover, no non-invasive rule-in for clinically significant portal hypertension reaches a 90% positive predictive value in obese MASLD, leaving a clinically meaningful grey zone. Endohepatology addresses these diagnostic limitations by providing complementary hemodynamic, elastographic, and histological information. Within a single sedated session, EUS-guided shear-wave elastography and EUS-guided liver biopsy can adjudicate F2-F3 fibrosis when treatment eligibility is uncertain; EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement can provide a direct gradient when HVPG or non-invasive tests are discordant with the clinical phenotype; and EUS-based vascular assessment can characterize collateral and variceal anatomy. The same platform extends to therapy, including EUS-guided gastric variceal obliteration and pre-bariatric risk stratification. Current evidence is largely early-phase and requires prospective validation. Rather than replacing established tools, endohepatology offers an integrated pathway tailored to the diagnostic and therapeutic problems most characteristic of MASLD.

Title: Blood- and Liver Stiffness-Based Non-Invasive Tests for Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension in Patients With cACLD and HCC.
Journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The applicability of non-invasive tests (NITs) for clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is controversial. We performed a head-to-head comparison of various NITs for CSPH and evaluated rule-in/-out criteria.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study including 283 patients with HCC undergoing hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement at the Vienna Hepatic Haemodynamic Lab with available, same-day data on NITs (i.e., liver stiffness measurement [LSM], platelet count [PLT], von Willebrand factor antigen [VWF:Ag], and the ratio of VWF:Ag and PLT [VITRO]). For the subsequent analysis, we focused on patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD).
RESULTS: Among 164 patients with cACLD, most were BCLC 0/A (50.6%) and CSPH prevalence was 46.3%, the median LSM was 20.0 kPa (IQR: 13.3-37.9), and mean VWF:Ag/VITRO was 266 ± 119%/2.30 ± 1.81. The VITRO score yielded the highest discriminative ability to detect CSPH (AUROC: 0.834), followed by ANTICIPATE ± NASH (AUROC: 0.822), PLT (AUROC: 0.803), LSM (AUROC: 0.779), and VWF:Ag (AUROC: 0.707). The application of the Baveno VII criterium (LSM ≤ 15 kPa & PLT ≥ 150G/L) and the VITRO score (≤ 1.0) individually showed an excellent performance for ruling-out CSPH (sensitivities: ≥ 95%, NPV: 100%/87.9%). For ruling-in CSPH by individual criteria, the VITRO score provided the highest PPV (≥ 2.5, specificity/PPV: 89.8%/83.0%), followed by the Baveno VII criteria (specificity/PPV: 81.8%/74.6%). When sequentially applying Baveno VII criteria and VITRO, the grey zone could be significantly reduced to 16% (sensitivity/NPV: 94.7%/92.2%; specificity/PPV: 73.9%/84.4%).
CONCLUSION: The discriminative ability in patients with cACLD and HCC was comparable to patients without HCC. However, PPVs of established criteria were < 90%, which may be explained by the comparatively low prevalence of CSPH in this context.

Title: Development and Internal Validation of a Clinical Prediction Model for Coronary Slow Flow Phenomenon in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may exhibit coronary slow flow phenomenon (CSFP) despite the absence of obstructive epicardial coronary stenosis. Dedicated prediction tools remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a model for estimating the probability of TIMI frame count (TFC)-defined CSFP in patients with T2DM.
METHODS: Among 501 patients with T2DM undergoing coronary angiography at a single center in Xinjiang, China (2021-2025), 429 met eligibility criteria. CSFP was defined as maximum coronary stenosis <40% and TFC >27 frames in at least one major coronary artery. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 300) and validation (n = 129) cohorts. Predictors selected by penalized regression were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR), calibration, bootstrap-corrected concordance index, and decision curve analysis; additional analyses were complementary.
RESULTS: CSFP occurred in 44 patients (14.7%) in the training cohort and 16 (12.4%) in the validation cohort. The final model included smoking history, systolic blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c, lymphocyte count, and uric acid. ROC-AUC was 0.832 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.774-0.889) in the training cohort and 0.840 (95% CI: 0.733-0.946) in the validation cohort; AUC-PR was 0.467 and 0.542, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (Brier scores 0.101 and 0.084); bootstrap-corrected concordance indices were 0.827 and 0.846. Decision curve analysis suggested net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. Given the limited number of CSFP events in the validation cohort, validation estimates should be interpreted cautiously.
CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a five-variable model for estimating the probability of TFC-defined CSFP in patients with T2DM. The model was translated into a nomogram and web-based calculator as a complementary tool for individualized risk characterization. External validation is required before broader clinical application.

Title: Holter-Detected Arrhythmias in Acute Exacerbations of COPD: NT-proBNP Correlates and Hypercapnia Associated with COPD-Related Readmission.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrhythmias are increasingly recognized during acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but their full spectrum and prognostic significance detected by continuous Holter monitoring remain insufficiently characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized for AECOPD between April 2022 and January 2025 who underwent continuous Holter monitoring.
