Arrhythmias were classified as atrial arrhythmias (AA), atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF/AFL), ventricular arrhythmias (VA), or coexistence of ≥2 arrhythmia types. Multivariable regression models were used to identify factors associated with arrhythmias and clinical outcomes. COPD-related readmission was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Among 548 patients, 60.4% experienced at least one arrhythmia during hospitalization. AA (37.6%) was the most frequent subtype, followed by VA (31.0%) and AF/AFL (12.2%), while 21.5% exhibited multiple arrhythmia types. Older age, male sex, higher heart rate, elevated NT-proBNP, and larger left atrial diameter were independently associated with in-hospital arrhythmias. NT-proBNP was consistently associated with all arrhythmia phenotypes and demonstrated moderate discrimination for arrhythmia identification (AUC=0.730; cutoff, 131.5 pg/mL). AF/AFL was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (adjusted ratio=1.26, P=0.010). After accounting for the time-dependent effect of age, hypercapnia (PaCO2 ≥45 mmHg) remained associated with a higher risk of COPD-related readmission (adjusted HR=1.85, 95% CI 1.19-2.88; P=0.007).
CONCLUSION: In-hospital arrhythmias are highly prevalent among patients hospitalized for AECOPD. NT-proBNP is consistently associated with multiple arrhythmia phenotypes and may aid arrhythmic risk stratification. Hypercapnia, but not arrhythmia status, remained independently associated with COPD-related readmission despite the limited sample and observational design.

Title: Development and Internal Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Severe Complications After Snakebite: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Snakebite envenomation is a global public health concern with high mortality and morbidity. Given the highly heterogeneous clinical progression and the potential for rapid deterioration in severe cases, early risk stratification is crucial for improving outcomes. This study aimed to develop a nomogram based on simple laboratory indicators to assist primary care clinicians in rapidly identifying high-risk patients, thereby optimizing interventions and reducing mortality and healthcare burden.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 10,505 snakebite envenomation cases admitted to the Medical Laboratory Center of Shaanxi Provincial People's Hospital between March 2014 and October 2025. After applying strict eligibility criteria, 2762 patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n=2072) and a validation cohort (n=690) at a 3:1 ratio. LASSO regression and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify independent risk factors for severe complications, which were then incorporated into a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: Of the 2762 patients, 64 (2.32%) developed severe complications, most commonly acute myocardial injury, acute liver injury, coagulopathy, and multiple organ dysfunction; the majority presented with two or more. Time from bite to presentation (OR=1.017, 95% CI 1.005-1.027), white blood cell count (OR=1.116, 95% CI 1.043-1.190), and prothrombin time (OR=1.103, 95% CI 1.011-1.203) were identified as independent predictors. The nomogram demonstrated strong discrimination, with AUCs of 0.812 (95% CI 0.741-0.882) and 0.839 (95% CI 0.734-0.945) in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration was excellent (Hosmer-Lemeshow P>0.05), and decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit.
CONCLUSION: This readily accessible nomogram, based on time to presentation, WBC, and PT, demonstrates strong predictive performance, high operability, and clinical accessibility, facilitating early identification of high-risk patients and optimization of treatment decisions.

Title: Macular Thickness and Associated Factors in African Immigrants: Insights from the Africans in America Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Normative optical coherence tomography (OCT) databases may not be generalizable to Africans, one of the fastest growing populations in the United States. Given the paucity of normative OCT data in Africans, we evaluated macular thickness in African immigrants.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed African-born participants enrolled in the Africans in America Study. They underwent history, physical, oral glucose tolerance tests, hemoglobin electrophoresis, and macular OCT (Cirrus HD-OCT). In the primary analysis, multivariable linear regression excluding eyes with retinopathy, glaucoma, or ocular hypertension was used to evaluate the association between the central subfield thickness (CST) and demographic, clinical, and metabolic factors. In the secondary analysis, multivariable analysis was used to evaluate the association between macular layer thicknesses and prediabetes status (prediabetes vs normal glucose tolerance). P values less than 0.05 and false discovery rate (FDR) within 10% were considered significant.
RESULTS: Six hundred forty-three eyes of 330 participants (60% male; mean age: 40 ± 11 years) were analyzed. The mean CST thickness for the cohort was 238.53 ± 21.48 µm. On average, women had a lower CST than men [-10.51 µm, 95% confidence interval: (-15.75, -5.26), P < 0.001, FDR < 0.001]. No significant associations were found between prediabetes status and the thickness of any macular layer.
CONCLUSION: These findings provide descriptive reference data on Cirrus-derived macular thickness measurements among African-born adults. Women had a lower CST, on average, than men. In contrast to prior studies, there was no difference in macular layer thicknesses between participants with prediabetes and those with normal glucose tolerance.

Title: Comparison of Classic Laryngeal Mask Airway and Endotracheal Intubation for Airway Management During Short Urologic Procedures in the Prone Position: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway management in the prone position remains a major challenge in anesthesia, particularly during short urologic procedures. Although endotracheal intubation (ETT) is considered the standard technique, the Classic laryngeal mask airway (LMA) has emerged as a less invasive alternative in patients without an anticipated difficult airway. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of Classic LMA versus ETT for airway management in prone-position urologic surgeries.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 70 patients undergoing prone-position urologic surgery with an operative duration of ≤ 90 min were assigned to either the Classic LMA group or ETT group (n = 35 each). Primary outcomes included intraoperative ventilatory performance assessed by peak airway pressure (Ppeak), need for conversion of airway technique, and airway-related complications. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic and respiratory parameters, including heart rate (HR), systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP/DBP), oxygen saturation (SpO2), end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2), Ppeak, minute ventilation (VE), and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: Baseline demographic and perioperative characteristics were comparable between groups. No significant differences were observed between the Classic LMA and ETT groups regarding intraoperative hemodynamic variables, SpO2, ETCO2, or VE. Ppeak was significantly higher in the ETT group (p < 0.001). During recovery, significant time-related changes were observed in hemodynamic and respiratory parameters in both groups, although no clinically significant intergroup differences were identified. Postoperative complications, including sore throat and laryngospasm, were infrequent and comparable between groups.
CONCLUSION: Classic LMA provided airway maintenance and ventilation comparable to ETT in short prone-position urologic surgeries and may be considered as a feasible airway device in patients meeting appropriate airway assessment criteria. Trial Registration: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT): IRCT20250729066688N1.

Title: Identification of Patients with Colon Ischemia in the Swedish ESPRESSO Cohort: A Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Colon ischemia is the most common form of intestinal ischemia, yet case identification in epidemiological research remains challenging due to heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and absence of a specific International Classification of Diseases (ICD) code. The use of SNOMED (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine) for gastrointestinal biopsies and surgical specimens enables a unique possibility to identify colon ischemia cases.
METHODS: In this validation study, 231 individuals with SNOMED code M54 (necrosis) and colorectal topography codes (T67-T68) were randomly selected from five Swedish regions. Medical charts were retrieved for 204 cases, where 143 contained sufficient information for evaluation. Cases were classified by clinical overall assessment and assigned an etiological group. Positive predictive values (PPVs) were calculated for overall colon ischemia based on histopathology alone and for etiological subsets where histopathology was combined with ICD codes.
RESULTS: Of 143 patients with sufficient clinical information for validation, histopathological ischemic injury of the colon was confirmed in 141, corresponding to a PPV of 99% (95% CI, 95-99%). Combining SNOMED codes with selected ICD codes yielded a PPV of 84% (95% CI, 73-92%) for clinically confirmed idiopathic colon ischemia, increasing to 92% (95% CI, 79-98%) when more restrictive ICD-based criteria were applied.
CONCLUSION: SNOMED-based histopathological case identification demonstrated a very high PPV for ischemic injury of the colon but could not distinguish idiopathic disease from ischemia secondary to identifiable clinical conditions. Combining SNOMED and ICD codes provides a feasible and reproducible strategy for identifying underlying causes of colon ischemia in Swedish nationwide health registers.

Title: Prophylactic Low-Dose Esketamine for Prevention of Intraoperative Penile Erection During Ureteroscopic Surgery Under General Anesthesia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Intraoperative penile erection (IPE) during ureteroscopic surgery may interrupt surgical procedures and increase the risk of urethral injury. Existing management strategies are largely reactive and frequently require rescue interventions after erection has already developed. Effective prophylactic strategies remain limited. We evaluated whether prophylactic esketamine reduces the incidence of intraoperative penile erection during ureteroscopic surgery under general anesthesia.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500114505) enrolled 356 adult men (ASA I-II) scheduled for elective ureteroscopic surgery. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive intravenous esketamine 0.3 mg/kg or saline before anesthetic induction; allocation was concealed, and patients, anesthetists, surgeons, and outcome assessors were blinded. The primary outcome was the incidence of IPE (Porst grade ≥1), assessed at nine predefined intraoperative time points (T0-T8), with rescue treatment for erections of grade ≥2. Secondary outcomes included erection severity, hemodynamic variables, recovery characteristics, and adverse events.
RESULTS: The incidence of IPE was 6.2% (11/178) with esketamine versus 21.9% (39/178) with saline (RR 0.282, 95% CI 0.149-0.533; ARR 15.7%; NNT 6.4; P < 0.001). Porst grades were lower in the esketamine group during disinfection, ureteroscope insertion, and 10 min after surgery commenced, and fewer patients required rescue treatment for clinically significant erection (Porst grade ≥ 2, 4.5% vs 21.3%; P < 0.001). Mean arterial pressure was higher with esketamine intraoperatively (adjusted mean difference 3.49 mmHg), and heart rate was higher, without clinically significant hemodynamic disturbance. Recovery and adverse events did not differ significantly between groups, no hallucinations occurred; postoperative catheter-related bladder discomfort was less severe with esketamine (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Prophylactic low-dose esketamine was associated with a lower incidence and severity of intraoperative penile erection, without evidence of impaired postoperative recovery. These findings suggest that prophylactic esketamine may be a useful strategy for preventing this perioperative complication, warranting confirmation in larger multicenter trials.

Title: Long-Term Cardiovascular, Thromboembolic, and Malignancy Safety of Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitors in Dermatologic and Rheumatologic Populations: A Narrative Comparative Review.
Abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors are increasingly used in dermatology and rheumatology, but concerns about cardiovascular events, thromboembolism, and malignancy continue to influence long-term treatment decisions. This narrative comparative review examines evidence from randomized trials, integrated safety analyses, long-term extensions, selected observational studies, and regulatory sources, focusing on rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, atopic dermatitis, and alopecia areata. Topical agents and selective tyrosine kinase 2 inhibition are considered separately because of important differences in systemic exposure and pharmacology. The original, informally assembled evidence base was supplemented by a targeted literature update. ORAL Surveillance identified an important safety signal for tofacitinib compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and cardiovascular risk factors. Long-term dermatology studies have generally reported low absolute event rates, although younger study populations, restrictive eligibility criteria, limited long-term comparator data, and treatment discontinuation affect how these findings should be interpreted. Observational studies in dermatology have produced mixed results, including thromboembolic associations that warrant further investigation. Psoriatic arthritis provides additional evidence across the clinical boundaries of both specialties. Differences in patient populations, study design, outcome definitions, and statistical measures limit direct comparisons across studies. Treatment decisions should follow indication-specific prescribing requirements and consider cardiovascular disease, prior thrombosis, smoking, age, malignancy history, and available alternatives. Additional long-term comparative studies are needed to better distinguish patient-, disease-, and treatment-related risks.

Title: Postnatal Hypertension Management and Discharge Documentation: A Retrospective Clinical Audit at a UK University Hospital.
Abstract: Background Postnatal hypertension requires timely blood pressure surveillance, treatment review, safety netting, and communication between maternity and community services. This audit assessed postnatal hypertension care and discharge documentation against local Trust standards at Princess Royal University Hospital. Methods A retrospective case-note audit included women with postnatal hypertension who delivered between April and September 2025. For audit eligibility, postnatal hypertension was defined as a pregnancy-related or chronic hypertensive disorder identified through prespecified Epic diagnosis filters and requiring postnatal surveillance. The clinical blood pressure threshold used for the audit was systolic blood pressure of at least 140 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure of at least 90 mmHg from birth through six weeks postpartum. Of 150 identified notes, 148 were included after exclusion of one pre-viable birth before 24+0 weeks and one immediate post-delivery transfer to another Trust. Statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.3.3 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria). Exploratory comparisons across pregnancy-induced hypertension, pre-eclampsia, and chronic hypertension/superimposed pre-eclampsia used Kruskal-Wallis tests for continuous variables and Pearson chi-square statistics with Monte Carlo p-values for categorical variables. Results Median maternal age was 34.0 years (IQR 30.0-37.0); 76/148 women (51.4%) had pregnancy-induced hypertension, 50/148 (33.8%) had pre-eclampsia, and 22/148 (14.9%) had chronic hypertension or superimposed pre-eclampsia. A valid discharge blood pressure was recorded in 146/148 records (98.6%); 118/146 (80.8%) were below 140/90 mmHg. Blood-pressure parameter plans, two-week general-practitioner review, and clear discharge communication were documented in 27/148 (18.2%), 34/147 (23.1%), and 16/148 (10.8%) records, respectively. Documentation of a blood pressure parameter plan (Pearson chi-square=8.551, p=0.014) and clear discharge communication (Pearson chi-square=8.349, p=0.013) differed across hypertensive disorder groups. Any postnatal antihypertensive was documented in 109/148 records (73.6%); medication documentation differed across groups (Pearson chi-square=12.669, p=0.001). Community re-referral for raised blood pressure occurred in 12/148 records (8.1%); any documented readmission occurred in 14/148 (9.5%). Conclusions Discharge blood pressure documentation, safety netting, and breastfeeding drug safety advice were high, but documentation of individualized blood pressure plans, early general practitioner review, and clear discharge communication were low. An electronic discharge template and prospective re-audit are appropriate quality-improvement interventions.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Lucitanib in Advanced Thymic Carcinoma: A Randomized Phase II Trial.
Abstract: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

Title: Association of Glycaemic Control and Blood Pressure With Clinical Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis in Obese Adult Men.
Abstract: Background In obese adults, acute pancreatitis is often complicated by metabolic abnormalities, and suboptimal glycaemic control and hypertension may be linked to worse clinical outcomes and severity of disease. Objective To evaluate the association of glycaemic control and blood pressure status on clinical outcomes of acute pancreatitis in obese adult men. Methodology A prospective observational study was conducted at Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Islamabad, over one year (January 2025-December 2025). A total of 394 obese adult male patients with acute pancreatitis were enrolled using consecutive sampling. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, glycaemic status, blood pressure, radiological findings, and clinical outcomes were assessed. HbA1c was categorized as <7% or ≥7% to characterize glycaemic status, while blood pressure was categorized as controlled or uncontrolled based on repeated inpatient measurements according to the prespecified threshold. Clinical outcomes were compared according to glycaemic and blood pressure status using Pearson chi-square tests. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with severe acute pancreatitis, with adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) reported. Results Among 394 patients, 243 (61.68%) had HbA1c ≥7%, while 151 (38.32%) had HbA1c <7%. Uncontrolled blood pressure was observed in 222 (56.35%) patients compared with 172 (43.65%) with controlled blood pressure. Poor glycaemic status was associated with higher frequencies of severe acute pancreatitis (n=49; 20.16% vs. n=10; 6.62%), ICU admission (n=58; 23.87% vs. n=14; 9.27%), and in-hospital mortality (n=25; 10.29% vs. n=5; 3.31%) (all p<0.05). Uncontrolled blood pressure was associated with higher frequencies of severe acute pancreatitis (n=44; 19.82% vs. n=15; 8.72%), but the difference in in-hospital mortality was not statistically significant (n=22; 9.91% vs. n=8; 4.65%; p=0.051). In multivariable analysis, poor glycaemic control (AOR=2.84, 95% CI: 1.61-5.02, p<0.001) and uncontrolled blood pressure (AOR=2.31, 95% CI: 1.34-3.98, p=0.003) were independently associated with higher odds of severe acute pancreatitis. Conclusion Poor glycaemic control and uncontrolled blood pressure were associated with adverse clinical outcomes among obese adult men with acute pancreatitis. Poor glycaemic control and uncontrolled blood pressure were also independently associated with higher odds of severe acute pancreatitis in the final adjusted model. These findings support the clinical value of assessing metabolic characteristics in obese patients with acute pancreatitis, but the observational design does not establish causality or demonstrate that modifying these factors would improve outcomes. Further multicenter prospective and interventional studies are warranted to confirm these associations and determine whether targeted metabolic management can improve clinical outcomes.

Title: The Epidemiology and Associated Factors of Ectopic Pregnancy in Saudi Arabia: A Literature Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopic pregnancy (EP) is a serious maternal complication with a worldwide prevalence of about 2%. It is defined as the implantation of the product of conception outside the uterine cavity. Patients with EP may present with a wide range of clinical symptoms, including abdominal/pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, missed menstrual cycle, and an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound. After diagnosing EPs, medical and/or surgical treatment options are available based on the patient's hemodynamic status, ectopic location, fetal cardiac activity, size of the gestational sac, level of β-HCG, and patient profile.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative literature review aims to summarize published primary studies on the epidemiology and reported associated factors of EP in Saudi Arabia between 2000 and 2024.
RESULTS: A total of 1342 EP cases were reported across the included studies. Reported prevalence estimates ranged from 0.23% to 1.20%. The reviewed studies were from different regions of the Kingdom, including Abha, Khamis Mushait, Yanbu, Makkah, Madina, Jeddah, Khobar, and Majmaah. The prevalence of EPs fluctuated between 2000 and 2019 and had three peaks: 1.13% (2012), 1.14% (2013), and 1.2% (2019). Multiple associated factors linked to EP were reported in this review, including a history of pelvic surgery, C-sections, previous EP, abortions, intrauterine contraceptive device (IUCD) use, and pelvic inflammatory diseases (PIDs).
CONCLUSIONS: EP is a serious complication that causes significant maternal morbidity and mortality and has a substantial burden on the healthcare system. In this review, eleven studies were reviewed regarding the epidemiology of EPs in the Kingdom. No clear pattern or trend in prevalence was identified, although the majority of studies reported lower EP rates than the worldwide prevalence. Several associated factors were reported across the included studies; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because most studies were retrospective and descriptive in nature.

Title: Beyond the Threatened Limb: Acute Limb Ischemia as a Diagnostic Attractor.
Abstract: Acute limb ischemia is a time-sensitive vascular emergency, but in older patients with active cancer and multimorbidity, the threatened limb can become a diagnostic attractor: a correct specialized diagnosis that narrows attention before whole-patient physiology is integrated. We report an 81-year-old man with metastatic cecal adenocarcinoma receiving folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) who presented on day one with three days of progressive left lower limb claudication, coldness, discoloration, absent pulses, preserved motor and sensory function, and no rest pain. The presentation was clinically compatible with Rutherford I-IIa acute limb ischemia; bedside Doppler signals were not documented, precluding a definitive retrospective distinction between these categories. Concurrent findings included new atrial fibrillation, basal crackles, peripheral edema, markedly elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and troponin, bilateral pleural effusions, and radiological concern for low cardiac output. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed severe distal superficial femoral artery stenosis, long popliteal occlusion, slow distal flow, and limited runoff, favoring an acute-on-chronic ischemic process. On day two, a 6 mm x 60 mm covered stent was placed across the distal superficial femoral artery lesion. The treated lesion had a satisfactory technical result, but distal runoff remained severely compromised. Therapeutic anticoagulation initiated on day one was not maintained; discharge treatment on day three included prophylactic-dose enoxaparin and aspirin, with no rationale for the change documented in the available record. He returned on day five with recurrent coldness and toe necrosis despite normal lactate. No repeat vascular imaging was available to define the mechanism. Care became palliative on day 13, and he died on day 58. This case illustrates that a correct vascular diagnosis should not terminate integrative emergency reasoning. We propose that a vascular-plus-physiology cross-check may help preserve attention to systemic physiology and goals of care, but it is an educational framework rather than a validated clinical algorithm.

Title: HADS-Assessed Anxiety/Depression Status and Ocular Outcomes in Vision-Threatening Diabetic Retinopathy: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Vision-threatening diabetic retinopathy (VTDR) poses significant blindness risks and the study aimed to identify the impact of psychological factors on its ocular outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 782 VTDR patients from three ophthalmological centers (2018-2021). DR severity was graded using ETDRS criteria. Primary outcomes included tractional retinal detachment (TRD) involving the fovea, neovascular glaucoma (NVG), final best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) <0.3, and recurrent vitreous hemorrhage (VH). Anxiety and depression were assessed via the hospital anxiety and depression scale (HADS). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression evaluated the associations between HADS scores and ocular outcomes.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 24.8 months, depressive symptoms (HADS-D ≥8) were associated with higher rates of BCVA <0.3 (67.8% vs. 57.2%, p = 0.033) and NVG (13.6% vs. 6.9%, p = 0.020). Recurrent VH was more frequent in patients with anxiety (21.0% vs. 10.6%, p = 0.031) or depression (20.3% vs. 10.7%, p = 0.045). Multivariable logistic analysis revealed that each 1-point increase in HADS-D score significantly increased adjusted odds of TRD (aOR = 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11), BCVA <0.3 (aOR = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.02-1.11), recurrent VH (aOR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.17), and NVG (aOR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.03-1.17; all p < 0.05). There was a consistent positive gradient between HADS severity and adverse outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Depressive symptoms are independently associated with worse ocular prognoses in VTDR patients. Systematic psychological screening and intervention is essential to mitigate vision deterioration risk in this population.

Title: Effects of Psycho-Cardiology Model-Based Psychological and Behavioural Management on Negative Emotions and Sleep Disorders in Patients With Resistant Hypertension Complicated by Anxiety and Depression.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To explore the effect of psychocardiology model-based psychological and behavioural management on top of routine cardiovascular treatment on negative emotions and sleep disorders in patients with resistant hypertension complicated by anxiety and depression.
METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed electronic medical records and follow-up data of patients treated in the Department of Cardiology of Tonglu Hospital, Hangzhou First People's Hospital Tonglu Campus between August 2022 and May 2025. A total of 126 patients diagnosed with resistant hypertension complicated with anxiety and depression who met the predefined inclusion criteria were enrolled. Based on whether the psycho-cardiology model-related assessment and psychological and behavioural management were systematically documented in their medical records, the patients were divided into a psycho-cardiology group (n = 63) and a regular group (n = 63). Changes in anxiety, depression, sleep quality, and blood pressure level were compared between the two groups during the follow-up period.
RESULTS: At the end of follow-up, the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, Hamilton Depression Rating Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores of the psychocardiology group were significantly lower than those of the regular group (p < 0.05); Reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure were greater in the psycho-cardiology group than in the regular group (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In the long-term management of patients with resistant hypertension and anxiety and depression, the psycho-cardiology model combined with psychological and behavioural management was associated with milder negative emotions, better sleep status, improved autonomic function and more stable blood pressure profiles in this retrospective cohort.

Title: Anxiety Symptoms Assessed by the Goldberg Anxiety and Depression Scale, Lifestyle Habits, and Cardiometabolic Risk in Spanish Workers.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety has been increasingly recognized as a relevant contributor to cardiometabolic dysfunction through neuroendocrine, inflammatory, and behavioral mechanisms. However, evidence evaluating the relationship between anxiety symptoms, lifestyle habits, and cardiometabolic risk in large occupational populations remains limited. This study aimed to analyze the association between Goldberg Anxiety and Depression Scale (GADS) scores, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic risk factors in a large cohort of Spanish workers.
METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 119,336 Spanish workers undergoing routine occupational health examinations between 2021 and 2023. Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the GADS. Lifestyle variables included smoking status, physical activity assessed with the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and adherence to the Mediterranean diet evaluated through the Prevention with Mediterranean Diet (PREDIMED) questionnaire. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, lipid profile, fasting glucose, obesity, abdominal obesity, and metabolic syndrome were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for cardiometabolic abnormalities according to anxiety status and lifestyle factors.
RESULTS: Elevated GADS scores were significantly associated with worse cardiometabolic profiles in both sexes, including higher blood pressure, triglycerides, fasting glucose, body mass index, waist circumference, and lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations. Workers with elevated anxiety presented markedly higher prevalences of hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, impaired fasting glucose, abdominal obesity, and metabolic syndrome (all p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, elevated anxiety remained independently associated with hypertension (OR 6.48; 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.89-7.09), hypertriglyceridemia (OR 5.31; 95% CI 4.60-6.02), and impaired fasting glucose (OR 5.23; 95% CI 4.64-5.83). Physical inactivity and low adherence to the Mediterranean diet were associated with a less favorable cardiometabolic profile among participants with elevated anxiety scores. Elevated GADS scores were independently associated with all major cardiometabolic outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with the strongest associations observed for hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and impaired fasting glucose.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated GADS scores are strongly associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles in Spanish workers, particularly when combined with unhealthy lifestyle behaviors. These findings support the integration of mental health assessment and lifestyle interventions into occupational cardiometabolic prevention strategies.

Title: Effects of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Combined With Perioperative Refined Nursing on Postoperative Sleep Disturbances, Anxiety, and Depression in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess whether integrating mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) into refined perioperative nursing is associated with improvements in postoperative sleep disturbances, anxiety, and depression in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 146 CABG patients treated at Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, from July 2023 to August 2025. To reduce selection bias, 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed based on baseline characteristics, yielding 73 matched pairs for analysis. Based on the nursing protocol documented in the medical records, patients were classified into two groups: a standard care group had received standard refined perioperative nursing, while an MBSR group had received the same care supplemented with MBSR. Outcome measures included Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) scores assessed preoperatively and on postoperative day 7, objective sleep architecture indices obtained via actigraphy on the day of surgery and on postoperative day 7, length of hospital stay, time to first postoperative ambulation, incidence of sleep disturbances on postoperative day 7, and serum levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6), cortisol, orexin, and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) measured preoperatively and at 24 and 72 hours postoperatively. Statistical analyses included t-tests, repeated measures analysis of variance, and chi‑square tests.
RESULTS: After PSM, 73 patients were included in each group, with all standardized mean differences <0.1. Baseline preoperative HADS scores did not differ between groups (p > 0.05). On postoperative day 7, bothgroups showed reductions in (HADS-Anxiety) HADS-A and HADS-Depression (HADS-D), with the MBSR group exhibiting significantly lower scores on all HADS subscales than the standard care group (p < 0.05). PSQI scores on the day of surgery were similar (p > 0.05); On postoperative day 7, both groups improved in total PSQI and across its seven domains versus the surgical day. The MBSR group had significantly better scores than the standard care group for all PSQI domains and total score except subjective sleep quality and hypnotic use(p < 0.05). Time to first postoperative ambulation was shorter and the rate of sleep disturbance on postoperative day 7 was lower in the MBSR group (p < 0.05); mean hospital stay did not differ (p > 0.05). Objective sleep parameters on the day of surgery were comparable (p > 0.05); on postoperative day 7 both groups showed increased total sleep time and sleep efficiency, with greater gains in the MBSR group (p < 0.05). Nighttime awakenings decreased in both groups, with the MBSR group showing a larger reduction (p < 0.05). Repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed significant effects of time, group, and time-by-group interaction for cortisol, orexin, IL-6, and TNF-α (p < 0.05). Within-group analyses showed postoperative increases in cortisol, IL-6, and TNF-α at 24 and 72 hours and declines in orexin versus baseline (p < 0.05). Between-group comparisons at 24 and 72 hours postoperatively demonstrated lower cortisol, IL-6, and TNF-α and higher orexin in the MBSR group compared with the standard care group (p < 0.05), and the temporal patterns differed significantly between groups (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Refined perioperative nursing incorporating MBSR was associated with alleviation of negative emotions in patients undergoing CABG, a lower incidence of sleep disturbances on the 7th postoperative day, and shorter time to first postoperative ambulation.

Title: Neurodevelopmental Trajectories and Neurodevelopmental Disorders Following Neonatal Intracranial Hemorrhage: A Long-Term Follow-Up Study and Analysis of Influencing Factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the neurodevelopmental trajectories, the incidence of neurodevelopmental disorders, and associated influencing factors in children following neonatal intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), thereby providing a reference for clinical intervention and prognostic improvement.
METHODS: A total of 80 neonates diagnosed with ICH and admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of the Second Affiliated Hospital and Yuying Children's Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University were enrolled in this study. All participants completed long-term follow-up assessments over a period of 3-5 years. Baseline clinical data and imaging findings were collected. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were evaluated using the Gesell Developmental Schedules, and neurodevelopmental disorders were identified according to the diagnostic criteria for Brain Damage Syndrome (BDS). The characteristics of neurodevelopmental trajectories, the incidence of neurodevelopmental disorders, and relevant influencing factors were systematically analyzed.
RESULTS: At the conclusion of follow-up, the proportion of children with neurodevelopmental abnormalities (defined as any Developmental Quotient [DQ] <85 on the Gesell Developmental Schedules) was 43.75%, while the incidence of neurodevelopmental disorders (defined according to the diagnostic criteria for BDS) was 38.75%. Gesell Developmental Schedule scores at the 1-, 3-, and 5-year follow-ups showed a gradual increase, with statistically significant differences between time points; the mean total scores were 72.36 ± 5.84, 81.57 ± 6.24, and 86.71 ± 5.93, respectively (F = 113.78, p < 0.001). Univariate analysis revealed that Papile grade of hemorrhage (p < 0.001), hemorrhage location (p < 0.001), birth weight (p < 0.001), gestational age (p < 0.001), perinatal asphyxia (p < 0.001), and concurrent hydrocephalus (p = 0.003) were significantly associated with neurodevelopmental disorders. Multivariate logistic regression identified parenchymal hemorrhage (odds ratio [OR] = 4.215, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.723-10.312, p = 0.002), Papile Grade IV (intraventricular hemorrhage with parenchymal hemorrhage) (OR = 3.826, 95% CI: 1.612-9.083, p = 0.003), birth weight < 2500 g (OR = 3.561, 95% CI: 1.458-8.697, p = 0.005), and perinatal asphyxia (OR = 3.294, 95% CI: 1.347-8.053, p = 0.009) as independent risk factors for the development of neurodevelopmental disorders following neonatal ICH.
CONCLUSIONS: Although neurodevelopmental outcomes exhibit gradual improvement following neonatal ICH, a substantial proportion of affected children continue to experience long-term neurodevelopmental abnormalities and disorders. Parenchymal hemorrhage, larger hemorrhage volume, low birth weight, and perinatal asphyxia are identified as key determinants influencing the occurrence of neurodevelopmental disorders. Early intervention strategies targeting these risk factors should be implemented in clinical practice to enhance long-term prognosis.

Title: Associations of Combined Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Psychological and Functional Outcomes After Stroke: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To examine whether combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), delivered with standard rehabilitation, was associated with post-stroke depression and anxiety symptoms and secondary neurological and motor outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 180 patients classified according to treatment received in routine clinical practice: combined TMS + tDCS + standard rehabilitation (n = 60), standard rehabilitation alone (n = 60), TMS + standard rehabilitation (n = 30), or tDCS + standard rehabilitation (n = 30). Treatment selection reflected physician recommendations and patient preference. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item scale (GAD-7) scores were primary outcomes; National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), modified Rankin Scale (mRS), and Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) scores were secondary outcomes. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks. Generalized estimating equations adjusted for prespecified measured covariates assessed group, time, and group × time associations. Dunnett-adjusted comparisons used standard rehabilitation as the reference.
RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were detected in the measured baseline characteristics (all p > 0.05). At 8 weeks, the combined group had lower median BDI scores [8.0 (6.0, 10.0) vs. 14.5 (11.5, 17.0)] and GAD-7 scores [6.0 (4.0, 8.0) vs. 9.0 (7.0, 11.0)] than the Standard Rehabilitation Group (both Dunnett-adjusted p < 0.001). Significant group × time associations were identified for BDI, GAD-7, NIHSS, mRS, and FMA outcomes (all p < 0.05). The combined group also had lower NIHSS and mRS scores and higher FMA scores than the standard rehabilitation group at 4 and 8 weeks. No severe adverse events were documented. Total recorded adverse-event rates were 8.3%, 5.0%, 3.3%, and 3.3% across the four groups, respectively, with no significant between-group difference (Fisher's exact p = 0.584).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, combined TMS and tDCS with standard rehabilitation was associated with lower depression and anxiety symptom scores and more favorable neurological and motor outcome trajectories than standard rehabilitation. Non-random treatment allocation and residual confounding preclude causal interpretation; prospective randomized studies are required.

Title: Joint Association of Longitudinal Single-Point Insulin Sensitivity Estimator Patterns and Hypertension Status with Incident Stroke Among Adults with Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages 0-3: A Nationwide Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of longitudinal single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) patterns for stroke, particularly when considered in combination with hypertension (HTN), remains unclear among adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.
AIMS: This study aimed to examine the association of combined longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status with incident stroke among adults with CKM syndrome stages 0-3.
STUDY DESIGN: A nationwide prospective cohort study.
METHODS: We included adults aged ≥ 45 years with CKM stages 0-3 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. SPISE was calculated at Waves 1 and 3, and incident stroke was ascertained through Wave 5. K-means clustering was used to identify longitudinal SPISE patterns, which were dichotomized as persistently low or non-persistently low. Participants were then cross-classified according to longitudinal SPISE pattern and baseline HTN status. Cumulative SPISE exposure was calculated from repeated SPISE measurements. Cox models were used to examine associations with incident stroke. Dose-response, subgroup, sensitivity, and model-performance analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: Among 4,443 participants, 348 incident strokes occurred. A persistently low longitudinal SPISE pattern was associated with a higher risk of incident stroke than a persistently high pattern [hazard ratio (HR), 2.29; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.59-3.29]. Compared with the group with no HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern, stroke risk was higher in the group with no HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.12-1.95), the group with HTN and a non-persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.10-2.23), and the group with HTN and a persistently low SPISE pattern (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.84-3.26). Higher cumulative SPISE exposure was inversely associated with incident stroke (HR per 1-unit increment, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.93-0.97), with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. Incorporating the combined longitudinal SPISE pattern and HTN status increased the apparent C-index from 0.612 to 0.646. However, optimism-corrected discrimination was comparable between the combined model and the HTN-only model.
CONCLUSION: The combination of longitudinal SPISE patterns and HTN status identified a subgroup at the highest risk of incident stroke in this CKM population.

Title: Achieving Risk-Specific Absolute LDL-C Threshold with PCSK9 Inhibitors: A Real-World, Single-Center Analysis.
Journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors emerged as an effective treatment for hypercholesterolemia in clinical trials, however real-world evidence shows considerable heterogeneity. We aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of injectable PCSK9 inhibitors in real-world patients.
METHODS: Our retrospective analysis included 45 consecutive adults, 18 (40%) men, mean age 57.4 years, inadequately controlled on, or intolerant to, statins and/or ezetimibe, and newly initiated on alirocumab 75 mg or 150 mg, evolocumab 140 mg, or inclisiran 284 mg. Biochemical parameters and adverse events were recorded at baseline and when LDL-C reached the risk-specific absolute threshold or the lowest LDL-C closest to it after starting PCSK9 inhibitors (<55 mg/dL very high, <70 mg/dL high cardiovascular risk, per European Society of Cardiology). LDL-C was also assessed at standardized time points (3, 6, 12, 18, 24 months).
RESULTS: At 3 and 6 months, LDL-C decreased by a median of 54.4% and 59.2% (both p < 0.001), with 52.4% and 50.0% of patients below threshold. The best LDL-C reduction was 66.9% (from 145 mg/dL to 50 mg/dL; p < 0.001) at a median time to first documented threshold attainment of 5 months. In an exploratory analysis, no significant association was detected between LDL-C reduction and sex, diabetes, statin intensity or ezetimibe use. No clinically relevant hepatic or muscular toxicity was attributed to PCSK9 inhibitors.
CONCLUSION: In real-world patients aiming to achieve the absolute LDL-C threshold on PCSK9 inhibitors, treatment was associated with marked LDL-C reduction after a median of 5 months.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Patients Hospitalized With Diabetic Foot Ulcer at a Tertiary Hospital in Ethiopia: A 5-Year Retrospective Audit.
Abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer is a major cause of hospitalization and lower extremity amputation, particularly in low-resource settings where patients frequently present with advanced wound. This study assessed the clinical outcomes of patients admitted with diabetic foot ulcer. We conducted a retrospective study of patients admitted to a public hospital in Ethiopia with diabetic foot ulcer. The primary outcome was lower-extremity amputation. Descriptive analyses, bivariate comparisons, and logistic regression were performed. A total of 146 patients hospitalized with diabetic foot ulcer were included. The mean (±SD) age was 59.4 (±11.7) years. Most patients presented with advanced disease: 86.3% had Wagner grade ≥ 3% and 60.3% had Texas stage C/D. Overall, 53.4% underwent lower-extremity amputation. Factors associated with higher odds of amputation were: long standing diabetes (duration ≥ 10 years: Adjusted Odds Ratio: 2.42; [95% Confidence Interval: 1.01-5.80]), longer ulcer duration (every day of delayed presentation: 1.02 [1.01-1.03]), previous foot ulcer (4.34 [1.55-12.13]), advanced ulcer stages with University of Texas stage C or D (2.86 [1.19-6.90]). Hospitalized diabetic foot ulcer patients presented with advanced disease and experienced a very high lower-extremity amputation burden. This high in-hospital amputation rate in a low-income country highlights the profound disparity in preventive and limb-saving diabetic foot interventions.

Title: Effectiveness of Digital Commitment Devices in Improving Lifestyle and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Adults with Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
AIM: Lifestyle modification is crucial for cardiovascular disease prevention but remains challenging due to complex behavioural factors such as the intention-behaviour gap. Digital commitment devices (DCD) could narrow this gap by leveraging behavioural economics, but its effectiveness remains unclear. Therefore, this review aims to evaluate the effects of DCDs on lifestyle and cardiometabolic outcomes in adults with elevated cardiometabolic risk.
METHODS: A systematic search of 12 electronic databases was conducted from database inception to August 2025. Study selection and methodological quality appraisal using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Where appropriate, effect sizes were pooled using random effects meta-analyses. The certainty of evidence for meta-analysed outcomes was assessed using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: A total of 7,378 articles were retrieved, of which 29 randomised controlled trials involving 7,534 participants were included. DCDs were found to significantly increase daily step count (WMD=664.87, 95% CI: 463.22 to 866.51, T=6.88, p<0.00001; I2=0%) and weight loss (WMD=-1.90kg, 95% CI: -2.59 to -1.21, p<0.0001; I2=70%), improve self-reported emotional (WMD=-1.34, 95% CI: -2.59 to -0.09, p=0.04; I2=0%) and uncontrolled eating (WMD=-1.74, 95% CI: -3.05 to -0.43, p=0.02; I2=0%) behaviours, body fat percentage, diet and medication adherence.
CONCLUSION: DCDs could improve lifestyle and cardiometabolic outcomes by improving physical activity and weight management, thus enhancing cardiometabolic disease prevention. Future research should prioritise long-term trials with extended follow-up periods beyond 12 months to observe physiological improvements and assess maintenance of effects.

Title: Comparison of Optical Coherence Tomography Biomarkers in Nonproliferative and Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Marmasia Study Group Report No. 2.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers and visual acuity between eyes with nonproliferative (NPDR) and proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) in real-life clinical settings.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional, multicentre study included 818 eyes of 534 patients with treatment-naive diabetic macular oedema (DMO) from nine tertiary clinics. Evaluated parameters included central macular thickness (CMT), DMO morphology, disorganisation of the retinal inner layers, ellipsoid zone (EZ) integrity, vitreoretinal interface abnormality (VRIA), and posterior hyaloid status. Analyses used eye-level data with patient-clustered robust standard errors and study-centre fixed effects. A joint multivariable logistic model mutually adjusted EZ integrity, posterior hyaloid status and VRIA together with clinical covariates, with Holm correction across six structural-domain tests.
RESULTS: Of the 818 eyes, 646 had NPDR and 172 PDR. Mean best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was worse in PDR (0.74±0.54 versus 0.57±0.42 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution; p<0.001). In univariable clustered comparisons, no biomarker survived false discovery rate correction across ten comparisons (lowest q=0.095, VRIA). In the joint model (636 eyes, 431 clusters), none survived Holm correction: posterior hyaloid detachment was nominally associated with PDR (odds ratio [OR] 2.03, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-3.92; Holm p=0.208), the global EZ term was not significant (p=0.221), and VRIA was not significant after adjustment for posterior hyaloid status (OR 1.36, 95% CI 0.67-2.75; p=0.388). Centre-adjusted CMT did not differ (p=0.890). Secondarily, PDR, disrupted EZ, higher CMT and VRIA were each associated with worse BCVA.
CONCLUSION: In treatment-naive DMO, no structural OCT biomarker was independently associated with proliferative disease after accounting for fellow-eye correlation, centre effects, mutual adjustment, and multiplicity. Posterior hyaloid detachment gave the most consistent nominal signal, and the vitreoretinal interface variables carried overlapping rather than independent information. These findings do not establish prognosis.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Comparative Study

Title: Longitudinal effects of CGRP-targeting migraine therapies on blood pressure and body mass index: A 12-month retrospective analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare blood pressure (BP) and body mass index (BMI) trajectories associated with individual calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeting migraine therapies versus matched CGRP-unexposed controls.
BACKGROUND: CGRP is a potent vasodilator with established roles in vascular homeostasis and metabolic regulation. Postmarketing surveillance identified BP elevations in erenumab-treated patients, prompting a U.S. Food and Drug Administration label update; however, comparative longitudinal data across CGRP monoclonal antibodies and gepants remain limited. Real-world evidence is needed to characterize medication-specific cardiovascular and metabolic effects in clinical practice.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using structured electronic health record data from the Jefferson Headache Center in Philadelphia, PA, USA (2018 to 2025). Adults initiating erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, atogepant, or preventive rimegepant were compared with propensity score-matched patients receiving migraine care without CGRP-targeting therapy. Twelve-month systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), and BMI trajectories were evaluated.
RESULTS: A total of 6361 patients were included (1892 controls; 4469 CGRP-treated; 80.4% female; mean age 45.6 ± 15.3 years). Controls demonstrated a positive within-group SBP trajectory (0.16 mmHg/month; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06 to 0.27) and BMI trajectory (0.022 kg/m2/month; 95% CI 0.004 to 0.040) but not DBP trajectory (0.06 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.02 to 0.14). Among CGRP-treated groups, only erenumab showed a positive within-group SBP trajectory (0.11 mmHg/month; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.20); however, the difference in slope between erenumab and controls was not significant (-0.05 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.19 to 0.09). Compared with controls, atogepant (-0.38 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.61 to -0.15), fremanezumab (-0.27 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.42 to -0.11), and galcanezumab (-0.31 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.46 to -0.16) demonstrated more negative SBP trajectories. For DBP, only atogepant showed a more negative trajectory than controls (-0.18 mmHg/month; 95% CI -0.32 to -0.04). For BMI, both atogepant (-0.113 kg/m2/month; 95% CI -0.159 to -0.067) and erenumab (-0.031 kg/m2/month; 95% CI -0.053 to -0.008) had more negative trajectories compared to controls.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center study, CGRP-targeting therapies were not associated with greater BP increases than matched controls. Cardiometabolic trajectories varied by medication, with generally small BP differences and a robust BMI reduction with atogepant. These findings do not support a uniform adverse cardiometabolic class effect, though prospective studies with systematic monitoring are needed to confirm long-term clinical significance.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure.
RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Four weeks of isometric handgrip training results in lower awake ambulatory blood pressure compared with control: a randomized clinical trial.
Abstract: We compared the effects of upper-limb (handgrip) and lower-limb (knee extension) isometric training on ambulatory blood pressure in individuals with controlled hypertension. In this randomized controlled trial, 67 adults receiving antihypertensive medication were allocated to a control group (CG, n = 22), small muscle mass isometric training (SMM, handgrip; n = 22), or large muscle mass isometric training (LMM, knee extension; n = 23). Participants completed 12 supervised sessions over 4 weeks, with the exercise protocols performed at 30% of upper-limb MVC or lower-limb maximal isometric load, respectively. Ambulatory blood pressure outcomes were compared using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for the corresponding baseline office blood pressure. Hourly 24-h profiles were analyzed using generalized estimating equations with Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc tests. Significant between-group differences were observed only for awake ambulatory blood pressure. Compared with CG, SMM showed lower awake systolic blood pressure (121.8 ± 3.1 vs. 124.2 ± 2.6 mmHg; p = 0.017) and awake diastolic blood pressure (76.3 ± 3.6 vs. 80.8 ± 4.2 mmHg; p = 0.009). No significant differences were observed between LMM and CG, between the two exercise groups, or for 24-h and sleep blood pressure. These findings indicate that, after 4 weeks of supervised isometric training, modest between-group differences in awake ambulatory blood pressure were observed only for handgrip training compared with the control group. Greater muscle mass recruitment did not result in superior antihypertensive effects, suggesting that the chronic blood pressure response to isometric exercise is not determined solely by the amount of muscle mass involved. Trial registration: "ClinicalTrials.gov," "NCT07147595."
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Expanding Primary Care-Based Echocardiography Access in a Value-Based Care Network: Impact on Heart Failure Detection, Utilization, and Spending.
Abstract: This retrospective observational study assessed whether expanding primary care-based echocardiography access within a rural Pennsylvania value-based care network was associated with differences in heart failure (HF) diagnosis patterns, health care utilization, and spending compared with internal controls and a state-level benchmark. Eligibility, medical, and pharmacy claims were analyzed from 2 sources: third-party payers covering the primary care network and Merative's MarketScan Medicare data as a state-level reference. Members with HF-related risk factors were identified using diagnosis codes and followed for 12 months after index risk factor documentation, and the inverse probability of treatment weighting was used, incorporating age, sex, risk score, HF risk-factor category, and eligibility duration to address baseline demographic and clinical differences. Among members with HF risk factors, 21.0% of internal study members received an incident HF diagnosis compared with 13.7% of MarketScan members (P < 0.01). Internal cohort diagnoses were less likely to occur in inpatient (IP) settings than MarketScan diagnoses (0.53% vs. 10.2%; P < 0.01) and occurred after longer intervals from risk factor documentation (202 vs. 142 days; P < 0.01). Among diagnosed members, the internal cohort had lower HF-related IP admissions (21 vs. 28 per 1,000 member-years; P < 0.01), fewer HF-related emergency department visits (34 vs. 49 per 1000 member-years; P < 0.01), and lower average monthly spending ($1,937 vs. $2,826; P < 0.01). These findings suggest that expanding primary care-based echocardiography access in a rural value-based care setting was associated with greater HF detection, more outpatient-based diagnosis, and lower downstream acute care use and spending, broadly applicable to health systems and payers investing in diagnostics.

Title: Effects of Virtual Reality Based Aerobic Exercise on Pulmonary Function and Cardiopulmonary Fitness in Parkinson's Disease: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Background:Respiratory dysfunction in Parkinson's Disease (PD) contributes to exercise intolerance and morbidity, yet video gaming-based aerobic exercise remains underexplored.Method: This single-blinded pilot Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) aimed to evaluate the effects of exergaming-based aerobic exercise using the Nintendo Wii Fit Plus platform (EG) program on pulmonary function, cardiopulmonary fitness, and dyspnea in 30 patients with PD (Hoehn and Yahr stages II to III) with respiratory impairment, randomized to a EG exercise group (n = 15) or control group (n = 15). Supervised aerobic training was conducted using the Wii Fit Plus platform, performed 3×/week for 12 weeks at 40%-70% of peak heart rate (HRpeak). Controls maintained usual activity. Primary outcomes were spirometry (forced vital capacity [FVC], forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1), FEV1/FVC ratio, and peak expiratory flow [PEF]). Secondary outcomes were peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak), HRpeak, Borg rating of perceived exertion (RPE), and dyspnea scale (mMRC). Outcomes were assessed at baseline and post-intervention using mixed-model repeated-measures Analysis of Variance (ANOVA).Results: The EG group showed significant group × improvements in FVC (P = 0.018), FEV1 (P = 0.021), FEV1/FVC (P = 0.039), PEF (P = 0.011), VO2peak (P = 0.004), dyspnea Borg RPE (P = 0.006), and mMRC (P = 0.028). While HRpeak showed no significant difference (P = 0.071). Adherence to the EG program was high (92%), with no reported adverse events. EG-based aerobic exercise significantly improved pulmonary function, aerobic capacity, and perceived dyspnea in individuals with PD.Conclusion:Findings support the feasibility and potential clinical value for PD. Larger trials are warranted to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

Title: Early outcomes after complete atrioventricular septal defect repair beyond one year of age: a single-centre comparative study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete atrioventricular septal defect is usually repaired during early infancy, but delayed referral remains common where access to specialised congenital cardiac surgery is limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare early outcomes after repair in patients aged 12 months or younger and those older than 12 months.
METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included 81 patients who underwent repair between 2020 and 2024. All patients evaluated for repair underwent cardiac catheterisation, and those with elevated pulmonary vascular resistance underwent vasoreactivity testing with 100% oxygen and inhaled nitric oxide. In-hospital mortality, major complications, pulmonary artery pressure, atrioventricular valve regurgitation, and perioperative outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Thirty-five patients were aged 12 months or younger and 46 were older than 12 months. Median ages were 8 and 14 months, respectively. In-hospital mortality occurred in 3 of 35 and 4 of 46 patients, respectively. Major complications occurred in 6 of 35 and 11 of 46 patients. No statistically significant differences were detected in mortality, major complications, ventilation duration, ICU stay, pulmonary artery pressure, or early atrioventricular valve regurgitation. Confidence intervals around mortality and major-complication estimates were wide.
CONCLUSION: Repair beyond 12 months was feasible in selected patients considered operable after invasive assessment, but in-hospital mortality remained substantial and estimates were imprecise. These findings do not establish equivalence and should not support intentional delay of repair.

Title: Mitigation Strategies: A Standardized Multimodal Pathway to Reduce the Severity of Clinically Relevant Pancreatic Fistula After Pancreaticoduodenectomy.
Abstract: BackgroundPancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) carries significant morbidity, primarily due to clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF). This study investigated the clinical impact of a multimodal mitigation strategy in patients undergoing PD, encompassing prehabilitation, standardized surgical techniques, and optimized postoperative management. The secondary aim was to identify factors associated with grade C POPF.MethodsA single-center retrospective analysis was conducted using a prospective database of 520 patients who underwent pancreatic surgery at our hospital between January 2016 and December 2025. One hundred eighty-four patients who underwent PD were selected and divided into two cohorts using 2022 as a cutoff, the year in which our multimodal mitigation strategy was introduced.ResultsIn the after-2022 cohort, a significant reduction in CR-POPF was observed (39% vs 55%, P = .036), with specific decrease in grade C POPF cases (5% vs 23%, P < .001). A statistically significant reduction in PPH was also observed in the after-2022 cohort (3% vs 17%, P < .001). Furthermore, in after-2022 cohort, there were a reduction of reoperation rate (8% vs 25%, P = .001) and LOS (23.0 days vs 14.5 days, P < .001). For the secondary aim, the multivariate analysis identified the after-2022 period and the occurrence of cardiac and pulmonary complications as factors associated with grade C POPF (respectively P < .001, P = .017 and P < .001).ConclusionsThis study highlights the potential of a structured, multi-level mitigation strategy in improving outcomes after pancreatoduodenectomy, in particular, the severity of pancreatic fistula and its consequences.

Title: Blood transcriptomic signatures of vascular risk in Alzheimer's disease.
Journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lifestyle and environmental factors contributing to cardiovascular risk are components of the exposome, yet molecular signatures associated with cumulative cardiovascular risk in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: We analyzed blood-based transcriptomics data from two independent cohorts: Seoul National University Bundang Hospital (SNUBH; N = 148, Korean) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI; N = 743, predominantly European ancestry). Framingham cardiovascular risk score (FRS)-associated co-expression network modules were identified, followed by pathway-based enrichment, hub gene-based participant stratification, and bidirectional cross-cohort discovery-replication analyses.
RESULTS: Two co-expression modules were associated with FRS in SNUBH, and six in ADNI. Bidirectional analyses identified two preserved modules with consistent module-FRS associations across cohorts, enriched in pathways implicated in cellular responses to exposure, including RNA-protein homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and hematopoietic processes. Hub genes in the two modules stratified participants into molecularly distinct subgroups concordant with clinical FRS categories.
DISCUSSION: FRS-associated molecular pathways were identified and warrant further investigation as potential targets for risk modification.

Title: Need for a definitive trial of local versus general anaesthesia in chronic subdural haematoma; survey and literature review of ongoing trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural haematoma (cSDH) is a common neurosurgical condition, many patients have significant comorbidity or are living with frailty. Surgery is effective and can be performed under local anaesthesia (with or without sedation) (LAS) or general anaesthesia (GA). Optimal technique for both GA and LAS is poorly defined but similar questions have been explored in other surgical settings. We sought to clarify the breadth of evidence for anaesthetic technique in cSDH surgery, while drawing on relevant literature from other disciplines to understand how a definitive trial of this question could be performed.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used a combination of review of trial registries, the Cochrane database, and a survey of anaesthetic and neurosurgical practitioners.
RESULTS: We identified a paucity of high-quality studies, especially randomised trials, exploring this question. The literature, and survey of anaesthetists and surgeons suggest that LAS may achieve equivalent outcomes, but significant confounding exists in current studies. Registered trials are single centre, and Cochrane reviews in other fields present issues of equipoise, study design, and outcome choice as key challenges in designing a definitive trial.
CONCLUSIONS: There is significant interest in this topic as evidenced by published and emerging literature and views of anaesthetists and surgeons. No registered trial is multi-centre or draws on challenges identified in similar trials from other disciplines.

Title: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction: is it the new Ariadne's string?
Abstract: Heart failure with supranormal ejection fraction (HFsnEF) is an emerging and incompletely characterized phenotype within the heart failure (HF) spectrum. Although no universally accepted LVEF threshold for HFsnEF has been established and different definitions have been used across published studies, for the purposes of this review HFsnEF is operationally defined as HF with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) > 65%. Importantly, a supranormal LVEF should not be interpreted as evidence of enhanced ventricular performance. Patients with HFsnEF may exhibit smaller left ventricular (LV) volumes, concentric remodeling, increased myocardial stiffness, impaired longitudinal deformation, reduced stroke volume and preload reserve, and elevated filling pressures, particularly during exercise. HFsnEF is unlikely to represent a single disease entity; rather, it encompasses heterogeneous pathophysiological substrates and clinical phenotypes, including hypertensive and cardiometabolic remodeling, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), and other conditions associated with hyperdynamic ventricular function. Accordingly, the diagnostic evaluation should extend beyond recognition of an elevated LVEF and systematically identify the underlying phenotype and potentially treatable causes through comprehensive echocardiography, myocardial deformation imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, disease-specific testing, and exercise or invasive hemodynamic assessment when indicated. Therapeutic evidence specific to HFsnEF remains limited. No randomized clinical trial has specifically evaluated conventional HF pharmacotherapy in a population prospectively defined by LVEF > 65%; therefore, evidence for conventional HF and cardiometabolic therapies is derived predominantly from broader HFpEF populations or subgroup analyses and should be regarded as indirect rather than definitive evidence for HFsnEF. In contrast, recognition of specific underlying diseases, particularly ATTR-CM, HCM, and significant valvular heart disease, may permit evidence-based disease-specific treatment. This review summarizes the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical phenotypes of HFsnEF and proposes a practical phenotype-guided approach to diagnosis and management. Standardized definitions and prospective trials specifically addressing patients with LVEF > 65% are needed to establish evidence-based therapeutic strategies for this population.

Title: Comparison of visual estimation of ventricular systolic function with quantitative echocardiographic markers in newborn infants.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatologist-performed echocardiography (NPE) is increasingly practiced. NPE operators typically use visual estimation of systolic function and, if indicated, confirm function using quantitative echocardiographic markers. This exploratory study aims to compare the concordance between qualitative and quantitative echocardiographic markers among NPE and non-NPE operators.
METHODS: We studied a cohort of newborn infants, undergoing routine NPE by the authors at Homerton University Hospital and Aberdeen Maternity Hospital from April 2024 to October 2024. Blinded NPE and non-NPE operators independently assessed left and right ventricular systolic function visually. We compared visual estimation with standard quantitative echocardiographic markers such as shortening fraction, Simpson's ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain for left ventricle and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and fractional area change for right ventricle. We examined the concordance between visual estimation and quantitative echocardiographic markers for biventricular systolic function.
RESULTS: Sixty infants with a mean (SD) gestation and birth weight of 34 (6.2) weeks and 2311 (1319) grams respectively were examined. Sensitivity testing for all echocardiographic parameters ranged from 25% to 80% whereas specificity ranged from 38% to 78%. Sensitivity increased with worsening grades of LV dysfunction defined using shortening fraction. While concordance between NPE and non-NPE operator was generally limited across most echocardiographic parameters, test-retest reliability was acceptable for several quantitative measures, including Simpson's ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain and right ventricular fractional area change.
CONCLUSION: Visual estimation may be a useful bedside tool for detecting severe ventricular dysfunction in newborn infants; however; quantitative echocardiographic measures are likely to improve the assessment of mild to moderate dysfunction. Further studies should confirm these findings in a larger cohort with a higher representation of infants with ventricular dysfunction.

Title: Beyond the primer: anatomical site and cyst viability drive the molecular detection of Taenia saginata in slaughterhouse samples.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bovine cysticercosis, caused by the larval stage of Taenia saginata, results in significant economic losses for the beef industry due to carcass condemnation. While routine post-mortem inspection is mandatory, visual diagnosis lacks specificity, particularly for degenerated or calcified cysts. This study primarily aimed to evaluate how anatomical site and cyst viability influence the molecular confirmation of suspected lesions. As a secondary methodological objective, we assessed the performance of three conventional PCR assays-a widely used large subunit (LSU) rRNA target (328 bp), a previously described Cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 (COX1) target (253 bp), and a novel COX1 target (428 bp) designed herein-to ensure primer selection did not bias our findings. A total of 232 suspect macroscopic lesions (180 calcified cysts, 12 viable cysts, and 40 non-specific lesions) were collected from cattle slaughtered in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.
RESULTS: Our results demonstrated no statistically significant difference in diagnostic sensitivity among the three primer sets (p > 0.05), indicating that molecular confirmation is not limited by primer selection. Instead, molecular detection was profoundly driven by cyst viability and anatomical location (p < 0.001). While viable cysts yielded high positivity rates (up to 66.7%; 95% CI: 34.9%-90.1%), detection in calcified lesions dropped to approximately 28.9% due to severe DNA degradation. Crucially, calcified hepatic lesions exhibited drastically lower PCR positivity (11.4%-15.2%) compared to those in the heart (46.0%-54.0%) and head muscles (50.0%-60.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that the anatomical location of a lesion heavily dictates molecular detection rates. While visual inspection of hepatic tissue often conflicts with molecular results, negative PCR in the liver does not necessarily indicate the absence of infection. Rather, this discrepancy highlights a critical limitation in detecting highly degraded DNA, likely driven by rapid clearance within the enzymatically aggressive hepatic parenchyma, combined with the potential misclassification of non-parasitic granulomas. Due to the high rate of false negatives in calcified cysts, conventional PCR cannot be safely recommended for real-time carcass clearance. Instead, to improve diagnostic accuracy, epidemiological surveillance and retrospective sanitary audits should prioritize suspect lesions in the heart and striated muscles over those found in the liver.

Title: AI-based automated body composition analysis from whole-body MRI and (PET-) CT: an intermodal comparison from same-day examinations.
