Journal: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine intermodal agreement of AI-derived volumetric body composition metrics between [18 F]FDG-PET/CT-derived low-dose CT and whole-body MRI (wb-MRI).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed same-day whole-body low-dose CT, obtained from [18F]FDG-PET/CT, and wb-MRI from consecutive multiple myeloma patients from the prospective GMMG-HD7- and GMMG-HD8-/DSMM-XIX-trials. An automated deep learning pipeline based on the TotalSegmentator model, and its MRI variant were used to segment skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous- (SAT) and abdominal visceral adipose tissue (VAT) from CT and MRI, respectively. Volumetric measures and single-slice estimates were derived. Agreement between CT- and MRI-based metrics was assessed using Pearson r, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), and Bland-Altman analyses.
RESULTS: Forty-two multiple myeloma patients with same-day PET/CT and wb-MRI were included. For AI-based volumetric body composition metrics, CT and MRI demonstrated high agreement (ICC > 0.95) across all SM, SAT and VAT. However, Bland-Altmann plots revealed systematic modality-related differences between MRI and CT: both SM (bias: -2582 ml, p < 0.0001) and VAT (bias: -211 ml, p < 0.0001) were significantly lower when extracted from MRI compared to CT, while for SAT, the difference was not statistically significant (bias: -263 ml, p = 0.1629). For AI-based single slice analysis, agreement remained high for SAT and VAT (ICC > 0.97), while being lower for SM (ICC 0.87). Bland-Altman plots showed that SM was systematically and significantly lower when obtained from MRI than from CT (bias: -18.4cm2, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated body composition measures from (PET-)CT and wb-MRI are highly concordant but show consistent intermodal biases that should be considered when pooling multimodal data or applying modality-agnostic thresholds.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Novel surgical approach to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction: an acute volume overload rat model.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction frequently complicates cardiac surgery, primarily driven by perioperative acute volume overload (AVO). This study aimed to establish a novel surgical rat model that recapitulates AVO-mediated left ventricular diastolic dysfunction for translational research.
METHODS: Twenty male Sprague Dawley rats (6-8 weeks old) were equally and randomly divided into AVO group (intraventricular saline infusion at 3 ml/h) and Sham group (no fluid infusion). A 22-gauge cannula was inserted into left ventricle chamber to record pressure and inject fluid after left thoracotomy. Hemodynamic and echocardiographic statistics were obtained at baseline, 10 min, 20 min, 30 min and 40 min. Two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was applied to compare longitudinal cardiac parameters, with Mauchly's sphericity test and Greenhouse-Geisser correction for sphericity violation; Bonferroni post-hoc tests corrected for multiple pairwise comparisons.
RESULTS: RM-ANOVA detected statistically significant main effects of group, time, and group×time interaction for LV systolic pressure (LVSP), LV diastolic pressure (LVDP), and LV end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) (all P < 0.001). In the AVO group, LVEDP increased progressively over time, rising by 102.7% relative to baseline at the 40 min time point. Post-hoc testing confirmed substantially higher LVEDP in AVO rats versus sham animals at 40 min (15.2 ± 0.79 mmHg vs. 7.5 ± 0.71 mmHg, adjusted P < 0.001). A prominent group×time interaction was also observed for the mitral E/A ratio (P < 0.001): this ratio declined to 0.54 in the AVO group at 40 min, which differed significantly from sham controls (0.54 ± 0.01 vs. 1.73 ± 0.01, adjusted P < 0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) exhibited a significant group×time interaction as well, falling to 62.82% at 40 min in AVO rats compared with 76.34% ± 0.36 in sham animals (adjusted P < 0.001). All hemodynamic and echocardiographic readouts remained stable across all time points in the sham group, with no statistically significant temporal changes observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute volume overload induced heart diastolic dysfunction in rats is a cost-effective and time-efficient experimental animal model.

Title: Superb microvascular imaging versus CT angiography for assessing disease activity in pediatric Takayasu arteritis: a comparative study with high consistency.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the value and consistency of superb microvascular imaging (SMI) and CT angiography (CTA) for assessing disease activity in pediatric Takayasu arteritis (TA), and to explore the feasibility of SMI as a non-invasive screening tool.
METHODS: Forty-seven children with TA treated at our hospital between May 2019 and January 2025 were included. Disease activity was determined using the National Institutes of Health (NIH) criteria, and patients were classified into active (n = 26) and inactive (n = 21) groups. All patients underwent both SMI and CTA. The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of SMI grading and CTA for diagnosing TA activity were analyzed. Kappa tests were used to assess consistency with NIH criteria. Inter-observer agreement for SMI grading was also evaluated.
RESULTS: SMI grading was significantly higher in the active group than in the inactive group (Z = 5.388, p < 0.001). Using SMI grade ≥ II as the cutoff, SMI had a sensitivity of 84.62%, specificity of 95.24%, and accuracy of 89.36%. CTA had a sensitivity of 88.46%, specificity of 90.48%, and accuracy of 89.36%. The AUC values were 0.885 for SMI and 0.895 for CTA. SMI showed good consistency with NIH criteria (Kappa = 0.788), as did CTA (Kappa = 0.786). Inter-observer agreement for SMI grading was good (Kappa = 0.865, 95% CI: 0.777-0.953), with 43 of 47 cases (91.49%) showing complete concordance.
CONCLUSIONS: SMI and CTA demonstrate comparable diagnostic performance and high consistency in assessing disease activity in pediatric TA. Given its non-invasive nature, absence of radiation, no need for contrast agents, and repeatability, SMI is recommended as the preferred screening tool for long-term follow-up of disease activity in pediatric TA, with CTA reserved for cases where SMI suggests activity or when precise vascular assessment is needed.

Title: Machine learning-based radiomic analysis of T2-FLAIR white matter hyperintensity predicts hemorrhagic transformation after endovascular thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains a major complication after endovascular therapy (EVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study aimed to develop and validate a machine-learning model based on T2-FLAIR white matter hyperintensity (WMH) radiomics combined with clinical variables to predict HT after EVT.
METHODS: In this dual-center retrospective study, 446 patients (mean age 61.88 ± 10.98 years; 332 [74.4%] male) with AIS who underwent EVT were enrolled from two centers. Patients from the primary center were randomly assigned to a training cohort and an internal test cohort, and patients from the second center served as an independent external validation cohort. Clinical risk factors were identified by univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Preoperative T2-FLAIR images were used to segment WMH lesions and extract radiomics features. After feature selection, three predictive models were then developed: a clinical model based on the independent clinical predictors, a radiomics model based on the radiomics signature, and a combined model integrating both. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, DeLong testing, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: Among the 446 patients, 153 (34.3%) developed HT within 24-48 h after EVT. Multivariate analysis identified NIHSS score, occlusion site, and atrial fibrillation as independent clinical predictors of HT. In the internal test cohort, the combined model achieved the best discriminative performance (AUC = 0.818, 95% CI: 0.651-0.986), outperforming the clinical model (AUC = 0.740, 95% CI: 0.562-0.917) and the radiomics model (AUC = 0.806, 95% CI: 0.621-0.990). In the external validation cohort, the combined model maintained robust performance (AUC = 0.817, 95% CI: 0.746-0.889), which was comparable to the clinical model (AUC = 0.818, 95% CI: 0.742-0.894) and higher than the radiomics model alone (AUC = 0.764, 95% CI: 0.682-0.845).
CONCLUSIONS: A combined model incorporating T2-FLAIR WMH radiomics and key clinical variables provides a feasible tool for individualized prediction of HT after EVT in patients with AIS, although its incremental discriminatory value over the clinical model alone was limited in the external validation cohort. This approach may help improve perioperative risk stratification and support personalized clinical decision-making.

Title: Safety and tolerability of rapid vericiguat initiation and titration alongside GDMT optimization in HFrEF: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remains challenging to manage, particularly in Asian populations. Although vericiguat may complement guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), the safety and tolerability of rapid initiation and titration in Chinese patients with HFrEF require further evaluation.
METHODS: This single-center, prospective, single-arm, self-controlled cohort study included 140 patients who received at least 1 dose of vericiguat 5 mg and constituted the treated population; 133 had evaluable 14-day titration and short-term safety data. Patients were monitored for dose-titration success, blood pressure, renal function, electrolytes, hepatic function, hemoglobin, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) over 14 days. Echocardiography was performed at 12 and 20 weeks.
RESULTS: The mean age was 61.5 ± 14.2 years, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was 32.87 ± 8.51%. On a treated-population basis, 131 of 140 patients (93.6%) achieved the target vericiguat dose of 10 mg by day 14; among patients with evaluable titration data, 131 of 133 (98.5%) achieved target-dose uptitration. Median NT-proBNP decreased by 44.0% from baseline to day 14 (p < 0.001), without clinically notable blood pressure changes on the day after vericiguat initiation. At 20 weeks, LVEF increased by 8.26% (p < 0.001), accompanied by reductions in left ventricular diastolic diameter and left atrial diameter. No significant renal, hepatic, or electrolyte safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Rapid initiation of vericiguat 5 mg alongside GDMT optimization showed acceptable short-term safety and tolerability in Chinese patients with HFrEF. These findings support further randomized controlled trials to clarify the independent contribution of vericiguat to cardiac remodeling.

Title: Comparative detection of diabetic retinopathy microvascular lesions using single-capture ultrawide-field swept-source OCT angiography versus widefield colour fundus photography.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the detection and quantification of intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMAs) and neovascularization (NV) between widefield colour fundus photography (WF CFP) and single-capture ultrawide-field swept-source OCT angiography (UWF SS-OCTA) across diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity stages, and to evaluate whether paired multimodal review enhances lesion detection and disease classification.
METHODS: Eyes of different DR stages were imaged using 133° WF CFP and 150° UWF OCTA imaging modalities. Images were independently graded by masked, trained graders for the presence and quantification of NVs and IRMAs. Paired multimodal review was then performed bidirectionally for WF CFP and UWF OCTA to assess whether lesion detection could be improved by cross-referencing the corresponding image from the other modality. Intergrader agreement and inter-modality agreement during independent and paired multimodal review were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC).
RESULTS: A total of 120 eyes were analysed (NPDR: 64.6%; PDR: 35.4%). Under independent grading, UWF OCTA detected significantly more lesions than WF CFP across all DR stages (all p < 0.001), with poor inter-modality agreement. Paired multimodal review significantly increased WF CFP lesion counts across all groups (all p < 0.001), while UWF OCTA counts remained unchanged or showed no significant increase. Inter-modality agreement improved after paired review (mild-moderate NPDR IRMA ICC: 0.219; severe NPDR IRMA ICC: 0.334; PDR NV ICC: 0.726), however, UWF OCTA continued to detect significantly more lesions (all p < 0.001). Inter-grader agreement for both NV and IRMA grading was higher for UWF OCTA than WF CFP (NV ICC: 0.974 vs. 0.694; IRMA ICC: 0.635 vs. 0.420). In an exploratory finding, 12 eyes (10%) were reclassified from NPDR to PDR following multimodal review.
CONCLUSIONS: Single-capture UWF OCTA detects significantly more IRMAs and NV than WF CFP, with superior reproducibility. Multimodal review enhances lesion recognition on WF CFP but does not eliminate inter-modality discrepancies. These findings highlight the potential of UWF OCTA to refine DR staging and influence clinical decision-making, supporting its complementary role alongside fundus photography in specialised diabetic eye care.

Title: Thymic-thoracic ratio combined with cardiac axis as a rapid primary screening index for fetuses with conotruncal anomalies: based on sequential cross-sectional scanning.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Conotruncal anomalies are complex and variable and difficult to diagnose. The aim of this study is to investigate the diagnostic value of thymic-thoracic ratio (TT ratio) and Cardiac Axis(CAx) in rapid screening of fetal conotruncal anomalies.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective case-control study was conducted on fetuses from January 2021 to December 2024. Fetal CAx and TT ratio were routinely measured. The Mann-Whitney U test and the Kruskal-Wallis test were used to compare the data. Curve estimation and Pearson correlation were performed to assess the correlation between CAx and TT ratios and gestational age within the group. Logistic regression analysis and ROC curves were conducted.
RESULTS: A total of 91 fetuses with conotruncal anomalies were identified and compared with 104 fetuses with non-conotruncal anomalies and 127 fetuses with normal structures. Compared with the normal group, the TT ratio was significantly reduced in the conotruncal anomalies group (P < 0.001), and the CAx significantly skewed to the left (P < 0.001). In the non-conotruncal anomalies group, only the CAx deviation was significantly different (P < 0.001). Logistic regression analysis revealed that both TT ratio and CAx serve as indirect indicators of conotruncal anomalies, with the area under the ROC curve for the combined prediction model, including TT ratio and CAx, being 0.875. Measurement results demonstrated good consistency both between and within observer groups.
CONCLUSIONS: CAx and TT ratio present distinct manifestations in fetuses with conotruncal anomalies. Their combined use yields potential diagnostic performance for rapidly identifying fetuses with conotruncal anomalies.

Title: Long-term donor and graft safety despite subclinical mitochondrial abnormalities: mechanistic insights from a 22-year follow-up of a carrier-to-MELAS kidney transplant.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ideally, deceased donor kidney transplantation is preferred for patients with mitochondrial nephropathy caused by the m.3243 A > G mutation to avoid genetic risks. However, in regions where deceased donation is limited and living donation predominates, such as Japan, family members are often the only available donors. The safety of using maternal relatives, who are obligate carriers of the mutation, remains highly controversial due to the risk of unmasking renal failure in both the donor and the allograft.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 22-year follow-up of an inadvertent living kidney transplant from a 55-year-old mother to her 26-year-old daughter. The recipient presented with MELAS (Mitochondrial Myopathy, Encephalopathy, Lactic Acidosis, and Stroke-like episodes) and end-stage kidney disease due to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), with the m.3243 A > G mutation confirmed prior to transplantation. Conversely, the donor mother was phenotypically normal regarding renal function without diabetes, and conventional genetic testing at the time failed to detect the mutation. Consequently, the recipient's mutation was presumed to be de novo, allowing the donation to proceed. Notably, the donor's zero-hour allograft biopsy revealed ultrastructural mitochondrial abnormalities but no overt light microscopic damage (i.e., no FSGS). At 22 years post-transplant, both the recipient's graft function (serum creatinine 1.16 mg/dL, albuminuria 5.0 mg/gCr) and the donor's remaining kidney function (serum creatinine 0.98 mg/dL, albuminuria 10.4 mg/gCr) remain excellent. Current highly sensitive genetic analysis revealed an extremely low blood heteroplasmy in the donor (0.1%) compared to 20% in the recipient, demonstrating a severe "genetic bottleneck" effect. Furthermore, the recipient's older sister was found to have a 4% mutational load, definitively confirming maternal inheritance rather than a de novo mutation.
CONCLUSIONS: This case represents the longest reported follow-up of a living kidney transplant from an m.3243 A > G carrier. It demonstrates that maternal carriers with extremely low heteroplasmy and no light microscopic evidence of overt renal damage on biopsy can be safe donors and provide excellent long-term graft outcomes. Precise risk stratification based on genotype and biopsy findings, rather than uniform exclusion, may expand transplant options.

Title: Quantitative assessment of aortic wall thickening disease by dual energy computed tomography angiography.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A broad spectrum of etiologies can lead to aortic wall thickening. This study aimed to evaluate the utility of quantitative parameters derived from dual-layer computed tomography (CT) in differentiating intramural hematoma (IMH), non-calcified plaques, and aortic thrombosis, and to explore their associations with laboratory inflammatory markers.
METHODS: 365 patients were retrospectively enrolled, including atherosclerosis (n = 98), aortic dissection (n = 126), and IMH (n = 141). Laboratory indicators were collected from the electronic medical record system. Regions of interest (ROI) of non-calcified plaques, thrombi, hematomas, and periaortic adipose tissue around lesions were outlined. The lesion enhancement values and degree of enhancement were calculated from the CT values in polyenergetic and virtual non-contrast image. The slope of the energy spectrum curve was determined using the formula: K = (CT40keV - CT100keV) / 60. Normalization was performed for the effective atomic number (Z), iodine density (ID), and iodine non-water density (IW) using the aortic lumen as the standard reference, resulting in normalized Z values, normalized iodine density (NID), and normalized iodine non-water density (NIW).
RESULTS: The enhancement values and degrees of enhancement differed among the three lesions (all P < 0.05). Differences in Z value, ID, IW, and K were observed among non-calcified plaques, thrombi, and hematomas (all P < 0.05). The NID of hematoma was the largest, while the NIW of thrombus was the smallest. Normalized Z value of non-calcified plaque was significantly smaller than those of thrombus and hematoma (both P < 0.05), with no difference between thrombus and hematoma (P > 0.05). The Zperiaortic fat pre- and post-normalization were significantly smaller around the plaques than around the thrombi and hematomas (both P < 0.05). Significant correlations were found between aortic wall normalized Zlesion, Zperiaortic fat, and laboratory parameters, including neutrophil % and neutrophil count, lymphocyte % and lymphocyte count, C-reactive protein, and D-dimer.
CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative spectral CT parameters show promise for the non-invasive identification of aortic wall lesions. The weak correlations with laboratory inflammatory markers suggest a potential but limited link between imaging parameters and local inflammation. These exploratory findings require further validation. If confirmed in future studies, this approach may complement conventional CTA and guide targeted therapy.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

Title: Exploratory safety analysis of tislelizumab-based regimens in patients with lung cancer: a retrospective real-world study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors, including tislelizumab, are used in China and other countries for the treatment of lung cancer. However, the safety profile of tislelizumab has been poorly reported in lung cancer patients based on real-world data. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) and identify associated risk factors.
METHODS: A retrospective, single-center study was conducted using electronic medical records of 212 lung cancer patients treated with tislelizumab-based regimens between February 2021 and February 2023. TrAEs were assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events, version 5.0. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors for trAEs.
RESULTS: Among 212 patients, 98.11% experienced at least one trAE, and 19.81% experienced grade 3-4 trAEs. The most commonly affected systems were hematological (91.98%), hepatobiliary (66.51%), renal (55.19%), and immune (40.57%). The most frequent trAEs included anemia (83.96%), decreased lymphocyte count (53.30%), and increased lactate dehydrogenase (47.64%). Hypothyroidism (25.47%) was the most common immune-related adverse event (irAE). Severe irAEs (grade 3-4) occurred in 1.89% of patients, leading to treatment discontinuation in 4.72%. Risk factors for myelosuppression included squamous non-small cell lung cancer (sq-NSCLC) (OR 3.21, 95% CI 1.48-6.95, P = 0.003) and combination therapy with chemotherapy (OR 3.44, 95% CI 1.79-6.59, p < 0.001). Abnormal liver function was associated with cerebrovascular disease (OR 5.38, 95% CI 1.35-21.49, P = 0.017), elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels (OR 3.74, 95% CI 1.27-11.00, P = 0.016), and decreased creatinine levels (OR 38.82, 95% CI 2.54-592.59, P = 0.009). Renal dysfunction was linked to sq-NSCLC (OR 4.60, 95% CI 2.16-9.82, p < 0.001), decreased eGFR (OR 4.31, 95% CI 2.19-8.48, p < 0.001), and current smoking status (OR 2.75, 95% CI 1.06-7.16, P = 0.038). Thyroid dysfunction was strongly associated with elevated thyrotropin levels (OR 8.09, 95% CI 2.11-31.02, P = 0.002) and cardiovascular disease (OR 4.07, 95% CI 1.75-9.45, P = 0.001). Sq-NSCLC, decreased levels of creatinine and eGFR were more likely to result in electrolyte disturbances, while coagulation dysfunction was influenced by liver disease and decreased eGFR, with female sex being protective.
CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study demonstrated that the safety profile of tislelizumab-based regimens is comparable to that observed in clinical trials, with hematological, hepatic, renal, and immune systems most commonly affected. Several clinical and biochemical factors were identified as potential risk factors for trAEs. Given the single-center retrospective design and lack of a comparator group, these findings should be considered exploratory and need for validation in prospective, multicenter studies to better inform clinical management.

Title: Early neurological deterioration after endovascular treatment in acute ischemic stroke with large vessel occlusion.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to explore the occurrence, identify independent predictors, and assess the clinical implications of END following EVT in individuals with acute LVO.
METHODS: Participants were enrolled from the ANGEL-ACT registry. END was characterized by a rise of ≥ 4 points in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score from baseline to 24 h post-EVT. We conducted logistic regression analyses to pinpoint independent predictors of END.
RESULTS: Among the 1557 patients included in the study, the occurrence of END stood at 9.8%. Factors independently associated with END included an admission NIHSS (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 4.067, 95% CI 2.513 to 6.582, p < 0.0001), an admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) exceeding 5 (aOR = 1.811, 95% CI 1.246 to 2.632, p = 0.0018), the use of general anesthesia (GA) (aOR = 0.474, 95% CI 0.330 to 0.682, p < 0.0001), longer procedure duration (aOR = 5.500, 95% CI 1.45 to 20.871, p = 0.0122), and more than three retrieval attempts (aOR = 1.294, 95% CI 1.177 to 1.422, p < 0.0001).
CONCLUSIONS: END manifested in 9.8% of patients undergoing endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute large vessel occlusion (LVO). This investigation highlights various independent predictors of END, providing valuable insights for daily clinical practice aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of intravascular thrombectomy.

Title: Association of NMR metabolic signatures of healthy lifestyle with hypertension: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lifestyle factors play a critical role in the prevention and management of hypertension, while metabolomics provides valuable insights into the biological mechanisms underlying disease development. However, the relationships among lifestyle-related metabolic signatures, lifestyle behaviors, and hypertension risk remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study used data from the UK Biobank. A composite healthy lifestyle score was calculated, and a lifestyle-related metabolic signature was developed using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)-based metabolomics and elastic net regression. Multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations between the healthy lifestyle score and the metabolic signature and incident hypertension. Causal mediation analysis based on a counterfactual framework (CMAverse package) was performed to quantify the mediating effect of the metabolic signature on the association between lifestyle and hypertension. Subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses were also conducted.
RESULTS: A total of 126,677 eligible participants (mean age, 54.92 ± 8.12 years; 46.47% male; 96.09% White) were included. During a median follow-up of 13.43 years, 18,720 participants developed hypertension. A healthy lifestyle-related metabolic signature comprising 76 metabolites was identified and showed a strong correlation with the healthy lifestyle score. Both a higher healthy lifestyle score (HR: 0.927; 95% CI: 0.913-0.940) and a higher metabolic signature level (HR: 0.675; 95% CI: 0.641-0.711) were independently associated with a significantly lower risk of incident hypertension, with significant inverse dose-response trends. These associations remained generally consistent across subgroups stratified by age, education, and income. Mediation analysis indicated that the metabolic signature explained 57.08% (95% CI: 31.89%-83.15%) of the protective association between a healthy lifestyle and hypertension risk. The primary findings remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: A healthy lifestyle is associated with a distinct metabolomic profile that substantially mediates its protective association with hypertension. These findings provide new insights into the metabolic mechanisms linking lifestyle behaviors to hypertension risk and highlight the importance of metabolic health in hypertension prevention.

Title: Feasibility of multidomain cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic biomarker assessment for in-hospital mortality in older heart failure inpatients: an exploratory retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) dysfunction integrates cardiac, renal, metabolic, and inflammatory risk and is particularly relevant for older patients hospitalized with heart failure. Whether standardized multidomain CKM-related biomarker assessment is feasible using real-world hospital data in older heart-failure inpatients and what limitations arise from such data remains poorly characterized.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using hospital records from Zhongnan Hospital (Jan 2022-Dec 2024). Patients with missing in-hospital outcome status were excluded. Primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Associations between age, sex, ECG major abnormality, BNP, BUN, IL-6, and mortality were evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression in complete-case patients. Nested ROC models described apparent discrimination (DeLong tests), bootstrap resampling estimated optimism-corrected discrimination, and an exploratory CKM biomarker burden analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Among 1,645 records, 1,131 patients had interpretable in-hospital outcomes (64 deaths, 1,067 survivors). A complete CKM biomarker panel (BNP, BUN, and IL-6) was available in only 186 patients (16.4%; 17 deaths, 169 survivors; median non-survivor age 82 years), who were older and had higher observed mortality than patients excluded for incomplete data. In this selected complete-case cohort, only older age (adjusted OR per year, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.04-1.16; P < 0.001) and BNP per doubling (OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.05-1.86; P = 0.021) were independently associated with mortality; sex, ECG major abnormality, BUN, and IL-6 were not. Apparent discrimination was numerically higher for the biomarker-enriched than the clinical-ECG model (AUC 0.841 vs. 0.762), but nested DeLong comparisons were not significant (P ≥ 0.060) and the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.79. Observed mortality rose across exploratory CKM-burden groups (8.3%, 12.0%, 20.0%), but these subgroups were very small. The incremental biomarker, ECG, discrimination, and CKM-burden findings remained exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected complete-case cohort of older heart-failure inpatients, age and BNP were the most consistent markers of in-hospital mortality. A complete CKM biomarker panel was available in only a minority of patients, indicating that standardized multidomain CKM-related assessment was not systematically implemented in routine care. The feasibility, incremental prognostic value, and clinical utility of broader CKM-related multidomain biomarker assessment remain unproven and require standardized prospective validation; these findings should not be interpreted as a prognostic model ready for clinical use.

Title: Long-term trends, age-period-cohort patterns, and future projections of incident stroke with comorbid hypertension and diabetes among older adults in Shenzhen, China: a population-based surveillance study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with stroke frequently have coexisting hypertension and diabetes, a high-risk cardiometabolic profile that complicates prevention, long-term management, and health service planning. However, population-based evidence on the long-term incidence trajectory of stroke occurring with both conditions remains limited, particularly in rapidly urbanizing settings undergoing population ageing. This study examined long-term trends, age-period-cohort patterns, and future projections of incident stroke with comorbid hypertension and diabetes among older adults in Shenzhen, China.
METHODS: This population-based retrospective surveillance study used data from the Shenzhen Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Disease Registry System. Incident stroke events registered between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 among adults aged ≥ 60 years were identified, and 40,128 events with comorbid hypertension and diabetes were included. Crude incidence rates (CIRs) and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs) were calculated. Joinpoint regression, age-period-cohort analysis, and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling were used to assess temporal trends, estimate age, period, and cohort effects, and project incidence trends from 2024 to 2033.
RESULTS: From 2004 to 2023, the number of incident stroke events with comorbid hypertension and diabetes increased from 314 to 3,336, and the ASIR rose from 141.12 per 100,000 in 2004 to 414.78 per 100,000 in 2023. Joinpoint regression showed overall increasing trends in CIR and ASIR across the study period, with average annual percent changes of 5.44% and 6.14%, respectively, while identifying a late-period decline after 2017. Incidence levels were generally higher in males than in females. Age-period-cohort analysis showed marked age effects, elevated period-related risks in recent periods, and increasing cohort effects across successive birth cohorts. Bayesian projections suggested that both CIR and ASIR may increase from 2024 to 2033, with larger projected increases in males.
CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults in Shenzhen, the burden of stroke with comorbid hypertension and diabetes showed a long-term upward trajectory over the study period. Model-based projections suggested that the burden may increase from 2024 to 2033, particularly among males and older age groups. These findings provide population-level descriptive and projection evidence that may inform risk stratification and health service planning for ageing urban populations.

Title: Estimated glucose disposal rate stratifies mortality risk, especially in younger adults with cardiovascular-liver-metabolic overlap.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular-liver-metabolic (CLM) overlap population faces an elevated risk of mortality, yet prognostic tools integrating dynamic insulin resistance (IR) remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) on mortality within the CLM overlap population.
METHODS: An analysis of a prospectively linked national dataset was conducted on 1,126 eligible NHANES participants (1999-2018) with concomitant cardiovascular disease (CVD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). eGDR was calculated using clinical parameters. Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and causal mediation models were employed to assess mortality associations and the mediating role of inflammation.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 85 months, 453 deaths occurred, including 155 cardiovascular deaths. Lower eGDR showed a borderline inverse association with cardiovascular mortality (HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.70-1.01, P = 0.065). eGDR exhibited a threshold-dependent non-linear association with all-cause mortality (P for non-linearity = 0.001), with lower mortality below the inflection point of 5.5901 mg/kg/min (HR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.66-0.91) and higher mortality above it (HR = 1.16, 95% CI: 0.99-1.36). The pathway from eGDR through systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) to mortality was statistically detectable for all-cause mortality (indirect effect = 6.530, 95% CI: 2.146-11.878), and SIRI mediated 11.3% of the total effect for cardiovascular mortality. Notably, the reduction in mortality risk per 1-unit increase in eGDR was significantly stronger in patients aged < 60 years (all-cause mortality HR = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.60-0.85, P = 0.003; P for interaction = 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In the CLM overlap population, eGDR demonstrates a linear association with cardiovascular mortality and a non-linear association with all-cause mortality, partially mediated by systemic inflammation. Its enhanced prognostic value in younger adults highlights its potential for early risk stratification and could inform targeted interventions focusing on IR-driven pathways.

Title: Prior CABG and native-vessel CTO PCI: lesion complexity, strategy planning, procedural burden, and technical success in a multicenter registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) has been associated with greater lesion complexity and lower success rates in chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). In native-vessel CTO PCI, prior CABG may also indicate greater preprocedural complexity and more advanced strategy planning. We examined whether prior CABG was associated with lesion complexity, strategy selection, procedural burden, and technical success in a contemporary multicenter registry.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospective multicenter CTO PCI registry including 1,800 consecutive native-vessel procedures performed between January 2020 and June 2025. Of these, 205 were performed in patients with prior CABG and 1,595 in patients without prior CABG. The primary endpoint was technical success, defined as final TIMI 3 flow with residual stenosis < 30%. The key secondary endpoint was procedural success, defined as technical success without in-hospital major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events.
RESULTS: Prior-CABG procedures had greater lesion complexity, more frequent planned retrograde/hybrid crossing, longer procedural and fluoroscopy times, higher dose-area product, and greater adjusted contrast use. Technical success was lower in prior-CABG procedures (85.9% vs. 93.3%, p < 0.001), as was procedural success (84.9% vs. 92.4%, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, prior CABG was independently associated with technical failure (adjusted OR, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.19-3.18; p = 0.008). Planned retrograde/hybrid strategy was also associated with technical failure (adjusted OR 2.82, 95% CI 1.81-4.40, p < 0.001), a finding interpreted as reflecting case selection and lesion difficulty rather than a causal effect of the strategy. In a companion model, prior CABG was independently associated with the selection of a planned retrograde/hybrid strategy (adjusted OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.40-2.96, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In native-vessel CTO PCI, prior CABG was associated with more complex lesions, more frequent retrograde/hybrid planning, greater procedural burden, and lower technical success. However, its incremental prognostic value beyond the J-CTO score was limited. Prior CABG should therefore be interpreted primarily as a marker of an unfavorable procedural phenotype rather than as a standalone risk-stratification tool.

Title: The Illusion of Recovery From Atrial Fibrillation, a Review of Postcardioversion Anticoagulation Guidelines.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia in clinical practice and an independent, well-established risk factor for ischemic stroke. However, restoring sinus rhythm via cardioversion does not eliminate this risk. Cardioversion itself transiently increases thromboembolic risk more than 10-fold, driven by atrial stunning, a state in which the left atrium and left atrial appendage remain mechanically dysfunctional despite normalized electrical activity seen on an electrocardiogram. Retrospective data show that thromboembolic events are clustered heavily within the first 2 weeks postcardioversion, supporting the near-universal recommendation of at least 4 weeks of continued therapeutic anticoagulation postcardioversion for AF duration more than 12 to 48 hours, regardless of baseline stroke risk score. Beyond this initial 4-week recommendation, the decision to continue anticoagulation is based on a comprehensive assessment of the patient's thromboembolic risk profile, rather than rhythm status or cardioversion success. Multiple trials have demonstrated a significant increase in the incidence of ischemic strokes in patients who had a premature discontinuation of anticoagulation postcardioversion. Additionally, having a prior stroke, the heaviest weighted risk-stratification variable, favors indefinite anticoagulation regardless of postcardioversion rhythm outcome. Current guidelines provide a framework for approaching postcardioversion anticoagulation, including a fixed 4-week anticoagulation course encompassing the atrial stunning period, followed by individualized risk-stratification to determine the indication for continued anticoagulation. Nevertheless, future research is still required to better elucidate whether anticoagulation can be safely discontinued after completion of the recommended 4-week postcardioversion anticoagulation course in patients with a prior AF-related stroke.

Title: Herpes Zoster and Cardiovascular Disease: An Unexpected Association.
Abstract: Herpes zoster (HZ), the reactivation of latent varicella zoster virus (VZV), is increasingly being recognized as more than a dermatologic and neurologic disease. In recent years, multiple meta-analyses have linked HZ infection to a clinically significant increase in the risk of stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and other major adverse cardiovascular events, an effect that is most pronounced in the first days to weeks following the acute HZ infection, with a gradual decrease in risk over time. The proposed mechanism centers on a productive viral infection of arterial walls, a phenomenon described as VZV vasculopathy, with transmural inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and thrombosis, all superimposed on the systemic inflammatory and prothrombotic state that accompanies the acute HZ infection. The evidence for an association between HZ infection and cardiovascular events has grown stronger with recent multiple large cohort studies demonstrating that patients who received HZ vaccination had a significantly lower rate of major adverse cardiovascular events, MI, stroke, heart failure, and arrhythmia. However, while these cohort studies have helped researchers identify the potential association of HZ vaccination and reduced cardiovascular risk, there remains a need for a randomized controlled trial to establish causality between these factors. Currently underway, a randomized controlled trial is directly evaluating whether HZ vaccination in a large population lowers the incidence of cardiovascular events, including stroke, MI, and cardiovascular death. Nevertheless, the 2026 American College of Cardiology guidelines now include a strong recommendation for HZ vaccination given the growing body of evidence regarding the association of HZ vaccination with cardiovascular events.

Title: Characteristics and Treatment Utilisation Patterns of Individuals Using Tirzepatide for Type 2 Diabetes in Germany.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study describes real-world characteristics and utilisation patterns of tirzepatide among adults with type 2 diabetes in German office-based practice.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study analysed data from the CompuGroup Medical Healthcare Database. Cohort 1 initiated tirzepatide between 1 December 2023 and 31 March 2024 and cohort 2 between 1 July and 30 September 2024. A subgroup of cohort 1 with ≥ 6 months' follow-up data and uninterrupted tirzepatide use (cohort 1a) was also analysed. Descriptive statistics summarised baseline characteristics, prior therapy, and dosing patterns.
RESULTS: Cohort 1 included 1223 individuals and cohort 2 included 2300; mean (± standard deviation) age was 59 ± 12 and 60 ± 12 years, respectively, and approximately 54% were male. Comorbidities, especially hypertension and dyslipidaemia, were frequent. Most individuals had prior insulin and/or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) treatment (cohort 1, 72.1%; cohort 2, 59.6%). A total of 458 individuals had 6 months' follow-up (cohort 1a). The most common starting dose was 2.5 mg (71.2%). Use of higher doses gradually increased over time, with 5.0 mg becoming the most prevalent; at 6 months, 35.9% of individuals received 5.0 mg and 18.6% received 10.0 mg.
CONCLUSION: This first comprehensive real-world study of tirzepatide use in Germany showed tirzepatide initiation primarily after GLP-1 RA and/or insulin therapy. Most individuals remained on 5.0 mg, with a notable proportion escalating to 10.0 mg. Cohort characteristics were generally similar to those in the SURPASS trials, supporting the relevance of trial findings to clinical practice.

Title: Choosing Cardiovascular Assessment and Risk-Prediction Tools Across the Care Pathway: A Clinician-Oriented Review.
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making accurate and efficient risk stratification essential across the care pathway. Numerous tools support emergency triage, disease assessment, procedural decision-making, long-term prevention, atrial fibrillation management, and evaluation of functional status, but no single model is applicable across all clinical settings or populations. This clinician-oriented review categorizes and critically compares commonly used cardiovascular assessment and risk-prediction tools, including History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, Troponin, Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events, and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction for emergency triage; Agatston, Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, and Synergy Between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery for anatomical and clinical assessment; European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation, Society of Thoracic Surgeons, and Revised Cardiac Risk Index, for procedural risk; and Framingham, the pooled cohort equations implemented in the Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Risk Estimator, Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2, QResearch Cardiovascular Risk Algorithm 3, and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs for long-term prediction. Congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75, diabetes, stroke/transient ischemic attack (2 points), congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 (2 points), diabetes, stroke/TIA (2 points), vascular disease, age 65-74, sex category (female), and hypertension, abnormal renal/liver function, stroke, bleeding history, labile international normalized ratio, elderly, drugs/alcohol, are discussed in the context of atrial fibrillation, alongside New York Heart Association and the Seattle Angina Questionnaire as measures of functional status and quality of life. For each tool, we examine its clinical purpose, principal variables, strengths, limitations, practical applications, and areas of overlap. Differences in implementation across healthcare systems and patient populations are considered to support context-appropriate selection. Persistent limitations include poor standardization, reliance on data that may be unavailable in resource-constrained settings, limited transportability, and incomplete integration into clinical workflows. Greater harmonization, external validation, digital automation, and the careful incorporation of biomarkers and artificial intelligence may support more accessible, dynamic, and personalized cardiovascular risk assessment.

Title: Effects of Lens Status and Prophylactic Transscleral Retinopexy on Vision Outcomes in Boston Terriers Following Phacoemulsification.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the effects of surgical lens status (pseudophakia or intentional aphakia) and prophylactic transscleral retinopexy (PTR) on postoperative ocular hypertension (POH), glaucoma, retinal detachment, and vision loss following phacoemulsification in Boston Terriers.
ANIMALS STUDIED: Thirty-seven Boston Terriers.
PROCEDURE: A retrospective single-cohort study was conducted on Boston Terriers that underwent phacoemulsification between January 1997 and June 2025, with pseudophakia or intentional aphakia. Time-to-event analyses were performed using parametric interval-censored survival models. Analyses were performed unadjusted and adjusted separately for 4 potential confounders identified using a directed acyclic graph (of which year of surgery was considered the most important).
RESULTS: POH occurred in 22/63 (35%) eyes (46% of pseudophakic and 26% of aphakic eyes), glaucoma in 21/62 (34%) eyes (52% of pseudophakic and 20% of aphakic eyes), and vision loss in 16/61 (26%) eyes (36% of pseudophakic and 18% of aphakic eyes). Only 3 cases of retinal detachment precluded further analysis. Estimated hazard ratios (pseudophakia compared to aphakia, unadjusted and adjusted for year of surgery) were, respectively, 2.0 (95% CI = 0.8 to 5.5; p = 0.157) to 2.8 (95% CI = 1.0 to 7.9; p = 0.052) for POH and 2.9 (95% CI = 0.9 to 9.2; p = 0.075) to 2.7 (95% CI = 1.0 to 7.3; p = 0.050) for glaucoma. Estimated effects of lens status on vision loss and effects of PTR on all three outcomes were imprecise and inconclusive.
CONCLUSIONS: In Boston Terrier eyes undergoing phacoemulsification, pseudophakia may result in higher risks of postoperative ocular hypertension and glaucoma compared to intentional aphakia.

Title: Artificial intelligence in myeloproliferative neoplasms: From digital bone marrow pathology to clinical decision support.
Abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders whose diagnosis, prognostication, and management depend on integrating heterogeneous clinical, morphological, and molecular data. This narrative review (PubMed/MEDLINE searched through August 2026, supplemented by hand-searching and conference abstracts) appraises the evidence for AI applications across the MPN continuum. Artificial intelligence (AI), and its principal subfields, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), learn predictive patterns directly from data rather than from explicitly programmed rules, and are increasingly suited to this multidimensional complexity. Across the MPN continuum, AI has produced substantial technical progress across several domains: automated bone marrow biopsy analysis and continuous quantification of fibrosis and megakaryocyte morphology; peripheral blood- and complete blood count-based diagnosis, including blood-based prediction of marrow fibrosis and emerging liquid-biopsy approaches; quantitative disease assessment such as spleen volume segmentation; risk stratification for survival, thrombosis, disease progression, and post-transplant outcomes; therapy response prediction; in silico drug discovery; and natural language processing for large-scale mining of electronic health records; maturity and level of validation differ markedly across these domains. External validation is increasingly reported in selected applications, though most published models to date remain confined to internal or single-cohort validation, and prospective evaluation has been reported only for blood count-based fibrosis prediction. Correspondingly, to our knowledge, no tool has yet been shown to change clinical decision-making or improve patient outcomes, and predictive performance should not be conflated with clinical utility. As multimodal data integration, foundation models, and generative approaches mature, AI has the potential to support a faster, more objective, and more personalized diagnostic and decision-making pathway in MPN.

Title: Extreme cardiovascular risk as a major barrier to LDL-C target achievement: insights from ITACARE-P registry.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Achieving low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets remains challenging in secondary cardiovascular prevention despite the availability of effective lipid-lowering therapies. The 2025 ESC/EAS dyslipidaemia guidelines introduced an "extreme cardiovascular risk" category requiring LDL-C levels <40 mg/dL, potentially increasing the difficulty of target attainment. We aimed to identify clinical and therapeutic predictors of LDL-C target achievement according to the 2025 ESC/EAS recommendations and estimate the probability of goal attainment across different risk categories and treatment strategies.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This sub-analysis of the multicentre ITACARE-P registry included 1904 outpatients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation, and stable predictors were selected through Elastic Net regularization across 20 imputed datasets. A multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects model was internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples. Overall, 38% of patients achieved guideline-recommended LDL-C targets. Independent predictors of target attainment included PCSK9 inhibitor therapy (OR = 7.65), high-intensity statins (OR = 4.73), ezetimibe (OR = 2.64), male sex (OR = 1.99), diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.99), coronary artery disease (OR = 2.73), participation in cardiac rehabilitation (OR = 1.81), and high physical activity (O = 1.54). Current smoking, prior dyslipidaemia, and longer disease duration were associated with lower odds of achievement. Very-high-risk patients were more likely to achieve LDL-C targets than extreme-risk patients (OR = 5.66). Predicted target attainment ranged from 9.8% to 88.6% according to treatment intensity and risk category. Model discrimination was good (optimism-corrected AUC = 0.782).
CONCLUSIONS: LDL-C target attainment under the 2025 ESC/EAS guidelines remains suboptimal, particularly among extreme-risk patients. Earlier therapeutic intensification and individualized lipid-lowering strategies may be necessary to improve real-world goal achievement.

Title: Association of single nucleotide polymorphisms in lipid metabolism and vascular function genes with risk of cardiovascular disease.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Atherosclerosis progressively leads to cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Genetic variants in lipid and vascular related genes can impact cardiovascular health due to altered levels or functions of resulting proteins/enzymes. Therefore, we aimed to analyze the genetic variants in such genes in a cohort of Pakistani CVD patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this case-control study, 100 CVD patients and 50 healthy controls were sampled and their biochemical parameters were analyzed. Furthermore, five SNPs including; PCSK9 rs562556(G/A), APOE rs429358(T/C), FURIN rs4702(G/A), and rs6224(G/T), and TIE2/TEK rs1322052(T/C) were genotyped using in-house developed tetra-primer ARMS-PCR assays. Data were analyzed in SPSS and R programing. Genetic analyses showed that AA genotype frequency (69% vs. 46%) for rs562556, TT (19% vs. 4%) of rs6224 and TT (72% vs. 52%) of rs429358 were significantly higher in CVD patients relative to healthy controls. Logistic regression analysis revealed significant associations for rs429358 (OR = 0.17, p = 0.014) with CVD, whereas, other polymorphisms including rs562556 (OR = 0.32, p = 0.27), rs4702 (OR = 4.04, p = 0.21), and rs6224 (OR = 0.94, p = 0.85) were not significant after adjusting for the confounding factors (i.e. age, gender, BMI and smoking). Moreover, diastolic blood pressure, uric acid and urea were significantly different between CVD patients having genotypes: TC and TT for rs429358. Similarly, albumin levels were significantly higher in TC genotype carriers for rs1322052 SNP in CVD patients (p = 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: Heterozygous genotype carriers of APOE rs429358 (TC) appeared to be protected from the development of CVD.

Title: The Role of Aeromonas Species as Enteropathogens in Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
Journal: The Korean journal of gastroenterology = Taehan Sohwagi Hakhoe chi
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Aeromonas species are Gram-negative, flagellated bacilli suggested to be associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) flare-ups, but their precise role remains controversial. This retrospective study investigated Aeromonas as an enteropathogen in patients with IBD.
METHODS: This study analyzed patients who tested positive for Aeromonas via stool multiplex PCR at Kangdong Sacred Heart Hospital between June 2023 and May 2025.
RESULTS: Among the overall IBD cohort, Aeromonas was detected in 11/94 patients (11.7%; five with ulcerative colitis and six with Crohn's disease), identifying it as the second most prevalent pathogen, closely following Clostridioides difficile (14.9%, 14/94). This positivity rate was significantly higher than the 3.6% (111/3,056) observed in patients without IBD (p<0.001). IBD patients showed significantly lower PCR cycle threshold values (34.68±4.5 vs. 39.24±4.5, p=0.004), indicating a higher abundance of genetic material.
CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, Aeromonas positivity is significantly more prevalent in IBD patients and is associated with a higher abundance of genetic material and inflammatory markers. Nevertheless, it is unclear if Aeromonas, acting as an enteropathogen, directly triggers acute flare-ups or is merely a consequence of a pre-existing compromised mucosal environment in patients with IBD.

Title: [Effect of mycophenolate mofetil on in-stent restenosis after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with autoimmune hepatitis and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease].
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the effect of mycophenolate mofetil on in-stent restenosis (ISR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease. Methods: Patients with autoimmune liver diseases (AILD) [including AIH, primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), and overlap syndrome] complicated with coronary heart disease who underwent PCI at Tianjin Medical University Second Hospital between January 2019 and December 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, they were divided into mycophenolate mofetil group and non-mycophenolate mofetil group according to postoperative use of mycophenolate mofetil, and followed up until March 31, 2026 to compare the baseline characteristics of the two groups of patients. Firth penalized likelihood-corrected Cox regression models and Fine-Gray competing risk models (with all-cause death as the competing event) were used to evaluate the association between mycophenolate mofetil use and ISR after PCI in patients with AIH and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease (because few patients with PBC and PSC received mycophenolate mofetil, this analysis only included patients with AIH and overlap syndrome). The Benjamini-Hochberg method was applied for multiple comparison correction to calculate the FDR q values. A 1∶1 propensity score matching (PSM) was employed to balance baseline characteristics between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier method was used to plot survival curves to compare the ISR-free survival rates. Sensitivity analysis was performed on all AILD patients to validate the robustness of the results. Results: A total of 172 patients with AILD complicated with coronary heart disease were enrolled, including 48 cases (27.9%) in the mycophenolate mofetil group and 124 cases (72.1%) in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The follow-up duration [M(Q1, Q3)] was 13 (7, 16) and 10 (5, 16) months respectively. The proportion of patients with hyperlipidemia [12.5% (6/48) vs 32.3% (40/124), P=0.009] and diabetes mellitus [8.3% (4/48) vs 27.4% (34/124), P=0.007] were lower in the mycophenolate mofetil group than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group, while the proportion of patients with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP)>0.8 mg/L [47.9% (23/48) vs 27.4% (34/124), P=0.010], previous use of prednisone [79.2% (38/48) vs 22.6% (28/124), P<0.001] and azathioprine [54.2% (26/48) vs 9.7% (12/124), P<0.001] were higher than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The levels of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) [59.5 (35.5, 76.8) vs 43.0 (32.0, 52.7) U/L, P=0.002] and immunoglobulin G (IgG) [19.6 (15.0, 26.0) vs 15.2 (14.0, 16.8) g/L, P=0.006] were higher in the mycophenolate mofetil group. Among 100 patients with AIH and overlap syndrome (82 and 18 cases, respectively), mycophenolate mofetil use was associated with a reduced risk of ISR in both Firth-corrected Cox regression model and competing risk model (Firth-corrected Cox model: HR=0.17, 95%CI: 0.04-0.51, FDR q=0.004; competing risk model: sHR=0.14, 95%CI: 0.05-0.43, FDR q=0.003). After PSM (40 cases in each group), there was no statistically significant difference in all covariates between the two groups (all SMD<0.1). After PSM, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that the follow-up duration was 12 (7, 15) months in the mycophenolate mofetil group and 8 (3, 17) months in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group. The 12-month ISR-free survival rate was higher in the mycophenolate mofetil group than that in the non-mycophenolate mofetil group (97.0% vs 64.5%, P<0.001). In the sensitivity analysis, mycophenolate mofetil use is associated with a reduced risk of ISR (Firth-corrected Cox regression model: HR=0.29, 95%CI: 0.09-0.73, FDR q=0.030; competing risk model: sHR=0.26, 95%CI: 0.10-0.72, FDR q=0.022). Conclusion: Mycophenolate mofetil use is associated with a reduced risk of ISR after PCI in patients with AIH and overlap syndrome complicated with coronary heart disease.

Title: [Expert consensus on practice of echocardiography in adult pulmonary hypertension (2026 edition)].
Abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a clinical syndrome characterized by elevated pulmonary arterial pressure and increased pulmonary vascular resistance, which eventually leads right failure or even death. Early screening and diagnosis are the core steps to improve prognosis, and early assessment of right heart changes is a key component of risk assessment and treatment strategies. Echocardiography has long been recommended as the first-line screening tool for PH and the most widely used non-invasive modality for right heart structure assessment. It is the most important routine examination throughout the PH disease course. However, there is no unified national standards for echocardiographic assessment of PH, resulting in vastly different results. On this basis, the Pulmonary Vascular Group of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association of Cardiology, the Chinese Society of Echocardiography and the Specialized Committee of Cardiovascular Disease Prevention and Rehabilitation of Chinese Association of Rehabilitation Medicine organized experts in relevant fields to draft Expert consensus on practice of echocardiography in adult pulmonary hypertension (2026 edition), resulting in seven recommendations. The consensus provides a step-by-step interpretation of the acquisition and assessment of essential and optional parameters, using standard images as references, with the aim of offering unified and standardized operational guidance for echocardiographers and other relevant professionals.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Consensus Statement; English Abstract

Title: Acute Profound Hypotension Following Intraoperative Plasma Transfusion-A Case Series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood transfusions can be lifesaving but carry risks of serious adverse reactions, including the less recognized hypotensive transfusion reaction, characterized by hypotension that may be difficult to distinguish from other transfusion reactions or haemorrhage-related shock. At the Karolinska University Hospital, an increased incidence of perioperative hypotensive transfusion reactions without typical allergic features has been observed during recent years. The aim of this study was to identify and describe common clinical characteristics among patients who experienced perioperative transfusion reactions.
METHODS: This case series utilized data from a local quality registry at the Karolinska University Hospital, Sweden, covering the period from June 2024 to June 2025. Data collected included patient demographics, relevant clinical parameters and summaries of each reaction. Descriptive statistics were applied to identify potential common traits.
RESULTS: Seventeen patients with perioperative transfusion reactions were included. All but one developed hypotension and in 11 cases hypotension was the sole manifestation. None of these 11 showed elevated serum tryptase levels. All patients except one received plasma via a Belmont Rapid Infuser RI-2 and seven patients also received packed red blood cells. In 11 cases, the blood pressure drop occurred immediately after plasma infusion. During this period, the Belmont Rapid Infuser was withdrawn after 7 months. No reactions were reported in the 4 months following withdrawal. However, reactions recurred following subsequent device use.
CONCLUSION: Most transfusion reactions were characterized by profound and immediate hypotension following plasma transfusion, often presenting as isolated hypotension without biochemical or clinical evidence consistent with IgE-mediated anaphylaxis. A temporal association with the use of the Belmont Rapid Infuser RI-2 was observed. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating, warranting further prospective mechanistic and safety studies.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: Hypotensive transfusion reactions are uncommon but clinically important, and may be mistaken for bleeding or anaphylaxis. This case series describes 17 perioperative cases, mainly presenting as abrupt isolated hypotension after plasma administration. The absence of device-use denominators, signs of anaphylaxis in most patients and the incomplete, delayed calcium measurements mean that other mechanisms cannot be separated from a device-related effect. The main message for practice is therefore active vigilance when using a rapid plasma infusion device.

Title: Estimated Small Dense LDL Cholesterol and Coronary Artery Disease in Familial Hypercholesterolemia.
Abstract:
AIM: Recent evidence reports good agreement between measured and estimated small-dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (EsdLDL-C) using a readily applicable formula. Its clinical utility in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) has not yet been evaluated. We aimed to evaluate the sex-specific associations of pre-treatment EsdLDL-C with coronary artery disease (CAD) prevalence in adult patients with HeFH and its discriminative value beyond LDL-C.
METHODS: Data from consecutively recruited adults with a clinical diagnosis of HeFH from an ongoing registry (HELLAS-FH, n = 3,276) were analyzed. Patient demographics, lipid parameters, CAD risk factors, and CAD prevalence at registry enrollment were evaluated. EsdLDL-C was calculated at pre-treatment (i.e., before any hypolipidemic therapy initiation) using the Sampson equation.
RESULTS: EsdLDL-C was associated with an increased prevalence of type 2 diabetes and hypertension, a higher body mass index and triglycerides, and lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. EsdLDL-C was also the strongest independent lipid-associated factor for CAD (OR: 1.24, p＜0.001). This association was more pronounced in women (OR 1.57, p＜0.001). EsdLDL-C showed higher CAD discrimination than LDL-C (AUC 0.611 vs. 0.522). Incorporating EsdLDL-C into the best discriminative model improved discriminative ability vs the core model (AUC 0.831 vs 0.828, p = 0.038) and overall model fit (ΔAIC) = -10.3). This incremental predictive value was driven predominantly by females (ΔAIC = -14.1; AUC 0.787 vs 0.769, p = 0.015).
CONCLUSION: In a large sample of patients with clinical HeFH, EsdLDL-C was incrementally associated with CAD beyond LDL-C. This finding was more pronounced in women. The clinical utility of this readily available lipid marker as a risk enhancer should therefore be further investigated.

Title: Alcohol Non-Abstinence and Hypertension as Independent Risk Factors for Esophageal Cancer Recurrence After Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol consumption is a well-established risk factor for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Recently, metabolic abnormalities have been reported as a risk factor for ESCC. However, the impact of these risk factors on recurrence after curative endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether alcohol consumption and metabolic abnormalities independently contribute to ESCC recurrence following curative ESD.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study including 147 patients with ESCC who underwent curative ESD at four institutions between 2003 and 2021. Independent predictors of recurrence were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression. Risk stratification was further explored using decision tree analysis and Kaplan-Meier curves.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 2.34 years, 31 patients (21.1%) developed recurrence of ESCC. Cox regression analysis identified alcohol non-abstinence (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.01-4.76, p = 0.0123) and hypertension (HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.01-9.23, p = 0.0327) as independent predictors of recurrence. Decision tree analysis identified alcohol non-abstinence as the strongest classifier, followed by hypertension. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that abstainers or non-drinkers with hypertension had a recurrence risk comparable to that of non-abstainers, with 3-year recurrence rates of 28.2% in non-abstainers, 23.4% in abstainers/non-drinkers with hypertension, and 0.0% in abstainers/non-drinkers without hypertension.
CONCLUSION: Alcohol non-abstinence and hypertension independently increased the risk of ESCC recurrence after curative ESD. These findings support sustained alcohol abstinence and suggest that hypertension may help identify patients who require careful post-ESD surveillance. Whether blood pressure control reduces recurrence requires prospective evaluation.

Title: Transitions in metabolically healthy obesity based on a novel definition and their association with incident cardiovascular disease: A cohort study.
Journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: A new metabolic health definition has been developed for cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk stratification. This study aimed to assess the stability of this newly defined metabolic health status and evaluate the association of its transitions with CVD risk.
METHODS: This study included 7 395 UK Biobank participants. Metabolic health was defined using the new and the Adult Treatment Panel-III (ATP-III) definition. Participants were cross-classified based on their body mass index (BMI) (normal weight, overweight/obesity) and metabolic health (healthy, unhealthy) at baseline. The transitions of metabolic health status were assessed at the first repeat assessment. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the association between metabolic health transitions and CVD risks. Extreme gradient boosting and Shapley additive explanations were used to explore predictors of metabolic transition within the metabolically healthy overweight/obesity (MHOO) population.
RESULTS: Using the new and ATP-III definition respectively, 40.9% and 23.7% of participants with MHOO transitioned to metabolically unhealthy status. Under the new definition, baseline MHOO participants who became metabolically unhealthy exhibited an elevated CVD risk (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.14-2.56), whereas maintaining metabolic health was not significantly associated with increased CVD risk, compared with normal-weight participants maintaining metabolic health. Systolic blood pressure, age, and BMI were the main predictors of metabolic transition.
CONCLUSIONS: The newly defined metabolic health yielded a higher reclassification rate over time and maintaining metabolic health was not significantly associated with increased CVD risk. These findings emphasize the importance of periodic health monitoring and preventing metabolic deterioration.

Title: External Ventricular Drainage for Refractory Intracranial Hypertension in Traumatic Brain Injury: Efficacy, Safety, and Outcomes.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: External ventricular drainage (EVD) is commonly used to manage refractory intracranial hypertension following traumatic brain injury (TBI), yet its efficacy, timing, and prognostic value remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the short-term efficacy of EVD in controlling intracranial hypertension in TBI patients.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-center study including consecutive adult patients with TBI who underwent EVD placement for refractory intracranial hypertension between 2020 and 2024. Demographic, clinical, radiological, surgical, and ICP data were collected. Trauma severity was assessed using the ISS and the SOFA score. EVD efficacy was defined as a sustained reduction in mean ICP below 20 mmHg for at least 24 hours. Functional outcome was assessed at 1 year using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS).
RESULTS: Fifty-three patients were included (51±18 years; 75% male). Median ICP significantly decreased after EVD placement (30 [25-35] vs. 15 [10-35] mmHg; p<0.01). Sustained ICP control was achieved within the first 24 hours in 25 patients (47%), whereas 28 (53%) did not reach control, including 8 patients (29%) with transient improvement. Patients with uncontrolled ICP had higher pre-EVD ICP values and greater injury severity scores. Normal basal cisterns were more frequent in the controlled group. One-year mortality was 70%, and 32% of the patients with controlled ICP had a GOS 4 at 12 months. EVD-related complications occurred in four patients (8%).
CONCLUSION: EVD significantly reduces ICP in selected TBI patients, but sustained control occurs in fewer than half of cases and appears associated with baseline injury severity. Prospective studies are needed.

Title: Same Class, Different Risk? Dapagliflozin versus Empagliflozin and Genitourinary Safety in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
Journal: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors are guideline-directed therapy for heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but comparative genitourinary safety data for dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in HFpEF-treated populations remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To compare 6-month symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI), asymptomatic bacteriuria, and other genitourinary adverse events among patients newly initiated on dapagliflozin or empagliflozin for HFpEF.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-centre comparative cohort study included 239 adults with physician-documented HFpEF retained after a requirement for at least 6 months of continuous follow-up: 113 received dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily and 126 received empagliflozin 10 mg once daily. The original outcome of any documented bacteriuria/UTI was separated into symptomatic UTI and asymptomatic bacteriuria. Risk differences and 95% confidence intervals were calculated; a multivariable logistic model of the original documented bacteriuria/UTI composite adjusted for age, sex, and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).
RESULTS: Any documented bacteriuria/UTI occurred in 21/113 (18.6%) dapagliflozin-treated participants and 25/126 (19.8%) empagliflozin-treated participants. Symptomatic UTI occurred in 4/113 (3.5%) and 5/126 (4.0%), respectively; 17/113 (15.0%) and 20/126 (15.9%) had documented asymptomatic bacteriuria. The risk difference for the composite, calculated as empagliflozin minus dapagliflozin, was 1.3 percentage points (95% CI -8.9 to 11.2). The adjusted odds ratio was 1.62 (95% CI 0.76-3.45; p = 0.208). Other genitourinary events were uncommon and estimates were imprecise.
CONCLUSIONS: No statistically detectable between-group difference was found in symptomatic UTI, asymptomatic bacteriuria, or the original composite outcome. Confidence intervals were wide and compatible with clinically meaningful differences in either direction. These exploratory findings require confirmation in prospective multicentre studies with standardized culture ascertainment and complete follow-up.

Title: Genetic Insights Into Cardiomyopathy With Restrictive Phenotype: Implications for Diagnosis and Personalized Care.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype is uncommon, genetically heterogeneous, and difficult to distinguish from advanced hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy. We aimed primarily to determine the diagnostic yield and spectrum of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants among patients with an echocardiographically defined restrictive phenotype; genotype-imaging and survival comparisons were prespecified exploratory analyses.
METHODS: We screened 568 patients with cardiomyopathy who underwent whole-exome sequencing and comprehensive echocardiography. Thirty-three met the operational definition of restrictive phenotype. Variants were classified. Genotype-imaging associations and survival were analyzed exploratorily.
RESULTS: Among the 568 patients, 33 exhibited a restrictive phenotype: 7 had restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM), 20 had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HRCM), and 6 had dilated cardiomyopathy with a restrictive phenotype (HDRCM). Variant carriers had a smaller aortic sinus diameter. In addition, MYBPC3 variant carriers had greater ventricular wall thickness and more frequent septal hypertrophy. Both the HRCM and HDRCM groups showed hypertrophic features, with interventricular septal hypertrophy occurring more frequently in the HDRCM group. The estimated 5-year survival was 54.5%, and survival did not differ significantly according to genetic-variant status.
CONCLUSIONS: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were frequent in this single-center cohort with restrictive physiology and were associated with selected imaging features. These exploratory findings support integrated genetic and echocardiographic evaluation.

Title: Cerebral Safety of Two Pulsed Field Ablation Workflows for Pulmonary Vein Isolation: Results From the Randomized TWOSOME MRI Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on silent cerebral events/lesions (SCE/SCL) following pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) are limited. This study aimed to assess the incidence of SCE/SCL using cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI) in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients undergoing PVI with two distinct PFA systems and workflows.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center TWOSOME MRI substudy, patients with paroxysmal AF were randomized 1:1 to single-shot or single-tip PFA. Single-shot PVI was performed using a pentaspline PFA catheter (single-transseptal access, PV-angiography, no 3D mapping) and single-tip PVI using a PFA generator with a focal ablation catheter (double-transseptal access, 3D mapping). A predefined consecutive cohort underwent 1.5-T cMRI 24 h after the procedure. SCE were defined as acute cMRI-detected lesions resolving on 6-week follow-up cMRI, and SCL as persistent lesions. Baseline characteristics, neurological symptoms, procedural data, and cMRI findings were assessed.
RESULTS: Fifty patients underwent cMRI (25 per group). Acute SCE were detected in 3/50 patients (6%; 95% CI 1.3-16.5), with 1/25 (4%) in the single-shot group and 2/25 (8%) in the single-tip group (p = 1.00). All SCE resolved on follow-up imaging, with no evidence of persistent SCL. One symptomatic stroke occurred in the single-shot group, unrelated to PFA, and was attributed to air embolization during transseptal puncture. No permanent neurological deficits occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cMRI study, both PFA workflows showed a low incidence of SCE without evidence of SCL or PFA-related neurological complications. Larger studies are required to compare cerebral safety profiles of PFA technologies.
