As secondary outcomes of the trial, plasma lipids and lipoprotein particle subfractions were quantified by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy assay, and coronary artery calcium score by CT imaging. Data were analysed by constrained linear mixed-effects modelling.
FINDINGS: Attrition was 74 (39%), 114 (59%), 128 (67%), 135 (70%), and 162 (84%) at 3, 6, 9, 12 and 24 months, respectively. Self-reported adherence ranged from 63 to 85% up to 12 months and 40-60% for the last 12 months. During the first 9-12 months, the LCHF group showed significantly greater reductions than the A-HCLF comparator and C-HCLF diets in very low-density lipoprotein particles (VLDLs), triacylglycerols (TAGs), remnant cholesterol, and the TAG/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) ratio, alongside increases in HDL-C, total apolipoprotein A1 (apoA1), apoA1 in large HDL particles, LDL-C (attributed to large LDL particles), and the LDL-C/apolipoprotein B ratio. At 24 months, there were still greater reductions on the LCHF compared to the A-HCLF diet for TAGs, VLDL particles, remnant cholesterol, and the TAG/HDL-C ratio, as well as a greater increase in large LDL particles.
INTERPRETATION: In adults with obesity, an LCHF diet rich in SFA markedly lowered TAG-rich remnants and raised HDL-C and apoA1 compared to higher-carbohydrate diets, while shifting LDL toward larger particles without significantly increasing apoB or small LDLs-a pattern that may indicate greater lipid turnover.
FUNDING: This work was supported by the Trond Mohn Research Foundation, Bergen (Norway), the University of Bergen (Norway), Kostfonden, Stockholm (Sweden), and the Norwegian Health Association.

Title: Risk factors associated with increased mortality in patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to diabetic foot.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetes is a public health problem that has been increasing in recent years. Infected diabetic foot is established by the presence of inflammatory response data associated with ulcers or tissue loss. Multiple risk factors are associated with diabetic foot and the need for amputation secondary to infection.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective observational cohort study conducted between 2019 and 2024. A total of 403 patients with supracondylar amputation secondary to soft tissue infection due to diabetic foot were included. Demographic, clinical, and biochemical variables were analyzed between deceased and surviving patients.
RESULTS: A total of 403 patients were included (median age: 58 years, IQR: 50-67; 72.7% male). Overall, in-hospital mortality was 13.4% (54/403), primarily driven by septic shock (44.4%) and decompensated chronic kidney disease (33.3%). Surgical reintervention was required in 11.1% of cases. In multivariable analysis, age (OR=1.06), pre-existing cardiac disease (OR=7.17), bilateral amputation (OR=4.36), Clavien-Dindo complication grade (OR=2.67), and surgical reintervention (OR=6.46) were independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality. Baseline serum albumin exerted a protective effect (OR=0.20).
CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality following supracondylar amputation for diabetic foot is independently associated with acute septic burden, admission hypoalbuminemia, cardiorenal comorbidity, and surgical reintervention, rather than long-term glycemic control. Early identification of this high-risk profile at admission is critical to prioritize prompt infection control and perioperative optimization.

Title: Association between postoperative complications and recurrence-free survival in patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2 negative breast cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined the association between 30-day postoperative complications (POC) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) among patients with hormone receptor-positive human epidermal growth factor negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer.
METHODS: Patients aged ≥ 18 years with stage I-III HR+/HER2- breast cancer were identified from the James Cancer Registry. Recurrence was defined as local, regional, or distant disease after treatment. POC included technical, infectious, respiratory, cardiovascular, and urinary complications. Multivariable regression assessed associations between time-varying postoperative complications and RFS or overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Among 3022 patients, 103 (3.4%) developed recurrent breast cancer. On univariable analysis, postoperative complications were associated with worse RFS (HR 2.20, 95% CI 1.32-3.68). After adjustment, complications were not associated with RFS (aHR 1.56, 95% CI 0.88-2.74) or OS (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.59-1.69).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with stage I-III HR+/HER2- breast cancer, 30-day postoperative complications were not associated with RFS or OS.

Title: Quantitative analysis of tissue oxygenation trajectories in DIEP flaps using near infrared spectroscopy: A retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) is an adjunct for monitoring breast free flaps. However, there is a paucity of studies using large NIRS datasets to characterize how patient-, flap-, and operative-level factors and systemic hemodynamics influence postoperative tissue oxygen saturation (StO2).
METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed early postoperative NIRS data from DIEP-based breast reconstructions, comprising >676,000 continuous StO₂ measurements from an exteriorized skin paddle (ViOptix). Trajectories were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with nonlinear time effects and fixed effects for patient-, flap-, and operative-level variables. Trajectory metrics (desaturation burden, variability, and overall slope) were calculated. A separate model examined the associations with matched vital signs.
RESULTS: Overall, 107 flaps in 65 patients (676,308 measurements) were analyzed. StO₂ followed a non-linear postoperative course, and most variance was between the patients (67.1%) rather than within flaps. Large skin paddles were the dominant flap-level predictor, with significantly higher mean StO₂ (adjusted +9.7% points, 95% CI 3.5-16.0; p=0.003, robust across estimators), whereas coupler diameter, arterial and venous anastomosis counts, and flap weight showed no association. Among the systemic factors, higher mean arterial pressure and peripheral oxygen saturation were robustly associated with higher StO₂, whereas temperature and heart rate did not survive autocorrelation correction. Bilaterally monitored flaps diverged among the patients (median 4.9 points). Trajectory metrics separated the two venous-failure flaps from normal variation, though negative slope alone was non-specific.
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative DIEP flap StO₂ reflects flap characteristics and systemic physiology; small skin paddles may mimic venous compromise. Combining trajectory features with physiologic data may improve discrimination of true vascular compromise.

Title: Mortality after ventriculoperitoneal shunting for idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus and its clinical predictors.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) often have comorbid conditions that may adversely impact survival, but long-term mortality risk in this population remains incompletely characterized.
METHODS: Patients who underwent VPS placement for iNPH at a single tertiary care center between 2017 and 2025 were identified. Comorbidities, demographic characteristics, and perioperative complications were evaluated using univariable Cox regression analyses to identify factors associated with mortality at the last follow-up. Comorbidities were quantified with the modified Frailty Index-5 (mFI-5) and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).
RESULTS: 452 patients were included (median age, 75.3 years; 61.9% male). Forty-four (9.7%) died during follow-up (median 39.1 months), with a median postoperative survival of 19.8 months and a median age at death of 78.4 years. Median mFI-5 was 1.0 and median CCI was 2.0. Baseline comorbidities in total cohort included prior myocardial infarction (MI) in 5.8% of patients, congestive heart failure (CHF) in 6.9%, cerebrovascular accident (CVA) in 14.4%, dementia in 27.1%, and functional dependence in 54.9%. At presentation, 96.0% had gait impairment, 84.5% had cognitive deficits, and 81.6% had urinary incontinence. Regarding perioperative outcomes, 57 patients (12.6%) were hospitalized more than one day and 30 (6.7%) required non-home discharge. Postoperative subdural fluid collections occurred in 13.6% of patients, while 6.9% underwent shunt revision. On multivariable Cox regression analysis, higher CCI (HR 1.27, p = 0.005) and hospitalization >1 day (HR 3.20, p = 0.001) were independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: Nontrivial rates of mortality are seen following VPS in iNPH - approximately estimated at 10% over four years in the present study. Increased mortality appears correlated with more extensive comorbidities and poorer functional status, highlighting the importance of careful patient selection in this frail population. Notably, this mortality rate closely approximates the mortality expected on an actuarial basis for an age- and sex-matched general population and is substantially lower than mortality previously reported for patients with mild cognitive impairment, suggesting that VPS may mitigate the excess mortality otherwise anticipated in this population.

Title: Monitoring the incidence of hypotension and hypoxemia as systemic secondary insults in patients with catastrophic brain injury evolving to brain death. A prospective observational pilot study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Maintenance of systemic homeostasis and prevention of secondary injury are a cornerstone of treatment in neurocritical care to prevent organ dysfunction and adverse clinical outcome. This is a pilot descriptive and hypothesis generating study aiming to measure and characterize the incidence of systemic hypotension and hypoxemia occurring during the intensive care unit (ICU) stay in patients with catastrophic brain injury potentially evolving to brain death.
METHODS: Adult patients admitted to ICU with catastrophic brain injury and Glasgow coma scale ≤5 have been enrolled. Arterial blood pressure and SpO2 were collected minute by minute from a central station connected to patients' bedside monitors.
RESULTS: We report on 24 patients recruited prospectively from the University Hospital of Messina, Italy as a part of a larger ongoing multi-centre study. Patient monitoring data ranged from 8-3000 hours (0.3-125 days). Admission diagnoses were intracerebral haemorrhage (N= 13), TBI (N=4), SAH (N=3), ischaemic stroke (N=3) and hypoxic encephalopathy (N=1). The proportion of valid monitoring time spent with secondary insults and the pressure time index (PTI) are presented and discussed. Day 3 and 4 demonstrated the largest number of secondary insults which were mainly hypotension. Patients who progressed to brain death (n = 9) or who died in ICU from cardiac complications (n = 7) exhibited a more severe and sustained hypotensive burden compared with patients alive at discharge (n = 8). This descriptive study proved useful for identifying an optimal window for tracking insults as well as piloting several key summary measures and visualisations which will be utilized in a larger multi-centre study.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with catastrophic brain injury, the incidence of hypotension remains the highest among systemic secondary insults in patients progressing to brain death and cardiac death.

Title: Timing, dose, and Behavioral engagement in perioperative Behavioral activation: a secondary analysis of predictors of improvement in a randomized clinical trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression and anxiety are associated with poor outcomes in older adults undergoing surgery. Perioperative psychological interventions may improve symptoms, but the optimal dose, timing, and therapeutic processes remain unclear.
METHODS: This secondary analysis examined the intervention arm of a randomized clinical trial. Participants were aged ≥60, scheduled for cardiac, oncologic, or orthopedic surgeries, and had clinically meaningful depression and/or anxiety symptoms on the Patient Health Questionnaire-Anxiety Depression Scale (PHQ-ADS). Analyses included participants who completed baseline and 3-month assessments. Associations between intervention components and changes in PHQ-ADS, PHQ-9 depression and GAD-7 anxiety scores were evaluated across four a priori domains: intervention dose and perioperative timing, behavioral engagement through activity plan enactment, implementation quality and target engagement through measures of activation, compassion, and surgical preparedness scores.
RESULTS: Among 138 intervention participants, greater intervention dose was associated with larger reductions in anxiety at 3 months. Pre-operative initiation was consistently associated with symptom improvement. Participants completing ≥3 pre-operative sessions had a 6.05-point greater reduction in PHQ-ADS than those completing none (p = .003). Greater mean activity-plan completion was associated with larger reductions in PHQ-ADS (b = -2.42, SE = 1.00, p = .02), PHQ-9 (b = -1.35, SE = 0.65, p = .04), and GAD-7 scores (b = -1.07, SE = 0.53, p = .05).
CONCLUSIONS: More sessions, earlier initiation, and greater behavioral engagement of patients were associated with greater reductions in depression and anxiety. Initiating behavioral activation before surgery and supporting activity-plan enactment may improve postoperative depression and anxiety symptoms for older surgical patients. Limitations include lack of random assignment to the variables studied and single-site population.

Title: Myocardial External Efficiency and Energetic Adaptation After Heart Transplantation: An Exploratory Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired myocardial energetics may contribute to graft dysfunction after heart transplantation (HTX). We aimed to characterize early posttransplant myocardial external efficiency (MEE) and its relationship with mitochondrial capacity.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 22 HTX recipients underwent [11C]acetate positron emission tomography, echocardiography, biomarker testing, and high-resolution respirometry of endomyocardial biopsies once between week 1 and 3 and at 6 mo post-HTX. Temporal changes in positron emission tomography-derived MEE, cardiac output, and myocardial oxygen consumption were evaluated within patients and compared with those of 20 control participants. Mitochondrial capacity was assessed only in HTX recipients.
RESULTS: MEE increased from 18 ± 5% to 21 ± 5% at 6 mo post-HTX (P = 0.003) but remained lower than in control participants (26 ± 6%, P < 0.0001). Cardiac output, myocardial oxygen consumption, and mitochondrial oxidative capacity did not change significantly over time. At 6 mo, both MEE and mitochondrial oxidative capacity correlated with left-ventricular global longitudinal strain (r = -0.49, P = 0.002; r = -0.58, P = 0.010, respectively). Furthermore, MEE was inversely associated with troponin I (r = -0.49, P = 0.030) and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (r = -0.35, P = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: MEE improved significantly from 1-3 wk to 6 mo after HTX. Both MEE and mitochondrial respiratory function were associated with left-ventricular contractile performance. Overall, these findings suggest alterations in myocardial energetics during early graft recovery and support a link between oxidative metabolism and graft performance.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.
STUDY SELECTION: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).
RESULTS: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

Title: Risk factors and long-term prognosis of catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in neonatal foals.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombophlebitis is a possible complication of the use of indwelling catheters in hospitalized neonatal foals. Limited data are available concerning associated risk factors, and long-term prognosis regarding vein patency is currently unknown.
HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: Identify risk factors for catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in neonatal foals and assess long-term prognosis in a small subset.
ANIMALS: Two hundred twenty-three foals < 31 days of age, hospitalized in Utrecht University Equine Hospital between 2019 and 2024.
METHODS: Retrospective review of medical records. Foals that received an indwelling intravenous catheter and lived for at least two subsequent days were included. Odds ratios were determined, using logistic regression, for factors potentially associated with thrombophlebitis. Owners of affected horses were contacted, and horses available for follow-up were visited for clinical evaluation.
RESULTS: Twenty-one foals (9.4%) developed catheter-associated thrombophlebitis. In a multivariable model, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU, OR 5.2, 95%CI 1.5-19.7), diarrhea (OR 4.6, 95%CI 1.4-17.3), Friesian breed (OR 4.1, 95%CI 1.1-13.9) and dwell time over four days (OR 3.9, 95%CI 1.3-14.8) were significantly associated with thrombophlebitis development. Seventeen affected foals survived to discharge. Eight horses, aged five months to five years, were available for follow-up by clinical evaluation and demonstrated appropriate blood flow.
CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: Risk factors for developing catheter-associated thrombophlebitis in hospitalized neonatal foals were identified. This knowledge can aid in implementation of preventive measures.

Title: Aerobic physical activity is associated with lower pneumonia and COVID-19 mortality in adults with cognitive impairment.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease and pneumonia are major causes of death in dementia, but cause-specific mortality has rarely been examined in clinically confirmed cognitive-impairment cohorts. In this nationwide retrospective cohort study, 116,563 individuals with clinically confirmed mild cognitive impairment or dementia in the Korean Dementia Relief Center registry (2016-2021) were linked to health screening and death registry data. Aerobic physical activity (APA) was quantified in metabolic-equivalent minutes per week (MET·min/week). Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and subdistribution HRs (sHRs). The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate (FDR) across 18 cause-specific comparisons. During 400,500 person-years of follow-up (mean, 3.4 years), 5022 participants (4.31%) died. Compared with inactivity, low, moderate, and high APA were associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR [95% CI], 0.728 [0.652-0.813], 0.704 [0.636-0.781], and 0.636 [0.590-0.687], respectively). High APA was associated with lower pneumonia mortality (sHR, 0.554; 95% CI, 0.437-0.702) and COVID-19 mortality (sHR, 0.520; 0.368-0.735). These point estimates were numerically lower than for ischemic heart disease and cerebrovascular disease (sHRs, 0.613 and 0.630). Pneumonia mortality was lower across all APA levels after FDR control (q ≤ 0.023). The E-value for the high APA-pneumonia association was 3.01. APA was associated with lower mortality even at modest activity levels, especially for pneumonia deaths. Achievable activity goals may therefore merit prospective evaluation as part of supportive care for adults with cognitive impairment. Because APA may also indicate preserved physiological reserve, these findings do not establish causality and require confirmation using repeated, objective activity measurements.

Title: A reference-based approach using whole-brain segmentation for estimating blood activity concentration in CBV quantification.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived and reference-based input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C15O PET images.
METHODS: Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44). In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling.
RESULTS: The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between reference-based and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, -1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were -0.60 ± 8.8%, -1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The reference-based blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.

Title: Changes in management of FETO-treated infants with severe CDH.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to evaluate changes in outcomes and management of infants with severe congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) undergoing fetoscopic endoluminal tracheal occlusion (FETO) across two eras, and to compare outcomes by side of defect over the last decade. Retrospective review of liveborn infants with severe CDH (observed to expected lung to head ratio [O/E LHR] < 0.25 left-sided; < 0.45 right-sided) who underwent FETO at King's College Hospital, London, UK, and survived to delivery. Fifty-eight infants were included across two 5-year periods (2002-2007 and 2020-2025). Survival improved from 44.1% to 70.8% (p = 0.044). Right-sided defects were more common in the second epoch (9% versus 54%, p < 0.001). All infants in the second era had echocardiography-guided inotropic and ventilatory management, which was not universally available earlier. In the second epoch surgical repair occurred later (4.0 versus 6.5 days, p = 0.018), repair by two-stage abdominal closure (laparostomy) increased from 0% to 77.8% (p < 0.001) and recurrence fell from 33 to 0% (p = 0.042). Mechanical ventilation, oxygen therapy and admission were longer latterly. In thirty-one infants delivered between 2015 and 2025, preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurred in 67% of left-versus 92% of right-sided CDH, but at an earlier gestational age in left (p = 0.032). Left CDH infants had longer duration of mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and hospital stay (p = 0.006) with no mortality difference (exploratory).
CONCLUSION: Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH infants improved from 44 to 71% alongside later repair, staged abdominal closure and echocardiography-guided management. Left-sided defects had greater respiratory morbidity and longer admission than right-sided defects without changing survival.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • FETO improves survival in severe left-sided CDH, but postnatal management has changed substantially since its introduction.
WHAT IS NEW: • Survival of FETO-treated severe CDH rose from 44 to 71% over two decades despite more right-sided defects. Repair occurred later, following haemodynamic and respiratory stabilisation (as guided by echocardiography) with staged abdominal closure in 77.8% of recent repairs; recurrence decreased from 33 to 0%. • Left-sided CDH infants had greater respiratory morbidity and length of stay than right-sided CDH infants, without a significant difference in mortality.

Title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of an mHealth intervention to improve hypertension control in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of a mobile health technology (mHealth) based care model to facilitate home blood pressure (BP) monitoring and remote hypertension management.
METHODS: We used a Markov microsimulation model to study health and cost outcomes for three hypertension control strategies: an mHealth-based care model (mGlide) vs. Enhanced Usual Care (EUC) vs. No-Intervention. We sampled patient characteristics from the mGlide randomized controlled trial (RCT) and randomly transitioned patients through three possible health states over a 10-year horizon with monthly cycles: 1) No Cardiovascular Event, 2) Cardiovascular Event, and 3) Deceased. We determined transition probabilities from literature, allowing the probabilities to vary by patient characteristics, including BP values. We evaluated health and cost outcomes across a range of plausible deterministic treatment effects (expected BP reductions) supported by the RCT. We performed probabilistic sensitivity analysis to assess cost-effectiveness while randomly varying the treatment effect magnitude.
RESULTS: The mHealth-based care model was cost-effective compared to No-Intervention and EUC across all deterministic scenarios. 10-year mortality absolute risk reductions ranged from 4.9-5.8% (vs No-Intervention) and 0.6-3.3% (vs EUC) across scenarios. In probabilistic sensitivity analysis, mHealth-based care (vs EUC) was less costly in 59.6% of iterations and had better health outcomes in 99.6%. Comparing all care models, mHealth-based care had the greatest net monetary benefit in 95% of iterations at $26,000/QALY and in 99% of iterations at $72,000/QALY.
CONCLUSIONS: In the current study, we estimated that mHealth-based care models can be cost-effective approaches to improve hypertension control in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk.

Title: Anatomical and clinical characteristics of pediatric endoscopic third ventriculostomy performed with a small-diameter neuroendoscope.
Journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) is an established treatment for selected pediatric patients with obstructive hydrocephalus. Although the foramen of Monro constitutes the principal anatomical corridor to the third ventricle, its preoperative radiological characterization has been scarcely investigated. This study aimed to describe the radiological characteristics of the foramen of Monro in a consecutive pediatric ETV cohort treated with a small-diameter rigid neuroendoscope and to explore its relationship with ventricular morphology and clinical outcome.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was performed including the complete consecutive series of 17 pediatric patients who underwent ETV at our institution between March 2022 and November 2024. All procedures were performed using the PaediScope® neuroendoscope. The radiological diameter of the right foramen of Monro was measured on axial T2-weighted MRI together with the Evans Index and third ventricular diameter. Clinical, radiological, and operative variables were retrospectively collected. Correlations between radiological parameters and clinical outcome were analyzed using non-parametric statistical methods.
RESULTS: The mean radiological diameter of the right foramen of Monro was 2.79 ± 0.81 mm. Moderate positive correlations were observed between the foramen of Monro diameter and the preoperative Evans Index (ρ = 0.588, p = 0.013), preoperative third ventricular diameter (ρ = 0.606, p = 0.010), and postoperative third ventricular diameter (ρ = 0.568, p = 0.017). No significant association was found between the radiological diameter of the foramen of Monro and the subsequent requirement for definitive ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement or postoperative ventricular reduction. Three patients (17.6%) required definitive ventriculoperitoneal shunting during the available clinical follow-up. These patients had significantly lower Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy Success Scores than patients who maintained ETV function (p = 0.016). Intraoperative visualization was good in 16/17 procedures and moderate in one, and no major intraoperative complications were recorded.
CONCLUSIONS: The radiological measurement of the foramen of Monro correlated with ventricular morphology but was not associated with clinical outcome after pediatric ETV. Rather than representing the true anatomical diameter of the surgical corridor, this measurement should be interpreted as a standardized radiological descriptor of ventricular anatomy. The small diameter neuroendoscope was technically applicable across the range of ventricular anatomy represented in this complete consecutive cohort, although the absence of a comparator precludes conclusions regarding device-specific benefit. The study demonstrates the feasibility of obtaining this measurement from routine preoperative MRI and provides preliminary anatomical data that may support future prospective studies evaluating technical planning for pediatric ventricular endoscopy.

Title: Prospective evaluation of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation for refractory ventricular tachycardia: initial clinical experience in Japan.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This prospective study evaluated the 1 year safety and efficacy of stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) delivered using the CyberKnife system for refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) in Japanese patients, in accordance with a prespecified clinical protocol.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three male patients with radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA)-refractory VT and structural heart disease, namely hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), and ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM), were enrolled. A single fraction of 25 Gy was delivered to the target volume defined by multimodal image fusion. The primary endpoint was the absence of Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events within 12 months.
RESULTS: The primary endpoint was achieved, with no acute or subacute Grade ≥ 3 toxicities observed in any patient during the first year. Although all patients experienced a reduction in VT burden, the clinical course differed by etiology. Cases 2 (DCM) and 3 (ICM) showed typical responses, including delayed efficacy and late recurrence requiring repeat RFCA. In contrast, Case 1 (HCM), with a substantially larger target volume (133 mL), showed a rapid response but a progressive decline in left ventricular ejection fraction by myocardial scintigraphy, from 59.7% to 40.0%, during the 24 month extended follow-up.
CONCLUSION: STAR demonstrated preliminary feasibility as a noninvasive salvage therapy for refractory VT in this initial Japanese pilot experience. However, the late functional decline observed in Case 1 highlights the need for long-term follow-up and myocardium-sparing techniques for large target volumes. (jRCTs042230030).

Title: Trunk Acceleration and Lower-limb Kinematics after Cerebellar Stroke: Associations with Walking Speed and Clinical Ataxia Severity.
Abstract: The relationship between gait characteristics and clinical ataxia severity, after accounting for walking speed, remains insufficiently characterized following cerebellar stroke. We examined direction-specific trunk acceleration and lower-limb kinematics during comfortable walking. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 55 patients with subacute cerebellar stroke and 56 healthy controls. Inertial measurements quantified lower-limb kinematics, trunk acceleration root mean square (RMS; without speed normalization), and sample entropy (SampEn). Analyses included group-by-speed models, speed-matched one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping, and exploratory patient-only, speed-adjusted regressions and partial Spearman correlations with the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA). Patients walked more slowly, with lower anteroposterior and mediolateral RMS but higher anteroposterior and vertical SampEn. After speed adjustment, each five-point higher SARA score was associated with smaller peak limb flexion (- 1.01°; 95% confidence interval, - 1.99 to - 0.02) and less-negative extension (+ 1.21°; 0.08 to 2.34), both with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P = 0.045. None of the six full-cohort group-by-speed interactions met the adjusted significance criterion. In speed-matched comparisons (11 per group), significant waveform differences were confined to limb angles near the beginning and end of the gait cycle. In speed-adjusted rank analyses, vertical RMS correlated with SARA (partial ρ = 0.471) and limb angles, but the original-scale linear SARA coefficient remained uncertain. Vertical SampEn showed no clear association with SARA or limb kinematics. Higher ataxia severity was associated with smaller whole-limb excursions in speed-adjusted models. These exploratory findings support interpreting trunk acceleration magnitude and regularity alongside whole-limb movement and clinical severity.

Title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated cardiotoxicity: incidence, diagnosis, and management.
Journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized cancer therapy but are associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including cardiotoxicity. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the incidence, mechanisms, diagnosis, and management of ICI-associated cardiotoxicity, highlighting emerging biomarkers, diagnostic algorithms, and risk stratification strategies.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of the literature, synthesizing findings from recent clinical studies, guidelines, and case reports concerning ICI-associated cardiovascular complications such as myocarditis, pericarditis, and arrhythmias. As a narrative rather than systematic review, studies were selected to illustrate current concepts and were not appraised against predefined eligibility criteria.
KEY FINDINGS: ICIs are associated with a low overall incidence of cardiovascular toxicities; however, myocarditis remains the most severe and potentially life-threatening manifestation. Reported case-fatality estimates vary widely, and the highest figures derive largely from early case series and pharmacovigilance data. Emerging biomarkers, evolving risk stratification tools, and updated diagnostic and management frameworks may improve early recognition, guide timely intervention, and support multidisciplinary care for patients with suspected ICI-associated cardiotoxicity, although most supporting evidence remains retrospective.
CONCLUSIONS: Early recognition and prompt management of ICI-associated cardiotoxicities are essential for improving patient outcomes. This review provides oncologists and cardiologists with updated diagnostic approaches, treatment frameworks, and practical considerations for monitoring at-risk patients, while acknowledging that current recommendations rest largely on low-certainty evidence.

Title: Baseline OCT-features predicting retinal atrophy in optic disc swelling.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers at initial presentation of optic disc swelling (ODS) in predicting retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell layer (GCL) atrophy using volumetric macular and optic nerve head (ONH) analysis.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, patients with first-episode ODS and 6- and 12-month follow-up were included. Spectral-domain OCT (SD-OCT) volumetric scans of the macula and ONH were analysed using an AI-based platform (Discovery). Macular RNFL, ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCL + IPL), and ONH RNFL volumes were quantified across ETDRS grid fields. Longitudinal change was modelled with linear mixed-effects models; predictors of 12-month outcomes were identified by multiple linear regression.
RESULTS: Fifty-two eyes from 32 patients (mean age 39 ± 13.8 years) were analysed across papilloedema (n = 24), uveitic disc oedema (n = 22), ischaemic (n = 4), and infiltrative (n = 2) aetiologies. At baseline, uveitic disc oedema eyes showed significantly higher macular RNFL and GCL + IPL volumes than papilloedema, while ONH RNFL was similarly elevated. All OCT parameters declined significantly over 12months, with greater macular loss in uveitic disc oedema cases (p < 0.001). GCL + IPL reduction was more pronounced in the uveitic disc oedema group (- 296 ± 241 nL vs. - 110 ± 160 nL) and persisted beyond 6 months only in this group (p = 0.012). Baseline GCL + IPL volume strongly predicted 12-month GCL + IPL volume loss (β = 0.91, p < 0.001), and worse baseline visual acuity independently predicted more severe GCL + IPL volume loss (β=-317, p = 0.002). ONH RNFL did not predict visual outcomes.
CONCLUSION: ODS is associated with measurable structural change over 12 months. Baseline macular OCT biomarkers, particularly GCL + IPL, predicted 12-month outcomes largely independent of aetiology, and macular OCT may aid risk stratification alongside aetiological diagnosis.

Title: Choroidal structural changes following intravitreal injection of faricimab or aflibercept 8 mg in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare choroidal structural changes following the initial three injections of faricimab or high-dose (8 mg) aflibercept in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 38 eyes (comprising both treatment-naïve and switch cases) that received three consecutive intravitreal injections of either faricimab (n = 24) or aflibercept 8 mg (n = 14). Subfoveal choroidal area was manually segmented on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography and binarized using Niblack's method. The evaluated parameters were central choroidal thickness (CCT) and the luminal-to-choroidal area ratio (L/C ratio).
RESULTS: CCT significantly decreased in the aflibercept 8 mg group (P < 0.001), whereas the faricimab group showed no significant post-hoc pairwise differences. Conversely, faricimab was associated with a significant longitudinal reduction in the L/C ratio (P = 0.0011), which was evident after both the first (P = 0.022) and third injections (P = 0.0013). In contrast, the aflibercept 8 mg group showed no significant changes in the L/C ratio (P = 0.53). Consequently, changes in the L/C ratio after the third injection were significantly greater in the faricimab group than in the aflibercept 8 mg group (-1.6% vs. 0.4%, P = 0.016).
CONCLUSIONS: Aflibercept 8 mg was associated with reduced overall choroidal thickness, whereas faricimab was associated with reduced luminal choroidal proportion. These findings may indicate differences in choroidal structural changes between the two agents during the first three injections, although further studies with larger sample sizes are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Sex differences in the association of late-life blood pressure decline with postmortem brain vessel pathology.
Abstract: Although hypertension is the leading modifiable risk factor for cerebrovascular disease, less is known about the relation of late-life change in blood pressure (BP) and cerebrovascular pathology beyond brain infarcts. Our previous work found sex-specific associations between declining systolic BP (SBP) and cognitive decline in late-life, suggesting that cerebrovascular pathology may be an upstream contributor to these sex differences. However, postmortem studies have not examined whether BP change differentially relates to vascular brain pathology in men and women, despite well-established sex differences in BP trajectories and cerebrovascular pathology. We examined associations between change in late-life BP and postmortem cerebrovascular (arteriolosclerosis, atherosclerosis, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy) pathology from 2033 community-dwelling older adults (mean baseline age = 79.7 [SD = 7.1] years; 69% women) from four longitudinal cohort studies with brain autopsy (mean age-at-death = 89.8 [6.6] years). Person-specific late-life BP slopes estimated from annual clinical evaluations over an average of 9.1 [5.7] years were entered in ordinal regressions adjusted for age-at-death, sex, antihypertensive medication use, and BP slope × sex, age-at-death × sex, and BP slope × age-at-death interactions. Faster SBP decline was associated with greater severity of arteriolosclerosis (OR = 1.24, 95%CI 1.08-1.42) and atherosclerosis (OR = 1.41, 95%CI 1.22-1.63). A sex × SBP slope interaction (p = 0.01) revealed a stronger association of SBP decline with arteriolosclerosis severity in women than men. This longitudinal, clinical-pathologic study of older decedents showed sex differences in the association of declining SBP in late-life with severity of arteriolosclerosis, extending prior associations with cognitive decline to cerebrovascular pathology, and suggests potential for longitudinal BP monitoring for precision medicine approaches in cerebrovascular disease risk stratification.

Title: Long-term cost-effectiveness of CKD screening in middle-aged adults.
Journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common in Finland and frequently remains undiagnosed until advanced stages. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) slow CKD progression and reduce cardio-renal events when used in addition to Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System inhibitor (RAASi) treatment. We hypothesized that a one-time CKD screening program using measurements of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for identified CKD, would be cost-effective in Finland.
METHODS: We developed a cohort-based Markov model to simulate lifetime CKD progression in a Finnish cohort aged 55 years under two strategies: (1) current practice (no screening) and (2) one-time screening with follow-up and SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for screen-positive CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² and/or UACR ≥3 mg/mmol; confirmed on a repeat sample after ≥ 3 months to establish chronicity). All CKD stages (G1-G5, dialysis, transplant, and death) were included in the model, and screening could detect CKD at any stage, although the incremental detection was concentrated in earlier, previously undiagnosed stages (G1-G3). Outcomes included discounted costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), life years, and clinical outcomes (acute kidney function decline, heart-failure hospital days, dialysis and transplant patient-years, and deaths). Results are reported as means with 95% confidence intervals (CI).
RESULTS: Screening increased discounted lifetime costs per person by €907 (95% CI €334-2 553) and QALYs by 0.14 (95% CI 0.07-0.31), yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €6 478/QALY. Screening increased life years by 0.30. Screening reduced acute kidney function decline (0.88 vs 0.90 events/person), heart-failure hospital days (6.47 vs 6.69 days/person), dialysis exposure (0.29 vs 0.32 patient-years/person) and transplant exposure (0.13 vs 0.14 patient-years/person).
CONCLUSIONS: In Finns aged 55 years, one-time CKD screening with eGFR/UACR followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment improves long-term outcomes and is likely cost-effective.

Title: Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy.
RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016).
CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

Title: Minimally invasive anaortic quadruple and quintuple coronary artery bypass grafting: Feasibility and early outcomes of automated titanium suture fastener - a case series.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo describe the feasibility and early outcomes of automated terminal suture fastening and conventional hand tying during complex anaortic total-arterial minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG).MethodsThis retrospective, descriptive, single-center surgical case series included 12 patients who underwent elective anaortic off-pump MICS-CABG between January 2024 and May 2025. The first seven patients underwent conventional hand-tied terminal suture securing, whereas the subsequent five underwent automated terminal suture fastening, reflecting the chronological introduction of the device later in the surgeon's experience. Nine patients underwent quadruple and three underwent quintuple bypass grafting. Clinical follow-up was performed at 30 days and six months after surgery, with CT coronary angiography performed at six months.ResultsAll patients were male, with a mean age of 69.4 ± 7.5 years. Mean operating-room time was 373.0 ± 60.1 minutes overall, 384.3 ± 50.0 minutes in the hand-tied group, and 358.0 ± 75.6 minutes in the automated fastener group. No device-related technical failures, incomplete deployments, or device-related anastomotic revisions occurred. No deaths, perioperative myocardial infarctions, strokes, conversions to sternotomy or cardiopulmonary bypass, or repeat revascularizations occurred. Two patients developed pleural effusion, one developed atrial fibrillation, and one patient with pleural effusion required rehospitalization. At six-month CT angiography, all 30 arterial grafts were evaluable; 28 were classified as FitzGibbon grade A, one as grade B, and one as grade O. Both non-grade-A findings occurred in the hand-tied group, whereas all 13 grafts in the automated fastener group were grade A.ConclusionsIn this selected 12-patient, single-surgeon case series, automated terminal suture fastening using COR-KNOT® MICRO was technically achievable during complex anaortic total-arterial MICS-CABG without observed device-related failure. The small sample, chronological device introduction, operator learning curve, and short follow-up preclude conclusions regarding comparative operating-room time, safety, or graft outcomes. Larger prospective studies with anastomosis-specific timing and graft-level follow-up are required.

Title: A retrospective analysis of health care utilization and costs by body mass index category among adults with, or at risk of, cardiovascular disease.
Journal: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a need for more real-world evidence to better understand the long-term effect of excess weight on health care resource utilization (HCRU) and costs over time among people at risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (primary prevention population) and those with established ASCVD (secondary prevention population).
OBJECTIVE: To describe all-cause HCRU and costs during a 5-year follow-up period, stratified by body mass index (BMI) category among commercially insured US adults at risk of or with known ASCVD in both primary and secondary prevention populations.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Optum administrative claims and electronic health record (EHR) data from January 1, 2007, to December 31, 2023 (study period). Included adult patients had at least 1 BMI measure in the identification period (January 1, 2008, through December 31, 2018), with the date of the first BMI measure being the index date. Patients had to have continuous health plan enrollment on a commercial insurance plan and EHR clinical activity for 12 months before index (baseline period) and 5 years after index (follow-up period). Patients were assigned to the primary prevention cohort if there was evidence of ASCVD risk factors, and patients with evidence of ASCVD conditions were assigned to the secondary prevention cohort. Cohort-specific results were reported by BMI category. The outcomes of interest were all-cause HCRU and costs. Descriptive results were reported, and adjusted cost ratios were calculated using multivariable modeling with repeated measures.
RESULTS: A total of 26,430 patients were included in the primary prevention cohort (37.9% female, 73.5% non-Hispanic White, and mean [SD] age = 53.9 [9.0] years), and 9,020 patients were included in the secondary prevention cohort (28.9% female, 73.9% non-Hispanic White, and mean [SD] age = 56.1 [9.8] years). Numerically, unadjusted total all-cause HCRU and costs increased with higher BMI classes; this was consistent across years of follow-up. In both the primary and secondary prevention cohorts, total costs among people with obesity ranged from 1.1-fold (class 1, ≥30 to <35 kg/m2) to 1.3-fold (class 3, ≥40 kg/m2) higher than those of people with normal weight after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: This real-world study highlights the increasing economic impact of obesity in commercially insured people with or at risk of ASCVD. Future research is warranted to examine weight management strategies as an integral part of the primary and secondary prevention of ASCVD.

Title: Age, Gender, and Adherence in Low-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Reduction with Statin Therapy: A Real-world Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend achieving ≥50% reduction in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in high-risk patients. Real-world data on response patterns, age and gender differences, and determinants of nonresponse remain limited. The aim of the study is to evaluate LDL-C reduction following statin therapy in routine clinical practice and to examine the influence of age, gender, and medication adherence on treatment response and cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: In this observational cohort study, adults initiated on statin therapy with documented baseline and follow-up lipid measurements were included. LDL-C levels were recorded at baseline and follow-up. The primary outcome was achievement of ≥50% LDL-C reduction.
RESULTS: In a total study population of 652 patients, statin therapy was associated with substantial early reductions in LDL-C that were largely maintained at 1 year. More than half of the patients achieved a ≥50% reduction, and nearly one-third achieved LDL-C levels <55 mg/dL. Patients >45 years demonstrated greater sustained LDL-C reduction compared with younger individuals. Numerical differences in LDL-C response were observed between men and women, although these were not statistically significant. Failure to achieve ≥50% LDL-C reduction appeared to be more closely associated with lower medication adherence rather than treatment intensity within this uniformly treated cohort. Greater proportional LDL-C reduction was associated with lower cardiovascular event rates during follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: In routine practice, approximately half of patients achieved ≥50% LDL-C reduction with high-intensity statin therapy. Adherence emerges as an important determinant of response. Age was associated with sustained response, whereas gender differences were not statistically significant. Nonresponse is primarily associated with modifiable treatment-related factors.

Title: Statin Utilization in High-risk Hypertensive Nigerians.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Individuals with high cardiovascular (CV) risk face major adverse CV events without statin use. However, the study of statin use among these populations in Nigeria remains limited. We examined statin use in high-risk hypertensives.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the data from 1040 patients in the Federal Medical Center Abuja Hypertension registry, recruited between 2016 and 2021. Statin use was examined among patients classified as high risk by the World Health Organization/International Society of Hypertension (WHO/ISH), the Predicting the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations, and the pooled cohort equation (PCE) scores.
RESULTS: The mean age of high-risk patients was 62.7 ± 9.3 years using the WHO/ISH model, with no difference between males and females. The prevalence rate of dyslipidemia of the total cohort was 70.7% (735), while the prevalence of statin use was 61.9% (78), 50.0% (119), and 43.3% (345) using the 10-year CV WHO/ISH, PREVENT, and PCE risk scores, respectively. Furthermore, the proportions of those with high 10-year CV risk were 12.1% (126), 22.9% (238), and 76.6% (797) for the WHO/ISH, PREVENT, and PCE risk scores, respectively. Adjusted multivariable logistic regression showed that increasing age (odds ratio [OR] =1.03 [confidence interval (CI): 1.01-1.05]), diabetes mellitus (OR = 2.45 [CI: 1.69-3.55]), and increased total (OR = 1.90 [CI 1.38-2.60]) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR = 1.83 [CI 1.32-2.52]) (P < 0.05) were the factors associated with statin use.
CONCLUSION: Our study revealed suboptimal statin utilization and significant CV risk scores disparities in identifying high-risk hypertensive patients. Co-ordinated efforts are crucial for enhancing statin use and developing locally validated CV risk prediction tools.

Title: Prenatal ambient ozone exposure and risk of offspring congenital heart disease: A three-level meta-analysis.
Journal: Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association (1995)
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal exposure to ambient ozone has been hypothesized to increase the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring; however, epidemiological evidence remains inconclusive.
OBJECTIVE: To quantitatively synthesize the available evidence on the association between prenatal ambient ozone exposure and the risk of congenital heart defects (CHD) in offspring, and to explore potential effect modifiers through subgroup analyses and meta regression.
METHODS: The PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase and CNKI databases were systemically searched from from 1970 until April 2026 to find articles related to offspring CHD and periconceptional ozone exposure. Inverse variance weighted random-effects multilevel models were conducted to pool estimates and stratify associations by heart defect type, country income level, study design, investigation time period, and data source. Dose-response relationships were examined via meta-regression and the heterogeneity and publication bias in relevant studies was also examined.
RESULTS: A total of 29 studies comprising 302 effect estimates were identified. The overall pooled odds ratio for the association between prenatal ozone exposure and CHD was 1.032 (95% CI: 1.004-1.060). Stronger associations were observed for transposition of the great arteries (OR =1.172), conotruncal defects (OR =1.134), and atrioventricular septal defects (OR =1.204). The embryonic period was the most susceptible exposure window (OR =1.064, 95% CI: 1.006-1.126). Stronger effects were found in upper-middle-income countries (OR =1.039), studies conducted after 2020 (OR =1.145), and hospital-based data (OR =1.112). Dose-response analysis suggested a 1% odds increase per 10 μg/m3 ozone increment, though not statistically significant. Considerable heterogeneity was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis suggests that prenatal ozone exposure may modestly increase CHD risk. The substantial heterogeneity highlights the need for standardized exposure assessment and further prospective studies.Implication Statement: This meta-analysis provides quantitative evidence that prenatal ozone exposure is associated with a modest increase in congenital heart defect risk, with stronger effects observed in upper-middle-income countries and more recent studies. The embryonic developmental window emerged as the most susceptible exposure period. These findings inform air quality management by identifying specific exposure windows and vulnerable populations for targeted intervention, and support the refinement of WHO ozone guidelines and national ambient air quality standards to better protect fetal health.

Title: Gender Differences in Ischemic and Hemorrhagic Stroke Patients: Data from Ludhiana Population-Based Urban Stroke Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke affects older women and is associated with greater severity in women than in men. Stroke characteristics differ between high- and low-and-middle-income countries. Hence, the aim of this study was to explore if these gender differences hold true for Ludhiana population-based stroke registry.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was a part of the Ludhiana Urban population-based Stroke Registry. Data were collected using the WHO STEPS method. All patients aged ≥18 years of age, who developed stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) between March 26, 2011 and March 25, 2013, were included. Data on demographic details, clinical features, and risk factors were collected. Outcome was assessed at 28 days using the modified Rankin Scale. The statistical analyses performed included descriptive statistics, Chi square test, Fischer's exact test, and the independent t -test.
RESULTS: A total of 2948 were included in the final analysis, of whom 1811 (61.4%) were men. Women were older (≥75 years) [283 (16%) vs. 234 (21%), P = 0.001], were more illiterate [132 (13%) vs. 195 (32%), P < 0.0001], and had more ischemic strokes [1134 (68%) vs. 756 (73%), P < 0.01], hypertension [907 (79%) vs. 599 (84%), P = 0.003], hyperlipidemia [194 (17%) vs. 153 (23%), P = 0.008], and rheumatic heart disease (RHD) [26 (2%) vs. 32 (5%), P = 0.005].
CONCLUSION: Stroke was more common among men. However, gender differences were noted. Women were older and had a higher incidence of ischemic stroke, hypertension, RHD, and hyperlipidemia. Both men and women had comparable short-term outcomes.

Title: Different Patterns of Progression in Nonproliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: Findings From a 10-Year Cohort Study.
Abstract: Characterization of the 10-year progression of diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetes was sought. We evaluated whether noninvasive optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) can identify eyes that progress and may develop vision loss. Of 222 participants, 62% completed the study, with 115 reaching the 10-year visit: 27% of eyes worsened, 50% remained stable, and 21% improved, based on Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study severity grading (2% unclassified); microvascular nonperfusion, measured using noninvasive OCTA, distinguished the eyes that worsened or remained stable from those eyes that improved. Progression of microvascular nonperfusion identified by OCTA enables identification of patients at higher risk for disease progression.

Title: A Retrospective Evaluation of Safety Outcomes of Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate & Tranexamic Acid Versus Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate Alone in Patients Requiring Emergent Anticoagulation Reversal.
Abstract: Utilizing four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) and tranexamic acid (TXA) concomitantly may theoretically elevate the risk of thromboembolism compared to either agent alone. Certain clinical situations arise where a patient may be a candidate for both TXA and 4F-PCC, such as trauma with major hemorrhage requiring anticoagulation reversal. In the absence of published literature, it is largely unknown whether coadministration of both agents increases the risk of thromboembolic events. The objective of this study was to explore safety outcomes of utilizing both 4F-PCC and TXA concomitantly in patients requiring emergent anticoagulation reversal due to a major hemorrhage. A single-center, retrospective chart review was conducted in adult patients who received 4F-PCC + TXA or 4F-PCC alone for emergent anticoagulation reversal of warfarin, apixaban, or rivaroxaban. The primary endpoint was the occurrence of thromboembolic events. The secondary endpoint was all-cause in-hospital mortality. Of the 110 patients included, 74 received 4F-PCC only and 36 patients received both 4F-PCC and TXA. The occurrence of thromboembolism was significantly higher in the 4F-PCC + TXA group compared to the 4F-PCC group (16.7% vs 2.7%; P = 0.0144). The incidence of all-cause in-hospital mortality was similar between groups [19.4% (4F-PCC + TXA) vs 10.8% (4F-PCC); P = 0.346]. The utilization of both 4F-PCC and TXA for patients with major hemorrhage requiring emergent anticoagulation reversal was associated with a significantly higher risk of thromboembolism than 4F-PCC alone. Clinicians should use caution when utilizing 4F-PCC and TXA concomitantly.

Title: Cardiovascular and Cancer Mortality Among Texas Residents With Cancer: A Population-Based Study in Texas.
Journal: Cancer control : journal of the Moffitt Cancer Center
Abstract: IntroductionCancer and cardiovascular disease (CVD) are leading causes of death among Texas residents. While advances in cancer treatment have increased survival, long-term survivors face elevated CVD risk. We examined temporal trends in cancer- and CVD-related incidence-based mortality (IBM) rates among Texas residents diagnosed with cancer by cancer stage, primary site, and county, and associations between the CVD-to-cancer IBM ratio and survival.MethodsUsing Texas Cancer Registry data, this retrospective cohort study calculated cancer- and CVD-related IBM rates overall and by stage and the five sites with the highest cancer- and CVD-related deaths, and assessed annual percentage change (APC) using Joinpoint regression. County-level heatmaps displayed cumulative IBM rates and CVD-to-cancer IBM ratios, defined as CVD-related IBM rate divided by cancer-related IBM rate, by these groupings. Weighted Pearson correlations with bootstrap standard errors examined associations between CVD-to-cancer IBM ratios and 1- and 5-year survival among patients diagnosed during 2010-2015, followed through 2020.ResultsIn 2010-2019, cancer-related IBM rates declined (APC = -2.51%, 95% CI -3.02 to -2.01, p < 0.001), while CVD-related IBM rates increased (APC = +1.87%, 95% CI 0.81-2.93, p < 0.001). Cancer-related IBM rates decreased, and CVD-related IBM rates generally increased across localized, regional, and distant-stage groups. CVD-to-cancer IBM ratios were higher for high-survival cancers including prostate and breast cancers. Across stages (n=4), correlations between CVD-to-cancer IBM ratio and survival were r = 0.81 (1-year) and r = 0.86 (5-year); inferential statistics were unobtainable. Across sites (n=29), correlations were r = 0.86 (5-year; 95% CI 0.80-0.93, p < 0.001) and r = 0.81 (1-year; 95% CI 0.74-0.89, p < 0.001).ConclusionsCancer-related IBM rates declined while CVD-related IBM rates increased, especially in localized-stage, high-survival sites, and specific Texas counties. Incorporating cardiovascular risk assessment and prevention early in cancer care, focusing on underserved areas, may improve long-term survival.

Title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts.
RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

Title: Advantages and Limitations of the Use of Robots in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Results From a Matched Direct Comparison.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the surgical outcomes of nonrobotic and robotic minimally invasive mitral valve repair.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair from January 2014 to March 2024. After excluding the learning curve cases, early and midterm outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 422 patients who underwent minimally invasive mitral valve repair (nonrobotic, n = 103; robotic, n = 319) were enrolled. The robotic group had a higher EuroSCORE II (P < 0.001). After propensity matching, the final cohort included 84 and 168 patients in each group. In the robotic group after matching, concomitant procedures remained significantly more frequent (P = 0.030). However, operative time (P = 0.782) and cross-clamping time (P = 0.452) were comparable, whereas cardiopulmonary bypass time was significantly longer in the robotic group (P = 0.031). Postoperative blood transfusion (P < 0.001), chest tube output within 24 h (P < 0.001), and intensive care unit stay (P = 0.042) remained higher in the robotic group after matching. Postoperative mitral regurgitation was no greater than mild in both groups (P = 0.146). At 4 years, overall survival was 94.4% versus 98.4% (P = 0.215), and freedom from recurrence of moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5% versus 97.9% (P = 0.230) after matching. These results are consistent with those observed before matching.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic mitral valve repair demonstrated comparable perioperative and midterm outcomes despite greater transfusion requirements and a higher frequency of concomitant procedures. The higher rate of concomitant procedures should be interpreted with caution because it may partly reflect differences in surgical era and patient selection.

Title: Optimizing Saphenous Vein Grafts: From Workhorse to an Evidence-Based Conduit Strategy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The saphenous vein graft (SVG) remains the most common conduit in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) but suffers from inferior long-term patency compared with arterial grafts. This review evaluates the concept of viewing the SVG not as an inherently flawed conduit but as one that can be systematically optimized through evidence-based strategies.
METHODS: A narrative review was conducted to address the following clinical question: "In patients undergoing CABG, how do contemporary surgical harvesting techniques, intraoperative preservation methods, and postoperative pharmacologic strategies interact to optimize the long-term patency of saphenous vein grafts?" We synthesized evidence from recent landmark randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses to define a comprehensive optimization strategy.
RESULTS: SVG failure is a cascade initiated by surgical trauma and propagated by hemodynamic stress. The "no-touch" harvesting technique, which preserves protective perivascular tissue, has demonstrated superior long-term patency in classic trials, although recent evidence has sparked debate regarding its universal reproducibility. Intraoperative preservation with endothelial-sparing solutions and aggressive postoperative pharmacotherapy-including high-intensity statins and tailored antiplatelet strategies-provide crucial secondary protection. Notably, when graft failure occurs, recent randomized evidence challenges the dogma of a strict "native vessel first" approach, supporting instead an individualized, anatomy-driven strategy that balances early procedural hazard against long-term durability.
CONCLUSIONS: The SVG is an optimizable conduit. A modern, integrated approach-combining meticulous harvesting, biological preservation, and aggressive secondary prevention-can substantially improve graft durability. By shifting focus from simple conduit selection to comprehensive conduit optimization and appropriate patient-specific target selection, the Heart Team can significantly improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Berberine improves diabetic foot ulcer healing after tibial transverse osteotomy by inhibiting the PDGF-B/PDGFRβ signaling pathway.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tibial transverse osteotomy (TTO) is a promising but limited surgical option for diabetic foot (DF). Berberine, a natural compound from Coptis chinensis, exhibits anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic effects relevant to metabolic diseases.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate whether adjunctive berberine enhances the therapeutic outcomes of TTO in DF patients and to explore its potential association with the platelet-derived growth factor-B (PDGF-B)/PDGF receptor-β (PDGFRβ) signaling pathway.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, blinded trial. Of 200 screened DF patients, 96 eligible participants (Wagner grade 2-4) scheduled for TTO were randomized 1:1 to receive either TTO plus local berberine injections (n=48) or TTO plus local saline placebo (n=48). An additional non-randomized diabetic reference group (n=10) and healthy control group (n=10) were included for exploratory cellular studies only. The primary outcome was the total effective rate of ulcer healing at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included changes in Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI), ulcer area, Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain score and serum inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6). Exploratory outcomes comprised serum VEGF, bFGF and PDGF-B levels, as well as fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue.
RESULTS: All 96 randomized participants completed the 3-month follow-up, with no dropouts. The berberine group demonstrated a significantly higher total effective rate than the surgery-alone group (87.5% vs. 68.8%; risk difference, 18.7%; 95% CI, 1.2% to 36.2%; P < 0.05). At 3 months, the berberine group also showed greater improvements in ABI (mean difference, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.18; P < 0.01) and ulcer healing rate (mean difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 9.5% to 23.9%; P < 0.01), along with more significant reductions in hs-CRP and IL-6. Berberine treatment was associated with reduced fibroblast apoptosis in wound tissue (mean difference, -1.10%; 95% CI, -1.56% to -0.64%; P = 0.001) and lower protein expression of PDGF-B and PDGFRβ. No severe adverse events related to berberine injections were reported.
CONCLUSION: In DF patients undergoing TTO, adjunctive local berberine therapy significantly improves the total effective rate and promotes ulcer healing, with benefits associated with reduced inflammation and fibroblast apoptosis and downregulation of the PDGF-B/PDGFRβ pathway. These findings are correlative and require further mechanistic validation. Larger multi-center trials are needed to confirm efficacy and safety.

Title: Association Between Ellipsoid Zone Area and Fixation Stability in Macular Telangiectasia Type 2.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether ellipsoid zone (EZ) area loss, a biomarker of photoreceptor degeneration, is associated with fixation stability in macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel).
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 212 adults from two Phase 3 trials of revakinagene taroretcel-lwey for MacTel. EZ area loss was quantified with optical coherence tomography. Fixation stability (P1 index) was measured by microperimetry. Linear and logistic regressions evaluated associations between EZ area loss and P1 over 24 months. A median split stratified the population to evaluate whether baseline EZ area loss influenced the therapeutic effect of the implant versus sham. A receiver operating characteristic analysis identified a structural threshold for unstable fixation.
RESULTS: EZ area loss was significantly associated with reduced fixation stability at baseline (P = 0.002) and month 24 (P = 0.01). Each 1-mm² increase in EZ area loss doubled the odds of poor fixation stability (defined as a P1 <80%) (odds ratio, 2.07; P = 0.047). P1 change did not significantly differ between the treatment and sham groups. In exploratory analyses, stratification by median baseline EZ area loss, despite a nonsignificant treatment-by-baseline interaction (P = 0.17), revealed a greater decline in fixation stability in sham-treated eyes (mean, -3.8%) versus the implant group (+0.6%). The receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an EZ area loss threshold of 1.075 mm² for unstable fixation.
