Title: Preeclampsia Risk in Obese Pregnant Women without Diabetes Mellitus: a Meta-Analysis Comparing Metformin versus Control Group.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of metformin on reducing the risk of pre-eclampsia in obese pregnant women without diabetes.
SOURCES OF DATA: Following PRISMA guidelines, Scopus, Embase, PubMed (MEDLINE), Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, LILACS, SciElo, and Web of Science were searched for articles published between 2014 and April 2024. Search terms: ("Metformin" OR "Biguanide" OR "Glucophage" OR "dimethylbiguanide") AND ("pre-eclampsia" OR "preeclampsia") AND ("obese pregnant women" OR "obesity in pregnancy" OR "maternal obesity" OR "pregnancy" OR "obesity").
STUDY SELECTION: From 2022 studies identified, three randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care in obese pregnant women without diabetes were included. Primary outcomes were pre-eclampsia incidence; secondary outcomes included gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, cesarean delivery, postpartum hemorrhage, and NICU admission.
DATA COLLECTION: Data were extracted, and odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.
DATA SYNTHESIS: Metformin did not significantly reduce PE risk (OR: 0.42; 95% CI: 0.10-1.68; p=0.22; I2=81%). Secondary outcomes showed no significant differences. Subgroup analysis excluding a methodological outlier suggested potential benefit (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.10-0.38; p<0.00001; I2=0%). Metformin alone may not effectively prevent PE in these women, but efficacy could improve with lifestyle modifications. Study heterogeneity highlights the need for larger, rigorous trials.
CONCLUSIONS: Metformin should not be routinely recommended for pre-eclampsia prevention in obese pregnant women without diabetes until robust evidence from further research supports its efficacy.Prospero registry: CRD42024611538.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Meta-Analysis; Systematic Review

Title: Glycated hemoglobin in immediate postpartum, overweight, and pre-gestational arterial hypertension: effect on fasting glycemia one year postpartum.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the relationship between overweight, pre-gestational hypertension, and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels in the immediate postpartum and fasting glycemia (FG) in low-income women one year after birth.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study assessed women who gave birth between February and August 2017 with gestational age > 35 weeks. Interviews and anthropometric evaluations were conducted within the first 24 hours after delivery. Pre-gestational anthropometric nutritional status was assessed based on maternal height measurement. Blood samples were collected after delivery and over the next year, and HbA1c ≥ 5.7% and FG > 100 mg/dL indicated a high risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). A generalized linear mixed-effects regression model was applied.
RESULTS: Among the 130 women included, 28.0% and 2.3% were overweight and had pre-pregnancy hypertension, respectively; 20.0% had altered HbA1c in the immediate postpartum. As for FG, 4.6% and 14.8% were at risk of T2DM at the 6th and 12th months postpartum, respectively. The mean ± standard deviation of FG among the evaluated women was 77.9 ± 10.98 mg/dL after 6 months and 81.8 ± 15.49 mg/dL after one year of follow-up. In the model adjusted for age and schooling, the effect of overweight and pre-pregnancy hypertension was observed, as well as altered HbA1c in the immediate postpartum period, on the elevation of FG, increasing the risk of T2DM.
CONCLUSION: Altered HbA1c in the immediate postpartum period, pre-gestational overweight, and pre-gestational hypertension are risk factors for T2DM among low-income women, indicating the need to monitor postpartum glycemia.

Title: Comparative econometric cost analysis of inpatient versus outpatient laser treatment for twin-twin transfusion syndrome.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the costs of inpatient versus outpatient laser ablation of placental vessels treatment of severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome. To evaluate if outpatient is non-inferior to inpatient treatment with regards to feasibility and safety.
METHODS: Case-control study of 71 pregnant women who underwent laser ablation of placental vessels for treatment of severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome between 2019 and 2022. To compare the costs of outpatient versus inpatient treatments we used conditional estimation of the average costs of each procedure and the differences between them with paired data estimators: multivariate distance matching and propensity score matching. Comparisons of surgical and clinical variables were performed using the Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and Student's t-test.
RESULTS: Laser ablation of placental vessels was performed in 71 patients with severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome. Sixteen (16/71 - 23%) patients were operated on in the outpatient clinic and 55 (55/71 - 77%) were operated on as inpatients. The cost of inpatient intervention was 28% and 29% higher than the cost of the outpatient treatment, according to the multivariate distance matching and propensity score matching estimates, respectively. Apart from ex-recipient intrauterine death (greater in the outpatient group), there were no significant differences between the two groups regarding laser ablation of placental vessels, post laser treatment, perinatal variables and variables from delivery until hospital discharge.
CONCLUSION: Laser ablation of placental vessels to treat severe twin-twin transfusion syndrome in an outpatient setting is significantly cheaper than in inpatients, without any compromise in feasibility and safety, as most fetal, neonatal and maternal results were similar.

Title: Comparison of 25 µg Vaginal Misoprostol Versus Dinoprostone Gel for Induction of Labor in Term Prelabor Rupture of Membranes: A Retrospective Record-Based Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) at term occurs in 8-10% of pregnancies, and a long latency period is associated with infection in both the mother and the newborn. In women with an unfavorable cervix, cervical ripening and induction of labor are widely used with prostaglandin analogs. However, the preferred agent in women with term PROM remains unclear. This study compared the efficacy and safety of 25 µg vaginal misoprostol (prostaglandin E1) and dinoprostone (prostaglandin E2) gel in women with term PROM.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a record-based, comparative, observational study with a retrospective design conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in West India over 12 months. Records of 200 women with term PROM (≥37 weeks), singleton cephalic pregnancy, and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop's score ≤6) were reviewed. The primary outcome was the induction-to-delivery interval and the proportion of vaginal deliveries within 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included change in Bishop score at six hours, oxytocin dose, interval from induction to active labor, need for oxytocin augmentation, mode of delivery, and maternal and neonatal safety outcomes. An independent-samples t-test was employed for continuous variables, and chi-square or Fisher's exact test was used for categorical variables; p < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: The two groups did not differ in maternal age, parity, PROM duration, or baseline Bishop score. The mean Bishop score at six hours was significantly higher in the misoprostol group (5.68 ± 1.31 vs 4.78 ± 1.26; p < 0.001). The mean induction-to-active-labor interval (6.80 ± 1.58 vs 8.19 ± 2.06 hours; p < 0.001) and the induction-to-delivery interval (11.81 ± 3.06 vs 13.78 ± 3.99 hours; p < 0.001) were significantly shorter with misoprostol, which also required fewer doses (1.62 ± 0.63 vs 1.91 ± 0.67; p = 0.002) and less oxytocin augmentation (16 (16.0%) vs 46 (46.0%); p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in the proportion of vaginal deliveries within 24 hours (92 (92.0%) vs 94 (94.0%); p = 0.780) or cesarean deliveries (8 (8.0%) vs 6 (6.0%); p = 0.780). The groups did not differ in uterine hyperstimulation (5% vs 2%), abnormal fetal heart rate (8% vs 6%), postpartum hemorrhage (4% vs 5%), mean birth weight, or NICU admission (4% vs 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: 25 µg vaginal misoprostol was associated with more effective cervical ripening and shorter time to delivery than dinoprostone gel, with fewer doses and a lower rate of oxytocin use, similar cesarean rates, and comparable maternal and neonatal safety. The use of low-dose vaginal misoprostol may represent a practical alternative to dinoprostone gel in term PROM.

Title: Soluble E-selectin and QRISK3-based Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Prospective Case-control Study from India.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with metabolic abnormalities and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Endothelial dysfunction is considered an early event in atherogenesis, and soluble E-selectin has been proposed as a marker of endothelial activation. However, its role in cardiovascular risk assessment in PCOS remains uncertain.
AIM: The study aimed to compare circulating soluble E-selectin levels between women with PCOS and healthy controls and evaluate their association with metabolic parameters and QRISK3-based cardiovascular risk scores.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: Prospective hospital-based case-control study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two hundred women with PCOS diagnosed according to the Rotterdam criteria and 50 age-matched healthy controls aged 18-40 years were enrolled. Clinical assessment, anthropometry, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, C-reactive protein and soluble E-selectin levels were evaluated. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk was calculated using the QRISK3 algorithm.
STATISTICAL ANALYSIS USED: Group comparisons, correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: Mean soluble E-selectin levels were comparable between women with PCOS and controls (0.61 ± 0.33 vs. 0.61 ± 0.29 ng/mL, P = 0.935). Within the PCOS group, soluble E-selectin correlated positively with HbA1c (r = 0.326, P = 0.001) and fasting blood glucose (r = 0.271, P = 0.001), while no significant associations were observed with anthropometric measures, lipid parameters, blood pressure or QRISK3 scores. In multivariable analysis, fasting blood glucose remained independently associated with soluble E-selectin.
CONCLUSION: Soluble E-selectin levels did not differ between women with PCOS and controls and showed limited associations with cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not support a major role for soluble E-selectin in cardiovascular risk assessment among young women with PCOS.

Title: Pharmacological therapy and dietary intervention for obesity management: A one-year prospective cohort study in Baghdad.
Journal: Journal of education and health promotion
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence directly comparing long-term pharmacological therapy and structured dietary intervention for obesity in Middle Eastern populations is limited. This study provides 12-month real-world comparative data from specialized obesity clinics in Baghdad, Iraq.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study included 120 adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) from June 2024 to June 2025. Participants received either pharmacological therapy (orlistat 120 mg three times daily or liraglutide 3.0 mg/day; n = 60) with standard lifestyle advice, or intensive individualized dietary counseling by board-certified dietitians (n = 60). The primary outcome was percentage weight loss at 12 months. Secondary outcomes assessed body composition, metabolic parameters, physical activity, adherence, adverse effects, and quality of life. Between-group differences were analyzed using independent t-tests with exact P values and 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: At 12 months, pharmacological therapy associated with greater early weight loss but reached a plateau (13.5 ± 3.7% vs. 11.3 ± 4.3%, P < 0.001; 95% CI: 1.1-2.8%). Dietary intervention associated with higher fat-mass loss (68.9% vs. 53.1%, P < 0.001), better lean-mass preservation (P = 0.003), and superior improvements in LDL-cholesterol (P = 0.012), fasting glucose (P = 0.047), systolic blood pressure (P = 0.041), and physical activity (P = 0.001). Adherence (73.3% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.038) and patient satisfaction (P < 0.001) were higher with diet, while gastrointestinal side effects were more common with pharmacotherapy (68.3% vs. 11.7%, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Intensive dietary counseling yielded to superior long-term metabolic, behavioral, and patient-centered outcomes with better adherence, supporting its use as a first-line obesity treatment. Pharmacological therapy may be an adjunct for selected patients, highlighting the importance of structured, dietitian-led lifestyle programs within health systems.

Title: Kidney Outcomes in Structural Heart and Cardiac Surgical Trials: The Case for Longitudinal Endpoint Reporting.
Abstract: The 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/American Diabetes Association/American Society of Nephrology guideline on cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome establishes kidney function as a determinant of cardiovascular risk rather than an adjacent comorbidity. Endpoint architecture in structural heart and cardiac surgical research has not been revised accordingly. Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 standardized acute kidney injury reporting with considerable rigor, staging injury on Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine criteria and requiring that new renal replacement therapy be reported discretely, but its scope is confined to the periprocedural window. No endpoint tracks filtration trajectory across follow-up, no threshold within the standard defines chronic kidney disease stage progression, and initiation of maintenance dialysis years after intervention has no reporting convention distinct from temporary replacement therapy in the immediate postoperative period. Pivotal trials consequently adjudicate cardiovascular outcomes for five years and kidney outcomes for 30 days. Registry evidence suggests the omission is consequential, with rapid filtration decline documented in more than a third of patients carrying preexisting kidney impairment within five years of cardiac surgery. This editorial argues for longitudinal reporting of estimated glomerular filtration rate, prespecification of stage progression and maintenance dialysis as adjudicated endpoints, and nephrology representation on trial steering committees with a defined role in kidney endpoint specification.

Title: Cardiac camp: An outreach program to build health literacy among underrepresented in medicine adolescents and increase diversity in medicine.
Journal: Journal of education and health promotion
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eliminating racial and ethnic disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires multilevel action, including improving health literacy and diversifying the healthcare workforce. To contribute to this goal, UCSF medical students designed an immersive summer camp to teach underrepresented minority backgrounds in medical professions (URM) high school students about CVD and encourage interest in healthcare careers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A stipend-supported, 1-week cardiology summer camp for URM Bay Area high school students was implemented by medical students. Participating students completed a preprogram and postprogram survey to assess various metrics, including knowledge of CVD, comfort discussing and teaching concepts of CVD, and interest in medical careers on a Likert scale of 1-5. The mean differences in preprogram and postprogram scores in the second cohort in 2024 (n = 25) were assessed.
RESULTS: Twenty-five students participated in the second iteration of Cardiac Camp @ UCSF (80% female) from July 24 to 28, 2024. Most identified as URM (84%), and many came from households where English was not the primary language (76%). Postcamp surveys showed increased mean scores in CVD knowledge and awareness of medical careers. Open-ended responses indicated that students enjoyed the camp activities and felt more motivated to pursue healthcare careers.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac Camp @ UCSF provides a novel framework for a pipeline program aimed at inspiring URM high school students to pursue careers in medicine. Short-term survey results showed increased CVD knowledge and confidence teaching others, aligning with Healthy People 2030 goals to reduce cardiovascular disparities and strengthen workforce diversity.

Title: A randomised controlled trial comparing a 100% chitosan haemostatic dressing and a manual compression device following transradial coronary intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemostasis at radial access sites following transradial coronary intervention (TRCI) is usually achieved using manual compression devices (MCDs). Despite their widespread use, MCDs have limitations, including prolonged compression and haemostasis times as well as increased risk of radial artery occlusion (RAO), thus highlighting the need for alternative strategies to achieve faster and safer radial haemostasis.
AIMS: We sought to compare the safety and efficacy of a 100% chitosan haemostatic dressing (CHD) with an MCD in achieving radial access site haemostasis following TRCI.
METHODS: A total of 258 patients were randomly assigned to receive either a CHD (n=130; Axiostat) or an MCD (n=128; TR Band) for radial haemostasis following TRCI. Time to haemostasis, post-application pain, and access site complications - including rebleeding, haematoma, RAO, and allergic reactions - were assessed.
RESULTS: Both groups had similar baseline and procedural characteristics. The CHD significantly reduced haemostasis time (5.84±2.19 min) compared with the MCD (120.2±21.88 min; p<0.001). Post-application pain scores were low and comparable between both groups. The CHD was associated with lower rates of haematoma and rebleeding. RAO occurred in 3.12% of MCD patients, while no RAO events were observed with the CHD. No serious adverse events or device-related complications were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: The CHD provided rapid haemostasis with a shorter compression time, lower RAO risk, and reduced patient-reported pain, along with minimal rebleeding, few haematomas, and no allergic events compared with MCD, without compromising safety. This clearly illustrates that the CHD is a safe and effective alternative for achieving haemostasis following TRCI, potentially enabling earlier patient ambulation and discharge.

Title: A semi-rapid deployment workflow to reduce device time in Evolut FX self-expanding transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: As transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) expands, improving deployment efficiency is increasingly important. We developed and implemented a semi-rapid pacing-assisted deployment workflow for the Evolut platform.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the procedural efficiency and early safety of this workflow for transfemoral (TF) Evolut FX TAVI.
METHODS: In a single-centre registry, we performed a retrospective before-and-after analysis of consecutive TF Evolut FX procedures: semi-rapid deployment (n=48) versus conventional deployment (n=53). Device time was defined as the interval from initial advancement of the delivery system to final release of the Evolut FX valve. Prolonged device time was defined as >14 minutes (>75th percentile), and determinants were assessed using Firth's penalised logistic regression.
RESULTS: The device time was shorter with semi-rapid deployment (9.0 [interquartile range [IQR] 6.0-13.0] minutes vs 14.0 [IQR 11.0-16.0] minutes; p<0.001), while operation and procedure times were similar (p=0.13 and p=0.16, respectively). The mean recapture count was higher in the semi-rapid group (0.85±1.09 vs 0.53±0.70; p=0.08), and contrast volume was higher (32.0 [IQR 25.0-42.0] mL vs 25.0 [IQR 15.0-33.0] mL; p=0.008). Paravalvular leak >=mild (31.2% vs 32.1%; p=1.0) and in-hospital pacemaker implantation (2.1% vs 7.5%; p=0.37) did not differ significantly between the groups. In multivariable analysis, recapture predicted a prolonged device time (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 4.74, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.75-14.19; p=0.002), whereas the semi-rapid workflow predicted a reduced device time (adjusted OR 0.10, 95% CI: 0.01-0.66; p=0.015).
CONCLUSIONS: Semi-rapid pacing-assisted Evolut FX deployment selectively reduced device time without compromising early in-hospital safety outcomes. Deployment efficiency represents a practical procedural target for workflow refinement in self-expanding TAVI.

Title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
Abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

Title: γ-Butyrobetaine, L-carnitine and acylcarnitines and their association with incident atrial fibrillation among men and women with suspected chronic coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
AIMS: Carnitine-metabolites play a key role in cell energy metabolism and have been implicated in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, any associations between L-carnitine and the precursor γ-butyrobetaine (γBB) with new-onset AF are not established. We therefore examined the relationship between serum γBB, L-carnitine and selected acylcarnitines with incident AF.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 3815 patients who underwent coronary angiography due to suspected chronic coronary syndrome and followed up for incident CVD events, including new-onset AF. Risk associations between the biomarkers and incident AF were explored by logistic regression for the total population and stratified according to sex. The majority (71.6%) of the patients were men, the median age was 61 years. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years, 412 (10.8%) were reported with new-onset AF. In a multivariate model higher serum γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine [OR per 1SD (95% CI): 1.15 (1.01-1.31), P = 0.04; 1.14 (1.01-1.27), P = 0.03 and 1.15 (1.03-1.28), P = 0.01] were associated with increased risk of incident AF. These associations were particularly stronger among women (P for interaction < 0.04, all).
CONCLUSION: In this large cohort of patients with suspected chronic coronary syndrome elevated circulating levels of γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine were associated with increased risk of incident AF, with stronger associations among women. Our results motivate further studies examining the relationship between carnitine metabolites and cardiac arrhythmias and highlight the need for sex specific analyses.

Title: First Report of Real World Utilization of an Activin Signaling Inhibitor in Patients With Severe Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in the Middle East PH RISE-ME Study.
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality despite advances in combination therapy. Sotatercept, an activin-signaling inhibitor, is a novel disease-modifying therapy targeting pulmonary vascular remodeling. Real-world data from Middle Eastern populations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study evaluating the real-world effectiveness and safety of Sotatercept in adults with PAH treated at a tertiary pulmonary hypertension expert center in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, between January 2025 and September 2026. Clinical, echocardiographic, biochemical, and risk-stratification data were extracted from electronic medical records. Primary outcomes were changes in right atrial (RA) area and NT-proBNP. Secondary outcomes included systolic pulmonary arterial pressure (SPAP), TAPSE/SPAP ratio, 6-min walk distance (6MWD), risk profile, and safety. Thirty-six patients were prescribed Sotatercept, of whom 33 received at least one dose. Most patients were female (80.6%), with a mean age of 55 years. Significant reductions occurred in RA area (- 2.67 cm2; 95% CI, -4.16 to -1.18; p < 0.001), NT-proBNP (- 46.7 pmol/L; 95% CI, -87.19 to -20.39; p < 0.001), and SPAP (- 6.00 mmHg; 95% CI, -12.00 to -0.50; p = 0.031). TAPSE increased significantly (+ 0.25 cm; 95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33; p < 0.001), and TAPSE/SPAP improved significantly (+ 0.064; 95% CI, 0.030 to 0.108; p < 0.001). Patients improved by at least one risk category. The 6MWD did not change significantly. Treatment was well tolerated, with no adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation or death; two all-cause deaths occurred during follow-up. In this real-world Middle Eastern PAH cohort, Sotatercept was associated with improved right-heart remodeling, NT-proBNP, and risk profile, with acceptable short-term safety. These findings complement trial evidence and provide early regional support for activin pathway inhibition in routine practice.

Title: Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension With Cold Agglutinins Needing Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: The Use of Therapeutic Plasma Exchange.
Abstract: Cold agglutinins can be detected in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) during pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) pre-operative testing. Peri-operative management of these patients in anticipation of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest can be challenging and has not been standardized. We describe our relevant experience and suggest a potential protocolized pre-operative approach with this observational, retrospective cohort study. A chart review of all patients undergoing PTE surgery for CTEPH (1107 patients) at UC San Diego between 2019 and 2025 was performed. An Institutional Review Board approved quality improvement database on all patients undergoing PTE surgery was used. Twenty-one patients (1.9%) screened positive for cold agglutinins pre-PTE. A high co-prevalence of antiphospholipid syndrome and cold agglutinins was noted (17/21; 81%). Thermal amplitude testing (when possible) was positive for nine patients between 15°C and 18°C. Fifteen patients underwent therapeutic plasma exchange (median of two sessions) with albumin and plasma replacement fluid followed by PTE surgery with standard cooling protocol. There were no incidents of agglutination or hemolysis peri- or post-operatively. Three patients had post-operative airway hemorrhage, two of which developed heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT). There was one mortality in the setting of HIT with recurrent thrombosis and bleeding. Median intensive care unit and hospital length of stays were 3 and 12.5 days, respectively. We suggest a protocolized approach for the identification and management of high-risk patients with cold agglutinins, which may include therapeutic plasma exchange pre-operatively. This can successfully mitigate the potential risk of hypothermic circulatory arrest causing agglutination during surgery.

Title: Cenobamate in super-refractory status epilepticus: current evidence from a patient-level synthesis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE) represents a challenging neurological emergency, with limited therapeutic options after conventional intravenous antiseizure medications (ASMs) and continuous anesthetic therapy have failed. Cenobamate has shown remarkable efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, but its role in SRSE is currently supported only by isolated case reports.
METHODS: We performed a patient-level synthesis of published cases of cenobamate-treated SRSE, focusing on treatment latency, titration strategy, electroclinical response, concomitant therapies, safety, and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: Three publications reporting six patients were identified. Cenobamate was introduced between 13 and 103 days after SRSE onset, following failure of multiple intravenous and oral ASMs, anesthetic agents, and, in most cases, immunomodulatory therapies. Although the timing of treatment initiation varied substantially, electroencephalographic improvement generally occurred within two weeks after cenobamate initiation and was usually accompanied by clinical recovery, successful withdrawal of anesthetic therapy, and liberation from the intensive care unit. Most patients initiated cenobamate at the recommended dose of 12.5 mg/day but underwent individualized dose-escalation schedules compared with the approved outpatient regimen. No cases of drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, severe cardiac adverse events, or treatment discontinuation attributable to cenobamate were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the available evidence remains limited to a small number of observational reports, this patient-level synthesis identified consistent clinical patterns that support further investigation of cenobamate as an adjunctive therapy for SRSE. At present, no conclusions regarding treatment efficacy can be drawn. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to clarify cenobamate optimal timing, titration strategy, safety, and potential role within SRSE treatment algorithms.

Title: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) in right ventricular failure and preserved LV ejection fraction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) failure with preserved left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (LVEF ≥50%) is a distinct clinical entity often associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH), chronic lung diseases, or congenital heart defects, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitors (ARNI), such as sacubitril/valsartan, have demonstrated efficacy in left-sided heart failure, but their role in isolated RV failure remains understudied.
METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted from 2010 to 2025 for RCTs and prospective cohorts assessing ARNI in patients with RV failure and preserved LVEF. Inclusion: Adults with RV dysfunction (e.g., TAPSE <17 mm or RV S' <9.5 cm/s) and LVEF ≥50%; ARNI vs. standard care or pre-treatment; reporting RV parameters, sPAP, NT-proBNP, 6MWD, or NYHA class.
RESULTS: Three studies (1 RCT, 2 prospective cohorts; n=120 patients) were included. ARNI improved TAPSE (WMD 1.2 mm, 95% CI 0.7-1.7; p<0.001; I²=0%), RV S' (WMD 0.5 cm/s, 95% CI 0.2-0.8; P=0.002; I²=0%), and reduced sPAP (WMD -7.5 mmHg, 95% CI -10.2 to -4.8; p<0.001; I²=15%). NT-proBNP decreased (WMD -1200 pg/mL, 95% CI -1700 to -700; p<0.001; I²=0%). 6MWD increased (WMD 30 m, 95% CI 10-50; P=0.003; I²=0%). NYHA class improved (RR 1.65 for ≥1 class improvement, 95% CI 1.15-2.37; P=0.007; I²=0%).
CONCLUSION: ARNI enhances RV function, reduces pulmonary pressures, and improves functional status in RV failure with preserved LVEF.

Title: Outcomes by Comorbidities with Tremelimumab and Durvalumab in the Randomized, Controlled Phase 3 HIMALAYA Study in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often have underlying comorbidities, which may impact prognosis and lead to safety challenges following treatment. This exploratory, post hoc analysis of the phase 3 HIMALAYA study (NCT03298451) assessed outcomes in participants with unresectable HCC and cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities at baseline.
METHODS: Participants with unresectable HCC were randomized to STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab), durvalumab monotherapy, or sorafenib. Comorbidities were based on medical history assessed at baseline and qualified using preferred terms from cardiovascular or metabolic Standardised Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Queries. Overall survival (OS) rates were evaluated in participants with or without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities within and by treatment group. The proportion of long-term survivors (alive ≥36 months post-randomization) and safety were assessed in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities. Data cutoffs: August 27, 2021 (primary analysis); January 23, 2023 (4-year updated analysis, OS, and serious treatment-related adverse events).
RESULTS: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus were the most common cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, respectively. The 48-month OS rates with STRIDE were 28.0% and 21.7% in participants with and without cardiovascular comorbidities and 20.4% and 28.5% in those with and without metabolic comorbidities, respectively. In total, 28.2% of participants with cardiovascular comorbidities and 22.6% of participants with metabolic comorbidities experienced long-term survival with STRIDE. Safety in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities was generally consistent with all participants in the safety analysis set; no new safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: OS benefits with STRIDE were similar in participants with vs. without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities, with manageable safety in participants with comorbidities. These results support the durable benefits of STRIDE in a broad population reflective of unresectable HCC globally.

Title: Blood Pressure Trajectories during Graded Exercise for the Prediction of Future Hypertension.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: An exaggerated increase in systolic blood pressure (SBP) during exercise is associated with future hypertension. While previous studies evaluated peak SBP or two-point slopes, we aimed to identify SBP response patterns from the full SBP time-series during maximal incremental exercise and assess their value for predicting future hypertension diagnosis.
METHODS: In this cohort study, we analysed SBP recordings from 3,486 normotensive adults (mean age 50.6 years; 45% women) undergoing maximal cycle ergometry. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) extracted sex-specific responses from the full SBP time-series. Associations with incident hypertension were evaluated using multivariable Cox analyses by sex and stratified by prehypertensive status (SBP 130-150 mm Hg or DBP 85-90 mm Hg).
RESULTS: In both sexes, GBTM identified three SBP response profiles, reflecting low, mid, and high responders. Over 7.9 years, 171 (8.8%) men and 169 (10.9%) women were diagnosed with hypertension. Incidence was markedly higher in high versus low responders (e.g., in women: 27.8 vs. 2.5 events per 1,000 follow-up years). The increased risk was independent of traditional risk factors, including resting SBP (hazard ratio relative to average risk (HRadj): 1.26 [95% confidence interval: 1.00-1.57] in men, 1.59 [1.22-2.07] in women). The association attenuated with increasing resting SBP in women (p interaction = 0.003). Notably, high SBP response was independently associated with future hypertension diagnosis in those without prehypertension (e.g., in women, HRadj: 2.17 [1.49-3.17]), but not in those with prehypertension. Reclassification analyses indicated incremental predictive value beyond resting and peak SBP in women without prehypertension.
CONCLUSIONS: Time-series analysis of exercise SBP revealed distinct response profiles predicting future hypertension diagnosis beyond resting blood pressure. Comprehensive interpretation of exercise SBP may improve risk stratification, particularly in women without prehypertension.

Title: Enterococcus faecalis bacteraemia and infective endocarditis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of infective endocarditis (IE) in Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection (EF-BSI) vary more than 20-fold across published cohorts. We aimed to estimate the true IE prevalence, quantify the role of echocardiographic ascertainment in driving this variation, and assess the diagnostic performance of IE prediction scores.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science searched from inception to 16 August 2026; PROSPERO registration CRD420251240242) of observational studies reporting IE prevalence in confirmed EF-BSI episodes. Risk of bias was assessed with the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool. Pooled prevalence was estimated with a generalised linear mixed model (logit scale). Meta-regression with echocardiographic coverage as the moderator was used to derive an ascertainment-adjusted prevalence. Diagnostic performance of the NOVA, DENOVA, and MEFIER scores was summarised by random-effects pooling.
FINDINGS: Fifteen studies (11,157 EF-BSI episodes) were included. Crude pooled IE prevalence was 11.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 8.1-16.8; I2 = 97.3%). In studies with systematic echocardiography (k = 2), pooled prevalence was 24.2% (21.5-27.2; I2 = 0.0%). Meta-regression explained up to 91.5% of between-study variance; estimated plateau IE prevalence was approximately 30%. Pooled DENOVA sensitivity was 88.7% (78.9-94.3%) and specificity 84.0% (77.8-88.7%); prospective validation yielded sensitivity 79.2% (negative predictive value [NPV] 93.0%). NOVA had high sensitivity (95.6%) but low specificity (30.7%). Certainty of evidence was low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation [GRADE]).
INTERPRETATION: Once ascertainment is accounted for, approximately one quarter of EF-BSI episodes are complicated by IE. These findings support a shift from selective to routine echocardiography, with transoesophageal echocardiography (TEE) as the definitive modality. Existing scores can prioritise and sequence imaging but do not identify a subgroup in whom it may be safely omitted.

Title: The burden of medically indicated preterm birth due to preeclampsia and its association to the fullpiers score in a high-risk maternity setting.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Describe the prevalence of medically indicated preterm birth due to preeclampsia (PE), maternal and perinatal outcomes, and the use of the fullPIERS calculator for risk assessment.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at a high-risk maternity center through a review of women records with medically indicated preterm birth due to PE between January 2020 and December 2023. Sociodemographic data, maternal and perinatal outcomes were evaluated. The fullPIERS calculator was applied using a cutoff value ≥2.15%, proposed as a predictor of adverse outcomes.
RESULTS: During the study period, 24,507 births were recorded, which 2,523 were preterm (10.2%). Preterm birth attributed to PE occurred in 9.75% of cases (n=246), with 2.4% (n=6) progressing to eclampsia. The mean maternal age was 31.7 years and mean systolic/diastolic blood pressures were 157.3 mmHg and 100.9 mmHg, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was observed in 25.6% of women, and elevated transaminases occurred in 14%. The mean gestational age at delivery was 34.06 weeks, and 68.8% of deliveries were indicated due to worsening blood pressure control. The stillbirth rate was 2.45% (n=6). Women with fullPIERS scores ≥2.15% (n=53) presented greater disease severity, including higher rates of thrombocytopenia, elevated creatinine (15%), lower gestational age at delivery (mean 32.8±3.2 weeks), and increased prevalence of HELLP syndrome (9.3%) and perinatal mortality (2.45%).
CONCLUSION: Preeclampsia is an important cause of medically indicated preterm birth and is associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes. The fullPIERS model may represent a useful adjunct tool for assessing disease severity and supporting clinical decision-making in this context.

Title: Fetal arrhythmia and heart disease during COVID-19 pandemic in patients who underwent echocardiography.
Journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the characteristics and the occurrence of fetal heart diseases and arrhythmias in pregnancies that underwent fetal echocardiography examination during COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data extracted from the Fetal Ultrasound and Fetal Medicine Departments of Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, a tertiary hospital in São Paulo, Brazil, from January to December 2021. The sample was analyzed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney test. Logistic regression was performed to assess the risk of fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease.
RESULTS: A total of 148 fetuses were included in the analysis. The prevalence of fetal heart disease/arrhythmia was higher among patients with maternal comorbidities (73.3% vs. 39.1%), fetal defects (14.3% vs. 0.8%), and functional abnormalities (26.7% vs. 4.5%). Maternal COVID-19 showed no significant association with fetal cardiac outcomes. Maternal comorbidity, fetal malformation, and the presence of functional abnormalities were identified as independent risk factors.
CONCLUSION: Maternal comorbidities were associated with fetal arrhythmia and/or heart disease, but no causal relationship was found between COVID-19 and adverse fetal cardiac outcome.

Title: Topical Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors in Macular Edema: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: In order to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (CAIs) in the treatment of macular edema across different retinal disorders, a systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 13, 2026, without language or publication date restrictions. Clinical studies evaluating topical dorzolamide or brinzolamide for macular edema of any etiology were included. Data regarding study characteristics, treatment protocols, visual and anatomical outcomes, and follow-up were extracted independently by two reviewers. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, cohort studies, case series, and one analytical cross-sectional study. Overall, the included studies were of moderate-to-high methodological quality. Retinitis pigmentosa-associated cystoid macular edema was the most frequently investigated condition (13 studies), followed by X-linked retinoschisis (10 studies), diabetic macular edema (four studies), and one macular edema following vitrectomy and epiretinal membrane removal. Topical dorzolamide was the most commonly evaluated agent, whereas topical brinzolamide was investigated less frequently. Across retinal disorders, topical CAIs consistently reduced central macular thickness and improved retinal morphology as assessed by optical coherence tomography. Functional outcomes were more variable, with improvements in best-corrected visual acuity observed primarily in selected patients with retinitis pigmentosa and diabetic macular edema, whereas visual gains were generally modest in X-linked retinoschisis. Long-term studies reported recurrence of macular edema despite continued treatment, particularly in retinitis pigmentosa. Topical CAIs were well tolerated, with no serious ocular or systemic adverse events reported. Topical CAIs provide consistent anatomical improvement in macular edema, particularly in inherited retinal disorders, while functional benefits are less predictable. This discrepancy between anatomical and functional outcomes may be attributed to prolonged photoreceptor loss, retinal pigment epithelium dysfunction, and irreversible disruption of the ellipsoid zone. Their favorable safety profile and non-invasive administration support their use as a therapeutic option, especially for retinitis pigmentosa-associated cystoid macular edema and selected cases of X-linked retinoschisis and diabetic macular edema. However, the current evidence is limited by predominantly observational studies and clinical heterogeneity. Well-designed multicenter randomized controlled trials are needed to establish their optimal role in the management of macular edema.

Title: Open, laparoscopic, and robotic liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma: evolving roles, comparative outcomes, and future perspectives.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide and frequently arises in the setting of chronic liver disease, cirrhosis, and portal hypertension. Liver resection represents a cornerstone of curative-intent treatment, but its role is uniquely influenced by the need to balance oncologic radicality with preservation of functional liver parenchyma. Over the last two decades, minimally invasive liver surgery has progressively expanded from selected laparoscopic minor resections to complex laparoscopic and robotic hepatectomies, challenging the historical dominance of open surgery. This narrative review critically examines the evolving roles of open, laparoscopic, and robotic liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma, emphasizing patient selection, technical considerations, scenario-based platform choice, and comparative outcomes. Particular attention is given to hepatocellular carcinoma-specific challenges, including impaired liver function, clinically significant portal hypertension, future liver remnant adequacy, recurrence risk, and the need for parenchymal-sparing strategies. The review also discusses distinct clinical scenarios, including small solitary tumors, posterosuperior lesions, central or deeply located tumors, multifocal disease, and recurrent HCC. Current evidence consistently suggests that minimally invasive approaches are associated with reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications, and shorter hospital stay compared with open surgery, while maintaining comparable oncologic outcomes in selected patients. Laparoscopy remains the most established minimally invasive platform, whereas robotics may offer technical advantages in complex resections through improved dexterity, three-dimensional visualization, and enhanced suturing capability. However, available evidence remains largely retrospective and influenced by selection bias and institutional expertise. Platform selection should therefore be individualized according to tumor anatomy, liver function, technical complexity, and center experience, with the goal of maximizing oncologic benefit while minimizing functional liver loss.

Title: Biolimus- versus sirolimus-eluting stents in percutaneous coronary intervention: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-eluting stents (SES) are a benchmark in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), while biolimus-eluting stents (BES), which combine a more lipophilic analogue with a biodegradable polymer, may enhance healing and reduce thrombosis. Whether these BES features translate into improved survival and cardiac outcomes compared with SES remains uncertain.
AIMS: We sought to perform a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating BES compared with SES in adult patients undergoing PCI.
METHODS: This meta-analysis encompassed randomised and controlled clinical trials that directly compared BES with SES in the setting of percutaneous coronary intervention. A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials up to June 2025. The main outcomes assessed were all-cause and cardiac mortality, while secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), myocardial infarction, target lesion revascularisation (TLR), and stent thrombosis (ST). Outcomes were evaluated at <=1 year (early) and >1-5 years (midterm) using pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) in random-effects models, with heterogeneity assessed by the I2 test.
RESULTS: Six trials (12,109 patients: 6,088 BES, 6,021 SES) were analysed. BES reduced 1-year cardiac death by 30% (RR 0.70, 95% CI: 0.52-0.93) and showed a non-significant 19% reduction in all-cause death (RR 0.81; p=0.058). MACE, myocardial infarction, and TLR were similar between stents across timepoints. BES showed a non-significant early increase in ST (RR 1.85; p=0.12) but a 46% reduction in late ST (RR 0.54, 95% CI: 0.33-0.88). Mortality rates converged after 1 year.
CONCLUSIONS: BES offer a short-term reduction in cardiac mortality and late stent thrombosis compared with SES, with otherwise similar morbidity outcomes. These results support the short-term safety of BES and indicate a possible long-term thrombotic and cardiac survival benefit, warranting confirmation in longer-term trials.

Title: Classic case report: concomitant pulsed field ablation, cavotricuspid isthmus ablation and percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion in a patient with prior intracranial haemorrhage.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (pLAAO) offers single-procedure rhythm control and stroke prevention in patients unable to tolerate long-term oral anticoagulation. Patients with prior intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) from suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) have among the strongest contraindications to anticoagulation yet are absent from randomized trials of concomitant procedures, and combining pulsed field ablation (PFA) with pLAAO introduces energy-specific considerations.
CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old woman with persistent AF, cavotricuspid isthmus-dependent atrial flutter and a CHA2DS2-VA score of 3 had been off anticoagulation for 2 years after an ICH. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed microhaemorrhages and siderosis suggestive of CAA. Through a single transseptal puncture, four-vein PFA was performed first to avoid electrical interaction with the nitinol pLAAO frame, followed by WATCHMAN FLX deployment under transoesophageal echocardiographic and computed tomography (CT)-fluoroscopy guidance and radiofrequency cavotricuspid isthmus ablation. She received edoxaban without aspirin for three months. Cardiac CT then confirmed device seal without device-related thrombus, and all antithrombotic therapy was withdrawn.
DISCUSSION: Randomized trials show that anticoagulation after ICH prevents ischaemic stroke at the cost of a marked increase in recurrent haemorrhage, and lobar or CAA-related haemorrhage carries the least favourable balance. Concomitant ablation and pLAAO delivers rhythm control and stroke prevention with one transseptal access and one time-limited exposure to anticoagulation. Combining PFA with pLAAO requires sizing the occluder before ablation, because PFA induces acute pulmonary ridge oedema, and completing pulmonary vein isolation before deployment to avoid arcing against the nitinol frame.

Title: Dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for pure native aortic regurgitation via transfemoral access: a meta-analysis of contemporary outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR) poses unique technical challenges for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), including annular dilatation and absent calcification for anchoring. Whilst dedicated aortic regurgitation (AR) devices have been developed, their comparative performance against off-label devices specifically via transfemoral access - the contemporary standard approach - remains incompletely defined.
AIMS: We aimed to compare the outcomes of dedicated versus off-label transcatheter devices for PNAR via transfemoral access in contemporary practice.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed (MEDLINE) and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2020-November 2025) for studies reporting transfemoral TAVI outcomes in PNAR. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Random-effects meta-analysis with meta-regression was performed.
RESULTS: Twenty-four studies (2,956 patients) were included comprising 25 cohorts: 4 cohorts (537 patients) evaluated dedicated devices, and 21 cohorts (2,419 patients) assessed off-label devices. Overall, 30-day mortality was 3.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.3-4.8%). Dedicated devices showed a trend towards lower mortality (1.9% vs 4.1%, odds ratio [OR] 0.45, 95% CI: 0.20-1.00; p=0.051; risk ratio 0.40, 95% CI: 0.19-0.83). Dedicated devices achieved higher device success (95.8% vs 85.7%, OR 3.64; p=0.012), lower rates of residual AR >=moderate (0.6% vs 6.2%, OR 0.11; p=0.048), reduced valve embolisation (2.0% vs 7.3%, OR 0.26; p=0.048), and fewer reinterventions (2.0% vs 7.9%, OR 0.22; p=0.010). Permanent pacemaker implantation (20.8%), stroke (2.6%), and major bleeding (3.0%) were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary transfemoral TAVI for PNAR, dedicated devices demonstrated superior procedural outcomes compared with off-label devices. These findings support the preferential use of dedicated devices in this population, though randomised trials are needed to establish definite treatment recommendations.

Title: Viral Hepatitis, Potential Aflatoxin B1 Exposure, and Projected Metabolic Risk Factors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Somalia: A Call for Integrated Prevention, Surveillance, and Research.
Abstract: This commentary is a narrative synthesis of Somali, regional, and global evidence on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in Somalia; it does not report new epidemiological data, and claims are graded according to whether they are directly demonstrated in Somalia or inferred from broader African or global literature. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality globally and presents a particularly difficult challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, hepatitis C virus (HCV), food-borne aflatoxin exposure, limited surveillance, and restricted access to curative treatment intersect. Somalia has no mature population-based cancer registry, yet available hospital-based evidence indicates that liver cancer is an important component of the national cancer burden. Directly documented Somali evidence is limited to hospital case series and to donor-, hospital-, and laboratory-based HBV studies: a Somali series of 268 patients with HCC documented a predominantly male population, a relatively young mean age, large tumors, and portal-vein thrombosis associated with poor prognostic features, and recent Mogadishu studies have shown continuing HBV transmission and important gaps in vaccination, testing, and linkage to care. By contrast, the contribution of aflatoxin B1 exposure and of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to HCC in Somalia is not directly documented. No Somali biomonitoring, dietary-exposure, or MASLD-prevalence data exist; the discussion of these pathways in this commentary is therefore inferred from regional and global literature and should be read as a precautionary, hypothesis-generating projection of future risk rather than an established local driver of current disease. This commentary argues that Somalia should nonetheless not address viral, toxic, and metabolic exposures through isolated programs. An integrated, phased HCC prevention strategy should combine timely HBV birth-dose vaccination, maternal screening and antiviral prophylaxis, adult testing and treatment, HCV diagnosis and cure, precautionary food-safety surveillance for aflatoxins, metabolic-risk assessment embedded in liver care, risk-based liver ultrasound surveillance with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) used only as an adjunct, strengthened diagnostic imaging and pathology, and a national liver-cancer registry. Locally led epidemiological and implementation research, including population-attributable-fraction scenario modelling and representativeness analyses of existing hospital series, is urgently needed to quantify the relative contribution of viral, toxic, and metabolic pathways and to identify feasible models for surveillance and referral in a resource-constrained setting.

Title: Correction: Impact of left subclavian artery management on surgical efficiency and perioperative cerebral infarction in type A aortic dissection under deep hypothermic circulatory arrest: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fcvm.2026.1855005.].

Title: Vascular aging biomarkers: the role of ADMA, SDMA, and inflammation.
Abstract: Cardiovascular risk assessment based on traditional risk factors may not fully capture subclinical vascular injury and vascular aging, supporting interest in biomarkers reflecting underlying vascular mechanisms. Endothelial dysfunction, altered methylarginine metabolism, and chronic low-grade inflammation represent interconnected processes that may contribute to vascular aging. This narrative review summarizes evidence on the associations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, symmetric dimethylarginine, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with subclinical atherosclerosis and vascular aging. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched between January and August 2026, with priority given to studies evaluating associations of these biomarkers with subclinical vascular changes, vascular aging, and cardiovascular outcomes. ADMA shows the most consistent associations with subclinical atherosclerosis, although these vary across arterial territories and vascular measures. Evidence for SDMA in early vascular disease is more limited, and interpretation is complicated by its dependence on renal function, although some associations persist after adjustment for renal function. IL-6 has biological and genetic evidence supporting a role in atherogenesis, but its associations with subclinical atherosclerosis are not consistently independent of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. hsCRP is an established cardiovascular risk marker and has also been associated with progression of carotid stenosis and arterial stiffness. Differences in vascular endpoints, study populations, confounder adjustment, and analytical methods contribute to heterogeneity across studies. Overall, these biomarkers appear to reflect partly distinct but interconnected components of vascular aging. Their potential relevance may lie in their complementarity; however, current evidence does not establish that combined assessment improves evaluation beyond conventional approaches. Prospective studies should determine whether their combined assessment improves identification of accelerated vascular aging beyond conventional risk assessment.

Title: Association between low limb joint replacement with risk of peripheral arterial occlusive disease in osteoarthritis patients.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD) is a clinical manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis that is commonly associated with cerebrovascular disease and various complications. This study aimed to investigate the risk of PAOD in patients who had undergone hip or knee joint replacement.
METHODS: In this study, patients with hip or knee joint replacement were recruited from the Longitudinal Health Insurance Database 2000 (LHID 2000) and their risk of PAOD was studied.
RESULTS: A total of 10,346 patients with joint replacement and 99,597 patients without joint replacement were identified. The incidence density of PAOD in joint replacement and non-joint replacement group was 6.71 and 7.08 persons per 1,000 person-years. After adjusting for age, sex, comorbidities, antiplatelet, and anticoagulant, the HR was 0.92 (95% C.I. = 0.81-1.04). Further analysis of knee (HR = 1.23; 95% C.I. = 0.85-1.78) and hip replacement (HR = 2.05; 95% C.I. = 0.87-4.86) compared with non-joint replacement revealed that there was no significant association with peripheral arterial occlusive disease.
CONCLUSIONS: This cohort study demonstrates that undergoing hip or knee joint replacement does not significantly elevate the likelihood of peripheral arterial occlusive disease, offering reassurance regarding the vascular safety of these procedures in osteoarthritis patients.

Title: Optimal depolarization sequence for cardiac resynchronization therapy patients.
Abstract:
AIMS: Electrical ventricular dyssynchrony is a hallmark of intraventricular conduction disease in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Although cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is effective, a proportion of patients with electrical dyssynchrony evidenced by an electrocardiogram (ECG) remain non-responders. Besides the QRS duration, visualization and quantification of the depolarization sequence could contribute to improving CRT response. The study aimed to evaluate the CineECG-derived mean temporo-spatial isochrone trajectory of depolarization in CRT patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Among the adult cohort of 121 patients who underwent CRT implantation, there were 93 (33% female) responders and 28 (7% female) non-responders. ECGs recorded before and immediately after CRT implantation were collected and analysed using the CineECG modality with a generic heart/torso model. The CineECG-derived path directions were computed for the QRS on anteroposterior, interventricular, and apicobasal axes within the cardiac anatomy. Spatial depolarization characteristics were tested for the association with left ventricle reverse-remodelling at 6-month follow-up. The pre-implantation depolarization sequence was predominantly from the right to the left ventricle, and after the CRT implant, it has been transformed into an apicobasal direction. In multivariate logistic regression, the pre-implant QRS duration, apicobasal depolarization gradient, and CRT-induced QRS shortening independently predicted CRT response. The Akaike information criterion indicated that combining all three yielded the strongest predictive model.
CONCLUSION: CineECG-derived depolarization gradients, which reflect ventricular activation sequence, changed significantly after CRT, and the pre-implantation apicobasal gradient independently predicted echocardiographic outcome, with a less pronounced gradient associated with better haemodynamic response.

Title: Plasma neurofilament light chain and risk of death and stroke in community-dwelling elderly individuals.
Abstract:
AIMS: Circulating neuroinjury biomarkers such as neurofilament light chain (NFL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) have emerged as indicators of brain health. While NFL predicts stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation, its prognostic value in unselected elderly populations is uncertain. We investigated the associations of NFL and GFAP with cardiovascular events and death in community-dwelling older adults.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Baseline plasma NFL and GFAP concentrations were determined using high-sensitivity Simoa® assays in 806 participants aged 75 years from the Prospective Investigation of the Vasculature in Uppsala Seniors (PIVUS) study. Cox regression models with sequential adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, renal function, and NT-proBNP assessed associations with ischaemic stroke, myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death, all-cause death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; stroke, myocardial infarction, and all-cause death). During a median follow-up of 10 years, 55 ischaemic strokes, 48 myocardial infarctions, 52 cardiovascular deaths, and 188 all-cause deaths occurred. Neurofilament light chain was not independently associated with ischaemic stroke or myocardial infarction and showed no independent association with cardiovascular death after adjustment including NT-proBNP. In contrast, higher NFL was independently associated with all-cause death (adjusted hazard ratio per doubling 1.91; 95% CI 1.49-2.46) and MACE (1.53; 95% CI 1.21-1.93), and improved discrimination for all-cause death beyond established risk factors. Glial fibrillary acidic protein was not associated with any outcome.
CONCLUSION: In community-dwelling elderly individuals, higher NFL was associated with increased risk of death but not with specific cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that NFL reflects overall physiological vulnerability rather than discrete vascular risk.

Title: Sex-Specific Cross-Sectional Associations and Exploratory Mediation Analysis of Cardiovascular Disease Risk by Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio in Cadmium-Exposed Populations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, with its burden continuing to rise. Environmental cadmium (Cd) exposure has emerged as a potential risk factor for CVD. This study aimed to investigate the associations between Cd exposure and CVD risk, and to explore cross-sectional associations and a potential inflammatory pathway using exploratory mediation analysis.
METHODS: This study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Logistic regression models were used to identify factors influencing CVD risk. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using restricted cubic splines (RCS). Exploratory mediation analysis was conducted to assess the potential mediating role of NLR in the association between Cd exposure and CVD risk.
RESULTS: Individuals with CVD had significantly higher levels of blood Cd, urinary Cd, and NLR than controls (p < 0.05) in both sexes. In males, the highest quartile (Q4) of blood Cd (OR = 3.06, 95% CI: 1.45-6.46, p = 0.004) and urinary Cd (OR = 3.02, 95% CI: 1.52-6.02, p = 0.002) were significantly associated with higher CVD prevalence. Conversely, no significant association was observed in females for blood Cd (p = 0.505), and the association for urinary Cd (p = 0.046) was notably weaker and less robust than that in males. Interaction analyses confirmed sex-specific differences (p-interaction < 0.05). NLR showed significant exploratory mediating effects (indirect effects), accounting for 9.4% (95% CI: 3.5%-15.2%) of the blood Cd-CVD link and 5.0% (95% CI: 1.9%-8.1%) of the urinary Cd-CVD link in males. Similar significant mediation was observed in the general population for blood Cd: 7.2% (95% CI: 2.2%-12.2%), and for urinary Cd: 6.4% (95% CI: 2.8%-10.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: This cross-sectional study identified significant sex-specific and dose-dependent associations between Cd exposure and CVD risk. Inflammatory responses, particularly those reflected by elevated NLR, were cross-sectionally associated with the observed Cd-CVD link, suggesting a potential pathway that warrants prospective validation, especially in males.

Title: SGLT-2 inhibitor dapagliflozin improves left ventricular diastolic function and reduces circulating inflammatory markers in HFpEF patients: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study sought to evaluate the efficacy of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor Dapagliflozin in ameliorating left ventricular diastolic function (LVDF) and attenuating systemic inflammatory biomarkers in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
METHODS: A total of 114 patients diagnosed with HFpEF were retrospectively enrolled and allocated into either the SGLT-2 inhibitor group (Dapagliflozin combined with standard guideline-directed therapy; n = 58) or the Control group (standard guideline-directed therapy alone; n = 56). Echocardiographic parameters at baseline and 6-month follow-up were measured, including early diastolic transmitral flow velocity/early diastolic mitral annular velocity ratio (E/e') and left atrial volume index (LAVI). Circulating inflammatory markers comprising high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) were examined. In addition, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels and Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire (MLHFQ) scores were collected for functional and symptomatic assessments.
RESULTS: After six months of treatment, the SGLT-2 inhibitor group exhibited significant improvements in cardiac diastolic parameters. E/e' ratio decreased significantly from 14.8 ± 3.2 to 12.1 ± 2.7 (P < 0.001), and LAVI decreased from 38.6 ± 8.4 to 34.2 ± 7.1 mL/m2 (P = 0.003). Consistently, systemic inflammation was markedly alleviated. hs-CRP decreased from 4.82 ± 1.73 to 2.94 ± 1.28 mg/L (P < 0.001), IL-6 decreased from 8.46 ± 2.91 to 5.73 ± 2.14 pg/mL (P = 0.002), and TNF-α decreased from 12.8 ± 4.6 to 9.4 ± 3.8 pg/mL (P = 0.011). Moreover, NT-proBNP levels in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group exhibited a substantial 28.4% reduction, which was significantly greater than the 8.7% reduction observed in the Control group (P = 0.004). There was also a striking reduction in MLHFQ scores in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group (average reduction: -8.6 ± 4.2 points, P < 0.001), demonstrating significant symptomatic improvement.
CONCLUSION: SGLT-2 inhibitor Dapagliflozin effectively improved LVDF and reduced systemic inflammatory burden in patients with HFpEF. These findings support the role of Dapagliflozin as a promising disease-modifying therapeutic agent for HFpEF.

Title: Prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes of infective endocarditis in people living with HIV: A systematic review and meta-analysis of intravenous drug use and microbiological profiles.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) poses a significant challenge in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLWH), with risk factors and outcomes potentially differing from HIV-negative counterparts. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to explore the prevalence, risk factors, mortality, and clinical characteristics of IE in PLWH versus HIV-negative patients.
METHODS: Methods : Six databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Embase, and ProQuest) were searched up to January 2025 using terms including "Infective Endocarditis" and "Human Immunodeficiency Virus." Random-effects meta-analyses with Freeman-Tukey transformation were used to estimate pooled prevalence, mortality, and odds ratios (ORs) for IE by HIV status. Between-study heterogeneity (I²) and meta-regression were assessed to explore sources of variation.
RESULTS: Results : Seventeen independent studies collectively reported 3,082 IE cases (2,095 among PLWH and 987 among HIV-negative individuals), analyzed as separate study-level data rather than a single combined cohort. The pooled prevalence of IE among PLWH was 33.2% (95% CI: 14.97-54.45%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%), highlighting the exploratory nature of these estimates. Among PLWH with IE, 85.5% (95% CI: 65.8-98.1%) reported intravenous drug use (IVDU), and 60-80% had right-sided IE (predominantly tricuspid valve), contrasting with left-sided predominance in HIV-negative patients. Mortality among PLWH with IE was 14.7%, compared with 22.3% in HIV-negative individuals. Staphylococcus aureus was the leading pathogen (24-73%).
CONCLUSIONS: Given the high and persistent heterogeneity, findings should be interpreted as exploratory. PLWH with IE frequently exhibit IVDU and right-sided involvement, while mortality appears comparable to HIV-negative patients after accounting for IVDU, emphasizing behavioral rather than virologic determinants of risk.

Title: Quality of Care of Patients with Stable and Stabilized Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction at the Medical Wards of a Tertiary Center in the Philippines: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) remains a major contributor to morbidity and mortality among Filipinos. Contemporary ESC and ACC/AHA guidelines emphasize quality indicators aimed at optimizing outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the quality of care received by stable and stabilized HFrEF patients admitted to the medical wards of a tertiary center in the Philippines, focusing on physician adherence to guideline-recommended quality indicators.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was done through review of charts involving all adult HFrEF patients aged ≥19 years admitted to the medical wards of a tertiary hospital from November 2022 to April 2023. Quality-of-care assessment included prescription of Class I guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) at discharge for eligible patients, as well as non-pharmacologic indicators such as scheduling of post-discharge follow-up and referrals to a heart failure clinic or cardiac rehabilitation. Descriptive statistics were used; analyses were performed using STATA 13.1. QI of 80% was considered to be optimal quality of care.
RESULTS: A total of 148 patients were included; most were male (69.6%) with a mean age of 56 ± 14 years. Hypertension (62.8%) and diabetes (41.2%) were the most frequent comorbidities. Beta-blockers, ACEi / ARB / ARNI, and diuretic prescription were high (95.17%, 91.41%, and 100%, respectively). In contrast, prescription of MRA and SGLT2i was 68.50% and 55.56%, respectively. Post-discharge physician appointments within 4 weeks were arranged in 91.54%. Only 27.7% were referred to cardiac rehabilitation, and 2.31% were referred to the heart failure clinic.
CONCLUSION: Quality of heart failure care at the medical wards upon discharge is acceptable for pharmacologic quality indicators and post-discharge appointments. However, referrals to specialized heart failure services and cardiac rehabilitation remain suboptimal and represent opportunities for quality improvement.

Title: Severe Pulmonary Hypertension in Critically Ill Children: A 10-Year Single-Center Case Series and Practical Management Considerations.
Abstract: Severe pulmonary hypertension (PH) in children may decompensate rapidly during intercurrent illness and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). We describe the clinical presentation, intensive care management, and outcomes of four children with severe PH admitted to a tertiary PICU between January 2014 and December 2024. Three patients were infants, and one was an 11-year-old girl with a history of extreme prematurity and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. All four presented with acute respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and cardiovascular compromise following a recent respiratory tract infection. PH was documented predominantly by echocardiography, with findings including elevated estimated pulmonary pressures, right ventricular (RV) pressure overload, interventricular septal flattening, and/or RV dysfunction. Right heart catheterization was performed in one patient. All patients received supplemental oxygen, diuretics, and sildenafil. Two required invasive mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support, while one patient received additional prostanoid and endothelin receptor antagonist therapy. The median PICU length of stay was 15 days (range: 10-24 days). Two patients survived to hospital discharge, whereas two died following refractory pulmonary hypertensive crises. These cases highlight respiratory infection as an important potential precipitant of acute decompensation in children with severe PH and illustrate the challenges of supporting the failing RV in the PICU. Although the small sample size and retrospective design preclude conclusions regarding treatment efficacy or prognostic factors, the cases emphasize several practical management priorities: early recognition of deterioration, prompt correction of factors that increase pulmonary vascular resistance, preservation of RV function and systemic perfusion, cautious escalation of respiratory support, and early multidisciplinary involvement. Based on these principles and the published pediatric PH literature, we propose a practical, physiology-based management algorithm for severe PH and pulmonary hypertensive crisis in the PICU.

Title: Curative Locoregional Therapy following Objective Response to Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (Atezo-Bev) is a standard first-line systemic therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We aimed to explore the benefits of adding curative locoregional therapy (LRT) to patients who achieve a partial response (PR) to Atezo-Bev treatment.
METHODS: This multinational retrospective study enrolled patients who received Atezo-Bev as first-line systemic therapy for unresectable HCC and reached complete response (CR) or PR. Patients were categorized into three cohorts: patients who underwent curative LRT after PR, patients with PR but did not receive curative LRT, and patients achieving CR without LRT. Curative LRT included surgery, ablation, and definitive radiotherapy with imaging evidence showing disease-free status afterward.
RESULTS: A total of 243 patients were enrolled from 8 countries or regions; 31 patients received curative LRT after PR, 180 patients obtained PR but did not receive curative LRT, and 32 patients achieved CR without LRT. The curative-LRT group, compared with patients who did not receive curative LRT after PR, exhibited significantly longer PFS (median, 44.4 months vs. 18.2 months, p = 0.004) and overall survival (OS) (median, not reached vs. 34.3 months, p < 0.001). The differences remained significant after inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjustment.
