In the eligibility cascade, the single patient within the window had no absolute contraindication and could not be treated because no thrombolytic agent was available. The in-hospital mortality rate was 2 (8.7%), and a good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-2) occurred in 5 of 20 patients with an assessable score.
CONCLUSION: Non-administration of thrombolysis reflected late presentation and, above all, the complete unavailability of the thrombolytic agent, whereas imaging and organizational capacity were largely in place. Drug supply was the proximate, modifiable obstacle to reperfusion in this setting.

Title: Identification and characterization of a human antibody profile inversely associated with adverse cardiovascular events.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The immune response is linked to the progression of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD). We sought to characterize a predictive cardiovascular antibody biomarker using two independent cohorts.
APPROACH AND RESULTS: A human IgG profile serendipitously identified by ELISA was quantified in a well characterized cohort of 359 patients with a history of coronary artery disease (CAD) who experienced a total of 71 incident adverse CVD events (death, myocardial infarction, and stroke) over a median 4.1-year follow-up. Using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis, low biomarker levels were an independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular outcomes after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, estimated glomerular filtration rate, presence of obstructive CAD, heart failure, total cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol (adjusted hazard ratio of 1.90 [95% CI: 1.03-3.49; p=0.038] between lowest and highest tertiles). Validation was then performed in a larger secondary cohort using 4356 baseline samples from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), a prospective study of cardiovascular outcomes resulting in adjusted odds ratio of 50.5 per unit decrease in log-transformed biomarker [95% CI: 2.4-2773.1; p=0.030] over one year by logistic regression analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Low levels of human IgG antibodies targeting Bovidae IgG are independently associated with increased incidence of CVD events in patients with or without a history of CAD, indicating the potential clinical predictive power of this antibody profile as an inverse biomarker for CVD.

Title: Sex Differences in the Impact of Allosensitization on Waitlist Access and Post-Transplant Outcomes in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) patients are prone to HLA-antibody formation from multiple surgeries, transfusions, and prosthetic surgical material. Females with ACHD may accrue additional, non-surgical alloantigen exposure. Whether sex modifies the impact of allosensitization on heart transplant (HT) access and outcomes in ACHD remains unknown.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the OPTN/UNOS registry of adults with ACHD listed for first-time HT (2018-2025). Sensitization was defined by calculated panel reactive antibodies (cPRA) at listing. We tested the sex × sensitization (highly sensitized, cPRA >50%) interaction on transplant access using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression, treating transplantation as the event of interest and death or removal from the waitlist as competing events, and on post-transplant survival using multivariable Cox proportional-hazards regression, both adjusted for age at listing, mechanical support at listing, and the number of distinct prior cardiac surgery categories.
RESULTS: Among 856 candidates (38% female), females were more often highly sensitized than males (23% vs 14%; age-adjusted OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.26-2.61), even after adjusting for surgical burden. Sensitization reduced transplant access in females (84% to 71%; median wait 60 to 110 days, p < 0.001) but not males (79% vs 79%, median wait 88 vs 98 days). In adjusted Fine-Gray models, the subdistribution hazard for transplant was reduced in sensitized females (sHR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.72) with no effect in males (sHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.73-1.26), and the sex × sensitization interaction was significant (interaction sHR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44-0.94, p = 0.02). Post-transplant mortality was numerically higher in sensitized than non-sensitized candidates in both sexes and the sex × sensitization interaction on 1-year mortality was not significant. The sex-asymmetric effect persisted and was more pronounced in the multiorgan candidates.
CONCLUSIONS: Allosensitization is not a sex-neutral barrier to transplant in HT candidates with ACHD. Females are more sensitized and have reduced transplant access without differences in 1-year mortality. The female excess in sensitization is not accounted for by surgical burden, and the exposures responsible remain to be defined. These findings warrant a sex-aware listing strategy and further studies.

Title: Clinical Reference Percentiles for AI-derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue: A Multicenter Study.
Journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has emerged as an important cardiovascular biomarker that reflects both inflammatory and cardiometabolic risk. EAT volume and density vary significantly across populations, yet there is a lack of multicenter studies investigating the predictive value of population-specific EAT percentiles.
METHODS: In this multicenter study, we retrospectively analyzed low-dose computed tomography correction scans from 42,842 patients undergoing myocardial perfusion imaging. A derivation cohort of 15,082 patients was used to establish sex- and age-specific nomograms for EAT density and EAT volume indexed to body surface area. Percentile-based thresholds were tested for outcome prediction in a validation cohort of 27,760 patients. For clinical implementation, we developed an online EAT percentile calculator.
RESULTS: Percentile curves demonstrated increased BSA-indexed EAT volume and decreasing EAT density with age. Over a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR: 1.83 - 5.14), 4,956 patients experienced a nonfatal myocardial infarction or death. In multivariable Cox models, patients above the 95th sex- and age-specific percentile had significantly worse outcomes for BSA-indexed EAT volume [adjusted hazard ratio 1.30, 95% CI: 1.14 - 1.49, p < 0.001] and EAT density [adjusted hazard ratio 1.7, 95% CI: 1.51 - 1.92, p<0.001] when compared to patients below the 50th percentile (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Age- and sex-specific EAT percentiles provide a clinically interpretable framework for contextualizing automated EAT measurements and identifying patients at increased cardiovascular risk. EAT density was a stronger prognostic marker and identified elevated risk even among patients with normal BMI, supporting its potential to provide information beyond conventional anthropometric assessment.

Title: Menstrual cycle length trajectories and their health correlates across the reproductive lifespan.
Abstract: Although the menstrual cycle is a vital sign for women's health, research investigating menstrual cycle length (MCL) trajectories across reproductive life is scarce, often categorizing just two patterns: regular and irregular. We used latent class mixed models (LCMMs) to identify MCL trajectories among 9,332 females enrolled in the Growing Up Today Study, a United States prospective cohort followed from 1996-2023. Participants who self-reported their MCL three or more times were included in the analysis. Additional demographic and health information collected from surveys were included in the descriptive statistics, stratified by trajectory classification. The best fitting LCMM identified four MCL trajectories: "always regular" (94.2% of study population), "early long transition" (2.5%), "late long transition" (3.0%), and "long to short transition" (0.2%). Those classified in the "early long transition" trajectory had a higher proportion of adulthood obesity and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS); "late long transition" individuals had higher proportions of childhood and adulthood obesity, hirsutism, severe acne in adolescence, PMOS, hypothyroidism, hypertension, and endometriosis. The identified MCL trajectories serve as a proof of concept for identifying menstrual irregularity as a signal of disease markers warranting clinical evaluation, though further validation is needed before clinical application.

Title: TRPV1-cardiac afferent ablation after completed myocardial infarction prevents arrhythmogenic remodeling.
Journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
Abstract:
STRUCTURED ABSTRACT BACKGROUND: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias after completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited. Although TRPV1 afferent ablation at acute MI improves cardiac remodeling, the effect of delayed subacute targeting remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated whether ablating cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute post-MI window mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmias.
METHODS: Yorkshire pigs underwent sham surgery or anterior MI creation. Two weeks post-MI, animals were randomized to percutaneous epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX, for cardiac-selective TRPV1 afferent depletion) or vehicle administration. Four weeks later, terminal studies assessed the effects of RTX on cardiac structure and function, ventricular arrhythmogenesis, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling using in vivo electrophysiologic mapping, real-time neurotransmitter sensing, immunohistochemistry, and transcriptomic profiling.
RESULTS: Cardiac TRPV1 afferent depletion was confirmed by blunted responses to TRPV1 agonists. RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced end-diastolic diameter, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility. Endocardial electroanatomic mapping revealed improved VT/VF electrophysiologic correlates in RTX-treated animals, including fewer deceleration zones and late potentials. Epicardial multielectrode mapping demonstrated reduced electrophysiologic heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time release of adrenergic neurotransmitters (noradrenaline and neuropeptide Y) was normalized during sympathoexcitation in RTX-treated animals. Histologically, RTX treatment attenuated scar border zone myocardial fibrosis and sympathetic nerve sprouting, while suppressing T cell infiltration in cardiac sensory ganglia. Bulk RNA-sequencing of stellate ganglia revealed downregulation of adrenergic genes.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation post-completed MI alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural, functional, and neuro-cardiac axis remodeling. Targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents represents a promising subacute post-MI therapeutic strategy.
UNSTRUCTURED ABSTRACT: Therapies to prevent ventricular arrhythmias following completed myocardial infarction (MI) remain limited, and the impact of targeting cardiac TRPV1 afferents during the subacute phase is unknown. We evaluated whether epicardial resiniferatoxin (RTX) administration two weeks post-MI in swine mitigates structural, electrophysiological, and neuro-cardiac remodeling to suppress ventricular arrhythmogenesis. Four weeks post-treatment, RTX-treated animals exhibited improved left ventricular function, reduced chamber dilation, and suppressed ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) inducibility compared with controls. Electroanatomic and multielectrode mapping revealed fewer deceleration zones, smaller late potential areas, and reduced repolarization heterogeneity in the scar border zone. Real-time neurotransmitter sensing demonstrated normalized adrenergic release during sympathoexcitation. Histological and transcriptomic profiling showed that RTX attenuated border-zone fibrosis, decreased sympathetic nerve sprouting, suppressed sensory ganglion T-cell infiltration, and downregulated stellate ganglion adrenergic gene expression. Cardiac TRPV1 afferent ablation during the subacute post-MI window alters disease trajectory by mitigating structural and autonomic remodeling, representing a promising disease-modifying therapeutic strategy.

Title: The Role of Line-Field Confocal Optical Coherence Tomography in the Diagnosis of Melanoma and Melanocytic Lesions: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Line-field confocal optical coherence tomography (LC-OCT) is an emerging non-invasive imaging technique that provides real-time vertical, horizontal, and three-dimensional visualization of the skin at near-cellular resolution. We systematically reviewed the available evidence on LC-OCT in melanocytic lesions to identify diagnostic features associated with melanoma and to clarify its current clinical role. MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2026 in accordance with PRISMA recommendations. Thirty-two studies were included, encompassing cutaneous melanoma, lentigo maligna, and facial pigmented lesions, benign and atypical melanocytic lesions, and mucosal melanoma. Across studies, melanoma-associated findings included irregular or disorganized epidermal architecture, numerous or pleomorphic pagetoid cells, disruption or blurring of the dermoepidermal junction, atypical dermal nests, and clefting. In lentigo maligna and facial melanoma, peri-adnexal atypia and follicular involvement emerged as particularly relevant features, whereas mucosal melanoma was characterized by diffuse pagetoid spread, epithelial disarray, atypical junctional cells, and discohesive melanocytic nests. Benign lesions more often showed preserved epidermal architecture, a well-defined junction, organized nests, and a regular wave-like dermal pattern. However, substantial overlap was observed with atypical nevi, spitzoid lesions, blue nevi, melanosis, and other intermediate entities. Although selected studies reported promising diagnostic performance, the evidence remains heterogeneous and is largely based on small, descriptive cohorts. LC-OCT may therefore serve as a useful adjunct in clinically or dermoscopically equivocal melanocytic lesions, but prospective multicenter validation and assessment of reproducibility are required before widespread routine implementation.

Title: Dual Versus Mono Antiplatelet Therapy in Mild Versus Moderate Ischemic Stroke: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ATAMIS Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prespecified post hoc analysis of the ATAMIS trial (Antiplatelet Therapy in Acute Mild to Moderate Ischemic Stroke) aimed to investigate whether the benefit of dual antiplatelet therapy versus aspirin alone differs in patients with mild versus moderate stroke.
METHODS: Using data from the modified intention‑to‑treat population of the ATAMIS trial, eligible patients were divided into mild (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score 4-5) and moderate (NIHSS score 6-10) groups. The primary outcome was early neurological deterioration at 7 days, defined as an increase in the NIHSS score of ≥2 points from baseline. Safety outcomes included bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage within 90 days. Binary logistic regression, Cox regression, and generalized linear models were used as appropriate. Adjusted models included age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, onset-to-treatment time, stroke cause, and other imbalanced baseline variables. Treatment-by-baseline stroke severity interaction was assessed.
RESULTS: A total of 2915 patients were included, including 1992 (68.4%) with mild stroke and 923 (31.6%) with moderate stroke. Median age was 66 years (interquartile range, 59-73); 35.0% were women. Clopidogrel plus aspirin was associated with a significantly lower risk of early neurological deterioration compared with aspirin alone in the moderate stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.17-0.59]; P<0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed in the mild stroke group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.66-1.41]; P=0.841). A significant interaction was identified between treatment effect and NIHSS score subgroup (Pinteraction=0.003). The occurrence of bleeding events and intracranial hemorrhage was similar between treatment groups in both severity subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute mild-to-moderate ischemic stroke, the benefit of clopidogrel plus aspirin versus aspirin alone in preventing early neurological deterioration at 7 days may be greater among patients with moderate stroke (NIHSS score 6-10) than among those with mild stroke (NIHSS score 4-5), without an increased risk of bleeding. These findings suggest that baseline stroke severity may inform antiplatelet therapy selection, and warrant confirmation in future prospective studies.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02869009.

Title: Dyspnea Reduction With L-Menthol Inhalation Improves High-Intensity Endurance Running Performance in Healthy Trained Adults.
Abstract: Dyspnea occurs during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals and may limit endurance performance. Given that L-menthol inhalation can alleviate dyspnea in other contexts, we investigated whether L-menthol inhalation reduces dyspnea and improves endurance performance during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals. Nine females (mean ± standard deviation;  V ˙   O2peak = 55.8 ± 6.8 mL/kg/min) and nine males (  V ˙   O2peak = 60.3 ± 4.6 mL/kg/min) endurance runners with normal spirometry completed a randomized crossover counterbalanced trial with L-menthol inhalation or a strawberry scent (placebo). Performance was measured with a treadmill time-to-exhaustion (TTE) test at 85% of the peak velocity achieved during a preliminary cardiopulmonary exercise test. Cardiorespiratory, metabolic, and perceptual responses were measured throughout. Compared with the placebo, L-menthol inhalation reduced dyspnea across the TTE test (∼1 AU; p = 0.004) and extended the TTE test duration (406 ± 94 vs. 445 ± 106 s; p = 0.009). Pulmonary ventilation (p = 0.377), tidal volume (p = 0.298), O2 consumption (p = 0.277), CO2 production (p = 0.786), pulse O2 saturation (p = 0.766), and heart rate (p = 0.974) did not differ between conditions. Breathing frequency was lower with L-menthol inhalation than with placebo (p = 0.045). L-menthol inhalation attenuated dyspnea and enhanced high-intensity running endurance performance without substantial changes in cardiorespiratory and metabolic responses to exercise. These results suggest that dyspnea constitutes an important constraint on endurance performance during high-intensity running in healthy trained individuals, and identify acute L-menthol inhalation as an effective ergogenic strategy for this exercise modality and population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (U1111-1289-3438).

Title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Despite continuous improvements in diagnostic tools, the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is still based on electrocardiogram (ECG) and cardiac biomarkers supported by other non-invasive imaging techniques. However, ECG has limited sensitivity, while high-sensitivity troponin assays may show reduced specificity, particularly in older or multimorbid patients. Widely adopted clinical pathways (e.g. ESC 0/1 h algorithm) have reported high diagnostic discrimination in external cohorts (with AUC ranging from 0.93 to 0.96) which provides clinical context for interpreting our findings. These diagnostic tests have limitations that can be addressed through automated computer-based diagnostic systems using Artificial Intelligence (AI). Several studies in the literature have presented machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) models to quickly and accurately assess the diagnosis of AMI to optimize treatment.
METHODS AND RESULTS: The aim of our analysis was to evaluate the performance of AI-based models for the diagnosis of AMI using data from all validation and test cohorts available in literature. Sensitivity and specificity for all MIs, and for STEMI and NSTEMI separately, were analysed for different types of AI approach (non-DL or DL) and for different data sources (ECG or troponin-based). Hierarchical models were used to estimate the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity and specificity.A total of 24 studies evaluating 27 AI-based diagnostic algorithms were included encompassing 166.052 patients, of which 18.850 (11.3%) had a final diagnosis of AMI. Patients were predominantly male (61.8%) with a median age of 60.7 (IQR 59.0-64.1) years. Discrimination of AI-based algorithms for the diagnosis of AMI was high with an AUC of 0.97 (sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.92). This result remained consistent when considering the ability to diagnose STEMI (AUC 0.96, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.94) or NSTEMI (AUC 0.97, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.90) separately. No significant difference was found regarding type of AI. ECG and troponin-based models were both extremely accurate, with the first ones being less sensitive and the latter less specific.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based diagnostic algorithms for AMI diagnosis were associated with particularly efficient performance. These results were consistent for both STEMI and NSTEMI considered separately. Rather than replacing conventional diagnostic pathways, AI has the potential to enhance existing tools by identifying subtle ECG features and integrating multiple data streams. While direct head-to-head comparisons with traditional statistical models are currently limited, future prospective studies evaluating AI and conventional approaches within the same clinical populations are warranted.AI did not lose accuracy depending on the data source or the type of AI applied.

Title: Corneal Aberrations and Layer-Specific Changes in Fuchs' Dystrophy: A Scheimpflug and AS-OCT-Based Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the relationship between layer-specific corneal structural changes and optical aberrations in Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy (FECD), using Scheimpflug imaging and anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT).
SETTING: Academic tertiary referral center.
DESIGN: Prospective, cross-sectional observational study.
METHODS: A total of 130 eyes (70 FECD, 60 controls) underwent high-resolution imaging using Pentacam AXL Wave and REVO HR OCT. Parameters measured included corneal thickness, Descemet's membrane thickness, epithelial thickness, keratometry, densitometry, and wavefront aberrations. Correlation and multiple regression analyses were performed. Principal component analysis (PCA) identified major structural and optical contributors to visual quality.
RESULTS: Anterior higher-order aberrations (HOAs) significantly correlated with Kmax, anterior densitometry, and Descemet's membrane thickness. Posterior HOAs correlated with central corneal thickness and posterior densitometry. Regression models identified Kmax and trefoil components as significant predictors of posterior HOAs. PCA revealed anterior HOAs, stromal haze, and optical degradation as dominant contributors to visual decline. These features varied with FECD grade and inversely correlated with best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA).
CONCLUSIONS: Corneal aberrations in FECD are driven by layer-specific structural changes, notably anterior stromal haze and Descemet's membrane thickening. These precede clinical edema and contribute to early visual impairment. Combined AS-OCT and aberrometry improve disease staging and surgical planning.

Title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
Journal: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.
SETTING: 10 European study centers.
DESIGN: Prospective observational multicenter study.
METHODS: Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.
RESULTS: In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

Title: Caries experience in patients with coronary heart disease: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CHD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, sharing several behavioral and metabolic risk factors with dental caries. While extensive research has explored links between periodontal disease and cardiovascular health, the association between dental caries experience and coronary artery disease is less understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize existing evidence regarding dental caries burden, measured by decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), among individuals with coronary artery disease.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in April 2025 across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar. Studies published from 1966 to 2025 were eligible if they assessed adult patients with CHD, ischemic heart disease (IHD), myocardial infarction (MI), or related conditions and reported dental caries experience using the DMFT index. Observational studies, including cross-sectional, case-control, or cohort designs, were included. Duplicate records were removed using specialized software. Two independent reviewers screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, resolving discrepancies by discussion. Data extraction included study characteristics, caries indices, and key findings. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Due to heterogeneity, results were synthesized narratively.
RESULTS: From 2339 records identified, 1677 unique studies were screened, leading to 38 full-text articles reviewed for eligibility. Ultimately, 4 studies met inclusion criteria, representing populations from Iran, Sweden, Poland, and India, with sample sizes ranging from 100 to nearly 4000 participants. All studies employed either cross-sectional or case-control designs. Findings generally indicated higher mean values of DMFT among individuals with coronary artery disease, particularly for missing teeth. Some studies showed significantly greater untreated decay and tooth loss in patients with coronary artery disease compared to controls, while restorative care levels were often similar between groups. The small number of studies and their observational nature limit definitive conclusions.
CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review suggests that patients with coronary artery disease may experience a higher burden of dental caries, primarily through increased missing and decayed teeth. These findings underscore the potential shared risk environment and highlight the importance of integrating oral health within cardiovascular prevention frameworks. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship and explore whether managing caries can contribute to cardiovascular risk reduction.

Title: Early detection of emergent central apnoea in patients on positive airway pressure therapy: A five-year telemonitoring cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Treatment-emergent central sleep apnoea (TE-CSA) during positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy is recognised, yet its onset timing and contributing factors remain unclear. This study aimed to ascertain the onset time of TE-CSA via telemonitoring (TM) and identify associated factors.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 4,021 obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) patients treated with PAP and monitored via TM from 2017 to 2022 was analysed. TE-CSA was defined as a residual apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) >15 with 50% or more central events. Moreover, if the obstructive apnoea index (OAI) was > 5, patients were excluded. Patients with a central apnoea index (CAI) ≥5 at baseline were excluded. TE-CSA was categorised as transient (<12 weeks), prolonged (12-24 weeks), or persistent (>24 weeks without resolution during the follow-up period). Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed time to TE-CSA onset. A nested case-control study evaluated demographic, cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, sedative use, and PAP treatment type as risk factors.
RESULTS: TE-CSA occurred in 171 (4.3%, 95% CI: 3.7-4.9) patients, predominantly prolonged (90.6%), with transient (5.9%) and persistent (3.5%) forms. TE-CSA primarily emerged within the first 60 days of PAP therapy. Multivariate analysis identified older age (Odds Ratio (OR) = 1.03, p < 0.001) and male sex (OR = 2.35, p = 0.003) as significant predictors of TE-CSA development.
CONCLUSION: Telemonitoring detected that TE-CSA onset was most commonly identified within the first 2 months of PAP therapy. Older age and male sex are key predictors. Early detection through TM could facilitate timely interventions, although therapeutic adjustments were implemented throughout the observation period and may have influenced the temporal patterns observed.

Title: Non-cancer causes of death following cervical cancer diagnosis: a SEER database study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify non-cancer mortality after cervical cancer diagnosis and examine how these risks vary over time, by disease stage, race, and registry-recorded treatment patterns.
METHODS: We analyzed 65,852 women diagnosed with cervical cancer in Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-17 (2000-2021). Standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) compared observed deaths with age-, race-, sex-, and calendar-period-specific mortality in the U.S. general population. Fine-Gray models retained every death other than the target cause as a competing event.
RESULTS: Of 24,857 deaths, 19,975 (80.4%) were cancer-related and 4,882 (19.6%) were non-cancer-related. The overall non-cancer SMR was 1.65 (95% confidence interval [CI]=1.60-1.70). After International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage- and race-exact propensity score matching (4,506 pairs; maximum absolute standardized mean difference, 0.079), registry-inferred combined radiotherapy plus chemotherapy without surgery was not associated with overall non-cancer death (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]=1.01; 95% CI=0.88-1.16); the infectious-disease (sHR=1.72; 95% CI=0.75-3.95) and septicemia estimates (sHR=1.60; 95% CI=0.69-3.72; 23 events) were imprecise. Among 31,617 patients surviving beyond 5 years, the conditional non-cancer SMR remained elevated (1.44; 95% CI=1.38-1.49).
CONCLUSION: Non-cancer mortality remains elevated among cervical cancer survivors, including beyond the 5-year landmark. Treatment-group contrasts are strongly affected by disease stage, treatment-selection mechanisms, and unmeasured clinical factors; they should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal. Survivorship care should integrate cardiovascular, infectious, renal, respiratory, and metabolic risk management.

Title: Why early preventive check-ups matter: Unmasking subclinical abnormalities in adults aged 18-45 via systemic ultrasound phenotyping (the LUMINA score).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aim: To evaluate systemic multi-organ ultrasound phenotyping using VScan Air™ CL for detecting subclinical abnormalities in healthy adults aged 18-45 years and develop an integrated scoring system (LUMINA System) for early risk stratification.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Materials and Methods: A prospective cohort study (2010-2025) enrolled 188 clinically healthy adults with normal biochemical markers, stratified into three age groups (18-26, 27-35, 36-45 years). Standardized ultrasound assessments of liver, kidneys, carotid arteries, heart, and thyroid were performed. The LUMINA System (score range: 0-29) integrated findings across organ systems.
RESULTS: Results: Subclinical abnormalities were detected in 79.8% of participants despite normal laboratory values. Early liver steatosis occurred in 20.7%, correlating with higher BMI, triglycerides, and HOMA-IR. Increased renal echogenicity was found in 28-35% despite preserved kidney function. Carotid intima-media thickness exceeded the 75th percentile in 22.6%, with progressive vascular stiffness. Thyroid abnormalities appeared in 47.35%, suggesting autoimmune activation. Mean LUMINA scores increased from 0.44±0.31 (18-26 years) to 12.12±3.68 (27-35 years), strongly correlating with BMI (r=0.68), waist circumference (r=0.71), and HOMA-IR (r=0.54).
CONCLUSION: Conclusions: Systemic ultrasound phenotyping enables early detection of multi-organ abnormalities in young adults with normal laboratory profiles. The LUMINA System provides unified preclinical risk stratification, revealing that metabolic, vascular, and endocrine remodeling coexist years before disease onset, enhancing preventive medicine through personalized intervention.

Title: Effectiveness of Quality Improvement Strategies in Preventing Healthcare-Associated Infections Among Neurosurgical Patients Admitted to Intensive Care Units: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) remain a major and largely preventable cause of morbidity, excess mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and escalating healthcare costs in intensive care units (ICUs) worldwide. Neurosurgical patients are particularly vulnerable because of frequent exposure to invasive devices such as external ventricular drains (EVDs), central venous catheters, urinary catheters, and mechanical ventilation, combined with impaired neurological status and prolonged ICU stays. Although quality improvement (QI) strategies have been widely implemented across critical care settings, evidence specific to neurosurgical and neurocritical care populations remains fragmented.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically evaluate the effectiveness of QI interventions in reducing HAI incidence among neurosurgical and neurological ICU patients and to assess their impact on secondary outcomes including ICU length of stay, device utilization, and bundle compliance.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from January 2010 to May 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies for the primary evidence synthesis included randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, and observational cohort studies evaluating structured QI interventions for HAI prevention in neurosurgical or neurological ICU populations, or mixed ICU settings with extractable neurocritical care data. Systematic reviews identified during screening were retained for contextual interpretation and reference screening but were excluded from the primary evidence synthesis to avoid duplication of overlapping primary data. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, Cochrane RoB 2, and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale according to study design.
RESULTS: Seventeen primary studies from 14 countries met eligibility criteria and were included in the primary narrative synthesis. Three systematic reviews were retained for contextual interpretation. Structured QI interventions consistently reduced device-associated infection rates across studies. The strongest evidence was observed for EVD-specific care bundles, with EVD-related infection rates decreasing from 14.35 to 3.21 per 1,000 catheter-days following bundle implementation, and one study reporting 20 consecutive infection-free months after interprofessional bundle adoption. Device-associated infection prevention bundles also demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions, including VAP rates decreasing from 68.2 to 47.4 per 1,000 ventilator-days and CAUTI rates from 24.9 to 13.4 per 1,000 catheter-days following structured educational interventions. CLABSI rates declined substantially following standardized central venous catheter bundle implementation, reaching zero in one study with sustained monitoring. Risk of bias was predominantly low to moderate across included primary studies.
CONCLUSIONS: Structured QI interventions, particularly EVD-specific care bundles, device-associated infection prevention protocols, and staff education programs with compliance monitoring, consistently reduce HAI incidence in neurosurgical and neurological ICU settings. Although the evidence base is predominantly non-randomized, findings are directionally consistent across diverse healthcare systems and institutional contexts. Universal adoption of evidence-based infection prevention frameworks in neurocritical care is strongly supported.

Title: Albuminuria as a Clinical Marker of Subclinical Myocardial Dysfunction in Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical myocardial dysfunction is common in diabetes and may precede clinically overt heart failure by several years. Albuminuria reflects systemic microvascular injury, but its relationship with the severity of myocardial dysfunction in patients with diabetes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether adults with diabetes and albuminuria have greater echocardiographic evidence of subclinical myocardial dysfunction than those with diabetes and normoalbuminuria.
METHODS: Four electronic databases were searched from inception to March 2026 for observational studies comparing adults with diabetes and albuminuria with those with normoalbuminuria. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects models were used to pool mean differences in global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e', left ventricular mass index, e', and ejection fraction. Adjusted regression coefficients and odds ratios were also synthesized, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.
RESULTS: Eighteen reports representing 17 independent cohorts were included, with eight contributing to quantitative synthesis. Absolute GLS was significantly lower in patients with albuminuria (MD, -1.38 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.13 to -0.63; P < 0.001; I² = 82%). A greater strain deficit was observed from microalbuminuria to macroalbuminuria, although formal trend analysis was not possible. E/e' was higher in albuminuric patients (MD, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.18-2.24; P = 0.021), whereas ejection fraction did not differ. Albuminuria remained independently associated with impaired strain (pooled β = 1.06; 95% CI, 0.44-1.68) and higher odds of subclinical dysfunction (OR = 5.55; 95% CI, 3.43-8.98).
CONCLUSIONS: Albuminuria identifies patients with diabetes who have greater subclinical systolic and diastolic myocardial impairment despite preserved ejection fraction. Urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio may help identify asymptomatic patients who could benefit from deformation imaging, although prospective validation is required.

Title: Outcomes of a Multidisciplinary Endovascular Aortic Program at the Vietnam National Heart Institute: A Single-Center Observational Study of TEVAR, EVAR, and Registry Data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary aortic programs integrate advanced imaging, standardized clinical pathways, procedural expertise, and longitudinal surveillance. We evaluated the evolution and outcomes of endovascular aortic care at Vietnam National Heart Institute (VNHI), Bach Mai Hospital, using institutional TEVAR and EVAR cohorts and the prospective VNHI Aortic Registry through June 2026.
METHODS: Single-center observational report drawing on two historical institutional endovascular cohorts (TEVAR from January 2014 to December 2020, n=102; EVAR from January 2019 to August 2025, n=235) and a prospectively maintained registry (January-June 2026, n=96) in the VNHI Aortic Registry, Bach Mai hospital. Cohorts were summarized separately because enrollment periods, disease profiles, and follow-up differed. Outcomes were analyzed within each source cohort. Prespecified outcomes included technical success, perioperative mortality, major procedure-related complications, aortic remodeling, secondary reintervention, and mid-term survival.
RESULTS: Technical success was 100/102 (98.0%) TEVAR and 235/235 (100%) EVAR cases. In-hospital mortality was 3/102 (2.9%) in the dedicated TEVAR cohort; 30-day mortality was 2/235 (0.9%) in the EVAR cohort. Spinal cord ischemia occurred after TEVAR in 5/102 (4.9%) patients; all affected patients recovered before discharge following a standardized rescue protocol. Thoracic aortic coverage ≥ 270 mm was independently associated with spinal cord ischemia (odds ratio, 10.11; 95% confidence interval, 1.41-72.55; P=0.021). In the historical TEVAR source, complete false-lumen thrombosis in the covered thoracic segment was reported in 87.1% at 12 months; the imaging denominator remains to be confirmed. Estimates of long-term survival and regression-derived associations are withheld from this abstract pending verification of follow-up dates, numbers at risk, and model specifications. The 2026 registry contains 96 recorded entries but is not treated as an additional independent patient cohort until overlap is assessed. Four-year cumulative survival was 87.9% TEVAR and 84.6% EVAR; secondary reintervention occurred in 3.9% and 4.3%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: A structured multidisciplinary endovascular aortic program at VNHI was associated with high technical success and favorable mid-term outcomes in selected patients undergoing TEVAR or EVAR. These findings support the feasibility of organized aortic care in an emerging healthcare system; however, prospective risk-adjusted evaluation is required to determine the independent effect of the program on clinical outcomes. Complete patient-level reconciliation and standardized longitudinal surveillance are necessary for robust benchmarking.

Title: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR and in-hospital cardiovascular complications in patients with acute coronary syndrome without known diabetes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance measured during acute coronary syndrome (ACS) may reflect pre-existing metabolic vulnerability as well as the response to acute illness. We examined its association with cardiovascular complications arising during the index hospitalization in patients with ACS and no known diabetes.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort, 252 patients with ACS and an admission HbA1c <6.5% had fasting glucose and insulin measured 24-48 hours after admission. Insulin resistance was defined by a HOMA2-IR threshold of ≥1.35 prespecified from independent healthy controls. The composite MACE outcome comprised five prespecified complications occurring between sampling and discharge or death. Logistic and modified Poisson regression were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking, and hypertension.
RESULTS: Insulin resistance was present in 137 patients (54.4%), and the composite MACE occurred in 57 (22.6%): 28.5% with versus 15.7% without insulin resistance; risk difference 12.8 percentage points (95% CI 2.5-22.6). Insulin resistance was associated with the composite (adjusted OR 3.08, 95% CI 1.55-6.14; adjusted RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.39-3.75); each doubling of HOMA2-IR was associated with higher odds (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.09-1.99). The association persisted after GRACE adjustment (adjusted OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06) and was attenuated after adding left ventricular ejection fraction, a possible mediator (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 0.97-5.22). Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, or pulmonary edema accounted for 53 of the 57 events.
CONCLUSIONS: Acute-phase HOMA2-IR-defined insulin resistance was associated with cardiovascular complications during the index hospitalization, mainly heart-failure-related events. These findings are associational and require confirmation in multicenter cohorts.

Title: Association of Regular Yoga Practice with Metabolic and Physiological Health in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The present study aimed to examine whether regular yoga practice is associated with differences in metabolic, cardiopulmonary, cognitive, and psychological health among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
METHODS: This analytical cross-sectional study included 236 adults with T2DM, comprising 79 regular yoga practitioners and 157 non-practitioners. Anthropometric measurements, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, blood pressure, peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR), heart rate variability (HRV), Diabetic Neuropathy Score (DNS), Letter Cancellation Test (LCT), and Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21) scores were assessed using standardized procedures. Data were analyzed using the unpaired Student's t-test and Chi-square test, with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Compared with non-practitioners, participants practicing yoga demonstrated significantly lower fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, diabetic neuropathy scores, anxiety, and stress levels (P < 0.05). They also demonstrated better cognitive performance on the Letter Cancellation Test (P = 0.041).
CONCLUSIONS: Regular yoga practice was associated with better metabolic control, selected cardiopulmonary parameters, cognitive performance, and psychological well-being among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. These findings suggest a potential role for yoga as a complementary lifestyle practice; however, prospective randomized controlled studies are required to establish causality.

Title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

Title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. This research ascertains periodontitis and its correlation to autonomic dysfunction by HRV analysis.
METHODOLOGY: In total, 54 periodontitis patients were involved in the study, categorized under four groups, namely Gingivitis (n=14), Mild Periodontitis (n=13), Moderate Periodontitis (n=13), and Severe Periodontitis (n=14). Kubios HRV software version 3.5 was used for the analysis of time-domain and frequency-domain parameters of lead II ECG for HRV analysis. The indices of SNS and PNS were calculated for the assessment of autonomic balance. The correlation between the HRV parameters with the severity of periodontal disease was performed statistically.
RESULTS: The SNS index was higher in the periodontitis groups than in the gingivitis group (Gingivitis: 1.09 ± 0.60; Mild: 4.25 ± 2.4; Moderate: 3.82 ± 2.2; Severe: 4.45 ± 1.5; p < 0.001), although the pattern was not strictly progressive.
CONCLUSION: Differences in autonomic regulation, including higher SNS index and lower PNS index values, were associated with periodontal disease categories. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study lacked a healthy control group and was cross-sectional.

Title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Patients Receiving Chemotherapy: A Prospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Centre.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and locally validated thresholds for global longitudinal strain (GLS) are lacking in Vietnamese patients.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the frequency and risk factors of CTRCD in patients receiving chemotherapy, and to validate a localised GLS threshold and a biomarker-based surveillance strategy for early detection.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 235 patients at Cho Ray Hospital (September 2023-December 2025). Patients were assessed at baseline and every three months with two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (GLS), high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). CTRCD was defined by international consensus criteria. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; as the outcome was common, associations were quantified as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated by modified Poisson regression.
RESULTS: CTRCD occurred in 82 patients (34.9%). Incidence was highest with anthracyclines (41.2%) and HER2-targeted therapy (37.2%). A relative GLS reduction ≥12.1% predicted CTRCD with 73% sensitivity and 83% specificity. hs-TnT achieved a 100% negative predictive value (NPV), and combining GLS with hs-TnT in parallel retained a 100% NPV. Hypertension (RR 2.50, 95% CI 1.78-3.50), coronary artery disease (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.82-3.35) and dyslipidaemia (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.49-2.97) were associated with CTRCD. HFA-ICOS stratification was strongly predictive, with a stepwise increase in risk up to the very-high-risk category (RR 18.6, 95% CI 7.94-43.6 versus low risk; 100% event rate).
CONCLUSIONS: CTRCD affected one-third of patients. A locally validated GLS threshold combined with hs-TnT enables early, resource-efficient detection, supporting a shift from reactive to proactive cardiac surveillance.

Title: A Systematic Approach to Nontraumatic Falls: Integrating Tilt Table Testing and Amnesia Screening in Clinical Practice.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic falls in older adults pose a significant public health issue. Syncope, a temporary loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, is a frequent and often underrecognized cause of falls. Early identification of syncope is vital for effective management and fall prevention.
AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to assess the prevalence of syncope as a cause of nontraumatic falls in individuals over fifty years of age, characterize their clinical profiles, and evaluate the effectiveness of the Tilt Table Test (TTT) in diagnosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This observational study was conducted in patients over 50 years of age presenting with nontraumatic falls. Those with recent transient ischaemic attack/stroke, significant carotid stenosis, severe cardiac conditions, or inability to comply with instructions were excluded. Data collection involved a proforma covering demographics, fall characteristics, and diagnostic evaluations, including TTT and carotid sinus massage (CSM), following ESC 2018 guidelines. Statistical analysis was performed via SPSS (version 29).
RESULTS: Sixty-five participants were included, with a mean age of 68.34 ± 10.95 years; 63.1% were male. Intrinsic factors were responsible for falls in 72.3% of cases. TTT results indicated 32.7% positive results for syncope. A significant association was noted between syncope and amnesia (p=0.015).
CONCLUSION: Syncope is an overlooked cause of nontraumatic falls in elderly individuals. The TTT proved valuable in diagnosing syncope-related falls. The strong association between amnesia and syncope in our study emphasizes the need for detailed evaluation to improve outcomes and reduce the incidence of recurrent falls.

Title: Levels of Physical Activity and Ischemic Heart Disease Risk Among Adult Hospital Attendees in Mangalore. A cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of mortality globally, with physical inactivity identified as a major modifiable risk factor. There is limited data from Indian settings assessing physical activity using standardized tools and its association with ischemic heart disease (IHD) risk.
AIM: This study aimed to assess physical activity levels and examine their association with 10-year IHD risk among adults in Mangalore.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 101 patient bystanders aged 40-74 years at Government Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore. Physical activity was assessed using the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire (GPAQ), and metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week) were calculated. Participants were categorized based on WHO recommendations (≥600 MET-min/week). The 10-year IHD risk was estimated using WHO/ISH non-laboratory-based risk charts. Data were analyzed using Jamovi, and associations were tested using the Chi-square test with p<0.05 considered significant.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 48.9±7.1 years, with 58.4% males. A majority (93.1%) met WHO physical activity recommendations, with a mean activity level of 5803±2964 MET-min/week. Most participants (67.3%) had a low IHD risk (<5%), while 24.8% and 7.9% had moderate (5-<10%) and high (10-<20%) risk, respectively. A statistically significant inverse association was observed between physical activity and IHD risk (χ²=13.22, p=0.001). Among those meeting activity recommendations, 71.3% had low IHD risk, compared to only 14.3% among those not meeting recommendations.
CONCLUSIONS: Adequate physical activity is strongly associated with lower IHD risk. Promoting active lifestyles and integrating routine risk assessment using standardized tools can play a crucial role in reducing cardiovascular disease burden in similar populations.

Title: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery versus Thoracotomy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Survival Analysis and Exploratory Predictive Modelling.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component.
METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded.
RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology.
CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Observational Study

Title: Risk factors associated with rapid progression of chronic kidney disease. A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of various risk factors with rapid progression of chronic kidney disease.
METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted in CKD patients admitted in a tertiary care hospital between January 2018 to December 2020 with a minimum follow up of one year. Variables including age, sex, hemoglobin, uric acid, serum creatinine, eGFR, proteinuria, presence of AKI and other comorbidities were recorded at baseline. The primary outcome was association of various risk factors with rapid progression of CKD (sustained decline in eGFR of more than 5 ml/min/1.73 m2 /yr.). Each potential risk factor was first evaluated using univariate logistic regression with rapid CKD progression as the dependent variable. Variables with p<0.2 and clinically important variables were taken for multivariate analysis to identify independent predictors.
RESULTS: A total of 993 patients were included in study. Of these 442 (43.5%) were having rapid progression of CKD. Risk factors independently associated with rapid progression of CKD included presence of AKI (OR=1.589, CI= 1.092-2.311, p=0.015), baseline eGFR (OR=1.043, CI= 1.031-1.054, <0.01) and anemia (OR=1.805, CI= 1.178-2.766, p=0.007). Additionally, HbA1c (OR= 1.035, P=0.383), hypertension (OR= 1.258, P= 0.352), proteinuria (OR= 1.242, P= 0.243) and retinopathy (OR= 1.234, P= 0.291) showed a higher odd of rapid CKD progression in multivariable analysis, but the associations did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: This study identified presence of AKI, level of baseline eGFR and anemia as risk factors significantly associated with rapid CKD progression.

Title: Myocardial remodelling during sacubitril/valsartan therapy in patients with chronic heart failure.
Abstract: The aim of the study was to identify differences between aliskiren and sacubitril/valsartan in their ability to influence cardiac remodelling, metabolic balance, neurohumoral activation, and clinical symptom severity. A comparative assessment of the clinical effectiveness and impact on the structural and functional state of the myocardium was conducted for two therapeutic strategies in patients with chronic heart failure in Georgia over a 12-month follow-up. The results demonstrated fundamentally different trajectories of therapeutic response. In the sacubitril/valsartan group, early clinical improvement was observed by 6 months, including significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (-6.2%, p<0.001), respiratory rate (-4.5%, p<0.001), and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (-10.0%, p<0.05), along with improved oxygen saturation (+3.5%, p<0.001). Left ventricular ejection fraction increased significantly already at 6 months (from 34.2±4.7% to 37.4±4.0%, p<0.001) and further at 12 months (40.5±3.5%, p<0.001), accompanied by rapid improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, with 9.3% of patients achieving New York Heart Association I by study end. In contrast, the aliskiren group exhibited slower but more pronounced structural reverse remodelling. Significant reductions in left ventricular end-systolic volume (-15.8%, p=0.009), end-diastolic volume (-17.6%, p=0.016), and end-systolic diameter (p=0.002) were observed only at 12 months, along with a modest but significant increase in ejection fraction (p=0.030). Regression of functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation and a significant decrease in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (-19.7%, p<0.05) were more prominent in this group. Both therapies led to significant improvements in carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, including reductions in glycated haemoglobin, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and triglycerides (p<0.05 for all), indicating a favourable systemic metabolic effect. Overall, findings suggest that sacubitril/valsartan may be preferable when rapid clinical stabilization is required, whereas aliskiren may represent an effective therapeutic option for patients with advanced structural cardiac remodelling.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Randomized Controlled Trial; Clinical Trial

Title: Effect of Facilitated Tucking on Procedural Pain During Heel Prick in Late Preterm Neonates: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preterm neonates frequently undergo painful procedures such as heel pricks, which can adversely affect physiological stability and neurodevelopment. Non-pharmacological interventions like facilitated tucking may help reduce procedural pain. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of facilitated tucking on procedural pain during heel prick in late preterm neonates.
METHODS: This quasi-experimental study was carried out among 100 late preterm neonates (34 to < 37 weeks) admitted to a tertiary care hospital. Neonates were allocated into two groups: routine heel prick (n=50) and facilitated tucking (n=50) groups using alternate allocation. We assessed the pain using the Premature Infant Pain Profile-Revised (PIPP-R) score at 30 seconds post-procedure along with heart rate and oxygen saturation monitoring. We analyzed the data using the Mann-Whitney U test and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), with effect sizes reported as partial eta squared (partial η²) for ANCOVA analyses.
RESULTS: The facilitated tucking group demonstrated significantly lower pain scores compared to the routine care group (median PIPP-R score 4.00 vs. 9.00, p < 0.001). Neonates who underwent facilitated tucking showed a smaller rise in heart rate and less reduction in oxygen saturation following the procedure, indicating better physiological stability.
CONCLUSION: Facilitated tucking was associated with lower procedural pain scores and better physiological stability during heel prick in late preterm neonates. It may offer a simple non-pharmacological approach to procedural pain management, although these findings need confirmation in randomized studies.

Title: Secondary Intervention Burden After Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Patient-Level and Procedure-Level Analysis of a 14-Year Single-Center Experience.
Journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify the patient-level and procedure-level burden, concentration, timing, and characteristics of secondary interventions after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR), and their association with subsequent mortality.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 189 consecutive patients treated with FEVAR between 2007 and 2021. Secondary interventions were classified by clinical magnitude, approach, timing, and primary indication. The cumulative incidence of a first secondary intervention was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method with death as a competing event. The association with subsequent mortality was assessed using a time-dependent Cox model.
RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 185 of 189 patients (97.9%). Median observed follow-up was 40.9 months (interquartile range, 25.1-61.2), and median potential follow-up was 57.4 months. Forty-eight patients (25.4%) underwent 67 secondary procedures. Nine patients, representing 4.8% of the cohort, underwent repeated interventions and accounted for 28 procedures (41.8%). Of the 67 procedures, 25 (37.3%) were major, 42 (62.7%) were minor, and 52 (77.6%) were endovascular. Thirty-seven procedures (55.2%) occurred more than 1 year after FEVAR. The 48-month cumulative incidence of a first secondary intervention was 24.7%, compared with 27.0% using 1 minus Kaplan-Meier. At the last available imaging examination, 610 of 615 assessable fenestrated target vessels were patent (99.2%). Secondary intervention was not statistically associated with subsequent mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.11; 95% confidence interval, 0.68-1.80; P = .687).
CONCLUSION: Secondary interventions affected approximately one quarter of patients after FEVAR, but a small subgroup accounted for a disproportionate share of the procedural burden. Most procedures were minor and endovascular, and more than half occurred beyond 1 year. No statistically significant average association with subsequent mortality was identified. Reporting both patient- and procedure-level burden may better characterize FEVAR durability and follow-up requirements.Clinical ImpactSecondary interventions after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) are commonly reported as the proportion of patients undergoing at least 1 procedure, which does not capture cumulative procedural burden. In this cohort of 189 patients, 48 underwent 67 secondary interventions, whereas only 9 patients, representing 4.8% of the cohort, accounted for 41.8% of all procedures. Most interventions were minor and endovascular, but more than half occurred beyond 1 year. These findings indicate that first reintervention rates alone incompletely describe FEVAR durability. Reporting both patient- and procedure-level burden may better inform patient counseling, surveillance planning, and comparisons across devices and centers by highlighting the concentration of procedures in a small subgroup.

Title: Deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound images and clinical-ultrasound texts for differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a deep learning multimodal fusion model based on ultrasound (US) images and clinical-US texts to differentiate benign and malignant renal tumors.
METHODS: The retrospective dataset from January 2012 to February 2023 in a tertiary hospital was used for model development and randomly allocated to training and validation sets. An independent prospective test set was obtained from March 2023 to October 2024. We developed Model-G using grayscale US (GUS) images, Model-GC using GUS and color Doppler flow imaging images, Model-T using clinical-US texts, and Model-UT using US images and clinical-US texts. ResNet50 was used for image feature extraction, BERT for text encoding, and ViT for multimodal classification.
RESULTS: In total, 1008 patients (740 in training set, 186 validation set, and 82 prospective test set) with a single renal tumor were included. In the validation set, Model-UT achieved the highest diagnostic performance in comparison to Model-G, Model-GC, and Model-T with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.86-0.93) (all p-values < 0.05). In the prospective test set, Model-UT yielded an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.97), outperforming high-level, mid-level, and low-level radiologists (all p-values < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The multimodal fusion model presents promising potential in differentiating benign and malignant renal tumors.
ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Deep learning model integrating US images with clinical-US texts improved benign-versus-malignant renal tumor differentiation. Decision-curve, controlled ablation, and SHAP analyses support its potential use as a clinical decision-support tool.

Title: Standard Prenatal Ultrasound Markers Associated With MRI-Only Central Nervous System Abnormalities in Fetal Ventriculomegaly.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify standard prenatal ultrasound markers associated with central nervous system abnormalities detected only by fetal MRI in fetuses with ventriculomegaly considered apparently isolated on standard prenatal ultrasound.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 199 singleton pregnancies with fetal ventriculomegaly evaluated by standard prenatal ultrasound and fetal MRI within 72 h. Dedicated fetal neurosonography was not routinely performed. Ventriculomegaly severity was classified according to the maximum lateral ventricular atrial width. Among fetuses without additional central nervous system abnormalities on standard prenatal ultrasound, cases with and without MRI-only abnormalities were compared. Ultrasound-based markers were assessed using exploratory logistic regression, and the discriminatory ability of initial ventricular width was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: Among 183 fetuses considered apparently isolated on standard prenatal ultrasound, fetal MRI detected additional central nervous system abnormalities in 19 cases (10.4%). In the exploratory multivariable model, greater ultrasound-defined ventriculomegaly severity was associated with MRI-only abnormalities (OR, 2.947; 95% CI, 1.375-6.313), and interval ventricular progression showed a stronger association (OR, 25.217; 95% CI, 6.496-97.895). Initial ventricular width showed exploratory discriminatory ability, with different performance in early-onset and late-onset cases.
CONCLUSIONS: In fetuses with ventriculomegaly considered apparently isolated on standard prenatal ultrasound, greater ventriculomegaly severity and interval ventricular progression were associated with additional CNS abnormalities detected by fetal MRI. These findings support risk-stratified consideration of fetal MRI after standard prenatal ultrasound but should not be extrapolated to fetuses evaluated with dedicated fetal neurosonography. The ventricular-width thresholds identified in this cohort should be considered exploratory.

Title: Taiwan GEST-TASL-TMASO Joint Position Statement in Managing Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Obesity.
Journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and obesity share common pathogenesis and are increasingly relevant in clinical care. This joint statement addresses the need for comprehensive guidance in Taiwan for MASLD patients with obesity. The Gastroenterological Society of Taiwan, the Taiwan Association for the Study of the Liver, and the Taiwan Medical Association for the Study of Obesity conducted an evidence-based review, integrating epidemiological data, clinical trial outcomes, and expert consensus to develop position statements covering diagnosis, disease burden, pathogenesis, surveillance, and therapeutic strategies. MASLD prevalence in Taiwanese adults is 30%-45%, reaching 60%-70% in individuals with obesity, with similar high prevalence in children and adolescents. Obesity accelerates hepatic and extrahepatic disease progression, including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and cardiovascular complications. Lifestyle interventions, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, resmetirom, and bariatric surgery demonstrate efficacy in improving hepatic and metabolic outcomes. Risk stratification using noninvasive tools such as Fibrosis-4 and vibration-controlled transient elastography effectively guides referral and management. A multidisciplinary, precision-based approach, integrating lifestyle modification, pharmacotherapy, surgical options, and risk stratification, is essential for effective MASLD management in patients with obesity, while research into artificial intelligence-driven biomarkers, gut microbiota modulation, and genetic factors represents future directions.

Title: Association of Risk-Stratified WeChat-Based Tele-Nursing With Self-Care Outcomes and Short-Term Readmission Among Patients With Chronic Heart Failure: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is frequently complicated by post-discharge readmission. This study evaluated structured risk-stratified WeChat-based tele-nursing in routine post-discharge care. This retrospective cohort study included 112 patients with CHF hospitalized during 2023-2024; 58 received tele-nursing and 54 routine follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed. The primary outcome was 6-month heart failure-related readmission. Six-month readmission occurred in 13.8% versus 31.5% in the unmatched cohort (p = 0.02) and 15.2% versus 32.6% after 1:1 PSM (46 pairs; p = 0.04). The unmatched adjusted Cox estimate was HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.18-0.99), whereas the matched Cox estimate was HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.18-1.08); penalized, complete-case, and Fine-Gray sensitivity analyses were also not statistically significant. The exploratory 12-month HR was 0.55 (95% CI 0.30-1.02; n = 94). All three SCHFI v7.2-C subscales improved more with tele-nursing (all p < 0.001). Tele-nursing was associated with greater improvement in patient-reported self-care and a possible association with lower short-term readmission, which requires prospective confirmation.

Title: BCG Scar Reactivation (BCGitis) in Kawasaki Disease: A Scoping Literature Review.
Journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) scar reactivation (BCGitis) is a distinctive clinical sign reported in Kawasaki disease (KD), yet evidence remains scarce across the literature. We aimed to summarize the epidemiology, chronology, clinical correlates, and coronary outcomes associated with BCGitis in KD.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of studies describing BCGitis in KD. Data were synthesized descriptively across retrospective cohorts and case reports/series.
RESULTS: Forty studies published between 1997 and 2024 were included (10 retrospective cohorts; 30 reports of 36 cases). BCGitis was most frequently described in infants and young children (< 2 years, often < 6-12 months) and was commonly associated with earlier recognition and treatment. Reported BCGitis prevalence varied across cohorts, from 11.8% to 49.9%. Coronary artery lesions (CAL) and IVIG resistance were reported at lower rates in some cohorts; however, these findings were not statistically significant. In the case reports, most patients were infants, male predominance was observed, and incomplete KD was frequent. BCGitis was often reported during the early febrile phase, sometimes preceding complete KD diagnostic criteria. Most reported cases responded to IVIG. Coronary abnormalities were usually mild or transient, although two giant aneurysms, one case of Kawasaki disease shock syndrome, and one mortality were reported.
CONCLUSIONS: BCGitis may support earlier recognition of KD, particularly in incomplete presentations, potentially facilitating timely recognition and treatment. Incorporation of BCGitis into diagnostic algorithms may improve patient outcomes. Future studies should standardize reporting of BCGitis chronology, coronary outcomes, and evaluate the incremental diagnostic value of BCGitis in prospective cohorts.

Title: [Non-pharmacological management of chronic heart failure].
Abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) requires precise diagnosis and management combining pharmacological treatments and non-pharmacological interventions. Although their level of evidence remains variable, their place in the management of CHF is now well established. This article summarises data on the main non-pharmacological interventions in patients with stable CHF. Current data remain insufficient to justify systematic fluid restriction, while moderate sodium restriction proves preferable to strict restriction. Structured therapeutic education, exercise-based rehabilitation programs, and multidisciplinary management improve quality of life, reduce hospitalizations and, for certain interventions, mortality.
Publication Types: English Abstract; Journal Article; Practice Guideline

Title: Bridging Thrombolysis Versus Direct Endovascular Thrombectomy in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients With ASPECTS ≤5: A Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by large vessel occlusion (LVO). However, the efficacy and safety of bridging thrombolysis (BT) compared to direct EVT (dEVT) remain controversial, particularly in patients with large core infarcts (Alberta stroke program early CT score [ASPECTS] ≤5). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of BT versus dEVT in this population.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from January 1, 2010, to September 21, 2024, for studies comparing BT and dEVT in AIS patients with ASPECTS ≤5. Outcomes included functional outcomes (mRS 0-2 and 0-3), intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), symptomatic ICH (sICH), 90-day mortality, and successful reperfusion. Data were pooled using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Twelve studies (3907 patients) were included. BT significantly improved favorable (OR: 1.43, 95% CI: 1.17-1.76) and moderate functional outcomes (OR: 1.28, 95% CI: 1.10-1.48) compared to dEVT. No significant differences were observed in sICH, ICH, 90-day mortality, or successful reperfusion.
