This study extends prior work by showing that a longitudinal measure of neonatal whole-brain network development, rather than a single imaging timepoint, predicts neurodevelopment across multiple domains. These findings identify early network development as a potential biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk and resilience, and support future risk-stratification and intervention studies in this population.

Title: Fish intake and mortality in Japan, a high fish-consuming country: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies.
Abstract: Fish consumption has been linked to decreased mortality risk in several prospective studies. However, most existing evidence is based on multi-regional analyses, and the dose-response relationship in populations with high habitual fish intake remains insufficiently characterised. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies among Japanese adults to assess the associations between fish consumption and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to investigate potential dose-response relationships in a high-fish-intake population. We systematically searched the MEDLINE and Ichushi-Web databases. Prospective cohort studies conducted in Japan that reported hazard ratios or relative risks for fish intake and mortality outcomes were included. The protocol was registered a priori in the PROSPERO database (CRD42025635066). Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled estimates by comparing the highest and lowest intake categories. Dose-response relationships were evaluated using generalised least-squares trend estimation and restricted cubic spline models. A total of 113 articles were assessed for eligibility, and 16 studies met the inclusion criteria, and nine were eligible for meta-analysis. Higher fish intake was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.98) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.80-0.91), with low heterogeneity. According to the GRADE framework, the certainty of evidence was rated low. Visual inspection suggested that mortality risk reduced with increasing fish intake up to approximately 100 g/day, after which the decline slowed, implying a plateau effect at higher intake levels. Among Japanese adults, high fish consumption was associated with a lower risk of all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality. Further research is required to clarify the dose-response relationship in populations with high fish consumption.

Title: Impact of extramedullary plasmacytoma on outcomes in patients with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma treated with talquetamab: U.S. Myeloma Immunotherapy Consortium.
Abstract: Talquetamab, a GPRC5D-targeting bispecific antibody, shows promising activity in relapsed-refractory multiple myeloma. However, real-world outcomes in patients with extramedullary disease (EMD) remain poorly described. We studied 360 patients treated with talquetamab at 15 U.S. centers by Dec 2024. Soft tissue plasmacytomas (STP) were classified as EMD (not contiguous with bone) or paraskeletal disease (PSD; contiguous with bone). If both were present, patients were assigned to the EMD category. Of those, 97 (27%) had EMD, 22 (6%) had PSD, and 241 (67%) had No-STP. Median follow-up was 12.8 months. Overall response rates were 68% in EMD, 63% in PSD, and 65% in No-STP (p = 0.8). Median progression-free survival was 4.3, 4.5, and 7.8 months, respectively (p = 0.009), and median overall survival was 10.3 months, 13.0 months, and not reached (p = 0.070). These findings demonstrate that EMD and PSD are associated with preserved response rates but shorter PFS and OS with talquetamab. While systemic markers of tumor burden and inflammation-particularly lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and ferritin-emerged as independent predictors of inferior PFS, elevated LDH also retained independent prognostic significance for OS. While EMD was associated with shorter PFS and OS on univariate analysis, it did not retain independent prognostic significance on multivariable analysis, suggesting that inferior outcomes are driven by aggressive disease biology rather than by lesion anatomy alone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. Talquetamab retains clinical utility in this high-risk population with EMD, though outcomes are suboptimal with a need for further refinement of treatment approaches.

Title: Comparison of Data-Driven Phenotyping Systems for metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Implications for Treatment Response.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although emerging classification systems address the pathophysiological heterogeneity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the implications of these subtypes for treatment responses remain unclear. We systematically evaluated three phenotyping frameworks for stratifying responses to lifestyle management.
METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 618 patients with MASLD who received 48 weeks of guideline-based lifestyle management. The classification systems assessed were metabolic clusters-mild obesity/dyslipidemia-associated MASLD (MODM), age-related MASLD (AM), severe insulin resistance-associated MASLD, high lipoprotein(a)-associated MASLD (HLPAM), and severe mixed hyperlipidemia-associated MASLD (SMHLM); hepatic and cardiometabolic traits (control, liver-specific, and cardiometabolic); and biochemical patterns (hepatocellular, mixed, and cholestatic). The primary endpoints were responses in magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) (≥30% relative liver fat reduction), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (≥17 IU/L decrease), and liver stiffness measurements (LSM) (≥1-stage improvement in the LSM-defined fibrosis stage).
RESULTS: Metabolic clusters demonstrated significantly greater temporal stability than the hepatic and cardiometabolic trait and biochemical pattern systems (62.8% vs. 56.6% vs. 53.4%, P=0.003). The HLPAM cluster demonstrated an attenuated MRI-PDFF response (odds ratio [OR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.79), while the AM cluster showed a lower ALT response (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.18 to 0.62), and the MODM cluster displayed a superior LSM response compared to the others (all P<0.05). Moreover, the liver-specific cluster showed better MRI-PDFF, ALT, and LSM responses than the control cluster. However, biochemical patterns selectively stratified ALT responses, with the hepatocellular pattern demonstrating a greater response than the mixed and cholestatic patterns.
CONCLUSION: Metabolic cluster-based MASLD subtypes exhibited differential responses to lifestyle management, supporting the integration of metabolic subtyping into clinical algorithms to optimize management.

Title: The Impact of Postoperative Mechanical Ventilation Duration on Visual and Auditory Hallucinations After Cardiac Surgery: Insights from the VAACS Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether postoperative mechanical ventilation duration is associated with the risk and timing of visual and auditory hallucinations after adult cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Prospective multicenter cohort study.
SETTING: Ten major cardiac surgery centers in the West Bank, Palestine.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 1,332 adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting or valve surgery, stratified by postoperative ventilation duration: ≤6 hours or >6 hours.
INTERVENTIONS: No experimental intervention was performed; patients were grouped by early versus delayed postoperative extubation.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Visual and auditory hallucinations were assessed during the first 7 postoperative days using the Questionnaire for Psychotic Experiences. Cox regression and restricted mean survival time analyses evaluated associations between ventilation duration and hallucination outcomes. Delayed extubation (>6 hours) was associated with lower overall adjusted risk of visual hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.62-0.80; p < .001) and auditory hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% confidence interval, 0.31-0.77; p = .002). However, time-varying analysis showed increased immediate postoperative hazard in the delayed-extubation group, with risk declining rapidly over time. Restricted mean survival time analysis showed that auditory hallucination-free time was approximately 0.24 days shorter in patients with delayed extubation (p < .001). Preoperative white blood cell count was the most consistent predictor.
CONCLUSION: Delayed postoperative extubation was associated with lower overall 7-day hallucination risk but higher immediate postoperative vulnerability, suggesting that the early postextubation period may represent a critical window for targeted monitoring and preventive neuropsychiatric care after cardiac surgery.

Title: A Prospective Evaluation of Right Ventricular Function in High- and Low-Flow Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia

Title: Indocyanine green dosing and imaging conditions for intraoperative fluorescence assessment during coronary artery bypass grafting: A systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative indocyanine green fluorescence is used to assess graft filling and myocardial perfusion during coronary artery bypass grafting, although dosing and imaging protocols vary. This review evaluated dose, imaging conditions, visualization, technical abnormality detection, revision, quantitative perfusion, and safety.
METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, CINAHL Plus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched. Three reviewers selected studies and extracted data. Overlapping reports were reconciled into clusters. Doses were normalized to milligrams per injection. Risk of bias was assessed with design-appropriate instruments and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework. Findings were synthesized by application and imaging method.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven reports represented 20 clusters. Fluorescence appeared within 2-20 seconds. Fluorescence was detected in 525 of 533 conduits, and 379 of 507 grafts were fully analyzable. Indocyanine green findings prompted correction or revision in 5 of 348 conduits and 6 of 289, 8 of 533, and 4 of 107 grafts, with restored fluorescence or confirmed patency after intervention. In 139 grafts assessed against angiography, indocyanine green identified stenosis or occlusion with 83.3% sensitivity and 100% specificity. One randomized study reported normal indocyanine green findings in all 8 grafts meeting combined revision criteria. Quantitative fluorescence identified reduced intensity in 5 of 6 graft failures. Perfusion thresholds were met in 275 of 359 and 63 of 75 myocardial territories. Fixed doses ranged from 0.0125 to 6.25 mg per injection, without direct evidence defining an optimal regimen.
CONCLUSION: Indocyanine green fluorescence supports rapid visualization of graft filling and may assist intraoperative reassessment during coronary artery bypass grafting. This review defines the reported dose range and identifies the exposure, acquisition, outcome, and safety variables required for more consistent comparison and interpretation.

Title: Electrocardiogram Embeddings Beyond Chronological Age for Prediagnostic Cognitive Impairment and Dementia: Development and External Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dementia is a growing health burden worldwide; however, scalable, low-cost strategies for early risk identification are lacking. Because cardiac and cognitive aging are closely associated, a routinely collected 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), interpreted using foundation model embeddings, is a promising and accessible candidate marker. However, it is unclear whether such embeddings carry predictive information independent of chronological age-the dominant risk factor for dementia-and whether the underlying changes follow a detectable prediagnostic trajectory.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate whether foundation model embeddings of routine ECGs carry information that distinguishes patients later diagnosed with cognitive impairment or dementia from matched controls, beyond chronological age, and, if so, whether the underlying ECG changes intensify as diagnosis approaches.
METHODS: In a retrospective two-site Korean cohort (Severance Hospital, development n=52,355; Yongin Severance Hospital, external n=6500), embeddings from the knowledge-enhanced diagnosis foundation model supported an ECG-only classifier that discriminated patients diagnosed with cognitive impairment or dementia within the following 10 years from matched controls, using only ECGs interpreted as normal sinus rhythm. We compared an age-only model with a late fusion of age and ECG-derived probability and tested whether age-residualized embedding is predictive as direct evidence of age-independent information. Discrimination was summarized by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with 95% bootstrap CIs, and DeLong tests and net reclassification improvement (NRI) were used for between-model comparisons. To trace the prediagnostic time course, we analyzed ECG phenotype labels across four windows before diagnosis in an exact-age-matched case-control set.
RESULTS: Chronological age strongly discriminated cases from controls in both cohorts (external AUROC 0.809, 95% CI 0.799-0.819). Adding ECG-derived probability improved discrimination, calibration, and net benefit over age alone (external AUROC 0.825, 95% CI 0.816-0.834; DeLong P<.001; positive NRI). Critically, even after removing the age-predictable component, age-residualized embedding retained modest but reproducible discrimination in both internal (AUROC 0.590, 95% CI 0.581-0.599) and external (AUROC 0.579, 95% CI 0.567-0.592) validation (both P<.001), indicating dementia-relevant information that was not explained by chronological age. Of the 105 ECG labels, 19 (18.1%) showed a case-control difference that widened significantly toward diagnosis, dominated by nonspecific ST segment and T wave changes, acute ischemic patterns (acute myocardial infarction), and atrial and junctional arrhythmias (atrial flutter, ectopic atrial, and accelerated junctional rhythms), with divergence emerging mainly in the proximal (1-3-year) and imminent (0-1-year) windows.
CONCLUSIONS: Routine ECG foundation model embeddings encode aging-related electrophysiological information that is complementary to and not fully explained by chronological age and intensifies as diagnosis approaches, with concurrent shifts toward ischemic and arrhythmic ECG patterns whose mechanism cannot be determined from these data. These findings suggest that routine ECG is a low-cost, age-complementary triage signal for cognitive impairment and dementia screening, rather than a stand-alone diagnostic test.

Title: Clinical triage concordance of a point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I assay using the ESC 0/1-hour algorithm.
Journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) assays have demonstrated good analytical agreement with central laboratory (CL) testing, it remains uncertain whether they yield the same clinical triage decisions. We evaluated the clinical concordance of a POC hs-cTnI assay with a CL assay using the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 0/1-h algorithm.
METHODS: This prospective diagnostic agreement study included 127 patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected acute coronary syndrome. The primary outcome was concordance of patient classification according to the 0/1-h algorithm, assessed using the quadratic weighted kappa (κ) statistic. Secondary outcomes included quantitative agreement assessed by the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis, and analytical comparability between whole blood and plasma on the POC platform.
RESULTS: Overall, 114/127 patients (89.8%) were assigned to the same triage category (κ = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.878-0.964). All 13 discordant classifications (10.2%) occurred between adjacent categories, with no CL rule-in patient classified as POC rule-out. Quantitative agreement between assays was good (ICC = 0.882; 95%CI 0.835-0.917), with a mean bias of -5.27 ng/L. Whole blood and plasma showed close agreement (ICC = 0.999; 95%CI 0.998-0.999), with a mean bias of 0.50 ng/L.
CONCLUSIONS: The POC assay showed high clinical concordance with CL-based ESC 0/1-h triage classification, with all discordances confined to adjacent categories. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of POC hs-cTnI testing under routine bedside conditions.

Title: Cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks of sex hormone therapy: from contraception to transgender care.
Abstract: The risk of venous thromboembolism is increased with combined oral contraceptives, rises with the dose of ethinylestradiol, and is higher with desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone or cyproterone acetate than with levonorgestrel; the determinant is not the generation of the pill but the residual androgen-receptor activity of the progestin, which modulates the hepatic effect of the estrogen. Age over 35 years, obesity, smoking and a family history of thrombosis amplify it. Pills based on a native estrogen have a more limited hepatic impact and rank below most ethinylestradiol combinations in contemporary cohorts, but their clinical safety is not demonstrated and no comparative outcome data exist for estetrol/drospirenone. Androgenicity is not a general marker of venous safety: injectable depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, given alone at supraphysiological doses, carries an increased risk. Myocardial infarction and stroke are also more frequent, but against a very low background - about 21 additional strokes and 10 additional infarctions per 100,000 person-years, four times fewer than the venous excess - and, unlike venous events, independent of progestin type. Menopause hormone therapy increases venous thromboembolic risk, especially in the first year; the route of administration is the main determinant, transdermal estradiol with micronized progesterone appearing safest. In cisgender men, testosterone deficiency carries increased cardiovascular risk, and randomized and real-world data support the safety of transdermal replacement, although more pulmonary embolism and atrial fibrillation have been observed. In trans women, observational data show an increased risk of stroke and venous thromboembolism, particularly with oral estradiol and cyproterone acetate, whereas recent large-scale data show no excess of major cardiovascular events with testosterone in trans men. The practical consequences are specific: no combined pill is acceptable after a venous thromboembolic event, with a thrombogenic mutation or with migraine with aura, native-estrogen pills included; transdermal estradiol should be preferred for menopause and feminising hormone therapy; and haematocrit should guide the dose and route of testosterone.

Title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with REML estimation of between-study variance (ORs); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI).
RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (8 studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

Title: Acute Limb Ischemia: Medicare and Medicaid Reimbursement Gaps Threaten Sustainability of Care.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a vascular emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial resource utilization. However, contemporary data evaluating the financial sustainability of ALI care across insurance types remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate hospitalization costs, reimbursement, profitability, and contribution margin for operative ALI care stratified by insurance status and revascularization strategy.
METHODS: A retrospective review of patients admitted with ALI at a quaternary medical center (2016-2024) was performed. Patients were identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes. Exclusion criteria were outpatient encounters and non-operative or non-procedural management. Hospitalization cost was defined as the sum of variable and fixed costs. Profit was reimbursement minus cost. Analyses were stratified by insurance status and treatment modality. Continuous variables were compared using nonparametric tests, with statistical significance set at p<0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 565 patients were included, of whom 60.2% were insured by Medicare, 24.2% by Medicaid, and 15.6% by commercial insurance. Median total hospitalization costs exceeded $50,000 per admission and did not differ by insurance status (Medicare $50,894 [IQR $33,496-$90,923], Medicaid $49,417 [$33,775-$83,379], commercial $56,603 [$35,823-$96,067]; p=0.577) or by revascularization strategy (open vs endovascular; p>0.05). Professional and technical cost components were similarly comparable across payer groups. Despite similar costs, reimbursement varied significantly by insurance status. Medicare and Medicaid admissions were associated with median hospital losses of -$12,673 [-$28,732 to -$1,425] and -$3,176 [-$10,035 to $3,859], respectively, while commercially insured admissions generated a median profit of $30,622 [$7,602-$50,208] (p<0.001). These differences persisted across both open and endovascular subgroups.
CONCLUSION: Operative management of ALI is associated with substantial hospitalization costs that are consistent across revascularization strategies and payer types. While commercially insured admissions generated positive contribution margins, Medicare and Medicaid reimbursements were insufficient to offset costs. Given that most patients were insured through Medicare, the reimbursement disparities translated into an overall negative financial impact for ALI care. Without reimbursement reform or payment adjustment, the long-term financial sustainability of ALI care, and equitable patient access to timely revascularization, may be jeopardized.

Title: Chronic thoracic aortitis versus primary medial degeneration in ascending aorta: a digital morphometric analysis of aortic layers remodelling.
Journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic aortitis (CA) represents a diverse group of inflammatory conditions often diagnosed incidentally in ascending aorta biopsies. While the 2015 and 2016 Consensus Statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta provide standardised histological classifications, data quantifying structural remodelling within individual aortic layers remain limited. Furthermore, distinguishing CA from primary non-inflammatory medial degeneration (MD) can be challenging, particularly when inflammation is sparse or burnt out, and secondary degenerative changes predominate. We aimed to compare morphological changes in CA and MD aneurysms and apply digital image analysis to quantify aortic wall layers.
METHODS: Retrospective histological analysis was performed on 63 ascending aortic specimens: CA (n=21), MD (n=21), and autopsy controls (n=21). Digitised elastic-stained sections were analysed using QuPath software to measure the thickness and cross-sectional area of the intima (I), media (M), and adventitia (A). Overall MD scores (i.e., summaries of each MD grade component) were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis based on binary logistic regression models.
RESULTS: CA demonstrated a profound architectural shift, characterised by medial thinning alongside marked intimal and adventitial expansion, resulting in significantly lower M/(I+A) thickness and area ratios compared with MD and controls (p <0.001). CA specimens also exhibited the most severe secondary degenerative changes, with significantly higher overall MD scores (median: 15 vs. 8; p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis revealed diagnostic utility of both the M/(I+A) thickness ratio (AUC = 0.964) and the M/(I+A) area ratio (AUC = 0.955) for identifying CA. A multivariable model combining the overall MD score with the M/(I+A) thickness ratio achieved an AUC of 0.971 (accuracy 88.1%), whereas combining it with the M/(I+A) area ratio yielded an AUC of 0.968 (accuracy 90.5%).
CONCLUSION: Digital morphometric analysis provides a reproducible and feasible method for quantifying structural remodelling in chronic aortitis. Changes in the proportions of the aortic layers, specifically intimal and adventitial expansion combined with medial thinning and severe secondary medial degeneration, can facilitate accurate differentiation of aortic wall pathologies, particularly in cases with sparse inflammation.

Title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.
METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.
RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.
CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

Title: Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD.
METHODS: This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared.
RESULTS: Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications.
CONCLUSION: The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.

Title: Distal-to-Proximal Conduction System Ablation as a Bailout Strategy in Refractory Multi-Exit Purkinje-Related Premature Ventricular Contractions and Ventricular Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ablation of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) originating from the Purkinje network-particularly those with multiple exit sites and morphologies-poses a significant clinical challenge. In refractory cases where conventional ablation fails, proximal conduction system ablation may represent a viable alternative strategy.
OBJECTIVE: to evaluate the safety and efficacy of proximal conduction system ablation in patients with refractory multi-exit Purkinje PVCs with diverse morphologies.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included consecutive patients with drug-refractory, symptomatic Purkinje PVCs who underwent proximal conduction system ablation. Multiple exit sites and morphologies were observed during mapping and ablation, indicating complex activation within the Purkinje network.
RESULTS: Among the 22 patients included, 14 (63.6%) had PVC-triggered ventricular fibrillation. Acute elimination of the PVC by distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation achieved in 21 patients (95.5%), while one procedure (4.5%) was discontinued at the patient's request due to the anticipated risk of conduction system injury. The initial site of earliest activation arose from the posterior fascicle in 63.6% (n=14), the septal fascicle in 22.7% (n=5) and the anterior fascicle in 13.6% (n=3). During ablation, all patients demonstrated a shift in the site of earliest activation. Conduction disturbances occurred in 5 patients (22.7%). During a median follow-up of 32.3 months (IQR 17.5-54.5), one patient (4.5%) experienced PVC recurrence requiring repeat ablation; however, no patient experienced recurrent ventricular fibrillation.
CONCLUSION: Distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation can be an effective bailout strategy for patients with refractory multi-exit fascicular/Purkinje-related PVCs and recurrent VF. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm its long-term safety and efficacy.

Title: High- and moderate-intensity interval training for cardiac-psychological comorbidity: Results from a 4-week intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and are associated with poorer prognosis. Exercise-based rehabilitation may improve both psychological and cardiopulmonary outcomes in this population.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the short-term effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT) in CVD patients with comorbid anxiety and/or depression.
METHODS: This retrospective real-world study screened 1020 cardiac rehabilitation patients, of whom 112 were included in the final analysis. All participants completed a 4-week supervised outpatient HIIT or MIIT. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the GAD-7 and PHQ-9, and cardiopulmonary fitness was evaluated by standardized cardiopulmonary exercise testing.
RESULTS: After 4 weeks, in the HIIT group, GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores decreased by 4.4 ± 4.3 and 3.7 ± 4.3 points (Cohen's d = -1.023 and -0.860; p < 0.001); in the MIIT group, the corresponding reductions were 4.8 ± 4.9 and 3.5 ± 4.0 points (Cohen's d = -0.980 and -0.875; p < 0.001). Both groups also demonstrated significant improvements in multiple cardiopulmonary parameters (all p < 0.05). Nominal between-group differences were observed for AT VO₂ and PETCO₂ before multiplicity correction, but neither difference remained statistically significant after FDR correction.
CONCLUSIONS: In clinical practice, short-term HIIT and MIIT may both be feasible strategies to alleviate psychological symptoms and improve cardiopulmonary fitness in CVD patients with comorbid anxiety or depression.

Title: Exercise Capacity, Muscle Mass, and Quality of Life in Pediatric Patients with Fontan Circulation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how measures of cardiac, vascular, and muscle health relate to Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory TM (PedsQL) score in a cohort of children and adolescents with Fontan circulation.
STUDY DESIGN: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from children and adolescents (8-19 years) with Fontan circulation enrolled in a prospective study. Participants underwent a series of tests, including a cardiopulmonary exercise test, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry measures of appendicular lean mass index (ALMI, kg/m2), leg dynamometry, and the 23-item PedsQL. The survey quantifies Physical, Emotional, Social, and School functioning into 1 total score and 2 summary scores for physical and psychosocial health.
RESULTS: 135 patients (median age 12.7 [IQR 10.2, 15.6] years) completed the baseline visit. Median time from Fontan operation was 8.7 years [IQR 5.9, 12.0]. Peak VO2 was 1309 [IQR 1070, 1670] mL/min, and indexed peak VO2 was 31.1 [IQR 25.2, 36.1] mL/kg/min. Physical and Psychosocial PedsQL summary scores were 78.1 [IQR 67.2,90.6] and 76.7 [IQR 63.3, 90], respectively, and the total score was 76.1 [IQR 65.2, 88.0]. Absolute peak VO2 was weakly correlated with PedsQL Physical Summary Score (ρ=0.21, P=0.015), but indexed peak VO2, % predicted peak VO2, and Fontan-specific peak VO2 z-score were not ALMI z-score was -0.84 [IQR -1.56, -0.14] and positively correlated with total PedsQL score (ρ=0.28, P=0.001) and the Physical Functioning domain (ρ=0.30, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal muscle mass was associated with quality of life in children with Fontan circulation. The association between VO2 and physical function was attenuated with body-size normalization.

Title: Life's Essential 8 Cardiovascular Health Characteristics in Children and Adolescents with Congenital Heart Disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the cardiovascular health (CVH) characteristics in children and adolescents with congenital heart disease (CHD) using a modified version of the American Heart Association (AHA) Life's Essential 8 criteria and examine differences in CVH by CHD complexity.
STUDY DESIGN: This single-center, cross-sectional study included youth 8-19 years old with CHD and an available total cholesterol within 3 years of a clinic visit. Patients were categorized into simple, moderate, or complex anatomic groups according to AHA anatomic classification guidelines for CHD. Modified CVH scores were calculated using 3 to 5 CVH metrics: nicotine exposure, body mass index (BMI), blood lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure. The association between anatomic complexity and CVH was assessed using multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: The study cohort included 629 patients. Modified CVH scores were low or moderate in 46.1% of patients, with prevalent low or moderate scores in blood lipids (49.4%), blood pressure (42.4%), and BMI (31.9%). Median CVH scores differed across anatomic groups (simple 83 vs moderate 78 vs complex 84, P=0.01). Complex CHD was associated with a higher (more favorable) modified CVH score and blood pressure score than moderate CHD and a higher blood lipids score than simple and moderate CHD.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite vulnerable cardiac anatomy, almost half of youth with CHD had suboptimal CVH, with prevalent deficits in blood lipids, blood pressure, and BMI. Complex CHD anatomy was associated with a more favorable CVH profile. These findings highlight the need to incorporate health screening and promotion into the routine care of the pediatric CHD population.

Title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD: current evidence and challenges in clinical practice.
Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by a complex pathophysiology driven by intertwined metabolic and hepatic pathways, enabling the identification of multiple therapeutic targets and a rapidly expanding drug development pipeline. This review summarizes the current and emerging therapeutic landscape for MASLD and discusses key challenges for clinical implementation. The imminent availability of several new therapies is expected to pose important clinical challenges, particularly in accurately identifying patients most likely to benefit. Currently, resmetirom and semaglutide are the only two drugs conditionally approved for patients with fibrosis stages 2-3, pending final phase 3 outcomes, and represent the main liver-directed and metabolic-focused therapeutic strategies, respectively. Treatment selection should follow a phenotype-based approach integrating metabolic profile and liver disease stage. Non-invasive tests are central for assessing treatment eligibility; however, strategies incorporating metabolic risk profiling and longitudinal monitoring will be essential to optimize real-world management of MASH.

Title: Survival Outcomes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Decade of Treatment in a Western Tertiary Referral Center.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a challenging malignancy with various available treatments. This retrospective study provides clinical outcomes on staging, treatment, and overall survival (OS) of HCC patients.
METHODS: All included patients were diagnosed between 2013 and 2022. OS was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, stratified by BCLC stage and diagnosis period.
RESULTS: A total of 1,306 patients were analyzed: 9.1% BCLC-0, 44.3% BCLC-A, 19.1% BCLC-B, 17% BCLC-C, and 10.4% BCLC-D. Median OS (mOS) for the cohort was 19.7 months (95% CI 16.9-23.0), ranging from 86.1 months (95% CI 47.6-not reached) for BCLC-0 to 2.4 months (95% CI 1.7-3.4) for BCLC-D. Poor survival was associated with Child-Pugh (CP) classification (CP-B: HR1.49, 95% CI 1.17-1.89, CP-C: HR2.45, 95% CI 1.57-3.81), and portal vein tumor thrombosis (HR1.75, 95% CI 1.19-2.58). In 2013-2017, 609 patients (46.6%) were diagnosed with mOS of 21.7 months (95% CI 18.4-25.1), while 697 patients (53.4%) in 2018-2022 had mOS of 18.9 months (95% CI 14.8-22.7). Stratified by BCLC stage, mOS in 2013-2017 ranged from 86.1 months (95% CI 41.6-not reached) for BCLC-0 to 2.9 months (95% CI 2.2-5.7) for BCLC-D. In 2018-2022, mOS was 59.8 months (95%CI 44.2-not reached) for BCLC-0, and 1.8 months (95% CI 1.4-3.1) for BCLC-D.
CONCLUSIONS: Our clinical data from a consecutive decade-long HCC cohort support the evolution of staging and survival data in HCC management, with CP classification, portal vein tumor thrombosis, and treatment modality as key survival predictors.

Title: Myocardial Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder with Anxious Distress: Evidence from Oxygenation-Sensitive CMR and Entropy Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with major depressive disorder with anxious distress (MDD-A) frequently experience cardiovascular symptoms (CVS), which are associated with impaired quality of life and poorer long-term prognosis. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate myocardial alterations in MDD-A patients using oxygenation-sensitive cardiovascular magnetic resonance (OS-CMR) and mapping-derived entropy analysis, and to explore their associations with CVS as well as the severity of depressive and anxiety symptoms.
METHODS: In this prospective study, 58 consecutively enrolled medication-naïve patients with MDD-A diagnosed according to DSM-5 criteria and 61 healthy controls were included. All participants underwent CMR examinations at 3.0T. Left ventricular (LV) function, native T1 and T2 values, T1-entropy and T2-entropy, LV strain parameters, and oxygenation-sensitive signal intensity change (OS-SI%) were measured and compared between the two groups. Associations between CMR-derived parameters and CVS, anxiety symptom severity, and depressive symptom severity were assessed separately. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, patients with MDD-A exhibited significantly higher T1-entropy (8.3 ± 0.3 vs. 7.5 ± 0.3, p < 0.001) and T2-entropy (9.2 ± 0.4 vs. 8.1 ± 0.3, p < 0.001), whereas OS-SI% was significantly lower (11.4 ± 7.5% vs. 14.5 ± 4.5%, p = 0.007). After adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, and heart rate, multivariable regression analyses revealed that OS-SI% was inversely associated with HAMD scores (β = -0.205, p = 0.043) and HAMA scores (β = -0.453, p < 0.001), and inversely associated with CVS (OR= 0.801, p = 0.002). T1-entropy (β = 4.105, p = 0.022) and T2-entropy (β = 2.793, p = 0.042) were positively associated with HAMD scores.
CONCLUSION: OS-SI% and mapping-derived myocardial entropy measures may serve as valuable noninvasive imaging biomarkers for assessing early myocardial alterations in patients with MDD-A.

Title: Longitudinal analysis of structural biomarkers for disease progression in intermediate age-related macular degeneration: a MACUSTAR study report.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the prognostic impact of qualitative and quantitative structural biomarkers including their topographic distribution for progression to geographic atrophy (GA) or neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) in eyes with intermediate AMD (iAMD) within the longitudinal part of the MACUSTAR study (NCT03349801).
DESIGN: Longitudinal, prospective low-interventional European multicenter cohort study.
SUBJECTS: 577 eyes of 577 study patients with iAMD.
METHODS: Study eyes with iAMD underwent multimodal retinal imaging at each study visit followed by a standardized grading of structural biomarkers, including presence of subretinal drusenoid deposits (SDDs), vitelliform lesion, pigmentary abnormalities (PAs), refractile deposits, pigment epithelium detachment (PED), non-exudative choroidal neovascularization (nCNV), incomplete (i) retinal pigment epithelium and outer retinal atrophy (RORA), complete (c) RORA, and hyperreflective foci presence (HRF). Automated assessment of the retinal pigment epithelium drusen complex (RPEDC) volume and HRF area including their topographic distribution based on spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging was conducted using a deep-learning based algorithm. Disease progression (GA/nAMD) was assessed at each study visit up to a follow-up time of 4 years. Multivariable time-discrete hazard models were used to evaluate the biomarkers' relevance for disease progression in the entire OCT volume, the central 3 mm disk, and the central subfield of the Early Treatment Diabetes Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) Grid.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Disease progression to GA/nAMD, hazard ratios of structural biomarkers for disease progression RESULTS: A total of 577 study eyes of 577 iAMD study patients (mean age 72.01 ± 7.01 years, 66.1 % female, median follow-up 3 years) were included. Disease progression was detected in 82 eyes (9.01 %), 37 (6.4 %) progressed to GA, and 45 (7.7 %) to nAMD. Inside the central 3 mm presence of SDDs, PED, nCNV and cRORA conferred overall risk for progression, whereas PAs, RPEDC volume, iRORA, cRORA were associated with risk for progression to GA. Only nCNV volume increased risk for nAMD.
CONCLUSIONS: Structural biomarkers indicate risk for iAMD progression and may differentiate eyes progressing to GA from eyes progressing to nAMD. Biomarker topography impacts their prognostic relevance and needs to be considered in clinical trial design.

Title: Distal Reinterventions after Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER): A Report from a Prospective Trial.
Journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Optimal timing for distal reintervention after frozen elephant trunk repair remains debated. We evaluated patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and predictors of distal aortic reintervention following Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER).
METHODS: From May 2021 to January 2025, 405 patients underwent B-SAFER in a prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized PS-IDE cohort. Among them, 117 patients required 148 distal reinterventions. Indications for initial repair were acute type A dissection (36/189, 31%), chronic dissection (62/138, 53%), and degenerative aneurysm (19/78, 16%). Most reinterventions (n=132, 92%) were planned. Primary endpoints were operative mortality, stroke, and paralysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed survival and freedom from reintervention. Median follow-up was 1.3 years, and median time to reintervention was 8.7 months.
RESULTS: Mortality after first reintervention was 6.5% (n=8). Permanent stroke occurred in one patient (0.8%), with no cases of paralysis. Causes of death included sepsis (n=4), hemorrhagic shock (n=2), pulmonary embolism (n=1), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=1). Freedom from reintervention at 2 years was 64%, lowest in chronic dissections (48%), intermediate in degenerative aneurysms (71%), and highest in acute dissections (74%). Larger descending and abdominal aortic diameters were the strongest predictors of reintervention. Survival at 2.5 years was similar across groups (81% acute, 81% chronic, 77% degenerative).
CONCLUSIONS: Distal reinterventions after B-SAFER are common, safe, and are associated with acceptable early outcomes. Disease chronicity and aortic diameter predict reintervention risk. Frozen elephant trunk is an effective platform for staged aortic repair, and earlier reintervention in high-risk patients warrants further study. (245).

Title: Effect of Microvascular Disease on Re-amputation Risk after Unilateral Amputation due to Diabetes or Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between manifestations of microvascular disease (MVD) and other factors on re-amputation risk within 12 months following incident unilateral lower extremity amputation.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 8 924 patients with first unilateral transmetatarsal, transtibial, or transfemoral amputation secondary to diabetes and or peripheral arterial disease, identified through a Veterans Affairs database. Re-amputation was defined as any subsequent ipsilateral soft tissue or bony revision or amputation to a higher level. The presence of MVD was determined using a composite variable that required the involvement of each subcomponent (neuropathy, nephropathy, and retinopathy), and also by evaluating each of the subcomponent MVD variables separately. Twenty-nine additional risk factors were evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of re-amputation. A competing risk analysis estimated the cumulative incidence of re-amputation. The effect of risk factors on re-amputation risk was estimated by computing subdistribution hazard ratios (sub-HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: The twelve month re-amputation risk was 38.0% (transmetatarsal), 27.2% (transtibial), and 14.1% (transfemoral). The combined MVD variable was not significantly associated with re-amputation risk. However, re-amputation after transmetatarsal amputation was significantly elevated in patients with retinopathy, leukocytosis, or those who were on kidney dialysis, with the highest risk in those with all three (sub-HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.8 - 2.6). Similarly, for transtibial patients, the risk was higher in the presence of retinopathy, leukocytosis, and kidney dialysis, and in those with a prior ipsilateral revascularisation and those on warfarin. The highest risk was observed in those with all factors present (sub-HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.7).
CONCLUSION: This study identified an important association between the pre-amputation diagnosis of retinopathy and risk for subsequent failure of primary healing and need for re-amputation. Presence of retinopathy should be considered when evaluating potential failure of healing during amputation level decisions.

Title: Comparison of delivery room wrist versus earlobe pulse oximetry in newborns: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition.
METHODS: Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications.
RESULTS: Ninety-six neonates were randomized, with 48 in each group. Time from completion of sensor application to reliable signal was similar between ear and wrist groups (67.1±41.4 vs 74.5±48.2 seconds; mean difference -7.4 seconds; 95% CI -25.6 to 10.8; P=0.42). Sensor application time was shorter in ear group (mean difference -16.3 seconds; 95% CI -17.7 to -14.9; P<0.001), resulting in shorter time from birth to reliable signal (mean difference -28.8 seconds; 95% CI -53.9 to -3.7; P=0.02). Perfusion index was lower, and reapplication rates were higher in ear group.
CONCLUSION: Time to reliable signal acquisition after probe placement did not differ between the earlobe and wrist. Further studies using neonatal-specific ear probes are warranted.

Title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 inhibitor use during or after acute kidney injury and the risk of major adverse kidney events and Mortality: A systematic review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and pharmacologic strategies to improve outcomes after AKI remain limited. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have established cardiovascular and renal benefits, but their role during or after AKI remains less clearly defined.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420261298733). Six databases were searched through February 9, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with established AKI, compared SGLT2i use with control or nonuse, and reported at least one clinical outcome. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse kidney events (MAKE). Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for mortality and odds ratios (ORs) from crude event counts for MAKE.
RESULTS: Seven studies were included (six observational, one randomized). SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.59-0.71; I2 = 32%; three cohorts) and lower odds of MAKE (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.44-0.88; I2 = 91%; five studies), but the MAKE estimate was not robust to exclusion of individual studies and MAKE definitions varied. Kidney replacement therapy (two studies) was not pooled. The randomized trial (n = 200) was inconclusive for mortality (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.12-1.29) and MAKE (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.52-1.67). Certainty of evidence was very low.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i use during or after AKI was associated with lower mortality and MAKE in observational studies (very low certainty of evidence), whereas the only randomized trial was too small to be conclusive. Confounding by indication is likely, and the evidence remains limited by heterogeneity and the predominance of observational data. Randomized trials are needed.

Title: Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients who have sepsis often experience persistent physiological instability, which may increase vulnerability to postoperative complications. However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted utilizing an insurance database. Patients who had a preoperative diagnosis of sepsis within two years prior to TKA were matched 1:3 to controls based on demographics and comorbidities. Patients who had sepsis were stratified according to the following timeline: sepsis three months prior to surgery, three to six months prior, six to 12 months prior, 12 to 18 months prior, and 18 to 24 months prior. Medical and surgical complications were assessed at 90 days and two years following surgery. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: Patients who had sepsis within two years prior to surgery exhibited increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (odds ratio (OR): 1.6), postoperative sepsis (OR: 2.7), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.4), urinary tract infection (OR: 1.8), blood transfusion (OR: 2.0), readmission (OR: 1.3), and wound dehiscence (OR: 1.4) within 90 days of surgery. At two years following surgery, sepsis was associated with elevated rates of revision surgery (OR: 1.3), PJI (OR: 1.6), osteomyelitis (OR: 1.9), and mortality (OR: 1.3). Sepsis within three months of operation was associated with elevated rates of myocardial infarction (OR: 2.1) and deep vein thrombosis (OR: 2.0). All findings were statistically significant at P < 0.05.
CONCLUSION: Preoperative sepsis is associated with increased complications following TKA, including periprosthetic joint infection and mortality. Sepsis within three months of surgery confers a particularly elevated risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis following TKA.

Title: Unexpected coagulopathy in thrombolyzed stroke: experience from a single center in Chile.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is time-dependent, and waiting for coagulation tests (COT) may delay treatment initiation. In several countries, IVT is initiated without waiting COT results; this approach has not been evaluated in South America. In this region, excessive alcohol consumption may increase the prevalence of unrecognized chronic liver disease.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the frequency of unsuspected coagulation abnormalities among patients with AIS treated with IVT at a single tertiary care center in Chile.
METHODS: A prospective analysis of all patients treated with IVT at Clínica Alemana between June 2016 and July 2025, assessing the proportion of individuals with unexpected coagulation abnormalities.
RESULTS: A total of 480 patients with AIS received IVT. The COTs were normal in 445 patients (92.7%), abnormal in 9 (1.88%), and incomplete or not performed in 26 (5.42%). No clinical differences were observed among the three groups. Patients with coagulation abnormalities or incomplete/not performed COT were significantly less frequent in the Emergency Room (ER) during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (p = 0.001). Among those with abnormal COT results, significant differences were found in international normalized ratio (INR) values (p < 0.000) and platelet count (p = 0.001). The functional outcomes at 3 months, as well as mortality and rate of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, did not differ across groups.
CONCLUSION: Unexpected coagulation disorders are an infrequent finding in patients with AIS treated with IVT at our center in Santiago, Chile. Therefore, blood test results should not be awaited before initiating IVT.

Title: Development and evaluation of a family-based graphical tool for longitudinal monitoring of poststroke sequelae.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical information regarding patient health is traditionally managed by healthcare professionals, often leaving patients and families in a passive role during the recovery process.
OBJECTIVE: To describe and evaluate a family-based functional graphic tool-the Family Observation of Limits and Learning on Well-being (FOLLOW)-designed for the monthly assessment of post-stroke sequelae by nonprofessionals.
METHODS: The tool is a color-coded visual graphic (red for no improvement, yellow for stability, and green for improvement) designed for intuitive understanding without specialized training. It evaluates seven domains: motor independence, sleep patterns, cognition and language, family quality of life, patient quality of life, fatigue, and emotional state. This study included 51 patients and assessed the usability and proficiency evaluation among three groups: family caregivers, healthcare professionals, and poststroke individuals.
RESULTS: Significant differences were observed in the proficiency of completing the tool across the groups. Success rates were 94.1% for family caregivers and 100.0% for healthcare professionals, compared with 69.2% for poststroke individuals (p = 0.008). The graphic proved to be easily interpretable for both caregivers and professionals.
CONCLUSION: The functional graphic is an effective tool when completed by family members or caregivers, though it is less reliable when completed by patients themselves. It provides a practical, longitudinal overview of the patient's home environment and clinical needs, while also serving as a complementary monitoring aid that enables early identification of complications and facilitating prompt intervention.

Title: Novel Relationships between the ICAD, CD53, GRM1, and GSTmu Protein Levels and Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
Abstract: The aim of the present study was to identify serum proteins associated with atherosclerosis and its comorbidities. The 3-year follow-up included 216 patients subjected to coronary angiography. Gensini score was used to quantify coronary atherosclerosis, and peripheral atherosclerosis was assessed by B-mode ultrasound. Serum proteins were profiled using an Explorer antibody microarray (Full Moon Biosystems, USA). In-house ELISA or commercial ELISA kits were used to validate the microarray data in the total cohort for the top five proteins from the atherosclerotic profile. Only ICAD (DNA fragmentation factor subunit, DFF45/ICAD) was linked to type 2 diabetes and the presence of coronary artery stenosis regardless of the severity of stenosis. CD53 was also associated with coronary stenosis. IL-6 was associated with diabetes, and GSTmu (glutathione S-transferase Mu3) was associated with brachiocephalic stenosis ≥ 60% and with femoral and coronary arterial lesions. Only GRM1 (glutamate metabotropic receptor 1) showed inverse associations with coronary stenosis and cardiovascular outcomes (r = -0.24 and P = 0.025 and r = -0.31 and P = 0.007, respectively). Moreover, GRM1 was inversely associated with femoral lesions ≥ 30%. Thus, we identified previously unreported associations of the ICAD, CD53, GRM1, and GSTmu proteins with atherosclerosis, diabetes, and nonfatal cardiovascular outcomes.

Title: Urinary Proteomic Panel Distinguishes Acute Myocarditis from Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Reliable noninvasive discrimination of acute myocarditis (AM) from acute myocardial infarction (AMI) in patients presenting with acute chest pain remains an unmet clinical need. We aimed to identify urinary proteomic markers using mass spectrometry and LASSO regression. Patients with suspected AM or AMI were prospectively enrolled. Urinary proteomes were profiled by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. The discovery cohort was stratified by age and sex and randomly divided into training and internal validation sets at a 3:1 ratio. Differentially expressed proteins were screened, and a diagnostic model was constructed using LASSO with 1000 bootstrap resamplings in the training set. The model was validated internally and further verified in an independent cohort using ELISA. A total of 42 AM and 80 AMI patients were included in the discovery cohort. Differential expression analysis in the training set identified 880 and 1099 differentially expressed proteins in AM and AMI, respectively, compared with controls. A three-protein panel comprising TNFRSF1A, F9, and PRDX3 achieved an AUC of 0.954 in the training set and exceeded the clinical models (all DeLong's P < 0.05). Addition of the protein panel to either clinical model further improved diagnostic performance (both P < 0.001). Similar performance was confirmed in the validation cohorts. A urinary proteomic panel comprising TNFRSF1A, F9, and PRDX3 may provide a noninvasive approach for differentiating AM from AMI.

Title: Age-Dependent Heterogeneity Trends in the Associations between Urban Green Space and Cardiovascular Health in a Humid-Subtropical Megacity.
Abstract: Urban green space (UGS) is a promising nature-based solution for cardiovascular health, yet its associative pathways in pollution-saturated, high-density environments remain contested. We applied a two-stage framework combining gradient boosting decision trees and structural equation modeling to a clinical cohort of 23,312 patients in Nanjing, China. Air-quality-related pathways accounted for more than 75% of the relative statistical contribution to model variance, exceeding psychological restoration proxies. At the macroscale, the aggregated air-quality pathway showed a marginal positive coefficient; although this may conceptually resemble aerodynamic interference, the interpretation remains speculative because no morphological or fluid-dynamics data were available. Stage 2 models identified distinct protective associative networks. For chronic ischemic heart disease, vegetation vitality was inversely associated with NO2 and SO2 and was linked to more favorable metabolic markers. For heart failure, the vegetation condition was associated with mixed pollutants and hemodynamic-metabolic indicators. Age-stratified analyses suggested heterogeneity in canopy density-PM2.5 associations, but subgroup slopes were nonsignificant, and effect sizes were extremely small, indicating fragile relative fluctuations rather than structural reversal. These findings characterize UGS primarily as a biophysical modulator and support targeted ecological strategies in traffic corridors and aging communities.

Title: Strontium and Lead Accelerate, Calcium Protects: Arterial Stiffness Progression in an 11-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract: Arterial stiffness measured by estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is an established predictor of cardiovascular disease. Long-term metal exposure may drive arterial stiffness progression, but prior studies largely relied on single-time assessments of exposure or outcome, overlooking heterogeneity in ePWV progression and its longitudinal links to long-term metal exposure. In an 11-year prospective study of 707 participants from the Manganese-Exposed Workers Healthy Cohort, we repeatedly quantified blood cell metals and computed cumulative exposure indices (CEIs). Latent class mixed models identified low and high ePWV trajectories. A one-quantile increase in CEI of a five-metal mixture [strontium (Sr), calcium (Ca), lead (Pb), magnesium, and manganese] was associated with belonging to the high ePWV trajectory (OR = 1.62; 95% CI: 1.14-2.31), with CEI_Sr and CEI_Pb as positive drivers and CEI_Ca inversely associated. The stronger CEI_Sr and CEI_Pb effects were observed in participants with high body mass index or smokers. The distinct trajectories of metal exposure were further identified; we found that the high-decreasing Pb trajectory was associated with higher odds of the high ePWV trajectory compared with the low-decreasing Pb trajectory (OR = 3.98; 95% CI: 1.28-13.26). We provided insights into the longitudinal links between long-term metal exposure and arterial stiffness progression, emphasizing the critical role of metal biomonitoring and primary prevention of arteriosclerosis in high-risk populations.

Title: Artificial Light at Night and Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: Socioeconomic Inequality in the China Birth Cohort Study.
Abstract: Evidence regarding the association of outdoor artificial light at night (ALAN) with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) remains limited. Between February 2018 and December 2022, 241,608 participants from the China Birth Cohort Study (CBCS), which enrolled individuals from 17 provinces across China, were included in the analysis. HDP was defined by physician clinical diagnosis. We estimated outdoor ALAN within 500 m, sourced from the VIIRS/DNB, using the address of each participant, and categorized it into quartiles (lowest [Q1] as reference). We used generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) to assess the association between ALAN exposure and HDPs. Effect modification by province-level per capita gross domestic product (GDP), household income, and other factors was also explored. A total of 9383 (3.88%) participants were diagnosed with HDPs. After adjusting for covariates, compared with Q1, the odds ratios (ORs) for HDPs were 1.14 (95% CI: 1.07-1.21) for quartile 2 (Q2), 1.21 (95% CI: 1.13-1.29) for quartile 3 (Q3), and 1.09 (95% CI: 1.02-1.17) for quartile 4 (Q4). Furthermore, province-level per capita GDP and household income modified the associations between the ALAN and HDPs. Compared to participants residing in low-GDP areas with low income, the strongest effect estimate was observed among participants residing in high-GDP areas with low income (OR: 1.15 [1.09-1.20] vs 0.97 [0.91-1.04] for HDPs).

Title: Learning curve and clinical outcomes of robotic-assisted heart bypass surgery: Real-world evidence from India.
Abstract: BackgroundRobotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) using bilateral internal mammary arteries (BIMA) provides a minimally invasive option for advanced coronary artery disease (CAD), but evidence on its learning curve and outcomes in the Indian population remains limited.ObjectivesTo evaluate the learning curve associated with robotic CABG using BIMA and to compare perioperative and clinical outcomes between the early and late phases of surgical experience in a real-world setting.DesignRetrospective, single-center, observational chart review conducted at a high-volume quaternary cardiac care center in India.MethodsThis retrospective chart review was performed for 341 patients who underwent robotic-assisted BIMA CABG between 2020 and 2025. The learning curve was assessed using risk-adjusted cumulative summation (CUSUM), while complication trends were examined through sequential probability CUSUM failure analysis.ResultsThe cohort comprised 295 (86.51%) males with a mean age of 59.56 ± 9.93 years and a body mass index (BMI) of 25.98 ± 3.74 kg/m2. Mean console time was 101.66 ± 29.99 minutes, ICU stay 2.85 ± 0.98 days, and hospital stay 6.01 ± 2.38 days; conversion to open surgery occurred in 2.93% of cases, with in-hospital mortality of 3.52%. CUSUM analysis identified case 125 as the proficiency inflection point, after which console time significantly decreased (94.95 ± 24.32 vs. 113.38 ± 35.04 minutes; p<0.001), while ventilator duration, ICU and hospital stay, complications, and mortality remained comparable between phases. Readmission and re-exploration rates were low (2.05% each), with no deaths at 6-month follow-up. CUSUM failure analysis confirmed complication rates remained within acceptable thresholds throughout the study.ConclusionsRobotic-assisted BIMA CABG demonstrated acceptable outcomes, with operative efficiency improving after approximately 125 cases. These findings support its feasibility in experienced, high-volume centers and warrant further multicentre evaluation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Predictive factors of functional and anatomical response to dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To identify clinical and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) biomarkers predictive of functional and anatomical response to intravitreal dexamethasone implant in refractory diabetic macular edema (DME).
METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included 185 eyes of 98 diabetic patients with center-involving DME refractory to a mean of 7.1±2.8 prior aflibercept (2mg) injections. All eyes received a 0.7mg intravitreal dexamethasone implant and were followed for at least 6 months, with a mean follow-up of 12.9±2.1 months. Functional outcome was assessed by best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA, logMAR) and anatomical outcome by central macular thickness (CMT) on SD-OCT. Baseline OCT biomarkers included CMT, serous retinal detachment (SRD) height, integrity of the ellipsoid zone and external limiting membrane (ELM), and disorganization of retinal inner layers (DRIL).
RESULTS: Baseline BCVA was 0.72±0.31 logMAR, and CMT 432±128μm. At 6 months, BCVA improved to 0.55±0.28 logMAR, and CMT decreased to 301±96μm (both P<0.001). Functional and anatomical responses were observed in 56% and 70% of eyes, respectively. Lower baseline CMT (OR=1.42, P=0.003), smaller SRD height (OR=0.76, P=0.005), fewer prior injections (OR=1.31, P=0.010), preserved ellipsoid zone (OR=2.18, P=0.002), and intact ELM (OR=1.94, P=0.004) were independently associated with favorable functional outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Baseline SD-OCT biomarkers are significant predictors of treatment response in refractory DME and may support individualized therapeutic decision-making.

Title: Machine-learning differentiation of precordial T-wave inversion in pulmonary embolism and acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiating acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in emergency settings is a notorious diagnostic challenge due to their overlapping symptoms and shared electrocardiographic abnormalities, such as precordial T-wave inversion (TWI). This study evaluated the ability of machine learning (ML) algorithms to distinguish acute PE from ACS by analyzing the morphology of inverted T waves in precordial leads.
METHODS: This retrospective, case-control study included 200 patients (100 ACS confirmed by coronary angiography; 100 PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography) admitted to Shahid Madani Hospital, Tabriz, Iran (2023-2024), who exhibited precordial TWI. Image processing with a region-growing technique traced negative T waves in leads V1, V2, and V3. Signals were filtered using Savitzky-Golay and Empirical Wavelet Transform (EWT) methods to extract time-frequency statistical parameters. Multiple supervised ML models were trained (80% training, 20% test with 5-fold cross-validation) over 50 random iterations.
RESULTS: The Ensemble (AdaBoost) model achieved the highest diagnostic performance, yielding an accuracy of 84.44%, sensitivity of 83.96%, specificity of 84.87%, and F1-score of 83.56%. Neural Network models performed comparably, achieving 84.00% accuracy and 85.14% sensitivity. Other evaluated algorithms (SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes) also generated acceptable discriminative accuracy (ranging from 78% to 82%).
CONCLUSION: Machine-learning algorithms can extract potentially disease-specific features from precordial T-wave morphology to differentiate PE from ACS. These findings support further investigation of AI-enhanced ECG interpretation as a rapid, low-cost, non-invasive adjunct to clinical decision-making in acute care. External validation in larger, clinically representative populations is required before clinical application.

Title: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy is an electrocardiographic pattern characterized by a regular alternation of two distinct cardiac events. It can arise from normal operation of device algorithms or indicate underlying dysfunction, such as sensing abnormalities. Accurate differentiation is crucial to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate clinical intervention.
OBJECTIVE: To systematically elucidate the mechanisms underlying pacemaker-associated bigeminy and establish a practical diagnostic framework.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of six patients exhibiting pacemaker-associated bigeminy on ambulatory electrocardiograms (ECGs). The patients were identified from the databases of the Children's Hospital of Soochow University and the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between March 2020 and December 2025.
RESULTS: We delineate six distinct mechanisms: 1) Non-competitive atrial pacing (NCAP) triggered by sinus tachycardia; 2) Fusion beat exclusion due to evoked response (ER) undersensing; 3) Auto capture (AC) operation with start-stop pattern constrained by maximum tracking rate (MTR); 4) Window of atrial rate acceleration detection (WARAD) activation by non-conducted atrial premature complexes; 5) A Pace on Premature Ventricular Contraction (A Pace on PVC) triggered by PVCs; and 6) Dynamic atrioventricular (AV) delay operation following atrial premature beats.
CONCLUSIONS: Pacemaker-associated bigeminy represents a spectrum of phenomena driven by specific "algorithm-rhythm interactions." Recognition of these characteristic patterns is essential for correctly distinguishing normal device function from malfunction, thereby guiding appropriate clinical management and optimizing patient outcomes.

Title: Dose-dependent administration of quetiapine induces myocardial damage associated with altered cGAS-STING-TBK1-IRF3 and Nrf-2/Keap-1 gene expression.
Abstract: Quetiapine (QTP) is an atypical antipsychotic drug commonly prescribed for psychiatric illnesses, which have been linked to a range of cardiovascular side effects. However, molecular mechanisms underlying QTP-induced cardiotoxicity are not yet thoroughly understood. The current investigation was conducted to evaluate QTP-mediated cardiotoxicity at varying dose administrations. Thirty-two rats were randomly divided into four groups including the control group, QTP (20 mg/kg), QTP (55 mg/kg), QTP (100 mg/kg) by oral gavage for 28 days. Echocardiographic and electrocardiographic evaluations of cardiac function were performed and levels of cardiac injury, oxidative stress, inflammatory and apoptotic markers were determined. QTP intoxication increased the mRNA expression of MB21D1, TMEM173, TBK1, IRF3, IFNB1, and ISG15 and antioxidant responses (NFE2L2, HMOX1, NQO1, GCLC, GCLM), while decreasing KEAP1 expression, indicating transcriptional alterations in genes associated with innate immune and antioxidant defense pathways. Exposure to QTP triggered oxidative imbalances which were clearly progressive and were associated with a decrease in the activities of GST, CAT, SOD, GPx, GSR, GSH and HO-1 and increase in the levels of ROS and MDA. There was evidence of progressive impairment of LV systolic function by echocardiographic analysis characterized by elevated levels of LVEDD, LVESD, EDV and ESV. QTP intoxication induces ventricular repolarization (long QT, QTc, JT-peak, T-peak-Tend) and associated tachycardia (high heart rate). Furthermore, QTP administration provoked the levels of cTnI, cTnT, CK, CK-MB, and LDH at all the administered doses. The levels of NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6 and COX-2 enhanced QTP administration. Similarly, QTP exposure augmented the levels of Bax, Caspase-9, and Caspase-3 while suppressing the levels of Bcl-2. Histopathological analysis showed dose dependent QTP-mediated myocardial degeneration, necrosis, inflammatory infiltration, edema and vascular congestion.
