However, persistently positive blood cultures (PPBC) at 48 to 72 hours are already associated with a worse prognosis. We aimed to assess the clinical profile, temporal trends, and impact of surgical timing on outcomes in patients with left-sided IE and PPBC at 48 to 72 hours.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 3 Spanish tertiary centers (1998-2024). We compared patients with PPBC with those with blood culture clearance and assessed the effect of surgical timing using a time-dependent Cox model, inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, and a day-7 landmark analysis to minimize immortal time bias and confounding by indication.
RESULTS: Among 1265 patients with positive baseline cultures, 283 (22.4%) had PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. These patients exhibited a more severe clinical and microbiological profile and higher in-hospital mortality (36.0% vs 22.3%; P < .001). In the day-7 landmark analysis, surgery within the first 7 days was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (HR, 0.53; 95%CI, 0.30-0.95), with consistent trends across the time-dependent Cox and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting models.
CONCLUSIONS: PPBC at 48 to 72 hours identifies a high-risk subgroup of patients with left-sided IE. In these patients, early surgery within the first 7 days was associated with a potential survival benefit in adjusted models, supporting earlier reassessment of infection control to optimize surgical timing.

Title: Fetal brain volumes in complete vascular ring: A cross-sectional MRI study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between complete vascular ring (CVR) and prenatal brain development remains poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To compare global and regional fetal brain volumes between fetuses with CVR and controls, accounting for gestational age (GA), fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight.
METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 70 prenatally diagnosed CVR fetuses and 200 GA-matched controls with normal brain anatomy (22-37 weeks) underwent 1.5-T fetal MRI. Motion-corrected three-dimensional brain reconstructions were generated by slice-to-volume registration, and 19 regions were automatically segmented using a deep-learning pipeline. Linear regression included continuous GA, group, their interaction, fetal sex, and estimated fetal weight. Regional-to-intracranial volume ratios and sensitivity analyses incorporating maternal body mass index were evaluated. Multiple comparisons were controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
RESULTS: At the 28-week reference age, adjusted supratentorial brain, cortical gray matter, white matter, thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular volumes were smaller in the CVR group (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted P < 0.05). Intracranial volume did not differ significantly. Thalamic, lentiform nucleus, brainstem, and lateral ventricular proportions were also smaller. No group-by-GA interaction survived correction in the primary model.
CONCLUSIONS: CVR was associated with differences in selected fetal brain volumes, including regional differences relative to intracranial volume. Larger longitudinal studies with postnatal follow-up are needed.

Title: Escalation of Resting Heart Rate and Tachycardia as a Response to Thoracic Radiotherapy: Implications for Cardiovascular Outcomes after Radiotherapy.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac toxicity is a well-recognized, but poorly understood complication of radiotherapy (RT). In non-oncological settings, there is an established relationship between resting heart rate and cardiovascular health.
OBJECTIVES: To study the incidence and pattern of resting heart rate (rHR) as an early sign of cardiotoxicity among patients with non-metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed serial rHR measurements of consecutive patients with locally advanced NSCLC treated with definitive chemoradiation (CRT) over 6-7 weeks of daily radiation treatments followed by immunotherapy (durvalumab) between 2017-2022. Radiation dose to the heart and 17 cardiac substructures were extracted. Associations between heart rate elevation, tachycardia, cardiac substructure dose and outcomes were evaluated using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) and regression analysis.
RESULTS: We identified 110 patients, 56.4% with pre-existing heart disease. Median follow-up was 33.6 months. Median age was 70.4 years. Median rHR increased significantly during RT, rising from 81.5 bpm to 93 bpm at end of RT (p < 0.0001), remaining elevated in 30.6% of patients 12 months post-RT. Tachycardia incidence rose from 11.2% at baseline to 36.5% at 1-month post-RT (p < 0.0001). After adjusting for comorbidities, higher mean sinoatrial node (SAN) dose was associated with higher rHR elevation, delayed HR recovery and persistent tachycardia (all p < 0.05). Higher rHR during and after RT (β = 0.23, p = 0.005, and β = 13.49, p = 0.049, respectively), as well as the incidence of tachycardia episodes during RT were associated with increased odds of developing an arrhythmia (OR, 2.97, 95% CI, 1.17-7.52, p = 0.022).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated rHR and tachycardia are observed during and after RT for NSCLC and are associated with higher mean SAN dose. HR elevation was associated with increased risk of de novo arrhythmias, suggesting that heart rate may represent a non-invasive biomarker of subclinical cardiac injury. Prospective studies might be warranted to test the potential of routine HR monitoring and proactive dose reductions to the SAN to enable early detection and help mitigate the risk of post-treatment arrhythmia.

Title: Development and Evaluation of a Two-Stage Machine Learning Multivariable Model to Support Clinical Decision-Making in Thrombophilia Management.
Abstract: Thrombophilia is a disease characterized by an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Diagnosing and treating thrombophilic patients requires the nuanced interpretation of a great number of medical data. In this single-center, retrospective study, we evaluated the use of a two-stage machine learning (ML) model to predict the thrombophilia risk category and subsequent anticoagulation recommendation. The model was trained and tested using clinical and laboratory data obtained from 496 patients who underwent a complete thrombophilia work-up at the University Hospital Bonn between 2019 and 2024. The hybrid nature of the diagnostic categories, which combine ordinal classes including thrombophilia diagnosis, severity, and treatment recommendations and categorical classes (e.g. antiphospholipid syndrome), necessitated a two-stage approach. First, XGBClassifier was used to distinguish between the two classes, and then an ordinal-specific XGBOrdinalV2 model was used. Performance was assessed across 100 random 80/20 train-test splits. For exact class prediction (primary analysis), mean macro-averaged sensitivity, specificity, and precision were 58%, 91%, and 56.2% for diagnosis and 54.4%, 91.3%, and 58.5% for treatment. Performance was highest for frequent classes and poor for rare high-risk classes. When predictions within one adjacent class were accepted (secondary analysis), macro-averaged sensitivity was 91.9% and 86.2%, respectively. Antiphospholipid antibody status, age at first thrombosis, and unprovoked thrombosis were the most influential features for diagnosis. Model predictions and physician decisions were concordant in 395 of 496 patients (79.6%). This study demonstrates that ML models can support standardized thrombophilia management and improve diagnostic accuracy. However, external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

Title: Endoscopic ultrasound in hepatology: A European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Technical and Technology Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided techniques are increasingly applied in hepatology, including for tissue acquisition, vascular access, pressure measurement, and selected therapeutic interventions. However, adoption remains heterogeneous because of variability in technical approaches, devices, outcome definitions, operator expertise, and the quality of available evidence.
METHODS: This European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Technical and Technology Review summarizes the current evidence on selected EUS-guided techniques in liver disease and portal hypertension, including liver stiffness assessment, focal liver lesion characterization and sampling, EUS-guided liver biopsy, EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement, therapy for gastric varices, and portal vein sampling for liquid biopsy applications. Evidence was identified through a structured literature search up to April 2026, and recommendation statements were graded using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Eight ESGE statements were developed. The available evidence supports selected use of EUS-guided shear wave elastography and contrast-enhanced EUS as adjunctive techniques; EUS-guided liver biopsy and EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement as complementary approaches in selected patients and expert centers; and EUS-guided treatment of gastric varices as a valid alternative to direct endoscopic injection where appropriate expertise is available. Portal vein sampling remains investigational. Across the indications, the evidence base is limited by small studies, heterogeneous techniques, variable outcome definitions, and limited prospective comparative data.
CONCLUSIONS: This review provides an evidence-based framework for the selective use of EUS-guided techniques in hepatology and portal hypertension. Wider adoption will require standardized techniques, structured training, consistent outcome definitions, and prospective comparative studies.

Title: Analysis of survival in patients with sporadic hemangioblastoma versus that linked to von Hippel-Lindau. Experience of two reference centers.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish the overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) profiles regarding the patients diagnosed with hemangioblastoma in the context of a von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease and those of sporadic presentation.
METHODS: An observational and analytical study was conducted using a retrospective historical cohort, followed prospectively. The inclusion criteria consisted of patients operated of hemangioblastoma in two reference hospitals, between 2000 and 2023. A total of 39 patients were included. The Kaplan-Meier estimator was used to summarize data, and the log-rank test was used in comparative analysis.
RESULTS: The OS at 5 years was around 94%. No differences were found between VHL patients compared to sporadic tumours (p = 0.683). DFS at 2 years was 59% in VHL patients and 96% in sporadic, with statistically significant differences (p < 0.0001). In addition to this, DFS at 5 years in patients with a predominant cystic component was 73% and 95% in those with a solid component (p = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: The DFS of hemangioblastomas in patients with VHL is significantly lower than in sporadic hemangioblastomas, but no difference in OS can be claimed. DFS in cystic-predominant hemangioblastomas is significantly lower than in solid-predominant hemangioblastomas.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Rehabilitation care for human communication sequelae secondary to cerebrovascular disease.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the care process in the rehabilitation of patients with sequelae of language, speech and swallowing, secondary to cerebrovascular disease, in a third-level hospital in Mexico.
METHODS: Retrospective and descriptive study. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were obtained from 233 records of patients with sequelae of language, speech and swallowing, secondary to cerebrovascular disease, who received therapy. A descriptive analysis was performed; χ2 and Wilcoxon tests were used to assess differences before and after therapy. Three indicators were created to evaluate and identify the factors that participated in the rehabilitation process of the patients.
RESULTS: A significant difference was found in the affected structure and level of disability in function, activity and participation categories between the initial and final evaluation. The quality indicators showed the beginning of rehabilitation at 8.9 months, elaboration of the work program in the first two weeks in 90.1% of cases and revaluation by the medical area at 6 effective months of therapy in 81.1%.
CONCLUSIONS: The care process shows opportunities for improvement. The most important corresponds to the time that passes for the patient to start rehabilitation. Therapeutic intervention decreases the degree of disability.

Title: Lumbar fenestration to avoid shunting after posterior fossa tumor resection and failed ventriculostomy clamp trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Posterior fossa tumors in children frequently present with hydrocephalus. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion with an external ventriculostomy drain (EVD) is often used preoperatively or inserted at the time of surgery and continued into the postoperative setting. Despite tumor resections to restore fourth ventricular CSF passage, some patients fail EVD clamping and still require shunting for persistent hydrocephalus despite postoperative imaging showing patent CSF pathways. Increasing CSF gradient and transient CSF absorption during the postoperative period with a percutaneous, modified lumbar puncture technique-referred to herein as "lumbar fenestration"-may help avoid a permanent shunt in some of these patients. The aim of this study was to evaluate the safety and potential benefit of lumbar fenestration for avoiding a shunt in patients who fail a ventriculostomy clamp trial following resection of posterior fossa tumor.
METHODS: Procedurally, a 14-gauge Touhy needle percutaneously enters the L4-5 lumbar subarachnoid space. Once CSF is encountered, it is angled cranially and caudally to widen the needle durotomy. A retrospective review of pediatric patients was conducted at a single children's hospital from January 1, 2006, to January 1, 2022, for lumbar fenestration. All patients who underwent lumbar fenestration had clinical factors suggesting the need for ongoing CSF diversion during a clamp trial of their ventriculostomy. Inclusion criteria were 1) resection of a newly diagnosed posterior fossa tumor; 2) hydrocephalus on presentation; 3) ventriculostomy drain insertion at the time of or prior to surgery; and 4) lumbar fenestration following surgery.
RESULTS: In total, 44 patients met the inclusion criteria. The follow-up ranged from 1.8 to 191.1 months; the median follow-up was 84.2 months, the mean was 84.6 months, with a standard deviation of 60.2 months. There were 5 patients with < 1 year of follow-up. The most common pathology was medulloblastoma (n = 21), followed by pilocytic astrocytoma (n = 11), atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (n = 5), ependymoma (n = 4), pineoblastoma (n = 2), and malignant glioneuronal tumor (n = 1). The age at time of surgery ranged from 3 months to 15 years. Of the 44 patients included, 33 avoided a shunt. Stable or increased ventricular size after lumbar fenestration was statistically correlated with subsequent shunt placement (p = 0.0019). There were no complications linked to lumbar fenestration.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, there were minimal complications linked to lumbar fenestration and 75% of patients who had lumbar fenestration after failing a clamp trial avoided a shunt.

Title: Long-Term Outcomes of Mortality and CTEPH in Patients With Massive/Submassive Pulmonary Embolism Treated With Thrombolytics: Retro-Prospective Analysis.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: AimThis study aimed to determine mortality and morbidity in patients receiving fibrinolytic therapy for massive/submassive PE and the clinical factors affecting these outcomes.Materials and MethodsAll patients diagnosed with massive/submassive PE who received fibrinolytic therapy (alteplase) in our clinic between 2012 and 2024 were included in the study. Patients' medical records were retrospectively reviewed using the automation system and patient files.ResultsA total of 50 cases (31 women, 62%; 19 men, 38%) were included in the study. The mean age of the cases was 64±16 years (min: 21 - max: 93), and the median follow-up period was 1661 days (min: 1 - max: 4566 days). Half-dose fibrinolytic therapy was administered to 26% of cases, and full-dose therapy to 74%. The 2-day mortality rate was 10% (5/50), the 10-day mortality rate was26% (13/50), and the 30-day mortality rate was 28% (14/50). The median survival was found to be 2352 days (standard error: 304 days) for all cases who underwent reperfusion therapy. The 30-day mortality rate was significantly higher in patients receiving half-dose fibrinolytic therapy compared to those receiving full-dose therapy (53.8% vs. 18.9%, p=0.029). According to Cox regression analysis, malignancy was an independent risk factor negatively affecting survival, while obesity was a positive factor. CTEPH was detected in 28.5% (6/21) of the long-term followed cases.ConclusionThe effects of factors such as malignancy, obesity, and half-dose fibrinolytic therapy on mortality and morbidity in patients undergoing thrombolytic therapy with a diagnosis of massive/submassive PE should be investigated in more comprehensive studies.

Title: Dose-Response Associations of Exercise Modalities With Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure.
METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79).
CONCLUSIONS: The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

Title: An update on post-marketing safety signals of sugammadex: A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
Abstract: ObjectiveWith the expanding use of sugammadex, continued post-marketing surveillance remains warranted. This study aimed to characterize reporting patterns and update potential sugammadex-associated safety signals in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).MethodsWe conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study of FAERS reports from January 2012 through September 2025 in which sugammadex was the primary suspect drug. Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) preferred terms (PTs) were compared with all other drugs in the OpenVigil 2.1 FAERS reference set using the proportional reporting ratio (PRR), reporting odds ratio (ROR), and chi-square statistic. Signals were hypothesis-generating and did not establish incidence, comparative risk, or causality.ResultsA total of 1,077 unique cases were included. Among 887 cases with known sex, 443 (49.9%) were male and 444 (50.1%) were female; the median age among 710 age-known cases was 51 years (interquartile range, 29-66 years). Of 501 PTs evaluated, 92 met the prespecified statistical criteria. After separating 15 medication-error/product-use terms, 2 exposure terms, and 4 procedure/management descriptors, 71 clinical adverse-reaction PTs remained. In sensitivity analyses, 59 of 92 signals and 43 of 71 clinical PTs persisted at a ≥ 5; IC025 was >0 for 80 signals and conservative BH q-value upper bounds were <0.05 for 87 signals. Prominent clinical clusters involved hypersensitivity, cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuromuscular events. Kounis syndrome, complete atrioventricular block, and hypercapnia were absent from the approved adverse-reaction list, whereas post-procedural hemorrhage was interpreted in the context of labeled coagulation warnings.ConclusionsFAERS identified patterns of disproportionate reporting for sugammadex that warrant further evaluation, particularly for hypersensitivity and selected cardiovascular, respiratory, and neuromuscular events. These findings are signals rather than estimates of incidence, comparative risk, or causality. The three PTs absent from the approved adverse-reaction list require independent confirmation, and the post-procedural hemorrhage signal should be interpreted alongside labeled coagulation warnings.

Title: Respiratory Instability-driven Cardiac Dose Deviation in Postmastectomy Deep Inspiration Breath-hold Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy (DIBH VMAT): Development and External Validation of a Respiratory-informed Predictive Framework.
Journal: Clinical oncology (Royal College of Radiologists (Great Britain))
Abstract:
AIMS: Deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) reduces cardiac exposure during left-sided breast radiotherapy; however, treatment-day cardiac dose may differ from the planned dose because of variations in respiratory reproducibility and anatomy. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a framework for predicting fraction-level cardiac dose variation using routinely acquired respiratory, anatomical, and dosimetric information.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 150 patients treated with postmastectomy DIBH VMAT (volumetric modulated arc therapy) was analyzed. Models were developed using a 30-patient development cohort with patient-wise-nested cross-validation, externally validated in 20 independent patients using cone-beam CT-derived synthetic CT dose recalculation, and applied to a 100-patient deployment cohort. Separate models predicted deviation from planned per-fraction mean heart dose (ΔMHD) and left anterior descending coronary artery dose (ΔLADCA D0.03 cc) using treatment-day real-time position management (RPM)--derived respiratory features, planning computed tomography (CT)-derived geometric variables, and plan-derived dosimetric parameters. SHAP-based analysis was performed to identify influential predictors.
RESULTS: The final Gradient Boosting model for ΔMHD achieved an internal validation mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.541 ± 0.035 centigray (cGy) and coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.642 ± 0.069. The Ridge Regression model for left anterior descending coronary artery (ΔLADCA) achieved an MAE of 23.413 ± 1.617 cGy and R2 of 0.413 ± 0.082. External validation demonstrated good agreement for ΔMHD (MAE 0.58 cGy, R2 = 0.641), whereas ΔLADCA showed lower performance (MAE 24.14 cGy, R2 = 0.435). Stability index and baseline drift were key predictors.
CONCLUSION: Treatment-day-respiratory characteristics combined with anatomical and dosimetric variables can estimate fraction-level cardiac dose variation during DIBH radiotherapy. The framework may support verification-based clinical review, with further validation required before implementation.

Title: Decoding Atrial Fibrillation Heterogeneity: A Nationwide Phenome-Wide Association Study in England.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age and sex influence atrial fibrillation (AF) prevalence and outcomes, yet comprehensive data on sex- and age-specific health care utilization in patients newly diagnosed with AF remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to address this gap using a phenome-wide association study (Phe-WAS) approach.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using nationwide Clinical Practice Research Datalink data linked to Hospital Episodes Statistics. Adults diagnosed with AF between 1998 and 2016 (n = 199,433) were matched 1:1 by age and sex to non-AF control subjects. Primary and secondary care interactions 5 years post diagnosis were analyzed using Phe-WAS with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios for conditions in AF vs control groups, stratified by sex and age. Associations were assessed for novelty through literature review and causality using published Mendelian randomization studies.
RESULTS: Patients with AF had higher rates of cardiovascular and noncardiovascular conditions than control subjects, with marked sex- and age-specific patterns. Women had more bleeding complications, pneumonia, Clostridium difficile enterocolitis, cholangitis, and electrolyte disturbances, whereas men had higher rates of alcohol-related disorders, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, and cardiomyopathy. Younger patients with AF (<50 years) more often had alcohol-related mental and behavioral disorders, gout, and dilated cardiomyopathy, while older patients (>60 years) more often had heart failure, ischemic stroke, renal failure, and respiratory infections. Of 51 phenotypes more common in AF, 28 were previously reported, and 23 were potentially novel. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested AF was causal for 19 associations.
CONCLUSIONS: This Phe-WAS demonstrates the broad spectrum of health care interactions in AF beyond traditional cardiovascular complications.

Title: Incidence and clinical impact of venous thromboembolism during immunotherapy for gynecologic cancer.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes associated with venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with gynecologic cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with gynecologic malignancies treated with ICI at a single institution between January 2017 and April 2026. The primary outcome was the development of VTE from ICI initiation through one month after the final cycle. Incidence, clinical characteristics, risk factors, and healthcare utilization were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 458 patients who received ICI therapy, 37 (8.1%) experienced a VTE. Deep vein thrombosis was the most common event (48.6%, n = 18), followed by pulmonary embolism (40.5%, n = 15). The median time from ICI initiation to VTE was 1.43 months (IQR, 0.70-2.93). Endometrial cancer was the most common disease site among patients with VTE (54.1%, n = 20). Smoking history differed significantly between groups (p < 0.01). ICI monotherapy was more common among patients who experienced VTE compared with those who did not (64.9% vs. 44.9%, p = 0.020), and patients with VTE had received fewer total lines of therapy (2.4 vs. 3.3, p = 0.008). Most events required emergency department evaluation (64.9%, n = 24) and hospitalization (59.5%, n = 22), and ICI therapy was delayed in 24.3% (n = 9) of cases. Breakthrough thrombosis was observed in 18.9% (n = 7) of patients receiving anticoagulation.
CONCLUSION: VTE occurred in 8.1% of gynecologic cancer patients receiving ICI, was early in onset, and carried significant clinical burden. These data can guide provider awareness and patient counseling when initiating ICI in this population.

Title: AGraphHF: Adversarial graph-based multimodal learning for heart failure risk prediction.
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare utilization worldwide, yet early risk stratification remains challenging because prognostic information is distributed across heterogeneous clinical narratives and subtle electrophysiological abnormalities. We propose AGraphHF, a multimodal framework for incident HF risk prediction that integrates 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) with demographic-aware clinical text under a survival objective. The prediction task is temporally anchored at an index ECG and estimates the relative risk of subsequent HF onset under a longitudinal time-to-event formulation. The ECG encoder models individual leads as graph nodes and learns both inter-lead relationships and temporal dependencies using dual graph attention mechanisms. To enhance sensitivity to weak but prognostically relevant signal deviations, the model employs a two-phase adversarial training strategy with dual decoders, where stable reconstruction of typical ECG morphology is followed by deviation-focused refinement conditioned on reconstruction residuals. In parallel, clinical notes are encoded using a demographic-aware language model that extends BioClinicalBERT through age- and sex-conditioned contrastive pre-training. ECG and text representations are aligned in a shared latent space and fused hierarchically to produce patient-level risk estimates. We evaluate AGraphHF on high-risk cohorts derived from the MIMIC-IV database, including patients with hypertension and myocardial infarction. Experimental results demonstrate improved survival risk discrimination compared with established baselines on the hypertension and myocardial infarction cohorts, while also revealing cohort-dependent differences in the contribution of ECG and clinical text. These findings support the use of coordinated graph-based ECG modelling and demographic-aware multimodal integration for HF risk stratification, while emphasizing the need for cohort-specific interpretation of model performance.

Title: Postoperative recruitment and remodeling of middle meningeal artery collaterals in adult moyamoya disease: implications for preservation during combined revascularization.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The middle meningeal artery (MMA) may provide pre-existing transdural flow and postoperative collateral recruitment in adult moyamoya disease (MMD). We evaluated MMA remodeling, recruitment, and the safety relevance of preserving visible branches during combined revascularization.
METHODS: This retrospective hemisphere-level study included 110 operated hemispheres from 85 adults undergoing superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery bypass with encephaloduromyosynangiosis. Preoperative angiography showed visible MMA collaterals in 38 hemispheres and none in 72. Outcomes included vessel diameters, MMA caliber change ratio (MMA-CCR), Matsushima grade, and perioperative infarction. Groups were further classified by intraoperative MMA preservation or injury and by postoperative recruitment.
RESULTS: Hemispheres with visible preoperative collaterals had more advanced Suzuki stages (P < 0.001), larger postoperative MMA diameters (P = 0.006), and smaller postoperative donor superficial temporal artery diameters (P < 0.001). Among collateral-absent hemispheres, 56/72 (77.8%) developed postoperative MMA collaterals. Recruited hemispheres had better Matsushima grades (P = 0.001), larger preoperative (3.05 ± 1.14 vs 2.23 ± 1.19 mm; P = 0.016) and postoperative MMA diameters (P < 0.001), and higher MMA-CCR values (P < 0.001). Perioperative infarction occurred in 3/10 hemispheres with MMA injury and 0/28 with preservation (P = 0.014); this three-event association was exploratory.
CONCLUSION: The MMA showed postoperative recruitment and caliber remodeling. Visible branches should be preserved when technically feasible, although the observed association between injury and infarction requires validation.

Title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant.
CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

Title: Recurrence analysis of cardiac arrhythmias: A systematic review of methods, substrate characterisation and clinical translation.
Abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and catheter ablation depends on accurate identification of the underlying substrate. Cardiac signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, which limits Fourier-based analysis. Recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) and related recurrence methods make fewer assumptions, but their use in arrhythmia research has not been systematically synthesised. This review examines what recurrence analysis has demonstrated, how consistently its methods have been applied, and what remains before it can support clinical substrate characterisation. Of 309 records retrieved from four databases (207 after deduplication), 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and citation searching added one, giving 49. Each study was examined in full text for its signals, cohorts, embedding parameters, threshold selection, metrics and results, and assigned to one of six methodological categories. The three studies that tested recurrence against surrogate or shuffled data each found structure in fibrillatory signals that matched stochastic surrogates did not reproduce. Recurrence metrics and dominant frequency were weakly correlated and diverged in substrate characterisation, so they are not interchangeable. Threshold selection was the most consequential uncontrolled variable: five strategies were in use, ten of the 35 studies that apply a threshold reported no selection rule, and only three examined how their results depended on it. Determinism and laminarity, although the most frequently reported metrics, were not consistently the strongest discriminators. Clinical readiness is not established: only one study used recurrence mapping prospectively to guide ablation, in ten patients without randomisation. A shared threshold-selection standard and prospective multicentre validation are needed.

Title: Outcomes and Challenges of Redo Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Propensity-Matched Comparative Analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aims to compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of reoperative coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with primary CABG in a propensity score-matched patient cohort.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,021 patients who underwent CABG between January 2003 and January 2024. Among them, 35 (1.7%) patients underwent redo CABG. Using 1:1 propensity score matching based on age, ejection fraction, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension, 36 patients who underwent primary CABG were selected for comparison. Patients with incomplete records or combined cardiac procedures were excluded. Perioperative variables, in-hospital mortality, and long-term survival were analyzed.
RESULTS: The redo CABG group had significantly longer intensive care unit stays (2.15 ± 2.37 vs. 1.39 ± 1.36 days, P = 0.006), hospital stays (12.11 ± 17.40 vs. 7.36 ± 2.21 days, P = 0.009), and postoperative bleeding (899.12 ± 445.17 vs. 576.39 ± 323.92 ml, P = 0.001). Hospital mortality occurred in two patients (5.7%) in the redo group and one patient (2.8%) in the primary group (P = 0.614). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showed higher long-term survival in the redo CABG group (77.1%) compared to the primary CABG group (58.3%), though not statistically significant (P = 0.168).
CONCLUSION: Despite the increased perioperative complexity, redo CABG is associated with low in-hospital mortality and promising long-term outcomes when appropriate patient selection and meticulous surgical technique are employed. These findings are especially relevant in guiding revascularization strategies for patients with prior CABG, where redo surgery is often underutilized despite its clinical viability.

Title: Initiation of Medical Therapy for Storage Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms After Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Surgery.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: De-novo anticholinergic or beta-3 agonist (Ach/B3a) initiation for storage lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) is a clinically significant but understudied outcome after benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) surgery. We estimated procedure-specific cumulative incidence of Ach/B3a medication initiation and identified associated patient- and procedure-level factors.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using Michigan statewide claims data (2017-2022) from the Michigan Value Collaborative, Ach/B3a-naive patients who underwent BPH surgery were identified. Procedures included transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP), laser photovaporization (PVP), laser enucleation of the prostate (LEP), robotic waterjet therapy (RWJT), prostatic urethral lift (PUL), water vapor thermal therapy (WVTT), transurethral microwave thermotherapy (TUMT), prostatic artery embolization (PAE), and simple prostatectomy (SP). De-novo Ach/B3a initiation was defined as a prescription fill for an Ach/B3a between 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Cumulative incidence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis; Cox proportional hazards models identified associated factors.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 11,519 Ach/B3a medication-naive patients. Twelve-month cumulative incidence ranged from 5.7% (TUMT) to 11% (PVP). On multivariable analysis, PVP was associated with higher hazard of initiation compared to TURP (HR 1.49, 95% CI 1.25-1.79). Prior BPH medication use, and prior anticoagulation use were associated with higher hazard of initiation, while preoperative catheter dependence was associated with lower hazard.
CONCLUSIONS: In this statewide cohort of Anticholinergic and Beta-3 agonist naive patients undergoing contemporary BPH procedures, de-novo Ach/B3a medication initiation was uncommon but procedure-specific, with 12-month cumulative incidence ranging from 5.7% - 11%, with PVP carrying the highest hazard. These findings provide real-world benchmarks to guide counseling across contemporary BPH interventions.

Title: Wireless Home Blood Pressure Monitoring With Health Coaching for Hypertension Management at a Federally Qualified Health Center: Pilot Randomized Controlled Feasibility and Acceptability Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Only approximately half of adults with hypertension, a leading cardiovascular risk factor, achieve blood pressure (BP) control, with persistent disparities among low-income and minority populations. Wireless home BP monitoring (HBPM) with remote patient monitoring can improve BP control, but evidence is limited in medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic populations served by federally qualified health centers (FQHCs).
OBJECTIVE: The primary objective was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of wireless HBPM among predominantly Hispanic adults with hypertension receiving FQHC care. Comparing BP outcomes between wireless and conventional HBPM was a secondary exploratory objective.
METHODS: We conducted a 6-month, 2-arm randomized controlled pilot feasibility and acceptability trial nested within the San Diego: Heart Attack and Stroke Free Zone program. Adults aged ≥18 years with uncontrolled or newly diagnosed hypertension (BP ≥140/90 mm Hg) were enrolled across 3 FQHC networks and randomized 1:1 by unrestricted simple randomization to wireless HBPM (Bluetooth cuff and cellular hub; weekly transmitted summaries reviewed by health coaches) or standard HBPM (home monitor with paper log). Both arms received standardized health coaching. The primary outcomes were feasibility (proportion of 210 expected BP readings transmitted) and acceptability (postintervention satisfaction survey in the wireless arm). Exploratory analyses compared BP outcomes between arms among participants with >2 BP measurements.
RESULTS: Of 316 recruited participants, 290 (92%) were eligible, and 200 (63%) were analyzed (wireless: n=73, 23%; and standard: n=127, 40%); arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The mean age was 61 years (SD 9.1), 57% (115/200) were women, and 51% (n=102) self-identified as Hispanic, with no significant baseline differences between arms. Among analyzed wireless-arm participants, 86% (63/73) transmitted multiple readings (mean 160.6, SD 129.1) over 6 months, corresponding to 76.2% (160/210) of expected readings among transmitting participants and 66% across all 73; only 5% (7/127) of standard-arm participants returned paper logs. Of 60 respondents (82.2% response rate), 95% (n=57) agreed or strongly agreed that the device was easy to set up and use. Both arms showed significant within-arm BP reductions at 6 months (P<.001). At 6 months, 63% (46/73) of the wireless arm and 74% (94/127) of the standard arm achieved systolic BP <140 mm Hg (P=.08; adjusted odds ratio, standard vs wireless, 1.6, 95% CI 0.78-3.4; P=.19). These exploratory comparisons were not powered and do not constitute evidence of equivalence.
CONCLUSIONS: Among analyzed participants, wireless HBPM was feasible, and survey respondents reported high acceptability in a medically underserved, predominantly Hispanic FQHC population. Feasibility among all randomized participants could not be estimated because arm-level allocation counts were not retained. The absence of a between-arm difference in BP control is not evidence of equivalence because this pilot was not powered to compare clinical effectiveness; the BP findings are hypothesis generating.

Title: Temporal Patterns of Multimorbidity Progression Among Inpatients With a Recorded Hypertension Diagnosis Across Three Counties in Rural Henan, China: Retrospective Cohort Study Using Temporal Network Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a key driver of multimorbidity; however, its role in shaping dynamic disease progression, especially in rural populations, remains underexplored.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize temporal patterns of multimorbidity progression among inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis and to examine whether these patterns differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county.
METHODS: We analyzed electronic health record data from 34,099 inpatients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis across 3 rural counties in Henan, China (2019-2023), constructing a temporal comorbidity network of 250 disease nodes and 1512 disease transitions. Statistical validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, case-dropping, and permutation tests. Subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, insurance type, and county.
RESULTS: The temporal comorbidity network revealed a densely interconnected core involving hypertension, atherosclerotic heart disease, and cerebral infarction, with type 2 diabetes occupying a bridging position between cardiovascular and multisystem disease clusters. The ordering of dominant recorded pathways differed by sex (earlier coronary involvement among female inpatients vs more direct progression to stroke among male inpatients), was more complex in inpatients older than 70 years of age, and was more diffuse among those covered by urban-rural resident insurance compared with urban employee insurance.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimorbidity among inpatients with recorded hypertension followed structured and heterogeneous temporal patterns that differed by sex, age, insurance type, and county. Cardiovascular and cerebrovascular conditions formed the principal recorded progression pathways, while type 2 diabetes connected cardiovascular pathways with broader multisystem complications. These findings support further evaluation of risk-stratified and locally adapted approaches to chronic disease prevention and longitudinal care.

Title: Abdominal circumference and its relationship with the incidence of hypotension during elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypotension is a common complication in pregnant mothers during cesarean section after spinal anesthesia. Identifying the association between abdominal circumference and the likelihood of developing hypotension following a cesarean delivery while under spinal anesthesia can facilitate preventing hypotension.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to assess the relationship between the abdominal circumference of pregnant women and the occurrence of hypotension during cesarean section under spinal anesthesia at public hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, 2024.
METHOD: A prospective observational study through a simple systematic random sampling technique was conducted on 360 pregnant mothers who underwent elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia from January 7, 2024, to March 30, 2024. Data was collected using a data collection questionnaire and checklist. The data was entered using Epi Info 7.2 and exported into SPSS 26. The Patients were categorized by their median abdominal circumference, < 102 cm (small abdominal circumference (SAC)) and ≥102 cm (large abdominal circumference (LAC)). The chi-square test was used to compare the numerical and percentage representations of the categorical variables. Descriptive analyses, bivariate logistic regression, and multivariate regression were carried out. In multivariate variables, p ≤ 0.05 was used as statistical significance, and an odds ratio was used for the strength of association.
RESULT: Among 360 study subjects, the incidence of post-spinal hypotension was 76.67% with 95%CI [71.9-80.9]. The Large abdominal circumference (LAC) group showed a greater maximal decrease in MAP from baseline compared to the SAC group (LAC 85.6% and SAC 63.3%, p < 0.001). The identified associated factors with the incidence of hypotension were LAC (AOR = 2.98, 95% CI [1.57, 5.65] p = 0.01); BMI > 25 kg/m2 (AOR = 2.3, 95%CI [1.16-4.6], P = 0.018); baby weight> 4 kg (AOR = 11.41 95%CI [2.0-64.86] P = 0.006); sensory block of above T6 level (AOR = 2.22, 95%CI [1.12, 4.42]) p = 0.023) and greater than 500 ml preload given (AOR = 0.42 [95%CI 0.2-0.89] p = 0.023.
CONCLUSIONS: The study found that there was a high incidence of hypotension during elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia and a significant difference between the SAC and LAC groups. Also, the study found that the independent factors significantly associated with the incidence of hypotension were LAC, higher BMI, higher baby weight, and higher sensory block level, while greater preload volume was protective.

Title: A public-data audit of transcriptomic prognostic transportability in R-CHOP-treated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
Abstract: Gene-expression biomarkers for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) are often transported across retrospective cohorts that differ in treatment, assay platform, and clinical annotation. Using REMARK as the reporting framework, we audited prognostic associations with fixed scoring rules. Four Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts were harmonized for survival analysis. Treatment context was assessed after outcome-blind transcriptional state discovery. A directly mapped five-gene historical benchmark was evaluated with continuous Cox models in four R-CHOP cohorts. A 76-gene program selected in GSE31312 and GSE10846 served as a case study of two-cohort discovery, with GSE87371 as the only full-coverage independent evaluation and GSE32918 as a cross-platform sensitivity analysis. Coverage ablation, technical replicates, matched random programs, meta-analysis, and clinical-increment analyses assessed attenuation. The survival analyses included 470, 232, 87, and 140 patients. State composition was strongly associated with CHOP versus R-CHOP context in GSE10846 (Cramer's V = 0.986). The historical score's unadjusted random-effects hazard ratio (HR) was 1.35 (95% confidence interval 1.04-1.75); the prediction interval crossed the null (0.77-2.37). Common age/sex adjustment yielded HR 1.27 (1.05-1.54), with a prediction interval of 0.94-1.72. The 76-gene program was not independently validated in GSE87371 (unadjusted HR 1.23, 0.87-1.75; IPI/COO-adjusted HR 0.88, 0.56-1.40; age/sex-adjusted HR 1.09, 0.76-1.55). Its effect exceeded most matched random programs, but cross-cohort attenuation was pronounced and estimated clinical increment was negligible. With only 32 validation events, modest effects remain compatible with the data. Public DLBCL transcriptomic associations can be cohort-specific despite fixed scoring rules. Independent full-coverage evaluation and transparent treatment and platform audits should precede claims of general prognostic utility.

Title: Risk of myocardial infarction in adults with gout treated with allopurinol: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: AimsAlthough allopurinol is used for urate-lowering therapy, its effect on myocardial infarction risk remains unclear. This study assessed the association between allopurinol use and myocardial infarction in adults with gout.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PROSPERO registration (CRD420261305257). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to January 2026. Observational studies of adults with confirmed gout that reported adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) for myocardial infarction and separately identifiable allopurinol exposure were included. Pooled estimates were calculated using an inverse-variance random-effects model with the Paule-Mandel estimator. Robustness was assessed through leave-one-out, active-comparator, and Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses.ResultsFour retrospective cohort studies met the revised eligibility criteria. In the primary random-effects analysis, allopurinol use was associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.76-0.94; I2 = 0%). However, the association was not statistically significant after excluding the study contributing the greatest weight (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), when restricted to active comparators (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.79-1.36), or using the Hartung-Knapp adjustment (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-1.00).ConclusionAllopurinol therapy was associated with a modest but significant reduction in myocardial infarction risk in adults with gout.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Search for the glycated hemoglobin target minimizing mortality among people with type 2 diabetes with rare incidence of treatment-related severe hypoglycemia - Epidemiologic analysis of J-DOIT3 randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In recent years, with the considerable changes in the therapeutic armamentarium for diabetes, the incidence of hypoglycemia events, especially severe hypoglycemia events, associated with drug treatment in people with diabetes has markedly decreased. We were prompted to evaluate the threshold for each intervention target, especially glycemic control, associated with a minimized risk of the macrovascular complications of diabetes in this setting.
METHODS: In the Japan Diabetes Optimal Integrated Treatment study for 3 major risk factors of cardiovascular diseases (J-DOIT3) conducted by us previously, we recruited 2542 participants and assigned them to a conventional therapy group (n = 1271) and an intensive therapy group (n = 1271; two ineligible participants were removed from all analyses afterwards), and the incidence of severe hypoglycemia events was low in both groups (7 in the intensive therapy group and 4 in the conventional therapy group during a median 8.5 years' follow-up). Towards the objective of this study, we undertook a landmark analysis with a landmark time-point of 1 year after the baseline of the J-DOIT3 study. Then, using the updated mean values of the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), systolic blood pressure, and LDL-cholesterol and HDL-cholesterol levels, we determined the optimal levels of each of these variables associated with the lowest hazard ratios for outcomes, including the primary and cardiovascular outcomes.
RESULTS: For glycemic control, our results revealed no clear lower threshold of the glycated hemoglobin associated with the lowest risk of myocardial infarction or all-cause mortality; for other risk factors, it might be an important treatment target to maintain the LDL-cholesterol levels at below 80 mg/dL to minimize the risk of stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: The present analysis suggested that the treatment target for HbA1c to minimize the risk of all-cause mortality in participants with diabetes with a low incidence of severe hypoglycemia episodes could be < 6.5% (ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00300976).
Publication Types: Equivalence Trial; Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Lens dislocation, OCTA, and archived FBN1 reports: An exploratory study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis) is a recognized anterior-segment manifestation of fibrillinopathy. This exploratory phenotype-first study compared macular optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) parameters between participants with and without documented lens dislocation and descriptively reviewed available archived clinical FBN1 reports.
METHODS: This retrospective, availability-based study included 16 participants classified by verified current or historical lens-dislocation status. Participant-level superficial capillary plexus (SCP) vessel density was calculated by averaging valid bilateral measurements or using the single valid eye. Five OCTA endpoints were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests; Benjamini-Hochberg q values were used as a multiplicity sensitivity analysis. Seven archived clinical FBN1 reports from lens-dislocation-positive (LD+) participants were summarized without variant reclassification. No genotype-OCTA association was assessed.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 7 LD+ and 9 lens-dislocation-negative (LD-) participants; 15 participants (6 LD+ and 9 LD-) contributed quantitative OCTA data. Foveal SCP vessel density was lower in LD+ participants (median [IQR], 19.38% [18.68-20.04] vs 30.20% [29.20-31.85]; p = 0.036), but the finding was not retained after multiplicity sensitivity analysis (q = 0.180). Whole-image, parafoveal, and perifoveal vessel-density comparisons were not significant (p = 0.328, 0.272, and 0.238; q = 0.410 each), and OD-only foveal avascular zone area did not differ (n = 14; p = 0.606; q = 0.606). Six of seven archived reports documented an FBN1 variant; one was negative within its assay scope.
CONCLUSIONS: The unadjusted foveal signal was not robust to multiplicity analysis, and other OCTA endpoints did not differ significantly. Marked between-group differences in spherical equivalent and axial length, the small sample, and heterogeneous routine-care genetic reports limit interpretation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish OCTA as a diagnostic or prognostic test or demonstrate an individual-level genotype-OCTA association.

Title: Longitudinal blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients: A Bayesian multivariate joint modeling study in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hypertension being its most important modifiable risk factor. Although the association between elevated blood pressure and stroke is well established, the extent to which longitudinal blood pressure patterns influence the timing of stroke remains poorly understood, particularly in low-resource settings. We investigated the association between longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories and time to stroke among hypertensive patients in Ethiopia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 494 newly diagnosed hypertensive patients receiving follow-up care at two general hospitals in Benishangul-Gumuz, Ethiopia, between January 1, 2015, and September 1, 2024. Time to stroke was analyzed using a Cox proportional hazards model, while repeated systolic and diastolic blood pressure measurements were modelled using linear mixed-effects models. The longitudinal and survival processes were jointly estimated using a Bayesian multivariate joint modelling framework. Posterior adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated.
RESULTS: The incidence of stroke was 2.19 per 100 person-years (95% CI: 1.60-2.64). Higher current underlying systolic and diastolic blood pressure levels were associated with increased stroke risk, with posterior AHRs of 3.25 (95% CrI: 1.85-5.83) and 2.32 (95% CrI: 1.35-4.27), respectively. Older age (≥65 years; AHR: 6.18; 95% CrI: 2.32-18.05), comorbidity (AHR: 4.00; 95% CrI: 1.72-10.25), and stage II hypertension (AHR: 4.06; 95% CrI: 1.49-16.36) were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. Rural residence was associated with a lower hazard of stroke (AHR: 0.16; 95% CrI: 0.05-0.40).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher longitudinal systolic and diastolic blood pressure trajectories were associated with earlier stroke occurrence. These findings support regular blood pressure monitoring and targeted prevention strategies among older adults and patients with comorbidities in similar resource-limited settings.

Title: Correction: Ultrasound-guided microwave ablation versus conventional surgery for Granulomatous Lobular Mastitis: A two-center retrospective comparative stud.

Title: Feasibility of 2% Taurolidine Lock Therapy in 1-2 Fr Neonatal PICCs: A Three Patient Case series.
Abstract: Introduction Catheter-related bloodstream infection remains a major complication of neonatal central venous access. Although taurolidine lock therapy has been used in neonatal populations, experience with taurolidine locking in ultra-small (1-2 Fr) neonatal peripherally inserted central catheters (n-PICCs) remains extremely limited. This study describes the feasibility of repeated 2% taurolidine lock therapy in neonates requiring prolonged central vascular access. Methods We retrospectively reviewed three neonates who received repeated 2% taurolidine lock therapy during routine care in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit. Locks were administered using a standardized local protocol for therapeutic or prophylactic indications. Collected data included catheter characteristics, lock administration and aspiration, flushing requirements, catheter patency, adverse events, and clinical outcomes. Results Taurolidine lock therapy was performed in 1-2 Fr n-PICCs, with all 30 planned procedures completed. Aspiration after the dwell period was unsuccessful in every procedure, requiring flushing of the residual solution. Catheter patency was maintained, with no occlusion, thrombosis, mechanical complications, or taurolidine-related adverse events. Bloodstream infection resolved with concomitant systemic antimicrobials in the therapeutic case, while no catheter-related bloodstream infection occurred during prophylactic locking. Conclusion This preliminary clinical experience demonstrates the technical feasibility of repeated 2% taurolidine lock therapy in ultra-small n-PICCs while maintaining catheter patency. The consistent inability to aspirate the lock solution represents an important practical observation for future investigation. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the feasibility and safety of taurolidine lock therapy as a catheter-preserving strategy in neonates. A multicentre randomized controlled trial is planned to further investigate this approach.

Title: Comparative evaluation of YOLO models for retained root fragment detection.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and comparatively evaluate four YOLO nano-scale one-stage object detectors-YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLO11n, and YOLO12n-for the automated detection of retained root fragments in dental radiographic images, under identical preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocols.
METHODS: A curated dataset was organized in the YOLO format and evaluated using a nested 5-fold cross-validation strategy to prevent data leakage. An ablation study was additionally conducted to validate the combined bilateral filtering and histogram equalization (BF + HE) preprocessing pipeline. Four YOLO models were fine-tuned from official pretrained weights over 200 epochs. Detection performance was assessed at both the epoch level and the decision-threshold level, reporting the unbiased mean and standard deviation across the independent test folds for precision, sensitivity, F1 score, mean average precision (mAP), and false positives per image (FP/image).
RESULTS: In the primary multi-model benchmark, YOLO12n achieved the highest overall detection performance across the held-out test folds, yielding a mean best-epoch F1 score of 0.885 ± 0.007, mAP@0.5 of 0.919 ± 0.021, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.447 ± 0.025 (reaching an optimal-threshold F1 score of 0.888 ± 0.016 with 0.346 ± 0.052 FP/image). YOLO11n followed closely as the second-best performing architecture (F1 = 0.874 ± 0.012, mAP@0.5:0.95 = 0.445 ± 0.019). Furthermore, the preprocessing ablation study confirmed that the hybrid BF + HE pipeline improved detection performance over raw radiographs, elevating YOLO12n's F1 score from 0.856 ± 0.013 to 0.888 ± 0.016 and mAP@0.5:0.95 from 0.438 ± 0.011 to 0.461 ± 0.008. All models demonstrated stable convergence behavior.
CONCLUSIONS: Modern YOLO architectures, particularly YOLO12n and YOLO11n, demonstrate technical efficacy for automated RRF localization. The observed performance advantages of YOLO12n are associated with its overall architectural refinements, though dedicated modular ablation studies are warranted to isolate the exact contribution of individual attention mechanisms. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of lightweight one-stage object detectors for identifying retained root fragments in dental panoramic radiographs, serving as a baseline for future prospective clinical evaluations.

Title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624).
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

Title: Bridging the Evidence Gap: A Call to Action for Anticoagulation Research in Pediatric Burned Patients on Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
Journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
Abstract: Although early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) improves respiratory complications in unburned populations, it remains a rarely utilized rescue therapy in pediatric burn care, averaging just 3 to 6 cases annually worldwide despite a promising 53-62% survival rate. This underutilization stems from a profound therapeutic paradox: the high bleeding risks and need for coagulation inherent to burn wounds with necessary surgical debridement directly conflict with the systemic anticoagulation required to prevent ECMO circuit thrombosis. Importantly, emerging evidence demonstrates that systemic anticoagulation may not be an absolute requirement for veno-venous ECMO. Despite this, no guidance exists for anticoagulation management specifically in pediatric burned patients. A scoping review spanning three databases identified no studies describing a coagulation strategy developed or validated for this population. Addressing this evidence gap is essential to safely transition ECMO from a late rescue modality to an earlier, evidence-based intervention capable of reducing mortality in this patient population. We therefore call for (1) a multicenter collaboration to aggregate sufficient case volume for meaningful analysis; (2) a prospective collection of serial viscoelastic and conventional coagulation data in pediatric burned patients on ECMO to characterize the temporal evolution of coagulopathy on circuit; and (3) the development and validation of coagulation management protocols tailored to this population. Until such evidence exists, pediatric burned patients will continue to be denied a therapy that offers meaningful survival-not because ECMO does not work-but because we have not yet determined how best to manage coagulation while on circuit.

Title: Q-AortaECG: A Quantum-Inspired Multi-Agent 12-Lead ECG System for Early Triage of Acute Aortic Syndrome.
Journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
Abstract: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a time-critical vascular emergency in which delayed recognition may occur because the presenting symptoms and electrocardiographic phenotypes often overlap with acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, pericarditis, and other emergency diagnoses. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) remains the confirmatory standard, but the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is usually obtained earlier, is universally available at triage, and may carry distributed signatures of malperfusion, ischemia mimicry, autonomic stress, conduction delay, and hemodynamic compromise. We developed Q-AortaECG, a classically implemented quantum-inspired multi-agent ECG system that integrates multiscale waveform representations, specialist ECG agents, density-state uncertainty fusion, a variational-circuit style consensus layer, and a safety-gated multidisciplinary team-style report for early AAS triage. The system was evaluated in three suspected-AAS/CTA-evaluable cohorts comprising 1,251 patients, including 467 with CTA-, surgery-, or autopsy-confirmed AAS. Across 700 locked-test patients, Q-AortaECG achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.881 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.852-0.908), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.743 (95% CI, 0.695-0.790), sensitivity of 0.955 (231/242; 95% CI, 0.920-0.977), specificity of 0.721 (330/458; 95% CI, 0.677-0.761), positive predictive value (PPV) of 0.643, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.968 at the prespecified high-sensitivity threshold. Performance remained consistent in external retrospective validation and prospective silent-run evaluation, although AUPRC decreased in the lower-prevalence prospective cohort. Ablation experiments supported the contributions of self-supervised ECG pretraining, agent specialization, density-matrix uncertainty fusion, and differential diagnosis modeling. In a counterbalanced paired reader study, Q-AortaECG assistance improved overall clinician sensitivity from 0.696 to 0.870 while preserving specificity (0.851 ver sus 0.846). In prospective silent-run analysis, counterfactual alerts would have advanced the median time to the correct diagnostic pathway from 187 to 61 minutes among initially unsuspected AAS presentations. These findings support ECG first, calibrated, safety-gated decision support as an early warning scaffold for AAS triage, while preserving CTA and expert imaging interpretation as the diagnostic standard.

Title: Survival and Functional Status Outcomes in Heart Transplant Recipients: An Analysis of Organs From Donors Who Overdosed.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Escalating deaths associated with the opioid crisis has increased availability of transplant organs from donors who died of a drug overdose, yet perception of these organs as "increased risk" contributes to their unnecessary discard. Previous research addressing this issue has focused solely on survival outcomes, but quality of life is also a crucial factor in determining transplant success.
METHODS: In this study, a secondary analysis of data representing adult, first-time heart transplant recipients from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients between January 1, 2016, and March 1, 2020 was conducted. Logistic regression modeled one-year survival and functional status at one-year, and Cox proportional hazards modeled survival time post-transplant. Non-inferiority testing compared survival and functional status outcomes for overdose donor (n = 2240) and non-overdose donor (n = 9427) organ recipients.
RESULTS: When not controlling for significant covariates, one-year survival rates, post-transplant survival time, and one-year Karnofsky scores were at least as good or better for overdose donor organ recipients compared to non-overdose organ recipients based on a-priori non-inferiority thresholds; estimated OR for one-year survival is 1.0207 (95% CI [0.863, 1.213]), estimated hazards ratio is 0.9425 (95% CI [0.823, 1.079]), and estimated OR for having high one-year functional status is 0.9035 (95% CI [0.769, 1.066]). Controlling for significant covariates, one-year survival (OR 0.9613, 95% CI [0.790, 1.176]) and functional status (OR 1.0181, 95% CI [0.855, 1.218]) remained at least as good or better for overdose donor recipients; survival time was also estimated to be as good or better for overdose organ recipients when controlling for significant covariates (HR 0.9611, 95% CI [0.828, 1.115]), but not to the level of statistical significance based on the non-inferiority threshold.
CONCLUSION: Overall, post-transplant survival times, one-year survival rates, and one-year functional status are similar for overdose and non-overdose organ heart transplant recipients. These findings support a broader utilization of the drug overdose donor pool, especially as the demand for heart transplantation increases.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Dietary Behaviors and Urinary Biomarkers in a Self-Management Support Program Among Low-Income Adults with CKD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: CKD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged populations, among whom adoption of kidney-friendly diets is often constrained by structural barriers. Self-management support (SMS) programs can improve CKD awareness and cardiovascular risk factors; however, their ability to influence dietary behaviors and diet-related physiologic markers when nutrition content is limited remains uncertain. We evaluated whether participation in a culturally tailored SMS program with modest dietary education was associated with changes in self-reported dietary behaviors and urinary biomarkers among low-income adults with CKD.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary exploratory analysis of a randomized controlled trial (NCT01530958) among low-income adults with early-to-moderate CKD. Participants were randomized to an SMS program that included limited dietary education focused on reducing sodium, refined sugar, and fast-food consumption. Outcomes included self-reported intake of soda, fruit-flavored drinks, and fast food, as well as urinary biomarkers reflecting sodium-potassium balance and inflammation, including sodium-to-potassium ratio (Na/K), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1). Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and body mass index were used to assess associations at intervention completion and 6-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Among 266 participants (mean age 57.5 years; 51% men; 34% African American, 36% Hispanic, 19% Asian/Pacific Islander, and 9% non-Hispanic White), 97% reported annual household income below $50,000. The intervention was not associated with significant changes in self-reported dietary behaviors, urinary Na/K ratio (β [95% CI]: 0.24 [ -0.61, 1.09]), urinary IL-6 (-1.86 [-4.96, 1.25]), or urinary TGF-β1 (5.41 [-1.08, 11.54]). A modest reduction in urinary TNF-α was observed (-0.24 [-0.43, -0.02]).
CONCLUSIONS: In this low-income CKD population, an SMS program with limited dietary content was not sufficient to produce measurable changes in dietary behaviors or most diet-related urinary biomarkers. These findings underscore the need for more intensive, nutrition-focused, and structurally supported interventions to achieve meaningful dietary and physiologic change in CKD.

Title: High cardiometabolic burden among people with HIV and obesity in Peru.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiometabolic disease has been studied in people with HIV, but evidence focused on people with HIV and obesity remains limited. This study assessed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, metabolic abnormalities, markers of inflammation, and cardiovascular risk scores among people with HIV and obesity.
METHODS: We conducted an observational, cross-sectional study in clinically stable people with HIV aged ≥35 years and BMI >30 kg/m² in Lima-Callao, Peru, in 2024.
RESULTS: Participants enroled were 126; 77.7% were male, mean age was 50.6 years, mean time on antiretroviral therapy (ART) was 12.4 years, mean CD4 count was 759.8 cells/µL, and 97.6% had HIV-RNA <200 copies/µL. Mean BMI was 34.0. Clinical cardiovascular disease history was uncommon (2.4%); however, carotid Doppler ultrasound showed atherosclerotic changes in 34.4% (increased CIMT or carotid plaque), which associated with older age and longer time of ART. Abnormal glucose metabolism was identified in 89.7%, dyslipidemia in 82.5%, metabolic syndrome in 50.8%, elevated inflammatory markers in 28.2%, and low apolipoprotein A1 in 22.6%. Only 8.1% had normal findings across all evaluations. High cardiovascular risk was observed in 19.4% by Framingham, 9.4% by ACC/AHA, and 75.4% by HIV-CARDIO-PREDICT score.
CONCLUSIONS: This population of middle-aged, clinically stable people with HIV and obesity presented substantial burden of subclinical atherosclerosis and metabolic abnormalities despite low reported cardiovascular disease history. Cardiovascular risk estimates varied substantially across scores, with an HIV-specific score identifying a much higher proportion of patients as high risk than general-population scores. Targeted evaluation and timely preventive management may help reduce cardiometabolic complications.

Title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling.
