IMPACT: By leveraging nurses and a widely accessible instant messaging platform, this study will demonstrate a scalable mobile health approach to address the leading dietary risk factor for stroke burden in China, potentially applicable to similar settings where sodium intake is amenable to behavioural interventions and contributing to the World Health Organization's global sodium reduction target.
REPORTING METHOD: SPIRIT 2013 Statement.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Health professionals, stroke survivors and family caregivers were invited to evaluate the intervention development.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400086708.

Title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns.
METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.
RESULTS: Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18]; P=0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62]; P=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis' benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (P=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

Title: Comparison of DOAC Versus VKA for Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. Studies published between January 2007 and July 2025 were included. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, DOAC class (anti-factor Xa inhibitors versus direct thrombin inhibitors), and VKA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions for observational studies. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies (8 randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 6 observational studies) were included. Among 3698 patients, 1669 (45.1%) received DOACs and 2029 (54.9%) received VKAs. Rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (10.24% versus 10.99%), major bleeding (4.26% versus 6.18%), clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (2.63% versus 1.66%), good functional outcomes (95.09% versus 89.25%), and mortality (3.37% versus 3.30%) were similar in DOACs and VKAs. Recurrent venous thromboembolism was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.35-3.24]) and in the overall pooled analysis of all studies (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55-1.53]). Major bleeding did not differ between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.24-2.22]) or in the overall analysis (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44-1.25]; P=0.26). Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was also comparable in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.25-4.48]) and overall (RR, 1.22 [95% CI, 0.38-3.86]). Good functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2) were similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.84-1.19]) and in the combined analysis of all studies (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.11]). Mortality was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.28-4.68]) and in the pooled analysis. When direct thrombin inhibitors were compared with factor Xa inhibitors, there were no significant differences in outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to VKAs in the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. These findings support the use of DOACs as a reasonable alternative.

Title: Computed-Tomography Angiography-Based Carotid Plaque-RADS, Recurrent Vascular Events, and the Effect of Colchicine: An Imaging Substudy of the CONVINCE Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) provides a standardized framework for evaluating plaque morphology, but prospective validation remains limited. We investigated the association between computed tomography angiography-based Plaque-RADS categories and subsequent ischemic events in patients with noncardioembolic stroke/transient ischemic attack, from a completed clinical trial of colchicine. Second, we assessed whether the effect of colchicine differed by Plaque-RADS risk classification.
METHODS: We conducted a posthoc observational cohort analysis of 517 participants in the CONVINCE trial (Colchicine for Prevention of Vascular Inflammation in Non-CardioEmbolic Stroke) from 13 European sites. Associations between Plaque-RADS and recurrent ipsilateral stroke, any stroke/transient ischemic attack, and major adverse cardiovascular events were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Plaque-RADS was analyzed as both dichotomized (<3 versus ≥3) and ordinal (per 1-point increase) variables. Treatment effects were assessed by Plaque-RADS classification using interaction and stratified analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 510 patients (median age, 67.0 years; 72.2% male) with 966 internal carotid arteries were included. Among 321 internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, 12 recurrent ipsilateral strokes, 32 any strokes/transient ischemic attacks, and 37 major adverse cardiovascular events occurred over a median 35.7-month follow-up. Plaque-RADS ≥3 (n=140) was independently associated with recurrent ipsilateral stroke (adjusted hazard ratio, 7.80 [95% CI, 1.55-39.30]; P=0.01), any stroke/transient ischemic attack (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.94 [95% CI, 1.68-9.24]; P<0.01), and major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.52 [95% CI, 1.19-5.34]; P=0.02) after adjustment for age, sex and cardiovascular risk factors. A significant interaction with colchicine treatment was observed for major adverse cardiovascular events (P=0.047), with greater benefit among patients with Plaque-RADS scores ≥3 (hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.15-0.82]).
CONCLUSIONS: In internal carotid arteries ipsilateral to the index ischemic stroke, computed tomography angiography-based carotid Plaque-RADS was associated with recurrent ischemic stroke and cardiovascular events. Importantly, treatment effects of colchicine varied across Plaque-RADS classification (<3 versus ≥3), suggesting that plaque vulnerability assessment may help refine patient selection for anti-inflammatory therapy beyond stenosis-based classification.

Title: Impact of Guideline-Recommended LDL-C Goals on Coronary Plaque in a Post-PCI Setting: A Posthoc OCT Substudy of the CUT-DRESS Trial.
Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

Title: Association of Hemispheric Laterality With Neurosurgical Intervention in Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Posthoc Bayesian Analysis of ATACH-2 and ERICH.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemispheric laterality influences clinical management in stroke. Given the increasing enthusiasm for surgical management of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), we evaluated the association of hemispheric laterality with the likelihood of receiving neurosurgical intervention and subsequent 90-day functional outcomes.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis included 3477 patients with supratentorial ICH from 2 prospective studies: the ATACH-2 trial (Antihypertensive Treatment of Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage II), conducted at 110 sites in the United States, Japan, China, Taiwan, South Korea, and Germany (2011-2015), and the ERICH study (Ethnic/Racial Variations of Intracerebral Hemorrhage), conducted across 19 centers in the United States (2010-2015). The primary outcome was neurosurgical intervention (hematoma evacuation, decompressive craniectomy, or other craniotomy). Secondary outcomes included external ventricular drain placement, 90-day modified Rankin Scale score, and EuroQOL domains. Hierarchical Bayesian regression models estimating the association between ICH laterality and outcomes were adjusted for age, admission Glasgow Coma Scale, ICH location, ICH volume, and intraventricular hemorrhage.
RESULTS: Of 3477 patients, right hemispheric ICH was associated with a higher likelihood of receiving neurosurgical intervention (adjusted odds ratio, 1.65 [95% credible interval, 1.28-2.14]) and external ventricular drain placement (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% credible interval, 1.04-1.44]) compared with left hemispheric ICH. This association was directionally consistent across ICH locations, study cohorts, and prior specifications. Despite the lower rates of surgical intervention in left hemispheric ICH, there was no meaningful difference in 90-day functional outcomes in patients with left and right hemispheric ICH.
CONCLUSIONS: Right hemispheric ICH is associated with a higher likelihood of neurosurgical intervention compared with left hemispheric ICH, though 90-day functional outcomes remain similar between groups. Although these findings highlight a potential laterality-associated variation in neurosurgical intervention, residual confounding from unmeasured anatomic severity and family preferences cannot be excluded. Prospective studies are needed to delineate the explicit clinical and prognostic drivers of surgical decision-making to optimize treatment allocation in ICH.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT01176565 and NCT01202864.

Title: Contemporary US Practice Patterns Regarding Anticoagulation and LAA Closure in ICH Survivors With Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal secondary stroke prevention remains uncertain for patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and atrial fibrillation (AF). Anticoagulation reduces ischemic stroke in AF but increases hemorrhage. Left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion is emerging as an alternative to anticoagulation, but few data exist on its safety in patients with ICH. Amid this uncertainty, little is known about US practice patterns in this scenario.
METHODS: We performed a study using linked electronic health record, pharmacy, and insurance claims data on >11 million patients at 29 US healthcare organizations, each with multiple hospital sites, in the TriNetX Linked platform. Validated International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes were used to identify adults with AF hospitalized for ICH during 2016 to 2024. To identify antiplatelet and anticoagulant prescriptions, we used RxNorm codes, a standardized drug naming system from the National Library of Medicine. LAA occlusion was defined using validated Current Procedural Terminology codes. Kaplan-Meier statistics were used to calculate cumulative rates of therapy utilization from discharge through 5 years. We created 3 mutually exclusive treatment groups with censoring at LAA occlusion for analyses of antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy and at anticoagulation for analyses of antiplatelet therapy.
RESULTS: We identified 2276 patients with AF hospitalized with ICH. Their mean age was 65.4 (±12.8) years, 40.6% were female, median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 5 (interquartile range, 5-6), 19.6% had Medicare, 26.9% received an anticoagulant prescription within 90 days before ICH, and half were discharged home or to an acute rehabilitation facility. Cumulative 5-year rates were 59.8% (95% CI, 55.5%-64.2%) for anticoagulation, 39.9% (95% CI, 34.1%-46.3%) for antiplatelet therapy, and 4.5% (95% CI, 2.6%-7.6%) for LAA occlusion. LAA occlusion rates did not differ by index ICH date (P=0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: In a contemporary, multicenter US cohort of patients with ICH and AF, 60% were prescribed anticoagulation after discharge, and the remainder were mostly treated with antiplatelet therapy only. These findings suggest widespread use of different secondary stroke prevention strategies in patients with AF and ICH.

Title: Robot-assisted kidney transplantation for right versus left living donor kidneys: A single-center outcome and learning curve analysis.
Journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Robot-assisted kidney transplantation (RAKT) is the standard of care in experienced hands. Transplantation of right kidney (RK) from a living donor (LD) is challenging because the right renal vein is shorter and thinner, which can lead to underutilization of RKs from LD. Data for RK-RAKT are scarce. We aim to compare the surgical, peri-operative, and long-term outcomes after RAKT from RK donors versus left kidney (LK) donors and the learning curve (LC) for the entire RAKT cohort.
METHODS: After ethical committee approval, we retrospectively analyzed 409 adult RAKTs from LDs performed by a single surgeon between 2013 and 2021. We compared donor/recipient demographics, intra-operative data, immediate and late graft function, and graft/patient survival.
RESULTS: Overall, 18.5% were RK-RAKT. Donor/recipient demographics were similar between the groups. Total vascular (32.9 ± 8.9 vs. 29.6 ± 5.8 min, P = 0.003) and venous anastomosis times (14.4 ± 6.1 vs. 11.4 ± 2.5 min, P < 0.0001) were significantly longer in the RK group. No significant differences were observed in the serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate levels at day 1 and 7; 1 month; 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 years. 10-year Death-censored graft survival (77.4% for left vs. 79.17% for right, P = 0.917) and patient survival (83.9% for left vs. 75% for right, P = 0.10) were comparable. LC was shorter for critical vascular steps and graft functional outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: RK-RAKT achieves equivalent functional and survival outcomes to LK-RAKT. Concerns regarding vascular thrombosis are not supported by our findings. These results advocate for broader use of RK, potentially decreasing the wait times and improving the access to transplantation.

Title: Supine versus prone percutaneous nephrolithotomy: A narrative and analytical review of technique.
Journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) remains the gold standard for large and complex renal calculi. Although the prone position has traditionally been used since the introduction of PCNL in 1976, supine PCNL and its modifications have gained increasing acceptance with growing evidence supporting their efficacy and safety. This narrative review aims to compare supine and prone PCNL across various domains.
METHODS: Databases, PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were included. Priority was given to randomized-controlled trials, meta-analyses, and large prospective studies (>100 patients). Evidence was synthesized across operative, anesthetic, safety and technological domains.
RESULTS: Supine PCNL demonstrated stone-free rates comparable to prone PCNL. Multiple meta-analyses showed significantly shorter operative times (by 13-25 min), improved anesthetic safety, reduced radiation exposure, shorter learning curve, lower infectious complications, and superior ergonomics with the supine approach. Supine PCNL facilitates Endoscopic Combined Intrarenal Surgery and is particularly advantageous in obese, pediatric, elderly, and cardiovascular high-risk patients. Miniaturized PCNL techniques further enhance these benefits. Ultrasound-guided access contributes to improved procedural safety, whereas gravity-assisted drainage helps maintain low intrarenal pressure and facilitates gravity-assisted fragment evacuation. Emerging technologies such as vacuum-assisted systems and robotic-assisted PCNL appear inherently more compatible with the supine position.
CONCLUSION: Supine PCNL offers significant operative, anesthetic, and technological advantages while maintaining equivalent stone-free outcomes. It can be considered an equally useful approach in most clinical scenarios, whereas prone PCNL has definite advantages in selected anatomical situations.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Benmelstobart Plus Anlotinib in Advanced Endometrial Cancer: Results of a Multi-Cohort, Phase II Study (ETER200).
Abstract: Patients with advanced endometrial cancer (EC) have a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options after failure of prior systemic therapy. In this multi-cohort Phase II study (ETER200), patients with metastatic or recurrent EC who had received at least one chemotherapy regimen were enrolled. Based on MSI/MMR status, patients received benmelstobart plus anlotinib (Cohort 1), benmelstobart (Cohort 2), or anlotinib (Cohort 3) every 3 weeks. Primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by independent review committee (IRC) per RECIST v1.1. Here, the results of Cohort 1 expansion stage were reported. As of May 9, 2024, 85 of the 107 non-MSI-H/pMMR EC patients enrolled in Cohort 1 constituted the expansion stage population for primary efficacy analysis. The IRC-assessed ORR was 34.1% (95% CI, 24.2-45.2), with a median duration of response of 15.2 months (95% CI, 6.9-not evaluable). Median progression-free and overall survival were 8.8 months (95% CI, 5.8-15.2) and 21.8 months (95% CI, 19.5-29.1), respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 69.2% of patients, most commonly hypertension (21.2%) and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia syndrome (9.4%). Overall, benmelstobart plus anlotinib showed promising anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in advanced non-MSI-H/pMMR EC, supporting further evaluation of this combination in randomized Phase III studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04574284.

Title: Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling by Serial TAPSE/sPAP: A Noninvasive Predictor for Clinical Outcomes in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract: The ratio of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to systolic pulmonary artery pressure (TAPSE/sPAP) is a noninvasive surrogate of right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, but its value for dynamic risk stratification in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) remains uncertain. This multicenter prospective cohort enrolled adults with CTEPH between 2016 and 2023. Patients were stratified by quartile-based baseline TAPSE/sPAP cutoffs into < 0.15, 0.15 to 0.30, and > 0.30. The primary outcome was clinical worsening (CW) within 12 months, comprising all-cause death, hospitalization for worsening pulmonary hypertension, escalation of pulmonary hypertension-targeted therapy, or a > 30% increase in pulmonary vascular resistance. Associations were examined using Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, and time-dependent Cox analyses. Among 949 patients, 868 had follow-up and 212 (24.4%) experienced CW during a median follow-up of 10.3 months (interquartile range, 5.4-12.2 months). Lower baseline TAPSE/sPAP was associated with worse functional and hemodynamic profiles, and CW-free survival differed across strata (log-rank p = 0.004). Each 0.1-unit increase in baseline TAPSE/sPAP was associated with lower CW risk (adjusted HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.79-0.99; p = 0.039). Among 593 patients with serial measurements, higher time-updated TAPSE/sPAP (adjusted HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.52-0.83; p < 0.001) and greater improvement from baseline (adjusted HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92; p = 0.002) were associated with lower subsequent CW risk. Lower TAPSE/sPAP identifies greater disease severity and CW risk in CTEPH. Serial TAPSE/sPAP may support noninvasive dynamic risk stratification and residual risk assessment during follow-up.

Title: Gallbladder Volvulus Mimicking Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Acalculous Cholecystitis: A Case Report.
Abstract: Gallbladder volvulus (GV) is a rare surgical emergency whose clinical and radiological presentation closely mimics acute cholecystitis. This diagnostic difficulty is amplified in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), as gallbladder inflammation may initially be misattributed to an immune-related adverse event (irAE). We report the case of an 82-year-old woman with microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) duodenal adenocarcinoma treated with pembrolizumab. Following a temporary discontinuation of immunotherapy and initiation of corticosteroids for a suspected gastrointestinal irAE, she presented with acute right upper quadrant pain. Computed tomography (CT) showed a markedly distended, displaced gallbladder with absent mural enhancement. Initially suspected to be ICI-related cholecystitis, emergency laparoscopy instead revealed a >180° GV with transmural ischemic necrosis. A retrospective CT review identified a subtle cystic-pedicle "whirl sign." Following laparoscopic cholecystectomy, the patient recovered uneventfully, and pembrolizumab was later resumed. GV should remain in the differential diagnosis of acute acalculous cholecystitis in elderly patients, even those on immunotherapy. A plausible immune-mediated explanation should not lead to diagnostic anchoring when clinical and radiological signs - such as ischemia or a whirl sign - indicate an acute mechanical surgical emergency.

Title: More than Boils and Abscesses: Surgical Management of Acne Inversa in a Tertiary Care Center.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) typically experience painful lumps, abscesses, draining sinus tracts, and scarring, all of which can seriously affect their physical comfort, mental health, social life, and ability to work.
METHODS: A retrospective study was carried out at Christian Medical College, Vellore, and included patients with Hurley stage II and III HS who underwent surgical treatment between 2020 and 2024.
RESULTS: Eleven patients (64.7%) had stage II disease and 6 patients (35.3%) had stage III disease. The axilla was the most commonly involved region (70.27%). Associated comorbidities included tuberculosis, inflammatory bowel disease, systemic hypertension, and hypothyroidism. Flap reconstruction was the most common procedure (54.83%). Recurrence was seen in 2 patients.
CONCLUSION: Careful disease clearance and site-specific reconstruction seem to play an important role in achieving favorable short-term outcomes with low early recurrence.

Title: The Analgesic Efficacy of Adding Dexmedetomidine to Ropivacaine in Preoperative Interscalene Block for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative pain management is essential after arthroscopic shoulder surgery. Ultrasound-guided interscalene block (ISB) is widely used for perioperative analgesia; however, the benefits of adding dexmedetomidine to local anesthetics remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the analgesic efficacy and hemodynamic effects of dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to ropivacaine for ultrasound-guided ISB in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.
METHODS: This double-blind randomized clinical trial included patients aged ≥ 18 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-III who were scheduled for elective arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. Forty-two patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio using a random-number table to receive ultrasound-guided ISB with either 20 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine plus 2 mL of normal saline (R group) or 20 mL of 0.25% ropivacaine plus dexmedetomidine (1.5 μg/kg), diluted to a total volume of 2 mL (ropivacaine-dexmedetomidine (RD) group). Randomization and preparation of the study solutions were performed by an independent investigator. The anesthesiologist performing the block, the patients, and the postoperative outcome assessor remained blinded to the treatment allocation. Pain intensity was assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) in the recovery room and at 2, 6, 18, and 24 hours postoperatively. Intraoperative remifentanil consumption, time to the first patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) request, number of PCIA requests, pethidine requirements, and hemodynamic variables were recorded. Data were analyzed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, independent-samples t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate.
RESULTS: Forty patients completed the study and were included in the per-protocol analysis (20 patients in each group). Compared with the R group, the RD group had significantly lower intraoperative remifentanil consumption (0.11 ± 0.02 vs 0.24 ± 0.04 μg/kg/min, P < 0.001), a longer time to the first PCIA request (17.57 ± 0.93 vs 13.37 ± 1.25 hours after ISB, P < 0.001), fewer PCIA requests (4.50 ± 1.19 vs 9.95 ± 1.50, P < 0.001), a longer time to the first pethidine administration (19.20 ± 0.83 vs 16.33 ± 1.52 hours after ISB, P < 0.001), and fewer pethidine administrations (0.35 ± 0.67 vs 3.45 ± 1.05, P < 0.001). NRS pain scores at 18 and 24 hours were also significantly lower in the RD group. No significant between-group differences were observed in systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and heart rate.
CONCLUSIONS: The addition of dexmedetomidine to ropivacaine for an ultrasound-guided interscalene block significantly prolonged postoperative analgesia, reduced intraoperative remifentanil consumption, decreased postoperative analgesic requirements, and improved postoperative pain control, without significant adverse effects on hemodynamic parameters, in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.

Title: Early Post-transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) Haemodynamics With SAPIEN Balloon-Expandable and Evolut Self-Expanding Valve Platforms: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study.
Abstract: Introduction Balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and self-expanding valves (SEVs) have different frame architectures, leaflet positions and distinct deployment mechanics that may influence prosthetic haemodynamics. We compared early echocardiographic gradients after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) between SAPIEN BEV and Evolut SEV platforms in a routine-practice cohort spanning several device generations. Materials and methods We retrospectively analysed 665 TAVI procedures: 250 BEV procedures using SAPIEN 3 variants and 415 SEV procedures using Evolut variants. The primary endpoint was the early post-TAVI echocardiographic mean transvalvular gradient obtained within three months of TAVI. Secondary endpoints were absolute and relative gradient reductions, achievement of a post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg, and a residual mean gradient ≥20 mmHg. Because the continuous variables were skewed, they were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Results were reported as medians with interquartile ranges, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for differences in medians. Categorical variables were compared using Pearson chi-square tests without continuity correction when expected counts were adequate and Fisher's exact tests when cell counts were small. Paired pre- and post-TAVI measurements were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Multivariable ordinary least-squares regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors was used to adjust the post-TAVI gradient for the baseline gradient and available prespecified covariates. Results Complete pre- and post-TAVI gradients were available for 664 procedures (249 BEV and 415 SEV). The median post-TAVI gradient was 8.4 (5.85-11.63) mmHg with SEV and 10.0 (7.93-13.90) mmHg with BEV (median difference, -1.60 mmHg; bootstrap 95% CI: -2.97 to -1.00; Mann-Whitney U test: p < 0.001). The median absolute gradient reduction was also greater with SEVs (36.0 vs 32.0 mmHg; median difference, 4.0 mmHg; p < 0.001), as was the relative gradient reduction (81.52% vs 76.19%; median difference, 5.33 percentage points; p < 0.001), although SEVs had a higher pre-procedural baseline transvalvular gradient. A post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg was recorded in 61.2% of SEV procedures compared with 43.4% of BEV procedures (risk ratio 1.41; p < 0.001). Residual gradients of ≥20 mmHg were uncommon and did not differ between the two groups (6.0% in SEV procedures vs 5.6% in BEV procedures; p = 0.831). After adjustment, in 575 completed cases, SEV use remained associated with a 1.48 mmHg lower post-TAVI mean gradient (95% CI: -2.42 to -0.55; p = 0.0019). Conclusions In this cohort, Evolut SEV procedures were associated with a modestly lower early post-TAVI mean gradient than SAPIEN BEV procedures. The magnitude of this association, and its interpretation alongside baseline gradient, anatomy, and other device-selection factors, can inform further comparative evaluation. No clinical outcomes or valve-durability measures were assessed.

Title: Resolution of hypertension following adrenalectomy in patients with pheochromocytoma and Conn's syndrome: A comparative cohort study.
Journal: Indian journal of urology : IJU : journal of the Urological Society of India
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is limited literature comparing the resolution of hypertension after adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma and Conn's syndrome endocrine hypertension. We assessed the rate of hypertension remission and factors predicting it among patients undergoing adrenalectomy.
METHODS: As part of an institutional review board-approved study, we retrieved data of patients who underwent adrenalectomy for localized pheochromocytoma or Conn's syndrome between 2020 and 2024 at our institution. Patients were contacted telephonically to assess the status of their hypertension.
RESULTS: Out of 61 eligible patients, 31 with pheochromocytoma and 16 with Conn's syndrome were included in this study. Patients with pheochromocytoma were younger (mean age: 30.8 years vs. 42.8 years), had a lower body mass index (20.7 kg/m2 vs. 28.4 kg/m2), had a lower preoperative duration of hypertension (median- 12 vs. 84 months), and had fewer antihypertensive medicines (median 2 vs. 4) than patients with Conn's syndrome. At discharge, 82.6% (n = 19/23) of pheochromocytoma patients achieved complete hypertension remission vs. 31.2% (n = 5/16) of Conn's syndrome patients (P < 0.01). At 1 year after surgery, remission was maintained in 85% (17/20) and 50% (7/14) of patients, respectively (P = 0.05). Older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.08), worse preoperative disease burden (OR: 2.23), multifocal lesions on histopathology (OR: 12.27), and chronic kidney disease (OR: 15.43) were associated with persistence of hypertension postoperatively.
CONCLUSIONS: Adrenalectomy achieves quicker and more complete resolution of hypertension in patients with pheochromocytoma than in Conn's syndrome. Persistent hypertension is more likely in older patients with long standing, severe baseline hypertension, and other comorbidities.

Title: Digital technology-enabled healthcare services and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with cardiovascular disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: Digital technology-enabled healthcare services may support secondary prevention in patients with cardiovascular disease; however, their effects on clinical outcomes remain uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate their impact on cardiovascular outcomes. PubMed and Embase were searched from inception to 11 March 2025. Randomized controlled trials evaluating digital technology-enabled healthcare services in patients with established cardiovascular disease were included. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), as defined in each trial. Secondary outcomes included rehospitalization, coronary artery disease-related events, all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, revascularization, and adverse events. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251186138) Among 3603 records identified, 14 randomized controlled trials were included. Digital technology-enabled healthcare services were associated with a reduced risk of MACCE (risk ratio 0.595; 95% confidence interval 0.471-0.752; I 2 = 0%). Rehospitalization (risk ratio 0.676; 95% confidence interval 0.496-0.923; I 2 = 73.9%) and coronary artery disease-related events (risk ratio 0.594; 95% confidence interval 0.354-0.996; I 2 = 0%) were also reduced. There were no significant differences in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, or revascularization (all I 2 = 0%). No significant difference in adverse events was observed between groups (I 2 = 45.9%). Digital technology-enabled healthcare services were associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular events in patients with established cardiovascular disease. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed for rehospitalization, and no significant reductions were observed in mortality outcomes. Registration PROSPERO identifier: CRD420251186138.

Title: 2026 Focused Update of the Saudi Heart Association Guidelines on Best Practices in the Management of Chronic Coronary Syndromes.
Journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) continue to impose a substantial clinical and economic burden in Saudi Arabia. Since publication of the 2022 Saudi Heart Association (SHA) CCS guidelines, important advances have emerged in diagnosis, pharmacotherapy, cardiometabolic risk reduction, antiplatelet management, and revascularization. This 2026 focused update selectively revises and clarifies key recommendations to reflect these advances within the Saudi context.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary SHA expert panel conducted a structured review of randomized trials, meta-analyses, and relevant international guidance published since 2022. Updates were restricted to areas with substantive new evidence or evolving clinical practice. Recommendations were formulated through expert consensus in accordance with SHA methodological standards. This document complements the 2022 guideline and does not replace it.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: This focused update advances a more personalized, risk-driven approach to CCS management. Diagnostic algorithms now explicitly integrate pre-test probability, reinforce coronary computed tomography angiography as the preferred initial modality in low-to-intermediate probability, and refine the positioning of functional stress imaging. Residual risk assessment and preventive strategies are also strengthened. Importantly, this update introduces a dedicated diagnostic and management framework for angina and ischemia with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA/INOCA), emphasizing endotype-specific evaluation and targeted therapy for this historically under-recognized population. Anti-anginal therapy positions beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers as equivalent first-line agents, upgrades long-acting nitrates, and integrates ranolazine, ivabradine, and trimetazidine as evidence-based add-on options. Antiplatelet guidance emphasizes individualized dual antiplatelet therapy duration after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), early de-escalation strategies, and selective use of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. Lipid management and cardiovascular risk reduction options are now expanded and revascularization recommendations are restructured. Collectively, these updates strengthen the delivery of contemporary, evidence-based, and patient-centered CCS care and provide a clear framework for implementation across diverse healthcare settings.

Title: Heart Failure Progression in the Setting of Persistent Atrial Fibrillation, Frequent Premature Ventricular Complexes, and Malignancy-Related Limitations to Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy: A Case Report.
Abstract: Persistent atrial fibrillation and frequent premature ventricular complexes may contribute to worsening heart failure, particularly when malignancy limits guideline-directed medical therapy. In patients with progressive ventricular dysfunction and limited pharmacologic options, atrioventricular nodal ablation with cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator implantation may provide durable rate control and support subsequent ventricular functional recovery.

Title: LC-MS/MS-based metabolomics and PK/PD correlation analysis reveal the mechanism of hyperlipidemia treatment with Gastrodia elata fine powder.
Abstract: Gastrodia elata Blume is used as both a food and a traditional medicine in East Asia. This study evaluated the lipid-lowering effects of G. elata fine powder (GFP) and the associated metabolic responses in Sprague-Dawley rats with high-fat diet (HFD)-induced hyperlipidemia. Thirty-five rats were assigned to seven groups: a normal-diet control, an untreated HFD model, three GFP groups (150, 300, or 500 mg kg-1 per administration, three times daily), and two positive-control groups receiving simvastatin or fenofibrate. Following a 6 week modeling period and a 2 week intervention, serum biochemical parameters, liver histology, and serum, urinary, and fecal metabolic profiles were assessed using biochemical assays, histological examination, and untargeted liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry. A separate cohort of six hyperlipidemic rats received gastrodin (25 mg kg-1) for pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analysis. Compared with the untreated HFD group, medium- and high-dose GFP improved serum lipid profiles, reduced serum aminotransferase activities, and ameliorated hepatic histopathological changes. Metabolomic profiling revealed 14 urinary, 8 fecal, and 16 serum metabolites whose HFD-associated alterations shifted toward normal-control levels following high-dose GFP treatment. The associated pathways included phenylalanine metabolism, taurine and hypotaurine metabolism, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Gastrodin exhibited a biphasic plasma concentration-time profile, whereas responses of five endogenous metabolic markers lagged behind systemic drug exposure. These findings support the short-term lipid-lowering activity of GFP in HFD-fed rats and its association with changes in amino acid, bile-acid-related, and energy metabolism.

Title: Reduction in Right Ventricular Stroke Work Index After Balloon Pulmonary Angioplasty is Associated With Long-Term Prognosis in Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract: The prognostic relevance of the relative change in right ventricular stroke work index (RVSWI) after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) remains uncertain. This retrospective single-center study included 38 patients with CTEPH. Follow-up began at post-BPA catheterization. Relative change in RVSWI (%RVSWI; negative values indicate reduction) and conventional measures were compared using Cox models and direction-fixed C-indices. Bootstrap resampling assessed selection optimism across 14 candidates. RVSWI decreased from 16.96 to 9.83 g·m/m2/beat. During a median 4.1 years, 7 patients reached the composite endpoint of all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. A smaller reduction was associated with higher risk (hazard ratio 1.24 per 1 percentage-point increase in %RVSWI, 95% confidence interval 1.06-1.44; p = 0.007). %RVSWI had the highest apparent C-index (0.942, 95% confidence interval 0.86-0.99), but its difference from achieved mean pulmonary artery pressure (C-index 0.855) was not statistically distinguishable. %RVSWI ranked first in 62% of bootstrap resamples; the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.922. Component log-ratios were essentially uncorrelated (r = 0.01, 95% confidence interval -0.31 to 0.33). Greater RVSWI reduction after BPA was associated with better prognosis. With seven events, these findings are hypothesis-generating; superiority over conventional measures and the physiological interpretation of the SVI component remain unestablished.

Title: Chronic Complications Following Dengue Infection: A Scoping Review.
Abstract: Dengue virus infection has increased substantially in Latin America, prompting epidemiological alerts from regional health authorities in recent years. While most published research focuses on the acute phase, chronic multisystemic sequelae remain poorly characterized. This scoping review aimed to identify and describe chronic complications in adult patients following dengue infection, as reported in the available scientific literature. A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A structured Population, Concept, Context (PCC) question guided searches of PubMed (National Library of Medicine, Bethesda, Maryland), Scopus (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Google Scholar (Google, Mountain View, California), EMBASE (Elsevier, Amsterdam, the Netherlands), Cochrane Library (John Wiley & Sons, Hoboken, New Jersey), and LILACS (BIREME, São Paulo, Brazil), and gray literature from January 2005 to June 15, 2026. Articles were screened independently by eight reviewers using Rayyan; inter-rater reliability was assessed using Fleiss' kappa (κ = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.74-0.88), and disagreements were resolved by consensus. Of the 222 identified records, 62 studies met the inclusion criteria after deduplication and full-text screening. Neurological complications were the most frequently represented category among the included publications (30.6%, n = 19), followed by ophthalmological (19.4%, n = 12), heterogeneous persistent symptoms (12.9%, n = 8), fatigue (9.7%, n = 6), multisystemic (9.7%, n = 6), psychiatric (9.7%, n = 6), cardiological (4.8%, n = 3), and immunological (3.2%, n = 2) complications. These proportions reflect the distribution of the published literature rather than the clinical prevalence of complications among dengue patients, given that approximately one-third of the included studies were case reports or case series. The evidence base includes the largest population-based cohort of post-acute dengue sequelae to date (n = 55,870, Singapore), a two-year disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) burden analysis from the same registry, the first systematic review of dengue-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome, the first reported case of chronic dengue encephalitis with brain-tissue DENV RNA confirmed by metagenomic sequencing, and two narrative reviews that substantially expanded the evidence base on psychiatric sequelae. Dengue infection is associated with a broad and heterogeneous spectrum of chronic complications affecting multiple organ systems, including elevated post-acute cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric, and autoimmune risks, as well as a measurable disease and healthcare cost burden. The absence of a consistent relationship between acute severity and chronic outcomes supports structured, evidence-based, long-term post-dengue follow-up, particularly for patients with persistent symptoms or clinically relevant risk factors and for underrepresented Latin American populations.

Title: Conduction System Pacing Versus Biventricular Pacing for Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) is an emerging alternative to biventricular pacing (BVP) for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have yielded divergent results, creating uncertainty about the comparative effectiveness.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CSP with BVP for CRT, searching PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL through May 2026 (updating a prior review). The primary outcome was change in left ventricular ejection fraction (ΔLVEF), analyzed with random-effects models and prediction intervals.
RESULTS: Eight parallel-group RCTs including 799 patients (396 CSP, 403 BVP) were included. Pooled ΔLVEF did not differ significantly (MD +2.40%, 95% CI -0.49 to 5.29, p = 0.091; I 2 = 75%). CSP showed a non-significant trend toward shorter paced QRS (MD -7.6 ms, p = 0.14) and improved NYHA class (SMD -0.33, p = 0.12). Heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.69), mortality (RR 1.17), complications (RR 0.84), and procedure time did not differ. The four trials enrolling exclusively LBBB patients favored CSP (MD +5.00%, 95% CI 3.01 to 6.98, p = 0.004; I 2 = 0%), consistent in the three using confirmed LBBAP/LBBP (MD +5.37%, 95% CI 3.23 to 7.52, p = 0.008; I 2 = 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of randomized trials of CRT, no statistically significant difference was observed between CSP and BVP for any outcome. Because no non-inferiority margin was prespecified and the clinical-event analyses were underpowered, these findings should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence or comparable safety. Exploratory analyses suggest that patients with LBBB undergoing LBBAP/LBBP may derive incremental benefit, warranting confirmation in adequately powered trials.

Title: Regional blood-brain barrier dysfunction maps to lower performance in cognitive ageing.
Abstract: Age-related cognitive decline is a common and growing public health challenge, associated with loss of independence, reduced quality of life, increased caregiver burden and substantial healthcare and societal costs. Yet cognitive decline in ageing is heterogeneous, and current clinical constructs do not reliably capture the underlying biological mechanisms or predict progression to dementia. This cross-sectional study examined whether blood-brain barrier dysfunction (BBBD) provides a biologically supported correlate of cognitive performance beyond clinical diagnosis. The study included 46 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 46 age-matched controls and 43 young controls. BBBD was assessed using dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI in 42 patients with MCI and all controls, alongside volumetric brain analysis. Standardized NeuroTrax cognitive assessment data were analysed for 41 MCI patients and 19 age-matched controls. BBBD was analysed using the BBBdetect software (Emagix Inc, Nova Scotia, Canada), quantifying voxelwise and region-wise blood-brain barrier permeability; volumetric analysis was performed using the Volbrain software; and cognitive performance was stratified into low- and high-performance subgroups based on modified z-scores. Compared with young controls, the older cohort (MCI patients combined with age-matched controls) showed significantly greater BBBD volume and regional extent. Permeability increased with age and showed marked inter-individual variability. Across participants, lower cognitive performance was associated with a greater number of regions exhibiting BBBD. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified domain-specific spatial patterns of BBBD linked to poor performance in memory, executive, attention, verbal and motor domains, implicating frontal, cingulate, hippocampal, basal ganglia and cerebellar regions. In contrast, volumetric analyses revealed expected age-related reductions in grey and white matter and cortical thickness along with increased ventricular volume; however, these structural changes showed weak to no associations with cognitive performance. These findings suggest that BBBD is widespread in ageing and that regional BBBD maps to domain-specific cognitive deficits. BBBD thus emerges as a biologically relevant biomarker of age-related cognitive impairment and a potential therapeutic target for preserving cognitive function in ageing.

Title: Imaging Correlation of Color Doppler Ultrasound, CT Angiography, and MR Angiography Findings in Extracranial Carotid and Vertebral Artery Disease Among Ischemic Stroke Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
Abstract: Background and objective Extracranial carotid and vertebral artery (VA) atherosclerosis is an important contributor to ischemic stroke and recurrent cerebrovascular events. Color Doppler ultrasound is widely used as an accessible first-line modality, whereas CT angiography (CTA) and MR angiography (MRA) provide additional anatomical information regarding stenosis, plaque morphology, occlusion, and vascular variants. The objective of this study was to describe extracranial carotid and VA abnormalities in ischemic stroke patients using color Doppler ultrasound, CTA, and MRA and to assess aggregate distributional patterns of plaque characteristics and stenosis grades across these imaging modalities. Methods This prospective observational imaging correlation study included 50 patients with clinically suspected and neuroimaging-confirmed ischemic stroke who underwent extracranial vascular assessment. Demographic profile, vascular risk factors, Doppler plaque type, spectral broadening, CTA plaque morphology, MRA findings, and stenosis grades were analyzed. Additional descriptive and exploratory aggregate statistics included 95% CIs, chi-square tests for categorical distributions, aggregate modality-wise comparison of stenosis grades, and correlation of matched vessel-category stenosis percentages. Results The mean age was 63.6 ± 13.34 years (95% CI, 59.8-67.4), and 30 patients (60.0%) were male. Hypertension and smoking were the most frequent risk factors, each present in 27 patients (54.0%, 95% CI, 40.4-67.0), followed by diabetes mellitus in six patients (12.0%). The highest age-group burden was observed in the 61-70-year category (18/50, 36.0%; χ² = 13.00, p = 0.011). Doppler identified 76 plaque-positive vessel observations across eight evaluated vessel segments, with type II plaque being most frequent (32/76, 42.1%; p < 0.001). CTA plaque assessment showed an irregular plaque surface in 40/74 plaque observations (54.1%) and fatty or mixed plaques in 30/74 observations each (40.5%). Across five vessel segments and 250 vessel observations per modality, clinically significant stenosis (≥50% stenosis or occlusion) was noted in 14 observations (5.6%) by Doppler, 14 (5.6%) by CTA, and 18 (7.2%) by MRA; the aggregate between-modality difference was not statistically significant (χ² = 0.74, p = 0.690). Matched vessel-category stenosis percentages showed very strong aggregate correlations between Doppler and CTA (Pearson r = 0.981), Doppler and MRA (r = 0.988), and CTA and MRA (r = 0.970; all p < 0.001). Conclusions Color Doppler ultrasound demonstrated useful screening capability for extracranial carotid disease in ischemic stroke patients, while CTA and MRA added anatomical clarification of plaque morphology, stenosis, occlusion, and vertebrobasilar variants. The stenosis-grade distribution appeared comparable across modalities at an aggregate level; however, patient-level agreement, diagnostic accuracy measures, and outcome correlation could not be established without larger datasets containing paired raw imaging results and standardized reference criteria.

Title: Orexin-A and Periosteal Pressure Sensitivity during acute mental and physical stress: a randomized cross-over study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Objective physiological markers reflecting central autonomic regulation remain limited. The orexin (hypocretin) system, localized in the lateral hypothalamus, integrates arousal, metabolic state, cardiovascular control, homeostatic control, and stress responsiveness. Periosteal Pressure Sensitivity (PPS) at the sternum has been proposed as a peripheral marker for central sympathetic activation. The present study examined for the first time the association between PPS and salivary orexin-A during experimentally induced mental and physical stress and subsequent recovery.
METHODS: In this randomized cross-over study, 20 healthy female participants (20-28 years) completed two experimental procedures in randomized order: Maastricht Acute Stress Test (MAST) and Moderate-Intensity Interval Training (MIIT). PPS, systolic blood pressure, heart rate, Pressure-Rate Product (i.e., systolic blood pressure × heart rate) and salivary orexin-A were measured at baseline, immediately post-procedure, as well as 15 and 30 mins into recovery. MIIT results were analyzed both for the full sample (n = 20) and for the participants who fulfilled the protocol-defined cardiovascular response criterion (n = 12).
RESULTS: MAST did not induce significant baseline-to-post-stress changes in PRP, PPS, or salivary orexin-A, although PRP decreased significantly during early recovery from S2 to S3 (p = 0.045). A significant negative correlation was observed between ΔPPS and ΔPRP from S1 to S2 (r = -0.47, p = 0.035). MIIT induced a marked increase in PRP followed by a decrease during recovery. Changes in PPS and salivary orexin-A were not significantly correlated in the full MIIT sample. In the separate MIIT sub-analysis, a positive correlation was observed during the 30-min recovery period (r = 0.76, p = 0.029, and n = 8).
CONCLUSION: MIIT produced a clear cardiovascular response, whereas MAST did not produce the expected immediate cardiovascular stress response. The MIIT sub-analysis supports a possible association between changes in salivary orexin-A and PPS during recovery but does not establish a causal or central orexin-mediated mechanism. Replication in a larger population using technically successful and standardized MIIT and MAST procedures is required.

Title: Artificial intelligence in cardiology: an evidence map across subspecialties, 2014-26.
Abstract:
AIMS: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied in healthcare, including cardiology, with growing interest in its potential to support diagnosis, prognosis, and clinical decision-making. The rapid pace of technological advancements is not matched by equivalent progress in the regulation and appraisal of these systems. This review aims to provide a structured evidence map of AI models in cardiology, by grading the robustness of clinical validation and mapping it against the quantity of publications across main subspecialties.
METHODS AND RESULTS: To assess the strength of evidence, we defined, developed, and applied a novel classification tailored for AI models that ranks evidence into five Grades of Validation according to the level of clinical validity. We screened literature from 2014 to 2026 according to the PRISMA guidelines, identifying a total of 2807 articles on AI applications within cardiology, 490 of which met the inclusion criteria (validation was performed in at least one external, independent patient population), revealing a highly heterogeneous distribution of evidence across subspecialties. Most studies in AI focused on improved diagnostics (n = 322, 65.7%); however, advanced integration in prognostic (n = 122, 24.9%) and therapeutic applications remains limited (n = 46, 9.4%). Cardiovascular imaging leads AI applications, especially in coronary computed tomography and echocardiography, followed by non-invasive electrophysiology, predominantly in atrial fibrillation screening and ventricular dysfunction detection.
CONCLUSION: The scarcity of prospective validations across different resources and geographical settings (n = 134, 27.3%) and randomized controlled trials (n = 35, 3.8%) limits the adoption by clinical guidelines and widespread implementation of AI algorithms.

Title: Hippo signaling-linked circulating microRNA networks are associated with cardiovascular disease in type 2 diabetes.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) markedly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers for patient stratification and may provide mechanistic insight into dysregulated pathways in T2D-associated CVD.
OBJECTIVE: This work aimed to identify circulating miRNA signatures in T2D patients with CVD (T2D-CVD) vs T2D patients without CVD using a novel network-based medicine approach.
METHODS: Patients (n = 110) were stratified into T2D and T2D-CVD groups based on the absence or presence of macrovascular complications. Circulating miRNAs, proinflammatory cytokines, and growth factors were profiled in a discovery cohort (n = 80) and confirmed in a validation cohort (n = 30). Differential expression, network-based approaches, and pathway enrichment analyses identified miRNA signatures, coexpression communities, hub miRNAs, and associated signaling pathways.
RESULTS: T2D-CVD patients showed a set of elevated inflammatory cytokines and circulating miRNAs. Particularly, 19 miRNAs were differentially expressed between T2D-CVD and T2D patients. Pathway enrichment of these miRNAs highlighted Hippo signaling together with transforming growth factor-β, mechanistic target of rapamycin, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt pathways. Network analysis identified a coexpression community of 34 miRNAs, including hub miRNAs let-7a-5p, miR-132-3p, and miR-1306-3p, all linked to Hippo signaling. Key miRNA interactions were validated, and differentially expressed and hub miRNAs both correlated with inflammatory mediators such as PAR-1, CXCL1, and NEMO, which are linked to Hippo pathway regulation.
CONCLUSION: This study identified a network of circulating miRNAs associated with inflammatory cytokines and Hippo signaling pathway in T2D-CVD. These findings reveal novel molecular aspects of the systemic inflammation characterizing T2D-CVD and support the potential of Hippo-related circulating miRNAs as mechanistic biomarkers for cardiovascular risk in T2D.

Title: Nutrient-, Food-Group-, and Food-Item-Level Dietary Signatures of Psoriasis Comorbidity Among Adults With Anxiety Disorder: An Explainable Machine Learning Study.
Abstract: Psoriasis and anxiety disorders frequently co-occur, yet the dietary features associated with this comorbidity remain poorly characterized. This cross-sectional study compared nutrient-, food-group-, and food-item-level dietary representations among adults with medication-defined anxiety disorder using linked National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), Food Patterns Equivalents Database/MyPyramid Equivalents Database (FPED/MPED), and What We Eat in America (WWEIA) data. Three analytic datasets were constructed at the nutrient level (n = 1016; 37 psoriasis-comorbidity cases), food-group level (n = 1215; 46 cases), and food-item level (n = 1257; 46 cases). Each dataset was divided using a fixed stratified 7:3 training-validation split. Correlation filtering, shadow-feature selection, scaling, class-imbalance handling, and hyperparameter tuning were confined to the training workflow, with five-fold stratified cross-validation and an untouched validation set. Seven models, including conventional multivariable logistic regression, were compared. In locked validation, the nutrient-level logistic regression model showed the strongest validation signal (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC-ROC] 0.645, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.464-0.811; area under the precision-recall curve [AUC-PR] 0.063; Brier score 0.176). The food-group logistic regression model (AUC-ROC 0.396, 95% CI 0.256-0.539) and the food-item extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model (AUC-ROC 0.401, 95% CI 0.273-0.537) provided more limited validation signals in the present sample. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses of the cross-validation-selected models identified niacin, carbohydrate intake, β-cryptoxanthin, fat-related variables, hypertension, body mass index, and selected food categories as influential model features. These contributions are best interpreted as model-derived signals that prioritize candidate dietary and clinical features for further study. Together, the findings highlight nutrient-level dietary information as the most promising representation for subsequent development of nutrition-informed risk assessment in adults with anxiety. Larger prospective cohorts and external validation may further strengthen the clinical applicability of these signals.

Title: Predictors and Patterns of Metastatic Candidozyma auris Infection, Spain, 2016-2024.
Abstract: Metastatic infection after Candidozyma auris candidemia remains poorly characterized. We retrospectively studied patients with C. auris candidemia at a tertiary hospital in Spain during 2016-2024. Of 108 patients, 24 (22.2%) experienced metastatic infections; endocarditis was most frequent (7.4%), followed by osteoarticular infection, meningitis, and hepatosplenic infection (3.7% each). In multivariable Fine-Gray regression, a cardiac device or prosthetic valve was independently associated with metastatic infection (subdistribution hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 [95% CI 1.21-6.91]), although that association was attenuated in a sensitivity analysis restricted to echocardiographed patients. Persistent candidemia showed a higher, nonsignificant risk for metastatic infection in the day-5 landmark analysis (subdistribution HR 2.67 [95% CI 0.86-8.32]). Metastatic infection was associated with increased deaths in time-dependent analyses at 60 days (adjusted HR 2.21 [95% CI 1.04-4.67]) and 90 days (adjusted HR 2.26 [95% CI 1.09-4.67]). Our findings support echocardiography in patients with intracardiac devices.

Title: Invasive Enterovirus and Parechovirus Infections in Adults, Alberta, Canada, 2023-2025.
Abstract: We conducted a retrospective, population-based laboratory surveillance study during May 2023-December 2025 in Alberta, Canada, to characterize adult invasive enterovirus and parechovirus infections and to identify groups at high risk for those infections. Of 15,621 samples tested, 162 (1.0%) were virus positive, of which 51 (31.5%) samples from 39 patients indicated invasive infections. Cerebrospinal fluid, blood, and cardiac tissue were the most frequent virus-positive specimens. The invasive enterovirus and parechovirus incidence rate was 0.37 cases/100,000 person-years; rates were higher in patients <50 versus >50 years of age (incidence rate ratio 8.2; p<0.001). The annual incidence rates were 0.20-0.56 cases/100,000 person-years; rates appeared higher in 2025 than in 2024 (incidence rate ratio 2.1; p = 0.11). Severe disseminated enterovirus infection occurred in 2 patients who received ocrelizumab. Continuous surveillance and ongoing optimization of enterovirus and parechovirus detection assays is essential for comprehensive public health tracking.

Title: Safety and Efficacy of Microhook Ab Interno Trabeculotomy Combined with Cataract Surgery in Older Patients with Glaucoma.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence regarding minimally invasive glaucoma surgery in very old patients remains limited, making surgical decision-making challenging in this population. We investigated age-related differences in the safety and efficacy of microhook ab interno trabeculotomy combined with cataract surgery (combined µLOT).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study in Japan included 67 consecutive glaucomatous eyes of 67 patients who underwent combined µLOT and were followed for at least 6 months. The cohort comprised 27 male and 40 female patients. Patients were divided by median age into younger (< 76 years, n = 32) and older (≥ 76 years, n = 35) groups. Qualified success was defined irrespective of postoperative glaucoma medication use and without the need for additional glaucoma surgery, and was evaluated using three intraocular pressure (IOP) criteria: criterion A, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 18 mmHg; criterion B, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 15 mmHg; and criterion C, 6 ≤ IOP ≤ 13 mmHg.
RESULTS: The mean age of the older group was 82.5 years. At 6 months, qualified success probabilities were 94.0%, 82.1%, and 60.0% for criteria A, B, and C, respectively. Although the older group had higher qualified success under criterion C (71.4% vs. 46.9%; nominal P = 0.04) and lower IOP from week 2 to month 6, age was not independently associated with surgical failure in multivariable Cox analyses. Higher preoperative IOP, hypertension, and antithrombotic therapy showed exploratory associations with failure. Postoperative hyphema, transient IOP elevation, corneal endothelial cell loss, and systemic complications were not increased in the older group.
CONCLUSION: Combined µLOT provided favorable short-term IOP control without an increased complication burden in older patients, although baseline medication burden may have confounded the age-group comparison. These real-world findings provide clinically relevant evidence for surgical decision-making in very old patients and may be informative for other aging societies.

Title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
Abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

Title: Assessing physical activity using Fitbit trackers and the association with quality of life among newly diagnosed patients with hematologic cancer.
Journal: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
Abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated associations between real-world activity data based on daily steps and heart rate, measured by wearable activity trackers, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in newly diagnosed patients with hematologic cancers.
METHODS: In this observational cohort study, 314 patients completed HRQoL questionnaires at diagnosis, 3, 6, and 12 months. Of these, 130 patients wore Fitbit Inspire HR trackers. HRQoL was measured using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and disease-specific modules. Mixed models assessed associations between daily steps (physical activity), heart rate (general fitness/health status) and HRQoL over time. Outcomes were presented based on quartiles of daily steps.
RESULTS: The median number of daily steps per quartile at diagnosis was approximately 3,000, 6,000, 8,000 and 11,000, respectively. Patients in the first quartile were older, more likely to be male, overweight, current smokers, report ≥2 comorbidities and/or have multiple myeloma diagnosis, and less likely to have higher education or income, compared to the fourth quartile. Clinically relevant better HRQoL increased with step count, but plateaued at high activity (±8,000 steps/day). Higher heart rate was associated with greater symptom burden. For every 1,000 additional steps per day, physical (β=1.0 p<0.001) and role (β=1.1 p=0.03) functioning, global health status/QoL (β=1.0 p<0.001), fatigue (β=-0.9 p=0.03) and dyspnea (β=-1.1 p=0.01) improved significantly.
CONCLUSION: Physical activity and general fitness/health status at diagnosis may be important predictors of maintaining HRQoL in the first year after diagnosis.
IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: These findings underscore the potential of wearable technology to inform supportive care and empower self-management. Even small increases in daily steps may contribute to maintaining HRQoL after diagnosis.

Title: Intracuff alkalinized lidocaine attenuates airway irritation and hemodynamic responses during extubation: a retrospective observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endotracheal intubation and extubation are commonly associated with airway irritation, including coughing, sore throat, and hemodynamic instability during the periextubation period. Intracuff lidocaine diffuses across the endotracheal tube cuff to provide topical tracheal anesthesia, and alkalinization enhances this diffusion by increasing the non-ionized fraction.
AIMS: This retrospective observational study aimed to compare the effects of intracuff alkalinized lidocaine and intravenous lidocaine on airway irritation and hemodynamic responses during the periextubation period.
METHODS: Periextubation airway responses and hemodynamic parameters were retrospectively evaluated in patients receiving either intracuff alkalinized lidocaine or intravenous lidocaine as part of routine clinical practice. Perioperative data were independently recorded by anesthesiologists and subsequently extracted from anesthesia records. Outcome assessment and data extraction were performed by an investigator not involved in intraoperative management and unaware of group allocation. Statistical analyses followed a predefined analytical approach.
RESULTS: Of 155 patients assessed, 120 were included in the final analysis (intracuff alkalinized lidocaine, n = 60; intravenous lidocaine, n = 60). The number of cough episodes within the first 10 min after extubation was significantly lower in the intracuff alkalinized lidocaine group. Postoperative sore throat and foreign body sensation were also less frequent. Within-patient analysis showed smaller and more transient postoperative heart rate increases in patients receiving intracuff alkalinized lidocaine.
CONCLUSION: Intracuff alkalinized lidocaine was associated with reduced airway irritation and improved periextubation hemodynamic stability compared with intravenous lidocaine, suggesting it may be a simple and clinically effective strategy to improve extubation quality.

Title: Making vascular outcomes visible: an implementation framework for an Irish national vascular registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ireland lacks a coordinated national vascular registry, despite a 2023 National Model of Care recommendation to establish one for quality improvement and implant surveillance.
AIMS: To identify transferable features of established national vascular registry and audit systems and translate them into a proportionate implementation framework for Ireland.
METHODS: A structured narrative review and comparative implementation analysis. Five mature comparator systems, purposively selected for relevance to predefined implementation domains, were characterised using contemporary programme documentation and targeted peer-reviewed literature. Features were mapped to Irish policy objectives.
RESULTS: Transferable functions included explicit measurement of case ascertainment, clinically granular procedure-specific modules, recurrent provider feedback, linkage to routinely collected data, and progressive development of risk-adjusted benchmarking and research capability. We propose an Irish registry beginning with infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, carotid intervention, lower-limb arterial revascularisation, and major amputation. The initial architecture should combine a limited universal clinical core with procedure-specific modules, reconciliation against Hospital In-Patient Enquiry activity, structured implant capture, and rapid feedback to participating centres. Procedure-specific risk adjustment, longitudinal linkage, complex aortic modules, and participation in VASCUNET should follow only after completeness and data quality are established. Prospective pilot evaluation should measure denominator validity, case ascertainment, mandatory-field completion, data-entry burden, provider acceptability, staffing requirements, and cost per completed case.
CONCLUSIONS: Ireland does not require further proof that national vascular audit is feasible; it requires a deliberately limited, testable, and sustainably commissioned implementation model.

Title: Polysocial risk score predicts chronic kidney disease incidence and prognosis: mechanistic insights from plasma metabolome, proteome and lifestyle.
Abstract: The cumulative impact of multiple social determinants of health (SDHs) on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly understood. This prospective study examined the association of a polysocial risk score (PsRS) with CKD incidence and subsequent risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, and explored potential mediating pathways via multi-omics profiling and lifestyle factors. We analyzed 279,548 participants free of CKD at baseline and 19,761 patients with established CKD in the UK Biobank. The PsRS integrated 15 factors across economic, educational, healthcare, neighborhood, and social domains. Plasma metabolomic and proteomic profiles were analyzed to identify omics signatures associated with the PsRS. An unhealthy lifestyle score (uHLS) was derived based on body mass index, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, sleep, and diet. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between the PsRS and outcomes. Mediation analyses were performed in subsets with available omics and lifestyle data. Over a median follow-up of 13 years, 6,628 incident CKD cases, 3,724 CVD events, and 2,486 deaths were documented. The PsRS demonstrated a positive association with incident CKD risk among CKD-free participants (per 1-point increase: HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.11-1.14), as well as with CVD (HR=1.08; 95% CI: 1.07-1.10) and all-cause mortality (HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.10-1.14) in CKD patients. The PsRS significantly improved the predictive performance of conventional clinical models across all outcomes, as indicated by increases in the C-index, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Multi-omics analyses revealed a PsRS-associated metabolomic signature (94 metabolites primarily involved in amino acids, fatty acids, and lipoproteins) and a proteomic signature (428 proteins primarily involved in immune/inflammatory responses, cellular signaling, and fibrosis). These omics signatures mediated substantial proportions of the PsRS-outcome associations (metabolomic: 16.64%-27.09%; proteomic: 53.09%-85.21%), as did the uHLS (8.26%-12.51%). In conclusion, the PsRS effectively predicts CKD development and prognosis, largely mediated through metabolomic and proteomic pathways.

Title: Arrhythmic Risk Stratification in Non-Ischaemic Cardiomyopathy: The Role of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to evaluate the contemporary and evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in arrhythmic risk stratification for patients with non-ischaemic cardiomyopathy, specifically focussing on dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and non-dilated left ventricular cardiomyopathy (NDLVC). This review synthesises current data on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping, strain imaging and artificial intelligence (AI), and contextualises these among emerging genetic risk stratification approaches.
RECENT FINDINGS: Left ventricular ejection fraction has been the cornerstone for guideline-based arrhythmic risk stratification in patients with DCM, despite limited precision. Observational data and meta-analyses have established the presence of replacement fibrosis through LGE-CMR as a powerful independent predictor of ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) and sudden cardiac death. Crucially, the absence of LGE identifies a low-risk cohort. Much recent focus has been on understanding whether more precise characterisation of scar can further enhance arrhythmic risk stratification, for example through scar quantification. Although data exists supporting a potential role for T1 mapping for arrhythmic risk prediction in this cohort, further research is required to support its widespread adoption. Emerging multimodal approaches using artificial intelligence and personalised computational "digital twins" are areas of important interest, offering scope for integration of imaging, electrocardiographic and genomic data layers. Arrhythmic risk stratification in non-ischaemic cardiomyopathies remains challenging despite significant advances.
