Progressive refinement in precision has accompanied a shift from a restrictive, functional assessment towards an integrated, substrate-driven precision model. CMR represents the cornerstone of this evolution.

Title: The AGT M235T variant and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system parameters in a predominantly hypertensive elderly black South African cohort: a hypothesis-generating descriptive case series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension (HTN) is a key cardiovascular risk factor, with its pathogenesis remaining incompletely understood. Blood pressure (BP) regulation involves the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS), including the Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), Angiotensin I (Ang I) and Angiotensin II (Ang II). The rs699 variant (M235T) may influence BP via the RAAS.
AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the relationships between the rs699 genotypes, RAAS parameters, BP, Body mass index (BMI) and gender in a black elderly population.
METHODS: Data were collected from 48 participants aged ≥60 years, using World Health Organization (WHO) obesity guidelines and South African Hypertension Society (SAHS) 2019 standards for HTN categories. Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS version 27 and Python 3.14.
RESULTS: Most participants possessed the rs699 variant (GG: 93.8%, AG: 4.2%). ACE levels were low in 64.6%, while Ang II was elevated in the same percentage. The majority were classified as hypertensive and obese. No significant associations were found between the rs699 variant and ACE, Ang I, Ang II, HTN, BMI or gender, though BMI showed sex-related differences in females.
CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest no significant association of the rs699 variant on RAAS or cardiometabolic parameters within the study population, warranting cautious interpretation. These findings require validation in larger and more diverse populations, as meaningful statistical inferences cannot be drawn from the current data.

Title: Amyloid-targeted PET after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy for cardiac amyloidosis: a systematic review.
Journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
Abstract: To assess myocardial positron emission tomography (PET) positivity after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy, while distinguishing test discordance from independently confirmed cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through 5 August 2026, with targeted source assessment through 2 October 2026. Negative and low-grade imaging denoted Perugini grades 0 and 1, respectively; study-defined negative results were described separately. Eligibility required linked PET and bone-scan results with an extractable denominator. Acquisition modality, PET thresholds and cardiac reference standards were examined. A restricted synthesis required documented tomographic acquisition; a broader three-report synthesis was exploratory. Nine reports provided extractable paired results. In the hereditary transthyretin subgroup examined with carbon-11 Pittsburgh compound B, 20/23 participants were PET-positive after excluding one acquired, domino-transplant case. The exploratory pooled proportion was 87.0% (95% profile-likelihood confidence interval, 68.5-97.8%). Restriction to clearly documented cohort-wide tomography retained only two reports, precluding the planned pooled analysis. Uptake definitions and cardiac verification differed substantially. General diagnostic studies without complete bone-grade denominators, including REVEAL, were excluded from the eligible synthesis and retained as context. PET positivity is common in selected hereditary transthyretin cohorts with negative or low-grade bone scans, but does not establish cardiac amyloidosis or earlier diagnosis. Conditional diagnostic accuracy remains unresolved. Prospective paired studies require tomographic localization, tracer-specific thresholds and independent cardiac verification.

Title: Anterior segment biometric changes following SMILE surgery and their implications for effective intraocular lens position calculation.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study quantified short-term postoperative changes in corneal refractive power, axial length, and anterior chamber depth following SMILE surgery using two complementary instruments, and assessed the correlation between anterior chamber depth change and corneal ablation depth. The suitability of selected IOL power calculation formulae for post-SMILE eyes was evaluated through theoretically derived effective lens position (ELP) estimates.
METHODS: This prospective study enrolled a consecutive cohort of patients undergoing SMILE surgery during the second half of 2020 at a tertiary referral center affiliated with Hebei Medical University. Uncorrected visual acuity, manifest refraction, intraocular pressure, and slit-lamp biomicroscopy were assessed preoperatively and at one and three months postoperatively. Corneal dioptric power, central corneal thickness, and anterior chamber depth were measured with the Pentacam; corneal power, aqueous depth, and axial length were obtained with the IOL Master. Corneal thickness and ablation depth were additionally recorded. Continuous data are expressed as mean ± standard deviation. All analyses were performed in SPSS (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA), with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant. A linear mixed model (LMM) was applied to account for inter-eye correlation. Pairwise comparisons of internal anterior chamber depth (ICACD), total corneal refractive power (TCRP), simulated keratometry (SimK), mean keratometry (Km), and ELP across time points, instruments, eye laterality, and formulae incorporated Bonferroni correction. Pearson correlation analysis examined associations between continuous variables.
RESULTS: Axial length (AL) was significantly reduced at one and three months postoperatively relative to the preoperative baseline (p < 0.05). ICACD measurements from the Pentacam and IOL Master were strongly and positively correlated. Km, SimK, and TCRP each changed significantly from baseline at both postoperative time points (p < 0.05), with Km exceeding SimK and SimK exceeding TCRP consistently across all assessments. ELP estimates from the Holladay 1 and Haigis formulae were closely correlated (p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Following SMILE, the reduction in total axial length observed at one and three months, spanning from the anterior corneal surface to the macula, reflected corneal tissue removal, while the endothelium-to-macula distance remained unaffected. Of the corneal refractive power metrics assessed, TCRP proved the most accurate, with SimK and Km following in descending order. Short-term ACD measurements from the Pentacam and IOL Master were in close agreement, and ICACD showed no significant correlation with corneal ablation depth. Although SMILE-induced anterior chamber shallowing may compromise ELP estimation, the Holladay 1 and Haigis formulae yielded highly consistent ELP predictions over the short-term follow-up period.

Title: Immediate vs delayed extubation after pediatric liver transplantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Immediate extubation (IE) in the operating room following orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) is increasingly adopted in adults but pediatric evidence remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify factors associated with IE and compare outcomes between IE and delayed extubation (DE) after pediatric OLT. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 30, 2025. Studies comparing IE and DE in pediatric OLT recipients were included. Outcomes included reintubation, mortality, thrombosis, reoperation, tracheostomy, PICU, and hospital length of stay (LOS). Random-effects meta-analysis was pre-specified for all outcomes; sensitivity, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Twelve retrospective single-center studies comprising 1323 patients (1158 unique children after accounting for two center-level cohort overlaps) were included. IE was associated with lower odds of reintubation (OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59) and mortality (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.18-0.68); both estimates were confirmed by a correction-free Peto odds ratio (0.29 and 0.31, respectively). No significant differences were observed for thrombosis or reoperation. IE was associated with shorter PICU LOS (SMD - 0.88, 95% CI - 1.39 to - 0.37), hospital LOS (SMD - 1.16, 95% CI - 2.00 to - 0.31). Donor-type subgroup analyses showed effect sizes in the same direction as the overall analysis for PICU and hospital LOS, but none of the within-subgroup estimates reached statistical significance. Meta-regression identified intraoperative transfusion differences as predictor of hospital LOS (β =  - 0.045, p = 0.006, R2 = 57.1%), a pattern more consistent with confounding by indication than with a beneficial mechanism of transfusion itself.
CONCLUSIONS: IE was associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter LOS in pediatric OLT, but these findings derive exclusively from retrospective studies at high risk of selection bias, and causality cannot be established. Children undergoing IE were likely older and in better preoperative condition; hospital LOS findings are particularly susceptible to confounding. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these outcomes benefit.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Delayed extubation with prolonged mechanical ventilation has been standard after pediatric orthotopic liver transplantation. • Immediate extubation in the operating room is increasingly used after adult liver transplantation experiences. • Pediatric evidence on immediate extubation comes from single-center retrospective studies.
WHAT IS NEW: • This meta-analysis of 12 studies found immediate extubation associated with lower reintubation, mortality, and shorter length of stay. • These associations likely reflect selection bias rather than a proven causal benefit. • Immediate extubation appears feasible and safe in selected children, but prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine patients benefiting from this approach.

Title: Maternal Anxiety Surrounding Fetal Cardiac Evaluation: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract: Fetal echocardiography has transformed prenatal cardiac diagnosis, yet the emotional burden of referral and evaluation remains poorly characterized. We aimed to quantify maternal anxiety before and after fetal cardiac evaluation (FCE), identify clinical predictors of anxiety, and assess whether anxiety changes following evaluation and consultation regardless of outcome. In this prospective cohort study, 117 pregnant women undergoing initial or follow-up FCE completed pre- and post-consultation assessments using a seven-item symptom inventory adapted from the Stanford Acute Stress Reaction Questionnaire (SASRQ; score range 7-42). Participants were classified as anxious or non-anxious by direct self-report. Scores were compared with paired t-tests; exploratory multivariable models adjusted for clinical, demographic, and referral covariates, including prior pregnancy loss, psychiatric history, and diagnostic outcome. 80% of participants (94/117) reported anxiety about the FCE before evaluation; prior pregnancy loss was associated with anxious state (p = 0.049). Following FCE and consultation, mean symptom scores in the anxious group fell from 15.07 to 9.03, a 6.04-point (40.1%) reduction (p < 0.001), with reductions across symptom domains regardless of diagnostic outcome. Scores in the non-anxious group did not change significantly (8.48 to 7.87; p = 0.27). Most women referred for FCE report anxiety before evaluation. FCE with consultation was associated with a substantial reduction in anxiety symptoms in these women, irrespective of whether a cardiac abnormality was found. Although the uncontrolled pre-post design cannot establish causation, these findings suggest that diagnostic clarity and expert consultation may themselves be anxiety-reducing and support evaluation of integrated psychosocial care models in fetal cardiology.

Title: Contact Aspiration Versus Combined Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion: Clinical Severity and First-pass Recanalization Are Associated with Outcome.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) carries high rates of death and disability despite endovascular therapy, and the optimal technique remains unclear. We compared contact aspiration (CA) alone with combined CA plus stent retriever (CA + SR) and identified factors associated with first-pass reperfusion and 3‑month outcome.
METHODS: In the prospective multicenter SARA-3 registry, the primary outcomes compared between CA and CA + SR were first-pass recanalization (modified Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3) and 3‑month functional independence. Secondary outcomes were final recanalization, procedural time, safety, 24‑h NIHSS, and mortality. Factors associated with unfavorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 3-6) were assessed by Firth penalized logistic regression, with first-line technique forced in as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 68 patients (median admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] 11), 50 (73.5%) received CA and 18 (26.5%) CA + SR. The two techniques showed no statistically significant differences in reperfusion, safety, or 3‑month unfavorable outcome (48% vs. 53%; underpowered), but CA was faster (21 vs. 38 min; P = 0.007). Admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.08 per point; P = 0.004) and first-pass mTICI 2b-3 (OR 0.06; P < 0.001) were independently associated with outcome; their combination discriminated well (area under the curve 0.83). Forcing technique into the model did not change these associations (CA + SR adjusted OR 1.19; P = 0.81). No baseline characteristic was independently associated with first-pass reperfusion.
CONCLUSIONS: CA and CA + SR showed no statistically significant difference in 3‑month outcomes, but CA was faster. First-line technique was not associated with functional outcome; instead, outcome reflected baseline stroke severity and first-pass reperfusion, which defined prognostic groups that may aid risk stratification if externally validated.

Title: Adjunctive topical bromfenac and the 3-year bevacizumab injection burden in macular edema secondary to branch retinal vein occlusion.
Journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy for macular edema secondary to branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) imposes a substantial long-term injection burden. We evaluated whether eyes prescribed adjunctive topical bromfenac required fewer intravitreal bevacizumab injections over 3 years than those receiving bevacizumab monotherapy.
METHODS: This retrospective, nonconcurrent historical-control cohort study included 62 treatment-naïve eyes followed for 36 months under the same optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided pro re nata protocol. Twenty-nine eyes received intravitreal bevacizumab alone during 2016-2019, whereas 33 received bevacizumab with adjunctive topical bromfenac during 2023-2026.
RESULTS: The adjunctive bromfenac group received fewer injections over 36 months than the bevacizumab monotherapy group (5.8 ± 2.5 vs. 8.9 ± 3.7; p < 0.001) and the association persisted after adjustment for baseline visual acuity, macular thickness, OCT biomarkers, and nonperfusion area (Poisson adjusted rate ratio 0.62; 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.77; p < 0.001). Best-corrected visual acuity and central macular thickness at 36 months did not differ significantly between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive topical bromfenac was associated with fewer bevacizumab injections over 36 months in BRVO-associated macular edema.

Title: The role of extracardiac radiotracer biodistribution in the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis: a retrospective multicenter study on [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP.
Journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone scintigraphy using [99mTc]Tc-DPD or [99mTc]Tc-HMDP is a non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosing transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). However, their interchangeability and the clinical relevance of systemic extracardiac uptake (ExtCU) remain poorly defined.
AIM: To systematically compare the diagnostic performance and whole-body biodistribution profiles of [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP in patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA).
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated a multicenter cohort of patients investigated for suspected CA who underwent late planar whole-body scintigraphy and targeted SPECT/CT with either radiotracer as part of their diagnostic workup. Inclusion required a final, confirmed diagnosis of ATTRwt, ATTRv, or AL amyloidosis. Myocardial visual Perugini score (VISUAL_PS) and systemic ExtCU (pulmonary, appendicular muscular, visceral, and miscellaneous) were recorded.
RESULTS: The study included 224 patients (DPD: n = 109, comprising 70 ATTRwt, 20 ATTRv, 19 AL; HMDP: n = 115, comprising 90 ATTRwt, 13 ATTRv, 12 AL). In ATTRwt, the DPD cohort presented predominantly with Perugini Grade 2 (76%), whereas the HMDP cohort skewed toward Grade 3 (72%, p < 0.001). DPD was significantly associated with appendicular muscular uptake (ATTRwt: 84% vs. 38%, p < 0.001), creating a competitive "soft-tissue sink effect". Conversely, HMDP demonstrated a unique predilection for pulmonary retention (ATTRwt: 68% vs. 46%, p = 0.008; ATTRv: 61% vs. 10%, p = 0.006). Visceral uptake was rare in ATTR but was a robust negative predictor strongly favoring AL amyloidosis (OR 0.016, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: not applicable.

Title: Combined multimodal monitoring during neonatal transition in preterm infants: feasibility, safety and post-implementation evaluation.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: The transitional period involves major cardiovascular adaptations that could affect cerebral perfusion. Combined multimodal monitoring (CMM) may provide a more comprehensive physiological assessment than individual monitoring modalities. We aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of CMM integrating near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), targeted neonatal echocardiography (TNE), and head ultrasound (HUS) during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and to explore healthcare professionals' perceptions following its implementation. Prospective observational cohort study. Participants underwent continuous NIRS and aEEG monitoring, two TNE assessment and one HUS during the first 72 h of life. Feasibility was defined as acquisition of ≥ 75% of intended NIRS and aEEG recording time, and completion of all imaging studies. Safety outcomes included TNE-related procedural intolerance and NIRS-related skin reactions. Healthcare professionals completed a post-implementation survey assessing acceptability and perceived clinical usefulness. Forty-seven infants were included. Overall CMM feasibility was 78.7%. Individual monitoring completion was 93.6% for NIRS, 95.7% for aEEG, 89.3% for TNE and 100% for HUS. Transient desaturations occurred in 7.9% of 89 TNE assessments, while mild NIRS-related erythema occurred in 11.3% of monitored infants. Healthcare professionals reported favorable perceptions of CMM, particularly regarding clinical relevance and complementarity with standard monitoring.
CONCLUSION: CMM was feasible and well tolerated during the first 72 h of life in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation and was perceived favorably by healthcare professionals. Future studies are needed to explore its impact on clinically relevant outcomes.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • The transitional period in preterm infants involves complex cardiovascular and cerebral adaptations associated with an increased risk of brain injury. • Individual monitoring modalities (NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS) provide complementary information on cardiovascular and cerebral physiology but are commonly assessed separately.
WHAT IS NEW: • Structured CMM integrating NIRS, aEEG, TNE and HUS is feasible and well tolerated during the transitional period in preterm infants ≤ 32 weeks' gestation. • Healthcare professionals perceive CMM as clinically relevant and complementary to standard monitoring, supporting further evaluation of integrated multimodal assessment in neonatal care.

Title: Polidocanol foam sclerotherapy for patients with Goligher grade IV hemorrhoidal disease unwilling to undergo surgery: preliminary outcomes from a retrospective study with 6-month follow-up.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polidocanol foam (PF) sclerotherapy has shown promising results in low- and intermediate-grade hemorrhoidal disease (HD), but evidence in advanced stages remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate patient-reported outcomes following PF sclerotherapy in patients with Goligher grade IV HD who declined surgical treatment.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients with Goligher grade IV HD that declined hemorrhoidectomy after appropriate counseling and underwent 3% PF sclerotherapy between June and October 2025. Outcomes were assessed using symptom-focused subsets derived from the PROM-HISS and HDSS instruments at baseline, 7 days, 30 days, and 6 months. Primary outcome was the change in scores over time. Secondary outcomes included need for additional treatment, complications, and subsequent surgery.
RESULTS: Fifteen patients were included (mean age 58 ± 11 years; 53.3% male). At 6 months, 66.7% of patients requested no further hemorrhoidal treatment. Significant improvements were observed in both scores across all follow-up timepoints (p < 0.05). Pain, bleeding, and prolapse showed the most consistent reductions. One patient (6.7%) required hemorrhoidectomy within 30 days, four patients (26.7%) a second sclerotherapy session. No major complications were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with Goligher grade IV HD who are unwilling or unfit to undergo surgery, PF sclerotherapy may be associated with short-term symptom improvement and may represent a symptom-oriented minimally invasive option for selected patients unwilling or unfit to undergo surgery.

Title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
Abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

Title: [Evidence-based treatment of valvular heart disease].
Abstract: Valvular heart disease is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As the prevalence of most valvular heart diseases increases with age, population ageing has led to a substantial increase in disease burden. Due to advanced age or significant comorbidities, many patients are considered unsuitable for conventional surgery. Whereas medical therapy was therefore often the only treatment option in the past, the rapid evolution of transcatheter interventions has fundamentally transformed the management of valvular heart disease over the past two decades. Today, effective catheter-based treatment options are available for virtually all valvular pathologies. For patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, the prognostic benefit of transcatheter aortic valve replacement is firmly established. Large randomized trials have demonstrated non-inferiority of transcatheter aortic valve replacement compared with surgical aortic valve replacement across most patient populations, leading to an expanding use of this approach in younger and lower-risk patients. Similarly, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral and tricuspid regurgitation has been shown to improve symptoms, quality of life, and heart failure-related hospitalizations. In carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, this strategy also confers a survival benefit. In addition, dedicated transcatheter devices have recently emerged as promising treatment options for native aortic regurgitation. Given the rapid evolution of transcatheter therapies, current efforts are increasingly focused on selecting the optimal treatment strategy for the individual patient and determining the optimal timing of intervention.

Title: Sirolimus-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease Without Tissue Loss: A Secondary Analysis of the SirPAD Trial.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty performs better than uncoated balloon angioplasty among patients with exertional symptoms due to femoropopliteal artery disease remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to describe 1-year outcomes after sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty among participants in the SirPAD (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease) trial with femoropopliteal artery disease.
METHODS: In this analysis of the multicenter, randomized, blinded-endpoint SirPAD trial, we evaluated outcomes for patients with femoropopliteal target lesions and without tissue loss (Rutherford category ≤4, Fontaine stage ≤III). A secondary subgroup was restricted to patients with a lower disease burden, excluding ischemic rest pain, prior major amputation, or below-the-knee revascularization. We compared the 1-year rate of: 1) target-lesion revascularization (TLR); 2) the composite of TLR and any unplanned amputation; 3) major adverse limb events; and 4) all-cause death.
RESULTS: Among 597 patients, median age was 71 years, 34.7% were women, and median target-lesion length was 150 mm; 53.8% had total occlusion. After 1 year, 50 patients (17.0%) had undergone TLR in the sirolimus-coated balloon group vs 82 (27.1%) among control subjects (absolute risk difference [ARD]: -10.1%; 95% CI: -16.6 to -3.0). Any amputation or any TLR occurred in 17.7% and 27.1% of patients respectively (ARD: -9.4%; 95% CI: -16.0 to -2.7). Major adverse limb events occurred in 4.1% vs 8.9% of patients, respectively (ARD: -4.8%; 95% CI: -9.0 to -0.8). One-year all-cause death was similar (3.7% vs 5.3%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with femoropopliteal artery disease and no tissue loss, sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with a lower 1-year rate of TLR compared with uncoated balloon angioplasty. These findings are descriptive rather than confirmatory. (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease; NCT04238546).

Title: Heart Rate Surge Improves Cardiovascular Risk Stratification Beyond Hypoxic Burden in Sleep Apnea.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) imposes cardiovascular stress through intermittent hypoxia and event-related responses. Whether heart rate surge adds prognostic information beyond hypoxic burden (HB) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to evaluate heart rate surge for cardiovascular mortality and its incremental value beyond HB in OSA.
METHODS: We analyzed 4,790 participants from a community-based cohort with overnight polysomnography. Heart rate surge was defined as peak heart rate within the event-aligned window minus mean heart rate during the 60-second pre-event baseline. Associations with cardiovascular mortality were assessed using Cox models. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by C-index, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.6 years (IQR: 10.4-12.4), 334/4,790 participants (7.0%) died of cardiovascular causes. Heart rate surge was weakly correlated with HB (Spearman ρ = 0.08; 95% CI: 0.04-0.10). The highest vs lowest heart rate surge quintile was associated with higher cardiovascular mortality risk (HR: 3.00; 95% CI: 2.10-4.30; P < 0.001) and each 1-SD increment was associated with a 27% higher risk (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.19-1.35). Participants with elevated HB and heart rate surge had the highest risk (HR: 2.65; 95% CI: 1.79-3.92). Adding heart rate surge increased the C-index from 0.77 (95% CI: 0.74-0.79) to 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.83), with ΔC of 0.04 (95% CI: 0.03-0.06), continuous NRI of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.51-0.74), categorical NRI of 0.16 (95% CI: 0.09-0.24), and integrated discrimination improvement of 0.05 (95% CI: 0.04-0.06).
CONCLUSIONS: Heart rate surge was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and improved risk stratification beyond HB in OSA.

Title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.
METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).
RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.
CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

Title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group.
METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia.
RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout.
CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

Title: Acute Myocardial Infarction in Cancer Patients Treated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium.
OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia.
RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35).
CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.

Title: Stereotactic guidance for ventricular catheter placement in ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery: a state-of-the-art review on technical rationale, clinical outcomes, and future directions.
Abstract: Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunting remains the most frequently performed surgical treatment for hydrocephalus; however, shunt failure rates remain substantial despite technical refinements. Proximal catheter malfunction, often associated with malposition, ventricular wall contact, or choroid plexus obstruction, represents a common cause of shunt revision. Conventional freehand ventricular cannulation is based on surface anatomical landmarks and surgical experience, which may be unreliable in patients with small or distorted ventricles. Stereotactic guidance-including frame-based systems, frameless neuronavigation, and electromagnetic navigation-has been introduced to improve placement accuracy and reproducibility. Randomized and cohort studies consistently demonstrate improved radiographic accuracy and higher first-pass success rates with guided techniques. However, systematic reviews have not uniformly shown reductions in overall shunt revision rates, likely reflecting the multifactorial etiology of shunt failure. Hemorrhagic complications after VP shunt placement are uncommon but clinically important; evidence from VP shunt cohorts and from the broader stereotactic neurosurgery experience (notably deep brain stimulation) suggests that trajectory planning and vascular/sulcal avoidance may reduce bleeding risk. This review synthesizes epidemiological context, technical rationale, comparative outcomes, hemorrhage considerations, health economic implications, and future research priorities regarding stereotactic ventricular catheter placement.

Title: Very low HDL cholesterol in infectious mononucleosis with hepatitis: a real-world evidence study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infectious mononucleosis (IM) with hepatitis suppresses HDL cholesterol (HDL-C), but its magnitude, specificity, recovery, and cardiovascular implications are uncharacterised.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence, specificity, recovery, and long-term cardiovascular significance of very low HDL-C in IM hepatitis.
METHODS: In the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (∼190 million patients), we studied 1,944 adults with IM and hepatitis. Presenting HDL-C distributions were compared against 15 propensity-score-matched (PSM) comparator cohorts and characterised by Gaussian mixture modelling; longitudinal trajectory was assessed across six post-index windows. Long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were analysed in PSM cohorts with very low HDL (≤20 mg/dL, n = 979/arm) versus without, over up to 20 years, with independent COVID-19 (n = 83,888/arm) and pharyngitis (n = 10,618/arm) cohorts as external validation. Robustness was tested with E-values. All cross-sectional and survival analyses were repeated in sex-specific PSM cohorts, and pre-illness HDL-C was retrieved for patients with a lipid measurement recorded at least three months before the index illness.
RESULTS: Mean presenting HDL was 36.7±22.6 mg/dL versus 49.7 pre-illness; 23.9% had HDL ≤20 mg/dL. Suppression matched CMV hepatitis but exceeded pharyngitis and IM without hepatitis, indicating a hepatitis-driven mechanism. Mixture modelling identified a discrete suppressed subpopulation (mean 16 mg/dL, 41%) absent in non-hepatitis controls. Across repeated cross-sectional sampling, HDL returned to pre-illness values by 16-30 days in the cohort overall and by 31-90 days in patients presenting ≤20 mg/dL. Patients who suppressed most deeply had pre-illness values ∼10 mg/dL below the rest of the cohort, and referred to their own baseline had recovered fully by 1-3 years. Very low acute HDL predicted higher long-term MACE (HR 1.92-2.47), reproduced in COVID-19 (HR 2.04-2.70) and pharyngitis (HR 1.43-1.69). Women presented with higher HDL-C than men (36.8 vs 31.3 mg/dL; p < 0.001), but the proportion ≤20 mg/dL did not differ by sex (28.3% vs 31.2%; RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.77-1.07), and hazard ratios were similar in women and men for every outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Very low HDL-C is a prevalent, hepatitis-driven finding in IM that identifies a subgroup at elevated long-term cardiovascular risk. However, the acute HDL-C dip is likely a marker of lipid phenotype rather than an independent risk factor, warranting prospective evaluation of cardiovascular follow-up.

Title: Association of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential with cardiovascular mortality in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: a large prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a progressive pathophysiological continuum. While clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is known to increase the risk of CKM disease onset and adverse prognoses, its overall and stage-specific impacts on cardiovascular mortality within the CKM framework, alongside the circulating proteomic mechanisms mediating this excess risk, remain largely unknown.
METHODS: Participants from the UK Biobank with available CHIP data across the CKM syndrome continuum were included. The primary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were utilized to evaluate the incremental risk conferred by CHIP. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted to ascertain result robustness. Within UKB Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP), circulating proteins jointly associated with CHIP and cardiovascular mortality were identified, followed by functional enrichment and mediation analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 16.5 years, 6,515 cardiovascular deaths were recorded among 288,384 participants across CKM stages 1-4. Across all varying CKM stages, individuals harboring Large CHIP exhibited a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular mortality compared to the non-CHIP group (all log-rank P < 0.05). Following multivariable adjustment, Large CHIP emerged as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.24; 95% confidence interval, 1.09-1.40), with subgroup analyses confirming consistent effects regardless of CKM stage or established cardiometabolic and renal diseases. Proteomic profiling, corroborated by UKB-PPP, revealed that the mechanisms driving this excess risk predominantly involve immune-inflammatory dysregulation and tissue structural remodeling. This pathway was highlighted by critical downstream mediators, including the structural component DSC2 (mediating 34.3% of the risk) and key immune-regulatory receptors such as VSIG4 (33.1%) and CD300C (29.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: CHIP is an independent risk factor for cardiovascular mortality across all stages of CKM syndrome. Mechanistically, CHIP exacerbates this adverse outcome primarily by driving systemic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and aberrant tissue remodeling.

Title: Beyond tessellation: AI-derived choroidal vessel density on multi-channel cSLO as a surrogate biomarker for OCT choroidal parameters.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop an AI-based method for quantifying choroidal vessel density (CVD) from ultra-widefield confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (UWF-cSLO) and to validate this metric against swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) choroidal parameters.
METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 633 eyes from 354 participants underwent simultaneous UWF-cSLO and SS-OCT imaging on an integrated platform, ensuring precise spatial co-registration. A TransUNet deep-learning model segmented choroidal vessels from red-channel (R; 665 nm) and infrared-channel (IR; 785 nm) images, yielding channel-specific metrics (R-CVD and IR-CVD) and a combined metric (IR + R CVD). Eight SS-OCT parameters-including choroidal thickness (CT), choroidal vascularity index (CVI), luminal area, stromal area (SA), total choroidal area (TCA), and vessel volume index (VVI)-served as reference measures. Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlations with participant-level clustered bootstrap confidence intervals, multivariable generalised estimating equations (GEE) adjusted for age and sex, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: Segmentation accuracy exceeded 0.95 (Dice coefficient) in both channels. R-CVD exhibited the strongest inverse correlations with structural and volumetric OCT parameters (SA: ρ = -0.619; CT: ρ = -0.615; TCA: ρ = -0.615; all q < 0.001), whereas IR + R CVD correlated most closely with proportion-based indices (VVI: ρ = -0.34; CVI: ρ = -0.29). These channel-dependent patterns persisted after adjustment for age and sex in multivariable GEE models. On ROC analysis, R-CVD discriminated thin from thick choroids with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.789 (sensitivity 72.5%; specificity 74.8%), whereas IR-CVD alone showed near-chance performance (AUC 0.517).
CONCLUSIONS: AI-derived CVD from UWF-cSLO correlates strongly with SS-OCT choroidal parameters in a wavelength-dependent manner and may serve as an accessible surrogate for choroidal structural assessment in settings without OCT.

Title: Retinal and coronary imaging in type 1 diabetes: links between retinopathy and subclinical cardiovascular disease.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality in individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), despite advances in glycemic management and cardiovascular prevention. Conventional cardiovascular risk assessment may underestimate risk in T1DM, particularly among younger asymptomatic individuals, highlighting the need for markers of early vascular injury. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of T1DM, is increasingly recognized as a marker of systemic vascular dysfunction rather than an isolated ocular disorder. Non-invasive retinal visualization may provide insight into vascular and atherosclerotic disease. This mini-review summarizes evidence linking DR with subclinical coronary artery disease (CAD) and cardiovascular outcomes in T1DM, focusing on coronary artery calcium (CAC) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Observational and longitudinal studies consistently link DR severity with CAC burden, coronary plaque burden, silent CAD, and cardiovascular outcomes, independent of traditional risk factors. Albuminuria and diabetic kidney disease may provide complementary evidence of a broader microvascular phenotype associated with cardiovascular risk. Advances in retinal imaging, including optical coherence tomography angiography and artificial intelligence-based oculomics, support the role of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular risk prediction. CAC scoring remains valuable for detecting subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, while CCTA characterizes calcified and non-calcified plaque. Emerging evidence suggests that integrating retinal and microvascular markers with coronary imaging may improve identification of asymptomatic individuals at increased cardiovascular risk and support intervention. Although data are observational and prospective validation is required, multimodal strategies combining clinical risk factors, retinal biomarkers, albuminuria, CAC, and CCTA may enhance cardiovascular risk stratification in T1DM.

Title: Chronic Non-Communicable Disease Burden among Recently Arrived Refugees in Syracuse, New York.
Abstract: Background: Refugees resettling in the United States often come from regions with limited healthcare infrastructure. While communicable diseases are routinely screened for, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension and diabetes mellitus, remain underrecognized. Lifetime adverse events contributing to chronic stress further increase cardiovascular disease risk in refugees. Objective: To evaluate the chronic disease burden of blood pressure measurements in the hypertensive range and point-of-care capillary glucose values in the prediabetic and diabetic ranges among refugees arriving in Syracuse, New York and to examine how a community-based health screening program informs current U.S. refugee screening practices. Associations between elevated cardiometabolic measures (blood glucose, blood pressure, and heart rate) and demographic and clinical characteristics are explored. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of health screening data collected from recently arrived adult refugees in Syracuse, New York, between May 2023 and March 2025. Health screenings were conducted within the first few months of arrival and were offered to refugees aged 18 and older, with 529 total participants. Findings: Participants were 55.8% female, with 69.8% of participants between 18 and 44 years old. Predominant regions of origin included the Eastern Mediterranean region (39.3%, including Somalia 14.2%, Syria 13.2%), the African region (36.1%, including Democratic Republic of Congo 17.8%), and region of the Americas (12.5%, including Venezuela 7.0%). Elevated heart rate was associated with glucose values in the diabetic range and gender. Glucose values in diabetic range were associated with blood pressure and age. Blood pressure was associated with age, gender, and BMI. Conclusions: Our refugee cohort showed a notable burden of undiagnosed NCDs, including hypertension and hyperglycemia in the prediabetic/diabetic ranges. Statistically significant associations between cardiometabolic risk factors, including increased BMI, age, and gender, with chronic diseases underscore the need for continued interventions to improve access and uptake of preventive health services for refugees.

Title: Inhaled nitric oxide: Expanding indications beyond traditional boundaries.
Abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is a selective pulmonary vasodilator that improves ventilation-perfusion matching with minimal effect on systemic blood pressure. Although the FDA approval is restricted to neonatal hypoxic respiratory failure associated with pulmonary hypertension, many clinicians now use iNO in adults with conditions where elevated pulmonary vascular resistance, right ventricular dysfunction threaten stability and hypoxic respiratory failure. This review examines both the mechanistic rationale and the available evidence for such off-label use. Examples range from acute RV failure in the ICU to perioperative support in cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, including COVID-19-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). In these settings, iNO offers rapid afterload reduction and short-term improvement in oxygenation, but randomized trials are lacking and limited studies to date have failed to consistently show outcome benefits. Adverse effects such as methemoglobinemia, nitrogen dioxide toxicity, rebound pulmonary hypertension, and a potential increase in acute kidney injury risk in certain non-cardiac surgical populations. Additionally, cost considerations and other practical limitations must be weighed carefully. Overall, current evidence supports the use of iNO as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected critically ill patients.

Title: Burden of cardiovascular disease in Brazil, 1996-2023: a retrospective descriptive study of the epidemiology and impact on public healthcare.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of death worldwide, and their epidemiology is correlated with genetic predisposition and exposure to risk. Brazil is a developing country with a vast territory, which leads to structural inequalities. We aimed to comprehensively characterise the epidemiology and burden of CVD in Brazil between 1996 and 2023, examining temporal trends, regional disparities, demographic patterns, healthcare costs, and heart transplantation.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective descriptive ecological study using aggregated administrative data from the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), Brazil's publicly funded national health system. Mortality, hospitalization, and heart transplantation data from 1996 to 2023 were analysed according to sex, race/ethnicity, age, and geographic region. We estimated mortality rates for the major CVD, hospital length of stay, healthcare expenditures, and heart transplantation activity.
FINDINGS: Acute myocardial infarction remained the leading cause of cardiovascular mortality throughout the study period, while hypertensive diseases overtook heart failure after 2016 as the second leading cause of death. The overall CVD mortality rate-calculated as the number of CVD-related deaths divided by the total population and expressed as a percentage-increased from 7.3% in 1998 to 8.3% in 2023, peaking at 10.1% in 2021. Marked regional, age-, sex-, and race/ethnicity-related disparities were observed, including the complete absence of heart transplantation in the North region throughout the study period. Although hospitalization rates remained relatively stable, CVD-related healthcare expenditures and heart transplantation activity increased over time.
INTERPRETATION: CVD remains a major and growing public health challenge in Brazil, with substantial regional and demographic inequalities in disease burden and access to specialised care. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health strategies and more equitable allocation of healthcare resources to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.
FUNDING: This study was funded by CNPq, CAPES, FAPEMIG, INCT.

Title: Deep brain stimulation and spinal cord stimulation for chronic disorders of consciousness: a decade of clinical evidence, mechanistic insights, and critical appraisal.
Abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) and spinal cord stimulation (SCS) have been investigated for over four decades as neuromodulatory treatments for chronic disorders of consciousness (DOC), including the vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (VS/UWS) and the minimally conscious state (MCS), for which no disease-modifying pharmacological therapy exists. This narrative review synthesizes literature published between 2016 and 2026 on the neurobiological rationale, clinical evidence, neurophysiological biomarkers, and safety of DBS and SCS for chronic DOC. The 'mesocircuit hypothesis', supported by human intraoperative electrophysiology and nonhuman primate causal manipulation, provides a coherent rationale for central thalamic and centromedian-parafascicular targeting. Across case series, cohort studies, and individual patient data meta-analyses, both DBS and SCS produce clinically meaningful improvement in a minority of patients, consistently more often in MCS (63-74% response) than in VS/UWS (26-30% response), with younger age and shorter injury-to-treatment interval predicting better outcomes. However, the two largest individual patient data meta-analyses of DBS concur that current evidence is insufficient to conclude that stimulation alters the natural history of neurological recovery beyond what would be expected from patient selection and spontaneous recovery, and adverse event rates (8.1% for SCS, 18.2% for DBS) indicate non-trivial surgical risk in this vulnerable population. Neurophysiological and neuroimaging biomarkers derived from EEG, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, functional MRI, and FDG-PET show promise for objective outcome prediction but await prospective validation. We conclude that DBS and SCS remain experimental, mechanistically motivated but not yet definitively proven therapies for chronic DOC, and that adequately powered randomized controlled trials, biomarker-guided patient selection, and dedicated ethical frameworks are needed before either modality can be recommended outside of research settings.

Title: Lipoprotein(a): a potential target for the reduction of residual cardiovascular risk in patients with chronic kidney disease.
Abstract: Epidemiological evidence demonstrates that atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a major cause of death and disability in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). From the early stages of CKD, and in addition to specifically related conditions, the coexistence of traditional risk factors contributes to a process of accelerated atherosclerosis. In patients with CKD, increased cardiovascular risk persists even after correction of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes, indicating a residual risk likely related to additional subtle factors. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an LDL-like particle containing apoB100 covalently linked to apo(a) and is now recognized as a genetically determined risk factor for ASCVD. Following its initial description, Lp(a) aroused extraordinary interest, which then waned in the late-1990s due to the controversial results of some prospective studies and the lack of effective interventions to reduce its circulating levels. Over the past two decades, clinical studies have provided robust evidence supporting the causal and independent contribution of Lp(a) to ASCVD, also suggesting a significant contribution to residual cardiovascular risk. This contribution may be particularly significant in patients with CKD, who exhibit elevated Lp(a) levels from the earliest stages of disease. The recent development of potent Lp(a)-lowering drugs offers an exciting opportunity to effectively address residual risk in the general population and in patients with CKD. No data are yet available on their use in patients with CKD but pending future definition of their efficacy on cardiovascular outcomes, approval, dosing, and long-term safety, these drugs might possibly represent a useful tool for cardiovascular prevention in these patients.

Title: A standardized ECPR activation protocol and resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load: a retrospective multicenter study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in resuscitation efficiency, patient outcomes, and nursing cognitive load associated with implementation of a standardized extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) activation protocol.
METHODS: This retrospective multicenter observational study included 103 consecutive patients with in-hospital cardiac arrest who underwent ECPR at three tertiary hospitals in Guangdong Province, China. The control group included 30 patients treated from September 2019 to December 2023, and the post-implementation group included 73 patients treated from January 2024 to December 2025. Outcomes included resuscitation-process measures, clinical outcomes, and perceived nursing workload assessed using the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), a multidimensional measure of perceived workload.
RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the post-implementation group had shorter ECPR preparation time (2.87 ± 2.32 vs. 8.60 ± 1.34 min), ECMO priming time (14.83 ± 2.88 vs. 19.07 ± 1.18 min), and ECMO initiation time (35.01 ± 2.36 vs. 54.12 ± 3.55 min), and a higher one-time readiness rate of disposable supplies (100% vs. 50.0%; all P < 0.001). The total NASA-TLX score was lower after implementation (415 ± 26 vs. 452 ± 25, P < 0.001). Thirty-day survival was numerically higher in the post-implementation group but did not differ statistically (42.5% vs. 23.3%; crude OR 2.43, 95% CI 0.92-6.37; P = 0.069). Favorable neurological outcome at discharge was more frequent after implementation (30.1% vs. 10.0%; crude OR 3.88, 95% CI 1.07-14.15; P = 0.036), and the association persisted after adjustment for SAVE score and time-to-ECPR-decision (adjusted OR 3.79, 95% CI 1.02-14.08; P = 0.047).
CONCLUSION: Implementation of the standardized ECPR activation protocol was associated with shorter ECPR preparation, priming, and initiation times, lower perceived nursing workload, and higher odds of favorable neurological outcome at discharge. Thirty-day survival was numerically higher but did not differ statistically. Given the retrospective pre-post design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

Title: Prevalence of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Patients With Cervical Cancer.
Abstract: Background Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a life-threatening complication that occurs in patients with cervical cancer. The purpose of the study was to determine the prevalence of DVT in patients with cervical cancer at recruitment and to assess clinically suspected DVT during treatment and up to four months after completion of primary treatment. Methods The study was performed at Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh. Fifty-three histopathologically proven patients with cervical cancer were taken for ultrasound (compression and Doppler) at recruitment. Patients were then followed up during treatment and until four months after completion of primary treatment to monitor for any clinical signs or symptoms of DVT. Results Out of 53 patients evaluated, no cases of DVT were identified among patients with cervical cancer at recruitment on compression and Doppler ultrasound, during treatment, and until four months after completion of primary treatment, based on clinical features. A negative report could result from the small number of patients studied; most were at an early stage (stage II) and may have led to a false-negative result. Additionally, none of the patients had clear cell carcinoma, and only 16 (30.18%) patients were in advanced stages (III and IV) based on radiological evaluation. Conclusions DVT was not observed in patients with cervical cancer during the study period. These findings suggest that the prevalence of DVT may be low in this population. However, they should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size and the absence of routine follow-up imaging. Larger prospective studies are needed to further evaluate the risk of DVT in patients with cervical cancer.

Title: Evaluation of Management Pathways for Pseudophakic Cystoid Macular Edema in a Large United States Cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify the common management pathways in the treatment of pseudophakic cystoid macular edema (CME).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted from 2005 to 2024 using the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network. Patients diagnosed with pseudophakic CME were included in the study, and patients with retinal comorbidities were excluded. Treatments initiated after the diagnosis of pseudophakic CME, including topical corticosteroids and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), periocular and intravitreal (IVT) corticosteroids, antivascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) injections, suprachoroidal corticosteroids, and pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), were tracked, and treatment sequences and imaging use over time were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 23 035 patients met the inclusion criteria, with a mean age of 72 years; 54% were women, and 68% identified as White. The incidence of pseudophakic CME increased from 2.45% in 2005 to 17.6% in 2024. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) use increased over time, becoming the most common imaging modality (used in 90% of cases), while 20% of patients underwent no imaging. No treatment was documented in 40% of patients. Among those treated, 77% received topical corticosteroids and/ or NSAIDs as first-line therapy, followed by IVT steroids (7.4%), periocular steroids (6.5%), PPV (3.4%), and anti-VEGF injections (2%). IVT steroids were the most common second-line treatment (10.2%), primarily dexamethasone implants (82.8%), followed by triamcinolone (12.2%). Use of newer agents, including fluocinolone acetonide implants and suprachoroidal triamcinolone, was uncommon.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the increased use of OCT and earlier detection of subclinical cases, a substantial proportion of patients with pseudophakic CME have no documented treatment. Topical steroids and/ or NSAIDs represent the most common first- line therapy, with IVT steroids commonly used after inadequate response to treatment.

Title: Artificial Intelligence Predicts Failure of Nonoperative Treatment in Degenerative Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop an artificial intelligence-based algorithm to predict success of nonoperative treatment in degenerative posterosuperior tears and to identify the most influential features.
METHODS: Patients with degenerative rotator cuff tears initially treated nonoperatively were enrolled prospectively from January 2022 to November 2024. Exclusion criteria included age >75 years; <24 months of follow-up; massive, traumatic, and partial tears; arthritic changes (Hamada >2); and severe fatty degeneration (Goutallier >2). All patients followed a standardized physiotherapy protocol and could choose surgery if symptoms persisted; failure was defined as opting for surgery. Collected variables included demographics, comorbidities (diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and smoking), magnetic resonance imaging tear characteristics (size; International Society of Arthroscopy, Knee Surgery, and Orthopaedic Sports Medicine classification; associated cuff involvement; and biceps pathology), corticosteroid injection history, and functional scores (American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, Subjective Shoulder Value, and the visual analog scale). First, a standard statistical analysis between groups was performed. Later, the dataset was split into a train (80%) and test (20%), and a random forest algorithm model was developed. Finally, SHapley Additive exPlanations values were computed to assess feature importance.
RESULTS: Of the 412 patients enrolled, 347 patients met the inclusion criteria. After 24 months, 66 (19%) patients opted for surgery. Mean follow-up was 30.4 months (range, 24-32). Compared with the successful nonoperative treatment group, patients who failed treatment were younger (58.5 vs 64.6 years, P = .001) and had higher body mass index (28.8 vs 27.2, P = .016), greater subscapularis involvement (13.5% vs 3%, P = .042), higher visual analog scale scores (7.7 vs 7.2, P = .018), lower Subjective Shoulder Value (30.9 vs 38.9, P = .003), and lower American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons scores (40.6 vs 47.1, P = .001). The model achieved an area under the curve of 84%, predicting success rate of the nonoperative treatment with 94% sensitivity, 62% specificity, 89% positive predictive value, and 77% negative predictive value. The most influential variables for the model were age, tear size, and pretreatment functional scores.
CONCLUSIONS: The artificial intelligence-based algorithm accurately predicted nonoperative treatment outcomes in degenerative posterosuperior rotator cuff tears (area under the curve 0.84, sensitivity 94%). Age, tear size, and function were the main predictors.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, prognostic retrospective case series.

Title: The Obesity Paradox in Chronic Kidney Disease: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Is Associated With Mortality Independent of Body Mass Index.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: The obesity paradox, in which a higher body mass index (BMI) is associated with better survival, has been observed in chronic disease populations. However, the interaction between BMI, cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), and mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains incompletely understood. We examined the association between BMI, age-adjusted CRF, and all-cause mortality in a large CKD cohort.
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 13,521 predominantly male US veterans (97.4% male) with CKD from the Exercise Testing and Health Outcomes Study within the Veterans Affairs health care system.
PREDICTORS: BMI categories (normal weight <25.0, overweight 25.0-29.9, and obese ≥30.0 kg/m2) and age-adjusted CRF quartiles based on metabolic equivalents achieved during maximal exercise tolerance testing using the Bruce protocol. The index date was the date of exercise testing.
OUTCOME: All-cause mortality.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease assessed mortality risk across BMI-fitness combinations, with normal BMI and least fit as references.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up period of 7.4 years, 5,144 (38.0%) deaths occurred. A higher BMI was associated with a lower mortality risk: overweight (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.95) and obese (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.61-0.82) versus normal BMI. Higher CRF was associated with progressively lower mortality: moderate fit (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.50-0.74) and most fit (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.40-0.60) versus least fit. The combination of obese BMI and highest fitness was associated with a 64% lower mortality risk (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.25-0.51).
LIMITATIONS: Predominantly male veteran population; single baseline BMI and fitness measurements; observational design precludes causal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: In this predominantly male veteran CKD cohort, a higher BMI was associated with lower all-cause mortality across all fitness levels. Age-adjusted CRF demonstrated a strong, graded inverse association with mortality independent of BMI. These observational findings support integrating fitness assessment into CKD management.

Title: Enhancing Inpatient Echocardiogram Request Appropriateness and Timeliness Using British Society of Echocardiography Guidelines: A Quality Improvement Project.
Abstract: Introduction Inpatient echocardiography is an important component of cardiovascular assessment, but inappropriate requests and inadequate clinical information may complicate prioritisation and delay diagnostic imaging. This quality improvement project aimed to improve the appropriateness of inpatient echocardiography requests in accordance with British Society of Echocardiography (BSE) guidance and to improve the timeliness of echocardiogram completion. Methodology This was an uncontrolled before-and-after quality improvement study conducted at Colchester Hospital, England, using two measurement points. The baseline audit covered 15-24 March 2025, and the reaudit covered 6-15 June 2025. The latest 100 eligible inpatient echocardiography requests from each period were reviewed using a pragmatic sampling approach. Pre-operative and peri-operative requests and requests relating to patients who had been discharged before audit assessment were excluded. The intervention, delivered between April and May 2025, comprised clinician education, dissemination of BSE guidance and baseline findings by email, educational posters, and teaching sessions. Appropriateness was assessed against BSE recommendations by a single cardiology consultant blinded to the audit period. Time to completion was measured from the recorded request timestamp to echocardiographic image acquisition. Results Appropriate requests increased from 82/100 (82%) at baseline to 90/100 (90%) at reaudit, an absolute change of 8 percentage points (95% CI -1.7 to +17.8; Fisher's exact p=0.153). Completion within 24 hours changed from 77/100 (77%) to 79/100 (79%), an absolute change of 2 percentage points (95% CI -9.5 to +13.4; Fisher's exact p=0.865). The median time to completion was 14.8 hours (IQR 5.6-21.4) at baseline and 17.5 hours (IQR 3.3-23.4) at reaudit. Retrospective BSE urgency adjudication classified 71/100 (71%) baseline and 77/100 (77%) reaudit requests as urgent. Among urgent requests, 55/71 (77.5%) at baseline and 59/77 (76.6%) at reaudit were completed within 24 hours. Conclusion Following the implementation of a guideline-based educational intervention, an increase in request appropriateness was observed, while overall completion within 24 hours changed only modestly. The findings support continued use of guideline-based education and iterative audit while highlighting the need to evaluate service-level and process measures when assessing echocardiography timeliness.

Title: Metabolic syndrome in stable long-term antipsychotic monotherapy and polypharmacy among patients with schizophrenia: a real-world comparative study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome is a major contributor to premature cardiovascular morbidity and mortality among people with schizophrenia. Antipsychotic polypharmacy is common, but its independent metabolic burden remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare metabolic syndrome in patients receiving stable long-term antipsychotic monotherapy or polypharmacy and to examine high metabolic-risk exposure, chlorpromazine-equivalent dose, and long-acting injectable (LAI) use.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 370 adults with schizophrenia spectrum disorders receiving an unchanged antipsychotic regimen for at least five years at a community mental health center. Patients received monotherapy (n=144) or polypharmacy (n=226). Metabolic syndrome was defined using International Diabetes Federation criteria. Antipsychotic dose was standardized to chlorpromazine equivalents, and multivariable logistic regression was used.
RESULTS: Metabolic syndrome was present in 143 patients (38.6%) and was numerically more frequent with polypharmacy than monotherapy (41.2% vs. 34.7%, p=0.216). LAI use (67.3% vs. 37.5%, p<0.001) and median chlorpromazine-equivalent dose (1010.0 vs. 454.5 mg/day, p<0.001) were higher with polypharmacy. However, neither LAI use (adjusted OR = 1.220, 95% CI 0.767-1.941, p=0.401) nor chlorpromazine-equivalent dose per 100 mg/day (adjusted OR = 1.003, 95% CI 0.954-1.055, p=0.899) was independently associated with metabolic syndrome. Current smoking remained associated with metabolic syndrome (adjusted OR = 1.996, 95% CI 1.251-3.185, p=0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort with stable long-term treatment, polypharmacy was associated with greater dose and LAI exposure, but independent associations of treatment modality, current dose, LAI use, or olanzapine/clozapine exposure with metabolic syndrome were not detected. Comprehensive cardiometabolic monitoring and smoking cessation remain priorities.

Title: Cardiovascular Autonomic Function and HRV in Healthy Adults of Rajasthan: A Cross-sectional Study on the Influence of Age and Gender.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart rate variability (HRV) and cardiovascular autonomic reflex tests (CARTs) serve as non-invasive clinical indicators of central autonomic network function and cardiovagal regulation.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to establish regional normative reference values for HRV and CART parameters in healthy adults from northwestern India to evaluate the modulating effects of age, biological sex and subclinical cardiometabolic risk factors.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study evaluated 142 healthy subjects (74 males, 68 females) aged 18-70 years. Baseline vital signs and time-domain HRV parameters (standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN) and root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD)) were recorded. Autonomic reactivity was assessed using deep breathing (expiration-to-inspiration (E:I) ratio), the Valsalva manoeuvre, isometric handgrip and orthostatic challenge. A high-risk sub-cohort (n = 21) with subclinical obesity or elevated blood pressure was analysed. Adherence to Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines was maintained.
RESULTS: The total study sample comprised 142 participants, including 74 males (52.1%) and 68 females (47.9%). The high-risk subset comprised 11 males (52.4%) and 10 females (47.6%). Resting heart rate was higher in females (74.6 ± 8.2 bpm) than in males (70.1 ± 7.6 bpm; t(140) = 3.39, p = .02), while blood pressure was higher in males (p = .03). Time-domain HRV and reflex indices declined significantly with age (p < .001), with optimal thresholds for autonomic senescence occurring at 47 years (SDNN, area under the curve (AUC) = 0.82) and 49 years (Valsalva, AUC = 0.79). Healthy females exhibited enhanced cardiovagal responses (E:I, Valsalva and 30:15 ratios; p < .05). This female autonomic advantage was entirely blunted in the high-risk subset (n = 21), where autonomic parameters fell below the 5th percentile limits (SDNN = 25 ms, RMSSD = 18 ms, Valsalva ratio = 1.09).
CONCLUSION: Healthy adults exhibit an age-related decline in parasympathetic function and a female-specific cardiovagal advantage. Subclinical cardiometabolic risk factors override these physiological buffers, blunting gender-related protection and accelerating autonomic senescence.

Title: Clinical and resting-state EEG changes following neurofeedback in adult refugees with persistent trauma-related symptoms: a transdiagnostic pre-post observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurofeedback has shown promise as an adjunctive intervention for persistent trauma-related psychopathology, but its electrophysiological effects in refugees following war, torture, and forced displacement remain poorly understood.
