Data were analyzed using linear regression models adjusted for age and sex and separately for systolic blood pressure, body fat percentage, and pubertal stage.
RESULTS: No statistically significant associations were found in the complete sample or in boys (P > .05). Higher cumulative PA energy expenditure (β = -0.260; 95% CI, -0.495 to -0.025) and moderate to vigorous PA (β = -0.341; 95% CI, -0.570 to -0.112) were associated with lower carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, and higher cumulative moderate to vigorous PA (β = -0.346; 95% CI, -0.573 to -0.118) was associated with lower cardio-ankle vascular index at 8 years in girls.
CONCLUSION: In girls, higher PA, especially moderate to vigorous PA, may slow arterial stiffening, whereas boys may already be physically active beyond levels that yield further benefits.

Title: Navigating Treatment Pathways in Diabetic Foot Infection: A Practical Retrospective Analysis of Healing Predictors and the WIfI System.
Abstract: Diabetic foot infection (DFI) is a major cause of lower-extremity amputation. Evidence on optimal management remains inconsistent, and real-world data from multidisciplinary centres are limited. This study describes the characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes of patients with DFI at a tertiary referral centre. This retrospective cross-sectional study included all patients with diabetes and confirmed DFI presenting since 2022. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiologic, and wound-related data were recorded, and wounds were classified using the Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) system. Correlation and multiple linear regression analyses identified predictors of healing duration. 69 patients were included (mean age 56.4 ± 13.2 years; 58% male). Most wounds were deep (88.2%); osteomyelitis occurred in 42.2%. Conservative wound care was used in 73.9%, and 79.7% underwent bedside debridement. Minor and major amputation rates were 16.2% and 1.4%. The median healing time was 45 days (interquartile range [IQR] 54), and the mean healing time was 56.0 ± 44.9 days. Healing duration correlated with wound grade, WIfI stage, infection severity, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), white blood cell (WBC) count, international normalized ratio (INR), wound area, and delay to specialist assessment. Wound grade was the only independent predictor of healing time (β = 0.606, p = 0.001). Limb-preserving management was associated with a low major amputation rate. Wound severity was the strongest determinant of healing duration, underscoring the importance of early referral and structured risk stratification in DFI care.

Title: Preoperative respiratory muscle strength, muscle mass, and respiratory sarcopenia as predictors of postoperative pulmonary complications after thoracic and cardiac surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are common after thoracic and cardiac surgery and are associated with adverse outcomes. Respiratory sarcopenia (RS), characterized by coexisting reductions in respiratory muscle mass and strength, may represent a clinically relevant prognostic phenotype, but its prognostic value remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess whether low preoperative respiratory muscle mass, reduced strength, or their coexistence as RS or probable RS predicts PPCs after thoracic and cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL from January 1990 to February 2026 for studies relating preoperative respiratory muscle mass, strength or flow, or RS to PPCs. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality In Prognosis Studies tool. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models after harmonizing effect directions such that ORs >1 denoted higher risk.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included; all involved thoracic or cardiac surgery, and none included an upper abdominal cohort. Cutoff-based respiratory muscle strength or flow impairment was associated with increased odds of PPCs (OR 2.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.50-3.37; I2 = 51.2%), with the most consistent association observed for percent-predicted peak expiratory flow (PEF) (OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.43-2.90; I2 = 0%). Continuous PEF was associated with PPCs, whereas ultrasound-based diaphragm indices showed smaller, non-significant associations. RS or probable RS was associated with PPCs (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.33-3.26; I2 = 0%).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative functional respiratory muscle impairment, particularly reduced PEF, and RS or probable RS were associated with PPCs. Given that the evidence was limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly derived from thoracic surgery, prospective confirmation is needed.

Title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

Title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Cardio-Oncology: An Expert Consensus Statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance. Endorsed by the International Cardio-Oncology Society (ICOS).
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract: This document represents a position statement from the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) on recommendations for clinical utilization of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with cancer. The document was prepared by the SCMR Consensus Group on CMR Imaging for Cardio-Oncology and endorsed by the SCMR Publications Committee and SCMR Executive Committee. This document aims to: (1) guide the informed selection and timing of CMR; (2) inform clinical decision-making based on CMR findings; (3) educate stakeholders on the advantages and limitations of CMR in specific clinical scenarios; and (4) provide suggested protocols to tailor the CMR exam to the particular clinical question. The statements of clinical utility presented in the current document focus on the following clinical scenarios: evaluating left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction and volumes; identifying pre-clinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction with myocardial strain; and myocardial injury or edema with parametric mapping and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE); myocarditis; vascular toxicity, with a focus on coronary artery disease (CAD); iron overload; cardiac amyloidosis; pericardial disease; valvular disease; pulmonary hypertension; and cardiac masses. Sections devoted to the special situations of radiation therapy (RT), hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and survivorship and pediatrics are also included. As an expert consensus statement, some recommendations are based on expert opinion and accepted best practices. This position statement emphasizes the optimal utilization of CMR in oncology patients with known or suspected cardiovascular disease; however, the authors acknowledge that CMR is not always locally available or accessible. Finally, the principal aim of this position statement is to provide specific recommendations on the use of CMR to help improve the health of cancer patients with cardiovascular disease.

Title: Reanimationless Rapid Recovery Versus Thoraco-Abdominal Normothermic Regional Perfusion for Donation After Circulatory Death Heart Transplantation Following Prolonged Asystolic Warm Ischemia.
Journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) heart transplantation has expanded the donor pool, yet contemporary recovery strategies remain constrained. Rapid Recovery with Extended Ultra-Oxygenated Preservation (REUP) is a non-reanimation DCD recovery strategy that eliminates the need for donor heart reperfusion prior to transplantation. As prolonged asystolic warm ischemic time (AWIT) during circulatory arrest has raised ongoing concerns, whether REUP achieves outcomes comparable to TA-NRP in DCD donors with prolonged AWIT remains unknown.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center study of DCD heart transplant recipients whose donor hearts were recovered using either TA-NRP or REUP and preserved with 10°C static cold storage. Donors with AWIT <10 minutes were excluded. The primary outcomes were severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD) and 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: Eighty-two DCD heart transplant recipients met inclusion criteria, including 55 TA-NRP and 27 REUP recipients. Compared with TA-NRP donors, REUP donors were older (42.0 vs 33.7 years) and experienced longer total ischemic times (285 vs 219 minutes). Severe PGD occurred in 4 TA-NRP recipients (7.3%) and no REUP recipients (0.0%). Ninety-day mortality was 12.7% versus 7.4%, respectively. In weighted bootstrap analyses, REUP was associated with a directional signal toward lower severe PGD (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09-1.02; directional consistency 97.4%) and lower 90-day mortality (OR 0.56, 95% CI 0.09-2.57; directional consistency 76.3%), although confidence intervals were wide.
CONCLUSIONS: Among DCD heart transplant recipients with AWIT ≥10 minutes, REUP demonstrated early graft function and short-term survival comparable to TA-NRP despite a more challenging donor profile. These findings support further prospective multicenter evaluation of REUP as a broadly deployable non-reanimation DCD heart recovery strategy.

Title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Balancing thrombotic and bleeding risk in patients requiring direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains challenging. This study evaluated the safety of dual antithrombotic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel in patients undergoing PCI for acute coronary syndrome or with high thrombotic risk.
METHODS: The ReDUAL PCI Real Life study was a Dutch, open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomized controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry (ZON-HR), aiming to enrol 850 patients. Patients requiring DOAC were randomized 1:1 to DOAC plus ticagrelor or DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI. The primary endpoint was any bleeding (BARC ≥2) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and net adverse clinical events (NACE: MACCE plus major bleeding). Outcomes were compared with a non-randomized ZON-HR cohort eligible for inclusion.
RESULTS: The study was terminated prematurely due to slow recruitment, with 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel). Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance. In 397 eligible non-randomized clopidogrel-treated patients, major bleeding rate was 3.4%, MACCE occurred in 12.5% and NACE in 14.5%.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing PCI requiring oral anticoagulation, DOAC plus ticagrelor showed similar overall bleeding but numerical increase in major bleeding without apparent ischemic benefit compared with DOAC plus clopidogrel. This prematurely terminated study was underpowered, limiting abilities to draw definitive conclusions.

Title: Multimodality imaging for predicting regional wall motion recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting regional left ventricular (LV) functional recovery is essential for optimizing patient selection for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in chronic total occlusion (CTO), yet direct comparisons of imaging modalities remain limited. We aimed to compare the predictive performance of dobutamine stress echocardiography (DSE), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), alone and in combination, for regional LV wall motion recovery after PCI for CTO.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We prospectively examined 66 patients with CTO undergoing successful PCI. Multimodality imaging was performed within 3 months prior to PCI. Wall motion recovery was defined as an improvement of ≥1 grade in segmental wall motion score assessed by resting echocardiography at 6 to 8 months post-PCI. Among 153 dysfunctional segments within the CTO territory, recovery was observed in 115 (75%). DSE at 20 μg/kg/min demonstrated high sensitivity (96.5%), CMR demonstrated high specificity (68.4%), and SPECT showed moderate sensitivity (76.5%) and specificity (52.6%). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of CMR and DSE (0.819) was comparable to that of all three modalities combined (0.825) and significantly exceeded that of any single modality (CMR: 0.738, DSE: 0.733; both P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CTO undergoing PCI, multimodality imaging provides complementary information for predicting regional LV wall motion recovery. An imaging strategy in which modalities are selected and combined according to the clinical context may help optimize decision-making for revascularization.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000046847). Short tweet: Can multimodality imaging predict LV wall motion recovery after PCI for chronic total occlusion? Combining dobutamine stress echo and cardiac MRI matched 3-modality performance, aiding CTO revascularization decisions. #CTO #CardioTwitter.

Title: The triglyceride-glucose index and intramyocardial hemorrhage identify a high-risk phenotype in STEMI.
Abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic value of combining the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) in STEMI is unclear. We assessed their individual and combined association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 456 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. TyG index was calculated from admission blood samples; IMH was assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance. The primary outcome was MACE (median follow-up 4 years). Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, incremental prognostic assessment (C-index, NRI, IDI), and interaction testing were performed.
RESULTS: MACE increased across TyG tertiles (15.79% → 27.63% → 43.42%). The highest tertile remained independently associated with MACE (adjusted HR 1.86; 95% CI 1.09-3.20). Patients with high TyG (≥8.66) plus IMH had the worst prognosis (HR 4.00; 95% CI 2.49-6.39; P < 0.001), far exceeding either factor alone. Adding the combined variable to a base model improved discrimination and reclassification (C-index 0.640 → 0.658; NRI = 0.216, P = 0.020; IDI = 0.025, P = 0.008). Neither additive nor multiplicative interaction was significant, and results were consistent in diabetic and non-diabetic patients. A significant interaction was observed between TyG index and infarct location (P for interaction = 0.037), with a stronger effect in anterior (HR 1.59) than non-anterior infarction (HR 0.75).
CONCLUSIONS: The TyG index independently predicts long-term MACE in STEMI. Combining high TyG with IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with a 4.0-fold higher MACE risk and incremental prognostic value. The TyG effect is stronger in anterior infarction, suggesting infarct location should be considered in metabolic risk stratification.

Title: Clinical phenotypes, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic signatures in inflammatory myocardial disease: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory myocardial disease encompasses diverse clinical phenotypes, from subtle symptoms to fulminant heart failure. Differentiating myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis (CS), and non-confirmed cardiomyopathy (NC) remains diagnostically and prognostically challenging. We compared clinical presentation, outcomes, and myocardial transcriptomic profiles across these groups.
METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 218 adults undergoing evaluation for cardiomyopathy were classified as myocarditis (n = 81), CS (n = 84), or NC (n = 53). The primary composite outcome was all-cause mortality, mechanical circulatory support, or heart transplantation. RNA sequencing of endomyocardial biopsies was performed in 53 patients with differential expression analysis adjusted for age, RNA integrity number, and systolic blood pressure.
RESULTS: Patients with myocarditis were younger than those with CS or NC (34.7 ± 15.8 vs 57.4 ± 8.7 vs 57.6 ± 14.0 years); 70-75% were male. Myocarditis was characterized by chest pain and elevated inflammatory biomarkers, whereas CS was associated with arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction. Although unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested differences in event-free survival, adjusted Cox regression showed no significant between-group differences (myocarditis vs NC: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.22-4.43, p = 0.985; CS vs NC: HR 1.67, 95% CI 0.63-4.43, p = 0.307). Transcriptomic profiling revealed a more pronounced inflammatory gene expression profile in myocarditis, whereas CS showed limited differential expression and substantial overlap with NC.
CONCLUSIONS: Inflammatory myocardial disease shows distinct clinical presentations, while adjusted analyses did not demonstrate significant differences in long-term outcomes. Myocarditis showed a stronger inflammatory transcriptional signature, whereas CS exhibited limited transcriptomic differences. These findings support further investigation of RNA-based profiling as a complementary tool.

Title: Systematic Review of Clinical Utility of Multimodal Imaging in Infectious Posterior Uveitis. Multimodal imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Taskforce Report 12.
Abstract:
TOPIC: To systematically evaluate the clinical utility of multimodal imaging (MMI) for the diagnosis, activity assessment, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications in the five most prevalent infectious posterior uveitides.
DESIGN: Systematic review and evidence-based quality appraisal.
PARTICIPANTS: Original research studies published between January 2018 and September 2025(primary cohort) and 2012-2017(supplemental cohort) evaluating MMI in ocular toxoplasmosis(TOXO), cytomegalovirus retinitis(CMVR), ocular tuberculosis(TB), syphilitic uveitis(SYPH), and acute retinal necrosis(ARN).
METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus were systematically searched. Independent reviewers extracted reported imaging findings and clinical utility statements for: color fundus photography (CFP), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and certainty of evidence was graded using a bespoke consensus-based scheme informed by GRADE principles.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: (1)reported imaging findings for each entity and modality; and (2)statements of clinical utility for diagnosis, detection of disease activity, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications.
RESULTS: Among 122 included studies (82 primary and 40 supplemental), the primary studies contributed 5,522 individual patient examinations and 574 imaging statements, while the supplemental studies provided corroborating evidence. Overall, 366 clinical utility statements were identified across the four prespecified domains, including 30 statements supporting synergistic MMI strategies. CFP, including studies using ultra-widefield imaging, achieved high certainty for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring in four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with moderate certainty in ARN. OCT achieved high certainty across all four clinical utility domains for four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with lower certainty in ARN owing to its limited evidence base. FFA achieved high certainty for complication detection in three of five entities. FAF achieved high certainty for disease activity in four of five entities. OCTA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for two of five entities, whereas ICGA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for only one of five entities.
CONCLUSIONS: Substantial evidence exists regarding the imaging findings and clinical utility of MMI in infectious posterior uveitis. Combined MMI enables integrated structural, vascular, and choroidal assessment beyond conventional clinical examination.

Title: Quantitative Analysis of Retinal Thickness and Blood Flow Changes Using SS-OCTA in Patients with Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy After Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Based on optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), we investigate the effects of Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment on retinal thickness and blood perfusion in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
METHODS: Retrospective clinical study.Forty patients (40 eyes) diagnosed with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) who underwent primary 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy (25G PPV) at our hospital between January 2023 and January 2026 were enrolled. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) was performed preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively to measure central macular thickness (CMT), superficial capillary plexus vessel density (SCP), deep capillary plexus vessel density (DCP), and the foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and postoperative complications were also recorded, and changes in all parameters before and after treatment were compared.
RESULTS: A total of 40 patients (40 eyes) were enrolled, including 21 males (21 eyes) and 19 females (19 eyes), with a mean age of (52.65±12.91) years. The mean duration of diabetes was (10.47±6.81) years, and the baseline glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level was (7.68%±1.34) %. At the final follow-up, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) improved significantly (P < 0.001), central macular thickness (CMT) decreased significantly, and macular edema was alleviated, showing statistically significant differences compared with preoperative values (P < 0.001). The vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus in the foveal and nasal regions was significantly improved, with a significant difference compared with the preoperative status (P < 0.05). No statistically significant differences were found in the remaining parameters ( P > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The study found that in eyes with PDR following Pars plana vitrectomy Combined with Treatment, visual acuity improved and macular edema resolved. In addition to relieving vitreous traction and clearing opacified refractive media, PPV also promoted partial recovery of the superficial retinal microcirculation. However, the perfusion status of the deep capillary plexus and the architecture of the FAZ may remain relatively stable in the short term after surgery.

Title: Hemoadsorption to prevent acute kidney injury in elective cardiac surgery: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials with meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) improves postoperative outcomes compared with the standard of care.
METHODS: We systematically searched EMBASE, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing hemoadsorption versus standard care in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB. Data were analyzed using a frequentist approach and trial sequential analysis (TSA). The primary outcome was the incidence of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) within 7 days after surgery. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025634991).
RESULTS: A total of six RCTs comprising 798 patients were included. Four RCTs (n = 723; 355 hemoadsorption, 368 control) reported CSA-AKI incidence, which did not significantly differ between groups (RR = 0.93 [95% CI: 0.71-1.21], p =  0.57; I² = 42.0%). Hemoadsorption was not associated with significant differences in secondary outcomes: interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor, 28-day mortality, SOFA score, and ICU length of stay.
CONCLUSION: Hemoadsorption during CPB was not associated with a reduction in CSA-AKI or with improvement in secondary clinical outcomes in elective patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, the accrued sample represented only 48% of the heterogeneity-adjusted required information size (1,491 patients), and the cumulative Z-curve crossed neither the monitoring nor the futility boundary.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO International Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42025634991; January 31, 2025).

Title: Initiation of Apixaban Versus Warfarin in Patients With Kidney Failure on Hemodialysis With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation: A Target Trial Emulation.
Journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Patients with kidney failure on hemodialysis (KFHD) and atrial fibrillation (AF) are at high risk of ischemic stroke. Oral anticoagulation (OAC) may reduce this risk but at the expense of excess bleeding. We emulated a randomized comparative effectiveness trial of apixaban versus warfarin initiation in patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF.
STUDY DESIGN: Trial emulation embedded in the US Renal Data System.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Medicare-insured patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed AF without recent OAC use (2014-2019).
EXPOSURES: Initiation of apixaban versus warfarin within 30 days from AF diagnosis.
OUTCOMES: Ischemic stroke, clinically important bleeding (co-primary outcomes). Other thromboembolic and bleeding events, death (secondary).
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: We compared propensity-matched new users of apixaban and warfarin using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: Among previously OAC-naïve patients with KFHD and newly diagnosed with AF, 3985 initiated apixaban and 6426 initiated warfarin. Propensity matching 3978 apixaban users with 3978 warfarin users balanced all measured characteristics. Median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4 (IQR: 3-5). Apixaban was initiated a median 6 (IQR: 3-12) days after AF and used for a median 58 (IQR:37-135) days; warfarin was initiated a median 5 (IQR: 2-12) days after AF and used for a median 93 (IQR:38-238) days. In intention-to-treat analyses, rates of ischemic stroke were 34% lower (HRITT=0.66; 95%CI, 0.47-0.94; p=0.02) and rates of clinically important bleeding were 28% lower (HRITT=0.72; 95%CI, 0.63-0.83; p<0.001) in patients who initiated apixaban. All-cause mortality did not differ between groups; neither did negative control outcomes of hip fracture and pneumonia. Results were robust when restricting analyses to patients with CHA2DS2-VASc score of ≥2.
LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding.
CONCLUSIONS: Initiating apixaban soon after newly diagnosed AF was associated with lower risks of ischemic stroke and clinically important bleeding compared with initiating warfarin.

Title: Heart Rate-Lowering Therapies for Tachycardia in Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is defined by a sustained increase in heart rate of ≥30 beats/min within 10 minutes of standing, accompanied by symptoms of orthostatic intolerance persisting for at least 3 months. Prior research has focused on determinants of tachycardia, raising the question of whether the tachycardia represents a compensatory mechanism or the primary driver of symptoms. In this review, we summarize the available literature on heart rate-lowering interventions in POTS and examine whether reducing heart rate is associated with symptom improvement.
METHODS: We systematically searched for studies of patients with POTS evaluating interventions primarily intended to lower heart rate and reporting heart rate and symptom outcomes. Because of heterogeneity, findings were narratively summarized by direction of effect.
RESULTS: Twenty studies comprising 707 participants met inclusion criteria. Interventions included β-blockers, ivabradine, pyridostigmine, clonidine, transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation, and sinus node-sparing hybrid ablation. All studies reported a reduction in orthostatic tachycardia or tachycardia burden, and 17/20 studies (85%) reported parallel symptomatic improvement. Across interventions, therapies that achieved a clinically meaningful and hemodynamically tolerated reduction in heart rate were most consistently associated with symptom benefit.
CONCLUSION: Available evidence, including recent randomized trials directly evaluating heart rate-lowering therapy, demonstrates that reductions in orthostatic tachycardia are frequently accompanied by symptomatic improvement. These findings support the hypothesis that excessive tachycardia in POTS may not merely be an epiphenomenon nor compensatory, but a clinically relevant and treatable contributor to symptom burden. Heart rate-lowering therapy may therefore represent a useful management strategy in appropriately selected symptomatic patients.

Title: Incidence, Modifiable Risk Factors, and Management of Cardiomyopathy After Ventricular Leadless Pacemaker Implantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless ventricular pacemakers (LPM) provide only RV pacing, which may lead to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM). It is unclear whether LPM implant site or atrioventricular synchronous pacing using the Micra AV device influence PICM occurrence.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence of cardiomyopathy after LPM implantation and explore the association of implant site and AV-synchronous pacing with cardiomyopathy risk and LVEF evolution.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 401 patients implanted with an LPM (Micra AV n=145) between July 2015 and March 2025. PICM was defined as cardiomyopathy (≥10% LVEF decline to <50%) in the presence of >20% ventricular pacing, where pacing was considered the primary cause. Risk factors for cardiomyopathy and LVEF evolution were assessed using Cox regression and mixed-effects modelling.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 33.0 months, all-cause cardiomyopathy occurred in 13.6% (4.8%/year), while PICM was identified in 5.5% (1.9%/year). RVOT implantation was independently associated with a lower incidence of all-cause cardiomyopathy (HR 0.48, P=0.019), and a slower LVEF decline (-0.56%/year vs -1.43%/year, P=0.013) compared with mid-septal implantation. Device type (Micra AV vs VR) was not associated with clinical outcomes or LVEF evolution. Among patients developing cardiomyopathy, 92.7% were medically treated, with 57.9% achieving ≥10% LVEF improvement, and 36.8% complete recovery. CRT upgrade was uncommon (7.3%).
CONCLUSION: Cardiomyopathy occurred in a substantial proportion of LPM recipients. RVOT implantation was associated with lower cardiomyopathy incidence and slower LVEF decline, whereas Micra AV implantation did not improve clinical outcomes. However, higher AV synchrony was linked to slower LVEF deterioration.

Title: 2026 North American Spine Society Patient Safety Position Statement on Education, Training, and Competency for Spine Interventions.
Journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
Abstract: The rapid expansion of minimally invasive, endoscopic, percutaneous, and implant-based spine interventions has outpaced standardized training requirements. This statement provides recommendations based on current training pathways, contemporary practice, and expert consensus, with patient safety as the guiding principle. These recommendations are not intended to define or restrict scope of practice; credentialing decisions remain the responsibility of institutions and governing bodies. Formal surgical spine training currently occurs through orthopaedic surgery residency with spine fellowship or neurological surgery residency with or without spine fellowship. These pathways include substantial supervised operative experience and ACGME residency case minimums. Anesthesiology, physical medicine and rehabilitation, radiology, and pain medicine pathways provide procedural training but do not include operative spine training, and nationally recognized training pathways for these specialties do not have minimum required case volumes across the spectrum of advanced spine interventions. Minimum case numbers, where established, are only one component of competency and should be considered alongside appropriate education, supervised experience, and demonstrated competency. Training and credentialing should reflect procedural complexity, anatomy at risk, biomechanical alteration, and potential complications. A surgical intervention treats structural spinal anatomy and meaningfully alters biomechanics or directly visualizes and decompresses the spinal cord and/or nerve roots. Based on current training pathways, spinal fusion or permanent stabilization, direct spinal cord and/or nerve root decompression, lateral sacroiliac fusion, vertebral augmentation with structural vertebral implants beyond cement or bone graft, and spinal cord stimulation paddle lead placement should be performed by physicians with formal surgical spine training. Other non-structural interventions, including basivertebral nerve ablation, percutaneous neuromodulation, cement or bone-graft vertebral augmentation, and endoscopic branch neurectomy, should require structured procedure-specific education, supervised experience, appropriate minimum case numbers, and competency assessment. Educational courses should complement rather than replace structured clinical experience. This statement encourages prospective registries for emerging technologies to evaluate outcomes, complications, reinterventions, durability, subsequent surgical consequences, and inform training standards. Transparent informed consent and documented complication-management arrangements established before the procedure in every practice setting, including physician offices, are essential.

Title: Doxapram increases respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood lactate concentration in juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the physiologic effects of IM doxapram compared to a control on respiratory rate, heart rate, venous blood gas, electrolytes, glucose, and lactate parameters in clinically healthy, rehabilitated juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas).
METHODS: In a randomized, complete crossover design completed from 2023 through 2025 with a 24-hour washout period, juvenile green sea turtles (2.9 to 7.6 kg) under care at a sea turtle rehabilitation center received either IM doxapram (5 mg/kg) or 0.9% sodium chloride (equivalent volume) in the pectoral muscle. Turtles were left unstimulated out of water, and venous blood was collected for blood gas, electrolyte, glucose, and lactate evaluation at 0, 30, and 60 minutes. Serial heart and respiratory rates (0 to 60 minutes) were collected by a blinded observer. Data were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models (P < .05).
RESULTS: 8 turtles were included. Doxapram administration resulted in significantly higher respiratory rate (5 to 30 minutes; 2.3 to 3.9 times higher), heart rate (15 to 60 minutes; 9.1 to 10.2 beats/min higher), and blood lactate concentration (30 to 60 minutes; 1.6 to 2.5 times higher) compared to control.
CONCLUSIONS: IM doxapram, 5 mg/kg, increased respiratory rate and heart rate for up to 30 and at least 60 minutes, respectively, and increased blood lactate concentration for at least 60 minutes in juvenile green sea turtles.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: While net effects of oxygenation are unknown, potential outcomes should be evaluated, and clinical discretion should be used when considering doxapram administration as a short-lived respiratory and/or cardiac stimulant in juvenile green sea turtles.

Title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients with Left Ventricular Assist Devices: Perioperative Management and Clinical Outcome.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) are commonly utilized in severe left-sided heart disease as a bridge to transplantation or long-term treatment. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) improves mobility in these patients but entails numerous perioperative risks. Our study focused on perioperative management and clinical outcomes for LVAD patients undergoing THA, aiming to provide insights into this complex setting.
ABSTRACT: METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with LVADs who underwent THA at our institution from May 2019 to November 2023. The outcomes of interest were perioperative anticoagulation management, thrombotic or bleeding events, transfusion needs, mortality, surgical site complications, and reoperations. The functional outcome was evaluated using the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS) and the EQ-5D quality of life score at their last follow-up.
ABSTRACT: RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 11 male patients, mean age 68.1 years. Patient survival was recorded over a 22.8-month mean follow-up (range, 1-53). Seven patients (63.6%) required postoperative transfusions and 5/11 patients (45.5%) experienced thromboembolic events. The mean hospital stay after THA was 13.5 days. The overall mortality related-to-disease rate in our series of LVAD patients undergoing primary THA was 27%. Three patients (27.3%) developed surgical site hematomas, which required one additional reoperation, and one of those was infected. Hip functionality improved markedly, with the mean mHHS rising from 27.5 to 72.3.
ABSTRACT: CONCLUSIONS: THA in LVAD patients is challenging yet feasible, offering significant functional improvements despite the increased perioperative morbidity. Mortality was associated with their underlying disease, but not the surgery.

Title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.
METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.
FINDINGS: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
INTERPRETATION: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.
FUNDING: The Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development.

Title: Weight loss during intermittent fasting, not Mediterranean diet quality alone, is associated with lower inflammation: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract: Whether the anti-inflammatory effects of a Mediterranean diet reflect diet quality itself or accompanying weight loss is unclear. In a 16-week randomized controlled-feeding trial, 53 adults (77% female; mean age 54.7 years) with metabolic risk factors received a fully provided Mediterranean diet or their habitual western diet for 8 weeks, then added twice-weekly fasting days for a further 8 weeks. The primary outcome, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, did not change during the diet-only phase despite clear dietary separation. After fasting began, C-reactive protein fell in the Mediterranean-diet group relative to controls, alongside greater weight loss, improved insulin sensitivity, and lower blood pressure; lipid improvements had already emerged during the diet-only phase. Multi-omic analyses showed parallel reductions in inflammatory signaling, with gut microbiome composition largely stable. Thus, diet quality alone does not lower inflammation over 8 weeks; negative energy balance and weight loss during fasting appear to be the stronger drivers. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02148458).

Title: Exploratory heart rate variability patterns across sleep stages following a 7-day multicomponent mantra-based cognitive intervention: A pilot randomized pre-post controlled study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive-contemplative practices could potentially affect autonomic function, but existing research has focused on waking measures of heart rate variability (HRV). It remains unclear whether changes associated with brief interventions differ across sleep stages.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether differences in HRV according to sleep stage would differ in a group undergoing a 7-day, multicomponent, Hare Krishna mantra-based cognitive therapy (HMBCT) intervention compared to a group engaging in their normal routine activities.
METHODS: Thirty-four healthy males aged 18-30 years were randomized to HMBCT (n = 17) or a usual-routine control condition (n = 17). Overnight polysomnography with continuous ECG was conducted at baseline and after the 7-day intervention period. HRV variables were calculated using time-domain and Poincaré/geometric HRV indices separately for REM, N2, and N3 sleep stages. Group × Time interactions were analyzed using repeated measures ANOVA, and then subjected to Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction in 30 primary tests.
RESULTS: Nine interactions reached the nominal uncorrected threshold (p < .05): four in REM (SDNN, RMSSD, SD1, SD2) and five in N2 (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, SD1, CVI), while none did so in N3. Effect sizes of REM/N2 interaction were estimated as partial η2p = 0.120-0.173. However, none remained statistically significant after FDR correction (smallest q = 0.148).
CONCLUSIONS: Nominal interactions were more pronounced in REM and N2 sleep stages, but none of the primary interactions survived multiple testing correction. Thus the results are exploratory and should be confirmed in other studies.

Title: COVID-19 severity among individuals with chronic diseases.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies reported that individuals with underlying chronic diseases who are infected with COVID-19 are at greater risk for more severe outcomes. In this study, we measured these risks among a wide range of comorbidities in a large cohort.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed the risk for hospitalization and the severity and mortality risk of COVID-19 among adults with obstructive lung diseases, hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, kidney diseases, malignancies and immunosuppression states before the emergence of the Omicron variant. We used univariant analyses and adjusted for age, sex, Body Mass Index (BMI), smoking habits, Socioeconomic Status (SES) and the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI).
RESULTS: Of the 44,866 individuals who were positive for COVID-19, 2358 were hospitalized. The adjusted Odds Ratio (aOR) for hospitalization was significantly greater for most chronic diseases, with the highest risk for individuals who underwent a kidney transplant (15.06; 95% Confidence Interval [95% CI 7.86-28.73]). A significantly greater risk for severe COVID-19 than for mild to moderate disease (602 and 1657 patients, respectively) was found for patients with cerebrovascular diseases (aOR = 1.46; 95% CI 1.07-1.99). A greater mortality risk was demonstrated for individuals who had undergone kidney transplantation (aOR = 4.23; 95% CI 1.36-11.82) and those with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) (aOR = 1.43; 95% CI 1.02-1.99).
CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with cerebrovascular disease were at increased risk for severe COVID-19, whereas individuals with CKD and past kidney transplantation were at increased mortality risk. These individuals should receive early medical intervention when they are diagnosed.

Title: Cardiovascular disease-specific mortality after partial versus radical nephrectomy for stage II renal cancer: A SEER-based propensity-matched analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgery remains standard treatment for localized renal cancer. Whether partial nephrectomy (PN), compared with radical nephrectomy (RN), affects long-term cardiovascular disease-specific mortality (CVD-SM) in stage II disease is uncertain. We assessed this association using competing-risk methods.
METHODS: Patients with T2N0M0 renal cancer diagnosed in the SEER database from 2004 to 2022 were included. Missing tumor grade and unspecified T2 subclassification were addressed by multiple imputation. Propensity-score matching was performed within 10 imputed datasets. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Fine-Gray models were primary, with cause-specific Cox models as supportive analyses; estimates were pooled across imputations.
RESULTS: The cohort included 14,602 patients (PN, n = 1294; RN, n = 13,308), with a median follow-up of 85 months. After matching, 1290-1292 patients per group were retained. Five-year CVD-SM cumulative incidence was 2.68% after PN and 3.07% after RN; 10-year estimates were 7.18% and 6.63%, respectively. No significant association was observed (Fine-Gray sHR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.69-1.74; P = 0.690; Cox HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.66-1.64; P = 0.867). PN was associated with lower cancer-specific mortality (Fine-Gray sHR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.42-0.80; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with stage II renal cancer, surgical approach was not significantly associated with CVD-SM. However, estimate imprecision and unavailable cardiovascular and renal risk factors preclude claims of equivalence or exclusion of clinically meaningful effects. The potential cardiovascular benefit of PN remains uncertain. Its lower cancer-specific mortality should be interpreted cautiously because residual surgical-selection confounding may persist.
SYNOPSIS: Cardiovascular disease-specific mortality represents an important long-term competing risk in patients with stage II renal cancer. No statistically significant association between surgical approach and cardiovascular disease-specific mortality was detected, leaving the cardiovascular survival advantage of partial nephrectomy uncertain.

Title: Impact of diabetes mellitus on clinical outcome in burns patients managed in a national burns centre.
Journal: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes following burn injury remains unclear. This study aimed to characterise diabetic burn patients and their outcomes at a national burns centre.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed at the National Burns Unit, St. James's Hospital, Dublin, reviewing admissions from 2012 to 2022. Patients with complete data (n = 870) were divided into diabetic (n = 55) and non-diabetic (n = 815) groups. Demographics, comorbidities, injury characteristics, complications, length of stay and mortality were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted to determine the association between diabetes and mortality, adjusting for age and total body surface area (TBSA).
RESULTS: Diabetic patients were older (mean age 65.6 vs 47.8 years, p <0.001) and had increased rates of cardiovascular, respiratory and renal comorbidities. They experienced more complications including acute decompensated heart failure, acute kidney injury and urinary tract infection. Median length of stay was longer (13 vs 9 days, p <0.001). Mortality was higher in diabetic patients on univariable analysis (13% vs 4.4%; OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.33 - 7.46, p = 0.009). However, after adjusting for age and TBSA, diabetes was no longer significantly associated with mortality (Adjusted OR 1.29, 95% CI 0.41 - 4.10, p = 0.667).
CONCLUSION: At Ireland's national burns centre, diabetic burn patients were older, more comorbid, suffered greater morbidity and required longer hospital stays. Their higher mortality rate may be attributable to increased age rather than diabetes itself. These single-centre findings require confirmation elsewhere.

Title: Endovascular management of arteriovenous fistula postbiopsy of pediatric transplanted kidney using embolization with detachable coils.
Abstract:
AIM: Ultrasound (US)-guided transplant kidney biopsy is required to exclude rejection or other causes of allograft dysfunction. Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is a known complication, with occurrence rates from 1.5% to 18%. AVF may heal spontaneously; however, persistent lesions may result in hypertension, renal impairment, or hematuria. The purpose of the present study was to investigate the technical details and outcomes of postbiopsy kidney transplant AVF in children, treated by interventional radiology.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a retrospective review (2019-2026) of renal transplant AVF embolization procedures in a pediatric tertiary care center. Clinical details, including transplant history, biopsy, AVF diagnosis, embolization procedural details, and postembolization clinical course, were collected. Technical success was defined as occlusion of the lesion with cessation of early venous filling, and improved flow to the adjacent parenchyma.
RESULTS: Four cases were identified, with a mean age of 15 years 1 month. Embolization was indicated due to long-term persistence and increasing lesion size on serial imaging. US and computed tomography (CT) were used for procedural planning. In all cases, a femoral arterial access approach was used, with a combination of two detachable coils (anchoring and packing), obtaining AVF occlusion. A 100% technical success rate was achieved. This has persisted in postprocedure imaging follow-up (mean follow-up: 17 months [2-36]). No minor or major adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSION: This study illustrates that embolization with detachable coils is a viable option to treat postbiopsy kidney transplant AVF in children. An anchoring and packing coil combination was feasible and effective in this small cohort.

Title: Benign enlargement of subarachnoid spaces (BESS) is not associated to bridging vein rupture/thrombosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is some controversy as to whether benign enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces (BESS) in infants predisposes to bridging vein rupture/thrombosis and subdural hematomas following minor trauma.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prevalence of subdural collections and bridging vein rupture/thrombosis in infants with BESS undergoing brain MRI for macrocephaly more or less rapid increase in head circumference.
METHODS: In a single-center retrospective observational study, infants younger than one year who underwent brain MRI for macrocephaly (head circumference > 2 SD) more or less rapid head circumference increase, between January 2017 and August 2023, were included. Early preterm infants and those with incomplete MRI protocols were excluded. MRI was reviewed for subarachnoid space enlargement, subdural collections and bridging vein abnormalities. BESS was defined by a craniocortical distance above 5 mm.
RESULTS: Of 92 infants, 78 were diagnosed with BESS. Six infants with BESS (7.7%) had unilateral or bilateral non-compressive subdural collections: fluid-like signal intensity (n = 4), intermediate signal intensity (n = 1) or a hemorrhagic component with a hypointense rim (n = 1) without bridging vein abnormalities or vertex clots. In this last case, the child had no reported previous trauma and no acute clinical symptoms but had hypotonia. No history of trauma or acute clinical symptoms was reported and no direct or indirect MRI signs of bridging vein rupture or thrombosis were identified in any infant, including those with subdural collection.
CONCLUSIONS: Non-traumatic BESS may be associated with non-compressive subdural fluid collections but not with imaging evidence of direct or indirect signs of bridging vein rupture.

Title: Effects of paternal and maternal voice on procedural pain and physiological responses during arterial blood sampling in preterm infants in a neonatal intensive care unit: a three-arm randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of paternal and maternal voice interventions on procedural pain, comfort, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and behavioral state during arterial blood sampling in preterm infants, and to compare their effects with routine care and with each other.
METHODS: A three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in China between May 2024 and June 2025. Of 135 randomized preterm infants, 119 completed the study (paternal voice, n = 39; maternal voice, n = 39; routine care, n = 41). Parental voice recordings were played from 10 min before until 10 min after arterial blood sampling. Outcomes were assessed at five time points. Generalized estimating equations were used for repeated-measures analyses.
RESULTS: GEE analysis showed significant group and time effects for pain (P = 0.027 and P < 0.001), with lower pain scores in the paternal voice group than in routine care (mean difference = -0.51; 95% CI -0.96 to -0.06; P = 0.021). Paternal voice was also associated with lower heart rates during sampling, and better comfort scores at 1 and 5 min after sampling, although the overall group effect for comfort was not significant. Maternal voice intervention did not differ significantly from routine care. No between-group differences were observed for oxygen saturation or behavioral state.
CONCLUSIONS: Paternal voice was associated with favorable pain and heart rate responses in preterm infants during and after arterial blood sampling, with time-specific differences in comfort during early recovery. Its overall effect on comfort and relative effectiveness compared with maternal voice require further investigation.
IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Paternal voice may offer a simple, safe, and feasible adjunct to procedural pain management and family-centered care in preterm infants.

Title: Effects of atropine on hemodynamic parameters following electroconvulsive therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) plays an important role in the treatment of refractory psychiatric disorders. However, it poses hemodynamic risks, such as blood pressure and heart rate elevation, arrhythmias, and transient asystole. Although atropine administration during ECT was considered a standard procedure in Western countries until the 1970s, in recent years, its use is generally limited to patients at high risk of bradycardia and asystole. We performed this meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to understand the effects of atropine on post-ECT hemodynamics and adverse events.
METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and Embase was conducted to identify RCTs investigating the relationship between atropine administration and post-ECT hemodynamics through September 30, 2025. The primary outcomes included maximum heart rate and maximum blood pressure after ECT, as well as the incidence of ECT-related adverse events. The secondary outcomes included seizure duration, arrhythmia incidence, severe salivation, and cognitive function.
RESULTS: Of the 2465 studies identified, eight RCTs were included in the meta-analysis. Maximum heart rate after ECT was significantly higher in the atropine group (p < .001). There was no significant difference in the risk of serious adverse cardiovascular events requiring intervention. Bradyarrhythmia was significantly less frequent in the atropine group (risk ratio 0.35, p < .0001).
CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis to evaluate the hemodynamic effects of atropine administration during ECT. The findings suggest that atropine increases maximum heart rate after ECT reduces the incidence of bradyarrhythmia. Although no increased risk of cardiovascular adverse events requiring intervention was observed, the small sample size remains an important limitation.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero) registration number: CRD 42022346729.

Title: Prescribing Patterns of Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis and VTE Incidence After Colorectal Cancer Resection: Insights From a Single Institution.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery are at increased risk for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Several societies recommend extended duration pharmacologic prophylaxis after discharge for selected high-risk patients, but real-world use is inconsistent, and the absolute benefit in the era of minimally invasive surgery and enhanced recovery remains uncertain.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing colon or rectal resection for cancer at a single academic center between 2020 and 2023. Patients receiving therapeutic anticoagulation, those with recent VTE or nonmalignant indications for surgery were excluded. Demographic, operative, and oncologic variables were collected along with inpatient and postdischarge VTE prophylaxis practices. Primary outcomes were (1) prescription of extended pharmacologic prophylaxis at discharge and (2) 90-d symptomatic VTE incidence.
RESULTS: A total of 177 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most operations were minimally invasive and performed within an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery pathway. Despite the presence of traditional VTE risk factors, only a minority of patients were discharged on extended pharmacologic prophylaxis. Within 90 d, two patients developed symptomatic lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (1.1%); no pulmonary emboli or VTE events were identified. Both patients had high-risk features, including advanced age and emergent surgery. Routine screening imaging was not performed, and all events were clinically detected.
CONCLUSIONS: In this enhanced recovery after surgery-based colorectal cancer cohort, extended postdischarge VTE prophylaxis was rarely prescribed; yet, the symptomatic VTE rate was low and limited to two high-risk individuals. These findings support a risk-stratified rather than universal approach to extended prophylaxis after colorectal surgery.

Title: Predictive performance of bleeding risk scores for extended anticoagulation in pulmonary embolism: Insights from the CURES-2 registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bleeding risk assessment is critical at the 3-month decision point for extended anticoagulation in patients with pulmonary embolism (PE), yet it remains unclear which existing bleeding risk score best predicts bleeding during the extended phase.
METHODS: Based on the CURES cohort, this study enrolled patients with PE undergoing extended-phase anticoagulation, which was defined as regular anticoagulant therapy for ≥90 days. We compared the performance of 6 bleeding risk scores (PE-SARD, BACS, Kuijer, RIETE, HAS-BLED, and VTE-BLEED) in predicting major bleeding (MB) events within 1 year during the extended phase. The predictive performance was assessed through time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 4896 patients with acute PE receiving extended-phase anticoagulation were included in the study, among whom 18 patients (0.4%) experienced major bleeding. Compared with the other 5 bleeding scores, VTE-BLEED exhibited the highest predictive accuracy (time-dependent AUC = 0.72; 95% CI: 0.63-0.81), accompanied by superior overall calibration (Brier score = 0.0039). In subgroup analyses by anticoagulant type, VTE-BLEED maintained favorable robustness with AUCs exceeding 0.70 for patients treated with either VKAs or DOACs.
CONCLUSIONS: VTE-BLEED offers potential utility for guiding risk-stratified management of MB during extended anticoagulation in patients with PE, particularly at the 3-month reassessment point. Nonetheless, the limited number of MB events and follow-up attrition necessitate cautious interpretation and further validation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Right ventricular function across different non-invasive respiratory support strategies in severe community-acquired pneumonia.
Journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) systolic impairment is clinically relevant in acute respiratory failure, but its relationship with respiratory support modality in severe community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) outside the intensive care unit (ICU) is poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: To compare RV longitudinal systolic performance and hospital length of stay (LOS) among patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), or Venturi-mask oxygen therapy.
METHODS: In this single-centre prospective observational study, adults with severe CAP (Pneumonia Severity Index class IV-V) requiring high-concentration oxygen or non-invasive respiratory support were enrolled. The modality was selected in the emergency department according to the treating physician's clinical and gas-exchange assessment. Echocardiography was performed shortly after ward admission while patients remained on the initial support modality.
RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (NIV, n = 21; HFNC, n = 22; Venturi mask, n = 27). Baseline demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics were comparable across groups. TAPSE and lateral tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S') showed a graded pattern, with the lowest values during NIV, intermediate values during HFNC, and the highest values with the Venturi mask (p < 0.001 for both). Mean LOS was 27.8 ± 5.0, 27.4 ± 2.9, and 15.2 ± 4.0 days, respectively (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, age and respiratory support modality were associated with LOS.
CONCLUSIONS: RV systolic performance and LOS differed across clinically selected respiratory support groups. These associations may reflect clinical severity rather than device-related effects. These findings reinforce the often-overlooked clinical importance of RV assessment in acute respiratory failure, extending observations from ARDS cohorts to severe CAP outside the ICU.

Title: White and Dark Without Pressure Associated With Congenital Hypertrophy of the Retinal Pigment Epithelium.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the prevalence, spatial distribution, and multimodal imaging features of white without pressure (WWOP) and dark without pressure (DWOP) associated with congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (CHRPE).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 101 patients (104 eyes; 106 lesions) with clinically diagnosed CHRPE evaluated between 2010 and 2025. Ultra-widefield fundus photography and optical coherence tomography (OCT) were reviewed for WWOP and DWOP prevalence, adjacency to CHRPE, and outer retinal changes.
RESULTS: WWOP was identified in 24 eyes (23%) and DWOP in 19 eyes (18%); four eyes (4%) exhibited both. WWOP was lesion-adjacent in 42% of cases, and DWOP was adjacent in 79% of cases. DWOP was associated with progressive ellipsoid-zone attenuation beyond the CHRPE margin on OCT. WWOP typically spanned a broader retinal area.
CONCLUSION: WWOP and DWOP are relatively common in CHRPE and demonstrate distinct spatial and OCT features. Multimodal imaging may aid differentiation of CHRPE from other pigmented lesions.

Title: Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation With Previous Intracranial Bleeding: Competing Adverse Events in a Nationwide Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and previous intracranial bleeding are at high risk of ischemic and bleeding events, and the benefits and risks of oral anticoagulation (OAC) remain uncertain. We investigated competing risks of recurrent intracranial bleeding, ischemic stroke (IS), and death from other causes according to anticoagulation strategy.
METHODS: This nationwide Finnish cohort study using linked administrative registries included patients with first-ever AF diagnosed in 2010-2018 and intracranial bleeding at least 120 days earlier. Follow-up began 90 days after AF diagnosis. Patients were categorized as receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), warfarin, or no OAC based on drug purchases. Warfarin users were further stratified by time in therapeutic range (TTR). Inverse probability of treatment weighting balanced baseline characteristics. Competing risks were analyzed using adjusted cumulative incidence functions and cause-specific Cox regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,502 patients (median age 78 years [IQR 71-85], 44% female, 41% with only traumatic intracranial bleeding), 15% received DOACs, 29% warfarin, and 56% no OAC. At 1 year, adjusted absolute risks of IS were 0.7%, 2.1%, and 4.1%; intracranial bleeding, 1.2%, 2.7%, and 1.9%; and death from other causes, 4.7%, 8.6%, and 14.7%, respectively. Compared with no OAC, DOAC use was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.04-0.71) and death (HR 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.46) without increased intracranial bleeding risk (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.19-2.50). Warfarin use was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.93) and death (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.44-0.80), but increased intracranial bleeding risk (HR 1.85, 95% CI 1.01-3.41). Among warfarin users, TTR ≥70% was associated with lower risks of IS (HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.08-0.79) and death (HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.10-0.36); associations were attenuated with poorer or missing TTR.
DISCUSSION: In patients with AF and previous intracranial bleeding, OAC was associated with lower risks of IS and death. DOAC use was not associated with increased intracranial bleeding risk, whereas warfarin use was. Limited information on previous intracranial bleeding and potential residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation. These findings support individualized anticoagulation decisions in this high-risk population.

Title: Early Rhythm Control vs Usual Care After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early rhythm control reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF); however, its effectiveness in the setting of acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We aimed to examine whether early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke is associated with a lower risk of recurrent stroke or systemic embolism (SE) in patients with AF.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study used the DeSC-IQVIA integrated database, an administrative claims database covering approximately 16 million individuals in Japan. Adults hospitalized for acute ischemic stroke with AF present at admission between 2014 and 2025 were included. The exposure was initiation of rhythm control (antiarrhythmic drugs, catheter ablation, or electrical cardioversion) within 8 weeks of admission (early rhythm control) vs no initiation (usual care), assessed at a landmark. The primary outcome was hospitalization for recurrent ischemic stroke or SE. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. Baseline differences were adjusted using propensity score overlap weighting. Cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs), cumulative incidence with death as a competing risk, and risk differences at 5 years were estimated.
RESULTS: Among 14,355 patients who survived event-free through the 8-week landmark (median age, 83 years [IQR, 78-88]; 6,935 [48.3%] women), 268 (1.9%) received early rhythm control. During 23,583 person-years, early rhythm control was associated with a lower risk of stroke/SE (HR, 0.56; 95% CI 0.32-0.97; weighted 5-year cumulative incidence, 8.0% vs 13.8%; risk difference, -5.9 percentage points [95% CI -11.0 to 0.8]). Among secondary outcomes, no association was observed with major bleeding (HR, 1.44; 95% CI 0.74-2.82) or HF hospitalization (HR, 0.73; 95% CI 0.39-1.38); early rhythm control was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.72; 95% CI 0.53-0.97). Results were consistent across landmark periods of 4-24 weeks.
DISCUSSION: In this nationwide cohort study, early rhythm control after acute ischemic stroke in patients with AF was associated with a reduced risk of recurrent stroke or SE. These findings suggest that early rhythm control may serve as an additional secondary prevention strategy for ischemic stroke, with flexible timing of initiation. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized controlled trials.

Title: 25 Years of Cardiac Ion Channel QSAR: From hERG Dominance to Multi-Channel Modeling.
Journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
Abstract: In 2013 the Comprehensive In Vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) initiative proposed multi-channel assessment for proarrhythmic risk evaluation, yet ligand-based predictive modeling has remained largely single-channel. To quantify and explain this mismatch, we survey 155 ligand-based modeling studies on cardiac ion channels (including conventional QSAR, machine learning, and pharmacophore- and other 3D ligand-based approaches) published between 2001 and mid-2026. Across this period, 88.4% of studies target hERG as their sole ion channel endpoint, a proportion that reflects data availability, regulatory incentives, and research inertia rather than scientific necessity. Although public data for Nav1.5 and Cav1.2 were sufficient for modeling years earlier, both channels received only isolated studies until 2022. Since then, multi-channel modeling has expanded substantially, with multiple groups now addressing the primary channels (hERG, Nav1.5, and Cav1.2) jointly. In contrast, the secondary channels (Kv7.1, Kv4.3, and Kir2.1) remain largely understudied: Kv4.3 and Kir2.1 are entirely unmodeled in the surveyed literature, and models for Kv7.1 remain scarce, likely due to the sparsity and heterogeneity of public data. A retrospective analysis of the reported model performance found no discernible improvements attributable to methodological advances. Reliability-related aspects, such as applicability domain and uncertainty quantification, were also rarely addressed. The field should treat joint modeling of the primary channels as the expected standard rather than a novel contribution. Other important aspects include the development of standardized benchmarks for multi-channel evaluation, integration with physiological models, and greater emphasis on prediction reliability. For the secondary channels, progress would additionally require coordinated data release or federated learning, methods suited to data-scarce targets, and community coordination, none of which individual research groups can establish alone.

Title: Evolutionary Weighted Hodge Laplacian Descriptors for rs-fMRI Brain Networks.
Journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
Abstract: Complex biological networks often exhibit multiscale organization that is not fully characterized by pairwise edge weights or fixed graph summaries, motivating compact descriptors that retain both topological and spectral information. Here, we present an evolutionary weighted Hodge Laplacian (EWHL) framework for resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) connectivity, in which the functional connectivity matrix of each subject is represented as a weighted Vietoris-Rips filtration and 0-dimensional and 1-dimensional weighted Hodge Laplacian spectral descriptors are extracted across 13 positive connectivity thresholds. In an autism spectrum disorder (ASD) classification task using 884 participants from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE I) cohort, EWHL reduced the original 6670-dimensional functional connectivity vector to 130 features and, with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), yielded 87.7% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.946 under 20 repetitions of 10-fold cross validation. Under the same internal protocol, EWHL outperformed a rerun raw functional connectivity baseline and a single threshold ablation, suggesting that multiscale weighted Hodge spectra provide informative descriptors for functional brain networks derived from rs-fMRI, although confound control within each fold and external validation remain necessary before clinical interpretation.

Title: Comparing the Post-Omicron Impact of COVID-19 and Non-COVID-19 Respiratory Viral Infections in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Effective treatment and prevention for respiratory viral infections (RVI) in solid organ transplant recipients (SOTR) are lacking; clinical differences in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 (ncRVI) post-omicron are unknown. We compared severity and outcomes across SOT groups.
METHODS: A single-center retrospective study of health system RVI in adult SOTR during 2022-2023 was conducted.
RESULTS: Overall, 520 RVI episodes in 504 patients were included: 488 had 1 episode and 16 had 2 episodes. Lung, kidney, and heart transplant recipients comprised of 40.9%, 34.3%, and 20.8% of the cohort. There were 352 episodes of COVID-19 RVI and 148 ncRVI. All-cause and RVI-related hospitalization were comparable between COVID-19 and ncRVI (47.7% vs. 43.9%, p = 0.50; 32.1% vs. 31.1%, p = 0.91 respectively). Oxygen supplementation occurred in 11.9% of COVID-19 RVI and 11.5% of ncRVI with a maximum requirement (median, IQR) of 4.0 (2.0-18.8) and 2.0 (2.0-3.0) liters respectively (p = 0.005). Intensive care unit (ICU) admission occurred in 7.1% and 6.1%; non-invasive ventilation (NIV) in 2.3% and 4.1%; mechanical ventilation (I&V) in 4.0% and 2.0%; and inotropic/vasopressor support in 1.7% and 1.4%, for COVID-19 versus nCRVI, respectively. Patients with COVID-19 had ongoing symptoms in 16.8%, 10.2%, and 2.6% at 30 days, 3 month, and 12 month follow up respectively, compared with 16.9%, 4.7%, and 2.0% in ncRVI. Twelve-month mortality, rejection and graft dysfunction were similar between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 and ncRVI pose significant and comparable risk to SOTR in this post-omicron era, in hospitalization, oxygen requirement, and persistent symptoms. Treatment and prevention should be prioritized in this population.

Title: Sedation and anaesthesia in pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, procedural requirements, and real-world practice.
