A combination of CP with epilepsy or seizures was more frequent in infants with AIS than in those with other stroke types.
CONCLUSION: The distribution of stroke types, symptoms, and adverse outcomes aligns with the previous literature. Acute seizures were common in AIS and HS patients. No recurrent strokes occurred during follow-up and underlying infant-related etiologies were rarely identified.

Title: Equity Gaps in Sex, Racial, and Ethnic Inclusion in United States Heart Transplant Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVE: Heart transplantation (HT) remains the definitive therapy for select patients with end-stage heart failure. Equitable representation in clinical trials is essential to ensure that evidence guiding HT practice is generalizable across populations. However, the extent of sex, racial, and ethnic inclusion in U.S. HT clinical trials has not been systematically evaluated at the level of clinical trials.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of U.S.-based HT clinical trials, with publicly available results, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov between 2000 and 2025. Demographic data on sex, race, and ethnicity were independently extracted and categorized using federal reporting standards. Trial enrollment distributions were compared with 2010 and 2020 U.S. Census data and with the overall HT data. Proportions were estimated with Wilson 95% confidence intervals, and racial distributions were assessed using multinomial confidence intervals with Bonferroni adjustment.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven eligible trials encompassing 2,271 participants were included. Female representation was low at 24.2% (95% CI: 22.5%-26.0%), below both U.S. population benchmarks (∼50%) and HT recipient proportions (27.0% in 2010; 28.4% in 2020). White participants were overrepresented (75.3%) compared with 61.6% in the 2020 U.S. population and 59.3% of HT recipients. Black participants comprised 15.5% (95% CI: 12.2%-19.5%), lower than HT populations (25.0% in 2020). Hispanic/Latino (9.7%) and Asian (1.7%) participants were markedly underrepresented relative to national (18.7%and 6.0%, respectively) populations. Multiracial (0.3%) and Indigenous and Pacific Islander participants (0%) were nearly absent. Race and ethnicity reporting improved over time, with universal reporting in trials conducted after 2020.
CONCLUSION: U.S. HT clinical trials demonstrate persistent and clinically meaningful inequities in sex, racial, and ethnic representation. These gaps may compromise the external validity of trial findings and perpetuate disparities in transplant care. Deliberate efforts to standardize demographic reporting, implement equity-focused enrollment strategies, and align trial populations with the evolving demographics of advanced heart failure are urgently needed.

Title: Lipidomics Analysis Reveals That Lipid Profile Is Associated With the Liver and Plasma in ApoE-/- Atherosclerotic Mice.
Abstract: The key pathogenesis of atherosclerosis is lipid disorders resulting from aberrant liver metabolism and release of lipids into the bloodstream, leading to endothelial damage and deposition of lipids beneath the endothelial layer. Currently, there exists a limited amount of information pertaining to alterations in liver and blood lipid metabolism. This study aimed to examine the lipid profile associated with the liver and plasma of ApoE-/- mice. ApoE-/- mice were selected because one high-fat dietary challenge produces aortic lesions and hepatic steatosis in the same animal, allowing plaque and hepatic lipid disturbance to be sampled together. Mice were randomly divided into a normal diet (ND) group and a high-fat diet (HFD) group. To validate the atherosclerosis model, histopathologic analysis techniques such as HE stain, Oil Red O stain, and Masson stain were employed. The lipid profile in both liver and plasma was evaluated using UHPLC-Q Exactive plus MS, utilizing positive and negative ionization modes. In comparison to the ND group, the HFD group exhibited elevated levels of lipid deposition, plaque area, and collagen fiber. Specifically, the liver contained 40 distinct lipids, while the plasma contained 177 distinct lipids. Further examination demonstrated that 11 distinct lipids exhibited differential content in both the liver and plasma. This study demonstrated the existence of a comprehensive lipid profile in the liver and plasma of atherosclerotic mice, with a particular emphasis on PC and TG, which may provide a new biomarker and a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying atherosclerosis.

Title: [Safety of diet therapy using ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids].
Journal: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to study the dose-dependent hypolipidemic effect of ϖ-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) in patients with cardiovascular diseases.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: An open, single-center, prospective study was conducted at the clinic of the Federal Research Center for Nutrition and Biotechnology. The tolerability, safety, and effectiveness of dietary therapy enriched with various sources of ϖ-3 PUFAs at dosages ranging from 300 to 3000 mg per day were evaluated in patients with cardiovascular diseases.
RESULTS: The study of different sources and dosages of ω-3 PUFAs demonstrated their good tolerability and safety, and revealed a dose-dependent effect on lipid profile parameters. The study demonstrated the dominant effect of different sources of ω-3 PUFAs on serum TG levels in patients with CVD.
CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that the inclusion of ω-3 PUFAs in the basic diet of patients with CVD and hyperlipidemia has an additional anti-atherogenic effect.

Title: Superior cervical sympathetic ganglion enlargement in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: An exploratory case-control study.
Journal: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
Abstract: AimIdiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) may involve bidirectional interactions between elevated intracranial pressure (ICP) and sympathetic nervous system activity along an ICP-sympathetic axis. We hypothesized that superior cervical sympathetic ganglion (SCG) volume is increased in IIH and investigated whether SCG enlargement on MRI may serve as a potential imaging covariate of disease severity associated with cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure (OP).MethodsIn this retrospective case control study, we selected IIH patients with a brain MRI within six weeks prior to lumbar puncture, and control participants with normal MRIs. We measured bilateral SCG volumes on MRI, and performed group comparisons and linear regression analyses.ResultsThirty-six IIH patients and 36 controls were included. Median OP in IIH was 24.5 cmH2O. Right, but not left, SCG volume was greater in IIH than controls (281 vs. 208 mm3, P = 0.038; BMI-adjusted P = 0.032). Combined bilateral SCG volume was also increased (631 vs. 381 mm3, P = 0.030; BMI-adjusted P = 0.026). A right SCG cutoff of ≥442 mm3 discriminated elevated OP (AUC = 0.713, optimal point for OP = 37.5 cmH2O) and was associated with increased odds of elevated OP (12.11, P = 0.016).ConclusionSCG enlargement may provide a potential imaging covariate for disease severity. However, given the exploratory nature of this investigation, future validation studies will determine its value in clinical decision-making and longitudinal assessment.

Title: Age-Friendly Health System Recognition and Its Association with Improved Clinical Outcome Measures.
Journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
Abstract: The number of adults 65 years of age and older is rapidly increasing, as is health care utilization by older adults with multiple chronic conditions. The Age-Friendly Health Systems (AFHS) movement, with a focus on What Matters, Medication, Mentation, and Mobility (the 4Ms), was launched in 2017 to improve management of older adults across health care settings. However, evidence of impact on outcomes remains limited. Using a national cohort of 4002 hospitals (388 with AFHS recognition from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement, as of December 31, 2024, and 3614 controls), the authors explore the associations between AFHS recognition and hospital readmission rates, mortality, and patient-reported experiences. Using difference-in-differences analyses, the authors find that level 2 AFHS recognition (i.e., hospitals with at least 3 months of data of older patients who have received 4Ms care) is associated with lower 30-day mortality rates for acute myocardial infarction (-0.41 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.75 to -0.06), pneumonia (-0.71; 95% CI, -1.29 to -0.13), and stroke (-0.56; 95% CI, -1.06 to -0.07). Level 1 recognition (i.e., hospitals that have successfully developed plans to implement the 4Ms) is associated with lower readmission rates only for pneumonia (-0.40; 95% CI, -0.69 to -0.10). Furthermore, both level 1 and level 2 recognition are associated with modest reductions in Medicare spending per beneficiary. No determinative associations were identified between AFHS recognition and patient-reported experience measures. These findings provide one of the first national studies to suggest that organizations with AFHS recognition could be associated with improvement in certain outcomes and spending.

Title: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin T and I Discordance in Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serial troponin monitoring is used during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, but guidelines do not specify whether high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) or T (hs-cTnT) should be measured. Unlike cardiac-specific hs-cTnI, hs-cTnT can rise from noncardiac sources.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of hs-cTnT/hs-cTnI discordance, identify clinical correlates, and evaluate prognostic implications in ambulatory ICI-treated patients.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center cohort, patients starting ICI therapy underwent paired hs-cTnT (Roche Elecsys) and hs-cTnI (Siemens Atellica) measurements in the same banked samples at baseline and 1 month. Patients with adjudicated ICI-associated myocarditis or myositis were excluded by design.
RESULTS: Among 433 patients with paired baseline measurements, hs-cTnT was elevated in 37.9% and hs-cTnI in 1.8%; 158 (36.5%) were discordant (elevated hs-cTnT, normal hs-cTnI), and 267 (61.7%) had normal levels of both (κ = 0.036). Among 329 patients with paired data at baseline and 1 month, discordance prevalence was unchanged (38.3% vs 38.0%; McNemar P > 0.99). Independent correlates were older age, male sex, and chronic kidney disease (all P < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 30.1 months (reverse Kaplan-Meier), elevated hs-cTnT was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.00-1.81; P = 0.048); only 8 of 231 deaths (3.5%) were cardiac.
CONCLUSIONS: In ambulatory patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy, over one-third had elevated hs-cTnT with normal hs-cTnI: a stable, nonspecific pattern present before ICI exposure and consistent with noncardiac sources rather than acute cardiac injury. hs-cTnI is the more cardiac-specific assay; paired baseline measurement of both troponins may help contextualize later elevations when myocarditis is suspected.

Title: Immune Responses in Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Cardiovascular Immune-Related Adverse Events: JACC: CardioOncology State-of-the-Art Review.
Abstract: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved cancer outcomes, their use can trigger autoimmune toxicities affecting essentially any organ system. In the cardiovascular system, these immune-related adverse events can manifest as myocarditis, pericarditis, accelerated atherosclerosis, vasculitis, arrhythmias, and other conditions. These cardiovascular toxicities are driven by the loss of peripheral tolerance, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Recent murine and human studies, particularly in immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated atherosclerosis and myocarditis, have begun to reveal the cellular and molecular mediators. Disinhibited T cell function is a central driver, but other immune and nonimmune cell types have also been implicated. Multiple inflammatory and chemokine receptor signaling pathways are activated, offering potential targets for intervention. The growing mechanistic understanding of these cardiovascular toxicities has begun to inform new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, though additional prospective trials are needed.

Title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
Abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) provides direct recordings of cortical activity and remains central to the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy. However, the high dimensionality and complexity of iEEG data increasingly challenge conventional visual interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have accelerated quantitative analyses in electrophysiology, supporting localization, outcome prediction, and therapeutic decision-making in epilepsy. This article reviews recent advances in the application of AI to iEEG in epilepsy and in particular stereo-EEG, although the concepts discussed are broadly relevant across iEEG modalities. Although many of these approaches have shown encouraging results, the current evidence remains largely preliminary, with most studies being retrospective, single-center investigations that lack independent external validation. AI-based integration of iEEG with multimodal magnetic resonance imaging shows promise for improving surgical planning in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Concurrently, early studies suggest that AI-driven iEEG analysis may enhance epileptogenic zone identification by detecting subtle electrophysiological signatures, network interactions, and temporal dynamics. These multimodal frameworks emphasize distributed epileptic networks rather than isolated focal abnormalities. AI is also reshaping how iEEG-guided stimulation is designed and interpreted. Data-driven approaches have the potential to optimize stimulation parameters, predict network responses, and clarify mechanisms underlying diagnostic and therapeutic stimulation, laying the groundwork for adaptive, patient-specific neuromodulation. Beyond short-term epilepsy monitoring, AI applications increasingly incorporate continuous sensing, longitudinal network modeling, and integration with implantable neurotechnology platforms. Although these developments require prospective multicenter studies with external validation before widespread clinical implementation, advances in multimodal data integration, interpretable modeling, and continuous sensing position AI-enhanced iEEG as an emerging platform for precision brain network medicine for epilepsy.

Title: Oxytocin selectively enhances the recognition of infant sadness in postpartum depression.
Abstract: BackgroundLittle is known about the role of oxytocin in the processing of positive emotional infant cues in mothers with PPD.ObjectivesWe therefore examined whether intranasal oxytocin influences postpartum mothers' processing of positive infant emotional cues, both visual (facial expressions) and auditory (laughter), and intended caregiving responses.DesignThis double-blind randomized controlled crossover study included 45 mothers, with 3- to 9-month-old infants, who exhibited clinically relevant scores on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, with 35 mothers fulfilling the criteria of a major depressive episode assessed with the SCID-5.MethodsMothers participated in two randomized counterbalanced sessions, receiving oxytocin and placebo in separate sessions with a washout period in between. During both sessions they completed an infant facial emotion recognition (FER) task and listened to infant laughter while physiological and self-report measures were collected.ResultsWe found that oxytocin shifted response bias away from fear and toward sadness, while increasing accuracy for sad infant faces. This pattern suggests that oxytocin selectively reallocates attention from threat-related cues to those signaling infant need. Additionally, oxytocin elevated heart rate in response to infant laughter, indicating greater physiological engagement with positive cues, although self-reported affect and caregiving intentions were unaffected.ConclusionsThese findings suggest that oxytocin may fine-tune perceptual and physiological responsiveness to emotionally salient infant signals rather than uniformly enhancing positive emotion recognition. The adaptive implications of this shift remain mixed: enhanced sensitivity to sadness may facilitate caregiving, yet excessive focus on distress could increase negative affect in vulnerable mothers. Oxytocin's effects thus appear emotion-specific, potentially providing mechanistic insight into altered maternal perception in postpartum depression. Future work should examine real-world caregiving behaviors and individual moderators, such as depression severity and trauma history, to clarify oxytocin's potential therapeutic relevance. Registration: The study is registered at the European Clinical Trial Registry.

Title: Cumulative exposure to integrase inhibitors and metabolic factors as independent predictors of severe hepatic steatosis in people with HIV.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The progressive ageing of people living with HIV (PLWH) has increased hepatic and metabolic comorbidities.
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluates the impact of HIV-related, metabolic and behavioural factors on hepatic steatosis and fibrosis development using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE).
METHODS: This is a single-centre cross-sectional study evaluating an Italian cohort of PLWH at an academic medical centre. Steatosis (via CAP, dB/m) and fibrosis (kPa) were assessed using VCTE. Lifestyle habits were investigated through a structured questionnaire. Factors associated with severe steatosis (S3) and with fibrosis were analysed.
RESULTS: Overall, 265 patients were included (median age 53.9 years; 89.4% with HIV-RNA < 50 copies/mL; median CD4 count 758 cells/mm3). Moderate-to-severe steatosis (S2-S3) affected 49% of the cohort (S3: 28.5%). In multivariate analysis, independent predictors of severe (S3) steatosis were longer cumulative integrase inhibitor (InSTI) exposure (aOR 1.19/year, P = 0.002), higher BMI (aOR 1.45 per kg/m2, P < 0.001), daily alcohol consumption (aOR 2.41, P = 0.031) and higher LDL cholesterol (aOR 1.20 per +10 mg/dL, P = 0.003). Regular physical activity was associated with lower CAP. Higher CAP values showed an independent association with increased liver stiffness (mean change +0.07 kPa per +10 db/m, P = 0.016), while virological suppression (HIV-RNA < 50 copies/mL) was significantly associated with reduced liver stiffness (mean change -1.61 kPa, P = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic steatosis and fibrosis are highly prevalent in PLWH. Cumulative InSTI exposure and metabolic factors may drive severe steatosis, which may accelerate fibrotic damage, whereas effective virological suppression can significantly lower fibrosis risk. Strict metabolic monitoring and lifestyle interventions should be integrated into PLWH long-term care protocols.

Title: Variability of Right Ventricular Structure and Function in Infants Across Different High-Altitude Regions: ANDES-CHD-ECHO Sub-Study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Srour, MHD Osama, Darla Carvallo-Castañeda, Monica Medina, Gian Huaman, Rafael Marquez, and Katia Bravo-Jaimes.Variability of right ventricular structure and function in infants across different high-altitude regions: ANDES-CHD-ECHO sub-study. High Alt Med Biol. 00:00-00, 2026.
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) predominance is a normal fetal state that rapidly regresses postnatally at sea level. High-altitude hypobaric hypoxic environment may alter this adaptation process. This study evaluated echocardiographic RV variations in healthy infants across different altitudes in the Peruvian Andes.
METHODS: This sub-study of the ANDES-CHD cohort included 81 healthy infants from sea level to 4,338 meters (m) in Peru. RV fractional area change (FAC) and indexed RV free wall thickness were measured. Multivariate linear regression assessed the independent effect of altitude, adjusting for relevant confounders.
RESULTS: Infants at higher altitudes exhibited a statistically significant reduction in RV FAC compared with sea level (45.5% at sea level vs. 38% at 3,259 m [p = 0.021] and 4,338 m [p = 0.006]), though all median values remained within normal physiological ranges. Sixteen percent of infants had an RV FAC < 35%, with no significant difference between high- and low-altitude groups, and no adverse outcome at 12-month follow-up. Indexed RV free wall thickness did not differ significantly across groups.
CONCLUSION: Healthy Andean infants demonstrate a physiological adaptation to high-altitude hypobaric hypoxia characterized by a statistical reduction in RV systolic function without pathological compromise, alongside normal postnatal regression of RV wall thickness.

Title: Early and Mid-Term Mortality After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Five-Year Experience from the KOSUTAVI Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) outcomes are well-documented, predictors of mortality beyond conventional surgical risk scores and valve-related factors in real-world, high-risk cohorts require further elucidation. This study aimed to identify the key determinants of 30-day and 1-year mortality following TAVI, with a focus on both patient-specific and procedure-specific complications.
METHODS: The KOSUTAVI study is a single-center, retrospective cohort analysis of 859 consecutive high-risk individuals with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI between 2020 and 2025. Primary endpoints were 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Mean age was 78.7 ± 6.5 years, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score was 7.4 ± 2.2. The 30-day and 1-year mortality rates were 6.5% (n = 56) and 12.4% (n = 107), respectively. The 5-year all-cause mortality rate was 26.3%. In multiple Cox's analysis, chronic renal failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 7.75, P = .008, 95% CI = 1.29-16.54), presentation with cardiogenic shock (HR = 5.83, P = .028, 95% CI = 1.19-15.41), major vascular injury (HR = 22.7, P = .019, 95% CI = 1.89-45.91), and cardiac tamponade (HR = 17.9, P = .012, 95% CI = 8.13-52.62) were independently associated with 30-day mortality. While these factors were all significant in univariate analysis for 1-year mortality, they did not retain independence in the multiple model. Valve type, access route, and sex were not associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSION: In a high-risk TAVI population, early mortality is predominantly driven by pre-existing renal dysfunction and acute procedural complications (shock, vascular injury, and tamponade), rather than valve-specific factors. These findings underscore the critical importance of optimizing renal function before the procedure and implementing advanced vascular protection strategies to improve early survival after TAVI.

Title: Osteonecrosis in Antiphospholipid Syndrome: An Evidence Map and Diagnostic Attribution Framework for a Noncriteria Manifestation.
Abstract: Osteonecrosis has been reported in antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) positivity, but because it also follows glucocorticoid exposure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), alcohol use, trauma, pregnancy, transplantation, and thrombophilia, its status as an APS-related manifestation is uncertain, and clinicians lack a structured way to decide whether it is APS-attributable or coincidental. We conducted a structured narrative review with evidence mapping, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus from inception to May 2026 with citation chasing; eligible reports described osteonecrosis, avascular necrosis, aseptic necrosis, or bone infarction in confirmed APS or documented aPL positivity. Twenty-two publications were charted for design, phenotype, osteonecrosis site, diagnostic modality, competing etiologies, and attribution, and synthesized narratively. Reported frequencies ranged from 3.75% and 4.5% for clinically ascertained disease to 20% for asymptomatic magnetic resonance imaging screen-detected disease in steroid-naïve primary APS-estimates that are not directly comparable. Femoral-head disease predominated, but multifocal, bilateral, and atypical-site lesions were repeatedly described. Attribution was strongest in young patients with persistent high-risk aPL, minimal traditional risk factors, and concurrent thrombotic, obstetric, or microvascular features, yet competing causes, especially glucocorticoids and SLE-frequently coexisted. We propose the APSO framework, stratifying attribution into four tiers (high-confidence, probable, uncertain/mixed, and aPL-positive osteonecrosis without classifiable APS) by APS certainty, aPL risk, osteonecrosis phenotype, and competing-cause burden. Osteonecrosis is a candidate noncriteria skeletal manifestation of APS, but aPL positivity alone is insufficient for causal attribution; prospective validation is required.

Title: Cystatin C, Neutrophil Gelatinase-associated Lipocalin, and Pro-atrial Natriuretic Peptide as Biomarkers in the Assessment of Diabetic Nephropathy Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a significant microvascular complication linked with diabetes mellitus which leads to chronic kidney disease worldwide. Conventional biomarkers, namely, serum creatinine and albuminuria often fail to detect early renal impairment.
AIM: The study aimed to compare the utility of serum cystatin C, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), and pro-atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) for assessing the severity of DN.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, observational study was conducted on 52 DN cases and 52 controls. Clinical and laboratory parameters of all were assessed at baseline. Serum creatinine, cystatin C, NGAL, and pro-ANP of cases were measured at baseline, 6 months and 12 months. Statistical analysis, including group comparison, correlation and regression analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and longitudinal analysis, was done on IBM SPSSv26.
RESULTS: At baseline, cases had significantly higher serum creatinine, cystatin C, and NGAL than controls. Pro-ANP was higher in cases but not significant. A significant Pearson's correlation appeared between cystatin C (r = -0.852), creatinine (r = -0.833), pro-ANP (r = -0.553), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (all P < 0.001). No significant correlation was observed between NGAL and eGFR. ROC analysis showed that cystatin C had the highest diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.995, P < 0.001). Time trend analysis highlighted a significant increase of cystatin C, pro-ANP, and serum creatinine (P < 0.001), but not for NGAL (P = 0.093), with increasing renal impairment over 12 months.
CONCLUSION: Cystatin C demonstrated strongest correlation with eGFR and highest diagnostic accuracy. Time trend analysis revealed significant increase in cystatin C level over 12 months, highlighting its potential role as biomarker for monitoring DN patients.

Title: A Cross-sectional Study for Estimation of Prevalence of Cognitive Impairment in Epileptic Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a frequent, but frequently overlooked, complication of epilepsy that has a negative impact on patients' quality of life and functioning. Recurrent seizures and neurological factors can have a deleterious effect on multiple cognitive domains such as memory, attention, and executive function. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scale was used to assess cognitive impairment in patients with epilepsy in this study.
OBJECTIVES: The objectives of this study were to estimate the prevalence of cognitive impairment in patients with diagnosed epilepsy for more than 2 years using the MoCA scale, assess cognitive function using the MoCA score in epilepsy patients, and determine the prevalence of cognitive impairment.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A hospital-based prospective observational study was conducted among 97 patients with epilepsy for 18 months. A MoCA scale (0-30) was used to evaluate cognitive function. Means and standard deviations were given for numerical variables, and frequencies and percentages were reported for categorical variables. The Fisher's exact test or Chi-square test was used for the analysis of categorical variables as appropriate.
RESULTS: The prevalence of cognitive impairment was significantly higher in the group with hypertension (45, 95.7%) than in the group without hypertension (40, 80.0%) (χ2 = 5.54, P = 0.02). The association between cognitive impairment and diabetes mellitus was not statistically significant. The associations with hypothyroidism, cerebrovascular accident, and ischemic heart disease were not statistically significant, as per Fisher's exact test (P = 0.99, 0.07, and 0.99, respectively).
CONCLUSION: Based on these findings, it is concluded that there is a need to consider cognitive impairment as an important and often unrecognized comorbidity with the overall disease burden of patients with epilepsy. The authors emphasize that it is crucial to include routine cognitive assessments in daily clinical practice.

Title: Diabetes, stone composition, and renal function in a large cohort of patients with nephrolithiasis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrolithiasis is linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetic patients may be at higher risk for renal decline. However, the interaction of diabetes, stone composition, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectory in patients with nephrolithiasis remains underexplored, particularly in community-based populations.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of adult stone formers with a urinary stone composition analysis on file, diabetes status and stone composition were extracted from electronic records of a large health maintenance organization. Longitudinal eGFR measurements assessed renal function decline, and the effects of stone type, diabetes, and recurrent stone events on eGFR trajectory were evaluated.
RESULTS: This study included 6,771 stone formers; 1,543 (23%) had diabetes. Diabetic patients had a significantly higher prevalence of uric-acid stones (18.3% vs. 6.5%, p<0.0001). Baseline eGFR differed robustly by stone type and diabetes status. After adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension, the rate of eGFR decline did not differ significantly by diabetes status within either the calcium-oxalate nor uric-acid subtype. Recurrent stone formers had greater renal function loss, while socioeconomic status had limited impact on eGFR change.
CONCLUSION: Diabetic and non-diabetic stone formers show distinct baseline eGFR profiles that differ by stone composition, and diabetes was strongly associated with uric-acid stone formation; however, diabetes was not associated with an accelerated rate of eGFR decline once adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and hypertension. These findings support baseline risk stratification, rather than an accelerated-decline phenotype, as the key actionable insight for diabetic stone formers.

Title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome as an Under-Recognized Cause of Ischemic Stroke in Older Adults: A Retrospective Case Series.
Abstract: Background, objective, and methods: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is classically regarded as a cause of thrombosis and stroke in younger patients and is often considered a rare etiology beyond the sixth decade. We retrospectively describe seven older adults (ages 67-90 years; median 76; four females) with ischemic stroke in whom antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) were identified during evaluation, most after one or more cerebrovascular events. Results: Six of the seven had radiographic or clinical evidence of prior cerebrovascular disease, and several had experienced recurrent events despite antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy. Antibody profiles were heterogeneous, ranging from triple positivity with confirmed persistence to isolated lupus anticoagulant and IgM-only positivity, and competing stroke mechanisms (patent foramen ovale, large-artery atherosclerosis, and small-vessel disease) were frequently present. All patients were transitioned to a vitamin K antagonist. Conclusions: This series illustrates that aPL-associated stroke does occur in older adults and supports considering APS in the differential of cryptogenic or recurrent ischemic stroke in this population, while underscoring the need for high-specificity, persistently confirmed testing before committing a patient to lifelong anticoagulation.

Title: Metabolic, Atherogenic, and Anthropometric Markers for Discrimination of Premature Coronary Artery Disease in a Predominantly Statin-Treated Cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD) is increasingly recognized in younger adults and requires improved risk stratification. Conventional lipid markers may have limited discriminative value, particularly when lipid levels reflect ongoing statin therapy. This study evaluated the associations and discriminatory performance of metabolic, atherogenic, and anthropometric indices for PCAD and developed internally validated dynamic nomograms for PCAD case discrimination.
PATIENT AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective case-control study used data from the Iran Premature Coronary Artery Disease registry. A total of 3063 adults undergoing coronary angiography were included, comprising 1929 patients with PCAD and 1134 controls. Twelve metabolic, lipid-based, and anthropometric indices were calculated from fasting glucose, lipid profiles, and body measurements. Participants were randomly divided into training and validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, integrated discrimination improvement, net reclassification improvement, and decision-curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance.
RESULTS: Atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), and a body shape index (ABSI) showed consistent independent associations with PCAD. Individually, these indices showed modest discrimination. The conventional clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.677. Adding AIP and binary ABSI increased the AUC to 0.721, while the TyG plus binary ABSI model showed the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.724, representing modest but statistically significant improvements over the conventional model. Both final models showed favorable internal calibration, and improvement in reclassification metrics, and decision-curve net benefit. Two dynamic web-based nomograms were developed for individualized PCAD case discrimination.
CONCLUSION: TyG, AIP, and ABSI were independently associated with PCAD and provided modest incremental discrimination beyond conventional risk factors in this predominantly statin-treated case-control cohort. The resulting dynamic nomograms provide an accessible framework for PCAD case discrimination; however, their clinical applicability and estimation of absolute risk require external validation in independent, preferably prospective, populations.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Brain edema progression rate on serial CT predicts neurological outcome after cardiac arrest: a region-specific biomarker of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prognostic performance of the attenuation change rate on serial brain computed tomography (CT), a novel quantitative marker of temporal cerebral attenuation change, for predicting poor neurological outcome after cardiac arrest (CA).
METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort. CA patients who underwent cranial CT both within 12 h and between 12 h and one week after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) were included. The attenuation change rate, calculated as the HU difference between paired scans divided by the time interval, was measured in 12 predefined brain regions. Neurological outcome was assessed using the Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) at discharge.
RESULTS: Of 53 patients enrolled, 17 (32.1%) had favorable neurological outcomes at discharge. Patients with poor outcomes exhibited significantly greater attenuation decline rates in all gray matter regions except for gray matter at the centrum semiovale level, including the caudate nucleus (-0.01 vs. 0.02 HU/h), putamen (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), thalamus (-0.02 vs. 0.01 HU/h), gray matter of the high convexity (-0.02 vs. 0 HU/h), and cerebellar gray matter (-0.02 vs. 0.03 HU/h) (all P < 0.01), whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in any of the white matter regions. ROC analysis demonstrated AUCs ranging from 0.725 to 0.778, with cerebellar gray matter achieving the highest AUC (0.778; sensitivity, 75.0%; specificity, 76.5%). At the 100% specificity threshold, the caudate nucleus showed the highest sensitivity for predicting poor outcome (36.1% at a decline rate of -0.040 HU/h).
CONCLUSION: Serial CT-derived attenuation change rate may serve as an exploratory quantitative marker of cerebral edema progression after cardiac arrest. However, this single-center, small-sample study does not support its use for withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment decisions. Multicenter validation is warranted.

Title: Thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risks after mastectomy with vs without direct-to-implant reconstruction.
Abstract: Immediate direct-to-implant (DTI) breast reconstruction after mastectomy provides aesthetic and logistic advantages, including single-stage restoration and avoidance of tissue expansion. However, concerns persist that increased operative duration and procedural complexity may elevate thromboembolic and hemorrhagic risk. This study compared 90-day postoperative complication rates between mastectomy and mastectomy+DTI reconstruction. A multicenter cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult female patients with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy with or without immediate DTI between 2010 and 2025 were included; autologous and staged reconstructions were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced demographics, body mass index, comorbidities, oncologic history, and preoperative medications. Outcomes included hematoma, acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE). After matching, 11 538 patients (5769 pairs) were analyzed. Mastectomy+DTI was associated with lower hematoma rates (54 patients [0.94%] vs 81 [1.40%]; risk ratio [RR], 0.675; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48-0.95; P = .024) and fewer DVT events (22 patients [0.38%] vs 48 [0.83%]; RR, 0.458; 95% CI, 0.28-0.76; P = .002). PE occurred in 17 patients (0.29%) vs 29 (0.50%) (RR, 0.586; 95% CI, 0.32-1.07; P = .076). Immediate DTI after mastectomy was associated with lower short-term rates of hematoma and DVT, with a nonsignificant trend toward lower PE rates. These findings suggest that immediate DTI was not associated with increased short-term thromboembolic or hemorrhagic morbidity in this matched cohort. Given the limitations of coding-based observational data and potential residual confounding, prospective multicenter studies incorporating granular perioperative variables are required to confirm these associations and refine risk-stratified decision-making in reconstructive care.

Title: Real-world thrombotic and survival outcomes with ESAs in cancer-related anemia.
Abstract: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) are commonly used to treat cancer-related anemia by increasing hemoglobin levels and reducing transfusion requirements. However, randomized trials and meta-analyses have linked ESA use to increased thrombotic risk. Contemporary real-world data across diverse cancer populations and ESA formulations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network (from 1 January 2015 to 31 July 2024) evaluating adult patients with cancer-related anemia. Patients receiving ESAs were propensity score-matched 1:1 with patients not receiving ESAs based on demographics, cancer type, and comorbidities. Individuals with previous thrombotic events or anticoagulant use were excluded. Outcomes included incident deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), new anticoagulant use, and 1-year survival. Risk differences, relative risks, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were performed. After matching, 1606 patients were included in each cohort, with prostate, breast, bladder, colon, and kidney cancers being the predominant cancer. There was no significant difference in DVT (1.5% vs 2.1%; P = .19) or PE (0.75% vs 1.1%; P = .27) between ESA and non-ESA groups. New anticoagulant use was significantly lower in patients treated with ESAs (6.3% vs 10.2%; risk ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49-0.78; P < .001). One-year survival was higher in the ESA cohort (73% vs 69%; hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.72-0.94; P = .004). In this large real-world cohort, ESA use was not associated with increased short-term thrombotic risk and was associated with lower anticoagulant use and improved 1-year survival. These findings suggest that guideline-concordant ESA use may be safe in selected patients with cancer-related anemia.

Title: Acute Effects of Inspiratory Muscle Training with Different Loads on Peripheral Muscle Oxygenation Kinetics and Autonomic Response in Patients with COPD: A Protocol for a Randomized Crossover Study.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) leads to inspiratory muscle weakness, which may contribute to an altered cardiovascular response during the respiratory cycle. In this context, inspiratory muscle training (IMT) emerges as one of the available tools for the treatment and monitoring of patients with respiratory muscle dysfunction.
METHODS: This is a randomized crossover study, with blinding of both the evaluator and the researcher responsible for statistical analysis. The study will evaluate the acute effects of IMT on peripheral muscle metabolism and the autonomic response in 30 patients with COPD. The primary outcomes will be peripheral muscle oxygenation kinetics, assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), and autonomic response, assessed through heart rate variability (HRV). Participants will be randomly assigned to undergo three different intervention conditions at separate times, with a minimum interval of 48 hours between each session: IMT-S (Strength), aimed at improving inspiratory muscle strength; IMT-E (Endurance), focused on enhancing inspiratory muscle endurance; and Sham, consisting of a Sham IMT intervention. For statistical analysis, continuous variables will be presented as mean ± standard deviation, and data normality will be assessed using histograms and the Shapiro-Wilk test. All analyses will follow the intention-to-treat principle. In cases of missing data due to dropouts or absence in crossover sessions, participants with incomplete data will be retained in the analysis, assuming that data are missing at random. Between-intervention differences will be analyzed using mixed linear models with Bonferroni adjustment for multiple comparisons. The level of statistical significance will be set at 0.05.
CONCLUSION: This study may help to better understand the effects of IMT performed at different loads on peripheral muscle oxygenation behavior, as well on the autonomic response in patients with COPD. These findings may improve the understanding of the physiological impacts of this therapy and support its application in pulmonary rehabilitation programs.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry NCT06827379.

Title: Impact of motor guided imagery therapy on stroke patients with pain symptoms: a three-level meta-analysis and systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke pain is a common and intractable complication that hinders neurorehabilitation progress. Motor Guided Imagery (MGI), an emerging rehabilitation technique based on brain-computer interaction principles, has shown potential in relieving post-stroke pain, yet high-quality evidence on its multi-dimensional efficacy remains insufficient. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of MGI on pain, sensorimotor function, sleep quality, life status, and psychological mood in stroke patients using a three-level meta-analysis.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to quantitatively assess the therapeutic effects of Motor Guided Imagery for stroke-related pain and explore potential intervention moderators using a three-level meta-analysis framework.
METHODS: Eight Chinese and English databases were searched from inception to June 29, 2025, to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of MGI for stroke patients with pain. A three-level random-effects model was adopted to pool Hedges' g effect sizes, accompanied by heterogeneity testing, moderator analysis, influence analysis, and publication bias assessment. Influence-based outlier detection was implemented; analyses retaining all effect-size observations were treated as the primary main analysis, while outlier-removed analyses were reported only as supplementary sensitivity checks.
RESULTS: Motor-guided imagery training significantly relieved pain (g = -0.524, 95% CI -0.779 to -0.269, p = 0.0006; negative Hedges' g indicates clinical improvement for this outcome) and improved sleep quality (g = -1.658, 95% CI -2.115 to -1.201, p < 0.001; negative Hedges' g indicates clinical improvement for this outcome) in stroke patients. Meanwhile, it significantly enhanced motor function (g = 1.395, 95% CI 0.963 to 1.826, p < 0.001), life status (g = 1.757, 95% CI 0.966 to 2.549, p = 0.0012), and psychological-emotional status (g = 1.729, 95% CI 1.045 to 2.413, p = 0.0002); positive Hedges' g indicates clinical improvement for the latter three outcomes. Moderator analysis indicated that acute-phase intervention (≤4 weeks) and high-frequency regimens (>5 sessions/week) tended to produce better analgesic effects, while age, gender, single-session duration, and pain location had no significant moderating effects.
CONCLUSION: MGI may produce beneficial rehabilitation effects that can alleviate post-stroke pain and synergistically improve motor function, sleep, daily-living ability, and psychological state of stroke patients. Exploratory subgroup trends indicated potentially larger effects for early implementation within the acute phase and high-frequency short-duration regimens. However, these observations should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating clues given non-significant overall moderator tests. Further high-quality research is required to confirm these findings.
REGISTRATION: The systematic review protocol was retrospectively registered with PROSPERO under registration ID CRD420261278812, after literature search and full-text screening had been completed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261278812; identifier: CRD420261278812.

Title: Left atrial and left ventricular radiation exposure predict long-term cardiovascular events after breast cancer radiotherapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant breast cancer (BC) radiotherapy (RT) improves survival and local control, but cardiovascular (CV) toxicity remains a concern.
AIM: This retrospective study investigated the association between RT doses to cardiac substructures and CV toxicity 15 years after BC RT.
METHODS: Women with unilateral BC diagnosed between 2007 and 2008, treated with RT at [Anonymous] were retrospectively included. Patients with major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were matched to controls by CV risk factors, anthracycline and anti-HER2 therapy. Cardiac substructures were delineated on simulation scans, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess associations between RT doses to these substructures and MACE or other CV events.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 16.5 years (IQR 16.1-17.1), and inclusion of 878 patients, 173 patients experienced MACE and were matched to 167 controls. All patients underwent adjuvant RT using 3-dimensional conformal RT to a total dose of 50 Gy in 25 fractions, with or without a boost to the tumor bed. New individual cardiac toxicities included: atrial fibrillation (AF) 98/878 (11.16%), heart failure (HF) 82/878 (9.34%), coronary artery disease (CAD) 46/878 (5.24%) and valvular disease 180/878 (20.50%). Mean heart doses were 6.62 ± 5.20Gy (MACE) and 5.76 ± 4.96Gy (controls) (p = 0.0916). Compared with controls, patients with MACE had significantly higher disease stage and more frequent histories of CAD, AF and HF. Maximum RT doses to the left atrium (LA) were associated with MACE, new-onset HF, AF and valvular disease, while mean RT dose to the left ventricle (LV) was associated with development of CAD (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients treated with RT for BC may experience diverse CV toxicities during long-term follow-up. Higher doses to left-sided cardiac substructures, particularly the LA and LV, were associated with specific CV endpoints, while MHD was not associated with toxicity.

Title: Three-dimensional laparoscopic partial nephrectomy for hilar versus non-hilar tumors: outcomes from a large contemporary series.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The management of renal hilar tumors remains a technically demanding aspect of nephron-sparing surgery. Although robotic partial nephrectomy has been widely reported in this setting, evidence from large series of purely laparoscopic procedures performed with three-dimensional vision is still limited.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 342 consecutive patients who underwent 3D laparoscopic partial nephrectomy between July 2022 and July 2025 at a high-volume tertiary center. Tumors were stratified as hilar (n = 55) or non-hilar (n = 287). The primary endpoint was warm ischemia time. Secondary endpoints included operative time, estimated blood loss, perioperative complications, need for postoperative ureteric stenting, renal function preservation, and trifecta achievement.
RESULTS: Median operative time was modestly longer in the hilar group (78 min vs 73 min, p = 0.04). Median warm ischemia time was also higher for hilar tumors (24 min vs 16 min, p <0.001) but consistently remained within the accepted threshold (<25 min). Estimated blood loss was comparable (270 ml vs 250 ml, p = 0.39). Overall complication rates were similar, though postoperative stent placement was more frequent in the hilar cohort (28% vs 7%, p <0.001). Median postoperative eGFR decline at 3 months was similar between groups. Trifecta achievement was 67.2% for hilar and 71.1% for non-hilar tumors (p = 0.27).
CONCLUSIONS: Three-dimensional laparoscopic partial nephrectomy for hilar tumors is associated with slightly longer operative and ischemia times and a higher need for postoperative stenting, but without an increase in major morbidity. In experienced hands, the functional and oncological outcomes were comparable between hilar and non-hilar tumors.

Title: Office-based transperineal laser ablation for benign prostatic hyperplasia: Functional outcomes and predictors of clinical improvement.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transperineal laser ablation (TPLA) is an ultrasound-guided, office-based procedure for the treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). This study evaluates short-term functional outcomes following TPLA and identifies predictors of clinical improvement.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This cohort included men undergoing TPLA between January 1, 2025, and February 1, 2026, using a transperineal interstitial laser system (EchoLaser, Elesta SpA). Minimum follow-up was 6 months. Variables included age, body mass index (BMI), prostate-specific antigen (PSA), PSA density, testosterone, prostate volume, International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), peak urinary flow rate (Qmax), and post-void residual (PVR). Intraoperative variables included ablation time and energy delivered. Pre- and post- treatement differences were assessed using the Wilcoxon signed rank test. Spearman correlation analysis evaluated predictors of improvement.
RESULTS: Thirty-five of forty men met the inclusion criteria. Mean prostate volume was 71.6 cm3 (range 29.8-196). Mean IPSS improved from 23.5 to 10.6 (p <0.001). Qmax increased from 7.2 to 18.4 ml/s (p = 0.007). PVR decreased from 396.8 to 70.6 ml (p <0.001). Comorbidities included urinary tract infection or urosepsis history, hypertension, diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, and anticoagulation use. Postoperative complications included three patients with urinary retention requiring catheterization and one patient with urosepsis requiring hospitalization. Greater improvement correlated with higher baseline IPSS and PVR (p <0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Office-based TPLA produced significant short term functional improvement. Functional gains were comparable to those achieved with hospital based surgical interventions. Prospective, multicenter, randomized studies are warranted to further evaluate long term durability.
