Follow-up was completed by 12.5% of patients at 3 months and 15.2% of patients at 1 year; paired baseline-follow-up assessments of physical capacity and frailty demonstrate the data structure for capturing functional recovery. Risk-adjusted benchmarking, network-wide analyses, and donor outcomes are designed capabilities of the framework that were not evaluated in this pilot. The platform is available in 16 languages and participation is open to further institutions.

Title: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for craniofacial hyperhidrosis: a 10-year retrospective cohort study on long-term outcomes and development of a prognostic predictive model.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for CFH, to characterize the 10-year longitudinal trajectory of postoperative CH and recurrence, and to identify clinically accessible predictors of CH and postoperative satisfaction that may assist in preoperative risk communication. Preliminary nomograms were developed and internally validated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 127 patients who underwent bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for CFH between April 2013 and April 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline characteristics, operative details, and follow-up outcomes were extracted from medical records and structured telephone interviews. Predictive features were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Cox proportional hazards and multivariate logistic regression models were subsequently applied to identify independent predictors of CH and satisfaction, respectively. Nomograms were developed and internally validated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity.
RESULTS: All patients achieved immediate resolution of craniofacial sweating, accompanied by a significant postoperative heart rate reduction (84.8 ± 11.68 → 72.17 ± 7.54 bpm, P < 0.001). Severe CH (grade IV) developed in 70.1% of patients, predominantly involving the thoracoabdominal (84.3%) and thigh (54.3%) regions. Cox regression identified preoperative heart rate > 79.5 bpm (HR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.61-3.75, P = 0.0002) and sympathetic clamping (HR = 5.69, 95% CI 3.03-10.67, P = 0.001) as independent risk factors for severe CH. Logistic regression showed that lower preoperative thoracoabdominal sweating was associated with higher postoperative satisfaction (OR = 0.05, 95% CI 0.01-0.23, P = 0.001). The nomograms demonstrated adequate discrimination and calibration.
CONCLUSION: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery achieves rapid and durable relief of craniofacial hyperhidrosis with sustained high satisfaction over 10 years. Beyond confirming efficacy, the extended follow-up uniquely demonstrates that CH severity stabilizes within the first postoperative year and does not worsen over time-a critical finding for patient reassurance. Preoperative resting heart rate > 79.5 bpm and the use of sympathetic clamping independently predict severe CH, whereas lower baseline thoracoabdominal sweating predicts superior satisfaction. Although the proposed nomograms require external validation before routine adoption, they offer a practical, individualized reference for preoperative risk communication and, combined with the intraoperative choice of electrocautery, support a dual-phase strategy for optimizing surgical outcomes in CFH patients.

Title: Clinical utility of SPECT/CT radionuclide shuntgraphy in suspected ventriculoperitoneal shunt dysfunction.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop and validate a more efficient diagnostic system for suspected ventriculoperitoneal shunt dysfunction by integrating traditional radionuclide shuntgraphy with SPECT imaging.
METHODS: This retrospective study examined patients with suspected shunt malfunction admitted to our neurosurgery department from 2021 to 2024, who underwent SPECT/CT imaging of the ventricular shunt. SPECT/CT results were categorized as three groups based on tracer behavior: normal shunt function, partial obstruction, and shunt obstruction. Baseline data, imaging characteristics and clinical management were recorded. Diagnostic agreement with surgery was analyzed only in patients who underwent revision, the only subgroup with a definitive intraoperative reference standard.
RESULT: A study of 46 SPECT/CT images from 42 patients found 14 normal shunt functions, 23 with partial obstruction, and 9 with complete obstruction. Nineteen patients underwent surgery, and SPECT/CT demonstrated good agreement with intraoperative findings (16/19), corresponding to a sensitivity of 88.9%. Specificity could not be reliably estimated because there were no true-negative surgical cases. Thin-slice CT scans assessing shunt catheter position and morphology revealed abnormalities such as malposition of the ventricular or abdominal catheter, tortuosity in the abdominal segment, and obstruction or rupture of the catheter body. Abnormal shunt tube positioning or morphology was more prevalent in the obstruction group (p = 0.0083).
CONCLUSION: In this heterogeneous clinical population, the SPECT/CT shunt imaging diagnostic system prove0d feasible and clinically informative.

Title: Associations between dietary scores and metabolic health in later reproductive years: results from the ROLO longitudinal study.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in women globally. Healthy dietary patterns are associated with favourable metabolic health profiles in women; however, most studies focus on the reproductive years or post menopause. This research aimed to explore associations between dietary scores and cardiometabolic health in women in later reproductive years.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This is a cross-sectional analysis of 372 women from the ROLO (Randomised cOntrol trial of a LOw glycaemic index diet in pregnancy to prevent macrosomia) longitudinal study with mean age of 42.7 (range 31.6-52.4 years), 10 years postpartum. Food frequency questionnaires were used to calculate Energy-Adjusted Dietary Inflammatory Index (E-DII) and Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015) scores. Anthropometry, body composition and non-fasting blood samples were obtained. Metabolic outcomes were examined across E-DII and HEI-2015 score tertiles. Linear regression models examined associations between dietary scores and metabolic outcomes to adjust for confounders. The median (IQR) HEI-2015 score was 62.8 (60.0,66.7) and the median (IQR) E-DII score was -0.77 (-1.5,0.12). In crude and adjusted models, highest E-DII scores (more pro-inflammatory diet) were associated with lower 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels (nmol/L) (Tertile 3: B = -10.2, 95% CI -19.5, -0.94; p = 0.031), compared to the lowest E-DII scores (more anti-inflammatory diet). No significant associations between HEI-2015 score and metabolic outcomes were found.
CONCLUSIONS: The inflammatory potential of the diet may be associated with cardiometabolic health in women in later reproductive years, highlighting an avenue for further investigation to reduce cardiovascular risk in midlife.

Title: External validation of the prognostic performance of a heart failure-specific skeletal muscle mass equation: insights from the J-Proof HF registry.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Skeletal muscle depletion in heart failure (HF) represents a key metabolic abnormality associated with adverse outcomes. However, most anthropometric equations for estimating appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (eASMI) were developed in non-HF populations, limiting their clinical applicability in HF. This study aimed to externally validate the prognostic performance of an HF-specific eASMI equation and compare it with that of general-population equations.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This secondary analysis included 9693 patients aged ≥65 years hospitalized for HF from a nationwide multicenter registry. The HF-specific eASMI equation was compared with five established equations using Cox regression, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), C-statistics, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Lower eASMI was independently associated with increased 1-year mortality (adjusted hazard ratio per 1-SD decrease, 1.50; 95% confidence interval, 1.40-1.60), with a nonlinear dose-response relationship (p for nonlinearity, 0.016 in males and 0.009 in females). In males, the HF-specific equation showed better model fit than the general-population equations (ΔAIC: 4 to 60), whereas in females, it did not (ΔAIC: -12 to 43); discrimination was similar across equations in both sexes. Despite these differences, DCA demonstrated comparable clinical utility across all equations.
CONCLUSIONS: In older patients with HF, the HF-specific eASMI equation provides robust prognostic information reflecting disease-specific metabolic alterations. While statistical advantages were observed in males, all equations demonstrated comparable clinical utility. These findings support the use of anthropometric muscle mass estimation as a practical tool for metabolic risk stratification in HF.

Title: [Novel Drugs and Therapeutic Strategies for Acute Ischemic Stroke:Focus on Tenecteplase].
Abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis remains a cornerstone of acute ischemic stroke treatment, but alteplase has a short half-life and requires complex administration. Tenecteplase (TNK) , a genetically modified variant of alteplase, is regarded as a next-generation recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator. TNK has greater fibrin specificity, a longer half-life, and greater resistance to plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, enabling single-bolus administration. Several randomized trials have supported its efficacy and safety, and its clinical use has expanded internationally. However, in Japan, alteplase at 0.6 mg/kg is the approved standard dose, and direct evidence comparing this regimen with TNK has been lacking. The investigator-initiated T-FLAVOR trial directly compared TNK 0.25 mg/kg with alteplase 0.6 mg/kg in patients with large-vessel occlusion scheduled for mechanical thrombectomy. In the T-FLAVOR trial, TNK achieved a higher rate of reperfusion on initial angiography, with comparable safety outcomes. These findings provide important evidence supporting the potential regulatory approval and clinical implementation of TNK in Japan. Other emerging therapies, including thrombolytic agents (JX10), neuroprotective agents (nerinetide), anti-edema drugs (glibenclamide), and antithrombotic agents such as factor XIa inhibitors (milvexian and asundexian), may further broaden treatment options across the acute treatment and secondary prevention phases of ischemic stroke.

Title: [Ethical Issues in Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke].
Abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has become the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) caused by large vessel occlusion, and its indications have expanded substantially over the past decade. Recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have extended eligibility to patients presenting in extended time windows, those with large ischemic cores, and other populations previously considered unsuitable for intervention. However, the expansion of MT indications has also raised important ethical challenges. Patients with AIS often lack decision-making capacity, requiring physicians to balance respect for patient autonomy with the principles of beneficence, nonmaleficence, and justice under severe time constraints. Moreover, RCTs have enrolled highly selected populations, and evidence remains limited for many patients encountered in clinical practice. This review discusses ethical issues related to MT across clinical contexts involving treatment beyond conventional time windows, large ischemic cores, medium or distal vessel occlusions, futile recanalization, active malignancy, and prestroke disability. Representative cases illustrate situations in which ethical considerations extend beyond guideline recommendations. Whenever possible, treatment decisions should incorporate each patient's premorbid functional status, values, anticipated quality of life, procedural risks, and expected neurological recovery. Continued evidence generation in understudied populations will be essential to support the ethically sound, patient-centered application of MT.

Title: [Acute-Phase Medical Treatment:Treatment to "Reduce" the Risk of Symptom Worsening].
Abstract: Acute medical management after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is often perceived as a supportive or conservative treatment, following decisions regarding intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. However, it should be regarded as an active strategy to reduce the risk of neurological deterioration and support subsequent recovery. Acute medical treatment can be divided into two components: prevention of recurrent stroke or infarct expansion, and prevention of systemic complications that may delay recovery. This approach mainly aims at preventing early neurological deterioration (END), a clinically important but variably defined phenomenon associated with poor functional outcomes. Estimating the risk of END at admission using the clinical background, comorbidities, frailty, stroke mechanism, vascular imaging, and infarct distribution guides treatment intensity and monitoring. In patients with non-cardioembolic AIS with a high risk of END, antithrombotic strategies, including prasugrel and argatroban, may be considered while balancing the risk of bleeding. Recent randomized trials support earlier initiation of direct oral anticoagulants in selected patients with cardioembolic stroke. General medical care, including hemodynamic management, mobilization, swallowing assessment, and nutrition, is essential to prevent deterioration and promote recovery.

Title: [Overview of MELT-Japan].
Abstract: MELT-Japan was a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) conducted in Japan between 2002 and 2005, in which the efficacy and safety of local fibrinolytic therapy using urokinase for acute ischemic stroke due to middle cerebral artery occlusion was compared with the best medical treatment available at the time. The results were reported in 2007. While there was no difference between the two groups in the primary endpoint (modified Rankin score[mRS], 0-2 at 90 days), the efficacy of endovascular treatment was confirmed in one of the secondary endpoints (mRS, 0-1 at 90 days), and there was no difference in safety between the two groups. MELT-Japan established a foundation for conducting multicenter RCTs, including standardization of treatment methods and imaging diagnostics, and it has assisted clinicians to understand the requirements necessary to plan and conduct RCTs, thus greatly contributing to the subsequent development of clinical research in Japan.

Title: Operator-level variation in the extensiveness of percutaneous coronary intervention for acute coronary syndrome.
Troponin elevation strongly predicts hospital admission but not 30-day outcomes in emergency department paroxysmal SVT: a propensity-matched cohort study.
