Title: Later-line Treatment Selection in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Trifluridine/Tipiracil Plus Bevacizumab, Regorafenib, and Fruquintinib.
Abstract: Later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) increasingly requires selection among treatments with different mechanisms, toxicity profiles, and sequencing evidence. Trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab has robust randomized evidence from SUNLIGHT, but objective response remains uncommon and hematologic toxicity can limit treatment delivery in heavily pretreated patients. Regorafenib and fruquintinib are minimally myelosuppressive oral alternatives, yet they differ in dose strategy, hepatotoxicity, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, and proteinuria. This narrative review updates pivotal and recent evidence and proposes an evidence-informed framework that treats hematologic reserve as a clinical fitness construct rather than a fixed laboratory threshold. We additionally examine the clinical implications of low response rates, prior anti-angiogenic exposure, emerging molecular predictors including KRAS G12, evidence in older or vulnerable patients, and recent phase III developments. Current data do not support a validated molecular biomarker for choosing among these three options, and no randomized head-to-head comparison of regorafenib and fruquintinib exists. Accordingly, treatment selection should be individualized according to prior therapies, toxicity vulnerability, organ function, tumor tempo, and patient goals. Hypertension and proteinuria are important selection factors but may also be modifiable treatment-delivery factors. The proposed algorithms and adverse-event radar chart are intended as practical visual syntheses rather than validated guidelines or formal cross-trial comparisons.

Title: 20-year analysis of protocol-driven quality improvement in cardiac homograft banking.
Abstract: Cardiac homografts are indispensable in complex cardiac surgery, particularly in the paediatric population. Optimising procurement and minimising discard rates are important for maintaining graft availability, especially in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated 20 years of cardiac homograft procurement at a tertiary cardiovascular centre, focusing on discard rates, causes of discard, microbiological profiles, and the impact of protocol refinements. A retrospective analysis was conducted using procurement records from the Cardiac Homograft Tissue Bank at the Institut Jantung Negara, Malaysia, between January 2004 and December 2024. The data collected included annual procurement volume, reasons for discarding, and microbiological culture results. In 2015, a revised procurement protocol was introduced, which incorporated instrument and operative field segregation, aseptic redraping, and enhanced donor screening. A total of 190 hearts were procured (mean 9.05 ± 4.18 hearts/year), with an overall discard rate of 13.7% (of 26/190). Prior to 2015, the discard rate was 17.2% (20/116), with environmental contamination accounting for the majority of the discards (75%; n=15). Fifteen microbial isolates were identified in the pre-revision period: Candida (n=6), Klebsiella (n=4), Acinetobacter (n=2), Streptococcus spp. (n=1), Streptococcus viridans (n=1), and Pseudomonas spp. (n=1). Following the 2015 protocol revision, the overall discard rate decreased to 8.1% (6/74), representing a 53% reduction, although this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.074). Environmental contamination-related discards decreased significantly from 12.9% (15/116) to 1.4% (1/74) (89% reduction; p=0.005), with only one Candida isolate identified post-revision. Protocol refinement has therefore produced a statistically significant reduction in contamination-related discards and a shift in the microbiological spectrum.

Title: Cardiomyocyte-derived IL-30 improves cardiac repair by reducing splenic germinal center activation after myocardial infarction.
Abstract: Following myocardial infarction (MI), splenic humoral immune responses contribute to cardiac injury and repair, yet the cardiac signals that govern these responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identified ischemic cardiomyocytes as a source of interleukin 30 (IL-30; the interleukin 27 p28 subunit) and investigated its role in heart-spleen communication. In mice, cardiomyocyte-specific IL-30 deficiency enhanced splenic germinal center responses and signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) phosphorylation. This deficiency increased myocardial IgG deposition, TNF-α expression in Fc gamma receptor III-positive macrophages, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis, while impairing cardiac function and aggravating ventricular remodeling. Recombinant IL-30 suppressed splenic germinal center responses and STAT1 phosphorylation and improved cardiac function. The effects of recombinant IL-30 on germinal center responses and cardiac function were abolished by B cell-specific deletion of glycoprotein 130 (gp130). Furthermore, no detectable improvement in cardiac function was observed following IL-30 treatment in splenectomized mice. In patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI; n = 75), lower circulating IL-30 levels were associated with higher peripheral IgG-positive B cell frequencies. In a separate longitudinal cohort of 247 patients with STEMI, low circulating IL-30 was independently associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling at 6 months (odds ratio, 4.44; 95% confidence interval, 2.16-9.80; P< 0.001). Circulating IL-30 discriminated patients with and without adverse remodeling with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.738. These findings identify cardiomyocyte-derived IL-30 as an endogenous regulator of heart-spleen communication that restrains splenic humoral responses and limits adverse cardiac remodeling after MI.

Title: Contemporary outcomes after 100 consecutive HeartMate 3 LVAD implantations: a single-centre cohort study from a Swiss tertiary centre.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The HeartMate 3 left ventricular assist device (LVAD) is an established therapy for advanced heart failure, yet contemporary real-world data from low- or medium-volume centres remain limited. We aimed to describe the characteristics, management and clinical outcomes of patients undergoing HeartMate 3 LVAD implantation at a Swiss tertiary centre.
METHODS: We conducted an observational study including consecutive adult patients who underwent HeartMate 3 implantation at Lausanne University Hospital between November 2015 and January 2026. Baseline characteristics, INTERMACS profiles, perioperative data, survival and LVAD-related complications were assessed. The primary outcome was survival on LVAD support. Comparisons by LVAD indication were pre-specified exploratory analyses (destination therapy vs bridge-to-transplant). Survival analyses on LVAD support, with heart transplantation or LVAD explantation treated as censoring events, were reported.
RESULTS: A total of 100 patients (mean age 58 [standard deviation 12] years, 84% male, 29% destination therapy) underwent HeartMate 3 implantation. Ischaemic heart disease was the predominant aetiology (69%) and most patients (68%) were classified as INTERMACS profiles 3-4 at implantation. Over a median follow-up of 1.5 (IQR 0.5-3) years, 27 patients died on LVAD support, corresponding to a mortality incidence rate (IR) of 13.5 deaths per 100 patient-years, while 51 patients underwent heart transplantation, corresponding to an IR of transplantation of 25.4 per 100 patient-years. Five-year survival on LVAD support was 64%, with patients censored at LVAD explantation for recovery or transplantation. LVAD-related complications included bleeding (48%), infection (50%), ischaemic stroke (12%) and right ventricular failure (39%). Survival did not differ by LVAD indication (bridge-to-transplant as reference, adjusted HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.14-2.72).
CONCLUSIONS: In this contemporary, real-world, medium-sized cohort, HeartMate 3 therapy provided durable long-term support across a broad spectrum of advanced heart failure patients, with outcomes consistent with those reported in large multicentre registries.

Title: Semantic distance metrics in anatomy education: Toward AI-assisted mapping of anatomy-to-clinical reasoning.
Abstract: Anatomy education traditionally emphasizes structural knowledge acquisition, with the implicit assumption that clinical reasoning capabilities will naturally follow. However, the cognitive pathway from anatomical understanding to clinical application is rarely linear or uniform. This article proposes a conceptual framework in which semantic distance-the conceptual separation between anatomical knowledge and clinical endpoints-operates at three analytically distinct levels: (1) the learner's internal cognitive network, shaped by prior experience and schema formation; (2) the structural distance within curriculum maps, ontologies, or knowledge graphs; and (3) the distributional proximity within large language model (LLM) embedding spaces, which may serve as a scalable computational proxy indicator for the first two levels. These three levels must be explicitly distinguished if semantic distance is to function as a useful construct in anatomy education. To illustrate the framework's utility, three worked examples are developed-the femoral nerve, coronary circulation, and spinal cord anatomy-accompanied by a preliminary computational illustration of embedding distances rather than an empirically validated diagnostic instrument. A practical educator workflow is proposed through which computational signals may be translated into targeted curriculum decisions. The article positions semantic distance metrics as complementary to curriculum network analytics and highlights how cross-domain transitions (from anatomy through physiology and pathology to clinical presentation) represent qualitatively different educational problems requiring different interventions. Prospective validation studies, multimodal computational approaches, and longitudinal curriculum outcome analyses are needed before this framework can be applied systematically.

Title: Enhanced liver fibrosis score is associated with cognitive performance during an 11-year follow-up period.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has been associated with poorer cognitive performance and greater cognitive decline. However, the liver-brain axis and the role of liver health in cognitive decline are still poorly understood. Thus, using both cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, we aimed to study how liver fibrosis score (ELF), an indicator of liver fibrosis, is associated with cognitive performance.
METHODS: This study was based on the Health 2000 Survey and its follow-up, the Health 2011 survey, which collected data from a nationally representative sample of the Finnish adult population. At baseline, verbal fluency, wordlist learning, delayed wordlist recall, and simple and multiple-choice reaction time tests were conducted. At follow-up, all tests except the reaction time tests were repeated. A global z-score was derived from the individual cognitive domains. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to study the association between ELF and cognitive performance while adjusting for demographic, metabolic, and cardiovascular covariates.
RESULTS: Cross-sectionally (n=5115; mean age 53.2 y; 58.6% women), high ELF was associated with poorer global cognition and slower simple and multiple-choice reaction times compared with low ELF. High ELF was also associated with worse global cognition and performance in the wordlist learning test, both cross-sectionally and longitudinally (n=2490; mean age 48.7 y at baseline; 58.0% women).
DISCUSSION: High ELF, an indicator of liver fibrosis, was associated with poorer global cognition both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. Worse performance was observed in cognitive domains that reflect poorer processing speed and executive function, verbal learning, attention, and working memory. These results imply that liver fibrosis could represent an early modifiable marker of cognitive vulnerability.

Title: Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression: Plaque-Free vs Plaque-Adjacent Segments.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) density on coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) reflects pericoronary inflammation, but measurements adjacent to existing plaques may be confounded by local inflammatory signaling from the plaque itself-a form of reverse causation. Whether systematically comparing patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches (including measurements restricted to plaque-free segments) can identify a more robust inflammatory biomarker has not been evaluated.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to compare the predictive performance of 4 patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches for coronary plaque progression.
METHODS: From the PARADIGM serial coronary CTA registry, 412 patients with baseline coronary plaque who underwent serial coronary CTA at identical tube voltages were included (mean age: 61.1 ± 9.3 years; 61.7% male; mean interval: 3.2 ± 1.2 years). Four patient-level PVAT measures were compared: proximal right coronary artery (pRCA), whole-coronary, plaque-free, and plaque PVAT. Multivariable regression models were constructed for annualized plaque volume (PV) progression with adjustment for clinical risk factors and imaging covariates.
RESULTS: Annualized increases in pRCA PVAT (β = 0.804; P = 0.033), whole-coronary PVAT (β = 1.142; P = 0.022), and plaque-free PVAT (β = 1.419; P = 0.007) were each independently associated with total PV progression, whereas plaque PVAT did not reach significance (β = 0.755; P = 0.083). For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT was the only significant measure (β = 1.086; P = 0.026). None of the 4 baseline PVAT measures were significantly associated with plaque progression (all P > 0.50). Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences among the 4 measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure. (Progression of AtheRosclerotic PlAque DetermIned by Computed TomoGraphic Angiography Imaging [PARADIGM]; NCT02803411).

Title: Electromechanical Window Negativity and Arrhythmic Risk in Arrhythmogenic Mitral Valve Prolapse.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) is generally a benign valvular heart disease, but a subset of patients is at particular risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (AMVP).
OBJECTIVES: The authors evaluated the electromechanical window (EMW) as an arrhythmia-risk marker in (A)MVP (the sum of all MVP and AMVP patients).
METHODS: Healthy controls, patients with MVP without ventricular arrhythmia (MVP/-VA), and patients with AMVP with nonsustained (AMVP/nsVA) or sustained ventricular arrhythmia (AMVP/VA) (ventricular arrhythmia >30 seconds) were retrospectively included from 3 centers (derivation cohort). An independent validation (A)MVP cohort was recruited from 2 centers. EMW was calculated blinded from apical Doppler echocardiography by subtracting the QT time from the simultaneous Q-to-aortic-valve closure time (QAoC).
RESULTS: In the derivation cohort (31 controls, 31 MVP/-VA, 29 AMVP/nsVA, 14 AMVP/VA), patients with (A)MVP displayed a borderline shorter QAoCc (P = 0.06) and significantly longer QTc than controls (P < 0.0001), resulting in a more negative EMW (-18 ms [-47 to -8 ms]; P < 0.0001). EMW was most negative in patients with AMVP/VA (-71 ms [-177 to -30 ms]). These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort (n = 76 with [A]MVP), albeit at different absolute values. In a pooled receiver-operating characteristic analysis, EMW identified patients with AMVP/VA with an area under the curve of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.91), significantly outperforming QTc and QAoCc. An EMW threshold of -30 ms was the optimal cutoff (sensitivity: 0.71; specificity: 0.83). EMW was independently associated with AMVP/VA status and improved model performance in addition to established risk parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: EMW is markedly negative in patients with AMVP/VA, reflecting electromechanical discordance. Thus, EMW emerges as a promising risk-associated marker in (A)MVP.

Title: Long-Term Outcome Following Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation and Potential Emerging Etiologies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unexplained cardiac death and cardiac arrest associated with idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF) are heterogeneous pathologies responsible for significant mortality in young people.
OBJECTIVES: This retrospective multicenter cohort study evaluated the natural history of a large cohort of IVF survivors including recurrence burden, emerging etiologies, and long-term management.
METHODS: This study included IVF patients from 46 tertiary centers and followed for at least 5 years. Patients over the age of 15 years who had documented ventricular fibrillation and extensive negative investigations supporting the diagnosis of IVF were included. Patients were followed in each center with their outcome being established on data collection from subsequent clinical records, new investigations, genetic results, and implanted defibrillator recordings. Recurrent arrhythmias and mortality were assessed. Diagnoses were graded as definite (direct evidence) or probable (indirect criteria).
RESULTS: A total of 825 patients (37% women; age 35.7 ± 12 years) were followed for a median duration of 120 months (Q1-Q3: 78-180 months). Death occurred in 27 patients (3.3%) from cardiac (n = 10; 1.2%), noncardiac (n = 9; 1.1%), and unknown (n = 8; 1%) causes, and few patients (4.5%) developed overt cardiomyopathy. Overall arrhythmia recurrence increased steadily over 2 decades, reaching 52.7% of patients, with a median time to first recurrence of 20 months (Q1-Q3: 5-48 months) and a similar incidence in men and women. Emergent etiologies occurred in 68.8% of the total population, and were associated with new information during recurrences, structural changes, genetic results, and mapping procedures. They included reclassified inherited arrhythmia conditions in 73 (8.8%), focal sources in 272 (33.0%), and definite or probable microstructural myocardial alterations (MiCMs) with normal imaging in 223 (27.0%), while no diagnosis was identified in 257 (31.2%). Compared with MiCM, focal IVF included more women, occurred more frequently at rest/sleep, and was associated with narrow QRS complexes (90.1 ± 12 milliseconds vs 104.8 ± 16 milliseconds; P < 0.001). Quinidine appeared effective in preventing focal IVF (68.3%) whereas beta-blockers appeared effective (49.3%) in MiCM-IVF. Catheter ablation was performed in 181 patients with no recurrence observed in 75.7%.
CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter long-term cohort study of IVF survivors shows low cardiac mortality, a persistent risk of arrhythmia recurrences over time, and identifies potential emerging etiologies.

Title: Circular RNAs in Drug-Induced Cardiotoxicity: Roles, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Potential.
Journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
Abstract: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major challenge in drug development and clinical practice, often resulting in treatment interruption, drug attrition, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. DIC has been associated with a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anthracyclines, HER2-targeted therapies, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other cardiotoxic drugs. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have attracted increasing attention as stable and versatile regulatory RNAs involved in cardiovascular injury. This review summarizes the biogenesis and functional mechanisms of circRNAs, their pathological roles in DIC, biomarker potential, therapeutic implications, and translational challenges. CircRNAs regulate gene expression through diverse mechanisms, including miRNA sequestration, interactions with RNA-binding proteins, transcriptional regulation, modulation of alternative splicing, and, in some cases, peptide translation. These regulatory functions have been implicated in apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, pyroptosis, and cardiac remodeling during DIC. Emerging evidence suggests that circRNAs may serve as candidate molecular markers and potential therapeutic targets for DIC. However, the current evidence is derived predominantly from cellular and animal models, with doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity accounting for a substantial proportion of available studies. Clinical validation, particularly in well-characterized patient cohorts and across different drug classes, remains limited. Overall, further efforts are needed to establish standardized circRNA detection and quantification methods, validate their functional roles, conduct prospective clinical studies, and determine their incremental value in combination with established cardiac biomarkers before circRNA-based approaches can be translated into clinical management of DIC.

Title: No Reflow at Perfusion Imaging: Thresholds That Distinguish Functional and Tissue Outcome Groups in Acute Stroke.
Abstract: Background Poor outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may reflect microvascular dysfunction, or no-reflow phenomenon, but operational definitions are lacking. Purpose To identify the most informative candidate no-reflow definition at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging for outcome assessment. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis used data from two prospective multicenter imaging registries of patients with acute stroke who were recruited between June 2016 and July 2022, achieved modified thrombolysis in cerebral infarction grade 2c or 3 recanalization after EVT, and underwent pre-EVT and 24-hour post-EVT CT or MR perfusion imaging. Candidate no-reflow definitions were evaluated across eight perfusion maps and their corresponding stepwise thresholds. Delay time (DT) quantifies the delay in contrast material arrival between arterial input and brain tissue. For primary screening, no-reflow status was defined as any residual hypoperfusion lesion for each map-threshold combination. The best-performing combination was evaluated using residual volume and reperfusion index cutoffs. The primary outcome was poor 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score >2); infarct growth was secondary. Associations with the outcome were evaluated using multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression. Results The primary cohort included 67 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 56-77 years]; 41 male), and the independent cohort comprised 54 patients (median age, 69 years [IQR, 62-78 years]; 28 female). In the primary cohort, lesions with DT longer than 4 seconds showed the strongest discrimination for poor 90-day functional outcome (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.72 [95% CI: 0.57, 0.86]; P < .001). According to this definition, 14 of 67 patients (21%) had no reflow. Poor functional outcome occurred in 11 of 14 patients (79%) with no reflow and 11 of 53 (21%) with reflow (odds ratio, 12.14 [95% CI: 3.38, 54.63]; P < .001). Infarct growth was greater with no-reflow status than with reflow (median, 24.1 mL [IQR, 3.7-40.7 mL] vs 0 mL [IQR, -10.1 to 6.1 mL]; P < .001). Findings were consistent in the independent cohort. Conclusion The presence of a lesion with DT longer than 4 seconds at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging appeared to be the most informative candidate no-reflow definition. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Gemmete in this issue.

Title: [Cognitive status in elderly patients with chronic cerebral ischemia treated with Mexidol].
Journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of sequential Mexidol therapy, administered intravenously and orally over 74 days as part of a comprehensive treatment regimen, on cognitive status in elderly patients with chronic cerebral ischemia (CCI) and cognitive impairments.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: AThis prospective open-label study included 90 elderly patients with CCI (mean age 81±3 years). The main group (MG, n=43) received standard therapy plus Mexidol, and the comparison group (CG, n=47) received standard therapy alone. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Stroop test, and Schulte test at baseline and after three months.
RESULTS: At baseline, the groups were comparable in sex, age, and clinical and cognitive status. After three months of therapy, the median MMSE score in the main group (MG) was 27 points, significantly higher than the 26 points observed in the comparison group (CG) (p<0.001; Δ=8.0%). In the MG, no patients had mild dementia, whereas the percentage in the CG remained unchanged at 18.6%. In the Stroop test, the increase in the number of words named in the MG was 7 (95% CI 5; 8), compared to 2 (95% CI 0; 3) in the CG; the median was 70 and 66 words, respectively (Δ=8.0%; p<0.001). Nine patients (21.9%) in the CG scored fewer than 65 words, while none in the MG did so. The interference ratio decreased by 5.5% in the MG compared to 2.5% in the CG (p=0.004). The time to complete the Schulte test in the MG decreased by 8.0 seconds (95% CI -10.9; -5.1), compared to 2.0 seconds (95% CI -4.8; 0.8) in the CG; the difference between groups was 6.0 seconds (95% CI -9.2; -2.8). Work efficiency (WE) increased from 0.14 to 0.19 in the MG (35.7%), and by 6.7% in the CG. Four patients in the MG (9.3%) and nine in the CG (19.1%) had WE >0.25. Mental stability improved by -4.0% (95% CI -6.3%; -1.7%) in the MG versus -1.0% (95% CI -3.2%; +1.2%) in the CG, with a difference of 3.0% (95% CI -6.2%; +0.2%; p>0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Sequential administration of Mexidol as part of comprehensive therapy in elderly patients with chronic cerebral ischemia led to greater improvements in cognitive status, speed and efficiency of mental performance, cognitive control, and mental resilience than standard therapy alone. These findings indicate pro-cognitive and neuroprotective effects of Mexidol.

Title: Risk of venous thromboembolism in chronic inflammatory skin diseases: A retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

Title: Stroke Mortality in Adults Aged 20-59 Years in Chile, 2002-2021: An Epidemiological Study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Stroke is a major cause of death and disability in Chile and worldwide. Although its greatest burden affects older adults, its impact on individuals of working age is concerning. In Chile, the Explicit Health Guarantees (GES) program has improved access to stroke diagnosis and treatment; however, differences in mortality by sex, age, and region persist.
AIM: To describe the magnitude, temporal trends (2002-2021), and regional distribution of stroke mortality among Chilean adults aged 20-59 years.
METHODS: An ecological, observational, and analytical study based on records of stroke-related deaths (ICD-10: I60-I69) from the Department of Health Statistics and Information (DEIS) and population projections from the National Statistics Institute (INE) for the period 2002-2021. Mortality rates were calculated by sex, age decade, and region. Temporal trends were assessed using Prais-Winsten regression, and spatial distribution was assessed using mortality rate ratios (MRR) by five-year periods.
RESULTS: Between 2002 and 2021, 19,438 deaths from stroke were recorded among adults aged 20-59 years, 57.6% of which occurred in men. Age-specific mortality rates increased with age and were higher in men. However, a significant reduction in mortality was observed, particularly in individuals aged 40-59 years. Regional disparities were evident, with mortality rate ratios between two and three times higher in the country's extreme regions compared with the national average Conclusions: From 2002 to 2021, stroke mortality among Chilean adults aged 20-59 years showed a steady decline, although regional inequalities persisted. Enhanced surveillance, prevention, and timely access to diagnosis and treatment are recommended in regions showing disproportionately high mortality.

Title: Impact of Coronary Artery Disease on Long-Term Valve Function After the Ozaki Procedure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study (2015 - 2020).
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Ozaki procedure reconstructs the aortic valve with autologous pericardium, but long-term leaflet durability remains uncertain. Coronary artery disease (CAD) may reflect a systemic atheroinflammatory milieu associated with impaired leaflet integrity.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 733 patients undergoing Ozaki reconstruction from 2015 to 2020 and assessed the association between CAD and aortic regurgitation (AR) ≥ 2 at last echocardiographic follow-up. Baseline heterogeneity was addressed using propensity-score overlap weighting based on age, sex, body mass index, body surface area, weight, diabetes, European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II, aortic stenosis, bicuspid valve, and peripheral artery disease. Effects were estimated as weighted risk ratios (RRs) using Poisson models with robust variance. Sensitivity analyses used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and an extended model including prior myocardial infarction/percutaneous coronary intervention.
RESULTS: Of 733 patients, 365 (49.8%) had CAD. Unadjusted AR > 2 rates were 10.1% in CAD vs. 5.7% in no-CAD patients (P = 0.037). After overlap weighting, weighted risks were 12.7% vs. 6.2%, yielding RR 2.05 (95% CI, 1.01 - 4.18; P = 0.048), with excellent covariate balance. IPTW showed consistent results: RR 2.22 (95% CI, 1.38 - 3.56; P = 0.001). Regurgitation-free survival was lower in CAD patients (log-rank P = 0.0087).
CONCLUSION: CAD was associated with an approximately two-fold higher risk of AR ≥ 2 after Ozaki reconstruction. This association likely reflects systemic atheroinflammatory processes rather than a direct mechanical effect, supporting closer postoperative surveillance in CAD patients.

Title: Surgical Treatment of Rare Multiple Cardiac Myxomas: A 13-Year Clinical Experience at a Single Institution.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac myxoma (CM) is the most common primary cardiac tumor. Multiple CMs are rare and can lead to heart failure and arterial embolism. This study aimed to explore clinical characteristics, surgical treatment experience, and follow-up strategies for multiple CMs.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on eight patients with multiple CMs who underwent surgical treatment. Clinical characteristics were analyzed by extracting relevant clinical data, electrocardiography and echocardiography findings, surgical treatment details, and postoperative follow-up information. All patients had undergone cardiopulmonary bypass surgery. Pathological analysis was performed on all tumors, and postoperative cardiac ultrasound follow-up was also conducted.
RESULTS: Multiple CMs were uncommon, representing only 5.9% of all cases. Among 136 patients with cardiac tumors admitted during the same period, only eight had multiple CMs. All patients with multiple CMs underwent complete tumor resection. The size of the resected tumors was approximately 5-80 (39.3 ± 20.3) mm. The follow-up period ranged from one to nine years. The recurrence rate was 37.5% (3/8), and all recurrent cases underwent reoperation for tumor resection. There were no perioperative deaths, and overall surgical outcomes were satisfactory.
CONCLUSION: Our study reveals that surgery is the best strategy for multiple CMs. The tumor should be completely resected, and color Doppler echocardiography is recommended every six months postoperatively to detect tumor recurrence. Those cases of multiple myxomas have had high recurrence rate after resection (37.5%) but were submitted successfully to a new resection. Timely surgical resection provides favorable outcomes for patients with multiple or recurrent CMs.

Title: Association between thyroid feedback quantile-based index and the risk of in-hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer.
Abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback quantile-based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles. Model 1 was unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and smoking; Model 3 additionally adjusted for diabetes duration, HbA1c, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, CRP, and dyslipidemia. RCS assessed dose-response patterns; Firth regression was used for sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Fifty-six patients underwent amputation. In Model 3, each 1-SD increase in TFQI (equivalent to a 1-unit increase in pre-scaled TFQI) was associated with higher odds of amputation (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.63-3.15; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, ORs were 2.94 (0.98-8.83; P = 0.055), 5.60 (1.88-16.67; P = 0.002), and 14.79 (5.22-41.89; P < 0.001) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS showed an overall association (P = 0.002) and nonlinearity (P = 0.046) in Model 3. Firth estimates were broadly consistent with conventional regression.
CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized DFU patients with normal thyroid function, higher TFQI levels are associated with an increased risk of amputation during hospitalization. Nevertheless, the clinical utility of TFQI requires further validation in prospective studies.

Title: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: IntroductionSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) and lupus nephritis (LN) carry substantial cardiorenal risks. Conventional immunosuppressive therapies primarily target inflammation but leave a burden of residual renal and metabolic damage. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide clear cardiorenal protection in general populations, but data specific to SLE remains limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of SGLT2i in patients with SLE and LN.MethodsComprehensive searches across five electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus) were conducted up to April 2026 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies assessing SGLT2i in adult SLE/LN patients. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize cardiorenal and safety outcomes using R Software.ResultsSix studies published between 2024 and 2025 were included. Pooled data demonstrated that SGLT2i use was associated with a significant improvement in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) compared to controls (MD: 4.02; 95% CI: 1.39-6.65; I2 = 60.1%). SGLT2i significantly reduced the risks of progression to end-stage kidney disease (RR: 0.37; 95% CI: 0.25-0.56; I2 = 11.0%), heart failure development (RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.56-0.75; I2 = 0.0%), incident lupus nephritis (RR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.44-0.76; I2 = 0.0%), and re-hospitalizations (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.57-0.79; I2 = 0.0%). Furthermore, a significant reduction in all-cause mortality was observed (RR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.36-0.86; I2 = 76.2%). SGLT2i treatment demonstrated an acceptable safety profile across the included cohorts. The certainty of evidence for these findings was rated as low to very low, and results remain vulnerable to residual confounding from variables such as disease activity, corticosteroid burden, and immunosuppressive regimen.ConclusionPreliminary exploratory evidence suggests potential associations between SGLT2 inhibitors and cardiorenal outcomes in lupus nephritis. Given the low certainty of evidence and vulnerability to residual confounding from disease-specific variables, these hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in well-designed randomized controlled trials.

Title: Treatment attrition and outcomes of myeloma patients in Finland: a real-world study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Relapses, need for further treatment lines and significant treatment attrition are typical for multiple myeloma (MM). This retrospective study investigates attrition and outcomes among MM patients in Finland. Patient, material and methods: Study included all adult MM patients (n = 1733) diagnosed and treated in four hospital districts in Finland in 2013-2022. Data were collected from hospital data lakes, Statistics Finland and Social Insurance Institution. Treatment attrition was defined as death before next treatment line.
RESULTS: By the end of follow-up 31% of patients without stem cell transplantation (non-SCT) had died before initiation of second line treatment (2L), compared with 5% of stem-cell transplant (SCT) patients. The factors associating with this early attrition in the non-SCT cohort were older age (over 75 years), higher comorbidity burden, International Staging System (ISS), and (R)-ISS scores (p < 0.001). Furthermore, non-SCT patients were more likely administered less intensive therapy during 1L (p < 0.001). During the first 6 months post diagnosis in the non-SCT cohort, the most common immediate cause of death was MM. Also, during later stages MM was responsible for 54% of deaths in the non-SCT and 68% in the SCT cohorts whereas infections were linked principally with early deaths before 2L treatment.
INTERPRETATION: This study highlights significant treatment attrition across disease course and also early mortality especially in the non-SCT cohort resulting primarily from progressive MM or infections. The findings underscore the need for more tolerable and effective anti-myeloma treatments in earlier course of the disease to enhance patient survival.

Title: Efficacy of tafamidis across age groups in ATTR-CM: insights from real-world data.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Elderly patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remain underrepresented in clinical trials. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of tafamidis 61 mg in patients with ATTR-CM across different age groups.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients with ATTR-CM treated with tafamidis 61 mg were stratified into age groups: < 75, 75-85, > 85 years. Clinical and echocardiographic data were collected at baseline and follow-up. The primary outcome - cardiovascular-related hospitalization and cardiovascular death - was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 89 patients with ATTR-CM were included: < 75 (n = 23), 75-85 (n = 40), and > 85 years (n = 26). Hereditary ATTR-CM was more prevalent in younger patients (p < 0.001). Older patients (≥ 75) were more often in NYHA class II/III (p = 0.009), required higher diuretic doses (p < 0.001), and had higher NT-proBNP (p = 0.002). At baseline, patients ≥ 75 years had greater maximal wall thickness (p < 0.001) and left ventricular mass (p = 0.034); global longitudinal strain was most impaired in those > 85 years (p = 0.039). Over a mean follow-up time of 27.4 ± 19.3 months, tafamidis treatment in patients > 85 years was associated with a greater reduction in NT-proBNP (p = 0.041) and in diuretic doses compared to those < 75 years (p = 0.044). No significant changes were observed in NYHA class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire scores, or echocardiographic parameters. The composite outcome of cardiovascular-related hospitalization and cardiovascular death did not differ significantly among age groups (Log-Rank 5.71, p = 0.06).
CONCLUSIONS: This study underscores the benefits of tafamidis in elderly patients, including those aged > 85 years, and supports its use across all age groups to improve cardiovascular outcomes in ATTR-CM.

Title: Preoperative, operative, and immediate postoperative predictors of the onset of low cardiac output syndrome in CHD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low cardiac output syndrome is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality after CHD surgery. Early, transparent risk estimation at paediatric cardiac ICU admission could guide monitoring and resource allocation.
OBJECTIVES: To develop and evaluate a multivariable model that estimates the risk of low cardiac output syndrome using routinely available preoperative, intraoperative, and immediate postoperative variables.
METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective observational cohort, children ≤18 years undergoing CHD surgery between February 2023 and November 2024 were included. Low cardiac output syndrome was defined using prespecified criteria from the Paediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium. Candidate predictors were screened in univariate analyses; independent associations were estimated with multivariable logistic regression and backward elimination.
RESULTS: Among 191 patients, 46 (24%) developed low cardiac output syndrome. Independent predictors were higher surgical complexity ([RACHS-1] ≥ 4; AOR 3.69, 95% confidence intervals 1.38–9.81), preoperative inotrope use (AOR 2.75, 1.02–7.43), longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (AOR 1.01 per minute, 1.00–1.02), and a greater number of prior cardiac operations (AOR 2.00 per operation, 1.34–2.97); higher operative weight was protective (AOR 0.92 per kilogram, 0.87–0.97). Model performance metrics were AUROC 0.88 and AUPRC 0.71; at a prespecified decision threshold, accuracy 0.82, positive predictive value 0.66, sensitivity (recall) 0.50, F1 score 0.57, and negative predictive value 0.85.
CONCLUSIONS: A parsimonious, interpretable model derived from routinely collected data identifies children at increased risk of low cardiac output syndrome at ICU arrival and can inform early intervention and staffing. Prospective multicentre validation and dynamic updating with continuous postoperative physiology are warranted.

Title: Long-term ozone exposure and adverse outcomes in atrial fibrillation: the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remain at high risk of cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events, but evidence on long-term ozone (O3) exposure in this population is limited.
OBJECTIVES: We examined whether long-term O3 exposure was associated with adverse cerebrovascular and cardiovascular outcomes.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed the population-based ARS-PARTICLES cohort of 20757 adults with prevalent AF residing in Podlaskie Voivodeship, northeastern Poland, in 2014, with follow-up through December 31, 2019. O3, nitrogen dioxide and fine particulate matter concentrations were estimated using the GEM-AQ model and assigned by residential municipality. The primary endpoint was a composite of ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke-related death; cardiovascular mortality was the key secondary endpoint. Associations were estimated using Fine-Gray competing-risk models with annually updated previous-year O3 exposure, adjusted for clinical characteristics, meteorology, area-level socioeconomic status, co-pollutants and outdoor artificial light at night.
RESULTS: The mean (SD) age was 72.6 (11.5) years, and 52.9% were women. The median follow-up was 5.6 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-6), during which 3,139 primary composite events and 5,400 cardiovascular deaths occurred. The median annual O₃ concentration was 43.48 μg/m³ (IQR, 42.6-46.63). Each IQR increase in annually updated O₃ exposure (4.03 μg/m³) was associated with higher risks of the primary composite endpoint (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.27; 95% CI, 1.02-1.59), cardiovascular mortality (sHR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01-1.29), and ischemic stroke (sHR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.08-1.77). Associations were directionally consistent across adjustment strategies and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term O3 exposure was associated with higher cerebrovascular and cardiovascular risks in patients with AF. O3 may contribute to residual risk in this clinically vulnerable population and warrants evaluation in other high-risk cardiovascular cohorts.

Title: Diagnostic Impact of Intracranial Vessel Wall MRI on Ischemic Stroke Etiology in Young Adults.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial vessel wall imaging (VWI) enables visualization of arterial wall pathology and may improve etiologic classification of ischemic stroke, but existing evidence is largely based on retrospective studies. We aimed to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic impact of VWI in young stroke patients.
METHODS: In this two-centre study, consecutive patients aged 18-59 years with acute ischemic stroke in the middle cerebral or anterior choroidal artery territory underwent contrast-enhanced VWI within 2 weeks of stroke onset. Stroke etiology was assessed using the Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) and the Causative Classification of Stroke (CCS) classifications before and after incorporating VWI findings. Changes in etiologic classification and predictors of diagnostic change were analyzed.
RESULTS: Sixty-nine patients were included (median age 53 years, 72% male). Incorporation of VWI findings resulted in a change in etiologic classification in 9/69 (13%) patients according to TOAST and 10/69 (14%) according to CCS. For TOAST classification, the proportion of large artery atherosclerosis increased from 17% to 28%, while cryptogenic stroke decreased from 22% to 14%. Baseline cryptogenic stroke was associated with etiologic reclassification after adjustment for age and sex (OR 7.8, 95% CI: 1.2-49.7; p = 0.029).
CONCLUSIONS: VWI frequently identified intracranial atherosclerotic plaques not evident on luminal imaging, leading to etiologic reclassification predominantly toward large artery atherosclerosis. These findings suggest incremental diagnostic value in the etiologic assessment of young stroke, particularly in cryptogenic cases. Larger prospective studies are warranted to determine its role in routine diagnostic algorithms.

Title: Clinical Risk Factors for Advanced Fibrosis in Pathology-Proven Steatotic Liver Disease: Emphasis on Nonelder Subjects.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) may lead to advanced liver diseases. We aimed to identify clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis in pathology-proven SLD patients in a hepatitis B virus (HBV) endemic population, with emphasis on nonelder subjects.
METHODS: Adult SLD patients diagnosed via pathology at National Taiwan University Hospital between June 2009 and December 2023 were recruited. Advanced fibrosis was defined as F2 to F4 fibrosis. Patients were stratified by age (< 50 years defined as nonelder), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and HBV infection. Clinical risk factors for advanced fibrosis and at-risk steatohepatitis were investigated, and the predictive performance of noninvasive scores was examined.
RESULTS: Among 223 pathology-proven SLD patients, older age (odds ratio [OR]: 1.04), alcohol consumption (OR: 5.77), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (OR: 2.13), chronic HBV infection (OR: 2.52), and obesity (OR: 2.64) were independent risk factors for advanced fibrosis. In the nonelder subgroup, older age (OR: 1.10) and obesity (OR: 3.75) were significant. In the MASLD subgroup, older age (OR: 1.04), hypertension (OR: 2.31), T2DM (OR: 3.07), and chronic HBV infection (OR: 3.59) remained significant. Obesity (OR: 4.14) was a significant risk factor for at-risk steatohepatitis in the nonelder subgroup. NAFLD fibrosis score had the highest AUROC (0.724) for advanced fibrosis in the entire cohort, while FIB-4 performed best in nonelder subjects.
CONCLUSIONS: Older age, alcohol, T2DM, chronic HBV infection, and obesity were associated with advanced fibrosis. Risk factors and noninvasive score performance varied in nonelder subjects.

Title: Prognostic Value of Heart-Type Fatty Acid-Binding Protein in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP) is rapidly released following myocardial injury, but its prognostic significance in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between elevated H-FABP and adverse clinical outcomes in confirmed or suspected ACS.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science and Scopus were searched from inception to 30 August 2026 without date restriction. Studies assessing diagnostic and/or prognostic relevance of circulating H-FABP in adults with confirmed or suspected ACS were eligible. Prognostic outcomes included all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure (HF)-related hospitalisation and recurrent myocardial infarction (MI). Risk of bias was assessed using QUIPS. Crude odds ratios (ORs) from extractable 2 × 2 event data were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation.
RESULTS: Twelve studies were included, with five contributing to meta-analysis. Elevated H-FABP was associated with higher odds of all-cause mortality (OR 5.68; 95% CI 3.98-8.09; I2 = 30%), MACE (OR 4.56; 95% CI 1.97-10.55; I2 = 47%), HF-related hospitalisation (OR 4.29; 95% CI 2.94-6.26; I2 = 0%) and recurrent MI (OR 1.65; 95% CI 1.15-2.37; I2 = 0%). Pooled estimates were unadjusted; seven studies were synthesised narratively.
CONCLUSION: Elevated H-FABP is associated with adverse outcomes in ACS, but current evidence does not establish independent prognostic value. Further prospective studies should determine whether H-FABP adds predictive value beyond established clinical and biochemical risk markers.

Title: EXPRESS: Cerebral Microbleed Burden After Aortic and Cardiac Surgery Is Associated With Extracorporeal Circulation Exposure: Evidence From Young Patients With Heritable Connective Tissue Disorders.
Journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) occur after surgery involving extracorporeal circulation (ECC), though confounding risk factors may obscure this association. Patients with heritable connective tissue diseases (HCTDs) requiring early surgery provide an ideal model to investigate ECC-related CMBs. We aimed to assess CMB prevalence, distribution, and surgical correlates in a genetically confirmed HCTD population.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 111 HCTD patients with brain magnetic resonance. CMBs number and location were correlated with clinical and surgical data, including procedure frequency, type, and, when available, ECC duration.
RESULTS: All 58 patients exposed to surgery under ECC exhibited CMBs, compared to only four surgery-naïve individuals. CMBs showed a predominantly lobar pattern. CMB burden was significantly higher in patients with multiple surgeries and longer ECC duration (P<0.001), whereas valve type and surgical technique showed no associationDiscussion:In our cohort, CMBs were identified in all individuals with ECC exposure. The absence of significant differences in CMB burden across surgical techniques weakens the hypothesis that CMBs originate solely from metallic microemboli. In young, normotensive patients with HCTDs, ECC exposure was uniformly associated with CMBs, with burden increasing with repeated procedures and ECC duration.

Title: Electronic Dementia Assessment Score: Screenings and Receipt of Home and Community-Based Services.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: With population aging, ensuring that people living with dementia receive appropriate assessment and services is critical. The objective of this study was to determine whether electronic dementia assessment is associated with increased receipt of home-based and community-based services (HCBS) among Veterans with heart failure and newly diagnosed dementia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of community-dwelling Veterans with heart failure who received an incident dementia diagnosis between 2010 and 2023. Electronic health record (EHR) data were used to identify completion of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments from 365 days before to 90 days after dementia diagnosis. The primary outcome was receipt of HCBS. Logistic regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, and health care utilization.
RESULTS: Among 46,157 Veterans with heart failure and incident dementia, 4% had documented cognitive, 82% psychiatric, and 41% functional assessments. Overall, 25% received HCBS. IPTW-adjusted odds of receiving HCBS significantly increased with electronic health record documentation of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments.
CONCLUSIONS: Among Veterans with heart failure and newly diagnosed dementia, documentation of cognitive, psychiatric, and functional assessments was associated with greater odds of receiving HCBS. Electronic dementia assessment may support system-level efforts to align dementia care with the goals of aging in place.

Title: Nocturia ≥ 3/Night and 5-Year Fragility Fracture Risk in Older Urology Outpatients.
Abstract:
AIM: To evaluate whether nocturia ≥ 3/night stratifies 5-year fragility-fracture risk in older urology outpatients and to explore its prognostic performance alongside the N-QoL and IPSS.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of urology outpatients aged ≥ 65 years at Hachinohe City Hospital, Japan, between 2015 and 2024. After exclusion of patients with prior fragility fracture, bone metastasis, or pathological fracture, and application of a 3-month landmark, 2290 participants were included. The primary outcome was first non-pathological fragility fracture. Bone metastasis and death were treated as competing events. Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were adjusted for age, sex, hypertension, and diabetes. To complement effect estimates, standardized 5-year cumulative incidence was estimated using model-based standardization.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 48.1 months, 98 fragility fractures occurred; 42 bone metastases and 18 deaths were treated as competing events. Nocturia ≥ 3/night was associated with higher fracture risk than nocturia < 3/night (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.41-3.17). Impaired N-QoL was also associated with higher risk (sHR 1.92, 95% CI 1.12-3.30), whereas severe IPSS showed a weaker association (sHR 1.79, 95% CI 1.00-3.22). The standardized 5-year fracture risk was 9.8% for nocturia ≥ 3/night and 4.8% for nocturia < 3/night, corresponding to an absolute difference of 5.0 percentage points.
CONCLUSIONS: Nocturia ≥ 3/night was associated with higher 5-year fragility-fracture risk and may prompt consideration of falls and bone-health assessment in older urology outpatients.

Title: Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers and the Risk of Alzheimer's Disease Progression: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
Abstract: We investigated the effects of angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) on the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This retrospective cohort study used data from the Korean nationwide claims data to identify patients with AD aged 60-79 years in 2010. ARB users and nonusers were 1:1 propensity score matched. Cox proportional hazards regression evaluated AD progression, defined as memantine initiation and mortality. Active-comparator and dose-response analyses were conducted. ARB use was associated with lower risks of memantine initiation (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.70-0.89) and mortality (HR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.76-0.89). Cumulative exposure analyses showed stronger associations in the highest exposure categories, including 2-3 years of ARB use and ≥ 2 DDD-years, whereas associations in the lower exposure categories were not statistically significant. In active-comparator analyses, ARBs were associated with lower mortality risk than ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers, but not with dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (CCBs). ARB use may be a reasonable antihypertensive choice in patients with AD, although the comparable outcomes between ARBs and CCBs suggest that these associations may not be unique to ARBs and may instead reflect shared blood pressure-lowering and vascular effects. Further prospective research is warranted to optimize antihypertensive selection in patients with AD.

Title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).
RESULTS: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

Title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care.
METHODS: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1. Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants' effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case-control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed.
RESULTS: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case-control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants.
CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

Title: Interrelationships Between Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Domains, Age, and Sex for Patients With Heart Failure: Findings From the CHAMP-HF and CORC Registries.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) domains independently quantify patients' symptoms, physical and social functioning, and quality of life, the interrelationships between domains (eg, symptoms impacting physical limitations) have not been described, nor whether these vary by age or sex.
METHODS: Cross-sectional data from adult outpatients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction from 2 multicenter US registries, the Change the Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (2015-2017) and Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (2001-2002), were used to fit recursive path analysis models relating age, sex, and KCCQ domain scores. The interrelationships of these factors were quantified using unstandardized and standardized effect estimates. Unstandardized effects denote the linear effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable in units specific to both variables. Standardized effects are unitless and are obtained by multiplying the unstandardized effect by the ratio of the standard deviations of the dependent and independent variables.
RESULTS: The analytic cohorts included 4839 patients from the Change the Management of Patients With Heart Failure Registry (mean age, 66.1±12.5 years, 29.3% women) and 547 patients from the Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Consortium (mean age, 66±12 years, 23.8% women). Standardized effect estimates revealed moderate to strong interrelationships among the KCCQ domains (effect size range, 0.34-0.70). Symptoms were strongly associated with all other domains (range, 0.61-0.70). Quality of life was most associated with symptoms and social limitations (range: 0.48-0.60), and less so with physical limitations (effect size=0.34). By comparison, the associations of age and sex with KCCQ domains were much smaller (effect sizes <0.2), and no interactions by age and sex were found.
CONCLUSIONS: KCCQ domains were strongly interrelated, and these relationships did not differ appreciably by age or sex. These data enhance the interpretation of KCCQ domain scores in research and clinical practice; in particular, symptoms and social limitations may be key drivers of impaired quality of life in heart failure. Targeted interventions prioritizing these domains may most effectively improve patients' overall health status.

Title: Dietary strategies to combat arterial stiffness in cardiometabolic disease: a network meta-analysis.
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and hypertension (HTN) are leading causes of global morbidity and mortality. Arterial stiffness, assessed via augmentation index (AIx) and pulse wave velocity (PWV), serves as an independent prognostic marker of vascular damage; however, the comparative efficacy of dietary interventions on these parameters remains poorly characterized. This network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to compare and rank the efficacy of dietary interventions, including supplements, nutraceuticals, and dietary patterns, on AIx and PWV in individuals with CVD or HTN. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to January 2025. Two independent reviewers screened and extracted data following PRISMA-NMA guidelines. A total of 48 RCTs comprising 2719 participants and 31 dietary interventions were included. Study quality and certainty of evidence (CoE) were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and GRADE approach, respectively. A random-effects NMA within a frequentist framework estimated mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For PWV, grape seed extract (MD: -1.70; 95%CI: -3.36 to -0.04; CoE: Moderate) and vitamin B9 (MD: -1.46; 95%CI: -2.61 to -0.31; CoE: Moderate) reduced arterial stiffness versus placebo. No intervention reached significance for AIx, though alpha-linolenic acid, dietary nitrate, and wine extract showed the greatest numerical improvements. Sensitivity analyses yielded results consistent with the primary analyses, with no publication bias detected. The grape seed extract and folic acid show potential to reduce arterial stiffness. Future population-specific, dose-optimized RCTs are warranted to establish definitive therapeutic recommendations.

Title: Cerebral Ventriculomegaly With Abnormality of the Aqueduct of Sylvius: A Case Series.
Abstract: Fetal cerebral ventriculomegalies are brain anomalies with potentially poor neurodevelopmental prognosis. They are amenable to prenatal imaging, isolated or associated with other cerebral and/or extra-cerebral abnormalities. Most are obstructive due to a focal or diffuse dysgenesis of the ventricular system, disturbing the cerebro-spinal fluid outflow. Triventricular dilatation is the most common, predicting a lesion at the level of the aqueduct of Sylvius (AS). Although variants in several genes have recently been linked to ventriculomegaly, their role remains unclear, compromising our ability to predict the impact of such variations when detected prenatally. To go further, we report here a monocentric cohort of 51 fetuses with cerebral ventriculomegaly linked to dysgenetic AS and discuss phenotype/genotype correlations after neuropathological study. A genetic cause has been identified in 15 cases (29.4%) using different genetic methods available between 1992 and 2021: standard karyotyping, targeted mutation screening (Sanger sequencing), and Next Generation Sequencing. Dysgeneses of the AS are still controversial in their nosology and etiology; most are discussed on the basis of brain imaging findings alone. In this series, complete fetal and neuropathological examination allowed detection of key clinical and histopathological clues, allowing the orientation of molecular screenings and the identification of cellular mechanisms involved in triventricular dilatations.

Title: Frequency and Clinical Correlates of Sarcopenia in Patients With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
Abstract: Introduction Sarcopenia may occur in people with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease; however, the condition's frequency and correlation with liver fibrosis vary by group. Patients with reduced muscle mass and strength may also have a higher metabolic burden and more severe liver involvement. Because these relationships remain inconsistent across available studies, this study aimed to estimate the prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and examine its association with clinical findings, metabolic profile, body composition, and liver-related features. Methods A total of 276 people suffering from MASLD were recruited consecutively from a tertiary care hospital for this cross-sectional study. Sarcopenia was diagnosed when low appendicular skeletal muscle mass was present together with either low handgrip strength or reduced physical performance. Severe sarcopenia was defined by the presence of low muscle mass, low muscle strength, and reduced physical performance. Liver steatosis was assessed using the Control Attenuation Parameter (CAP), and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was utilized to evaluate fibrosis. The differences between patients with and without sarcopenia were assessed. A binary logistic regression was employed, taking into account relevant clinical parameters, to ascertain if sarcopenia and fibrosis were significantly correlated. Results Among 276 patients, the prevalence of sarcopenia was 23.2% (64/276; 95% confidence interval (CI), 18.6-28.5%). Sarcopenia patients were older (54.9 ± 10.6 vs. 48.1 ± 11.1 years; p < 0.001), more likely to have diabetes mellitus (56.2% vs. 32.5%; p < 0.001) and hypertension (57.8% vs. 35.8%; p = 0.002), and less likely to be physically active (21.9% vs. 53.3%; p < 0.001). Sarcopenia patients exhibited greater median LSM (8.4 (6.0-10.6) vs. 6.6 (5.3-8.1) kPa; p < 0.001) and CAP (311.7 ± 28.7 vs. 297.8 ± 34.1 dB/m; p = 0.001). Significant fibrosis was present in 51.6% of patients with sarcopenia compared to 26.4% of patients without sarcopenia (p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, and diabetes, sarcopenia remained statistically associated with significant fibrosis (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 2.03, 95% CI 1.10-3.77; p = 0.024). Conclusion Sarcopenia remained statistically associated with significant fibrosis after adjustment for relevant clinical factors; however, further prospective studies are needed to determine whether assessment of muscle status has clinical utility in patients with MASLD.

Title: Prescribing Trends of Osteoporosis Medications, Adherence and Persistence with Denosumab versus Alendronate: A Real-World Retrospective Study in China.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Osteoporosis, a common metabolic bone disease with high fracture risk and heavy global burden, requires long-term medication adherence and persistence for fracture prevention, yet both remain suboptimal. Prescribing trends, adherence, and persistence data for denosumab and alendronate remain limited, especially in Chinese populations.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used hospital data. Patients aged ≥50 who newly initiated denosumab or alendronate in 2023-2025 were screened; 2025 initiators were excluded for insufficient 1-year follow-up. New users had no prior prescription of either drug since 2009. The proportion of days covered (PDC) was assessed, with good adherence defined as ≥80%. Persistence was time from initiation to discontinuation, with >60-day gap after coverage end defining discontinuation for both drugs. Propensity score matching (PSM) balanced baseline characteristics. Multivariable logistic regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis compared adherence and persistence.
RESULTS: A shift in prescribing from oral to injectable formulations, with alendronate decreasing by 44% and denosumab increasing by 94% in 2023-2025. Denosumab demonstrated greater persistence and adherence than alendronate. The 1-year persistence rate was 46.28% (95% CI: 41.88%-50.80%) for denosumab vs 2.89% (95% CI: 1.60%-4.79%) for alendronate, with a 90.80% lower risk [HR: 0.092 (95% CI: 0.077-0.110), p < 0.001]. PDC was 0.530 (IQR: 0.493-0.975), adherence rate 46.90% (227/484) for denosumab vs 0.077 (IQR: 0.077-0.153), 2.48% (12/484) for alendronate; adherence was 41.29-fold higher with denosumab (95% CI: 22.41-76.07, p < 0.001). Multivariate analysis showed hypertension and fracture history with better adherence and persistence; inpatient status was associated with poorer persistence and adherence; and female sex with poorer persistence (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: A shift from oral to injectable formulations was observed. Denosumab was associated with higher persistence and adherence than alendronate. Hypertension and fracture history were associated with better persistence and adherence, whereas inpatient status was associated with poorer persistence and adherence. Female sex was associated with poorer persistence without affecting adherence.

Title: Multi-Omics Prioritization and Clinical Evaluation of CYP4V2 as a Candidate Biomarker in Venous Thromboembolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has a substantial genetic component, but the effector genes and clinically relevant biomarkers remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: We analyzed FinnGen R12 genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for VTE and its subphenotypes. The Mixture model for estimating polygenicity and discoverability (MiXeR) was used to characterize the shared genetic architecture between deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. Cross-tissue Unified Test for Molecular SignaTures (UTMOST) and single-tissue Functional Summary-based Imputation (FUSION) transcriptome-wide association analyses were integrated with Multi-marker Analysis of GenoMic Annotation (MAGMA) gene and pathway analyses to prioritize candidate genes. FUSION conditional and joint analysis was applied to evaluate locus-level independence. Single-variant cis-expression quantitative trait locus (cis-eQTL)-based Mendelian randomization (MR) with Steiger directionality testing was performed for CYP4V2. External validation included GSE48000 whole-blood expression analysis, Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT) immune deconvolution, and serum CYP4V2 measurement by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in an independent clinical cohort.
RESULTS: MiXeR indicated extensive shared polygenicity between deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. Across UTMOST, FUSION, and MAGMA, CYP4V2 emerged as the only consensus candidate gene for VTE and its subphenotypes. FUSION conditional analysis supported locus-level prioritization. Single-variant cis-eQTL-based MR showed directionally consistent associations between genetically proxied higher CYP4V2 expression and lower risks of VTE, deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. However, regional colocalization did not support a shared CYP4V2 expression-outcome causal variant. In GSE48000, CYP4V2 expression differed between controls and study-defined recurrence-risk phenotypes and was associated with myeloid-cell composition. Serum CYP4V2 levels were lower in patients with VTE than in non-VTE controls.
CONCLUSION: Integrated gene-prioritization analyses and preliminary transcriptomic and serum-protein associations nominate CYP4V2 for further evaluation as a VTE-associated candidate biomarker. Colocalization does not establish expression-mediated causality. Larger prospective studies and functional validation are required to determine its biological relevance and clinical utility.

Title: Sleep Disturbances in Chronic Kidney Disease - The CKD-REIN Cohort Study.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Insomnia and excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) are common in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their determinants are poorly understood. We analyzed multiple factors likely to affect sleep with the aim of disentangling the contributions of CKD markers and symptoms from those of social factors, lifestyle, comorbid conditions, and drug-induced effects, with the latter 2 highly prevalent in this population.
STUDY DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: In total, 2,765 patients with CKD stages 2-5 not receiving dialysis (mean age, 67 ± 13 years; 66% men) from a representative sample of 40 nephrology clinics in France.
EXPOSURES: Albuminuria, estimated glomerular filtration rate, CKD symptoms, lifestyle, comorbid conditions, and medications collected annually.
OUTCOMES: Insomnia and EDS ≥ 3 times/week in the past 3 months assessed with a standardized questionnaire at baseline, 1-, 3-, and 5-year follow-ups, providing 7,264 observations overall.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Adjusted odds ratios of insomnia and EDS associated with time-updated exposures estimated with mixed effects logistic regressions.
RESULTS: Baseline prevalence of reported insomnia was 22% (95% confidence interval, 21%-24%) and that of EDS, 15% (14%-16%). Based on the 7,264 observations, neither prevalence was associated with albuminuria after adjustment for age and gender. The odds ratio of EDS alone increased significantly with decreasing estimated glomerular filtration rate, 1.16 (1.05-1.28 mL/min/1.73 m2) per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2, independent of social factors, physical activity, obesity, heart failure, and long half-life benzodiazepine use. It was no longer significant after adjustment for fatigue, which displayed a strong dose-effect relation with EDS, depression, insomnia, and sleep apnea. Insomnia prevalence increased strongly with severity of cramps, itching, and stress, independent of other determinants including female gender, heart failure, thyroid hormone use, depression, and sleep apnea.
LIMITATIONS: Self-reported sleep disturbances and limited longitudinal inference.
CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the multifactorial nature of sleep disturbances in CKD and the potentially modifiable contribution of CKD symptoms and drug-induced effects.

Title: Optimization of Anticoagulation Strategy During Cardiopulmonary Bypass in Neonates with Congenital Heart Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Neonatal hemostatic immaturity complicates anticoagulation during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Current practice largely follows the strategy of 400 U/kg from adult protocols, as neonatal-specific guidelines and high-quality evidence remain lacking, which frequently fails to achieve adequate anticoagulation. This single-center randomized controlled trial evaluated the initial heparin dose of 600 U/kg to refine neonatal CPB anticoagulation.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, controlled, single-blind trial, 76 neonates undergoing CPB were assigned to receive an initial heparin dose of either 600 U/kg (n = 38) or 400 U/kg (n = 38). The primary endpoint was the pre- to post-CPB change in prothrombin fragment 1+2 (ΔF1+2). Secondary endpoints included the proportion of neonates achieving the ACT threshold after the initial heparin bolus, perioperative coagulation measures, postoperative blood loss, transfusion requirements, and adverse clinical outcomes.
RESULTS: Mean ΔF1+2 was 0.70 vs 4.08 nmol/L in the 600 and 400 U/kg groups, respectively (treatment-minus-control mean difference, -3.38 nmol/L; 95% confidence interval, -4.58 to -2.18; P <0.001). ACT target achievement rate after the initial dose was higher in the 600 U/kg group (84.2% vs 44.7%, P < 0.001). Surgical preparation time was shorter (median 31.50 vs 36.50 mins, P = 0.028), and supplemental heparin use was lower, while total heparin dose did not differ significantly. Secondary endpoints showed lower 72-hour chest drainage and albumin use and shorter mechanical ventilation duration (P = 0.036, 0.028, and 0.031, respectively). Red-cell, plasma, and platelet transfusion requirements and most other clinical outcomes did not differ significantly. One in-hospital death occurred with 600 U/kg and none with 400 U/kg. Complete-case sensitivity analysis supported the primary finding.
CONCLUSION: An initial heparin dose of 600 U/kg in neonatal CPB was associated with a smaller F1+2 increase and greater initial ACT response. Larger studies are needed to establish clinical benefit and safety.
