CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NUMBER: ChiCTR2300069157.

Title: Hand-in-Hand-improving occupational health and quality of care in early education and care: study protocol for a cluster-randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In Norway, the early education and care (ECEC) sector has the highest rate of work-related fatigue and sickness absence across all sectors. Work in ECEC can be characterized as physically and emotionally demanding, which may lead to fatigue and the two most common causes of sickness absence in the ECEC sector, i.e., musculoskeletal and mental health issues. Improvements to the work environment can lead to better health for ECEC employees and improve ECEC quality. Therefore, work environment, employee health, and ECEC quality go Hand-in-Hand. This paper presents the protocol for conducting a trial to evaluate the effectiveness and implementation of the tailored participatory Hand-in-Hand workplace intervention.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The study is a 1-year pragmatic cluster-randomized controlled trial with a wait-listed control group. Nineteen ECEC centers were recruited from two Norwegian municipalities, with an estimated 350 employees. The intervention is facilitated by external consultants and includes one workshop and two workplace visits. This includes training the employees in the Hand-in-Hand toolbox, a systematic method for developing workplace measures. Data collection will consist of accelerometer and heart rate measurements, questionnaires, diaries, interviews and registry data; baseline measurements were conducted in October/November 2025. The primary outcome of the effect evaluation will be work-related fatigue. The effectiveness of the intervention will be analyzed using multilevel analyses. In addition, a process evaluation will assess intervention implementation to help understand why the intervention is effective (or not), and for whom and under which circumstances.
DISCUSSION: The intervention adopts an interdisciplinary approach, integrating emotion work, sensor-based measurements of physical workload, and quality in early childhood education and care. The study aims to provide theoretical, methodological, and practical insights into how to design and implement a complex intervention in an ECEC setting.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN81684777, identifier: ISRCTN81684777.

Title: Unraveling the Genotype-Phenotype Landscape of Kleefstra Syndrome Through EHMT1 Variant Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Kleefstra syndrome type 1 (KLEFS1) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in EHMT1, which play a key role in epigenetic regulation. Core features include global developmental delay (GDD), intellectual disability (ID), facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects (CHDs), and neuropsychiatric manifestations.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with KLEFS1 evaluated at Seoul National University Hospital between January 2022 and April 2025. Genetic diagnoses were made using chromosomal microarray or whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing, and clinical data were extracted from medical records. To enhance statistical power, we conducted a joint analysis with established cohorts of at least 30 clinically characterized patients.
RESULTS: Among the 15 patients with KLEFS1, 14 (93.3%) exhibited GDD or ID, with frequent comorbidities such as CHDs (8/12, 66.7%), orthopaedic manifestations (6/12, 50.0%), epilepsy (6/15, 40.0%), and sleep problems (4/11, 36.4%). Brain MRI revealed abnormalities in 10 of the 12 patients (83.3%), including pituitary anomalies in 2 (16.7%). By combining our data with recently published multicenter international cohorts, we assessed genotype-phenotype correlations by comparing the clinical features of 202 patients with different variant subtypes. Patients with multigene deletions had a significantly higher prevalence of CHDs (53.5% vs 25.8%, p value = 2 × 10-4), cortical visual impairment (12.5% vs 1.7%, p value = 0.004), microcephaly (37.1% vs 17.8%, p value = 0.009), corpus callosum abnormalities (17.9% vs 5.9%, p value = 0.02), and hearing impairment (39.7% vs 25.6%, p value = 0.04) than those with single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) or short insertions/deletions (indels), in addition to the previously identified features including epilepsy, constipation, and short stature. We also observed that a recurrent EHMT1 variant (p.Arg948Trp), identified in multiple unrelated patients, was linked to significant phenotypic heterogeneity, including late-onset neurocognitive regression.
DISCUSSION: Our study showed that patients with multigene deletions are significantly more likely to exhibit multiorgan involvement, including CHDs, cortical visual impairments, microcephaly, corpus callosum abnormalities, and hearing impairments, compared with those with SNVs or indels, emphasizing the importance of genotype-informed management. We report pituitary gland abnormalities in KLEFS1, expanding the phenotypic and neuroimaging spectrum of KLEFS1. The patient showing regression in their 30s necessitates long-term, comprehensive studies to support care.

Title: Low end-tidal carbon dioxide identifies high-severity pulmonary embolism and shock-level haemodynamics.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: End-tidal carbon dioxide tension (P ETCO2 ) may be reduced when lung units are ventilated but under-perfused, as occurs in pulmonary embolism (PE). We sought to determine whether early P ETCO2 measurement reflects PE severity according to European Society of Cardiology (ESC) risk categories and identifies shock-level haemodynamics among patients undergoing catheter-directed therapy (CDT).
METHODS: Patients admitted with acute PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography were enrolled in this prospective observational study. P ETCO2 was measured using nasal capnography within 24 h of presentation or immediately prior to urgent CDT. P ETCO2 was compared between lower and higher severity PE groups and between patients referred for CDT or not. In patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (CDT) with invasive haemodynamic assessment, pulmonary arterial pressures and cardiac indices were recorded. A subgroup analysis evaluated patients with cardiogenic shock defined as cardiac index ≤1.8 L·min-1·m-2.
RESULTS: 62 patients were analysed. P ETCO2 was significantly lower in the combined higher risk group compared to the combined lower risk group (mean 21.7 (95% CI 20.2-23.3) versus 30.2 (95% CI 27.8-32.6) mmHg; p<0.001). P ETCO2 was also lower in patients referred for CDT compared to those not referred (mean 20.4 (95% CI 18.7-22.0) versus 28.2 (95% CI 26.2-30.1) mmHg; p<0.001). Among patients who underwent CDT and met haemodynamic criteria for cardiogenic shock (n=16), P ETCO2 was the lowest (mean 18.6 (95% CI 16.1-21.1) mmHg).
CONCLUSIONS: P ETCO2 can be rapidly obtained early in PE evaluation and reflects ESC-defined severity. A P ETCO2 level <20 mmHg was associated with shock-level haemodynamics among normotensive intermediate-high-risk patients undergoing CDT. P ETCO2 may serve as a non-invasive marker of physiological severity.

Title: Diffusion tensor MR neurography reveals altered sciatic and tibial nerve microstructure in chronic dialysis patients.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Uremic polyneuropathy is a complication of chronic kidney disease, presenting as a distal symmetric neuropathy mainly attributed to axonal damage. Electrophysiology provides limited insight into microstructural nerve alterations. Magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) may enable assessment of peripheral nerve integrity. This study aimed to quantify sciatic and tibial nerve microstructural changes in chronic dialysis patients and evaluate their clinical relevance.
METHODS: Thirty patients on chronic dialysis (DP)-without prediabetes or diabetes-and 30 healthy controls (HCs) underwent MRN, including diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). All MRN datasets of the distal thigh (30/30) were suitable for analysis. Four lower-leg examinations in the patient cohort (26/30) and three in the healthy group (27/30) were excluded because of motion artifacts. Fractional anisotropy (FA) was defined as the primary imaging outcome, while axial diffusivity (AD) and radial diffusivity (RD) were analyzed as secondary metrics. Electrophysiological testing was not available in four patients in the dialysis cohort (26/30). Results were compared between groups and correlated with electrophysiological, clinical, and laboratory findings.
RESULTS: FA of the sciatic (DP 0.44, HC 0.48, P < .001) and tibial nerve (DP 0.38, HC 0.43, P < .0001) and AD were significantly reduced in dialysis patients, while RD did not differ between groups. Lower FA correlated with electrophysiological measures, neuropathy scores, and was independently associated with group after adjustment for age, BMI, and sex. Subgroup analyses showed lower FA in patients fulfilling electrophysiological criteria for uremic polyneuropathy but no difference according to dialysis modality.
DISCUSSION: The reduction in FA and AD, together with electrophysiological and clinical correlations, is compatible with a predominantly axonal pattern of peripheral nerve involvement in chronic dialysis patients. DTI detected peripheral nerve microstructural alterations associated with chronic dialysis. These findings support further longitudinal and disease control studies to determine the clinical utility of DTI as an imaging biomarker in chronic dialysis patients.

Title: Minimally Invasive Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Predominantly Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: Early Perioperative Outcomes of 149 Patients.
Abstract: Background Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG) has evolved from single-vessel revascularization to multivessel surgery without median sternotomy. Although favorable outcomes have been reported, experience remains concentrated in specialized centers. This study evaluated the demographic, operative, and early postoperative characteristics of patients undergoing MICS-CABG, off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OP-CABG) at a single institution. Methods This retrospective observational study included 149 CABG/OPCAB procedures identified from an institutional database of 186 cardiac surgical records. Demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, operative details, number of grafts, cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and cross-clamp times, postoperative ventilation, chest drainage, transfusion requirements, and documented complications were analyzed. Continuous variables were summarized as mean ± standard deviation and median with interquartile range (IQR), and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. Missing data were not imputed. Results The mean age was 57.8 ± 9.5 years; 139 (93.3%) patients were men. Diabetes mellitus was present in 86 patients (57.7%), hypertension in 100 (67.1%), and tobacco exposure in 65 (43.6%). Procedures included eight one-graft, 41 two-graft, 86 three-graft, and 13 four-graft operations; one procedure lacked standardized graft documentation. Overall, 140/149 (94.0%) procedures had two or more explicitly coded grafts. CPB data were available for 137 patients, with a mean duration of 170.2 ± 37.4 minutes and a median of 168 minutes (IQR: 148-190). Mean cross-clamp time was 94.6 ± 30.5 minutes. Ventilation data were available for 146 patients, with a mean duration of 7.6 ± 4.4 hours and a median of six hours (IQR: 4-11). Chest drainage was documented in 134 patients, with a mean of 899 ± 510 mL. Early postoperative outcomes included conversion to sternotomy in nine patients (6.0%), return to the operating room for bleeding in nine (6.0%), stroke in 3 (2.0%), respiratory insufficiency in two (1.3%), new-onset atrial fibrillation in 36 (24.2%), and 30-day or in-hospital mortality in three (2.0%). Outcome-specific denominators were based on the number of patients for whom the corresponding variable was available. Conclusion This institutional experience demonstrates the feasibility of minimally invasive coronary surgery for predominantly multivessel revascularization. Most procedures involved two or more grafts, with three-graft surgery being the most common. Postoperative ventilation was generally short; however, incomplete complication and transfusion documentation limits interpretation of other perioperative outcomes. Prospective standardized data collection and comparative studies with conventional CABG are warranted.

Title: Blood Donor Deferral Patterns at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Central India: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract: Background and aim Blood donor deferral is an essential safeguard for donors and recipients, but it also reduces the immediately available donor pool. Because deferral patterns reflect local demographics, health conditions, and screening practices, center-level data are important for donor recruitment and retention planning. The aim of this study was to evaluate the frequency, pattern, and causes of blood donor deferral among prospective donation presentations at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Central India. Methods A retrospective, record-based cross-sectional study was conducted at the Blood Centre of Dr. Laxminarayan Pandey Government Medical College, Ratlam. A recorded donation presentation was defined as an age-eligible prospective donor entered after initial age screening into either the Main Register following successful donation or the Deferral Register following pre-donation deferral. Individuals outside the center's routine age criterion of 18-60 years were screened at the initial counter and were not entered into either register. All 11,354 recorded donation presentations between March 2024 and March 2026 were included. Hemoglobin was screened using the copper sulfate specific-gravity method, with a minimum eligibility threshold of 12.5 g/dL for both male and female donors; the same screening procedure was used in in-house and blood donation camp sessions. Deferral reasons were standardized into predefined categories and classified as temporary or permanent; where more than one reason was documented, all recorded reasons were retained in the reason-specific analysis. Associations of sex, age group, and study period with deferral were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Results Of 11,354 recorded donation presentations, 216 (1.9%; 95% CI, 1.7-2.2%) resulted in deferral. There were 10,219 male presentations (90.0%) and 1,135 female presentations (10.0%). Deferral rates did not differ significantly between male (188/10,219, 1.8%) and female (28/1,135, 2.5%) presentations (p = 0.142). Most deferrals were temporary (193/216, 89.4%), while 23/216 (10.6%) were permanent. Self-reported alcohol intake within the preceding 72 hours (37/193, 19.2%) and low hemoglobin (27/193, 14.0%) were the leading temporary causes, while cardiovascular disease was the most frequent permanent cause (7/23). Deferral rates were 73/3,143 (2.3%) in March-December 2024, 70/6,233 (1.1%) in January-December 2025, and 73/1,978 (3.7%) in January-March 2026 (χ²(2) = 57.15, p < 0.001). Conclusions Among recorded donor presentations after initial age screening, 216/11,354 (1.9%) resulted in deferral, and most deferrals were temporary. Recent alcohol intake and low hemoglobin were the most frequent temporary causes and represent practical targets for pre-donation guidance, appropriate clinical evaluation when indicated, and structured reentry of temporarily deferred donors.

Title: Position Statement by the Saudi Heart Failure Working Group of the Saudi Heart Association on the Management of Advanced Heart Failure in Saudi Arabia.
Journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Saudi Arabia. Despite remarkable progress in guideline-directed medical therapy, a significant proportion of patients progress to advanced HF and require evaluation for heart transplantation or mechanical circulatory support (MCS). In response to this growing burden, the Saudi Heart Association (SHA) developed recommendations to guide identification, timely referral, and optimal management of candidates for advanced HF therapies in Saudi Arabia.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel of 10 HF experts from Saudi Arabia convened for a series of structured virtual meetings to review local and international evidence. The panel integrated Saudi-specific clinical practice patterns and healthcare considerations into the deliberation process. Consensus was achieved through discussion and majority agreement. Recommendations were formulated using the SHA methodology, supported by a comprehensive literature review of published evidence.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The SHA consensus establishes a structured, comprehensive framework for recognizing advanced HF, optimizing guideline-directed therapy, and determining candidacy for heart transplantation or MCS in tertiary and quaternary centers in Saudi Arabia. The document emphasizes timely prognostic stratification using clinical indicators and standardized tools such as INTERMACS and SCAI classifications. Referral pathways and multidisciplinary coordination are delineated to facilitate efficient evaluation and timely intervention. These recommendations aim to minimize delays in referral, expand access to advanced HF therapies and improve patient outcomes across Saudi Arabia.

Title: Warfarin for Left Ventricular Thrombus in Nonischemic Cardiomyopathy With Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report and Literature Review of Anticoagulation Strategies in Renal Impairment.
Abstract: Left ventricular (LV) thrombus is a serious complication of cardiomyopathy with severely reduced ejection fraction, carrying significant risk of systemic embolization. While direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have emerged as a reasonable alternative to warfarin for LV thrombus treatment in the general population, no guideline-directed evidence exists for their use in patients with concomitant acute kidney injury (AKI) or significant renal impairment in this specific clinical context. We present the case of a 47-year-old male with newly diagnosed nonischemic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 25%), LV apical thrombus, and Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO)-defined AKI attributed to type 1 cardiorenal syndrome, who was managed with heparin bridging to warfarin due to the absence of evidence supporting DOAC use for LV thrombus in the setting of renal dysfunction. The requirement for heparin-to-warfarin bridging prolonged the patient's hospitalization by five days, illustrating the tangible clinical and resource burden imposed by the current guideline gap. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is present in approximately 45% of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; roughly two-thirds of heart failure hospitalizations are associated with a discharge estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60 mL/min/1.73 m², and AKI complicates approximately one-third of heart failure admissions, so this clinical scenario is far from rare. We additionally provide a literature review of the current evidence comparing DOACs and vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for LV thrombus, DOAC pharmacokinetics in renal impairment, and the guideline landscape at this clinical intersection. Notably, every randomized trial comparing DOACs with warfarin for LV thrombus to date has explicitly excluded patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment. This case and review underscore the need for prospective studies evaluating DOAC safety and efficacy for LV thrombus in patients with impaired renal function, which could reduce unnecessary hospital days and healthcare costs while maintaining safe anticoagulation.

Title: Need-based Compared to Guidelines-based Fluid Administration in Dengue Patients with Warning Signs: An Open-label Randomized Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fluid therapy is fundamental in dengue management. We evaluated an individualized, hemodynamic parameter-guided fluid strategy compared with standard World Health Organization (WHO) guideline-based care in dengue patients with warning signs.
METHODS: In this open-label randomized controlled trial conducted at a tertiary care hospital in New Delhi (December 2019-October 2023), 80 adult dengue patients with warning signs were randomized (1:1) to receive either WHO guideline-based fluid therapy (control) or need-based therapy guided by noninvasive cardiac output monitoring (NICOM) and point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) (intervention). The primary outcome was hemodynamic stability assessed by systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse pressure (PP), and mean arterial pressure over 48 h. Secondary outcomes included hospital stay, progression to severe dengue, and mortality.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. The intervention arm demonstrated higher mean PP at 8 h (45.2 ± 11.6 mmHg vs. 39.8 ± 8.7 mmHg), 12 h (45 ± 11.3 mmHg vs. 38.9 ± 8.1 mmHg), and 24 h (44.1 ± 9.6 mmHg vs. 39.1 ± 6.6 mmHg) (P < 0.05). SBP was higher at 8 h (P = 0.02). However, progression to severe dengue (17.5% in both groups), hospital stay (5.4 vs. 5.5 days; P = 0.87), and mortality (none) were similar.
CONCLUSION: Although NICOM/POCUS-guided fluid therapy improved selected hemodynamic parameters, it did not translate into measurable improvements in clinical outcomes compared with WHO guideline-based care. Larger, multicenter studies powered for clinical endpoints in high-risk subgroups are warranted.

Title: Pulmonary hypertension optimal screening in interstitial lung disease (PHOS-ILD): a scoring system for the detection of pulmonary hypertension in patients with interstitial lung disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common comorbidity of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Timely detection may improve outcomes through implementation of PH specific treatments.
METHODS: Retrospective, multicenter study aiming to identify features that predict PH in patients with ILD. In the derivation cohort (ILD cohort-University of South Florida), we identified predictors of PH in ILD and created a scoring system using the rounded value of odds ratio for each significant parameter. Correlation with hemodynamic parameters was investigated in the derivation and validation cohort (Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis cohort-Cleveland Clinic).
RESULTS: We included 164 patients with ILD that underwent right heart catheterization (RHC) [derivation cohort: n = 118, median age (years, 95% CI): 69.0 (65.9-71.0), female gender: 65 (54.6%), median mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) (mmHg, 95% CI): 25.0 (23.0-27.0), median pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) [Wood units (WU), 95% CI]: 3.6 (3.0-4.3), validation cohort: n = 46, median age (95% CI): 63.0 (60.0-66.0), female gender: 17 (37%), median mPAP (mmHg, 95% CI): 20.5 (18.0-27.2), median PVR (WU, 95% CI): 3.1 (2.2-3.4)]. Parameters and optimal cut-offs that significantly predicted precapillary PH in the derivation cohort were: age>42 years, heart rate recovery (HRR) at 1 min ≤ 15 bpm in 6-min walk test (6 MWT), 6-min walk distance (6 MWD) ≤ 270 meters, B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) > 136 pg/mL, pulmonary artery to ascending aorta diameter ratio (PA/AA) > 1 in high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), main PA diameter > 29 mm in HRCT, right ventricular systolic pressure > 42 mmHg on echocardiogram. We created a PH detection model that ranged from 0 to 28. The optimal cut-off threshold for the detection of PH was > 14 (80% sensitivity, 68% specificity, AUC: 0.78). A simplified scoring system without BNP and main PA diameter (range: 0-21) maintained the same AUC. The simplified scoring system exhibited positive correlation with mean pulmonary artery pressure both in the derivation (rho = 0.47, p < 0.0001) and validation cohort (rho = 0.36, p = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that incorporation of demographic, functional, imaging, and echocardiographic characteristics can optimize the early identification of precapillary PH in patients with ILD, paving the way to structured screening strategies. Timely detection of PH might lead to timely implementation of emerging PH specific treatments in patients with ILDs.

Title: Correction: Implementation of guideline-recommended organ-protective therapy in people with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or kidney disease: real-world evidence from a German University Hospital.
Abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fendo.2025.1736984.].

Title: 4D-Flow MRI-Derived Wall Shear Stress as a Non-Invasive Biomarker for the Detection and Hemodynamic Characterization of Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract: Invasive right heart catheterization (RHC) remains the reference standard for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), but there is a pressing need for non-invasive techniques to assess pulmonary hemodynamics. This study evaluates 4D-flow MRI-derived wall shear stress (WSS) for PH detection using the updated 2022 hemodynamic criteria, and the prediction of right ventriculo-pulmonary arterial (RV-PA) uncoupling to assess disease severity. 3D WSS was measured in the main (MPA), right (RPA), and left (LPA) pulmonary arteries in a retrospective validation cohort (41 PH patients, 23 non-PH) and then assessed in a prospective test cohort (23 PH patients, 17 healthy controls). For methodological validation, a patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) was performed in a subset of 16 patients from the validation cohort. RV-PA uncoupling was assessed on the cine MRI, using RV global longitudinal strain (GLS) < -15.3% and RVSV/RVESV < 1. Both 3D peak and time-averaged WSS were significantly reduced in PH patients compared with healthy controls. Global WSS metrics demonstrated the strongest correlations with invasive hemodynamic parameters, including mPAP (r = -0.75, p < 0.001) and PVR (r = -0.76, p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis identified a peak WSS cutoff of < 0.30 Pa (AUC 0.98) for PH detection, a threshold achieving 90% sensitivity and 100% specificity in the test cohort. Furthermore, a peak WSS threshold of < 0.18 Pa demonstrated excellent discriminative ability for RV-PA uncoupling. These findings support the potential integration of WSS analysis into routine CMR protocols as a non-invasive complement to RHC, showing promise for both diagnosis and a longitudinal biomarker for monitoring PH.

Title: From validation to public health impact: implementing equitable AI-enabled diabetic retinopathy screening.
Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a preventable cause of vision loss as diabetes prevalence rises worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled retinal screening has progressed from retrospective validation to prospective and real-world deployment, with recent reviews showing high diagnostic performance across fundus photography, smartphone-based systems, and autonomous platforms. Yet diagnostic accuracy alone does not ensure public health benefit. Population impact can be lost when eligible people are not reached, images are ungradable, results are delayed, referrals are incomplete, treatment capacity is insufficient, or disadvantaged groups face financial, geographic, or digital barriers. Unlike reviews centered mainly on diagnostic accuracy or economic performance, this Mini Review reframes AI-enabled DR screening as a population-health intervention spanning detection through completion of effective eye care. We synthesize evidence on diagnostic validity, implementation, economics, referral completion, care cascades, patient-centered outcomes, equity, and governance. We argue that effectiveness and cost-effectiveness are properties of the complete screening-to-treatment pathway, not the algorithm alone, and propose a four-domain framework encompassing technical validity, service integration, population impact, and equity and sustainability. Future research should prioritize comparative implementation studies and outcome sets that capture screening reach, gradability, referral completion, treatment initiation, time to treatment, avoidable vision loss, vision-related quality of life, acceptability, costs, and subgroup equity. The policy question is no longer whether AI can detect DR, but whether health systems can translate automated detection into equitable completion of effective eye care at scale.

Title: A Clinical Study of Retinal Nerve Fibre Layer and Ganglion Cell Layer changes in patients with Migraine at a Tertiary Care Hospital.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess and compare retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness in migraine patients versus controls and to analyze differences between chronic and episodic migraine.
METHODS: A cross-sectional, case-control study was conducted from June 2022 to December 2023. A total of 100 migraine patients (33 chronic, 67 episodic) and 102 controls underwent detailed ocular evaluation using OCT. RNFL and GCL parameters were compared between cases and controls using an independent t-test. Paired t-tests assessed differences between chronic and episodic migraine, as well as between the right and left eyes.
RESULTS: Photophobia (90%) and ocular pain (85%) were the most common symptoms. Migraine patients showed a significant reduction in average (106 µm), superior (129 µm), and nasal (80 µm) RNFL thickness compared to controls. Chronic migraine patients exhibited significant thinning in the temporal (67 µm) and nasal (72 µm) RNFL quadrants and superotemporal (67 µm) and superonasal (70 µm) GCL quadrants in the right eye. Episodic migraine patients had reduced superotemporal GCL thickness (71 µm) in the left eye.
CONCLUSION: The retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness is reduced in chronic and episodic type of migraine patients. Hence, ophthalmologists should consider the potential impact of migraine headaches on the thickness of RNFL and GCL.

Title: Normal-weight obesity and adverse health outcomes in women: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Normal body mass index (BMI) can coexist with excess adiposity, a phenotype termed normal-weight obesity (NWO). Female-specific evidence remains fragmented; we synthesized associations between NWO and female adverse health outcomes.
METHODS: This was a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 28, 2026, for eligible female-specific studies comparing NWO with normal-weight lean/non-obese controls. Odds ratios (OR) and other effect ratios were synthesized separately; continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs). Outcomes reported in ≥3 studies were pooled with random-effects models using Paule-Mandel between-study variance and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs) with an ad hoc correction. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Exposures tool and the Joanna Briggs Institute cross-sectional checklist.
RESULTS: Twenty studies (200,461 women with normal BMI) were included; 17 were cross-sectional. NWO was associated with metabolic syndrome (number of studies [k] = 4; OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.60 to 2.55), abdominal obesity (k = 3; OR 3.62, 95% CI 1.22 to 10.70), higher triglycerides (k = 7; MD 10.99 mg/dL, 95% CI 2.03 to 19.94), total cholesterol (k = 6; MD 6.86 mg/dL, 95% CI 2.60 to 11.11), and total cholesterol-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) ratio (k = 3; MD 0.76, 95% CI 0.11 to 1.42). Associations with fasting glucose, diabetes, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), HDL-C, fasting insulin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance, and blood pressure were uncertain. Hard clinical outcomes were sparse, and two of three longitudinal studies had high risk of bias.
CONCLUSION: Among women with normal BMI, excess adiposity is associated with a less favorable cardiometabolic phenotype, most consistently metabolic syndrome and selected lipid measures. Evidence for diabetes, blood pressure, cardiovascular events, mortality, cancer, and reproductive or functional outcomes remains limited. Standardized NWO definitions and prospective female-specific studies are needed. (PROSPERO: CRD420261408853).

Title: Associations between the Planetary Health Diet in Late Pregnancy and Pregnancy Outcomes in Women with a Raised BMI: Insights from the PEARS Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diet quality in pregnancy is a modifiable factor with important implications for maternal and neonatal outcomes. The Planetary Health Diet (PHD), designed to promote both human health and environmental sustainability, has not been comprehensively evaluated in high-risk obstetric populations.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to examine the PHD in a pregnant cohort with a raised body mass index (BMI) and its associations with pregnancy outcomes, hypothesizing that greater adherence is associated with more favorable pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of data from the pregnancy exercise and nutrition research study with smartphone application support study. Pregnant women (n = 319) with a BMI ≥25 kg/m2 an 11 d ≤39.9 kg/m2 in early pregnancy were included in the analysis, and the cohort was dichotomized into "Low" (≤92.9) and "High" (>92.9) PHD Index (PHDI) groups based on the median score in late pregnancy (∼28 wk gestation). Differences in pregnancy outcomes between the "High" and "Low" groups were explored, with results adjusted for multiple testing.
RESULTS: In adjusted models, a "High" PHDI score was associated with a lower odds of preeclampsia and/or pregnancy-induced hypertension [adjusted odds ratio (OR): 0.21; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.06, 0.68; P = 0.01), and a higher likelihood to initiate breastfeeding postpartum (adjusted OR: 1.84; 95% CI: 1.04, 3.24; P = 0.04). In the adjusted model, those in the "High" PHDI group had a lower risk of delivering an infant born small for gestational age (SGA) (birthweight <10th centile) (OR: 0.31; 95% CI: 0.10, 1.93, P = 0.04).
CONCLUSIONS: : This diet is associated with lower odds of hypertensive outcomes among pregnant women with a raised BMI, while promoting more sustainable food choices. Greater adherence to the PHD is also associated with a lower risk of delivering an infant born SGA and higher breastfeeding initiation rates, highlighting its potential benefits beyond pregnancy.

Title: Association of early neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio trajectories with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SIC) is characterized by potentially reversible myocardial dysfunction accompanied by a profound systemic inflammatory response. However, the prognostic significance of early dynamic changes in the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in patients with SIC remains unclear. This study aimed to identify distinct early NLR trajectories and examine their associations with cardiac recovery and live discharge from the intensive care unit (ICU).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with SIC admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Hebei Cangzhou Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine. NLR values were collected at ICU admission and at 24, 48, and 72 h thereafter. Latent class mixed modeling was used to identify distinct 72-h NLR trajectories. A 72-h landmark design was applied. The primary outcome was live ICU discharge within 28 days, with ICU death treated as a competing event and analyzed using Fine-Gray regression. The secondary outcome was cardiac recovery by days 5-7, defined as a follow-up left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of ≥50% or an absolute increase of ≥10 percentage points from baseline. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery.
RESULTS: A total of 510 patients contributed 2,040 longitudinal NLR measurements. Three distinct trajectories were identified: low-stable (n = 230, 45.1%), high-decreasing (n = 170, 33.3%), and persistent-high (n = 110, 21.6%). The geometric mean NLR changed from 7.85 to 6.16, from 18.47 to 8.01, and from 14.95 to 22.87, respectively, during the first 72 h. Live ICU discharge occurred in 85.7%, 67.1%, and 36.4% of patients in the three groups, respectively. Compared with the low-stable group, the adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios for live ICU discharge were 0.49 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.38-0.63; P < 0.001] for the high-decreasing group and 0.25 (95% CI, 0.17-0.37; P < 0.001) for the persistent-high group. Cardiac recovery occurred in 80.4%, 61.8%, and 42.7% of patients, respectively. The corresponding adjusted odds ratios were 0.48 (95% CI, 0.29-0.79; P = 0.004) and 0.27 (95% CI, 0.14-0.51; P < 0.001). Associations with live ICU discharge were consistent across predefined subgroups. Septic shock showed an exploratory interaction with the association between NLR trajectories and cardiac recovery (P for interaction=0.034). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results.
CONCLUSIONS: Early 72-h NLR trajectories were independently associated with cardiac recovery and live ICU discharge in patients with SIC. A persistent-high trajectory identified patients with the poorest prognosis, whereas a high-decreasing trajectory was associated with intermediate outcomes. Serial assessment of NLR may provide a simple and clinically accessible tool for early risk stratification in SIC, although prospective external validation is warranted.

Title: Cognitive frailty and mortality among patients on the heart transplant waiting list: A prospective cohort study.
Abstract: Frailty is an important prognostic factor in patients with heart failure and in transplant candidates, while cognitive impairment remains an under-recognized component that may further worsen clinical outcomes. This prospective study aimed to determine the prevalence of physical and cognitive frailty among heart transplant candidates and their association with mortality. Physical frailty was assessed using the Fried criteria; cognition was evaluated using the MoCA (cognitive screening) and WASI (general intellectual functioning); and depressive symptoms were measured using the BDI. Cognitive frailty was defined as the presence of ≥3 of 6 criteria in a modified Fried phenotype, which incorporated cognitive impairment as an additional domain. A total of 150 patients listed for heart transplantation within the previous 30 days were included at a tertiary center in Brazil. The study population was predominantly male (70%), with Chagas disease etiology (35%), and a mean age of 49.8 ± 10.4 years. Physical frailty was present in 78.7% of patients, cognitive frailty in 88.7% (MoCA) and 86.7% (WASI), and depressive symptoms in 44%, which were significantly associated with physical frailty (p = 0.021). During 1-year follow-up, 41.3% of patients died and 67.3% underwent transplantation. Physical frailty was associated with an increased risk of early mortality after listing (initial SHR = 5.47; p = 0.023), with significant attenuation of this effect over time (TVC SHR = 0.99; p = 0.008). A similar pattern was observed for cognitive frailty, measured by both MoCA (initial SHR = 1.61; p = 0.011; TVC SHR = 1.00; p = 0.011) and WASI (initial SHR = 1.57; p = 0.012; TVC SHR = 1.00; p = 0.007), indicating a reduction in its impact on mortality risk over time. However, after multivariable adjustment, neither physical nor cognitive frailty remained independently associated with overall mortality. Physical and cognitive frailty were highly prevalent among heart transplant candidates and showed a time-dependent association with early mortality risk. After adjustment for disease severity markers, this association lost significance, suggesting that frailty may, at least in part, reflect the underlying clinical status at the time of listing rather than acting as an independent prognostic factor. These findings also raise questions regarding the adequacy of the Fried phenotype as a frailty assessment tool in this specific population.

Title: Temporal phase coverage and patient cohort size in deep learning-based cardiac cine computed tomography angiography segmentation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Annotating all phases of cine computed tomography angiography (CTA) is burdensome. We evaluated how temporal phase coverage and patient cohort size affect deep learning-based cardiac segmentation.
METHODS: Twelve 3D U-Net models were trained using a 110-patient single-phase CTA dataset or a 20-patient, 20-phase cine CTA dataset. Phase-coverage ablations used one, two, or 20 phases; patient-count ablations were performed within both datasets. One cine patient was used for validation and four independent patients were used for testing. Five cardiac structures were evaluated using Dice and the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95). Phase-wise and patient-level Dice consistency and structure-specific volumetric variability within and between subjects were assessed.
RESULTS: Full cine training produced higher overall Dice (0.89 vs. 0.87) and lower overall HD95 (4.87 vs. 9.78 mm) than the single-phase reference (both p < 0.05). Right ventricular (RV) Dice was higher (0.91 vs. 0.84) and HD95 was lower (5.16 vs. 22.75 mm; both p < 0.05). The two-phase model achieved an overall Dice of 0.88 and an overall HD95 of 7.85 mm; neither metric differed significantly from the single-phase reference. HD95 generally increased with smaller cohorts, and both metrics deteriorated markedly in the five-patient configurations. Full cine training showed flatter phase-wise Dice profiles and lower across-phase variability. Between-subject volume differences exceeded phase-related within-subject differences for all structures (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: In this cross-cohort comparison, full cine training showed higher overall Dice, lower overall HD95, and greater phase-wise consistency than single-phase training. The evaluated two-phase configuration may inform annotation-efficient cine CTA dataset design, but broader validation is needed.

Title: Thirty-Day Outcomes in Ultrasound Versus CT-Only Imaging in Obese Adults With Acute Appendicitis.
Abstract: Background Acute appendicitis is one of the most common surgical emergencies affecting people worldwide. Current guidelines suggest imaging with an immediate computed tomography (CT) scan as the gold standard imaging pathway. However, emerging research has suggested that the addition of an ultrasound (US) can play a role in the diagnosis of acute appendicitis. In this study, we wanted to see if US as an adjunct to the existing imaging pathway of a CT scan had any improvement in 30-day outcomes in adult obese patients. Method Using data gathered from real patients using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study on adult obese patients (BMI ≥ 30) with acute appendicitis who were diagnosed by US, with or without a CT scan, versus those who received only a CT scan. In order to balance for possible confounding variables, propensity score matching (1:1) was used to match for common demographic information and comorbidities known to worsen surgical outcomes (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, BMI). The study's primary outcome was emergency room revisit rate after their initial visit. Secondary outcomes included peritoneal abscess, perforation, and peritonitis. All outcomes were measured at 30 days after the acute appendicitis diagnosis. Results After propensity score matching, 968 patients were deemed eligible for analysis, with 484 patients within each cohort. There were no detectable statistical differences between these groups after matching for patient demographics and comorbidities. Those who underwent a US did not show significant differences in outcomes compared to those who received a CT scan only. The rates of emergency room revisits were similar between the US and CT scan groups, at 11.98% and 13.64%, respectively (RR = 0.879, p = 0.44). For secondary outcomes, no statistical difference was found for the risk of peritoneal/abdominal abscess (RR = 0.69, p = 0.16), perforation (RR = 1.32, p = 0.35), or peritonitis (RR = 0.90, p = 0.59). Conclusion Our study demonstrated no statistically significant difference in outcomes for adult obese patients diagnosed with acute appendicitis who received an ultrasound, compared to those who received a CT scan only.

Title: Treatment of oligometastatic disease in colorectal cancer: from molecular biology to multimodal strategies.
Abstract: The management of oligometastatic colorectal cancer (OMD-CRC) has undergone a profound evolution, transforming what was once a uniformly fatal diagnosis into a clinical scenario in which long-term survival and even cure are attainable for a carefully selected subset of patients. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of integrated, multidisciplinary strategies for OMD-CRC, with particular emphasis on hepatic and pulmonary metastases. We examine the biological foundations that differentiate oligometastatic from polymetastatic disease, including molecular subtypes that inform prognosis and therapeutic responsiveness. Local treatment modalities are critically evaluated, ranging from surgical metastasectomy-the standard of care in adequately selected patients-to minimally invasive approaches such as thermal ablation and Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT). Recent randomized trials and prospective studies have suggested possible non-inferiority of these alternatives to surgery in selected contexts, thereby broadening the spectrum of curative-intent interventions. Equally pivotal is the integration of systemic therapy. We discuss optimal timing (neoadjuvant, adjuvant, perioperative) and regimen selection for both resectable and initially unresectable disease. The role of conversion therapy, combining intensive chemotherapy with targeted agents guided by molecular determinants such as RAS/BRAF mutational status and tumor sidedness, is highlighted as a cornerstone in expanding surgical eligibility. Looking ahead, emerging technologies-including radiomics and liquid biopsy approaches such as circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-hold promise for refining patient selection, detecting minimal residual disease, and further individualizing treatment pathways. The convergence of advanced local therapies, precision-guided systemic regimens, and novel biomarkers delineates the new frontier in optimizing outcomes for patients with OMD-CRC.

Title: The application of Chicago classification 4.0 in esophageal motility disorders of scleroderma: a case-control study in China.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by multi-organ fibrosis and vasculopathy that frequently involves the esophagus. This study assessed esophageal motility disorders in patients with SSc using High-resolution manometry (HRM) and classified these disorders according to the Chicago Classification version 4.0, aims to investigate the associations between esophageal dysfunction and clinical phenotypes in Chinese SSc patients, while exploring potential modifications to enhance the applicability of the Chicago v4.0 protocol in SSc patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified SSc patients fulfilling 2013 ACR criteria who underwent HRM classified by Chicago v4.0 at our center (2021-2023). Demographics, organ involvement, pulmonary-function tests, echocardiography and reflux symptom scores (RDQ/GERDQ) were extracted from the hospital information system; age and sex matched non-SSc HRM subjects served as controls. Associations between Chicago categories and clinical variables were examined by multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: In our study, esophageal motility disorders were present in 76.7% of patients with systemic sclerosis, predominantly characterized by ineffective esophageal motility (IEM) (35%) and absent contractility (AC) (36.67%). The occurrence rate of AC rose with age. Symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux were more common in the AC group [Odds Ratio: 3.23 (1.02-10.22) vs 1.43(0.52-3.95), P<0.05, E value=2.99]. Diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) was significantly reduced in both IEM and AC (-2.03 vs -2.70, P value<0.05), with a more pronounced decrease in AC. Total lung capacity (TLC) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) exhibited stronger associations with AC (-1.04 and -0.8 respectively, p value<0.05). Upright HRM revealed more marked decreases in EGJ pressure and distal contractile integral (DCI) relative to the supine position in SSc patients, indicating that esophageal abnormalities may be more readily apparent during upright examination.
CONCLUSIONS: Esophageal motility disorders in SSc were common and significantly associated with older age, gastroesophageal reflux symptoms, and reduced lung function. Future studies are needed to clarify whether early esophageal motility disorders are associated with disease progression and prognosis in patients.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Incidence and epidemiological characteristics of congenital adrenal hyperplasia in Hangzhou newborns, China (2014-2024): a population-based cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is a rare but potentially life-threatening autosomal recessive disorder. Its incidence varies by region and ethnicity. This study aimed to evaluate the birth incidence, trends, and clinical characteristics of neonatal classic CAH in Hangzhou (2014-2024) to support regional clinical prevention and management.
METHODS: This retrospective population-based study collected data from Hangzhou's information systems. Classic CAH cases were identified through newborn screening and clinical follow-up to age 3, with diagnosis confirmed by pediatric endocrinologists. Incidence was calculated per 100,000 live births. Categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Temporal trend was assessed by Poisson regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,235,815 live births, 40 CAH cases were identified, giving an incidence of 3.24/100,000. The annual incidence ranged from 0/100,000 (2020) to 6.56/100,000 (2017), with no significant temporal trend (P = 0.297). The incidence was highest in urban (4.28/100,000), followed by suburban (2.37/100,000) and rural areas (1.93/100,000) (P = 0.16). Males accounted for 65% (26/40) of cases and females 35% (14/40), with a male-to-female ratio of 1.86:1. The incidence was 4.03/100,000 in males and 2.37/100,000 in females (P = 0.104). Among the 40 cases, salt-wasting (SW) was the predominant phenotype (33/40, 82.5%), and 21-hydroxylase deficiency accounted for 95% (38/40) of cases. Two neonates (5%) presented with salt-wasting crises, and two female infants with the simple virilizing (SV) form were initially misclassified as male. Prenatal ultrasound showed increased nuchal translucency in 6 cases (15%), adrenal enlargement in 3 cases (7.5%), and ambiguous genitalia in 1 case (2.5%). CAH was strongly associated with congenital heart defects (OR: 13.93, P < 0.001), and congenital hypothyroidism (OR: 42.26, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The incidence of classic CAH in Hangzhou (3.24/100,000) was lower than many global estimates. Although temporal and regional differences were not statistically significant, the predominance of SW cases, the occurrence of adrenal crises, and the presence of comorbidities (congenital heart defects, hypothyroidism, and cognitive developmental delay), highlight the need for improved early recognition, strengthened diagnostic capacity in suburban and rural areas, and long-term multidisciplinary management.

Title: Opium Consumption and Myocardial Infarction in Osteoarthritis Patients: A Propensity Score Matched Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In recent years, the use of drugs with opioid compounds in patients with osteoarthritis has attracted increasing attention. However, long-term use of these drugs may cause severe side effects, including cardiovascular diseases. The present study aimed to investigate the relationship between the use of opium substances and myocardial infarction in osteoarthritis patients using a propensity score matching (PSM) approach.
METHODS: We designed this study as a retrospective cohort study. The data were collected from 2016 to 2020. We identified confounding variables using the modified disjunctive cause criterion method. We matched individuals exposed to opium (opium users) and those unexposed to opium (non-users) by propensity score. We examined the distributions of opium users and non-users, both with and without propensity score matching. To determine the relationship between exposure to opium and heart attack in osteoarthritis patients, the Cox regression method was used.
FINDINGS: The participants' mean age was 49.85±9.61 years, with 32.3% being men and 67.7% being women. We excluded individuals with cardiovascular disease from the baseline examination. Before PSM, the incidence rate in the total study sample was 2.96 per 1000 person-years. The relationship between opium consumption and heart attack was inverse before matching (hazard ratio, HR 0.73, 95% confidence interval (95% CI 0.58-0.98). After matching, the HR showed an increase of 24% (HR 1.24, 95% CI 0.87-1.76).
CONCLUSION: The findings of the present study suggest that opioid consumption is associated with an increased risk of heart attacks in osteoarthritis patients. Confirmation of this finding in future studies would indicate the need for monitoring these patients with a view towards primary prevention of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors.

Title: Prevalence of migalastat-amenable variants in patients with Fabry disease from Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia: an observational study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fabry disease is a progressive, X-linked lysosomal disorder caused by GLA variants that result in dysfunctional α-galactosidase A (α-Gal A) enzyme. One treatment option is migalastat, an oral small-molecule pharmacological chaperone treatment for patients with migalastat-amenable GLA variants.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, medical records were used to determine the prevalence of migalastat-amenable variants among individuals managed for Fabry disease at centers in Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia (primary endpoint). Demographic and clinical characteristics were explored using available data. Medical records of males or females of any age with a diagnosis of Fabry disease (based on genetic testing and/or α-Gal A enzymatic activity) were eligible for inclusion.
RESULTS: Data were collected for 1,196 individuals diagnosed with Fabry disease in Brazil (n = 1,000), Argentina (n = 122), and Colombia (n = 74); of these, 720 (60.2%) had migalastat-amenable GLA variants (650 [65.0%] patients in Brazil, 32 [26.2%] in Argentina, and 38 [51.4%] in Colombia). The migalastat-amenable variants differed by country with little overlap among the cohorts in Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia in the most common variants. Median age (in years) at the study reference date (July 1, 2021) for individuals with migalastat-amenable variants was 45.6, 44.1, and 21.8 years in Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia, respectively. Data on clinical characteristics were available only in Argentina and Colombia.
DISCUSSION: In those for whom data were available, there appeared to be both objective and subjective manifestations of Fabry disease, as evidenced by renal impairment, cardiac involvement, and classic Fabry disease signs and symptoms.

Title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps-Mediated Intraplaque Angiogenesis and Microvascular Permeability Promote Rapid Plaque Progression following Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract: Despite adherence to guideline-recommended therapies, survivors of myocardial infarction (MI) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events. This study aimed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms responsible for this residual risk. Using Mendelian randomization analysis and retrospective cohort study, we established a causal relationship between MI and plaque progression, potentially mediated by neutrophils. In a murine atherosclerotic model, MI precipitated a marked expansion in plaque volume accompanied by reduced stability; these pathological changes are consistent with the hallmark features of rapid plaque progression, which may trigger recurrent ischemic events. Pharmacological inhibition and adoptive transfer experiments using Padi4flox/floxLyz2Cre mice confirmed the pivotal role of neutrophils in MI-driven rapid plaque progression via neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation. Further investigations revealed that NETs promote intraplaque hemorrhage by facilitating intraplaque angiogenesis and enhancing microvascular permeability, thereby exacerbating post-MI atherosclerotic inflammation. Mechanistically, bioinformatics analyses and in vitro experiments identified the transcription factor ETS proto-oncogene 1 as a critical regulator of NETs-mediated angiogenesis and endothelial permeability through the activation of the vascular endothelial growth factor A/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 signaling pathway. In vivo pharmacological inhibition of ETS proto-oncogene 1 with TK216 markedly attenuated the rapid plaque progression after MI. In summary, this study provides the first comprehensive evidence that neutrophils and NETs drive rapid plaque progression following MI by modulating intraplaque angiogenesis and hemorrhage. These findings offer novel insights into the mechanisms underlying post-MI ischemic event recurrence and highlight promising therapeutic targets for clinical prevention.

Title: Blood pressure changes after stair climbing in busy and quiet outpatient clinic environments among Tanzanian adults: a randomised crossover study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Blood pressure (BP) measured soon after activity may differ from later seated readings. We examined serial BP changes after stair climbing in busy and quiet outpatient settings, without assuming that a particular waiting period represents complete physiological recovery.
METHODS: In this randomized crossover study at Mbeya Zonal Referral Hospital, Tanzania, adults with and without a previous hypertension diagnosis drew folded numbered slips to determine environmental order. Staff recording BP were not blinded. Participants ascended and descended 19 steps before measurements immediately and every 3 min for 30 min in each environment. Mixed-effects models included period, sequence, age, sex and body mass index, with session-specific random slopes and autoregressive residual correlation. Classification was compared with each participant's environment-specific average at 24, 27 and 30 min. Exploratory laboratory analyses accounted for reporting limits and used the available observations for each marker. Clinical sensitivity analyses examined alcohol, diabetes history and medication classes.
RESULTS: The analysis included 443 participants-223 with hypertension and 220 without a previous diagnosis-contributing 9,746 measurement occasions. At 15 min, adjusted busy-minus-quiet systolic BP differences were 2.87 mmHg (95% CI 1.39-4.35) and 4.07 mmHg (2.58-5.56), respectively. Classification disagreement at that time was 10.8% (7.3%-15.5%) in quiet and 7.6% (4.8%-11.9%) in busy settings among participants with hypertension; corresponding values without a previous diagnosis were 2.3% (1.0%-5.2%) and 5.9% (3.5%-9.8%). First-period-only systolic contrasts remained positive but were larger and less precise. Evidence for differences in trajectory shape between diagnostic groups depended on the covariate-adjustment specification. No routine laboratory marker showed a clear adjusted association with the signed SBP difference from the late-session average at 12 or 15 min. Environmental systolic estimates changed little after clinical adjustment within matching samples.
CONCLUSIONS: BP changed during seated observation after stair climbing, and early readings disagreed more often with the late-session average. Persistent disagreement and within-session variability do not support 12-15 min as a universally sufficient resting interval. The absence of a pre-exercise resting reference and a no-exercise comparator limits attribution of the decline to recovery from activity.

Title: Association of Value of Fibrosis-4 Index with Long-Term Mortality in Patients with Heart Failure: A Comparison Study with Fibrosis-5 Index.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) and fibrosis-5 (FIB-5) indices are non-invasive biomarkers originally developed for hepatic fibrosis but may reflect systemic pathophysiological changes related to adverse cardiovascular prognosis. We aimed to investigate whether baseline FIB-4 and FIB-5 values predict long-term mortality in patients with heart failure (HF).
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 593 patients with HF who had available long-term mortality data. FIB-4 and FIB-5 indices were calculated at admission. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality, and outcomes were evaluated at 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year intervals. Clinical, laboratory, and echocardiographic parameters were compared between survivors and non-survivors.
RESULTS: During follow-up, 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year mortality rates were 24.6%, 39.0%, and 49.7%, respectively. Non-survivors had significantly higher FIB-4 and FIB-5 values compared with survivors (P<0.001 for both). ROC curve analyses demonstrated that both indices had significant predictive performance for long-term mortality. Optimal cut-off values showed good sensitivity and specificity for identifying high-risk patients.
CONCLUSION: Higher FIB-4 and FIB-5 values are associated with greater long-term mortality risk in HF patients. These indices may serve as practical, cost-effective prognostic biomarkers for mortality risk stratification in routine clinical care.

Title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk is associated with AT(N)V neuroimaging biomarkers and cognitive impairment in the health and aging brain study-health disparities cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk is increasingly recognized as relevant to cognitive aging and dementia-related brain changes, yet its relationship to multimodal neuroimaging biomarkers of amyloid, tau, neurodegeneration, and vascular injury (AT(N)-V) remains incompletely understood in racially and ethnically diverse cohorts. We examined whether ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk was associated with AT(N)-V neuroimaging biomarkers and cognitive domain scores.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 1,626 Health and Aging Brain Study-Health Disparities (HABS-HD) participants without cardiovascular disease or dementia who had amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) imaging linked to visit 1. Ten-year ASCVD risk was estimated using the Pooled Cohort Equations and modeled continuously. Neuroimaging outcomes included global florbetaben amyloid PET standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), medial temporal lobe (MTL) PI-2620 tau PET SUVR, cortical thickness, hippocampal volume, and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) volume. Cognitive domain outcomes included memory, executive function, processing speed, and language. Multivariable linear regression models accounted for apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 status, relevant neuroimaging biomarkers, and imaging scanner/protocol covariates as appropriate, with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. Amyloid-status-stratified analyses were also conducted using a global amyloid PET SUVR threshold of 1.08.
RESULTS: Increasing ten-year ASCVD risk was associated with increasing global amyloid and MTL tau PET SUVR, smaller cortical thickness, smaller hippocampal volume, and increased WMH volume. Increasing ten-year ASCVD risk was also associated with lower memory, executive function, processing speed, and language scores after accounting for APOE ε4 status, amyloid burden, neurodegeneration, vascular injury, and scanner covariates. Associations between ten-year ASCVD risk and structural and vascular injury markers were observed in both amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative participants, whereas associations with amyloid and MTL tau PET were modest and statistically significant only among amyloid-negative participants.
CONCLUSION: In this diverse HABS-HD sample, increasing ten-year ASCVD risk was associated with greater AT(N)-V biomarker burden and poorer cognitive performance across multiple domains. These cross-sectional findings suggest that ten-year ASCVD risk may serve as a marker of co-occurring cardiovascular and brain health burden, but they do not establish causality or temporal direction.

Title: Advancing cardiac xenotransplantation: overcoming challenges and ethical considerations for clinical integration.
Abstract: Advanced heart failure affects over 6 million adults in the United States alone. Orthotopic heart transplantation remains the definitive treatment, with over 90% one-year survival and meaningful gains in functional status and quality of life. The therapy is, however, constrained by an intractable supply problem. For decades, xenotransplantation (XTx), the transplantation of organs across species, has been proposed as a means of closing this gap, though for most of that time it remained a theoretical aspiration. With the discovery of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, improved immunosuppressive strategies, and refined preclinical models, the field has accelerated at an unprecedented pace. Multi-gene-edited porcine donors have survived for more than 200 days in orthotopic non-human primate models, and two compassionate-use pig-to-human cardiac transplants at the University of Maryland (2022 and 2023) demonstrated some feasibility for clinical cardiac XTx for the first time. In May 2026, the FDA granted clearance under an investigational new drug application to allow the EXPRESS study, the first prospective clinical trial of a gene-edited porcine heart, to proceed. In this perspective, we discuss the ethical, regulatory, and equity considerations that remain as decisive barriers to clinical integration and may shape how this therapy is introduced along the remaining immunologic and virologic challenges. We outline what we regard as the near-term priorities: defining the antibody targets that drive xenograft rejection, standardizing virologic surveillance, candidate selection and outcome benchmarking, and building access patterns with embedded distributive justice from the outset of its implementation.

Title: Does Concurrent Carotid Endarterectomy with Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting Improve Outcomes in Patients with Dual Arterial Disease? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
Abstract: Patients with coexisting carotid and coronary artery disease face a complex surgical decision regarding whether to undergo coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) alone or combined with carotid endarterectomy (CEA). Evidence remains conflicting, with some studies suggesting stroke reduction from a combined approach while others report increased perioperative morbidity without a survival advantage, contributing to weak ACCF/AHA and ESC/EACTS guideline recommendations. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials and propensity-matched studies comparing CABG alone versus CABG+CEA. Five studies involving 23,916 patients were included, of whom 29% underwent combined surgery. CABG+CEA was associated with a significantly higher incidence of perioperative stroke (OR 1.5; 95% CI 1.1-2.0; P=0.03), but no significant differences were observed in 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, myocardial infarction, or hospital length of stay. These findings indicate that adding CEA to CABG increases stroke risk without providing a clear survival benefit, supporting guideline recommendations for a selective, risk-based strategy. Until higher-quality evidence becomes available, concurrent CEA+CABG should be reserved for carefully selected patients in whom the anticipated benefits outweigh potential harms.

Title: Impact of Empagliflozin on mRNA Levels of Cardiotrophin-1 and GDF-15 in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing PCI: A Double-Blind Pilot Trial.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Given the proven cardiovascular benefits of Empagliflozin (EM), we aimed to investigate the effect of Empagliflozin on Cardiotrophin-1 (CTF-1) and growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) expressions in circulating monocytes in type 2 diabetic patients after MI.
METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study included 33 patients referred to Ayatollah Mousavi Hospital in Zanjan between 5 of September to 25 of December, 2024. Eligible patients with type 2 diabetes and MI who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were randomly assigned (17:16) to receive either 10 mg of EMPA daily or placebo for 12 weeks. Target genes expression levels were quantified by real time PCR, and data were analyzed by SPSS version 26.
RESULTS: Thirty-three patients were included in this study (mean age: 61.27±9.07, 66% male), mean diabetes duration was longer in intervention group (7.82±5.13) compared to placebo group (3.75±2.74), hypertension was the most common comorbidity (57%). CTF-1 expression in the intervention group was 0.3±0.28 and in placebo group was 5.66±6.52. GDF-15 expression in the intervention group was 0.198±0.22 and in placebo group was 1.66±1.04. EMPA significantly reduced expression of CTF-1 (13-fold) (P=0.003) and GDF-15 (7-fold) (P ˂ 0.0001). The CTF-1 and GDF-15 expression reduction were not associated with any other clinical variables. Significant reduction observed in LDL (P=0.045) and triglycerides (P=0.013) after intervention.
CONCLUSION: EMPA significantly reduced the expression of CTF-1 and GDF-15 in type 2 diabetic, post MI patients, which are associated with atherosclerosis, and suggest that potential anti-atherosclerotic effect of EMPA mediated through modulation of GDF-15 and CTF-1 gene expression.

Title: Single versus double transseptal puncture for atrial fibrillation radiofrequency ablation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The single puncture technique has emerged as an alternative to conventional double transseptal puncture for radiofrequency ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF). This meta-analysis aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of these two approaches.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library up to 1st March, 2026. Prospective and retrospective cohort studies comparing single vs. double transseptal puncture during AF ablation were included. The primary outcome was the sinus rhythm maintenance. Secondary outcomes included total procedure time, fluoroscopy time, and periprocedural complications. Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was assessed with the I² statistic.
RESULTS: Four studies involving 1811 patients were included. No significant difference was observed in 3-month sinus rhythm maintenance between the single- and double-puncture groups (OR 1.20, 95% CI: 0.95-1.51, P = 0.13). While fluoroscopy time presented similar values (MD -0.84, 95% CI: -4.80-3.11, P = 0.68), procedure duration was significantly longer with single transseptal puncture (MD 11.65, 95% CI: 2.62-20.69, P = 0.01). The incidence of periprocedural complications was similar between the two strategies (OR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.47-1.38, P = 0.43).
CONCLUSIONS: Single transseptal puncture represents an effective and safe alternative to double puncture for atrial fibrillation ablation, with comparable rhythm outcomes, fluoroscopy exposure and complication rates, despite longer procedural duration.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/view/CRD420261300869, Identifier: CRD420261300869.

Title: Longitudinal dynamics of serum neurofilament light chain and prognostic value for functional outcome after acute stroke: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) is a blood biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but its early longitudinal dynamics and prognostic value in clinically heterogeneous acute stroke populations remain insufficiently defined. This study characterized early sNfL changes and examined their association with functional outcome after acute stroke.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study consecutively enrolled 104 patients with acute stroke and 86 healthy controls (HCs) between January 2023 and December 2024. Patients were grouped as intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH, n = 28), ischemic stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IS+IVT, n = 33), and ischemic stroke without intravenous thrombolysis (IS-IVT, n = 43). sNfL was measured within 24 h after onset (D1) and on day 7 (D7). Functional outcome was assessed by modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 3 and 6 months. Linear mixed-effects models assessed longitudinal sNfL trajectories. Multivariable logistic regression assessed prognostic associations, with the 3-month outcome as the primary endpoint and the 6-month outcome as the secondary endpoint. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) and interaction analyses were exploratory.
RESULTS: sNfL increased significantly from D1 to D7 (p < 0.001) and was higher in patients with stroke than in HCs at D1 (p < 0.001). In the linear mixed-effects model adjusted for age and admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, longitudinal sNfL trajectories did not differ significantly among the clinical stroke groups (time × group interaction, p = 0.225). The predominantly mild-to-moderate severity profile may have limited the detection of trajectory differences. In multivariable logistic regression, each 10-pg/mL increase in D1 sNfL was associated with 5% higher odds of poor functional outcome at 3 months (OR = 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.12; p = 0.047) and 7% higher odds at 6 months (OR = 1.07; 95% CI, 1.01-1.14; p = 0.025). D7 sNfL was not independently associated with poor functional outcome after adjustment. Exploratory RCS analyses found no statistical evidence of nonlinearity for D1 sNfL and suggested a nonlinear association between D7 sNfL and 3-month poor functional outcome.
CONCLUSION: sNfL levels increased during the first week after acute stroke. Higher D1 sNfL was associated with poor functional outcome at 3 and 6 months, suggesting potential value for early prognostic assessment.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitors' Effects on Biomarkers of Myocardial Injury: A Systematic Review.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular and thoracic research
Abstract: There is a lack of clinical data regarding sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors' effects on myocardial injury, a common clinical condition that deteriorates patient prognosis. Hence, this systematic review aims to investigate the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on myocardial injury, using the cardiac injury biomarkers, particularly high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn). We performed a literature review on Embase, MEDLINE (PubMed), and the Cochrane Library, up to May 27, 2025. All potentially relevant randomized clinical trials (RCTs) assessing the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on myocardial injury in individuals with diabetes or cardiovascular diseases were identified. The outcome measures were the most relevant cardiac injury biomarkers, including hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI, creatine kinase (CK)-MB, heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), ischemia-modified albumin, and glycogen phosphorylase BB. In total, 1770 articles were identified through the literature search. After eliminating duplicates and screening articles, 10 studies involving 10440 participants were included. Of them, 6 studies evaluated hs-cTnT and 4 studies evaluated hs-cTnI. Among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), four of six trials showed significant attenuation in hs-cTn rise with SGLT2 inhibitors. In contrast, studies on HFrEF populations reported no significant change in hs-cTn levels. One study, including patients with acute myocardial infarction, also did not demonstrate a significant effect on hs-cTnI. The outcomes of this systematic review may suggest the potential effects of SGLT2 inhibitors in reducing myocardial injury by lowering hs-cTn levels in T2DM individuals. However, more studies are recommended to provide robust evidence.

Title: Investigating risk factors and developing a predictive model for venous thromboembolism in patients with sepsis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with sepsis are at high risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, existing assessment tools designed for general medical or surgical populations may inadequately capture the specific risk profile of septic patients. This study aimed to identify independent predictors of VTE in sepsis and develop a sepsis-specific prediction model.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, adult patients with sepsis diagnosed at a single center (2015-2024) were enrolled. Candidate predictors and treatments were restricted to data available within the first 24 h of diagnosis. After exclusions, 157 VTE cases and 703 matched non-VTE controls formed the prediction cohort, which was split into training (n = 602) and validation (n = 258) sets. The Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique was applied to the training set. LASSO regression followed by multivariable logistic regression identified independent factors for the nomogram. Model performance was assessed via discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis and compared with the Padua and Caprini scores in the validation cohort.
RESULTS: Among 3,228 sepsis patients, 157 (4.86%) developed VTE. Multivariable analysis identified four independent predictors: surgery within 3 months, central venous catheterization within 24 h, history of VTE ≥1 year prior, and absence of early anticoagulant therapy (all P < 0.001). The resulting nomogram showed excellent discrimination (AUC: 0.905, 95% CI: 0.875-0.935 in training; 0.909, 95% CI: 0.867-0.951 in validation) and good calibration. Decision curve analysis supported its clinical utility. In the validation cohort, the nomogram significantly outperformed the Padua (AUC: 0.712) and Caprini (AUC: 0.738) scores, demonstrating superior incremental predictive value (P < 0.001 for net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement).
CONCLUSIONS: A sepsis-specific nomogram incorporating recent surgery, early catheterization, previous VTE, and absence of early anticoagulation demonstrated good discrimination and calibration. It outperformed the Padua and Caprini tools in internal validation. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Simple renal cysts are associated with ischemic stroke in young adults: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of ischemic stroke among young patients is increasing, and ischemic stroke has become a major cause of death and disability in young adults. The key to alleviating this problem is to identify the risk factors and causes of stroke to optimize treatment.
