The current study aims to assess whether simple renal cysts are associated with the occurrence of ischemic stroke among young adults.
METHODS: Data from patients with acute ischemic stroke aged 18-50 years and age- and sex-matched controls who underwent medical examinations at the Affiliated Changsha Central Hospital, Hengyang Medical School, University of South China, from October 2022 to September 2025 were retrospectively collected. Potential risk factors (including blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, dyslipidemia, homocysteine, and simple renal cysts) were compared between young patients with stroke and controls. Binary logistic regression analysis was conducted to identify risk factors for ischemic stroke among young patients.
RESULTS: A total of 219 young patients with acute ischemic stroke and 219 controls were enrolled for analysis. Patients with elevated blood pressure, elevated blood glucose, and concurrent simple renal cysts had a higher risk of ischemic stroke. Simple renal cysts were associated with a higher risk of ischemic stroke in young adults, but they did not correlate with greater stroke severity.
CONCLUSION: Simple renal cysts are associated with ischemic stroke in young adults and thus merit clinical awareness. Prospective multicenter cohort studies are expected to confirm this association and clarify potential mechanisms.

Title: Comment on "The impact of underdiagnosis and delay in care for patients with moderate and severe aortic stenosis: A real-world database cohort study".
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

Title: Incident Type 2 Diabetes in Individuals With CKD: The REGARDS Study.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and diabetes are comorbid metabolic diseases that share common factors such as insulin resistance. Few studies have examined the association between CKD and incident diabetes, with limited consensus and associated risk factors. We conducted an analysis of participants in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in stroke study to investigate incident diabetes among participants with CKD compared with non-CKD participants.
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective cohort study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Total of 7,511 participants who completed 10 years of follow-up were included in the analysis, of whom 994 had CKD (an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73m2 or albumin-to-creatinine ratio >30mg/g) at baseline.
EXPOSURE: CKD.
OUTCOME: Incident diabetes.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Logistic regression analysis was performed to estimate the odds of incident diabetes among CKD participants, with odds ratio (OR) and 95% CI. Risk factors for incident diabetes among CKD participants were also examined.
RESULTS: After 10 years of follow-up, 11.0% (717) of non-CKD participants and 15.8% (157) of CKD participants developed diabetes. Incident diabetes was higher among CKD participants than in non-CKD participants using creatinine-based equations, which was not seen when using a creatinine-based and cystatin C-based equation for CKD. Several risk factors such as race, prediabetes, age, body mass index, hypertension, current smoking, and exercise ≥ 4 times/week increased the odds of incident diabetes, whereas current alcohol use had a lower risk of incident diabetes. Prediabetes had the highest risk of incident diabetes (OR = 4.94, 95% Cl: 4.22-5.78; P < 0.01).
LIMITATIONS: Attrition bias, limited generalizability, and limited diagnostic classification.
CONCLUSIONS: The association between CKD and incident diabetes depends on how CKD is defined. These findings highlight the need for future studies to explore how renal function is assessed when determining adverse outcomes related to CKD.

Title: Association between early intravenous magnesium sulfate administration and mortality according to systemic immune-inflammation index in critically ill patients with acute heart failure: A retrospective cohort study.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnesium sulfate is commonly administered in acute heart failure (AHF). We investigated the association between early intravenous magnesium sulfate and mortality across baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) strata in critically ill patients with AHF.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using the MIMIC-IV database of critically ill patients with AHF. Early intravenous magnesium sulfate was defined as treatment initiated from 6 h before to 24 h after intensive care unit admission. SII was categorized into quartiles. The primary and secondary outcomes were 30-day and 90-day all-cause mortality. Multivariable Cox regression, restricted cubic spline, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among 4293 patients, 1561 (36.4%) received intravenous magnesium sulfate. Magnesium sulfate administration was associated with lower 30-day (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.82) and 90-day mortality (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.63-0.86). For 30-day mortality, multivariable Cox regression demonstrated significant associations in the lowest (aHR 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.95) and highest (aHR 0.52, 95% CI 0.36-0.75) SII quartiles, whereas no significant associations were identified in the intermediate quartiles. Comparable patterns were observed for 90-day mortality. Restricted cubic spline analyses showed visual separation between treatment groups at the extremes of the SII distribution, although formal interaction testing was not significant. Sensitivity analyses consistently reproduced the association in the highest SII quartile.
CONCLUSIONS: Stratified analyses suggested that the association between early magnesium sulfate administration and lower mortality was most evident in the highest SII quartile and less consistent in the lowest quartile. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

Title: Predictive value of monocyte-to-HDL and neutrophil-to-HDL cholesterol ratio for obstructive coronary artery disease in Patients undergoing coronary angiography.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR) and neutrophil-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (NHR) are emerging composite biomarkers that reflect systemic inflammatory status and lipid metabolism. Although both indices have individually been associated with coronary artery disease (CAD), evidence directly comparing their diagnostic performance for obstructive CAD remains scarce.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to compare the diagnostic performance of MHR and NHR in identifying obstructive CAD among patients undergoing elective coronary angiography.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted involving patients who underwent diagnostic coronary angiography in Jordan. Obstructive CAD was defined as stenosis of 50% or more in a major epicardial vessel on invasive coronary angiography.
RESULTS: A total of 215 patients were included, of whom 129 (60%) were male, with a mean age of 58.4 ± 11.4 years; 43.7% had obstructive CAD. After adjusting for age, sex, and prior CAD history in multivariate regression analysis, MHR remained an independent predictor of obstructive CAD (OR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.34-2.97, p < 0.001), whereas NHR was not independently associated (OR = 1.66, 95%CI: 0.74-3.69, p = 0.21). The clinical model integrating MHR demonstrated an AUC of 0.801 (95% CI: 0.74-0.86); however, this numerical increase was not statistically significant (DeLong test, p = 0.216).
CONCLUSION: MHR may have potential value for risk stratification in obstructive CAD. Although adding MHR to the clinical model resulted in a numerically higher AUC, the incremental improvement in discrimination was not statistically significant. Further studies involving larger, multicenter cohorts are needed to establish the incremental predictive and clinical utility of MHR.

Title: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion versus oral anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: A pragmatic meta-analysis of randomized trials within the DOAC era.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC). However, its safety and efficacy boundaries remain incompletely defined in dedicated comparisons against direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).
OBJECTIVE: This study applied a pragmatic framework to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of LAAO versus OAC in a DOAC-predominant setting.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAO with OAC, restricted to a DOAC-predominant comparator. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated via a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model.
RESULTS: Four trials comprising 5890 patients were included (96.4% of controls assigned to DOACs). Overall stroke (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.87-1.60; p = 0.28), systemic embolism (RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.29-4.08; p = 0.89), major bleeding (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.81-1.19; p = 0.85), hemorrhagic stroke (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.45-1.51; p = 0.53), and all-cause mortality (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.85-1.17; p = 0.99) did not differ significantly. Ischemic stroke presented numerical asymmetry favoring OAC that approached statistical significance (RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.99-1.89; p = 0.06). Conversely, within available protocol-defined datasets, LAAO significantly reduced nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.43-0.60; p < 0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: In a pragmatic analysis of the DOAC era, randomized data show no statistically significant differences for hard individual endpoints, though broad confidence intervals reflect precision limits. A numerical asymmetry for ischemic stroke favored OAC, while LAAO reduced nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding. Current evidence remains non-definitive, warranting shared clinical decision-making to balance individual thromboembolic risks against long-term bleeding susceptibility.

Title: Circulating musclin as a potential prognostic biomarker for major adverse cardiovascular events in surgically treated acute aortic dissection: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Musclin is a skeletal muscle-derived myokine with reported cardioprotective effects; however, its prognostic relevance in acute aortic dissection (AAD) remains uncertain. This study examined whether admission Musclin levels were associated with postoperative major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and whether they added prognostic information beyond conventional clinical indicators.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 108 surgically treated AAD patients from 2022 to 2023. Musclin levels were measured by ELISA in residual serum samples collected at admission. The primary endpoint was composite MACE. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, multivariate Cox regression, time-dependent ROC, IDI and NRI were used to evaluate the predictive and incremental value of Musclin.
RESULTS: During 400-day follow-up, 36 patients (33.3%) developed MACE. The CART-derived optimal Musclin cutoff was 4.815 ng/mL. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that low Musclin group had significantly higher MACE cumulative incidence than high Musclin group (48.2% vs. 17.3%, log-rank P < 0.001). Multivariate Cox regression confirmed circulating Musclin associated with a lower risk of MACE (HR = 0.314, 95%CI: 0.104-0.943, P = 0.039). Time-dependent AUC analysis demonstrated that the combined model incorporating Musclin (model 2) achieved superior AUC compared with the clinical model (model 1). Even at the 250-day time point, where the incremental gain (ΔAUC) was minimal, the combined model still exhibited significantly better discriminative performance (0.876 vs. 0.837, DeLong P = 0.013). At the 250-day landmark, IDI was 0.153 (95%CI: 0.018-0.286, P = 0.012) and overall NRI was 0.167 (95%CI: 0.003-0.336, P = 0.044), with event-specific NRI reaching 0.361 (P = 0.012). Sensitivity analyses yielded directionally consistent associations when Musclin was analyzed using the cohort median or as a continuous variable.
CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective cohort, lower admission Musclin was associated with a higher risk of postoperative MACE. Musclin may be a severity-related biomarker that could complement conventional risk indicators, but its independent clinical utility, optimal threshold, and role in risk stratification require prospective multicenter validation with comprehensive perioperative adjustment before clinical use.

Title: Remnant cholesterol, C-reactive protein, cholesterol-lowering medication, and cardiovascular outcome: novel findings from UK Biobank.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial reductions in cardiovascular events with intensive LDL-C lowering, significant residual risk persists. Remnant cholesterol (RC) and C-reactive protein (CRP) reflect lipid dysregulation and inflammation, respectively, and may synergistically promote atherosclerosis. However, large-scale cohort evidence on their combined impact, particularly the quantitative interaction between the two and the modifying role of cholesterol-lowering therapy, remains limited.
METHODS: This study included 376,817 participants with a median follow-up of 13.4 years. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate the individual and joint associations of RC and CRP with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) risk. Stratified analyses by cholesterol-lowering therapy were further conducted to explore its modifying effect on the combined risk.
RESULTS: Both RC (≥0.8 mmol/L) and CRP (≥2 mg/L) were independently associated with MACE risk, with adjusted hazard ratios (HR) of 1.074 [95% confidence interval (CI): 1.024-1.126] and 1.168 (95% CI: 1.129-1.207), respectively. Concurrent elevation of both biomarkers conferred the highest risk (HR = 1.239, 95% CI: 1.167-1.316), and a significant positive multiplicative interaction was observed between RC and CRP. Stratified analyses suggested effect modification by cholesterol-lowering medication: the association between isolated RC elevation and MACE was attenuated in medication users, whereas risks remained significant for isolated CRP elevation and combined elevation of both markers.
CONCLUSION: Concurrent elevation of RC and CRP yields the highest MACE risk with a positive additive interaction. Cholesterol-lowering therapy reduces RC-related risk but not inflammation-driven risk in isolated CRP elevation. These findings support combined assessment of both biomarkers for personalized cardiovascular risk stratification.

Title: Evaluating HEART: Student Engagement and Health System Impact in a Person-Centered Learning Health System Initiative.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare Education and Research Training (HEART) is a cocurricular, engaged learning initiative that supported undergraduate students in acquiring and applying healthcare research skills. The project was guided by a learning health system (LHS)-aligned model focused on the collection, synthesis, and rapid translation of patient-reported experience data into actionable recommendations. In the 2023/2024 academic year, a cohort of 28 students completed the pilot project to report LHS-based recommendations to healthcare directors. This paper reports the qualitative evaluation conducted in August 2024 following the pilot to assess the initiative's implementation, participant experience, and healthcare system impacts.
METHODS: Virtual, semi-structured interviews were conducted with students who participated in HEART and health system directors from a provincial health authority. Interview guides were developed by the research team in collaboration with Patient Partners. Inductive content analysis (ICA) was used to categorize information significant to the research questions. Final themes were established using a team-based approach.
RESULTS: Student interviews indicated that participants found HEART to be a meaningful learning experience that strengthened their understanding of the healthcare system and patient experiences and helped them build applied research skills. Health system directors also expressed strong satisfaction with the project, noting that student-collected qualitative data identified service gaps, supported patient and community engagement, and contributed to measurable care improvements in at least one clinic. Suggested areas for project improvement included adjusting length of training sessions, increasing clarity around expectations and timelines, streamlining final reporting, and refining the patient interview process to gather more detailed information about specific patient experiences.
CONCLUSION: While various opportunities for improvement were identified, overall, HEART was determined to be a valuable opportunity for developing student healthcare research skills and was of direct benefit to health system partners as an LHS-aligned initiative providing actionable data used to identify healthcare gaps and improve patient care. Feedback and recommendations drawn from the evaluation were used to adapt and improve HEART for the following academic year.

Title: Angiographic prevalence of occlusion myocardial infarction and the limited value of serial troponin in patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: An estimated 25%-34% of patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) are diagnosed with an occluded culprit artery during catheterization. Whether early serial troponin kinetics discriminate angiographically defined occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) in catheterized patients with NSTE-ACS remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 481 patients with NSTE-ACS who underwent coronary catheterization between 2017 and 2023. OMI was defined by a purely angiographic criterion: >90% culprit-vessel stenosis with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction flow grade 0, 1, or 2. Seven contemporary sensitivity troponin I metrics (absolute values at 0, 3, and 6 h; deltas; and ratios) were evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Operating characteristics are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and likelihood ratios.
RESULTS: Ninety-eight patients (20.4%) met the angiographic definition of OMI. These patients were younger (median, 65.5 vs. 70.0 years; p = 0.025), had fewer comorbidities, and more often presented with chest pain (92.9% vs. 82.8%; p = 0.013). The left circumflex artery was the most common culprit in OMI (36.7%). Twenty-nine patients with OMI (29.6%) had a presentation ECG classified as normal (no ST-T change or bundle branch block. No troponin metric reliably discriminated OMI from non-occlusion MI. The prespecified primary predictor, the 0-6-h change in troponin concentration, had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.623 (95% CI, 0.544-0.703) and the best single metric, the 6-h value, of 0.654 (0.580-0.727); all seven unadjusted troponin-metric AUCs were under 0.66. At its Youden cutoff (≥0.379 ng/mL), the 6-h troponin had a sensitivity of 69.4%, a specificity of 57.7%, a positive predictive value of 27.2%, and a negative predictive value of 89.3%. The highest positive predictive value of any metric was 41.3%, the first troponin (at 0 h) identified fewer than 40% of patients with OMI at its optimal threshold, and likelihood ratios produced only limited shifts in post-test probability.
CONCLUSION: Among analyzable patients with NSTE-ACS undergoing catheterization, approximately one in five met the study-defined angiographic criteria for OMI. Early serial troponin kinetics showed only modest discrimination, and upper confidence bounds fell below levels expected of a standalone triage biomarker. Complementary strategies for identifying these patients, including expert ECG interpretation, warrant further study.

Title: Cardiovascular risk factors in autoimmune thyroiditis: role of adiponectin, resistin, inflammation and auto-immunity - a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Autoimmune thyroiditis (AIT) has been associated with an increased cardiovascular risk. Whether adipokines, inflammation and auto-immunity contribute to this increased risk is uncertain. Our aim was to evaluate the interrelationships of adipokines, inflammation, auto-immunity, and thyroid function with cardiovascular risk in autoimmune thyroiditis.
METHODS: Sixty-two patients with AIT, with normal free T4 (FT4) and free T3 (FT3), without other comorbidities were studied. Patients were divided into two groups: AIT with thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) ≤2.5 mU/L and AIT with TSH >2.5 mU/L. Parameters of thyroid function tests, serum lipid, high sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and homocysteine levels, anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, anti-thyroid peroxidase (TPO) antibodies, adiponectin and resistin were measured.
RESULTS: Patients with TSH >2.5 mU/L had significantly higher body mass index, higher low density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol levels, and lower lipoprotein(a) levels. No differences in triglycerides, apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), adiponectin, or resistin levels were observed between groups. In the overall cohort, adiponectin levels were positively correlated with high density lipoprotein (HDL)-cholesterol and lipoprotein(a), whereas resistin was positively correlated with hs-CRP and triglyceride levels. Hs-CRP levels were positively correlated with anti-thyroglobulin antibody titers, and homocysteine levels were negatively correlated with FT3. In the subgroup with TSH >2.5 mU/L, FT4 was positively correlated with ApoA1 and HDL-cholesterol and negatively correlated with lipoprotein(a), while resistin was positively correlated with TSH. In patients with TSH ≤2.5 mU/L, adiponectin levels were negatively correlated with TSH.
CONCLUSION: Our study highlights a complex interrelationship between cardiovascular risk factors in patients with AIT. Patients with AIT and TSH >2.5 mU/L may have a more atherogenic lipid profile.

Title: Combined assessment of fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio and ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic risk stratification of severe multivessel coronary disease in NSTEMI.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual inflammation and dysregulated lipid metabolism are closely associated with the extent of severe multivessel coronary disease (MVD) in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). The fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio (FPR) and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 (ApoB/ApoA1) ratio reflect these two residual risk pathways, respectively, whereas the clinical value of their combined assessment for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD remains to be evaluated.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incremental value of combining FPR with the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI and to develop an adjunctive risk-stratification model.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 580 patients with NSTEMI who underwent coronary angiography. Correlation analyses, logistic regression, and restricted cubic spline models were used to assess the associations between the two biomarkers and MVD. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to evaluate the incremental value of the biomarkers. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to assess net clinical benefit, and subgroup analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: FPR remained independently and positively associated with severe MVD, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship; the association of the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio was attenuated after full adjustment, although it showed complementary value in patients with a very high coronary lesion burden. With the combined model, the AUC increased from 0.683 to 0.719, while the continuous NRI and IDI were 0.488 and 0.037, respectively; adding the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio to the model containing FPR did not significantly improve the AUC (P = 0.266) but yielded further improvements in NRI and IDI. Potential effect modification by diabetes status was observed (P for interaction = 0.025).
CONCLUSION: FPR is an important adjunctive biomarker for the pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI, whereas the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio provides complementary reclassification information. The nomogram incorporating both biomarkers may facilitate pre-angiographic risk stratification.

Title: Early efficacy of oral lipid lowering therapy in achieving LDL-C targets following acute coronary syndrome: A real-world observational study.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity statins are the cornerstone of post-ACS management. Real-world data frequently indicate suboptimal adherence and low attainment of guideline-recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the early efficacy of oral lipid-lowering therapy in achieving LDL-C targets following ACS in a recent cohort of Indian patients.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled 511 statin-naive ACS patients. High-intensity statin monotherapy (atorvastatin 80 mg daily or rosuvastatin 40 mg daily) was initiated following diagnosis. Lipid profile, including total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-C, LDL-C, and VLDL-C, were assessed at baseline, Day 7, Day 14, and Day 28. Primary endpoints included the proportion of patients achieving LDL-C goals at Day 28.
RESULTS: 50.5% of patients achieved the 2019 ESC/EAS LDL-C target (<55 mg/dL) at day 28. Similarly, 68.9% achieved the 2018 ACC/AHA target (<70 mg/dL), and 44.6% achieved the 2020 Lipid Association of India (LAI) target (<50 mg/dL) at day 28. The mean LDL-C reduced from 73.43 ± 13.99 mg/dL at Day 0 to 61.26 ± 27.00 mg/dL at Day 28, corresponding to a 16.6% reduction from baseline. On multivariate analysis, baseline LDL-C, type 2 diabetes mellitus and multivessel coronary disease were found to be independent negative predictors for achieving LDL-C goal <50 mg/dL at day 28.
CONCLUSION: LDL-C target attainment following ACS remains suboptimal despite high-intensity statin therapy, highlighting the need for earlier and more intensive lipid-lowering strategies in high-risk Indian patients.

Title: The value of cardiopulmonary ultrasound in diagnosing cardiogenic pulmonary edema in patients with heart failure.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Heart failure (HF) is generally complicated with cardiogenic pulmonary edema (CPE), the early diagnosis and treatment is essential. We aimed to evaluate the effects of cardiopulmonary ultrasound (CPUS) in the diagnosis of CPE in HF patients, to provide reference for the management of HF.
METHODS: HF patients entering The People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region & Guangxi Academy of Medical Sciences intensive care unit (ICU) between March 2025 and July 2026 were included. All patients underwent CPUS and chest computed tomography (CT), and comparison of the detection rates of cardiogenic pulmonary edema between CPUS and CT.
RESULTS: A total of 117 patients with HF were enrolled in this study. Of the 117 HF patients, 46 were diagnosed with CPE, and 43 were correctly diagnosed by CT, with a diagnostic accuracy of 94.9%, the positive predictive value (PPV) was 93.5%, the negative predictive value (NPV) was 95.8%, the sensitivity was 93.5%, the specificity was 95.8%, the positive likelihood ratio (PLR) was 22, and the negative likelihood ratio (NLR) was 0.07. While 41 were correctly diagnosed by CPUS, with a diagnostic accuracy of 92.3%, the PPV was 91.1%, NPV was 93.1%, the sensitivity was 89.1%, the specificity was 94.3%, the PLR was 16, and the NLR was 0.12. Comparison of CT and CPUS in the diagnosis of CPE, there was no statistically significant difference between the two methods (X 2 = 0.111, P > 0.05). And The Cohen's kappa for the diagnosis of CPE by CT and CPUS is 0.873 (95% CI was 0.782-0.963, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, the present study suggests that CPUS is feasible for identifying cardiogenic pulmonary edema in ICU patients with heart failure. Based on diagnostic agreement analysis, CPUS demonstrates promising performance for CPE detection in this critically-ill cohort.

Title: A simplified Fazekas scale for efficient assessment of white matter hyperintensities.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are key neuroimaging markers of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and are associated with neuropsychiatric symptoms in older adults. Although the Fazekas visual rating scale is widely used in research, its clinical adoption remains limited. Therefore, we developed a simplified Fazekas visual rating scale (sFazekas) for overall WMH assessment to facilitate clinical application.
METHODS: We randomly selected 900 participants from three MRI scanners and evaluated the reliability and scoring efficiency of sFazekas versus the Fazekas scale. Then, all participants were grouped according to the sFazekas scores, and intergroup differences among the different scores were analyzed. Next, we examined correlations among the sFazekas, the Fazekas, and WMH volume. Finally, we explored associations between the sFazekas and vascular risk factors related to CSVD.
RESULTS: The sFazekas demonstrated excellent inter-rater reliability (κ = 0.851) and required significantly less time to complete than the conventional Fazekas (p < 0.01). Significant differences in age, WMH volume, and vascular risk factors were observed across sFazekas score groups (p < 0.01). The sFazekas scores were strongly correlated with Fazekas scores for both deep and periventricular white matter, as well as with WMH volume (p < 0.001). Ordinal logistic regression indicated that age, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and a history of stroke were independent predictors of higher sFazekas scores (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The simplified Fazekas visual rating scale (sFazekas) demonstrates reliability comparable to the conventional Fazekas scale, with the practical advantage of shorter scoring time, suggesting its potential utility in the clinical assessment of overall white matter hyperintensity burden in patients with cerebral small vessel disease.

Title: The impact of an adaptive patient-centered web application on medication optimization in patients with HFrEF: Rationale and design of the SmartHF trial.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Heart failure (HF) remains a significant public health burden, with frequent readmissions often driven by a lack of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) optimization. While clinical decision support (CDS) can improve healthcare processes, patient-centered tools that empower individuals to participate in their own care are increasingly needed. We developed SmartHF, an adaptive web application that provides patients with tailored HFrEF GDMT recommendations based on their clinical data.
METHODS: This 12-week, multicenter randomized controlled trial enrolled adults with HFrEF (LVEF </=40%). Participants were randomized 1:1 to either the SmartHF intervention or usual care. The application uses a computable algorithm to integrate electronic health record (EHR) data, including medications, laboratory results, and vitals, via patient portal authorization. The primary endpoint is the change in a GDMT medication optimization score from baseline to Week 12.
RESULTS: Enrollment concluded in August 2025 with a total of 225 participants. The study population had a mean age of 61.9 years, with 36% identifying as female and 52% as Black or African American. At baseline, 84% of participants were prescribed an ACEi/ARB/ARNI, 90% were on beta-blockers, 67% were prescribed an SGLT2i, while only 53% were on a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA). The mean baseline medication optimization score was 68.5. Final trial results are expected in Winter 2026.
CONCLUSIONS: SmartHF is an innovative, low-touch digital health intervention that leverages EHR integration to facilitate patient-provider discussions on medication optimization. By providing personalized, guideline-based recommendations, the tool aims to improve GDMT prescribing in patients with HFrEF.
CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05858320.

Title: Ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: evidence from human peripheral blood and mouse brain.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) has high morbidity and mortality. Ferroptosis may contribute to aSAH-related brain injury, but its peripheral and brain-associated signatures remain unclear.
METHODS: Human peripheral-blood dataset GSE36791 (43 aSAH, 18 controls) was analyzed using limma, FerrDb intersection, WGCNA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and PPI-based prioritization. qPCR validation was performed in peripheral blood from 10 aSAH patients and 10 non-SAH controls; aSAH samples were collected within 24 h after rupture. Mean ages were 60.2 ± 7.7 and 63.6 ± 8.9 years, with 5 and 4 males, respectively. Brain-level validation used GSE79416 mouse cortex and OMIX006611 mouse SAH single-cell RNA-seq data. Male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks, 20-22 g) underwent cisterna magna autologous blood injection; brain tissues were collected 1 day after SAH (n = 6/group). Immune infiltration and molecular docking were also performed.
RESULTS: Among 2,645 DEGs, 35 were ferroptosis-related. MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD were prioritized as ferroptosis-associated candidate genes and were upregulated in human aSAH peripheral blood, mouse SAH cortex, and the clinical qPCR cohort. Single-cell analysis showed expression of the corresponding mouse genes across annotated brain cell types, especially immune/glial populations. In mouse SAH brain tissue, MAPK3/ERK1, STAT3, PGD, and G6PD protein levels increased, p-STAT3/STAT3 ratio was elevated, MDA content increased, and GPX4 activity decreased. Immune profiling showed increased neutrophils, mast cells, and activated dendritic cells. Ganoderic acid A was prioritized as a preliminary in silico candidate.
CONCLUSION: MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD are ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aSAH, supported by human peripheral-blood, mouse cortex, single-cell, and mouse brain validation. Ganoderic acid A remains an exploratory in silico candidate requiring further functional validation.

Title: Effect of meso-and micro-level quality improvement interventions to improve intrapartum care and birth outcome in Nepal- stepped wedge cluster randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-quality intrapartum care benefits from implementation of quality improvement (QI) interventions. However, scale-up of meso- and micro-level QI interventions to improve health facility performance have shown mixed results in Nepal.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effect of such interventions to intrapartum care and intrapartum mortality (intrapartum stillbirth and first day neonatal death) in public health facilities of Nepal.
STUDY DESIGN: A stepped-wedge cluster randomized design was applied to implement the SUSTAIN package, comprising meso- and micro-level QI interventions in 8 hospitals across all provinces of Nepal over a 21-month period. Each hospital had a 2-month window to introduce QI interventions in their governance and clinical processes. Women with gestational age ≥22 weeks were included with research teams established in each hospital to monitor mortality and health workers' performance. For each outcome, hospital-specific incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated by comparing event rates in the intervention period with those in the control period.
RESULTS: The study enrolled, 55,325 and 53,578 women were enrolled in the control and intervention periods, respectively. The SUSTAIN package resulted in a statistically non-significant reduction (16%) in intrapartum mortality at the hospital level (IRR 0.84 (95% CI: 0.66, 1.08)), while at the individual level there was also statistically non-significant lower odd (37%) of mortality (aOR: 0.63 (0.38, 1.04), P<.0001)). Improvement in intrapartum care were consistent in most of care indicators with adherence to hand-washing increased by 2.36 fold (IRR 2.36 (95% CI: 1.03, 5.39)), fetal heart-rate monitoring increased by 1.55 fold (IRR 1.55 (95% CI: 1.10, 2.17)), delayed cord clamping increased non-significantly by1.14 fold (IRR 1.14 (95% CI: 0.96, 1.35)), immediate skin-to-skin contact increased by 9.92 fold (IRR 9.92 (95% CI: 3.21, 30.64)), early breastfeeding increased by 4.09 fold (IRR 4.09 (95% CI: 2.07, 8.11)), and bag-and-mask within 1 minute increased by 3.30 fold (IRR 3.30 (95% CI: 2.02, 5.40).
CONCLUSION: A synergistic and multi-faceted QI package implementation can improve intrapartum care with a statistically non-significant reduction in intrapartum mortality even during the COVID-19 pandemic.
TRIAL: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN16741720.

Title: Perioperative ASL-derived CBF changes are associated with complications after Moyamoya bypass surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative hyperperfusion and insufficient perfusion augmentation are important contributors to morbidity after revascularization surgery for Moyamoya disease (MMD). Arterial spin labeling (ASL) enables noninvasive assessment of cerebral blood flow (CBF), but the relationship between perioperative ASL-derived CBF changes and specific postoperative complications after direct bypass remains incompletely defined. This study evaluated whether perioperative ASL-derived CBF changes were associated with postoperative complications after direct bypass surgery in patients with MMD.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 146 patients with MMD who underwent first-time direct bypass surgery between June 2020 and October 2024. Preoperative ASL and a standardized postoperative ASL examination on postoperative day 5 were performed, and CBF values were measured in the recipient vascular territory. Subsequent intracranial hemorrhage, cerebral infarction, and postoperative seizures occurring within 90 days after surgery were analyzed. Firth penalized logistic regression was used for the hemorrhage outcome, conventional logistic regression was used for cerebral infarction, and ROC analyses included bootstrap assessment of cutoff uncertainty and 0.632 + bootstrap correction of AUC optimism.
RESULTS: Postoperative intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 8 patients (5.5%), cerebral infarction in 14 patients (9.6%), and postoperative seizures in 9 patients (6.2%); all events occurred after the day-5 ASL examination and within 90 days after surgery. ASL-derived CBF change was associated with postoperative intracranial hemorrhage in Firth penalized logistic regression (OR, 1.219; 95% profile-likelihood CI, 1.102-1.580; p < 0.001). The exploratory cutoff was >43.48 mL/100 g/min, with an apparent AUC of 0.9891 and a 0.632 + corrected AUC of 0.9890. ASL-derived CBF change was inversely associated with postoperative cerebral infarction (OR, 0.885; 95% CI, 0.839-0.933; p < 0.001). The exploratory cutoff was ≤4.48 mL/100 g/min, with an apparent AUC of 0.9150 and a 0.632 + corrected AUC of 0.9150. No significant association was observed between ASL-derived CBF change and postoperative seizures.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative ASL-derived CBF change was associated with hemorrhagic and ischemic complications after direct bypass surgery for MMD. Marked postoperative CBF elevation was observed in patients with intracranial hemorrhage, whereas insufficient perfusion augmentation was associated with cerebral infarction. The proposed thresholds are exploratory, cohort-specific estimates and require external validation before clinical application.

Title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Two-Tined Three-Site Conventional Radiofrequency Ablation of Genicular Nerves for Chronic Knee Pain.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation (GNRFA) has emerged as an effective therapy for chronic knee pain. Although some studies have evaluated its effectiveness, there is limited real-world data on the long-term patient-reported outcome (PRO) data for GNRFAs.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate PROs following conventional GNRFAs performed using two-tined electrodes and the classical three-site technique targeting the superior medial, superior lateral, and inferior medial genicular nerves.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review to gather data from consecutive GNRFAs at an academic medical center from 2016 to 2023. Inclusion criteria were all adult patients who received a conventional GNRFA performed using the classical three-site technique using two-tined electrodes. All included subjects were confirmed to have a positive diagnostic response (≥50% Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) reduction) to a previous genicular nerve block. Primary outcomes were NRS pain scores, Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Global Health, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9).
RESULTS: A total of 31 patients underwent 38 GNRFAs. Relative to the pre-procedure baseline, the average NRS reduction post-procedurally was -3.17 during 0-3 months (p<0.0001), -1.31 during 3-6 months (p<0.05), and -1.92 during 6-12 months (p<0.05). Half of all patients maintained pain relief (NRS reduction greater than or equal to a minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of -2.0) for 11.17 months (95% CI: 7.29, 13.40). Although there was a positive trend for improvement in the quality-of-life measures, no statistically significant post-procedure improvement or worsening was observed during all time periods for PROMIS Physical Health, PROMIS Mental Health, and PHQ-9. Lastly, a history of depression was associated with treatment failure.
CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, conventional GNRFA using the classical three-site technique demonstrated robust short-term pain reduction, and at least half of the cohort maintained clinically meaningful pain improvements for 11 months. For chronic knee pain, GNRFA is a reasonable therapeutic option in appropriately selected patients.

Title: Prospective evaluation of donor-derived cell-free DNA for noninvasive detection of acute rejection in an Asian heart transplant population.
Journal: Transplant international : official journal of the European Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract: Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) is the gold standard for diagnosing post-heart transplant acute rejection (AR) but is invasive. Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) is a promising noninvasive biomarker, yet thresholds for Asian recipients remain undefined. This prospective study enrolled 80 patients, with 299 dd-cfDNA specimens analyzed via a novel Chinese-developed next-generation sequencing assay targeting 48 Indel sites. A reference cohort (n = 42) established post-transplant dd-cfDNA kinetics, while a biopsy cohort (n = 41, 18 acute cellular rejection [ACR], 9 antibody-mediated rejection [AMR], 14 no rejection [NR]) paired with EMB evaluated diagnostic performance. dd-cfDNA peaked at week 1, with a stable trend emerging from week 4 and stable levels reached by week 8. AR patients had significantly higher dd-cfDNA levels than NR patients (0.87% vs. 0.23%, P < 0.001). The optimal composite AR threshold was 0.33% (AUC = 0.874, sensitivity 81.0%, specificity 85.7%). dd-cfDNA decreased post-therapy (P = 0.011) and showed an inverse association with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (P = 0.004). This study provides initial evidence for an assay- and cohort-specific dd-cfDNA threshold (0.33%) for AR detection in Chinese recipients. Given the modest NPV (75.0%), this threshold is better suited for a "rule-in" strategy, and low values should not be used in isolation to defer biopsy. External validation in multicenter cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

Title: Efficacy, safety, and strategy-modifying factors of pulsed field ablation for persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly applied in persistent atrial fibrillation (PerAF) and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation (LSPAF). Previous reviews of mixed AF populations suggested potential advantages in procedural efficiency and esophageal safety, but PerAF/LSPAF-specific evidence on long-term rhythm outcomes and on the value of posterior wall or extended substrate strategies remains limited, with substantial heterogeneity in lesion sets, endpoint definitions, and comparator types.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Scopus through April 18, 2026, with an updated verification search performed in August 2026. Because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity, formal pairwise pooling was restricted to comparisons supported by at least two clinically homogeneous head-to-head studies; single-study comparisons were synthesized narratively, and strategy-level outcomes were explored with single-arm proportion meta-analysis of exact-count cohorts. Off-antiarrhythmic drug (off-AAD) outcomes were prioritized when available. Certainty of evidence was rated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies (approximately 3,100 patients) were included. In an exploratory pooled analysis of the only two available head-to-head comparisons (380 patients, with imbalanced study weights and different lesion sets: PVI-only vs. PVI plus posterior wall isolation), PFA was associated with lower 12-month atrial arrhythmia recurrence than cryoballoon ablation [risk ratio [RR] 0.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-0.98; GRADE certainty: very low]; this is best regarded as a preliminary signal. No statistically detectable difference in major complications was observed between PFA and cryoballoon [risk difference (RD) 0.00, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.02], reflecting absence of a demonstrable difference rather than proven equivalence. Single-study comparisons against radiofrequency ablation (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.45-0.94) and hybrid-convergent ablation (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.67-1.86) yielded directionally discordant results and are presented narratively. Exploratory, non-comparative single-arm analyses yielded pooled 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia of 66.0% (95% CI 55.5%-75.2%; I²=79.0%) for PVI plus posterior wall cohorts and 82.6% (95% CI 76.3%-87.5%; I 2 = 0%) for beyond-PV/extended substrate cohorts; these estimates derive from different, non-randomized cohorts and are hypothesis-generating only.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests favorable efficacy and safety of PFA in PerAF/LSPAF, but certainty is low to very low for all key outcomes. The lower recurrence vs. cryoballoon ablation is an encouraging but preliminary signal requiring confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials with uniform lesion sets. Whether extended substrate strategies improve outcomes cannot be determined from current non-comparative data. Future studies should apply standardized off-AAD endpoints, uniform rhythm monitoring, and stratification by atrial myopathy burden and PFA platform.
