Over two years, MACE per 1000 patient-years were 276.3 for dialysis and 85.9 for transplantation. CKD hospitalization rates were 245.7 and 183.0, with mortality rates of 253.8 and 35.6, respectively. First-year health costs averaged €25,410.4 (SD €17,369.0) for dialysis patients and €4,472.8 (SD €2,859.1) for transplant recipients. Most costs among dialysis and kidney transplant patients were driven by hospitalization, 72.4% and 39.8%, respectively. Indirect costs due to sick leave were also substantial.
CONCLUSION: Non-technique-related costs represent a substantial component of the overall economic burden in patients receiving KRT, largely driven by hospitalizations. These findings provide important context for healthcare planning, although they do not represent total costs of care and should be interpreted as descriptive estimates.

Title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and the risk of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM) in a population of postmenopausal women.
METHODS: A total of 2,859 postmenopausal women from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included, with 4 repeated measurements of night sleep duration collected from 2011 to 2018. Group-based trajectory modeling was adopted to identify distinct sleep duration trajectory patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between sleep trajectories and incident CRMM ascertained between 2018 and 2020. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to validate the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: Three sleep duration trajectory patterns were identified: normal-stable (33.9% of the cohort), normal-fluctuating decline (52.0%), and short-rapid decline (14.1%). During a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome (incident CRMM) occurred in 108 participants (3.8%). Compared with normal-stable group, those in normal-fluctuating decline and short-rapid decline groups had an increased risk of CRMM (ORs of 2.30 [95%CI, 1.35-3.91] and 3.75 [95%CI, 1.99-7.07], respectively) after adjustment for multiple covariates. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations, which were independent of key baseline characteristics and missing data.
CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women, short and declining sleep duration trajectories are strong, independent risk factors for CRMM. Public health and clinical interventions should prioritize maintaining stable, adequate sleep to mitigate multimorbidity risk in this population.

Title: Antihypertensive treatment non-adherence and spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a prospective observational study from Northern India.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a leading cause of stroke-related mortality and long-term disability, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries. Hypertension, and particularly non-adherence to antihypertensive therapy, represents the most important modifiable risk factor. This study aimed to evaluate the epidemiological, clinical, and radiological characteristics of hypertensive ICH and to identify preventable risk factors with public health relevance.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary-care referral center in Northern India between March 2023 and February 2024. Adult patients with non-traumatic spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage were enrolled. Data on demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, antihypertensive treatment adherence, clinical severity, and radiological characteristics were collected and analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: One hundred patients were included (mean age 61.2 ± 12.4 years; 63% male). Hypertension was present in 78% of patients; among these, 70.5% (95% CI 59.6 to 79.5) reported non-adherence to antihypertensive therapy. Active smoking was observed in 62%. Deep hemorrhages involving the basal ganglia (46%) and thalamus (26%) accounted for 72% of cases. Hydrocephalus occurred in 28%. Higher admission blood pressure was observed in patients with larger hematoma volumes.
CONCLUSIONS: Hypertensive ICH in this Northern Indian cohort disproportionately affects individuals in the sixth decade of life and is strongly associated with uncontrolled blood pressure, antihypertensive treatment non-adherence, and tobacco use. Targeted primary prevention through strengthened antihypertensive care and behavioral risk factor programs is essential to reducing the regional burden of this largely preventable condition.

Title: Effects of systemic isotretinoin therapy on tear function and choroidal thickness in nodulocystic acne patients: a prospective comparative study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This research intended to assess how systemic isotretinoin therapy influences subfoveal choroidal thickness (CT) along with superficial (SVD), deep (DVD), and choriocapillaris (CCD) vascular densities in nodulocystic acne patients, utilizing optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA).
METHODS: This prospective, non-randomized comparative study was conducted between April 2024 and July 2025. It included 32 patients with nodulocystic acne who completed a six month course of systemic isotretinoin (Group 1) and 28 patients with nodulocystic acne who did not receive systemic treatment (Group 2). In both groups, SVD, DVD, CCD and subfoveal CT data were obtained using OCTA. All patients underwent the Schirmer test. A post hoc power analysis was performed with G Power software. Data were analyzed with SPSS version 27.0. A p value below 0.05 was considered significant, and a Bonferroni corrected threshold of 0.01 was additionally applied across the five primary between group comparisons.
RESULTS: In Group 1, the average treatment duration was 5.66 ± 1.10 months, with a mean isotretinoin dose of 33.44 ± 10.66 mg/day, the mean cumulative dose was 98.6 ± 44.7 mg per kg. Mean CT was 314.75 ± 55.72 μm in Group 1 and 282.70 ± 48.46 μm in Group 2. This difference was statistically significant (p = 0.022) but did not meet a Bonferroni corrected threshold of 0.01 applied across the five primary comparisons. SVD, DVD, CCD did not differ significantly between groups (p > 0.05). Within Group 1, cumulative isotretinoin dose showed a positive correlation with CT (Spearman rho = 0.403,p = 0.022), which also did not meet the stricter correction threshold used for the correlation analyses. Mean Schirmer values were 14.27 ± 6.76 mm in Group 1 and 20.38 ± 6.71 mm in Group 2. This difference was statistically significant and remained significant after Bonferroni correction (p < 0.001). In Group 1, longer treatment duration was associated with lower Schirmer values within a multivariate model that also included age and drug dose (B=minus 2.96,p = 0.009), although the overall model approached but did not reach the conventional significance threshold (p = 0.055).
CONCLUSIONS: Systemic isotretinoin treatment was associated with a significant reduction in basal tear secretion. CT was significantly greater in the treated group at a conventional significance threshold, with a positive correlation to cumulative drug exposure, although neither finding survived correction for multiple comparisons. No significant differences were found in the retinal vascular density parameters assessed. The results of the study should be interpreted with appropriate caution and considered together with hypotheses for future confirmation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: (NCT07675460) (29.06.2026). Because this was a nonrandomized observational comparison rather than a clinical trial, registration was retrospective and occurred after study completion.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Observational Study

Title: Combined albumin-adjusted ischemia-modified albumin ratio and uterine artery Doppler for differentiating early-onset preeclampsia from gestational hypertension: a prospective exploratory pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distinguishing early-onset preeclampsia (EO-PE) from gestational hypertension (GHT) at initial presentation remains challenging, particularly when classical diagnostic features are absent or evolving. We evaluated whether combining the albumin-adjusted ischemia-modified albumin ratio (IMAR) with uterine artery pulsatility index expressed as multiples of the median (UtA-PI MoM) provides complementary information in this setting.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center exploratory study, 90 singleton pregnancies (30 EO-PE, 30 GHT, 30 controls) were included. IMAR and UtA-PI MoM were assessed individually and in combination using receiver operating characteristic analysis and logistic regression with bootstrap internal validation.
RESULTS: IMAR and UtA-PI MoM were higher in EO-PE than in GHT (p = 0.003 and p < 0.001, respectively), whereas raw IMA did not distinguish the groups. IMAR demonstrated moderate discrimination (AUC 0.727, 95% CI 0.600-0.854), and UtA-PI MoM demonstrated higher performance (AUC 0.844, 95% CI 0.743-0.946). The combined model showed the highest apparent discrimination (AUC 0.898, 95% CI 0.818-0.977; optimism-corrected AUC 0.889), with 83.3% sensitivity and 86.7% specificity at the exploratory operating point.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining IMAR with UtA-PI MoM may provide complementary information for distinguishing EO-PE from GHT at initial presentation. This exploratory model is not intended to replace established angiogenic biomarkers and requires validation in larger, multicenter studies before clinical application.

Title: Intravitreal methotrexate as a prophylactic strategy for proliferative vitreoretinopathy in high-risk retinal detachment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) remains the major cause of surgical failure in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD). This study evaluates the anatomical and functional outcomes, as well as the safety, of a standardized intraoperative intravitreal methotrexate infusion protocol during pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in eyes with early stage PVR (grade B) or with advanced PVR (grade C).
METHODS: A retrospective case series was conducted on 60 consecutive eyes of 59 patients with RRD and PVR grade B (n = 29) or grade C (n = 31) undergoing PPV with adjunct intraoperative methotrexate between November 2024 and February 2026 at a German tertiary center. Methotrexate 40 mg was administered via a 500 mL balanced salt solution infusion. Functional and structural testing included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure, multifocal electroretinogram, perimetry, and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography. The primary outcome measure was single-surgery anatomical success (SSAS) at 12 weeks after primary surgery or after silicone oil removal. Secondary outcomes included BCVA changes and complication rates.
RESULTS: SSAS was achieved in 81.7% of all eyes, with a significantly higher success rate in eyes with PVR grade B compared to PVR grade C (93.1% versus 71.0%; p = 0.043). At 12 weeks, BCVA improved significantly in macula-off cases (p < 0.001) and remained stable in macula-on cases. In an exploratory subset of 17 patients postoperative multifocal electroretinogram and perimetry demonstrated preserved central retinal function. No ocular or systemic adverse events related to methotrexate occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: The standardized intraoperative intravitreal methotrexate infusion protocol was safe, feasible, and associated with high single-surgery reattachment rates, particularly in PVR grade B eyes. Anatomical outcomes in PVR grade C eyes were comparable to other complex PVR cohorts, without any drug-related local or systemic toxicity.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable (retrospective observational study).

Title: Dexmedetomidine-based opioid-sparing anesthesia in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dexmedetomidine has increasingly been incorporated into opioid-sparing anesthetic strategies during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) because of its analgesic properties and minimal respiratory depression. However, dexmedetomidine remains associated with dose-related hemodynamic adverse effects, particularly bradycardia and hypotension. We evaluated whether a reduced-dose dexmedetomidine regimen decreases intraoperative opioid requirements while maintaining acceptable hemodynamic safety during VATS.
METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 68 patients undergoing VATS were randomly assigned to either a dexmedetomidine group or a control group (34 patients each). The dexmedetomidine group received a loading dose of 0.5 µg/kg followed by continuous infusion at 0.5 µg/kg/h during surgery. The control group received conventional fentanyl-based anesthesia. The primary outcome was maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), postoperative respiratory complications, and perioperative safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (18.7 vs. 33.2 µg, P = 0.009). Postoperative pain scores, rescue analgesic requirements, PONV, and respiratory complications were comparable between groups. However, the dexmedetomidine group demonstrated a higher incidence of intraoperative bradycardia (23.5% vs. 0%, P = 0.005) and postoperative hypotension during PACU stay (23.5% vs. 2.9%, P = 0.027). These hemodynamic events were transient and responsive to pharmacologic intervention.
CONCLUSIONS: Dexmedetomidine-based opioid-sparing anesthesia reduced maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl administration during VATS. However, the reduction was modest, was not associated with clear postoperative benefits, and was accompanied by increased bradycardia and hypotension.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05431322), registered on 14 June 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05431322 .

Title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacotherapy is recommended as the first-line treatment for adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), yet some individuals show partial or inadequate response associated with adverse effects. These limitations have prompted interest in adjunctive or alternative interventions. Electroencephalography (EEG) neurofeedback is a non-pharmacological intervention for ADHD, which enables self-regulation of neural activity. This systematic review synthesised clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD, and examined standard versus personalised training protocols.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, four databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, Ovid, Web of Science) were searched from 1960 to October 2025 for this PROSPERO-registered review (ID: CRD420251020898). Eligible studies included adults (≥ 18 years) with a formal ADHD diagnosis undergoing EEG neurofeedback. Outcomes comprised symptom severity, cognitive performance, electrophysiology, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2.
RESULTS: Seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n = 390) met inclusion criteria. Protocols included theta/beta (n = 1), slow cortical potential (n = 1), alpha downregulation training (n = 1) and personalised approaches guided by individual alpha peak frequency (n = 3) or QEEG profiles (n = 1). Naturalistic and personalised studies reported large symptom reductions, whereas RCTs revealed small, generally non-significant effects relative to controls. Cognitive improvements were inconsistently reported and largely attributable to practice effects. Electrophysiological changes were protocol-specific without convergence across studies. No treatment-related adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, small samples, variable controls, inconsistent learning metrics, and risk of bias. Current RCTs do not demonstrate evidence of efficacy over placebo. Blinded, adequately powered trials using standardised learning measures are needed to clarify mechanisms of neurofeedback.

Title: Association of preoperative forced vital capacity with prolonged mechanical ventilation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged mechanical ventilation (PMV) is a serious complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), yet the association between preoperative pulmonary function and PMV risk remains to be comprehensively evaluated.
METHODS: This study included adult patients who underwent isolated CABG with preoperative pulmonary function testing. Predicted forced vital capacity (FVC), predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV₁), and the FEV₁/FVC ratio were assessed for their association with PMV.
RESULTS: Among 1,702 patients, 151 (8.9%) experienced PMV. Patients with PMV were older (65.1 ± 8.5 vs. 62.8 ± 8.8 years, P = 0.003), had higher rates of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (9.9% vs. 5.4%, P = 0.034) and on-pump CABG (8.6% vs. 1.2%, P < 0.001), lower left ventricular ejection fraction (57.1 ± 10.3% vs. 59.1 ± 8.7%, P = 0.007), lower predicted FVC (82.9 ± 14.0% vs. 88.1 ± 14.9%, P < 0.001), and lower predicted FEV₁ (88.7 ± 15.5% vs. 92.6 ± 16.2%, P = 0.007). They also had higher perioperative mortality (4.0% vs. 0.1%, P < 0.001), longer postoperative hospital stays (10.9 ± 4.2 vs. 8.0 ± 2.6 days, P < 0.001), and greater hospitalization costs (25,309.4 [22,119.4-33,359.3] vs. 18,155.4 [16,665.8-20,001.5] USD, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no non-linear relationship between pulmonary function parameters and PMV. After multivariable adjustment, predicted FVC remained independently associated with PMV (odds ratio [OR] 0.97, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.95-0.99, P = 0.005), whereas predicted FEV₁ did not.
CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-tenth of patients undergoing CABG required PMV, which was associated with greater healthcare resource utilization and higher perioperative complications. Predicted FVC, but not predicted FEV₁, is an independent predictor of PMV.

Title: Clevidipine vs. nicardipine in hypertensive crisis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clevidipine and nicardipine are commonly used intravenous calcium channel blockers for the management of hypertensive crises. However, comparative evidence regarding their efficacy and safety remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing intravenous clevidipine and nicardipine in adults with hypertensive crises. The primary outcome was achievement of target blood pressure reduction. Secondary outcomes included medication volume and blood pressure over-reduction. Random-effects models were used, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Three studies involving 599 patients were included. Clevidipine and nicardipine demonstrated comparable achievement of target blood pressure reduction (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.48-1.94; I² = 60%; very low-certainty evidence). Clevidipine was associated with lower odds of blood pressure over-reduction (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93; I² = 0%) and lower medication volume (MD - 258.43 mL, 95% CI - 313.38 to - 203.48 mL; I² = 0%).
CONCLUSION: Clevidipine and nicardipine demonstrated comparable efficacy in achieving target blood pressure reduction in hypertensive crises. Although clevidipine was associated with lower odds of blood pressure over-reduction and lower medication volume, the evidence base was limited and the certainty of evidence for the primary outcome was very low. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and considered hypothesis-generating until confirmed by larger, high-quality randomized controlled trials.

Title: Advancing care coordination to enhance shared care for complex cancer survivors in primary care (ACCESS-PC): protocol for a hybrid type 3 effectiveness-implementation trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer survivors with chronic conditions (e.g., complex cancer survivors) are a growing population that faces greater cancer-specific and cardiovascular disease (CVD) related morbidity and mortality. A shared care model, which involves primary care and cancer clinicians, is the optimal care delivery model for complex cancer survivors. Yet, there is little guidance on how to effectively implement and support complex cancer survivors' continued engagement with primary care during the cancer treatment phase.
METHODS: This protocol describes a multi-phase, mixed methods, stakeholder-engaged research process that tailors and tests a multi-level health system intervention to improve primary care provider and cancer team 'shared care' for complex cancer survivors. This study employs a design-for-dissemination, theory-guided perspective, blending implementation science and care delivery conceptual frameworks: Exploration, Planning, Implementation, and Sustainment (EPIS) and Cancer Multi-team System (cMTS). These frameworks guide our understanding and strategies deployed on the multi-level factors of implementing shared care in a health system. Primary Care Connect (PCC) is a health system intervention designed to align complex cancer survivors, healthcare team members, and health system implementation actors' understandings, capacities, and practices to promote the adoption of shared care delivery models for complex cancer survivors. A hybrid type 3 effectiveness-implementation study design will test the effectiveness of PCC (n = 266 patients) in a patient-level randomized controlled trial on primary care connection, chronic disease management, and patient-reported outcomes. PCC implementation (e.g., feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness) will be evaluated using a mixed methods approach to inform sustainable usage of the intervention. A concurrent learning evaluation will assess PCC's adaptations over time and convene health system stakeholders to explore intervention properties to inform adoption and sustainment considerations.
DISCUSSION: The overarching goal of this protocol is to examine whether cancer survivors becoming "lost in transition" is a preventable problem. PCC tests whether the challenge of transitioning patients back to primary care can be avoided altogether by re-engineering care coordination with primary care at the outset of cancer treatment. Study findings are poised to have a profound impact on the adoption of shared care delivery models throughout the U.S. to optimally mitigate complex cancer survivors' CVD risks.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered with ClinicalTrials.gov on February 19, 2025: NCT06834204.

Title: Comparison of dexmedetomidine and droperidol-fentanyl for asleep-awake-asleep techniques in awake craniotomy anesthesia: a randomized controlled study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In this study, we aimed to compare dexmedetomidine with droperidol-fentanyl during the intraoperative awakening phase of awake craniotomy (AC), focusing on wake-up time.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center randomized controlled trial in China from January 2018 to December 2018. Patients aged 36-60 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-II, scheduled for brain glioma resection, were screened for eligibility; 61 were randomized, and 60 were included in the final analysis. The patients were randomized to either the dexmedetomidine group (intravenous loading dose of dexmedetomidine 0.5 µg·kg- 1 after discontinuation of propofol and remifentanil, followed by a maintenance infusion of dexmedetomidine 0.3-0.5 µg·kg- 1·h- 1) or the droperidol-fentanyl group (intravenous loading doses of fentanyl 2 µg·kg- 1 and droperidol 5 mg after discontinuation of propofol and remifentanil, followed by continuous maintenance infusions of fentanyl 2 µg·kg- 1·h- 1 and droperidol 0.1 mg·kg- 1·h- 1). A wake-up assessment was performed during maintenance of the assigned study regimen. The primary outcome measure was wake-up time. Secondary outcomes included the Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (OAA/S) scale, Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), eloquent brain area mapping status, vital signs, and adverse events.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups. Compared with the droperidol-fentanyl group, the dexmedetomidine group had lower mean arterial pressure at T4-T7, lower heart rate at T1-T4 and T7, and a shorter wake-up time, with a between-group difference of 3.5 min (95% CI, 1.95 to 5.05; P < 0.001). No statistically significant differences were detected in OAA/S scores at wake-up (T2), NRS scores, eloquent area mapping status, or adverse events between the groups.
CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences were detected in OAA/S scores at wake-up or intraoperative brain mapping performance between the two groups. The dexmedetomidine regimen was associated with a shorter measured wake-up time.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR1800014329) was retrospectively registered on 6 January 2018.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Ferritin and LDH predict thrombotic risk beyond conventional scoring systems in DLBCL.
Abstract: Thrombotic events are clinically significant complications in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that adversely affect treatment continuity and outcomes. Despite their importance, no standardized predictive approach exists, and traditional cancer-associated thrombosis models perform suboptimally in hematological malignancies. We retrospectively analyzed 133 adult patients with DLBCL treated at a single center between 2009 and 2021. Thrombotic events required objective radiological confirmation. Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters were compared between patients with and without thrombosis. ROC analysis determined the optimal ferritin cutoff, and Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray competing-risk models (with death as a competing event) identified independent predictors. Thrombosis occurred in 16 patients (12.0%), all venous. Baseline clinical characteristics and the Khorana score did not differ between groups. Patients with thrombosis had significantly higher ferritin (median 331.5 vs. 113 ng/mL; p = 0.026) and LDH (median 459.5 vs. 256 U/L; p = 0.022). ROC analysis identified a ferritin cutoff of ≥ 227 ng/mL (AUC 0.686, 95% CI 0.532-0.840), associated with a 6.1-fold increased risk (OR 6.10, 95% CI 1.75-21.28). In multivariate Cox regression, ferritin ≥ 227 ng/mL (HR 3.77, 95% CI 1.13-12.60, p = 0.031) was an independent predictor and remained significant in competing-risk analysis (sHR 4.68); LDH was significant in Cox analysis (HR 1.002 per unit increase, p = 0.034) but was attenuated in the competing-risk model. In DLBCL, where no standardized thrombosis risk-stratification approach exists, elevated ferritin at diagnosis independently predicted thrombotic events, while LDH was significant in univariate analysis. These readily available parameters may contribute to lymphoma-specific thrombosis scoring systems and warrant prospective validation.

Title: Construction and validation of a predictive model for sleep disorders among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment.
Journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: to construct and validate a risk assessment model for sleep disturbance among rural older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), to support early screening and targeted intervention.
DESIGN: a cross-sectional study using data from the 2024 baseline survey of the Active Aging Cohort in Rural Areas, Shandong Province, China.
SUBJECTS: 1,049 rural older adults aged ≥ 60 years with MCI.
METHODS: demographic, lifestyle, disease history, and psychological factors were collected through face-to-face survey questionnaires and health examinations. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Logistic regression identified independent predictors, which were used to build a nomogram. Model performance was evaluated with ROC curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis, and bootstrap validation.
RESULTS: the prevalence of sleep disturbance was 54.2%. Sex, hypertension, self-rated health, and depression were identified as independent predictors. The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (AUC = 0.759, 95%CI: 0.731-0.778) and calibration, with internal validation confirming robustness.

Title: Association between PM2.5 and coronary artery dilatation with Kawasaki disease in China.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Kawasaki disease is an acute febrile systemic vasculitis that predominantly affects children and can lead to coronary artery dilatation (CAD), coronary artery aneurysm, and/or thrombosis. This study aimed to investigate whether exposure to particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 µm (PM2.5) is associated with an increased risk of CAD. A case-crossover study was conducted to investigate the relationship between PM2.5 exposure and coronary Z value in children. The study included 847 participants from 2017 to 2021. The Z value was calculated for each participant, and PM2.5 exposure levels were assigned. The risk effect of PM2.5 on the Z value was assessed using the distributed lag Poisson generalized linear model. Correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the mechanisms underlying CAD, and sensitivity analysis was conducted to verify the stability of the model. PM2.5 exposure was found to increase the risk of CAD at lag 2-4 days. On the 3rd day of lag, PM2.5 exposure led to the highest risk of CAD, with RR = 1.11, (95%CI = 1.02, 1.21). Mediation analysis showed that PM2.5 may induce CAD through C-reactive protein (CRP), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and hemoglobin (HB), and the effect size was significant, indicating that CRP, ALT and HB were the main mediating factors between PM2.5 and CAD.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that PM2.5 exposure is a potential risk factor for CAD in children. CRP, alanine aminotransferase, and hemoglobin were identified as the main mediators regulating the relationship between PM2.5 and CAD.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • PM2.5 may lead to an increased incidence of Kawasaki disease in children.
WHAT IS NEW: • We found that inhalation of PM2.5 may cause coronary artery dilatation in Kawasaki disease through a population-based cohort study. • This process may be mediated by increasing C-reactive protein. • The model results remained stable after sensitivity analysis.

Title: Cost Analysis of Percutaneous Segmentectomy Versus Chemoembolisation and Radioembolisation in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the costs of percutaneous segmentectomy, a single-session combination of transarterial embolisation and microwave ablation, against chemoembolisation and radioembolisation for hepatocellular carcinoma.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cost analysis of 66 patients treated with percutaneous segmentectomy at five Italian centres, using bottom-up micro-costing. Comparator costs were derived from published Italian per-session costs multiplied by mean sessions per patient, and survival from published curves. A partitioned survival model estimated life-years and incremental net monetary benefit at 50,000 euros per life-year.
RESULTS: Procedural cost per treated patient was 6331 euros for percutaneous segmentectomy, 9792 euros for chemoembolisation (mean 2.94 sessions), and 21,673 euros for radioembolisation (1.52 sessions). At 24 months, percutaneous segmentectomy had lower total cost and a small life-year deficit (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio approximately 70,800 euros per life-year versus chemoembolisation and 57,500 versus radioembolisation, both above threshold). This life-year-adjusted advantage reversed versus chemoembolisation, and became neutral versus radioembolisation, in a worst-case sensitivity analysis, and reversed against both when transplantation costs for the eight transplanted patients (19%) were attributed to percutaneous segmentectomy alone.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, percutaneous segmentectomy appeared to have a lower procedural cost per treated patient than chemoembolisation and radioembolisation, mainly because it is delivered in a single session. However, because costing routes, cohorts, and survival sources were not equivalent and the life-year-adjusted comparison was not robust, no formal cost superiority can be established. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective, matched studies.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Retrospective Cohort Study with Historical Comparators.

Title: Effects of inhaled nitric oxide during mechanical circulatory support: a prospective pilot study.
Abstract: Among patients with cardiogenic shock receiving Impella-based mechanical circulatory support, pulmonary vascular load and right ventricular dysfunction may affect left ventricular preload and device flow. Prospective data on the acute hemodynamic effects of inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) in this setting are limited. We evaluated short-term hemodynamic changes after iNO initiation in patients receiving Impella or Impella combined with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECPELLA) support. We conducted a prospective single-center pilot study of adult patients receiving Impella or ECPELLA support who were treated with iNO. iNO was initiated at 20 ppm after initial circulatory resuscitation once pulmonary artery pulse pressure could be reliably assessed. Hemodynamic variables were recorded immediately before iNO initiation (T0) and 30 min (T1) and 24 h (T2) after initiation. The primary endpoint was the change in mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) from T0 to T1. We enrolled 11 patients, and 10 were analyzed. mPAP decreased from 19.0 (14.8-20.3) mmHg at T0 to 16.5 (12.8-19.3) mmHg at T1 (P = 0.004). The T0-T2 difference was not significant. Lactate levels decreased, but this temporal change could not be attributed directly to iNO without a control group. Methemoglobin levels increased slightly at T2 without clinical methemoglobinemia. iNO was temporally associated with an early reduction in mPAP in patients receiving Impella-based support, without clear improvement in systemic hemodynamic indices. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger controlled studies.

Title: Association between dietary patterns and the dental caries experience among postmenopausal women.
Abstract: Aims To examine the association between dietary patterns and the decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT) score cross-sectionally and prospectively among postmenopausal women.Methods Study sample included postmenopausal women enrolled in the OsteoPerio study. Dietary patterns, including the Healthy Eating Index (HEI)-2020, Alternative HEI (AHEI)-2010, dietary approaches to stop hypertension, and alternate Mediterranean Diet (aMed), were scored based on two food frequency questionnaires administered across three years preceding baseline (1997-2001). Dental examinations at baseline and year five assessed 28 teeth (excluding third molars). Numbers of DMFT were aggregated according to the World Health Organization's definition. Cross-sectional associations of dietary pattern scores with decayed teeth, missing teeth, and filled teeth, and DMFT at baseline (n = 1,214) and prospective associations with changes in MT and DMFT (n = 934) were examined.Results Cross-sectionally, higher HEI, AHEI, and aMed scores were associated with less MT (rate ratios: 0.93, 0.91, and 0.96, respectively) and less DMFT (ß: -0.32, -0.50, and -0.23, respectively). No significant prospective associations were observed.Conclusions In this group of postmenopausal women, better adherence to healthy dietary patterns was associated with fewer prevalent dental caries but not with the progression in five years.

Title: Real-world renoprotective effects of polyethylene glycol-loxenatide in type 2 diabetes: a multicenter, ambispective cohort study.
Abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

Title: Weight Regain After Incretin Treatment: The Lean Mass Deficit Hypothesis and a Role for Testosterone Combination Therapy in Men.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1RA and triple (GIP)/GLP-1RA/glucagon agonists achieve placebo-subtracted weight loss of 15% to 22%. Their long-term value depends on how well the weight loss is maintained and on the composition of weight loss, not only amount of weight loss. Part of incretin-induced weight loss is lean tissue. It is unknown whether the proportion of lean mass, and especially, muscle mass loss is greater than with other weight-loss interventions, and whether it may cause clinically meaningful harm. Men with obesity commonly have low or low-normal testosterone, which is associated with reduced muscle mass, increased visceral adiposity, impaired insulin sensitivity, and increased cardiovascular risk.
HYPOTHESIS: We propose, as an exploratory hypothesis, that in men with obesity and low testosterone, combining incretin therapy with testosterone therapy may preserve muscle mass, increase the proportion of weight lost as fat mass, and reduce fat-predominant weight regain after incretin discontinuation.
RATIONALE: Resistance exercise and adequate protein intake are first-line measures for preserving muscle mass during weight loss. No lifestyle measure reliably prevents the fat-predominant weight regain that follows diet discontinuation, and long-term adherence to lifestyle interventions is poor. We position testosterone therapy as a pharmacological adjunct for weight loss maintenance in men with obesity and low testosterone, to be evaluated in clinical trials.
CONCLUSIONS: The only direct human data come from a small, non-randomized pilot study and are hypothesis-generating. The clinical consequences of incretin-associated loss of lean mass, and particularly muscle mass, should be investigated in future studies. The hypothesis requires evaluation in randomized controlled trials that properly assess changes in lean mass and muscle mass, along with safety monitoring, before it can inform clinical practice.

Title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Insulin Degludec Versus Insulin Glargine in Trial-Eligible and Ineligible Populations: A DEVOTE-Inspired Target Trial Emulation Using the Swedish National Diabetes Register.
Abstract:
AIMS: To compare cardiovascular outcomes associated with the initiation of insulin degludec versus insulin glargine using a target trial emulation approach in nationwide real-world data.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a nationwide observational cohort study using Swedish health registers, including the National Diabetes Register. Individuals with type 2 diabetes initiating insulin degludec or insulin glargine between 2012 and 2022 were included. Two complementary approaches were applied: a trial-eligible emulation cohort reflecting the eligibility criteria of the DEVOTE trial, and a trial-ineligible emulation cohort representing routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, i.e., myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular mortality). Secondary outcomes included the individual components of MACE, all-cause mortality and heart failure. Average treatment effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation.
RESULTS: Among 96 731 individuals identified, 44 890 met the study eligibility criteria and were included in the analyses. In the trial-eligible cohort, degludec was associated with a similar risk of MACE compared with glargine (risk ratio: 1.10; 95% CI: 0.91-1.34; p = 0.34), but a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.62-0.92; p = 0.002). In the trial-ineligible emulation cohort, degludec was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.67-0.95; p = 0.004) as well as reduced risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal stroke and heart failure.
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study, degludec was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with glargine, consistently observed in both trial-eligible and trial-ineligible populations, despite similar cardiovascular risk in the trial-eligible cohort.

Title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.
RESULTS: In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.

Title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).
OBJECTIVES: To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.
METHODS: We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.
RESULTS: Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).
CONCLUSIONS: In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.

Title: Considering counterfactual prediction models in sleep research: A demonstration of incident stroke prediction in an observational cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Data-driven risk prediction algorithms are increasingly common. However, studies suggesting that a single set of variables are most "important" within a given risk prediction model ignore the reality that other equally useful models containing entirely different features may exist. We aim to use a novel approach (Model Path Selection) to demonstrate that, for any given health outcome, there are likely many comparable counterfactual models including different sets of variables. We focus on incident stroke as a scientifically meaningful outcome to motivate this demonstration.
METHODS: Model Path Selection uses an iterative model-building procedure to illustrate a set of counterfactual prediction models ("paths"). We applied Model Path Selection to Sleep Heart Health Study data (N = 4,512 adults) to predict 5-year incident stroke, considering 30 features comprising demographics, self-reported and measured medical risk factors, polysomnography, and self-reported sleep. Area Under the Curve was estimated for each resulting path based on 10-fold cross-validation.
RESULTS: Model Path Selection identified 61 unique counterfactual models. 13 of these achieved Area Under the Curves between 0.81 and 0.82. Area Under the Curves of the remaining models ranged from 0.53 to 0.68 (median 0.61). All 13 top models included age plus various combinations of other features (polysomnography indices, body mass index, and/or the Short Form 36 mental and physical component scores).
CONCLUSIONS: Model Path Selection can illuminate counterfactual prediction models, differentiate features that may be uniquely predictive from those that can be swapped out with other features, enhance reproducibility, inform the design of clinically practical predictive tools, and suggest sleep-related risk factors to be targeted for health promotion.

Title: [Pulmonary rehabilitation: A 2026 updated expert consensus].
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The effectiveness of pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is supported by a high level of evidence. More recently, the indications for PR have expanded and new models of care have emerged.
STATE OF ART: This position statement summarizes recent evidence on PR regarding: 1) its objectives; 2) the key outcomes to be assessed at baseline, during, and at the end of the program, along with the recommended assessment tools; 3) its integration within the care pathway; 4) modalities of implementation, including home-based programs, telerehabilitation, and hybrid formats; 5) its core components, based on therapeutic education (including psychosocial and motivational support), exercise training, and adapted physical activity; and 6) the strategies and professionals involved in maintaining long-term benefits.
PERSPECTIVES: The extension of PR indications to other respiratory conditions (interstitial lung diseases, pulmonary hypertension, thoracic oncology) and the development of new delivery models are expected to facilitate PR access.
CONCLUSION: This position statement from French-speaking experts aims to support greater recognition of PR and to promote its integration into patient care pathways.

Title: Incremental reach of 30-year PREVENT-ASCVD risk assessment in adults with MASLD and low 10-year risk: population implications of the 2026 dyslipidemia guideline.
Journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Low 10-year ASCVD risk can coexist with substantial long-horizon risk in younger adults. The 2026 dyslipidemia guideline introduced 30-year PREVENT-ASCVD risk ≥10% as a criterion for considering moderate-intensity statin therapy in adults aged 30-59 years with 10-year risk <3%. We aimed to quantify the population scale and incremental classification reach of this criterion among U.S. adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed NHANES 2017-March 2020 and August 2021-August 2023 as independent complex surveys. Adults aged 30-59 years with VCTE-defined operational MASLD, no clinical ASCVD, no lipid-lowering therapy, LDL-C 70-189 mg/dL, no observable automatic-treatment indication, and 10-year PREVENT-ASCVD risk <3% were included. G1 was defined as 30-year risk ≥10% with LDL-C <160 mg/dL. The complete primary cores included 529 and 303 participants. G1 prevalence was 33.3% and 27.9%, representing 5.85 and 4.50 million U.S. adults. Among participants leaving G0 through either the long-horizon or LDL-C 160-189 mg/dL criterion, 85.7% and 75.1% were identified uniquely by 30-year risk. In the broader operational MASLD pathway, G1 accounted for 15.8% and 13.9% of the weighted distribution and was more concentrated than in confirmed non-MASLD. Findings were stable across alternative specifications and neighboring thresholds.
CONCLUSION: Among adults with operational MASLD who remained at low 10-year ASCVD risk, the 30-year PREVENT criterion identified a substantial population not captured by the parallel LDL-C 160-189 mg/dL pathway and accounted for most downstream classification beyond G0. These findings define the disease-specific population reach of long-horizon risk assessment in MASLD.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

Title: Time-matched Secondary Fracture Prevention in Older Adults: A Narrative Review of Imminent Risk, Time-to-Benefit, and Treatment Sequencing.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: After a fragility fracture, subsequent fracture risk is highest during the first 6 to 12 months and remains elevated for 1 to 2 years. Anti-osteoporosis therapies differ in onset, persistence, discontinuation kinetics, and safety constraints, yet guidelines rarely operationalize treatment timing within this imminent-risk period. This narrative review examines temporal mismatch between post-fracture risk and treatment effect and proposes a time-matched secondary fracture prevention framework.
METHODS: We conducted an argument-driven narrative review using a structured, non-systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar from January 2000 through July 26, 2026. English-language guidelines, pivotal randomized trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and implementation or health-services studies relevant to secondary fracture prevention were included, with priority given to 2024 to 2026 publications. Selection was purposive; no formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled statistical analysis was performed.
FINDINGS: The evidence base comprised 103 publications and one trial-registry record. Subsequent fractures consistently clustered within the first 12 to 24 months after an index fracture. A pooled meta-analysis of bisphosphonate trials in postmenopausal osteoporosis estimated 12.4 months (95% CI, 6.3 to 18.4 months) to prevent one nonvertebral fracture per 100 treated women; this population-level estimate is not a drug-specific onset threshold and was not derived specifically from recent-fracture patients. Several injectable antiresorptive and bone-forming therapies show early fracture-risk reduction in pivotal trials, but treatment choice must remain safety qualified. In particular, romosozumab requires cardiovascular risk assessment because of the imbalance in serious cardiovascular events observed in ARCH and current labeling restrictions. Rare medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw and denosumab-associated hypocalcemia in advanced chronic kidney disease are additional counseling and monitoring considerations. Treatment cessation is also time-sensitive, especially for denosumab because delayed dosing or discontinuation without follow-on therapy can lead to rebound bone turnover and vertebral fractures.
IMPLICATIONS: Secondary fracture prevention may be improved by initiating appropriate therapy promptly after the index fracture, matching treatment characteristics to the period of highest risk, planning sequential therapy from the outset, and minimizing delivery delays. The framework is hypothesis-generating and should not override drug-specific contraindications, local labeling, or individualized benefit-risk assessment. Prospective studies should test whether explicitly time-matched care reduces early re-fracture compared with conventional risk-stratified treatment.

Title: Evaluation of Inpatient Epoetin Alfa Dosing in Patients With Anemia of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Epoetin alfa labeling and clinical guidelines recommend weight-based dosing for the management of patients with anemia and chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, fixed dosing continues to be used in inpatient practice, and comparative data in hospitalized populations are limited. This study aimed to compare fixed versus weight-based dosing in hospitalized patients with CKD.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included hospitalized adult patients with anemia of CKD who were initiated on epoetin alfa at a large academic medical center between January 2014 and August 2024. The primary outcome was hemoglobin exceeding targets (>10 g/dL for non-dialysis-dependent CKD and >11 g/dL for dialysis-dependent CKD). Secondary outcomes included 90-day all-cause mortality, rehospitalization, major adverse cardiovascular events, packed red blood cell transfusion, new or worsening hypertension, and iron deficiency.
FINDINGS: Among 100 patients (50 in the fixed-dose group and 50 in the weight-based dose group), hemoglobin exceeded targets in 8% and 4% of patients, respectively (P = 0.678). Ninety-day all-cause mortality occurred in 18% and 4% of patients, respectively (P = 0.160); no statistically significant differences were observed in other secondary outcomes. Fixed-dose regimens resulted in higher weight-normalized epoetin alfa doses than weight-based dosing (119.8 vs 67.1 units/kg; P < 0.001).
IMPLICATIONS: Among hospitalized patients with CKD, fixed-dose epoetin alfa was associated with substantially higher weight-normalized doses and numerically higher rates of hemoglobin exceeding targets and mortality, though differences in clinical outcomes were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that adherence to guideline-recommended weight-based dosing may minimize excessive epoetin alfa dosing. Larger prospective studies are needed to clarify optimal inpatient erythropoiesis-stimulating agent dosing.

Title: Perioperative Management for Placement of Patent Ductus Arteriosus Stents in Infants With Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Circulation.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Stenting of the patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) offers a minimally invasive alternative to the modified Blalock-Thomas-Taussig shunt in infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow. This study reviews the periprocedural management of infants undergoing ductal stenting in the cardiac catheterization laboratory.
DESIGN: A retrospective single-center review.
SETTING: Quaternary children's hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Infants receiving PDA stents in the cardiac catheterization laboratory from 2018 to 2021 were included.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included; median age was 5 days [1-62]; 95.6% (65/68) were neonates and 23.5% (16/68) premature. Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum was the most common cardiac diagnosis (n = 23, 33.8%); 22.1% (15/68) presented with a syndrome and 35.3% (24/68) with noncardiac comorbidities. In total, 39.7% (27/68) developed intraoperative events. Median time to extubation was 19.4 hours [3.2-372.5].
CONCLUSIONS: Infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow undergoing ductal stenting may present with a wide range of challenges in the perioperative period. Meticulous care and interdisciplinary coordination are required to optimize the outcomes for this particularly vulnerable patient group.

Title: New Dialysis-Dependent Renal Failure After Durable LVAD Implantation: Risk Factors and Potential Targets for Improvement.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify preoperative predictors of postoperative renal replacement therapy (RRT) in patients undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation to help guide interventions that could decrease the incidence of new dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI).
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: A single-center, university hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: There were 159 adult patients undergoing LVAD implantation between July 2012 to July 2024 INTERVENTIONS: Retrospective analysis of preoperative variables, including hemoglobin, creatinine, MELD score, and intraoperative RBC transfusion volume and their effect on the primary outcome of new dialysis-dependent AKI.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: New dialysis-dependent AKI occurred in 17% of patients. Preoperative hemoglobin was inversely associated with RRT risk; every 1-g/dL increase was associated with a 21% reduction in odds ratio (OR 0.79; CI 0.65-0.97, p = .023). Intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volume was a major predictor, with patients receiving 0 to 5 units having significantly lower OR than those receiving ≥11 units (OR 0.01; 95% CI 0.001-0.11; p < .001). MELD scores between 10 and 20 also increased the OR (OR 3.10; 95% CI 1.07-9.00; p = .038). Additionally, needing new dialysis was strongly associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation (OR 8.76; 95% CI 2.52-30.5; p = .001) and postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding (OR 3.73; 95% CI 1.48-9.40; p = .005).
CONCLUSION: Preoperative hemoglobin and perioperative red blood cell transfusion volume are significant and potentially actionable, modifiable risk factors for postoperative RRT in LVAD recipients. Optimizing preoperative hemoglobin may offer a targeted strategy to reduce RRT rates in this high-risk population.

Title: Sex differences in lipid-lowering therapy after atherothrombotic ischemic stroke: The multicenter MaLIC study.
Journal: Clinica e investigacion en arteriosclerosis : publicacion oficial de la Sociedad Espanola de Arteriosclerosis
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women have poorer outcomes after ischaemic stroke. The primary objective was to assess sex-based differences in the management and intensity of lipid-lowering therapy following non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA). Secondary objectives were to analyse sex-based differences in vascular risk profile, pre-event functional status, and stroke severity.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: Subanalysis of the second phase of the MaLIC study (Management of Stroke in Catalonia and the Balearic Islands), a prospective, multicentre study conducted in 20 hospitals. Adults with non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or TIA were included. Vascular risk factors, stroke severity, lipid profile, and intensity of lipid-lowering therapy at hospital discharge were compared according to sex.
RESULTS: A total of 591 patients were included, of whom 223 (37.7%) were women. Women were older (76 vs. 70 years; P<.0001), had greater pre-event functional dependence (mRS>2: 16.1% vs. 7.9%; P=.003), and a lower prevalence of ischaemic heart disease (4.9% vs. 14.4%; P<0001) and peripheral arterial disease (6.3% vs. 13.0%; P=.01). Although women had higher LDL cholesterol levels at admission (103.5 vs. 92mg/dl; P=.004), they were less frequently prescribed high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy at discharge (64.1% vs. 72.3%; P=.04). No differences were observed in stroke code activation or reperfusion therapies.
CONCLUSIONS: Women were less frequently prescribed high-intensity lipid-lowering therapy at discharge than men, despite having higher LDL cholesterol levels. These findings highlight an opportunity to optimise lipid-lowering therapy after the cerebrovascular event.

Title: [Application of Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction technique in chronic limb wounds following popliteal artery injury].
Journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effectiveness of Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction combined with debridement and dressing changes in the treatment of chronic limb wounds after popliteal artery injury.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 24 patients with chronic limb wounds after popliteal artery injury who were admitted between January 2023 and June 2025 and met the selection criteria. There were 15 males and 9 females, aged 24-79 years (mean, 52.6 years). Causes of injury included traffic accident injury in 16 cases, mechanical injury in 6 cases, and fall from height in 2 cases. The time from injury to revascularization ranged from 4 to 16 hours (mean, 9.6 hours). There were 29 wounds in total, with wound sizes ranging from 3 cm×2 cm to 12 cm×9 cm. Among them, 18 wounds in 16 patients were persistent chronic wounds after injury, and 11 wounds in 8 patients were recurrent muscle liquefaction wounds after healing of the limb soft tissue. Wound reconstruction was performed sequentially using debridement, continuous dressing changes, Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction, and other methods. The external fixation configuration for soft-tissue distraction was individually assembled according to wound location and morphology. Wound healing, limb salvage rate, complications, and limb functional recovery were observed.
RESULTS: Of the 29 wounds in 24 patients, 28 ultimately healed, with a healing rate of 96.6%. Limb salvage was successful in 23 patients, with a limb salvage rate of 95.8%; 1 patient underwent amputation due to severe ischemic necrosis of the limb caused by thrombosis, with an amputation rate of 4.2%. All patients were followed up 12-29 months (mean, 24.1 months); 17 had more than 2 years of follow-up. The Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) score was 58-85 (mean, 72.4); Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS) score was 32-68 (mean, 58.6). Twenty-two patients recovered two-point discrimination (range, 10-40 mm), and 2 patients recovered protective sensation.
CONCLUSION: Ilizarov soft-tissue distraction technique combined with debridement and dressing changes can effectively promote the healing of chronic limb wounds after popliteal artery injury, improve the limb salvage rate and limb function, representing a feasible treatment strategy.

Title: Directional OCT Assessment of Henle's Fiber Layer in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of Henle's fiber layer (HFL) in eyes with mild to moderate primary open-angle glaucoma and to compare its performance with established optical coherence tomography (OCT) parameters, including the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL).
DESIGN: Retrospective cross-sectional study.
PARTICIPANTS: Twenty-five eyes of 25 patients with mild to moderate primary open-angle glaucoma and 50 age- and sex-matched healthy control eyes.
METHODS: Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) was used to obtain macular and peripapillary measurements. HFL was visualized with directional OCT and quantified using ImageJ within a standardized 6,000-μm horizontal region centered on the fovea. One eye from each participant was included in the analysis to avoid inter-eye correlation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate diagnostic accuracy.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: HFL area and its ability to distinguish glaucomatous eyes from healthy controls in comparison with RNFL and GC-IPL measurements.
RESULTS: HFL area was significantly smaller in glaucomatous eyes than in healthy controls (p < 0.001). ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic accuracy for HFL (AUC, 0.990; 95% confidence interval, 0.974-1.000). HFL showed higher diagnostic performance than average RNFL and GC-IPL in DeLong analysis. All GC-IPL parameters and selected RNFL quadrants were significantly thinner in the glaucoma group (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: HFL was significantly reduced in eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma and showed high diagnostic accuracy. HFL assessment may provide complementary information about retinal structural changes in glaucoma. Because of the relatively small sample size, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

Title: Comparative Effectiveness of Rehabilitation Nursing Interventions in Patients With Post-Stroke Dysphagia: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Japan journal of nursing science : JJNS
Abstract:
AIM: To compare the effectiveness of rehabilitation interventions integrated into nursing care on swallowing function and safety in patients with post-stroke dysphagia.
METHODS: We searched Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, ProQuest, CINAHL, PubMed, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating rehabilitation nursing interventions for patients with post-stroke dysphagia, from database inception to September 2025. The primary outcomes were the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) and the Penetration-Aspiration Scale (PAS), while secondary outcomes included the Videofluoroscopic Dysphagia Scale (VDS) and the Swallowing Quality of Life Scale (SWAL-QOL).
RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs were included. Rehabilitation nursing interventions were more effective than conventional care in improving FOIS, PAS, and VDS. For FOIS, kinesiology taping (KT) combined with neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) (surface under the cumulative ranking curve [SUCRA] = 78.7%, mean rank = 2.7) and respiratory muscle training (RMT) (SUCRA = 78.1%, mean rank = 2.9) ranked highest. For PAS, KT combined with NMES (SUCRA = 95.9%, mean rank = 1.3) and KT (SUCRA = 84.1%, mean rank = 2.1) ranked highest.
CONCLUSIONS: Rehabilitation nursing interventions may improve swallowing function and safety in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. RMT, KT, and KT + NMES showed potential benefits for different aspects of swallowing recovery. However, the superiority of KT + NMES requires confirmation in high-quality multicenter RCTs with head-to-head comparisons and long-term follow-up.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ID: CRD420251155222.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study; Review

Title: Carotid Body Detection Rate and Size on Photon-Counting Versus Energy-Integrating Detector CT.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the carotid body (CB) detection rate and size measured on photon-counting CT (PCCT) versus energy-integrating detector CT (EIDCT), and to evaluate the effects of laterality and contrast phase.
METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at a single institution on 48 adult patients who underwent head and neck CTA on both PCCT and EIDCT on arterial and venous phase imaging. CB detection was analyzed as a binary outcome using a mixed-effects logistic regression model with modality, phase, side, and modality-by-phase interaction as fixed effects, and patient as a random effect. CB size was analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with the same fixed effects and patient as a random effect. Sensitivity analysis for CB size adjusted for age, sex, and hypertension.
RESULTS: CB detection rates were higher on PCCT than on EIDCT, particularly on the right side (arterial, 96% vs 77%; venous, 96% vs 82%), and slightly higher on the left side (arterial, 85% vs 81%; venous, 83% vs 82%). In mixed-effects logistic regression, PCCT was associated with higher odds of CB detection than EIDCT (OR, 3.97; P = .009). CB size was significantly smaller when measured on PCCT than on EIDCT (estimated difference, -2.7 mm³; P = .01). The right CB was larger than the left across modalities (estimated difference, +4.7 mm³; P < .001). There was no significant difference in CB measurements between arterial and venous phases (P = .53), and no significant modality-by-phase interaction (P = .98). In sensitivity analysis, the modality and side effects remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, and hypertension.
CONCLUSION: PCCT improves CB detection compared with EIDCT but yields smaller CB measurements. CB size is greater on the right than on the left, with minimal effect of contrast phase. These findings remained robust after adjustment for age, sex, and hypertension.

Title: Laparoscopic Versus Laparotomy for Cytoreductive Surgery in Advanced Ovarian Cancer: A Prospective Cohort Study Comparing Surgical Outcomes, Postoperative Complications, Quality of Life, and Survival.
Journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare surgical outcomes, postoperative complications, quality of life, and survival between laparoscopic surgery and laparotomy for cytoreductive surgery in patients with advanced ovarian cancer.
METHODS: This cohort study included 60 patients with FIGO Stage III-IV advanced ovarian cancer, allocated to the control group or the study group. Quality of life was measured. Overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and progression-free survival (PFS) were analyzed.
RESULTS: Laparoscopic surgery significantly reduced operative time, blood loss, time to bowel recovery, and chemotherapy initiation. It also resulted in higher lymph node yield and optimal cytoreduction rate. Postoperative complication rates, including hypokalemia, hypoproteinemia, wound infection, and venous thrombosis, were significantly lower in the laparoscopic group. Quality of life improved significantly post-treatment in the laparoscopic group. Five-year OS rates were 75.0% vs. 51.9% (p = 0.055), DFS rates were 75.0% vs. 51.9% (p = 0.057), and PFS rates were 75.0% vs. 51.9% (p = 0.072) for laparoscopic and laparotomy groups, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed trends favoring the laparoscopic group, with OS approaching statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Laparoscopic cytoreductive surgery in advanced ovarian cancer improves perioperative outcomes, reduces complications, and enhances postoperative recovery while maintaining comparable long-term survival outcomes to laparotomy.

Title: Prenatal Maternal Phosphatidylcholine and Children's Behavior and Cognition through 4 Years of Age: Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: American journal of obstetrics and gynecology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increasing popularity of choline supplements may prompt patients to seek advice on safe, effective doses during prenatal visits. Rationale for prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements stems from the fetal developmental role of α7-nicotinic cholinergic receptor gene CHRNA7, associated with Schizophrenia, Attention Deficit Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder. Fetal brain developmental problems, including those linked to CHRNA7, convey risk for these mental illnesses. Choline derived from maternal phosphatidylcholine intake activates fetal α7-nicotinic receptors, which facilitate brain neurosynaptic development, observed after birth as robust inhibition of cerebral neurophysiological responses to repeated stimuli. A previous study found that maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo significantly improved newborns' neurophysiology and thereby decreased the children's attention and social withdrawal problems at 40 months of age.
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo in a larger randomized clinical trial supports fetal brain development to decrease childhood attention and social behavioral problems and increase cognitive performance.
STUDY DESIGN: A clinical trial at University of Colorado Hospital Prenatal Clinics and affiliated community hospitals randomized 206 women to 9000 mg phosphatidylcholine (the form of choline occurring naturally in food) or placebo from 16 weeks' gestation through delivery. From 18 months to 4 years of age, 142 children were assessed by parents on the Child Behavior Check List 1.5-5-year version (CBCL1.5-5yr). The 2 primary outcomes were Withdrawn and Attention Problems. A secondary outcome was the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-IV Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (Full Scale-IQ). Cerebral neurophysiological inhibition, assessed soon after birth, confirmed phosphatidylcholine's fetal developmental effects.
RESULTS: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements compared to placebo produced fewer children with multiple or pervasive Withdrawn problems and increased WPPSI-IV Full-Scale IQ (mean difference 7.78, 95% CI 1.88, 13.7; p = .010). Attention problems did not decrease significantly. In exploratory analyses, 11 children had CBCL1.5-5yr Autism Spectrum T-scores in the clinical referral range and language deficits typical of Autism Spectrum Disorder, 10 of 71 from women who had placebo and 1 of 71 who had phosphatidylcholine, Risk Ratio 10.0; 95% CI 1.31, 76.1; p = .026. Twelve children had Full-Scale IQ > 120 (>90 %ile), 10 of 54 from women who had phosphatidylcholine and 2 of 49 who had placebo, Risk Ratio 4.54; 95% CI 1.05, 19.7; p = .044. Positive effects were observed regardless of presence or absence of maternal mental disorders. Phosphatidylcholine produced no significant adverse effects or safety problems for women or children. Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and hypertension were not increased. The children had normal physical parameters at birth and through childhood. Several limitations temper the study's findings: effects on Attention problems did not reach significance, parents rated social behavior, and one-third of women were lost between prenatal enrollment and 4-year assessments.
CONCLUSION: Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements provide safe, effective support of fetal brain development. Comparison of doses from this and previous trials suggests 6300 mg phosphatidylcholine or 900 mg choline, beginning as early as possible in gestation. Outcomes for the children include fewer social withdrawal problems and increased cognitive test performance.

Title: Association of Occupational Noise Exposure with Hypertension and the Mediating Role of Metabolic Dysregulation: A Combined Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence linking occupational noise to hypertension remains inconsistent, and potential metabolic pathways are insufficiently characterised.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 70,759 workers in Jiangsu Province and a retrospective five-year cohort analysis of 2,188 workers. We combined multivariable regression, machine-learning prediction, mediation analysis, and longitudinal modelling to examine associations and potential pathways.
RESULTS: Hypertension prevalence was 28.19%. Compared with unexposed workers, noise exposure of 70-< 85 dB(A) and 85-< 90 dB(A) was associated with higher hypertension odds (OR = 1.16 and 1.21, p < 0.001), whereas the association at ≥ 90 dB(A) was not significant after adjustment. XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance (AUC=0.84), with metabolic indicators including triglycerides, glucose, and γ-glutamyl transferase ranking among the important predictors, while noise exposure also contributed to prediction. Mediation analyses identified potential indirect pathways involving γ-glutamyl transferase, glucose, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the association between occupational noise exposure and systolic blood pressure. Longitudinal analyses showed delayed divergence in metabolic markers and larger systolic blood pressure differences during the later follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS: Occupational noise exposure was associated with elevated blood pressure even at levels below the Chinese occupational noise exposure limit of 85 dB(A) for an 8-hour working day, which is primarily intended to prevent noise-induced hearing loss. The findings are consistent with a potential role of oxidative stress-related glucose and lipid metabolic dysregulation in this association. Future occupational health strategies should incorporate longitudinal metabolic surveillance to mitigate noise-induced risks in exposed populations.

Title: Visualization of post-STEMI myocardial infarction and microvascular obstruction with non-contrast, free-breathing whole- heart iT2prep-IR BOOST.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical adoption of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for risk stratification in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is often limited by long scan times and the requirement for breath-holding and contrast agents.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to validate a non-contrast, free-breathing 3D whole-heart T1/T2 CMR method (iT2prep-IR BOOST) for rapid assessment of myocardial injury in STEMI patients, hypothesizing that this technique provides promising diagnostic accuracy and quantitative assessment to conventional contrast-enhanced CMR.
METHODS: A free-breathing 3D isotropic whole-heart iT2prep-IR BOOST sequence was performed with a scan time of <8minutes.
