This review incorporates the most recent data on psilocybin's chemistry, pharmacology, metabolism, and mechanistic actions; it highlights the drug's therapeutic potential across a variety of neurodegenerative diseases and emphasizes the necessity of carefully planned randomized controlled trials to determine clinical efficacy, long-term safety, and its place in multimodal treatment approaches.

Title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
Abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

Title: Physical and psychological pathways associated with cognitive recovery following Baduanjin exercise combined with digital cognitive training in older adults with atrial fibrillation: A secondary mediation analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
Volumetric Analysis versus Diameter Measurement for Early Detection of Post-EVAR Sac Progression.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo compare diameter- and volume-based surveillance after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and determine whether volumetric sac assessment identifies postoperative remodeling not captured by conventional maximum diameter measurement.MethodsThis retrospective single-center study included 383 patients who underwent elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm between January 2016 and April 2024. All patients had preoperative and postoperative computed tomography angiography and at least 1 year of follow-up. Maximum sac diameter, total aneurysm sac volume, thrombus volume, thrombus density, neck morphology, and other anatomical variables were assessed using standardized morphometric and three-dimensional morphovolumetric measurements. Sac dynamics were classified by diameter criteria (≥5 mm decrease, stable, or ≥5 mm increase) and volumetric criteria (>10% decrease, stable, or >10% increase).ResultsEndoleaks occurred in 26.1% of patients (n = 100), and secondary interventions were required in 14.1% (n = 54), with a mean time to reintervention of 21.7 ± 10 months. At final follow-up, 74.7% demonstrated sac diameter reduction, 18.5% were stable, and 6.8% had enlargement, whereas volumetric analysis showed shrinkage in 81.7%, stability in 6.0%, and enlargement in 12.3%. At 1, 6, and 12 months, cohort mean diameter changed by -0.6%, -3.1%, and -6.5% from baseline, respectively, while cohort mean volume changed by -0.5%, -5.7%, and -12.5%. Among diameter-stable sacs, 32.4% enlarged volumetrically and 38.0% regressed volumetrically. In enlarging sacs, a 10% volume increase corresponded to an approximately 4 mm diameter increase (R2 = 0.72; P < 0.001); this 4 mm value was a regression estimate, not the diameter threshold used for sac classification. Preoperative morphometric and morphovolumetric variables were associated with endoleak and secondary intervention in exploratory analyses.ConclusionVolumetric sac analysis identified additional postoperative remodeling beyond maximum diameter measurement, particularly in apparently stable sacs. A practical surveillance strategy combining rapid diameter-based screening with selective volumetric analysis in stable, borderline, or clinically suspicious cases may improve recognition of adverse sac behavior without requiring routine volumetry in every follow-up study.

Title: Intravascular imaging improves outcomes in left main PCI: insights from acute and chronic presentations.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has emerged as an established revascularization strategy for selected patients with left main coronary artery (LMCA) disease. However, data regarding outcomes in unselected real-world populations and the impact of intravascular imaging remain limited. We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes following LMCA PCI according to clinical presentation and to assess the prognostic impact of intravascular imaging guidance.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre study including consecutive patients undergoing LMCA PCI between 2019 and 2022. Patients were classified as having chronic (CCS) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were assessed during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression and stabilised inverse probability of treatment weighting (SIPTW) analyses were performed.
RESULTS: A total of 107 patients were included (19 CCS and 88 ACS; mean age 68.6 ± 11.3 years; 80.4% male). During a mean follow-up of 1121 ± 574 days, ACS patients experienced higher rates of MACCE (40.9% vs. 15.8%; p = 0.039) and all-cause mortality (29.5% vs. 5.3%; p = 0.027) compared with CCS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with a significantly lower risk of MACCE in multivariable analysis (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.14-0.75; p = 0.009). In a SIPTW-adjusted analysis, the association remained directionally favourable, although statistical significance was not maintained (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.26-1.29; p = 0.178).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical presentation significantly influences outcomes after LMCA PCI, with worse long-term prognosis among ACS patients. Intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with lower rates of MACCE and remained directionally favourable after weighting analyses, supporting its role in optimising LMCA interventions.

Title: Development and Initial Psychometric Validation of a Nurse-Assessed Discharge Readiness Scale for Patients With Coronary Heart Disease Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) face multiple disease- and treatment-related self-management demands after discharge. Accurate assessment of discharge readiness is essential for identifying areas in which patients may require additional discharge education and transitional care support. The widely used Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale (RHDS) assesses overall discharge readiness across four domains: personal status, knowledge, coping ability and expected support. As a generic instrument, however, its broadly framed items may not adequately capture PCI-specific aspects of readiness, including treatment adherence, puncture-site healing, recognition of warning symptoms and preparedness for cardiac rehabilitation.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and initially validate a nurse-assessed Discharge Readiness Scale for Patients with CHD Following PCI (DRS-CHD-PCI).
METHODS: A multistage instrument development and validation study was conducted. Candidate items were generated using transition theory, a targeted review of relevant literature, clinical guidelines and existing discharge-readiness instruments, and semistructured interviews with patients with CHD following PCI and with healthcare professionals. Items were refined through two rounds of Delphi expert consultations and a pilot test with 20 patients. During psychometric validation, nurses assessed 444 patients on the planned discharge day; assessments took approximately 10-15 min. The sample was randomly split into two subsamples for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. Psychometric evaluation included item analysis, content validity, structural validity, convergent and discriminant validity, internal consistency and split-half reliability.
RESULTS: The final scale comprised 17 items across five dimensions. Exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor structure that explained 75.84% of the total variance. Both the first- and second-order confirmatory factor analysis models showed acceptable fit. Cronbach's α was 0.945 for the total scale and ranged from 0.813 to 0.894 across the five dimensions.
CONCLUSIONS: The DRS-CHD-PCI is a 17-item, five-dimensional scale with initial evidence supporting its content validity, structural validity and internal consistency. Further multicentre longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate its predictive validity and clinical utility and to determine how its scores can be meaningfully interpreted in clinical practice.
IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING MANAGEMENT: The DRS-CHD-PCI may assist nursing managers and cardiovascular nursing teams by providing a structured, assessment of discharge readiness before discharge and informing nurse-led transitional care planning following PCI. Lower total or dimension scores may highlight areas in which patients require further clinical assessment, additional education, or follow-up.

Title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis.
RESULTS: Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21]; P=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (P for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

Title: Life-Course Blood Pressure Trajectories and Focal Myocardial Fibrosis in Older Age in MyoFit46.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of life-course blood pressure (BP) trajectories on later-life focal left ventricular (LV) fibrosis by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) remains elusive.
METHODS: MyoFit46 prospectively recruited ≈500 participants from a 1946 birth cohort for a cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan at 77 years, assessing LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method or 5-SD method. Systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP were recorded at 36, 43, 53, 63, 69, and 77 years. For each participant, annual rates of BP change (steepness) and area under the BP trajectory (cumulative burden) for each age interval were calculated using mixed-effects models. Associations between life-course BPs and LGE were tested using generalized linear models, adjusted for antihypertensives, demographics, lifestyle, and comorbidities. Time-to-event associations between LGE and incident major adverse cardiovascular event (hospitalizations for coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, and atrial/ventricular arrhythmias; n=29) were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 472 participants (54% male), each 10 mm Hg greater individual SBPs at 36 to 69 years were associated with 6% to 11% greater LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method (all P≤0.033), whereas each 10 mm Hg sustained greater SBPs on any age interval from 36 to 69 associated with 16% to 24% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77(all P≤0.005), independent of SBP at 77 years. Each 1 mm Hg/y steeper SBP rise during age intervals 36 to 43, 43 to 53, and 53 to 63 was associated with 6% to 12% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77 years. LGE presence was associated with greater major adverse cardiovascular event rates (hazard ratio, 2.5 [95% CI, 1.2-5.2]).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher life-course BPs, cumulative burden, and steeper increases were associated with greater older-age LV LGE, which was linked to incident major adverse cardiovascular events. BP trajectories, beyond single-point BP measurements, warrant further investigation as tools to guide BP management strategies.

Title: Pyrophosphatase 2 Deficiency: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis and Management.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPA2 (pyrophosphatase 2) deficiency is a relatively newly recognized condition caused by biallelic variants in the PPA2 gene. The gene encodes the mitochondrial enzyme PPA2, involved in the production of orthophosphate in the mitochondrial matrix. Affected individuals typically present with sudden cardiac death or acute heart failure following common viral illnesses in infants and toddlers, or following exposure to small amounts of alcohol as teenagers. The condition has a high mortality rate in these situations. Here, we explore the clinical presentations and current management of these patients with a view to guiding future emergency clinical management of cases.
METHODS: Case records from published and unpublished affected individuals diagnosed with PPA2 deficiency were compiled in a retrospective cohort study of genotypes, phenotypes and clinical management protocols in individuals with biallelic (likely) pathogenic PPA2 variants.
RESULTS: We collated 93 affected individuals from 53 families, 14 of which have not previously been reported. Patient presentation is invariably acute, often associated with fatigue, vomiting, seizures and collapse. Generally, presenting individuals received standard emergency management with cardiopulmonary resuscitation and appropriate management of arrhythmia, and here we present compiled clinical management protocols for emergency and ongoing treatment of PPA2-deficient patients. A pronounced inheritance rate of pathogenic alleles from carrier parents is noted, and further research is warranted to confirm and investigate any selective advantage for gametes carrying pathogenic PPA2 variants.
CONCLUSIONS: PPA2 deficiency has a high mortality rate following exposure to common childhood viruses in children around and under the age of 3 and in teenagers exposed to ethanol. We have presented current therapeutic approaches gathered from a worldwide survey of clinicians treating their patients, possible pathogenic mechanisms and inheritance peculiarities of the condition and provide a comprehensive review of the current recommendations surrounding patients' clinical management.

Title: Standardization of Collected Biobank Data to Facilitate Cardiovascular Research: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease has been the focus of extensive biomedical research, yet it remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. One recent approach to support scientific discovery has been the development of large-scale population-based prospective studies that couple phenotypic data, including outcomes, to collection and analysis of biological samples. Large, data-dense biobanks, particularly those linked to electronic health records (including laboratory, electrocardiographic, imaging, and therapeutic data) and genomic data, have demonstrated value for interdisciplinary research into the epidemiology, cause, treatment, and prevention of disease and yield increasingly refined insights into monogenic and complex traits. One limitation to wider use of these resources is that they may collect phenotypic and biological data in a nonuniform fashion, limiting data harmonization, analysis, and validation. The purpose of this scientific statement is to discuss the current state of available biobanks, endorse biobanks for discovery and implementation science, and propose opportunities for future harmonization to increase the potential for novel studies aimed at understanding mechanisms and developing novel therapies for cardiovascular disease treatment and prevention.

Title: Racial Disparities in Longitudinal Functional Outcome After Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The burden of stroke is unequally distributed in the United States, with Black individuals experiencing more incident stroke. It remains unclear whether Black individuals also experience worse stroke recovery. We sought to study disparities in longitudinal functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke in a population-based study.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study in the Greater Cincinnati Northern Kentucky region over an 18-month period (July 2019 to December 2020). All acute ischemic stroke events were captured. The modified Rankin Scale scores were determined at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months for patients who survived the index event. We studied the association between Black race and longitudinal modified Rankin Scale (across all time points) with mixed-effects ordinal regression, initially adjusting for age, sex, and time since stroke. Hierarchical regression was used to sequentially adjust for stroke severity and management, premorbid health, and social determinants.
RESULTS: Among 2796 patients with acute ischemic stroke (mean age, 69.0; 31% Black; 52% female), 2537 survived and were included (mean age, 68.4; 32% Black; 52% female). Black race was associated with a worse longitudinal modified Rankin Scale score (cOR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.89-3.60]). Excluding patients with recurrent events did not change this association (cOR, 2.69 [95% CI, 1.92-3.78]). Adding variables reflecting initial stroke severity and management partly attenuated the association (cOR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.43-2.60]). Adding variables reflecting premorbid health further attenuated the association (cOR decreased to 1.43 [95% CI, 1.09-1.87]). The remaining association between Black race and the modified Rankin Scale score was fully attenuated by social determinants, with cOR, 1.09 (95% CI, 0.80-1.47). There was no interaction between race and time since stroke.
CONCLUSIONS: Starting at discharge and persisting out to 12 months, acute ischemic stroke functional outcomes are worse among Black individuals. These disparities are significantly attenuated by clinical factors and social determinants; future studies should explore whether the social determinants can be intervened upon in the recovery period.

Title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED.
METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days.
RESULTS: Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54).
CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

Title: Cardiovascular Genetic Counseling Is Associated With Improved Patient-Reported Outcomes Across Clinical Indications and Settings.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary guidelines recommend genetic counseling for potentially inherited cardiomyopathies, channelopathies, aortopathies, and dyslipidemias, but few small studies characterize cardiovascular genetic counseling (CVGC) outcomes, impeding efforts to improve CVGC service delivery. We aimed to (1) quantify psychosocial CVGC outcomes, (2) identify clinical, demographic, and service delivery characteristics associated with the extent of benefit from CVGC, and (3) determine how outcomes are associated with patient-reported quality of the genetic counselor:patient alliance.
METHODS: The MCVGC-GO (Multicenter Cardiovascular Genetic Counseling Outcomes Study) is a longitudinal survey-based study with pre- and post- genetic counseling data collection. Eight hundred ninety adults attending a first outpatient CVGC appointment at 8 United States and Canadian medical centers completed questionnaires assessing empowerment (Genetic Counseling Outcome Scale-24), worry (modified Cancer Worry Scale), cardiac anxiety (Cardiac Anxiety Questionnaire [CAQ]), and genetic counselor:patient alliance (Working Alliance Inventory-patient) before and up to 4 weeks post-CVGC, but before results of genetic tests ordered were returned to decouple CVGC and genetic test result impact.
RESULTS: Following CVGC, empowerment increased (Genetic Counseling Outcome Scale score change, +5.94±11.6; P<0.001), worry decreased (Cancer Worry Scale score change, -0.40±3.55; P=0.002), and cardiac fear decreased (CAQ fear subscale change, -0.034±0.46; P=0.033) with no change in whole-scale CAQ (0.013±0.34; P=0.29). In linear regression, worry decreased most in patients with less formal education (P=0.0021), with an arrhythmia indication (P=0.013), and who were at-risk family members (P=0.016) and the strength of the genetic counselor:patient alliance had no impact. In contrast, the genetic counselor:patient alliance was strongly positively associated with change in empowerment (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This observational, multicenter, multiprovider study provides foundational evidence that CVGC is associated with increased empowerment and decreased worry in adults attending outpatient CVGC and suggests opportunities for optimizing CVGC services.

Title: Prognostic Evaluation of Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients After Mechanical Thrombectomy Incorporating Imaging, Inflammatory, and Rehabilitation Aspects.
Abstract:
AIM: We aimed to perform a prognostic evaluation for patients with acute ischemic stroke after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) incorporating imaging, inflammatory, and rehabilitation aspects.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) was conducted, systematically evaluating baseline demographics, neuroimaging features, hematological inflammatory indices, and time to start rehabilitation. Prognostic correlations were examined using multivariate logistic regression, with poor functional outcome defined as 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) >2. Model discrimination was assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis of the composite prediction framework.
RESULTS: The analytical cohort comprised 144 subjects. Five independent predictors of unfavorable outcomes emerged: pre-existing hypertension (adjusted Odds Ratio [aOR] 6.48, 95% Confidence Interval [CI] 1.03-40.80), lower baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) (aOR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06-0.49), elevated NLR (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46), extended onset-to-reperfusion time (OTR) (per minute aOR 1.01, 95% CI 1.01-1.02), and delayed starting rehabilitation (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.52-3.46). The multivariable model demonstrated excellent discriminative capacity (area under the curve [AUC] 0.964, 95% CI 0.940-0.988).
CONCLUSIONS: Beyond successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3), functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy were independently influenced by factors across the three core domains of our prognostic framework: imaging (baseline ASPECTS), inflammation (elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, NLR), and rehabilitation (delayed starting rehabilitation). Additional significant clinical variables included pre-existing hypertension and longer onset-to-reperfusion time (OTR). These findings support the potential value of a multidimensional prognostic assessment integrating imaging, inflammatory, and rehabilitation aspects in patients with acute ischemic stroke after mechanical thrombectomy.

Title: Comparison of Primary Patency Rates and Influencing Factors Between Drug-Coated Balloons and Drug-Eluting Stents in the Endovascular Treatment of Lower Extremity Arteriosclerosis Obliterans.
Abstract:
AIM: To compare the 1-year patency rates of drug-coated balloon (DCB) and drug-eluting stent (DES) in the treatment of lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (LEASO), and to systematically analyze the factors influencing post-treatment patency.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 302 patients with LEASO who received treatment at Fuyang People's Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Based on the treatment modality, patients were divided into a DCB group (n = 152) and a DES group (n = 150). Comprehensive baseline demographic, clinical, and procedural data were collected. The 1-year primary patency rates of the two groups were compared using imaging assessment, primarily based on ultrasonography. Independent risk factors affecting patency were identified using a multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression model.
RESULTS: The 1-year primary patency rate was 87.5% (133/152) in the DCB group and 89.3% (134/150) in the DES group. No statistically significant difference in the 1-year primary patency rates was observed between the two groups (p > 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that diabetes mellitus, lesion length, and severe calcification were independent risk factors affecting patency after endovascular treatment (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The 1-year patency rates did not differ significantly between the DCB and DES groups. Diabetes mellitus, long lesion length, and severe calcification were identified as key factors associated with reduced patency rates. Clinical management should emphasize individualized intervention strategies and postoperative management for these high-risk patients.

Title: Multidimensional Echocardiographic Parameters Predict Left Ventricular Functional Recovery After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
Abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of preoperative and early postoperative echocardiographic parameters for left ventricular function recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to evaluate the relationship between functional recovery and 1-year clinical prognosis.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 214 patients undergoing first-time elective CABG at The First Affiliated Hospital of Yangtze University between January 2022 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, 3-7 days postoperatively, and at 6 months to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial volume index (LAVI), and ratio of early mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e'). Based on 6‑month LVEF change, patients were divided into recovery (ΔLVEF ≥5%) and non‑recovery (ΔLVEF <5%) groups. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, and the corresponding models were established and validated. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded at 1‑year follow‑up.
RESULTS: Of the 214 patients enrolled in the study, functional recovery of the left ventricle was observed in 128 individuals, corresponding to 59.8% of the cohort. Multivariate analysis identified several preoperative and procedural variables as independent predictors of functional recovery, including left atrial volume index (LAVI), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left atrial diameter (LAD), Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score, and the number of graft vessels. Age, preoperative LVEF, and e' velocity were independently associated with lower odds of functional recovery. Global longitudinal strain (GLS) and diabetes history showed no independent predictive value. The clinical-echocardiographic combined model demonstrated excellent discrimination and showed higher discriminative performance than the basic clinical model and conventional echocardiographic model. Subgroup analysis revealed that GLS showed no independent predictive value across all LVEF subgroups (p > 0.05), whereas LAVI and LAD were significant predictors in patients with LVEF ≥40% (including the 40%-49% subgroup), but showed no predictive relevance in those with LVEF <40%. Early postoperative ΔLVEF predicted 6-month functional recovery with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.846. After one year of follow‑up, the recovery group exhibited a markedly lower rate of MACE than the non‑recovery group, with left ventricular functional recovery serving as an independent protective factor against MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative structural parameters, including LAVI, LVEDD, LVESD, and LAD, are independent imaging biomarkers for predicting left ventricular functional recovery after CABG. GLS and E/e' ratio show no independent predictive value in this study. The integrated model combining clinical factors with multi-dimensional echocardiographic parameters demonstrates excellent discriminative ability. Early postoperative LVEF improvement strongly predicts 6-month functional recovery, while postoperative recovery of left ventricular function is associated with a significantly lower 1-year MACE risk.

Title: Long-term outcomes in adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot: a single-centre retrospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot represent a growing clinical population at risk for long-term cardiovascular complications. Characterising their postoperative course and late outcomes is essential to guide surveillance and management.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical characteristics and long-term outcomes of adult patients (≥18 years) with repaired tetralogy of Fallot who received care at a quaternary-care institution between January 2000 and December 2024.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study. Adult patients with a diagnosis of repaired tetralogy of Fallot who had undergone complete surgical repair either during the study period or before it were included. Clinical and sociodemographic data were obtained.Variables related to prior palliative procedures, type of surgical repair, reinterventions (surgical or catheter-based), and long-term outcomes were analysed.
RESULTS: A total of 56 patients were included; 31 (55.4%) were women. The median duration of follow-up after repair was 23 years; twenty patients (35.7%) had undergone a palliative or prior intervention before complete repair. The most common type of outflow tract reconstruction was a transannular patch (37.5%), followed by homograft implantation (25.0%). Reinterventions occurred in 29 patients (51.8%), most commonly pulmonary valve replacement (23 patients, 41.0%), mainly due to progressive pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular dilation. Arrhythmic complications included premature ventricular contractions in 35.7% of patients. Long-term mortality was 3.6%.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with repaired tetralogy of Fallot demonstrate high long-term survival; however, late complications are common and frequently require surgical or catheter-based reintervention. These findings underscore the need for lifelong specialised follow-up in adult CHD programmes.

Title: Dynamic change in soluble suppressor of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) during acute decompensated heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction, and its mortality implications.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association of soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) concentrations measured at clinician-determined decompensation and recompensation, and their change between these states, with one-year mortality in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF).
METHODS: Paired sST2 samples were obtained at decompensation and recompensation from 168 patients hospitalized with ADHF and a left ventricular ejection fraction of <50%. Associations with one-year all-cause mortality were assessed using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analysis. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, with exploratory cut-offs derived using Youden's index.
RESULTS: The median age was 71.5 years (IQR 62-80.8), 39 (23.2%) were women, median LVEF was 26% (IQR 17.5-32.5), and 158 (94.1%) had NYHA class III or IV symptoms. During one-year follow-up, 34 patients (20.2%) died. Each doubling of decompensation sST2 was associated with higher mortality after adjustment for creatinine (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.23-2.25). Recompensation sST2 remained associated with mortality after adjustment for creatinine and NT-proBNP (HR per doubling 1.71, 95% CI 1.18-2.48). The respective areas under the curve were 0.686 and 0.688, with exploratory cut-offs of 66.5 and 57 ng/mL. Unchanged or increased sST2 was associated with higher mortality than decreased sST2 in unadjusted analysis (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.37-5.59, p = 0.003).
CONCLUSION: Elevated sST2 at decompensation and unchanged or increased concentrations during recompensation were associated with one-year mortality in patients with ADHF. These findings support further evaluation of sST2 as an adjunctive prognostic biomarker in this setting; the cohort-derived cut-offs require validation.

Title: Real-world impact of coronary artery calcium scoring on primary prevention management in a community cardiology practice.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring on lipid-lowering therapy intensification, aspirin initiation, and downstream cardiac testing in primary prevention patients in a community cardiology setting.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SETTING: Single community cardiology practice.
PARTICIPANTS: Four hundred consecutive patients undergoing CAC scoring in 2022.
INTERVENTIONS: CAC scoring used for risk stratification and clinical decision-making.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Changes in lipid-lowering therapy, aspirin initiation, and downstream cardiac testing across CAC categories (0, 1-99, 100-399, ≥400); risk reclassification using Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) and Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) risk scores.
RESULTS: Among 400 patients (mean age 60.2 ± 10.6 years; 46.5% male), 30% had CAC = 0, 37% CAC 1-99, 18% CAC 100-399, and 16% CAC ≥400. Lipid therapy modification increased across categories (7.7%, 33.3%, 69.0%, 81.7%; p < 0.001), as did aspirin initiation among aspirin-naive patients (1.0%, 8.0%, 51.9%, 52.5%; p < 0.001) and stress testing (2.7%, 6.5%, 29.0%, 68.6%; p < 0.001). Each one-category CAC increment was independently associated with lipid therapy modification (adjusted OR 4.36, 95% CI 3.13-6.06), aspirin initiation (OR 4.48, 95% CI 2.85-7.03), and stress testing (OR 5.11, 95% CI 3.33-7.84; all p < 0.001). CAC changed MESA risk category in 192/348 patients (55.2%): 87 upward and 105 downward.
CONCLUSIONS: CAC burden was independently associated with graded intensification of lipid-lowering therapy, aspirin initiation, and downstream testing after multivariable adjustment, extending prior descriptive literature with persistent, quantified associations in real-world community practice. Improvement in clinical outcomes cannot be assessed from this retrospective, six-month implementation study.

Title: Epimeric Vitamin D is Not Associated With Arterial Stiffness or Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Advanced CKD.
Abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: 3-epi-25(OH)D3, an epimeric form of 25(OH)D3 generated by C-3 epimerization, declines with advancing chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its role in vascular health and related outcomes remains largely unknown. We aimed to determine whether circulating 3-epi-25(OH)D3 levels are associated with arterial stiffness and longitudinal cardiovascular (CV) outcomes in advanced CKD (stages 5 and 5D).
STUDY DESIGN: A prospective observational study.
SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: A total of 270 patients with advanced CKD using the Cambridge Coventry Vascular cohort.
EXPOSURE S OR PREDICTOR S: Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D3 measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.
OUTCOME S: Arterial stiffness was assessed by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (AIx75). Longitudinal outcomes included a composite of major CV events and all-cause mortality.
ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D3 was categorized into quartiles. Associations were assessed using multivariable regression adjusted for age, race, and dialysis status. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed longitudinal outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 270 participants, quartiles were Q1 < 0.30 ng/mL (n = 64), Q2: 0.30-0.456 ng/mL (n = 71), Q3: 0.457-0.729 ng/mL (n = 68), and Q4 ≥ 0.73 ng/mL (n = 67). Strata were similar in age (44.9 years), sex, and BMI (all P > 0.05). Race differed by quartile (P < 0.001); 87.4% were White. 24.8% were pre-dialytic, 61.1% treated with hemodialysis, and 14.1% treated with peritoneal dialysis. Arterial stiffness was similar across quartiles (AIx75 ∼20-21%, P = 0.99; PWV: 7.8-8.0 m/s, P = 0.94). 3-epi-25(OH)D3 showed no association with AIx75 or PWV before or after adjustment using multiple regression modeling. Over 9.3 years, 115 composite events occurred (97 CV events, 18 deaths). Kaplan-Meier analysis did not discriminate risk across 3-epi-25(OH)D3 quartiles for the composite outcome (log-rank P = 0.23), and adjusted Cox models showed no association.
LIMITATIONS: Observational design with possible residual confounding.
CONCLUSION: In advanced CKD, 3-epi-25(OH)D3 showed no independent association with arterial stiffness or CV events and mortality. Further studies are needed to determine the role of epimeric vitamin D in patients with CKD.

Title: Microplastics, nanoplastics, and thrombogenesis.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are produced through mechanical, chemical, and ultraviolet-mediated degradation of plastics and may enter the human bloodstream via ingestion, inhalation, dermal exposure, and iatrogenic sources. Their detection in human blood, atheromas, and thrombi has raised concerns that they may contribute to thrombogenesis. We conducted a structured narrative review of English-language studies indexed in PubMed, Embase, and Scopus over the preceding 15 years, up to March 31, 2026. The search identified 981 database records and 39 additional manually identified articles; after removing duplicates and screening, 72 articles were included. Evidence was synthesized according to Virchow's triad, focusing on endothelial injury, altered blood flow, hypercoagulability, cellular uptake, polymer type, surface charge, weathering, and protein corona formation. MNPs may contribute to all 3 components of Virchow's triad. Proposed mechanisms include oxidative endothelial injury, glycocalyx disruption, monocyte adhesion, foam-cell formation, plaque instability, immune cell-mediated microvascular obstruction, platelet activation, NETosis, von Willebrand factor interactions, factor XII activation, thrombin generation, and fibrin-rich clot stabilization. These effects appear to vary with particle size, polymer composition, surface charge, and environmental weathering. However, mechanistic evidence largely comes from polystyrene nanoparticle models, whereas human thrombus and atheroma studies more commonly detect polyethylene and polyvinyl chloride. MNPs are biologically plausible contributors to thrombogenesis, but their clinical relevance remains uncertain. Prospective human studies, standardized contamination-controlled detection methods, and dose-response experiments using clinically relevant particles and concentrations are required.

Title: Acute and Chronic Resistance Training Differentially Modulate Myocardial Angiogenesis-Related Gene Expression in Wistar Rats.
Abstract: Myocardial angiogenesis contributes to the maintenance of myocardial perfusion and cardiac function. Resistance training (RT) induces cardiovascular adaptations, but the myocardial transcriptional responses to acute RT (ART) and chronic RT (CRT) remain incompletely understood. This study compared the expression of angiogenesis- and metabolic adaptation-related genes in the left ventricle following a single RT bout and 8 weeks of repeated RT in healthy male Wistar rats. Twenty-four rats were randomized to three groups: sedentary control (CON) (n = 8), ART (one ladder-climbing session), or CRT (ladder-climbing 5 days/week for 8 weeks). RT was performed on a 1-m ladder inclined at 80° using progressive loads attached to the tail. Left-ventricular tissue was collected 1 h after the exercise bout in ART and 1 h after the final training session in CRT. Compared to CON, ART showed significantly higher HIF-1α and FSTL1 expression, whereas PGC-1α and VEGF did not differ significantly. CRT also showed significantly higher HIF-1α and FSTL1 expression than CON, together with significantly higher PGC-1α and VEGF expression. No significant differences were observed between ART and CRT for any of the genes examined. These findings demonstrate distinct myocardial transcriptional profiles following ART versus CRT, characterized by an HIF-1α- and FSTL1-associated response after a single bout and a PGC-1α- and VEGF-associated response following CRT.

Title: Prehospital predictors of clinical outcomes in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity: a JCS-ReSS report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with pulseless electrical activity (PEA) has a poor prognosis and is aetiologically heterogeneous. We aimed to identify prehospital predictors of a favourable outcome, overall and by presumed aetiology.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study analysed 442,630 adults with OHCA and an initial rhythm of PEA from the All-Japan Utstein Registry between 2005 and 2024. The primary outcome was a favourable neurological outcome at 1 month. Two models were fitted, at the scene and at hospital arrival, each also within each aetiology. Epinephrine and advanced airway management (AAM) were assessed by time-dependent propensity score sequential matching.
RESULTS: At the scene, a witnessed arrest (risk ratio [RR], 1.65) predicted a favourable neurological outcome, and a longer response time predicted a worse one (RR, 0.66; 10 versus 5 min). The gradient with age was steeper in cardiac than non-cardiac PEA (RR, 0.38 versus 0.78). At hospital arrival, prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (RR, 23.31) was the strongest predictor, but conversion to a shockable rhythm predicted a favourable outcome only in cardiac PEA and a worse outcome in non-cardiac PEA (RR, 1.37 versus 0.73). Standardised to a common covariate distribution, 1-month survival was higher in non-cardiac PEA, whereas a favourable neurological outcome was more likely in cardiac PEA. After time-dependent adjustment, the apparent harm from epinephrine and AAM was attenuated.
CONCLUSIONS: Prehospital information available before hospital arrival predicted a favourable neurological outcome, but its prognostic meaning depended on the presumed aetiology. These independent prehospital predictors could inform future risk stratification.

Title: The effect of time-varying left ventricular ejection fraction on clinical outcome in critically ill COVID-19 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although right ventricular (RV) dysfunction and acute cor pulmonale are associated with adverse outcomes in critically ill patients with COVID-19, the prognostic significance of left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction remains insufficiently characterized. In particular, dynamic changes in cardiac function during intensive care has seldom been studied. We therefore investigated the association between time-varying LV systolic function, assessed by LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and intensive care unit (ICU) mortality in patients with COVID-19, taking into account right ventricular function and forward flow.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study combined three ICU data repositories comprising 808 patients with 1614 echocardiographic examinations. Time-varying LV systolic function (LVEF ≤ 50%, 51-70%, >70%) was the primary exposure, and ICU mortality was the outcome. Multivariable Cox models with time-varying covariates, including, acute cor pulmonale, left ventricular outflow tract velocity time integral and key clinical characteristics were used to assess associations between LV systolic function phenotypes and outcome.
RESULTS: At baseline, 27% of patients had abnormal LV systolic function (LVEF ≤ 50%) and 17% had hyperdynamic LV function (LVEF > 70%). The proportion of patients with normal LV systolic function increased over time. Abnormal LV systolic function was most prevalent at the first echocardiographic examination (27%) and least prevalent at the fifth examination (17%), whereas hyperdynamic LV function became more frequent during ICU stay, peaking at the 4th echocardiographic examination. Abnormal (aHR; 1.174, 95% CI: 0.901-1.531) or hyperdynamic (aHR: 1.041, 95% CI: 0.785-1.379) LV systolic dysfunction was not independently associated with ICU mortality.
CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients with COVID-19, LV systolic dysfunction, including both abnormal and hyperdynamic LV phenotypes, were common and dynamic during ICU stay. LV systolic dysfunction was not independently associated with ICU mortality when modelled longitudinally and adjusted for RV dysfunction, forward flow and other clinical covariates. These findings suggest that the prognostic value LVEF phenotypes in severe COVID-19 may be limited. Further studies incorporating more sensitive measures of LV function and biomarkers of myocardial injury may be required to delineate subtle changes not captured by LVEF.

Title: Treatment Strategies for Achieving and Maintaining Low-Risk Status in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Achieving and maintaining low-risk status is now the main treatment goal in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), but the evidence connecting individual treatment strategies with low-risk attainment and long-term outcomes is scattered across trials, registries, and cohorts that use different risk tools. We conducted a systematic review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Scopus, Dimensions, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to August 27, 2026, for studies of adults with Group 1 PAH that evaluated a treatment strategy and reported a validated risk-stratification outcome. Results were synthesised narratively under the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline, with certainty graded using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Forty-eight reports were included: 10 randomised or prospective interventional studies, 12 secondary analyses of trial data, and 26 observational cohorts. Few patients reached low risk under any strategy, and fewer than half did so after upfront dual oral therapy in most cohorts. Prostacyclin-pathway therapy improved risk status across oral, inhaled, and parenteral routes, although the clearest survival advantage came from parenteral regimens in registry data. Add-on sotatercept improved functional, haemodynamic, and composite clinical outcomes, and these gains were largely sustained at one year. Low-risk status predicted survival, yet it often did not last, and the risk category reached at the first annual review strongly predicted later course. In mediation analyses, change in risk score accounted for only part of the treatment effect, and studies disagreed on whether patients already at low risk benefit from further treatment. Low-risk status is a valuable treatment target and prognostic marker, but it has not been validated as a surrogate endpoint. Early, repeated risk assessment and prompt escalation during the first year after diagnosis are supported by the available evidence.

Title: Timing of Cardiac Rehabilitation After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a cornerstone of post-acute care for patients experiencing cardiovascular events or interventions. It aims to improve cardiorespiratory capacity, enhance quality of life, and maximize physical function, facilitating a return to daily activities. However, the optimal timing for initiating CR following acute coronary events or procedures remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this randomized clinical trial, 40 patients diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction and treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were randomly assigned to two groups. Group A commenced cardiac rehabilitation one month after PCI, while Group B initiated rehabilitation two months post-PCI. Both groups completed a supervised 12-session rehabilitation program under the guidance of a physical medicine specialist. Functional outcomes were assessed before and after rehabilitation using the SF-36 quality of life questionnaire and echocardiographic parameters. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25. Within-group changes were evaluated with paired t-tests, and between-group comparisons of change scores were conducted using independent samples t-tests. A P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Post-rehabilitation, the mean SF-36 score was 65.85±6.67 in Group A and 67.05±5.96 in Group B (P=0.192). The mean change in Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) was 2.25% in Group A and 0.15% in Group B (P=0.305). After rehabilitation, grade 1-2 diastolic dysfunction remained present in 85% of patients in both groups, while 15% of patients in each group showed no evidence of diastolic dysfunction (P=0.506).No significant differences were found between groups in heart rate (HR) Max (107.45±15.04 vs. 115.20±13.12; P=0.091), HR Recovery (22.50±7.05 vs. 23.10±7.78; P=0.800), or MET change (6.60±1.83 vs. 6.20±2.39; P=0.556).
CONCLUSION: Initiating cardiac rehabilitation one month as opposed to two months after primary PCI did not yield significant differences in quality of life or cardiac functional parameters. These findings indicate that there may be flexibility in the timing of CR initiation without compromising short-term functional outcomes.

Title: Predictive Factors of Abnormal Brain CT Scan in Patients with Opioid Poisoning: A Single-Center Study.
Journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid poisoning is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in Iran; however, no clear guidelines exist regarding the appropriate timing for non-contrast BCTS in these patients. This study aims to identify clinical and laboratory factors that predict abnormal BCTS findings in individuals with opioid poisoning. We conducted the study among patients presenting to the emergency department of Shiraz Namazi Hospital with opioid poisoning.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study was performed on 208 patients with opioid poisoning who were referred to the emergency department of Namazi Hospital between March 2019 and March 2021. Data collection involved accessing the archives of Namazi Hospital to gather the necessary information for this study.
RESULTS: Among 208 patients with opioid poisoning who underwent brain CT, 57 (27.4%) exhibited abnormal BCTS findings within this selected subgroup. Multivariable logistic regression identified two independent predictive factors for abnormal BCTS: advanced age (OR 1.041 per year; 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P=0.008) and lower serum bicarbonate (OR 0.908 per mEq/L; 95% CI 0.83-0.99; P=0.025). The most prevalent abnormal findings included microvascular ischemic damage, followed by ischemic infarctions.
CONCLUSION: Advanced age and lower serum bicarbonate levels are independent predictors of abnormal BCTS findings in patients with acute opioid poisoning. Clinicians should consider urgent BCTS in older patients or those with metabolic acidosis, as these groups are at higher risk and may derive the greatest benefit from emergent neuroimaging.

Title: Hematological inflammatory markers as predictors of atherosclerotic progression in patients with psoriasis: A retrospective case-control study from the SH-YIMED database.
Journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
Abstract: Chronic inflammation drives cardiovascular comorbidity in psoriasis. Clinical-only risk models have limited utility, whereas the predictive value of blood inflammatory markers for psoriatic atherosclerosis is unconfirmed. This hospital-based case-control study enrolled 636 patients with psoriasis who underwent vascular ultrasonography, and 134 matched pairs were obtained through 1:1 propensity score matching. We analyzed primary and exploratory hematological inflammatory markers, examined their links to atherosclerosis using logistic regression and supplementary stratified and nonlinear analyses, and constructed risk prediction models that were assessed by area under the curve, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) (OR = 16.33, 95% confidence interval = 7.54-35.35, P < .001) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) (OR = 20.78, 95% confidence interval = 7.92-54.53, P < .001) were stronger independent predictors of atherosclerosis than C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, with significant age interactions for NLR (interaction OR = 7.45, P = .018) and SII (interaction OR = 28.03, P = .008). Models incorporating NLR (area under the curve = 0 .894, integrated discrimination improvement = 0.439, net reclassification improvement = 1.339) or SII (area under the curve = 0.891, integrated discrimination improvement = 0.413, net reclassification improvement = 1.281) exhibited favorable calibration and a higher clinical net benefit across decision curve analysis thresholds of 0.05-0.75. The combined C-reactive protein + NLR + SII model attained the highest area under the curve of 0.906. NLR and SII improved cardiovascular risk prediction for patients with psoriasis with atherosclerosis, enabling effective risk stratification.

Title: Demographic and clinical factors associated with intraoperative patient cooperation during LASIK.
Journal: Medical hypothesis, discovery & innovation ophthalmology journal
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor patient cooperation during ophthalmic surgery is demonstrated to result in a variety of complications. The purpose of this study is to evaluate demographic and clinical factors associated with intraoperative patient cooperation during laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients who underwent LASIK at a single institution. Patients were graded intraoperatively by three observers using a 5-point scale for cooperation during flap creation, fixation during excimer laser ablation, and head/body movement, with lower scores indicating better cooperation. Ordinal regression models were used to evaluate associations between cooperation scores and demographic characteristics or medical history.
RESULTS: A total of 836 patients were included, with a mean age of 35 years (SD, 10.3; range, 18-80 years), 454 (54.3%) male and 382 (45.7%) female; 70% of patients achieved the best overall cooperation score. Patients were significantly less cooperative during flap creation than during head/body movement (P < 0.05). Older age was associated with improved cooperation during flap creation (odds ratio [OR], 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.96 to 1.00; P < 0.05), laser fixation (OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96 to 0.99; P < 0.05), and movement (OR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96 to 0.99; P < 0.05). Female patients displayed significantly better cooperation only during flap creation (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.96; P < 0.05). Longer laser duration was associated with worse cooperation during laser fixation (OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.05 to 1.26; P < 0.05) and movement (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.02 to 1.23; P < 0.05). No significant associations were observed between overall cooperation and medical history diagnoses (all P > 0.05); however, anxiety showed an imprecise association with poorer cooperation (OR, 2.20; 95% CI, 0.97 to 5.00).
CONCLUSIONS: Patient cooperation during LASIK was generally excellent, although cooperation was worst during flap creation. Older age was modestly associated with improved cooperation across all three categories, female sex was associated only with flap-creation cooperation, and longer excimer laser duration was associated with laser fixation and movement, while no statistically significant associations with the assessed medical-history or medication variables were detected. Prospective studies in LASIK and other refractive procedures are warranted to validate and further elucidate the preliminary findings of this study.

Title: Proteomic markers associated with blood pressure, hypertension, and treatment-resistant hypertension.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to investigate associations between 92 proteins and blood pressure (BP), prevalent hypertension (HT) and apparent treatment-resistant HT (aTRH) in a population-derived sub cohort.
METHODS: Excluding subjects with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (n = 189), linear regression models assessed associations between proteins and systolic BP. Proteins showing significant associations (false discovery rate 5%) with systolic BP were analysed adjusting for clinically relevant covariates. Associated proteins were further analysed for associations with diastolic BP, prevalent HT, and aTRH, in multivariable regression models.
RESULTS: Complete data was available in 1527 individuals (mean age 67.1 ± 6.0 years; 30.5% women). Interleukin-1 receptor type 2 (IL1R2) associated with systolic BP (β 2.79, p 0.008), diastolic BP (β 1.78, p < 0.001), HT (odds ratio (OR), 1.34 [95% CI, 1.01-1.78]) and aTRH (OR, 1.94 [1.11-3.39]) while chitinase-3-like-protein 1 (CHI3L1) associated with systolic BP (β 1.53, p 0.004) and prevalent HT (OR 1.20, [1.04-1.38]). Pathway analysis suggested "metabolism of angiotensinogen to angiotensins", "neutrophil degranulation" and "peptide hormone metabolism" as significantly enriched, in relation to blood pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: Among 1527 individuals without established ASCVD, IL1R2 was associated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure, as well as with both HT and aTRH, while CHI3L1 associated with systolic blood pressure and prevalent HT. These findings may offer novel insights and inspire future research on HT and inflammation.

Title: Single-Cell and Spatial Multi-Omics in Small-Intestinal Homeostasis and Ischemia/Reperfusion Injury: Current Advances, Applications, and Future Perspectives.
Abstract: The intestinal tract acts as a dynamic barrier between the external and internal environments, and intestinal homeostasis fundamentally influences human health. This homeostasis depends on complex interactions among the epithelium, immune cells, and microbiota. Intestinal ischemia/reperfusion (II/R) disrupts these interactions and can cause local barrier failure and distant organ injury. However, the transition of the intestinal microenvironment from homeostasis to injury and repair remains incompletely characterized. This narrative review summarizes single-cell RNA sequencing, single-cell multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial multi-omics, including their underlying methods. We compare intestinal reference atlases with direct II/R studies and examine how these approaches complement bulk sequencing and histology. Human intestinal atlases reveal spatially organized epithelial states, whereas experimental II/R studies identify altered Paneth-cell states, endothelial regenerative signals, and epithelial stress responses. These findings differ in their model systems, sampling times, and degree of functional validation. Dissociation bias, batch effects, limited biological replication, spatial resolution, and uncertain integration across modalities constrain interpretation. Most disease-specific evidence remains preclinical, and inferred cell interactions should not be equated with demonstrated therapeutic mechanisms. Translation will require standardized human sampling, spatial and protein-level validation, causal perturbation, and prospective assessment of clinically accessible markers. Single-cell and spatial omics can therefore refine mechanistic hypotheses and guide validation in II/R, but currently do not constitute established clinical diagnostic or treatment pathways.

Title: The Impact of Age and Physical Assessment Measures on Performance Among Non-Weightbearing Walking Aids: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Walking aids for non-weightbearing (NWB) ambulation are often arbitrarily provided with no evidence that physical assessment predicts ambulatory performance.
PURPOSE: We sought to determine if convenient physical assessment measures could guide NWB walking aid prescription and to determine how age impacts ambulatory performance.
METHODS: This prospective randomized crossover study examined 22 healthy adults, recruited from Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, and surrounding area through flyers and word of mouth. Inclusion criteria were independent unrestricted community dwellers with no self-reported neuromusculoskeletal or cardiovascular conditions who were age 18 years or older. Participants were stratified into 2 age cohorts: younger (age <50 years) and older (age ≥50 years). Physical assessment measures included triceps and latissimus dorsi strength, single lower-limb balance, and arm endurance. Performance measures included distance traversed, rate of perceived exertion, and peak stance limb plantar force (SLPF) evaluated among 4 walking conditions: unaided, NWB with crutches, standard walker, and wheeled knee walker. Two analyses were performed, one using the entire sample population and another split by age.
RESULTS: There were no differences in physical assessment measures between the younger and older cohort, yet distance traversed in the older cohort was highly dependent on all physical assessment measures when using crutches or a standard walker. Peak SLPF was reduced in the younger cohort when using the wheeled knee walker, but not in the older cohort. In the younger participants, reducing peak SLPF was highly dependent on arm endurance when using a standard walker or crutches and latissimus dorsi strength when using the wheeled knee walker. Surprisingly, older participants with stronger latissimus dorsi strength reported a higher rate of perceived exertion when using the wheeled knee walker compared to other devices.
CONCLUSION: Arm strength, single lower-limb balance, and arm endurance should be considered when prescribing walking aids in older adults, and the wheeled knee walker should be considered in younger adults in need of reduced peak SLPF.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, prospective randomized comparative study.

Title: Nebulized Magnesium Sulfate as an Adjunct to Standard Therapy in Infants with Acute Bronchiolitis: A Double Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
Journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The evidence regarding the efficacy of magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) in bronchiolitis is conflicting, and high-quality trials involving very young infants are limited. To compare the efficacy of nebulized magnesium sulfate, salbutamol, and 3% hypertonic saline against nebulized salbutamol and 3% hypertonic saline in infants aged 1-6 months who are admitted with a first episode of mild-to-moderate bronchiolitis. The primary outcomes were physiological parameters including oxygen saturation (SpO₂), respiratory rate (RR), and pulse rate (PR). Length of hospital stay (LOS), and Respiratory Distress Assessment Instrument (RDAI) score were evaluated as exploratory outcomes, along with escalation of care and adverse events.
METHODS: In this parallel, double-blind randomized controlled trial conducted from August 2022 to February 2023, 62 eligible infants were allocated (1:1) to receive three consecutive 20-minute nebulizations of salbutamol, MgSO₄, and 3% saline (intervention) or salbutamol and 3% saline (control), followed by identical doses every 6 hours for up to 72 hours. All caregivers, clinicians, and outcome assessors were blinded. Outcome assessments were performed at baseline (pre-intervention), 1 hour after the initial dose, and every 24 hours thereafter (± 2 hours) until discharge or 72 hours, whichever occurred first. LOS was defined as the duration (in hours) from randomization until predefined discharge criteria were met (SpO₂ ≥ 94% in room air for ≥ 12 hours, adequate oral intake, respiratory rate within age norms, RDAI ≤ 3).
RESULTS: Among the 62 infants, 33 (53.2%) received triple-drug therapy, while 29 (46.8%) received standard dual therapy. The baseline characteristics were comparable, with a mean age as 3.6 ± 1.25 months and 56.5% male. The median Length of stay (LOS) was shorter in the MgSO₄ group (6.0 days, IQR 5-7) compared to the control group (7.0 days, IQR 6-9; P = 0.046, Mann-Whitney U). No significant differences were observed between groups for daily RDAI, RR, PR, or SpO₂ (repeated-measures ANOVA, P > 0.05). None of the infants required intensive care, mechanical ventilation, or experienced serious drug-related events.
CONCLUSION: This double-blind randomized trial did not demonstrate a statistically significant effect on its prospectively registered primary outcomes (oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, heart rate). The observed difference in length of hospital stay (a secondary, unregistered outcome; median 6.0 vs. 7.0 days; unadjusted P = 0.046) did not reach statistical significance after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (corrected threshold: P < 0.01) and should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating only. This trial should be interpreted as null and inconclusive. Adequately powered, prospectively registered confirmatory trials are necessary before any clinical recommendations can be made.

Title: Incidence and Progression of Acute Kidney Injury Following Head and Neck Surgeries for COVID-19-Associated Mucormycosis: A Prospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: COVID-19-associated mucormycosis (CAM) surged because of the combination of systemic corticosteroids, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, and altered host immunity. Rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis (ROCM) requires extensive surgical debridement and systemic nephrotoxic liposomal amphotericin B (L-AMB) therapy. This study evaluated the incidence, temporal course, and association of postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) with various clinical factors in this high-risk surgical cohort.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study enrolled 49 adult patients who underwent major head and neck surgical debridement for ROCM and required postoperative critical care management. We excluded patients with established renal failure. We performed and recorded serial clinical and biochemical monitoring daily over the next five days. AKI incidence and severity were staged according to Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN) criteria.
RESULTS: A total of 49 patients were evaluated for AKI, of which 9 developed AKI (18.4%). Patients who developed AKI had a higher mean age (56.6 ± 10.0 years versus 49.4 ± 10.3 years) and preoperative serum creatinine (1.1 ± 0.5 vs 0.9 ± 0.2 mg/dL), but these differences were not statistically significant. However, patients who developed post-operative AKI had a significantly lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (87.4 ± 27.1 vs 102.9 ± 17.4 mL/min/1.73 m²; p = 0.03), and a significantly higher prevalence of AKI was found in patients having pre-existing hypertension (77.8% vs. 32.5%; p = 0.02). Conversely, mean duration (p = 0.35), cumulative preoperative L-AMB dose (p = 0.319), and background diabetes mellitus (p = 0.136) did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: AKI was noted in nearly one-fifth of patients after ROCM surgery and was more common in older patients with hypertension and poorer baseline renal function. Baseline renal function appeared more important than cumulative L-AMB exposure or diabetes, highlighting the need for early renal risk assessment and close postoperative monitoring.

Title: Non-Surgical Therapies for Knee Osteoarthritis: Current Evidence and Emerging Strategies.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by pain, stiffness, and functional impairment. As many patients seek to avoid surgery, a synthesis of conservative treatment options is clinically relevant for evidence-based management.
METHODS: A structured PubMed literature search was conducted through December 15, 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, cohort and case-control studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses evaluating nonsurgical interventions for knee OA. Extracted outcomes included pain, function, safety, and comparative effectiveness across reported follow-up durations.
RESULTS: Intra-articular hyaluronic acid (HA) has a favorable safety profile and may delay progression to total knee arthroplasty, though benefits over placebo are modest and guideline recommendations inconsistent. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) improves pain and function and may outperform HA, although outcomes vary with preparation methods and study quality. Autologous conditioned serum and dextrose prolotherapy demonstrate symptomatic benefit, whereas corticosteroid injections primarily provide short-term relief. Disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs), including sprifermin, lorecivivint, LNA043, cathepsin-K inhibition, ADAMTS-5 inhibition, and repurposed metabolic agents such as metformin, are emerging investigational strategies with variable structural and symptomatic results. Early evidence suggests mesenchymal stem cell-based therapies may improve outcomes but remain investigational. Core conservative measures, including exercise therapy, physical therapy, and weight reduction, consistently reduce pain and improve function. Assistive devices and valgus bracing provide additional symptomatic and biomechanical benefit. Among device-based interventions, cooled radiofrequency ablation offers durable pain relief compared with HA or corticosteroids, while sustained acoustic medicine and extracorporeal shockwave therapy show functional improvement; evidence for pulsed electromagnetic field therapy is mixed. Topical nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs provide effective analgesia with reduced systemic risk.
CONCLUSION: Non-surgical management of knee OA should follow a stepwise approach, with rehabilitation and weight optimization as first-line therapy, selective injection- and device-based options for persistent symptoms, and timely surgical referral when disability remains refractory. Future progress will depend on standardized protocols and higher-quality long-term comparative trials to improve treatment selection and disease modification.

Title: Tirofiban vs standard antiplatelet therapy in acute branch atheromatous disease-related stroke: a multicenter, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint, parallel-group, phase III clinical trial.
Journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirofiban is sometimes used empirically for branch atheromatous disease (BAD)-related stroke, but its benefit in this population remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of intravenous tirofiban administered within 48 h of onset in patients with acute BAD-related stroke.
METHODS: This multicentre, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint clinical trial enrolled patients with BAD-related stroke within 48 h of onset from 25 hospitals in China between 9 November 2023 and 22 November 2025. Eligible patients were randomly assigned to the tirofiban group (intravenously, 0.4 μg/kg per minute for 30 min, followed by a 0.1 μg/kg per minute for 47.5 h) or standard antiplatelet therapy group (oral aspirin with or without clopidogrel) for 48 h. The primary endpoint was an excellent functional outcome, defined as a score of 0 or 1 on the modified Rankin Scale at 90 days. Safety outcomes included major bleeding within 90 days. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06037889).
FINDINGS: Among 516 patients randomized, 513 were included in the primary analysis (258 with tirofiban and 255 with standard antiplatelet therapy). An excellent functional outcome was observed in 181 of 258 patients (70.2%) in the tirofiban group and 178 of 255 (69.8%) in the standard antiplatelet therapy group (risk ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.90-1.13]; P = 0.93). Major bleeding occurred in 0 of 259 participants in the tirofiban-exposed safety population and 1 of 245 (0.4%) in the standard-antiplatelet-exposed safety population.
INTERPRETATION: Among patients with acute BAD-related stroke, intravenous tirofiban administered within 48 h of onset without concomitant oral antiplatelet therapy was not superior to standard antiplatelet therapy for achieving an excellent functional outcome at 90 days. These findings should not be extrapolated to substantially earlier treatment or to other tirofiban-based antiplatelet strategies.
FUNDING: National High Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding, Capital's Funds for Health Improvement and Research, CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences (CIFMS), Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, and China Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Company (CSPC) NBP Pharmaceurical Co., Ltd.

Title: Five-Day Glycemic Patterns and 3-Month Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Admission hyperglycemia is associated with poor outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, but whether post-EVT glycemic pattern determines functional outcome remains unknown.
METHODS: A Retrospective Study for the Prediction of Clinical Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients with Thrombectomy study was a hybrid prospective-retrospective multicenter cohort study nested within the Rescue on Reperfusion Damage in Cerebral Infarction by Nelonemdaz trial (NCT05041010) across 24 tertiary stroke centers in South Korea. Patients with ≥80% measurements within 80-140 mg/dL and no value ≥200 mg/dL were classified as normoglycemic (Group 1); the remainder were classified by group-based trajectory modeling into persistently elevated (Group 2) and variable hyperglycemia (Group 3). The primary outcome was 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) distribution.
RESULTS: Among 457 patients, 319 were included (mean age 73.6±12.2 years; 53.6% male): 97 (30.4%) in Group 1, 159 (49.8%) in Group 2, and 63 (19.7%) in Group 3. Groups 2 and 3 had more diabetes and higher hemoglobin A1c; stroke severity, Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Scores, and reperfusion status were comparable.
