Multivariate analysis did not identify predictors of constipation resolution.
CONCLUSIONS: Children affected by PUV exhibit a likely increased prevalence of CC. Endoscopic PUV ablation leads to significant normalization of bowel function, supporting a bidirectional interplay between urinary and gastrointestinal systems. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings in order to clarify the underlying mechanisms and optimize long-term care for affected patients.

Title: Sustained improvement in sickle cell cardiomyopathy after haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is superior to that with disease-modifying therapy.
Abstract: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative for sickle cell disease (SCD) - a group of inherited haemoglobin disorders encompassing homozygous haemoglobin S (HbSS) and compound heterozygous sickling disorders, including haemoglobin SC disease (HbSC), haemoglobin S/β0-thalassaemia (HbSβ0), haemoglobin S/β+-thalassaemia (HbSβ+), etc., but its long-term impact on SCD myocardial remodelling is incompletely characterized. We performed serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography in children and young adults with SCD undergoing matched-sibling or haploidentical HSCT in a prospective clinical trial with up to 36 months of post-HSCT follow-up. CMR assessments were conducted before HSCT and through the post-HSCT period. Echocardiographic parameters at 12 months post HSCT were compared with those of age-matched participants receiving disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Among 20 HSCT recipients (mean age 14.8 years), CMR demonstrated progressive reductions in biventricular volumes and left atrial volume over 36 months, with preservation of ejection fraction. Extra-cellular volume, a surrogate marker of myocardial fibrosis, showed significant improvement from baseline, having normalized in nearly all participants assessed at 36 months. Compared with age-matched DMT recipients, HSCT recipients had lower tricuspid regurgitant jet velocity and improved diastolic parameters at 12 months post-HSCT, with normalization of cardiac output on echocardiography. These findings demonstrate sustained reversal of myocardial fibrosis and structural cardiac remodelling after HSCT for SCD. HSCT may, therefore, modify the trajectory of SCD cardiomyopathy beyond the improvements achieved with current DMTs.

Title: Reduced Adverse Events Without Survival Benefit With HeartMate 3 vs. HeartMate II in Japan.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: HeartMate 3 (Abbott Laboratories), a fully magnetically levitated left ventricular assist device (LVAD), has shown improved hemocompatibility vs. previous devices, but nationwide real-world data in Japan remain limited.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese nationwide registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed patients who underwent de novo implantation of HeartMate 3 or HeartMate II between 2013 and 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, stroke, and device dysfunction requiring exchange or explantation within 2 years. In all, 978 patients were included in the study (HeartMate 3, n=486; HeartMate II, n=492). The 2-year cumulative incidence of the primary outcome was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group than in the HeartMate II group (9% vs. 23%; P<0.001). HeartMate 3 was independently associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.35; 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.51; P<0.001), which remained consistent in competing-risk and several statistically matched analyses. The incidence of hemocompatibility-related adverse events, including major bleeding, stroke, and device dysfunction, was significantly lower in the HeartMate 3 group. In contrast, 2- and 5-year overall mortality did not differ significantly between groups (<10% for both devices).
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide Japanese registry, HeartMate 3 reduced major LVAD-related complications without improving survival, supporting its clinical advantages in contemporary LVAD management.

Title: High Lipoprotein(a) Is a Predictor of Adverse Events and Heart Failure in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a well-established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but its prognostic role after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in patients with AMI.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 1,235 patients with AMI from the NARA-MI registry who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention and had serum Lp(a) measured at admission. Based on receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, patients were categorized into high (≥24 mg/dL) and low (<24 mg/dL) Lp(a) groups. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, recurrent AMI, HF hospitalization, or unplanned coronary revascularization. During a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 497 MACE events occurred. The incidence of MACE (48.0% vs. 38.3%; P=0.004) and HF hospitalization (9.3% vs. 5.0%; P=0.008) was significantly higher in the high Lp(a) group. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, high-Lp(a) independently predicted MACE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.73; P=0.001) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.15-3.04; P=0.016). Among patients with HF, 39.7% were classified as HFpEF.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after AMI, particularly HF. Measurement of Lp(a) may improve risk stratification after AMI and help identify patients at high risk of developing HF, including HFpEF.

Title: Transient apnoea for motion control during flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: a randomised trial.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether transient apnoea (TA) during flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy improves active lithotripsy efficiency compared with regular mechanical ventilation (RMV) and small tidal-volume ventilation (STVV).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-centre, three-arm randomised trial, 150 adults with a single computed tomography (CT)-confirmed renal, ureteropelvic, or proximal ureteric stone measuring 10-<20 mm were assigned one-to-one-to-one to RMV, STVV, or TA. TA followed 5-min 100% oxygen pre-oxygenation, with 9-min maximum and pre-specified stopping criteria under continuous anaesthetic monitoring. The primary endpoint was active lithotripsy efficiency, defined as CT-estimated stone volume divided by elapsed active lithotripsy time. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
RESULTS: The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm3/min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm3/min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm3/min) and 6.8 mm3/min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm3/min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative Day 1/1-month stone-free rates were 88%/92%, 80%/96%, and 88%/90%, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. The median (interquartile range) achieved apnoea duration was 5.0 (4.5-6.8) min; 46/50 resumed ventilation before the 9-min maximum, most commonly for heart-rate decline/bradycardia (n = 27) or blood-pressure decline/hypotension (n = 20). No patient had a peripheral oxygen saturation <90% or a Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥III complication; transient hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis improved after ventilation resumed.
CONCLUSION: Transient apnoea improved lithotripsy efficiency and shortened operative time compared with RMV and STVV, with higher surgeon-rated targeting stability. The benefit was primarily intraoperative, without evidence of greater postoperative stone clearance. Protocolised TA may provide a brief intraoperative motion-control option with pre-oxygenation, continuous anaesthetic monitoring, and individualised termination.

Title: Drug-Specific Associations of Angiotensin Receptor Blockers With Parkinson's Disease Risk in a Multicenter Electronic Health Record Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) have demonstrated neuroprotective effects in preclinical models of Parkinson's disease (PD), but individual ARBs differ in pharmacological properties that may influence their neuroprotective potential.
OBJECTIVES: Using large-scale hospital electronic health records of the University of California health system, we tested whether specific ARBs are associated with lower PD risk.
METHODS: We conducted a new-user, active-comparator cohort study in the University of California Health Data Warehouse, encompassing 890 712 hypertensive patients across six academic medical centers from 2012 to 2025. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios for individual ARB associations with incident PD, adjusting for demographics, nine preindex comorbidities, and index date. Robustness was assessed through propensity score matching and negative-control analysis.
RESULTS: Drug-specific Cox analysis identified irbesartan (HR = 0.588, 95% CI 0.434 to 0.796, p = 0.0006) and olmesartan (HR = 0.797, 95% CI 0.665 to 0.956, p = 0.015) as associated with lower PD risk. Irbesartan survived Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and propensity score matching supported both associations.
CONCLUSION: In this large multicenter EHR cohort, irbesartan and olmesartan were associated with lower incident Parkinson's disease risk. These findings support further investigation of the renin-angiotensin system as a therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease and may inform the development or repurposing of agents with favorable central nervous system penetration and neuroprotective potential.

Title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

Title: Perinatal Outcome of Sickle-cell Disease in Pregnancy: A Retrospective Cross-sectional Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sickle-cell disease (SCD) poses significant maternal and neonatal risks during pregnancy. Assessing the perinatal outcomes in pregnant women with homozygous SCD (HbSS) to optimize management strategies is the goal of this study.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, AIIMS Raipur, Chhattisgarh, over 18 months (September 1, 2021, to February 28, 2023). All pregnant women in the third trimester with HbSS admitted to the antenatal care ward were included. Patients with chronic hypertension, diabetes, renal diseases, thalassemia syndromes, or compound sickle-cell syndromes were excluded. Data on maternal and neonatal outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean hemoglobin at admission was 7.98 + 2.19 g/dL. 65.9% of women required antenatal transfusions. 38.2% of women developed sickle-cell crisis. 23.5% of women required intensive care unit admission in the antenatal and postnatal period. Notable was the mortality of 5.8% of women, which occurred in the postnatal period. 61.8% of women underwent cesarean section, with fetal distress as the most common indication. The mean birth weight was found to be 2.51 ± 0.47 kg. However, there was no neonatal mortality.
CONCLUSION: Optimizing perinatal care requires an understanding of the maternal and neonatal problems linked to SCD during pregnancy. This study emphasizes how crucial multidisciplinary management is to reducing unfavorable results.

Title: Evaluating Darbepoetin Treatment Strategies for Managing Anaemia in Haemodialysis Patients: Effects on All-Cause Mortality From a Target Trial Emulation Using Electronic Health Record Data.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Anaemia is a common complication of chronic kidney disease, often treated with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs), but the optimal haemoglobin (Hb) target remains uncertain. Using electronic health records, we emulated a target trial comparing different Hb targets in haemodialysis patients to estimate their effects on mortality.
METHODS: We used electronic health records from UK kidney centres reporting to the UK Renal Registry. Adults aged ≥ 18 years, receiving haemodialysis for ≥ 3 months, and without marked ESA resistance were eligible. Using the clone-censor-weight method, we emulated trials comparing Hb targets: (1) 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L and (2) 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L. Darbepoetin dosing followed a standardised protocol with predefined dose adjustments and a maximum dose of 150 μg/week. The outcome was all-cause mortality over 8 months.
RESULTS: The study included 8628 patients from 10 centres between 2004 and 2016; 62% male, median age 66 years (IQR 52-76). At baseline, mean Hb was 97.7 g/L (SD 15.1), and 79% of patients were receiving darbepoetin. The hazard ratio for mortality was 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.12) for the 105-125 versus 95-115 g/L comparison, and 1.20 (95% CI 0.94-1.54) for the 125-145 versus 95-115 g/L comparison. Adherence to the highest Hb target was lower, limiting precision.
CONCLUSIONS: Targeting an Hb range of 105-125 g/L under controlled ESA dosing was not associated with increased mortality compared with 95-115 g/L. Targeting Hb levels above 125 g/L may increase mortality risk, consistent with previous trial findings.

Title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.
Abstract:
AIMS: Hip fracture is a global health issue. Complications are common, leading to reduced quality of life or death. These occur more frequently if anaemia is present. We hypothesize that correcting anaemia in the perioperative period may decrease major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and death after hip fracture.
METHODS: This multicentre prospective randomized trial compares transfusion strategies after hip fracture in patients aged ≥ 60 years. We initially planned to randomize 1,984 participants with anaemia, defined as haemoglobin ≤ 90 g l-1, to one of two transfusion strategies: liberal transfusion (aim haemoglobin 90 g l-1 to 110 g l-1), or restrictive transfusion (aim 75 g l-1 to 90 g l-1). The intervention lasts from randomization to hospital discharge or 30 days post randomization, whichever is soonest. The primary outcome measure was a composite of death or MACE adjudicated by blinded clinical experts. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and quality of life, evaluated at 120 days. Cost-effectiveness and health economic evaluation will also be reported.
RESULTS: This trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, HTA award (National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) 130875) and registered at ISRCTN 28818784. Ethical approval was obtained to recruit patients in the UK. As recruitment fell short of the initial target, and following consultation with the funder, we refined our primary outcome to include myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery (MINS), and reduced the required sample size to 842.
CONCLUSION: Recruitment commenced on 10 June 2022. The first participant was recruited on 16 June 2022. We will engage clinicians and healthcare planners to implement the findings. We plan to recruit until 31 October 2026. Results will be disseminated to clinicians, policymakers, patients, and the public.

Title: Multi-center study of CMR versus cardiac catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy for pediatric transplant surveillance: study protocol.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract: Notwithstanding advances in post-transplant care, acute allograft rejection (AR) remains the leading cause of mortality in pediatric heart transplant recipients (PHTX). Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) continues to be the standard of care for AR detection, despite being invasive, costly, and associated with patient discomfort and potential complications. Non-invasive alternatives, including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) with T1 and T2 parametric mapping and blood biomarkers (BB) such as cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and microRNA (miRNA), have shown promise in the adult transplant population, but their validation in the pediatric transplant population is lacking. The "Predictive Modeling of Acute Rejection in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients" (PEACE) study is a prospective, multicenter trial aiming to assess the diagnostic accuracy of CMR and BB in comparison to EMB. The goal of this manuscript is to describe the purpose and experimental protocol of the PEACE study. The PEACE study's overarching hypothesis is that CMR and BB can consistently and accurately detect myocardial abnormalities, potentially guiding the need for EMB. Secondary objectives include cost-analyses of CMR and BB, as well as a biomarker performance evaluation in biopsy-negative, but symptomatic and suspected AR cases. PEACE will enroll PHTX ages 6-25 years, across approximately 20 U.S. pediatric hospitals. All subjects will undergo EMB for surveillance or suspected AR as standard of care. As part of the research protocol, subjects will undergo blood collection for BB prior to the EMB and CMR within 5 days of EMB. Central core labs will conduct blinded analysis for imaging, pathology, and biomarkers to ensure consistent data interpretation. PEACE represents a critical step in reducing reliance on invasive biopsies in the clinical care of PHTX. By validating non-invasive tools in a large, diverse population, the PEACE study could transform AR detection, resulting in improvement of the patient experience and outcomes in this vulnerable population. (Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07770659, Non-invasive Prediction of EArly Cardiac rEjection (PEACE)).

Title: A randomized controlled trial of a novel AI-based prognostic decision support tool integrated into the electronic health record for ischemic heart disease: Rationale and design of the PM Heart trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading global cause of years of life lost. Although the clinical presentation and progression of IHD differ widely, clinical management is relatively uniform. To improve risk stratification and clinical management, we developed a decision support tool - the PMHeartIHD Algorithm (also named PMHNet) - based on extensive clinical, registry and biochemical data. This algorithm automatically calculates one-year survival following an IHD event. We hypothesize that presenting the prognoses calculated by the PMHeartIHD Algorithm to the treating physicians will improve both the clinical management and outcome of the individual patient.
OBJECTIVE: The objectives of the PM Heart trial include clinical and technical aspects. First, the primary aim is to investigate if the clinical use of the prognosis calculated by the algorithm improves patient prognosis and minimizes the risk of re-hospitalization, compared to standard of care. A secondary objective is to generate knowledge on how decision support tools in cardiology may be implemented, received, and used directly in clinical practice.
METHODS: The PMHeartIHD Aalgorithm has been integrated into the electronic health record (EHR) system (Sundhedsplatformen (SP), EPIC) for clinical use. The PM Heart trial is designed as a multicenter, prospective, randomized, open-label, clinical trial, automatically enrolling and randomizing hospitalized patients with coronary artery disease at the cardiology departments in The Capital Region and Region Zealand in Denmark. Patients are randomized (1:1 ratio) immediately after coronary angiography, to either show or hide the calculated PMHeartIHD-prognosis or not in the electronic health record.
RESULTS: The primary outcome is a composite outcome consisting of re-admissions within 30 days and one-year survival rates after randomization. Inclusion began September 2023, and follow-up is expected to finish in 2026.
CONCLUSIONS: We present the design of and rationale for the PM Heart trial. Our aim is to assess the clinical value of implementing an artificial intelligence-based decision support tool in clinical practice.

Title: Trends in cardiovascular disease and risk factors between 2004 and 2021: Findings from the U.S. Millennium Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in the United States (U.S.). Military veterans have notably high prevalences of CVD. The study aimed to report the prevalence of self-reported CVD and risk factors among post-9/11 veterans from 2004 to 2021.
METHODS: The U.S. Millennium Cohort Study prospectively follows service members and veterans. Eligible participants enrolled in 2001, separated from the military by 2021, and provided CVD information post-separation. Data from cross-sectional snapshots were used to examine unadjusted and standardized prevalences of CVD and risk factors. Linear trends in prevalence tested for significant changes.
RESULTS: Among 43,769 participants (average baseline age 37.2) between 2004-2006 and 2019-2021, results show current smoking decreased from 23.7 to 8.2 per 100. Prevalence estimates for all other examined factors increased; obesity from 22.2 to 47.7 per 100, hypertension from 9.0 to 23.5 per 100, diabetes from 1.6 to 7.0 per 100. CVD outcomes were less common and increased from <0.8 to <3.0 per 100.
CONCLUSIONS: Among a population of post-9/11 veterans, most CVD factors increased between 2004 and 2021. Treatment and intervention programs targeted toward veterans transitioning to civilian life should consider weight management and healthy lifestyle factors related to CVD prevention.

Title: Differing subjective and psychophysiological response patterns to a music-based auditory intervention for anxiety.
Journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
Abstract: Anxiety comprises partially dissociable cognitive and somatic components, yet it remains unclear whether brief interventions are capable of modulating these systems in parallel. This randomized controlled trial examined subjective and psychophysiological responses to a brief personalized music-based auditory intervention relative to an active auditory control (pink noise) in undergraduate students reporting recent generalized anxiety symptoms. Participants (N = 83) were randomized to the auditory intervention or pink noise. Cognitive and somatic anxiety were assessed before and after the intervention, while salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), and electroencephalography (EEG) indexed endocrine, autonomic, and neural processes. Cortisol showed a significant Condition × Time interaction, with larger reductions following the auditory intervention. Midline theta power also exhibited a significant Condition × Time interaction, increasing numerically following the auditory intervention but decreasing significantly following pink noise. Cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, affective arousal, frontal alpha lateralization, and HRV did not show significant differential baseline-to-post change. During listening, HRV increased across conditions, but the Condition × Epoch interaction observed in the primary growth model was not retained when participant-specific slopes were included. Together, these findings indicate differing patterns of response across levels of analysis, with broad reductions in self-reported anxiety and arousal across both auditory conditions, but larger cortisol reductions and divergent midline theta responses in the primary analyses. Although the cortisol and theta interactions were not retained when all physiologically valid observations were included, both persisted under two different outlier-exclusion thresholds, suggesting meaningful condition-dependent responses that warrant further investigation.

Title: Serum Glycoprotein VI in Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Association With Radiological Thrombus Burden and Clinical Risk Indicators.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a life-threatening condition requiring rapid diagnosis and accurate risk stratification. Biomarkers reflecting thromboinflammatory processes may improve early clinical assessment. Glycoprotein VI (GPVI), a key receptor involved in platelet activation, has been implicated in thrombus formation; however, its clinical relevance in PE remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association of serum GPVI with radiological thrombus burden and clinical risk indicators in acute PE, while retaining the original PE-versus-control comparison only as a secondary exploratory case-control discrimination analysis, not as a diagnostic-accuracy analysis.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, the analytic cohort comprised 50 patients with CTPA-confirmed acute PE and 25 control participants. Serum soluble GPVI (sGPVI) was measured by a colorimetric sandwich ELISA. The study-recorded CTPA thrombus-burden categories were analyzed as lower, intermediate, and higher radiological burden and separately from an exploratory ESC-aligned risk reconstruction. For ICU admission, parsimonious multivariable and incremental analyses evaluated GPVI beyond PESI with internal validation. A PE-versus-control ROC comparison with D-dimer was retained only as a secondary exploratory case-control discrimination analysis and was not treated as an estimate of diagnostic accuracy.
RESULTS: Among patients with PE, GPVI differed across the study-recorded radiological burden categories (lower, n = 16: 192.95 [185.80-215.39]; intermediate, n = 13: 258.54 [238.60-276.29]; higher, n = 21: 307.90 [285.92-321.95] ng/L; p < 0.001). In the exploratory ESC-aligned analysis, GPVI differed across risk categories (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.045) and showed an ordinal association with increasing risk category (Spearman ρ = 0.331, p = 0.02). GPVI was higher in patients admitted to the ICU than in those not admitted (298.24 [278.42-315.89] vs. 206.17 [191.15-238.33] ng/L, p < 0.001) and had an ICU-admission AUC of 0.969. In a parsimonious model adjusted for PESI, GPVI remained associated with ICU admission (OR per 10 ng/L, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.36-3.92; p = 0.002), although the magnitude should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size, limited number of ICU events, and strong separation. These effect estimates are exploratory and should not be interpreted as stable clinical effect sizes. Adding GPVI to PESI increased the apparent AUC from 0.885 to 0.968 (ΔAUC, 0.083; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.013-0.200); the optimism-corrected AUC was approximately 0.954, and repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of approximately 0.916. In the secondary PE-versus-control analysis, GPVI was higher in PE (268.12 [215.39-298.47] vs. 114.07 [89.10-136.80] ng/L, p < 0.001) and showed an AUC of 0.968 versus 0.884 for D-dimer (ΔAUC, 0.084; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.008-0.168; p = 0.03); this case-control estimate is susceptible to spectrum bias and is not an estimate of real-world diagnostic accuracy.
CONCLUSION: Serum GPVI was associated with radiological thrombus burden and severity-related clinical indicators in acute PE. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of GPVI as a potential risk-stratification biomarker but do not establish diagnostic utility. Confirmation in larger, clinically representative prospective cohorts with hard clinical outcomes is required.

Title: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome. Current concepts, dilemmas, and challenges.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome (PAES) results from extrinsic compression of the popliteal artery as it passes through the popliteal fossa due to congenital musculotendinous anomalies or acquired muscle hypertrophy. The consequence of this compression is a progressive damage to the arterial wall, which can ultimately cause irreversible injury. This damage initially manifests as intermittent claudication, which usually occurs in young, athletic individuals with no cardiovascular risk factors. There may be an overlap of symptoms with other conditions, making diagnosis challenging. Beyond clinical suspicion, dynamic tests with provocation manoeuvres are essential. Early decompression treatment of symptomatic cases can prevent the onset of potentially serious complications, including amputation.
SOURCES OF DATA: This review integrates evidence from peer-reviewed literature focusing on popliteal entrapment syndrome.
AREAS OF AGREEMENT: Shortening the timeline from diagnosis to referral can help prevent irreversible damage to the arteries.There are a significant number of publications on PAES, based on retrospective single-centre experiences, short series or case reports, and limited scientific evidence. All publications repeatedly conclude that prospective multicentre studies are needed to standardize diagnostic and therapeutic protocols and develop guidelines for PAES.
AREAS OF CONTROVERSY: There are many points of disagreement regarding the management of PAES, and this does not help in addressing two key issues: avoiding misdiagnosis and unnecessary surgeries, which promote delayed diagnosis in worse clinical conditions.
GROWING POINTS: The creation of multicentre working groups seems necessary due to the limited number of cases at individual centres for conducting prospective studies.
AREAS TIMELY FOR DEVELOPING RESEARCH: Creation of international consensus protocols on definition, diagnosis, and treatment of PAES.

Title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
Abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications.
RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen.
SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

Title: Antithrombin III use in pediatric and neonatal ECMO: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract: BackgroundAntithrombin (AT) supplementation has been increasingly incorporated into pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) anticoagulation protocols to address heparin resistance and optimize anticoagulation. However, considerable variability exists in monitoring practices, replacement strategies, and reported clinical outcomes. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate contemporary evidence regarding AT supplementation in pediatric ECMO.MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies evaluating AT monitoring or supplementation during neonatal or pediatric ECMO through September 2025. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on monitoring strategies, replacement protocols, anticoagulation parameters, thrombosis, bleeding, and mortality. Comparative studies reporting extractable dichotomous outcomes were included in random-effects meta-analyses.ResultsTwenty-five studies met inclusion criteria, consisting predominantly of retrospective single-center cohorts. Marked heterogeneity was observed in indications for supplementation, replacement thresholds (50-100%), therapeutic targets (60-120%), formulations, dosing strategies, and anticoagulation monitoring. AT supplementation consistently increased AT activity, improved anti-factor Xa measurements, and in several studies, reduced unfractionated heparin requirement. However, higher anti-Xa levels and increased AT activity did not consistently translate into improved clinical outcomes. Meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between AT supplementation and thrombosis (OR 1.10, 95% 0.54-2.24), bleeding (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.85-1.54), or mortality (OR 1.24, 95% CI 0.63-2.43). Pharmacokinetic investigations suggested standard dosing frequently underestimates replacement requirements in pediatric ECMO.ConclusionCurrent evidence supports the role of AT supplementation in improving laboratory markers of anticoagulation, but does not demonstrate consistent reductions in bleeding, thrombosis, or mortality. Wide variation in monitoring, dosing, and outcome definitions limits comparisons across studies. Future multicenter investigations should prioritize standardized definitions, age-specific therapeutic targets, and prospective evaluation of replacement strategies to better define the role of AT supplementation in pediatric ECMO.

Title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear.
METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows.
DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Comparison of outcomes between transperitoneal and retroperitoneal robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the perioperative and functional outcomes of transperitoneal (TP) and retroperitoneal (RP) approaches in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) for renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
METHODS: A systematic literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted from inception to April 2026. Comparative studies that reported the outcomes of interest between TP RAPN and RP RAPN for renal cell carcinoma were included. Pooled effective sizes, including odds ratio (OR) and weighted mean differences (WMD) with 95 confidence intervals (CI), were estimated under fixed or random effect models. Further sensitivity analyses were performed to explore potential sources of heterogeneity. The study protocol was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261390561).
RESULTS: A total of 32 comparative studies were included, involving 6299 patients in the TP RAPN group and 4583 in the RP RAPN group, respectively. No significant differences were observed in baseline characteristics. Patients undergoing RP RAPN had a shorter operation time (OT, WMD: 15.53 min, 95%CI 9.24-21.83, P < 0.001), lower estimated blood loss (EBL, WMD: 32.34 ml, 95%CI 21.9-42.78, P < 0.001), and shorter length of stay (LOS, WMD: 0.42 days, 95%CI 0.22-0.63, P < 0.001) compared to TP RAPN. No significant differences were observed in warm ischemia time (WIT, P = 0.24), conversion to open or radical surgery (P = 0.11 and P = 0.18, respectively), positive surgical margin (PSM, P = 0.22), overall complications (P = 0.08), major complications (the Clavien-Dindo classification ≥ 3, P = 0.32), or postoperative renal function (postoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR): P = 0.22; postoperative 3-6 month eGFR: P = 0.49; postoperative 1-year eGFR: P = 0.55). Further sensitivity analyses validated the above findings.
CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that the RP RAPN may be superior to TP RAPN in terms of shorter OT, lower EBL, and shorter LOS. Nevertheless, given the limitations of this analysis, these findings should be interpreted cautiously, and further well-designed randomized controlled trials are required to validate our results.

Title: Indirect Echocardiographic Signs of Increased Right-sided Afterload in Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis: Insights from a Multicentre Italian Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Pulmonary vascular involvement is a determinant of worse outcomes in fibrotic lung diseases. Its prevalence and prognostic relevance in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) is unknown. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of indirect echocardiographic abnormalities in progressive pulmonary fibrosis before antifibrotic therapy, characterize a baseline high-risk cardiopulmonary functional profile, and assess 12-month clinical trajectories.
METHODS: Observational, retrospective, multicentre study.
RESULTS: 158 patients (median (IQR) age of 71 (65.2-77.0) years) with PPF were enrolled. Thirty (19.0%) had ≥ 1 echocardiographic indirect sign of increased right-sided afterload, 15 (9.5%) ≥ 2, 9 (5.7%) ≥ 3 and 1 (0.6%) all four. A shortened right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (< 105 ms) was the most frequent alteration (12.7%), followed by right atrial dilation (10.8%). In univariable analysis, ≥1 sign was associated with male sex, a lower DLCO% predicted, a higher FVC%/DLCO% ratio and a shorter 6MWD; in the multivariable model only, male sex remained independently associated (aOR 3.45, 95% CI 0.99-12.07; p = 0.052). Twelve-month FVC trajectories did not differ by baseline echocardiographic status; nonetheless, ≥1 sign was associated with shorter time to acute exacerbation (log-rank p = 0.007) and all-cause hospitalisation (p = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic signs suggestive of increased right-sided afterload are present in a substantial proportion of PPF patients at the time of antifibrotic initiation. They identified patients at higher risk of acute exacerbation and hospitalisation, regardless of FVC decline. This higher-risk subgroup warrants specific pulmonary vascular evaluation and tighter clinical follow-up.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Foundation Model-Enabled Pathology-Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
Abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

Title: β3-Adrenergic Receptor Agonism Reduces Right Ventricular Systolic Pressure in a Preclinical Model of Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular pharmacology and therapeutics
Abstract: PurposePulmonary hypertension (PH) commonly complicates heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), driving morbidity and mortality, yet no therapies exist for HFpEF-PH. β3-adrenergic receptor (ADRB3) agonists may provide cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory benefits. We evaluated pharmacological ADRB3 modulation in a preclinical HFpEF-PH model.MethodsHFpEF-PH was induced in male and female AKR/J mice via high-fat diet feeding for 16-20 weeks. At 12-16 weeks of feeding, mice were randomized to low-dose mirabegron (LDM, 3.6 mg/kg/day), high-dose mirabegron (HDM, 14.4 mg/kg/day), nebivolol (1.0 mg/kg/day), or vehicle for 4 weeks. A separate cohort received the ADRB3 antagonist SR59230A (0.5 mg/kg/day) or vehicle. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP), body weight change, and gene expression of nitric oxide synthases (Nos1, Nos2, Nos3), thermogenic markers (Ucp1, Ppargc1a), and inflammatory cytokines (Il1b, Il6, Tnf) were assessed.ResultsHDM and nebivolol significantly reduced RVSP compared to controls (P=0.010 and P=1.0×10-4), whereas SR59230A increased RVSP (P=0.006). LDM did not significantly affect RVSP, and LVEDP was unchanged across all treatment groups. HDM also reduced weight gain vs. control (P=0.023). HDM increased Ucp1 and Ppargc1a expression in adipose tissue, and nebivolol increased Ppargc1a expression in adipose tissue. These molecular findings remained significant in sensitivity analyses.ConclusionHDM and nebivolol reduced RVSP in a preclinical model of HFpEF-PH, whereas ADRB3 antagonism increased RVSP. These findings provide pharmacological evidence consistent with involvement of ADRB3 signaling and support further investigation of ADRB3-targeted approaches; the molecular pathways underlying these hemodynamic effects remain to be established.

Title: Endothelial dysfunction and long-term survival in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: An EASIX-based national cohort study.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the association of the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in adults at cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.MethodsThis retrospective analysis of a population-based cohort included 10,885 adults aged ≥30 years from NHANES 1999-2018, with mortality follow-up through 2019. EASIX was calculated as lactate dehydrogenase × creatinine/platelet count. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses evaluated mortality associations.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 97 months, 1,122 participants died, including 295 from cardiovascular causes. Each one-unit increase in EASIX was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.24-1.61) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.13-1.49). There was no evidence of non-linearity for all-cause mortality (P = 0.466), while the cardiovascular association was non-linear (P = 0.008). Associations persisted after additional lifestyle adjustment. CKM-stage interactions were not significant in the full cohort.ConclusionsHigher EASIX was associated with greater all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in CKM stages 0-3. Its potential role in clinical risk assessment warrants further validation.

Title: Outcomes After Major Amputation in Octogenarians.
Abstract: BackgroundMajor lower extremity amputations, defined as above-ankle amputations, are morbid and significantly life-changing. Older patients may be more susceptible to poor outcomes. Our goal was to assess the short- and long-term outcomes of major amputations in octogenarians.MethodsA retrospective single-center chart review was performed on all octogenarian patients who underwent a major amputation at a safety-net hospital between 2014-2023. Demographics, operative characteristics, postoperative outcomes, and 30-day and 1-year outcomes were collected and analyzed. Multivariable binary logistic regression evaluated factors associated with 1-year mortality. Fisher's exact test evaluated univariate categorical comparisons because of small cell frequencies.Results56 octogenarian patients underwent a major amputation: 96.4% underwent an amputation for chronic limb-threatening ischemia while 3.6% of patients had acute limb ischemia. Above-knee and below-knee amputations accounted for 73.2 and 26.8% of procedures, respectively; 10.6% were guillotine amputations. Intensive care unit (ICU) admission was required in 26.3% of cases, and total mean hospital length of stay (LOS) was 13.7 days. Postoperatively, 55.4% were discharged to a skilled nursing facility, 17.9% patients to an acute rehab facility, and 12.5% to home with assistance. Thirty-day emergency department use rate was 14.3%, and hospital readmission rate was 12.5%. Most patients (83.9%) were non-ambulatory at 1-year. In-hospital mortality was 8.9%, 30-day mortality was 14.3%, and 1-year mortality was 35.7%. Univariate analyses demonstrated no statistically significant differences among evaluated variables. Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was also not statistically significant.ConclusionMajor amputations in octogenarians are highly morbid with high ICU utilization and prolonged LOS with frequent discharge to acute care facilities. About one-third of patients are not alive at 1-year. These findings suggest the need to identify opportunities for improvement in this high-risk patient population undergoing amputations, such as early revascularization, aggressive rehabilitation in concert with geriatrician collaboration, medical optimization, and improved goals-of-care discussions.

Title: Cardiology Support Utilization Patterns and Associated Barriers Across Northwestern Ontario.
Abstract: The Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre On-Call Cardiology Support Service serves a geographically vast region across Northwestern Ontario where cardiovascular disease is a major burden. The objective is to analyze service utilization patterns including locations, indications, interventions, and barriers. In this 6-month prospective study, cardiologists collected data via survey on calls from rural and remote providers. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's exact test were used. The Canadian Institute for Health Information's Rural Health Systems Model was used for interpretation. Two hundred and six responses across 19 locations identified: common consultations-chest pain, dyspnea, and atrial fibrillation; frequent interventions-medical recommendations, education, and transfer decisions; key barriers-limited personnel knowledge and infrastructure. Significant associations were identified. This study characterized cardiology support service utilization across Northwestern Ontario, identifying key barriers and opportunities to strengthen rural health systems planning and cardiovascular care. These findings can inform targeted initiatives and support future evaluations.

Title: Clinical characteristics, risk factors, and prognosis of incidental and symptomatic hospital-acquired pulmonary embolism: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: ObjectivesTo compare the clinical characteristics, risk factors, and prognosis of incidental pulmonary embolism (IPE) and symptomatic pulmonary embolism (SPE), and to inform risk-stratified management.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed 287 patients with hospital-acquired pulmonary embolism (HA-PE). Demographic, clinical, imaging, and laboratory data were collected. Survival outcomes were assessed using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses.ResultsAmong 287 patients, 87 had IPE and 200 had SPE. IPE was more frequently classified as low-risk PE (63.22% vs. 31.50%, p < 0.001) and more often involved pulmonary artery branches (73.56% vs. 58.00%, p = 0.01), whereas SPE was more commonly intermediate- or high-risk. The 1-month survival rate was higher in the IPE group than in the SPE group (95.4% vs. 75.5%, hazard ratio [HR]: 5.95, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.51 - 16.5, p < 0.001), but this difference was not significant after 1 month. In IPE, cancer and bleeding were associated with increased mortality, whereas anticoagulation and lower PE risk categories were associated with reduced mortality. In SPE, cancer and immobilization were associated with increased mortality, whereas anticoagulation, thrombectomy, and lower PE risk categories were associated with reduced mortality.ConclusionsIPE is generally associated with lower-risk, more peripheral PE, but anticoagulation should be individualized. SPE requires prompt risk stratification and timely anticoagulation, with reperfusion or thrombectomy considered for selected high-risk or deteriorating patients.

Title: The "living well with lupus" lifestyle intervention: Effects on gut microbiota in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and high cardiovascular risk.
Abstract: BackgroundSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease associated with increased cardiovascular risk and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Although lifestyle can modulate the microbiome, the impact of multidisciplinary interventions in SLE remains unclear. Thus, the aim of the present study was to investigate the effects of a multidisciplinary lifestyle intervention on gut microbiota diversity and composition in women with SLE and high cardiovascular risk.Materials and methodsThis study analyzed a subsample (n = 31) from the "Living Well with Lupus" (LWWL) study, a 6-month randomized controlled trial. Patients were assigned to a lifestyle intervention + standard care (LWWL) or a standard care control group (CG). Gut microbiota (16S rRNA sequencing), fecal short-chainfatty acids (SCFAs), selected cardiovascular risk factors, dietary intake, and physical activity levels were assessed before and after the intervention.ResultsNo significant changes were observed in cardiovascular risk factors, food intake, or physical activity levels. Fecal SCFA concentrations and alpha/beta diversity also remained stable. Exploratory taxonomic analyses nevertheless identified distinct relative-abundance patterns across groups and time, including a numerical increase in the Firmicutes-to-Bacteroidota (F/B) ratio in LWWL and different trajectories of several SCFA-associated genera. Among these, Blautia and Parasutterella increased, whereas Butyricimonas, Coprococcus, and Odoribacter decreased from pre- to post-intervention in LWWL, with different trajectories observed in CG across these genera.ConclusionsThese findings suggest that taxonomic features of the gut microbiota may show compositional variation following a lifestyle intervention even in the absence of detectable changes in the measured cardiometabolic or behavioral outcomes. However, the functional and clinical significance of these exploratory taxonomic patterns remains uncertain and warrants further investigation.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Etomidate Versus Ketamine for Endotracheal Intubation in Critically Ill Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract: Rapid sequence intubation (RSI) is a commonly used technique for critically ill patients requiring emergency intubation, and the choice of induction agent is crucial for minimizing peri-intubation morbidity and maintaining hemodynamic stability. The most commonly used induction agents are etomidate and ketamine, although controversy remains about their effectiveness and safety. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis compared the efficacy and safety of etomidate versus ketamine for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2000 and May 2026 were systematically searched in PubMed, The Cochrane Library, and ScienceDirect. The included studies compared etomidate with ketamine for emergency endotracheal intubation in critically ill adults. We analyzed data with RevMan 5.4 and Mantel-Haenszel random-effects models and calculated risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Seven RCTs involving 5234 patients were included in the final analysis. No significant difference was observed between etomidate and ketamine regarding 28-day mortality (RR 1.01; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93-1.10; p=0.84), cardiac arrest (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.62-1.34; p = 0.64), failed intubation (RR 1.09; 95% CI 0.68-1.76; p=0.71), or vasopressor requirement (RR 1.27; 95% CI 0.94-1.72; p=0.13). Sensitivity analyses suggested possible hemodynamic differences between the two agents, which should be interpreted cautiously, and etomidate was relatively cardiovascularly stable in some analyses. Overall, etomidate and ketamine showed similar efficacy and safety for endotracheal intubation in critically ill patients. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two agents in mortality, cardiac arrest, failed intubation, or vasopressor use. Thus, clinicians should choose the induction agent on a case-by-case basis, based on patient, hemodynamic, and clinician-specific factors. Randomized trials in selected critically ill patient populations should be conducted on a larger scale.

Title: Prediction of acute mountain sickness risk by pre-plateau uric acid and albumin levels in Chinese young males: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To screen and identify pre-plateau hematological parameters that can predict the risk of acute mountain sickness (AMS) in individuals rapidly ascending to high altitudes.
METHODS: A total of 297 healthy adult males with an average age of 20.88 ± 1.76 years were included in the study. Baseline data were collected at an altitude of 300 m using questionnaire surveys, on-site testing, and hematological parameter tests (including routine blood and serum biochemical parameters with validated clinical detection systems). After ascending to an altitude of 4,200 m, the Lake Louise Score (LLS) 2018 and physiological indicator measurements were obtained on the second day. AMS was defined as an LLS 2018 ≥3 points accompanied by headache. A univariate logistic regression model was used to screen for the hematological parameters associated with AMS. Multivariate logistic regression was then used to adjust for covariates and determine the relationship between pre-plateau albumin (ALB) levels, uric acid (UA) levels, UA-to-ALB ratio (UAR), and AMS risk. Additionally, the predictive value was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, and the optimal cutoff value was determined using the Youden index. Finally, a subgroup analysis was conducted to determine the consistency of associations.
RESULTS: The incidence of AMS after arriving at the 4,200 m plateau was 29.97%. Univariate logistic regression analysis revealed associations between factors at 300 m, including heart rate, alcohol consumption, ALB, UA, and AMS. In the fully adjusted multivariate Model 3, pre-plateau ALB, UA, and UAR showed moderate predictive performance for AMS, with area under the ROC curve values of 0.710, 0.701, and 0.711, respectively (all P < 0.001). The optimal cutoff values were 47.25 g/L for ALB, 420.10 μmol/L for UA, and 7.45 for UAR. The UAR exhibited favorable predictive performance in populations with a body mass index <25 kg/m2, a history of low-altitude residence, or alcohol consumption.
CONCLUSION: Pre-plateau UA levels, ALB levels, and UAR are independent predictors of AMS risk in young healthy Chinese males. All three biomarkers exhibited moderate predictive performance, with the UAR showed particular utility in specific subgroups.

Title: Prevalence and Severity of Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis Across Glycemic Categories Among Patients Attending a Tertiary Care Hospital: A FibroScan-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hepatic steatosis is strongly associated with metabolic dysfunction and is common among individuals with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Noninvasive assessment using controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) may help characterize hepatic steatosis and fibrosis risk. This study evaluated the distribution and severity of hepatic steatosis and liver fibrosis across glycemic categories in patients undergoing FibroScan assessment at a tertiary care hospital.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional observational study included 350 adults who underwent FibroScan assessment at a tertiary care hospital. We assessed hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness using the FibroScan Compact 530 (Echosens, Paris, France). We recorded the probe type (M or XL) where available. We performed examinations according to the manufacturer's recommendations after the required fasting period. We used LSM (kPa) to assess hepatic fibrosis and CAP (dB/m) to assess hepatic steatosis. We assigned steatosis and fibrosis categories using prespecified CAP and LSM thresholds from the clinical FibroScan protocol. We categorized participants as nondiabetic, prediabetic, or with T2DM. In addition to unadjusted chi-square analyses, multivariable ordinal logistic regression assessed associations between glycemic category and increasing steatosis and fibrosis severity, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, dyslipidemia, alcohol use, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and relevant antidiabetic medications. We assessed the proportional-odds assumption and used multinomial logistic regression when it was not met. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs), 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and model diagnostics were reported.
RESULTS: Among 350 participants, 82 were nondiabetic, 102 prediabetic, and 166 had T2DM. Steatosis severity differed significantly across glycemic categories (χ² = 28.96, df = 6, p < 0.001). Severe steatosis (S3) occurred in 2.4% of nondiabetic, 6.9% of prediabetic, and 18.7% of T2DM participants. After adjustment, prediabetes (aOR: 2.22, 95% CI: 1.26-3.94; p = 0.006) and T2DM (aOR: 3.58, 95% CI: 1.58-8.14; p = 0.002) were independently associated with greater steatosis severity compared with nondiabetic status. Higher BMI and ALT were also independently associated with greater steatosis severity. Fibrosis distribution did not differ significantly across glycemic groups (χ² = 3.49, df = 4, p = 0.480). In the adjusted fibrosis model, prediabetes was not significantly associated with greater fibrosis severity (aOR: 1.09, 95% CI: 0.36-3.25; p = 0.880), while T2DM showed higher but nonsignificant odds (aOR: 2.98, 95% CI: 0.81-10.96; p = 0.102). Age and ALT were independently associated with greater fibrosis severity.
CONCLUSION: In this tertiary care FibroScan-evaluated cohort, hepatic steatosis was increasingly severe across worsening glycemic categories, with the greatest burden observed among participants with T2DM. The association between glycemic status and steatosis remained significant after adjustment for major metabolic and clinical covariates, whereas the adjusted association between glycemic status and fibrosis was not statistically significant. These findings support using noninvasive liver assessment for metabolic risk stratification in individuals with prediabetes and T2DM, while recognizing that transient elastography does not establish a histological diagnosis of steatohepatitis.

Title: Impact of an integrated hospital-community care pathway on the management of venous thromboembolism: the venous thromboembolic disease care pathway 93 study.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) carries a high risk of recurrence and bleeding complications. Care transitions represent a vulnerable period, particularly in medically underserved areas where loss to follow-up is common. Integrated hospital-community care pathways may improve outcomes, but data are limited.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether an integrated hospital-community care pathway for patients with venous thromboembolism was associated with improved clinical outcomes and continuity of care compared with standard care.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, observational study of 161 consecutive patients managed for VTE in the day hospital at Avicenne Hospital (Bobigny, France) from December 2022 to December 2024. Patients enrolled in a structured city hospital care pathway (n = 64) were compared with those receiving standard care (n = 97). The primary endpoint was a composite of thrombotic recurrence, bleeding, hospitalization, or death. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to address confounding.
RESULTS: The structured pathway was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite endpoint (hazard ratio [HR], 0.44; 95% CI, 0.21-0.93; P = .03), consistent with the inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.21-0.92; P = .03). Loss to follow-up was markedly lower in the structured pathway group (7.8% vs 30%; P = .002), and patients lost to follow-up had a 3.5-fold higher risk of complications (HR, 3.50; 95% CI, 1.71-7.18; P < .001). Enrollment in the pathway was associated with lower odds of loss to follow-up (odds ratio, 0.21; 95% CI, 0.07-0.53; P = .002).
CONCLUSION: In this single-center, retrospective cohort study, a structured city hospital care pathway was associated with a lower risk of composite complications and a lower loss-to-follow-up rate among patients managed for VTE. These findings support the potential value of integrated care coordination pathways, particularly in medically underserved areas.

Title: In situ Simulation as a Training Tool in a Tertiary Pediatric Emergency Department in Italy: Enhancing Preparedness Where it Matters.
Journal: Advances in medical education and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In situ simulation differs from in-centre simulation as it is conducted in the actual clinical environment rather than a simulation laboratory, thereby enhancing contextual realism and enabling identification of system-level vulnerabilities within clinical workflows.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of in situ simulation on self-perceived competence, clinical performance, team dynamics, and system readiness in a tertiary pediatric emergency department in Italy.
METHODS: This prospective single-center observational study was conducted in a tertiary pediatric emergency department in Italy. A total of 55 healthcare professionals participated in 11 high-fidelity in situ simulation sessions. Participants completed pre- and post-intervention self-assessment questionnaires using a Likert-scale instrument developed for the study. Clinical performance was evaluated using a structured ABCDE-based checklist. No formal qualitative interviews were conducted. Statistical analysis was performed using paired t-tests with a significance threshold of p<0.05.
RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed across all assessed domains, particularly in ABCDE assessment, ventilation, and defibrillator use (p<0.001). Junior residents and participants without recent EPALS certification demonstrated the greatest improvement. In situ simulation also identified latent safety threats related to equipment availability and clinical workflow.
CONCLUSION: In situ simulation improves perceived clinical competence and team performance while providing actionable insights into system-level safety vulnerabilities. Future research should incorporate objective performance metrics and validated assessment tools.

Title: Cardiovascular exercise mitigates inflammation in the early subacute phase of stroke recovery: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive inflammation in early phases post-ischemic stroke is associated with poor long-term outcome and increased stroke recurrence. Interventions capable of downregulating persistent states of inflammation could improve recovery and prevent secondary stroke. Cardiovascular exercise (CE) has well-established anti-inflammatory effects but its capacity to attenuate the exaggerated inflammatory response triggered by ischemic stroke is unclear.
METHODS: We investigated the impact of eight weeks of CE on the serum concentration of inflammatory mediators in the early subacute phase post-stroke. Seventy-one patients with first-ever ischemic stroke were randomly assigned to moderate-to-vigorous CE (n = 45) or standard care (SC) (n = 26). Concentrations of CRP, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α and IL-1β were measured at baseline and after the interventions. Differences between groups were analyzed with linear mixed models adjusted for age and sex.
RESULTS: Compared with the CE group, the SC group showed significant increases in IL-6 (β = 0.585, 95% CI = 0.164-1.006, p = 0.0073), IL-8 (β = 0.160, 95% CI = 0.004-0.317, p = 0.0447), and TNF-α (β = 0.0845, 95% CI = 0.0137-0.1553, p = 0.0206). The SC group also showed greater increases in CRP (β = 0.250, 95% CI = -0.407, 0.906, p = 0.4499) and IL-10 (β = 0.251, 95% CI = -0.024, 0.527, p = 0.0729) but group differences were not significant. IL-1β levels remained stable and differences between groups were not significant (β = -0.008, 95% CI = -0.058, 0.042, p = 0.7618).
CONCLUSIONS: When introduced in the early subacute phase of stroke recovery, moderate-to-vigorous CE mitigates increases in inflammation, but the effect differs across mediators. To what extent reducing the inflammatory response in the early stages post-stroke with CE can impact long-term recovery and stroke recurrence needs to be determined.

Title: Baseline Serum HMGB1 and the Composite of All-Cause Mortality or First Heart Failure Rehospitalization in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between baseline serum high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) and the composite of all-cause mortality or first heart failure rehospitalization in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort included 224 patients with HFpEF. The primary endpoint was the first occurrence of all-cause mortality or heart failure rehospitalization.
RESULTS: During a median observation time of 58 months, 37 of 224 patients (16.5%) experienced the composite endpoint. Baseline HMGB1 was higher in patients with events than in those without events (8.76 ± 3.18 vs 5.99 ± 1.86 µg/L; P<0.001). After adjustment for NT-proBNP, age, and sex, each 1 µg/L increase in HMGB1 was associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint (hazard ratio, 1.399; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.242-1.576; P<0.001). Apparent areas under the curve were 0.753 (95% CI, 0.653-0.853) for HMGB1, 0.790 (95% CI, 0.708-0.872) for NT-proBNP, and 0.870 (95% CI, 0.793-0.947) for their combination. The combination did not significantly outperform NT-proBNP alone (ΔAUC, 0.080; 95% CI, -0.012 to 0.171; nominal P=0.088; Holm-adjusted P=0.176). The optimism-corrected Cox concordance index was 0.828, and sensitivity analyses showed associations in the same direction.
CONCLUSION: Higher baseline serum HMGB1 was associated with the composite of all-cause mortality or first heart failure rehospitalization in this exploratory HFpEF cohort. Incremental discrimination beyond NT-proBNP and clinical utility remain unestablished. Independent prospective multicenter validation is required.

Title: Pro-inflammatory cytokines moderated by visceral adiposity from a pragmatic randomized crossover trial of portable HEPA air purifiers.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airborne particulate matter (PM) increases the risk of cardiovascular disease. High efficiency particulate arrestance (HEPA) filtration can reduce indoor PM, but evidence is lacking as to whether HEPA filtration has an effect on pro-inflammatory cytokines.
METHODS: This pragmatic crossover trial randomly assigned participants to 30 days of HEPA or sham filtration, followed by a 30-day washout, and then 30 days of the alternative. Concentrations of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) were measured in quality-controlled peripheral blood plasma samples using ultra-sensitive assays. Linear mixed models compared HEPA to sham filtration. The moderating effect of visceral adipose tissue (VAT) was assessed using a dichotomized A Body Shape Index (ABSI) z-score and other measures of adiposity.
RESULTS: Among 116 participants, mean age was 41.5 years, 58.6% were female, and 72.4% were non-Hispanic White. No overall difference in mean IL-1β concentration was observed between HEPA and sham filtration. However, VAT significantly moderated the results (test for interaction p = 0.001). Among participants with excessive VAT (ABSI z-score ≥ +0.229, N = 12), HEPA filtration significantly reduced mean IL-1β concentration by 22.8% compared with sham filtration (0.138 versus 0.179 pg/mL, p < 0.001). No reduction was observed among participants with healthy VAT. Similar non-significant patterns were observed for IL-6, but little effect for hsCRP. Other measures of adiposity, including BMI, were less effective or did not moderate the results.
CONCLUSIONS: VAT moderated inflammatory responses to HEPA filtration, with a significant reduction in IL-1β among participants with excessive VAT.

Title: Association of adverse pregnancy outcomes with coronary microvascular dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) are recognized cardiovascular risk enhancers, yet their association with coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) has not been systematically quantified.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between APOs and CMD and to provide pooled estimates of CMD prevalence and severity in women with APO history.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched through December 2025. Observational studies evaluating coronary microvascular function using PET, Doppler echocardiography, stress CMR, or invasive physiology in women with APOs versus controls were included. Multivariate random-effects meta-analysis was performed to account for non-independent effect estimates arising from shared control groups. Risk of bias was assessed using NOS; certainty of evidence using GRADE.
RESULTS: Five studies (1,183 participants; 583 APO, 600 controls) were included. Women with APO history demonstrated significantly reduced CFR (SMD -0.94; 95% CI, -1.43 to -0.45; p<0.0001; I²=88.2%) and elevated CMD prevalence (OR 6.74; 95% CI, 1.55-29.42; p0.011; I²=92.2%). An exploratory graded pattern was observed, with combined preeclampsia and gestational diabetes associated with the largest CFR reduction (SMD -1.27); however, this was driven primarily by a single study with shared controls. Publication bias assessment was non-significant for CFR (p0.312) but borderline for CMD prevalence (p0.078).
CONCLUSIONS: APOs are associated with reduced CFR and elevated CMD prevalence, suggesting CMD may represent a plausible intermediate phenotype linking pregnancy complications to long-term cardiovascular disease. Given low to very low certainty evidence and substantial heterogeneity, these findings are hypothesis-generating and support further prospective research.

Title: Effectiveness of Yoga-based guided meditation In Improving the quality of sleep in patients with coronary artery disease: The Yoga Nidra Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor sleep quality has emerged as a risk for coronary artery disease (CAD) and is also associated with poor prognosis and increased mortality. Sleep aids, among CAD patients, lead to increased heart failure, hospitalisation, and mortality. Yoga Nidra, a form of guided meditation, has been shown to improve sleep quality and duration. The aim of the study is to evaluate the adjunctive effect of Yoga Nidra on actigraphy-measured sleep quality parameters, psychological outcomes, and health-related quality of life in patients with CAD.
METHODS: This is a two-arm,1:1 allocation, randomised, controlled, open-label, blinded-endpoint, single-centre trial conducted in a tertiary care hospital between 22-9-2021 and 30-03-2024.144 out of 678 consecutively screened patients with stable CAD and poor sleep quality met the eligibility criteria and were enrolled. Participants were randomised to either a 35-minute, 12-week Yoga Nidra intervention group (n = 72) or a standard care group (n = 72) with sleep hygiene counselling imparted to all patients.The primary outcome was to assess actigraphy-measured sleep efficiency. Secondary outcomes included assessments of actigraphy-derived sleep parameters, ambulatory blood pressure (BP), echocardiographic diastolic function (E/E'), psychological health, and quality-of-life evaluations using validated scales.
RESULTS: The Yoga Nidra group exhibited significant improvements in sleep efficiency (82% [76-86] vs. 64% [57-74]; p < 0.05), total sleep time (357 ± 99 min vs. 298 ± 83 min; p < 0.05), reduced sleep latency (15 [11-24] vs. 30 [14-70] min; p < 0.05), and lower wake after sleep onset (48 [28-67] vs. 67 [37-119] min; p < 0.05). Significant improvements were also observed in perceived stress, depression levels, and quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Yoga Nidra is effective in improving sleep quality inpatients with coronary artery disease.Stress, depression, and health-related quality of life also improved with Yoga Nidra.

Title: Prehospital extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a protocol for the Rapid prehospital ACcess to ECPR in Prague (RACE Prague) single-arm pilot feasibility study.
Abstract:
AIM: The benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is strongly time dependent, yet in established in-hospital ECPR systems, including Prague, the median collapse-to-flow time has remained around 60 min or more, dominated by intra-arrest transport. Evidence for prehospital ECPR remains limited, particularly its comparison with in-hospital ECPR. RACE Prague evaluates whether dispatching a mobile cannulation team to the scene shortens this interval within the same ECPR system.
METHODS: Single-centre, prospective, interventional, single-arm pilot feasibility study. Twenty adults aged 18-70 years with witnessed refractory OHCA (three unsuccessful defibrillations and/or ≥10 min of resuscitation in pulseless electrical activity), receive prehospital percutaneous femoro-femoral veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) from a mobile ECPR team.
