Furthermore, significant improvements were also observed in muscle mass and endurance capacity (p < 0.05), as well as in health-related quality of life, including vitality [baseline-adjusted ANCOVA: p = 0.042, adjusted mean difference = 6.94 (0.29 to 13.6)] and mental health [p < 0.001, g = 1.61 (0.53 to 2.68)]. Handgrip strength was preserved in INT despite a significant decline in CON (p = 0.042). In secondary exploratory analyses, HDL cholesterol increased, and HbA1c decreased (p < 0.05). Echocardiography revealed no adverse structural or functional cardiac adaptations, and no adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: A brief, twice-weekly low-load cycling program combined with BFR elicited significant rises in lower-limb strength with associated clinically meaningful improvements in mobility despite a minimal exercise dose. Endurance-based BFR appears to be a feasible, safe, and well-tolerated strategy to improve physical function and support independent living in healthy older adults. This trial was not prospectively registered in a public trial registry. It was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (registration number: NCT07825987).

Title: Efficacy of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in Urinary and Fecal Symptoms Caused by Rectocele and Cystocele.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) has received increasing interest and application as a noninvasive modality for the local treatment of solid tumors. In this study, we aim to evaluate the efficacy of HIFU in rectocele and cystocele.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical trial study was conducted on patients who have symptomatic grade 1 and 2 rectocele and cystocele. All patients randomized in two groups; one received HIFU therapy, and the other group underwent Kegel exercises on a daily basis. All patients were followed 2 and 6 months after intervention. The efficacy of HIFU therapy and Kegel exercises were measured based on the pelvic floor discomfort index questionnaire (PFDI-20) and Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI).
RESULTS: Both Kegel exercises and HIFU improved the scores of all sections of FSFI and PFDI questionnaires (P value < 0.05) significantly. Our data in comparison of Kegel exercises versus HIFU therapy showed no significant difference.
CONCLUSION: Our data showed good results in both sexual function and urinocolorectal symptoms after HIFU therapy.

Title: Associations between inflammatory-lipid indices and clinical outcomes in ischemic stroke patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Inflammation and dyslipidemia are critical in post-stroke prognosis. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of six common inflammatory-lipid indices to evaluate the associations between these indices and four clinical outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), and to identify generalizable consistently associated markers for all four clinical outcomes.
METHODS: In this retrospective studyassociations between inflammatory-lipid indices, namely monocyte-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (MHR), platelet-to-HDL-C ratio (PHR), neutrophil-to-HDL-C (NHR), lymphocyte-to-HDL-C ratio (LHR), fibrinogen-to-HDL-C ratio (FHR), and C-reactive protein-to-HDL-C ratio (CRP/HDL-C), and four post-MT clinical outcomes comprised hemorrhagic transformation (HT), malignant cerebral edema (MCE) 90-day unfavorable outcome and all-cause mortality were evaluated using multivariable analyses. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied for multiple comparisons. NHR, which demonstrated consistent significance for all four clinical outcomes, was subjected to further analyses.
RESULTS: A total of 513 patients were included., demonstrated The incidences of HT, MCE, unfavorable outcome, and all-cause mortality were 30.6% (157), 22.6% (116), 54.8% (281), and 25.9% (133), respectively. The NHR was significantly associated with all four clinical outcomes (HT: odds ratio [OR] 1.079, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.023-1.142, p-FDR = 0.034; MCE: OR 1.089, 95% CI 1.031-1.154, p-FDR = 0.008; unfavorable outcome: OR 1.177, 95% CI 1.098-1.269, p-FDR < 0.001; all-cause mortality: hazard ratio [HR] 1.047, 95% CI 1.012-1.084, p-FDR = 0.022). In the subgroup analysis for all-cause mortality, an interaction between NHR and TOAST classification was observed (p for interaction = 0.023), indicating that the association with all-cause mortality was pronounced in patients with cardioembolic stroke (HR 1.109, 95% CI 1.055-1.165). Mediation analysis showed that HT (23.9%, p < 0.001) and MCE (23.8%, p < 0.001) statistically accounted for part of the associations between NHR and unfavorable outcome. The relationship between NHR and unfavorable outcome may be partially mediated by HT (23.9%, p < 0.001) and MCE (23.8%, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: NHR may serve as a potentially useful complementary marker of post-MT HT, MCE, unfavorable outcome, and all-cause mortality. Its association with all-cause mortality appears stronger in patients with cardioembolic stroke. HT and MCE may act as mediators linking NHR to unfavorable outcomes. External validation is required to verify these findings.

Title: Divergent aortic root cusp-to-cusp measurement techniques on CMR: geometric implications and threshold reclassification.
Journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate discrepancies between current European guidelines (ESC vs. EACTS) regarding aortic root cusp-to-cusp measurements and assess their impact on risk stratification for prophylactic root replacement.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A retrospective analysis was performed on a relative young cohort of 50 patients (mean age 42 years) who underwent non-contrast 3D cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging. We compared the widest-to-widest cusp measurements and the middle cusp-to-cusp measurements with each other and against a traced aortic root perimeter. The widest cusp-to-cusp measurement yielded systematically higher values compared to the middle measurement, showing a significant mean difference of 3.60 mm (P < 0.001). The middle measurement demonstrated better statistical agreement with the traced aortic root perimeter, achieving a Lin's Concordance Correlation Coefficient (CCC) of 0.98 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 3.96 mm. Conversely, widest cusp-to-cusp measurements exhibited substantially lower agreement (CCC 0.80) and significantly higher error rates (MAE 16.88 mm), consistently overestimating the perimeter. This led to the upward reclassification of 10.0% (5/50) and 16.0% (8/50) of patients across the 40 and 45 mm guideline thresholds, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Cusp-to-cusp measurement techniques recommended by ESC and EACTS produce systematically divergent aortic root dimensions, resulting in significant patient reclassification across clinical thresholds. Although the middle measurement aligns more closely with the traced anatomical perimeter, the principal finding of this study is that guideline choice fundamentally alters patient categorization. Standardization of aortic root measurement conventions is essential to ensure consistent international care, improve research comparability, and reconcile historical risk thresholds with modern 3D imaging.

Title: Treatment context is associated with thrombocytopenia report phenotypes in lung cancer: an active-comparator analysis of FAERS and JADER.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombocytopenia during immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment in lung cancer may be coded as immune, marrow suppression, coagulation, or non-specific. We tested whether coding-defined report phenotypes differed across co-reported treatment contexts.
METHODS: We analyzed FAERS (2015Q1-2026Q2) and JADER through Japanese fiscal 2025Q4 (31 March 2026). Strict primary lung cancer reports were grouped as ICI without chemotherapy (C1), ICI plus chemotherapy (C2), or chemotherapy without ICI (C3). Firth models compared mutually exclusive immune-like and marrow-like anchors. Complementary analyses evaluated the broad cohort, treatment date compatibility, C3 small-cell influence, phenotype variants, onset windows, treatment-variable ablation in elastic-net report phenotype models, and a 120-report random stratified blinded review with independent ratings, third-person adjudication, inverse-selection weighting, and bootstrap uncertainty.
RESULTS: FAERS included 1,362 immune-like or marrow-like anchors. Relative to C1, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for immune-like versus marrow-like phenotype were 0.111 (95% CI, 0.069-0.173) in C2 and 0.014 (0.006-0.029) in C3; C3 was exploratory because only eight reports were immune-like. In 2,835 broad cohort reports, adjusted immune-like composition was 13.0% (95% bootstrap interval, 11.0%-15.1%) in C1 and 4.7% (3.4%-6.2%) in C2. Treatment date and stricter phenotype analyses were directionally consistent. JADER reproduced the C2 versus C1 direction but showed calibration shift; treatment-variable ablation reduced cross-database discrimination. Reviewers agreed on 111/120 reports (92.5%; 95% CI, 87.5%-96.7%; Cohen's κ, 0.897; Gwet's AC1, 0.901). In the locked 927-report frame, design-weighted final categories were 23.4% immune probable, 37.3% immune possible, 13.6% indeterminate, and 25.8% non-immune probable. Among 100 determinate reports, weighted AUROC was 0.892 (0.827-0.948), PR-AUC 0.956 (0.922-0.982), and calibration-in-the-large intercept 2.054 (1.707-2.432), indicating underprediction.
CONCLUSION: Coding-defined thrombocytopenia report composition differed across treatment contexts. Blinded review supported reproducible structured category assignment and score-based report ordering, while calibration shift and treatment-variable ablation defined important limits. Findings support pharmacovigilance case prioritization and hypothesis generation, not clinical diagnosis, incidence estimation, patient-level etiologic attribution, or causal inference.

Title: microRNA-15b modulates stress-induced premature senescence in chronic doxorubicin cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Doxorubicin (DOX) is the most widely used anthracycline in hematologic and solid tumors, whose clinical utility is constrained by dose-dependent cumulative cardiotoxicity that can progress to chronic heart failure. Although previously attributed to overt cardiomyocyte loss, emerging evidence indicates that stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS) constitutes the dominant mechanism of chronic cardiotoxicity at clinically relevant concentrations. SIPS is defined by permanent cell cycle arrest, activation of the p53/p21 and p16/Rb tumor suppressor axes, mitochondrial dysfunction, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) that sustains a pro-inflammatory myocardial milieu. Nevertheless, the post-transcriptional mechanisms that govern this process remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: The post-transcriptional regulation of DOX-induced SIPS was evaluated in vitro using neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) exposed to sublethal DOX (0.1 μM) with or without prophylactic miR-15b restoration via a synthetic mimetic to assess the p53/p21, p16, SASP, lysosomal, and mitochondrial responses. In vivo, a chronic cardiotoxicity model was established in female C57BL/6 mice receiving a cumulative dose of 30 mg/kg DOX to analyze myocardial miR-15b suppression, SIPS markers, and SASP profiles across survival cohorts.
RESULTS: Sublethal DOX treatment (0.1 μM) suppressed miR-15b expression by approximately 50% in NRVMs, resulting in post-transcriptional derepression of its mitochondrial target, SIRT4. This miR-15b loss triggered a multiparametric SIPS phenotype encompassing accumulation of γH2AX foci, p53/p21 and p16 activation, SASP induction (IL-6, IL-1β, Mcp-1 and Mmp13), lysosomal dysfunction (increased SA-β-Gal staining) and mitochondrial dysfunction. Prophylactic restoration of miR-15b via a synthetic mimetic selectively attenuated the p53/p21 axis, genomic damage foci, lysosomal dysfunction, mitochondrial dysfunction and SASP (IL-6 and IL-1β), without rescuing the p16/Rb pathway. In the female C57BL/6 chronic cardiotoxicity model, the cohort spontaneously stratified into animals completing the protocol (ND; 67%) and a premature death subgroup (PD; 33%). The PD subgroup exhibited the most profound myocardial miR-15b suppression and greater accumulation of SIPS markers, including γH2AX, p16, and reduced Lamin B. Notably, the SASP displayed distinct qualitative profiles between PD and ND animals, suggesting that SASP composition, rather than magnitude alone, determines the cardiotoxic outcome.
CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings position miR-15b as a key post-transcriptional regulator of DOX-induced SIPS in the cardiomyocyte, whose sustained loss associates with cardiotoxicity severity in vivo.

Title: World Stroke Organization mechanical thrombectomy workshops combined with the Global Stroke Alliance builds regional capacity.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Access to mechanical thrombectomy (MT) remains limited in many low- and middle-income or resource-limited regions because of gaps in trained personnel, procedural experience, public awareness, and stroke-system readiness. The World Stroke Organization paired simulation-based MT workshops with the Global Stroke Alliance to combine hands-on neurointerventional education with regional advocacy, Ministry of Health engagement, public awareness activities, and stakeholder collaboration. This study evaluated the feasibility, scalability, and self-reported educational impact of MT workshops delivered within this broader WSO/GSA capacity-building framework.
METHODS: A comprehensive 22-h curriculum was developed, incorporating didactic sessions, hands-on simulations, and complex case studies in collaboration with the Global Stroke Alliance between August 2023 and July 2025. The workshops were designed for neurointerventional physicians and tailored to regional needs. Pre- and post-course assessments measured physician confidence in MT procedures, while a three-month follow-up survey evaluated changes in MT volumes and clinical practice. Data were analyzed using summary statistics, chi-square tests, and McNemar's tests as appropriate.
RESULTS: Among 112 participating physicians from 24 countries, 81% completed the pre-test and 72% completed the post-test; 67% had paired pre- and post-test responses. The proportion of participants rating themselves as "very comfortable" increased from 15% pre-workshop to 41% post-workshop (p < 0.001), with notable improvements in patient selection for MT (15-48%, p < 0.001), procedural access knowledge (15-46%, p < 0.001), thrombectomy technique (9-41%, p < 0.001), and avoiding harmful maneuvers (7-33%, p < 0.001). At 3 months, 32 participants completed follow-up, of whom 37.5% self-reported an increase in overall thrombectomy numbers.
CONCLUSION: Simulation-based MT workshops are feasible and scalable across multiple regions and were associated with improved self-reported procedural confidence and early self-reported changes in clinical practice. These findings support structured hands-on training as one component of broader capacity-building efforts, while highlighting the need for objective procedural volume, patient outcome, and registry-based data to determine the effect of such programs on MT access and stroke care delivery.

Title: Incremental value of dedicated [201Tl] cadmium-zinc-telluride thallium SPECT over rest/stress [99mTc] technetium sestamibi SPECT MPI: a comparative analysis of fixed perfusion defects.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rest/stress [99mTc]technetium sestamibi single-photon emission computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (SPECT MPI) is a mainstay for evaluating coronary artery disease. However, fixed defects on standard MPI present a well-documented clinical challenge, as they can represent either non-viable scars or viable hibernating myocardium. We aimed to examine the incremental value and rate of diagnostic reclassification provided by performing subsequent dedicated cadmium-zinc-telluride (CZT) [201Tl]thallium myocardial SPECT in patients presenting with fixed defects on standard sestamibi MPI.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed 174 patients-totaling 2,958 myocardial segments-who underwent both protocols. Intermodality correlation was assessed, and the rates of segmental and patient-level reclassification (segments converting from <50% maximum uptake on sestamibi to ≥50% maximum uptake on thallium) were quantified.
RESULTS: While a moderately high correlation was observed between the baseline uptake scores of the two modalities (Spearman's r = 0.817 for rest sestamibi vs. thallium), thallium imaging provided substantial additional information, with 48.0% of segments classified as fixed defects on sestamibi SPECT demonstrating improved uptake on thallium SPECT. At the patient level, 78.9% of individuals who had fixed defects on the initial sestamibi SPECT had at least one segment reclassified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that a rest sestamibi uptake score of <20% predicted a lack of reclassification with 99% specificity, although with low sensitivity (12%).
CONCLUSION: In a selected cohort of patients presenting with fixed defects on standard rest/stress sestamibi SPECT MPI, supplementary imaging with thallium myocardial CZT SPECT provided incremental data, altering the clinical interpretation in nearly 80% of patients. However, in the absence of an independent viability reference standard, this finding represents intertracer diagnostic reclassification rather than proven functional recovery. A rest sestamibi uptake of <20% demonstrated high specificity for non-reclassification; however, this cutoff should be interpreted cautiously as a potential gatekeeping finding when considering downstream testing rather than a rigid rule for omitting further myocardial viability evaluation.

Title: Global Co-Occurrence of COPD and Peripheral Artery Disease in Older Adults: A Machine Learning Analysis of Spatial Patterns and Population-Attributable Risks.
Journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and peripheral artery disease (PAD) significantly contribute to morbidity and mortality among older adults. The geographic co-occurrence may indicate shared exposures; however, global population-level evidence remains scarce.
METHODS: Utilizing Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 estimates, the analysis focused on COPD and PAD incidence in adults aged ≥ 70 years across 202 countries and territories. Disease-specific incidence quartiles characterized spatial co-occurrence. Random forest models with SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) ranked exposure contributions, while negative binomial regression with population offsets estimated associations and population-attributable fractions (PAFs). A quartile-based composite risk index summarized cumulative exposure.
RESULTS: The global median incidence was 1150.16 per 100,000 for COPD and 695.4 per 100,000 for PAD. High-incidence regions exhibited partial geographic overlap. Smoking, high LDL cholesterol, and kidney dysfunction correlated with the incidence of both diseases, whereas several additional exposures were disease-specific. Elevated LDL cholesterol had the largest positive association with COPD incidence (RR 1.149), whereas high sugar-sweetened beverage intake exhibited the largest positive association among PAD-specific exposures (RR 1.059). Model-derived cumulative PAFs were 29.7% for COPD and 23.7% for PAD.
CONCLUSION: COPD and PAD demonstrate distinct yet overlapping global spatial patterns among older adults, sharing several population-level exposure correlates. Due to the cross-sectional and ecological nature of this study, the observed associations and PAFs should not be interpreted as individual-level causal effects. These findings may inform regional public health planning and generate hypotheses for prospective validation of integrated cardiopulmonary risk assessment.

Title: Lactate-Informed Exercise Prescription in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease: A Translational Framework for Preserving Cognition, Mobility, and Independence.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review proposes a conceptual, lactate-informed framework for individualized exercise prescription in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Exercise is recommended in these populations, but fixed external doses do not account for heterogeneity in disease stage, frailty, sarcopenia, cardiovascular risk, or recovery.
MAIN TEXT: We integrate clinical exercise evidence, geriatric assessment, lactate physiology, muscle-brain signaling, implementation science, and trial methodology. The framework uses peripheral blood lactate as one component of a monitoring matrix with workload, heart rate, blood pressure, perceived exertion, fatigue recovery, gait safety, adherence, and caregiver support. Repeated, standardized lactate responses are classified as low, adaptive and recoverable, excessive, or non-interpretable/unsafe, prompting stepwise adjustment of aerobic, resistance, balance, and cognitive-motor training. Peripheral blood lactate is an internal-load marker; it does not directly quantify blood-brain barrier transport, CNS lactate kinetics, or target engagement. Mechanistic pathways involving monocarboxylate transport, HCAR1, BDNF/VEGF, myokines, and lactylation therefore remain hypotheses to be tested in humans with MCI or AD.
CONCLUSIONS: The novelty of the framework is its integration of disease stage, geriatric phenotype, peripheral metabolic response, and recovery into clinically actionable dose decisions rather than a universal lactate threshold. Prospective multicenter trials should standardize sampling, validate response thresholds, and determine whether this approach improves cognition, mobility, independence, safety, and caregiver-relevant outcomes beyond usual advice or fixed-dose exercise.

Title: Complete Dacron reinforcement of Ross autograft does not increase neoaortic valve regurgitation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The Ross procedure offers superior hemodynamics and growth potential for patients with unrepairable aortic valve disease, but pulmonary autograft dilation and progressive neoaortic valve regurgitation remain key limitations. Complete autograft reinforcement with Dacron has been proposed to enhance structural stability and prevent dilation. However, concerns persist regarding potential autograft distortion, impaired leaflet coaptation, and increased valve regurgitation. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares clinical outcomes of fully Dacron-supported versus unsupported or partially supported autografts in the Ross procedure.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and Scopus databases was conducted from inception through March 30, 2026. Five retrospective comparative cohort studies including a total of 526 patients met inclusion criteria. Outcomes evaluated were early mortality (≤30 days), overall survival, freedom from autograft reoperation, and incidence of moderate or greater neoaortic valve regurgitation. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis.
RESULTS: No significant differences were observed between fully supported and unsupported/partially supported groups for early mortality (RR, 2.52; 95% CI, 0.28-22.51; P = .41, I 2 = 0%), overall survival (RR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.97-1.00], P = .14, I 2 = 0%), freedom from autograft reoperation (RR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.76-1.07], P = .25, I 2 = 79.1%), or incidence of moderate or greater neoaortic valve regurgitation (RR, 2.00; 95% CI, 0.39-10.25; P = .41, I 2 = 73.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Complete Dacron reinforcement of the pulmonary autograft does not increase the risk of neoaortic valve regurgitation or adversely affect clinical outcomes compared with unsupported or partially supported autografts. This technique offers a viable strategy to improve autograft durability and may enable the Ross procedure's application in patients previously deemed suboptimal candidates. Surgical technique should be tailored to individual patient profiles and institutional expertise, rather than standardized adoption of one technique.

Title: Elevated platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio is associated with stroke-associated pneumonia in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is a common and serious complication of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) that substantially worsens clinical outcomes. The platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), an accessible composite index derived from routine complete blood counts, may reflect post-stroke immune imbalance. However, its role in predicting SAP in AIS patients remains unexplored.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1,745 patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) after systematic screening of 2,150 patients. After the original screening, 1,766 eligible patients remained; 21 additional patients with extreme PLR values (>1,000) were excluded. HbA1c missing values were imputed once using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) with a random forest estimator. PLR was calculated as platelet count divided by lymphocyte count and log2-transformed. Multivariable logistic regression, generalized additive modeling (GAM), and two-piecewise logistic regression were used to examine associations between PLR and stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP). Subgroup analyses were performed across seven clinical variables with interaction tested by likelihood ratio test. Predictive performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and compared with C-reactive protein (CRP) and A2DS2 score using the DeLong test.
RESULTS: SAP occurred in 359 patients (20.6%). PLR was higher in patients with SAP than in those without SAP (median 136.17 vs. 113.69, p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, log2-PLR remained associated with SAP (OR = 1.36 per 1-unit increase, 95% CI: 1.12-1.65, p = 0.0021). Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest PLR quartile was associated with increased SAP odds (OR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.03-2.54, p = 0.0386). GAM and two-piecewise regression identified a threshold at PLR = 224.8 (log2-PLR = 7.812). Below this threshold, the association was not significant (OR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.93-1.57, p = 0.1551), whereas above it the association was significant (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.10-3.87, p = 0.0240). The AUCs were 0.584 for PLR, 0.825 for CRP, and 0.757 for A2DS2. The AUCs of the PLR + CRP and PLR + A2DS2 models were 0.803 and 0.763, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Elevated PLR is associated with SAP in AIS patients, exhibiting a non-linear threshold-dependent relationship. Although standalone discriminatory performance is modest, PLR is universally available from routine blood counts and may serve as a cost-effective tool for early SAP risk stratification. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

Title: Outcome-specific value of longitudinal clinical information and model complexity for dynamic prediction of type 2 diabetes-related outcomes: a pooled landmarking study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcome-specific incremental value of longitudinal clinical history and model complexity for annual dynamic prediction of multiple type 2 diabetes-related outcomes using pooled landmarking.
METHODS: We included 646 patients with complete annual records from baseline through year 3. Landmark times at years 1 and 2 were used to predict the first recorded occurrence of hypertension, coronary heart disease, diabetic kidney disease, diabetic retinopathy, or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease during the subsequent year. Four progressively expanded feature sets were compared using elastic-net logistic regression and Light Gradient Boosting Machine. The primary history-current estimand was a paired within-algorithm contrast with the risk set, validation splits, preprocessing, tuning, calibration, and evaluation records held constant. Internal validation used patient-level repeated nested cross-validation. We also evaluated fully nested model selection and model-development stability using 500 patient-level bootstrap replicates with out-of-bag evaluation.
RESULTS: Pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.722 to 0.952 across the five representative models. The paired history-current comparison showed higher AUC for hypertension with elastic-net (ΔAUC 0.097, 95% confidence interval 0.057 to 0.136) and LightGBM (0.118, 0.081 to 0.158), and for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with elastic-net (0.022, 0.002 to 0.042) and LightGBM (0.025, 0.009 to 0.041). The other three outcomes showed no comparable improvement. Algorithm differences were modest and outcome dependent.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort with complete annual T0-T3 follow-up, the incremental value of longitudinal information and model complexity was outcome specific. Longitudinal history showed greater benefit for selected outcomes, whereas algorithm differences were modest and outcome dependent. The smaller MASLD signal was supported primarily by the pooled L1-L2 analysis. Independent external validation is required before clinical application.

Title: Right ventricular strain analysis in acute pulmonary embolism and its role for late complications.
Journal: European heart journal. Imaging methods and practice
Abstract:
AIMS: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) can result in long-term complications, including post-PE impairment (PPEI) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). Right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) is a sensitive measure of RV myocardial deformation that may detect subclinical dysfunction and predict adverse outcomes; however, its value in the follow-up of post-PE assessment has not been yet elucidated.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective sub-study of the FOCUS cohort, 175 consecutive PE survivors from the Mainz centre underwent echocardiographic follow-up at 3 and 12 months, including speckle-tracking assessment of RVGLS, RV free wall strain (RVFWLS), and strain-derived ventriculoarterial coupling indices. Conventional RV parameters, volumetric measures, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Overall, 175 patients were included, of whom 16 developed PPEI or CTEPH during follow-up. RV function improved over time in patients without PPEI/CTEPH, including increases in RVGLS (from -16 to -18%), RVFWLS, ejection fraction, and strain-based ventriculoarterial coupling, accompanied by reductions in RV volumes. In contrast, patients who developed PPEI/CTEPH (n = 16) displayed progressive deterioration of RV strain and strain-derived coupling despite relatively preserved TAPSE-based indices. At 3 months, RVGLS was significantly associated with the combined PPEI/CTEPH endpoint over 2 years (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01-1.21), whereas strain-derived ventriculoarterial coupling parameters demonstrated borderline associations [RVGLS/systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP): OR 0.11, 95% CI 0.01-0.91; RVFWLS/sPAP: OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.02-1.17]. TAPSE/sPAP was not associated with the outcome.
CONCLUSION: RV strain and strain-derived ventriculoarterial coupling may provide sensitive early markers of maladaptive RV remodelling after acute PE and were associated with the development of PPEI/CTEPH, highlighting their potential value in post-PE follow-up strategies.

Title: Early neuro biomarker changes and electrophysiological nerve dysfunction in Swedish V50M hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis: a pilot study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This exploratory pilot study aimed to evaluate serum levels of neurofilament light chain (NfL), peripherin (PRPH), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and to explore their potential associations with nerve conduction studies (NCS) and nerve ultrasound (NUS) in a Swedish cohort of newly diagnosed patients with V50M transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis (ATTRv).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seventeen V50M-ATTRv patients exhibiting varying initial clinical symptoms were included for NCS, NUS, and blood analyses of NfL, PRPH, and GFAP.
RESULTS: V50M-ATTRv patients had a short disease duration (median, 7 months) and predominantly (52.9%) presented with self-reported neuropathic clinical symptoms at disease onset. Sixteen had recently initiated TTR-stabilizing therapy, whereas one remained untreated. Overall, NfL levels were significantly higher in patients than in age-matched controls (p < 0.001). This difference remained significant among older individuals (p < 0.001), but not among younger individuals (p = 0.071). Patients with an earlier age at disease onset had significantly higher PRPH levels compared with those with later disease onset (p = 0.030). Among younger individuals, PRPH levels were higher in patients compared with age-matched controls, but the difference was not significant (p = 0.200). NCS parameters showed significant associations with both NfL and PRPH, but no such associations were seen with GFAP. None of the neurobiomarkers demonstrated any associations with NUS.
CONCLUSION: In this pilot cohort of newly diagnosed Swedish V50M-ATTR patients, NfL was associated with electrophysiological measures of axonal dysfunction, whereas PRPH showed an exploratory signal of interest in younger patients with early disease onset. Larger longitudinal studies are required to determine whether PRPH may serve as a complementary biomarker for the early detection and monitoring of peripheral nerve involvement in ATTRv. Given the pilot design and limited sample size, the subgroup and regression findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects of a Prescription for Produce Subsidy on Diabetes Care Management.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: "Food Is Medicine" approaches are popular disease management strategies for patients experiencing food insecurity (FI) and diet-sensitive conditions; however, few studies consider heterogeneous treatment effects (HTE) across patient subpopulations. We estimate HTE of a prescription for produce (PRx) tested within a randomized controlled trial of patients with diabetes at risk of FI.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We use machine learning to estimate HTE of a PRx conducted within an integrated health system, academic medical center, and primary care network in the southeastern U.S. This trial included 2,155 patients enrolled in the health system's diabetes registry with at least one hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) measurement in the prior year and at-risk status for FI. Participants received $80/month for 12 months on a debit card covering fruit and vegetable purchases. Outcomes included HbA1c change (post- minus preintervention) and any postintervention emergency department (ED) utilization.
RESULTS: For HbA1c, the largest negative standardized difference in HbA1c change between intervention arms was observed among participants with HDL cholesterol >50.67 mg/dL and triglycerides >82.5 mg/dL (estimate [SE] -0.25% [0.12], -2.7 mmol/mol [1.3]; P = 0.019). For ED visits, the largest reduction in probability of any postintervention visits between arms was observed among individuals with low outpatient (OP) utilization, nonprivate and non-Medicare insurance, LDL cholesterol >78.5 mg/dL, and age >50.5 years (estimate [SE] -0.2 [0.05]; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that social factors (e.g., age and OP utilization) and clinical factors (e.g., cholesterol) may impact PRx effectiveness for diabetes management.

Title: CagriSema versus Semaglutide 2.4 mg monotherapy for weight management in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is the reference pharmacotherapy for weight management, yet many patients do not reach ambitious weight-loss targets. CagriSema, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, may offer additional benefit through complementary mechanisms. We quantified its incremental efficacy and safety against semaglutide 2.4 mg monotherapy in adults with overweight or obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes.
METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-compliant review (PROSPERO CRD420261380458) searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, ScienceDirect, ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP to 30 June 2026 for randomised controlled trials comparing CagriSema with semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo. Effects were pooled within two prespecified comparator strata using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of τ² and a Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman small-sample adjustment, with prediction intervals, leave-one-out and phase-3a-restricted sensitivity analyses, trial sequential analysis.
RESULTS: Five trials (4,746 unique participants) were included. Versus semaglutide 2.4 mg, CagriSema produced greater weight loss (mean difference -6.89 percentage points, 95% CI -8.70 to -5.06; I² = 33%; prediction interval -8.91 to -4.86), a greater absolute reduction in body weight (-7.16 kg, 95% CI -9.15 to -5.17) and in body-mass index (-2.41 kg/m², 95% CI -2.83 to -1.99), and roughly twice the likelihood of reaching a 20% reduction (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.78 to 2.47). Waist circumference fell further (-4.07 cm, 95% CI -5.10 to -3.04). No incremental glycaemic benefit was detected, with intervals for glycated haemoglobin (-0.07, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.01) and fasting plasma glucose lying entirely within prespecified minimal important differences. Injection-site reactions were more frequent (RR 3.14, 95% CI 1.42 to 6.96); gastrointestinal adverse events were not significantly increased under the primary model (RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.21).
CONCLUSION: CagriSema produces clinically meaningful additional weight loss and modest improvements in surrogate cardiometabolic measures compared with semaglutide 2.4 mg alone, at the cost of more frequent injection-site reactions and, at most, modestly more frequent gastrointestinal events. The evidence is insufficient to determine whether serious adverse events or neoplasms differ between treatments, and long-term durability, cardiovascular outcomes and body composition remain undetermined.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261380458.

Title: Sex-specific clinical profiles in patients with acute ischemic stroke and chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common among patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and is associated with worse outcomes. Although sex-related differences in stroke are well recognized, it remains unclear whether clinical characteristics associated with sex differ according to CKD status. We characterized sex-associated clinical profiles among patients with AIS with and without documented CKD.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the PRISMA Health Stroke Registry. Baseline characteristics were compared between patients with and without documented CKD in the overall cohort and after stratification by sex. Multivariable logistic regression with backward likelihood-ratio selection was used to identify independent clinical characteristics associated with documented CKD in the overall cohort and with male sex within the CKD and non-CKD subgroups. Adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Internal stability was assessed using bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Among 5,469 patients with AIS, 447 (8.2%) had documented CKD. Independent characteristics associated with CKD included prosthetic heart valve (OR, 3.73), elevated serum creatinine (OR, 2.79), obesity (OR, 2.51), heart failure (OR, 2.21), hypertension (OR, 2.20), African American race (OR, 2.11), and depression (OR, 1.97). In stratified analyses, associations of male sex with sleep apnea, smoking, and diastolic blood pressure ≥80 mmHg were numerically stronger in the CKD group than in the non-CKD group: sleep apnea, OR 4.62 vs. 2.38; smoking, OR 3.19 vs. 1.31; and diastolic blood pressure ≥80 mmHg, OR 2.58 vs. 1.43. However, formal interaction testing did not demonstrate statistically significant effect modification by CKD status. The sex-association model among patients with CKD demonstrated greater apparent discrimination than the corresponding non-CKD model (AUC, 0.785 vs. 0.630).
CONCLUSION: Patients with AIS demonstrated distinct sex-associated clinical profiles according to CKD status. Although several associations were numerically stronger among patients with CKD, formal interaction testing did not establish statistically significant effect modification. These findings characterize clinical heterogeneity among men and women with established AIS and warrant further investigation to determine whether these profiles have implications for treatment or outcomes.

Title: Association of Sex and Other Demographic Characteristics With Hemoglobin A1c in Older Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Cross-Sectional Analysis of the U.S. Premier Healthcare Database.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In type 1 diabetes, results for hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) sex-based differences are mixed, with limited data in later ages. The study objective was to determine whether female sex is independently associated with higher HbA1c in the U.S. older adult population.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was performed on real-world data from the Premier Healthcare Database from January 2020 to December 2022 examining adults with type 1 diabetes, ages 55-75 years. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were used to determine demographic variables independently associated with HbA1c. Predictor variables included age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance payor, testing location, marital status, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
RESULTS: Of 12,088 individuals with HbA1c data (52.4% women, mean age 64.7 ± 5.8 years), HbA1c was 0.13% (95% CI 0.08, 0.18; P < 0.001) higher on average in women and 0.81-0.97% higher in Black patients, adjusting for all other variables. Female sex (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.13; 95% CI 1.05, 1.21; P < 0.001; adjusted OR [aOR] 1.16; 95% CI 1.07, 1.26; P < 0.001), Black compared with White race (aOR 1.78; 95% CI 1.49, 2.12; P < 0.001), and Medicaid compared with Managed Care payor (aOR 1.63; 95% CI 1.28, 2.07; P < 0.001) were independently associated with increased odds of HbA1c above target, ≥7% for ages 55-64 years and ≥8.5% for ages ≥65 years.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort with type 1 diabetes, women experienced slightly higher HbA1c and higher odds of HbA1c above recommendations. Individuals with Black race and Medicaid insurance payor experienced clinically significantly higher HbA1c levels. Further interventions to address HbA1c disparities are needed.

Title: Open surgical repair of complex non-Type A and non-Type B aortic dissection in a right aortic arch-case report.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report the diagnostic and treatment process of a patient with complex non-Type A and non-Type B aortic dissection, and to discuss its clinical characteristics and surgical strategy.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of a patient with complex non-Type A and non-Type B aortic dissection.
RESULTS: After admission, the patient was diagnosed with complex non-Type A and non-Type B aortic dissection through computed tomography angiography (CTA). The aorta exhibited a right-sided arch, with the left common carotid artery originating from the ascending aorta and the aberrant left subclavian artery arising from the distal aortic arch. The right vertebral artery originated from the right-sided aortic arch. The dissection tear was located at the distal part of the aortic isthmus, approximately 2 cm in width. The dissection flap extended proximally to the distal aspect of the right subclavian artery origin and distally to the proximal aspect of the left renal artery origin. Due to the high difficulty of endovascular repair and the increased risk of long-term complications, an open surgical approach was chosen. This involved deep hypothermic circulatory arrest with elephant trunk stenting, left common carotid to left subclavian artery bypass. The patient was discharged one week after surgery in good health.
CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that open surgical repair can be a feasible and effective option for selected patients with non-A non-B aortic dissection and complex arch anatomy that limits endovascular repair. Treatment should be individualized according to entry-tear location, arch-branch anatomy, landing-zone feasibility, malperfusion risk, and institutional expertise. Due to the special anatomical structure and high surgical difficulty, a personalized treatment plan must be developed. Open surgery still offers irreplaceable advantages in certain cases.

Title: External Lumbar Drainage for Refractory Intracranial Hypertension in Acute Brain Injury: A Narrative Review and Case Series.
Abstract: Refractory intracranial hypertension in the setting of acute brain injury (ABI) is defined as sustained intracranial pressure (ICP) elevation above 22 mmHg despite escalating medical management. When unresponsive to these therapies, mortality reaches 84%-100%. External lumbar drainage (ELD) has emerged as a minimally invasive adjunct for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion, either as complementary to or alternative to external ventricular drainage (EVD), potentially avoiding the need for barbiturate coma or decompressive craniectomy. The objective of this paper is to review current evidence on the use of ELD in refractory intracranial hypertension following ABI and to present a single-center case series illustrating its clinical application, efficacy, and safety. We conducted a narrative review of the literature and retrospectively analyzed five consecutive patients admitted to a neurointensive care unit between August 2025 and April 2026 who were treated with ELD for refractory intracranial hypertension. Patient demographics, clinical severity scores (Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), Simplified Acute Physiology Score 3 (SAPS 3), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)), ICP values, timing of ELD placement, treatment escalation, length of stay, mechanical ventilation days, destination at discharge, and 28-day Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) were recorded. Five patients (four male; mean age 38.4 years) were treated with ELD: three with traumatic brain injury (TBI), one with hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage, and one with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). The median time to ELD placement was three days (range 2-8). In two patients, ELD was implemented as a tier 2 measure following sedation and analgesia, osmotherapy, and head-of-bed elevation. In the remaining patients, ELD was used as a tier 3 intervention, combined with decompressive craniectomy (n = 2) and/or barbiturate coma (n = 2). CSF drainage was guided by ICP elevation, performed only when it exceeded 20 mmHg; however, three of the five patients required continuous rate-based drainage (5 mL/h in Cases 1 and 5 and 10 mL/h in Case 4) because of sustained intracranial hypertension. Sustained ICP reduction with a favorable neurological outcome (GOS 4) was observed in one patient treated with early ELD (second day). Three patients died (one of whom died following transfer to another institution), and one patient developed two episodes of over-drainage due to accidental system disconnection, requiring ELD removal after one day. No infectious complications were recorded. Our conclusion is that ELD is a feasible, minimally invasive therapeutic option for refractory intracranial hypertension in ABI. Early placement, appropriate patient selection based on neuroimaging (patent basal cisterns, absence of significant mass effect), and continuous neuromonitoring are critical for safety and efficacy. Prospective randomized trials are needed to define optimal timing, patient phenotype, and drainage protocols.

Title: Effectiveness of Nursing Interventions on Stress and Functional Capacity Among Patients After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) frequently experience psychological stress and reduced functional capacity during the postoperative period. This randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on stress and functional capacity in post-CABG patients.
METHODS: A prospective parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in North India. Two hundred adult CABG patients were randomized to receive either nurse-led interventions (educational booklet, visual CD, and face-to-face counseling) or routine postoperative care. Stress was assessed using the Depression Anxiety and Stress Scale (DASS-21) stress subscale, and functional capacity using the Duke Activity Status Index (DASI) and metabolic equivalents (METs). Assessments were performed at baseline, one week, one month, and three months. Data were analyzed using Mann-Whitney U test, chi-square test, effect sizes, and linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Baseline stress and functional scores were comparable between the two groups. At one week, one month, and three months, patients in the intervention group demonstrated significantly lower stress, depression, and anxiety scores than those in the control group (p ≤ 0.001). However, at three months, the intervention group demonstrated significantly greater functional capacity than the control group (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The nurse-led interventions significantly improved psychological outcomes and functional recovery during the postoperative period in the post-CABG patients.

Title: Totally Thoracoscopic Atrial Fibrillation Ablation With the Gemini S Bipolar Clamp: A Single-Center Descriptive Cohort Study of 1-Year Rhythm, Safety, and Quality-of-Life Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outcome data for the Gemini S bipolar radiofrequency clamp are almost absent; the only indexed report being a three-patient case series. We describe 1-year outcomes in a consecutive cohort.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients treated with the Gemini S clamp between January 2021 and August 2024. Epicardial box isolation was combined with left atrial appendage (LAA) exclusion; completeness was confirmed by entry and exit block on epicardial three-dimensional mapping. The primary outcome was freedom from AF recurrence at 12 months, on and off antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) after a 90-day blanking period.
RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included (mean age 64.4 ± 8.0 years; 82.6% male). AF was paroxysmal in 34.8%, persistent in 26.1%, and long-standing persistent in 39.1%; 60.9% had prior catheter ablation and 69.6% had failed or were intolerant to a Class I or III agent. A complete block-verified box lesion was achieved in 95.7% and LAA exclusion in 91.3%. Three patients (13.0%) required conversion to sternotomy for bleeding, exceeding larger series. There was no death, stroke, phrenic nerve palsy, or pacemaker implantation. At 1 year, 87.0% (95% CI 67.9-95.5) were in sinus rhythm, all off Class I/III AADs.
CONCLUSIONS: Sinus rhythm was achieved in 87.0% of patients at 1 year. As the largest reported experience with this device, the series provides device-level evidence where little existed, but it is descriptive, not powered for comparison, and the conversion rate needs confirmation.

Title: Spectrometer matching for balanced detection in spectral-domain optical coherence tomography by autocorrelation minimization.
Abstract: Precise matching of spectrometers is essential to realizing the full benefits of balanced detection in spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT). A retrospective approach to match spectrometers, based on the observation that the autocorrelation signal should be zero in a perfectly balanced system, is presented. This approach requires only a single calibration B-scan, does not depend on the source noise or image properties, and can be used either to guide alignment or to obtain balanced results from previously acquired data. The performance of this method is demonstrated on a fiber-based SD-OCT system with a pair of commercial spectrometers and for a super-luminescent diode or supercontinuum laser source.

Title: Association of the Hemoglobin, Albumin, Lymphocyte, and Platelet Score with Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Mortality in Patients Underwent Coronary Angiography: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a frequent complication in patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG), which can cause deterioration of renal function and adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to explore the relationships between the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score and CA-AKI risk, as well as all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients undergoing CAG.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing CAG, including those receiving concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and stratified them according to the quartiles of the HALP score. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between HALP score and CA-AKI, and the Cox regression model was adopted to evaluate the relationship between HALP score and mortality.
RESULTS: This study included 42554 patients undergoing CAG. Among these, 5130 patients (12.1%) experienced CA-AKI. HALP score showed a significant inverse association with CA-AKI, with lower HALP score linked to higher CA-AKI risk. After adjusting for all the potential confounding variables, participants in the highest quartile of HALP score had the lowest risk of CA-AKI (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.73-0.90, p < 0.001). In Cox regression models, patients undergoing CAG with the highest HALP score exhibited the lowest risks of all-cause mortality (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.60-0.70, p < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality. (HR=0.65, 95% CI: 0.58-0.73, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The HALP score was independently associated with CA-AKI, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality among patients undergoing CAG.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Hybrid pin penetration open stent technique: Retrospective study of a new approach to frozen elephant trunk procedure.
Journal: Journal of vascular surgery cases and innovative techniques
Abstract: Total arch replacement using the frozen elephant trunk technique for acute type A aortic dissection involving the aortic arch remains technically demanding because of complex supra-aortic branch reconstruction and prolonged circulatory arrest. We developed a modified fenestrated open stent technique, termed the hybrid pin-penetration open stent (HIPPOS) technique, to simplify branch reconstruction while minimizing supra-aortic vessel manipulation. We retrospectively reviewed 15 consecutive patients who underwent total arch replacement using HIPPOS between May 2024 and May 2026 at a single institution by a single surgeon. Following deployment of a Frozenix open stent graft (Japan Lifeline), antegrade fenestrations were created under direct vision using needle penetration and sequential dilation, followed by reconstruction with balloon-expandable covered stent grafts. All procedures were successfully completed. Operative durations decreased with increasing numbers of fenestrations, reflecting procedural refinement and the surgical learning curve. Two perioperative deaths occurred in patients with profound preoperative shock, and one patient experienced a nondisabling stroke. No postoperative hoarseness, paraplegia, fenestration-related endoleak, or distal stent-induced new entry was observed. Follow-up computed tomography angiography confirmed satisfactory graft conformability and durable branch patency. HIPPOS is a reproducible modification of the frozen elephant trunk procedure with encouraging early clinical outcomes.

Title: Renal Outcomes in Hereditary Fibrinogen A Alpha-Chain Amyloidosis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hereditary fibrinogen A alpha-chain (AFib) amyloidosis is characterized by progressive proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) and early progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). A large series published in 2009 showed renal survival <5 years from diagnosis and renal transplant survival of <10 years. Since then, advances in diagnostic techniques and nephroprotective care have transformed both nephrology and amyloidosis. We evaluated contemporary diagnostic and renal outcomes in the largest cohort of patients with AFib amyloidosis to date.
METHODS: A total of 194 patients with confirmed AFib amyloidosis who were followed at a large national center and diagnosed between 1993 and 2025 were included. Patients were stratified by the era of diagnosis, pre- or post-2009. Diagnostic approaches, renal outcomes, transplant outcomes, and patient survival were evaluated.
RESULTS: Median age at diagnosis was 60 years with mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 37 ml/min per 1.73 m2. Proteomics-based amyloid typing became the predominant diagnostic modality post-2009 (60.5%). 62.8% progressed to ESRD. The mean annual rate of eGFR decline was 6.7 ml/min per 1.73 m2 in the pre-2009 era and 4.8 ml/min per 1.73 m2 in the post-2009 era. Renal survival improved post-2009, particularly among patients with CKD stage IIIA or B at diagnosis. Median renal allograft survival improved from 7.7 years in the pre-2009 era to 15.5 years in the post-2009 era (P = 0.006) (hazard ratio [HR], 4.5 [95% confidence interval [CI], 1.2-22.6]). Overall patient survival did not differ significantly between eras (median, 12 years; P = 0.69, log-rank).
CONCLUSIONS: Renal and allograft survival have improved since 2009, likely reflecting advances in supportive nephrology care. Isolated kidney transplantation is associated with favorable long-term outcomes. Despite improvements in renal survival, overall survival remains unchanged, underscoring the need for effective amyloid-targeted therapies.

Title: Inter-vessel heterogeneity in coronary microvascular dysfunction: A three-vessel physiological assessment.
Journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is typically assessed in the left anterior descending artery (LAD); however, inter-vessel differences involving the left circumflex (LCX) and right coronary arteries (RCA) remain unclear. We investigated inter-vessel variations in CMD and their associations with patient characteristics.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analyzed 91 patients (overall cohort) to evaluate patient characteristics across different coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) phenotypes based on physiological cutoffs: isolated CFR impairment, isolated IMR impairment, and combined impairment. Additionally, in a subgroup of 34 patients who successfully underwent physiological assessments in all three major coronary arteries (three-vessel cohort), we compared the CMD diagnostic rates between LAD-only and three-vessel assessments and evaluated vessel-specific correlations between CFR and IMR. In the Overall cohort, analysis of vessel-specific phenotypes revealed that patients with isolated IMR impairment in the LAD had a significantly higher body mass index (26.4 ± 4.90 kg/m2, p = 0.038). In the RCA, patients with isolated CFR impairment were significantly older (77.0 ± 9.18 years, p = 0.044). In the three-vessel cohort, the CMD diagnostic rate was significantly higher with a three-vessel assessment than with an LAD-only assessment (52.9% vs. 23.5%, p = 0.044). Furthermore, a significant inverse correlation between CFR and IMR was observed only in the LCX (r = -0.326, p = 0.033).
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary microvascular physiology varies across the LAD, LCX, and RCA, indicating that conventional LAD-only assessments may underestimate CMD burden. These preliminary retrospective findings require validation in prospective, multicenter studies before routine clinical adoption.

Title: A Comparative Outcomes Study: Is Routine Hip Abduction Bracing Necessary After Gluteus Medius Repair?
Abstract: Introduction Postoperative protocols regarding hip bracing after the surgical repair of a gluteus medius tear remain variable. It is unclear whether hip bracing improves short-term outcomes in patients undergoing gluteus medius repair. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the combined six-month complication and reoperation rate before and after discontinuing postoperative hip brace use after a gluteus medius repair. Methods A retrospective review of 162 patients undergoing gluteus medius repair by a single, fellowship-trained surgeon was performed. The no-brace protocol was implemented in October 2020. Prior to October 2020, all patients were prescribed a postoperative brace, and this served as the historical control group. Starting in October 2020, the postoperative brace was no longer prescribed, and this served as the study group. The remainder of the perioperative protocol was the same for both groups. All patients immediately began physical therapy and had toe-touch weightbearing restrictions for three weeks postoperatively. The primary endpoint was the combined complication and reoperation rate within six months postoperatively. Results The groups were similar demographically, with the only significant difference being that the no-brace group had a higher percentage of patients undergo open repair (29 (33.7%) vs. 14 (18.4%); p=0.028). There were no significant differences in outcomes at 30 days when looking at emergency department returns (2 (2.3%) vs. 4 (5.3%); p=0.421) and readmissions (0% vs. 2 (2.6%); p=0.219). At six weeks, there were no significant differences in falls (2 (2.3%) vs. 1 (1.3%); p=1.000) and other complications (1 (1.2%) vs. 2 (2.6%); p=0.601). Similarly, at six months, there were no significant differences in falls (4 (4.7%) vs. 1 (1.3%); p=0.372) and other complications including deep vein thrombosis, re-tear, fibromyalgia flare, and fracture (5 (5.8%) vs. 5 (6.6%); p=0.840). There was also no significant difference between groups in reoperation rates within six months (0% vs. 2 (2.6%); p=0.219). The combined six-month complication and reoperation rate was also not significant between groups (10 (11.6%) vs. 9 (11.8%); p=0.966). Conclusion In patients undergoing gluteus medius repair, postoperative bracing was not associated with differences in complication rates over the six-month postoperative period. Based on this result, discontinuation of postoperative bracing appears safe in this population. Further study is needed to replicate these results with a larger sample size.

Title: Feasibility and safety of an F16 small-caliber catheter-based, irrigation-free protocol in BPH patients undergoing green laser enucleation of the prostate: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: GreenLight laser enucleation of the prostate (GreenLEP) offers superior hemostasis, raising the possibility of omitting postoperative continuous bladder irrigation. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and safety of an F16 small-diameter catheter non-irrigation protocol in BPH patients.
METHODS: A retrospective single-center study included 300 consecutive BPH patients undergoing GreenLEP at Yangjiang Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine between January 2024 and June 2025. The exposure was implementation of the F16 non-irrigation protocol. The primary outcome was successful completion without continuous bladder irrigation or secondary hemostatic intervention. Covariates included age, prostate volume (PV), operative time, ASA score, anticoagulant/antiplatelet use, urinary retention, preoperative catheterization, and concomitant bladder stones. Stratified analysis and ROC curve analysis were performed to explore predictors of failure.
RESULTS: Overall, 265 patients (88.3%) successfully completed the non-irrigation protocol. Median hemoglobin decrease was 2.0 g/L (IQR 1-3), with no blood transfusions. In the parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for age, prostate volume, ASA classification, and anticoagulant/antiplatelet use, prostate volume was not independently associated with MajorFailure (adjusted OR 1.14 per 10-mL increase, 95% CI 0.76-1.71, P = 0.527). ROC analysis suggested a PV cutoff of 76.35 mL for predicting failure (AUC 0.65, 95% CI 0.55-0.75).
CONCLUSION: The F16 non-irrigation protocol after GreenLEP is safe and feasible, with high success rates and minimal perioperative bleeding. Increased PV and anticoagulant therapy modestly reduce success but do not preclude application. These findings support broader implementation of non-irrigation strategies to enhance postoperative comfort and recovery.

Title: Demographic Factors Influencing the Need for Repeat Radiofrequency Ablation in Chronic Pain Management: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a common noninvasive intervention for chronic pain management; however, the large variability in patient response underscores the need to better understand factors impacting treatment and patient outcomes. This study investigated whether demographic variables, specifically race, sex, age, and body mass index (BMI), are associated with the frequency of repeat RFA procedures in patients with chronic pain.
METHODS: This retrospective case series study was conducted at a single outpatient academic pain management clinic. A total of 170 clinic patients (mean age: 58.8 years; mean BMI: 31.5) who underwent at least two radiofrequency ablation (RFA) procedures between January 2019 and January 2023 were included. All patients had complete demographic and procedural data and at least one follow-up visit after their initial RFA; patients with incomplete or missing records or no follow-up visits were excluded. The primary outcome measure was the number of RFA procedures per patient.
RESULTS: One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) demonstrated no statistically significant differences in the number of repeat RFA procedures across racial groups (F(4,165) = 0.58, p = 0.68) or between genders (F(1,168) = 1.85, p = 0.18). Linear regression analysis found no statistically significant associations between number of repeat RFA procedures and age (F(1,168) = 3.06, p = 0.08) or BMI (F(1,166) = 0.00, p = 0.95). Ordered logistic regression further illustrated that the demographic variables examined - race, sex, age, BMI - were not associated with the number of repeat RFA procedures (χ²(4) = 5.53, p = 0.24).  Conclusions: Overall, our results showed that demographics including sex, race, age, and BMI were not associated with the frequency of RFA procedures in chronic pain management. Other variables like procedural variance, social support, or other comorbidities may serve as better potential determinants for treatment response and pain outcomes. These findings suggest that demographic variables alone may not explain variability in repeat RFA utilization.

Title: Beyond Prognosis: A Systematic Review of the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Modifiable Cardiovascular Biomarker.
Abstract: The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an accessible marker of systemic inflammatory activity associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, but whether it is modifiable through intervention and whether its reduction corresponds to cardiovascular benefit remain uncertain. This systematic review evaluated randomized evidence concerning the effects of pharmacological, nutritional, lifestyle, and procedural interventions on NLR among adults with established cardiovascular disease or elevated cardiovascular risk. MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched for studies published from January 1, 2021, through July 31, 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, randomized crossover trials, and secondary analyses of randomized trials reporting treatment-related changes in NLR. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidance. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, its crossover adaptation, and the Quality In Prognosis Studies (QUIPS) tool, where appropriate. Twelve studies involving 1,741 participants were included and synthesized narratively. Direct interleukin-6 (IL-6) inhibition produced the clearest dose-dependent reduction in NLR, while glutathione, cardiac rehabilitation, time-restricted eating, curcumin, normobaric hyperoxia, and selected nutritional strategies also demonstrated potentially favorable effects. Findings for sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors were inconsistent, with early empagliflozin initiation modulating inflammatory activity in one trial but producing no treatment-specific reduction in NLR during post-infarction recovery in another. Several studies associated lower inflammatory activity with improved ventricular function, global longitudinal strain (GLS), coronary plaque behavior, infarct volume, or neurological severity; however, few formally examined whether NLR independently predicted or mediated these effects. Clinical cardiovascular outcomes were infrequently reported and generally underpowered. Methodological limitations included small sample sizes, heterogeneous measurement schedules, post hoc analyses, multiple biomarker comparisons, and incomplete reporting of NLR outcomes. NLR appears to be a modifiable, context-dependent inflammatory marker, but current randomized evidence does not establish it as a therapeutic target or validated surrogate for cardiovascular benefit. Future trials should prespecify serial NLR assessments and determine whether phenotype-specific changes provide incremental prognostic or treatment monitoring value.

Title: Anatomical determinants of DTI-ALPS: Effects of ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and periventricular deformation.
Abstract: The diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is increasingly used as a non-invasive MRI biomarker proposed to reflect glymphatic and perivascular function, yet the anatomical validity and measurement stability of the metric remain incompletely characterised. Using diffusion MRI data from 850 healthy young adults and 150 healthy ageing participants from the Human Connectome Project, I systematically evaluated the influence of region-of-interest (ROI) placement and ventricular anatomy on ALPS measurements. Reference ALPS implementations demonstrated substantial hemispheric variability, with a median left-right difference of 12.5% and marked asymmetry in the underlying numerator and denominator tensor components. A two-stage optimisation framework incorporating fibre-pool alignment, hemispheric symmetry, component stability, and directional purity identified anatomically improved ROI configurations that significantly increased fibre specificity and reduced measurement variability in independent validation cohorts. Despite these improvements, residual hemispheric asymmetry persisted, suggesting an intrinsic anatomical contribution to ALPS variability. In the healthy ageing cohort, ventricular volume emerged as the strongest predictor of ALPS, explaining substantially more variance than chronological age. Voxel-wise deformation-based morphometry demonstrated that lower ALPS values were associated with ventricular and periventricular expansion, while optimisation increased coupling between ALPS and ventricular anatomy. Collectively, these findings indicate that ALPS measurements are strongly influenced by ROI definition, ventricular morphology, and surrounding periventricular tissue architecture. Rather than functioning as a direct measure of glymphatic transport in isolation, ALPS appears to represent a composite anatomical diffusion biomarker shaped by both methodological implementation and underlying neuroanatomy. These results provide a framework for improving methodological standardisation and interpretation of ALPS measurements in future neuroimaging studies.

Title: Efficacy and safety of selected Chinese herbal medicine preparations in treating carotid atherosclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although conventional therapies for Carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) remain the standard treatment, their effectiveness is often limited and accompanied by adverse effects. Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) is a promising adjunctive therapy for CAS; however, robust clinical evidence supporting its efficacy and safety remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of CHM for CAS treatment and characterizes its medication patterns.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating oral CHM for CAS were included. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool. Data were extracted and analyzed using RevMan v5.3 and R software. Sources of heterogeneity were investigated through meta-regression and subgroup analyses. Network analysis reveals herbal medication patterns across 21 studies.
RESULTS: Twenty-one RCTs involving 3,078 patients were included. Compared with conventional therapy alone, adjunctive CHM significantly reduced carotid plaque area (MD = 4.94, 95% CI: 3.13 to 6.76, p < 0.01), intima-media thickness (IMT) (MD = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.07 to 0.17, p < 0.05), total cholesterol (TC) (MD = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.22 to 0.42, p < 0.01), triglycerides (TG) (MD = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.11 to 0.37, p < 0.01), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) (MD = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.21 to 0.53, p < 0.01), while greatly increasing high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) (MD = -0.20, 95% CI: -0.29 to -0.10, p < 0.01). CHM did not significantly increase the risk of adverse events (RR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.64 to 1.10, p = 0.20) or impair liver/kidney function. Network analysis identified core actions as clearing phlegm and removing blood stasis, with Danshen (Salvia miltiorrhiza Bge.) and Banxia [Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Breit.] as pivotal botanical drugs exerting anti-stasis and lipid-regulating effects.
CONCLUSION: As an adjunct to conventional therapy, CHM may further reduce carotid IMT and plaque burden, improve lipid metabolism, and demonstrate a favorable safety profile. However, the overall quality and heterogeneity of the included studies limit the strength of the evidence, highlighting the need for well-designed, high-quality RCTs to confirm these findings.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261285381, identifier CRD420261285381.

Title: Safety of lecanemab in real-world patients with Alzheimer's disease: a prospective, observational case series supported by FAERS signal analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Lecanemab, a humanized immunoglobulin monoclonal antibody, has been approved for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although clinical trials have demonstrated its favorable safety profile, real-world studies are crucial for identifying rare adverse events (AEs) and evaluating post-marketing safety. This study aimed to evaluate the safety of lecanemab by combining a clinical prospective, observational case cohort with data from the FAERS database, thereby providing a robust basis for the identification of potential safety signals.
METHODS: A prospective and observational study was conducted on patients with mild-to-moderate AD receiving lecanemab treatment at a tertiary medical center in China from July 2024 to February 2026. Extracted data included demographic characteristics, time to onset of AEs, and clinical symptoms. Exposure-adjusted incidence rates were calculated per 100 patient-years (PYs). Disproportionality analysis was performed using the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), and safety signals for AEs observed in the cohort were evaluated utilizing reporting odds ratios (RORs) and proportional reporting ratios (PRRs). Additionally, data from these two real-world sources were compared and cross-validated.
RESULTS: The single-center prospective study enrolled a total of 91 patients. The median duration of lecanemab treatment was 185 days. Thirteen AEs were recorded (56.48/100 PYs), with the most frequent being amyloid-related imaging abnormalities-hemosiderin deposition (ARIA-H; defined as microhemorrhages and hemosiderin deposition) (12.39/100 PYs) and infusion-related reactions (IRRs) (8.85/100 PYs). In the FAERS database, the most frequently reported preferred terms (PTs) included headache, amyloid-related imaging abnormalities-edema/effusion (ARIA-E), ARIA-H, and IRRs. The majority of AEs occurred within the first 1-2 months after initiating lecanemab treatment (n = 393, 45.65%). Furthermore, FAERS analysis revealed a potential safety signal for cerebral infarction. However, this finding must be interpreted cautiously due to the lack of complete data on traditional stroke risk factors and concomitant antithrombotic use in spontaneous reports.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center prospective observational study, lecanemab demonstrated a generally favorable safety profile. Patients with AD aged 65 to 85 years represent a high-risk demographic for AEs. Particular clinical vigilance is required regarding the occurrence of AEs within the first two months of lecanemab initiation. Notably, ARIA (including both ARIA-E and ARIA-H) can occur at any phase during the treatment course.

Title: Clinical characteristics and early hematoma dynamics in a selected cohort of 199 patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage who underwent 24-hour follow-up imaging: a retrospective single-center study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) is a devastating subtype of stroke with high morbidity and mortality. Early hematoma expansion (HE) is a key modifiable factor associated with neurological deterioration. Data on early HE dynamics in China populations with relatively late presentation (median time to admission >6 h) remain limited.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 199 adult patients with sICH who had baseline and 24-h follow-up non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) scans. Hematoma volume was measured using the ABC/2 method. Early HE was defined as an absolute volume increase >6 mL or a relative increase >33% on the 24-h scan. Clinical characteristics, systemic inflammatory markers (peripheral leukocyte counts), and early neurological changes (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] and Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]) were analyzed.
RESULTS: The mean age was 58.7 ± 11.8 years, with male predominance (71.9%). Hypertension was present in 75.4% of patients. Median time from onset to admission was 10.0 h (IQR 6.0-19.5). Median initial hematoma volume was 16.2 mL (IQR 6.8-26.1). In this selected cohort of patients who survived to 24-h imaging without early surgical evacuation (median onset-to-admission 10.0 h), the observed rate of early HE was 6.0% (12/199).
