Title: Probiotics and synbiotics as adjunctive therapies for heart failure: a systematic review with network and pairwise meta-analyses.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the use of probiotics and synbiotics as microbiome-directed adjunctive therapies for heart failure (HF), while explicitly determining whether any eligible prebiotic-only trials existed.
METHODS: We searched eight English- and Chinese-language databases from inception to 1 May 2026 and conducted expanded sensitivity searches in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science on 15 July 2026. Random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) was used only for connected multi-node evidence; two-node evidence was analyzed pairwise. As placebo, usual care, and food comparators were not clinically exchangeable, comparator-stratified sensitivity analyses of direct evidence were conducted using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and Hartung-Knapp (HK) confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 12 randomized studies were included in the systematic review (14 reports); 11 contributed to at least one primary or sensitivity quantitative analysis, and 10 contributed to the primary analyses. The revision-stage search audit identified no additional eligible randomized trials and no eligible prebiotic-only trials. Across all the trial populations, 1,021 participants were randomized, 973 of whom were allocated to review-eligible arms. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) network included 7 studies and 539 participants in the analysis set; however, this network was star-shaped, had no closed loops, and depended on a combined comparator node. The exploratory NMA estimate for multi-strain bacterial probiotics versus the combined comparator was a mean difference (MD) of 2.13 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI] -0.10 to 4.35). The comparator-stratified sensitivity analysis for usual care yielded an MD of 1.83 percentage points (95% CI -2.33 to 5.98). All synthesized results were assessed as having either some concern or a high risk of bias. The effect estimates were generally imprecise, and the certainty of evidence was low or very low. Adverse event definitions and denominators were inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: The available evidence is sparse and affected by significant non-transitivity, risk of bias, and imprecision. Network comparisons and rankings should be considered hypothesis-generating; therefore, no probiotic or synbiotic adjunct can be recommended for routine HF management.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: CRD420261413595. Public URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261413595.

Title: Efficacy and safety of nafamostat mesilate for anticoagulation during ECMO/CRRT: insight from the integrated meta-analysis and FAERS pharmacovigilance study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) require a balance between maintaining circuit patency and minimizing bleeding risk. Nafamostat mesilate (NM) is a short-acting anticoagulant with distinctive pharmacokinetic properties, including rapid metabolism and a short half-life, which may reduce prolonged systemic anticoagulant exposure. These characteristics make NM a potential alternative to conventional anticoagulation strategies, particularly for patients at high risk of bleeding. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of NM as an anticoagulant for ECMO/CRRT.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were systematically searched for randomized controlled trials and cohort studies comparing NM with sodium citrate, unfractionated heparin (UFH), or no anticoagulation. A meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate filter lifespan, bleeding events, thromboembolic events, and 28-day/intensive care unit (ICU) mortality. Reporting characteristics and potential safety signals for the three anticoagulants were also compared using data from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 17 studies involving 1,893 patients. Filter lifespan did not differ significantly between the NM and control groups (mean difference [MD] = 1.29 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.09-3.66), whereas the risk of bleeding events was significantly lower in the NM group (odds ratio [OR] = 0.61; 95% CI, 0.43-0.86). Subgroup analyses showed that NM was associated with a significantly lower risk of bleeding than sodium citrate (OR = 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.90) and no anticoagulation (OR = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.19-0.90); sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of this finding. The FAERS analysis included 24,238 reports, comprising 233 for NM, 1,612 for sodium citrate, and 22,393 for UFH, with distinct reporting profiles observed among the three anticoagulants. Representative signals for NM included disseminated intravascular coagulation (n = 17; ROR = 112.68, 95% CI: 69.69-182.19), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (n = 12; ROR = 15.44, 95% CI: 8.74-27.29), and decreased platelet count (n = 13; ROR = 7.52, 95% CI: 4.35-13.00).
CONCLUSION: NM may reduce bleeding risk while maintaining a filter lifespan comparable to that achieved with other anticoagulation strategies, potentially providing an individualized anticoagulation option for patients at high risk of bleeding. In clinical practice, coagulation abnormalities, changes in platelet counts, and bleeding-related events should be closely monitored.

Title: Empowering rural physicians through an AI-assisted intervention for deprescribing in older adults with comorbid diabetes and hypertension: protocol for a feasibility study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In China's primary healthcare system, older adults with both hypertension and diabetes are a key focus. These patients often deal with polypharmacy, which heightens the risk of adverse drug reactions, lowers treatment adherence, and increases medical burdens. Deprescribing, an evidence-based approach to optimizing medication regimens, is challenging for rural physicians due to barriers like limited clinical knowledge, lack of systematic decision support, and time constraints. Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents a promising solution, yet the feasibility of AI-assisted deprescribing in rural primary care is underexplored. This protocol describes a study designed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of an AI agent for rural physicians managing older adults with these comorbidities.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol outlines a single-arm, pre-post feasibility study to be conducted in rural primary healthcare institutions across 11 administrative regions in Zhejiang Province, China. The study aims to recruit 30 eligible rural physicians and at least 150 older patients (aged ≥65 years) who have concurrent diagnoses of hypertension and diabetes and are taking five or more long-term medications. The intervention utilizes an AI agent with clinical medication guidance functions to assist rural physicians in the deprescribing process. The follow-up period spans 6 months. The primary outcome is the change in the total number of medications per patient after the intervention. Secondary outcomes include patient clinical outcomes and rural physicians' acceptance of the AI agent. Quantitative data will be analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data from semi-structured interviews will undergo thematic analysis to identify barriers and facilitators to implementation.
DISCUSSION: This protocol introduces the inaugural study evaluating the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of a low-cost, independently developed AI agent tailored for rural physicians managing older adults with both hypertension and diabetes. It aims to generate empirical data on implementation processes, participant experiences, and contextual barriers. This evidence will directly inform the refinement of recruitment strategies, optimization of intervention protocols and AI agent functionality, and support future large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The study addresses critical practical challenges in deprescribing within resource-limited rural settings.Clinical Trial Registration: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=309897, identifer ChiCTR2600126204.

Title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and functional outcome at discharge in patients receiving standardized treatment for atherosclerotic and cardioembolic stroke.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is gaining considerable attention as an emerging marker of metabolic syndrome. The TyG index is strongly associated with atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease development. However, the impact of the TyG index on the functional outcome at discharge of patients receiving standardized treatment and its variability in different types of stroke have not been fully elucidated.
METHOD: Baseline data, neurological scale scores, and laboratory indicators were retrospectively collected from ischemic stroke patients at Lianyungang Second People's Hospital and Lianyungang First People's Hospital. Patients were categorized into good and poor functional outcome groups based on the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score at discharge. A logistic regression model was used to evaluate the relationship between the TyG index and functional outcome at discharge of patients with atherosclerotic and cardioembolic stroke.
RESULTS: A total of 854 patients were included in the analysis, including 712 patients with large artery atherosclerotic (LAA) and 142 patients with cardioembolism (CE). Subgroup comparisons based on different discharge-level functional outcomes showed that the TyG index of the 187 patients in the poor functional outcome at discharge group was higher than that of patients in the good functional outcome group (8.98 vs. 8.69). The restricted cubic curve revealed a nonlinear association between the TyG index and discharge-level functional outcome among LAA stroke patients (for nonlinearity, p = 0.026). Multivariate logistic regression showed that the TyG-Q2 and TyG-Q3 groups were not associated with discharge-level functional outcome compared with the TyG-Q1 group, and the TyG-Q4 group was a risk factor for the occurrence of poor functional in the LAA group (odds ratio (OR) = 2.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.52-4.55). After adjusting for age, National Institute of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score at admission, glucose, diastolic blood pressure, uric acid, and low-density lipoprotein, the TyG-Q4 group remained a risk factor for the occurrence of poor functional outcome at discharge in the LAA group (OR = 2.38, 95% CI = 1.03-5.51). However, the TyG index did not correlate with functional outcome at discharge in the CE group. Of note, this negative CE subgroup result should be interpreted cautiously due to the limited sample size and insufficient endpoint events, which may cause inadequate statistical power and false-negative outcomes; thus, the potential predictive value of the TyG index for discharge-level functional outcome in CE stroke cannot be excluded.
CONCLUSION: The TyG index was identified as a risk factor for poor functional outcome at discharge in LAA stroke but was not correlated with the functional outcome at discharge of CE stroke. Considering the limited sample size and insufficient statistical power of the CE subgroup, this negative result should not be over-interpreted, and large-scale clinical studies are required to further explore the potential prognostic value of the TyG index in cardioembolic stroke.

Title: Development of a machine learning-based multicenter study for predicting severe intraventricular hemorrhage in preterm infants using perinatal variables.
Abstract:
AIM: To develop and validate machine learning models for predicting severe intraventricular hemorrhage (SIVH) in preterm infants using only prenatal and intrapartum variables, and to identify the optimal model.
METHOD: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included preterm infants (gestational age ≤34 weeks) who required noninvasive or invasive respiratory support, using data from the Jiangsu Neonatal Respiratory Failure Collaborative Network (2019-2021). Data were split 7:3 into training and validation sets. Eight machine learning algorithms were compared. Performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis. An independent cohort served for temporal validation.
RESULTS: Among 3,320 infants, the incidence of SIVH was 6.66%. Six predictors were identified: gestational age, birth weight, endotracheal intubation in the delivery room, chest compressions in the delivery room, surfactant administration in the delivery room, and chorioamnionitis. In the training set, logistic regression achieved the highest mean AUC based on 10-fold cross-validation. Bootstrap internal validation of the LR model yielded a corrected AUC of 0.809. In the independent hold-out validation set, the LR model again demonstrated the best discriminative ability among the eight algorithms (AUC: 0.804), with satisfactory calibration and favorable net benefit. Sensitivity analyses showed that the LR model maintained robust performance in temporal validation using an independent cohort (AUC: 0.822) and across geographic subgroups (AUC range: 0.729-0.885). An online interactive tool was also developed to facilitate clinical application.
INTERPRETATION: A LR model using six readily available perinatal variables provides good discrimination and calibration for predicting SIVH in preterm infants, enabling immediate risk stratification at birth for SIVH occurring during the neonatal hospitalization period.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study; Validation Study

Title: Harmonizing Vietnamese traditional and western medicine: a digital health blueprint and the IMKE architectural framework.
Abstract: The concurrent use of traditional and Western medicine is a global healthcare reality. In countries like Vietnam, dual-paradigm clinical guidelines actively mandate integrated treatments for high-prevalence chronic diseases. However, safe integration at the point of care is severely hindered by data fragmentation, profound epistemological differences, and a critical "shadow pharmacovigilance" crisis regarding underreported herb-drug interactions (HDIs). This paper analyzes the state-of-the-art of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in integrative healthcare and proposes the Integrative Medicine Knowledge Engine (IMKE), a novel architectural blueprint designed to safely bridge Vietnamese traditional medicine (VTM) and Western biomedicine. Shifting from siloed technical models to a clinical-first perspective, the IMKE conceptualizes a three-stage digital health pipeline: (1) advanced medical text mining to digitize unstructured traditional practitioner notes; (2) an Integrative Knowledge Graph (IKG) that maps holistic VTM diagnostic patterns to Western pharmacological databases and ICD-10 standards; and (3) an AI-driven Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for proactive HDI safety monitoring. We illustrate this architectural data flow through three clinical scenarios-Essential Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes, and Rheumatoid Arthritis. These scenarios demonstrate the system's theoretical capacity to retrieve culturally appropriate treatments, identify cross-paradigm therapeutic synergies, and generate explainable, mechanistic safety alerts that augment physician judgment while mitigating clinical alert fatigue. Ultimately, the IMKE framework provides a scalable, culturally inclusive roadmap for digital health. By translating centuries of experiential medical wisdom into an interoperable, computationally safeguarded infrastructure, this blueprint sets the foundation for evidence-based integrative care, future retrospective clinical validation, and enhanced patient safety.

Title: A pilot genome-wide association study of ischemic heart disease with co-occurring arterial hypertension in a Kazakh cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of ischemic heart disease (IHD) remain underrepresented in Central Asian populations. We conducted a pilot GWAS of ischemic heart disease with co-occurring arterial hypertension (IHD-HTN) in an ethnic Kazakh cohort to identify candidate loci for future replication.
METHODS: This study included 470 Kazakh individuals, comprising of 240 cases and 230 controls genotyped using the Illumina Infinium Global Screening Array-24 v 3.0. Association testing was performed using logistic regression under an additive genetic model adjusted for age, sex, and the first 10 principal components. Post-imputation GWAS was performed using high-quality imputed variants. Secondary analyses included MAGMA and KGWAS prioritization.
RESULTS: In the array-based GWAS, no variant reached the Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold (P < 1.53 × 10-7). The strongest SNP association was observed for rs1511924 at chromosome 16 mapped to the ZFHX3 gene (OR = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.37-0.66; P = 1.00 × 10-6). Post-imputation GWAS supported the same locus with rs12598508 (P = 4.93 × 10-7) and rs1511924 (P = 5.15 × 10-7) among the strongest signals, although neither reached the genome-wide significance. Secondary MAGMA and KGWAS analyses did not provide stable evidence for additional loci.
CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first pilot GWAS focused on IHD with co-occurring arterial hypertension in a Kazakh cohort. Although no Bonferroni-significant SNP associations were identified, the ZFHX3 region emerged as the strongest suggestive candidate locus and requires independent replication. Larger Central Asian cohorts and population-specific reference resources are required to validate these findings.

Title: Soluble guanylate cyclase modulation in heart failure and chronic kidney disease: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational boundaries.
Abstract: Heart failure (HF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) frequently coexist and amplify one another through hemodynamic, neurohormonal, inflammatory, oxidative, and microvascular mechanisms. Impaired nitric oxide (NO)-soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)-protein kinase G (PKG) signaling represents a biologically plausible component of this cardiorenal interaction. However, clinical translation of sGC modulation requires careful interpretation because sGC stimulators and activators preferentially engage distinct biochemical states of the enzyme, and available evidence remains heterogeneous across compounds, phenotypes, and endpoint domains. This narrative review integrates mechanistic, preclinical, and clinical evidence for clinically evaluated sGC modulators, including vericiguat, riociguat, praliciguat, runcaciguat, avenciguat, and cinaciguat, with emphasis on HF-CKD translational relevance. Vericiguat demonstrated benefit in a specific population of clinically stabilized patients with symptomatic chronic HF, LVEF below 45%, and a recent worsening-HF event. In VICTORIA, the reduction in the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death or first HF hospitalization was primarily driven by fewer HF hospitalizations, with no statistically significant reduction in cardiovascular death alone. Conversely, the VICTOR trial was neutral for its primary endpoint in stable ambulatory HFrEF, and HFpEF studies of vericiguat or praliciguat did not improve their prespecified biomarker, health-status, or exercise endpoints. In CKD populations, runcaciguat and avenciguat have shown short-term albuminuria reductions, but these surrogate signals have not established durable kidney protection, including long-term preservation of eGFR or prevention of kidney failure. To contextualize heterogeneous evidence, we propose an evidence-interpretation framework incorporating HF phenotype and clinical state, CKD phenotype, putative sGC redox biology, and endpoint domain. This framework is intended for evidence interpretation and hypothesis generation rather than patient-level treatment selection; no validated clinical assay defines tissue sGC redox state, and no prospective treatment-by-biomarker interaction has established redox-guided selection. Future studies should prioritize phenotype-enriched HF-CKD populations, contemporary background therapy, and prespecified cardiovascular and kidney outcomes to define the clinical role of sGC modulation.

Title: Clinical presentation and management patterns of ureteral calculi in pregnancy: a 14-year single-institution retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the clinical presentation, diagnostic pathway, and management patterns of ultrasound-confirmed ureteral calculi during pregnancy at a single institution.
METHODS: This study collected, summarized, and analyzed clinical data from 120 pregnant patients diagnosed with ureteral calculi at Fujian Provincial Hospital between March 2010 and March 2024. Primary descriptive outcomes were initial symptom response, documented spontaneous stone passage, subsequent urinary decompression, and residual calculi after pregnancy. Secondary outcomes included technical success of decompression and changes in selected laboratory findings. Maternal-fetal follow-up was not standardized through delivery, and comprehensive obstetric and neonatal outcomes were not systematically available.
RESULTS: All patients were initially managed with conservative treatment and achieved symptomatic relief within 24 h. Spontaneous stone expulsion was documented in 90 patients: 51 at ≤1 month, 17 at >1-3 months, and 22 at >3 months. Urinary decompression was required in 57 patients because of fever, aggravated hydronephrosis, or recurrent renal colic. Retrograde D-J stent placement was attempted in all 57 patients and was successful in 47 (82.5%); the remaining 10 patients underwent percutaneous nephrostomy after unsuccessful stent placement. Cystoscopic D-J stent placement attempts were performed using topical urethral anesthesia with 10% lidocaine, whereas percutaneous nephrostomy was performed under local infiltration anesthesia; no miscarriage or preterm labor temporally associated with urinary decompression or the related anesthesia was documented among the 57 patients who underwent decompression. Post-procedural fetal heart rate monitoring was performed in all 57 patients, and no abnormal findings were documented. Thirty cases retained calculi after completion of pregnancy; among them, 8 underwent postpartum ESWL and 22 underwent postpartum ureteroscopic lithotripsy. Among the 120 analyzed patients, neither ESWL nor ureteroscopic holmium laser lithotripsy (URS-HLL) was performed during pregnancy. Among eight febrile patients, mean white blood cell (WBC) count decreased from 14.9 ± 0.19 × 109/L to 6.7 ± 0.30 × 109/L (paired t-test, P < 0.001). Mean procalcitonin (PCT) was 13.86 ± 3.57 ng/mL before treatment, whereas post-treatment values were reported as 0 ng/mL because they fell below the laboratory reporting limit; accordingly, the PCT change was summarized descriptively without inferential testing. Of 38 patients with positive urine leukocytes pretreatment, all tested negative post-treatment (P < 0.001). Among 101 cases with pretreatment hematuria, 86 converted to negative after treatment (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This cohort describes a conservative-first management pathway with selective urinary decompression when symptoms or complications persisted. No procedure- or anesthesia-related miscarriage, preterm labor, abnormal post-procedural fetal heart rate finding, or serious urological complication were documented during hospitalization or available urological follow-up among patients who underwent decompression; however, these observations do not establish comprehensive maternal-fetal safety.

Title: Early-admission serum albumin and hospitalization burden in a selected serial-culture cohort of patients with diabetic foot ulcers and subsequent Pseudomonas aeruginosa detection: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) who undergo repeat wound culture and subsequent Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) detection form a selected clinical trajectory. Early-admission serum albumin reflects inflammation, capillary permeability, hepatic synthesis, protein loss, hydration, and nutritional reserve; it is not a stand-alone measure of nutritional status. We examined its association with hospitalization burden conditional on this serial-culture trajectory.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 408 hospitalized patients with DFU who had a PA-positive wound culture after an earlier non-PA culture during the same admission. Because cohort eligibility required continued hospitalization until repeat sampling and later PA detection, inference was conditional on a post-admission selection event susceptible to immortal-time and collider-selection bias. The culture sequence was an operational ascertainment pattern, not evidence of nosocomial acquisition, microbiological conversion, or invasive PA infection. The co-primary outcomes were length of stay (LOS) and institution-specific nominal hospital charges. Negative binomial and gamma log-link models estimated adjusted within-cohort associations. Exploratory prognostic analyses used bootstrap optimism correction and same-center temporal assessment (development, 2013-2016; assessment, 2017-2018).
RESULTS: Among 408 patients [261 men (64.0%)], median LOS was 14 days [interquartile range (IQR), 9-19] and median nominal hospital charges were CNY 18,708 (IQR, 12,532-27,979). Compared with albumin ≥35 g/L, albumin 30 to <35 g/L was associated with longer LOS [adjusted rate ratio (aRR), 1.24; 95% CI, 1.10-1.40] and higher charges [adjusted charge ratio (aCR), 1.28; 95% CI, 1.12-1.46]; corresponding estimates for albumin <30 g/L were 1.52 (95% CI, 1.29-1.78) and 1.67 (95% CI, 1.40-1.99). Per 5-g/L lower albumin, the aRR for LOS was 1.19 (95% CI, 1.14-1.25) and the aCR for charges was 1.22 (95% CI, 1.16-1.28). Baseline-only estimates changed by less than 3% on the log-ratio scale. Adding albumin increased the apparent area under the curve (AUC) from 0.679 to 0.758 (optimism-corrected, 0.643 to 0.729; ΔAUC, 0.079; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.036-0.120). In the same-center temporal assessment sample (126 patients; 50 events), the AUC was 0.592 for the core model and 0.719 after albumin was added; corresponding Brier scores were 0.234 and 0.204, and calibration slopes were 0.625 and 0.994. These small-sample performance estimates were treated as descriptive. The median bootstrap-optimal albumin cutoff was 35 g/L (95% bootstrap percentile interval, 33-37 g/L).
CONCLUSIONS: Within this selected serial-culture cohort, lower early-admission albumin was associated with greater hospitalization burden and with numerically better exploratory prognostic performance in same-center analyses. These findings do not establish causality, transportability, a diagnosis of malnutrition, or a clinically actionable albumin threshold.

Title: The association of triglyceride-glucose body roundness index with carotid atherosclerosis in type 2 diabetes: a cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose body roundness index (TyG-BRI) has emerged as a promising biomarker correlated with elevated risks of adverse cardiovascular events. Notably, the potential linkage between TyG-BRI and carotid atherosclerosis (CAS) has not been formally evaluated in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study consecutively enrolled 1060 adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Fujian, China. Anthropometric measurements and fasting venous blood biochemical data were collected to calculate TyG-BRI. CAS was ascertained using high-resolution B-mode ultrasound. Spearman correlation analysis was performed to examine the correlations between TyG-BRI and metabolic indicators. Following stepwise adjustment for confounding variables, hierarchical binary logistic regression and restricted cubic spline curves were applied to evaluate the association of TyG-BRI with CAS risk as well as potential effect modifiers. Finally, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was conducted to evaluate the identification capability of TyG-BRI for CAS.
RESULTS: Patients with CAS had significantly higher TyG-BRI levels than non-CAS controls. TyG-BRI was positively correlated with carotid intima-media thickness, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), blood pressure, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and uric acid. In fully adjusted models, elevated TyG-BRI was non-linearly associated with higher CAS risk (P for overall association < 0.001, P for non-linearity < 0.01). Per 1-standard-deviation increment in TyG-BRI, the ORs were 1.503 (95% CI 1.281-1.763, P < 0.001) for carotid intima-media thickening, 1.453 (95% CI 1.236-1.709, P < 0.001) for carotid plaque, and 2.247 (95% CI 1.820-2.773, P < 0.001) for CAS. Associations remained consistent across subgroups stratified by age, sex, body mass index (BMI), HbA1c and hypertension, with a stronger effect in participants with BMI < 24 kg/m² (OR 4.838, 95% CI 3.007-7.784, P < 0.001). ROC analysis showed TyG-BRI significantly identified CAS (AUC = 0.698, 95% CI 0.664-0.731, P < 0.001), outperforming TyG and TyG-BMI while matching the performance of the composite indices of TyG combined with waist circumference or waist-to-height ratio.
CONCLUSION: TyG-BRI demonstrated an independent, non-linear dose-response association with CAS risk in type 2 diabetes. Its integration into cardiovascular risk stratification holds promise for enabling earlier identification of CAS.

Title: Joint Control of Inflammation, Cholesterol, and Lipoprotein(a) With Incident Cardiovascular Events in People With Type 2 Diabetes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to investigate the joint associations of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), LDL cholesterol (LDL-C), and lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] with cardiovascular disease (CVD) among patients with type 2 diabetes.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study identified patients with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank. Baseline hsCRP, LDL-C, and Lp(a) were dichotomized according to guideline-recommended target levels. Patients were followed for incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), total CVD (ASCVD plus heart failure), death, or study end. Competing risk models adjusted for important covariates were used.
RESULTS: There were 29,658 patients with type 2 diabetes who were followed for a median of 15 years. Those with all three biomarkers above target had significantly increased risks compared with those with all at target: fatal and nonfatal ASCVD (adjusted hazard ratio 1.59; 95% CI 1.24, 2.03) and total CVD (adjusted hazard ratio 1.44; 95% CI 1.13, 1.83). Cardiovascular risk increased progressively as fewer biomarkers achieved target levels (all P trend < 0.001), with stronger associations in patients with shorter diabetes duration (<2 years vs. ≥2 years).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated hsCRP, LDL-C, and Lp(a) showed dose-dependent associations with cardiovascular risk in patients with type 2 diabetes, supporting their control in cardiovascular risk prevention.

Title: Prasugrel Outperforms Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Real-World Analysis.
Abstract: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor is standard for patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet real-world comparisons of ticagrelor and prasugrel remain limited. We evaluated their relative effectiveness and safety using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (2010-2024). Adult ACS patients receiving prasugrel or ticagrelor within 24 h post-PCI were included. The primary endpoint was a 1-year composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and cerebral infarction; secondary endpoints included individual components, major bleeding, and repeat revascularization. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses assessing robustness. Among 14,895 matched pairs (n = 29,790) from 126,273 patients, prasugrel was associated with lower risk of the composite endpoint (HR 0.641; 95% CI 0.613-0.671), all-cause mortality (HR 0.557; 95% CI 0.487-0.637), and MI (HR 0.648; 95% CI 0.616-0.680), without increased bleeding (HR 0.945; 95% CI 0.824-1.084). Repeat revascularization was higher with prasugrel (HR 1.791; 95% CI 1.639-1.957). Effects were consistent across subgroups. In this real-world setting, prasugrel demonstrated superior effectiveness over ticagrelor in reducing mortality and ischemic events without increasing the risk of bleeding, although higher rates of repeat revascularization warrant further study. These findings support prasugrel as a potentially preferred P2Y12 inhibitor in selected ACS patients undergoing PCI.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Observational Study

Title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification).
RESULTS: Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012).
SIGNIFICANCE: MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

Title: Dapagliflozin in phenotypically stratified HFpEF without myocardial fibrosis: the STADIA-HFpEF randomized crossover trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction(HFpEF) is characterized by increased diastolic left ventricular(LV) stiffness resulting from variable contributions of myocardial extracellular matrix(ECM) remodeling and titin-based cardiomyocyte stiffness. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors(SGLT2i) improved cardiomyocyte distensibility, inflammation, and oxidative stress in experimental and human HFpEF myocardium. We investigated whether dapagliflozin improves LV distensibility in phenotypically stratified HFpEF patients without significant myocardial fibrosis.
METHODS: STADIA-HFpEF was a 34-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. HFpEF patients underwent multi-level phenotypic stratification including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to exclude structural cardiomyopathies and significant myocardial ECM remodeling. Participants were randomized to dapagliflozin 10 mg or placebo for two 13-week treatment periods separated by an 8-week washout.The co-primary endpoints were changes in E/e'/LV end-diastolic volume index(LVEDVi) and mean LV e', reflecting LV distensibility and relaxation. Secondary endpoints included echocardiographic variables, quality of life, 6-minute walk distance, and inflammatory biomarkers.
RESULTS: Between February 2020 and October 2022, 32 patients were randomized and 29 completed the study protocol. Median age was 73(68-76) years including 28 women(88%). Dapagliflozin did not significantly modify E/e'/LVEDVi compared with placebo 0.24 (0.20-0.32) to 0.26 (0.22-0.34) vs. 0.23 (0.22-0.29) to 0.25 (0.21-0.31); p=0.370 nor did it change mean LV e' 6.2 (5.6-7.5) to 6.2 (5.7-7.1) vs. 6.6 (5.6-7.4) to 6.7 (5.4-7.5); p=0.448. Most secondary outcomes were neutral. However, an isolated improvement in LA conduit strain and numerical reductions in inflammatory biomarkers were observed during dapagliflozin treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: In phenotypically stratified HFpEF patients without significant myocardial fibrosis, dapagliflozin did not improve LV distensibility or relaxation. An isolated improvement in LA conduit strain and numerical reductions in inflammatory biomarkers were observed; however, these exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies.

Title: Post-Operative Acute Kidney Injury After Pediatric Heart Transplantation and Longitudinal Invasive Assessment of Cardiac Filling Pressures.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) has been associated with diastolic dysfunction in pre-clinical studies, but with limited evaluation in clinical settings. We sought to examine the association between post-operative AKI and diastolic function after pediatric heart transplantation.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective review of patients ≤ 21years undergoing first-time heart transplantation between May 2010-July 2023. AKI was defined and staged per the KDIGO creatinine criteria, with Stage 2 or 3 classified as severe. Right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) obtained from surveillance cardiac catheterizations in the first two years post-transplant were used to assess diastolic function. Linear mixed-effects models were used to compare hemodynamics between groups.
RESULTS: We included 101 patients, aged 0-20 years, median 4 years (IQR 0-13). Pre-transplant diagnosis was congenital heart disease (CHD) in 51 (50%) and cardiomyopathy in 50 (50%) patients. Post-operative AKI occurred in 29 (29%) patients; 16/29 had severe AKI. AKI was more common in patients with CHD than cardiomyopathy [20/29 (69%) vs. 9/29 (31%), p = 0.02]. On mixed-effects model analysis adjusting for pre-transplant diagnosis, ischemia time > 4 h, and time since transplantation, severe AKI was associated with higher filling pressures over the first 2 years post-transplant, including a 2.2 mmHg increase in RVEDP (95% CI 1.3-3.1; p < 0.0001) and a 1.8 mmHg increase in PCWP (95% CI 0.8-2.8; p = 0.0005).
CONCLUSIONS: Severe post-transplant AKI was independently associated with higher biventricular filling pressures, suggesting a clinically relevant kidney-heart interaction. Larger studies are needed to further define its mechanistic and clinical implications.

Title: Urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and clinical outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a focus on patients with impaired ejection fraction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the prognostic value of urinary neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) normalized to creatinine in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS), focusing on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 144 patients emergently admitted for ACS, with urinary NGAL measured 4-48 h postadmission. Primary and secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), respectively. Optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoffs were determined using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Associations between urinary NGAL/creatinine and clinical outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models.
RESULTS: During a median 734.5-day follow-up, 8 deaths and 44 MACCE occurred. The optimal NGAL/creatinine cutoff for predicting MACCE was 20.85 ng/mg creatinine. All deaths occurred in the high NGAL/creatinine group (≥20.85), but mortality analyses were limited by statistical separation. High NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with MACCE (hazard ratio = 3.47, 95% confidence interval = 1.61-7.47) and remained associated with a higher event hazard after adjustment for age, brain natriuretic peptide, LVEF, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (adjusted hazard ratio = 2.75; P = 0.017). In subgroup analyses, the area under the curve for MACCE was numerically higher in patients with LVEF <50% than in those with LVEF ≥50% (0.753 vs. 0.581). Formal interaction testing in the Cox model, however, did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF category (P for interaction = 0.100).
CONCLUSION: Urinary NGAL/creatinine was significantly associated with long-term MACCE in patients with ACS. Although subgroup analyses showed numerically different associations according to LVEF, formal interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by LVEF.

Title: Postpartum Blood Pressure After Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Subsequent Cardiovascular Disease: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
Journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between blood pressure values at 6 weeks postpartum and subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) over a 20-year period among women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.
SETTING: English primary and secondary care data, linked to cause-specific mortality records from 2000 to 2020.
POPULATION: A cohort of 39 934 women between 15 and 49 years of age at birth who had HDP, were registered with a general practitioner (GP) contributing to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD), and eligible for linkage to hospital episode statistics (HES) data were included. We excluded 22 100 (55.3%) women with no blood pressure values recorded at 6 weeks postpartum.
METHODS: Primary analysis included multivariable Cox regression modelling (weighted by the inverse probability of having a severe HDP).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Validated composite outcome of 12 cardiovascular diseases.
RESULTS: The rate for incident cardiovascular events was 109 per 10 000 person-years; 794 (68%) of them occurred in women aged < 40 years. Women with abnormal blood pressure at 6 weeks postpartum had a higher risk of subsequent CVD than women with normal blood pressure: 10.9% vs. 5.4% - adjusted hazard ratio 1.96 (95% CI 1.51-2.54).
CONCLUSIONS: Less than half of women with HDP had a blood pressure record in their GP notes at 6 weeks postpartum. The absence of a record of normal blood pressure at this time point was associated with an increased risk for subsequent CVD The immediate postpartum period may be a crucial window in preventive care to improve women's health.

Title: Circulating tumor plasma cells correlate with tumor burden and routine laboratory markers in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma: A retrospective single-center study.
Abstract: Circulating tumor plasma cells (CTPCs) detected by multiparameter flow cytometry may serve as a minimally invasive marker of disease burden in multiple myeloma (MM). However, the relationship between CTPC burden, routine laboratory parameters, and bone marrow (BM) involvement remains insufficiently characterized in regional clinical settings. This retrospective single-center study included 51 consecutive patients with newly diagnosed MM. Peripheral blood CTPCs were quantified using ten-color flow cytometry. Among them, 41 patients with evaluable CTPC data were stratified into CTPC-higher (n = 20) and CTPC-lower (n = 21) groups using a 0.07% cutoff. Laboratory variables and immunophenotypic features were compared between groups, and correlations were assessed using Spearman rank analysis. Exploratory logistic regression adjusted for age and sex was performed, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied to multiple comparisons. Compared with the CTPC-lower group, the CTPC-higher group had lower hemoglobin levels (73.5 vs 107.0 g/L; P < .001), lower albumin levels (30.9 vs 38.2 g/L; P = .006), higher β2-microglobulin levels (6.97 vs 3.25 mg/L; P = .004), and higher BM plasma cell percentages on smear examination (34.75% vs 12.00%; P = .005). CTPC levels were positively correlated with BM plasma cell percentage on smear examination (ρ = 0.67; P < .001) and negatively correlated with hemoglobin levels (ρ=-0.68; P < .001). These group differences and correlations remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction (all q ≤ 0.018). In age- and sex-adjusted analyses, hemoglobin, albumin, β2-microglobulin, and BM plasma cell percentage on smear remained associated with CTPC-higher status. Higher peripheral blood CTPC levels were associated with greater BM tumor burden and more abnormal routine laboratory markers in patients with newly diagnosed MM. CTPC quantification may serve as an adjunctive marker for baseline disease assessment in regional clinical settings. These cross-sectional findings from this limited sample do not establish prognostic value.

Title: Malignant transformation in diabetic foot ulcers: A cross-sectional analysis of the impact of pathology results on patient management after diabetic foot surgery.
Abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are a major cause of lower-extremity amputation, hospitalization, and mortality. Although management focuses on wound care, infection control, and limb preservation, malignancies may develop in chronic, nonhealing wounds, and tumors may mimic DFUs. Evidence on malignancy in DFUs is limited, and the diagnostic contribution of routine histopathological examination in surgically treated cases remains unclear. This study aimed to determine the frequency of histopathologically confirmed malignancy in patients undergoing surgery for chronic DFUs and assess its impact on management and care. This retrospective, cross-sectional, single-center study was conducted at a Training and Research Hospital. We included 678 consecutive patients admitted with chronic DFUs between January 2019 and June 2021 who underwent surgical treatment and histopathological examination. Patients managed conservatively and those without a pathology specimen were excluded. Demographic characteristics, ulcer features, surgical procedures, histopathological findings, and changes in treatment and care were obtained from medical records. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0. The malignancy rate and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using the Clopper-Pearson method. A total of 678 patients were included. Of these, 74% were male, and the mean age was 64.69 ± 10.92 years. Wagner grade 4 ulcers accounted for 61.7% of cases, while 65.0% were classified as PEDIS grade 3. Histopathological examination identified malignancy in 4 patients (0.6%; 95% CI, 0.16-1.50); two of these patients had metastatic involvement. The treatment and care plan was modified for all patients in whom malignancy was detected. Overall, 95.6% of patients healed with wound care after surgery, without further changes to their treatment or care plan. However, 1.9% required amputation at a more proximal level, 1.3% experienced limb loss, and 1.2% died from other diabetes-related complications. Although uncommon, malignancy and metastatic involvement may occur in chronic DFUs. The possibility of malignancy should therefore be considered, particularly in nonhealing, atypical, or clinically suspicious ulcers. Ensuring appropriate histopathological evaluation of such ulcers may help healthcare professionals and wound care nurses identify primary or metastatic malignancies at an earlier stage.

Title: Acute ischemic stroke despite NOAC therapy in atrial fibrillation: Clinical factors associated with AIS in a 2-center observational case-control study.
Abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) can occur in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (AF) despite treatment with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs). This study evaluated clinical, treatment-related, inflammatory, and echocardiographic factors associated with AIS in NOAC-treated patients with AF. This retrospective, 2-center case-control study included 322 patients with non-valvular AF who had received NOAC therapy for at least 3 months. Of these, 112 were hospitalized with AIS and 210 were outpatient controls without AIS at the study assessment. Group differences and factors associated with AIS were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. ROC analyses were exploratory. Patients with AIS were older than controls and more often had hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, prior stroke, and prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use. In the adjusted analysis, prior stroke (OR = 32.79), coronary artery disease (OR = 3.47), prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use (OR = 2.55), female sex (OR = 2.26), diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.99), and C-reactive protein (OR per mg/L = 1.10) were associated with AIS. HAS-BLED (area under the curve = 0.881, 95% CI = 0.844-0.918) and CHA2DS2-VASc (area under the curve = 0.840, 95% CI = 0.795-0.885) distinguished AIS cases from controls in exploratory ROC analyses. Among NOAC-treated patients with AF, prior stroke and cardiovascular comorbidities were strongly associated with AIS. Prescribed reduced-dose NOAC use was also associated with AIS. Inflammatory markers measured during acute stroke had limited additional value. Because this was a case-control study, the findings do not estimate stroke incidence or future stroke risk and require prospective validation.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy: A comprehensive review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management.
Abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is a prevalent yet frequently underrecognized cardiac complication of liver cirrhosis, characterized by impaired myocardial contractile reserve, diastolic dysfunction, and electrophysiological abnormalities. Despite its clinical significance, particularly in the setting of liver transplantation, CCM remains largely overlooked. We performed a narrative review of the literature on CCM published up to December 2025, covering pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, imaging modalities, biomarkers, and management strategies. Depending on the diagnostic criteria used, the prevalence of CCM ranges from 29% to 67.2%. Advanced imaging techniques, particularly global longitudinal strain and cardiac magnetic resonance, enable early detection of subclinical systolic dysfunction. A "toxic triangle" comprising systemic inflammation, metabolic derangements, and neurohormonal activation represents an integrated pathophysiological model that drives myocardial fibrosis and dysfunction. Beta-blockers and aldosterone antagonists remain mainstays of pharmacological management, while liver transplantation is currently the only definitive therapy. CCM is an underrecognized condition with substantial clinical implications. Standardized diagnostic criteria, validated biomarkers, and large-scale prospective studies are urgently needed to improve patient outcomes.

Title: Comparison analysis of the triglyceride-glucose index, triglyceride-glucose and frailty index in cardiovascular disease and mortality association among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based cohort study.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of excess mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Conventional risk assessment may not fully capture the metabolic abnormalities and physiological vulnerability associated with RA. We investigated whether the triglyceride-glucose-frailty index (TyG-FI), which combines a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with accumulated health deficits, was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among adults with RA. We analyzed 1090 adults with self-reported RA from 10 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 1999 and 2018. TyG-FI was calculated as the product of the triglyceride-glucose index and a 49-item deficit-accumulation frailty index. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association with prevalent CVD, whereas Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and discrimination analyses were conducted as secondary analyses. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-unit higher TyG-FI was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD (odds ratio, 4.50; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-6.33) and a higher hazard of cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.77; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.70). The reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.80 for prevalent CVD and 0.81 for cardiovascular mortality in models incorporating TyG-FI, compared with 0.73 and 0.80, respectively, in models incorporating TyG. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a stronger association between TyG-FI and prevalent CVD among participants aged ≤65 years (P for interaction = .044). Higher TyG-FI was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among US adults with self-reported RA. TyG-FI may capture complementary metabolic and frailty-related information; however, its incremental predictive value, calibration, clinical utility, and external validity require further evaluation before clinical implementation.

Title: The effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on heart rate and physiological parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased sympathetic activity and an elevated cardiovascular risk. Noninvasive interventions targeting autonomic regulation may offer complementary therapeutic strategies.
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial aimed to investigate the acute effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters of patients with OSA. Patients with polysomnography-confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 15 events/hour) were randomly assigned to an intervention group that received a standardized 16-minute multiregional fascial mobilization protocol or a control group that rested quietly in the supine position for the corresponding period without receiving manual or tactile intervention. The intervention targeted the cervical, thoracic, and abdominal regions, under controlled conditions. The primary outcomes included heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and peripheral oxygen saturation. Measurements were obtained at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and 5 and 15 minutes post-intervention.
RESULTS: A total of 95 male patients (mean age: 48.12 ± 10.21 years) completed the study. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups, except for heart rate. After adjustment for baseline heart rate using mixed analysis of covariance, no significant group × time interaction was observed for heart rate (P = .476, partial ηp2 = .008). Similarly, no significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, or peripheral oxygen saturation (all P > .05). Although significant time effects were observed for some physiological parameters, the magnitude of these effects varied across outcomes, and none was accompanied by a significant group × time interaction. Therefore, these temporal changes were not interpreted as intervention-specific effects. No adverse events were reported.
CONCLUSION: Heart rate changed significantly over time following the interventions; however, after adjustment for baseline heart rate, the pattern of change did not differ significantly between the fascial mobilization and control groups. Similarly, no significant between-group differences in changes over time were observed for blood pressure or oxygen saturation. These findings do not demonstrate a specific acute effect of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters assessed. Further studies using advanced measures of autonomic function and longer follow-up periods are warranted.

Title: Deaths involving chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and cardiac arrest in older US adults, 1999-2023: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
Abstract: National long-term trends and disparities in deaths in which both chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and cardiac arrest are recorded on death certificates are not well characterized. We used CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data (1999-2023) to identify US adults aged ≥ 65 years whose death certificates listed both COPD (ICD-10 J41-J44) and cardiac arrest (I46) as underlying or contributing causes. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization; the urbanization analysis was limited to 1999 to 2020 because those data were not available after 2020. Trends were analyzed using annual percentage changes (APCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); P < .05 was considered statistically significant. Among 7,18,280 deaths involving concurrent coding of COPD and cardiac arrest, AAMRs declined from 86.4 in 1999 to 52.5 in 2023. A significant decrease occurred from 1999 to 2006 (APC: -2.87; P = .01), followed by a plateau and a further decline from 2021 to 2023 (APC: -4.77; P < .001). Older men exhibited higher AAMRs than older women (86.8 vs 55.2). Non-Hispanic (NH) White individuals had the highest mortality (69.7), followed by NH Black/African American (64.3) and Hispanic/Latino (60.7) populations. The West region reported the highest AAMR (98.9). During 1999 to 2020, nonmetropolitan residents had higher AAMRs than metropolitan residents (70.8 vs 67.9). Population-level mortality records involving both COPD and cardiac arrest declined overall but remained heterogeneous across demographic and geographic strata. These findings describe concurrent coding on death certificates and do not establish that COPD increases the risk of cardiac arrest or causes the observed deaths.

Title: Association of Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) with long-term mortality in type 2 diabetes patients with coronary heart disease: A prospective national cohort study.
Abstract: Endothelial dysfunction is prevalent in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) with coronary heart disease (CHD), increasing cardiovascular risk. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) is a novel composite biomarker, yet its prognostic value in this comorbid population remains unclear. In this prospective cohort study, we analyzed 909 participants with T2DM and CHD from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999 to 2010, followed until 2019. EASIX was calculated using lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and platelet count. Multivariable Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing-risk models assessed associations between EASIX and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, respectively. Time-dependent C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement evaluated the incremental prognostic value of EASIX beyond established risk factors. During a median follow-up of 111 months, 617 all-cause and 251 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Higher EASIX levels were significantly associated with increased mortality risks. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile had a hazard ratio of 1.93 (95% confidence interval = 1.48-2.50) for all-cause mortality and a subdistribution hazard ratio of 1.56 (95% confidence interval = 1.05-2.33) for cardiovascular mortality compared with the lowest quartile. Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a significant nonlinear positive relationship. Adding EASIX to a base model (age, HbA1c, and estimated glomerular filtration rate) significantly improved the C-statistic, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement for both outcomes (all P < .001). Elevated EASIX levels are independently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with T2DM and CHD. In this population, its inclusion in risk assessment protocols enhances the predictive value for long-term clinical outcomes.

Title: Prognostic value of systemic inflammatory markers in patients with malignancy-associated pulmonary thromboembolism: A retrospective observational study.
Abstract: Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) is a severe and potentially fatal complication in patients with malignancy. Systemic inflammation plays an important role in both cancer progression and thrombogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the association of systemic inflammatory indices with in-hospital mortality and clinical risk classification in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. This retrospective study included 75 adult patients diagnosed with both malignancy and PTE at a tertiary chest diseases center between February 2018 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, cancer types, laboratory values at diagnosis, treatment details, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), lymphocyte-to-CRP ratio (LCRPR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated from blood samples obtained at diagnosis. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, and the secondary outcome was the association between systemic inflammatory markers and ESC PTE clinical risk classification. The mean age was 69.5 ± 11.8 years, and 56% of patients were male. Lung (24%), colorectal (13.3%), and breast (9.3%) cancers were the most common malignancies. In-hospital mortality was 20%. Neutrophil count (P = .026), NLR (P = .032), and lactate (P = .027) were significantly higher in patients who died during hospitalization. ROC analysis identified an NLR cutoff value of 4.95, with a sensitivity of 86.7% and a specificity of 51.7%. Neutrophil count and SIRI were significantly higher in the intermediate-risk group (P = .036 and P = .049, respectively), whereas troponin was highest in the high-risk group (P < .001). Neutrophil count, NLR, and lactate levels were associated with in-hospital mortality in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. Neutrophil count and SIRI were also associated with ESC clinical risk classification. These findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Causal effects of antihypertensive drugs on thyroid diseases: A trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization study.
Abstract: Thyroid disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular disease, including hypertension, but whether long-term modulation of antihypertensive drug targets influences thyroid disease risk remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the associations of 7 antihypertensive drug-target classes with thyroid diseases in European and East Asian populations using a trans-ancestry drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) framework. We performed a two-sample, trans-ancestry drug-target MR analysis of 7 antihypertensive target classes. Target-proximal single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with systolic blood pressure (SBP) were used as genetic proxies. Estimates were scaled per 1-mm Hg genetically predicted increase in SBP; the putative effect of target inhibition that lowers SBP was therefore interpreted in the opposite direction. Summary statistics were obtained for 4 primary thyroid diseases, benign thyroid tumors where available, and 3 thyroid-related proteins in European and East Asian datasets. Hypertension was used as a positive-control outcome. Random-effects inverse-variance weighting was the primary method, with Wald ratio estimation for single-nucleotide polymorphism instruments and weighted-median, Cochran's Q, MR-Egger, and Mendelian Randomization Pleiotropy RESidual Sum and Outlier analyses as sensitivity assessments. Within the European populace, genetic surrogates for β-blockers exhibit (odds ratio = 0.93; 95% confidence interval = 0.87-0.99) a close association with heightened susceptibility to thyroid carcinoma, whereas KCNH2 (1.15; 1.01-1.32) demonstrates an inverse correlation with thyroid cancer risk. Moreover, calcium channel blockers exhibit a conspicuous linkage with an elevated incidence of hyperthyroidism (0.97; 0.96-0.99) alongside a diminished likelihood of thyroid cancer (1.07; 1.03-1.10). CYP17A1 exerts a protective influence against hyperthyroidism (1.04; 10.1-1.07) and Graves disease (1.10; 1.05-1.16) but manifests a pathogenic effect concerning hypothyroidism (0.99; 0.97-1.00) and thyroid cancer (0.92; 0.86-0.98). Conversely, KCNJ11 demonstrates a proximate correlation between diminished hypothyroidism risk and augmented thyroid cancer susceptibility (0.83; 0.73-0.95). Analogous estimations were noted for CYP17A1 within the East Asian cohort. Genetically proxied perturbation of several antihypertensive drug targets was associated with thyroid disease risk, with CYP17A1 showing the broadest cross-ancestry pattern. These estimates reflect lifelong target-proximal genetic effects rather than the clinical effects of prescribed drugs and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending replication, pharmacoepidemiological studies, and randomized clinical trials.

Title: TyG-ABSI and TyG-WWI as insulin-resistance body shape markers of mortality in middle-aged and older adults within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework: A multi-cohort observational study with external survival-model validation.
Abstract: Insulin resistance, adiposity, kidney dysfunction, and cardiovascular disease are closely interconnected in middle-aged and older adults and are central to the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework. Triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-related indices combine routine lipid, glucose, and anthropometric information, but their cross-population consistency and incremental prognostic value for mortality-risk assessment remain uncertain. We analyzed harmonized participant-level data from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), and Health and Retirement Study (HRS), with HRS used as a sensitivity cohort. Eligible participants were aged ≥ 50 years, had follow-up beyond baseline, available mortality status, and complete data for 7 TyG-related indices. Cohort-specific Cox models estimated associations of standardized TyG, TyG-body mass index, TyG-waist circumference, TyG-waist-to-height ratio, TyG-weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), TyG-a body shape index (ABSI), and TyG-body roundness index with all-cause mortality. Nonlinearity, proportional-hazards assumptions, sensitivity analyses, NHANES heart disease mortality, incremental prediction, and survival machine learning with external validation were further assessed. The primary analytic sample included 21,044 NHANES participants, 5454 ELSA participants, and 11,157 CHARLS participants, among whom 5566, 116, and 1393 deaths occurred during follow-up, respectively. The HRS sensitivity cohort included 4103 participants and 484 deaths. In fully adjusted Cox models, all 7 TyG-related indices were associated with higher all-cause mortality in NHANES, with the strongest associations observed for TyG-ABSI (hazard ratio [HR] 1.159, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.115-1.205) and TyG-WWI (HR 1.155, 95% CI 1.113-1.199). In CHARLS, TyG-ABSI was positively associated with mortality (HR 1.088, 95% CI 1.029-1.151), whereas estimates in ELSA were imprecise. In HRS sensitivity analyses, TyG-WWI and TyG-ABSI remained positively associated with mortality. Adding TyG-related indices to a clinical Cox prediction framework produced only minimal absolute gains in discrimination. The final TyG-ABSI extreme gradient boosting survival model yielded 5-year time-dependent area under the curves of 0.808 in the NHANES internal test set and 0.760 in CHARLS. A research-use web calculator was developed for 5-year and 8-year mortality-risk estimation. TyG-ABSI and TyG-WWI were the most consistent TyG-related body shape markers of all-cause mortality across international aging cohorts. Although TyG-ABSI supported externally validated survival prediction, its incremental predictive value beyond established clinical and CKM variables was limited. These findings suggest that TyG-related body shape indices may serve primarily as interpretable, low-cost CKM risk markers rather than standalone prediction tools.

Title: Impact of portal hypertension on clinical outcomes in critically Ill adult patients: A retrospective study: Outcomes in critically Ill patients with portal hypertension.
Abstract: Liver dysfunction is a common complication in critically ill patients, and portal hypertension (PHT) represents a severe hepatic pathological condition closely associated with adverse patient outcomes. This study aims to investigate the impact of PHT on clinical outcomes in critically ill adult patients. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Market for Intensive Care IV database. All critically ill patients admitted to the hospital were included in this study. Logistic regression analysis was used to assess the correlation between PHT and hospital mortality, length of stay in the intensive care unit (LOS-ICU), and length of stay in hospital in critically ill patients, and multiple collinearity checks were performed. Propensity score matching was used to minimize group differences, and subgroup analyses were conducted. A total of 46,804 adult critically ill patients were included in this study. The hospital mortality rate for critically ill patients with PHT was 19%, significantly higher than the 8.8% mortality rate for patients without PHT (P < .05). Critically ill patients with PHT also had longer LOS-ICU and length of stay in hospital and higher total bilirubin levels (P < .05). Furthermore, multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that PHT was significantly associated with hospital mortality (OR: 2.716, 95% CI: 2.330-3.158, P < .001). After propensity score matching, the baseline differences between the 2 groups were significantly reduced, and the results showed that critically ill patients with PHT had worse clinical outcomes. However, the LOS-ICU was not significantly different after matching. PHT is a significant predictor of poor prognosis in critically ill adult patients, necessitating enhanced clinical monitoring and management to improve their clinical outcomes.

Title: Prognostic impact of moderate secondary mitral regurgitation after optimized medical therapy in heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The prognostic significance of moderate secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) after optimized guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.
METHODS: We analysed 2468 ambulatory HF patients with paired transthoracic echocardiography at baseline and after 12 months of optimized GDMT. The primary composite was all-cause death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH). Secondary endpoints included all-cause mortality and recurrent HFHs.
RESULTS: The mean age of patients was 66.2 ± 12.5 years, 70.6% were male, and the mean baseline left ventricular ejection fraction was 36.1% ± 13.6%. At 12 months, 80.5% of patients had no/mild MR, 15.6% had moderate MR, and 3.9% had severe MR. During a median 6.9-year follow-up, 1240 patients experienced the primary endpoint. Compared with no/mild MR, both moderate and severe MR at 12 months were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint [moderate: hazard ratio (HR) 1.69, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.47-1.95; severe: HR 1.81, 95% CI 1.44-2.29; both P < .001). Moderate MR was also independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.32-1.79; P < .001) and recurrent HFHs (incidence rate ratio 2.17, 95% CI 1.81-2.60). Heart failure hospitalization rates were 9.03, 20.0, and 26.1 per 100 person-years in patients with no/mild, moderate, and severe MR, respectively. Among patients with moderate MR at 12 months, outcomes did not differ according to baseline MR severity.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large-scale study, residual moderate secondary MR after 12 months of optimized GDMT was common and was independently associated with increased long-term mortality and HFHs.

Title: The Impact of Anaesthesia Method on the Use of Anaesthesia Department Resources in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health-related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact. In this study, we analysed time, costs, and disposable materials associated with spinal anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia during total knee arthroplasty.
METHODS: A total of 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to spinal or general anaesthesia. Outcomes were total operating room time, non-operative operating room time, post-anaesthesia care unit time, use of drugs affecting haemodynamics, and the need for arterial cannulation and urinary catheterisation. In addition, we evaluated the financial costs and waste produced by single-use equipment and medicines in both anaesthesia methods.
RESULTS: Anaesthesia method did not affect operating room time (median 152 min [interquartile range 136-168 min] vs. 150 min [137-165 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 2 min [95% CI -3 to 6 min], p = 0.49). However, after spinal anaesthesia, patients appeared to spend more time in the postanaesthesia care unit than after general anaesthesia (median 104 min [71-148 min] vs. 73 min [49-98 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 32 min [95% CI 23-42 min], p < 0.001). Medication for hypotension was more common in the general anaesthesia group, whereas medication for hypertension was more common in the spinal anaesthesia group. General anaesthesia generated more disposable material (1252 vs. 611 g), and both medicine and equipment expenses were higher (total costs €83 vs. €36).
CONCLUSION: With this anaesthesia regimen, knee arthroplasty patients occupied the operating room for a similar duration regardless of anaesthesia method, but patients required longer recovery in the postanaesthesia care unit after spinal anaesthesia. Regarding disposable material and medicine use, spinal anaesthesia appeared to be more economical and material-sparing than total intravenous anaesthesia. Furthermore, spinal anaesthesia appeared to cause less hypotension requiring haemodynamic interventions than general anaesthesia.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This health-economic analysis estimates for how different aspects of general or spinal anaesthesia care contribute to process flow and item costs. Findings suggest that there may be measurably more costs associated with one of the anaesthesia type choices compared with the other, though this will depend on choices for materials and more.
