The findings describe contemporary surgeon-selected practice but do not determine the optimal allocation strategy, thereby reinforcing a clinically relevant message for contemporary vascular surgery: appropriate patient selection, meticulous technical execution, and comprehensive revascularization strategy are the key drivers of clinical outcomes, whereas patch material should likely be regarded as a complementary component within an individualized reconstructive framework.

Title: Asymptomatic vs. Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid disease, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations.
METHODS: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level one stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction, and death at 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates.
RESULTS: 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (IQR 6-11). SD patients had a longer median length of stay (2 vs 1 day, p = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs 36%, p = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30- and 90-day and 0.9% at 1-year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30-day, 90-day, and one year, with no difference between AD vs SD. 1-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90-day and one year, without a difference by AD vs SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer LOS, SD patients did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.

Title: External Validation of the CARE-BMT and Modified CARE-BMT Scores for Cardiac Event Prediction After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac events after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) are associated with increased non-relapse mortality (NRM) and inferior survival. The CARE-BMT score predicts cardiovascular events after hematopoietic cell transplantation but does not incorporate post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy). We aimed to externally validate the original CARE-BMT score and a modified version incorporating standard-dose PTCy exposure in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) undergoing allo-HCT.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter study including 809 adults with AML who underwent first allo-HCT across 11 Spanish transplant centers. The original and modified CARE-BMT scores were retrospectively applied. The primary endpoint was the cumulative incidence of post-transplant cardiac events, with relapse and death considered competing risks.
RESULTS: Sixty patients developed a cardiac event, corresponding to a cumulative incidence of 6.9% (95% CI, 5.2-8.8). Cardiac events were associated with inferior 3-year overall survival (50.1% vs 62.5%; P = 0.001) and higher 3-year NRM (21.3% vs 6.2%; P = 0.001). Using the original CARE-BMT score, patients were classified as intermediate-risk (n = 246) or high-risk (n = 563), with no low-risk patients identified. Cardiac event incidence was higher in the high-risk group (8.6% vs 3.0%; HR, 2.89; P = 0.005). The modified CARE-BMT score classified patients as low-risk (n = 85), intermediate-risk (n = 558), or high-risk (n = 166), with progressively increasing cardiac event incidence (2.4%, 6.1%, and 11.8%, respectively; P = 0.011). High-risk patients had a significantly greater risk of cardiac events than low-risk patients (HR, 5.37; P = 0.024).
CONCLUSIONS: In this AML allo-HCT cohort, cardiac events occurred in approximately 7% of patients and were associated with worse survival and increased NRM. Incorporating standard-dose PTCy improved risk stratification, supporting inclusion of transplant-specific variables in cardiovascular risk prediction after allo-HCT.

Title: Pregnancy and Offspring Outcomes After Prenatal Stimulant or Atomoxetine Exposure: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of prenatal exposure to stimulants and atomoxetine for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with pregnancy, congenital, perinatal, and neurodevelopmental outcomes.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to March 2026. Protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD42024506319).
STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomized trials and observational studies comparing pregnancies or offspring exposed to stimulant medications, methylphenidate- or amphetamine-based agents, or atomoxetine with unexposed comparators and reported outcomes were eligible.
STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: Reporting guidance for systematic reviews and observational meta-analyses was followed. Two reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled unadjusted and adjusted estimates separately. For neurodevelopmental outcomes, comparators restricted to attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder populations were prioritized when available.
RESULTS: Twenty-five studies were included; 23 contributed to quantitative analyses. Exposure windows included periconceptional, first-trimester, early-, late-, or continued-pregnancy exposure. Exposure was associated with major congenital malformations in unadjusted analyses (risk ratio, 1.25; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-1.37), but not after adjustment (adjusted risk ratio, 1.04; 95% confidence interval, 0.97-1.12). No adjusted association was observed with cardiovascular malformations (adjusted risk ratio, 1.20; 95% confidence interval, 0.88-1.63), although methylphenidate showed a modest increase (adjusted risk ratio, 1.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-1.74). In adjusted analyses, exposure was not associated with miscarriage, preterm birth, low birth weight, small for gestational age, neonatal intensive care unit admission, neurodevelopmental disorders, autism spectrum disorder, or offspring attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Low 5-minute Apgar score remained associated with exposure after adjustment (adjusted risk ratio, 1.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-1.42). Lower adjusted autism spectrum disorder risk with stimulants was not replicated in methylphenidate-specific analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal exposure to stimulants or atomoxetine for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder was not associated with increased adjusted risk of major congenital malformations or most adverse pregnancy, perinatal, and neurodevelopmental outcomes. Attenuation of crude associations after adjustment suggests confounding by indication, residual confounding, and maternal characteristics. The observed associations between methylphenidate and cardiovascular malformations and between exposure and low 5-minute Apgar score warrant continued investigation but should not be interpreted as evidence of causal harm.

Title: Transcarotid Access for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement With the Evolut Self-Expanding Valve: Outcomes from a Real-World Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcarotid access for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is the most commonly used alternate access in the United States. Real-world evidence on transcarotid access using the Evolut self-expanding valve based on larger numbers of patients may help inform treatment optimization towards better outcomes.
METHODS: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapies Registry™ was queried for patients undergoing native TAVR using transcarotid access with an Evolut (January 2015-December 2024). In-hospital, 30-day, and 1-year outcomes are reported.
RESULTS: We identified 2,105 patients (mean age 78.3±7.9 years) with mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons predicted risk of mortality 6.4±5.3. Most were high/extreme surgical risk (60.0%) with New York Heart Association class III/IV heart failure symptoms (66.8%) and mean baseline Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) Score 45.3±25.4. Implant success was 99.6% primarily using general anesthesia (95.8%) with median procedure time of 88.0 (Q1=68.0, Q3=115.0) minutes. Median length of stay was 2.0 (Q1=1.0, Q3=3.0) days; 89.0% were discharged to home. In-hospital, 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality was 2.1%, 3.8% and 16.5%; stroke occurred in 3.1%, 3.8% and 5.1% of patients, respectively. At 30 days, major vascular complications (1.9%), valve related (0.4%) and non-valve related (10.9%) readmissions were low. The mean change in KCCQ score from baseline to 1-year was +30.5±27.1 points.
CONCLUSIONS: Transcarotid TAVR with the Evolut TAV is an effective, safe approach for patients with unfavorable iliofemoral anatomy. Heart teams should become facile with this technique to provide optimal care across the anatomy spectrum.

Title: Functional outcome after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury following thoracic aortic surgery.
Journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury and to assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery.
METHODS: Single-centre retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024. Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was diagnosed by postoperative vocal cord paralysis. Aortic arch surgery included partial and total arch replacement, while thoracoabdominal surgery involved the proximal descending aorta. The primary endpoint was full voice recovery. Secondary endpoints included recovery of normal vocal cord mobility, residual dysphonia, the need for voice therapy, and vocal cord interventions.
RESULTS: Among 2,983 patients undergoing aortic surgery, 70 (2.3%) were diagnosed with postoperative recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. Median follow-up was 17 [IQR: 7-25] months. The incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury was 1.7% after arch surgery and 5.3% after thoracoabdominal procedures. At final follow-up, 34 patients (50%) achieved full voice recovery, while 20 (30%) had mild dysphonia, 9 (13%) moderate dysphonia, and 5 (7%) severe dysphonia. Voice therapy was performed in 49 (70%) patients, and 10 (14%) required additional vocal cord interventions.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, the incidence of recurrent laryngeal nerve injury after aortic surgery was lower than previously reported. Functional outcomes were favourable, with most patients achieving full or near-complete voice recovery through conservative or interventional management. Structured follow-up and multidisciplinary care remain essential to optimize outcomes after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.

Title: Dietary supplementation with plant sterols for obesity management and related metabolic disorders: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover clinical trial.
Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although plant sterols (PS) lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL cholesterol) in normal-weight individuals; their efficacy in obesity is unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of PS supplementation on LDL cholesterol (primary outcome) and on body composition, other biochemical, lifestyle, and sarcopenia parameters (secondary and exploratory outcomes) in individuals with overweight or class I to III obesity and mild hypercholesterolemia.
METHODS: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover clinical trial was conducted in 23 participants (body mass index: 36.4 ± 4.2 kg/m2). Participants consumed a food supplement with 2 g/d of PS or a placebo for 8 wk per phase, with a 6-wk washout period.
RESULTS: LDL cholesterol did not differ between PS and placebo (P = 0.632): the change from baseline was +0.1 mg/dL [95% confidence interval (CI): -7.1, 7.3 mg/dL] after PS compared with +3.9 mg/dL (95% CI: -7.6, 15.4 mg/dL) after placebo. No difference was found between PS and placebo in any other lipid parameter, in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, or in the glucose regulation parameters, and no between-treatment difference in body composition, sarcopenia, or lifestyle parameters remained significant after correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: In individuals with overweight or class I to III obesity, 2 g/d of PS did not reduce LDL cholesterol compared with placebo, and no effect was found on any other cardiometabolic parameter. This may reflect reduced PS efficacy in this population. The trial was powered only for LDL cholesterol. Therefore, the secondary findings are exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered trials. This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT06481020.

Title: Sivelestat sodium improves post-resuscitation brain outcomes possibly by inhibiting cell pyroptosis via inactivating the cGAS/STING/TBK1 pathway.
Abstract: Sivelestat sodium (SS) is shown to protect vital organs against regional ischemic stimuli. We investigated its effects on brain outcomes after global ischemic stimuli resulted from cardiac arrest (CA) and resuscitation. Adult pigs were randomly divided into sham (S), cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and CPR + SS groups. The animals were subjected to 9 mins of CA followed by 6 mins of CPR. After resuscitation, a dose of 10 mg/kg of SS was intravenously administered for 60 mins. Post-resuscitation brain injury and neurological function were regularly evaluated. Brain hippocampus tissues were harvested to measure histopathological injury, cell apoptosis, pyroptosis-related proteins and proinflammatory cytokines, and the cGAS/STING/TBK1 pathway. Consequently, post-resuscitation brain injury and neurological dysfunction were observed in those animals experiencing the CA/CPR procedure. However, they were significantly milder in the CPR + SS group than in the CPR group. Hippocampal histopathological injury and apoptosis were observed after resuscitation in the CPR and CPR + SS groups. Nevertheless, SS treatment significantly decreased both of them compared with the CPR group. Furthermore, pyroptosis-related proteins were upregulated, its-related proinflammatory cytokines were increased, and the cGAS/STING/TBK1 pathway was activated in post-resuscitation hippocampus in the CPR and CPR + SS groups. Likewise, SS treatment significantly reversed the changes of pyroptosis-related proteins and proinflammatory cytokines, and the cGAS/STING/TBK1 pathway compared to the CPR group. Thus, SS treatment was effective in improving post-resuscitation brain outcomes, and its protective role was possibly related to the inhibition of cell pyroptosis through the inactivation of the cGAS/STING/TBK1 pathway.

Title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry.
METHODS: A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter < 7 mm, iliac artery tortuosity index > 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention.
RESULTS: Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively.
CONCLUSION: The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

Title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.
METHODS: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy.
RESULTS: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents.
CONCLUSION: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

Title: Long Term Results of Surgical Treatment of Chronic Venous Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: A Single Centre Experience.
Journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis aimed to evaluate the surgical and long term functional outcomes of a structured treatment algorithm for patients with chronic venous thoracic outlet syndrome (cVTOS).
METHODS: Patients with cVTOS and treated at this tertiary centre between 2016 and 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of transaxillary thoracic outlet decompression (TOD), venolysis, and subclavian vein (SCV) recanalisation. In case of persistent venous obstruction during the primary procedure, anticipated repeat percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) was planned. Anticoagulation (rivaroxaban) was prescribed until 48 hours before surgery, resumed the day after surgery for six weeks, or until 48 hours before re-PTA. The primary endpoint included SCV patency and secondary outcomes included functional outcomes (DASH and Derkash scores).
RESULTS: Seventy patients were included (mean age 35 years; 56% women). Median time to presentation was 40 (20.0 - 104.0) months after initial upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT). Eleven patients (16%) had an operative complication (haematoma n = 6, pneumothorax n = 1, UEDVT n = 1, transient Horner syndrome n = 1, phrenic nerve injury n = 1, and SCV rupture n = 1). Median length of hospital stay was 1.0 day. Venography post-TOD/PTA showed persistent venous obstruction in 15 patients (21%) for which re-PTA was planned. Over time, 20 patients (29%) developed re-stenosis. A total of 35 (50%) re-PTAs were performed. Primary patency was 56%, primary assisted patency was 86%, and secondary patency was 93% at last follow up (12 months). Median post-operative DASH score decreased significantly (pre-op: 32.9 (15.8 - 48.3) vs. post-op 8.0 (2.3 - 27.8); p < .001) with a mean follow up of 45.7 ± 27.5 months. Zero patients reported a poor Derkash score.
CONCLUSION: Chronic VTOS can be effectively treated with good long term functional outcomes. Re-PTAs were necessary in half of the cases (anticipated). This treatment algorithm diminished the need of secondary interventions in 50% of the cases, as well as the need for long term anticoagulation usage.

Title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications.
OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes.
METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events.
RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157).
CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.

Title: Stroke Risk-Based Anticoagulation After Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: ALONE-AF Post-Hoc Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Discontinuation of oral anticoagulant (OAC) in patients without recurrent atrial arrhythmia after ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) has been demonstrated to reduce composite outcomes of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding compared with continued OAC.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the optimal OAC strategy according to baseline stroke risk and AF recurrence.
METHODS: In this post-hoc analysis of the Long-Term Anticoagulation Discontinuation after Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation (ALONE-AF) trial, patients were stratified according to CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 and ≥3. Within each stratum, outcomes were compared between the OAC discontinuation and continuation subgroups. The cumulative incidence of stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding at 2 years was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with competing risk analysis accounting for AF recurrence.
RESULTS: Among 840 patients, 584 and 256 had a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≤2 (mean age 62.0±7.5 years, 15.9% female) and ≥3 (mean age 68.9±7.3 years, 45.3% female), respectively. In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≤2 stratum, the primary outcome occurred in one patient (0.4%) in discontinuation subgroup vs. six (2.4%) in continuation subgroup (absolute difference -1.9 percentage points, P=0.066). In the CHA2DS2-VASc ≥3 stratum, two events (1.8%) occurred in the continuation subgroup only (absolute difference -1.8 percentage points, P=0.172). All major bleeding events (n=5) occurred in the continuation subgroups. Competing risk analysis yielded consistent results.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post-hoc analysis, no statistically significant differences in outcomes were observed between OAC strategies when stratified by CHA2DS2-VASc score, though event numbers were limited. Larger prospective trials are needed to confirm these observations.
TRIAL REGISTRATIONS: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04432220.

Title: Steatotic liver disease phenotypes and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The updated nomenclature of steatotic liver disease (SLD) recognizes distinct phenotypes, including Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). Although cardiovascular risk may differ across SLD phenotypes, their association with stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between SLD phenotypes and ischemic stroke risk in AF patients.
METHODS: AF patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Korean health insurance database. According to SLD phenotype, patients were categorized into No-SLD, MASLD, MetALD, and ALD. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke. Subgroup analyses were conducted by CHA2DS2-VA score.
RESULTS: Among 196,242 patients (No-SLD: 101,308; MASLD: 77,715; MetALD: 8,678; ALD: 8,541), median follow-up was 5.9 years. Compared with No-SLD, MASLD was not associated with stroke risk (adjusted hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval; 1.00, 0.97-1.04), whereas MetALD and ALD were associated with higher risk (1.09, 1.00-1.18 and 1.16, 1.08-1.26, respectively). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the higher risk associated with alcohol-related phenotypes appeared more apparent at lower CHA2DS2-VA scores; however, the 6-year absolute risk differences were approximately 1% or less, and these findings are regarded as hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSION: In patients with AF, stroke risk was significantly higher in the alcohol-related SLD phenotypes, MetALD and ALD, whereas MASLD was not associated with stroke risk. These findings are consistent with the current recommendations for comprehensive risk-factor management in AF, with particular attention to alcohol intake in patients with alcohol-related SLD phenotypes.

Title: Association of Air Pollution Exposure and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Consistent evidence indicates that air pollution negatively impacts cardiovascular health. However, the relationship between air pollution and atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear, and exposure measurement error has been a significant concern for prior studies.
OBJECTIVE: This prospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the association of chronic air pollution exposure and risk of AF.
METHODS: We used data from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, a community-based cohort study conducted in 6 U.S. metropolitan areas. Concentrations of 4 pollutants (PM2.5, NO2, NOx, and O3) were assessed from 2000-2018 using hierarchical spatiotemporal models that incorporated cohort-specific monitoring to estimate ambient exposure at participants' residences. In Cox regression models, pollution estimates were represented as time-varying exposures, with 2-year rolling averages updated every 30 days. In our primary model, we adjusted for demographics and health behaviors.
RESULTS: Our study included 6618 participants (mean age 62; 53% female). Over 16.5 years median follow-up, we identified 1055 AF events. In our primary model, an interquartile range increment of NO2 (13.5 ppb) was associated with 29% higher risk of AF (hazard ratio 95% CI: 1.00, 1.67). Associations with PM2.5, NOx, and O3 were weaker but also directionally consistent with higher risk.
CONCLUSION: We found evidence linking air pollution exposure to risk of incident AF. These results can be used to inform policy and other public health efforts aimed at alleviating the burden of AF, especially given that NO2 exposure estimates (median 17.3 ppb) fell well below the current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency annual standard of 53 ppb.

Title: Genetic predisposition to cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicates 5-10% of acute myocardial infarctions (AMI) and remains associated with in-hospital mortality of approximately 40-50%. The clinical predictors established do not fully explain why patients with comparable infarct severity have divergent outcomes, raising the hypothesis that host genetic factors modulate susceptibility to CS. Therefore, we conducted this systematic review to synthesize published evidence describing genetic variants associated with the development of CS complicating AMI.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through Jun 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidance. Eligible studies included any study type enrolling adults with AMI and reporting association of any specific genetic variants with CS.
RESULTS: Of 480 records identified, 9 studies met inclusion criteria. Reported variants clustered into five biological pathways: inflammatory/cytokine signaling (TNF-α -308G>A, IFN-γ +874T>A, RANTES/CCL5 -403G>A), lipid metabolism (APOE ε2/ε3/ε4), thrombosis and fibrinolysis (PAI-1/SERPINE1 4G/4 G, MTHFR C677T/A1298C), clonal myeloproliferative disease (JAK2 V617F), and hypercoagulable/antioxidant pathways (protein C/S-related thrombophilia, PON1 Q192R). The APOE ε3/4 genotype and the TNF-2 allele showed the most direct associations with CS incidence and survival, respectively; JAK2 V617F and combined PAI-1/MTHFR variants were reported in severe, thrombus-driven case presentations of CS. RANTES and PON1 genotypes were not associated with CS occurrence, although circulating RANTES levels correlated with CS severity.
CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence is limited, but the variants reported to date span inflammatory, lipid, thrombotic, and myeloproliferative pathways, suggesting that genetic susceptibility to CS complicating AMI is polygenic and mechanistically heterogeneous, requiring prospective genetic association studies.

Title: Cardiovascular toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: Clinical phenotypes, mechanisms, diagnosis, and management-A narrative review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved cancer outcomes, yet cardiovascular toxicities remain difficult to recognize and manage. We review their clinical spectrum, mechanistic evidence, diagnostic work-up, surveillance, and treatment, with particular attention to where evidence is established and where it remains preliminary.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of PubMed through September 2026 and hand-searched reference lists of relevant guidelines, reviews, and primary studies. We prioritized international guidance, systematic reviews, multicenter registries, prospective cohorts, and clinically informative mechanistic studies. Case reports and experimental studies were retained when they addressed questions not covered by higher-level evidence. The review was not protocol driven and did not include duplicate screening, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or a PRISMA flow diagram.
RESULTS: ICI-related cardiovascular toxicity extends beyond myocarditis to temporally associated atherosclerotic events, pericardial disease, and heart failure without demonstrable myocardial inflammation, although causal attribution is less secure for these non-myocarditis phenotypes. Current guidance supports baseline cardiovascular assessment and risk-adapted surveillance, but neither a universal troponin threshold nor an outcome-proven monitoring schedule has been established. Corticosteroids remain first-line treatment for clinically significant ICI myocarditis. Abatacept, ruxolitinib, alemtuzumab, and other intensified regimens are off-label and rest largely on nonrandomized or case-level evidence.
CONCLUSION: Management should combine early recognition, careful exclusion of competing diagnoses, and coordinated oncology-cardiology decision-making. Current evidence does not justify uniform screening thresholds or a standard rescue regimen, and investigational biomarkers, imaging probes, and targeted immunomodulators require prospective validation.

Title: ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device as a Cost-Dominant Limb-Salvage Strategy for No-Option Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia: A Decade and Half, Single-Centre Cohort Study with Health Economic and Q-TWiST Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) a median €88,820 per patient; long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist SCBD is lacking.
METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with non-reconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary centre (January 2008-June 2025). Primary endpoints were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness versus primary amputation, and Q-TWiST. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.
FINDINGS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischaemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (HRs 1·70, 1·80, 1·71; all P ≤ ·012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = ·008). 90-day rental (€1,373/patient) reduced total expenditure six-fold versus primary amputation (€5·3M vs €30·8M), saving €76,500/patient. Q-TWiST yielded a gain of 3·37 QALYs per patient; ICER €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.
INTERPRETATION: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a six-fold reduction in costs versus primary amputation, +3·37 QALYs/patient, and an ICER of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-centre cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for non-reconstructible CLTI.

Title: Differential sensitivity of MRI-based brain-age models to chronic noise exposure: an exploratory comparative study.
Abstract: Chronic noise exposure is associated with cardiovascular and mental health outcomes, yet its neurobiological effects remain poorly characterized. MRI-based brain-age models estimate structural brain aging, but their sensitivity to environmental and occupational noise exposure has not been systematically evaluated. We examined associations of environmental and occupational noise exposure, separately and in combination, with brain age gap (BAG) across six MRI-based brain-age prediction models. We analyzed 108 Korean hospital workers who underwent high-resolution three-dimensional T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging. Residential environmental noise exposure was classified as high when daytime noise was ≥60 dB or nighttime noise was ≥55 dB. Because no participant had occupational noise exposure ≥85 dBA as an 8-h time-weighted average, occupational exposure was categorized as relatively lower or higher using the cohort-specific median. BAG was calculated as predicted brain age minus chronological age using brainageR, XGBoost, ENIGMA, pyment, DenseNet, and TSAN models. Primary analyses used covariate-adjusted linear models for BAG, controlling for age, sex, and intracranial volume. Age-bias-corrected and Z-standardized brain-age advancement (BAA) was used for descriptive joint-exposure visualization and exploratory trend analysis. High environmental noise exposure was associated with a less negative BAG in the TSAN model than low environmental noise exposure (-8.1 vs. -12.1 years; p = 0.0036), indicating a relatively older-appearing brain. Daytime and nighttime environmental noise levels were positively correlated with TSAN-derived BAG (Spearman's rho = 0.253, false discovery rate-adjusted p = 0.008; rho = 0.215, false discovery rate-adjusted p = 0.025, respectively). Occupational noise exposure alone was not significantly associated with BAG in any model. No environmental-noise-by-occupational-noise interaction remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. In an exploratory TSAN analysis, each additional high-exposure domain was associated with a 0.27-standard-deviation increase in BAA (95% confidence interval, 0.01 to 0.59; p for trend = 0.048). Environmental noise exposure was associated with relatively older-appearing brain structure in the TSAN model, whereas occupational noise exposure alone was not consistently associated with BAG. Concurrent environmental and relatively higher occupational noise exposure showed a model-specific joint-exposure burden gradient but did not provide formal evidence of synergistic or non-additive effects. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to replicate these findings and clarify the utility of brain-age measures in environmental and occupational health research.

Title: Pregnancy after renal transplant: Truth or dare? A retrospective analysis from a tertiary care centre in India.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) often face fertility challenges due to hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis disruption. While pregnancy is rare during dialysis, kidney transplantation restores fertility potential, albeit with increased maternal and foetal risks. This study evaluates maternal and foetal outcomes in post-renal transplant pregnancies at a tertiary care centre.
METHODOLOGY: A retrospective study was conducted at our hospital on female renal transplant recipients between January 2010 and January 2024. All patients who conceived post-transplant were included. Clinical data were extracted from hospital electronic medical records, including transplant details, immunosuppression, antenatal course, and pregnancy outcomes.
RESULTS: Out of 215 female transplant recipients, 11 conceived post-transplant (5.1%). Among them, 9 pregnancies resulted in live births, 1 in stillbirth, and 1 ended in abortion. Mean age at pregnancy was 28.6 ± 1.74 years. All patients underwent ABO-compatible transplantation. Induction therapy included ATG (54.5%), basiliximab (27.3%), or none (18.2%). All patients were maintained on triple immunosuppression with tacrolimus, prednisone (≤10 mg/day), and azathioprine. Complications included maternal viz. gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, preterm delivery, and fetal viz. stillbirth and fetal growth restriction (FGR). Fetal outcomes included 81.8% live births, 9.1% intrauterine death, and 9.1% abortion. Graft outcomes showed stable function in 45.5%, dysfunction in 54.5%, and graft loss in 36.3%.
CONCLUSION: Pregnancy after kidney transplantation is feasible and frequently successful, though associated with maternal and foetal complications. Meticulous multidisciplinary care and regular monitoring are essential to optimize outcomes and preserve graft function.

Title: Athyreosis and Thyroid Hormone Signaling: A System-Based Framework for Long-Term Endocrine Health.
Journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
Abstract: Thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine therapy are definitive treatments for Graves' disease, toxic nodular disease, and differentiated thyroid cancer. With improving survival rates and expanding indications for definitive therapy, a growing population is living for decades in a state of athyreosis requiring lifelong thyroid hormone replacement. Current management strategies largely emphasize serum thyroid-stimulating hormone targets and oncological surveillance, yet the long-term metabolic and physiological implications of chronic athyreosis remain incompletely explored. The potential longevity implications of long-term athyreosis are examined through a system-based framework integrating hormonal balance, mitochondrial regulation, metabolic adaptation, skeletal and cardiovascular health, and inflammatory signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from endocrinology, metabolism, oncology, and aging research to evaluate physiological differences between endogenous thyroid hormone secretion and pharmacological replacement in athyreotic patients. Particular attention is given to tissue-level triiodothyronine availability, deiodinase activity, and downstream bioenergetic effects. Athyreotic patients lack intrinsic thyroidal triiodothyronine secretion and depend entirely on the peripheral conversion of levothyroxine to generate circulating and intracellular triiodothyronine. Emerging evidence suggests that levothyroxine monotherapy may not fully replicate physiological thyroid hormone dynamics in all individuals, potentially influencing mitochondrial biogenesis, resting energy expenditure, body composition, bone turnover, and cardiovascular remodeling. In thyroid cancer survivors, chronic thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression introduces additional considerations for skeletal and cardiac outcomes. Patients treated for autoimmune thyroid disease may also exhibit persistent immune dysregulation despite gland ablation. Athyreosis represents a distinct and permanent endocrine state with implications extending beyond biochemical euthyroidism. A system-based perspective that considers mitochondrial resilience, cardiometabolic integrity, skeletal preservation, and inflammatory tone may enhance long-term management strategies for this expanding survivorship population. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the impact of various thyroid hormone replacement paradigms on functional aging and longevity outcomes.

Title: Disease progression in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis treated with disease-modifying therapies: a multicenter real-world experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is a progressive disease associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. The multimodal progression criteria proposed in 2025 integrate clinical, biomarker, and functional parameters to improve disease monitoring. However, evidence regarding their applicability in real-world practice remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter ambispective observational cohort study including 68 consecutive patients with ATTR-CM receiving disease-modifying therapies across hospitals in Castilla-La Mancha, Spain. Disease progression was assessed by comparing baseline status with the follow-up assessment available within the first 12 months after treatment initiation; no data obtained after month 12 were used to establish progression status. Progression was defined as abnormalities in at least two domains (clinical, biomarker, and functional). To assess the temporal association with subsequent cardiovascular events, a 12-month landmark analysis was performed among patients who were alive and free from the composite cardiovascular event at month 12 and had subsequent follow-up.
RESULTS: Disease progression according to the 2025 criteria was observed in 42.4% of evaluable patients. The biomarker domain was the most frequently affected (62.1%), followed by the clinical (42.4%) and functional (37.9%) domains. Patients with progression had significantly higher baseline NT-proBNP levels and worse renal function. In multivariable analysis, baseline NT-proBNP was independently associated with progression (OR 2.49, 95% CI 1.15-5.43; p=0.021). Among the 66 patients evaluable for progression, the composite cardiovascular event was more frequent in progressors than in non-progressors during overall follow-up (60.7% vs. 15.8%; p<0.001). In the 12-month landmark analysis (n=40), first-year progression was associated with a higher incidence of subsequent cardiovascular events (42.9% vs. 7.7%; HR 5.88, 95% CI 1.19-29.19; p=0.030).
CONCLUSIONS: Progression according to the 2025 multimodal criteria was common among ATTR-CM patients despite disease-modifying therapy. Progression identified during the first year was associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular events occurring after month 12 in an exploratory landmark analysis. The biomarker domain, particularly NT-proBNP and renal function, was relevant for identifying progression. These criteria may be useful for longitudinal monitoring and risk stratification in routine clinical practice.

Title: ANOCA Patients With Prior Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease and PCI Have Higher Odds of Epicardial Spasm.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of patients undergoing coronary angiography have angina with no obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Among ANOCA patients, 2 distinct groups exist: patients with and without a history of prior obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate associations between history of prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI and coronary microvascular and vasomotor dysfunction endotypes in ANOCA patients.
METHODS: A prospective Coronary Microvascular and Vasomotor Dysfunction Registry of consecutive ANOCA patients undergoing invasive coronary functional testing (ICFT).
RESULTS: Among 624 ANOCA patients undergoing ICFT, 11% had prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI. ANOCA patients with prior obstructive CAD had a higher prevalence of males, were older, and had higher rates of cardiovascular risk factors. Prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI was associated with an 11-point lower Seattle Angina Questionnaire 7 summary score in unadjusted (β -11.0; 95% CI: -17.0 to -4.4; P = 0.001) and adjusted models. Patients with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had a higher prevalence of epicardial spasm by angiographic criteria (70% vs 34%; P < 0.001) and 4.55-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm in unadjusted (OR: 4.55; 95% CI: 2.65-8.07; P < 0.001) and adjusted models, with similar odds of coronary microvascular dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: Among ANOCA patients, those with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had over a 4-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive ICFT in ANOCA patients with prior PCI.

Title: Atrial Septostomy and Left Ventricular Venting During Peripheral VA-ECMO.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral venoarterial (VA)-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, and therefore the risk of LV distension, pulmonary edema, and cardiac stasis. Balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) provides atrial-level unloading, but the durability of LV venting remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of BAS for LV venting in patients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock (CS).
METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective study of consecutive adults with CS supported with peripheral VA-ECMO who underwent BAS for LV unloading at an academic center (2019-2024). The primary endpoint was LV venting failure, a composite of pulmonary edema, LV distension, spontaneous echocardiographic contrast, LV or aortic root thrombus, stroke due to ECMO, or escalation to additional mechanical support.
RESULTS: A total of 28 patients were included in the study. BAS resulted in a significant reduction in mean left atrial pressure (20.5-13.5 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Durable LV venting was achieved in a subset of patients; however, LV venting failure occurred in 53.6%, driven primarily by pulmonary edema. Pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting-failure status (interaction P = 0.018). Model-estimated pulse pressure was higher at 48 hours (P = 0.010) and 72 hours (P = 0.031) among patients who ultimately did not experience venting failure.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for CS, BAS achieves atrial-level decompression and may provide durable LV venting in select patients, although venting failure remains common. Observed arterial pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting failure status.

Title: Effect of mitral valve repair on outcomes in dogs with preclinical myxomatous mitral valve disease: a retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Mitral valve repair (MVR) for myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) in dogs has favorable results, but its effectiveness compared with medical treatment in preclinical (stage B2) dogs remains unclear. This study investigated whether MVR improves survival in preclinical dogs with MMVD.
ANIMALS, MATERIALS, AND METHODS: Dogs diagnosed with stage B2 MMVD between October 2016 and September 2020 were divided into an MVR group and a control group receiving medical treatment. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and the first onset of pulmonary edema. The waiting period between diagnosis and surgery in the MVR group was adjusted as a time-dependent exposure, and survival analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Overall, 91 and 171 dogs were enrolled in the MVR and control groups, respectively. The median observation period was 599.5 days (lower and upper quartiles: 374.0-1001.5). The primary outcome occurred in 10 dogs (11.0%) in the MVR group and 69 dogs (40.4%) in the control group. Cox proportional hazards analysis adjusted for time-dependent exposure yielded hazard ratios of 0.12 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.05-0.25, P < 0.001) for MVR and 2.85 (95% CI: 1.69-4.80, P < 0.001) for diuretic use.
STUDY LIMITATIONS: Limitations include potential selection bias, limited survey response rate, inter-observer variability in diagnostic assessment, and a short follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS: Dogs undergoing MVR had a lower risk of reaching the composite endpoint than medically managed dogs. These findings may assist veterinarians and owners in decision-making regarding MVR for stage B2 dogs.

Title: Glatiramer acetate attenuates the cytokine surge associated with acute decompensated heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is characterized by a systemic inflammatory response with elevated circulating cytokines that correlate with adverse outcomes. Glatiramer acetate (GA), an established immunomodulatory agent, exerts broad effects on innate and adaptive immunity and has demonstrated cardioprotective properties in preclinical models. We hypothesized that GA could reduce the cytokine surge associated with ADHF.
METHODS: We conducted a small, investigator-initiated, hypothesis-generating randomized clinical trial to evaluate the effects of GA on inflammatory cytokines in patients with ADHF and reduced ejection fraction. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard care or an add-on treatment with GA. Circulating cytokines were measured using multiplex ELISA assays at baseline, day 2, and day 14. Secondary outcomes included changes in NT-proBNP and troponin.
RESULTS: Fourteen patients were enrolled. GA therapy was associated with a broad attenuation of the cytokine response, with a significant reduction in IL-6 levels compared with standard care (adjusted p = 0.01). Analysis of normalized data demonstrated a marked blunting of the cytokine surge in the GA group at days 2 and 14 (pooled log2 fold-change -5.2 vs. +7.3, p < 0.0001). GA treatment was also associated with a reduction in NT-proBNP levels at both time points, whereas troponin levels were unchanged. No treatment-related adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: In this proof-of-concept study, GA was associated with attenuation of the inflammatory cytokine surge and reduction in NT-proBNP levels in ADHF. These findings support further evaluation of GA in larger trials.

Title: The implications of molecular alterations in cytologically benign thyroid nodules.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ablation of benign thyroid nodules has gained clinical favor. However, reliably excluding malignancy remains a diagnostic challenge. We assessed the frequency and spectrum of molecular abnormalities in cytologically benign nodules.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study of national and institutional cohorts reviewed nodules with cytologically benign fine-needle aspiration results referred for next-generation sequencing-based molecular testing (2017-2024). Frequency/type of molecular abnormalities, histopathology, and clinical variables predictive of positive molecular testing were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 825 cases in the national cohort, 121 (15%) tested positive, including 97 (80%) for low-risk RAS/RAS-like alterations, 19 (16%) for intermediate-risk BRAF V600E and BRAF V600E-like alterations, and 5 (4%) for high-risk molecular profiles including TERT and TP53. Twenty-four nodules with intermediate- or high-risk molecular alterations represented 20% of cytologically benign molecular testing-positive nodules and 3% of all nodules. Among 36 patients with surgical outcomes, 16 (44%) nodules were malignant, and 3 (8%) were noninvasive follicular thyroid neoplasm with papillary-like nuclear features. Among 38 cases in the institutional cohort, 11 (29%) tested positive, 7 (64%) carried low-risk, 2 (18%) carried intermediate-risk, and 2 (18%) carried high-risk alterations. Intermediate- or high-risk alterations were present in 36% of nodules with positive molecular testing and 11% of all nodules. Age <55 years (odds ratio, 13.4) and history of nodule growth (odds ratio, 13.6) were independent predictors of positive molecular testing. Of 9 molecular testing-positive nodules managed with surgery, 4 (44%) were malignant.
CONCLUSION: Among thyroid nodules with benign cytology referred for molecular testing, 3%-11% demonstrated intermediate- or high-risk alterations. Considering this molecular heterogeneity, further investigation of clinicopathologic factors is warranted to inform nonoperative or preablation molecular risk stratification and ensure accurate exclusion of malignancy.

Title: Geriatric nutritional risk index and outcomes following a major surgical procedure: A national cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite a rising incidence among older adults, the effect of malnutrition on perioperative morbidity remains unclear. We assessed the prognostic value of the geriatric nutritional risk index for outcomes after major surgery.
METHODS: The nationwide Epic COSMOS electronic health record database identified adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting, lung resection, abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, or major gastrointestinal resection. The geriatric nutritional risk index was calculated from serum albumin and anthropometric measurements and categorized using established cutoffs as major risk (<82), moderate risk (82-91), low risk (92-98), and no risk (>98). Associations with 30-day mortality, complications, readmission, and nonhome discharge were evaluated using entropy-balanced weighted logistic regression adjusted for patient and operative factors.
RESULTS: Among 506,040 patients undergoing major surgery, mean age was 66.9 years and 46.2% were female. Patients with a major geriatric nutritional risk index were older than patients with no geriatric nutritional risk index (median, 71 vs 68 years), more often had a Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥1 (81.1% vs 75.2%), and were Black (16.4% vs 11.5%) (all P < .001). Outcomes worsened with increasing geriatric nutritional risk index: mortality (no risk, 1.7%; low risk, 4.1%; moderate risk, 6.6%; and major risk, 13.3%), readmission (no risk, 12.3%; low risk, 17.0%; moderate risk, 19.0%; and major risk, 23.5%), and nonhome discharge (no risk, 33.1%; low risk, 46.1%; moderate risk, 53.3%; and major risk, 64.3%) (all P < .001). Compared with no geriatric nutritional risk index, low and major geriatric nutritional risk index were independently associated with higher odds of any 30-day complication (low risk: adjusted odds ratio, 1.79; 95% confidence interval, 1.75-1.82; major risk: adjusted odds ratio, 2.47; 95% confidence interval, 2.40-2.54) and mortality (low risk: adjusted odds ratio, 3.35; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-3.50; major risk: adjusted odds ratio, 8.03; 95% confidence interval, 7.70-8.38) (all P < .001). The geriatric nutritional risk index demonstrated a strong inverse association with 30-day mortality, with the highest risk observed among patients with a major geriatric nutritional risk index.
CONCLUSION: Greater geriatric nutritional risk index-defined nutrition-related risk was independently associated with higher mortality, major complications, and readmission compared with no geriatric nutritional risk index. Geriatric nutritional risk index-based assessment may identify nutritionally vulnerable patients for preoperative optimization, early intervention, and tailored postoperative discharge planning.

Title: Self-reported difficulty reading small print and in-hospital behavioral change in older adults with cardiovascular disease: Implications for post-discharge cardiovascular outcomes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Visual dysfunction may hinder patient education and self-care in older patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD); however, its association with behavioral change during hospitalization and subsequent cardiovascular prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated whether self-reported difficulty reading small print is associated with transtheoretical model (TTM) stage progression during hospitalization and whether such change predicts post-discharge outcomes.
METHODS: This prospective multicenter cohort study enrolled older patients who underwent cardiac rehabilitation during hospitalization. Visual dysfunction was assessed by self-reporting of difficulty reading small print. Behavioral change was evaluated using the TTM. The primary outcome was unplanned rehospitalization due to major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within one year. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with TTM improvement, and Cox proportional hazards models were applied to examine the association between TTM improvement and MACCE rehospitalization.
RESULTS: Among 351 included patients, 31.9% had difficulty reading small print. After multivariable adjustment, difficulty reading small print was independently associated with lower odds of TTM improvement (odds ratio, 0.31; p=0.006). Patients achieving TTM improvement had a significantly lower risk of MACCE rehospitalization after adjustment for age, sex, institution, heart failure, renal disease, and TTM stage at discharge (hazard ratio, 0.37; p = 0.042).
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported difficulty reading small print was independently associated with reduced TTM stage improvement during hospitalization, and TTM stage improvement predicted a lower risk of MACCE rehospitalization. These findings highlight the importance of focusing on the behavioral change process during hospitalization and incorporating visual considerations into behavioral support strategies for secondary prevention in older CVD patients.

Title: Amyloidosis and risk of psychiatric disorders-insights from a real-world nationwide registry.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This is a National Health Insurance (NHI) database research investigating the association between amyloidosis and psychiatric disorders risk.
METHODS: The amyloidosis cohort was identified from insured individuals with amyloidosis, who were newly diagnosed from 2009 to 2019. Both cohorts were followed up and the subsequent psychiatric disorder was the major outcome event for the research. The multivariable model were used to examine the effect of amyloidosis and risk factor on the risk of developing psychiatric disorder.
RESULTS: The psychiatric disorder incidence was higher in the amyloidosis than in the comparison cohort (11.3 vs. 10.3 per 1000 person-years, crude HR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.19), with adjusted HR (aHR) of 1.26 (95% CI 1.16-1.36). After controlling for the confounders, amyloidosis cohort had a 1.38- fold higher risk of senile and pre-senile organic psychotic conditions (95% CI 1.22‒1.57), 1.26-fold higher risk of bipolar affective disorder (95% CI 1.10‒1.45), and 1.16-fold higher risk of other organic psychotic conditions than comparison cohort (95% CI 1.01-1.32).
CONCLUSIONS: The authors found that compared to a matched amyloidosis naïve cohort, psychiatric disorders risk was significantly higher in patients with amyloidosis. Among different psychiatric disorders, risks of senile and pre-senile organic psychotic conditions, bipolar affective disorder and other organic psychotic conditions were higher among people with amyloidosis.

Title: Forensic cause-of-death determination of myocardial infarction-related sudden cardiac death in histopathologically similar cases using computational pathology.
Abstract: Determining whether myocardial infarction-related sudden cardiac death (MI-SCD) is the cause of death remains particularly challenging in forensic practice because different causes of death can produce highly similar myocardial histopathological changes. This study developed a computational pathology framework to support forensic cause-of-death determination by distinguishing MI-SCD from other causes associated with similar myocardial alterations and identifying characteristic myocardial injury patterns associated with MI-SCD. The study included 412H&E-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) of left ventricular myocardium from the GTEx database (221 MI-SCD and 191 control cases) and an independent external validation cohort of 43 slides (18 MI-SCD and 25 control cases). Image features were extracted using the UNI encoder, and slide-level classification was performed using a clustering-constrained attention multiple-instance learning model (CLAM). The UNI-CLAM model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.895, 0.908, and 0.829 and accuracies of 0.815, 0.824, and 0.790 in the test, validation, and external cohorts, respectively. Beyond classification, attention-guided analysis indicated that the model integrated histopathological information from multiple tissue patterns rather than relying on any single lesion. Subsequent spatial co-localization analysis identified characteristic myocardial injury patterns in MI-SCD, including the frequent co-occurrence of myocardial rupture and degeneration and the close spatial association of myocardial fibrosis with both degeneration and inflammatory cell infiltration. These findings suggest that MI-SCD is characterized by distinctive myocardial injury patterns despite substantial histopathological overlap with other causes of death and may provide a more objective basis for forensic cause-of-death determination.

Title: Optimal exercise modalities and doses for blood pressure management in adults with prehypertension and hypertension: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to identify the most effective exercise modalities and optimal estimated dose range for reducing blood pressure in adults with prehypertension and hypertension, to support more precise exercise prescription.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to December 28, 2025. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if they included adults with prehypertension or stage 1 or stage 2 hypertension, evaluated structured exercise interventions, and reported resting systolic blood pressure and/or diastolic blood pressure.
RESULTS: A total of 284 randomized controlled trials, including 18,750 participants with a mean age of 56.8 years, covering ten exercise modalities were included. Aquatic exercise achieved the greatest reduction in systolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -10.28 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -13.05 to -7.49; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 93.26%. Whole-body vibration and cycling also showed favorable estimates for systolic blood pressure. Mind-body exercise showed the largest estimated reduction in diastolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -4.69 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -6.45 to -2.92; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 85.90%. Aquatic exercise and isometric exercise training also showed favorable effect estimates. Dose-response modelling indicated that 750 metabolic equivalent task minutes per week was the estimated dose associated with maximal modeled systolic blood pressure benefit for isometric exercise training, with a mean difference of -13.52 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -23.22 to -3.86. In contrast, 3600 metabolic equivalent task minutes per week was the estimated dose associated with maximal modeled diastolic blood pressure benefit for aerobic exercise, with a mean difference of -7.11 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -11.89 to -2.18.
CONCLUSION: Ten exercise modalities were associated with reductions in blood pressure, with particularly strong effects for aquatic, mind-body, and isometric exercise at specific doses. These findings may inform more tailored exercise prescription strategies for adults across hypertension phenotypes.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Endovascular treatment of tandem lesions: prognostic factors of functional outcome and the efficacy of emergent carotid stenting.
Journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the prognostic risk factors for endovascular therapy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke with tandem lesions, and to evaluate the efficacy and safety of emergent carotid artery stenting.
METHODS: Patients with acute internal carotid artery tandem occlusion who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) were enrolled. Baseline clinical and procedural data were collected. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, and the safety endpoint was symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH). Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to balance covariates between patients receiving emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) and non-stenting controls. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors. Subgroup analyses were conducted on relevant risk factors.
RESULTS: A total of 112 eligible patients were included, with a mean age of 66.19 ± 9.23 years; 76 (67.86%) were male. Fifty-eight patients (51.79%) achieved a favorable functional outcome (good prognosis group). Univariate analysis revealed significant differences (P < 0.05) between the two groups in baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, puncture-to-reperfusion time, history of hypertension, and history of atrial fibrillation. After multivariable adjustment, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time were identified as independent risk factors for unfavorable 90-day functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients undergoing EVT. Emergent carotid artery stenting (eCAS) was not an independent predictor of 90-day favorable functional outcome (adjusted OR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.17-1.58, P = 0.246). Significant differences in stroke history and smoking history were found between the emergent stenting and non-stenting groups at baseline. Female sex and puncture-to-reperfusion time were independent risk factors for sICH in tandem lesion patients. Subgroup analysis indicated that in those aged ≥ 65 years, emergent stenting was associated with unfavorable 90-day functional prognosis (OR = 0.042, 95% CI 0.004-0.469, P = 0.01).
CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, hypertension, baseline NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, and puncture-to-reperfusion time may serve as independent predictors of 90-day favorable functional outcomes in tandem lesion patients treated with EVT. Female sex and longer puncture-to-reperfusion time appear to be potential risk factors for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. Emergent carotid artery stenting was not found to be an independent predictor of 90-day functional prognosis in our cohort, and no significant increase in sICH risk was observed in association with eCAS. These preliminary findings require further validation in large-scale multicenter prospective studies.

Title: Combining responsive neurostimulation with resection or ablation for treatment of epilepsy: a multicenter experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite advances in surgical and neuromodulatory treatments, a substantial proportion of patients with drug-resistant epilepsy remain ineligible for standalone resection or ablation. Combining resection or laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) with responsive neurostimulation (RNS) has emerged as a promising approach for patients with multifocal seizure onset or eloquent cortex involvement. However, the clinical impact of combination surgery remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to characterize the clinical rationale and surgical decision-making used across multiple high-volume epilepsy centers performing combination surgeries, and to evaluate the seizure outcomes and safety profile associated with this approach.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who underwent RNS implantation in combination with resection or LITT at 9 epilepsy centers and had ≥ 1 year of follow-up. Demographic, clinical, surgical, and seizure outcome data were collected. The primary outcome was seizure reduction at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the Clinical Global Impression and adverse events.
RESULTS: Overall, 73 patients (40 male, mean age 34 years) with a mean epilepsy duration of 21 years were included in this analysis. The most common etiology was unknown (37%), followed by cortical malformation (16%). Most patients experienced focal impaired consciousness (FIC, 78%) and focal to bilateral tonic-clonic (FBTC, 70%) seizures. Prior resection was performed in 23%. Combination procedures were performed on the same day in 89% of patients. RNS implantation was concurrent with resection in 92% and with LITT in 8.2% of patients. Neocortical and mesial temporal regions accounted for 61% of resection/ablation targets. More than two-thirds of RNS leads were subdural strips, most commonly in the left hemisphere (73%). Indications for the combined approach included eloquent cortex involvement (67%) and multifocal seizure onset (33%) or both (9.6%). At 1 year, mean seizure reductions were 53% for focal impaired, 69% for FIC, and 67% for FBTC seizures. Overall, 48% of patients had at least a 6-month period of seizure freedom, and 4 patients had no seizures after surgery. Significant global clinical improvement (much or very much improved) was observed in 79% of patients. Three patients experienced infection, and 1 patient died due to causes unrelated to surgical treatment (sudden unexpected death in epilepsy).
CONCLUSIONS: Combined RNS with resection or ablation might provide meaningful seizure control in complex drug-resistant epilepsy with acceptable safety profiles. These findings describe current practice and support further investigation of hybrid surgical strategies in patients with challenging seizure networks as a potential treatment strategy.

Title: Quantitative MRI to assess baseline shunt flow in patients with hydrocephalus: a noninvasive tool to aid clinical decision-making.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hydrocephalus is a common yet serious condition, and ventricular shunts are used for lifesaving CSF diversion. Existing methods for shunt evaluation provide correlative/qualitative information, leading to commonplace clinical diagnostic challenges. The aim of this study was to determine accurate and noninvasive measures of volumetric CSF flow rates through ventricular shunts using the phase-contrast (PC) sequence in routine MRI for pediatric patients with hydrocephalus.
METHODS: The authors conducted a prospective observational cohort study of patients with ventricular shunts who underwent a clinically indicated brain MRI and the adjunct PC-MRI shunt flow sequence at a single center between January 2023 and January 2024. At the study institution, PC-MRI has been integrated as a supplementary imaging technique to quantify shunt flow alongside fast protocol MRI for shunted patients. Clinical and imaging data were collected. Data distributions and paired changes in flow measurements over time were assessed using appropriate statistical tests.
RESULTS: Overall, 207 patients (107 male, mean age 11.3 years [range 8 days-27 years]) who underwent PC-MRI were included; 98% had a VP shunt. The mean CSF flow rate was 9.9 ± 8 mL/hour (range 0.5-54 mL/hour). No significant differences were noted by age, sex, etiology of hydrocephalus, valve type, time interval since shunt placement, BMI, fronto-occipital horn ratio, and frontal horn or atrial width. Repeat PC-MRI was performed in 11 patients, and there was no significant difference in flow measurements between initial and follow-up images (p = 0.83) among these patients. PC-MRI identified alterations that accurately demonstrated failure in 3 patients and avoided unnecessary surgery in a fourth patient.
CONCLUSIONS: Addition of PC-MRI to routine imaging examinations in patients with ventricular shunts accurately and noninvasively measured CSF shunt flow. Flow rate data can provide supplementary information regarding shunt function and serve as a baseline for future comparison assessments. These findings suggest a role for routine acquisition of patient-specific baseline shunt flow measurement in shunted pediatric patients with hydrocephalus.

Title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing utilization and clinical outcomes among patients with heart failure across racial and ethnic groups.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) carries a Class I recommendation for advanced heart failure (HF) therapy candidacy. Whether CPET utilization and outcomes differ by race is unknown.
METHODS: Using TriNetX, adults with HF (ICD-10 I50.x, 2010-23) were stratified by race/ethnicity and CPET receipt (CPT 94621) within 1 year of diagnosis. All-cause mortality and HF hospitalization were assessed at 1, 3, and 5 years after 1:1 propensity score matching for demographics, HF subtype, comorbidities, and guideline-directed medical therapy.
RESULTS: Among 807 379 patients with HF (mean age 69.2 years, 46.2% female), 10 268 (1.27%) underwent CPET within 1 year. Utilization was 1.39% in White, 1.20% in Black, 0.69% in Hispanic, and 0.79% in Asian patients. After matching, 8355 pairs were analysed. CPET was associated with lower 1-year mortality in White (hazard ratio [HR] 0.58, 95% CI 0.51-0.65, P < .001) and Hispanic (HR 0.50, 0.25-0.98, P = .040) patients. Asian patients reached borderline significance at 5 years (HR 0.54, 0.29-1.00, P = .048). Black patients showed a non-significant trend (1-year HR 0.70, 0.39-1.24, P = .214). HF hospitalization was higher in White (1-year HR 1.18, 1.14-1.23, P < .001) and Asian (HR 1.73, 1.35-2.21, P < .001) CPET recipients, suggesting surveillance bias.
CONCLUSIONS: CPET utilization was associated with lower mortality in White and Hispanic patients, with borderline significance in Asian patients at 5 years and a non-significant trend in Black patients. These associations may reflect engagement with speciality HF care rather than testing itself. Minority patients were under-represented among CPET recipients, highlighting CPET access as a marker of inequity in advanced HF care.

Title: [Multiple myeloma in Argentina: results from a Delphi panel of experts].
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In recent decades there have been significant advances in the diagnosis and treatment of multiple myeloma (MM). However, in fragmented health systems such as Argentina's, structural barriers continue to limit equitable access to diagnostic technologies and innovative therapies.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A modified Delphi process including two asynchronous rounds followed by a structured synchronous discussion was conducted to explore expert perspectives on the main barriers affecting MM management in Argentina. Nine expert hematologists with extensive clinical experience, representing different regions of the country and the major health subsectors, participated in the study. The analysis addressed diagnostic, therapeutic, and organizational dimensions of care.
RESULTS: Experts estimated the median overall survival to be approximately 7.8 years, suggesting sustained improvement compared with previous decades. Nevertheless, important inequities persist in access to key diagnostic tools, particularly fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and positron emission tomographycomputed tomography (PET-CT).
