Marked heterogeneity was also identified in access to innovative therapies, especially anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies, across the public, social security, and private health subsectors. In addition, the panel highlighted the need for more efficient coverage mechanisms, implementation of a national patient registry, and stronger continuing medical education strategies.
CONCLUSION: The inequities identified reflect structural weaknesses in Argentina's health system that extend beyond MM itself. Addressing these challenges requires a comprehensive approach that integrates clinical evidence and health economic evaluation into coverage decisions, strengthens diagnostic and therapeutic capacities across levels of care, and promotes innovative financing mechanisms to improve equitable access while preserving system sustainability. This study contributes locally situated expert knowledge, offering a consensusbased foundation to inform policy and support a more equitable and efficient model of MM care.

Title: Midlife and Late-Life Alzheimer Disease Blood Biomarkers and 11-Year Cognitive Decline.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer disease (AD) neuropathology (amyloid-β42 to amyloid β40 [Aβ42/40] ratio, phosphorylated tau at threonine [p-tau181]), neurodegeneration (neurofilament light [NfL]), and neuroinflammation (glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) in late-life are associated with cognitive decline. Whether these biomarkers in midlife are predictive of subsequent cognitive decline, and whether they are associated with different cognitive domains, is uncertain. In this study, we investigated associations of midlife and late-life plasma Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP with late-life change in domain-specific (memory, language, and executive function) and global cognitive function.
METHODS: We performed a prospective cohort analysis of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study (ARIC-NCS). Outcome follow-up was from ARIC visit 5 (2011-2013) to visit 9 (2021-2022). We included all individuals from ARIC field centers (Jackson, Mississippi; Forsyth County, North Carolina; Washington County, Maryland; and Minneapolis suburbs, Minnesota) with biomarkers measured from stored specimens in midlife (visit 3, 1993-1995, mean age 59.0 years) and late-life (visit 5, 2011-2013, mean age 76.8 years). Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were measured with the Quanterix Simoa platform and standardized to visit 3 to facilitate cross-biomarker comparisons of their rate of change from midlife to late-life. We estimated change in memory, language, executive function, and global cognition factor scores from visit 5 to visit 9 with linear mixed-effect models.
RESULTS: In 1,515 included participants, 60.7% (n = 920) were female and 25.5% (n = 387) were Black. Each SD increase in p-tau181 in midlife was significantly associated with faster late-life memory decline (β = -0.030 [95% CI -0.059 to -0.001] SD. Midlife Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP were not associated with subsequent decline in any cognitive domain. In late-life, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were significantly associated with faster decline in different cognitive domains, with the strongest associations seen with memory (β = -0.091 [95% CI -0.123 to -0.058] SD; β = -0.064 [95% CI -0.106 to -0.023] SD; and β = -0.048 [95% CI -0.082 to -0.013] SD, respectively).
DISCUSSION: Midlife p-tau181 was associated with faster 11-year memory decline beginning 20 years later in the ARIC cohort, which underscores a potentially long prodromal phase of cognitive decline that could precede dementia onset. In late-life, biomarkers for AD, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation were associated with faster decline across different cognitive domains, but associations remained strongest for p-tau181 and memory.

Title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR.
METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death.
RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037).
CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

Title: Ten years of concomitant aortic and mitral replacement: trends, outcomes and the role of patient-prosthesis mismatch.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary data comparing double mechanical prostheses (DMP) vs. double biological prostheses (DBP) for concomitant aortic and mitral valve replacement are scarce, and the cumulative hemodynamic burden of simultaneous prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) at both positions has never been systematically assessed.
RESULTS: DMP recipients had lower in-hospital mortality (1.9% vs. 15.2%; P = 0.010) and superior 7-year survival (91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003), but significantly higher stroke rates (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023). Combined PPM occurred in 64.6% of DBP vs. 14.8% of DMP (P < 0.001).
MAJOR FINDINGS: Concomitant double valve replacement confirmed its high-risk profile, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 10.5%. DMP demonstrated superior unadjusted survival (7-year: 91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003) but significantly higher stroke risk (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023), without differences in major bleeding rates at follow-up (8.2% vs. 11.3%; P = 0.478), although baseline differences precluded definitive prosthesis-type recommendations after multivariable adjustment. Combined PPM is highly prevalent after DBP (64.6%) and emerged as a univariable mortality predictor (hazard ratio 1.97; P = 0.046); given the exploratory nature of the cPPM definition and its collinearity with prosthesis type, this should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrants validation in larger, ideally multicenter, cohorts.

Title: Arrhythmias in patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and the impact of contemporary disease-modifying therapies.
Abstract: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is an increasingly recognized infiltrative cardiomyopathy characterized by extracellular deposition of misfolded transthyretin fibrils, leading to progressive myocardial stiffening, electrical remodeling, and conduction-system disease. These pathophysiological changes create a complex arrhythmic substrate, resulting in a high burden of atrial, bradyarrhythmia, and ventricular arrhythmias that significantly contribute to morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in disease recognition, the optimal management of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM remains challenging, with limited evidence guiding antiarrhythmic strategies and device therapy. In particular, the prognostic significance of ventricular arrhythmias and the role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) remain controversial. Recent disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), including transthyretin stabilizers (tafamidis, diflunisal) and gene-silencing agents (patisiran, vutrisiran), have transformed the therapeutic landscape and may modify disease progression and arrhythmic burden, although their direct antiarrhythmic impact is not yet fully defined. This narrative review provides a structured overview of the mechanisms, epidemiology, and clinical management of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM, with a focus on clinically relevant decision-making and the potential influence of contemporary DMTs. Finally, it highlights key unresolved questions and areas requiring further prospective research.

Title: Beta-blocker therapy and aortic growth in nonsyndromic ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms: a serial CT analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of beta blockers in slowing aneurysm progression in patients with nonsyndromic ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms (aTAA) remains uncertain. We investigated the association between beta blocker therapy and longitudinal ascending aortic growth measured by serial computed tomography (CT).
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 390 adults with nonsyndromic aTAA who underwent at least two contrast-enhanced CT examinations separated by a minimum of 2 years. Patients were classified according to beta blocker therapy (311 users and 79 nonusers). The primary outcome was the annual ascending aortic growth rate. Secondary outcomes included changes in the ascending aortic size index (ASI) and ascending aortic height index (AHI). Univariate and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of annual aortic growth.
RESULTS: Baseline ascending aortic diameter was comparable between beta blocker users and nonusers (45.1 ± 3.5 vs. 45.2 ± 3.6 mm, P = 0.73). During a mean CT follow-up of 73.2 ± 39.1 months, annual ascending aortic growth rates were similar between groups (0.40 ± 0.54 vs. 0.45 ± 0.65 mm/year, P = 0.49). Likewise, changes in ASI and AHI did not differ according to beta blocker therapy. In multivariable linear regression analysis, beta blocker use was not independently associated with annual ascending aortic growth (standardized β = -0.031, P = 0.548). Exploratory subgroup analyses demonstrated numerically lower annual growth rates among beta blocker users with baseline ascending aortic diameters ≥48 mm and bicuspid aortic valves; however, neither comparison reached statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: In this long-term CT-based cohort of patients with nonsyndromic aTAA, beta blocker therapy was not independently associated with slower ascending aortic growth or changes in indexed aortic dimensions. Larger prospective studies are needed to further clarify the role of beta blockers in limiting aneurysm progression.

Title: Polyvascular disease by systematic vascular screening and adverse outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
Abstract:
AIMS: The prognostic significance of systematically screened extra-coronary vascular disease in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains incompletely understood. We investigated the prevalence and prognostic impact of polyvascular disease (PVD) identified using a routine vascular screening strategy in patients with AMI.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center observational study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement and carotid ultrasonography were routinely performed during index hospitalization. PVD was defined as the presence of peripheral artery disease (ABI ≤ 0.90) and/or carotid artery disease, defined as carotid plaque according to the Mannheim consensus (maximal wall thickness ≥ 1.5 mm) or ≥50% carotid stenosis. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and unplanned coronary revascularization after discharge.
RESULTS: Among 233 eligible patients, PVD was identified in 73 patients (31.3%), including 55 (23.6%) with single-territory PVD and 18 (7.7%) with multiterritory PVD. During a median follow-up of 419 days, the primary endpoint occurred in 43 patients. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a graded decrease in event-free survival according to increasing PVD burden (log-rank P = 0.014; P for trend = 0.007). In Cox proportional hazards analysis, the presence of PVD was significantly associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, and renal dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: PVD is common in patients with AMI and is associated with poor long-term clinical outcomes. Routine systematic assessment of extra-coronary vascular disease may improve cardiovascular risk stratification.

Title: Prevalence and prognostic role of left atrial reverse remodeling in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair: insights from the Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
Abstract:
AIMS: Atrial enlargement is a complex maladaptive process related to pressure and volume overload. Left atrial reverse remodeling (LARR) has been described as a result of medical and interventional therapies. We sought to explore LARR prevalence and its prognostic implications following mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER).
METHODS AND RESULTS: Four-hundred and twenty-five patients from the MERIT-TEER (Multicenter Echocardiographic Registry of patients undergoing M-TEER) who received a successful procedure from 2012 to 2024 with available left atrial volume (LAV) have been analyzed. LARR was defined as a reduction in LAV of at least 15%. LARR prevalence and its association with the risk of heart failure hospitalization and all-cause mortality at 4 years' follow-up were evaluated in the overall population and according to mitral regurgitation etiology.At short-term follow-up, LARR was observed in 124 patients (29.20%). LARR was more prevalent among primary mitral regurgitation (PMR) patients compared with those with ventricular secondary (vSMR) and atrial secondary mitral regurgitation (aSMR) (37.23, 27.19, and 18.33%; P = 0.017). At long-term follow-up, the composite outcome occurred in 153 patients (36.2%). LARR was independently associated with lower risk of events in the overall population [adjusted hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.85, P = 0.005] and among vSMR patients (adjusted hazard ratio 0.43, 95% CI 0.26-0.71, P = 0.001), but not in aSMR or PMR.
CONCLUSION: LARR was observed in less than one-third of patients undergoing M-TEER (29.2%), occurring more frequently in PMR. LARR was independently associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization in the overall population and particularly in patients with vSMR.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Interventions to reduce cognitive decline post-stroke: an umbrella review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains a common problem that can lead to significant disability and dependency. Previous work suggested that methodologically robust trials were lacking and that there is continued uncertainty on the benefits and limitations of pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. This umbrella review aims to update and synthesise evidence on pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions for PSCI.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This review was pre-registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024611909) with searches from 2019 to 2024. Eligible studies were systematic reviews (SRs) of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating pharmacological or non-pharmacological interventions in adult stroke survivors (≥18 years) of any severity and reporting change in global cognition (eg, Mini-Mental State Examination). AMSTAR2 was used for risk of bias.
RESULTS: Of 4889 records identified, 69 SRs (global cognition data from 747 unique RCTs; 57,176 participants) met inclusion criteria. Interventions were grouped into 37 categories including both single (eg, acupuncture, exercise, cognitive rehabilitation) and combined modalities and assessed at categorical level. Most intervention types were associated with statistically significant improvements in global cognition. Substantial heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals indicate that effect sizes may vary considerably across populations and settings.
DISCUSSION: This review identifies promising evidence that several interventions may produce clinically meaningful improvements in global cognition post-stroke. However, confidence in this evidence is low: despite a substantial increase in the number of RCTs most included reviews were rated as critically low in quality with methodological limitations.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence is insufficient to support firm recommendations for the inclusion of specific interventions in guidance.

Title: Multimodal Imaging Characteristics of Sarcoid Retinal Granulomas.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the clinical presentation and multimodal imaging characteristics of retinal granulomas in patients with ocular sarcoidosis.
METHODS: In this retrospective observational case series, patients with definite or presumed ocular sarcoidosis presenting with retinal granulomas were evaluated. Multimodal retinal imaging was reviewed to characterize lesion morphology, imaging patterns, and longitudinal evolution.
RESULTS: Retinal granulomas were identified in three patients with ocular sarcoidosis from diverse racial backgrounds. On fundus photographs, lesions ranged from multiple, superficial, small, faint yellow-gray nodules to more distinct, deeper yellow lesions, predominantly located in the mid- to peripheral retina. All retinal granulomas demonstrated hyperreflectivity on OCT with four distinct morphologic patterns: (1) inner and/or outer retinal granulomas; (2) retinal granulomas associated with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) disruption and hypertransmission defects; (3) sub-RPE granulomas located between the RPE and Bruch's membrane; and (4) combined chorioretinal granulomas extending from the choroid. FAF demonstrated predominantly isoautofluorescent lesions in the absence of RPE involvement, whereas hypoautofluorescence was observed when the RPE was involved. FA was available for one patient and demonstrated late hyperfluorescent staining of the retinal granulomas. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated evolution from active inflammatory nodules to regression with residual retinal and/or RPE changes, commonly manifesting as punched-out atrophic lesions.
CONCLUSION: Retinal granulomas may represent an underrecognized manifestation of ocular sarcoidosis. In our series, multimodal imaging allowed detailed characterization of their morphologic patterns and longitudinal evolution. Recognition of these characteristic imaging features of sarcoid retinal granulomas may facilitate consideration of sarcoidosis in the differential diagnosis of retinal infiltrative lesions.

Title: Rates of nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) regression among patients with very mild or mild NPDR in an Indian Health Service teleophthalmology program, 2015 - 2020.
Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) regression is not regularly reported; yet understanding of its prevalence in early-stage DR may impact strategies for eye care management. This study's primary aim was to examine DR regression in patients initially diagnosed with very mild or mild nonproliferative DR (NPDR). A secondary aim was to assess the association between retinopathy regression and diabetes therapy, diabetes duration, and Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c). This was a retrospective, longitudinal cohort study using medical record data from the United States's Indian Health Service's teleophthalmology program for DR evaluation. Baseline exams occurred in 2015-2017 and follow-up (FU) exams occurred within 3 years of baseline. There were 2,348 patients included in this cohort with very mild NPDR at baseline and 705 patients with mild NPDR. For the whole sample, mean age was 56 ± 12.8 years, 55% were female, diabetes duration was 13.0 ± 9.1 years, and HbA1c was 8.8 ± 2.1%. Proportions for DR regression were 0.47 (CI = .45 - .50) (from very mild NPDR) and 0.36 (CI = 0.33-0.40) (from mild NPDR). Proportions for any DR progression were 0.27 (CI = 0.25-0.29) (from very mild NPDR) and 0.34 (CI = 0.30-0.38) (from mild NPDR). Multivariable analyses showed that lower HbA1c levels were associated with greater odds of diabetic retinopathy regression in patients with either very mild or mild baseline NPDR, whereas insulin use was associated with lower odds of regression. Shorter diabetes duration was associated with greater odds of regression only among patients with very mild NPDR at baseline. DR regression was more frequent than DR progression particularly for patients initially with very mild NPDR. DR reversal was more likely in early-stage DR. Behavioral modifications such as increased physical activity and weight loss that lower HbA1c and subsequent risks for DR progression are important to emphasize in diabetic eye care.

Title: Rising stroke burden in Uganda: A national time-series analysis and forecasts, 2016-2028.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally, with a disproportionate and growing burden in low- and middle-income Countries. However, evidence on national temporal trends and potential impacts in Uganda remains limited. This study examined trends in stroke cases and deaths in Uganda and forecast of future stroke burden through December 2028.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective time-series analysis of District Health Information System (DHIS2) from 2016 to 2025. Monthly stroke cases, and deaths were analyzed. Monthly populations of Uganda were estimated using exponential growth interpolation and incorporated as an offset term in Bayesian negative binomial regression models to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR) at 95% confidence interval (CI). Decomposition analysis using the Kitagawa method was applied to derive contributions from population growth and epidemiological change, based on model estimates. Stationarity and autocorrelation were assessed using the unit root and Ljung-Box tests. Forecasting was performed using the exponential smoothing state-space (ETS) model at 80% prediction intervals (PI).
RESULTS: Trend analysis showed sustained monthly increases in stroke incidence and mortality with IRR; 1.005 (95% CI: 1.004-1.006), and 1.006 (95% CI: 1.005-1.007), respectively (all p < 0.001). The epidemiological effect was approximately twice as large as the population effect, indicating that the majority of the increase in stroke cases and deaths is attributable to rising incidence rates rather than population growth alone. ETS model demonstrated that by December 2028, monthly cases and deaths are projected to reach approximately 927 (80% PI: 709-1,156) and 126 (80% PI: 94-160), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Stroke burden in Uganda is projected to continue increase further over the next years in the absence of effective prevention measures. Strengthened primary prevention, expanded acute stroke care capacity, and improved surveillance systems are urgently needed to mitigate the growing health system impact.

Title: Fluctuations of micronutrients during pregnancy in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China: A prospective longitudinal cohort study.
Abstract: Pregnancy is accompanied by substantial physiological adaptations that may alter maternal micronutrient concentrations. A prospective longitudinal pregnancy-neonatal cohort of 51 healthy pregnant women was established at 6-8 weeks of gestation in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China, confirmed by fetal heart and bud on B-ultrasound. Pregnancy complications, outcomes, and neonatal health at day 42 were confirmed. Forty-three women who completed all assessments and had uncomplicated pregnancies with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes were included in the final analysis. Whole-blood trace elements and serum vitamins were quantified during the first trimester (12.3 ± 0.9 weeks), second trimester (25.6 ± 1.2 weeks), and third trimester (32.7 ± 2.3 weeks) using ICP-MS and UHPLC-MS/MS. The results showed that copper, calcium, and vitamin D peaked in the second trimester, whereas iron, zinc, magnesium, and lead reached their nadir in the second trimester. Meanwhile, manganese and vitamins E and K increased progressively throughout gestation. In contrast, several B vitamins showed an overall downward trend, while vitamin B12 remained relatively stable. These findings demonstrate clear trimester-specific changes in maternal micronutrient levels during healthy pregnancy. Given the relatively small sample size, these longitudinal data provide preliminary evidence to inform the establishment of region-specific and trimester-specific reference intervals and deficiency thresholds for micronutrients in healthy pregnant women.

Title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced electrocardiography for predicting mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events: A systematic review and narrative synthesis.
Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. While clinical scores provide modest predictive accuracy, the electrocardiogram (ECG) is rarely leveraged for prognosis. Artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning now enable extraction of high-dimensional features from ECG waveforms for predicting cardiovascular outcomes. Our objective was to systematically evaluate the prognostic performance of AI-enabled ECG models for predicting all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). We searched PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar through November 2025 for studies using AI/ML models with 12-lead or single-lead ECGs to predict all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, or MACE in adults (≥18 years old). Eligible studies included adults (≥18 years) using ECG as primary input. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Narrative synthesis was conducted due to heterogeneity. Thirteen studies were included (~5.9 million patients). Eleven reported all-cause mortality (8 short-term: 30-day to 1-year), four reported cardiovascular mortality, and eight assessed MACE (4 composite MACE, 4 individual components). Models predominantly used convolutional neural networks [CNNs] on raw ECG waveforms. C-statistics ranged 0.70-0.89 for mortality prediction. Definitions and follow-up durations varied, limiting direct comparison. AI-ECG models demonstrate strong potential for predicting mortality and cardiovascular events with consistent performance and scalability. However, prospective validation and standardization are essential before clinical implementation.

Title: Radiofrequency Ablation for Selective Reduction in Complicated Monochorionic Twin Pregnancies: Pregnancy-Level and Neonatal Outcomes.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Monochorionic twin pregnancies may be complicated by shared placental vascular anastomoses and hemodynamic interdependence between fetuses. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a vaso-occlusive option for selective reduction when continuation of the affected fetus is expected to endanger the co-twin.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 39 monochorionic twin pregnancies treated with RFA at two tertiary centers between January 2017 and December 2025. Indications were grouped as TTTS/TAPS-related conditions, selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR)-related conditions, twin reversed arterial perfusion (TRAP) sequence, and discordant major fetal anomaly. The primary outcome was live birth of at least one fetus. Secondary outcomes included miscarriage, stillbirth/intrauterine fetal demise, termination after RFA, preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM), gestational age at delivery, birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, neonatal death, and survival to neonatal hospital discharge.
RESULTS: The main indications were sFGR-related conditions (14/39, 35.9%) and TTTS/TAPS-related conditions (12/39, 30.8%). Live birth of at least one fetus occurred in 38/39 pregnancies (97.4%), and pregnancy-level survival to neonatal hospital discharge occurred in 37/39 pregnancies (94.9%). PPROM after RFA occurred in 2/39 pregnancies (5.1%). Among pregnancies with live birth, median gestational age at delivery was 38.00 weeks (IQR, 34.00-39.00). Exploratory comparisons across indication groups, including direct TTTS/TAPS-related versus TRAP comparisons for gestational age at delivery and procedure-to-delivery interval, were not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: RFA was associated with high rates of live birth and survival to neonatal hospital discharge in this cohort of complicated monochorionic twin pregnancies. Exploratory subgroup comparisons were not statistically significant; therefore, observed indication-specific patterns should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger multicenter cohorts.

Title: Prenatal echocardiographic predictors that increase the risk of urgent Ballon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) after birth in patients with Dextro-Transposition of the Great Arteries- Retrospective Study from Tertiary Center Lodz- Poland ICZMP (2014-2024).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Dextro-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA) is a critical congenital heart disease (CHD) requiring prompt postnatal intervention, primarily: a line for Prostin infusion, hospitalization in an Intensive Care Unit, and in some cases, Balloon Atrial Septostomy (BAS) as a rescue procedure before planned Arterial Switch Operation (ASO). In this part, we focus on prenatal prediction of postnatal BAS.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study was conducted at the Department of Prenatal Cardiology, Polish Mother's Memorial Hospital in Lodz, covering the years 2014-2024. From a total of 112 prenatally diagnosed d-TGA cases, 70 fetuses (46 with isolated d-TGA and 24 with d-TGA and VSD) met the inclusion criteria; follow-up of four pregnancies ended up in other hospitals, so the final series was 66 cases. Statistical analyses were performed using Statistica software.
RESULTS: Out of 66 analyzed cases, 32 newborns (48%) required postnatal BAS, with 87.5% of these procedures performed within the first 24-48 hours of life. Prenatal echocardiography correctly predicted the postnatal management pathway in 90.9% of cases (60/66), identifying all 26 neonates requiring urgent balloon atrial septostomy (100% positive predictive value), while 6 neonates in the planned group required unexpected postnatal septostomy. We noted that the 18% (n=6) of cases not identified prenatally occurred when the last scan was performed > 14 days before birth, suggesting that the time interval significantly impacts the reliability of late-gestation FO assessment. The study identified 10 prenatal "red flags," including FO size < 3 mm, bi-directional FO flow, and pulmonary vein velocity ≥ 45 cm/s and other features, as high-reliability indicators for urgent postnatal intervention.
CONCLUSION: Prenatal functional assessment of the foramen ovale in the late third trimester was highly effective in predicting the need for postnatal urgent BAS in d-TGA cases. The accuracy of these "red flags" was significantly higher when the last fetal echocardiogram was performed within 14 days to delivery.

Title: Urinary biomarkers at hospital admission and community-acquired acute kidney injury: A prospective cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine the sensitivity and specificity of a 13-urinary biomarker (uBM) panel for identifying community-acquired acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) and to assess whether these biomarkers were independently associated with CA-AKI.
METHODS: This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital. Adults admitted through the emergency department were included. CA-AKI was defined as a ≥0.3 mg/dl decrease in serum creatinine (SCr) within 48 hours or a ≥50% decrease within 7 days. Blood samples were collected daily for SCr measurement, and urine samples were obtained at admission for uBM assessment. All the uBM were classified as abnormal when they exceeded the 75th percentile of the distribution.
RESULTS: 731 patients were included (55% male, median age of 61 years; 48% had hypertension, 28% had diabetes mellitus, and 23% had heart failure). The main reasons for hospitalization were respiratory (32%), genitourinary (15%), and cardiovascular (11%) diseases. CA-AKI was diagnosed in 26% of the patients. Compared with patients without CA-AKI, those with CA-AKI showed higher rates of elevation in four uBM: KIM-1 (31% vs. 23%; p=0.032), TIMP-2*IGFBP-7 (30% vs. 23%; p=0.045), clusterin (32% vs. 22%; p=0.011), and MCP-1 (33% vs. 22%; p=0.003). The sensitivity and specificity of uBM for detecting CA-AKI ranged from 23% to 33% and from 74% to 78%, respectively, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) ranged from 0.485 to 0.554. Logistic regression analyses identified conditions independently associated with CA-AKI, including: hypotension [OR (95% CI): 2.07 (1.33-3.23); p=0.001], dehydration [OR (95% CI): 2.01 (1.40-2.91); p<0.001], chronic kidney disease [OR (95% CI): 2.00 (1.19-3.35); p=0.009], genitourinary tract disease [OR (95% CI): 2.00 (1.26-3.10); p=0.003], chronic liver disease [OR (95% CI): 1.69 (1.09-2.61); p=0.018], and elevation of one or more of the following uBM: KIM-1, TIMP-2*IGFBP-7, clusterin, and MCP-1 [OR (95% CI): 1.51 (1.06-2.14); p=0.022].
CONCLUSION: The expression of one or more of four uBM at emergency department admission (KIM-1, TIMP-2*IGFBP-7, clusterin, and MCP-1) may help identify patients with a higher probability of having CA-AKI, even with modest AUC results.

Title: Telehealth and Digital Interventions for Type 2 Diabetes and Hypertension in Latin America and the Caribbean: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Telemedicine journal and e-health : the official journal of the American Telemedicine Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telehealth, remote monitoring, and other digital interventions may support chronic disease management, but evidence from Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) remains fragmented. We evaluated clinical effectiveness and characterized human support, clinical integration, and implementation.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, and LILACS were searched through July 2026 for studies of digital interventions in adults with type 2 diabetes or hypertension in LAC. Random-effects meta-analyses were restricted to randomized trials and used restricted maximum likelihood estimation, Hartung-Knapp adjustment, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs). Evidence certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Thirty-six studies (41 reports) from 12 countries were included: 15 randomized and 21 nonrandomized. Six trials (n = 689) showed lower HbA1c (mean difference [MD] -1.23 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI] -2.19 to -0.26; I2 = 83.8%; PI: -3.64 to 1.18). Seven trials (n = 2,280) showed lower systolic blood pressure (SBP; MD: -4.97 mmHg; 95% CI: -7.15 to -2.79; I2 = 26.1%; PI: -8.85 to -1.09), and five (n = 1,825) showed lower diastolic blood pressure (DBP; MD: -3.46 mmHg; 95% CI: -5.69 to -1.22; I2 = 76.1%; PI: -9.24 to 2.33). Certainty was moderate for SBP and low for HbA1c and DBP. Professional support and clinical integration were common, whereas sustainability, scalability, interoperability, costs, and equity were inconsistently evaluated.
CONCLUSIONS: Digitally enabled chronic care may improve glycemic and blood-pressure control in LAC, with the most consistent evidence for SBP. Heterogeneous intervention models and limited implementation evidence warrant comparative effectiveness-implementation studies.

Title: Association between serum transaminase elevations and clinical course in patients with familial Mediterranean fever.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical features, disease course, genetics, and treatment responses of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) patients with elevated serum transaminase levels.
METHODS: The charts of the FMF patients with at least one year of follow-up were retrospectively investigated for the presence of elevated serum transaminase levels. The genetic and clinical findings and disease course of identified patients were compared with a group of FMF patients with no transaminase elevations.
RESULTS: A retrospective chart review included 780 registered patients diagnosed with FMF. Forty-two patients (5.3%) were excluded because of the insufficient follow-up duration, associated viral hepatitis, alcoholic hepatitis, and biopsy-proven liver amyloidosis. A total of 83 patients (11.2%) with elevated serum transaminase levels were identified, and their findings were compared with a control group of 655 patients with no transaminase elevation. FMF attacks began at a significantly older age (17.0±12.9 vs. 12.4±9.0 years, p=0.01), and the percentage of patients experiencing more frequent (≥ 3 attacks/month) attacks was higher (35.4% vs. 24.1%, p=0.01) in the elevated transaminase group. No significant differences were observed between the two groups regarding age at diagnosis, delay in diagnosis, presenting features of FMF, CRP levels at baseline and during attacks, frequency of amyloidosis, and the colchicine dose, as well as the frequency of patients requiring anti-IL-1 treatments. The frequency of MEFV gene exon 10 mutations and p.M694V homozygosity did not differ significantly between the groups. Hepatosteatosis was observed by abdominal ultrasonography in 46.7% of the patients with elevated liver enzymes. A follow-up study after 6 years revealed that transaminase levels remained elevated in 21 out of 49 patients (42.9%), and one patient developed liver cirrhosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated serum transaminase levels can be detected in approximately 11.2% of FMF patients, and this finding is not associated with colchicine use or manifestations of FMF. Ultrasonographic evidence of hepatosteatosis was observed in nearly half of the patients. Follow-up analysis showed that serum transaminase elevations may persist in 43% of the patients, which suggests further studies to determine whether this abnormality is a feature of FMF or not.

Title: Patient Blood Management Adoption and Transfusion-Threshold Concordance Among Romanian Anesthesiologists: National Survey Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Romania issued national patient blood management (PBM) guidelines in 2018. A 2023 national survey described the overall uptake of PBM among anesthesiologists but did not examine which clinicians and institutions adopted PBM, nor whether stated transfusion thresholds aligned with a study-defined restrictive reference.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify determinants of PBM adoption and to quantify transfusion-trigger concordance, using a planned, exploratory, cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2023 survey.
METHODS: We analyzed 511 responses to the 38-item Romanian Society of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care (SRATI) PBM survey. Three adoption outcomes (applying PBM, a formal hospital PBM group, and routine preoperative anemia treatment) were modeled by multivariable logistic regression against physician grade, hospital category, and local PBM educational events. Eight standardized clinical vignettes (age×cardiac disease×bleeding state) were scored against a restrictive hemoglobin reference (7 g/dL general; 8 g/dL with cardiac disease). The reported timing of the preanesthetic consultation (4 frequency items) was additionally examined as a determinant of preoperative anemia treatment. This was a planned, exploratory secondary analysis; the robustness of the main findings was examined in sensitivity analyses that accounted for survey attrition and for alternative transfusion-threshold scoring rules.
RESULTS: Overall, 73.7% (373/506) reported applying PBM, 33.1% (158/477) reported a formal PBM group, and 33.5% (117/349) reported routine preoperative anemia treatment. Local PBM educational events were the strongest adjusted correlate of reported adoption (applying PBM: adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 9.78, 95% CI 4.33-22.07; P<.001; formal group: aOR 7.72, 95% CI 4.30-13.88; P<.001). Earlier preanesthetic consultation was associated with routine preoperative anemia treatment (aOR 1.79 per frequency level for consultation more than 7 days before surgery, 95% CI 1.36-2.35; P<.001). Transfusion-trigger concordance was lower for older than younger patients in otherwise identical scenarios (eg, active bleeding without cardiac disease: 195/345, 56.5% at ≥65 years vs 288/347, 83% at <65 years), and 56.5% (196/347) endorsed a liberal trigger (hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL) in at least one noncardiac scenario. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with a restrictive transfusion pattern (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 0.69-1.98; P=.56). Findings were unchanged across scoring rules, and reported PBM application was similar among respondents who did and did not complete the demographic block (246/329, 74.8% vs 127/177, 71.8%; P=.53).
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory cross-sectional analysis, reported PBM adoption was associated more strongly with local educational activity than with hospital category or physician seniority. Self-reported PBM application was not associated with restrictive stated thresholds in hypothetical scenarios, and respondents selected more liberal thresholds for older patients. Standardized multidisciplinary pathways, earlier anemia screening shared with the surgical team, and education focused on transfusion decisions may help address these gaps. Prospective studies using observed process measures, transfusion practice, and clinical outcomes are needed.

Title: Prehospital Risk Stratification for Early Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric criteria remain limited for identifying injured children who may benefit from early blood transfusion for hemorrhagic shock. This study evaluated whether emergency medical services (EMS)-observable variables in a national trauma registry could identify children at risk for early hospital blood transfusion.
METHODS: We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study using the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2020). Among 391,126 records for patients aged 1-15 years, we included children transported by EMS directly from the scene to a participating trauma center after excluding burn injuries, interfacility transfers, and missing pre-identified EMS variables (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, or Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]). The primary outcome was any blood product administered within 4 h of emergency department arrival. Five prespecified EMS-observable predictors composed the model: age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest. We fit a multivariable logistic regression and a classification and regression tree (CART) using an 80/20 stratified train-validation split. Missing data sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and CART refitting in the broader eligible cohort.
RESULTS: Among 79,764 children, 2,634 (3.3%) received early transfusion in the hospital. All five predictors were independently associated with early transfusion, led by GCS ≤ 14 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.61-9.22), penetrating mechanism (aOR 5.87; 95% CI, 5.28-6.51), and age-adjusted hypotension (aOR 5.39; 95% CI, 4.74-6.13). In the validation cohort, CART analysis stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk tiers comprising 77.0%, 19.7%, and 3.3% of patients, respectively. Early-transfusion rates were 1.2%, 6.1%, and 36.7% across these tiers. The high-risk tier accounted for 36.8% of all early transfusion events. Using the high-risk tier as a decision threshold, sensitivity was 36.8%, specificity 97.8%, positive predictive value 36.7%, and negative predictive value 97.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: Five EMS-observable features, including age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤ 14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest, identified a small subgroup of pediatric trauma patients with substantially elevated risk of early hospital transfusion. This parsimonious framework may inform prospective validation of prehospital transfusion criteria.

Title: Influence of Perioperative Variables on Surgical Site Infection in Patients With Frailty and Prefrailty Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) in patients with frailty undergoing myocardial revascularization is a major clinical challenge, and there is a gap in the literature related to this topic.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify perioperative variables associated with SSI in patients with frailty and prefrailty undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting within 30 days of the procedure.
METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 467 patients with frailty or prefrailty aged 60 years and older who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting in 6 Brazilian centers between January 2018 and December 2024. Frailty was defined using the Fried criteria. SSI was defined as a wound with exposed tissue with positive culture requiring antibiotic treatment. Univariate and multivariate analyses were carried out.
RESULTS: The rate of SSI was 5.6% (26/467). The New York Heart Association classification (P=.02), Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI; P=.01), use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB; P=.003), CPB time (P=.02), total surgery time (P<.001), occurrence of bleeding (P=.04), mechanical ventilation time (P=.001), length of hospital stay (P<.001), intensive care unit stay (P<.001), and need for reoperation (P<.001) variables were associated with SSI in unadjusted comparisons. In the multivariate model, the CCI (odds ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.25-1.99; P<.001) and use of CPB (odds ratio 4.89, 95% CI 1.71-13.94; P=.003) were independently associated with SSI.
CONCLUSIONS: The CCI and the use of CPB were independently associated with SSI.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of immune-inflammatory biomarkers for predicting no-reflow in patients with acute myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether routine immune-inflammatory biomarkers predict no-reflow (NR) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients, quantify their incremental predictive value over clinical variables, and build an interpretable peri-procedural prediction model.
METHODS: This prospective cohort recruited 382 AMI patients undergoing PCI. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified independent correlates; confounder-adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS) assessed nonlinear associations. LASSO regression selected core predictors with variance inflation factor (VIF) assessing multicollinearity. Four machine-learning models underwent 1000-iteration bootstrap internal validation and SHAP interpretation. Incremental value was tested via ΔAUC (DeLong test), continuous NRI, and IDI. Stratified regression and interaction tests evaluated AMI-subtype effect modification.
RESULTS: NR occurred in 91 patients (23.8%). Multiple neutrophil-centred indices independently correlated with NR after adjustment. Seven predictors constituted the final model (all VIF < 2.5). LightGBM yielded optimal discrimination and modest net clinical benefit (AUC 0.799, 95% CI 0.699-0.899); AMI subtype and neutrophil-related markers dominated SHAP outputs. Neutrophil count, NAR, NHR, SII, and PIV significantly improved discrimination. Seven of the 16 tested markers yielded significant continuous NRI, and ten demonstrated significant IDI gains. In stratified analyses, neutrophil count, NLR, and MHR were associated with NR in STEMI but not NSTEMI patients; interaction tests found no significant AMI-subtype effect modification.
CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural neutrophil-centred inflammatory biomarkers are independent correlates of post-PCI NR and offer incremental predictive value over conventional clinical variables. The interpretable LightGBM model supports peri-procedural NR risk stratification, though external validation and recalibration are mandatory before clinical application.

Title: Cardiovascular risk associated with first-line Janus kinase inhibitors versus TNF inhibitors in patients with RA: a nationwide cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) between TNF inhibitors (TNFi) and Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) when initiated as first-line advanced therapy in patients with RA.
METHODS: Using the Korean nationwide claims database, we identified patients newly diagnosed with RA between 2010 and 2015. Patients who initiated TNFi or JAKi as first-line advanced therapy were selected for analysis. Patients were followed from initiation of TNFi or JAKi through June 2024. The primary outcome was incident MACE, defined as myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke or coronary revascularization. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied in the total cohort. We additionally performed propensity score (PS)-matched analyses to address confounding by indication. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to baseline cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: The study included 6174 patients (TNFi = 5152; JAKi = 1022). The incidence rates of MACE were 4.1 and 3.6 per 1000 person-years in the TNFi and JAKi groups, respectively. MACE risk did not differ significantly between JAKi and TNFi in the total study cohort (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.636, 95% CI 0.283-1.429) or in the PS-matched population (adjusted HR 0.715, 95% CI 0.187-2.739). Results were consistent across all prespecified subgroups, including patients with baseline cardiovascular risk factors.
CONCLUSION: First-line use of JAKi was not associated with an increased risk of MACE compared with TNFi. These findings provide real-world evidence supporting the cardiovascular safety of JAKi as first-line advanced therapy in patients with RA.

Title: Outcomes of systemic sclerosis with overlapping myositis: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest disease-specific mortality among rheumatic diseases, with cardiac involvement and interstitial lung disease (ILD) as leading causes of death. We aimed to determine whether overlapping myositis independently contributes to cardiac involvement and mortality in SSc.
METHODS: We did a 1:1 propensity score matched retrospective cohort study of 880 SSc patients (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) at a single centre. SSc myositis required proximal weakness and elevated muscle enzymes without alternative causes. Cardiac involvement used SCTC criteria (pericardial effusion, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmia, conduction disease). We used standard and Firth penalised logistic regression for cardiac predictors, Cox regression for survival, and Fisher's exact test for cause specific mortality. All p values were Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted.
RESULTS: Of 880 patients, 92 (10.4%) had myositis. After matching, 92 pairs (n = 184) were analysed. Myositis independently predicted cardiac involvement (standard aOR=19.99, 95%CI 2.19-182.26, p = 0.008; Firth OR = 12.84, 95%CI 2.31-98.47, p = 0.006). Higher mRSS also predicted cardiac involvement (aOR=2.34 per 10 points, p = 0.006). Anti-Scl70 was less common in myositis (25.0% vs. 50.0%, p = 0.009). Overall mortality did not differ (13.0% vs. 9.8%, p = 0.620). In non-myositis deaths, ILD caused 33.3%; in myositis deaths, cardiac failure caused 25% and no ILD-related deaths (Fisher's p = 0.229). Cardiac involvement was significantly associated with mortality (aHR=8.09 (1.36-48.26), p = 0.022), independent of myositis.
CONCLUSION: Overlapping myositis in SSc is associated with an increased risk of cardiac involvement and a shift in the cause-of-death profile away from ILD, without a detectable difference in overall survival over the observed median 21-month follow-up. Systematic cardiac surveillance is needed in these patients.

Title: Effects of Single-Session High-Definition Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation (HD-tACS) Combined with Robot-Assisted Hand Exercises on Corticospinal Excitability in Chronic Stroke.
Journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This preliminary study investigated whether a single session of high-definition transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD-tACS) could improve corticospinal tract (CST) excitability compared with sham stimulation in healthy individuals and individuals with chronic stroke.
DESIGN: Twelve healthy adults and 7 individuals with chronic stroke received active and sham HD-tACS over the primary motor cortex (M1) flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) hotspot, ipsilesional in stroke subjects, for 30 minutes at 2mA and 21 Hz in a randomized crossover design. All subjects performed robot-assisted grasp-and-open hand exercises during active and sham stimulation.
RESULTS: HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in the healthy group (15.3%). In the stroke group, FDS MEP amplitudes were increased by ∼22.3% after HD-tACS, but this change was not statistically significant. When MEP amplitudes were normalized as percentage change, HD-tACS significantly increased FDS MEP amplitudes in both groups compared with the sham condition. No significant extensor digitorum communis (EDC) modulation was observed in either group.
CONCLUSION: HD-tACS combined with robot-assisted hand exercises may enhance CST excitability compared with robot-assisted hand exercises alone after a single session in both healthy and stroke subjects. However, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Cost-utility of expanded hypertension screening and treatment among adults covered by Peru's Seguro Integral de Salud: a Markov model using national data.
Journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We assessed the cost-utility of expanding hypertension screening, diagnosis, and treatment among adults covered by Peru's Seguro Integral de Salud (SIS).
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Analyses assembled in May 2026 used a 10-year cohort Markov model parameterized with the 2024 Peruvian Demographic and Family Health Survey (ENDES), SIS administrative data for 2022-2024, and published parameters. Universal and risk-targeted scenarios were compared with population-specific usual care, using S/ 25,007 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY).
RESULTS: The baseline sample included 6,098 adults aged 40-74 years; hypertension prevalence was 28.9%. Universal 80-80-80 expansion averted 60.7 cardiovascular events and 6.1 cardiovascular deaths and gained 51.3 QALYs per 100,000 eligible adults. Incremental cost was S/ 7,784,979, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of S/ 151,686/QALY. The scenario targeting 10-year cardiovascular risk ≥10% had an ICER of S/ 60,171/QALY in its eligible subgroup.
CONCLUSIONS: All scenarios exceeded the threshold. Lower targeted-scenario ICERs concern different eligible populations. Estimates depend on modeled effects, the 10-year horizon, and exclusion of event-related savings.

Title: Large language model assistance for report-based carotid plaque AHA classification: a multi-reader study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether large language model assistance improves radiologists' agreement with a text-based reference standard in inferring the modified American Heart Association carotid plaque classification from free-text MRI reports, and whether a lightweight model can perform well under criteria-guided prompting.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 433 patients from three institutions. In a report-based reader study, four radiologists classified MRI reports with and without large language model assistance. In standalone evaluation, a rule-based baseline and 10 models were compared under naive and criteria-guided prompting. The reference standard was expert consensus based on the report text.
RESULTS: Among 433 patients (mean age, 65.9 years ± 13.4; 248 males), AI assistance improved six-class agreement with the text-based reference standard. At the vessel level, junior radiologists improved from 61.75% to 83.12% (Qwen3-8B) and 87.75% (DeepSeek-R1); senior radiologists from 77.00% to 87.50% and 92.25%, respectively (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). Patient-level agreement increased from 41.0% to 78.8% (junior) and from 59.8% to 87.8% (senior) with DeepSeek-R1. Agreement increased (quadratic-weighted κ: 0.231 without AI vs 0.775 with DeepSeek-R1). In standalone evaluation, criteria-guided prompting improved Qwen3-8B agreement from 38.91% to 81.52% (95% CI: 78.87-84.06%), remaining 5.89 percentage points below DeepSeek-R1 (87.41%; 95% CI: 85.10-89.61%).
CONCLUSION: In this report-based classification setting, large language model assistance improved radiologists' agreement with the text-based reference standard, with larger gains in junior radiologists. When prompts explicitly encoded AHA criteria, an 8B local candidate model performed well, supporting its potential use as a standardization aid for text-based workflows.
KEY POINTS: Question Report-based modified AHA classification of carotid plaques is experience-dependent and difficult to standardize, as mapping multi-sequence imaging findings to classification conclusions imposes substantial cognitive load. Findings Large language model assistance improved agreement with a text-based reference standard and raised inter-reader consistency (weighted κ 0.231-0.775), narrowing the junior-senior gap. Critical relevance statement Embedding explicit AHA criteria in the prompt let an 8B model approach 671B-model agreement (38.91-81.52%), supporting standardized text-based workflows without fine-tuning.

Title: Higher TIGIT expression in the intraperitoneal immune microenvironment is associated with shorter progression-free survival in patients with gastric cancer with peritoneal metastasis treated with intraperitoneal paclitaxel.
Journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Gastric cancer with peritoneal metastasis has a poor prognosis. This exploratory study evaluated whether immune checkpoint molecules in the intraperitoneal immune microenvironment are associated with clinical outcomes during intraperitoneal paclitaxel (ipPTX)-based combination chemotherapy.
METHODS: Twenty-nine previously untreated patients with gastric cancer and macroscopic peritoneal metastasis who underwent staging laparoscopy and received ipPTX-based combination chemotherapy were retrospectively analyzed. Lymphocyte subsets in peritoneal lavage fluid were evaluated by flow cytometry. TIGIT, TIM-3, and LAG-3 expression was assessed in cell block specimens prepared from peritoneal lavage fluid by immunohistochemistry. Biomarker analyses were exploratory. Immune-related markers were analyzed primarily as continuous variables, and multivariable progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) models were restricted to TIGIT and baseline Peritoneal Carcinomatosis Index (PCI) using Firth's penalized Cox regression.
RESULTS: Median PFS and OS were 10.6 and 17.2 months, respectively. Among 27 patients evaluable for TIGIT, higher TIGIT expression was associated with shorter PFS in a continuous-variable Cox model (hazard ratio [HR] per 10-percentage-point increase, 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.12-2.08; p = 0.008). After adjustment for baseline PCI, the association remained (HR, 1.48; 95% CI 1.04-2.10; p =0.030). TIM-3 did not show a clear association with survival outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher TIGIT expression in the intraperitoneal immune microenvironment was associated with shorter PFS in this small exploratory cohort receiving ipPTX-based combination chemotherapy.

Title: Anticoagulation in Mechanical Circulatory Support: Contemporary Challenges and Future Directions in Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy.
Abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) is increasingly used in patients with cardiogenic shock, advanced heart failure, and severe respiratory failure; however, anticoagulation management remains challenging due to the competing risks of thrombosis, bleeding, hemolysis, and device dysfunction. In this review, we synthesize contemporary evidence on anticoagulant selection, monitoring strategies, and device-specific management across major MCS platforms, including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, temporary ventricular assist devices, Impella devices, and durable left ventricular assist devices. Unfractionated heparin remains the cornerstone anticoagulant across most MCS platforms, while anti-factor Xa-guided monitoring is increasingly incorporated into clinical practice in many centers alongside activated partial thromboplastin time and other monitoring modalities. Direct thrombin inhibitors represent important alternatives, particularly for patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or heparin resistance. Recent advances include bicarbonate-based purge strategies for Impella support and evolving antithrombotic approaches in HeartMate 3 recipients, introduced by the ARIES-HM3 trial. Emerging investigational strategies, including direct oral anticoagulants, factor XI/XII inhibition, and precision anticoagulation approaches, show promise for improving hemocompatibility; however, current evidence remains limited, and further prospective studies are required before these strategies can be routinely adopted. Overall, contemporary evidence supports an individualized approach to anticoagulation based on device characteristics, patient-specific risk profiles, and current guideline recommendations, while highlighting important knowledge gaps that warrant further high-quality prospective investigation.

Title: Joint association of physical activity and sedentary time with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among advanced CKM syndrome participants, insights from NHANES 2007-2018.
Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents the interconnection of metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease, with advanced stages associated with high mortality. However, the associations of leisure-time physical activity (PA) and sedentary time with mortality in participants with advanced CKM syndrome remain unclear. This study conducted a prospective cohort study using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2018. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses, and subgroup analyses were applied to examine the independent and joint associations of leisure-time PA and sedentary time with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among participants with advanced CKM syndrome. Among advanced CKM participants, physical inactivity was associated with higher risks of all-cause (HR = 2.43, 95% CI: 1.98-2.97, P < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 2.62, 95% CI: 1.79-3.82, P < 0.001). Compared with < 4 h/day, sedentary time > 8 h/day was independently linked to elevated risks of all-cause (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.33-2.19, P < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.34-3.38, P = 0.005). Joint analyses showed that the group characterized by physical inactivity combined with ≥ 6 h/day sedentary time was associated with the highest risk of all-cause (HR = 2.77, 95% CI: 2.16-3.56, P < 0.001) and cardiovascular mortality (HR = 3.39, 95% CI: 2.13-5.40, P < 0.001). These associations were further supported by RCS analyses and sensitivity analyses. The findings underscore the potential survival advantages associated with enhancing physical activity and reducing sedentary behavior in this high-risk population.

Title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
Abstract: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

Title: Are we Adhering to Guidelines for Follow-up Imaging in Neonates with Simple Congenital Heart Defects? What are the Healthcare Costs of Non-adherence?
Abstract: Simple congenital heart defects (CHDs) are frequently identified via neonatal echocardiograms ("echos"). In 2020, the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology issued guidelines for follow-up imaging of CHDs. In this retrospective study, we evaluated adherence to these guidelines at an academic health center in Southeastern Ontario. The cohort included neonates who had one or more simple CHDs diagnosed in the first 30 days of life between April 1, 2020, and March 31, 2024. We reviewed electronic medical records up to September 30, 2025 to examine (a) rates of non-adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up imaging; (b) factors that may contribute to non-adherence; and (c) the costs of excessive imaging. Among 248 patients, 376 echos were performed over the study period. Adherence status could be determined for 320. Follow-up for 39.7% of echos did not adhere to the guidelines, primarily because repeat echos were performed earlier than recommended. Non-adherence was substantially higher for lesions requiring surveillance imaging, as per guidelines, compared with lesions where follow-up imaging is not recommended or findings were normal (91.9% vs. 12.0%; OR = 83.4, 95% CI: 37.5-185.5). The pediatric cardiologist's recommendation was documented for 74.5% of echos, but only 48.9% of recommendations aligned with the guidelines. Non-adherence was higher when recommendations were not documented or deviated from the guidelines. Sixty-two echos were deemed excessive, corresponding to $13,339 in extra imaging costs. The high rate of non-adherence to guideline-recommended follow-up imaging for simple CHDs highlights an opportunity to reduce unnecessary healthcare costs through consistent documentation of guideline-aligned follow-up recommendations by pediatric cardiologists.

Title: Comparison of Feeding, Nutritional, and Procedural Outcomes in Infants with Ductal-Dependent Pulmonary Blood Flow Undergoing Surgical Systemic-to-Pulmonary Artery Shunt Versus Ductal Stenting.
Abstract: Ductal stenting and surgical systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunting (surgical shunt) are alternative strategies to establish pulmonary blood flow in infants with ductal-dependent circulation. The impact of palliation strategy on feeding, nutrition, and neurodevelopment remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 100 infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow (2017-2024) undergoing surgical shunt (n = 57) or ductal stenting (n = 43). Outcomes included feeding, nutrition, hospital course, and neurodevelopment. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors associated with gastrostomy tube (GT) placement. Baseline demographics were similar except for cardiac anatomy. Ductal stent patients reached target enteral feeds post-procedurally sooner (3 vs. 6 days, p < 0.001), had higher discharge weight-for-age z-scores (- 1.30 vs. -1.98, p = 0.02), and smaller declines in growth during hospitalization (p = 0.007). GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting (26% vs. 51%, p = 0.011), but palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.14-1.24, p = 0.12). Oral feeding or breastfeeding within 5 days following palliation was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement (OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.81, p = 0.03). Ductal stent patients also had shorter mechanical ventilation and ICU stays and required less vasoactive-inotropic support. Total hospital length of stay, need for reintervention, suspected or diagnosed necrotizing enterocolitis, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups. Ductal stenting was associated with improved early post-procedural recovery, faster feeding progression, and better preservation of growth compared with surgical shunt palliation. Although GT placement was less frequent following ductal stenting in unadjusted analysis, palliation strategy was not independently associated with GT placement after adjustment. Early post-procedural oral feeding was independently associated with lower odds of GT placement but may also reflect feeding readiness and clinical recovery.

Title: Transplantation for Congenital Heart Disease in Children-A Quest to Do Better.
Abstract: Children with congenital heart disease (CHD) represent the largest group of pediatric heart transplant recipients but experience lower graft survival than those transplanted for cardiomyopathy. We evaluated post-transplant outcomes among CHD recipients at the Hospital for Sick Children (HSC) and identified predictors of graft loss. Pediatric patients (< 17 years) undergoing heart transplantation for CHD between 1993 and 2023 were analyzed using the Pediatric Heart Transplant Society registry. Outcomes of CHD recipients at HSC (CHD HSC) were compared with cardiomyopathy HSC recipients, CHD recipients at other centers (CHD Non-HSC), and a propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort adjusting for pre- and peri-transplant risk factors. Kaplan-Meier survival and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Among 4,362 pediatric CHD transplant recipients, 152 underwent transplantation at HSC. Freedom from graft loss for CHD HSC at 5, 10, and 15 years was 71.8%, 63.0%, and 58.4%, lower than in Cardiomyopathy HSC recipients (p < 0.0001), but similar to CHD Non-HSC (p = 0.6043). Survival remained comparable in the PSM cohort (n = 140, p = 0.4599). Conditional survival beyond 1 year was similar between groups, suggesting early mortality drives differences. CHD HSC recipients demonstrated longer freedom from CAV (p = 0.0041) and infection (p = 0.0335). Predictors of graft loss included pre-transplant ECMO (HR 3.11), ICU admission (HR 2.39), PRA > 10% (HR 2.49), African American/Black race/ethnicity (HR 2.71), and longer waitlist duration (HR 1.06). Graft survival in CHD recipients at HSC remains lower than in cardiomyopathy recipients but comparable internationally. Optimizing pre-transplant care, sensitization management, and equity-focused interventions may enhance outcomes.

Title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
Abstract: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

Title: Retinal and choroidal microvascular changes in hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis: a comparative OCT and OCTA study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate retinal and choroidal structural and microvascular parameters using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) in patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD) and peritoneal dialysis (PD). Furthermore, it aimed to compare short-term dialysis-associated ocular changes between the two dialysis modalities.
METHODS: This prospective observational study encompassed 84 eyes from 46 patients undergoing either HD or PD. Ocular measurements were conducted at two time points according to the dialysis modality. Measurements for HD patients were taken before and after dialysis, whereas for PD patients, measurements were performed after dialysate drainage and following refilling. Comprehensive ophthalmologic assessments and OCT/OCTA imaging were performed. Statistical analyses were used to compare pre- and post-dialysis measurements and changes between the HD and PD groups.
RESULTS: CMT significantly increased after dialysis, whereas subfoveal choroidal thickness significantly decreased. Systolic and diastolic blood pressures also decreased significantly. No significant changes were observed in OCTA-derived retinal microvascular parameters, including vessel density and FAZ parameters. A significant difference in ΔCMT was observed between the HD and PD groups (p = 0.002). Correlation analysis showed a moderate negative correlation between ΔCMT and the change in systolic blood pressure and a moderate positive correlation between ΔCMT and dialysis session duration.
CONCLUSION: Most OCTA-derived retinal microvascular parameters remained stable following dialysis, whereas small but statistically significant structural changes were observed in CMT and subfoveal choroidal thickness. The magnitude of short-term CMT change differed between HD and PD; however, the mechanism underlying this difference remains uncertain. OCT and OCTA may serve as useful non-invasive tools for evaluating ocular structural and microvascular changes in patients with ESRD undergoing dialysis.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Tenecteplase, alteplase, and endovascular thrombectomy in extended-window acute ischemic stroke with intracranial large-vessel occlusion: a Bayesian network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The comparative effects of intravenous thrombolytic agents, endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), and bridging therapy in imaging-selected patients with acute ischemic stroke treated beyond 4.5 hours remain uncertain. We compared these strategies while distinguishing confirmed large-vessel occlusion (LVO) evidence from broader mixed populations.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for randomized trials evaluating reperfusion treatments administered 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset or last known well. The primary network included trials requiring confirmed intracranial LVO or basilar artery occlusion (BAO). An anterior-circulation LVO network and an all-available network were examined as sensitivity and exploratory analyses. Bayesian random-effects consistency models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The primary outcome was functional independence, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 at 90 days.
RESULTS: Fifteen randomized trials were included, of which 8 contributed to the primary confirmed LVO/BAO network. Compared with placebo or best medical care, EVT significantly improved functional independence (OR, 2.93 [95% CrI, 1.40-6.53]) and excellent functional outcome, defined as mRS 0 to 1 (OR, 2.22 [95% CrI, 1.30-4.11]), reduced 90-day mortality (OR, 0.71 [95% CrI, 0.50-0.98]), and increased trial-defined recanalization or reperfusion at approximately 24 hours (OR, 5.27 [95% CrI, 1.83-16.04]); sICH was also increased (OR, 2.65 [95% CrI, 1.28-5.81]). Compared with EVT, tenecteplase plus EVT showed numerically favorable but statistically inconclusive estimates for functional independence (OR, 1.10 [95% CrI, 0.34-3.52]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.16 [95% CrI, 0.52-2.64]). Direct pairwise analyses of 2 trials were similarly inconclusive. Tenecteplase alone did not show clear differences from placebo or best medical care. Findings were directionally consistent in the anterior-circulation sensitivity and all-available exploratory networks.
CONCLUSIONS: Among imaging-selected patients with confirmed intracranial LVO or BAO treated 4.5 to 24 hours after onset or last known well, EVT had the most consistent evidence of benefit versus placebo or best medical care. Tenecteplase plus EVT showed favorable but imprecise estimates, and neither network nor direct pairwise analyses established superiority over EVT alone. The incremental benefit of bridging tenecteplase remains uncertain.

Title: Evolving phenotype of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: a 15-year population-based comparison.
Abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Our aim was to describe the phenotype at diagnosis and the early therapeutic profile of newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes across two periods spanning approximately 15 years within the same integrated healthcare system.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health record data from Clalit Health Services (Haifa & Western Galilee, Israel). Adults with incident type 2 diabetes in 2005-2008 (period 1: n=80,201) were compared with those diagnosed in 2020-2023 (period 2: n=101,392).
