Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.

Title: Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease.
METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty.
RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

Title: Combined Associations of Glycoprotein Acetylation With Lipoprotein (a) and hs-CRP (High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein) on Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in MESA.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Higher plasma glycoprotein acetylation (GlycA) concentrations are associated with an increased risk for incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). We investigated the combined associations of GlycA with lipoprotein (a) (Lp[a]) and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) with incident CVD.
METHODS: We followed 6676 MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) participants, aged 45 to 84 years, without baseline CVD. Lp(a), GlycA, and hs-CRP were evaluated categorically using standard cut points (Lp[a]: 50 mg/dL; GlycA: 400 μmol/L; hs-CRP: 2 mg/L). We used multivariable-adjusted Cox hazards models to evaluate individual and combined associations of these 3 biomarkers with incident CVD, coronary heart disease, and stroke.
RESULTS: Compared with those with low GlycA and low Lp(a) levels, an increase in both incident CVD and coronary heart disease risk was observed for those participants with high levels of either or both of these biomarkers. Risk was highest for those with both high GlycA and high Lp(a) levels (CVD hazard ratio [HR]=1.55 [95% CI: 1.15-2.10) and coronary heart disease (HR=1.92 [95% CI, 1.33-2.77). A similar pattern was not observed for individuals with high levels of both GlycA and hs-CRP. Compared with participants with low levels of GlycA, Lp(a), and hs-CRP, those with high levels of all 3 biomarkers had a 1.98-fold higher CVD risk (95% CI, 1.39-2.82), a 2.23-fold higher coronary heart disease risk (95% CI, 1.45-3.44), and a 2.51-fold higher stroke risk (95% CI, 1.24-5.08).
CONCLUSIONS: Routine assessment of GlycA in addition to Lp(a) and hs-CRP may help to identify individuals at particularly increased CVD risk who may benefit from more aggressive preventive therapies.

Title: Comparison of Unfractionated Heparin and Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin in Acute Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Subanalysis of the CLOT-VENUS Registry.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal anticoagulation in acute cerebral vein thrombosis remains uncertain. We compared unfractionated heparin (UFH) and enoxaparin, and identified predictors of functional recovery and UFH responsiveness.
METHODS: This retrospective 2-center study from the multicenter international CLOT-VENUS (Collaboration on Cerebral Venous Thrombosis) registry included adults with acute cerebral vein thrombosis treated with UFH or enoxaparin (2004-2024). Baseline clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected. UFH response was measured via a composite responsiveness index (Unfractionated Heparin Composite Response Index) based on partial thromboplastin time. The primary outcome was 6-month functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]), and secondary outcomes included discharge mRS and death.
RESULTS: Among 359 patients (median age, 40 [interquartile range, 28-54] years; 68.5% women), 220 (61.3%) received UFH and 139 (38.7%) enoxaparin. Only 64% of partial thromboplastin time values fell within the therapeutic range. UFH was associated with worse outcomes at discharge (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.89; mRS score, 2-6: adjusted odds ratio, 1.90; ordinal mRS score, adjusted odds ratio, 1.56) and at 6 months (mRS score, 3-6: adjusted odds ratio, 2.63). Poor recovery was independently linked to the UFH composite responsiveness index and frequent infusion adjustments. Notably, in the sensitivity analysis limited to patients on UFH with ≥50%, ≥67%, and ≥79% therapeutic partial thromboplastin time values, the outcome differences diminished. Age was independently associated with UFH responsiveness, and female sex, body mass index, and NLR with the number of UFH infusion-rate adjustments.
CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with UFH was associated with worse clinical outcomes compared with enoxaparin, largely attributable to suboptimal and inconsistent anticoagulation. However, when UFH achieves consistent therapeutic levels, the outcomes are comparable. Early predictors may help guide individualized anticoagulation strategies.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

Title: Early Introduction and Prolonged Full-Dose Anakinra Reduce Recurrence Risk After Discontinuation in Recurrent Pericarditis: An International Multicenter Cohort.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anakinra is effective in recurrent pericarditis, yet optimal treatment duration and strategies for safe drug discontinuation remain uncertain. Identifying predictors of sustained remission after discontinuation is important for clinical management.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 185 consecutive adult patients with corticosteroid-dependent and colchicine-resistant refractory recurrent pericarditis across 16 international referral centers, who permanently discontinued therapy after clinical remission. The primary end point was pericarditis recurrence after drug discontinuation. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify demographic, clinical, and therapeutic predictors of postdiscontinuation relapse.
RESULTS: Among 185 patients who discontinued anakinra (58.4% women, mean age 50.4±17.8 years, 77% idiopathic cause), treatment was initiated a median of 10 months (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-19.5) after the first episode and continued at 100 mg/d for a median of 6 months (IQR, 4-12). Over a median follow-up of 7.2 months (IQR, 1.5-23.3) after discontinuation, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 2.1 months (IQR, 0.7-8.5). Initiation within 12 months from the first pericarditis episode and maintenance of full-dose therapy (100 mg/d) for ≥6 months were independently associated with lower recurrence risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.18-0.66]; P=0.001 and HR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-0.86]; P=0.017; respectively).
CONCLUSIONS: Early initiation of anakinra and maintenance of full-dose therapy for at least 6 months are associated with a significantly lower risk of relapse after discontinuation and may inform treatment duration and discontinuation strategies in recurrent pericarditis.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
Journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty.
METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models.
RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05).
CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

Title: Hypertension as a Metabolic Disease: New-Onset Diabetes in the Korean Hypertension Cohort.
Association of Poor Adherence to Guideline-Directed Medical Treatment With Adverse Events Including Fatal Arrhythmia in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Nationwide Cohort Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Poor adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) correlates with increased risks of mortality and hospitalization. Whether it is associated with life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias (VA) remains unclear. We assessed GDMT adherence levels and clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF.
METHODS: Using the National Health Insurance Service database, patients who underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator or cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator implantation between 2008 to 2020 for primary prevention were included. Those with sustained ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation/flutter, or aborted sudden cardiac death were excluded. Adherence to renin-angiotensin system blockers (RASB), beta blockers (BB), and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) was assessed using the weighted proportion of days covered method. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and life-threatening VA.
RESULTS: Among 3,780 patients, prescription rates were 87.5% for RASB, 89.7% for BB, and 74.2% for MRA. Poor adherence was associated with an increased risk of the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR], 1.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.31-1.82) and all-cause mortality (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.52-2.20) compared with optimal adherence. These associations were more pronounced in ischemic heart failure (HF). Although crude VA event rates were numerically higher with lower adherence, these associations were insignificant after covariate adjustment, regardless of HF etiology.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower GDMT adherence was independently associated with increased mortality despite device therapy, particularly in ischemic HF. Although its relationship with arrhythmic outcomes was unclear, sustained adherence remains important and supports targeted interventions to enhance treatment continuity.

Title: Neonatal and 18-24-Month Growth and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Very Low Birth Weight Infants With Severe Congenital Heart Disease: A Korean Neonatal Network Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Severe congenital heart disease (CHD) in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants poses substantial risks, yet contemporary national data remain limited. This study evaluated the prevalence, lesion spectrum, and neonatal and 18-24-month outcomes of VLBW infants with severe CHD in South Korea.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cohort study using the Korean Neonatal Network registry (2013-2021). Severe CHD was defined as a structural defect requiring surgical or catheter-based intervention within the first year of life and was categorized by physiological lesion type. Neonatal mortality, mortality before neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) discharge, major neonatal morbidities, and growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 18-24 months' corrected age were compared between infants with and without severe CHD.
RESULTS: Among 15,145 VLBW infants, 147 (1.0%) had severe CHD. Infants with severe CHD had higher neonatal mortality within 28 days (27.2% vs. 9.3%; adjusted odds ratio [OR], 3.37; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.26-5.04) and mortality before NICU discharge (35.4% vs. 10.6%; adjusted OR, 5.95; 95% CI, 3.94-9.00) than those without severe CHD. Pulmonary hypertension, moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and necrotizing enterocolitis (stage ≥2) were more frequent in the severe CHD group. At 18-24 months, severe CHD was associated with higher rates of growth failure and neurodevelopmental impairment (34.1% vs. 20.0%; OR, 2.07, 95% CI, 1.32-3.24).
CONCLUSIONS: Severe CHD occurred in ~1% of VLBW infants and was associated with markedly higher mortality, greater neonatal morbidity, and increased risks of impaired growth and neurodevelopment at 18-24 months' corrected age.

Title: Mid-Term Outcomes of Endovascular Aneurysm Repair With the INCRAFT Stent Graft System: Retrospective Combined Korean Multi-Center and Single-Center Registry Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUNDS AND OBJECTIVES: Endovascular aneurysm repair is widely used for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Although short-term outcomes are favorable, concerns persist regarding long-term durability, particularly due to higher rates of secondary reintervention. This study aimed to evaluate the mid-term clinical outcomes of the ultra-low-profile INCRAFT stent-graft system.
METHODS: We analyzed 146 patients treated with the INCRAFT stent-graft system using a combined Korean multicenter prospective and single-center retrospective registry. Clinical follow-up was performed until the last clinical contact through electronic medical records, and imaging follow-up with computed tomography or ultrasonography was performed up to 3 years.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 44 months, there were no cases of aneurysm-related death or aneurysm rupture. At 3-year follow-up, sac shrinkage was observed in 41.5%, whereas sac enlargement was noted in 9.6%. Endoleaks were observed in 24.5% at 3 years. Type II endoleak was the most frequent endoleak type and cause of reintervention. Reinterventions were required in 17.1% (n=25), predominantly due to endoleaks (9.6%) and limb-related complications (6.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: In Korean patients with AAA, the INCRAFT stent-graft system demonstrated favorable mid-term outcomes, with low rates of aneurysm-related mortality, acceptable reintervention rates, and stable aneurysm sac behavior.

Title: Prophylactic Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Standard Wound Care Among Lower Extremity Amputations: A Meta-Analysis.
Journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
Abstract: Prophylactic closed incisional negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce postoperative wound complications following lower extremity amputation in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether closed incisional NPWT reduces wound complications compared with standard wound care (SWC) in this high-risk vasculopathic population. A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2025 using predefined search strings. Six studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models as the primary analysis to account for anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Leave-one-out analyses and an analysis excluding the study in which NPWT was delivered as part of a multifaceted care bundle were performed to assess robustness. A total of 893 patients were included, including 408 in the closed incisional NPWT group and 485 in the SWC group. Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) (OR = 0.370; 95% CI = 0.143-0.957; P = .044) and wound dehiscence (OR = 0.224; 95% CI = 0.125-0.401; P = .008). Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative SSI and wound dehiscence following lower extremity amputation in patients with PAD. Because the evidence is predominantly observational and prediction intervals included the null value, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered randomized trials.

Title: Thoracic Pathologies Requiring Surgical or Interventional Management in Solid-Organ Transplant Recipients.
Journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Thoracic pathologies are important causes of morbidity in solid-organ transplant recipients because of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-related complications, and diverse underlying etiologies. We aimed to evaluate thoracic pathologies requiring surgical or interventional management after solid-organ transplantation, present our clinical outcomes, and propose an anatomical management framework for these complex conditions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary referral center of solid-organ transplant recipients who underwent surgical or interventional treatment for thoracic pathologies between 2010 and 2025. Patients who were managed conservatively or patients who had incomplete clinical data were excluded. Demographic characteristics, transplant-related variables, thoracic pathology type, surgical or interventional procedures, histopathological findings, postoperative complications, and clinical outcomes were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Twenty-one transplant recipients underwent 28 thoracic interventions during the study period. The cohort included 12 liver, 8 kidney, and 1 heart transplant recipient, with a mean age of 42.0 ± 22.2 years; 66.7% were male. Thoracic pathologies involved pleural, parenchymal, and mediastinal compartments and required individualized management using tube thoracostomy, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, thoracotomy, or mediastinoscopy. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated a broad spectrum of infectious, inflammatory, and malignant diseases, including aspergilloma, tuberculosis, primary lung carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis, inflammatory pseudotumor, and polymorphic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease. Postoperative complications occurred in 2 patients (9.5% ). One patient required 2 subsequent thoracotomies for prolonged air leak caused by a parenchymal fistula and postoperative hemothorax, whereas another underwent rethoracotomy for recurrent hemorrhage after initial surgical treatment of hemothorax.
CONCLUSIONS: Thoracic pathologies following solid-organ transplant comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions requiring individualized multidisciplinary management. Surgical and interventional procedures play a pivotal role in both establishing definitive diagnoses and providing effective treatment. Early recognition, careful patient selection, and pathology-specific management strategies may improve clinical outcomes in this complex and high-risk population.

Title: Etiologies and Independent Risk Architecture of 7-Day Graft Loss in Adult Liver Transplantation: A National Registry Analysis.
Journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Seven -day graft loss (first postoperative week graft failure or recipient death ) has not been systematically characterized at a national scale in adult liver transplantation. We identified etiologies and independent predictors of 7 -day graft loss, primary nonfunction, and 7 -day posttransplant death in adult deceased donor liver transplant recipients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 54 646 adult deceased donor liver transplant recipients (Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network, 2015 -2024 )and evaluated etiologies and independent predictors of 7 -day graft loss, primary nonfunction, and 7 -day posttransplant death using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 1442 events of 7 -day graft loss (2.6 % ), primary nonfunction predominated (43.6 % ), followed by graft thrombosis (10.3 % ) and infection (3.8 % ). Cardiovascular failure (42.6 % ) was the leading cause of 7 -day death. Retransplant (odds ratio 3.72; P < .001 ), Status 1 (odds ratio 2.24; P < .001 ), donation after circulatory death (odds ratio 1.82; P < .001 ), dialysis dependence (odds ratio 1.79; P <.001 ), and Black recipient race (odds ratio 1.74; P < .001 ) independently predicted 7 -day graft loss. Male recipient sex was protective (odds ratio 0.86; P = .01 ). Each additional hour of cold ischemia time increased 7 -day graft loss odds by 10 % (odds ratio 1.10; P < .001 ). The primary nonfunction model identified Hispanic (odds ratio 1.27; P = .03 ) and Asian (odds ratio 1.60; P = .02 ) recipient race as additional predictors, with 34 % lower odds from 2020 onward (odds ratio 0.66; P < .001 ), coincident with acuity circle allocation and expanded machine perfusion adoption. The 7 -day death model added recipient age ≥60 years (odds ratio 1.58; P < .001 ) and elevated Model for End -Stage Liver Disease score (odds ratio 1.01; P = .003 ) as independent contributors.
CONCLUSIONS: Every predictor is ascertainable before transplant, supporting risk stratification during organ offers, informed donor -recipient matching, and perioperative optimization to reduce early graft loss.

Title: Sequential Kidney-First Retrieval and Early Graft Outcomes in Deceased Donor Kidney Transplantation: A Paired-Donor Comparative Cohort Study.
Journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Prolonged cold ischemia is a principal modifiable determinant of delayed graft function after deceased donor kidney transplant. In conventional multiorgan procurement, kidneys are removed last, prolonging ischemic exposure, a problem magnified in resource-constrained programs. We assessed whether retrieving 1 kidney first, from a heart -beating donor before aortic cross -clamping, improves early graft outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective paired-donor cohort study included 88 adult recipients of kidneys from 44 brain dead donors at collaborating centers in central India between January 2018 and December 2024. Group 1 (n = 44 ) received kidney retrieved first, before aortic clamping; group 2 (n = 44 ) received kidney retrieved last, after procurement of thoracic and remaining abdominal organs. Primary outcomes analyzed were cold ischemia time, delayed graft function, retrieval injury, and posttransplant hemodialysis. Secondary outcomes were first -hour urine output, day 8 serum creatinine, complications, graft loss, and mortality. We used multivariable logistic regression analyses to identify predictors of graft dysfunction.
RESULTS: Cold ischemia time was shorter in group 1 than in group 2 (78.4 ± 48.37 vs 299.4 ± 108.65 min; P <.001 ). Group 1 recipients had higher first -hour urine output (374.2 ± 208.62 vs 186.1 ± 124.92 mL;P < .001 ), lower day 8 serum creatinine (1.3 ± 0.8 vs 3.1 ± 2.83 mg /dL; P < .001 ), lesser delayed graft function requiring hemodialysis (9.1 %vs 36.4 %; P = .002 ), and fewer retrieval injuries and posttransplant complications (6.8% vs 38.6 %; P < .001 ). Comparable advantages were observed among recipients of kidneys from expanded criteria donors. Retrieval of the kidney last independently predicted delayed graft function (adjusted odds ratio 3.92; 95 % CI, 1.41-10.87; P = .008 ).
CONCLUSIONS: Kidney -first retrieval markedly shortened cold ischemia time and improved early graft function and retrieval safety without compromising procurement of other organs and proved to be a pragmatic ischemia -minimization strategy.

Title: Beyond Body Mass Index Cutoffs: Donor Quality and Ischemic Burden Shape Kidney Transplant Outcomes in Recipients With Severe Obesity: An Analysis of the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients Dataset.
Journal: Experimental and clinical transplantation : official journal of the Middle East Society for Organ Transplantation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Obesity remains a common barrier to kidney transplant access, but the clinical relevance of severe obesity depends on donor and ischemic risk.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients aggregate summary tables for deceased donor kidney transplants performed in the United States from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2024, stratified by recipient body mass index (calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) of <35, 35 to 40, and >40. Primary outcomes measured were graft survival and delayed graft function. We compared delayed graft function across body mass index groups using X²test and evaluated graft and patient survival by using Kaplan-Meier estimates from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients.
RESULTS: Among 180,849 transplants (131,379 donation after brain death recipients and 49,470 donation after circulatory death recipients), delayed graft function increased stepwise across the body mass index groups (29.3%, 37.8%, and 42.4%; P < .001). Compared with body mass index <35, the 35 to 40 (odds ratio 1.46; 95% CI, 1.42-1.51) and >40 (odds ratio 1.77; 95% CI, 1.65-1.90) body mass index groups were associated with higher odds of delayed graft function. In donation after brain death recipients, 5-year graft survival declined from 77.51% to 74.33% and to 70.03% across ascending body mass index strata. Lower graft survival with higher body mass index persisted across Kidney Donor Profile Index, donor age, and cold ischemia time.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher recipient body mass index was associated with substantially increased risk of delayed graft function and decreased graft survival after deceased donor kidney transplant. The adverse association appeared strongest when obesity coexisted with less favorable donor or ischemic characteristics, sup-porting individualized donor-recipient risk stratification rather than stand-alone body mass index exclusion thresholds.

Title: Association between late-life blood pressure and incident dementia in older men: The Kuakini Honolulu-Asia aging study.
Abstract: BackgroundThe relationship between late-life blood pressure and incident dementia (including Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia) remains controversial.ObjectiveTo examine whether late-life blood pressure is associated with incidence of dementia.MethodsWe analyzed 2649 participants aged 71 to 93 years without prevalent dementia at baseline in a prospective cohort of Japanese-American men (the Kuakini Honolulu Heart Program). Diagnosis of dementia was conducted based on standardized protocols and participants were followed for up to 20 years. Cox proportional hazards models were applied to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for incident dementia across blood pressure categories, adjusting for demographic, medical, lifestyle, and genetic factors.ResultsDuring follow-up, 716 cases of incident dementia were identified (519 cases of Alzheimer's disease and 88 cases of vascular dementia). After adjustment, high late-life systolic blood pressure (≥160 mmHg) was associated with a lower risk of Alzheimer's disease [HR 0.72 (95% confidence interval: 0.56-0.93)] and a higher risk of vascular dementia [HR 1.95 (95% confidence interval: 1.03-3.68)] compared to the reference (120 to <140 mmHg) group. The protective effect of high late-life systolic blood pressure (≥160 mmHg) on Alzheimer's disease was seen only in participants with the protective version of the FOXO3 genotype. No significant associations were found between diastolic blood pressure and incidence of dementia.ConclusionsHigh late-life systolic blood pressure was associated with a protective effect against Alzheimer's disease, after adjusting for confounders, including the FOXO3 longevity genotype, and an increased risk of vascular dementia in older men aged over 71 years.

Title: [Functional and anatomical outcomes of various perioperative treatment strategies for diabetic macular edema after cataract phacoemulsification].
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Selecting the optimal perioperative treatment strategy for diabetic macular edema (DME) in patients undergoing cataract phacoemulsification remains an important clinical challenge. The effects of different approaches on changes in morphological OCT biomarkers remain insufficiently studied.
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to compare the functional and anatomical outcomes of three perioperative strategies for DME treatment after cataract phacoemulsification.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 102 patients (102 eyes) with type 2 diabetes mellitus, DME, and cataract. In group 1 (n=42), patients received preoperative anti-VEGF therapy followed by treatment according to the Treat-and-Extend regimen, group 2 (n=29) in addition to the same anti-VEGF regimen underwent intraoperative dexamethasone implantation, and group 3 (n=31) first underwent intraoperative dexamethasone implantation and then received anti-VEGF therapy. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central retinal thickness (CRT), central choroidal thickness (CCT), fluid OCT biomarkers, hyperreflective foci, and the inter-injection interval were assessed.
RESULTS: BCVA improved significantly in all groups by month 12 of follow-up (from 0.22±0.12 to 0.64±0.17; p<0.001). The combined strategy provided the earliest reduction in CRT and CCT, rapid resolution of intraretinal and subretinal fluid, a decrease in the number of hyperreflective foci, and prolongation of the inter-injection interval. With the DEX-first strategy, after a pronounced early effect, by month 6 DME had reactivated with loss of anatomical response.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite comparable functional outcomes at 12 months, the perioperative strategies differed substantially in the speed of achieving and maintaining anatomical response. The combined strategy provided the most favorable trajectory of morphological response and the most effective control of the inflammatory and exudative activity of DME in the early postoperative period.

Title: Structural Evaluation of Retinal and Choroidal Features in Eyes With Primary Microtropia.
Journal: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the structural characteristics of the macula, optic nerve head, and choroid in eyes with primary microtropia using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT).
METHODS: This prospective case-control study included 50 pediatric patients with a diagnosis of primary microtropia. Each participant contributed data from both eyes. Eyes were categorized as microtropic, fellow, or healthy control. All patients underwent comprehensive ophthalmic evaluation, including SD-OCT imaging. Parameters assessed included central macular thickness, total macular volume, regional retinal thickness, peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, subfoveal and regional choroidal thickness, and choroidal vascular index.
RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed among microtropic, fellow, and control eyes in terms of central macular thickness, total macular volume, or peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness (P > .05). Although microtropic eyes showed a mild trend toward increased parafoveal and perifoveal retinal thickness across all quadrants, this variation did not reach statistical significance. Similarly, subfoveal, nasal, and temporal choroidal thickness measurements, as well as choroidal vascularity index, luminal area, stromal area, and total choroidal area, were comparable across all groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Primary microtropia was not associated with measurable retinal or choroidal structural abnormalities on SD-OCT. Although reduced visual acuity was present, the lack of detectable anatomical changes warrants further investigation to determine whether functional impairment in microtropia occurs independently of structural alterations.

Title: Collaborative Technology-Assisted Depression Program for Chronic Disease Patients in Santiago, Chile.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of a collaborative, computer-assisted psycho-educational intervention for managing depression in patients with hypertension and/or diabetes in comparison with usual care in primary care clinics in Santiago, Chile.
METHODS: Adults with moderate-to-severe depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] ≥15) enrolled in the Cardiovascular Health Care Program were recruited. The active arm (n = 180) received an eight-session computer-assisted, psycho-educational program, telephone monitoring, and usual care for chronic diseases, while the control group (n = 179) received usual care for depression and chronic diseases. Outcomes were assessed at 3-, 6-, and 12-month follow-ups, with the primary outcome being depression improvement (50% decrease in PHQ-9 score) at 6 months. Intention-to-treat analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: The active arm showed non-statistically significant reductions in depressive symptoms and improvements in mental health-related quality of life, treatment adherence, and health care utilization compared to the control arm.
CONCLUSIONS: While results did not demonstrate statistical difference within the programs to treat the health problems included in the study, the findings support the use of computer-assisted psychoeducation intervention.
CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: These findings advocate for optimizing current care models by incorporating scalable, evidence-based interventions, such as technology-assisted programs, to address remaining gaps in mental health integration.

Title: Preoperative echocardiographic parameters do not predict early outcomes after arterial switch operation in late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether preoperative echocardiographic parameters can predict early postoperative outcomes after arterial switch operation in late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum.
METHODS: This prospective study examined preoperative demographic characteristics, echocardiographic findings, and left ventricular strain parameters in 35 patients undergoing arterial switch operation for late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. Further, their correlation with postoperative variables, including length of ICU stay, postoperative hospital stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support, and inotropic score, was assessed.
RESULTS: The median age at surgery was 45 days, and the median weight was 3.4 kg. The median interventricular septal thickness was 4.1 mm, and the median left ventricular mass index was 26.4 g/m2. The median average left ventricular strain was -24.19. Thirteen patients required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support. The whole cohort had a median extracorporeal membrane oxygenation duration of 0 days. The median length of ICU stay was 12 days, and the median length of postoperative hospital stay was 17 days. The median inotropic score was 28. There was no case of early mortality. None of the preoperative echocardiographic parameters showed a statistically significant association with postoperative outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative echocardiographic parameters, including left ventricular strain, did not significantly predict early postoperative outcomes after arterial switch operation in patients with late-presenting transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum. Postoperative outcomes in this patient group are likely influenced by multiple preoperative factors rather than a single preoperative echocardiographic parameter.

Title: Predicting prolonged mechanical ventilation in neonates after cardiac surgery: development of a nomogram for risk prediction based on preoperative and intraoperative factors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite improvements in neonatal cardiac surgery, prolonged mechanical ventilation remains a prevalent postoperative complication. This study was designed to build a prolonged mechanical ventilation prediction model based on preoperative and intraoperative factors in neonates (0-28 days) after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on perioperative data of 385 newborns undergoing cardiac surgery at Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital from 2018 to 2024. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was defined as postoperative mechanical ventilation duration >7 days.
RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors, visualised via a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by area under receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified airway anomalies (odds ratio = 2.280, 95% confidence interval 1.217-4.271, P = 0.010), preoperative mechanical ventilation (odds ratio = 2.244, 95% confidence interval 1.283-3.925, P = 0.005), radical surgery (odds ratio = 0.220, 95% confidence interval 0.091-0.533, P < 0.001), intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volumes (odds ratio = 1.529, 95% confidence interval 1.065-2.195, P = 0.021), intraoperative elevated lactate levels (odds ratio = 2.352, 95% confidence interval 1.256-4.403, P = 0.008), and higher vasoactive-inotropic score at the end of surgery (odds ratio = 1.060, 95% confidence interval 1.023-1.199, P = 0.001) as risk factors for prolonged mechanical ventilation. The nomogram achieved an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.784, with robust calibration and clinical utility. Prolonged mechanical ventilation was associated with prolonged hospital stay (median 23 vs. 16 days, P < 0.001) and increased hospital mortality (12.3% vs. 1.1%, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This model accurately stratifies the risks of prolonged mechanical ventilation in neonates after cardiac surgery, potentially guiding postoperative management.

Title: Prediction of 10-Year Incident Hypertension After Pregnancy: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
Journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a model including pregnancy-related factors for the prediction of incident hypertension after pregnancy and to assess the impact of pregnancy-related factors on model performance.
DESIGN: Population-based cohort study.
SETTING: Routine primary care data linked to the data from the Dutch Perinatal Registry and Statistics Netherlands.
POPULATION: Women with a first childbirth at ≥ 24 weeks' gestation between 2007 and 2019 were included and were followed for up to 10 years after childbirth.
METHODS: Two Cox proportional hazards models were developed to estimate the 10-year risk of hypertension. Model 1 included sociodemographic factors and CVD-related factors, while model 2 additionally included pregnancy-related factors.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Ten-year risk of incident hypertension.
RESULTS: We included 28 234 women, of which 639 developed hypertension (cumulative 10-year incidence 3.3%). The C-index of model 1 was 0.659 (95% CI: 0.642-0.684) and increased to 0.772 (95% CI: 0.754-0.796) after the addition of pregnancy-related factors. The C-index difference was 0.113 (95% CI: 0.092-0.132), mostly driven by the inclusion of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Net reclassification improvement was 0.213 (95% CI: 0.159-0.273) for events and 0.001 (95% CI: -0.004 to 0.006) for non-events.
CONCLUSIONS: Our prediction model for hypertension showed good discrimination and calibration after the addition of pregnancy-related factors. This model may help to target cardiovascular risk management for women with a high risk of hypertension after pregnancy in order to improve women's cardiovascular health.

Title: Acute kidney injury in pregnancy is associated with increased risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes: an integrated health system study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-related acute kidney injury (PrAKI) is an uncommon but serious complication associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with limited data in high-resource settings.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 29 586 deliveries at Mayo Clinic hospitals between 2017 and 2022. PrAKI was defined using Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) creatinine criteria. Maternal characteristics, nephrotoxin exposure, clinical interventions, and neonatal outcomes were compared between patients with and without PrAKI.
RESULTS: PrAKI occurred in 341 patients (1.15%). Compared with controls, PrAKI was associated with higher rates of chronic hypertension (28.7% vs 5.2%), cesarean delivery (68.5% vs 35.1%), intensive care unit (ICU) admission (59.1% vs 6.2%), and nephrotoxin exposure (58.7% vs 31.6%) (all P < .0001). Dialysis was required in 7.1% of patients with PrAKI, with 1.17% remaining dependent at discharge and 0.88% at 30 and 90 days; no control patients required dialysis. Neonates of mothers with PrAKI had higher rates of prematurity and neonatal ICU (NICU) admission (48.7% vs 9.8%; P < .0001). Maternal mortality was rare.
CONCLUSIONS: PrAKI is a marker of severe maternal illness and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Although most patients recover kidney function, a subset develop persistent dysfunction. Early identification, cautious use of nephrotoxic medications, and structured postpartum follow-up are essential.

Title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
Abstract:
AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo.
METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers.
RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

Title: Neonatal abstinence syndrome in Norway - a registry study.
Journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Medications and illicit substances taken during pregnancy are transferred to the foetus via the placenta. When the supply ceases after birth, the infant can develop withdrawal symptoms. The aim of the study was to investigate the incidence, neonatal morbidity and regional differences in hospital admissions of infants with neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) in Norway.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: Using the Norwegian Neonatal Network quality registry, we identified all neonates in Norway with a gestational age of ≥ 36 weeks who were discharged from a neonatal unit and diagnosed with NAS during the study period from 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2023. We extracted key register data, including additional diagnoses and length of stay in the neonatal unit.
RESULTS: We identified 621 neonates with NAS over the 12-year period, corresponding to a national incidence of 0.95 per 1,000 liveborn infants with a gestational age of ≥ 36 weeks. The median length of stay in a neonatal unit for all infants included in the study was 6-8 days throughout the study period. However, the hospital stay was ≥ 14 days for 134 infants (22%). A total of 119 infants (19%) had a birth weight below the 10th percentile, defined as small for gestational age. Seven infants (1%) were diagnosed with neonatal seizures. Congenital heart defects were identified in 14 infants (2%).
INTERPRETATION: The incidence of NAS in Norway was lower than reported figures in other Western countries. Consistent with findings in the literature, one in five infants with NAS were small for gestational age.

Title: Predictors of Complications and the Role of Early Revision in Reverse-Flow Posterior Interosseous Artery Flaps: A Multivariable Analysis of 110 Cases.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pedicled reverse-flow posterior interosseous artery (PIA) flap is a reliable option for soft-tissue reconstruction of the hand and wrist. However, the predictors of complications and the impact of early revision surgery have not been adequately evaluated using multivariable analysis. This study aimed to investigate the factors affecting flap survival, complication rates, and outcomes of salvage surgery.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 110 patients who underwent reconstruction with a pedicled reverse PIA flap between 2010 and 2025. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of venous congestion, flap loss, and donor site grafting. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to determine the dimensional thresholds.
RESULTS: The mean patient age was 34.2 years, and the majority of defects were traumatic in etiology (80.9%). Venous congestion occurred in 30 patients (27.3%), whereas total and partial flap loss occurred in five (4.5%) and 15 (13.6%) patients, respectively. On multivariable analysis, flap length was independently associated with venous congestion (OR = 1.45, 95% CI 1.17-1.79; p < 0.001) and flap loss (OR = 1.47, 95% CI 1.17-1.85; p < 0.001). ROC analysis identified a flap length of 9 cm as a practical reference threshold (high specificity, modest sensitivity) for these complications. In a separate donor-site grafting model, flap width > 4 cm was associated with grafting on univariable analysis but became only borderline significant after multivariable adjustment (OR 1.60, 95% CI 0.98-2.60; p = 0.059), while traumatic etiology was independently associated with donor site grafting (OR = 8.00, 95% CI 2.20-29.03). Among patients with venous congestion, early revision was associated with a lower flap loss rate than conservative management (43.75% vs. 92.86%, p = 0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: In reverse-flow PIA flap reconstruction, greater flap length was independently associated with venous congestion and flap loss. Traumatic etiology emerged as an independent predictor of donor-site grafting, an association that has received little prior attention. In patients with venous compromise, early revision was associated with a lower overall flap loss rate, although this observational finding requires confirmation in prospective studies.

Title: Active Helicobacter pylori Infection and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
Journal: Annals of noninvasive electrocardiology : the official journal of the International Society for Holter and Noninvasive Electrocardiology, Inc
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection may promote systemic inflammation and has been proposed as a contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF), but clinical evidence is inconsistent. The aim of the study was to explore whether active H. pylori infection was associated with AF in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included adults from a two-center observational AMI cohort. Active H. pylori infection was assessed during hospitalization using a urea breath test (UBT). AF was defined as AF documented before admission or identified during the index hospitalization. Associations were estimated using logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, center, and smoking. Exploratory multivariable interaction analyses were also performed.
RESULTS: Of 310 enrolled patients, 300 had conclusive H. pylori screening results; 60 (20.0%) were positive. AF was recorded in 4 of 60 H. pylori-positive patients (6.7%) and 30 of 240 H. pylori-negative patients (12.5%). H. pylori positivity was not significantly associated with recorded AF (unadjusted OR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.17-1.41; p = 0.228; adjusted OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.16-1.46; p = 0.235). These estimates refer to pooled AF; only four AF cases occurred among patients testing positive.
CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant association was detected between H. pylori breath-test positivity and pooled documented AF among patients hospitalized with AMI, but a clinically meaningful association cannot be excluded. Larger prospective studies with longitudinal follow-up are needed to clarify whether active H. pylori infection is associated with incident AF after AMI.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

Title: Chios Mastic in Well-Controlled Hypertension: Findings From the HYPER-MASTIC Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Residual cardiovascular risk persists in patients with adequately controlled hypertension, driven partly by inflammation, oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Chios mastic (Pistacia lentiscus var. Chia) has shown antihypertensive, antioxidant and vascular effects in experimental and clinical settings. This trial evaluated whether Chios mastic supplementation confers additional cardiovascular benefits in well-controlled hypertensive individuals. In this double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 106 adults with stable, well-controlled hypertension and variable cardiovascular risk, based on SCORE2, received low-dose Chios mastic (1500 mg/day), high-dose Chios mastic (2800 mg/day) or placebo for 3 months. Primary endpoints were changes in 24-h ambulatory systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Secondary endpoints included vascular function, oxidative stress and proteasome activity in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and red blood cells. Transcriptomic profiling was performed in a predefined high-risk subgroup. Chios mastic supplementation was well tolerated, with high adherence confirmed by dose-dependent increases in plasma masticadienonic and isomasticadienonic acids. No significant between-group differences were observed in 24-h systolic or diastolic blood pressure after the intervention. Oxidative stress markers and proteasome activity remained unchanged across groups. In high-risk participants, mastic supplementation induced distinct transcriptomic changes, particularly in pathways related to endothelial junction organization and vascular integrity. Overall, in adults with well-controlled hypertension and low baseline cardiovascular risk, Chios mastic supplementation did not lower blood pressure over 3 months, likely reflecting a ceiling effect. Transcriptomic findings suggest biologically meaningful vascular effects in individuals with higher residual cardiovascular risk, supporting future investigation in higher-risk populations.

Title: Pediatric Multiorgan Lung Transplantation: Four Decades of National Trends and Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric lung transplantation (LTx) and multiorgan lung transplantation (MOLT) remain uncommon, and national data describing temporal trends and outcomes are limited. We characterized four decades of MOLT in the United States, with particular emphasis on the evolving pediatric experience.
METHODS: We analyzed Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network Standard Transplant Analysis and Research files provided by the United Network for Organ Sharing from 1987 to 2024. The cohort included 54 797 isolated LTx recipients and 1 963 MOLT recipients, classified into mutually exclusive groups of dual-organ lung-heart (n = 1557), lung-liver (n = 216), lung-kidney (n = 154), and other multiorgan configurations (n = 36). Cox regression, Fine-Gray competing-risks, landmark, and interaction analyses evaluated graft-failure associations across four transplant eras and seven age groups.
RESULTS: Pediatric transplant volume declined substantially, comprising 0.8% of isolated LTx procedures in 2020-2024. Lung-heart transplantation decreased from 9.0% of lung-involved procedures before 2000 to 1.8% in 2020-2024, whereas lung-liver and lung-kidney transplantation increased modestly, predominantly among adults. Pretransplant ECMO use increased across cohorts, reaching 27.6% among lung-heart and 27.8% among lung-kidney recipients in 2020-2024. One-year graft survival improved progressively across eras.
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric MOLT has evolved within a changing national lung-transplant landscape characterized by declining pediatric volume, shifting procedural patterns, increasing recipient acuity, and improving early graft outcomes. Continued evaluation is needed as long-term follow-up from recent eras matures.

Title: Investigating Fibrinolysis Resistance in Sepsis Using High-Multiplex Plasma Proteomics: A Statistical Analysis Plan.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy is characterised by consumptive coagulation abnormalities and resistance to fibrinolysis, which is increasingly recognised as a driver of microvascular thrombosis, organ dysfunction and mortality. The molecular determinants of the fibrinolysis-resistant phenotype remain incompletely defined.
OBJECTIVE: To present a pre-specified statistical analysis plan for a plasma proteomic investigation of fibrinolysis resistance in 89 samples collected serially from 32 critically ill patients with sepsis, using the Olink Explore HT platform (approximately 5400 proteins). The plan is designed to characterise protein associations with a validated bedside measure of fibrinolysis resistance, the ratio of tissue plasminogen activator-induced lysis time to fibrin clot amplitude (TPA-LT/FIBA10). The associations will be examined across the fibrinolysis resistance severity continuum and between three ordinal severity grades, and over time within individual patients.
METHODS: The analytic framework combines five complementary approaches: (i) limit-of-detection-based data filtering, (ii) continuous-variable modelling of protein abundance against TPA-LT/FIBA10 using limma-trend regression, (iii) categorical comparison across severity grades using empirical Bayes moderated statistics, (iv) linear mixed-effects modelling of longitudinal intra-patient trajectories and (v) pathway-level enrichment analysis to translate statistical associations into mechanistic hypotheses. A semi-supervised pathway clustering analysis will describe how proteins change by fibrinolysis resistance in eight a priori defined domains.
DISCUSSION: This multi-model design is intended to define genuine biological signals in a high-dimensional dataset while remaining transparent about the exploratory nature of several components. The statistical reasoning behind each method is discussed alongside anticipated limitations.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06680180.

Title: Real-World Invasive Evaluation of Myocardial Bridging: A Multicenter Italian Survey of Interventional Cardiologists' Practices.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial bridging (MB) is increasingly recognized as a potential cause of ischemia through heterogeneous mechanisms, yet real-world management remains heterogeneous. We surveyed interventional cardiologists to describe contemporary MB practice, focusing on functional assessments, perceived value, and barriers to the "full-physiology" approach, and priorities for standardization and research.
AIMS: To characterize contemporary MB management among interventional cardiologists, focusing on physiology approaches, imaging strategies, and perceived barriers to implementation and treatment.
METHODS: An anonymized online survey was conducted among interventional cardiologists from 28 Italian centers. Items covered MB-specific functional assessment strategies, therapies, implementation barriers, operational infrastructure, and research interest.
RESULTS: Ninety-three cardiologists responded (mean age 38.8 ± 8.6 years; 82.8% male). Pressure-based indices were widely used for epicardial CAD, but phenotyping in MB was uncommon: 57.0% performed physiology in < 10% of MB cases, and 19.4% never did. Epicardial MB assessment relied mainly on adenosine-FFR (33.3%) or iFR (31.2%), whereas stress-enhanced protocols were rarely used. Although intracoronary acetylcholine testing was commonly used in general practice (79.6%), only 49.5% of respondents reported using it to assess MB-related coronary spasm, and most did so in only a small proportion of cases. CMD testing in MB was rare (< 10% in 66.7%). Despite this, most respondents (87.1%) endorsed "full-physiology" as useful for mechanism identification and personalized therapy, but cited evidence uncertainty, procedural time, and limited experience as key barriers. Operational readiness was low (dedicated protocols: 26.9%; registries: 39.8%; routine capture: 34.4%). Willingness to join a randomized trial was high (93.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite the widespread availability of invasive functional assessment tools and operators' recognition of their relevance, their use in MB remains limited and heterogeneous, reflecting the lack of evidence-based guidance and underscoring the need for dedicated mechanistic studies and standardized invasive workflows.

Title: Serum vs. Dietary Magnesium and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Saudi Adolescents.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Magnesium (Mg) is an essential micronutrient that participates in more than 300 enzymatic reactions, with well-established functions in glucose and lipid metabolism and cardiovascular health. Although serum Mg is routinely used in clinical practice, circulating concentrations may not accurately represent total body Mg status because of tight physiological regulation. The present study evaluated the associations of serum Mg concentration and dietary Mg intake with cardiometabolic outcomes in a cohort of Saudi adolescents. Methods: This cross-sectional study involved 234 Saudi adolescents (166 girls, 68 boys; mean age 14.8 ± 1.7 years) who were assessed for anthropometrics, biochemical parameters and dietary intake. Hypomagnesemia was classified as serum Mg <0.75 mmol/L, while inadequate dietary Mg intake was based on age- and sex-specific cutoffs for children. Results: Hypomagnesemia was present in 87 participants (37.2%) and was more common among boys than girls (50% vs. 31.9%, p = 0.011). No significant differences in the assessed cardiometabolic measurements were observed across serum Mg tertiles. Absolute dietary Mg intake was strongly correlated with total energy and other dietary intakes and was inversely associated with body mass index. Associations based on absolute dietary Mg intake were attenuated after energy adjustment for overweight/obesity. For elevated triglycerides, the highest vs. lowest tertile of residual-adjusted Mg showed a nominal inverse association in the age- and sex-adjusted model (OR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.17-0.96). However, the corresponding trend did not remain statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. Conclusions: Serum Mg showed limited associations with cardiometabolic outcomes, while associations between dietary Mg and cardiometabolic outcomes were sensitive to energy adjustment and multiple-comparison correction. The inverse association between residual-adjusted Mg and elevated triglycerides should therefore be considered exploratory. These findings highlight potential differences between serum and dietary Mg as indicators of Mg status and underscore the importance of accounting for total energy intake when examining dietary Mg in relation to cardiometabolic health in adolescents.

Title: Association Between Diet Quality and 20-Year Heart Failure Incidence: Findings from the ATTICA Cohort Study (2002-2022).
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Diet quality is a potentially modifiable determinant of heart failure (HF), yet evidence regarding its long-term association with HF incidence remains limited. This study examined the association between baseline diet quality and 20-year incident HF in the population-based ATTICA cohort. Methods: Among 3042 adults free of cardiovascular disease at baseline (2001-2002), HF status was available for 2159 participants in 2022, of whom 241 (11.2%) developed HF. Diet quality, including the relative contributions of healthy and unhealthy food groups, was assessed using the Global Diet Quality Score (GDQS), derived from a validated food-frequency questionnaire. Logistic regression models were sequentially adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, education, physical activity, smoking burden, hypertension, diabetes, and hypercholesterolemia. Results: HF incidence was 20.7%, 5.1%, and 6.6% among participants with low, intermediate, and high diet quality, respectively (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted analysis (n = 1973), better overall diet quality was associated with lower odds of HF (odds ratio [OR] per 1-point increment, 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94-0.99). A greater contribution of healthy foods was also inversely associated with HF (OR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.93-0.98), whereas the unhealthy-food component was not independently associated with the outcome (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.96-1.13). Conclusions: Better diet quality, particularly greater consumption of health-promoting foods, was independently associated with lower 20-year HF incidence in a Mediterranean population.

Title: Ketogenic Dietary Therapies and β-Hydroxybutyrate as Modulators of Mitochondrial Function: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
Abstract: Ketogenic dietary therapies (KDTs) have been used for a century in drug-resistant epilepsy, and β-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), the major ketone body, is recognized as a signaling metabolite. This review examines how KDTs and BHB modulate mitochondrial function and evaluates evidence supporting these mechanisms. BHB is oxidized through D-β-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase 1 and succinyl-CoA:3-oxoacid-CoA transferase and alters redox balance and oxidative phosphorylation. It also inhibits class I histone deacetylases, serves as the substrate for lysine β-hydroxybutyrylation, activates hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 2, and blocks the NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 inflammasome. These pathways influence redox defense, organelle quality, and inflammation. However, ketogenic feeding suppresses mitochondrial one-carbon metabolism and some signaling effects occur only at BHB concentrations exceeding those typically achieved through dietary ketosis. Clinical benefits are best established in drug-resistant epilepsy and appear genotype-dependent in primary mitochondrial disease, with potential benefit in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variant carriers but possible harm in DNA polymerase gamma-related disease and mtDNA deletion myopathy. Outside neurology, human evidence includes a hemodynamic response to infused 3-hydroxybutyrate in heart failure, sustained glycemic improvement in non-randomized diabetes cohorts, and small trials in psychiatric and oncological populations. Most clinical studies have not directly measured mitochondrial outcomes. Proposed mitochondrial mechanisms of KDTs and BHB remain plausible but are not established explanations for clinical benefit. Genotype-stratified trials, ketone exposure assessment, and direct measurement of mitochondrial variables in patients are needed.

Title: Effects of Body-Mass-Scaled Protein and Leucine Supplementation on Body Composition and Cardiometabolic Blood Markers During Weight Loss in Older Men-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Background: Overweight and obesity are burgeoning health epidemics. Diets including alternate-day fasting (ADF) promote weight loss but risk significant muscle loss, posing health implications to seniors at risk of sarcopenia. Leucine, the key muscle protein synthesis (MPS) driver, effectively stimulates MPS with lower calorie intake than protein. However, the effects of body-mass-scaled protein and leucine intakes are unclear. Objectives: To evaluate body-mass-scaled leucine or protein supplementation on body composition, sarcopenic, and cardiometabolic markers in older men during ADF. Methods: Sixty-one older men (BMI ≥ 23.0 kg/m2) underwent 28 days of ADF, randomized across three calorie-matched supplement groups: Control (C: 0.0 g/kg protein, 0.0 g/kg leucine), Leucine (L: 0.0 g/kg protein, 0.08 g/kg leucine), or Protein (P: 0.4 g/kg protein, 0.04 g/kg leucine), consuming three doses on feeding days and one on fasting days. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, sarcopenic metrics, and blood markers (blood pressure, lipid panels, diabetic profiles) were measured. Results: There were no significant interactions (p > 0.05) in body composition, sarcopenic or health outcomes, except for diastolic blood pressure (p = 0.016) and HDL cholesterol (p = 0.013). There were significant main effects of time (p ≤ 0.05) with reductions in all body composition measures (excluding bone mineral density, p = 0.274), systolic blood pressure and lipid profiles (total and LDL cholesterol, total/HDL cholesterol ratio, triglycerides), and improvements in all muscle strength and functional sarcopenic outcomes. Conclusions: Dietary interventions alone that increase leucine and/or protein intake did not result in additional measurable improvements during this four-week intervention on body composition, sarcopenic, and cardiometabolic outcomes during weight loss.

Title: Effects of Blueberry and Collard Greens Dietary Intervention on Metabolic and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Zucker Obese Rats.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Obesity is a global health challenge associated with metabolic and inflammatory health outcomes. Dietary interventions such as phytochemical-rich foods may offer a sustainable and cost-effective approach to improving health outcomes associated with obesity. This study evaluated the effects of diets containing 4% blueberry powder and extracts, and 4% collard greens powder and extracts, and a combination of 2% blueberry and 2% collard greens on metabolic and inflammatory biomarkers in obese Zucker rats. Methods: Fifty-six male rats were randomly assigned to seven treatment groups (n = 8), including five diet treatment groups, an AIN- 93 control group, and an Ozempic® (semaglutide)-treated group. Body weight, feed intake, plasma glucose, lipid profile, and inflammatory biomarkers were assessed following an 8-week dietary intervention. Results: A high mortality rate was observed in the Ozempic® (semaglutide)-treated group, with five out of eight rats dying during the third week of intervention. The semaglutide-treated group showed the greatest reductions in fasting plasma glucose concentrations. Diets supplemented with blueberry and collard greens significantly increased HDL cholesterol and reduced LDL cholesterol concentrations compared with the control group, while also improving selected inflammatory biomarkers. The collard green extract group had the lowest IL-6 concentration (34.65 ± 3.90 pg/mL) compared with the control group (339.57 ± 185.65 pg/mL) (p < 0.05). Conclusions: Overall, blueberries and collard greens consumption improved dyslipidemia and inflammation in obese Zucker rats. These preliminary findings suggest that phytochemical-rich fruits and vegetables may provide a cost-effective dietary strategy for improving metabolic and inflammatory outcomes associated with obesity.

Title: Combined Association of High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein and Vitamin D with Short-Term Functional Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
Abstract: Background/Objectives: Whether high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and vitamin D (Vit D) provide complementary prognostic information for acute ischemic stroke is unclear. We examined the separate and joint associations of serum hsCRP and Vit D levels with short-term functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 192 patients with brain magnetic resonance imaging-confirmed acute ischemic stroke admitted to a single tertiary center. Stroke severity at admission was graded using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale. Physical and cognitive recovery were assessed using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), Manual Function Test (MFT), Korean Mini-Mental State Examination (K-MMSE), and Korean version of the modified Barthel Index, while disability was graded using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at discharge. Results: Among 192 patients stratified into low- (<1.0 mg/L, n = 76), moderate- (1.0-3.0 mg/L, n = 57), and high- (>3.0 mg/L, n = 59) hsCRP groups, serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D fell stepwise as hsCRP rose, and high hsCRP was independently associated with poorer BBS, MFT, K-MMSE, and mRS outcomes. Patients with both high hsCRP and Vit D deficiency (<20 ng/mL) formed the highest-risk group (adjusted odds ratio up to 12.54), with the risk increasing stepwise as the number of adverse markers increased. No significant multiplicative interaction was observed, whereas a significant additive interaction was found only for cognitive impairment. Conclusions: Patients with both elevated hsCRP and Vit D deficiency showed the highest odds of poor short-term outcomes. A simple count of these adverse markers may help identify patients at higher risk after acute ischemic stroke and may help define a subgroup for further evaluation in prospective intervention trials of Vit D supplementation.

Title: Enteral Feeding During Therapeutic Hypothermia for Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy in Neonates: A Multicentre Study from Italy and Belgium.
Abstract: Background: Enteral feeding during therapeutic hypothermia (TH) for hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains heterogeneous across centres because of concerns regarding feeding intolerance and the risk of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). Evidence regarding optimal feeding initiation and advancement remains limited. Methods: We performed a secondary analysis of a multicentre retrospective cohort of infants with HIE treated with TH at two tertiary neonatal intensive care units in Italy and Belgium between 2011 and 2024. We included survivors with complete nutritional data, aware that this restriction, adopted because feeding-related endpoints cannot be assessed in non-survivors, may introduce survivor bias. Feeding practices, enteral feeding progression, feeding tolerance, and gastrointestinal outcomes were evaluated. Results: Of 302 infants in the original cohort, 276 were included. Enteral feeding during TH was administered to 166 infants (60.1%). Enteral feeding volumes remained low during the first three days of life but progressively increased thereafter. Despite inter-center differences in feeding strategies (initiation and advancement), time to full enteral feeding (median 9 days; IQR 7-12) was comparable overall (Italy: median 9 days, IQR 7-12; Belgium: median 10 days, IQR 7-14; p = 0.323). Infants receiving enteral nutrition during TH were observed to achieve full enteral feeding earlier than those not fed during cooling (median 8.0 vs. 12.0 days, p < 0.001) and to have a shorter length of hospital stay (median 11.0 vs. 15.0 days, p < 0.001). Breastfeeding at discharge was also observed more frequently among infants who received enteral nutrition during TH (79.5% vs. 54.5%, p < 0.001). Feeding intolerance occurred in 47 infants (17.0%) and temporary feeding withdrawal in 31 (11.2%). Only three infants (1.1%) developed Bell stage IIA NEC, with no progression to more advanced disease or surgery. NEC was more frequent among infants with Sarnat stage III HIE than among those with stage I-II disease (8.3% vs. 0.4%, p = 0.022). Conclusions: Enteral feeding during TH was feasible, and gastrointestinal complications were uncommon. These findings support the feasibility of cautious enteral feeding during TH. The concentration of NEC events among infants with severe HIE, although based on only three cases, is hypothesis-generating and suggests that future studies should evaluate feeding strategies according to both neurological severity and physiological stability. Whether earlier initiation or faster advancement is beneficial in clinically stable infants cannot be determined from these observational data and should be addressed in prospective studies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Longitudinal Changes in Left Ventricular Structure and Function During a Dietary Weight-Management Trial in Adults with Heart Failure, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity: A Secondary Analysis of Pro-HEART.
Abstract: Background: Obesity is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in heart failure (HF), but changes during dietary weight management are not well described. We examined longitudinal changes in left ventricular (LV) structure and systolic function during a dietary weight-management intervention. Methods: Pro-HEART participants were randomized to high-protein or standard-protein hypocaloric diets. LV end-diastolic dimension (LVEDD), ejection fraction (LVEF), and posterior wall thickness (LVPWT) were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 15 months. Linear mixed-effects models tested time and diet effects. Results: At 15 months, LVEDD data were available for 31 of 92 participants (33.7%). Achieved protein intake was similar between randomized groups. Among 92 participants, LVEDD changed significantly over time (F(2, 51.20) = 7.45, p = 0.001), with model-estimated mean LVEDD decreasing from 59.00 mm at baseline to 54.56 mm at 15 months.
