SCD was assessed in 2020. Logistic regression models were used to examine associations between MDRF categories and SCD.
RESULTS: Survey-weighted responses indicated 8.6% of older adults experienced SCD. Diabetes, hearing impairment, current vision impairment, stable presence of physical inactivity, depression, and current loneliness were associated with increased odds of SCD.
CONCLUSIONS: Both the onset and reduction of psychosocial and sensory MDRFs in mid- and later life have measurable implications for subjective cognitive outcomes in a general population sample. Prevention and reduction of diabetes, sensory loss, physical inactivity, depression, and social isolation represent meaningful targets for supporting cognitive well-being among older adults.

Title: ChatGPT Versus MediSearch: A Comparative Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Platforms for Patient Education in Cardiac Surgery and Cardiac Anesthesia.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the reliability and readability of responses generated by two artificial intelligence (AI) platforms-ChatGPT and MediSearch-to common patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and its anesthetic implications.
DESIGN: Prospective, comparative, cross-sectional evaluation.
SETTING: Single-institution academic study; no direct patient involvement. Questions were sourced from publicly available online data (Google "People Also Ask" feature).
PARTICIPANTS: One hundred unique patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and anesthesia, categorized using the Rothwell classification system (80 fact, 14 policy, 6 value).
INTERVENTIONS: Each question was submitted individually to the free versions of ChatGPT (version 4.0) and MediSearch. Responses were evaluated using three validated metrics: reliability, assessed using the modified DISCERN tool; readability, assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FK) and Coleman-Liau index (CL); and clinical accuracy, assessed by a board-certified cardiothoracic anesthesiologist and a board-certified cardiothoracic surgeon using a 3-point Likert scale.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: MediSearch demonstrated significantly higher reliability (mean DISCERN score, 4.64 v 2.47; p < 0.001). ChatGPT generated significantly more readable responses (mean FK score, 10.33 v 11.34 [p < 0.01]; mean CL score, 15.72 v 17.30 [p < 0.001]) and significantly higher clinical accuracy (mean, 0.82 v 0.71; p < 0.01). Subgroup analysis by Rothwell category confirmed MediSearch's reliability advantage across all question types, while ChatGPT's readability advantage was most pronounced for fact-based questions.
CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals a critical trade-off between evidence-based reliability and linguistic accessibility in AI-generated cardiac surgery patient education content. MediSearch offers superior reliability, while ChatGPT provides more readable and accurate responses. Neither platform achieves the sixth-grade readability level recommended for broad public accessibility. These findings underscore the need for AI platforms to balance clinical accuracy with health literacy standards before being endorsed as patient education tools in high-stakes settings.

Title: Global Longitudinal Strain as a Predictor of Challenging Separation from Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although reduced left ventricular ejection fraction is a risk factor for adverse postoperative outcomes, its ability to predict challenging cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) separation remains limited. We aimed to determine whether preoperative left ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), measured with a fully automated speckle-tracking echocardiographic software (LV AutoStrain) before induction of general anesthesia, can predict challenging separation from CPB.
DESIGN: Single-center prospective observational study.
SETTING: Adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB.
PARTICIPANTS: Fifty-two consecutive patients were scheduled for cardiac surgery requiring CPB, with adequate preoperative transthoracic echocardiographic windows. Patients with preoperative atrial fibrillation, inotropic and mechanical circulatory support, or mechanical ventilation were excluded.
INTERVENTIONS: GLS was obtained non-invasively by transthoracic echocardiography using LV AutoStrain.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: CPB separation was classified as easy or challenging. Compared with the easy-weaning group, patients in the challenging weaning group showed more impaired preoperative GLS values (-11.8% [IQR -14.0% to -10.3%] v -16.1% [IQR -18.6% to -15.4%]; p < .01) and longer CPB (132.5 minutes [94.0-164.0] v 100.0 minutes [69.2-132.5]; p = .036) and aortic cross-clamp times (89.0 [67.5-116.0] v 61.0 [40.0-79.0]; p = .004). On multivariable analysis adjusted for EuroSCORE II, left ventricular ejection fraction category, CPB duration, and type of surgical procedure, GLS remained the only independent predictor of challenging CPB separation (odds ratio 1.40, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-1.79; p < .01). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis showed good discrimination for challenging weaning (area under the curve 0.864, 95% CI 0.740-0.969; p < .001); the optimal threshold of -14.0% for preoperative GLS yielded 80.0% sensitivity and 90.9% specificity.
CONCLUSION: Fully automated, operator-independent preoperative GLS was strongly and independently associated with challenging separation from CPB, with a clinically applicable threshold. GLS may represent a rapid, reproducible adjunct to perioperative risk stratification.

Title: Comparing High-Flow Nasal Cannula Therapy and Conventional Oxygen Therapy in Adult Patients Post-Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass structurally alters respiratory mechanics and carries a substantial risk of postoperative morbidity. Historically, patients have routinely received conventional oxygen therapy (COT) following extubation. High- flow nasal cannula (HCNC) therapy has emerged as an innovative respiratory support system. By synthesizing all currently available high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs), this study aimed to rigorously evaluate the efficacy and safety of HFNC compared to COT, focusing primarily on determining the need for escalation of respiratory support.
METHODOLOGY: A thorough electronic search was carried out in the PubMed, Embase, and Scopus databases from their inception to May 2026. Only RCTs were considered for analysis. A random-effects model was applied to compute pooled estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 11 RCTs, comprising 2473 patients, were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. HFNC had a statistically significant effect on reducing the requirement for escalation of respiratory support (risk ratio [RR] = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.55-0.93; p = 0.01). HFNC had a statistically significant effect on improving the arterial partial pressure of oxygen, as well as forced expiratory volume in 1 second, while also increasing delirium complications (RR = 3.63; 95% CI, 1.80-7.30; p = 0.0003). There were no statistically significant differences between the 2 approaches in the other secondary clinical and resource utilization outcomes, including intubation, overall mortality, hospital length of stay, intensive care unit length of stay, and postoperative atrial fibrillation.
CONCLUSION: In adult patients recovering from cardiac surgery, HFNC therapy improves oxygenation and significantly curtails the need to escalate respiratory support compared to COT. However, these physiologic and intermediate clinical benefits do not translate into reductions in mortality, reintubation rate, or hospital length of stay and may come at the cost of increased postoperative delirium.

Title: Outcomes of Patients Undergoing Mitral Valve Replacement After Failed Attempt at Mitral Valve Repair.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mitral valve repair (MVr) is the ideal treatment strategy for degenerative mitral regurgitation. Mitral valve replacement (MVR) may be required if MVr is unsuccessful during the index surgery. The consequences of MVR following failed MVr during the same surgery are unclear.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.
SETTING: Single institution, university affiliated.
PARTICIPANTS: All patients who underwent MVR from 2010 through 2024 were included. Patients with concomitant surgeries were included.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were dichotomized into the intended repair (IR) or de novo replacement (DR) groups based on the intended procedure.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 1,661 patients (mean age, 64 years; 57% female) underwent MVR. MVr was attempted in 133 patients (8%, IR group), and 1,528 underwent planned MVR (92%, DR group). The mean ejection fraction was 55%. Female sex (58.0% in the DR group v 48.9% in the IR group, p = 0.04), history of infective endocarditis (23.8% v 15.0%, p = 0.02), history of cerebrovascular disease (32.1% v 19.5%, p = 0.03), and prior sternotomy (32.1% v 15.8%, p < 0.001) were more prevalent in the DR group. After propensity score matching, perioperative morbidity and mortality were similar. The median cardiopulmonary bypass time and cross-clamp time were longer in the IR group (207 minutes v 134 minutes in the DR group and 163 minutes v 102 minutes in the DR group, respectively). Kaplan-Meier curve analysis showed similar 5-year survival (p = 0.91).
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative outcomes were similar despite longer operative times in the IR group. Failure of initial MVr, leading to MVR, did not translate into adverse early or long-term outcomes. These findings suggest that repair may be more aggressively considered in patients with repairable anatomies.

Title: Optimizing pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis in medical inpatients using sequential IMPROVE risk assessment models: Clinical, economic and environmental implications.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients. Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discrepancy between real-world thromboprophylaxis prescribing and a prespecified sequential IMPROVE-based strategy and assess its economic and environmental implications.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in internal medicine over one month. Adults hospitalized for>48h were included, excluding those receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. IMPROVE VTE and Bleeding scores were calculated retrospectively. Pharmacologic prophylaxis was supported by the strategy for patients with an IMPROVE Bleeding score<7 and IMPROVE VTE score≥2. Observed prescriptions were compared with the prespecified strategy using contingency analysis and Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: Among 99 patients, 79.8% received pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, whereas 46.5% met the strategy criteria. Among treated patients, 46.8% did not meet these criteria. Strict application of the strategy would theoretically result in 292 fewer doses over one month, corresponding to €233.60 in estimated savings and approximately 405kg CO2eq.
CONCLUSION: Real-world prescribing differed substantially from the prespecified strategy. Strict application would theoretically reduce anticoagulant use, costs, and carbon emissions. However, clinical outcomes were not assessed, and RAMs should complement rather than replace clinical judgment. Prospective studies incorporating VTE and bleeding outcomes are required to assess the safety of this approach.

Title: A prognostic model for use at labour onset to estimate the risk of severe fetal compromise at birth: a retrospective, model development and validation study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Absence of reliable risk assessment and monitoring of fetal wellbeing during labour remains a major clinical challenge worldwide. Cardiotocography (CTG) is commonly used to monitor the fetal heart rate, but its misinterpretation or delays in clinical escalation contribute to poor birth outcomes. We aimed to develop a novel prognostic model for the prediction of severe fetal compromise at birth, combining known clinical risk factors with the first 20 min of CTG monitoring.
METHODS: In this retrospective, model development and validation study, we used routinely collected, fully anonymised maternity data from three databases: the John Radcliffe Hospital (Oxford, UK; 1993-2024; model training and testing), the Rosie Hospital (Cambridge, UK; 2016-22; external validation), and the Stockholm-Gotland region (Sweden; 2018-20; independent external validation). Oxford and Cambridge datasets were accessed from maternity and neonatal unit electronic health records; Stockholm-Gotland data were accessed as part of the larger Stockholm-Gotland Perinatal Cohort. Singleton births at 36 weeks and 0 days of gestation or more undergoing intrapartum CTG monitoring, whether labour was spontaneous or induced, were included. Clinical risk factors used for model development were maternal age, gestational age, nulliparity, pre-eclampsia, diabetes in pregnancy, thick meconium, and maximal recorded maternal temperature in labour. Quantitative CTG features included in the model were fetal heart rate baseline, short-term variability, decelerative capacity, number of accelerations, and number of prolonged decelerations, and were extracted using the Oxford intrapartum computer-based algorithms. Birth outcomes were defined in three mutually exclusive groups: severe compromise, intermediate compromise, and healthy. Fit4Labour risk score (ie, estimated probability of severe compromise) was stratified into four risk groups: >95th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, >85th and ≤95th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, >25th and ≤85th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, and ≤25th centile of Fit4Labour risk score. Model accuracy was assessed by use of partial receiver operating characteristic curves and comparison with a clinical benchmark (sensitivity at 15% screen-positive rate).
FINDINGS: 147 350 births with at least 20 min of CTG data were analysed: 91 378 from Oxford 1993-2024 (73 443 for training and testing [Oxford 1993-2019] and 17 935 for internal validation [Oxford 2020-24]), 14 709 from Cambridge 2016-22 (external validation), and 41 263 from Stockholm-Gotland 2018-20 (independent external validation). The rate of severe compromise was higher in the highest-risk group (>95th centile) than in the lowest-risk group (≤25th centile) across all validation datasets: 0·9% (95% CI 0·28-1·51) in the highest risk group versus 0·1% (0·01-0·21) in the lowest-risk group in the Oxford 2020-24 dataset; 0·3% (0·00-0·65) versus 0·1% (0·00-0·22) in the Cambridge 2016-22 dataset; and 0·9% (0·47-1·27) versus 0·2% (0·08-0·23) in the Stockholm-Gotland 2018-20 dataset. At a fixed screen-positive rate of 15%, 20-min Fit4Labour had a sensitivity of 33·4% (95% CI 28·31-38·56), compared with the clinical benchmark sensitivity of 39·9% (95% CI 32·59-47·18, p=0·18), and showed consistent performance across all validation datasets.
INTERPRETATION: Fit4Labour is a robust prognostic model, readily applicable around labour onset and extensively validated with retrospective data from sites with different maternity demographics and clinical care practices. Fit4Labour relies on routinely available data and could produce interpretable output in real time, providing timely individualised risk stratification that is data-driven, objective, and reproducible.
FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research.

Title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease as a risk factor for postoperative complications in the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program registry (2015-2022): implications for preoperative evaluation.
Journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is frequently reported in metabolic surgery patients and has been associated with increased postoperative complications. However, variability in GERD diagnosis, reliance on self-reported symptoms, and medication use may be confounding factors.
OBJECTIVES: Evaluate GERD as an independent risk factor for postoperative outcomes.
SETTING: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program (MBSAQIP), 2015-2022.
METHODS: A total of 1,577,175 cases (sleeve gastrectomy [SG], Roux-en-Y gastric bypass [RYGB], or biliopancreatic diversion/duodenal switch) were available for inclusion. Exclusions included age <18, body mass index <30, missing sex or operative length, and revisions/conversions. Adjusted logistic regression models evaluated GERD as a predictor of 30-day and procedure-specific outcomes (SG, RYGB). All statistical analyses were performed using R, version 4.4.1.
RESULTS: Overall, a total of 1,282,883 patients met inclusion criteria, and patients were more likely to undergo SG than RYGB regardless of the GERD status. GERD diagnosis was present in 30.5% of patients. Preoperatively, GERD was associated with clinically relevant differences in cardiac history and was also associated with increased odds of postoperative complications, including infections (odds ratio [OR], 1.27), serious complications (OR, 1.20), and 30-day readmission (OR, 1.26).
CONCLUSION: After adjustment for co-morbidities, GERD was associated with modestly increased odds of adverse events after metabolic and bariatric surgery. In addition, SG was the most performed procedure among patients with GERD despite clinical recommendations favoring RYGB. Surgeons should consider a preoperative GERD diagnosis-as defined in the MBSAQIP-as a potential marker for identifying patients who may warrant enhanced perioperative risk assessment and optimization of coexisting co-morbidities.

Title: Diabetic nephropathy and postoperative complications in metabolic and bariatric surgery: a propensity score-matched nationwide cohort study.
Journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is increasingly prevalent among people with obesity undergoing metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) in the United States, yet its impact on perioperative complications remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVES: This study utilizes a large nationwide database to investigate the association between DN and in-hospital postoperative complications after MBS.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2019). Adults with obesity undergoing MBS were identified using International Classification Of Diseases, tenth revision (ICD-10) codes. DN patients were matched 1:1 to non-DN controls using propensity score matching, balancing demographics, hospital characteristics, and 24 Elixhauser co-morbidities. Multivariate logistic regression assessed the association between DN and perioperative complications.
RESULTS: DN patients had significantly higher odds of blood transfusion (odds ratio (OR): 1.178, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.026-1.353), anastomotic complications (OR: 1.669, 95% CI: 1.158-2.492), acute myocardial infarction (OR: 1.553, 95% CI: 1.276-1.891), acute kidney injury (AKI) (OR: 3.024, 95% CI: 2.786-3.281), urinary tract infection (UTI) (OR: 1.175, 95% CI: 1.054-1.309), and extended length of stay (LOS) (OR: 1.205, 95% CI: 1.118-1.300).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that DN is a significant independent risk factor for blood transfusion, anastomotic complications, acute myocardial infarction, AKI, UTI, and prolonged hospitalization after MBS. These findings highlight the need for enhanced preoperative counseling and targeted perioperative management in this high-risk population.

Title: Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.
Abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

Title: [Livedoid vasculopathy: A case report].
Journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
Abstract: Livedoid vasculopathy (LV) is a painful and thrombotic obliterative vascular disorder characterized by spontaneous thrombus formation within skin capillaries or small veins, ultimately leading to localized hypoxia and the development of skin ulcers. LV is a rare condition predominantly affecting young women, with an incidence rate of approximately 1/100 000. Clinically, it manifests as recurrent reticular green spots and painful ulcers on the distal lower extremities, which subsequently heal, leaving behind white and atrophic scars, termed "white atrophy". The skin manifestations of the disease are prominent, often seen in dermatology. Recently, the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology of Honghui Hospital, Xi ' an Jiaotong University, admitted a patient with LV. This young female patient presented with recurrent lower limb skin purpura and ulcers, which had occurred spontaneously during the summer for the past three years. Following a skin biopsy conducted at another hospital, she was diagnosed with LV and subsequently treated with phototherapy, anticoagulation therapy, and topical corticosteroids, yet there was no improvement in her condition. In April of this year, she sought further treatment at our hospital and was admitted for comprehensive care. After completing a thorough battery of relevant examinations, we excluded other potential vascular disorders, abnormal coagulation profiles, and autoimmune diseases, such as cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (cPAN), leukocyte-cracking vasculitis (LCV), and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). The patient remained definitively diagnosed with LV. Under our department's care, she received oral glucocorticoids, tacrolimus for immune modulation, and colchicine for anti-inflammatory effects. Subsequently, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged from the hospital. Four months post-discharge, a follow-up examination revealed significant improvement in her symptoms. The therapeutic approaches for LV encompassed general therapy, antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy, glucocorticoid and immunosuppressant therapy, intravenous human immunoglobulin therapy, and hyperbaric oxygen therapy. Additionally, the use of biologics, including tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and small molecule targeted JAK inhibitors, had been reported in LV cases. Further randomized controlled trials are necessary to validate these treatment options. This report presented a case of LV where favorable outcomes were achieved through a combination of anticoagulant and immunosuppressive therapies. Nevertheless, given that the patient has been afflicted with the disease for three years and we have only conducted a four-month follow-up, which is relatively short, continued long-term follow-up of this patient remains imperative.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Case Reports; English Abstract

Title: [Clinical characteristics and risk factors of patients with rheumatoid arthritis complicated with urinary tract infection].
Journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the clinical characteristics of urinary tract infection (UTI) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), to evaluate the effects of different treatment regimens on the risk of UTI, and to identify independent risk factors for UTI complicated with RA.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. RA patients hospitalized in the Department of Rheumatology and Immunology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Baotou Medical College from September 2020 to September 2023 were enrolled. General clinical data, laboratory indicators and medication information of the patients were collected. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence or absence of UTI for comparative analysis. Patients were grouped based on different treatment regimens received, and the proportions of UTI occurrence were compared among each group. The results of urine culture and drug susceptibility test in the RA patients with UTI were analyzed. Univariate and multivariate Logistic regression analyses were further performed to screen relevant factors for UTI in the RA patients, and the diagnostic value of combined indicators was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.
RESULTS: A total of 196 RA patients were included, among whom 99 cases were complicated with UTI and 97 cases without UTI. Compared with the non-UTI group, the UTI group had higher proportions of female patients, patients aged ≥65 years, patients with RA disease duration ≥10 years, patients hospitalized for infection within the past two years, and patients with comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, hypertension, etc.). Peripheral blood leukocyte count, percentage of neutrophils, serum procalcitonin, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein level were elevated (P < 0.05), while hemoglobin, percentage of lymphocytes and plasma albumin level were decreased (P < 0.05). The RA patients were divided into four groups according to different treatment regimens: ①glucocorticoids (GCs) monotherapy group; ②conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) monotherapy group; ③csDMARDs combined with GCs group; ④ csDMARDs combined with biological DMARDs (bDMARDs)/ targeted synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs) group. The overall difference in UTI proportion among the four groups was statistically significant (P < 0.001). After Bonferroni correction, the UTI proportion in group ① and group ③ was higher than that in group ② and group ④ (adjusted P < 0.05). GSs use was associated with increased UTI risk, and the risk of UTI showed an upward trend with the increase of daily dose. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that RA disease duration ≥10 years, previous hospitalization due to infection within the past two years, comorbid diabetes mellitus, and elevated disease activity score in 28 joints based on ESR (DAS28-ESR) were independent risk factors for UTI in the RA patients. The area under the ROC curve of the diagnostic model constructed with the above combined predictors was 0.82 (95%CI: 0.76-0.88), with a sensitivity of 0.67 and a specificity of 0.94. Gram-negative bacteria were the predominant pathogens in urine culture of the RA patients with UTI, among which Escherichia coli accounted for 67.71%. Among evaluable single-isolate bacterial strains with available drug-susceptibility results, the resistance rates to levofloxacin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole were 65.4% and 52.8%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Clinical infection surveillance should be strengthened in RA patients. GCs should be rationally used on the premise of effective RA disease control, and bDMARDs/tsDMARDs therapy should be initiated timely according to disease status to reduce GCs exposure and minimize the risk of UTI. Meanwhile, antimicrobial agents should be selected in a standardized manner based on urine culture and drug susceptibility test results.

Title: [Association between different types of first-degree relatives' stroke history and the incidence risk of stroke: A prospective cohort study].
Journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between different types of first-degree relatives' stroke history and the incidence risk of stroke, and to explore the familial aggregation and intergenerational transmission of stroke risk.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study design was adopted, based on the data of the Fangshan Family-based Ischemic Stroke Study in China(FISSIC). The Cox proportional hazards model was used to analyze the association between different types of first-degree relatives' stroke history (paternal stroke history, maternal stroke history, parental history of stroke, and sibling stroke history) and the incidence risk of stroke. The hazard ratio (HR) and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were estimated. Stroke was classified as early-onset and late-onset, and the association between different types of first-degree relatives ' stroke history and the risk of early-onset and late-onset stroke was further analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 3 631 subjects were included in the study, with 1 650 males (45.4%) and a mean age of (56.7±8.4) years. The median follow-up duration was 6.98 years, during which 1 337 new cases of stroke occurred. The risk of stroke occurrence was higher in those with a first-degree relative history of stroke (HR=1.24, 95%CI: 1.08-1.43, P=0.002). For different types of first-degree relatives ' stroke history, the association between maternal and sibling history of stroke and the incidence risk of stroke was statistically significant (maternal history of stroke: HR=1.15, 95%CI: 1.00-1.32, P=0.049; sibling history of stroke: HR=1.17, 95%CI: 1.03-1.33, P=0.013). No association was observed between a paternal history of stroke or a parental history of stroke and the risk of stroke (both P>0.05). Compared with those without a family history, the HRs for early-onset and late-onset stroke in those with a maternal history of stroke were 1.40 (95%CI: 1.10-1.77, P=0.005) and 1.19 (95%CI: 1.01-1.41, P=0.043), respectively. Compared with those without a family history, the HRs for early-onset and late-onset stroke in those with a sibling history of stroke were 1.28 (95%CI: 1.02-1.61, P=0.034) and 1.17 (95%CI: 1.00-1.37, P=0.045), respectively.
CONCLUSION: Stroke exhibits familial aggregation, and the history of stroke in first-degree relatives is associated with the incidence risk of stroke. In particular, the maternal and sibling stroke history demonstrate a stronger association with the incidence risk of stroke. This finding suggests that during the intergenerational transmission of stroke risk, the genetics and family environment reflected by the maternal and sibling stroke history may play an important role.

Title: [Correlation between trimethylamine-N-oxide and cardiovascular metabolic markers].
Journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between serum trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) levels and cardiovascular metabolic biomarkers, so as to provide a basis for clarifying the impact of TMAO on cardiovascular metabolic disease.
METHODS: Based on baseline data from the Beijing Fangshan Family Cohort collected from 2013 to 2017, totally 500 participants from 173 families were selected from the survey subjects. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits. The correlation between TMAO and cardiovascular and metabolic disease indicators was analyzed by a linear mixed effects model.
RESULTS: The mean age of the participants was (56.52±12.52) years, with 54.20% being male. Serum TMAO levels showed significant positive correlations with systolic blood pressure (SBP) and pulse pressure (PP). Each 1 μmol/L increase in TMAO was associated with a 0.74 mmHg increase in SBP (95%CI: 0.19-1.30, P=0.009) and a 0.64 mmHg increase in PP (95%CI: 0.21-1.08, P=0.004). Subgroup analysis showed that for each 1 μmol/l increase in TMAO in men, SBP and PP increased by 0.91 mmHg (95%CI: 0.24-1.57, P < 0.05) and 0.85 mmHg (95%CI: 0.37-1.35, P < 0.05), respectively. No significant correlation was found in women. In the population aged ≥60 years, each 1 μmol/L increase in TMAO was associated with a 1.10 mmHg increase in SBP (95%CI: 0.23-1.96, P < 0.05) and a 0.98 mmHg increase in PP (95%CI: 0.23-1.73, P < 0.05). No significant correlation was found in people aged < 60 years.
CONCLUSION: The current study found that high TMAO level was correlated with the increase of SBP and PP, and TMAO might be an influencing factor of blood pressure level. No statistically significant correlation was found between TMAO and blood glucose and lipid indicators.

Title: [Correlation between acute kidney injury diagnosed by serum creatinine and urine output criteria and short-term prognosis in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery].
Journal: Beijing da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Peking University. Health sciences
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the correlation between acute kidney injury (AKI) diagnosed by elevated serum creatinine (Scr) versus only meeting the urine output (UO) reduction criteria and short-term adverse outcomes in critically ill patients following non-cardiac surgery, and to evaluate the association between even mild elevations in Scr and clinical outcomes furthermore.
METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of data from a prospective cohort study. A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgery adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Peking University First Hospital from May 20, 2019 to March 7, 2022 were included. According to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline, AKI patients were classified into two groups: the AKI-Scr group (those meeting the Scr elevation criteria) and the AKI-UO group (those fulfilling only the UO reduction criteria). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality in patients with AKI, and the secondary outcomes were major renal adverse events, post-operative renal replacement therapy (RRT), postoperative complications, postoperative mechanical ventilation time, ICU stay, postoperative hospital stay, total hospital stay, and total medical costs. Multivariate Logistic regression analysis was used to identify risk factors of hospitalized death in critically ill patients with AKI following non-cardiac surgery.
RESULTS: A total of 1020 non-cardiac surgical patients admitted to the ICU were enrolled, among whom 429 were diagnosed with AKI. There were 91 cases in the AKI-Scr group and 338 cases in the AKI-UO group. The primary study endpoint: no statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was observed between the AKI-Scr and AKI-UO groups (5.5% vs. 2.1%, P>0.05). The secondary study endpoints: compared with the AKI-UO group, the patients in the AKI-Scr group had a higher incidence of major renal adverse events (9.8% vs. 4.4%), postoperative RRT (4.4% vs. 0.3%) and postoperative complications (50.5% vs. 24.0%, all P < 0.05), a significantly longer duration of postoperative mechanical ventilation (12.0 d vs. 7.5 d), ICU stay (2 d vs. 1 d), postoperative hospital stay (14 d vs. 9 d) and total hospital stay (21 d vs.17 d, all P < 0.05), and a significantly higher total medical expenditure (112000 yuan vs. 89000 yuan, P<0.001). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that postoperative RRT (OR=33.164, 95%CI: 1.305-842.794, P=0.034) and sepsis during hospitalization (OR=23.096, 95%CI: 4.242-125.175, P < 0.001) were independent risk factors for hospitalized death in the critically ill patients with postoperative AKI. Compared with the ΔScr≤24% patients (Scr increased by less than 24% from baseline within 7 d), even in the patients with only a minor elevation in Scr (ΔScr increase of 25%-49% from baseline but < 26.5μmol/L), the incidence of postoperative complications was significantly higher (48.6% vs. 19.2%, P < 0.001), along with prolonged ICU stay [1(1, 3) d vs. 1(1, 2) d], postoperative hospital stay (13 d vs. 9 d), and total hospital stay (23 d vs. 16 d, all P < 0.05). Compared with the non-AKI group, the incidence of in-hospital mortality (2.1% vs. 0.3%, P < 0.05) and postoperative complications (24.0% vs. 18.3%, P < 0.05) was higher in the AKI-UO group, and the ICU stay [1(1, 3) d vs. 1(1, 2) d, P < 0.001] was longer.
CONCLUSION: In critically ill patients with AKI following non-cardiac surgery, the short-term prognosis of patients with AKI whose diagnosis was mainly based on increased Scr was worse than patients who only met the diagnostic criteria of oliguria. Even a mild elevation in serum creatinine was associated with adverse patient outcomes.

Title: Early indicators of NICU admission for ongoing respiratory support in caesarean-delivered late preterm and term neonates requiring non-invasive respiratory support within the first 15 min after birth: a post hoc analysis.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Non-invasive respiratory support during immediate postnatal transition is common in caesarean-delivered late preterm and term neonates yet distinguishing those, who will require neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission and those who will stabilise with initial respiratory support, remains challenging. This exploratory study assessed whether clinical parameters obtained within the first 15 min after birth are associated with NICU admission for ongoing respiratory support lasting beyond 60 min.
DESIGN AND SETTING: Post hoc analysis of prospectively collected data from three observational studies (2018–2024) conducted at a single tertiary NICU (Medical University Graz).
PATIENTS: A total of 105 neonates with a gestational age (GA) ≥34 weeks delivered by caesarean section and requiring non-invasive respiratory support within 15 min after birth were eligible.
RESULTS: Neonates admitted to the NICU for ongoing respiratory support (NICU group, n=30, GA 354/7 (344/7–380/7)) were compared with those who stabilised in the delivery room (non-NICU group, n = 75, GA 384/7 (374/7–390/7)). Neonates in the NICU group were significantly more often male, had lower GA, birth weight, 10 min Apgar scores, peripheral arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2), SpO2/fraction of inspired oxygen ratio (S/F ratio) and higher heart rates 15 min after birth. In multivariable regression, lower GA (p = 0.010) and a lower S/F ratio at 15 min (p < 0.001) were independently associated with NICU admission.
CONCLUSION: Among this cohort of caesarean-delivered late preterm and term neonates requiring non-invasive respiratory support in the first 15 min after birth, lower GA and a lower S/F ratio at 15 min were independently associated with subsequent NICU admission. These findings identify candidate early clinical indicators; larger prospective studies are needed to validate their predictive value and determine their role in clinical decision-making.

Title: The spectrum of cardiovascular disease in systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis: a nationwide case-control postmortem study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine cardiovascular pathology in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) vs. population-based controls, and its association with cause of death.
METHODS: A case-control postmortem study was performed in Australia using the National Coronial Information System (2000-2025). SLE/RA cases were identified via keyword/ICD-10 code search. Controls were selected from motor vehicle accident deaths (3:1 ratio). Cardiovascular findings/histology were extracted from autopsy reports. Associations between SLE/RA and cardiovascular findings/outcomes using logistic regression (odds ratios (OR), 95% confidence intervals (CI)).
RESULTS: 363 cases (240 RA&123 SLE) and 123 controls of similar age (cases 63y (IQR 53-72), vs. controls 59y (47-73), p=0.166) and sex (female 69% vs. controls 75%, p=0.235) were included. Adjusting for age, sex and BMI, myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR3.66, 95%CI2.00-6.72, p<0.001; RA OR3.96, 95%CI2.37-6.60, p<0.001), myocardial inflammation (SLE OR14.79, 95%CI3.35-65.37, p<0.001; RA OR6.35, 95%CI1.44-28.09, p=0.015) and cardiomegaly (SLE OR5.70, 95%CI2.99-10.86, p<0.001; RA OR3.50, 95%CI2.02-6.08, p<0.001) were more frequent in SLE and RA, as were coronary artery disease (CAD; SLE OR2.46, 95%CI1.34-4.51, p=0.004; RA OR2.56, 95%CI1.54-4.27, p<0.001) and microvascular disease (SLE OR10.28, 95%CI2.28- 46.31; RA OR6.74, 95%CI1.53-29.57, p=0.012). Associations between cardiovascular findings and SLE/RA status were strongest in under-60s, and persisted after adjusting for CAD. Cardiovascular death was associated with myocardial fibrosis (SLE OR2.35, 95%CI1.02-5.43, p=0.045; RA OR3.62, 95%CI1.81-7.27, p<0.001), cardiomegaly (SLE OR3.77, 95%CI1.71-8.27, p=0.001; RA OR2.52, 95%CI1.44-4.43, p=0.001) and CAD (SLE OR4.12, 95%CI1.76-9.66, p=0.001; RA OR12.71, 95%CI6.59-24.49, p<0.001); and microvascular disease (OR5.26, 95%CI1.40-19.77, p=0.014) and valvular pathology (OR2.68, 95%CI1.11-6.43, p=0.028) in SLE only.
CONCLUSION: This unique dataset identified increased atherosclerotic, inflammatory and fibrotic cardiovascular disease in SLE and RA, particularly in younger individuals. These pathologies were frequently associated with cardiovascular death.

Title: Patterns of NT-proBNP in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated patterns of N-terminal prohormone of n-terminal brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP, a biomarker of cardiac disease) in SLE, and associations with demographic and clinical characteristics.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the McGill SLE Research Cohort, including yearly serum NTproBNP. We assessed prevalence of baseline elevated NT-proBNP (≥133 ng/L) , and associations with baseline variables: age, sex, race/ethnicity, age at SLE diagnosis, SLE duration, smoking, and SLE International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index. Patients were classified into four NT-proBNP patterns: abnormal at baseline and remaining abnormal; abnormal and normalizing; normal and becoming abnormal; normal and remaining normal. We compared baseline characteristics across patterns using multivariate logistic regressions.
RESULTS: We studied 294 patients with ≥2 measurements. At baseline, 101 (34.4%) had elevated NT-proBNP. Higher levels were associated with older age at SLE diagnosis, longer SLE duration, cardiovascular damage, pulmonary hypertension, and renal damage. Of 101 individuals with abnormal baseline NT-proBNP, 79 (78.2%) remained abnormal. Of the 193 with normal baseline levels, 30 (15.5%) became abnormal. No patient with a baseline level ≥350 normalized to <133. High-risk patterns (abnormal-remaining-abnormal and normal-becoming-abnormal) were more likely to have cardiovascular damage (OR 3.90, 95% CI 1.49-12.5, renal damage (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.61-5.51), and pulmonary hypertension (OR 32.0, 95% CI 4.59-651.1).
CONCLUSION: Over one-third of SLE patients had abnormal baseline NT-proBNP; most (78%) remained abnormal. Over 15% of those with an initially normal value became abnormal. Higher levels were associated with age, SLE duration, and organ damage. Levels ≥350 ng/L did not normalize over our evaluation.

Title: A Retrospective Chart Review of Tirzepatide and Semaglutide Use in Prediabetes Management and Cardiometabolic Outcomes in a Rural Primary Care Setting.
Abstract: Background: Prediabetes and obesity are highly prevalent conditions associated with increased risk of progression to type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and cardiovascular disease. While clinical trials demonstrate the efficacy of glucagon-like peptide-1 and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, limited evidence exists in routine primary care, particularly in rural populations. Objective: This review aimed to examine associations between tirzepatide and semaglutide use and changes in glycemic status and cardiometabolic risk factors among rural-dwelling adults with prediabetes treated in a single rural primary care clinic. Methods: A retrospective chart review was conducted among 40 adults with prediabetes and overweight or obesity treated for 3-24 months with semaglutide or tirzepatide. Primary outcomes included body mass index (BMI) and hemoglobin (A1c). Secondary variables included blood pressure (BP), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and triglycerides. Results: Significant improvements were observed in A1c, BMI, systolic and diastolic BP, LDL, and triglycerides (p < .001). All participants achieved normoglycemic A1c levels. No significant changes were observed in HDL levels. Conclusions: In this rural primary care setting, treatment with tirzepatide or semaglutide was associated with improvements in glycemic control and cardiometabolic risk factors. Findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the observational design and potential confounding factors. Implications for Nursing: Nurse practitioners are positioned to advocate for and implement pharmacological therapies for early management of prediabetes. Providers can drive meaningful changes in T2DM prevention and cardiometabolic health optimization.

Title: Mortality Risk in Steatotic Liver Disease Stratified by Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Alcohol Consumption: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) has emerged as a new nomenclature; however, the long-term outcomes of SLD associated with its subtypes have been understudied. We aimed to investigate the all-cause and cause-specific mortality risk across SLD subtypes.
METHODS: Health checkup results of 2,049,641 Korean individuals were analyzed. SLD was defined as a Fatty Liver Index ≥30. Mortality risks in metabolic dysfunction-associated SLD (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-related liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) were investigated considering cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) and alcohol consumption. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to calculate the adjusted hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Compared with no SLD, MASLD (HR, 1.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24 to 1.30), MetALD (HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.36 to 1.44), and ALD (HR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.65 to 1.75) showed higher risks of all-cause mortality. All subtypes had an increased cause-specific mortality risk from liver-related disease, extrahepatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with liver-related mortality being the most prominent (HR, 2.57; 95% CI, 2.36 to 2.80 for MASLD; HR, 4.34; 95% CI, 3.93 to 4.78 for MetALD; HR, 6.23; 95% CI, 5.65 to 6.91 for ALD). The cumulative incidence of all-cause mortality increased as the number of CMRFs increased in all subtypes. The number of CMRFs affecting the mortality risk was the most pronounced in MASLD but the least pronounced in ALD.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that MASLD, MetALD, and ALD had an increased risk of all-cause and cause-specific mortality compared with no SLD. The impact of the number of CMRFs on mortality risk was most pronounced in MASLD, calling for more customized management strategies.

Title: ITACARE-P cardiorehab registry: real-world data on quality and outcomes in heart failure and ischaemic heart disease - a prospective observational study protocol of the Italian early post-acute cardiac rehabilitation network.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rehospitalisation and mortality for heart failure and coronary artery disease remain high despite continuous acute-care improvements. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a cornerstone of post-acute care, integrating optimised therapy, exercise, education and psychosocial support within a multidisciplinary pathway, tailored to patient complexity and facilitating continuity between acute, post-acute and community care. Nevertheless, the number of referrals is low, describing the lack of alliance and common belief between acute and post-acute care. From this perspective, the Don Gnocchi Foundation along with the Italian Alliance for Cardiovascular Rehabilitation and Prevention Association (ITACARE-P) has launched the CardioRehab Registry as a quality improvement initiative.
METHODS: The ITACARE-P CardioRehab Registry is a prospective, multicentre observational cohort established to epidemiologically characterise CR management across Italy and evaluate its impact on a holistic profile of patient health following acute coronary artery disease or heart failure events. It aims to bridge the gap between acute care and long-term tertiary prevention. The Registry aims to support quality improvement through national standardisation of CR pathways and target patient outcomes (both functional as historically defined and clinically oriented to tertiary prevention using common metrics as in the acute setting). Moreover, the Registry is aligned to comparable data collection across European centres, enabling assessment of functional and clinical outcomes and adherence to guideline-recommended quality indicators. The Registry, using a REDCap-based case report form, covers demographic/psychosocial information, comorbidities, risk factors and acute-phase and CR complications. In addition, it explores patient-reported outcomes through the anxiety and depression domain (Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7/Patient Health Questionnaire-9) and the quality-of-life domain (EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale and Heart-Related Quality of Life Questionnaire or Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire according to the index diagnosis).
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This is an investigator-initiated, non-sponsored study. Ethical approval was granted by the Territorial Ethics Committee Lombardy 4 (CET 12–25). Informed consent will be obtained from each participant before enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through the ITACARE-P. Moreover, data will be delivered through open-access publications and academic conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07094737.

Title: Hyperuricaemia risk and its association with kidney failure and mortality in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes with preserved renal function: a multicentre machine learning study.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: Hyperuricaemia is prevalent in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and associated with adverse renal and mortality outcomes; however, existing predictive models have primarily targeted populations with diabetic nephropathy or reduced renal function, limiting their applicability to early-stage T2DM. We developed a machine learning (ML)-based model to predict incident hyperuricaemia in newly diagnosed patients with T2DM with preserved kidney function and evaluated its association with long-term cardiorenal and mortality outcomes.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Using multicentre electronic health record databases in South Korea, ML models were developed to predict incident hyperuricaemia within 1 year of T2DM diagnosis. Model performance was externally validated across three independent databases. Based on model-derived risk stratification, 5-year risks of kidney failure, cardiovascular outcomes and all-cause mortality were evaluated. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to compare cumulative incidence between risk groups in the development cohort. HRs were estimated using Cox regression and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, with adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, insulin use and diuretic use.
RESULTS: The Extreme Gradient Boosting model achieved the highest discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.769 in the development cohort (n=5263); 0.709–0.750 in external validation). In fully adjusted pooled analyses, high-risk patients exhibited significantly elevated 5-year risks of kidney failure (HR=2.47; 95% CI 1.18 to 5.18) and all-cause mortality (HR=2.56; 95% CI 1.81 to 3.62). The association with cardiovascular outcomes was attenuated after full adjustment (HR=1.12; 95% CI 0.96 to 1.30).
CONCLUSIONS: In newly diagnosed patients with T2DM with preserved kidney function, individuals classified as high-risk for incident hyperuricaemia by ML model were found to have higher long-term risks of kidney failure and all-cause mortality, independent of traditional risk factors. These findings suggest that model-derived hyperuricaemia risk may serve as a prognostic marker reflecting underlying renal and systemic vulnerability before overt organ damage occurs.

Title: Clinical profile, risk factors and in-hospital outcomes of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction in young versus older adults: a 5-year retrospective cohort study at a tertiary care centre in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVES: To compare the clinical profile, cardiovascular risk factor burden, in-hospital management and outcomes of young (≤45 years) versus older (>45 years) adults presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to describe lifestyle factors and disease perceptions among surviving young patients.
DESIGN: Two-phase retrospective cohort study: Phase I, a review of electronic health record data for all STEMI presentations; Phase II, a structured telephone interview of surviving young patients.
SETTING: A single tertiary care centre with a 24-hour cardiac catheterisation laboratory (King Abdulaziz Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia), January 2019 to December 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: 852 consecutive patients with confirmed STEMI; 191 (22.4%) aged ≤45 years (young group) and 661 (77.6%) aged >45 years (older adult group). In Phase II, all 191 young patients were contacted by telephone: 68 (35.6%) completed the interview, 6 (3.1%) declined consent and 117 (61.3%) could not be reached after three attempts on separate days or had an inactive number.
INTERVENTIONS: None; this was an observational study.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcome: in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes: baseline cardiovascular risk factor prevalence, laboratory parameters, angiographic and procedural characteristics, in-hospital complications, ejection fraction, length of stay and (Phase II) self-reported lifestyle behaviours and perceptions of disease causation.
RESULTS: The young group was predominantly male (94.8% vs 84.4%; p<0.001) and had significantly higher rates of smoking (71.7% vs 47.5%), obesity (body mass index >29 kg/m²; 33.2% vs 27.2%), illicit drug use (13.6% vs 2.4%) and family history of premature coronary artery disease (11.3% vs 2.2%) (all p<0.001). The older adult group had higher rates of diabetes (62.3% vs 34.6%), hypertension (62.2% vs 28.8%) and dyslipidaemia (47.4% vs 25.7%) (all p<0.001). Mean glycated haemoglobin was lower in the young group (7.05±2.36% vs 7.71±2.27%; p=0.001) but remained above the normal range, and low-density lipoprotein was higher (3.46±1.29 vs 3.19±1.18 mmol/L; p=0.012). In-hospital mortality was lower in the young group (2.1% vs 6.8%; p=0.014), and more young patients maintained an ejection fraction >35% (78.3% vs 68.6%; p=0.011). Among the 68 young survivors interviewed, 74% were people who actively smoked before their STEMI, 72% reported no regular physical activity, 25% used shisha (waterpipe), 16% used e-cigarettes, 28% reported having ‘no idea’ why they had a STEMI, 81% rated their post-STEMI health as good or very good and 37% reported ongoing chest pain.
CONCLUSIONS: Young adults accounted for nearly one-quarter of STEMI presentations and carried a disproportionate burden of modifiable risk factors—smoking, obesity and drug use—alongside unexpectedly poor glycaemic and lipid parameters, despite better short-term survival than older patients. These findings highlight smoking, obesity and adverse metabolic parameters as potential targets for prevention efforts in this population; prospective, interventional studies are needed to determine whether targeted screening or prevention programmes improve outcomes.

Title: Prevalence of amyloidosis among older cardiac patients with left ventricular hypertrophy: a cross-sectional single-centre study in Moscow, Russia.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence and clinical characteristics of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and light-chain cardiac amyloidosis (AL-CA) among older patients presenting with significant left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH).
DESIGN: Single-centre observational cross-sectional study.
SETTING: Pirogov City Clinical Hospital No. 1 (Moscow, Russia), from January 2023 to August 2024.
PARTICIPANTS: 113 patients aged≥65 years with interventricular septal or posterior wall thickness≥14 mm were included. Main exclusion criteria were previously diagnosed infiltrative or hypertrophic cardiomyopathies, severe aortic stenosis and recent myocardial infarction.
PROCEDURES: Participants underwent 12-lead electrocardiography, echocardiography with global longitudinal strain analysis and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy. Immunochemical testing and transthyretin (TTR) gene sequencing were performed according to predefined criteria.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the prevalence of ATTR-CM and AL-CA among older patients with LVH. Secondary outcomes included the frequency of clinical ‘red flags’, imaging findings associated with amyloidosis and correlations between clinical and laboratory markers and instrumental parameters.
RESULTS: ATTR-CM was confirmed in 18 patients, corresponding to a prevalence of 15.9% (95% CI 10.3% to 23.8%). AL-CA was diagnosed in seven patients (6.2%, 95% CI 3.0% to 12.2%). Among those with ATTR-CM, 4 patients (3.5% of the total cohort; 22% of the ATTR-CM group) carried pathogenic TTR mutations, whereas 14 (12%) had the wild-type form. Five additional patients (4.4%) with grade 2 uptake showed no clinical signs of heart failure, suggesting possible detection of preclinical cardiomyopathy. Higher radiotracer uptake grades (2–3) were significantly associated with greater wall thickness, higher biomarker levels (N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide, troponin I) and worse New York Heart Association class.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the substantial prevalence of cardiac amyloidosis (22.1%, 95% CI 15.5% to 30.6%) among older patients with LVH. The results emphasise the need for heightened clinical awareness and targeted screening strategies to identify patients at early or asymptomatic stages. Further multicentre studies to refine the understanding of ATTR-CM epidemiology in Russia.

Title: High levels of MCP-1 in menopause and their relationship with components of the metabolic syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The menopause stage involves a significant reduction in circulating estrogen levels, resulting in notable changes to the cardiovascular, metabolic, bone, and immune systems. Monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) is strongly associated with cardiovascular diseases and obesity. However, it is crucial to establish and clarify the relationship between MCP-1 and metabolic parameters in postmenopausal women.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess the relationship between MCP-1 concentrations and various anthropometric and metabolic markers in premenopausal and postmenopausal women.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A case-control study, including 82 women (41 in postmenopausal stage, and 41 in premenopausal stage), was matched by body mass index (BMI). Insulin, estradiol, and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were quantified by chemiluminescence and MCP-1 by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays.
RESULTS: Age was 46.3 ± 2.4 years in premenopausal women and 55.6 ± 5.1 years in postmenopausal women. The MCP-1 level was higher in postmenopausal than premenopausal women (28.7 ± 10.4 vs. 21.3 ± 16.3 pg/mL, p = 0.04). The MCP-1 correlated with BMI (r = 0.39, p = 0.0001), waist circumference (r = 0.34, p = 0.002), CRP (r = 0.33, p = 0.03), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (r = -0.28, p = 0.02), and visceral adipose tissue (VAT) (r = 0.38, p = 0.0001). Multiple stepwise regression analysis showed that VAT influenced the MCP-1 level.
CONCLUSION: Menopausal status influences MCP-1 concentrations; however, the relationship of MCP-1 with VAT favors the activation of inflammatory mechanisms, outweighing the effects of hormonal status.

Title: Clinical and cardiovascular impact of pregnancy in women with Marfan syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome (MS) is associated with mutations in the FBN1 gene, which encodes fibrillin-1, an essential protein in elastic fibers. Cardiovascular damage in MS has serious complications such as aneurysms and aortic dissection (AD), which increase during pregnancy.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cardiovascular and clinical status of women with Marfan syndrome and pregnancy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study in women with MS or other connective tissue diseases (CTD) classified according to the 2010 Ghent criteria.
RESULTS: One hundred women were included, 35 were admitted as pediatric patients, and 65 as adults. Ten women without medical records were excluded. Forty-eight non-pregnant women and 46 pregnant women were analyzed. 20 births, 26 cesarean sections, 9 preeclampsia, and 14 miscarriages. Of the total group, 14 had con-genital heart disease, 36 had AD, 47 had aortic regurgitation, 22 had mitral valve regurgitation, 15 had tricuspid valve regurgitation, 39 had valve prolapse, 67 had surgeries, and 15 had stents. 19 died, 5 due to aneurysm rupture, 4 had AD, 3 had cardiogenic shock, 5 had septic shock, and 2 had hypovolemic shock.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular damage in pregnancies of women with MS or CTD is complex. The diagnosis of MS is late in some cases; it is at the time of delivery, and genetic counseling is not timely. These are areas of opportunity to impact on prevention, timely gynecological and obstetric status, and surgery.

Title: Lipid profile in mexican women at cardiaovascular risk.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women, particularly postmenopausal. Metabolic and social gender differences influence lipid profiles and cardiovascular risk. In Mexico, factors such as obesity, diabetes, hormonal contraceptive use, and limited healthcare access exacerbate this issue.
OBJECTIVE: To describe the lipid profile of Mexican women with high and very high cardiovascular risk, and compare it to that of men.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study from the REMEXDIS (Mexican Registry of Dyslipidemia) cohort. Clinical, demographic, and biochemical variables were analyzed in 17,532 patients (9536 women). Statistical tests were applied to identify sex-related differences.
RESULTS: Women had a higher body mass index and a lower rate of suspected familial hyper-cholesterolemia. Men had significantly higher levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and glucose. However, women were more frequently classified as very high cardiovascular risk (59.44% vs. 35.90%; p = 0.01). Notably, 48.36% of dyslipidemic women were previously undiagnosed.
CONCLUSIONS: Mexican women with cardiovascular risk exhibit distinct clinical and metabolic characteristics compared to men. These findings highlight the importance of gender-specific strategies for prevention, diagnosis, and management of cardiovascular disease in women.

Title: Sex differences in hospital mortality with the myocardial infarction code.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are differences in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), with a worse prognosis in women.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate sex differences in presentation, management of the myocardial infarction code and in-hospital mortality in the National Registry of Acute Coronary Syndromes.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A total of 62,118 adults (74% men and 26% women) with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) or non ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) treated in 177 hospitals were included. Treatment and prognosis were compared.
RESULTS: Women had higher comorbidity and lower smoking rates. STEMI was more prevalent in men (73.0% vs. 63.6%), and Non ST Elevation-Acute Coronary Ayndrome (NSTE-ACS) was more prevalent in women (36.4% vs. 27.0%). Under the heart attack code, reperfusion rates were higher in men: percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) 28.3% vs. 27.9%, fibrinolytic therapy (FT) 36.4% vs. 31.9%, and pharmaco-invasive strategy (PIS) 7.9% vs. 7.2%, respectively; non-reperfusion rates were higher in women (27.3% vs. 33%; p < 0.0001). Complications were more frequent in women, and mortality was also higher in women (15.3% vs. 10.4%; OR: 1.56; 95% CI: 1.48-1.65). In logistic regression, female sex, age, diabetes, and hypertension independently predicted in-hospital death.
CONCLUSIONS: Women received less reperfusion, greater comorbidity and mortality, therefore timely and equitable care in the myocardial infarction code must be guaranteed.

Title: Evaluation of Four-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate Dosing for Major Bleeding Following Cardiac Surgery.
Abstract: Four-factor prothrombin concentrate complex (4F-PCC) may be used for significant bleeding following cardiac surgery but the optimal dosing has not been established. The purpose of this study was to compare two dosing strategies of 4F-PCC in cardiac surgery patients. This retrospective chart review evaluated 4F-PCC dosing of 25 units/kg compared to 12.5 units/kg in cardiac surgery patients following a protocol change for 4F-PCC dosing. The primary outcome was major bleeding, defined as the number of patients receiving ≥3 packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusions within 24 h of 4F-PCC administration. Secondary outcomes included other surrogate markers for bleeding (eg, Use of other blood products and hemostatic agents), thrombotic events within 14 days of surgery, hospital length of stay, and all-cause mortality. A total of 42 patients were included (31 patients in the 25 units/kg group and 11 patients in the 12.5 units/kg group). There was no difference in the number of patients that received ≥3 PRBC transfusions between the two groups with 15 patients (47.4%) in 25 units/kg group and 3 patients (27.3%) in 12.5 units/kg (P = .299). Additionally, no difference was observed in amount of additional hemostatic agents administered, hospital length of stay or mortality between the two groups. A higher rate of thromboembolic events was observed among patients receiving 25 units/kg vs 12.5 units/kg (22.6% vs 0%, P = .161). Reduced dosing of 4F-PCC from 25 units/kg to 12.5 units/kg following cardiac surgery resulted in no difference in clinical or effectiveness outcomes.

Title: Tofacitinib 20 vs 30 mg in acute severe ulcerative colitis: a double-blind randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Tofacitinib has emerged as a promising therapy for acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) due to its rapid onset of action. We compared the efficacy and safety of tofacitinib 20 mg/day vs 30 mg/day, both administered with intravenous corticosteroids (IVCS), in patients with ASUC.
METHODS: This was a double-blind, pilot, randomized controlled trial. Adult patients with ASUC were randomized to receive either tofacitinib 20 mg/day (Group 1) or 30 mg/day (Group 2) along with IVCS (hydrocortisone, 100 mg IV every 6 hours). The primary endpoint was clinical response by day 7. The secondary outcome was the cumulative probability of medical rescue therapy or post discharge escalation of therapy or colectomy within 90 days.
RESULTS: Seventy-two patients were randomized, with 36 allocated to each treatment group. At day 7, clinical response was achieved in 33/36 (91.7%) patients in Group 1 and 31/36 (86.1%) in Group 2(RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.90-1.25; P = .46). The absolute difference in response rates was 5.6% (95% CI -9.98% to 21.34%). Rescue therapy was required in 3 patients in Group 1 (all received infliximab) and 5 patients in Group 2 (2 underwent colectomy and 3 received infliximab). Event-free survival at 90 days, defined as the absence of rescue therapy, treatment escalation, or colectomy, was similar between groups (83.3% vs 80.2%; log-rank P = .74). Adverse events were predominantly mild, with no reported venous thromboembolism or major adverse cardiovascular events.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory pilot trial, no statistically significant differences were observed with tofacitinib 30 mg/day compared with 20 mg/day when administered with IVCS.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Clinical Trials Registry-India: CTRI/2024/10/075098.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Clinical Relevance of Magnesium Supplementation In Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Abstract: Magnesium deficiency is common in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), affecting up to 48% of patients, yet remains underrecognized in routine clinical practice. A bidirectional relationship between hypomagnesemia and insulin resistance has been well characterized, and observational data consistently link higher magnesium intake to reduced risks of T2DM, hypertension, stroke, and heart failure. However, supplementation trials have yielded inconsistent results, limited by small sample sizes, short follow-up, heterogeneous formulations with differing bioavailability, and variable glycemic endpoints. Serum magnesium, the most widely used clinical measure, reflects less than 1% of total body stores and may fail to detect clinically significant depletion. No randomized trial has been powered for hard clinical outcomes such as diabetes prevention or cardiovascular events. Current American Diabetes Association guidelines recommend magnesium screening and supplementation only in high-risk groups with documented deficiency, with emphasis on dietary optimization as a first-line strategy. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through December 2025, with priority given to meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, prospective cohort studies, and clinical practice guidelines, particularly the ADA position statement and the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Magnesium Fact Sheet. This narrative review critically examines the evidence linking magnesium to glycemic control and cardiovascular risk in T2DM, highlights key methodological limitations, and identifies research priorities such as biomarker validation, formulation comparison trials, and adequately powered cardiovascular outcome studies needed to determine whether magnesium optimization should be incorporated into routine diabetes care.

Title: The Burden of Type 1 Peri-Operative Myocardial Infarction After Non-Cardiac Surgery: Insights From the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project From 2010-2023.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence of perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI), the quality-of-care patients receive and their outcomes, and how this varies across different operations.
METHODS: We included adults from England with AMI between Jan 2010 and March 2023 from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project registry, linked to Hospital Episode Statistics (HES). Cox-regression models compared risk of all-cause mortality at thirty-days and five-years, subgroup analyses compared operation type (orthopaedic, vascular, upper (UGI) and lower gastrointestinal (LGI) and urological).
RESULTS: We identified 2,821 episodes of type 1 PMI in 533,026 eligible patients (0.5%). Orthopaedics were the largest contributing speciality (45%). Risk of thirty-day mortality was significantly higher in PMI patients at thirty-days (adjusted Hazard Ratio):1.34 [95% CIs 1.21-1.49]) and five-years (1.36 [1.29-1.43]) (both P<0.001). For thirty-day mortality, risk was not significant in orthopaedics and urology but was for vascular (1.75 [1.40-2.18]), UGI (1.95 [1.43-2.66) and LGI surgery (1.94 [1.50-2.51]) (all P<0.001). For those who survived to hospital discharge, PMI patients had higher mortality risk at five-years (1.26 [1.19-1.34), especially high in the UGI (1.76 [1.44-2.13]), LGI (1.34 [1.13-1.59]) and urology groups (1.61 [1.34-1.93]) (all P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: PMI mortality is significantly higher than AMI all-comers, seen across all subspecialties up to five-years, with variation in the risk of mortality from PMI according to operation type. PMI may identify a high-risk vulnerable group of patients, whose increased mortality risk persists long term, even in those who survive to discharge.

Title: Multi-Institutional Review of Inferior Vena Cava Filter Use in Pediatric Patients.
Journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Children at risk for pulmonary embolism (PE) may be treated with inferior vena cava (IVC) filter insertion when anticoagulation is impossible or ineffective. The purpose of this multi-institutional retrospective review is to better understand the indications and technical and clinical outcomes related to IVC filter placement and removal in pediatric patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was open to all institutions that placed IVC filters in pediatric patients. Data collected included demographics, indications, procedural details of filter insertion and/or removal, and clinical follow-up. Univariate analysis was performed.
RESULTS: A total of 250 filters were placed in 242 pediatric patients (135 male) at 12 participating hospitals between October 1994 and June 2020. Thrombosis was present in 82.8% of patients, PE in 34.8%, and anticoagulation adverse events (AEs) or contraindications in 45.9%. Most filter insertions were technically successful (99.1%); 3.1% were associated with minor AEs, and 0.4% with moderate AEs. Breakthrough pulmonary embolism occurred in 1.4% following filter placement. Filter retrieval rate was 76%. Removal was technically successful in 88% of attempts and resulted in minor AEs in 1.1% and severe AEs in 6.5%. Minor, moderate, and severe device-associated AEs occurred in 8%, 1.6%, and 3.2% of filters, respectively. There was no correlation between age or weight and outcomes, including breakthrough PE, AEs, or mortality.
CONCLUSION: IVC filter insertion in pediatric patients is feasible and associated with a high retrieval rate.

Title: Diabetes, Long-term mortality, and LDL-C target attainment after an acute coronary syndrome: A population-based cohort study (2016-2024).
Abstract:
AIMS: To quantify the excess acute coronary syndrome (ACS) burden and post-ACS mortality associated with diabetes and assess LDL-C target attainment, focusing on sex differences.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 5,361 patients with the first ACS admission identified during the study period (2016-2024) in a Spanish healthcare department. Hospitalization trends were analyzed using population-based regression models. Long-term mortality was assessed by Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression. LDL-C target attainment was evaluated according to ESC/EAS recommendations.
RESULTS: Diabetes was present in 36.9 % of patients. ACS hospitalization rates declined by 8.3 % annually (95 % CI 6.1-10.4), with no diabetes-by-time interaction (p = 0.17). In-hospital case fatality was 6.3 % and did not differ by diabetes status. During a median 4.9-year follow-up, diabetes was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.22, 95 % CI 1.11-1.33), with a stronger association in women than men (interaction p = 0.009). Only 28.9 % achieved LDL-C < 55 mg/dL, with no temporal improvement; female sex independently predicted poor LDL-C control (adjusted OR 1.65, 95 % CI 1.38-1.97).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite declining ACS hospitalizations, DM remained associated with increased long-term mortality, particularly in women. LDL-C target attainment remained suboptimal, highlighting persistent gaps in secondary prevention.

Title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease Without Dedicated Guidelines.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms (SAAs) represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695) RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported.
