OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings.
METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62).
CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

Title: Graph neural network for predicting reentrant drivers in atrial digital twins.
Journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Atrial Fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with high risk of stroke and heart failure. While pulmonary vein isolation is a standard treatment, its efficacy is suboptimal for patients with persistent AF (PsAF), resulting in high recurrence rates. Increasing evidence indicates that fibrotic remodeling can create arrhythmogenic substrates outside the pulmonary veins, which may contribute to recurrence. Previous works have shown that PsAF Digital Twins (DT) can locate these arrhythmogenic regions and inform ablation targets for AF treatment, characterizing the full arrhythmogenic substrate through iterative simulations, including emergent reentries. While PsAF DTs are effective, their use in clinical practice is constrained by substantial computational demands.
METHODS: In this study, we developed a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to directly identify regions sustaining reentrant drivers (ablation targets) without the need of computationally expensive simulations. The GNN was trained on 31 high-resolution PsAF DTs. Afterwards, the GNN's predictions were prospectively validated on four new PsAF DTs, where the predictions served as virtual ablation targets and new simulations were performed to evaluate the GNN's predictions to eliminate reentrant drivers on new geometries and fibrotic distributions.
RESULTS: Across 8-fold cross validation, the GNN achieved an AUROC of 0.884 and an AUPRC of 0.174, both of which surpassed all other tested models. GNN's positive predictions with the greatest confidence were refined to regions with high fibrotic density and moderate fibrotic entropy. In the proof-of-concept prospective validation, GNN-guided ablation reduced emergent reentries by over 70% relative to the wide antral circumferential ablation pulmonary vein isolation (WACA PVI)-only control and reduced the mean number of additional simulation rounds required to reach non-inducibility by 66%.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the potential of a GNN to guide DT-based ablation for PsAF patients and to reduce the iterative simulation burden of DT workflows. These findings support the feasibility of GNN-guided substrate prioritization, with further validation supporting clinical integration.

Title: High- and low-nitrate vegetable intake produce similar effects on redox, inflammatory, and cardiometabolic markers in older adults: a randomized crossover trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare effects of high-nitrate (HN) and low-nitrate (LN) vegetable intake on redox, inflammatory, and cardiometabolic biomarkers in community-dwelling older adults.
METHODS: In this randomized, crossover trial, 39 older adults ≥60 years consumed 250 g/day of either HN or LN vegetables for 7 days, separated by a 7-day washout period. Assessments before and after each intervention included plasma and urinary NOx (nitrate and nitrite), blood pressure, lipid profile, triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase [SOD], catalase [CAT], glutathione peroxidase [GPx], glutathione S-transferase [GST]), serum total antioxidant capacity (sTAC), oxidative damage markers (malondialdehyde [MDA], protein carbonyls), cytokines (IL-6, IL-10; reduced subsamples, n = 18 and n = 35, respectively), and dietary/physical activity recalls. Treatment effects (HN vs. LN) were assessed using covariate-adjusted linear mixed-effects models (p < 0.05); effect size was calculated as Cohen's d (|d|).
RESULTS: The HN intervention provided a measured mean nitrate intake of 431.5 ± 163.6 mg/day and substantially increased plasma and urinary NOx concentrations compared to LN (p < 0.001). However, this did not translate into significant differences in any redox, inflammatory, or cardiometabolic markers (all p > 0.05). Effect sizes for between-intervention comparisons were consistently small (|d| ≤ 0.40), with the largest effects observed for GST (|d| = 0.40), TyG index (|d| = 0.32), and systolic blood pressure (|d| = 0.28).
CONCLUSIONS: No incremental contribution of nitrate-rich vegetable matrices to redox, inflammatory, or cardiometabolic markers was detected. The clinical relevance of nitrate-rich vegetables may be more apparent in populations with compromised vascular or metabolic function.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NUMBER: RBR-102bc3f2, website: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-102bc3f2. Date of registration: 26th September, 2022.

Title: Transplacental Flecainide and/or Digoxin for Fetal Tachyarrhythmias: Therapeutic Efficacy and Clinical Experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the efficacy and safety of transplacental flecainide and/or digoxin for fetal tachyarrhythmias when sotalol is unavailable.
METHOD: We evaluated transplacental flecainide, digoxin, or combination therapy in a retrospective and prospective cohort across two Thai tertiary centers. Outcomes were classified as complete cardioversion, partial response (rate control), or treatment failure.
RESULTS: Of 24 eligible pregnancies, 14 (58.3%) had supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), 8 (33.3%) had atrial flutter (AFL), and 2 (8.3%) had ventricular tachycardia (VT). Overall, clinical responses occurred in 91.7% (22/24) of fetuses. Flecainide monotherapy achieved 100% (9/9) complete cardioversion in SVT, compared with 50% (1/2) for digoxin. SVT combination therapy (n = 3) yielded 1 complete and 1 partial response. Among 7 flecainide-treated AFL cases, 5 (71.4%) achieved rate control and 2 (28.6%) achieved cardioversion; one digoxin-treated case fully converted. Flecainide resolved 1 of 2 VT cases (50%). Response rates were unaffected by hydrops, gestational age, or cardiac defects (p = 0.087-1.000). Maternal adverse events were mild and required no treatment discontinuation.
CONCLUSION: Transplacental flecainide demonstrates high efficacy in SVT and effective rate control with preserved cardiac function in AFL. Its favorable safety profile makes it a practical alternative for first-line therapy where sotalol is unavailable and flecainide monitoring is infeasible.

Title: Standardized Technique for Full Laser Ablation of Feeding Artery in Fetuses With Bronchopulmonary Sequestration and Large Pleural Effusion: Lessons Learned Over 14 Years of Experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report on perinatal outcomes and technical aspects of standardized fetal surgery technique with full laser coagulation of the feeding artery in fetuses with bronchopulmonary sequestration and large pleural effusion.
METHOD: During a 14-year period, a prospective cohort of fetuses with BPS and large pleural effusion were selected for laser coagulation in a single national reference center for fetal surgery. Feasibility, perinatal outcomes, complications, survival, respiratory morbidity, and need for neonatal lung mass resection are reported.
RESULTS: 29 fetuses were treated at a median gestational age of 28.4 weeks. Hydrops was present in 13 (44.8%) cases. In 2 fetuses (6.9%), an intrathoracic bleeding was observed during fetal intervention, one presenting with intrauterine demise at 23 weeks of gestation. Median gestational age at birth was 38.9 weeks. Two fetuses (6.9%) were born preterm (33 and 35 weeks). Neonatal respiratory morbidity was reported in 3 neonates requiring oxygen support and in 2 neonates requiring mechanical ventilation. One fetus required postnatal thoracic surgery. There were no neonatal deaths; hence, the overall survival rate was 96.6% (28/29).
CONCLUSIONS: Fetuses with BPS and large pleural effusion treated by laser coagulation of the feeding vessel have good perinatal outcomes and low risk of complications.

Title: AI-Driven Lifestyle Interventions for Reducing Diabetes Risk: Systematic Review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven lifestyle interventions are increasingly used for reducing diabetes risk. However, whether they produce clinical benefit beyond standard Diabetes Prevention Programs (DPPs) and whether effects vary by AI type, population, or delivery setting, remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of AI-driven lifestyle interventions on clinical, behavioral, and engagement outcomes among people with prediabetes or elevated diabetes risk and to assess whether effects differed by AI type, population, or delivery setting.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ClinicalTrials.gov, and citation searches were completed on August 3, 2026, for English-language reports published from 2015. Eligible studies evaluated AI-driven digital lifestyle interventions among people with prediabetes or elevated diabetes risks, or healthy participants in feasibility studies. One reviewer (OIE) screened records and extracted data; a second reviewer (TN) independently verified exclusions and extraction. Study quality was assessed with National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute tools appropriate to each design. Given substantial heterogeneity in designs, estimands, and outcome metrics, findings were synthesized narratively following the Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis guideline rather than pooled statistically.
RESULTS: Of 8032 records, 11 studies were included: 1 randomized, 1 nonrandomized comparative, 4 observational, and 5 uncontrolled pre-post studies. Seven evaluated AI lifestyle coaching systems, 2 predictive AI platforms, and 2 conversational AI chatbots. Ten of 11 studies used commercially developed platforms. Study quality was rated good for 5 studies, fair for 3, and poor for 3. The randomized controlled trial showed noninferiority of an AI-DPP versus human coach-led DPP for the combined 12-month outcome (23/183, 12.6% vs 23/185, 12.4%; risk difference 0.1%, 1-sided 95% CI -5.5%). Program initiation (171/183, 93.4% vs 153/185, 82.7%; risk difference 10.7%, 95% CI 4.2%-17.3%) and completion (117/183, 63.9% vs 93/185, 50.3%; risk difference 13.7%; 95% CI 3.6%-23.7%) were higher with AI, but this did not translate into superior clinical outcomes. The nonrandomized comparison found no advantage of AI-personalized messaging over static messaging in terms of BMI or physical activity. The remaining studies reported uncontrolled changes precluding causal inference. Evidence was insufficient to determine whether effects differed by population or delivery setting.
CONCLUSIONS: One randomized trial supports noninferiority, not superiority, of a specific AI-driven DPP relative to human coaching; the remaining evidence was nonrandomized, predominantly commercially developed, and hypothesis-generating. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic review to stratify evidence on AI-driven diabetes prevention by AI mechanism-coaching, predictive, and conversational-and by outcome domain, extending prior scoping work that mapped apps without appraising study quality or comparative effectiveness. This structured mapping shows where evidence is the strongest (engagement and weight) and the weakest (glycemic causality and generalizability), giving health systems a concrete basis for deciding where AI-DPP tools may supplement, rather than replace, standard DPP delivery, pending independent, adequately powered randomized trials.

Title: A Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Functional Status and Estimating Health Care Costs in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and progressive disease associated with substantial clinical heterogeneity and high health care costs. While machine learning (ML) has been increasingly applied to predict clinical outcomes, approaches that integrate clinical prediction with downstream economic modeling remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study proposes and evaluates an ML-based framework that combines prediction of future functional status with estimation of associated health care costs in patients with PAH.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, data from 181 patients with PAH were analyzed. A total of 6 supervised ML algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator [LASSO] regression, ridge regression, k-nearest neighbors, decision trees, random forest, and gradient boosting) were trained to predict the relative change in World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC) from baseline to 12-month follow-up using baseline clinical variables. Predicted change rates were subsequently converted to predicted WHO-FC values at the 12-month follow-up for downstream health care cost estimation. Missing values in predictor variables were imputed using median substitution. Median imputation was performed before the dataset was split into training and test sets. Model performance was evaluated using Pearson correlation coefficient (r), and error metrics (RMSE, MAE, and MedAE), based on cross-validation and independent test set validation. Predicted WHO-FC values were subsequently linked to externally validated, stratified real-world health care cost estimates to approximate future economic burden.
RESULTS: Among the evaluated models, k-nearest neighbors showed the highest predictive performance (r=0.40; R2=0.16), followed by LASSO regression (r=0.30; R2=0.09). Prediction errors were comparable across models. Estimated mean health care costs ranged from US $12,481 to $12,614 per patient per month. Despite a significant improvement in WHO-FC over 12 months, estimated health care costs remained largely unchanged, reflecting persistent economic burden across functional class strata.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility of an ML-based framework that integrates prediction of functional status with health care cost estimation in PAH. While predictive performance was moderate, the approach illustrates how ML models can be extended beyond clinical end points toward system-level applications such as cost forecasting and resource planning. Further validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is required before clinical or health system implementation.

Title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses.
METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests.
RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata.
CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits.

Title: Loncastuximab and Rituximab in Elderly Unfit/Frail Patients With Previously Untreated Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma.
Abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) therapy is typically treated with multi-agent chemotherapy with curative intent but is often challenging or poorly tolerated in patients who are elderly, frail, or have significant comorbidities. LOTIS-9 was a phase 2 trial of loncastuximab tesirine (loncastuximab tesirine-lpyl [Lonca]) plus rituximab (Lonca-R) in patients with newly diagnosed DLBCL who were unfit (cohort A) or frail with or without cardiac comorbidities (cohort B), the majority of whom typically would be ineligible for trials. Patients received Lonca (150 µg/kg during cycles 1-2, 75 µg/kg for subsequent cycles) and R (375 mg/m2) intravenously Q3W for 3-6 cycles, adapted based on response after cycle 3. The primary endpoint of cohort A was complete response (CR) rate; coprimary endpoints of cohort B were CR rate and proportion of patients who completed treatment per protocol. The median age was 84 years (range, 80-91) in cohort A (n=17) and 80 years (range, 67-92) in cohort B (n=24). The CR rates were 52.9% (A: 9/17) and 41.7% (B: 10/24), respectively. In cohort B, 8 (33.3%) patients completed treatment. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 31 (75.6%) patients, including 11 fatal events. Due to toxicity concerns in this medically fragile population, LOTIS-9 was voluntarily terminated prematurely though meaningful efficacy was demonstrated in patients who typically would be ineligible for clinical trials and/or standard of care therapies. These findings provide important insights for future trials. Additional investigation of targeted therapies in vulnerable unfit and frail patients with DLBCL is warranted. (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05144009).

Title: Clinical characteristics and severity classification in mixed connective tissue disease: a nationwide retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize clinical manifestations, major organ involvement, real-world treatment patterns and factors associated with severity classification in Japanese patients with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), aiming to clarify its heterogeneous clinical spectrum.
METHODS: This nationwide retrospective multicentre study analyzed clinical data from 249 patients who strictly fulfilled the 2019 Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare diagnostic criteria for MCTD, derived from an initial real-world registry of 311 clinically diagnosed patients. Clinical features, autoantibodies and therapeutic regimens were summarized and compared between patients with severe vs nonsevere disease.
RESULTS: The cohort was 93.1% female (median onset age 40.6 years). Common findings, specifically Raynaud's phenomenon and/or swelling of the fingers or dorsum of the hands, were present in 100%. Phenotypically, an overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-like and systemic sclerosis (SSc)-like features was most frequent (56.0%), while 32.0% had manifestations across all three phenotypic domains (SLE-, SSc- and IIM-like). Major organ involvement occurred in 32.9% of patients, including pulmonary arterial hypertension in 12.8%. Approximately 28.7% of evaluable patients were classified as severe. Off-scale-high anti-U1-RNP antibody status was not associated with severity classification (P = 0.492) or with broad phenotypic categories. Glucocorticoids and immunosuppressive agents were used in 66.7% and 56.5% of the patients, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Mixed connective tissue disease exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity. Severity classification was not associated with off-scale-high anti-U1-RNP antibody status or broad phenotypic categories. These findings support rigorous cardiopulmonary screening and management tailored to the dominant clinical phenotype.

Title: Intracerebral Hemorrhage Expansion in Late Presenters: Proposed Target Expansion Criteria.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The benefit of therapies targeting hematoma expansion (HE) in acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is highly time dependent and greatest within the first 2 hours after onset. We aimed to develop imaging-based "target expansion criteria" to identify late presenters (2-12 hours from onset/last seen well) who remain at high risk of HE. To achieve this goal, a practical risk score (target expansion score) was developed.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, international, retrospective cohort study. To mirror a clinical trial population, we excluded patients with brainstem ICH, anticoagulation, and baseline ICH volume >100 mL. The primary outcome was HE (>33%/6 mL). The following imaging predictors of HE were analyzed: high ultra-early hematoma growth (uHG) (baseline volume/onset to imaging time >10 mL/h), hypodensities on noncontrast CT (NCCT), and spot sign on CT angiography (CTA). The study population was randomly divided into development and validation cohorts, and a weighted score was derived from estimates from multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Overall, 492 patients were included: 345 (70.1%) in the development and 147 (29.9%) in the validation cohort. A 4-point score was created, based on independent predictors of HE (high uHG: 1 point, NCCT hypodensities: 1 point, and CTA spot sign: 2 points). The score showed good discrimination in the development and validation cohorts (area under the curve [AUC] 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.83, and AUC 0.79, 95% CI 0.71-0.87, respectively). We observed a nonlinear increase in the frequency of HE and mean absolute hematoma growth with higher scores: 9.8% and 0.9 mL (score 0), 17.1% and 3.9 mL (score 1), 48.3% and 11.5 mL (score 2), 70.8% and 13.0 mL (score 3), and 87.5% and 26.9 mL (score 4). These findings were confirmed in the validation cohort. A dichotomized score greater than or equal to 2 predicted HE with 0.61 sensitivity and 0.85 specificity in the development cohort and 0.64 sensitivity with 0.84 specificity in the validation cohort.
DISCUSSION: Imaging-based target expansion criteria, defined as a target expansion score ≥2, identified late-presenting patients with ICH at high risk of HE. These findings might inform future trials targeting HE and increase the pool of eligible patients.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Organ damage profiles and associated factors in juvenile versus adult-onset SLE: a matched analysis from the Japanese ANSWER-SLE cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To elucidate differences in organ damage in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) between juvenile-onset (<18 years) and adult-onset (≥18 years) using the Systemic Lupus International Collaborating Clinics Damage Index (SDI).
METHODS: Among patients in the multicenter registry, ANSWER-SLE (2019-2023), total-SDI and organ domains of SDI were compared between juvenile- and adult-onset patients after 1:2 matching based on sex and current age. Factors associated with total SDI and organ domains of SDI were analyzed by regression models in the total population.
RESULTS: A total of 615 patients were included. Among them, 83 juvenile- and 166 adult-onset patients were matched. Juvenile-onset showed higher total-SDI (juvenile-onset vs. adult-onset, 2.17 vs. 1.16) and higher damage in the ocular, nervous system, renal, cardiovascular, and musculoskeletal domains than adult-onset. In the multivariable negative binomial regression analysis of the total cohort, younger age at onset (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.99, p=0.005) and older current age (IRR 1.03, p<0.001) were independently associated with higher total SDI scores. These associations persisted in the matched cohort (IRR 0.96 and IRR 1.03, respectively). In multivariable analyses of organ-specific damage adjusted for sex, current age, and age at onset, younger age at onset was associated with a higher SDI in the cataract, angina/coronary artery bypass, valvular disease, avascular necrosis, skin ulceration, and premature gonadal failure in the total cohort, and additionally with renal domain in the matched cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Juvenile-onset SLE is associated with organ damage compared to adult-onset SLE, with prominent ocular, neurological, renal, cardiovascular, and musculoskeletal systems.

Title: Relationship between Endothelial Activation and Stress Index and Coronary Artery Ectasia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery ectasia (CAE) is characterized by abnormal dilatation of the coronary arteries and is associated with endothelial dysfunction and systemic inflammation. The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) has emerged as a novel biomarker reflecting endothelial activation and inflammatory stress.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between EASIX score and the presence of CAE.
METHODS: A total of 300 patients who underwent coronary angiography between July 2018 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The study was designed as a case-control study. Patients were divided into two groups according to the presence of CAE (150 CAE, 150 controls). The EASIX score was calculated using the following formula: EASIX = LDH × Creatinine / Platelet . Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine the predictive value of EASIX for CAE. Youden index statistical analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic power of ROC analysis and to calculate the optimal cut-off value. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Patients with CAE had significantly higher EASIX score compared with controls (1.46 ± 0.33 vs. 0.98 ± 0.74). In the ROC analysis, EASIX score had 72% sensitivity and 58% specificity when the cut-off value for EASIX≥ 0.74 (AUC=0.688, 95% CI:0.618-0.759, p<0.001). In Multivariable logistic regression analysis, the EASIX score was identified as an independent predictor of CAE (OR =2.12, 95% CI: 1.35-3.34, p=0.001).
CONCLUSION: The EASIX score was independently associated with the presence of CAE and demonstrated moderate discriminative ability.

Title: Effectiveness of a fully digital mandibular advancement appliance compared with CPAP in the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinicians often face the decision of recommending Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) or a Mandibular Advancement Appliance (MAA) for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA).
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of a fully digital workflow MAA and compare its outcomes with CPAP therapy.
METHODS: Twenty adults with OSA confirmed by Type I polysomnography (AHI < 50 events/hour), non-adherent to CPAP, were enrolled in a crossover clinical study. After MAA titration (50% and 75% of maximum protrusion), participants underwent home sleep testing under three conditions: no treatment, CPAP, and MAA. Outcomes included oxygen desaturation index (ODI), snoring score, oxyhemoglobin saturation (SpO₂), hypoxic burden, and mean heart rate. Treatment-induced changes (Δ = treatment - no treatment) were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (α = 5%).
RESULTS: Both therapies significantly reduced ODI and snoring, compared to baseline. Median ODI decreased from 13.55 events/hour (untreated) to 6.05 with MAA and 5.30 with CPAP. No statistically significant differences were found between MAA and CPAP for ΔODI (p = 0.401), snoring (p = 0.103), hypoxic burden (p = 0.165), or heart rate (p = 0.824). A significant difference in SpO₂ was observed (p = 0.003), favoring CPAP; however, the difference was small.
CONCLUSIONS: The fully digital MAA was effective in reducing oxygen desaturation, snoring, and hypoxic burden, showing no clinically meaningful difference compared with CPAP, supporting its use as a viable therapeutic alternative for OSA.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Comparative Study

Title: Clinical features and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana: Insights from a retrospective study (2015-2021).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a re-emerging public health threat in French Guiana with a broad clinical spectrum. Neurological involvement (neuroleptospirosis) lacks a consensus definition and may be underrecognized. This study aimed to characterize its epidemiology, clinical features, outcomes, and associated factors.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted across healthcare facilities in French Guiana from 2015 to 2021. Consecutive hospital-managed patients with laboratory-confirmed or probable leptospirosis were included. Neuroleptospirosis was defined by neurological symptoms combined with objective cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and/or neuro-imaging abnormalities. Patients with and without neurological involvement were compared.
RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 18 (12%) met the criteria for neuroleptospirosis, corresponding to a mean annual incidence of 0.88 cases/100,000 inhabitants (95% conference interval [CI], 0.52-1.39). Presentations were meningeal (78% [14/18]), encephalitic (17% [3/18]) or meningoencephalitic (6% [1/18]). Lumbar puncture was performed in 28/146 (19%) patients; pleocytosis was observed in 18/28 (64%). The median CSF leukocyte count was 42 cells/mm3 (interquartile range [IQR], 13-240 cells/mm3), with lymphocytic predominance in 8/13 differential counts (62%). CSF protein was mildly elevated (median, 0.51 g/L; IQR, 0.32-0.88), without hypoglycorrhachia. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed abnormalities in 2/8 patients with neuroleptospirosis: one cerebral infarction and one case of pachymeningitis. Age under 30 years (odds ratio [OR], 5.56; 95% CI, 1.72-18), absence of leukocytosis during hospitalization (OR, 3.29; 95% CI, 1.04-10.39), and absence of thrombocytopenia (OR, 4.46; 95% CI, 1.39-14.32) were associated with neuroleptospirosis. Under our diagnostic criteria, neuroleptospirosis cases were associated with favorable outcomes, with lower odds of sepsis (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.10-0.79), no intensive care unit admissions or deaths.
CONCLUSIONS: This study clarifies the clinical spectrum and outcomes of neuroleptospirosis in French Guiana, highlighting the importance of clinical awareness in tropical endemic settings. Prospective studies incorporating systematic CSF analysis and microbiological testing are needed to improve understanding of its pathophysiology and standardize diagnostic pathways.

Title: Lifestyle factors and clustered patterns of body shape change in Korean adults: A longitudinal observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major health problem driven by lifestyle habits and changes in body composition, particularly increased body fat mass and reduced skeletal muscle mass. Body mass index alone cannot fully characterize adiposity distribution or changes in muscle mass. Body-shape indicators such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio predict metabolic and cardiovascular disease risk; however, few studies have assessed longitudinal changes in these measures together with lifestyle factors. In this study, we aimed to identify clusters of body-shape change using 2-year follow-up data from Korean adults and to elucidate the body-composition and lifestyle factors underlying these changes.
METHODS: K-means cluster analysis was applied to 1,404 participants in the Korean Medicine Daejeon Citizen Cohort using 2-year changes in body mass index, waist circumference, hip circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio, and body weight. Baseline body shape, body composition, and lifestyle indicators were compared across clusters, and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify variables associated with cluster membership.
RESULTS: Three clusters were identified: Stable (48.0%), Adiposity-Increasing (31.0%), and Adiposity-Decreasing (21.0%). At baseline, cluster membership was significantly associated with body fat mass. Over follow-up, changes in body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass showed strong associations with cluster assignment. In addition, clinically meaningful worsening in sleep quality (increase of ≥2.5 points in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index) and reduced physical activity (decrease in activity as measured by the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire) were significantly associated with the Adiposity-Increasing cluster.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in body composition, especially body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass, were closely associated with body-shape trajectories, while worsening sleep quality and declining physical activity were associated with the Adiposity-Increasing trajectory. These findings support an integrative approach that considers body shape, body composition, and modifiable lifestyle factors when characterizing adiposity-related trajectories and designing tailored lifestyle interventions.

Title: Change in hearing loss and its association with general health in a community-based longitudinal study of middle-aged individuals: The Busselton healthy ageing study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: With the ageing of the global population, disabling hearing loss is a major health concern. While age and sex are established determinants, the relation between general and environmental health factors and the progression of hearing loss remains incompletely understood, particularly in middle-aged adults.
METHODS: We used data from the Busselton Healthy Ageing Study (BHAS), a population-based cohort in Western Australia. Adults aged 45-70 years at baseline (2010-2015) underwent audiometric testing and health assessments with a six-year follow-up. The better-ear four-frequency Pure Tone Averages for 0.5-4kHZ (4FPTA) and for high frequencies (4 & 8 kHz) (HFPTA) were calculated. Hearing loss was classified according to WHO criteria. Demographic, ear-related, general health, and environmental factors were analysed and their association with change in hearing thresholds using linear mixed models.
RESULTS: 3596 participants with reliable audiometry at baseline and follow-up were included (mean baseline age 57.9 years, 55% female). Over 6 years follow-up, the prevalence of mild-or-greater hearing loss increased from 14% to 26% (4FPTA) and from 53% to 71% (HFPTA). Thresholds worsened across all age categories, with greater deterioration in men and at higher frequencies. In univariate models, older age, male sex, higher BMI, smoking, tinnitus, chronic ear infection, noisy workplace exposure (particularly with inconsistent or absent hearing protection), hypertension and pre-diabetes were significantly associated with faster hearing decline after adjustments for age and sex.
CONCLUSIONS: In this longitudinal population-based study of middle-aged Western Australians we demonstrated that hearing thresholds significantly declined over a six-year period with greater deterioration in men and at higher frequencies. Findings suggest that hearing loss progression in midlife is shaped not only by age and sex, but also by broader metabolic and environmental health profiles. These outcomes highlight the need for future research to further clarify the complex interplay between metabolic health, environmental exposures, and hearing outcomes.

Title: Incremental Predictive Value of Month-1 OCT and OCT Angiography for Residual Exudative Activity After Anti-VEGF Loading in Treatment-Naive Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: During the anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) loading phase for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), the month-1 follow-up visit represents the earliest standardized imaging time point, yet whether month-1 optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA) improve prediction of short-term anatomical outcome beyond baseline OCT has not been formally tested. This study quantified the incremental predictive value of month-1 imaging using a nested-model framework that mirrors the sequential clinical workflow.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included 124 treatment-naive nAMD eyes from 105 patients that completed three monthly anti-VEGF injections and had evaluable baseline, month-1, and month-3 imaging. Poor anatomical outcome was defined as residual intraretinal fluid and/or subretinal fluid at month 3. Nested generalized estimating equation logistic models accounted for inclusion of bilateral eyes and evaluated baseline OCT variables, the incremental contribution of month-1 structural OCT, and the additional contribution of month-1 OCTA-derived macular neovascularization (MNV) area. Discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with ΔAUC confidence intervals estimated by patient-level cluster bootstrap.
RESULTS: At month 3, 47 of 124 eyes (37.9%) had residual exudative activity. In the final model, month-1 central subfield thickness (OR 2.065 per 100-µm increase, 95% CI 1.107-3.853), residual month-1 intraretinal fluid (OR 14.623, 95% CI 3.305-64.703), residual month-1 subretinal fluid (OR 6.975, 95% CI 1.963-24.785), and month-1 MNV area (OR 1.130 per 1-mm² increase, 95% CI 1.030-1.240) were associated with poor month-3 anatomical outcome. AUC improved from 0.742 (95% CI 0.658-0.822) with baseline OCT alone to 0.889 (95% CI 0.828-0.940) after adding month-1 structural OCT (ΔAUC 0.147, 95% CI 0.072-0.226), and to 0.908 (95% CI 0.853-0.952) after adding month-1 MNV area. Baseline-to-month-1 quantitative changes were not associated with outcome.
CONCLUSION: Month-1 structural OCT substantially improved prediction of month-3 residual exudative activity beyond baseline OCT alone, whereas OCTA-derived MNV area contributed modest additional discrimination. These findings identify the first post-treatment imaging visit as an informative point for short-term anatomical risk assessment, but external validation is required before clinical application.

Title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices.
AIMS: The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI.
METHODS: Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance.
RESULTS: Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions.
CONCLUSION: The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.

Title: Mechanical Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation - Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention during Cardiac Arrest: Feasibility and Outcomes.
Journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
Abstract: Cardiac arrest complicating acute coronary syndromes requires immediate coronary reperfusion; however, performing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) during active manual cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) presents significant technical challenges. The Lund University Cardiac Arrest System (LUCAS) provides automated mechanical chest compressions and enables uninterrupted CPR during coronary angiography and PCI. Existing evidence is primarily limited to case reports and small observational studies, mechanical CPR has emerged as a practical adjunct in catheterization laboratories where manual compressions are unsafe or logistically challenging. We report two cases from our center in which LUCAS-assisted PCI was performed during ongoing cardiac arrest in the setting of cardiogenic shock and acute coronary syndromes, alongside a structured narrative synthesis of contemporary literature addressing feasibility, procedural considerations, and clinical outcomes. Mechanical chest compressions allowed uninterrupted angiography and successful revascularization in both cases, with return of spontaneous circulation achieved in 1 patient. Despite procedural success, survival remained poor, reflecting severe global ischemia and metabolic derangement. LUCAS-assisted PCI is a technically feasible strategy that facilitates coronary reperfusion in carefully selected patients. Evidence of survival benefit remains limited and derives predominantly from observational studies and case reports rather than randomized controlled trials. The role of extracorporeal CPR as a complementary or alternative strategy warrants explicit consideration at appropriately resourced centers. Improved patient selection and integration into structured resuscitation pathways may enhance clinical outcomes.

Title: Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation; results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
Journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis after pLT.
METHODS: Our study analyzed data from the Portal vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers, across 18 countries, over a 20-year period. Graft- and patient survival rates were determined after PVS diagnosis.
RESULTS: This study included 239 patients (53% female; median age at pLT 1.1 years) diagnosed with PVS. The median age at diagnosis was 2.7 years. The overall ten-year graft survival was 90%, and the ten-year patient survival was 96%. One-year graft and patient survival was lowest in patients with PVS diagnosed ≤7 days after pLT (80% and 92%, respectively). Initial treatment strategies comprised of mostly endovascular procedures (87%), followed by conservative (11%) and surgical treatment (3%). Patient outcome did not differ between these treatment groups. Within the endovascular group, graft survival in patients treated with stent (n=26) was significantly lower compared to those with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (n=181) (88% vs 98%, respectively, p=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.

Title: Differences in treatment and outcome of patients with ST- elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI in Germany.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-STEMI (NSTEMI) are very similar regarding pathophysiology and clinical treatments, especially NSTEMI comprises a much more heterogenic group of patients and underlying diseases. We therefore aimed to assess the treatments and outcomes of both entities in a large contemporary cohort.
METHODS: Patients with STEMI and NSTEMI between 01/01/2010-31/12/2018 were identified from the largest German health insurance (AOK, ≈ 26 million members). Patient demographics, their hospital course, adherence to guideline-directed drug therapy and overall survival were assessed.
RESULTS: In total 544,529 patients (mean age 74, IQR 62-82), one third of whom had a STEMI. Chronic kidney disease, peripheral arterial disease, and heart failure were more common in patients with NSTEMI. Patients with STEMI were more likely to get coronary angiograms and percutaneous coronary interventions. Although STEMI more frequently led to cardiogenic shock, the rate of serious cardiac events was lower. Mortality was higher for STEMI only within the first 30 days, whereas long-term survival rates were better. The combination of statins, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin receptor blockers, beta blockers, and oral anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents was associated with higher overall survival in patients with STEMI (hazard ratio [HR] 0.21; 95% confidence interval [95%CI] 0.20-0.23; p < 0.001) or NSTEMI (HR 0.40; 95%CI 0.38-0.42; p < 0.001). Nevertheless, the prescription rates decreased over time, particular in patients with NSTEMI.
CONCLUSION: Clear differences between STEMI and NSTEMI were observed regarding short- and long-term survival. Guideline-recommended therapy improved long-term survival, but decreased during the follow-up period.

Title: Attributable Macroeconomic Burden and Projected Trends of Ischemic Stroke due to Hypertension, Hyperglycemia, and Hyperlipidemia in Chinese Working-Age Adults Using a Bayesian Productivity-Adjusted Life-Year Framework.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension, hyperglycemia, and hyperlipidemia are the leading modifiable risk factors for ischemic stroke in China, yet their combined long-term macroeconomic consequences for the working-age population remain poorly quantified.
METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we assessed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to these three metabolic risk factors among Chinese adults aged 20-64 years from 1990 to 2023. Temporal trends were evaluated via Joinpoint regression. Future disease burden through 2,050 was projected using a Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model. The macroeconomic burden from 2024 to 2030 was estimated using a Bayesian productivity-adjusted life-year (PALY) framework, with GDP losses expressed in purchasing power parity (PPP) international dollars (Intl$).
RESULTS: In 2023, these risk factors accounted for 105,469 deaths and 5,246,634 DALYs, with age-standardized rates of 12.98 and 645.85 per 100,000, respectively. Age-standardized rates declined consistently from 1990 to 2023 (AAPC: -3.07% for mortality; -2.18% for DALYs). Despite this, the absolute number of deaths is projected to reach 249,779 by 2050. The macroeconomic burden is projected to escalate to 4.08 million PALYs lost and a GDP loss of PPP Intl$ 162.74 billion by 2030, disproportionately affecting males and adults aged 55-64 years.
CONCLUSION: Although age-standardized burden has declined, the absolute and macroeconomic burden attributable to metabolic risk factors is projected to rise substantially, underscoring the urgent need for integrated prevention targeting high-risk working-age groups.

Title: Clinical Features and Genetic Diversity of Primary Hyperoxaluria: A Case Series Analysis of Chinese Patients.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to characterize the clinical features, genetic profiles, and outcomes of primary hyperoxaluria (PH) in a Chinese cohort.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients diagnosed with PH between 2008 and 2025 at our institution. Diagnosis was established through genetic analysis or histopathological findings combined with clinical manifestations and positive family history. Clinical, laboratory, genetic, imaging, histopathological, treatment, and outcome data were collected.
RESULTS: Thirteen patients were included (PH1, n=7; PH2, n=3; PH3, n=2; unclassified, n=1). Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 7 and 21 years, respectively. Renal involvement manifested as urolithiasis (92.3%) and nephrocalcinosis (30.8%). At diagnosis, the overall median serum creatinine was 335 µmol/L, and the median 24-hour urinary oxalate excretion was 0.8 mmol/1.73m² (n = 6). Systemic oxalate deposition was observed in 30.8% of patients, predominantly affecting bone and heart. Five previously unreported genetic variants were identified. Treatment consisted of supportive care, with vitamin B6 for PH1. Over a median follow‑up of 13.0 years, 100% of PH1 and 66.7% of PH2 patients progressed to end-stage renal disease, with two infantile-onset PH1 patients demonstrating rapid progression; conversely, PH3 patients preserved renal function (chronic kidney disease stage 1). Three PH1 patients developed recurrent oxalate nephropathy following isolated kidney transplantation. The overall mortality was 15.4%.
CONCLUSIONS: PH commonly presents with non-specific symptoms of urolithiasis, frequently resulting in diagnostic delay. PH1 is associated with a more severe clinical course than other subtypes, particularly in infantile-onset cases. This study expands the known genetic variant spectrum and underscores the importance of early genetic diagnosis.

Title: Premenopausal Depression and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease After Menopause: A Large Real-world Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: While depression has been linked to adverse cardiometabolic profiles in postmenopausal women, its temporal relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) when occurring before menopause remains unclear. This study examined whether depression diagnosed prior to menopause was associated with incident CVD after menopause.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Postmenopausal women were assigned to two cohorts: cohort 1 included women with depression diagnosed before menopause and without preexisting CVD, premature menopause, or conventional CVD risk factors (smoking, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, overweight/obesity, or family history of ischemic heart disease); cohort 2 included comparable women without premenopausal depression. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, including age at menopause, current age, and ethnicity. Risk differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals(CIs) were calculated to compare incident CVD (myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Time-to-event outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: Initial queries identified 90,638 women in cohort 1 and 1,237,202 in cohort 2. After matching, 88,884 women remained in each cohort, with a mean (SD) age of 57.6(11.4) years. Follow-up varies according to database entry time, with maximum follow-up of 20 years. Women with premenopausal depression had a higher incidence of postmenopausal CVD than those without depression (4.0% vs. 3.3%; RR,1.23; 95% CI, 1.17-1.29; p<.001), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 0.7% (95% CI, 0.6%-0.9%). Because the proportional hazards assumption was not satisfied, the Cox hazard ratio was interpreted as a secondary average time-to-event summary rather than as the primary effect estimate. The estimated hazard ratio for incident CVD was 1.21 (95% CI, 1.15-1.27; log-rank p<.001), representing an average association across the follow-up period rather than a constant hazard over time.
CONCLUSION: Women with premenopausal depression had a higher cumulative incidence of postmenopausal cardiovascular disease than matched women without depression, suggesting that premenopausal depression may represent a marker of increased cardiovascular vulnerability in midlife women.

Title: Mortality and Causes of Death among Individuals in a National Opioid Agonist Treatment Cohort.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People with opioid use disorder experience markedly elevated all-cause and cause-specific mortality. Opioid-agonist treatment (OAT) reduces mortality risk, and OAT populations across Europe are ageing, with cardiovascular, respiratory, and liver diseases accounting for a growing proportion of deaths. However, cause-specific mortality beyond overdose remains poorly characterized in large national cohorts.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including all 26,031 individuals (76% men) recorded in the Austrian national OAT registry between January 1, 2002, and December 31, 2019, linked to the national causes of death registry with follow-up through December 31, 2021. We calculated sex-specific age-standardized mortality rates per 100,000 person-years (2013 European Standard Population), standardized rate ratios (SRRs), and cause-specific standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) compared with the Austrian general population.
RESULTS: Across 278,959 person-years of follow-up, 2,358 deaths occurred. Cohort members had substantially higher mortality across all causes, with greater excess among women (SRR 7.06, 95% CI 6.45-7.72) than men (3.86; 3.69-4.04). Beyond substance use-related causes (SMR 33.2, 95% CI 31.4-35.2), the highest SMRs were found for viral hepatitis (63.8, 52.3-77.8), HIV (48.6, 39.0-60.6), and valvular heart diseases and endocarditis (28.4, 18.6-43.6). By the early to mid-40s, deaths from non-communicable diseases collectively exceeded those from substance use-related causes.
CONCLUSION: Austria's national OAT cohort experiences substantial excess mortality across all major causes, with high relative excess for substance use-related, infectious, and liver-related conditions. As OAT populations age, non-communicable diseases account for an increasing share of deaths. Future analyses linking the cohort to additional data sources will be needed to disentangle the underlying contributions to this excess mortality.

Title: SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy and Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation in Patients With HFpEF and Type 2 Diabetes.
Abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction, particularly in patients with Type 2 Diabetes, due to shared cardiometabolic and inflammatory mechanisms. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiovascular benefit in HFpEF, but data regarding prevention of incident AF remain limited. Objectives To evaluate the association between SGLT2 inhibitor therapy and incident atrial fibrillation/flutter in patients with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus. Methods We performed a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus receiving oral antihyperglycemic therapy were identified. Patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors were matched 1:1 with those receiving Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. The primary outcome was incident AF/flutter. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, ischemic stroke, and composite major adverse cardiovascular events (cMACE; all-cause mortality, ischemic stroke, or acute myocardial infarction). Associations were assessed using hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs). Results After propensity matching, 37,108 patients were included (18,554 per group). Compared with DPP4 inhibitor therapy, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower incidence of AF/flutter (17.8% vs 19.2%; HR 0.84, RR 0.93), all-cause mortality (12.5% vs 21.4%; HR 0.53, RR 0.59), ischemic stroke (7.4% vs 8.7%; HR 0.78, RR 0.85), and cMACE (24.4% vs 33.0%; HR 0.66, RR 0.74). Conclusions In patients with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus, SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with lower rates of incident AF/flutter and adverse cardiovascular outcomes, supporting a potential role for SGLT2 inhibitors in modifying arrhythmic risk in addition to established cardiometabolic benefits.

Title: Target weight optimization based on a modified VExUS protocol in hemodialysis: the VexHD prospective multi-center study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical examination has limitations in estimating fluid overload in hemodialysis patients. The aim of the present study is to evaluate the impact of target weight optimization using a modified Venous Excess Ultrasonography Score (VExUS) protocol on blood pressure control in euvolemic hemodialysis patients.
METHODS: We enrolled clinically euvolemic patients in hemodialysis from ten Spanish centers. Baseline clinical data, bioimpedance, and an extensive panel of cardiac, congestion, and inflammatory biomarkers were collected. Patients with congestion on modified VExUS protocol (excluding intrarenal vessels) underwent protocol‑driven ultrafiltration adjustments. Blood pressure, bioimpedance, and biomarkers were reassessed at study completion, and paired statistical analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Among the 72 clinically euvolemic patients included (60% male, mean age 69±18 years), 23 (32%) showed venous congestion on modified VExUS protocol and entered the intervention group and 49 were followed under routine care conditions (reference). Volume values obtained by bioimpedance spectroscopy were similar in the congestion intervention and non-congestion reference groups. After four weeks, the intervention group experienced a significant improvement in modified VExUS protocol parameters compared to baseline (2.1±0.5 vs 1.3±0.5; p<0.001) and a systolic blood pressure reduction compared with reference group participants (-14 [-37;4] vs 4 [-9;14] mmHg) (p=0.025). The reduction in systolic blood pressure was more notable in patients with higher baseline values. There were no differences in hemodialysis tolerance or biomarker changes between intervention and reference group participants.
CONCLUSION: Modified VExUS protocol is a promising tool for evaluating volume overload and optimizing target weight. Its incorporation in the multiparametric assessment of target weight is associated with better blood pressure control.

Title: Utilities of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor in the Intensive Care Units.
Abstract: Background Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become foundational therapies for heart failure and chronic kidney disease and are increasingly used in critically ill patients. Their established benefits for kidney and heart health, along with emerging evidence from acute-care settings, indicate growing interest in their potential role in intensive care medicine. However, whether these benefits can be translated to critically ill populations remains uncertain, and concerns regarding safety continue to influence clinical practice. Summary Clinical evidence supporting the use of SGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) during acute illness is expanding. Benefits have been most consistently observed in acute heart failure, perioperative care, and renal outcomes, where randomized and observational studies suggest improved decongestion, reduced acute kidney injury, and favorable cardiorenal outcomes. These observations are supported by several biological effects of SGLT2i that extend beyond glucose lowering, including modulation of fluid balance, renal hemodynamics, metabolic adaptation, inflammation, and endothelial function-pathways that are central to the development of organ dysfunction during critical illness. However, important uncertainties remain regarding which critically ill patients are most likely to benefit, whether chronic therapy should be continued during acute illness, and how potential benefits should be balanced against safety concerns in the ICU. This review integrates current mechanistic and clinical evidence, examines the balance between potential benefits and risks, discusses practical management considerations, and highlights key research priorities to better define the role of SGLT2i in critical care medicine.   Key Messages - SGLT2 inhibitors show promise in critical care but are not established therapies. - Cardiorenal benefits must be balanced against metabolic and hemodynamic risks. - Future research should define the right patient, the right timing, and the right treatment strategy.

Title: Prevalent Sodium-Glucose Co-Transporter 2 Inhibitor Use, Baseline Laboratory Profile, and Clinical Outcomes in a Real-World Heart Failure Cohort.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the prevalence of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, baseline laboratory profiles, and associated clinical outcomes in a real-world heart failure (HF) cohort.
METHOD: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included consecutive patients with HF who were evaluated between January 2022 and January 2024. Of the 609 patients, 581 with known SGLT2i use status constituted the analytic cohort. The primary outcome was HF hospitalization. A composite outcome comprising all-cause death, HF hospitalization, stroke, or peripheral embolism was assessed as an exploratory endpoint. Propensity score matching and overlap-weighted Cox regression models were used in sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Among the 581 patients, 349 were SGLT2i users and 232 were non-users. Users had a lower left ventricular ejection fraction, higher B-type natriuretic peptide concentrations, a higher prevalence of diabetes and ischemic etiology, and more intensive background therapy. In the unadjusted analyses, the rates of HF hospitalization and composite events were higher among users; however, these associations were attenuated after adjustment. In the overlap-weighted propensity score analysis, SGLT2i use was not associated with HF hospitalization (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.57-1.47; P=0.700), the study-defined composite endpoint (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.61-1.48; P=0.827), or exploratory all-cause mortality (HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.45-2.42; P=0.931).
CONCLUSION: SGLT2i users represented a treated population with more advanced clinical characteristics, and their higher unadjusted event burden did not persist after adjustment. These findings reflect treatment selection rather than therapeutic benefit or harm. Therapies proven to reduce mortality should be systematically implemented in all eligible patients with HF, regardless of their clinical status or estimated mortality risk.

Title: Saroglitazar improves hepatic steatosis and liver enzymes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome and MASLD: A multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is the leading endocrine disorder in reproductive-age women. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in women with PCOS, but they are underrepresented in MASLD therapeutic trials. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of saroglitazar, a novel peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors α/γ agonist, for the treatment of hepatic steatosis in women with PCOS and MASLD.
METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2A trial, 60 women (18-45 y) with PCOS and MASLD were randomized 1:1 to either saroglitazar 4 mg or placebo for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was relative (percent) change in hepatic fat content, measured by MRI proton density fat fraction. Primary analysis was performed in the per-protocol population (saroglitazar: 25; placebo: 23).
RESULTS: Participants in the saroglitazar group showed a significant reduction in percent hepatic fat content at 24 weeks from baseline compared to placebo ([least squares mean±SE]: -14.81±5.52 vs. 1.96±5.75, p =0.041). When controlled for baseline HbA1c imbalance, the beneficial effect of saroglitazar was more pronounced ([least squares mean±SE]: -18.93±4.83 vs. 6.43±5.04, p <0.009). A higher proportion in the saroglitazar group achieved ≥30% reduction in magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (36.0% vs. 8.7%; p =0.025). Saroglitazar also significantly reduced aminotransferase levels, lipid parameters, and the FibroScan AST score. Adverse events were comparable between the groups, and none were serious. One pregnancy in the saroglitazar arm resulted in uneventful maternal and neonatal outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In women with PCOS and MASLD, saroglitazar significantly improved hepatic steatosis, liver enzymes, lipid profile, and FibroScan AST score. These findings support further evaluation of saroglitazar in larger studies in women with PCOS.

Title: Veterinary Student Experience and Learning Using a 4D Electrocardiogram Simulator.
Abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology and electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation present challenges for veterinary and medical education. Various resources and simulators exist to address this challenge. This study investigates the impact on learning and student experience of Epicardio Simulation™-VET in a UK undergraduate veterinary curriculum. This multi-method study invited students at the University of Liverpool School of Veterinary Science to complete a survey, comprising Likert-type and free-text questions, exploring their Epicardio experience. A case-control study used a pre- and post-learning quiz to compare learning gain in a self-directed clinical rotation ECG tutorial between a group learning with Epicardio and one learning with traditional resources. Survey responses were generally positive, with median scores of 4/5, except in response to the statement "Epicardio is easy to navigate" (Mdn 3/5), and "Epicardio workshops should replace traditional lectures" (Mdn 2/5; considerable variability in responses). Students also varied on whether "the tutorials were easy to follow." Thematic analysis identified positive themes around application, clarification, visualization, interactivity, formative assessment, and user-friendliness. Negative themes highlighted technical difficulties including navigation and structure of the software, as well as curricular integration. The case-control study showed learning gains in both groups and no difference between groups before or after the self-directed tutorial. Students valued Epicardio as an additional learning tool and learned equally well with Epicardio and traditional resources in a self-directed format.

Title: Association of Life's Essential 8 with Risk of End-Stage Kidney Disease in the United Kingdom Biobank Study.
Journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Life's Essential 8 (LE8) is a comprehensive cardiovascular health (CVH) metric integrating eight behavioral and biological factors and has been associated with cardiovascular disease risk. However, evidence linking LE8 to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) is lacking.
METHODS: We analyzed the United Kingdom (UK) Biobank data prospectively on participants who were free of ESKD at baseline. The LE8 score, calculated as the unweighted average of eight components (range, 0-100), was categorized as low (0-49), moderate (50-79), and high (80-100), with higher scores indicating more favorable health status. The primary outcome was incident ESKD, defined as needing kidney replacement therapy or reaching CKD stage G5. We used Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for incident ESKD, separately for LE8 categories and for continuous LE8 scores, with nonlinear associations assessed using restricted cubic splines (RCS). We also estimated population-attributable fractions (PAFs) for non-optimal LE8 and its subscales and components.
RESULTS: Among 276,494 participants (mean [SD] age 56 [8] years; 48% male; 95% White), 455 incident ESKD events occurred over a median follow-up of 14.1 years. In fully adjusted Cox models, each 10-point decrement in LE8 score was associated with higher ESKD risk (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.34-1.60). Compared with high LE8, moderate LE8 was associated with a 2.1-fold higher risk of incident ESKD (HR, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.39-3.21), and low LE8 was associated with a more than five-fold higher risk (HR, 5.57; 95% CI, 3.42-9.07). Subscale analyses showed similar patterns. RCS analysis suggested nonlinear associations for overall LE8 and the biological subscale, with steeper risk gradients at lower scores. Blood pressure, blood glucose, physical activity, and smoking had statistically significant estimated PAF for incident ESKD, with the largest fractions observed for blood pressure and blood glucose.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large prospective cohort, low LE8 was associated with a substantially higher risk of incident ESKD. These findings highlight the potential relevance of LE8-guided improvement in behavioral and biological factors for ESKD prevention.

Title: Socioeconomic Inequality and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Low socioeconomic status is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease, yet it remains unclear whether this association has changed over time. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) are key contributors to cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, and health care costs and, thus, are indicators of the overall cardiovascular burden.
OBJECTIVE: To describe temporal trends in incident MACE by equivalized income groups in the Danish population from 1988 to 2023.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide, population-based open cohort study using data from Danish national registries included all residents of Denmark aged 30 years or older who were alive in each year between January 1, 1988, and January 1, 2023, and had available income observations in the current or preceding 5 years. Individuals were followed up to December 31 of each year, to death, or to emigration. Data were analyzed from August 2025 to July 2026.
EXPOSURE: Equivalized disposable household income.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Incident MACE, defined as the first hospital admission for acute myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke, or heart failure. Age-standardized incidence rates were calculated annually, stratified by income quartile and sex.
RESULTS: A total of 5 932 672 individuals aged 30 years or older were registered in the Danish Civil Registration System from 1988 to 2023. The annual study population increased from 3.06 million in 1988 to 3.85 million in 2023. Most residents in 1988 were female (52.1%), and most in 2023 were male (51.1%); the median age increased from 50.8 years (IQR, 40.2-65.6 years) in 1988 to 55.8 years (IQR, 43.3-68.8 years) in 2023. Age-standardized incidence rates of MACE decreased across all income groups from 1988 to 2023 but remained highest in the lowest income quartile. For males, the rate decreased from 191.1 (95% CI, 186.3-196.0) per 10 000 person-years to 119.6 (95% CI, 116.0-123.2) per 10 000 person-years in the lowest income quartile, while in the highest quartile it decreased from 153.5 (95% CI, 142.9-164.0) per 10 000 person-years to 85.9 (95% CI, 81.2-90.6) per 10 000 person-years. For females, the rate decreased from 116.0 (95% CI, 113.0-118.9) per 10 000 person-years to 70.4 (95% CI, 68.1-72.6) per 10 000 person-years in in the lowest income quartile and from 89.5 (95% CI, 81.9-97.2) per 10 000 person-years to 53.1 (95% CI, 49.0-57.1) per 10 000 person-years in the highest.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of Danish residents aged 30 years or older from 1988 to 2023, the incidence of MACE declined across all socioeconomic groups. Although individuals with lower income generally experienced higher incidence rates, the overall decline occurred in all socioeconomic groups.

Title: Ultraprocessed Food Intake and Adiposity, Vascular Brain Injury, and Cognition in Middle-Aged Adults.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) account for a substantial and increasing proportion of dietary intake in Canada. Although UPFs are consistently associated with adiposity and cardiometabolic disease, their associations with subclinical vascular brain injury (VBI) and cognitive performance in midlife are unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of UPF consumption with adiposity, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined VBI, and cognitive performance in middle-aged adults in Canada.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study included 8783 adults aged 35 to 69 years without cardiovascular disease who were enrolled in the Canadian Alliance for Healthy Hearts and Healthy Minds (CAHHM) and Prospective Urban and Rural Epidemiology-MIND (PURE-MIND) studies. Participants from CAHHM were recruited from January 1, 2014, to December 31, 2018, and participants from PURE-MIND were recruited from January 1, 2010, to December 31, 2018. Data analyses were conducted between July 16, 2024, and August 16, 2026.
EXPOSURES: UPF consumption assessed using previously validated semiquantitative food frequency questionnaires and expressed as servings per 2000 kcal/d.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were body fat (BF) percentage (bioelectrical impedance), visceral adipose tissue (VAT) volume, hepatic fat fraction (HFF), VBI defined as covert brain infarcts or high white matter hyperintensities (HWMHs) (measured by MRI), and cognitive performance measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) and the Digital Symbol Substitution Test (DSST).
RESULTS: In this cross-sectional study of 8783 participants (mean [SD] age, 57.7 [8.7] years; 4917 females [56.6%]), those in the highest quartile of UPF intake had a BF percentage that was 1.7 (95% CI, 1.2-2.2) percentage points higher and a 5.7 (95% CI, 3.2-8.3) mL greater VAT volume compared with those in the lowest quartile, but no significant difference in HFF. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest UPF quartile had higher odds of VBI (adjusted OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.10-1.77; P for trend = .009). No significant associations were observed between UPF intake and MOCA or DSST performance.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study of middle-aged adults in Canada, higher UPF intake was associated with greater adiposity and higher odds of MRI-defined VBI but not cognitive performance. Associations with VBI were sensitive to UPF exposure definition. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporality.

Title: Prehospital Point-of-Care GFAP for Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage in Acute Nontraumatic Coma.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Rapid identification of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with acute nontraumatic coma is critical to guiding triage and early management; however, prehospital diagnostic tools remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of prehospital whole-blood point-of-care measurement of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for detecting ICH.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This diagnostic study used data collected by a UK physician-paramedic helicopter emergency medical service between January 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. A consecutive sample of adult patients (aged ≥16 years) presenting with acute nontraumatic coma, defined as Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 or less, who underwent prehospital rapid sequence induction (RSI) of anesthesia with clinical suspicion of ICH were eligible for inclusion. Patients with traumatic pathology and those without follow-up data were excluded. Patients were observed for up for 30 days from hospital admission. Data analysis was performed in June 2026.
