METHODS: Using a retrospective observational design, Big Data from the Hospital Information System (HIS) were processed between March and August 2025. Care trajectories and functional interdependence with 19 clinical services were evaluated using network analysis techniques in RStudio, with associations determined through Relative Risk (RR).
RESULTS: The results demonstrate an operational integration network in which dental functions complement one another, yet with a predominant linkage to Internal Medicine Emergency services (n = 397). A low density of interdependence was detected with strategic specialties for chronic disease management, such as Cardiology (n = 97) and Diabetology (n = 79). A critical finding was that patients accessing services through scheduled care were 4.16 times more likely to receive proactive and continuous care than those entering through emergency departments (RR = 4.16; 95% CI; p < 0.001). Furthermore, a capacity gap was observed: while global hospital demand grew by 10.2%, the dental supply only increased by 0.5%. In light of these arguments, although the IHSDN structure is solid, its operability remains reactive and fragmented.
CONCLUSIONS: The study demonstrates that scheduled management is the key to quadrupling care integration. The HIS is positioned as an essential governance tool to identify bottlenecks, eliminate access barriers, and strengthen proactive referrals, ensuring that oral health is effectively integrated into the comprehensive care of patients with chronic conditions.

Title: Comparative Outcomes of Left Anterior Thoracotomy Versus Resternotomy for Pulmonic Valve Replacement After Tetralogy of Fallot Repair.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Redo pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in patients with prior tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair is surgically challenging. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of the left anterior minithoracotomy (LAT) approach with the traditional resternotomy approach for PVR.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 38 TOF patients who underwent redo PVR, categorized into LAT (n = 20) and resternotomy (n = 18) groups. Patients requiring concomitant valvular surgeries or repair of residual intracardiac shunts were excluded. We compared demographics, operative details, and postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: Baseline demographics were comparable between groups, except for a higher proportion of males in the LAT group (75% vs 38.9%, P = 0.047). The LAT approach demonstrated nonsignificant favorable trends, including shorter operative times (157.05 ± 49.42 vs 178.06 ± 58.69 min, P = 0.239) and shorter postoperative hospital stays (4.75 ± 1.21 vs 6.17 ± 4.38 days, P = 0.173). Vasoactive-inotropic scores were significantly lower in the LAT group both immediately postoperatively (0.05 ± 0.22 vs 4.36 ± 6.95, P = 0.009) and on postoperative day 1 (0 vs 2.17 ± 4.52, P = 0.039). Postoperative complications, such as atrial fibrillation and pleural effusion, were similar between groups. There was no mortality in either group.
CONCLUSIONS: The LAT approach for PVR after TOF repair is a safe alternative to resternotomy. Comprehensive preoperative imaging evaluation is crucial for determining the optimal incision site. Further studies with larger cohorts are needed to confirm the potential benefits of this approach.

Title: Diet Quality and Physical Activity at 3-4 Years Following a Hypertensive Pregnancy: A Blood Pressure Postpartum Cross-Sectional Sub-Study.
Journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), as well as being a leading global cause of maternal mortality, confer lifelong increased maternal cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Although lifestyle interventions may mitigate these risks, robust evidence remains scarce.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This cross-sectional sub-study of the three-armed, multicenter BP2 randomised controlled trial primarily assessed diet quality, physical activity, and their association with CVD risk markers in women 3-4 years after HDP, following different BP2 postpartum care/lifestyle intervention strategies implemented between six and 12 months post-HDP. Diet quality was evaluated using the Australian Recommended Food Score (ARFS) derived from the Australian Eating Survey. Duration of moderate-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) was estimated using the International Physical activity Questionnaire. Associations between key lifestyle outcomes and clinical cardiovascular markers were examined using linear regression models. Secondary lifestyle outcomes include estimated daily energy intake, food consumption, nutrients, estimated duration and engagement of specific physical activity types, and sedentary behaviour.
RESULTS: In 180 participants, the mean ARFS was 33.8 ± 10.5 (SD), with 61% scoring < 38 indicating suboptimal diet quality. Median MVPA was 515 (IQR 690) minutes/week with 87% meeting physical activity recommendations of at least 150 min/week. No significant differences were observed across BP2 lifestyle intervention strategies, HDP subtypes (chronic hypertension, gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and superimposed preeclampsia), or baseline body mass index (BMI) categories (< 30 vs. ≥ 30 kg/m2). Neither ARFS nor MVPA showed significant associations with blood pressure, BMI, or waist circumference.
CONCLUSIONS: Suboptimal diet was observed 3-4 years after HDP despite prior lifestyle interventions, highlighting the need for postpartum support and long-term lifestyle interventions to reduce CVD risks post-HDP.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Immunometabolic dysregulation in gastric ulcer: Association of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, trace elements, and atherogenic lipid profile.
Abstract: Gastric ulcer remains a prevalent gastrointestinal disorder characterized by disruption of the gastric mucosal barrier due to an imbalance between injurious and protective factors. Recent attention has focused on the role of inflammatory mediators, micronutrient status, and metabolic alterations in the progression of this condition. Cytokines are known to promote inflammatory cascades and mucosal damage and modulates immune responses during gastric injury. Also, trace elements including zinc and copper are essential for maintaining antioxidant defense, immune function, and tissue repair. This case control study included 60 patients diagnosed with gastric ulcer and 60 apparently healthy individuals as normal controls. All participants were recruited from the Gastroenterology and Hepatology Hospital in Al-Najaf. The two groups were matched in terms of age and body mass index to minimize potential confounding effects. Serum levels of IL-10, IL-1beta, zinc, copper, and lipid profile parameters were assessed using standard laboratory methods. Statistical analysis was carried out using SPSS version 26. Due to non-normal distribution of variables, median values were used for data representation. Spearman's rank correlation test was applied to evaluate associations among variables, and the receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to determine the diagnostic performance of the studied parameters. The findings revealed a significant elevation in both IL-1beta and IL-10 levels among gastric ulcer patients compared to controls, indicating activation of inflammatory and regulatory immune pathways. Zinc levels were significantly reduced in patients, suggesting a possible link between micronutrient depletion and impaired mucosal defense. The present study demonstrated a combined pattern of inflammatory activation, zinc deficiency, and lipid profile disturbance in gastric ulcer patients. These alterations may collectively contribute to disease pathogenesis and could serve as useful indicators for disease assessment and monitoring.

Title: Von Willebrand Factor Biomarkers in Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction: An Adjunct to Imaging and Hemodynamic Assessment.
Abstract: Imaging remains the foundation of prosthetic valve surveillance because it identifies valve morphology, lesion mechanism, and hemodynamic severity. However, acoustic shadowing, eccentric or multiple regurgitant jets, loading conditions, and reader variability can complicate assessment, particularly for paravalvular regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High shear stress unfolds von Willebrand factor (VWF), promotes proteolysis of its high-molecular-weight multimers, and produces a measurable defect in primary hemostasis. Multimer analysis, closure time with adenosine diphosphate (CT-ADP), and the VWF activity-to-antigen ratio therefore provide a biologic signal of abnormal flow rather than an anatomic image. Prospective studies show that VWF abnormalities track residual paravalvular regurgitation during transcatheter aortic valve replacement, occur with dysfunctional prostheses, change after mitral paravalvular-leak repair, and are associated with bleeding. The evidence nevertheless remains observational; most diagnostic cohorts are small and single-center, thresholds lack independent validation, assays are vulnerable to hematologic and preanalytic confounding, and no completed randomized trial has shown that VWF-guided management improves outcomes. VWF testing is best viewed as an investigational adjunct when imaging and the clinical picture are discordant or when prosthetic dysfunction coexists with otherwise unexplained bleeding. It should not replace guideline-directed echocardiography or be used for routine surveillance outside research protocols.

Title: Corticosteroid Exposure in Autoimmune Hepatitis: Early Toxicity, Cumulative Burden and Associations With Long-Term Patient-Reported Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) requires corticosteroid-based induction therapy, but prolonged exposure is common in practice.
AIMS: This study quantified corticosteroid utilization patterns and associations with adverse outcomes from a patient perspective.
METHODS: A cross-sectional patient-reported survey recruited AIHA network members with physician-confirmed AIH (N = 563). Corticosteroid exposure was quantified using annual duration thresholds (≥ 90 days/year at ≥ 5 mg/day prednisone-equivalent). Early side effects (within 6 months; n = 491) and long-term metabolic complications (≥ 2 years disease duration; n = 385) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex and disease duration.
RESULTS: Among 563 participants (median age 53 years; 87.4% female), all participants received a corticosteroid at diagnosis (77.6% prednisone; 11.4% budesonide). Side effects within 6 months were near-universal (96.6%; median 5 symptoms) and greater with predniso(lo)ne than budesonide (5.82 vs. 3.55 symptoms; p < 0.001); 51.2% of predniso(lo)ne-initiated patients developed a new metabolic condition within 6 months. Long-term complications affected 75.9% of the chronically exposed cohort, including weight gain > 5% (47.0%), osteoporosis (30.4%) and hypertension (18.1%). Each additional cumulative year of extensive exposure was independently associated with the composite adverse outcome (adjusted OR 1.11, 95% CI 1.02-1.22; p = 0.014), osteoporosis, Type 2 diabetes, weight gain and cataracts, with significant dose-response gradients (p-trend ≤ 0.008). Patients with > 5 cumulative years had 4-fold higher odds of the composite outcome versus patients in the None exposure group (OR 4.21, 95% CI 1.51-11.71).
CONCLUSIONS: Corticosteroid exposure in AIH is associated with dose-dependent toxicity from the first months of treatment. Reduced induction dosing and budesonide represent potential steroid-minimization strategies in appropriate patients, warranting prospective evaluation.

Title: Meta-Analysis of Long-Term Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events of Different Biologics in Psoriatic Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease associated with systemic inflammation and an increased risk of cardiovascular events.
AREAS OF UNCERTAINTY: Although biologic therapies have transformed psoriasis treatment, the long-term impact of different biologic classes on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remains unclear.
DATA SOURCES: A systematic search of PubMed was performed up to May 27, 2026. We included Comparative cohort studies of biologic therapies for psoriasis with follow-up durations of at least 52 weeks, as well as long-term open-label extension phases of randomized controlled trials that reported MACE outcomes. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale for cohort studies. Hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were pooled using the generic inverse variance method.
RESULTS: Four comparative cohort studies involving 57,331 patients were included in the quantitative synthesis. No significant difference in MACE risk was observed between interleukin (IL)-12/23 inhibitors and tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) inhibitors (HR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.68-1.23), or between IL-12/23 inhibitors and IL-17 inhibitors (HR: 1.38, 95% CI: 0.73-2.62). Long-term open-label extension studies reported low MACE event rates (0%-1.33%) across biologic therapies.
CONCLUSIONS: Among biologic therapies with available long-term comparative data, no significant differences in MACE risk were observed between IL-12/23, TNF-α, and IL-17 inhibitors in patients with psoriasis. Further long-term, large-scale studies are warranted to better define the cardiovascular safety profiles of emerging biologic therapies.

Title: SETI-The Semi-Elective Transplant Initiative: A Systems-Based Approach to Expanding Kidney Transplant Access Through Operational Redesign.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether formal integration of preservation strategy with predictable operating room access was associated with measurable changes in transplant timing, preservation practice, the logistical profile of transplanted grafts, and early clinical outcomes.
SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: Deceased donor kidney transplantation remains a reactive process requiring urgent mobilization of hospital resources. As volumes increase and hospitals operate near capacity, this creates operational barriers that limit organ utilization. We report a retrospective evaluation of a prospectively implemented operational redesign; the design does not support causal inference.
METHODS: Adult deceased-donor kidney transplants (January 2022-June 2025) were grouped into pre-SETI, SETI-1 (expanded machine perfusion), and SETI-2 (morning operating room access). A contemporaneous SRTR cohort (N=12,302) served as the comparator.
RESULTS: Among 936 transplants, mean cold ischemia time (CIT) increased after SETI (20.2→21.9 h, P=0.0039). Donation after circulatory death (DCD) kidneys with CIT >30 hours increased from 0.5% pre-SETI to 7.7% after full implementation (P<0.0001). Overnight perfusion increased more than 3-fold, and operative starts shifted toward 8-10 AM. Kidney Donor Profile Index rose across eras (median: 29→33→43, P<0.001). No significant differences were observed in DGF (41.4→38.2%, P=0.071) or graft failure (5.4→3.2%, P=0.34); these comparisons were underpowered and do not establish equivalence. Donor hypertension predicted graft failure, whereas CIT, DCD status, and SETI era did not.
CONCLUSIONS: Systems-based operational redesign transformed reactive deceased-donor kidney transplantation into a proactive model, enabling transplantation of a greater proportion of logistics-sensitive grafts, including DCD kidneys and organs with prolonged CIT, within existing healthcare resources. Whether this increases net organ utilization was not established by these data.

Title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Aspirin Monotherapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With GRADE Evaluation and Trial Sequential Analysis.
Abstract: The optimal duration of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) following drug-eluting stent implantation remains uncertain. We evaluated extended DAPT versus aspirin monotherapy in patients who completed approximately 12 months of uneventful DAPT after percutaneous coronary intervention. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through August 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing these strategies. The primary outcome was myocardial infarction (MI); secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, stroke, and clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 2-5). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a Mantel-Haenszel random-effects model. Certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and trial sequential analysis was performed for MI. Six trials involving 28,601 patients were included. Extended DAPT significantly reduced MI compared with aspirin monotherapy (RR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85; P = 0.001; I2 = 37%). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, cardiac death, stent thrombosis, repeat revascularization, or stroke. Clinically relevant bleeding was also not significantly different (RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.66-2.15; P = 0.56), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 87%) and certainty was low. GRADE certainty was high for MI, cardiac death, and repeat revascularization; moderate for all-cause mortality; and low for stent thrombosis and bleeding. Trial sequential analysis for MI crossed the conventional significance boundary but not the trial sequential monitoring boundary or required information size. Extended DAPT may reduce MI, but individualized assessment of ischemic and bleeding risk remains important, and further adequately powered trials are warranted.

Title: Economic Evaluation of Prolonged Hypothermic Oxygenated Machine Perfusion Enabling Daytime Liver Transplantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Short-duration (1-2 h) dual hypothermic oxygenated machine perfusion (DHOPE) reduces ischemia-reperfusion injury-related complications. Prolonged DHOPE preservation (DHOPE-PRO) may facilitate logistics. We assessed the economic impact of DHOPE-PRO versus conventional short-duration DHOPE, hypothesizing that DHOPE-PRO would not be associated with increased one-year transplantation-related costs.
METHODS: This post hoc economic evaluation of the prospective DHOPE-PRO trial (NL8740) included adult recipients of livers donated after brain death. All transplantation-related medical expenses up to one year post-transplant were collected. The cost of resource use was calculated using 2022 full hospital prices indexed to 2024. Time-driven variable costing was applied to perfusion, surgery, and intensive care costs. The primary outcome was total one-year transplantation-related cost.
RESULTS: Of 24 patients, 12 received a liver after DHOPE and 12 after DHOPE-PRO. Median one-year total costs were €83 583 [interquartile range (IQR) 78 400-104 158] for DHOPE and €78 582 [IQR 73123-92 855] for DHOPE-PRO (p = 0.347). Perfusion costs were higher with DHOPE-PRO (€23 926 [IQR 22711-24 697] versus €17 306 [IQR 16928-17 594]; p < 0.001), while surgery costs were lower (€18 560 [IQR 17806-20 747] versus €21 303 [IQR 19535-25 418]; p = 0.033). Costs related to other medical activities did not differ between groups.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory single-center economic evaluation, DHOPE-PRO enabled daytime liver transplantation without evidence of increased one-year transplantation-related costs compared with short-duration DHOPE. Higher perfusion-related costs were accompanied by lower surgery-related costs in this cohort. These findings warrant confirmation in larger studies.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Netherlands Trial Registry number: NL8740.

Title: Cumulative average metabolic indices and cardiovascular disease risk: additive predictive effects and partial mediating role of intrinsic capacity in early-stage CKM syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early stages (0-3) of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome represent a critical window for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention. Triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-derived indices reflect insulin resistance and metabolic burden, but their cumulative effects and the role of intrinsic capacity (IC) remain unclear.
METHODS: In this prospective study from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), 3,832 adults with CKM stages 0-3 and without baseline CVD were included. Fourteen cumulative average metabolic indices were derived from repeated measurements. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models were used to evaluate associations and dose-response relationships, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied for multiple comparisons. Joint effects with IC, predictive performance (AUC, calibration, decision curve analysis, NRI, and IDI), and mediation effects were assessed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4.0 years, 303 incident CVD cases (7.9%) occurred. Five indices (TyG-BMI, TyG-WHtR, TyG-CI, TyG-CVAI, and METS-IR) were significantly associated with higher odds of new-onset CVD after full adjustment and FDR correction (per SD OR range: 1.27-1.36), with approximately linear dose-response relationships. Lower IC was associated with higher CVD risk. Individual indices showed modest discrimination (AUC range: 0.580-0.604), and incorporating IC provided incremental predictive information (AUC up to 0.621, both NRI and IDI P < 0.01). IC partially mediated these associations, with modest mediation proportions (≈ 4%-7%).
CONCLUSIONS: Cumulative metabolic burden is independently associated with CVD risk in early-stage CKM syndrome. IC showed joint associations and modest mediating effects and provided complementary information for CVD risk assessment. Integrating metabolic and functional assessments may enhance early risk stratification.

Title: Correction: Protocol for a randomized controlled trial comparing saturated and unsaturated fat sources of a ketogenic diet (KETO-IM) investigating cardiovascular, inflammatory and immune function outcomes in adults living with overweight and prediabetes or type 2 diabetes in Edmonton, Canada.

Success of femtosecond laser-assisted deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (Femto-DALK): a clinical case series of 42 eyes using an intraoperative optical coherence tomography (iOCT)-guided laser-generated pre-descemet tunnel.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the success of Femto-DALK with an iOCT-guided generated intrastromal pre-Descemet tunnel.
METHODS: This monocentric, retrospective study evaluated all patients treated with Femto-DALK between January 2020 and December 2023 at the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of Düsseldorf (Germany). The iOCT-guided tunnel was generated 30 microns anterior of Descemet's membrane. BB generation, surgery time and conversion to penetrating keratoplasty (PK) were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 42 eyes of 41 patients were identified. BB creation was successful in 78.6% of cases. Intraoperative conversion to PK was necessary in 28.6% of the eyes and microperforation of Descemet's membrane (DM) occurred in 16.7% of completed DALKs. Mean operation time was 118.6 ± 40.68 min. Among successful Femto-DALKs (n = 30), double anterior chamber was observed in 26.7%, and re-bubbling was needed in 23.3%. Re-keratoplasty was performed in one eye (3.3%).
CONCLUSION: Femto-DALK with an iOCT-guided pre-Descemet tunnel generation is a feasible technique that achieves BB success rates comparable to the upper range reported for manual dissection, without a clear demonstrated improvement over manual technique.

Title: Association of Cardiac MRI-Derived Epicardial Adipose Tissue Index With Adverse Clinical Outcomes in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
Journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical relevance of the epicardial adipose tissue index (EATI) is increasingly recognized, but its association with clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains inadequately investigated.
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between cardiac MRI-derived EATI and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with HFpEF.
STUDY TYPE: Retrospective.
POPULATION: Two hundred sixty-five patients with HFpEF (135 male; mean age 55 years).
FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 1.5 T/balanced steady-state free precession.
ASSESSMENT: EATI was quantified on cardiac MRI cine images. MACE was defined as cardiac death or readmission for heart failure.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Welch t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, Cox proportional hazards regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank test, and global χ2 model comparison. A p value < 0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 33 months (22-65), 42 patients experienced MACE. EATI was significantly higher in the MACE group than in the no-MACE group (33.65 ± 13.91 vs. 26.13 ± 11.28 mL/m2, Z = -3.52, effect size r = -0.22). EATI was independently associated with MACE (multivariable HR = 1.04 [95% CI: 1.01-1.06]). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis confirmed that patients with low EATI had significantly higher event-free survival rate. A model combining EATI with other clinical and conventional imaging risk factors (χ2 = 42.3) showed significantly improved model discrimination for identifying patients at risk of MACE compared with models with clinical variables (χ2 = 26.0) or clinical and conventional imaging variables (χ2 = 34.3).
DATA CONCLUSION: Cardiac MRI-derived EATI was independently associated with MACE in patients with HFpEF and showed favorable discriminatory performance compared with clinical and conventional imaging risk factors.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.

Title: Habitat Radiomics and Machine Learning for Preoperative Three-class Classification of Pediatric Acute Appendicitis: A Dual-center Study with External Validation.
Journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
Abstract: Accurate preoperative differentiation of pediatric acute appendicitis subtypes is relevant to treatment planning. We developed and externally validated a machine-learning framework combining habitat-based computed tomography (CT) radiomics with clinical variables for three-class classification (simple, complex, and appendiceal abscess). This retrospective dual-center study included 317 children undergoing appendectomy at Institution A (training n = 222, internal validation n = 95) and 174 children at Institution B (external validation). K-means + + habitat segmentation (k = 3) of preoperative noncontrast CT volumes of interest yielded 1218 radiomic features; ten features selected on the training cohort were combined with 20 preoperative clinical variables. Eight classifiers were compared using macro-averaged one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, and macro-F1, with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs), DeLong tests, calibration statistics, and decision curve analysis. In external validation, naive Bayes achieved the highest macro-AUC (0.946, 95% CI 0.910-0.974), accuracy 0.776 (0.713-0.833), and macro-F1 0.766 (0.674-0.837), significantly exceeding all seven comparators among the configurations evaluated (p < 0.001); the internal validation macro-AUC was 0.940 (0.893-0.977). Per-class external AUCs were 0.920 (simple), 0.948 (complex), and 0.971 (abscess). Calibration slopes (0.23-0.30) indicated that probability outputs require recalibration before probabilistic use. In a five-arm ablation of the input feature blocks, the fusion model combining clinical variables with habitat radiomics performed best (external macro-AUC 0.971), ahead of habitat radiomics alone (0.952), clinical variables plus conventional whole-VOI radiomics (0.776), clinical variables alone (0.763) and conventional whole-VOI radiomics alone (0.582). Habitat radiomics combined with machine learning provided accurate, externally validated three-class classification of pediatric acute appendicitis in children undergoing appendectomy. Naive Bayes offered the most balanced subtype discrimination. The model is a subtype-stratification aid rather than a stand-alone diagnostic or treatment-selection tool.

Title: Refining risk prediction in geriatric heart failure: the emergency heart failure mortality risk grade‑BI model under scrutiny.
Abstract: Risk stratification is critical for managing acute heart failure in older adults, yet existing tools often underperform in geriatric populations. Özdemir recently introduced the EHMRG‑BI model, integrating brain natriuretic peptide and endotracheal intubation with the Emergency Heart Failure Mortality Risk Grade score to improve 30‑day mortality prediction. While the model demonstrates improved discrimination in a single‑center derivation cohort, several methodological considerations warrant attention. The inclusion of intubation, a treatment decision rather than a baseline characteristic, may introduce bias and limit its utility as an arrival‑time tool. The absence of key geriatric domains such as frailty, functional status, and cognitive impairment may result in residual confounding. Additionally, modelling BNP as a linear predictor disregards its well‑documented non‑linear association with mortality. This Matters Arising offers a perspective on these challenges and proposes refinements, including external validation, integration of geriatric assessments, and flexible BNP modelling, to strengthen the model's clinical applicability.

Title: Risk factors associated with hypertension in patients attending a pediatric sleep clinic: a prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pediatric patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are at risk of hypertension due to an interplay of factors. Twenty-four-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is required to diagnose white coat hypertension (WCH) and masked hypertension (MH). However, ABPM is not routinely performed. We aim to detect hypertension using ABPM and to identify risk factors associated with hypertension. This was a prospective cohort study of pediatric patients (5-18 years of age) who had been referred to the sleep clinic. Polysomnography (PSG) or overnight pulse oximetry (OPO) were performed as per standard of care. ABPM was performed for all recruited patients. The primary outcome was hypertension, i.e., ambulatory hypertension or MH. Sixty-eight patients were recruited. Median age was 12.6 (interquartile range [IQR] 10.0-14.7) years. Fourteen (21%) did not return for the ABPM and ten (15%) had insufficient readings. Of the remaining 44 patients with complete ABPM data, hypertension was diagnosed in 18/44 (41%) with 10 (23%) having ambulatory hypertension and 8 (18%) having MH. Among the 18 patients with hypertension, one defaulted sleep study; 3/17 (18%) had primary snoring; 6/17 (35%), 4/17 (24%), and 4/17 (24%) had mild, moderate, and severe OSA, respectively. The prevalence of hypertension was 6/20 (30%), 4/10 (40%), 4/8 (50%), and 3/5 (60%) among patients with mild, moderate, and severe OSA and primary snoring, respectively. Age (relative risk [RR] 1.27, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.52, p = 0.008) and primary snoring (RR 3.52, 95% CI 1.38-8.97, p = 0.004) were independently associated with hypertension.
CONCLUSION: Increasing age and primary snoring may be independently associated with hypertension among pediatric patients attending the sleep clinic. Larger studies will be required to validate these risk factors.
WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are at risk of hypertension which is often due to an interplay of multiple factors. • Twenty-four-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is required to diagnose white coat hypertension (WCH) and masked hypertension (MH).
WHAT IS NEW: • In this prospective single-center study, ABPM was performed for all patients, classifying hypertension based on the 2022 update on ABPM in children from the American Heart Association. • Increasing age and primary snoring were independently associated with hypertension in pediatric patients attending the sleep clinic.

Title: Metabolic and oncological effects of metformin added to ADT in prostate cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis including STAMPEDE.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) is the cornerstone of advanced prostate cancer treatment but induces a metabolic syndrome phenotype that heightens cardiovascular risk. Metformin, an insulin-sensitising biguanide with emerging anticancer properties, is a rational ADT adjunct. Following STAMPEDE's 2025 publication, we aimed to quantify metformin's metabolic benefit and characterise its oncological signal by disease volume.
METHODS: This PRISMA 2020-guided review (PROSPERO CRD420261384520) searched five databases through 12 May 2026. Eligible RCTs compared metformin plus ADT versus ADT alone in prostate cancer. Primary metabolic outcomes were body weight, waist circumference, HbA1c, fasting glucose, and LDL cholesterol. Secondary (exploratory) oncological outcomes were overall survival (OS) and castration-resistant prostate cancer-free survival (CRPC-FS), derived predominantly from a single trial. Random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp correction were used; GRADE assessed certainty.
RESULTS: Six trials enroling 2415 participants (78% from STAMPEDE) were included: STAMPEDE (n = 1 874), PRIME (n = 166), PREMIUM (n = 83), MANSMED (n = 124), Mahalingam (n = 36), and Alagizy (n = 132). Disease status ranged from metastatic (STAMPEDE, Alagizy, majority MANSMED) to locally advanced or biochemically recurrent (PREMIUM, PRIME, Mahalingam); all excluded diabetes mellitus except MANSMED ( ~ 20%). At 12 months, metformin significantly reduced waist circumference (MD -1.12 cm; p = 0.014), HbA1c (MD -0.070%; p = 0.029), and fasting glucose (MD -0.100 mmol/L; p = 0.031). Body weight and LDL cholesterol reductions were non-significant (MD -1.60 kg; p = 0.090 and MD -0.130 mmol/L; p = 0.343, respectively). In STAMPEDE, metformin did not improve OS (HR 0.91; p = 0.15); the high-volume subgroup showed a survival benefit (HR 0.79; p = 0.007; volume interaction p = 0.12, non-significant). In MANSMED, CRPC-free survival was significantly prolonged (HR 0.50; p = 0.01), though this signal derives from a single small, open-label trial.
CONCLUSIONS: Metformin added to ADT produces moderate-certainty reductions in waist circumference and HbA1c. Oncological benefit in unselected patients was not demonstrated; the hypothesis-generating STAMPEDE high-volume subgroup signal, derived from a single trial, warrants evaluation in a prospective, volume-stratified RCT.

Title: Evening high-intensity interval exercise attenuates the next-morning decline in flow-mediated dilation in healthy young men.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Vascular endothelial function (VEF), assessed by flow-mediated dilation (FMD), shows diurnal variation and is reduced in the early morning. Although exercise improves VEF, whether the vascular effects of evening high-intensity interval exercise (HIIE) persist into the following morning remains unclear. This study examined whether evening HIIE affects next-morning VEF.
METHODS: Eleven healthy young men completed exercise and control conditions in a randomized crossover design. In the exercise condition, participants performed 30 min of late-afternoon HIIE. FMD, blood pressure, and heart rate were measured from the afternoon of Day 1 to the afternoon of Day 2.
RESULTS: FMD increased following HIIE at 18:00 (6.5 ± 0.76% to 9.3 ± 0.93%, p < 0.05). In the control condition, FMD was lower at 08:00 than at 12:00 on Day 2 (4.7 ± 0.47% vs. 7.0 ± 0.79%, p < 0.05). At 08:00 on Day 2, FMD was higher in the exercise condition than in the control condition (7.6 ± 0.57% vs. 4.7 ± 0.47%, p < 0.05). Systolic blood pressure was lower in the exercise condition than in the control condition at 21:00 on Day 1 (114.6 ± 1.7 vs. 126.1 ± 1.8 mmHg) and 04:00 on Day 2 (88.7 ± 2.1 vs. 95.0 ± 1.2 mmHg) (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: A single bout of HIIE attenuates the morning decline in endothelial function. These findings suggest that the vascular benefits of exercise extend beyond the immediate post-exercise period and may influence the diurnal pattern of endothelial function.

Title: Impact of Dimethyl Sulfoxide on Early Cardiotoxicity After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
Abstract:
UNLABELLED: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of cryopreserved grafts in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) increased substantially. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), used as a cryoprotective agent, is well recognized for its infusion-related toxicity; however, its impact on cardiac function remains unclear.
METHODS: This prospective study included 96 consecutive patients (median age 46 years) undergoing allogeneic HSCT. Patients were divided according to graft type into cryopreserved (n = 59, 61.5%) and non-cryopreserved (n = 37, 38.5%) groups. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment was performed before and after transplantation.
RESULTS: Significant changes were observed in diastolic parameters (E/A, and E/E'), structural parameters (left ventricular mass and left ventricular mass index), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and right ventricular ejection fraction following HSCT. In the cryopreserved group, E/A ratio decreased below the normal range and E/E' ratio increased significantly, whereas no such changes were observed in the non-cryopreserved group. During the 30-day follow-up period, symptomatic cardiovascular toxicity occurred in 5 patients (5.2%), while subclinical cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction was detected in 16 patients (16.7%). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that GLS predicted cardiotoxicity with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.79-0.98; p < 0.0001). At a cut-off value of - 16.8%, sensitivity was 100% and specificity was 79%.
CONCLUSION: Cryopreserved graft administration may be associated with early alterations in left ventricular diastolic function, potentially reflecting DMSO-related cardiotoxicity. GLS appears to be a sensitive marker for the early detection and prediction of cardiotoxicity in patients undergoing allogeneic HSCT.

Title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat.
Abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans.

Title: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study.
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of heart failure cases but remains poorly defined due to its clinical heterogeneity. In the prospective PACIFIC-Preserved cohort (NCT04189029, n = 155), we applied multimodal deep phenotyping, including high-throughput proteomics, and unsupervised machine learning to identify biologically distinct HFpEF subgroups. Multiview clustering revealed two major HFpEF phenogroups: PEF1, characterized by inflammatory signaling, TNF receptor activation, cardio-skeletal injury, and greater renal dysfunction; and PEF2, marked by endothelial stress and milder perturbations. Conventional diagnostics alone could not reliably distinguish these subgroups, but a multimodal classifier integrating clinical, imaging, and proteomic variables achieved high predictive accuracy (F1-score 0.87). External validation in the MEDIA-DHF cohort (n = 456) confirmed that PEF1 was independently associated with adverse outcomes (adjusted HR 2.27, 95% CI 1.04-4.94). These findings establish a classifier-driven, biologically informed stratification of HFpEF, providing a framework for precision medicine in heart failure.

Title: Characterizing vaginal misoprostol induction in individuals with and without severe obesity.
Journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare labor induction characteristics and delivery outcomes among individuals with body mass index < 40 versus ≥ 40 kg/m2 undergoing induction at term.
STUDY DESIGN: This secondary analysis utilized data from the vaginal misoprostol arm of a cluster randomized controlled trial comparing vaginal to oral misoprostol for induction. Individuals at ≥ 37 weeks gestation with cervical dilation ≤ 2 cm undergoing induction using a standardized protocol were included. Vaginal misoprostol was given in 25 µg doses every three hours for up to five doses, followed by a standardized oxytocin protocol. We compared labor progression among individuals with BMI < 40 and ≥ 40 kg/m2 at delivery, including labor duration, misoprostol use, and obstetric and neonatal outcomes. Generalized estimating equations were used to account for clustering and comorbid conditions. Effect sizes were presented as odds ratios and adjusted mean differences with 95% confidence intervals.
RESULTS: From May 2021 to September 2022, 1,322 patients received vaginal misoprostol for labor induction at term. Among these, 1,058 (80.0%) had a BMI < 40 kg/m2 and 264 (20.0%) had a BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2. Individuals with severe obesity were more likely to start induction with a closed cervix. After adjustment for clustering, initial cervical dilation, hypertension, and diabetes, inductions in the group with severe obesity had longer total durations (adjusted mean difference 3.5h, 95% CI 1.9-4.8), first stage of labor (adjusted mean difference 2.2h, 95% CI 0.6-3.8), and duration of oxytocin use (adjusted mean difference 2.5, 95% CI 1.1-3.8). Individuals with BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2 also had lower odds of vaginal delivery (aOR 0.6, 95% CI 0.4-0.8) and required more doses of misoprostol for induction.
CONCLUSION: Severe obesity, defined as BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2, is associated with longer time to delivery, increased misoprostol requirement, longer duration of oxytocin use, and lower odds of vaginal delivery compared to individuals with lower BMI. Consideration of alternative labor induction protocols must be balanced with increased comorbidities and overall obstetric morbidity in this group.

Title: Short-frame, self-expanding, fully recapturable transcatheter aortic valve replacement device in pure aortic regurgitation: Procedural performance and 30-day outcomes.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Achieving stable anchoring and effective sealing remains the principal limitation of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with pure native aortic regurgitation (PNAR). A short-frame, fully recapturable self-expanding valve may expand the procedural margin by enabling iterative repositioning and implantation depth optimisation in non-calcified anatomy.
METHODS: We analysed 13 consecutive patients with symptomatic moderate-to-severe or severe PNAR who underwent transfemoral TAVR with the ScienCrown® (Lepu Medical, Beijing, China) system. The primary endpoint was technical success at exit from the procedure room according to VARC-3 criteria. Secondary endpoints included device success and early safety at 30 days.
RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all patients (13/13, 100%), and device success at 30 days was also achieved in all patients (13/13, 100%). The 30-day early safety endpoint was met in 12 patients (92.3%). The mean prosthesis size was 27.62 ± 1.26 mm, with a mean prosthesis diameter oversizing relative to the average annular diameter of 12.90 ± 3.54%; no balloon predilatation was performed. The mean number of deployment attempts was 1.62 ± 0.77. All procedures were completed without valve embolisation/migration, coronary obstruction, second-valve implantation, or emergency surgery. One patient (7.69%) developed complete atrioventricular block on postoperative day 3 and underwent permanent pacemaker implantation; no additional pacemaker implantations occurred through 30 days. Predischarge diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated no new acute cerebral infarction. At 30 days, there were no deaths, strokes or transient ischaemic attacks, myocardial infarction, life-threatening/major bleeding, major vascular complications, endocarditis, or valve-related reinterventions. Mean transvalvular gradients were 7.67 ± 5.20 mmHg, and all patients had improved or stable NYHA functional class with no moderate or severe residual aortic regurgitation.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory single-centre series, transfemoral TAVR using a short-frame, fully recapturable self-expanding valve achieved 100% technical success and favourable early safety and haemodynamic performance in selected patients with PNAR. Prospective multicentre studies with longer follow-up and appropriate comparator groups are warranted.

Title: Rationale and design of a randomized controlled trial to evaluate thrombus modification efficacy of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in patients with ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction: The CAPTURE AMI study.
Journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal myocardial perfusion remains impaired in up to half of patients after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), partly through the distal embolization of thrombus and plaque debris. Reduction of thrombus burden prior to PCI in STEMI has been associated with improved markers of perfusion. However, traditional manual syringe aspiration thrombectomy has demonstrated inconsistent efficacy of thrombus extraction in prior studies. Sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy may achieve more reliable coronary thrombus extraction, with promising early results in non-randomized analyses thus far.
OBJECTIVES: CAPTURE AMI (ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT07687576) will test whether sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy reduces pre-stent thrombus burden compared with standalone PCI in patients with highly thrombotic STEMI.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, single-center randomized controlled trial, 60 patients undergoing primary PCI with TIMI thrombus grade ≥ 4 will be randomized 1:1 to optical coherence tomography (OCT) guided PCI alone, or to sustained mechanical aspiration using the CAT-RX (Penumbra) Aspiration System followed by OCT-guided PCI. The primary endpoint is the absolute change in thrombus burden between two paired pre-PCI OCT runs, measured offline by blinded readers. Exploratory endpoints include pre-PCI thrombus volume, thrombus area and flow area, post-PCI in-stent thromboatheroma and flow volumes, final stent expansion and apposition on OCT, indices of coronary microvascular physiology and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events over 6-month follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: CAPTURE AMI will provide randomized, imaging- and physiology-based evidence on the thrombus-modifying efficacy of sustained mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in STEMI.

Title: Echocardiography-Detected Elevated Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure and Outcomes After Living Donor Liver Transplantation.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The clinical significance of mild to moderate elevation in pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) detected by transthoracic echocardiography during liver transplant evaluation remains uncertain, particularly in living donor liver transplantation (LDLT).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of adult living donor liver transplant recipients between 2018 and 2023. Preoperative PASP was estimated using transthoracic echocardiography, and patients were stratified into PASP ≤35 mm Hg and elevated PASP (>35 mm Hg) groups. The primary outcome was 5-year overall survival, and the secondary outcome was intensive care unit (ICU) stay.
RESULTS: Among 230 recipients, 141 had PASP ≤35 mm Hg and 89 had PASP >35 mm Hg. Five-year overall survival was similar between groups (70%vs 72%; log-rank p = 0.905). Elevated PASP was not associated with mortality on univariate Cox regression analysis. The proportion of patients with prolonged ICU stay (>5 days) did not differ significantly between groups. Higher body mass index was identified as a significant predictor of increased mortality risk.
CONCLUSION: Mild to moderate PASP elevation detected by echocardiography was not associated with inferior long-term survival or increased ICU utilization following LDLT. Modest PASP elevation on preoperative echocardiography alone should not preclude transplantation in carefully selected candidates.

Title: Randomized trial of counter-pressure and position maneuvers to prevent vasovagal syncope after intravenous cannulation for cardiac CT: The CoPPMan-IVC trial.
High-Frequency Low-Tidal Volume Ventilation and Procedural Efficiency in Atrial Fibrillation Catheter Ablation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare high-frequency low-tidal volume (HFLTV) ventilation with standard ventilation (SV) regarding procedural efficiency, airway mechanics, and clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation.
DESIGN: Retrospective, observational, nonrandomized cohort study.
SETTING: Electrophysiology laboratory of a single tertiary-care university hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: There were 160 consecutive eligible adults undergoing first-time AF radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia between June 2023 and May 2024.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients received HFLTV (n = 80; respiratory rate 25-30 breaths/min, tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg, ETCO₂ maintained <50 mmHg) or SV (n = 80; tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg, respiratory rate 10-12 breaths/min) per attending anesthesiologist practice. All received propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Primary outcomes were total procedure time and radiofrequency ablation time; secondary outcomes were airway pressures, oxygenation, AF recurrence at 1 and 6 months, AF-related hospitalization, and complications. HFLTV was associated with lower median procedure time (110 v 128 minutes; p < .001) and ablation time (23 v 28 minutes; p < .001). Peak (14 v 18 cmH₂O) and minimum (13 v 15 cmH₂O) airway pressures were lower with HFLTV (both p < .001), whereas ETCO₂ and SpO₂ nadir were comparable. Multivariable regression identified HFLTV as an independent predictor of shorter ablation time (nonstandardized β=-5.48 minutes; 95% CI -7.05 to -3.91; p < .001). In exploratory analyses, recurrence at 1 month (7.5% v 15.0%; p = .211) and 6 months (13.8% v 18.8%; p = .520) and 6-month AF-related hospitalization (12.5% v 18.8%; p = .384) were numerically lower with HFLTV but confidence intervals were wide and included no difference.
CONCLUSION: In a consecutive cohort including paroxysmal and persistent AF, HFLTV was associated with shorter procedure and ablation times and lower measured airway pressures without compromising gas exchange. Clinical outcome analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, warranting prospective randomized evaluation.

Title: Serratus Posterior Superior Intercostal Plane Block Versus Superficial Parasternal Intercostal Plane Block With Local Infiltration for Postoperative Analgesia in Open Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Postoperative pain after open cardiac surgery arises from both sternotomy and chest drains and is often inadequately controlled by anatomically limited techniques. This study compared the serratus posterior superior intercostal plane block (SPSIPB, C3-T10 spread) with superficial parasternal intercostal plane block (PSIPB) plus chest drain-site infiltration.
DESIGN: Prospective, randomized, controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment.
SETTING: Single-center tertiary referral cardiac surgery center.
PARTICIPANTS: Adults undergoing elective open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy; 80 assessed for eligibility, 76 randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Bilateral SPSIPB (n = 35) or bilateral PSIPB plus local anesthetic infiltration at mediastinal and pleural chest drain sites (n = 41), performed preoperatively under ultrasound guidance.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was cumulative 24-hour opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME); the registered secondary outcomes were Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores at rest and on coughing and the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) at 24 hours. All other comparisons were exploratory. Twelve patients were excluded after randomization (2 SPSIPB, 10 control), leaving 33 and 31 for analysis. Opioid consumption was significantly lower in the SPSIPB group (36.6 ± 17.5 v 56.7 ± 16.1 mg of MME; mean difference 20.1 mg of MME; 95% CI, 11.7-28.5; p < 0.001). NRS scores were comparable during the first postoperative hour but lower in the SPSIPB group from 2 hours onward during coughing and at 4, 8, and 24 hours at rest (all p ≤ 0.019). QoR-15 scores were higher in the SPSIPB group (119 [112-126] v 108 [105-111.5]; median difference 10 points; 95% CI, 6-15; p < 0.001), exceeding the minimal clinically important difference of 6 points. Adverse events, including postoperative nausea and vomiting, did not differ between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with PSIPB plus drain-site infiltration-an active comparator targeting both the sternal and drain regions-SPSIPB reduced opioid consumption and improved quality of recovery and may be a valuable component of multimodal analgesia within Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols.

Title: The effect of near-infrared spectroscopy guided intraoperative care on neurocognitive and functional outcomes after cardiac surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse neurocognitive and functional outcomes are common after cardiac surgery. Cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitors regional cerebral oxygen saturation, allowing clinicians to detect and reverse cerebral desaturation. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs to evaluate whether intraoperative NIRS monitoring improves neurocognitive outcomes after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science for RCTs comparing NIRS-guided intraoperative management with usual care in adults undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, assessing the outcomes of postoperative cognitive decline, delirium, stroke, mortality, and functional recovery. We pooled data using random-effects meta-analysis and assessed certainty of evidence using GRADE methodology.
RESULTS: We included 17 RCTs (N=2288). NIRS-guided management probably reduces early postoperative cognitive decline (risk ratio [RR] 0.65, 95% CI 0.42-0.99; I2=65%, moderate certainty), may have little or no effect on stroke (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.42-1.91; low certainty) or mortality (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.47-1.52; low certainty), and may have no effect on delirium (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56-1.09; I2=32%, low certainty). Findings were primarily derived from small, single-centre trials with heterogenous NIRS thresholds and intervention algorithms. Few studies evaluated outcomes beyond 30 days, and none evaluated validated measures of quality of life or function.
CONCLUSIONS: Although NIRS-guided intraoperative care shows promise for reducing early postoperative cognitive decline after cardiac surgery, evidence of benefit for other neurocognitive or clinical outcomes remains limited. Large multicentre studies are needed to confirm its utility, refine intervention thresholds, and determine its impact on long-term cognition, function, and quality of life. Systematic review protocol. PROSPERO (CRD42022336468).

Title: [miR-376b-5p and immune-inflammatory indicators for predicting in-hospital mortality in acute myocardial infarction].
Journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the early predictive efficacy of serum microRNA-376b-5p (miR-376b-5p) combined with immuno-inflammatory markers for all-cause mortality during hospitalization in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted. A total of 316 patients with AMI admitted to the Department of Cardiovascular Medicine of Hengshui People's Hospital from June 2023 to June 2025 were enrolled. Peripheral venous blood was collected immediately before percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI, within 24 hours after admission) to detect serum miR-376b-5p, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR), Systemic Immune Inflammation Index (SII), platelet/lymphocyte ratio (PLR) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) levels. All patients underwent emergency or elective PCI. The outcome event was all-cause mortality during hospitalization, and patients were divided into a death group (52 cases) and a survival group (264 cases). The clinical data and the levels of the aforementioned indicators were compared between the two groups. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify the influencing factors of in-hospital mortality; receiver operator characteristic curves (ROC curves) were plotted to evaluate the predictive value of serum miR-376b-5p and immune inflammation indicators for in-hospital mortality risk in AMI patients, and the area under the curve (AUC) was calculated.
RESULTS: The proportion of patients with Killip class III in the death group and the levels of serum miR-376b-5p, NLR, SII, PLR, and hs-CRP were all higher than those in the survival group (all P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that elevated levels of NLR [odds ratio (OR)=2.097, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.453-3.027], SII (OR=2.011, 95%CI was 1.286-3.144), PLR (OR=1.067, 95%CI was 1.034-1.101), and miR-376b-5p (OR=1.831, 95%CI was 1.282-2.616) were independent risk factors for in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI (all P<0.05). The ROC curve indicated that NLR, SII, and PLR all had predictive value for in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI, and the combined prediction of NLR+SII+PLR had a higher predictive value than each individual marker (AUC=0.859), with sensitivity and specificity of 82.69% and 76.89%, respectively. The AUC of serum miR-376b-5p for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with AMI was 0.812, with sensitivity and specificity of 75.00% and 75.38%, respectively. The AUC of serum miR-376b-5p combined with NLR+SII+PLR increased to 0.903, which was higher than that of each individual marker (both P<0.05), with sensitivity and specificity of 88.46% and 82.58%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated serum miR-376b-5p, NLR, SII and PLR levels immediately before PCI are independent risk factors for in-hospital death in AMI patients. Serum miR-376b-5p combined with NLR+SII+PLR has a higher predictive value for in-hospital death in AMI patients.

Title: [Application of a spontaneous breathing trial based on high-flow oxygen therapy in weaning of mechanically ventilated patients].
Journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the application efficacy of a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) based on high-flow oxygen therapy (HFOT) during the weaning process in mechanically ventilated patients.
METHODS: A randomized controlled trial was conducted. A total of 163 patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation admitted to the Department of Critical Care Medicine, Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University, from September 2024 to July 2025 were enrolled and randomly assigned to the HFOT group (80 cases) or the pressure support ventilation (PSV) group (83 cases). The HFOT group received SBT based on HFOT, while the PSV group received SBT based on PSV. Baseline data were collected and compared between the two groups, and adverse events during SBT were recorded. The primary outcome was the success rate of extubation within 48 hours. Secondary outcomes included vital signs, sputum grade, arterial blood gas parameters measured before SBT and 30 minutes after SBT initiation, SBT success rate, and prognostic outcomes [duration of mechanical ventilation, length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay, hospitalization costs, ICU mortality, in-hospital mortality, and 28-day mortality].
RESULTS: A total of 163 mechanically ventilated patients were included, with 80 in the HFOT group and 83 in the PSV group. There were no statistically significant differences in baseline data or prognostic outcomes between the two groups. The SBT success rates were 100% (80/80) in the HFOT group and 98.8% (82/83) in the PSV group, and the 48-hour extubation success rates were 87.5% (70/80) and 80.5% (66/82), respectively, with no statistically significant differences (both P>0.05). At 30 minutes after SBT initiation, the heart rate (HR0.5) and the decrease in HR (ΔHR0.5) in the HFOT group were significantly lower than those in the PSV group [HR0.5: 87.10±12.73 vs. 94.28±13.60; ΔHR0.5: 0.0 (-3.0, 2.0) vs. -1.0 (-5.0, 1.0); both P<0.05]. No significant differences were observed in other vital signs, sputum grade, or arterial blood gas parameters between the two groups. No safety events occurred in either group during the trial, indicating good safety. Subgroup analysis showed statistically significant interactions between intervention modality and both age and duration of mechanical ventilation (both P<0.05). In patients aged≥65 years, the ICU length of stay in the HFOT group was significantly shorter by a mean of 83.12 hours [95% confidence interval (95%CI) was -151.28 to -14.96] compared with the PSV group. In patients with mechanical ventilation duration≥24 hours, the ICU length of stay in the HFOT group was significantly shorter by a mean of 157.40 hours (95%CI was -254.60 to -60.20) compared with the PSV group.
CONCLUSIONS: SBT based on HFOT is safe for weaning mechanically ventilated patients and offers certain physiological advantages in improving HR. In elderly patients (≥65 years) and those with prolonged mechanical ventilation (≥24 hours), HFOT-based SBT can significantly shorten ICU length of stay, but it does not show a clear advantage in improving the 48-hour extubation success rate.

Title: [Development and validation of a predictive model for high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy failure in patients with type I respiratory failure].
Journal: Zhonghua wei zhong bing ji jiu yi xue
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the independent risk factors for failure of high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy (HFNC) in patients with type I respiratory failure, and to establish and validate an effective risk prediction model.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted, Patients with type I respiratory failure who received HFNC treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University from January 2019 to December 2024 were selected as the research subjects. Clinical data within 24 hours after admission to the ICU were collected, including demographic information and general conditions, underlying diseases, early acute organ dysfunction, vital signs, laboratory examinations, disease severity scores, and treatment measures. Patients were divided into the HFNC success group and the HFNC failure group based on whether HFNC failure (endotracheal intubation and/or death during treatment) occurred. The overall cohort was randomly divided at a ratio of 7 : 3 into a training set and a validation set. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to screen independent predictors of HFNC failure, and a nomogram prediction model was constructed accordingly. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate the model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility.
RESULTS: A total of 700 patients with type I respiratory failure were included, of whom 601 experienced HFNC success and 99 experienced HFNC failure, with a failure rate of 14.1%. Compared with the HFNC success group, patients in the HFNC failure group had lower height, proportion of coronary heart disease, serum sodium, oxygenation index, Glasgow Coma Score (GCS), and proportion of patients receiving human albumin, while exhibiting significantly higher incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI), heart rate, respiratory rate, blood urea nitrogen level, serum creatinine level, blood lactate level, Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score, and Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II(APACHE II) score, as well as longer prothrombin time (all P<0.05). Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that the presence of AKI [odds ratio (OR)=2.113, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.159-3.854, P=0.015] and elevated blood lactate level (OR=1.148, 95%CI was 1.027-1.283, P=0.015) were independent risk factors for HFNC failure, while elevated oxygenation index (OR=0.973, 95%CI was 0.963-0.983, P<0.001) and higher GCS score (OR=0.815, 95%CI was 0.760-0.874, P<0.001) were independent protective factors. Based on these four independent predictors, a nomogram prediction model was established. The ROC curves showed that the area under the curve (AUC) of the training set and validation set were 0.844 (95%CI was 0.794-0.895) and 0.794 (95%CI was 0.706-0.881), respectively. At a cutoff value of 0.160, the sensitivities were 73.9% and 60.0%, the specificities were 81.0% and 82.8%, and the accuracies were 80.0% and 79.5% in the training set and validation set, respectively. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test showed good fit for the model in both the training set (χ 2=8.636, P=0.374) and validation set (χ 2=6.652, P=0.575). The calibration curves indicated good agreement between the model predicted probabilities and the actual observations. DCA demonstrated that the model exhibited good clinical net benefit over a wide range of threshold probabilities.
CONCLUSIONS: The nomogram model constructed based on AKI, blood lactate level, oxygenation index, and GCS score has good predictive performance for the risk of HFNC failure in patients with type I respiratory failure, providing a reference for early identification of high-risk patients and optimization of clinical decision-making.
