Title: Nationwide Evolution of Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Outcomes Following Introduction of the HeartMate 3 and Destination Therapy in Japan　- The Third Official Report From J-MACS.
Journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nationwide impact in Japan of contemporary improvement in the clinical management of durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), together with the introduction of the HeartMate 3 (Abbott, Pleasanton, CA, USA), on clinical outcomes remains uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Using the Japanese Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (J-MACS), we analyzed all patients undergoing durable LVAD implantation in Japan between 2011 and 2025. Patients were divided into an early era (up to 2018) and the contemporary era (since 2019), reflecting introduction of the HeartMate 3 in Japan. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during LVAD support. Among 1,859 patients, 1,587 underwent bridge-to-transplantation and 272 underwent destination therapy. Survival improved significantly in the contemporary era compared with the early era (5-year survival 84% vs. 76%, respectively; P=0.0002). Device dysfunction-free, pump thrombus-free, stroke-free, major bleeding-free, and pump exchange-free survival also improved significantly after 2019 (all P<0.0001). Right ventricular failure and ventricular arrhythmia that required appropriate defibrillation remained frequent complications. Among patients who received a durable LVAD since 2019, destination therapy recipients had lower survival than bridge-to-transplantation recipients (3-year survival 81% vs. 91%; P=0.0057).
CONCLUSIONS: Clinical outcomes after durable LVAD implantation improved substantially following the introduction of HeartMate 3 in Japan, particularly regarding pump-related and hemocompatibility-related complications. However, right ventricular failure and ventricular arrhythmia remain major unresolved challenges.

Title: Ulinastatin Protects Cognition in Cardiac Surgical Patients.
Journal: Annals of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery : official journal of the Association of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons of Asia
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the incidence of postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in patients undergoing cardiac valve surgery and the potential protective effects of ulinastatin on POCD.
METHODS: This was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind clinical trial. A total of 300 patients undergoing cardiac valve surgery were enrolled across the 3 hospitals and randomized to the control or ulinastatin treatment groups. The patients' cognition was evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). POCD was defined as a lower cognitive score after surgery than the baseline score. Serum levels of proinflammatory cytokines were measured by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.
RESULTS: The incidence of POCD in the control group was significantly higher than those in the ulinastatin group (42/150 vs. 24/150, p <0.05). The MMSE score in the control group was significantly lower after the operation [D0 vs. D3: 27.72 (1.88) vs. 27.09 (2.61), p <0.05], but did not change in the ulinastatin group [D0 vs. D3: 27.63 (2.29) vs. 27.31 (2.47), p >0.05]. In the ulinastatin group, plasma levels of matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9) and S100 calcium-binding protein B (S100β) were significantly lower than those in the control group after the operation.
CONCLUSIONS: The present study confirms that a transient proinflammatory state impairs cognition in patients undergoing cardiac surgery and indicates that perioperative administration of ulinastatin protects cognition.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Continuous wound infiltration with local anesthetics in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: Chinese medical sciences journal = Chung-kuo i hsueh k'o hsueh tsa chih
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postoperative analgesia is critical to recovery after cardiac surgery. Continuous wound infiltration (CWI) with local anesthetics (LAs) has been proposed as an opioid-sparing adjunct, but its efficacy beyond pain control and its safety profile remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing CWI with control in adult cardiac surgery. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to August 30, 2025, and updated on April 2, 2026. Primary outcomes were postoperative Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain scores and cumulative morphine consumption. Secondary outcomes included mechanical ventilation duration, length of stay, mortality, complications, patient satisfaction, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).
RESULTS: Twelve RCTs involving 2,117 patients were included. CWI significantly reduced VAS during mobilization at 24 h (MD=-0.93, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -1.53--0.33, P = 0.002) and 48 h (MD=-0.80, 95% CI: -1.17--0.44, P < 0.001), and decreased 48-hour morphine consumption (MD=-8.10 mg, 95% CI: -13.41--2.79, P = 0.003). No significant effects were observed on VAS at rest, mechanical ventilation duration, ICU or hospital length of stay, mortality, or major cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal, gastrointestinal complications, or postoperative infections. Patient satisfaction was higher with CWI. Technical complications were uncommon, and no clinically significant LA toxicity was reported.
CONCLUSIONS: In adult cardiac surgery, CWI with LAs modestly improves analgesia during mobilization and reduces opioid requirements without clear improvement in major clinical outcomes or length of stay. CWI appears safe and feasible and may serve as an adjunct in multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia strategies. Further adequately powered trials are warranted to define its comparative effectiveness within contemporary enhanced recovery after surgery pathways.

Title: A predictive model for heart failure in patients with hypertension and persistent atrial fibrillation: A retrospective single-center study.
Journal: Chinese medical sciences journal = Chung-kuo i hsueh k'o hsueh tsa chih
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive nomogram for heart failure in patients with hypertension and persistent atrial fibrillation (HT-PeAF).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed clinical data from patients with HT-PeAF hospitalized at Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital between 2010 and 2019. Predictive variables were selected based on multivariable logistic regression analysis and clinical relevance, which were then incorporated into a clinical nomogram. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for discrimination, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test for calibration, and decision curve analysis for clinical utility.
RESULTS: Of the 395 enrolled patients, 151 experienced heart failure. Nine predictive variables were identified: prior catheter ablation, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, hemoglobin, uric acid, creatinine, total bilirubin, fasting blood glucose, red blood cell distribution width, and coronary artery disease. The nomogram demonstrated good discriminative ability (AUC = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.72-0.81), good calibration (P = 0.44), and favorable clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: This accessible tool facilitates individualized risk stratification for heart failure in HT-PeAF patients, though prospective validation in multicenter Asian cohorts is warranted.

Title: "Not so minor" - Digital Amputation as a precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish tertiary vascular centre.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for five-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality.
METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017-2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry (HIPE) data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality.
RESULTS: 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least one minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (± 12.7). 70% had PAD and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n=73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major re-amputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischaemic heart disease (IHD) (OR 2.796, 95% CI 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136) and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularisation at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8% and 48% at one, three and five years, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

Title: THE CLINICAL PROFILE OF RUPTURE: A 19-YEAR CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSMS.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds.
METHODS: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation. The primary model included maximum aneurysm diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year; the extended model additionally included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Discrimination was evaluated using optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC).
RESULTS: Among 394 patients with infrarenal AAA, 194 presented with rupture and 200 underwent elective repair. Median diameter was 80.0 versus 53.0 mm (P < .001), and women comprised 10.9% versus 3.0% (P = .002), respectively. Diameter per 10-mm increase (odds ratio [OR], 2.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.84-2.61) and female sex (OR, 4.72; 95% CI, 1.49-14.94) were independently associated with ruptured presentation. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.836 for diameter alone, 0.832 for the primary model (diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year), and 0.840 for the extended model (primary model plus hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia). Sixteen of 160 ruptures (10.0%) occurred below sex-specific thresholds.
CONCLUSIONS: Diameter was the dominant factor associated with ruptured presentation, but female sex remained independently associated. These findings support diameter-based practice while highlighting the need for prospective, sex-aware, multiparametric risk assessment.

Title: The type of portal vein reconstruction does not affect the outcomes of pancreatic surgery or the patency of the portal vein.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety of the four types of portal vein reconstruction (PVR) as defined by the International Study Group of Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) and to analyse long-term survival outcomes in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
METHODS: A prospectively collected pancreatic surgery registry that was supplemented retrospectively was used. Patients who underwent open pancreatic resection with PVR between 2005 and 2024 were included. Clinicopathological characteristics, outcomes, and computed tomography images were analysed and tested in multivariate and survival analyses. For survival analyses, patients with PDAC who underwent pancreatectomy without PVR served as controls.
RESULTS: Pancreatectomies with PVR (n=386) comprised 63 tangential resections with venorrhaphy (ISGPS type I), 25 patch reconstructions (type II), 147 end-to-end anastomoses (type III), and 151 resections with graft interposition (type IV). Most type IV reconstructions (98.7%) used spiral grafts, predominantly made from the great saphenous vein (GSV). PVR thrombosis rate was 3.1% at 30 days and 5.7% at 90 days following surgery. There were no significant differences between PVR types I-IV in the incidence of PVR thromboses, complications, or mortality. Median survival for PDAC patients with PVR was 22.8 months, with no survival differences between types I-IV, compared with 31.7 months in patients without PVR, p=.003.
CONCLUSIONS: In this setting, where PVR was performed using GSV spiral grafts for interposition, the type of PVR did not associate with pancreatic surgery outcomes or portal vein patency. The rate of PVR thrombosis was low, and other complication rates and long-term survival outcomes were comparable with international standards.

Title: Postoperative complications following carotid endarterectomy are differentially impacted by sex and plaque instability.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in post-carotid endarterectomy outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for carotid endarterectomy rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing carotid endarterectomy for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes.
RESULTS: Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year post-surgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery. Additionally, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact post-endarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.

Title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality After Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization (DVA) has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and amputation-free survival (AFS). Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality.
RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%) (Table 2). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point (Figure 1). All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs 71 years; P = .047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs 47.1%; P = .064) (Table 3).
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure. All-cause mortality remained substantial throughout follow-up, consistent with the comorbidity burden of this population. These findings support TADV as a limb-salvage option for patients with no-option CLTI who would otherwise face major amputation, although larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm long-term durability.

Title: Association between increased superficial calcification clusters in carotid atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events after carotid artery stenting: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS.
METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on CTA. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n=24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n=96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P= 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P= 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P= 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P= 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P= 0.0256, HR= 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P= 0.0265, HR= 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323).
CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

Title: Embolic and atherosclerosis-associated acute mesenteric ischemia: distinct clinical entities with different outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute arterial occlusive mesenteric ischemia is associated with high mortality. Embolic and atherosclerosis-associated forms differ in vascular pathology, collateral circulation, and ischemic tolerance, which may contribute to differences in clinical presentation and outcomes. This study compared clinical presentation, treatment strategies, and outcomes between embolic acute mesenteric ischemia (EAMI) and atherosclerosis-associated acute mesenteric ischemia (AAMI).
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive patients diagnosed with acute arterial occlusive mesenteric ischemia between January 2004 and March 2026. Patients were stratified into EAMI and AAMI groups. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Secondary analyses evaluated clinical presentation, imaging findings, and treatment strategies. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between etiology and in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Of 216 patients identified, 190 were included in the final analysis (EAMI, 56.8%; AAMI, 43.2%). Patients with EAMI more frequently presented with sudden-onset abdominal pain, whereas AAMI was characterized by acute-on-chronic symptoms and longer symptom-to-treatment intervals. Imaging findings indicative of advanced bowel ischemia, including pneumatosis intestinalis and portomesenteric venous gas, as well as bowel resection at initial surgical exploration, were more common in AAMI (40.2% vs. 21.3%, p = 0.005). In-hospital mortality was higher in AAMI than in EAMI (75.6% vs. 60.2%, p = 0.025). In multivariable analyses, EAMI was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratios 0.41-0.47; both p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: EAMI and AAMI represent distinct clinical entities with different presentations and outcomes. AAMI is associated with delayed presentation, more advanced ischemic injury at diagnosis, and higher in-hospital mortality. Etiology is independently associated with in-hospital mortality and should be considered in risk stratification and the design of future studies.

Title: Outcomes of Open vs Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting.
METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into two groups based on the intervention: EVAR vs OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed.
RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.25, 95%CI: 0.18-0.34, p<0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95%CI: 0.23-0.42, p<0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95%CI: 0.19-0.31, p<0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the two treatment modalities.

Title: Potential clinical actionability of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for antimicrobial stewardship for urinary tract infections: a retrospective, single-centre, BI-Biotia UTI cohort study.
Journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) take 48-72 hours, leaving empirical therapy for urinary tract infections (UTIs) without resistance data. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) reports resistance within hours, but its potential clinical actionability for prescribing is underexplored.
METHODS: In a retrospective single-centre cohort (Bangkok tertiary hospital, 2018-2020), BIOTIA-DX results were compared with culture and AST in 251 culture-paired samples. Potential clinical actionability was assessed for 54 same-day empirical prescriptions and a post hoc ablation estimated what a rule-based policy would have prescribed under different information from mNGS.
RESULTS: Twenty-two of 54 prescriptions (40·7%, 95% CI 28·7-54·0) were potentially actionable: treatment failure prevention 9 (16·7%) and de-escalation 13 (24·1%). Excluding blaEC and blaACT raised cephalosporin specificity from 25·6% to 78·9% with a small tradeoff in sensitivity. NPVs were at least 89·7% for carbapenems, cephalosporins, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, aminoglycosides and the fluoroquinolone classifier reached 100·0% PPV in Escherichia coli. Our refined resistance classification rules achieved a good tradeoff between the risk of ineffective antibiotics and the use of broad-spectrum carbapenem, compared with observed prescribing.
CONCLUSIONS: In a high-resistance setting, a same-day mNGS report was potentially actionable for two in five empirical prescriptions, mainly through resistance calling. However, the findings rest on a small number of cases.

Title: Effects of a 12-week yogic breathing intervention on metabolic syndrome severity and cardiovascular risk factors: A randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the effects of Yogic breathing (Sudarshan Kriya Yoga [SKY]) on conventional and atypical cardiovascular risk factors in adults with metabolic syndrome (MetS).
METHODS: In this 12-week, two-arm randomized controlled trial, 72 adults (30-60 years) with MetS were randomized (1:1) to SKY plus standard care or waitlisted standard care control group. Conventional and atypical cardiovascular risk factors, spanning behavioral, biological, inflammatory, oxidative, and autonomic markers, were assessed at baseline and 3 months. Between-group effects were evaluated by ANCOVA (adjusted for baseline values and medication use) using per-protocol (PP) and intention-to-treat (ITT; last observation carried forward) analyses.
RESULTS: 64 participants completed follow-up (SKY, n = 34; control, n = 30). Improvements consistent across PP and ITT occurred in waist circumference (p = 0.025/0.035), MetS severity score (MetSSS) (p = 0.020/0.014), and heart rate variability (HRV) low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) power (p = 0.035/0.010). Self-regulation of eating behavior, systolic blood pressure (SBP), and LF/HF ratio were significant only under ITT (p = 0.0498, 0.035, 0.041), not PP (p = 0.146, 0.056, 0.118). No significant between-group differences were observed for other outcomes. Within SKY, changes in HF power and superoxide dismutase (SOD) correlated inversely with changes in MetSSS (r = -0.36, p = 0.039; r = -0.55, p = 0.001). No adverse events occurred.
CONCLUSION: 12-week of SKY improved waist circumference, MetS severity, and selected HRV measures in MetS adults. These findings were robust across analyses, while other outcomes were non-significant or inconsistent. Exploratory associations between HRV, SOD, and MetSSS warrant testing in larger, longer-duration trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Prospectively registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2023/08/056540) on 16-Aug-2023.

Title: 4D Flow Acquisition Parameters as Technical Correlates of Hemodynamic Measurements: An Analysis of the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot Registry of 4D flow Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced 4D flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) biomarkers such as kinetic energy (KE), vorticity (ω), and viscous energy loss (VEL) are increasingly used to characterize abnormal flow in repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF), but their sensitivity to acquisition parameters including magnet vendor, sequence and signal quality has not been defined. We sought to evaluate the real-world variability in 4D flow sequences and technical correlates to 4D flow measurements of the aorta (Ao) and right ventricle, leveraging the multicenter Tetralogy of Fallot 4D flow Registry of Energetics and Kinetics (TREK).
METHODS: This was a multicenter observational analysis of clinically acquired 4D flow CMR processed at a core laboratory. The technical analysis focused on systolic Ao and diastolic RV hemodynamic measurements of KE, ω and VEL. Time-resolved hemodynamic curves were summarized and compared across sequence/reconstruction type, contrast agents and sequence parameters. Interobserver variability was assessed with Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients. Apparent signal-to-noise ratio (aSNR), apparent velocity-to-noise ratio (aVNR) and presence of velocity aliasing were also measured. Multivariable linear/logistic regression was used to identify acquisition parameters associated with aSNR, aVNR and aliasing. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed to evaluate associations of aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing with KE, ω, and VEL after adjustment for clinical covariates.
RESULTS: The cohort included 345 datasets (295 rTOF studies and 50 controls). Sequence/reconstruction type, field strength, voxel volume, temporal resolution, and VENC were associated with aSNR and aVNR in multivariable models. Aliasing was associated with lower VENC. ω and VEL varied substantially across sequence/reconstruction type and contrast groups, whereas KE was comparatively more stable. In multivariable models, lower aSNR was associated with higher measured hemodynamic values after adjustment for clinical covariates, with stronger associations for ω and VEL rather than KE.
CONCLUSIONS: In a real-world multicenter 4D flow CMR registry, measured advanced hemodynamic biomarkers were associated with acquisition/reconstruction characteristics, apparent image quality, and residual aliasing. 4D Flow harmonization efforts should therefore extend beyond vendor types alone and explicitly account for aSNR, aVNR, and aliasing when interpreting derivative-based 4D flow measurements.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Transperitoneal vs Retroperitoneal Approaches of Open Aortic Repair for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Stratified by the Iliac Bifurcation Involvement.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared to OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study aims to compare the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by the iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting.
METHODS: The SVS Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery (CIA) bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses, as well as a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), were performed.
RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA, and 1,791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared to RPA, TPA was associated with higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.05-1.49, p=0.011), MACE (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.11-1.44, p=0.001), and a lower 1-year survival rate (HR: 1.23, 95%CI: 1.09-1.39, p=0.001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of lower extremity (LE) ischemia (OR: 0.47, 95%CI: 0.25-0.91, p=0.024) without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR: 0.80, 95%CI: 0.42-1.51, p=0.485), MACE (OR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.52-1.42, p=0.563), and 1-year survival (HR: 0.93, 95%CI: 0.59-1.47, p=0.768).
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, involvement of the iliac bifurcation in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. Whereas for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of LE ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

Title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
Abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) non-thoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with non-thoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with < 2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

Title: Non-invasive Left Ventricular End Diastolic Wall Stress and the Risk of Incident Heart Failure in a Clinical Population.
Abstract: Greater left ventricular (LV) wall stress has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes among patients with heart failure (HF). We examined the relation between LV wall stress and the risk of incident HF. Using data from the Vanderbilt Synthetic Derivative, we studied 29,246 adult patients without prevalent HF or ≥ moderate valve disease who underwent transthoracic echocardiography between 2014-2020. LV end diastolic wall stress (LVEDWS) was calculated from chamber and wall thickness measures and E/e' as a surrogate for LV end diastolic pressure. Incident HF was ascertained from ICD-9/10 codes. Correlates of LVEDWS were examined with multivariable linear regression. The association between LVEDWS and risk of incident HF was tested in Cox regression adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, blood pressure, body mass index, laboratory data including B-type natriuretic peptide, LVEF, and LV mass index. The cohort had a median age of 59 years, 54% females, with 11% of individuals identifying as Black. Median LVEDWS was 14.5 (IQR: 11.8-18.0) kdynes/cm2. Cross sectional correlates of LVEDWS ranked according to Chi-squared value were LVEF, heart rate, female sex, and LV mass index. Over a maximum follow-up time of 8.2 years (median 3.7 years), 3,082 (11%) individuals developed incident HF. In multivariable Cox regression, each 1-unit increase in LVEDWS significantly associated with an increased risk of incident HF (aHR: 1.019; 95%CI 1.014-1.024), which was largely consistent across subgroups. In conclusion, among a broad range of patients clinically referred for echocardiography, greater non-invasively measured LVEDWS associates with higher risk for incident HF.

Title: Epivascular glia and macular pigment changes after faricimab or aflibercept during the loading phase in diabetic macular edema: a prospective non-randomized pilot study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore short-term changes in epivascular glia (EVG), macular pigment optical density (MPOD), visual acuity, and retinal thickness after faricimab or aflibercept in treatment-naive eyes with center-involving diabetic macular edema (DME).
METHODS: This prospective, non-randomized pilot study included 30 eyes with DME and EVG on en face optical coherence tomography. Fifteen eyes received three monthly injections of faricimab 6 mg and 15 received aflibercept 2 mg. The primary exploratory outcome was complete EVG regression after loading. Secondary outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), MPOD, fluid resolution, and resolution of traction-related abnormalities.
RESULTS: Complete EVG regression occurred in 12/15 eyes (80.0%) with faricimab and 6/15 (40.0%) with aflibercept (Fisher's exact p = 0.060). Resolution of traction- related abnormalities occurred in 11/15 (73.3%) and 5/15 eyes (33.3%), respectively (p = 0.066). Post-loading CMT was 274.5 ± 61.3 versus 328.7 ± 72.4 µm (unadjusted p = 0.035), MPOD was 0.46 ± 0.07 versus 0.39 ± 0.08 (unadjusted p = 0.017), and BCVA was 0.27 ± 0.14 versus 0.36 ± 0.16 logMAR (p = 0.112).
CONCLUSIONS: EVG and traction- related outcomes were numerically more favorable with faricimab but were not statistically significant. Exploratory anatomical and MPOD differences require confirmation in larger randomized studies.

Title: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) exposure during cardiopulmonary bypass: A narrative review of human clinical evidence and future directions.
Abstract: BackgroundDi(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is widely used as a plasticizer in polyvinyl chloride medical devices employed during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). Although migration from these devices and blood-storage systems has long been recognized, the human clinical evidence remains limited and methodologically heterogeneous.MethodsThis narrative review used a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from database inception through 23 August 2026. Original peer-reviewed human clinical studies measuring parent DEHP or its metabolites in blood, plasma, or urine among patients undergoing CPB were eligible for the primary synthesis. Relevant mechanistic, biomaterial, transfusion-medicine, guideline, and regulatory sources were used for context.ResultsThe searches identified 237 database records; 33 duplicates were removed, and 204 unique records were screened. Thirteen full-text reports were assessed, and seven human clinical studies published between 1983 and 2025 were included. Across adult and pediatric settings, perioperative increases in parent DEHP and/or urinary or circulating metabolites were documented. The studies implicated multiple sources, including CPB components, blood-storage systems, and ancillary blood-contacting devices, but none provided complete patient-level source apportionment. DEHP-free tubing reduced, but did not eliminate, exposure. RBC washing reduced DEHP and MEHP in vitro, but a reduction in patient-level internal exposure has not been established.ConclusionHuman clinical evidence consistently demonstrates internal exposure to DEHP or its metabolites during cardiac surgery involving CPB. However, small heterogeneous cohorts, variable analytes and sampling schedules, and limited outcome follow-up preclude causal inference regarding clinical harm. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized biomonitoring and source-apportionment methods are required.

Title: Weight-stratified analysis of the heterogeneous effects of miniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass on perioperative outcomes in children with congenital heart disease: A retrospective cohort study.
Abstract: IntroductionMiniaturized cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) circuits may reduce intraoperative transfusion in pediatric cardiac surgery, but their effects across body weight categories remain unclear. This study compared transfusion and outcomes between conventional and miniaturized CPB circuits, emphasizing weight-stratified analyses.MethodsThis retrospective study included 3,196 pediatric cardiac surgery patients (2015-2024) receiving conventional (n = 548) or miniaturized (n = 2,648) circuits. Primary outcomes were transfusion avoidance during CPB, in the ICU, and combined. Secondary outcomes included ICU length of stay, mechanical ventilation, ultrafast-track extubation, 24-h chest tube drainage (normalized to mL/kg), and hematocrit dynamics. Multivariable logistic regression and subgroup analyses were performed.ResultsMiniaturized circuits improved CPB transfusion avoidance overall (47.9% vs. 29.0%; P < 0.001), especially in children weighing 3-9 kg (all P < 0.01). ICU transfusion avoidance was lower with miniaturized circuits overall (82.1% vs. 94.5%; P < 0.001), except in the 1-2 kg subgroup. Combined avoidance was higher with miniaturized circuits across 3-9 and 12-13 kg (all P < 0.05). ICU length of stay was shorter with miniaturized circuits in most weight subgroups, whereas it was prolonged in the 2-3 kg subgroup (150 vs. 75 h; P < 0.001). Overall mean 24-h chest tube drainage was significantly lower in the miniaturized group (9.05 ± 9.10 vs. 10.82 ± 7.76 mL/kg; P < 0.001); however, stratified analysis showed a significant increase only in the 4-5 kg subgroup (14.52 ± 7.88 vs. 11.96 ± 6.69 mL/kg; P = 0.046), with no differences in other weight strata. Multivariable analysis indicated that miniaturized circuits were an independent predictor of increased ICU transfusion risk (OR 2.59; P < 0.001), whereas higher body weight was associated with reduced risk (OR 0.76 per kg; P < 0.001).ConclusionsMiniaturized CPB circuits reduce intraoperative transfusion, particularly in children weighing 3-9 kg, but are associated with higher postoperative ICU transfusion and variable effects on chest tube drainage that are weight-dependent. The net benefit appears weight-dependent. These findings underscore the need for weight-stratified circuit selection, although further prospective studies are warranted.

Title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation.
METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644.
FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis.
INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication.
FUNDING: None.

Title: Reframing traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury as chronic multisystem disorders: toward integrated, long-term care.
Abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. However, most health systems still treat neurotrauma (TBI and SCI, collectively) as a time-limited event, leaving long-term surveillance of these patients fragmented or absent, which leads to preventable mortality and avoidable readmissions. TBI and SCI in adults should be reclassified as acute-onset multisystem chronic-risk conditions. Existing cardiovascular, endocrine, and psychiatric services do not capture neurotrauma-specific risks, including trauma-induced hypopituitarism, autonomic dysregulation, accelerated ageing, and cognitive-behavioural impairment, so neurotrauma care is best framed as a missing node in chronic neurological care. We propose a risk-stratified pathway of care navigation, multisystem screening, and telehealth; convergence with adjacent stroke, cardiometabolic, memory, psychiatric, pain, and epilepsy services; and the financing, workforce, and registry reforms needed to deliver measurable reductions in 5-year mortality, avoidable rehospitalisation, and long-term disability.

Title: Management of breakthrough pain during advanced labor with epidural alkalinized lidocaine 0.3%-epinephrine: a single-center retrospective study (2022-2026).
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breakthrough pain during advanced labor requires rapid analgesia while limiting motor block. We describe responses to epidural alkalinized lidocaine 0.3% with epinephrine 10 µg/mL.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included women receiving epidural alkalinized lidocaine 0.3%-epinephrine for breakthrough pain at cervical dilation of at least 7 cm after satisfactory neuraxial analgesia. Women with recurrent epidural boluses suggesting catheter dysfunction were excluded. Median bolus volume was 3 mL [interquartile range, 3-5]. The primary outcome was contraction-pain visual analog scale change from baseline to 5-15 min. Secondary outcomes included sensory and motor changes. Brackets indicate interquartile ranges. Paired assessments preceded delivery.
RESULTS: Of 153 women, 143 were analyzed. Median visual analog scale decreased from 50 [30-60] to 0 [0-0] mm (mean reduction, 45.2; 95% confidence interval, 41.9-48.4); 126 (88.1%) scored 10 mm or less. Median rescue-to-delivery interval was 52 min [31-88]. Median cephalad cold-loss extension was one dermatome [1-2]. Modified Bromage scores were unchanged in 138 (96.5%) and worsened in five (3.5%). Maternal hypotension and new fetal heart rate abnormalities each affected six women (4.2%). Among vaginal deliveries, operative delivery rates were 9.3 and 0.6 percentage points higher in nulliparous and parous women, respectively, than in same-period deliveries with neuraxial analgesia without the study rescue.
DISCUSSION: Epidural alkalinized lidocaine 0.3%-epinephrine (3-8 mL) was followed by early pain reduction with infrequent motor block increase, supporting clinical application of prior laboratory findings. Prospective comparisons should assess motor function and delivery outcomes.

Title: Transient coronary occlusion during elective PTCA: QRS changes are consistent with the timing of regional ventricular activation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrocardiographic assessment of acute myocardial ischemia has traditionally emphasized ST-segment changes, whereas QRS alterations have received comparatively less attention. Whether the timing of ischemia-induced QRS changes is related to the normal timing of regional ventricular activation remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the timing of QRS changes during acute coronary occlusion follows the timing of regional ventricular activation according to the occluded coronary artery.
METHODS: Electrocardiograms from 45 patients were recorded during controlled balloon occlusion of the left anterior descending (LAD), right coronary (RCA), and left circumflex (LCx) arteries. High-resolution, time-aligned analysis (1-ms) was performed using standard and derived leads, including regional loops and precordial bipolar and averaged signals. The timing and distribution of ischemia-induced QRS changes were compared between baseline and coronary occlusion.
RESULTS: The onset of ischemia-induced QRS changes differed according to the occluded coronary artery. In LAD occlusions, QRS vector changes occurred significantly earlier (40.7 ms), whereas RCA occlusions showed later changes (53.6 ms, p = 0.003 for LAD vs RCA comparison). Overall, the timing of QRS vector changes was consistent with the expected activation sequence of the myocardial territory supplied by the occluded artery.
CONCLUSIONS: During acute coronary occlusion, ischemia-induced QRS changes were consistent with the expected activation timing of the myocardial territory supplied by the occluded artery. These exploratory findings support a physiological framework for interpreting QRS changes during ischemia and suggest that the standard ECG contains underrecognized temporal information. Whether these temporal features can help identify the occluded coronary territory remains a hypothesis that requires prospective diagnostic-performance studies.

Title: Association of beta-blocker therapy with outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction stratified by GRACE risk score: A nationwide registry analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between beta-blocker use following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and clinical outcomes remain uncertain in the contemporary era of near-universal early revascularization and drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly for patients with preserved left ventricular function. We sought to determine whether associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied across Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) risk strata.
METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of 11,866 STEMI survivors from two prospective nationwide Korean registries who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with second-generation DES. Patients were categorized by beta-blocker prescription at discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at one year; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability treatment weighting were employed to mitigate confounding. Variation in associations was examined across the continuous GRACE risk spectrum, categorized into low-risk (GRACE <85), intermediate-risk (GRACE 85-179), and high-risk (GRACE ≥180) strata.
RESULTS: Beta-blockers were prescribed to 83.8% of the cohort. After propensity matching, beta-blocker use was associated with lower one-year all-cause mortality (2.7% vs. 4.2%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.91) and MACE (6.0% vs. 8.3%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.55-0.92). These associations attenuated by three years. The GRACE 2.0 score exhibited robust discrimination for mortality (AUC = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.76-0.82). Continuous interaction analyses showed small model-estimated absolute risk differences in low-risk patients (GRACE <85), whereas the largest model-estimated absolute risk difference was observed in intermediate-risk individuals (GRACE 85-179).
CONCLUSIONS: Among STEMI survivors treated with contemporary PCI, associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied according to baseline GRACE risk. No statistically significant association was observed in low-risk individuals (GRACE <85), whereas the association with lower mortality was most evident in the intermediate-risk group (GRACE 85-179). These hypothesis-generating findings warrant evaluation in randomized trials before being used to guide treatment decisions.

Title: Development and external validation of a non-laboratory model to predict early-onset cardiovascular disease risk: a multicohort machine learning study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a questionnaire-based model for two related tasks in adults younger than 65 years: classification of incident early-onset cardiovascular disease (EOCVD) among participants without cardiovascular disease at baseline, and time-to-event prediction of all-cause mortality among participants with EOCVD at baseline.
METHODS: Longitudinal data were obtained from CHARLS, HRS, KLoSA, ELSA, and SHARE. The incidence classification analysis included 37,082 participants, and the prognostic survival analysis included 19,478. Eighteen questionnaire or routinely obtainable predictors were used. No laboratory biomarker or imaging measurement was entered into either model, although reported diagnoses may have depended on earlier clinical testing.
RESULTS: CatBoost achieved an AUROC of 0.6869, an AUPRC of 0.1438, a precision of 0.1105, and a recall of 0.6512 in the independent SHARE cohort. The Cox proportional hazards model achieved a test-set C-index of 0.7175; its 3-, 5-, and 7-year AUROCs were 0.7314, 0.7348, and 0.7350.
CONCLUSIONS: P-EOCVD provides questionnaire-based risk stratification for incident EOCVD and subsequent mortality. Its low precision precludes diagnostic use. The model may support first-step screening where laboratory testing is not immediately available, but prospective validation and recalibration are required before use in under-resourced populations.

Title: Implementation of IRRAflow active irrigation in neurosurgical patients: A case series and literature overview.
Journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Active fluid management systems such as IRRAflow aim to overcome the limitations of passive external drains by enabling simultaneous automated irrigation and aspiration in a closed circuit. In acute and chronic subdural hematoma (a/cSDH), it enables active subdural irrigation, whereas in subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and ventriculitis, it allows continuous ventricular CSF exchange and, when indicated, intrathecal administration of therapeutic agents.
METHODS: A literature analysis identified studies reporting IRRAflow use for SAH, SDH, IVH, or ventriculitis. Additionally, a single-center retrospective series of 13 consecutive patients treated with IRRAflow was analyzed, focusing on clinical course, complications, and outcomes.
RESULTS: Thirty studies comprising 345 patients were included in the literature analysis. In cSDH, clinical resolution was reported in 40 cases (90.9%), with recurrence in 3 patients (6.8%) and no reported infections or catheter obstructions. In aSDH, only 1/11 patient experienced clinical deterioration and required conversion to craniotomy. In IVH, outcomes were more variable, with complete resolution in 14/36 cases (38.9%), clinical improvement in 15/36 (41.7%), deterioration in 1/36 (2.8%), and death in 6 (16.7%). In ventriculitis, largely reported in case reports and small case series, resolution or improvement was achieved in 27/35 patients (77.1%), while mortality was 8/35 (22.9%). In aSAH, 7/23 (30.4%) patients died from complications of the hemorrhage. Vasospasm occurred in 7/23 (30.4%) patients, including two who subsequently died, while 2/23 (8.7%) required permanent shunting; both were survivors who had experienced vasospasm. No device-related complications were reported. Our institutional cohort included 6 patients with IVH, 4 with cSDH, and 3 with ventriculitis. Among the IVH cases, 3/6 patients died before discharge, 1 died during follow-up, whereas the other 2 had an mRS score of 3 and 2 at last follow-up. Among patients with cSDH, 3/4 achieved favorable functional recovery at follow-up, while 1/4 died before discharge because of complications unrelated to IRRAflow. Among the 3 patients with ventriculitis, 1 died following a complication related to urokinase infusion after adjunctive urokinase administration, whereas the remaining 2 (66.7%) achieved resolution or improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: Both the institutional cohort and the literature search showed promising results for the use of IRRAflow in cSDH. Results on ventriculitis, aSAH and aSDH are still uncertain due to the small sample sizes. Regarding IVH, neither the exploratory review nor our institutional case series identified a clear clinical benefit associated with IRRAflow use. Nevertheless, the available evidence remains limited by predominantly observational, small and heterogeneous studies, precluding comparative conclusions.

Title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of triiodothyroacetic acid (Triac) in patients with resistance to thyroid hormone β (RTHβ): a multicentre, international, retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disease features in resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ), caused by THRB mutations, arise from insensitivity to thyroid hormone in tissues expressing thyroid hormone receptor (TR)β and from lifelong thyrotoxic effects in TRα1-expressing tissues, posing substantial cardiovascular morbidity/mortality. The T3-analogue triiodothyroacetic acid (Triac) holds potential as an effective treatment. Systematic data on Triac therapy in RTHβ are lacking, and the mechanisms through which Triac acts are unclear. This study aims to elucidate these knowledge gaps.
METHODS: Clinical and biochemical data were obtained through an, international retrospective cohort study in patients with RTHβ. Transcriptional activity of all TRβ mutants, on the background of the pituitary-expressed β2 receptor isoform and positively (DR+4-TRE) or negatively (TSHα-TRE) regulated reporter genes plus T3 or Triac, was studied. Thyroid function and TSH responses to T3 and Triac were tested in zebrafish expressing TRβ mutants.
FINDINGS: We collected data from 28 patients with RTHβ (range: 0.4-73.1 years) with 18 unique mutations treated with Triac in 6 centres. Triac reduced TSH (by 43%) and FT4 (by 37%) concentrations in all heterozygous patients, supported by consistent findings in zebrafish. Our functional studies showed that TRβ2 mutants exhibited reduced (all) or absent (G432del) T3-dependent transcriptional activity, with similar EC50 and IC50 values for T3 and Triac, except for R316H, which showed a 5-times lower EC50/IC50 value for Triac compared to T3.
INTERPRETATION: In this international, multicentre study we have documented that Triac lowers elevated FT4 concentrations in patients with RTHβ effectively. Integrating our clinical and molecular observations we suggest that Triac can act via different modes of action, with activation of the wild-type receptor being a relevant mechanism. Our study may inform clinical management and could shape future interventional studies in patients with RTHβ.

Title: Identification of symptomatic carotid atherosclerotic plaques using dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography-derived perivascular adipose tissue parameters and plaque morphology.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish and validate a multidimensional model for identifying symptomatic carotid plaques based on the combination of plaque morphological characteristics and perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) parameters obtained from dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography (DLCT).
METHODS: This single-center study included 256 patients with carotid atherosclerosis. Patients were divided into symptomatic and asymptomatic groups based on the presence or absence of transient ischemic attack or ipsilateral ischemic stroke within 2 weeks before DLCT. The study comprised a retrospective training cohort (n = 133), a retrospective internal validation cohort (n = 58), and a prospectively enrolled independent temporal test cohort (n = 65). Conventional plaque characteristics and multiple PVAT parameters were compared between the two groups. Imaging variables independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques were identified using multivariable logistic regression and incorporated into classification models.
RESULTS: Degree of stenosis, plaque burden, and the effective atomic number (Zeff) of PVAT were independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques. Model 2 incorporated all three parameters demonstrating strong discriminatory performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.907, 0.825, and 0.848 in the training, validation, and test sets, respectively. Incorporation of PVAT Zeff improved the discriminative performance and reclassification beyond conventional stenosis and plaque-burden assessment.
CONCLUSIONS: Degree of stenosis, plaque burden, and PVAT Zeff were independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques. Adding PVAT Zeff to conventional plaque characteristics improved model discrimination and provided complementary information for the characterization of symptomatic lesions.

Title: Signs of Life and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Multicenter Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of individual signs of life (SOLs) remains unclear in patients experiencing traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (t-OHCA).
OBJECTIVES: To describe clinical outcomes among patients with t-OHCA by the presence of each SOL at the scene.
METHODS: Data from the SOS-KANTO 2017 study, a multicenter prospective registry of OHCA cases treated between 2019 and 2021, were retrospectively analyzed. Adult patients diagnosed with t-OHCA were included, excluding those with a palpable pulse upon emergency medical service (EMS) arrival. Patients were categorized into eight subgroups based on the presence of three SOLs at the scene-the pupillary light reflex, spontaneous respiration, and cardiac electrical activity - and descriptive analyses were performed. The primary outcome was survival beyond the emergency department (ED).
RESULTS: Of the 462 patients included in the analysis, two (0.4%) exhibited all three SOLs, and 18 (3.9%) exhibited two SOLs; in the latter group, two demonstrated cardiac activity and a pupillary reflex, and 16 had cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration. Among the 124 patients (26.8%) with only one SOL, 117 had cardiac activity, three showed a pupillary reflex, and four exhibited spontaneous respiration. No SOLs were observed in 318 patients (68.8%). Overall, 22 patients (4.8%) survived beyond the ED. The highest survival rate was observed in the subgroup with both cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration (4/16; 25%), followed by the subgroup with cardiac activity alone (10/117; 8.5%).
CONCLUSIONS: Among the t-OHCA patients, survival beyond the ED was observed more frequently in those with cardiac electrical activity at the scene.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Exploratory Analysis of the Innate Immune System in Aortic Stenosis Patients With and Without ASCVD.
Abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) leads to aortic stenosis (AS) through inflammation and fibro-calcific remodeling. Although CAVD and atherosclerosis share features, not all patients with AS develop atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), suggesting mechanistic heterogeneity. This case-control study evaluated inflammatory profiles and valvular remodeling in 128 patients with AS (59.4% with ASCVD) and 105 controls. Immune cell composition and monocyte markers were analyzed by flow cytometry, whereas cytokine production was assessed after peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) stimulation. Both AS groups had higher interleukin (IL)-6, leukocyte, monocyte, and neutrophil counts than controls, with lower monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR isotype and higher C-C chemokine receptor (CCR)2 expression. Cytokine responses were also elevated, particularly in AS patients with ASCVD. They also showed higher IL-6 concentrations, higher proportions of classical monocytes, and lower intermediate and non-classical monocytes compared with patients without ASCVD. Overall, AS was associated with a pro-inflammatory monocyte phenotype and function, most prominently in patients with ASCVD. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04717219.

Title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency.
Journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/- mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II-treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/- mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility-HFpEF interactions.

Title: Impact of HIV on Perioperative Organ Injury and Surgical Outcomes in 41 Million Surgical Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While antiretroviral therapy has improved surgical safety for people living with HIV, comprehensive data on perioperative organ injury and its impact on patient safety remain limited. This study aimed to compare the incidence of perioperative organ injury, in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay, and hospitalization costs between people living with HIV and HIV-negative individuals undergoing surgery in the United States.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2021. The population-based sample included adult patients (age >18 years) identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. Of 41,622,004 eligible surgical admissions, 2,088,307 (5.0%) were people living with HIV and 39,533,697 were HIV-negative. Primary outcomes were perioperative organ injury incidence and associated mortality; secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay and total hospital charges. Adjusted models accounted for baseline characteristics and surgical complexity.
RESULTS: Among the 41,622,004 surgical admissions, people living with HIV were found to be older and carried a significantly higher comorbidity burden, with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 8 compared to 1 in the HIV-negative group. Perioperative organ injury occurred in 1,348,363 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (64.6%) compared with 7,867,547 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (19.9%). Acute myocardial infarction (33.5%) and acute kidney injury (22.0%) were the most common injuries among people living with HIV. In-hospital mortality occurred in 66,935 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (3.2%) compared with 872,170 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (2.2%). Hospital length of stay and hospital charges were also significantly higher. Adjusted analyses demonstrated that HIV status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-1.78), longer hospital length of stay (β = 2.73 days; 95% CI, 2.56-2.90), a decreased likelihood of home discharge (hazard ratio [HR], 0.73; 95% CI, 0.72-0.73), and increased hospitalization costs (β = $18,423; 95% CI, 16,712-20,134). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that elevated perioperative risk persisted among patients with asymptomatic HIV infection, although the greatest risk was observed among patients with symptomatic HIV disease/AIDS.
CONCLUSIONS: People living with HIV incur a significantly higher risk of perioperative organ injury and worse surgical outcomes despite advances in antiretroviral therapy. HIV status was independently associated with adverse perioperative outcomes in adjusted models, supporting its inclusion as a risk stratification variable in surgical planning. Future research should incorporate immunologic markers, such as CD4 count and viral load, to further refine perioperative risk prediction and optimize outcomes for this population.

Title: Evaluating the Role of Lower Extremity Elastic Bandage in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower extremity compression therapy has been proposed as an adjunct to mitigate diuretic resistance during acute decompensation of heart failure (ADHF). We evaluated the effect of lower leg compression with elastic bandages on diuretic efficiency in patients with diuretic-resistant ADHF.
METHODS: Historical cohort study enrolling adult cardiac ICU admissions with ADHF who used elastic bandages (EB) at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota from 2007 to 2017. The diuretic efficiency before and after applying EB was the primary outcome.
RESULTS: A total of 176 patients with heart failure who received elastic bandages were included. The in-hospital mortality rate, the median hospital length of stay, and 30-day hospital readmission were 9.7%, 11.4 days (IQR 7.1-19.0), and 11%, respectively. When EB was applied, the average daily loop diuretic dosage was decreased by a mean difference of 1.19 mg per 40 mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: 0.22 to 2.2; p = 0.016). The average post-EB diuretic efficiency was 1,355 mL (IQR 1,119, 1,590) per 40-mg furosemide, which was significantly higher than before EB application, with a mean difference of 340 mL per 40-mg furosemide equivalent (95% CI: -554, -125; p = 0.002). A higher diuretic efficiency led to lower diuretic doses. Average daily urine output before and after EB application was not different (2,642 pre-EB vs. 2,792 post-EB mL/day; 95% CI: -455 to 154; p = 0.33).
CONCLUSION: EB use enhances diuretic efficacy during ADHF. Further studies are needed to determine the potential clinical benefits and risks of applying EB compression treatment in ADHF.

Title: Association of Neutrophil-To-Lymphocyte Ratio and Atherogenic Index of Plasma With Angiographically Confirmed Coronary Artery Disease.
Journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis
Abstract: BackgroundThe neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) have been associated with coronary artery disease (CAD). We investigated their associations with angiographically confirmed CAD and lesion severity.MethodsThis retrospective study included 2,933 patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD at Wuhan Third Hospital. CAD was defined as ≥50% luminal stenosis in at least one major coronary artery or branch. Lesion severity was assessed using the Gensini score. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.ResultsAmong 2,933 patients, 1,615 had CAD and 1,318 had no significant stenosis. NLR and AIP were higher in patients with CAD and increased across Gensini score categories (all P<0.05). After adjustment, AIP remained independently associated with CAD (OR=1.557, P=0.042), whereas NLR did not (OR=1.019, P=0.581). AIP alone showed limited discrimination (AUC=0.537). A multivariable model including age, blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, and AIP showed an AUC of 0.779. Adding AIP did not significantly improve AUC (DeLong P=0.153) or NRI (0.071, P=0.106), although IDI improvement was significant (0.002, P<0.05).ConclusionsIn patients undergoing coronary angiography for suspected CAD, NLR and AIP were associated with CAD and angiographic disease burden. AIP remained independently associated with CAD, whereas NLR did not. However, AIP showed limited discrimination and no clear incremental improvement beyond conventional variables. These findings do not support population screening or routine clinical implementation.

Title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Significant Fibrosis in Steatotic Liver Disease: A Model Development Study.
Journal: Online journal of public health informatics
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent and noninvasive identification of patients with significant fibrosis remains a clinical challenge.
OBJECTIVE: We conducted an exploratory evaluation of explainable machine-learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a U.S. population-based cohort of adults with SLD, with particular attention to sensitivity, false-negative risk, and the limitations of using AUROC alone to assess screening suitability.
METHODS: We evaluated explainable machine-learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a U.S. population-based dataset. Forty-three routinely available clinical, demographic, anthropometric, laboratory, and lifestyle variables were included. After preprocessing and imputation, data were split into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) addressed class imbalance in the training set. Logistic regression, random forest, support-vector machine, XGBoost, k-nearest neighbors, naïve Bayes, artificial neural network, and a stacked ensemble were trained and evaluated. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, Cohen's kappa, and area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC). Because the intended use case was screening or triage, sensitivity was given particular interpretive importance. In addition to overall discrimination, a primary analytical objective was to examine sensitivity trade-offs, false-negative classifications, and the implications of model performance for screening suitability. Global and local model interpretability were assessed using feature importance, Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values, individual conditional expectation (ICE) plots, and individualized explanations.
RESULTS: Among 7,056 participants, 716 (10.1%) had significant fibrosis.
