METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.
RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.
CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

Title: Preoperative anaesthetic and cardiology MDT: Enhancing perioperative efficiency in elective non-cardiac surgery.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delays in obtaining specialist cardiology input for elective non-cardiac surgery can postpone definitive perioperative decision-making, increase short-notice cancellations and reduce theatre efficiency. In January 2021, our NHS trust introduced a weekly virtual Preoperative Anaesthetic and Cardiology Multidisciplinary Team meeting as a pathway redesign to improve access to specialist perioperative cardiovascular assessment.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective service evaluation of consecutive Preoperative Anaesthetic and Cardiology Multidisciplinary Team referrals between 1 January 2021 and 31 December 2024. Registry data were reviewed for referral indication, specialty, time from referral to first multidisciplinary team review and initial multidisciplinary team outcome. The impact on cardiology outpatient activity was estimated by comparing the Preoperative Anaesthetic and Cardiology Multidisciplinary Team pathway with the previous practice whereby non-emergency pre-assessment referrals were directed to a routine cardiology clinic.
RESULTS: A total of 869 patients were reviewed; four were excluded because of incomplete records, leaving 865 analysable cases. Mean time from referral to first multidisciplinary team review was under 14 days. In a typical 1-h meeting, six to ten cases were discussed (mean 8), with a mean discussion time of approximately 8 min per patient. At first review, 64% of patients received a definitive advisory outcome: 62% were considered fit to proceed and 2% unfit for surgery. The remaining 36% required further action; 24% were triaged to cardiology clinic and 12% were managed through expedited investigation or treatment adjustment pathways. Compared with the pre-existing pathway, this represented a 76% reduction in pre-assessment referrals to a general cardiology clinic, equivalent to 657 outpatient appointments avoided over 4 years.
CONCLUSIONS: A virtual anaesthetic-cardiology multidisciplinary team can provide timely specialist perioperative cardiovascular decision-making, reduce reliance on outpatient cardiology review and support elective pathway efficiency. This model is pragmatic, reproducible and may be valuable for NHS organisations seeking to streamline preoperative assessment while preserving access to specialist input for patients who need it most - a promising strategy for addressing elective surgery backlogs.

Title: Clinical application of volatile sedation in adult intensive care units: pharmacological mechanisms, delivery systems, and safety.
Abstract: Sedation is essential in critically ill mechanically ventilated patients, yet conventional intravenous agents carry risks of accumulation, organ-dependent clearance, and adverse effects. Volatile anesthetics offer several pharmacokinetic advantages, but their adoption in the intensive care unit has historically been limited by technical constraints. This review offers an updated, clinically focused overview of volatile- based sedation in adult intensive care units, covering pharmacological mechanisms, delivery systems, clinical outcomes, safety, and practical application. This review was conducted through systematic searching of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2016 and December 2025. Sevoflurane and isoflurane achieve sedation primarily via γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor modulation and offer organ-independent clearance, rapid onset/offset, and real-time end-tidal monitoring. Modern delivery systems, including reflection devices (Sedaconda-ACD) and automated platforms (MIRUS), have improved intensive care unit feasibility. Clinical evidence suggests volatile sedation may reduce awakening times and duration of mechanical ventilation compared with intravenous agents; however, results across randomized trials and meta-analyses are heterogeneous. Potential benefits have been reported in acute respiratory distress syndrome, post-cardiac arrest care, neurocritical illness, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and refractory agitation, but robust evidence is lacking across all settings. Limitations include hemodynamic effects, increased circuit dead space, renal safety concerns with sevoflurane, infrastructure requirements, occupational exposure, environmental impact, and cost. Volatile sedation is a feasible and pharmacologically rational option for selected mechanically ventilated intensive care unit patients, particularly those requiring prolonged sedation or with organ dysfunction limiting conventional agents. Current evidence does not support universal superiority over intravenous sedation. Inhaled anesthetics should be incorporated into individualized, multimodal sedation strategies within structured institutional frameworks. Large multicenter trials are needed to clarify effects on mortality, long-term neurological outcomes, and quality of life.

Title: Prioritization and Severe Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary graft dysfunction (PGD) is the leading cause of early morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation (LTx). Critically ill candidates may receive priority on the transplant waiting list; however, the relationship between prioritization and the development of severe PGD remains unclear.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained cohort including all consecutive LTx performed at a tertiary center between January 2016 and June 2025. Recipients were categorized according to prioritization status. Severe PGD was defined as grade 3 PGD according to the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation criteria. Clinical characteristics and outcomes were compared between prioritized and non-prioritized recipients. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of severe PGD, and survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
RESULTS: Among 310 LTx recipients, 74 (23.8%) were prioritized. They were younger, had a higher prevalence of pulmonary hypertension, and were more frequently hospitalized before transplantation, particularly in the intensive care unit. Severe PGD occurred more often among prioritized recipients (24% vs 7%). However, prioritization was not independently associated with PGD after adjustment. Pre-transplant extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support emerged as the strongest independent predictor of severe PGD. Thirty-day mortality was similar between groups, whereas prioritized recipients had higher 90-day and 1-year mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Prioritized LTx recipients have greater pre-transplant clinical severity, higher crude rates of severe PGD, and worse short-term survival. However, prioritization itself was not independently associated with PGD, suggesting that underlying disease severity and need for advanced support are the main drivers of post-transplant outcomes.

Title: Machine Learning of Band Gaps and Thermodynamic Stability in A2BB'X6 (X = F, Cl, Br, I) Double Perovskites with Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Objective Screening.
Abstract: A2BB'X6 double perovskites offer broad compositional flexibility, requiring screening strategies that jointly consider electronic properties and thermodynamic stability. We developed a leakage-controlled machine learning workflow integrating canonical-formula grouping, robustness tests, descriptor-cost analysis, and prediction uncertainty. The dataset contains 1975 Materials Project entries represented by 398 descriptors. Extra Trees predicted band gaps with a held-out MAE of 0.2031 eV and R2 of 0.9437, whereas histogram gradient boosting predicted energy above the hull with an MAE of 0.02122 eV atom-1 and R2 of 0.8601. The stability classifier achieved ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, and MCC values of 0.9603, 0.9632, and 0.8192, respectively. Removing 39 relaxed-structure descriptors increased hull-energy MAE by approximately 12.5%, supporting a two-stage workflow of composition-based triage followed by structure-informed refinement. Chemical-distribution-shift tests revealed substantial performance degradation and defined the applicability domain. Seventeen held-out compounds met the screening criteria, representing retrospective recovery rather than prospective discovery. Path-specific phonon calculations for one Tier-1 candidate and two representative Tier-2 fluorides showed no imaginary modes along L-Γ-X-W, but cannot establish full-zone dynamical stability. Their HSE06+SOC gaps of 2.148-2.919 eV exceeded the original 1.0-2.0 eV window, underscoring the need for multi-fidelity validation. Overall, the workflow provides a reproducible and well-defined strategy for prioritizing and validating double perovskites.

Title: Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Ventilation Rates and Outcomes.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Evaluate the association between cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) ventilation rates and survival to hospital discharge, and identify novel ventilation targets.
DESIGN: Multicenter prospective ancillary observational cohort study of the ICU-RESUS trial (NCT02837497).
SETTING: A total of 18 ICUs from 10 U.S. clinical sites from October 2016 to March 2021.
PATIENTS: Hospitalized children (≤ 18 yr) with endotracheal or tracheostomy tubes and evaluable intra-arrest end-tidal carbon dioxide data to calculate ventilation rate.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 234 included events, 86 events (36.8%) had guideline-recommended (20-30 beats per min [bpm]) average ventilation rates during CPR. The association between guideline-recommended CPR ventilation rate and survival to hospital discharge was evaluated with Poisson regression using generalized estimating equations, controlling for a priori covariables (initial pulse status, immediate cause of arrest). We found no association between guideline-recommended ventilation rates and survival to hospital discharge (adjusted relative risk [aRR], 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.21; p = 0.68). In exploratory analyses, novel age-stratified ventilation rates were identified using natural cubic splines and subsequently evaluated in multivariable models. We identified potential thresholds (< 8 yr, ≥ 26 bpm; ≥ 8 yr, < 26 bpm). For children younger than 8 years, average CPR ventilation rate greater than or equal to 26 bpm was associated with improved survival to hospital discharge compared with less than 26 bpm (aRR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.00-1.73; p = 0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: CPR ventilation rates in the currently recommended range (20-30 bpm) were not associated with survival in children with in-hospital cardiac arrest. In exploratory analyses in children younger than 8 years, higher ventilation rates (≥ 26 bpm) were associated with improved survival and warrant confirmation in future studies.

Title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention.
RESULTS: Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

Title: Association of Iron Homeostasis With One-Year All-Cause Mortality Among Intensive Care Unit Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Retrospective Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perturbations in iron homeostasis can substantially affect cardiovascular outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the prognostic value of various iron homeostasis indicators for all-cause mortality in critically ill AF patients.
METHOD: Data for this retrospective study were obtained from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. Based on the iron homeostasis-related indicators (ferritin, serum iron, transferrin, and total iron-binding capacity [TIBC]), the risks of 1-year mortality among critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation were calculated using Cox proportional-hazards regression. Associations of iron homeostasis indicators with all-cause mortality in critically ill AF patients were assessed via Kaplan-Meier curves, restricted cubic splines, and subgroup analyses.
RESULTS: After multivariable adjustment, patients in the highest ferritin quartile had a greater risk of 1-year mortality than those in the lowest quartile (Q4 HR 1.277, 95% CI 1.083-1.506, p < 0.01). In contrast, the highest quartiles of transferrin (Q4 HR 0.732, 95% CI 0.622-0.861, p < 0.01) and TIBC (Q4 HR 0.732, 95% CI 0.622-0.861, p < 0.01) were associated with lower mortality. No significant association was observed between serum iron quartiles and 1-year mortality (Q4 HR 1.067, 95% CI 0.914-1.245, p = 0.41). Restricted cubic spline analyses further characterized the exposure and outcome patterns for these iron-related parameters.
CONCLUSION: Among critically ill patients with AF, ferritin, transferrin and TIBC levels were independently associated with 1-year all-cause mortality. No significant association was observed for serum iron.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) and long-term revascularization burden: a recurrent-event analysis of the UK Biobank.
Abstract:
AIMS: To investigate whether elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with cumulative coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization burden in a primary prevention cohort.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 237 729 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry free of ASCVD at baseline, followed for a median of 14.1 years. Lp(a) was analysed using the ESC/EAS 2025 threshold of 105 nmol/L and continuously (per 50 nmol/L increment). The primary outcome was the total number of coronary, peripheral, and carotid revascularization procedures per person. Given the genetically determined, lifelong nature of Lp(a) exposure, to capture the full sequence of procedures over time, rather than time-to-first-event alone, we applied recurrent-event statistical models, including the Andersen-Gill model, negative binomial regression, and the Prentice-Williams-Peterson gap-time model. Overall, 10 731 revascularization procedures occurred in 237 729 participants. The proportion undergoing ≥1 procedure was higher with Lp(a) ≥ 105 vs. <105 nmol/L (4.36% vs. 2.96%), with larger differences for ≥2 (1.53% vs. 0.95%) and ≥3 procedures (0.36% vs. 0.18%). In Andersen-Gill analysis, Lp(a) ≥ 105 nmol/L was associated with a higher revascularization rate (HR 1.50, 1.42-1.60), with a 55% higher rate of revascularization procedures during follow-up by negative binomial regression (IRR 1.55, 1.45-1.65). The association was strongest for the first procedure (HR 1.48, 1.40-1.56), attenuated for the second (HR 1.28, 1.09-1.50), and non-significant for the third (HR 1.23, 0.94-1.62). Findings were consistent across coronary and peripheral territories.
CONCLUSION: In this large primary prevention cohort, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with a higher long-term revascularization burden across multiple vascular territories. The association was robust for coronary, supportive for peripheral, and inconclusive for carotid revascularization owing to limited statistical power. These findings, derived from recurrent-event methodology, provide a more complete quantification of Lp(a)-associated cardiovascular procedural risk than time-to-first-event analyses alone.

Title: Repositioning Vericiguat after VICTOR: Towards a Risk- and Timing-Based Framework in Contemporary HFrEF.
Abstract: Vericiguat, an oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, provides a mechanistically distinct approach to reducing residual risk in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The VICTORIA trial demonstrated a reduction in cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation among patients with recent worsening heart failure, whereas vericiguat did not significantly reduce the primary endpoint in the subsequent VICTOR trial in a more stable HFrEF population. Nevertheless, the prespecified pooled analysis of VICTORIA and VICTOR showed a significant reduction in cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalisation across the combined HFrEF population, without significant heterogeneity between the trials. Together, these findings shift the focus from efficacy alone to clinical prioritisation according to baseline risk and timing, while recognising that validated treatment-selection criteria and an optimal timing strategy remain undefined. Contemporary observational studies have identified associations between blood pressure, disease severity, prior heart failure hospitalisation, and clinical or biomarker outcomes during vericiguat treatment; however, these characteristics have not been validated as predictors of vericiguat-specific treatment benefit. This review integrates evidence from VICTORIA, VICTOR, pooled analyses, and contemporary real-world studies and proposes a hypothesis-generating, risk- and timing-based framework for vericiguat use. Clinically meaningful worsening heart failure may represent a period of increased absolute risk in which consideration of vericiguat may be particularly relevant after clinical stabilisation, but neither an optimal therapeutic window nor a validated responder phenotype has been established. Prospective studies specifically evaluating treatment-by-risk and treatment-by-timing interactions are required to validate this framework.

Title: Neoadjuvant Treatment of BRAFV600E Papillary Craniopharyngiomas: A Case Series.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Craniopharyngiomas are locally invasive and frequently recurrent tumors of the sellar/suprasellar region. Historically, the mainstay of treatment has been surgical resection. The papillary type of craniopharyngiomas (PCP) frequently harbors a BRAFV600E mutation, rendering them amenable to targeted therapies. We present our institution's initial experience of using a minimally invasive endoscopic transventricular approach for biopsy, followed by neoadjuvant targeted BRAF/MEK inhibition.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 5 cases of patients with BRAFV600E-mutated PCP diagnosed by endoscopic transventricular biopsy between July 2018 and August 2023, who then received BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy. Patient characteristics, symptoms, tumor volumes, and treatment outcomes were collected from the electronic medical record. Tumor volumes were collected from radiology reports.
RESULTS: All 5 patients underwent endoscopic transventricular biopsy of a third ventricular tumor. The mean tumor volume postbiopsy was 23.8 ± 19.1 cm3 (range, 11.5-57.3 cm3). After confirmation of BRAFV600E mutation by biopsy, all patients received at least 1 cycle of BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy (median, 5 cycles; range, 1-16 cycles). Two patients elected to undergo radiation treatment after 5 cycles of therapy. No patients experienced decline in endocrine function; notably, none of them developed arginine-vasopressin deficiency. Two patients with abnormal visual findings at baseline experienced improvement after treatment. At the last follow-up (mean, 5.1 ± 2.3 years after treatment initiation; range, 2.1-7.8 years), the mean tumor volume was 0.5 ± 0.4 cm3 (range, 0.07-1.2 cm3), corresponding to a mean reduction of 97.8% ± 1.2% (range, 96.2%-99.6%).
CONCLUSION: When anatomically feasible, endoscopic transventricular biopsy appears to be a safe method for confirming BRAFV600E-mutated PCP. In our cohort, neoadjuvant BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy after biopsy resulted in substantial, durable tumor shrinkage, visual improvement, and endocrine stability, without permanent treatment-related morbidity or need for more surgical management. The long-term follow-up reported here supports this novel, minimally invasive management pathway for BRAFV600E-mutated PCP.

Title: Impact of Methamphetamine Use on Injury Characteristics and Postoperative Outcomes in Upper Extremity Fractures.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methamphetamine use in orthopedic trauma carries an indeterminate risk, with prior studies suggesting increased rates of deep vein thrombosis and elevated mortality. Upper extremity fractures (UEFs) have distinct mechanisms of injury and operative risk. This study evaluates outcomes following operative management of UEFs in patients with and without documented methamphetamine use.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective chart review was conducted of adults undergoing surgical fixation of UEFs (distal radius/ulna to clavicle; phalangeal, metacarpal, and carpal fractures were excluded) from January 2022 to March 2025. Outcomes included urinary tract infection, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, myocardial infarction, pneumonia, emergency department (ED) visits, readmission, surgical site infection, hardware removal, and mortality. A post hoc subgroup analysis of isolated UEFs was performed.
RESULTS: There were 426 patients meeting study criteria: 40 with methamphetamine use, and 386 without. Methamphetamine users were more likely to experience polytrauma (27.5% vs 10.9%, P = .003), higher-energy injuries (75.0% vs 53.6%, P = .003), interpersonal violence, such as altercations (22.5% vs 5.7%, P < .001), and ED visits within 30 days (20.0% vs 9.1%, P = .047). No other estimable postoperative outcome differed significantly. For isolated UEFs, methamphetamine users had shorter follow-up (85.9 vs 116.3 days, P = .022).
CONCLUSION: Methamphetamine use was associated with higher-energy injury mechanisms and increased health care use, namely ED visits. No other estimable perioperative complication differed significantly, and no deaths occurred. Operative management should not be withheld solely because of methamphetamine use; targeted case management may reduce postoperative use.

Title: Cross-sectional Comparison of the PREVENT and Pooled Cohort Equations for 10-Year Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Risk Estimates in a U.S. Cohort of Black and Latina Transgender Women with HIV.
Journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transgender women with HIV face higher rates of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) than the general population. However, ASCVD risk estimators use binary sex variables that may misclassify their risk. We examined the effects of sex variable inputs in the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) and Pooled Cohort Equation (PCE) risk calculations and tested for associations of ASCVD risk scores with HIV and hormone use.
SETTING: Participants were recruited from health centers in Boston, New York, and Washington, DC.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional comparison of PCE and PREVENT scores by sex variable inputs using data from 108 Black and Latina transgender women with HIV. Logistic regression models tested whether hormone duration and time since HIV diagnosis were associated with hyperlipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or cardiac events.
RESULTS: Using an illustrative ≥ 5% risk score as the threshold for statin initiation, 40.6% with PCE versus 9.5% with PREVENT met or exceeded 5% risk when male was entered for all, compared with 17.7% with PCE versus 9.5% with PREVENT when female was entered for all, and 24.0% with PCE versus 8.4% with PREVENT when female was entered for participants taking hormones. Neither years since HIV diagnosis nor hormone duration were associated with ASCVD risk factors or events.
CONCLUSION: Use of the PREVENT calculator generates lower ASCVD risk estimates than PCE in transgender women with HIV. Research is needed to determine how best to incorporate gender diversity and intersecting factors into ASCVD risk calculations.

Title: Restoration of frequency-dependent myocardial reserve after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis: an invasive hemodynamic study.
Journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
Abstract: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic pressure overload may impair frequency-dependent myocardial reserve despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). We investigated whether acute afterload reduction with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) restores force-frequency relationships (FFR) and relaxation frequency relationships (RFR). In this prospective study, patients with severe normal-flow, high-gradient AS and preserved LVEF underwent invasive left ventricular pressure recording during incremental atrial pacing at 80 and 100 beats/min before and immediately after TAVI. Systolic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmax and preload-adjusted indices [dP/dtmax/left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) and left ventricular peak systolic pressure (LVSP)/LVEDP], whereas lusitropic reserve was assessed using dP/dtmin, the relaxation constant τ, and LVEDP. Echocardiography was performed at baseline and 3 mo. Forty-six patients completed the pacing protocol. Before TAVI, pacing produced only a modest increase in dP/dtmax (Δ + 150 mmHg/s; P = 0.004), without improvement in dP/dtmin (P = 0.329) or τ (P = 0.182). Immediately after TAVI, pacing increased dP/dtmax (P < 0.001), dP/dtmax/LVEDP (P = 0.004), and LVSP/LVEDP (P = 0.031), while improving dP/dtmin (Δ + 56 mmHg/s; P = 0.050) and τ (P = 0.033) and reducing LVEDP (P = 0.017). Correlation analyses supported the emergence of physiological FFR and RFR after valve implantation. At 3 mo, echocardiography showed lower pulmonary artery systolic pressure (P = 0.002), improved left atrial reservoir strain, and lower diastolic dysfunction grade (P = 0.006). Thus, acute afterload relief with TAVI reveals preserved dynamic systolic and lusitropic reserve in severe AS, with subsequent group-level improvement in diastolic function.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study provides direct invasive human evidence that frequency-dependent myocardial reserve is acutely restored after TAVI in severe aortic stenosis. Controlled atrial pacing revealed blunted force-frequency and relaxation-frequency responses before valve replacement, despite preserved ejection fraction, with rapid recovery after afterload relief. These findings show that impaired myocardial reserve in pressure-overload remodeling is functionally reversible and tightly linked to loading conditions.

Title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care.
OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.
RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.
CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).
Publication Types: Clinical Trial, Phase II; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Venous Thromboembolism and Associated Indicators for Catheter-Related Thrombosis Subtypes.
Abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a severe and life-threatening complication in hospitalized patients, and central venous catheter (CVC) insertion significantly increases the risk of catheter-related thrombosis (CRT). Epidemiological profiles of hospitalized patients with confirmed VTE are characterized; indicators correlated with CRT subtype are identified; the discriminative performance of circulating biomarkers is evaluated; and VTE recurrence metrics are contrasted between cohorts with and without CVC placement. A single-center retrospective case-case comparative analysis is conducted on 862 patients with imaging-confirmed VTE. Analytical methodologies incorporate univariate and multivariate logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve testing. The in-hospital VTE incidence was 2.1%, concentrated in elderly, malignancy, and postoperative patients. CRT incidence was 10.2%, highest with peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC). Five clinical indicators correlated with CRT subtype were identified: prolonged catheter indwelling, catheter malposition, elevated D-dimer levels, malignant tumor history, and prior VTE events. The combination of D-dimer and catheter indwelling time exhibited robust discriminative power (AUC = 0.82) for differentiating CRT from non-CRT VTE among patients with confirmed VTE. The 6-month VTE recurrence rate was 28.4% in the CVC group and 9.7% in the non-CVC group. These observational findings yield only tentative clinical hypotheses aimed at distinguishing thrombotic subtypes among VTE patients. Further multicenter prospective research is necessary to validate these indicators and develop mature, standardized prevention protocols for broad clinical application.

Title: Epidemiology of uncontrolled and treatment‑resistant hypertension: a registry‑based observational study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to describe blood pressure control rates and prevalence of treatment resistant hypertension among diagnosed individuals.
METHODS: Randomly selected adults who had at least one primary or secondary healthcare visit and who were registered residents of Stockholm County, Sweden, on December 31st, 2019, were included. Blood pressure control in diagnosed individuals was assessed using two targets: <140/90 mmHg and <130/80 mmHg. The prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension defined by three commonly used criteria was calculated and its association with clinical characteristics, drug treatment patterns, and comorbidities were assessed.
RESULTS: By the end of 2019, among those with a hypertension diagnosis, 57% (<140/90 mmHg) or 19% (<130/80 mmHg) had controlled blood pressure depending on the threshold used. The point prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension ranged from <1% to 17% depending on definition and was associated with older age, higher body mass index, and multiple comorbidities including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.
CONCLUSION: Blood pressure control remains a major clinical challenge, with fewer than one in five patients with a hypertension diagnosis achieving <130/80 mmHg. The prevalence of treatment-resistant hypertension varied widely depending on the definition used and was closely associated with a greater burden of comorbidities, indicating an unmet need for improved strategies for this clinically challenging subgroup.

Title: Therapeutic Potential of Flavonoids and Their Metabolites in Hyperlipidaemia: Molecular Mechanisms, Bioavailability and Clinical Perspectives.
Abstract: Hyperlipidaemia is a major modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and remains a global health concern. Although conventional lipid-lowering drugs are effective, their long-term use is often associated with adverse effects, prompting interest in safer dietary alternatives. Flavonoids, such as quercetin, naringenin, and catechins, have gained attention for their hypolipidemic and cardioprotective properties. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on the therapeutic potential of quercetin, catechins, naringenin, and their bioactive metabolites in the management of hyperlipidaemia. The literature was identified through comprehensive searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and March 2026 using combinations of the keywords flavonoids, quercetin, catechins, naringenin, metabolites, hyperlipidaemia, dyslipidaemia, lipid metabolism, cardiovascular disease, and gut microbiota. Original research articles, clinical studies, experimental investigations, and high-quality review articles published in English were considered, while duplicate, non-English, and unrelated reports were excluded from the study. Evidence indicates that flavonoids and their metabolites modulate multiple pathways involved in lipid homeostasis, including the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, activation of AMPK and PPARα, suppression of SREBP-1c, enhancement of LDL receptor expression, regulation of gut microbiota, and attenuation of oxidative stress and inflammation. Despite encouraging preclinical and clinical findings, limited bioavailability, extensive metabolism, inter-individual variability, and insufficient long-term clinical evidence remain important challenges. Overall, flavonoids and their metabolites represent promising adjunctive dietary strategies for improving lipid metabolism and reducing cardiovascular risk. However, welldesigned randomized clinical trials and advanced delivery systems are needed to establish their therapeutic efficacy and clinical applicability.

Title: Maintaining Quality of Genetic Counseling Services While Maximizing Efficiency: Protocol for the GC-PRO Intervention Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial.
Abstract: The rapid integration of genomic medicine into clinical care has created an unprecedented demand for genetic counseling (GC) services. Attempts to streamline care have involved integration of GC assistants, group counseling sessions, and development of educational technology supplements; meanwhile, improving the efficiency of the core clinical interaction itself remains understudied. This study will evaluate the GC-PRO Intervention, a targeted communication training for genetic counselors designed to optimize visit time by aligning counseling with patient-centered needs and removing processes that do not contribute to positive patient experiences. Using a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial design across clinical specialties (e.g., prenatal, cancer, cardiology, and general genetics) at two academic health centers, we will recruit approximately 20 genetic counselors and 994 patients. To ensure the intervention and study design are culturally responsive, we are utilizing a community-based participatory research approach with four multicultural community advisory boards. The intervention training focuses on three evidence-based communication skills: Tailoring (assessing and integrating patient needs and values), Streamlining (reducing time spent gathering patient medical and family history information), and Main Messaging (reducing lecturing through increasing conversational exchanges). The primary outcome is visit time, and secondary outcomes include patient-reported measures of empowerment, activation, trust, working alliance, patient-centered communication, and overall satisfaction. Data will be analyzed using linear and generalized mixed-effects models to compare the intervention to standard of care, accounting for calendar time, counselor nesting, and pre-specified patient characteristics to improve precision. We hypothesize that this intervention will significantly reduce average visit time while maintaining or improving session quality, as measured against pre-specified non-inferiority thresholds. With 80% power to detect a 5-min difference in session length, this study aims to provide a scalable framework for efficient GC services without sacrificing the counselor-patient relationship or patient-centered outcomes.

Title: The Mediating Role of Hypoalbuminemia in the Association Between Frailty and Poor Outcomes in Stroke Patients.
Abstract:
AIM: Frailty is associated with adverse stroke outcomes. This study aimed to examine whether hypoalbuminemia mediates this association.
DESIGN: A prospective cohort study.
METHODS: A total of 175 patients with stroke admitted to a tertiary hospital between March and November 2023 were included. Frailty was assessed within 24 h of admission using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) and categorised as frail (CFS ≥ 5) or non-frail (CFS ≤ 4). Demographic, clinical and biochemical data were collected. Hypoalbuminemia (serum albumin < 35 g/L) was determined based on the lowest serum albumin level during hospitalisation. Functional outcomes were evaluated using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at discharge, 30 days and 90 days after discharge, with scores ≤ 3 defined as good outcome and > 3 as poor outcome.
RESULTS: Among the 175 stroke patients included in the study, 52 (29.71%) were frail and 64 (36.57%) developed hypoalbuminemia during hospitalisation. The proportions of poor outcomes were 47.43% at discharge, 42.86% at 30 days and 37.14% at 90 days after discharge. After adjusting for confounding factors, frailty was significantly associated with the occurrence of hypoalbuminemia [relative risk (RR) = 1.61, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.08-2.40, p = 0.019]. Frailty was also significantly associated with poor outcomes at discharge (RR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.12-2.16, p = 0.008), at 30 days (RR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.41-2.89, p < 0.001) and at 90 days (RR = 2.79, 95% CI: 1.81-4.30, p < 0.001). Hypoalbuminemia was also independently associated with poor outcomes at all time points (all p < 0.05). Mediation analysis showed that hypoalbuminemia partially mediated the association between frailty and poor outcomes, with mediation proportions of 22.21%, 16.85% and 14.03% at discharge, 30 days and 90 days, respectively (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Hypoalbuminemia partly mediates the impact of frailty on poor outcomes in stroke patients. The findings suggest that nurses should place greater emphasis on frailty assessment and serum albumin monitoring in patients with stroke to facilitate the early identification of high-risk patients and to inform individualised nursing assessment and management.
REPORTING METHOD: The research findings are reported following the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) guidelines for observational studies.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

Title: Efficacy of Home-Based Telerehabilitation Versus Center-Based Cardiac Rehabilitation on Cardiopulmonary Function and Exercise Capacity in Patients After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL.
Journal: Journal of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation and prevention
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The objective is to compare the effects of a home-based telerehabilitation (HBTCR) program, traditional center-based cardiac rehabilitation (CBCR), and usual care on cardiopulmonary function and exercise capacity in patients after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 111 patients, 4 to 8 weeks after CABG surgery, were assigned to 12 weeks of HBTCR (n = 37), CBCR (n = 37), or to a control group (n = 37). The HBTCR group utilized wearable sensors and a mobile app for remote monitoring and coaching. The CBCR group underwent supervised on-site sessions. Primary outcomes were changes in peak oxygen uptake () and 6-minute walk distance. Secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction, psychological status, and quality of life.
RESULTS: Among 101 completers, both HBTCR and CBCR groups showed significant improvements in (HBTCR: +5.1; CBCR: +4.8 mL/kg/min) and 6-minute walk distance (HBTCR: +85.2 m; CBCR: +81.5 m) versus control (P < .001), with no difference between interventions. Significant improvements in left ventricular ejection fraction, psychological scores, and quality of life were also observed in both intervention groups compared with control (P < .05). Adherence was high (HBTCR: 92.1%; CBCR: 85.3%) with no major adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that an HBTCR program has similar efficacy as CBCR in improving cardiopulmonary function, exercise capacity, and patient-centered outcomes after CABG. An HBTCR program represents a viable, accessible alternative model for delivering comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation and secondary prevention.

Title: OneRF radiofrequency ablation system for the minimally invasive treatment of trigeminal neuralgia: initial clinical experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous radiofrequency ablation is an established treatment for medically refractory trigeminal neuralgia (TN). Conventional systems use a single active tip and often require repeated repositioning. A multi-contact radiofrequency platform may permit contact-level interrogation and lesioning along a single fixed trajectory.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective review of patients with medically refractory TN treated with a multi-contact thin-film radiofrequency probe. Demographics, operative details, Barrow Neurological Institute (BNI) pain scores, medication use, and complications were reviewed. Contact-level localization was performed intraoperatively, including low-temperature thermal interrogation, followed by definitive lesioning.
RESULTS: Fifteen patients (mean age 66.5 years; 12 women) underwent treatment. Most had classical or idiopathic TN, purely paroxysmal involving the V2-V3 distribution. Contact-level mapping was successfully achieved in all cases with definitive lesioning along a fixed trajectory. At mean follow-up of 6.0 months, all patients had a good outcome (BNI I-IIIB), and most had reduced or discontinued pain medications. No off-target lesioning was observed.
CONCLUSIONS: This early clinical series suggests that a multi-contact radiofrequency platform can facilitate contact-level mapping and lesioning of trigeminal distributions along a single trajectory without repeated probe repositioning. Initial pain outcomes were favorable, although larger cohorts and longer follow-up are needed to define durability and comparative effectiveness.

Title: Influencing factors analysis and prediction model development for ROSC in adult non-traumatic OHCA: a retrospective study based on pre-hospital emergency settings.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest is a major global public health problem. This study aimed to explore factors influencing return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and develop a prediction model for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.
METHODS: We retrospectively collected electronic medical records of adult non-traumatic OHCA patients at Tianjin Emergency Medical Center from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024. The primary outcome was sustained ROSC up to emergency department arrival and handover to receiving-hospital staff. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression with clinician ID as random intercept adjusted clustering bias; predictors with p < 0.05 formed the nomogram. Patients were randomly split 7:3 for training and internal testing. Discrimination was assessed by ROC-AUC (acceptable threshold >0.7). We performed 1000 bootstrap resampling to correct C-index against overfitting. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA) further evaluated predictive consistency and net clinical benefit.
RESULTS: Among 9,386 included cases, 678 (7.2%) achieved ROSC. Mixed-effects regression identified independent ROSC predictors: public location (aOR = 1.285, 95% CI:1.038-1.592), 06:00-12:00 onset (aOR = 1.308, 95% CI:1.018-1.682), prolonged emergency response time (aOR = 0.971, 95% CI:0.945-0.999), extended onset-to-ambulance intervals (5-10 min: aOR = 0.758;10-30 min: aOR = 0.578;>30 min:aOR = 0.498 vs ≤5 min), no OHCA occurred at emergency call (aOR = 1.540, 95% CI:1.048-2.262), male attending physicians (aOR = 1.255, 95% CI:1.077-1.464), longer physician practice years (aOR = 1.043, 95%CI: 1.022-1.065), intermediate physician title (aOR = 1.236, 95% CI:1.047-1.459), shockable initial rhythm (aOR = 2.850, 95% CI:2.390-3.397), endotracheal intubation (aOR = 2.294, 95% CI:1.936-2.718), epinephrine >5 mg (aOR = 0.765,95% CI:0.626-0.935). The nomogram AUC reached 0.775 (95% CI:0.756-0.794) in the training set and 0.775 (95% CI:0.745-0.805) in the test set; 1000 bootstrap internal validation gave an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.7679 with minimal optimism of 0.0071, showing negligible overfitting, good calibration and favorable net clinical benefit via DCA.
CONCLUSION: This study identified multiple factors significantly associated with ROSC in OHCA patients; the constructed model showed good predictive value.

Title: Burden of RSV hospital disease and its comorbidities in adults in Spain (2016-2023).
Abstract: This observational descriptive study analyses the hospital burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults in Spain using the Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS) from the Spanish National Hospital Data Surveillance System. Hospital admissions of adults diagnosed with non-bronchiolitis RSV infection between 2016 and 2023 were identified using ICD-10-CM codes. A total of 288,297 RSV-related hospitalizations were recorded, with a mean patient age of 76.18 years. The overall hospitalization rate was 92.43 per 100,000 inhabitants, and the mortality rate was 5.32 per 100,000. The most common severe comorbidities at admission were congestive heart failure, diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Patients aged over 65 years had a significantly higher risk of in-hospital mortality (OR 1.78; 95% CI: 1.64-1.93) compared to those aged 40-64 years, increasing to 2.22 (95% CI: 2.05-2.40) in the presence of at least one severe comorbidity. Male sex was also associated with increased mortality risk (OR 1.24; 95% CI: 1.20-1.28). In conclusion, RSV represents a substantial cause of hospitalization and mortality among adults in Spain, particularly in patients over 60 years, males, and those with underlying comorbidities.

Title: Study of Krüppel-like Factor 14 rs4731702 Polymorphism in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Journal: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Krüppel-Like Factor 14 (KLF14) polymorphism has been investigated as a potential genetic risk factor for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study aimed to evaluate the association between KLF14 rs4731702 (C/T) polymorphism and T2DM susceptibility in Egyptians.
METHODS: A case-control study was conducted on 100 patients with T2DM and 100 healthy controls. Genotyping of KLF14 rs4731702 (C/T) was performed using restriction fragment length polymorphism polymerase chain reaction (RFLP-PCR). Clinical and biochemical parameters were compared among different genotypes.
RESULTS: The CT and TT genotypes were significantly more frequent in diabetic patients (40% and 30%, respectively) than in controls (15% and 20%, respectively) (p<0.001). Subjects carrying CT and TT genotypes showed significantly higher fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, total cholesterol, and triglyceride levels than those carrying the CC genotype.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest a possible association between the T allele and metabolic abnormalities associated with T2DM.
CONCLUSION: KLF14 rs4731702 (C/T) polymorphism is significantly associated with susceptibility to T2DM in the Egyptian population. The increased prevalence of CT and TT genotypes, along with their association with hyperglycemia and dyslipidemia, suggests that the T allele may contribute to metabolic disturbances and disease development. Further large-scale studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify the underlying mechanisms.

Title: Disparities in Social Determinants of Health and Health Outcomes Among Autistic Individuals Without Intellectual Disability in Middle-to-Late Adulthood.
Journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
Abstract: Autism is increasingly recognized across the lifespan, yet little is known about how structural social disadvantage contributes to long-term health risks among autistic adults in middle and later adulthood. Participants were identified from the UK Biobank study, comprising 576 autistic adults with no intellectual disability and an average of 15.2 years of education, and 5,760 controls matched on age, sex, residing area, race, and educational attainment. Social determinants of health (SDH) were assessed using a composite score calculated from 12 indicators that characterized economic, health care, neighborhood, and social domains. Mediation analysis was performed to estimate the extent to which SDH disparities mediated the elevated mortality and chronic disease risks among autistic adults. The study sample was 66.4% male and had a mean age of 51.6 years (SD, 8.03). Autistic adults had worse SDH levels across almost all dimensions. These disparities mediated 39% of the elevated mortality risk. In addition, autistic adults showed increased incidence of cardiovascular disease, dementia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, depression, and anxiety, with SDH disparities mediating 17% to 38% of these elevated risks. These findings indicate that multifaceted disadvantage plays a substantial role in the health inequities experienced by autistic adults, underscoring the need for cross-sector interventions and policy reforms.Lay AbstractAutistic adults face persistent disadvantage in social conditions that shape health outcomes. These disadvantages may partially explain why autistic adults face higher rates of chronic illnesses and earlier death. From a large cohort in the United Kingdom, we compared 576 autistic adults with 5,760 adults without autism across 12 indicators of social determinants of health (SDH), covering economic, health care, neighborhood, and social domains. Autistic adults showed disadvantage across nearly all domains. These disparities mediated 39% of excess mortality and 17% to 38% of the increased risk for chronic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, dementia, type 2 diabetes, depression, and anxiety. Economic deprivation and social isolation showed relatively larger mediating effects. This study provides evidence that structural inequities in SDH substantially contribute to the long-term health trajectories of autistic adults. Addressing these inequities will require policies and interventions that move beyond individual-level supports to tackle systemic barriers in employment, health care access, housing, and community participation.

Title: Steatotic liver disease in autoimmune liver disease: Prevalence and clinical impact in a Southeast Asian cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is increasingly common in patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) and autoimmune hepatitis (AIH). We sought to determine the prevalence and clinical impact of SLD among Southeast Asian patients with PBC, AIH, and AIH/PBC overlap syndrome.
METHODS: We included all patients diagnosed with PBC, AIH and AIH/PBC overlap syndrome between 2000 and 2024. SLD was defined based on either radiological or histological evidence of hepatic steatosis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, treatment response, liver-related events (LRE), and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
RESULTS: Among 273 patients (PBC: 184, AIH: 69, AIH/PBC overlap syndrome: 20), one third had concomitant SLD. Patients with PBC/SLD were more likely to have a higher BMI (24.6 versus 22.6 kg/m2, p = 0.002) and less likely to have liver cirrhosis (36.7% versus 59.3%, p = 0.011) than PBC without SLD. AIH patients had a significantly higher risk of developing de novo SLD. Patients with PBC/SLD have a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (unadjusted HR 0.33, adjusted HR 0.18, p < 0.05 for both). Concomitant SLD did not influence the treatment response, occurrence of LRE, or MACE in patients with PBC, AIH, or AIH/PBC overlap syndrome.
CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant SLD does not influence treatment response, liver-related events, or cardiovascular outcomes in patients with autoimmune liver disease.

Title: Asperginase-based chemotherapy regimen for acute lymphoblastic leukemia: A cohort study with promising outcomes on adults.
Journal: Journal of research in medical sciences : the official journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a malignancy of lymphoid progenitor cells. Asparaginase-based regimens are highly effective in pediatric ALL, but concerns over toxicity have limited their use in adults. This study evaluates the incidence of adverse events following asparaginase treatment in the adult ALL population.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we assessed drug-related adverse events among 67 adults with ALL treated with either a hyper-central vascular access device (CVAD) (n = 34) or an asparaginase-containing regimen (n = 33). Those under asparaginase-containing treatment were evaluated solely and divided into two groups of pegylated asparaginase (PEG-asparaginase) (n = 21) and L-asparaginase (n = 12). We compared the incidence of hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, hyperglycemia, hypersensitivity, neurological disorders, and thrombotic events.
RESULTS: Age-adjusted analysis showed the risk of thrombosis was significantly higher in the asparaginase group compared to hyper-CVAD (odds ratio [OR] = 17.9, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.69-2512, P = 0.012). In contrast, risks of fungal infection (OR = 0.081, 95% CI: 0.0006-0.83, P = 0.032) and neutropenic fever (OR = 0.0006, 95% CI: 2.8e-17-0.010, P < 0.0001) were significantly lower. A sub-analysis revealed the elevated thrombosis risk was specific to PEG-asparaginase versus hyper-CVAD (OR = 47.05, 95% CI: 3.83-6905, P = 0.001), not L-asparaginase (P = 0.55). Neutropenic fever risk was lower for both L-asparaginase (OR = 0.0015, P < 0.0001) and PEG-asparaginase (OR = 0.0011, P < 0.0001).
CONCLUSION: Asparaginase use in adults with ALL was associated with fewer overall adverse events, specifically lower infection risks, compared to hyper-CVAD. However, it significantly increased the risk of thrombosis, an effect driven primarily by the PEG-asparaginase formulation. While L-asparaginase appeared more favorable, the small sample size limits generalizability. These findings indicate that asparaginase remains a viable option for adults, but requires vigilant monitoring and prophylaxis for thrombotic events.

Title: Phase Angle at Completion of Cardiac Rehabilitation Predicts Unplanned All-cause Readmission: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Phase angle (PhA) reflects cellular integrity and systemic physiological resilience. This study investigated whether PhA measured at the completion of late-recovery-phase cardiac rehabilitation (CR) predicts unplanned all-cause readmission in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD), comparing its predictive value with baseline PhA and exercise capacity.
METHODS: We analyzed 83 patients with CVD. PhA, peak oxygen uptake (peak V̇O2), and anaerobic threshold (AT) were assessed at both CR initiation and completion. The primary endpoint was unplanned all-cause readmission.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 615 days, 21 patients (25.3%) experienced unplanned all-cause readmission. Multivariable Cox analysis revealed that PhA at CR completion was a significant independent predictor of readmission [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) = 0.49, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.26-0.93, P = 0.03], whereas neither PhA at initiation (P = 0.08) nor the change in PhA (ΔPhA; P = 0.41) showed significant associations. Receiver operating characteristic analysis indicated that no statistically significant difference in the area under the curve (AUC) was observed between PhA (AUC = 0.69) and AT (AUC = 0.78, P = 0.14) or peak V̇O2 (AUC = 0.75, P = 0.27).
CONCLUSIONS: PhA measured at the completion of late-recovery-phase CR is an independent predictor of unplanned readmission, whereas baseline PhA and ΔPhA were not significantly associated with readmission risk. Assessing PhA at this transition point may provide useful information for risk stratification and individualized long-term management in patients with CVD.

Title: Cytochrome P450 2D6 Metabolizer Phenotype Is Associated With Metoprolol Pharmacodynamics But Not With Metoprolol Discontinuation: A Retrospective Cohort Study in the All of Us Research Program.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2024 Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) guideline assigns a high level of evidence to the association between cytochrome P450 2D6 (CYP2D6) metabolizer status and both metoprolol exposure and heart-rate response and recommends genotype-informed dosing for poor metabolizers. Whether this well-characterized pharmacodynamic effect translates into a patient-level tolerability consequence, differential discontinuation has not been established at population scale in a diverse cohort. The aims of this study were to estimate the association between CYP2D6 metabolizer phenotype and metoprolol discontinuation, and to test whether metabolizer status was associated with the intermediate pharmacodynamic phenotypes (attained heart rate, bradycardia, and attained dose) through which such an effect would plausibly act. Discontinuation is treated throughout as a composite behavioral and clinical endpoint and not as a direct measure of drug tolerability.
METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study that used whole-genome sequencing linked to electronic health records (EHRs) in the All of Us Research Program (Controlled Tier, Curated Data Repository v9). Adult metoprolol users who had a CYP2D6 diplotype call and at least two metoprolol dispensings were included, so that the target population is patients who continued beyond a first fill. CYP2D6 metabolizer phenotype (normal (NM, reference), intermediate (IM), poor (PM), and ultrarapid (UM)) was derived from Cyrius diplotype calls using the CPIC and Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group consensus activity-score system, and a collapsed reduced-metabolizer contrast (PM plus IM vs NM) was prespecified. The primary outcome, time to metoprolol discontinuation, was modeled with cause-specific Cox regression that treated death as a competing event and adjusted for age, sex, 10 genetic-ancestry principal components, indication, comorbidity, atrioventricular-nodal cotherapy, CYP2D6 inhibitor exposure, calendar year, and EHR density. The secondary pharmacodynamic outcomes were attained on-treatment heart rate, bradycardia, and attained maximum daily dose. Sensitivity analyses addressed the discontinuation definition, phenoconversion by CYP2D6 inhibitors, and heterogeneity across genetic-ancestry strata.
RESULTS: Among 44,485 metoprolol users (PM, 2,470 (5.6%); IM, 16,687 (37.5%); NM, 24,123 (54.2%); UM, 1,205 (2.7%)), 29,999 (67.4%) discontinued and 629 (1.4%) died during follow-up. Metabolizer phenotype was not associated with discontinuation (PM vs NM: cause-specific hazard ratio (HR), 1.04 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.99-1.09), P = 0.12; IM: 1.01 (0.99-1.03), P = 0.41; UM: 1.01 (0.94-1.08), P = 0.89). The reduced-metabolizer contrast was null (HR, 1.01 (0.99-1.04), P = 0.24). The PM estimate was stable across three discontinuation definitions producing event rates of 67% to 98% (HR range, 1.01-1.04). Reclassifying inhibitor-exposed NM and UM participants for phenoconversion did not change the result (effective reduced-metabolizer vs NM: HR, 1.00 (0.93-1.06), P = 0.91). In the same cohort, the attained heart rate decreased with metabolizing capacity in PM and IM and increased in UM, relative to NM (PM, -1.85 beats per minute (bpm) (-2.36 to -1.34), P < 0.001; IM, -0.84 bpm (-1.09 to -0.60), P < 0.001; UM, +0.79 bpm (0.07 to 1.51), P = 0.03); PM and IM had higher odds of bradycardia (PM, odds ratio (OR), 1.19 (1.05-1.36), P = 0.009; IM, 1.16 (1.09-1.23), P < 0.001); and IM reached a lower attained dose (-6.68 mg (-10.26 to -3.09), P < 0.001) and was less likely to reach target dose (OR, 0.91 (0.85-0.97), P = 0.006).
CONCLUSIONS: CYP2D6 metabolizer status produced the expected graded effect on metoprolol pharmacodynamics but was not associated with metoprolol discontinuation in this real-world cohort. The biological basis for pre-emptive CYP2D6-guided metoprolol dosing is supported at the level of measured physiology, yet the downstream behavioral endpoint of continuation appears to be determined by factors that outweigh the genetic signal. Because discontinuation is a composite behavioral and clinical endpoint rather than a direct measure of tolerability, these data do not exclude a genotype effect on adverse drug effects that were not directly ascertained, including symptomatic bradycardia, fatigue, dizziness, and hypotension.

Title: Evaluation of different artificial intelligence-based coronary artery calcium scoring algorithms in nongated chest computed tomography.
Journal: Journal of research in medical sciences : the official journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the accuracy of coronary artery calcium scores (CACSs) automatically measured by two artificial intelligence (AI) systems on nonelectrocardiogram (ECG)-gated chest computed tomography (CT) and to investigate the relationship between CACS and the degree of coronary artery stenosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on 182 patients who underwent both ECG-gated Coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) and non-ECG-gated chest CT. Images from all patients were processed using postprocessing software and two AI systems (Software A/B). The manually measured CACS by experienced physicians using ECG-gated Coronary CTA was used as the gold standard. The agreement between two AI systems and the gold standard was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. In addition, Spearman's correlation analysis was performed to evaluate the relationship between CACS and the degree of coronary artery stenosis.
RESULTS: Both AI systems demonstrated high ICCs for CACS measurement (0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.871-0.926 for Software A; 0.96, 95% CI: 0.943-0.968 for Software B). The mean differences (95% limits of agreement) were 23.59 ± 442.35 for Software A and -80.35 ± 292.99 for Software B. Both systems showed good agreement in CACS measurement, with Software B exhibiting higher accuracy than Software A. Spearman's correlation analysis revealed weak-to-moderate positive correlations between CACS measured by different methods and the degree of coronary artery stenosis (r = 0.151-0.560, P < 0.05) across all coronary branches.
CONCLUSION: The two AI-based CACS systems, when applied to nongated chest CT, demonstrated consistency with manually measured CACS from ECG-gated coronary CTA. Software B showed superior accuracy compared to Software A. The correlation between CACS and the degree of vascular stenosis is influenced by vascular remodeling patterns, with positive remodeling reducing its consistency. Therefore, a comprehensive assessment of vascular stenosis should integrate vascular remodeling patterns and other diagnostic indicators.

Title: Bone Morphogenetic Protein-10 as a Predictor of Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biomarkers of atrial cardiomyopathy may improve the prediction of recurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) after catheter ablation. Bone morphogenetic protein-10 (BMP10) is an atrial-specific cardiomyocyte protein and a potential biomarker, but evidence is limited and not comprehensively synthesized.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies to evaluate the association between circulating BMP10 concentrations with AF recurrence after catheter ablation. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were computed using a random-effects model. The primary analysis used unadjusted HRs per continuous BMP10 levels from all included studies. Secondary analyses were conducted based on the adjusted HRs of studies with continuous BMP10 and all studies, including one study that reported adjusted HRs based on quartiles.
RESULTS: Three studies were included. In the primary analysis without adjustment (n = 3), increased levels of BMP10 were significantly associated with recurrence of AF (pooled HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.13-2.07; P = 0.006), with moderate-to-high heterogeneity (I2 = 69%). The association was attenuated and non-significant in the adjusted analysis of two studies with continuous BMP10 (HR 1.46, 95% CI 0.94-2.25; I2 = 59%). However, after the inclusion of a third study with adjusted quartile-based HR, the statistical significance was re-demonstrated (HR 1.33, 95% CI 1.16-1.53; P < 0.001) with low heterogeneity (I2 = 20%).
CONCLUSION: Elevated BMP10 levels are correlated with higher risk of AF recurrence following catheter ablation. Although the results are consistent across analyses, they should be interpreted with caution due to the small number of studies and methodological heterogeneity. BMP10 needs to be confirmed as a clinically applicable biomarker by larger prospective studies.

Title: Early-term and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion of high-risk subacute and early chronic residual dissection after type A repair.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Late mortality, progressive aneurysmal degeneration, and major reinterventions remain frequent after repair of type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to evaluate early- and midterm outcomes of endovascular completion in patients with high-risk residual dissection treated during the subacute or early chronic phase.
METHODS: This study was a single-center retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained institutional database. All consecutive patients undergoing endovascular completion for high-risk residual aortic dissection after type A dissection repair between January 2017 and September 2025 were included. Completion was performed using thoracic endovascular aortic repair alone or combined with the stented-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination technique when distal extension exceeded Ishimaru zone 5. Primary outcomes were 30-day mortality and morbidity, as well as 3- and 5-year survival and reintervention rates.
RESULTS: Among 127 patients surviving initial type A repair, 48 (37.8%) underwent endovascular completion (subacute n = 33; early chronic n = 15). No 30-day deaths occurred, and technical success was achieved in all cases. Major adverse events occurred in 6.2%, with no spinal cord ischemia. Five patients (10.4%) required early reintervention. Median clinical follow-up was 54 months. Estimated survival was 97.9% at 3 years and 90.3% at 5 years. Freedom from major reintervention was 93.5% at 3 years and 89.1% at 5 years. False lumen thrombosis was achieved in 89.6% of thoracic and 81.4% of visceral segments.
CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular completion of high-risk residual dissection after type A repair is safe and effective, providing excellent midterm survival, low major reintervention rates, and high rates of aortic remodeling.

Title: Antithrombotic Therapy Use in Children With Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract: The role of antithrombotic therapy in pulmonary hypertension (PH) remains uncertain, with conflicting adult data and limited pediatric evidence. This study aimed to describe real-world antithrombotic use in pediatric PH utilizing Pediatric Pulmonary Hypertension Network (PPHNet) registry data and a survey of PPHNet centers. We analyzed data of 1,716 patients from the PPHNet registry (2014-2024), comparing characteristics of those who received aspirin or warfarin with those who did not. A survey on real-world antithrombotic use was also distributed to 12 North American PPHNet centers in 2023. Eighteen percent of subjects received aspirin and 7% received warfarin. Patients who received aspirin or warfarin were more likely to have idiopathic/heritable PH. Aspirin or warfarin-treated patients demonstrated higher-risk features as evidenced by use of PH-targeted triple therapy (aspirin vs. no aspirin: 22% vs. 9%, p < 0.01; warfarin vs. no warfarin: 31% vs. 10%; p < 0.01) and higher mortality over a median follow-up of 3.2 years (aspirin vs. no aspirin: 14% vs. 9%, p = 0.008; warfarin vs. no warfarin: 19% vs. 9%, p = 0.001). Center-specific aspirin and warfarin use varied widely. Survey data demonstrated general agreement that antithrombotic therapy was not indicated for patients at lowest risk and probably indicated for patients at highest risk, but management of intermediate-risk patients varied considerably. Antithrombotic therapy is used infrequently in pediatric PH and primarily reserved for high-risk patients, with significant variation across centers. These findings highlight the need for further research to define which patients may benefit and guide evidence-based practice.

Title: Effects of different exercise types on visceral adipose tissue and glycemic parameters in adults with stage 1 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, particularly at stage 1, is increasingly prevalent worldwide. Although exercise interventions are recognized as effective in reducing visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and improving glucose metabolism, their effects in adults with stage 1 CKM syndrome remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically analyze the effects of different exercise types on VAT, fasting blood glucose (FBG), and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) in adults with stage 1 CKM syndrome.
METHODS: We searched six bibliographic databases-China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), WanFang Database, VIP Database, Web of Science, Embase, and PubMed-from inception to 15 April 2026, using the PICOS framework. A frequentist random-effects Network Meta-Analyses was conducted using STATA 18.0 software to evaluate the effects of interventions on VAT, FBG and HbA1c. The effectiveness of various exercise intervention types was ranked by calculating the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), and the risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB 2.0) tool. This study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261304633).
RESULTS: Thirty-seven randomized controlled trials involving 3483 participants were included. Compared with the control group, aerobic training significantly decreased VAT [standardized mean difference = -0.44, 95% confidence interval (CI): (-0.62, -0.26)], while mind-body exercise (MBE) significantly improved FBG [mean difference (MD) = -1.16 mmol/L, 95% CI: (-1.57, -0.75)] and HbA1c [MD = -0.35%, 95% CI: (-0.62, -0.07)]. Subgroup analysis revealed that high-intensity interval training with an intervention duration of ≤ 12 weeks (SUCRA = 67%) and aerobic training with a duration of >12 weeks (SUCRA = 94.9%) had the highest probability of being the most effective intervention for reducing VAT in included studies. In addition, mind-body exercise ranked highest for FBG improvement, though with limited certainty.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide evidence that different exercise types exert distinct benefits on metabolic health in adults with stage 1 CKM syndrome. In particular, aerobic training may be more effective than other exercise types in reducing VAT, while MBE may contribute to more benefits in improving FBG and HbA1c.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261304633, Identifier CRD420261304633.

Title: Azilsartan ameliorates angiotensin II-induced skeletal muscle atrophy via AT1R-mediated PI3K/AKT/FOXO3a signaling pathway.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a progressive age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by the loss of muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. Increasing evidence suggests that activation of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) contributes to muscle wasting through promotion of protein degradation and impairment of anabolic signaling. Azilsartan (AZL), a highly selective angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) blocker, has demonstrated pleiotropic effects beyond blood pressure control. However, its effects on skeletal muscle atrophy and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: We combined a prospective observational study with mechanistic investigations in animal and cellular models. Older adults with hypertension and sarcopenia received AZL (40 mg/day) or other antihypertensive therapies for 6 months, and muscle strength, gait speed, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass were assessed. Moreover, Ang II-induced skeletal muscle atrophy models were established in mice and C2C12 myotubes to evaluate the effects of AZL on muscle morphology and signaling pathways.
RESULTS: AZL treatment was associated with significant improvements in handgrip strength, gait speed, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass in older hypertensive patients. In experimental models, Ang II induced skeletal muscle dysfunction and atrophy, characterized by reduced exercise capacity, decreased grip strength, and muscle fiber loss, were attenuated by AZL treatment. Mechanistically, AZL restored PI3K/Akt/FOXO3a signaling and suppressed the expression of the muscle-specific ubiquitin ligases Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. The protective effects of AZL were abolished by the AT1R agonist TRV120027 in both in vivo and in vitro models and were further attenuated by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 in C2C12 myotubes.
CONCLUSIONS: AZL attenuates Ang II-induced skeletal muscle atrophy through AT1R blockade and subsequent activation of PI3K/Akt/FOXO3a signaling, thereby suppressing ubiquitin-proteasome system-mediated muscle protein degradation. These findings provide mechanistic and translational evidence supporting the potential of AZL as a therapeutic strategy for preserving skeletal muscle health in older adults with hypertension.

Title: Intensive titration for elderly patients with heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) relies on quadruple therapy, including beta-blockers (BB), angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNi), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA), and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i). Elderly patients with HF represent a high-risk population and often face therapeutic inertia but also more adverse events.
