We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of an intensive titration program (ITP) for elderly HFrEF patients.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-center, observational study including HFrEF patients aged ≥ 75 years managed with an ITP between January 2024 and February 2025. The primary outcome was the prescription rate of quadruple GDMT at 3 months, irrespective of dose. Secondary outcomes included prescription of quadruple therapy at ≥ 50% of GDMT target doses and identification of predictors of limited implementation. Safety outcomes included adverse events occurring during titration and within 3 months after completion.
RESULTS: Sixty-four patients were included (Median age 80 years, 70% male, 28% diabetes, median eGFR 50 mL/min). The mean titration period was 100 days (14 weeks). At 3 months, 33% of patients were prescribed quadruple therapy, with 5% achieving ≥ 50% of the recommended target dose in each drug class. Target dose achievement improved across all drug classes between baseline and 3 months: ARNi (1% vs. 31%), MRA (1% vs. 14%), and BB (3% vs. 5%) (all P <0.05). These improvements were associated with short-term clinical and biological benefits (NT-proBNP reduction, improved left ventricular ejection fraction). Reported adverse events included symptomatic hypotension (8% with treatment discontinuation) and acute kidney injury (8 % requiring hospitalization). Older age and chronic kidney disease were associated with limited initiation of quadruple therapy.
CONCLUSION: An intensive titration program for HFrEF therapy appears feasible and relatively safe in elderly patients.

Title: Early postoperative galectin-3 for risk stratification of delayed graft function after kidney transplantation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed graft function (DGF) is a major early complication after kidney transplantation. Galectin-3 (Gal3), a mediator of inflammation and fibrosis, is associated with renal injury, but its role in predicting DGF remains unclear. This study evaluated whether early postoperative Gal3 levels predict DGF and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult kidney transplant recipients from deceased donors (January 2021-December 2022). Gal3 was measured preoperatively, at intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and at ICU discharge. The primary outcome was DGF, defined as renal replacement therapy within 7 days. A base clinical model (age, cold ischemia time, creatinine at ICU admission) was compared with a Gal3-extended model, assessed by area under the curve (AUC), Brier score, calibration, bootstrap optimism correction, and categorical net reclassification improvement.
RESULTS: Among 182 patients, 35 (19.2%) developed DGF. Gal3 at ICU admission was significantly higher in DGF patients (52.3 vs. 40.0 ng/ml, P < .001) and was independently associated with DGF (odds ratio per 5-ng/ml increase: 1.19; 95% confidence interval: 1.05-1.35; P = .008). Adding Gal3 modestly improved the AUC from 0.705 to 0.744 and the Brier score from 0.144 to 0.139. The Gal3-extended model retained superior discrimination after bootstrap correction. An exploratory prediction score demonstrated increasing DGF risk across score categories.
CONCLUSION: Gal3 measured at ICU admission was independently associated with DGF and provided modest incremental risk-stratification value. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Prognostic Significance of Serum Sodium in Patients With Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyponatremia has been associated with adverse outcomes in several cardiovascular diseases; however, its independent prognostic value in patients with acute pulmonary embolism (APE) remains uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of 105 hospitalized patients with confirmed APE between January 2020 and June 2025. Baseline clinical characteristics were compared between 1-year survivors and non-survivors. Serum sodium levels at the time of APE diagnosis were assessed, and hyponatremia was defined as a serum sodium level < 135 mmol/L. Univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to evaluate the association of serum sodium and other potential prognostic factors with 1-year mortality.
RESULTS: Among 105 hospitalized patients with confirmed APE, 41 (39.0%) died within 1 year. Non-survivors had a higher prevalence of active cancer (61.0% vs. 15.6%, P < 0.001) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (21.9% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.001), lower systolic blood pressure (108.9 ± 25.9 vs. 130.8 ± 21.6 mm Hg, P<0.001), and higher Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (PESI) scores (157.3 ± 56.0 vs. 91.0 ± 32.7, P < 0.001) than survivors. Serum sodium at diagnosis was significantly lower in non-survivors than in survivors (130.6 ± 5.9 vs. 136.4 ± 4.4 mmol/L, P < 0.001), and hyponatremia was more frequent among non-survivors (78.1% vs. 35.9%, P < 0.001). In univariable Cox regression, hyponatremia was associated with increased 1-year mortality (univariable hazard ratio (uHR), 4.20; 95% confidence interval (CI), 2.00-8.81; P < 0.001). After adjustment for disease severity and relevant clinical risk factors, serum sodium at diagnosis remained independently associated with 1-year mortality (multivariable hazard ratio (mHR) per 1-mmol/L increase, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.86-0.99; P = 0.043).
CONCLUSIONS: Lower serum sodium at diagnosis was independently associated with increased 1-year mortality in hospitalized patients with APE. Hyponatremia may represent a simple and readily available prognostic marker for early risk stratification in APE. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Title: Higher Risk of Loss to Follow-up Among Transgender People With HIV in Italy: Findings From the ICONA Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Official data on transgender people with human immunodeficiency virus (PWH) in Italy are lacking because gender identity is not recorded in national reports. We aimed to characterize transgender PWH in Italy and assess retention in care and clinical outcomes.
METHODS: We included PWH enrolled between 2010 and 2023 in 40 Italian Cohort Naive Antiretrovirals centers where gender identity could be reliably ascertained. Transgender PWH were compared with cisgender participants. Univariable and multivariable regression models assessed the association between gender identity and (1) loss to follow-up (LTFU; no visit or exam for ≥18 months) using Fine-Gray models and (2) a composite clinical endpoint including mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, cancer, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome-defining events, and end-stage kidney and liver disease using Cox models. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to individuals who initiated antiretroviral therapy (ART) from 2016 onward.
RESULTS: Overall, 256 transgender and 9922 cisgender PWH were included. Transgender PWH were younger (median 32 vs 39 years, P < .0001), more often assigned male at birth (99.6% vs 82.4%, P < .0001). Transgender PWH had a higher unadjusted risk of LTFU (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 1.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.60-2.22), confirmed after adjustment (adjusted sHR [asHR] 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.68) and in the post-2016 subgroup (asHR 1.39, 95% CI 1.11-1.77). Composite endpoint analyses were inconclusive (transgender PWH vs cisgender PWH: overall adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.30 [95% CI .79-2.14], P = .293; post-2016 aHR 1.69 [95% CI .91-3.16], P = .098).
CONCLUSIONS: Transgender PWH had a substantially higher risk of LTFU than cisgender participants in this national Italian cohort. Tailored interventions are needed to improve retention and health outcomes.

Title: Lower-extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis after Plastic Surgery: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in a Retrospective Case Series.
Journal: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a significant complication in plastic surgery, particularly affecting the lower extremities. Understanding the associated characteristics can aid in developing effective prevention strategies.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, quality improvement-oriented case series of 5 ultrasound-confirmed symptomatic postoperative lower-extremity DVT events after plastic surgery under general anesthesia at a single institution (January 2020-May 2024). Among 39,055 general anesthesia procedures during the study period, de-identified records were reviewed for patient and procedural characteristics, prophylaxis and mobility pathways, duplex ultrasonography confirmation, management, and short-term outcomes. No non-DVT comparator cohort was extracted; analyses were descriptive and not intended for risk-factor inference. One patient with postoperative chest/back pain and transfer for suspected pulmonary embolism without in-hospital lower-extremity DVT confirmation was excluded from the final case series.
RESULTS: The 5 included cases were clinically heterogeneous and involved complex perioperative settings, including post-massive weight loss body contouring, craniofacial reconstruction with implant use, neurosurgical-related reconstruction, extensive head and neck lesion surgery, and posttraumatic facial reconstruction. All DVTs were confirmed by duplex Doppler ultrasonography, with thrombi involving the posterior tibial, peroneal, or calf muscular veins. Several cases involved prolonged procedures, reoperation for postoperative hematoma, or delayed mobilization. Postoperative anticoagulation was administered in most cases, whereas postoperative mechanical prophylaxis was not consistently documented.
CONCLUSIONS: In a very low-frequency setting, this series highlights potentially actionable prevention gaps-especially postoperative mechanical prophylaxis and mobility disruptions-rather than establishing causal risk factors.

Title: Impact of Perioperative Buyang Huanwu-Based Traditional Chinese Medicine Intervention on Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism, Coagulation Markers and Systemic Inflammation: A Propensity Score-Weighted Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) evaluate, in a propensity-score-weighted retrospective cohort, the effectiveness and safety of a standardised perioperative Buyang Huanwu-based traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction combined with standard low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) prophylaxis on the 30-day incidence of symptomatic and asymptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE), (2) characterise the longitudinal trajectories of coagulation (D-dimer, fibrinogen) and inflammatory (C-reactive protein [CRP]) biomarkers and (3) quantify the net clinical benefit of this integrative approach.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1847 adult patients undergoing major general-surgical or gynaecological procedures between January 2020 and December 2024 at a tertiary integrative-medicine centre. Patients receiving a standardised perioperative TCM decoction based on the modified Buyang Huanwu Tang in addition to standard LMWH prophylaxis (n = 892) were compared with patients receiving standard prophylaxis alone (n = 955). The TCM decoction comprised seven herbal components dispensed at fixed daily doses (Huangqi, 60 g; Danggui, 9 g; Chishao, 6 g; Chuanxiong, 6 g; Honghua, 3 g; Taoren, 6 g; Dilong, 9 g) supplemented with 15 g of Danshen; granules were prepared as a single-batch good manufacturing practice-certified concentrated formulation, with the principal bioactive markers astragaloside IV, ferulic acid, paeoniflorin and salvianolic acid B quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography and required to fall within ±10% of the label content to ensure dose standardisation. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcome was 30-day VTE confirmed by duplex ultrasonography or computed tomography pulmonary angiography, with symptomatic and asymptomatic events recorded separately. Secondary outcomes included major bleeding, length of stay, patient-reported pain and 90-day all-cause mortality. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyse longitudinal trajectories of D-dimer, fibrinogen and CRP measured at baseline and on postoperative days 1, 3 and 7.
RESULTS: After IPTW adjustment, TCM intervention was associated with significantly reduced 30-day VTE incidence (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.58, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.41-0.82, p = 0.002), with consistent protection observed for both symptomatic VTE (HR: 0.55, 95% CI: 0.34-0.89) and ultrasound-detected asymptomatic distal deep-vein thrombosis (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.39-0.94). Landmark analysis revealed sustained protection during both hospitalisation (HR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.33-0.81) and the post-discharge period (HR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.42-0.93). Linear mixed-effects modelling demonstrated significant group-by-time interactions for D-dimer (p < 0.001) and CRP (p = 0.003), indicating accelerated biomarker clearance in the TCM group: 42% faster D-dimer resolution and 38% faster CRP normalisation than in controls. No significant difference was observed for major bleeding (2.1% vs 2.4%, p = 0.68) or 90-day all-cause mortality (1.6% vs 2.0%, p = 0.51). Decision-curve analysis confirmed superior net clinical benefit across the clinically relevant threshold-probability range.
CONCLUSION: Perioperative Buyang Huanwu-based TCM combined with standard LMWH prophylaxis significantly reduces postoperative VTE risk - for both symptomatic and ultrasound-detected asymptomatic events - through accelerated resolution of coagulation and inflammatory cascades, without increasing bleeding or 90-day all-cause mortality. These findings support the integration of standardised TCM into enhanced-recovery-after-surgery protocols, particularly for moderate- to high-risk surgical patients in whom anticoagulation intensification may be contraindicated.

Title: Integrated Clinical, Biological, and Echocardiographic Factors Independently Associated With In-Hospital Mortality in Infective Endocarditis: A Single-Centre Cohort Study From Morocco.
Abstract: Background Infective endocarditis (IE) remains associated with substantial in-hospital mortality worldwide, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Identifying clinical, biological, microbiological, and echocardiographic factors associated with adverse outcomes may help characterize patients at increased risk of death. Objectives To identify clinical, biological, microbiological, and echocardiographic factors independently associated with in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalized with IE in a North African tertiary referral centre. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including 260 consecutive patients admitted with definite IE according to the 2023 Duke-International Society for Cardiovascular Infectious Diseases (Duke-ISCVID) criteria, between January 2020 and April 2026. Patients were classified as survivors (n = 188) or non-survivors (n = 72). Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, biological parameters, microbiological data, and echocardiographic findings were systematically collected. Univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed. Multivariable analysis used backward Wald elimination. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and calibration was evaluated using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test. Results Among 260 patients with definite IE, 188 (72.3%) survived to hospital discharge, and 72 (27.7%) died during hospitalization. The mean age was 47 ± 16 years, with a male predominance. Rheumatic heart disease was the most frequent underlying valvular condition. In multivariable analysis, septic shock was associated with increased in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 28.45; 95% CI, 3.42-106.80; p < 0.001), as were local cardiac complications (aOR, 3.52; 95% CI, 1.42-8.72; p = 0.007), age ≥60 years (aOR, 3.84; 95% CI, 1.48-9.96; p = 0.010), vegetation diameter >15 mm (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.00-6.20; p = 0.049), male sex (aOR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.12-6.42; p = 0.027), haemoglobin <10 g/dL (aOR, 2.80; 95% CI, 1.10-7.22; p = 0.031), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (aOR, 2.70; 95% CI, 1.03-7.01; p = 0.042). The final model showed good discrimination, with a C-statistic of 0.84 (95% CI, 0.78-0.90), and no evidence of poor calibration according to the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (χ² = 6.42, df = 8, p = 0.60). Given the sparse distribution of septic shock among survivors (n = 2), a Firth-penalized sensitivity analysis yielded an OR of 9.80 (95% CI, 2.85-33.70), supporting the robustness of the direction of this association despite sparse-data concerns. Conclusions In this contemporary Moroccan cohort, septic shock, local cardiac complications, older age, vegetation diameter >15 mm, male sex, anaemia, and severe renal dysfunction were independently associated with in-hospital mortality. These findings may support early recognition of high-risk clinical features and multidisciplinary assessment, but should not be interpreted as a validated mortality prediction model. Prospective multicentre studies with internal and external validation are warranted to assess the generalizability of these findings.

Title: Link Between the Cardiometabolic Index and Stroke Risk Across Different Glucose Metabolic Status in Chinese Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiometabolic index (CMI) encompasses central obesity and atherogenic dyslipidemia, two metabolic abnormalities that are closely associated with insulin resistance and issues in glucose metabolism. However, whether the association between CMI and incident stroke differs across glucose metabolic states remains unclear.
METHODS: Utilizing data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), we carried out a cohort study with 7980 individuals aged 45 years and above who were free of stroke. We explored the associations between the initial CMI and stroke incidents across various glucose metabolism status through Cox proportional hazards models, restricted cubic spline analyses, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, and receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: Incident stroke risk was independently associated with both log (CMI) and CMI quartiles, increasing with higher values and quartiles. The fully adjusted model showed that each 1-unit rise in log (CMI) was associated with an increased risk of stroke (HR = 1.13, 95% CI 1.00-1.28; p = 0.044). Compared to Q1, Q4 had a higher risk of stroke (HR = 1.52; 95% CI 1.11-2.08; p = 0.008). Moreover, for individuals with diabetes mellitus (DM), a higher CMI was associated with a greater likelihood of stroke, with Q4 presenting an increased risk (HR = 1.49, 95% CI: 1.02-2.31, p = 0.019) when compared to Q1. By contrast, no significant association was observed among individuals with prediabetes or normal glucose regulation. The findings' robustness was further corroborated by conducting subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In those with DM, the CMI had a moderate level of accuracy in predicting new stroke cases, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.675.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher baseline CMI was associated with an increased risk of incident stroke, with a more apparent association among individuals with DM. These findings suggest that the vascular relevance of the CMI may vary according to the underlying glucose metabolic status and support its potential role as a marker of cardiometabolic dysfunction. Further research is essential to shed light on the metabolic pathways involved in these associations and to establish the clinical value of CMI.

Title: Myosteatosis as a prognostic biomarker for post-transplant survival and cardiometabolic outcomes: A retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic health significantly impacts long-term survival among liver transplant (LT) recipients. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic health in the general population is related to skeletal muscle quality. However, this has not been well investigated in the transplant patient population. While myosteatosis, characterized by fat infiltration into skeletal muscle, has been closely associated with metabolic health in the general population, it has not been thoroughly explored as a risk factor for outcomes in LT recipients.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study of 503 adult LT recipients at the University Health Network, we evaluated the prognostic value of myosteatosis on post-transplant survival and cardiometabolic outcomes. Pre-transplant contrast-enhanced CT scans of LT recipients within 6 months prior to transplantation were analyzed using the nnU-Netv2 convolutional neural network, and myosteatosis was quantified by skeletal muscle radiation attenuation adjusted for BMI.
RESULTS: The mean age of LT recipients was 56.89 years; patients with myosteatosis were significantly older (58.69 y) than those without (54.96 y). LT recipients were predominately male (75.9%). Cox proportional hazards models showed that myosteatosis independently predicted both all-cause mortality (HR 1.50 [95% CI 1.06-2.12]; p = 0.024) and the incidence of post-transplant metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) (hazard ratio [HR] 2.25 [95% CI 1.28-3.98]; p = 0.0051). Notably, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, and malignancy did not differ significantly by myosteatosis status.
CONCLUSIONS: The presence of myosteatosis could identify LT recipients at higher risk for metabolic complications. As a modifiable and non-invasive biomarker, the presence of myosteatosis could guide personalized interventions to improve long-term outcomes.

Title: Transfascial Paraspinal Versus Conventional Open Posterior Pedicle Screw Fixation for Thoracolumbar Fractures: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Posterior pedicle screw fixation is the standard treatment for unstable thoracolumbar fractures requiring surgery. The conventional open posterior approach, however, requires extensive subperiosteal stripping of the paraspinal muscles, causing ischemia, denervation, greater intraoperative blood loss, more postoperative pain, and delayed recovery. The Wiltse paraspinal, or transfascial, approach exploits the natural intermuscular plane between the multifidus and longissimus muscles to limit this soft-tissue disruption while preserving adequate exposure. Still, robust randomized evidence comparing the two techniques remains limited. Our objective was to compare the perioperative, clinical, and radiological outcomes of pedicle screw fixation performed through the transfascial paraspinal approach versus the conventional open posterior approach in patients with AO Spine Type A thoracolumbar fractures.
METHODS: Fifty patients aged 18-60 years with a single-level AO Spine Type A thoracolumbar fracture were randomized 1:1 using a computer-generated sequence with allocation concealment to transfascial paraspinal (n=25) or conventional open posterior (n=25) fixation and followed for 12 months. Outcomes included operative time, blood loss, postoperative drain output, mobilization time, hospital stay, Visual Analog Scale pain scores at two weeks and three, six, and 12 months, fluoroscopy time, sagittal Cobb angle correction, and surgical site infection. Continuous variables were compared using the independent-samples t-test or Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, with p<0.05 considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The transfascial group had significantly shorter operative time (96.16±13.77 vs. 106.64±17.70 min, p=0.047), less intraoperative blood loss (173.76±37.94 vs. 294.00±89.35 mL, p<0.001), lower drain output (37.60±18.94 vs. 93.20±43.48 mL, p<0.001), earlier mobilisation (2.44±1.04 vs. 4.08±2.77 days, p=0.033) and shorter hospital stay (3.08±1.82 vs. 5.48±4.30 days, p=0.012) than the conventional group. VAS pain scores were significantly lower in the transfascial group at two weeks, three, six, and 12 months (all p≤0.004), despite similar baseline pain (p=0.533). Postoperative Cobb angle correction (4.40±1.15° vs. 4.60±1.19°, p=0.549) and fluoroscopy time (7.04±1.35 vs. 7.68±1.65 sec, p=0.140) did not differ significantly between groups. Surgical site infection distribution was also similar (Fisher-Freeman-Halton test, p=0.349), though deep infection occurred only in the conventional group (8.0% vs. 0%).
CONCLUSION: The transfascial paraspinal approach achieves radiological correction equivalent to that of the conventional open posterior approach while significantly reducing operative time, blood loss, wound drainage, hospital stay, and postoperative pain. In appropriately selected patients with AO Spine Type A thoracolumbar fractures, it represents an effective, reproducible, and safe muscle-sparing alternative to conventional open fixation, supporting wider adoption pending confirmation in larger multicenter randomized trials with longer follow-up.

Title: A Team-Based Patient Engagement Approach to Selexipag Initiation and Maintenance in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (TEAM PAH): Real-World Dosing Patterns and Persistence Among Patients With and Without a History of Methamphetamine Use.
Abstract: Selexipag is an oral prostacyclin receptor agonist approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). This single-center, retrospective study described oral selexipag dosing patterns and persistence, overall and stratified by history of methamphetamine (meth) use, at an expert center in California, USA, using a multidisciplinary, nurse-directed protocol entailing frequent follow-up and individualized side effect management. Medical charts of patients with PAH initiating oral selexipag between January 2016 and March 2023 were abstracted. Patient characteristics and dosing patterns were described up to 14 months post-initiation. The individualized maintenance dose (IMD) was the first dose maintained for ≥ 14 days after reaching the maximum tolerated dose. Persistence was described using Kaplan-Meier analysis. A total of 200 patients initiated oral selexipag (median age 52 years; 69.5% female; 54.5% White; 70.5% on triple therapy; 41% with a history of meth use). Most patients (89.0%) achieved maintenance (median IMD: 900 μg twice daily; median time to maintenance: 2.5 months). Selexipag persistence at 1 year was 76.2%, with most discontinuations occurring within 2 months of initiation. Similar proportions of patients with and without a history of meth use achieved maintenance (85.4% vs. 91.5%; p = 0.3) and persisted on selexipag at 1 year (74.0% vs. 77.5%; p = 0.9). Using a multidisciplinary nurse-directed protocol, most patients with PAH were titrated to their IMD and persisted on oral selexipag, including those with a history of meth use. These findings highlight the importance of frequent patient contact for dose adjustment and side effect management, particularly earlier in the titration process.

Title: Identifying a high-risk CKM syndrome phenotype: association of albuminuria with subclinical hemodynamic alterations via portable noninvasive cardiometer.
Abstract:
OBJECT: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely linked to heart failure.
METHODS: This prospective study of 274 asymptomatic patients with T2DM without clinical heart failure or coronary artery disease used portable noninvasive cardiometry to assess hemodynamic parameters.
RESULTS: Patients with albuminuria (n=119) showed significantly lower stroke volume and index of contractility (ICON 29.44 ± 9.48 vs 34.78 ± 10.18, p<0.0001), and higher systemic vascular resistance compared with those without albuminuria (n=155). Albuminuria remained independently associated with reduced ICON after multivariable adjustment that included sex, body mass index, and metabolic parameters. Higher BMI was also strongly associated with lower ICON. Patients with albuminuria also had a higher all-cause medical hospitalization rate (39.5% vs 24.5%) during follow-up.
DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that T2DM patients with albuminuria may represent a high-risk CKM phenotype characterized by subclinical hemodynamic alterations, supporting further investigation of noninvasive approaches for early cardiovascular risk assessment.

Title: Ocular Manifestations and Visual Outcomes of Patients with Giant Cell Arteritis.
Journal: Journal of ophthalmology and advance research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ocular involvement in giant cell arteritis (GCA) is common, yet there is limited literature addressing its specific ocular manifestations and their impact on visual outcomes. The objective was to evaluate the incidence of visual involvement, treatment, relapse rate, and visual outcome in patients with GCA.
METHODS: This is a single center retrospective cohort study. The study included 35 eyes from 37 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven GCA (TAB+), 39 eyes from 39 consecutive patients with clinically diagnosed GCA and negative biopsy (TAB-), and 16 eyes from 21 consecutive patients clinically diagnosed with GCA without undergoing a biopsy (no TAB). We collected demographic and clinical presentation. 26/37 (70%) in the TAB+ group, 29/39 (74%) in the TAB- group, and 14/21 (67%) in the no TAB group underwent at least one neuro-ophthalmic exam. Eyes were grouped into no, mild, or severe ocular involvement. At each visit, patients underwent neuro-ophthalmic evaluation, ophthalmic imaging, and visual fields. The main outcome measures were best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), color perception (% correct), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell complex (GCC), area of foveal avascular zone (FAZ), and Humphrey visual field (HVF).
RESULTS: Within our entire cohort of 97 patients, 69 (71%) underwent neuro-ophthalmic examinations, 5 had unilateral involvement and 42 had bilateral involvement. At diagnosis, all patients were started on high dose prednisone, 9/37 (24%) intravenously and 28/37 (76%) orally. 16/37 (43%) patients were treated with adjuvant tocilizumab. Within our cohort, 5/97 (5%) patients had visual relapses, all within the first year after diagnosis. 15/50 (30%) eyes had no OI, 22/50 (44%) eyes had mild OI, and 13/50 (26%) eyes had severe OI. After 12 months of GCA diagnosis, patients with no OI compared to severe OI demonstrated: BCVA (logMAR 0.164 vs. 1.26, p<0.001), color perception (87% vs 6%, p<0.001), RNFL (93μm vs. 56μm, p<0.001), GCC (76μm vs. 52μm, p<0.001), FAZ (0.119 mm2 vs. 0.314 mm2, p<0.001), and HVF (-2.58 vs. -19.18, p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Visual involvement in GCA is common. The affected eyes had irreversible vision loss. GCC, RNFL, and FAZ were associated with poor visual outcome.

Title: Venous thromboembolism in Cushing syndrome: current evidence and a practical thromboprophylaxis algorithm.
Abstract: Cushing syndrome (CS) is a rare endocrine disorder associated with a markedly increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Chronic hypercortisolism induces a prothrombotic state through activation of coagulation pathways, impaired fibrinolysis, and endothelial dysfunction. VTE represents a major source of morbidity and mortality in this population, yet optimal strategies for prevention and treatment remain insufficiently standardized. To summarize current evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, risk factors, prevention, and treatment of VTE in patients with endogenous CS and to propose a practical thromboprophylaxis approach. A narrative review of the literature was conducted using MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases. Observational studies, registry data, systematic reviews, and expert consensus statements addressing VTE in CS were analyzed, with particular attention to peri-operative risk and persistence of hypercoagulability after remission. Patients with CS have a 10-20-fold higher risk of VTE compared with the general population. The peri-operative period, especially after TSS or adrenalectomy, represents the highest-risk phase, although increased thrombotic risk may persist for 3-6 months after biochemical remission. Key mechanisms include elevated factor VIII, von Willebrand factor, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, increased thrombin generation, and endothelial dysfunction. Recent evidence from the ERCUSYN registry and the 2025 Delphi consensus supports early and extended thromboprophylaxis. Current expert consensus supports low-molecular-weight heparin as the preferred peri-operative pharmacological agent, whereas direct oral anticoagulants may be considered in selected patients during long-term management. CS should be regarded as a persistent prothrombotic condition in which early and, when appropriate, extended thromboprophylaxis should be considered following individualized assessment of thrombotic and bleeding risk. Prospective studies are needed to develop evidence-based, individualized prevention strategies.

Title: Mechanical circulatory support devices in heart failure: a narrative review of current evidence, clinical applications, complications, and future directions.
Abstract: Mechanical circulatory support devices (MCSDs) have evolved from rescue therapy for refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) to an essential component of advanced heart failure management, spanning temporary support, bridge strategies, durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD), and total artificial heart (TAH). This structured narrative review summarizes the historical evolution, current indications, device classification, major short-term and long-term platforms, adverse events, and future directions of MCSDs. Literature was selected in a structured narrative manner with emphasis on contemporary guidelines, randomized or comparative studies, major registries, and representative Chinese experience. Available evidence shows that MCSDs can improve hemodynamics and, in selected populations, survival and quality of life; however, these benefits must be balanced against bleeding, stroke, infection, right heart failure, device malfunction, cost, and major ethical and access constraints. Current practice thus necessitates careful patient selection, stage-based therapeutic escalation, and rigorous evaluation of mixed evidence pertaining to temporary MCSDs, LVAD and TAH, instead of merely describing individual devices.

Title: Association Between Left Atrial Volume Index (LAVI) and Glycemic Control (HbA1c) in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glycemic control and left atrial remodeling in patients with concomitant type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. In this study, we examined the association between glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and left atrial volume index (LAVI) in this high-risk population.
METHODS: A total of 700 patients with AF and T2DM were included in this retrospective study. We used medical records to obtain HbA1c and echocardiographic parameters. We assessed LAVI as a continuous variable and as a binary variable (enlarged LAVI > 34 mL/m²). We used Spearman correlation, multivariable linear regression, and binary logistic regression to examine the relationship between HbA1c and LAVI.
RESULTS: There was a significant association between higher HbA1c and greater LAVI (Spearman's ρ = 0.287, p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each 1% increase in HbA1c was associated with a 1.678 mL/m² increase in LAVI. Higher HbA1c was independently associated with increased odds of enlarged LAVI (adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 1.701, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.391-2.081, p < 0.001). Hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease were also independently associated with enlarged LAVI.
CONCLUSION: In patients with concurrent AF and T2DM, higher HbA1c was independently associated with larger LAVI and higher odds of left atrial enlargement (LAE). Future prospective studies are warranted to determine whether improved glycemic control can influence atrial remodeling.

Title: From Adiposity to Diastolic Dysfunction: The Integrated Role of Epicardial Fat, Autonomic Dysregulation, and Morning Blood Pressure Surge in Obesity.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although the association between obesity and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (LVDD) is well established, the concurrent associations of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), sleep-trough (prewaking) morning blood pressure surge (MBPS), and autonomic imbalance with LVDD have not been fully elucidated. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EAT thickness, MBPS, and heart rate variability (HRV) parameters with LVDD in obese adults and to assess the cross-sectional discriminatory performance of these multimodal markers.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 240 individuals, comprising 120 obese participants (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m2) and 120 age- and sex-matched normal-weight controls (body mass index 18.5-24.9 kg/m2). All participants underwent transthoracic echocardiography, 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, and 24-h Holter electrocardiographic analysis, with HRV data available for the entire cohort (n = 240). EAT thickness was measured echocardiographically, and LVDD was classified using contemporary guideline-based echocardiographic criteria. SDNN was predefined as the primary autonomic marker, while RMSSD and the LF/HF ratio were reported as supportive indices. Associations with LVDD (≥ Grade I) were evaluated using correlation analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Cross-sectional discrimination analysis and performance assessment were performed within the obese subgroup (n = 120).
RESULTS: Compared with controls, obese participants exhibited greater EAT thickness (6.5 ± 1.7 vs. 4.0 ± 1.2 mm), higher MBPS (33 ± 10 vs. 21 ± 7 mmHg), increased LF/HF ratio, and lower SDNN and RMSSD values (all p < 0.001). The prevalence of LVDD was significantly higher in obese individuals than in controls (45% vs. 15%, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, EAT thickness (odds ratio [OR] = 1.20 per 1 mm; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08-1.34), MBPS (OR = 1.35 per 10 mmHg; 95% CI 1.10-1.65), and SDNN (OR = 0.88 per 10 ms; 95% CI 0.80-0.97) were independently associated with LVDD. The parsimonious model demonstrated discrimination and calibration comparable to or superior to the full clinical model (AUC: 0.89 vs. 0.85).
CONCLUSION: In obese adults, increased epicardial adiposity, exaggerated MBPS, and autonomic dysfunction coexist with LVDD. Integrated assessment of structural (EAT), hemodynamic (MBPS), and autonomic (SDNN) markers may facilitate cross-sectional identification of LVDD and improve phenotypic characterization in obesity.

Title: Predictive Factors for Diabetes Insipidus and Syndrome of Inappropriate Secretion of Antidiuretic Hormone After Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma.
Abstract: Objective The objective of this study is to determine preoperative predictors of diabetes insipidus (DI) and syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) after transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) for pituitary adenomas. DI and SIADH are common complications associated with TSS. Methods This small unicentric retrospective study was conducted in a tertiary referral hospital in Saudi Arabia. The study enrolled 42 patients. We reviewed the medical records of all patients who underwent surgical resection of pituitary adenoma at our hospital between January 2010 and December 2022. The results of urine and serum analyses were collected to establish a diagnosis. Pre- and post-surgery sodium differences were categorized by the pre-surgery value to calculate the percent change in sodium levels. The tumor function was confirmed using histopathology, and radiological reports were reviewed for the size, location, extent, invasiveness of the tumor, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leaks. Results Among the 42 patients included, seven (16.7%) had DI and two (4.8%) had SIADH. Two-thirds underwent resection using the microscopic approach, and the remaining patients underwent endonasal TSS. Approximately 43% of patients had functioning pituitary adenomas, with prolactin-secreting adenomas being the most common (21.4%). Three-quarters of the tumors were macroadenomas. No significant between-group differences were observed in the length of hospital stay, preoperative sodium levels, and percentage change in serum sodium (P>.05). Smoking and chronic hypertension were not associated with DI or SIADH. The number of patients with panhypopituitarism (P<.01) or hypothyroidism (P<.01) was significantly different between the DI and no DI groups. However, no factor significantly predicted the development of DI. No significant differences were observed between the SIADH and non-SIADH groups. Conclusion The risk of DI increases in patients who develop panhypopituitarism, including central hypothyroidism after surgery. However, no factor reliably predicts the development of DI or SIADH after TSS.

Title: Patient-derived stem cell models of brain endothelial-neuron interactions in early course psychosis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early-course psychosis (ECP) exhibits marked heterogeneity in illness trajectories, with a substantial subset of individuals developing progressive symptomatic, cognitive, and functional decline. Although growing evidence implicates blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular unit (NVU) dysfunction in psychosis spectrum disorders, direct links between longitudinal clinical trajectories and disease-related cellular phenotypes remain insufficiently characterized.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This protocol describes a standardized stem cell-based framework to model BBB and NVU dysfunction in ECP using induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) within a longitudinally characterized clinical cohort. The approach integrates donor-specific ex vivo cellular assays with repeated clinical, cognitive, and functional assessments for up to 5 years. Procedures are detailed for iPSC reprogramming from PBMCs, differentiation of iPSCs to brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs) and cortical neurons, and functional assessment of BBB integrity using trans-endothelial electrical resistance (TEER), paracellular permeability, and tight junction protein expression. NVU effects are examined by exposing cortical neurons to BMEC-conditioned media under matched and cross-culture conditions, with quantification of dendritic spine morphology, synaptic puncta, and neuronal activity using micro-electrode arrays. The protocol further incorporates modular mechanistic perturbations, including pharmacological and genetic modulation of matrix metalloproteinase 1 (MMP1), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNFα)-related signaling, and evaluation of antipsychotic effects on barrier function.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval and informed consent for this study was obtained and the findings will be disseminated through publication in peer-reviewed journals and presentations at scientific conferences.

Title: Bone marrow necrosis and rapidly progressive liver metastases after breast-conserving surgery in a 33-year-old woman with triple-negative breast cancer, followed by death 288 days after surgery: a case report.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone marrow necrosis (BMN) is rare, and malignancy-associated BMN often reflects high tumor burden, rapid progression, and poor prognosis. BMN after definitive treatment for early triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), followed by visceral progression and coagulation-fibrinolytic abnormalities, is rarely reported.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 33-year-old woman underwent breast-conserving surgery and sentinel lymph node biopsy for a 1.8 cm grade 3 invasive carcinoma of no special type. One of four sentinel nodes was positive (pT1cN1a, cM0); the surgical specimen was estrogen receptor (ER)-negative, progesterone receptor (PR)-negative, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) 0, with Ki-67 approximately 90%, consistent with TNBC. She completed four cycles of epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide followed by four cycles of liposomal paclitaxel and adjuvant radiotherapy. Six days after radiotherapy, recurrent fever, bone pain, and progressive thrombocytopenia developed, followed by pancytopenia. Bone marrow biopsy on October 23, 2025 showed extensive necrosis with only a few degenerating nucleated cells and no clearly identifiable viable malignant cells. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) on November 21 showed liver metastases. On November 25, white blood cell count (WBC) was 1.9×109/L, hemoglobin 54.0 g/L, platelets 4×109/L, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 308.9 U/L, total bilirubin 60.8 μmol/L, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 2758.1 U/L. D-dimer was 19.49 mg/L, approximately 39 times the laboratory upper reference limit of 0.5 mg/L; prothrombin time (PT) was 15.3 s, below the documented upper reference limit of 21 s; and fibrinogen was 2.11 g/L. Retrospective application of the 2025 International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) score yielded 5 points, meeting the scoring threshold. D-dimer later exceeded 40.00 mg/L, activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and thrombin time increased, and fibrinogen fell to 1.11 g/L. Hepatic and renal dysfunction and multiorgan failure ensued, and she died on December 2, 2025, 288 days after surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: In aggressive breast cancer, persistent fever, progressive bone pain, rapidly falling blood counts, and elevated LDH should prompt early evaluation for BMN and possible marrow involvement, with assessment for infection, coagulation disorders, hemophagocytic syndrome, and systemic progression. Marked thrombocytopenia with striking D-dimer elevation warrants dynamic DIC assessment even when PT remains within the local reference range. The temporal relationships among BMN, DIC, and prior therapy should be interpreted cautiously.

Title: Diabetes Status and the Association Between a Coronary Artery Disease Polygenic Risk Score and Incident Coronary Artery Disease in an Iranian Prospective Cohort.
Journal: Medical journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) for coronary artery disease (CAD) may provide a quantitative assessment of inherited susceptibility that extends beyond conventional clinical risk factors. However, the relationship between CAD PRS and the incidence of CAD may differ across various cardiometabolic risk groups. This study aimed to evaluate whether baseline diabetes status influences the association between CAD PRS and the incidence of CAD.
METHODS: This cohort comprised 5,139 adults from the Tehran Cardiometabolic Genetic Study (TCGS) who were free of CAD at baseline. The CAD PRS was constructed using a maximum clumping-and-thresholding approach based on external CAD genome-wide association summary statistics. Associations between the PRS and cumulative incident CAD were assessed according to diabetes status using logistic regression. Model discrimination and prediction error were evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) and the Brier score.
RESULTS: Among 5,139 participants, 1,171 had diabetes while 3,968 did not; incident CAD occurred in 334 diabetic and 427 non-diabetic participants. After adjusting for traditional risk factors, each 1-SD increase in the PRS was associated with higher odds of incident CAD in diabetic participants (OR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.20-1.55) and non-diabetic participants (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.14-1.41). A significant interaction between PRS quintiles and diabetes status was observed (P = 0.017). The model incorporating the PRS alongside traditional risk factors demonstrated greater discrimination in non-diabetic compared to diabetic participants (AUC, 0.776 vs 0.600).
CONCLUSION: CAD PRS was associated with incident CAD across diabetes-defined strata; however, its predictive relevance varied according to baseline diabetes status. These findings support the use of PRS as a marker of inherited susceptibility rather than as evidence for clinical risk reclassification or as a stand-alone predictive tool.

Title: Occurrence and Determinants of Periprosthetic Fractures of the Femur During Intraoperative and Post-operative Period in Patients Undergoing Hip Arthroplasty: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic femoral fractures (PPFs) are serious complications of hip arthroplasty, leading to increased morbidity and the need for revision surgery. Data on determinants of PPFs in Indian populations are limited. This study aimed to evaluate the occurrence and risk factors for PPFs during intraoperative and postoperative periods in patients undergoing hemiarthroplasty (HA) or total hip arthroplasty (THA).
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary care center between January 2021 and December 2022. Patients aged 18-80 years undergoing primary HA or THA were enrolled. Demographic, clinical, biochemical, and radiological data-including bone mineral density (BMD), serum vitamin D₃ levels, comorbidities, and femoral morphology (Dorr classification)-were collected. Surgical details and postoperative outcomes were recorded. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of PPFs.
RESULTS: Among 402 patients, 25 (6.2%) sustained PPFs, all intraoperatively. Fractures predominantly involved the greater trochanter (92%). Multivariate analysis identified Dorr type C femoral canal (adjusted OR [aOR] 13.5, 95% CI 3.06-59.3), severe osteoporosis (BMD T ≤ - 2.5; aOR 5.63, 95% CI 1.56-20.3), and absence of preoperative vitamin D₃ supplementation (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.08-0.50) as independent predictors of PPFs. Other significant associations were advanced age, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, smoking, bipolar hemiarthroplasty, anterolateral approach, and higher ASA grade.
CONCLUSION: PPFs during hip arthroplasty are multifactorial, with bone quality, femoral canal morphology, and preoperative vitamin D₃ supplementation being key determinants. Preoperative optimization of bone health and careful surgical planning can reduce fracture risk and improve outcomes in high-risk patients.

Title: Gut microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites in cardiovascular disease: mechanisms, biomarkers, and precision interventions.
Abstract: The gut microbiota plays a significant role in cardiovascular disease (CVD), through its metabolic products. Tryptophan is a key signaling molecule in the microbiota-host network; its gut microbial metabolites, including indole derivatives, kynurenine and serotonin, have dual effects on cardiovascular homeostasis. This review summarizes research progress on gut microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites in atherosclerosis, hypertension, heart failure and other CVDs, focusing on metabolic flux in three pathways, the indole, kynurenine (KYN) and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) pathways, and their mechanisms via gut barrier maintenance, immune regulation through Th17/Treg and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) axis, and neuroendocrine blood pressure control. It also evaluates clinical evidence for key metabolites, such as indoxyl sulfate (IS), indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), as novel biomarkers, and explores precision interventions including dietary regimens, probiotic or postbiotic supplementation, traditional Chinese medicine ingredients, and host genetic background-guided strategies. Current evidence shows these metabolites exert both protective and pathogenic effects, highly dependent on disease context, microenvironment and host genetics. However, most data are from animal models and small cohort studies; remaining challenges include detection standardization, causality establishment and clinical translation. Future research should employ large prospective cohorts, multi-omics integration and mechanism-driven intervention trials to systematically elucidate the regulatory network and advance precision prevention and treatment.

Title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
Abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 ×  reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR,   KRAS G 12 C    , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90  per condition; all p > 0.20  ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

Title: Modeling heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) likelihood among women with suspected coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD).
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) can precede development of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in patients with ischemia and no obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA). The H2FPEF score is used to estimate HFpEF likelihood but has not been evaluated among women with suspected INOCA.
METHODS: Women (n = 98) with suspected INOCA enrolled in prospective cohort studies at a single center with both cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) and echocardiography to calculate H2FPEF score. CMR evaluated left ventricular (LV) structure, function, myocardial perfusion reserve index (MPRI) and fibrosis. Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression were performed.
RESULTS: Group mean age was 56 years, BMI 27 kg/m2, 39% had hypertension, and 12% had diabetes. Median H2FPEF score was 2 (range 0-7), with 43 (44%), 53 (54%), and 2 (2%) ranked as having low (0-1), intermediate (2-5), or high (6-9) probability of HFpEF, respectively.H2FPEF score was inversely related to MPRI, native T1, extracellular volume, and Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) physical limitation score (all p < 0.05), but not related to LV strain or remodeling. Regression modeling demonstrated that low MPRI, SAQ physical limitation, and diabetes were independent predictors of H2FPEF, adjusted for dyslipidemia and native T1.
CONCLUSIONS: Among women with suspected INOCA, 54% had an intermediate or higher H2FPEF score. Compromised microvascular perfusion, fibrosis, angina, and history of diabetes predicted H2FPEF score. These findings support the hypothesis that CMD may contribute to development of HFpEF in women with INOCA. Longitudinal studies and intervention trials are needed.

Title: The role of sitagliptin in modifying metabolic, hormonal and clinical parameters in polycystic ovarian syndrome patients: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is a disease that is not limited to reproductive symptoms; it is also significantly linked to metabolic problems such as obesity, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia. Sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor, may play a significant role in metabolic, inflammatory, and hormonal abnormalities in PCOS patients.
OBJECTIVE: This randomized clinical trial aimed to investigate the impact of sitagliptin on metabolic disturbances, hormonal abnormalities, and clinical outcomes in patients with PCOS. The study is registered on Clinicaltrials.gov with an ID of (NCT05972928).
METHODS: This randomized controlled trial was conducted at Beni-Suef University Hospital, involving 80 women diagnosed with PCOS based on the Rotterdam criteria. Participants were equally allocated into either a sitagliptin group, receiving 100 mg daily, or a control group, with a follow-up period of 3 months. Changes in body weight served as the sole primary outcome of the study. Meanwhile, changes in BMI, HOMA-IR, lipid profile, and hormonal indicators, along with clinical improvements in infertility, hirsutism, acne, and menstrual irregularity, were evaluated as secondary outcomes.
RESULTS: Regarding the primary outcome, a highly significant reduction in body weight was observed within the sitagliptin group (p < 0.001). Similarly, secondary outcomes including BMI, HOMA-IR, DHEA, HbA1c, total and free testosterone, and LH levels, all demonstrated significant decreases (p < 0.05). Clinical secondary outcomes also showed potential improvements, with menstrual regularity increasing significantly (p = 0.006), alongside visible reductions in hirsutism (p = 0.006) and exploratory reduction in the infertility rates (p = 0.031), that needs further confirmation. Furthermore, the intervention was well-tolerated, as recorded side effects were both rare and mild in intensity.
CONCLUSION: Sitagliptin has potential impact on the hormonal, metabolic and clinical aspects of PCOS, and an exploratory effect on reproductive function. This makes it a potentially promising option for managing this complex condition.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05972928, identifier NCT05972928.

Title: Derivation of a blood count-based machine learning model to prioritise sequencing for high-risk clonal haematopoiesis: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal haematopoiesis is a precursor of myeloid neoplasia and common in older adults, Precursor risk stratification is critical to early cancer detection, guiding surveillance and prevention efforts to high-risk populations. Existing clonal haematopoiesis risk scores use molecular features to estimate risk of myeloid neoplasia, but only around 1% of adults with detectable clonal haematopoiesis are at high risk of myeloid neoplasia transformation. Moreover, sequencing based molecular diagnostics are expensive with limited global availability highlighting the need for pre-sequencing strategies which identify populations enriched for individuals with high-risk clonal haematopoiesis.
METHODS: We used blood count parameters, age, and sex as input features to and develop a multi-class machine learning model that pre-classifies individuals based on their probability of having high-risk clonal haematopoiesis or developing future myeloid neoplasia. Stratified splitting was used to divide 461,576 eligible UK Biobank participants (recruited October 1, 2006 to March 13, 2010) into a training cohort for model derivation (n = 369,260) and a test cohort for internal validation (n = 92,316). Ground truth output class assignments were defined based on documented progression to incident myeloid neoplasia and presence of clonal haematopoiesis with high-risk features defined using molecular parameters of the clonal haematopoiesis risk score. Individuals were labelled positive if they had high-risk clonal haematopoiesis and progressed to myeloid neoplasia, negative if they lacked clonal haematopoiesis with high-risk features, and equivocal if they had higher risk features but had no documented incident myeloid neoplasia event. We then compared model predictions against ground truth labels for validation in the UKB test cohort as well as in independent clinical and population cohorts from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hematologic Malignancy Data Repository (HMDR; n = 2233; March 26, 2010, to June 5, 2024) and the All of US database (n = 14,674; May 31, 2017 to October 1, 2023), respectively.
FINDINGS: The resulting pre-sequencing risk model (PRISM) categorises all cases of high-risk clonal haematopoiesis as positive and pre-classifies 40% (2158 of 5383) of low-risk clonal haematopoiesis and 55% (47,894 of 86,429) of clonal haematopoiesis-negative cases as negative. Validation of PRISM revealed an area under the curve of 0.89 (95% CI 0.85-0.93) in the UK Biobank test cohort, 0.74 (0.61-0.84) in HMDR, and 0.87 (0.77-0.96) in All of US. Negative predictive values for negative class assignments were 0.993 (95% CI 0.992-0.993) in the UKB test cohort, 0.968 (0.943-0.981) in HMDR, and 0.998 (0.997-0.999) in All of US.
INTERPRETATION: PRISM positive class assignment defines a population most enriched for high-risk clonal haematopoiesis, while negative class predictions, mark individuals without high-risk clonal haematopoiesis. PRISM therefore provides a framework for reproducibly assigning blood count-based risk thresholds to prioritise clonal haematopoiesis screening in populations at risk for myeloid neoplasia.
FUNDING: Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation, Edward P Evans Foundation for MDS, and the National Heart Lung and Blood Institute.

Title: Application and evidence gaps of sarcopenia diagnostic criteria in patients with heart failure: a scoping review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnostic criteria for sarcopenia show heterogeneity in patients with heart failure (HF). This study reviews existing evidence through a scoping review.
METHODS: We searched six databases (PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure [CNKI], and Wanfang) from inception to May 2026. Two reviewers screened literature and extracted data independently. We used narrative synthesis.
RESULTS: We included 23 studies covering 8 diagnostic criteria. The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019 (9 studies) and the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) (7 studies) were most common. The overall prevalence ranged from 8.9% to 65.8%, with wide variation within the same criterion. Only 3 studies performed head-to-head comparisons. Heart failure-specific factors (edema interference, New York Heart Association [NYHA] class limitation, timing of assessment in acute phase) received limited attention. No study assessed sarcopenia at acute decompensation before diuresis. One study evaluated patients with stage B HF, generally considered pre-HF, and was interpreted separately. Eleven studies reported prognostic associations, yet only 1 reported discrimination and reclassification metrics such as concordance index (C-index), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). External validation of diagnostic and prognostic performance was insufficient.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not support a unified heart failure-specific diagnostic framework for sarcopenia. Future work should include multicenter prospective cohort studies to establish HF-specific cut-off values, develop assessment protocols for acute decompensated HF and NYHA class IV patients, and conduct large-sample external validation of diagnostic and prognostic performance.

Title: Endovascular retrieval of bone cement entrapped in an inferior vena cava filter after percutaneous vertebroplasty: a case report.
Abstract: Percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) is widely used to treat osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures, however, bone cement leakage may enter the venous system and cause potentially serious embolic complications. Entrapment of migrated bone cement within an inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) is rare and may pose substantial technical challenges during filter retrieval. We report the case of a 67-year-old woman with bilateral deep vein thrombosis who underwent placement of a Denali retrievable IVCF after thrombus progression while receiving a nonstandard initial rivaroxaban regimen selected because of concern about bleeding risk. She subsequently underwent PVP for osteoporotic thoracolumbar compression fractures and returned 5 months after filter placement for elective retrieval. Pre-retrieval ultrasonography showed a patent inferior vena cava (IVC) but did not identify the intrafilter abnormality. Intraoperative inferior vena cavography revealed an obvious filling defect within the IVCF. A radiopaque shadow on fluoroscopy and retrospective review of prior PVP images suggested an impacted bone cement foreign body. Conventional retrieval through the right internal jugular vein failed. After reassessment of the procedural risks and discussion with the patient and her family, a 22F large-bore sheath was introduced through the femoral vein, and a temporary protective IVCF was deployed in the infrarenal IVC, caudal to the renal vein ostia and cephalad to the mobilized Denali filter-cement complex. The Denali retrievable IVCF and entrapped bone cement were retrieved en bloc through femoral venous access, and the protective filter was subsequently removed using the LOOP technique. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and had no fever, chest tightness, dyspnea, or abdominal pain. Follow-up computed tomography showed no hematoma, IVC stenosis, or IVC occlusion, and she was discharged in stable condition. This case highlights that, in patients with a history of PVP and an indwelling IVCF, intrafilter bone cement entrapment should be considered before planned filter retrieval. Careful review of previous fluoroscopic or interventional images, preoperative abdominal radiography followed by selective IVC CT venography (CTV) when radiopaque material is suspected, routine intraoperative cavography, preparation of large-bore sheaths and protective filters, and readiness for open surgical conversion may improve procedural safety.

Title: Impact of social determinants of health on perioperative and interstage outcomes in congenital heart surgery a systematic review.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Social determinants of health (SDoH)- conditions in which patients live, grow, and age,-are increasingly recognized to influence the health of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).
OBJECTIVE: To explore the impact of SDoH on short-term mortality and morbidity, interstage outcomes, and resource utilization, among patients following congenital heart surgery.
EVIDENCE REVIEW: A systematic review was completed according to PRISMA guidelines. Relevant studies evaluating the association of SDoH with surgical outcomes of pediatric and adult CHD patients were identified from five databases queried including PubMed, SCOPUS, CINAHL, PYSCINFO, and Cochrane between January 1999 and February 2024. Inclusion criteria incorporated prior systematic reviews and meta-analyses, secondary analyses of prospectively collected trial data, and prospective or retrospective cohort studies. Subsequent reference searches identified 39 related articles. SDoH included patient and neighborhood level metrics. Two independent reviewers screened studies for full-text review, with data extraction by an expert panel.
FINDINGS: Among 1,224 studies identified, 157 articles underwent full-text review and 121 were ultimately selected for data extraction. Eighty-Five articles did not address acute postoperative outcomes and were excluded. Thirty-six studies focused on acute or interstage outcomes following congenital heart surgery and served as the source information. The remainder were retrospective cohort studies using various databases. The number of study participants ranged from 98 to 174,352 (median = 6,979). Factors found to be linked with greater likelihood of in-hospital mortality included Black race, Hispanic/Latino ethnicity, Medicaid insurance, and lower neighborhood socioeconomic status. Both individual and neighborhood level determinants were associated with longer interstage periods, higher complication rates, as well as greater resource utilization and hospital readmissions. Two critical timespans for intervention to reduce inequities in care were the neonatal period and young adulthood.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: SDoH impact both acute and interstage outcomes in patients following surgery for CHD. Developing interventions to increase access to and engagement with quality care and out-of-hospital support may improve both short-term outcomes and reduce systems-level financial burden. Systematic Review Registration.

Title: Absolute stress myocardial blood flow is reduced in patients with prior cardiac disease despite normal perfusion and ejection fraction on rubidium-82 PET: an Arabian Gulf cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Rubidium-82 (⁸2Rb) PET is typically interpreted using perfusion category and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), but absolute myocardial blood flow (MBF) and flow reserve (MFR) may add information. We investigated whether absolute stress MBF differs between patients with and without prior cardiac disease when studies appear normal, in an Arabian Gulf population with high rates of diabetes and obesity. A secondary exploratory aim compared quantitative parameters between predefined PET categories.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 292 source-verified patients (mean age 63.1 ± 12.1 years; 56.8% male) who underwent adenosine-stress ⁸2Rb PET/CT, classified by the PET C-category system. The primary analysis compared, within normal-appearing studies (C1 perfusion with resting LVEF ≥ 50%; n = 84), those with prior cardiac disease (n = 38) and those without (n = 46). A secondary exploratory analysis compared these same 46 patients (Normal) with the remaining 246 (Abnormal). Analyses used Mann-Whitney U tests with Cohen's d and 95% confidence intervals, with Bonferroni correction.
RESULTS: Among normal-appearing studies, patients with prior cardiac disease had lower global stress MBF (2.25 vs. 2.99 mL/min/g; d = -0.78, 95% CI -1.22 to -0.33) and lower RCA stress MBF (2.25 vs. 3.29; d = -1.02, -1.47 to -0.56); rest MBF was also lower (d = -0.47, -0.91 to -0.04), whereas MFR (d = -0.37, -0.80 to 0.07), LVEF and LV volumes did not differ. In the secondary comparison, stress MBF and MFR separated the predefined categories comparably (DeLong Z = 0.89, p = 0.372) and both more strongly than LVEF (Z = 3.54, p < 0.001); because the categories are defined in part by these parameters, this represents relative separation within the classification scheme and not diagnostic accuracy.
CONCLUSIONS: In this Arabian Gulf cohort, patients with prior cardiac disease had lower absolute stress MBF despite normal perfusion category and ejection fraction. These exploratory findings support further prospective evaluation of absolute stress MBF as an adjunct to conventional PET interpretation. Because rest and stress flow fell together with a preserved ratio, and because haemodynamic, medication and infarct-related explanations could not be excluded, no mechanism is inferred.

Title: Efficacy and specific toxicity profiles of GPRC5D- versus BCMA-targeted bispecific antibodies in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: a meta-analysis of clinical trials and real-world studies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) experience poor outcomes following multiple lines of therapy. Available evidence has largely pooled disparate immunotherapy platforms. The present systematic review and meta-analysis was performed to describe, separately by target, the efficacy and toxicity spectra of BCMA×CD3-directed, GPRC5D×CD3-directed, and dual-target bispecific antibody therapy in RRMM, in order to inform toxicity monitoring and supportive-care planning.
METHODS: The Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and PubMed were systematically searched up to January 28, 2026, to identify clinical trials and real-world studies evaluating GPRC5D×CD3 or BCMA×CD3 bispecific antibodies and their combinations for RRMM. Methodological quality was appraised with the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies. Proportions and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled utilizing fixed-effects or random-effects models in R, selected according to heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies-comprising 13 single-arm clinical trials and 14 real-world investigations involving 4,045 patients-met the inclusion criteria. The pooled objective response rate (ORR) for bispecific antibodies in RRMM was 65.54%. Target-stratified subgroup analysis yielded an ORR of 78.51% for GPRC5D×CD3 combined with BCMA×CD3, 69.67% for GPRC5D×CD3 alone, and 60.85% for BCMA×CD3 alone. The pooled minimal residual disease-negativity rate was 23.6%. Regarding safety, distinct antigen-specific toxicity spectra emerged across different targets. The BCMA×CD3 group exhibited elevated incidences of any-grade infection (56.37%) and grade 3-4 infection (26.37%), accompanied by pronounced hematological toxicity. The GPRC5D×CD3 group was characterized by epithelium-related toxicity: the incidence of grade 1-2 taste-related changes was 69.89%, that of any-grade nail-related adverse events (AEs) was 42.33%, and that of any-grade non-rash skin-related AEs was 58.3%; however, grade 3-4 nail-related AEs reached only 0.21%, and grade 3-4 non-rash skin-related AEs reached only 0.33%. The dual-target group bore a substantial burden of infection (84.53%) and hematological toxicity.
CONCLUSION: Bispecific antibodies demonstrate clear antimyeloma activity in RRMM. BCMA×CD3-directed therapy is mainly related to infection and hematological toxicity, whereas GPRC5D×CD3-directed therapy is distinguished by epithelium-related toxicity, although severe events are rare.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/ identifier, CRD420261296139.

Title: Evidence, strategies, and pathways for thrombectomy in medium vessel occlusion stroke: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medium vessel occlusions (MeVOs) account for 25-40% of acute ischemic strokes and present a significant therapeutic frontier. Despite high technical success rates of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), recent randomized trial results have been nuanced, creating a paradox and underscoring the need for a precision-based approach.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. After screening, 42 original studies were included (4 RCTs and 38 cohort studies). Evidence was synthesized and appraised using a three-tiered hierarchy. The GRADE framework was applied. Overall certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.
RESULTS: Observational studies, which often enrolled populations with higher baseline NIHSS scores and stricter imaging selection criteria, generally reported favorable functional independence rates (mRS 0-2 in 60-80% of EVT-treated patients). However, these rates may partly reflect selection bias rather than a purely treatment-related effect. Successful recanalization is frequently achieved (>85%), but safety concerns like symptomatic hemorrhage and vessel perforation require careful management. Success hinges on a precision strategy integrating advanced imaging (e.g., CT perfusion for "Target Mismatch") with a tailored technical arsenal. This includes dedicated low-profile stent retrievers and aspiration catheters, selected based on occlusion site, thrombus burden, and anatomy. A "Eight Keys" framework interprets neutral trial results, highlighting patient selection heterogeneity. Future progress depends on refined imaging criteria, dedicated device development, and validated selection tools.
CONCLUSION: Current randomized evidence does not demonstrate an overall functional benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for unselected MeVO stroke, while procedure-related hemorrhagic risk appears higher than with best medical therapy. EVT may be reasonable in carefully selected patients with disabling deficits, salvageable tissue, and favorable anatomy, when performed by experienced teams using distal-appropriate techniques. Future work should prioritize validated selection tools, standardized imaging definitions, distal-specific devices, and trial designs enriched for patients most likely to benefit.

Title: Reading discordant bedside indices in sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: an evidence-mapping framework for diagnosis and trial design.
Abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) affects 20%-30% of patients with septic shock and independently predicts mortality, yet it lacks a consensus definition or validated reference standard. Bedside diagnostic indices-left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain, E/e', troponin level, and cardiac index-are frequently discordant, and no principled framework exists for interpreting this discordance. In parallel, every major pharmacological intervention targeting SICM, including levosimendan, corticosteroids, and beta-blockers, has failed to demonstrate consistent mortality benefit across randomised trials. Herein, we propose that both impasses may share a single root cause: a construct validity failure in which bedside indices used for diagnosis and trial enrolment do not reliably identify the specific pathophysiological processes that they are assumed to represent. We present a structured evidence-mapping framework that organises six bedside diagnostic methods against seven pathophysiological trait dimensions of SICM, grading the evidence for each combination against explicit criteria and identifying structural blind spots. The framework explains why index discordance is a diagnostic signal rather than a measurement error, identifies two dimensions-metabolic dysfunction and cardiac-specific inflammatory signalling-that are structurally invisible to all current bedside diagnostics and whose invisibility offers a testable explanation for repeated trial failures, and translates these insights into a three-step bedside reasoning framework. When LVEF is depressed but longitudinal function is preserved, the framework directs assessment towards ventriculo-arterial uncoupling rather than inotrope escalation; when right ventricular dysfunction predominates, it directs assessment towards reverse resuscitation. The framework reframes index discordance from a source of diagnostic paralysis into a source of clinical precision and defines the enrolment biomarker agenda required to make future SICM trials mechanistically interpretable.
