Title: Window leakage in clinical EEG machine learning: matched subject-independent evaluation across ADHD and Parkinson cohorts.
Abstract: Windowed electroencephalography (EEG) pipelines can produce misleadingly high performance when segments from the same participant occur in both training and testing. We define this contamination as window leakage and test it in two clinically and technically distinct public cohorts: 121 children (61 attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder [ADHD], 60 controls) and 149 adults (100 Parkinson's disease, 49 controls). Signals were harmonized to 18 common channels and 128 Hz. All primary models used stratified 8-fold participant-disjoint evaluation, 50%-overlapping windows, participant-level probability aggregation, and validation participants drawn exclusively from each outer-training fold. A deliberately contaminated Random Forest audit contrasted random-window and participant-disjoint splitting. Random-window balanced accuracy reached 95.59% in ADHD and 92.02% in Parkinson's, but fell to 60.98% and 56.17%, respectively, when participants were held out. Thus, the inflation replicated across disorders, ages, recording tasks, and acquisition systems. Under correct evaluation, CNN-LSTM achieved the highest ADHD subject-level balanced accuracy (73.21%), whereas EEGNet achieved the highest Parkinson's balanced accuracy (63.75%). No architecture comparison remained significant after Bonferroni correction. One-, 2-, 4-, and 8-s windows produced no consistent cross-cohort ranking. Removing ATCNN-SA components also yielded dataset-dependent changes, and no ablation difference was significant after correction. Participant-bootstrap intervals remained wide despite tens of thousands of windows, indicating that inferential precision was governed by participant count rather than segment count. Window-level random splits contaminate clinical EEG performance estimates and must not be used to claim generalization to unseen individuals. Participants should be separated before model fitting, results should be reported at subject level, and split, windowing, aggregation, and uncertainty procedures should be disclosed explicitly.

Title: Trajectory-based associations between a structured acupressure protocol, blood pressure variability, and autonomic balance in patients with primary hypertension.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a major global public health problem, with suboptimal rates of blood pressure control despite widespread pharmacological treatment. Beyond mean blood pressure levels, blood pressure variability (BPV) and autonomic nervous system imbalance, reflected by heart rate variability (HRV), have emerged as important predictors of cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to examine trajectory-based associations between a structured acupressure intervention, blood pressure variability, and autonomic balance in patients with primary hypertension.
METHODS: Participants received either structured acupressure (12 sessions over 4 weeks) plus usual care or usual care alone. Blood pressure variability was assessed using 24-hour ambulatory monitoring. Autonomic balance was measured via heart rate variability indices. Linear mixed-effects models estimated longitudinal trajectories. Mediation was tested using structural equation modelling.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, the intervention group showed greater reductions in systolic blood pressure variability (β = -1.92, 95% CI -2.78 to -1.06, p < .001). High-frequency heart rate variability increased (β = 84.60, 95% CI 47.60 to 121.60, p < .001), and the low/high-frequency ratio decreased (β = -0.42, 95% CI -0.60 to -0.24, p < .001). Exploratory mediation analysis identified a significant indirect association, suggesting that changes in autonomic balance may partially account for the observed relationship.
CONCLUSION: Structured acupressure was associated with favorable longitudinal changes in blood pressure variability and autonomic function compared with usual care. Mediation analysis suggested that changes in autonomic balance may partially account for the observed association; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because the quasi-experimental design does not allow causal inference. Randomized sham-controlled studies are required to confirm these findings.

Title: Association between insulin resistance-related indices and cardiovascular disease in patients with atopic dermatitis: mutual validation using real-world and NHANES data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The number of patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) who develop cardiovascular disease (CVD) has been increasing year by year. However, reliable biomarkers for identifying AD patients with a higher burden of prevalent CVD remain lacking.
METHODS: This study included patient data from the First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University from 2014 to 2023 and data from the U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), and CTI-body mass index (CTI-BMI) with prevalent CVD in patients with AD. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings. Seven machine learning (ML) models and SHAP analysis were applied to assess the discriminative performance of these indices for prevalent CVD status.
RESULTS: In the real-world dataset, 145 patients had prevalent CVD, whereas 75 participants had prevalent CVD in the NHANES dataset. Multivariable logistic regression analyses showed that, after adjustment for clinical covariates, all four indices were significantly and positively associated with prevalent CVD among patients with AD. These associations remained consistent across most subgroup analyses. Restricted cubic spline analyses showed no evidence of nonlinear associations, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Among the evaluated ML models, CTI-BMI demonstrated the highest discriminative performance for prevalent CVD status in both datasets and contributed most substantially to model discrimination.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated that TyG, TyG-BMI, CTI, and CTI-BMI were significantly associated with prevalent CVD among patients with AD. CTI-BMI showed the strongest discriminative performance among the evaluated indices and provided modest incremental discrimination when incorporated into machine learning models. These findings suggest that these indices may serve as potential adjunctive markers for cardiovascular burden assessment in patients with AD; however, further prospective studies are required to determine their value for predicting future cardiovascular events.

Title: Accelerating cardiovascular digital twin creation using precomputed virtual populations as Bayesian priors.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mechanistic lumped-parameter models of the cardiovascular system can provide insight into underlying physiological processes that cannot be measured directly. When tailored to an individual patient, these models have the potential to inform treatment for conditions such as heart failure. We aim to develop a robust and repeatable method of constructing a virtual population, defined as a collection of parameter sets that spans the full range of expected phenotypic variability of a population of interest. Such virtual populations can then accelerate patient-specific Bayesian inference by serving as a precomputed prior distribution to determine probabilistic cardiovascular digital twins.
METHODS: This work presents a Bayesian approach to establishing a virtual population based on population-level measurement data. It utilizes the DiffeRential Evolution Adaptive Metropolis (DREAM) algorithm to approximate a Bayesian posterior distribution consistent with the published clinical data of healthy populations (19 pressure and volume measurements across samples of at least 125 patients apiece). It subsequently applies weight-based allometric scaling of the resulting posterior parameter sets to more fully match target measurement variability. We applied this technique to a mechanistic hemodynamic model beginning with 23 parameters of interest. The final virtual population is then used to rapidly compute 17 proof-of-concept patient-specific digital twins, using patient data from an independent cohort not considered during virtual population development.
RESULTS: Our methodology effectively replicated at least 74.6% of the expected coverage of the target measurement distributions, with 17 of 19 measurements being represented at more than 80% of the expected coverage. Seventeen patient-specific digital twins were then computed from within this virtual population, with mean absolute percentage error across measurements for each patient ranging from 0.71% to 8.61% relative to the clinical measurement targets and a mean error across patients of less than 3%.
CONCLUSION: The proposed methodology represents a promising approach to developing a virtual population and demonstrates the feasibility of rapid posterior reweighting within such a precomputed virtual population, according to individual patient data. This computational proof-of-concept may help set the stage for future scalable creation of patient-specific digital twins to aid in clinical decision-making.

Title: Timing and Causes of Systemic Readmissions After Hip Fracture Surgery: An 8-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic readmissions after hip fracture surgery impose a substantial clinical and economic burden. Hip fracture represents a sentinel orthopedic injury with prolonged postoperative vulnerability extending beyond the index admission. Evidence from the Middle East remains scarce, particularly regarding the incidence, causes, and timing of systemic readmissions in multiethnic populations. This study aimed to determine the one-year incidence, etiologies, and temporal distribution of systemic readmissions following proximal hip fracture surgery, and to explore whether commonly documented comorbidities showed any association with systemic readmission.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary-care hospital in the Middle East from January 2017 to January 2025. Kaplan-Meier analysis was the primary method used to describe one-year systemic readmission-free survival, while logistic regression was performed on an exploratory basis.
RESULTS: Among 284 patients, 35 experienced systemic readmissions within one year (12.3%). Infectious (31.4%), cardiovascular (20.0%), and pulmonary (20.0%) complications were the most frequent etiologies. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a one-year systemic readmission-free survival of 87.7%, with most readmissions clustering between 90 and 180 postoperative days. No comorbidity-including American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class-was significantly associated with systemic readmission. Stratified survival curves showed no significant difference by ASA classification (log-rank p = 0.54).
CONCLUSION: Although no stable association between individual comorbidities and systemic readmission was identified in exploratory analyses, a distinct late postoperative vulnerability window (3-6 months) was identified. These findings provide important region-specific evidence and support the need for structured mid-term follow-up and multidisciplinary care pathways to reduce late systemic complications after hip fracture surgery. From an orthopedic perspective, these findings emphasize hip fracture surgery as the beginning of a prolonged recovery trajectory rather than an isolated surgical event.

Title: Excessive supraventricular ectopic activity and new-onset ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study with prospective outcome ascertainment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive supraventricular ectopic activity (ESVEA), a marker of both paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (pAF) and underlying atrial cardiomyopathy, may serve as an earlier electrographic predictor of cryptogenic ischemic stroke than pAF itself. This study aimed to investigate the association between ESVEA and the risks of new-onset ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality in an Asian population, and to explore a potential data-driven threshold that requires external validation.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study with prospective outcome ascertainment, data were collected from 446 patients without a history of atrial fibrillation or stroke across three hospitals in China. Based on the results of 24-h ambulatory ECG monitoring, patients in the top 15% of the cohort (premature atrial complex [PAC] rate ≥100 beats/24 h or paroxysmal atrial tachycardia [PAT] episode count ≥22 episodes/24 h) were defined as the ESVEA group; the remainder comprised the non-ESVEA group. The incidence of new-onset ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality was compared between groups during follow-up, after adjustment for confounding factors such as age and hypertension.
RESULTS: The median follow-up duration was 13 months. In a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model with a time-varying coefficient for age, using new-onset ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality as endpoints, after adjusting for other risk factors, ESVEA was significantly associated with new-onset ischemic stroke (HR:2.798; 95% CI:1.064 to 7.359; p = 0.037) and all-cause mortality (HR:7.584; 95% CI: 1.302 to 44.163; p = 0.024). In subgroup analysis, no significant interaction was observed between age groups for the effect of ESVEA on new-onset ischemic stroke. The rates of new-onset stroke in the ESVEA- group (without PAC/PAT), the ESVEA+/- group (with PAC/PAT not meeting ESVEA criteria), and the ESVEA+ group were 0.70, 5.90, and 16.30%, respectively, demonstrating a stepwise increase.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort study with prospective outcome ascertainment, ESVEA was associated with an increased risk of new-onset ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality in Asian subjects without prior stroke or AF. These exploratory findings suggest that ESVEA may be a useful risk marker, but require validation in larger prospective studies before clinical application.

Title: Comparison of hybrid coronary revascularization and minimally invasive multivessel CABG for multivessel coronary artery disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to compare the perioperative and early-to-mid-term outcomes of hybrid coronary revascularization (HCR) and minimally invasive multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG) for treating multivessel coronary artery disease (MVCAD).
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study including MVCAD patients who underwent HCR or MICS-CABG at Ruijin Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. The primary endpoint was the incidence of major perioperative complications within 30 days after surgery, including all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction (MI), and stroke. Secondary endpoints included 1-year all-cause survival and 1-year graft or target-vessel patency. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to reduce baseline imbalance between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to evaluate 1-year survival.
RESULTS: A total of 169 patients were included, of whom 91 underwent HCR and 78 underwent MICS-CABG. After 1:1 PSM, 132 patients remained, with 66 patients in each group. Major perioperative complications within 30 days after surgery were comparable. In the HCR group, MI occurred in 1 patient (1.52% vs. 0.00%; P = 1.000), stroke in 2 patients (3.03% vs. 0.00%; P = 0.476), and death in 1 patient (1.52% vs. 0.00%; P = 1.000), whereas no such events occurred in the MICS-CABG group. The MICS-CABG group had significantly longer operative time (250 vs. 160 min, P < 0.001) and greater 24-hour postoperative drainage (420 vs. 185 mL, P < 0.001). Postoperative respiratory complications were numerically more frequent after MICS-CABG. The 1-year survival rate was comparable between the HCR and MICS-CABG groups after PSM (98.5% vs. 98.4%; log-rank P = 0.996). The 1-year left anterior descending artery (LAD) revascularization patency rate was comparable between the HCR and MICS-CABG groups (94.6% vs. 90.0%; P = 0.366), as was non-LAD target-vessel patency (86.5% vs. 87.0%; P = 0.922).
CONCLUSIONS: HCR and MICS-CABG provided comparable perioperative safety, early-to-mid-term survival, and 1-year revascularization patency in selected patients with MVCAD. Treatment strategy may be individualized according to coronary lesion characteristics and cardiopulmonary function.

Title: From wrist to heart: clinical validation and real-world translation of wearable and portable AI-enhanced electrocardiography.
Abstract: Wearable and portable electrocardiogram (ECG) devices are shifting cardiovascular monitoring beyond clinician-directed testing, driven by consumer-led self-monitoring, remote care, and preventive cardiology. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance the value of these devices by supporting automated interpretation, but clinical translation remains uneven. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on AI-enhanced ECG (AI-ECG) analysis in wearable and portable systems, with emphasis on the gap between technical performance and real-world implementation. Although many advances have been developed using conventional 12-lead ECG datasets, deployment in wearable and portable devices introduces additional challenges related to device-specific signal acquisition, preprocessing, domain shift, and user-led recording. Evidence is most mature for atrial fibrillation detection, while applications across conduction disease, other arrhythmias, structural phenotypes, and prognostic assessment remain earlier in development and are supported by fewer prospective, device-specific evaluations. Across the field, retrospective and dataset-based studies predominate, with limited evidence that improved detection translates into better patient outcomes or health-system efficiency. Future research should evaluate performance using the intended device, population, and clinical pathway, and determine whether AI-ECG changes management without increasing unnecessary investigation or workload. Establishing clinical value, rather than improving classification accuracy alone, will determine the role of wearable and portable AI-ECG in routine cardiovascular care.

Title: Changes in birth certificate-reported prevalence of congenital anomalies at live birth during the COVID-19 pandemic: a nationwide study of 26 million United States live births.
Journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although the majority of studies have indicated that maternal severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination are not associated with neonatal birth defects, it is relevant to examine whether the disease burden changed during the COVID-19 pandemic, as other influencing factors may have also changed. We aimed to compare the birth certificate-reported prevalence of congenital anomalies at live birth before and during the pandemic.
METHODS: Using public birth data, all live births from 2016 to 2022 in the United States of America (USA) were retrospectively included. The birth certificate-reported prevalence at live birth of selected congenital anomalies identified from the birth certificate, including anencephaly, meningomyelocele/spina bifida, cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD), congenital diaphragmatic hernia, omphalocele, gastroschisis, limb reduction defect, cleft lip, cleft palate, Down syndrome, chromosomal disorder, and hypospadias, was estimated and compared by calendar year of birth using logistic regression.
RESULTS: A total of 26,345,765 live-born infants from 2016 to 2022 were included. The mean gestational age of the infants was 38.4 weeks (SD = 2.1 weeks), 48.9% were female babies, and 96.7% were singleton. The overall reported prevalence of congenital anomalies was highest in 2018 (3.51‰, 95%CI = 3.45‰-3.57‰) and has since shown a decreasing trend [3.38‰ (95%CI = 3.32‰-3.44‰) in 2019 and 3.35‰ (95%CI = 3.29‰-3.41‰) in 2022]. Using 2019 as a reference, it did not differ in 2020 and 2021 [odds ratio (OR) = 1.01 (0.98-1.03) and OR = 1.00 (0.98-1.03), respectively, after adjusting for maternal age, ethnicity/race, and socioeconomic status] and was slightly lower in 2022 [OR = 0.97 (0.95-0.99)]. For the majority of the congenital anomalies, the reported prevalence during the pandemic (2020-2022) remained unchanged or showed a decreasing trend (i.e., gastroschisis and Down syndrome) compared with that in 2019. The reported prevalence of CCHD was higher in 2021 and 2022 than in 2019. However, the increase had begun before the pandemic, and after correction for multiple comparisons, only the 2021 contrast remained significant. Segmented regression confirmed a significant pre-pandemic upward trend in CCHD with a level change dated to infants born in March 2020. When exposure was re-indexed by estimated year of conception, neither pandemic conception cohort differed from the 2019 conception cohort [2020: OR = 1.03 (0.97-1.09); 2021: OR = 1.02 (0.97-1.08)]. The direction of these results was consistent when stratified by gestational age (≥37 or <37 weeks), with wider intervals in the preterm stratum.
CONCLUSIONS: The birth certificate-reported prevalence of congenital anomalies at live birth did not increase during the COVID-19 pandemic in the USA and decreased for several specific anomalies. The higher reported prevalence of CCHD continues a trend that began before the pandemic and is null once exposure is aligned with organogenesis.

Title: TRPV4-linked oxidative-lysosomal stress in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion: disease-matched transcriptomics and functional analysis in OGD/R cardiomyoblasts.
Journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (MI/R) injury involves oxidative stress, lysosomal dysfunction, and altered autophagy. TRPV4 may link Ca2+ dysregulation to these processes, but its role in lysosomal membrane permeabilization (LMP) and autophagic impairment remains unclear.
METHODS: Three disease-matched mouse-heart GEO cohorts (GSE281940, GSE130217, and GSE160516) were analyzed using limma-based differential expression, prespecified oxidative, lysosomal, and autophagy-related gene sets, cross-cohort comparisons, and within-cohort correlations. H9C2 cardiomyoblasts subjected to OGD/R were used to examine intracellular Ca2+, ROS, LMP, autophagy-related changes, inflammatory cytokine release, and cell injury after pharmacological modulation of TRPV4 and ROS.
RESULTS: All three cohorts showed clear MI/R-associated transcriptional changes. Hmox1 was consistently increased across all five prespecified contrasts, whereas Trpv4 showed modest, time-dependent changes without reaching FDR-adjusted significance. Trpv4 was positively correlated with Map1lc3b in all three cohorts (Spearman ρ = 0.73-0.83, nominal P < 0.05), while associations with oxidative and lysosomal genes were more variable. In H9C2 cardiomyoblasts, OGD/R increased TRPV4 mRNA expression, intracellular Ca2+, and ROS levels. TRPV4 inhibition reduced ROS accumulation, attenuated LMP-related changes, and decreased LC3B and p62 accumulation, whereas TRPV4 activation produced the opposite effects. NAC attenuated TRPV4 activation-induced ROS and lysosomal injury, while t-BHP partially reversed the effects of TRPV4 inhibition. OGD/R also increased IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α release, which was reduced by TRPV4 inhibition.
CONCLUSION: The transcriptomic data indicate a context-dependent TRPV4 response within a conserved MI/R stress background. The H9C2 cardiomyoblasts experiments support the involvement of the TRPV4-ROS-LMP pathway in lysosomal injury, impaired autophagic degradation, inflammatory responses, and OGD/R-induced cardiomyoblast injury.

Title: Serum free eicosapentaenoic acid-to-arachidonic acid ratio and long-term risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The eicosapentaenoic acid to arachidonic acid (EPA/AA) ratio reflects the balance between n-3 and n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids. We examined the association between the serum free (non-esterified) EPA/AA ratio and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with angiographically confirmed coronary artery disease (CAD).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 308 patients with CAD. Serum free fatty acids were quantified by LC-MS/MS, and the free EPA/AA ratio was evaluated as the primary fatty-acid biomarker. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs), and principal component analysis (PCA) was used to explore fatty-acid patterns.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 48.7 months, 201 first MACE events occurred. In the fully adjusted primary analysis, each 1-SD increase in the free EPA/AA ratio was associated with a lower risk of MACE (HR = 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.96, P = 0.011; FDR-adjusted P = 0.049). The association was attenuated after additional adjustment for analytical batch (HR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.77-1.10, P = 0.375) and in a Cox model stratified by batch (HR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.77-1.11, P = 0.398).
CONCLUSIONS: A higher serum free EPA/AA ratio was associated with a lower risk of MACE in the primary multivariable analysis, but the association was attenuated in additional sensitivity analyses. These findings should be interpreted cautiously and require validation in independent cohorts.

Title: The associations between dynapenic obesity and cognitive disorder in older hypertension patients: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding the associations between dynapenic obesity and cognitive disorder in older adults is limited. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of cognitive disorder among the older patients with hypertension (HTN), explore the association between dynapenic obesity and cognitive disorder, and explore a hypothesized path structure.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional study from July 2023 to March 2024 among the older HTN patients aged 65 years and older. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and standardized measurement. Logistic regression models were used to test the association between dynapenic obesity and cognitive disorder. Multiple imputation by chained equations under a missing-at-random assumption was conducted. Structural equation modeling was employed to explore the hypothesized path analysis. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to validate the robustness of the findings.
RESULTS: The study included 9,568 older HTN patients. The prevalence of cognitive disorder in this population was 15.67% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 14.94-16.40%). After adjusting for potential confounders, a significant positive association was observed between dynapenic obesity and cognitive disorder (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.418, 95% CI: 1.263-1.591). In the path model, dynapenic obesity was associated with lower odds of adequate physical activity (PA) (aOR = 0.708, 95% CI: 0.640-0.783). Adequate physical activity was associated with lower odds of depressive disorders (aOR = 0.441, 95% CI: 0.367-0.529) and cognitive disorder (aOR = 0.521, 95% CI: 0.452-0.601). Participants with depressive disorders had higher odds of cognitive disorder than those without depressive disorders (aOR = 1.312, 95% CI: 1.031-1.669). This association remained consistent across different age groups (all p < 0.05). Almost all results of sensitivity analysis were consistent with the main findings.
CONCLUSION: Dynapenic obesity was positively associated with cognitive disorder. PA and depressive disorders were regarded as variables within a hypothesized cross-sectional path structure.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: A systematic review of mortality and long-term functional outcomes after decompressive craniectomy for acquired brain injury: The missing rehabilitation reporting.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive craniectomy (DC) is a surgical procedure for refractory intracranial hypertension following severe acquired brain injury (sABI) and is an effective, life-saving treatment. However, there is significant controversy regarding its impact on long-term functional outcome. Furthermore, the role of postoperative rehabilitation in shaping recovery after DC has been largely overlooked in the literature.
OBJECTIVES: To systematically review randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the long-term functional outcomes of DC in patients with sABI, stratified by underlying etiology, with particular attention to the assessment tools employed, their alignment with the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, and the reporting of post-operative rehabilitation data.
METHODS: We searched PubMed and Scopus for all RCTs related to DC published between 2000 and 2024. Eligible studies included adults (≥18 years) who underwent DC for acute brain injury and reported at least one functional outcome measure (GOS-E, mRS, GOS, or Barthel Index). Outcomes were dichotomized into favorable and unfavorable categories. A narrative summary was performed because of the substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity.
RESULTS: We included 16 RCTs (1803 participants) in our analysis. The etiologies included traumatic brain injury, intracerebral hemorrhage, acute subdural hematoma, and malignant cerebral infarction. DC was associated with lower overall mortality compared to those not receiving it (24% vs. 31%). However, in 8 RCTS, a higher proportion of patients with DC had unfavorable functional outcomes. All outcome scales mapped exclusively to the ICF domain of "Activities and Participation", while any assessment of cognitive function, emotional well-being, social participation, or quality of life was reported. Rehabilitation was largely unmeasured rather than necessarily absent: Only one study reported any rehabilitation data, limited to the number of patients admitted to inpatient rehabilitation. Most RCTs reported outcomes at 6 months or before; only one RCT extended the follow-up period to 24 months.
CONCLUSIONS: DC is an effective, life-saving procedure that reduces mortality and has an etiology-dependent effect on functional outcomes. Available functional outcome measures do not adequately capture the multifaceted nature of recovery following severe brain injury. Crucially, the post-DC rehabilitation trajectory is not captured by current trials; this argues for the routine, prospective collection of rehabilitation data in future RCTs to determine the contribution of postoperative rehabilitation to long-term functional recovery rather than against the use of a life-saving procedure.

Title: Night-to-night sleep variability and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a prospective cohort study with a complementary in vitro circadian-disruption experiment.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Irregular sleep-wake patterns may disrupt circadian rhythms, but the dose-response relationship between night-to-night sleep variability and mortality and the association of sleep onset variability with death remain unclear.
METHODS: Using 4-7 valid days of wrist accelerometer data, including ≥1 weekend day, from 7,604 adults aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2011-2014, linked to mortality through December 2019, we examined the within-person SDs of sleep midpoint, sleep onset, and total sleep time across nights and the sleep regularity index (SRI) in relation to all-cause and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality. Survey-weighted Cox models were fitted across 20 imputed datasets and combined using Rubin's rules. Restricted cubic splines examined dose-response relationships. Complementary categorical, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) experiments repeated in three independent runs compared cellular responses under a regular dexamethasone schedule and four prespecified irregular schedule variants.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 81 months, 714 all-cause and 229 CVD deaths occurred. Each 1-hour increase in the across-night SD of sleep midpoint, sleep onset, and total sleep time was associated with all-cause mortality HRs of 1.22 (95% CI, 1.12-1.33), 1.19 (1.11-1.29), and 1.17 (1.05-1.31), respectively. The corresponding CVD mortality HRs were 1.21 (1.09-1.35), 1.22 (1.05-1.42), and 1.16 (0.94-1.42), respectively. Each 10-point lower SRI was associated with all-cause mortality (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.21-1.38) and CVD mortality (HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.18-1.45). Across three independent HUVEC runs, the mean response across the four prespecified irregular schedule variants showed lower core clock-gene expression, lower Griess assay absorbance, and higher inflammatory and adhesion-marker expression than the regular schedule.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater night-to-night sleep irregularity was associated with higher hazards of all-cause and CVD mortality, although these associations were modest compared with those of older age, hypertension, and diabetes in the same models. The complementary cellular experiment showed differences between the regular dexamethasone schedule and the prespecified irregular schedule set.

Title: Maternal risk factors for hypertension in pregnancy: A quantitative study on the role of demographics, obesity, and healthcare compliance.
Abstract: Hypertension in pregnancy is a major contributor to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. This study examined the associations between maternal risk factors and hypertension in pregnancy. A prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Wonoayu Health Center, Sidoarjo, Indonesia, from November 2024 to January 2025. Fifty-seven pregnant women with a gestational age of at least 28 weeks and a positive mean arterial pressure screening result were recruited through consecutive sampling. Data were collected from medical records, interviews, adherence cards, physical examinations, blood pressure measurements, and proteinuria tests and analyzed using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression. Maternal age (p = 0.022; adjusted OR = 11.848; 95% CI: 1.422-98.739) and adherence to calcium lactate supplementation (p = 0.021; adjusted OR = 0.371; 95% CI: 0.160-0.858) were significantly associated with hypertension in pregnancy. Maternal age and adherence to calcium lactate supplementation may be important factors associated with hypertension in pregnancy.

Title: Incremental diagnostic value of coronary CT angiography-derived pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics for identifying hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) radiomics may complement coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-based anatomical and physiological assessment. This study aimed to evaluate its incremental diagnostic value for identifying hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis.
METHODS: This retrospective study screened 21,438 consecutive patients and included 81 patients with 107 target vessels who underwent CCTA, invasive coronary angiography, and invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) measurement within 30 days. Patients were allocated at the patient level to training and validation cohorts in a 7:3 ratio. A radiomics score (Radscore) was developed from lesion-specific PCAT features using training-only preprocessing and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression. Models incorporating diameter stenosis (DS), CCTA-derived FFR (CT-FFR), fat attenuation index (FAI), and Radscore were evaluated against invasive FFR ≤0.80 using patient-cluster bootstrap inference.
RESULTS: The training and validation cohorts comprised 57 and 24 patients with 75 and 32 vessels, respectively, without patient overlap. In validation, Radscore alone had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.684 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.451-0.873). CT-FFR+ Radscore showed higher discrimination than CT-FFR alone (AUC, 0.879 vs. 0.762; difference, 0.117; 95% CI, 0.005-0.229; P = 0.041), as did DS+ Radscore vs. DS alone (AUC, 0.812 vs. 0.619; difference, 0.193; 95% CI, 0.018-0.367; P = 0.030). The FAI comparison was not significant (P = 0.238). At training-derived cutoffs, CT-FFR+ Radscore had lower sensitivity (50.0% vs. 78.6%) and negative predictive value (69.6% vs. 81.3%) but higher specificity (88.9% vs. 72.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: Adding Radscore was associated with higher discrimination for CT-FFR and DS in internal validation but did not uniformly improve threshold-dependent classification. Independent external validation is warranted.

Title: Radial artery characteristics before and after intra-arterial administration of nitroglycerin and verapamil: an optical coherence tomography study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radial artery dimensions before and after intra-arterial vasodilator administration remain incompletely characterized along the vessel. This study used optical coherence tomography (OCT) to assess paired changes in mean lumen diameter.
METHODS: Twelve patients underwent baseline OCT 5 min after limited sheath insertion and post-administration OCT after intra-arterial nitroglycerin and verapamil, before coronary angiography. The full OCT-imaged radial artery span was divided into equal proximal, middle, and distal thirds before selecting anatomically matched analyzable portions. Analysis included 1,482 matched cross-sectional pairs (2,964 frames), with a cumulative matched analyzable length of 1,404.4 mm. Measurements at matched 1-mm intervals were aggregated within patients. Mean lumen diameter was the representative lumen metric; area and volume were supportive measurements.
RESULTS: Mean lumen diameter increased from 3.06 ± 0.49 to 3.35 ± 0.56 mm (mean paired change, 0.29 mm; 95% CI, 0.20-0.39; P < 0.001). The mean patient-level relative increase was 9.6%. Mean increases were observed in all three thirds in exploratory analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Mean radial artery lumen diameter was greater after intra-arterial nitroglycerin and verapamil than at baseline.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://www.chictr.org.cn/hvshowproject.html?id=270,922&v=1.1, Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) ChiCTR2500097574.

Title: The CKM-GDM multi-organ precision model: reframing gestational diabetes as an early cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic event in Southeast Asia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is amongst the commonest complications of pregnancy and an early marker of lifetime cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) risk. Its burden is heavy in Southeast Asia, where prevalence ranges from about 8% to nearly 30% and a lean phenotype - with marked over-representation of the insulin-secretion-limited subtype - diverges from Western cohorts, yet its definition, timing, and treatment remain contested.
AIM: This clinically oriented narrative review synthesises the diagnostic landscape, the shift to early diagnosis, the vascular mechanism, and precision care, centred on Southeast Asia.
KEY THEMES: Competing criteria (IADPSG one-step, WHO 2013, NICE, ADA two-step and the pragmatic Indian DIPSI test) identify different populations. The TOBOGM trial shows that early (pre-20-week) treatment improves outcomes, and first-trimester biomarkers-low adiponectin and sex-hormone-binding globulin, glycosylated fibronectin, atherogenic lipids, and multimarker or machine-learning panels including a non-fasting Asian-women panel-show potential to make early prediction feasible. Vascular and endothelial dysfunction (oxidative stress, eNOS uncoupling, sFlt-1/PlGF imbalance, and arterial stiffness) is proposed as the unifying early signal and a mechanistic bridge to later type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and chronic kidney disease. GDM is increasingly recognised as heterogeneous (insulin-resistant, insulin-deficient, and mixed subtypes), inviting subtype- and phenotype-guided precision diagnosis and treatment.
CONCLUSION: We propose that GDM may be productively reframed as an early, vascular, and potentially precisely treatable CKM event-screened early, matched to phenotype and linked to lifelong follow-up, and fitted to the epidemiology, genetics, and health systems of Southeast Asia. This reframing is a testable hypothesis that requires prospective validation before routine adoption.

Title: High-fat diet and portal hypertension: a triangulation approach combining Mendelian randomization with retrospective clinical analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portal hypertension is a major complication of chronic liver disease, but the causal role of dietary factors, particularly high-fat diet, remains unclear due to confounding in observational studies. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between high-fat diet and portal hypertension using a triangulation approach combining Mendelian randomization (MR) and retrospective clinical analysis.
METHODS: We conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomization analysis using summary-level genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for dietary fat intake (n = 268,922) and portal hypertension-related traits. Eighteen independent SNPs served as genetic instruments (mean F-statistic = 34.2, collectively explaining 2.8% of phenotypic variance). Inverse variance weighted (IVW), weighted median, MR-Egger regression, and mode-based methods were employed. Sensitivity analyses included MR-Egger intercept test, Cochran's Q statistic, MR-PRESSO, and leave-one-out analysis. Additionally, a retrospective cross-sectional clinical study was conducted on 72 patients with portal hypertension who underwent hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) measurement.
RESULTS: MR analysis provided evidence consistent with a causal association between genetically predicted high-fat diet and increased risk of portal hypertension (IVW OR = 1.28 per SD increase, 95% CI: 1.15-1.42, p = 1.0 × 10-5). Results were consistent across multiple MR methods. Sensitivity analyses showed no evidence of directional pleiotropy (MR-Egger intercept p = 0.178), significant heterogeneity (Cochran's Q p = 0.241), or MR-PRESSO-detected outliers (global test p = 0.312). In the clinical cohort, high-fat diet score was positively correlated with HVPG (r = 0.700, p < 0.001), and this association remained significant after multivariate adjustment (β = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.52-1.18, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Using a triangulation approach, we found consistent evidence from both Mendelian randomization and retrospective clinical analysis that a high-fat diet is linked to increased portal pressure. These complementary findings strengthen the overall evidence base and highlight the potential importance of dietary fat modification in portal hypertension management.

Title: SGLT2 inhibitors as a strategy for volume management in peritoneal dialysis: a case series.
Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits in chronic kidney disease, yet their role in peritoneal dialysis (PD) remains largely unexplored, and clinical experience is limited. We describe, at the individual-patient level, seven consecutive patients treated with an SGLT2i at a single centre (median age 69 years, range 43-73; five men; one with type 2 diabetes; six dapagliflozin, one empagliflozin). The PD prescription was not modified during treatment, and ultrafiltration refers to the 24-hour drained volume. In the four patients in whom the drug was added to established, unchanged PD, ultrafiltration rose in three and fell in one; the single non-responder was also the only low-average transporter and was later transferred to haemodiafiltration. Both patients anuric at baseline increased their ultrafiltration, and in one of them PD was the only feasible modality. Peritoneal transport category was unchanged wherever paired equilibration tests were available. Serum urate fell in the patients with preserved diuresis but not in those who were anuric, whereas the largest ultrafiltration gain occurred in a patient anuric throughout, dissociating the peritoneal response from any renal effect. The erythropoietin resistance index fell in all treated patients, although the magnitude was clinically relevant in a minority and must be read alongside the haemoglobin trajectory. No patient developed anuria de novo. One patient died of fungal peritonitis in the context of documented non-adherence, an event reported here with its mechanistic implications. These observations support a direct peritoneal mode of action and warrant prospective evaluation with surveillance for fungal infection.

Title: Transaxillary access for ascending aortic and root surgery: a single-center comparison with full and partial sternotomy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive approaches for ascending aortic and root surgery remain controversial regarding operative complexity and safety. The transaxillary (TAX) approach avoids sternotomy entirely but has not been compared with both full sternotomy (FS) and partial upper sternotomy [minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MIC)]. This study evaluates perioperative outcomes across these three access strategies.
METHODS: Between January 2022 and December 2025, 194 consecutive patients undergoing elective isolated ascending aortic or root surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Surgical access was FS (n=52), MIC (n=106), or TAX (n=36). TAX suitability was assessed by team consensus on electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated computed tomography (CT). Primary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, major complications [Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) composite], and hospital length of stay. TAX was compared with MIC after 1:2 propensity score matching. FS served as descriptive reference.
RESULTS: FS patients had higher EuroSCORE II (median 2.7 vs. MIC 2.2 vs. TAX 2.3%, P=0.006). Cardiopulmonary bypass time was longer in TAX {196 [interquartile range (IQR): 175-239] vs. MIC 160 [138-192] vs. FS 172 [140-198] min, P<0.001}, while cross-clamp time did not differ (P=0.34). In-hospital mortality was 3.8% (FS), 0% (MIC), and 0% (TAX). Major complications occurred in 26.9%, 12.3%, and 8.3% (P=0.02), and acute kidney injury (AKI) in 28.8%, 8.5%, and 2.8% (P<0.001). One stroke occurred in the FS group. In the matched cohort (34 TAX vs. 68 MIC), bypass time remained longer in TAX {196 [175-240] vs. 160 [139-190] min, P<0.001}, whereas cross-clamp time, intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital stay, major complications (5.9% vs. 11.8%), AKI (2.9% vs. 10.3%), atrial fibrillation, and wound complications did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: TAX ascending aortic and root surgery was feasible in carefully selected patients, with no in-hospital mortality, no stroke, and no wound complications. In a propensity-matched comparison with partial upper sternotomy, early outcomes did not differ significantly despite longer bypass time. TAX extends the sternal-sparing concept to the aortic root and ascending aorta and warrants prospective evaluation.

Title: Cannabinoids in oncology: pharmacology, clinical applications, and translational perspectives.
Abstract: Cannabis and cannabinoid products are increasingly used by patients with cancer for symptom management and supportive care. Although cannabis is widely used to alleviate cancer- and treatment-related symptoms, many patients also believe that it possesses direct anticancer activity. This review provides a comprehensive pharmacologic and clinical assessment of cannabinoids in oncology, integrating the endocannabinoid system, cannabinoid receptor signaling, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic applications, adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, and emerging antitumor research. The strongest clinical evidence supports selected cannabinoid preparations for refractory chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, whereas evidence for cancer-related pain, appetite stimulation, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and opioid-sparing effects remains limited or inconsistent. Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) differ substantially in receptor pharmacology, psychoactive effects, metabolism, and toxicity, with important implications for product selection, dosing, and interactions with anticancer and supportive-care medications. Preclinical studies demonstrate antiproliferative, proapoptotic, antiangiogenic, and immunomodulatory effects across multiple tumor models; however, cannabinoid signaling is highly context dependent and may also promote tumor progression in selected settings. Human evidence for direct anticancer activity remains sparse, consisting predominantly of small early-phase studies and observational data, with no established improvement in tumor response, progression-free survival, or overall survival. Particular caution is warranted regarding neuropsychiatric and cardiovascular toxicity, pharmacokinetic drug interactions, and the potential influence of cannabis on immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Overall, cannabinoids have defined but limited roles in supportive oncology, while their direct antitumor potential remains investigational. Future studies should prioritize standardized formulations, pharmacologically informed dosing, rigorous randomized designs, clinically meaningful endpoints, and biomarker-based approaches to define therapeutic benefit and risk.

Title: Early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke: an explainable model based on routine clinical data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate early prediction of 3-month functional outcome after acute ischemic stroke is essential for prognostic communication, early management planning, and resource allocation. However, clinically applicable and interpretable prediction tools based on routinely collected data remain limited.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective prediction-model study, we analyzed 770 adults with acute ischemic stroke admitted within 24 h of symptom onset. Baseline clinical and early laboratory variables were collected. After an 80/20 train-test split, key predictors were selected using cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) in the training set. Several supervised learning models were developed and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated. The final gradient boosting machine (GBM) model was interpreted using TreeSHAP, and an online Shiny-based calculator was developed.
RESULTS: LASSO identified 12 predictors. Test-set discrimination was similar across models, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.854 to 0.867. The final GBM achieved AUCs of 0.910 in the training set and 0.872 in the test set, with corresponding areas under the precision-recall curve of 0.814 and 0.741. Calibration was satisfactory in both sets. SHAP analyses identified NIHSS, age, and C-reactive protein as dominant contributors, showing predominantly non-linear effects with limited interaction strength.
CONCLUSION: An explainable model based on routinely collected clinical data showed good discrimination and calibration in internal validation for predicting 3-month functional outcome after AIS. Independent external validation is required before the model can be considered for clinical application.

Title: Cardiovascular outcomes of oral incretin-based drugs in type 2 diabetes: a GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of 67,679 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: While injectable GLP-1 receptor agonists like semaglutide have demonstrated clear cardiovascular benefits in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), the role of oral incretin-based therapies, including oral semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors-remains less well defined. Comprehensive evaluation of their cardiovascular efficacy is warranted.
RESEARCH QUESTION: What are the cardiovascular outcomes associated with oral incretin-based therapies, specifically oral semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors, in patients with T2DM compared to placebo or standard care.
METHODS: We searched electronic databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Meta-analysis was conducted in R version 4.4.3 using the "meta" and "metasens" packages. Statistical analysis was performed using R software and RStudio (version 4.4.2). We calculated pooled estimates using risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 9 studies comprising 67,679 patients were included, of which two evaluated oral semaglutide and the remaining seven assessed DPP-4 inhibitors. There was no significant reduction in all-cause mortality (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90-1.04, p = 0.35) or cardiovascular death (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91-1.05, p = 0.48). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) showed a non-significant reduction overall (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-1.00, p = 0.06), with oral semaglutide demonstrating a significant benefit (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.95, p = 0.003). Non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI) (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.88-1.09) and non-fatal stroke (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.83-1.03) were not significantly affected. Hospitalizations due to heart failure (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.84-1.13) and unstable angina (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.15) remained unchanged. Coronary revascularization was slightly reduced with oral semaglutide (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.91). Adverse events leading to discontinuation were higher with oral semaglutide (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.15-1.98), while serious adverse events were significantly reduced (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99, p = 0.003). Sensitivity analyses were conducted due to significant heterogeneity in key outcomes. While omitting certain studies reduced heterogeneity, the overall results remained consistent.
CONCLUSION: Oral incretin-based therapies were not associated with significant reductions in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, or MACE overall, though oral semaglutide showed a significant MACE benefit and reduced coronary revascularization on subgroup analysis. Non-fatal MI, fatal or non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke, fatal or non-fatal stroke and hospitalization due to heart failure or unstable angina were unaffected, and oral semaglutide carried a higher risk of treatment discontinuation. These findings suggest no clear class-wide cardiovascular benefit of oral incretins, with signals specific to oral semaglutide warranting confirmation in dedicated trials.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251113835.

Title: Efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided microwave "Near-Total Ablation" for refractory hyperthyroidism: a retrospective study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The current study aims to investigate the efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided microwave "Near-Total Ablation" in the treatment of refractory hyperthyroidism, with a particular focus on the postoperative drug-free euthyroidism rate and the incidence of hypothyroidism.
METHODS: A total of 60 patients with refractory hyperthyroidism who met the clinical diagnostic criteria for refractory hyperthyroidism were enrolled in this study. All patients underwent ultrasound-guided microwave "Near-Total Ablation" targeting the bilateral thyroid lobes and isthmus.
RESULTS: Of the 60 enrolled patients, 57 were included in the postoperative follow-up, while 3 were excluded. The postoperative follow-up duration ranged from 6 to 36 months, with a mean of 10.6 ± 4.6 months. During follow-up, 35 patients achieved hyperthyroidism remission (remission group), with a remission rate of 61.4%, while 22 patients had unrelieved hyperthyroidism (non-remission group), with a non-remission rate of 38.6%. In the remission group, 4 patients with decreased thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and 8 patients with recurrent hyperthyroidism received one session of supplementary ablation. In the non-remission group, 18 patients received one session of supplementary ablation, 3 patients received two sessions, and 1 patient received three sessions. At the final follow-up, the remission rate of hyperthyroidism was 98.2% (56/57), with a non-remission rate of 1.8% (1/57). The rate of drug-free euthyroidism was 68.4% (39/57), and the incidence of hypothyroidism was 29.8% (17/57). The recurrence rate of hyperthyroidism was 17.5%, and the incidence of major complications was 3.5% (2/57).
CONCLUSION: Microwave "Near-Total Ablation" is a safe and effective method for the treatment of refractory hyperthyroidism, with a high postoperative euthyroidism rate and a low incidence of hypothyroidism. This technique is expected to become an alternative to surgical thyroidectomy for hyperthyroidism.

Title: A NET-associated immunothrombotic phenotype is associated with coronary no-reflow and myocardial injury after primary PCI in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a real-world translational cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary no-reflow after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) reflects failure of myocardial reperfusion despite treatment of the culprit epicardial lesion. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and immunothrombosis provide a plausible link between sterile inflammation, thrombus biology, and microvascular obstruction. We evaluated whether a clinically measurable NET-associated immunothrombotic phenotype (NET-IP) was associated with no-reflow and myocardial injury after primary PCI.
METHODS: This single-center translational cohort included 742 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary PCI. NET-IP was calculated in 725 patients from five admission or pre-PCI variables-neutrophil count, D-dimer, fibrinogen, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and platelet-neutrophil product-by averaging log-transformed component z scores when at least four components were available, followed by standardization of the composite score. The primary endpoint was angiographic no-reflow, defined as final thrombolysis in myocardial infarction flow grade < 3 in the absence of mechanical epicardial obstruction. A case-enriched nested enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) biomarker subcohort was used to measure MPO-DNA, citrullinated histone H3 (H3Cit), and double-stranded DNA.
RESULTS: Angiographic no-reflow occurred in 110 of 742 patients. NET-IP was calculable in 725 patients, and the fully adjusted complete-case models included 700 patients. Patients with no-reflow had higher admission NET-IP scores than those with normal reflow (0.73 [0.24, 1.25] vs. -0.06 [-0.77, 0.54]; P < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, NET-IP remained associated with angiographic no-reflow (OR per SD, 1.96; 95% CI, 1.46-2.62; P < 0.001) and tissue-level reperfusion failure (OR per SD, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.32-2.02; P < 0.001). In the case-enriched ELISA subcohort, adjusted associations with no-reflow were observed for MPO-DNA (OR per SD log2, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.26-2.81; P = 0.002) and H3Cit (OR per SD log2, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.33-3.02; P < 0.001), whereas double-stranded DNA was weaker after adjustment (P = 0.074). NET-IP was also associated with higher peak high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I, higher peak creatine kinase-MB, lower discharge left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), large myocardial injury, and discharge LVEF < 50%.
CONCLUSION: A NET-IP was linked to impaired coronary reperfusion and myocardial injury after primary PCI in STEMI. The findings support NET-associated immunothrombosis as a clinically measurable immune phenotype but do not establish direct NET burden, causal mediation, or immediate clinical treatment guidance.

Title: Comparative midterm outcomes of contemporary revascularization strategies for acute lower limb ischemia: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute lower limb ischaemia (ALLI) is a vascular emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Contemporary revascularization strategies include open surgery,endovascular intervention,and hybrid approaches,yet comparative midterm outcomes remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: We conducted a single - center retrospective cohort study of 842 consecutive patients with ALLI treated at Xinxiang City Central Hospital between January 2019 and December 2023,with follow - up complete through May 2026.Patients underwent open surgery(n = 452),endovascular intervention(n = 198),or hybrid procedures (n = 192). Baseline characteristics, peri-operative outcomes, and long - term events were collected. The pre - specified primary outcome was the composite of major amputation and/or all-cause mortality at 3 years. Secondary outcomes included individual components, peri-operative mortality, acute kidney injury, and re-intervention. Multivariable Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were applied, together with propensity score inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The mean age was 74 ± 13, 70 ± 12,and 71 ± 13 years in the open, endovascular, and hybrid groups, respectively. Endovascular treatment was associated with lower peri - operative mortality (adjusted OR 0.32,95% CI 0.15-0.68, p = 0.003) and reduced acute kidney injury (OR 0.48,95% CI 0.25-0.92,p = 0.027).Over a median follow - up of 34 months (IQR 28-41),cumulative 3 - year major amputation rates were 11.6%, 21.9%, and 13.5%,and all - cause mortality 24.1%,12.8%,and 20.3% in the open, endovascular, and hybrid groups,respectively.In adjusted competing-risk regression, endovascular treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard of major amputation (sHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.49-0.97, p = 0.034); however, this association was model-dependent and contrasted with the higher crude amputation incidence observed in the endovascular group. Endovascular treatment was also associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint of major amputation and/or all-cause mortality (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.56-0.90, p = 0.006), whereas hybrid approaches did not differ significantly from open surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for ALLI offers improved peri - operative safety and favorable midterm composite outcomes compared with open surgery in this observational cohort. Hybrid strategies demonstrate intermediate results. These findings support individualized treatment selection, but definitive causal inferences are limited by the non - randomized design and potential residual confounding.

Title: Serum MGP and ECP are commonly elevated in first-onset and recurrent ischemic stroke: a two-phase DIA proteomic study in a Chinese cold-region cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) has a high recurrence rate, yet effective biomarkers for distinguishing first-onset from recurrent IS remain limited. This study aimed to identify serum proteomic biomarkers commonly elevated in both first-onset and recurrent IS and to evaluate their ability to discriminate each disease state from healthy controls in a Chinese cold-region population.
METHODS: The study was conducted in two phases. In the discovery phase, 10 patients with first-onset IS, 10 with recurrent IS, and 10 healthy controls were analyzed using Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA) proteomics; the validation phase expanded the sample to 49 patients with first-onset IS, 30 with recurrent IS, and 50 healthy controls. Differentially expressed proteins were defined as fold change≥1.5 or ≤0.67. Multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for age and sex constructed diagnostic models, with data randomly split into training and test sets (2:1) for receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: Two core proteins were identified: matrix Gla protein (MGP) and eosinophil cationic protein (ECP). Both were significantly elevated in the first-onset and recurrent IS groups compared with healthy controls (all p < 0.05). Two separate logistic models incorporating these proteins discriminated first-onset IS (test-set AUC 0.993) and recurrent IS (test-set AUC 0.959) from healthy controls, confirmed by repeated 10-fold cross-validation; the two proteins did not differ significantly between the patient groups. Enrichment analysis of their interaction partners revealed involvement in neutrophil extracellular trap formation, inflammatory responses, and immune regulation.
CONCLUSION: Serum MGP and ECP were commonly elevated in both first-onset and recurrent IS, and two separate combinatorial models discriminated each disease state from healthy controls with high accuracy. This biomarker panel covers three core pathological processes-atherosclerosis and vascular calcification, chronic inflammation, and hypercoagulable state-providing candidate biomarkers that warrant further investigation for disease-state characterization and risk stratification, particularly in high-latitude cold-region populations.

Title: Interpretable deep learning and radiomics for predicting the occurrence of brain metastases following prophylactic brain irradiation in small cell lung cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain metastasis remains an important clinical concern in patients with small cell lung cancer (SCLC), even after prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI). Accurate identification of patients at high risk of brain metastasis after PCI may facilitate individualized surveillance and management. This study developed a fusion model based on two-and-a-half-dimensional (2.5D) multi-channel deep learning features, clinical features, and radiomics features to predict whether patients with SCLC will develop brain metastases following PCI.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 185 patients with SCLC who underwent PCI and randomly divided them into a training set (N=148) and a testing set (N=37). A 2.5D multi-channel convolutional neural network (CNN) model was constructed based on multi-planar regions of interest (ROI) derived from CT images to extract 2.5D deep learning features. Based on the largest cross-section and three-dimensional (3D) volume of the tumor ROI, two-dimensional (2D) and 3D deep learning features were extracted, respectively. Subsequently, features from different dimensions were fused with clinical features and traditional omics features to construct the 2D_clinic_Rad, 2.5D_clinic_Rad, and 3D_clinic_Rad models, respectively. The performance differences between the 3D models and the clinical and traditional radiomics models were then compared.
RESULTS: The 2.5D_clinic_Rad fusion model demonstrated the best performance in predicting brain metastases, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.841 on the test set, outperforming clinical models, traditional radiomics models, and 2D and 3D deep learning fusion models. Analysis of decision curves and calibration curves indicated that the 2.5D_clinic_Rad model demonstrated the highest clinical net benefit and the best calibration consistency compared to other models.
CONCLUSIONS: The fusion model based on 2.5D_clinic_Rad can effectively predict the risk of brain metastasis in patients with SCLC following whole-brain prophylactic irradiation.

Title: Vietnamese expert consensus on the diagnosis and multidisciplinary management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved rapidly from a surgery-centered approach toward biomarker-informed, multimodality care integrating staging, pathology, surgery, perioperative systemic treatment, and postoperative surveillance. In Vietnam, implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions, particularly in access to fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT), invasive mediastinal staging, molecular testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. This project aimed to develop a Vietnamese multidisciplinary expert consensus to contextualize contemporary international evidence for clinical practice in Vietnam.
METHODS: A structured, modified Delphi-informed consensus process was conducted in Vietnam between August 2025 and January 2026. The workflow comprised seven stages: scoping; a baseline practice survey; initial draft development; expert review of parts 1 and 2; post-meeting written feedback, revision, electronic recirculation, and formal voting for these sections; a multidisciplinary consensus meeting and formal voting for parts 3 and 4; and editorial harmonization and consolidation. The panel included specialists in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, respiratory medicine, pathology, nuclear medicine, radiation oncology, and related disciplines. Classes of recommendation were adapted from the European Society of Cardiology framework. All statements submitted to formal consensus voting were formally rated, with consensus predefined as at least 75% agreement.
RESULTS: The final document comprised 35 consensus statements across four domains: preoperative diagnosis and staging (n=7), surgery and postoperative surveillance (n=8), neoadjuvant and perioperative treatment (n=12), and adjuvant treatment (n=8). Across the meeting rosters, 32 unique experts were identified, with strong representation from thoracic surgery and medical oncology. The baseline survey and expert discussions highlighted implementation gaps in FDG-PET/CT, invasive mediastinal staging, biomarker testing, perioperative therapy, pathology standardization, and multidisciplinary review. All 35 consensus statements met the predefined threshold, with agreement ranging from 82% to 100%.
CONCLUSIONS: These consensus statements provide a multidisciplinary, evidence-informed framework for the diagnosis and management of resectable NSCLC across the perioperative pathway. By contextualizing international evidence within Vietnamese clinical practice, the document may help improve consistency of care, support biomarker-guided and multimodality treatment, and strengthen multidisciplinary decision-making across institutions.

Title: Efficacy and safety of osimertinib combined with anlotinib in EGFR-mutant non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer with gradual progression after first-line osimertinib therapy: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osimertinib, a third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), has substantially improved clinical outcomes in patients with EGFR-mutant non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Nevertheless, acquired resistance inevitably develops, leading to disease progression in the majority of patients. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that anlotinib, a multi-targeted anti-angiogenic TKI, may overcome osimertinib resistance. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of continued osimertinib in combination with anlotinib in patients with EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC who developed gradual progression following first-line osimertinib therapy.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable stage III or IV EGFR-mutant non-squamous NSCLC who received first-line osimertinib therapy at The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China between January 2021 and December 2024. Eligible patients developed gradual progression after first-line osimertinib therapy. Subsequently, patients received combination therapy with osimertinib (80 mg orally once daily) plus anlotinib (10 mg orally on days 1-14 of every 3-week cycle). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included PFS rates at 6 and 12 months, objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS), OS rates at 12 and 24 months, and safety profile.
RESULTS: A total of 52 patients were enrolled. The median age was 66 years. 40(76.9%) had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) of 0-1, 16 (30.8%) presented with brain metastases, 23 (44.2%) harbored exon 19 deletions, and 29 (55.8%) had L858R mutations. Molecular testing was performed in 12 patients after gradual progression. As of September 6, 2025, the median follow-up was 34.8 months, 48 PFS events were recorded and 22 patients died. The ORR was 7.7% (4/52), and the DCR was 86.5% (45/52). The median PFS (mPFS) was 9.9 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 4.2-12.1], with PFS rates of 61.5% at 6 months and 40.4% at 12 months. The median OS was not reached. OS rates were 86.3% at 12 months and 62.4% at 24 months. The exploratory multivariate COX analysis revealed that ECOG PS [hazard ratio (HR): 3.115, 95% CI: 1.111-7.706, P<0.001] and brain metastasis (HR: 2.242, 95% CI: 1.341-7.842, P=0.009) were associated with mPFS. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 9.6% (5/52) of patients. The most frequently observed AEs were diarrhea (42.3%, 22/52), hypertension (34.6%, 18/52), proteinuria (30.8%, 16/52), decreased appetite (28.8%, 15/52), and weight loss (28.8%, 15/52).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort focusing on the specific pattern of gradual progression following first-line osimertinib therapy, continued osimertinib combined with anlotinib demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity, which warrants further evaluation in prospective comparative studies.

Title: Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy-guided three-dimensional conformal microwave ablation for unresectable peripheral high-risk pulmonary nodules: a mid-term assessment with no real-time intraoperative CT/cone-beam computed tomography guidance.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical resection is the gold standard for high-risk pulmonary nodules; however, many patients are not candidates for surgery or who decline surgery. Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy-guided three-dimensional conformal microwave ablation (ENB-DCMA) is a promising minimally invasive option. This study aimed to assess the mid-term safety and efficacy of a novel ENB-DCMA strategy which employs three-dimensional conformal planning to offset respiratory-induced lesion displacement.
METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, we enrolled consecutive patients with peripheral high-risk pulmonary nodules who received ENB-DCMA owing to unsuitability for or refusal to surgery and radiotherapy between March 2021 and August 2023. The three-dimensional conformal strategy enlarged the ablative margin to compensate for respiratory-induced target motion exploratively, in the absence of real-time intraoperative computed tomography/cone-beam computed tomography (CT/CBCT) guidance. The primary efficacy endpoint was local progression-free survival (LPFS) post-ablation. Safety was evaluated according to the incidence of adverse events.
RESULTS: In total, 50 patients with 62 eligible pulmonary nodules were included, with 65 ablation procedures performed in total, including repeated ablation for three lesions. The technical success rate of this procedure was 95.2%. No procedure-related mortality was observed. The median follow-up was 37.1 (range, 14.7-59.9) months. The overall 3-year LPFS rate was 82.3%, and this rate reached 95.8% among patients with sub-solid nodules. The overall incidence of adverse events was 18.0% (9/50), including 12.0% (6/50) pneumothorax, 2.0% (1/50) postoperative fever, and 4.0% (2/50) self-limiting pulmonary hemorrhage; the rate of events requiring intervention was 4.0% (2/50).
CONCLUSIONS: ENB-DCMA serves as a safe and feasible minimally invasive therapeutic option for patients with high-risk pulmonary nodules. Further multicenter prospective trials are required to verify its long-term outcomes and broader clinical popularization value.

Title: Surgery that looks like transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the transaxillary concept for minimally invasive aortic valve replacement in 1,848 consecutive patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transaxillary (TxA) approach for minimally invasive aortic valve replacement (MICS-AVR) is a sternum-sparing technique that combines surgical valve replacement with virtually no visible scarring. We report institutional outcomes of the first 1,848 consecutive TxA MICS-AVR procedures.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included all consecutive patients undergoing isolated TxA MICS-AVR between January 2019 and June 2026. Patients with active endocarditis, redo surgery, or concomitant procedures were excluded. Primary endpoints were 30-day mortality and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Univariable and multivariable logistic regression explored associations with adverse outcomes.
RESULTS: Mean age was 67.7±8.1 years, Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Operative Mortality (STS-PROM) 1.39%±2.90%, and European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) 1.65%±1.12%. TxA use among surgical treatments for isolated aortic valve disease rose from 18.8% in 2019 to 99.2% in 2025. Mean operative, cardiopulmonary bypass, and cross-clamp times were 132±34, 69±23, and 43±16 minutes. No intraoperative death occurred; 1.6% required conversion to sternotomy. Thirty-day mortality was 0.5%, and MACCE occurred in 1.6%, including stroke in 0.9% and myocardial infarction in 0.5%. In multivariable analysis, mortality associations were strongest for insulin-treated diabetes [odds ratio (OR) 8.56], left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <40% (OR 8.45), and intraoperative transfusion (OR 17.86); corresponding MACCE associations included insulin-treated diabetes (OR 3.06), coronary artery disease (OR 2.46), peripheral arterial disease (OR 3.23), sternotomy conversion (OR 5.33), and transfusion (OR 5.49). These outcomes accompanied rapid institutional adoption of the technique, while operative efficiency remained favorable and the need for sternotomy conversion stayed low throughout the cohort. Given only 10 deaths and 30 MACCEs, multivariable findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.
CONCLUSIONS: Across 1,848 consecutive procedures, TxA MICS-AVR showed excellent reproducibility and safety. As long-term evidence increasingly supports surgical valve replacement in patients with extended life expectancy, TxA uniquely combines durable surgery with a cosmetic result comparable to transcatheter therapy, offering a scalable and strategically relevant platform for contemporary aortic valve care.

Title: Comparative effectiveness of acupuncture combined with rehabilitation for post-stroke hemiplegia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemiplegia, as a common sequela of stroke, can severely affect patients' quality of life. Although rehabilitation therapy can improve neurological function and motor abilities, a single therapy often has limited effectiveness in meeting the comprehensive rehabilitation needs. Clinical observations have demonstrated that the integration of acupuncture with rehabilitation therapy yields significant synergistic benefits. However, given the paucity of direct comparative studies between distinct combination therapies, the optimal treatment regimen remains to be definitively established. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of rehabilitation combined with different acupuncture techniques in treating patients with post-stroke hemiplegia using a network meta-analysis (NMA).
METHODS: We systematically searched eight databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) related to acupuncture combined with rehabilitation (ACU + RT) for post-stroke hemiplegia, with the searched period from database inception to March 5, 2026. The included literature was analyzed using Bayesian NMA with R software version 4.5.0.
