RESULTS: This study included 71 RCTs, involving 6,121 patients and nine interventions. The NMA results indicated that for Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) efficacy, the top three interventions were floating acupuncture combined with rehabilitation (FACU + RT), warm needle moxibustion combined with rehabilitation (WNM + RT), and moxibustion combined with rehabilitation (MOX + RT). However, according to the SUCRA ranking, WNM + RT emerged as the most likely optimal intervention (SUCRA = 76.06%; MD = 16.1, 95%CI: 9.25 to 23.1). Regarding Barthel Index (BI) scores, scalp acupuncture combined with rehabilitation (SA + RT) ranked first (MD = 17.4, 95%CI: 7.47 to 27.1; SUCRA = 86.20%), followed by ACU + RT and MOX + RT. In terms of Modified Barthel Index (MBI) scores, FACU + RT demonstrated the highest efficacy (MD = 16.4, 95%CI: 2.88 to 29.9; SUCRA = 87.87%), followed by MOX + RT and electroacupuncture combined with rehabilitation (EA + RT). Finally, for Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) scores, SA + RT was ranked first (MD = -1.10, 95%CI: -2.05 to -0.15; SUCRA = 78.38%), with MOX + RT ranking second.
CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates that combining different acupuncture methods yields varying therapeutic effects. Regarding the improvement of FMA scores, WNM + RT may be considered the preferred clinical regimen due to the limited evidence supporting FACU + RT (based on a single study). Furthermore, SA + RT proves most effective for improving BI scores and reducing MAS, while FACU + RT exhibits potential benefits for MBI scores. However, as the number of studies reporting MAS data is relatively small (5 cases), the robustness of this result still needs to be further confirmed in future research.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: CRD420261334951, https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261334951.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study

Title: Transaxillary minimally invasive mitral valve surgery: early and mid-term outcomes in 763 patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transaxillary (TAxA) approach has been developed as a simplified direct-vision minimally invasive access for heart valve surgery. We report a large single-center cohort of patients undergoing TAxA minimally invasive mitral valve surgery and evaluate early safety, procedural efficacy, recovery and mid-term outcomes.
METHODS: Consecutive patients who underwent TAxA mitral valve surgery at the University Hospital of Marche, Ancona, Italy, between January 2017 and April 2026 were included. Mitral repair or replacement procedures were considered with or without concomitant tricuspid valve repair, atrial fibrillation ablation or left atrial appendage occlusion. Early outcomes were analyzed in the overall cohort. Mid-term survival and reoperation were assessed in patients undergoing repair for degenerative mitral regurgitation.
RESULTS: The study included 763 patients. Mitral valve repair was performed in 640 patients and replacement in 123. The repair rate was 89% in patients with mitral regurgitation and 92% in patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. Concomitant tricuspid repair, atrial fibrillation ablation and left atrial appendage occlusion were performed in 17%, 5% and 10% of patients, respectively. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were 103 and 63 minutes. Thirty-day mortality was 0.4%, stroke or transient ischemic attack occurred in 0.7%, and conversion to sternotomy was required in 0.7%; no conversion was due to poor exposure. Median ventilation time was 2 [interquartile range (IQR), 0-6] hours, 54% of patients were extubated in theatre and 80% were extubated within 6 hours. Median intensive care unit and hospital stays were 24 (IQR, 22-48) hours and 7 (IQR, 6-9) days. In the degenerative repair cohort, Kaplan-Meier survival was 97.0% at 5 years, and cumulative incidence of reoperation was 4.3% at 5 years.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large contemporary experience, TAxA minimally invasive mitral valve surgery was associated with low early mortality and morbidity, reasonable operative times, frequent ultra fast-track extubation, and satisfactory mid-term results.

Title: Associations of the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) with myocardial injury markers in patients with coronary heart disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI) is a potential cardiovascular risk indicator. Its association with contemporaneous myocardial injury in coronary heart disease (CHD) patients remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the association between AISI and elevated myocardial injury markers and evaluate its discriminatory performance.
METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective study of consecutive CHD patients, AISI was calculated at admission. The patients were assessed at admission and before coronary angiography. Elevated cTnT was defined as >0.014 ng/mL and elevated CK-MB as >24 U/L. Logistic regression, subgroup analyses, ROC curves, and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used.
RESULTS: Significant differences across AISI tertiles were observed in adverse profiles. In multivariable-adjusted models, each unit increase in continuous AISI was associated with higher odds of elevated cTnT (OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.10, 1.55, p = 0.003) and elevated CK-MB (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02,1.17, p = 0.01). Compared with T1, T3 showed a significantly increased risk of elevated cTnT (OR = 3.14, 95% CI: 1.93,5.12, p < 0.01). Subgroup analyses revealed that AISI was more strongly associated with cTnT elevation in patients aged <70 years and in men, while the association with CK-MB was more evident in women and those aged ≥70 years. ROC analysis demonstrated moderate predictive value for cTnT (AUC = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.69, 0.75) and limited value for CK-MB (AUC = 0.65). RCS identified a nonlinear relationship with cTnT (P for nonlinearity = 0.0016), with an inflection point at 212.41.
CONCLUSION: Elevated AISI is independently associated with myocardial injury biomarkers in CHD patients, particularly for cTnT elevation, with a nonlinear threshold effect near 212.4. This association varies by age and sex, suggesting that AISI may serve as a simple, cost-effective adjunctive marker for identifying CHD patients at risk of myocardial injury.

Title: Beyond conventional anthropometry: Muscle-related indicators and muscle strength in adults with congenital heart disease: A retrospective study with a comparison group.
Journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
Abstract: Anthropometric characteristics and muscle strength remain insufficiently characterized in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). The aim of the study was to characterize anthropometric indicators and muscle strength in hospitalized adults with CHD and examine differences according to cardiac lesion complexity. Exploratory comparisons with adults without CHD were performed as secondary analyses. This cross-sectional study included 109 hospitalized adults with CHD and an external convenience group of 115 adults without CHD. Body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), triceps skinfold thickness (TSF), mid-arm muscle circumference (MAMC), arm muscle area (AMA), corrected arm muscle area (cAMA), and handgrip strength (HGS) were assessed. Cardiac defects were classified as mild, moderate, or complex. Associations of lesion complexity and previous cardiac surgery with anthropometric indicators and HGS were examined using multivariable linear regression. Comparisons with adults without CHD were conducted as exploratory analyses using the same approach. Among adults with CHD, 57.8% had mild, 24.8% moderate, and 17.4% complex defects. Lesion complexity was associated with MAMC (P = 0.032); participants with complex defects had lower MAMC than those with mild defects (B = -2.44 cm; 95% CI: -4.26 to -0.63). Previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. In adjusted exploratory comparisons, adults with CHD had lower weight, height, BMI, MUAC, MAMC, AMA, and HGS than adults without CHD, whereas TSF was similar. Values below reference ranges for BMI, MUAC, MAMC, cAMA, and HGS were more frequent in CHD. Greater lesion complexity was associated with lower MAMC, whereas previous cardiac surgery was associated with higher BMI, MUAC, MAMC, and AMA. Muscle-related anthropometric measures and HGS may provide complementary information beyond body size and adiposity in adults with CHD.

Title: Minimally Invasive Hematoma Evacuation for Acute Spontaneous Supratentorial Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a severe form of stroke associated with high morbidity and mortality. While surgical evacuation aims to reduce hematoma burden and improve outcomes, its clinical benefit over medical management remains uncertain. Previous systematic reviews have evaluated a broad range of surgical interventions for ICH; however, evidence specific to MIS remains less clearly defined. Therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the efficacy and safety of minimally invasive hematoma evacuation in patients with acute spontaneous supratentorial ICH.
METHODS: This meta-analysis was performed in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and Cochrane recommendations. A comprehensive search of MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov was conducted from inception to February 2026. We included randomized controlled trials that compared minimally invasive hematoma evacuation with medical or conventional surgical management. Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) were pooled using a random-effects model.
RESULTS: A total of 12 RCTs involving over 2302 patients were included. Minimally invasive hematoma evacuation significantly reduced all-cause mortality (RR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.97; p = 0.02) and 6-month mortality (RR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.64-0.96; p = 0.02). No significant differences were observed in 7-day or 30-day mortality, although a trend favoring the intervention was noted. Functional outcomes, including mRS 0-1 and mRS 0-3, did not improve significantly. Among secondary outcomes, minimally invasive approaches were associated with greater hematoma volume reduction (MD = 62.47; p = 0.04) but also a higher risk of rebleeding (RR = 2.37; p = 0.002) and cardiac events (RR = 5.08; p = 0.009). No significant differences were found in ischemic stroke, renal failure, gastrointestinal bleeding, seizures, urinary tract infections, or length of hospital and ICU stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive hematoma evacuation significantly decreases mortality in patients with spontaneous ICH, especially with endoscopic techniques; however, it does not markedly enhance functional outcomes and may elevate the risk of complications such as rebleeding and cardiac events. These results underscore the necessity for meticulous patient selection and additional high-caliber trials to enhance treatment strategies.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD/MASH: approved therapies, drug repurposing, and emerging mechanism-based candidates.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASLD/MASH) pharmacotherapy is changing rapidly after the approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for selected adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis; management must also address obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular risk, and kidney disease.
AREAS COVERED: This structured narrative review evaluates approved, comorbidity-directed, repurposed, and emerging therapies according to mechanism, regulatory status, endpoint strength, safety, interactions, and implementation. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched without a lower date limit through September 2026 and supplemented by U.S. and European regulatory documents, society guidance, randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected mechanistic studies. Therapies include thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonism, incretin and glucagon-containing agonists, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor pathways, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition, de novo lipogenesis/fatty acid synthase inhibition, fibroblast growth factor 21 analogues, lipid/remnant pharmacology, farnesoid X receptor signaling, antioxidants, and lower-evidence repurposing candidates.
EXPERT OPINION: Resmetirom and semaglutide anchor approved MASH-directed treatment in eligible F2-F3 disease, while comorbidity-directed therapy should be individualized by liver stage and cardiometabolic priorities. Tirzepatide, FGF21 analogues, denifanstat, and rational combinations may broaden treatment, but cross-trial comparisons and surrogate endpoints require cautious interpretation.

Title: The Impact of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Bleeding and Thrombotic Risks in Diabetic Patients Following Coronary Stent Implantation: A Prospective Study.
Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the 12-month clinical outcomes of short-term versus extended dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) in diabetic patients following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation.
METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, 536 diabetic patients undergoing DES implantation were categorized into short-term (< 6 months, n = 312) or extended (≥ 6 months, n = 224) DAPT groups based on actual treatment duration. Primary endpoints were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization) and BARC type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding events at 12 months.
RESULTS: Extended DAPT significantly reduced the incidence of MACE compared to short-term therapy (7.8% vs. 10.5%; HR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.53-0.98, p = 0.033), primarily driven by lower rates of target vessel revascularization (3.1% vs. 5.1%; p = 0.030). While overall bleeding rates did not differ significantly between groups (8.1% vs. 6.2%; p = 0.192), extended DAPT was associated with a significantly higher risk of recurrent bleeding in patients with a prior bleeding history (HR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.20-3.60, p = 0.011).
CONCLUSION: Extended DAPT effectively mitigates ischemic risks in diabetic patients following stent implantation without significantly increasing overall clinically significant bleeding. However, clinicians should prioritize individualized DAPT durations, specifically avoiding extended regimens in patients with a history of bleeding to minimize the risk of hemorrhage recurrence.

Title: Influence of Metabolic Syndrome on Peri-Implant Tissue Health and Disease: A Comparative Evaluation of Clinical, Radiographic, and Red Complex Microbiological Parameters.
Journal: Journal of long-term effects of medical implants
Abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a systemic human health condition characterized by obesity, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and insulin resistance, all of which may compromise peri-implant tissue health and contribute to peri-implant disease. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of MetS on peri-implant clinical, radiographic, and microbiological parameters one year after functional implant loading, with relevance to public health and implant-related wellbeing. This case-control study was conducted at the Department of Implantology, Saveetha Dental College, Chennai, India, from March to December 2024. Ninety-eight systemically screened, periodontally healthy adults (35-65 years) with functional dental implants were enrolled and divided into MetS (n = 49) and non-MetS groups (n = 49) based on NCEP ATP III criteria. Clinical parameters [Plaque Index (PI), Gingival Index (GI), probing pocket depth (PPD), and clinical attachment level (CAL)], radiographic crestal bone level (CBL), and the prevalence of Porphyromonas gingivalis, Tannerella forsythia, and Treponema denticola (via PCR analysis) were assessed. Statistical analyses were performed using independent t-test and Chi-square test (P < 0.05). MetS patients exhibited significantly higher PI (2.4 ± 0.3), GI (2.5 ± 0.2), PPD (6.5 ± 1.3 mm), CAL (7.2 ± 1.2 mm), and CBL loss (2.6 ± 0.4 mm) than non-MetS participants (all P = 0.00). Microbiological analysis revealed higher detection of P. gingivalis (59.2% vs. 10.2%), T. denticola (28.6% vs. 2.0%), and T. forsythia (22.4% vs. 4.1%) among MetS cases, with significant group differences (P ≤ 0.01). MetS is associated with greater peri-implant plaque accumulation, inflammation, bone loss, and colonization by red complex pathogens, underscoring its potential role as a risk indicator for peri-implantitis.

Title: Dual-track Parallel and Integrated Innovation: Recent Advancements of Clinical Decision Support Systems in Cardiovascular Diseases from the Perspective of Integrative Chinese and Western Medicine.
Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading causes of death worldwide, have a growing disease burden, and present multiple challenges for precision management. Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) are tools that leverage information technology to assist clinicians in diagnosis and treatment decisions and provide references for clinical decision-making by offering personalized suggestions, prompts, or reminders. By integrating multisource data, evidence-based guidelines, and artificial intelligence algorithms, CDSS can support diagnosis, prescribing, and comorbidity management. Studies in hypertension have reported improvements in prescribing and blood pressure, while effects on major cardiovascular events and mortality require further evaluation. Notably, with the continuous development of informatization and digitalization of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), traditional Chinese medicine clinical decision support systems (TCM-CDSS), as an innovative achievement integrating traditional medicine with modern information technology, have shown promise in supporting the prevention and treatment of CVDs. TCM-CDSS achieves an intelligent diagnosis and treatment closed loop from "syndrome differentiation" to "formula recommendation" by integrating TCM theory of "principles, methods, formulas, and medicinals," renowned TCM experts' clinical experience, TCM knowledge graphs, and intelligent syndrome differentiation algorithms, providing a new paradigm for individualized diagnosis and treatment of CVDs such as hypertension and coronary heart disease (CHD). However, reviews addressing the integration of Chinese and Western medicine in cardiovascular CDSS remain limited. To address this knowledge gap, this review adopts a conceptual framework of "dual-track parallel and integrated innovation" to systematically elaborate on the current application status of CDSS across major CVDs. We critically stratified current clinical evidence tiers, highlighting the widespread reliance on retrospective studies and the urgent need for large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Furthermore, we propose that the future paradigm lies in mechanism-data, dual-driven hybrid architectures that quantitatively anchor Western physiological indicators to TCM macrosyndromes. Finally, we provide targeted solutions for the core technical bottlenecks, including Electronic Health Record workflow integration, cross-system comorbidity management, and grassroots application feasibility. These results provide an important reference for the precise treatment of CVDs and a basis for developing new paradigms for CVD prevention and treatment.

Title: Impact of Socioeconomic Status and Rurality on the Rate of Prenatal Detection of Major and Critical Congenital Heart Disease in Western Australia.
Journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
Abstract:
AIM: Prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) is associated with reduced infant morbidity and mortality. Location and subsequent socioeconomic status influence rates and timing of prenatal diagnoses of CHD. We investigated the impact of socioeconomic status and rurality on the rate of prenatal diagnosis of critical and major CHD in Western Australia (WA).
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study reviewed all critical (surgical intervention ≤ 30 days of life) and major (surgical intervention ≤ 1 year of life) CHD in WA between 2017 and 2021. Patients were identified from the WA Fetal Cardiology and Perth Children's Hospital Cardiology Databases. Clinical records were used to identify diagnoses, outcomes, postcode, rurality (via the Modified Monash Model [MMM]) and socioeconomic status (Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas [SEIFA] Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage). Postcode was used to estimate SEIFA index and MMM rurality.
RESULTS: There were 478 cases with major CHD; 282 (59%) were prenatally diagnosed, of which 268 cases were critical CHD, with a 77% detection rate. Seventy-four percent of patients were from metropolitan areas. The distribution of SEIFA decile (p = 0.15) and MMM (p = 0.09) were not significantly different between pre- and postnatal groups. The diagnosis rate of univentricular CHD was 94% (n = 102) and 49% (n = 180) for CHD undergoing biventricular repair.
CONCLUSION: Critical CHD increases the likelihood of prenatal diagnosis in WA; however, rurality and socioeconomic status were not found to influence diagnosis rates. Further studies are needed to review the availability of obstetric services in rural communities to ensure equitable healthcare.

Title: High Yield of Pharmacogenetic Testing for Clopidogrel Resistance in a Canadian Outpatient Stroke Population.
Journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel is commonly prescribed for secondary stroke prevention, but routine pharmacogenetic testing is not typically performed. As the CYP2C19 enzyme activates clopidogrel into its effective form, clopidogrel-treated patients who carry CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles may face an increased risk of recurrent stroke. We examined the prevalence of CYP2C19 loss-of-function variants and their potential influence on patient management within a Canadian stroke clinic population.
METHODS: We randomly selected and invited outpatients attending a regional stroke prevention clinic in Toronto, Canada, who had a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack and were prescribed clopidogrel for secondary stroke prevention. Participants completed a self-administered home DNA test (cheek swab) to determine their CYP2C19 status. The primary outcome was the prevalence of intermediate or poor metabolizers. The secondary outcome was the proportion of participants whose antiplatelet regimen was changed as a result of the testing.
RESULTS: Among 93 eligible participants who underwent the test (mean age 68.1; female 37.6%), 31 (33.3%) were intermediate metabolizers, 8 (8.6%) were poor metabolizers, 20 (21.5%) were rapid metabolizers, 9 (9.7%) were ultrarapid metabolizers and 25 (26.9%) were normal metabolizers. In 8 (100.0%) of the poor metabolizers and 20 (64.5%) of the intermediate metabolizers, treating physicians changed their antiplatelet prescriptions based on the test results.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort of post-stroke patients treated with clopidogrel, genetic testing showed a high prevalence (41.9%) of intermediate or poor clopidogrel metabolizers, resulting in a change in antiplatelet therapy prescriptions in over 70% of those cases. These findings have implications for secondary stroke prevention.

Title: Neurological Assessment Tools and Inflammatory Biomarkers for Predicting Cerebral Palsy in Neonatal HIE.
Journal: Pediatrics international : official journal of the Japan Pediatric Society
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate temporal changes in serum interleukin-40 (IL-40), hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α), and procalcitonin (PCT) levels between early and post-rewarming measurements in neonates with moderate-to-severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) undergoing therapeutic hypothermia (TH), and to determine the prognostic value of these biomarkers together with the Hammersmith Neonatal Neurological Examination (HNNE), amplitude-integrated electroencephalography (aEEG), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for predicting cerebral palsy (CP).
METHODS: Thirty-five neonates with HIE treated with TH and 20 healthy term neonates were prospectively enrolled. Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels were measured before and after TH. Associations between biomarkers, HNNE, aEEG, MRI findings, and CP at follow-up were evaluated.
RESULTS: Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels decreased significantly between the early and post-rewarming measurements (all p < 0.001). Although biomarker levels differed from controls, they were not associated with subsequent CP. In contrast, HNNE, aEEG, and MRI showed strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP among surviving infants.
CONCLUSION: Serum IL-40, HIF-1α, and PCT levels showed significant temporal decreases between the early and post-rewarming measurements in neonates with HIE undergoing TH; however, these biomarkers did not predict subsequent CP among surviving infants. HNNE, aEEG, and MRI each demonstrated strong prognostic performance for subsequent CP when evaluated individually in this cohort.

Title: Transition-Specific Associations of Cardiometabolic Biomarker Burden With Cardio-Renal-Metabolic Multimorbidity Progression: A Multistate Cohort Study.
Abstract:
AIMS: To identify representative cardiometabolic biomarkers and examine how individual biomarkers and combined biomarker burden are associated with transition-specific progression of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM).
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 262 464 UK Biobank participants free of cardiovascular disease (CVD), type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline. Forty-nine candidate biomarkers across five domains, including inflammation, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, adiposity and blood pressure, were evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve and concordance index to select representative markers. Multistate models estimated associations of individual biomarkers, elevated-marker count and a weighted 5-Item Cardiometabolic Risk Score (5-CMRS) with sequential transitions from baseline to first cardio-renal-metabolic disease (FCRMD), FCRMD to Double CRMD and Double to Triple CRMD.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.62 years, 44 339 participants developed FCRMD, 7218 progressed to Double CRMD and 721 progressed to Triple CRMD. Five representative biomarkers were selected: C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR), triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio, waist-to-height ratio and systolic blood pressure. Higher elevated-marker count showed graded associations across all transitions. Compared with the lowest 5-CMRS category, the highest category was associated with hazard ratios of 2.80, 1.84 and 1.71 for the three sequential transitions. Disease-specific analyses showed the strongest associations with incident T2D. METS-IR showed the largest relative contributions across all transitions, whereas additive interactions were mainly observed during early CRMM progression.
CONCLUSION: Combined cardiometabolic biomarker burden was associated with graded, transition-specific risks across CRMM progression, supporting integrated cardiometabolic risk assessment across inflammatory, metabolic, adiposity, lipid and blood-pressure domains.

Title: Development and validation of a multibiomarker model for 12-month adverse outcomes in acute heart failure.
Abstract:
AIMS: To develop a multibiomarker model for predicting 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with acute heart failure (AHF) and assess incremental value.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 675 patients with AHF, comprising a development cohort (n = 303) and a validation cohort (n = 372). MACE comprised all-cause death or heart failure rehospitalization. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox regression and multivariable Cox regression were used for model development. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and incremental value.
RESULTS: The final model included monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), heparin-binding protein (HBP), and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2). Harrell's concordance index, the 12-month area under the time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Brier score were 0.710, 0.804, and 0.180 in the development cohort and 0.710, 0.760, and 0.203 in the validation cohort, respectively. Calibration demonstrated overall agreement between predicted and observed risks, and DCA suggested potential clinical net benefit. Adding HBP, sST2, and MLR to clinical variables and NT-proBNP increased the 12-month AUC from 0.753 to 0.824.
CONCLUSIONS: The multibiomarker model showed moderate predictive performance and may support post-discharge risk stratification in patients with AHF.

Title: Physical activity and quality of life in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in Japan: a quantitative study.
Abstract:
AIM: To describe the burden of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) using patient-reported outcome tools and a study-specific questionnaire.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This two-phase, cross-sectional, non-interventional, observational study (qualitative [previous] and quantitative [current]) included adults with HCM and New York Heart Association functional classification 2/3 recruited from healthcare facilities across Japan. The International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ), Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Symptom Questionnaire (HCMSQ), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) were used alongside a questionnaire developed using the qualitative findings.
RESULTS: The analysis included 120 patients (mean age, 59.1 ± 16.3 years; 55.5% [66/120] male), 60 each with non-obstructive and obstructive HCM. Patients with (vs. without) lifestyle changes had lower median IPAQ score (495.0 [363.0-1803.5] vs. 990.0 [369.4-2295.0], p = 0.159) and KCCQ - Clinical Summary Score (81.3 [65.6-90.7] vs. 92.0 [81.4-97.9], p < 0.001), and higher HADS-Depression (5.0 [3.0-8.0] vs. 2.0 [1.0-6.0], p = 0.001) and HCMSQ-shortness of breath (5.0 [2.0-6.0] vs. 3.0 [0.0-4.5], p < 0.001) scores. Most patients (83.9%) noticed HCM symptoms, and some patients attributed symptoms to causes other than HCM. Most patients (89.0%) told others about their HCM. Primary care physicians were the main information source (99.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: In this quantitative analysis, HCM affected patients' lifestyles and physical activity.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06181617 (ClinicalTrials.gov).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Multicenter Study

Title: Retinal Nerve Fibre Layer and Ganglion Cell Complex Thickness in Diabetes Mellitus without Diabetic Retinopathy.
Journal: Nepalese journal of ophthalmology : a biannual peer-reviewed academic journal of the Nepal Ophthalmic Society : NEPJOPH
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic retinopathy is on the rise and understanding mechanisms of retinal neurodegeneration in diabetes mellitus will help in halting retinopathy.
OBJECTIVE: The study was done to assess the retinal nerve fibre layer and ganglion cell complex thickness in type two diabetes mellitus without clinically evident vascular retinopathy and compare them with the normal population to understand the early neurodegenerative changes.
METHODOLOGY: This was a hospital-based, prospective, observational study conducted in South India from 2022 May to 2023 March. This study included one hundred and seventeen eyes with type two diabetes mellitus without clinical diabetic retinopathy and 115 normal age-matched controls after ethical approval using a consecutive sampling technique. Participants with other systemic co-morbidities and retinal pathology were excluded. Average, superior, and inferior retinal nerve fibre layer thickness and average, superior, inferior, inferonasal, superonasal, superotemporal, and inferotemporal macular ganglion cell complex thickness were measured using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography. A student's unpaired t-test was used for comparing the thickness between cases and controls, and analysed using SPSS Statistics version 26.
RESULT: The retinal nerve fibre layer thickness was significantly reduced in all quadrants in type two diabetes mellitus without diabetic retinopathy when compared to normal controls (p <0.001), with the mean nerve fibre layer thickness of 100.3μm ± 12.5μm in cases and 110.9μm ± 8.7μm in controls. The mean macular ganglion cell complex thickness was also significantly decreased in diabetes without retinopathy (p <0.001), with values of 99.9μm ± 8.1μm in diabetics and 109.3μm ± 4.9μm in controls. In diabetics, increased glycosylated haemoglobin correlated negatively with the nerve fibre layer and ganglion cell complex thickness.
CONCLUSION: Neurodegeneration of the retinal nerve fibre layer and ganglion cell complex in diabetics occurs before clinically visible vascular changes appear. Higher glycosylated haemoglobin is a risk factor for early neurodegeneration.

Title: Analysis of Ocular Surface Tumours and Lesions by High-definition Anterior-segment Optical Coherence Tomography.
Journal: Nepalese journal of ophthalmology : a biannual peer-reviewed academic journal of the Nepal Ophthalmic Society : NEPJOPH
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: High resolution AS-OCT (Anterior segment- Optical coherence tomography) is an imaging modality predominantly used in tertiary ophthalmologic centres to diagnose and characterise various ocular surface tumours as well as an adjunct to monitor treatment response.
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to evaluate the utility of AS-OCT for ocular surface tumours.
METHODOLOGY: This was a prospective cohort study of patients done at a tertiary care hospital in Nepal over one year from 2023 August to 2024 July. A consecutive sampling was done in the patients aged 18 years and older who were suspected of having ocular surface tumours and lesions during the study period. Demographic data, slit lamp biomicroscopic examination including size, site and morphology of tumour and AS-OCT using High Definition Zeiss Cirrus 6000 were carried out for all patients enrolled. Diagnosis was based on clinical evaluation and AS-OCT features. Those patients suspected of malignancy surgical excision and their histopathology was analysed.
RESULT: Among the 110 enrolled patients, the median age was 50 (range: 18-87) years. Of them, 63 (57%) were female and 47 (43%) were male. A total of 5 (4.5%) participants had bilateral involvement. Based on clinical picture and AS-OCT features, 84 eyes (73.04%) were diagnosed to have ocular surface squamous neoplasia (OSSN), 18 eyes (15.65%) with conjunctival nevus and two eyes (1.73%) were suspected to have melanoma. Histopathology of 80 eyes who underwent surgical excision, OSSN of various grades in 86% eyes was the most common diagnosis followed by conjunctival melanoma in 3%.
CONCLUSION: Though HPE is a gold standard for diagnosing ocular surface tumours, AS-OCT can provide a noninvasive optical biopsy. Additional research in AS-OCT is needed to increase the sensitivity and specificity of accurately diagnosing ocular surface lesions.

Title: Post-treatment risks of transcatheter aortic valve implantation: should we be increasing preventative measures?
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across an expanding risk spectrum. As indications extend to younger and lower-risk patients, post-treatment complications with implications for survival, quality of life, and valve durability require attention.
AREAS COVERED: This narrative review discusses major post-TAVI complications with direct implications for procedural planning and lifetime management, including cerebrovascular events, conduction abnormalities, coronary obstruction and aortic root injury, bioprosthetic valve dysfunction, valve thrombosis, residual regurgitation, and TAVI-associated infective endocarditis. Evidence was reviewed from pivotal randomized trials, contemporary registries, consensus documents, systematic reviews, and mechanistic studies addressing incidence, pathophysiology, predictors, prognosis, prevention, diagnosis, and management of these complications.
EXPERT OPINION: Post-TAVI risk reduction should move beyond reactive complication management toward individualized prevention. Meticulous computed tomography-based planning, optimized valve selection and implantation technique, rational antithrombotic therapy, structured rhythm and valve surveillance, selective use of cerebral embolic protection, timely correction of clinically or hemodynamically significant residual regurgitation, and infection-prevention pathways are central components of contemporary care. Future progress will depend on better risk stratification, longer-term durability data, and targeted preventive strategies adapted to lower-risk patients with longer life expectancy.

Title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in cardiogenic shock.
Abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains a heterogeneous syndrome associated with persistently high mortality despite advances in temporary mechanical circulatory support. One recent randomized controlled trial suggested a mortality benefit of a percutaneous microaxial flow pump in a cohort of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by CS, whereas routine veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in populations with acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS has not improved survival and is associated with higher complication rates. These findings underscore the importance of phenotype-driven patient selection, incorporating the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) and Shock Academic Research Consortium (SHARC) classifications to guide device selection, timing, escalation, and de-escalation. This clinical consensus statement from the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) and the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) updates the 2020 expert consensus document and provides updated practical guidance based on the recent evidence on the use of temporary mechanical circulatory support in acute myocardial infarction complicated by CS. Emphasis is placed on patient/device selection according to recent evidence, multidisciplinary shock teams, regionalized hub-and-spoke systems, structured protocols for escalation and futility, and the integration of contemporary trial data and best practices to optimize outcomes in this high-risk population.

Title: Immune signatures in primary hypertension: The roles of IL-10, IgM, and IgG.
Abstract: Hypertension (HTN) is the leading modifiable risk factor of cardiovascular diseases. Implicated immunological mechanisms are of great interest nowadays. This study aimed to assess the role of B cells by measuring serum immunoglobulin (IgG) and IgM levels, regulatory T cell levels, and interleukin (IL)-10 levels in hypertensive patients. This observational case-control study included 100 subjects. Sixty newly diagnosed untreated HTN patients were subdivided into three equal groups based on HTN severity. Another twenty patients controlled on their antihypertensive medications over the past three months were enrolled. Patients were compared to twenty apparently healthy subjects. Serum IgG, IgM, and IL-10 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), along with complete labs, including complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, S-creatinine, C-reactive protein, lipid profile, glycated hemoglobin, glomerular filtration rate, fundus examination, echocardiography, and carotid duplex, which were performed for all participants. IL10 levels were significantly lower among patients (54.84±9.91 pg/ml) compared to the control group (91.12±12.24 pg/ml) (p < 0.001). The lowest level was among the mild HTN group. Serum IgG and IgM levels were not significantly higher in patients than in the healthy group. (p = 0.71 and 0.31, respectively). Significant correlation was detected in the moderate HTN group; IL10 was negatively correlated with right common carotid artery intima media thickness (RTCCA IMT) (r = -0.44, p = 0.05). In conclusion, IL10 is significantly lower among patients with HTN. Dysregulation of immune mechanisms may be associated with HTN. Further studies are needed to reveal nature of this relationship.

Title: Nonselective beta-blockers and hepatic encephalopathy in liver cirrhosis:A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver cirrhosis leads to portal hypertension and related complications, including ascites, esophageal varices, and hepatic encephalopathy (HE). Non-selective beta blockers (NSBBs) decrease portal pressure, but it is not yet clear whether they contribute to HE development. Therefore, we examined the association between NSBB therapy and HE in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving patients with cirrhosis.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library (from inception to December 31, 2024) for RCTs comparing NSBBs with a placebo, endoscopic band ligation, or injection sclerotherapy for variceal bleeding prevention in relation to HE. The risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model. Subgroups were defined according to the comparator, NSBB type, and hepatic function status (weighted mean Child-Pugh score ≤6 vs. >6). The risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2).
RESULTS: There were 12 relevant studies, which included 775 NSBB-treated and 771 comparator patients (54 and 57 HE events). NSBB therapy was not associated with a statistically significant change in HE risk (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.73-1.47; p = 0.84; I² = 0%). Estimates were consistent across all subgroups of hepatic function statuses (compensation, RR 1.18, 0.44-3.14; decompensation, RR 1.02, 0.70-1.48; p = 0.79), comparators (placebo, RR 1.19, 0.79-1.80; endoscopic therapy, RR 0.72, 0.38-1.39; p = 0.20), and NSBB types (propranolol/timolol, RR 1.06, 0.72-1.55; carvedilol, RR 0.95, 0.42-2.15; p = 0.82).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not indicate a statistically significant association between NSBB therapy and HE development in patients with cirrhosis, regardless of disease severity.

Title: Perioperative Outcomes of Acute Normovolemic Hemodilution in Cardiac Surgery: Evidence From Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract: Acute normovolemic hemodilution (ANH) is a blood conservation strategy used in cardiac surgery, but its efficacy in reducing allogeneic blood transfusion remains debated. This systematic review and meta-analysis updates the existing evidence by incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to provide a contemporary assessment of ANH's impact on perioperative transfusion outcomes. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane Central up to August 2025 for RCTs comparing ANH to standard care in adult cardiac surgery. Primary outcomes were the number of allogeneic red blood cell units transfused, the rate of allogeneic blood transfusion, and estimated total blood loss. Data were pooled using random-effects models, and subgroup analyses were performed by type of surgery. Thirty-one RCTs involving 4426 patients (ANH = 2242, control = 2184) were included. ANH significantly reduced the rate of allogeneic blood transfusion (risk ratio 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66-0.87; P < 0.0001), the number of allogeneic red blood cell units transfused (standardized mean difference -0.42, 95% CI -0.64 to -0.20; P = 0.0001), and estimated total blood loss (standardized mean difference -0.42, 95% CI -0.63 to -0.21; P < 0.0001). Substantial heterogeneity was observed. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that benefits were most consistent in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting. In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, particularly coronary artery bypass grafting, ANH reduces exposure to allogeneic blood transfusion and decreases perioperative blood loss. Despite significant heterogeneity across studies, these findings support the inclusion of ANH within multimodal blood management protocols. Further large, high-quality RCTs with standardized protocols are warranted to confirm its role in modern practice.

Title: What is the significance of intra-operative oliguria with regard to post-operative acute kidney injury? A physiology-informed framework for intra-operative oliguria management.
Journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-operative oliguria is frequently interpreted as a surrogate for hypovolaemia or impaired renal perfusion, often prompting reflexive and potentially harmful fluid administration. However, urine output during anaesthesia is influenced by a complex interplay of neurohormonal activation, surgical stress, and positive pressure ventilation, which can decouple diuresis from actual renal blood flow. This perspective articles critically appraises the evidence linking intra-operative oliguria to acute kidney injury (AKI) and explores the physiological pitfalls of interpreting urine output as an isolated haemodynamic target.
RESULTS: Recent high-level evidence confirms a significant correlation between intra-operative oliguria and post-operative AKI, yet also highlights substantial heterogeneity in the thresholds and durations used across clinical practice. To address this, we propose a conceptual, physiology-informed framework that categorises reduced urine output into four distinct clinical phenotypes: adaptive (a physiologic neurohormonal response to stress), haemodynamic (potentially reversible hypoperfusion), high-risk/complex (occurring in major surgery or vulnerable patients), and injury-associated (established renal damage). In one highly selected high-risk population, a single randomised trial reported that targeting supranormal, urine-guided hydration was associated with a lower incidence of AKI. These findings are hypothesis-generating only and should not be generalised, but they raise the possibility that oliguria in narrowly defined contexts may represent a potentially modifiable signal warranting further prospective study rather than passive observation. Bedside adjuncts, such as ultrasound assessment of cardiac output or venous congestion, may assist in differentiating these phenotypes, although their intra-operative validation remains limited. This framework is intended as a hypothesis-generating conceptual aid to clinical reasoning, not as a validated clinical algorithm or practice recommendation.
CONCLUSION: Interpreting intra-operative oliguria requires a fundamental shift from binary thresholds to context-dependent phenotyping. Effective management must prioritise individualised assessment-integrating surgical risk, baseline patient vulnerability, and dynamic monitoring-rather than responding to isolated urine output triggers.

Title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison.
CONCLUSION: Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis; Comparative Study

Title: Acute cardiovascular, autonomic and endocrine responses to a one-hour competitive esports session: a randomized controlled crossover study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Competitive esports involve prolonged sedentary behavior combined with high cognitive and emotional demands, potentially influencing acute physiological responses. However, evidence regarding acute cardiovascular, autonomic, and endocrine responses to competitive gaming remains inconsistent and methodologically heterogeneous.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled crossover study, sixteen healthy male EA Sports FC players completed a one-hour competitive gaming session and a control condition (documentary viewing). Heart rate (HR), root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and standard deviation of NN-intervals (SDNN) for heart rate variability (HRV) were recorded continuously. Peripheral and central blood pressure, pulse wave velocity (PWV) and salivary cortisol were assessed at baseline, post-session, and after 15 min of rest. Linear mixed-effects models examined the effects of condition, time, and their interaction while accounting for period and sequence effects.
RESULTS: RMSSD (p = 0.005, ηₚ² = 0.13) and SDNN (p = 0.040, ηₚ² = 0.08) showed a significant Condition x Time interaction, with an increase in the control condition, whereas no significant temporal changes were observed during gaming. No significant Condition x Time interactions were observed for HR, PWV, peripheral and central blood pressure. Salivary cortisol decreased over time in both conditions (p < 0.001, ηₚ² = 0.33) without condition-specific effects (p = 0.765).
CONCLUSION: In this laboratory setting, no significant condition specific temporal changes in acute hemodynamic or cortisol responses were detected during competitive gaming compared with passive documentary viewing. The observed differences in cardiac autonomic regulation were primarily driven by an increase in HRV during the control condition, whereas no significant temporal changes in HRV were observed during gaming.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was preregistered in the German Clinical Trials Registry on 05 June 2024 (ID: DRKS00034399).

Title: Evaluating sedation efficacy and perioperative safety of fospropofol disodium versus propofol in elderly patients undergoing elective TURP: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fospropofol disodium is the first novel water-soluble propofol prodrug in China. After administration, it is mainly converted to propofol by alkaline phosphatase on the surface of endothelial cells to exert its pharmacological effects. Compared with propofol, fospropofol disodium has the characteristics of longer duration of action, lower incidence of injection pain and adverse events related to the respiratory and circulatory systems, and no adverse reactions related to lipid metabolism. At present, there are few reports on the safety and efficacy of fospropofol disodium in the induction and maintenance of general anesthesia. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of fospropofol disodium in routine anesthesia for elective surgery in the elderly, so as to provide new medication guidance for its application in the induction and maintenance stages of general anesthesia in the elderly population.
METHODS: Seventy elderly patients aged 65-85 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status II or III, scheduled for elective transurethral resection of the prostate under general anesthesia, will be enrolled. Patients will be randomly divided into the propofol group (group E) and the fospropofol disodium group (group F) using a random number table, with 35 cases in each group. Anesthesia induction: sufentanil 0.2-0.4 µg/kg and cisatracurium besilate 0.15 mg/kg will be administered intravenously. Group E will receive an intravenous bolus of propofol 1-1.5 mg/kg, while group F will receive an intravenous bolus of fospropofol disodium 10-15 mg/kg, both infused within 60 s. Tracheal intubation will be performed when the patient's Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) score decreases to 1 with BIS < 60 sustained for ≥3 min, followed by routine mechanical ventilation. For anesthesia maintenance, group E will receive continuous intravenous infusion of propofol 4-12 mg/(kg·h) and remifentanil 0.2-0.4 µg/(kg·min) via a syringe pump; group F will receive continuous intravenous infusion of fospropofol disodium 10-20 mg/(kg·h) and remifentanil 0.2-0.4 µg/(kg·min) via a syringe pump. During the operation, the infusion rates of maintenance anesthetics will be adjusted according to hemodynamic status to maintain blood pressure and heart rate fluctuations within 20% of the baseline values, and the Bispectral Index (BIS) value will be maintained between 40 and 60. After the operation, patients will be transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU). Primary outcomes of this study: success rate of sedation and time to onset of sedation.
SECONDARY OUTCOMES: (1) perioperative indicators, (2) hemodynamic indices at each time point, (3) adverse reactions.
DISCUSSION: Elderly patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) are often complicated with multiple comorbidities, leading to a relatively high anesthetic risk. This trial takes the success rate of sedation and time to onset of sedation as the primary endpoints, to compare the application differences between fospropofol disodium and propofol. The aim of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of fospropofol disodium in routine anesthesia for elective surgeries in the elderly population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trials Registry (ChiCTR2500115343) on December 24, 2025 ( http://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=294899 ).

Title: Integration of Collaborative Cross and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel studies does not significantly improve genome wide association study results.
Abstract: Genome-wide association studies rely on maximizing cohort size and minimizing environmental noise to increase their efficacy. Model organism Genetic Reference Populations offer significantly reduced environmental noise and deep phenotyping, yet rarely are multiple populations merged together. We evaluated whether combining the Collaborative Cross (CC) and Hybrid Mouse Diversity Panel (HMDP), two well-studied murine Genetic Reference Populations would improve GWAS outcomes. Utilizing two prior studies by our group that had performed the same study for heart failure in each cohort, we examined each cohort individually and then together using the pyLMM GWAS algorithm. Surprisingly, the combined cohort of 175 strains produced only 123 loci, a modest gain over the 104-strain HMDP (114), and fewer than in the 71-strain CC (149) and did not systematically improve resolution. Locus overlap between the CC and HMDP cohorts was very sparse, with only a single locus (near Eprs1) found to be significant in each cohort, although nearly half of all combined loci were also found in the CC cohort. These results caution that merging divergent GRPs may act to dilute signal and complicate interpretation, despite larger sample sizes.

Title: Anticoagulation-associated hemorrhage in atrial fibrillation as a marker of occult malignancy: a narrative review.
Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in adults and significantly increases the risk of stroke. Due to common threats like systemic inflammation and treatment-related cardiotoxicity, individuals with cancer have a noticeably increased chance of developing AF. Managing AF in this population presents dual challenges: reducing thromboembolic risk while minimizing bleeding complications. Traditionally, warfarin, a vitamin K antagonist, has been the most widely used anticoagulant. However, the emergence of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), which offer equal or superior efficacy compared to warfarin with fewer dietary and drug interactions, has shifted clinical practice. This narrative review explores the complex clinical relationship between AF, anticoagulation, and bleeding as a potential early indicator of occult cancer. An expanding body of evidence from extensive cohort studies and meta-analyses supports this association, showing a significantly increased risk of gastrointestinal, genitourinary, respiratory, and, to a lesser extent, intracranial bleeding in anticoagulated patients that may precede cancer diagnosis. Although bleeding is a recognized difficulty of oral anticoagulation, it may expose occult malignancy, resulting in timely detection of cancer and more favorable outcomes. Perhaps it is time to regard occult gastrointestinal bleeding for what it may be: an early warning sign of malignancy. The increased risk of both thromboembolism and bleeding in cancer patients poses a challenge in clinical practice. Though bleeding has increasingly been recognized as a potential harbinger of occult cancer, uniform guidelines for malignant lesion screening after a hemorrhagic episode remain to be established. It is essential to establish a solid, evidence-based therapeutic protocol to achieve the best possible treatment and results for patients.

Title: Early versus deferred intravenous calcium in patients with sepsis and ionized hypocalcemia: a target-trial emulation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous calcium is frequently administered during sepsis, yet whether early treatment improves 24-h hemodynamic recovery remains uncertain. We compared 24-h hemodynamic recovery between calcium initiation within 2 h of a non-emergency low-ionized calcium (iCa) result and no calcium initiation during the first 6 h after the result.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective target-trial emulation of 2016-2025 high-resolution electronic health records from Zigong Fourth People's Hospital. Adults with sepsis, final or corrected iCa of 0.90-1.10 mmol/L, and no emergency indication were eligible at result availability. Strategies were executed calcium within 2 h versus no calcium through 6 h; care after 6 h was unrestricted. Clone-censor weighting and overlap tilting addressed grace periods, measured time-varying confounding, and clinical equipoise. The primary outcome was being alive and vasopressor-free at 24 h. Estimates and two-sided 95% percentile intervals came from 2,000 patient-level bootstrap samples with model refitting.
RESULTS: Of 5,993 patients, 1,538 initiated calcium within 2 h, 147 initiated at 2-6 h, and 4,308 received none through 6 h; none of the latter initiated calcium during 6-24 h. The standardized probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery was 69.9% with early calcium and 61.1% with deferral, corresponding to a risk difference of + 8.69 percentage points (95% percentile interval, + 4.66 to + 12.84) and a risk ratio of 1.142 (1.074-1.214). The estimated association varied with baseline norepinephrine-equivalent dose (Holm-adjusted P = 2.00 × 10⁻⁶), whereas the iCa interaction did not remain statistically supported after adjustment (P = 0.097). Early calcium was associated with a 1.29-percentage-point higher observed risk of hypercalcemia (95% percentile interval, + 0.64 to + 2.05). Intervals for severe arrhythmia, new renal replacement therapy, and hospital mortality included the null.
CONCLUSIONS: Early intravenous calcium was associated with a higher probability of 24-h hemodynamic recovery than the deferred strategy, whose observed pathway involved no calcium through 24 h. Estimated effects were larger at higher vasopressor doses. Early calcium was associated with a modestly higher observed risk of hypercalcemia. These findings support randomized evaluation in vasopressor-treated patients. Baseline iCa modification remains exploratory.

Title: Platelet P2Y12 inhibitor use and risk of colorectal cancer incidence and colorectal cancer-related mortality: a Swedish registry-based cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose aspirin use is associated with reduced CRC incidence and CRC-related mortality. A similar association with P2Y12 inhibitor use remains uncertain. We investigated whether the use of P2Y12 inhibitors was associated with CRC incidence and CRC-related mortality among individuals diagnosed with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD).
METHODS: From the ESPRESSO cohort, we identified 334,882 patients diagnosed with ASCVD between 2006 and 2021. We identified patients who initiated P2Y12 inhibitors ≥ 84 consecutive Defined Daily Doses (cDDDs). We estimated the risk of incident CRC and CRC mortality according to P2Y12 inhibitor use using Cox proportional-hazards regression models adjusting for potential confounders including comorbidities and regular aspirin use.
RESULTS: We documented 4,015 incident CRC cases and 2,610 CRC-related deaths during a median follow-up of 5.1 years (IRQ, 2.1-9.0 years). We did not observe an association between P2Y12 inhibitor use and CRC incidence. In contrast, a longer duration of P2Y12 inhibitor use was associated with lower CRC-related mortality. Compared to non-users, multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for CRC mortality were 0.73 (95% CI, 0.60-0.89) in patients with 336-671 cDDDs of P2Y12 inhibitor and 0.81 (95% CI, 0.68-0.97) in those with ≥672 cDDDs. Among patients with incident CRC diagnosis, subsequent initiation of P2Y12 inhibitor after CRC diagnosis was associated with significantly lower CRC mortality (HR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.29-0.60).
CONCLUSIONS: P2Y12 inhibitor use was not associated with risk of incident CRC but was significantly inversely associated with CRC mortality, which appeared to be due to improved survival among individuals who initiate P2Y12 inhibitors after CRC diagnosis. These findings merit further study given the observational nature of the analysis and potential for residual confounding.

Title: Biventricular Assist Devices Versus Total Artificial Heart as Bridge-to-Transplantation Strategies: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Biventricular assist devices (BiVADs) and total artificial heart (TAH) are the principal bridge-to-transplantation strategies for patients with advanced biventricular heart failure awaiting heart transplantation, but their comparative effectiveness and safety remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared pretransplant outcomes between the two approaches.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for studies comparing BiVADs and TAH as bridge-to-transplantation strategies. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. Random-effects models were used to compare survival to transplantation, mortality during support, support-related complications, and duration of support.
RESULTS: Ten retrospective studies involving 2,242 patients met the inclusion criteria. The overall analysis showed no significant difference in survival to transplantation between patients supported with BiVADs and TAH (RR = 0.97, 95% CI (0.84, 1.13), P = 0.74). However, after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts, sensitivity analysis showed a higher rate of survival to transplantation in those supported with TAH (RR = 0.88, 95% CI (0.80, 0.97), P = 0.01). No significant difference was observed in mortality during support in the overall analysis (RR = 1.19, 95% CI (0.88, 1.61), P = 0.26) or after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts (RR = 0.98, 95% CI (0.79, 1.21), P = 0.84). BiVADs were associated with higher rates of bleeding and stroke (RR = 2.79, 95% CI (1.70, 4.59), P < 0.0001 and RR = 2.31, 95% CI (1.53, 3.50), P < 0.0001, respectively), whereas infection did not differ significantly between the two groups (RR = 1.18, 95% CI (0.50, 2.78), P = 0.70). Sensitivity analysis for stroke after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts showed a similarly higher rate in patients supported with BiVADs (RR = 2.39, 95% CI (1.46, 3.93), P = 0.0006). Duration of support did not differ significantly between both groups in the overall analysis (MD = 2.25 days, 95% CI (- 16.46, 20.96), P = 0.81) or after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts (MD = - 0.90 days, 95% CI (- 24.26, 22.46), P = 0.94).
CONCLUSION: TAH may be associated with higher rates of survival to transplantation after excluding potentially overlapping cohorts, while BiVAD support may be associated with higher rates of bleeding and stroke. However, all included studies were retrospective, and the certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. These findings should therefore be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in prospective multicenter studies.

Title: Beyond Pain Intensity: A Patient-Informed Framework for Documenting Burden in Small Fiber Neuropathy.
Abstract: Small fiber neuropathy (SFN) is a sensory-autonomic neuropathy of thinly myelinated Aδ and unmyelinated C fibers that can produce neuropathic pain and multisystem autonomic symptoms. Although diagnostic criteria and confirmatory testing have improved recognition, SFN burden may remain underrecognized even after diagnosis. This narrative review identifies two complementary documentation failures. The translation problem arises when symptom labels and intensity ratings do not capture effects on sustainable function, cognitive workload, emotional well-being, and participation. The fragmentation problem arises when specialties assess multisystem symptoms without preserving their temporal pattern, co-occurrence, shared triggers, treatment trade-offs, and recovery costs. Reverse availability bias is proposed as a conceptual mechanism that may intensify both failures: symptoms or mechanisms not represented in clinicians' mental models may be overlooked in consideration and documentation. The review proposes an SFN Burden Integration Framework (SFN-BIF) that separates symptom presence, burden, and causal attribution and combines validated measures with six core documentation fields: temporal pattern, triggers and relievers, co-occurrence, recovery cost, functional consequences, and cognitive-emotional consequences. Longitudinal patient-reported information is integrated with neurological examination, skin biopsy, quantitative sensory testing, autonomic or organ-specific testing, and cognitive or functional assessment when indicated. Better integration may inform diagnosis and referral, treatment selection and trade-offs, rehabilitation and psychological care, disability assessment, phenotyping, and clinical trial outcome selection while preserving diagnostic rigor. The framework remains conceptual and requires prospective evaluation of validity, feasibility, clinical utility, and administrative burden.

Title: Assessing the Impact of Routine Intervention for Perioperative Hyponatremia on Postoperative Outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative hyponatremia is associated with poorer outcomes, including increased mortality, ICU admissions, prolonged hospital stays, and readmissions. Whether routine intervention improves outcomes remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess an institutional protocol requiring internist referral and treatment for serum sodium < 130 mmol/L before surgery.
DESIGN: Retrospective registry-based study using a quasi-experimental regression discontinuity design. Sharp, kink, and triangular kernel models estimated effects at the intervention threshold. Subgroup analyses included patients with cardiac disease, chronic kidney disease, moderate operative risk, and emergency surgery.
PARTICIPANTS: Of 180,926 adult patients between 2013 and 2020, 24,846 had preoperative serum sodium 125-135 mmol/L. After excluding 43 with incomplete data, 24,803 remained.
INTERVENTIONS: Protocolized internist referral and treatment for preoperative serum sodium < 130 mmol/L.
MAIN MEASURES: The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included 1-year mortality, ICU admissions, length of stay, and rapid postoperative sodium correction.
KEY RESULTS: Compared with serum sodium 130-135 mmol/L, sodium < 130 mmol/L was associated with higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (3.32% vs 1.33%), 1-year mortality (21.25% vs 11.03%), ICU admission (18.65% vs 11.50%), and mean length of stay (20.64 ± 25.51 vs 13.42 ± 21.01 days; all p < 0.001). No significant threshold effects were seen for 30-day mortality (treatment effect = 1.22, p = 0.138), ICU admissions (0.014, p = 0.564), or length of stay (0.184, p = 0.943). Significant discontinuity was observed for 1-year mortality (0.081, p = 0.010), particularly among patients with cardiac disease (0.162, p < 0.001), with chronic kidney disease (0.071, p = 0.012), with moderate operative risk (0.779, p = 0.013), or undergoing emergent surgery (0.100, p = 0.001). Lower preoperative sodium predicted rapid postoperative correction (OR = 1.190, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Protocolized internist referral and treatment for preoperative serum sodium < 130 mmol/L did not affect short-term perioperative outcomes but may have reduced 1-year mortality, particularly in subgroups with cardiac and renal disease. Further studies are required to determine if this reflects treatment of underlying comorbidities rather than the effect of sodium normalization alone.

Title: Sex-related differences in clinical characteristics, management, and outcomes of Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection.
Journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with Enterococcus faecalis bloodstream infection (EF-BSI) differ by biological sex.
METHODS: Quasi-experimental study conducted at two hospitals, comprising a retrospective phase (2017-2019) and a prospective intervention phase (2022-2024), including adults with a first episode of monomicrobial EF-BSI. Patients who died within 72 h or were receiving palliative care were excluded. A structured management bundle was implemented in the intervention phase. Clinical features, bundle adherence, and 90-day mortality were compared by sex. Cox regression was used to assess the association between sex and 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: Among 250 patients, 77 (31%) were females and 173 (69%) males. Females were younger than males (median 63 [50-76] vs. 73 [63-80] years; p < 0.001). Cardiovascular disease was more frequent in males (30 [39%] vs. 94 [54%]; p = 0.025), whereas immunosuppressive therapy (29 [38%] vs. 35 [20%]; p = 0.004) and connective tissue disease (9 [12%] vs. 2 [1%]; p < 0.001) were more frequent in females. Persistent bacteraemia (2/57 [4%] vs. 30/139 [22%]; p = 0.002) and infective endocarditis (14 [18%] vs. 59 [34%]; p = 0.011) were more frequent in males. Females received fewer bundle measures (5 [3-6] vs. 5 [4-6]; p = 0.028), largely because echocardiography and colonoscopy were less frequently indicated. Ninety-day mortality was 22% (17) in females and 14% (25) in males (p = 0.136). Female sex was associated with higher 90-day mortality after adjustment (aHR 2.00, 95%CI 1.04-3.83).
CONCLUSIONS: Further studies should explore the underlying causes of these differences and potential implications for individualized management.

Title: Radiological features of peritumoral brain injury and neurological outcomes after glioma surgery: a prospective observational study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Despite significant advances in glioma surgery, early postoperative neuroimaging frequently reveals signs of surgical brain injury (SBI). This prospective observational study aimed to investigate the incidence, radiological characteristics, neurological outcomes and risk factors of SBI following glioma resection.
METHODS: Patients with newly diagnosed supratentorial gliomas who undergo tumor resection were prospectively enrolled. Serial MRI examinations were administrated early postoperative (≤ 72 h) and on postoperative days 7, 14 and 28 to assess the characteristics of infarction, edema and microhemorrhage. Neurological outcomes were evaluated using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at postoperative day 28.
RESULTS: A total of 64 patients was included. Postoperative infarction was identified in 14 patients (21.9%), with all anatomically localized to the basal ganglia, thalamus, or insular regions. Intraoperative blood loss ≥ 300 mL was independently associated with postoperative infarction (Odd Ratio [OR]: 4.62, p = 0.035). Microhemorrhage was observed in 53.8% of patients. Peritumoral edema occurred in all cases and exhibited two distinct patterns: residual tumor-associated edema (n = 42) and de novo surgery-induced edema (n = 22). The average volume of tumor-associated edema decreased, whereas that of surgery-induced edema increased over time. Among the 53 patients who completed neurological outcome assessments, 13 developed disability (mRS ≥ 2). Risk factors were higher intraoperative blood loss (OR: 8.88, p = 0.013) and postoperative infarction (OR: 6.33, p = 0.031).
CONCLUSION: SBI, including infarction and edema, is common following glioma surgery and associated with adverse neurological outcomes. Meticulous intraoperative hemostatic management is essential to prevent postoperative infarction and even disability outcome.

Title: Clinical impact of admission estimated glomerular filtration rate categories in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a well-established risk factor in acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, the clinical relevance of admission estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-based categories remains unclear. We analyzed 10,870 patients from a prospective multicenter AMI registry in Japan. Patients were stratified into stages 1 (≥ 90), 2 (60-89), 3a (45-59), 3b (30-44), 4 (15-29), and 5 (< 15 mL/min/1.73 m2) based on the admission eGFR. The primary endpoint was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Bleeding was defined as BARC type 3 or 5. More advanced admission eGFR stages were associated with a higher risk of adverse events. After multivariable adjustment, stages 4 and 5 were associated with a significantly higher risk of MACE compared with the reference group of stages 1 and 2 (stage 4: HR 2.12, 95% CI 1.03-4.33; stage 5: HR 4.14, 95% CI 1.54-11.09), whereas stages 3a and 3b were not significantly associated with MACE. In patients with AMI, clinical outcomes varied across admission eGFR categories, with more advanced renal dysfunction, particularly stages 4 and 5, associated with a higher risk of short-term MACE. Detailed categorization of admission eGFR may provide additional prognostic information for early risk assessment.

Title: Central and peripheral vascular recovery following resistance exercise with and without blood flow restriction across age groups: a parallel group crossover randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity resistance training (HIRT) benefits musculoskeletal and vascular health but may be poorly tolerated by older adults. Low-intensity resistance training (LIRT) is an alternative, yet evidence on arterial stiffness is mixed, and it often fails to improve vascular health due to insufficient stimulus. Blood flow restriction (BFR) enhances hemodynamic stimulus, but its acute cardiovascular effects in older adults remain unclear.
PURPOSE: To compare central and peripheral vascular responses following acute LIRT with BFR versus HIRT across age groups.
METHODS: In a randomized crossover design, 19 young (22±3 years) and 19 older (70±9 years) adults completed three sessions: HIRT (3 × 10 reps at 75%1RM), LIRT+BFR (4 × 20 reps at 30%1RM with continuous cuff occlusion), and no exercise. Central and peripheral vascular function were assessed via oscillometric pulse wave analysis at rest, 5-min (RECOV1), and 30-min (RECOV2) post-exercise.
RESULTS: In older adults, neither HIRT nor LIRT+BFR altered total peripheral resistance (TPR), aortic reservoir function, or subendocardial viability ratio (SEVR) throughout post-exercise, with no differences observed between conditions. Conversely, young adults exhibited reductions at RECOV1 following HIRT in TPR (Δ = -  0.176 PRU), reservoir function (Δ = -  11.9%), and SEVR (Δ = -  47.1%), persisting at RECOV2 (all p < 0.05). LIRT+BFR elicited minor changes. Most variables normalized within 30 min for both groups.
CONCLUSION: In older adults, LIRT+BFR elicits post acute central vascular responses comparable to HIRT, with stable coronary perfusion and rapid recovery supporting the short-term tolerability of both modalities. LIRT+BFR thus represents a viable alternative to HIRT for older population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT06596304).

Title: Joint association of growth hormone and cerebral small vessel disease with antihypertensive treatment burden after stroke: an exploratory prospective study.
Abstract: Growth hormone (GH) and cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) may influence blood pressure regulation. This study investigated the individual and joint associations of GH and SVD severity with antihypertensive management following stroke. We prospectively enrolled patients admitted for acute stroke between October 2020 and December 2022.
