Patients with pre-existing or newly diagnosed hypertension during the initial hospitalization were included. We examined whether baseline GH levels and severe SVD burden (total SVD score ≥2) during the index hospitalization were associated with high antihypertensive medication burden defined as the use of ≥2 antihypertensive agents, as well as with high antihypertensive treatment intensity using an antihypertensive treatment intensity score (TIS) ≥ 1 at 12 months post-stroke. Among 171 registered patients, 129 were included (107 ischemic stroke/transient ischemic attack and 22 intracerebral hemorrhage; median age, 60 years; 95 male). High antihypertensive medication burden at 12 months was observed in 19 patients (15%). Elevated GH levels (≥0.49 ng/mL) and severe SVD burden were independently associated with high antihypertensive medication burden and TIS ≥ 1. Moreover, the coexistence of elevated GH and severe SVD burden was significantly associated with high antihypertensive medication burden and TIS ≥ 1 compared with the absence of both factors. Elevated GH levels and severe SVD burden were independently associated with antihypertensive medication burden and treatment intensity 12 months after stroke. The combined presence was associated with both outcomes, suggesting a potential joint contribution of neuroendocrine and structural vascular factors to post-stroke blood pressure management.

Title: Association between caregiving duration and hypertension among family caregivers: the TMM CommCohort study.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Abstract: With the global increase in elderly individuals requiring long-term care, family caregivers face significant physical and psychosocial burdens. This study examined the association between caregiving duration and hypertension using three indices: morning and evening home blood pressure (HBP) and research blood pressure (BP). This cross-sectional study included 13,518 participants from the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study. Caregiving time was categorized via questionnaire. Hypertension was defined according to the Japanese Society of Hypertension Guidelines for the Management of Elevated Blood Pressure and Hypertension 2025 (HBP ≥ 135/85 mmHg, research BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg, or medication use). Multivariable robust Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs), adjusted for demographics, lifestyle and social psychological factors. Participants providing care "almost all day" had significantly higher PRs for morning (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.07-1.48) and evening hypertension (PR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.03-1.56) than non-caregivers. Notably, no significant association was observed with research BP-defined hypertension. Stratified analyses revealed that these associations were particularly prominent among caregivers aged <65 years (P-interaction for morning hypertension = 0.003). The interaction between sex and caregiving time was not significant. Prolonged caregiving burden is associated with a higher prevalence of hypertension in the morning and evening, particularly among working-age caregivers. Because these risks were not captured by research BP, HBP monitoring is essential for cardiovascular risk management in caregivers. Social policies and clinical interventions should target younger caregivers to mitigate the physiological strain of 24-h caregiving responsibilities.

Title: The Effects of Fluid Management Approaches on Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System Activity and Blood Pressure Control in Patients on Dialysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic fluid imbalance in maintenance hemodialysis can increase cardiovascular risk through activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone pathway. This study compared the endocrine and hemodynamic effects of three fluid management strategies in adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis in a prospective two-center observational cohort study.
METHODS: Six hundred patients were assigned to fluid management by clinical assessment, bioimpedance-guided monitoring, or absolute blood volume monitoring, with 200 patients in each group. Plasma renin activity, angiotensin II, aldosterone, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and arterial stiffness were measured at baseline and Weeks 6 and 12. Between-group and over-time differences were analyzed using adjusted longitudinal and covariance-based models. Additional analyses examined variation by age, fluid status pattern, and sodium self-management.
RESULTS: By Week 12, plasma renin activity, angiotensin II, and aldosterone increased in the clinical assessment group showed smaller increases or minimal change in the bioimpedance-guided group and declined in the absolute blood volume monitoring group. The absolute blood volume monitoring group also showed the greatest improvement in blood pressure and arterial stiffness over follow-up. In addition, this group had the lowest frequency of intradialytic hypotension and the strongest improvement in patient self-management measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Absolute blood volume monitoring was associated with greater short-term suppression of endocrine activation and better hemodynamic outcomes than clinical assessment or bioimpedance-guided monitoring during the 12-week follow-up period.

Title: [Evidence mapping analysis of clinical research on Chinese patent medicines for treating carotid atherosclerosis].
Journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
Abstract: This study aims to systematically map and visualize the landscape of clinical research evidence on Chinese patent medicines for treating carotid atherosclerosis(CAS), evaluating the current status, strengths, and limitations of research in this field to provide guidance for future studies. A systematic search was conducted across eight Chinese and English databases from their inception to November 14, 2025. The results were presented using a combination of figures, tables, and textual descriptions. A total of 343 publications were included, comprising 331 randomized controlled trials( RCTs), 8 systematic reviews/Meta-analyses, 1 network Meta-analysis, and 3 expert consensus statements. The publication trends showed an initial rise followed by a decline. The studies involved 68 distinct Chinese patent medicines, with Tongxinluo Capsules, Naoxintong Capsules, and Ginkgo biloba preparations being the most widely used. Most studies had treatment durations of 12 to 24 weeks and sample sizes ranging from 51 to 100 cases. The outcome measures encompassed 19 domains, including plaque parameters, lipid metabolism, safety evaluation, inflammatory factors, and clinical efficacy. The identified limitations included a lack of clear distinction between primary and secondary outcomes, low standardization of outcome measures, insufficient reflection of TCM advantages, absence of clinical endpoints and quality of life assessments, and a lack of health economics indicators. In terms of methodological quality assessment, the RCT exhibited significant deficiencies in randomization, allocation concealment, blinding implementation, and missing data processing, indicating a high risk of bias. The quality of systematic reviews/Meta-analyses was generally low, while expert consensus statements lacked rigor and applicability in their development. Future efforts should focus on conducting multicenter, large-sample, high-quality clinical trials, refining the standardization of TCM syndrome patterns, establishing core outcome indicator sets, and enhancing the overall research quality. This will fully realize the potential of Chinese patent medicines in treating CAS.

Title: Preoperative C-Reactive Protein to Albumin Ratio Is Associated With Incremental Prognostic Information Beyond EuroSCORE II After Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery.
Journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the prognostic performance of the preoperative C-reactive protein to albumin ratio (CAR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index, pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score for predicting mortality after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and to determine whether these biomarkers provide incremental prognostic value beyond European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II.
DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.
SETTING: Single-center tertiary training and research hospital.
PARTICIPANTS: Six hundred eighteen consecutive adults undergoing isolated CABG between January 1, 2022, and December 1, 2024, with complete 1-year follow-up.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcomes were intensive care unit mortality rate (11.8%) and 1-year all-cause mortality rate (16.2%). Among all evaluated biomarkers, CAR demonstrated the strongest prognostic performance for both outcomes and independently predicted in-hospital and 1-year mortality after adjustment for EuroSCORE II and base excess. Incorporating CAR into EuroSCORE II improved discrimination and showed favorable internally validated calibration and decision-curve net benefit within the proposed perioperative management framework, whereas the remaining inflammatory indices provided little or no incremental prognostic information. Cell count-based indices, including SII and PIV, did not demonstrate meaningful prognostic discrimination or independent associations with the evaluated mortality outcomes in the present cohort. The optimal CAR threshold was derived and evaluated within the same cohort and should therefore be considered exploratory pending external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative CAR was independently associated with both in-hospital and 1-year mortality after isolated CABG and provided incremental prognostic information beyond EuroSCORE II in the present cohort. Rather than replacing EuroSCORE II, it provides complementary prognostic information by capturing inflammatory and nutritional dimensions not represented in conventional surgical risk models. External multicenter validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

Title: IHPBA 2026 global guideline for the management of hepatocellular carcinoma in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
Journal: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines for the management of patients with HCC are predominantly focused on well-resourced healthcare systems. In 2024, the IHPBA Legacy committee initiated a process to develop global resource-sensitive guidelines for the management of HCC.
METHODS: An IHPBA global guideline group produced and circulated statements on the management of HCC from diagnosis to treatment, discussed these in online webinars and generated guidelines. This document focuses on the diagnosis and management of patients with HCC in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
RESULTS: Initial diagnosis by ultrasound is supported by cross-sectional imaging. Alfa-feto protein and assessment of liver synthetic function are recommended at diagnosis. Lesion biopsy is not mandated. Liver resection is the recommended treatment of choice for single HCC in patients with preserved liver function and up to 3 lesions ≤3 cm. Radiofrequency and microwave are regarded as equivalent and can be used if resection is not available. Ethanol injection can be used if thermal ablation is not available but should be restricted to small lesions. TACE and TAE can be used for intermediate stage disease. Atezolizumab/bevacizumab combination is recommended as first line systemic therapy with sorafenib and Lenvatinib being recommended if first line is not an option. Advice for the care of the patient with advanced or terminal disease is provided.
CONCLUSIONS: This document provides resource-sensitive HCC guidelines that prioritise feasibility, maximise benefit, and reduce default reliance on best supportive care alone and are produced for the IHPBA by discussion with the global community of IHPBA.

Title: Life-course associations of early-life risk factors, modifiable adult lifestyles, and transitions of cardiometabolic disease and multimorbidity: A prospective cohort study.
Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether associations of early-life risk factors with cardiometabolic disease (CMD) transitions vary by adult lifestyles remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to examine the associations between early-life risk factors and CMD transitions, and to assess whether adult lifestyles can modify these associations.
METHODS: We analyzed data from 174,718 adults participating in the United Kingdom Biobank prospective cohort study. We defined 5 CMD transitions using a multistate model: from CMD-free to first CMD (FCMD; including stroke, ischemic heart disease, and type 2 diabetes), from FCMD to cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), and from CMD-free, FCMD, and CMM to death. An early-life risk score (ERS; 0-3) summed low birth weight, maternal smoking around birth, and absence of human milk feeding in infancy. Adult lifestyle was quantified using an adult lifestyle score (ALS) adapted from 4 behavioral metrics of the Life's Essential 8 framework, and data were collected at study enrollment when participants had a median age of 55 y.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14.6 y, individuals with both high early-life risk (ERS ≥2) and an unhealthy adult lifestyle (ALS: 0-49) had the highest risks for most adverse transitions, including CMD-free to FCMD [hazard ratio (HR): 2.04; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.89, 2.21], FCMD to CMM (HR: 1.46; 95% CI: 1.27, 1.69), CMD-free to death (HR: 2.31; 95% CI: 1.95, 2.72), and FCMD to death (HR: 1.64; 95% CI: 1.34, 2.01). The associations of ERS with the risk of most CMD transitions were less pronounced among participants with a healthy adult lifestyle than among those with an unhealthy adult lifestyle.
CONCLUSIONS: Joint exposure to adverse early-life experiences and an unhealthy adult lifestyle was associated with elevated risks of CMD progression and mortality. Notably, the detrimental associations of early-life risk factors with specific CMD transitions were less pronounced among individuals with healthier adult lifestyles.

Title: Lipoprotein(a) identifies premature coronary artery disease in patients with low LDL-cholesterol: A large multicenter cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Whether elevated Lp(a) is associated with premature coronary artery disease (pCAD) in young and middle-aged adults with low levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) remains poorly characterized in real-world practice.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between elevated Lp(a) (≥50 mg/dL) and incident pCAD after comprehensive lipid adjustment, including among patients with LDL-C <100 mg/dL.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study across 3 Mayo Clinic sites of adults without prior CAD (males 18-50 years; females 18-60 years) who underwent Lp(a) testing (enrollment 2000-2020; follow-up through 2024). The exposure was Lp(a) ≥50 mg/dL; the outcome was incident pCAD. Multivariable Cox models were adjusted for LDL-C, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and standard risk factors, with competing-risk, multiple-imputation, and prespecified sensitivity analyses, including patients with LDL-C <100 mg/dL.
RESULTS: Among 35,622 patients (55.9% female; median age 46 years), 459 (1.3%) developed pCAD over a median of 6.0 years (incidence rate 1.85 per 1000 person-years; 95% CI, 1.69-2.03). Elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with pCAD (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.40; 95% CI 1.12-1.74; P = .003), with a log-linear dose-response. The association did not weaken when LDL-C was low: among 10,949 patients with LDL-C <100 mg/dL, elevated Lp(a) carried a 67% higher adjusted risk (HR 1.67; 95% CI 1.15-2.43; P = .007). The Lp(a) × LDL-C interaction was nonsignificant (P = .571), indicating the effect was undiminished rather than amplified by low LDL-C.
CONCLUSION: In young and middle-aged adults with low LDL-C, elevated Lp(a) is significantly associated with premature coronary risk that is not captured by conventional lipid panels. These real-world data support Lp(a) measurement at a younger age as a tool for individual risk reclassification, identifying patients who carry occult residual atherogenic risk and may benefit from emerging Lp(a)-targeted therapies.

Title: Need for population-specific lipid guidelines for South Asians: Focus on the Indian population and its distinct cardiometabolic risk profile.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: South Asian individuals bear a disproportionately high burden of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), characterized by earlier onset, greater severity, and higher mortality compared with Western populations. This is despite lower average low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and is driven by a distinctive cardiometabolic phenotype, including adverse lifestyle factors, high prevalence of insulin resistance and diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia, increased small dense LDL particles, elevated lipoprotein(a), and low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels.
OBJECTIVE: To review the cardiometabolic risk profile of South Asians and the rationale for population-specific lipid management strategies, with a focus on contemporary evidence and recommendations from the Lipid Association of India (LAI).
METHODS: The relevant evidence was identified from published prospective cohort studies, randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, and international and Indian guidelines with emphasis on studies evaluating South Asian/ Indian populations. The literature was evaluated with specific attention to differences in ASCVD burden, age at disease onset, cardiometabolic risk factors, lipid and lipoprotein profiles, and treatment responses between South Asian/Indian and Western populations. Evidence supporting intensive LDL-C lowering and combination lipid-lowering therapy was reviewed.
RESULTS: South Asians demonstrate a high prevalence of atherogenic dyslipidemia characterized by hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL-C, elevated non-HDL-C, and increased apolipoprotein B (apo B) containing particles, often with relatively modest LDL-C levels. Western risk prediction models and lipid thresholds may therefore underestimate ASCVD risk in this population. LAI guidelines recommend lower LDL-C targets than Western counterparts, refined ASCVD risk stratification including extreme-risk group categories, and the use of non-HDL-C and apo B as complementary therapeutic targets. Combination lipid-lowering therapy with statins, ezetimibe, bempedoic acid, and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors is often required to achieve recommended goals and address residual lipid-related risk.
CONCLUSION: Given the distinctive cardiometabolic profile and high ASCVD burden, population-specific lipid guidelines are essential. Intensive LDL-C and non-HDL-C lowering, comprehensive risk stratification, and early combination therapy, alongside sustained lifestyle modification and optimal management of comorbidities, are key strategies to mitigate the growing epidemic of ASCVD in South Asian populations.

Title: Real-world threshold-based eligibility for emerging lipoprotein(a)-targeted therapies in chronic and acute coronary syndrome.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Phase 3 programs are evaluating Lp(a)-lowering therapies using high entry thresholds; however, the real-world prevalence of trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds in secondary prevention remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prevalence of trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds, national apheresis criteria, and the prognostic impact of elevated Lp(a) in a contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) cohort.
METHODS: Patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary center with Lp(a) reported in nmol/L were analyzed. The proportion meeting trial-aligned thresholds (≥150, ≥175, ≥200 nmol/L) and the European Society of Cardiology/European Atherosclerosis Society risk-enhancing threshold (≥105 nmol/L) was estimated. National apheresis criteria were applied. 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and target lesion failure (TLF) were assessed.
RESULTS: Among 5942 patients with PCI, 25.2% had Lp(a) ≥105 nmol/L, with progressively smaller proportions meeting higher thresholds: 18.4% ≥150 nmol/L, 14.8% ≥175 nmol/L, 11.6% ≥200 nmol/L. Lp(a) concentrations were similar in chronic and acute coronary syndrome (CCS and ACS) (CCS, median 28.0 [IQR 9.0-118.5] vs ACS, 25.0 [IQR 9.0-96.5] nmol/L; P = .117). 1.8% to 6.1% met national apheresis criteria. Over 5 years, higher Lp(a) was independently associated with risk of MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1 SD 1.06 [95% CI 1.01-1.12]; P = .015) and TLF (adjusted HR per 1 SD 1.05 [95% CI 1.00-1.10]; P = .044).
CONCLUSION: Elevated Lp(a) was highly prevalent and independently predicted adverse 5-year outcomes in a contemporary PCI cohort. While a substantial proportion met trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds for emerging therapies, few fulfilled apheresis criteria. Systematic Lp(a) testing may improve risk stratification and identify patients meeting trial-aligned Lp(a) thresholds for emerging therapies.

Title: One-year outcomes of hepatic artery stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the international, multicenter HEPATIC registry.
Journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
Abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort.
METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed. Donor-, recipient-, and transplant-related characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was one-year graft and patient survival.
RESULTS: HAS was diagnosed in 1.2% of patients (n = 130; 51% female; median age 4.4 years [IQR 1.4-11.6]), of whom 5% (n = 7) progressed to thrombosis (HAT). One-year graft and patient survival were 93% and 96%, respectively. Management consisted mainly of antithrombotic therapy alone (41.5%) or endovascular therapy (EVT; 41.5%), with no significant difference in one-year graft or patient survival between these approaches. Early HAS (≤21 days post-pLT) was associated with significantly higher one-year graft loss than late HAS (16%vs. 1%; p < 0.001). All deaths occurred in the early HAS group.
CONCLUSIONS: One-year graft and patient survival after HAS were high. Antithrombotic therapy alone and EVT were the most common management strategies. Early HAS was associated with lower one-year survival. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic and treatment criteria are needed for validation.

Title: Development and Prospective Validation of an Interpretable Machine Learning Model Integrating Cardiac MRI Extracellular Volume for 1-Year MACE Prediction Post-STEMI.
Abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Extracellular volume (ECV) quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is a key indicator of myocardial fibrosis and strongly linked to outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). This research focused on the development and validation of an interpretable machine learning (ML) model that incorporates ECV to predict 1-year major adverse cardiac events (MACE) in patients with STEMI following percutaneous coronary intervention.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: MACE prediction models were developed using clinical variables combined with CMR-ECV parameters and validated in a prospective cohort. Feature selection was conducted through Boruta algorithms and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithms, and eight ML algorithms were trained. Model performance was assessed by discrimination and calibration. The top performer was interpreted by Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. An interactive online nomogram was deployed to facilitate personalized perioperative risk management.
RESULTS: Among 673 STEMI patients (derivation: n = 398; prospective validation: n = 275), five key predictors were identified: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), myocardial infarction ECV (MI-ECV), age, and creatine kinase-MB. The random forest model achieved the highest discriminative performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.825, 95% confidence interval: 0.763-0.876). SHAP analysis identified NT-proBNP as the most impactful feature, with LVEF class and MI-ECV ranking next.
CONCLUSION: Integration of CMR-derived ECV into an interpretable machine learning framework enables accurate 1-year MACE risk prediction following STEMI. This approach combines robust discriminative performance with clinical transparency through SHAP-based explanations, offering a proof-of-concept tool for precision cardiovascular care.

Title: Performance of large language models in complex coronary artery disease decision-making and potential improvement strategy in a real-world cohort.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Previous studies have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can achieve performance comparable to multidisciplinary heart teams (HTs) in coronary revascularisation decision-making but limited by population bias. We aimed to assess LLMs’ performance in complex coronary artery disease (CAD) decision-making using a real-world cohort and to explore the potential improvement strategy.
METHODS: Patients with stable CAD and angiographically confirmed three-vessel or left main disease randomly selected from a consecutive angiography registry study were included in this cross-sectional study. ChatGPT-4.1 was used to provide five-category treatment decisions based on inputted patient information and a prompt most commonly used by real-world patients. The primary outcome was the agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations. Three predefined prompting strategies were further evaluated for their potential to enhance agreement rates.
RESULTS: A total of 564 patients were included. The agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations was 47.0% based on initial prompt. LLM performed poorly in further testing (sensitivity=0.0%) decision. LLM performed well in patients with Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery score ≥33 (94.1%) but poorly in 23–32 (61.7%) and 0–22 (20.9%). After using prompting strategies, the agreement rate increased significantly (79.3%, p<0.001).
DISCUSSION: Simple patient-style queries cannot independently generate reliable decisions for real-world complex revascularisation scenarios. While prompt engineering and subgroup analysis can partially improve LLM’s performance, the potential safety risk remains emphasised.
CONCLUSION: Among a real-world cohort of patients with complex CAD, the agreement rate of decision-making between LLM and HTs was only half, but could be improved with appropriate prompts.

Title: Clinical heterogeneity in performance of a commercial prediction model for clinical deterioration.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although the Epic Deterioration Index (EDI) model is widely used in US hospitals, heterogeneity in its performance among patient subgroups remains unclear. Our objective was to assess EDI performance when applied across clinical service lines and hospital locations to inform clinical utility.
METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated EDI performance among adult inpatients at a Northern California academic hospital from 2021 to 2024. The EDI score, calculated every 15 min, was assessed for its ability to predict deterioration events defined as intensive care unit transfer, rapid response team activation, comfort care initiation or death. Model performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration curves and confusion matrix statistics using individual EDI scores and an event horizon of 12 hours. Sensitivity analysis considered event horizons of 2, 4, 8 and 24 hours.
RESULTS: Among 77 478 encounters, 10 579 events occurred, with an overall AUROC of 0.763 (95% CI 0.759 to 0.768). Performance varied by clinical service, highest in haematology/oncology/bone marrow transplant (AUROC 0.815) and lowest in cardiology (0.670) and neurosciences (0.677). Similar variability was observed across hospital locations.
DISCUSSION: Considerable variability in predictive performance was found across clinical subpopulations in a hospital setting, highlighting the limitations of the common practice of hospital-wide deployment of predictive models.
CONCLUSION: Understanding the differential performance of predictive models among clinically relevant patient subgroups is paramount to the safe, effective and precise deployment of models in the inpatient setting.

Title: Effectiveness and safety of coenzyme Q10 in people with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
OBJECTIVES: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) supplementation has previously shown efficacy in improving symptoms and outcomes for people with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. This review aims to assess whether CoQ10 may also be effective and safe for those with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
DATA SOURCES: We searched databases including Embase, MEDLINE, CENTRAL, Web of Science, CINAHL, AMED, ClinicalTrials.gov and the ISRCTN registry on 25 June 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults (≥18 years) with HFpEF, defined as an ejection fraction of ≥50%. Eligible studies compared any CoQ10 regimen with placebo or standard care.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB2 and the certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). We conducted random-effects pairwise meta-analysis where possible, using the RevMan V.5.4 software. Synthesis without meta-analysis was conducted for other outcomes.
RESULTS: Three RCTs (264 participants) with a treatment duration of 8–24 weeks were included. The effect of CoQ10 on mortality in individuals with HFpEF was very uncertain (2/101 participants receiving CoQ10 vs 0/105 participants receiving placebo). No cardiovascular deaths occurred in either group (206 participants, very low certainty evidence). The effect of CoQ10 on hospitalisation due to heart failure was very uncertain (1/19 participants receiving CoQ10 vs 0/20 participants receiving placebo). Evidence on quality of life was mixed and also considered very uncertain, with one study indicating benefit from CoQ10 (mean difference (MD) 22.41 points on the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire, 95% CI 12.18 to 32.64, 73 participants) and another indicating no benefit (MD −8.52 points, 95% CI −19.20 to 2.16, 66 participants).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence is insufficient to determine whether CoQ10 improves outcomes in HFpEF. Larger, high-quality and adequately powered RCTs using consistent diagnostic criteria are needed before CoQ10 can be recommended in clinical practice.

Title: Causal discovery and treatment effect heterogeneity of futile recanalisation (CADISTH) for large vessel occlusion stroke: protocol and rationale for a multicentre prospective cohort study.
Abstract:
ABSTRACT: 
INTRODUCTION: Endovascular therapy (EVT) achieves high rates of successful recanalisation (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥2 b) in large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke; however, functional recovery remains limited. Futile recanalisation (FR)—defined as poor functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 3–6) despite successful reperfusion—occurs in over half of patients. The underlying causal mechanisms and inter-individual heterogeneity of FR remain poorly understood, hindering effective prevention and personalised management. This study aims to apply causal discovery algorithms to identify determinants of FR and to quantify heterogeneous treatment effects using causal forest models.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Causal discovery and treatment effect heterogeneity (CADISTH) is a multicentre prospective cohort study. Consecutive acute ischaemic stroke patients with LVO who achieve successful reperfusion after EVT initiated within 24 hours of onset will be enrolled. The primary outcome is FR (mRS 3–6 at 90 days). Secondary outcomes include: (a) efficacy—neurological status (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS)) and quality of life (EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level Version (EQ-5D-5L)) assessed at 24 hours, 7 days and 90, 180 and 365 days and (b) safety—symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage within 48 hours and all-cause mortality at 90, 180 and 365 days. The CADISTH study will: (1) explore candidate causal structures underlying FR by integrating real-world data with automated causal discovery algorithms and (2) characterise heterogeneity in treatment effects of modifiable factors across patient subgroups to inform prevention strategies and individualised patient selection.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study protocol has been approved by the Biomedical Research Ethics Committee of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University (No. [2025] 41) with local approval at each site. All participants will provide written informed consent prior to enrolment. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and conferences.

Title: Antithrombotic therapy regimens after transcatheter valve-in-valve and valve-in-ring procedures: a scoping review.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe the existing literature on antithrombotic strategies employed after transcatheter valve-in-valve (ViV) and valve-in-ring (ViR) procedures across all valve groups and to provide recommendations for areas of further research.
DESIGN: We conducted a scoping review reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines.
DATA SOURCES: We systematically searched CENTRAL, EMBASE and MEDLINE from database inception until 19 January 2026. Reference lists of included studies were also manually screened.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised-controlled trials, cohort or case-control studies reporting efficacy and/or safety outcomes of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing transcatheter ViV or ViR procedures involving aortic, mitral, tricuspid and/or pulmonary valves were included.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Records were screened for eligibility and data were extracted using a structured charting form. Results were synthesised descriptively and grouped according to valve type.
RESULTS: Of 444 studies screened, 41 were included (10 aortic ViV, 27 mitral ViV/ViR, 1 pulmonary ViV, 1 tricuspid ViV and 2 aortic and mitral ViV). Median sample size was 32 (IQR 14–91; range 5–4243). Ten studies reported a uniform antithrombotic strategy; 30 reported variable strategies, and 1 reported only a protocol-recommended strategy without observed use or adherence. Anticoagulation, with or without antiplatelet therapy, was commonly reported following mitral ViV/ViR, while regimens reported following aortic ViV were highly variable but antiplatelet therapy predominated slightly over anticoagulant therapy. Thrombotic and bleeding outcomes were reported in a highly heterogenous manner.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence guiding antithrombotic therapy after ViV is heterogeneous and largely observational, underscoring the need for high-quality studies to inform optimal management.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: This scoping review is registered on the Open Science Framework and can be accessed at: https://osf.io/exvc2/overview?view_only=aeb99d7b79734510826a8ce408e70b03.

Title: Impact of atrial fibrillation catheter ablation o'n tricuspid regurgitation severity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) commonly coexist and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Whether restoration of sinus rhythm through catheter ablation improves TR severity has not been systematically quantified. We evaluated the association between AF catheter ablation and changes in moderate or greater TR.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating patients with AF undergoing catheter ablation and reporting paired preablation and postablation assessments of TR severity. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and Web of Science were searched from inception to 22 April 2026. The primary outcome was change in the prevalence of moderate or greater TR following ablation. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed using restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Meta-regression evaluated prespecified study-level modifiers, including sex proportion, mean age and baseline AF type.
RESULTS: 17 studies comprising 2747 patients were included. AF catheter ablation was associated with a lower prevalence of moderate or greater TR (risk difference −0.21, 95% CI −0.33 to −0.09; pooled risk ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.60), although heterogeneity was substantial (I²=98.3%) and the 95% prediction interval was wide (−0.74 to 0.31). Patients who maintained sinus rhythm had greater TR reduction than those with recurrent AF (risk difference −0.28, 95% CI −0.55 to −0.01). In meta-regression, higher proportions of female participants and persistent AF were associated with greater TR improvement, whereas mean left ventricular ejection fraction was not. Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to studies at low-to-moderate risk of bias, observational studies and leave-one-out analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: AF catheter ablation was associated with a significant reduction in moderate or greater TR, with greater improvement among patients maintaining sinus rhythm. These findings support prospective evaluation of rhythm control as a potential strategy for patients with moderate or greater TR and AF.

Title: Multimodal artificial intelligence to predict cardiomyopathy development in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) is a rare multisystem disorder with marked phenotypic heterogeneity. Cardiac involvement, a major prognostic determinant, often develops years after neurological onset and remains clinically silent in early stages, delaying diagnosis and treatment. We developed a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model integrating clinical, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic data to predict cardiomyopathy in patients with ATTRv but without baseline cardiac involvement.
METHODS: Adult patients with genetically confirmed ATTRv amyloidosis evaluated at four Italian tertiary referral centres between 2011 and 2026 were retrospectively included. Only patients without evidence of cardiac involvement at baseline were eligible. A machine learning model was developed using structured clinical variables, while deep learning models were trained on electrocardiographic and echocardiographic data. These models were integrated into a multimodal ensemble framework. Primary endpoint was development of ATTRv cardiomyopathy (ATTRv-CM), defined as scintigraphy-based diagnostic criteria for ATTR-CM in the absence of monoclonal gammopathy and evidence of left ventricular maximal wall thickness exceeding 12 mm.
RESULTS: The cohort included 97 patients (63 mutation carriers and 34 with only mild neurological involvement). Over a mean follow-up of 2.5±2.2 years (IQR 1–3), 15 patients developed cardiomyopathy. Unimodal models showed good predictive performance (all training set area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the range of 0.86–0.94, all test set AUC within 0.74–0.89). The multimodal ensemble achieved optimal performance, with 100% accuracy and an F1 score of 1.0, in predicting ATTR-CM.
CONCLUSIONS: Multimodal AI enables early prediction of cardiac involvement in ATTRv, supporting personalised surveillance and optimised clinical management.

Title: Putative Butyrate-Producing Gut Bacteria Profile and Muscle Health in Older Post-Stroke Patients.
Abstract:
AIM: Muscle health is a clinically relevant dimension of vulnerability in older post-stroke patients, but its gut microbial correlates remain unclear. We examined whether a taxonomy-based putative butyrate-producing gut bacteria profile was associated with admission muscle health.
METHODS: This registry-based cross-sectional study included patients aged 65 years or older with 16S rRNA gut microbiota data and no systemic antibiotic exposure within 4 weeks before stool sampling. A six-genera profile was constructed from genus-level relative abundance using centered log-ratio transformation, standardization, and averaging. Outcomes were handgrip strength, skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), body mass index-indexed appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM/BMI), and sarcopenia by Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 criteria. Models adjusted for age, sex, comorbidity, premorbid function, nutritional risk, and inflammation.
RESULTS: Among 136 patients (mean age 78.7 years; 55.1% men), 80 (58.8%) had sarcopenia. After adjustment, a higher profile was associated with higher handgrip strength (β 1.85 kg, 95% CI 0.61-3.09), SMI (β 0.30 kg/m2, 95% CI 0.07-0.54), and ASM/BMI (β 0.04, 95% CI 0.01-0.07), and lower sarcopenia prevalence (prevalence ratio 0.81 per standard deviation, 95% CI 0.71-0.93). Exploratory genus-level signals were most apparent for Agathobacter and Butyricicoccus.
CONCLUSION: A taxonomy-based putative butyrate-producing gut bacteria profile was associated with better admission muscle health in older post-stroke rehabilitation patients. These findings support a gut-muscle phenotype association, not microbial function or causality.

Title: Evidence on Valve Selection for Small Aortic Annuli in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
Abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients with small aortic annuli presents unique challenges related to prosthesis-patient mismatch, residual gradients, conduction disturbances, and lifetime valve management. Recent observational data have suggested potential differences in mid-term survival between self-expanding valve and balloon-expandable valve platforms; however, these findings have not been consistently supported by other observational studies or long-term randomized evidence. Importantly, both severe prosthesis-patient mismatch and permanent pacemaker implantation may carry prognostic implications, underscoring the competing risks involved in valve selection. In conclusion, current evidence does not establish the clinical superiority of one transcatheter valve platform over another, supporting an individualized approach to valve selection.

Title: Schisandra chinensis in sepsis intervention through multi-target mechanisms and organ protection.
Abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by overwhelming inflammation, oxidative stress, immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive multiple organ injury. Schisandra chinensis (S. chinensis) and its bioactive constituents possess anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and organ-protective properties, but their sepsis-related evidence has not been comprehensively summarized. This narrative review critically summarizes the current evidence on S. chinensis and its bioactive constituents in sepsis, with emphasis on inflammatory regulation, immune homeostasis, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, regulated cell death, and sepsis-associated organ injury. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched without restriction on publication year, and the reference lists of relevant publications were also screened. Eligible studies were narratively synthesized according to intervention type, experimental model, biological effects, signaling pathways, and organ outcomes, with evidence from isolated or chemically characterized constituents distinguished from that derived from multicomponent preparations. Current evidence, derived predominantly from in vitro and LPS- or CLP-induced animal studies, indicates that S. chinensis constituents may attenuate inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, endothelial barrier disruption, and sepsis-associated lung and myocardial injury through the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB, JAK2/STAT3, NLRP3, Nrf2/GPX4, RhoA/ROCK1/MLC and MAPK pathways. However, clinical evidence remains limited and is mainly based on multicomponent traditional Chinese medicine preparations, preventing determination of the independent contribution of S. chinensis. Overall, S. chinensis is a promising but investigational adjunctive candidate for sepsis. Future studies should prioritize chemically standardized preparations, pharmacokinetic and safety characterization, causal validation of reproducible mechanisms, and biomarker-based identification of responsive sepsis phenotypes before early-phase and randomized clinical trials.

Title: Dietary Patterns and Chronic Disease Risk: A Proteomic Framework to Strengthen Causal Inference.
Abstract: The strength of evidence in nutrition research is hampered by the difficulty of maintaining long-term dietary compliance in randomized trials. Despite providing valuable evidence, short-term feeding trials typically rely on a limited set of surrogate outcomes, and observational studies are susceptible to measurement error and residual confounding. We propose a complementary research framework that integrates randomized feeding trials with Mendelian randomization (MR) using proteomic markers to strengthen causal inference in nutrition research. In this approach, feeding trials are used to identify proteins that respond to dietary patterns, and MR analyses are subsequently used to assess whether these diet-responsive proteins are relevant to the development of chronic diseases. In addition to instrumenting individual proteins, we propose using genetic scores to instrument proteomic signatures of dietary patterns in MR analyses. We argue that proteins are particularly informative biomarkers because they reflect multiple biological pathways involved in disease pathophysiology and can often be instrumented with cis-protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs), which reduces concerns about horizontal pleiotropy compared with other MR approaches. To illustrate the feasibility of several steps in the proposed approach, we highlight studies of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet. This research shows that randomized feeding trials can identify reproducible proteomic changes and that several of these associations can be confirmed in population-based cohort studies. We further note that selected diet-related proteins have been associated with the risk of type 2 diabetes in prospective studies and, in some cases, supported by MR and colocalization analyses. We also discuss potential limitations, including incomplete proteomic coverage, measurement error, epitope effects, and challenges in satisfying MR assumptions. In sum, we argue that a cross-design, proteomic-based research strategy can contribute to the triangulation of evidence in nutrition research, generating more specific and robust dietary recommendations for chronic disease prevention.

Title: Characterizing One-Year Mortality in Early Survivors of Open Thoracoabdominal Aortic Repair.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although operative mortality after open thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is well characterized, only limited data describe 1-year survival among patients who survive the index hospitalization. This study sought to further characterize 1-year mortality among operative survivors of open TAAA repair.
METHODS: From January 1986 through July 2025, 3838 open TAAA repairs were performed within our single practice. After operative deaths and patients lacking 1-year follow-up were excluded, 3378 early survivors comprised the study cohort. Demographic, operative, and postoperative data were compared between patients who survived ≥1 year after repair and those who did not. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 1-year mortality.
RESULTS: Among early survivors, 328 (9.7%) died within 1 year. One-year mortality was associated with older age, prior percutaneous coronary intervention, prior stroke, and chronic kidney disease. Postoperative complications-namely paraplegia (odds ratio [OR] 1.96, P=.03), dialysis dependence (OR 2.00, P=.001), arrhythmia (OR 1.48, P=.01), tracheostomy (OR 2.17, P<.001), and 1-year repair failure (OR 5.13, P<.001)-independently predicted death, whereas elective repair (OR 0.57, P<.001) and discharge home (OR 0.38, P<.001) predicted 1-year survival. Model discrimination was good (C-statistic=0.77 [0.74-0.81]). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed markedly greater 1-year survival in patients initially discharged home (94%) versus elsewhere (73%; P<.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among operative survivors of open TAAA repair, 1-year mortality remains considerable and is primarily determined by persistent postoperative complications and repair durability rather than intraoperative variables. Vigilant surveillance, structured rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary follow-up may be needed to ensure success beyond the perioperative period.

Title: The role of vitamin D in pulmonary arterial hypertension: From vascular biology to patient outcomes.
Abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease characterized by endothelial dysfunction, excessive vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and right ventricular failure. In recent years, vitamin D (VitD) has emerged as a potential modulator of several biological pathways implicated in PAH pathobiology. Beyond its classical role in calcium and phosphate homeostasis, VitD exerts pleiotropic effects through activation of the VitD receptor, which is expressed in pulmonary artery endothelial cells and smooth muscle cells. Experimental evidence indicates that VitD signaling is associated with the regulation of key mechanisms involved in PAH, including endothelial nitric oxide production, prostacyclin and endothelin pathways, Endothelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition, smooth muscle cell proliferation, inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Studies conducted in experimental pulmonary hypertension models, including models with PAH-like vascular remodeling, have reported associations between VitD restoration and improved pulmonary hemodynamics, right ventricular function, endothelial function, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. However, these models do not fully recapitulate human Group 1 PAH and therefore their findings should be interpreted cautiously. Clinical studies have demonstrated a high prevalence of VitD deficiency among patients with PAH, although several studies have included heterogeneous pH populations, and lower circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels have been associated with worse functional class, reduced exercise capacity, more severe hemodynamic impairment, right ventricular dysfunction, and poorer survival. However, clinical evidence regarding the benefits of VitD supplementation remains limited and is mainly derived from small observational studies and uncontrolled interventions. This narrative review summarizes the current experimental and clinical evidence linking VitD to PAH pathobiology and patient outcomes, highlighting potential mechanistic pathways and discussing the opportunities and challenges for future therapeutic strategies. Although available data support a biologically plausible association between VitD/VitD receptor signaling and pulmonary vascular homeostasis, adequately powered randomized controlled trials are required to determine whether correction of VitD deficiency is associated with improved clinical outcomes in PAH.

Title: American Radium Society Appropriate Use Criteria: Accelerated hypofractionated radiotherapy in the multidisciplinary management of locally-advanced non-small cell lung cancer ineligible for concurrent chemotherapy.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While accelerated hypofractionated radiotherapy has increasingly been adopted in the multidisciplinary management of locally-advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ineligible for concurrent chemotherapy, there is a paucity of randomized prospective evidence guiding utilization. Given the marked heterogeneity in the presentations of locally-advanced NSCLC, the American Radium Society (ARS) Thoracic Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) Panel evaluated the appropriateness of accelerated hypofractionation in the context of multidisciplinary management.
METHODS: Five clinical variants representing manifestations of locally-advanced NSCLC were developed by the 15-member multidisciplinary ARS Thoracic AUC panel. The English-language medical literature was formally reviewed from 2010-2025 and scrutinized for prospective clinical trials utilizing accelerated hypofractionation for concurrent chemotherapy ineligible patients. All case variants were evaluated with respect to use of radiation technique, radiation fractionation, and utilization of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy with Modified Delphi methodology. Consensus recommendations were reviewed and approved by the ARS Executive Committee and subject to public comment.
RESULTS: The literature review identified 228 articles, of which there were 14 prospective trials/registries including nine Phase I-II trials, four prospective registries, and one randomized Phase III trial. There was consensus that it is appropriate to utilize intensity modulated radiation therapy and proton therapy across presentations of locally-advanced NSCLC, with the aim of constraining the lung V20Gy<30% and heart V40Gy<20% with accelerated hypofractionation. When utilizing 15-fraction accelerated hypofractionation for disease abutting the esophagus or brachial plexus, there was consensus that it is inappropriate to exceed doses of 45-55 Gy. With respect to PD-L1 immunotherapy, there was consensus that consolidative immunotherapy after definitive radiation therapy is appropriate, but that concurrent immunotherapy is inappropriate. There was panel consensus that it may be appropriate to utilize induction PD-L1 immunotherapy prior to radiation therapy in cases of bulky or N3 disease to test disease biology. Across variants, there was consensus that conventionally fractionated radiotherapy to 60 Gy in 30 fractions remains appropriate.
CONCLUSIONS: The ARS Thoracic AUC Panel has provided consensus case-based guidelines on the multidisciplinary management of locally-advanced NSCLC ineligible for concurrent chemotherapy reflecting the heterogeneity of disease presentation in this population. In absence of randomized prospective data demonstrating superiority of accelerated hypofractionation, conventionally fractionated radiotherapy remains an appropriate option.

Title: The Liver-Heart Axis: Linking Liver Stiffness to Early Cardiac Dysfunction in MASLD.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder with cardiovascular consequences. Conventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction fail to identify early myocardial impairment. The present prospective study was undertaken to evaluate subclinical myocardial dysfunction in MASLD using global longitudinal strain (GLS), assess its correlation with liver stiffness measurement (LSM), and identify its independent predictors.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 128 patients with MASLD. GLS was assessed by speckle-tracking echocardiography, and liver stiffness was measured using vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan). A GLS value ≥ 18% was considered abnormal (indicative of subclinical left ventricular dysfunction). Correlation and regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of subclinical myocardial dysfunction.
RESULTS: Subclinical myocardial dysfunction (GLS ≥ 18%) was detected in 74.2% of MASLD patients despite preserved ejection fraction. Liver stiffness correlated strongly with impaired GLS (r = 0.722, p < 0.001). Patients with abnormal GLS had significantly higher liver stiffness (8.98 ± 1.24 kPa vs. 6.95 ± 0.85 kPa, p < 0.001). Fibrosis stage showed a graded association with worsening GLS. On regression analysis, liver stiffness and body mass index (BMI) emerged as independent predictors of subclinical myocardial dysfunction, while steatosis (CAP) did not correlate with GLS.
CONCLUSIONS: MASLD patients demonstrate a high prevalence of early cardiac dysfunction that is strongly associated with liver stiffness. Myocardial strain imaging combined with liver stiffness measurement offers a valuable approach for early cardio-hepatic risk stratification and integrated care of MASLD patients.
IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: MASLD confers a "silent" cardiac burden, with nearly three-quarters of patients showing subclinical left ventricular dysfunction despite normal ejection fraction. Our study identifies liver stiffness as the key correlate of this cardiac impairment, whereas steatosis alone was not correlated with myocardial dysfunction. These findings suggest that integrating myocardial strain imaging and liver stiffness assessment can enable earlier identification of at-risk MASLD patients, underscoring the need for multidisciplinary management bridging hepatology and cardiology.

Title: From animal behavior to human perioperative neurocognitive disorders: Translational boundaries of the gut-brain axis.
Abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), including postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder, are common after surgery in older adults, and the gut-brain axis has been proposed as a contributing pathway. Most mechanistic support rests on rodent behavioral assays, yet these endpoints and human clinical diagnoses are routinely treated as interchangeable. This critical narrative review examines that translational boundary. PND is used here as a clinically consequential test case for a broader behavioral-neuroscience problem: how animal behavioral phenotypes, microbiome-associated signals, and intervention effects should be translated into human diagnostic constructs. A structured search identified and appraised the principal evidence rather than an exhaustive synthesis; no formal risk-of-bias or certainty-of-evidence assessment was performed. Evidence was separated into human perioperative studies reporting a neurocognitive outcome with either a measured gut-brain exposure or a gut-directed intervention; those reporting gut-brain change without a cognitive outcome; perioperative preclinical evidence; and indirect non-perioperative evidence. The retrieved human perioperative evidence spans observational cohorts across gastric, orthopedic, spinal and cardiac surgery, multi-omic and metabolomic cohorts, and randomized perioperative probiotic trials reporting lower rates of study-defined cognitive outcomes. It nonetheless remains heterogeneous and largely single-center, with modest event numbers, inconsistent sampling and assessment, and limited external validation. Mechanistic support still comes mainly from perioperative rodent models using water maze, fear-conditioning, recognition-memory, and delirium-like readouts, which measure narrow, species-specific capacities and are not diagnostic equivalents of POD, DNR, or postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Microbiome-mediated causation is unproven, and cross-species endpoint alignment remains a central route to improved translation.

Title: First-in-Human Safety and Pharmacokinetic Evaluation of Seralutinib, an Investigational Inhaled Tyrosine-protein Kinase Inhibitor for Pulmonary Hypertension.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: First-in-human studies were conducted to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of single and multiple doses of inhaled seralutinib in healthy participants.
METHODS: Two phase I, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies were conducted. In Study 1, participants received single ascending doses of seralutinib (3.75-48 mg) or placebo (Part 1) and multiple ascending doses of seralutinib (18 mg BID, 24 mg TID, and 48 mg TID) or placebo for 7 days (Part 2). In Study 2, participants received a single dose of seralutinib 90 mg or placebo (Part 1) and multiple doses of seralutinib (90 mg BID) or placebo for 7 days (Part 2). Sentinel dosing strategy was utilized for all cohorts. Safety was assessed. Seralutinib PK was characterized.
RESULTS: 82 healthy participants completed the studies (20 received placebo; 37, single doses of seralutinib; 25, multiple doses of seralutinib BID or TID for 7 days). No serious adverse events (AEs) or AEs leading to withdrawal were reported. Most AEs were mild in severity. Following single and multiple dose inhalations, seralutinib was quickly absorbed (median tmax 5 minutes) into, and rapidly cleared from the systemic circulation. Mean terminal elimination half-life was 3.08-5.75 hours. Seralutinib exposures increased in an approximately dose-proportional manner. Steady-state plasma levels were reached by Day 3 (multiple doses). Minimal accumulation in plasma was observed after multiple days of BID or TID doses.
CONCLUSION: Consistent with its PK profile, seralutinib administered as single or multiple doses was generally well tolerated, with a favorable safety profile in healthy adults.

Title: Preoperative white matter lesions and functional recovery after revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Restoring ambulation is an important goal of revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), but predictors of functional recovery remain limited. We investigated whether preoperative white matter lesion (WML) burden was associated with ambulatory recovery after revascularization.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 196 patients with CLTI, tissue loss, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) ischemia grade 2 or 3, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) within 3 months before revascularization. Preoperative brain MRI was routinely obtained in patients considered for open surgical revascularization for cerebrovascular risk assessment. Periventricular and deep subcortical white matter hyperintensities were graded using the Fazekas scale; a total score of 3 or greater defined high-grade WML burden. The primary outcome was achievement of a Functional Ambulation Category score of 3 or greater within 180 days. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox models.
RESULTS: High-grade WML burden was present in 120 patients. Six-month ambulatory recovery was lower in the high-grade group than in the low-grade group (63.1% vs 82.4%; P = .019). High-grade WML burden was independently associated with slower ambulatory recovery (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.96; P = .032) and delayed final discharge (adjusted HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43-0.92; P = .017), but not with wound healing or wound-free functional limb achievement.
CONCLUSIONS: High-grade WML burden was associated with impaired ambulatory recovery and delayed discharge after CLTI revascularization. When preoperative brain MRI is available, WML assessment may complement limb staging and help anticipate rehabilitation and discharge needs.

Title: Mid-Term Outcomes of Percutaneous Decannulation for Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning: A Single-Centre Experience.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is an established therapy for severe cardiac failure, but femoral decannulation remains associated with significant morbidity. Percutaneous decannulation has emerged as an alternative to surgical cutdown; however, published experience remains limited. This study evaluates a fully percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation strategy using the Abbott ProStyle vascular closure device compared with open surgical cutdown.
METHODS: A retrospective single-centre matched cohort study identified all patients undergoing intended percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation between November 2023 and January 2026 and matched them to a surgical cutdown cohort according to age and sex. Outcomes were assessed by intention-to-treat, with technically successful cases evaluated secondarily.
RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients underwent intended percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation. Technical success was achieved in 82% (n = 23), with five conversions to open cutdown. On intention-to-treat analysis, procedural duration was shorter (94.1 ± 26.3 vs 121.7 ± 46.9 minutes, p = .063) and groin wound complications were less frequent (7.1% vs 25.0%, p = .077), although neither reached statistical significance. Among technically successful percutaneous decannulations, procedural duration was significantly shorter (88.0 ± 28.7 vs 120.8 ± 50.0 minutes, p = .020) and groin wound complications significantly lower (4.3% vs 30.4%, p = .047). Survival to discharge was similar between groups (p = .78).
CONCLUSION: Percutaneous VA-ECMO decannulation achieved 82% technical success, with numerically shorter procedural duration and fewer groin wound complications on intention-to-treat analysis. Among technically successful cases, both outcomes were significantly improved compared with surgical cutdown.

Title: Anatomic Level as a Modifier of Racial/Ethnic Disparities in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: Outcomes After First-Time Endovascular Revascularization.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Racial and ethnic disparities in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) outcomes are well documented, but whether these disparities vary by anatomic level of endovascular intervention remains unclear. We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in limb outcomes following endovascular revascularization for CLTI stratified by intervention level.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, including adults undergoing first-time lower extremity endovascular revascularization for CLTI between 2015-2024. Patients were stratified by intervention level: iliac, femoropopliteal, tibioperoneal, or combined femoropopliteal and tibioperoneal (multilevel). Propensity score matching balanced demographics and comorbidities across racial/ethnic cohorts. The primary outcomes were rates of 1-year major amputation and amputation-free survival (AFS). Outcome comparisons were reported as risk ratios (RR).
RESULTS: Among 14,786 patients, there were 3,071 iliac, 5,178 femoropopliteal, 2,363 tibioperoneal, and 3,718 multilevel interventions. After matching, Black patients demonstrated increased major amputation risk following iliac intervention (RR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.13-2.88, p=0.012) and femoropopliteal intervention (RR: 1.83, 95% CI 1.39-2.41, p<0.001) compared with White patients. No significant differences in amputation were observed following tibioperoneal or multilevel interventions. Hispanic patients exhibited increased amputation risk only in the multilevel cohort (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.40, p=0.037). Despite differences in amputation, AFS remained similar across racial and ethnic groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Racial and ethnic disparities in CLTI outcomes following endovascular revascularization varied by anatomic intervention level. Disparities were most pronounced after proximal interventions and attenuated in distal disease, suggesting anatomic disease pattern may modify inequities in limb outcomes after revascularization.

Title: Learning How to Implement Glaucoma Coaching in Academic Medical Centers from a Successful Clinical Trial using Implementation Science.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate implementation of the Support, Educate, Empower (SEE) personalized glaucoma coaching program.
DESIGN: Prospective, two-site randomized clinical trial with an implementation evaluation using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework and the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR).
PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged ≥40 years with glaucoma, glaucoma suspect, or ocular hypertension and poor self-reported medication adherence who were prescribed ≥1 glaucoma medication (n=236 enrolled; additional screened individuals declined [n=1,750] or were ineligible [n=1,701]). Stakeholders (n=8) and participants (n=32) contributed qualitative data.
METHODS: Participants were randomized to a motivational interviewing (MI)-based glaucoma coaching intervention (SEE program) or standard education. Reach was assessed by comparing demographics across recruitment stages. Effectiveness was evaluated by changes in medication adherence, coach autonomy support, and attrition. Implementation fidelity was measured using counselor MI competency scores (passing ≥5). Adoption and maintenance were evaluated through CFIR-guided interviews, post-intervention adherence monitoring, and cost estimates.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Glaucoma medication adherence, program reach, implementation fidelity (MI competency scores), qualitative, stakeholder-informed measures of adoption and maintenance, including post-intervention adherence and program cost.
RESULTS: Of 2057 individuals screened, 356 (17.3%) were eligible, of which 236 (66.3%) enrolled; no demographic differences were observed between enrollees and non-enrollees, however those who declined screening (n=1750) were older and more likely to be White (both p<0.0001) . Adherence was better with personalized coaching than standard education (77.6%±19.7% versus 58.0%±25.2%; p<0.001). MI fidelity was high (mean score 5.7). Facilitators of implementation included participant engagement and workflow compatibility, while barriers included limited awareness, resource constraints, and concerns about financial sustainability. Participants reported improved engagement and motivation. 84% of participants continued monitoring after counseling ended; adherence declined by 10.0%±21.1% at 1 month and an additional 3.6%±11.7% by 2 months and remained below intervention levels thereafter. A coach could manage approximately 431 patients per year, with an estimated net revenue of $19,272 annually after costs.
CONCLUSIONS: The SEE MI-based program demonstrated high fidelity and improved adherence during the intervention. Post-intervention adherence decline demonstrates the need for continued coaching. Strong uptake, stakeholder support, and projected reimbursement suggest feasibility and organizational sustainability in clinical practice.

Title: Epilepsy-associated potassium channel KCNT1 is required for multiciliated cell specification in Xenopus.
Abstract: Pathogenic, presumed gain-of-function variants in the gene KCNT1, which encodes a sodium-activated potassium channel, cause a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with intractable epilepsy. In addition to seizures, affected individuals commonly present with severe respiratory issues and structural heart defects not commonly observed in other genetic pediatric epilepsies, suggesting additional developmental functions for KCNT1 in organs beyond the brain. Here we characterized the spectrum of clinical diagnoses present in a cohort of 46 individuals with genetic variants in KCNT1, ranging from 0 to 19 years of age, by medical record review. We documented the prevalence of diagnoses across organ systems, including dependence on assisted breathing, congenital structural heart defects, urinary dysfunction, and spine deformities, among others. Next, we explored the embryonic expression and function of KCNT1 in diploid frogs (Xenopus tropicalis) and observed expression in developing ciliated tissues such as the brain, heart, kidney, and epidermis. Embryonic perturbation of KCNT1 disrupted developmental signaling pathways and caused ciliogenesis defects in the mucociliary epidermis, a common model for the human airway. Loss of KCNT1 disrupted development of multiciliated cells, reminiscent of recent work on the ion channel Piezo1. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of Piezo signaling enhanced the ciliogenesis phenotype observed following KCNT1 inhibition, while activation of Piezo1 activity partially rescued ciliogenesis in the context of KCNT1 inhibition. Finally, KCNT1 loss reduced expression of foxj1, a key transcriptional regulator of multiciliated cell specification, linking KCNT1 activity to the transcriptional programs underlying multiciliated cell formation and specification. Together, this work establishes that KCNT1 has embryonic functions in Xenopus beyond regulating neuronal activity, specifically in multiciliated cell development, and identifies an interaction with pharmacologically-tractable Piezo channels that may be productive for therapeutic efforts aimed at inhibiting KCNT1 activity.

Title: Preoperative Risk-assessment Score for Elective Total Aortic Arch Repair: AAORTA Risk Tool.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Total transverse aortic arch replacement is a complex operation performed to address aortic aneurysm with and without chronic aortic dissection. To predict 90-day survival after this procedure, we created a holistic tool for predicting postoperative mortality in patients who undergo total arch repair (TAR): the Aortic Arch Operation Risk Tool for Assessment (AAORTA) score.
METHODS: Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed on data from patients (N=470; 243 with nondissecting aneurysm, 227 with chronic Type A dissection) who underwent TAR at a high-volume practice between April 2006 and November 2024. Regression analysis identified variables to be used in the AAORTA score. The predictive performance of the score was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCC), Brier score, and linear fitting.
RESULTS: Of 470 patients who underwent TAR, 65 (13.8%) died within 90 days of repair. The AAORTA score relied on five preoperative variables: heritable thoracic aortic disease, prior coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), kidney disease, pulmonary disease (restrictive or obstructive), and no history of smoking. Previous CABG was the strongest predictor of 90-day mortality. The AAORTA score had an AUROCC of 0.784, a Brier score of 0.105, and a goodness-of-fit R 2 of 0.954.
CONCLUSION: The AAORTA score can accurately stratify 90-day mortality risk in patients who undergo elective TAR, using only five variables easily acquired during standard preoperative evaluation. This score could be used to aid preoperative counseling with patients and families. Prospective multicenter validation will help establish its generalizability.

Title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Coronary Embolism: A Multicenter Study.
Abstract: Coronary embolism (CE) is an uncommon cause of acute myocardial infarction, and the optimal postdischarge antithrombotic strategy remains uncertain.Retrospective multicenter study including patients with definite or probable CE. Three groups of patients were identified: (1) requiring specific management, (2) with atrial fibrillation (AF), and (3) with no indication for oral anticoagulation (OAC). The latter two groups were further classified according to the antithrombotic treatment received, and long-term outcomes (composite of recurrent CE, stroke, systemic embolism, cardiovascular or all-cause death, and major bleeding at 5 years) were subsequently evaluated.A total of 489 patients were considered. Among 189 patients with AF, 85 received direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and 104 vitamin K antagonists (VKAs). VKA users showed a higher rate of the composite endpoint compared with DOACs (40 vs. 18%, p < 0.001), with the difference primarily driven by all-cause mortality. In multivariable analysis, VKA therapy remained independently associated with worse outcomes (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.9, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.02-3.5; p = 0.04). In the 182 patients without an indication for anticoagulation, 115 received antiplatelet therapy and 67 received OAC. Those treated with OAC had a higher incidence of the composite outcome (16 vs. 7%, p = 0.049), with the difference primarily driven by all-cause mortality. Multivariable analysis confirmed OAC as an independent predictor of adverse prognosis (HR: 3.4; 95% CI: 1.2-9.7; p = 0.02).In patients with CE, stratification based on underlying etiology and embolic risk before hospital discharge might serve as a decision-making approach for determining optimal antithrombotic strategies and improved clinical outcomes.

Title: Low complication rates are reported in cats presenting for neurological complaints and undergoing cerebrospinal fluid collection.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess complications, outcomes, and associated risk factors of cats undergoing CSF collection.
METHODS: This was a single-center retrospective cohort study of client-owned cats presenting to 3 referral hospitals for CSF collection from January 2012 through December 2022. Cats were excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaints. If cats had multiple CSF collection presentations, only the first was included. Records were retrospectively assessed for signalment, physical examination findings, modified Glasgow coma scale, general anesthesia (GA) records, diagnostic imaging, clinical pathology results, and suspected or confirmed final diagnosis. Outcomes included complications and nonsurvival > 24 hours following CSF collection. Univariable logistic regression included breed, sex, body weight, age, modified Glasgow coma scale, evidence of herniation, evidence of intracranial hypertension (ICH) without herniation, GA protocol, GA duration, CSF analysis, collection site, inflammatory/infectious, and neoplasia diagnosis. P values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
RESULTS: 120 cats were identified, with 2 excluded for nonspecific and/or extraneural presenting complaint, leaving 118 cats. Seven (5.9%) did not survive > 24 hours following CSF procedure, and 9 (7.6%) reported complications, including apnea, suspected iatrogenic spinal cord trauma, and Cushing reflex. After multiple-comparison correction, no variable was significantly associated with outcome. Evidence of ICH without herniation and nonsurvival reported the largest effect estimate (OR, 36.99). Estimates are imprecise and reported as hypothesis generating.
CONCLUSIONS: Feline CSF collection in this cohort reported low complication rates, and the majority survived > 24 hours after CSF collection.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Imaging review for abnormalities associated with ICH is recommended prior to CSF collection.
