Title: Directional discordance between a deployed commercial 12-lead ECG interpretation algorithm and expert cardiologists, and its distribution by sex and age: a post-deployment audit using PTB-XL.
Abstract: Automated 12-lead ECG algorithms are widely used, yet their disagreement with cardiologists across patient subgroups is rarely audited on public data. We characterized the directional discordance of the GE Marquette 12SL algorithm against expert labels.Methods: In this retrospective audit of 14,885 ECGs from 13,480 patients (PTB-XL/PTB-XL+ dataset), we compared 12SL (v23) statements with standardized cardiologist labels for myocardial infarction (MI), conduction disturbance (CD), and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). We calculated observed agreement and paired marginal differences with 95% confidence intervals. Discordance was modeled using generalized estimating equations incorporating age, sex, and their interaction.Results: Observed agreement was high (0.842-0.896) but directionally divergent. 12SL produced fewer positive statements than cardiologists for CD (paired marginal difference 0.092, 95% CI 0.085-0.098) and more for LVH (-0.070, 95% CI -0.075 to -0.064); MI showed no net difference. The false-negative proportion for CD decreased with age, while false-positive proportions rose with age for CD and MI. For LVH false positives, the age association was strongly modified by sex (interaction 1.60, 95% CI 1.47-1.73), being absent in women but steep in men. The LVH direction was specific to primary 12SL statements and reversed if supportive statements were included.Conclusion: A widely deployed commercial ECG algorithm exhibits diagnosis-specific, directional discordance with expert reading that varies by age and sex, underscoring the value of reproducible post-deployment auditing. Because no clinical gold standard was available, these findings describe agreement with experts rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy.

Title: Arterial-to-end-tidal carbon dioxide gradient as a risk marker for recorded 90-day mortality in intracranial neurosurgery: a retrospective INSPIRE cohort study of patients with early blood gas monitoring.
Abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the first-hour arterial-to-end-tidal carbon dioxide gradient as a marker of recorded 90-day mortality, distinguishing association, component interpretation and incremental prediction.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: INSPIRE v1.4.2, covering surgery from 2011 to 2020.
PATIENTS: Adults undergoing their first eligible intracranial operation with arterial carbon dioxide tension (PaCO₂) recorded within 60 min of anesthesia start. End-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO₂) was paired within ±5 min.
MEASUREMENTS: The outcome was database-recorded all-cause death within 90 days. Firth regression evaluated the gradient without conditioning on either component. The revised principal association model included clinical covariates and contemporaneous mean arterial pressure, heart rate and minute ventilation. Component and internally validated prediction models were secondary.
MAIN RESULTS: Among 1907 patients, 95 deaths were recorded. The clinical gradient odds ratio (OR) per 5 mmHg was 1.38 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.73). The revised principal association model included 1830 patients and 92 events (OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.06-1.69). Conditional component estimates did not establish predominance of either component. Adding the gradient to clinical variables, contemporaneous physiology and ETCO₂ changed optimism-corrected area under the curve from 0.832 to 0.833, without improving the Brier score.
CONCLUSIONS: A larger first-hour gradient was associated with recorded mortality in patients selected for early paired monitoring. Within the evaluated models and metrics, incremental prediction was limited. These findings do not establish a causal mechanism, treatment target or externally validated prediction tool.

Title: Enhanced Early Risk Stratification in Cardiogenic Shock Using Machine Learning: A Hierarchical Clustering Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) exhibits marked clinical heterogeneity, limiting the performance of conventional risk stratification tools like the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) staging system. Machine learning (ML) has identified reproducible CS phenotypes that improve risk prediction, but their temporal consistency across the progression of shock remains incompletely described.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the temporal evolution of ML-derived CS phenotypes across the first 3 intensive care unit (ICU) days and determine whether phenotype trajectories enhance mortality stratification beyond SCAI staging.
METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective registry of 2,906 adults with CS admitted to ICUs between 2016 and 2022, hierarchical agglomerative clustering was applied independently to clinical variables on ICU days 1, 2, and 3.
RESULTS: On day 1, 3 phenotypes emerged: Cardiac (younger, acute myocardial infarction-predominant, preserved renal function; 15% mortality), Cardio-Renal (older, non-acute myocardial infarction-predominant, isolated renal extracardiac impairment, predominantly SCAI A and B on admission; 27% mortality), and Cardio-Metabolic (severe renal and tissue malperfusion, predominantly SCAI D and E on admission; 55% mortality). Similar phenotypes persisted on day 2 and day 3. These ML-derived phenotypes enhanced mortality stratification within each SCAI stage across days 1 to 3.
CONCLUSIONS: Hierarchical clustering reproduced previously identified CS phenotypes that were consistent across the first 3 days of ICU stay, providing an enhanced framework for early risk stratification. Prospective validation is required for clinical implementation.

Title: Electrophysiologic Phenotype Outperforms Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction for Mortality Prediction in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis carries mortality rates approaching 50%. Risk stratification relies heavily on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), yet many fatal cases occur despite preserved systolic function.
OBJECTIVES: The study aims to compare the prognostic value of electrophysiologic involvement vs LVEF in ICI-associated myocarditis.
METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed for ICI-associated myocarditis cases with extractable patient-level data. Electrophysiologic phenotype (EP) was defined by clinically significant conduction disease or ventricular arrhythmia, including high-grade atrioventricular block, ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, or cardiac arrest. LVEF was dichotomized at ≤35%. Cluster-robust logistic regression was used to assess associations with mortality.
RESULTS: From 242 publications, 319 cases were extracted; 180 with complete data comprised the analytical cohort (77 deaths; 42.8% mortality). EP involvement (66.7% of cases) was associated with significantly higher mortality vs EP-negative cases (55.0% vs 18.3%; risk ratio: 3.00; 95% CI: 1.72-5.24; P < 0.001). LVEF ≤35% was not significantly associated with mortality (50.7% vs 38.1%; P = 0.125). Among patients with an LVEF >35%, EP involvement was associated with markedly higher mortality (55.1% vs 11.4%; P < 0.001). In adjusted models, EP remained associated with mortality on both the odds-ratio scale (OR: 5.27; 95% CI: 2.29-12.13; P < 0.001) and risk-ratio scale (RR: 2.94; 95% CI: 1.54-5.59; P < 0.001), whereas LVEF ≤35% was not independently associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Electrophysiologic involvement is a dominant prognostic marker in ICI-associated myocarditis, particularly for risk stratification among patients with an LVEF >35%. Risk stratification should prioritize cardiac rhythm monitoring and identification of conduction abnormalities over reliance on LVEF alone.

Title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Physiology-Guided vs Angiography-Guided Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: From the FARGO Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) may reduce unnecessary grafts and improve outcomes. However, in the FARGO (Fractional Flow Reserve vs Angiography Randomization for Graft Optimization) trial, FFR was reduced significantly after 6 months in deferred lesions.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term clinical outcomes after FFR-guided CABG compared to angiography-guided CABG.
METHODS: In this multicenter randomized clinical trial, 100 patients were randomized to FFR-guided (n = 50) or angiography-guided CABG (n = 50). Patients underwent a 6-month follow-up coronary angiography with FFR in deferred lesions. In this extended long-term follow-up revascularization, myocardial infarction, stroke, death, and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), a composite of the individual endpoints, were assessed.
RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 8.8 years (IQR: 8.3, 9.3), patients in the FFR-guided group had significantly more MACCE compared to the angiography-guided group, (26 [52%] vs 16 [32%], log-rank test P = 0.03). This difference was driven by significantly more long-term revascularization, FFR-guided CABG 32% vs angiography-guided 12%, log-rank test P = 0.01. The revascularization rate was significantly higher from 0 to 1 year (12 [24%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.01), whereas beyond 1 year, rates were similar (4 [8%] vs 3 [6%], log-rank test P = 0.47). Most patients had stable symptoms, and revascularization was symptom-driven. Myocardial infarction (6 [12%] vs 3 [6%]), death (10 [20%] vs 7 [14%]), and stroke (6 [12%] vs 6 [12%]) did not differ significantly between the groups.
CONCLUSIONS: FFR-guided CABG was associated with a significantly higher rate of MACCE after CABG, driven by more revascularization within the first year.

Title: Machine Learning of Echocardiographic Left Ventricular Myocardial Radiomics for Identification of Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is an important cause of heart failure (HF) with increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness that can be challenging to distinguish from other LV hypertrophic processes. Echocardiographic myocardial radiomic texture analysis may identify imperceptible amyloid-induced structural changes.
OBJECTIVES: The study aims to develop and validate an echocardiography-based machine learning model using myocardial radiomics to identify ATTR-CM.
METHODS: In this retrospective and prospective multicenter study, 854 echocardiographic scans were analyzed. Conventional and novel radiomic features were extracted from parasternal short-axis views at basal, mid, and apical LV levels, with incorporated age and sex from echocardiogram metadata. A machine learning pipeline was developed using a balanced training set (150 ATTR-CM, 150 nonamyloid HF). Performance was evaluated on an independent internal validation set (50 ATTR-CM, 399 nonamyloid HF) and an external validation set (10 ATTR-CM, 10 immunoglobulin light-chain-amyloid, 10 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, 75 nonamyloid HF).
RESULTS: In internal validation, the model achieved 86% sensitivity (95% CI: 73.8%-93%), 92% specificity (95% CI: 88.9%-94.3%), 57.3% positive predictive value (95% CI: 46.1%-67.9%), 98.1% negative predictive value (NPV) (95% CI: 96.2%-99.1%), and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve 0.938 (95% CI: 0.891-0.985). Performance was consistent in the external validation (100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity, 33.3% positive predictive value, 100% NPV, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve of 0.917). The model correctly classified 77.3% of nonamyloid HF, 70% of AL-amyloid cases, and 100% of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cases as non-ATTR in subgroup analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed an echocardiographic radiomics-based tool to identify ATTR-CM with excellent discrimination and very high NPV in a cohort that approximates clinical experience. These preliminary findings require validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

Title: Perioperative nicotine replacement therapy and 30-day outcomes following coronary artery bypass graft surgery: A propensity matched analysis of patients with documented tobacco use.
Abstract: Smoking cessation is important after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but perioperative nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) remains inconsistently used because of concerns regarding wound healing and cardiovascular complications. CABG-specific evidence is limited. We evaluated the association between perioperative NRT exposure and 30-day outcomes among patients with tobacco use undergoing isolated CABG. Patients undergoing isolated CABG (2018-2023) were identified in TriNetX. Perioperative NRT was defined by a medication order or administration record 14 days before though 7 days after surgery. Patients without NRT records were comparators. After propensity matching, 2622 patients were included in each cohort. Mortality was similar (1.79% vs 1.68%; RR 1.07; 95% CI 0.71-1.61; P = 0.75). Major postoperative outcomes were similar. Perioperative NRT exposure was not associated with increased 30-day morbidity or mortality. Because smoking behavior, NRT adherence, formulation, and dose were unavailable, the independent effect of NRT versus nicotine abstinence cannot be determined.

Title: 12-week yoga intervention effect on metabolome in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS): An LC-MS-based study.
Journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a complex, heterogeneous disorder affecting endocrine, reproductive, and metabolic health. It is fundamentally a systemic metabolic defect that, if not addressed in time, can compromise the function of multiple systems, resulting in conditions such as impaired glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is a lifestyle disorder with long-term health implications, requiring a holistic approach for management.
METHODS: This prospective quasi-experimental study involved 60 women (30 diagnosed with PMOS, 30 age and BMI-matched controls). Women with PMOS underwent a 12-week Yoga practice that included physical postures (Asanas), regulated breathing practice (Pranayama), and meditation (Dhyana) under the guidance of a trained therapist. Clinical characteristics and laboratory biochemical data were recorded, followed by an untargeted metabolomics analysis using high-resolution Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid Mass Spectrometer technology to study plasma metabolome changes.
RESULTS: Following Yoga intervention, women with PMOS showed significant improvements in hormonal, anthropometric parameters, and lipid profile. The metabolomics analysis showed that post-Yoga intervention, several key metabolites were significantly downregulated, including glucose, fructose, d-ribose, 3-hydroxybutanoate, taurine, and methylmalonate. However, metabolites like succinate and ascorbate were upregulated. Besides, AUC suggests significant metabolic shifts following Yoga intervention.
CONCLUSION: Yoga offers a holistic, integrated mind-body approach to managing the endocrine, metabolic, and reproductive dysfunction in PMOS and lowers the risk of developing long-term comorbidities.

Title: Maternal and neonatal exposure to mercury in the Amazon: A systematic review.
Journal: Journal of trace elements in medicine and biology : organ of the Society for Minerals and Trace Elements (GMS)
Abstract: This systematic review investigated maternal and neonatal mercury (Hg) exposure in traditional Amazonian populations. Based on a comprehensive search of five databases (Science Direct, Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and Google Scholar), 13 observational studies (cohort and cross-sectional) published between 1998 and 2022 were selected and assessed using the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) Quality Assessment Tool. The results showed transplacental and lactational transfer of Hg, demonstrating consistent positive associations between maternal and fetal contamination levels. However, the absence of significant impacts on growth or neurodevelopment suggests that the nutritional benefits of fish consumption may counteract the deleterious effects of Hg, or that social determinants exert a greater influence than chemical exposure itself. However, it is possible that social variables may have masked the toxicity of Hg in the methodologies used. These findings highlight the complexity of exposure in the region and the need for continuous monitoring of the mother-child dyad.

Title: Early hemodynamic profiles in severely burned patients: A single center cohort study.
Journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Large burns are associated with a massive inflammatory response and catecholamine release leading to complex cardiovascular disorders. Our aim was to describe the early hemodynamic trajectories following severe burns and to identify distinct hemodynamic trajectory patterns.
METHOD: We retrospectively collected data from patients admitted to our burn center for severe burn injuries between January 2017 and April 2025. Hemodynamic data were obtained by transpulmonary thermodilution coupled with pulse wave analysis. Time series for cardiac index (CI), systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI) and heart rate (HR) were analyzed for the first 96 h. Hemodynamic profiles were compared using dynamic time warping (DTW). Clusters were identified through hierarchical clustering.
RESULTS: A total of 107 patients were included (median age 52 years [IQR: 36-65], median total burn surface area burned 40% [IQR: 30-54]); 22 patients died during their ICU stay. In the entire cohort, the hemodynamic profile progressively shifted from a low-cardiac output, vasoconstrictive state to a hyperkinetic, vasoplegic state (CI 2.6 ± 0.8-4.8 ± 1.3 L/min/m2; SVRI 3362[2659-4489] to 1382[1118-1698] dyn.s.cm-5.m2, p < 0.05). Cluster analysis identified two hemodynamic trajectory patterns, one with CI stabilization after an initial rise and another with a continuous increase in CI. SVRI decreased similarly in both clusters. ICU mortality differed between clusters in univariate analysis.
CONCLUSION: This study confirms a two-phase hemodynamic response to severe burns under active fluid resuscitation. It provides evidence for distinct hemodynamic trajectory patterns. These profiles could help optimize individual resuscitation strategies.

Title: A prospective exploratory study on the effects of Baduanjin exercise on cardiopulmonary and functional capacity in adults with severe burns.
Journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To preliminarily explore the effects of Baduanjin exercise on cardiac function, pulmonary function, and functional capacity in adults with severe burns.
METHODS: In this prospective, exploratory, non-randomized, controlled study, 32 adults with severe burns were assigned into a control group (standard burn rehabilitation, n = 16) or an exercise group (additional Baduanjin exercise, n = 16) based on preference. During the study, one patient in the control group withdrew due to the placement of a tissue expander; in the exercise group, one patient withdrew due to the placement of a tissue expander, and another was lost to follow-up. Finally, 15 patients were included in the control group and 14 in the exercise group. At rest, heart rate (HR), stroke volume (SV), respiratory rate (RR) and vital capacity (VC), as well as 6 min walk distance (6MWD) and upper limb function were measured before and after the intervention. Adherence and actual training frequency were recorded using rehabilitation diaries.
RESULTS: No significant differences in baseline characteristics or pre-intervention indicators were found (all p > 0.05).After intervention, the exercise group showed significantly higher SV, VC, and 6MWD, and lower RR and Quick DASH scores than the control group (all p < 0.05), with no significant group difference in HR (p = 0.907). Multiple linear regression confirmed significant effects of Baduanjin on all outcomes (all p < 0.05). Adherence was comparable between groups (92.85% vs. 73.33%, p = 0.330), but actual training frequency was higher in the exercise group (34.64 ± 4.56 vs. 30.67 ± 5.71, p = 0.049).
CONCLUSION: The findings of this study preliminarily suggest that Baduanjin exercise combining with standard burn rehabilitation may have positive effects on improving cardiopulmonary function and functional capacity in adults with severe burns. However, these conclusions require validation in future randomized controlled trials.

Title: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in burn patients: A 12-year retrospective cohort study in the era of "trauma dosing" low molecular weight heparin.
Journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
Abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a recognized complication of burn injury, yet the contemporary incidence in the setting of routine pharmacologic prophylaxis remains uncertain. We conducted a twelve-year retrospective cohort study of adult patients admitted to a single academic burn center between 2012 and 2023. The primary outcome was clinically significant venous thromboembolism, defined as pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis above the popliteal vein confirmed by imaging. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions were performed to identify factors associated with venous thromboembolism. A total of 1056 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean age was 54.7 years, and the mean total body surface area (TBSA) burned was 8.1%. Nineteen patients developed clinically significant venous thromboembolism, corresponding to an overall incidence of 1.8%. Incidence increased stepwise with burn severity, reaching 7.4% among patients with greater than 20% TBSA. Increasing age (1.01, 1.00-1.06) and intensive care unit length of stay (1.02, 1.00-1.03) were independently associated with venous thromboembolism on multivariable analysis. Over the study period, venous thromboembolism incidence decreased, alongside an increase in institutional use of low molecular weight heparin; however, this decline was not statistically significant. In a modern burn population receiving near-universal pharmacologic prophylaxis, the incidence of clinically significant venous thromboembolism was low. These findings support consistent prophylaxis in hospitalized burn patients while highlighting the need for prospective studies to refine risk stratification and dosing strategies.

Title: Coronary Plaque Burden and Progression in Los Angeles Firefighters Versus Matched Controls: A Cohort Study.
Journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess coronary plaque burden in Los Angeles Fire Department firefighters compared to matched control subjects.
METHODS: 302 LAFD subjects matched 1:1 with control subjects. Coronary artery calcium imaging, coronary computed tomography angiography, and AI-assisted quantitative plaque analysis compared coronary plaque burden between groups. 62 underwent follow-up CCTA.
RESULTS: The LAFD cohort had significantly higher total plaque volume (138 vs 84 mm³), non-calcified plaque volume (108 vs 73 mm³), percent atheroma volume (3.5% vs 2.3%), and prevalence of low-density plaque (31% vs 19%), all p ≤ 0.01. In the serial-CCTA subset, annualized progression of total plaque volume, calcified plaque, and percent atheroma volume was significantly higher than NATURE-CT.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal an elevated burden and accelerated progression of coronary plaque in LAFD firefighters, emphasizing the need for comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment and prevention strategies.

Title: Evaluation of coagulation factor concentrates for persistent bleeding after cardiothoracic surgery.
Journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of changes to a protocol for refractory bleeding after cardiothoracic surgery. The protocol changes included adjusting from a weight-based to a fixed-dosing strategy for 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) and decreasing the weight-based dosing of recombinant activated factor VII (rFVIIa).
METHODS: This was a pre-post retrospective cohort study evaluating 198 adult patients after cardiothoracic surgery requiring cardiopulmonary bypass at an academic medical center between May 2019 to October 2021 (before protocol change) and November 2021 to September 2022 (after protocol change). The primary outcome was chest tube output at 24 hours after the operation in patients who received at least one dose of 4F-PCC or rFVIIa. Secondary endpoints included transfusion volume, the rate of re-exploration events, length of stay, and 30-day mortality.
RESULTS: The primary outcome of chest tube output at 24 hours was 720 mL in the pre-change group and 700 mL in the post-change group (P = 0.982). The volume of fresh frozen plasma (FFP) transfusions significantly decreased from a median of 4 units to 2 units (P < 0.001). The median dose of 4F-PCC in the pre- vs post-change group was 24.6 vs 26.3 units/kg (P = 0.011), while that of rFVIIa was 59.5 vs 24.5 μg/kg (P = 0.000). The other secondary and safety outcomes were similar between the groups. The average cost savings was $3,585.45 per patient.
CONCLUSION: Patients in the post-change group had similar chest tube output, re-exploration rates, and incidence of thrombotic events. The post-change group received significantly less FFP and less coagulation factor concentrate while maintaining hemostasis and reducing cost.

Title: External Validation of the Risk Assessment of Morbidity in Pediatric Surgery Score.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Risk Assessment of Morbidity in Pediatric Surgery (RAMPS) score was developed by a tertiary care children's center to predict risk of noncardiac pediatric surgical morbidity using intrinsic surgical risk (ISR) and individual comorbidity. The score demonstrated good internal validity, discrimination, and generalizability. This study seeks to externally validate the score in a similar patient population at a different tertiary care children's hospital.
METHODS: Following institutional review board (IRB) approval, data for all noncardiac, nontrauma, and nontransplant pediatric surgeries performed at the external children's hospital in 2019 were collected via review of medical records. The RAMPS score for each patient was calculated. A composite morbidity score defined as transfer to intensive care unit (ICU), cardiac arrest, unplanned endotracheal intubation, or unplanned initiation of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) in the 72 hours following surgery was calculated. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and calibration between predicted and observed risk of morbidity was assessed.
RESULTS: Of 13,718 patients included, 409 (2.98%) experienced the composite morbidity outcome. The most common morbidity was postoperative PPV-361 (2.63%). Only 1.5% (n = 205) of the cohort was critically ill, though 14.1% (n = 1934) had at least three chronic conditions and 19.5% (n = 2668) of patients had a procedure in ISR quartiles 3 or 4. Each component of the RAMPS score was significantly associated with the outcome. The RAMPS score had very good discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.829; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.809-0.849) and good calibration between observed and predicted probabilities (Brier score = 0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: The RAMPS score performed well in this external validation with overall less patient complexity and less morbidity than in the original cohort included for development and internal validation. The score moderately overestimated risk in the most complex patients, which does not diminish its utility in guiding resource allocation to manage or prevent perioperative adverse events. In summary, the RAMPs score is a simple, highly discriminant, well-calibrated, and externally validated tool clinicians and health systems can use to predict morbidity among pediatric surgery patients.

Title: Determining Cerebrovascular Sensitivity to pH Using Continuous Arterial Blood Gas Analysis-A Prospective Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although carbon dioxide (CO2) is widely regarded as a driver for cerebral vasomodulation, often termed cerebrovascular CO2-reactivity, experimental evidence has shown that this response is primarily mediated through changes in pH rather than CO2. This complicates the management of cerebral blood flow (CBF) during the treatment of acid-base disorders with partial respiratory or metabolic compensation, when the CBF has normalized together with pH equilibration, despite persistent hyper- or hypercapnia. Although a pH-guided approach would therefore be preferred, no quantitative estimate of the relationship between pH and CBF has currently been reported in the literature. Therefore, this study aims to estimate the cerebrovascular sensitivity to pH and explore whether changes in CBF velocity (CBFV) are more closely related to arterial pH or CO2.
METHODS: In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, CBFV and continuous in-line arterial blood gas monitoring, incorporated in the cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, were analyzed. Mixed-effects models were constructed with percentage change in CBFV as response variable and arterial pH and/or CO2 as explanatory variable(s). Model fit of the explanatory variables was compared using marginal and conditional R2. Improvement of model fit and parsimony were assessed with the likelihood-ratio test (LRT) and change in Akaike information criterion (ΔAIC), respectively.
RESULTS: Thirteen patients were included in the analysis with a total of 1960 datapoints. CBFV decreased by 30.6% per 0.1 increase in arterial pH (95% confidence interval [CI], 28.9-32.2; P < .0001), and increased by 1.95% per mm Hg increase in PaCO2 (95% CI, 1.76-2.14; P < .0001). Arterial pH explained a greater proportion of variance than PaCO2 (marginal R2: 0.444 vs 0.294; conditional R2: 0.744 vs 0.530). Furthermore, adding arterial pH to the null CO2-model considerably improved model fit (LRT = 616.4) and parsimony (ΔAIC = -615), whereas adding arterial CO2 to the pH-model barely improved model fit (LRT = 4.6) and parsimony (ΔAIC = -3).
CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory study provides a quantitative estimate of the relationship between CBFV and pH, and suggests that changes in CBFV are more closely related to arterial pH than to CO2. This estimate of the cerebrovascular sensitivity to pH was used to describe a feasible pH-guided approach in the management of CBF during the treatment of partially compensated acid-base disorders.

Title: Treatment Failure After Laparoscopic Radiofrequency Ablation Compared With Myomectomy.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare treatment failure and factors associated with failure between laparoscopic radiofrequency ablation (RFA) of leiomyomata and laparoscopic myomectomy.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the multicenter prospective ULTRA (Uterine Leiomyoma Treatment with Radiofrequency Ablation) study, which investigated laparoscopic RFA and laparoscopic myomectomy for symptomatic uterine leiomyomata. Our primary outcome was receipt of any subsequent procedure (surgical failure) for leiomyomata within 2 years of the procedure. Our secondary outcome was composite failure (surgical failure or any self-reported failure, eg, continued leiomyomata symptoms affecting quality of life) within 2 years of the procedure. Odds ratios (ORs) were generated from multivariable logit models adjusting for a priori selected covariates.
RESULTS: We identified significant baseline differences between our groups. The RFA group (n=231) was older and had higher body mass index (BMI), gravidity, and parity than the myomectomy group (n=110). In the RFA group, 15.2% experienced surgical failure compared with 3.8% in the myomectomy group (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.17; 95% CI, 1.39-12.50), and 46.4% experienced composite failure in the RFA group compared with 25.5% in the myomectomy group (aOR 3.18; 95% CI, 1.80-5.60). Submucosal leiomyomata were associated with failure in the RFA group (OR 2.76; 95% CI, 1.21-6.28); there was a nonsignificant trend toward failure in the myomectomy group (OR 3.00; 95% CI, 0.99-9.05). Lateral leiomyomata were associated with higher odds of RFA failure (OR 2.49; 95% CI, 1.32-4.69), but no leiomyoma position was associated with myomectomy failure.
CONCLUSION: Laparoscopic RFA of leiomyomata is associated with higher odds of surgical and composite failure compared with laparoscopic myomectomy at 2 years, even after adjusting for baseline differences between groups.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02100904.

Title: Tablet-Based Neurocognitive Tests for Ugandan Adolescents Living With HIV: Cross-Sectional Validation Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents living with perinatally acquired HIV (PHIV) remain at risk of neurocognitive difficulties, yet access to valid neurocognitive tests is limited in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where most of this population resides. Tests that can be administered by nonspecialist personnel are culturally and linguistically appropriate for SSA's diverse populations and are brief enough for routine use are needed to expand access, but few such tools exist.
OBJECTIVE: We adapted NeuroScreen, a brief tablet-based neurocognitive test battery, into Luganda and evaluated its validity and acceptability for use among Ugandan adolescents with PHIV.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional validation study, 100 Ugandan adolescents aged 11 to 20 years (50 with PHIV; 50 HIV-negative controls) completed the Luganda- or English-language NeuroScreen battery and a commonly used traditional test battery. Participants were recruited from an existing longitudinal cardiovascular cohort at the Joint Clinical Research Centre in Kampala, Uganda. We examined convergent validity with correlations between the 2 batteries' individual and global z-scores, known-groups validity with unadjusted and age-adjusted group comparisons, criterion validity by examining classification agreement between the 2 batteries quantified with Cohen κ, and acceptability through self-reported technology use and ease of use.
RESULTS: NeuroScreen and the traditional battery global z-scores were strongly correlated (r=0.75; P<.001). Correlations between tests assessing similar domains were generally small to moderate, and were strongest for processing speed, attention, and working memory. Adolescents with PHIV scored significantly lower than controls on global scores for both NeuroScreen (P=.008) and the traditional battery (P=.003), even after adjusting for age. Agreement between batteries in classifying participants ≤1 SD (κ=0.56) and ≤2 SD (κ=0.66) below the global z-score mean was moderate, with both batteries classifying more adolescents with PHIV than controls below these thresholds. Although fewer than half of participants (42/97, 43%) had previously used a tablet, most rated NeuroScreen as easy to use, and prior tablet experience was not independently associated with NeuroScreen performance after age adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: The Luganda-adapted NeuroScreen demonstrated convergent, known-groups, and criterion validity in Ugandan adolescents with PHIV. By delivering automated administration, automated scoring, and standardized multimedia instructions in the local language on a portable tablet, NeuroScreen addresses several persistent barriers to neurocognitive assessment in low-resource settings, including shortages of specialist personnel, the time burden of traditional batteries, and the scarcity of culturally and linguistically appropriate tools. The NeuroScreen battery was found to be highly acceptable among adolescents with little or no prior tablet experience. These findings add to a growing body of evidence supporting tablet-based assessment as a practical and scalable mobile health approach to expanding access to neurocognitive testing. Future research should evaluate test-retest reliability, sensitivity to change over time, normative benchmarks, and implementation within real-world clinical workflows.

Title: Body Composition Assessment and Correlation to Metabolic Profile in Survivors of Childhood Brain Tumors.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Survivors of childhood brain tumors (CBT) are at increased risk for metabolic syndrome, contributing to long-term cardiometabolic morbidity. BMI may underestimate risk by failing to capture altered body composition in this population. More precise tools such as air displacement plethysmography (ADP) may improve early risk detection. This study aimed to identify ADP-derived markers of adiposity and characterize early metabolic abnormalities at the end of cancer therapy.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-visit study enrolling pediatric survivors of high-grade CBT aged 2 to 21 years, off therapy for <5 years. Data included anthropometric measurements, metabolic markers (glucose, insulin, lipids, adiponectin, leptin, IL-6), and body composition (fat mass, fat-free mass, percent fat, measured by ADP). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographics and clinical characteristics, and categorical variables were presented as counts and percentages. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated for log adiponectin versus percent body fat and BMI z-score.
RESULTS: Thirty survivors of CBT (n=30; age: 6 to 23 y) were evaluated a median of 0.3 years after treatment. Over half were normal weight (53%), and 47% were overweight or obese; 20% had hypertension and 23% had elevated waist circumference. Body composition (n=29) showed high adiposity, with a mean fat mass of 33% and 59% having elevated fat percentage. Metabolic assessment demonstrated early cardiometabolic dysfunction: insulin resistance and significant insulin resistance by HOMA-IR were seen in 50% and 33%, respectively, and lipid abnormalities and the metabolic syndrome were seen in 27% and 15%, respectively. Higher adiposity was associated with worse metabolic health, with greater fat mass percentage in insulin-resistant patients (P<0.01) and higher BMI z-score (P=0.02). Adiponectin was inversely correlated with fat mass% (r=-0.72), but not with BMI z-score.
CONCLUSION: Childhood brain tumor survivors demonstrated a high prevalence of metabolic abnormalities and excess adiposity shortly after therapy completion. BMI underestimated abnormal adiposity compared with ADP-derived body composition assessment, supporting the need for comprehensive metabolic screening and early intervention during survivorship.

Title: Reassessing cardiometabolic health disparities among young adult sexual minority women: Evidence from a population-based cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: We compared objective measures of cardiometabolic health (CMH) between women who identify as lesbian/gay or bisexual (LGB) and women who identify as heterosexual. In addition, we aimed to test whether group differences in stress reactivity partially explained disparities in CMH health.
METHODS: Participants from a longitudinal study were identified for enrollment in 2017. The LGB group self-identified as LGB in 2017 (n = 239), and the heterosexual group identified as straight or heterosexual in each year that sexual identity was asked (study years 2010-2017) (n = 160). CMH was assessed via measurements and biomarkers, and stress reactivity via heart rate variability and cortisol levels during a social stress test. Participants also provided self-reports of stress and health. We tested group differences using sexual identity at Study Year 17, at the time of the visit, and as a proportion of years identifying as LGB.
RESULTS: Group differences were tested using t-tests for continuous measures, logistic regression for dichotomous measures, and repeated-measures ANOVA for change over time. There were no significant differences in measures of CMH or stress reactivity by sexual identity group. LGB participants had worse self-reported health and higher levels of stress compared to heterosexual participants.
CONCLUSION: We discuss several frameworks for interpreting the present results of no differences in objective markers of health in the context of the existing literature, including developmental, socio-political, and methodological frameworks, and suggest directions for research to link the previous research with the results of the current study.

Title: Investigation on the use of ceftazidime-avibactam at a national hospital in Vietnam.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the utilization of ceftazidime-avibactam at Thong Nhat Hospital, a national hospital in Vietnam.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using retrospective data from medical records of inpatients aged ≥ 18 years who received ceftazidime-avibactam for at least 2 days between January 2023 and March 2025 at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. The appropriateness of ceftazidime-avibactam use was evaluated based on Thong Nhat Hospital's antibiotic use guideline. The backward conditional method was used to identify factors associated with patient treatment outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 101 patients were included, with a median age of 78 years (68-86). Respiratory and bloodstream infections were the most common types, accounting for 84.15% and 44.55% of cases, respectively. Gram-negative bacteria comprised 76.05% of isolates, with Klebsiella pneumoniae (26.47%), Klebsiella aerogenes (18.50%) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (10.50%) being the most frequent. The susceptibility rate to ceftazidime-avibactam was 71.43% for Klebsiella pneumoniae, 95.65% for Klebsiella aerogenes and 42.86% for Pseudomonas aeruginosa. OXA-48 was the most detected carbapenemase gene (37.84%). The overall appropriateness rate of ceftazidime-avibactam use was 70.30%. The treatment success rate was 39.60%. Treatment in the intensive care unit was associated with decreased treatment success, while comorbid heart failure showed a potential association.
CONCLUSIONS: The treatment success rate with ceftazidime-avibactam in this study was relatively low. Continuous surveillance of microbiological profiles and antibiotic resistance, particularly to ceftazidime-avibactam, is essential to better guide the management of drug-resistant Gram-negative infections at the hospital.

Title: Bridging the Gap: Thrombolysis Access and Treatment Times Before and After Telestroke Implementation in Matão, Brazil.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) rates for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remain suboptimal in Brazil, largely due to limited access to specialized stroke teams. Telestroke (TS) has emerged as a potential strategy to overcome geographic and structural barriers to timely stroke care, particularly in countries with continental dimensions such as Brazil. However, robust evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of telestroke in the country remains scarce. The primary aim was to compare access to IVT before and after the implementation of a mobile TS program in the municipality of Matão, São Paulo. Secondary objectives included comparing treatment metrics, safety outcomes-specifically, intracranial hemorrhage and mortality-and functional independence at 90 days.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected stroke registry, using an uncontrolled before-and-after (pre/post-implementation) design at Carlos Fernando Malzoni Hospital (Matão-SP), including patients with confirmed AIS between September 1, 2016, and August 31, 2022. Patients were divided into two groups: pre-TS (36 months before implementation) and post-TS (36 months after implementation). The TS platform used was the JOIN® app (Allm Inc., Tokyo, Japan).
RESULTS: Of 379 patients diagnosed with AIS during the 72-month period, the mean age was 69.8 ± 13.6 years, and 59.1% were male. The most common risk factors were hypertension (76.8%), diabetes mellitus (38.5%), and smoking (26.1%). Although 65.4% of patients arrived within 4.5 hours from symptom onset, only 58 (15.3%) received IVT. Nevertheless, the number and proportion of patients receiving IVT increased from 11 (6.7%) in the pre-TS period to 47 (22.0%) in the post-TS period (p < 0.001). Among thrombolysed patients, median door-to-needle time was significantly reduced from 145.0 minutes (IQR 119.0-265.0) pre-TS to 92.0 minutes (IQR 66.0-129.0) post-TS (p = 0.004). There were no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (p = 1.000), 90-day mortality (p = 0.729), or 90-day functional outcomes (p = 0.742). In multivariable analysis, post-TS period (OR 5.65; 95% CI 2.68-11.93; p < 0.001) and higher NIHSS score at admission (OR 1.05; 95% CI 1.02-1.08; p = 0.002) were independently associated with IVT.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center before-and-after study, implementation of a mobile telestroke program was associated with higher rates of intravenous thrombolysis and shorter treatment times. No statistically significant differences were observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, 90-day mortality, or functional outcomes. These findings support further evaluation of mobile telestroke strategies in low- and middle-income settings.

Title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear.
METHODS: This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint.
RESULTS: Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group.
CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

Title: Real-World Use and Outcomes of Post-Discharge Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis After Thoracic Cancer Operation.
Journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-discharge venous thromboembolism prophylaxis is conditionally recommended after thoracic cancer operation, but real-world use and associated outcomes across procedures and operative approaches remain poorly characterized.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective Epic Cosmos cohort study of adults undergoing lung or esophageal cancer resection from 2016-2025. Post-discharge prophylaxis was defined as prophylactic-dose anticoagulation prescribed within 7 days of discharge. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using 1:3 propensity-score matching stratified by procedure and operative approach.
RESULTS: Among 157,619 patients (14,277 esophagectomy; 143,342 lung resection), 11.15% and 1.48%, respectively, received post-discharge prophylaxis. After open esophagectomy, prophylaxis was associated with lower DVT (1.23% vs 2.63%; p=0.039), PE (0.46% vs 1.44%; p=0.047), and mortality (1.70% vs 5.20%; p<0.001), without significantly increased bleeding. Findings were similar after minimally invasive esophagectomy: DVT 0.32% vs 1.46% (p=0.003), PE 0.21% vs 0.89% (p=0.034), and mortality 1.28% vs 3.20% (p=0.003). After open lung resection, prophylaxis was associated with lower PE and mortality but higher bleeding and healthcare use. After minimally invasive lung resection, thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ, while bleeding and healthcare use were higher. Enoxaparin accounted for 79.35% of prophylaxis prescriptions; thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ between apixaban and enoxaparin.
CONCLUSIONS: Associations between post-discharge thromboprophylaxis and outcomes differed across thoracic procedures and operative approaches. Favorable associations after esophagectomy contrasted with less consistent lung resection findings, supporting prospective studies to define procedure- and risk-specific prophylaxis strategies.

Title: Association of an Exploratory Iron Index Score With Observed NT-proBNP Trajectory in SGLT2-Treated Heart Failure and Clinical Outcomes in a Broader Cohort.
Journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Iron-related risk in heart failure is multidimensional, yet routine assessment still relies primarily on single laboratory-based definitions. This study evaluated whether an exploratory composite Iron Index Score was associated with the observed routine-care NT-proBNP trajectory after SGLT2 inhibitor therapy and with adverse clinical outcomes in a broader score-complete cohort.
METHODS: This retrospective real-world cohort study used a nested analytic design. The primary biomarker analysis included a final SGLT2-treated cohort with paired baseline and follow-up NT-proBNP measurements and complete score components (n=238). The supportive clinical analysis included a broader score-complete cohort regardless of SGLT2 use (n=472). The cohort predominantly comprised patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The Iron Index Score assigned 1 point each for transferrin saturation <20%, hemoglobin <12 g/dL, ferritin <100 ng/mL, albumin <3.5 g/dL, and red cell distribution width >14.5%. The primary outcome was the change in log-transformed NT-proBNP from baseline to the lowest recorded on-treatment value. Secondary analyses examined NT-proBNP response, heart failure hospitalization, and exploratory all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: In the final SGLT2-treated biomarker cohort, the adjusted ordinal score showed a directionally less favorable delta log NT-proBNP estimate but did not reach conventional statistical significance (beta 0.15, 95% CI -0.00 to 0.30; P=0.054). The high-risk group showed a stronger exploratory adverse signal compared with the low-risk group (beta 1.00, 95% CI 0.40 to 1.59; P<0.001). NT-proBNP responder status was not independently associated with score burden. In the broader score-complete cohort, higher score burden was associated with heart failure hospitalization in the unadjusted analysis, but this association was attenuated after adjustment (hazard ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.27; P=0.690). All-cause mortality analyses were interpreted as exploratory because only 21 deaths occurred.
CONCLUSION: A higher exploratory Iron Index Score showed a hypothesis-generating signal toward a less favorable observed NT-proBNP trajectory in a predominantly HFrEF SGLT2-treated cohort. Broader cohort analyses showed supportive but less stable clinical outcome signals.

Title: Characteristics of patients hospitalized for diabetic foot in a national hospital in Peru, 2024.
Journal: Revista peruana de medicina experimental y salud publica
Abstract: With the objective of describing the clinical characteristics of patients hospitalized for diabetic foot in the internal medicine service of the Edgardo Rebagliati Martins National Hospital during the year 2024, a retrospective observational study was conducted. 114 medical records were reviewed. Sociodemographic and clinical variables, metabolic profile (HbA1c), lesion severity (Wagner scale), and in-hospital outcomes were analyzed. 114 patients were included with a mean age of 66.9 years and a predominance of male sex (69.3%). The average glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was 8.37%. According to the Wagner scale, 43.9% were admitted with grade 4 (localized gangrene) and 31.6% with grade 3. The median hospital stay was 12.5 days, the overall amputation rate was 46.5%, and mortality was 7.0%. In conclusion, the population hospitalized in Internal Medicine presents high clinical severity, characterized by poor metabolic control, critical ischemia, and gangrene at admission, which is associated with a high rate of major amputations.

Title: Elevated lithium levels in drinking water are associated with higher prevalence of Wolff-Parkinson-White diagnoses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) are potentially highly symptomatic and, rarely, lethal arrhythmias associated with atrioventricular accessory pathways. While the etiology of accessory pathways remains largely unknown, they are frequently observed with Ebstein's Anomaly, a congenital heart disease associated with maternal medicinal lithium use. Therefore, we evaluated whether in utero exposure to lithium from environmental sources is associated with the prevalence of accessory pathways.
METHODS: We conducted a county-level ecological comparison of lithium levels in drinking water versus prevalence of WPW diagnoses among patients < 18-years-old in California using multivariable logistic regression. Children were analyzed given their high likelihood to reside in the same county during fetal development. WPW cases were identified using diagnostic codes. Positive and negative controls, including falsification endpoints, were analyzed.
RESULTS: Among 2,329,090 patients (mean age 8.2 ± 5.9 years, 47.8% female), 686 (0.03%) were diagnosed with WPW. Areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with 71% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.44 to 2.03). Areas above the lithium health-based screening limit had 29% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.58). Similar results existed in a New York statewide cohort. In validation analyses, areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with a higher prevalence of SVT, syncope, palpitations, and catheter ablation procedures.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher lithium levels in drinking water were associated with a greater prevalence of childhood-diagnosed WPW, implicating a potentially modifiable risk factor for the development of accessory pathways.

Title: From call to home: The role of dispatcher-assisted CPR in patient survival.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dispatcher-assisted cardiopulmonary resuscitation (DA-CPR) is a key strategy to reduce no-flow time in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet its impact on long-term survival remains various across emergency medical systems.
PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the association between DA-CPR and resuscitation outcomes in a nationwide cohort of OHCA patients presenting with an initial shockable rhythm.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study including all adult OHCA cases with ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia (VF/VT) in which resuscitation was carried out by emergency medical services in Hungary during 2019, 2022, and 2023. Patients were stratified according to whether DA-CPR was ongoing upon ambulance arrival, or initiated by the ambulance crew. Primary outcomes were return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and hospital admission with sustained circulation. Utstein-style consensus reporting guidelines were followed.
RESULTS: A total of 3,674 VF/VT OHCA cases were included, of whom 1,744 (47.5%) received DA-CPR. Patients in the DA-CPR group had significantly higher rates of ROSC (92.0% vs. 12.4%), hospital admission with sustained circulation (90.8% vs. 11.7%), 30-day survival (54.6% vs. 7.1%), and one-year survival (45.8% vs. 6.2%) compared with those without DA-CPR (all P < 0.001). DA-CPR occurrence increased over time, while declined in 2022 followed by partial recovery in 2023.
CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort of OHCA patients with shockable rhythms, dispatcher-assisted CPR was strongly associated with improved early resuscitation success and long-term survival. These findings support DA-CPR as a critical system-level intervention and highlight the importance of centralised protocols and continuous performance monitoring.

Title: Effects of Active Video Games on Cardiometabolic Health in Children and Adolescents: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic risk factors emerging during childhood and adolescence may persist into adulthood and increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Although physical activity improves cardiometabolic health, maintaining regular participation remains challenging. Active video games (AVG), which combine physical activity with video game enjoyment, may provide an engaging approach to promote physical activity participation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effects of AVG on cardiometabolic health in children and adolescents and to explore potential moderators of these effects.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase were searched from database inception to July 2026. Eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating AVG in children and adolescents aged 4-18 years were included, with comparisons against no intervention, sedentary video games, or regular physical activity. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate pooled effects. Subgroup analyses explored potential moderators. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool (RoB 2; Cochrane), sensitivity analyses examined robustness, and small-study effects were evaluated when feasible. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation).
RESULTS: A total of 14 RCTs involving 942 children and adolescents were included. AVG were associated with a small but significant reduction in BMI (Hedges g=-0.23, 95% CI -0.35 to -0.10; 95% prediction interval [PI] -0.43 to -0.01; P=.002). SBP (Hedges g=-0.18, 95% CI -0.36 to -0.001; 95% PI -0.43 to 0.07; P=.0497) showed a small statistically significant reduction, although the 95% PI crossed the null. No significant effects were observed for diastolic blood pressure (DBP) (Hedges g=-0.11, 95% CI -0.86 to 0.63; 95% PI -2.09 to 1.75; P=.59), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL) (Hedges g=0.05; 95% CI -0.21 to 0.31; 95% PI -0.54 to 0.57; P=.65), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL) (Hedges g=-0.26, 95% CI -0.64 to 0.13; 95% PI -1.18 to 0.69; P=.15), total cholesterol (TC) (Hedges g=-0.96, 95% CI -3.79 to 1.88; 95% PI -5.71 to 3.86; P=.37), triglycerides (Hedges g=-0.20, 95% CI -0.70 to 0.31; 95% PI -1.41 to 0.99; P=.38), heart rate (HR) (Hedges g=-0.14, 95% CI -1.74 to 1.46; 95% PI -4.23 to 5.38; P=.47), or glucose (Hedges g=-0.17, 95% CI -0.37 to 0.02; 95% PI -0.42 to 0.07; P=.07) following AVG. No significant BMI subgroup differences were observed by gender, intervention type, or nutritional status.
CONCLUSIONS: This review extends previous evidence by providing an updated RCT-only evaluation of a broader pediatric population and a wider range of cardiometabolic outcomes. AVG were associated with small reductions in BMI and systolic blood pressure (SBP), although evidence for other cardiometabolic outcomes remains uncertain. By clarifying both potential benefits and remaining evidence gaps, this review provides a broader basis for future research and intervention development. AVG may serve as an engaging adjunct to support physical activity participation among children and adolescents.

Title: Risk Visualization With Petal-X and Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Support Person-Centered Care and Lifestyle Change in Cardiovascular Prevention: Qualitative Descriptive Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. In primary prevention, effective communication of individual risk and support for behavior change are crucial. Interactive risk visualizations can enhance understanding and engagement, while continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) offers immediate feedback on the physiological effects of daily choices.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore how patients at increased CVD risk and family medicine nurses perceive CVD risk visualization (Petal-X) and the integration of real-time glucose monitoring, with a focus on perceived person-centered care (PCC), motivation, and lifestyle change. This manuscript reports the qualitative phase of a larger sequential mixed methods study; the quantitative randomized controlled trial is reported separately.
METHODS: Using total population (census) sampling within a closed, predefined trial cohort, we invited every eligible patient who had completed the intervention arm of a parallel randomized controlled trial and every eligible registered nurse providing preventive consultations at the same single community health center in central Slovenia who had been familiarized with the intervention and with the Petal-X dashboard; 6 patients at increased CVD risk who had used the Petal-X dashboard in combination with CGM, and 6 nurses familiar with the intervention, took part, and interviews were conducted between September and December 2024. Data were collected through individual, face-to-face semistructured interviews that explored perceptions of the visualization, real-time glucose monitoring, and lifestyle change. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed by inductive qualitative content analysis within a qualitative descriptive design; coding continued until code saturation and data adequacy were judged to have been reached.
RESULTS: The analysis produced 11 subcategories, which were grouped into 4 categories, with an overarching theme running across them: visualization and digital tools as support for PCC to enhance motivation and lifestyle change in individuals at risk of CVD. Patients and nurses reported that personalized visual displays improved understanding of risk factors, facilitated dialogue and shared decision-making, and increased patients' sense of involvement, responsibility, and control, although the 2 groups differed in emphasis: patients foregrounded personal meaning and self-regulation, whereas nurses foregrounded communication and fit with the consultation workflow. CGM was perceived as particularly motivating by linking behavior (food, activity, and stress) to real-time glucose changes, encouraging dietary and activity adjustments that some participants maintained after the intervention. Key barriers included variable digital literacy (especially among older users), fear or mistrust of technology, the attentional burden of continuous monitoring, potential information overload, workflow integration needs, and affordability or accessibility of CGM.
CONCLUSIONS: Interactive CVD risk visualization Petal-X, especially when complemented by CGM, was perceived as a meaningful support for PCC and a driver of motivation and lifestyle change in primary prevention. Implementation should address training, usability, integration into routine workflows, and equity of access.

Title: Out-of-Pocket Costs for Chronic Illness Management in High-Deductible Health Plans.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: High-deductible health plans (HDHPs) enroll a substantial share of privately insured Americans and are associated with reduced use of care, even care that is considered medically necessary. However, the magnitude of patient out-of-pocket (OOP) costs required to obtain evidence-based medical care when enrolled in HDHPs remains poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate patient OOP costs required to receive guideline-concordant care for common chronic conditions when enrolled in an HDHP vs a non-HDHP.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used 2022 to 2023 national commercial insurance claims data. Participants included adults aged 18 to 64 years with employer-sponsored insurance and previously diagnosed diabetes, hypertension, or both. To enter the cohort, persons had to have received guideline-concordant care for their chronic illnesses. Data were analyzed from July 2025 to April 2026.
EXPOSURE: Enrollment in an HDHP vs a non-HDHP.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was annual patient OOP costs to receive evidence-based care. Entropy balancing and generalized linear models with geographic fixed effects estimated the mean OOP costs of receiving minimum recommended medical care for diabetes, hypertension, or both in HDHPs and non-HDHPs. Estimates were weighted to ensure that observed costs were representative of the full sample of chronically ill persons.
RESULTS: There were 539 590 adults receiving guideline-concordant care who entered the cohort. After entropy balancing, groups exhibited mean covariate balance, with males representing 57.9% of HDHP enrollees and 57.8% of non-HDHP enrollees, and similar age distributions across groups, with 45.4% of both HDHP and non-HDHP enrollees 55 to 64 years of age. The estimated annual OOP cost for individuals to receive guideline-concordant diabetes care was $153.91 (95% CI, $150.18-$157.64) in HDHPs vs $68.06 (95% CI, $66.34-$69.78) in non-HDHPs; $128.94 (95% CI, $127.25-$130.64) in HDHPs vs $53.89 (95% CI, $53.20-$54.58) in non-HDHPs for guideline-concordant hypertension care; and $164.18 (95% CI, $160.93-$167.44) in HDHPs vs $100.60 (95% CI, $98.80-$102.39) in non-HDHPs for guideline-concordant care for comorbid diabetes and hypertension (all P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of a large, national sample of chronically ill adults with hypertension, diabetes, or both, annual patient costs were 1.6 to 2.4 times as high to receive recommended care in HDHPs vs non-HDHPs, although the magnitude of the difference in OOP costs was relatively small (range, $63.68 to $85.85). Findings provide novel evidence quantifying the magnitude of cost burden experienced by chronically ill patients under various insurance mechanisms and complement prior HDHP studies evaluating health care utilization.

Title: Thrombectomy for Acute Stroke Due to Medium Vessel Occlusion Across Perfusion Mismatch Profiles: A Post Hoc Analysis of the ESCAPE-MeVO Trial.
Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Recent trials have not demonstrated a benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) over medical therapy in acute stroke due to medium vessel occlusion (MeVO). However, it remains uncertain whether selected patients with favorable perfusion may benefit from EVT.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between perfusion mismatch profiles and functional outcomes in MeVO stroke and to determine whether these profiles modify the effect of EVT.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study was a post hoc analysis of ESCAPE-MeVO (Endovascular Treatment to Improve Outcomes for Medium Vessel Occlusion), a multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in North America, Europe, and the United Kingdom between April 2022 and June 2024, with a 90-day follow-up. Trial participants included patients with acute MeVO stroke presenting within 12 hours from last known well and evidence of salvageable brain tissue. This analysis included only patients with interpretable baseline perfusion imaging. Data were analyzed from March to July 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Randomization to EVT plus usual care vs usual care alone.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour follow-up infarct volume and 90-day mRS score of 0 to 1 and 0 to 2. Perfusion mismatch ratio and volume were defined as the ratio and difference between the critically hypoperfused area and the ischemic core, with volume thresholds defined by site-specific postprocessing software.
RESULTS: Of 530 enrolled patients, 309 (58.3%) had available baseline perfusion imaging and were included in this study (EVT: n = 146; usual care: n = 163). Patient median (IQR) age was 73 (63-82) years, and 141 (45.6%) were women. Median (IQR) perfusion mismatch volume was 37.2 (22.1-57.2) mL, and the median (IQR) mismatch ratio was 6.1 (2.8-10.0). Ordinal 90-day mRS score was not associated with perfusion mismatch volume (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.03 [95% CI, 0.99-1.07] per 10-mL increase) or perfusion mismatch ratio (AOR, 1.03 [95% CI, 0.97-1.09] per 1-unit increase). There was no modification of EVT effect by perfusion mismatch volume or ratio on ordinal 90-day mRS. Results were consistent across secondary outcomes and subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this exploratory post hoc analysis of acute MeVO stroke, perfusion mismatch profiles were not associated with functional outcomes and did not modify the effect of EVT. These findings suggest that perfusion imaging profiles based on currently used thresholds and cutoffs did not identify patients likely to benefit from EVT in the ESCAPE-MeVO trial.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05151172.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Fibro-Inflammatory Signaling, Fibrosis, and Microvascular Ischemia as Convergent Translational Substrates of Sudden Cardiac Death in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
Abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) remains an important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD), but the biological determinants of ventricular arrhythmic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. This systematic translational review examined whether fibro-inflammatory signaling, fibrotic remodeling, and microvascular ischemia represent convergent components of the arrhythmogenic substrate in HCM. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to January 2026. Of 167 records, 37 full-text reports were assessed and 11 studies included. Fibrosis emerged as the most clinically mature substrate marker, while microvascular ischemia appeared to amplify electrical instability, particularly in remodeled myocardium. Molecular and tissue studies suggested upstream fibro-inflammatory programs involving activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix dysregulation, SMAD/TGF-beta signaling, CRLF1/LIFR-JAK-STAT signaling, and altered multicellular communication. Overall, the evidence supports an integrated mechanism-to-substrate model, but prospective outcome-validated studies are needed before these biological layers can refine SCD risk stratification beyond established clinical and imaging markers in contemporary HCM practice.

Title: Cardiac injury in children with severe hand, foot and mouth disease: risk factors and clinical outcomes.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the risk factors and clinical outcomes of cardiac injury in pediatric patients with severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD).
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study at two tertiary children's hospitals in southern Vietnam, including hospitalized patients with severe HFMD and suspected cardiovascular complications. Cardiac injury was identified according to cardiac enzyme results and findings from electrocardiography and echocardiography. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify risk factors associated with cardiac injury.
RESULTS: A total of 395 patients were included, with a male predominance, and 96.5% were younger than 36 months. Typical skin rash and herpangina remained the most common clinical manifestations. Intensive care unit admission was required in 72.2% of cases, and 50.9% required endotracheal intubation with mechanical ventilation. Cardiac injury was identified in 7.3% (29/395) of severe HFMD cases with suspected cardiovascular complications. Fever ≥ 39 °C (aOR 10.5, 95% CI 3.4-32.6, p < 0.001), C-reactive protein > 20 mg/L (aOR 3.3, 95% CI 1.3-8.4, p = 0.012), and aspartate aminotransferase > 40 U/L (aOR 4.1, 95% CI 1.7-9.8, p = 0.002) were independent risk factors for cardiac injury. Patients with cardiac injury had higher mortality, longer hospital stays, and a greater incidence of neurological sequelae compared with those without cardiac injury.
CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac injury in pediatric patients with severe HFMD is associated with adverse clinical outcomes, underscoring the need for early risk stratification and comprehensive cardiac assessment.

Title: Machine learning-assisted monitoring of radiofrequency ablation in hepatic tumors using spectral traces.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate intraoperative assessment of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) margins in hepatic malignancies remains a significant clinical challenge.
METHODS: This study investigates the efficacy of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) for objective, spatially resolved discrimination of ablated tissue, viable tumor, and normal parenchyma in 10 ex vivo liver specimens. Analysis of visible-near-infrared (VNIR) reflectance revealed distinct spectral signatures, characterized by a consistent monotonic hierarchy (ablated < normal < tumor), enabling reliable tissue differentiation. Segmentation performance was systematically evaluated using four supervised classifiers: Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). The total delineated tissue area exhibited notable inter-method variability, ranging from 137,283 to 189,289 pixels (+ 37.9%), underscoring sensitivity to classifier architecture.
RESULTS: Nevertheless, all approaches maintained biologically coherent tissue distributions, with normal parenchyma predominating (44-56%), followed by tumor (25-39%) and ablated regions (17-20%). That is consistently indicating the necessity for monitoring ablative margins. SAM, SVM, and LDA classifiers achieved class-specific detection errors around 3.5% and 18%. LDA attained the highest overall accuracy (94.5%), demonstrating the potential of HSI for reliable, intraoperative image-guided tissue characterization. Dimensionality reduction across 462 spectral bands identified an optimal discriminative window within 643-698 nm, supporting the development of streamlined multispectral systems.
CONCLUSION: Overall, HSI is neither a contact nor destructive modality for quantitative RFA assessment. Despite classifier-dependent variability necessitating standardized or ensemble strategies, these findings support its prospective integration into real-time surgical guidance, pending in vivo validation.

Title: Establishing the reliability of non-contrast 4D flow in congenital heart disease at 1.5T.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: 4D flow has been shown to correlate well with 2D phase-contrast (2D PC) flow measurements, although most of the current literature is based on post-contrast imaging.
OBJECTIVE: Given recent interest in non-contrast techniques, we hypothesized that non-contrast 4D flow (NC 4D Flow) would correlate well with 2D PC and ventricular stroke volumes.
METHODS AND MATERIALS: A prospective cohort of pediatric and young adult patients with suspected/confirmed congenital heart disease (CHD) underwent cardiac MRI at 1.5T with acquisition of NC 4D Flow and 2D PC. Pearson correlation, linear mixed-effect correlations, and Bland-Altman comparisons were performed to compare these methods with secondary analyses of internal consistency and image quality/noise.
RESULTS: In our cohort of 30 patients (age, 8-20 years), NC 4D Flow correlated strongly with 2D PC for net flow (r=0.76), peak velocity (r=0.9, P<0.001), and regurgitant fraction (r=0.75, P<0.001). By Bland-Altman comparison, NC 4D Flow was 10.1% lower for net flows and 18.9% higher for peak velocity compared to 2D PC. NC 4D Flow also slightly underestimated ventricular stroke volumes (18.1% lower for ascending aorta vs. left ventricular stroke volume and 13.9% lower for main pulmonary artery vs. right ventricular stroke volume). Both datasets were internally consistent; 2D PC had a higher relative signal intensity, but no difference in signal-to-noise or contrast-to-noise ratios (SNR/CNR).
CONCLUSION: Non-contrast 4D flow correlates well with 2D PC in CHD with a slight underestimation in flows and overestimation in peak velocities, but good internal consistency and comparable SNR/CNR.

Title: Beyond Atrial Fibrillation: Clinical and Echocardiographic Predictors of Ischaemic Stroke and Systemic Thromboembolism in Rheumatic Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the best-established thromboembolic risk factor in rheumatic heart disease (RHD), but stroke and thromboembolism also occur without documented AF. We systematically synthesised associations between non-AF clinical/echocardiographic predictors and thromboembolism in RHD, comparing AF-adjusted with unadjusted estimates.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation screening. Eligible studies evaluated RHD patients with ≥1 non-AF predictor of stroke or thromboembolism. Two reviewers performed selection, extraction, and QUIPS risk-of-bias assessment; certainty was graded using GRADE. Unadjusted, adjusted, and AF-adjusted estimates were extracted separately, and random-effects meta-analysis was performed when feasible.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies (∼8,206 patients) met eligibility criteria. SEC, LA size/volume, LA/appendage thrombus, LA appendage flow, LA mechanical function, mitral valve severity, age, and previous thromboembolism were most frequently examined. Four studies provided comparable crude ORs for SEC (pooled OR 8.27, 95% CI 3.21-21.29; I2 = 66%), substantially attenuated after AF adjustment (as low as OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.1-3.0). Older age and previous stroke remained associated with thromboembolism in AF-inclusive models, and LA mechanical/reservoir function showed consistent inverse associations, including in sinus rhythm. Certainty was low for SEC, age, and LA function; moderate for previous stroke/thromboembolism; very low for anticoagulation non-use.
CONCLUSION: In RHD, thromboembolic risk extends beyond documented AF. SEC showed the strongest unadjusted association but was substantially attenuated after AF adjustment, likely partly reflecting subclinical AF; it is TEE-dependent and inconsistently graded. Older age, previous thromboembolism, and impaired LA mechanical/reservoir function showed more persistent associations after AF-inclusive adjustment; prospective validation is needed.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Cangrelor Dosing, Administration, and Clinical Outcomes for Patients Undergoing Complex and High-Risk Percutaneous Coronary Interventions.
