Journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cangrelor reduces thrombotic events in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), with the advantage of rapid onset and offset. However, premature discontinuation may increase the risk of acute thrombosis for patients undergoing complex/high-risk PCI (CHIP).
AIMS: We evaluated the real-world administration of cangrelor and related health outcomes for CHIP patients.
METHODS: A US retrospective physician panel medical chart review (1/1/2020 to 6/26/2025) included patients 18+ years old who received cangrelor (1st dose = index date) during CHIP. We summarized patients' characteristics in the 6 months pre-index (baseline), cangrelor dosing and administration (IV bolus and/or infusion), and clinical outcomes within 48 h. We described MACE occurrence by dosing adherence.
RESULTS: Patients (n = 200) were mostly male (85.5%), had a mean age of 63 years, and had a BMI of 30.2 kg/m2. Most (87.5%) received a cangrelor bolus (30.0 µg/kg) and maintenance infusion (4.0 µg/kg/mins), aligned with intended use recommendations. Of patients analyzed for infusion duration (n = 134), 64.9% deviated from the recommendation of at least 2 h or PCI length. Forty (29.9%) received cangrelor for less than the recommended duration. Overall, 30 (15%) patients experienced MACE, with a higher proportion of MACE seen in those who deviated from the recommended duration (16.1% [95% CI: 3.5%-23.1%] vs. 10.6% [95% CI: 9.1%-25.5%]).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides real-world insight into cangrelor use and clinical outcomes in CHIP patients, highlighting notable variability in infusion duration and differences in MACE occurrence by dosing adherence. Further comparative effectiveness studies are warranted to examine the potential impact of deviation from intended dose/duration on clinical outcomes in CHIP.

Title: Effects of tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1 dual receptor agonist) on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity in heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, has demonstrated clinical benefits in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity. However, its effects on cardiorenal biomarkers and functional capacity have not been comprehensively synthesized. We hypothesized that tirzepatide produces significant reductions in cardiorenal biomarkers and improvements in functional capacity compared to placebo or standard of care.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42026137255) searched PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 17, 2026, without restrictions. Randomized controlled trials and prospective observational studies reporting NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS), 6-minute walk test (6 MWT), or renal outcomes with tirzepatide vs placebo or standard of care were included. Data were pooled using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.
RESULTS: Seven studies (5 RCTs, 2 observational; 5406 participants) were included. Tirzepatide significantly reduced hsCRP by 34.3% (95% CI: -38.4% to -30.1%; P < .0001; I2 = 0.0%; 6 studies) and NT-proBNP by 17.6% (95% CI: -26.7% to -8.5%; P = .0001; I2 = 58.1%; 3 studies). In the SUMMIT trial, KCCQ-CSS improved by 5.1 points (P < .001) and 6 MWT by 15.8 m (P = .004). Single-trial data demonstrated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) preservation (+2.90 mL/min/1.73 m2/year; 95% CI: 0.94 to 4.86) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio reduction (-25.0%; 95% CI: -36.0% to -13.0%).
CONCLUSION: Tirzepatide produces consistent anti-inflammatory effects and significant natriuretic peptide reductions, supported by moderate Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation certainty. Evidence for functional and renal outcomes remains limited to single-trial analyses and should be considered hypothesis-generating pending larger dedicated heart failure trials.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD42026137255.

Title: "Baseline Characteristics and Utilization of Medical Therapies in Acute Hospitalized and Chronic Heart Failure Patients Enrolled in GRASP-HF: Differences Between ICARe-HF and Non-ICARe-HF Centres".
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Global Registries and Surveys Programme-Heart Failure (GRASP-HF) is a prospective, multicentre, international observational study assessing implementation of the 2021/2023 ESC-HF-Guidelines. GRASP-HF is aligned with the Improving Care through Accreditation and Recognition in Heart Failure (ICARe-HF) programme, which links centre-characteristics with guideline-implementation performance.
AIMS: To compare baseline characteristics, guideline-directed-medical-therapy (GDMT) implementation, and in-hospital outcomes between GRASP-HF patients managed in centres participating or not participating in the ICARe-HF programme.
METHODS: GRASP-HF patients were stratified by ICARe-HF participation, clinical settings, acute (AHF) vs chronic HF (CHF) and ejection fraction (EF) subtypes. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models evaluated associations with quadruple therapy implementation and in-hospital mortality.
RESULTS: Among 10,936 patients (63.3% CHF, 36.7% AHF), patients from ICARe-HF participating centres (51.3%) were older, more comorbid but with less severe congestion. In both CHF and AHF, ICARe-HF centres demonstrated greater GDMT utilization, particularly angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors and sodium-glucose-cotransporter-2 inhibitors. In HFrEF, quadruple therapy was more frequently implemented (47% vs 40% in CHF; 27% vs 24% at AHF discharge) and remained associated with ICARe-HF participation after adjustment, Odd Ratio (OR) =1.73, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) :1.17-2.55. Target doses remained suboptimal, particularly after AHF. Although crude in-hospital mortality was lower in ICARe-HF centres (2.3% vs 5.5%), this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (OR=0.87, 95% CI:0.48-1.56).
CONCLUSIONS: Participation in the ICARe-HF programme was associated with more comprehensive implementation of contemporary GDMT, particularly in HFrEF. The association with in-hospital mortality was attenuated after adjustment and should be considered exploratory.

Title: Myocardial T1 Mapping at 3 T: A Comparison of MOLLI and ShMOLLI across Healthy Volunteers and Various Cardiovascular Pathologies.
Abstract: Background The clinical utility of quantitative T1 mapping in cardiac MRI is constrained by variability across acquisition protocols, and a comprehensive comparison between commonly used sequences remains unavailable. Purpose To provide a full range of cardiac MRI native T1 and extracellular volume fraction (ECV) values at 3 T in healthy Chinese adults and participants with various cardiovascular diseases and, as a secondary aim, to establish the relationship between modified Look-Locker inversion recovery (MOLLI) and shortened MOLLI (ShMOLLI) measurements. Materials and Methods This prospective study included healthy volunteers, participants with normal cardiac MRI findings, and participants representing 13 cardiovascular conditions. All participants underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences during a single examination. Global native T1 and ECV values were quantified and compared between sequences and across disease groups. Statistical approaches included t tests, Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen D standardization. Results This study included 1237 clinical participants (mean age ± SD: 51 years ± 14.8; 854 men). Reference values (adjusted mean ± SE) in healthy volunteers were 1170 msec ± 9 (MOLLI) and 1135 msec ± 10 (ShMOLLI) for native T1 and were 24.8% ± 0.6 (both MOLLI and ShMOLLI) for ECV, with women showing higher native T1 values than men (all P ≤ .002). MOLLI yielded systematically higher native T1 than ShMOLLI across all conditions (mean difference: 46.0 msec ± 27.2; all P < .01), whereas ECV did not differ for most conditions (10 of 15 groups; P > .05). Strong intersequence correlations were observed for native T1 (Pearson r = 0.93; P < .001) and ECV (r = 0.95; P < .001). After standardization to sequence-specific baselines, pathologic deviations were comparable between sequences (Cohen D differences ≤0.5 in most groups). A supplementary swine study supported the technical validity of both sequences (r = 0.87-0.90; P < .001). Conclusion In participants who underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences, native T1 was higher with MOLLI than ShMOLLI, but ECV was consistent across sequences. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Dacher and Cadour in this issue.

Title: Temporal trends of heart failure epidemic in the Rotterdam Study over three decades.
Abstract:
AIM: There is limited information on the heart failure (HF) epidemic and its temporal changes. Current research aimed to report the HF epidemic over the past three decades in the Rotterdam Study, covering the prevalence and incidence of HF, comorbidities and risk determinants.
METHODS: Using data from the population-based Rotterdam cohort, three Epoch groups [Epoch 1990s (1989-1993, N=7,983), Epoch 2000s (1997-2001, N=7,738), and Epoch 2010s (2009-2014, N=6,170)] were identified, with a mean age of nearly 70 years. For each Epoch group, point prevalence at baseline and 5-year HF incidence rate, comorbidities at baseline, and HF risk determinants (using Cox proportional hazards models) were calculated.
RESULTS: Point prevalence of HF was 3.3% in Epoch 1990s, 6.0% in Epoch 2000s, and 4.8% in Epoch 2010s, with an increase from the 1990s to 2000s followed by a decline in the 2010s, yielding an overall statistically significant upward trend (p<0.001). 5-year incidence of HF per 1,000 person-years was 16.3 (95%CI: 15.0 to 17.8), 10.3 (95%CI: 9.2 to 11.4) and 7.9 (95%CI: 6.9 to 9.0) in respective epochs, with a downward trend. Hypertension was the most common comorbidity in HF patients, followed by dyslipidemia and kidney dysfunction. The association of hypertension and diabetes with risk of incident HF decreased over time. Coronary heart disease (CHD), atrial fibrillation (AF) and stroke all showed increasing hazard ratios across groups.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of HF increased during the past decades in a population-based setting, while HF incidence declined. Hypertension and diabetes tended to become less critical risk factors for new-onset HF nowadays, while CHD, AF, and stroke showed trends toward stronger associations with HF risk over time.

Title: Ten-Year Experience with Combined Hyperbaric Oxygen and Steroid Therapy for Idiopathic Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss: A Retrospective Cohort of 332 Patients.
Journal: The journal of international advanced otology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) combined with systemic corticosteroids in patients with idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL), with particular focus on treatment timing, predictors of hearing recovery, and the impact of comorbidities.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center (AOU "San Giovanni di Dio e Ruggi d'Aragona," Salerno, Italy). A total of 332 adult patients with ISSNHL treated between 2014 and 2024 were included. All patients received combined therapy with systemic corticosteroids (oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day, tapered over 10-15 days) and HBOT (2.4 atmospheres absolute, 90 minutes per session; median of 10 sessions). Audiometric outcomes were assessed using pure-tone average (PTA). Treatment response was defined as a ≥30% improvement in PTA compared with baseline. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of hearing improvement. Safety outcomes were also recorded.
RESULTS: Mean baseline PTA was 61.3 ± 21.5 dB HL, improving to 44.6 ± 22.7 dB HL after treatment, with a mean hearing gain of 16.7 ± 14.2 dB HL (P < .001). Overall, 151 patients (43.5%) met the response criteria. Responders presented with significantly higher baseline PTA compared with nonresponders (67.6 vs. 56.8 dB HL, P < .001) and more frequently reported tinnitus (64.2% vs. 51.5%, P = .014). Median time to treatment initiation was 15 days (interquartile range: 7-30). Multivariate analysis identified shorter time to treatment (odds ratio [OR]: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98), presence of tinnitus (OR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.15-2.80), and higher baseline PTA (OR: 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05) as independent predictors of hearing improvement. Common comorbidities, including hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, were not significantly associated with treatment response. No serious adverse events related to HBOT were observed.
CONCLUSION: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy combined with systemic corticosteroids was associated with improved audiometric outcomes in patients with ISSNHL, particularly when initiated early. Shorter time to treatment, greater baseline hearing loss, and the presence of tinnitus emerged as independent predictors of hearing recovery. Overall, these findings suggest an association between early HBOT use and improved audiometric outcomes and support its consideration as an adjunctive component of multimodal treatment strategies for ISSNHL.

Title: Progression of Tricuspid Regurgitation After Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Implantation and Its Impact on Mortality and Hospitalization: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) progression is a recognized complication of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation, yet its prognostic impact on long-term clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this single-center retrospective cohort, 303 patients undergoing CIED implantation between 2005 and 2023 were followed for a median of 4.8 years. TR severity was assessed echocardiographically at baseline and 12 months. The primary endpoint was TR progression (≥ 1-grade worsening); secondary endpoints were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular hospitalization, their composite, and progression to severe TR, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression. TR progressed in 103 patients (34.0%), regressed in 33 (10.9%), and remained stable in 167 (55.1%), a net rightward shift (p < 0.001). Progression differed by device type (p = 0.031): among the larger subgroups, VVI-ICD showed the greatest net progression (31.8% worsened vs. 6.9% improved; p < 0.001) and CRT-D the highest regression (18.8%). During follow-up, 67 patients (22.1%) died and 164 (54.1%) were hospitalized. Overall TR progression was not independently associated with mortality (HR 1.118, p = 0.693) but independently predicted cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 1.640, p = 0.003) and the composite endpoint (HR 1.480, p = 0.014). On unadjusted analysis, progression specifically to severe TR (n = 15) was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.99, p = 0.024) and cardiovascular hospitalization (HR 2.45, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: TR progression occurs in approximately one-third of CIED recipients within the first year and independently predicts cardiovascular hospitalization. Progression to severe TR identifies a higher-risk subset, supporting routine post-implant echocardiographic surveillance.

Title: David G. Sherman Lecture: The Eternal Quest for Optimal Stroke Prevention.
Abstract: Despite decades of clinical trial activity in stroke prevention, critical gaps remain in the evidence base guiding management of symptomatic carotid and intracranial stenosis and the quality of anticoagulation care delivered to patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This article synthesizes recent evidence and ongoing research efforts addressing 2 enduring challenges: demonstrating the value of intensive medical therapy relative to interventional approaches and improving the quality of stroke prevention care in AF. Previous trials focused on intracranial stenosis established that aggressive, protocol-driven medical management substantially reduces recurrent vascular events. In the realm of carotid stenosis, landmark trials conducted >3 decades ago no longer reflect modern pharmacological capabilities. Emerging evidence from plaque imaging, particularly intraplaque hemorrhage on magnetic resonance imaging, suggests that stenosis severity alone is an insufficient determinant of treatment strategy. Simultaneously, strokes related to AF continue to rise in the United States, driven by demographic aging, and large vessel occlusion strokes attributable to undertreated AF represent a preventable burden on the health system. Patient-centered, precision stroke prevention requires contemporary prospective data, integration of advanced vascular imaging biomarkers, and systematic improvements in preventative therapies for patients with AF. Targeting these areas holds promise for improving stroke prevention in the coming decades.

Title: Admission White Blood Cell Count and Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio for Early Risk Stratification after Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the adjusted associations and incremental prognostic value of admission white blood cell count (WBC) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for unfavorable discharge outcome after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH).
METHODS: Consecutive adults with CT-confirmed sICH admitted to a tertiary academic hospital in northwestern China from August 2021 through August 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. After eligibility screening, 764 patients formed the study cohort. Admission WBC and log2-transformed NLR were analyzed as continuous exposures; the primary outcome was discharge modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ≥ 3. Multivariable models were benchmarked against the ICH score and a clinical severity model. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples. A three-level outcome-derived WBC-NLR burden classification was treated as exploratory and evaluated with 1000 nested bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: The primary complete-case analysis included 752 patients, of whom 358 (47.6%) had an unfavorable discharge outcome. Each 1 × 109/L increase in WBC was associated with higher odds of unfavorable outcome (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.116; 95% CI, 1.035-1.204; p = 0.004), and each doubling of NLR was associated with an adjusted OR of 2.187 (95% CI, 1.687-2.835; p < 0.001). Adding WBC and NLR increased the ICH score AUC from 0.757 to 0.848 (ΔAUC, 0.091; p < 0.001) and the clinical model AUC from 0.875 to 0.909 (ΔAUC, 0.034; p < 0.001). The optimism-corrected AUC of the full model was 0.900, with a corrected calibration slope of 0.932 and Brier score of 0.129. The nested-bootstrap-corrected AUC was 0.776 for the exploratory burden-only model and 0.899 after adding clinical covariates.
CONCLUSIONS: Admission WBC and NLR remained associated with unfavorable discharge outcome after adjustment and improved discrimination beyond established severity measures. They may support preliminary short-term risk assessment, whereas the outcome-derived burden categories require external validation. The discharge endpoint should not be interpreted as a substitute for 90-day functional outcome.

Title: Efficacy and Safety of Enlicitide in Hypercholesterolemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high-risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL-C targets. Enlicitide (MK-0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9-directed therapies.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of enlicitide in adults with hypercholesterolemia and assess its dose-dependent effects on lipid parameters.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched from inception through March 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis using restricted maximum likelihood estimation was performed. The primary outcome was the percentage change in LDL-C from baseline. Secondary outcomes included non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), apolipoprotein B (ApoB), lipoprotein(a), triglycerides, and safety outcomes. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using RoB 2.0 and GRADE.
RESULTS: Three placebo-controlled RCTs involving 3593 participants were included. Enlicitide significantly reduced LDL-C compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], -56.19%; 95% CI, -64.14 to -48.25; p < 0.0001), with moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 56.9%). Significant reductions were also observed in non-HDL-C (MD, -51.36%), ApoB (MD, -47.09%), lipoprotein(a) (MD, -20.10%), and triglycerides (MD, -13.12%). A numerical dose-response gradient was observed, although subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. Rates of adverse events, serious adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were comparable between groups.
CONCLUSION: Enlicitide produced substantial reductions in LDL-C and other atherogenic lipid parameters without an apparent increase in adverse events. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, moderate heterogeneity, and reliance on surrogate endpoints. Dose-response, duration-related lipoprotein(a), and triglyceride findings were exploratory and substantially driven by single trials. Long-term cardiovascular outcomes trials are needed to establish clinical benefit.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Meta-Analysis; Review

Title: Characterization of Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Treated Inadequately with Anticoagulants: Why Hospitalization Is Not an Opportunity to Correct Errors.
Journal: The Israel Medical Association journal : IMAJ
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common cardiac arrhythmia. Prevalence increases with age. It is a major public health concern due to high risk of thromboembolic complications such as stroke and systemic embolism. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have been shown to have improved safety and efficacy profiles and are the preferred therapy in all recent guidelines. However, patients are still discharged from internal medicine wards without appropriate DOAC therapy.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the effectiveness of hospitalization in correcting inappropriate therapy for AF in patients who were hospitalized in the internal medicine departments for any reason and discharged without receiving DOAC therapy.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we gathered data from electronic medical records at Sheba Medical Center on 222 patients. The patients were divided into three groups based on the anticoagulation therapy they received.
RESULTS: The patient cohort (mean age of 77.1 years; 42.3% males; 21.6% presented with cognitive impairment. Researchers identified several potential contraindications for DOACs (renal disease in 24.3%, mechanical valves in 14.4%). When comparing patients with and without DOAC contraindications, there were no statistically significant differences regarding cognitive impairment rates or the lack of anticoagulation therapy. We further divided patients who did not receive DOACs into two groups: 134 due to contraindications and 88 mistakenly. Between these groups, baseline factors showed no statistically significant differences.
CONCLUSIONS: We found that older patients received less standardized care. Findings emphasize the need to consider individual patient characteristics and co-morbidities to eliminate management errors and improve the quality of clinical care.

Title: Efficacy of Diabetic Foot Ulcer Treatment and Possible Ways for Improvement: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Journal: The Israel Medical Association journal : IMAJ
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot (DF) is a dangerous complication of diabetes mellitus (DM). Modern treatment modalities and good organization of care can improve prognosis.
OBJECTIVES: To analyze results of DF treatment in a tertiary care setting and the degree of implementation of international guidelines in practice.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 90 patients treated for DF ulcers/wounds in our center (May-December 2023). Thirty-five patients received only outpatient care. The median age was 65 (37-90) years, 96% had type 2 DM.
RESULTS: Median wound duration was 29 (1-1461) days. Previous treatment was conducted by a family doctor in 30%, at a local wound clinic in 7%, by other medical specialists in 27%, or by the patient/relatives in 29%. At this stage off-loading devices were prescribed for 37%, and 35% were referred to a vascular surgeon. Limb ischemia occurred in 44 patients (49%), revascularization was conducted for 16 patients. At 6 months, healing rates were 48%. Minor or major amputation rates were 4% and 5%, respectively; 6% died, 29% stayed unhealed, and 8% were lost to follow-up. Multivariable analysis revealed independent predictors of non-healing (ethnic group and impossibility of revascularization) and of amputation (previous major amputation, presence of osteomyelitis, and white blood cell count).
CONCLUSIONS: To prevent diabetes-related amputations, healthcare professionals must prioritize preventive care, provide regular podiatry services for high-risk patients, ensure early specialist treatment for any foot ulcer, implement international guidelines at all levels of DF care, and increase the capacity of secondary wound clinics and access to revascularization.

Title: Hydrogen-rich jelly exhibits a positive effect on heart rate variability during orthostatic loading in healthy adults: a randomized crossover trial.
Journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
Abstract: Hydrogen gas may improve autonomic regulation. The effects of hydrogen-rich jelly (HRJ) on autonomic responses during postural transition have not yet been investigated. This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial evaluated HRJ effects on heart rate variability (HRV) in 50 healthy adults (21 men; mean age, 44.2 ± 11.3 years). HRJ (30-40 ppm, 10 g) or placebo was orally administered 24 h, 1.5 h, and immediately before testing. HRV was recorded during an orthostatic loading protocol with four 1 min phases: seated rest, stand-up, standing, and resitting. Among the 48 participants with complete data, no significant difference in the primary endpoint of high-frequency was observed. Exploratory analyses revealed lower coefficient of variation of the R-R interval (CVRR) during the stand-up phase (mean difference: -0.46, p = 0.047) and lower low-frequency-to-high-frequency (L/H) ratio during the resitting phase (mean difference: -1.51, p = 0.027), with no significant differences at rest or during standing. Subgroup analyses suggested stronger responses in women and those with lower skeletal muscle mass (CVRR), and in younger participants, those with higher body mass index, and habitual alcohol consumption (L/H). HRJ may induce mild, stage-specific changes in HRV during postural transitions. However, their physiological and clinical significance remains uncertain and should be clarified in future studies.

Title: Haemodiafiltration, haemofiltration and haemodialysis for adults with kidney failure.
Journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Convective extracorporeal dialysis modalities, haemofiltration (HF), haemodiafiltration (HDF), and acetate-free biofiltration (AFB), remove excess body fluid across the dialysis membrane through an interplay of positive and negative pressures and accumulated middle- and larger-sized solutes more efficiently than haemodialysis (HD). This increased removal of larger solutes, combined with the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid in convective dialysis, is hypothesised to reduce the frequency and severity of symptoms during HD and improve long-term clinical outcomes. This is an update of a review first published in 2006 and updated in 2015.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the benefits and harms of convective (HF, HDF, or AFB) versus diffusive (HD) dialysis modalities, or expanded HD (HDx), in preventing all-cause and cardiovascular death, cardiovascular morbidity, fatigue, and vascular access problems in adults with kidney failure.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers up to 3 April 2025. Additionally, handsearching of journals and conference abstract books was performed, and the references of the included studies were reviewed.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing convective therapy (HF, HDF, AFB) with another convective therapy or with diffusive therapy (HD or HDx) for treating adults with kidney failure.
OUTCOMES: Critical and important outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular death, nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, problems with vascular access, hospitalisation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL).
RISK OF BIAS: Two authors independently assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We summarised treatment effects using the random-effects model and reported risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous data with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the confidence of the evidence using the GRADE approach.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We identified 62 eligible studies (6897 participants). In total, 54 studies (6525 participants) compared HF, HDF or AFB with HD (both high-flux and low-flux); two studies (24 participants) compared AFB with HDF; three studies (62 participants) compared HDF with HF; and four studies (163 participants) compared HDx with HDF/HD.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Convective dialysis, compared with diffusive therapy, likely reduces the risk of death (any cause) (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.96; I² = 0%; 15 studies, 5463 participantss; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92; I² = 0%; 9 studies, 4761 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Cardiovascular morbidity was likely not different between convective and diffusive dialysis (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.22; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 2074 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Little to no differences were found between convective and diffusive dialysis on fatigue (MD -0.95, 95% CI -2.50 to 0.60; 1 study, 543 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), problems with vascular access (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.50; 1 study, 124 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), hospitalisation (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 600 participants; low-certainty evidence due to indirectness and imprecision), or physical quality of life (MD 0.66, 95% CI -1.08 to 2.40; 1 study, 538 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision). Direct comparisons between different convective modalities were limited and underpowered to detect meaningful differences.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Convective dialysis likely reduces all-cause and cardiovascular death. Effects on nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, vascular access failure, and hospitalisation are inconclusive. Future RCTs should prioritise methodological rigour and could focus on unresolved questions, including the impact of convective therapies on patient-centred outcomes such as symptom burden, HRQoL, functional status, and intradialytic tolerance, as well as investigating barriers to uptake, evaluating health system readiness, assessing cost-effectiveness, and identifying strategies to promote equitable access.
FUNDING: No specific funding.
REGISTRATION: Previous versions available via DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD006258 and DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD006258.pub2.

Title: Performance of the Expanded Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Score for Rheumatoid Arthritis: An External Validation in the BRASS Registry.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular (CV) disease occurs more frequently in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) than in the general population and is difficult to predict. The Expanded Risk Score for Rheumatoid Arthritis (ERS-RA) has demonstrated good discrimination and calibration in prior studies, but additional external validation studies are needed to understand clinical utility. The goal of this study was to perform an external validation of ERS-RA.
METHODS: Data from a single-center RA registry was integrated with electronic health records (EHR) and linked to Medicare or Medicaid administrative claims data. A less restrictive CV outcome was defined as an event identified in any of the three data sources (questionnaires, EHR, or claims), and a more restrictive outcome included events in EHR and claims. External validation of the ERS-RA examined model discrimination and calibration.
RESULTS: The longitudinal RA registry has 1,332 participants aged 20 to 80 years without prior evidence of CVD, observed for a mean of 6.8 years. The mean age was 54 years, and 84% were female. We observed 164 (12.3%) and 69 (5.2%) participants with a CV event with the less and more restrictive CV definitions, respectively. The mean ERS-RA predicted score was 7.1%, and 424 participants (32%) had a predictive score ≥7.5%. We observed C-statistics of 0.66 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62-0.71) for less restrictive and 0.80 (95% CI 0.76-0.85) for more restrictive. The ERS-RA also demonstrated good calibration, with better performance for the more restrictive CV event definition.
CONCLUSION: The ERS-RA demonstrated good discrimination and calibration for CV risk prediction in an external validation RA cohort. It also highlights the importance of using multiple sources of data to find CV events in a non-CV registry.

Title: Association of Retinal Age Gap with Socioeconomic Deprivation: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of a Large Diverse Urban Cohort.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Socioeconomic deprivation is a profound determinant of health, driving systemic physiological dysregulation that may accelerate biological ageing. Retinal age gap (RAG) is a validated deep-learning-derived biomarker for accelerated ageing and systemic disease risk. This study investigates the relationship between socioeconomic deprivation and RAG in two large, distinct United Kingdom cohorts.
METHODS: We performed cross-sectional analysis within the UK Biobank (UKB) (N = 38,412) and the London-based AlzEye (N = 49,681) cohorts. Socioeconomic deprivation was defined using Townsend Index for UKB and Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) for AlzEye. RAG was generated from colour fundus photography using a pre-trained deep learning model. We applied linear regression modelling to examine associations between deprivation and RAG, sequentially adjusting for chronological age, sex, ethnicity, hypertension, and diabetes.
RESULTS: The AlzEye cohort was older, more diverse, and had more comorbidities compared to the UKB cohort. Modelled per decile of decreasing deprivation, there was significant association with decreased RAG in both UKB (-0.11 years per decile; 95% CI -0.13 to -0.10; p < 0.001) and AlzEye (-0.43 years per decile; 95% CI -0.46 to -0.39; p < 0.001). Following full adjustment, association remained significant in UKB (-0.04 years per decile; p < 0.001) but was attenuated and non-significant in AlzEye (-0.002 years per decile; p = 0.82).
CONCLUSIONS: Socioeconomic deprivation is associated with accelerated retinal ageing, although influenced by cohort characteristics and underlying health status. Signal attenuation in AlzEye suggests comorbidities may mediate impact of deprivation on retinal ageing. Longitudinal research is required to disentangle complex interplay, ensuring equitable utility of oculomic biomarkers in precision medicine.

Title: Association of Intraoperative Trigeminal Cardiac Reflex With Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Skull Base Tumor Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between intraoperative trigemino-cardiac reflex (TCR) and postoperative myocardial injury in patients undergoing skull base tumor resection remains unclear.
METHODS: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled patients undergoing elective skull base tumor resection between April 2023 and September 2024. The primary outcome was postoperative myocardial injury, defined as a cardiac troponin I level >16 ng/L within 24 hours after surgery. Patients were categorized into TCR and non-TCR groups. Logistic regression analyses were performed to explore factors associated with intraoperative TCR and postoperative myocardial injury.
RESULTS: Among 476 included patients, intraoperative TCR occurred in 27.9%, and postoperative myocardial injury occurred in 4.83%. Patients experiencing TCR had a higher rate of myocardial injury (8.3% vs. 3.5%, P=0.029). Multivariable analysis suggested that brainstem compression (adjusted OR=1.86; 95% CI: 1.19-2.91; P=0.007) and larger tumor diameter (adjusted OR=1.04; 95% CI: 1.02-1.07; P<0.001) independently associated with intraoperative TCR. TCR (adjusted OR=2.70; 95% CI: 1.12-6.53; P=0.028), older age (adjusted OR=1.06; 95% CI: 1.02-1.10; P=0.003), lower BMI (adjusted OR=0.80; 95% CI: 0.70-0.93; P=0.003), and tumor recurrence (adjusted OR=4.07; 95% CI: 1.43-11.57; P=0.009) were associated with postoperative myocardial injury after adjusting for selected confounders.
CONCLUSION: Postoperative myocardial injury occurred in 4.83% of skull base tumor surgery patients. Intraoperative TCR increased the risk of this injury, though the link may relate to surgical complexity and patient characteristics. TCR may therefore serve as a potential clinical marker of patients at elevated perioperative cardiovascular risk rather than a direct causal mechanism.

Title: Association between the inferior vena cava collapsibility index and Fontan pressure in patients with Fontan physiology: a two-centre prospective pilot study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with functional single ventricle anatomy undergo staged surgical palliation in early childhood culminating in the Fontan procedure whereby the inferior vena cava is connected to the pulmonary artery. Fontan circulation inherently requires elevated central venous pressure to maintain adequate pulmonary blood flow; however, excessive elevation is associated with morbidity and mortality. In adults, a key component of echocardiographic evaluation is the use of a "sniff test" as a surrogate of downstream right atrial pressure. This technique has not yet been validated as a measure of pressure assessment in patients with Fontan circulation.
METHODS: This was a two-center prospective study of patients with functional single ventricle physiology who had undergone the Fontan procedure and were undergoing previously scheduled transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac catheterization as part of their standard clinical care. We correlated collapsibility index on echocardiogram with directly obtained Fontan pressure measurements from cardiac catheterization performed the same day.
RESULTS: 15 patients were enrolled and analyzed for the study. Collapsibility index demonstrated an inverse correlation with Fontan pressure, (Pearson r = -0.72, R2 = 0.51, p = 0.003). Collapsibility index was significantly higher for patients with non-elevated Fontan pressure (45% vs 30%, p = 0.0005). Using a collapsibility index threshold of 35.0% demonstrated a 100% positive predictive value for detecting elevated Fontan pressure (greater than 14 mmHg).
CONCLUSIONS: There was a significant inverse relationship between the collapsibility index and Fontan pressure. These findings may suggest a possible association between collapsibility index and Fontan pressure, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

Title: Combined ischaemia and vulnerable plaque percutaneous coronary intervention to reduce cardiovascular events: design and rationale of the COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial.
Journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
Abstract: Fractional flow reserve (FFR) assessment represents the most widely used revascularisation strategy of the last two decades. However, many FFR (+) lesions, particularly those in the grey zone, can be safely treated medically, while other lesions carrying vulnerable plaque (VP) features can cause future events despite the absence of ischaemia. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) can identify lesions with VP morphology. The objective of this study is to determine whether a combined revascularisation strategy - targeting only severely ischaemic lesions (FFR ≤0.75) and extending treatment to OCT-assessed VP, even in the absence of ischaemia (FFR>0.80) - could reduce future adverse events compared with the current revascularisation practice based exclusively on the presence of ischaemia (FFR ≤0.80). The COMBINE-INTERVENE Trial is a global, prospective, randomised, single-blinded, sham-controlled, superiority trial. A total of 1,223 all-comer patients with multivessel disease (≥2 lesions with a diameter of stenosis ≥50%) will be randomised 1:1 to revascularisation if the FFR is ≤0.75 or a VP is present (experimental arm) versus FFR ≤0.80 in the comparative arm. The primary endpoint is a composite of cardiac death, any myocardial infarction, or any clinically driven revascularisation within 24 months. The trial has already completed enrolment in 50 centres worldwide. COMBINE-INTERVENE is the first trial evaluating the impact of a revascularisation strategy that targets lesions that are either severely ischaemic or carry an OCT-assessed VP versus revascularisation based on ischaemia alone. The trial is powered for superiority. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05333068).

Title: Guideline directed medical therapy and decongestion in patients with acute heart failure.
Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

Title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups.
METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks.
RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; P=0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; P=0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; P=0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly.
CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

Title: Impact of 18FDG-Avidity and Immunosuppression on Idiopathic and Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial 18fluorodeoxyglucose (18FDG)-avidity is frequently seen in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy, as well as a growing "idiopathic 18FDG-avidity" group of genotype-negative patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis. The prognostic implications of 18FDG-avidity in patients with and without genetic cardiomyopathy, and the effects of immunosuppression in the latter, remain uncertain.
METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study included all patients who were referred for both 18FDG-PET and cardiomyopathy genetic testing. Patients with acute myocarditis, biopsy-proven sarcoidosis, or extracardiac 18FDG-avidity were excluded. We investigated heart failure (HF) composite (left ventricular assist device, heart transplant, HF hospitalization, or death) and arrhythmia composite (sustained ventricular arrhythmias [ventricular tachycardia/VF], atrioventricular block, or death) outcomes using survival analysis, including Cox proportional hazards modeling and inverse probability of treatment weighting.
RESULTS: Among 372 patients, 142 (38%) were 18FDG-avid. The prevalence of genetic cardiomyopathy among 18FDG-avid patients (12%) was similar to that of 18FDG-negative patients (18%; P=0.11). Unadjusted, 18FDG-avidity was associated with an increased risk of HF composite (hazard ratio, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.04-2.75]; P=0.034) and arrhythmia composite (hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.1-2.4]; P=0.014) outcomes compared with 18FDG-negative patients. However, these associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, nor were there significant differences in 18FDG-associated risks in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy versus genotype-negative patients. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, immunosuppression of 18FDG-avid patients (n=49) was not associated with a reduction in HF or arrhythmia composite outcomes compared with those who were not immunosuppressed (n=93).
CONCLUSIONS: Myocardial-only 18FDG-avidity is not significantly associated with HF or arrhythmia risk in patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis (including those with genetic cardiomyopathy). Immunosuppression therapy does not seem to modify the disease course, suggesting that not all myocardial 18FDG uptake reflects clinically significant inflammation.

Title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions.
METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0-42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P<0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm2, regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm2, regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]).
CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

Title: National Survival Estimates After Surgical Repair of Congenital Heart Disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survival estimates after congenital heart surgery (CHS) in the United States are essential for planning healthcare services for this growing, resource-intensive patient population. However, the absolute number of individuals living after interventions for congenital heart disease is unknown because nationally representative survival estimates are unavailable. Understanding postoperative survival from a representative national sample is a critical first step toward estimating the size and future healthcare needs of this population. This study aimed to develop nationally representative long-term survival estimates after CHS in the United States, focusing on benchmark procedures defined by the Society of Thoracic Surgeons.
METHODS: We used 3 US data sets of children aged 0 to 20 years at the time of their benchmark CHS from 1998 to 2002 and surviving to hospital discharge. The Pediatric Cardiac Care Consortium (PCCC), a multi-institutional clinical registry, was matched to the National Death Index to determine mortality through December 2019. The Kids' Inpatient Database 2000, a nationally representative administrative claims data set, was used to derive age- and sex-specific weights. Kaplan-Meier curves were estimated from the PCCC-National Death Index cohort for benchmark operations, and Kids' Inpatient Database 2000 weights were applied. Unweighted PCCC survival estimates were also compared with those of Boston Children's Hospital, a large tertiary care center.
RESULTS: Nationally representative survival curves were generated for 7 benchmark CHS from 7973 cases; 3802 (48%) were female, and 4505 (57%) were infants at the time of CHS. These weighted national survival curves closely mirrored the unweighted curves derived from PCCC-National Death Index. Unweighted survival estimates from PCCC also closely approximated those from BCH, with only modest differences observed for selected lesions.
CONCLUSIONS: The weighted PCCC-National Death Index methodology provides the first nationally representative estimates of long-term survival after benchmark congenital heart disease in the United States. These estimates provide an important resource for healthcare planning and research for the growing population of individuals with congenital heart disease.

Title: The Impact of Local Heat Therapy on Comfort and Physiological Parameters in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome leads to disturbances in physiological parameters and reduces patient comfort due to the nature of the disease and its associated complications. This study examined the effect of local heat therapy on the comfort and physiological parameters of patients with acute coronary syndrome.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This clinical trial utilized a block randomization method to allocate 80 patients with acute coronary syndrome into two groups of 40 participants each. In the intervention group, a heat pack warmed in water to 75 °C was wrapped in a special towel and applied to the posterior thoracic region (T4-T11 vertebrae). During the intervention, the patient lay in the supine position on the heat pack. Each heat therapy session lasted 23 minutes. In the control group, a similar heat pack was used at a temperature of 37°C. Heat therapy was performed every 12 hours for 2 days (a total of four sessions). The Kolkaba Comfort Questionnaire and physiological parameters were assessed pre- and post-intervention. Data analysis was performed with statistical significance established at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Before the intervention, no significant differences were found between the groups. However, at the end of the intervention, heat therapy in patients with acute coronary syndrome significantly increased comfort, regulation of physiological parameters was observed, and enhanced oxygen saturation (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Heat therapy can be used as a safe and complementary intervention alongside modern medicine to enhance comfort and regulate physiological parameters in patients with acute coronary syndrome.

Title: Gastroparesis in heart failure: temporal trends, clinical correlates, and outcomes in a large national cohort.
Abstract: Gastrointestinal complications of heart failure are increasingly recognized, but the epidemiology and clinical significance of gastroparesis in this population remain poorly defined. We evaluated a national multicenter cohort of adults with heart failure to characterize temporal trends in gastroparesis incidence, identify factors associated with its development, and assess its association with clinical outcomes. We used a national multicenter database to identify adults diagnosed with heart failure from 2005 to 2025. Temporal trends in gastroparesis incidence were evaluated at 5-year intervals, multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify factors associated with its development, and 5-year cardiorenal and healthcare utilization outcomes were compared between patients with and without gastroparesis. Among 3,913,826 patients with heart failure, gastroparesis incidence increased more than tenfold during the study period, from 35.6 to 402.3 cases per 100,000 person-years. Diabetes mellitus [hazard ratio (HR) =4.54], chronic mesenteric ischemia (HR =2.16), ascites (HR =1.55), and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HR =1.60) were independently associated with gastroparesis. Patients with concomitant gastroparesis experienced significantly higher risks of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) [31.8% vs. 19.7%; odds ratio (OR) =1.90; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.80-1.99; P<0.001], acute kidney injury, end-stage renal disease, emergency department visits, and intensive care unit admission (38.9% vs. 22.6%; OR =2.19; 95% CI: 2.11-2.27; P<0.001). These findings identify gastroparesis as an increasingly recognized comorbidity in patients with heart failure that may represent a high-risk phenotype. The observed associations further suggest that venous congestion and impaired splanchnic perfusion may contribute to the development of gastric dysmotility in this population.

Title: Determinants of hypertensive retinopathy among non-diabetic adults in comprehensive specialized hospitals of the Amhara region, northwest Ethiopia: a case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive retinopathy is a common microvascular complication of hypertension associated with visual impairment and increased cardiovascular risk, but evidence regarding its associated factors in Ethiopia is limited. This study aimed to identify factors associated with hypertensive retinopathy among adult hypertensive patients in northwest Ethiopia.
METHODS: An institution-based unmatched case-control study was conducted from 4 June to 30 June 2024, among 309 participants (76 cases and 233 controls). Cases were hypertensive patients with retinopathy diagnosed by ophthalmologists, while controls were hypertensive patients without retinopathy. Systematic random sampling was used to select study participants. The primary outcome measure was the presence of hypertensive retinopathy (yes/no), as diagnosed and documented in medical records. Data were collected through interviewer-administered questionnaires, medical record reviews, and physical measurements (blood pressure, weight, and height). Self-care and social support were assessed using validated scales. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with retinopathy, and model fit was assessed by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (P > 0.05). Significance was set at P < 0.05.
RESULTS: The mean age of study participants was 51.75 ± 8.84 years. Factors associated with hypertensive retinopathy included: urban residence (AOR = 10.6; 95% CI: 2.9-37.9), BMI ≥25 kg/m2 (AOR = 7.9; 95% CI: 2.6-24.2), diastolic BP > 90 mmHg (AOR = 25.3; 95% CI: 3.1-212.1), poor self-care (AOR = 5.6; 95% CI: 2.1-15.9), and lack of social support (AOR = 5.1; 95% CI: 2.1-12.4).
CONCLUSION: Urban residence, elevated BMI, uncontrolled diastolic blood pressure, poor self-care, and lack of social support independently increase the odds of hypertensive retinopathy. Comprehensive management that integrates retinal screening, self-care education, and social support is needed, especially in urban areas.

Title: Aloe Vera Gel Compared to Cold/Warm Compresses for Reducing Ecchymosis at the Saphenous Vein Graft Harvest Site: Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
Journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The saphenous vein harvest site in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery is highly susceptible to edema and local complications such as ecchymosis. This study aimed to compare the efficacy of aloe vera gel with that of cold and warm compresses in reducing ecchymosis at the lower leg harvest site in patients undergoing CABG surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This two-group randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted on 60 patients scheduled for CABG surgery. Eligible participants were selected through convenience sampling and randomly assigned to either Group A (aloe vera gel) or Group B (cold and warm compresses). For each participant, one leg was randomly assigned as the intervention site and the other as the control. Data collection tools included a demographic and surgical information form and an ecchymosis assessment chart. The intervention lasted for 6 days. Control legs received routine postoperative dressing. Photographs were taken on postoperative days, and the ecchymosis area was measured using ImageJ software.
RESULTS: Before the intervention, there was no significant difference in the mean ecchymosis area between the two groups (p > 0.05). The mean ecchymosis area in the treated leg decreased significantly compared to the control leg in both groups on days 5, 7, 10, and 30 (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Aloe vera gel was significantly more effective than cold and warm compresses in reducing ecchymosis at the saphenous vein graft (SVG) harvest site. Aloe vera gel can be considered an effective adjunctive treatment to minimize ecchymosis in patients following CABG surgery.

Title: Trial sequential analysis of the efficacy of amino acid and protein therapy in preventing cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication after cardiac surgery, with varying severity and outcomes. Despite studies on corticosteroids, remote ischemic preconditioning, and amino acid therapies like glutamate, results have remained inconsistent. This review aims to clarify the therapeutic role of intravenous amino acids in improving outcomes of cardiac surgery-related AKI.
METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines, analyzing studies on intravenous amino acids to prevent cardiac surgery-associated AKI. Databases were searched using MeSH terms, and strict inclusion criteria were applied. Data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, and meta-analysis were conducted with standardized tools, including RevMan and TSA, to ensure reliability and statistical validity.
RESULTS: This meta-analysis included eight studies (seven RCTs and one cohort) evaluating amino acid/protein administration, with over 5000 participants per group. Results showed a non-significant trend toward reduced AKI risk (RR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.63-1.02; P = 0.07), a significant reduction in kidney replacement therapy (RR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.40-1.08; P = 0.07), and shorter hospital stays (SMD = -0.62). No significant effects were observed for mortality, stroke, arrhythmias, or dialysis. Heterogeneity varied, with the highest for hospital stays (I 2 = 95%).
CONCLUSION: Intraoperative amino acid/protein administration may reduce the risk of AKI and the need for renal replacement therapy, although this intervention appears to have limited impact on mortality or other complications. The observation of shorter hospital stays is promising, but further research is needed to standardize protocols and understand the underlying mechanisms.

Title: Prevalence, causes, and predictors of 30-day readmissions after acute myocardial infarction with ventricular arrhythmias: a cohort study using the 2016-2017 national readmissions database.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients surviving acute myocardial infarction (AMI) complicated by ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) are at high risk of early post-discharge readmissions due to multiple complications. These readmissions worsen clinical outcomes and add substantial financial strain to the U.S. healthcare system. This study investigates the prevalence, causes, and predictors of 30-day readmissions following hospitalization for AMI complicated by VAs.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Hospitalizations for AMI complicated by VAs were identified from the 2016-2017 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Independent predictors of 30-day readmission were analyzed using multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression in the R statistical software (version 4.5.0). Among 93 588 index hospitalizations, 8154 (8.7%) resulted in 30-day readmissions. In-hospital mortality occurred in 16.43% of index admissions and 5.92% of readmissions. Significant predictors of readmission included older age (OR: 1.01; P < 0.001), female sex (OR: 1.13; P = 0.002), prior heart failure (OR: 1.28; P < 0.001), peripheral vascular disease (OR: 1.18; P = 0.002), COPD (OR: 1.43; P < 0.001), atrial fibrillation (OR: 1.24; P < 0.001), diabetes (OR: 1.29; P < 0.001), previous MI (OR: 1.12; P = 0.009), end-stage renal disease (ESRD) (OR: 1.52; P < 0.001), stroke (OR: 1.52; P < 0.001), and hospital stay >4 days (OR: 1.94; P < 0.001). Higher income quartiles were associated with lower readmission risk. The mean index charges were $151 722, whereas charges per readmission were $64 122.
CONCLUSIONS: AMI complicated by VAs is associated with high 30-day readmission rates, driven mainly by noncardiac and select cardiac causes such as heart failure and atrial fibrillation. Enhanced monitoring of high-risk groups may improve outcomes and reduce healthcare costs.

Title: Electrolyte disturbance profiles and associated factors in Somali patients with heart failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrolyte disturbances are frequent yet under-monitored complications of heart failure (HF), contributing to arrhythmias, prolonged hospitalization, and increased mortality. Data from Somalia remain scarce, despite the growing HF burden.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted among 369 adult HF patients admitted to Mogadishu Somali-Turkish Training and Research Hospital between January 2023 and January 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics v29. Electrolyte disturbances were classified by standard cut-offs, and associations with clinical variables were tested using Chi-square and Pearson correlation analyses.
RESULTS: The mean age was 60.1 ± 15.2 years, and 43.6% were female. The mean ejection fraction was 31.3 ± 8.0% (range 10-45%), with most patients having reduced EF. Hyponatremia occurred in 38.5%, hypokalemia in 17.1%, and hypomagnesemia in 16.3%. Among affected patients, severe hyponatremia was most frequent (26.8%), while hypokalemia was largely mild (73.0%). Loop-diuretic therapy was significantly associated with hyponatremia and hypokalemia (P < 0.05), while electrolyte levels showed no significant correlation with age or ejection fraction (|r| ≤ 0.14).
CONCLUSION: Electrolyte disturbances - particularly hyponatremia and hypokalemia - are highly prevalent among Somali HF patients. These findings highlight the need for improved electrolyte monitoring in HF management in low-resource settings. Strengthening electrolyte monitoring and improving diagnostic capacity are essential for optimizing HF management in low-resource settings.

Title: The triglyceride-glucose index as a predictor of cardiovascular disease: an umbrella review of meta-analyses.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index has gained recognition as a tool for assessing cardiovascular disease risk. This umbrella review synthesized findings from multiple meta-analyses examining the association between the TyG index and cardiovascular outcomes.
METHODS: In this umbrella review of meta-analyses, we followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.
RESULTS: A higher TyG index was associated with increased odds of arterial stiffness [categorical: odds ratio (OR) = 1.83, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.55-2.17, P < 0.01; I 2 = 68%; per 1-unit increase: OR = 1.51, 95% CI: 1.35-1.69, P < 0.01; I 2 = 82%]; coronary artery stenosis (OR = 3.49, 95% CI: 1.71-7.12, P < 0.01; I 2 = 0%); coronary artery calcification (CAC) (highest vs. lowest: OR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.51-1.82, P < 0.01; I 2 = 0%; continuous: OR = 1.73, 95% CI: 1.36-2.20, P < 0.01; I 2 = 51%); CAC progression (categorical: OR = 1.66, 95% CI: 1.21-2.27, P < 0.01; I 2 = 0%; continuous: OR = 1.47, 95% CI: 1.29-1.68, P < 0.01; I 2 = 41%); and atrial fibrillation (AF) (categorical: OR = 1.98, 95% CI: 1.35-2.91, P < 0.01; I 2 = 92%; continuous: OR = 1.80, 95% CI: 1.50-2.17, P < 0.01; I 2 = 88%).
CONCLUSION: Current meta-analytic evidence suggests that higher TyG index values are associated with several adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, substantial heterogeneity and the generally low methodological quality of the included meta-analyses limit confidence in the magnitude and clinical applicability of these associations. The TyG index may serve as an adjunctive cardiovascular risk marker, but further high-quality prospective validation is required before routine clinical implementation.

Title: Association between coffee consumption and risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism - Results from the Trøndelag Health Study and Tromsø Study.
Journal: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epidemiological studies have shown that coffee consumption is associated with a lowered risk of incident venous thromboembolism (VTE). No previous study has explored whether coffee consumption influences the risk of VTE recurrence.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate whether the amount of coffee consumption (cups/d) is associated with the risk of VTE recurrence in a population-based cohort of incident VTEs.
METHODS: The cohort consisted of 2071 patients with incident VTE recruited from 4 surveys of the Tromsø Study (enrolment, 1994-2008) and the third survey of the Trøndelag Health Study (enrolment, 2006-2008), followed from the date of the index VTE until 2020. Information on coffee consumption (cups/d) and potential confounders was extracted. Cox regression models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CIs for VTE recurrence.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 310 recurrent VTEs occurred. There was no linear relationship between increasing coffee intake and VTE recurrence. The HR for recurrence was 0.49 (95% CI, 0.30-0.81) for those consuming 1 to 2 cups of coffee per day and 0.71 (95% CI, 0.44-1.12) for those consuming >6 cups compared with noncoffee consumers. The association between coffee consumption (yes/no) and lowered recurrence risk was more pronounced for provoked index VTE event (HR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.30-0.82) than for unprovoked index VTE (HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.53-1.94).
CONCLUSION: Coffee consumption was associated with a nonlinear, lowered risk of VTE recurrence, particularly after provoked VTE. Our findings suggest that coffee can be safely consumed after VTE, potentially with a beneficial effect on recurrence risk.

Title: Hybrid Explainable Deep Ensemble Framework with self-attention mechanism for early prediction of depression severity using PHQ-9 clinical and behavioral data.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression is a major global mental health disorder that requires accurate, reliable, and interpretable prediction models to support early identification and timely intervention. This study proposes a Hybrid Explainable Deep Ensemble Framework for multiclass prediction of depression severity using PHQ-9 clinical responses and behavioral characteristics.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional machine learning study was conducted using a dataset comprising 682 anonymized participants. Predictor variables included demographic characteristics, PHQ-9 questionnaire items, sleep quality, academic pressure, and financial pressure. A hybrid ensemble integrating TabNet, multilayer perceptron (MLP), and XGBoost was developed with a self-attention mechanism for adaptive feature weighting and a weighted soft-voting strategy for final prediction. Model performance was evaluated using five-fold stratified cross-validation and an independent test set. Accuracy, precision, recall, macro F1-score, ROC-AUC, Matthews correlation coefficient, confusion matrix analysis, and SHAP-based explainability were employed to assess predictive performance and model interpretability.
RESULTS: The proposed framework achieved an overall accuracy of 91.3%, precision of 0.907, recall of 0.898, macro F1-score of 0.902, and a macro-ROC-AUC of 0.940, outperforming the baseline machine learning models. Class-wise evaluation demonstrated the strongest performance for severe depression (F1-score = 0.934), whereas the mild depression category exhibited comparatively lower predictive performance (F1-score = 0.861) because of overlap with adjacent severity levels. Confusion matrix analysis indicated that misclassification primarily occurred between neighboring depression categories while clinically implausible predictions were rare. SHAP analysis identified sleep disturbance (PHQ-4), fatigue (PHQ-3), academic pressure, depressed mood (PHQ-2), and financial pressure as the most influential predictors. The ablation study further demonstrated that incorporating the self-attention mechanism and ensemble learning strategy improved both predictive performance and model robustness.
CONCLUSION: The proposed Hybrid Explainable Deep Ensemble Framework combines high predictive accuracy with transparent decision-making for multiclass depression severity assessment. By integrating deep learning, ensemble learning, self-attention, and explainable artificial intelligence, the framework provides accurate and clinically interpretable predictions and represents a promising approach for future clinical decision-support systems and precision mental health screening.

Title: Association of the Triglyceride-Glucose Index with Systolic and Diastolic Blood Pressure Among Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
Abstract: Background Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist, substantially increasing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Insulin resistance is a key mechanism linking these conditions. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, derived from fasting triglyceride and glucose levels, has emerged as a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance. While TyG has been associated with blood pressure in non‑diabetic populations, its relationship with systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) among patients with established T2DM remains less clearly defined. Methods A cross‑sectional study was conducted among 219 patients with T2DM (149 [68.0%] males, 70 [32.0%] females) attending a tertiary care hospital in Kerala, India. Of these, 109 (49.8%) had good glycemic control and 110 (50.2%) had poor glycemic control. Demographic, anthropometric, and biochemical data were collected using standardized procedures. SBP and DBP were measured using a standardized protocol. The TyG index was derived from fasting triglyceride and glucose values. Pearson's correlation and multiple linear regression analyses (adjusted for age, gender, and BMI) were performed to examine associations between TyG and blood pressure components. Results A total of 219 patients with T2DM (149 [68.0%] males, 70 [32.0%] females) were included, of whom 109 (49.8%) had good glycemic control and 110 (50.2%) had poor glycemic control. The mean SBP was 140.0 ± 18.0 mmHg, and the mean DBP was 97.1 ± 11.4 mmHg. The mean TyG index was 10.10 ± 0.44. Pearson's correlation analysis demonstrated a weak but statistically significant positive association between TyG and DBP (r = 0.149, p = 0.027), while no significant correlation was observed with SBP (r = 0.035, p = 0.612). In regression analysis adjusted for age, gender, and BMI, TyG remained independently associated with DBP (B = 3.52, p = 0.047) but not with SBP. Conclusion In patients with T2DM, the TyG index demonstrated a weak but significant association with diastolic blood pressure, whereas no relationship was observed with SBP. These findings suggest that TyG may provide complementary insights into the metabolic determinants of diastolic hypertension. However, given the modest strength of association and low explanatory power, larger prospective studies are required to validate its predictive utility.

Title: Association between Cardiovascular Health by Life's Essential 8 and Subsequent Coronary Artery Calcium Score: The Cardiovascular and Metabolic Diseases Etiology Research Center Cohort.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although "Life's Essential 8" (LE8) is a key metric for cardiovascular health (CVH), its longitudinal association with subclinical atherosclerosis in Koreans remains unclear. We examined the association between baseline LE8 scores and the presence of coronary artery calcium (CAC).
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Cardiovascular and Metabolic Diseases Etiology Research Center cohort study, a prospective cohort (baseline: 2013-2018; follow-up: 2022-2024). Baseline CVH scores, comprising 8 metrics (diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, sleep health, body mass index, blood lipids, blood glucose, and blood pressure), were categorized as low (0-<50), moderate (50-<80), and high (80-100). The main outcome was the presence of CAC at the follow-up. Multivariable logistic regression was used for statistical analysis.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 7.3 years, among 1,746 participants (mean age: 52.3 years, 65.2% female), the overall prevalence of CAC was 41.4%, which decreased with increasing CVH scores (low: 64.6%, moderate: 41.5%, and high: 30.4%). Compared to the low CVH group, the fully adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for the presence of CAC were 0.34 (0.23-0.51) in the moderate and 0.25 (0.15-0.39) in the high CVH group. Higher baseline CVH scores were log-linearly associated with lower odds of CAC presence, demonstrating a linear and dose-dependent relationship in the restricted cubic spline plot (p = 0.102). The association between CVH and CAC was consistently observed across subgroups and sensitivity analyses.
CONCLUSION: Our study showed that higher baseline CVH scores were associated with a lower risk of subsequent CAC, highlighting the importance of promoting ideal CVH early to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease.

Title: Comparison of Primary Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection versus Primary Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Barrett's Esophageal Neoplasia Treatment.
Abstract: Background Endoscopic resection of Barrett's esophageal neoplasia is commonly performed using either endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) or endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). While submucosal dissection enables en bloc resection, institutional approaches vary. We compared clinical, histopathologic, and oncologic outcomes between a primary submucosal dissection strategy and a mucosal resection-based strategy with selective use of submucosal dissection. Methods This retrospective cohort study included all patients with Barrett's esophageal neoplasia treated at two European tertiary referral centers. At Karolinska University Hospital, the primary submucosal dissection strategy was adopted, whereas at Erasmus Medical Center the mucosal resection-based strategy was employed. Patients with prior endoscopic therapy or hematologic disorders were excluded.
