Primary outcomes were local recurrence, synchronous and metachronous lesions prior to ablation, and cancer- or treatment-related mortality. Secondary outcomes included resection quality, adverse events, and the need for repeated resections. Time-to-event analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models. Results A total of 332 patients were included (132 in the primary submucosal dissection group and 200 in the mucosal resection-based group). En bloc resection was more frequent with the primary submucosal dissection strategy (98.5% vs 40.0%, p < 0.001). Compared with the EMR-based strategy, the pESD strategy was associated with significantly lower local recurrence (3.0% vs 10.0%, p = 0.02) and fewer resection sessions per patient, whereas rates of synchronous and metachronous lesions were similar between groups. Adverse events and cancer- or treatment-related mortality did not differ between strategies. Conclusions Both strategies are safe. However, the primary submucosal dissection strategy is associated with lower local recurrence and fewer resection sessions.

Title: Vibroacoustic lung therapy and early postoperative oxygenation after cardiac surgery: a multicentre prospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative respiratory dysfunction remains a clinically significant problem after cardiac surgery. However, clinical evidence on vibroacoustic pulmonary therapy in adult cardiac surgery patients remains limited. The study aimed to compare early postoperative oxygenation following vibroacoustic pulmonary therapy using VibroLUNG with routine manual chest physiotherapy after cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, observational, non-randomized comparative study included adult patients aged 18-80 years who underwent elective cardiac surgery and developed postoperative respiratory dysfunction meeting the study eligibility criteria. Group allocation reflected routine clinical practice and device availability at the participating centers. Patients received either vibroacoustic pulmonary therapy using VibroLUNG or routine manual percussion chest physiotherapy. The principal respiratory outcome analysed in this manuscript was the P/F ratio at the early postoperative assessment. Key secondary outcomes included FiO₂ requirement, SpO₂, PaO₂, PaCO₂, acid-base status parameters, clinical scales, radiographic findings, length of stay, and recorded safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 354 screened patients, 317 were included in the analysis: 156 in the VibroLUNG group and 161 in the control group. Baseline anthropometric characteristics were comparable; however, the distribution by center/region differed substantially between the groups. At the early postoperative assessment, the VibroLUNG group had a lower administered FiO₂ [35.0% [30.0-41.0] vs. 41.5% [40.0-50.0], p < 0.001]. In the principal centre-adjusted analysis, the P/F ratio was higher in the VibroLUNG group by 23.8 units (95% CI 8.1-39.5; p=0.003). Before extubation, FiO₂ remained lower in the VibroLUNG group [30.0% [30.0-35.0] vs. 35.0% [30.0-50.0], p < 0.001], whereas the unadjusted difference in the P/F ratio was not statistically significant. No device-related adverse events, device deficiencies, or deaths during study participation were recorded.
CONCLUSION: VibroLUNG use was associated with a higher early postoperative P/F ratio and lower administered FiO₂. No adverse events, device deficiencies, or deaths were recorded during the study observation period. Causal inference is limited by the non-randomized design and centre-level differences.

Title: Characteristics of Youth With Type 2 Diabetes Prescribed Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors Surrounding FDA Approval at an Academic Pediatric Medical Center.
Journal: The journal of pediatric pharmacology and therapeutics : JPPT : the official journal of PPAG
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) were approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in children aged 10 years and older on June 20, 2023. We describe SGLT2i prescribing trends among all specialties at a quaternary care pediatric medical center surrounding the approval of empagliflozin, then identify characteristics of patients with T2DM associated with a higher likelihood of SGLT2i prescription by pediatric endocrinologists.
METHODS: We compared the total number of new SGLT2i prescriptions sent by all specialties before and after FDA approval of empagliflozin, between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2024. We then identified children aged 10 years and older with T2DM who were newly prescribed an SGLT2i by pediatric endocrinologists. Demographic and clinical characteristics were compared with those of children with T2DM not prescribed SGLT2i.
RESULTS: The number of SGLT2i prescriptions sent by pediatric endocrinologists increased, and the top prescribing specialty shifted from Cardiology to Endocrinology. Increasing glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was associated with higher odds of SGLT2i prescription (OR 1.2 [95% CI, 1.1-1.3]; p < 0.001) regardless of empagliflozin approval status, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, or urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio. Those prescribed SGLT2i before FDA approval were older, male, more frequently on insulin, and less frequently on metformin. These differences between groups were not seen post-approval.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2is were more likely to be prescribed for youth with higher HBA1c by pediatric endocrinologists. The presence of risk factors for cardiovascular or renal disease was less important in the decision to prescribe SGLT2i, despite their reno- and cardioprotective effects in adults. Prospective and qualitative data would be useful in further understanding prescribing practices.

Title: Comparison of the approaches to combine Renal Replacement Therapy with Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation - a Scoping Review.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used for cardiac and respiratory failure and is associated with high rates of acute kidney injury (AKI) and fluid overload requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). ECMO and RRT can be run independently in parallel, or RRT hemofilter or device can be integrated into the ECMO circuit. Several parallel and integrated ECMO-RRT configurations have been described, but the optimal approach remains uncertain.This scoping review mapped the available literature comparing at least two ECMO-RRT configurations, summarized reported outcomes, and identified knowledge gaps.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov without restrictions, with the final search conducted on February 9, 2026. Eligible studies compared at least 2 ECMO-RRT configurations linked to reported outcomes. Data on study characteristics, configurations, outcomes, and anticoagulation were extracted and synthesized.
RESULTS: Of 6,806 records, 20 studies were included: 12 were clinical including 1 randomized controlled trial, 3 in vitro, 1 in silico, and 4 surveys. More than 8 ECMO-RRT connection schemes have been described by clinical studies since 2013. No consistent differences in efficiency or clinical outcomes were observed between the configurations compared. Integrated methods were associated with longer or comparable hemofilter lifespan. Surveys confirmed heterogeneous medical practices, and 2 safety concerns (unstoppable pressure alarms and air embolism) were reported.
CONCLUSION: Evidence on ECMO-RRT configurations is limited and heterogeneous. Future systematic and rigorous comparison of all the configurations through preclinical and clinical studies is needed to harmonize medical practices and inform the development of guidelines.

Title: Right ventricular remodeling after veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation bridge to lung transplantation in adults with severe lung disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a common complication of advanced lung disease, yet data on RV remodeling and long-term outcomes following veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) as a bridge to lung transplantation remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult patients bridged to lung transplant on VV-ECMO from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2022. Transthoracic echocardiograms were analyzed pre-transplant (on VV-ECMO) and post-transplant in the "early" ( ≤ 3 months) and "late" (3-12 months) phases. Within-patient changes in echocardiographic parameters were assessed using paired nonparametric tests. The association between pre-transplant RV systolic function, quantified by RV fractional area of change (RVFAC), and 3-year post-transplant survival was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards modeling.
RESULTS: Twenty patients were included (65.0% male, median age 47.5 [IQR: 41.5-56.4]) with primary etiologies of interstitial lung disease (50.0%) and COVID-19 (30.0%). In the "early" post-transplant phase, median RV systolic pressure decreased from 70.0 to 31.2 mm Hg (p < 0.001) and RVFAC increased from 25.9% to 31.9% (p = 0.004), whereas tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion decreased from 15.0 to 10.3 mm (p < 0.001). RV and right atrial dilation improved, while RV free-wall thickness remained unchanged (5.4-5.8 mm, p = 0.601). Among patients with greater baseline RV dysfunction, substantial functional and structural recovery was observed at 1-year. Three-year survival was 85.0% and preoperative RV dysfunction was not associated with mortality (HR: 0.96 [95% CI: 0.14-6.87]).
CONCLUSIONS: Meaningful RV recovery and favorable 3-year survival appear achievable after VV-ECMO bridge to transplantation, even among patients with moderate-to-severe pre-transplant RV dysfunction.

Title: Coronary artery calcium burden and metabolic indices in relation to arteriovenous fistula functionality and post-functionality failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred haemodialysis access, but functionality failure and subsequent post-functionality AVF failure remain common. Whether coronary artery calcium (CAC), a marker of systemic vascular calcification, is associated with either outcome is unclear; competing events are frequently ignored.
OBJECTIVE: To examine CAC and metabolic markers in relation to AVF functionality and post-functionality AVF failure.
METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 645 patients with end-stage kidney disease underwent first-time radiocephalic AVF creation. The primary outcome was functionality failure (n = 139 events; assisted functionality or abandonment before cannulation), with unassisted functionality, death and transplantation as competing events. A secondary outcome was post-functionality AVF failure among 568 fistulas that achieved successful functionality, with death and transplantation as competing events. Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were fitted after multiple imputation (n = 20).
RESULTS: Independent predictors of functionality failure were age (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-1.93, P < 0.001 per 1 standard deviation [SD]), CAC score (SHR 1.21, 95% CI 1.06-1.38, P = 0.004 per 1 SD) and left ventricular diastolic dysfunction (SHR 1.44, 95% CI 1.02-2.04, P = 0.040). Categorically, CAC 1-100 and >100 vs. 0 yielded SHRs of 5.38 (95% CI 3.02-9.58) and 6.61 (95% CI 3.57-12.22), respectively, both P < 0.001. For post-functionality AVF failure, assisted functionality (SHR 1.68, 95% CI 1.25-2.25, P < 0.001), diabetes (SHR 1.42, 95% CI 1.07-1.89, P = 0.015), serum albumin (SHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.56-0.88, P = 0.002 per 1 SD) and C-reactive protein (SHR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.97, P = 0.022 per 1 SD) were independently associated. The C-index was 0.746 (95% CI 0.70-0.79) at 180 days for the primary outcome and 0.677 (95% CI 0.632-0.725) at 2 years for the secondary outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: Older age and higher CAC burden are independently associated with AVF functionality failure, whereas the strongest determinant of subsequent patency loss is the need for assisted functionality. Preoperative static markers discriminate moderately; postoperative haemodynamic parameters are likely required for individual risk prediction.

Title: Physical activity and improvement of physiological parameters by training.
Journal: Frontiers in sports and active living
Abstract: Living a better life greatly depends on maintaining healthy physiological parameters, including cardiovascular fitness, a well-balanced neuro-immuno-endocrine axis, and cognitive function-all of which contribute to focus, sharp memory, and self-esteem while mitigating age-related cognitive decline. Physical activity (high, moderate and resistance training, RT) is one of the most important lifestyle choices for reducing disease risk and improving overall health, particularly aerobic training, which increases maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max), a marker of cardiorespiratory fitness. Here, we focus on how exercise influences physiology that may contribute to improvements in health-related quality of life (QoL). Specifically, we discuss based on evidence from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and experimental animal models the neurobiological, endocrine, immune, metabolic, and cardiovascular adaptations induced by exercise, including changes in neurochemical signaling, trophic mediators, hormones, cytokines, and cardiorespiratory fitness. Specific nutrients as supplements (creatine, omega-3 fatty acids and some amino acids) and dietary patterns (mediterranean, ketogenic, intermittent fasting) are also discussed. It is never too late to start moving-regular physical activity has been shown to counteract several deleterious effects of a sedentary lifestyle by reducing systemic inflammation, attenuating age-related brain changes, and lowering the risk of neurodegenerative diseases.

Title: Treatment strategies for unilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma with ipsilateral cervical lymph node metastasis: a narrative review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Unilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) with ipsilateral cervical lymph-node metastasis carries intermediate-to-high recurrence risk. Although total thyroidectomy is conventionally recommended by multiple clinical guidelines, accumulating real‑world evidence has triggered ongoing debates regarding surgical extent, neck dissection scope, adjuvant radioactive iodine administration and molecular‑guided risk stratification. This narrative review intends to synthesize contemporary clinical evidence and provide references for individualized therapeutic decision‑making for this specific patient population.
METHODS: Literature was retrieved from PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science up to January 2026. English articles were screened by two reviewers through consensus. This is a narrative review without formal systematic-review procedures.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: For properly-selected patients, lobectomy provides similar oncological outcomes as total thyroidectomy with fewer complications. Unilateral central neck dissection plus selective lateral neck dissection balances tumour control and surgical morbidity. Aggressive pathological variants and concurrent B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase (BRAF) V600E/telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter dual mutations indicate elevated recurrence and mortality risk. Radioactive iodine (RAI) ablation ought to be determined by integrated risk assessment rather than routine application. Lymph‑node yield and lymph‑node ratio serve as key prognostic markers reflecting dissection quality and recurrence likelihood. Serum thyroglobulin, interfered by thyroglobulin antibodies, remains the core surveillance biomarker.
CONCLUSIONS: Risk‑stratified individualized management is strongly recommended for unilateral PTC patients with ipsilateral cervical lymph‑node metastasis. This review may facilitate clinical practice. Nevertheless, most available evidence comes from retrospective studies; further high‑quality prospective investigations are required to refine treatment strategies.

Title: Peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonists for recovery of bowel function after radical cystectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative ileus (POI) is common after radical cystectomy (RC) and contributes to prolonged hospital stay, increased healthcare costs, and reduced patient quality of life. Peripherally acting μ-opioid receptor antagonists (PAMORAs), including alvimopan, naloxegol, and methylnaltrexone, have been investigated as strategies to reduce POI while preserving opioid-mediated analgesia. Previous systematic reviews have shown benefit of PAMORAs, particularly alvimopan, in abdominal procedures such as bowel resection and hysterectomy, but evidence specific to RC remains heterogeneous and limited. We aimed to evaluate whether incorporation of PAMORAs (alvimopan, naloxegol, or methylnaltrexone) into enhanced recovery pathways reduces POI compared with enhanced recovery pathways alone in patients undergoing RC.
METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) was conducted to identify studies evaluating PAMORAs for prevention of POI following RC. Search terms included alvimopan, naloxegol, methylnaltrexone, and RC. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized trials, and observational studies comparing PAMORAs with placebo or standard care. Two independent reviewers extracted data using Covidence software. Outcomes included time to gastrointestinal recovery, time to first flatus, time to first bowel movement, length of stay (LOS), POI incidence, adverse events (including cardiovascular events), and costs. Results were summarized in a Summary of Findings table.
RESULTS: Across included studies, PAMORAs were associated with improved postoperative gastrointestinal recovery, although certainty of evidence varied. PAMORAs shortened time to first flatus by approximately 1 day [mean difference (MD) =-0.97 days; 95% confidence interval (CI): -1.07 to -0.87] across six observational studies with no detectable heterogeneity (I2=0%), but certainty of evidence was very low due to non-randomized designs and risk of bias. Time to first bowel movement was reduced by approximately 1.3 days (MD =-1.30 days; 95% CI: -1.81 to -0.79) across nine studies, although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2=84%).
CONCLUSIONS: PAMORAs appear to improve postoperative gastrointestinal recovery following RC. However, overall certainty of evidence remains low due to reliance on non-randomized studies and heterogeneity. Alvimopan has the strongest supporting evidence, while data for naloxegol and methylnaltrexone remain limited.

Title: Peri-areolar dermal reinforcement to prevent prosthetic-related complications in prepectoral reconstruction with a compromised nipple-areola complex: a surgical technique.
Abstract: In prepectoral direct-to-implant (DTI) breast reconstruction following nipple-sparing mastectomy (NSM) via a hemi-periareolar incision, intraoperative ischemia of the nipple-areola complex (NAC) presents a critical challenge. Existing salvage procedures often require secondary interventions or NAC sacrifice, while leaving a vulnerable suture line resting directly over the implant-acellular dermal matrix (ADM) construct. To address this, we modified a de-epithelialized dermal flap technique, executed directly through the pre-existing incision, to interpose a protective biological barrier beneath the NAC base. This technique was applied in three female patients (aged 43 to 50 years) with breast cancer undergoing unilateral NSM and immediate prepectoral DTI reconstruction with ADM-wrapped implants. Following mastectomy and prior to implant placement, compromised NAC perfusion was recognized by dusky skin discoloration, qualitative indocyanine green angiography demonstrating reduced fluorescence, a capillary refill time of approximately 2 seconds, and preserved dermal edge bleeding. The maneuver was initiated based on the operating surgeon's clinical judgment. A 5- to 10-mm crescent adjacent to the areolar margin was de-epithelialized-leaving a 2- to 3-mm dermal bed-onto which the NAC-bearing flap was advanced and inset. Over follow-up periods ranging from 12 to 48 months, all three patients achieved complete NAC viability without partial or full-thickness necrosis, wound dehiscence, infection, implant exposure, or reoperation. Transient superficial epidermolysis developed on postoperative day 2 but resolved completely by days 14 to 17 with routine local wound care, and nipple position symmetry showed improvement in all cases. This preliminary experience demonstrates that immediate crescent de-epithelialization is technically feasible and yields acceptable clinical outcomes in selected cases. By establishing a dermal safety buffer against implant exposure, this maneuver offers a practical intraoperative salvage strategy. However, three cases from a single center cannot establish overall efficacy or superiority over alternative salvage methods, and larger prospective studies with standardized outcome metrics are required.

Title: Exploratory analysis of serum FGF-21 and CK-18 as biomarkers for ultrasound-detected MASLD in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a UAE multicenter study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, particularly among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This exploratory multicenter study evaluated the association and diagnostic performance of the serum biomarkers cytokeratin 18 fragment M30 (CK-18 M30) and fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF-21) in T2DM patients with and without ultrasound-detected MASLD.
METHODS: A multicenter case-control observational study was conducted on a total of 125 T2DM patients in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Two groups of T2DM patients, MASLD and non-MASLD, were recruited for investigation of different serum biomarkers. An overnight fasting blood sample was collected for investigation of two biomarkers, including CK-18 M30 and FGF-21.
RESULTS: The study included 125 participants (mean age 55.9±8.9 years; 52.8% female). A subset of 66 participants was analyzed for serum biomarkers (FGF-21 and CK-18). Overall, 50.4% were obese (body mass index >30 kg/m2), and 97% had elevated waist circumference. Uncontrolled glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was more frequent in MASLD patients (58.1%) than in non-MASLD patients (35.9%; P=0.02). In the MASLD group, FGF-21 levels were positively correlated with alanine transaminase levels (P=0.04) and negatively correlated with CK-18 levels (P=0.047). Median FGF-21 levels were significantly higher in the MASLD group versus the non-MASLD group (P=0.03).
CONCLUSIONS: Dyslipidemia and uncontrolled HbA1c were significantly associated with MASLD in T2DM patients. FGF-21 levels were higher in MASLD patients; however, its diagnostic performance was modest, and it was not independently associated with MASLD after multivariate adjustment.

Title: Digital and algorithmic strategies for guideline-directed medical therapy initiation and up-titration in adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) reduces morbidity and mortality in heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet underuse and suboptimal up-titration remain common. Digital and algorithmic strategies are increasingly being used to address these gaps, but their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain.
METHODS: This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidance and was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251268580). PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through 26 December 2025. Randomized and comparative studies enrolling adults with HFrEF were eligible if they evaluated digital, algorithm-based, or telemonitoring strategies designed to facilitate GDMT initiation, titration, or optimization versus usual care.
RESULTS: Six randomized comparative trials involving 3706 participants were included. Interventions comprised provider-facing electronic health record alerts and digitally enabled remote titration or telemonitoring pathways. Five of the six trials showed improvements in medication-optimization outcomes; the single neutral trial was a provider-facing alert intervention that showed no difference in GDMT prescribing at hospital discharge. Remote pathway-based strategies demonstrated the largest effects, including higher titration completion (82.1% vs 53.8% at 6 months; an absolute difference of approximately 28 percentage points) and greater improvements in therapy scores. Alert-based interventions showed mixed findings, including no difference in overall GDMT class prescribing at discharge in one inpatient trial (34% vs 34%). Meta-analysis was not performed because of substantial heterogeneity in interventions, outcomes, and reporting formats.
CONCLUSION: Digital strategies appear to improve GDMT optimization in HFrEF, particularly when embedded within structured care pathways that enable repeated reassessment and protocol-driven titration. Passive alerts alone appear less effective. Standardized outcome measures and trials evaluating clinical endpoints are needed.

Title: Prognostic impact of long-term beta-blockers post-stemi: a meta-analytic review.
Abstract:
AIMS: This meta-analysis assessed the long-term impact of beta-blocker therapy on all-cause mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) who continued beta-blocker use for a minimum of 1 year after hospital discharge.
METHODS: Electronic databases were searched through September 2024 to identify studies comparing long-term outcomes in patients treated with beta-blockers versus those untreated. A random-effects model was used to estimate Hazard Ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: A total of 21 studies involving 270 566 patients were included. In pooled analyses, extended beta-blocker was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality in STEMI patients [HR: 0.74 (0.66, 0.83); P < 0.0001] and showing non-significant trend toward reducing cardiac death [HR: 0.77 (0.56, 1.04); P = 0.09], an effect observed predominantly in observational studies. However, in randomized controlled trials (N = 3), no significant benefit was demonstrated (all-cause mortality: P = 0.67; cardiac death: P = 0.62). No meaningful differences were found for major adverse cardiovascular events [HR: 0.90 (0.76, 1.07); P = 0.22], myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, or revascularization.
CONCLUSION: Long-term beta-blocker use is associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality among STEMI patients, though this benefit was not seen in RCTs. Effects on other cardiovascular outcomes remain uncertain, highlighting the need for further large-scale trials.

Title: Membrane anatomy-guided robot-assisted partial nephrectomy: operational definition and association with warm ischemia time in a single-surgeon cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: A standardized anatomical framework for robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) is lacking. This study evaluates a stepwise membrane anatomy-guided pathway and its association with warm ischemia time (WIT) and clamping-phase efficiency, controlling for surgical experience and temporal confounding.
METHODS: We evaluated 151 consecutive RAPN cases (30 conventional vs. 121 membrane anatomy-guided) performed by a single-center, single-surgeon cohort using the da Vinci Xi System (2022-2025). Multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors was performed to assess the primary outcome (WIT), adjusting for clinical covariates and nonlinear cumulative case sequence (natural cubic spline, df = 3). Chronology-adjusted sensitivity analyses and propensity-score overlap weighting were conducted.
RESULTS: Despite substantial chronological overlap between pathways, the membrane-guided pathway was independently associated with a 4.05-min reduction in mean WIT (95% CI -6.82 to -1.28; P = 0.004) without compromising surgical margin safety. This effect was consistent across linear, calendar-time, propensity-weighted, and overlap-cohort sensitivity analyses (-3.67 to -4.19 min; all P < 0.05). The membrane-guided approach also significantly increased the odds of WIT ≤ 25 min (adjusted OR 5.25; P = 0.003) and modified Trifecta achievement (adjusted OR 4.97; P = 0.005).
CONCLUSION: The membrane anatomy-guided pathway consistently improves clamping-phase efficiency and shortens WIT in RAPN after accounting for learning curves and temporal trends. Given the retrospective design, these findings reflect associative rather than definitive causal effects.

Title: Therapeutic efficacy and safety of newly approved FDA drug levoketoconazole in cushing syndrome: a systematic review.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cushing syndrome is a severe endocrinopathy due to chronic hypercortisolism with etiology that includes the administration of exogenous glucocorticoids, pituitary adenomas, ectopic ACTH-producing tumors, and adrenal tumors. Expressed as central obesity, hypertension, glucose intolerance, and psychiatric symptoms, it greatly affects the QoL and has a high association with morbidity and mortality.
AIM: This systematic review summarizes data from clinical trials to compare the effectiveness and safety of a newly approved drug, levoketoconazole, for the treatment of Cushing syndrome.
METHODOLOGY: An extensive search was conducted in PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library for terms related to the effectiveness and safety of levoketoconazole in Cushing syndrome. Selected studies included phase 2 and phase 3 interventional trials enrolling adult patients (≥18 years) with confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome (ECS). Outcomes of interest included mean urinary free cortisol (mUFC), clinical signs and symptoms, quality of life measures, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration Risk of Bias Tool.
RESULTS: Six interventional studies were included. In the SONICS phase 3 trial, 62% of patients achieved normalization of mUFC at the end of the 6-month maintenance phase, with sustained biochemical and clinical benefits during extended evaluation. During the randomized withdrawal phase of the LOGICS trial, loss of mUFC response occurred in 95.5% of patients switched to placebo compared with 40.5% of patients who continued levoketoconazole treatment (P = 0.0002), demonstrating maintenance of biochemical control with active therapy. Common adverse events included nausea, headache, hypokalemia, and fatigue. Serious drug-related adverse events were uncommon but clinically relevant, including hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation, and adrenal insufficiency.
CONCLUSION: Levoketoconazole significantly lowers cortisol levels and alleviates clinical manifestations in patients with Cushing syndrome with reasonable safety. There is a need to perform a periodic checkup of the liver function and adrenal insufficiency. Additional long-term research is needed to strengthen its place in treatment plans.

Title: Triple-Action Seroma Prevention Protocol in Subcutaneous Onlay Endoscopic Repair.
Journal: JSLS : Journal of the Society of Laparoendoscopic Surgeons
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Postoperative seroma is a common surgical site occurrence following procedures that create large subcutaneous dead spaces. This case series describes a triple-action seroma prevention protocol used during subcutaneous onlay endoscopic repair and reports early postoperative outcomes.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 36 consecutive adults who underwent modified subcutaneous onlay laparoscopic abdominal wall reconstruction for rectus diastasis and midline hernias, with or without postoperative incisional hernia, between March 2024 and December 2025. The protocol combined progressive-tension quilting sutures, irrigation with 20 mL of 12% hypertonic saline retained for 10 minutes, and fibrin sealant application. Closed-suction drains and an abdominal binder were used routinely.
RESULTS: Seroma was recorded in 2 of 36 patients (5.6%). Among 15 patients with postoperative incisional hernia and rectus diastasis, seroma occurred in 1 patient (6.7%). Both affected patients were men with obesity and dense subcutaneous fibrosis. Drain output decreased to approximately 20 mL within 10 hours, and drains were removed on postoperative day 1 in all but 1 patient. No infection, mesh infection, skin necrosis, flap ischemia, hypernatremia, or fibrin sealant-related anaphylaxis was recorded. One additional small fluid collection detected at 6 weeks was managed conservatively.
CONCLUSION: In this descriptive series of subcutaneous onlay endoscopic repair, the triple-action seroma Prevention protocol was associated with a low observed seroma rate and early drain removal. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger prospective controlled studies.

Title: Precision surgical oncology for hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a heterogeneous tumor-liver-host disease in which treatment selection depends on tumor burden, liver function, portal hypertension, performance status, and patient preferences. Although hepatic resection and other established treatment modalities remain central to curative and disease-controlling strategies, emerging biological and digital technologies may provide additional information beyond conventional clinical assessment. However, their prognostic performance does not necessarily establish clinical utility, and many remain insufficiently validated for routine treatment selection. This narrative review examines the evolving role of precision-oriented approaches in HCC, including molecular and immune profiling, radiomics, circulating tumor DNA, artificial intelligence, and digital pathology. We classify these approaches into three evidence tiers: established clinical practice, investigational clinical tools, and future hypotheses. We then propose Precision Surgical Oncology as an author-developed, hypothesis-generating framework in which guideline-based assessment is followed by biological and host-risk refinement, multidisciplinary interpretation, individualized treatment within established therapeutic pathways, and longitudinal reassessment. Precision Surgical Oncology is intended to complement, rather than replace, evidence-based HCC management. Its future clinical value will depend on prospective validation, reproducibility, defined clinical actionability, equitable implementation, and demonstration of improved patient outcomes.

Title: Association of the triglyceride-glucose index and triglyceride-glucose-body mass index with postoperative atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is a common complication following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG). Insulin resistance (IR) contributes to the pathogenesis of POAF. IR-related markers, including the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the triglyceride-glucose-body mass index (TyG-BMI), have demonstrated prognostic value for cardiovascular events. However, their associations with POAF specifically after OPCABG remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of TyG and TyG-BMI with POAF and their incremental value beyond conventional clinical risk factors.
METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adult patients who underwent isolated OPCABG between December 2020 and December 2021. Of 757 otherwise eligible patients, 93 without the preoperative fasting glucose and/or triglyceride measurements required to calculate the indices were excluded, leaving 664 participants in the primary analysis. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), discrimination and reclassification analyses, and bootstrap internal validation were performed.
RESULTS: Of the 664 participants, 180 (27.1%) developed POAF. In the fully adjusted model, each standard deviation increase in TyG and TyG-BMI was associated with higher odds of POAF [TyG: odds ratio (OR), 1.55; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.28-1.89; TyG-BMI: OR, 1.60; 95% CI: 1.31-1.96; both P<0.001]. RCS analysis showed an approximately linear association for TyG (P for nonlinearity =0.16) and a nonlinear association for TyG-BMI (P for nonlinearity =0.02). Adding TyG or TyG-BMI to the baseline model increased the C-statistic from 0.682 to 0.708 or 0.707, respectively, although the changes were not statistically significant (P=0.07 and P=0.08). Both indices improved the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI) (all P<0.001). Associations were stronger among patients with diabetes (P for interaction =0.02 for TyG and 0.005 for TyG-BMI).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative TyG and TyG-BMI values were independently associated with POAF after OPCABG. These routinely available indices provided modest incremental risk information beyond conventional clinical risk factors. External validation is required before their use for clinical decision-making.

Title: Does thermal ablation plus chemotherapy improve survival in small-cell lung cancer ineligible for surgery?
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thermal ablation (TA) is a safe and feasible alternative for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer. However, data on the clinical efficacy of TA in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) are scarce. This study aimed to explore the clinical efficacy of TA plus chemotherapy (CHT) in treating SCLC.
METHODS: This is a population-based retrospective cohort study based on the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database. We collected data from the SEER database for 51,273 SCLC patients who received CHT from 2000 to 2019. Using propensity score matching (PSM), we balanced covariate differences between two treatment groups: CHT alone and TA plus CHT. Kaplan-Meier survival curves for overall survival (OS) and lung cancer-specific survival (LCSS) were generated. Cox regression analysis was conducted to assess independent prognostic indicators.
RESULTS: After PSM, the TA + CHT group exhibited superior OS and LCSS compared to the CHT-only group. Age subgroup analysis revealed that for patients aged ≥70 years, TA + CHT resulted in improved OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone. For patients <70 years, a survival benefit was observed, but the difference was not statistically significant. Tumor size subgroup analysis showed that for patients with tumor sizes of 0-3 cm, TA + CHT led to superior OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone, while no statistically significant differences were observed in other tumor size subgroups. N stage subgroup analysis indicated that for N0 and N1 patients, TA + CHT had better OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone, with no statistically significant differences in the N2 and N3 subgroups. Multivariable analysis indicated that TA + CHT was an independent favorable prognostic indicator for both OS and LCSS.
CONCLUSIONS: TA + CHT may be a promising treatment option for patients with SCLC, especially those aged ≥70 years with tumor size ≤3 cm, and N0-1 disease.

Title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics in small cell lung cancer: a narrative review of imaging and multisource data integration.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics are increasingly used to analyze imaging and multisource data in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the directness and clinical maturity of the available evidence remain uncertain. This narrative review aimed to summarize and critically evaluate SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, and indirect evidence across diagnostic classification, prognostic prediction, treatment-associated outcomes, and lesion segmentation.
METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted to identify human studies evaluating AI, deep learning (DL), radiomics, or machine learning within imaging-based or imaging-integrated workflows. Studies were selected according to clinical relevance, directness of SCLC evidence, methodological strength, and reporting completeness, and were classified as SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, or indirect/transferable evidence.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Direct SCLC-specific evidence was strongest for multicenter computed tomography (CT)-based prognostic models and lesion segmentation, whereas diagnostic classification relied mainly on mixed cohorts or public image-level datasets. Treatment-response models showed preliminary value but were predominantly retrospective and lacked prospective clinical validation. Retrospective studies suggested associations between model-derived risk scores and outcomes following prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI), but did not establish treatment-benefit prediction. Pathomic and radiogenomic analyses also identified associations between quantitative features, immune-cell infiltration, genomic alterations, and treatment response; these findings remain hypothesis-generating. Interpretation is limited by small SCLC cohorts, retrospective single-center designs, non-independent image-level analyses, and limited external validation and interpretability.
CONCLUSIONS: AI and radiomics show potential in SCLC, particularly for CT-based prognosis and segmentation. However, treatment-response prediction, non-invasive subtype classification, and clinical decision support remain investigational and require prospective multicenter validation and patient-level external evaluation before clinical implementation.

Title: Factors associated with 30-day mortality in patients with post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal rupture: a retrospective cohort study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal rupture (VSR) is associated with high mortality, and comparative outcome data across contemporary treatment strategies remain limited. We aimed to identify factors associated with 30-day mortality, compare observed outcomes across four treatment strategies, including surgical repair combining an occluder and a patch (SurCOP), and develop an internally validated multivariable model incorporating the treatment ultimately received for retrospective prognostic assessment.
METHODS: Between May 2012 and October 2025, 214 patients with post-myocardial infarction VSR were included and classified according to 30-day survival status. Baseline characteristics, clinical presentations, and treatment strategies, including conservative medical therapy, transcatheter closure, traditional surgical repair, and SurCOP, were compared. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with 30-day mortality. The prognostic model was developed in a 187-patient complete-case cohort defined before variable selection. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and internal validation was performed using stratified 10-fold cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction with 500 resamples.
RESULTS: Among the 214 enrolled patients with VSR, the overall 30-day mortality rate was 51.9%. Notably, observed 30-day mortality was lowest in the SurCOP group (21.8%), although treatment-group comparisons should be interpreted in light of non-random treatment allocation. Among the 123 patients who underwent a definitive invasive intervention, the median interval from VSR diagnosis to treatment differed among the SurCOP, traditional surgical repair, and transcatheter closure groups (6.5, 31.4, and 17.8 days, respectively; P<0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that conservative medical therapy was associated with a higher odds of mortality compared to the SurCOP technique [odds ratio (OR), 27.822]. Additionally, elevated admission creatinine (OR, 1.010) and lactate (OR, 1.337) were independently associated with higher 30-day mortality. Conversely, a history of angina pectoris or myocardial infarction (OR, 0.235) was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality. A retrospective prognostic model incorporating the treatment ultimately received was subsequently constructed. The model demonstrated good discriminatory performance, with an apparent area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.906 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.863-0.948], a sensitivity of 0.768, and a specificity of 0.943. Stratified 10-fold cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.825-0.925), and the bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.884.
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center cohort, treatment modality, admission creatinine, admission lactate, and a history of angina or myocardial infarction were associated with 30-day mortality. The combined model showed good apparent discrimination and retained acceptable discrimination after internal validation. Because treatment allocation was non-random and the model incorporated the treatment ultimately received, the findings should be interpreted as prognostic associations and require external validation before clinical application.

Title: Incidental pulmonary nodules detected on computed tomography pulmonary angiography: prevalence and malignancy outcomes from a Thai tertiary-care center.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is widely used for diagnosing pulmonary embolism (PE) and frequently reveals incidental pulmonary nodules. However, data regarding the prevalence and malignant outcomes of incidental pulmonary nodules, particularly among patients with PE, remain limited in Thailand. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of incidental pulmonary nodules detected on CTPA and to evaluate malignancy outcomes, particularly in patients with concurrent PE.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≥18 years who underwent CTPA at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital between January 2017 and December 2018. Patients with active lung cancer or known pulmonary metastases were excluded. Clinical characteristics, CTPA findings, and follow-up data were reviewed. Pulmonary nodules were followed until a definitive diagnosis was established, until May 2024, or for a minimum of 2 years in the absence of interval growth.
RESULTS: A total of 376 patients were included in the analysis. Incidental pulmonary nodules were identified in 129 patients (34.3%), while PE was diagnosed in 110 patients (29.3%). The prevalence of incidental pulmonary nodules did not differ significantly between the PE-positive and PE-negative groups (29.1% vs. 36.5%; P=0.17). Category-specific analyses demonstrated that patients with PE had a higher proportion of pulmonary nodules >8 mm (21.9% vs. 9.3%) and malignant outcomes (18.8% vs. 3.1%) than those without PE. Relative risks (RRs) with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) are reported in the Results section. Among the 9 patients ultimately diagnosed with malignancy, most received a definitive diagnosis within 6 months following CTPA.
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of incidental pulmonary nodules detected on CTPA were common and occurred more frequently than previously reported in several international studies. Patients with concurrent PE were more likely to have pulmonary nodules >8 mm and malignant outcomes than patients without PE. These findings suggest that incidental pulmonary nodules detected in patients with concomitant PE may identify a subgroup warranting careful clinical follow-up. Because of the retrospective design and limited number of malignant outcomes, larger prospective studies are required before changes to current surveillance strategies can be recommended.

Title: Treatment of idiopathic segmental infarction of the greater omentum in children via transumbilical single-port laparoscopy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic segmental infarction of the omentum represents a rare etiology of acute abdominal pain in pediatric patients. The atypical clinical presentation often leads to misdiagnosis and delayed intervention. This study aimed to summarize the treatment procedure of idiopathic segmental infarction of the omentum in children via transumbilical single-port laparoscopy and to offer a reference for clinical diagnosis and management of this condition.
METHODS: Clinical information, including blood tests, imaging examinations, intraoperative findings, postoperative pathological results, and follow-up outcomes, was collected from children with idiopathic segmental infarction of the omentum at our institution from September 2023 to September 2025, and a retrospective analysis was conducted.
RESULTS: There were 1 girl and 7 boys, whose ages ranged from 7 to 11 years, with an average of 9.1±1.2 years, and whose body mass index (BMI) ranged from 18.35 to 24.00 kg/m2, with an average of 21.95±2.11 kg/m2 among the 8 pediatric patients. The initial symptom was abdominal pain without any other accompanying symptoms. Ultrasound examinations revealed a hyperechoic abdominal mass in each patient without obvious blood flow signals, and computed tomography (CT) examinations revealed a mixed-density shadow mass in the abdomen without significant enhancement. Postoperative pathology confirmed infarction of the greater omentum, consistent with the preoperative diagnosis. All patients underwent transumbilical single-port laparoscopic surgery, with a hospital stay of 3-7 days and an average duration of 4.88±1.55 days. No complications, such as intestinal obstruction or incisional hernia, were observed during an average follow-up period of 21 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Transumbilical single-port laparoscopic surgery is safe, effective, and feasible for treating idiopathic segmental infarction of the omentum in children, and could serve as an alternative surgical approach for this condition.

Title: Risk factors for acute gastrointestinal injury after cardiac surgery in underweight children with congenital heart disease: a single-center retrospective study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute gastrointestinal injury (AGI) is an underrecognized complication after cardiac surgery in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), particularly in those with low body weight. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for postoperative AGI in underweight children (≤10 kg) undergoing CHD surgery.
METHODS: This single‑center retrospective study enrolled 386 underweight children who underwent CHD surgery between October 2021 and July 2022. Patients were divided into AGI and non‑AGI groups based on postoperative occurrence. Multivariate binary logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Of the 386 enrolled patients, 91 cases (23.6%) developed clinically significant postoperative AGI. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that the minimum intraoperative rectal temperature (P=0.002) was an independent risk factor. In addition, patients with AGI had significantly longer duration of mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay and longer overall hospital stay (all P<0.001). They also presented with higher transfusion requirements and a higher rate of extubation failure (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: The minimum intraoperative rectal temperature is an independent risk factor for AGI in underweight children with CHD. Early identification of this factor facilitates risk stratification and guides targeted perioperative gastrointestinal protection strategies, thereby improving therapeutic outcomes in this high‑risk population.

Title: The Innovex RS Delivery Catheter as a Single-Platform Endoscopic System for Upper Urinary Tract Intervention: A Two-Case Report of Upper Ureteral Lithotripsy and Ablation of a Suspected Renal Pelvis Urothelial Lesion.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional upper urinary tract endoscopy requires two instruments-a rigid ureteroscope for initial access and a flexible ureteroscope for intraluminal treatment-resulting in intraoperative scope exchange and dual-tower dependency. The Innovex RS delivery catheter is a rigid stainless-steel sheath that enables a single-use 7.5 Fr flexible ureteroscope to function in both rigid and flexible operative modes from one platform. To our knowledge this is the first report of a rigid-delivery sheath system used as the sole endoscopic instrument across two distinct upper urinary tract indications, and the first describing its use for ablation of a renal pelvis lesion.
CASES: Two patients underwent upper urinary tract endoscopy using the RS catheter as the sole instrument: a 53-year-old male with a 12 mm impacted proximal ureteral stone (holmium:YAG lithotripsy), and a 76-year-old female with a 10 mm renal pelvis filling defect, radiologically suspected to represent urothelial pathology on the basis of CT attenuation, who underwent cold-cup biopsy followed by thulium:YAG ablation. No rigid ureteroscope, tower switching, or fluoroscopic guidance was used in either case; this reflected operator judgement rather than any intrinsic capability of the device.
RESULTS: Stone-free status was confirmed by non-contrast computed tomography on postoperative day 1 in Case 1. Macroscopic complete ablation was achieved in Case 2. Histopathological examination of the biopsy specimen demonstrated inflammatory exudate with focal urothelial mucosa and mild epithelial atypia, without definitive invasive malignancy. The ablated lesion therefore remains a radiologically suspected but histopathologically unconfirmed urothelial neoplasm, and the patient has entered a structured surveillance programme. Operative times were 55 and 90 minutes respectively; in Case 2, approximately 60 of the 90 minutes were attributable to intrapelvic clot evacuation. Clavien-Dindo grades were 0 and I respectively.
CONCLUSION: The RS delivery catheter system enabled single-platform, single-tower ureteroscopy without scope exchange in two patients. These proof-of-concept observations establish technical feasibility only. They are not sufficient to demonstrate superiority, equivalent efficacy, improved safety, or cost-effectiveness relative to the conventional two-instrument workflow, and any such advantages remain hypotheses requiring prospective comparative evaluation.

Title: A predictive model for adverse events in left heart failure patients based on cardiopulmonary ultrasound parameters and clinical predictors.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left heart failure (LHF) is the most common in clinical setting and is more likely to experience adverse cardiovascular events. This study aims to establish a predictive nomogram of adverse events based on cardiopulmonary ultrasound (CPUS) parameters and clinical predictors for LHF patients. And the predictive performance of the nomogram was assessed.
METHODS: Potential risk factors associated with the occurrence of adverse events in LHF were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) or univariate logistic regression. A multivariate logistic regression model was subsequently constructed, and the results were visualized with a nomogram. Then the predictive ability and clinical application value of the nomogram were verified by the concordance index (C-index), calibration curve and decision curve.
RESULTS: A total of 329 heart failure patients including 278 males and 51 females, with an average age of (53.62±15.85) years were enrolled in this study. Independent influencing factors of adverse events were identified through multivariate logistic regression. Finally, four indicators were included, namely, systolic pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP) [odds ratio (OR) =15.53, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.53-157.19, P=0.02], left atrial transverse diameter (LAD) (OR =1.190, 95% CI: 1.031-1.373, P=0.02), E/e' ratio of left ventricle (LV-E/e') (OR =1.241, 95% CI: 1.101-1.399, P<0.001), and the number of B lines (OR =1.591, 95% CI: 1.123-2.254, P=0.009). The C-index of the nomogram model for predicting the risk of adverse events in LHF patients were 0.888 (95% CI: 0.826-0.950). Furthermore, the calibration curve demonstrated great consistency between the predicted probabilities and the observed outcomes, and the decision curve analysis confirmed the important clinical advantage of the model in LHF patients.
CONCLUSIONS: CPUS may provide valuable prognostic information in patients with LHF. The constructed prediction model for adverse events, incorporating CPUS parameters including sPAP, LAD, LV-E/e', and number of B lines, demonstrated favorable discriminative ability and accuracy within the study cohort.

Title: Remnant cholesterol and cardiovascular risk in maintenance haemodialysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remnant cholesterol (remnant-C) has emerged as a marker of residual cardiovascular risk beyond low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) but data in haemodialysis populations remain limited. We investigated the association of remnant-C with cardiovascular and mortality outcomes in maintenance haemodialysis patients.
METHODS: This post-hoc analysis included 624 patients from the prospective RISCAVID cohort. Remnant-C was calculated as total cholesterol minus high-density lipoprotein cholesterol minus directly measured LDL-C. The primary endpoint was 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal ischaemic stroke. All-cause mortality was analysed as a secondary endpoint. Associations were assessed using multivariable Cox regression models.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 31 months, 328 patients experienced a 3-point MACE and 375 died. Remnant-C was independently associated with 3-point MACE after adjustment for age, sex, traditional cardiovascular risk factors, LDL-C, and statin therapy (HR 1.06 per 10 mg/dl increase, 95% CI 1.01-1.11). The association remained significant after additional adjustment for the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and normalized protein catabolic rate. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a progressive increase in cardiovascular risk across increasing remnant-C concentrations without evidence of a nonlinear threshold effect. For all-cause mortality, neither remnant-C nor LDL-C retained prognostic significance after multivariable adjustment. Conversely, GNRI was independently associated with mortality risk, whereas it was not associated with cardiovascular events.
CONCLUSION: In maintenance haemodialysis patients, remnant-C was independently associated with major cardiovascular events but not with all-cause mortality, whereas the GNRI was associated with mortality but not cardiovascular outcomes. These findings suggest distinct contributions of residual atherogenic risk and nutritional status to cardiovascular and survival outcomes in end-stage kidney disease.

Title: Combined statin and fenofibrate therapy and cardiorenal outcomes in patients with CKD, dyslipidemia, and ischemic heart disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adults with non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease (CKD), ischemic heart disease (IHD), and hypertriglyceridemia are at high cardiorenal risk; whether starting fenofibrate together with statin therapy is effective and safe in this population is uncertain.
METHODS: In a multicenter retrospective cohort study emulating a target trial in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (2018-2024), 112 003 (28.5%) of 392 969 statin initiators with CKD and hypertriglyceridemia had IHD. Those without dialysis dependence were assigned to statin-fenofibrate combination therapy or statin monotherapy according to fenofibrate initiation within 3 months of the first statin prescription. The main outcomes were expanded major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) (acute myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, cardiac arrest, or all-cause death) and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) necessitating dialysis. Propensity score matching yielded 3191 pairs. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs).
RESULTS: Median follow-up was 881 days with combination therapy and 925 days with statin monotherapy. Combination therapy was associated with lower risks of MACE [1472 [46.1%] vs 1576 [49.4%] events; HR, 0.93; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.86-0.99] and ESKD necessitating dialysis (264 [8.3%] vs 335 [10.5%]; HR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67-0.92). Risks of all-cause mortality (377 vs. 375), acute myocardial infarction (537 vs. 570), heart failure (1059 vs. 1134), stroke (310 vs. 312), acute kidney injury (825 vs. 840), and coded safety events were not significantly different between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among selected adults with non-dialysis-dependent CKD, hypertriglyceridemia, and IHD, statin-fenofibrate combination therapy was associated with lower risks of MACE and of ESKD necessitating dialysis, without a significant increase in coded safety events.

Title: Overcoming Hyperkalaemia to Optimise Heart Failure Therapy: The Emerging Role of Novel Potassium Binders.
Abstract: Hyperkalaemia is common in patients with heart failure. It limits the initiation, optimisation and continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy, particularly mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. Two potassium binders, patiromer and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC), have emerged as strategies to address this barrier. SZC is an inorganic crystalline compound that binds potassium in exchange for sodium and hydrogen throughout the gastrointestinal tract, resulting in rapid potassium lowering, whereas patiromer is a non-absorbed organic polymer that exchanges potassium for calcium in the colon and has a slower onset of action. Both agents have demonstrated efficacy in maintaining normokalaemia and enabling the continuation of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitor therapy in heart failure. Differences in electrolyte effects and tolerability have clinical implications: patiromer is associated with hypomagnesaemia, while SZC delivers a sodium load that may predispose patients to fluid retention. However, no head-to-head randomised trials are available and evidence for improvement in heart failure morbidity or mortality remains limited, underscoring the need for adequately powered outcome studies.

Title: A blood test-derived skeletal muscle index combined with handgrip strength identifies a sarcopenia-related high-risk phenotype in non-dialysis-dependent chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is associated with adverse outcomes in CKD, but direct assessment of skeletal muscle mass is not always available. We examined whether serum creatinine- and cystatin C-derived estimated skeletal muscle index (SMI), combined with handgrip strength, identifies a sarcopenia-related high-risk phenotype in non-dialysis-dependent CKD.
METHODS: We derived a new equation for appendicular skeletal muscle mass using bioelectrical impedance analysis as the reference in 100 patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD. In an independent multicenter cohort of 1403 patients, SMI was estimated using this equation and a published creatinine-cystatin C-based formula. The sarcopenia-related high-risk phenotype was defined as low handgrip strength plus low estimated SMI using sex-specific cutoffs. Outcomes were all-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality.
RESULTS: During 5 years, 173 patients died, including 43 from cardiovascular causes. Low estimated SMI was identified in 218 patients (15.5%) with the published formula and 312 (22.2%) with the new equation; the corresponding phenotype prevalences were 11.9% and 11.7%. The phenotype was independently associated with all-cause mortality using either formula: adjusted hazard ratios were 1.54 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.07-2.21] for the published formula and 2.14 (95% CI, 1.52-3.00) for the new equation. Four-category and sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings.
CONCLUSIONS: Combining handgrip strength with creatinine- and cystatin C-derived estimated SMI identifies a sarcopenia-related high-risk phenotype and stratifies mortality risk in non-dialysis-dependent CKD. This approach may support screening when direct muscle mass assessment is unavailable but requires further validation before use as a diagnostic substitute.

Title: Restrictive vs. liberal blood transfusion strategies in Africa: clinical outcomes, resource stewardship, and future directions.
Abstract: Blood transfusion continues to be a vital part of contemporary healthcare, especially in treating severe anemia, bleeding, trauma, obstetric crises, and critical conditions. In Africa, where transfusion-dependent conditions are prevalent and blood supplies often limited, establishing the best transfusion threshold is crucial for enhancing patient outcomes while maximizing the use of scarce resources. Restrictive transfusion practices that typically use lower hemoglobin thresholds (7-8 g/dL) are now widely accepted globally as they minimize unnecessary transfusions while maintaining safety across various clinical environments. In contrast, liberal approaches, defined by elevated transfusion thresholds (9-10 g/dL), might still be suitable for specific patient groups, such as individuals with acute coronary syndromes, persistent significant bleeding, or serious symptomatic anemia. This review analyzes the existing evidence regarding restrictive vs. liberal blood transfusion strategies in the African context, focusing on clinical outcomes, resource management in healthcare, and prospective avenues for practice and investigation. Research from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and global guidelines consistently shows that restrictive transfusion strategies correlate with similar mortality, morbidity, hospital stay duration, and functional recovery in most stable hospitalized patients, while minimizing transfusion-related complications and preserving limited blood resources. Nevertheless, the direct relevance of evidence produced mainly in high-income countries needs thorough evaluation due to Africa's distinct epidemiological characteristics, healthcare system constraints, and blood service deficiencies. Enhancing patient blood management initiatives, increasing voluntary blood donations, improving transfusion oversight, and producing robust African clinical evidence are essential priorities.

Title: Heart failure in Somalia: a scoping review of the epidemiology, etiology, clinical characteristics, management, outcomes, and evidence gaps.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure is an important cause of morbidity, hospitalisation, disability, and mortality, but evidence from Somalia remains fragmented and largely confined to individual hospital-based studies. This scoping review mapped the available evidence on the epidemiology, aetiologies, clinical and diagnostic characteristics, management, outcomes, and research gaps relating to heart failure in Somalia.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to 27 July 2026. Backward citation searching was conducted on 3 August 2026. Original studies reporting heart-failure-specific findings from Somalia, including Somaliland and Puntland, were eligible. Screening was conducted independently by two reviewers. Data were charted using a structured form and verified by a second reviewer. Findings were synthesised descriptively without meta-analysis because of substantial heterogeneity and possible participant overlap.
RESULTS: The searches identified 111 records, of which 56 were duplicates. Fifty-five records underwent title and abstract screening, 13 reports were assessed in full text, and 12 studies published between 2011 and 2025 were included. Eleven studies were associated with a single tertiary hospital in Mogadishu, and no study provided nationally representative or multicentre evidence. Reported aetiologies and associated conditions included hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, anaemia, thyroid dysfunction, renal disease, and thiamine-deficiency wet beriberi. Echocardiography was the principal diagnostic method, but heart-failure definitions and ejection-fraction thresholds varied substantially. Management data were limited mainly to selected populations with thyroid dysfunction, left ventricular thrombus, or wet beriberi. Outcome reporting was sparse and included in-hospital mortality, first-year outcomes in a thrombus cohort, length of stay, stroke, thrombus resolution, and exploratory prognostic indices.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence on heart failure in Somalia is emerging but remains geographically concentrated, methodologically heterogeneous, and insufficient to estimate national burden, treatment coverage, or long-term outcomes. Prospective multicentre studies and a staged heart-failure registry using standardised diagnostic definitions, clear denominators, treatment indicators, and longitudinal follow-up are needed.

Title: Diabetic retinal neurovascular unit injury: mechanisms, imaging evaluation, and integrated therapeutic strategies.
Abstract:
AIM: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) has long been regarded as an isolated retinal microvascular disease. Histopathological, molecular, imaging, and multi-omics evidence now supports disruption of retinal neurovascular unit (NVU) homeostasis as a central mechanism of DR, in which neuronal degeneration, reactive gliosis, and microvascular damage reinforce one another. This narrative review summarizes the anatomy and physiology of the NVU, its temporal evolution in DR, the molecular pathways of neurovascular crosstalk, quantitative imaging assessment, and integrated therapeutic strategies, and indicates where the evidence remains uncertain.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to July 2026 for reports on the retinal NVU in diabetes, and reference lists of retrieved articles were screened. Because this is a narrative rather than a systematic review, records were screened by the authors without a formal risk-of-bias assessment or quantitative synthesis. English-language reports addressing retinal NVU structure, diabetes-related injury mechanisms, imaging quantification, or NVU-directed interventions were eligible, and priority was given to human histopathological studies, prospective imaging cohorts, and translational intervention studies. Eighty-two references were included.
KEY FINDINGS: Neurodegeneration is the earliest readily detectable change of NVU dysfunction in most cohorts, whereas microvascular injury amplifies retinal damage. Combined optical coherence tomography (OCT), OCT angiography (OCTA), and electroretinography (ERG) allow stage-specific quantification, and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) and deep capillary plexus vessel density (DVD) are among the most consistently reported early markers, although this evidence varies. Polyol pathway activation, AGE-RAGE and protein kinase C signaling, oxidative stress, HIF-1α/vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, microglial STING and inflammasome activation, and non-coding RNA dysregulation jointly mediate bidirectional neurovascular injury. Vascular-targeted monotherapy cannot halt inner retinal neuronal loss, whereas multi-target strategies remain largely preclinical or at an early trial stage.
CONCLUSIONS: In our interpretation, early neurodegeneration is the most readily detectable biomarker, microcirculatory damage acts as a disease amplifier, and complete NVU disintegration is the terminal common pathway. This framework is proposed to support ultra-early risk stratification and synergistic multi-target intervention, and is offered as one interpretation of a still-evolving evidence base rather than an established consensus.

Title: Serum T50 is not independently associated with coronary artery calcification in early chronic kidney disease.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The serum T50 test quantifies calcification propensity, with lower values indicating a higher propensity for calcification. Lower T50 values have been associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, particularly in advanced chronic kidney disease. Whether serum T50 is associated with coronary artery calcification (CAC) in individuals with mildly to moderately reduced kidney function remains unclear. We examined this association in a population-based cross-sectional study.
METHODS: We analysed 1945 participants from the population-based Lifelines ImaLife cohort with mildly to moderately reduced kidney function (estimated glomerular filtration rate, 37.5-87.6 ml/min/1.73 m²). Serum T50 was measured using a standardized nephelometric assay. CAC was assessed by electrocardiographically triggered non-contrast computed tomography and categorized into 0, 1-99, 100-399, and ≥400 Agatston units. Associations between continuous T50 (per 10-min increase) and CAC categories were examined using multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of the 1945 participants, 56.5% had detectable CAC (CAC 1-99: 30.9%, 100-399: 14.4%, ≥400: 11.2%). In crude analyses, higher T50 values were associated with the presence of CAC [odds ratio (OR) 1.02, 95% confidence interval 1.01-1.03] and with CAC categories 1-99, 100-399, and ≥400 versus 0 (ORs 1.01, 1.02, and 1.03, respectively). These associations were no longer significant after adjustment for age, body mass index, and sex. Subgroup analyses did not identify risk groups in which T50 was significantly associated with the presence or severity of CAC.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort with mildly to moderately reduced kidney function, T50 was not independently associated with prevalent CAC after multi-variable adjustment.

Title: Clinicopathological Evolution of Pyrrolizidine Alkaloid-induced Liver Injury: Transition From SOS to PSVD?
Journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS) is characterized by hepatic sinusoidal endothelial cell injury and detachment, hepatic sinusoidal congestion, and hepatic cell necrosis. Currently, limited data exist concerning changes during the recovery period, especially histopathological changes. The purpose of this study was to investigate the evolution of pathology in patients with pyrrolizidine alkaloid (PA)-induced SOS and in a monocrotaline-induced SOS rat model.
METHODS: Patients diagnosed with PA-induced SOS who underwent liver biopsy after achieving clinical remission were consecutively enrolled in this retrospective study. To compare the clinical and pathological differences between patients with acute and convalescent SOS, a 2:1 matched analysis was performed based on age, sex, treatment regimen, and baseline Drum Tower Severity Scoring (DTSS) during the acute phase. Additionally, an animal model of PA-induced SOS was established through the administration of monocrotaline.
RESULTS: Fourteen consecutive patients with SOS who had adequate liver biopsy specimens obtained during recovery were identified. During convalescence, most laboratory and imaging findings, such as the map-like enhancement observed on computed tomography, also disappeared. However, histopathological analysis revealed a distinct shift from hepatic sinusoidal endothelial cell injury in the acute phase to portal tract abnormalities, primarily characterized by portal vein stricture, in the recovery phase. These pathological changes were corroborated in our animal model.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that both patients with PA-induced SOS and rats in the convalescent stage may exhibit porto-sinusoidal vascular disease-like changes. Regular follow-up and dynamic pathological assessment are therefore recommended to facilitate the early detection of potential signs of portal hypertension.

Title: Applications of artificial intelligence in personalized nutrition interventions.
Abstract: Unhealthy dietary patterns remain a major modifiable contributor to the global burden of obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), cardiovascular disease, and cancer. However, individuals can respond markedly differently to identical foods, limiting the effectiveness of one-size-fits-all dietary guidance. This review examines the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to personalized nutrition interventions across three interconnected layers. At the biological level, inter-individual variability can be characterized by three mechanistic dimensions: nutrigenomic variation, which influences nutrient metabolism and disease susceptibility; metabolomic biomarkers, which objectively capture dietary exposure and early metabolic alterations; and the gut microbiome, which bidirectionally mediates diet-host interactions. At the technological level, AI integrates these dimensions into multimodal digital profiles. Machine learning models predict individual postprandial glycemic and lipemic responses, with reported correlations of up to r = 0.77 in large cohorts; deep learning and computer vision automate dietary assessment; natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) support nutrition counseling; knowledge graphs enable constraint-aware food recommendations; and digital-twin and adaptive closed-loop systems incorporating continuous glucose monitoring and wearable-device data support real-time nutritional interventions. However, the strength of clinical evidence varies across disease domains. Glycemic management in T2DM and prediabetes currently has the most mature randomized controlled trial evidence: an AI-enabled personalized intervention combining algorithmic dietary personalization with CGM-linked feedback improved glycemic endpoints compared with a Mediterranean diet, while a fully automated AI-delivered diabetes prevention program achieved outcomes non-inferior to those of human coaching. In obesity, cardiovascular disease, oncology, and gastrointestinal disorders, the evidence remains mixed or preliminary. Clinical translation also faces substantial challenges, including biased and inconsistently standardized dietary and multi-omics data; the underrepresentation of non-European populations, which limits model generalizability and raises concerns about health equity; limited model explainability; privacy and data-governance challenges; immature regulatory pathways for adaptive software as a medical device; and specific risks associated with LLMs, such as hallucinated or guideline-discordant dietary advice. AI-enabled personalized nutrition is therefore progressing from proof of concept toward clinical translation. Realizing its potential equitably will require multi-ethnic nutrition-omics cohorts, privacy-preserving multicenter collaboration, dietitian-led human-AI collaboration, and lifecycle safety governance for generative models.

Title: New insights into the gut-heart axis: microbial metabolite biomarkers, multi-omics, and engineered bacterial delivery systems.
Abstract: Despite rapid growth in gut-heart axis research, clinical translation remains limited. This review addresses that gap by critically synthesizing recent evidence on microbiota-derived metabolites, biomarkers, multi-omics workflows, and engineered bacterial interventions in cardiovascular disease (CVD). We examine how TMAO, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, indole derivatives, and phenylacetylglutamine exert context-dependent cardiovascular effects, and why functional microbial gene markers and integrated biomarker panels may outperform single-taxon signatures.
