CONCLUSION: Preoperative APTT exceeding 34.5 s was independently associated with massive bleeding after type A aortic dissection repair and may, pending prospective validation, help identify patients who could potentially benefit from earlier hemostatic intervention.

Title: Plerixafor and G-CSF Versus Placebo and G-CSF in Moderately Mobilizing Patients With Multiple Myeloma to Optimize Hematopoietic Stem Cell Collection Results (OPTIMIZE).
Abstract: Efficient collection of hematopoietic progenitor cells (HPCs) is essential for autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in multiple myeloma (MM). Although plerixafor is routinely used in poor mobilizers, its role in patients with intermediate mobilization capacity remains unclear. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase IV trial, MM patients with peripheral blood (PB) CD34+ counts of 15-40 cells/μL after steady-state G-CSF mobilization were randomized to receive plerixafor or placebo. The primary endpoint was successful collection of ≥ 6.0 × 106 CD34+ cells/kg, sufficient for two ASCTs, during a single apheresis session. Secondary endpoints included CD34+ kinetics, graft composition, colony-forming capacity, engraftment, immune reconstitution, and safety. Twenty-one patients were enrolled before premature study termination due to changes in first-line MM therapy and the COVID-19 pandemic. Plerixafor significantly increased PB CD34+ cell counts compared with placebo (p < 0.001). All patients receiving plerixafor achieved the primary endpoint, whereas none in the placebo group achieved it (p < 0.001). Mean CD34+ yield was significantly higher with plerixafor (10.4 ± 1.9 × 106/kg vs. 2.9 ± 1.3 × 106/kg; p < 0.001). Plerixafor-mobilized grafts contained significantly higher numbers of primitive hematopoietic progenitor subsets and demonstrated increased CFU-GM formation, indicating enhanced clonogenic potential. Despite marked differences in graft quantity and quality, engraftment kinetics, graft sustainability, and immune reconstitution were comparable between groups. In MM patients with intermediate mobilization capacity, the addition of plerixafor markedly improved stem cell mobilization efficiency and enriched grafts with functionally robust progenitor cells. These findings suggest that selected patients beyond conventional poor mobilizers may benefit from plerixafor-assisted mobilization. Trial Registration: EudraCT nr.: 2016-004122-41.

Title: Systemic inflammation in optic neuropathies: comparative insights from hematological and composite indices.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices among patients with multiple sclerosis-associated optic neuritis (MS-ON), non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), idiopathic intracranial hypertension-related optic neuropathy (IIH-ON), and healthy controls, while accounting for demographic confounding.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 135 participants: 36 patients with MS-ON, 29 with NAION, 34 with IIH-ON, and 36 healthy controls. Six composite inflammatory indices, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score, were calculated from routine laboratory measurements obtained at diagnosis before treatment. Log-transformed indices were compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for age and sex. False discovery rate correction was applied across the six indices. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed for indices showing significant adjusted group effects.
RESULTS: Significant differences in age and sex distribution were observed among the groups. After adjustment for age and sex, overall group effects remained for NLR (p = 0.008) and SIRI (p = 0.033), although only NLR remained significant after false discovery rate correction (q = 0.047). Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons demonstrated higher NLR in MS-ON than in healthy controls (adjusted geometric means 2.83 vs. 1.80, p = 0.005). NLR discriminated MS-ON from controls with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.681 (95% CI, 0.554-0.807), while SIRI showed a comparable AUC of 0.661 (95% CI, 0.535-0.787). Among conventional hematological parameters, red cell distribution width remained elevated in IIH-ON, whereas serum albumin remained lower in MS-ON and IIH-ON after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In the primary analysis, NLR was the only index that retained significance after adjustment for age, sex, and multiple testing, with higher values in MS-ON than in healthy controls. The sensitivity of several other indices to robust inference and the modest ROC performance warrant cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

Title: Comparative effectiveness of dietary supplements in dilated cardiomyopathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure and cardiovascular mortality, partly due to impaired myocardial energy metabolism. Dietary supplements may offer benefits through improved mitochondrial function and antioxidant effects, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) suggest they can enhance cardiac function in DCM. However, direct comparisons among supplements are lacking, and the optimal strategy and dose-response relationship remain undetermined.
METHODS: Eight databases were searched for RCTs evaluating dietary supplements in DCM. Continuous outcomes were analysed by frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA; Stata/MP 18.0); N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class were synthesised by pairwise meta-analysis. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
RESULTS: Fourteen RCTs (1,259 participants) were included. For left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) 150 mg/d produced the largest improvement versus conventional treatment (CT) (mean difference [MD] = 11.26, 95% confidence interval [CI] 8.55 ~ 13.98; surface under the cumulative ranking curve [SUCRA] 93.4%), followed by taurine and CoQ10 90 mg/d. CoQ10 150 mg/d also ranked first for reducing left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD; -5.40, - 8.14 ~ - 2.66) and end-systolic diameter (LVESD; -6.31, - 8.60 ~ - 4.01). For heart rate, n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs) gave the most robust reduction (- 3.94 bpm, - 5.11 ~ - 2.77). In pairwise meta-analysis, CoQ10 lowered NT-proBNP and improved NYHA status (risk ratio [RR] for ≥ 1-class improvement 1.23, 1.10 ~ 1.38). Network inconsistency was significant for LVESD (P = 0.008). Certainty of evidence (GRADE) was low to very low, and moderate only for n-3 PUFAs; all supplements were well tolerated.
CONCLUSIONS: In this network, higher-dose CoQ10 (150 mg/d) showed the most favourable overall profile for systolic function and ventricular dimensions, while n-3 PUFAs offered the most reliable benefit for heart rate. Given small samples, predominantly Chinese open-label trials, a heterogeneous and time-varying CT comparator, local inconsistency, and poor safety reporting, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, well-designed international RCTs with longer follow-up.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Systematic Review; Network Meta-Analysis

Title: Long-Term Quantitative MRI and Quality-of-Life After Endovascular Therapy in Acute Ischemic Stroke - A MR CLEAN-NO IV Substudy.
Abstract: This study aims to explore the long-term evolution of endovascular treatment after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) using quantitative MRI, and its relationship with quality of life (QoL). In this long-term substudy of patients from the MR CLEAN-NO IV trial, patients were included who received 24-hour post-stroke MRI and were functionally independent 90 days after stroke onset. Patients underwent a quantitative MRI exam three years after stroke onset to measure focal volume loss, myelin damage, iron deposition, and atrophy within and around the ischemic lesion seen on 24-hour-MRI, in addition to a QoL assessment. Bayesian statistical analyses were used to assess MRI measures lateralized to the ipsilateral hemisphere and to evaluate the relationship of these measures with baseline and treatment characteristics along with QoL. The Bayes Factor (BF) reflected moderate, strong or very strong evidence (BF = 3.0;20;1.5⋅102 respectively). In the 24 included patients, prominent focal volume loss, iron deposition, ventricular enlargement and myelin damage (BF:2.0⋅102) were observed peripheral to the initial 24-hour DWI lesion at long-term FU MRI. In the basal ganglia nuclei, very strong evidence of focal volume loss (BF > 8.1⋅102) and moderate to very strong evidence of iron deposition (BF: 5.0 to 2.7⋅102) were observed at long-term assessment. Higher systolic blood pressure was associated with reduced long-term ventricular atrophy (BF:5.8). Long-term differences in ipsilateral versus contralateral hippocampal volume difference (BF:8.0) and iron deposition (BF:4.1) were moderately associated with QoL. Long-term subtle yet widespread demyelination and iron deposition were observed, and these changes correlated with long-term recovery.

Title: Advanced Age is Not Associated With An Increased Risk of Postoperative Complications in Breast Reduction Surgery: A Comparative Study on 1716 Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Age is frequently cited as a surgical risk factor; yet, its influence on outcomes following breast reduction remains unclear. With increasing numbers of elderly patients presenting with macromastia, determining whether advanced age independently affects complication rates is clinically important.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether age ≥ 65 years is an independent risk factor for postoperative complications following bilateral reduction mammaplasty and to identify associated patient- and procedure-related variables.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 1716 female patients who underwent bilateral breast reduction at a single tertiary center (2005-2024), stratified into older (≥ 65 years, n = 174), and non-older (< 65 years, n = 1542) groups. Primary outcome was Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications requiring surgical intervention. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors.
RESULTS: Older patients had significantly higher comorbidity prevalence (69.0% vs. 46.1%; p < 0.001), including diabetes and hypertension, and greater bilateral resection weights. Despite this, overall complication rates were significantly lower in the older group (8.6% vs. 16.1%; OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.28-0.85; p = 0.009). Hematoma and deep wound infection rates were also lower, while fat necrosis occurred more frequently and was managed conservatively in most cases. On multivariable analysis, higher BMI (OR 1.10; p = 0.004) and active smoking (OR 1.80; p = 0.004) were independent predictors of complications; age ≥ 65 was not significantly associated with complications (OR 0.55; p = 0.062).
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced age alone was not independently associated with increased complications. BMI and smoking were the main modifiable factors associated with postoperative risk. Age-based exclusion criteria are not supported by these findings in this cohort of selected surgical patients; individualized risk assessment should be applied to all candidates.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

Title: Effects of immersive virtual reality and non-immersive video distraction on preoperative anxiety in patients undergoing elective abdominal surgery: a three-arm randomised controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative anxiety negatively impacts surgical outcomes. This study evaluated the effects of immersive virtual reality (VR) vs non-immersive video distraction on preoperative anxiety, physiological stress, and heart rate in elective abdominal surgery.
METHODS: In this three-arm randomized controlled trial (NCT05718661), 96 elective abdominal surgery patients were allocated to immersive VR, non-immersive video, or a control group ( n = 32  per group). Both intervention groups viewed identical relaxing audiovisual content for 15 min via a VR headset or a smartphone screen; controls received standard care. Preoperative anxiety was measured with the Visual Analogue Scale-Anxiety (VAS-A). Physiological stress scores and heart rate were tracked using a wearable smart band before and after the intervention.
RESULTS: VAS-A scores worsened in controls (p < 0.001) but decreased significantly in both the VR (p < 0.001) and video (p = 0.002) groups, with no significant difference between the two active interventions (p > 0.05). Device-derived stress scores increased in controls (p = 0.018) and decreased in the video group (p = 0.017), with no change in the VR group (p = 0.568). Heart rate changes did not differ significantly among groups (p < 0.206).
CONCLUSIONS: Both immersive VR and non-immersive video distraction significantly reduce preoperative anxiety compared with standard care; however, VR is not superior to conventional video viewing. Given its equivalent efficacy, lower cost, and simpler implementation, non-immersive video represents a practical, scalable non-pharmacological strategy for perioperative anxiety management.

Title: Oral eplerenone in first-episode acute central serous chorioretinopathy: results of a double-masked randomized trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) is a pachychoroid disorder characterized by serous retinal detachment driven by choroidal vascular dysfunction and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) overactivation. Eplerenone, a selective MR antagonist, has been proposed as a therapeutic option, although clinical evidence remains inconsistent.
METHODS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 44 patients with first-episode acute CSCR received either oral eplerenone (25 mg twice daily) or placebo for three months. Outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), subretinal fluid (SRF) height, subfoveal choroidal thickness (CT), and OCT-angiography parameters of retinal and choroidal microvasculature.
RESULTS: Both groups demonstrated significant reductions in CMT and SRF over time, but SRF absorption was significantly greater in the eplerenone group at 3 months (P < 0.05). Choriocapillaris vessel density and flow index improved significantly with eplerenone (P < 0.001), while superficial, deep, and radial peripapillary plexus densities did not differ between groups. BCVA improved similarly in both groups.
CONCLUSION: Eplerenone accelerates SRF resolution and enhances choriocapillaris perfusion in acute CSCR, although visual outcomes remain comparable to placebo. Early MR antagonism may offer anatomical and microvascular benefits in CSCR management.

Title: Autonomic function and signal complexity reflect level and severity of traumatic spinal cord injury.
Abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Observational single-centre cohort study.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and signal complexity (SC) and their relationships with neurological injury level and severity, as well as their prognostic value for six-month mortality and functional recovery in patients with traumatic spinal cord injury (TSCI).
SETTING: Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden.
METHODS: This study included 164 adult patients with TSCI treated in neurointensive care (NIC) (2008-2022). Continuous high-frequency physiological data from the first 7 post-injury days were analysed to derive HRV, BRS, and SC for heart rate (HR), mean arterial pressure, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Associations with neurological injury level, injury severity, NIC physiology, neurological improvement, and six-month mortality were assessed.
RESULTS: Patients with cervical injuries had higher HRV, BRS (both p < 0.01), and SC for DBP (p < 0.05) than those with thoracic injuries. Complete cervical injuries had higher HRV (p < 0.05), but lower HR SC (p < 0.01) compared with incomplete cervical injuries. Higher HR SC was associated with neurological improvement at discharge (odds ratio 1.08 [95% confidence interval 1.01-1.16]; p < 0.05), whereas higher HRV was associated with increased six-month mortality (odds ratio 1.01 [95% confidence interval 1.00-1.02]; p < 0.05). Other autonomic and complexity measures showed limited prognostic value.
CONCLUSION: Systemic autonomic indices after TSCI vary with injury level and severity and may capture distinct aspects of autonomic dysfunction beyond clinical grading. However, their limited prognostic value for neurological recovery and mortality suggest that outcome prediction after TSCI may depend more on other clinical factors and, possibly, more direct intraspinal physiological markers.
SPONSORSHIP: NA.

Title: Impact on mortality of inhaled nitric oxide in newborns ≤34 weeks with early hypoxemic respiratory failure: systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is approved for hypoxemic respiratory failure (HRF) associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH) in term and near-term neonates; however, its use in preterm infants ≤34 weeks' gestation remains controversial, with limited and inconsistent evidence of survival benefit.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between iNO use and mortality in preterm neonates ≤34 weeks' gestation.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Major databases were searched up to October 11, 2025. Observational studies and clinical trials reporting mortality in preterm infants with early HRF treated with iNO were included. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and six (n = 556 infants) in the meta-analysis. Study quality ranged from poor to good, with limitations related to confounding and heterogeneity. No significant reduction in mortality was observed with iNO compared with standard care (RR 0.65; 95% CI 0.29-1.48; I² = 55.7%). Infants receiving iNO were more severely ill at baseline. A positive oxygenation response was associated with improved outcomes and varied by gestational age (GA), timing of PH onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and hypoxemia severity.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence regarding the survival benefit of iNO in preterm infants ≤34 weeks remains inconclusive.
IMPACT: This systematic review and meta-analysis show that inhaled nitric oxide (iNO) is not associated with a consistent reduction in mortality in preterm infants ≤34 weeks at the population level. It adds evidence that outcomes are strongly influenced by clinical context, particularly, illness severity, gestational age, timing of pulmonary hypertension onset, echocardiographic confirmation, and response to therapy. These findings support a selective, phenotype-driven approach rather than routine iNO use in all preterm infants with hypoxemic respiratory failure. The results may inform clinical decision-making and highlight the need for well-designed randomized trials in this high-risk population.

Title: Testing neurobiological models of reward/incentive sensitization in the continuation of alcohol use disorder (AUD) symptoms in young adults with AUD: A four-year longitudinal study.
Journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
Abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) remains an urgent public health problem. Alcohol response phenotype may be an important factor underlying vulnerability to and progression of AUD. This study examined the prospective association between acute alcohol responses and continued or remitted AUD over time in young adults with AUD. This sample was N = 101 AUD participants (Mage=27.1 ± 4.0 SD yrs) comprising the third cohort of the Chicago Social Drinking Project. They completed two beverage challenge  laboratory sessions (0.8 g/kg fixed-dose alcohol vs. placebo) and four years of follow-up to ascertain future AUD symptoms, drinking behaviors, and consequences. Retention was high with an overall 99.2% follow-up rate. Analyses identified three AUD trajectory subgroups over follow-up including a high AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 37), a medium AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 48), and a low AUD trajectory subgroup (n = 16). Generalized estimating equations showed that greater sensitivity to alcohol's pleasurable effects, including stimulation and hedonic and motivational reward (liking and wanting, respectively) predicted more AUD symptoms over follow-up (ps<0.001) and were positively associated with AUD trajectory subgroups. However,  sedation, heart rate, and cortisol response to alcohol were not  significantly associated with AUD trajectory subgroups. In sum, greater alcohol stimulation, liking, and wanting prospectively predicted the continuation and increasing severity of AUD over a four-year period. The findings challenge theoretical models emphasizing reward deficit and global tolerance in addiction and support the role of positive reinforcement, indexed by sensitivity to alcohol's pleasurable effects, as an important factor in AUD  persistence. CLINICAL TRIAL: Name: Chicago Social Drinking Project Registration #: NCT00961792 URL: http://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT00961792.

Title: Angiotensin peptide and aldosterone concentrations in response to four classes of blood-pressure-lowering drugs in hypertensive patients: A randomized trial.
Abstract: The renin angiotensin aldosterone system (RAS) regulates blood pressure and fluid balance by a cascade of angiotensin (Ang) peptides. Antihypertensive drug classes differentially modulate this cascade. This study examined how four mechanistically distinct antihypertensive drugs affect plasma concentrations of 10 Ang peptides and aldosterone in untreated hypertensive patients. In this randomized, open-label, parallel-group study, 88 patients received 4 weeks of monotherapy with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi), angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB), calcium channel blocker (CCB), or hydrochlorothiazide (HCT). Equilibrium concentrations of 10 Ang peptides and aldosterone were quantified by LC-MS at baseline and after 4 weeks, both pre- and 4 h post-dose; drug exposure was confirmed by measured drug concentrations. Seventy-two participants completed the 4-week treatment (ACEi n = 18, ARB n = 17, CCB n = 20, HCT n = 17). The most prominent effects were seen for Ang I, Ang II, and aldosterone and were reflected in biomarkers for plasma renin activity (PRA-Q; Ang I+Ang II), ACE activity (ACE-Q; Ang II/Ang I), and the aldosterone/Ang II ratio (AA2-R). Downstream peptides showed minimal or no changes. Relative to baseline, ACEi increased Ang I and reduced ACE-Q. ARB increased Ang I and Ang II and lowered AA2-R without altering ACE-Q. CCB and HCT produced only minor changes. ACE-Q < 1.05 pM/pM identified ACEi use, and AA2-R < 0.85 pM/pM as well as Ang II > 175 pM identified ARB use. RAS-targeted monotherapy produces distinct peptide-level signatures that can be captured by Ang-derived biomarkers, supporting their potential utility for monitoring drug intake in personalized hypertension management.

Title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on serum vitamin D levels and health outcomes in pediatric population with obesity/overweight: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Because 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol is lipophilic, children with obesity/overweight are at increased risk of its deficiency, potentially leading to health issues such as compromising bone mineralization and cardiometabolic health.
OBJECTIVES: Our goal was to assess the impact of 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol supplementation on serum Vitamin D levels and various health parameters such as BMI and cardiovascular risk markers.
METHODOLOGY: Data were extracted from PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar. Following search string was used in each database: (Vitamin D OR 25(OH)D OR cholecalciferol) AND (Obese OR Overweight) AND (randomized trial OR RCT OR intervention) AND (children OR adolescent OR pediatric). Clinical trials assessing the impact of 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol D supplementation in pediatric populations with overweight or obesity, regardless of formulation, dosage, or duration, were included. A total of 24 studies were included in the systematic review, of which 11 randomized controlled trials were eligible for meta-analysis. The included studies' quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias (ROB-2) tool. Primary outcome was serum Vitamin D levels while secondary outcomes include cardiovascular risk markers, lipid profile, insulin sensitivity, and change in BMI. Follow-up done at 8 weeks, 12 weeks, 24 weeks, 26 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months.
RESULTS: Supplementing with 25-hydroxy cholecalciferol significantly raised the levels of serum vitamin D in children with obesity/overweight. No adverse events occurred following supplementation. Decrease in BMI, serum triglycerides and inflammatory markers were observed but its effects on metabolism and cardiovascular health remained insignificant. According to meta-analysis, vitamin D supplementation (interventional) arm group differed from the placebo by a standardized mean difference of 3.12 ng/ml (95% CI:1.72-4.52).
CONCLUSION: Vitamin D supplementation in children with overweight /obesity correct the deficiency and significantly raise Vitamin D levels with no adverse events. To assess effective therapies to enhance metabolic and cardiovascular outcomes in the pediatric population with overweight/obesity, new trials should be conducted.

Title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Thromboembolic Risk in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation or Flutter and Type 2 Diabetes: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
Comparative Cardiorenal Efficacy and Safety of SGLT2 Inhibitors and Finerenone in Chronic Kidney Disease With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
AIMS: No randomized trial has compared SGLT2 inhibitors with finerenone in chronic kidney disease (CKD) with Type 2 diabetes. We estimated their comparative cardiorenal efficacy and safety.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and trial registries were searched from inception to August 2026 for placebo-controlled outcome trials. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled in a frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis, and the between-class contrast was derived indirectly through placebo. Risk of bias followed RoB 2 and certainty followed CINeMA.
RESULTS: Ten trial datasets formed a star network without closed loops. Versus placebo, both classes reduced kidney function progression (SGLT2 inhibitors HR: 0.64, 95% CI: 0.56-0.73; finerenone 0.84, 0.77-0.92) and heart-failure hospitalization (0.61, 0.53-0.69; 0.78, 0.66-0.92). Indirectly, SGLT2 inhibitors were favoured for kidney function progression (0.76, 0.64-0.90) and heart-failure hospitalization (0.77, 0.63-0.95), with no significant difference for atherothrombotic events or mortality. The kidney contrast remained significant after excluding high-risk-of-bias datasets, restricting to dedicated CKD trials and applying a uniform endpoint; the heart-failure contrast did not persist in dedicated CKD trials. Finerenone increased hyperkalemia without increasing acute kidney injury. Certainty was low or very low for every between-class comparison.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors and finerenone both provide cardiorenal protection and appear complementary rather than interchangeable. Indirect differences favouring SGLT2 inhibitors derive from a loop-free network with unverifiable transitivity and low certainty; they are hypothesis-generating and should not be used to rank the agents. Safety domains are not reported comparably across classes.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: CRD420261439899.

Title: Prognostic Value of Pulmonary Elastance Methods in HFrEF: A Comparative Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is commonly used to quantify right ventricular (RV) afterload in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet it reflects primarily the steady component of pulmonary vascular load. Simplified pulmonary arterial elastance indices may better characterise the integrated arterial load experienced by the RV. The comparative prognostic value of different elastance formulations in HFrEF remains incompletely defined.
METHOD: This retrospective study included 352 patients with HFrEF who underwent right heart catheterisation between 2018 and 2022. Pulmonary elastance was calculated using three simplified formulations: systolic pressure-based elastance (EasPAP=sPAP/SV), transpulmonary gradient-based elastance (EaTPG=[mPAP PCWP]/SV), and pulse pressure-based elastance (EaPP=PP/SV), together with their indexed forms. Discriminatory performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Associations with all-cause mortality were assessed using univariate and multivariable Cox regression analyses adjusted for age, New York Heart Association functional class, and renal function. Subgroup analyses by PVR (<3 vs ≥3 Wood units [WU]) and combined PVR-EaPP phenotype analyses were performed.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 23 months, 139 patients (39.5%) died. In multivariable models, EasPAP (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.31; p=0.002), EaPP (adjusted HR 1.63; p=0.005), and their indexed forms remained independently associated with mortality, whereas EaTPG-based formulations did not. In patients with PVR <3 WU, EasPAP and EaPP demonstrated stronger associations with mortality than in the high-PVR subgroup. In the combined phenotype analysis, elevated EaPP identified increased mortality risk irrespective of PVR category.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HFrEF undergoing right heart catheterisation, simplified pulsatile elastance indices, particularly EasPAP and EaPP, were independently associated with all-cause mortality. Notably, elevated EaPP identified higher-risk patients even in the absence of elevated PVR, suggesting that resistance-based metrics alone may not fully capture RV afterload. Prospective validation is warranted.

Title: Coronary Revascularisation Strategies for Patients with Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Requiring Lung Transplantation: A Narrative Review and Single-Centre Experience.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung transplant (LTx) candidates often have multiple risk factors for coronary artery disease (CAD), which was previously considered a contraindication to transplantation. Improvements in revascularisation techniques have broadened transplant eligibility; however, because available evidence is based on small and heterogeneous cohorts, the optimal revascularisation strategy remains unclear.
METHOD: We conducted a literature review and describe our centre's experience with current approaches to revascularisation in LTx candidates with obstructive CAD.
RESULTS: The literature review identified 174 studies in the initial search, of which 29 studies were considered relevant. However, only six retrospective studies directly compared percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), comprising 376 revascularised patients. In some cohorts, CABG was associated with longer ventilation time and longer intensive care unit (ICU) stay and overall hospital stay, although this finding was not consistent across all studies. At our centre, 20 patients underwent concomitant CABG, and 11 underwent PCI within 12 months before transplant listing, after obstructive CAD was diagnosed during transplant assessment. Procedure time in patients undergoing concomitant CABG was significantly longer (1.2 hours; p<0.05); however, all patients in this group underwent bilateral transplantation. Three patients in the PCI group experienced postoperative coronary events, and overall mortality was higher in this group. There were no differences in other outcomes, including ICU and overall length of stay.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the heterogeneity and complexity of this patient cohort. Although no patients who underwent CABG experienced postoperative coronary events, the limited published evidence does not support a single preferred revascularisation strategy for patients being considered for lung transplantation. Case-by-case management guided by a multidisciplinary team is therefore warranted.

Title: Interpretation and reporting of coronary computed tomographic angiography (2026 update): An expert consensus document of the Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography (SCCT).
The Role of Varying Cardiac Troponin Levels in Long-Term Mortality in Liver Transplant Patients.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increased serum concentrations of (High-sensitivity) ultrasensitive Troponin (hsTn) could predict short-term mortality in patients undergoing liver transplant (LT). This study aimed to determine whether there is an association between changes in intraoperative hsTn values during LT and long-term mortality.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on adult LT recipients who underwent orthotopic LT from deceased donors. HsTn levels were obtained during surgery at baseline and 60 minutes after graft reperfusion. Survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. The association between troponin delta and mortality was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, and discriminatory performance was evaluated by ROC analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 101 LT recipients were included and followed for 3 years; 17 patients (16.8%) died during follow-up. No significant differences were observed in baseline hsTn concentrations between survivors and non-survivors. HsTn levels measured 60 minutes after graft reperfusion were significantly higher in patients who died (median 45.2 ng/L [IQR: 30-105] vs 35 ng/L [IQR: 23-54]; p < .05). The difference between baseline and 60-minute hsTn values (delta-hsTn) was analyzed. ROC analysis identified an optimal cut-off of 26.45 ng/L (AUC, 0.65). Patients with delta-hsTn ≥26 ng/L had increased 3-year mortality (sensitivity 62.5%, specificity 71.7%). In Cox proportional hazards analysis, delta-hsTn ≥26 ng/L was independently associated with mortality (HR, 3.31, 95% CI: 1.3-8.4).
CONCLUSION: Intraoperative hsTn changes, reflected by delta-hsTn, were associated with long-term mortality after LT and may represent a clinically accessible marker of perioperative myocardial stress and risk stratification.

Title: Role of shear wave elastography in differentiating Bland vs tumoral portal vein thrombosis.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of shear wave elastography (SWE) in distinguishing bland from tumoral (malignant) portal vein thrombosis (PVT), using dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) as the reference standard.
METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted on patients with ultrasound-confirmed PVT. SWE was performed, followed by DCE-MRI within 48 hours. Mean and median SWE values of the thrombus, liver parenchyma, and any focal hepatic lesions were calculated, and novel SWE ratios (liver-to-PVT and lesion-to-PVT) were derived. At least five RoI measurements were obtained to ensure reliability. Using MRI as the reference standard, diagnostic performance metrics for SWE, including sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and overall accuracy, were calculated. Fisher's exact test and Chi-square test were used to compare these parameters between bland and tumoral thrombus groups. A p value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Fifty patients (mean age: 54.3 ± 10.7 years; 82% males) were included. 16 patients (32%) had bland portal vein thrombosis (PVT), whereas 34 (68%) had tumoral PVT. The mean SWE of PVT was 8.74 ± 4.24 kPa, with significantly lower values in bland PVT (4.63 ± 3.31 kPa) compared with tumoral PVT (10.68 ± 3.11 kPa; p < 0.001). Significant differences were also observed in the ultrasound diameters of the main, right, and left portal veins. The liver SWE/PVT SWE ratio was significantly higher in bland PVT (3.47 ± 3.08 vs. 1.68 ± 0.70; p = 0.033), while the lesion SWE/PVT SWE ratio was higher in tumoral PVT (p = 0.041). ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance of SWE for differentiation of bland versus tumoral thrombus, with AUROC values of 0.903 and 0.915 at cutoff values of ≥6.1 kPa and ≥5.7 kPa for mean and median SWE, respectively.
CONCLUSION: SWE is a reliable, non-invasive tool for differentiating tumoral from bland PVT, with diagnostic performance comparable to MRI.

Title: Development and internal validation of an oxygen saturation-based prehospital cardiac risk assessment index (P-CRAI) for predicting 30-day mortality in acute myocardial infarction: a multicentre registry study from the Mie ACS Registry, Japan.

OCT-guided versus angiography-guided stent optimisation for post-interventional FFR in patients with complex coronary artery lesions: protocol for a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial (PRECISION-COMPLEX).
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) reduces adverse events in complex coronary lesions remains debated. Although optical coherence tomography (OCT) improves stent optimisation, its effect on the physiological result of PCI has not been tested in a dedicated randomised trial. The PREcise percutaneous coronary intervention for stent OptimizatION in treatment of COMPLEX lesion (PRECISION-COMPLEX) trial aims to determine whether algorithm-driven OCT-guided stent optimisation improves the physiological result of PCI, assessed by post-optimisation fractional flow reserve (FFR), compared with angiography-guided PCI.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PRECISION-COMPLEX is an investigator-initiated, multicentre, open-label, superiority randomised controlled trial at four Korean academic hospitals. Patients with stable or unstable angina and at least one prespecified complex lesion are randomised 1:1 to OCT-guided or angiography-guided PCI with current-generation drug-eluting stents. In the OCT arm, stent sizing follows a prespecified algorithm, and post-PCI OCT must confirm adequate expansion, apposition and absence of major edge dissection. Post-PCI FFR is mandated in both arms. The primary endpoint is the proportion of patients with a suboptimal post-optimisation FFR (<0.85); secondary endpoints at 2 years include target-vessel failure and its components, any revascularisation and stent thrombosis. A total of 320 patients gives 90% power to detect a reduction in the primary endpoint from 30% to 15%. Enrolment ran from 15 November 2022 to 4 December 2024; follow-up is ongoing, with main results expected in early 2027.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The trial protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Chonnam National University Hospital (CNUH-2022-283), the Institutional Review Board of Samsung Medical Center (SMC2022-11-012), the Institutional Review Board of Seoul National University Hospital (H2303-104-1414) and the Institutional Review Board of Chung-Ang University Gwangmyeong Hospital (2212–048-077). It conforms to the Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice. All participants provide written informed consent. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and presentation at scientific meetings. PRECISION-COMPLEX will define the incremental impact of OCT-based optimisation on the physiological result of PCI and indicate whether anatomy-integrated and physiology-integrated guidance improves outcomes in complex coronary lesions.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05493904.

Title: [A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF DONATION AFTER BRAIN DEATH, DONATION AFTER CARDIAC DEATH, AND LIVING-DONOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION].
Journal: Nihon Hinyokika Gakkai zasshi. The japanese journal of urology
Abstract: (Objective) Since the revision of the Organ Transplant Law in our country in 2010, the primary source of deceased organ donation has shifted from donation after cardiac death (DCD) to donation after brain death (DBD). Although the graft survival rate of living donor (LD) kidney transplantation has generally surpassed that of deceased donor kidney transplantation, few studies have directly compared outcomes between DCD and DBD. (Subjects and methods) We conducted a retrospective analysis of 213 patients who underwent kidney transplantation at our institution between 2011 and 2023. ABO-incompatible transplants and those with pre-existing anti-donor HLA antibodies were excluded. Patients were categorized into three groups according to donor status: DCD (n = 25), DBD (n = 39), and LD (n = 149). (Results) The median recipient ages were 56 years (DCD), 52 years (DBD), and 41 years (LD), while the median donor ages were 47 years (DCD), 45 years (DBD), and 61 years (LD). The proportion of HLA-DR 0 mismatch was 36% in DCD, 59% in DBD, and 24.8% in LD. Graft survival rates at 10 years were 83.2% for DCD; 100% for DBD; and 88.3% for LD, respectively.Multivariate analysis identified biopsy proven rejection as the only independent predictor of graft survival. (Conclusion) Despite the disadvantages of longer ischemic times and dialysis durations prior to transplantation, DBD grafts demonstrated the highest graft survival rates. These favorable outcomes may be attributed to a lower frequency of HLA-DR mismatches and reduced incidence of rejection.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; English Abstract

Title: The effects of low-dose medetomidine and butorphanol premedication on anesthetic induction and recovery for intramuscular alfaxalone anesthesia in cats.
Journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
Abstract: This study evaluated effects of premedication with low-dose medetomidine (MED), butorphanol (BTR), or their combination on intramuscular (IM) alfaxalone (ALFX) anesthesia in cats. Five healthy purpose-bred cats were used in a completely randomized crossover study with a minimum 1-week washout period. Cats received three types of premedication: MED (5 µg/kg), BTR (0.3 mg/kg) or their combination via IM injection. After 15 min, anesthesia was induced with low (1.0 mg/kg), medium (2.5 mg/kg) or high (5.0 mg/kg) doses of IM ALFX. Anesthetic depth, tracheal intubation scores, and cardiorespiratory variables were evaluated over 120 min. Dose-dependent anesthetic effects of ALFX were observed across all protocols. Although tracheal intubation was difficult with MED alone, premedication with BTR alone or in combination with MED facilitated successful intubation. Notably, the MED-BTR combination resulted in a significantly greater sedation/anesthetic effect, even with lower doses of ALFX. The MED-BTR combination completely prevented MED-induced emesis. Cardiorespiratory evaluation revealed a decrease in heart rate with MED and MED-BTR premedication, and percutaneous arterial oxygen saturation dropped below 93% temporarily at higher ALFX doses. In summary, premedication combining BTR and low-dose MED facilitates reliable and smooth anesthetic induction with low-dose ALFX (1.0 mg/kg), achieving sufficient anesthetic depth without inducing prolonged or turbulent recovery. However, careful monitoring for bradycardia and hypoxemia is recommended, and its clinical application should be limited to young and healthy cats with sufficient cardiorespiratory reserve.

Title: Optimal Catheter Size for Medium Vessel Occlusion in Aspiration Thrombectomy.
Abstract: The efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion remains controversial, and optimal recanalization strategies are lacking. We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025. We examined the factors associated with successful recanalization by focusing on the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio). Overall, 64 patients were included. First-pass successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥ 2c) was achieved in 24 patients. In patients with successful recanalization, the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio) was significantly higher than in those without successful recanalization (p = 0.029). In multivariate analysis, the Catheter-to-vessel ratio was independently associated with successful recanalization after adjustment for catheter position and thrombus size (odds ratio per 0.1 increase, 3.688; 95% confidence interval, 1.478-9.202; p = 0.0007). In the receiver operating characteristic analysis, the threshold for the Catheter-to-vessel ratio distinguishing successful recanalization was 0.70, with a sensitivity of 79% and a specificity of 63%.In aspiration thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion, a Catheter-to-vessel ratio ≥ 0.70 may be an exploratory indicator associated with first-pass successful reperfusion.

Title: Two-point Loop Suture Fixation May Reduce Catheter Displacement in Cisternal and External Ventricular Drains.
Abstract: In this retrospective, single-center, before-and-after comparison study, we report a simple and reliable method for securing cisternal or external ventricular drain catheters to the scalp to prevent accidental catheter displacement. This method involves fixation of the catheter at 2 points with loop sutures. A 10-year retrospective review was conducted in 39 consecutive patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage who underwent placement of either a cisternal drainage catheter (n = 15) or an external ventricular drainage catheter (n = 24) at our institution. Conventional single-point suture fixation (non-loop method, n = 15) was compared with two-point loop suture fixation (loop method, n = 24).No accidental pullout occurred in the loop method group, whereas one pullout was observed in the non-loop method. The mean duration of catheter placement did not differ significantly between the 2 groups (4.93 vs. 4.13 days, p = 0.25). However, the mean daily catheter displacement was greater with the non-loop method than with the loop method (1.05 vs. 0.28 mm/day, p = 0.01). These findings suggest that the loop method was associated with reduced daily catheter displacement. The loop suture fixation method is a simple and reliable method for securing cisternal drainage catheter or external ventricular drainage catheters to the scalp and may reduce the risk of accidental catheter displacement.

Title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR.
METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months.
RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.
Publication Types: Comparative Study; Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease is present in one-half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The recent randomized controlled PRO-TAVI (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial indicated that deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is safe in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease at 1-year follow-up. The SYNTAX (Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery) score quantifies the extent of coronary artery disease, which may guide individualized revascularization strategies.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between SYNTAX score (SS) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR.
METHODS: This study was a substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial, including 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR randomized to deferral of PCI or PCI before TAVR. SS was calculated from preprocedural coronary angiograms, and patients were stratified by SS quartiles. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major bleeding at 1 year. An ischemic composite outcome of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and stroke was also assessed.
RESULTS: The primary composite outcome did not differ across SS categories between the deferral and PCI groups at 1-year follow-up, which was completed by all but 1 patient. In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke. Bleeding events were less frequent in the deferral group across all SS subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with concomitant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR, deferral of PCI reduced bleeding risk and appeared safe across all SS categories. Deferral of PCI in patients with more complex coronary artery disease (SS >17) was associated with higher risk for the ischemic composite outcome. These post hoc findings require confirmation in randomized trials. (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation [PRO-TAVI]; NCT05078619).
Publication Types: Journal Article; Randomized Controlled Trial; Multicenter Study

Title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac arrest (CA) during percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) is a catastrophic procedural complication. Contemporary rates of CA during PCI are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to understand contemporary rates of CA, associated mortality, and identify predictors of CA during PCI.
METHODS: Patients with CA during PCI from 2018 to 2023 were identified from the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI Registry. Trends in intraprocedural CA (IPCA) incidence and in-hospital death were evaluated. Predictors of IPCA and risk-adjusted mortality were identified.
RESULTS: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%), including in 0.24% of elective PCIs, 0.32% of PCIs for stable coronary artery disease, and 1.28% of acute coronary syndrome interventions. The incidence of IPCA increased over time (0.62% in 2018 to 1.07% in 2023; P < 0.0001). In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA, 45.4% of whom died in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Notably, although risk-adjusted IPCA increased (0.79% to 0.95%; P = 0.042), slight declines in risk-adjusted mortality (45.1% to 43.6%; P = 0.027) were observed over time. PCI for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, non-ST-segment acute coronary syndromes, increasing age, ventricular arrhythmias, severe aortic stenosis, vasopressors or inotrope use, mechanical circulatory support, coronary perforation, coronary dissection, cardiac tamponade, intraprocedural heart failure or myocardial infarction, and temporary cardiac pacemaker implantation were associated with increased adjusted odds of IPCA.
CONCLUSIONS: IPCA complicates 0.93% of contemporary PCI. Despite an increasing incidence of risk-adjusted IPCA, there were slight declines in risk-adjusted in-hospital mortality in the study period. Several patient and procedural characteristics were independently associated with intraprocedural CA.

Title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI.
METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207).
RESULTS: After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I2 = 0%; τ2 = 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

Title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/NSTEMI framework may not fully identify patients with ACO who present without diagnostic STE. Although immediate invasive management is recommended for patients with very-high-risk NSTEMI features, these criteria are inconsistently applied in clinical practice. The OMI/NOMI framework has been proposed as an alternative strategy.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare the occlusive and nonocclusive myocardial infarction (OMI/NOMI) classification with guideline-defined very-high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) criteria for the identification of acute coronary occlusion (ACO) in patients without diagnostic STE.
METHODS: This was a substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 (Time for a Diagnostic Paradigm Shift From ST-Elevation/Non-ST-Elevation to Occlusion/Non-Occlusion Myocardial Infarction-3) trial. Consecutive adult patients without diagnostic STE on the admission electrocardiogram were included and managed according to either the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI or the OMI/NOMI approach. Very-high-risk NSTEMI was defined according to current guidelines. Outcomes included immediate invasive management (within 2 hours) and adjudicated ACO.
RESULTS: Among 4,398 patients, very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria identified a small proportion of patients and were inconsistently translated into early intervention. The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001). Adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently under the OMI/NOMI approach (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001), without reduction in angiographic yield.
CONCLUSIONS: An occlusion-focused diagnostic approach was associated with substantially higher rates of immediate invasive management and earlier identification of patients with adjudicated ACO.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Comparative Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients may present with acute coronary occlusions (ACOs) without manifesting electrocardiographic criteria for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine the incidence, clinical characteristics, and in-hospital outcomes of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with ACO.
METHODS: The study included patients with STEMI and NSTEMI in the CathPCI Registry who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention between April 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023. ACO was defined as 100% stenosis deemed acute. The cohort was stratified into STEMI (including STEMI equivalents), NSTEMI-ACO, and NSTEMI-no-ACO. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular mortality. A sensitivity analysis with ACO defined as 100% acute occlusion or TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 in the culprit artery was performed.
RESULTS: Of 1,198,544 patients, 26.1% had STEMI, 11.0% had NSTEMI-ACO (15% of whom had NSTEMI), and 62.9% had NSTEMI-no-ACO. Compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO, NSTEMI-ACO patients had more cardiogenic shock (9.0% STEMI vs 3.8% NSTEMI-ACO vs 1.9% NSTEMI-no-ACO; P < 0.001), ventricular arrhythmias (4.9% vs 2.0% vs 1.3%; P < 0.001), and in-hospital cardiac arrest (6.1% vs 2.7% vs 1.6%; P < 0.001). Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001). Using a definition of ACO including TIMI flow grade 0 or 1, NSTEMI-ACO accounted for 216,054 presentations (24.4% of NSTEMI). In-hospital outcomes were similarly worse compared with NSTEMI-no-ACO and better compared with STEMI.
CONCLUSIONS: ACO occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with NSTEMI and is associated with worse in-hospital outcomes relative to those with NSTEMI-no-ACO. Further studies of early identification and reperfusion practices for NSTEMI-ACO are warranted.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission.
STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years.
METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years.
RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148).
CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

Title: First-trimester metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: A prospective cohort study.
Journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is the most common chronic liver condition globally, increasingly relevant in pregnancy due to rising maternal metabolic risks. The study explores MASLD in early pregnancy as a potential independent risk factor for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs).
METHODOLOGY: In this prospective study, we assessed MASLD in 198 pregnant women at 10-14 weeks' gestation using demographic, clinical, metabolic, and hepatic parameters measured by transient elastography. We followed participants prospectively for the development of HDPs. We used standardised protocols, blinded operators, and validated cutoff values. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess the association between MASLD and HDPs, adjusting for prespecified clinical and metabolic covariates.
RESULTS: MASLD was present in 48 (24.2%) women. HDPs developed in 11/48 (22.9%) women with MASLD compared with 9/150 (6.0%) without MASLD (p = 0.002). In the fully adjusted model, MASLD was associated with higher odds of HDPs, although the association did not reach statistical significance (adjusted OR 2.89, 95% CI 0.90-9.54; p = 0.075). In the exploratory bidirectional stepwise model, MASLD remained associated with HDPs (aOR 2.99, 95% CI 1.08-8.29; p = 0.035).
CONCLUSION: MASLD was detected in 24% of women in early pregnancy. Early-pregnancy MASLD was associated with higher odds of subsequent HDPs in this cohort. Although the fully adjusted model did not demonstrate a statistically significant association, the effect estimate was approximately threefold and was similar in the exploratory stepwise model. Given the small number of HDPs events and the limitations of stepwise variable selection, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Glaucoma Severity and Progression in Individuals with Asymmetric β-zone Parapapillary Atrophy: An Intra-patient Comparative Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate inter-eye differences in glaucoma severity and progression in patients with asymmetric baseline β-zone parapapillary atrophy (PPA) morphology.
DESIGN: Retrospective, intra-patient comparative study.
PARTICIPANTS: Sixty-four eyes of 32 patients with bilateral primary open-angle glaucoma and asymmetric β-zone PPA morphology.
METHODS: Baseline β-zone PPA was quantitatively assessed using optic disc photographs. Each eye was classified according to angular extent as either Crescent type (<180°) or Solar-eclipse type (≥180°), and according to radial extent as either Short-extent type or Long-extent type. Glaucoma progression was evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts and random slopes at both the patient and eye-within-patient levels.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Rates of change in visual field mean deviation (MD), visual field index (VFI), and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness.
RESULTS: The mean age was 53.2 ± 15.6 years, and the mean follow-up duration was 11.4 ± 3.2 years. Eyes with the Solar-eclipse type demonstrated significantly faster functional progression, with greater model-estimated rates of VFI loss (-1.37 vs. -0.71 %/year; P = 0.004) and MD decline (-0.49 vs. -0.27 dB/year; P = 0.006), whereas no significant differences were observed in the rates of change in average, superior, inferior, or temporal RNFL thickness (all P ≥ 0.30). Similarly, eyes with the Long-extent type showed faster decline than those with the Short-extent type for both VFI (-1.33 vs. -0.76 %/year; P = 0.014) and MD (-0.47 vs. -0.29 dB/year; P = 0.026). In multivariable mixed-effects models, β-zone PPA angular extent was the only factor independently associated with the rate of functional progression for both MD (standardized β = -0.123; P = 0.008) and VFI (standardized β = -0.312; P = 0.022). A complementary paired inter-eye difference analysis did not reach statistical significance (all P > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this intra-individual analysis, eyes with greater angular extent of β-zone PPA showed faster functional progression, whereas structural progression did not differ. Although this association was not confirmed in a paired inter-eye difference analysis, these findings suggest that β-zone PPA angular extent may be a useful marker of future functional worsening in glaucoma.

Title: Cutaneous Effects and Aesthetic Management of Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: A Narrative Review.
Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are among the most widely prescribed medications in the United States, with expanding indications beyond type-2 diabetes mellitus to include obesity, cardiovascular risk reduction, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. As their utilization increases, the dermatologic effects of these agents become increasingly relevant to clinical practice. This narrative review examines the cutaneous effects of GLP-1RAs across six domains: facial volume loss and accelerated skin aging, changes in hair density, wound healing, striae distensae and body skin laxity, cutaneous adverse events, and emerging therapeutic benefits in inflammatory skin disease. Herein, we review proposed mechanisms and evidence-based management strategies for each domain, including biostimulatory fillers, energy-based devices, nutritional optimization, and pharmacologic interventions. Prospective, large-scale clinical studies are needed to clarify mechanisms of GLP-1RA modulation in skin and to guide management of these AEs as next-generation agents enter clinical practice.

Title: Optimal sound-color matching scheme of five-element music and lighting colors for emotional responses in patients with GAD: A randomized, two-factor mixed-design trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sound-color matching offers a novel approach to enhance music therapy, but the optimal combinations for emotional dysregulation in generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) remain untested.
OBJECTIVE: To identify the optimal sound-color matching scheme for emotional responses in GAD patients using Five-Element music and different lighting colors.
METHODS: A randomized two-factor mixed-design trial was conducted between June 2024 and February 2025 at Grade-A tertiary hospitals. Lighting color (cyan, red, yellow, white, black) was the between-subjects variable, and musical emotional valence (positive, neutral, negative) was the within-subjects variable. 210 eligible GAD patients were randomly assigned to five lighting color groups. The audiovisual stimulation combined calibrated LED lighting and validated Five-Element music segments in a standardized laboratory environment. Primary outcomes were subjective valence and arousal scores (Self-Assessment Manikin). Secondary outcomes included skin conductance (SC), skin temperature (ST), heart rate (HR), and electroencephalography (EEG) power spectral density (PSD).
RESULTS: All 210 patients were included in the subjective data analysis, with 205 providing valid physiological data and 204 yielding EEG data. Significant interactions between lighting color and music valence were observed for valence scores (F=2.02, p < 0.050), arousal scores (F=2.77, p < 0.050), ST (F=51.18, p < 0.050), and HR (F=39.77, p < 0.050). Cyan lighting with positive music produced the highest valence scores (7.79 ± 0.81) and optimal physiological regulation (lowest HR: -15.44 ± 1.89 beats per minute (bpm); highest ST: 0.84 ± 0.09°C). Red lighting with positive music induced the highest arousal (6.83 ± 1.23). EEG analysis revealed a significant interaction only in the theta band (F=1.98, P = 0.024), with positive music showing lower PSD across all bands.
CONCLUSION: Among the tested pairings, positive Five-Element music with cyan lighting elicited the most favorable immediate emotional and physiological responses in patients with GAD, supporting further investigation of sound‑color matching as a multimodal adjunctive strategy for emotional regulation.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This clinical trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (clinical trial number: ChiCTR2400079878).

Title: Cohort-specific dosimetric and delivery tradeoffs for proton dynamic arc vs. IMPT for breast and chest wall irradiation.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare proton dynamic arc therapy (DynamicArc) with conventional intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) for breast/chest wall irradiation across diverse clinical anatomies.
METHODS: Forty patients were analyzed (10/cohort): tissue expanders, permanent implants, no reconstruction, and bilateral disease. DynamicArc plans used coplanar partial arcs (150-160°) with arc retracing; paired IMPT plans used 2-4 static fields. RayStation 2023BDTK-generated plans shared contours and prescriptions (50.4 Gy[RBE]/28; subset bilateral 42.56 Gy[RBE]/16) and were robustly optimized/evaluated (±5 mm setup,±3.5% range) with Monte Carlo dose calculation (0.5%uncertainty,40000ions/spot) and a 7.5cm range shifter. Target coverage and OAR endpoints were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with FDR correction. Additionally, robustness pass rates, LETd metrics, and estimated treatment times were compared.
RESULTS: DynamicArc achieved target coverage comparable to IMPT and improved robustness pass rates for selected targets. In the expander cohort, DynamicArc improved coverage posterior to the expander port and increased coverage of the chest wall evaluation volume and nodal targets. Improved D95% was accompanied by increased target V105% in several targets. DynamicArc increased thyroid mean dose and skin V95% in multiple cohorts, although skin D2cc and skin V100% remained low. Focal hotspot metrics for the esophagus, heart, and LAD were largely unchanged, with LAD D0.03cc numerically lower though not statistically significant in the expander cohort. Ipsilateral lung V20 was generally similar, with a reduction in implant cases. Several unadjusted significant findings did not remain significant after FDR correction. High-dose CTV LETd was broadly comparable between techniques with changes in the tails of the distribution. DynamicArc increased spots, energy layers, and beam-on time, but estimated total treatment time was comparable after accounting for IMPT room entry and imaging.
CONCLUSION: DynamicArc achieved comparable target coverage with improved robustness in challenging anatomies, at the cost of increased V105%, thyroid mean dose, and skin V95% while maintaining comparable treatment times.

Title: The Prognostic Value of Entropy from T1 Mapping in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
Journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of left ventricular (LV) entropy from T1 mapping in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unexplored.
STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This prospective study enrolled patients with PAH who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) within 72h of right heart catheterization (RHC). Myocardial native T1, extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and entropy were calculated in mid-ventricular short-axis slice. The primary endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Outcomes were further analyzed across groups stratified by survival status using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 312 patients were analyzed over a median follow-up of 36.10 months, with 59 deaths. Elevated LV entropy was positively correlated with log-transformed NT-proBNP, right ventricular (RV) end-systolic, end-diastolic volume indices, LV native T1 and ECV, and inversely correlated with RV ejection fraction (all P < 0.01). LV entropy did not differ significantly across etiological subgroups, whereas LV entropy without IPs was higher in congenital heart disease-associated PAH. Both LV entropy ≥8.60 and LV entropy without IPs ≥8.30 independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR, 2.207; 95% CI, 1.324-3.678; P = 0.002; and HR, 2.357; 95% CI, 1.405-3.955; P = 0.001, respectively) and were associated with reduced survival (both log-rank P < 0.005). Adding LV entropy improved ESC models (χ²: 55.79 to 60.61, C-statistic: 0.782 to 0.801) and ESC-CMR models (χ²: 35.31 to 41.77, C-statistic: 0.805 to 0.813).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated LV entropy was related to disease severity, RV dysfunction, and adverse clinical outcomes, and served as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients with PAH.

Title: Genetic susceptibility in Takotsubo syndrome: a candidate gene association analysis in the French TAKOGENE cohort.
Abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a stress-induced left ventricular (LV) cardiomyopathy with an unclear genetic predisposition. We investigated whether single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with other cardiomyopathies or LV physiological traits contribute to TTS susceptibility. We conducted a case-control study based on the French multicentre TAKOGENE study (NCT01520610), including 261 unrelated TTS patients and 259 sex- and age-matched controls presenting with acute coronary syndrome. All participants were of European ancestry. A total of 325 SNPs were selected from large-scale genome-wide association studies of cardiomyopathies (n=202) and LV structural/functional traits (n=123), derived from polygenic risk scores. Genotyping was performed using the Infinium OmniExpressExome-8 array. Associations were assessed by logistic regression under an additive model, adjusted for age and sex, with group-specific Bonferroni correction. A sensitivity analysis compared the 261 TTS cases with 973 French population controls from the EPP3 cohort. After quality control and statistical analysis, seventeen SNPs (nine related to cardiomyopathies and eight to LV traits) showed nominal associations (P < 0.05), but none remained significant after group-specific Bonferroni correction. The strongest signal was observed for rs6885658 in the CPEB4 gene (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.23-2.15; P = 5.8 × 10-4) related to cardiomyopathy traits. The EPP3 population-control sensitivity analysis was consistent with the primary analysis, with no association remaining significant after correction. In conclusion, common genetic variants previously associated with cardiomyopathies or LV traits do not appear to have a major effect on TTS risk. These findings support a disease-specific polygenic architecture of TTS, distinct from that underlying chronic cardiomyopathies and baseline LV traits. Future studies should explore alternative approaches, such as pathway-based analyses focusing on stress-response mechanisms.

Title: More is not necessarily better: A comparison of 2-mA and 4-mA prefrontal cortex anodal tDCS on endurance performance, head oxygenation, cognition, and psychophysiological responses in cyclists.
Abstract: We evaluated the effects of 2-mA and 4-mA anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), on endurance performance, prefrontal head oxygenation, cognition, and psychophysiological responses in trained cyclists. Eighteen trained male cyclists (age: 36.0 ± 8.52 years; V̇O2max: 58.82 ± 8.16 ml·kg-1·min-1) performed 20-km time trials (TT) after receiving 20-min 2 mA, 4 mA, or sham tDCS in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. Head oxyhemoglobin (HbO2) and deoxyhemoglobin (Hbb), and cognitive performance (Stroop test) were assessed pre-tDCS, post-tDCS, and post-TT. Power output, heart rate (HR), and HbO2/Hbb were also monitored, with ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) and affective response collected during TT. The intervention was well-tolerated with successful blinding. Relative to sham, 2 mA increased average power and reduced completion time, with no difference from 4 mA; it also raised HR above both sham and 4 mA. During exercise, 2 mA raised left-hemisphere HbO2 relative to 4 mA and Hbb relative to both sham and 4 mA. The 2-mA power gain was greater with slower baseline reaction time. No condition affected cognition, RPE, or affective responses. A single session of 2 mA anodal tDCS produced small, practically relevant improvements in endurance performance relative to sham alongside intensity-dependent changes in prefrontal head oxygenation, with the largest performance benefit associated with poorer baseline cognitive performance; 4 mA did not differ from sham on either outcome.
