These findings suggest a non-monotonic intensity-response relationship, where higher intensity does not necessarily produce a larger effect.

Title: Technical and clinical feasibility of a pulmonary telerehabilitation model for people with COPD.
Journal: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate (1) the technical feasibility of transmitting data from devices connected to an application used for pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, (2) the clinical feasibility of a home-based PR (HBPR) program using an application integrating essential components of PR, and (3) exploratory clinical outcomes. (NCT05314686).
DESIGN: Prospective two-phase feasibility study.
SETTING: Single-center HBPR program.
PARTICIPANTS: Twenty participants were included in Phase 1 and 20 in Phase 2.
INTERVENTIONS: Phase 1 assessed technical feasibility during endurance sessions using a pulse oximeter and a physical activity tracker connected to the application. Phase 2 assessed clinical feasibility of an 8-week HBPR program.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Technical feasibility was assessed using the percentage of clinical agreement between locally stored and transmitted data. Clinical feasibility included retention, satisfaction, and usability. Exploratory clinical outcomes were assessed before and after the program.
RESULTS: Locally stored data and those transmitted throughout the application were similar for heart rate, transcutaneous oxygen saturation, and daily step count with a percentage of clinical agreement of at least 99%. Nineteen participants (95%) completed HBPR with high level of satisfaction (Client Satisfaction Questionnaire-8 (median 30, IQR 25 to 32)), and usability (System usability scale (median 80.0, IQR 62.5 to 100.0)). Endurance time during the constant work-rate exercise test increased following HBPR (median of paired differences 171.00 seconds, 95% CI 17.00 to 725.00).
CONCLUSIONS: Devices connected to the application can monitor patients accurately while delivering PR. The HBPR program was feasible and highly accepted by patients and their family members. Future randomized controlled studies are needed to further assess its clinical efficacy.

Title: Abnormal left ventricular mass as a prognostic marker for outcomes in infants and children with cirrhosis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality.
METHODS: 2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height)2.7(LVMI g/m2.7) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores.
RESULTS: LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m2.7, ≥ 91 g/m2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death.
CONCLUSION: LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

Title: Early pregnancy exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: A cohort study in China.
Abstract: Maternal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) has shown inconsistent associations with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). This prospective cohort study examined the associations between early pregnancy serum PFAS concentrations and HDP risk, evaluating potential effect modification by fetal sex among 2984 pregnant women in Henan Province, China (2018-2021). Sixteen PFAS were measured in early pregnancy serum samples, with nine retained for analysis based on detection rates ≥70%. Multivariable logistic regression models estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) adjusting for confounders. Of the participants, 112 (3.8%) developed gestational hypertension and 137 (4.6%) developed preeclampsia. Doubling of serum PFDoA concentration was nominally associated with increased odds of both gestational hypertension (OR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.08, 1.60) and preeclampsia (OR = 1.21; 95% CI: 1.01, 1.45). Conversely, doubling of 6:2Cl-PFESA was nominally associated with lower odds of preeclampsia (OR = 0.86; 95% CI: 0.77, 0.97). Quantile g-computation indicated that although the overall PFAS mixture was not significantly associated with HDP risk, PFDoA consistently contributed substantial positive weights to the mixture effects for both outcomes. In exploratory analyses, fetal sex appeared to modify the association between PFDoA and gestational hypertension (P-interaction = 0.035), with elevated odds observed among female fetuses (OR = 1.71; 95% CI: 1.27, 2.35) compared to male fetuses (OR = 1.07; 95% CI: 0.82, 1.39). These findings suggest congener-specific effects and sex-modulated susceptibility, indicating that early pregnancy PFDoA exposure may be associated with elevated HDP risk, warranting further investigation to validate these associations.

Title: Metagenomic and systematic analyses reveal the association between hemoglobin levels and metabolic disorders: an open cohort study of Tibetan adults in Qinghai Plateau.
Abstract:
AIM: Hemoglobin (Hb) varies with altitude, but evidence linking Hb levels to metabolic diseases in high-altitude populations remains limited. We examined associations between Hb and seven metabolic diseases in high-altitude adults and potential mediation by gut microbiota.
METHODS: We analyzed an observational cohort of 1,646 Tibetan adults from the Qinghai Plateau, stratified by Hb tertiles. Mixed-effects logistic regression and generalized additive mixed models assessed Hb-metabolic disease associations using pooled person-time data. Gut metagenomic sequencing and mediation analysis were performed on 534 fecal samples, with KEGG annotation characterizing microbial functional potential.
RESULTS: Hb correlated positively with six metabolic diseases (P < 0.05). Compared with the lowest tertile (122-151 g/L), the highest Hb tertile (169-252 g/L) showed significantly increased adjusted ORs for diabetes (10.02; 95% CI 3.00-33.43), hypertension (2.08; 1.14-3.80), hypercholesterolemia (3.04; 1.24-7.45), hypertriglyceridemia (4.66; 1.60-13.56), overweight/obesity (5.15; 1.83-14.48) and metabolic syndrome (4.58; 2.50-8.38). High Hb were associated with differences in gut microbiota β-diversity (P = 0.001) and composition. Prevotella and Collinsella were enriched in high-Hb, Bifidobacterium and Anaerostipes dominated low-Hb. Twenty-three microbial species mediated Hb-metabolic relationships. Fructose-mannose metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation were enriched in high-Hb, while ABC transporters and fatty acid biosynthesis/metabolism were upregulated in low-Hb.
CONCLUSION: Hb may serve as a useful biomarker for metabolic risk assessment in high-altitude populations, with gut microbiota potentially mediating this association.

Title: Hypertension and clinical outcomes following thoracic radiotherapy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiation therapy (RT) is highly efficacious in treating thoracic malignancies. However, RT has been linked to potential cardiotoxicity. Yet, the long-term incidence, severity, and implications of HTN-development post-RT are unknown.
METHODS: Leveraging a large US-based Comprehensive-Cancer-Center-cohort of patients treated with thoracic-RT from 2007 to 2019, we included patients ≥18 years old with histologically confirmed esophageal or lung cancers. The primary outcome was incidence of incident/new or worsened HTN [systolic-blood-pressure-(SBP) ≥130 mmHg] after RT-initiation. The secondary outcomes were major-adverse-cardiac-events (MACE- heart-failure, myocardial-infarction, arrhythmia, stroke, and sudden-death), disease-progression, and overall-survival, by HTN-status. Differences in outcomes by HTN-status were also evaluated via landmark-analysis, excluding those with undiagnosed HTN. Observed new HTN rates were compared to Framingham-predicted-rates, and absolute-excess-risks were estimated. Multivariate regression was used to define the relation between clinical and RT measures and both new or worsened HTN-development and survival-outcomes.
RESULTS: Overall, 439 RT-treated patients (238 esophageal; 201 lung; 66.7% male; mean age 63.6 years; 65% baseline HTN) were identified. Over a median follow-up of 23 months, 255 (58.1%) developed new or worsened HTN; median SBP increase of 7 mmHg. In landmark-analysis, the cumulative incidence of new or worsened HTN by 1-year was 48.0% and 63.4%, respectively. Using the JNC-8 cutoff of ≥140/90 mmHg, the new HTN rate was 21.6% at 1-year, translating to a 3.4-fold higher rate than the Framingham-predicted-rate (RR 3.37, P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, RT-dose was consistently associated with new or worsened HTN-development (P < 0.05); those with RT-induced-HTN saw improved progression-free-survival and overall-survival (HR 0.67 and 0.54, P < 0.01, respectively). Beyond traditional factors, only RT-dose is consistently associated with MACE (P < 0.05). No specific antihypertensive class prevented RT-related HTN.
CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that thoracic-RT increases early HTN risk.

Title: Obesity and Change in NT-proBNP with Angiotensin-Neprilysin Inhibition in Patients with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction and a Worsening Heart Failure Event: PARAGLIDE-HF.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the relationship between obesity status and the effect of sacubitril/valsartan (sac/val) vs valsartan (val) on change in NT-proBNP and a hierarchical outcome of clinical benefit among patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).
BACKGROUND: In the PARAGLIDE-HF trial, patients with HFpEF and a recent worsening HF event randomized to sac/val vs. val had a greater decrease in NT-proBNP over 8 weeks and showed a trend towards clinical benefit. Patients with HFpEF and obesity represent a unique population with high symptom burden and elevated risk for HF hospitalization. The efficacy and safety of sac/val in this high-risk population following a recent worsening HF event is not well characterized.
METHODS: To assess the interaction between obesity status and sac/val vs val on NT-proBNP, the time-averaged proportional change in NT-proBNP from baseline to Weeks 4 and 8 was assessed with an analysis of covariance model that included the interaction of treatment-by-BMI group (obese with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 vs not obese with BMI 18.5 to <30 kg/m2). A win ratio consisting of a hierarchy of cardiovascular death, total HF hospitalizations, urgent HF visits, and change in NT-proBNP was calculated for both BMI groups.
RESULTS: Overall, 65% (n=298) of participants had obesity and 35% (n=164) of participants did not have obesity. When the interaction between BMI category and the effect of sac/val vs val on the time-averaged proportional change from baseline NT-proBNP was assessed, participants with obesity had a numerically larger decrease in NT-proBNP (ratio of change 0.82 (95% CI 0.68 to 0.99) with obesity vs 0.96 (95% CI 0.71 to 1.29) without obesity that was not statistically significant, p interaction 0.37. Participants with obesity were significantly more likely to derive benefit overall from sac/val vs val as compared to participants without obesity (win ratio 1.38, 95% CI 1.01-1.90 vs 0.90, 95% CI 0.62-1.32, p-interaction = 0.09).
CONCLUSION: In this prespecified secondary analysis of PARAGLIDE-HF, patients with HFpEF and obesity had a similar magnitude of decrease in NT-proBNP with randomization to sac/val vs val, but may derive greater clinical benefit as assessed by a win ratio. This hypothesis-generating evidence suggests that patients that patients with obesity and HFpEF may particularly benefit from sac/val.

Title: Real-World Adoption and Associated Outcomes of Aspirin Avoidance After HeartMate 3 Implantation: The PRAISE HM3 Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: ARIES-HM3 (Antiplatelet Removal and Hemocompatibility Events With the HeartMate 3 Pump) demonstrated that aspirin can be safely omitted after HeartMate 3 (HM3) implantation when vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation is continued, resulting in reduced nonsurgical bleeding without an increased risk of thromboembolic events. The pace, extent, and pattern of adoption in clinical practice, and whether real-world outcomes after adoption are consistent with the trial, remain uncertain.
METHODS: Using the Truveta electronic health record network (30 US health systems), we identified adults undergoing de novo durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation with documented warfarin therapy from January 2016 through March 2026. Recorded early aspirin use was defined as an aspirin administration, dispense, or active order on postoperative days 2-7. Temporal trends were examined relative to ARIES-HM3 publication (November 2023) and the US Food and Drug Administration labeling revision (August 2024). Among HM3 recipients implanted after ARIES-HM3 publication and event-free at a postoperative day 14 landmark, the 12-month composite of death or first major nonsurgical hemocompatibility-related adverse event was compared using Kaplan-Meier methods and sequentially adjusted Cox regression.
RESULTS: In the overall LVAD cohort (n = 3365), recorded aspirin use declined from 90.2% in 2023 to 55.7% in 2024 and 52.7% in 2025. Of 739 post-ARIES HM3 recipients, 404 (54.7%) had recorded early aspirin use. Aspirin was continued in 67.1% of patients with prior percutaneous coronary intervention, coronary artery bypass grafting, stroke, or peripheral vascular disease vs 43.4% of those without. The 12-month composite end point occurred in 29.3% of patients with and 21.7% without recorded aspirin (unadjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.70, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.51-0.94); after multivariable adjustment, no significant association remained (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.61-1.22). Major nonsurgical bleeding occurred in 22.0% and 15.0% of patients, respectively (unadjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.45-0.94; adjusted HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.54-1.26). Stroke (4.7% vs 2.7%) and peripheral arterial thromboembolism (4.3% vs 2.6%) were not more frequent without aspirin; pump thrombosis was rare (2 events vs 3 events).
CONCLUSIONS: After ARIES-HM3 publication and the US Food and Drug Administration labeling revision, aspirin use in HM3 LVAD implantation declined substantially but persisted in approximately one-half of recipients, most often in those with established vascular disease, the population in which ARIES-HM3 showed preserved safety and a numerically greater bleeding reduction with aspirin avoidance. In this observational analysis, aspirin avoidance was not associated with a higher adjusted risk of the composite outcome, and no excess of stroke or arterial thromboembolism was observed.

Title: Effectiveness and safety of target-specific RNA-based lipid-lowering therapies: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
Abstract: RNA-based therapies target distinct pathways involved in lipid metabolism and may therefore exhibit differential pharmacological effects according to their molecular targets. However, comparative evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of these target-specific therapies remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of PCSK9-, APOC3-, and ANGPTL3-targeting RNA-based therapies in patients with hyperlipidemia or hypertriglyceridemia. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing inclisiran, olezarsen, plozasiran, or zodasiran with placebo. Treatment effects were expressed as mean differences (MDs) or risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and pooled analyses were stratified according to molecular target. Sixteen randomized controlled trials involving 5604 participants were included. PCSK9-targeting therapy produced the greatest reductions in LDL-C (MD -53.01%, 95% CI -57.56 to -48.45), ApoB (MD -39.59%, 95% CI -43.33 to -35.85), and non-HDL-C (MD -44.62%, 95% CI -47.73 to -41.51), whereas APOC3-targeting therapies produced the greatest reduction in triglycerides (MD -52.26%, 95% CI -56.50 to -48.02). Total adverse events, serious adverse events, and adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were comparable between RNA-based therapies and placebo. Overall, these findings indicate that RNA-based lipid-lowering therapies exhibit target-specific pharmacological effects, with PCSK9 inhibition predominantly reducing atherogenic lipoproteins and APOC3 inhibition producing greater triglyceride lowering. Although the overall safety profile was comparable with placebo, differences in individual adverse outcomes and the limited availability of long-term clinical outcome data highlight the need for further investigation.

Title: Edible fungus polysaccharides and metabolism: A review.
Abstract: Metabolic disorders constitute a severe global health challenge, with dietary intervention serving as a cornerstone of prevention and treatment. As primary bioactive macromolecules isolated from edible fungus, Edible Fungus Polysaccharides (EFPs) possess a broad spectrum of physiological activities. This review consolidates recent progress surrounding EFPs, encompassing extraction techniques, structural features, gut microbiota-driven biotransformation within the body, and how these compounds help sustain metabolic homeostasis. EFPs tune glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism through crosstalking signaling cascades, while systemic benefits arise from immunoregulation, anti-inflammatory properties, and signaling communication along the microbiota-gut-brain axis. EFPs have shown promising effects in the treatment of metabolic syndrome, obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and metabolism-associated malignancies. Existing evidence varies considerably by disease setting. While certain data support the use of EFPs as auxiliary reagents in tumor treatment, solid clinical evidence targeting metabolic complications remains largely lacking. Most relevant observations stem from cell cultures and animal experiments. Available clinical datasets focusing on metabolic outcomes tend to be small, short-duration and geographically limited, restricting broader extrapolation. EFPs hold great research potential as preclinical agents to support metabolic wellness, yet efforts to translate these findings into treatments for metabolic disease remain preliminary. Progress toward practical clinical use hinges on conclusive data from large randomized controlled trials, prolonged toxicology evaluation, and comprehensive pharmacokinetic characterization. Such work will lay the groundwork to define consistent safety benchmarks, therapeutic efficacy and suitable dosage protocols.

Title: Usefulness of serum amyloid A to differentiate feline inflammatory lower respiratory tract diseases from cardiac or neoplastic disease: a retrospective study of 22 cats (2021-2024).
Journal: The Journal of small animal practice
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the usefulness of serum amyloid A concentration in differentiating inflammatory lower respiratory tract diseases from cardiac/neoplastic respiratory diseases in cats.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of medical records of cats presented between 2021 and 2024 to a single referral centre was performed. Cats in respiratory distress with serum amyloid A assay performed within 48 hours after admission were included and divided into two groups (inflammatory and cardiac/neoplastic). The inflammatory group included infectious or non-infectious inflammatory lower respiratory tract diseases, and the cardiac/neoplastic group was subdivided into cardiac and neoplastic subgroups. Signalment, clinical signs and diagnostic testing results, including serum amyloid A concentration, were recorded and compared between groups (P < .05).
RESULTS: Twenty-two cats were included. Median serum amyloid A concentration was significantly higher in the inflammatory group (57.5 μg/mL (12.2 to 70.3); n = 15) compared to the cardiac/neoplastic group (5 μg/mL (5); n = 7; P = .003). There was also a significant difference among the inflammatory, cardiac (5 μg/mL (5); n = 3) and N (5 μg/mL (5); n = 4) subgroups (P = .01); however, pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant. The optimal serum amyloid A concentration cut-off to differentiate between inflammatory and cardiac/neoplastic groups was 8.6 μg/mL (sensitivity of 80% (95% confidence interval: 59.5 to 91.6) and specificity of 100% (95% confidence interval: 84.6 to 100)).
CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Cardiac and neoplastic diseases were associated with low serum amyloid A concentration. Serum amyloid A concentration could be a potential diagnostic tool but larger studies are needed to validate the proposed cut-off value. Further prospective studies are also needed to establish the usefulness of serum amyloid A concentration in distinguishing between infectious and non-infectious inflammatory diseases.

Title: Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study.
Abstract:
AIMS: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences.
CONCLUSION: Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

Title: A 12-week randomized controlled trial of the dietary approaches to stop hypertension (DASH) diet in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis: Effects on disease activity and outcomes.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Dietary interventions may improve rheumatoid arthritis (RA) outcomes through anti-inflammatory and metabolic pathways. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet on disease activity and treatment outcomes in patients with seropositive RA.
METHODS: In this 12-week parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 82 patients with seropositive RA were randomly assigned to a DASH diet intervention (n = 40) or a control group maintaining their usual diet (n = 42). The primary outcome was change in disease activity assessed using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS-28 E SR). Secondary outcomes included change in DAS-28 based on C-reactive protein (DAS-28 CRP), as well as tender and swollen joint counts, ESR, CRP, visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for pain and general health, the Health Assessment Questionnaire (HAQ), and the Short Form-36 (SF-36). Adherence to the intervention was evaluated using the DASH diet score. Assessments were performed at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Data were analyzed according to the intention-to-treat principle. Repeated clinical outcomes were analyzed using robust mixed ANOVA or generalized estimating equations (GEE), as appropriate.
RESULTS: Of the 82 randomized patients, 49 completed the 12-week study. Adherence to the DASH diet increased significantly in the intervention group compared with the control group (p < 0.001). From baseline to Week 12, DAS-28 ESR decreased by 0.92 points in the DASH group versus 0.17 points in the control group, corresponding to a 0.75-point greater reduction (group × time interaction, p = 0.001). Significant between-group differences in change were also observed for DAS-28 CRP (-0.62), ESR (-3.90 mm/h), VAS-pain (-2.19), VAS-general health (-2.12), and HAQ (-0.38) (all group × time p˂0.05). For SF-36, significant between-group differences in change were observed for physical functioning (+10.15), role-physical (+47.30), bodily pain (+22.17), vitality (+18.52), role-emotional (+38.61), and mental health (+12.06) (all group × time p < 0.05). CRP, tender and swollen joint counts did not show significant group × time interactions (p > 0.05). Furthermore, in the intervention group, improvements in DASH diet adherence were negatively correlated with changes in DAS-28 ESR and DAS-28 CRP scores (both p < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: A 12-week DASH dietary intervention may provide clinically meaningful improvements in disease activity and patient-reported outcomes in patients with seropositive RA. These findings support the potential role of the DASH dietary pattern as a promising dietary approach to complement the management of RA. However, the relatively high attrition rate should be considered when interpreting the findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered with Clinicaltrials.gov (ID: NCT07170033). https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07170033.

Title: Long-term functional outcome after post-anoxic brain injury: model development and internal validation from a multicentre cohort.
Journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: To identify biomarkers of long-term functional recovery after cardiac arrest (CA).
METHODS: This is a prospective longitudinal cohort study based on the Veneto Registry of CA (July 2021- June 2023). We collected demographic, clinical, biochemical, and electroencephalography and short- and middle-latencysomatosensory-evoked-potentials (S-SSEP and ML-SSEP) within 72 hours. Functional scales were collected at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months after the event. Multiple imputation was used to avoid statistical loss. Calibration was verified. A penalised logistic regression and a penalised continuation ratio were fitted to model the effect of covariates. The quality of prediction or fitting was verified computing the rank probability score for ordinal outcomes, the Brier score, and area under the ROC curve for binary outcomes. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical utility.
RESULTS: We included 160 persons (mean 62.80 ± SD 14.36 years; 123 males) out of 186. The interaction between continuous/nearly continuous EEG and N20/P25 predictor of survival (β = 0.840) and recovery (β = 1.160) of consciousness at 12 months after CA. ML-SSEP was a predictor of good outcome on all scales at 12 months after CA (0.739<β <1.708).
CONCLUSION: ML-SSEPs associated with standard neurophysiological assessments are robust predictors of long-term functional outcomes after CA.
SIGNIFICANCE: ML-SSEPs associated with EEG and standard SSEP might be incorporated in routine clinical practice in ICU post-anoxic coma assessment.

Title: Validating ECG-Based Artificial Intelligence Models for Cardiomyopathy Detection in Obstetric Patients: A Multisite International Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy significantly impacts maternal health worldwide. Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiograms (AI-ECG) have shown effectiveness in detecting left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) in adults and limited obstetric cohorts; however, broad validation in diverse obstetric populations remains unexplored.
OBJECTIVES: Our primary objective was to validate the performance of 2 versions of an AI-ECG model for detecting cardiomyopathy in an international obstetric cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multisite study of pregnant or postpartum women (≤12 months) across 11 institutions in 4 countries (Israel, Nigeria, Pakistan, and the United States). Two AI-ECG models (Food and Drug Administration-cleared v2.5.0 and refined v3.0.0) were evaluated against echocardiography. LVSD was defined as left ventricular ejection fraction ≤40% in keeping with the model's training target. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUROC).
RESULTS: We included 1,820 women with paired ECG-echocardiogram data, of whom 7.3% had LVSD. Model 1 (v2.5.0) demonstrated strong discriminative performance with an AUROC of 0.865, sensitivity of 46.1%, and negative predictive value of 95.8%. Model 2 (v3.0.0) showed significantly improved performance, with an AUROC of 0.925, sensitivity of 64.1%, and negative predictive value of 97.2% (P < 0.001) for LVSD detection.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-ECG models demonstrated strong external validity in a global obstetric cohort, with significantly improved performance in the refined model trained on expanded data. These findings support the potential role of AI-ECG for a scalable LVSD screening tool in obstetric populations, while underscoring the importance of population-specific validation prior to clinical implementation.

Title: Improvised cardiac function of siddha formulation Sikkanjar elixir® through CAMK2 and VEGF mechanism-in experimentally induced cardiac hypertrophy model in rats.
Journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sikkanjar elixir® (SE) contains 29 herbs, honey and fermented rice water. It is a modified and fortified form of Sikkanjar Manappagu (Manappagu means syrup), a Siddha traditional medicine. SE has its reference to treat vascular block, high cholesterol, varicose vein, hypertension; improved cardiac efficiency and blood circulation. However, the validation of Siddha claim of SE has not been carried out in experimentally conditions.
OBJECTIVE: The present study designed to validate the scientific claim of SE and investigate the cardio-protective prospective of SE, in a rat model of cardiac hypertrophy (CH).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: CH was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats via ligation of the descending abdominal aorta. The cardio-protective effects of SE were evaluated through behavioral assessments, biochemical parameters, antioxidant profiling, liver and kidney function tests, ATP, troponin I levels measurement. The cardiac hypertrophy markers like CAMK2, VEGF, and SIRT3 expression were measured through qRTPCR.
RESULTS: HPTLC evaluation of SE denotes 1.221 mg RUE/g and 4.604 mg GAE/g, of total flavonoid and phenolics content respectively. CH induction led to elevated heart rate, troponin I, and liver/kidney function markers, along with decreased plasma glucose, cholesterol, tissue ATP, catalase, glutathione, and VEGF levels. SE treatment significantly reversed these changes, as evidenced by reduced heart rate, normalization of biochemical markers, and improved antioxidant status. Notably, SE treatment suppressed CAMK2 expression and upregulated VEGF, suggesting enhanced myocardial contractility. Histopathological analysis further supported these findings, showing reduced myocyte fibre thickness and septal volume.
CONCLUSION: SE reversed the CH induced pathology through restoration of cardiac pumping efficiency (ejection fraction) via CAMK2 and VEGF mechanism. Normalization of cardiac output might contribute to the recovery of kidney, metabolic functions and promotion of anti-oxidant effect. These observations can also be extrapolated in CCF or MI conditions in clinical situations.

Title: Incremental prognostic value of left atrial minimum volume index and late gadolinium enhancement in acute myocardial infarction patients with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤35.
Abstract:
AIM: Patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤35% are at high risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). The left atrial minimum volume index (LAVImin) and late gadolinium enhancement of the left ventricular myocardium (LGE) have each been reported as stand-alone predictors, but their combined risk stratification and incremental prognostic value in this specific population remains unclear.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-centre study included 338 patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% (training cohort, n = 235; external validation cohort, n = 103) imaged by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) between January 2014 and October 2024. Two blinded radiologists quantified LAVImin, LGE, and other CMR parameters. Cox regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis evaluated the separate and combined prognostic value of LAVImin and LGE. Five nested prediction models were developed and validated internally and externally.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 37 months, 55 of 235 training cohort patients (23.4%) experienced MACE. Patients with LAVImin ≥20.4 mL/m2 and LGE ≥29.5% had the poorest MACE-free survival (log-rank P < .001). The model combining clinical factors, conventional CMR risk factors, LAVImin and LGE (Model 5) discriminated best (apparent Harrell C statistic 0.77, optimism-corrected 0.73; external validation 0.78, calibration slope 0.96) and improved modestly but significantly on the conventional CMR model (Model 2; likelihood ratio P < .001, ΔAUC = 0.051, P = .04).
CONCLUSION: In patients with AMI and LVEF ≤35% who underwent CMR, combined LAVImin and LGE enable survival risk stratification and provide modest but significant incremental prognostic value for MACE.

Title: Biopsychological burden phenotypes and cognitive performance in older Chinese and U.S. adults: an observational study using CHARLS and NHANES.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on combined physiological-psychological burden phenotypes and cognition in older adults remains limited. We examined cross-sectional associations of burden phenotypes with global cognition and memory using CHARLS and NHANES.
METHODS: Adults aged ≥60 years from CHARLS 2011 and NHANES 2011-2014 were included. A physiological dysregulation index incorporated cardiovascular, metabolic, inflammatory, and renal indicators; depressive symptoms were assessed using CES-D-10 in CHARLS and PHQ-9 in NHANES. Participants were classified as low burden, physiological burden, depressive symptoms, or dual burden. Survey-weighted regression, fixed-effect synthesis, and sensitivity analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Complete phenotype data were available for 3977 CHARLS and 2558 NHANES participants. Physiological burden predominated in CHARLS, whereas low and physiological burden predominated in NHANES. In NHANES, dual burden was associated with lower global cognition and memory. In CHARLS, corresponding estimates were negative but statistically inconclusive. Fixed-effect synthesis showed associations of dual burden with poorer global cognition (β = -0.24, 95% CI: -0.34 to -0.14) and memory (β = -0.17, 95% CI: -0.28 to -0.07). These pooled estimates were considered supportive rather than definitive because only two datasets were available and measurements differed between cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Burden phenotype distributions differed between older Chinese and U.S. adults. Dual burden was cross-sectionally associated with poorer cognitive performance, although association strength and precision varied by cohort. These findings support joint consideration of physiological dysregulation and depressive symptoms, but do not establish temporal or causal relationships.

Title: Development and Validation of a Blood Test Informed Risk Prediction Model for Lung Cancer-The Copenhagen Lung Cancer Risk Model (CPH-Lung).
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Lung cancer screening reduces lung cancer mortality, but identifying high-risk individuals remains difficult. We wanted to develop a blood test-based risk model (CPH-Lung) to improve risk stratification before image-based screening.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included individuals from two prospective general population cohorts to model 6-year lung cancer risk; the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) for training and the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS) for validation. We analyzed clinical and biochemical variables from ever-smokers (689 cases and 1,924 controls) nested within CGPS to train a 6-year lung cancer risk model. CPH-Lung was validated in a cohort of ever-smokers age ≥50 years in the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS, 3,195 individuals) and compared with the validated PLCOm2012 model.
RESULTS: There were 689 and 68 events of 6-year lung cancer in the CGPS and the CCHS. In the CCHS validation study, the CPH-Lung versus the PLCOm2012 yielded AUCs of 0.783 (95% CI, 0.731 to 0.835) versus 0.720 (95% CI, 0.669 to 0.770) for detection of all 6-year lung cancers (P = .0059). The discrimination was similar in the CGPS. At specificity of 77.7% (as would have been achieved using currently applied screening criteria, eg, NELSON or NLST), sensitivities were 57.6% versus 39.2% in women (P < .0001) and 61.4% versus 54.7% in men (P = .004) for CPH-Lung versus PLCOm2012. The mean age at diagnosis was 68.2 years (standard deviation [SD], 7.50) in the 120 individuals with lung cancer predicted exclusively by CPH-Lung compared with 76.5 years (SD, 8.04) in the 37 individuals predicted exclusively by PLCOm2012 (P < .0001).
CONCLUSION: After inclusion of blood test information, the CPH-Lung model was more sensitive in the Danish population than PLCOm2012 for prediction of 6-year lung cancer risk particularly among women and younger individuals.

Title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.
METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.
RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.
CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

Title: Beyond the Average Patient: The Ergodicity Problem in Evidence-Based Medicine and a Proposal for Individual-Dynamic Medicine.
Journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
Abstract:
RATIONALE: Evidence-based medicine (EBM) replaced authority with appraisal and has reduced harm. Its own methodologists have documented a persistent gap between what its methods conclude and what its practice does: average effects that are marginal for most treated patients, guidelines that misfit the individual, widespread difficulty converting relative into absolute effects, and no built-in trigger for stopping a treatment that is not helping.
AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: To identify a common source of these problems in the application of population-level estimates to individuals, and to propose a framework that corrects it without abandoning controlled evidence.
METHODS: Conceptual and critical analysis drawing on the methodological critique of EBM published by its founders and leading epidemiologists; the theory of ergodicity in dynamical systems and its empirical tests; the reference class problem; and existing clinical existence proofs of individual-level measurement and closed-loop intervention.
RESULTS: The assumption that a population estimate applies to an individual is the ergodic assumption, which holds when a process is homogeneous across persons and stationary over time. Homogeneity fails whenever treatment response differs between people, which is common; where an individual's responses are reproducible, individual-level inference is both necessary and feasible. Large within-person variability weakens every inference and must be measured rather than assumed away. The N-of-1 randomised trial, which estimates an effect in the individual, was published by Guyatt and Sackett in 1986 and ranks at Level 1 of the Oxford 2011 Levels of Evidence, yet a systematic review found 108 published trials in twenty-five years.
CONCLUSIONS: I propose Individual-Dynamic Medicine, a biocybernetic framework of six principles, each with an existence proof in mainstream medicine, specifying how population evidence and within-person trials divide the work of an individual decision, and state its assumptions, limitations, and the predictions on which it could fail.

Title: Changes in Macular Area Following Epiretinal Membrane Removal and Its Correlation With Anatomical and Functional Parameters.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate changes in macular area after pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with epiretinal membrane (ERM) peeling and determine correlations with visual acuity (VA) and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-based anatomical parameters.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 29 eyes with idiopathic ERM undergoing PPV and membrane peeling. Macular area was quantified using infrared images at baseline and 7 to 9 days, and 30 days and 3 months postoperatively. OCT parameters-including central macular thickness (CMT), inner retinal thickness (IRT), macular volume, disorganization of retinal inner layers (DRIL), and ellipsoid zone (EZ) status-were analyzed. Correlations between macular area change, VA (logMAR), and OCT parameters were assessed.
RESULTS: Macular area significantly increased from 37.59 ± 11.67 mm2 to 42.77 ± 10.92 mm3 at 3 months (P < .001). VA improved from 0.48 ± 0.19 to 0.20 ± 0.17 (P < .001). CMT decreased from 508.68 ± 74.01 µm to 395.03 ± 63.62 µm (P < .001). DRIL decreased from 82.8% to 31%. EZ disruption decreased from 37.9% to 17.2%; however, this change did not reach statistical significance (exact McNemar P = .070). Macular area change was not significantly correlated with visual acuity improvement at 3 months (r = 0.081, P = .758), although macular area at 3 months was negatively correlated with CMT (r = -0.560, P = .016).
CONCLUSION: Macular area expansion after ERM peeling appears to reflect structural recovery following release of retinal traction. Although some associations with visual outcomes were observed, independent prognostic value remains uncertain and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

Title: Correction to: Infective Endocarditis: Diagnosis, Antibiotic Therapy, and Management: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
Prolonged Donor Warm Ischemia in Pure Laparoscopic Donor Right Hepatectomy Is Associated With Increased Recipient Biliary Stricture Risk: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pure laparoscopic donor right hepatectomy has been increasingly adopted because of its minimally invasive nature and established donor safety. However, its impact on recipient biliary complications remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate biliary outcomes after pure laparoscopic donor right hepatectomy using accumulated single-surgeon experience and assess the effect of donor warm ischemic time (DWIT).
METHODS: We reviewed 264 living donor liver transplantations performed by a single surgeon between 2011 and 2023. Donor hepatectomies were categorized as open (group O; n = 103) or laparoscopic, which was subdivided into early (group EL; n = 49) and late (group LL; n = 112) periods. All recipients were ABO-compatible, underwent duct-to-duct reconstruction, and were followed up for ≥1 y. DWIT was defined as the interval between hepatic artery ligation and cold perfusion. The primary outcome was biliary strictures requiring intervention.
RESULTS: Biliary stricture-free survival did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.278). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified a DWIT cutoff of 12.5 min as a potential reference point for increased biliary stricture risk (area under the curve, 0.543; P = 0.043). In the multivariate analysis, DWIT ≥13 min was an independent predictor (hazard ratio, 1.88; P = 0.020).
CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged DWIT appears to increase the risk of recipient biliary strictures, suggesting that minimizing DWIT in laparoscopic donor hepatectomy could help optimize outcomes.

Title: Comparative effectiveness of amlodipine versus nifedipine prescribed at discharge in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack: A nationwide 5-year follow-up registry study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amlodipine and nifedipine are the most commonly prescribed calcium channel blockers (CCB) for patients suffering from ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). Nevertheless, there is a scarcity of direct comparative evidence on their effectiveness. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of amlodipine and nifedipine in patients with ischemic stroke or TIA.
METHODS AND FINDINGS: This observational study was based on the Third China National Stroke Registry, which recruited consecutive adult patients with ischemic stroke or TIA from 2015 to 2018. In this study, ischemic stroke or TIA patients were prescribed either amlodipine or nifedipine at discharge. The primary outcome was the distribution of modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, which assesses functional outcomes in patients with stroke, at 5 years. The intergroup differences were examined using ordinal logistic regression, yielding odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Patient age, gender, body mass index, systolic blood pressure at admission, and onset date were adjusted. To improve baseline characteristic balance, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was implemented. A total of 2,859 eligible patients were included, and there were 1847 patients in the amlodipine group and 1,058 patients in the nifedipine group after IPTW. The amlodipine group demonstrated significantly lower 5-year mRS scores in comparison to the nifedipine group, with an OR of 0.76 (95% CI [0.65, 0.89]; p < 0.001). A total of 956 (51.76%) amlodipine users and 632 (59.74%) nifedipine users achieved a mRS score > 0 at 5 years, with an OR of 0.71 (95% CI [0.61, 0.83]; p < 0.001). The sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. The main limitations include the inherent observational design, the exclusive reliance on registry data, and relatively high loss-to-follow-up rate at 5 years.
CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that amlodipine, compared to nifedipine, may be associated with improved functional recovery in ischemic stroke or TIA patients. Randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and refine CCB therapy.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Observational Study; Comparative Study

Title: Updated Guidelines for the Management of Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration by the European Society of Retina Specialists.
Journal: Ophthalmologica. Journal international d'ophtalmologie. International journal of ophthalmology. Zeitschrift fur Augenheilkunde
Abstract: Since the publication in 2014 of the original EURETINA guidelines for the management of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), the treatment landscape for this prevalent and potentially devastating condition has evolved substantially. Along with the introduction of new anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents and the release of biosimilar agents, anti-VEGF dosing strategies have been refined, and increasing amounts of clinical trial and real-world evidence are available to inform practice. To provide an updated European perspective on nAMD management, the EURETINA panel systematically reviewed European guidelines published since 2014 alongside recent randomized controlled trials and other relevant evidence. Areas of broad consensus across guidelines were identified, including the importance of early diagnosis and prompt initiation of anti-VEGF therapy, and the central role of optical coherence tomography (OCT) in both diagnosis and monitoring. Treat-and-extend regimens are now established as the preferred approach for retreatment, with disease activity defined primarily by changes in retinal fluid accumulation detected by OCT imaging. Recommendations also address follow-up, switching or discontinuing therapy, and referral to low vision support services. Incorporating the EURETINA panel's expertise into this synthesis, this update to the EURETINA guidelines for nAMD provides recommendations to guide high-quality, evidence-based care for patients with nAMD across Europe.

Title: A machine learning model for in-hospital mortality prediction in patients with sepsis-related myocardial injury.
Abstract: Sepsis-related myocardial injury (SRMI) is associated with high mortality, but the transportability of prediction models across heterogeneous cohorts remains uncertain. We developed and externally validated a machine learning model for in-hospital mortality prediction in SRMI and evaluated its discrimination, calibration, interpretability, and distributional shift across cohorts. Using MIMIC-IV for development and MIMIC-III and a local cohort for external validation (n = 1,226, 962, and 280, respectively), we compared eight classification algorithms. A two-stage feature-selection strategy, recursive feature accumulation and sequential elimination with incremental feature evaluation, ranked 31 candidate variables to derive a parsimonious predictor set. The selected model was evaluated for discrimination, precision-recall performance, calibration, clinical utility, and risk stratification. Logistic recalibration, population stability index (PSI) analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to assess probability alignment, cross-cohort distributional shift, and model interpretability. Feature selection reduced 31 candidate variables to 8 predictors with little loss of cross-validated performance (AUC, 0.819 with 31 variables versus 0.810 with 8 variables). The selected random forest model achieved an AUC of 0.819 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.787-0.848) and a PR-AUC of 0.702 (0.657-0.751) in MIMIC-III, and an AUC of 0.758 (0.693-0.816) and a PR-AUC of 0.525 (0.435-0.630) in the local cohort. Recalibration reduced the Brier score from 0.162 to 0.147 in MIMIC-III and from 0.233 to 0.196 in the local cohort. PSI indicated minimal distributional shift between MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-III but substantial shift in the local cohort, particularly for SOFA score, respiratory rate, and prothrombin time. SHAP identified prothrombin time, invasive ventilation, lactate, temperature, and urine output as major contributors to model predictions. In two external cohorts, an 8-variable random forest model showed moderate discrimination for mortality prediction in SRMI. The evaluation of external performance, calibration, distributional shift, and SHAP-based explanations provides an assessment of model transportability. Prospective validation is needed before clinical deployment.

Title: Perceived Stress, Sleep Quality, and Their Impact on Glycemic Control among Type 2 Diabetes Patients in Riyadh: Cross-Sectional Evidence.
Journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between perceived stress and sleep quality with glycemic blood levels in T2DM patients in Riyadh.
SUBJECT AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study evaluated a total of 309 patients diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The study comprised an initial validation and Arabic translation phase involving 160 participants, followed by an analytical phase focusing on 149 adult patients. To investigate the impact of psychosocial and metabolic factors on glycemic control (hemoglobin A1c [HbA1c]), data were collected using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), alongside clinical metrics such as body mass index (BMI) and dyslipidemia extracted from medical records. A multivariable linear regression model was utilized to identify independent factors associated with glycemic regulation within the local population.
RESULTS: The multivariable regression model demonstrated robust explanatory power (adjusted R2 = 0.726, p < 0.001). Traditional risk factors, specifically elevated BMI (β = 0.448, p < 0.001) and dyslipidemia (β = 0.304, p < 0.001), were significantly associated with higher HbA1c levels. Notably, poor sleep quality emerged as a significant independent factor associated with elevated HbA1c (β = 0.261, p < 0.001), whereas perceived stress did not exhibit a significant correlation. Conversely, physical activity demonstrated a significant protective effect, correlating with lower HbA1c (β = -0.271, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Poor sleep quality, rather than perceived psychological stress, is a primary factor independently associated with hyperglycemia in this patient cohort. These findings suggest that standard diabetes care should integrate formal sleep assessments alongside patient care management.

Title: Quantitative assessment of myocardial dysfunction in mild focal left ventricular hypertrophy using CMR feature tracking.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate cardiac dysfunction in patients with mild focal left ventricular hypertrophy (MF-LVH) by analyzing the left ventricular (LV) and left atrial (LA) deformation parameters derived from cardiac magnetic resonance feature tracking (CMR-FT).
METHODS: This retrospective study included 36 patients with MF-LVH, 44 patients with HCM without late gadolinium enhancement (HCM-non-LGE), and 32 healthy controls who were examined between November 2020 and August 2025. The LA and LV strain parameters were obtained using CMR-FT. Statistical comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were conducted.
RESULTS: While conventional parameters showed no difference, all global LV strains and most strain rate parameters were significantly impaired in both patient groups, showing a stepwise decline with advancing hypertrophy severity. In multivariable analyses, the peak diastolic radial strain rate (PD-RSR) was the primary discriminator distinguishing MF-LVH from controls, and LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) was the key discriminator differentiating MF-LVH from HCM-non-LGE. LV-GLS and LA minimal volume index (LAVImin) were the key discriminators for HCM-non-LGE versus controls. ROC analysis confirmed LV-GLS as an excellent discriminator (AUC 0.85 for MF-LVH vs. HCM-non-LGE; AUC 0.96 for HCM-non-LGE vs. controls), with notably similar optimal cutoff values (-13.94% and -13.99%, respectively). PD-RSR showed good accuracy in identifying MF-LVH.
CONCLUSION: PD-RSR indicates early diastolic impairment, and LV-GLS sensitively detects systolic dysfunction in patients with MF-LVH. The overlapping LV-GLS values between patients with MF-LVH and HCM-non-LGE suggest a potential pathophysiological continuum. CMR-FT enables early detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction in this population.

Title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Medical Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation is often limited by the significant risk of bleeding, and difficulties maintaining consistent adherence over time. These challenges have led to the development of left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) as an alternative stroke prevention strategy in this patient population. Our study aimed to evaluate LAAC versus medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation.
METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library from database inception through April 1, 2026. The predefined endpoints were composite outcome of systemic embolism, cardiovascular mortality, or stroke in addition to other endpoints including all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, strokes, and major bleeding. All outcomes were pooled using a random effect Mantel-Haenszel model. The between-study variance (τ2) was estimated using the Paul Mendel method, which is the preferred method when the number of included studies is small.
RESULTS: A total of five randomized controlled trials, 5,404 patients were analyzed; 2,878 underwent LAAC and 2,526 received medical therapy. The median follow-up across studies was 4 years. LAAC met noninferiority compared with medical therapy in atrial fibrillation for major bleeding (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.59-1.26) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.71-1.22). In contrast, noninferiority was not met for the composite outcome (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.64-1.47), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.51-1.42), systemic embolism (RR 1.93; 95% CI 0.21-17.5), and all stroke (RR 1.11; 95% CI 0.73-1.67).
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis showed that LAAC was noninferior to anticoagulation for all-cause mortality and major bleeding, but it did not meet noninferiority for the other assessed outcomes, including stroke, cardiovascular mortality, and/or systemic embolism.

Title: A 'First-Time-Right' strategy in secondary prevention of coronary artery disease: Rationale and design of the prospective, temporally controlled observational GOLDEN study.
Abstract: Introduction After an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or coronary revascularisation, the risk of recurrent vascular events remain substantial. Despite clear guideline recommendations, secondary prevention and long-term adherence to preventive treatment is often suboptimal. Current secondary prevention strategies typically involve initiating a limited number of pharmacologic therapies during hospitalisation, followed by sequential intensification after discharge to achieve individualized guideline-recommended targets. However, this strategy is prone to therapeutic inertia and negatively affects patient motivation and long-term adherence. We hypothesise that a 'first-time-right' strategy, where individualised, guideline-based pharmacological treatment is proactively initiated during hospitalisation, can improve risk factor control and adherence compared to current practice, and thereby reduce major cardiovascular events. Methods and analysis GOLDEN (Guided Optimisation for Long-term Disease rEduction in secoNdary Prevention of cardiovascular disease) is a prospective, temporally controlled observational cohort study aiming to include 5,586 patients hospitalised for ACS or coronary revascularisation. A guidelines-based 'first-time-right' pharmacological optimisation strategy will be compared to current practice on the 3-year incidence of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularisation (4-point MACE). This strategy targets both patients and healthcare professionals and aims to utilise the teachable moment during hospitalisation to optimise pharmacological strategies, apply key behavioural principles to improve adherence, and reframe follow-up from reactive up-titration to proactive de-escalation. A pocket card and online tool will be provided to check applicable guidelines during hospitalisation and formulate follow-up recommendations. An on-site training visit and communication aids are intended to support implementation and promote adherence. Summary This study will evaluate the effects of a 'first-time-right' strategy - focused on early in-hospital initiation and optimisation of guideline-based pharmacotherapy after acute coronary syndrome or coronary revascularisation - on the risk of recurrent MACE compared to current practice.

Title: Prospective assessment of myocardial deformation in fetuses with suspected aortic coarctation.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prenatal identification of true aortic coarctation (CoA) remains challenging as evidenced by high false-positive rates. Myocardial deformation has been proposed to improve prediction of postnatal outcome. This prospective study aimed to determine whether fetal myocardial deformation analysis can differentiate true CoA from false-positive cases throughout gestation.
METHODS: All fetuses with a prenatal suspicion of isolated CoA were prospectively recruited at our fetal cardiology services. Cases were classified as true CoA or false-positives based on their postnatal diagnosis. Speckle-tracking echocardiography was performed longitudinally to assess left and right ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), strain rate, and segmental strain throughout gestation. Measurements were compared between true CoA and false-positive cases.
RESULTS: Thirty-eight fetuses were included (19 true CoA, 19 false-positives). True CoA cases exhibited smaller left-sided cardiac dimensions, including the aortic valve (mean Z-score -3.2 vs. -1.6, p<0.001), aortic isthmus (-3.5 vs. -1.7, p=0.001), and mitral valve (-4.9 vs. -3.1, p<0.001), whereas right-sided cardiac dimensions were comparable (pulmonary valve Z-score 3.0 vs. 2.6, p=0.64; arterial duct Z-score 1.9 vs. 3.2, p=0.61). No clinically relevant differences in myocardial deformation parameters were observed between groups, with similar left ventricular GLS (-20.1% vs. -20.5%, p=0.57), right ventricular GLS (-20.0% vs. -19.1%, p=0.13), strain rates and segmental strain.
CONCLUSION: Fetal myocardial deformation analysis does not provide additional predictive value for postnatal outcome in prenatally suspected isolated CoA. Conventional assessment of cardiac dimensions and flow patterns remains the cornerstone of prenatal CoA diagnosis, yet current imaging modalities cannot provide sufficient diagnostic certainty to safely triage perinatal management.

Title: Clinical Validation of the Nursing Diagnosis "Risk for Shock" in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Admitted to the ICU.
Abstract: ObjectiveTo clinically validate the nursing diagnosis "Risk for shock" in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) admitted to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).MethodA retrospective case-control study conducted at a high-complexity university hospital in Brazil. The sample consisted of 116 medical records of adult patients with AMI, equally distributed between the case group (with cardiogenic shock; n = 58) and the control group (without cardiogenic shock; n = 58). Diagnostic accuracy measures (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios) were calculated, and multivariate binary logistic regression using the Stepwise Forward method was applied to identify independent predictors and control for confounders.ResultsIn the accuracy analysis, the indicator "Unstable blood pressure" showed the best clinical balance, with a sensitivity of 85.0% (95% CI: 76.2-93.8) and a specificity of 83.6% (95% CI: 74.4-92.8). "Hyperthermia" and "Inadequate fluid volume" showed the highest individual specificities (90.1% and 80.3%, respectively). After adjusting the logistic regression model (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.614; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.782), only four factors remained significant as independent predictors of the outcome: unstable blood pressure (aOR = 7.80; 95% CI: 3.10-19.60; p < 0.001), hypoxia (aOR = 3.70; 95% CI: 1.50-9.20; p = 0.006), hypoxemia (aOR = 2.90; 95% CI: 1.40-6.10; p = 0.004), and inadequate fluid volume (aOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.00-4.50; p = 0.048). Thermal and hemorrhagic indicators lost significance after adjustment.ConclusionThe study clinically validated the diagnosis and confirmed a robust predictive model composed of four indicators. Prioritizing the monitoring of these risk factors enables critical care nurses to anticipate hemodynamic collapse, support targeted care protocols, and optimize multiprofessional decision-making at the bedside.

Title: Semaglutide in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity: The Gap Between Discussion and Use.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Semaglutide improves symptoms and physical function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity. Whether discussion of treatment is accompanied by its use in routine care is less well understood.
METHODS: We retrospectively assessed treatment discussion, follow-up medication records and documented reasons for non-initiation in 159 patients from a prospective registry. Available follow-up information was retained when assessment dates were incompletely transcribed. Associations with registry-recorded diabetes or prediabetes were explored using Firth logistic regression.
RESULTS: Semaglutide was discussed or offered in 148/159 patients (93.1%). Among 148 baseline nonusers with subsequent medication information, it was newly recorded in 23 (15.5%). Recorded diabetes or prediabetes was associated with this outcome (adjusted odds ratio 3.76, 95% confidence interval 1.08-19.93), but a sensitivity analysis restricting the reference group by glycated haemoglobin was inconclusive. Among 125 patients without subsequently recorded semaglutide, affordability concerns were documented in 55 (44.0%), safety concerns in 48 (38.4%), and both in 38 (30.4%).
CONCLUSION: Frequent discussion of semaglutide coexisted with infrequent documentation of subsequent use. Financial and medication-related concerns commonly overlapped. These findings identify a gap in routine care without establishing its causal determinants or verifying treatment initiation.

Title: Failure of P-Wave Duration as a Surrogate Marker for Left Atrial Enlargement in African Americans: Insights from the Jackson Heart Study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electrocardiographic (ECG) criteria for left atrial enlargement (LAE) serve as clinical surrogates for structural and hemodynamic left atrial (LA) overload. Their diagnostic performance compared to echocardiography remains suboptimal, and African Americans are consistently underrepresented in relevant diagnostic accuracy studies.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of the Jackson Heart Study (JHS), a large community-based cohort of African American adults (aged 21-94 years). P-wave duration was evaluated as the index test across continuous thresholds using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). The main reference standard was echocardiographic LAE defined by American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) sex-specific left atrial (LA) two-dimensional (2D) diameter thresholds (>40 mm in men; >38 mm in women).
RESULTS: A total of 3,572 participants were included, of whom 647 (18.1%) met ASE diameter criteria for LAE. Overall discriminatory performance was poor (AUC 0.603; 95% CI 0.580-0.627). At the traditional ≥120 ms threshold, sensitivity (Sn) was 58.3% (95% CI 54.4-62.1%), specificity (Sp) was 56.8% (95% CI 55.0-58.6%), positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 1.35 (95% CI 1.25-1.46), and negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.73 (95% CI 0.67-0.81), reflecting limited capacity to rule in or out LAE.
CONCLUSION: In this cohort, P-wave duration demonstrated poor diagnostic accuracy for diameter-defined echocardiographic LAE. These findings highlight the inadequacy of this ECG criterion as a surrogate marker across a historically underrepresented population. Machine learning models may offer a path forward for higher performance of ECG as a screening tool for LAE in African Americans.

Title: Association of 24-Hour Anion Gap Difference with Short-Term Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Heart Failure and Infection.
Abstract: Introduction High anion gap (AG) indicates poor prognosis in critical illness. However, the prognostic significance of dynamic early AG changes in patients with concurrent heart failure and infection remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between the 24-hour AG difference and short-term mortality in this population. Methods This retrospective cohort study utilized the Zigong Fourth People's Hospital database. Patients with HF and infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) were included. A 24-hour landmark analysis was applied. The AG difference was categorized based on the change (ΔAG) from admission to 24 hours: Decreasing (ΔAG < -2 mmol/L), Stable (-2 to 2 mmol/L), and Increasing (ΔAG > 2 mmol/L). The primary outcome was 7-day all-cause mortality. Results A total of 299 patients were included. The 7-day mortality was 24.1%. In multivariable Cox analysis adjusted for confounders including baseline lactate and renal function, the Stable difference was significantly associated with increased 7-day mortality compared to the Decreasing group (HR 2.43, 95% CI 1.27-4.63, p=0.007). The Increasing group showed a trend toward higher risk (HR 1.74, p=0.126). Subgroup analyses revealed significant interactions, where the risk of an increasing difference was amplified in patients with hyperlactatemia (>2.0 mmol/L, HR 2.65), or renal dysfunction (eGFR <60, HR 6.27). Albumin-corrected AG sensitivity analysis confirmed these findings. Conclusion Failure to decrease the anion gap within the first 24 hours of ICU admission is associated with a higher risk of short-term mortality in patients with HF and infection. The prognostic value of AG difference is particularly pronounced in high-risk subgroups with hemodynamic or metabolic instability.

Title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time.
DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016.
RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk.
CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

Title: Response to Comments on Comparison of Analgesic Efficacy of Intrathecal Morphine and Ultrasound - Guided Bilateral Erector Spinae Plane Block in Patients Undergoing Open Heart Surgery with Midline Sternotomy: An Open Label Randomized Control Trial.
Reply to: Comment on: "A Review on the Echocardiographic Estimation of Left Ventricular Filling Pressures: From Guideline to What is in the Pipeline".
Understanding Anti-Diuretic Hormone Dynamics in Off pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (OPCABG) Patients: A Case Series.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The conundrum of Polyuria witnessed post-cardiac surgery has been attributed to altered antidiuretic hormone (ADH) release secondary to both osmotic and non-osmotic stimulus. This transient DI-like state is more often seen in on-bypass cardiac surgeries but a few off-bypass occurrences have also been reported. A lot of conflicting evidence has accumulated trying to explain this altered water balance but a broader conceptual framework is lacking, which we have attempted to provide, with an objective of designing a future prospective study.
DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS INTERVENTIONS: This prospective observational case-series included 12 cases, who underwent off pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) at a single tertiary care hospital. All were operated and managed by the same anesthetist-cardiac surgeon team following a structured protocol, hence negating various confounders. Serum and urine osmolality samples were collected post-Intubation (Baseline) and within 1 hour of ICU-transfer and all relevant data associated with these cases was recorded for analysis.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The data was systematically analyzed in terms of descriptives, paired T-test and correlation statistics. The pre-post serum osmolality was found to increase (P value 0.389, Cohen's d -0.26) whereas urine osmolality decreased significantly (P value 0.013, Cohen's d 0.85). This mean fall in urine osmolality was much higher compared to the rise seen in serum osmolality, both being negatively correlated (r -0.59, P value 0.04).
CONCLUSION: This case series investigating the changes in osmolality alongside pre-perfusion reduced urine output and post-perfusion a state of polyuria, is our primer for a future assay-based objective study. We have created a framework of concepts that provide clarity to the dynamics of ADH-release in OPCABG patients. Furthermore, we are presenting a different hypothesis to explain increase in ADH-release that is evidence-based and open to critical comments.

Title: Comparison of Effectiveness of Caudal Dexmedetomidine vs. Caudal Fentanyl with Bupivacaine during Pediatric Cardiac Surgery with regards to Hemodynamic Fluctuations and Postoperative Pain.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimum analgesia, reflecting into attenuation of stress response, is pertinent in pediatric cardiac surgery. Narcotics are still the mainstay in providing analgesia, and they are a common adjunct in caudal epidural analgesia. Unwanted effects of narcotics warrant a constant search for nonopioid analgesics.
OBJECTIVE: To compare dexmedetomidine vs. fentanyl as an adjuvant in caudal anesthesia in pediatric cardiac surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty patients, 1 to 8 years of age, with acyanotic congenital heart disease were divided into two groups randomly: group A received caudal dexmedetomidine 0.5 µg/kg with 2 mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 1.6 ml/kg with normal saline. Group B received caudal fentanyl 1 µg/kg with 2 mg/kg bupivacaine diluted to 1.6 ml/kg with normal saline.
RESULTS: Stress response assessed by surge in heart rate and blood pressure after induction was significantly lower in group A (Dexmedetomidine group). The mean time to successful discontinuation of mechanical ventilation was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group (1.2 ± 0.4 vs. 1.73 ± 0.58 h). Children in the dexmedetomidine group had lower FLACC pain scores at 4 hours postextubation (2.93 ± 1.04 vs. 3.83 ± 0.83), implying better pain control. The time to need for rescue analgesia was longer in the dexmedetomidine group (6.1 ± 1.21 vs. 3.96 ± 0.96 h).
CONCLUSION: Caudal dexmedetomidine gave better control of hemodynamic parameters when compared with fentanyl and was associated with earlier extubation postoperatively. It also has superior and prolonged analgesia compared to caudal fentanyl as an adjunct.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Comparative Study; Randomized Controlled Trial

Title: Cerebral Oxygenation-Guided Indexed-Flow Normothermic Cardiopulmonary Bypass with Vasopressor-Sparing Pressure Management: A Retrospective Descriptive Cohort Study.
Abstract:
CONTEXT: Mean arterial pressure targets during cardiopulmonary bypass remain debated; vasopressor-driven pressure augmentation may not improve oxygen delivery.
AIMS: The aim of the paper is to describe clinical outcomes and physiologic markers during normothermic cardiopulmonary bypass managed with indexed flow, cerebral oximetry, calculated indexed oxygen delivery (DO2i), and vasopressor-sparing pressure management.
SETTINGS AND DESIGN: Single-center retrospective descriptive cohort study at a cardiac surgery center.
