Title: The association between albuminuria and coronary atherosclerotic burden in the general population.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Albuminuria predicts cardiovascular events, but its association with prevalent subclinical coronary atherosclerosis is less well defined. We examined the cross-sectional relationship between urinary albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) and coronary atherosclerotic burden in middle-aged adults from Sweden nationwide.
METHODS: UACR was measured in fasting spot urine in 9424 SCAPIS participants from Uppsala and Malmö. Coronary atherosclerosis was quantified by coronary artery calcium score (CACS; n = 9277) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA; n = 9187) for stenosis. Linear regression related log(UACR) to log(CACS) with sequential adjustment: Model 1 (age, sex, ethnicity, site), Model 2 (+blood pressure, antihypertensive treatment, diabetes and antidiabetic treatment), and Model 3 (+LDL cholesterol, lipid-lowering treatment, smoking status, and eGFR). Logistic regression examined prevalent calcification (CACS>0) and stenosis; subgroup analyses excluded CKD, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and diabetes stepwise.
RESULTS: Higher UACR was associated with higher CACS in the full cohort: β = 0.21 (95% CI 0.14-0.27), 0.08 (0.01-0.15), and 0.07 (0.00-0.14) in Models 1-3, respectively. Associations persisted after excluding CKD and cardiovascular disease (n = 8448): β = 0.20 (0.13-0.27), 0.19 (0.12-0.26), and 0.07 (0.00-0.15). With further exclusions, Model 3 estimates attenuated and were non-significant (no CKD/cardiovascular disease/hypertension: β = 0.06 [-0.02 to 0.14]; additionally no diabetes: β = 0.05 [-0.03 to 0.14]). In Model 1, each log-increase in UACR was associated with higher odds of CACS>0 (OR 1.08, 95% CI 1.05-1.12) and stenosis (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.08), but associations attenuated and were non-significant in Models 2-3.
CONCLUSIONS: Albuminuria is associated with greater coronary calcification burden, including in broadly healthy individuals, supporting the concept that albuminuria may reflect vascular disease early in the cardiovascular disease continuum.

Title: Prevalence, Health Care Burden, and Longitudinal Outcomes of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Among People With Heart Failure.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are common comorbidities. We aimed to assess health care resource use and outcomes associated with COPD in patients hospitalized for HF.
METHODS: This was an exploratory cohort analysis of patients hospitalized for HF and enrolled in the Patient-Centered Care Transitions in HF cluster-randomized trial. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included all-cause and HF hospitalization, health care resource use, and direct health care costs. Survival was evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for baseline variables.
RESULTS: Among 4441 patients discharged alive, 1136 (25.6%) had COPD at baseline. All-cause mortality was higher at 5 years among patients with vs without COPD (75.2% vs 60.9%, adjusted hazard ratio 1.29, 95% confidence interval 1.19-1.40). Patients with COPD had more frequent all-cause rehospitalizations (mean [standard deviation] 3.4 [6.6] vs 2.7 [8.6] per patient, P = 0.01), but no significant difference in HF rehospitalizations (0.9 [2.3] vs 0.9 [4.5] per patient, P = 0.74). Patients with COPD had more annual physician visits, multidisciplinary clinic visits, and supportive care (all P < 0.01), as well as greater annual direct health care costs in Canadian dollars (at 5 years: $91,888 [$109,319] vs $76,823 [$116,218]) than those without COPD, primarily driven by rehospitalizations.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients discharged alive after hospitalization for HF, COPD is common and is associated with higher all-cause mortality and all-cause rehospitalizations, greater health care use, and higher direct health care costs. Interventions to reduce the health care burden in HF should include broad approaches that address important comorbidities.

Title: Effect of statins on the mortality of long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a population-based study in endemic area.
Journal: The Lancet regional health. Western Pacific
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) are at risk of excessive mortality. This territory-wide cohort study aims to investigate the relationship between statin use and mortality among 5-year survivors of NPC.
METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study conducted with data from a territory-wide registry. Patients who survived five years after being diagnosed with non-metastatic NPC in Hong Kong between 1 January 1997 and 30 December 2015 were included. Patients were divided into statin users and statin non-users. We performed the inverse propensity of treatment weighting (IPTW) method to balance confounding factors. The primary outcome of overall survival (OS) was compared between the two groups and stratified by the cause of death, statin types and duration of statin usage.
FINDINGS: 7872 subjects (2439 statin users and 5433 statin non-users) were included in the final analysis. The 10-year, 15-year, and 20-year survival probabilities of statin users compared to non-users were 89.1 vs. 71.8%, 77.2 vs. 55.1%, and 59.2 vs. 42.4% respectively (HR 0.46, p < 0.001). After adjusting for immortal time bias, the hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.71 (p < 0.001). Statin use was associated with reduced risk of death due to secondary malignancy (HR 0.51; p = 0.002), cardiovascular disease (HR 0.64; p = 0.002), and pulmonary disease (HR 0.64; p = 0.011). Mortality was significantly lower in long-term statin usage of >6 years (HR 0.31; p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, patients who received second- or third-generation statins were associated with a lower risk of mortality (HR 0.66 and HR 0.41, respectively), although this finding requires further validation.
INTERPRETATION: Our study suggests that statin usage is associated with reduced mortality in long-term NPC survivors. Further prospective study is warranted.
FUNDING: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

Title: Atorvastatin Prevents Early Lipotoxic Remodelling in Right Ventricular Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) pacing can induce metabolic and structural alterations in left ventricular (LV) myocardium, including lipid accumulation, glycogen depletion, and increased endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. This study evaluated protective effects of atorvastatin on RV pacing-induced metabolic dysfunction.
METHODS: Fifteen male Lanyu miniature pigs were randomized into sham control (n = 5), RV pacing (n = 5), and RV pacing with atorvastatin treatment (n = 5) groups. RV pacing was achieved via ventricular lead implantation at the RV outflow tract, followed by complete atrioventricular block, with ventricular pacing maintained for at least 80 beats/min in dual-chamber, dual-sensing, dual-response, rate-responsive mode to provide atrial-synchronous ventricular pacing while allowing atrial sensing or pacing. The RV pacing with atorvastatin treatment group received atorvastatin (40 mg/d) starting 2 weeks before surgery until euthanasia at 6 months. Metabolic, histologic, and molecular parameters were assessed in LV myocardial tissue.
RESULTS: Compared with sham controls, RV pacing significantly increased myocardial lipid accumulation, with higher triglyceride (2.43 ± 0.17 vs 1.74 ± 0.14 μg/mg, P < 0.01) and diacylglycerol (2902 ± 567.7 vs 977.5 ± 182.5 μg/mg, P < 0.01) levels, and significantly reduced glycogen content (0.09 ± 0.03 vs 0.21 ± 0.03 μg/mg, P < 0.05). ER stress markers binding immunoglobulin protein and cleaved caspase-9 were markedly increased in the RV pacing group (P < 0.0001). Atorvastatin significantly reduced lipid accumulation (triglycerides: 1.83 ± 0.08 μg/mg; P < 0.05), ER stress, and apoptosis, but did not significantly restore glycogen levels.
CONCLUSIONS: RV pacing induces lipid accumulation, glycogen loss, and increased ER stress in the LV myocardium. Atorvastatin partially mitigated these effects by normalizing fatty acid metabolism and reducing ER stress and apoptosis, suggesting a potential role in attenuating early/subclinical RV pacing-induced metabolic remodelling.

Title: Validation of the discriminatory performance of the iPREFACE score for clinically significant fetal acidemia: an outcome-enriched nested case-control study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiotocography is widely used for monitoring fetal well-being during labor; however, its clinical utility remains limited due to a high false-positive rate, particularly in predicting adverse neonatal outcomes such as cerebral palsy. Despite its implementation, the incidence of cerebral palsy has not decreased, whereas cesarean section rates have increased. Severe fetal acidemia has been shown to be associated with neonatal brain injury. The iPREFACE score was developed to address this limitation by evaluating the accumulation of fetal stress due to uterine contractions based on the five-tier classification of fetal heart rate (FHR) patterns defined by the Japanese Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology. Previous studies have demonstrated that the iPREFACE score significantly correlates with umbilical artery (UmA) blood gas parameters, including pH, base excess (BE), and lactate, and has a high predictive ability for fetal acidemia.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to validate the discriminatory performance of the iPREFACE score for clinically significant fetal acidemia, defined as UmA pH<7.1, using an outcome-enriched artificially balanced cohort. Secondary analyses evaluated performance at UmA pH<7.2 and <7.0, and an exploratory analysis assessed UmA pH<7.3 to examine stepwise fetal deterioration during labor.
STUDY DESIGN: A nested case-control study was conducted involving women who had full-term vaginal deliveries at a single center between January 2017 and July 2023. To construct an outcome-enriched cohort, cases with UmA pH<7.2 were matched 1:1 with randomly selected controls with UmA pH≥7.2. The iPREFACE score was calculated by summing the levels of FHR waveform patterns in the 30 minutes before delivery. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate discriminatory performance at different thresholds of UmA pH (<7.1, <7.2, <7.0, and <7.3). Correlations between the iPREFACE score and UmA blood gas parameters (pH, pCO₂, pO₂, HCO₃⁻, BE, and lactate) were assessed using linear and quadratic regression models. Bland-Altman analysis was performed to assess agreement between predicted and measured UmA pH values.
RESULTS: Of the 272 patients, 15 (5.5%) had UmA pH<7.1 and 6 (2.2%) had UmA pH<7.0. The ROC-AUC for the iPREFACE score was 0.851 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.771-0.931) for the primary outcome of UmA pH<7.1. The AUC was 0.912 (95% CI: 0.879-0.945) for UmA pH<7.2 and 0.823 (95% CI: 0.656-0.989) for UmA pH<7.0. In the exploratory analysis, the AUC for UmA pH<7.3 was 0.833. Quadratic regression analysis revealed that the iPREFACE score had the highest coefficient of determination (R²) with pH (0.415), followed by BE (0.357), pCO₂ (0.230), lactate (0.165), and HCO₃⁻ (0.106), whereas pO₂ showed a notably lower correlation (R²=0.02). Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean difference of -0.16 between predicted and measured UmA pH values, with limits of agreement from -0.41 to 0.09.
CONCLUSION: In an outcome-enriched cohort, the iPREFACE score demonstrated discriminatory performance for clinically significant fetal acidemia (UmA pH<7.1) and significant correlations with key UmA blood gas parameters, particularly pH and BE. Consistent discriminatory performance across multiple pH thresholds supports further evaluation of the iPREFACE score for stepwise assessment of progressive fetal deterioration during labor.

Title: Blood lead exposure, renal hyperfiltration, and accelerated kidney function decline among people living with HIV in northern Tanzania: A longitudinal cohort study.
Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: People living with HIV (PLWH) face a high burden of kidney disease from HIV-related injury, antiretroviral toxicity, and environmental lead exposure. Renal hyperfiltration, an early compensatory state, may precede accelerated kidney function decline, yet its relationship with lead exposure remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa.
METHODS: We analyzed prospective longitudinal data from the Mwanza HIV and Cardiovascular Disease cohort in northern Tanzania (baseline analytic sample N = 943; 467 PLWH and 476 HIV-uninfected partners). Linear mixed-effects models used all available repeated eGFR measurements over four years; parent-cohort retention was 93.9% at 36 months. Blood lead levels were measured from dried blood spots using ICP-MS. eGFR was calculated using the CKD-EPI 2021 equation at baseline and over four years. Hyperfiltration was defined using sex-specific thresholds (>130 mL/min/1.73 m² for males, >125 mL/min/1.73 m² for females). Associations were evaluated using multivariable linear regression and linear mixed-effects models, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, hypertension, smoking, and HIV status.
RESULTS: Baseline eGFR: Higher log₁₀ blood lead levels were independently associated with lower baseline eGFR (fully adjusted β = -1.3; 95% CI: -2.5 to -0.17; p = 0.025), indicating an inverse cross-sectional association between lead exposure and kidney function at baseline. Longitudinal eGFR decline: Baseline hyperfiltration was strongly associated with subsequent eGFR decline over the four-year follow-up. Compared with participants with normal baseline filtration, those with hyperfiltration experienced an additional annual reduction of -9.5 to -9.9 mL/min/1.73 m² compared with normal filtration (p < 0.001) over four years follow-up. Consequently, participants with baseline hyperfiltration experienced the steepest declines over four years (approximately -25 to -26 mL/min/1.73 m²). Higher lead exposure was also associated with progressively worsening eGFR trajectories, with the greatest deterioration observed among participants with baseline hyperfiltration. Sensitivity analyses using an age-adjusted hyperfiltration definition and excluding extreme blood-lead values produced results consistent with the primary models.
CONCLUSION: Baseline renal hyperfiltration was strongly associated with subsequent kidney decline among people living with HIV, with greater declines observed among those with higher blood lead levels. These findings highlight the potential importance of lead exposure and kidney function monitoring in PLWH, particularly in resource-limited settings, while recognizing that the observed associations do not establish causality.

Title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
Journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
Abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.

Title: Prognostic Impact of a Simple GDMT Score on Clinical Outcomes and Cardiac Reverse Remodelling in Patients with ADHF: Insights from the JROADHF-Next Registry.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reported results indicate that implementation rates of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) are associated with improved prognosis and cardiac function in heart failure (HF) patients. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between what we term a "simple GDMT score" calculated at discharge and subsequent cardiac reverse remodelling and long-term outcomes in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF, using data from the Japanese Registry of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure (JROADHF-NEXT) prospective registry.
METHODS: We analyzed 2313 hospitalized patients with HFrEF or HFmrEF, stratifying them into high-score (≥ 5 points) and low-score (< 5 points) groups based on their discharge GDMT score.
RESULTS: The high-score group demonstrated a significantly lower risk of the composite endpoint of cardiovascular death or HF rehospitalization (hazard ratio = 0.64, 95% confidence interval: 0.55-0.76), an association that remained significant following multivariable adjustment (adjusted model: hazard ratio = 0.70, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-0.88). Furthermore, the high-score group exhibited significantly greater improvements in echocardiographic indices, including absolute changes in left ventricular ejection fraction (P < 0.001), left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (P < 0.001), and left ventricular end-systolic volume index (P < 0.001), and showed significant reductions in brain natriuretic peptide (P = 0.005) and N-terminal pro brain natriuretic peptide levels (P < 0.001) at 1-year follow-up assessment.
CONCLUSIONS: A higher simple GDMT score at discharge is independently associated with better 2-year clinical outcomes and favourable cardiac reverse remodelling in this cohort of HFrEF/HFmrEF patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF. These findings suggest that a simple assessment of GDMT at discharge may serve as a practical benchmark of discharge medical optimization in routine clinical care.

Title: Frailty and Bleeding Events in Heart Failure: Insights from the JROADHF-NEXT.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frail patients are considered to be at higher risk of bleeding than non-frail patients; however, the association between frailty and bleeding risk in patients with heart failure (HF) remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the prevalence of bleeding events, examine the relationship between frailty severity and bleeding risk, and assess the association between bleeding events and subsequent mortality in patients with HF receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy.
METHODS: This post hoc analysis used data from the Japanese Registry of Acute Decompensated Heart Failure-Next, a prospective, multicentre, nationwide registry. Frailty was evaluated using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS). Bleeding events were defined as major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding, based on the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis Bleeding Scale.
RESULTS: Among 4016 patients, 3029 (75.4%) were discharged on antiplatelet or anticoagulant medication. After excluding 89 with missing CFS data, 2940 patients were analyzed (mean age: 75 ± 12 years; 64.0% male). Patients were grouped by CFS scores: 1-3 (n = 1033); 4-5 (n = 1364); and 6-9 (n = 543). At 2 years, 149 (5.0%) experienced bleeding. Higher CFS scores were associated with increased bleeding risk (CFS score 4-5: hazard ratio [HR]: 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-2.34; CFS score 6-9: HR: 1.75; 95% CI: 1.04-2.93). In addition, bleeding events were associated with a higher risk of mortality (HR: 2.80; 95% CI: 1.88-4.17, P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is associated with bleeding risk in patients with HF receiving antithrombotic therapy. Bleeding events were associated with a higher risk of subsequent death.

Title: Single-view echocardiography-based deep learning for pulmonary hypertension detection: a multi-level supervised and explainable approach.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of pulmonary hypertension (PH), particularly mild disease, remains challenging. We aimed to develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model for noninvasive PH screening using single-view transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), without reliance on Doppler measurements.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, apical four-chamber (A4C) TTE cine loops were collected between January 2023 and June 2025. A total of 144 patients with PH confirmed by right heart catheterization (RHC), 17 RHC-confirmed non-PH patients, and 95 non-PH controls defined by TTE under strict inclusion criteria were included. An additional temporally independent validation cohort of 40 RHC-confirmed subjects was enrolled between December 2025 and May 2026. Multiple DL architectures were evaluated for detecting PH. Model performance was assessed at both sample and patient levels using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity.
RESULTS: A total of 256 patients with 318 TTE examinations were included for model development and independent validation, and an additional 40 RHC-confirmed subjects with 40 TTE examinations were included for temporal validation. The multi-level supervised model achieved the best performance among the evaluated architectures, with a patient-level AUROC of 1.000 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.998-1.000], sensitivity of 0.954, and specificity of 1.000 in the independent validation cohort. In the temporal validation cohort, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.932 (95% CI: 0.843-0.992), with sensitivity of 0.875, specificity of 0.813, and accuracy of 0.850. In an analysis of 50 RHC-confirmed subjects, the DL model achieved an AUROC of 0.937 (95% CI: 0.865-0.987) for distinguishing mild PH from non-PH, with sensitivity of 0.857 and specificity of 0.864, compared with AUROCs of 0.607-0.825 for conventional echocardiographic parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed an interpretable DL framework based on single-view A4C echocardiography for noninvasive PH assessment. The model showed promising performance, including preserved sensitivity for mild PH. Further multicenter prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

Title: Impact of hypertriglyceridemia on right ventricular deformation in patients with left ventricular myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a significant risk factor for myocardial infarction (MI), adversely affecting left ventricular (LV) structure and function and worsening clinical outcomes. Given the interaction between ventricles, the right heart may also be affected by MI. This study investigated the additional effects of HTG on right ventricular (RV) deformation in patients with acute MI.
METHODS: The study included 101 patients with MI [58 without HTG (HTG-) and 43 with HTG (HTG+)] and 83 control participants, all of whom underwent cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. The patients with MI were categorized into HTG+ and HTG- subgroups. RV and LV function and strain were assessed, and multivariate linear regression was performed to identify determinants of RV peak strain (PS).
RESULTS: Compared with the HTG- group, the HTG+ group exhibited higher total cholesterol and troponin levels (P=0.002 and P=0.043, respectively), as well as significantly lower RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05 after Bonferroni correction). RV radial PS was inversely correlated with LV mass (r=-0.349, P=0.021), total cholesterol (r=-0.402, P=0.007), troponin (r=-0.584, P<0.001), and infarct size (r=-0.410, P=0.006). RV circumferential PS was correlated with multiple LV parameters, lipids, and infarct extent (r=0.323 to 0.574; all P<0.05). After adjusting for age, sex, and blood pressure, HTG remained independently associated with impaired RV radial, circumferential, and longitudinal PS (all P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: HTG is associated with greater RV strain impairment in patients with MI. Our findings suggest that triglyceride levels and LV infarct extent may be associated with RV strain impairment, warranting further investigation in prospective studies.

Title: Association between microwave ablation and remission in patients with Graves' hyperthyroidism receiving continuous antithyroid drug treatment: a single-arm prospective study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Graves' disease (GD) is the most common cause of hyperthyroidism. Nearly half of patients develop persistent/recurrent GD (prGD) after antithyroid drug (ATD) therapy. Microwave ablation (MWA) is a precise minimally invasive therapeutic modality; however, evidence regarding its efficacy for prGD remains limited. This study therefore evaluated the efficacy of MWA in treating prGD and investigated factors predictive of post-MWA remission.
METHODS: This single-arm prospective study enrolled 45 patients with prGD who underwent bilateral thyroid MWA under ultrasound guidance at the Affiliated Hospital of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine between January 2023 and April 2024. The primary outcome was the remission rate during follow-up, defined as maintenance of normal thyroid function for at least 6 months after ATD discontinuation. Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test was used to analyze remission, and logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to identify factors associated with remission.
RESULTS: The cohort included 34 females and 11 males, with a median follow-up of 31.00 (28.00, 33.00) months. Notable findings included a significant reduction in the median thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) receptor antibody level at the last follow-up (P<0.001). Both thyroid volume and the average methimazole (MMI) dose were significantly reduced (both P<0.001). At the last follow-up, remission was achieved in 29 patients, yielding a total remission rate of 64.44%. Patients in the remission group had smaller baseline thyroid volumes than those in the non-remission group. Preoperative thyroid volume was independently associated with remission [odds ratio (OR) =0.829; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.707-0.971; P=0.020], with an optimal cutoff of 29.35 mL [area under the curve (AUC) =74.4%; 95% CI: 0.596-0.892; sensitivity =72.4%; specificity =68.7%]. All nine patients with thyroid volumes less than 20 mL achieved remission. No severe complications were reported during the follow-up period.
CONCLUSIONS: MWA was associated with decreased thyroid volume and reduced MMI dosage in patients with prGD, and clinical remission was observed in a subset of these patients. A preoperative thyroid volume of less than 29.35 mL is associated with a higher likelihood of remission.

Title: Allostatic Load and Severe Clinical Phenotypes in Major Depressive Disorder: A Cross-Sectional Statistical Mediation Analysis of Perceived Stress, Cognitive Impairment, and Suicidal Ideation.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perceived stress is associated with adverse clinical features of major depressive disorder (MDD), but the role of multisystem physiological dysregulation remains uncertain. We examined whether allostatic load (AL) was statistically associated with the relationship between perceived stress and cognitive impairment or severe suicidal ideation.
METHODS: This retrospective, cross-sectional electronic medical record study included 385 adults with DSM-5 MDD assessed within a single three-day index window. Perceived stress was measured with the 14-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14), and chronic exposure context was characterized from documented negative life events. AL was calculated from 15 cardiovascular, metabolic, immune-inflammatory, and neuroendocrine indicators. Cognitive impairment was defined as Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) <26 and severe suicidal ideation as Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) ideation severity ≥4. Sequential logistic regression and bootstrap product-of-coefficients statistical mediation analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Compared with Low AL, High AL was associated with cognitive impairment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.17, 95% CI 2.89-13.15) and severe suicidal ideation (aOR 6.43, 95% CI 2.98-13.88; both P<0.001). Continuous AL showed consistent associations with both outcomes. The indirect effect through AL was supported for cognitive impairment (0.39, 95% bootstrap CI 0.16-0.69), but not for severe suicidal ideation (0.14, 95% bootstrap CI -0.12 to 0.41).
CONCLUSION: Higher AL was independently associated with both adverse clinical phenotypes. Statistical mediation was supported for the perceived stress-cognitive impairment association but not for suicidal ideation. Because exposure, mediator, and outcomes were assessed within the same index window, temporal and causal mediation cannot be inferred.

Title: Preprocedural Q-wave Depth Does Not Predict Mortality After Primary Coronary Intervention for ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathologic Q waves on the admission electrocardiogram (ECG) have historically been markers of myocardial necrosis and adverse outcomes after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Although quantitative markers such as Q-wave width may add prognostic value, they can be difficult to apply clinically. We hypothesised that maximal and average pre-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) Q-wave depth could predict short- and medium-term mortality.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI (N = 625). Pre-PCI ECGs were analysed using European Society of Cardiology/American Heart Association definitions to identify pathologic Q waves. Maximal and average Q-wave depth (mm) and infarct territory were recorded. Posterior patterns, bundle branch block confounding interpretation, and Q waves outside the culprit territory were excluded. Outcomes were all-cause mortality at 3 and 12 months.
RESULTS: Of the 625 patients studied, 203 with pathologic Q waves in the infarct territory had complete depth measurements for analysis. Twelve-month mortality was 7.4% (15 of 203). Neither maximal nor average Q-wave depth was associated with mortality at 3 or 12 months in any infarct territory. Pain-to-balloon time demonstrated a weak positive correlation with maximal (Spearman rho = 0.204, P = 0.004) and average (rho = 0.152, P = 0.033) Q-wave depth.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small, observational cohort of STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, preprocedural Q-wave depth was not associated with all-cause mortality at 3 or 12 months. These findings do not support Q-wave depth as a standalone pre-PCI prognostic marker; larger studies and alternative ECG measures may be more informative. Q-wave depth was weakly associated with total ischemic time, warranting further evaluation in larger multicentre cohorts.

Title: Inflammation Mediates the Relationship Between Serum Uric Acid and New-Onset Diabetes Risk in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease: Results from a Multicenter Cohort Study [Letter].

Title: Left ventricular function and volumes from cardiac magnetic resonance and gated [13N]-ammonia positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging in patients with ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries: a prospective head-to-head comparison using hybrid positron emission tomography/magnetic resonance.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) has been widely validated for the assessment of left ventricular (LV) volumes and function. This study aimed to compare the accuracy of LV volumes and functional parameters derived from 13N-ammonia PET with those obtained by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using CMR as the reference standard.
METHODS: A total of 75 consecutive patients with known or suspected ischemia with no obstructive coronary arteries (INOCA) who simultaneously underwent ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET and CMR using a hybrid PET/magnetic resonance (MR) scanner were enrolled in this prospective study. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV), left ventricular stroke volume (LVSV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and regional wall motion score (RWMS) were derived from both imaging modalities and compared using correlation and Bland-Altman (BA) analyses. Additionally, inter- and intraobserver variability in LV volumetric parameters and LVEF were evaluated for both imaging modalities.
RESULTS: The correlation between PET and CMR was strong for LV volumes (r>0.83) and moderate for LVEF (r=0.65). The moderate LVEF correlation may be partially explained by the narrow range of LVEF values across the study cohort. Moreover, the agreement between 13N-ammonia PET and CMR for LVEF was good, with minimal bias (-0.57%); however, 13N-ammonia PET systematically underestimated LV volumes, with negative biases for LVEDV (-7.76 mL), LVESV (-3.28 mL), and LVSV (-5.33 mL). Similar, strong correlations and good agreement were observed in patients with reduced myocardial flow reserve (MFR). For both PET and CMR, inter- and intraobserver agreement for LV volumes and LVEF was high and comparable between the two modalities. In addition, RWMSs derived from ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET and CMR also exhibited good agreement (kappa =0.84±0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: LVEF and RWMS can be reliably and accurately quantified by ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET, although LV volumes are systematically underestimated compared with those quantified by CMR. ECG-gated 13N-ammonia PET may serve as a complementary modality for the assessment of LV systolic function; however, CMR remains the benchmark for LV volumetric measurement and myocardial tissue assessment.

Title: Incremental prognostic value of hepatic tissue alterations derived from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy: a case-control study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic injury occurs in patients with cardiovascular disease and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. The prognostic value of hepatic tissue alterations in patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of hepatic native T1 in predicting sustained ventricular arrhythmia (VA) in patients with ARVC.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with definite ARVC who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) examinations between August 2014 and October 2024. Hepatic native T1 values were derived from standard cardiac T1 maps. The clinical outcome was the first occurrence of sustained VA. Cox regression analysis was used to determine the association of variables with sustained VA. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated according to the concordance statistic (C-statistic), likelihood ratio test, and the continuous net reclassification index.
RESULTS: A total of 94 patients with definite ARVC (mean age 37.3±14.2 years; 67% male) were included. At a median follow-up of 39 months, sustained VA occurred in 34 (36%) patients. In multivariable Cox analysis, hepatic native T1 was an independent predictor of sustained VA [hazard ratio (HR) =1.02, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.00-1.03; P=0.025]. A model combining hepatic native T1 with the ARVC risk score and CMR-derived right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RV GLS) showed improved discrimination and calibration for sustained VA (C-statistic =0.760; likelihood ratio =20.14) compared with models composed of ARVC risk score alone (C-statistic =0.680; likelihood ratio =9.20; P<0.001) or the ARVC risk score and RV GLS (C-statistic =0.735; likelihood ratio =15.30; P=0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: Hepatic native T1 derived from cardiac T1 maps was an independent predictor of sustained VA in patients with ARVC, providing incremental prognostic value when incorporated into a model with ARVC risk score and RV GLS.

Title: Optical Coherence Tomography Findings Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Calcified Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) has emerged as a novel technology for modifying calcified coronary lesions, whereas optical coherence tomography (OCT) enables high-resolution assessment of calcium modification and procedural outcomes. However, the mechanistic and procedural effects of IVL assessed by OCT across studies remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261332946). PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Epistemonikos were searched from inception through February 2026. Randomized controlled trials and observational studies with extractable quantitative OCT outcomes were included. The primary endpoint was OCT-detected calcium fracture. Secondary endpoints included multiple calcium fractures, minimum stent area (MSA), stent expansion, acute lumen gain, procedural success, and in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled proportions or mean values with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Thirty studies encompassing a total of 3030 patients were included. OCT-detected calcium fracture occurred in 68% (95% CI 56%-79%) of lesions, whereas multiple fractures were observed in 34% (95% CI 26%-41%). IVL-treated lesions achieved favorable procedural metrics, including a pooled final MSA of 6.45 (95% CI 6.07-6.82) mm2, stent expansion of 85.9% (95% CI 82.3%-89.5%), and acute lumen gain of 3.50 (95% CI 3.14-3.87) mm2. Procedural success was high (95%, 95% CI 93%-98%) with low in-hospital MACEs (2%, 95% CI 1%-3%). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across endpoints.
CONCLUSIONS: Coronary IVL assessed by OCT is frequently associated with calcium fracture and favorable procedural outcomes with high procedural success and low early adverse events.

Title: CT-guided hybrid cryo-thermal co-ablation versus microwave ablation for stage I renal cell carcinoma: a real-world propensity score-matched comparative study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive ablation is an established treatment for stage I renal cell carcinoma (RCC), but comparative evidence is limited. This study presents an exploratory feasibility comparison of co-ablation (Co-A), a hybrid cryo-thermal technique combining liquid-nitrogen freezing with ethanol-mediated heating, with microwave ablation (MWA) in perioperative safety, renal function preservation, and short-term oncologic outcomes.
METHODS: Consecutive patients with clinical RCC who underwent computed tomography (CT)-guided percutaneous ablation from January 2017 to December 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Treatment selection reflected routine clinical judgment. This retrospective study was designed as an exploratory analysis. Propensity score matching (1:2) was performed using age, sex, baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), tumor size, and RENAL nephrometry score (Radius, Exophytic/endophytic properties, Nearness to collecting system, Anterior/posterior, and Location relative to polar lines).
RESULTS: Among 102 screened patients, 78 met eligibility criteria before matching. After matching, 45 patients were included: 15 treated with Co-A and 30 with MWA. All Co-A procedures were completed under local anesthesia, whereas 9 MWA procedures required general anesthesia (P=0.012). Co-A had longer procedure duration (86.2±22.0 vs. 45.4±11.9 min; P<0.001) but shorter hospital stay (2.9±1.4 vs. 4.5±2.6 days; P=0.021). Notably, the shorter hospital stay in the Co-A group should be interpreted with caution, as it may be confounded by the exclusive use of local anesthesia rather than the ablation modality itself. Minor bleeding was more frequent after Co-A (60.0% vs. 23.3%, P=0.039). Short-term eGFR decline was similar between groups (-5.6±11.1 vs. -7.4±11.5 mL/min/1.73 m2; P=0.65). During a median 24-month follow-up, local recurrence occurred in 2 Co-A and 1 MWA patient (13.3% vs. 3.3%; P=0.278).
CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory feasibility study suggests that Co-A and MWA demonstrate similar short-term renal functional outcomes in patients with stage I RCC. Co-A was feasible under local anesthesia and associated with shorter hospitalization, but required longer procedure times and was associated with more minor bleeding events. Differences in hospital stay should be interpreted cautiously due to potential anesthesia-related confounding. Oncologic comparisons require cautious interpretation.

Title: Unipolar electrogram-guided vs. ablation index-guided high-power short-duration pulmonary vein isolation in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: a single-center randomized controlled trial.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone of catheter ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PAF). The ablation index (AI) provides an estimate of lesion size and depth, but does not definitively confirm transmurality. Complete elimination of the negative component of the unipolar electrogram (UPE) has been proposed as a marker of transmural lesion formation. High-power short-duration (HPSD) radiofrequency ablation (RFA) produces more homogeneous lesions with clearer boundaries and thus may be more suitable for PVI. This study aimed to assess the AI values achieved during PVI using UPE-guided HPSD RFA and to compare the efficacy and safety of UPE-guided vs. fixed AI-guided HPSD RFA in patients with PAF.
METHODS: A total of 276 patients with PAF were randomly assigned to two groups: the UPE group and the AI group. In the UPE group (n=136), the ablation endpoint for each lesion was defined as continuation of ablation for 2 seconds after conversion of the UPE morphology from RS to R. In the AI group (n=140), the ablation endpoint for each lesion was achievement of a predefined target AI value (400-450 for the anterior wall and 360-380 for the posterior wall). The pulmonary vein (PV) first-pass isolation rate, acute PV reconnection (APVR) rate, and atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence rate were compared between groups.
RESULTS: The AI values were significantly lower in the UPE group than in the AI group (P<0.001). The inter-lesion distance (ILD) was significantly greater in the UPE group than in the AI group (P<0.001). The left and right PV first-pass isolation rates were higher in the UPE group (93.4% vs. 85.0%, P=0.03; and 95.6% vs. 89.3%, P=0.048, respectively). APVR occurred less frequently in the UPE group than in the AI group (11.0% vs. 20.0%, P=0.040). At 12 months post-procedure, AF recurrence was observed in 13 patients (9.6%) in the UPE group and 14 patients (10.0%) in the AI group (P=0.902). Three patients in the UPE group and four patients in the AI group developed inguinal hematoma (2.2% vs. 2.9%, P>0.99).
CONCLUSIONS: Both UPE-guided and AI-guided HPSD RFA were effective and safe in patients with PAF. UPE-guided ablation was associated with lower AI values, higher PV first-pass isolation rates, and a lower incidence of APVR. These findings suggest that UPE-guided HPSD RFA may provide a more individualized approach to PVI than fixed AI-guided ablation alone.

Title: Serial changes in right ventricular function after mitral valve surgery: retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the clinical relevance of right ventricular (RV) function assessed on echocardiography, its predictive utility for patients receiving mitral valve surgery remains uncertain. The primary objectives of this study were to characterize RV function before and after valvular surgery and to establish the diagnostic value of this assessment.
METHODS: Echocardiograms were collected prospectively from patients undergoing mitral valve surgery between 2020 and 2023. Subsequently, a retrospective analysis of preoperative and postoperative echocardiographic parameters was performed to evaluate RV function, including tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S'TDI), RV fractional area change (FAC), RV free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS), RV global longitudinal strain (RVGLS), and three-dimensional RV ejection fraction (3D RVEF). The study included 115 patients with mitral valve surgery. Serial echocardiographic evaluations were performed at four time points: preoperatively, 1 week postoperatively, 6 months postoperatively, and 1 year postoperatively. Serial changes in echocardiographic parameters (TAPSE, FAC, S'TDI, RVFWLS, and 3D‑RVEF) were analyzed via repeated‑measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and DeLong tests were used to evaluate and compare diagnostic performance. Reproducibility for RVFWLS, RVGLS, and 3D‑RVEF was assessed according to intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman plots in a random subset of 20 observations.
RESULTS: The principal findings were as follows: (I) RV systolic function demonstrated a statistically significant reduction postoperatively as compared to the preoperative baseline level (P<0.0001). (II) One year after operation, TAPSE and S'TDI remained significantly lower than their corresponding preoperative values, with mean changes of -0.34 mm [95% confidence interval (CI): -0.55 to -0.14; P=0.0003] and 1.48 cm/s (95% CI: 0.45 to 2.52; P=0.0024), respectively. In contrast, RVFWLS and 3D RVEF recovered to levels comparable to those at baseline, with mean changes of 0.29% (95% CI: -2.19% to 2.77%; P>0.05) and -3.04% (95% CI: -9.98% to 3.91%; P>0.05), respectively. (III) According to the DeLong test, RVFWLS demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for RV systolic dysfunction (area under the curve =0.771), significantly outperforming conventional parameters (FAC, TAPSE, and S'TDI; all P values <0.001). (IV) RVFWLS exhibited stronger diagnostic agreement with the reference standard (3D RVEF) in identifying impaired RV systolic function, as indicated by the reclassification rate (31%), as compared to conventional parameters (57-64%).
CONCLUSIONS: RVFWLS may serve as a novel indicator for assessing RV systolic function both preoperatively and postoperatively in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR).

Title: Echocardiographic characteristics and clinical features of cardiac involvement in Behçet's disease: a retrospective single-center case series.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac involvement in Behçet's disease (BD) is uncommon but potentially life-threatening and may mimic other cardiovascular disorders, complicating early diagnosis. This study aimed to characterize the clinical and echocardiographic features, treatment, pathological findings, and clinical outcomes of patients with cardiac BD, with particular emphasis on the utility of echocardiography in raising diagnostic suspicion.
METHODS: We retrospectively screened 186 patients with diagnosed or suspected BD at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University between October 2020 and January 2026. Of the 112 patients who underwent transthoracic echocardiography, 23 met the International Criteria for BD and were determined by multidisciplinary evaluation to have cardiac lesions attributable to BD after exclusion of alternative etiologies. Clinical, laboratory, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, pathological, treatment, and follow-up data were descriptively analyzed.
RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (82.6%), with a mean age of 43.5±13.1 years. The most frequent systemic manifestations were oral ulcers (95.7%), cutaneous lesions (73.9%), and genital ulcers (60.9%). Elevated inflammatory markers, including erythrocyte sedimentation rate (87.0%) and C-reactive protein (82.6%), were frequently observed. B-type natriuretic peptide levels were elevated in 91.3% of patients. Among the 19 patients without a history of cardiac surgery, severe aortic regurgitation was the predominant echocardiographic finding (94.7%) and was most often associated with aortic valve prolapse (78.9%). Other echocardiographic findings included aortic cusp aneurysm with perforation (15.8%), echo-free spaces around the aortic root (21.1%), aortic root and/or ascending aortic dilatation (63.2%), pulmonary artery dilatation (52.6%), left-sided chamber enlargement (84.2%), four-chamber enlargement (10.5%), and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (21.1%). Among the four patients with a history of cardiac or great-vessel surgery, all three who had undergone aortic valve replacement developed prosthetic valve dehiscence with severe paravalvular leakage within 2-6 months of surgery. Pathological examination of 14 surgical specimens revealed inflammatory-destructive changes involving the aortic wall and valve, characterized by fibrosis, hyalinization, myxoid degeneration, and chronic inflammatory cell infiltration. All patients received glucocorticoid-based immunosuppressive therapy, and 17 also underwent surgical treatment. At the last follow-up, 16 of 23 patients were alive and clinically stable, four were lost to follow-up, and three had died.
CONCLUSIONS: In this case series, cardiac BD was mainly characterized by destructive valvulo-aortic lesions, particularly severe aortic regurgitation associated with cusp prolapse and periannular or aortic root abnormalities. Echocardiography plays an important role in defining lesion morphology and severity, detecting postoperative prosthetic valve complications, and identifying structural abnormalities that may raise suspicion for cardiac BD in the appropriate clinical context.

Title: Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging for preoperative evaluation of cerebral microstructure and neurodevelopment in children with congenital heart disease.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a type of heart structure defect caused by the abnormal development of the heart and major blood vessels during the embryonic stage. With the continuous innovation of surgical treatment techniques and the improvement of perioperative management, the survival rate of children with CHD has significantly improved. However, accompanying central nervous system development problems have become increasingly prominent. This study investigated the clinical utility of neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) in evaluating preoperative cerebral microstructural features and neurodevelopmental status in children with CHD.
METHODS: Fifty-five infants with CHD were prospectively enrolled in the CHD group, and 55 age- and sex-comparable typically developing infants were included as the control group. All participants completed the Gesell Development Schedules assessment. The developmental quotient (DQ) and domain-specific subscale scores for five core developmental domains were recorded: adaptive behavior (AB), fine motor (FM), gross motor (GM), language (L), and personal-social behavior (PSB). Diffusion spectrum imaging (DSI) was acquired in all participants, and multiparametric NODDI maps were generated on a postprocessing workstation (Siemens Healthineers). The derived quantitative parameters included extracellular volume fraction (ECVF), neurite density index (NDI), isotropic volume fraction (ISOVF), and the orientation dispersion index (ODI). Intergroup differences in NODDI parameters and Gesell developmental scores were statistically analyzed. Pearson product-moment correlation analysis was then applied to evaluate associations between region-specific NODDI parameters and individual Gesell domain scores within the CHD group.
RESULTS: The ECVF in the splenium of the corpus callosum (SCC) of the CHD group was significantly lower than that of the control group (t=-2.261; P=0.026), whereas the ECVF in the frontal white matter (FWM) was significantly higher (t=2.242, P=0.027). ODI measurements in the posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) were significantly lower in the CHD group than in the control group (t=2.401; P=0.018). Intracellular volume fraction (ICVF) values in the PLIC and SCC were also significantly higher in the CHD group (PLIC: t=4.489, P<0.001; SCC: t=2.388, P=0.019). ODI measurements in the occipital white matter (OWM) were significantly lower in the CHD group than in the control group (t=3.707; P<0.001). Compared to the control group, the CHD group had significantly lower ISOVF measurements in the PTR (t=-2.119, P=0.038), FWM (t=-2.825, P=0.006), OWM (t=-2.253; P=0.028), and temporal white matter (t=-2.164; P=0.034). Correlation analysis further showed that Gesell scores, including DQ, AB, FM, GM, L, and PSB, were consistently lower in the CHD group than in the control group. Within the CHD cohort, the NDI value of the PLIC showed a positive correlation with DQ, AB, FM, GM, L, and PSB, whereas the ODI value of the PLIC showed a positive correlation with PSB. The ISOVF value of the genu of the corpus callosum showed a positive correlation with DQ, AB, L, and PSB. The NDI value of the SCC showed a positive correlation with AB and L.
CONCLUSIONS: NODDI sensitively detects preoperative cerebral microstructural changes in children with CHD, and its key parameters correlate with preoperative neurodevelopmental performance. Thus, NODDI-derived parameters may serve as candidate imaging biomarkers for evaluating brain microstructure and development before surgery, offering objective imaging-based support for early clinical assessment and timely intervention.

Title: Atrial and ventricular mechanical dysfunction and myocardial injury predict long-term outcomes in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: a retrospective cohort study.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction is a hallmark of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and imposes chronic pressure overload on the left atrium, leading to progressive atrial remodeling and functional impairment. Conventional left atrial (LA) volumetric indices reflect comparatively advanced structural alterations and are incapable of identifying early functional deterioration. The present research sought to investigate the prognostic significance of LA and LV myocardial deformation parameters obtained from cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with HCM.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 126 HCM patients and 40 healthy volunteers who underwent comprehensive CMR examinations. LA longitudinal strain (reservoir, conduit, and booster components) was assessed using the fast long-axis method; LV global strain and torsion were derived using feature-tracking analysis. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was quantified to assess myocardial fibrosis. Patients with HCM were followed longitudinally for the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of MACEs.
RESULTS: Compared with healthy volunteers, patients with HCM exhibited significantly impaired LA reservoir, conduit, and booster strain, as well as reduced LV global strain parameters (all P<0.05). Following a median observational period of 1,055 days, 41 patients (32.5%) experienced MACEs. Patients with MACEs demonstrated markedly reduced LA strain and LV torsion compared with those without events. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, LA booster strain [hazard ratio (HR): 0.854, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.799-0.914], LV torsion (HR: 0.517, 95% CI: 0.298-0.895), and serum creatine kinase myocardial band (CKMB) (HR: 1.032, 95% CI: 1.018-1.047) emerged as independent predictors of MACEs. LA booster strain yielded the optimal prognostic efficacy for predicting MACEs [area under the curve (AUC): 0.827].
CONCLUSIONS: LA booster strain, LV torsion, and CKMB represent complementary markers reflecting atrial function, ventricular mechanics, and myocardial injury, respectively. Their independent associations with adverse outcomes highlight the multifactorial nature of disease progression in HCM and support a more integrative approach to risk stratification beyond single-domain assessment. Incorporating these parameters into routine CMR and clinical evaluation may facilitate earlier identification of patients at increased risk for MACEs and support individualized surveillance strategies.

Title: Preservation of Non-nidal Medial Veins During Microsurgical Resection of Cerebral Arteriovenous Malformations: Technical Considerations and Early Clinical Outcomes.
Abstract: Background The surgical management of cerebral arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) requires a meticulous balance between complete nidus eradication and the preservation of adjacent normal physiological structures. While the elimination of true malformed, nidal-draining veins is mandatory to avoid intraoperative rupture, sacrificing adjacent, non-malformed, medial cortical, and deep venous channels can cause localized venous congestion, tissue infarction, and poor functional outcomes. Objective This study analyzed the clinical, radiological, and functional outcomes of a deliberate microsurgical strategy focused on preserving critical medial venous pathways during AVM resection in an early patient series. Materials and methods A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of 16 adult patients (aged >18 years) who underwent micro-neurosurgical resection of cerebral AVMs (Spetzler-Martin grades I-IV) at a single private academic institution between 2018 and 2025. Preoperative baseline features, clinical presentation (hemorrhage, seizures, focal deficits), and structural profiles were documented. Microsurgical dissection emphasized circumferential nidal isolation with strict preservation of non-nidal medial veins. Long-term functional assessment was evaluated using the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) score and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at a minimum of six months postoperatively. Results A total of 16 patients were included in the study, of whom 10 were male (62.5%) and six were female (37.5%). Primary clinical presentations included intracranial hemorrhage in 10 patients (62.5%), seizures in eight patients (50.0%), and focal deficits in nine patients (56.3%). Complete angiographic eradication of the AVM nidus was achieved in all 16 patients. No perioperative mortality was observed. Postoperative outcome assessment demonstrated improvements or stabilization in functional capacity. Favorable neurological recovery, defined as mRS 0-2, was documented in 14 patients (87.5%), supported by increases in PROMIS physical and mental health T-scores. No delayed venous infarction or hemorrhagic transformation occurred in any patient. Conclusions In this early clinical series, prioritizing the integrity of non-malformed medial veins during cerebral AVM surgery was a safe, effective, and anatomically sound strategy. Preserving healthy venous pathways surrounding the malformation limits the incidence of secondary venous hypertension, leading to exceptional functional preservation and minimal morbidity across a range of Spetzler-Martin grades.

Title: Performance and incremental value of preoperative multimodal imaging and perioperative clinical characteristics in predicting postoperative major adverse events in type A aortic dissection.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative major adverse events (MAEs) can occur after surgical repair of acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), and conventional clinical assessment may not fully capture the prognostic information provided by preoperative multimodal imaging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a staged risk prediction model for postoperative MAEs and to evaluate the incremental value of preoperative multimodal imaging relative to conventional clinical and laboratory assessment in the prediction of MAEs.
METHODS: In this retrospective, two-center cohort study, patients with surgically treated ATAAD were screened between April 2016 and April 2026. After application of predefined exclusion criteria, 1,960 patients were included, comprising a development cohort from Center I (n=1,498) and an external validation cohort from Center II (n=462). The development cohort was further randomly divided into a training set (n=1,048) and an internal validation set (n=450). Preoperative multimodal imaging and perioperative clinical data were collected, including computed tomography angiography (CTA), transthoracic/transesophageal echocardiography (TTE/TEE), admission laboratory indices, disease-severity indicators, and surgery-related variables. Candidate predictors were screened via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression. Five progressively expanded models were constructed to assess the incremental value of Penn classification, echocardiography, CTA, and intraoperative variables. Model performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: In the development cohort, postoperative MAEs occurred in 375 patients and did not occur in 1,123 patients. LASSO-based multivariable analysis identified age, lactate level, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), Penn classification, severe true lumen compression, mesenteric artery involvement, and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time as the core predictors for incorporation into the final nomogram. Model discrimination improved progressively with staged expansion. In the training set, the areas under the curve of models 1-5 were 0.725, 0.768, 0.782, 0.852, and 0.868, respectively; in the internal validation set, they were 0.718, 0.755, 0.776, 0.841, and 0.858; and in the external validation cohort, they were 0.705, 0.742, 0.765, 0.832, and 0.848, respectively. The largest incremental gain was observed after addition of multimodal CTA variables. The final nomogram showed good calibration and favorable clinical utility in both the training and external validation cohorts. Risk stratification in the development cohort demonstrated a marked stepwise increase in observed MAE incidence from 3.7% in the low-risk group to 27.9% in the intermediate-risk group and 74.2% in the high-risk group (P for trend <0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A staged prediction model integrating preoperative multimodal imaging and perioperative clinical characteristics provided effective risk stratification for postoperative MAEs among patients with ATAAD. Preoperative CTA contributed the greatest incremental improvement beyond baseline clinical assessment, and the final nomogram demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. This multimodal framework may support more precise perioperative risk assessment and individualized management for patients with surgically treated ATAAD.

Title: Prognostic value of pulmonary artery pulsatility index for perioperative adverse cardiovascular events in patients undergoing surgery for mitral regurgitation.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pulmonary artery pulsatility index (PAPi) demonstrates prognostic value across cardiopulmonary conditions, yet its utility in mitral regurgitation (MR) perioperative risk stratification remains undefined. This study aimed to evaluate whether the PAPi could independently predict perioperative adverse cardiovascular events in patients with MR, and to explore whether its addition to the European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II provided incremental value.
METHODS: This ambidirectional cohort study enrolled 302 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe MR undergoing mitral valve surgery. PAPi was calculated as pulmonary artery pulse pressure (pulmonary artery systolic pressure minus diastolic pressure) divided by right atrial pressure, all estimated by echocardiography. Patients were grouped by PAPi tertiles and followed for 3 months. The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Exploratory endpoints included mechanical ventilation duration and inotropic support. Incremental value was assessed by integrating PAPi into EuroSCORE II.
RESULTS: Patients were stratified into low PAPi (<3.4, n=99), intermediate PAPi (3.4-4.8, n=101), and high PAPi (>4.8, n=102) groups. MACE incidence was 37.4% (37/99), 10.9% (11/101), and 3.9% (4/102), respectively (χ2=43.70, P<0.001). Lower PAPi was associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, inotropic support, and intensive care unit (ICU) stay (all P<0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis showed that PAPi predicted MACE with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.76-0.88]. At cutoff 3.45, sensitivity was 81%, specificity 75%, positive predictive value (PPV) 40.0%, and negative predictive value (NPV) 94.9%. Bootstrap validation confirmed stability (AUC 0.82, 95% CI: 0.761-0.878). Multivariate analysis identified PAPi [odds ratio (OR) =0.26, 95% CI: 0.15-0.45, P<0.001], EuroSCORE II (OR=1.15, 95% CI: 1.03-1.28, P=0.012), and tricuspid annular plane systolicexcursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure [TAPSE/PASP; OR =0.79 per 1-standard deviation (SD) decrease, 95% CI: 0.65-0.95, P=0.013] as independent predictors. Each 1-unit PAPi decrease was associated with a 3.8-fold increase in MACE risk. Adding PAPi to clinical risk score and echocardiographic right ventricular function models improved predictive performance [C-statistic 0.70 to 0.85; net reclassification improvement (NRI) =0.807; integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) =0.144; all P<0.001]. Bootstrap optimism correction yielded an AUC of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.80-0.90). Subgroup analyses showed consistent predictive value (all interaction P>0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The echocardiography-derived PAPi predicts perioperative MACE in patients with MR. Incorporation of this index into traditional risk scoring systems provides incremental value for preoperative risk assessment and facilitates the identification of high-risk patients.

Title: Test-bolus peak attenuation for predicting aortic enhancement in coronary computed tomography angiography: an exploratory subgroup analysis.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adequate intravascular enhancement is essential for accurate coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) evaluation; however, conventional empirical contrast protocols often result in significant variability in enhancement because they do not account for individual physiological differences. Test-bolus techniques represent a potential approach for individualized contrast delivery; however, their precise quantitative relationship with final vascular enhancement requires further clarification. This study aimed to investigate the quantitative association between test-bolus peak attenuation and final aortic enhancement (FAE) in CCTA and to describe subgroup variations based on body mass index (BMI) and cardiac output (CO).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 50 patients who underwent CCTA. Test-bolus peak attenuation and FAE were systematically recorded. To evaluate the quantitative association between test-bolus peak attenuation and FAE, univariate linear regression analysis was performed, followed by subgroup analyses stratified by BMI (normal, overweight, or obese) and CO (normal or high).
RESULTS: Test-bolus peak attenuation was a significant positive predictor of FAE (β=0.924, P<0.001), accounting for 26.1% of the overall variance in FAE. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed descriptive differences in the strength of this predictive trend across BMI categories. Notably, a stronger predictive trend was observed in obese patients (R2=0.812, P=0.037) than in normal weight (R2=0.310) and overweight (R2=0.247) patients. Conversely, while predictive efficacy remained significant in patients with normal CO (R2=0.288, P=0.001), it was attenuated and statistically non-significant in those with high CO (R2=0.240, P=0.090).
CONCLUSIONS: Test-bolus peak attenuation demonstrated significant potential as a quantitative predictor of aortic enhancement in CCTA, suggesting that test-bolus peak attenuation may be useful in exploring individualized contrast protocols. The descriptive trends observed in the obese subgroup are strictly hypothesis-generating. Exploratory findings suggest that the predictive trend might vary according to BMI and CO. Larger studies are needed to confirm these descriptive observations.

Title: Interindividual variability in platelet aggregation among aspirin-treated patients: a large retrospective analysis.
Abstract: Interindividual variability in response to aspirin remains a major challenge in antiplatelet therapy. Identification of patients with high platelet reactivity (HPR) and optimal or low platelet reactivity remains challenging and may be influenced by both biological and methodological factors, including interlaboratory variability. We report results of a large cohort of aspirin-treated patients to assess the gold standard light transmission aggregometry (LTA). We retrospectively analyzed 3065 patients treated with aspirin (ASA; 75-150 mg/d) who sequentially underwent LTA assessment using multiple agonists (adenosine diphosphate [ADP] 2μM, collagen 2 μg/mL, arachidonic acid [AA] 0.75mM, and epinephrine 10μM). Patients were stratified according to AA-induced platelet aggregation using a 16% cutoff (third quartile). Patients with AA >16% showed significantly higher platelet aggregation across all agonists (P < .0001). However, a substantial proportion of patients with AA ≤16%, consistent with effective COX-1 inhibition, still exhibited HPR when stimulated with ADP, epinephrine, or collagen. Collagen-induced aggregation was particularly informative in identifying residual platelet reactivity. Sex-related differences were observed, with female patients showing HPR, especially to ADP and collagen. Platelet reactivity in aspirin-treated patients is highly heterogeneous, with hyperreactive or hyporeactive phenotype potentially affecting the safety and efficacy of antiplatelet therapy. AA-induced aggregation alone is insufficient to fully characterize platelet responsiveness. A multiagonist approach, particularly including collagen, may improve identification of patients with residual platelet reactivity and support personalized antiplatelet strategies. These data support ongoing strategies of guided selection of antiplatelet therapy in patients with cardiovascular disease.

Title: Quantification of plaque and detection of high-risk plaque characteristics based on coronary computed tomography angiography: comparison between superresolution deep learning reconstruction and hybrid iterative reconstruction.
Journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In addition to stenosis evaluation, coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) also allows for noninvasive plaque quantification and characterization, which informs risk stratification and management strategies. This study aimed to compare a novel superresolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR) technique with a conventional hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) method in quantifying CCTA-derived plaque and detecting high-risk plaque (HRP) characteristics.
METHODS: A total of 255 consecutive patients (mean age 63.7±9.6 years; 184 men and 71 women) who underwent clinically indicated CCTA for assessment of suspected or known coronary artery disease were prospectively enrolled. The HIR algorithm with the FC43 kernel and the SR-DLR algorithm with the cardiac kernel reconstructed the same raw CCTA data. Total plaque, calcified plaque, noncalcified plaque (NCP), and low-attenuation plaque (LAP) volumes were quantified. Moreover, the ability to detect HRP characteristics (LAP, spotty calcification, positive remodeling, and napkin-ring sign) was evaluated. Paired comparisons were made between the two reconstruction pipelines.
RESULTS: Compared with the HIR pipeline, the SR-DLR pipeline obtained higher median volumes of total plaque {103.4 [interquartile range (IQR) 52.9-201.7] vs. 124.5 (IQR 66.8-236.2) mm3}, NCP [43.9 (IQR 20.1-87.7) vs. 56.4 (IQR 25.2-115.7) mm3], and LAP [0.1 (IQR 0-3.0) vs. 0.9 (IQR 0-8.7) mm3] (all P<0.001); meanwhile, calcified plaque volume did not differ significantly between the pipelines [44.8 (IQR 16.2-100.6) vs. 44.8 (IQR 17.3-98.2) mm3; P=0.87]. SR-DLR detected more LAPs than did HIR (91 vs. 67; P=0.01), but there were no detected differences in spotty calcification (63 vs. 56; P=0.33), positive remodeling (110 vs. 110; P>0.99), or napkin-ring sign (42 vs. 40, P=0.76).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the HIR pipeline, the SR-DLR pipeline indicated higher total plaque, NCP, and LAP volumes, but no difference in calcified plaque volume was observed. Moreover, SR-DLR detected more LAPs than did HIR, while other HRP characteristics did not differ significantly. Further large-scale prospective studies including a reference standard are warranted to investigate the clinical impact of SR-DLR.

Title: Efficacy of Mat Pilates on the resting blood pressure and health related quality of life in individuals with systemic hypertension versus standard care: study protocol for a single centered single blinded randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic hypertension is a global non-communicable disease that creates an essential need for alternate forms of lifestyle modifications, including exercise, to lower elevated blood pressure. Mat Pilates, a feasible form of mind-body coordinated exercise, may provide benefits with limited resources.
OBJECTIVE: This randomized controlled trial aims to assess the efficacy of Mat Pilates on resting blood pressure and health-related quality of life in individuals with systemic hypertension.
METHODS: A two-arm, single-blinded, block randomized controlled trial will be recruited with a total of 120 participants into control and experimental groups 60 participants in each group (1:1 ratio). Mat Pilates will be administered to the experimental group and standard care to the control group for 12 weeks. Resting and central blood pressure, health-related quality of life, and echocardiographic parameters will be measured before and after the trial. We hypothesized that Pilates may not be beneficial in lowering resting blood pressure in hypertensive patients. A repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) will test the within- and between-group effects of Mat Pilates on various outcomes.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The trial was approved by the Institutional Research Committee, Manipal College of Health Professions, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Kasturba Medical College, and Kasturba Hospital Institutional Ethics Committee, Manipal. Written informed consent will be obtained from all the participants. All stakeholders and committees will communicate key findings regarding the implementation of mind-body association exercises as a measure of lifestyle modification in individuals with systemic hypertension.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry of India: CTRI/2021/07/035002. Registered on July 20, 2021, http://ctri.nic.in.

Title: Opportunistic Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in the Eye Clinic: Validation of a Retinal Deep Learning-Based 10-Year Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Estimator.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: To derive and validate a retinal 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk estimator ("Dr Noon cardiovascular disease [CVD]") and compare its performance with the clinical gold-standard pooled cohort equation (PCE) in a US population.
DESIGN: Prospective cohort study with up to 10 years of follow-up.
PARTICIPANTS: A total of 3096 participants (aged 55-75 years) from the multicenter Age-related Eye Disease Study (AREDS) with gradable baseline fundus photographs, including 1013 with PCE.
METHODS: The Dr Noon CVD estimator, which incorporates a deep learning-derived retinal coronary artery calcium surrogate along with age and sex, was derived using a Cox proportional hazards model and validated within the AREDS cohort. Its predictive performance was compared directly with the PCE.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Incident fatal and nonfatal ASCVD events over 10 years. Performance metrics included risk stratification (hazard ratios [HRs]), discrimination (concordance index [C-index]), calibration (plot with intercept/slope), and reclassification (net reclassification index [NRI]).
RESULTS: Among 3096 participants, 202 (6.5%) experienced an ASCVD event. Although the PCE was precluded for 67.3% of the cohort (n = 2083) due to missing laboratory data, the retinal estimator provided scores for all participants with available imaging. Dr Noon CVD significantly stratified participants into low, moderate (HR, 1.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24-2.71), and high-risk groups (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.64-3.93; P-trend < 00.001). Beyond traditional risk factors, the model significantly improved discrimination (ΔC-index, 3.4%) and reclassification (overall NRI, 0.194; 95% CI, 0.044-0.344). In direct comparison among participants with PCE (n = 1013), Dr Noon CVD demonstrated numerically higher discrimination (C-index, 0.665 vs. 0.647; P = 0.74) and significantly superior calibration, whereas the PCE overestimated risk at higher deciles (P-intercept = 0.004 vs. 0.141 for Dr Noon CVD). Finally, performance was enhanced in hypertensive participants.
CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning analysis of routine retinal photographs provides cardiovascular risk stratification comparable to established clinical equations, offering a valid, noninvasive solution for opportunistic screening even when missing laboratory data precludes the standard risk calculators. These findings support the potential for opportunistic systemic risk assessment within the eye clinic, enhancing the role of the ophthalmologist in primary prevention.
