FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

Title: Comparative analysis of postoperative complications and 30-day readmissions after CABG in diabetic vs. non-diabetic patients: a nationwide readmissions database study.
Journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus is a known risk factor for long-term adverse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, its impact on 30-day readmission is less characterized. This study aimed to compare 30-day readmission rates and index hospitalization outcomes between diabetic and non-diabetic patients undergoing CABG and to identify independent predictors of readmission.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the 2016 and 2017 Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD). In keeping with HCUP guidance, each data year was analyzed as a separate sample rather than pooled. Adult patients undergoing CABG were identified in each year and stratified by diabetes status. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), hospital charges, and complications. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, hospital, and comorbidity characteristics as well as index-hospitalization complications and discharge disposition, was used to identify independent risk factors for readmission.
RESULTS: In the 2016 (weighted N = 100,010) and 2017 (weighted N = 100,669) cohorts, diabetes was present in 47.7% and 48.9% of patients, respectively. In both years the 30-day readmission rate was higher among patients with diabetes (2016: 10.0% vs. 8.3%; 2017: 9.3% vs. 7.3%; both p < 0.001), corresponding to adjusted odds ratios of 1.14 (95% CI 1.07-1.22) in 2016 and 1.15 (95% CI 1.07-1.24) in 2017. In each year, patients with diabetes had more complex index hospitalizations, with longer stays, higher complication rates, and greater hospital charges. Non-home discharge was the strongest independent predictor of readmission in both years (OR 1.66 in 2016 and 1.67 in 2017), with anemia, congestive heart failure, and chronic pulmonary disease also independently associated.
CONCLUSION: In both the 2016 and 2017 cohorts, diabetes was independently associated with 30-day readmission after CABG, even after accounting for index complications and discharge disposition, and was accompanied by a greater comorbidity burden and postoperative complexity. The strong association with non-home discharge suggests that care transitions warrant further study. These findings identify a high-risk population that may benefit from enhanced discharge planning and close post-discharge monitoring, although whether such measures reduce readmission requires prospective evaluation.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02103-2.

Title: Validation of Baveno VII Criteria using Liver and Splenic Elastography for Predicting Esophageal Varices Severity in Chronic Liver Disease: A Multiparametric, Observational Study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Baveno VII criteria prioritize Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) for portal hypertension risk stratification, primarily using transient elastography. We aimed to evaluate two-dimensional-shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) cutoffs, assess the etiology-dependent utility of spleen stiffness (SSM), and introduce a novel Combined Hepato-splenic Stiffness Index (CHSSI).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This ambispective, observational study enrolled 100 chronic liver disease patients. Participants underwent 2D-SWE for LSM and SSM, alongside endoscopy as the reference standard. A novel multiparametric index, CHSSI, was formulated. Diagnostic accuracy for Varices Needing Treatment (VNT; Grade >= II) was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC).
RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly Alcohol-related Liver Disease (ALD, 49%) and Viral Hepatitis (30%). LSM independently predicted VNT (P < 0.001), with an optimal 2D-SWE cutoff of 19.2 kPa (sensitivity 90% and specificity 82%). SSM utility diverged by etiology: it correlated significantly with variceal grade in ALD (r = 0.549, P < 0.001) but poorly in viral cirrhosis (r = 0.174, P = 0.358). The novel CHSSI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.892) for predicting VNT.
CONCLUSIONS: Liver stiffness remains the most robust single-parameter surrogate for esophageal varices. However, in heterogeneous cohorts where splenic stiffness alone yields inconsistent results, novel composite indices such as CHSSI and Liver Size-stiffness Index offer superior discriminative ability. These findings support a refined noninvasive risk stratification strategy, potentially reducing unnecessary screening endoscopies.

Title: An Exploratory Retrospective Comparison of Crisugabalin and Pregabalin Among 12-Week Treatment Completers With Postherpetic Neuralgia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregabalin (PGB) is commonly used for postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), but its clinical effectiveness may be limited by insufficient pain relief or adverse events (AEs). Crisugabalin (CGB) is a novel α2δ-1 ligand that has demonstrated efficacy in randomized placebo-controlled trials. However, comparative real-world evidence for CGB and PGB remains limited.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with PHN who completed at least 12 weeks of CGB or PGB monotherapy between January and June 2025. In October 2025, a single structured telephone interview was conducted to retrospectively assess patients' recalled status at treatment initiation (T0) and at Weeks 1, 4, and 12. Outcomes included the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and the physical and mental component summary scores of the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). Linear mixed effects models (LMMs) were designated as the primary analyses and adjusted for age, sex, pain location, pre-enrollment pain duration, hypertension, and diabetes. Repeated measures analysis of variance and the LMM analysis based on inverse probability weighting of propensity scores were performed as sensitivity analysis. Safety outcomes were descriptively assessed among treatment completers.
RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, including 56 in the CGB group and 57 in the PGB group. In the adjusted LMMs, significant treatment-by-time interactions were observed for NRS scores (p < 0.001), PSQI scores (p < 0.001), and SF-36 mental component summary scores (p = 0.003), the extent to which these three scores of the CGB group improved over time may be higher than that of the PGB group. The treatment-by-time interactions were not statistically significant for SF-36 physical component summary scores (p = 0.377). Sensitivity analyses using repeated measures analysis of variance produced concordant findings for NRS, PSQI, and SF-36 mental component scores but not for SF-36 physical component scores. At least one AE was reported by 11 of 56 patients in the CGB group and 18 of 57 patients in the PGB group, but there was no overall significant difference in AEs (p = 0.196).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who completed 12 weeks of treatment, the CGB group was associated with statistical differences to some extent in NRS, PSQI, and SF-36 mental component scores than PGB group, and these degree of improvement over time may be more pronounced. Due to the substantial bias in retrospective studies and the relatively small sample size, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory, merely have reference value, and require more confirmation in prospective controlled studies in the future.

Title: Methylphenidate and Long-Term Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiovascular safety of methylphenidate remains a matter of debate.
METHODS: To evaluate the long-term cardiovascular risk associated with methylphenidate use, a cohort study was conducted using the French National Health Data System. New users were defined by a first methylphenidate dispensation (index date) between January 1, 2014, and December 31, 2023. Each new user was matched with three nonusers by sex and by month and year of birth. Individuals with prior cardiovascular disease or relevant cardiovascular comorbidities were excluded. The primary outcome was cardiovascular disease, defined by International Classification of Diseases codes or antihypertensive drug use. Cox proportional hazards models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs), accounting for demographic and clinical covariates. Negative control outcomes were used to assess residual confounding, allowing the derivation of calibrated HRs and confidence intervals.
RESULTS: A total of 212 216 new users and 636 648 matching nonusers were included. Mean age was 13.7 years and 72% were males. Over a follow-up of ~4 years, 3858 cardiovascular diseases occurred (0.45%): 1960 in new users (9.2 per 1000) and 1898 in nonusers (3 per 1000). The adjusted HR was 2.37 (95% CI [2.21; 2.54]), with a calibrated HR of 1.85 (95% CI [1.55; 2.21]).
CONCLUSIONS: The results suggest that methylphenidate use may be associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular diseases. Although the calibrated estimates indicate attenuation due to residual confounding, the association remained statistically significant. This supports recommendations for cardiovascular monitoring during treatment.

Title: Event-Weighted Desaturation Burden and Cardiovascular Mortality in Sleep Apnoea: Findings from a Large Community-Based Prospective Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obstructive sleep apnoea's prognostic value is limited by reliance on the apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI), which fails to capture physiological heterogeneity of respiratory events. We developed a composite metric, event-weighted desaturation burden (EWDB), integrating weighted respiratory event load, regularity of consecutive inter-event intervals, and cumulative desaturation area. We evaluated its association with cardiovascular mortality and its incremental prognostic value compared with AHI and established hypoxic metrics.
METHODS: We analysed 4,904 adults from the Sleep Heart Health Study with baseline polysomnography and adjudicated follow-up. EWDB was derived by combining a respiratory weighted index, a distribution factor based on inter-event interval regularity, and event-linked hypoxic burden (HB).
RESULTS: The primary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Over a median follow-up of approximately 11 years, 341 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In fully adjusted multivariable Cox models, higher EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality. However, AHI and HB associations were attenuated and lost statistical significance after full adjustment. EWDB (per 1-SD increase) remained robustly associated with cardiovascular mortality, whereas AHI did not. Incorporating EWDB into a comprehensive clinical model provided incremental risk stratification. Similar robust associations were observed for fatal coronary heart disease and incident heart failure.
CONCLUSIONS: EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and provided incremental prognostic information beyond established clinical and sleep-related factors in this cohort. By integrating respiratory event intensity, cumulative burden, and inter-event interval regularity, EWDB may better characterize cardiovascular stress related to sleep-disordered breathing.

Title: Making the Diagnosis of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia in Australia.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic disorder associated with recurrent infections and irreversible airway damage. No single diagnostic test exists, necessitating use of a diagnostic algorithm that varies internationally. This retrospective study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics of patients, and algorithm used to diagnose PCD in New South Wales between 2014 and 2024.
METHODS: A retrospective review of patients diagnosed with PCD at Concord Repatriation General Hospital (CRGH) from 2014 to 2024 was performed.
RESULTS: This study included 52 patients with median age of diagnosis 7.0 years. The diagnostic algorithm consists of nasal nitric oxide (nNO) in patients > 5 years, and nasal brushings for high-speed video microscopy (HSVMA), immunofluorescence (IF) and electron microscopy (EM). Whole exome sequencing is not routine and was performed in 33% of the cohort. The diagnosis was confirmed by a multidisciplinary team that considered the test results and clinical phenotype. Non-diagnostic results occurred in 14% (nNO), 15% (HSVMA), 41% (IF) and 30% (EM) of patients eventually diagnosed with PCD or PCD "highly likely". Cumulatively, 56% of patients had at least one non-diagnostic result. Of the 17 patients who underwent whole exome sequencing with a PCD panel, 41% had diagnostic genetic results.
CONCLUSION: Ciliary studies continue to be the mainstay of PCD diagnosis at CRGH. Although genetic testing is not part of the CRGH diagnostic algorithm, the CRGH algorithm has similar diagnostic performance to the ERS and ATS guidelines.

Title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair in hyperacute type B aortic dissection: a mini review.
Abstract: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is established as the preferred treatment for many patients with complicated acute type B aortic dissection (TBAD). However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR. In patients with rupture, malperfusion, impending aortic rupture, persistent pain, refractory hypertension, or progressive true-lumen collapse, prompt entry-tear coverage can restore perfusion and prevent irreversible organ injury. Similarly, in patients without initial complications, high-risk anatomical features may help identify those who could benefit from early intervention. However, evidence supporting routine TEVAR within the first 24 hours remains limited and is predominantly observational. To ensure safe hyperacute TEVAR, careful assessment of the landing zones, conservative device sizing, avoidance of aggressive balloon molding, preservation of branch-vessel and spinal cord perfusion, and prompt recognition of retrograde type A dissection, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, and stent-graft-induced new entry are required. Ultimately, hyperacute TEVAR may be a reasonable option for selected patients with complicated TBAD, with a potential role in high-risk uncomplicated TBAD. Future prospective randomized trials integrating multimodal imaging and dynamic biomarkers are warranted to establish definitive criteria for timing and candidate selection.

Title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Motion artifacts remain a limitation of cardiac CT when assessing both native and prosthetic heart valves, particularly during phases of rapid motion. This may lead to reduced image quality, potentially impairing the evaluation of valvular movement and pathology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a novel reconstruction-based motion correction algorithm improves image quality and reduces motion artifacts of native and prosthetic heart valves compared with standard reconstructions in photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 57 patients [21 women; median age, 71 (interquartile range, 57 to 78 y)] who underwent clinically indicated 4D cardiac CT for suspected native and prosthetic valvular disease were included. Images were acquired using retrospectively electrocardiography (ECG)-gated spiral dual-source PCD-CT without ECG-pulsing. Images were reconstructed in 10% steps throughout the RR-interval using both standard (TrueStack) and an otherwise identical reconstruction using the novel motion correction algorithm (ZeeFreePlus). Subjective image quality and motion artifacts were independently assessed by 2 blinded, experienced readers using a 4-point visual analog scale for 3 categories: valve frame/annulus, valve leaflets, and valvular pathology. Objective analysis included quantification of the volume of artifacts throughout the cardiac cycle.
RESULTS: A total of 68 valves were evaluated, including 57 prosthetic valves (22 transcatheter aortic valve replacements and 19 surgical valves, 11 mitral valves, and 5 tricuspid valve interventions) and 11 native valves. Valvular pathology was present in 29 cases, with the most prevalent being hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in 14/29 (48%). Motion-corrected reconstructions significantly improved image quality and reduced motion artifacts across all cardiac phases and all categories (all, P<0.001). The largest improvements were observed during systole, particularly at 10% of the RR-interval, with significantly greater gains than during diastole (P<0.05). Improvements were consistent across aortic and atrioventricular prosthetic valves and translated into improved visualization of valvular pathology (P<0.001). Objective quantitative analysis corroborated the subjective image quality findings by demonstrating reductions in the volumes of motion-induced artifacts when using the algorithm (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

Title: Effects of Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise and deep-sea water consumption on metabolic syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: The increasing prevalence of metabolic syndrome poses significant health risks, particularly for cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes. Exercise interventions have shown promise in improving the components of metabolic syndrome, including blood pressure, lipid profiles, and glucose metabolism. Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise provides real-time feedback and personalized guidance, making it suitable for unsupervised training. Deep-sea water has beneficial effects on lipid metabolism and insulin sensitivity. However, the effects of Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise and deep-sea water on metabolic syndrome remain unclear.
METHODS: Fifty-six participants aged 30-65 years with a diagnosis of metabolic syndrome were randomly assigned to four groups for an 8-week intervention: control (CG), deep-sea water consumption (WG), Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise (EG), and combined deep-sea water consumption and Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise (WEG). The intervention comprised a 40-min Kinect-based mixed-reality circuit exercise three times per week and daily consumption of 440 mL of deep-sea water. The measurements included blood pressure, body composition, blood profiles, quality of life, physical activity, diet recall, and the metabolic syndrome score.
RESULTS: Forty-eight participants completed the study, demonstrating high compliance with the EG (98.4%) and WG (99.2%). Waist circumference significantly decreased in all intervention groups (WG, p = 0.002; EG, p < 0.0001; WEG, p < 0.0001), with a significant difference between CG and EG (p = 0.020). The metabolic syndrome component score decreased significantly in the EG (p = 0.004) and WEG (p = 0.002) groups, falling below the diagnostic threshold for metabolic syndrome.
CONCLUSION: These findings indicate the potential benefits of combining deep-sea water consumption and Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise in metabolic syndrome management.

Title: Pre-exercise chickpea milk consumption supports glycemic stability during endurance exercise in female runners.
Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study investigated the effects of pre-exercise chickpea milk consumption on glycemic stability and physiological responses during endurance exercise in trained female runners.
METHODS: Fourteen eumenorrheic female half-marathon runners (25-35 years) completed a randomized, double-blind, counterbalanced crossover trial. Participants consumed 250 mL of chickpea milk or soy milk or a maltodextrin placebo 30 min before exercise, with each trial conducted during the follicular phase and separated by a washout period of at least one week. The exercise protocol consisted of treadmill running at 60% of maximal heart rate for 60 min, followed by running at 80% of maximal heart rate until volitional exhaustion. Blood glucose, blood lactate, free fatty acids, creatine kinase, respiratory exchange ratio, rating of perceived exertion, and time to exhaustion were assessed.
RESULTS: Blood glucose concentrations differed significantly between the beverage conditions (p < 0.05). Compared with the placebo, chickpea milk produced a more stable glycemic response during exercise. Blood glucose variability, assessed using the coefficient of variation, differed significantly among beverage conditions (p = 0.031), with lower values following chickpea milk (13.07 ± 4.33%), and soy milk (12.37 ± 4.62%) compared with the placebo (16.07 ± 4.89%). No significant differences were observed among the beverage conditions for blood lactate, free fatty acids, creatine kinase, respiratory exchange ratio, rating of perceived exertion, or time to exhaustion (all p > 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Pre-exercise chickpea milk consumption supported glycemic stability during prolonged endurance exercise in trained female runners, but did not improve exercise performance or other physiological outcomes. Larger, adequately powered studies are warranted to determine whether this metabolic response translates into meaningful improvements in endurance performance.

Title: Predictive value of genetic and morphological evaluation (GAME) score for outcomes after thermal ablation in patients with colorectal liver metastases.
Journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the predictive value of the genetic and morphological evaluation (GAME) score for the prognosis of patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) receiving thermal ablation (TA) and compare it with the Fong score.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of CRLM patients who underwent TA between January 2016 and December 2021 at two tertiary medical centers in China. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing. Prognostic variables associated with early recurrence (ER) and OS were identified through univariate and multivariate Cox regression, and nomograms were developed based on significant factors.
RESULTS: Both the GAME and Fong scores effectively predicted RFS and OS in patients with CRLM undergoing TA treatment, though the GAME score showed superior discriminatory ability. Cox regression identified the largest liver metastasis diameter (HR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.29-0.69; p < 0.001) and GAME group (HR: 1.88, 95% CI: 1.13-3.12; p = 0.015) as independent prognostic factors for ER. The largest liver metastasis diameter (HR: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.31-0.78; p = 0.003), image-guidance technique (HR: 2.10, 95% CI: 1.04-4.27; p = 0.039) and GAME group (HR: 1.88, 95% CI: 1.12-3.16; p = 0.017) were independent prognostic factors for OS. Based on these findings, nomograms with good discrimination and calibration were constructed.
CONCLUSION: The GAME score, which outperforms the Fong score in predicting the prognosis of patients with CRLM who meet the stringent eligibility criteria of this study and undergo TA, should be considered a preoperative prognostic tool.

Title: Predictive Value of Preoperative Inflammatory and Nutritional Indices for Revision Surgery After Major Lower Extremity Amputation in Patients With Wagner Stage 5 Diabetic Foot.
Journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
Abstract: BACKGROUND Major lower extremity amputation is a severe complication of diabetic foot disease, leading to high morbidity and repeat surgeries. Although systemic inflammatory and nutritional markers have been studied as prognostic factors in diabetic foot ulcers, their role in predicting revision surgery after major amputation is unclear. This study aims to evaluate the link between preoperative inflammatory and nutritional indices and revision surgery after major lower extremity amputation. MATERIAL AND METHODS This multicenter retrospective study reviewed medical records of patients with Wagner stage 5 diabetic foot disease who had major lower extremity amputation at 3 hospitals. Revision included stump shortening or re-amputation at a more proximal level. Patients were divided into revision and non-revision groups. Demographic characteristics, amputation side and level, and preoperative laboratory parameters were recorded. The Prognostic Nutritional Index, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio were evaluated. Intergroup comparisons were performed to evaluate the association between these indices and the risk of revision surgery. RESULTS A total of 89 patients were studied; 35 (39.3%) needed revision surgery, while 54 (60.7%) healed successfully without further surgery. There were no significant differences between groups in age, sex, preoperative revascularization, amputation levels, laboratory parameters, or inflammatory and nutritional indices. No link was found between these indices and revision surgery. CONCLUSIONS Systemic inflammatory and nutritional indices before major lower extremity amputation in patients with diabetic foot were not linked to postoperative revision surgery. Risks may be more affected by local factors such as residual infection, limb perfusion, and stump viability. Future studies combining systemic biomarkers with vascular assessment could better predict revision risk.

Title: Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative and Breastfeeding Outcomes Across Social Determinants of Health in Oklahoma, USA: A Secondary Data Analysis.
Journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding improves maternal and infant health, reducing risks of cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and infant mortality. Despite national gains in breastfeeding initiation, disparities persist in exclusivity and duration across social determinants of health (SDOH). The Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) promotes evidence-based maternity care practices to support breastfeeding, yet its effectiveness across diverse populations remains unclear.
PURPOSE: This study examined whether BFHI designation is associated with breastfeeding outcomes including initiation, exclusive breastfeeding at 8 weeks, and any breastfeeding at 8 weeks among Oklahoma mothers who delivered between 2016 and 2018, and whether these associations differ across SDOH including race, ethnicity, household income, educational attainment, marital status, maternal age, parity, and geographic location.
METHODS: A retrospective secondary analysis of linked Oklahoma Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System and birth certificate data (2016-2018; N = 4,234) was conducted. Weighted logistic regression estimated associations between BFHI designation and breastfeeding outcomes, stratified by SDOH, and adjusted for demographic and socioeconomic factors.
RESULTS: BFHI designation at birth facility was associated with higher odds of initiation among primiparous mothers (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI]: [0.98-3.64]), Native American mothers (aOR = 1.43, 95% CI: [0.95-2.15]), and unmarried mothers (aOR = 1.34, 95% CI: [0.89-2.03]). Among mothers with moderate household income ($24,001-$48,000), BFHI designation was associated with significantly greater odds of exclusive breastfeeding at 8 weeks (aOR = 1.85, 95% CI: [1.19-2.89]); a similar, nonsignificant pattern was observed for any breastfeeding at 8 weeks (aOR = 1.63, 95% CI: [0.99-2.70]).
CONCLUSIONS: BFHI demonstrates differential effects across SDOH, benefiting first-time and moderate-income mothers but not Black mothers. Culturally responsive nursing care and tailored interventions are needed to achieve breastfeeding equity.

Title: Postoperative Vasoactive Exposure Patterns and Outcomes After Non-Cardiac Surgery: A Prespecified Analysis of the SQUEEZE Cohort.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative vasoactive therapy is usually summarised by its presence or duration, although haemodynamic support evolves over time. We investigated whether reproducible postoperative vasoactive exposure patterns provide prognostic information beyond the duration of postoperative vasoactive therapy.
METHODS: We performed a prespecified substudy of the international SQUEEZE cohort. Adults receiving postoperative vasoactive infusion within seven postoperative days after non-cardiac surgery were included. Unsupervised k-means clustering identified exposure patterns using duration of postoperative vasoactive infusion, cumulative vasoactive agent-days, and peak number of concurrent agents. Associations with 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), and hospital length of stay were assessed using multivariable regression. A prespecified landmark analysis evaluated early postoperative vasoactive exposure burden during postoperative days 0-1.
RESULTS: Among 25,672 patients, 6676 (26.0%) received postoperative vasoactive infusion. Four reproducible exposure patterns were identified. Adjusted 30-day mortality ranged from 9.7% in the low-burden pattern to 35.3% in the high-burden pattern but was not strictly monotonic, whereas adjusted AKI risk increased from 28.0% to 56.0% across patterns. In covariate-adjusted models fitted to the same complete-case cohort, discrimination was higher when exposure pattern rather than duration was included (AUC 0.818 vs. 0.795), while adding duration to pattern classification resulted in little additional discrimination (AUC 0.819). Findings were consistent in the early postoperative landmark analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative vasoactive exposure follows reproducible patterns characterised by persistence and overall treatment burden rather than binary classification alone. These patterns were associated with mortality, AKI, and hospital length of stay, and provided prognostic information beyond duration alone.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This substudy and analysis of the SQUEEZE cohort, which represents a large sample of cases with focus on post-operative vasopressor treatments, shows that more intensive vasopressor therapy was associated with worse postoperative outcomes, including for mortality and 30 days and postoperative acute kidney injury occurrence.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03805230.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: A Single Center Retrospective Study: Efficacy and Platelet Preservation of Double Plasma Molecular Adsorption System Therapy by Membrane Separation Versus Centrifugal Separation in Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure Patients With Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and liver failure. The double plasma molecular adsorption system (DPMAS) reduces bilirubin and may create a therapeutic window for anti-tumor therapy in HCC patients. Two plasma separation techniques are used: membrane-based (MBS-DPMAS) and centrifugal (CPS-DPMAS), but no study has compared them specifically in HCC patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). This retrospective study included 203 HBV-related HCC patients who received DPMAS without plasma exchange (93 MBS-DPMAS, 110 CPS-DPMAS), with citrate anticoagulation used in all cases. Bilirubin, liver enzymes, INR, and platelet count were compared between groups and before versus after treatment. Baseline characteristics were comparable. CPS-DPMAS showed superior bilirubin reduction (TBIL: 184.60 vs. 220.05 μmol/L, p = 0.002; DBIL: 156.04 vs. 183.55 μmol/L, p = 0.004), whereas platelet count was significantly higher after MBS-DPMAS than after CPS-DPMAS (135.35 vs. 106.32 × 109/L, p = 0.012). Both modalities decreased INR transiently, and only MBS-DPMAS significantly reduced ALT, AST, and creatinine. In conclusion, both techniques effectively reduce bilirubin and decrease INR, but CPS-DPMAS offers better bilirubin clearance while MBS-DPMAS provides better platelet protection, suggesting that technique selection should be individualized.

Title: Temporal Trends in Patient Characteristics, Anticoagulation Treatment Quality, and Clinical Outcomes of Individuals Receiving Vitamin K Antagonists in the Netherlands (2014 Until-2022).
Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe temporal trends in the clinical landscape of vitamin K antagonist (VKA) treatment in the Netherlands, after the introduction of a lower international normalized ratio (INR) target range in 2016 and direct oral anticoagulants.
METHODS: Data from 17 Dutch anticoagulation clinics between 2014 and 2022 were individually linked to nationwide healthcare data. Prevalent VKA users were identified on January 1 of each year, forming nine annual cohorts. We assessed baseline patient characteristics, anticoagulation treatment quality (using time in/above/below therapeutic range [TTR/ATR/BTR]), and annual odds ratios of major bleeding and thromboembolism for each cohort.
RESULTS: The number of patients treated with VKAs increased from 101 090 in 2014 to 121 916 in 2017, followed by a decline to 73 649 in 2022. Over time, cohorts were characterized by increasing age and a higher prevalence of comorbidities, with a doubling of kidney disease. After the introduction of the lower INR target range, mean BTR decreased (~30% in 2014 to ~15% in 2022), while mean TTR increased (~54% in 2014 to ~67% in 2022), with stable mean ATR. Across calendar years, the 1-year odds ratio of major bleeding decreased from 1.71% (95% CI 1.63-1.79) in 2014 to 1.52% (95% CI 1.44-1.61) in 2022, whereas the odds ratio of ischemic stroke/transient ischemic attack/systemic thromboembolism increased from 1.14% (95% CI 1.08-1.21) in 2014 to 1.32% (95% CI 1.24-1.40) in 2022. The 1-year odds ratio of mortality increased from 5.09 (95% CI 4.95-5.22) to 8.55 (95% CI 8.35-8.75), with an OR of 1.74 (95% CI 1.68-1.81).
CONCLUSIONS: VKA users declined between 2014 and 2022. The remaining patients using VKA became older and more comorbid. During this period, INR target ranges were lowered, while temporal changes were observed with decreasing odds ratio of major bleeding and increasing odds ratio of thromboembolism and mortality.

Title: Clinical outcomes of sacubitril/valsartan in patients with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction and acute heart failure: a multi-institutional study.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The long-term real-world effectiveness and safety of in-hospital initiation of sacubitril/valsartan in patients hospitalized for acute heart failure (HF) with mildly reduced or preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (HFmrEF or HFpEF) remain uncertain, particularly among patients with advanced chronic kidney disease or dialysis, who are often underrepresented in randomized trials.
PATIENTS/MATERIALS AND METHODS: We identified 9,107 patients with HFmrEF or HFpEF hospitalized for acute HF from the Chang Gung Research Database between January 1, 2016, and June 30, 2023. Propensity score weighting with overlap weights was applied to balance baseline characteristics between treatment groups. Risks of fatal and nonfatal outcomes were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models, respectively.
RESULTS: After overlap weighting, the incidence rates of the composite endpoint of HF rehospitalization and cardiovascular (CV) death were 39.7 and 40.3 per 100 person-years in the angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) and angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) groups, respectively (Hazard ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.79-1.20). In analyses stratified by chronic kidney disease stage, the association between treatment group and the primary endpoint was consistent among patients with eGFR ≥60, 30-59, <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, or dialysis.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multi-institutional real-world cohort of patients hospitalized for acute HF with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) >40%, in-hospital initiation of sacubitril/valsartan was not associated with lower risks of HF rehospitalization or CV death compared with ARB therapy, despite greater NT-proBNP reduction in a biomarker subcohort. Limited sample size precludes definitive conclusions regarding therapeutic equivalence.
Publication Types: Journal Article; Multicenter Study; Observational Study

Title: The effect of different exercise modalities on the maximal left ventricular outflow tract gradient in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assessment of maximally provoked LVOT obstruction (LVOTO) guides treatment decisions in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Guidelines recommend various maneuvers, with exercise stress echocardiography (ESE) as the preferred method if others fail. Comparative data are limited. Therefore, in this prospective study, 20 patients with obstructive HCM underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) with continuous wave Doppler measuring LVOT gradients at rest, during the Valsalva maneuver, handgrip exercise at 30% and 50% of maximal hand force, squats, and bicycle ESE, with the aim of comparing commonly used maneuvers and evaluating handgrip exercise as a potential alternative for eliciting LVOTO.
RESULTS: The mean resting LVOT gradient was 38.9 ± 31.4 mmHg. Handgrip exercise caused no significant change of LVOT gradients. In contrast, gradients increased markedly during the Valsalva maneuver (98.9 ± 52.8 mmHg), squats (120.3 ± 68.8 mmHg), and bicycle ESE (83.4 ± 43.3 mmHg; p < 0.001 vs. rest). There was no significant difference between Valsalva, squats, and ESE (p = NS). Squats induced the maximal gradient in 50% of patients. Performance time was significantly shorter for the Valsalva maneuver (15 s) and squats (1 min 23 s ± 28 s) than for bicycle ESE (15 min 54 s ± 5 min 46 s; p < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: The Valsalva maneuver, squats, and bicycle ESE are equally effective in provoking LVOTO, whereas handgrip exercise is not. Given their simplicity, low cost, and shorter testing time, squats may serve as a practical adjunct to the Valsalva maneuver for LVOT gradient provocation in routine clinical assessment of obstructive HCM.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register (ID: DRKS00034473).

Title: Racial and Socioeconomic Inequities in COVID-19 In-Hospital Mortality in Brazil in the Post-Emergency Era: A National Cohort Study of 19,718 Hospitalized Adults in 2024.
Journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, COVID-19 entered a post-emergency phase, but in-hospital mortality remains a relevant public health concern in Brazil. As population immunity, vaccination, and clinical management evolved, the hierarchy of mortality predictors may have shifted from traditional metabolic risk factors toward clinical severity and social vulnerability. This study aimed to identify sociodemographic, clinical, management, and vaccination-related variables associated with in-hospital COVID-19 mortality among adults in Brazil in 2024, with emphasis on racial and socioeconomic inequities.
METHODS: A retrospective national cohort study was conducted using the SIVEP-Gripe surveillance database. Adults aged ≥ 18 years hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 between January and December 2024 were included. The primary analysis was restricted to patients with observed hospital outcomes, resulting in an analytical sample of 19,718 individuals. Crude and adjusted associations were estimated using binary logistic regression. Race/color was modeled using White patients as the reference category. Robustness to unmeasured confounding was assessed using E-values, and model performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC.
RESULTS: The in-hospital fatality rate was 23.5% (n = 4,633). Invasive ventilatory support was the strongest predictor of death (aOR: 7.574; 95% CI: 6.801-8.435; E-value: 4.95). Black patients had higher odds of death compared with White patients (aOR: 1.506; 95% CI: 1.233-1.838; E-value: 1.76), as did Pardo/mixed-race patients, although with lower magnitude (aOR: 1.103; 95% CI: 1.006-1.209). A strong educational gradient was observed, with illiterate patients having more than twice the odds of death compared with those with higher education (aOR: 2.148; 95% CI: 1.628-2.833). Incomplete COVID-19 vaccination was also associated with increased mortality, while influenza vaccination was associated with lower odds of death. Diabetes, obesity, and chronic cardiovascular disease were not independently associated with mortality after adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital COVID-19 mortality in Brazil in 2024 was shaped by respiratory severity, incomplete vaccination, and persistent racial and socioeconomic inequities. Although structural racism was not directly measured, the persistence of racialized mortality differences after adjustment is compatible with structural barriers in the healthcare pathway. Equity-oriented strategies should complement vaccination and clinical management to reduce preventable mortality among socially vulnerable populations.

Title: Trajectory of preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm): patterns, predictors, and potential interventions.
Abstract: Preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm), an abnormal spirometry condition characterized by a decreased forced expiratory volume at the first second (FEV1), is recognized as a precursor of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Growing studies demonstrate that PRISm is associated with an increased risk of the development of fixed airflow obstruction (FAO) and cardiovascular mortality. However, there is still a lack of comprehensive understanding of the patterns and predictors of lung function trajectories in PRISm. Furthermore, standardized interventions that can prevent the deterioration of lung function in PRISm remain unclear. The purpose of this narrative review is to examine the natural history of PRISm by summarizing current evidence on its progression over time, key determinants, and modifiable factors, thereby identifying opportunities for early intervention. In this review, three main patterns of PRISm trajectories were reported, including PRISm to normal spirometry, persistent PRISm, and PRISm to FAO. In accordance, several important factors, such as body mass index (BMI), smoking status, baseline lung function values, comorbid respiratory symptoms and various diseases, and PRISm subtypes, were identified as predictors for the transition of PRISm to other lung function status. Additionally, several potential intervention strategies were developed to slow down the decline of lung function in PRISm and reduce PRISm-related mortality, including early screening and regular monitoring, non-pharmacological interventions, pharmacological interventions, and hierarchical management.
